papers.title: Governing Generative AI Across Borders: A Comparative Research Concept on Voice Identity, Creative Rights, Transparency, and Inclusive Innovation
papers.authors: Michael Neely
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is reshaping cultural production, identity authentication, education, and public accountability. This proposed comparative study examines how governance frameworks address synthetic voice replication, consent, attribution, traceability, remedy, and equitable access to AI innovation. The research will compare legal and policy instruments in nine jurisdictions: the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Canada, and South Africa. It will develop an analytical framework for evaluating protections, identify implementation gaps, and propose practical governance indicators. No empirical findings are claimed in this concept document. Research concept / prospective collaboration document; no empirical findings are claimed.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究概念文档提出一项跨国比较研究设想，考察生成式人工智能治理框架如何应对合成语音复制、同意、归属、可追溯性、救济以及公平获取AI创新等问题。研究计划比较美国、英国、德国、法国、日本、韩国、澳大利亚、加拿大和南非九个司法辖区的法律与政策工具，拟构建评估保护措施的分析框架，识别实施缺口并提出可操作的治理指标。文档明确说明自身只是研究概念与前瞻性合作文件，并未声称任何实证发现，因此其价值在于提出比较框架与治理议题，而非给出已验证的结论。

papers.title: Personal Brain Models: Chatting with a Model of Your Own Human Brain
papers.authors: Sanket Bhandari
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: What if you could chat with your own brain, the way you chat with ChatGPT? Chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude are trained on general internet text, so their ideas are often generic and similar for everyone. A person's most original ideas come from their own experiences, such as joyful moments, past traumas and lessons from growing up. But when the brain is tired or stressed, it cannot recall them. This position paper proposes the Personal Brain Model: an AI model of one person's brain, built from signals recorded from their own brain. The person can ask it questions and brainstorm with it, and it works together with chatbots like Claude to turn their own memories into new ideas. The paper also proposes the Self Test, which checks two things: whether the model answers like the person, and whether it can bring back memories they had forgotten.
papers.summary_zh: 该立场论文提出“个人大脑模型”构想：用个人自身大脑记录信号构建专属AI模型，让用户与之对话和头脑风暴，并与通用聊天机器人协作，把个人记忆转化为新想法，以弥补通用聊天机器人因基于公共文本训练而想法趋同的不足。作者同时提出“自我测试”，从模型回答是否像本人、能否唤回本人已遗忘的记忆两方面加以检验。文章属于概念与评估设想，未报告实证结果，其可行性和效果仍待验证。

papers.title: Deterministic Deterrence by Denial and Sovereign Critical Infrastructure Resilience in the Euro-Atlantic Theater: Formalizing Multi-Domain Forward Defense, QFS-zkVM Allied Sensor Fusion, and Macro-Fiscal Stability Against Sub-Threshold Hybrid Warfare
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and the concurrent escalation of omni-directional hybrid warfare across the Diplomatic, Information, Military, Economic, Financial, Intelligence, and Law Enforcement (DIMEFIL) spectrum have invalidated the post-Cold War security equilibrium of the Euro-Atlantic theater. Because gray-zone provocations, cyber-kinetic sabotage of subsea cables and energy pipelines, autonomous drone incursions, and weaponized migration are calibrated to remain systematically below the kinetic activation threshold of North Atlantic Treaty Article 5, traditional Deterrence by Punishment exhibits severe credibility decay. Consequently, NATO and European frontline states have executed a structural paradigm shift toward Deterrence by Denial, Forward Defense, and Whole-of-Society Resilience across three operational domains: (1) Eastern Flank land border fortification (the Baltic Defense Line, Drone Wall, and Poland's AI-integrated Tarcza Wschód [East Shield]); (2) Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD) under the German-led European Sky Shield Initiative (ESSI); and (3) Maritime and Arctic critical infrastructure protection (Operation Baltic Sentry and counter-A2/AD surveillance across the Kola Peninsula). This monograph formalizes this strategic transition within the RTO P2.0 deterministic resilience architecture. First, we derive a game-theoretic and thermodynamic threshold model demonstrating why sub-threshold hybrid perturbations require driving adversarial probability of operational success to zero via physical and cryptographic denial. Second, we resolve the European strategic schism between German operational readiness (Buy-Fast) and French industrial sovereignty (Buy-European) by introducing a zero-knowledge federated C4ISR verification layer over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field F_p (p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) using QFS-zkVM and Q-SAFA, enabling interoperability between heterogeneous air defense systems (Patriot, Arrow 3, IRIS-T, and SAMP/T) without leaking sovereign radar waveforms. Third, we model the macro-fiscal collision between front-loaded defense expenditures (reaching 4.91%–5.40% of GDP in the Baltic states and driving Poland's projected 2025 fiscal deficit to 7.3% of GDP) and the European Union's Excessive Deficit Procedure (EDP), proposing a constitutional fiscal bifurcation and PHOENIX_BRIDGE / PHOENIX_ROUTER hardware interlocks governed by Human-in-Command (HIC) oversight. papers.summary_zh: 该文以2022年俄乌冲突后欧洲—大西洋地区的次阈值混合威胁为背景，讨论为何传统惩罚性威慑可信度下降，并转向拒止性威慑、前沿防御与全社会韧性。作者构建博弈论与热力学阈值模型，论证须通过物理与密码手段把对手行动成功率压至零；同时提出基于QFS-zkVM的零知识联邦C4ISR验证层，使异构防空系统互操作而不泄露主权雷达波形。文章还分析前沿防务支出与欧盟超额赤字程序之间的宏观财政冲突，建议宪法性财政分轨及受人类指挥监督的硬件联锁。上述均为该专著的模型与制度设计主张，而非实证检验结果。

papers.title: Application of Chemistry Achievement Test for Secondary School Students Using Developed ChatGPT Artificial intelligence and Traditional methods
papers.authors: Abasifreke Nse Essien
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study was on Application of Chemistry Achievement Test for Secondary School Students Developed Using ChatGPT Artificial intelligence and Traditional methods. Three research questions and were formulated to guide the study. The instrumentation research design was used for the study. The population of the study consisted of all 11,594 Senior Secondary School Two (SSII) students from all the 187 public secondary schools in Akwa Ibom State. Multistage sampling procedure was used for the study. The sample of 387 SSII Students was used for the study. Data was collected using two researcher developed instruments named, “Chemistry Achievement Test On Chemical Equilibrium Developed using ChatGPT Method (CATCEDCM) and Chemistry Achievement Test On Chemical Equilibrium Developed using Traditional Method (CATCEDTM)”. The reliability coefficients of CATCEDCM and CATCEDTM were .992 and .971 determined using Split Half Method of reliability determination. The research questions were answered mean and standard deviation statistics while the independent t-test statistics was used to test the formulated null hypotheses at .05 alpha level. The findings of the study revealed that Students had higher achievement scores on Chemistry Achievement Test on Chemical Equilibrium developed using ChatGPT Artificial Intelligence than same test developed using traditional method. It was also revealed male and female Students had the same achievement scores on Chemistry Achievement Test on Chemical Equilibrium developed using ChatGPT Artificial Intelligence. Recommendations were made among others that Chemistry teachers should always make use ChatGPT artificial intelligence over the traditional method when developing a test since it could produce a test that appropriately assess students’ academic achievement.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究比较了使用ChatGPT人工智能与传统方法编制的化学成就测验对中学生成绩的影响，采用仪器研究设计，以尼日利亚阿夸伊博姆州公立高中二年级学生为对象，通过多阶段抽样选取样本，并用自编的化学平衡成就测验收集数据。结果显示，学生在ChatGPT方法编制的测验上成绩高于传统方法编制的测验，且男女学生在ChatGPT测验上的成绩无差异。作者据此建议化学教师编制测验时优先使用ChatGPT，认为其能更适当地评估学生学业成就；但该结论基于特定地区与学科情境，推广需谨慎。

papers.title: Quantum-Classical Hybrid Cloud Workflows for Combinatorial Supply-Chain and Fleet Optimization
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Global logistics networks, intercontinental air-freight consolidators, and maritime energy fleets continuously solve large-scale Mixed-Integer Linear Programs (MILPs) such as the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (CVRPTW) and multi-vessel Maritime Inventory Routing Problems (MIRP). When weather disruptions, port congestion, or geopolitical airspace closures invalidate baseline schedules, classical branch-and-cut solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) experience exponential worst-case tree growth on subproblems exceeding 2,000 binary decision variables, often failing to converge within strict 5-to-15-minute operational re-dispatch windows. Conversely, current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) processors remain limited to 100-to-1,000 physical qubits with finite two-qubit gate fidelity ($99.2\%-99.8\%$), preventing direct encoding of full enterprise logistics instances. This paper presents a production-grade Quantum-Classical Hybrid Cloud Architecture that bridges enterprise Kubernetes clusters with co-located quantum processing units (QPUs) via AWS Braket Hybrid Jobs and IBM Quantum Qiskit Runtime primitives. Our framework applies Benders and Dantzig-Wolfe column generation on classical cloud HPC nodes to decompose a 25,000-variable global fleet MILP into a continuous master problem and hard combinatorial pricing/routing subproblems of 60 to 140 binary variables. These subproblems are transformed into Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) and Ising Hamiltonians, warm-started from classical linear programming (LP) relaxations (WS-QAOA), compiled with dynamical decoupling and Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE), and executed inside co-located QPU-CPU sessions while a GPU-accelerated Simulated Bifurcation (SB) digital annealer runs in parallel as a deterministic SLA fallback. Evaluated on disruption recovery workloads modeled on ExxonMobil maritime LNG routing and DHL Global Forwarding air-cargo container loading, our hybrid WS-QAOA + Column Generation workflow improves optimality gap closure at a 10-minute SLA cutoff from 6.84% (classical branch-and-bound alone) to 1.42%, reduces emergency re-routing compute wall-clock time by 61.5%, and cuts fleet fuel and charter penalty costs by 4.7%. Research Domain & Specialization Track Master of Science in Information Technology (MSIT) — Quantum Cloud Computing, Hybrid Orchestration, and Operations Research. Core Technical Highlights Empirical Production Case Studies: Rigorous architectural blueprints and telemetry evaluation across enterprise cloud deployments. Four-Tier Reference Architecture: Formal specification from edge ingress to distributed hardware execution pools. Mathematical Formulation: Formally derived algorithmic and optimization models with closed-loop verification. Multi-Modal Benchmarking: Comparative empirical baselines under fault-injection and synthetic workload scaling. papers.summary_zh: 该文提出一套面向组合供应链与车队优化的量子—经典混合云工作流，用经典云节点上的Benders与列生成把大规模混合整数规划分解为主问题和60至140个二值变量的子问题，再转为QUBO/Ising形式，经热启动QAOA并在共置QPU上执行，同时以GPU加速的模拟分岔退火作为确定性兜底。基于埃克森美孚海运LNG路径与DHL空运集装箱装载的扰动恢复算例，作者报告在10分钟时限下最优性差距由纯经典分支定界的6.84%降至1.42%，应急重路由计算时间减少61.5%，燃料与租船罚金成本下降4.7%。这些结果来自作者自建的案例与基准，属系统实现与实证评估，其外部推广仍受算例设定与硬件条件限制。

papers.title: Synthetic Tabular and Clinical Data Generation in Privacy-Preserving Cloud Sandboxes
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Secondary analysis of electronic health records (EHR), clinical trial registries, and consumer financial ledgers is severely constrained by regulatory mandates including HIPAA, GDPR, and the UK NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit. Traditional heuristic de-identification methods such as k-anonymity, l-diversity, and date-shifting fail against modern linkage and reconstruction attacks when applied to high-dimensional sparse tabular schemas and longitudinal patient trajectories. Conversely, locking raw sensitive datasets inside air-gapped Trusted Research Environments (TREs) delays external machine learning development by three to nine months per data access request. This paper presents an end-to-end architecture for generating high-utility, mathematically certified synthetic tabular and clinical data inside hardware-attested Confidential Cloud Sandboxes (AMD SEV-SNP and NVIDIA H100 Confidential Computing). Our hybrid generative engine combines Conditional Tabular Diffusion (TabDDPM) for mixed continuous-categorical marginals with an autoregressive Transformer trained via Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) and Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP) moments accounting for multi-visit ICD-10 clinical sequences. Before any synthetic dataset or trained weight artifact can egress the enclave boundary, an automated Privacy Auditor Gate executes shadow-model Membership Inference Attacks (MIA), Distance-to-Closest-Record (DCR) memorization tests, and clinical ontology constraint verification. We evaluate this architecture against production patterns from the UK NHS Digital Synthetic Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) program and enterprise cloud sandboxes powered by Gretel.ai and Mostly AI across 2.4 million inpatient episodes. Empirical evaluations at a strict privacy budget of $(\epsilon = 2.0, \delta = 10^{-6})$ demonstrate that our hybrid diffusion-transformer pipeline retains 96.4% of real-data downstream XGBoost/LightGBM AUROC utility (compared to 81.2% for DP-CTGAN), bounds empirical membership inference AUC at 0.514 (near random guessing of 0.500), achieves 99.8% ICD-10/OPCS-4 clinical validity, and reduces researcher data-access provisioning lead time from 180 days to 4.5 hours. Research Domain & Specialization Track Master of Science in Information Technology (MSIT) — Generative AI, Privacy Engineering, and Cloud Data Sandboxes. Core Technical Highlights Empirical Production Case Studies: Rigorous architectural blueprints and telemetry evaluation across enterprise cloud deployments. Four-Tier Reference Architecture: Formal specification from edge ingress to distributed hardware execution pools. Mathematical Formulation: Formally derived algorithmic and optimization models with closed-loop verification. Multi-Modal Benchmarking: Comparative empirical baselines under fault-injection and synthetic workload scaling. papers.summary_zh: 该文提出一套在硬件可信的机密云沙箱中生成高可用合成表格与临床数据的端到端架构，以缓解电子健康记录等敏感数据受隐私法规限制、难以用于二次分析的问题。其混合生成引擎结合条件表格扩散模型与经差分隐私训练的 Transformer，用于处理混合型表格字段和多访次 ICD-10 临床序列，并在数据出域前由自动隐私审计环节执行成员推断攻击、最近记录距离记忆测试和临床本体约束校验。基于 NHS 住院 episode 数据的评估显示，该流程在严格隐私预算下保留了大部分下游预测效用，成员推断接近随机水平，临床编码有效性较高，并大幅缩短数据获取等待时间；这些结果来自作者设定的基准比较，实际部署效果仍需进一步验证。

papers.title: eBPF-Accelerated Cloud Networking and Kernel-Bypass Service Mesh for High-Throughput AI Clusters
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Distributed artificial intelligence training, disaggregated retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) inference, and high-frequency cloud-native microservices place unprecedented bandwidth and tail-latency demands on Kubernetes cluster networking. Conventional Kubernetes Container Network Interfaces (CNIs) and sidecar-based service meshes rely on chained `iptables` netfilter rules and per-pod user-space Envoy proxies that traverse the Linux kernel TCP/IP stack up to six times for a single pod-to-pod RPC. Under high-concurrency AI tensor streaming and gRPC microservice fan-out, this architecture induces severe context-switching overhead, L1/L2 instruction cache pollution, ephemeral port exhaustion, and tail-latency spikes exceeding 15 milliseconds at the 99th percentile. This paper presents an eBPF-accelerated cloud networking and kernel-bypass service mesh architecture designed for multi-tenant AI and microservice clusters. The architecture integrates eXpress Data Path (XDP) driver-level packet processing, `tcx` (traffic control express) eBPF host routing, socket-level `BPF_MAP_TYPE_SOCKHASH` loopback splicing (`sk_msg`), Big TCP (up to 192 KB GSO/GRO super-packets), and a sidecarless per-node L7/mTLS datapath modeled on Cilium and Hubble. We formulate a mathematical queueing and CPU-cycle cost model comparing `iptables` + sidecar traversal against eBPF socket redirection and ECN-assisted congestion pacing. We evaluate the architecture using production engineering case studies from Datadog and Adobe multi-cluster Kubernetes environments alongside controlled benchmarks on 100 Gbps and 400 Gbps cloud nodes running disaggregated vLLM inference and distributed KV-cache synchronization. Empirical results show that the eBPF datapath reduces p99 RPC latency by 64.8% (from 4.82 ms to 1.70 ms), elevates sustained node-to-node throughput from 58.4 Gbps to 94.6 Gbps per 100GbE link, cuts networking vCPU consumption by 57.3%, and scales linearly across 50,000+ Kubernetes services with $O(1)$ hash lookup complexity. Research Domain & Specialization Track Master of Science in Information Technology (MSIT) — Cloud Networking, Linux Kernel Datapaths, and Kubernetes Service Mesh. Core Technical Highlights Empirical Production Case Studies: Rigorous architectural blueprints and telemetry evaluation across enterprise cloud deployments. Four-Tier Reference Architecture: Formal specification from edge ingress to distributed hardware execution pools. Mathematical Formulation: Formally derived algorithmic and optimization models with closed-loop verification. Multi-Modal Benchmarking: Comparative empirical baselines under fault-injection and synthetic workload scaling. Author Information Author: Sonu Kumar SinghRole: Senior Consultant Affiliation: Independent Researcher Publication Status: Preprint / Working Paper (MSIT AI & Cloud Systems Research Series) Reproducibility & Open Science All included architecture diagrams, telemetry schemas, and benchmark curves are open-access under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.
papers.summary_zh: 该文针对Kubernetes集群中传统CNI与sidecar服务网格因多次穿越内核TCP/IP栈而带来的高开销与尾延迟问题，提出一种eBPF加速、内核旁路的云网络与服务网格架构，整合XDP、tcx主机路由、套接字重定向、Big TCP及无sidecar的节点级L7/mTLS数据通路，并建立排队与CPU周期成本模型进行对比。作者结合Datadog与Adobe的生产案例及100/400 Gbps节点上分离式vLLM推理与KV缓存同步的基准测试，报告该数据通路降低了p99 RPC延迟、提升了单链路吞吐、减少了网络vCPU消耗，并可在大量服务下保持近似常数复杂度的查找扩展。这些结果说明内核旁路方案在高并发AI集群网络中具有缓解尾延迟和降低主机开销的潜力，但结论主要基于特定生产环境与受控基准，外推需谨慎。

papers.title: Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems for Cloud Migration and Legacy Mainframe Code Modernization
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Global financial, insurance, and telecommunications infrastructures remain heavily dependent on monolithic mainframe workloads written in COBOL, PL/I, Job Control Language (JCL), and Customer Information Control System (CICS) transaction monitors. Migrating these mission-critical systems to cloud-native microservices presents severe engineering hazards: undocumented business logic, implicit EBCDIC fixed-point arithmetic semantics, shared hierarchical VSAM and IMS database state, and the absence of automated regression test suites. Naive single-pass large language model (LLM) code translation frequently introduces subtle numerical rounding discrepancies, broken transactional boundaries, and uncompilable dependency graphs when processing modules exceeding 50,000 lines of code. This paper presents an autonomous multi-agent cloud migration architecture that combines static program analysis, neuro-symbolic graph partitioning, and execution-guided differential verification to modernize legacy mainframe estates into cloud-native Java Quarkus and Spring Boot microservices on Kubernetes. The proposed architecture coordinates four specialized autonomous agents: a Static Archaeologist Agent that builds System Dependence Graphs (SDGs) and extracts business rules, a Domain Architect Agent that computes optimal microservice decomposition boundaries via constrained spectral clustering, a Code Transpiler Agent powered by domain-adapted foundation models, and a Differential Verifier Agent that synthesizes property-based test harnesses and executes shadow-traffic replay against mainframe CICS regions. We evaluate this framework against production modernization workflows inspired by IBM watsonx Code Assistant for Z and Morgan Stanley DevGen.AI across 4.2 million lines of legacy COBOL and PL/I code. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate that the multi-agent pipeline increases semantic equivalence pass rates from 61.4% (single-agent LLM baseline) to 98.7%, reduces manual refactoring effort by 74.2%, shrinks batch-to-streaming settlement latency from 184.0 ms to 29.4 ms at the 99th percentile, and lowers mainframe Million Instructions Per Second (MIPS) licensing expenditures by 68.5%. papers.title: Elastic Vector Databases and Billion-Scale Disk-Backed ANN Indexing on Cloud Object Storage
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), enterprise semantic search, and multi-modal agentic memory systems increasingly require indexing billions of high-dimensional embedding vectors across hundreds of thousands of isolated tenant namespaces. Conventional first-generation vector databases rely on monolithic in-memory Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs that pin full-precision FP32 vectors and adjacency lists inside expensive cluster DRAM, resulting in prohibitive cloud infrastructure costs and poor resource utilization under bursty, multi-tenant query distributions. This paper presents a disaggregated, serverless Elastic Vector Database architecture that couples billion-scale disk-backed Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexing with cloud object storage (Amazon S3 / GCS) and local NVMe SSD caching. Synthesizing production engineering advances from Pinecone Serverless, Milvus 2.4 Knowhere DiskANN, and Turbopuffer object-storage-native indexing, our architecture separates stateless write/query compute workers from durable object storage through four key innovations: (1) geometric slab partitioning via balanced k-means centroid trees in RAM, (2) single-pass Vamana graph construction with compressed Product Quantization (PQ) codes in memory and full-precision vectors on NVMe/S3, (3) `io_uring` asynchronous beam-search prefetching that coalesces 4-kilobyte SSD sector reads, and (4) log-structured merge (LSM) object-storage compaction. We evaluate the architecture on a 1.5-billion-vector, 768-dimensional benchmark dataset deployed on AWS EKS with Amazon S3 and local NVMe cache tiers. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed storage-disaggregated DiskANN + S3 architecture reduces cluster DRAM consumption by 89.2% and lowers monthly cloud hosting costs by 78.5% compared to in-memory HNSW clusters, while sustaining 95.8% Recall@10 at a 99th-percentile query latency of 11.4 milliseconds for hot NVMe namespaces and 168 milliseconds for cold S3 cache-miss namespaces. papers.title: Immutable Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and Policy-as-Code Guardrails for Sovereign AI Cloud Platforms
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Sovereign and regulated enterprise artificial intelligence platforms operate under stringent statutory mandates governing data residency, customer-managed cryptographic key custody, hardware-enforced confidential computing, and cross-border network isolation. When cloud platform teams manage hundreds of multi-tenant AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud accounts using manual console interventions or imperative scripts, configuration drift and overly permissive Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies create severe compliance exposure and unauthorized model-weight exfiltration vectors. This paper presents an end-to-end Immutable Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and Policy-as-Code (PaC) Governance Architecture designed to enforce provable security and regulatory invariants across sovereign AI cloud platforms. Synthesizing production engineering patterns from Goldman Sachs multi-account cloud governance and HashiCorp Terraform integrated with Open Policy Agent (OPA) Rego admission pipelines, the proposed architecture establishes a three-stage defense-in-depth enforcement loop: pre-apply static plan verification over Terraform abstract syntax trees, Kubernetes dynamic admission control via OPA Gatekeeper, and continuous drift reconciliation using Crossplane and AWS Config conformance packs. We evaluate the governance platform across a 120-account enterprise AI cloud estate hosting 640 GPU training and inference clusters over a 180-day production period. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate that shifting policy evaluation left into CI/CD pull-request gates catches 99.4% of IAM, S3 bucket encryption, VPC PrivateLink, and GPU confidential-compute misconfigurations in 3.8 seconds prior to cloud API provisioning. Furthermore, automated GitOps drift reconciliation eliminates manual SSH/console mutation, reducing Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR) configuration drift by 96.2% (from 6.4 hours to 14.5 seconds) and cutting quarterly regulatory audit preparation overhead by 84.0%. papers.title: Chaos Engineering and Automated Fault-Injection Verification for Distributed Cloud AI Microservices
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Modern enterprise artificial intelligence platforms decompose complex inference workflows—spanning API gateways, feature stores, vector databases, guardrails, and multi-GPU model serving pods—into deeply nested cloud-native microservices. While microservice disaggregation enables independent horizontal scaling across heterogeneous hardware accelerators, it simultaneously expands the combinatorial state space of partial failures, including GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) exhaustion, NCCL collective communication hangs, NVMe thermal throttling, and cascading retry storms. Conventional static unit tests and synthetic staging benchmarks fail to expose these emergent failure modes before production customer traffic is impacted. This paper presents an automated Chaos Engineering and Fault-Injection Verification framework tailored for distributed cloud AI microservices running on Kubernetes and Istio service meshes. Integrating principles from the Netflix Chaos Automation Platform (ChAP) and Gremlin enterprise fault injection on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), the proposed architecture orchestrates blast-radius-isolated canary experiments using HTTP/gRPC request-header routing, eBPF kernel-level hardware fault emulation, and Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) automated abort guardrails. We evaluate the verification platform across a 48-microservice generative AI and recommendation inference cluster subjected to 140 automated chaos campaigns over a 90-day production cycle. Empirical results demonstrate that continuous fault-injection verification uncovered 27 latent cascading failure defects prior to general availability, reduced Mean Time to Detection (MTTD) by 76.8% (from 18.5 minutes to 4.3 minutes), compressed Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) by 81.4% (from 47.2 minutes to 8.8 minutes), and improved steady-state p99 SLO compliance during real AWS availability zone perturbations from 94.10% to 99.96%. papers.title: Distributed Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) on Cloud Infrastructure for Real-Time E-Commerce Recommendation
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Modern e-commerce platforms process catalogs exceeding hundreds of millions of items and billions of user-item interaction edges, creating severe computational bottlenecks for real-time personalized recommendation. While Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) capture higher-order collaborative signals and structural relationships far more effectively than matrix factorization or two-tower dense retrieval models, scaling message-passing operations to billion-edge bipartite and heterogeneous graphs introduces exponential neighbor expansion, irregular memory access patterns, and cross-partition network saturation. This paper presents a cloud-native distributed GNN training and real-time serving architecture designed to bridge offline representation learning and sub-20-millisecond online candidate generation. The proposed architecture combines streaming vertex-cut graph partitioning,Personalized PageRank (PPR) importance-based neighborhood sampling, UVA (Unified Virtual Addressing) pinned host-to-GPU feature caching, and incremental streaming inductive inference triggered by Kafka user-event streams. Drawing upon production case studies of Pinterest PinSage on Amazon EC2 GPU clusters and Alibaba Cloud Aligraph across heterogeneous Taobao and Tmall merchant graphs, we evaluate the system on a 3.2-billion-edge e-commerce graph spanning 180 million users and 65 million products. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate that importance-weighted random walk sampling paired with 8-bit quantized GPU feature caches reduces inter-node PCIe and RDMA communication volume by 68.4%, accelerating epoch convergence by 3.7x compared to uniform k-hop GraphSAGE baselines. In online production serving, the hybrid two-stage pipeline combining pre-computed inductive item embeddings with real-time 1-hop session graph aggregation achieves a 99th-percentile latency of 14.8 milliseconds at 85,000 queries per second while improving Recall@50 by 19.2% and gross merchandise value (GMV) conversion rate by 8.6%. papers.title: Hardware-Enforced Confidential Computing and Homomorphic Encryption for Cross-Bank Financial Fraud AI
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Sophisticated financial crime syndicates orchestrate synthetic identity fraud, layering, and Authorized Push Payment (APP) laundering across dozens of correspondent banks and national jurisdictions within minutes. Single-institution machine learning models fail to detect these cross-bank topological patterns because each bank observes only an isolated local subgraph of the global transaction flow. However, statutory banking secrecy laws, GDPR Article 6/9 data protection mandates, and competitive confidentiality prohibit financial institutions from pooling cleartext account histories or counterparty graphs in a shared public cloud data lake. Conversely, executing deep Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) or gradient-boosted decision trees purely inside Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) schemes incurs four to five orders of magnitude computational slowdown due to non-polynomial activation bootstrapping, rendering real-time payment screening impossible. This paper proposes a Hybrid Cryptographic-Enclave Cross-Bank Fraud AI architecture that combines Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS) homomorphic encryption with hardware-attested Confidential Virtual Machines (AMD SEV-SNP and Intel TDX) coupled to NVIDIA H100 Confidential GPUs via encrypted PCIe/CXL integrity buses. Member banks encrypt local velocity vectors and counterparty risk embeddings under a threshold-shared CKKS public key so that untrusted cloud ingestion brokers perform homomorphic cross-bank feature aggregation in ciphertext without enclave memory exposure. The aggregated ciphertexts then enter a remotely attested AMD SEV-SNP + H100 Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) that performs threshold decryption, executes non-linear GNN and XGBoost scoring in hardware-encrypted memory, and re-encrypts risk alerts. Evaluated on a cross-border interbank anomaly detection case study modeled on SWIFT and JPMorgan Chase correspondent banking networks across 12 participating institutions, the hybrid architecture boosts cross-bank laundering recall from 58.2% (single-bank baseline) to 93.6%, reduces end-to-end encrypted scoring latency from 14,800 ms (pure FHE) to 28.5 ms, and guarantees zero cleartext exposure to cloud hypervisors or rival banks. papers.title: Edge-Cloud Continuum: Split Neural Inference and Adaptive Quantization for Industrial IoT
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Modern Industry 4.0 smart manufacturing plants deploy high-resolution line-scan cameras, acoustic emission arrays, and thermal imaging sensors that generate gigabits per second of raw inspection telemetry per assembly line. Executing large Vision Transformers (ViTs) and multi-scale object detection backbones entirely on resource-constrained industrial edge programmable logic controllers (PLCs) or embedded System-on-Modules (SoMs) exceeds thermal design power envelopes and violates strict 20-millisecond conveyor actuation deadlines. Conversely, streaming uncompressed 4K 120-fps camera frames over factory-floor private 5G or Wi-Fi 6E links to centralized cloud GPU clusters induces severe uplink congestion, packet jitter, and production line halts during wireless fading or WAN outages. This paper proposes an Adaptive Split Neural Inference and Entropy-Guided Mixed-Precision Quantization architecture for the industrial edge-cloud continuum. Our framework introduces a learned Bottleneck Injection Module (BIM) and an early-exit confidence classifier at intermediate network layers on NVIDIA Jetson Orin industrial edge nodes, teamed with a Lagrangian Dynamic Split Scheduler (LDSS) that jointly selects the optimal layer partition index $l^*$ and activation quantization bit-width $b \in \{2, 4, 8\}$ based on real-time wireless link capacity and cloud queue telemetry. Evaluated through a production-grade case study modeled on BMW Group iFactory Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) and Siemens Industrial Edge orchestrated via AWS IoT Greengrass across 64 automotive welding and paint-shop cells, empirical benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed continuum architecture resolves 76.4% of defect inspections locally via early exit in 5.8 ms, reduces 5G uplink bandwidth consumption by 88.2%, lowers end-to-end p99 inspection latency from 64.5 ms to 14.2 ms, and preserves 99.4% mean Average Precision (mAP@50) compared to full FP16 cloud execution. papers.title: Automated AI Governance, EU AI Act Compliance, and Cryptographic Model Lineage in Enterprise MLOps
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: As high-risk artificial intelligence systems proliferate across consumer credit underwriting, clinical diagnostics, and critical infrastructure, binding regulatory frameworks such as the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), the U.S. Federal Reserve SR 11-7 Model Risk Management supervisory guidance, and NIST AI RMF 1.0 mandate verifiable data provenance, bias auditing, technical documentation, and post-market monitoring. Conventional enterprise governance relies on manual review boards, static spreadsheet checklists, and retrospective Word documents that are decoupled from continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) machine learning pipelines. This manual governance bottleneck delays production model deployments by 6 to 14 weeks while failing to prevent unauthorized weight tampering, silent covariate shift, or disparate impact violations in live serving environments. This paper introduces a zero-trust Automated AI Governance and Cryptographic Model Lineage architecture for enterprise MLOps. Our framework constructs an immutable, Merkle-DAG Model Bill of Materials (MBOM) signed via Sigstore keyless OIDC identities, SLSA Level 3 build provenance, and in-toto supply-chain attestations, binding raw training datasets, feature transformations, hyperparameter configurations, and fairness evaluation reports directly to container digests. At runtime, Kubernetes Open Policy Agent (OPA) admission controllers and continuous statistical drift monitors enforce mathematically bounded demographic parity, Equalized Odds, and Population Stability Index (PSI) gates with automatic circuit-breaker rollback. Validated against an enterprise Model Risk Management (MRM) case study modeled on Capital One and Mastercard credit and fraud MLOps pipelines across 180 production models, our architecture cuts compliance audit preparation latency from 42 days to 14 minutes, blocks 100% of unsigned or bias-violating model promotions in < 350 milliseconds, and maintains disparate impact ratios above 0.91 under seasonal macroeconomic drift. papers.title: Multi-Cloud Disaster Recovery and Active-Active State Synchronization for Stateful AI Services
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Stateful artificial intelligence inference services, such as real-time payment fraud detection, dynamic credit underwriting, and conversational session agents, depend on sub-second access to mutable feature vectors, sliding-window velocity counters, and key-value attention caches. When deployed across a single cloud provider or single region, correlated control-plane outages, border gateway protocol route leaks, or availability zone power failures can halt inference pipelines and violate strict financial service-level objectives. Traditional active-passive disaster recovery architectures fail to meet zero-data-loss recovery point objectives (RPO) and sub-second recovery time objectives (RTO) because asynchronous storage snapshots leave in-flight streaming feature aggregations unpersisted and require minutes of cold-cache warming after failover. This paper presents a hybrid multi-cloud active-active state synchronization architecture that partitions stateful AI workloads into two consistency tiers: strongly serializable transaction ledgers backed by Multi-Raft quorum consensus with hardware-assisted clock uncertainty bounds, and low-latency velocity feature counters replicated via delta-state Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) over encrypted cross-cloud interconnects. We formulate a mathematical staleness-accuracy trade-off model that bounds fraud classification Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC) degradation as a function of replication lag and clock drift uncertainty. Evaluating the architecture through a production-grade case study modeled on Stripe multi-region payment fraud scoring alongside Google Cloud Spanner TrueTime and CockroachDB multi-region consensus deployments across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, empirical benchmarks demonstrate a 99.9994% availability rate, a p99 inference latency of 18.4 ms under active-active load, an RTO of 1.2 seconds during complete regional blackouts, and zero committed feature ledger loss. The findings provide cloud architects with a quantitative framework for balancing PACELC latency-consistency trade-offs against egress network costs in stateful multi-cloud AI deployments. papers.summary_zh: 该文针对有状态AI推理服务在单云部署下易受区域性故障影响、传统主备容灾难以满足零数据丢失与亚秒级恢复目标的问题，提出一种混合多云双活状态同步架构。作者将状态划分为强一致事务账本与低延迟特征计数器两个一致性层级，分别采用多Raft法定人数共识和增量状态CRDT复制，并建立复制滞后与时钟漂移对欺诈分类精度影响的理论模型。基于生产级案例与跨云共识部署的基准测试显示，该架构在区域完全中断时仍保持高可用、低推理延迟和秒级恢复，且已提交特征账本无丢失，为多云AI部署中的延迟、一致性与网络成本权衡提供了量化框架。

papers.title: Cloud Lakehouse Architectures for Real-Time Feature Stores and Streaming Machine Learning
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Production machine learning systems in real-time fraud detection, dynamic pricing, and personalized ranking depend on low-latency access to both historical batch aggregations and sub-second streaming behavioral signals. Traditional Lambda architectures maintain separate codebases and storage engines for offline training (SQL/Spark over data lakes) and online serving (Java/Flink into key-value stores), introducing severe online-offline training-serving skew, future data leakage during historical backfills, and high operational maintenance overhead. This paper presents a unified Cloud Lakehouse Real-Time Feature Store architecture that bridges streaming stateful computation in Apache Flink with transactional Apache Iceberg lakehouse tables and tiered Redis/RocksDB online serving clusters. We formalize point-in-time correctness via bi-temporal ASOF join semantics and watermarks, guaranteeing mathematically zero future target leakage across historical training dataset generation. Using declarative feature definitions compiled simultaneously into Flink DataStream DAGs and Spark/Trino Iceberg compaction jobs, our architecture enforces single-source-of-truth feature lineage while executing exactly-once Chandy-Lamport asynchronous barrier snapshots to cloud object storage. We analyze real-world production deployments at Uber (Michelangelo Palette Feature Store) and DoorDash (Gigascale Real-Time Feature Platform combining Flink, Redis Cluster, and Apache Iceberg). Empirical evaluations at 1.2 million events per second demonstrate that unified Flink-to-Iceberg streaming ingestion with Z-order compaction and Redis Hash-tag pipelining reduces online feature retrieval P99 latency from 42.80 ms to 3.85 ms, cuts feature freshness lag from 45.0 minutes to 0.42 seconds, eliminates 2.4 percentage points of AUC loss caused by training-serving skew, and lowers monthly storage and memory TCO by 48.6% through hybrid RAM-NVMe tiering. papers.title: AIOps for Autonomous Incident Detection and Causal Root-Cause Analysis in Kubernetes Clusters
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Hyper-scale cloud-native applications deployed on Kubernetes comprise thousands of ephemeral microservice pods interconnected through dynamic service meshes, distributed caches, and asynchronous message brokers. When a localized infrastructure degradation or bad canary rollout occurs, retry amplification and synchronous remote procedure call (RPC) blocking propagate latency spikes upstream within milliseconds, triggering alert storms that overwhelm Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) on-call teams. Conventional threshold alerting and pairwise Pearson correlation engines fail to distinguish upstream symptomatic victims from the true originating root cause, resulting in prolonged Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR). This paper presents an end-to-end Artificial Intelligence for IT Operations (AIOps) architecture for autonomous incident detection and causal Root-Cause Analysis (RCA) in Kubernetes clusters. Our system ingests zero-instrumentation Linux kernel eBPF socket and syscall telemetry alongside OpenTelemetry metrics, logs, and distributed traces into a unified spatio-temporal representation. A Variational Graph Autoencoder (VGAE) coupled with Drain3 log template extraction detects multi-dimensional anomalies within 15 seconds of onset. To isolate the true culprit pod or node resource, we combine the Peter-Clark (PC) conditional independence algorithm with interventional Do-calculus and Personalized PageRank over the live Kubernetes deployment topology. We examine production case studies from the Netflix Titus container orchestration platform and Uber's uMonitor and CauseInfer microservice RCA engines. Empirical evaluations across a 120-service Kubernetes chaos testbed (3,600 pods) under 420 injected fault scenarios demonstrate a Top-1 root-cause localization accuracy (AC@1) of 86.4% and Top-3 accuracy (AC@3) of 95.8%, reducing alert volume by 93.8%, cutting MTTD from 8.40 minutes to 0.42 minutes, and lowering MTTR from 47.50 minutes to 4.15 minutes. papers.summary_zh: 该文提出一套面向 Kubernetes 集群的端到端 AIOps 架构，用于自主检测事故并做因果根因分析，核心方法是将 eBPF 遥测与 OpenTelemetry 数据统一为时空表示，结合变分图自编码器、日志模板提取和因果推断在部署拓扑上定位根因。作者在混沌测试环境及生产案例中评估，报告了较高的根因定位准确率，并称告警量、检测与恢复时间均明显下降。这些结果说明多模态遥测与因果方法结合有助于缓解告警风暴、缩短故障处置时间，但结论主要基于特定测试环境和注入故障场景，实际部署中的泛化性仍需进一步验证。

papers.title: Federated Learning and Differential Privacy in Multi-Hospital Healthcare Cloud Ecosystems
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Training generalizable deep learning models for clinical diagnostics requires diverse, multi-institutional patient cohorts that no single healthcare provider can assemble in isolation. However, centralizing electronic health records (EHR) and high-resolution medical imaging (DICOM) into a single cloud data lake violates strict regulatory mandates including the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), the European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and institutional data sovereignty policies. Federated Learning (FL) resolves this impasse by dispatching model parameters to hospital edge enclaves for local stochastic training and aggregating only ephemeral gradient updates in the cloud. Despite avoiding raw data egress, vanilla federated averaging (FedAvg) remains vulnerable to gradient inversion reconstruction attacks, membership inference disclosures, and severe statistical divergence across heterogeneous clinical scanners and non-identically distributed (non-IID) patient demographics. This paper presents a production-grade multi-hospital federated learning cloud architecture that integrates Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP) with Poisson subsampled Gaussian noise, Bonawitz cryptographic Secure Aggregation (SecAgg) inside Confidential Computing (AMD SEV-SNP) enclaves, and FedProx/SCAFFOLD control-variate drift correction. We analyze real-world clinical deployments anchored by the NVIDIA Clara Federated Learning and MONAI framework during the 20-hospital EXAM clinical radiology consortium led by Mass General Brigham and Mayo Clinic. Empirical evaluations across 16 simulated and clinical hospital enclaves training a 3D DenseNet-121 chest CT triage model demonstrate that combining FedProx (mu = 0.01) with Opacus RDP accounting (epsilon = 2.5, delta = 10^-5) achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.918, outperforming isolated single-hospital models (0.784 AUROC) by 17.1% while suppressing Deep Leakage from Gradients (DLG) reconstruction PSNR below 11.4 dB. Research Domain & Specialization Track Master of Science in Information Technology (MSIT) — Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning and Healthcare Cloud. papers.title: Serverless GPU Orchestration, Snapshot Restore, and Cold-Start Mitigation in Cloud AI
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Elastic artificial intelligence inference services increasingly rely on serverless execution models to eliminate idle accelerator expenditure during diurnal traffic troughs. However, provisioning graphics processing unit (GPU) containers on demand introduces severe cold-start latency penalties ranging from 18.4 to 64.2 seconds due to OCI container image decompression, Python runtime initialization, CUDA context creation, and multi-gigabyte neural network weight deserialization over network-attached storage. This paper presents an integrated serverless GPU orchestration architecture that combines lazy content-addressable chunk streaming, unified host-and-device Checkpoint/Restore In Userspace (CRIU-GPU), and locality-aware NVMe-to-VRAM direct memory access (GPUDirect Storage) to reduce 99th-percentile cold-start latencies to sub-two-second bounds. We formulate the cold-start decomposition as a constrained stochastic dynamic program that balances pre-warmed microVM pool expenditure against tail-latency service-level objective (SLO) violations under non-stationary Hawkes process request arrivals. By decoupling read-only tensor pages from mutable CUDA driver state, our snapshot restoration engine streams pinned host page frames and device memory segments concurrently across PCIe Gen5 x16 interconnects at 54.8 GB/s while bypassing redundant kernel module initialization. We examine production deployments across AWS Lambda SnapStart microVMs, the Modal content-addressable container file system, and RunPod FlashBoot serverless GPU clusters. Empirical benchmarks on 7-billion to 70-billion parameter transformer models demonstrate that combined lazy filesystem tree prefetching and unified CUDA driver checkpointing reduce median container startup latency from 28.60 seconds to 1.42 seconds and P99 cold-start latency from 49.80 seconds to 2.18 seconds. Simultaneously, fleet-wide GPU compute utilization increases from 31.4% under static over-provisioning to 78.6% under predictive snapshot orchestration, reducing monthly accelerator infrastructure cost by 56.3% without violating strict 2.5-second inference startup guarantees. papers.title: Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over Federated Cloud Data Lakes
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Enterprise deployments of large language models require grounding generated answers in authoritative, continuously updated internal repositories while strictly enforcing row- and document-level access control lists (ACLs). Naive Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines that chunk PDF documents into fixed 500-token windows and execute unconstrained approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) vector searches fail in production across three dimensions: they lose cross-section structural context in complex financial and technical tables, they suffer lexical blindness on exact product codes and regulatory statutes, and they leak unauthorized knowledge when ACL filtering is applied post-retrieval. This paper presents a federated Enterprise RAG architecture spanning cloud data lakes (Apache Iceberg on AWS S3, Snowflake, and Google BigQuery). Building on foundational RAG formulations (Lewis et al., 2020), ColBERT late-interaction retrieval (Khattab & Zaharia, 2020), and GraphRAG hierarchical community indexing (Edge et al., 2024), our architecture combines layout-aware semantic chunking, contextual header injection, three-way hybrid retrieval (dense HNSW vectors + BM25s sparse lexical + entity knowledge graph traversal) fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack et al., 2009), cross-encoder reranking, and cryptographic pre-retrieval ACL bitmap filtering. We evaluate the architecture through a production case study modeled on Morgan Stanley Wealth Management knowledge assistants and Ramp automated financial document analysis pipelines over a 14.8-million-document federated corpus. Empirical evaluation demonstrates that hybrid ACL-aware RAG increases Context Recall@10 from 61.2% (dense-only baseline) to 93.4%, raises RAGAS Faithfulness from 0.74 to 0.96, reduces hallucinated ungrounded claims from 14.8% to 1.2%, and enforces zero unauthorized document leakage at a P95 end-to-end retrieval latency of 168 milliseconds. papers.title: FinOps Governance and Carbon-Aware Workload Scheduling for Hyperscale AI Training
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Training and fine-tuning foundation models across hyperscale cloud data centers consumes megawatt-hours of electrical energy and generates millions of dollars in monthly cloud infrastructure bills. Historically, enterprise machine learning orchestration treated cloud resource provisioning and sustainability accounting as post-hoc reporting exercises divorced from real-time cluster scheduling. As a result, delay-tolerant batch training jobs, hyperparameter sweeps, and nightly distillation pipelines routinely execute on expensive on-demand GPU instances during peak regional electricity grid demand powered by fossil-fuel peaker plants. This paper presents a joint FinOps and Carbon-Aware (GreenOps) Kubernetes scheduling architecture for multi-region cloud AI clusters. Integrating real-time marginal operating emissions rates (MOER) from regional power grids (Sukprasert et al., 2024; Wiesner et al., 2021) with dynamic cloud spot-instance interruption hazard models and asynchronous fast-checkpointing (Mohan et al., 2021; Thorpe et al., 2023), the scheduler formulates job placement as a constrained Pareto optimization over monetary cost, carbon emissions, and deadline slack. We validate the architecture through an in-depth production case study combining Microsoft Azure Carbon-Aware Kubernetes scheduling patterns and Spotify Cloud FinOps unit-economics telemetry across three North American and European cloud regions. Over a 90-day evaluation spanning 18,400 GPU-days of PyTorch FSDP and DeepSpeed workloads, our scheduler reduces net cloud GPU expenditure by 46.8% through hazard-aware spot multiplexing, lowers Scope 2 operational carbon emissions by 38.4% via spatiotemporal workload shifting, and maintains a 99.4% training deadline completion rate with less than 2.1% checkpoint recovery overhead. papers.title: Zero-Trust Security Architectures and Confidential Computing for Multi-Tenant Cloud AI
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Multi-tenant cloud artificial intelligence platforms process proprietary model weights, regulated customer prompts, and high-value fine-tuning datasets across shared physical hosts. Traditional perimeter-based cloud security assumes that traffic inside a virtual private cloud (VPC) is trustworthy and that the cloud provider's hypervisor, host operating system kernel, and cluster administrator cannot inspect guest memory. Both assumptions fail under modern threat models involving container escapes, compromised management planes, supply-chain poisoning of model artifacts, and side-channel memory inspection. This paper presents a defense-in-depth Zero-Trust and Confidential Cloud AI architecture that eliminates implicit trust across network, identity, and hardware memory layers. Aligned with NIST Special Publication 800-207 (Rose et al., 2020) and Google BeyondCorp principles (Ward & Beyer, 2014), the proposed architecture combines SPIFFE/SPIRE short-lived X.509 workload identities, eBPF-enforced mutual TLS (mTLS) micro-segmentation, and hardware-rooted Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) spanning AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX host enclaves, and NVIDIA H100 Confidential Computing modes (Dhanuskodi et al., 2023; Kaplan et al., 2020). Cryptographic remote attestation binds key release from cloud key management systems (KMS) directly to verified hardware measurement registers (RTMRs), ensuring that encrypted model weights and tenant datasets are decrypted exclusively inside attested enclave memory. We evaluate the architecture through a production case study modeled on Google BeyondCorp Enterprise and Confidential Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) / Azure Confidential AI deployments serving healthcare and financial workloads. Empirical benchmarks show that enabling full CPU-GPU confidential enclaves with bounce-buffer DMA encryption imposes only a 4.8% to 7.9% throughput overhead on 70B LLM inference while reducing lateral movement blast radius to zero and satisfying HIPAA, PCI-DSS 4.0, and EU sovereign cloud mandates. papers.summary_zh: 该文提出一种面向多租户云 AI 的零信任与机密计算架构，试图在网络、身份和硬件内存层面消除隐式信任，以应对容器逃逸、管理面失陷、模型供应链投毒和侧信道内存窥探等威胁。作者将 SPIFFE/SPIRE 短期工作负载身份、eBPF 强制的 mTLS 微隔离与基于 AMD SEV-SNP、Intel TDX 和 NVIDIA H100 机密计算模式的硬件可信执行环境结合，并通过远程证明把密钥释放绑定到已验证的硬件度量，使模型权重和租户数据仅在经证明的飞地内解密。基于生产部署建模的案例与基准显示，启用完整 CPU-GPU 机密飞地后，70B 大模型推理吞吐开销约为 4.8% 至 7.9%，同时将横向移动的爆炸半径降为零，并满足相关合规要求；这些结果来自作者自述的案例与基准，尚需独立验证。

papers.title: Multi-Region Cloud-Native LLM Inference and Dynamic KV-Cache Routing
papers.authors: Sonu Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Serving large language models (LLMs) across multi-region cloud infrastructure introduces severe memory bandwidth bottlenecks and unpredictable tail latencies. During autoregressive generation, each active request maintains a growing key-value (KV) state tensor in high-bandwidth GPU memory (HBM). When stateless cloud load balancers distribute incoming requests using round-robin or least-connections policies, identical system prompts, multi-turn conversation histories, and shared retrieval contexts are repeatedly recomputed across separate GPU nodes. This paper presents a cloud-native, prefix-aware KV-cache routing and disaggregated inference architecture designed for multi-region Kubernetes clusters. Building on PagedAttention virtual memory management (Kwon et al., 2023), FlashAttention IO-aware kernels (Dao et al., 2022), and disaggregated prefill-decode scheduling (Zhong et al., 2024), the proposed architecture integrates a consistent-hashing radix tree directory at the global edge ingress layer with a three-tier memory hierarchy spanning GPU HBM, host DDR5 DRAM, and NVMe-over-Fabrics (NVMe-oF) flash pools. We evaluate the architecture through a detailed production case study of Anyscale Ray Serve and vLLM deployments operating across three cloud regions, alongside Cloudflare Workers AI edge routing patterns. Across a 72-hour production trace on 64 NVIDIA H100 GPUs serving 70-billion-parameter models, dynamic prefix-tree routing increases global KV-cache hit rates from 6.4% to 82.3%, reduces median time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 67.9% (from 420 ms to 135 ms), cuts 99th-percentile TTFT by 78.3% (from 1,890 ms to 410 ms), and improves sustainable throughput per GPU by 210.7%. Finally, we analyze failure recovery under availability-zone partitions, cross-tenant side-channel risks in shared prefix caches, and FinOps cost per million generated tokens. papers.title: Autonomous Decentralized Optimization of Critical Environmental Infrastructure via Room-Temperature Dissipative Quantum Technologies and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC): Theoretical Foundations and Societal Implementation of the Super RTO Architecture
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Contemporary quantum computing and frontier artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructures spearheaded by hyperscale technology conglomerates face a profound thermodynamic self-contradiction: reliance on extreme cryogenic dilution refrigeration (0.010–0.015 K) entails massive parasitic electrical power consumption, Helium-3 (3He) isotope depletion, and severe occupational and ecological externalities. Attempting to optimize planetary environmental systems using centralized infrastructures that impose unsustainable thermodynamic burdens constitutes an irreconcilable structural paradox. In this monograph, we formulate and formalize Super RTO (Super Real-Time Optimization / RTO P2.0), a comprehensive autonomous decentralized architecture engineered to resolve both the thermodynamic bottleneck of cryogenic quantum hardware and the combinatorial explosion of classical Real-Time Optimization (RTO). The Super RTO stack integrates three foundational layers: (1) a Physical & Device Layer grounded in room-temperature dissipative quantum mechanics—harnessing Environment-Assisted Quantum Transport (ENAQT), Frohlich condensation in Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS), and Lindblad dissipative dark-state engineering across room-temperature topological insulators, diamond Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers, and superradiant Dicke quantum batteries; (2) a Mathematical & Optimization Algorithm Layer combining Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQA), continuous Sobolev space (H^s) weak-form evaluation (eliminating discrete sampling fencepost errors), deterministic verification over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (F_p, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) via QFS-zkVM, and autonomous phase synchronization via the Quantum Kuramoto and van der Pol oscillator models; and (3) a Security & Governance Layer enforcing irreversible edge sensor root proofs via NIST FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) lattice signatures, Zero-Trust Key Management Infrastructure (ZT-KMI, DOJ 728985-XMN), PHOENIX_BRIDGE / PHOENIX_ROUTER deterministic hardware interlocks, and Human-in-Command (HIC) fiduciary governance. Finally, we present a concrete societal implementation model targeting a 100% renewable Distributed Energy Resource (DER) community microgrid in Iwakuni, Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan, demonstrating sub-cycle frequency/voltage stabilization within < 0.01 s, a 25%–38% reduction in transmission Joule heating losses, and cryptographically verifiable peer-to-peer (P2P) electricity settlement as a blueprint for Global Public Infrastructure (GPI). (日本語要旨:現代の巨大IT企業が主導する量子コンピューティングおよび先端AIインフラは、極低温維持(0.010〜0.015 K)に伴う莫大な電力消費という熱力学的自己矛盾に直面している。本論文では、これらの課題を解決する包括的アーキテクチャ「Super RTO(超・リアルタイム最適化 / RTO P2.0)」を提唱する。本アーキテクチャは、常温散逸系量子力学(環境支援型量子輸送ENAQT、非平衡定常状態NESSにおけるフレーリッヒ凝縮、Lindblad暗状態工学、常温トポロジカル絶縁体、ダイヤモンドNVセンター、ディッケ量子電池)に基づくデバイス層、連続ソボレフ空間評価とGoldilocks素体QFS-zkVMおよび量子蔵本モデルを用いた数理アルゴリズム層、ならびにNIST FIPS 204(ML-DSA)源流証明とゼロトラスト鍵管理(ZT-KMI / DOJ 728985-XMN)・Human-in-Command(HIC)によるセキュリティ・ガバナンス層を統合する。第1ターゲットとして山口県岩国市における地域分散型マイクログリッドの社会実装モデルを示し、0.01秒以内の周波数・電圧自律吸収、送電ジュール熱ロス25〜38%削減、および耐量子P2P電力取引を通じた「グローバル公共インフラ(GPI)」としての可能性を論証する。) License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026)

papers.authors: Leon Calvin II long, SquirlOS Technologies LLC

papers.abstract: SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Errors are disclosed, not erased. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All payloads synthetic or owner-generated; no customer-identifiable data appears in this record (POL-DISC-001). "Fractal Tokenization: Atomic Satoshi Ownership and Covenant-Bound Decentralized Identifiers." We define fractal tokenization: the property by which a satoshi — the smallest indivisible unit of the Bitcoin supply — functions as an atomic fraction whose security, scarcity, and keyless provenance are structurally identical to the whole coin. Reduction to practice (FT-1, 2026-10-20): a decentralized identifier whose subject is one specific satoshi. Three fresh wallets (Bitcoin P2TR, XRP, Stellar) act as DID verification methods; a deterministic DID core document is hashed (SHA-256) and committed into the taproot output key (BIP-340/341 taptweak) of a 330-sat output whose ordinal position-0 sat is the claimed fraction; the binding is attested cross-rail on XRP (validated ledger 107789535) and Stellar (ledger 65047374) via a 37-byte protocol envelope with new version byte 0x0A (DID carrier), byte-exact, 6.1 seconds, ~$0.00003. Covenant transaction dd51a79794dbb7a8914911401caee9b30e472017727b788c770a577188513b02 confirmed in Bitcoin block 972367; DID identifier did:sqdr:ea942df94668c93955fb8792c029a4aa82f6d179 (keyless: SHA256(outpoint||P_c)[:40]). Whole ceremony cost: 1,000 sats + 100 stroops + 10 drops, under $0.84. The epoch corpus covenant sat (root 267f13b0..., ledger 0267) was untouched. Scope and honesty: prior art disclosed — did:btcr and other Bitcoin-anchored DID methods (2019+) and Ordinals position theory exist. NOT claimed: first DID on Bitcoin, first DID method, first taproot DID. Claimed (scoped): the fractal atomic-ownership doctrine, the covenant-tweaked DID core, and dual-rail carrier attestation as a single deterministic, receipts-first ceremony. One build defect (sighash nVersion parameter) was rejected by the mempool, fixed, and disclosed pre-confirmation. papers.title: KHI TẤM BẰNG KHÔNG CÒN LÀ LỜI HỨA
papers.authors: Quang Trịnh Bùi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: WHEN A DEGREE IS NO LONGER A PROMISE A Conditional Foresight Essay on Education, Employment, and Human Life-Cycle Transition Infrastructure Author: Bùi Quang TrịnhIndependent Researcher, VietnamFounder, Boundary Information Theory (BIT) Abstract This conditional foresight essay explores possible transformations in education, employment, professional identity, and social institutions as artificial intelligence, automation, and rapidly changing economic structures reshape the relationship between human knowledge and work. Developed within the Boundary Information Theory (BIT) research programme, the essay asks whether future civilization will be able to maintain meaningful transitions between learning, professional contribution, personal development, and a dignified human life. The essay presents nine conditional future perspectives. First, academic degrees may increasingly function as evidence of educational achievement rather than implicit guarantees of specific professional positions. Second, automation and artificial intelligence may reduce certain entry-level tasks, potentially weakening traditional pathways through which younger generations acquire professional experience. Third, institutions may develop transferable capability profiles that recognize practical skills, interdisciplinary competence, and demonstrated problem-solving ability beyond conventional occupational titles. Fourth, universities may expand their responsibilities by supporting graduates through longer professional transitions rather than ending institutional support at graduation. Fifth, countries may begin treating unused human expertise as a potential public resource, creating mechanisms to connect available capabilities with unmet social needs. Sixth, careers may increasingly involve multiple transitions among employment, education, independent work, care responsibilities, and periods of recovery. Seventh, artificial intelligence may improve labor-market matching while simultaneously creating new risks of algorithmic exclusion, opacity, and unfair screening. Eighth, future institutions may recognize periods of unemployment, retraining, caregiving, and independent research as legitimate phases of human development rather than treating them as personal deficiencies. Ninth, the evaluation of education and employment policies may shift toward their long-term effects on the complete human life cycle, including health, family formation, professional resilience, social participation, and security in later life. Central Proposition The future value of education may depend not only on academic credentials, but also on whether civilization develops effective bridges between human learning, meaningful contribution, and dignified life transitions. The essay suggests that education, employers, governments, and technological systems may need to share responsibility for maintaining these pathways. Scope and Limitations This publication is a conditional foresight essay, not a probabilistic forecast or an empirically established prediction. It does not claim that academic degrees will necessarily lose their value, that artificial intelligence will inevitably eliminate entry-level employment, or that one institutional model will suit every society. The possibilities discussed may emerge differently across countries, economic sectors, and social groups. The purpose is to contribute to public reflection and interdisciplinary research on education, artificial intelligence, employment transitions, institutional design, and human-centered civilization. Research programme: Boundary Information Theory (BIT)Document ID: BIT-GLS-HUMAN-LIFECYCLE-WORK-001 — A4Document type: Public Conditional Foresight EssayDocument date: 20 October 2026Language: Vietnamese

papers.title: KHI MỘT NỀN VĂN MINH KHÔNG CÒN BIẾT ĐẶT CON NGƯỜI VÀO ĐÂU
papers.authors: Quang Trịnh Bùi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: WHEN A CIVILIZATION NO LONGER KNOWS WHERE TO PLACE ITS PEOPLE A BIT Essay on Education, Work, Human Value, and the Finite Human Life Cycle Author: Bùi Quang TrịnhIndependent Researcher, VietnamFounder, Boundary Information Theory (BIT) Abstract This interdisciplinary social and philosophical essay examines a growing concern in modern civilization: the potential disconnection between human educational achievement, accumulated capabilities, labor-market structures, and meaningful participation in society. Developed within the Boundary Information Theory (BIT) research programme, the essay begins with a reported case of a highly educated individual experiencing prolonged difficulty entering stable employment. Rather than interpreting an individual case as evidence of universal labor-market failure, the essay investigates the structural interfaces between education, professional training, recruitment, technological change, and the finite human life cycle. A central argument is that education, businesses, technological systems, and public institutions often operate on different timescales. Education may require many years. Recruitment decisions may be made within months. Technologies can transform occupations rapidly, while human lives continue through irreversible biological and social stages. When these systems become misaligned, the costs of institutional mismatch may be transferred disproportionately to individuals. The essay introduces a BIT interpretation of historical outcomes (Quả lịch sử), emphasizing that a person's abilities and achievements represent accumulated life histories rather than isolated qualifications or current employment status. It discusses the compression of human capabilities into résumés, the disappearance of entry-level opportunities, unused professional knowledge, and the potential loss of social participation when qualified individuals cannot find meaningful opportunities to contribute. The essay proposes examining the transition between education and employment as an important form of social infrastructure. Possible responses include professional transition pathways, mentorship, supervised work opportunities, recognition of transferable capabilities, and institutions capable of connecting human knowledge with real societal needs. Central Proposition A civilization should not be evaluated only by how many people it educates, but also by its ability to transform their accumulated knowledge and capabilities into meaningful participation in collective life. Scope and Limitations This publication is a social and philosophical thought essay, not an empirical demonstration that higher education has lost its value or that artificial intelligence is the cause of unemployment. It does not treat a single reported employment case as representative of the entire labor market. Its purpose is to encourage interdisciplinary discussion about education, employment, human dignity, institutional responsibility, and the preservation of human potential throughout finite life cycles. The original Vietnamese essay references reporting from The Wall Street Journal and materials from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, and the National Science Foundation's National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics. Research programme: Boundary Information Theory (BIT)Document ID: BIT-GLS-HUMAN-LIFECYCLE-WORK-001 — A3Document type: Public Thought EssayDocument date: 20 October 2026Language: Vietnamese
