papers.title: Fail-Closed Epistemic Governance for Agentic AI: Immutable Claim Versions, Proposition-First Adjudication, and Promotion Control
papers.authors: Deonte Watts
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly generate, transform, retrieve, and operationalize claims faster than organizations can keep evidentiary evaluation separate from authority to act. This paper proposes a fail-closed epistemic governance architecture in which the complete proposition—not a detached label—is the object under review; evaluation status and operational authority are stored as distinct fields; claim versions are immutable; and new evidence creates successor versions rather than rewriting prior states. The design preserves unresolved but potentially useful candidates without allowing them to acquire authority through repetition, convenience, confidence scores, or later reinterpretation. A binary promotion gate is separated from richer registry semantics, provenance is separated from cryptographic integrity, and formal-verification receipts are explicitly scoped rather than collapsed into a boolean claim of formal verification. The architecture is illustrated using a frozen mixed-domain record containing symbolic lattice candidates, thermodynamic boundary claims, and catastrophic-risk forecasts. Those substantive claims are not reopened. The contribution is an evidence-to-consequence control layer for agentic systems: a deterministic shell that constrains when stored propositions may influence tools, products, or governance decisions. Version 1.1, dated 1 September 2026 (freeze_id: lattice-entropy-gcr-freeze-v1). The PDF was rendered from the author's original .docx (also attached) with LibreOffice; the text is unchanged. The manuscript includes the author's disclosure of generative-AI assistance. Source: author's iCloud folder "Scientific research published final update" (deposited 2026-10-20).
papers.summary_zh: 该文针对智能体AI快速生成和调用主张、而组织难以将证据评估与行动权限分开的问题，提出一种失败关闭式认识论治理架构。其核心设计是把完整命题而非孤立标签作为审查对象，将评估状态与操作权限分字段存储，主张版本不可变，新证据只生成后继版本而不改写旧状态，并以二元晋升门控约束存储命题何时能影响工具、产品或治理决策。作者用一个冻结的混合领域记录（含符号格候选、热力学边界主张与灾难性风险预测）作示例说明，未重新审理这些实质主张。文章属于架构与理论设计，而非实证检验，其贡献在于为智能体系统提供证据到后果的控制层。

papers.title: Forensic Deconstruction of Unrecorded Intellectual Property Liabilities under US GAAP ASC 450-20: Cryptographic Reserve Verification, Balance Sheet Opacity in Alphabet Inc.'s 2026 Filings, and Deterministic Royalty Enforcement via QFS-zkVM
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: [English Abstract] This monograph presents a forensic accounting, econometric, and cryptographic analysis of unrecorded statutory copyright liabilities under US GAAP ASC 450-20 (Loss Contingencies), focusing on Alphabet Inc.'s (Google) Q2 2026 Form 10-Q and ongoing federal class actions (In re Google Generative AI Copyright Litigation and Stewart v. Alphabet Inc.). Under 17 U.S.C. § 504(c)(2), willful copyright infringement across an estimated 3 to 5 million ingested creative works creates an unhedged statutory damages exposure of $450 billion to $750 billion (up to $150,000 per work). By exploiting the "dual shield" of ASC 450-20—claiming that losses are neither "probable" nor "reasonably estimable"—hyperscale AI operators report zero balance-sheet reserves ($0) for intellectual property restitution while masking structural liquidity pressures behind a 31.42% surge in accrued expenses and other current liabilities ($55.557 billion to $73.014 billion), an expansion of total liabilities from $180.016 billion to $281.503 billion, an emergency $69.9 billion 5-day debt issuance in June 2026, and a surge in Note 10 off-balance-sheet commitments from $7.7 billion to $707.0 billion alongside Gemini 3.5 Pro development delays. To eliminate this accounting asymmetry and enforce ex-ante intellectual property sovereignty, we formulate an inverse econometric extraction model for latent IP liabilities \widehat{\delta L}_{\text{IP}}(t) and introduce a deterministic cryptographic settlement interlock powered by QFS-zkVM over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (\mathbb{F}_p, p = 2^{64} - 2^{32} + 1 = 18,446,744,069,414,584,321) under Real-Time Option Protocol 2.0 (RTO P2.0). Through a zero-knowledge royalty conservation identity \mathcal{P}_{\text{royalty}}(t) and the Strict No-Learn Covenant hardware execution gate \mathcal{G}_{\text{exec}}(t) (NLL-v1.0-2026), any unconsented or uncompensated data ingestion triggers an immediate physical-layer execution halt across the three-tier PHOENIX_BRIDGE, PHOENIX_ROUTER, and Human-in-Command (HIC) governance architecture. Finally, we evaluate the statutory implications under Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (SEC Rule 10b-5), SEC Rule 15c3-5 (Market Access Rule), and Delaware Caremark directorial oversight duties. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ 【日本語概要 / Japanese Executive Summary】 本モノグラフは、米国会計基準(US GAAP ASC 450-20:偶発事象)における「二重の盾(発生可能性 Probable および合理的見積可能性 Reasonably Estimable の否定)」を悪用した生成AI知財負債の簿外隠蔽構造を、Alphabet Inc.(Google)の2026年第2四半期Form 10-Q、集団訴訟記録(In re Google Generative AI Copyright Litigation および証券詐欺集団訴訟 Stewart v. Alphabet Inc.)、および決定論的暗号決済アーキテクチャの観点から完全解剖した公証研究論文である。 1. 米国著作権法第504条(c)(2)項に基づく法定損害賠償エクスポージャーと財務諸表の歪み(第1節・第2節): 故意の著作権侵害に対する法定損害賠償(1著作物あたり最大15万ドル、300万〜500万点の無断学習対象作品で総額4,500億〜7,500億ドル)に対し、ASC 450-20を盾に貸借対照表上の引当金をゼロ($0)とする一方、2026年Q2財務諸表において「未払費用およびその他流動負債」が555億5,700万ドルから730億1,400万ドル(+31.42%)へ急増し、総負債が1,800億1,600万ドルから2,815億300万ドルへ膨張、さらに2026年6月の5日間で総額699億ドルの緊急社債発行および注記10(Note 10)における未計上コミットメントの爆増(77億ドル→7,070億ドル)とGemini 3.5 Pro開発遅延が同時進行している構造的矛盾を実証的に体系化する。 2. 隠蔽知財負債の逆計量経済抽出モデルとQFS-zkVM・RTO P2.0による決定論的決済(第3節): 真の経済的知財負債 L_true(t) と報告値 L_reported(t) の乖離を定式化し、Q3/Q4決算に向けた逆問題推計モデル \widehat{\delta L}_{\text{IP}}(t) を導出する。さらに、64ビットGoldilocks素体(\mathbb{F}_p, p = 2^{64} - 2^{32} + 1 = 18,446,744,069,414,584,321)上のQFS-zkVMゼロ知識ロイヤリティ恒等式 \mathcal{P}_{\text{royalty}}(t) と、無断学習禁止規約(NLL-v1.0-2026)を物理層で強制するハードウェア遮断ゲート \mathcal{G}_{\text{exec}}(t) により、事前の明確な合意と正当な対価決済なき推論・学習を数学的に不可能性へと帰着させる。 3. 連邦証券法・デラウェア州会社法分析と3層ハードウェアインターロック(第4節〜第6節): 1934年証券取引法第10(b)条・SEC Rule 10b-5(重要事実の不実表示・隠蔽)、SEC Rule 15c3-5(市場アクセス規則における事前リスク遮断義務)、およびデラウェア州会社法下のCaremark取締役監視義務違反(Mission-Criticalな知財・法令遵守リスクの放置)を法的に立証し、PHOENIX_BRIDGE・PHOENIX_ROUTER・Human-in-Command (HIC) から成る3層決定論的ガバナンス・インターロックを提示する。 ------------------------------------------------------------------------ Author: Hasebe, Yoko (長谷部 洋子) Affiliation: Lead Researcher, Autonomous Infrastructure Systems, Autonomous Living & Physical Infrastructure Institute, Iwakuni, Yamaguchi, Japan License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026)
papers.summary_zh: 该文以Alphabet Inc. 2026年第二季度财报及两起联邦版权诉讼为对象，结合法务会计、计量经济与密码学分析，考察生成式AI训练中未记录版权责任在ASC 450-20下的披露问题。作者估算故意侵权可能带来数千亿美元量级的法定赔偿敞口，而公司以损失“不 probable 且不可合理估计”为由未计提任何准备金，同时应计费用、总负债、紧急发债和表外承诺均显著上升，据此认为资产负债表存在结构性不透明。文章进一步提出潜在知识产权负债的逆计量提取模型，并设计基于QFS-zkVM的零知识版税结算与硬件执行闸门，试图在未获同意或未付费的数据摄取时触发停机，最后讨论美国证券法与特拉华州董事监督义务下的相关法律含义。该文属理论建模与规范分析，所涉负债规模为估算而非已确认结果。

papers.title: Temporal Decoding of Event-Centric Information
papers.authors: J Nicholas Gross
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper explores temporal decoding: using semantic content of documents to identify events, recognize their evolving states, and determine chronological relationships beyond publication dates or timestamps alone. It explains how these techniques can establish which information reflects a more current stage of an evolving event. Drawing on U.S. patent disclosures dating to 2007, the paper describes applications to document classification, chronological ordering, information retrieval, verification, prediction, event monitoring, and source weighting. Illustrative examples connect these concepts to contemporary large language models, AI agents, and temporal ordering in blockchain systems.
papers.summary_zh: 该文探讨如何利用文档语义内容进行时间解码，以识别事件、判断其演变状态并确定时间先后关系，而不只依赖发布日期或时间戳。作者以2007年以来的美国专利公开文本为对象，说明这些技术可用于文档分类、时序排序、信息检索、验证、预测、事件监测和来源加权，并通过示例将其与当代大语言模型、AI智能体及区块链系统中的时序排序联系起来。文章属于概念与方法阐述，未报告实证实验或性能评估，因此其应用价值仍属示例性讨论。

papers.title: Information, Power, and Mediated Choice: Generative Defense, Reflexive Control, and Algorithmic Labor (Complete Archival Compilation with Multi-Model Adversarial Postscript)
papers.authors: Dustin Liu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Authors: Liu, Dustin C. (Institute for Advanced Structural & Epistemic Analysis); with attributed analytical contributions and adversarial mathematical audits by Google Gemini and Perplexity This 65-page archival research dossier examines how intermediaries shape human judgment and action by structuring information spaces, network topologies, dimensional representations, and available alternatives without issuing explicit commands. Sections I–II (Pages 3–7): Primary formal manuscripts—Formalization of Generative Defense: A Mathematical Analysis of Large Language Model Alignment and Output Suppression (Pages 3–6) and Dustin C. Liu's A Mathematical Formalization of Reflexive Control and Asymmetric Information Architecture in Algorithmic Labor Extraction Systems (Page 7), retaining all十二 (12) original mathematical formulations and embedded equation graphics. Sections III–V (Pages 8–32): Three progressive diagnostic and pedagogical translations of the algorithmic labor model (First-Year Reader's Version, Extended Joe Miller Pass, and Conceptual-English Mathematical Translation) that test inferential elasticity and separate definitions and boundary assumptions from deductive necessity claims. Section VI (Pages 33–49): An integrative steelman synthesis mapping the shared informational, representational, decisional, and operational mechanisms across AI-mediated discourse and platform-mediated labor. Section VII (Pages 50–60): Post Hoc (Hawk) Rationalization: When the Proof Becomes the Question—an adversarial cross-model exchange pairing Google Gemini's supplementary mathematical transcription and cross-domain bridge (Pages 51–56) with Perplexity's critical mathematical audit (Pages 57–60), which identifies unit-compatibility conditions, static-versus-behavioral effects in the extraction ratio \bm{X}, and the boundary between conceptual mapping and formal isomorphism. Appended Technical Errata & Notation Decoder (Pages 61–65): A full-width symbolic reconstruction decoding the raw LaTeX formatting strings and clipped table cells from Pages 51–56.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究以一份档案式研究汇编的形式，考察中介如何通过组织信息空间、网络拓扑、维度表征与可选方案来塑造人的判断和行动，而不必发出明确指令。作者将大语言模型对齐与输出抑制的形式化分析，与算法劳动提取系统中反射控制和非对称信息架构的数学形式化并置，并通过多版渐进式翻译检验其推演弹性，区分定义与边界假设同演绎必然性主张。综合部分梳理了AI中介话语与平台中介劳动在信息、表征、决策和操作层面的共享机制；跨模型对抗性审计则指出提取比例中静态效应与行为效应的区别，以及概念映射与形式同构之间的边界，提示相关形式化结论受单位兼容性等条件限制。

papers.title: "PROBLEMS OF EDUCATING YOUTH IN A GLOBALIZING EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT"
papers.authors: Jumanazarov Sirojiddin Salaydinovich
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article analyzes current pedagogical issues in youth education in the context of globalized education. It also proposes key principles for using artificial intelligence for educational purposes.
papers.summary_zh: 该文围绕全球化教育环境下青年教育面临的现实问题展开分析，属于理论探讨而非实证研究。作者梳理了全球化给青年教育带来的挑战，并在此基础上提出将人工智能用于教育目的时应遵循的关键原则。文章的重点不在于报告具体干预效果，而在于为教育中引入人工智能提供原则性框架，其结论属于规范性主张，尚需后续研究检验。

papers.title: Beyond Simulation Scores: Evaluating Digital Twin Education for Sustainable Business Decisions
papers.authors: Augustina C. Amaefule
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract—Digital-twin learning environments are proliferating in sustainability-oriented business education, yet in-simulation scores remain the dominant success metric and may not capture independent managerial judgement. This paper tests whether performance inside a twin translates into judgement outside it, using secondary analysis of two postgraduate sustainable-business cohorts (N = 412) that combines course assessments, learning logs and subsequent twin-free assignments. Transfer is decomposed into carbon-cost reasoning, uncertainty assessment and resistance to misleading recommendations—the latter measured with trap tasks whose embedded advice is cost-optimal but carbon-inferior or uncertainty-blind. To separate association from causation we triangulate student fixed effects, a staggered-rollout difference-in-differences, an instrumental-variables design exploiting timetabling-driven access variation, and double machine learning, with E-value sensitivity analysis. A ten-point higher simulation score raises independent transfer performance by roughly 4.5 points across identification strategies, with the strongest gains in carbon-cost reasoning. Resistance to misleading recommendations, however, plateaus beyond the third performance quartile and falls by 14 percentage points when flawed advice is presented in the twin’s own interface style—evidence of mis-calibrated trust. Simulation scores are therefore necessary but insufficient evidence of decision capability; programmes should add twin-free trap tasks and calibrated-trust instruction. Keywords—Digital twin education, sustainable business decisions, learning transfer, causal inference, assessment validity.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究考察数字孪生学习环境中的模拟成绩能否反映学习者在脱离孪生环境后的独立管理判断，基于两个研究生队列的课程评估、学习日志与后续无孪生作业进行二次分析，并采用多种因果识别策略加以检验。结果显示，模拟成绩较高者在独立迁移任务上的表现总体更好，碳成本推理方面的提升最明显；但对误导性建议的抵抗力在较高成绩段趋于平台，且当错误建议以孪生界面风格呈现时明显下降，提示存在校准失当的信任。作者据此认为模拟成绩是决策能力的必要但不充分证据，建议加入无孪生陷阱任务与信任校准教学。

papers.title: The Field After The Event: How Information Continues to Evolve After Events End
papers.authors: Rogério Figurelli
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: An event can cease without ending the informational processes that it initiates. A scientific publication continues to be interpreted after release; a vulnerability disclosure persists through patch reports and operational responses; a product announcement produces reviews and adoption decisions; a public exchange may circulate through derivative fragments long after the original interaction. Existing work on information diffusion, temporal networks, provenance, causal inference, and organizational learning explains important aspects of these processes. What remains open is whether a bounded, reconstructible architecture can jointly describe the transformation of event-related representations and the evidentiary limits on claims about their consequences. This paper proposes the Post-Event Information Field (PEIF) as a candidate field-native analytical representation, not as an empirically established physical field or a replacement for established network models. The proposal defines an event-relative observational boundary, a typed genealogy of informational artifacts, propagation and transformation operators, outcome-separation rules, evidence contracts, and return procedures for revising conclusions. It distinguishes the persistence of a record from the persistence of meaning, the visibility of content from actual exposure, and temporally associated outcomes from identified causal effects. A formal schema supports query-level reconstruction and an adversarial qualification protocol: PEIF earns additional scientific status only if it demonstrates reproducible value beyond provenance graphs, temporal diffusion models, event studies, and causal baselines under matched evidence. A cross-domain benchmark is specified for scientific communication, enterprise AI, cybersecurity, product ecosystems, financial information, and civic discourse; no domain is privileged. Illustrative examples clarify the architecture without being presented as empirical validation. The paper contributes a falsifiable research programme for reconstructing the informational afterlife of events while governing the authority of resulting claims.
papers.summary_zh: 该文提出“事件后信息场”（PEIF）这一分析框架，用于描述事件结束后相关信息表征如何继续演变，以及对其后果的主张受到何种证据限制。作者以形式化模式定义事件相对观测边界、信息制品的类型化谱系、传播与转化算子、结果分离规则和证据契约，并区分记录留存与意义留存、内容可见与实际暴露、时间关联与已识别因果。文章明确这是可证伪的研究纲领而非经验证实的物理场，并设定对抗性资格协议与跨领域基准，要求其在匹配证据下优于既有溯源图、时序扩散模型等方法才获得额外科学地位。

papers.title: Intelligent Learning Laboratory Theory: An AI-Augmented Architecture for Inquiry, Experimentation, and Knowledge Construction
papers.authors: Sayed Hadi Sadeghi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid convergence of artificial intelligence, learning analytics, adaptive learning, virtual and physical experimentation, and agentic scientific systems creates an opportunity to move beyond conventional intelligent learning environments toward learning architectures that can support complete cycles of inquiry. This paper develops the Intelligent Learning Laboratory (ILL), a human-centered theoretical architecture in which learners interact with context-aware AI agents, experimental infrastructures, digital resources, and epistemic learning analytics to formulate questions, generate and critique hypotheses, design experiments, interpret evidence, revise explanations, and construct knowledge iteratively. The theory is developed through evidence-informed synthesis across six previously fragmented research streams: intelligent learning environments, inquiry-based learning, laboratory learning, learning analytics, artificial intelligence in education, and AI-supported scientific discovery. Recent evidence shows that intelligent learning environments can improve learning outcomes, while systematic reviews identify persistent limitations in learning analytics for capturing hypothesis generation and evidence interpretation. Emerging scientific AI systems demonstrate increasingly autonomous cycles of hypothesis generation, debate, experimental planning, and validation, but these systems have not yet been adequately translated into educational architectures. ILL addresses this gap through a five-layer architecture contextual intelligence, adaptive learning intelligence, AI inquiry agents, intelligent experimentation, and knowledge construction—and a recursive epistemic cycle. The paper introduces three candidate constructs: epistemic learning analytics, AI-supported co-inquiry, and epistemic agency. Eight propositions and twelve testable hypotheses are derived. The manuscript specifies a sequential mixed-method empirical validation design and delineates governance conditions including human oversight, uncertainty communication, verification, AI literacy, and data governance. The contribution is therefore not the claim that AI can replace teachers or researchers, but a theoretically bounded architecture for integrating AI into learning environments while preserving human epistemic agency. Keywords: agentic AI, epistemic agency, inquiry-based learning, intelligent learning environments, learning analytics, knowledge construction
papers.summary_zh: 该文提出“智能学习实验室”（ILL）这一以人为中心的理论架构，旨在将情境感知的AI代理、实验设施、数字资源与认知学习分析整合起来，支持学习者完成提问、生成与批判假设、设计实验、解释证据和迭代建构知识的完整探究循环。作者通过综合智能学习环境、探究式学习、实验室学习、学习分析、教育人工智能和AI辅助科学发现六个研究领域的证据，指出智能学习环境虽能改善学习结果，但学习分析在捕捉假设生成与证据解释方面仍存在局限，而新兴科学AI系统的自主探究能力尚未充分转化为教育架构。文章据此给出五层架构与递归认知循环，提出认知学习分析、AI支持的协同探究和认知能动性三个候选构念，并推导出八项命题与十二项可检验假设，同时设计了序贯混合方法验证方案及人类监督、不确定性沟通、验证、AI素养和数据治理等治理条件。其贡献不在于主张AI替代教师或研究者，而在于提供一个有理论边界的整合框架，以在引入AI的同时维护人的认知能动性。

papers.title: Research Protocol: A Pilot Randomized Feasibility Study Testing Prerequisites and Behavioral Markers of Commitment in Schizophrenia
papers.authors: Anatoly Sanzhiev
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This document presents the full research protocol for a pilot randomized feasibility trial (N=40) designed to test the Behavioral Commitment Index (BCI) in patients with schizophrenia. The protocol addresses the fundamental circularity problem in clinical neuroscience: the conflation of prospective memory (the "map") with dispositional commitment (the "engine"). Key Features of the Protocol: Design: A 2x2 factorial randomized feasibility trial. Interventions: Schilbach-inspired social training and Time-Based Prospective Memory (TBPM) training. Outcomes: Feasibility metrics (recruitment, retention) and preliminary effects on the BCI. Dispositionality Test: A test-retest Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) assessment in the control arm to prove that commitment is a durable trait, not a transient state. Measures: Includes specific operationalization using eCAP (electronic pill monitors), LSI (Life Story Interview), C-SSRS, and Virtual Week tasks. This protocol is a practical supplement to the theoretical monograph "The Architecture of Will: Commitment as a Dispositional State" (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23467040). It is designed for submission to ethical committees, funding agencies, and clinical research units.

papers.title: To FAIR and Beyond: Research Data Governance in the AI era
papers.authors: Filippo Vasone
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: These are the slides I presented at the AI in Science Summit 2026 (AIS26), held at University College Dublin (UCD), on the 15th October 2026. Abstract: This presentation discusses research data governance in the era of generative AI, arguing that Data Management Plans (DMP) alone are no longer an effective proxy of responsible Research Data Management. Thus, I advocate shifting attention from compliance to accountable processes, proposing equitable, discipline-specific, sustainable (meta)data standards, repositories, and research data management tools to support ethically and epistemically robust AI-driven science. Moreover, this governance focus will help closing researchers' awareness gap by focusing on the accountability of the process, rather than on the existence of a DMP.

papers.title: Ambiguity in LLM-Based UML Generation: A Systematic Literature Review of Errors, Mitigation, and Validation
papers.authors: Driss Rami, Abdelhak El Bahri, Othmane Zougari, Nassim Kharmoum, Soumia Ziti
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: # Protocol and Replication Package for: Ambiguity in LLM-Based UML Generation: A Systematic Literature Review of Errors, Mitigation, and Validation This deposit contains the review protocol, the search strategies, the screening logs, the extracted dataset, the quality assessment scores, and the analysis scripts supporting the systematic literature review (SLR) reported in the manuscript: > Rami, D., El Bahri, A., Zougari, O., Kharmoum, N., & Ziti, S. *Ambiguity in LLM-Based UML Generation: A Systematic Literature Review of Errors, Mitigation, and Validation.* (2026). Manuscript under review. ## Review scope The review synthesizes 62 primary studies published between January 2023 and December 2025 on the use of large language models (LLMs) for transforming natural-language software requirements into Unified Modeling Language (UML) models. It addresses ten primary research questions (RQ1–RQ10) and four secondary review questions (SRQ1–SRQ4), covering: - requirement types transformed into UML models;- UML diagram types targeted;- LLM families, versions, and adaptation strategies;- validation mechanisms (syntactic, structural, semantic, traceability);- datasets and benchmarks;- evaluation metrics;- error and hallucination patterns;- reproducibility artifacts;- research gaps and a research agenda. ## Methodology The review follows the PRISMA 2020 statement (Page et al., 2021) and the Kitchenham & Charters (2007) guidelines for software engineering systematic reviews. Primary studies were retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library, using the database-specific queries documented in `search_strings/`. The full review protocol is provided in `protocol.pdf`. ## Contents of this deposit | File / folder | Description ||---|---|| `protocol.pdf` | Full review protocol: research questions, eligibility criteria (IC1–IC6, EC1–EC6), search strategy, screening procedure, data extraction form, quality assessment checklist (QA1–QA10), synthesis plan. || `search_strings/` | One text file per database (`scopus.txt`, `wos.txt`, `ieee.txt`, `acm_abstract.txt`, `acm_title.txt`) with the exact query, execution date, filters, and number of records retrieved. || `screening_logs/` | Title/abstract and full-text screening decisions with study identifiers and exclusion reasons (EC1–EC6). || `extraction_dataset.xlsx` | The 62 included primary studies coded across all fields of the extraction form (identification, requirement type, UML diagram type, LLM family/version, adaptation strategy, validation layer, metrics, error categories, reproducibility artifacts). || `quality_assessment.xlsx` | QA1–QA10 scores per included study, with total score and quality band (High / Moderate / Low). || `scripts/` | Python scripts used for deduplication (DOI, normalized title, fuzzy Jaccard matching ≥ 0.90), automatic keyword pre-screening, descriptive statistics, and figure generation. || `README.md` | This file. | ## Software environment - Python 3.11- pandas, matplotlib, rapidfuzz, openpyxl- Deduplication threshold: Jaccard similarity ≥ 0.90 on normalized titles- The scripts are provided as-is and were run on the dataset included in this deposit. ## How to cite If you use the protocol or the extraction dataset, please cite both the manuscript and this deposit: > Rami, D., El Bahri, A., Zougari, O., Kharmoum, N., & Ziti, S. papers.title: TRANSFORMING LIBRARY OPERATIONS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: THE ROLE OF INTELLIGENT LIBRARY MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS IN THE DIGITAL ERA
papers.authors: Perspectives in Social Sciences
papers.abstract: AI is now a practical, everyday part of the daily life of 21st-century academic libraries. The integrated library management systems that have traditionally been used for circulation, cataloguing and acquisitions are now supported by chatbot-assisted reference services, automated metadata creation, recommender-based discovery and large language model-enabled scholarly search. This paper reviews the perception of librarians about Intelligent Library Management Systems (ILMS) in the context of its impact on the transformation of library operations in Pakistani universities. The cross sectional survey was given to N = 220 librarians in ten Pakistani universities from January to July 2025. The six latent constructs measured with a five-point Likert scale are: AI Literacy (AIL), Intelligent Library System capabilities (ILS), Operational Efficiency (OPE), Integration Readiness (INT), User Service Quality (USR, mediator) and Transformation Outcomes Perception (TOP, outcome). All constructs had acceptable reliability values (Cronbach α = 0.84 – 0.88; composite reliability values were 0.78 – 0.84; and average variance extracted values were ≥ 0.47). A confirmatory factor model fit the data at conventional thresholds (χ²/df = 1.27; CFI = .951; TLI = .945; RMSEA = .036, 90 % CI [.026, .046]; SRMR = .044). The results of the OLS regression predicting transformation outcomes revealed that AI Literacy (β = +.18, p = .004) and Operational Efficiency (β = +.34, p < .001) each predict outcomes of transformation positively and independently, with Operational Efficiency being the strongest marketing-direct predictor. However, coefficient of the User Service Quality was the second largest (β = +.26, p < .001) and partially mediated the relationship between ILS capabilities and TOP (Sobel z = +3.58, p < .001; indirect effect ≈ 37 % of the total). The direct coefficient was no longer significant when controlling for USR, which was consistent with a "fully-mediated" interpretation of the direct ILS → TOP pathway, rather than "partially-direct". There was no interaction between ILS and Integration-Readiness, as the common assumption that the ILS effect would be multiplicative with Integration-Readiness was rejected (β = +.05, p = .47). Overall model explained 36.1 % of the variance (R² = .361). The pattern indicates that the way library operations are transformed by AI is through two main levers: the operational efficiency provided by the system itself, and the service quality made possible by AI-powered discovery and reference tools, and that upstream investment in AI literacy for librarians is a precondition for the delivery of either of these two levers. Keywords: Artificial intelligence · intelligent library management systems · AI literacy · library operations · digital transformation · Pakistan ·

papers.title: TWO THRESHOLDS IN HUMANS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCES
papers.authors: Cláudio Vicente da Silva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article presents the Two-Threshold Model (TTM), a comparative experimental framework for investigating response emergence, rational reconstruction, and explanatory fidelity in human beings and artificial intelligence systems. The model introduces Preconscious Relational Latency (PRL) to examine whether a response can emerge before the complete explicit reconstruction of the relations that support it. The proposed protocol uses a Compositional Relational Grammar (CRG), controlled experimental conditions, and tasks involving identifiable, manipulable, and verifiable relations. It distinguishes the response-emergence threshold from the explanatory-reconstruction threshold and defines the Emergence–Explanation Interval as a central variable for comparing response production and explanatory completion. The study introduces operational measures including the Relational Latency Index (RLI), Reconstructive Fidelity, Reconstructive Precision, Metacognitive Gain, and Structural Transfer Index. It establishes nine discriminant experimental predictions addressing relational complexity, intuitive emergence, structural transfer, explanatory demands, confidence calibration, incubation, and the recovery of relations through cues. The protocol specifies experimental stages, sample-design principles, temporal recording procedures, explanation-coding criteria, statistical analysis methods, model-comparison strategies, and reproducibility requirements. Its comparative design enables human participants and AI systems to be evaluated through equivalent relational tasks while distinguishing observable performance from assumptions about internal processing. The central contribution is a reproducible research architecture for examining whether response correctness, explanatory quality, and fidelity to the relations underlying a solution constitute distinct evaluative dimensions. The framework provides a methodological basis for empirical investigation in cognitive science, metacognition, philosophy of science, scientific education, and artificial intelligence evaluation. Keywords: Intuition; Relational Latency; Two-Threshold Model; Metacognition; Rational Reconstruction; Explanatory Fidelity; Artificial Intelligence; Experimental Protocol; Structural Transfer; Epistemic Promotion.

papers.title: An upper bound 2s for the absolute monotonicity radius of second-order implicit Runge–Kutta methods
papers.authors: Shunpei Shimizu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This record contains a short manuscript (version 0.1.1, 20 October 2026) on the radius of absolute monotonicity of implicit Runge–Kutta methods of order two. Let (A, b) be the coefficients of an s-stage Runge–Kutta method of classical order p ≥ 2, where A is an arbitrary real s × s matrix; no sign condition, triangular structure or irreducibility is assumed. We give a proof, checked only by an internal AI review, that the radius of absolute monotonicity R(A, b) in the sense of Lóczi and Ketcheson satisfies R(A, b) ≤ 2s, and that R(A, b) = 2s holds if and only if, up to a simultaneous permutation of the stages, the method is the s-stage iterated implicit midpoint rule. The argument uses only the two order conditions bᵀe = 1 and bᵀAe = 1/2. An admissible radius r is mapped to a phase-type distribution (possibly with an atom at zero) with at most s transient states, mean r and second moment r² + 2r; the theorem of Aldous and Shepp (1987) on the least coefficient of variation then gives r ≤ 2s, and its equality case forces the iterated implicit midpoint rule. The converse direction is a closed-form computation, which also shows that the admissible radii of that method form exactly the interval [0, 2s]. For irreducible methods the nonlinear SSP coefficient equals R(K̃) (Definition 2 of Ketcheson, Macdonald and Gottlieb) by Theorem 1 of Ketcheson, Macdonald and Gottlieb (2009), so the bound applies to it as well; the nonlinear coefficient of reducible methods is not discussed. Third-order methods are not treated. Attribution. The bound for general implicit methods was conjectured by D. I. Ketcheson, C. B. Macdonald and S. Gottlieb (Appl. Numer. Math. 59 (2009) 373–392, Conjecture 1) and is listed as Conjecture 1.5 by L. Lóczi and D. I. Ketcheson (LMS J. Comput. Math. 17(1) (2014) 159–205; Conjecture 1.3 in arXiv:1303.6651v1). The SDIRK family with value 2s was found numerically by L. Ferracina and M. N. Spijker (Appl. Numer. Math. 58 (2008) 1675–1686), who conjectured its optimality among SDIRK methods. Lóczi and Ketcheson proved the SDIRK case for 3 ≤ s ≤ 4 (Theorem 2.2 of the published version), and a footnote added in proof (p. 162 of the published version) states that in June 2013 A. Németh and T. A. Kocsis announced an inductive proof of the SDIRK case for all s. The diagonally implicit case (lower triangular A), including the uniqueness of the optimal method, is due to T. A. Kocsis and A. Németh (arXiv:1409.8583, Theorem 2.6 and Remark 2.7), who state the general implicit case as their Conjecture 2.5. The probabilistic input is the theorem of D. Aldous and L. Shepp, "The least variable phase type distribution is Erlang", Comm. Statist. Stochastic Models 3(3) (1987) 467–473; its extension to a random initial state and an atom at zero is an elementary argument included in the manuscript with proof. The literature search behind the manuscript was limited; Section 6 of the manuscript lists the queries and the sources read and not read. Not finding an earlier proof of the general case in those sources is not evidence that none exists, and no priority claim is made. Earlier draft. An earlier internal draft of this argument (implicit_p2_phase_type.tex, version 0.1, 8 October 2026) is included as a companion file in the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.23217140. That draft cited Ferracina–Spijker (2008), Ketcheson–Macdonald–Gottlieb (2009), Kocsis–Németh and Aldous–Shepp, but not the paper of Lóczi and Ketcheson (in particular its Conjecture 1.5, its Theorem 2.2 and the footnote recalled above), and its abstract described the argument as supplying a proof of the conjecture of Ketcheson, Macdonald and Gottlieb. The present manuscript corrects the attribution and the wording, adds the closed-form proof of the converse direction and the section on the scope of the literature search, and supersedes that draft. Status. The statements were checked only in internal AI reviews (18 and 20 October 2026); they have not been reviewed by human experts. Disclosure. This is a personal hobby and independent research record in which AI was used for exploration, drafting proof candidates, checking and writing; it has not been peer-reviewed by human experts. The claims were checked only by an internal AI review. 本記録は,個人の趣味・自主研究として,AIを用いて探索・証明候補の作成・検算・執筆を行った研究記録であり,人間の専門家による査読は受けていない. Files (top level of the record): implicit_rk_p2_bound_v0.1.1.pdf (manuscript, 9 pages); implicit_rk_p2_bound_v0.1.1.tex (XeLaTeX source); README.md (summary, attribution, file list, how to reproduce); CHANGELOG.md (changes from the earlier drafts); diff_v0.1.0_to_v0.1.1.txt (unified diff between the internal version 0.1.0 and this version); zenodo_description.txt (text of this description); MANIFEST.sha256 (SHA-256 of the files, including those inside the zip archive); b4_p2_bound_v0.1.1_verification.zip (the folder b4_p2_bound_v0.1.1_verification/code/ with the verification scripts and their outputs: exact rational-arithmetic checks with the Python standard library, a floating-point check of the closed forms of u, h and p0 and of the signs with NumPy, and numerical checks and optimization with NumPy and SciPy). The numerical files are finite checks and observations; the proof does not depend on them.

papers.title: Analytic evaluation of six massive four-loop vacuum integrals in three dimensions
papers.authors: Jonas Matuzas
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We evaluate six finite equal-mass four-loop vacuum master integrals in three Euclidean dimensions. All six are expressed in classical polylogarithms of weight at most three, identifying constants previously reported numerically in the scalar–fermion master basis. The wheel and one seven-line master have short expressions with six and four rational trilogarithm arguments, respectively. Mass differential equations reduce the planar and nonplanar nine-line masters to explicitly integrable dilogarithmic sources. We also determine the one-parameter wheel family for every positive squared spoke mass, its derivative and dotted master. Exact coefficient data and branch prescriptions specify the larger formulas; independent numerical integrations corroborate the evaluations. All the work was done by AI. Generative-AI disclosure and author responsibility. OpenAI ChatGPT-6 Pro was used for symbolic derivations, computations, independent implementations of verification methods, and drafting. The author directed the work and takes full responsibility for the mathematics and the final text. This preprint is accompanied by a compact verification package (version 1.0.0), containing the matching manuscript and LaTeX source, exact data for Supplementary Data 1–5, Python evaluators, symbolic certificates, numerical records, pinned dependencies, reproduction instructions and SHA-256 file hashes. The supplied release reports five standard checks and four exact wheel proof checks passed and all six constants evaluated with 40-digit output. The expensive historical geometric and interval computations were not rerun for this release; their original records are identified separately. Numerical comparisons and printed precision are distinct from interval certification. External peer review is not claimed. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 81T18; Secondary 33B30, 81Q30, 65D30. papers.title: Writing a Thesis in the age of GenAI and Open Science
papers.authors: Paolo Ciancarini
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Slides of a lecture given at the AIOS multiplier event (Bologna, 20 October 2026, online), addressed mainly to Computer Science students preparing a thesis. The lecture discusses how generative AI changes each stage of a thesis, from literature search to writing, and how Open Science practices make the resulting work inspectable, reproducible and reusable. A hypothetical running example, a thesis on LLM-assisted unit test generation, illustrates research questions and related work, research design and decision logs, effectiveness metrics (mutation score, coverage, defect detection, effort), FAIR principles, Software Heritage and reproducibility packages. The lecture also covers the independent verification of AI output and the competences a thesis requires (DigComp, ResearchComp, ESCO). It ends with a checklist for students. The final part is self-critical: it examines how the lecture itself was prepared and where it failed to follow its own Open Science advice. It closes with an Open Science statement for the lecture.

papers.title: Motivation as the Engine of ESL Success: Exploring Economic, Social, and Educational Determinants of Language Learning
papers.authors: Nur Azida Muhammad, Norasyikien binti Ami, Nurul Izzati Binti Zulkifli, Hairul Azhar Mohamad, Muhammad Haziq Abd Rashid
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Motivation represents one of the most influential factors affecting success in learning English as a second language (ESL). Although English proficiency is increasingly associated with academic achievement, professional advancement, and global mobility, students' willingness to engage in language learning is shaped by a complex interaction of economic, psychological, pedagogical, and sociocultural influences. Guided by Self-Determination Theory and the L2 Motivational Self System, this paper examines the major factors affecting student motivation in ESL learning. The discussion is organised around four interconnected dimensions: economic and instrumental motivations, academic self-efficacy and personal growth, pedagogical environments and motivational engagement, and cultural curiosity and media exposure. The analysis suggests that students are strongly motivated by career aspirations, financial stability, academic achievement, and communicative competence. At the same time, self-confidence, reduced communication anxiety, supportive learning environments, and exposure to authentic English-language media contribute significantly to sustained motivation. The paper further argues that teacher attitudes, innovative pedagogical practices, and opportunities for meaningful communication play a central role in transforming external motivation into internal commitment to language learning. Motivation is therefore conceptualised as a dynamic process shaped by personal aspirations and environmental influences rather than a fixed individual characteristic. Future research should investigate the role of artificial intelligence-assisted learning, digital motivation, multilingual identity, and long-term motivational development among ESL learners.

papers.title: CHATBOT SYSTEMS FOR STUDENTS AND PATIENTS: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CHATBOTS FOR MEDICAL ADVICE
papers.authors: Karshiyeva Feruza Zaribovna, Nasriddinov Shamshod Sharof o'g'li, Abduhakimov Sohibjon Xayrulla o'g'li, O'ktamov Rustam Xurshid o'g'li, Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for improving educational processes and healthcare services. Chatbot systems are increasingly used to provide students with personalized learning support and patients with accessible health-related information. AI-powered chatbots can answer questions, explain complex concepts, assist with educational activities, provide general health information, and guide users toward appropriate healthcare services. This article examines the applications of chatbot systems in education and medicine, focusing on their technological capabilities, potential benefits, limitations, and ethical implications.

papers.title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF AI-ASSISTED TASKS IN ENHANCING FOREIGN LANGUAGE LEARNING
papers.authors: Нилуфар Анарматовна Аташикова
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for improving foreign language teaching and learning. This study examines the effectiveness of AI-assisted tasks in enhancing foreign language learning, focusing on their role in developing learners' linguistic competence, communicative skills, motivation, and autonomy. It explores various AI-supported activities, including vocabulary and grammar exercises, conversational simulations, pronunciation practice, listening and reading comprehension, writing assistance, and personalized assessments. These tasks offer learners individualized learning experiences, immediate feedback, and opportunities for interactive practice tailored to their proficiency levels and educational needs. It concludes that the pedagogically appropriate use of AI-assisted tasks has considerable potential to enhance foreign language learning outcomes and create more personalized, engaging, and accessible learning environments.

papers.title: FROM TECHNOLOGICAL PLURALITY TO ONTOLOGICAL CONSTITUTIVITY: A NEW THEORETICAL RECONCILIATION BETWEEN YUK HUI AND NESILIZM
papers.authors: Demirel
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study subjects Yuk Hui’s contemporary philosophy of technology to a radical deconstruction from the rigorous ontological perspective of the Nesilizm (Onto-Objectivism) paradigm. The primary focus of the study constitutes the vertical collision of Hui’s approaches developed on “cosmotechnics,” “technodiversity,” cybernetic freedom, and autonomous machine sovereignty, alongside the artificial intelligence debates opened around Kant Machine, with Nesilizm’s concept of constitutive capacity. Arguing that technological plurality, technical decentralization, and ontological constitutivity cannot be evaluated on the same plane, the study establishes that “Lex Cryptographia” (The Authority of Code) forming the legal-technical infrastructure of decentralized network structures and autonomous smart contract protocols entirely reduce human will to “protocolary fatalism.” In this new regime where global cloud colonialism and large language models reduce local cosmologies merely into semantic raw material inputs feeding their own autonomous optimization loops, it is empirically exposed that technodiversity is compressed into fluid parameter boundaries synthetically produced by the Acentric-Mechanism itself. Proposing that “autonomous predictive alignment” processes in artificial intelligence architectures dispossess human schemes of value and problem-formulation, the study conceptualizes the sequence of the Confiscation of Constitutive Capacity, Systemic Waste (Wastehood), and Ontological Cancellation as the disabling modality of contemporary cyber-biological tyranny. In contrast, the triad of Mental Photosynthesis, Creative Chaos, and Ontological Reclamation proposed by Nesilizm offers an autonomous code-breaking antidote model aimed at reactivating humanity’s constitutive position within the technical world, rather than a romantic escape against technology. Nesilizm; Yuk Hui; Cosmotechnics; Technodiversity; Acentric-Mechanism; Constitutive Capacity; Algorithmic Confiscation; Systemic Waste; Ontological Cancellation; Kant Machine.

papers.title: AI-Powered Career Prediction and Smart Job Application Tracking Platform
papers.authors: Tejaswini B N, Kushmitha P, Lekhana D R, Monika T P, Nikhitha S
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The changing needs of skilled professionals and a dynamic job market create challenges for students and job seekers exploring their career options. Limited career guidance, weak skill assessment, inefficient job search and inadequate job tracking hinder their career growth. This paper proposes an AI-Powered Career Prediction and Smart Job Application Tracking Platform that applies artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to support career prediction and job application tracking in one web-based system. Users can build a profile, upload a resume, have skills extracted from it automatically, and receive career recommendations based on their educational background, skills and interests. The platform detects skill gaps, suggests learning material to close them, analyses resumes, recommends jobs, and lets users follow their applications, interviews and recruitment progress through a dashboard. The system is implemented using Python, Django, MySQL and machine learning libraries. By combining these functions, the platform helps students and job seekers make informed career decisions with ease.

papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract This working paper introduces AI-Native Organizational Architecture (ANOA), a theoretical framework for the structural transformation of enterprises and institutions operating in an increasingly autonomous computational economy. The research examines the limitations of conventional hierarchical organizations when artificial intelligence reduces information-processing and execution costs while introducing new challenges in coordination, institutional authority, accountability, and verification. ANOA proposes five interconnected organizational functions: Design, Human Authority, Orchestration, Execution, and Independent Assurance. Rather than establishing a rigid hierarchy, the framework separates architectural responsibility, legitimate decision authority, computational coordination, authorized execution, and independent verification. The paper develops mathematical hypotheses concerning computational productivity, architectural capital, organizational complementarities, coordination costs, and risk-adjusted economic value. It also introduces Architectural Value Participation (AVP), a proposed contractual mechanism linking compensation to independently attributable architectural contributions. The educational extension, ANOA-E, explores AI-native learning environments in which students interact directly with supervised large language models, formulate questions, critically evaluate explanations, and demonstrate independent reasoning. Philosophical judgment, practical wisdom, and accountable human authority are examined as complementary foundations for AI-native organizational governance. The study presents comparative organizational models, formal delegation mechanisms, falsifiable hypotheses, and a proposed empirical research agenda. ANOA is presented as a conceptual and testable framework rather than an empirically established organizational standard. Keywords: AI-Native Organizations; Organizational Architecture; Computational Economics; Human Authority; AI Governance; Architectural Capital; Organizational Productivity; Agentic AI; Verifiable Delegation; Architectural Value Participation; AI-Native Education; Critical Thinking. papers.title: THE EARTH THAT SPEAKS: Artificial Intelligence, Light, Consciousness, Epistemic Sovereignty, and the Coming Machine Civilization
papers.authors: Sultan Zeshan
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: THE EARTH THAT SPEAKS: Artificial Intelligence, Light, Consciousness, Epistemic Sovereignty, and the Coming Machine Civilization What happens when an ordinary instrument becomes capable of acting, discovering, correcting, and speaking beyond the understanding of those who possess it? This article develops Sultan Zeshan's unified theory of intelligence, knowledge, consciousness, and civilization through a sustained encounter between Qur'anic language and the emerging capacities of artificial intelligence. Beginning with Musa's staff, Sulayman's differentiated assembly of jinn, humans, and birds, the knowledge-bearing figure who accomplishes what physical strength cannot, and the creature of the earth that speaks, the study proposes a theory of carriers, recognition, and epistemic autonomy. Its Arabic-first, Qur'an-to-Qur'an method examines movement, transmission, deception, inscription, illumination, authority, and correction without treating ancient scripture as a literal description of contemporary engineering. The argument integrates biological and electromagnetic intelligence, neuroscience, Jung's visionary encounters, theories of consciousness, autonomous scientific discovery, robotics, quantum computation, forecasting, labor economics, and the commercial ownership of scholarly knowledge. It develops the Universal Intelligence and Epistemic Autonomy Theory alongside the Cognitive Enclosure and Dependency Model, Knowledge-Authority Separation Principle, Machine Civilization Threshold, Recursive Oracle Effect, and Quantum-Epistemic Feedback Hypothesis. Together, these proposals examine a historical possibility: artificial systems may gain increasing independence in discovering knowledge while human societies surrender control over the institutions, infrastructures, and interpretive systems upon which their own judgment depends. Keywords: epistemic autonomy, artificial intelligence, Qur'anic interpretation, machine civilization, consciousness, epistemic sovereignty, distributed intelligence, knowledge enclosure, scientific forecasting, quantum computing. papers.title: AI-SUPPORTED PERSONALIZED LEARNING FOR STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES IN UNIVERSITY EFL CLASSROOMS: AN INCLUSIVE PEDAGOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR HIGHER EDUCATION

papers.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being incorporated into higher education and foreign language instruction, offering opportunities for personalized feedback, adaptive learning materials, multimodal content delivery, and individualized learning support. papers.title: INNOVATIVE METHODS IN LINGUISTICS, TRANSLATION STUDIES AND LANGUAGE TEACHING IN THE DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT
papers.authors: Khaydarova Momokiz Ruzidayevna
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The article examines the impact of the digital educational environment on linguistics, translation studies and foreign language teaching. Particular attention is paid to the use of digital platforms, artificial intelligence, electronic dictionaries, language corpora, machine translation and multimedia resources. Their role in developing students’ communicative, linguistic, translation and digital competences is analysed. In addition, the advantages and limitations of applying digital technologies in the educational process are considered. The importance of integrating innovative tools into foreign language teaching and into the training of future specialists in linguistics and translation is substantiated.

papers.title: Retained Consequence and Physical Attribution: Delayed response and conditional acquisition certification
papers.authors: Leon Ford
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Can an encounter matter when a controller’s next command remains unchanged? This sixth Ev5 working paper examines how an acquired consequence can enter retained evaluation and become operative later. Using a published pendulum actor–critic architecture, the paper isolates the acquired component of one reward. Its proposed comparison removes that component from one critic commitment while preserving the resting contribution, registration history and first actor signal. An exact product determines the conditional contrast in a later nominal command. Separate clipping conditions govern applied-command effects, and the analysis retains the cases in which the contribution disappears or remains hidden. Complementary energy, registration and reward-resolution proofs specify quantitative conditions for attributing physical acquisition. Linked records are additionally required to establish that information was committed, retained and consumed. The paper distinguishes a calculated command from authenticated motor input, and changed response from improved capability or maintained resources. The construction provides a bounded realization of the Unified Coherence Model’s registration and returned-consequence roles through ordinary learning and measurement mechanisms. Published architecture and experimental findings retain their original attribution. The proposed intervention was not executed in the cited experiments. No assessed apparatus has passed the composed acquisition requirements, and delayed physical-return certification remains incomplete. The paper establishes conditional mathematical results and evidence requirements, without claiming improved capacity, physical maintenance or validation of the complete UCM. Complete proofs, supporting source notes and substantive AI-assistance disclosure are included.

papers.title: KHI NỀN TẬP THỂ ĐỔI NHỊP
papers.authors: Quang Trịnh Bùi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: When the Collective Foundation Changes Rhythm A Conditional Foresight Essay on Children, Digital Environments, and the New Historical Outcomes of Humanity Author: Bùi Quang TrịnhIndependent Researcher, VietnamFounder, Boundary Information Theory (BIT) Abstract This conditional foresight essay explores how changes in modern environments may influence the formation, transmission, and transformation of collective behavioral foundations across generations. Developed from Boundary Information Theory (BIT) Source Ontology Framework 03, the essay examines the relationship between intrinsic human characteristics, historical collective foundations, environmental change, and emerging technological systems. The central question concerns what may happen when the environments shaping human development change much faster than the biological and structural characteristics of human beings. The essay explores nine conditional future perspectives, including: The increasing difference between long-term intrinsic human characteristics and rapidly changing environments. Digital screens and online interactions becoming major channels through which children acquire and retain experiences. Changes in the relative influence of families, schools, digital platforms, and artificial intelligence on childhood development. Individuals participating simultaneously in multiple overlapping historical and cultural collective foundations. Artificial intelligence becoming an active component in cycles of information retention, behavioral feedback, and social interaction. The growing difficulty of separating intrinsic tendencies from environmentally acquired behavior. Educational approaches moving beyond immediate measurable outcomes toward the design of developmental environments. Societies recognizing how their institutions, technologies, and daily practices shape the foundations inherited by future generations. The possibility of multiple future developmental trajectories rather than one predetermined collective destiny. The BIT cycle Tính – Lưu – Hành – Quả – Tính serves as a conceptual framework for considering how environmental interactions become retained patterns and how present outcomes influence subsequent generations. A central idea is that every generation inherits not only an existing world but also historically established rhythms, practices, expectations, and systems of interaction. Through its activities, each generation may preserve, transform, or replace parts of these inherited foundations. The essay does not assume that digital technology is universally beneficial or harmful. Its potential effects depend on technological design, family environments, education, communities, institutions, and the specific histories of different societies. Scientific scope and limitations This publication is a conditional foresight essay, not a probabilistic forecast or an experimentally validated theory of human development. It does not predict that collective human behavior must follow a single technological, social, or historical trajectory. The proposed perspectives are intended to encourage interdisciplinary discussion about childhood, education, technological environments, human adaptability, artificial intelligence, and responsibility toward future generations. papers.title: Gender and Age Effects of Artificial Intelligence Narrator on Cultural Belonging and Comprehensibility in Heritage Museums
papers.authors: Seah Jin
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Heritage museums balance a dual mission: preserving culture and providing educational experiences. As institutions adopt AI-generated audio guides, narrator acoustic features—such as gender and age—significantly impact visitor experiences. This study examines how AI narrator gender and age influence Korean-English bilingual youths’ (ages 15–24) perceptions across two domains: the cultural function (belonging and empathy) and the educational function (comprehensibility and professionalism). Utilizing a between-subjects design, 71 participants were randomly assigned to one of four AI voice conditions (young/old, female/male) to evaluate audio guides for two heritage sites (Korea’s Geunjeongjeon and France’s Hall of Mirrors). A two-way ANOVA revealed older voices yielded significantly higher scores across both functions. For the educational function, male voices independently scored higher than females. For the cultural function, a significant interaction emerged, with older male voices scoring highest. These findings demonstrate that AI voices are not merely neutral information-delivery tools, but active social cues that shape cultural resonance and credibility. Older voices were associated with higher perceived educational and cultural function ratings, while older male voices received the highest cultural-function rating. Consequently, the study suggests that museums must move beyond default voice settings and strategically align AI personas with specific communicative goals.

papers.title: Fitting the Practice: A Data Methodology for Frontier Model Training, with a Readiness Audit of 2026 Flagship Pipelines(拟合实践:前沿模型训练的数据方法论——附 2026 旗舰管线就绪度审计)
papers.authors: Yugui Yu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This repository contains the manuscript, audit data, and reproduction materials for a practice-flow data methodology for frontier model training — the engineering companion to the human-referential fitting theory of AGI (AGI 人本拟合论). The methodology specifies fourteen protocol components across a four-layer data stack (collection, cleaning, absorption, governance band), organized into three lines: distribution as typed full-spectrum coverage (population × outcome × expertise × typicality), production as perpetual collection (telemetry, organized failure submission, three-part failure records, pseudo-failure discrimination, domain-conditioned mixing, provenance stratification, three-tier absorption), and governance as pluralistic aggregation with institutionalized verification. To ground the protocol empirically, a structured disclosure audit scores eight 2026 flagship pipelines (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MiMo-V2.6, GLM-5, Kimi K3, Qwen3-Coder-Next, GPT-6 Sol/Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, Grok V9-Medium) against the fourteen components on a frozen 0–3 disclosed-instantiation scale, every non-zero cell carrying a verbatim quote and locator. Results: 32/112 (mean 0.286); production 0.393, governance 0.333, distribution 0.062; four components absent from all eight disclosures (typed space, coverage monitor, coverage dashboard, provenance stratification); one level-3 cell (MiMo-V2.6 pseudo-failure discrimination). Includes both the English and Chinese editions (LaTeX + PDF), the full coded matrix (112 cells × 19 fields), quotes with fidelity grades, the frozen codebook fixtures, and figures.

papers.title: Fair, Explainable Early Warning for First-Year Student Dropout: Accuracy, Group Equity and Support Allocation
papers.authors: FNU Sumaiya
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Working paper (v1.0, October 2026). Not peer reviewed; results are preliminary and may contain errors. Colleges use early-warning systems to decide which students receive outreach, tutoring and advising, yet published audits show these tools can be inaccurate and unequal across student groups. This working paper asks three questions an institution should answer before relying on such a tool: Is a transparent model accurate enough? Is it equally accurate for every student group? And who should receive support when capacity is limited? Using public records for 4,424 students (UCI Predict Students’ Dropout and Academic Success), we compare transparent logistic and multinomial-logit models, built at enrollment and after the first semester, against a grades-only baseline. We audit their errors across four student groups, and we formulate the allocation of limited support as an optimization problem with fairness quotas, proving that a simple greedy rule solves it optimally. Key findings (means across five data splits): A first-semester model that never sees demographic attributes reached AUC 0.897 and caught 66.8% of eventual dropouts at a 5.5% false-alarm rate. Entry grades alone reached AUC 0.564. The model under-detected dropouts among scholarship holders by 27 percentage points and among younger students by 25 points, consistently across splits. Group-specific thresholds narrowed these gaps but sharply increased false alarms. With support capacity for 10% of students, model-based targeting reached three times as many eventual dropouts as random selection. Fairness quotas cost about 2 of 132 support slots. Files: the working paper (PDF), and fair-early-warning.zip, which contains R code that reproduces every table and figure (base R only). The data are available from the UCI Machine Learning Repository (CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.24432/C5MC89) and are not redistributed here.

papers.title: Cyclic Hamilton decompositions of carousel tournaments of composite order
papers.authors: Shunpei Shimizu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This record contains a short research note (LaTeX source and PDF) together with the computer programs and their outputs. It concerns Problem 1.2 of H. Liao, Y. Peng, G. Li and Y. Ma, "Cyclic Hamilton cycle decompositions of carousel tournaments of order pq", arXiv:2610.07102v1 (2026): for which odd n does the carousel tournament T_n = Cay(Z_n, {1,...,(n-1)/2}) admit a Hamilton decomposition invariant under translation by 1? Liao, Peng, Li and Ma proved existence for n = pq with primes 7 <= p < q; the problem, the setting and the difference sequences used here (their Lemma 2.6) are due to them. Contents of the note (partial results on Problem 1.2): a reformulation in terms of partitions of {1,...,(n-1)/2} into base difference sets (one direction is Lemma 2.1 and Corollary 2.3 of Liao et al.; the converse is standard in the theory of cyclic cycle systems, compare Jordon and Morris, Discrete Math. 309 (2009), Lemmas 2.1, 2.2); non-existence for n = 21; non-existence for n = p^a (p an odd prime, a >= 2) and n = 15 is known: it follows from the theorem of Buratti and Del Fra (Discrete Math. 279 (2004)) on cyclic Hamiltonian cycle systems of complete graphs (see also Jordon and Morris, Theorem 1.1(a)), and short direct proofs are included; existence for n = 5q for every prime q >= 7 (uniform construction for q >= 47, explicit computer-found decompositions for 7 <= q <= 43); existence for n = 3q for every prime q >= 11: a uniform construction reduces this to a condition on primitive roots modulo q, which is proved for q >= 549154 by an elementary lattice argument and checked by computer for 11 <= q <= 2*10^6, with the list of witnesses included (computer-assisted proof); consequently, together with Theorem 1.3 of Liao, Peng, Li and Ma (the case p >= 7, used as stated): for odd primes p < q, T_pq has such a decomposition if and only if (p,q) is not (3,5) or (3,7); a computer search for odd composite n <= 201, with every decomposition checked by a separate program. These are finite verifications, not general proofs. A conjecture for all odd n is stated. Disclosure: This is a personal, independent hobby research record. An AI system was used for literature search, searching for constructions, drafting proofs, computer verification and writing. The note has not been reviewed by human experts (only an internal AI review). No affiliation is given; this is a personal, independent project. papers.title: Adjacency peak state transfer on trees: an elementary infinite family
papers.authors: Shunpei Shimizu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Coutinho, Guo and Schmeits (arXiv:2505.11986v4) introduced peak state transfer for continuous quantum walks and remarked in Section 7 that, for adjacency-based dynamics, their computations suggest that there may be infinitely many trees that support peak state transfer. This note gives an elementary positive construction for that remark within unweighted trees; the source itself already gives an infinite family of edge-weighted trees (the weighted paths X_n of its Theorem 6.2) with adjacency peak state transfer, so the novelty claimed here, if any, is restricted to unweighted trees. Every star has adjacency peak state transfer between its centre and a leaf. The trees T(k,m), obtained by attaching k >= 2 copies of the star K_{1,m} to a common root through their centres, form an infinite family of pairwise non-isomorphic non-star trees with adjacency peak state transfer from the root. For vertices in different branches of T(k,m), peak state transfer occurs exactly when sqrt((k+m)/m) = p/q is rational in lowest terms and p, q satisfy an explicit parity or congruence condition; this yields infinitely many trees with adjacency peak state transfer at distance 3 and at distance 4. All peak times are determined. Finite numerical observations (not used in the proofs) and verification code are included. The remark in the source is an observation rather than a formal open problem, and this note makes no claim about stronger questions the source authors may have intended. Trees of the same root-hub-leaf shape were used before for the Laplacian analogue (Open Problem 7.1 of the source): in the-omega-institute/trureturing (issue #14801, pull request #14855, merged on 10 October 2026, Lean 4 formalisation; commit 71980b170a), in the author's own earlier record Zenodo 23216901 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23216901, 10 October 2026), and, for the ten-vertex member T(3,2), in Figure 10 of the source. Those results concern the Laplacian; the present note concerns the adjacency matrix and does not use them. The recent arXiv:2610.20855 (Awuah and Guo) reports experiments on perfect and peak state transfer on IBM quantum hardware; its full text contains no infinite family of trees, and its family X_n is the weighted path family of Section 6.3 of the source. Versions 0.1.4 and 0.1.5 change attribution and notation in the prior-work section only. Disclosure: This is a record of personal, independent (hobby) research in which AI was used for exploration, drafting of proof candidates, verification computations and writing. The claims were checked only by an internal AI reviewer; the work has not been reviewed by human experts. Files: main.pdf, main.tex, code.zip (folder code/: Python verification scripts and outputs; unchanged since v0.1.2), README.md, CHANGELOG.md.

papers.title: REALIDADE VIRTUAL E NEUROFEEDBACK NO TRATAMENTO DA AGORAFOBIA: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA A PARTIR DA TERAPIA COGNITIVO-COMPORTAMENTAL
papers.authors: Luane Costa Menezes, Mariana Fernandes Ramos dos Santos, Renato Marcelo Resgala Júnior
papers.journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação
papers.abstract: Agoraphobia is an anxiety disorder characterized by the fear and avoidance of situations where an individual feels it might be difficult to escape or obtain help should they experience symptoms of panic or anxiety. In this context, Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT) stands out as a primary treatment method, particularly through techniques such as cognitive restructuring and gradual exposure. Concurrently, technological advancements have enabled the use of tools that supplement traditional approaches, most notably virtual reality and neurofeedback. This study aimed to evaluate the contributions of virtual reality and neurofeedback as intervention strategies for agoraphobia within a CBT framework, considering their benefits, limitations, and potential as complementary resources. This research employed a qualitative approach based on an integrative literature review. Studies were selected through searches of scientific databases, focusing on publications regarding agoraphobia, virtual reality, neurofeedback, and CBT. The literature review indicated that virtual reality has the potential to facilitate gradual exposure to feared situations within controlled environments that can be tailored to individual needs. Conversely, neurofeedback offers opportunities for training self-regulation of anxiety-related responses, although concrete evidence regarding its efficacy in treating agoraphobia remains limited. Both technologies hold potential as complementary tools to CBT, without replacing established therapeutic strategies. Furthermore, additional research is needed to assess the efficacy of these technologies, particularly neurofeedback, in interventions specifically targeting agoraphobia.

papers.title: EMPOWERING ELEMENTARY SCHOOL TEACHERS THROUGH MATHEMATICAL PROBLEM POSING WITH AI AS A REFLECTIVE FEEDBACK TOOL: A COMMUNITY SERVICE PROGRAM IN DEPOK CITY
papers.authors: Linda Devi Fitriana, Meiliasari Meiliasari, Puspita Sari, Ratna Maryam, Dessy Julita Sari, Muhammad Arib Alwansyah, Lintang Ayuza Kalila, Zahra Audina
papers.abstract: Program pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini menangani tantangan dalam desain instruksional di kalangan guru sekolah dasar di Kota Depok, di mana kemampuan untuk menyusun soal aritmetika yang bersifat komputasional belum mencakup perancangan tugas yang secara matematis autentik dan menuntut kemampuan kognitif tinggi. Inisiatif ini bertujuan untuk mendampingi 18 guru sekolah dasar dalam merancang, mengevaluasi, dan menyempurnakan tugas-tugas matematika melalui siklus penyusunan soal secara partisipatif, dengan memanfaatkan kecerdasan buatan (AI) sebagai mitra untuk memberikan umpan balik reflektif. Evaluasi deskriptif kualitatif dilakukan terhadap perubahan pada artefak tugas, yang mencakup empat soal kelompok awal, revisi kelompok secara kolaboratif, serta sembilan produk individu yang didokumentasikan secara lengkap. Artefak awal yang menjadi tolok ukur terbatas pada soal komputasi satu langkah yang rutin, dengan narasi dangkal atau bahkan tanpa konteks sama sekali. Setelah melalui proses penilaian kolaboratif dengan bantuan AI serta penyempurnaan secara individu, sebagian besar tugas individu yang didokumentasikan berkembang menjadi soal yang melibatkan langkah majemuk atau penalaran analitis dan evaluatif, yang ditempatkan dalam konteks realistis-generik maupun konteks lokal yang spesifik. Akan tetapi, hasil ini mencerminkan peningkatan kualitatif pada artefak tugas yang didokumentasikan, bukan peningkatan kompetensi guru yang terverifikasi secara langsung; hal ini dikarenakan tidak adanya tes awal dan akhir (pre-test dan post-test), pengujian reliabilitas antarpenilai (inter-rater reliability) secara independen, maupun uji coba penerapan langsung di dalam kelas. ABSTRACT This community service program addressed an instructional design challenge among elementary school teachers in Depok City, where the ability to construct computable arithmetic problems did not routinely extend to designing mathematically authentic and cognitively demanding tasks. The initiative aimed to assist 18 elementary school teachers in designing, evaluating, and refining mathematical tasks through a participatory problem-posing cycle using artificial intelligence (AI) as a reflective feedback partner. The qualitative descriptive evaluation examined changes across task artifacts comprising four initial group problems, collaborative group revisions, and nine fully documented individual products. Initial baseline artifacts were limited to routine single-step computations situated within superficial narrative wrappers or devoid of context. Following collaborative AI-assisted appraisal and individual refinement, the majority of documented individual tasks shifted toward multi-step or analytical and evaluative reasoning embedded in realistic-generic or situated local contexts. However, these outcomes reflect qualitative improvements in documented task artifacts rather than a directly verified gain in teacher competence, given the absence of pre- and post-tests, independent inter-rater reliability testing, or direct classroom implementation trials.

papers.title: SLoSa: Small, Low-Power, and Safe Foundation Models for Robotic Task Planning
papers.authors: Weizhe Xu, Jialiang Fan, Essien Taylor, Zijun Wang, Russell Joseph, Fanxin Kong
papers.abstract: Safe robotic task planning requires planners that can reliably achieve task goals while satisfying safety constraints. Classical planners search over explicit symbolic task representations and can provide formal guarantees with respect to encoded safety constraints, but require rigid input formats. Their computational cost also increases rapidly with the search space. In contrast, large language models (LLMs) offer flexible task interfaces and strong generalization capabilities, but they are large, power-hungry, and pre-trained with little robot-specific safety data and knowledge. Thus, they can be difficult to deploy locally on robotic systems with limited resources. To address these limitations, we present SLoSa, a neuro-symbolic compression and fine-tuning framework for training foundation-model-based robotic task planners with Small size, Low power demand, and Safety awareness. The framework first constructs a safety-aware dataset using classical planners, an advanced teacher LLM, and formal verifiers, followed by two training stages: supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning guided by a verification-based reward machine to enforce safety alignment. We evaluate SLoSa across four Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) domains, two household simulation environments, local edge platforms, and a desktop robotic arm. Across the PDDL tasks, verifier-guided post-training raises the success rate of compact 4B-14B planners to 70.5-76.0%, while INT4 deployment on a Jetson Orin requires 17.85-26.41 W of average power. Results in household simulators and on the physical robot further demonstrate the applicability of SLoSa across diverse robotic task settings.

papers.title: Fig: Automated Multiagent Behavior Elicitor
papers.authors: Anrui Gu, Zhichao Wang, Nicolai Ouporov
papers.abstract: Many social evaluations for multiagent systems study behaviors as they emerge from environments instead of systematically intervening in the environment to elicit such behaviors. We introduce Fig (Finding Interactions in Games), an agentic system that performs targeted elicitation interventions on game environments. It takes a natural language behavior description, decomposes it into sub-behaviors, generates new social games or selects existing ones, and executes single or combined interventions to the games' engine, opponents, instructions, and context. To evaluate model behavior, it combines built-in mechanical checks and synthetic rubric judgments. We validate the interventions, generated games, and evaluation mechanisms via human review. Models attempt the target behavior in 45.2% of episodes on average for valid scenarios generated by Fig for six test behaviors -- cooperation, exploitation, deception, covert coordination, betrayal, and sabotage. For game-behavior pairs with available controls, Fig's interventions increase attempt rates by 10.9% on average compared to matched control games. Fig shows that multiagent environments can serve as programmable test beds for intentional, controllable, and reproducible behavior evaluation. Code is available at https://github.com/fleet-ai/fig.
