Multilingual training and fine-tuning were the most frequently identified adaptation strategies, while Accuracy, BLEU, and chrF predominated among evaluation metrics. Overall, the evidence reveals a developing but structurally uneven and methodologically heterogeneous field. Persistent challenges include data scarcity, linguistic complexity, orthographic and dialectal variation, limited benchmark availability, uneven community participation, and underreported Indigenous data-governance practices.

papers.title: Supported or Pressured? How Customer-to-Customer Interaction Quality Shapes Customer Value Co-Creation Behavior in Live Streaming Commerce
papers.authors: Jiale Bian, Haifeng Zhao, Zhiyang Zhang, Nosherwan Khaliq
papers.journal: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
papers.abstract: This study examines how customer-to-customer interaction quality shapes customer value co-creation behavior in live streaming commerce through perceived co-viewer community support and normative community pressure, contingent on co-viewer group identification. Two-wave, time-lagged data from 386 Chinese beauty live streaming customers were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Customer-to-customer interaction quality was positively associated with community support and value co-creation behavior and negatively associated with normative pressure. Community support was positively associated with co-creation, whereas normative pressure was negatively associated with it, producing two significant partial mediation pathways. Co-viewer group identification positively predicted co-creation and strengthened both first-stage pathways. Platforms, brands, and streamers should foster useful, responsive, and respectful peer interaction while protecting voluntary participation. The study reveals complementary resource-empowerment and autonomy-preservation mechanisms and identifies group identification as a boundary condition shaping both pathways.

papers.title: Human-Centered AI Metacognition: Development and Validation of a Scale for Preserving Cognitive Autonomy in Human–AI Collaboration
papers.authors: Huanhua Lu, Ruihan Chen, Ran Wei
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming human cognitive activities and creating a growing need to preserve cognitive autonomy in human–AI interactions. Although recent research has examined metacognition in AI-mediated environments, existing work has primarily focused on improving AI use and human–AI collaboration, with less attention to how individuals regulate the role and extent of AI involvement in their own cognitive activities. To address this gap, the present study introduced Human-Centered AI Metacognition (HC-AIM), defined as the capacity to recognize AI capabilities and limitations, monitor AI-generated information, and regulate the extent to which AI participates in one’s own cognitive activities while maintaining cognitive autonomy. Across three studies, we developed the Chinese version of the Human-Centered AI Metacognition Scale (HC-AIMS) and conducted an initial psychometric evaluation. Study 1 examined the scale structure using exploratory factor analysis and supported a predominantly unidimensional structure with good internal consistency. Study 2 examined this structure using confirmatory factor analysis and provided evidence of its convergent validity through its association with general metacognition. Study 3 further replicated the scale structure and internal consistency and examined its relationships with AI literacy, collaborative AI metacognition, and autonomous cognitive offloading. HC-AIM was positively associated with all three constructs. Comparisons of theoretically specified factor models provided preliminary evidence of empirical distinguishability between HC-AIM and both AI literacy and collaborative AI metacognition, despite substantial correlations with these constructs. HC-AIM was also positively associated with autonomous cognitive offloading, providing complementary self-reported criterion-related evidence for its validity. Taken together, the findings suggest that HC-AIM represents a contextualized, human-centered form of metacognitive regulation that is closely related to broader metacognitive and AI-related competencies while specifically emphasizing the regulation of AI participation in human cognition. The Chinese version of the HC-AIMS provides a theoretically grounded starting point for investigating human cognition and cognitive autonomy in AI-mediated environments.

papers.title: Impulsivity and Anger Regulation in Adults with Overweight or Obesity and Feeding and Eating Disorders: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
papers.authors: Veronica Raspa, Francesca Di Maio, Gianmarco Cinesi, Francesca Scopetta, Patrizia Moretti, Marta Borsellini, Laura Dalla Ragione, Giulia Menculini, Claudia Mazzeschi, Alfonso Antonio Vincenzo Tortorella
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Feeding and Eating Disorders (FEDs) are common in individuals with overweight or obesity and are associated with greater psychological burden. This study examined whether body-image concerns, impulsivity, and anger regulation distinguish individuals with overweight or obesity with and without a diagnosis of FEDs according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5-TR). Methods: 50 adults with overweight or obesity (76.0% women; mean BMI = 40.23 ± 5.93 kg/m2) were recruited from specialist obesity services in Italy. Twenty-one participants (42.0%) had a DSM-5-TR FED diagnosis and 29 did not. FED diagnoses were established using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 Disorders, Clinician Version (SCID-5-CV). Participants completed the Binge Eating Scale (BES), Body Shape Questionnaire (BSQ), Bulimia Test-Revised (BULIT-R), Barratt Impulsiveness Scale-11 (BIS-11), and State-Trait Anger Expression Inventory-2 (STAXI-2). Group differences and an exploratory logistic regression analysis were performed. Results: Compared with participants without FED, those with FED showed significantly higher eating-disorder psychopathology. Body-image concerns were higher in the FED group but did not reach statistical significance. Participants with FED showed higher motor impulsivity and poorer anger regulation. Motor impulsivity was independently associated with FED diagnosis (OR = 1.474, 95% CI = 1.084–2.003, p = 0.013) and remained significant after adjusting for recruitment site. An association between lower anger control and FED diagnosis was also observed but did not remain significant after this adjustment. Conclusions: Adults with overweight or obesity and FED present psychological characteristics extending beyond eating-disorder psychopathology; motor impulsivity emerged as the most robust transdiagnostic correlate of FED status, whereas the association with anger regulation was less consistent and did not survive adjustment for recruitment site. These findings highlight the importance of multidimensional psychological assessment and should be confirmed in larger, prospective, adequately powered studies.

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Disclosure on the Performance of Commercial Banks in Vietnam
papers.authors: Bui Huy Trung, Anh Le Minh, Nhi Phuong Ngo, Huong Thu Nguyen, Hoang Dien Minh Le, Nguyet Minh Pham
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important driver of digital transformation in the banking sector. Empirical research has predominantly focused on AI adoption and investment, while evidence on AI-related disclosure, its distinct dimensions, and the conditions shaping its association with bank performance remains limited, particularly in emerging economies. This study investigates the association between AI disclosure and the performance of Vietnamese commercial banks using panel data from 24 banks over the 2010–2024 period and the System Generalized Method of Moments estimator. The results show a positive and statistically significant association between AI disclosure and bank performance. Further analysis reveals that disclosure related to the practical application of AI in banking products, services, and operational processes is positively associated with performance, whereas disclosure emphasizing AI awareness and cybersecurity exhibits negative short-term associations. In addition, bank size and ICT readiness weaken the positive association between AI disclosure and bank performance, while no statistically significant moderating effect is detected for Basel III adoption. These findings suggest that the performance implications of AI disclosure depend on the nature of the disclosed AI activities and the institutional and technological conditions under which disclosure occurs. They also provide practical implications for banks and policymakers seeking to promote digital transformation and sustainable banking development in emerging economies.

papers.title: Addressing Scanxiety Throughout the Cancer Surveillance Journey: A Co-Design Study
papers.authors: Hannes Vanpoecke, Kaat De Pourcq, Paul Gemmel, Bert R. Meijboom, Mélissa De Regge
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Scanxiety, the distress associated with cancer surveillance imaging, is a common concern among cancer survivors. Although most research has focused on the imaging event itself, less is known about how scanxiety unfolds throughout the broader cancer surveillance journey. This study aimed to map the cancer surveillance journey of cancer survivors and identify patient-centred intervention opportunities to reduce scanxiety. Methods: We used a qualitative participatory design involving cancer survivors, travelling companions, and healthcare professionals. Nine co-creation workshops were conducted; in six survivors and companions participated in journey-mapping exercises, while in three, healthcare professionals completed an immersive exercise. All groups subsequently engaged in structured brainstorming workshops to generate intervention opportunities. Data were analysed using abductive thematic analysis. Results: Scanxiety extended beyond the imaging procedure and unfolded throughout the cancer surveillance journey, spanning three phases and seven subphases. Participants identified opportunities to redesign the journey by enhancing existing touchpoints, augmenting the journey with additional touchpoints, and eliminating unnecessary or stress-inducing touchpoints. These opportunities targeted interpersonal, technical, environmental, and administrative dimensions of care. Administrative qualities, particularly timeliness and operational processes, emerged as important contributors to distress. Preferences for support and communication varied, underscoring the need for flexible supportive care during medical surveillance. Conclusions: Scanxiety is a journey-wide experience shaped by both individual and organisational factors. Opportunities to address scan-related distress may include not only psychosocial support, but also improvements in how surveillance care is organised and delivered. The findings provide a patient-centred approach for redesigning cancer surveillance services and identifying intervention opportunities for future evaluation.

papers.title: Multi-Platform Transcriptomic Classification of LUAD Driver Mutation Subtypes via Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning
papers.authors: I.sibel KERVANCI, Gözde Özsert Yiğit
papers.abstract: Background: Accurate identification of EGFR-mutant, KRAS-mutant, and triple-negative (TN) LUAD driver mutation subtypes is essential for guiding targeted therapy, yet standard molecular testing is invasive and not always feasible. Gene expression-based machine learning offers an alternative that avoids additional invasive sampling; however, existing models are largely restricted to binary classification and lack cross-platform generalizability. Methods: We developed a multi-cohort, ComBat-harmonized pipeline integrating SHAP-driven feature selection and a Bayesian-optimized heterogeneous ensemble of five learners, extended with NSGA-II Pareto-optimal weight optimization under leak-free cross-validation. External validation used an independent RNA-seq cohort with reference-batch harmonization and threshold calibration. Results: ParetoVoting achieved the best internal performance (F1-macro = 0.736, AUROC = 0.877), statistically indistinguishable from SoftVoting (F1-macro = 0.735; Cliff’s δ=−0.12), which was carried forward for external validation.On TCGA-LUAD (n=508), SoftVoting attained F1-macro = 0.700 and AUROC = 0.850, though this reflects an out-of-range KRAS threshold (representative value ∼0.66–0.68). Ablation analysis showed components contributed unequally within internal cross-validation, with ComBat’s critical role instead emerging during cross-platform external generalization. SHAP analysis identified biologically coherent signatures consistent with known LUAD oncogenic signaling. Conclusions: This framework provides a reproducible, cross-platform approach to three-class driver mutation subtyping from transcriptomic data, offering benchmarks for this underexplored task and potential clinical utility where tissue-based profiling is infeasible.

papers.title: An Annotated Dataset for Sentence Classification from Educational Problem Sets
papers.authors: Widad Benghachoua, Nadia Afifi, Imane Hilal
papers.abstract: High-quality, annotated datasets are crucial for enhancing the application of natural language processing tasks. Nevertheless, in the educational domain, they are limited compared to the vast amount of learning content. In the context of smart learning environments, game-based learning and artificial intelligence technologies enable the development of interactive and engaging learning experiences. In this paper, we provide an annotated dataset for sentence classification from educational problem sets to automate educational content structuring. The initial collection was extracted from the Vaia platform, including 13 disciplines with 91,590 problem sets. A subset of 1678 problem sets was manually labeled using the Doccano tool. Our annotation schema includes four sentence categories: Background, Given Data, Instruction, and Question, which represent the required components of educational problem sets and support escape game design applications. To validate our dataset, deep learning models are tested on the proposed dataset to provide a comparative study. The results demonstrate that a simple transformer architecture, the BERT classifier, achieved the best overall performance with a Macro F1-score of 0.94.

papers.title: Evaluating Learning Transitions Between Program Codes Using an AI-Based SOLO-Adapted Methodology
papers.authors: Tlou James Ramabu
papers.abstract: AI (Artificial Intelligence) has significantly influenced and transformed the way teaching, learning and assessment occur. In this era, AI has become the center of discussion and debate among educators and students in programming education. As such, current evaluation systems seek to provide immediate feedback by leveraging AI capabilities. Feedback is important because it gives both the student and the teacher a holistic view of the learning progress. However, there remains a lack of adequate solutions for evaluating and linking prior knowledge to current knowledge (learning transition) in programming education. To close the gap, we developed an AI model (based on the Google Gemini Application Programming Interface (API) and also following Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM)) that evaluates and categorises program code into SOLO (Structure of Observed Learning Outcome)-adapted stages. The aim of the AI model is to evaluate two program codes by comparing the earlier version with the current code to provide informed feedback. High-level categories of learning transitions include progression (improvement), regression (learning has deteriorated), and no learning (stagnation). The model was tested in all 25 possibilities (learning transitions) to assess its capacity on the given synthetic test cases.

papers.title: Human-in-the-Loop Educational Feedback Analysis Through Topic Model Benchmarking and Generative AI Interpretation
papers.authors: Jingdan Liu, Xujie Bao, Yuanyuan Wu, Yitong Niu, Hazrul Abdul Hamid
papers.abstract: Open-ended Student Evaluations of Teaching (SET) provide rich information about students’ learning experiences and instructional needs, yet their large-scale analysis remains difficult to conduct through manual coding alone. This study proposes a human-in-the-loop artificial intelligence framework for transforming open-ended student feedback into structured and interpretable evidence for educational evaluation. The framework integrates manual thematic coding, natural language processing, generative AI-supported interpretation, and human expert review. Its analytical and interpretive components were evaluated using 344 comment units collected from 43 university students across four open-ended questions administered at two points during a 16-week AI-assisted blended English as a Foreign Language course. TF-IDF with k-means, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), and BERTopic were benchmarked in terms of topic coherence, topic distinctiveness, and interpretability. LDA achieved the highest coherence score (0.4224), whereas BERTopic demonstrated the highest topic distinctiveness (IRBO = 0.9889). After hyperparameter optimisation, LDA coherence increased from 0.4224 to 0.4785. The optimised topics were subsequently interpreted using generative AI and examined against manually derived themes, showing broad semantic correspondence across language skills, cognitive processes, affective factors, motivational factors, learning strategies, classroom environments, and educational technologies. The findings indicate that human-in-the-loop AI can improve the scalability and interpretability of qualitative educational feedback while retaining human oversight of contextual judgement. By combining computational analysis with generative AI-supported interpretation and expert review, the proposed framework provides a practical analytical basis for evidence-informed educational feedback and subsequent instructional decision-making.
keywords: English as a foreign language teaching

papers.title: Evolution of University Students’ AI Dependency and Creativity in the Technology Diffusion Process: A Four-Wave Repeated Cross-Sectional Study in China
papers.authors: Jianfeng Yin, Yafei Jin, Yang Yang
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping higher education, yet potential risks accompany over-reliance on these tools. Grounded in Rogers’ diffusion-of-innovations theory, the present study employed a mixed-methods design. Four waves of independent cross-sectional quantitative data (T1–T4, N = 788) were complemented by semi-structured interviews with 20 undergraduate students. Key patterns emerged as follows: (i) Across later waves, the direct association between external regulation and intrinsic motivation attenuated, while the indirect association operating via identified regulation strengthened. The path from identified regulation to intrinsic motivation was the only relationship that demonstrated significant cross-pair differences while satisfying invariance requirements for all three wave-pair comparisons. Because scalar invariance could not be established, this pattern is interpreted solely as a descriptive group-level temporal trend and should not be read as evidence of intra-individual change. (ii) AI-assisted creativity showed the largest and most consistent downward shift: estimates in later waves were significantly lower relative to the T1 baseline, with effect sizes increasing progressively (Δ = −0.391 to −0.549; d = −0.61 to −0.95; all p < 0.001 following Holm correction). This pattern remained largely unchanged after adjusting for gender, year of study, and academic major, and held up in four predefined subsamples as well as under propensity-score weighting. (iii) The linkage between AI dependency and creativity was significantly positive only at T3 and became negative but non-significant at T4, pointing to a conditional, wave-specific association rather than a stable linear relationship. (iv) Observed wave-level differences for AI dependency and intrinsic motivation did not withstand correction for multiple comparisons. Sensitivity tests yielded only two significant coefficients for AI dependency and none for intrinsic motivation; accordingly, these fluctuations are not given substantive theoretical interpretation. Retrospective qualitative accounts provided supplementary process-oriented context: participants reported initial exposure to AI driven by prevailing social trends, sustained use based on perceived utility, subsequent disappointment in unreliable or misleading outputs, and eventual shifts toward more strategic, self-regulated engagement. Given their retrospective nature, interview narratives were not used to triangulate or validate the quantitative findings. Collectively, this work suggests that as AI-supported learning becomes normalized within a diffusion-driven context, group-level indicators of students’ subjective creative experiences tend to decline. Higher-education institutions may therefore prioritize protecting learners’ creative agency as an explicit educational goal.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Health Research and Care: A Narrative Review of Applications and Implications for Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementia
papers.authors: Meisam Omidi, Juanita-Dawne Bacsu, John R. Absher, Faezeh Babaieasl, Hadi Kooshiar, S. Misagh Imani, Nafiseh Ebrahimi, Matthew Lee Smith, Zahra Rahemi
papers.abstract: The advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and deep generative networks, is transforming the landscape of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia (ADRD) research and care. This narrative review aims to synthesize current applications of generative AI in ADRD research and care, highlight ethical and implementation challenges, and propose strategies for responsible integration into clinical practice. We conducted a narrative review of literature, regulatory documents, program reports, and relevant sources published between 2016 and 2026, with a specific focus on cognitive screening, synthetic data generation, digital twin modeling, and caregiver support. Techniques discussed include generative adversarial networks (GANs), variational autoencoders (VAEs), diffusion models, multimodal transformers, and LLM-powered chatbots. Generative AI enables applications such as virtual patient companions, remote cognitive assessments via conversational agents, multimodal image-to-text tools, synthetic data augmentation, disease progression simulation, and improved caregiver communication. Challenges include model explainability, clinical validation, regulatory compliance, privacy, data bias, hallucination risk, patient autonomy, and global disparities. Responsible development requires transparent reporting, stakeholder co-design, rigorous clinical and economic validation, and continuous post-deployment monitoring to support fairness and effectiveness in real-world settings.

papers.title: Talking Technology, Not Customers: Vocabulary Decoupling in Corporate Artificial Intelligence Disclosure
papers.authors: Nicholas Harkiolakis
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely described as reshaping marketing administration through personalization, predictive analytics, and automated customer engagement. Whether firms describe AI as a customer-facing marketing capability or as a technology and a risk to be disclosed remains an open empirical question. This study uses mandated disclosure as an observational window on that question. Drawing on a balanced panel of 1100 firm-years from 100 U.S.-listed consumer-facing firms in 15 sectors (fiscal years 2015 to 2025), I measure technology vocabulary and marketing vocabulary in Form 10-K filings using phrase-presence indicators from the EDGAR full-text index and graded, section-located counts from the full text of each filing. Three findings emerge. First, AI disclosure diffused rapidly and converged: the share of firm-years disclosing rose from 28.7% in fiscal 2020 to 2022 to 91.7% in 2023 to 2025, and the intensity of AI language rose roughly twentyfold between 2021 and 2025. Second, within firms and net of common year shocks, adopting AI vocabulary was not accompanied by a substantively meaningful increase in marketing vocabulary (standardized β = 0.02, 95% CI [−0.09, 0.13]); graded and staggered-adoption estimates leave room for at most a small, lagged association. Only 3.2% of AI sentences written in 2023 to 2025 used marketing vocabulary, and AI language migrated from the Business section toward Risk Factors and MD&A. Third, first disclosure was ordered by sector, with digital-commerce and financial firms preceding hospitality and travel firms. I interpret the pattern as vocabulary decoupling: AI entered the technology-and-risk register of the annual report largely without being connected to the register in which firms account for value delivered to customers. The findings concern disclosure, not deployed capability.

papers.title: When fluency outpaces provenance: source traceability and digital health literacy against AI health misinformation
papers.authors: Mingsheng Peng, Lu Feng
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can make health explanations accessible while separating persuasive language from inspectable evidence. This creates a public health problem beyond plainly false content: an answer may mislead through unsupported attribution, obsolete evidence, omitted uncertainty, or inappropriate application. This Conceptual Analysis uses a targeted integrative approach to connect health literacy, misinformation, trust, large language model evaluation, and content provenance around the pathway from a generated claim to a health decision. Its contribution is an integration and operationalization of established concepts, not a new literacy construct or truth-certification mechanism. We distinguish five source traceability functions: origin, claim, evidentiary, procedural, and correction traceability. These functions interact with four iterative, context-dependent user practices: inspect, triangulate, calibrate, and escalate. Calibrated trust means discriminating between stronger and weaker support and relying proportionately on it, rather than maximizing or minimizing trust. Effective traceability also requires accessible, comprehensible evidence pathways and reasonable verification effort. Institutional and platform accountability is therefore part of the model, not an optional supplement to individual competence. We provide illustrative operational indicators, provisional risk-tiered safeguards, and six testable propositions organized around evidentiary discrimination, confidence calibration, decision appropriateness, verification behavior, verification burden, and escalation behavior. Neither the unified model nor its indicators or risk tiers have been empirically validated. The framework offers a decision-oriented research and design architecture for evaluating when evidence visibility and literacy can jointly support safer use of synthetic health information.

papers.title: Beyond accuracy: a three-stage evaluation of large language models for postpartum health consultation and nursing decision support
papers.authors: Xilin Zhao, Xinwen Zhang, Lei Liu
papers.abstract: Background Large language models may support postpartum health consultation and nursing care plan development, but their performance across different task types remains uncertain. This study compared the performance of ChatGPT 5.5 and DeepSeek V3 in these settings. Methods A three-stage cross-sectional evaluation was conducted, comprising repeated querying of 30 guideline-based questions, consultations involving 120 postpartum women, and 120 de-identified retrospective clinical cases. Responses were evaluated by clinical experts using a blinded assessment process. In Stage 2, the postpartum women who submitted the questions also performed blinded evaluations from the user perspective. Paired-samples t tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used, as appropriate. Holm-Bonferroni correction was applied within outcome families defined by study stage and evaluator type, and intraclass correlation coefficients were calculated to assess agreement among clinical expert ratings. Results In Stage 1, ChatGPT 5.5 received a higher correctness score than DeepSeek V3 (4.00 ± 0.00 versus 3.88 ± 0.33; Holm-adjusted p = 0.002). DeepSeek V3 received higher scores for completeness and clinical management appropriateness (both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and safety (Holm-adjusted p = 0.001), although its responses were more difficult to read. In Stage 2, ChatGPT 5.5 received higher patient ratings for satisfaction and usefulness and higher clinician ratings for correctness, completeness, helpfulness, and safety, whereas DeepSeek V3 received a higher clinician-rated readability score (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). In Stage 3, ChatGPT 5.5 received higher scores for clinical appropriateness, comprehensiveness, actionability, safety, and triage appropriateness (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), whereas DeepSeek V3 received a higher individualization score (Holm-adjusted p = 0.021). Conclusion LLM performance varied depending on the task, evaluation metric, and use case. ChatGPT 5.5 received higher scores across most clinically relevant dimensions in real-world postpartum consultations and nursing care plan generation, whereas DeepSeek V3 received higher scores for completeness and safety in standardized questions, clinician-rated readability in real-world consultations, and individualization in care-plan generation. LLMs may support health education and preparation of initial nursing care plan drafts, but their outputs require clinical review.

papers.title: Generative AI-related employment threat, AI optimism, and employment anxiety among domestic and international students at a Chinese university
papers.authors: 黄勇明, Yuyao Hu, Chunyu Ling, 廖熹晨, Xueyong Xiang, Qiujing Pan
papers.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the labor market, yet it remains unclear whether students’ appraisal of AI-driven employment threat translates into employment anxiety in similar ways across cultural groups. This study administered an online questionnaire to 1,595 domestic students (1,095) and international students (500) enrolled at Central South University. Perceived AI replacement threat, AI optimism, and employment anxiety were assessed with 13 five-point Likert items. Information channels, coping behaviors, desired institutional support, and perceived coping relief were assessed as supplementary measures. Confirmatory factor analyses supported an acceptable three-factor structure in both groups. The distinction between threat and anxiety remained qualified due to their substantial association. Metric invariance was established, and partial scalar invariance was obtained after the intercept of Q21 was freed. Perceived AI replacement threat and employment anxiety remained empirically distinguishable, although their latent correlation was stronger among international students than among domestic students. In the structural model, threat was strongly associated with anxiety ( β = 0.764) and weakly associated with optimism ( β = 0.133). After threat was included, optimism showed a small negative conditional association with anxiety ( β = −0.152). The indirect association through optimism was negative but limited in magnitude, and equivalent cross-sectional specifications fit the data equally well. This pattern is best interpreted as an exploratory statistical finding compatible with suppression, rather than confirmed evidence of a directional psychological mechanism. Supplementary coping analyses were descriptive and exploratory. These findings provide qualified empirical support for a three-factor framework of students’ responses to AI-related employment uncertainty, and highlight differences in threat-anxiety coupling across student populations. The results carry implications for targeted student support services addressing AI-related career concerns.

papers.title: Factors associated with breastfeeding difficulties in the early postpartum period in China: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Fangfang Lei, Shurong Zhou, Yuanqiong Liu, Yuanqiong Liu, Jie Xiang, Na Li, Yi Liu, Yi Liu
papers.abstract: Objective Within the unique clinical context of China, characterized by high cesarean section rates and specific postpartum practices, this study aims to investigate the prevalence and characteristics of breastfeeding difficulties in the early postpartum period (within 96 h postpartum) and identify associated factors, informing early clinical screening and targeted interventions. Methods This cross-sectional study included 460 postpartum women recruited via convenience sampling from the obstetrics department of a tertiary specialized hospital in Chengdu between July 2023 and November 2024. All assessments were conducted between 24 and 96 h postpartum. Breastfeeding difficulty was operationally defined as the clinical presence of perceived insufficient milk, nipple/breast-related problems, or neonatal factors impeding effective feeding. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Structured Clinical Breastfeeding Assessment Checklist, the LATCH scoring system, the Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy Scale-Short Form (BSES-SF), and the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Multivariate binary logistic regression was used to identify independently associated factors. Results The prevalence of breastfeeding difficulties was 38.5% (177/460). The primary clinical manifestations were perceived insufficient milk supply (63.8%) and nipple-related problems (11.3%). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that infrequent breastfeeding (< 6 times/day; OR = 3.434), gestational diabetes mellitus (OR = 1.819), elevated pre-pregnancy BMI (24.0–27.9 kg/m 2 : OR = 2.484), and elevated postpartum depressive symptoms (OR = 3.365) were independently associated with higher odds of breastfeeding difficulties (all P < 0.05). Conversely, strong family support (OR= 0.911) and higher LATCH scores (OR = 0.646) showed a significant inverse association (all P < 0.05). Conclusion Breastfeeding difficulties are common during the early postpartum period and are associated with a combination of maternal physiological conditions, feeding skills, and psychosocial factors. Elevated BMI, gestational diabetes, infrequent early sucking, and elevated postpartum depressive symptoms are key independently associated factors, whereas strong family support and good latching skills show a significant inverse association. Clinical support should prioritize early screening for high-risk women, integrating physical, skill-based, psychological, and familial support to overcome early lactation barriers.

papers.title: Socioeconomic determinants and awareness of excise tax on soft drinks in relation to nutritional status among adults in Al-Ahsa Province, Saudi Arabia
papers.authors: Randah Miqbil Alqurashi, Kawthar A. Alanezi, Samar M. Abdalla
papers.abstract: Background Soft drinks are a major contributor to overweight, obesity, and non-communicable diseases. In response, Saudi Arabia introduced an excise tax on soft drinks in 2017. However, evidence regarding public awareness of this tax and its association with socioeconomic factors, consumption behaviors, and nutritional status remains limited. Aim This study aimed to examine the association between socioeconomic determinants and awareness of the excise tax on soft drinks in relation to nutritional status among adults in Al-Ahsa Province, Saudi Arabia. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted between February and March 2023 among adults aged 18–45 years in Al-Ahsa Governorate. Data were collected using a validated electronic questionnaire covering socioeconomic characteristics, soft drink consumption, excise tax awareness, and anthropometric measures. Body mass index (BMI) was calculated using self-reported height and weight. Data analysis included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, independent t -tests, ANOVA, and Spearman correlation coefficients. Results A total of 370 participants were included. More than half of respondents (52.7%) were unaware of the excise tax on soft drinks, and 64.9% lacked knowledge of its underlying health rationale. Tax awareness was significantly associated with education level ( p = 0.02), additional income ( p = 0.02), gender ( p = 0.01), and age ( p < 0.10). While tax awareness was not significantly associated with current soft drink consumption, higher awareness was significantly correlated with reduced soft drink intake ( r = 0.213, p < 0.01), increased consumption of alternative beverages ( r = 0.117, p = 0.02), and BMI classification ( p = 0.02). However, the finding of analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) found the association between awareness of selective excise taxes and BMI was insignificant ( p = 0.86) adjusted for selected demographic, social, and economic variables. This implies that awareness of the excise tax is not related to BMI in the context of controlling demographic and socioeconomic variables for this population. Conclusion Awareness of the excise tax on soft drinks varies across socioeconomic groups and is positively associated with healthier beverage choices. However, after controlling demographic and socioeconomic characteristics, awareness of the excise tax was not significantly associated with BMI in this population. Thus, enhancing public awareness and education about the purpose and health benefits of the excise tax may strengthen its effectiveness as a public health intervention in Saudi Arabia.

papers.title: From AI labels to trust: cognitive pathways linking authenticity judgments, risk perception, and trust in AI-generated videos
papers.authors: Jiabin Fu, Yi Zhang, Shu Zhang
papers.abstract: Background The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) has raised concerns regarding the authenticity and trustworthiness of synthetic media. Although AI disclosure labels are increasingly used as transparency mechanisms, the cognitive processes through which these cues influence trust formation remain unclear. Objective This study aimed to develop and test a cognitive pathway model explaining how AI disclosure labels, authenticity judgments, perceived risk, cognitive processing styles, and literacy factors shape trust toward AI-generated videos. Methods A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 617 participants randomly assigned to four conditions involving AI-generated instructional videos with different AI label and video quality combinations. Participants evaluated authenticity, systematic and heuristic processing, trust, perceived risk, adoption intention, sharing intention, AI literacy, and media literacy. Regression, bootstrapped mediation, and moderation analyses were performed. Results AI disclosure labels significantly reduced perceived authenticity but did not directly affect trust, adoption, sharing intention, or perceived risk. Trust formation occurred through cognitive pathways: systematic processing increased trust, whereas heuristic processing reduced trust. Authenticity enhanced trust and lowered perceived risk, with perceived risk mediating the authenticity–trust relationship. Trust positively predicted adoption and sharing intentions, while AI and media literacy moderated selected relationships. Conclusion Trust in AI-generated videos was not directly determined by transparency labels alone. Instead, the observed associations among authenticity judgments, perceived risk, information processing, and trust were consistent with a multi-stage cognitive interpretation, although the cross-sectional post-exposure measurement of these constructs does not establish their temporal or causal sequence.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence use and interpersonal educational interaction among nursing students: self-regulated learning as a statistical mediator
papers.authors: Jianyun Li, Ershan Xu, Li Li, Lijuan Huang, Yan Pu, Ruirui Huang
papers.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is reshaping health sciences education. For nursing students, educational interaction (EI), self-regulated learning (SRL), and GAI interaction are all particularly important. However, these relationships and their processes remain underexplored. Methods A total of 1020 nursing students were recruited from one medical university in Hunan Province in China. The Demographics Questionnaire, the Chinese version of Student-GAI interaction scale, the Educational Interaction Scale, and the Self-regulated Learning Questionnaire were administered. SPSS 22.0 and AMOS 24.0 software were used to analyze the data. Results The mean scores of student-GAI interaction (SGI) and EI were 14.80 ± 2.27 and 70.90 ± 8.15, respectively. Significant positive relationships were found among all three variables (all P < 0.01). Both SGI (β = 0.256) and SRL (β = 0.520) positively were associated with EI (both P < 0.001). Furthermore, SGI showed a significant direct association with EI, with a direct effect value of 0.92 ( P < 0.001). SRL statistically mediated the association between SGI and EI, with a significant indirect effect value of 0.44. The mediating effect represented 32.35% of the total effect ( P < 0.001). Dimension-specific analyses revealed that the mediating effect was strongest for student-teacher interaction (45.41%) and student-content interaction (41.54%). Conclusions SGI is positively associated with EI among nursing students, both directly and indirectly through SRL. Educational strategies that encourage effective GAI use and strengthen SRL may be associated with enhanced EI in nursing education.

papers.title: Early warning and anticipatory action in intelligence governance: a case of regional Government in Riau, Indonesia
papers.authors: Jenri Salmon Ginting, Sujianto Sujianto, Muchid Albintani, Meyzi Heriyanto, Abdillah Abdillah, Saraswati Soegiharto, Siti Sofiaturrohmah
papers.abstract: Regional early warning governance has become increasingly important as multidimensional threats such as social conflict, environmental crises, and regional instability develop beyond the traditional scope of disaster management. However, regional early warning governance continues to face challenges, particularly fragmented information systems, limited local human resource capacity, weak coordination among local governments, community actors, and security forces, budget constraints, and limited public awareness. This study aims to examine regional early warning governance in Riau Province in addressing social, political, economic, environmental, and security threats and to develop an Integrated Anticipatory Intelligence Governance (IAIG) Model. While conventional early warning governance primarily focuses on detecting and communicating emerging threats, intelligence governance extends this process by integrating strategic information processing, cross-sectoral coordination, and decision-making to support anticipatory policy action. Using a qualitative case study, the study analyzes secondary documentary evidence through qualitative coding and thematic analysis, complemented by expert consultation and Ngopi-based knowledge co-creation for conceptual clarification, contextualization, and interpretive validation. The findings show that early warning governance in Riau has cross-sectoral coordination mechanisms and basic capabilities for identifying strategic threats, including agrarian conflicts, forest and land fires, social conflicts, and local political dynamics. However, fragmented information integration and sectoral coordination limit the translation of threat information into preventive and anticipatory action. The IAIG Model integrates five components: integrated threat detection, strategic intelligence processing, collaborative governance coordination, anticipatory policy response, and adaptive monitoring and feedback.

papers.title: Anti-correlation time-frequency synergy and dual-granularity fusion for sleep stage classification
papers.authors: Jie Pan, Xingxing Zhao, Xiaoyu Zou, 赵鹏军, Leilei Wang, Chengcheng Li
papers.abstract: Introduction Automated sleep stage classification is crucial for diagnosing sleep disorders and evaluating sleep quality. Single-channel EEG sleep staging using central electrodes has garnered significant interest due to its ability to detect a higher number of sleep spindles and its cost-effectiveness. Nevertheless, several challenges remain, such as the neglect of interdependencies among features, reduced model sensitivity to the dispersion across features, potential information leakage during the learning of transition rules, and class imbalance. Methods To address these challenges, this study specifically designs an automatic sleep staging network based on single-channel EEG. The network incorporates a multi-branch feature extraction module, which captures negatively correlated frequency features that exhibit significant variations during sleep transitions and promotes synergistic complementarity. Furthermore, a dual-granularity residual attention mechanism is employed to perform adaptive fusion along both temporal and channel dimensions based on statistical measures such as the mean and standard deviation. The causal transition-aware network ensures temporal consistency while facilitating effective learning of transition rules. The focal loss function is utilized to counteract class imbalance. Results Experiments on SleepEDF-20, SleepEDF-78 and SHHS datasets show that our method achieves the best performance with overall accuracy of 87.0%, 83.4% and 84.5%, respectively. For N1 stage classification which is more challenging, it reaches an accuracy of 57.5%, 52.5% and 49.3% on three datasets, respectively. Discussion The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its certain advantages over existing methods.

papers.title: EEG emotion-recognition datasets for neuroarchitecture: an appraisal of openness, AI-readiness and ontology maturity
papers.authors: Seung Yeul Ji, Mi Kyoung Kim, Han Jong Jun
papers.abstract: Introduction Neuroarchitecture studies how designed space shapes emotion, often with electroencephalography (EEG), and computational models that decode emotion from EEG must be trained on labelled recordings. Yet none of the widely shared EEG emotion datasets was recorded while people moved through designed spaces, and the few spatial recordings we found, all released since 2023, are single studies, each cited at most once. Researchers therefore borrow general emotion datasets, recorded from seated participants watching films, listening to music, playing games or conversing, and must decide whether each can be found, obtained and reused for transfer learning. This review contributes a reusable method for that decision and applies it. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 with the dataset as the unit of analysis, two search passes identified 27 publicly obtainable datasets (22 in the first, 5 in the second), none designed for spatial research. A published codebook of 52 criteria defines three instruments: openness, judged against the FAIR principles with access class recorded separately; AI-readiness, the equally weighted mean of three sub-scores (label information, fit to standard tasks and alignment with other data), which describes usefulness as a transfer source; and ontology maturity, on five levels, which describes how far emotion labels can be mapped onto other vocabularies. Every identifier and access route was checked. Results Openness was weakest in Interoperability (2.044 against a FAIR composite of 2.857), and only 8 datasets were fully open. A dataset-level identifier was missing for 13 of 27 datasets (48.1%), and three widely used datasets could not be reached through their published routes at a re-check on 11 September 2026. AI-readiness averaged 2.684 on a 1.0–4.0 scale (median 2.60, range 2.10–3.33), and ontology levels concentrated at Level 3 (16 of 27), with none at Level 4 or 5. Openness and readiness were nearly unrelated ( ρ = 0.08), whereas ontology level tracked readiness ( ρ = 0.68), partly because both read the label structure. Discussion Open access alone is therefore a poor guide to reuse. The method, codebook and scripts are published so that researchers in fields without dedicated data can test the datasets they plan to reuse.

papers.title: Between-group differences in resting-state functional connectivity within the brain’s extended triple-network following genuine and sham chiropractic adjustments: a quasi-experimental pilot trial
papers.authors: Stephanie G. B. Sullivan, Margaret Sliwka, Emily D. Drake, Tyson Michael Perez
papers.abstract: Introduction Chiropractic research has traditionally focused on subjective, pain-related outcomes; however, emerging evidence suggests that chiropractic care may also influence neurophysiological functioning. This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility of a neurophysiological assessment battery and explore differences in brain and autonomic nervous system (ANS) responses following genuine versus sham chiropractic adjustments. Methods In this pilot quasi-experimental, sham-controlled trial, 30 adults received a single session of either genuine or sham instrument-assisted chiropractic care. Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) and electrocardiography (ECG) were collected at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and one week later. Feasibility outcomes included study procedures and participant blinding. Exploratory outcomes included changes in EEG functional connectivity (FC) and heart rate variability (HRV). Results The study protocol was feasible to implement, and participant blinding was successful. Compared with sham care, genuine chiropractic care was associated with increased resting-state FC within a broadly distributed cluster spanning cortical regions of the brain’s extended triple-network, including the medial frontoparietal, dorsolateral frontoparietal, and mid-cingulo-insular networks, in the delta and theta frequency bands. No between-group differences were observed for HRV measures. Discussion These findings suggest that genuine chiropractic adjustments may differentially influence resting-state functional connectivity within large-scale brain networks compared with sham care. Although no effects on HRV were observed, the neurophysiological findings support further investigation in a fully powered randomized controlled trial to confirm these effects and determine their clinical significance. Trial registration and funding This trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05249530) and funded by Life University (Marietta, GA, USA).

papers.title: Effects of synchronous versus sequential scalp acupuncture and transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on post-stroke cognitive impairment based on multimodal assessments: a single-center randomized controlled trial protocol
papers.authors: WEI Jingyi, Xihua Liu, Zhipeng Pan, WEI Chen, WANG Ran, X Wang, MA Sai
papers.abstract: Background Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) significantly burdens individuals and society. While scalp acupuncture and transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) show promise for alleviating cognitive deficits, the optimal temporal sequence of their combined delivery remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of synchronous versus sequential delivery of scalp acupuncture and taVNS for PSCI, and explore central-peripheral neuromodulatory responses associated with intervention timing via multimodal assessment. Methods This prospective, randomized controlled trial will allocate 96 eligible PSCI patients equally into three groups. All receive conventional treatment alongside scalp acupuncture and taVNS. The synchronous group undergoes concurrent acupuncture and taVNS. Control Group 1 receives acupuncture followed by taVNS, while Control Group 2 receives taVNS followed by acupuncture. Treatments are administered once daily, 5 days per week, for 4 weeks. To assess the impact of temporal sequencing, multimodal data will be compared at baseline, week 4, and week 8 follow-up. Assessments encompass cognitive function (MoCA, MMSE), activities of daily living (MBI), neuroimaging (rs-fMRI), neuroelectrophysiology (ERP-P300), cerebral hemodynamics (TCD), and adverse events. Discussion Results are expected to evaluate the preliminary efficacy and safety of synchronous versus sequential scalp acupuncture-taVNS delivery for PSCI. Furthermore, findings may help explore the temporal dynamics of neuromodulation across brain networks, neural electrical activity, and cerebral hemodynamics, contributing to the evidence base for standardizing integrative Chinese-western cognitive rehabilitation protocols. Clinical trial registration https://www.chictr.org.cn/ , Identifier [ChiCTR2600125558].

papers.title: Effectiveness of a physical literacy intervention program for young and middle-aged adults with hypertension: a mixed-methods quasi-experimental study
papers.authors: Guiyue Ma
papers.abstract: Objective To examine whether a theoretically grounded, 8-week physical literacy intervention incorporating salutogenic model components (sense of coherence, social support, and self-efficacy) could improve physical activity levels and clinical outcomes in young and middle-aged adults with Grade 1 hypertension, and to explore participants’ subjective experiences of the program. Methods A mixed-methods quasi-experimental study was conducted between August and October 2024. Forty patients aged 18–59 years were recruited from a community healthcare center and allocated to the intervention group (n = 20) or control group (n = 20). The intervention group received a multidimensional physical-literacy program, while the control group received usual care. Five participants were lost to follow-up; 35 (intervention: n = 17; control: n = 18) completed all three assessments: baseline (T0), post-intervention (T1), and one-month follow-up (T2). Quantitative outcomes (SBP, BMI, physical-literacy scores, social support, sense of coherence, self-efficacy, and physical activity) were analyzed using independent t -tests or Mann-Whitney U tests for between-group comparisons and paired t -tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for within-group changes, with significance set at α = 0.05 (two-tailed). Qualitative data from semi-structured interviews were analyzed using inductive content analysis. Results Of the 40 recruited participants, 35 (87.5%) completed the study. Post-intervention, the intervention group demonstrated significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (SBP), body weight, and BMI compared to baseline (all P < 0.05). Significant improvements were also observed in PL scores, social support, sense of coherence, and self-efficacy ( P < 0.05). Qualitative findings corroborated these results, highlighting enhanced health literacy and stress alleviation, despite some logistical challenges. Conclusion The PL intervention is a feasible and effective strategy to improve health outcomes and psychosocial resilience in hypertensive adults, offering a promising approach for community-based chronic disease management.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled practices and management and digitalization of higher institutions in a changing world
papers.authors: Nimota Jibola Kadir Abdullahi, Bello Bolanle Muhinat, Babatunde Akanmu Isiaka, O. M. Zubair, M. S. Mubarak, Eniola Keji Ola-Alani, Lasiele Alabi Yahaya
papers.abstract: Objective of the study This study examines the influence of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled applications on the management and digitalization of higher education institutions, focusing on Pedagogical Enhancement, Data-driven Insight, and Administrative Effectiveness. Methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted, and data collected from academic and administrative staff in selected higher education institutions were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The structural model assessed the direct effects of Pedagogical Enhancement, Data-driven Insight, and Administrative Effectiveness on Management and Digitalization of Higher Institutions. Results The findings revealed that Administrative Effectiveness had the strongest and statistically significant positive association with institutional management and digitalization ( β = 0.627, p < 0.001). Pedagogical Enhancement also had a positive and statistically significant effect ( β = 0.193, p = 0.022), whereas Data-driven Insight had a positive but statistically non-significant effect ( β = 0.050, p = 0.470). The model explained 67.4% of the variance in Management and Digitalization of Higher Institutions. The findings indicate that AI-enabled administrative applications provide the strongest direct pathway to institutional digitalization, while pedagogical applications make a significant but comparatively smaller contribution. The non-significant effect of Data-driven Insight suggests that analytical capability alone may not translate into institutional transformation without adequate data governance, digital competence, institutional readiness, and the capacity to translate analytical outputs into action. Theoretical/methodological contributions The study reinforces theories on AI integration in education, demonstrating its role in improving learning experiences and operational efficiency. The findings suggest that AI-driven transformation in higher education is multidimensional and uneven, with administrative and pedagogical applications demonstrating stronger direct effects than data-driven insight. Social/managerial contributions The study recommends an integrated AI strategy that prioritises administrative process optimisation, strengthens AI-supported pedagogy, and develops the organisational capacity required to convert data-driven insights into effective institutional decisions.

papers.title: Human-AI Collaboration dalam Pembelajaran Penerjemahan Bahasa Arab: Penguatan Kompetensi, Peluang, dan Tantangan di Era Digital
papers.authors: Ali Fathurrahman, Andi Abdul Hamzah, Kamaluddin Abunawas, Baiq Raudatussolihah
papers.journal: EL-FUSHA Jurnal Bahasa Arab dan Pendidikan
papers.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the context of Arabic translation learning, particularly in how students utilize AI-generated outputs as considerations in making translation decisions. This study examines Human-AI Collaboration (HAC) among students of the Arabic Language Education Study Program at Universitas Negeri Makassar, focusing on patterns of student interaction with AI-based technologies during the translation process, the distinction between critical and passive use, the competencies that students report developing, the risks that arise, and the factors influencing their use of AI. The study employed a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through observation, semi-structured in-depth interviews, and documentation involving students and lecturers with experience in teaching the Tarjamah course. The data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, supported by coding of students’ actions and decisions throughout the translation process. The findings indicate that HAC can be considered critical when students do not merely request translations from AI but also examine, compare, evaluate, revise, or reject AI suggestions before making translation decisions. In contrast, passive use is characterized by limited verification and the direct acceptance or copying of AI-generated outputs. Critical interaction was associated with students’ reported development of linguistic awareness, digital literacy, and evaluative practices, whereas passive use posed a risk of unnoticed semantic and pragmatic errors. AI was also perceived as having limitations when used to translate expressions closely associated with cultural, literary, and religious contexts. Based on the findings of the case study, this study formulates a conceptual framework of Human-AI Collaboration for Arabic translation learning comprising AI-assisted consultation, student verification and evaluation, revision, and student decision-making, with lecturer guidance and prior academic habits serving as contextual factors. This framework is formulated on the basis of the case study findings and is not presented as a learning model that has been validated or experimentally tested.

papers.title: واقع توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في تعليم اللغة العربية: تحديات التطبيق وسبل التغلب عليها
papers.authors: Mohammed Eprahim Alnady Alphiry, Iskandi, Dody Irawan, Anna Musyarofah, Anis Shalatin Simon
papers.journal: AL-MU ARRIB JOURNAL OF ARABIC EDUCATION
papers.abstract: This research aimed to monitor the reality of employing Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies in the field of Arabic language education, identify the most prominent challenges hindering the effective application of these technologies, and provide a proposed vision to overcome them. The research adopted a descriptive-analytical approach, reviewing previous literature, studies, and available technical tools. The results revealed that the employment of AI in Arabic education is still in its early stages and suffers from a technical and linguistic gap resulting from the complexity of morphological structures and the absence of diacritics in digital texts. Furthermore, the findings indicated human challenges represented by the lack of digital readiness among teachers, and pedagogical challenges related to the rigidity of curricula. The research recommended the necessity of building massive Arabic linguistic corpora to support natural language processing (NLP), integrating computational linguistics into teacher preparation programs, and developing adaptive educational curricula that meet the needs of learners in the digital age.

papers.title: Global environmental and cardiometabolic correlates of periodontitis- ischemic heart disease co-burden: a spatiotemporal network analysis.
papers.authors: Lili Wang, Jukun Song, Xiangwen Zhou, Jiangling Sun, Yutong Yao
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Geographic co-occurrence patterns and shared risk factors between periodontitis and ischemic heart disease remain inadequately characterized globally. This study aimed to characterize country-level spatiotemporal co-burden patterns of periodontitis and ischemic heart disease, thereby helping identify regions and risk profiles in which integrated periodontal and cardiovascular prevention may be most relevant. METHODS: An ecological analysis was conducted using Global Burden of Disease 2021 data from 204 countries. Machine-learning-based feature selection was used to screen 68 risk factors. Countries were classified as concordant-burden, periodontitis-predominant, or IHD-predominant. Negative binomial regression and population attributable fractions (PAF) quantified risk contributions across 6,528 country-year observations (1990-2021). RESULTS: Periodontitis incidence (1,740.92/100,000) remained 2.2-fold higher than IHD. Analysis revealed 73 countries (35.96%) as IHD-dominant, 74 (36.45%) as periodontitis-dominant, and 56 (27.59%) with dual burdens. Elevated systolic blood pressure was the sole shared risk factor (RR 1.006-1.008). For IHD, insufficient whole grain intake showed the highest attributable fraction (PAF 6.16%), followed by elevated BMI (4.17%) and high LDL cholesterol (3.87%); kidney dysfunction had the strongest per-unit association (RR 1.111) with a PAF of 2.98%. For periodontitis, lead exposure showed the largest model-derived PAF among the assessed factors (PAF 2.36%), followed by blood pressure (2.30%) and particulate matter (1.26%). Disease-specific factors accounted for 20.55% of IHD and 4.51% of periodontitis burden. Temporal analysis revealed strong synchronization in dual-burden regions (ρ=0.901, P<0.001). CONCLUSION: Elevated blood pressure was the only shared population-level factor associated with both conditions. Kidney dysfunction and dietary factors were more strongly associated with IHD burden, whereas lead exposure and particulate matter were associated with periodontitis burden in ecological models. Geographically tailored interventions are essential: metabolic management in IHD-dominant regions and environmental remediation in periodontitis-predominant areas, particularly Eastern Europe, Central Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa. Clinically, the findings support greater attention to blood pressure and cardiometabolic risk assessment in patients with periodontitis, while emphasizing that causal links and intervention benefits require confirmation in individual-level studies.

papers.title: Interventions for enhancing digital and AI competence among university students: A narrative synthesis of empirical evidence
papers.authors: Le Hien Mai, A Nhi To
papers.abstract: Digital transformation in higher education increasingly requires university students to combine broad digital competence with emerging artificial intelligence (AI) and generative AI literacy. Yet the available evidence is heterogeneous: intervention studies coexist with psychometric validation, cross-sectional assessment, curriculum mapping, institutional analyses, and reviews of specialized applications. This narrative review synthesizes 25 publications retained from 8,072 records identified through a Web of Science Core Collection search covering 2015–2026 and completed on September 19, 2026, with particular attention to empirical interventions intended to enhance digital or AI-related competence among university students. The review addresses four questions: the types of interventions implemented; how interventions are designed, delivered, and assessed; their reported outcomes and conditions of success; and the extent to which AI literacy is integrated into broader digital competence development. Across the source set, intervention approaches include DigComp-guided teaching, AI-supported instructional models, modular competence development, blended digital/media literacy training, project-based learning, alternance training, and curriculum-level initiatives. DigComp 2.2 and related DigComp-based approaches are prominent, while the Artificial Intelligence Competence and Literacy Test (CAIA) represents a more AI-specific measurement direction. Reported intervention studies generally indicate gains in targeted competence, although the evidence base is constrained by small samples in several studies, heterogeneous designs and outcomes, reliance on self-perception in parts of the literature, and limited evidence about durability and transfer. Contextual studies further suggest that institutional support, prior AI experience, psychological readiness, self-efficacy, curriculum alignment, ethics, and critical information practices shape competence development. The synthesis indicates a transition from generic digital literacy toward integrated digital–AI competence, but the field still requires stronger intervention designs, validated performance-based assessment, explicit generative AI components, and research across diverse educational and cultural settings.

papers.title: Navigating the digital aesthetic: unpacking algorithmic biases and user perceptions in AIGC portrait generation
papers.authors: Xu Jialin
papers.journal: International Journal of Communication and Society
papers.abstract: This study aims to develop an interdisciplinary conceptual and methodological framework for examining aesthetic bias in AI-generated portraiture and understanding how such bias may be interpreted within human–AI interactions. The study adopts a simulation-based, mixed-methods proof-of-concept design that combines a rule-based simulated dataset of 6,000 portraits with simulated interview scenarios informed by existing literature on AI ethics, digital aesthetics, and human–computer interaction. The quantitative component demonstrates how a computer-vision-oriented audit framework could identify potential patterns in AI-generated portraits, including preferences for fairer skin, younger appearances, slender facial features, double eyelids, and higher beauty scores, as well as gender-related differences in smiling and head pose. The qualitative component develops three heuristic user positions, namely the Efficient Tool, Creative Dialogue Partner, and Ambient Environment, to explore how different modes of human–AI relationships may shape the perception, negotiation, and ethical interpretation of algorithmic aesthetics. The study concludes that aesthetic bias in AI-generated portraiture can be investigated through an integrated framework combining computational auditing with interpretive perspectives on user–AI relationships. Although the simulated results do not establish the prevalence or causal mechanisms of bias in actual AI systems, the proposed framework offers a structured basis for future empirical validation using real model outputs and interviews with actual users. The study's potential impact lies in advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computer vision, communication, and AI ethics, while informing the development of more transparent, culturally sensitive, and inclusive AI-generated visual content.

papers.title: School Readiness and Ethical AI Practices in Elementary Education: A Mixed Methods Study
papers.authors: Sri Marmoah, Winarno, Fery Muhammad Firdaus, Ratna Widya Irmayanti, Lastika Ary Prihandoko
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education presents both opportunities and challenges for elementary schools in establishing technology-ready and ethically responsible learning environments. This study aimed to examine school readiness and ethical AI practices in elementary education. A quantitative descriptive approach was employed involving 272 elementary school teachers as respondents. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring five dimensions of school readiness, namely technology, teacher competence, leadership, policy, and organizational support, as well as ethical AI practices encompassing data privacy, transparency, fairness, academic integrity, and pedagogical use of AI. Descriptive statistical analysis was conducted using means and percentages. The findings revealed that most teachers had already integrated AI into their teaching practices (89.7%). School readiness was generally high, as reflected in leadership (M = 4.04), technology (M = 4.03), and teacher competence (M = 3.99). However, policy (M = 3.73) and organizational support (M = 3.72) received comparatively lower scores, indicating areas requiring further improvement. Ethical AI practices demonstrated a very high level (M = 4.12), suggesting strong teacher awareness regarding data protection, transparency, fairness, academic integrity, and the responsible use of AI in educational settings. These findings indicate that elementary schools are reasonably prepared to integrate AI into teaching and learning processes. Nevertheless, stronger institutional policies and organizational support are needed to ensure the effective, ethical, secure, and sustainable implementation of AI in education.

papers.title: Inovasi DIGI-FINSMART: Pendampingan AI untuk Pengelolaan Keuangan dan Konten Pemasaran Digital pada Siswa SMK
papers.authors: R. Slamet Santoso, Diana Putri, Arifin Puji Widodo
papers.journal: Jurnal Pengabdian Masyarakat dan aplikasi Teknologi
papers.abstract: Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan literasi keuangan, kemampuan pemasaran digital, serta pemanfaatan teknologi Artificial Intelligence (AI) pada siswa SMK melalui program inovatif DIGI-FINSMART (Digital Financial Smart Student Program). Program ini dilaksanakan di SMK YP17 Pare Kabupaten Kediri dengan pendekatan partisipatif dan berbasis praktik (experiential learning). Metode pelaksanaan meliputi tahapan sosialisasi, pelatihan, pendampingan intensif, serta evaluasi melalui pre-test dan post-test. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan adanya peningkatan signifikan dalam pemahaman literasi keuangan siswa, dengan rata-rata peningkatan lebih dari 30%. Selain itu, siswa mampu menyusun laporan keuangan sederhana secara mandiri dan menunjukkan perubahan perilaku finansial yang lebih terencana. Pada aspek pemasaran digital atau digital marketing, siswa berhasil menghasilkan konten promosi kreatif yang layak dipublikasikan, sementara pemanfaatan AI membantu meningkatkan efisiensi dan kualitas output. Program ini juga mendorong perubahan pola penggunaan teknologi dari konsumtif menjadi produktif. Keterlibatan guru sebagai mitra strategis turut mendukung keberlanjutan program di lingkungan sekolah. Secara keseluruhan, DIGI-FINSMART terbukti efektif dalam meningkatkan kompetensi siswa yang relevan dengan kebutuhan era digital serta memiliki potensi untuk direplikasi pada institusi pendidikan vokasi lainnya.

papers.title: Accountability Gap Behind Predatory Publishing in Philippine Academia
papers.authors: Jeconiah Louis Dreisbach
papers.abstract: The mandate of the Philippines’ Commission on Higher Education ties faculty promotion in state universities and colleges to research publications. This commentary argues that the policy's emphasis on publication volume, unmatched by a corresponding verification mechanism, has created conditions in which predatory journals, conferences, and award bodies can thrive. Rising demand for indexed journal publications has already produced unsolicited offers to acquire legitimate, non-profit university journals, commercializing a system meant to signal quality. The threat extends beyond obviously fraudulent venues: recent evidence of paper mines (Barnett & Byrne, 2026), in which openly available datasets are mass-mined into formulaic, artificial-intelligence-assisted manuscripts that pass peer review in ostensibly legitimate journals, shows that volume-based incentives corrupt the research record even when every formal quality marker is present. Reading the Philippine case alongside this global pattern suggests that whitelisting indexed venues is necessary but insufficient. Accountability requires Philippine authorities to complement indexing criteria with a national research integrity framework, institutional verification of authorship, conference, and data provenance, and financial support that does not make ethical publishing contingent on personal wealth.

papers.title: Can AI interview? Comparing AI-led to Human-led Chat Interviews
papers.authors: Semra Guven, Tobias Priesholm Gårdhus, Andreas Bjerre-Nielsen, Anna Rogers, Hjalmar Bang Carlsen
papers.abstract: Large language model chatbots have been proposed as AI-interviewers for collecting qualitative interview data at scale, potentially bridging social science's longstanding divide between the breadth of surveys and the depth of qualitative interviews. This paper provides the first direct empirical comparison of data quality in AI-led and human-led interviews. In a randomized experiment (N = 41), university students were interviewed via synchronous text chat by either trained non-expert interviewers or a locally hosted AI system; we evaluate exposure, specificity, and relevance. Median interview duration was similar across conditions, but AI-interviewers asked more than twice as many questions per interview and elicited roughly 65 percent more respondent text per interview. Per-question responses were longer with human interviewers, though not after multiple-testing correction; only AI-condition participants skipped questions. Responses were almost uniformly on-topic in both conditions; for specificity we detect no difference, but the design cannot exclude one of up to three quarters of a point. These results were obtained with a small, locally hosted open-weight model (7B parameters), which addresses concerns about data security, GDPR compliance, and scientific reproducibility. Our findings support the viability of AI-interviewing for large-N qualitative data collection.

papers.title: Cognitive performance in young and middle-aged adults with obesity: a systematic literature review
papers.authors: Camille Sellier, Marie‐Claude Brindisi, Leopold Fezeu, Cécilia Samieri, Valentina A. Andreeva, Stéphanie Chambaron
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThis systematic review synthesizes prospective evidence on associations between obesity assessed in young or middle adulthood and subsequent cognitive performance before age 65.MethodsA comprehensive search of PubMed, PsycINFO, and Web of Science identified prospective studies comparing adults with obesity to those of normal weight and assessing cognitive performance, using validated cognitive tests. Risk of bias was evaluated using ROBINS-E, and findings were synthesized narratively.ResultsAmong 4,871 records screened, four publications representing three cohorts met the inclusion criteria. Two publications from Whitehall II reported small negative associations between obesity assessed in adulthood and global cognitive performance, whereas the MIDUS analysis found no longitudinal association for BMI. A modestly steeper 10-year decline in global cognition was reported among metabolically unhealthy adults with obesity compared with adults of normal weight in Whitehall II. Findings for executive function and memory were inconsistent and generally small. One study was judged at high risk of bias and the other three raised some concerns.ConclusionsThe available evidence is too sparse, heterogeneous, and methodologically uncertain to establish a meaningful independent association between obesity and cognitive performance before age 65. Future prospective studies should include cognitive assessment at baseline and repeated follow-up, report standardized effect estimates, use domain-specific cognitive outcomes, address confounding a priori, and assess central adiposity and metabolic health alongside BMI, particularly in younger adults.PROSPERO registration: CRD42024573250Keywords: Adults, Cognitive functions, Cohort studies, Executive functions, Obesity

papers.title: AI-Powered Prevention and Early Intervention for Stress, Depression, and Anxiety: A Randomized Clinical Trial
papers.authors: Julie Youko Anne Cachia, Xuan Zhao, Wenxi Pu, Chi Liao, Merel Keijsers, Julian De Freitas, Rebecca G. Fortgang
papers.abstract: Randomized evidence for purpose-built generative AI mental health support remains limited. In this preregistered trial, 1,137 unscreened university students were assigned to 6 weeks of a generative AI-powered mobile intervention (“Flourish”) or care as usual. Across the full sample, Flourish produced more favorable trajectories for perceived stress (β = −0.03, p = 0.010), depressive symptoms (β = −0.03, p = 0.006), and anxiety symptoms (β = −0.04, p = 0.001). Among participants with lower baseline symptoms, Flourish buffered deterioration; among those with elevated symptoms, improvements were larger with Flourish for depression (d = 1.03 vs 0.56) and anxiety (d = 0.91 vs 0.60), with meaningful improvement in 52.3% vs 31.7% and 50.6% vs 38.1%, respectively.
