papers.title: Targeted Micronutritional Support in Adults with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): A Prospective, Single-Arm Pilot Study of Hepatic Steatosis and Cardiometabolic Outcomes
papers.authors: Montserrat Argemí Relat, Sergio Abanades, Ismael San Mauro, Jordi Esquirol Caussa, Núria Capdevila Menac
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves insulin resistance, altered iron homeostasis, and oxidative stress. We explored changes in hepatic steatosis and cardiometabolic parameters following targeted micronutritional supplementation. Methods: In this prospective, single-center, open-label, single-arm pilot study, 15 adults with ultrasound-confirmed moderate-to-severe hepatic steatosis received two standardized micronutrient formulations for four months, alongside previously established dietary recommendations. No new structured weight-loss program was introduced. The pre-specified primary efficacy target was a ≥10% reduction in Fatty Liver Index (FLI). Secondary outcomes included ultrasound steatosis severity, metabolic and biochemical parameters, quality of life, and safety. Results: The primary efficacy target was not achieved. Mean FLI decreased by 2.55 points (59.18 ± 26.67 to 56.63 ± 27.48), corresponding to a 4.3% relative reduction (p = 0.256). Exploratory analyses showed a shift towards lower ultrasound-defined steatosis grades (nominal p = 0.010), with severe steatosis decreasing from 46.7% to 6.7%. BMI remained unchanged, while waist circumference decreased by 0.89 cm (p = 0.046). Fasting glucose (p = 0.033), insulin (p = 0.025), homocysteine (−23%; p = 0.001), and ferritin (p = 0.007) decreased, while transferrin saturation increased (p = 0.005). No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusions: Although the primary endpoint was not met, micronutritional support was associated with exploratory improvements in ultrasound-defined steatosis and selected cardiometabolic biomarkers. Larger controlled trials are warranted.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Financial Reporting: Transforming Customized Financial Statements, Decision Intelligence, and Assurance Practices
papers.authors: Ashif Anwar
papers.abstract: Financial statements are prepared from trial balances that have passed internal-control checks and, for external reporting, have been audited before stakeholders rely on them. Converting this verified ledger into the views needed by investors, creditors, regulators, and management remains largely manual, causing rework, delays, and duplicated reconciliation. This study designs and evaluates an artificial intelligence (AI)-coordinated architecture that generates stakeholder-specific yet reconciled reports from a single governed trial balance. Following a design science approach, the architecture combines centrally configured accounting policies and KPI definitions, lineage metadata, account classification, anomaly detection, sequence forecasting, financial natural language processing (NLP), role-aware customization, and human-in-the-loop explainable AI (XAI). The prototype was evaluated on 15,000 trial balances for 500 entities (12,000 synthetic and 3,000 derived from public SEC filings) against rule-based, robotic process automation (RPA), and commercial generative-AI baselines. It achieved a line-item disclosure fidelity (F1) of 0.965, an AUC of 0.97 for misclassification detection, and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 4.8% for one- to four-quarter forecasts; in 250 simulated multi-entity scenarios, preparer effort fell from 38.0 to 4.2 person-hours per reporting cycle. Simulated stakeholder and auditor responses illustrate the expected gains in perceived usefulness and trust. Limitations include synthetic and statement-derived data, simulated rather than observed perception measures, and an unevaluated narrative-generation module.

papers.title: Review of the Association Between Neck Circumference and Multisystem Diseases: From an Anthropometric Indicator to a Clinical Risk Marker
papers.authors: Xuefeng Huang
papers.abstract: Background: Obesity is a core risk factor for multiple chronic diseases. Adipose tissue distribution has greater predictive value for metabolic and cardiovascular risk than total fat mass. Neck circumference, a simple anthropometric indicator of upper-body subcutaneous fat accumulation, has gained increasing attention in recent years for its value in metabolic and cardiovascular risk stratification.Objective: To systematically search for and synthesize evidence on the association between neck circumference and multisystem diseases and to evaluate the evidence base and key challenges for translating neck circumference from an anthropometric indicator into a clinical risk marker.Methods: This review is a systematically searched narrative review. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched from database inception to June 30, 2026. A supplementary search was performed for 2026 articles published online after the search cutoff date. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of the association between neck circumference and disease or risk factors served as the primary evidence source and were supplemented by large prospective cohort studies and key cross-sectional studies. Case reports, small-sample uncontrolled studies, purely hypothetical articles, conference abstracts, preprints, and registered trial protocols were excluded. Evidence was synthesized narratively, and effect sizes were not pooled. The review was not prospectively registered, and no formal evidence grading was performed with tools such as GRADE. Related limitations are discussed in Section 9.1.Results: A total of 130 articles were included. Current evidence indicates that increased neck circumference is epidemiologically associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), components of metabolic syndrome (MetS), dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), atrial fibrillation, heart failure, ischemic stroke, chronic kidney disease (CKD), hyperuricemia, gout, and the risk of cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality. Associations with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), cardiac electrical remodeling, subclinical atherosclerosis, arterial stiffness, retinal microvascular changes, decline in lung function, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), coronary heart disease, cognitive impairment, and reduced brain gray matter volume have also been reported, but the evidence is weaker, inconsistent in direction, or confined to subgroups. The prognosis of hemorrhagic stroke also requires further validation. The direction of associations for geriatric and nutritional outcomes such as sarcopenia, malnutrition, and decline in activities of daily living (ADL) is inconsistent, with some studies showing risk associated with lower neck circumference; presarcopenic obesity, in contrast, is positively associated with increased neck circumference. Evidence for associations with metabolic syndrome in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus, bone mineral density, depression, and sleep quality is weak, inconsistent in direction, or confined to specific subgroups. Some associations, such as those for T2DM and hypertension, remain significant after adjustment for body mass index (BMI), and the CKD evidence is partially supportive. Evidence strength was judged comprehensively based on study design, cross-population consistency, whether associations remained significant after adjustment for BMI or waist circumference, and the availability of Mendelian randomization (MR) evidence; overall, the evidence was heterogeneous. However, neck circumference is strongly collinear with waist circumference and BMI. Some meta-analyses have shown no significant association between neck circumference and the composite MetS endpoint. The Jackson Heart Study found no independent association between neck circumference and cardiovascular outcomes after full adjustment. MR studies have shown a protective causal association between neck circumference and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), contradicting observational studies; other MR studies have not found a causal association between neck circumference and bone mineral density. Wrist circumference outperforms neck circumference in predicting insulin resistance in children, and in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus, waist circumference has a higher area under the curve (AUC) than neck circumference for predicting MetS. Causality has not yet been fully established. Genetic evidence indicates that neck circumference has a genetic basis independent of overall obesity. Intervention studies suggest that neck circumference can be changed by lifestyle interventions, but its changes are not fully synchronized with improvements in neck adipose tissue or core OSA endpoints. Evidence from nontraditional cardiovascular risk markers, mechanistic studies, studies in special populations, measurement standardization studies, and evidence on local effects in head and neck cancer has further expanded the boundaries of clinical application of neck circumference. Prospective evidence in the field of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) shows that in postmenopausal women with normal BMI, baseline neck circumference still independently predicts NAFLD incidence. Studies in young Chinese adults suggest that there are significant sex differences in the performance of neck circumference for diagnosing obesity.Conclusions: As a systematically searched narrative review, this review suggests that neck circumference is epidemiologically associated with multisystem diseases, but the strength of evidence is heterogeneous. Current evidence supports its use as an adjunctive indicator for risk screening; however, it cannot yet serve as an independent causal risk marker. Cross-disease comparisons of effect sizes are influenced by differences in indicator type, baseline risk, and follow-up duration and should not be used as a direct basis for clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Nursing Education: Perceived Barriers Among South African Nurse Educators and Nursing Students
papers.authors: Miyelani Justice Mhlongo, Agnes Makhene, Sanele E. Nene
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study investigates the perceived barriers to integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into nursing education among nurse educators and nursing students at a public higher education institution in Gauteng, South Africa. Methods: A qualitative, exploratory, descriptive, contextual design was employed. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 12 nurse educators and 28 third-year nursing students. Data collection was conducted through semi-structured interviews with nurse educators and focus group discussions with nursing students. The data were analysed thematically, utilising Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework, with the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology(UTAUT) serving as an interpretative lens. Results: Four interrelated barriers emerged: infrastructure and resource constraints; limited AI literacy and skills; resistance and readiness challenges; and governance, ethical, and regulatory concerns. These barriers collectively influenced participants' willingness and capacity to engage with AI in nursing education. Conclusions: The effective integration of AI into nursing education necessitates coordinated institutional responses that address infrastructure, AI literacy, organisational readiness, and ethical governance. Developing contextually relevant policies, ensuring equitable access to technology, providing continuous professional development, and offering appropriate technical support may foster a more conducive environment for the responsible and sustainable integration of AI into nursing education.

papers.title: Knowing When to Hand Over: A Survey of Uncertainty, Deferral, and Escalation in Human–AI Fraud Investigation
papers.authors: Kailing Fu
papers.abstract: Language-model agents are being proposed to investigate fraud and money-laundering alerts under selective autonomy: the agent closes some cases itself and escalates the rest to a human analyst. Which cases it escalates determines the division of labor, the analysts' workload, and the errors that reach customers and regulators, yet the knowledge needed to design that rule is divided among learning to defer and selective prediction, uncertainty estimation for language models, and research on human reliance on AI advice. This survey connects the three through the escalation loop of a fraud-investigation team and restates known results from these literatures in one notation. We state the cost-optimal escalation rule, which requires different confidence thresholds for closing a case as benign and for concluding fraud, and its form under a fixed analyst capacity; show that calibration suffices for selective risk to be monotone and interpretable; state the conformal bound on the rate of cases that are both closed automatically and wrong; show when combining uncertainty signals helps and when correlated signals double-count; show that the error among automatically closed cases is not identified without audits and is estimable with them; and quantify how analyst reliance on the agent's verdict erodes the value of escalation. Against this basis we compare deferral rules and uncertainty signals, and conclude that threshold-based deferral rules assume a calibrated confidence that agents do not yet provide, that agent-level uncertainty estimation is only beginning, and that, to our knowledge, no peer-reviewed study has yet evaluated an escalation rule for a fraud-investigation agent together with the analysts who receive its cases.

papers.title: Trust in AI Chatbots and Perceived Consumer Protection in Digital Commerce: Evidence from Bangladesh
papers.authors: Israt Jahan Jui, Kazi Abdul Mannan
papers.abstract: Artificial-intelligence chatbots are becoming an increasingly important interface between consumers and digital-commerce firms, yet the legal significance of trust in these systems depends on whether trust coexists with effective consumer-protection expectations. This study examines that relationship in Bangladesh using 385 usable observations from the Group 7 Q7 survey. The questionnaire was designed around AI literacy, AI-driven consumer-rights awareness, AI-chatbot trust and consumer-protection expectations, and awareness of algorithmic manipulation. Rather than imposing a conventional latent-variable model on the data, the analysis first audits measurement quality and then uses robust ordinary least squares regression and item-level diagnostics. The results show moderate-to-high mean scores across all substantive domains: AI literacy (M = 4.05), consumer-rights awareness (M = 3.91), chatbot trust/consumer protection (M = 3.97), and algorithmic-manipulation awareness (M = 3.90). However, internal consistency is weak across the supplied five-item blocks (α = 0.16–0.20), and a 20-item factorability audit is only marginal (KMO = 0.60). The indices are therefore interpreted as descriptive measures rather than validated latent scales. At the predictive level, AI literacy and algorithmic-manipulation awareness are significant positive predictors of the composite chatbot-trust/consumer-protection score, whereas consumer-rights awareness is not statistically significant at the 5% level. The disclosure-conditioned trust item shows limited evidence of association with the protection/safeguard index (B = 0.004, p = 0.858). Algorithmic-manipulation awareness has the largest positive coefficient in the protection-index model (B = 0.192, p < .001). The pattern motivates an exploratory distinction between disclosure-conditioned trust and safeguard endorsement, while low internal consistency limits broader construct-level conclusions. The study informs discussion of transparency, human escalation, business accountability and complaint mechanisms as conditions of justified reliance in AI-mediated commerce.

papers.title: The Judge Under Trial: Monte Carlo Verification of the Reasoning-Aligned Rubric Tuning Lifecycle
papers.authors: Yoothana Suansook
papers.abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) as automated evaluators—commonly termed LLM-as-a-Judge—introduces a critical vulnerability: the “right answer, wrong reason” failure mode, where a judge reaches the correct verdict through unsound reasoning that is invisible to standard label-agreement dashboards. Kong et al. [1] propose Reasoning-Aligned Rubric Tuning (RART) to address this, anchoring the judge’s rationale to human judgment via a Meta-Judge and iterative rubric refinement. This paper presents a reproducible Monte Carlo simulation (300 replicates, 40 iterations) that empirically verifies the RART lifecycle against a label-only baseline (Vanilla). We formally model the latent rubric state θ_R = (q_R, b_R), the noisy meta-judge detection layer, the biased reflector update, and the statistical drift monitor. Our results confirm the framework’s central thesis. While Vanilla achieves marginally higher final label accuracy (q_R = 0.956) than RART (q_R = 0.875), its reasoning alignment collapses entirely (b_R = −0.842), whereas RART stabilizes reasoning (b_R = +0.910). Furthermore, the simulation visually exposes the structural vulnerabilities of the framework: Vanilla consumes 2.6× the computational budget (39.4 vs 14.8 iterations) due to the stopping-rule artifact; the standard 2σ drift band produces an unacceptable 11.3% false-alarm rate at K = 3 raters; and the blind-spot leak between shared judge-generator architectures decays only when human oversight (p_H > 0) is present. The simulation serves as both a pedagogical tool and an empirical validation that the LLM judge is an amplifier of human judgment, not a replacement for it.

papers.title: AI in Education from CAI to AGI: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework
papers.authors: Miao Jiang, Hangxing Wu, Fudeng Ding, Jinqiang Wang, Feifei Shi, Huansheng Ning, Jianguo Ding
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping education, yet research remains fragmented across technological streams and often conflates technical capability with demonstrated educational effectiveness. This narrative review synthesizes representative literature published mainly between 2010 and 2026 to trace the evolution of AI-enabled education from computer-assisted instruction toward adaptive, immersive, generative, and potentially more general forms of intelligence. It compares three major technological streams: intelligent tutoring and adaptive learning systems, extended reality (XR), and large language model-based generative AI. The review finds that intelligent tutoring systems support learner modeling, adaptive feedback, and personalization, but their evidence base is methodologically heterogeneous. XR shows comparatively more consolidated evidence, particularly through systematic reviews and meta-analyses, with generally positive but context-dependent effects on engagement and learning outcomes. Generative AI expands dialogic explanation, scaffolding, content generation, and personalized support, although learner-outcome evidence remains limited relative to capability benchmarking. Building on these findings, the review proposes a Technology–Mechanism–Outcome–Challenge framework and argues that future progress toward artificial general intelligence (AGI) should be evaluated through learning mechanisms, measurable outcomes, human oversight, equity, and responsible governance.

papers.title: Non-Recognition of Online Doctoral Programs in India in the Era of AI, Education 4.0, and Education 5.0: Challenges for Working Professionals
papers.authors: Rohit Kumar Pal, Shashi Kant Gupta, Kalyan Ghosh, Sagnika Pal, Dia Salama AbdElminaam, Deema Alsekait, Abdallah Mohammad
papers.abstract: The expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) and digitally mediated learning has intensified debate about flexibility, access, and quality assurance in higher education. This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the non-recognition of fully online doctoral education in India, focusing on career barriers, psychological burnout, acceptance of Education 4.0, institutional resistance, and support for policy reform. Using a cross-sectional questionnaire dataset of 832 respondents, the study applies descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), group comparisons, and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression. The findings indicate comparatively high mean scores for perceived career barriers and Education 4.0 acceptance. Group comparisons did not identify statistically significant differences across the categories examined. The overall regression model was statistically significant (F(7, 824) = 64.28, p < 0.001; R² = 0.353; adjusted R² = 0.348). Institutional resistance was positively associated with policy-reform support, whereas career barriers showed a smaller negative association. Education 4.0 acceptance also showed a positive association with reform support. These findings represent statistical relationships within the sample and do not establish causal effects. The study contributes to discussions on Indian higher-education policy by outlining considerations for a quality-assured framework that addresses research supervision, assessment, academic integrity, institutional accountability, and equitable access to doctoral education.

papers.title: Implementation of ChatGPT-Assisted Problem-Based Learning with a Deep Learning Approach on Students’ Scientific Literacy in Global Warming
papers.authors: Shera Rahmawati Magfiroh, Ratna Sari Siti Aisyah, Irah Namirah
papers.abstract: This study examined the implementation of ChatGPT-assisted Problem-Based Learning (PBL) with a Deep Learning approach in global warming instruction and analyzed changes in students’ scientific literacy before and after the intervention. A pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was used with 30 students in Class X-1 at SMA Negeri 5 Kota Serang during the 2025/2026 academic year. The research instruments consisted of instructional materials, a 22-item scientific literacy test that had passed content and empirical validation, and an observation sheet. Descriptive statistics and a paired-sample t-test were used to analyze the test data, while observation data were summarized as percentages across scientific knowledge, context, science competencies, and science identity. The mean scientific literacy score increased from 76.36 on the pretest to 85.60 on the posttest, and the paired-sample t-test showed a statistically significant difference, t(29) = -6.925, p < .001. Observation results also showed higher percentages in all four scientific literacy aspects during the second learning session. These findings indicate positive changes in students’ scientific literacy following the intervention; however, because the study did not include a comparison group, the changes cannot be attributed exclusively to the intervention.

papers.title: Evaluating Prompt Engineering for Large Language Models-Based Translation
papers.authors: Novriyanto Napu, Moon Hidayati Otoluwa, Hanisah Hanafi, Muhamad Hardiyanto Kiyai Mardjo
papers.journal: The International Journal of Technology Knowledge and Society
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have introduced new possibilities for machine translation (MT) by allowing translation outputs to be shaped through natural-language instructions. However, evidence about how different prompt configurations affect translation quality relative to established neural machine translation (NMT) systems remains limited, particularly for Indonesian–English translation. This exploratory mixed-methods comparative study examines three prompt configurations applied to ChatGPT and compares the resulting outputs with DeepL and Google Translate across six tourism, promotional, and proverbial texts. Translation outputs were assessed computationally using cross-lingual cosine similarity from text-embedding-3-large as an exploratory indicator of semantic proximity and qualitatively through evaluations by three professional translators focusing on accuracy, appropriateness, naturalness, and discourse style. In the observed sample, DeepL and the baseline-prompt condition tended to obtain higher similarity scores for factual tourism texts, whereas contextual- and persona-prompt outputs received comparatively favorable expert evaluations in selected promotional and culturally embedded cases. Contextual prompting also produced additions beyond the wording shown in the source excerpts, indicating a trade-off between rhetorical adaptation and source fidelity. Because the corpus is small, the prompt conditions bundle several instructional features, repeated generations were not documented, and some reproducibility metadata were not archived, the findings are interpreted descriptively rather than as causal or statistically generalizable effects. The study therefore highlights a genre- and criterion-sensitive relationship among prompt configuration, semantic preservation, and functional translation quality, while underscoring the need for human verification of adaptive LLM translations.

papers.title: INTRAOPERATIVE ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHIC MONITORING AS A PREDICTIVE TOOL FOR POSTOPERATIVE DELIRIUM: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW
papers.authors: Teófilo Augusto Araújo Tiradentes, Fernando Souza Sampaio, Carolina Farah Flores, Lorena Vieira Lopes, Marina Cardoso Mazzetto, Kendra Lohana Saldanha Araoz, Marina Ferrari, Gustavo Moreira Garcia, Matheus Olímpio Batista Cavalcante, João Manoel Guilherme Alves, Guilherme Gomes Romano, Vitória Alencar Pereira, Altair Martins Barasuol, Julia Fernandes Ribas, Ana Elisa Paulucci, Gabriel Bomfim dos Reis, Ana Luiza de Souza, Rodolfo de Oliveira Medeiros
papers.journal: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
papers.abstract: Introduction: Postoperative delirium is a common neuropsychiatric complication in older adults undergoing intermediate- and high-risk surgery, and it is associated with longer hospital stays, cognitive decline, and increased mortality. Because the intraoperative electroencephalogram records cortical activity directly during anesthesia, it has been investigated as a source of markers capable of identifying vulnerable patients at an early stage. Objective: To analyze the scientific evidence on the use of intraoperative electroencephalographic monitoring as a predictive tool for postoperative delirium in adults and older adults undergoing surgery under general anesthesia. Method: An integrative literature review was conducted, grounded in the principles of evidence-based practice. The review question was structured using the PICo strategy. Searches were carried out in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and LILACS databases. Included studies were characterized in terms of their methodological design and level of evidence, and the findings were subjected to interpretive thematic synthesis. Results: Twelve studies were included. Burst suppression and prolonged electroencephalographic suppression were consistently associated with delirium, and the duration of suppression proved to be the most informative parameter. Reduced frontal alpha power and emergence trajectories lacking spindle activity pointed to lower cerebral reserve. Machine learning models combining clinical and electroencephalographic variables achieved moderate to good discriminative performance. Trials that used the electroencephalogram to guide anesthetic depth, however, did not show a consistent reduction in the incidence of delirium. Conclusion: Intraoperative electroencephalographic monitoring has prognostic value as a marker of cerebral vulnerability, but current evidence does not support its isolated use as a preventive strategy. Its main usefulness appears to lie in risk stratification, combined with preoperative cognitive assessment, validated multivariable prediction models, and multicomponent prevention measures in the postoperative period.

papers.title: Cognitive and Creative Transformation in AI-Augmented Work: Rethinking Skills, Decision-Making and Value Creation in Marketing Practice
papers.authors: Tom Stables, Marcello Trovati
papers.journal: University of Salford Institutional Repository (University of Salford)
papers.abstract: The literature on generative AI in marketing frames the technology primarily as an operational productivity tool, leaving the cognitive and professional dimensions of AI-mediated work significantly undertheorised. This paper addresses that gap through a semantic network analysis of 1,540 Scopus abstracts, using a local large language model to extract semantic triplets and yielding 6,727 relationships from the 1,156 papers from which extractable triplets were identified. The dominant relationship verbs are augments, requires, and improves; prompt engineering appears in only 32 triplets and human judgement in just two, confirming the operational bias the paper identifies. On this basis, the paper makes two contributions. It demonstrates the extent to which the existing literature neglects the cognitive, epistemic, and professional dimensions of AI-augmented work. It then offers a conceptual framework identifying three emerging competencies as central to competent AI-augmented marketing practice: prompt engineering, evaluative literacy, and the meta-regulation of AI use.

papers.title: Is AI Productivity Mediated by User Skill? Prompting Skill, Subject Knowledge, and Human Capital in AI-Assisted Knowledge Production
papers.authors: Christoph Bierbrauer
papers.journal: University of Salford Institutional Repository (University of Salford)
papers.abstract: Generative AI is often treated as if output quality were a model property alone. We propose that AI-assisted outputs are the outcome of a joint production process driven by the AI system, subject knowledge, and prompting skill. Using 278 prompt-level observations from classroom experiments, we test a model-agnostic production function across two regimes: one where students prompt AI cold, and another where they first solve tasks independently. AI-assisted performance exceeds independently produced solutions on average. Stronger participants retain an absolute advantage, while AI-assisted performance is compressed relative to unaided performance.Efficient prompting as well as subject knowledge are productive, yet our empirical estimates cannot reject the hypothesis that they enter the production function for AI outputs as independent inputs. Our results suggest AI may compress performance gaps in relative terms but preserve them in absolute terms, challenging the narrative about AI as either a great equalizer or a skill-biased accelerant of inequality.

papers.title: Study-level data and R code for a three-level meta-analysis of AI chatbot effects on L2 learners‘ motivation, willingness to communicate, self-efficacy, and anxiety
papers.authors: Ruobing Qin, Tairong Kang, Jiang Yan
papers.abstract: This repository contains the extracted study-level data and R code supporting the meta-analysis, “The effects of AI chatbots on L2 learners’ motivation, willingness to communicate, self-efficacy, and anxiety: A three-level meta-analysis.” The dataset comprises 55 effect sizes from 37 studies, including randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies. The input files contain experimental- and comparison-group sample sizes, means and standard deviations, outcome classifications, moderator coding, effect-direction information, and overall risk-of-bias ratings. Separate files provide the parameters used to calculate five baseline-adjusted effects from three quasi-experimental studies and the domain-level risk-of-bias ratings for all included studies. Effect sizes represent immediate-posttest between-group comparisons and are expressed as Hedges’ g, with positive values indicating higher motivation, willingness to communicate and self-efficacy, or reduced anxiety. The R scripts reproduce effect-size calculations, the joint four-construct correlated and hierarchical effects (CHE) model with study-clustered CR2 inference, eleven moderator analyses, sensitivity analyses, heterogeneity and publication-bias diagnostics, model comparisons, and figures. The scripts are numbered in execution order. After extracting the archive, set the working directory to the R_code_and_data folder and run “00-Run All.R”. The code was verified using R 4.6.1. Required packages include metafor, clubSandwich, PublicationBias and svglite, together with their dependencies. All analyses use group-level summary statistics extracted from the included publications.

papers.title: Sex differences in empathy generalize across pain domains but are shaped by social context
papers.authors: Xiaoyun Li
papers.abstract: Behavioral and EEG-derived data, EEG processing and feature extraction scripts, and statistical analysis code accompanying research on sex differences in empathy across pain domains and social interaction.

papers.title: Trust and judgment in human- and AI-labeled information: Behavioral data
papers.authors: Hyunwoong Lee
papers.abstract: De-identified behavioral data (trust, judgment accuracy, judgment time) supporting the article "A comparative analysis of trust and judgment in human- and AI-labeled information: Evidence from behavioral and neural measures".

papers.title: Investigating the Interaction Between Generative AI and Critical Thinking in Higher Education: A Systematic Review-Supplementary Materials
papers.authors: Ajda Osifo, Ahmed Imran
papers.abstract: This repository contains supplementary tables and supporting materials accompanying the paper “Investigating the Interaction Between Generative AI and Critical Thinking in Higher Education: A Systematic Review” by Ajda Osifo and Ahmed Imran, accepted for presentation and publication at ICDTE 2026 in Okayama, Japan.

papers.title: Acting with machines: a systematic review and meta-analysis of the sense of agency in human-artificial agent interaction (retrospective registration)
papers.authors: Martina Nicole Modesti
papers.abstract: RETROSPECTIVE REGISTRATION. This registration is submitted after completion of the review. The protocol was prepared on 18 October 2026, after title/abstract screening and before full-text screening, data extraction and analysis, but was not registered at that time. The registration reproduces that protocol; deviations from it are disclosed in the attached document and in the corresponding fields. Systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental studies comparing the sense of agency (implicit: intentional/temporal binding; explicit: judgments of agency, control and authorship) when adults act or decide together with an artificial agent (robot, autonomous virtual agent, computer partner, AI advisor, chatbot/LLM) versus acting alone or with a human partner. Authors: Martina Nicole Modesti, Antonio Del Casale, Stefano Ferracuti (Sapienza University of Rome).

papers.title: Decisive Test of the Physical Invariant I(S) through Experimental Dissociation between Integration (Phi) and Workspace Access (W_GW) within the Q Framework
papers.authors: Angel Jose Toranzo Portela
papers.abstract: This study provides a decisive empirical test of the Q Framework's central falsifiable prediction: that phenomenal structure depends on the complete physical invariant I(S) = (Phi, C, A, W, R), not on integrated information (Phi) alone. Using a 2x2 within-subject design, we orthogonally manipulate integration (Phi, measured via TMS-EEG perturbational complexity) and global workspace access (W_GW, manipulated via stimulus visibility/masking), while holding attention (A) constant across all conditions. The critical comparison is between Condition A (high Phi, high W_GW) and Condition B (high Phi, low W_GW): if phenomenal reports differ systematically despite matched integration, the integration-only model is falsified and the full Q invariant gains support. Phenomenal reports (intensity, confidence, seen/not-seen) are analyzed with nested likelihood-ratio models: M0 (integration only) vs M1 (additive access) vs M2 (Phi x W_GW interaction). This pre-registration is frozen prior to data collection. Any exploratory analysis not specified here is declared a satellite hypothesis (Section 15.2 of the Q Framework v3.2) and cannot affect the status of the Q functor or its core derivations. Reference: Toranzo Portela, A. J. (2026). A Categorical Functorial Framework for Phenomenal Structure in Open Physical Systems (v3.2).

papers.title: AI Detection and Academic Report Analysis
papers.authors: Johannes J. Fahrenfort, Elsje van Bergen, Dennis van ‘t Ent, Matthias Nau, Bruno Sauce
papers.abstract: The primary objective of this project is to determine whether the validity of written coursework as an indicator of individual skill acquisition has changed across cohorts spanning the broad availability of generative AI in research methods in the social sciences (Psychology, Pedagogics). To this end, a data processing pipeline will evaluate pseudonymized student-written research reports from the course Research Methods 2 (BA level) across five academic years: 2021-2022, 2022-2023, 2023-2024, 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 using an AI detection platform (i.e. Pangram). By breaking down research report submissions into isolated, verified academic sections (Abstract, Introduction, Method, Results, and Discussion) and stripping all Personally Identifiable Information (PII), the project achieves section-level AI detection benchmarking. In the analysis, AI detection scores for all report sections will be compared across pre-LLM (Large Language Model) and post-LLM cohorts, and used to determine to what extent they moderate any covariation between report grades and exam grades across cohorts.

papers.title: Experience in the implementation of a comprehensive non-pharmacological therapeutic program at the Center for Cognitive and Psycho-Emotional Health
papers.authors: Vsevolod Vadimovich Belousov, Yu.S. Gureeva, R. T. Tairova, Anna Nicolaevna Bogolepova, E. A. Gileva, Е. А. Коваленко, Ekaterina Vladimirovna Makhnovich
papers.journal: S S Korsakov Journal of Neurology and Psychiatry
papers.abstract: Objective. To analyze the outcomes of a complex non-pharmacological treatment regimen administered to patients at the daytime hospital (DH) of the Center for Cognitive and Psycho-Emotional Health (CCPH) and to evaluate the changes in the cognitive and psycho-emotional state of the patients. Material and methods. The study included 103 patients attending the CCPH DH, with a mean age of 46.98±14.32 years; 76.7% were female. Participants were categorized into three distinct groups: Group 1 with predominantly cognitive impairments (CIs), Group 2 with predominantly psycho-emotional disorders, and Group 3 with sleep disorders. Cognitive and psycho-emotional statuses were assessed using widely accepted tests and assessment scales. Each participant underwent a tailored five-day course of non-pharmacological therapy, which integrated cognitive training, biofeedback-based electroencephalography training, physical therapy, and neurostimulation techniques. Treatment outcomes were assessed after the intervention. Results. Following the therapeutic intervention, 91.26% of participants demonstrated clinical improvement, with the greatest improvement observed in Group 2 (96.6%). No deterioration in clinical status was noted among any of the patients, thereby affirming the safety of the therapeutic interventions. Neuropsychological test results indicated a statistically significant improvement across all three groups (p<0.05), reflected in enhanced cognitive metrics and a reduction in anxiety and depressive symptoms among patients with pre-dementia CIs, anxiety disorders, and chronic insomnia. While a tendency towards improvement was noted in patients with severe ICs, the changes did not reach statistical significance, particularly in patients with isolated depressive disorders, potentially due to the limited sample size. Moreover, patients within Group 3 showed improvements in sleep during the therapy. Conclusions. The findings suggest that a five-day non-pharmacological intervention with an integrated approach represents an effective and safe method for the maintenance and enhancement of cognitive and psycho-emotional health.

papers.title: Neurocognitive characteristics in children with sluggish cognitive tempo
papers.authors: Leonid Semenovich Chutko, Elena A. Yakovenko, S Yu Surushkina, Лариса Васильевна Щеглова
papers.journal: S S Korsakov Journal of Neurology and Psychiatry
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the neurocognitive characteristics of children diagnosed with sluggish cognitive tempo (SCT) and to evaluate the efficacy of Cortexin in addressing this condition. MATERIAL AND METHODS: The main study group included 40 children aged 12 to 14 years with symptoms consistent with SCT manifestations. The comparison group consisted of 30 children with combined ADHD (ADHD-C), also aged 12 to 14 years. The control group comprised 30 children in the same age range without any neuropsychiatric disorders. The study used several methods, including S. Lee's SCT scale for assessing the severity of SCT symptoms, the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI-20), the Daytime Sleepiness Scale, and T.A. Fotekova and T.V. Akhutina's reading skills assessment method, the «Working Memory» method to quantifying working memory capabilities, the TOVA computer test, and EEG (routine and spectral analysis). Cortexin was administered intramuscularly at a standard dosage of 10 mg every other day across 10 injections to patients diagnosed with SCT. RESULTS: The study results showed that children with SCT, in comparison to their counterparts with ADHD-C and healthy peers, exhibited significantly more pronounced asthenic symptoms and a higher prevalence of comorbid learning disorders. Quantitative EEG analysis revealed a reduced theta-to-alpha wave power ratio in the anterior cerebral cortex of the SCT group compared with the ADHD cohort. These findings support the hypothesis that children with SCT are less prone to exhibiting deficits in inhibition processes, while instead demonstrating a decline in overall levels of functional activity maintenance. A follow-up assessment after treatment revealed improvements in inattention, severity of working memory impairment, asthenic symptoms, and reading skills in 82% of cases. Additionally, EEG analysis post-treatment indicated a reduction in alpha-band power in the frontal and central leads of both hemispheres, suggesting enhanced overall cortical activation. CONCLUSION: This study has delineated several cognitive characteristics associated with SCT in children and demonstrated that administering Cortexin significantly alleviates the primary symptoms of SCT and mitigates the manifestation of major comorbid disorders.

papers.title: Leveraging AI for Higher Education Human Resources:A Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Maria Elena Veronica, Wendi Usino, Arief Wibowo
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human Resource Development (HRD) policies for academic staff in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) is often constrained by the misalignment between computational capabilities and institutional governance. While HEIs generate substantial datasets through the Tri Dharma (the three pillars of higher education: teaching, research, and community service), this data remains underutilized for proactive policy-making. To map the state-of-the-art and identify existing research gaps, this study conducts a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis of 400 unique peer-reviewed documents, obtained from an initial 485 records retrieved from Scopus (n = 260) and Web of Science (n = 225) after removing 85 duplicates, covering the seven-year period from 2018 to 2024. Visual analysis using VOSviewer reveals a distinct semantic-policy discrepancy, showing that semantic technologies and predictive AI models are researched as isolated technical domains, seldom integrated into comprehensive institutional governance. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a framework for Higher Education Human Resources for Lecturer Career Development. The proposed framework integrates machine learning classifiers (Naïve Bayes, K-Means, and Apriori association) with a semantic Knowledge Graph layer to transform descriptive academic metrics into explainable, policy-conforming recommendations. Preliminary expert consultation with LLDIKTI Region II highlights the conceptual viability of the Framework for Higher Education Human Resources for Lecturer Career Development in mitigating administrative bottlenecks, supporting objective career path design, and minimizing human subjectivity in lecturer performance evaluations.

papers.title: Reassessing the Fair Use Doctrine in the Age of AI: Evaluating Bad Faith and Market Harm through Bartz v. Anthropic and Kadrey et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc.
papers.authors: Adelė Rusnė Dziegoraitytė, Eglė Zdanavičiūtė, Paulius Jurčys
papers.abstract: This paper examines how the fair use doctrine applies to large language model (LLM) training by analyzing Bartz v. Anthropic and Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc. LLMs such as “Claude’’ and “Llama’’, generate text from large datasets, raising novel copyright questions. In Bartz, lawfully acquired works were used fairly, while pirated copies weighed against fair use. In Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc., Meta’s use of unauthorized sources was deemed transformative and fair, highlighting inconsistent treatment of bad faith. Regarding market harm, courts focused on direct substitution but largely ignored broader effects such as market dilution or long-term impacts on creative markets. The paper agrees that fair use doctrine must evolve with technology, proposing a fifth factor focused on the legality of AI training sources and greater attention to market dilution and long-term economic harm to creators.

papers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence in Digital Pathology for Urological Applications: A Comprehensive Review
papers.authors: Kinju Adhikari, Talyshinskii Ali, Lingesh Chelliah, Deepak Krishnappa, Ravi Taori, Ankit Joshi, Aadhar Jain, Karthika Rani, S. K. Raghunath
papers.journal: British journal of healthcare and medical research
papers.abstract: Purpose: To conduct a scoping review of the literature identifying clinical scenarios for the use of digital pathology (DP) in urology, its advantages, and obstacles to clinical adoption. Material and Methods: A comprehensive literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar databases. Search terms included “digital pathology,” “artificial intelligence,” “urology,” “whole slide imaging,” “telepathology,” and “pathology diagnostics.” The PubMed/MEDLINE search yielded 173 articles; supplementary Google Scholar searches and reference-list screening broadened the scope. Inclusion criteria required peer-reviewed studies or reviews addressing AI or DP in a urological context. Studies lacking clinical relevance to genitourinary pathology were excluded. The search strategy and selection process are summarized in Figure 1. Results: In urological pathology, DP enables three-dimensional (3D) pathomorphological reconstruction, improves the accuracy of grading and staging, facilitates intraoperative real-time slice assessment, supports specialist training, and allows large-scale information storage—opening new horizons in telepathology. Artificial intelligence algorithms, difficult to apply in classical light microscopy, offer further significant prospects for pathologists. Despite these advantages, limitations including high equipment costs, large image file sizes, server dependency, data privacy concerns, and the need for specialist training continue to slow widespread adoption. Conclusion: DP empowers urologists, pathologists, and healthcare professionals with tools to achieve more precise diagnoses, personalize treatments, and deliver a new standard of patient care. While challenges accompany this digital transformation, the potential benefits are profound and far-reaching. Future efforts should prioritize standardization, regulatory approval, ethical frameworks, and training to accelerate clinical adoption.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence, ESG Disclosure Quality, and Corporate Sustainability Performance in Islamic Banking: The Role of Sharia Governance
papers.authors: Mutmainah _, Melinda Wijaya
papers.journal: Journal of Economics Business and Accountancy Ventura
papers.abstract: This study examines the relationships among Artificial Intelligence (AI), ESG Disclosure Quality (ESGDQ), Greenwashing, and Corporate Sustainability Performance (CSP), and investigates the moderating role of Sharia Governance in Islamic banking. The study employs a quantitative explanatory design using panel data from Islamic commercial banks in Indonesia and Malaysia during the 2021–2025 period. The study collected data from annual reports, sustainability reports, corporate governance reports, official corporate websites, and other publicly available disclosures through structured content analysis and disclosure-based indices. The hypotheses were tested using a fixed-effects panel regression model. The findings indicate that disclosed AI capability and implementation are positively associated with ESG Disclosure Quality, while AI is not significantly associated with Greenwashing. ESG Disclosure Quality is positively associated with Corporate Sustainability Performance, whereas Greenwashing is not significantly associated with sustainability performance. Sharia Governance strengthens the positive relationship between AI and ESG Disclosure Quality but does not significantly moderate the relationship between AI and Greenwashing. These findings highlight the importance of integrating technological capabilities with Sharia Governance to support more credible, transparent, and responsible sustainability reporting practices in Islamic banking.

papers.title: Transparency, accountability, and scholarly integrity: A systematic narrative review of artificial intelligence governance frameworks in healthcare publication
papers.authors: Amina Silva, Bruna Canever, Monica  Lino, Vanessa Silva e Silva
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare research and scholarly publication has produced a rapidly expanding but fragmented ecosystem of reporting guidelines, governance frameworks, editorial policies, and regulatory instruments, imposing significant burdens on researchers, reviewers, and editors. This systematic narrative review identified, stratified, and synthesized governance frameworks and reporting standards addressing transparent and ethical AI use in healthcare publications, and characterized the governance trajectory from predictive model standards to generative AI oversight. Fourteen Boolean search strings were executed in PubMed (MEDLINE) covering 1 January 2018-19 May 2026, supplemented by manual searching of the EQUATOR Network guideline library. Records were deduplicated and prioritized using a relevance-scoring algorithm. Of 30,276 deduplicated records, 888 progressed to human screening; 100 publications were included, comprising 69 governance instruments and policies classified across four evidence tiers and 31 contextual evidence sources. Included sources spanned six thematic groups: predictive and diagnostic AI frameworks (G1); sociotechnical and lifecycle governance (G2); generative AI and LLM-specific standards (G3); specialty-specific extensions (G4); surgical reporting updates (G5); and editorial and publication policy (G6). Analysis identified four consecutive phases of governance development from 2018 to 2026, characterized by a shift from model performance transparency toward comprehensive sociotechnical accountability. Three governance tensions emerged: the trade-off between framework specificity and universal applicability; the gap between disclosure-focused standards and lifecycle governance; and the risk of epistemic conflation, whereby heterogeneous instruments are perceived as carrying equivalent authority when treated as interchangeable. AI governance in healthcare publications remains fragmented and epistemically uneven. Advancing the field requires harmonization across evidence tiers, adaptive updating mechanisms, and lifecycle-oriented governance frameworks.

papers.title: Development of AI-Based Chatbot for Information Services at SMK Negeri 1 Sumedang
papers.authors: Ruli Faitsal, Lilis Widaningsih
papers.abstract: This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbot to improve communication and academic information management at SMK Negeri 1 Sumedang. Using the Rapid Application Development (RAD) methodology, the chatbot automated the delivery of schedules, announcements, and institutional information. The system integrated n8n workflow automation, a Supabase database, the WAHA API for WhatsApp communication, and natural language processing to handle user queries dynamically. Evaluation results showed strong performance, achieving 92% response accuracy with an average response time of less than one minute. Stress testing under high-concurrency conditions revealed slight performance degradation, particularly in processing informal language and handling peak user traffic. Future improvements include implementing Redis-based asynchronous queueing and server load balancing to enhance scalability. Overall, the chatbot reduced dependence on manual information dissemination, accelerated communication, and established a responsive digital ecosystem that benefits students, teachers, administrative staff, and parents.

papers.title: Global Trends in AI Research in Vocational Education: A Bibliometric Analysis 2020–2025
papers.authors: Wawan Eko Putra, Ade Gafar Abdullah, Saripudin Saripudin
papers.abstract: This study systematically maps the global development of research on the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in vocational education through bibliometric analysis. Using the Scopus database, 426 publications from 2020–2025 were analysed with Bibliometrix and VOSviewer. The findings indicate rapid publication growth, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 40.7%, particularly during 2024–2025. Conference papers accounted for 44.3% of publications, suggesting that the field remains in an exploratory stage. China led research output with 160 publications (37.6%), while the United States and India achieved higher citation impact per article. Four major research clusters were identified: Teaching and Learning, Technology Integration, Skills Development, and AI Methods. The Skills Development cluster emerged as a key research frontier, focusing on personnel training, employment, and competency-based assessment. Significant research gaps remain, including limited empirical impact studies, insufficient contextual research in developing countries, and the need for more systematic investigations of AI-based assessment of practical vocational skills.

papers.title: Integration Sustainable Fashion Learning in Vocational Education: a Systematic Study Literature 2019–2025
papers.authors: Asri Andarini Nurlita, Muslikhin Muslikhin
papers.abstract: This systematic literature review examined the integration of sustainable fashion education into vocational education between 2019 and 2025 using the PRISMA 2020 framework and Publish or Perish 8 to search Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar. From 665 identified publications, 88 studies met the inclusion criteria. The review found that sustainability is effectively integrated through Project-Based Learning, Challenge-Based Learning, Studio-Based Learning, digital learning, and artificial intelligence. Four core sustainability competencies emerged: cognitive, affective, behavioural, and transformative competence. Successful implementation depends on innovative pedagogies, institutional commitment, and strong industry collaboration. Although sustainable fashion education is expanding globally, major regional disparities persist in infrastructure, teacher capacity, and standardized competency assessment. The findings emphasize the importance of curriculum redesign, enhanced partnerships between vocational institutions and industry, and greater adoption of digital technologies to develop graduates with sustainability competencies, innovation skills, and the ability to drive change.

papers.title: Unpacking AI-powered versatile robotics for agile production: An interdisciplinary sociotechnical analysis
papers.authors: Michail A Mitsouridis, Evangelos Genitsaris, Prodromos Gkalimanis, Maximilien Naveau, Vladimír Petrík, Nicolas Mansard
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered versatile robotics can support agile manufacturing through adaptive task execution, multi-tasking, reconfiguration and continuous skill acquisition. However, successful deployment in industrial environments depends not only on technical performance, but also on workforce acceptance, trustworthy AI governance, interoperability with existing systems and compliance with evolving European requirements for safe and human-centric AI. This paper presents an interdisciplinary sociotechnical analysis of AI-powered versatile robotics for agile production, developed in the context of the Horizon Europe AGIMUS project. Methods A mixed-methods research design combined desk research, semi-structured interviews with 22 technical, industrial and ethics experts, industrial pilot case studies, and an online survey of 180 respondents from 16 European countries. The survey was conducted in March 2023. Given the rapid evolution of AI regulation, industrial robotics and generative AI-enabled human-robot interaction since then, the survey results are interpreted as a time-specific baseline rather than a real-time measurement of current market attitudes. Results The findings show that reliability, maintainability, increased accuracy, and adaptability were the most critical technical needs for industrial uptake, while technical robustness and safety, privacy and data governance, and transparency were comparatively difficult to achieve. Potential workforce resistance was associated primarily with job-security and role-identity concerns: fear of job loss, changes in work routines and perceived devaluation of human labour were stronger opposition factors than physical safety concerns. Acceptance measures receiving the strongest support included clear communication of operational changes, educational and training programmes, workforce-retention plans, and comprehensive briefing on the scope of robotics implementation. Conclusions The paper contributes a baseline framework for design, piloting and governance of trustworthy, human-centric, and industrially feasible robotic systems. Its practical value lies in combining technical requirements with ethical, organisational, and temporal interpretation criteria, supporting AGIMUS development and longitudinal assessment of AI-powered robotics adoption.

papers.title: Using AI Conversations for Challenging Clinical Encounters: A Brief Review
papers.authors: Rita Maher Wassef, Daniel Meehan
papers.abstract: Background Teaching communication skills in healthcare is challenging, particularly when preparing students for emotionally complex clinical encounters. Role-play is widely used but can be resource-intensive to organise, especially when professional actors are required. Effective communication underpins quality healthcare and patient safety by supporting meaningful patient participation, better clinical outcomes, and patient satisfaction. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) simulations can reproduce human response and offer a flexible, safe environment for practice; however, their effectiveness in communication skills teaching remains underexplored. This study aims to explore students’ perceptions of using AI role-play conversations in communication skills teaching. Methods In this exploratory qualitative study informed by an interpretivist approach, Physician Associate students engaged in three structured AI role-play conversations: smoking cessation counselling, breaking bad news, and telephone consultation. These exercises were introduced via Blackboard, following clinical skills sessions. Afterwards, students reflected and provided qualitative feedback. Debriefing by a facilitator was held at the end of each session to share insights, discuss communication choices, explore emotional responses to challenging scenarios, and identify both strengths and areas for growth. Reflections were analysed through a process of qualitative thematic analysis. Results Students appreciated the opportunity to practice independently and without judgment, they reported finding it easier than practising with a peer and enjoyed the opportunity to practice in their own space and own time. They valued the usefulness of this tool to develop empathy, although some found it challenging to maintain empathy in the virtual environment. It also helped them reflect on their individual learning and how to structure and refine their communication skills. Overall, students found these exercises beneficial. Conclusion AI role-play conversations may reduce anxiety and build confidence by revisiting challenging conversations. They represent a promising, scalable, accessible platform for developing communication skills. Successful implementation should consider contextual factors including technological infrastructure and facilitator support.

papers.title: Analysing Mathematical Communication between Pre-Service Mathematics Teachers and GenAI: A Case Study in Abstract Algebra Course
papers.authors: Elah Nurlaelah, Tia Purniati, Bill Chairy Rizki Bustaren, I Made Suarsana, Made Juniantari, Irianto Irianto
papers.abstract: Background The emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), particularly ChatGPT, offers new possibilities for mathematics learning in higher education. Although ChatGPT can provide explanations, examples, guiding questions, and feedback, its use in Abstract Algebra courses has largely been limited to answering questions and verifying mathematical answers or proofs. This study analyses pre-service mathematics teachers’ mathematical communication when interacting with ChatGPT through seven indicators, including: interpreting formal definitions; using mathematical terms, symbols, variables, and notation appropriately; constructing examples, non-examples, and counter-examples; explaining relationships between algebraic objects and their properties; justifying arguments or proofs; evaluating the validity of mathematical responses; and formulating coherent conclusions. Method A qualitative case study involved 18 pre-service mathematics teachers enrolled in an Abstract Algebra course in the department of mathematics education at a public university in Bandung City, West Java, Indonesia. Data comprised written dialogues between the pre-service mathematics teachers and ChatGPT while solving Abstract Algebra problems and were analysed using the seven indicators. Results The findings indicate that the pre-service mathematics teachers’ mathematical communication generally ranged from developing to adequate. They performed relatively well in using terminology and notation, constructing examples or counter-examples, and explaining relationships among algebraic objects and properties. However, justification, critical evaluation of ChatGPT responses, and independent conclusion-making remained weak. While some pre-service mathematics teachers accepted inaccurate AI responses, others identified and connected them. Conclusion The findings suggest that GenAI should serve as a dialogue partner and scaffolding, rather than an authority on mathematical truth. Mathematics course should emphasise verification, justification, critical evaluation, and argument reconstruction to foster independent mathematical communication skills.

papers.title: Autism: epidemiology, genetics, molecular mechanisms, clinical features, diagnosis, and management
papers.authors: Ruonan Fan, Yilin Wang, Tingting Miao
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors. Global prevalence has risen steadily, yet reported rates vary markedly across regions and populations. These discrepancies reflect inequities in diagnostic access and screening capacity rather than true differences in incidence. This review integrates recent advances across the full ASD research spectrum. We first examine global epidemiological patterns and demographic disparities. We then dissect the genetic architecture of ASD, including rare and common variants, copy number variations, and gene-environment interactions that disrupt prenatal and early postnatal brain development. At the molecular level, diverse risk factors converge on shared neurodevelopmental mechanisms. These include synaptic dysfunction, dysregulated signaling through mTOR, Ras-ERK-MAPK, Wnt and Notch pathways, impaired neurogenesis, chronic neuroimmune inflammation, and excitatory-inhibitory imbalance. We also discuss how these mechanisms manifest in core clinical features, including social deficits, repetitive behaviors, and sensory abnormalities. We summarize current diagnostic standards and their limitations. Cross-species animal models, from Drosophila to non-human primates, are evaluated for their essential roles in mechanistic validation and therapeutic screening. Finally, we assess clinical management strategies, ranging from behavioral and educational interventions to pharmacological and supportive services. By tracing a continuous path from risk factors at the population level through molecular pathophysiology to interventions guided by mechanism, this review offers an integrative synthesis that connects basic discovery to clinical translation. We further discuss how multi-omics and artificial intelligence may advance precise diagnosis rooted in mechanism and personalized treatment.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence literacy and technology acceptance model-related constructs among first-year nursing students: a multi-institutional cross-sectional network analysis
papers.authors: Yingying Wang, Yingxin Zhao, Lianhua Li, 余以游, Liqun Zhu, Shaoyong Ma, Zhengxia Yang
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence literacy is increasingly important in nursing education, but it remains unclear how its dimensions relate to three constructs related to the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM): perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use (PEU) and attitudes toward artificial intelligence (ATU). This study aimed to examine these relationships and to identify factors associated with artificial intelligence literacy. Methods A multi-institutional cross-sectional study surveyed first-year nursing students at six undergraduate institutions in one province of China from 20 April to 1 May 2026. Of 375 questionnaire submissions, 362 met the quality-control criteria and were analysed (analytic retention rate: 96.5%). Separate item-level confirmatory factor analyses evaluated the four-factor literacy structure and the distinctiveness of PU, PEU and ATU. Group comparisons and multivariable regression with heteroscedasticity-robust inference examined correlates of overall artificial intelligence literacy; Pearson correlations described pairwise associations. A regularised partial correlation network mapped conditional relationships, centrality and bridge connectivity among seven dimension-mean nodes: knowledge, skills, values, ethics, PU, PEU and ATU. Between-institution differences, clustering and robustness of pooled findings were assessed. Results In the fully adjusted multivariable model, more frequent artificial intelligence use, prior artificial intelligence education and interest in artificial intelligence were positively associated with the mean artificial intelligence literacy score. The four-factor model showed good fit and strong item loadings; skills and values were highly correlated. Measurement analyses supported PU, PEU and ATU as correlated but distinguishable constructs. Of 21 potential network edges, 17 were non-zero. Skills had the highest expected influence and PU the highest strength. One-step bridge rankings were partition-dependent: values ranked first under the primary two-community partition and PU under the alternative four-community partition; PEU ranked second in both. Bootstrap diagnostics supported strong stability of strength and expected influence under case removal (CS(cor = 0.7) = 0.751 for both). Intraclass correlation estimates were near zero; institution-adjusted analyses preserved the main regression and network findings. Conclusions Artificial intelligence use frequency, prior artificial intelligence education and interest were positively associated with artificial intelligence literacy. Skills, perceived usefulness, values and perceived ease of use may inform hypotheses for prospective evaluation of artificial intelligence education in undergraduate nursing programmes.

papers.title: De-Sludging High-Friction Frontlines: Designing an AI-Mediated Service Gateway for Mental Health
papers.authors: Yi Tang, Kingshuk Kanti Sinha, Adam Moen
papers.abstract: Nearly one billion people suffer from mental disorders globally, yet 35 to 85 percent receive no treatment even when services are available, affordable, and known to them. This paradox suggests that the primary barrier to utilization is not only structural supply failure but also behavioral friction at the mental health service entry threshold. Drawing on sludge theory and administrative burden research, we conceptualize these barriers as service sludge—cognitive, emotional, and process frictions preventing vulnerable consumers from crossing the threshold. We adopt a design science research methodology and design MyMatcher, an AI-mediated service gateway—a pre-encounter frontline entity comprising three modules: a sensing engine that infers clinical intent from vernacular distress language, a low automated social presence (ASP) chatbot designed to reduce the social risk of disclosure, and a provider-matching module that collapses provider search into a curated shortlist. Through diagnostic and evaluative interviews with mental health practitioners, complemented by classification validation on a labeled corpus of over 4,000 texts, we derive three design principles and three research propositions for de-sludging high-friction service frontlines. Theoretically, we extend the 3A (Affordability, Access, and Awareness) framework by introducing Agency as a fourth behavioral dimension; we introduce the service gateway as a pre-encounter entity distinct from augmentation and substitution models; and we theorize an inversion of intimacy, the proposition that lower ASP facilitates sensitive disclosure in stigma-laden contexts, which qualifies a central assumption in service technology research. The framework is designed to generalize beyond mental health to high-stigma, high-complexity domains where behavioral frictions prevent consumers from acting on structural access to relevant services.

papers.title: Musical Giftedness in Human-AI Creation: Interpreting Evidence Beyond the Finished Product
papers.authors: Isidoro García-Díaz
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence complicates a central problem in identifying musical giftedness: deciding which features of an outcome can reasonably be attributed to the student who presents it. A piece may display coherent formal design, an elaborate harmonic plan, idiomatic instrumentation, or convincing timbral balance even when those decisions were neither made nor understood by the learner. This conceptual article examines how music co-created with AI can be interpreted when the finished product no longer reveals the student’s contribution on its own. Drawing on research on musical talent development, AI-assisted creation, and assessment validity, it considers three sources of information: compositional problem framing, analytical listening and revision, and the traceability of musical decisions. Transfer across tasks provides a further check. These sources are not diagnostic criteria. They are intended to support more cautious interpretations of musical evidence in AI-mediated creative work and to complement broader developmental evidence used in identification processes.

papers.title: Africana Studies Priorities in Technology and Research: Change, Reinvention, and Google Books Ngram
papers.authors: Christel N. Temple
papers.abstract: This introduction to the Special Issue on Africana Digital Technologies offers a popular culture technology survey of the 1980s to the present to capture the average humanistic social scientist’s view of technology. Relying on a methodology that layers autoethnographical data with an applied case study of the subfield of comparative Black literature, this study isolates how Google Books Ngram is a useful technology for revisionist research. Its ongoing digitization of previously uncatalogued, unsearchable, and/or unavailable scholarship is a newer resource for research and revision that permits us to generate more accurate intellectual genealogies. This introductory essay chronicles key technology concerns on the culture’s social radar over the past nearly fifty years, culminating with our contemporary understanding of Africana frameworks of artificial intelligence (AI) and groundbreaking technologies in the digital humanities. This essay acknowledges the new technological landscapes that challenge us to expand our skillset and critical worldview through new curiosities, ambitions, and competencies that will mold Africana Studies into an even more comprehensive discipline. The goal is to ensure that Africana Studies’ sometimes overlooked subject area of science and technology becomes a foundational and integrated part of the discipline’s 21st century’s curriculum, maintained by stable Africana faculty lines in this area and by routinely merging technological practices with the field’s standard, core content.

papers.title: The Human-AI Collaborative Library Model for Supporting Teaching, Learning, and Research in Teacher Education
papers.authors: Eesha Sharma, Adit Gupta
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping teaching, learning, and research practices across higher education, and academic libraries are no exception. Increasingly positioned as intelligent, collaborative environments rather than static repositories, libraries are being called upon to integrate AI-driven tools while safeguarding the professional judgement, ethical guidance, and pedagogical mentoring that only librarians provide. Teacher education institutions present a particularly urgent context for this shift, since the pre-service teachers they train will themselves determine how AI is used in future classrooms. However, existing scholarship on AI in academic libraries remains concentrated on adoption rates, technology acceptance, and AI literacy, with comparatively little conceptual attention paid to how librarians and AI systems might function as structured, complementary partners within teacher education specifically. This conceptual paper addresses that gap by proposing the Human-AI Collaborative Library Model (HACLM), a five-dimensional framework comprising Human Expertise, AI Capabilities, Collaborative Library Services, Institutional Support, and Enhanced Educational Outcomes. Drawing on six complementary theoretical and conceptual perspectives—including human-AI complementarity, socio-technical systems theory, collaborative learning theory, knowledge management theory, the TPACK framework, and the ACRL Framework for Information Literacy for Higher Education—the model positions librarians as AI facilitators, research partners, and learning designers who mediate between intelligent technologies and the ethical, critical, and pedagogical demands of teacher preparation. The paper discusses practical implications for libraries, institutions, librarians, and faculty, and proposes directions for future empirical validation, offering both a theoretical contribution to library and information science and a practical foundation for teacher education libraries navigating the AI era.

papers.title: “It feels like hard work trying to talk to it”: Understanding How Older Adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) Experience and Repair Interactional and Conversational Breakdowns with Voice Assistants (VAs)
papers.authors: Niharika Mathur, Tamara Zubatiy, Agata Rozga, Elizabeth D. Mynatt
papers.abstract: Designing Conversational AI systems to support older adults with MCI necessitates robustness in handling complex and personalized interactions. In this study, we investigate how older adults with MCI experience, navigate and attempt to repair breakdowns while interacting with a voice-based AI system in their homes for medication management through the lens of interactional ”seams”. Through a 20-week in-home deployment with 7 participant dyads, we analyzed 844 interactions to identify interactional and conversational breakdowns and user repair strategies. Drawing on post-deployment interviews, we reflect on the nature of these breakdowns and older adults’ experiences of mitigating them. We further illustrate how older adults draw on their situated knowledge and environment to make sense of and recover from these disruptions, highlighting the cognitive effort required in doing so. Our findings emphasize the collaborative nature of interaction in human-AI contexts, and point to the need for voice assistants to better align with users’ expectations for memory, their routines and external resources in their environment. We conclude by discussing opportunities for voice assistants to integrate contextual knowledge from older adults’ sociotechnical environment and to facilitate more meaningful and user-centered interactions.

papers.title: Understanding community questions about HIV pre‐exposure prophylaxis ( PrEP ): A thematic analysis of reddit threads to inform development of an AI chatbot for PrEP education
papers.authors: Vincent Alexandar, William Wood, Catia Marzolini, Justin Chiong, Daryl Hodge, Sara Gibbons, Daniel Seddon, Jasmine Martin, Saye Khoo, Lauren E. Waker
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite growing availability of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), many potential users turn to online forums for advice and information collection. These forums provide a window into real-world questions, concerns and misinformation. They serve as a tool for users to query for sensitive information without revealing their identities. These platforms could therefore be a potential source of understanding of the unmet needs of users. This study systematically analyses the social media posts referring to the four drugs mentioned in the study to identify common questions and thematic concerns among the community and uses this insight to inform the design of an AI-driven, privacy-preserving chatbot for PrEP education based on evidence.
