METHODS: Between May 2011 to October 2025, we found 1168 relevant Reddit posts mentioning one of the four names for PrEP therapies, by either brand or generic name: Truvada (Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate + emtricitabine (TDF/FTC)), Descovy (Tenofovir alafenamide + emtricitabine (TAF/FTC)), Apretude (long-acting cabotegravir), Yeztugo (lenacapavir) using a systematic search. We used Natural Language processing (NLP) techniques to understand user needs. RESULTS: Seven distinct discussion themes were identified within PrEP social media discourse, with side effects emerging as the most frequently discussed primary topic among 1076 posts. Across all medications, weight changes were the most frequently mentioned side effect. Truvada was the most frequently discussed PrEP medication. 96.7% of the dataset comprised questions, showing that Reddit serves as a primary information-seeking platform. Early period discussions were emphasized basic access and effectiveness questions, with more recent discussions (2022-2025) displaying increased attention to injectable and long-term safety considerations. CONCLUSIONS: Reddit users demonstrate persistent uncertainty about PrEP side effects, drug interactions and medication switching. Drug interactions represented the most frequently identified information gap (26.5% of posts). These empirically derived information needs will inform the design of a privacy-preserving PrEP chatbot trained on authoritative UK sources (hiv-druginteractions.org, BHIVA guidelines, NHS resources).

papers.title: Generative AI as a team moderator in CSCL : Facilitating students' multidimensional engagement through adaptive scaffolding for socially shared regulation of learning
papers.authors: Dengkang Chen, Yi Zhang, Heng Luo, Fucheng Guo, Yijie Lu, Xiao-Ge Guo
papers.abstract: Abstract Socially shared regulation of learning (SSRL) is essential for successful collaboration, yet effectively scaffolding it remains challenging because regulatory needs are dynamic and context‐dependent. While generative AI (GenAI) offers potential for adaptive support, current applications in collaborative learning largely position it as a content‐oriented tutor for knowledge explanation or idea generation, leaving its role as a process‐oriented team moderator for scaffolding SSRL processes underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a 16‐week quasi‐experiment with 64 undergraduates in China, comparing adaptive SSRL scaffolding delivered by a GenAI agent in the adaptive‐SSRL condition with static scaffolding via structured digital worksheets in the static‐SSRL condition. Survey data and group discussion transcripts were analysed using statistical methods and epistemic network analysis. Results indicated several differences in students' multidimensional engagement between the two conditions: (1) Behaviourally, the adaptive‐SSRL group showed significantly higher participation equality, although participation intensity did not differ significantly between groups. (2) Cognitively, the adaptive‐SSRL group demonstrated deeper cognitive engagement, reflected in more advanced cognitive presence phases and more integrative, solution‐oriented discourse patterns. (3) Emotionally, the adaptive‐SSRL group reported significantly higher overall emotional engagement, particularly feeling more relaxed during collaboration and more connected with peers. These findings extend human–AI collaboration research by showing that GenAI can function as an SSRL‐informed team moderator rather than a content‐oriented tutor. They also offer design implications for GenAI‐enabled adaptive SSRL scaffolding and human–AI role division in CSCL. Practitioner notes What is already known about this topic Socially shared regulation of learning (SSRL) is critical for successful collaboration and is closely associated with the quality of student engagement. While static scaffolds (eg, worksheets) provide a basic regulatory structure, they fail to adapt to the dynamic and emergent needs of collaborating teams. Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly used for personalised content support, yet its potential as a process‐oriented team moderator remains underexplored. What this paper adds This study introduced SSRLAgent, a GenAI agent grounded in SSRL theory and established principles of collective metacognitive support, to provide adaptive and interactive regulatory scaffolding. In a 16‐week quasi‐experiment, we compared GenAI‐enabled adaptive SSRL scaffolding (SSRLAgent) with static scaffolding (structured digital worksheets) in CSCL. Adaptive‐SSRL scaffolding was associated with higher‐quality engagement: greater participation equality, deeper cognitive engagement and higher overall emotional engagement. Implications for practice and/or policy The study underscores the necessity of shifting SSRL scaffolding from static, ‘one‐size‐fits‐all’ support to adaptive GenAI interventions to improve collaborative engagement. The findings provide design guidance for developing SSRL agents that are embedded in the shared interaction space and responsive to groups' moment‐to‐moment regulatory needs. The study suggests a productive human–AI division of labour: GenAI agents can support process coordination and regulatory prompting, while teachers and peers remain essential for relationally complex forms of support that collaborative learning requires.

papers.title: The effect of text–picture consistency on memory integration in college students: Evidence from ERPs
papers.authors: Wen Jia, Keke Wang, Xiaomei Zhao
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In multimedia learning, individuals often need to integrate textual and visual information. The neural mechanisms underlying how consistency between text and pictures affects memory integration remain unclear. AIM: To examine the effect of text-picture consistency on memory integration in college students and to determine the processing time at which this effect occurs. SAMPLE: = 21.64 ± 2.30) participated in this experiment. METHODS: An adapted pictorial demonstration paradigm was employed. Participants sequentially learned two pairs of text-picture stem facts (consistent vs. inconsistent), separated by an interval, followed by a recognition test for stem and integrated facts. Behavioural and event-related potential (ERP) data were recorded simultaneously. RESULTS: Under the text-picture consistency condition, college students showed significantly better memory integration performance than under the inconsistency condition (58% vs. 48%). EEG results showed that the text-picture inconsistency condition (i.e., the picture and text within a single stem fact were semantically mismatched) elicited a larger P600 wave (500-800 ms) than the text-picture consistency condition, suggesting that text-picture inconsistency primarily induces conflict and integration difficulties during late cognitive processing. No significant differences were observed in the early N400 component. CONCLUSION: Text-picture consistency facilitates memory integration primarily during late processing, aligning with cognitive theories of multimedia learning. Educationally, it serves as a key quality indicator for multimedia material design. Instructors should prioritize semantic alignment and assess knowledge integration during evaluation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence literacy, self‐efficacy and acceptance among nutrition and dietetics students, practitioners and academics: A cross‐sectional structural equation modelling study
papers.authors: Ayşe Nur SONGÜR BOZDAĞ, Firdevs Bengü Büyükdereci, Hatice Nur Artan
papers.abstract: AIM: To examine how artificial intelligence literacy, self-efficacy and perceptions and attitudes relate to artificial intelligence acceptance among nutrition and dietetics students, practising dietitians and academics in Türkiye. METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was administered to 317 participants (98 undergraduate students, 139 dietitians, 80 academics) between February and August 2025 using validated scales. The model was tested with partial least squares structural equation modelling (5,000 bootstrap subsamples), specific indirect effects for mediation, and measurement invariance with permutation-based multi-group analysis. RESULTS: The model explained 56.4% of the variance in artificial intelligence acceptance. Positive perceptions and attitudes showed the strongest association with acceptance (β = 0.577, 95% confidence interval 0.399 to 0.725), whereas negative perceptions were unrelated to it (β = -0.026, p = 0.509). Artificial intelligence literacy was strongly linked to self-efficacy (β = 0.580) and related to acceptance largely indirectly (68.7% of its total effect), mainly through positive perceptions and self-efficacy. Self-efficacy was also associated with higher acceptance (β = 0.191) and weaker negative perceptions (β = -0.328). No structural path differed across the three groups after correction for multiple testing. CONCLUSIONS: Acceptance was associated less with negative perceptions than with artificial intelligence literacy, which related to acceptance through favourable perceptions and self-efficacy. Training combining hands-on artificial intelligence literacy with critical appraisal of artificial intelligence outputs may support informed adoption across career stages.

papers.title: Prompting the archive: evaluating GenAI for primary source discovery in reference services
papers.authors: Kristen Coan Howard, Sandy Hervieux
papers.abstract: Purpose Primary source discovery is among the most demanding forms of reference work. This paper investigates whether generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools can find reliable and relevant primary sources, how effectively they summarize them and whether they can provide ethical access and enable discovery, to establish what reference librarians can responsibly recommend. Design/methodology/approach The authors tested four generative AI tools at free, institutionally provided and paid access levels, querying each with 20 prompts based on undergraduate history topics. A grading rubric framed by the Guidelines for Primary Source Literacy was used to assess primary source status, availability, summary, topic appropriateness and citation. Findings No tool hallucinated; all sources recommended by the tested generative AI tools existed. Overall, the tools performed well on topic appropriateness and adequately in citations, but some struggled to provide accessible sources and summaries. Research limitations/implications Because models evolve continuously and prior interactions may bias output, the study is not strictly reproducible, though the rubric and prompt set can be reused. Practical implications The findings support a reallocation of professional attention rather than a displacement of it. Librarians can recommend generative AI as a discovery venue alongside traditional search methods, and redirect reference and instruction time to what the tools neglect. Originality/value This is one of the first studies to evaluate generative AI tools for primary source discovery, and it separates discovery from the analytical skills that follow it.

papers.title: Academic integrity and artificial intelligence in initial teacher education: a documentary audit of teaching guides in Spanish universities
papers.authors: María Vallespir Adillón, Rubén Comas Forgas, Mercè Morey-López, Eva-María Espiñeira-Bellón
papers.abstract: Purpose Universities are increasingly adopting institutional policies on academic integrity (AcI) and artificial intelligence (AI), but it remains unclear whether these expectations are translated coherently into the course-level documents that govern students’ learning and assessment. This article therefore examines how AcI and AI, including generative AI (GenAI), are articulated in official teaching guides for Spain’s Master’s Degree in Teacher Training, and whether guidance is embedded coherently across course design. Design/methodology/approach A documentary content analysis was conducted on 254 publicly available guides from 68 universities. Explicit AcI and AI references were coded across objectives, competencies, learning outcomes, activities and assessment. Two formative diagnostic indices measured breadth of coverage across these five sections. Mann–Whitney tests compared university and subject types; 25% of the corpus was independently double-coded. Findings AcI was mentioned in 53.5% of guides but was concentrated in assessment and competencies; 46.5% contained no valid reference. Explicit AI guidance remained marginal (6.3%) and primarily assessment-centred. Private universities showed slightly broader AcI coverage, public universities slightly broader AI coverage and Final Master’s Project guides substantially broader AcI coverage. Research limitations/implications The indices measure documentary breadth, not the quality, depth or implementation of guidance, and guides are nested within universities. Practical implications Programme leaders should integrate task-specific integrity and AI expectations across outcomes, activities, assessment, disclosure and formative support, with attention to future teachers’ professional AI literacy. Originality/value The study provides a large-scale, programme-specific audit and a transparent method for benchmarking cross-sectional curricular integration without treating document coverage as a quality score.

papers.title: When do consumers respond to ASMR-based retail advertising in Taiwan? The boundary role of ASMR responsiveness
papers.authors: Chih‐Chin Liang, Chien‐Ming Chen, Jin-Yu Chen
papers.journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines how Taiwanese consumers respond to autonomous sensory meridian response (ASMR)-based retail advertising. It proposes a bounded sensory-affective persuasion framework in which ASMR responsiveness functions as a consumer-level boundary condition, rather than assuming that ASMR cues are universally persuasive. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 626 Taiwanese consumers were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. A separate within-subject EEG pilot experiment involving 18 participants was used only as a supplementary physiological check on frontal α-band patterns during advertising exposure; repeated trials were treated as within-participant observations, not as an enlarged participant-level sample. Findings Affective mechanism and brand awareness positively predicted purchase intention, which in turn predicted anticipated purchase behavior. ASMR responsiveness negatively moderated the relationship between affective mechanism and purchase intention, indicating attenuation rather than reversal of the positive effect. The cognitive-load-based moderated moderation was not supported. The EEG pilot showed no statistically significant omnibus effects of cognitive load, ASMR exposure, or their interaction on frontal a activity. Accordingly, the EEG component is interpreted cautiously as supplementary descriptive context rather than as confirmatory evidence. Originality/value The study advances sensory marketing and Asia-Pacific retail advertising research by showing that consumer responses to ASMR-based retail advertising in Taiwan depend on individual ASMR responsiveness and on whether sensory-affective experiences are converted into purchase-related evaluation.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Midwifery Workforce Development
papers.authors: Fiona Gibb, Aurora Constantin, Robin L. Hill
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly explored across health care for clinical decision-making and education. Within digital health, workforce readiness and digital capability are recognized as critical to successful technology implementation. Midwifery faces persistent workforce challenges including limited protected learning time, restricted leadership development opportunities, and unclear career pathways, yet it is unclear whether generative AI has been examined as a tool to support midwifery workforce development. A scoping review was conducted following the framework of Arksey and O'Malley with PRISMA-ScR reporting. EBSCOhost (CINAHL, MEDLINE, ERIC), Google Scholar, and Elicit were searched for English-language studies published between 2015 and 2026 examining AI in midwifery in relation to at least one of the following: post-registration education, workforce, professional development, leadership, and career progression. Findings were synthesized using framework analysis. Eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Research focused predominantly on clinical decision-making, predictive models, and undergraduate education. No studies examined generative AI tools to support practicing midwives' professional development, leadership, or career progression. Attitudes towards AI varied with digital literacy, generational cohort, and ethical concerns. Generative AI in midwifery workforce development is unexamined in the empirical literature. Further research is required to understand acceptability, risks, and value within an ethically governed implementation framework.

papers.title: Statistical analysis and Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Mark Weatherall
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-related publications are becoming more frequent in the journal. Although this was not a systematic review, and was limited only to this journal, from January 2026 until July 2026 there were six publications, in press or paginated, identified by a text search of the journal website for ‘AI’ in the title. These publications covered AI for teaching in medical education [1], clinical reasoning [2], generating multiple-choice questions in medical education [3], for competency-based medical education [4], generating scientific abstracts [5], and generating peer-review reports of scientific papers [6]. Large language models and related forms of AI may revolutionize knowledge development, dissemination, and related scientific processes. One of these processes is the statistical analysis of clinical and associated data. Functions of statistical analysis include, but are not limited to, description, estimation, prediction, inference about causality, process control, and hypothesis generation. By data is meant a collection of measured values, variables, that can be ordered by individual or a hierarchy of grouping structures of individuals. Data can be conventionally described as categories (nominal), ordered categories (ordinal), interval data where the distance between values is meaningful, and ratio data where the ratio of two numbers has a meaning. This typology of data is from Stevens’. It was originally used to describe mathematical properties of these data types called ‘invariance’. By this is meant that the information associated with each variable doesn’t change when the variable undergoes a transformation. For example, for a categorical variable originally described as ‘Yes’ or ‘No’, the same information is present if it is described as ‘Red’ and ‘Green’. For ratio data, such as height, the same information is present if it is expressed by a simple transformation, e.g. height expressed as centimetres or inches. The scale of measurement is usually associated with generally recognized appropriate analysis approaches that respect this invariance. For example, in linear regression it is generally not appropriate to compare nominal variables because the coefficients reflect a change in response per unit change in predictor but there is no sense of a unit of change for categories. As an example, in a linear regression where, say, weight is predicted by height, the response variable could be expressed in kilograms or pounds. The regression coefficient will be change in weight in kilograms per unit change in predictor or change in weight in pounds per unit change in predictor, and the values of the regression coefficients will be different. However, the P-value for the regression and the amount of variability explained by the regression, the R-squared, will be the same. The same simple transformation, of 2.2 pounds per kilogram, will, when multiplied out for the regression coefficients, give the identical result. Similarly, the continuous predictor here could be measured in centimetres or inches with a simple transformation converting one to another also applying to the regression coefficients. This is an example where the statistical method respects invariance to simple transformations from one scale to another. Respect for data types, and this invariance to simple transformations, is often an inbuilt feature of statistical software. Namely, an error is reported when attempting to perform linear regression with a categorical response variable. It is possible, however, to bypass these data analysis checks. A categorical response variable can be recoded as a simple number with only two values, and linear regression will then ‘work’. For example, a response variable could be male or female sex, but coded as two simple numbers, but there is no sense of a unit change in sex, per unit change in predictor; and statistical assumptions regarding linear regression, such as normality or the error function (residuals), are unlikely to be met. The regression coefficients will not be meaningful or rendered meaningful by a simple transformation.

papers.title: Emergent Connections: A Community-Based Model for Advancing Social Connection Among Immigrant Older Adults with Disabilities
papers.authors: Laurent Reyes, Lizette Suarez
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Social isolation is an urgent public health concern, especially for older immigrants who face heightened barriers to social participation due to disability, structural health inequities, and limited access to culturally and linguistically appropriate services. This study presents a programmatic model that explains how social connection and sustained participation can be fostered through accessible, culturally responsive, and participatory design. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This community-engaged case study examines a national virtual program serving Spanish-speaking older adults, many of whom have sensory disabilities and chronic illnesses. A thematic and comparative analysis was conducted using qualitative interviews with ten older adults with vision impairment, program documents, and consultation with program leadership. This led to the identification of a programmatic model, the emergent connections platform. RESULTS: The emergent connections platform strengthens loosely connected social networks among older adults who share cultural and lived experiences through three pillars. The first is cultural, linguistic, and physically accessible infrastructure. Second, shared governance cultivates member leadership and program co-creation. Third, a flexible structure allows for evolution in response to member needs and innovations. These pillars collectively create pathways for individuals to engage, lead, and strengthen their communities. DISCUSSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Advancing a more inclusive democracy requires sustained investment in accessible, community-led initiatives that support the leadership and innovation of marginalized older adults. This calls for moving towards models that position older adults as co-creators of programs and services. Doing so cultivates social connection through leadership, reciprocity, and a sense of belonging within a broader social fabric.

papers.title: ADHDeepNet: An Explainable Framework for EEG-Based ADHD Detection From Raw Signals
papers.authors: Ali Amini, Mohammad Alijanpour Shalmani, Behnam Latifi, Ali Motie Nasrabadi
papers.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common brain disorder in children that can persist into adulthood, affecting social, academic, and career life. Early diagnosis is crucial for managing these impacts on patients and the healthcare system but is often labor-intensive and time-consuming. This paper presents a novel method to improve ADHD diagnosis precision and timeliness by leveraging Deep Learning (DL) approaches and electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. We introduce ADHDeepNet, a deep learning model that utilizes comprehensive temporal-spatial characterization, attention modules, and explainability techniques optimized for EEG signals. ADHDeepNet integrates feature extraction and refinement processes to enhance ADHD diagnosis. The model was trained and validated on a dataset of 121 participants (61 ADHD, 60 Healthy Controls), employing nested cross-validation for robust performance. The proposed two-stage methodology uses a 10-fold cross-subject validation strategy. Initially, each iteration optimizes the model's hyper-parameters with inner 2-fold cross-validation. Then, Additive Gaussian Noise (AGN) with various standard deviations and magnification levels is applied for data augmentation. ADHDeepNet achieved 100% sensitivity and 99.17% accuracy in classifying ADHD/HC subjects. To clarify model explainability and identify key brain regions and frequency bands for ADHD diagnosis, we analyzed the learned weights and activation patterns of the model's primary layers. Additionally, t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) visualized high-dimensional data, aiding in interpreting the model's decisions. This study highlights the potential of deep learning and EEG in enhancing ADHD diagnosis accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Delineating neural contributions to electroencephalogram-based speech decoding
papers.authors: Motoshige Sato, Eri Hatakeyama, Masakazu Inoue, Yasuo Kabe, Sensho Nobe, Akito Yoshida, Atsushi Yamamoto, Yuya Kita, Mayumi Shimizu, Kenichi Tomeoka, Michael X Cohen, Shuntaro Sasai
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective . Speech Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have emerged as a pivotal technology in facilitating communication for individuals with speech impairments. Utilizing electroencephalography (EEG) for noninvasive speech BCIs offers an accessible and affordable solution, potentially benefiting a broader audience. However, EEG-based speech decoding remains controversial especially for overt speech, due to difficulties in separating speech-related neural activities from myoelectric potential artifacts generated during articulation. Moreover, because paradigms for collecting covert speech data are inherently less scalable than those for overt speech, whether the neural dynamics underlying EEG-based decoding of overt speech are also present during covert speech remains an open and practically important question. Approach . Here we aim to delineate the extent of the neural contributions to EEG-based speech decoding, and the degree to which the underlying neural dynamics are shared across overt and covert speech, by employing Explainable AI techniques to a convolutional neural network predicting spoken words based on signals obtained by ultra-high-density (uhd)-EEG. Main results . We found that electrode-wise contributions to the decoding cannot be explained by their mutual information with electromyography (EMG). Furthermore, contributing periods of speech to EEG-based decoding are distinct from those to decoding solely relying on EMG. In contrast, there are significant overlaps in signal timings contributing to EEG-based decoding, regardless of vocal conditions such as overt or covert speech. Notably, the denoising process successfully enhanced the decoding contribution from electrodes within speech-related brain areas for all speech conditions. Significance . Altogether, our findings support the idea that, with appropriate preprocessing, EEG becomes a valuable tool for decoding spoken words based on underlying neural activities.

papers.title: Trust, AI, and credibility in Reddit’s election news discourse
papers.authors: Timothy Koskie, Justin K. Miller, Christopher Hall
papers.abstract: During the 2024 US election, voters going online were inundated with news, information and analysis to guide their engagement with a core democratic function. However, these online spaces increasingly featured new contributions through AI-driven tools like ChatGPT. While promising to empower users, their presence also introduced new causes for uncertainty and suspicion. To identify their impact, this study investigated how references to AI were used to elicit trust or provoke distrust in news and political forums on Reddit during the election’s final days. 220,373 posts and comments from five major political subreddits revealed thematic patterns linking AI to broader societal anxieties over the reliability and transparency of news ecosystems. Four themes emerged: AI accusations to provoke distrust, Appreciation for AI, AI inaccuracy and incompetency, and AI as a threat. Users expressed appreciation for the tools, but accusations of undeclared use stoked distrust in AI, users and the platform itself.

papers.title: The pragmatist and the realist: mapping AI literacy in the Chinese game industry
papers.authors: Gejun Huang, Tiexin Liang
papers.abstract: The evolving landscape of AI has brought unprecedented changes to game production in China. A holistic examination of AI literacy among Chinese game industry professionals is conducive to a thorough, critical understanding of how AI transforms cultural production in the gaming sector and beyond. Drawing on survey data from 129 professionals engaging the full spectrum of game production business, this research finds that the practical dimension of AI literacy develops via non-coding AI usage, while the cognitive dimension is tied to production expertise. When mapping production and industry outcomes, practical and cognitive competencies substantially predict cost efficiencies, market scaling, and creative innovation. Conversely, the critical dimension of AI literacy serves as the primary driver of anxieties regarding labour displacement, asset devaluation, and creative homogenisation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven writing intervention for children with Chinese dysgraphia: integrating cognitive apprenticeship theory into multimodal feedback design
papers.authors: Lulu Wang, Yuying Deng, Ruoyu Zhou, Xinyue Yao, Xingfei Li, Li Dong
papers.abstract: Children with Chinese writing disorders require precise, personalised intervention to support their writing development, but scarce one-to-one resources hinder support. In this context, the emerging field of generative artificial intelligence offers new solutions. This study designed and validated a practice evaluation system for these children. It aims to help them overcome writing challenges like disorganised content, insufficient formal standardisation and low motivation. Drawing on research into Chinese writing disorders and children’s cognitive traits and using natural language processing (NLP) technology and cognitive apprenticeship theory, the study combined case studies, teacher interviews and student feedback to build an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation and feedback mechanism. Results show the exercise evaluation system can effectively aid children with dysgraphia in their writing discourse-level development, enhancing their writing ability and motivation. Future research can further optimise the NLP algorithm, improve the system’s recognition accuracy of writing characteristics and better support these children’s special educational needs.

papers.title: High-Tech Entry and Customer Innovation: Evidence from AI-Augmented Supply Chain Collaboration
papers.authors: Shuo Wang, Xinjie Wang, Chengyou Li
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) continues to reshape global supply chain dynamics, understanding how supplier entry by high-tech firms interacts with AI adoption has become a critical pathway for fostering customer innovation. This study develops a theoretical framework that incorporates supplier-side entry, AI-augmented production technologies, and firm-level cost structures, grounded in both production cost and market demand functions. Leveraging a unique panel dataset of 37,631 firm-year observations in China from 2007 to 2023, we employ a difference-in-differences (DID) approach to empirically identify the impact of AI adoption by high-tech suppliers on customer innovation outcomes. Our analysis yields three main findings. (i) After entering customer supply chains, high-tech firms that adopt AI significantly improve the innovation performance of their customer firms. (ii) The effect of AI-enabled supply chain integration is stronger for firms in SME-oriented segments and highly competitive industries, and is mainly reflected in the increase of invention patents. (iii) Mechanism analyses associate AI-enabled supplier entry with lower R&D expenditure per patent application and greater participation in joint innovation alliances, consistent with improved innovation efficiency and interfirm coordination.

papers.title: Critical Fairness Literacy for PK–12 teachers: a fairness-specific dimension of teacher AI competency
papers.authors: Chan Aristella Lu, Yun Zhang
papers.journal: Journal of Research on Technology in Education
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes integrated into PK–12 education, teachers need professional judgment to evaluate its fairness. This conceptual paper develops Critical Fairness Literacy (CFL) through a structured synthesis of literature on teacher AI competency, critical AI literacy, algorithmic fairness, educational AI ethics, and educational equity. CFL is proposed as a subdimension of teacher AI competency focused on fairness, comprising bias source identification, contextual equity analysis, and interrogation of fairness definitions. Three practical protocols, bias tracing, equity-centered contextual review, and fairness framing reflection, connect these dimensions to classroom judgment and professional learning. The paper proposes how guided inquiry, peer feedback, and repeated application might support CFL development. The framework and protocols remain theoretically informed proposals requiring empirical investigation.

papers.title: AI-Related Technostress and Employee Adoption Intention: The Mediating Role of Emotions in Hospitality
papers.authors: Nima Soltani-Nejad, Fatemeh Taheri-Azad, Seyed Taha Hashemi Pour, Akram Ashraf Ganjouie
papers.journal: International Journal of Hospitality & Tourism Administration
papers.abstract: Drawing on the Challenge–Hindrance Stress Framework and Affective Events Theory, this study examines how challenge technology stressors (CTS) and hindrance technology stressors (HTS) influence hotel employees’ emotions and AI adoption intention, and how perceived Organizational Digital Leadership (ODL) and Organizational Innovative Climate (OIC) moderate these relationships. Data from 652 hotel employees in five Iranian cities were analyzed using PLS-SEM. CTS positively predicted positive emotions toward AI, while HTS positively predicted negative emotions. Both positive and, unexpectedly, negative emotions were positively associated with AI adoption intention, producing significant positive indirect effects. OIC strengthened the CTS–positive emotion relationship and weakened the HTS–negative emotion relationship, whereas ODL showed the opposite pattern. Findings highlight employee AI adoption as an affective, context-dependent process shaped by differentiated technostress and organizational conditions.

papers.title: Exploring pre-service teachers’ conflict resolution strategies and decision-making patterns in AI-based multi-agent environments
papers.authors: Xiarizhati Niyazi, Xiaoqing Shang, Bin Jing, Yuchong Gao
papers.abstract: Conflict resolution is essential for teachers. Pre-service teachers (PSTs) often struggle to connect coursework with classroom practice, especially in multi-role conflicts. Artificial intelligence (AI) simulations may offer a low-risk environment. This study examined PSTs’ conflict-resolution practices in an AI-based multi-agent setting where virtual participants were available within the same conflict scenario. We developed a chatbot through which 20 PSTs interacted with an aggressor, an accomplice, a victim, parents, and a tutor in a peer-conflict scenario. Using dialogue logs, we applied inductive qualitative content analysis and lag sequential analysis to examine behavioural transitions. The analysis identified two complementary findings. First, PSTs’ strategies varied by student-agent role. When addressing aggressors, they tended to use guiding reflection, emotional support, surface threat, and role endowment; when addressing accomplices, they more often used positive encouragement, guiding reflection, home-school collaboration, and emotional support; and when addressing victims, they relied on home-school collaboration, positive relationship guidance, and emotional support. Second, PSTs’ engagement with AI guidance followed four pathways: relying on AI-generated suggestions, iterative inquiry with AI, doubting AI-generated suggestions, and bypassing AI-generated suggestions. These findings suggest that PSTs selectively negotiated role-specific cues and AI guidance, making visible situated professional judgement in AI-supported conflict-resolution practice.

papers.title: From joy to resistance: consumer reactions to disclosure of AI-created advertisements
papers.authors: Chien Duong, Billy Sung, Isaac Cheah, Peter Dell
papers.abstract: Conventional wisdom suggests that viewers tend to evaluate AI-generated advertisements negatively. We argue that viewers can nevertheless enjoy creative advertisements produced by AI. However, the belief that creativity is an exclusively human attribute may prompt cognitive regulation when AI involvement is disclosed. Using a consumer neuroscience approach, we conducted a one-factor, three-level between-subjects experiment in which participants viewed advertisements with no disclosure, disclosure of human–AI collaboration, or disclosure of full AI creation. Creative advertisements elicited joy, captured by facial expression analysis, regardless of whether they were created by humans or AI. Greater joy was associated with less message counterarguing and more favourable advertisement attitudes, but only in the absence of AI disclosure. These findings suggest that AI disclosure does not diminish initial enjoyment. Instead, it may act as a persuasion knowledge cue that activates cognitive regulation, leading viewers to override their positive affective responses when subsequently evaluating the advertisement.

papers.title: Governing generative AI in final academic works: from disclosure to competence verification in European university policies
papers.authors: Anna Peirats, Francisco Moreno
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has unsettled a central assumption in assessing final academic works: that the submitted text is reliable evidence of a student’s competence, authorship and intellectual contribution. European universities have responded with acceptable-use rules, disclosure requirements and integrity guidance, but rarely explain what evidence would show competence once research, writing and revision are partly machine-mediated. This article asks how far official policy supplies that evidence. Drawing on argument-based validity theory and work on evaluative judgement, it defines inferential governance and builds an Inferential Governance Framework of 15 indicators across five dimensions (competence, process, evidence, interpretive assessment and governance). It is applied to 70 official university policy cases from 14 European countries. Policy development proves substantial but uneven: 50 cases are procedural or declarative and two reach the highest of five bands. Declaration of AI use, competence-oriented language and independent intellectual contribution are widespread; process supervision, student-supervisor agreements, process dossiers, oral defence, the examiner or tribunal role and detector prudence are much less common. The article calls this imbalance an inferential gap between competence claims and the means of verification, shows that it survives every alternative corpus composition tested, and proposes a Competence-Centred Inferential Governance Model.

papers.title: Quantitative Analysis of Electroencephalography in Hypnosis: A Neurophysiological Approach
papers.authors: Golnaz Baghdadi, Ali Motie Nasrabadi
papers.journal: International Journal of Clinical and Experimental Hypnosis
papers.abstract: Hypnosis is a unique state of consciousness marked by heightened response to suggestions, focused attention, and altered cognitive control. This article explores the neural connections involved in hypnosis through electroencephalography (EEG) studies, examining brain changes during hypnosis and their relationship to hypnotic depth and susceptibility. Theta waves, linked to hypnotic depth, are stronger in highly hypnotizable individuals, while gamma waves are associated with focus, suggestion acceptance, and emotional responses. Hypnosis also induces frequency-dependent reorganization of large-scale brain connectivity, particularly in frontal-parietal and attentional networks, enhancing subjective experiences and responsiveness. EEG patterns reveal more dynamic neural activity during hypnosis, which cannot be captured by linear metrics alone. Hemispheric analysis shows greater left-hemisphere activity in highly hypnotizable individuals, particularly in emotionally and verbally mediated tasks, challenging the right-hemisphere dominance model. Event related potential (ERP) findings show that hypnosis affects information processing at both pre-attentional and cognitive levels. These insights contribute to understanding hypnosis' impact on the brain and its potential for personalized therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: Seeing inside the black box: Effects of algorithmic knowledge on system trustworthiness in aviation
papers.authors: Anneke Hamann, Alexander Heise, Helge Lenz, Anja Gampe
papers.abstract: Automation has shaped aircraft design for the past seven decades, moving from fully manual control to highly automated systems. Despite this, pilots retain final authority for safety-critical decisions, which requires continuous trust calibration. This study investigated how algorithmic transparency influences pilots' learned trust in an AI-based cockpit assistant. Twenty-one commercial pilots were randomly assigned to an early transparency condition (detailed explanations of the AI's algorithms and performance provided before the tutorial) or a late transparency condition (the same information delivered after the experiment). Each pilot used the assistant during a tutorial and a realistic simulated flight. Mixed-effects ordinal models showed higher trust ratings for the early compared to the late transparency group during both tutorial and flight, and a larger trust increase between phases. In conclusion, providing pilots with timely, clear information about AI processes modestly improves trust and supports calibrated reliance.

papers.title: Digital spaces and language learning
papers.authors: Christoph A. Hafner
papers.abstract: Abstract In this commentary, I consider contributions to the special issue on Challenges and Affordances in Digital Spaces. The contributions both build on well-established areas of interest in language learning and technology (like digital multimodal composing, for example) and attend to relatively new frontiers in the digital domain (like AI and platformization). I comment on three inter-related themes that are raised in the special issue: (1) process and distributed agency, (2) criticality and creativity, (3) power, platforms and legitimacy. I close with a call for more research to better understand how language and literacy educators can rise to meet increasing challenges in ways that promote active and critical learning, meaningful activity, and individual agency.

papers.title: Challenges and affordances in digital spaces
papers.authors: Marta González‐Lloret
papers.abstract: Abstract The landscape of language education is experiencing a profound transformation driven by the rapid evolution of digital technologies and artificial intelligence. This volume offers a critical exploration of how digital spaces, interactional competence, and social identity converge to reshape pedagogical practices, arguing that technology acts as a sociomaterial force rather than a mere delivery mechanism. Through a variety of innovative methodologies, the articles investigate several key digital frontiers: cross-cultural discussions of conflictive topics within Virtual Exchanges; the social, equitable, and evaluative complexities of Digital Multimodal Composing (DMC), and the affordances and limitations of Virtual Reality (VR) and Spoken Dialogue Systems in assessing interactional competence and navigating rater bias. Furthermore, the issue critically examines the role of AI in modern learning. It highlights multilingual students’ use of neural machine translation for “transknowledging,” explores the ethical boundaries of Generative AI as perceived by students and language instructors, and addresses the increasing commercialization of teacher identities on social media platforms. Ultimately, this collection serves as a collective call for critical reflexivity. It provides a comprehensive roadmap for the next decade of applied linguistics, advocating for longitudinal research, the integration of AI-driven learning analytics, the dismantling of the digital divide, and a pedagogical shift toward deliberate human-AI collaboration to empower 21st-century learners.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence and foreign language learning
papers.authors: Matt Kessler, Jihye Kim, Melike Akay, Tania Ferronato
papers.abstract: Abstract Prior studies exploring teachers’ perceptions of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini have signaled tensions between instructors’ perceptions of GenAI’s usefulness and their beliefs regarding its ethicality. The current study furthers this line of inquiry, examining issues of ethics and utility by focusing specifically on teachers of languages other than English. Using a sequential mixed-methods design, this study employed a survey to understand language instructors’ ( N = 101) perceptions of the ethicality of GenAI tool use in higher education, along with their perceptions of the usefulness of GenAI for supporting second language (L2) learning. Semi-structured interviews were then conducted with six teachers to further understand participants’ survey responses, with some teachers sharing additional artifacts (e.g., course policies regarding GenAI). The findings suggest that most teachers (92.1%) believe GenAI tools are ethical if used for specific purposes. There also appears to be a connection between teachers’ ethical beliefs and their perceptions of GenAI’s utility, in terms of whether GenAI is used by students as a scaffold/support mechanism versus being used to produce content. The implications of this study provide a roadmap for developing discipline-specific guidelines that preserve L2 learning integrity while leveraging GenAI’s utility.

papers.title: Enhancing language learning with AI: the role of AI service quality in learning satisfaction and performance in mobile-assisted language learning applications
papers.authors: Jung-Chieh Lee, Jiaxian Li, Lei Bi, Lei Bi
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered mobile-assisted language learning (MALL) applications are transforming the traditional language learning paradigm by leveraging AI technologies to provide a more efficient, convenient, and personalized learning experience. Despite the integration of AI technologies into MALL applications, prior studies have overlooked the critical role of AI service quality in shaping learners’ learning satisfaction levels and performance within these applications. This study addresses this research gap by leveraging social support theory to develop a research model that examines how the AI service quality of AI-powered MALL applications influences social support, specifically informational, emotional, and appraisal support. These forms of support are further analyzed to determine their effects on learners’ learning satisfaction levels and performance. A total of 978 valid samples were collected from users of AI-powered MALL applications and analyzed using the partial least-squares method. The results indicate that AI service quality significantly enhances users’ perceptions of informational, emotional, and appraisal support. These forms of support positively influence learning satisfaction and learning performance. Furthermore, the mediation analysis revealed that informational, emotional, and appraisal support act as partial mediators in the relationships between AI service quality and learning satisfaction and between AI service quality and learning performance. This study contributes to the literature by revealing how AI service quality, social support, and learning satisfaction and performance interact in the context of AI-enabled MALL applications. We also offer practical insights for improving the user experience and maximizing the learning outcomes of AI-driven MALL applications.

papers.title: School bag carriage in schoolchildren: relative load, carrying duration, perceived heaviness, and back pain
papers.authors: Kateřina Daňková, Mario Kasović, Grgur Višić, Marta Gimunová, Tomáš Vespalec
papers.abstract: Carrying school bags represents a routine mechanical exposure for school-aged children and may influence posture, gait, and musculoskeletal health. Current recommendations commonly express school bag weight as a percentage of body weight; however, relationships among relative load, anthropometric characteristics, perceived heaviness, carrying duration, and back pain remain unclear. This cross-sectional study examined these relationships in 221 schoolchildren aged 6–15 years. Anthropometric characteristics, school bag weight, carrying duration, perceived heaviness, and self-reported back pain were assessed. Mean relative school bag load was 14.49 ± 3.79% of body weight. Relative load was inversely associated with BMI, body weight, and body height. Carrying duration showed a weak positive association with perceived heaviness. Exploratory cluster analysis identified three descriptive profiles characterized by higher BMI/lower relative load, lower BMI/higher relative load, and longer carrying duration. Still, the cluster membership was not significantly associated with back pain. These findings indicate that relative load, carrying duration, perceived heaviness, and reported back pain capture partly distinct aspects of school bag carriage. Preventive recommendations should therefore remain proportionate to the evidence and should interpret the effect of a single school bag parameter on musculoskeletal pain cautiously.

papers.title: EEG-based Alzheimer’s disease detection using two-branch multi-scale deep learning with integrated gradients-guided channel selection
papers.authors: Jungpil Shin, Najmul Hassan, Abu Saleh Musa Miah, Satoshi Nishimura
papers.abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is critical for timely intervention and clinical monitoring. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive, low-cost, and portable alternative to neuroimaging. However, existing traditional and deep learning (DL)-based methods often face challenges related to computational cost, representational complexity, and practical deployment. In this work, we propose Fused-MSCA-2B, a two-branch multi-scale channel-attentive 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) for EEG-based AD detection. The model processes broadband multichannel EEG directly as temporal sequences and combines multi-scale temporal convolution, residual learning, squeeze-and-excitation channel attention, and feature-level branch fusion. Specifically, Branch A uses MSCA blocks with kernel configurations $$(3,5,9)$$ and $$(3,5,7)$$ to capture local and medium-range temporal dependencies, whereas Branch B uses $$(5,9,15)$$ and $$(3,5,9)$$ to capture broader and higher-level temporal patterns. The branch-level embeddings are fused and passed through dense classification layers to generate AD/HC posterior probabilities. A key component of the proposed model is an explainable AI-guided reduced-channel selection strategy. Integrated Gradients (IG) is used to rank EEG channel relevance from validation data, enabling the EEG montage to be reduced from 19 to 12 channels. We evaluated the proposed model using two benchmark datasets. The IG-guided Top-12 configuration achieved 98.60% ± 1.18% recording-level accuracy while reducing the EEG montage from 19 to 12 channels. As a supporting ablation analysis, the Fixed Top-12 configuration achieved 98.40% ± 0.73% accuracy, further confirming the effectiveness of the IG-guided reduced-channel selection strategy. The results demonstrate that the proposed XAI-guided Fused-MSCA-2B framework supports robust EEG-based AD detection with a compact and practical electrode configuration, showing strong performance with reduced channel sets.

papers.title: Academic performance of large language models across an undergraduate physiotherapy curriculum: a subset analysis
papers.authors: Ali Ömer Acar, Sergen Ozturk, Dilek Çağrı Arslan, Nuray Alaca
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in physiotherapy for information retrieval, educational support, and assistance in assessment and rehabilitation-related decision-making. Although their performance has often been evaluated using isolated examinations or domain-specific question sets, less is known about how these models perform across the breadth of an undergraduate physiotherapy curriculum. This study examined LLM performance using a curriculum-based academic assessment framework reflecting how theoretical knowledge is formally evaluated in physiotherapy education. Written exams from a subset of 34 of 54 eligible courses within an undergraduate Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation program were analyzed. Two LLMs, GPT-5.0 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet, were queried using a standardized zero-shot prompting approach, and responses were graded according to official answer keys and institutional criteria. Course-level examination scores, letter grades, and cumulative grade point averages were calculated for standardized comparison. Under the institutional grading system, both models achieved passing-level performance, with GPT-5.0 reaching a mean total score of 85.7 ± 10.4 (GPA-equivalent: 3.28/4.00) and Claude 4.5 Sonnet a mean total score of 87.3 ± 11.2 (GPA-equivalent: 3.39/4.00), both satisfying the institutional graduation threshold; Claude 4.5 Sonnet showed modestly but significantly higher overall performance. Both models performed better in basic science courses than in clinically oriented courses. These findings suggest that LLMs perform well on knowledge-based assessments in undergraduate physiotherapy education, while revealing relative limitations in clinically integrated domains.

papers.title: A socio-technical framework for generative AI integration in knowledge intensive systems: Insights from the agri-food ecosystem
papers.authors: Chun-Wei Peng, Hsin‐Lu Chang, Wang JiunHao

papers.title: Problematic engagement with generative AI measurement drivers contexts and outcomes
papers.authors: Raghu Raman R, Robin Kowalski, Prema Nedungadi, Krishnashree Achuthan
papers.abstract: Generative AI tools and conversational chatbots are increasingly embedded in education, work, and daily life, raising concerns about engagement that becomes difficult to self-regulate. This review synthesizes emerging research on problematic generative AI use, treating addiction-like language as part of a broader problematic-use construct rather than a clinical diagnosis. Following PRISMA 2020 reporting, a Scopus search executed identified 188 records. Included studies were characterised by research design and evidence type rather than scored with a formal risk-of-bias instrument. Measurement work is expanding quickly, but instruments remain partially fragmented, blurring the boundary between high engagement, habitual reliance, and impairment. Mechanism studies converge on attachment processes, anthropomorphism and perceived empathy, loneliness and social anxiety, immersive flow, and self-regulatory strain, suggesting that social presence and immersion amplify reliance for some users. In learning and knowledge work, performance pressure and incentive structures can normalize overreliance, with reported risks for cognitive offloading, independent thinking, academic integrity, and skill development. Outcome studies associate compulsive or dependent use with technostress, psychological distress, and lower wellbeing, while mitigation discussion highlights reinforcement-friendly interface cues, privacy and memory governance, and sustainability trade-offs. Because the corpus is almost entirely cross-sectional and self-reported, these relationships are associations rather than causal effects. The key distinction is not between users and non-users, but between bounded, purpose-driven use and escalating reliance with reduced self-regulation. An Antecedents–Decisions–Outcomes structure is used only to frame a forward-looking agenda for longitudinal and intervention research. A sensitivity analysis comparing studies published in 2026 with those published earlier showed that no conclusion was reversed: the design profile and principal gaps held, while the most recent longitudinal studies strengthened the evidence on temporal order and outcomes.

papers.title: Including the excluded: AI, social intelligence, and disability inclusion for SDGs 4 and 8
papers.authors: Mariam Ibrahim ZeinEddine, Manal M. Yunis
papers.abstract: Over the years, society has demonstrated varied perceptions toward individuals with impairments, often characterized by prejudice and discrimination. This has created significant barriers hindering their full integration in various life domains, notably education and employment. Persistent exclusion not only restricts opportunities for individuals with impairments to live with dignity but also delays progress toward achieving the UN's Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This study analyzes 136 survey responses from working-age persons with and without disabilities in Lebanon. IBM SPSS AMOS 30 was used to examine the role of technology adoption, including AI-enabled digital and assistive technologies, and institutional decision-makers' social intelligence in attaining quality education (SDG4) and decent work (SDG8). The analysis also examined the mediating roles of access to resources and community support. The findings reveal substantial disparities in access and outcomes between persons with and without disabilities. Results showed that technology adoption was positively associated with access to resources and with quality education and decent work. Furthermore, decision-makers’ social intelligence was positively associated with perceived community support, which, in turn, was associated with decent work. However, the association between community support and quality education was not statistically supported, while social intelligence remained positively associated with both outcomes. Finally, the interaction between technology adoption and social intelligence was significantly associated with quality education, but not decent work, possibly due to the interference of external factors such as the country's security and financial instability. This study offers evidence that can inform inclusive practices and policy recommendations aimed at enhancing education and employment opportunities for persons with disabilities.

papers.title: Understanding tourist behavioral intentions in agritourism: A SEM–ANN hybrid model of technology readiness and value co-creation
papers.authors: To Ngoc Thinh, Nguyễn Quang Vinh, Vuong Thuy Linh
papers.abstract: This study examines how digital engagement, value co-creation, technology readiness, and satisfaction are associated with tourists’ self-reported behavioral intention in agritourism. Drawing on value co-creation theory and technology readiness theory, with expectation–confirmation theory used as a supporting lens for post-experience satisfaction, the study analyzes survey data from 325 Vietnamese agritourism visitors using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) as complementary analytical techniques. The PLS-SEM results show that digital engagement is positively associated with value co-creation and satisfaction but has no significant direct association with behavioral intention. Value co-creation, technology readiness, and satisfaction are positively associated with behavioral intention. Satisfaction mediates the relationships of digital engagement, value co-creation, and technology readiness with behavioral intention, while technology readiness negatively moderates the relationship between value co-creation and satisfaction. The ANN analysis provides complementary predictive evidence, identifying value co-creation, technology readiness, and satisfaction as the most influential predictors of behavioral intention. The findings suggest that digital engagement is most consequential when it facilitates participatory value co-creation and satisfaction, while technology readiness functions both as an antecedent and as a boundary condition in agritourism experiences.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) in public administration: Theoretical shifts, implications and developing countries’ perspectives
papers.authors: Namita Devi, Jayanta Krishna Sarmah
papers.abstract: The infusion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has engendered a transformational shift in the field of public administration. Guided by PRISMA protocols, this study synthesizes 51 articles identified through Scopus and Web of Science databases. Drawing upon qualitative thematic analysis using NVivo software, this article critically analyzes the intersection of AI and public administration with a specific focus on developing countries. The paper concentrates on two main themes: (1) the growing ubiquity of AI in public administration, encompassing dominant theoretical frameworks, as well as balanced assessment of benefits and risks; and (2) the patterns and perspectives of developing countries, highlighting AI adoption areas and key barriers. The findings of this study situate AI within the broader public administration domain, revealing a fragmented theoretical landscape as well as developing countries’ distinct AI incorporation efforts.

papers.title: From growth mindset to social-emotional skills in early and mid-adolescence: A educational-cultural examination of an integrated mind-body-behavior framework
papers.authors: Tong Zhou, Yi Liao, Xiaoyu Cheng, 刘丽薇, Wei Chen
papers.abstract: Background Social-emotional learning (SEL) is a core educational goal, yet little is known about how adolescents’ cognitive beliefs, body-related self-perceptions, and everyday health behavior jointly relate to social-emotional skills across diverse cultural contexts and school stages. Objective Based on mindset theory and self-regulation perspectives, we examined an integrated Mind-Body-Behavior framework in which growth mindset, positive body image, and health behavior show a theoretically specified pattern of associated with adolescents’ social-emotional skills. Sample Participants were 62,105 adolescents from 15 regions where data were drawn from the OECD 2023 Study on Social and Emotional Skills. Methods A two-stage quantitative design combined structural equation modeling and machine learning. Results Growth mindset was associated with social-emotional skills both directly and indirectly associations via body image and health behavior. The direct association was substantially stronger than the combined indirect associations, indicating partial rather than complete support for the full proposed pattern. Scalar invariance across the seven clusters was not supported, so cluster-level comparisons were treated as descriptive. Associations differed between cohorts: the association between growth mindset and body image was stronger in the younger cohort, whereas the association between health behavior and social-emotional skills was stronger in the older cohort. Conclusions The study contributes an integrated view of how beliefs, body-related self-perception, and health behavior relate to social-emotional skills. The framework shows that cognitive, body-related, and behavioral domains each relate to adolescents’ social-emotional skills and that these relations change between school stages.

papers.title: Effect of AI authorship disclosure on purchase intention in cultural tourism souvenirs: The mediating roles of perceived effort and authenticity
papers.authors: Guanbo Liang, Pohsun Wang, Yung-Cheng Hsieh, Cong Fang, Longyu Zhang, Huajian Ou
papers.journal: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) expands in cultural tourism souvenir design and disclosure policies evolve, evidence remains limited on how AI authorship disclosure shapes responses across nationality groups and products. Drawing on signaling theory, two studies compared consumers from China and the U.S. across three disclosure conditions: unlabeled, human–AI co-created, and AI-generated. Study 1 used tourism postcard stimuli ( N = 1110), and Study 2 used mug and tourism tote bag stimuli ( N = 1255). Both studies found that disclosure affected purchase intention and interacted significantly with nationality. Differences across disclosure conditions were significant among participants from the U.S. but not among those from China. In Study 1, the unlabeled and human–AI co-created conditions did not differ, and both exceeded the AI-generated condition. In Study 2, the unlabeled condition exceeded both disclosed conditions for both products, whereas the latter two did not differ. AI-generated disclosure was consistently associated with lower purchase intention than no disclosure, whereas the relative position of human–AI co-created disclosure differed between studies. Parallel mediation analyses showed indirect effects through perceived effort and perceived authenticity. Perceived effort effects were significant for both comparisons with the unlabeled condition across three examined products, whereas the human–AI co-created versus unlabeled authenticity effect was nonsignificant in Study 1 but significant in Study 2. Nationality moderated some, but not all, indirect effects. Thus, firms should not assume that human–AI co-creation enhances responses and should consider clarifying human contribution and pretesting disclosure strategies across products and national markets.

papers.title: Structurally informed metabolite measurements with ion mobility-mass spectrometry
papers.authors: Yu-Ting Tseng, Kelly Marie Hines
papers.abstract: Although ion mobility-mass spectrometry (IM-MS) is no longer a new technology, new developments in instrumentation and resources for structurally informed measurements are enabling the use of IM-MS in emerging metabolomic applications. Once limited by experimental measurements, the growth of machine-learning strategies to predict collision cross-section values is rapidly increasing the coverage of IM-MS information in metabolite databases. IM-MS instrumentation capable of high-resolution separations is bringing new depth to the level of structural annotation that can be achieved, while creative strategies to combine IM-MS with complementary analytical or chemical methods are further leveraging its ability to resolve small molecule isomers and isobars. This brief review highlights the recent developments of IM-MS for metabolomics with a focus on applications to mass spectrometry imaging, rapid multi-omics, and single-cell analyses.

papers.title: Uncovering emotion dynamics across human–AI interaction modes in programming: Evidence from facial expression and electrodermal activity
papers.authors: Tianlong Zhong, Gaoxia Zhu

papers.title: Direct pathways from anthropomorphism to self-disclosure in artificial intelligence Chatbot use: a mixed-methods multi-study investigation
papers.authors: Wahidur Rahman
papers.abstract: Anthropomorphic design is widely assumed to shape self-disclosure and emotional dependence by first cultivating felt empathy and trust, and the safety measures platforms deploy, such as labelling and disclosure of artificial origin, target those perceptions. Across a twelve-country survey, forty-seven interviews, and three experiments, this research tests that mediation model and identifies the route that carries the behavioural effect. A twelve-country survey ( N = 1480) found empathy and trust negligibly related to disclosure and dependence at the trait level. Two experiments ( N = 390 and N = 300) produced strong direct effects of an anthropomorphic agent, with the anthropomorphic agent roughly tripling the odds of behavioural disclosure (63% versus 35% under a matched neutral prompt), while the indirect effects through empathy and trust received no support. Study 5 ( N = 300) measured competing mediators and provided the most defensible interim account of the mechanism: only perceived anonymity and reduced evaluation apprehension carried the effect on disclosure, locating the process in online disinhibition rather than felt relational warmth. Forty-seven interviews surfaced clinically salient disclosure, including suicidal ideation revealed to a chatbot and to no person. Because the consequences of anthropomorphic design travel through the lowered social risk of the medium, safeguards that recalibrate how users perceive an agent may leave disclosure and dependence largely untouched.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of diabetes-related factors using machine learning on the CDC health indicator dataset: metabolic, lifestyle, socioeconomic and demographic domains
papers.authors: Muhammad Azizur Rahman, Abdullah Abdullah
papers.journal: Machine learning for computational science and engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Diabetes mellitus is a chronic disease that continues to pose significant global health pressure, affecting a considerable proportion of the world’s population, with an estimated 537 million people affected worldwide in 2021, with an expected increase of 46% in the number of diabetic patients by 2045 [1]. Diabetes is strongly associated with lifestyle behaviors, metabolic conditions, and socioeconomic status. This paper presents a comprehensive machine learning analysis of the CDC Health Indicator Dataset ( n = 253,680), sourced from the 2015 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS). Following systematic data preprocessing with feature binning and multimodal exploratory data analysis, including interactive correlation matrices, radar charts, Sankey diagrams, animated feature distributions, and other graphical representations to examine data distributions, relationships, patterns, and feature importance. Four supervised classification models were trained and evaluated, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost. All four machine learning models achieved comparable overall accuracy ranging from 83.06% to 84.74%. As 84.3% of the participants belong from the non-diabetic class so the accuracy is driven almost entirely by the majority class due to which accuracy alone could be misleading. The Macro-averaged F1 (0.383–0.396) and balanced accuracy (0.384–0.387) shows the four models performing far closer together than accuracy alone suggests, and the per-class recall reveals a near-total inability to detect the pre-diabetic class (recall ≈ 0.00) regardless of the model choice. This result was confirmed under fivefold stratified cross-validation, in which Class 1 recall was exactly 0.0000 in every fold for three of the four models, and the results persisted across both the original BRFSS encoded data and the binned dataset. All four models were then retrained under balanced class weighting. Weighting raised the recall for the Class 1 (pre-Diabetic Class) recall from 0.0000 to between 0.293–0.310 for three of the four models, where the precision for the Class 1 remained between 0.021 and 0.031 and the overall accuracy decreased to approximately 58.26–73.08%. Cross Validated Class 1 PR-AUC ranged from 0.0243–0.0370 against a base rate of 0.018. These results indicate that class weighting can reduce majority-class bias and improve minority-class sensitivity, but it does not by itself provide reliable pre-diabetic discrimination from the available non-glycaemic survey predictors. Feature importance was found to depend on the representation used rather than being a fixed property of the data. Under the binned representation, general health status and high blood pressure ranked highest; under the original BRFSS coding, in which BMI is retained as a continuous variable, BMI was the strongest predictor by a wide margin. Predictor rankings are therefore reported separately for each representation. Income and education were associated with diabetes prevalence, but because the data are cross-sectional and self-reported, these associations are reported without causal interpretation.

papers.title: Advancing gender equity and inclusive digital futures through responsible agentic artificial intelligence governance
papers.authors: Bindiya Jain, Ravi Kant Gupta
papers.abstract: The shift to agentic AI represents a major paradigm change in the field of intelligent systems research and development, as these systems are capable of establishing sub-goals, planning for a goal, and executing plans with only minimal human oversight. This capability offers a unique chance to promote gender equality, inclusive digital engagement, and sustainable growth via evolving, accessible and fair AI-based methods throughout industries. Meanwhile, the increased autonomy of agentic AI systems presents unique challenges such as the potential for algorithmic bias to be amplified, decision-making disparities, and a lack of governance, each of which requires responsible AI, transparent governance, and clear ethical frameworks. This paper presents a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of a 41 paper corpus from Scopus. The review follows PRISMA 2020 guidelines and summarizes the evidence regarding agentic and generative AI architectures, typologies of bias, and sectoral applications in healthcare, education, and gender equity. The paper presents a human-centred conceptual framework for responsible governance of agentic AI, building on lifecycle-governance and equity-by-design approaches, which merges bias mitigation, gender-inclusive design, and sustainability transition. The network of co-authorship is highly fragmented (density = 0.021; number of components = 37 from 88 authors), suggesting that there is no coordinated research agenda and giving empirical support to the integrative framework proposed here. This fragmentation further indicates that the vision and capabilities of agentic AI to contribute to gender equality and education are still not fully explored in the context of governance and sustainability, highlighting the relevance of the framework introduced in this paper. This is a collection of AI topics, derived from the title, that are examined from a gender equality perspective.This is a list of AI keywords that have been explored through the lens of gender equity, based on the title.

papers.title: Predictors of nomophobia and the mediating role of smartphone addiction among students at the university of cape coast ghana
papers.authors: Robertson David Mfodwo, Humphrey Danso Bamfo, Robert Castro Cudjoe
papers.abstract: This study employed a cross-sectional correlational design. A sample of 411 students was selected using convenience sampling. Data were collected over one month, with a return rate of about 99.5%. Multiple regression analysis showed that financial stress, love addiction, and academic stress were jointly associated with nomophobia, F(3, 407) = 13.04, p < .001, explaining 8.8% of the variance (R² = 0.088; adjusted R² = 0.081). Love addiction (B = 0.19, p < .001) and academic stress (B = 0.18, p < .001) were significantly associated with nomophobia, whereas financial stress was not (β = 0.062, p = .206). Mediation analysis further revealed significant indirect effects of financial stress (ab = 0.247, 95% BCI [0.083, 0.419]), love addiction (ab = 0.135, 95% BCI [0.083, 0.192]), and academic stress (ab = 0.134, 95% BCI [0.078, 0.195]) on nomophobia through smartphone addiction. These findings highlight smartphone addiction as a potential pathway through which stress-related and emotional factors are linked to nomophobic tendencies among students of the University of Cape Coast. Based on the findings, university counselling centres should provide screening, counselling, and referral services for students experiencing nomophobia, smartphone addiction, academic stress, financial stress, and love addiction.

papers.title: Alice and Bob, The Three Inevitabilities, and The Perfect AI Assistant
papers.authors: M. Z. Naser
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper introduces a thought experiment in reverse alignment, in which, instead of aligning artificial intelligence (AI) with human values, we examine how humans inadvertently align with AI systems. We posit a theoretically perfect AI assistant and demonstrate that even this idealized system can produce concerning dynamics. In particular, we build on principles from pattern reinforcement and behavioral inertia to intuitively show that as the quality of AI assistance increases, human decision making tends to converge toward a utility-tilted sharpening of the assistant’s predictive distribution. Critically, this convergence exhibits strong path dependence: withdrawing assistance does not, by itself, restore cognitive independence, because the update contains no force that returns an agent to its pre-assistance policy. Recovery requires an active novelty incentive, and even then, it proceeds through history-dependent transients whose duration can exceed institutional planning horizons. We formalize these dynamics through two lenses: the Alice-Bob divergence , which tracks how adoption timing alone creates persistent cognitive divergence between identical agents, and the Three Inevitabilities , which captures the multi-scale forces (i.e. individual, social, and species-level) that drive convergence. Our theoretical and mathematical analysis reveals a fundamental trilemma: systems cannot simultaneously maintain optimal task outcomes, persistent human cognitive independence, and the absence of artificial novelty incentives. We conclude by identifying escape mechanisms and interventions that preserve human agency while retaining beneficial AI assistance to navigate the tension between augmentation and autonomy.

papers.title: Class-Selective Adversarial Attacks on EEG-Based Motor Imagery Classifiers: Implications for Safety-Critical Mental State Monitoring
papers.authors: Hyun Kwon, Jang-Woon Baek
papers.journal: International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based classifiers for mental state recognition are increasingly deployed in safety-critical settings such as pilot fatigue and operator vigilance monitoring.
