This paper formalizes a class-selective adversarial threat model, in which an attacker forces misclassification of a designated source class while all remaining classes continue to be classified correctly, and characterizes it on real EEG. As the instrument of this characterization we introduce Selective Projected Gradient Descent, which applies opposing gradient directions to source-class and non-source-class samples independently. Under subject-independent leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Dataset and an independent sustained-attention driving dataset, an oracle setting that assumes ground-truth label access, reported as an analytical upper bound rather than as deployable performance, yields selectivity scores of 0.919 on a binary pilot-state task with a clean accuracy of \(71.5\%\) and 0.990 on a four-class motor imagery task at \(\epsilon = 16/255\) , against 0.286 and 0.015 for the Fast Gradient Sign Method and standard Projected Gradient Descent on the binary task. A deployable label-free variant that uses no ground-truth labels leaves the attack success rate unchanged to within a tenth of a percentage point; it attains the oracle level of non-target preservation on the two binary scenarios but only part of it on the four-class task; in every scenario it confers no measurable advantage over restricting a standard attack to the predicted source class. In the multi-class setting such manipulation leaves aggregate accuracy far less disturbed than a standard attack, substantially weakening accuracy-based anomaly detection. The contribution therefore rests on the formulation and characterization of the class-selective threat model, and underscores the need for dedicated defenses in biosignal-based safety systems.

papers.title: Financial self efficacy as a mediator of artificial intelligence use in detecting money laundering and financial fraud in Jordanian Islamic banks
papers.authors: Majdi Ali Ghaith, Zaid Othman Dannoun, Emad Abdel Hafiz Alzyadat, Munir Suliaman Al-Hakim
papers.abstract: This study examines the mediating role of financial self-efficacy in the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and the perceived effectiveness of detecting money laundering and financial fraud in Jordanian Islamic banks. The study addresses a behavioral and institutional gap in the literature by explaining how AI-supported monitoring capabilities may be translated into effective regulatory action through employees’ confidence in interpreting and using AI-generated outputs. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 115 employees working in compliance, Shariah compliance, Shariah supervision, internal audit, auditing, and risk management functions in Jordanian Islamic banks. The questionnaire consisted of 35 items measuring AI adoption, financial self-efficacy, perceived AML/fraud detection effectiveness, and demographic characteristics. The data were analyzed using reliability and validity tests, correlation analysis, standardized multiple regression, and regression-based mediation analysis. The results indicate that AI adoption has a statistically significant positive direct effect on perceived AML/fraud detection effectiveness after accounting for financial self-efficacy (β = 0.296, p = 0.001). AI adoption also has a significant positive effect on financial self-efficacy ( β = 0.640, p < 0.001), while financial self-efficacy has a significant positive effect on perceived AML/fraud detection effectiveness ( β = 0.491, p < 0.001). The mediation analysis shows a significant indirect effect of AI adoption on perceived detection effectiveness through financial self-efficacy (indirect effect = 0.314, Sobel z = 4.806, p < 0.001). The VAF value of 51.46% indicates complementary partial mediation. The findings suggest that AI adoption contributes to perceived AML/fraud detection effectiveness not only through technological capabilities but also through employees’ financial self-efficacy. The study recommends integrating AI-supported monitoring systems with structured training, human-in-the-loop governance, and Shariah-sensitive regulatory procedures in Islamic banks.

papers.title: Workflow Design, Editor Expertise and case Typology for AI-Generated OSCE Scripts
papers.authors: Zhanglei Mu

papers.title: Digital entrepreneurship intention among students from selected universities in China and Malaysia: evidence based on a hybrid SEM–ANN approach
papers.authors: Shaohua Ben, Mohamad Bilal Ali

papers.title: Innovation Is by Humans for Humans. Commentary on ‘Artificial Intelligence, Entrepreneurial Discovery, and Embodied Tacit Knowledge’ by Ismail Kurun
papers.authors: Emanuele Martinelli
papers.abstract: Abstract Kurun (2026) provides a new argument against the possibility of replicating entrepreneurship with AI. The reference is to the socialist calculation debate, where it is contended that AI technology may enable us one day to plan the economy centrally through data analysis and predictive techniques. The paper itself argues that entrepreneurial discovery and, subsequently, innovation and economic evolution cannot be recreated outside of the market, no matter our technological infrastructure, because AI systems are forms of disembodied cognition. Entrepreneurship needs an embodied, situated, and affective perspective. I briefly present the paper’s context and main argument. I wish to apply the paper’s consideration further to show how the creativity of human entrepreneurs cannot be recreated neither by dedicated generative AI models nor by cooperative entrepreneurship. Finally, I highlight the alternative approach to the same conclusion, namely, the ontological strategy, in the different angle and advantages it brings in.

papers.title: Artificial Emotional Intelligence
papers.authors: Angelina Chen, Raffaele Ciriello
papers.abstract: Artificial Emotional Intelligence (AEI) refers to Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems that mediate human affect by sensing, processing, and responding to emotional states through multimodal inputs, including text, voice, and physiological signals (Chen et al. 2024 ). As AI systems (especially generative AI) become more conversational, personalised, and multimodal, AEI increasingly mediates therapy, companionship, customer service, education, and work (De Freitas et al. 2026 ; Zao-Sanders 2026 ). This marks a shift from mediating information and behaviour to mediating affect in sensitive contexts: AEI already underpins chatbots designed to mitigate suicide risk (Maples et al. 2024 ), customer-service systems that respond to frustration (Fan et al. 2024 ), and personalised sexbot applications (Rubinsztein and Ciriello 2024 ). This shift reflects technical progress, but also intensifies concerns about social fragmentation, care-capacity gaps, and the expansion of monetisation-oriented platform logics into domains historically organised around care, trust, and professional duty (Arsel 2026 ; Leong et al. 2021 ; Seleznova et al. 2023 ). Despite its significance, this reconfiguration of digital intermediation remains under-conceptualised in Information Systems (IS) research.

papers.title: Adopting AI, inviting risk? An empirical analysis of corporate cybersecurity consequences in IT firms

papers.title: Effects of resistance training on subjective sleep quality, excessive daytime sleepiness, and quality of life in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a secondary analysis from a randomized controlled trial
papers.authors: José Ricardo Vieira de Almeida, Daniela Karina da Silva Ferreira, Victória Duarte de Arantes Lima, Enrique Nascimento Nazário dos Santos, Nadja Sylmara dos Santos de Oliveira Silva, José Lucas Porto Aguiar, Elton Carlos Felinto dos Santos, Antônio Henrique Germano-Soares, Rodrigo Pinto Pedrosa, Andrea Maculano Esteves, Breno Quintella Farah, Ozeas Lins-Filho
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to verify the effect of eight weeks of resistance training (RT) on subjective sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, and quality of life in adults with OSA. METHODS: In this randomized controlled clinical trial, 25 adults with moderate to severe OSA (age: 54.6 ± 7.2 years; BMI: 36.1 ± 7.9 kg/m²; apnea-hypopnea index: 52.2 ± 27.4 events/hour) were included. Participants were randomized into an RT group (three sessions per week) or a control group [CG (two sessions per week)]. Sleep quality, excessive daytime sleepiness, and quality of life were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), SF-36, respectively. Generalized estimated equations verified differences between groups over time. RESULTS: Differences were observed in domains sleep latency (RT: Δ -1.0 ± 0.3 vs. CG: 0.2 ± 0.2; p = 0.018), sleep duration (RT: Δ -0.6 ± 0.3 vs. CG: -0.2 ± 0.2; p = 0.012), sleeping medication (RT: Δ -0.2 ± 0.1 vs. CG: 0.8 ± 0.3; p = 0.007), and overall PSQI score (RT: Δ -3.2 ± 0.6 vs. CG: 0.2 ± 0.8; p = 0.004). Regarding SF-36, differences were found in emotional aspects (RT: Δ 29.6 ± 14.8 vs. CG: -17.9 ± 10.0; p = 0.008) and global score (RT: Δ 10.8 ± 3.3 vs. CG: -3.4 ± 3.1; p = 0.002) were observed. No difference was observed in ESS. CONCLUSION: An eight-week RT program improves subjective sleep quality and quality of life in adults with moderate to severe OSA. Clinical trial registration (Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry [ReBec]): # RBR-2rg97kz. Date of registration: 01/17/2025.

papers.title: Pre-usage Perceptual Signals as Early Warning Indicators: A Machine Learning Framework for At-risk Student Detection in the Educational Metaverse
papers.authors: Eyaa Naimi, Mourad Abed
papers.abstract: Immersive learning environments, particularly the educational metaverse, offer substantial opportunities for interactive, collaborative, and personalised learning. However, many students struggle during initial adoption, often leading to disengagement or dropout. This paper introduces and evaluates, at a proof-of-concept level, a perceptual prediction framework for the early identification of students showing low adoption propensity (a pre-usage risk marker for subsequent disengagement) in educational metaverse environments, relying exclusively on perceptual data. Distinct from traditional models, this framework purposefully excludes Behavioural Intention (BI) from the predictor set, using it solely to operationalise the risk target, and focuses instead on the instrumental and affective appraisals that precede explicit intent. The framework integrates seven perceptual dimensions drawn from the Technology Acceptance Model and its affective and trust-related extensions, including Hedonic Motivation, Perceived Enjoyment, Perceived Usefulness and Attitude. Analyses draw on a publicly available secondary dataset of 215 Malaysian university students, collected through a single cross-sectional questionnaire administration prior to any metaverse exposure. K-means clustering yields four engagement readiness strata (retained on pedagogical rather than statistical grounds; internal validity indices favour a two-cluster solution), with a low-readiness stratum ( $$n = 31$$ ; 14.4%) constituting the primary intervention target. Random Forest and Logistic Regression perform equivalently on the held-out test set (81.40% and 79.07%; exact McNemar test, $$p = 1.00$$ ) and show strong discrimination (macro ROC-AUC =.922 and.939). Because the risk labels are derived from Behavioural Intention, which correlates strongly with all predictors, these results should be read as evidence of perceptual discriminability rather than as an independently validated predictive system. They nonetheless indicate that pre-usage perceptual signals carry sufficient discriminative information to support proactive pedagogical intervention before platform entry. Two constraints qualify these findings: the risk labels derive from a construct that shares substantial variance with the predictors, and heterotrait–monotrait ratios indicate limited discriminant validity among the affective constructs. Future work should establish convergent validity against longitudinal behavioural traces and replicate the framework across culturally and institutionally diverse settings.

papers.authors: Şükrü Mehmet Ertürk, Sıtkı Safa Taflan

papers.title: When machines learn with organizations: AI ‐enabled knowledge creation and entrepreneurship
papers.authors: Linhui Wu, Shaker A. Zahra, Niron Hashai
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary To promote entrepreneurship and new business development, firms will increasingly rely on new forms of knowledge creation to manage environments marked by technological change and radical uncertainty. We argue that as generative artificial intelligence (Gen‐AI) becomes embedded in organizational processes, knowledge creation will no longer remain solely a human activity. Instead, it will increasingly emerge from hybrid interactions between human actors and firm‐specific, closed Gen‐AI systems. These systems begin to participate directly in how knowledge is generated, recombined, internalized, shared, and converted into entrepreneurial initiatives such as corporate entrepreneurship, spin‐offs, and new business models. We also reconceptualize organizational knowledge creation as a hybrid human–AI process and propose a reordered knowledge creation cycle that induces multiple knowledge spirals, captures the emergence of new agents, and the generation of diverse types of knowledge, with faster temporal dynamics. Building on this perspective, we offer a research agenda for future scholarship. Managerial Summary We discuss how firm‐specific generative AI systems are likely to fundamentally alter the ways firms generate knowledge, respond to change, and sustain long‐term renewal. We propose that rather than replacing human judgment, closed Gen‐AI changes where knowledge originates as well as how quickly it evolves, and how broadly it circulates across organizational boundaries. This means that the managerial challenge is less about adopting AI and more about designing knowledge systems and structuring knowledge flows. Executives and entrepreneurs alike need to decide how to structure human–AI collaborations, how much autonomy to grant closed Gen‐AI systems, and how to prevent speed from overwhelming sensemaking. Our work underscores that although hybrid knowledge creation promises faster and more diverse learning, it also introduces risks related to opacity, trust, and cognitive lock‐in. Firms that deliberately orchestrate the role of closed Gen‐AI in their learning systems will be better positioned to shape future advantage by promoting innovation and entrepreneurial activities of different types.

papers.title: Describe or Direct? Artificial Intelligence Explanation Type, Trust and User Behaviour in a Medical Imaging Rostering Task
papers.authors: Kait O’Callahan, Sharon Sitters, M O'Callahan, Adam Senior-Partridge, Max Kirtley
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare, with most healthcare AI applications concentrated in radiology. While explainable AI (XAI) has been proposed as a means of improving transparency and trust, the relationship between explanation features, trust and user behaviour remains underexplored, particularly in healthcare contexts. This study examined how final-year medical imaging students interacted with descriptive and prescriptive AI explanations during a simulated rostering task, with a focus on trust and user behaviour. METHODS: A human-grounded evaluation using an explanatory mixed methods design was undertaken. Final year medical imaging students completed simulated rostering tasks using an XAI system that generated either descriptive or prescriptive explanations. Quantitative measures collected included task completion metrics, explanation regenerations and self-reported trust scores. Participants took part in semi-structured discussion groups to explore user perceptions, explanation preferences and trust dynamics. RESULTS: Trust scores increased across the experiment for both explanation types. Prescriptive explanations were associated with significantly fewer explanation regenerations and higher trust scores. Task time and failed solutions showed small-to-moderate effects favouring prescriptive explanations, but these differences did not reach statistical significance. Qualitative findings indicated a strong participant preference for prescriptive explanations, alongside critical engagement with inaccuracies and regeneration patterns. CONCLUSION: Prescriptive AI explanations were preferred over descriptive explanations within a simulated medical imaging rostering task and were associated with higher trust and reduced explanation regeneration. Participants demonstrated critical engagement with AI-generated outputs rather than uncritical acceptance. These findings contribute to emerging evidence regarding human interaction with XAI systems in healthcare workflow settings.

papers.title: Synthetic diversity: Racial depictions influence consumer responses to AI ‐generated models in advertising
papers.authors: Rhonda Hadi, Esther Uduehi, Felipe Thomaz, Andrew STEPHEN
papers.abstract: Abstract As brands seek to increase racial representation in their advertising, many are turning to AI‐generated images of humans (i.e., synthetic models) as a scalable solution. This research demonstrates that consumer reactions to synthetic models are asymmetric, depending on the racial identity being depicted. Across five studies, we demonstrate that disclosing the AI‐generated nature of models lowers firm evaluations when the featured models are from racially underrepresented groups (e.g., Black, Hispanic, and Asian models), but not when they are White. This effect is driven by reduced perceptions of the authenticity of the firm's inclusion efforts, which in turn elevate inferences of manipulative intent. Importantly, these negative effects can be mitigated when consumers are informed that the firm is owned by members of the depicted racial community, suggesting that credible signals of authentic community ties can neutralize the evaluative penalty of AI disclosure. Our findings extend research on racialized depictions in advertising by identifying synthetic depiction as a novel threat to the evaluative benefits of minority representation, and by theorizing why this threat operates asymmetrically by race. More broadly, our results highlight that technological innovations in advertising cannot be divorced from the social and historical contexts that shape their meaning.

papers.title: Making emotional intelligence explicit in AI ‐enhanced medical education: A curriculum perspective
papers.authors: Sulthan Al Rashid, Ravithraa Balakrishnan
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing medical education through simulation, personalised learning, and automated feedback. However, its integration into medical curricula raises important questions about preserving the human qualities essential to medical practice. Emotional intelligence (EI), encompassing self‐awareness, empathy, emotional regulation, and relationship management, is fundamental to patient‐centred communication and professional development, yet it may remain an implicit rather than an explicitly defined curriculum outcome. This curriculum perspective argues for the longitudinal integration of EI into undergraduate medical education. Drawing on established curriculum theories and emerging evidence on EI development and AI‐supported communication training, it proposes aligning EI learning outcomes with teaching activities, authentic patient encounters, reflective practice, mentorship, and assessment. AI‐assisted simulations may provide safe opportunities for students to practise communication and receive feedback, but they should complement rather than replace authentic interpersonal experiences and educator‐guided reflection. The article highlights the importance of curriculum mapping to support progressive EI development across preclinical, simulation‐based, and clinical learning environments. Making EI explicit within the formal curriculum can help ensure that technological innovation strengthens, rather than compromises, the humanistic foundations of medical education.

papers.title: Semantic distance metrics in anatomy education: Toward AI ‐assisted mapping of anatomy‐to‐clinical reasoning
papers.authors: Ugur Baran Kasirga
papers.abstract: Anatomy education traditionally emphasizes structural knowledge acquisition, with the implicit assumption that clinical reasoning capabilities will naturally follow. However, the cognitive pathway from anatomical understanding to clinical application is rarely linear or uniform. This article proposes a conceptual framework in which semantic distance-the conceptual separation between anatomical knowledge and clinical endpoints-operates at three analytically distinct levels: (1) the learner's internal cognitive network, shaped by prior experience and schema formation; (2) the structural distance within curriculum maps, ontologies, or knowledge graphs; and (3) the distributional proximity within large language model (LLM) embedding spaces, which may serve as a scalable computational proxy indicator for the first two levels. These three levels must be explicitly distinguished if semantic distance is to function as a useful construct in anatomy education. To illustrate the framework's utility, three worked examples are developed-the femoral nerve, coronary circulation, and spinal cord anatomy-accompanied by a preliminary computational illustration of embedding distances rather than an empirically validated diagnostic instrument. A practical educator workflow is proposed through which computational signals may be translated into targeted curriculum decisions. The article positions semantic distance metrics as complementary to curriculum network analytics and highlights how cross-domain transitions (from anatomy through physiology and pathology to clinical presentation) represent qualitatively different educational problems requiring different interventions. Prospective validation studies, multimodal computational approaches, and longitudinal curriculum outcome analyses are needed before this framework can be applied systematically.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Technologies and Their Role in Improving the Quality of Higher Education Outcomes from the Perspective of Faculty Members: A Field Study in the Faculties of Information Technology and Science at Gharyan University
papers.authors: Nawal Said Barkat
papers.journal: المجلة الإفريقية للدراسات المتقدمة في العلوم الإنسانية والاجتماعية
papers.abstract: تُعد تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي من الاتجاهات الحديثة التي أسهمت في إحداث تحولات متسارعة في مجال التعليم العالي، لما توفره من إمكانات تساعد على تطوير العملية التعليمية، وتحسين أساليب التدريس والتقييم، والارتقاء بجودة مخرجات التعليم العالي. وعلى الرغم من تزايد الاهتمام بتوظيف هذه التقنيات في المؤسسات التعليمية، فإن مستوى استخدامها ودرجة إسهامها في تحسين جودة مخرجات التعليم العالي لا يزالان بحاجة إلى مزيد من البحث والدراسة، ولا سيما في البيئة الجامعية الليبية. ومن هنا تتمثل مشكلة الدراسة في التعرف إلى درجة إسهام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تحسين جودة مخرجات التعليم العالي بجامعة غريان. وتهدف الدراسة إلى التعرف على مستوى استخدام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي، وقياس درجة إسهامها في تحسين جودة مخرجات التعليم العالي. ولتحقيق أهداف الدراسة، اسْتُخْدِم المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، وجُمِعت البيانات الأولية عن طريق الاستبانة، حيث تم توزيع 50 استبانة على أعضاء هيئة التدريس في كليتي العلوم وتقنية المعلومات بجامعة غريان، واسترداد 44 استبانة، منها 42 استبانة صالحة للتحليل. وأظهرت النتائج أن مستوى استخدام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي جاء بدرجة متوسطة، كما كشفت عن وجود علاقة طردية ذات دلالة إحصائية بين استخدام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي وتحسين جودة مخرجات التعليم العالي، ووجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية تعزى إلى متغير الكلية وعدد الدورات التدريبية، في حين لم تظهر فروق تعزى إلى النوع. وأوصت الدراسة بتعزيز توظيف تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في العملية التعليمية، وتطوير برامج تدريبية مستمرة لأعضاء هيئة التدريس، والاهتمام بتطوير البنية التحتية الرقمية بما يدعم الاستخدام الفعال لهذه التقنيات ويسهم في تحسين جودة مخرجات التعليم العالي.

papers.title: OFFER (One-Formula-Facilitates-Every-Relation) for Calculus
papers.authors: Samuel S. P. Shen
papers.abstract: The large number of calculus formulas makes learning calculus heavily memory-dependent and can scare away many students. Based on Issac Newton's idea of prediction, this paper shows that calculus students need to master only one critical formula: his proposition that, given boundary data, one can predict the interior and vice versa. We can treat other formulas as consequences of the formula for this proposition. In 1-, 2-, and 3-dimensional spaces, this formula corresponds to the fundamental theorem of calculus, Green's theorem, and the divergence theorem. This approach is summarized as OFFER (one-formula-facilitates-every-relationship) for calculus education. This paper demonstrates the method and advantages of the OFFER pedagogy. The OFFER approach can accelerate the pace of calculus teaching, provide deeper insight into calculus, inspire questions from students, and naturally facilitate the inclusion of real-world data, artificial intelligence (AI), and computer coding in the calculus series. Consequently, OFFER may serve as a way to modernize calculus curricula in the era of AI and the digital economy.

papers.title: Functional neuroimaging as a tool to understand social determinants of health in cognitive aging and ADRD: a scoping review
papers.authors: Shirine Moukaled, Natalie L. Marchant, Jade E. Jenkins, Owen Carmichael, Isabella Manrique, Adea Rich
papers.abstract: The social, structural, and physical conditions in which individuals live, work, and age, collectively termed social determinants of health (SDOH), are associated with risk of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD). Differences in brain function in later life may offer understanding of how SDOH become biologically embedded and confer differential ADRD risk. However, how functional neuroimaging techniques have been used to study SDOH in cognitive aging and ADRD has yet to be systematically characterized. We therefore conducted a scoping review. Three databases were searched, 2,930 articles were screened, and 41 studies were included. Education was the most frequently studied SDOH domain, accounting for 65.9% (k = 27) of studies, followed by economic and occupation (k = 9, 22.0%), social and community (k = 5, 12.2%), food (k = 4, 9.8%), and physical environment (k = 3, 7.3%). Of the 41 studies, five (12.2%) examined multidomain determinants and one study (2.4%) examined three determinants each from different domains. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) was most frequently employed (k = 31, 75.6%), followed by electroencephalography (EEG; k = 7, 17.1%), and magnetoencephalography (MEG; k = 4, 9.8%). One study (2.4%) employed a multimodal approach, while none used functional near-infrared spectroscopy. Resting state paradigms (k = 27, 65.9%) outnumbered task-based (k = 14, 34.1%) and most studies were cross-sectional (k = 38, 92.7%). The predominant focus on education, fMRI, and cross-sectional designs highlights many opportunities for future investigation of how SDOH may be associated with later life brain function.

papers.title: Percepción y uso de la inteligencia artificial entre docentes de carreras biomédicas
papers.authors: Fernando Castro Sánchez, Carlos Troya
papers.abstract: Introduction: The incorporation of artificial intelligence into biomedical education presents opportunities to strengthen teaching and research, but also raises questions regarding teacher training, academic integrity, and the preservation of the humanistic component of training. Objective: To analyze the perception and use of artificial intelligence tools among faculty members in biomedical programs at an Ecuadorian university, considering their academic characteristics and prior training in this technology. Material and Methods: An observational, exploratory, cross-sectional study was conducted between April and June 2025. Participants included 46 faculty members from biomedical programs at the Universidad Regional Autónoma de los Andes who were selected via non-probability convenience and snowball sampling. A structured 13-item questionnaire—previously subjected to content validation and a pilot test—was administered; it demonstrated adequate internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.817). Frequencies, percentages, and descriptive measures were calculated; chi-square and Fisher’s exact tests were used to explore associations between categorical variables. Results: The results show that 89.1% of the faculty members considered training in artificial intelligence necessary, and over 60% acknowledged the favorable effects of its incorporation on teaching practice and learning. Moreover, 87% indicated a need for pedagogical guidelines. At the same time, 47.8% believed these tools could foster inappropriate academic practices, and 41.3% questioned their contribution to intellectual work. Although descriptive differences were observed based on sex, teaching experience, and prior training, the associations explored did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions: There is a favorable disposition toward incorporating artificial intelligence into biomedical education, accompanied by ethical and pedagogical reservations. Its integration requires continuous teacher training, institutional guidance, and clear criteria to promote a usage that is critical, responsible, and compatible with the humanistic dimension of health sciences education.

papers.title: D-HERTS: Dehumanisation as a regulatory strategy at perceiving the suffering of others. Laguntza 1: EEG experiment..
papers.authors: Enrique García Marco, Naira Delgado, Naira Delgado, Joana López-Pigüi, Katia Rolán
papers.abstract: The aim of this research project is to empirically investigate the role of dehumanisation in serving as an emotional regulation mechanism when individuals witness others in states of suffering, pain, and emotional exhaustion. One of the main novelties of this non-oriented research project is to incorporate the approach of social neuroscience into the study of processes of social exclusion and dehumanisation. This perspective will lead to exploring and understanding some of the cognitive and emotional brain mechanisms that intervene in dehumanisation, specifically when it is displayed as an emotional regulatory strategy. Integrating the dehumanisation theoretical models from social psychology and the body of knowledge on pain perception from social neuroscience will lead to a unique and valuable set of results, with significant theoretical and applied implications. Thus, the primary objective of this research project is to forge new avenues of inquiry within the realm of dehumanisation, expanding our comprehension by scrutinising the psychological processes and neural mechanisms underpinning this phenomenon. The proposal aligns with the criteria of non-oriented research modality, demonstrating a clear commitment to be multidisciplinary in pursuit of theoretical insights into a complex social problem. Its potential future applicability spans across various domains, making it a pertinent and impactful contribution to the understanding of dehumanisation.

papers.title: Jismoniy tarbiya ta’limida raqamli texnologiyalar va sun’iy intellektdan foydalanishning nazariy-metodik asoslari
papers.authors: Asliddin Nuriddinov
papers.abstract: This article analyses the theoretical and methodological foundations for using digital technologies and artificial intelligence in physical education, drawing on sources from Uzbekistan, Russia and international research. The methods include a comparative analytical review of literature, thematic classification and pedagogical modelling. The instructional potential and limitations of digital learning platforms, movement video analysis, wearable sensors, virtual and augmented reality, and generative artificial intelligence are examined. A five-component conceptual model is proposed, integrating pedagogical objectives, tool selection, data quality, teacher oversight and outcome assessment. The model has not undergone empirical validation.

papers.title: การสรางสรรคนวตกรรมเพอการบรการสาธารณะ ขององคการบรหารสวนตำบลมะขามเตย อำเภอเมอง จงหวดสราษฎรธาน
papers.authors: Natthawat Rakdang, Supreecha Chamnanputtipon
papers.journal: วารสารสันตยาภิวัฒน์ วัดหนองนกกด
papers.abstract: The objectives of this thematic were to 1) study the innovation creation for public services of Makham Tia Subdistrict Administrative Organization, Mueang District, Surat Thani Province, and 2) propose guidelines for innovation creation for public services of Makham Tia Subdistrict Administrative Organization, Mueang District, Surat Thani Province. A mixed-method research approach was employed, employing a quantitative methodology. Data were collected from eligible voters in Makham Tia Subdistrict Administrative Organization, Mueang District, Surat Thani Province. A sample of 306 people was used. Statistics used included frequency, percentage, mean, and standard deviation. Qualitative research was employed to collect data using in-depth, structured interviews with six key informants and content analysis. The research finding were as follows: The innovation creation for public services of the Surat Thani District Administrative Organization, in all 6 aspects, was at a high level ( = 3.85, S.D. = 0.65). When considering each aspect in order of average, it was found that all items were at a high level. In order of average from highest to lowest, it was found that the aspect with the highest average was good governance ( = 4.32, S.D. = 0.68), followed by natural resources and environmental management ( = 3.97, S.D. = 0.71), and the aspect with the lowest average was economic development ( = 3.52, S.D. = 0.71), with the lowest average, respectively. Guidelines for creating innovation for public services of the Makham Tia Subdistrict Administrative Organization, Mueang District, Surat Thani Province through a model called the DDCAM Model, namely D stands for Design Thinking (development of ideas), D stands for Digital Innovation (use of digital technology), C stands for Co-Creation (participation), A stands for Agile &Systems Thinking (systematic and flexible management), and M stands for Monitoring & Feedback (continuous evaluation and improvement).

papers.title: Data and materials for: Equal access, unequal conversion? First-generation college students, generative AI use, and critical-thinking dispositions
papers.authors: Wenye Li
papers.abstract: This project contains the materials supporting the article "Equal access, unequal conversion? First-generation college students, generative AI use, and critical-thinking dispositions" (Wenye Li, Ling Wang, Yifan Guo). The study draws on an online survey of 2,524 undergraduates at 35 Chinese research universities, administered from June 2025 by a research team at the Institute of Education, Nanjing University. Publicly available: the questionnaire (Chinese original with English translation), a codebook, and the Python code that reproduces all reported analyses. The de-identified data set is stored in the component "Data (restricted access)" and is available to authorised researchers for non-commercial academic use; requests should be sent to the corresponding author, Wenye Li (wenyeli@njau.edu.cn).

papers.abstract: This academic article aims to examine and synthesize knowledge concerning the transformation of higher education instructors’ roles in the era of artificial intelligence (AI). Specifically, the study focuses on: (1) analyzing the transition of instructors’ roles from knowledge transmitters to learning designers; (2) examining learning behaviors and challenges faced by digital-era students in using AI tools; (3) exploring challenges and limitations encountered by Thai higher education instructors and institutions in terms of digital competencies and supporting structures; (4) synthesizing integrative approaches to teaching and learning while upholding professional ethics in AI-enhanced classrooms; and (5) proposing policy and practical recommendations for sustainable faculty development and educational management. This study employs documentary and conceptual research methods. Data were collected from academic literature, related empirical studies, and national and international policy documents published between 2019 and 2025. The data were analyzed using content analysis and conceptual synthesis to identify key patterns, relationships, and implications relevant to higher education in the AI era.

papers.title: RESONANCE, CO-CREATION, SYMBIOSIS: RESEARCH ON COLLABORATIVE INNOVATION PATHWAYS IN THE INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE CIRCLE—CASE STUDY QINHUAI LANTERN
papers.authors: Chen Xi, Phuvanart Rattanarungsikul
papers.journal: วารสารสันตยาภิวัฒน์ วัดหนองนกกด
papers.abstract: China’s intensified efforts to safeguard intangible cultural heritage (ICH) have expanded development opportunities, yet disparities among ICH items persist. This study introduces the concept of an ICH cultural circle and uses Qinhuai lanterns as a case to examine cross-project linkages and shared inheritance challenges. Drawing on qualitative content analysis, field observations, and interviews with practitioners, the research identifies the cultural foundations that structure inter-ICH collaboration and their potential to reduce developmental asymmetries. The study proposes pathways—cultural excavation, resource integration, and industrial coordination—to advance collaborative innovation and enhance the sustainable transmission of ICH.

papers.title: Developing IELTS learners’ feedback literacy through AI-assisted self-assessment and revision
papers.authors: Zarnigor Mirzayeva
papers.journal: Academic Journal of Science, Technology and Education
papers.abstract: This conceptual and methodological article examines how IELTS Academic learners can develop feedback literacy when using generative artificial intelligence (AI) for Writing and Speaking practice. It distinguishes receiving an automated suggestion from interpreting its relevance, evaluating its evidence, making a revision decision and checking transfer to a new task. Drawing on established feedback theory, student feedback literacy and formative assessment scholarship, the article proposes a teacher-mediated decision protocol and a transparent revision log. Two illustrative task scenarios demonstrate how learners can compare AI suggestions with IELTS assessment criteria without treating automated comments as official band scores. The contribution is a practical pedagogical framework for cultivating critical engagement with AI feedback, not an experimental claim about score gains. The framework also identifies safeguards concerning learner authorship, privacy, and teacher verification.

papers.title: การจดการการสอสารในการพฒนาศกยภาพการทองเทยวเชงวฒนธรรมมณฑลไหหนาน
papers.authors: Zeng Ting, Puripat Kaewtathanawattan, Nisakorn Yindeecha
papers.journal: วารสารสันตยาภิวัฒน์ วัดหนองนกกด
papers.abstract: This research aimed to 1) study communication management and the development of cultural tourism potential in Hainan Province, and 2) study guidelines for developing communication management for cultural tourism in Hainan Province. This study employed a mixed-methods research design. Qualitative research utilized semi-structured interviews with 18 key informants, and data were analyzed using content analysis. Quantitative research used questionnaires with a reliability coefficient of 0.84. Data were collected from a sample of 376 tourists, derived from 400 distributed questionnaires, representing a response rate of 94.00%. Statistics used for data analysis included Mean, Standard Deviation, and Multiple Regression Analysis.. The research findings, classified by objectives, revealed that: 1) Regarding the first objective, current communication management faces a credibility crisis, where discrepancies between promotional content and actual experiences accounted for 37.6% of all complaints, resulting in a lack of efficiency in attracting repeat tourists. 2) Regarding the second objective, development guidelines consist of integrating four key dimensions: merging technological innovation, creating a consistent content calendar, integrating culture with ecology, and utilizing cultural heritage inheritors as primary communicators. Hypothesis testing indicated that technological innovation factors significantly impacted engagement (β=0.88), and sender credibility positively influenced satisfaction (β=0.53) The new knowledge gained is the Co-Creation Value Communication Model, which transforms the tourist's role from a message receiver to an experience co-creator.

papers.title: RESEARCH ON SUSTAINABLE COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES OF INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE UNDER EXPERIENCE DESIGN STRATEGIES: TAKING JIANGSU WOODBLOCK NEW YEAR PICTURES AS AN EXAMPLE
papers.authors: QIUTING ZHU, Anucha Pangkesorn
papers.journal: วารสารสันตยาภิวัฒน์ วัดหนองนกกด
papers.abstract: Jiangsu woodblock New Year pictures are an important form of China's intangible cultural heritage, but their contemporary dissemination is confronted with challenges such as a shrinking audience, a single form of experience, and weakened cultural contextualization. Existing research mainly emphasizes historical verification, style analysis or innovation at the product level, leaving a research gap in user-centered and sustainable communication frameworks. This study employs the theory of experience design to construct a new paradigm for the dissemination of Jiangsu woodblock New Year pictures. The research aims to: (1) clarify the cultural origin and social functions of woodblock New Year pictures in the Jiangnan region; (2) Diagnose core communication barriers in the digital and globalized media environment; (3) Build an experience-driven strategic model of "scenario-based - interactive - digital" to support long-term revitalization and public participation. This study employed a hybrid approach - including literature analysis, questionnaire surveys (n=167), field observations, and interviews with provincial inheritors - to identify major obstacles such as fragmented audience journeys, limited multi-sensory engagement, and disconnection from contemporary lifestyles. The research results show that integrating experience design into the dissemination of intangible cultural heritage can effectively promote emotional resonance, behavioral participation and meaning construction. The proposed strategic model forms a closed-loop path, ranging from digital archiving to scenario-based integration across education, cultural tourism and business Settings, and finally to user co-creation and social media dissemination.

papers.title: Beyond the Technological Turning Point: An Analytical Perspective on AI Trends and Policy Directions for Building Societal Resilience in Thailand
papers.authors: Sutida Lekawattana
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence is reshaping global systems, not only through technological innovation but also by transforming economic structures, labour markets, education systems, and governance paradigms. This article provides a critical analysis of key developments in artificial intelligence, from the evolution of large language models to advancements toward artificial general intelligence, and examines their multidimensional implications through a case study of KASIKORN Business Technology Group. Drawing upon both organisational practices and national policy frameworks, the article identifies five significant trends: (1) a shift from digitally confined artificial intelligence to forms that interact with the physical world; (2) a restructuring of labour and business operations; (3) emerging social and ethical risks stemming from excessive reliance on artificial intelligence; (4) the enduring importance of human leadership; and (5) adaptive strategies to prepare organisations for the AI era. The article argues that Thailand must move beyond passive adaptation and adopt proactive, system-level strategies in response to the transformation driven by artificial intelligence. These strategies should include strategic investment in lifelong learning, the establishment of ethical and inclusive innovation governance mechanisms, the advancement of interdisciplinary AI research, and the implementation of incentive schemes to support integration into business and education. In conclusion, artificial intelligence should not be perceived merely as a disruptive force, but rather as a transformative ecosystem that requires human-centred leadership to ensure equitable and sustainable integration into Thai society.

papers.title: THE EFFECT OF DEEP LEARNING ON STUDENTS' LEARNING MOTIVATION THROUGH THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGY IN ELEMENTARY SCHOOL (Case Study at SDN 1 Warung Jeruk Purwakarta)
papers.authors: Irma Nuraida, Sedarmayanti, Vip Paramarta, Yuyun Yuniarsih, Kosasih
papers.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of deep learning on students' learning motivation through the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology in elementary schools. The study uses a quantitative approach with a survey method. The research objects include deep learning , the use of AI technology, and students' learning motivation. The study population was all fifth and sixth grade students of SDN 1 Warung Jeruk Purwakarta in 2026, totaling 136 students, with a sampling technique using total sampling . Data were collected through a questionnaire with a five-level Likert scale and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The research model tested the direct effect of deep learning on the use of AI technology, the effect of AI use on learning motivation, the direct effect of deep learning on learning motivation, and the indirect effect through the use of AI. The results of the analysis showed that deep learning had a positive effect on the use of AI technology with a coefficient of 0.541, the use of AI had a positive effect on learning motivation with a coefficient of 0.342, and deep learning had a positive effect on learning motivation with a coefficient of 0.431. The use of AI also mediated the effect of deep learning on learning motivation, with an indirect effect of 0.185. This finding suggests that integrating deep learning and AI approaches can support more meaningful, interactive learning and enhance student motivation.

papers.title: Model Pembelajaran Menulis Kreatif untuk Keterampilan Abad ke-21: Eksplorasi Bibliometrik tentang Kreativitas, Berpikir Kritis, dan Literasi Digital
papers.authors: Indra Rasyid Julianto, Anugerah Agung Pohan, Arif Yuandana Sinaga, Hasnah Setiani, Yusro Edy Nugroho, Subyantoro Subyantoro, Diardana Prima Sintasari, Pramisdi Winanto Saputro, Ina Ina
papers.abstract: Transformasi pendidikan abad ke-21 menuntut pengembangan keterampilan kreativitas, berpikir kritis, komunikasi, dan literasi digital melalui pembelajaran yang adaptif terhadap perkembangan teknologi. Dalam konteks tersebut, pembelajaran menulis kreatif mengalami pergeseran paradigma dari pendekatan berbasis produk menuju pendekatan yang mengintegrasikan teknologi digital dan kecerdasan buatan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis tren penelitian model pembelajaran menulis kreatif serta mengidentifikasi keterkaitannya dengan kreativitas, berpikir kritis, dan literasi digital melalui pendekatan bibliometrik. Data penelitian diperoleh dari basis data Scopus periode 2016–2026 dengan total 344 publikasi yang memenuhi kriteria inklusi. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan VOSviewer melalui pemetaan ko-kemunculan kata kunci (co-occurrence analysis) untuk mengidentifikasi struktur intelektual dan arah perkembangan penelitian. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan empat klaster utama, yaitu pembelajaran menulis berbasis kecerdasan buatan (ChatGPT, GPT, LLM), pembelajaran berbasis proyek, literasi digital dan multimodalitas, serta pengembangan berpikir kritis dalam menulis. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa kreativitas tetap menjadi inti pembelajaran menulis, tetapi berkembang melalui integrasi teknologi digital, kolaborasi, dan pemecahan masalah autentik. Penelitian ini juga mengungkap kesenjangan berupa minimnya model yang mengintegrasikan kreativitas, berpikir kritis, literasi digital, dan kecerdasan buatan secara simultan. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini menawarkan arah pengembangan AI-Assisted Project-Based Creative Writing Model sebagai paradigma pembelajaran menulis kreatif yang relevan dengan tuntutan keterampilan abad ke-21 dan era Society 5.0.

papers.title: Разработка интерфейса группового взаимодействия агентов при передаче команды через ЭЭГ-сигнал: Аннотации
papers.authors: S. Akopyan, И. Брак, G. Kiselev, С. Акопян, И. Брак, Г. Киселев
papers.journal: ФИЗИКА ЭЛЕМЕНТАРНЫХ ЧАСТИЦ И АТОМНОГО ЯДРА
papers.abstract: This paper presents a cognitive architecture for controling robotic agents via a brain–computer interface (BCI). Aimed at patients with motor and speech impairments, the system translates high-level user intentions, decoded from EEG (Electroencephalography) signals, into conflict-free navigation for a group of wheelchairs. Experiments confirm the feasibility of multiagent control based on a single global command, without requiring direct human intervention.

papers.title: Системный подход к построению образовательной среды в инженерии искусственного интеллекта с применением когнитивно-смысловой интеграции
papers.authors: E. N. Cheremisina, E. Yu. Kirpicheva, V. N. Dobrynin, A. Milovidova, Е. Н. Черемысина, Кирпичева Елена Юрьевна, В. Н. Добрынин, A. Milovidova
papers.journal: ФИЗИКА ЭЛЕМЕНТАРНЫХ ЧАСТИЦ И АТОМНОГО ЯДРА
papers.abstract: This study aims to develop a methodology for meaning-centered organization of the educational process in artificial intelligence engineering. Its key component is a hierarchical system of metric conceptual templates (HMCT), which structures learning goals, objectives, and methods, with educational content built as a series of adaptive semantic trajectories. The novelty lies in the creation of a new type of educational environment architecture, where digital resources serve as an instrumental shell, and the semantic core is formed through HMCT. A supporting element is the virtual computer laboratory, which provides access to modern tools and interactive practices. Pilot testing showed that this cognitive-semantic architecture increases student engagement, enhances knowledge interpretation, and promotes the development of engineering thinking.

papers.title: Progettare con l'IA, insegnare il corpo: uno studio pilota sulla formazione iniziale degli insegnanti per l'Embodied Emotional Literacy
papers.authors: Dario Lombardi
papers.journal: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: Questo studio pilota indaga se e come l'intelligenza artificiale generativa possa fungere da mediatore embodied nella formazione universitaria, supportando 54 studenti di Didattica Generale (LM-85bis, a.a. 2025–2026) nella co-progettazione di interventi per l'Embodied Emotional Literacy (EEL). Il costrutto EEL — introdotto come contributo teorico originale — integra consapevolezza corporea, interocettività e movimento espressivo come percorsi fondativi della regolazione emotiva e dell'apprendimento situato. In una sessione strutturata secondo il modello ADDIE (120 minuti), i partecipanti hanno co-progettato interventi body-oriented per profili BES con un chatbot AI (Claude Sonnet, Anthropic). Al termine, un questionario unico con then-test retrospettivo documenta un incremento di autoefficacia di grande entità (d = 1,266; p < 0,001), un'elevata acquisizione teorica (Knowledge Test: M = 8,87/10) e una percezione medio-alta dell'utilità dell'AI (PAUID: M = 3,68/5). Il 98,1% riconosce la necessità di includere sistematicamente la formazione corporeo-emotiva nei curricula universitari.

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Performance of Small and Medium Enterprises in Kosovo
papers.authors: Blerim Dragusha, Saso Josimovski
papers.journal: Studia Universitatis „Vasile Goldis” Arad – Economics Series
papers.abstract: This study investigates the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption on the performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Kosovo, a context where firms face resource constraints but play a pivotal role in economic resilience. Using survey data from 210 SMEs and applying correlation and multiple regression analyses, the research explores how AI integration affects internal management processes, strategic adaptability, and overall organizational outcomes. The objectives were to assess the extent to which AI influences human resource management (HRM), decision-making quality, and customer experience, and to identify enabling factors such as digital readiness and employee training. The findings reveal a strong positive relationship between AI adoption and internal performance indicators, particularly HRM efficiency, where AI training emerged as the strongest predictor of improved outcomes. Decision-making quality was also positively associated with AI, albeit more modestly. However, results indicate a negative relationship between AI usage and customer experience, suggesting that current deployments prioritize internal efficiency at the expense of personalized service delivery. The study concludes that while AI can act as a catalyst for productivity and innovation, its benefits in customer-facing functions remain underutilized. These insights highlight the importance of aligning technological investment with workforce upskilling and customer-centric strategies. The paper contributes to the broader discourse on digital transformation in developing economies by offering recommendations for SME leaders and policymakers to foster inclusive and sustainable AI-driven growth.

papers.title: Адаптивная автоматизированная система ответов для виртуальной компьютерной лаборатории и LMS Moodle с использованием LLM, RAG и бессерверной архитектуры: Аннотации
papers.authors: Skulskiy, E. Cheremisina, E. Kirov, E. Kirpicheva, Yu. Medvedeva, S. Potemkina, D. Sidorov, N. Tokareva, Yu., Ye. Mazhitova, A. Nechaevsky, Скульский, Е. Черемисина, Е. Киров, Е. Кирпичева, Ю. Медведева, С. Потемкина, Д. Сидоров, Н. Токарева, Ю., E. Mazhitova, А. Нечаевский
papers.journal: ФИЗИКА ЭЛЕМЕНТАРНЫХ ЧАСТИЦ И АТОМНОГО ЯДРА
papers.abstract: An adaptive automated response system for Virtual Computer Lab and LMS Moodle is presented, leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), a finetuned Llama (or Gemma, Qwen, etc.) model, and serverless architecture. Integrated with Moodle and Supabase, it delivers context-aware responses tailored to user roles (student, instructor, administrator). A self-learning mechanism driven by feedback enhances response accuracy and reducing technical support workload. An interactive interface with custom widgets improves user experience.

papers.title: The Role of Technology in English Language Learning Among University Students
papers.authors: Nodira Xusanova, Tolibjon Yuldoshev
papers.journal: American Journal of Language, Literacy and Learning in STEM Education (2993-2769)
papers.abstract: Technology has become an essential part of English language learning, offering innovative ways to develop language skills through digital tools and platforms. Previous research has highlighted the benefits of technology in language learning, particularly in improving learners’ engagement and performance. However, there is still a lack of research examining how university students practically use these technologies, especially in terms of frequency, specific activities, and the integration of artificial intelligence tools in the context of Uzbekistan. Therefore, this study aims to investigate how university students use technology for learning English, the benefits they gain, and the challenges they face. A quantitative research design was employed, and data were collected through a structured survey administered to 39 undergraduate students at Kimyo International University in Tashkent. The results show that most students use technology daily, mainly through smartphones, and primarily for vocabulary learning, listening practice, and grammar support, while distraction is identified as the main challenge. Overall, the study concludes that technology positively supports English language learning, but its effectiveness depends on strategic use and the ability to manage distractions.

papers.title: Humanizing AI-generated exemplars: Human-source framing facilitates group creative ideation
papers.authors: Yueyue Ge, Yihui LIU, Qiannan Ruan, KelongLu, Yihui LIU, KelongLu, Ke Jiang
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated creative exemplars are increasingly used as scalable digital instructional resources in creativity education. However, it remains unclear whether labeling identical exemplars as human- or AI-generated shapes how learners engage in group creative activities. We tested this possibility in 113 dyads using an fNIRS hyperscanning group creative ideation paradigm. Dyads completed creative ideation tasks before, during, and after exemplar-stimulation. During stimulation, the human- and AI-attribution groups received identical exemplars labeled as produced by human or AI, whereas the control group received no exemplar. Human attribution increased idea uniqueness during stimulation relative to both the other phases and the AI-attribution and control groups. AI attribution temporarily increased switching among ideation pathways. Neither behavioral effect persisted after exemplar withdrawal. The two attribution groups did not differ in exemplar-category overlap or nearest-exemplar semantic distance, but human-attribution dyads rated the exemplars as more helpful. Human attribution also increased interbrain synchronization (IBS) in bilateral premotor and supplementary motor cortices during stimulation, whereas AI attribution was associated with decreased IBS in the left supramarginal gyrus and right frontopolar cortex from pre- to post-stimulation. Thus, exemplar-source attribution shapes the process and outcome of group creative ideation, revealing an important social-contextual factor in AI-supported creativity education.

papers.title: Citizen Trust in AI Regulatory Regimes in Four EU Countries
papers.authors: B.J.A. (Benjamin) Leidorf - Tidå, Pascal König
papers.abstract: Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) applications is deemed crucial for uptake of the technology and the development of an AI market. In the present article, we argue that the institutional design of regulatory regimes matters for whether citizens trust AI systems. We study how trust in AI systems depends on who the responsible regulator is, the scope of the regulator’s scrutiny of AI systems, and the involvement of external stakeholders in regulatory oversight. Based on a conjoint design, we examine how respondents value these institutional design choices for the case of high-risk AI systems used in health care. Using samples from Lithuania, Romania, Sweden, and the Netherlands, with 4001 respondents overall, the pre-registered experiment shows that citizens have more trust in AI systems if vendors, civil society and especially independent researchers are involved in oversight, and if regulators actively scrutinize AI systems rather than relying solely on self-reporting. At least in two countries, citizens also seem to have more trust in AI systems if the sectoral health care regulator is the responsible regulator instead of a cross-sectoral regulator such as the national Data Protection Authority or a specific AI regulator.

papers.title: NeuralCoach: a Smartphone-Based Brain-Computer Interface for Workplace Well-Being and Safety
papers.authors: Gabriela Herrera Altamira, Dennis Wobrock, Solène Le
papers.journal: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)
papers.abstract: NeuralCoach is a mobile brain-computer interface (BCI) platform for real-time cognitive monitoring and neurofeedback in ecological settings. Combining wearable electroencephalography (EEG), machine-learning algorithms, and smartphone-based feedback, the system estimates neurocognitive indicators such as vigilance, mental workload, and stress while supporting cognitive self-regulation. Originally designed for adaptive digital learning, NeuralCoach integrates calibration procedures, relaxation and cognitive activation exercises, neurofeedback tasks, and longitudinal performance tracking through a mobile interface compatible with multiple EEG devices. By enabling neurophysiological assessment outside laboratory environments, NeuralCoach facilitates real-world neurocognitive monitoring. Current developments extend its use to occupational and safety-critical domains, highlighting the potential of mobile BCIs for neuroergonomic research, cognitive support, and workplace safety.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning A 1.2B Large Language Model for Systematic Review Screening in Educational Technology
papers.authors: Kweku Andoh Yamoah, Noah L. Schroeder, Emmanuel Dorley, Neha Rani, Caleb Schutz

papers.title: Early Exposure to Artificial Intelligence in Medical Education: A Knowledge, Attitude and Practice Study among Preclinical Medical Students from Mangaluru, India
papers.authors: Md Aayan Afroz, Suriyan S. Nair, Manjula Shantaram
papers.journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
papers.abstract: Introduction: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the study of machines that learn from collected data and use human-like reasoning. AI applications are already used in healthcare, and there is a need to understand the need for AI training in the medical curriculum. Aim: To assess the Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) related to AI among first- and second-year MBBS students. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at AJ Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Centre, Mangaluru, Karnataka, India from April to May 2026, among first- and second-year MBBS students via an online questionnaire; the sample size was 327. Based on existing KAP studies, the questionnaire collected data on AI knowledge (e.g., AI/ML concepts and applications), attitudes (e.g., beliefs about fostering AI knowledge despite its future application), and AI application. Categorical associations were analysed using Chisquare tests. Statistical significance was set at p-value <0.05. Results: Of 327 survey participants, 204 (62.39%) were firstyear medical students. Most reported at least basic knowledge of AI; however, few had prior training {26 (7.95%) attended AI workshops, and 41 (12.54%) received curriculum training}. Most students believed medical schools should teach AI concepts (269, 82.26%) and supported incorporating AI into the curriculum (193, 59.02%). ChatGPT was the most popular AI tool, used by 315 (96.33%) respondents, primarily for exam preparation and studying, with other uses less frequent. The key obstacles included insufficient knowledge/lack of proper training in AI (222, 67.89%) and concerns about data privacy and ethical issues (157,48.01%). Conclusion: Despite extensive exposure to AI (as most students used AI tools), students had limited knowledge or training in it. Students were optimistic about AI in healthcare and strongly supported AI education. These results suggest incorporating AI training into the medical curriculum to bridge knowledge gaps and meet learners’ needs.

papers.title: The AI Labor Legitimacy Paradox: A Governance Framework for ICT and Platform Firms
papers.authors: Hyun-Ju Yu, Myoungsug Chung
papers.abstract: As ICT and platform firms deploy generative AI at scale, software-intensive work, machine-readable performance records, and network visibility make both productivity claims and workforce effects unusually observable. Capital markets may reward credible AI-attributed productivity, while labor, regulators, and communities may penalize visible AI-attributed displacement. We conceptualize this bounded contradiction as the AI Labor Legitimacy Paradox, an empirical instance of a stakeholder-induced legitimacy paradox that extends paradox and institutional-complexity research. Attribution asymmetry, skill hollowing, and talent-flight signaling sustain the tension, while a signed visibility gap describes the early excess of displacement attention over productivity attention. We derive a 2×2 response typology (Replacer, Quiet Cutter, Reskiller, Augmenter), five falsifiable hypothesis families, and an operational measurement design. Korean cases illustrate classification rather than causal effects. An analytical model and reproducible power calculations clarify comparative statics and empirical feasibility constraints. The framework predicts stronger effects in software- and platform-intensive settings with extensive algorithmic recording, network spillovers, employment protection, and evolving disclosure obligations. Technological capability alone may therefore be insufficient; firms must also maintain a social license to automate.

papers.title: From innovation to implementation: a global scoping review of artificial intelligence applications, governance, and challenges in humanitarian contexts
papers.authors: Mahima Jose, Fouzia Mueen, Junaid Qadir, Alaa Ali Abd-Alrazaq, Kwalombota Kwalombota, Diana Maddah
papers.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a tool for supporting humanitarian action through hazards and crisis prediction, real time monitoring of evolving crisis conditions and humanitarian needs, resource allocation, and decision-making. However, evidence on how AI is implemented, evaluated, and governed across humanitarian contexts remains fragmented. In this scoping review, we mapped the global evidence on the application of AI in humanitarian settings, including its distribution across the emergency management cycle, deployment maturity, and evaluation. We also identified any governance considerations, as well as enabling factors for and challenges to its implementation, with particular attention to the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, Gulf Cooperation Council countries (GCC), and Qatar. Methods: The methodology of this scoping review followed the framework set by Arksey and O'Malley, which comprises the formulation of the research question, selection of records, data charting, and synthesis of findings. We searched six databases (ProQuest, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus), queried Google Scholar, and ran targeted grey literature searches through the webpages of major humanitarian organisations for records reporting on the application, implementation, or governance of AI in humanitarian contexts. We descriptively and narratively synthesised the extracted data. Results: We included 57 scholarly publications and 17 grey literature reports. Application of AI was most frequently reported in sudden-onset natural disasters, particularly floods and earthquakes, and was commonly used to support disaster monitoring, crisis informatics, search-and-rescue, logistics optimisation, hazard prediction, and geospatial analysis. Deep learning and machine learning were the most common model families. Across the emergency management cycle, most applications of AI focused on preparedness and response, while recovery was rarely addressed. Geographically, most evidence originated from Asia, while research from the MENA and GCC regions remained limited. Most reported systems remained prototypes or retrospectively validated models, with relatively few seeing operational deployment or field implementation. Governance issues were discussed more extensively in grey literature than in scholarly publications. Community participation, equity considerations, and formal governance frameworks were inconsistently reported. Conclusions: AI is increasingly being applied in humanitarian contexts, but it is heterogeneously distributed across regions, humanitarian contexts, and emergency management. Greater emphasis is needed on real-world deployment, implementation-focused evaluation, participatory approaches, and governance frameworks that support responsible, equitable, and context-sensitive AI adoption.

papers.title: Evaluating COPD care assistance: a comparative study of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, and ERNIE bot performance
papers.authors: Zhongshang Dai, Zihang Zeng, Zijie Zhan, Yan Chen
papers.abstract: Background: Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used to provide health information, yet their reliability in addressing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) care questions in the Chinese context remains unclear. To evaluate and compare the performance of three publicly available LLM chatbots - ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0 (OpenAI), and ERNIE Bot (Baidu) - in answering chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) care questions in China. Methods: We performed a cross-sectional comparative evaluation of three publicly available LLM chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, and ERNIE Bot). We developed 40 COPD care questions spanning 7 prespecified domains relevant to patient education and self-management. All questions were submitted in Chinese in independent new chat sessions to minimise context carryover. Three consultant-level respiratory physicians independently rated each response for accuracy (1 = poor, 2 = borderline, 3 = good). We summarised accuracy as the sum of three ratings (range 3-9) and derived a majority-vote accuracy category. For responses rated 'good' by majority vote, physicians additionally rated comprehensiveness on a five-point scale. Information quality was further assessed using a modified DISCERN framework and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) understandability and actionability domains. Results: Most responses were rated as 'good' for accuracy across chatbots. ERNIE Bot achieved higher total accuracy scores than ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4.0, and a higher proportion of 'good' ratings in this Chinese-language evaluation. However, comprehensiveness scores for 'good' responses were low across all systems (mean ~ 1.4-2.0/5), and PEMAT actionability was limited, indicating that few responses included concrete, patient-executable steps. Conclusions: Our findings suggest that LLM chatbots may support basic COPD patient education in Chinese settings, but current responses often lack sufficient comprehensiveness and actionable guidance. These tools should not be used as standalone clinical advice and require appropriate safeguards and clinician oversight.

papers.title: Transformasi Manajemen SDM di Era Digitalisasi : Analisis Pengaruh Teknologi AI dan Fleksibilitas Kerja terhadap Produktivitas Karyawan
papers.authors: Ridha Afrillia Wibowo, Muhammad Syafi’i, Muhammad Renaldin
papers.journal: Jurnal Semesta Ilmu Manajemen dan Ekonomi
papers.abstract: Transformasi digital mendorong organisasi mengubah cara mengelola sumber daya manusia (SDM), termasuk melalui penggunaan artificial intelligence (AI), sistem informasi SDM, dan pengaturan kerja yang lebih fleksibel. Artikel ini bertujuan menelaah bagaimana pemanfaatan AI dan fleksibilitas kerja berkaitan dengan produktivitas karyawan serta mengidentifikasi manfaat, tantangan, dan kondisi yang memengaruhi keberhasilannya. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan Systematic Literature Review (SLR) terhadap delapan tautan sumber yang telah dipilih peneliti. Sumber dipetakan berdasarkan jenis publikasi, fokus, metode yang dilaporkan, dan relevansinya dengan pertanyaan penelitian. Sintesis tematik menunjukkan bahwa digitalisasi fungsi SDM, HRIS, AI, dan platform pembelajaran daring berpotensi mendukung efisiensi administrasi serta pengembangan kompetensi. Fleksibilitas kerja juga berpotensi meningkatkan otonomi dan membantu pengaturan waktu, tetapi memerlukan target yang jelas, komunikasi efektif, kompetensi digital, dan batas kerja-kehidupan pribadi. Karena beberapa tautan berupa buku atau profil Google Scholar dan sebagian metadata belum terverifikasi lengkap, hasil kajian diposisikan sebagai sintesis tematik, bukan estimasi kausal atau meta-analisis. Kajian menyimpulkan bahwa dampak teknologi dan fleksibilitas terhadap produktivitas bergantung pada kesiapan organisasi, kesesuaian teknologi dengan tugas, tata kelola data, serta dukungan manajemen.

papers.title: The Effect of Artificial Intelligence-Supported Education on Students’ Academic Resilience: The Mediating Role of Psychological Capital
papers.authors: Jani Khan Soomro, Muhammad Maqsood Veesar, Ishrat Rehman
papers.abstract: This study examined the effect of artificial intelligence (AI)-supported education on students’ academic resilience, with particular emphasis on the mediating role of psychological capital. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed, and data were collected from 323 undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in public and private universities across Pakistan. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling, and data were collected through a structured questionnaire measuring AI-supported education, psychological capital, and academic resilience. The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics, employing descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, linear and multiple regression, and PROCESS Macro Model 4 with 5,000 bootstrap samples to assess the indirect effect. The illustrative results indicated a positive association between AI-supported education and academic resilience (r = .58, p < .001), with AI-supported education explaining 34% of the variance in academic resilience (R² = .34). Furthermore, AI-supported education and psychological capital jointly explained 48% of the variance in academic resilience (R² = .48). The mediation analysis suggested a positive indirect effect of AI-supported education on academic resilience through psychological capital (B = .24, 95% bootstrap CI [.17, .33]), indicating a potentially significant mediating relationship. These findings suggest that AI-supported learning practices and students’ psychological resources may contribute jointly to academic resilience. The study highlights the importance of integrating AI-supported educational practices with strategies that foster students’ psychological capital to help them cope with academic challenges. However, the reported statistical values are provisional illustrative estimates and must be verified against the actual dataset before the abstract is submitted as an empirical research report. The cross-sectional design and convenience sampling also limit causal interpretation and generalizability.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Accounting Pedagogy and SDG Alignment
papers.authors: Olugbenga Agboola, Moses Hlongoane
papers.journal: Journal of Computer Adaptive Testing in Africa
papers.abstract: Despite this interest in artificial intelligence-based accounting pedagogy, the extent to which African scholarship contributes to the field and aligns with sustainable development priorities remains underexplored. This study fills this gap by applying a PRISMA-guided bibliometric analysis alongside an assessment of alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals. Data were drawn from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, yielding a final sample of 148 publications released between 1986 and 2026. Bibliometric techniques, including performance analysis, Bradford’s Law, Lotka’s Law, co-authorship mapping, thematic analysis and conceptual structure mapping, were employed using the Bibliometrix R package. The findings point to a fast-growing research area with an annual growth rate of 5.34%, in which publication output has risen sharply since 2022, following the emergence of generative AI technologies. Research productivity and citation impact remain heavily concentrated in developed economies, particularly the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom, while African contributions are comparatively limited and largely driven by South Africa. Thematic analysis identifies artificial intelligence, accounting education, data analytics, skills development and higher education as dominant research clusters. Furthermore, the study from African researchers demonstrates substantial implicit alignment with SDG 4 and SDG 9. However, explicit integration of SDG frameworks within the literature remains limited. The study concludes that although African scholarship is contributing meaningfully to AI-driven educational innovation, greater investment in research capacity, digital infrastructure, international collaboration, and SDG-orientated scholarship is required to strengthen the continent’s influence in the global accounting education discourse and to support sustainable education.

papers.title: AI-ASSISTED JOURNALISM AND THE REPORTING OF CORPORATE FINANCIAL INFORMATION IN NIGERIA
papers.authors: ATUKUM MARYAM AWUNGHAY, OLADOKUN PAUL OLAYIWOLA
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Politics and Humanities Research
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming contemporary journalism via support in information gathering, processing, transcription, analysis, translation, content generation and editorial production. The development has significant implications for financial journalism due to the complexity and time-sensitivity of corporate financial information. This study examines the implications of AI-assisted journalism for the reporting of corporate financial information in Nigeria. The study adopts a qualitative systematic literature-review approach and focuses on studies published between 2024 and 2026. The review examines recent evidence concerning AI adoption in journalism, automated and data-driven journalism, financial reporting quality, news credibility, AI disclosure and human editorial oversight. Seven recent empirical studies are critically reviewed. The evidence indicates that AI can enhance the speed of information processing, financial-data analysis, reporting efficiency and financial information disclosure. However, the use of AI also presents challenges involving hallucination, inaccurate interpretation, algorithmic bias, insufficient disclosure, reduced comprehensibility and threats to professional accountability. Recent Nigerian evidence indicates that journalists are already incorporating AI into newsroom activities, e.g., transcription, copyediting, research and preliminary drafting. Similarly, recent Nigerian accounting studies report positive relationships between AI adoption and financial reporting quality. The study concludes that AI should be deployed as an assistive technology rather than as a substitute for professional journalistic judgment. It recommends institutional AI policies, mandatory human verification of financial information, specialised AI and financial-journalism training, transparent AI disclosure and stronger collaboration between journalists and accountants.

papers.title: Research on the Transformation of China's Employment Structure under the Background of Artificial Intelligence: A Task Perspective
papers.authors: Hairui Lu
papers.abstract: With the development and application of artificial intelligence (AI) at present, changes in technology are gradually affecting the organisation of work and the structure of employment.
