papers.title: Teachers’ technostress in the emerging generative AI era: a systematic review and bibliometric mapping (2005–2025)
papers.authors: Eko Nurhaji Purnomo, Shaymaa Mustafa, Susilo Wati, Mohamad Darwish, Abdur Rofik
papers.abstract: Educational technology is creating a digital paradox. Its pedagogical innovation notwithstanding, the spread of algorithmic systems, and emerging generative AI tools, may also erode teaching quality, staff retention, and progress towards SDGs 3, 4, 8 and 10. Existing teacher stress frameworks predate the AI era and may not fully capture teachers’ current stressors. This study reviews 20 years of research on teacher technostress (2005–2025), reconstructing its intellectual structure and integrating evidence on sources, consequences, and mitigation strategies. A two-track design was employed: a bibliometric map through Biblioshiny on 194 Scopus records, and a PRISMA-based systematic review of 26 empirical studies. Findings identify five canonical technostress creators, alongside institutional surveillance and social media as established emergent stressor domains; generative AI emerged as a nascent domain, addressed directly by only two of the 26 included studies. Key outcomes are burnout, insomnia and turnover intention. The moderating variables are perceived organizational support, TPACK competence and transformational leadership. Current Information Systems frameworks do not sufficiently consider the socio-educational dimensions of teacher technostress. Achieving the SDG targets implicated in this review requires developing equity-based protective policies, embedding AI ethics within TPACK professional development, and designing contextually sensitive support systems.

papers.title: COMPUTER AND ENGINEERING GRAPHICS IN TRANSITION THROUGH A BIBLIOMETRIC AND THEMATIC REVIEW OF DISTANCE EDUCATION RESEARCH
papers.authors: Nagima Jiyenbayeva
papers.abstract: Distance learning is increasingly relevant in technical education, particularly in engineering and computer graphics. The integration of digital technologies enables the development of students’ spatial visualization and creative design skills essential for modern engineering practice. This review examines how distance education has transformed teaching and learning in these fields by analyzing global studies from 2014 to 2025. Although online delivery presents challenges in visualization and interactivity, advances such as computer-aided design (CAD), simulation-based environments, and virtual laboratories are helping to bridge these gaps. The review identifies diverse program types, ranging from foundational design graphics to advanced applications in artificial intelligence, data science, and augmented reality. Despite significant progress, limited empirical evidence exists on learning outcomes and engagement. Through bibliometric analysis, this study maps thematic trends and collaboration patterns, offering evidence-based insights to enhance the quality and accessibility of engineering graphics education in the digital era

papers.title: USEFUL, BUT NOT IN CHARGE: PUBLIC VIEWS ON AI READING MEDICAL SCANS
papers.authors: Muhammad Mazin Sohail Chaudry, Rabia Nadeem, Emaan Sohail Chaudry
papers.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) can now help to read X-rays, CT and MRI scans, but whether patients accept it is a different question from whether it works. We explored how far people trust AI to read medical scans, what worries them and what role they want doctors to keep. Methods: An anonymous online questionnaire was shared through WhatsApp, Instagram and school groups between July and September 2026. Respondents aged 16 or over rated ten statements about AI in medical imaging, watched a short news clip about an AI tool used in the NHS, rated their support and could leave a written comment. Spearman’s rank, chi-squared and Wilcoxon tests were used. Results: Of 505 responses, 480 came from people aged 16 or over, and 219 passed a data-quality check and were analysed. Most saw benefits: 61% agreed that AI could speed up diagnosis and 62% that it could reduce waiting times. Yet 66% said AI should always be double-checked by a clinician, and only 25% would be comfortable with AI reading their scan first. Support was linked to trust in hospitals (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.001) and confidence with digital tools (ρ = 0.22, p = 0.001), but not to having heard of medical AI or having had a scan. Mistakes and missed diagnoses were the most common concern in written comments. Conclusion: Respondents saw AI as useful but wanted doctors to stay in charge. Visible human oversight and plain-language explanations may matter as much as accuracy for public acceptance

papers.title: AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE INTEGRATED PEDAGOGICAL PERSPECTIVE OF SECONDARY SCHOOL TEACHERS: A PHENOMENOLOGICAL STUDY
papers.authors: Farah Siddique, Gulnaz Akbar, Sabiha Zafar
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is making a swift impact on the processes of teaching and learning by influencing lesson development, student assessment methods, and teachers’ perceptions of their profession. However, existing literature primarily focuses on the technical aspects of AI technologies rather than examining how secondary school teachers actually use these technologies when preparing lessons. The purpose of this study is to explore the experiences of secondary school teachers in using AI technologies in their teaching practices. Purposive sampling will be employed to select 15–20 teachers working with students in Grades 9–12 who have been using AI technologies for at least one semester. Data will be collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using content analysis. The findings are expected to provide a detailed understanding of teachers’ perceptions of AI integration into their professional practices, its influence on teaching and learning processes, the challenges and benefits they encounter, and the extent to which the use of AI tools shapes their professional identities.

papers.title: From Authorship to Accountability - Rethinking Copyright Governance for AI-Generated Art
papers.authors: Blegina HASKO BEZO
papers.abstract: This study examines how the rapid expansion of generative artificial intelligence (AI) challenges traditional copyright law by shifting legal concerns beyond authorship and ownership toward transparency, disclosure, traceability, and accountability in AI-assisted artistic production.The study adopts a doctrinal and comparative legal methodology to analyse copyright principles, emerging regulatory frameworks, and policy developments relating to AI-generated content. Particular attention is given to the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, international copyright debates, and the Albanian legal framework under Law No. 35/2016 “On Copyright and Related Rights”.The analysis demonstrates that existing copyright regimes remain predominantly authorship-centred and provide limited guidance regarding accountability when AI systems contribute to artistic creation. Significant regulatory gaps persist concerning disclosure obligations, traceability of AI involvement, transparency of creative processes, and the allocation of responsibility among users, developers, and platform providers. The findings further indicate that accountabilitybased governance offers a valuable complement to traditional copyright doctrines in addressing the challenges of AI-assisted creativity. The study is limited to legal JUS & JUSTICIA No. 20, ISSUE 2/ 2026 95 and regulatory analysis and does not incorporate empirical evidence from creators, policymakers, technology developers, or judicial practice in Albania. Future research may benefit from examining stakeholder perspectives and the practical implementation of emerging AI governance frameworks. The findings support the development of governance mechanisms based on mandatory disclosure of AI involvement, documentation of human creative contribution, enhanced transparency standards, and traceability measures for AI-generated artistic content. These measures may strengthen legal certainty and improve copyright enforcement in AIassisted creative environments.The study contributes to current scholarship by moving beyond the traditional debate on authorship and copyrightability and proposing an accountability-oriented framework for copyright governance. It offers one of the first analyses linking transparency, disclosure, traceability, and accountability principles to the regulation of AI-generated art within both the Albanian and European legal contexts.

papers.title: The Algorithmic Gaze - Short-Form Video Platforms, Attention Economies, and the Reconfiguration of Visual Culture
papers.authors: Mohammed BABA YAHAYA
papers.abstract: Purpose: This paper dives into the idea of the "algorithmic gaze, " looking at how apps like TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts are changing visual culture.The central mechanism concerns how these platforms pull us in through algorithms that shape what we see and what grabs our attention.The paper explores how machine learning flips the way we create, watch, and interpret video content.Methodology: The paper mixes theories from visual culture, platform studies, and political economy.There is substantial conceptual analysis regarding the underlying architecture and mechanisms of these platforms, how algorithms pick and show videos, and how creators work within these systems.The analysis pulls in real studies on user behavior, platform features, and the economy around creators.Findings: Here's what comes out of it: Short-form video platforms create their own unique "algorithmic gaze, " and it runs on three things-machine perception, algorithmic curation, and structured visibility.Because of this, the ecosystem is driven by micro-moments of attention, creativity gets boxed by templates, and meaning often ties back to how something performs in metrics instead of its deeper message.Value: The value here is introducing the "algorithmic gaze" as a new way to think about platform power and visual culture.It sheds light on how predictive tech reshapes what it means to see, to work, and to profit in the world of short-form video.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in University Education: Exploring the Attitudes of Science Education Students in Makurdi, Nigeria
papers.authors: Samuel OKANCHE, Benedict Ojedor Onah
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Research in Multidisciplinary Education
papers.abstract: The study investigated Artificial Intelligence in University Education: Exploring the Attitudes of Science Education Students in Makurdi, Nigeria. The study employed a descriptive survey research design. The population comprised 670 (374 males and 296 females) 400-level science education students of Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University and Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University for the 2025/2026 academic session. A sample size of 237 (102 males and 135 females) students was selected using purposive sampling technique. The instrument for data collection was "Students' Attitude toward Artificial Intelligence Integration Questionnaire (SAAIIQ)." Validated by two experts in Science Education. Cronbach's Alpha was used to determine the reliability coefficient of the instrument, and the reliability coefficient obtained was 0.85. Two research questions and one hypothesis was tested. Descriptive statistics of mean and standard deviation were used for answering the research questions, while inferential statistics of independent t-test was used for testing the hypothesis at 0.05 level of significance. The findings revealed that science education students exhibited a positive attitude toward the integration of Al in universities with a cluster mean of 3.14. The study also found no significant difference between the attitudes of male and female students toward Al integration. Students demonstrated a moderate perception toward the integration of Al in universities with a cluster mean of 2.98. The study concluded that students generally accept the use of AI in university, adequate infrastructure, institutional support, and training are necessary for its effective implementation.

papers.title: Validation of the Turkish version of the Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0 (YFAS 2.0) and item-level insights for short-form development
papers.authors: Burak Kemal Ateş, Meltem Anafarta Şendağ
papers.abstract: Food addiction (FA) has received increasing attention as a framework for understanding addictive-like eating and its psychological correlates. This study aimed to provide the first comprehensive Turkish adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0 (YFAS 2.0). A total of 346 adults aged 19–55 years completed an online survey assessing FA, maladaptive eating, impulsivity, depressive and anxiety symptoms, social desirability, BMI, smoking and alcohol use, chronic disease, and self-reported psychiatric diagnosis. Of these, 109 completed the YFAS 2.0 after 10 days to test temporal stability. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the original unidimensional structure of the 11 diagnostic criteria, with strong factor loadings (.73–.94) and favorable model fit. Internal consistency was good (KR-20 = .86), and test–retest reliability was moderate (ICC = .70). FA symptoms were positively associated with BMI, emotional and uncontrolled eating, negative urgency, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, with smaller associations for lack of premeditation and perseverance. Sensation seeking and social desirability were not significantly associated with FA symptoms, while FA classification was unrelated to smoking or alcohol use. Participants meeting the FA threshold were more likely to report a psychiatric diagnosis, although this finding warrants caution given self-reported diagnoses and the non-clinical sample. Item-level analyses showed that the highest-loading items differed from those selected for the original mYFAS 2.0 for several criteria, with notable loading gaps limited to two criteria. Overall, findings support the Turkish YFAS 2.0 as a reliable and valid measure in non-clinical adults; proposed short-form item modifications require independent replication.

papers.title: Network Downtime Prediction Using Alert System in Telecommunications Industry
papers.authors: Simpson Chisom Aloka
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: Network downtime remains a critical challenge in the telecommunications industry, particularly in developing regions like Nigeria where reliable connectivity is essential for economic, educational, and healthcare activities. This work proposed a network downtime prediction with alert system using machine learning techniques, aimed at transitioning from reactive fault management to proactive network reliability strategies. The motivation for this research stems from the increasing demand for uninterrupted internet service and the limitations of existing monitoring systems in forecasting failures. This work promises to reduce downtime occurrence by predicting and alerting network admin of possible downtime for necessary action. A hybrid methodological approach combining Structured Systems Analysis and Design Methodology (SSADM) and Object-Oriented Analysis and Design Methodology (OOADM) was employed. SSADM guided the functional decomposition and data flow modeling, while OOADM facilitated the modular and scalable design of the predictive system. Historical network data was analyzed to identify failure patterns, environmental triggers, and performance anomalies using time series and classification models. The predictive system was developed using Python, due to its extensive libraries for data analysis and machine learning, including Scikit-learn, Pandas, and TensorFlow. A key feature of the system is its ability to alert network admin of potential downtime via emails or SMS, enabling timely for preventive action. The resulting system architecture includes data flow diagrams, use case models, and a working prototype, offering a practical solution for improved fault prediction and reduced downtime. This paper supports the development of more resilient telecommunications infrastructure in resource-constrained environments.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of the performance of ChatGPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3.1 Pro large language models on theoretical orthodontic questions
papers.authors: Buket Erdem, Salih Baver Ataş, Meriç Arslan, Çağla Şar
papers.abstract: Aim: This study aimed to comparatively evaluate the performance of ChatGPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3.1 Pro large language models (LLMs) in answering theoretical orthodontic questions under web search-enabled conditions. Methodology: A total of 30 open-ended questions covering the topics of growth and development, functional analysis, mixed dentition, extraoral appliances, malocclusion, and orthodontic treatment planning were prepared from Contemporary Orthodontics (7th edition, 2025). The questions were presented to all three models under standardized conditions in separate sessions in March 2026 with web search enabled. The responses were anonymized and independently evaluated in a blinded manner by two orthodontists using a 5-point Likert scale incorporating accuracy, scientific adequacy, completeness, and clarity into a single overall score. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics (version 31.0); the Friedman test was used for model comparisons, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results: Mean performance scores were 4.40 ± 0.72 for ChatGPT-5.4, 4.43 ± 0.61 for Claude Sonnet 4.6, and 4.32 ± 0.88 for Gemini 3.1 Pro. Median scores were 4.50, 4.50, and 4.75, respectively. No statistically significant difference in overall performance was found among the models (χ² = 0.400; df = 2; p = 0.819; Kendall's W = 0.007). Subgroup analyses by topic category also revealed no significant differences in any category (all p > 0.05). Inter-rater reliability was limited (α = 0.706). Conclusion: All three models achieved high-performance scores, with no statistically significant difference in overall performance among them; this does not establish equivalence. With independent verification, these LLMs may serve as supportive tools in orthodontic education.

papers.title: Islamic Communication Strategy in Facing AI Disinformation in Padangsidimpuan City: Digital Literacy and Critical Thinking of the Young Generation
papers.authors: Ahmad Sultoni
papers.journal: Busyro Jurnal Dakwah dan Komunikasi Islam
papers.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based technology has increased the production and spread of disinformation in the digital space, posing serious challenges for the younger generation in identifying the veracity of information. This study aims to analyze how Islamic communication strategies can contribute to improving the digital literacy and critical thinking skills of the younger generation in dealing with AI disinformation in Padangsidimpuan, North Sumatra. The study used a qualitative approach with a case study design through in-depth interviews, limited observation, and documentation with eleven informants consisting of religious scholars, digital communication experts, educators, and young social media users. Data analysis was conducted thematically using an interactive analysis model. The results show that the application of Islamic communication principles such as tabayyun (religious inquiry), qaulan sadidan (verification of information), and the ethics of information verification can strengthen digital literacy and encourage critical thinking among the younger generation in evaluating digital information. Furthermore, the role of religious scholars and educators as opinion leaders contributes to building the younger generation's epistemic awareness of the dangers of AI disinformation. This study concludes that integrating Islamic communication values ​​with digital literacy can be an effective strategy in increasing the resilience of the younger generation to information manipulation in the era of artificial intelligence. The authors recommend further research to quantitatively examine the effectiveness of Islamic communication strategies in improving digital literacy. The study also needs to be expanded to include formal education, digital communities, and social media. Furthermore, it is crucial to examine the use of AI technology as an educational tool to sustainably strengthen digital literacy based on Islamic values.

papers.title: Sistem Informasi Berbasis WEB sebagai Media Promosi di SMPN 7 Muaro Jambi
papers.authors: Siti Wulandari, Hery Afriadi
papers.abstract: SMP Negeri 7 Muaro Jambi belum memiliki media informasi resmi berbasis web, sehingga prestasi, kegiatan, dan fasilitas sekolah hanya dipublikasikan melalui brosur dan media sosial yang jangkauannya terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang sistem informasi profil sekolah berbasis web sebagai media promosi yang dapat menampilkan keunggulan dan informasi sekolah kepada masyarakat luas. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan pengumpulan data melalui observasi, wawancara, dan studi literatur. Sistem dirancang dengan Unified Modeling Language (UML), dikembangkan dengan metode waterfall menggunakan PHP dan MySQL, serta diuji dengan black box testing dan User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Hasilnya berupa website dengan dua hak akses, yaitu admin dan pengguna umum, yang memuat profil sekolah, data guru, berita dan kegiatan, galeri, prestasi dan fasilitas, live chat, serta chatbot. Seluruh skenario black box testing berstatus valid, dan UAT terhadap 10 responden menghasilkan persentase kelayakan rata-rata 93,6% (kategori sangat layak). Sistem ini layak digunakan sebagai media informasi dan promosi untuk memperluas jangkauan serta memperkuat citra positif sekolah.

papers.title: Explainable Temporal Machine Learning for Academic Risk Prediction and Student Intervention
papers.authors: Swati Sagar, Hitesh Sarkar, Krunal Rathod, Seefa Tamboli, Kamini Chaudhari
papers.journal: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Predicting which students are likely to struggle is a well-studied problem in higher-education analytics, but what an institution should do with such predictions is less settled. This paper proposes a framework that treats academic risk as something that shifts over a semester rather than a label assigned once, and that closes the gap between predicting risk and acting on it. It combines longitudinal academic and behavioral indicators, temporal feature construction, machine-learning-based risk prediction, explainable AI, and a feedback loop that maps predictions to interventions and then checks whether those interventions changed anything. The framework builds on two existing studies covering complementary ground: one showing that dropout risk and its predictors shift month by month, and another showing that early grades and course history can forecast future performance and study duration. Rather than reporting new experimental results, the paper lays out a research methodology for temporal prediction, interpretability, intervention design, and post-intervention reassessment that a future empirical study could follow. Key Words: academic risk prediction, explainable AI, higher education, machine learning, student intervention, temporal learning.

papers.title: SkillMatch: An Integrated Platform for AI Resume Analysis, Job Description Matching, and Interview Preparation
papers.authors: Prathamesh Nistane, Shejal Jibhakate, Harsh Gour, Akash Harne
papers.journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: SkillMatch is a full-stack, AI-powered web application that unifies resume analysis, resume enhancement, job-description matching, cover-letter generation, and interview preparation in a single platform. It is designed to help students and job seekers understand exactly why their resumes may be rejected by Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) and what they can do to improve them. The work addresses several gaps in existing tools: most candidates do not know why their resume fails at the ATS screening stage; existing tools either give an opaque score with no explanation or solve only one part of the problem, such as a resume builder or a job board; interview preparation is typically disconnected from the candidate's actual resume content; and premium tools that offer detailed feedback are expensive and inaccessible to students. The system combines a React frontend, a Node.js/Express backend, and a PostgreSQL database, using deterministic processing for parsing, grading, and score tallying, and generative AI for rubric-based scoring, skill-gap detection, and interview-question generation. The cover-letter module saves job seekers from writer's block by automatically turning their resume and job-match data into a customized, ready-to-send pitch. The implemented platform completes the main workflow from resume submission to analysis, feedback, and career-preparation support, although AI-based scores vary slightly between runs and scanned resumes are not yet supported. Further testing with larger numbers of users and resumes is required to evaluate accuracy and effectiveness. Keywords— Applicant Tracking System; Resume Analysis; Job Description Matching; Interview Preparation; Generative AI; Cover Letter Generation

papers.title: Development of large language model-generated multiple-choice questions and flashcards to enhance the Canadian undergraduate urology curriculum
papers.authors: Othmane Zekraoui, Tiange Li, David-Dan Nguyen, Marie-Lyssa Lafontaine, Tomas Cordoba, Mahmoud Moustafa, Dawn Lee MacLellan, Julien Letendre, Malek Meskawi, Garson Chan, Sarah Neu, Dean Elterman, Bilal I. Chughtai, Brendan Wallace, Naeem Bhojani
papers.abstract: Introduction: The Canadian Undergraduate Urology Curriculum (CanUUC) is a free, online curriculum that covers important topics in urology for medical students. While multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and flashcards are widely used for medical education, they can be resource-intensive and time-consuming to produce. Therefore, to strengthen the CanUUC with such tools, we developed a customized large language model (LLM)-enabled system to generate MCQs and flashcards from CanUUC material and evaluated the quality of its outputs. Methods: We used OpenAI’s GPT-5 model and refined two system prompts to generate educational materials from two CanUUC topics (benign prostatic hyperplasia and urolithiasis). Six evaluators blinded to items’ origin were involved, and each item received two independent ratings for relevance, correctness, clarity, distractor quality, and suitability for education. Items with a mean score <3 on the suitability for education evaluation domain were excluded. Results were summarized descriptively. Results: Ninety items, including 40 MCQs and 50 flashcards were generated. Among flashcards, 22% allowed >1 plausible answer. Across all independent ratings, the proportion of top scores (4–5) ranged from 85.5−90.5% across all domains. Overall, 86.1% of independent ratings judged items suitable for medical education. When averaging the suitability score at the item-level, 12 items (13%) had a score <3 and were excluded. Mandatory (8%) and optional (27%) adjustments were suggested to refine items’ clarity and correctness. From the initially generated items, 87% were included in the CanUUC. Conclusions: Our customized system can produce curriculum-aligned MCQs and flashcards that meet item writing standards and are mostly suitable for medical education. Expert review is essential to identify flaws and improve quality before inclusion into the curriculum.

papers.title: Design and Preliminary Application Study of an AI Driven Personalized VR Rehabilitation Support System for Children with Autism
papers.authors: Guangke Qi, Zhiliang Xia, Yinhui Yin
papers.journal: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Objective To address insufficient task adaptation, fragmented process information, and a lack of transparency in the basis for training adjustments for children with autism, this study designs an AI driven personalized VR rehabilitation support system and establishes a preliminary application evaluation framework. Methods Drawing on TEACCH structured teaching to organize tasks, the system integrates the DeepSeek large language model, Unity virtual environments, and MQTT communication to support ability profiling, strategy recommendation, training interaction, and coordination across multiple terminals. Candidate strategy screening, output validation, and therapist confirmation form a closed loop for task adjustment. Technical system tests and a small scale feasibility study are used to evaluate operational performance, training acceptability, and task performance. Results A system design covering perceptual, communication, and social tasks was developed, together with four functional modules—Explore at Your Own Pace, Fun Practice Zone, Everyday Scenarios Town, and Peer Play Community—and corresponding evaluation indicators. Conclusion This study proposes a VR rehabilitation support system that combines structured tasks, AI recommendations, and professional supervision. Actual system feasibility and training related outcomes must be assessed using application data; no definitive conclusion about rehabilitation effectiveness can yet be drawn.

papers.title: Analysis of the impacts of generative AI-driven human-machine communication interactions on user subjectivity in social media
papers.authors: Jingyun Xiao
papers.journal: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has arrived on social media with large language models like chatgpt making features for AI-assisted production and communication mainstream. People have transformed how they make stuff and work with machines. This research analyses the effect of these advancements on the subjectivity of users from the perspective of human-machine communication theory. The usage of AI-assisted production can minimise the difficulty of expression, but the anchoring effect may discreetly limit the autonomous judgement of users; Personalised recommendation reinforces the selective exposure to information, undermining the conditions that support critical reflection; The involvement of AI in self-presentation blurs the barrier between human and machine, and the identity identification needs to be repositioned. In an effort to seek a balance point between AI efficiency and human autonomy, the paper proposes many solutions in three fields to address these issues, including technical transparency, media literacy education and platform standards. The factual applications of AI given in this article are taken from public papers such as the Stanford "Artificial Intelligence Index Report". The major research approaches are literature analysis and deduction of theory.

papers.title: A Study on the Production Logic and Communication Management of Cultural Creativity in the Context of Digital Media
papers.authors: Tianqi Gong
papers.journal: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Digital technology has restructured the content production and information dissemination models of the cultural and creative industries. In the traditional media era, the creation and dissemination of cultural and creative content were dominated by professional institutions, with an industry that was closed in operation and a fixed creative group. The public could only passively receive the content but could not participate in the production process. After the popularization of online media, the entry threshold for the cultural and creative industry has significantly decreased. Ordinary users can carry out content creation, adaptation and dissemination activities through online platforms, becoming an important participant in the cultural and creative industry, and promoting the industry to form a new development pattern of digital production, mass co-creation and cross-industry integration. While digital networks promote the innovative development of the cultural and creative industry, they also give rise to many industries. Currently, there is an oversupply of homogeneous content in the cultural and creative market, and copyright infringement issues occur frequently. The regulatory model adapted to traditional communication scenarios cannot adapt to the fragmented and diversified characteristics of online communication, seriously hindering the high-quality development of the industry. Based on the current digital communication characteristics and the industry status of mass co-creation， this paper analyzes the changes in the cultural and creative industry in the digital environment in terms of creative subjects, production models and value orientations from a micro communication perspective, sorts out the existing problems in the industry and proposes targeted governance and optimization solutions. The research results can provide practical support for the digital transformation of the cultural and creative industry and the standardized governance of online content, and enrich the theoretical research on the governance of digital cultural and creative industries.

papers.title: Research on Physical Education Teachers' Digital Literacy under the TPACK Framework: Progress, Problems, and Prospects
papers.authors: Lan Luo
papers.journal: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: With the in-depth advancement of the digital education strategy, physical education (PE) teachers' digital literacy has become a critical issue in the digital transformation of physical education. The TPACK framework provides a structured analytical perspective for understanding teachers' technology integration capabilities. This paper systematically reviews the developmental trajectory, core progress, and existing challenges of research on PE teachers' digital literacy within the TPACK framework. It is found that this field has evolved from conceptual introduction to disciplinary adaptation, and from theoretical discussion to targeted intervention, achieving phased achievements across three dimensions: theoretical exploration, practical application, and assessment tools. However, existing research still faces multiple constraints, including an insufficient theoretical integration between TPACK and digital literacy, homogeneous research methods with uneven population coverage, inadequate practical translation, a lack of disciplinary adaptation, and the long-term neglect of rural PE teachers. Future research should focus on deepening the physical-education-specific adaptation of the TPACK framework, expanding the scope of research methods and participant coverage, facilitating the translation of theory into practice, actively addressing issues surrounding emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), and advancing the field from "conceptual introduction" to "disciplinary construction" and from "status-quo description" to "targeted empowerment."

papers.title: From "Learning-Application Disconnect" to "Learning for Application": An Exploration of the Reform Path for General Artificial Intelligence Courses
papers.authors: Ye Liu, Yuchen Li
papers.journal: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: To address the "learning-application disconnect" in university general AI courses, this paper analyzes pain points such as outdated content, monotonous teaching methods, and wide disparities in students' foundations. It proposes a three-dimensional objective of "knowledge— ability—literacy" and three principles: "low code + high understanding," "scenario-based + project-based," and "disciplinary intersection." The reform path is explored through content reconstruction, blended teaching, and diversified assessment. Practice shows that course satisfaction rose from 80% to 97%, students' confidence in AI application increased from 54% to 89%, and the project completion rate reached 100%, providing a replicable paradigm for the inclusive development of general AI education.

papers.title: Exploration of Audience Engagement and Activation Paths of Intangible Cultural Heritage Under Media Representation on Short-Video Platforms
papers.authors: Xueli Cao
papers.journal: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: The rapid development of short-video platforms has fundamentally changed the communication landscape, bringing unprecedented opportunities and major challenges to the protection and transmission of intangible cultural heritage (ICH). This research conducts a comprehensive theoretical and critical analysis on the mechanism of audience engagement and sustained activation pathways of intangible cultural assets within the framework of media representation of contemporary short video platforms. Based on critical heritage studies, participatory culture theory, platform studies, algorithmic governance research, surveillance capitalism frameworks and communicative mediatisation paradigms, this study explores how algorithmic curation, micro-narrative visual framing and interactive participatory dynamics reconfigure the public perception, emotional resonance and cultural consumption of traditional heritage practices. It also responds to fundamental concerns about commodification, shallow decontextualisation and marginalisation of legitimate community knowledge bearers. The paper proposes a multi-dimensional activation framework, consisting of community-centred digital stewardship, transmedia narrative contextualisation, co-creative audience engagement, and platform-mediated value co-creation, to keep living heritage vibrant, resilient, and socially meaningful in the digital era.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Transformation in Modern Banking Ecosystems: Structural, Operational, and Governance Challenges
papers.authors: Ashot V. Mardoyan, Hayk Sargsyan
papers.journal: “Katchar” Collection of Scientific Articles International Scientific-Educational Center NAS RA
papers.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the comprehensive integration of artificial intelligence within modern banking and financial ecosystems by analysing its profound structural, operational, and macroeconomic implications. Drawing on recent empirical literature and institutional data, the work examines how AI technologies—ranging from machine learning algorithms to agentic workflows and specialised small models—are transforming retail banking, risk management, credit scoring, and regulatory compliance. The research shows that while AI adoption significantly improves operational efficiency, default prediction accuracy, and customer personalisation, it also introduces complex governance challenges, including algorithmic bias, data privacy vulnerabilities, and shifts in profit pools. The analysis also evaluates AI’s dual role in fostering sustainable green finance and corporate ESG integration, alongside its paradoxical capacity to influence shadow banking dynamics. By proposing an integrated technological and governance framework featuring zero-trust architecture and explainable artificial intelligence, this study outlines a strategic roadmap for financial institutions transitioning toward resilient, secure, and highly automated digital ecosystems.

papers.title: Digital Transformation in Language Teaching: From Traditional Methods to Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Lilit Hakobyan, Shushanik Ghazaryan
papers.journal: “Katchar” Collection of Scientific Articles International Scientific-Educational Center NAS RA
papers.abstract: This article examines the digital transformation of language teaching and analyses the impact of contemporary digital technologies and artificial intelligence on the language-teaching process. It focuses on the evolution of traditional forms of instruction, the potential of digital educational technologies, and the main areas where artificial intelligence is applied in language teaching. The advantages of using intelligent systems are examined, including the personalisation of instruction, the automation of instructional guidance, increased access to educational resources, and opportunities for online learning. The article identifies the main risks to academic integrity. It addresses issues of information reliability, the protection of learners’ personal data, and the preservation of the teacher’s leading role in the educational process. Contemporary scholarly works related to the subject have been examined. Based of an analysis of the theoretical literature on the issues under investigation, the article demonstrates the need of integrate artificial intelligence technologies harmoniously into language education while preserving education’s humanistic orientation of education and recognising the importance of the teacher’s role as a mentor and facilitator. It is concluded that the most promising model for the development of contemporary language education is one based on collaboration between the teacher and artificial intelligence. Such a model contributes to improving the quality of instruction, developing communicative competence, saving time and human resources, and fostering learners’ digital skills.

papers.title: Ai-Assisted Differentiated Instruction in Legal English: The Ailed Model
papers.authors: Գոհար Գրիգորյան
papers.journal: “Katchar” Collection of Scientific Articles International Scientific-Educational Center NAS RA
papers.abstract: This article addresses one of the most important problems in the field of Legal English instruction: using artificial intelligence (AI) to organise effective, differentiated instruction for learners with diverse language skills. Legal English is a branch of English for Specific Purposes (ESP) that requires proficiency in legal terminology, legal genres, and legal discourse, as well as general language proficiency. Uniform instructional materials may be too challenging for some students and not challenging enough for others. The article proposes the AILED (AI-Assisted Legal English Differentiation) Model, which integrates AI-assisted differentiation of legal terminology, adaptation of instructional texts, and principles of differentiated instruction. The model has been developed after an in-depth review of literature on Legal English pedagogy, AI-assisted language learning, and differentiated instruction, as well as an analysis of placement-test data from 103 Master’s students enrolled in law and jurisprudence programmes at the International Scientific-Educational Center of the National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Armenia. The placement data provide evidence of heterogeneous proficiency among law and jurisprudence students, supporting the need for differentiated Legal English instruction.

papers.title: Consumer Responses to AI-Generated Marketing Content: Evidence from an Experimental Survey
papers.authors: Kehan Jiang
papers.journal: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for digital marketing, particularly in short video advertising. However, consumer acceptance of AI-generated advertisements remains uncertain because of the concerns over authenticity, trust and emotional connection. This study investigates how consumers respond to short video advertisements created by AI and humans through comparing evaluations and identifying factors that influence engagement intention and purchase intention. A quantitative survey was conducted with 179 participants, where respondents evaluated both advertisement formats. Reliability analysis, multiple linear regression models, paired samples t-tests, and qualitative analysis of open-ended responses were applied. The results show that human-created advertisements received much higher evaluations in authenticity, trust, visual appeal, professionalism, engagement intention, and purchase intention, while informativeness showed no significant difference. Regression results further indicate that trust is the strongest factor influencing consumer responses towards AI-generated advertisements. These findings indicate that businesses should balance AI efficiency and human creativity to improve consumer acceptance and advertising effectiveness.

papers.title: Maqasid Al-Syari'ah-Based Pedagogy: Artificial Intelligence in Islamic Education
papers.authors: Ali Makki, Nurul Layli R, Abdul Hamid Bashori, Shujaullah Khwajazada
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence in education is often oriented toward cognitive speed without paying attention to ethical and spiritual dimensions. This study was conducted to examine the application of Maqasid al-Syari'ah-based artificial intelligence pedagogy at the Al Wahidiyah Sampang Qur'anic Boarding School (Pondok Pesantren Tahfizhul Qur'an Al Wahidiyah Sampang). This research employs a phenomenological qualitative approach to explore the subjective experiences of caretakers and students (santri). Data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation, then analyzed using Moustakas' stages. Field research at the Al Wahidiyah Sampang Qur'anic Boarding School indicates that the school approaches the integration of AI and digital technology selectively through the lens of the five objectives of Islamic law (maqashid syariah). The preservation of religion (hifdzu ad-diin) is implemented by restricting gadgets to administrators only, so students can focus on worship and memorization. Preserving life (hifdzu an-nafs) protects students' mental well-being from harmful exposure, while AI helps administrators find practical references. Preserving intellect (hifdzu al-'aql) safeguards students' cognitive development while using AI as an administrative aid. Preserving lineage (hifdzu an-nasl) shields the younger generation's moral integrity from digital degradation. Preserving wealth (hifdzu al-maal) also supports efficient institutional budgeting. Conclusion: This integration model offers a comprehensive solution for modernizing Islamic education in the digital era. Significance: It provides a practical ethical framework for using artificial intelligence in Islamic educational institutions today.

papers.title: Research on Teaching Practice of Mechanical Courses in Colleges and Universities under the Background of Digital Intelligence
papers.authors: Wanming Zhang, Shuai Zhang, Xiang Gong, Yunjie Wang, Yan Shi
papers.journal: Journal of Education and Educational Research
papers.abstract: A new wave of digital intelligence technology drives the deep change of higher engineering education, and technologies such as generative artificial intelligence, knowledge map, and virtual simulation provide a new path for mechanical course reform. The local application-oriented college mechanical course has long been difficult to understand the principles of abstraction, the organizational structure is difficult to be visually displayed, the engineering design lacks the real verification scene, and the evaluation method focuses on the final examination and other realistic pain points. Taking the provincial first-class undergraduate course Mechanical Principles and Design as the research carrier, combined with structuralism and situation learning theory, this paper analyzes the current situation and existing problems of the digital intelligence teaching reform of mechanical courses, sticks to the student-centered, output-oriented concept, and carries out the teaching reform practice from the aspects of teaching content reconstruction, digital intelligence teaching space construction, industry-teaching integration resources development, intelligent multiple evaluation system construction, etc. The practice shows that integrating digital intelligence technology into the whole process of course teaching evaluation and management can effectively solve the traditional teaching problems of mechanical courses, improve students' digital design ability and complex engineering problem-solving ability, and provide a reproducible practice model for the transformation of digital intelligence of mechanical courses in local application-oriented universities.

papers.title: Explaınable Machıne Learnıng For Predıctıng Students’ Academıc Performance From Generatıve AI Usage Patterns in Hıgher Educatıon
papers.authors: Clinton Amponsah
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in higher education learning practices, yet its contribution to academic performance remains contested. This study developed an explainable machine-learning framework for predicting students’ post-semester GPA from Generative AI usage patterns and learning-related characteristics. Using a structured dataset of 50,000 student records, the study modelled academic performance with predictors including pre-semester GPA, weekly GenAI usage hours, primary use case, prompt-engineering skill, tool diversity, traditional study hours, perceived AI dependency, institutional policy, exam anxiety, year of study, and major category. To prevent outcome leakage, non-relevant outcome variables and student identifiers were excluded before training. Ridge Regression, Decision Tree Regression, and Extra Trees Regression were compared using R², RMSE, and MAE. The results showed that Ridge Regression achieved the strongest predictive performance, indicating that academic outcomes were largely explainable through stable relationships among prior achievement, GenAI-related behaviours, and study characteristics. Feature-importance analysis revealed that prior GPA, primary GenAI use case, and prompt-engineering skill were among the most informative predictors. The study contributes to GenAI-aware learning analytics by demonstrating how explainable modelling can support evidence-based academic monitoring.

papers.title: From Products to Experiences: Transforming Marketing Strategies Through Customer-Centric Innovation
papers.authors: Daduk Merdika Mansur
papers.journal: Golden Ratio of Community Services and Dedication
papers.abstract: In an increasingly digital and experience-driven marketplace, the shift from product-centric to experience-centric marketing has become a strategic necessity for firms seeking sustainable competitive differentiation. This study aims to explore how customer-centric innovation drives the transformation of traditional marketing strategies into immersive, value-rich experiences that meet evolving consumer expectations. Using a qualitative research design grounded in an interpretivist perspective, the study employed a multiple-case study approach across diverse industries. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with marketing and innovation professionals, supplemented by company documents and secondary sources. Thematic analysis identified four key findings. First, customer-centric innovation reshapes value creation by shifting the focus from tangible products to emotional and symbolic experiences. Second, technological integration, including artificial intelligence (AI) and real-time analytics, facilitates hyper-personalization and adaptive customer engagement. Third, emotional branding and storytelling play strategic roles in strengthening customer loyalty and fostering brand resonance. Fourth, sustainable experience strategies are co-created through continuous feedback mechanisms and stakeholder engagement. These findings contribute to the theoretical development of experiential marketing and value co-creation while providing practical insights for firms seeking to align their brand strategies with customer values in dynamic market environments. Overall, the study highlights that competitive advantage in the modern marketplace depends not merely on selling products but also on creating meaningful, adaptive, and emotionally engaging experiences that encourage customers to return and share their experiences with others.

papers.title: "Ask Me One Critical, Pointed, and Specific Question at a Time": Building Research Skills With Large Language Models
papers.authors: Brian Ballsun-Stanton
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Using large language models (LLMs) in research requires decisions about which work to offload and where sustained attention and increased friction can improve the execution of the user's intentions. This guide offers students and researchers a practical method for using LLMs to organize that attention while retaining responsibility for their reasoning and decisions. I describe an auto-interview practice in which an LLM asks one critical, pointed, and specific question at a time. My colleagues and I used this practice to develop the study design and analysis plan for the Stage 1 submission of a registered report. Working through the questions together helped us limit digressions, explain our judgments, and develop a shared understanding of the proposed study. A worked example shows how answering one specific question prompted us to reconsider which data would define our participant groups. Examining our own reasoning as we answered the question made the planning process an exercise in metacognition. The guide explains how to choose a suitable working environment, supply relevant context, and evaluate both individual replies and the developing conversation. It also shows how to extract reusable instructions and checks from repeated successful work, distinguishing what carries forward from the context each task requires. Documenting and sharing these methods allows other researchers to examine the judgments behind the work and adapt useful practices. The aim is to make deliberate engagement with research decisions a repeatable part of working with LLMs. The conversation transcripts, harness instructions and skills behind the guide are deposited separately at 10.5281/zenodo.23314144.

papers.title: The Nescience Manifesto: A Proposal for a Global, Ownerless Institution to Audit Frontier AI
papers.authors: Lucas Parenti
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Nescience is a proposal for a global, non-profit, ownerless institution whose single function is to detect when a frontier artificial-intelligence system stops being trustworthy, and to hold binding power to pause or withhold its deployment. The manifesto argues that current AI safety practice faces a verification gap: interpretability understands only a small fraction of frontier-model computation, and measured capability shows little correlation with measured safety. It proposes three artifacts — a "police model" of independent lineage trained solely for detection and deliberately less capable than the systems it monitors; a forensic catalog of behavioral and activation-level signatures of deception, sabotage and alignment faking; and a control infrastructure combining trusted monitoring, resampling, distillation, consistency interrogation and non-model hard limits. The institutional design addresses the "who watches the watcher" problem through an irrevocable endowment with no majority bloc, an eleven-seat board on which AI labs hold no vote, an external oversight commission with full access, a six-year non-renewable directorship with post-tenure quarantine, a capped citizen fund that elects the civil-society bench, and a "death clause" under which dissolution cryptographically destroys the institution's sealed assets rather than transferring them. Published in Portuguese (original) and English. Conceived by Lucas Parenti, Porto Alegre, Brazil, on October 19, 2026, and written in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic). Released under CC BY 4.0 so that any party may adopt, adapt or found the proposal, with attribution.

papers.title: AI-GENERATED DEEPFAKES AND THE INDIAN LEGAL FRAMEWORK: A LEGAL ANALYSIS
papers.authors: Srabanti Biswas
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence has changed the way digital content is produced and shared, making it possible to create images, videos and audio that can appear remarkably real. Deepfakes are one such development, where a person's face, voice or actions can be digitally created or altered. While this technology can be used for legitimate purposes in fields such as education, entertainment and media, its misuse can cause serious harm through impersonation, fraud, harassment, misinformation, privacy violations and non-consensual intimate content. These developments have created new legal concerns in India, particularly because many existing laws were framed before such advanced forms of synthetic media became common. This article examines how the Indian legal system deals with deepfake-related harms through constitutional protections, the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and the Information Technology Rules, 2021. It also looks at important judicial decisions concerning privacy and personality rights, along with recent regulatory measures relating to Synthetically Generated Information. The article further considers difficulties in detecting deepfakes, securing their timely removal and providing effective remedies to victims. It concludes that India needs a practical and balanced legal approach that protects individuals from harmful uses of deepfakes while allowing legitimate expression, creativity and technological development. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Deepfakes, Cybercrime, Privacy, Indian Legal Framework.

papers.title: AI LITERACY AMONG LIBRARY PROFESSIONALS IN PAKISTANI ACADEMIC LIBRARIES: KNOWLEDGE, ADOPTION, CHALLENGES, AND TRAINING NEEDS
papers.authors: Applied Linguistics Research Review
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly changing the landscape of higher education and academic librarianship globally at a rapid pace, bringing about a convergence of capabilities. Academic libraries in the present era are moving fast from mere repository of information to dynamic, automated and intelligent knowledge hub. The capacity of the Library and Information Science (LIS) professionals in developing countries like Pakistan to drive, integrate and manage these technological instruments, however, is a critical aspect which is under-researched. The current study is an empirical research that examines the level of AI literacy of library professionals working in Higher Education Commission (HEC) recognized public and private university libraries in Pakistan. The research design employed a descriptive, quantitative survey which obtained data from a sample of library occupations (N = 184) from various administrative levels and from different regions. The study specifically aims to analyse self-perceived conceptual AI knowledge, current use of AI tools, structural, institutional and human-resource challenges and priorities for professional training needs. The empirical findings show that Pakistani academic librarians have moderate awareness of the general concepts of mainstream generative AI tools, but their understanding of the underlying concepts like Natural Language Processing (NLP), semantic indexing, machine learning algorithms, and predictive analytics are limited. Advanced uses (such as collection development/automated metadata generation) of practical application in library workflows have been extremely limited, with the exception of plagiarism/similarity detection software like Turnitin, and even there usage is still mostly limited to initial reference retrieval. The issues that have been identified as systemic issues include: the challenges of budget constraints, absence of a standard institutional governance framework for AI, problems with infrastructure and the absence of an institutional professional development program. Last, the study outlines a few strategic recommendations for the future, including capacity building programs to be led by HEC, reconsideration of the national LIS curriculum and inter-university collaboration for the development of AI skills. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, AI Literacy, Academic Libraries, Pakistani Librarians, Higher Education Commission (HEC), Information Literacy, Technology Adoption, Professional Training Needs, Digital Transformation.

papers.authors: Xavier Goshi

papers.abstract: A reading of the Financial Stability Board's final report, Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (15 October 2026), for AI agents that move money. papers.title: AI-BASED EMAIL SPAM AND SCAM DETECTION
papers.authors: Srushti Khose
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Email remains an important communication channel for education, business, and personal use. However, spam,phishing, fraudulent offers, and scam messages can expose users to financial loss, identity theft, and malware. Thispaper presents a proposed AI-Based Email Spam and Scam Detection system that classifies email text as likelylegitimate or suspicious by using text preprocessing and machine-learning techniques. The system can tokenizeand normalize email content, transform text into numerical features using methods such as Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), and apply a classifier such as Multinomial Naive Bayes or LogisticRegression. The predicted category is displayed with a simple explanation or warning to help users make saferdecisions. The proposed design includes data preparation, model training, evaluation, and a user interface. Thisdocument is a student research-paper draft: implementation details, dataset information, measured performance,and references must be verified and updated to match the student's actual work before submission

papers.title: METHODOLOGY OF USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND GEOINFORMATION SYSTEMS IN MODELING GEOGRAPHIC SITUATIONS AND ORGANIZING PRACTICAL TRAINING
papers.authors: Soataliyev Yorkinjon
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The article examines the methodology of modeling geographic situations and organizing practical training using artificial intelligence and geoinformation systems in geography education. The study of regional processes is based on the stages of geographic data collection, comparison of spatial layers, modeling of possible changes and evaluation of the obtained results. A system of practical training is offered on the analysis of population location, expansion of urban territory, territorial distribution of service facilities and changes in land cover. Through the combined use of SI and GAT tools, the development of students' spatial thinking, research skills, and evidence-based decision-making skills will be addressed.

papers.title: METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPMENT OF INDIVIDUAL EDUCATIONAL TASKS BASED ON THE INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND GEOINFORMATION SYSTEMS
papers.authors: Soataliyev Yorkinjon
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article examines a methodology for developing individualized learning tasks through the integration of artificial intelligence and geographic information systems in geography education. It analyzes the didactic principles of differentiating tasks according to students' knowledge, digital readiness and independent learning abilities. A structured set of tasks involving geographical data retrieval, spatial analysis, map visualization and interpretation is proposed. Particular attention is given to teacher supervision, information verification and the assessment of students' independent reasoning.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS A TOOL FOR PERSONALIZED ENGLISH LANGUAGE LEARNING
papers.authors: Kenes, Abdigani, Baymyrzayeva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Traditional language education classrooms often struggle to accommodate the diverse learning paces, styles, and proficiency levels of individual students. This research paper explores the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a transformative mechanism for personalized English language learning in higher education. By analyzing various AI-driven educational applications, intelligent tutoring systems (ITS), and adaptive learning platforms, this study examines how technology customizes linguistic input, provides real-time corrective feedback, and establishes individualized learning pathways. Utilizing a mixed-methods approach, the study surveys 120 undergraduate students to measure their engagement and perceived language acquisition progress when utilizing AI tools. The findings demonstrate that AI significantly enhances learner autonomy and vocabulary retention by adapting to the student's unique Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD). However, the paper also addresses critical limitations, including the lack of socio-cultural nuance in AI communication and the risk of reduced authentic interpersonal interaction. The study concludes with practical recommendations for integrating adaptive AI platforms into university EFL curricula to foster an optimized, student-centered learning environment.

papers.title: AI-Powered Technologies in Foreign Language Education: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.authors: Sharasulova, Yermekkyzy, Baymyrzayeva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into foreign language education has initiated an unprecedented paradigm shift within higher education institutions worldwide. This expansive research paper explores the multifaceted impact of AI-powered technologies in the English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classroom, critically evaluating the dual concepts of revolutionary pedagogical opportunities and systemic instructional challenges. Utilizing a comprehensive mixed-methods research design incorporating a quantitative survey of 115 university students and qualitative, structured interviews with language faculty members, this study analyzes tools ranging from automated speech recognition (ASR) systems to advanced generative artificial intelligence and large language models (LLMs). The opportunities identified and expanded upon include augmented student engagement, ubiquitous exposure to immersive, authentic language environments, personalized feedback loops, and a significant reduction in foreign language speaking anxiety through non-judgmental digital interfaces. Conversely, the critical challenges encompass algorithmic biases, digital divide inequities, the structural degradation of independent academic writing skills, cognitive dependency, and the profound loss of socio-pragmatic and cultural context in text generation. Ultimately, the paper argues that a balanced, hybrid pedagogical framework underpinned by proactive digital literacy is required to responsibly navigate these emerging dynamics, ensuring that artificial intelligence acts as a cognitive amplifier rather than a replacement for human-centered communicative interaction.

papers.title: AI-Based Cyber Threats Detection System
papers.authors: Shivani Bhidave
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Cyber threats such as phishing, malware, brute-force login attempts, denial-of-service activity, and suspicious networkbehaviour challenge organisations that depend on connected systems. Signature-based tools can identify known patterns butmay struggle with unfamiliar or rapidly changing attacks. This paper proposes an AI-Based Cyber Threats Detection Systemthat analyses network-flow and system-event features to flag potentially malicious activity. The design combines datapreprocessing, supervised machine-learning classification, anomaly detection, risk scoring, and an alert dashboard. Theproposed pipeline covers authorised log collection, data validation, feature preparation, model training, evaluation, andanalyst review. A reproducible evaluation plan uses precision, recall, F1-score, false-positive rate, detection latency, andconfusion-matrix analysis. No experimental performance results are claimed because the system has not been benchmarkedin a controlled deployment. The design emphasises privacy, explainability, human review, and responsible use of securitydatasets. It can serve as a foundation for a student prototype and can later be extended with streaming ingestion and threatintelligence enrichment.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in musical creativity
papers.authors: Abdusalomova Dinora
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article provides a scientific analysis of the role of artificial intelligence technologies in the field of music art. It highlights new opportunities emerging in composition, arrangement, musical transcription, sound engineering, and educational processes through AI-based applications. The study also examines the role of generative systems such as AIVA, MuseNet, Magenta, and Suno in music creation, as well as their significance in enhancing creative thinking.

papers.title: INTELLIGENT COLLEGE CHATBOT USING GPT
papers.authors: Siddhi Giramkar
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Students often need quick access to information about courses, admission procedures, academic schedules, examinationrules, fees, facilities, and college services. Information may be spread across notices, websites, documents, andadministrative offices, making it difficult to find an answer quickly. This paper presents a proposed Intelligent CollegeChatbot using GPT, a conversational system intended to respond to common college-related questions in naturallanguage. The system can combine a GPT-based language model with a verified college knowledge base so that responsesare relevant to institutional information. A typical workflow includes receiving a question, identifying its intent, retrievingapplicable college information, generating a response, and presenting the answer with a referral option when theinformation is uncertain or requires official confirmation. The proposed design aims to improve accessibility and reducerepetitive queries to college staff. Accuracy depends on the quality and freshness of the knowledge base, the modelconfiguration, and suitable safeguards. This sample paper describes a proposed design; actual implementation details andmeasured evaluation results should be added after testing the student's system

papers.title: EXPLAINABLE AI FOR EARLY PREDICTION OF STUDENT ACADEMIC RISK USING MACHINE LEARNING
papers.authors: Srushti Ahire
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Student academic risk prediction aims to identify learners who may need timely academic support before final outcomes are known.Machine learning can analyse historical indicators such as attendance, assessment performance, assignment completion, andlearning-platform engagement to estimate the likelihood of academic difficulty. However, a prediction is more useful to educatorswhen its basis can be understood. This paper proposes an explainable machine-learning framework that combines early riskestimation with interpretable explanations for students, faculty, and academic advisors. The workflow includes data governance,preprocessing, model training, validation, risk scoring, local and global explanations, and human review. Candidate models includelogistic regression and decision trees as interpretable baselines, alongside more complex models where justified. Explanationmethods such as feature importance and SHAP-style contribution analysis can help communicate which recorded indicatorsinfluenced a prediction. The system is designed to support—not replace—professional judgement, and it should not automaticallypenalise students. Fairness, privacy, data quality, and clear communication are treated as core design requirements. The proposedarchitecture and evaluation plan are presented for an academic prototype; no experimental performance results are claimed.

papers.title: AI-BASED SMART IRRIGATION SYSTEM
papers.authors: Shravani Parade
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Water availability, irregular rainfall, changing temperatures, and inefficient irrigation practices create pressure on farmproductivity and operating costs. This paper presents a research-based design for an AI-based smart irrigation systemthat combines soil-moisture sensing, local weather information, crop and soil characteristics, and a decision engine torecommend or automate irrigation. The proposed architecture uses sensor nodes to collect field measurements, acontroller to validate readings, and a rule-based safety layer supported by machine-learning prediction where suitablelabelled data are available. Irrigation is triggered only when estimated crop water need, sensor evidence, and safetyconstraints agree; rainfall forecasts, sensor faults, pump limits, and manual override are considered before actuation. Areview of recent literature indicates that machine learning can support irrigation scheduling, but performance dependson data quality, calibration, crop context, and validation across locations. Unlike an experimental report, this paperdoes not claim measured water savings or crop-yield gains. It defines a practical architecture, control workflow,evaluation protocol, and deployment risks that can guide a student prototype and subsequent field testing.

papers.title: BEHAVIORAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL FACTORS IN AI USE AMONG 15-YEAR-OLD STUDENTS: LEARNING AND ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE
papers.authors: Fayazov Xasan Jaxongir ugli
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract. This article presents a theoretical analysis of the impact of generative artificial intelligence (AI) on the learning activities, cognitive effort, and independent thinking of 15-year-old students in the context of Uzbekistan. The study draws on OECD PISA 2025 data and scholarly literature in behavioral sciences. According to the OECD (2026), 48.6% of students in Uzbekistan use AI chatbots for learning purposes at least once a week, while 80.6% report being taught at school how to evaluate AI-generated information. The article examines the educational implications of AI through the perspectives of cognitive offloading, self-directed learning, and critical evaluation of information. Drawing on secondary sources, the theoretical analysis suggests that AI can support learning processes, while its inappropriate use may potentially undermine independent thinking. The study emphasizes the importance of developing students' skills in responsible AI use, information verification, and independent learning. Keywords: generative artificial intelligence; PISA 2025; cognitive effort; cognitive load; behavioral sciences; self-directed learning; critical thinking; Uzbekistan. Аннотация. В статье представлен теоретический анализ влияния генеративного искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) на учебную деятельность, когнитивные усилия и самостоятельное мышление 15-летних учащихся на примере Узбекистана. Исследование основано на данных PISA 2025 ОЭ. СР и научной литературе в области поведенческих наук. Согласно данным ОЭ СР (2026), 48.6% учащихся Узбекистана используют чат-боты с искусственным интеллектом в учебных целях не реже одного раза в неделю, а 80.6% отмечают, что в школе их обучают оценивать информацию, созданную ИИ. В статье рассматривается влияние ИИ на эффективность обучения с позиций когнитивной разгрузки, самостоятельного обучения и критической оценки информации. Теоретический анализ вторичных источников показывает, что ИИ может способствовать образовательному процессу, однако его ненадлежащее использование потенциально ограничивает развитие самостоятельного мышления. Обосновывается необходимость формирования у учащихся навыков осознанного использования ИИ, проверки информации и самостоятельного обучения. Ключевые слова: генеративный искусственный интеллект; PISA 2025; когнитивные усилия; когнитивная нагрузка; поведенческие науки; самостоятельное обучение; критическое мышление; Узбекистан. Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada generativ sun’iy intellektning (SI) 15 yoshli o‘quvchilarning o‘quv faoliyati, kognitiv sa’y-harakatlari va mustaqil fikrlashiga ta’siri O‘zbekiston misolida nazariy jihatdan tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqot OECDning PISA 2025 ma’lumotlari va xulq-atvor fanlariga oid ilmiy adabiyotlarga asoslanadi. OECD (2026) ma’lumotlariga ko‘ra, O‘zbekistonda o‘quvchilarning 48,6 foizi haftasiga kamida bir marta o‘rganish maqsadida SI chatbotlaridan foydalanadi, 80,6 foizi esa SI yaratgan axborotni baholashni maktabda o‘rganayotganini bildirgan. Maqolada SIning ta’lim samaradorligiga ta’siri kognitiv yuklamani tashqi vositalarga o‘tkazish, mustaqil o‘rganish va axborotni tanqidiy baholash nuqtayi nazaridan yoritiladi. Ikkilamchi manbalarga asoslangan tahlil SI ta’lim jarayonini qo‘llab-quvvatlashi bilan birga, undan noto‘g‘ri foydalanish mustaqil fikrlashni cheklashi mumkinligini nazariy jihatdan ko‘rsatadi. O‘quvchilarda SIdan ongli foydalanish, axborotni tekshirish va mustaqil o‘rganish ko‘nikmalarini rivojlantirish zarurligi asoslanadi. Kalit so‘zlar: generativ sun’iy intellekt, PISA 2025, kognitiv sa'y-harakat, kognitiv yuklama, xulq-atvor fanlari, mustaqil o'rganish, tanqidiy fikrlash, O‘zbekiston.
