At the wholebody level, pyruvate levels and STAT1 pyruvylation can change with glucose supply [1]. However, in the highly glycolytic tumor microenvironment, pyruvate stays high. We hypothesize that this metabolic state keeps STAT1 pyruvylation high in tumor-infiltrating immune cells, weakens endogenous IFN-I signaling, and contributes to immunotherapy resistance.Future studies should measure protein pyruvylation in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and in paired ICB samples. In addition, the enzymes that control lysine pyruvylation still need testing in disease models. A recent systematic study of lysine pyruvylation identified HAT1 and p300 as candidate writers and SIRT3 as a depyruvylase (eraser). Kpy levels changed with glycolytic flux and pyruvate supply [11]. These findings give a clear molecular starting point. However, it is still unknown whether SIRT3, or other erasers, remove STAT1-K201 pyruvylation in TIL subsets and restore IFN-I activity in tumors. Support for studying eraser enzymes also comes from lactylation research. After lactylation was reported, HDAC1-3 and some sirtuins were shown to act as delactylases. This shows that metabolite-driven lysine acylation is often reversible and enzymecontrolled [12,13]. For methods, we suggest: (i) in vitro depyruvylation assays with pyruvylated STAT1 peptides or purified STAT1 plus recombinant SIRT3 and related deacylases; (ii) gain or loss of SIRT3, HAT1, and p300 in IFN-responsive immune and tumor cells, followed by STAT1-STAT2 binding, ISG induction, and IFN reporter assays; (iii) compartment-resolved proteomics to compare mitochondrial versus nuclear or cytosolic control of Kpy; and (iv) combined metabolic treatment and checkpoint blockade in models grouped by pyruvate or Kpy level. Collectively, clarifying writer and eraser specificity for STAT1 will help determine whether pyruvylation is a useful metabolic checkpoint in tumor immunity. Finally, we thank Zuo et al. for their important work, which opens a new direction in immunometabolism.

papers.title: Beyond passive rights-holders: toward student moral agency in assessment fairness
papers.authors: Amirhossein Rasooli
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, fairness research in classroom assessment has progressively repositioned students from passive objects toward partial subjects of assessment. By advocating for student active engagement in assessment processes via discourses such as student voice and rights, student agency, student assessment literacy, and student partnership in assessment, this research has extended students’ active positioning in assessment. This perspective article argues that one dimension has been left behind: students’ moral agency, that is their capacity to reason critically about what is fair and act as co-authors of assessment fairness, not merely its reporters. Drawing on moral agency theories, this article shows that across five domains of assessment literacy, self-assessment, peer and collaborative assessment, inclusive assessment, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment, research overwhelmingly asks what students perceive as fair, rather than how they reason and act about fairness or are supported to develop fairness reasoning and conduct. Even literatures organized around ethics and critical consciousness in assessment (e.g., critical assessment literacy) locate this fairness capacity in teachers and experts, with developmental work now emerging for preservice teachers but not students. AI has made this newly urgent, as student confusion about legitimate use is met chiefly with compliance instruments (e.g., declaration forms) rather than reasoning support. Drawing on recent work showing that agency in assessment is a developmental capacity, I argue the next decade needs to move from compliance-based instruments toward fairness deliberation that develops students’ moral agency, building on the small number of studies that already point the way.

papers.title: Perceptions, practices and governance of generative AI in university social science teaching in Ecuador
papers.authors: Abel Suing, José Marcelino Romero Gutierrez, Viviana Noemí Galarza-Ligña, Ximena Coronado-Otavalo
papers.abstract: The advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming academic production and confronting the social sciences with the challenge of preserving critical thinking in the face of mechanically generated content. This research examines the perceptions and practices of social science lecturers and students at Ecuadorian universities regarding the use of AI, together with their motivations, constraints and the institutional policies currently in force. A mixed-methods design was adopted, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches. The instruments comprised semi-structured interviews with lecturers and students at national and Ibero-American universities; a non-probabilistic survey of 200 students; and a content analysis of seven sets of regulations from universities in Ecuador, all aligned with the framework of competencies identified by UNESCO-IESALC. The results show a moderate-to-high level of AI use (mean = 3.68), explained by perceived usefulness and extrinsic motivation rather than ease of use, and a gap between the demand for regulation (4.00) and perceived regulatory clarity (3.21); only one of the seven universities has a policy formally designated as such, and ethics predominates over professional and disciplinary development. The study concludes that the governance of AI in Ecuadorian higher education requires an evaluative redesign and discipline-differentiated competencies.

papers.title: Use of a GenAI-patient for medical communication training for undergraduate medical students—a quasi-experimental study
papers.authors: Remco C. Jongkind, Jesper Pool, Eline Verberne, Jennita Meinema, Suzanne E. Geerlings, Inge Henselmans
papers.abstract: Background Effective communication is fundamental to high-quality healthcare. Communication skills training is a core component of medical curricula, yet opportunities to practice with standardized patients (SPs) are limited, costly, and can elicit anxiety in novice learners. Generative AI (GenAI) virtual patients may offer a scalable and accessible supplement. This quasi-experimental study examined the effect of practicing with a GenAI-patient on medical students’ self-reported nervousness, preparedness, self-efficacy, and self-perceived competence during their first SP encounter. Materials and methods First-year medical students ( n = 383) at the University of Amsterdam were allocated on the basis of the class schedule to a control group receiving standard e-learning preparation ( n = 182) or an intervention group offered voluntary additional access to a GenAI-patient built on a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework using GPT-4o ( n = 201). Students completed a 31-item questionnaire after their first SP class. Primary outcomes were nervousness, preparedness, self-efficacy, and self-perceived competence. Group differences were assessed using Mann–Whitney U tests with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. The primary analysis was by intention-to-treat, comparing all students allocated to the intervention with all control students; the comparison restricted to actual users of the tool was secondary. Results Of 180 students that completed the questionnaire, 84 were controls and 96 students were allocated to the intervention, of whom 49 had used the GenAI-patient. No statistically significant differences were found between groups on the outcomes after FDR correction. In the intention-to-treat analysis; all composite effect sizes were near zero (Cliff's delta −0.05 to 0.04, all 95% confidence intervals including zero), as were those in the per-protocol comparison (−0.12 to 0.07). Among tool users, experience was generally positive: 63%–71% gave positive ratings. The majority considered the GenAI-patient a valuable contribution to the standard class preparation (71%). Conclusions Voluntary, single-session text-based practice with a GenAI-patient did not significantly reduce nervousness or improve self-assessed communication competence before a first SP encounter. Positive user experience suggests potential for the format, provided future iterations incorporate mandatory minimum engagement, multiple patient cases, automated feedback, and higher-fidelity multimodal interaction.

papers.title: Toward an AI- and learning-analytics-enabled inclusive support framework for students with learning difficulties in Kuwait's higher education institutions
papers.authors: Abdullah Feraih Alenezi
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and learning analytics are transforming higher education by enabling personalised learning, adaptive support, and data-informed decision-making. These developments present significant opportunities for improving educational inclusion for students with learning difficulties, yet they also introduce challenges relating to privacy, algorithmic bias, explainability, accessibility, and governance. Although Kuwait has strengthened disability legislation while simultaneously investing in AI-enabled education under Kuwait Vision 2035, these policy agendas have largely evolved independently. Similar governance gaps are evident across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), where disability inclusion, AI adoption, and higher education reform remain weakly integrated. This conceptual paper develops the AI- and Learning-Analytics-Enabled Inclusive Support Framework for Learning Difficulties (ISF-LD) to guide the responsible implementation of AI within inclusive higher education. Using a conceptual framework development methodology, the study synthesises evidence from four complementary domains: research on learning difficulties and disability inclusion; scholarship on AI, learning analytics, and responsible AI; national and international policy documents; and established educational and disability theories. The framework is informed by six theoretical perspectives: the Social Model of Disability, Universal Design for Learning, Sociocultural Theory, Self-Determination Theory, learning analytics ethics, and responsible AI principles. The proposed framework comprises five interconnected implementation layers: national policy and governance, institutional leadership and disability services, faculty capability, AI-enabled inclusive pedagogy and assessment, and student self-determination. These layers operate through an iterative, non-linear governance model in which each layer informs and is informed by the others, supported by four cross-cutting principles: rights-based governance, stigma-aware disclosure, universal accessibility, and responsible AI. Together, they position AI as a governed educational capability that supports inclusion while safeguarding learner autonomy, transparency, and institutional accountability. The paper contributes to the literature in three ways. First, it integrates disability studies, AI governance, learning analytics, and inclusive higher education within a single conceptual model. Second, it addresses an important policy gap by linking disability inclusion with AI governance in the context of Kuwait and the GCC. Third, it proposes a theoretically grounded and empirically testable framework that can inform institutional strategy, educational policy, and future research on responsible AI in higher education. Although developed within Kuwait, the ISF-LD offers a transferable governance model for universities seeking to implement AI ethically while advancing equitable and inclusive learning.

papers.title: FROM INFORMATION TO INTEGRATION: INTEGRATIVE CAPACITY AND EDUCATIONAL TRANSFORMATION IN CONTEMPORARY UKRAINE IN THE CONTEXT OF COLLECTIVE TRAUMA, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AND SOCIAL CHANGE
papers.authors: Irina Valentin
papers.journal: Науковий вісник Вінницької академії безперервної освіти Серія «Педагогіка Психологія»
papers.abstract: Purpose. This paper argues that the dominant model of education, which assumes that access to information produces developmental change, is no longer adequate under conditions of collective trauma, symbolic acceleration, and AI-driven informational transformation. The paper introduces Integrative Capacity (IC) as a central developmental construct and proposes a reconceptualization of educational purpose: from information delivery to the cultivation of integration. Methodology. The paper employs theoretical-conceptual analysis, drawing on developmental psychology, clinical neuropsychology, and educational theory. The KINERGIA framework, a multi-level analytical model operating across intrapersonal, interpersonal, and collective domains, is applied as a theoretical architecture for understanding and addressing this challenge. Scientific novelty. To the author's knowledge, Integrative Capacity as formulated here – modeling coordination across three simultaneous substrates (biological regulation, symbolic meaning, relational consciousness) and three systemic levels (intrapersonal, interpersonal, collective) – has not been explicitly formulated in the existing educational literature in this form. Its educational manifestation, Integrative Perception, is introduced as an observable and assessable indicator of IC development in educational practitioners. Conclusions. The paper demonstrates that educational transformation in Ukraine requires not only resources and training, but a reconceptualization of educational purpose itself: from knowledge transmission to the cultivation of Integrative Capacity across all three levels – nervous system regulation, relational attunement, and collective meaning-making. Implications for Ukrainian education during wartime reconstruction are discussed

papers.title: From Instrument to Inquiry: A Conceptual Framework for the Future of Science- and Technology-Based Arts Education
papers.authors: Bolim Lee
papers.abstract: Arts education increasingly incorporates generative artificial intelligence, extended reality, sensors, and data as artistic materials. Yet debate about this shift remains dominated by the question of which technologies to introduce, rather than what technological engagement is _for_. This conceptual paper argues that science- and technology-based arts education can be analysed through four positions that technology may occupy in a learning design: as _instrument_, as _medium_, as _subject of critical inquiry_, and as _site of agency and governance_. Drawing on STEAM scholarship, critical data and AI studies, and arts-education theory, the paper proposes that programmes confined to the first two positions risk technological determinism, rapid obsolescence, and widening inequity. It advances four propositions regarding critical literacy, creative agency under generative AI, equity and local context, and educator and evaluation capacity. The paper concludes with implications for practice, policy, and empirical research. The framework is theoretical and has not been empirically tested.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS A TOOL FOR IMPROVING THE EFFICIENCY OF HEALTHCARE SYSTEM MANAGEMENT IN KAZAKHSTAN
papers.authors: J. Zhu, Zhazira Kusmoldayeva, O. Abraliyev
papers.journal: BULLETIN OF THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES OF THE REPUBLIC OF KAZAKHSTAN ( THE BULLETIN)
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of healthcare and the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies are creating new opportunities for healthcare delivery and managerial decision-making. This study assesses the prerequisites, application areas, and potential effects of artificial intelligence on the efficiency of healthcare system management in the Republic of Kazakhstan. The empirical base includes official statistical data for Kazakhstan for 2015–2025, materials of the Ministry of Healthcare of the Republic of Kazakhstan, national strategic and regulatory documents, and international research on the application of artificial intelligence in clinical and administrative healthcare processes. The study used dynamic, comparative, and structural analysis, document content analysis, a process-based approach, and systematisation of practical AI implementation cases. The findings show that the number of physicians increased from approximately 69.7 thousand in 2015 to 84.0 thousand in 2025, while the number of hospital organisations changed from 901 to 832. In 2025, more than 215 million healthcare services were provided, of which 190.8 million, or 88.6%, were delivered electronically. The development of the E-Densaulyq ecosystem, integration of fragmented information systems, and creation of a unified medical data repository establish a technological foundation for moving from digital record-keeping to data-driven, AI-supported management. The greatest managerial potential of AI is identified in patient-flow forecasting, resource planning, pharmaceutical supply management, quality control, clinical decision support, and anomaly detection. The study proposes an original AI-driven healthcare management framework that links digitalisation, data integration, AI applications, managerial processes, measurable efficiency outcomes, risk assessment, and evidence-based scaling. The study also shows that the independent macro-level effect of AI cannot yet be statistically separated from the broader impact of healthcare digitalisation because a sufficiently long and comparable national time series on AI adoption is lacking.

papers.title: Rethinking Lasswell's 5W Model of Communication in the Era of Generative AI
papers.authors: Anjali Sapkota
papers.abstract: Lasswell's five-question formula remains a durable frame for analyzing source, message, channel, audience and effect. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) underlying mass communication assumptions: intentional human sources, relatively static messages, channels as carries, audiences as receivers and effects as downstream outcomes. This conceptual paper argues for extension rather than abandonment. Its objectives are to examine the model’s analytical adequacy and develop an extension for generative communication. Using scholarship from AI-mediated communication, human-machine communication, algorithmic media, trust and synthetic content and accountability. research to illustrate how these systems can generate, revise, personalize messages (i.e. These competencies allow for the communication of agents that exist as a dispersed network, but ultimately moral agency lies with human and institutional figures. Critical comparative conceptual analysis relates this literature to Lasswell's five questions and integrates the resulting distinctions into a framework. The analysis identifies distributed communicative agency, synthetic and hybrid voice, intelligent mediation, audience co-participation and recursive effects. It distinguishes machine influence from human and institutional responsibility. The proposed framework makes trust appraisal, verification and accountability explicit, with transparency and provenance applying across all stages. Feedback connects outcomes to subsequent production and distribution. It is therefore required as an initial stage of analysis but in times and environments where the source, message and channel can be at least partially artificial, it becomes insufficient. The framework offers concepts for empirical research and practical guidance for documenting authorship, verifying claims and identifying responsible actors in journalism, education and public communication.

papers.title: Intersectional Inequalities in Educational Attainment – Cohort Trends in West Germany (1970-2008) and Comparison of Analysis Methods
papers.authors: Jascha Dräger, Tom Hartl
papers.abstract: Despite educational expansion, educational attainment still depends strongly on factors beyond individuals’ control, such as social origin, gender, and migration background. These social categories may intersect to produce compounded forms of disadvantage, but most existing research has studied them in isolation. This study describes trends in intersectional inequalities of educational opportunity at the intersection of social origin, gender, and migration background for the 1970-2008 birth cohorts in West Germany using data from the Socio-Economic Panel. We use three quantitative approaches to evaluate intersectional inequalities: regressions with interaction terms, the “multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy” (MAIHDA) approach, and a machine-learning approach, namely Conditional Inference Forests (CIF). Across analysis methods, the results show that intersectional inequalities remained stable across cohorts. Social origin is the dominant social category: no combination of gender and migration background compensates for low parental education. Intersectional interaction effects are negligible or very small. MAIHDA and regression analysis yield similar results. CIF suggests that Gymnasium attendance is more strongly determined by intersectional strata membership than suggested by the other two methods. Moreover, CIF suggests that intra-categorical interaction effects are more important for Gymnasium attendance than inter-categorical interaction effects. We discuss the substantive implications of these results and provide guidance on choosing an analysis method for quantitative intersectional research.

papers.title: Design Document and Clinical Rationale: A Two-Layer AI Digital Readiness Coach for Adolescent Vaping Cessation
papers.authors: Siddharth Kulkarni, Nicholas Glover, Arush Satasiya
papers.abstract: Nicotine vaping among adolescents is of growing concern, especially among those who usenicotine regularly and are not able to quit. School administrators most often respond to a case ofvaping by increasing discipline, often leading to the exclusion of the student. However, punitivemeasures may not address the student's dependence. The goal of this research is to develop atwo-layer, adaptable artificial intelligence (AI) digital coach to support adolescent vapingcessation using evidence-based clinical practices. The system employs TTM, MI, and CBT tocreate conversational strategies to address an individual's readiness to change, momentarymotivation, and barriers to change. The system is designed to respond to users' needs based onconversational assessments rather than rigid classifications of stages or behaviors. Theserver-side routing uses Change Talk and Sustain Talk to respond to users in an engaging,motivational manner, helping them develop a quit plan. Further, the system constructs a barrierprofile to determine the presence of nicotine dependence and polysubstance use. If a barrierprofile indicates high dependence, the system offers a referral to a school nurse or counselor forfurther judgment and engagement. The server-side employs risk screening and various safetymeasures, including localizing the machine-learning model, to mitigate potential harm to theadolescent. The system will be evaluated based on its fidelity to Motivational Interviewing andits ability to promote biochemical abstinence in a randomized, controlled setting.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Business Performance among Informal Youth Entrepreneurs in Zambia
papers.authors: Clement Mwaanga, Edwin Moyo
papers.journal: International Journal of Management Entrepreneurship Social Sciences and Humanities
papers.abstract: Informal enterprises absorb most youth employment in Sub-Saharan Africa, yet it remains unclear whether artificial intelligence (AI) improves their performance or widens the digital divide. This study extends the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) by linking perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) to AI adoption and to financial (FP), marketing (MP) and operational (OP) performance among informal youth entrepreneurs in Zambia. Survey data from owner-operators aged 18–35 were analysed with confirmatory factor analysis and covariance-based structural equation modelling, using a cluster bootstrap because the data file contained paired, near-identical records. PEOU, but not PU, predicted AI adoption. AI adoption was positively associated with all three performance dimensions, most strongly with operational performance. PEOU had significant indirect effects on performance through AI adoption; however, when we added direct paths from PEOU to performance, these indirect effects were no longer significant, and PEOU was directly associated with marketing and operational performance. Measurement quality was modest, particularly for the AI adoption scale, and model fit was below conventional benchmarks, so the findings should be read as exploratory. In informal, resource-constrained settings, usability, rather than perceived usefulness, appears to be the gateway to AI adoption, and AI's performance benefits are associated with how easily entrepreneurs can use it.

papers.title: Students’ Perceptions of Artificial Intelligence Use in English Writing: Evidence from Vocational High School Students
papers.authors: Rahayu Rahayu, Ira Maysarah, Ira Maysarah, Iis Sujarwati, Iis Sujarwati
papers.journal: Journal of English Language and Education
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in English writing instruction to support idea generation, drafting, revision, and editing. However, research on vocational high school students’ perceptions of AI-supported English writing in Indonesia remains limited. This study examined students’ perceptions of AI applications in English writing at SMK Negeri 2 Bengkulu City. A descriptive quantitative survey involved 70 tenth-grade students selected purposively based on their prior experience using AI applications. Data were collected using an adapted 20-item questionnaire covering motivation, learning quality, AI value, cognitive learning, affective learning, and course quality. Descriptive analysis examined mean scores and percentages to determine students’ perceptions across the six dimensions. The findings revealed a very high overall perception of AI-supported English writing learning (M = 4.22; 84.4%). Course quality received the highest rating (M = 4.26; 85.2%), whereas cognitive learning recorded the lowest (M = 4.16; 83.2%). These findings indicate that students generally perceived AI positively as a supportive tool for English writing instruction. The results highlight the perceived educational value of AI while underscoring the need to strengthen its contribution to students’ cognitive engagement and independent writing development.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence in education mapping research trends and future directions
papers.authors: Larisa Lutskovskaia, Oksana Chigisheva, Vagiz G. Gimaliev, Sergei P. Zhdanov, Valeria L. Zakharova, Lyudmila M. Smirnova
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) recently appeared as an issue of its time which has been changing the educational landscape at a considerable rate and opening new pathways and challenges for educators and learners. Therefore, in terms of GenAI for education this bibliometric analysis will characterize the change and development by mapping trends and patterns, examining prevalent subject areas in academia interest. Following the established criteria, we ran a systematic search on Scopus database with the identification and analysis of 121 peer-reviewed documents (journal articles, review articles and conference papers; selection reported with reference to the PRISMA 2020 guideline) published between January 2023 and March 2025 related to GenAI applied in education. The thematic labels attached to the algorithmically generated VOSviewer clusters were assigned by the researchers, and interpretations of regional patterns are presented as tentative. The article features papers discussing ways to use GenAI in learner-centered teaching, curriculum development and assessment. The findings reveal a rapid increase in research output between 2023 (23 articles) and 2024 (67 articles), followed by 31 articles in the first quarter of 2025, and substantial international collaboration (34% of the articles). Moreover, the thematic analysis shows that pedagogical integration and instructional design (55.4% of the articles), assessment and academic integrity (44.6%) and ethical and societal implications (39.7%) are the most prominent themes, with a shift from ethical and assessment concerns in 2023 towards pedagogical integration and learning outcomes in 2024-2025. Research affiliated with the United States, the United Kingdom, China and Germany dominates the corpus, whereas research from Latin America and Africa appears under-represented. The review proposes future directions of research and spells out an array of issues that have until now gone unexamined by helping the reader enter the intellectual landscape of GenAI in education. The bibliometric evidence indicates growing scholarly attention to the potential of GenAI in education; this study did not appraise the quality of the evidence on learning outcomes. Nonetheless, designers are being asked to collectively conduct further research to address any potential negative effects of the technology, and create useful design frameworks, to implement this technology into the education system worldwide, without compromising on justice and morality.

papers.title: Paper-first knowledge engineering as a pedagogical framework for cognitive agency in AI-assisted learning
papers.authors: Gary W. Collins
papers.abstract: This study investigates how a structured “paper-first” approach can support cognitive engagement during artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted academic work in higher education. Growing reliance on generative AI has increased concerns about surface-level learning, trial-and-error prompting, and reduced student ownership of academic writing. Using a two-year design-based research approach involving nine iterative cycles, the study developed and refined a framework that required students to construct manual logic diagrams before engaging with AI tools and expert system environments. Participants included a six-member interdisciplinary design team and 150 communication for academic purposes students from the faculty of information and communications technology at a South African university. Data were collected through iterative observations and focus group interviews and analyzed using grounded theory and constant comparative analysis. Findings indicate that the framework supported more structured reasoning, reduced inefficient prompting behaviors, and improved students’ ability to identify weaknesses in their own arguments before digital interaction. Students also reported increased confidence and greater ownership of their academic work. The study argues that structured pre-AI planning activities can strengthen critical thinking and academic literacy by positioning AI as a support tool rather than a substitute for cognitive effort. The findings contribute practical guidance for educators seeking to integrate AI into higher education while preserving student agency and deep learning.

papers.title: Miscalibrated trust: How academic perceptions and misconceptions shape ChatGPT adoption in higher education
papers.authors: Ramesh Kumar Moona Haji Mohamed, Nagaletchimee Annamalai, Yuvaraj Ganesan, ‎ Hermanto
papers.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models such as ChatGPT, has reshaped academic workflows while raising questions about trust, misconceptions, and future expectations. This study examines an integrated framework grounded in the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology and the technology acceptance model to assess how foundational acceptance drivers, cognitive evaluations, misconceptions, and trust are associated with academics’ forward-looking expectations of ChatGPT. Survey data from 252 academics in Malaysian public and private universities were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and facilitating conditions were positively associated with perceived ease of use (PEOU) or perceived usefulness (PU), while PEOU was positively associated with trust. Social influence was not significantly associated with PU. Two unexpected patterns were observed: PU was positively associated with misconceptions, and misconceptions were positively associated with trust. These cross-sectional associations suggest that functional appreciation can coexist with inflated capability beliefs and potentially miscalibrated trust, but they do not establish a causal mechanism of belief amplification. The Malaysian setting is analytically relevant because higher education institutions are expanding digitalization while national initiatives increasingly emphasize responsible AI governance, institutional capability, and digital skills. The findings highlight the importance of AI literacy, transparent institutional guidance, verification practices, and calibrated reliance when integrating GenAI into higher education.
keywords: Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology

papers.title: THE SOCIAL CONSTRUCTION OF CREATIVITY IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI: RETHINKING AUTHORSHIP AND VISUAL LABOR
papers.authors: Moch. Abdullah Faqih, Fajar Habibi, Reza Secoca
papers.abstract: Generative AI systems now produce images from short text prompts. This change raises sociological questions about who is seen as a creator and how visual work is valued. This study examines how creativity, authorship, and visual labor are socially constructed in the age of generative AI. The study uses qualitative documentary analysis with a constructivist approach. The data are four sets of public documents. They cover the 2022 Colorado State Fair case, the 2025 report of the United States Copyright Office and the ruling in Thaler v. Perlmutter, the 2023 agreement of the Writers Guild of America, and empirical studies of artists, audiences, and workers published from 2022 to 2025. The analysis draws on social construction, boundary-work, art worlds, and the sociology of work. The findings show three constructions. Recognition of the creator depends on the rules of each setting and not on the image alone. Definition by law assigns authorship to humans who contribute identifiable expression. Valuation of creative work depends on labor contracts, on how tasks change and become invisible, and on the labels that audiences read. The study argues that creativity is a social accomplishment that different groups negotiate. It offers practical implications for designers and design educators, including documentation of human contribution, disclosure of AI use, and clear contract terms.

papers.title: Relationship between Mediterranean Diet Adherence and Quality of Life, Anthropometry, and Dietary Intake among Turkish Adolescents
papers.authors: Şebnem Özgen Özkaya, Bahar Yalçın, Sezen Sevdin, Emrah Gökay Özgür, Muazzez Garıpağaoğlu
papers.abstract: Objective: Adolescence is a critical period for the development of lifelong dietary habits, and adherence to the Mediterranean diet is known to be associated with various health benefits. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between adherence to the Mediterranean diet and quality of life, anthropometric variables, and dietary intake among adolescents.Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted between October and November 2023 with 480 adolescents (51.3% female) aged 12–18 years residing in the Kadıköy district of Istanbul. Data were collected through face- to-face interviews using a questionnaire that included the Mediterranean Diet Quality Index, the Quality of Life Short Form (SF-36), a three-day dietary intake record, and sociodemographic information. Anthropometric measurements were taken by the researchers.Results: The mean age of participants was 15.15±1.99 years, with 51.3% being female, 15.6% overweight, and 11.6% obese. Among the adolescents, 27.5% had poor adherence to the Mediterranean diet. The prevalence of overweight (12.9%) and obesity (22.0%) was significantly higher among those with poor KIDMED scores (p <0.05). As the KIDMED score increased, body weight and body mass index decreased, whereas general health and vitality scores increased. The KIDMED score showed positive correlations with the intake of protein (%), fat (%), dietary cholesterol, fiber, vitamins A, B2, B6, C, folate, calcium, and magnesium, and a negative correlation with carbohydrate (%) intake.Conclusion: most adolescents had poor to moderate adherence to the Mediterranean diet. Since adherence to the Mediterranean diet was found to be associated with BMI, quality of life, and dietary intake, improving diet quality among adolescents may contribute to better quality of life and optimized anthropometric outcomes. Therefore, promoting the Mediterranean dietary pattern could be beneficial for enhancing adolescent health.

papers.title: Assessment of New Competencies for Human - AI Teaming in Air Traffic Control
papers.authors: Arif Tuncal, Erdal Dursun
papers.journal: Human factors in aviation and aerospace.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) integration into aviation operations is progressively reshaping the professional landscape of air traffic management, thereby placing new demands on the human workforce. The aim of the study was to determine the priority weights assigned to eight specific AI competencies within the domain of air traffic control. The study was based on the framework of AI competencies applicable to the aviation sector established by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA). Data were collected from a purposive sample of 19 air traffic controllers. The data were analyzed using the Best–Worst Method (BWM), a multi-criteria decision-making technique. The findings indicate a substantial shift in the relative importance of different competencies during human-AI collaboration. Cognitive skills were assigned the highest priority weight, followed by data literacy, information technology competencies, and general AI knowledge. Communication and sensory competencies were assigned a secondary tier, while social and physical skills were allocated the lowest priority weights. These findings suggest that AI integration may transform the nature of the cognitive competencies required from air traffic controllers.

papers.title: EXPLORING THE EFFECTS OF POLYCYSTIC OVARY SYNDROME ON SLEEP QUALITY USING THE PITTSBURGH SLEEP QUALITY INDEX AMONG YOUNG WOMEN ATTENDING A TERTIARY CARE CENTER IN SOUTH KERALA
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a mutual endocrine disorder between women of reproductive age and is frequently related with metabolic, reproductive, and psychological complications.Emerging evidence suggests that sleep instabilities are more predominant between women with PCOS and may adversely affect their general health and life quality.To assess sleep quality between women with PCOS and age-matched healthy controls using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and to measure the suggestion between body mass index (BMI), sleep quality and menstrual irregularities.A hospital-based case-control investigation was directed between 56 women attending a tertiary care centre in South Kerala.The research included 28 women diagnosed with PCOS and 28 age-matched healthy controls.Sleep quality was restrained using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index.Anthropometric measurements and menstrual history were recorded.Information were examined using correlation analysis, t-test, and chi-square test.Women with PCOS demonstrated suggestively advanced BMI and poorer sleep quality linked to controls.The mean global PSQI score was suggestively higher among women with PCOS.Poor sleep quality was more predominant in the PCOS group.Menstrual irregularities were observed exclusively among women with PCOS.A weak positive correlation was detected among BMI or PSQI scores; however, the association was not statistically significant.Women with PCOS exhibited suggestively inferior sleep quality than healthy controls.Routine assessment of sleep quality should be combined into the comprehensive management of PCOS to recover total health outcomes and life quality.

papers.title: Intelligent Academic Performance Forecasting using Integrated Machine Learning Models
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: In the era of data-driven education, unlocking hidden insights from student learning patterns holds the key to shaping the future of academic success.Accurate prediction of student performance is vital for improving educational standards and enabling proactive support for students at risk.Conventional prediction techniques frequently depend on single algorithms, which can be inadequate when handling the complexity and multidimensionality of educational datasets.This study introduces a novel hybrid machine learning framework that combines Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost to enhance both prediction accuracy and model reliability.By merging the parallel bagging capability of RF with the sequential boosting proficiency of XGBoost, the framework addresses typical shortcomings of opaque models and minimizes variance in individual predictions.The evaluation leverages established benchmark datasets, namely the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD) and the Chinese University Dataset (CUD), to assess performance across a broad array of variables, such as demographic data, online learning activities, and previous academic achievements.This methodology directly tackles crucial technical obstacles, including class imbalance and feature significance, which commonly impede effective outcome prediction.The integration of these ensemble methods is intended to equip educators with a dependable early warning system, supporting tailored instructional materials and efficient resource distribution.Additionally, the framework's effectiveness is assessed using various metrics Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F-Measure to provide a thorough evaluation of its predictive capabilities.This research advances the domain of educational data mining by highlighting the enhanced effectiveness of integrated models in early identification of pivotal student outcomes.

papers.title: ROLE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN CONTENT MARKETING: IMPACT ON CONSUMER PERCEPTION AND BRAND INTERACTION
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed content marketing by enabling the creation of personalized, scalable, and data-driven marketing content.This study aims to examine the role of generative AI in content marketing and its impact on consumer perception and brand interaction.The research adopts a descriptive and analytical design, using primary data collected from 120 respondents who actively engage with digital platforms.A structured questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale was employed to measure key constructs, including generative AI content quality, consumer perception, perceived authenticity, trust, and brand interaction.The collected data were analysed using SPSS, applying statistical techniques such as reliability analysis, factor analysis, correlation, and regression.The findings reveal that generative AI-driven content has a significant positive impact on consumer perception and brand interaction.The study also highlights that perceived authenticity plays a crucial role in building consumer trust, which in turn strongly influences brand interaction.Furthermore, consumer perception and trust partially mediate the relationship between AI-generated content and brand interaction.While generative AI enhances marketing efficiency and engagement, concerns related to authenticity and trust remain important considerations.The study contributes to the existing literature by providing empirical evidence on the effectiveness of generative AI in content marketing and offers practical insights for marketers to develop balanced strategies that integrate technological capabilities with human creativity.The findings are particularly relevant for organizations seeking to enhance consumer engagement and build sustainable brand relationships in the evolving digital marketing landscape.

papers.title: GENERATIVE AI IN ENGLISH FOR SPECIFIC PURPOSES: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF PEDAGOGICAL TRANSFORMATIONS
papers.authors: Nurfajri Ningsih
papers.journal: English Language Linguistics and Culture International Journal
papers.abstract: This study presents a systematic literature review examining the integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in English for Specific Purposes (ESP) instruction from 2020 to 2025. Using the PRISMA 2020 framework, 61 open-access empirical studies from the Scopus database were selected and analyzed through a hybrid bibliometric and thematic approach. The findings reveal a significant increase in research after 2023, reflecting the rapid adoption of large language models in educational contexts. The results indicate that GenAI has transformed ESP pedagogy by shifting from product-oriented to process-oriented learning, enabling real-time feedback, iterative writing practices, personalized learning, and more authentic, domain-specific communication tasks. These changes also redefine the roles of teachers as facilitators and learners as more autonomous participants. However, the integration of GenAI presents critical challenges, including learner overreliance, concerns over accuracy in specialized domains, issues of academic integrity and assessment validity, and limited pedagogical readiness among educators. Additionally, the review identifies key research gaps, particularly the lack of integrative frameworks, longitudinal evidence, and ESP-specific ethical guidelines. This study contributes by synthesizing fragmented findings into a comprehensive understanding of pedagogical transformation in AI-integrated ESP and offers theoretical insights and practical implications for educators, curriculum designers, and policymakers in advancing evidence-based and responsible implementation of GenAI in specialized language education.

papers.title: Can Generative AI Navigate Multicultural Pedagogical Dilemmas? A Scenario-Based Evaluation of Islamic Religious Education
papers.authors: Asman, Muhammad Irwan Putra, Maulid Agustin, Ria Nata Kusuma, Miftahul Hasan
papers.abstract: The increasing integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into educational practice raises critical concerns regarding its capacity to address religious diversity, cultural differences, and ethical complexities in Islamic Religious Education. This research evaluates the multicultural pedagogical quality of AI-generated instructional recommendations and examines the contribution of structured prompting to their contextual and instructional adequacy. Employing a scenario-based comparative design, 288 recorded responses were examined across 24 multicultural dilemmas, six thematic domains, two prompting conditions, and two response profiles. Pedagogical quality was assessed by two recorded raters using six evaluation dimensions, complemented by paired comparisons and categorical analysis of instructional limitations. Structured prompting achieved substantially higher quality scores than standard prompting (77.16 versus 58.80), with a mean difference of 18.36 points (95% CI: 15.82–20.91). Nevertheless, assessment quality remained the weakest dimension, while assessment-related limitations constituted the most frequent deficiency (32.3%). Context-dependent variations further highlighted persistent challenges in addressing religious exclusivism and complex pedagogical dilemmas. These findings suggest that structured pedagogical guidance improves the evaluated completeness of AI-generated recommendations without necessarily ensuring contextual or ethical adequacy. The research underscores the importance of human-guided evaluation, critical pedagogical judgment, and multidimensional accountability in responsible AI-supported multicultural religious education.

papers.title: Psychosocial Distress and Radiation Treatment Interruptions in Patients With Cancer Using Machine Learning and Regression: Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.authors: Soheil Hashtarkhani, Christopher L. Brett, Fekede Asefa Kumsa, Rezaur Rashid, Parnian Kheirkhah Rahimabad, Saba Kheirinejad, Robert Lowell Davis, David L. Schwartz, Arash Shaban‐Nejad
papers.abstract: Background: Uninterrupted delivery of radiation therapy is critical to cancer treatment quality. Unplanned radiation treatment interruptions compromise tumor control and survival. Although previous studies have explored clinical and sociodemographic factors influencing treatment adherence, the role of psychosocial distress and related symptoms remains unclear. Objective: This study aims to identify patient-reported psychosocial predictors of radiation treatment interruptions from patient-reported distress screening data integrated with clinical and socioeconomic correlates via traditional and machine learning-enhanced modeling. Methods: This institutional cohort study included 1953 patients who underwent external beam radiation therapy between August 2020 and May 2024. Patient demographics, clinical characteristics, treatment details, and baseline distress levels were extracted from a hospital-level electronic health record data repository. Distress was assessed using the Distress Thermometer developed by the National Comprehensive Cancer Network. These data were linked with census tract-level socioeconomic indicators. Predictors of treatment interruption (measured as missed treatment days) were evaluated using negative binomial regression and an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model with a Poisson objective function. Results: The study cohort missed a mean of 1.19 (SD 2.18) treatment days (range: 0-15). Higher distress scores, the presence of learning or communication barriers, and genitourinary malignancy were significantly associated with increased interruption risk in the negative binomial regression model. The XGBoost model confirmed these features as top contributors to prediction performance, while yielding an incrementally lower root mean squared error of 2.19 (vs 2.21 for the regression model). Conclusions: Patient-reported distress and health education barriers were modestly associated with treatment interruptions, underscoring the importance of incorporating psychosocial assessments into radiation oncology workflows. Both parametric and machine learning models provided stable and closely aligned predictions of missed radiation treatment days. Key predictors identified as statistically significant in the regression model were also among the top contributors in the XGBoost model, reinforcing the robustness of these findings and supporting integration of both approaches into future intervention strategies.

papers.title: Nonlinear Feature Modeling Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Electroencephalography for Depression Classification: Deep Learning Study
papers.authors: Bin Yang, YONGFENG FAN, Xinhong Wei, Chunlei Shi
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Depression is a common mental disorder that seriously affects mental health and quality of life. Traditional depression diagnosis mainly relies on clinical interviews and subjective assessments, which may lead to variability in diagnostic outcomes. Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based computer-aided diagnosis has emerged as a promising, objective approach for depression recognition. However, effectively modeling the complex nonlinear characteristics of EEG signals remains a major challenge for existing deep learning methods. Objective This study aimed to investigate the applicability of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for EEG-based depression recognition and to evaluate the effectiveness of KAN-based nonlinear modeling frameworks on frequency-domain EEG features. Methods KAN was introduced into EEG-based depression recognition to enhance nonlinear feature representation of brain electrical signals. Two representative KAN-based convolutional architectures, ConvKAN and its efficiency-optimized variant ConvKAN Efficient, were systematically investigated for EEG classification tasks. These architectures incorporated KANLinear layers together with dynamic grid updating, enhanced weight initialization, and regularization strategies to improve nonlinear modeling capability while maintaining computational efficiency. Extensive experiments were conducted on the EDRA dataset, and the proposed framework was compared with conventional convolutional neural network–based methods and traditional machine learning approaches. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F 1 -score metrics. Results Experimental results demonstrated that the KAN-based frameworks achieved superior EEG classification performance compared with conventional convolutional neural network–based methods and traditional machine learning approaches. Among the evaluated models, ConvKAN Efficient achieved the best overall performance, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F 1 -score all exceeding 94% on the EDRA dataset. The results indicate that KAN-based architectures can effectively capture the complex nonlinear characteristics of EEG signals while preserving high computational efficiency. Conclusions This study systematically demonstrates the applicability of KAN-based nonlinear modeling frameworks to EEG-based depression recognition. The proposed framework provides a scalable and effective approach for EEG signal analysis and offers valuable technical support for both theoretical research and clinical applications in computer-aided depression recognition.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Use Among Health Care Professionals in the United States and United Kingdom: Cross-National Survey
papers.authors: Emre Sezgın, Jennifer Lee, Tomasz Jadczyk, Alysha J. Taxter
papers.abstract: Unlabelled: This cross-sectional study examined AI use among 524 health care professionals in the United States and United Kingdom, focusing on current applications, access, barriers, and factors that could support adoption. AI use was common but varied across professional and national contexts, with findings highlighting the importance of evidence, organizational guidance, training, privacy safeguards, and integration into clinical workflows for responsible adoption.

papers.title: The Influence of Artificial Intelligence Technology Usage on Generation Z's Learning Styles in German Language Learning in Malang City
papers.authors: Nadia Ziadatul khusnia
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology utilization on the learning styles of Generation Z students in German language learning in Malang City. The study employs a quantitative approach using an explanatory survey method. The sample consists of 100 respondents selected via purposive sampling. Data collection was conducted using a Likert-scale questionnaire, and the data were analyzed using SPSS software. The results indicate that the research instrument is valid and reliable, and satisfies classical assumption tests regarding normality, multicollinearity, and heteroscedasticity. Multiple linear regression analysis reveals that both AI utilization and the intensity of AI usage positively influence Generation Z's learning styles. The t-test results show that both variables have a significant partial effect, while the F-test results demonstrate a simultaneous influence on Generation Z's learning styles. An Adjusted R-Square value of 0.653 indicates that AI utilization and usage intensity explain 65.3% of the variation in Generation Z's learning styles. Thus, the presence of AI technology plays a positive role in supporting German language learning for Generation Z

papers.title: Transforming Christian Religious Education for Character Development in the Digital Era: A Conceptual Framework for Higher Education
papers.authors: Juliana Simangunsong
papers.abstract: Character development has become one of the most pressing challenges in higher education as students navigate the complexities of the digital era, including rapid technological advancement, artificial intelligence, information overload, and ethical dilemmas in online environments. These challenges require educational approaches that extend beyond developing digital competence to fostering moral integrity, spiritual maturity, ethical reasoning, and responsible digital citizenship. In this context, Christian Religious Education (CRE) plays a strategic role as a transformative educational approach by integrating Christian values into meaningful learning experiences that support holistic character development. This study employed a library research approach by critically reviewing and synthesizing contemporary literature on character education, Christian Religious Education, digital literacy, digital citizenship, and technology-enhanced learning. The findings propose an integrative conceptual framework explaining how character development can be fostered through seven interconnected stages: Digital Era, Digital Literacy, Transformative Christian Religious Education, Internalization of Christian Values, Spiritual Reflection, Habit Formation, and Character Development. The proposed framework constitutes the principal contribution of this study by demonstrating that Christian Religious Education is not merely a medium for theological instruction but a transformative educational approach that fosters holistic character development through the ethical integration of digital technologies. The framework provides a theoretical foundation for future research and practical guidance for lecturers and higher education institutions in designing digitally enriched learning environments that intentionally promote character development.

papers.title: Harmonizing islamic values and artificial intelligence in the development of the madrasah ibtidaiyah curriculum
papers.authors: Hilmiyatul Abidah Assyarifah, Nadlir
papers.abstract: This study highlights the main aspects of the research, including its objectives, methodology, findings, and contributions to the field of education. The rapid advancement of science and technology has brought significant changes to various aspects of human life. Despite the growing development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), there remains a gap in understanding how this technology can be harmonized with Islamic values within the Madrasah Ibtidaiyah (MI) curriculum. Therefore, this study aims to explore strategies for harmonizing Islamic values and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in MI curriculum development by formulating an ethical and substantive integration model. This research employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through literature review and document analysis involving various references related to Islamic education and educational technology. The findings reveal that harmonization is structured upon three main pillars: ontological foundation (AI as a tool/wasilah), axiological framework (AI ethics grounded in akhlaqul karimah), and pedagogical implementation in the curriculum. The study contributes to the field of education by proposing a new theoretical framework for developing a madrasah curriculum that is adaptive to technological advancements while maintaining its Islamic identity. Furthermore, the findings suggest the necessity of AI literacy training for MI teachers that is grounded in the values of religious moderation.

papers.title: Implementing public value management in municipal disability services through universal design: Evidence from Vilnius
papers.authors: Ana Staseviciene
papers.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractShifting municipal disability services from new public management efficiency frameworks to public value management collaborative networks is essential to align local governance with human rights standards. This study aims to examine how formal rules, administrative routines, and stakeholder participation arrangements associated with Universal Design and Public Value Management evolved in local governance. Examining the Vilnius City Municipality (1999–2025) through a longitudinal single-case design, this study adapts the sector awareness framework to analyze a multi-source qualitative corpus of 122 administrative documents and participant observations from 52 working group sessions. The empirical analysis maps a non-linear institutional transition across five distinct phases, revealing a structural shift from terminology-level denial (the official use of "invalid" until 2017) to public value management-oriented integration in non-physical domains (cultural funding criteria requiring easy language in 2024). The findings demonstrate that while universal design functions as a practical mechanism to operationalize public value management, its implementation remains fragmented and constrained by a rigid "tick-box" compliance culture that privileges physical infrastructure over informational and cognitive accessibility. Furthermore, co-creation is obstructed by deeply rooted power asymmetries that position non-governmental organizations as passive funding seekers rather than equal strategic partners with binding decision-making authority. Ultimately, the study shows that sustainable public value management implementation depends on relationship-oriented metrics, formalized power-sharing safeguards, and the institutionalization of permanent, cross-sectoral participatory channels.AcknowledgmentThe author would like to express sincere gratitude to Agota Giedrė Raišienė, doctoral research supervisor, for valuable guidance, constructive comments, and continuous support throughout the preparation of this article.The author wishes to express their sincere gratitude to the Vilnius City Municipality for providing access to the administrative documents and the Legal Acts Portal. Special thanks are extended to the 22 members of the Universal Design Working Group for their participation and insights.
