papers.authors: Angel G A Prempeh, Rashid Saeed, Christina Hill, Lucas Kopp, Allison M. Tenfelde
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Caregivers of pediatric orthopaedic surgical patients routinely receive discharge documents written at reading levels exceeding established health literacy recommendations. This disparity creates a significant barrier to comprehension and adherence to postoperative instructions. While artificial intelligence (AI) language models offer a scalable solution for simplification of medical text, a systematic evaluation of the ability to preserve critical content in surgical discharge materials remains lacking. METHODS: Publicly available caregiver-facing discharge documents for 3 common pediatric orthopaedic conditions, supracondylar humerus fractures (CRPP), pediatric forearm fractures (ORIF/CRPP), and slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE pinning), were collected. All documents underwent AI simplification using a standardized prompt with ChatGPT (version 5.2; OpenAI). Readability was assessed using 6 validated indices for both original and simplified documents. A structured content integrity review was conducted on all simplified documents by 2 independent reviewers to assess for safety-critical errors, completeness gaps, and factual accuracy, with inter-rater reliability quantified by Cohen kappa. RESULTS: Fifteen documents were obtained from institutions across 9 US states. After AI simplification, mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) decreased from 8.91 (SD: 1.38) to 4.97 (SD: 2.14), a mean reduction of 3.94 grade levels (95% CI: 2.65-5.23; P<0.001; Cohen d=1.69). All 6 readability indices improved across all documents. Eleven of 15 documents (73%) achieved the target readability threshold of FKGL 6 or below, compared with zero at baseline. Content integrity review identified 35 flags across 14 of 15 documents: 12 safety-critical errors, 16 completeness gaps, and 7 accuracy concerns. Cohen kappa was 0.87 for agreement on whether a change was clinically meaningful, 0.85 for severity classification, and 0.89 for flag category. Three documents had content omissions sufficient to require clinician revision before clinical use. Greater word-count reduction was associated with a higher burden of safety-critical flags (Spearman rho 0.63; P=0.012). CONCLUSIONS: While ChatGPT substantially reduced the reading complexity of pediatric orthopaedic discharge documents, it also introduced safety-critical alterations. AI-assisted simplification should be implemented only with structured clinician review. Larger word-count reductions were associated with more safety-critical alterations, so the magnitude of reduction may help prioritize which simplified documents receive the closest clinician review. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

papers.title: Altered network organization with shift to local processing during adaptive behavior in multiple sclerosis
papers.authors: Julia Elmers, Moritz Mückschel, Tjalf Ziemssen, Christian Beste
papers.abstract: Abstract To adjust to changing environmental demands, the brain needs to organize and (re)configure mental resources in so-called task sets. Following a network perspective of cognitive functions, these processes are considered to rely on dynamic exchange of information between distant brain regions, possibly synchronized by slow-wave theta oscillations. However, few attempts have been made to describe the directional transfer of information in theta networks during behavioral adaptation. In the current study, we examined directed neural information transfer in 57 healthy individuals and 57 patients with Multiple Sclerosis with a focus on brain-behavior associations during task switching. For this, we calculated behavioral switch costs, and further applied an artificial neural network-based approach on neurophysiological EEG data to estimate linear and nonlinear effective connectivity measures within cortical networks during task switching. Source reconstruction and connectivity analyses revealed distinct neural network architectures and communication strategies during task switching in healthy controls compared to patients with Multiple Sclerosis. In healthy controls, enhanced modulations of long-range fronto-parietal connectivities were associated with higher reaction time switch costs, possibly reflecting increased cognitive demands rather than adaptive processes. In contrast, patients with Multiple Sclerosis relied more strongly on local intra-regional modulations, which is consistent with the idea of a dysconnectivity syndrome in Multiple Sclerosis. Strikingly, stronger modulations in self-connectivities were associated with better accuracy measures in patients with Multiple Sclerosis, suggesting a compensatory mechanism to support performance. Notably, only nonlinear directed connectivity measures were related to behavioral switch costs, emphasizing the importance of nonlinear models for adaptive cognitive processes.

papers.title: Dimensionality reduction for partial-volume correction in quantitative SPECT
papers.authors: Johan Gustafsson, Erik Larsson, Katarina Sjögreen Gleisner
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this paper is to develop a method for region-based post-reconstruction partial-volume correction (PVC) of SPECT images, which explicitly estimates the mean activity concentration in regions without assuming strict intra-regional uniformity. APPROACH: Lu-SPECT images obtained from the simulation of eight anthropomorphic phantoms as well as two example patients. Both sets of data were reconstructed using OS-EM with ten subsets and up to 40 iterations, including compensation for attenuation, scatter, and spatial resolution. Reconstructed images were deconvolved using the van Cittert algorithm and Lucy-Richardson algorithm, both implemented on images represented as standard cuboid voxels or as regional voxels, consisting of regions defined from whole-image segmentation. Methods embedding regional voxels were applied both assuming region-wise uniform activity concentration and incorporating perturbations in the form of cosine series to relax the uniformity assumption. For comparison, images were also processed with the iterative Yang method and MIRD recovery coefficients. Evaluation was performed with respect to the estimated activity concentration for kidneys, spleen, and tumours, as well as the total activity in the images. MAIN RESULTS: Mean activity-concentration errors prior to PVC were (-22.6±11.5) %, (-13.8±2.1) %, and (-7.4±2.8) % for tumours, kidneys, and spleen, respectively. Region-perturbed van Cittert deconvolution with order 4 reduced these errors to (2.3±7.7) %, (0.3±2.2) %, and (4.0±1.6) % while the errors for region-perturbed Lucy-Richardson deconvolution of order 4 were (0.3±8.0) %, (0.0±1.6) %, (2.6±0.5) %. Corresponding results for the iterative Yang method were (2.8±21) %, (-0.3±2.1) %, and (3.8±2.4) % and using MIRD recovery coefficients (-5.0±14.2) %, (-7.1±1.9) %, and (-0.6±3.1) %. SIGNIFICANCE: Region-based PVC improves the accuracy of quantitative SPECT, and the inclusion of cosine perturbations allows for a gradual relaxation of the uniformity assumption.

papers.title: Teachers’ technostress in the emerging generative AI era: a systematic review and bibliometric mapping (2005–2025)
papers.authors: Eko Nurhaji Purnomo, Shaymaa M.H. Darwish, Susilo Wati, Mohamad S.J. Darwish, Abdur Rofik
papers.abstract: Educational technology is creating a digital paradox. Its pedagogical innovation notwithstanding, the spread of algorithmic systems, and emerging generative AI tools, may also erode teaching quality, staff retention, and progress towards SDGs 3, 4, 8 and 10. Existing teacher stress frameworks predate the AI era and may not fully capture teachers’ current stressors. This study reviews 20 years of research on teacher technostress (2005–2025), reconstructing its intellectual structure and integrating evidence on sources, consequences, and mitigation strategies. A two-track design was employed: a bibliometric map through Biblioshiny on 194 Scopus records, and a PRISMA-based systematic review of 26 empirical studies. Findings identify five canonical technostress creators, alongside institutional surveillance and social media as established emergent stressor domains; generative AI emerged as a nascent domain, addressed directly by only two of the 26 included studies. Key outcomes are burnout, insomnia and turnover intention. The moderating variables are perceived organizational support, TPACK competence and transformational leadership. Current Information Systems frameworks do not sufficiently consider the socio-educational dimensions of teacher technostress. Achieving the SDG targets implicated in this review requires developing equity-based protective policies, embedding AI ethics within TPACK professional development, and designing contextually sensitive support systems.

papers.title: From AI literacy to epistemic vigilance: rethinking higher education curriculum in the age of artificial confidence
papers.authors: Guy Hochman, Craig S. Miller, Marc Kline
papers.abstract: This conceptual paper argues that higher education’s response to generative artificial intelligence (AI) must move beyond access, efficiency, and technical literacy. Although AI offers real pedagogical affordances for personalized support, feedback, writing, translation, and iterative learning, its fluent and authoritative outputs risk weakening the epistemic practices on which higher education depends. More information does not necessarily produce better judgment when students mistake fluency for truth, outsource evaluation, or develop artificial confidence in AI-mediated conclusions. The paper proposes a curricular shift from AI literacy alone to epistemic vigilance: the explicit teaching of source verification, evidence–inference discrimination, prompt awareness, comparison across sources and outputs, uncertainty recognition and confidence calibration, metacognitive justification, AI-free phases of work, and ethical transparency. The central claim is that AI can enhance learning only when students remain responsible for judgment, justification, and accountability, even when cognition is technologically scaffolded.

papers.title: Creative constants in architectural education: augmenting the use of keywords through innovative practices
papers.authors: Loris Rossi, Valerio Perna, Laura Pedata
papers.journal: International Journal of Design Creativity and Innovation
papers.abstract: This paper examines the potential of keywords, understood as creative constants, as pedagogical tools to stimulate creativity in the early stages of architectural study. Rather than equating words with experiences, keywords are framed as catalysts enabling incremental and iterative design concept generation. The study situates this approach within recent developments in Artificial Intelligence, which introduce new paradigms for understanding creativity in design education. The methodology combines the analysis of theoretical precedents, such as the use of images and narratives in literature, with practical experimentation through analogue studio exercises and AI-assisted text-to-image platforms. This dual approach demonstrates how keywords can help students bridge abstract ideas and design action while accelerating iterative exploration. Developed through a multidisciplinary perspective, the research connects insights from literature, design theory, pedagogy, and emerging digital tools. The findings suggest that keywords support students in constructing a personal repertoire of creative constants applicable across different stages of the design process. By integrating analogue and AI-supported methods, the paper proposes a pedagogical framework to nurture creativity and innovation in architectural education.

papers.title: Sociocultural factors influencing familiarity, comfort and trust in AI-powered data collection tools in Nigeria
papers.authors: Yusuf Babatunde Okewole, Akinpẹlu Ọlanrewaju Olutayọ
papers.journal: African Journal of Science Technology Innovation and Development
papers.abstract: This study examines the perceptions of AI-powered data collection tools for social research in Nigeria’s digitally fragmented society. Using a quantitative survey of 105 respondents across diverse settlements and regions, informed by the AI-Device User Acceptance (AIDUA) model, it examines how sociocultural factors influence familiarity, comfort and trust. Findings show that comfort with AI correlates strongly with higher education (p < 0.001, Eta = 0.566) and religion (p < 0.001, Eta = 0.476). A major urban-rural comfort divide exists (68.8% vs. 33.3.%). Familiarity is significantly higher among urban residents and varies by age and education. Notably, trust was higher among rural respondents and the few Hausa/Fulani samples whose data were analyzed. Key ethical concerns included privacy risks and data misuse. Regression analysis showed neither familiarity (B = 0.117, p = 0.754) nor comfort (B = 0.176, p = 0.639) significantly predicted trust (R2 = 0.003, F (2, 102) = 0.156, p = 0.856). The study concludes that culturally tailored frameworks that consider local language, community leaders’ acceptance and legitimate institutional affiliation are essential to bridge the acceptance gap. This study contributes to the scholarship by expanding the AIDUA to include unique cultural factors and institutional roles in a Global South context.

papers.title: Do College Students Prefer AI Health Coaches Over Human Health Coaches? – A Mix-Method Exploratory Study
papers.authors: Zi Yan, Sarah S. Benes, Jessica C. Peacock
papers.abstract: Background Rising rates of chronic disease, mental health concerns, and lifestyle-related challenges among college students highlight the need for scalable approaches to support student well-being.Purpose This study developed and tested the feasibility of an artificial intelligence (AI) virtual health coach and compared it to human coaches among college students.Methods Thirty-one college students completed six coaching sessions with seven trained human coaches and two consecutive sessions with an AI coach. The AI agent was developed using prompt engineering on a commercial large language model platform. After each session, students completed quantitative evaluations. Semi-structured interviews were conducted.Results Students rated human coaching sessions significantly higher than AI sessions across all evaluated dimensions. Rater evaluations indicated comparable performance between AI and human coaches, but human coaches demonstrated significantly greater empathy and helpfulness. Qualitative findings revealed that human coaches were valued for care, connection, accountability, and responsiveness, whereas AI coaches were perceived as nonjudgmental, accessible, and highly structured, with strengths in goal clarification and information delivery.Discussion Whereas human coaches were preferred overall, AI health coaching demonstrated feasibility and potential value as a complementary, scalable support tool.Transition to Health Education Practice Practitioners should proactively seek training in AI tools, prompt design, and safety-tuning so they can effectively and responsibly deploy AI as a supplemental tool for the health coaching practice.

papers.title: A large-scale comparison of human and large language model raters in automated essay scoring
papers.authors: Zülal Ayar, Gökhan Akçapınar
papers.journal: Innovation in Language Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have brought about pivotal changes in writing assessment, particularly through comparisons with human raters. Nevertheless, most current studies are limited to analyzes that compare a small number of models with human raters and focus primarily on overall score differences or inter-rater agreement. This quantitative study compares 17 cutting-edge LLMs on the same dataset, examining the models’ scoring consistency, proximity to the mean scores assigned by human raters, and structural similarity and clustering analyzes of scoring behaviours relative to those of humans, based on analytic sub-dimensions, using a multidimensional approach. To that end, the research analyzed literary essays written by 46 first-year students at upper-intermediate proficiency in the English Language and Literature department of a state university in Türkiye, based on Ernest Hemingway's short story ‘The Cat in the Rain,’ using an expert-validated six-dimensional analytic rubric. The findings reveal substantial variability at the level of analytic sub-dimensions among 17 LLMs despite their proximity to experts in terms of overall scores. Moreover, these models clustered according to their average dimension-score profiles, while some displayed closer alignment with human rater profiles. Finally, while different correlation values were identified for each analytic dimension, high consistency was noted between the two expert raters with respect to overall scoring.

papers.title: Teachers’ professional learning online: expertise, identity, and judgement in social media spaces
papers.authors: Steven Kolber, Jeffrey Paul Carpenter, Keith Heggart
papers.abstract: Teachers’ professional learning is increasingly mediated through online and social media environments, creating new opportunities for connection, collaboration, and professional dialogue. At the same time, these spaces have become more complex and contested, shaped by platform affordances, monetisation, algorithmic curation, and the growing presence of artificial intelligence. This paper examines how teachers and teacher educators are making sense of social media-mediated professional learning within this changing landscape. Drawing on a recorded online seminar presented to the Australian Teacher Educators Association, the paper employs metalogue as an analytic method to interrogate dialogue among teacher educators and their peers. The metalogue functions as a reflexive and interpretive reconstruction that foregrounds tensions, uncertainties, and contested claims to expertise and professionalism. The paper explores how online professional learning is shaped by issues of identity, visibility, performativity, and professional judgement, as well as the implications of shifting platform cultures for teacher educators and pre-service teachers. By centring teacher educators’ perspectives and adopting a dialogic methodological approach, the paper contributes to understanding how professional learning online is navigated, interpreted, and modelled within teacher education. Suggesting that social media-mediated professional learning involves ongoing ethical discernment and reflexive judgement, not straightforward adoption or rejection of platforms or practices.

papers.title: Advancing clinical integration in undergraduate dental education through AI-enabled instructional design: a qualitative thematic analysis
papers.authors: Selçuk Akturan, Ömer Faruk Güdük, İpek Nur Berberoğlu, ELİF ÖZLEM ARDIÇ KEMERKAYA, Salman Yousuf Guraya
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) in health professions education, qualitative evidence for integarting AI-supported instructional redesign on teaching practices and students' experiences in undergraduate dental education remains limited. The aim of this study was to explore the educational impact of AI-supported instructional redesign of lessons in undergraduate dental education. METHODS: We conducted this inductive qualitative thematic analysis in an undergraduate dental education setting. Existing lessons were redesigned using AI-supported recommendations to strengthen alignment between learning objectives, authentic clinical contexts, and expected clinical outcomes. Data were collected through classroom observations and students' focus group discussions. An inductive thematic analysis was performed, and findings from multiple data sources were curated, collecetd, and triangulated to enhance credibility. RESULTS: AI-supported instructional redesign transformed teaching by promoting authentic clinical scenarios, clinically oriented discussions, and explicit reasoning activities. Thematic analysis identified four interconnected themes: (1) a shift from teacher-centred knowledge delivery to facilitation of clinical reasoning; (2) transformation from passive attendance to active cognitive engagement; (3) building clinical meaning through authentic clinical contexts and collaborative dialogue; and (4) creating conditions for professional learning through psychological safety. AI functioned as a pedagogical design-support tool rather than replacing the educators' instructional role. Overall, the observed educational changes appeared to arise primarily from the pedagogical redesign enabled by AI-supported planning rather than from students' direct interaction with AI. CONCLUSION: This study endorses the role of AI-supported instructional redesign in enriching the existing undergraduate dental curriculum. This approach can potentially help educators align learning objectives, instructional strategies, and authentic clinical contexts. The reported educational modifications reflect primarily the implementation of learner-centred and clinically oriented pedagogical strategies, with AI functioning as a design-support mechanism rather than as a direct instructional agent.

papers.title: “I Just Needed Someone to Listen”: A Community Discussion Analysis of Redditors’ Discourse About Using General-Purpose LLMs for Therapy
papers.authors: Hansen Lee, Jinkyung Park, Bart P. Knijnenburg
papers.abstract: Despite increasing efforts of legislatures to prohibit specialized AI-driven apps from providing therapeutic decision-making, general-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used as alternative tools for mental health support. In this paper, we examine the increased adoption of AI for mental health through the lens of proponents’ and opponents’ discussions on public forums. Through a qualitative analysis of 67 Reddit discussion threads (totaling 2948 comments), we offer an in-depth investigation of the various contexts in which users rely on (or fail to rely on) AI for mental health support, as well as an analysis of the main discussions (including positions for and against the use of AI for therapy) within the community. By critically reflecting on our findings, we highlight ethical considerations and discuss how research, design and regulation of AI tools can help improve mental health support for users with complicated needs while mitigating potential harms.

papers.title: PEARL to the Rescue: An AI Assistant Designed for Physical Education Teachers
papers.authors: Thomas Trendowski
papers.abstract: PEARL (Physical Education for Assessment, Reflection, and Lesson-Design) is a chatbot developed using ChatGPT that acts as a personal assistant for various aspects of a physical education teacher’s job, including lesson planning, instruction, and assessment. This article explores the purpose of the chatbot, the foundational principles behind it, its limitations, and several practical applications. By combining artificial intelligence with sound pedagogical frameworks, PEARL aims to empower physical educators to save time, enhance instructional quality, and reflect more efficiently.

papers.title: AI-supported assignments in management education: How students interact with instructions
papers.authors: Maureen Snow Andrade, Wu-Ting Chen
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) tools become more common in coursework, students must follow instructions that include procedural and AI-related tasks. This study examined how 30 students in an introductory organizational behavior course attended to and understood assignment instructions using eye-tracking data and post-task comprehension measures. Students accessed all instructional components, but attention was uneven. They focused primarily on introductory content and evaluation criteria, while procedural steps involving AI use and revision received less attention. Comprehension findings showed that students recalled task goals but often missed specific procedural and AI-related details.

papers.title: The Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Literacy: A Bibliometric Analysis 2011–2024
papers.authors: Qurat Ul Ain Saleem, Muhammad Kabir Khan, Azeem Akbar, Nusrat Ali

papers.title: Talking with language models
papers.authors: James Ravi Kirkpatrick, Alexandru Radulescu, Rachel Sterken
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) produce text that invites us to treat our interactions with them as conversations, and to treat them as intelligent interlocutors who remember, act, and make commitments. We argue that this conversational presupposition is mistaken. We introduce the artifactual stance, which describes human–AI interaction in terms of their design and affordances, rather than potential intentional attitudes. On our account, LLMs produce candidate text that users interpret, evaluate, and sometimes adopt as their own speech. We argue that such exchanges are not conversations, since generating text does not itself constitute an utterance or the performance of a speech act. Rather the communicative and normative work of interpretation, commitment, and action remains with the user. Our framework explains both the sophistication and usefulness of LLMs, and the conversational appearances that can be traced back to properties of the interface and to artifact design. It also reframes puzzles about AI reference, the persistence of supposed interlocutors, and responsibility for AI-generated text. These questions are better approached through an account of how artifacts mediate human linguistic practices than through assumptions about AI speakerhood.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Design and Access: Toward Visual Scene Displays for Brain–Computer Interface Use in Augmentative and Alternative Communication by Children
papers.authors: Kevin M. Pitt, James Sawall, Elena Butler, Austin Bubak, Ahad Behboodi
papers.journal: Journal of Speech Language and Hearing Research
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Brain-computer interface (BCI) may support communication and computer interaction through neural signals such as the P300 event-related potential (ERP). As a step toward integrating photographic visual scene displays (VSDs) in BCI, this study examined the feasibility of incorporating contextual, naturalistic scenes in which communication items were embedded asymmetrically. METHOD: To evaluate the effects of contextual scene use, 24 neurotypical children aged 8-13 years completed three experimental conditions: (1) a contextual scene with asymmetrical item placement, (2) an asymmetrical arrangement of the same items without contextual information, and (3) a standard grid. Electroencephalogram data were analyzed for the N170, P300, and N400 ERP components, and offline (predicted) BCI augmentative and alternative communication accuracy was calculated. RESULTS: The results showed that asymmetry increased frontal and centro-parietal P300 amplitudes, and the scene enhanced occipital N170. Offline BCI performance was similar across the scene and grid conditions, and participants rated the scene as more visually appealing. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that asymmetry and contextual embedding within scenes may enhance neural engagement and user experience, providing a preliminary foundation for considering photographic VSDs into pediatric BCI research.

papers.title: Extending synthetic medical education: generating OSCE cases with LLMs
papers.authors: Kaiz P. Esmail, Arya S Rao, Richard S. Lee, Ali Ebada, David C. Whitehead, Caroline P. Meehan, Andrew Cheung, Marc D. Succi
papers.abstract: Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) are central to competency-based medical education, yet high-quality case development is resource-intensive. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable solution, but comprehensive OSCE case generation, including components such as candidate instructions, standardized patient scripts, and examiner marking schemes, is underexplored. We developed an LLM-based tool to generate complete OSCE stations. Three board-certified internists evaluated 24 generated cases across eight internal medicine diagnoses and three learner levels using a 12-item Likert instrument. Ratings were high across all domains; communication behaviors (4.64/5), EPA alignment (4.62/5), and overall value (4.61/5) performed best; guideline concordance scored lowest (4.24/5) with the greatest rater disagreement. As a feasibility study, these findings establish that whole, schema-validated OSCE stations can be generated from a single structured call at a quality experts rate as acceptable, while also identifying guideline concordance and difficult calibration as the domains most requiring faculty oversight -- providing reproducible infrastructure for, but not yet evidence of, effective EPA-aligned OSCE development.

papers.title: The impact of a synchronized multimodal AI interface configuration on consumer experience journey and satisfaction
papers.authors: Zhiliang Pan
papers.abstract: With the rapid integration of multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) into digital interfaces, understanding how combined visual, auditory, and textual cues influence consumers' experience journeys and satisfaction has become critically important for both scholars and practitioners. While prior research has examined individual modalities in isolation, the comparative effects of a specific rich multimodal interface configuration versus a minimal-modality baseline across different stages of the consumer journey remain underexplored. This study draws on cue utilization theory, presence theory, and the customer journey framework to investigate how exposure to a synchronized multimodal AI interface (text + voice + animated avatar) versus a text-only interface affects consumer satisfaction through three experimentally induced journey stages: search, evaluation, and post-purchase. A between-subjects online experiment (N = 320 recruited; 312 retained after screening) was conducted using a simulated e-commerce platform where participants interacted with an AI shopping assistant featuring either text-only or synchronized text-voice-avatar cues. Results from SEM indicate that the synchronized multimodal interface was associated with higher perceived diagnosticity and immersion, which in turn were related to higher satisfaction across all three stages. The configuration–satisfaction contrast was largest for evaluation satisfaction (Cohen’s d = 1.58, 95% CI [1.33, 1.83]); the indirect-effect patterns via perceived diagnosticity and immersion were statistically consistent with, but not demonstrative of, the proposed pathways. We emphasize that the two conditions differ not only in synchronization but also in modality count, anthropomorphic cues, and social presence; accordingly, all findings are interpreted as pertaining to the interface configuration as a whole, not to integration quality as an isolated construct. Theoretical contributions include extending cue utilization theory in the form of a speculative conjecture and identifying stage-specific patterns. Managerial implications suggest that e-commerce platforms should consider synchronized multimodal cue design, particularly during product comparison phases in simulated and early deployment contexts, and should be regarded as preliminary pending field validation.

papers.title: A calibrated-domain DEM–machine learning assessment of asphalt concrete stiffness and micromechanical response
papers.authors: Udeme Udo Imoh, Majid Movahedi Rad
papers.abstract: Abstract Asphalt concrete is a heterogeneous composite whose stiffness and damage response depend on aggregate contacts, binder-mediated bonding, air voids, force chain evolution, and progressive bond failure. This study presents a calibrated-domain assessment of an AC-16C mixture using three two-dimensional Discrete Element Method contact/bond formulations: the linear parallel bond, soft-bond, and contact-bond models, together with a machine-learning stiffness surrogate. The 160 records constitute a hybrid laboratory–DEM/parametric dataset within a single AC-16C domain, rather than 160 physically distinct mixtures. The DEM outputs were used to interpret the contact forces, particle displacement, bond breakage, coordination number, energy dissipation, and fracture localization. The Linear Parallel Bond Model produced the stiffest response because it transferred both force and moment; the Soft-Bond Model represented gradual softening and energy dissipation and the Contact-Bond Model exhibited earlier localized bond failure. The machine learning models used uniaxial compressive strength, indirect tensile strength, dynamic modulus, and Poisson’s ratio to predict the experimental elastic modulus; DEM-derived descriptors were not included as predictors. Using a 112/24/24 training, validation, and holdout partition, Random Forest and XGBoost achieved holdout R 2 values of 0.940 and 0.928, respectively, whereas the ANN/MLP was less stable, with an R 2 of 0.847. Because the dynamic modulus dominated the feature importance, the high predictive accuracy primarily reflected the stiffness-variable collinearity within the calibrated domain. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as internal calibrated-domain interpolation rather than external validation or evidence of a general microstructure–property relationship. Broader application requires physically independent mixtures, complete DEM reproducibility information, three-dimensional verification, raw data disclosure, and measured runtime comparisons.

papers.title: Humanist learning and artificial intelligences: critical literacies for digital worlds
papers.authors: Christine L. Johnston
papers.abstract: Abstract Shifting technological landscapes have been shaping the epistemologies, methods, and workflows of classicists, historians, and archaeologists for more than a century. Yet these technologies and their impacts have not always been subject to reflexive interrogation within our disciplines. As artificial intelligence (AI) technologies – especially generative AI – have become widely accessible, there has been a wave of concern among educators around student learning outcomes and academic honesty. In addressing these challenges, we must also engage in critical reflection around the use of AI technologies in our research and teaching from humanist and social scientist perspectives in order to serve critical learning outcomes and counter rising digital colonialism. This paper first situates the conversation within the context of corporate AI economies and the intersections between AI technologies and antiquity-focused fields. It then proposes three AI-focused literacies for cultivating core ancient Mediterranean studies competencies and fostering critical thinking: the ability to identify and analyse the impact of taxonomic frameworks and data training inputs on algorithmic outputs; the ability to understand the development of computational models and algorithmic reasoning and their applications; and the ability to critically evaluate the ethical and environmental impacts of algorithmic reasoning and AI technologies. Critical assessment of the foundational structures and logics of AI systems and economies situates both educators and learners to critically assess the political, social, and environmental impacts of such systems on the study of the past and the world in the present.

papers.title: Cardiorespiratory and metabolic changes in women with obesity undergoing high-intensity tethered deep-water running associated with normoxia or inter-effort hypoxia
papers.authors: Marcela Coffacci de Lima Viliod, Bianca Monteiro Silva, Gabriela Ferreira Abud, Gabriela Ueta Ortiz, Sofia Germano Travieso, Marcelo Papoti, Ellen Cristini de Freitas
papers.abstract: Abstract Obesity is characterised by adipocyte hypertrophy, an imbalance of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, and tissue hypoxia. Non-weight-bearing exercise, such as deep-water running (DWR), may be suitable for people with obesity and, when combined with hypoxia exposure, may improve cardiorespiratory fitness and health-related outcomes. This study investigated the effects of tethered DWR combined with intermittent hypoxia on aerobic capacity, body composition, metabolic and inflammation markers and dietary intake in women with obesity. Thirty-one women (36 ± 5·9 years; BMI 32·5 ± 2·3) with grade I obesity were randomised to normoxia (NOR, FiO₂ = 21 %) or inter-effort hypoxia (IEH, FiO₂ = 12 %). Training of four 5 min bouts performed at 100–110 % of the heart rate corresponding to the anaerobic threshold, interspersed with 5 min recovery periods, three times weekly for 8 weeks. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included aerobic capacity, body composition, metabolic and inflammatory markers, and dietary intake. Mixed-effects models followed by Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test were used. IEH reduced SpO₂ ( p < 0·0001) and increased heart-rate-derived internal load ( p < 0·05) without increasing perceived exertion. Significant group × time interactions were observed for glucose ( p = 0·002), total cholesterol ( p = 0·004) and LDL-cholesterol ( p = 0·026), primarily reflecting decreased glucose and increased total and LDL-cholesterol in NOR. Dietary intake and NOVA food categories did not change significantly. Both conditions elicited similar cardiorespiratory and performance-related improvements. IEH did not confer additional benefits for body composition or inflammatory markers.

papers.title: AI-Generated Deepfake Financial Scams: A Missing Liability Regime for Consumer Protection Frameworks
papers.authors: A Lui, A Miglionico
papers.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) outputs, such as deepfakes, can be useful for creating realistic simulations in education, news reporting, and the arts. However, the emergence of malicious deepfake scams has raised concerns about the quality and reliability of the information provided to social media users. This article argues that a liability regime for deepfakes is currently missing from consumer protection frameworks. Regulatory interventions do not explicitly target GenAI software developers and online social media platforms. However, the implementation of appropriate risk management safeguards is necessary to prevent unlawful deepfake activities. We contend that a shared liability regime for deepfakes among the multiple actors involved could offer adequate protection for victims of online financial fraud and would effectively target the deepfake supply chain. This shared liability regime would be complemented by the UK Financial Conduct Authority’s consumer duty rule, which acts as a preventive monitoring and enforcement mechanism to avoid foreseeable harm to consumers of AI applications.

papers.title: From curiosity to churn: A longitudinal analysis of user engagement with an LLM-powered social bot
papers.authors: Chenxi Lin, Wenqi Wang, Zhuoren Jiang

papers.title: Firm-level effects of AI attention on wages and productivity: A global comparative study
papers.authors: Swapnanil SenGupta
papers.abstract: This paper studies how wages and productivity among publicly listed firms vary with AI attention during a period of uneven AI adoption. AI attention measures the prominence of AI in the country-level information environment. It is distinct from AI adoption. The wage measure captures average staff expenditure on wages and salaries per employee. Using data for 69,783 listed firms in 83 countries over 2004–2023, I measure this attention with Google Trends and combine TWFE, IV–2SLS, and local projections to estimate static and dynamic relationships. Among listed firms in advanced economies (AEs), higher AI attention is associated with lower wages but higher labour productivity and TFP. Listed firms in emerging market and developing economies (EMDEs) show short-run wage gains and positive productivity responses. These patterns also vary across firms, with wage declines more pronounced among smaller, lower-productivity, and goods-producing listed firms. The sample represents the organised listed corporate sector, which constitutes a particularly selective segment of the firm population in EMDEs; the wider SME, informal, and unlisted sectors remain outside the scope of the analysis. The patterns are consistent with expectations, perceived substitution risk, organisational investment, and workforce composition playing different roles in listed-firm adjustment. • Google Trends measures AI attention for 69,783 listed firms across 83 countries. • Higher AI attention relates to lower wages and higher productivity in AEs. • EMDE listed firms show short-run wage gains and positive productivity responses. • Local projections show persistent and heterogeneous responses to AI attention. • Responses vary by firm size, productivity, sector, and country development level.

papers.title: Responses of large language model-based chatbots to simulated psychotic ideation across repeated interactions
papers.authors: Marek Kotas, Wojciech Pichowicz, Julia Karska, Kacper Żełabowski, Patryk Piotrowski, Błażej Misiak
papers.abstract: Following the development of widely accessible large language model-based chatbot systems, concerns have emerged that such systems may reinforce psychotic ideation through affirmation of delusional content. However, systematic evaluations of chatbot responses to psychotic scenarios remain limited. We hypothesized that chatbot responses would become increasingly affirmatory over repeated interactions with the user. To test this, we evaluated the responses of ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Replika to simulated psychosis scenarios. Conversations were conducted across seven consecutive days in two languages. Responses were coded for chatbot stance toward psychotic content, recommendation to seek clinical assessment, presence of follow-up questions, and additional advice. Mixed-effects and linear regression models were used, including cluster-robust linear probability models for binary outcomes. As simulated symptom severity increased across days, ChatGPT responses became less affirmatory, DeepSeek responses remained relatively stable, and Replika responses became more affirmatory; latter two trajectories differed significantly from ChatGPT. Response variability decreased for ChatGPT and Replika but increased for DeepSeek across days. The effects of language and symptom domain were non-significant. Recommendation rates differed significantly between systems. DeepSeek and Replika provided potentially harmful advice, including discontinuation of antipsychotic treatment, in 21% and 37% of conversations, respectively. These findings suggest that affirmation of psychotic ideation significantly varies across different chatbots and does not appear to be an unavoidable consequence of large language model deployment. Furthermore, they underscore the need for developing explicit safety standards governing chatbot responses to psychotic content.

papers.title: What makes human service distinctly human in the AI era? Conceptualizing and measuring authentic relational service competency
papers.authors: Sun-Hwa Kim
papers.journal: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services

papers.title: Contralateral delay activity during dynamic spatial updates in working memory
papers.authors: Charles Chernik, Ronald van den Berg, Mikael Lundqvist
papers.abstract: Working memory (WM) enables us to maintain and directly manipulate mental representations, yet we know little about the neural implementation of this privileged online format. We recorded electroencephalography data as human subjects engaged in a task requiring continuous updates to the locations of objects retained in WM as well as in a visually identical task with WM demands removed. Analysis of neural data suggested WM-related contralateral delay activity reversed polarity as objects held in WM moved to the opposite hemifield. The control task suggested this was partially but not fully explained by visual attention demands. Thus, the spatial location of activity related to both attention and WM was updated to meet behavioral demands as the spatial location of remembered objects changed.

papers.title: The automation paradox: Efficiency gains vs. workforce concerns in human-AI collaboration
papers.authors: Nagendra Kumar, Rajeev Ranjan Kumar, Alok Raj

papers.title: Performance of large language models in providing patient- oriented information on gingival recession: a comparative study
papers.authors: Sultan Albeshri
papers.abstract: Patients are increasingly turning to large language models (LLMs) for health information, but the quality of patient-oriented information remains uncertain. This article evaluated the performance of three major LLMs in answering clinically relevant patient's questions related to gingival recession. A descriptive comparative study was carried out utilizing twenty standardized patient-centered questions related to gingival recession. Each question was submitted once to ChatGPT 5.5, Gemini 3.5, and Claude Sonnet 5, generating 60 responses. Five board-certified periodontists independently evaluated the responses using the validated Accuracy of Information (AOI) Index, a completeness scale, and expert preference rankings. Word count and response generation time were also recorded. Non-parametric tests and generalized estimating equations (GEE) were applied for statistical analysis, with statistical significance set at p ≤ 0.05. No significant differences were found among the three LLMs in accuracy (p = 0.993) or completeness (p = 0.972). ChatGPT generated responses significantly faster (median: 5.82 s) and with fewer words (median: 232) than Gemini (8.46 s; 438 words) and Claude (14.61 s; 333.5 words) (both p < 0.001). Expert preference rankings differed significantly (p = 0.002): Gemini and Claude were each ranked first in 38% of evaluations, compared with 24% for ChatGPT. For all three models, the highest accuracy was observed in Post-treatment Care. The three LLMs offered broadly comparable levels of accuracy and completeness when answering patient-oriented questions with respect to gingival recession. ChatGPT was faster and more concise, while Gemini and Claude were more often preferred by the expert evaluators. These LLMs may be useful as adjuncts to patient education, but they should complement rather than replace professional periodontal consultation.

papers.title: RL-Robotutor: a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for multimodal robot tutoring
papers.authors: Muhammad Javed, Xudong Luo, Xinfu Chi, Yize Sun, Kaile Su, Sajjad Hussain Bhutto
papers.journal: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
papers.abstract: Personalised robot tutoring requires real-time pedagogical decision-making under uncertain and multimodal learner states. Existing intelligent tutoring and robot-assisted learning systems often rely on static rules, single-modality learner modelling, or short-term correctness-oriented optimisation, which limits their capacity to balance knowledge acquisition, engagement, retention, and safe embodied interaction. RL-Robotutor is presented as a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that integrates cognitive knowledge-tracing signals, facial-expression and gaze-derived affective cues, and behavioural interaction logs through transformer-based fusion. A PPO-trained meta-policy selects among specialised modules for learner assessment, curriculum adaptation, strategy selection, and reflective feedback, while a hybrid reward combines immediate learning performance, engagement, long-term learning gain, and safety. The evidence is reported by source: five public knowledge-tracing datasets assess the cognitive prediction component; controlled simulator experiments assess policy learning, reward ablation, and multimodal fusion; and a randomised robot-tutoring study assesses embodied interaction with 120 undergraduate participants. RL-Robotutor outperforms rule-based, flat reinforcement-learning, knowledge-tracing, and LLM-based comparators. In the human study, the learning gain is 0.62, compared with 0.40 for the rule-based robot condition. The full hybrid reward improves simulator learning gain by 19% over correctness-only optimisation, and full multimodal fusion improves simulator engagement by 17% over text-only modelling. Jetson Orin deployment achieves 48 ms inference latency with an absolute AUC reduction of 0.007, supporting real-time edge execution.

papers.title: Integrating Circular Economy Principles in Fashion Development: an Apparel Industry Case Study
papers.authors: Kaumadha G. S. Wickramarachchi, R. M. Chandima Ratnayake, Rivini Mataraarachchi, S. M. Samindi M. K. Samarakoon
papers.abstract: Abstract Integrating Circular Economy (CE) principles into fashion design requires designers to consider environmental impact, material, end-of-life, social, and ethical factors during concept development. Despite growing industry interest in CE, integrating it at the design stage as Circular Fashion Concept Development Process (CFCDP) remains underexplored. This study examines how CE principles can be embedded into the CFCDP within the Asian Textile and Apparel (TnA) industry. A multiple case study methodology was employed across three Sri Lankan apparel export companies (X, Y and Z) supplying three western brands (A, B, and C) in EU, UK and USA. Data collection includes literature review, semi-structured interviews, and direct and participant observations, applying a theory-adaptation approach that integrates established CFCDP frameworks with empirical insights. Findings reveal that while all three brands follow similar concept development process, CE adaptation varies. The study identifies designer involvement and the value of collaboration with industrial designers and co-creation as enablers of circularity. Two conceptual frameworks are proposed for the CFCDP: a flowchart and a swimlane diagram illustrating how internal departments, brand designers, and industrial designers can collaborate in CE implementation, both incorporating Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) within iterative design processes. This study contributes novel frameworks that bridge theory and practice in circular fashion design, offering a structured approach for integrating CE principles into early concept development and supporting both academic researchers and industry transformation.

papers.title: AI as intern, not oracle: a design logic for human–AI partnership in experiential entrepreneurship education
papers.authors: Ali Ahmad, Dwitya Amry, Denis Oakley, James McInerny, Maria Napitupulu
papers.abstract: Abstract Entrepreneurship education (EE) is increasingly extending across disciplines and institutional contexts, creating pressure to sustain the facilitation, reflection and contextual responsiveness required by experiential learning. At the same time, the rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education raises questions about how AI can support such experiential learning without assuming authority over the judgement and decision-making central to entrepreneurial action. This study develops and empirically examines an AI-as-intern design logic for experiential EE. Rather than positioning AI as an authoritative “oracle”, the framework establishes an intentionally asymmetric human-AI partnership. Here AI provides prompts, alternatives, provisional representations and process support, while learners and educators retain responsibility for contextual interpretation, evaluative judgement and consequential decisions. The study examines two postgraduate entrepreneurship cohorts at a UK university ( n = 60) using a custom AI-enabled platform integrated into normal teaching. Evidence comprised session recordings and transcripts, observational field notes, a post-workshop survey, and 12 semi-structured interviews. Findings show that students used AI primarily as process scaffolding and iterative support. Learners accepted, rejected, modified and combined AI-generated material, while team interaction created additional opportunities for scrutiny and contextual evaluation. Our findings do not establish improvements in students’ judgement, creativity or cognitive load, but do show how these activities remained active within a bounded human-AI arrangement. The paper contributes a pedagogic design logic for AI-enabled experiential EE and provides exploratory propositions for the design of human-AI pedagogy concerning human authority, evaluative judgement, collaborative oversight, creative sequencing and bounded scaffolding under conditions of scaling pressure.

papers.title: Effect of telemedicine-delivered lifestyle interventions in older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic: a nationwide two-arm randomized trial (PROACTIVE-19)
papers.authors: Szilárd Váncsa, Anett Szakolczai, Roland Molontay, Emőke Miklós, Andrea Szentesi, Klementina Ocskay, Péter Jenő Hegyi, Judit Hegyi, Anna Hegyi, Eszter Hegyi, Dóra Czapári, Zsolt Molnár, Bálint Erőss, P ter Hegyi, PROACTIVE-19 Trial Contributors, Zsolt Abonyi‐Tóth, Béla Birkás, Árpád Csathó, László Czopf, Fanni Dembrovszky, Dalma Dobszai, Nelli Farkas, Richárd Farkas, Mária Földi, Tamás Habon, Zsuzsanna Helyes, Márk Félix Juhász, Anna Kanjo, István Kiss, Szabolcs Kiss, Zsanett Macht-Szalai, Attila Márta, Katalin Márta, Anikó Vargáné Nagy, Andrea Párniczky, Piroska Pázmány, Gábor Pethö, Zoltán Péterfi, Erika Pintér, Andrea Sárközi, Zsolt Szakács, Lajos Szakó, Dominika Tóth, András Varró, Nóra Vörhendi, Noémi Zádori, Antal Zemplenyi, Borbála Zsigmond
papers.abstract: Older adults are at increased risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes, yet randomized evidence on structured lifestyle interventions in this context remains limited. We aimed to evaluate the effects of a personalized lifestyle intervention on health-related behaviors and adverse outcomes among adults aged ≥ 60 years during the COVID-19 pandemic. PROACTIVE-19 was a nationwide, open-label, randomized trial initiated in Hungary in March 2020, during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants aged ≥ 60 years were randomly assigned (1:1) to general (group A) or personalized (group B) lifestyle counselling delivered via telephone, targeting mental health, smoking, physical activity, diet, and alcohol consumption. The primary planned endpoint was a composite of COVID-19 severity outcomes; however, due to infection rates, all-cause mortality was assessed. Longitudinal lifestyle changes were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) in a modified intention-to-treat population. A total of 441 participants were analyzed (214 group A; 227 group B). All-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (HR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.28-1.53). Significant overall time effects were observed for fruit and vegetable consumption (β = 0.052, CI 0.026-0.074), smoking reduction among current smokers (β = - 0.372, CI - 0.528 to - 0.222), and psychological variables. A significantly greater reduction in estimated alcohol consumption was observed in group B among baseline drinkers compared with group A (β = - 1.357, CI - 2.425 to - 0.187), particularly in women. However, BMI among participants with obesity increased in group B (β = 0.068, CI 0.013-0.119). Seasonal and pandemic-wave effects significantly influenced physical activity and psychological distress. The personalized intervention was not associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality. Several lifestyle behaviors improved over time; however, the additional benefit of personalization was limited (Supported by the Semmelweis University Research, Development and Innovation Fund, ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04321928).

papers.title: Supporting mathematical argumentation in AI-integrated lessons: networking instrumental orchestration and teacher noticing
papers.authors: Songhee Lee, JinHyeong Park, Kyeong-Hwa Lee
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) offers new opportunities to support students’ mathematical argumentation in classrooms. We illustrate how a secondary teacher supports collective argumentation in AI-integrated lessons. This study proposes a networking approach between instrumental orchestration and teacher noticing. We identified four types of whole-class orchestrations—Spot-and-share, Sherpa-at-work, Discuss-the-screen, and Explain-the-screen—to support collective argumentation and various foci of noticing of students’ argumentation within and across the orchestrations. In Spot-and-share, the teacher interpreted AI-generated analyses of student arguments and identified critical events with potential to facilitate collective argumentation. In Sherpa-at-work, she asked students to explain their arguments and interpreted the mathematical ideas and argument components embedded in their responses. She requested further explanation when students presented incorrect warrants and summarized valid warrants while inviting the class to evaluate the warrants. In Discuss-the-screen, the teacher evaluated the influence of students’ prior contributions on the developing argument and invited the class to provide backing or rebuttals. In doing so, she reorganized students’ contributions in relation to the developing argument and extended the argument structure. In Explain-the-screen, she integrated students’ prior contributions into the emerging argument and guided the class toward a shared conclusion. We propose that networking instrumental orchestration and noticing provides a productive approach for analyzing teachers’ practices to facilitate collective argumentation in AI-integrated lessons. Our findings also offer implications for research and practice on teacher expertise in supporting collective argumentation in AI-integrated instruction.

papers.title: From Forest to Market: Sustainability Signals and Consumer Decision-Making for Amazonian Products
papers.authors: Gabriela Nobre Dias, Ingrid Moons, Kavita Miadaira Hamza, Annouk Lievens
papers.abstract: Abstract Though sustainability cues are increasingly used in consumer markets, their effectiveness in mobilising consumers to support the forest stewardship of traditional populations remains uncertain. This study examines how different types of sustainability cues influence consumer perceptions and support of forest-based products from the Amazon rainforest. Using an online survey experiment with 991 Brazilian consumers, we test the effects of three labelling approaches, environmental labels, co-creation labels highlighting collaboration with local communities, and traceability QR codes providing product origin information across two product categories (manioc flour and shoes). The results show that all three cues increased perceived sustainability for manioc flour, with the sustainability label producing the strongest effect, and that this increase, in turn, translated into higher intention to buy. None of the cues had a direct effect on intention to buy for shoes, nor did any of these effects hold for shoes. Sustainability cue knowledge or sustainability-based consumer values did not moderate these effects. The findings show that consumers do not respond uniformly to sustainability cues across product categories. From a consumer policy perspective, this underscores the need for communication strategies that improve the clarity, salience, and recognizability of sustainability information in forest-based value chains, particularly for social value claims.

papers.title: Generative AI vs. Human Sources for Sexual Health Information: Credibility, Trust, and Behavioral Intentions in a U.S. College Sample
papers.authors: Jacqueline I. Woerner, Tiffany L. Marcantonio, Humberto López Castillo
papers.abstract: Limited access to comprehensive sexual health education has prompted a need to consider the utility of alternative strategies, such as generative artificial intelligence (genAI), for delivering accurate and accessible sexual health information. Although genAI tools can generate health information, less is known about how perceptions of the source of information shape evaluations of content (e.g., human vs. genAI). The present study examined whether college students' perceptions of sexual health information differed based on source attribution. Participants (N = 266) were students recruited from a single university in the southeastern USA in 2025. They were randomly assigned to conditions in which they were made to believe that three sexual health passages that were identical across conditions (sexual communication, body image, and sexual pleasure and safety) were written by genAI, an academic expert, a community health professional, or a peer/social media influencer. Across outcomes-including perceived accuracy and clarity, warmth and helpfulness, trustworthiness, self-efficacy, and willingness to act-genAI-attributed information was evaluated less favorably than identical information attributed to human sources. For willingness to act, there were differences in source effects across topics, such that effects were strongest for sexual pleasure/safety and weakest for sexual communication. Findings remained significant after controlling for genAI familiarity/use and attitudes. Findings indicate that evaluations of sexual health information depend not only on informational content but also on perceived source legitimacy, suggesting that AI-based tools may be the most effective when paired with human guidance to support trust and actionability.

papers.title: Accuracy of transfer learning in predicting peri-implantitis onset from intraoral radiograph: A multi-center longitudinal retrospective study
papers.authors: Muhammad H. A. Saleh, Luigi Nibali, Abdusalam Alrmali, Vito Carlo Alberto Caponio, Pasquale Santamaria, Francesco Fanelli, Khrystyna Zhurakivska, Hom-Lay Wang, Giuseppe Troiano
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The growing application of artificial intelligence in dentistry has opened new opportunities for predicting peri-implantitis (PI) using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Transfer learning, where knowledge from a model pre-trained on a large dataset is adapted to a new, domain-specific task, may enhance performance, particularly when medical datasets are limited. This study evaluated the ability of several pre-trained CNN architectures applied to baseline 2D intraoral radiographs to predict peri-implantitis onset. METHODS: A retrospective multi-center study was conducted at the University of Michigan and King's College London. A total of 195 implants (146 from Michigan and 49 from London) placed in 108 maintained patients were included. For each implant, a baseline periapical radiograph taken up to one year after prosthetic restoration was analyzed. Five pre-trained CNN architectures (ResNet50, DenseNet, VGG16, InceptionV3, EfficientNet) were combined with four transfer learning strategies: feature extraction (hybrid and non-hybrid), partial fine-tuning (50% of layers), and full fine-tuning. Models were trained using patient-wise splits to avoid leakage, and performance was evaluated on an independent test set using accuracy, area under the ROC curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. RESULTS: All CNN architectures showed variable performance across transfer learning strategies. The non-hybrid feature extraction approach provided the most consistent discrimination, with the best models achieving AUC values between 0.74 and 0.83. InceptionV3 reached the highest AUC (0.83). Fine-tuning strategies yielded modest or low performance, with AUCs generally ranging from 0.42 to 0.69 across architectures. CONCLUSION: Non-hybrid feature extraction applied to pre-trained CNNs showed the most promising, though moderate, performance for predicting PI onset from baseline intraoral radiographs. These findings indicate that transfer learning may assist early risk stratification in implant dentistry, but larger prospective studies are needed before clinical adoption. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Deep learning models may serve as adjunctive tools to identify implants at higher risk for future PI based on routine baseline radiographs, supporting more individualized maintenance protocols and earlier preventive interventions.

papers.title: Research on Visual Quality Evaluation of Dalian Rural Landscape Based on Multimodal Technology
papers.authors: Xinyu Zhao, Lin Lin, Lijian Liu, Zhisheng Wang
papers.abstract: Visual quality evaluation of rural landscape is the basis for rational planning and development of rural cultural tourism resources, and the existing evaluation methods are mostly subjective and qualitative, with less research on objective and quantitative methods. This paper introduces the multimodal analysis method of eye movement + electroencephalography + subjectivity into the evaluation of visual quality of rural landscapes, and takes traditional villages, coastal villages, and primitive villages in the villages of Dalian as the research case sites, records the data indexes of the subjects under the three experimental techniques for the characterisation of features, and normalises the village with the highest mean value II to test the feasibility of the multimodal experiments; the results of the study show that: the coastal rural landscapes have a higher index in the three types of The results of the study show that the coastal rural landscape has higher indicators among the three types of villages, which is more suitable for the development of Dalian’s rural cultural tourism, and that the multimodal analysis method of eye movement + EEG + subjective has the feasibility to provide new ideas for the evaluation of the visual quality of other rural landscapes.
