papers.title: Interdisciplinary Weight Management in a Safety‐Net Health System: A Pilot Implementation Study
papers.authors: Courtney DeCan, Katie A. Thure, Nat Pedley, Brett Cervantes, Osbaldo Camargo, Karina Fing Castro, Jacqueline Cabral, Michelle Gallardo, Dailyn A Rodriguez Reyes, Alejandra Perez, Stephanie Young, Arash Nafisi, Soma Wali
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Despite the high prevalence of obesity and cardiometabolic diseases in safety-net populations, access to intensive, evidence-based lifestyle interventions and scalable implementation strategies remains limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness, acceptability, and feasibility of an interdisciplinary program in an urban safety-net health system. METHODS: This single-center, mixed-methods implementation evaluation assessed LA VIDA, a 6-month interdisciplinary weight management program for medically complex individuals. Outcomes included feasibility, patient engagement, self-rated health, quality of life, physical activity, dietary behaviors, and program satisfaction. RESULTS: Over 2 years, 95 participants completed the program. They were predominantly female (72.6%) and Latino (78.9%), with a mean age of 50 years, median BMI of 39.2 (IQR: 36.9 to 43.7), and 60% having ≥ 3 comorbidities. Median 6-month weight loss was 5.5% (IQR: -2.6% to -9.9%), with significant improvements in quality of life (p = 0.0003), physical health (p < 0.0001), moderate-intensity physical activity (p < 0.001), and dietary behaviors. Participants reported high satisfaction driven by personalized guidance, increased health knowledge, mindfulness, and the supportive group environment. CONCLUSIONS: LA VIDA was feasible and acceptable and improved patient-reported behaviors and outcomes in a safety-net setting. These findings support it as an effective model for integrated obesity care that combines lifestyle, behavioral, and pharmacologic treatment in the safety net.

papers.title: Technology‐Supported Formative Assessment in Higher Education: AI , Learning Analytics and the Future of Assessment for Learning
papers.authors: Aydın Bulut
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose This study examines the intellectual and thematic development of technology‐supported formative assessment (TSFA) in higher education and its convergence with feedback, learning analytics, artificial intelligence (AI) and self‐regulation. Design/Methodology/Approach A scoping review integrating bibliometric mapping, qualitative thematic synthesis and SWOT analysis was conducted on TSFA literature published between 2000 and 2026 (August). Findings The findings reveal accelerated growth after 2020 and a shift from technology‐centred applications towards learner‐centred, adaptive and data‐informed formative assessment. However, theoretical fragmentation, limited longitudinal evidence, ethical concerns and geographical inequalities remain. Originality/Value The study conceptualises TSFA as a technology‐mediated formative ecosystem integrating technological capacity, pedagogical regulation, learner agency and human judgement. Practical Implications Institutions should prioritise human‐centred AI integration, transparent governance, equitable access and professional development to ensure that technology supports rather than replaces formative pedagogical judgement.

papers.title: Validation of the diagnosis of Lennox–Gastaut syndrome: Challenges and lessons learned
papers.authors: Nicole Villalba, Marc B. Rosenman, Sandi Karen Lam, Kelly G. Knupp, Liu Lin Thio, W. Pete Welch, Stephanie Carapetian Randle, Rebecca Garcia‐Sosa, Laurel Reed, Tracy Dixon‐Salazar, Maura Carroll, Anup D. Patel
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by multiple seizure types, cognitive impairment, and distinct electroencephalographic (EEG) findings. However, evolving diagnostic criteria, heterogeneous clinical features, and inconsistent electronic health record (EHR) documentation complicate accurate diagnosis and cohort identification. As part of a Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute-sponsored study developing EHR-based computable phenotypes for LGS, we established a reference standard through retrospective chart review and epileptologist classification. METHODS: A multicenter retrospective chart review was conducted across seven pediatric epilepsy centers. Stratified sampling using PCORnet data selected patients based on the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision diagnosis code for LGS or other intractable epilepsy diagnoses between 2016 and 2022. Clinical teams abstracted seizure history, EEG findings, developmental status, and treatment history. Two epileptologists independently reviewed each case as classic LGS, pragmatic LGS, or not LGS. Discordant cases underwent adjudication by a senior epileptologist. Cases with incomplete or unclear data underwent repeat abstraction and review. RESULTS: Of 997 identified patients, 935 underwent classification after exclusions. Initial epileptologist disagreement occurred in 105 cases (11%, unweighted Cohen kappa = 82%). Following adjudication, 130 cases underwent reabstraction to retrieve additional EEG reports and clinical details. Rereview reclassified 67 cases initially considered "not LGS": 33 classic LGS, 12 pragmatic LGS, and 22 excluded for insufficient data. Key EHR challenges included inconsistent EEG reporting, incomplete seizure type characterization, fragmented documentation of cognitive impairment, unclear age at onset, and variable terminology across institutions and providers. Slow spike-and-wave EEG findings were the most frequently missing diagnostic element. SIGNIFICANCE: Validating LGS diagnoses using EHR data is complex and resource intensive. Standardized terminology, structured documentation, and rigorous multicenter validation may improve diagnostic accuracy, research cohort identification, computable phenotype development, and longitudinal care for individuals with LGS. Our results highlight important operational lessons for multicenter rare epilepsy studies and underscore the need for improved diagnosis pathways and longitudinal care systems for those with LGS and their families.

papers.title: Weight‐Control Exercise in Late Adolescence and Eating Disorder Psychopathology in Early Adulthood: A Prospective Analysis of the UK Millennium Cohort Study
papers.authors: Yulin Luo, Shubo Xu, Zhengyi Lu, Xiangqin Song
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine whether weight-control exercise at age 17 was prospectively associated with eating-disorder psychopathology at age 23 after accounting for age-14 characteristics, and whether associations differed by repeated-report combination or sex. METHOD: Data were from 5266 UK Millennium Cohort Study participants. Weight-control exercise at age 17 was self-reported; age-23 psychopathology was assessed with the EDE-QS-5 total score (0-15). Survey-weighted linear regressions across 50 imputed data sets adjusted sequentially for sociodemographic factors, age-14 BMI-for-age z score, weight-control exercise, eating restriction, appearance dissatisfaction, and depressive symptoms. RESULTS: In the analytic sample, survey-weighted prevalence of weight-control exercise at age 17 was 62.6% (53.1% among males; 70.6% among females). The unadjusted mean difference in age-23 scores was 2.81 points (95% CI [2.53, 3.09]); it was 1.19 (95% CI [0.89, 1.48]) after full adjustment, corresponding to 0.26 outcome SD units (95% CI [0.20, 0.33]). Participants reporting weight-control exercise at age 17 only or at both ages had higher scores than those reporting at neither age, but the two groups did not differ clearly in a post hoc contrast. The association was stronger among females than males (interaction difference = 0.87, 95% CI [0.36, 1.39]). DISCUSSION: Weight-control exercise in late adolescence was associated with greater eating-disorder psychopathology in early adulthood after adjustment for earlier characteristics. The association was modest and may reflect broader patterns of weight, eating, and emotional vulnerability.

papers.title: Persepsi Mahasiswa Terhadap Penggunaaan Artificial Intelligence dalam Pembelajaran: Students' perceptions of the use of Artificial Intelligence in learning
papers.authors: Cahaya Intan Pasaribu, Nazwa Pahira Dongoran, Yasmin Khairunisa
papers.journal: NUMBERS : Jurnal Pendidikan Matematika & Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam
papers.abstract: Perkembangan teknologi Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah memberikan berbagai kemudahan dalam proses pembelajaran, khususnya bagi mahasiswa dalam mencari informasi, memahami materi, dan menyelesaikan tugas akademik. Penggunaan AI dalam pembelajaran dapat memberikan manfaat, tetapi juga menimbulkan berbagai persepsi yang perlu dikaji lebih lanjut. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui persepsi mahasiswa terhadap penggunaan AI dalam pembelajaran serta mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor yang mendasari persepsi tersebut. Penelitian dilakukan melalui penyebaran kuesioner yang terdiri atas 20 pernyataan kepada 76 responden. Data yang diperoleh dianalisis menggunakan Principal Component Analysis (PCA), dengan tahapan pengujian kelayakan data melalui Kaiser-Meyer Olkin (KMO) dan uji Bartlett, ekstraksi faktor, serta rotasi Varimax untuk memperoleh struktur faktor yang lebih mudah diinterpretasikan. Hasil pengujian awal menunjukkan nilai KMO sebesar 0,906 dan uji Bartlett yang signifikan dengan nilai p < 0,001, sehingga data memenuhi indikasi awal untuk dilakukan analisis faktor. Berdasarkan kriteria nilai eigen lebih dari satu, diperoleh tiga faktor awal yang selanjutnya dianalisis untuk mengetahui pengelompokan pernyataan berdasarkan korelasi antarvariabel. Penelitian ini diharapkan dapat memberikan gambaran mengenai dimensi-dimensi persepsi mahasiswa terhadap penggunaan AI dalam pembelajaran serta menjadi bahan pertimbangan dalam pemanfaatan AI secara efektif dan bertanggung jawab di lingkungan akademik.

papers.title: Current Status and Dilemmas of Artificial Intelligence Usage by Vocational College Teachers in Henan: Evidence From Henan Vocational and Technical College
papers.authors: Ruilin Wang, Ekapum Jiemwittayanukul, Kusuma Yamgate
papers.journal: Journal of Social Development and Management Strategy
papers.abstract: Background and Aim: Artificial intelligence fully empowers the digital transformation of vocational education. The AI literacy and teaching technology adoption level of vocational college teachers directly determine the quality of skills training. Existing domestic empirical studies mostly focus on eastern institutions, lacking micro-quantitative research on the micro-level of public vocational colleges in the central region. This study fills the gap in regional research, identifies the stratification characteristics of vocational college teachers' AI literacy, and quantitatively analyzes the multiple influencing factors that constrain teachers' adoption of AI teaching behaviors. This paper takes Henan Vocational and Technical College as the observation sample, combined with the practical cases of many colleges in Henan Province, and analyzes the real situation of vocational college teachers in AI application. This study aims to explore the cognitive level and current knowledge and skills status of vocational college teachers regarding artificial intelligence technology and analyze the key factors that affect their improvement of AI capabilities. Materials and Methods: This study adopted a mixed-methods research design combining questionnaire surveys and focus group interviews. First, to ensure the rigor of research data, participating teachers were selected across diverse majors, teaching years and genders. Henan Vocational and Technical College had a total teaching staff of 800 individuals. Using the Yamane sampling formula with a margin of error controlled within 5%, the calculated required sample size was 267 participants, and a total of 276 valid questionnaires were collected in practice. A self-designed Questionnaire on the Current Status and Dilemmas of Artificial Intelligence Application among Higher Vocational Teachers was adopted in this research. Both its content validity and reliability coefficients exceeded 0.85 after inspection. For the focus group, five participants were recruited, comprising three frontline teachers from the target college covering industrial and business majors, one expert in educational technology, and one specialist in AI educational application. Descriptive statistics including means and standard deviations as well as perceptual grading analysis were applied to analyze questionnaire data. Findings from the focus group discussions were further used to supplement and interpret the quantitative results of the questionnaire.

papers.title: Automated multimodal deception detection: a scoping review, taxonomy of fusion architectures, and research agenda
papers.authors: Aurélio Murta
papers.abstract: Scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) examining automated multimodal deception detection as a problem of multimodal information fusion: how heterogeneous, asynchronous, and uncertain signals captured by video/audio — facial expression/micro-expressions, voice/prosody, ocular behavior/pupillometry, remote photoplethysmography (rPPG), body/gesture, and verbal content — are fused by AI, including LLM/MLLM-based fusion (2025–26). The review maps the evidence and contributes (i) a taxonomy of multimodal deception signals by their role in the fusion architecture, (ii) the SINAPSE fusion framework (language model as a fuser with individual baseline and quantified uncertainty, never as a judge; reliability weighting and cross-modal consistency), and (iii) an agenda of open fusion challenges. Five research questions: (RQ1) which per-modality signals have replicated evidence of association with deception; (RQ2, central) which multimodal fusion architectures/strategies exist, at what level they fuse, their cross-domain generalization, and how (M)LLMs position themselves as fusers; (RQ3) datasets, stakes, and data gaps (rPPG+deception; Portuguese); (RQ4) uncertainty, individual baseline, calibration, and false-accusation bias in fusion; (RQ5) the cognitive-load construct and its critiques. Methods: PCC framework; dual-LLM title/abstract screening with human arbitration (GLM + DeepSeek, temperature 0, seed 42, versioned prompts); recall validation (≈0.95) against a human-curated reference set; full-text extraction and risk-of-bias assessment verified by three independent human reviewers; narrative synthesis (SWiM). Single principal reviewer (declared limitation). Transparency: literature collection (Sep 2026) and a first LLM screening pass preceded the protocol registration; the timeline is disclosed in the manuscript. Data, prompts, and PRISMA-ScR materials are in this project; the protocol is registered at OSF DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/Q7MXU.

papers.title: AI Adoption in B2B Markets: Exploring Drivers and Barriers through Behavioural Reasoning Theory and a Care Approach
papers.authors: Sogand Akbari Tari, Vahid Makizadeh
papers.journal: AI and Tech in Behavioral and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: This study investigates AI adoption in B2B marketing within Iranian steel industry by integrating Behavioral Reasoning Theory with a care approach. Specifically, it examines how care value, reasons for and against AI adoption, and attitude shape intention adoption, while also assessing the moderating role of brand reputation. A quantitative survey-based design was employed, and data were collected from 275 respondents working in the Iranian steel industry. The proposed model was tested using PLS-SEM, with moderation effects assessed through PROCESS Macro. The findings indicate that attitude is a strong predictor of AI intention adoption and serves as a key mechanism through which organizational reasons influence intention. The results further show that both enabling and inhibiting reasons of AI adoption. By extending BRT with care value in B2B context, this study contributes to the AI adoption literature and offers practical insights for firms seeking to implement AI responsibly and effectively.

papers.title: TRACING TECHNOLOGICAL TRANSFORMATION IN EDUCATION: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF SPECIAL EDUCATION AND VIRTUAL LABORATORIES
papers.authors: Ece Altay, Sıla BALIM
papers.journal: Turkish International Journal of Special Education and Guidance & Counselling (TIJSEG)
papers.abstract: This study examines the literature at the intersection of special education and virtual laboratories through bibliometric methods, identifying research trends in the emerging field. Growing interest has been observed between STEM/STEAM education and special education, with virtual laboratories serving as a bridge connecting these domains. A total of 1000 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection between 2000 and 2025 were analyzed, using the keywords "Special Education" and "Virtual Laboratory," with data visualized through VOSviewer software. The analyses covered four main categories: international collaboration, institutional collaboration, author collaboration, and keyword distribution. Findings show that China and the United States lead in publication output. While international collaboration networks exist among many countries, they remain concentrated in specific geographic regions and limited at the global scale. At the institutional level, Chinese universities such as Nanjing University and Beijing University stand out, showing high publication volumes. The author collaboration network reveals intensive scientific production among China-based researchers, though interdisciplinary collaboration remains limited. Keyword analysis highlights the predominance of virtual reality and experience-based learning environments, alongside growing interest in virtual laboratory applications for specific groups such as autism spectrum disorder and Williams syndrome/intellectual disability. The study concludes that the field continues to expand, but greater interdisciplinary collaboration and global knowledge exchange are needed, noting that integrating virtual laboratories with special education within STEM/STEAM remains a still-emerging area. All ethical rules were observed at each stage of the research. The authors declare that he acted in accordance with ethical rules in all processes of the research. papers.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence by Bangladeshi Doctors and Its Impact on Medical Learning, Research, and Clinical Practice: An Internet-Based Pilot Survey
papers.authors: Md Moktadirul Hoque Shuvo, Mastura Marzana Trisha
papers.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being incorporated into healthcare education, research, and clinical practice.However, data regarding AI utilization patterns among doctors in Bangladesh remain limited.This pilot survey aimed to evaluate the frequency, applications, perceived benefits, and concerns regarding AI use among Bangladeshi doctors. MethodologyA cross-sectional, internet-based pilot survey was conducted among Bangladeshi doctors.Participants were asked about demographic characteristics; frequency of AI use; preferred AI platforms; applications in medical learning, research, and clinical practice; and their perceptions regarding the future role of AI in medical science.Data from 58 respondents were analyzed using descriptive statistics. ResultsAmong 58 respondents, 51.7% were female, and 48.3% were male.Most participants belonged to the 25-34year age group (62.0%), and most were postgraduate trainees (72.4%).ChatGPT was the most frequently used AI platform, reported by 93.1% of respondents.AI was commonly used for literature review (62.1%), protocol writing (58.6%), and symptom analysis (60.3%).Most respondents reported that AI improved medical learning, research, and clinical practice.However, only a minority reported frequent AI dependence in clinical practice.Many doctors also believe AI may replace doctors in the future. ConclusionsAI adoption among Bangladeshi doctors is increasing, particularly for educational and research purposes.While doctors recognize the potential benefits of AI, cautious integration with appropriate training and ethical considerations is necessary.

papers.title: AI Driven Personalized Learning and Learning Analytics in Higher Education: Effects on Student Engagement, Achievement and Research Integrity
papers.authors: Nighat Yasmin, Javed Ali, Shazia Ejaz
papers.abstract: The study aimed to examine the effect of personalized learning through artificial intelligence (AI) and learning analytics on student engagement and learning outcomes of higher education institutes in Pakistan with implications for Research Integrity at these institutes. Adopting a mixed methods approach, quantitative data gathered from 500 students from an undergraduate science program, with semi structured interviews with 30 students for the qualitative data. The descriptive statistics indicated that the mean engagement scores for those students who have access to AI based personalized learnings were significantly higher than the mean scores of students in traditional learning setting; it is from these that an increase in engagement by the students were observed. There was an improvement in Academic achievement as well, as indicated by higher grade point averages, and improved scores of the formative assessments. The regression analysis results showed that AI (personalized learning) and learning analytics (β = .41; p < .001) were among its most important models that were significant in predicting the variable of academic achievement; the analysis of correlation results showed that there was a good positive correlation between the variables of engagement and academic achievement (r = .63, p < .01). The qualitative results corroborated this as students felt there was a significant increase in motivation, personalized feedback, and adaptive learning pathways as being the most beneficial aspects of the AI integration. Issues were identified that could interfere in successful implementation: Data privacy concerns, uneven access to technology and insufficient faculty preparation. According to this study, personalized learning & learning analytics with AI have proved to be significant drivers of student engagement & academic performance, provided that the ethical issues and infrastructure are sorted out and this may influence the way research integrity and rigor will be upheld within Higher Education Institutions. The findings herein expand the conversation taking place around the role of AI in education and highlight the need to embed learning analytics in a learning design practice, to create inclusive and effective learning spaces.

papers.title: Human vs. ChatGPT Translation: Comparative Analysis of Accuracy, Fluency, and Cultural Adaptation
papers.authors: Javid Babayev
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has significantly transformed translation practices, creating new opportunities and challenges for professional translators, researchers, and language learners. ChatGPT, as a generative artificial intelligence system, can produce translations that are grammatically correct, contextually appropriate, and stylistically coherent. However, its performance must be evaluated in relation to human translation, particularly regarding semantic accuracy, linguistic fluency, and cultural adaptation. This study aims to compare human and ChatGPT translation through a qualitative analytical framework focusing on these three dimensions. The research draws on established approaches to translation quality assessment, functional translation theory, and machine translation evaluation. It examines how human translators and ChatGPT may differ in interpreting contextual meaning, reproducing stylistic features, and transferring culture-specific expressions. The analysis suggests that ChatGPT can offer considerable advantages in speed, consistency, and the production of fluent target-language texts. Human translators, however, retain important advantages in culturally sensitive interpretation, pragmatic judgment, creative adaptation, and the resolution of complex contextual ambiguities. The study argues that translation quality cannot be measured exclusively through grammatical correctness or lexical equivalence. Instead, it requires an integrated assessment of meaning, communicative purpose, target-audience expectations, and cultural appropriateness. A complementary human–AI translation model is proposed as a practical approach to improving translation quality while maintaining human responsibility for the final text.

papers.title: Nutritional History and Risk Factors of Autistic Children in Selected Care Centers in Misurata
papers.authors: Maryem Elbashier Ismail
papers.abstract: Autism is a universal health challenge that transcends geographic, social, and ethnic boundaries. It is estimated that autism occurs in 1 to 2 per 1,000 individuals, while autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects approximately 6 per 1,000, with a male-to-female ratio of about 4:1. This research sought to evaluate the nutritional status of children with autism attending specific care facilities in Misurata. A cross-sectional investigation was conducted focusing on children with a confirmed ASD diagnosis at various specialized centers. The study included both preschool and school-aged participants. Information was gathered through a systematic questionnaire and interview of parents or caregivers in 2024. The collected data highlight significant anthropometric and nutritional issues among the participants (N = 107; consisting of 90 boys [84.1%] and 17 girls [15.9%]). The survey indicated that 92.2% of the children do not follow any specific therapeutic diet, 23.4% skip breakfast frequently, and 11.2% exhibit inconsistent food acceptance. While significant correlations (p≤0.05) were found between different anthropometric markers (such as BMI, weight, MUAC, height, and age), no significant link (p≥0.05) was found between gender and factors like dietary adherence, use of ketogenic diets, breakfast habits, birth weight, food pickiness, or digestive issues (including constipation, flatulence, and abdominal pain). The findings emphasize critical nutritional gaps for autistic children in Misurata, characterized by a lack of dietary structure, inconsistent eating patterns, and irregular use of supplements. To mitigate these issues, there is a need for specialized parental training, integrated professional support, and the implementation of formal nutritional guidelines.

papers.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in University History Teaching: An Analytical Study
papers.authors: دينا محمد جاسم عاجب
papers.abstract: This research discusses the employment of Artificial Intelligence in teaching university history as one of the modern trends imposed by digital transformation and technological developments in higher education institutions. The study aims to clarify the importance of applying Artificial Intelligence technologies in developing history teaching methods by improving interaction between students and the educational material, enhancing historical thinking and analytical skills, and facilitating access to digital historical resources and information

papers.title: Machine Learning in Teaching Piano Touch Technique and Tonal Expression
papers.authors: Da Li, Jing Zhou, Qiyan Tan
papers.journal: Archives des sciences a multidisciplinary journal
papers.abstract: Music is an art involving both sound and hearing, and it is experienced through a combination of musical performance and attentive listening. Among the many musical instruments, the piano is often called the “king of instruments.” Unlike the violin, which is frequently described as delicate and soft, the piano possesses a tone that may be perceived as noble and graceful. A statement attributed to the pianist Nergoz emphasizes that the purpose of piano playing is to make sound and to create sound. This observation draws attention to the central importance of sound production in piano education, although the attribution needs confirmation from an identifiable original source. How, then, can a pianist use the instrument to produce a beautiful sound? This remains an essential concern for piano players at different levels of study and performance. Therefore, tonal quality deserves consistent attention during both technical practice and musical performance, because the fingers must engage with the keys to produce each intended sound. Tone plays an important role throughout the entire process of piano performance. Both the expressiveness of piano playing and its appeal to listeners are closely associated with the quality of the resulting tone. The area of key contact, the intensity of the touch, and the technique employed all have an important influence on the resulting sound. A systematic approach to finger touch is consequently an important skill and a valuable technical consideration, both when learning to play the piano and when performing musical compositions.

papers.title: Learning Skill Representations from Recruitment Data for Skill Gap Analysis and Career Path Optimization
papers.authors: Peng Cheng
papers.journal: Archives des sciences a multidisciplinary journal
papers.abstract: To address the mismatch between educational provision and labor-market demand affecting the employment of arts graduates, this paper proposes a skill-gap analysis framework integrating recruitment-text mining, semantic representation learning, and knowledge graphs. First, a corpus of job advertisements is compiled from online recruitment data, and a Transformer-based model is used to encode job descriptions semantically, enabling the extraction of skill entities and the development of context-sensitive representations. Second, semantic skill embeddings, hierarchical clustering, and BERTopic-based topic modeling are combined to construct a skill-classification system for arts-related positions, with the aim of identifying core skill groups and emerging competency requirements in the employment market. Furthermore, the proposed framework maps job positions, skill requirements, and students’ existing abilities into a shared semantic space and uses knowledge graphs to characterize structural relationships among jobs, skills, and competencies. On this basis, distributions representing market demand and educational skill supply are constructed and compared to quantify gaps affecting arts graduates. The reported experimental findings suggest that requirements for arts-related positions increasingly combine conventional professional expertise with digital technology, AI-assisted creative practices, data literacy, and transferable professional competencies. The results also identify apparent shortcomings in university preparation concerning computing skills, problem-solving, project implementation, and adaptability across disciplinary boundaries. Together, these analyses offer a structured basis for interpreting skill mismatches and informing curriculum development, individualized upskilling, and career planning.

papers.title: Generative AI dependence and decision-making independence in digital society: Evidence from Universitas Airlangga
papers.authors: Safa Naura Mawla Sakti, Boy Junior De Gier, Amaliyah Amaliyah, Erindah Dimisyqiyani, Gagas Gayuh Aji, Rizky Amalia Sinulingga
papers.journal: Societa Journal of Society and Change
papers.abstract: Dependence on generative artificial intelligence (AI) raises questions about students’ ability to maintain independence in decision-making. This study aims to examine the relationship between generative AI dependence and decision-making independence among active students at Universitas Airlangga. A quantitative correlational design was employed with 65 students selected through purposive sampling, using a Likert-scale questionnaire and Pearson correlation analysis. The results revealed a very weak, positive, and statistically nonsignificant relationship between the two variables (r = 0.103; p = 0.416). This finding indicates that generative AI dependence was not significantly associated with decision-making independence in the study sample. The study contributes to research on AI use in higher education by highlighting the importance of distinguishing technological dependence from students’ capacity to make independent decisions. Abstrak Ketergantungan terhadap artificial intelligence (AI) generatif menimbulkan pertanyaan mengenai kemampuan mahasiswa mempertahankan kemandirian dalam pengambilan keputusan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan antara ketergantungan terhadap AI generatif dan kemandirian pengambilan keputusan pada mahasiswa aktif Universitas Airlangga. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif korelasional dengan melibatkan 65 mahasiswa yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling, menggunakan kuesioner skala Likert dan analisis korelasi Pearson. Hasil menunjukkan hubungan positif yang sangat lemah dan tidak signifikan antara kedua variabel (r = 0.103; p = 0.416). Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa ketergantungan terhadap AI generatif tidak terbukti berhubungan secara signifikan dengan kemandirian pengambilan keputusan pada sampel penelitian. Penelitian ini berkontribusi pada kajian penggunaan AI di pendidikan tinggi dengan menekankan pentingnya membedakan ketergantungan teknologi dari kemampuan mahasiswa mengambil keputusan secara mandiri.

papers.title: Corporate Governance Practices in Ai-Powered Technologies: A Perspective of Engineering Students
papers.authors: Stephanie Grace V. Cortes
papers.journal: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into educational, professional, and technological environments, creating opportunities for innovation while raising concerns regarding transparency, accountability, ethical responsibility, privacy, and governance. Despite the growing use of AI-powered technologies among university students, limited research has examined how engineering students perceive corporate governance practices associated with these technologies. This study explored the perceptions of undergraduate engineering students regarding corporate governance in AI-powered technologies. A descriptive quantitative research design employing a cross-sectional survey approach was utilized. Data were collected from ninety-two (92) undergraduate engineering students at Cebu Institute of Technology–University (CIT-University) using a structured questionnaire. Frequency counts, percentages, weighted means, and ranking procedures were used to analyze the data. The findings revealed that respondents demonstrated positive awareness of corporate governance principles in AI systems, particularly regarding ethical responsibility, accountability, transparency, and data governance. The respondents also expressed a generally favorable level of trust in organizations utilizing AI-powered technologies, although concerns regarding privacy protection, data security, and responsible AI implementation remained evident. Among the governance dimensions examined, accountability received the highest rating, followed by ethical governance and transparency. Furthermore, the results showed that engineering students generally practiced responsible AI use, particularly in avoiding technologies that violate ethical and privacy standards. Large Language Models (LLMs), such as Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude, were identified as the most commonly used AI-powered technologies among the respondents. The study concludes that engineering students recognize the importance of responsible AI governance and view accountability, ethical responsibility, and transparency as essential components of trustworthy AI systems. These findings may contribute to the development of governance policies, educational initiatives, and responsible AI practices within academic and technological environments.

papers.title: IMPACT OF AI ON THE HEALTH AND BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES OF YOUNGER GENERATION
papers.authors: Dr. D. Aruna, Angela Blessi S, Mahalakshmi A, Rupa Shree N L
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a significant part of the daily lives of the younger generation, influencing their education, and decision-making. Although AI provides several advantages, such as easy access to information, enhanced learning opportunities, and improved productivity, excessive use of AI may result in health problems and behavioural changes. Both primary and secondary data were used for the research purpose. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire, and responses of 100 has been considered. Secondary data were collected from journals and previously published research articles. Data were analysed using SPSS software. The study concludes that AI has a significant impact on the health and behavioural changes of the younger generation. Excessive AI usage has reduced face-to-face social interactions, increased dependency on AI, and contributed to physical health issues such as eye strain, tiredness, and reduced physical activity. Therefore, responsible and balanced use of AI is essential to promote the overall well-being of the younger generation.

papers.title: ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN INVESTMENT DECISIONS
papers.authors: Shakthipriya R V, Dr. D. Sumathi
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: Investment behaviour has changed as a result of artificial intelligence (AI), which replaces human judgment with data-driven insights. Investors may analyse big information, spot trends, and optimize portfolios with the help of technologies like machine learning, robo-advisors, and predictive analytics, increasing productivity and lowering emotional biases. Adoption of AI is not without its difficulties, though, such as algorithmic bias, a lack of transparency, expensive costs, and problems with data quality. Automation bias and market volatility may increase if automated systems are overused. This study highlights AI’s impact on investor behaviour and emphasizes the importance of a balanced, responsible approach to effectively integrate AI into investment decision-making processes.

papers.title: PUBLIC PERCEPTION AND TRUST IN AI FOR FRAUD DETECTION AND INFLUENCER AUTHENTICITY IN INFLUENCER MARKETING
papers.authors: Ms.B.Akshaya, Dr.Sambamurthy Padmavathi
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of influencer marketing has created diverse opportunities for the brands to interact with the consumers. At the same time, concerns regarding manipulated follower counts, artificial engagement and questionable influencer authenticity have become increasingly relevant. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is used as a technological mechanism for finding skeptical patterns and supporting fraud detection. However, the use and acceptance of these systems are largely influenced by consumers’ perceptions and trust. The present study focuses trust and concerns of consumers regarding AI-driven fraud detection and consumer attitudes towards transparency, AI-based verification and measures intended to strengthen authenticity in influencer marketing. The study adopts a descriptive research design and uses primary data collected from 70 respondents through a structured questionnaire. The findings show that respondents demonstrate cautious acceptance of AI-driven fraud detection. Half of the respondents reported that they somewhat trust AI, whereas complete trust was comparatively limited. Concerns relating to transparency, privacy, false identification and possible bias were also identified. The findings further reveal that consumers attach considerable importance to transparency and generally support AI-based verification systems. Respondents also expressed favourable opinions regarding the use of AI tools by brands while evaluating influencers for collaboration. The study concludes that AI can contribute to improving authenticity in influencer marketing, but its acceptance depends on the development of transparent, reliable and accountable systems.

papers.title: AI ADOPTION AMONG WOMEN ENTREPRENEURS IN E-COMMERCE BUSINESS
papers.authors: Ms.D.Vinithra, Dr.G.K.Lavanya

papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutioning e-commerce business by providing automatic operation, improving customer engagement, market efficiency and data driven decision making.AI tools such as chatbots,personalised recommended engine ,demand forecasting systems have improved efficiency and enhanced customer experience.The study addresses the gap by exploring women entrepreneurs awareness level of AI tools and their purpose of using, satisfaction level,adoption challenges and the result impact on sales and profitability in e-commerce business. According to the findings of the study,majority of the women entrepreneurs are selling apparels, fashion and textiles and using AI tools to increase sales and revenue.Women entrepreneurs uses AI tools for customer engagement and content creation like chatgpt,claude in the ecommerce business.

papers.title: CAN ARTIFICIAL INFLUENCERS BE AUTHENTIC? THE ROLE OF AI DISCLOSURE IN THE AUTHENTICITY–TRUST–PURCHASE INTENTION PARADOX IN SOCIAL COMMERCE
papers.authors: Mr. Mohammed Saadh, Dr. Shriram K Ms. Swetha L
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in social media has introduced Artificial Influencers as a new form of digitally constructed endorser, challenging conventional assumptions about authenticity, trust, and consumer behaviour. Unlike human influencers, Artificial Influencers are technologically created personas whose appearance, personality, communication, and interactions can be deliberately designed and controlled. This raises an important question: Can consumers perceive an Artificial Influencer as authentic when they are aware of its artificial nature? The present study examines the role of AI disclosure in shaping perceived authenticity and explores how authenticity relates to consumer trust and purchase intention in the context of social commerce. The study specifically addresses an emerging authenticity–trust–purchase intention paradox, whereby consumers may recognise an influencer as artificial, perceive limitations in its authenticity, and nevertheless remain willing to trust its recommendations or consider purchasing promoted products. A quantitative, exploratory, and cross-sectional research design was adopted. Primary data were collected through a structured online questionnaire from 30 social-media users using non-probability convenience sampling. The questionnaire examined respondents’ social-media exposure, awareness of Artificial Influencers, perceptions of AI disclosure, perceived authenticity, consumer trust, and purchase intention. Frequency and percentage analysis were used to describe response patterns, while Spearman’s rank-order correlation was employed to examine associations among the principal constructs. Given the small sample size, the study is positioned as an exploratory investigation and does not seek to establish population-level generalisation or definitive causal relationships. The findings indicate that AI disclosure has a dual significance in consumer evaluation. While 73.3% of respondents supported AI disclosure always or in most cases, disclosure was also associated with increased scrutiny of recommendations and greater concerns regarding genuineness. At the same time, 73.3% of respondents indicated that an Artificial Influencer could be perceived as authentic under certain circumstances, particularly when communication was relatable and consistent. However, 70.0% reported that awareness of AI generation reduced their perception of authenticity to some degree. Consumer trust appeared to be conditional rather than automatic, with respondents emphasising transparency, credibility, consistency, product relevance, and information verification. Purchase intention was similarly cautious, with respondents indicating that willingness to purchase depended on the product and the credibility of the recommendation. The study concludes that artificiality and authenticity should not be treated as mutually exclusive concepts. Consumers may simultaneously recognise the technological construction of an Artificial Influencer, experience reduced perceptions of genuineness, and still regard the influencer as sufficiently credible to support trust and purchase consideration. The findings therefore provide preliminary support for the authenticity–trust–purchase intention paradox and suggest that AI disclosure functions not simply as a mechanism that reduces authenticity, but as a transparency cue that can coexist with scepticism. The study contributes to the emerging literature on AI-mediated influencer marketing by integrating AI disclosure, perceived authenticity, consumer trust, and purchase intention within a single exploratory framework. For marketers, the findings highlight the importance of transparent disclosure, credible and verifiable product information, consistent communication, and responsible consumer engagement when deploying Artificial Influencers in social commerce.

papers.title: Modeling Paralinguistic Features for Speech Neuroprostheses: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Manu Siddharth Yenikapati, Soham Deshpande, Shiv Prashant Desai, Donovan D Santine, Aryan Kia Roghani
papers.abstract: Abstract Recent advances in brain-computer interface (BCI) technology have brought speech neuroprostheses closer to restoring naturalistic communication for individuals with severe motor or speech impairments. Although current systems can decode phonemic and lexical information from cortical activity, they often fail to capture paralinguistic dimensions such as intonation, prosody, loudness, and affect that are essential for conveying emotion and intent. This review synthesizes emerging research on modeling and incorporating paralinguistic features into speech neuroprosthetic design. Foundational studies have mapped the cortical organization of speech production, identifying articulatory somatotopy within the sensorimotor cortex and functional subdivisions across planning, phonological, and semantic representations. More recent work has characterized expressive encoding within the ventral precentral and supplementary motor areas, while peripheral and multimodal sensing approaches have demonstrated promising accuracy in decoding emotional states. Collectively, these findings signal a shift toward closed-loop neuroprosthetic systems that integrate affective modulation with linguistic decoding, enabling restoration of speech that is not only intelligible but expressively human.

papers.title: Analysis of the Use of ChatGPT and DeepSeek in Solving HOTS Physics Problems in Kinematics Teaching Material
papers.authors: Nadya Aidilla Fitri Tanjung, Sahyar Sahyar
papers.journal: International Journal of Education Vocational and Social Science
papers.abstract: This study analyzes the ability of ChatGPT 5.1 and DeepSeek V3 to solve Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) problems in kinematics, in terms of answer accuracy and response consistency. A descriptive qualitative design with a desk-research approach was used. The sample consisted of 20 expert-validated HOTS items at cognitive levels C4 (analyzing) and C5 (evaluating), ten text-based and ten image-based. Accuracy was scored in binary form against three criteria: correctness of the final answer, conceptual understanding, and correct use of equations. Consistency was assessed by posing every item 30 times, each in a new conversation. On text-based items, both chatbots reached 80% accuracy (Good), with average consistency of 89% for ChatGPT and 91% for DeepSeek (both Very Good). On image-based items, ChatGPT achieved 100% accuracy and 100% consistency (Very Good), whereas DeepSeek achieved 60% accuracy and 73.7% consistency (Fairly Good). C5 items were the hardest for both chatbots, and DeepSeek’s errors on image-based items came mainly from misreading graphs rather than from wrong formulas. Chatbot output should therefore be verified by teachers and students before it is used as a learning aid in physics.

papers.title: The Impact of Using AI as an Alternative Solution Search: Reconstructing the Ontology of 'Thinking Humans' in Islamic Education
papers.authors: Nissa Bela Nurussalma, Mahfud Junaedi, Darmuin Darmuin, Aabidah Ummu 'Aziizah
papers.journal: International Journal of Education Vocational and Social Science
papers.abstract: The use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a primary reference for finding solutions is changing how people think and raises ontological questions for Islamic education. This study analyzes the impact of using AI as an alternative for finding solutions on thinking practices, reconstructs the ontology of the "thinking human" within an Islamic education framework, and formulates its implications for educational practice. The study employs a qualitative approach with a library research design. Data were gathered through documentation of primary and secondary sources and analyzed using thematic analysis and conceptual framework analysis. The review shows that AI use is associated with cognitive offloading, the risk of an illusion of competence, and challenges to integrity and ethics, while the Islamic education literature points to a tension between AI-driven personalization and the scholarly authority of teachers. The reconstruction is formulated along five dimensions: the nature of thinking, the position of the human being, responsibility, scholarly authority, and the role of AI. The human being is affirmed as a knowledge-seeking subject accountable for their knowledge, while AI is positioned as an auxiliary tool whose outputs must be verified. The study proposes adab-based AI literacy as an operational pathway for this reconstruction. As the findings are conceptual, they require empirical testing in Islamic educational institutions.

papers.title: Mapping University Students Risk of Dependence on Generative Artificial Intelligence Using K-Means Clustering
papers.authors: Hafiz Fadhillah, Taufiq Taufiq
papers.journal: Global Advances in Science Engineering & Technology (GASET)
papers.abstract: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has changed how university students approach academic tasks. Although these tools can support learning and improve efficiency, frequent reliance on them raises concerns about students' ability to study and solve problems independently. This study aims to identify patterns of GenAI use among university students and explore potential indicators of dependence through K-Means clustering. An exploratory quantitative approach was adopted, using questionnaire responses collected through 15 items measured on a five-point Likert scale. Of the 106 responses received, 104 met the inclusion criteria and were retained for analysis. The data underwent screening, numerical encoding, and reverse scoring before being grouped using the K-Means algorithm. The appropriate number of clusters was selected by comparing Silhouette Scores across solutions containing two to seven clusters. The analysis identified three student groups, with a Silhouette Score of 0.2443. The first group comprised 30 students (28.85%) who showed relatively higher GenAI use and stronger indications of behavioral dependence. The second group included 11 students (10.58%) who reported lower GenAI use but demonstrated limitations in academic independence and understanding. The remaining 63 students (60.58%) formed a group characterized by moderate GenAI use. These findings suggest that frequency of use alone does not adequately reflect the risk of dependence. However, the relatively low Silhouette Score indicates limited separation between groups, meaning that the resulting profiles should be interpreted as exploratory rather than definitive.

papers.title: ALGORITHMIC INCLUSION: A DUAL-SOFTWARE ANALYSIS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION AMONG SPECIAL EDUCATION TEACHERS IN JORDAN
papers.authors: Ayed Mohammad Ahmad Melhem
papers.abstract: This study is conducted to explore SE teachers' integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Irbid Governorate, Jordan and to understand the conditions impacting on this integration. The type behaved in the design of this research is cross sectional descriptive analytic type with respondents in this study being teachers who were touched by stratified random sampling techniques by a population of 144 teachers of the 197 teachers. Data collected was backed up with SmartPLS4 and Rstudio with a 30-item questionnaire. The overall integration of AI is mostly high (M = 3.71, SD = 0.48) with variance in integration of different applications in education. Performance Expectancy was the most noteworthy predictor of Behavioral Intention (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), followed by Facilitating Conditions (β = 0.312, p < 0.001) and Effort Expectancy (β = 0.185, p = 0.016), accounting for 58% of the variance in Behavioral Intention. There was no significant difference between the genders but teachers who have less experience in school report significantly higher incorporation. But there were also significant differences between disability groups. The results inform purposeful professional development, robust infrastructure, disability-sensitive implementation, and human-centered ethical governance for sustainable and equitable method within education.

papers.title: IS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE REDEFINING EDUCATIONAL LEADERSHIP? A TWENTY-YEAR BIBLIOMETRIC PERSPECTIVE
papers.authors: Resky Nuralisa Gunawan, Muhammad Imran Nur, Malik Salim, Lamanisa Rasid Saputra, Ummi Salamah Tianotak, Bonita Padang, Muhammad Taufiq Firdaus, Nur Kholis
papers.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on artificial intelligence (AI) in educational leadership, aiming to map key trends, identify leading contributors, and highlight thematic priorities in the field. A total of 323 Scopus-indexed and 842 Web of Science peer-reviewed publications published between 2004 and 2024 were analysed to provide an overview of the field’s evolution over two decades. Using R-based bibliometric analysis and VOSviewer, the study examines citation patterns, co-authorship networks, journal productivity, and keyword co-occurrence. The findings indicate a substantial growth in research output since 2015, aligning with global digitalisation and increased AI adoption in education. Prominent contributors include Mohammed Eunus Ali and Dragan Gasevic, while Cogent Education and Sustainability (Switzerland) emerge as leading publication outlets. The results also highlight the interdisciplinary nature of AI research in educational leadership. Thematic mapping reveals dominant themes such as artificial intelligence, leadership, and learning, alongside emerging topics including ethical integration, educator well-being, and AI-supported decision-making. This study advances existing scholarship by clarifying the intellectual structure of the field and outlining directions for future research and practice.

papers.title: AUTHENTIC ASSESSMENT AND CRITICAL THINKING IN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: AN EXPLANATORY MODEL
papers.authors: Patricia del Carmen Arellano Gualle, Luis Alberto Flores Rodriguez, Jorge Armando Acosta Villarraga, Alex Segundo García Crisanto, Luis Angel Vega Palomino, Alexander Pacaya Taminche
papers.abstract: The advent of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is disrupting traditional thinking about assessment in universities, as it is possible that final written products will not be the only indicator of students' independent thinking. This study investigated the relationship between participation in an authentic assessment process and the use of information problem solving with a critical thinking approach in a task carried out in the university by using the GenAI. The publicly available GenAI-Assisted Information Problem Solving dataset was used to extract secondary data for analysis, which included GenAI dialogue, writing-process activity, annotations, student background characteristics and tutor-assigned proposal scores [6]. There were 230 complete cases used in the multivariable regression and moderation analysis. The relationship between authentic-assessment engagement and critical-thinking-oriented GenAI dialogue was positive (β = 0.174, p = 0.004), and the relationship between evaluative GenAI engagement and authentic-assessment engagement was positive, but stronger (β = 0.379, p < 0.001). Authentic-assessment engagement and evaluative GenAI engagement, however, did not have a statistically significant interaction (β = −0.102, p = 0.110). Process indicators also failed to significantly predict final proposal scores, with 3.8% of the variance in the model of proposal performance explained by the process indicators. The results indicate that authentic assessment can help to set the stage for more evaluative and revision-driven interactions with GenAI, and more process-level critical thinking does not necessarily lead to higher assessment scores. The study underscores the need to separate out the amount of AI use from the quality of the AI use and to include process evidence in the design of assessments in the GenAI era.

papers.title: AI-ENABLED HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABLE ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE: THE SEQUENTIAL ROLES OF AI-SUPPORTIVE ORGANIZATIONAL CLIMATE AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT
papers.authors: Dr. B. Deepa, Dr.M.Farzana Begum, Dr. M. Gayathri, Dr. P. Thangamani, Dr. M. Radhakrishnan, Dr. P. Arivazhagan
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming Human Resource Management (HRM) from a predominantly administrative function into an increasingly predictive, data-driven and strategically oriented organizational capability. Although organizations are adopting AI for recruitment, performance management, employee development, rewards and workforce analytics, technological adoption alone does not necessarily translate into sustainable organizational performance. Existing studies have established important relationships among AI-enabled HRM, employee engagement and organizational outcomes; however, the organizational mechanisms through which different AI-enabled HR practices are translated into sustainable performance remain insufficiently integrated. This conceptual paper develops a multidimensional framework linking five AI-enabled HRM practices—AI-enabled talent acquisition, AI-enabled performance management, AI-enabled learning and development, AI-enabled rewards and recognition, and predictive workforce analytics—with sustainable organizational performance through AI-Supportive Organizational Climate and employee engagement. Drawing upon the Resource-Based View, Ability–Motivation–Opportunity framework and Socio-Technical Systems Theory, the paper proposes that AI-Supportive Organizational Climate constitutes an organizational mechanism through which technological HR capabilities are converted into positive employee experiences, while employee engagement represents the behavioural mechanism connecting this supportive environment with sustainable organizational outcomes. The framework further recognizes responsible AI principles including transparency, fairness, explainability, privacy, accountability and meaningful human oversight as important implementation conditions. By integrating technological capability, organizational Climate, employee behavior and strategic performance, the study contributes a testable sequential framework for future empirical research. The model also provides practical guidance for managers seeking to move beyond AI adoption toward responsible, human-centred and sustainable AI-enabled HRM.

papers.title: CRITICAL THINKING IN AI-SUPPORTED EFL WRITING: A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL MIXED-METHODS STUDY
papers.authors: Dr. Mahdi R. Aben Ahmed
papers.abstract: English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing classrooms are increasingly adopting generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, which provide additional scaffolding but also raise important questions about their impact on learners' critical thinking. Applying a quasi-experimental mixed-methods design, this study compared the writing performance and critical thinking of 94 undergraduate EFL learners who were assigned in equal numbers to an AI-supported instruction group (n = 47) and a teacher-mediated instruction group (n = 47). The 12-week intervention was guided by Paul and Elder’s Critical Thinking Framework for teaching, learning, and assessment. Data collection instruments included pre- and post-intervention writing tests, a critical thinking rubric, reflective journals, AI interaction logs, and semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests and one-way ANOVAs, with Cohen’s d used to estimate effect sizes; qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The results showed that the AI-supported group scored significantly higher than the teacher-mediated group on the post-intervention writing task, t(92) = 2.97, p = .004, and completed the task significantly faster, t(92) = 8.23, p < .001. Although both groups improved their writing performance over the intervention period, the within-group gain was larger in the AI-supported group (d = 2.12) than in the teacher-mediated group (d = 1.32). However, post-test critical thinking scores did not differ significantly between groups, t(92) = 0.69, p = .49. Thematic analysis further showed that, over the course of the semester, learners shifted from passively accepting AI suggestions to critically evaluating AI-generated content. Overall, the results indicate that AI-mediated instruction improved writing quality and efficiency without any evidence of a detrimental effect on learners’ critical thinking; instead, learners increasingly evaluated AI-generated content critically before incorporating it into their writing.

papers.title: CRITICAL THINKING IN AI-SUPPORTED EFL WRITING: A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL MIXED-METHODS STUDY
papers.authors: Dr. Mahdi R. Aben Ahmed
papers.abstract: English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing classrooms are increasingly adopting generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, which provide additional scaffolding but also raise important questions about their impact on learners' critical thinking.
