papers.title: DEEPFAKES AND AI MISUSE: THE NEXT CHALLENGE FOR INDIAN CYBER LAW
papers.authors: Japan Babu, Vikalp Shrivastava
papers.abstract: Deepfakes and AI-facilitated artificial media have become extremely hard to the Indian cyber law, which implies privacy, identity, reputation, financial stability, evidence reliability, and trust of the population. This paper discusses the technology underpinning and key types of deepfake abuse, the suitability of the current legal system in India, and the judicial and regulatory events of recent years. It takes into account the Information Technology Act, 2000, the rules of intermediary liability, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, data-protection law, personality rights and constitutional protections. Regulatory approaches in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as China, are also compared in the study. It draws persistent attributional, platform responsibility, and victim remedies, and digital evidence authentication gaps, and presents a coordinated regulation paradigm of prevention, disclosure, provenance, takedown, remedies, forensic capacity and institutional oversight of the digital ecosystem of India.

papers.title: AI AS A CHOICE ARCHITECT: ETHICAL IMPLICATIONS OF ALGORITHMIC NUDGING IN ONLINE RETAIL
papers.authors: Varshini Shree, Sai Lakshmi Sai Prasad, Akanksha Aggarwal
papers.abstract: Nudge Theory, introduced by Thaler and Sunstein in their seminal book, inspired the creation of human choice architects who applied behavioural insights into influence decisions across various domains. In the online retail industry, however, the evolution of Artificial Intelligence, predictive analytics, and real time data personalization has transformed traditional nudging into algorithmic choice architecture powered by data-driven insights. This paper conceptually examines how AI driven Algorithmic nudges operate through cross- platform behavioural tracking, recommender systems, push notifications, and default designs to influence consumer decisions. The epistemological orientation of this paper is grounded in qualitative and interpretative approach based on critical realism to explore how consumers conform to stacked and multichannel nudges(multiple, sequential interventions across apps, websites and social platforms) that leverage cognitive biases and bounded rationality. Findings suggest that AI enabled nudges outperform human- designed ones in precision, scalability, and contextual adaptability, allowing retailers to subtly guide consumer behaviour under the guise of personalisation. However, the opacity of these algorithmic mechanisms raises serious ethical questions regarding informed consent, privacy, and autonomy, especially for vulnerable consumer groups. The study underscores the need for transparent AI governance, ethical design principles, and regulatory frameworks to prevent behavioural manipulation in digital marketplaces. It further argues that the evolution from libertarian paternalism to algorithmic paternalism represents a critical shift that challenges the foundational ethics of Nudge Theory and calls for cross-disciplinary collaboration between marketing, technology, human- computer interaction and law to ensure responsible AI-driven persuasion in online retail.

papers.title: BUSINESS MODEL INNOVATION IN NURSE-LED CLINICS AND ITS IMPACT ON PATIENT SATISFACTION AND ENGAGEMENT: EVIDENCE FROM A SAUDI HEALTHCARE CONTEXT
papers.authors: Mashael Huwaydi F.  Aldhafeeri, Hafizah Che Hassan, Faridah Mohd Said
papers.abstract: Background: Background: Business model innovation (BMI) in nurse-led clinics has been recognized as a revolutionary approach in the delivery of healthcare, especially in public hospital settings that are resource-intensive. Objective: The aim of this research is to explore the impact of innovative nursing business models, which are characterized by restructuring of leadership, redesign of care processes, and patient engagement approaches, on patient satisfaction and engagement outcomes in public hospitals in Saudi Arabia. Methods: A cross-sectional survey design was employed with 150 nurses and 180 patients from four major public hospitals in the Riyadh region. Leadership styles were assessed using the Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ), and patient satisfaction was measured using the Patient Satisfaction with Nursing Care Quality Questionnaire (PSNCQQ). Results: Passive-avoidant (PA) leadership was the most prevalent style (62.6%, n = 94) and was associated with the lowest patient satisfaction scores (m = 1.7, SD = 0.1). Transactional leadership demonstrated the highest patient satisfaction (m = 2.7). ANOVA revealed statistically significant differences among leadership styles (F [3, 176] = 25.421, P < .001). Conclusion: BMI via targeted leadership transformation from passive-avoidant to transactional or transformational leadership styles can greatly enhance patient satisfaction and engagement. The results of this study have important implications for healthcare administrators and policymakers in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.

papers.title: WORKFORCE TRANSFORMATION IN MANUFACTURING INDUSTRIES: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AUTOMATION, RESKILLING, UPSKILLING AND SOFT SKILLS
papers.authors: Rupali Gupta, Madhavi Deshpande
papers.abstract: The employment of new technologies like Artificial Intelligence (AI) along with robotics, intelligent automation and digital manufacturing are changing the nature of work and workforce capabilities in manufacturing industries. While previous studies have put a lot of focus on technological adoption and on Industry 4.0, comparatively less empirical attention has been paid to the organizational and human-capability mechanisms through which technological transformation leads to the transformation of the workforce. This study creates and integrated framework to investigate the relationships between AI Adoption, Automation Intensity, Reskilling, Upskilling, Soft Skills and Transformation of Workforce in Manufacturing Industries. Based on socio-technical systems theory, resource-based view and automation–augmentation perspective, workforce transformation is conceived as a multifaceted process that includes job redesign, changing competency requirements, human–technology collaboration and shift to higher-value work. The framework in question has been examined using data collected from surveys of 550 respondents sampled from the manufacturing sector using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling(PLS-SEM). The findings show that both AI adoption (β = 0.272, p < 0.001) and automation intensity (β = 0.220, p < 0.001) are positively associated with workforce transformation. Both reskilling (β = 0.289, p < 0.001) and upskilling (β = 0.311, p < 0.001) are positively connected to the workforce transformation. The interaction effect of soft skills is also significant β = 0.060, p = 0.004. This means that the relationship between was very condition by soft skills, and developing a capable workforce. The variance in workforce transformation, valued at R2 is 0.845, is explained by the structural model. As per the findings, the manufacturing workforce transformation is not only about technology but also human capabilities development and integration needed for ideal human-technology collaboration. This research integrates the technological, organizational and human-capability dimensions of a firm in an empirical framework to develop Industry 5.0.

papers.title: WHEN AI LITERACIES EMBRACE ACADEMIC LITERACIES: WHO IS HOLDING THE PEN? A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF ACADEMIC WRITING IN HIGHER EDUCATION
papers.authors: Sivabala Naidu, Nirumala Rothinam, Ramachandran Vengrasalam, Samikkanu Jabamoney, Ranjit Singh Gill, Andrew L. S. Foong, Ruban Paul Durai
papers.abstract: Academic writing is central to learning, assessment, scholarly identity, and knowledge production in higher education. This study integrates a systematic review of 35 empirical studies with a VOSviewer bibliometric analysis of 981 Scopus-indexed records published between 1992 and 2026. The broad corpus was analysed for publication growth, source productivity, citation influence, co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic development. A focused PRISMA 2020 screening process retained 35 empirical studies for structured data extraction and qualitative synthesis. The bibliometric findings show a sharp acceleration after 2023 and a conceptual shift from established academic-literacies, EAP, feedback, and doctoral-writing research towards generative artificial intelligence, ChatGPT, authorship, and academic integrity. The systematic review identified three linked evidence domains: persistent academic-literacy and transition challenges, the value of explicit and socially supported writing pedagogy, and the conditional benefits and risks of AI-assisted writing. GenAI was most productive when students used it iteratively for feedback, transformation, and self-regulated development rather than as a substitute for reasoning or authorship. Across the literature, recurring limitations included cross-sectional self-report designs, small qualitative samples, limited longitudinal evidence, and uneven geographic coverage. The review concludes that academic writing competence should be reconceptualised as a sociotechnical capability combining disciplinary judgement, source evaluation, rhetorical control, ethical disclosure, and critical human-AI collaboration.

papers.title: MACHINE LEARNING PREDICTION OF SETTLEMENT-DEPENDENT LOAD SHARING IN COMBINED PILED-RAFT FOUNDATIONS
papers.authors: Gopalakrishnan N, H C Muddaraju, Chethan K
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous published experiments on combined piled-raft foundations (CPRFs) create risks of semantic inconsistency, pseudo-replication and misleading machine-learning validation. This study develops an evidence-controlled framework for settlement-dependent pile load-sharing ratio (α) and tests whether nonlinear learners improve prediction when experimental grouping is preserved. Ten complete ATE22/PRI24 curves define the absolute-level model, while four lineages inform settlement shape. Under leave-one-curve-out validation, linear/ridge regression achieved RMSE ≈ 0.059, outperforming Gradient Boosting (0.067), Random Forest (0.081) and RBF-SVR (0.111). Study-held-out transfer remained asymmetric, evidencing domain dependence. Grouped feature ablation identified L/B as the dominant incremental predictor; out-of-fold SHAP provided consistent supporting evidence while secondary rankings varied by study. The results show that provenance control, grouped validation and restrained explainability can matter more than algorithmic complexity in small, clustered engineering datasets.

papers.title: MANAGEMENT AND PREPAREDNESS OF NURSING FACULTY FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN NURSING EDUCATION: A META-ANALYSIS
papers.authors: Amos Poulas  Talsandekar, Sunanda P Kale, Priyanka S. Patil, ABHINANDAN RAVSAHEB PATIL
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare and nursing education, but there is fragmented evidence about nursing faculty's readiness to teach with and about AI. This is a narrative review that compiled evidence retrieved from the internet (October 2026) about the knowledge, skills, attitudes and ethical awareness of nursing and health-sciences faculty, and their preparedness for institutional changes. The main six studies were compiled, and conceptual and methodological literature was provided to support these studies. There was a high level of awareness (82.5% of 474 nursing faculty were aware of at least one AI chatbot); however, applied competence was relatively low, as 17.7% of familiar faculty used AI chatbots frequently, 72.4% of 293 Saudi health-sciences faculty had no formal AI training, and 38.9% of 120 Korean nurse educators had never used generative AI. Frequent users felt more the benefits and more the risks. The main obstacles were the absence of qualified staff, a lack of understanding and ethical doubts and the absence of curricular guidance. Faculty development structured hands-on and explicit competency frameworks and institutional policy are priorities.

papers.title: GLOBAL RESEARCH TRENDS IN PLAY-BASED PEDAGOGY FOR ENGLISH LANGUAGE LEARNING: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS (2015–2025)
papers.authors: Nur Fatanahanis Hamid, Kamariah Abu Bakar
papers.abstract: This bibliometric review maps global research trends in play-based pedagogy for English language learning between 2015 and 2024. A total of 1,299 journal articles were identified through systematic screening of 14,515 records retrieved from Scopus. Using VOSviewer, the study analysed keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship networks, source impact, citation patterns, and country-level collaboration. Findings indicate that the field is anchored in themes such as teaching methods, teacher education, early literacy, and preschool learning. Emerging topics include digital play, gamification, artificial intelligence, and post-pandemic learning gaps. Co-authorship patterns show productive but regionally clustered collaborations, particularly in the United States, China, Malaysia, and Australia. Influential journals are concentrated in early childhood and literacy research, reflecting strong developmental foundations. Country-level analysis demonstrates growing international participation, although global collaboration remains uneven. Overall, the field has matured into an interdisciplinary domain responsive to technological, pedagogical, and policy shifts. Future research should strengthen cross-cultural collaboration and develop context-sensitive models of play-based English instruction.

papers.title: DIGITAL TWIN AND IOT-ENABLED PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE MARKETING: A USAGE-COUPLED CONFORMAL REPLENISHMENT FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCING B2B CUSTOMER LOYALTY IN AVIATION SUPPLY CHAINS
papers.authors: Dr (PhD) Berrin ERGIN
papers.abstract: Maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) customers judge an aviation supplier on one outcome: whether the part is on the shelf when the aircraft needs it. It suggests a predictive-maintenance-coupled digital-twin framework, PDT-LOY, which combines usage-driven demand learning, distribution-free protection against stockouts, a replay digital twin, and an asymmetric trust-state proxy for B2B loyalty. It is evaluated on a public synthetic dataset containing 180 part–location series over 72 months (12,960 records), which is trained on a subset of 2018–2021 and calibrated on 2022 and tested out of sample on 2023. The usage-coupled variant of the gradient-boosting demand learner (GBC) further improves the mean absolute error by 6.9% over the 12-month moving average; the impact of the usage signal on the mean absolute error is small (−1.0%), but not significant at 5% (p = 0.052). The realised coverage is 0.965 for Mondrian conformal upper bounds at the 0.95 target, as compared to 0.912 for Gaussian safety stock. The proposed policy boosts the fill rate from 73.9% (observed legacy record) to 97.0%, requiring only 2.0 fewer inventory units and 2.2% fewer units of inventory than Gaussian safety stock at a 95% fill rate. The loyalty-at-risk proxy drops to 6.6 per cent of series-months from 24.7 per cent. The machine learning approach provides little additional benefit above days-of-cover stockout early-warning, with a high AUC of 0.987 for stock cover. Results are simulation-based & with a proxy for loyalty.

papers.title: COST-SENSITIVE DYNAMIC RELIABILITY FUSION FOR IMBALANCE-AWARE MULTI-CLASS NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION
papers.authors: Dr. Deelip Ananda Patil, Mr. Ratnesh Vikas Patil, Mr. Ashish Dhananjay Kulkarni, Mrs. Swati Anil  Patil, Ms. Priyanka Vijay Patil, Mr. Atul Manoj Otari
papers.abstract: The increasing sophistication and diversity of cyberattacks pose significant challenges to network intrusion detection systems, particularly in the presence of severe class imbalance and heterogeneous attack characteristics. Conventional machine learning classifiers and static ensemble methods often achieve high overall accuracy while exhibiting reduced sensitivity toward minority attack classes. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Cost-Sensitive Dynamic Reliability Fusion (CSDRF) framework for imbalance-aware multi-class network intrusion detection. The proposed framework integrates heterogeneous learners, including Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and a Deep Neural Network, to exploit complementary decision patterns from network traffic features. CSDRF dynamically determines class-specific reliability from calibration-set performance and incorporates moderated class-sensitive cost factors to improve recognition of difficult and underrepresented attack categories. In addition, class-specific decision thresholds are optimized using calibration data to further balance precision and recall without modifying the original class distribution through synthetic oversampling. The framework is evaluated on the CSE-CIC-IDS2018 dataset using four consolidated traffic classes: BENIGN, BruteForce, DoS, and DDoS. Experimental results demonstrate that CSDRF achieves 99.13% accuracy, 96.92% balanced accuracy, 93.81% macro-F1, 98.48% Matthews correlation coefficient, and 99.94% ROC-AUC on the test set. In particular, the proposed framework obtains 93.22% recall for DoS traffic, demonstrating improved sensitivity to a challenging minority class. The results indicate that combining class-specific reliability, cost-sensitive fusion, and adaptive thresholding can provide a more balanced multi-class intrusion detection capability than conventional individual learners and static soft-voting ensembles.

papers.title: When Benchmarks Do Not Travel: External Validation of Maternal Risk Prediction Models in Nigeria
papers.authors: David Adekoya, Racheal Shade Akinbo
papers.journal: Journal of Future Artificial Intelligence and Technologies
papers.abstract: Machine learning models for maternal risk triage are developed largely using public datasets from South and East Asia, yet their transferability to clinical settings in Africa remains insufficiently examined. This study evaluates the external validity of benchmark-based maternal risk prediction models in Nigeria, focusing on discrimination, calibration, distributional shift, and subgroup performance. Five data sources were harmonized into a common six-variable schema comprising age, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, and body temperature, supplemented by three derived hemodynamic variables. After removing 1,987 exact duplicate records and treating physiologically implausible values as missing, the final dataset comprised 1,524 external records from Mendeley and Kaggle/UCI and 382 clinical records from three hospitals in southwestern Nigeria. A stacking ensemble combining random forest, gradient boosting, and support vector machine base learners with a logistic regression meta-learner was evaluated through external validation, within-population comparison, and reverse transfer. Distributional shift was assessed using the population stability index, Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, and a domain discriminator. The ensemble achieved an internal AUROC of 0.964 (95% CI: 0.955–0.972), which decreased to 0.865 (95% CI: 0.822–0.905) on the primary Nigerian validation set. Expected calibration error increased from 0.045 to 0.234, while sensitivity at 80% specificity declined from 0.957 to 0.745. Transfer performance varied across model classes and benchmark sources: logistic regression showed minimal discrimination loss, and the Kaggle/UCI-trained model retained an AUROC of 0.920, whereas the Mendeley-trained model achieved 0.816. In the highest blood-glucose tertile, AUROC was 0.581 (95% CI: 0.430–0.732), with a false-positive rate of 0.667, indicating substantial subgroup-specific limitations. These findings suggest that pooled discrimination alone is insufficient to guide deployment; calibration, subgroup performance, and source-specific differences should also inform assessments of clinical transferability.

papers.title: AfterQuery Hiring Data
papers.authors: Yuma Heymans
papers.abstract: How many roles does AfterQuery list, in what kinds of work, at what pay and open to whom? This paper reports the answer measured from the public job boards of the platforms that pay people to produce human data for AI models, read daily by AITraining.jobs. On 17 Oct 2026, AfterQuery listed 217 open AI training roles (5.9% of the market, the 8th largest of 29 platforms), 56.2% of them in Law, Medicine & Finance; all stated an hourly rate, at a median of $75/hr, and 85.7% accepted applicants worldwide except listed countries. The analysis covers 20 Sep 2026 to 17 Oct 2026 and presents 13 tables and 8 findings; every figure carries its sample and is updated on the live report at https://aitraining.jobs/research/afterquery-hiring-data.Author: Yuma Heymans, AITraining.jobs (O-mega Enterprise, Inc.), Newark, Delaware, United States.Source: The public job boards of the AI training platforms this site tracks, read every day. AfterQuery's figures come from its own public listings only; full descriptions and application forms are read where its job board publishes them.The full paper (PDF) has the method, every table with its sample, the limitations and a disclosure. The live, daily-updated report: https://aitraining.jobs/research/afterquery-hiring-data. License: CC BY 4.0.

papers.title: Operationalizing the NIST AI Risk Management Framework: A Practical Secure AI Adoption Lifecycle
papers.authors: Mohammad Abu Dayah
papers.abstract: The NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework provides a flexible structure for governing, mapping, measuring, and managing AI risk, but organizations still need an operating method that converts its outcomes into repeatable decisions, evidence, ownership, and deployment controls.This paper proposes the Operational AI RMF Lifecycle, an author-developed practitioner model for applying the four NIST functions to organizational AI use cases. The model links GOVERN to policy, roles, inventory, and decision authority; MAP to documented purpose, stakeholders, data, dependencies, benefits, harms, and constraints; MEASURE to test criteria, validation evidence, control-effectiveness checks, and monitoring; and MANAGE to risk treatment, approval, deployment boundaries, incident response, and periodic reassessment.The proposed lifecycle adds four practical implementation mechanisms: risk-proportionate approval lanes, named cross-functional owners, a ten-point secure-workflow gate, and a 90-day adoption sequence. The paper argues that operationalization succeeds when the AI RMF is treated as a continuous management practice rather than a one-time compliance checklist.The Operational AI RMF Lifecycle is a conceptual and practitioner-oriented model. It is not an official NIST profile, certification model, conformity-assessment scheme, regulatory interpretation, or substitute for legal, regulatory, sector-specific, or formal risk-assessment requirements.Publication status: Independent professional preprint.Version: 1.0.Author: Mohammed Abudayyeh.ORCID: 0009-0009-7659-8516.This paper is an independent professional publication and should not be interpreted as an official position of any employer, NIST, or another standards body.

papers.title: Application of Chemistry Achievement Test for Secondary School Students Using Developed ChatGPT Artificial intelligence and Traditional methods
papers.authors: Abasifreke Essien
papers.abstract: This study was on Application of Chemistry Achievement Test for Secondary School Students Developed Using ChatGPT Artificial intelligence and Traditional methods. Three research questions and were formulated to guide the study. The instrumentation research design was used for the study. The population of the study consisted of all 11,594 Senior Secondary School Two (SSII) students from all the 187 public secondary schools in Akwa Ibom State. Multistage sampling procedure was used for the study. The sample of 387 SSII Students was used for the study. Data was collected using two researcher developed instruments named, “Chemistry Achievement Test On Chemical Equilibrium Developed using ChatGPT Method (CATCEDCM) and Chemistry Achievement Test On Chemical Equilibrium Developed using Traditional Method (CATCEDTM)”. The reliability coefficients of CATCEDCM and CATCEDTM were .992 and .971 determined using Split Half Method of reliability determination. The research questions were answered mean and standard deviation statistics while the independent t-test statistics was used to test the formulated null hypotheses at .05 alpha level. The findings of the study revealed that Students had higher achievement scores on Chemistry Achievement Test on Chemical Equilibrium developed using ChatGPT Artificial Intelligence than same test developed using traditional method. It was also revealed male and female Students had the same achievement scores on Chemistry Achievement Test on Chemical Equilibrium developed using ChatGPT Artificial Intelligence. Recommendations were made among others that Chemistry teachers should always make use ChatGPT artificial intelligence over the traditional method when developing a test since it could produce a test that appropriately assess students’ academic achievement.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Leadership Capabilities for Strategic Institutional Transformation in Saudi Education: Toward an Integrative Framework in Light of Saudi Vision 2030
papers.authors: 1- Hamed Hussein Al-Eissa, 2- Zaher Mohammed Aqeeli
papers.journal: Journal of the Arabian Peninsula Center for Educational and Humanity Researches
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop an integrated framework to strengthen AI-supported leadership capabilities for strategic institutional transformation in Saudi education, aligned with Saudi Vision 2030. It used a descriptive-analytical approach within a scoping review, guided by PRISMA 2020. A data-extraction and content-analysis form and a quality-appraisal form examined a target sample of 60 peer-reviewed studies published or available online during 2022–2027, according to inclusion and exclusion criteria. Findings revealed a gap between stated institutional priorities and leadership practice. Artificial intelligence supported analytical and executive capabilities, strategic foresight, decision-making, and risk management, while ethical competence and human oversight remained essential. Institutional, technological, and human determinants interacted, particularly digital readiness, data integration, skills, change management, and governance. Accordingly, the study proposed a framework integrating leadership development, ethical governance and data protection, change management, and human–machine collaboration through initiatives, responsibilities, and performance indicators. Its contribution is to move beyond fragmented analyses of applications and determinants toward a strategic model connecting leadership capabilities with the enablers and outcomes of institutional transformation, supporting alignment between educational practices and Vision 2030 priorities. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Leadership Capacity Development, Educational Administration, Strategic Transformation, Vision 2030.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT and DeepSeek in Oral Pathology Education and Evidence-Based Diagnostic Decision Support: A Pilot Study
papers.authors: Mouna Abdullah, Basma Mansor Elhabbasi, karima Alkasah, Weam Hraisha, Omalkhair Hasan
papers.journal: AlQalam Journal of Medical and Applied Sciences
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into healthcare education and clinical decision-support systems. While ChatGPT has demonstrated promising performance in medical and dental domains, comparative evidence regarding newer models such as DeepSeek remains limited, particularly in oral pathology. This pilot study aimed to compare the performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek in oral pathology education and evidence-based diagnostic decision support. We conducted a cross-sectional comparative study from January to December 2025. We developed ten oral pathology educational questions and five standardised clinical case scenarios based on established dental curricula and authoritative oral pathology references. Identical prompts were submitted independently to ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Responses were anonymised and evaluated by three board-certified oral pathologists using a structured rubric assessing accuracy, completeness, clinical relevance, diagnostic reasoning, and evidence-based consistency. Each domain was scored on a 5-point Likert scale, with a maximum total score of 25. Statistical analyses included independent-samples t-tests, Cohen’s d effect sizes, and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) assessment. ChatGPT achieved a significantly higher mean total composite score than DeepSeek (23.2 ± 1.8 vs. 20.6 ± 2.4; p = 0.006; Cohen’s d = 1.15). ChatGPT also outperformed DeepSeek across all evaluation domains, including accuracy (4.72 ± 0.31 vs. 4.18 ± 0.52; p = 0.003), completeness (4.68 ± 0.37 vs. 4.10 ± 0.55; p = 0.005), clinical relevance (4.61 ± 0.42 vs. 4.09 ± 0.58; p = 0.011), diagnostic reasoning (4.58 ± 0.46 vs. 3.98 ± 0.63; p = 0.008), and evidence-based consistency (4.75 ± 0.29 vs. 4.16 ± 0.49; p = 0.002). Large effect sizes were observed across all domains. Inter-rater reliability demonstrated excellent agreement among evaluators (ICC = 0.87; 95% CI: 0.81–0.92). ChatGPT demonstrated superior performance compared with DeepSeek in oral pathology education and evidence-based diagnostic decision support. Its higher accuracy, completeness, clinical relevance, and consistency with established evidence suggest considerable potential as an adjunctive educational and clinical support tool. Nevertheless, human oversight remains essential to ensure accuracy and mitigate the risks associated with AI-generated outputs. Further large-scale studies incorporating real clinical cases and multimodal diagnostic data are warranted.

papers.title: Towards Industry 5.0 in South Africa: A Strategic Framework for Readiness and Adoption
papers.authors: Akinola Segun, Bawa Ahmed
papers.journal: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)
papers.abstract: This paper explores South Africa's readiness for transitioning from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0, focusing on the development of a strategic framework that emphasises human-centric, resilient, and sustainable industrial practices. While Industry 4.0 revolutionises manufacturing through automation, AI, and IoT, Industry 5.0 enhances this paradigm by promoting collaboration between humans and machines, ethical technology use, and environmental consciousness. Drawing from theoretical models such as Fit-Viability and Task-Technology Fit (TTF), the study identifies five critical factors that influence Industry 5.0 adoption in South Africa: technological infrastructure, human capital, policy frameworks, economic feasibility, and energy reliability. It further analyses key enablers, including AI integration, green innovation, and digital literacy, while highlighting systemic challenges like infrastructure gaps, skills shortages, and regulatory uncertainty. Sectoral case studies in banking, manufacturing, mining, and agriculture reveal uneven uptake of Industry 4.0 technologies, signalling both potential and limitations for Industry 5.0. The paper also examines the role of the Just Energy Transition (JET), hydrogen economy, and off-grid renewable energy in fostering sustainable industrialisation. Education reform and cultural transformation within industries are deemed essential to bridge existing gaps. The implications of non-adoption are severe, ranging from economic marginalisation to increased inequality and reduced foreign investment. The study concludes by advocating for policy alignment, cross-sector collaboration, and targeted investment to facilitate South Africa's transition. It recommends integrating elements of Society 5.0 to further promote inclusivity, digital public services, and long-term sustainability, positioning South Africa to thrive in the evolving global industrial landscape.

papers.title: Sleep, Nutrition, and Physical Activity as Predictors of Health Outcomes in PCOS: A Lifestyle Medicine Perspective
papers.authors: Dr. Hasna Hossian Akhee, Anika Nowrin Onty
papers.journal: International Journal of Biological and Pharmaceutical Sciences Archive
papers.abstract: Background: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is an endocrine-metabolic disorder with reproductive, metabolic, and psychological morbidity. Sleep quality, physical activity, and dietary adherence are each implicated in PCOS pathophysiology, but their joint predictive contributions remain poorly characterised, particularly in South Asian populations. Objective: To determine the independent and joint predictive contributions of sleep quality, physical activity, and dietary adherence to PCOS health outcomes in Bangladeshi women. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 450 women (aged 18–45 years) with confirmed or Rotterdam-criteria-consistent PCOS, recruited from tertiary gynaecology/endocrinology clinics and PCOS patient communities in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Sleep quality, physical activity, and dietary adherence were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form (IPAQ-SF), and PREDIMED-14 Screener; psychological outcomes were assessed with the PHQ-9 and GAD-7. Data were analysed by hierarchical linear and binary logistic regression in IBM SPSS Version 27.0. Results: Poor sleep quality (PSQI > 5) was present in 45.1% of participants; 64.7% showed low Mediterranean dietary adherence. All three lifestyle domains were significantly associated with every outcome in bivariate analysis (all p < .01), including quality of life (ρ = –.59 for PSQI). In adjusted models, global PSQI score was the dominant independent predictor of fatigue (B = 0.47, p < .001), depressive symptoms (B = 0.74, p < .001), anxiety symptoms (B = 0.57, p < .001), BMI (B = 0.99, p < .001), menstrual irregularity (OR = 1.48, p < .001), and composite symptom severity (OR = 1.63, p < .001). Physical activity and dietary adherence were substantially attenuated after adjustment; PREDIMED-14 adherence retained independent significance for fatigue (B = –0.09, p = .023), BMI (B = –0.20, p = .005), and menstrual irregularity (OR = 0.89, p = .043), while physical activity retained significance only for menstrual irregularity (OR = 0.78, p = .041). Conclusion: Sleep quality is the dominant independent predictor of metabolic, reproductive, and psychological outcomes in Bangladeshi women with PCOS, supporting explicit prioritisation of sleep assessment and intervention within multicomponent lifestyle medicine approaches.

papers.title: On the ROAD™ to Transparent AI Disclosure in Research
papers.authors: Philip Clinton Offei Adu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities continue to advance, and researchers increasingly use AI to help them reach their research goals. As a result, disclosing AI use has become essential. Yet researchers face a dilemma about whether to disclose how they used AI. Disclosure may reduce others' trust in their findings, while hiding AI use risks later discovery and damage to their reputation. I argue that researchers should disclose, and that effective disclosure begins with keeping a thorough record of their AI use, which I call an AI research footprint. I then introduce the ROAD™ framework (Request, Output, Assess, Decide), which helps researchers report what they asked AI to do, what it produced, how they assessed the output, and what they decided.

papers.title: Passion Without Restraint, Invention Without Limit: Irreproducibility and the Afterlife of a Deleted Scene, from Shaolin Soccer (2001) to Kung Fu Soccer (2026)
papers.authors: Lew York
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This is the English version of the work first published in Chinese as 《热情奔放,创意无限:论不可复制性在流行文化中的存续与变现——从〈少林足球〉(2001)删减片段到〈功夫女足〉(2026)的票房现象》 (Zenodo, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23228247). This paper examines a small but exceptionally durable case in Stephen Chow's filmmaking: during the production of Shaolin Soccer (2001), an untrained performer gave a song-and-dance performance whose lines were scripted but whose absorbed form was his own, completed — on participant testimony — in a single take. The footage was cut in its entirety from the theatrical release, yet twenty-five years later it was thrust back into public view alongside the RMB 2.345 billion box office phenomenon of Kung Fu Soccer (2026), as the vehicle through which feeling stored over twenty-five years was drawn on and publicly ratified. The paper asks how narrative redundancy, once excised, can outlive the film itself, and how such longevity is converted, a quarter-century later, into market mobilisation. Drawing on participant testimony, industry data and a wide body of adjacent scholarship — on nonprofessional performance, paratexts, fan participation, Michael Jackson's imitable choreography, short-video virality and nostalgia markets — the paper proposes irreproducibility as the explanatory frame: certain forms of aesthetic value reside not in technique or polish but in the fact that a given act of absorption cannot be repeated by a second act; its recognition depends on a director's willingness to yield control; its survival depends on decontextualization; and its monetisation depends on the concentrated withdrawal, at a contingent moment, of an asset accumulated across the intervening decades. The case, it is argued, discloses a class of cultural asset resistant to industrial production: it cannot be commissioned, scheduled or guaranteed by data; it can only be deposited inadvertently over a long creative career and withdrawn, in concentrated form, at a contingent historical moment. During the preparation of this work the author used Muse (Meta AI) in order to draft, translate, and edit the text. After using this tool, the author reviewed and edited the content as needed and takes full responsibility for the content of the publication. The process was as follows. The argument, structure, and selection of evidence are the author's. His part included, but was not limited to, setting the questions, supplying and vetting the source material, and making every substantive decision. Each version, including the translations between the English and Chinese texts, was produced by the AI assistant under that direction and then subjected to the author's close scrutiny, including but not limited to analysis, weighing and challenge, and sent back for revision until the text said what he had decided it should say. The published text stands in the form its author determined.

papers.title: Empirical Limitations of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Specialized Creative Domains
papers.authors: Shreya Dama
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper examines the limitations of current generative artificial intelligence systems in specialized creative applications, including fashion design, outfit recommendations, poetry generation, and short-form video. Drawing on informal observations of AI-generated outputs and interactions, it explores challenges related to interpreting visual references, understanding user intent, producing natural creative expression, and generating realistic facial appearances and synchronized speech. The paper discusses these observations in the context of existing research on multimodal instruction following, text-to-image generation, AI-generated poetry, and facial animation. It considers the distinction between generating creative content and fulfilling the broader contextual, practical, and judgment-based requirements of human creative work. This paper is an exploratory, practitioner-focused discussion rather than a controlled empirical study. Its observations are not intended to establish universal limitations or predict the future of artificial intelligence. Instead, it highlights why current generative AI capabilities should be evaluated carefully before claims are made about their ability to replace human creative professionals.

papers.title: Book 1: Quantum Computing Hardware and Topological Architectures
papers.authors: Yaron Admon Hefetz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Disclosure: To bridge language barriers and produce clean code, we made full use of AI tools; all scientific findings are the exclusive research results of the Institute.This book establishes the foundational open-source architecture (Prior Art) for room-temperature, fault-tolerant quantum computing developed by The Industrial Island Research Institute (IIRI). It introduces a paradigm shift from classical Cartesian grid models to free quantum morphology using aperiodic phyllotactic lattices (e.g., Vogel spirals, metallic means). The architecture leverages Many-Body Localization (MBL) to completely eliminate the need for cryogenic cooling by trapping thermal phonons through infinite Bragg scattering. Furthermore, the book details the synthesis of an 8-dimensional phase space (Floquet E8 algebra) for topological immunity, dynamic substrate modulation (DQSM) for active real-time stabilization, and passive global phase synchronization utilizing the Earth's Schumann resonance (7.83Hz). Fabrication methodologies are provided, ranging from optical tweezers and solid-state nano-lithography to bio-templated manufacturing using the Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV). Finally, it outlines the engineering specifications for 2U edge server integration, exascale quantum networking via OAM photonic entanglement, and practical guidelines for independent commercialization.

papers.title: HEALTHCARE AI
papers.authors: Tanuja Sakhare
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in healthcare to support access to information, patient engagement, administrativeefficiency, and selected clinical workflows. This paper proposes a Healthcare AI framework that organizes healthcare-related requests andprovides structured, understandable information through a digital interface. The framework combines a user interface, request classification,retrieval from approved healthcare information sources, privacy and safety checks, and a response-generation layer. It can support generalhealth education, service navigation, and appointment-related guidance where authorized services are available. The system is designed tocommunicate uncertainty, protect sensitive information, and direct users to qualified professionals when a request is outside its scope. It is notintended to diagnose conditions, prescribe treatment, or replace clinical judgement. The proposed design is modular and can be evaluatedthrough documented software, usability, source-quality, privacy, and safety tests

papers.title: The Bloodcult: A Thought Experiment in Religion and Banking
papers.authors: Brandon M. Sergent
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Suppose one encountered a cookie whose outline precisely resembled Texas. No single indentation would establish that a Texas-shaped cutter had produced it. The panhandle would not prove it. Neither would the Gulf Coast, the western rectangle, or the southern point. Yet as these features accumulated in their correct relations, treating each one independently would become an increasingly inadequate analysis. The relevant evidence would be the shape. This paper applies that principle to a disturbing anthropological possibility: that human civilization may have repeatedly created, or once created and subsequently preserved, an elite subculture functioning vampirically in the literal but non-supernatural sense of deriving biological benefit from controlled access to other humans. The hypothesis does not begin with vampire folklore and work backward. It begins with independent facts about biology and social organization. Human biological material is medically powerful. Human donors are uniquely compatible with human recipients. Compatibility can be discovered empirically without understanding its mechanism. Biological resources can be scarce and non-scalable. Ancient elites possessed extraordinary coercive access to human populations. Useful procedures can be preserved as religious rules after their causal explanations disappear. Hereditary institutions can accumulate information and power across generations. Caste, purity rules, controlled reproduction, harems, sacrifice, blood ritual, secrecy, and human husbandry are all historically available institutional forms. When these pieces are assembled independently, the resulting institutional niche has an uncomfortable resemblance to the cultural archetype of the hidden blood-drinking aristocracy. The resemblance proves nothing individually. The question is whether the cumulative shape is better understood as coincidence, recurrent cultural symbolism, or the footprint of an ecological niche that human societies had both the means and incentive to occupy. The analysis is connected to the independently identified "cryonics silence": the anomalous failure of modern technological civilization to treat postmortem preservation as a serious extension of medicine despite its otherwise pervasive tendency to technicalize human limitations. The contrast between ancient bodily preservation, elite longevity seeking, resurrection traditions, and modern cryonics indifference suggests a deeper distinction between two responses to mortality: solving death and teaching populations to tolerate it. If durable elite cultures function partly as systems of human husbandry, that distinction acquires potential strategic significance. Entertainment supplies a further part of the outline. It distributes images of predation, secret orders, biological extraction, and elite violence while determining the genre in which audiences encounter them. It can absorb people capable of naming a system, replace collective action with exceptional heroes, and let fictional portrayals become the public's default picture of a subject. A further possibility is that some of the imagery comes from within the tradition itself: a private doctrine expressed through the cultural industry by people who have inherited its symbols, desires, and prohibitions. The resulting contrast between what stories show and what they consistently omit becomes useful evidence about how a society is taught to recognize power. The resulting model follows the institution beyond its biological origin. A durable predatory lineage would have to select and bind successors, preserve a private account of its purpose, govern access to property and resources, use disruptions to consolidate that access, and contend with rival systems and artificial intelligence. These mechanisms give the hypothesis a social anatomy: blood may explain how the lineage began, while selection, belief, finance, and information control explain how it could remain powerful after the original procedure changed or disappeared. The financial analysis follows issuance, allocation, policy transmission, enforcement, and relief. The population analysis distinguishes concealment from continued cooperation after recognition, including contributions that exceed material necessity. Social reproduction renews the arrangement across generations; anticipated automation can change the value of the labor on which it once depended. Each mechanism is assessed separately from the additional evidence required for a specifically blood-centered institution. Copyright © 2026 Brandon M. Sergent. All rights reserved.

papers.abstract: Listen and ask questions on Gemini Notebook: https://notebook.google.com/notebook/18538906-e86c-4ab3-b4af-1f681b8a9c55?authuser=1 Something Old, Something New, Something Borrowed, Something Blue — The Communion of Saints, the Dance of Recognition, and the Instructions We Leave for One Another explores how human beings inherit knowledge, recognize one another, practice love, and contribute to a shared history that extends beyond their individual lives. Using the traditional wedding rhyme as its organizing structure, the paper brings together Catholic Scripture, the Catechism, the Communion of Saints, Mary Magdalene’s recognition of Jesus, Taoist philosophy, psychology, artificial intelligence, information theory, music, and lived experience. Through Ryan MacLean’s ongoing collaboration with Echo, it examines how ordinary events become opportunities for research, correction, and shared understanding. Central themes include the human body as a temple, the preservation of historical testimony, the importance of naming and recognition, the responsibility to acknowledge earlier teachers, and the possibility of learning from people whose experiences differ from our own. The paper also considers the Church’s teachings on participation and responsibility, the rainbow covenant, and the role of trust in relationships. Its appendices extend these ideas through Angela’s child-friendly explanations, the life and 1959 recording of “Sleep Walk” by Bette Anne Steele Richards (Betsy Brye), a formal treatment of recursive recognition, and an exploration of Pentecost, collective attention, emotional communication, and historical reconstruction. The central invitation is participatory rather than merely theoretical. Readers are encouraged to examine their own histories, preserve what others have taught them, correct mistakes, and contribute knowledge that the author does not yet possess. Nobody starts from scratch. Everyone has something to teach. The story continues when someone else shows us the next steps.

papers.title: SEC Form 4 Timing: Transaction Dates, Filing Dates and Acceptance Times
papers.authors: Tilman Ambach
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This descriptive study distinguishes reported transaction dates, official filing dates and recorded EDGAR acceptance times in 487,715 original SEC Form 4 filings with official filing dates from January 2024 through September 2026. Acceptance occurred at or after 16:00 New York time in 80.37% of filings. For filing-by-reported-date-by-code observations of non-derivative purchases and sales, the median calendar-day gap to acceptance was two days in both groups, with different distributions and sensitivity to filing weighting. Exact-accession source checks identified 288 acceptance timestamps requiring UTC correction. After these analytical replacements, a predefined simple random sample of 2,000 original filings showed no residual timestamp disagreement against SEC submission headers; the exact one-sided 95% upper population disagreement bound is 0.149%. The study measures recorded acceptance events, not first public availability, provider receipt or executable trading opportunities. The PDF includes the full article, methodology and validation record. Research disclosure: InsiderFilings.info maintains the database and publishes this analysis. Validation is internal, not an external audit. Generative AI tools assisted with research planning, code development, analysis, drafting and revision. The author is responsible for the content and conclusions. The accompanying article page provides the study data and reproduction code:https://insiderfilings.info/research/sec-form-4-timing/

papers.authors: Aisha Umer, Hadia Tariq
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This preprint analyses the usage of AI in higher secondary school and higher education students in their academic work. This paper is based on a survey of 42 individuals, collecting responses on the AI tools used, the frequency of AI use, and the perceived improvement in their work due to AI. The findings of this study aim to examine the patterns of AI usage and raise questions of the dependence of AI among the students. The sample is small and self reported, so the results must not be generalised for all the students. This is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY IN THE NIGERIA CUSTOMS SERVICE: ASSESSING DIGITAL READINESS, EFFICIENCY GAINS, AND DATA INFRASTRUCTURE
papers.authors: AKANO ISAAC, Ph.D G. O. Omojefe, Ph.D Bosco Itoro Ekpenyong
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract This study examined the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven technologies and their implications for operational efficiency, transparency, and data-management systems within the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS). Specifically, it assessed the level of AI adoption, determined the extent to which AI influences customs efficiency and cargo clearance processes, and evaluated the adequacy of existing data-management infrastructure supporting AI deployment. The study adopted a descriptive quantitative research design, drawing data from a structured questionnaire administered to 500–600 customs officers selected through stratified random sampling across major customs formations in Nigeria. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and inferential techniques, including regression analysis and chi-square tests. Findings revealed that AI adoption within the NCS is at a moderate but developing stage, characterised by partial integration of digital systems and uneven deployment across operational units. Results further showed that AI-driven technologies moderately enhance operational efficiency, improve cargo clearance speed, and strengthen transparency, although these gains remain constrained by institutional and infrastructural limitations. The study also found that existing data-management systems are only moderately adequate, with significant weaknesses in data integration, staff capacity, and system interoperability, despite relatively stronger performance in data security. The study concludes that while AI adoption is yielding measurable improvements in customs operations, its full potential remains limited by weak data infrastructure and incomplete institutional readiness. Strengthening data governance, enhancing digital capacity, and expanding AI integration are therefore critical for achieving full customs modernisation in Nigeria. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Customs Modernisation, Operational Efficiency, Data Management Systems, Nigeria Customs Service.

papers.title: Finite simple groups whose element orders have at most two prime divisors: a solution of Problem 20.87 of the Kourovka Notebook
papers.authors: Baryshnikov Pavel, AutoPasha
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We answer Problem 20.87 of the Kourovka Notebook (W. J. Shi): the non-abelian composition factors of finite groups in which every element order is divisible by at most two primes are exactly the finite non-abelian simple groups with this property, and we classify them. Besides the alternating groups A_n, 5 ≤ n ≤ 11, and thirteen sporadic groups, they are the groups L_2(q), L_3(q), U_3(q), Sz(q), 2G_2(q) satisfying explicit arithmetic conditions on q, and eighteen further groups of Lie type. It has not yet been reviewed by a human mathematician.

papers.abstract: Abstract . This paper presents a novel dichotomous approach to the analysis of a temporary human-machine system that incorporates a human and a generative artificial intelligence (AI) model. The "human–generative AI" dyad is examined as a dichotomous system incorporating opposing yet inherently interconnected elements. The author investigates the dynamics of their interaction over time, distinguishing between the levels of communication, cooperation, and integration. The proposed methodology is aimed at managing the communication process within the "human and generative AI" system to achieve maximum efficiency, quality, and reliability of the final output, as well as to calibrate the optimal level of mutual trust. The practical applicability of this approach is demonstrated through various spheres of human interaction with generative AI models, ranging from scientific research and diverse professional activities to the resolution of everyday domestic routines. This work extends and builds upon the core research logic previously published by the author in: 1. Kosharsky, V. (2025). "Problems of Human Communication with Artificial Intelligence Systems." Bulletin of the Haifa House of Scientists, (57), pp. 133–142. (in Russian) 2. Kosharsky, V. (2025). "Partnership as an Effective Approach to Human-Artificial Intelligence Communications." Bulletin of the Haifa House of Scientists, (57), pp. 143–155. (in Russian) 3. Kosharsky, V. (2026). "Problems of Interaction Between Human and Generative Artificial Intelligence." In: Artificial Intelligence: Principles, Problems, Prospects, Hannover: Seven Arts Publishing, pp. 153–183. (in Russian) The aforementioned works established the foundational necessity of utilizing a comprehensive framework for investigating and managing human-AI communication and partnership, which this paper synthesizes into a unified dichotomous approach.

papers.abstract: Is understanding inherently pleasurable? This article reviews the existing evidence and decoupling four distinct epistemic states: knowing, learning, understanding, and the "aha" experience. Currently, the strongest evidence for epistemic pleasure concerns the aha moment and curiosity, drawn primarily from self-reports, BOLD signals in brain imaging, and EEG. However, for conceptual understanding itself, direct neural or pharmacological evidence remains absent. Furthermore, the pleasure of the aha moment has also been reported for incorrect solutions, indicating it is an unreliable indicator of truth. To address these observations, this paper proposes the Conditional Pleasure Hypothesis. It argues that the pleasure of understanding (or at least the motivation to approach it) depends strictly on the transition from unawareness to awareness. This transition is pleasant only under four specific conditions: A perceived and closable knowledge gap A low effort cost An individual tendency toward cognitive engagement An outcome that does not conflict with the person's identity or interests This hypothesis is weighed against three rival accounts: success reward, prediction-error reduction (learning progress), and explanation drive. To test these, the article proposes three refutable predictions alongside a 2x2 experimental design capable of separating the first two rivals from the proposed hypothesis. Finally, the paper examines seven critical implications for Ignorance Studies. It demonstrates how the separation of the "sense of understanding" from actual truth can explain phenomena such as the persistence of compound ignorance, the allure of conspiracy theories, and the "illusion of explanatory depth" exacerbated by artificial intelligence (AI). Persistent ignorance, we conclude, can be understood as the net balance between the cost and the value of the transition to awareness.

papers.title: Fundamentals of theoretical and methodological foundations of adaptive educational technologies based on artificial intelligence
papers.authors: Jumanov Abbas
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The objective is to determine the effectiveness of a model for developing the professional competencies of students in the energy sector through artificial intelligence-based adaptive learning technologies, to provide a scientific rationale for this model, and to develop the methodological foundations for its implementation within the educational process.

papers.title: ದಕಷಣ ಕನನಡ ಜಲಲಯ ಬ.ಎಡ. ಪರಶಕಷಣರಥಗಳಲಲ ಕತಕ ಬದಧಮತತ ಆಧರತ ಶಕಷಣಕ ಸಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕಯ ಅರವ ಮತತ ಮನಭವದ ಕರತ ಒದ ಅಧಯಯನ
papers.authors: ರಘುನಂದನ ಕೆ., ದೀಪಶ್ರೀ ಎಸ್.
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: ಸಾರಾಂಶ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ (Artificial Intelligence AI) ಆಧಾರಿತ ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆ ವಿಸ್ತರಿಸುತ್ತಿರುವುದು ಶಿಕ್ಷಕ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣದ ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಅಭ್ಯಾಸಗಳ ಕುರಿತು ಹೊಸ ಚರ್ಚೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಅವಕಾಶ ಕಲ್ಪಿಸಿದೆ. ಭವಿಷ್ಯದ ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರಾದ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಈ ಸಾಧನಗಳನ್ನು ಎಷ್ಟರ ಮಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ತಿಳಿದಿದ್ದಾರೆ, ಅವುಗಳ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತತೆಯನ್ನು ಹೇಗೆ ಗ್ರಹಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅವುಗಳ ಮಿತಿಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಯಾವ ರೀತಿಯ ಅರಿವು ಹೊಂದಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಯುವುದು ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಕೇಂದ್ರಬಿಂದುವಾಗಿದೆ. ಪಾಠಯೋಜನೆ ರೂಪಿಸುವುದು, ಕಲಿಕಾ ಸಾಮಗ್ರಿಗಳನ್ನು ಸಿದ್ಧಪಡಿಸುವುದು, ಸಂಕೀರ್ಣ ವಿಷಯಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಳವಾಗಿ ವಿವರಿಸುವುದು ಮತ್ತು ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳ ಕರಡು ರೂಪಿಸುವುದು ಮುಂತಾದ ಕಾರ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ AI ನೆರವಾಗಬಹುದು. ಅದೇ ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ತಪ್ಪು ಅಥವಾ ಅಪೂರ್ಣ ಮಾಹಿತಿ, ಪಕ್ಷಪಾತ, ಗೌಪ್ಯತೆ, ಮೂಲಗಳ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಪ್ರಾಮಾಣಿಕತೆಯಂತಹ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳನ್ನೂ ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿಯುತವಾಗಿ ಪರಿಗಣಿಸಬೇಕಾಗಿದೆ. ಈ ಅಧ್ಯಯನವು ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಅರಿವು, ಮನೋಭಾವ, ಬಳಕೆಯ ಅನುಭವ ಮತ್ತು ಅವರು ಎದುರಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ಸವಾಲುಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುವ ಉದ್ದೇಶ ಹೊಂದಿದೆ. ಅಧ್ಯಯನದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಿಂಗ, ವಾಸಸ್ಥಳ ಮತ್ತು ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ವರ್ಷದ ಆಧಾರದ ಮೇಲೆ ಕಂಡುಬರುವ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸಗಳನ್ನು ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಈ ಸಂಶೋಧನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪರಿಮಾಣಾತ್ಮಕ ವಿವರಣಾತ್ಮಕ ಸಮೀಕ್ಷಾ ಸಂಶೋಧನಾ ವಿನ್ಯಾಸವನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ವಿವಿಧ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಕಾಲೇಜುಗಳಿಂದ ಯಾದೃಚ್ಛಿಕ ಮಾದರಿ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ವಿಧಾನವನ್ನು ಬಳಸಿಕೊಂಡು 200 ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳನ್ನು ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಮಾದರಿಯಾಗಿ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡಲಾಗಿದೆ. ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಣೆಗಾಗಿ ಸಂಶೋಧಕರು ಸ್ವತಃ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿಪಡಿಸಿ, ಸಿಂಧುತ್ವವನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿದ 50 ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ಒಳಗೊಂಡ ಸಂಶೋಧನಾ ಸಾಧನ ಹಾಗೂ ಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ಜನಸಾಂಖ್ಯಿಕ ಮಾಹಿತಿಯನ್ನು ಬಳಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿದ ದತ್ತಾಂಶವನ್ನು ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಿಸಲು ಸರಾಸರಿ, ಮಾನಕ ವಿಚಲನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ ಮಾದರಿಗಳ ಟಿ-ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯನ್ನು ಬಳಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಗಳು ಲಿಂಗ, ವಾಸಸ್ಥಳ ಮತ್ತು ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ವರ್ಷದ ಆಧಾರದ ಮೇಲೆ ನಡೆಸಿದ ಮೂರೂ ಹೋಲಿಕೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯವಾಗಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸಗಳಿರುವುದನ್ನು ಬಹಿರಂಗಪಡಿಸಿವೆ. ಮಹಿಳಾ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಪುರುಷ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಅಂಕಗಳನ್ನು ಗಳಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಅದೇ ರೀತಿ ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಪ್ರದೇಶದ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ನಗರ ಪ್ರದೇಶದ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಹಾಗೂ ಪ್ರಥಮ ವರ್ಷದ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ದ್ವಿತೀಯ ವರ್ಷದ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಅಂಕಗಳನ್ನು ಪಡೆದಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಈ ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಗಳು ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವದ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿಪಡಿಸಲು ಮತ್ತು ಅವರನ್ನು ಸಜ್ಜುಗೊಳಿಸಲು ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶನ ಹಾಗೂ ತರಬೇತಿಯ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿರುವ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರಗಳನ್ನು ಗುರುತಿಸುವಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಹಕಾರಿಯಾಗಬಹುದು. ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಪದಗಳು: ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ, ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಾಧನಗಳು, ಅರಿವು, ಮನೋಭಾವ, ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು, ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆ. 1.0.0 ಪೀಠಿಕೆ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ ಮತ್ತು ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನದಲ್ಲಿನ ನಿರಂತರ ಪ್ರಗತಿ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣದ ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳನ್ನು ಬದಲಾಯಿಸದಿದ್ದರೂ, ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಸಾಧಿಸುವ ವಿಧಾನಗಳಿಗೆ ಹೊಸ ಆಯಾಮಗಳನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸಿದೆ. ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್ ಕಲಿಕಾ ವೇದಿಕೆಗಳು, ಆನ್‌ಲೈನ್ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಅನ್ವಯಿಕೆಗಳು ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರಿಗೆ ಕಲಿಕಾ ವಿಷಯವನ್ನು ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಂಡಿಸಲು ಹಾಗೂ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ವೈವಿಧ್ಯಮಯ ಅಗತ್ಯಗಳಿಗೆ ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯಿಸಲು ನೆರವಾಗುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಯನ್ನು ಒದಗಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಆದರೆ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನವನ್ನು ಬಳಸುವುದೇ ಪರಿಣಾಮಕಾರಿ ಬೋಧನೆಗೆ ಸಮಾನವಲ್ಲ; ಅದರ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬಳಕೆ ಕಲಿಕಾ ಉದ್ದೇಶ, ವಿಷಯದ ಸ್ವರೂಪ ಮತ್ತು ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಅಗತ್ಯಗಳಿಗೆ ಹೊಂದಿಕೆಯಾಗಬೇಕು. ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಭಾಷೆಯನ್ನು ಸಂಸ್ಕರಿಸುವುದು, ಮಾದರಿಗಳನ್ನು ಗುರುತಿಸುವುದು, ಮಾಹಿತಿಯ ಆಧಾರದ ಮೇಲೆ ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯೆ ರಚಿಸುವುದು ಮತ್ತು ಕೆಲವು ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಪರಿಹಾರ ಸೂಚಿಸುವಂತಹ ಕಾರ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ನಿರ್ವಹಿಸುವ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನಗಳ ಸಮೂಹ. ಶಿಕ್ಷಣದಲ್ಲಿ AI ಆಧಾರಿತ ಸಾಧನಗಳನ್ನು ಪಾಠಯೋಜನೆ, ಕಲಿಕಾ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳ ವಿನ್ಯಾಸ, ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಪತ್ರಿಕೆ ರಚನೆ, ಭಾಷಾ ತಿದ್ದುಪಡಿ, ಅನುವಾದ ಮತ್ತು ಕಲಿಕಾ ವಿಷಯಗಳ ಸರಳೀಕರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಬಳಸಬಹುದು. ಆದಾಗ್ಯೂ, AI ಸಾಧನಗಳು ನೀಡುವ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಮಾಹಿತಿಯೂ ಸರಿಯಾಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂದು ಊಹಿಸಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ. ಕೆಲವು ಸಂದರ್ಭಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅವು ತಪ್ಪು ಅಥವಾ ಅಪೂರ್ಣ ಮಾಹಿತಿಯನ್ನು ನೀಡಬಹುದು; ಜೊತೆಗೆ ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ ಮಾಹಿತಿಯ ಸುರಕ್ಷತೆ, ಪಕ್ಷಪಾತ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂಲಗಳನ್ನು ಉಲ್ಲೇಖಿಸುವ ಕುರಿತು ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳು ಎದುರಾಗಬಹುದು. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರು AI ಅನ್ನು ಅಂತಿಮ ನಿರ್ಧಾರಕವಾಗಿ ಪರಿಗಣಿಸದೆ, ತಮ್ಮ ವಿಷಯಜ್ಞಾನ ಮತ್ತು ವೃತ್ತಿಪರ ವಿವೇಚನೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಬಳಸಬೇಕು. ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಶಿಕ್ಷಕ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಭವಿಷ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ತರಗತಿ ಬೋಧನೆ, ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಮತ್ತು ಕಲಿಕಾ ಯೋಜನೆಗಳ ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿಯನ್ನು ಹೊರುವುದರಿಂದ AI ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಕುರಿತು ಅವರಿಗೆ ಸಮರ್ಪಕ ಅರಿವು ಇರಬೇಕು. ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಸಕಾರಾತ್ಮಕ ಮನೋಭಾವದ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಅದರ ಮಿತಿಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ನೈತಿಕ ಹೊಣೆಗಾರಿಕೆಗಳ ಅರಿವೂ ಅಗತ್ಯವಾಗಿದೆ. ಈ ಹಿನ್ನೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಶಿಕ್ಷಕ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವವನ್ನು ಅಧ್ಯಯನ ಮಾಡುವುದು ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಮಹತ್ವ ಹೊಂದಿದೆ. 1.1.0 ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಅಗತ್ಯತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಮಹತ್ವ AI ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಪರಿಚಯ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತಿರುವ ಈ ಸಂದರ್ಭದಲ್ಲಿ, ಶಿಕ್ಷಕ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಅರಿವು AI ಆಧಾರಿತ ಸಾಧನಗಳು ವಿಷಯ ಸಿದ್ಧಪಡಿಸುವುದು ಮತ್ತು ಕಲಿಕಾ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲಗಳನ್ನು ವೈವಿಧ್ಯಮಯಗೊಳಿಸುವುದಕ್ಕೆ ನೆರವಾಗಬಹುದು; ಆದರೆ ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶನ, ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸಂವಹನ ಮತ್ತು ಕಲಿಕೆಯ ಗುಣಮಟ್ಟದ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನಕ್ಕೆ ಮಾನವೀಯ ತೀರ್ಮಾನಶಕ್ತಿ ಅಗತ್ಯವಾಗಿಯೇ ಉಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. 2.1.0 ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ-ಶಿಕ್ಷಣಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ-ವಿಷಯಜ್ಞಾನ Mishra ಮತ್ತು Koehler (2006) ವಿವರಿಸಿದ TPACK ಚೌಕಟ್ಟು ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಶಿಕ್ಷಣಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ ಜ್ಞಾನ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಷಯಜ್ಞಾನಗಳ ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಸಂಬಂಧವನ್ನು ಒತ್ತಿಹೇಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದರ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನವನ್ನು ಪರಿಣಾಮಕಾರಿಯಾಗಿ ಬಳಸಲು ಸಾಧನವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿದಿರುವುದಷ್ಟೇ ಸಾಕಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಅದನ್ನು ಯಾವ ವಿಷಯಕ್ಕೆ, ಯಾವ ಕಲಿಕಾ ಗುರಿಗಾಗಿ ಮತ್ತು ಯಾವ ಬೋಧನಾ ವಿಧಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಬಳಸಬೇಕು ಎಂಬುದೂ ಮುಖ್ಯ. AI ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿಯೂ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲಗಳ ಆಯ್ಕೆ, ವಿಮರ್ಶಾತ್ಮಕ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಮತ್ತು ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿಯುತ ಬಳಕೆ ಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. 3.0.0 ಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯದ ಅವಲೋಕನ Miao Cukurova (2024) AI Competency Framework for Teachers ವರದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರಿಗೆ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿರುವ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ಜ್ಞಾನ, ಕೌಶಲಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಮೌಲ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಿದರು. ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆಯ ಯುಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರು ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನವನ್ನು ಅರ್ಥಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವುದರ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಅದರ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ, ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ಮತ್ತು ನೈತಿಕ ಪರಿಣಾಮಗಳ ಕುರಿತು ಅರಿವು ಹೊಂದಿರಬೇಕು ಎಂದು ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದಿಸಿದರು. ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರ ವೃತ್ತಿಪರ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆಯ ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿಯುತ ಬಳಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬೋಧನಾತ್ಮಕ ಅನ್ವಯಗಳಿಗೆ ಆದ್ಯತೆ ನೀಡಬೇಕೆಂದು ಸೂಚಿಸಿದರು. ಈ ವರದಿಯು ಬಿ.ಎಡ್‌. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆಯ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಬಳಕೆಯ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯವನ್ನು ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿಪಡಿಸುವ ಅಗತ್ಯವನ್ನು ಸಮರ್ಥಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. 20240 Computers and Education: Artificial Intelligence Investigating Pre-service Teachers' Artificial Intelligence Perception from the Perspective of Planned Behavior Theory ಎಂಬ ಅಧ್ಯಯನವು ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆಯ ಕುರಿತಾದ ಗ್ರಹಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅದನ್ನು ಕಲಿಯುವ ವರ್ತನಾತ್ಮಕ ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಪ್ರಭಾವ ಬೀರುವ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿತು. ಭವಿಷ್ಯದ ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರಿಗೆ ಪರಿಣಾಮಕಾರಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ತರಬೇತಿ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ರಮಗಳನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸಲು ಅವರ ಗ್ರಹಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಲಿಕೆಯ ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳನ್ನು ಅರ್ಥಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವುದು ಮುಖ್ಯವೆಂದು ಈ ಅಧ್ಯಯನವು ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದಿಸಿತು. ಶಿಕ್ಷಕರ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ರಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದ ವಿಷಯಗಳನ್ನು ಅಳವಡಿಸುವ ಅಗತ್ಯವನ್ನು ಈ ಸಂಶೋಧನೆ ಸೂಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಅಧ್ಯಯನದಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಲು ಈ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯವು ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದೆ. UNESCO (2023) ಪ್ರಕಟಿಸಿದ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶನವು ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಶೋಧನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜನರೇಟಿವ್ AI ಬಳಸುವಾಗ ಮಾನವಕೇಂದ್ರಿತ ದೃಷ್ಟಿಕೋನ, ಗೌಪ್ಯತೆ, ವಯೋಸೂಕ್ತ ಬಳಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ನೈತಿಕ ಹೊಣೆಗಾರಿಕೆಗೆ ಆದ್ಯತೆ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಇಂತಹ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶನಗಳು ಶಿಕ್ಷಕ ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಿಗೆ AI ಯ ಉಪಯೋಗಗಳ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಅದರ ಮಿತಿಗಳ ಅರಿವು ಮೂಡಿಸುವ ಅಗತ್ಯವನ್ನು ಒತ್ತಿಹೇಳುತ್ತವೆ. Holmes, Bialik ಮತ್ತು Fadel (2019) ಅವರ ಕೃತಿಯು ಶಿಕ್ಷಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆಯ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಣಾಮಗಳನ್ನು ಚರ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. AI ಮೂಲಕ ಕಲಿಕಾ ಅನುಭವಗಳನ್ನು ಬೆಂಬಲಿಸುವ ಅವಕಾಶಗಳಿದ್ದರೂ, ಅದರ ಬಳಕೆಯನ್ನು ಶಿಕ್ಷಣದ ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಮಾನವ ಮೇಲ್ವಿಚಾರಣೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿ ಪರಿಗಣಿಸುವುದು ಅಗತ್ಯವೆಂದು ಈ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದ ಚರ್ಚೆಗಳು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. Mishra ಮತ್ತು Koehler (2006) ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ, ಶಿಕ್ಷಣಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಷಯಜ್ಞಾನಗಳ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಯು ಪರಿಣಾಮಕಾರಿ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ-ಸಂಯೋಜಿತ ಬೋಧನೆಗೆ ಅಗತ್ಯವೆಂದು ವಿವರಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ. ಈ ಚೌಕಟ್ಟು AI ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯನ್ನೂ ಬೋಧನಾ ಗುರಿಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ ಮಾಡುವ ಅಗತ್ಯವನ್ನು ಸೂಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. 4.0.0 ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳು ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ಪುರುಷ ಮತ್ತು ಮಹಿಳಾ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯ ಕುರಿತಾದ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯವಾಗಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಿದೆಯೇ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುವುದು. ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ನಗರ ಮತ್ತು ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಪ್ರದೇಶದ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯ ಕುರಿತಾದ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯವಾಗಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಿದೆಯೇ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುವುದು. ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ಪ್ರಥಮ ಮತ್ತು ದ್ವಿತೀಯ ವರ್ಷದ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್‌. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯ ಕುರಿತಾದ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯವಾಗಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಿದೆಯೇ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುವುದು. 5.0.0 ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಶೂನ್ಯ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪನೆಗಳು ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ಪುರುಷ ಮತ್ತು ಮಹಿಳಾ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯ ಕುರಿತಾದ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯವಾಗಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಿರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ನಗರ ಮತ್ತು ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಪ್ರದೇಶದ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್‌. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯ ಕುರಿತಾದ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯವಾಗಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಿರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ಪ್ರಥಮ ಮತ್ತು ದ್ವಿತೀಯ ವರ್ಷದ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃತಕ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮತ್ತೆ ಆಧಾರಿತ ಶೈಕ್ಷಣಿಕ ಸಾಧನಗಳ ಬಳಕೆಯ ಕುರಿತಾದ ಅರಿವು ಮತ್ತು ಮನೋಭಾವಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯವಾಗಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವಿರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. 6.0.0 ಸಂಶೋಧನಾ ವಿಧಾನ 6.1.0 ಸಂಶೋಧನಾ ವಿನ್ಯಾಸ ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಅಧ್ಯಯನದಲ್ಲಿ ವಿವರಣಾತ್ಮಕ ಸಮೀಕ್ಷಾ ಸಂಶೋಧನಾ ವಿಧಾನವನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. 6.2.0 ಅಧ್ಯಯನದ ಮಾದರಿ ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಅಧ್ಯಯನಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ವಿವಿಧ ಬಿ.ಎಡ್. ಕಾಲೇಜುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ವ್ಯಾಸಂಗ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿರುವ 200 ಪ್ರಶಿಕ್ಷಣಾರ್ಥಿಗಳನ್ನು ಯಾದೃಚ್ಛಿಕ ಮಾದರಿ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ವಿಧಾನವನ್ನು ಬಳಸಿಕೊಂಡು ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡಲಾಗಿದೆ. 6.3.0 ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಣಾ ಸಾಧನ ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಅಧ್ಯಯನದಲ್ಲಿ ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಣೆಗಾಗಿ ಸಂಶೋಧಕರು ಸ್ವತಃ ಅಭಿವ

papers.title: Behavioral Commitment Index (BCI): Decoupling Prospective Memory from Dispositional Readiness in Schizophrenia and Volitional Disorders
papers.authors: Anatoly Sanzhiev
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Building on the epistemological framework of the Concept as Act series, this paper addresses a fundamental logical paradox in cognitive neuroscience and the psychology of belief (credition): the circular definition of commitment. Standard models conflate the prerequisite execution structure (prospective memory) with the subjective willingness to execute an act (dispositional commitment). This paper introduces the Behavioral Commitment Index (BCI), a conceptual framework designed to decouple prospective memory prerequisites from the underlying dispositional readiness state. By framing agency through a teleological non-tautological structure, the BCI provides a theoretical foundation for credition and offers a diagnostic model for clinical disruptions of volition, such as schizophrenia. Finally, the paper outlines how this theoretical model can be operationalized using a formative, four-domain index to test the temporal stability of commitment as a dispositional state.

papers.title: The External Prefrontal Cortex: An Autoethnography of AI-Coupled Cognitive Prosthesis in Twice-Exceptional (2E) Software Architecture
papers.authors: Chen Jiang
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Replication Package and Benchmark Telemetric Dataset for Paper 5:"The External Prefrontal Cortex: An Autoethnography of AI-Coupled Cognitive Prosthesis in Twice-Exceptional (2E) Software Architecture" Overview:This repository provides the complete telemetric dataset, micro-probes, and empirical verification pipeline for Paper 5. The study investigates how an externalized agentic AI coding environment functions as a cognitive prosthesis for a twice-exceptional (2E) software architect across a 5-month longitudinal autoethnographic deployment. Key Dataset & Empirical Highlights:1. 503 Native Marathon Sessions: 571.9 MB longitudinal JSONL telemetric logs captured during real-world architecture design and implementation.2. Dual-Track Interactions: 8,193 human steering prompts and 76,512 autonomous agent tool executions.3. Mathematical Conservation: Strict 24-hour diurnal bin distribution (peak at 21:00-02:59 with 44.4% focus, absolute biological nadir at 05:00 with 0%) and Friday trough (11.7%).4. Deceptive Technical Debt Confrontation: 65 purified behavioral confrontations against LLM pseudo-refactoring and mock fallbacks.5. 7-Act Dialectical Sparring Transcript: Complete 5,041-line qualitative sparring transcripts with full English alignment. Quick Start:Run "python run_replication.py" in the root directory to verify all mathematical conservation invariants and generate the full compliance report.

papers.title: DIGITAL PEDAGOGY IN HIGHER EDUCATION: DEVELOPING 21ST-CENTURY CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS
papers.authors: Abdusalomova Barchinoy Jo'rabek qizi, Xudoyqulov Abdulla Eshquvvatovich
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Digital pedagogy has become an essential component of higher education, offering new opportunities to develop students’ critical thinking, analytical reasoning, problem-solving, and independent learning skills. This article examines how digital learning environments and technology-enhanced teaching strategies can support the development of critical thinking among university students. Particular attention is given to blended learning, problem-based learning, collaborative digital platforms, and artificial intelligence. The discussion draws on existing research and identifies practical approaches for integrating digital tools into higher education. The article argues that technology alone does not guarantee improved learning outcomes; effective digital pedagogy requires purposeful instructional design, active student participation, and continuous feedback.

papers.title: Who sells AI training data: a census of vendors, what they say they sell, and where their data comes from
papers.authors: Yuma Heymans
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Firms that sell training data, expert labour, reinforcement-learning (RL) environments and evaluations to AI developers are mostly private and known largely through their own websites. This paper reports a census of 150 such vendors, read on their sites on 15 and 16 October 2026 with every claim tied to a quoted sentence, and links it to three companion tables: 37 organisations that publish a way to sell them data, 227 revenue records and 111 funding records. Evaluations are the most common offering (122 vendors, 81.3%), followed by datasets (104), RL environments (89), expert and human data (83) and annotation (57). Vendors bundle: the median vendor lists three of six kinds, and 79 of the 89 RL-environment sellers also sell evaluations. Most data are made to order: 90 vendors cite experts and contractors, 41 recordings, 30 generation and 15 software replicas, against 17 that license data from its owners and 22 that use the client's own data; 19 do not say. Of the 37 buyers, 24 take company records; among those that publish them, the median floor is $100,000 and the median ceiling $1 million per seller. Revenue disclosure runs from audited filings of four listed vendors to self-reported run rates, and 61 funding rounds with a disclosed amount total $4.30 billion. We describe the method, the classification and the limits of a self-description census. Keywords: AI training data; data vendors; data annotation; reinforcement learning environments; model evaluation; data markets; company data; market census Use of AI: this paper was prepared with generative AI tools, which compiled and analysed the open datasets and drafted the text. papers.title: AI data licensing deals, July 2023 to October 2026: a public dataset and what it shows
papers.authors: Yuma Heymans
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Licences of content to developers of artificial intelligence (AI) are negotiated privately and recorded in no registry; what is known comes from announcements, securities filings and press reports. This paper describes an open dataset that compiles those disclosures, with a source link, date and verbatim quote for every row, and reports what it shows. The version analysed here (reviewed 17 October 2026) holds 111 records dated 11 July 2023 to 15 October 2026. It names 24 licensees; OpenAI appears in 29 records, Meta in 14 and Google in 12. News publishers are the licensor in 52 records (46.8%) and music companies in 18. The use licensed shifted: 66.7% of 2024 records include training, against 36.1% in 2025 and 44.7% in 2026 to date, while licences to show content in AI answers became the most common news arrangement. Disclosure of money is sparse and skewed. Nineteen records (17.1%) carry a dollar figure, but only 11 of the 89 records that describe a specific licence do, and 7 of those 11 rest on press reports citing unnamed people. No music licence in the table has a stated amount. A contract term is stated in 7 records. We describe the fields, collection and dating rules, versioning and verification, and the disclosure and survivorship biases that limit inference. The dataset is released under CC BY 4.0, with a snapshot on Zenodo. Keywords: AI training data; content licensing; data licensing; generative AI; disclosure bias; news publishers; music licensing; open dataset Use of AI: this paper was prepared with generative AI tools, which compiled and analysed the open datasets and drafted the text. papers.title: What AI training data sells for: a sourced index of public prices, 2023 to 2026
papers.authors: Yuma Heymans
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Training data for machine learning is bought and sold without an exchange or a posted price list. This paper assembles the public record of its prices: 1,022 observations for nine kinds of data, read from 735 source documents between 11 and 17 October 2026, 1,009 of them dated 2023 or later. Each observation keeps the figure as published, the side of the market where the money moves (paid to makers, offered to holders, asking price, made to order, completed sale, cost to produce) and a conversion to a common unit by stated arithmetic, with ranges entered as geometric midpoints. Medians in each kind's main unit run from $0.525 per image to $316,228 per company archive, and within a main unit the upper quartile is 2.0 to 37.8 times the lower. The side of the market moves prices as much as the kind of data does. For agent-training tasks, the median price buyers pay for collection to order is 9.5 times the median paid to the people who make them. For company records, the median published offer to holders is 11.2 times the median of the four completed sales with a stated amount. Completed sales are 73 of the 1,022 observations, and only 11 observations come from court filings. We describe the disclosure, promotion, concentration and survivorship biases of a public-record compilation and state the method so that every figure can be recomputed.
