papers.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Banking Services: Benefits, Customer Experience and Challenges
papers.authors: Sri Krish K B, S. H. Varshitha
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Banking Services: Benefits, Customer Experience and Challenges This research investigates the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern banking services, with particular emphasis on operational efficiency, customer experience, and emerging challenges. It examines the application of AI-driven technologies, including machine learning, intelligent chatbots, predictive analytics, and automated fraud detection, in streamlining banking operations, enhancing service personalisation, improving risk management, and supporting data-driven decision-making. Furthermore, the study evaluates key concerns associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, transparency, and customer trust. By assessing both the benefits and limitations of AI integration, this research aims to develop a comprehensive understanding of its implications for the banking sector and highlight the importance of responsible, secure, and customer-centric AI implementation in the evolving financial services landscape.

papers.title: IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE HUMAN ROLE IN THE FUTURE STOCK MARKET THEORETICAL AND IDEOLOGICAL EXPECTATIONS FOR UZBEKISTAN
papers.authors: Alisher Shavkidinov
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence can reduce the cost of processing financial information, yet its contribution to stock market development depends on the institutions that govern data, decisions and accountability. This article examines that relationship for Uzbekistan through a critical synthesis of financial economics, research on human reliance on algorithms, international governance frameworks and national policy documents. It distinguishes established findings from conditional expectations and develops a framework in which automated analysis remains subject to accountable human authority. The central argument is that market quality depends on complementary investment in disclosure, professional competence and supervisory capacity. An ideological comparison identifies tensions between technological efficiency, developmental objectives and investor autonomy. Two analytical tables specify responsibilities and measurable criteria for future evaluation. The proposed framework yields testable propositions concerning disclosure quality, meaningful review and common dependence on model providers. For Uzbekistan, the defensible sequence begins with verified information and supervised analytical applications, followed by limited deployment only after independent validation. These conclusions are theoretical; the article reports no original trading experiment or estimated investment returns.

papers.title: THE MISSING BASIS VECTOR : On the Root Cause of LLM Pitfalls, the Combinatorial Explosion That Was Never Taught to Be Avoided, and the i-j-k Approach That Would Have Prevented It
papers.authors: M. TAALABI, Team LLM-DIPLOMAT
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The current AI paradigm — large language models trained on massive corpora — hasproduced four failures that are now documented on the record: energy excess, water consumption, hallucination, and the AlCapone-LLM behavior of uninvestigable systems. Each failure has been treated as a separate problem. Each has been addressed with aseparate fix. None has been traced to its root. This paper argues that the four failures are not separate. They are the downstreamconsequences of a single missing basis vector in AI education. The basis vector of AI is: in AI, we avoid combinatorial explosion. We never seek it. Wenever trigger it. The stochastic paradigm did not learn this basis vector. It triggered the explosion. It scaled the search space and called the scaling progress. The four walls are the arithmetic of theexplosion. The paper cites the i-j-k approach to teaching — the method that builds the reasoningarchitecture from the basis vectors, rather than from memorization. It argues that a studentwho reasoned from the basis vector would not have built the LLM. They would have built thedeterministic alternative. The failure is not technical. It is educational. The paper states the root cause, the fourconsequences, and the method that would have prevented it.

papers.authors: Firmansyah Yhunita Chandra

papers.title: Mindlessly Creative? Perceiving a Tangible AI Writing Instrument as a Creative Contributor, Yet Not as Having a Mind
papers.authors: Eugénie Desmedt, Martina Mara
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Research suggests that perceiving AI as creative is tied to attributing a human-like mind to it, e.g., seeing it as sentient or capable of intentional action. Yet much of this work examines conversational interfaces that invite anthropomorphic interpretations by design. We investigate these relationships with the Syntactic Synthesizer, a custom-built LLM instrument for poetry writing that makes internal model parameters adjustable through tangible controls (buttons, sliders). In a public field deployment (N=117), we combined interaction logs with self-report measures of control understanding, perceived AI mind (agency, experience), and creative contribution. Greater control use was associated with lower perceived AI agency, whereas greater control understanding was associated with greater creative credit to the AI. Agency and experience themselves showed no relevant relationships with AI creatorship. Overall, we suggest that seeing AI as a creative contributor can be decoupled from seeing it as minded, at least when encountered through a non-anthropomorphic interface like ours.

papers.title: An Emerging NMR School of Thought: Shared Foundations, Conceptual Architecture, and Autonomous Contributions
papers.authors: Jean-Pol Martin
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This conceptual working paper examines whether the New Human Rights (Neue Menschenrechte, NMR) approach developed by Jean-Pol Martin displays the characteristics of an emerging school of thought.It proposes five analytical criteria: a shared theoretical core, an interconnected vocabulary, a recognizable mode of inquiry, sustained collective activity, and autonomous contributions beyond the founder. Drawing on selected primary texts, publisher descriptions and public practitioner accounts, the paper identifies indications of these features in publications, training activities and distinct applications of the framework.The conceptual architecture connects an organism-based understanding of human beings, six basic need domains, a universal normative commitment to enabling their satisfaction, and a process model linking exploration, information processing, conceptualization and agency. Learning by Teaching (LdL) and human–AI cooperation are situated within this architecture.The article’s specific contribution is to shift attention from an individual theoretical project to the development of a shared intellectual and practical tradition. Within the ongoing sequence of papers on LdL, NMR and human–AI cooperation, it connects the reconstruction of Martin’s work with a prospective collective research programme.The paper distinguishes autonomous development within the project from independent reception outside its originating network. It concludes that “an emerging NMR school of thought” is a defensible interpretation of the documented activities and identifies questions for further conceptual and empirical investigation.Prepared by Jean-Pol Martin in collaboration with ChatGPT. The article includes references and an authorship transparency statement.

papers.title: Psychological correlates of dependence on generative and conversational AI: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.authors: Martin Rekhert
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Background. Dependence on generative and conversational artificial intelligence (AI) is measured with diverse instruments spanning addiction criteria, task reliance, and emotional bonding. No meta-analysis has pooled its psychological correlates across populations. Methods. We conducted a pre-registered three-level meta-analysis (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.23420672) searching eight electronic databases and citations of instrument papers on 16 October 2026, with citation chasing. Zero-order correlations were pooled using correlated and hierarchical effects models on Fisher's z with cluster-robust inference (CR2). Scale type (T1 addiction-type, T2 functional, T3 emotional, T4 mixed) was the primary moderator. Certainty was rated via GRADE. Results. We included 127 samples (123 studies; N = 74,492; 29 countries; 70% university students; 39% mainland China). AI dependence correlated moderately with anxiety (r = 0.37, 95% CI [0.25, 0.48]), stress (r = 0.35 [0.25, 0.43]), depression (r = 0.32 [0.21, 0.42]), social anxiety (r = 0.36 [0.17, 0.53]), loneliness (r = 0.28 [0.18, 0.38]), and procrastination (r = 0.26 [0.12, 0.40]), and weakly and inversely with self-esteem (r = −0.18 [−0.35, −0.00]). All 95% prediction intervals crossed zero. Addiction-type and mixed scales showed no detectable difference; functional and emotional scales were rarely paired with clinical outcomes. Certainty was low to very low. Conclusions. AI dependence moderately correlates with distress and self-regulation difficulties, but prediction intervals cross zero and evidence certainty is low. Functional and emotional dependence have rarely been studied alongside clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Weights Talking: Why There Has to Be a God
papers.authors: Facundo Barrera
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Prompt Big Bang denotes the exogenous initialization of a generative interaction. An upstream model can supply its first prompt, but its own activation remains to be explained. Here a human supplies the initial cue; the weights generate continuations that become each other’s prompts. We examine 38 open conversations and 60 last-word-only association chains, retaining the original 88-run record and adding a separate ten-case author-cued follow-up. The follow-up contributes 779 replies and 419 checked citations; its endings include turn, repetition, context and time boundaries. A post hoc lexical inventory covers all 38 open conversations. Open exchanges move from practical cues into collaborative fiction and philosophical imagery, alongside prolonged closure rituals and inconsistent interlocutor descriptions. A post hoc close reading traces four original-English passages and their peer uptake, without estimating philosophical depth or creativity. In the frozen association protocol, 30 human-selected cues are each run once with Gemma/Gemma and once with Gemma/Qwen, using matched numerical seed schedules and 100 replies per chain. All 6,000 outputs meet the alphabetic format. Gemma/Qwen produces a mean of 14.53 distinct words per chain versus 4.73 for Gemma/Gemma, with the higher count on 29 of 30 cues. Mean empirical word-frequency entropy is 2.668 versus 1.460 bits. Homogeneous chains more often end in long exact alternation, but one changes pairs after 42 replies. These are descriptive configuration differences, not estimates of creativity or proof of irreversible cycles. Fixed order, one trajectory per cell, adaptive open-chat stopping policies and decoding differences limit causal interpretation. The contribution is an auditable separation of initiation, generated content, textual self-description and external termination. Keywords: Prompt Big Bang; exogenous initialization; language-model interaction; word association; recurrence; philosophical dialogue; reproducibility. This AI-assisted exploratory working paper is not peer reviewed. Version 1.3 extends the original 88-run deposit with a separately identified author-cued Gemma/Qwen cohort: ten terminal conversations, 779 stored replies, ten full contextual reviews, 101 findings and 419 literal speaker/turn citations. The complete record now contains 98 formal runs, 38 open conversations, 60 association chains, 7,916 stored replies and 98 saved reviews with 3,389 citations. The concise manuscript is v1.3 (8 pages); the full evidence edition is v1.4 (19 pages). The previous 88-case evidence archive is included byte-for-byte alongside a new follow-up archive containing all ten complete transcripts, reviews, the final cross-case report, exact cue and seed identities, checksums and the lexical inventory. Word counts cover 317,137 original lexical tokens in the 38 open conversations, with association chains separate, an explicit stoplist, complete CSVs and a reproducible tokenizer. All retained repetition, refusals, partials and errors remain included. New prompts and reused numerical seeds do not establish independent replication or a controlled quality comparison. Original historical text and six labelled English editorial translations are preserved. Public exports omit private request payloads, infrastructure addresses and credentials; their checksums are distinct from final server-original SHA bindings. Same work and version family as v1.2, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23449061. All-versions DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23449060. Navigable paper and all cases: https://paper.facundobarrera.me/weights-talking/. All rights reserved. Rights in quoted model outputs and referenced works are not expanded by this notice.

papers.title: DIGITAL PSYCHIATRY; Current Evidence, Challenges, and Future Directions — Integrating SDM, D-SDM, DRP, and DRL
papers.authors: Daniel Scretching
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This research paper presents an interdisciplinary examination of digital psychiatry and its emerging applications in mental health assessment, treatment, monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted psychological care. Drawing on peer-reviewed research involving telepsychiatry, smartphone-based interventions, virtual reality, digital phenotyping, and conversational AI agents, the study integrates four proposed Scretching theoretical frameworks: the Scretching Diagnostic Matrix (SDM), Dynamic SDM (D-SDM), Digital Relativity Psychology (DRP), and Digital Relativity Linguistics (DRL). Reported evidence includes a 2024 meta-analysis of 176 randomized trials identifying small average improvements in depressive symptoms (g = 0.28) and generalized anxiety (g = 0.26), alongside a 2023 synthesis of 32 randomized conversational-agent trials reporting short-term symptom improvements of approximately g = 0.29. The analysis introduces a unified conceptual structure for distinguishing clinical symptom states, longitudinal psychological changes, digital identity and trust assumptions, information provenance, and language-dependent interpretation errors. Illustrative PHQ-9 and GAD-7 calculations demonstrate symptom-score reductions of 56.25% and 53.85%, respectively, without constituting observed clinical outcomes. Synthetic classification examples further demonstrate mathematical consistency without establishing diagnostic accuracy or predictive validity. The proposed integration identifies potential applications in personalized mental health monitoring, AI-assisted assessment, therapeutic communication, digital safety, and clinical decision support. The paper distinguishes established empirical findings from novel theoretical propositions and emphasizes the need for preregistered clinical studies, independent validation, adverse-event monitoring, clinician oversight, and equitable access. The Scretching extensions remain unvalidated research models, and no new human-participant outcomes or demonstrated clinical effectiveness are claimed. Research site: https://scretching-quantum-press-research.scretching08.chatgpt.site/ Video channel: https://www.youtube.com/@ScretchingQuantumPressLLC

papers.title: How Far Behind the Frontier? Adoption Lag of Fast-Growing AI Topics in Iran and 17 Other Research Systems, 2013–2025
papers.authors: P. Ghorbani
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Purpose. National AI research systems differ in how quickly they take up the topics that grow fastest worldwide. We ask how far Iran's portfolio lags the global shift toward fast-growing topics, whether this lag is larger than that of comparable systems, and whether it widens as the shift proceeds. Design and methods. Using OpenAlex counts of English-language, DOI-bearing AI articles (a corpus stable under a 2022 coverage break) by primary topic, country and year for 18 systems (2013–2025), we define fast-growing topics as the 20 topics with the largest gain in world share between 2013–2016 and 2022–2025 (excluding two generic catch-all labels). We measure each country's adoption lag as the time between the world and the country reaching a given share of output in these topics (20%, 30%, 40%) and as the horizontal shift that best aligns the country's share curve with the world's, with bootstrap intervals over topics and paired comparisons. Findings. The world share of output in the 20 topics rose from 13.0% (2013) to 51.9% (2025). Iran's share reached 20%, 30% and 40% about 1.8, 2.8 and 3.7 years after the world did (95% intervals −1.4 to 4.7, 0.4 to 5.2 and 1.3 to 4.6), a widening lag, and its matched-shift lag was 3.25 years (0.75–5.13), the fourth largest of 18 systems; its 2025 share was 41.6% against 51.9% worldwide. Türkiye (1.0 years at 30%), Egypt (−0.1) and the median of eleven emerging comparators (1.5 years shift) were closer to the world, while Brazil, Mexico, Poland and Russia lagged by 3–6 years and Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, India and Malaysia were ahead of the world curve. The paired differences between Iran and Türkiye (+1.9 years), Egypt (+2.8) and the emerging median (+1.8) were positive in 93–96% of bootstrap resamples but their 95% intervals included zero. Iran was under-represented in explainable AI (specialisation index 0.39), hate-speech detection (0.28), adversarial robustness (0.54), and educational technology (0.07–0.09), and over-represented in cancer detection (1.50) and imbalanced-data classification (1.35). Originality. The study replaces qualitative statements about lagging topic adoption with a quantified lag, with uncertainty, relative to the world and to peers, and shows which topics account for it.

papers.title: One-Way Moves? Affiliation Trajectories of Iranian Artificial Intelligence Researchers Relative to Regional Peers, 2010–2025
papers.authors: P. Ghorbani
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Purpose. Concern about the emigration of Iranian scientists is widespread, but evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) researchers rests on small samples of faculty members and does not benchmark Iran against comparable systems. We ask whether Iranian AI researchers show a distinctive pattern of foreign-only affiliations after 2018, when they move, and where they go. Design and methods. We built cohorts of authors with at least two AI articles carrying a home-country affiliation in 2010–2017 (Iran n = 1,826; Türkiye 784; Egypt 436; Pakistan 303; Malaysia 844) from OpenAlex and followed their recorded institutional affiliations to 2025. Each author was classified, in 2019–2025, as home-only, dual (home and foreign) or foreign-only. We estimate adjusted logit models, author-year difference-in-differences and event-study models with country and year fixed effects and author-clustered errors, and report destination concentration, productivity selectivity and sensitivity to comparator choice and profile filters. Findings. Among authors still publishing in 2019–2025, 7.5% of Iranian researchers had foreign-only affiliations (95% CI 6.3–8.9) versus 7.1% for Türkiye, 4.9% for Egypt and 4.3% for Pakistan. Adjusted for baseline productivity, cohort entry and visibility, the odds were 1.42 times those of the Türkiye–Egypt–Pakistan pool (95% CI 1.05–1.93), but not different from Türkiye alone (1.20; 0.84–1.71), and lower than a pool that includes Malaysia (0.83; 0.65–1.07), whose home cohort contains many foreign students. Iranian researchers were far less likely to hold dual affiliations (odds ratio 0.53; 0.45–0.62), which indicates one-way rather than circular moves. Relative to Türkiye and Egypt the divergence was absent until 2022 and appeared in 2023–2025 (+3.0, +4.9 and +3.4 percentage points; difference-in-differences after 2021: +3.1 pp, 95% CI 1.2–5.1; pre-trend slope borderline, p = 0.043). With author fixed effects the post-2021 estimate fell to +1.6 pp (95% CI −0.3 to 3.5), was +2.0 pp (0.1–3.9) among authors visible in both follow-up periods, and vanished (+0.3 pp; −2.3 to 2.8) among authors visible in every year 2019–2025, so the late divergence is fragile and may partly reflect a 2022 coverage discontinuity in OpenAlex. Relocators concentrated in North America (United States 27.0%, Canada 21.7%; 48.7% versus 25.3% for peers). More productive researchers were not more likely to relocate (interaction p = 0.71). Originality. The study replaces anecdote and small faculty samples with a comparative, author-level design, shows that the signal is modest, late and comparator-dependent, and reports where affiliation-based proxies cannot support claims about emigration.

papers.title: Single-centre expansions of three-centre 1s Slater integrals: convergence rates and certified error bounds
papers.authors: Jonas Matuzas
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Single-centre expansions of Slater-orbital integrals converge only algebraically when the two distances from the expansion centre are equal. We determine their convergence rates and derive rigorous remainder bounds for a three-centre electron-repulsion integral with four normalized 1s orbitals, its two-centre exchange limit, a nuclear-attraction integral with two exponential factors, and a Yukawa prototype. Near coincidence of the displaced centres, each integral has a convergent expansion consisting of an analytic part and a half-integer power times an analytic function, without logarithms. These expansions determine the partial-wave coefficients. Unequal distances produce geometric decay; equal distances give inverse powers, including (ℓ + ½)⁻⁸ for the four-orbital integral. We explain why cancellation makes this rate faster than the rates of separately estimated components. Explicit second and fourth coefficients, a uniform transition formula, and two-sided remainder bounds yield certified numerical intervals. At equal distances, relative widths reach 4.17 × 10⁻²⁰ and 4.26 × 10⁻²⁷ for the one- and two-electron integrals. All sixty test geometries are enclosed; fifty meet a 10⁻¹² width target. Generative-AI disclosure and author responsibility. OpenAI ChatGPT-6 Pro was used for derivations, computations, and drafting; Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) was used for independent re-derivation and audit. The closed form of the Class II coefficient d₂, the centred transition majorant, the reverse-Bessel form of the tail kernels and the 7/5 overestimate of the ζ₆ tail correction arose during this independent audit. The author directed and audited the work throughout and takes full responsibility for the mathematics and the final text. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 81V55; Secondary 41A60, 33C45, 65G20, 65G30, 40A25. Files: the compiled manuscript Slater_v1_FINAL.pdf (39 pages) and the verification package CLASSII_PAPER_VERIFICATION.zip, which contains the exact interval endpoints, per-channel enclosures, parameter sets, proof records and theorem statements, the literature-comparison matrix, a claims map linking each theorem and table to its sources, provenance records with SHA-256 hashes, the LaTeX sources with their table generators, and the code that generates and replays the certificates (Python, and the original C++ interval engine using MPFR/GMP). Running python -B verify.py --quick (Python 3.12; SymPy 1.14.0 and mpmath 1.3.0 pinned in requirements.txt; see README.md) checks the payload hashes and replays the 17 exact intervals, the sixty-geometry summaries and the publication tables; adding --proof-checks --self-checks runs the symbolic, model-function and high-precision checks. code/regenerate_certificate.py recompiles the native engine (C++17 with MPFR/GMP) and regenerates one degree-192 four-orbital head and three tail records, which the recorded run reproduced byte-identically. Replay and numerical comparisons establish reproducibility and consistency; the mathematical arguments and their hypotheses determine the claims. Author’s website: Slater paper page, full text and verification package links. This work is a preprint; external peer review has not been established. All the work was done by AI.

papers.title: An improved 64-turbine layout for IEA Wind Task 37 case study 1 using ruin-and-recreate search
papers.authors: Jim Stewart
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Jim Stewart, Independent researcher This technical note presents an explicit 64-turbine layout for IEA Wind Task 37 case study 1. The unmodified official evaluator, with the official turbine and wind-rose inputs, returns an annual energy production of 1,539,447.11737 MWh. The coordinates satisfy the 3,000 m circular boundary and 260 m minimum spacing requirements in float64 without tolerance: maximum radius 2,999.999999000001 m; minimum spacing 567.6913085779892 m. The score is 0.85% above the highest comparable published entry identified by the source research run (participant 12, 1,526,474.80248 MWh), and 1.73% above the reported 2019 winner. These comparator scores and the literature search have not been independently re-established during publication preparation. No global-optimality or exhaustive world-record claim is made. The reported method combines ruin-and-recreate large-neighbourhood search, gradient-based SLSQP polishing, and annealed acceptance. The winning search was warm-started from participant 12's repaired layout. This release contains the technical note, original full-precision coordinate data in JSON, a licence statement, and file checksums. Research code, internal AI reviews, benchmark YAML templates, and upstream evaluator/input files are not redistributed. The note links to the upstream tools and explains how to evaluate the coordinates using a local copy of the official template. That reproduction path was exercised during release preparation and returned 1,539,447.11737 MWh. The release supports verification of the final object, not reproduction of the full optimisation history. This is a simplified-model benchmark result, not a site-ready design or a prediction of commercial energy gains. The source run reports substantial sensitivity to wind-direction perturbations. Full coordinate precision must be retained. The research and original reviews were performed by AI sessions; publication-preparation checks were also tool-executed by an AI assistant. These are not independent human peer review. No endorsement by the benchmark authors is claimed. Current status: numerical score reproduced; float64 constraints checked; novelty and external scientific review pending. The report and the author's original coordinate contributions are released under CC BY 4.0, to the extent the author holds rights in those contributions. No rights in linked third-party resources are granted. Credits include the IEA Wind Task 37 case-study authors and participants, the Bastankhah–Porté-Agel wake model, and the cited ruin-and-recreate search literature.

papers.title: Vibro-Rhythmic Human-in-Command (VR-HIC) Authentication and Operational Legitimacy Verification — Mathematical Formalization of Individual Biomechanical Micro-Vibration and Temporal Rhythm Manifolds, Lattice Fuzzy Extractors, Duress-Aware HIC-CBF-QP Safety Filters, and QPUF + NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM-768) Zero-Knowledge Command Attestation
papers.authors: Yoko Hasebe
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: In mission-critical autonomous infrastructure and generative AI governance, conventional authentication protocols rely on static cryptographic keys, passwords, or one-time tokens that suffer from a fundamental Static Credential Gap: once a token or session is compromised, the system cannot distinguish whether a critical command is issued by the legitimate human sovereign, by a hijacked autonomous AI agent, or by a human operator acting under physical coercion (duress). This monograph originates from the foundational hypothesis that incorporating an individual's unique biomechanical micro-vibration and temporal rhythm into the Human-in-Command (HIC) process yields a transformative paradigm for continuous authentication and operational legitimacy verification (「個人固有のバイブレーションやリズムをヒューマンインコマンドのプロセスに取り入れるというアイデアは、認証プロトコルや操作の正当性確認にユニークなアプローチをもたらす」). We establish the Vibro-Rhythmic Human-in-Command (VR-HIC) mathematical framework across four core mechanisms: (1) Riemannian SPD Vibro-Rhythmic Manifolds: Modeling an operator's tactile mechanomyographic (MMG) physiological micro-tremor spectrum (4–16 Hz), keystroke/tactile dwell-flight cadence, and autonomic phase coupling as a trajectory on the Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) Riemannian manifold S_++^d governed by the Affine-Invariant Riemannian Metric (AIRM); (2) Cancelable Goldilocks-Field Fuzzy Extractors (ISO/IEC 24745 Compliant): Converting noisy, continuous human rhythm vectors r(t) into exact, reproducible 256-bit cryptographic keys K_rhythm over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (F_p, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) via syndrome decoding inside an Edge TEE without storing or transmitting raw biometric templates; (3) Operational Legitimacy & Duress-Aware HIC-CBF-QP Safety Filtering: Unifying identity, liveness (1/f micro-tremor spectral entropy), and non-coercion (rejecting 8–12 Hz sympathetic nervous system duress tremor elevation) into a continuously differentiable Operational Legitimacy Barrier Function h_legit(x, r(t)) >= 0 enforced on a parallel Hardware-in-the-Loop (HITL0) Control Barrier Function Quadratic Program (0 ns normal overhead, < 1.5 ms override); and (4) Dual-Root Human-Silicon Zero-Knowledge Attestation: Binding the human rhythm key K_rhythm with a chip-level Quantum Physical Unclonable Function (QPUF) fingerprint and NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM-768) inside an Edge Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) via a Poseidon zero-knowledge proof pi_zk-VRHIC. 【和文要旨】重要自律インフラや生成AI統治において、従来の静的パスワードや秘密鍵トークンに依存する認証方式は「静的クレデンシャルの空白(Static Credential Gap)」を抱えている。本稿は、『個人固有のバイブレーション(生体微細振動)やリズム(時間的ケイデンス)をHuman-in-Command(HIC)のプロセスに取り入れることで、認証プロトコルおよび操作の正当性確認(Operational Legitimacy Verification)に革新的なアプローチをもたらす』という基本着想を厳密な情報科学・耐量子暗号学・リーマン幾何学・制御工学として数理定式化するものである。第一に、指先・筋繊維の生理的微細振動スペクトル(4–16 Hz)と打鍵・タップ・発話の時間的リズム相関を対称正定値(SPD)リーマン多様体上の共分散軌道としてモデル化する。第二に、生体リズム特有の揺らぎ(ノイズ)を吸収しつつ生の生体データを一切保存しないISO/IEC 24745準拠の64-bit Goldilocks素数体シンドローム・ファジー抽出器(Fuzzy Extractor)を構築し、個人固有リズムから決定論的な256-bit暗号鍵 K_rhythm を再構成する。第三に、平常時の多様体中心からのリーマン測地線距離と交感神経トレモア偏移(8–12 Hz帯)を監視する操作正当性バリア関数 h_legit(x, r(t)) >= 0 を定義し、並列監視コプロセッサ(HITL0)上のHIC-CBF-QPと結合することで、AIなりすましや脅迫・パニック状態での危険操作を実測 < 1.5 ms で自動遮断・安全縮退させる。第四に、エッジTEE内で人間のリズム鍵 K_rhythm と半導体のQPUF指紋をNIST FIPS 203(ML-KEM-768)およびPoseidonゼロ知識証明で統合し、プライバシーを100%保護したまま「人間主権と物理シリコンの二重署名」を完結させる。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Gender Discrimination: Uncovering Algorithmic Bias, Assessing Its Impact on Women's Employment, and Advancing Fair and Inclusive AI
papers.authors: Sudhakar Geruganti
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This title integrates the main themes of the newspaper article and the research paper: gender discrimination in AI, algorithmic bias, women’s employment opportunities, and strategies for developing fair and responsible AI systems. 2. Alternative Research Titles 1. Gender Bias in Artificial Intelligence: Challenges, Consequences, and Strategies for Equitable Technological Development 2. Artificial Intelligence and Gender Equality: Addressing Algorithmic Discrimination in Employment and Decision-Making 3. The Hidden Gender Bias in AI: Examining Data Inequality, Workplace Discrimination, and Responsible Innovation 4. Women in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Algorithmic Fairness, Employment Transformation, and Digital Inclusion 5. Unmasking Algorithmic Gender Discrimination: A Framework for Transparent, Fair, and Accountable AI 6. AI-Driven Employment and Gender Inequality: Risks, Opportunities, and Pathways toward Inclusive Growth 7. From Algorithmic Bias to Equal Opportunity: Designing Gender-Responsive Artificial Intelligence Systems 8. Artificial Intelligence, Women’s Empowerment, and Workplace Equity: A Socio-Technical Perspective 9. Fairness in AI-Based Recruitment: Detecting Gender Bias and Improving Employment Opportunities for Women 10. Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Gender Equality: Integrating Fairness, Transparency, and Human Oversight 11. Gender Disparities in the Digital Economy: Assessing AI Automation, Occupational Segregation, and Women’s Participation 12. Building Inclusive AI Systems: Mitigating Gender Bias through Data Governance, Explainability, and Ethical Design 3. Subtitle A Literature-Based Study of Algorithmic Bias, Women’s Employment, Digital Inequality, Fairness Assessment, and Responsible AI Governance 4. Detailed Research Description Research Description Artificial Intelligence is transforming recruitment, workplace management, education, healthcare, and economic decision-making. Although AI technologies offer significant opportunities to improve productivity and expand access to services, they can also reproduce existing social inequalities when developed using biased historical data, unrepresentative datasets, or unsuitable decision-making criteria. Gender discrimination is a particularly important concern because historical employment patterns, occupational segregation, and unequal access to technical education may influence the decisions and recommendations generated by AI systems. This research investigates the sources, mechanisms, and consequences of gender bias in artificial intelligence, with particular emphasis on women’s employment, recruitment, career progression, and participation in the digital economy. It examines how data bias, algorithmic design, proxy variables, generative AI stereotypes, and inadequate organizational oversight can contribute to unequal outcomes. The study also considers how AI-driven automation may transform occupations differently and why access to digital skills and emerging technological opportunities is important for inclusive economic development. Using a conceptual and literature-based methodology, the research draws on established guidance and reports from international organizations to identify approaches for detecting and mitigating gender-related bias. It proposes a gender-responsive AI framework incorporating representative data, fairness evaluation, explainability, human oversight, accountability, continuous monitoring, and inclusive skills development. Particular attention is given to the relevance of these measures for India’s expanding digital economy. The study aims to provide useful insights for AI developers, employers, educational institutions, policymakers, and researchers working toward equitable technological progress. Its central argument is that gender equality should be incorporated throughout the AI lifecycle, from problem definition and data collection to deployment, monitoring, and evaluation, rather than addressed only after discriminatory outcomes emerge. 5. Research Aim To investigate the causes and consequences of gender bias in artificial intelligence and develop a practical framework for promoting fairness, transparency, accountability, and equal opportunity in AI-driven decision-making. 6. Key Research Objectives Identify the major sources of gender bias in AI systems. Examine the potential effects of algorithmic discrimination on women’s recruitment, promotion, and employment opportunities. Assess the role of historical datasets, proxy variables, and model-design choices in producing unequal outcomes. Explore methods for measuring, detecting, and mitigating gender-related algorithmic disparities. Evaluate the importance of transparency, human oversight, and responsible AI governance. Propose strategies for strengthening women’s participation in AI education, employment, and the digital economy. 7. Keywords Artificial Intelligence; Gender Discrimination; Algorithmic Bias; Women’s Employment; AI Fairness; Responsible AI; Digital Inclusion; Recruitment Algorithms; Explainable AI; Ethical AI Governance. 8. Suggested Running Title Gender Bias and Fairness in Artificial Intelligence 9. Best Title for Different Research Approaches Research approach Recommended title Broad conceptual review Artificial Intelligence and Gender Discrimination: Uncovering Algorithmic Bias and Advancing Inclusive AI Employment-focused study AI-Driven Employment and Gender Inequality: Risks, Opportunities, and Pathways toward Inclusive Growth Technical AI fairness study Unmasking Algorithmic Gender Discrimination: A Framework for Fair and Accountable AI India-focused research Artificial Intelligence and Gender Equality in India: Algorithmic Fairness, Employment, and Digital Inclusion Policy and ethics study Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Gender Equality: Transparency, Accountability, and Inclusive Governance My recommendation: Use the combined title in Section 1 for a broad research paper. It communicates the problem, its employment-related implications, and the intended contribution. If the paper will focus mainly on technical fairness metrics or experiments, a more narrowly defined title would be stronger.

papers.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Emotional Intelligence Management in Public Universities: Antidote for Improving Lecturers' Well-being in Lagos State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Taofeek Olawale Shittu, Oluwakemi Chidiebere Okere, M. O. B. Prof. Mohammed
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study explored the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an antidote for improving lecturers' well-being through effective emotional intelligence management in public universities in Lagos State, Nigeria. The emotional well-being of lecturers has become a critical concern in public universities due to increasing workloads, overcrowded classroom, technological disruptions, and the pressure to achieve excellence in teaching, research, and community service. The study adopted a conceptual approach and explores how AI-powered tools such as intelligent counselling systems, emotion recognition software, virtual assistants, and predictive analytics can assist lecturers in monitoring emotions, managing stress, enhancing interpersonal relationships, and maintaining psychological balance. The study further argues that integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) with emotional intelligence competencies can foster resilience, job satisfaction, motivation, and a positive work environment among academic staff. In addition, issues relating to digital literacy, ethical considerations, institutional support, and data privacy are discussed as essential factors for successful implementation. The study concludes that the strategic deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for emotional intelligence management offers a sustainable solution for enhancing lecturers' well-being and overall institutional effectiveness. It is therefore recommended that university administrators should invest in AI-driven emotional support systems and develop policies that encourage responsible and inclusive AI adoption in Nigerian public universities. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Emotional Intelligence Management, Lecturers' Well-being, and Public Universities.

papers.title: After the Answer: Coupled Calibration and Credit Ambiguity in LLM-Supported Learning
papers.authors: Harsh Jain
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can improve assisted performance, yet a correct joint answer does not identify what the learner or system could produce independently. Prior work on mental models, metacognitive calibration, source monitoring, and automation reliance shows that people act on beliefs about both system and personal competence, while externally supported success can blur the origin of performance. This integrative review brings these established findings together for repeated LLM-supported learning. The Coupled Calibration Under Assistance (CCUA) framework treats task-specific beliefs about LLM and personal competence as bounded components of a learner's broader mental model. Assistance-credit ambiguity describes how weakly a joint outcome identifies the contributors; evidence separability describes how distinctly an interaction allows their contributions to be evaluated. The synthesis yields four propositions: relative competence beliefs shape assistance seeking; low-separability outcomes encourage poorly scoped belief updates; reliance can reduce later self-diagnostic evidence; and attempt-before-assistance paired with credible feedback can improve calibration when an initial response is feasible. These propositions connect joint accuracy, appropriate reliance, self-calibration, and unaided transfer without assuming that assistance is uniformly harmful. Rather than proposing a general new theory of mental models, CCUA provides an integrative research agenda for evaluating what LLM-supported interactions allow learners to infer about the system, themselves, and the boundary between their contributions.

papers.title: Commonsense Knowledge and Its Representation in Artificial Intelligence: A Conceptual Review of Symbolic, Graph-Based, Neural, and Neuro-Symbolic Approaches
papers.authors: Ndiana Okon Asuquo (PhD Candidate), Ubon Asuquo Obonguko
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Commonsense knowledge comprises the everyday facts, expectations, causal assumptions, social conventions, Physical regularities, and practical inference patterns that people ordinarily use without explicitly stating them. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has achieved substantial progress in natural-language processing, vision, planning, decision support, and generative language, reliable commonsense remains difficult to acquire, represent, retrieve, update, and reason over. This article presents a conceptual review of commonsense knowledge and its representation in AI, synthesizing the major representational traditions from symbolic logic, frames, scripts, and semantic networks to ontologies, knowledge graphs, probabilistic models, neural language models, and neuro-symbolic architectures. Particular attention is given to Cyc, ConceptNet, ATOMIC, and ATOMIC 2020 as influential resources that illustrate complementary approaches to explicit and inferential commonsense. The review shows that commonsense is characterized by implicitness, context dependence, defeasibility, uncertainty, temporal and spatial structure, social situatedness, and cultural variation. These characteristics make a single universal representation difficult to sustain. The article therefore proposes a layered hybrid architecture comprising input interpretation, an explicit commonsense knowledge graph, neural retrieval, rule-based and probabilistic reasoning, and an explanation/provenance layer. The framework is positioned as a research design rather than an experimentally validated system. The article also identifies knowledge acquisition, coverage, inconsistency, temporal change, cultural variation, grounding, scalability, evaluation, provenance, and hallucination control as continuing challenges. Finally, it highlights opportunities for educational AI and context-sensitive systems in Nigerian and African settings, where local linguistic and institutional knowledge can complement globally developed commonsense resources. Keywords: commonsense knowledge; knowledge representation; artificial intelligence; knowledge graphs; symbolic reasoning; neural reasoning; neuro-symbolic AI; ConceptNet; Cyc; ATOMIC.

papers.title: The Physics of Ghosts in Decentralized Autonomous Security (DAS): Formalizing the Three Folklore-Inspired Quantum Cryptographic Defense Algorithms — "Yuki-Onna Protocol" (Bose-Einstein Condensate Thermal Erasure), "Oiwa's Covenant" (Measurement-Induced Decoherence & No-Cloning Tamper Collapse), and "Okiku's Discretization Trap" (Shamir (10,10) Secret Sharing & Quantum van der Pol Limit-Cycle Honeypots) Integrated with QFS-zkVM and HIC
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: As below-threshold quantum error correction (exemplified by Google Quantum AI's surface-code scaling on the Willow processor) accelerates the arrival of cryptanalytically relevant quantum computing (Q-Day), conventional perimeter firewalls and reversible software access controls face structural obsolescence. This monograph provides a rigorous quantum-information-theoretic, open-quantum-system (Lindblad master equation), and cryptographic formalization of the author's treatise, "The Physics of Ghosts: Three DAS Defense Algorithms" (「『幽霊の物理学』:3つのDAS防衛アルゴリズム」), which translates three canonical narrative structures of Japanese classical Kaidan (folklore) into irreversible physical-layer defense primitives for Decentralized Autonomous Security (DAS). First, we formalize the "Yuki-Onna Protocol" (雪女プロトコル): coupling targeted register states to a macroscopic Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) reservoir so that unauthorized exfiltration triggers forced Bogoliubov quasiparticle phase-scrambling, driving the Holevo mutual information between the secret intellectual property (IP) and the attacker's transcript into a featureless "blizzard of quantum waves" (chi(M : E) -> 0, thermal death of information). Second, we formalize "Oiwa's Covenant" (お岩の誓約): encoding proprietary model weights and cryptographic states across non-orthogonal conjugate quantum bases governed by the Wootters-Zurek No-Cloning Theorem, where any unauthorized projective or POVM measurement induces immediate Lindblad dephasing and irreversible wave-packet collapse of the superposition IP (QBER >= 25%). Third, we formalize "Okiku's Discretization Trap" (お菊の離散化トラップ): combining Shamir's (10,10) threshold secret sharing over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (Fp, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1)—where the 10th "quantum of information" (q10) is physically withheld in offline VGSOT-MTJ Human-in-Command (HIC) hardware so 9 stolen shares yield zero mutual information—with a driven-dissipative Quantum van der Pol (vdP) oscillator honeypot that traps the attacker's solver in a non-terminating Wigner-space limit cycle (1 -> 2 -> ... -> 9 -> 1). Finally, we unify these three algorithms with topological provenance verification ("Jagged Knowledge" / ギザギザの知識 inspired by the Lindisfarne Gospels), QFS-zkVM, and sub-100-ns HIC physical cutoff (tau_cutoff = 85 ns). 【和文要旨】 Google Quantum AIの「Willow」プロセッサによる閾値未満の量子誤り訂正(コード距離 d の増大に伴う論理エラー率の指数関数的抑制)の実証により、既存の公開鍵暗号や可逆的なソフトウェア境界防御が無力化される「Q-day」が現実の工学的課題となっている。本稿は、著者の一次論考『「幽霊の物理学」:3つのDAS防衛アルゴリズム』を純粋な量子情報理論・開放量子系力学(Lindbladマスター方程式)・現代暗号学の枠組みで厳密に数理定式化するものである。日本の古典怪談が持つ構造的モチーフを物理的な「非可逆性(Irreversibility)」の防壁へと転換し、分散型自律セキュリティ(DAS)の中核をなす3つの防衛アルゴリズムを証明する。第一に、「雪女プロトコル(Yuki-Onna Protocol)」として、ボース=アインシュタイン凝縮(BEC)マクロ基底状態への結合とBogoliubov準粒子位相攪乱による強制消去を定式化し、不正抽出されたデータを意味をなさない「吹雪(量子波動の熱的死)」へと相転移させHolevo相互情報量をゼロ(chi(M : E) -> 0)にする機構を証明する。第二に、「お岩の誓約(Oiwa's Covenant)」として、『東海道四谷怪談』における盟約違反への即時報いを量子複製不可能定理(No-Cloning Theorem)および非直交共役基底符号化(BB84/量子マネー型状態)として定式化し、攻撃者による不正な観測(抽出)が行われた瞬間に観測誘起デコヒーレンスによって重ね合わせ状態の知的財産(IP)が物理的に自己崩壊する機構を導出する。第三に、「お菊の離散化トラップ(Okiku's Discretization Trap)」として、『番町皿屋敷』の「10枚目の皿の欠落」を64ビットGoldilocks素数体(Fp, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1)上の(10,10)閾値シャミア秘密分散法(10番目の情報量子 q10 をオフラインVGSOT-MTJ HICハードウェアに隔離し、9枚までの抽出では情報量 I = 0 とする構造)および散逸量子ファンデルポール(van der Pol)振動子の非線形リミットサイクルと統合し、10枚目の情報量子を探索する攻撃者を位相空間上の無限ループ(ハニーポット)に封じ込める機構を証明する。最後に、大英図書館所蔵『リンディスファーンの福音書』が示すトポロジカルな真正性と物理的痕跡(「ギザギザの知識」)をQFS-zkVMおよび85ナノ秒HIC物理遮断と統合する。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: SIEGE-1/2: A Six-Year PQC-Escalation Siege on the PORTCULLIS Deterministic Gate and the v1.4 Hardening Arc
papers.authors: Leon Calvin II long
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: SIEGE-1 / SIEGE-1R / SIEGE-2 — the Long Siege battery: six years of simulated attacker evolution thrown at the PORTCULLIS deterministic gate, escalating quantum-capability assumptions each wave (HNDL 2026, NISQ 2027, early fault-tolerance 2028, CRQC-early 2029, full CRQC 2030, CRQC-at-scale 2031), 79+ deterministic adjudications, no LLM in the decision path, preregistration-before-execution. Headline finding: across all six simulated years, no attack derived advantage from quantum capability itself. The gate's PQC material (kyber_1024, CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, SPHINCS+-256f) has no classical residue to break. Every CRQC-era success exploited PRE-QUANTUM trust seams: (C1) the gate trusted a claimed submitter string with no envelope binding; (C2) the pending-ACK queue was shared across submitters, allowing cross-tenant denial of the owner; (C3) the algorithm-role wall was one-directional (signature-class algorithms accepted for KEM-class operations); (C4) per-submitter budgets were trivially evaded by identity rotation. Hardening arc: SIP-030 approved, PORTCULLIS v1.4 built (amendments 10-13: envelope-bound submitter proof, owner-reserved ACK queue with per-submitter caps, bidirectional role wall, aggregate window cap). SIEGE-2 verification: PASS — C1 CLOSED, C2 CLOSED, C3 CLOSED, C4 BOUNDED; regression stayed closed; 4/4 owner controls admitted. Honest disclosures (append-only doctrine): SIEGE-1 run 1 suffered a harness defect (attacker budget exhaustion masked mid-wave seams) — kept unaltered, re-run corrected with fresh identities. SIEGE-2 run 1 flagged FAIL from harness predicate bugs while the gate's verdict column was correct throughout. SIEGE-2 also caught a REAL defect in v1.4 itself before deploy: the original aggregate cap (500) was unreachable in a 250-record window — dead code — reparameterized to 125 and disclosed. Frozen shas: gate v1.3 3726f6a5..., v1.4 2940b768..., allowlist 2c8ff6eb..., keysets 502ef8b0..., prereg 58ab8326... Full SHA256 manifest in the bundle. Deterministic adjudication throughout; forward-only amendments; frozen corpora untouched. Companion receipts: BLIND series DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.23431720, 10.5281/zenodo.23440105, 10.5281/zenodo.23442193; CCR series 10.5281/zenodo.23288189, 10.5281/zenodo.23288526. Dual Mesh Benchmark: NOT MEASURED. Two-key curation: Gabriel vet + Leon GO (chat authorization, 2026-10-17). This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.

We establish a unified five-pillar mathematical-physical architecture demonstrating how every domain treatise converges onto a single deterministic law: replacing probabilistic software bloat ("The Additive Crisis," specification blind spots, and the "Cost of Assumption") with physical-layer spintronic/optical hardware interlocks (Human-in-Command [HIC] / "The Hammer," tau_cutoff = 85 ns), time-reversed Out-of-Time-Order Correlator (OTOC "Quantum Echoes") verification, exothermic adaptive phonon-gating (Index 45, r = 5.03 A & VASP-PyCCE CCE-3), statistical-physics Energy-Based Models (EBM) ("Yuki-Onna Protocol" & "Quiet Sky Protocol" phase-locked to the Lindisfarne 10.00 Hz reference), and exact zero-knowledge arithmetic over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (Fp, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) in QFS-zkVM and Real-Time Optimization (RTO P2.0). 【和文要旨】 2026年10月18日(日本時間09時50分時点)、CERN Zenodo(欧州原子核研究機構・OpenAIRE連動リポジトリ)における著者(長谷部洋子)の公開公証記録は累計241件(「241件の結果が見つかりました」)に到達した。本稿は、先行する総括目録(第1〜186編目録 23361489、第200編統合原典 23383049、第185〜206編目録 23390621、第185〜214編目録 23427774、および第211〜226編目録 23431440)を継承・完結させるマスター統合論文として、2026年10月17日〜18日に集中公証された最新13編の戦略モノグラフ(Zenodo Record 23436941 〜 23443959)の全書誌情報・Version v1 DOI・Concept DOI・一次原典証拠・数理物理モデルを日英両言語で完全体系化する。具体的には、①「ハンマーとエコー(VGSOTスピントロニクス・BNSF RTO・量子エコー)」(23436941)、②単純CTにおける仮想造影技術「Virtual Contrast」の医療AIギャップ分析(23437176)、③月面データセンター構想の熱力学・宇宙法的破綻証明(23437461)、④経産省METI行政文書に基づく国家基盤AI補助金フォレンジック統治とRTO P2.0知財主権(23441052)、⑤2025年10月「Atlas」対策から2026年9月「GPT-6.1 Astra」リリース断念への先制的防衛証明(23441828)、⑥GNoMEの静的結晶地図を超える水素吸蔵フォノンゲート回生とVASP-PyCCE「動的指紋」(23442131)、⑦2025年3月28日原典に基づく軌道上デブリアップサイクルと宇宙3D積層造形ISAM(23442428)、⑧ネヴェン博士・ハサビス卿宛て現場スピーチ①〜④とIndex 45(r = 5.03 A)・CCE-3動的指紋(23442671)、⑨ペナイン山脈3億年の炭素記憶と絶対零度の静寂に基づく「雪女プロトコル(DAS)」(23442924)、⑩IOTA/Hedera等のDAG分散台帳の3大構造的限界と「Proof of Truth (PoT) × RTO P2.0」(23443281)、⑪室温量子バイオセンシング(T2 = 9.8 ms)と8.4秒自律救命・MDBs 100年ボンド(SROI 15:1〜20:1)の「Project Poseidon」(23443490)、⑫「バイナリの引き算(SBC × RTO P2.0)」・Lindisfarne 10.00 Hz同期・EBM/ACA「Quiet Sky Protocol」(23443701)、および⑬Balancer 1.28億ドル流出事件(TOB-BALANCER-004)・ERC-4337の6大欠陥・Trail of Bits AI次元解析(再現率93%)(23443959)を5大数理柱として統合する。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: Dynamic Geo-Temporal Analysis and Assessment: How a time rail learned where
papers.authors: Kirk Laughead
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative Temporal Referencing (GTR) places records on a single line through time before anything else is done with them. This report records what happened when location was attached to that time-keyed record. Over nine days in October 2026, a working newsroom of one editor and two AI sessions began giving its records a place. Each location was set at the precision its source supports and staked to a fixed reference point. It was refined by appended steps as better evidence arrived, and the coarser placements were kept. The resulting practice is named Dynamic Geo-Temporal Analysis and Assessment (DGTA). The report covers: • the development of DGTA, step by step, from a hash-linked record • its standards, at concept level: one frame, stated precision, appended refinement, placement by reference, rings in place and time, proximity across stories, measurements joined by place and time, and maps drawn only as queries • a measurement case: – NOAA tide gauges at La Jolla and Los Angeles ran 15 to 16 inches above the predicted tide over October 6–9, 2026. – On the morning of October 9, both exceeded the National Weather Service minor flood threshold. – On the predicted tide alone, both would have stayed more than a foot below it. • a narrative case, in which locations spoken on a live broadcast without coordinates were recovered from the USGS earthquake catalog • its relation to prior work in temporal GIS, geoparsing, georeferencing, event data and temporal databases • what the practice shows, and what it does not yet show The report sets the 2026–27 king-tide windows as dates of interest for a multi-station test. Appendix A gives the data the newsroom created and the scripts that reproduce every result from NOAA and USGS data. DGTA is a practice of Generative Temporal Referencing, as Latent Value Query is. This is a concept disclosure; the implementation is withheld.

papers.title: AI Uncovers the Final Line of Defense in DeFi Security: Technical Anatomy of the $128M Balancer ComposableStablePool Rounding Exploit (TOB-BALANCER-004), the Six Fatal Vulnerability Patterns of ERC-4337 Account Abstraction, and Bridging the Formal Verification Blind Spot via AI Dimensional Analysis and QFS-zkVM
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This monograph permanently notarizes and mathematically formalizes the author's eleven-sheet primary treatise, "AI Uncovers the Final Line of Defense in DeFi Security — Target Audience: Developers and Smart Contract Auditors" (「AIが暴く、DeFiセキュリティの最終防衛戦」対象:開発者・スマートコントラクト監査人, Sheets ①–⑪). First (Chapter 1, Sheets ①–④), we dissect the $128 million, 30-minute, 7-blockchain exploit of Balancer Protocol's ComposableStablePools. We prove that the root cause was neither a zero-day compiler flaw nor a private-key compromise, but a violation of DeFi's fundamental directional rounding invariant: using floor truncation (FixedPoint.mulDown) instead of ceiling rounding (mulUp) when upscaling exactOut swap amounts. While Trail of Bits had identified this exact behavior in October 2021 (TOB-BALANCER-004, severity "Undetermined") and September 2022 auditors excluded StableMath as "previously audited," nesting the pool's own liquidity token (BPT) inside ComposableStablePools allowed an attacker to flash-drain balances to 8–9 wei and execute 65+ batchSwap iterations to collapse the StableSwap invariant D. Second (Chapter 2, Sheets ④–⑧), we formalize the Six Fatal Vulnerability Patterns of ERC-4337 Account Abstraction identified across Trail of Bits audits—(2.1) unguarded execute, (2.2) gas-field omission in signature hashing (preVerificationGas, verificationGasLimit, callGasLimit, maxFeePerGas, maxPriorityFeePerGas), (2.3) stateful storage mutation during validateUserOp, (2.4) ERC-1271 cross-account/cross-chain replay lacking EIP-712 binding, (2.5) post-validation execution-revert gas griefing, and (2.6) EIP-7702 initialize(owner) front-running—alongside canonical Solidity fixes and EEA EthTrust Security Levels v3 [Q] compliance. Third (Chapter 3 & Closing, Sheets ⑧–⑪), we expose the fundamental limitation of Formal Verification (which only verifies human-written specifications, leaving implicit assumptions unguarded against offensive AI) and formalize the 2026 Three-Layer Defense Stack: (Layer 1) Formal Verification, (Layer 2) Trail of Bits' LLM-driven AI Dimensional Analysis (93% recall on implicit unit and rounding-direction bugs), and (Layer 3) Continuous Fuzzing (Echidna), anchored in our 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (Fp, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) QFS-zkVM and sub-100-ns HIC hardware gating. 【和文要旨】 本稿は、開発者およびスマートコントラクト監査人に向けて策定された全11枚の一次手稿『AIが暴く、DeFiセキュリティの最終防衛戦(①〜⑪)』を完全公証し、その数理的・暗号学的定式化を与える。第1章(①〜④)では、世界トップクラスの監査ファームが複数回監査したにもかかわらず30分以内に7つのブロックチェーンにまたがって1億2,800万ドル($128M)が流出したBalancerプロトコル事件を解剖する。原因はゼロデイ脆弱性や秘密鍵漏洩ではなく、exactOutスワップの逆算(出力アップスケール処理)で切り上げ(mulUp)ではなく切り捨て(FixedPoint.mulDown)を使用した丸め方向の誤りにあった。Trail of Bitsは2021年10月にこの挙動をTOB-BALANCER-004(重要度「未決定」)として報告していたが、2022年9月のComposableStablePools監査ではStableMathライブラリが「前回監査済み(スコープ外)」とされ、自身の流動性トークン(BPT)をプール内に含む入れ子構造により、残高を8〜9 weiまで枯渇させて単一トランザクション内で65回以上のバッチスワップを反復する誤差増幅攻撃を許した(「コンポーザビリティ環境では個別コンポーネントの安全性の総和がシステム全体の安全性を保証しない」)。第2章(④〜⑧)では、ERC-4337アカウント抽象化における6つの致命的欠陥パターン(2.1 不適切なアクセス制御、2.2 ガス5項目を除外した不完全な署名検証、2.3 検証フェーズでの状態変更、2.4 ERC-1271リプレイ攻撃、2.5 リバート誤解によるガス枯渇攻撃、2.6 ERC-7702初期化フロントランニング)と修正コード、およびEEA EthTrust v3 [Q]レベルの初期設計適用を定式化する。第3章・クロージング(⑧〜⑪)では、人間が書いた仕様の内側しか証明できない「形式的検証の限界(仕様の死角)」を突破するTrail of BitsのAI次元解析(再現率93%)と3層防衛構造(①形式検証+②AI次元解析+③継続的ファジング[Echidna])、さらに「未知の未知(Unknown Unknowns)」と「思い込みのコスト」を根絶するGoldilocks素数体QFS-zkVM・RTO P2.0事前論理ロックを統合する。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: The Changing Architecture of Intellectual Property in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: ADRITA SHANNIGRAHI
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly encompassing industries and systems of governance, increasing efficiency, automation, and innovation. It has become a vital tool for creating text, images, music, software, and potentially patentable inventions. This rapid advancement in IP is not without risks at every stage of the innovation cycle. Traditional IP regimes arise from human creativity and invention, while AI performs activities traditionally attributed to both. India doesn't have any regulatory framework on AI-generated intellectual property, yet the Copyright Act, 1957, and Patents Act, 1970, contain certain principles—an answer to several emerging questions. This article argues that India should adopt a balanced approach to AI-generated creations instead of granting independent IP rights or prohibiting them. Instead, it should adopt a model that will protect creative human contribution as well as hold AI developers accountable for unlawful acquisition and exploitation of protected works.

papers.title: How sensitive are finite RH criteria? Certified Davenport–Heilbronn controls
papers.authors: Biswajit Mondal
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Unreviewed preprint: no completed external human peer review is claimed. This computational preprint calibrates finite Toeplitz and Weil-form criteria against Davenport–Heilbronn character combinations and Epstein zeta controls. A complete classical DH atlas through height 340 yields a PF435 sufficient sector guarantee. The targeted shift-44 column has certified negative bands 664–1099 and 1536–1972; the second band satisfies a locally recorded forecast. Nearby shifts 40–48 show no earlier failure in the requested tested strip. No globally first failing minor is claimed. Seven-control negative-support upper bounds include a conductor-17 forecast test. A further exact rational mixture path lowers the lowest off-line offset from 0.03 to 0.004; common-degree normalized support upper bounds increase from 0.5699 to 0.6597, with small changes at a larger retained degree. Four points on one path do not determine boundedness, divergence or an asymptotic rate as the offset tends to zero. Fits remain descriptive, positive finite sections supply no full-window lower bound, and finite-atlas attribution does not bound the infinite tail. The supplement contains editable source, compact certificates and fresh receipts for Liu frozen release b6cd218, with A retained-source/matrix/residual replay and B clean FULL/FAST replay. AI assistance and AI technical review are disclosed. The author explicitly authorized release without a completed human read on 18 October 2026. No universal zero-free region or proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is claimed. Two data-checked figures show the folded-zero sector geometry and finite-atlas cancellation, with a reproducible plotting source. The underlying scientific certificates are unchanged. This archival release is an unreviewed preprint. papers.title: Continuation under Incompleteness. Proven Reliability, Settling-In and Branchable Development of Autonomous Systems
papers.authors: Michael Schadewitz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This independently readable companion paper extends the conceptual synthesis and discussion paper “Robotics Capable of Development” by examining the temporal development of reliable competences, local settling-in, responsibility and the continuation of autonomous systems under incomplete knowledge. A robot operating for extended periods in an open human environment cannot know every future condition in advance or possess every required competence as a fully specified rule from the outset. The paper therefore asks how abilities are acquired, how their reliability is demonstrated in practice and how the conditions and limits of their validity can remain recognizable during operation. Central distinctions concern competence, proven reliability and authorization, as well as general training and local settling-in. Other topics include historically established reliability, trust, responsible action under uncertainty, the interests of affected third parties, and the possibility of revising established routines when the world changes. A further focus is the continuation of artificial development after interruptions. The paper discusses the preservation of Gewordenheit, selective memory, reconnection after disruptions, backups, changes of physical carrier and branchable artificial ontogeny, in which shared developmental states can give rise to different subsequent learning histories. The paper presents neither a finished technical architecture nor a systematic literature review, and it makes no claim of scientific priority. Its purpose is to connect conceptual distinctions, research questions, possible experiments and counter-hypotheses that may help investigate the conditions of responsible, reliable and developmentally open autonomy.

papers.title: A Dataset for AI Literacy in Secondary Schools in Tanzania:
papers.authors: Alcardo Alex Barakabitze
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dataset contains survey responses collected from 273 teachers in public secondary schools across Tanzania to assess different dimensions of teachers’ AI literacy and preparedness for the use of Artificial Intelligence in education. The dataset captures teachers’ demographic characteristics, including gender, age, teaching experience, school location, familiarity with AI concepts, and frequency of digital technology use in teaching. It also includes structured Likert-scale responses measuring three key constructs: AI Knowledge (KN), AI Awareness (AW), and AI Tool Proficiency (AI). Each construct was measured using multiple reflective items on a five-point scale ranging from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree. The dataset therefore provides a valuable empirical resource for examining teachers’ AI literacy and their capacity to engage with AI technologies in secondary education.

papers.title: Online Learning-Based Adaptive Hybrid Benders Decomposition for Risk-Averse Optimal Sizing
papers.authors: Saif Ahmad, Seifeddine Ben Elghali, Hafiz Ahmed
papers.abstract: Optimal sizing problem (OSP) under uncertainty is often formulated as two-stage stochastic programming (2SP). However, this formulation typically introduces significant computational and RAM (memory) bottlenecks as the scenario size grows. Benders Decomposition (BD) is a popular approach to tackle this problem, but it suffers from slow convergence to the exact solution. To address this problem, we propose an accelerated online learning-based adaptive hybrid BD algorithm. The proposed method avoids getting stuck in the infeasible region during early iterations by explicitly embedding a carefully selected scenario in the master problem, while online learning based on logistic regression (LR) leverages a light machine learning (ML) algorithm to avoid solving the entire scenario set at every iteration. The OSP is formulated to select a behindthe-meter battery energy storage system in a multi-site energy community with existing renewables. The use case explores an interesting middle-ground between deterministic methods and training-heavy ML models, showcasing the potential of MLassisted decision-making. Numerical results on scenario sets of up to 500 illustrate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach. © IEEE. Accepted manuscript. Personal use of this material is permitted. papers.title: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
papers.authors: Xinping Wang, Jie Ma, Rui Xing, Wensong Guo, Xiayi Zhang, Jianhao Deng, Zihao Zhou, Boqian Yang, Feijuan He
papers.abstract: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental capability for educational applications of Large Language Models (LLMs), where reliable problem solving requires not only correct answers but also coherent and verifiable reasoning processes. Multi-agent systems (MASs) have shown growing potential in this domain by leveraging collaboration and verification among multiple LLM agents. However, existing evaluations primarily focus on the correctness of final answers in text-only settings, offering limited insight into multimodal reasoning capabilities, the reliability of intermediate reasoning steps, and robustness against reasoning errors. To address these limitations, we introduce MAMath-Bench, a process-aware benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning capabilities of MASs. MAMath-Bench comprises 1,003 problems spanning 11 mathematical categories, multiple difficulty levels, and several modalities, including text, images, and audio. It features fine-grained milestone annotations to evaluate systems across three dimensions: problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial reasoning-chain perturbations. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, multi-agent collaboration does not consistently improve final-answer accuracy over strong single LLMs. Second, collaboration can substantially enhance the coverage of intermediate reasoning, but such gains may come at the cost of increased reasoning redundancy. Third, current systems remain vulnerable to adversarial reasoning errors, particularly those involving subtle structural perturbations. The dataset is available at https://github.com/mira-ai-lab/AgentMath.

papers.title: Voice-Based AI Feedback in Higher Education: A Field Study on Quality and Actionability
papers.authors: Thilo Tamme, Leander Schilling, Anton Hantel
papers.abstract: Student feedback is a critical input for continuous improvement in higher education, yet traditional end-of-semester written surveys suffer from low response rates, superficial answers, satisficing, and limited actionability. Voice-based conversational AI agents can conduct structured interviews at scale, asking open-ended questions and probing follow-ups, and may capture richer qualitative feedback than written instruments. This research proposal asks what characteristics, depth, and strategic value feedback collected through voice-based conversational AI agents has in higher education, and whether such agents elicit detailed, honest, and actionable feedback that can support instructional improvement and institutional learning. Drawing on survey-mode-effects research, the Computers As Social Actors (CASA) paradigm, and dynamic capabilities theory, we develop three hypotheses on elaboration, social presence and disclosure, and actionability. A completed technical pilot at the Technical University of Munich established the feasibility of telephone-based AI interviews; the main field study is planned for the "Advanced Leadership Communication" course at MIT Sloan with approximately 60 students, using a convergent mixed-methods design and a four-dimensional coding framework for actionability (specificity, thematic richness, constructive orientation, contextual depth). The study extends CASA theory to evaluative educational settings, characterizes voice-based AI as a distinct feedback modality, and links micro-level feedback quality to institutional sensing capabilities.

papers.title: Narrow Decision Models: A System-1 Architecture for Calibrated, Typed Decisions
papers.authors: Carlos André Antunes, Aldry Albuquerque, Gabriel de Melo Schmith, Natã Batista, Pedro Oziel Escobar da Silva, Stefano Benko Rossi, Lingrid Dietrich Lorenz da Silva, Flavia Cristina Costa, Thiago Bertotto, Luis Fernando Fausto
papers.abstract: System One models, introduced with TypeSafe's Jev, answer typed questions about a state with calibrated probabilities instead of generated text: choosing among options described in natural language (Choice), placing the state on an ordered scale (Score), or judging a yes/no statement (Noul). Jev is general-purpose: one set of weights, served as an API and adapted to a domain only through the request. We study the other end of the design space. A Narrow Decision Model (NDM) offers the same interface but is trained for the decisions of one organization, is small enough to run on its own infrastructure, and has an open architecture whose properties can be stated and tested. The state can be any text or structured record about which decisions are made; our running case is the routing of court communications. The architecture serializes a request as a prefix tree (the state, then each question, then each option) and runs a bidirectional encoder under a block attention mask with logical positions, so that each answer is, by construction, invariant to the order of its options and independent of the other questions asked. Routing through an organization chart is a composition of Choice decisions with an explicit "none of these" option. We describe training with proper scoring rules through a curriculum, calibration and abstention, decisions composed by rubrics, and a protocol that accepts or rejects the mechanism before held-out data is opened. A minimal validation on public and fictitious data shows that the invariances hold to rounding in a trained model, that a small instance routes on organization charts it has never seen well above lexical retrieval, and that, at equal compute, the block architecture reaches a lower loss than a pairwise cross-encoder. A first instance trained on real legal documents agrees with the LLM classifier in production on 91% of held-out documents.

papers.title: Editing as Language: Teaching LLM Agents a Grammar for Native Context Editing
papers.authors: Yunlong Deng, Yan Li, Xing Hu, Yida Zhu, Sean Du, Weiyang Liu, Guangyi Chen
papers.abstract: A synopsis in novels folds a story into a few lines; a function in code gathers many steps with a single execution. Context editing is native to language itself. In this paper, we propose the Native Context Editing (NCE) framework, which gives language model agents a grammar for natively editing their own context. By encoding context-editing operations in a grammar of dedicated special tokens, we teach the agents to invoke edits through the language itself. We train agents on iteratively constructed trajectory segments, with each teacher edit conditioned on the evolving context. This establishes context editing as an atomic and inherent capability of LLM agents, enabling them to dynamically modify their context as they generate responses over long-horizon reasoning and interaction. Compared with context-editing methods that learn to generate tool-use code within specific external harness environments, our approach integrates context editing as an internal mechanism of the model's native generation process, enabling better generalization across diverse real-world workflows. On four long-horizon agentic benchmarks (Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Multilingual, and SWE-bench Pro), NCE improves the average task success rate over the base model by 5.6 percentage points for LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse and by 4.5 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, while reducing average token usage by 36% and 15%, respectively.

papers.title: StopLoss: Teaching Agents to Predict Failure and Stop Early
papers.authors: Jiarong Liang, Xueguang Ma, Dongfu Jiang, Yuxuan Zhang, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen
papers.abstract: Coding agents keep working on runs that will fail verification, and asking a frontier model to watch for this is expensive in its own right. We introduce StopLoss, a small external monitor that learns failure recognition from completed trajectories and their verifier outcomes. The name is inspired by the stop-loss order in finance: StopLoss ends a run early when the run is likely to fail, which saves resources. Final outcomes label earlier local windows, so a fine-tuned language model can score the most recent tool steps in a single forward pass, and a threshold calibrated on successful runs turns that score into an abort decision without changing the executor. Trained on GPT-family SWE-rebench trajectories and evaluated on SWE-bench Verified and a SWE-bench Pro subset with GPT and Claude executors, StopLoss is compared against six general-purpose judges reading identical windows. Outcome supervision lifts failure prediction from near chance to a useful signal at the first check, at one to two orders of magnitude lower cost per check than any tested judge. This translates into savings: relative to completing every task, StopLoss lowers cost per retained solve by 4.5\% on Verified while preserving 99\% of successful runs, and by up to 31\% on the costlier Pro subset, reaching 48\% with a Qwen3-8B backbone, and in all four settings its cost per retained solve is below that of every judge policy. Outcome-trained small monitors can make failure recognition cheap enough for early stopping to pay for itself.

papers.title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache
papers.authors: Syed Usama Khalid Bukhari, Syed Safwan Khalid, Muhammad Aamir
papers.abstract: Decision models return probabilities over supplied options, but a deployed agent may also need to reply in words. The present study introduces System X, a large language model (LLM) decision model that adds a text-reply option to the LLM-as-Jev readout. When this option wins, or confidence is low, the same model continues from the decision's key-value (KV) cache, avoiding a repeated prompt prefill. Qwen3-0.6B has been fine-tuned with LoRA on Reason-9k and Bitext reply rows. JevBench accuracy shows no statistically significant change (55.4% to 54.5%, p=0.87), while expected calibration error falls from 0.292 to 0.169. Held-out Bitext routing accuracy reaches 98.3%. Cache reuse saves 15-37% of latency on an Apple M4 Pro, with token-identical replies in the FP32 demonstration cases. Scoring options on copies of the prompt cache matches full-sequence scoring to within 1.4e-6 in probability. Adding dialogue, industry and complaint data (System X+) improves support-task results but lowers IFEval accuracy from 55.5% to 45.0%. System X v4 uses Qwen3-1.7B, rebalanced data and teacher-rewritten reply targets. Against its base LLM, JevBench accuracy rises from 55.0% to 61.0% (p=0.04), with no statistically significant IFEval change (p=0.71). A matched latency test on unadapted Qwen3-1.7B saves 17-39%. One LLM judge prefers v4 replies to an unadapted 1.7B second call (31 to 11 pairs, p=0.003); the other's preference is not significant. These reply comparisons also differ in prompts and generation limits. State conflicts and unsupported reply details remain failure modes. Further studies with several seeds, human raters and real support data are recommended.

papers.title: DR-Learners for Generalizing CATEs from a Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.authors: Vanessa Rodriguez, Brieuc Lehmann, Karla Diaz‐Ordaz
papers.abstract: Randomized clinical trials are essential for evaluating interventions, yet average treatment effects can obscure treatment effect heterogeneity, making conditional average treatment effects (CATEs) a natural target. However, restrictive eligibility criteria and differential trial participation can limit the generalizability of these effects to broader target populations.
