Building on existing DR-Learners, we develop the gDR-Learner for generalizing RCT CATEs to a target population, using cross-fitted machine-learning nuisance estimation. We derive excess-risk bounds in which nuisance errors enter only as products, showing that the estimator achieves oracle-rate convergence despite slower individual nuisance estimation. The variables needed to generalize are rarely measured across the entire target population. We therefore extend the methods to two settings with incomplete covariate information: when certain covariates are measured only in the trial (e.g., biomarkers), and covariates driving trial participation measured only in a subsample of the target population, such as a representative cohort or registry. We construct weighted conformal prediction intervals for individual treatment effects, accounting for covariate shift between the trial and target population. In simulations, the gDR-Learner achieved the lowest estimation error when all covariates were observed relative to standard T- and DR-Learners and an inverse-probability-weighted T-Learner, and also outperformed the latter under incomplete covariate observation. We illustrate the methods by reanalyzing the Coronary Artery Surgery Study, examining treatment effect heterogeneity by prior myocardial infarction and baseline ejection fraction.

papers.title: TILDE: Teacher-in-the-Loop Distillation from Embodied Foundation Models
papers.authors: Yuxiang Lu, Yantong Liu, Jinghua Hou, Xueli Sun, Ruihua Han, Zhe Liu, Hengshuang Zhao
papers.abstract: Large-scale action pretraining equips Embodied Foundation Models (EFMs) with strong manipulation capabilities, with particular strengths in generalization and closed-loop robustness, but reproducing such pretraining requires substantial robot data and computation. To transfer these capabilities from pretrained EFMs to policies without action pretraining, we introduce TILDE (Teacher-In-the-Loop Distillation from EFMs), which synergizes on-policy distillation at student-induced states with learning from teacher-executed recovery trajectories. We further propose AutoDAgger, an autonomous data aggregation pipeline in which a robotic reward model is utilized to monitor task progress and trigger teacher intervention, thereby collecting recovery experience without human monitoring or manual control. AutoDAgger accelerates recovery-trajectory collection by more than $2\times$ compared with the human-in-the-loop method. By unifying learning from demonstrations, on-policy teacher supervision, and teacher's corrective behavior, TILDE improves task performance by up to $4.1\times$ over behavior cloning across three real-world tasks and supports effective cross-architecture distillation.

papers.title: UnexpectedParrots: Iterating Behavioral Experiment Design with In-Silico Simulations
papers.authors: Sanchaita Hazra, Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder, Pao Siangliulue, Peter Clark, Amy Xian Zhang, Joseph Chang
papers.abstract: Running behavioral experiments is expensive, slow, and prone to design flaws, often detectable after collecting data. We introduce UnexpectedParrots to iteratively refine behavioral study designs before a researcher recruits costly human participants. UnexpectedParrots relies on reasoning traces in addition to responses from LLM participants to uncover diagnostic critiques of structural errors and missed opportunities in existing study designs. When evaluated against a human-pilot or a no-simulation design-only baseline, UnexpectedParrots adds most value, producing unique, high-quality critiques. In a moderated user study with 12 proficient researchers, we find UnexpectedParrots useful, time-saving, and thought-provoking. Critiques provided by UnexpectedParrots often converge on issues researchers identify only during independent human pilots or additional formative interviews, even when the fidelity of the simulated populations remains questionable. Our users deem UnexpectedParrots useful not only as a tool to conduct early pilot studies and identify errors but also as an ideation tool to expand one's research horizon.

papers.title: It's Complicated: Factors Influencing the Effectiveness of LLM-Generated Feedback in a Live Programming Course
papers.authors: Tsvetomila Mihaylova, Arto Hellas, Bita Akram, Narges Norouzi, Peter L. Brusilovsky, Juho Leinonen
papers.abstract: We report on three iterations of an LLM-generated feedback system deployed in a live web development course, spanning three underlying models and three feedback formats. We ask how feedback presence and its characteristics (length, complexity, format) relate to student performance, whether prior feedback exposure is associated with final-project performance, and how performance changes after first exposure. Feedback was associated with more favorable immediate outcomes in several comparisons, but the pattern varied by outcome and period. In pooled models, longer feedback was associated with lower next-submission correctness, more remaining attempts, and longer resubmission time. Prior same-part feedback was associated with lower final-project solve probability. Student-level comparisons found differences on final-project steps begun before exposure, while within-student changes across steps were uncertain. These comparisons do not identify the causal effect of feedback. Changes on standard exercises were more favorable among exposed students, but the groups' different course-stage splits limit causal interpretation. Bounded message length and student choice of format are directions for experimental evaluation. Our final-project analysis captures follow-up performance rather than directly measuring learning or understanding.

papers.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research
papers.authors: Wei Xiong, Jiangtong Li, Han Zhao, Linxiao Yang, Jie Li, Changjun Jiang
papers.abstract: EEG analysis and decoding underpin brain-computer interfaces, cognitive assessment, and sleep monitoring. Fixed pipelines and reward-driven search do not explicitly determine how signal structure, representations, predictor behavior, and training dynamics contribute to performance or generalization gaps, leaving intervention choice underdetermined. We introduce NeuroAct, an autonomous research agent framework for EEG analysis and decoding. NeuroAct implements dual-loop autonomous research across EEG foundation models, task-specific predictors, and model combinations. In an inner loop, research, development, and review roles use evidence on signal structure, representations, predictor behavior, and training dynamics to test hypotheses, select analyses or interventions, and refine candidates using performance, stability, and cost feedback. An outer loop distills outcomes into conditional, testable recommendations with task and model conditions, then validates and revises them on subsequent tasks.We evaluate four settings: (A) EEG General Analysis, (B) Cross-task Model Optimization, (C) Single-task Open Research, and (D) Collaborative Prediction. In Setting A, NeuroAct's 80.88 macro-average exceeds BrainAgent's 63.13 by 17.75 points. In Setting B, NeuroAct raises EEGPT's mean balanced accuracy (BA) by 7.34 points and HBN Pearson's (r) from 0.6894 to 0.7362; in Setting C, it improves ADFTD BA by 16.33 points; and in Setting D, it raises Workload BA from 79.69% to 85.02%. Experience reuse raises BCIC-IV-2a BA from 34.66% to 50.81% while reducing LLM tokens by 64.02%, indicating recommendations improve cross-task performance. NeuroAct enables evidence-guided EEG research improved by cross-task experience.

papers.title: Acharya 2.0: An AI Tutor for Self-Learning Subjects in Hindi
papers.authors: Shantipriya Parida, Debasish Dhal, Sonal Khosla, Sambit Sekhar, Muhammed Abdur Rahmaan Kamaldeen
papers.abstract: Text processing is crucial for low-resource languages as it enables the development of tools and technologies that bridge the digital divide and provide equitable access to information and services. By empowering low-resource languages with robust text processing, we can preserve linguistic diversity, enhance education, improve communi- cation, and foster inclusivity in a rapidly digitizing world. Due to the lack of sufficient annotated datasets and lin- guistic resources, it is challenging to develop accurate and reliable language technologies for these low-resource languages. Large Language Models (LLMs) have attracted sig- nificant attention with their performance and the value they produce. However, with the ever-evolving language, adapting LLMs for a specific task is time-consuming and resource-intensive. Thus, Retrieval-Augmented Genera- tion (RAG) has overcome this limitation by augmenting LLMs with external knowledge, thereby improving their efficiency and extensive task-specific adaptation. Most applications of the RAG technique have been limited to English and has seen limited application in In- dic languages. This paper introduces the RAG-powered AI-Tutor application, Acharya 2.0, designed to produce academic assistance to Hindi-speaking students. The client-server-based web application integrates many fea- tures to support students in accessing and interacting with educational content.

papers.title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Wu, Zhaoxin Yu, Xinglin Xiao, Nan Xu
papers.abstract: Advancing physics reasoning in large language models requires scalable training data that connect physical laws, concrete problem scenarios, and verifiable numerical answers. Expert-designed problems offer top-down control over physical laws, conditions, and scenarios, but require costly human effort. LLM-based synthesis from texts scales efficiently, but model-generated answers and assessments leave supervision vulnerable to hallucinations. We introduce TIRE, a framework for Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution that brings knowledge-driven problem construction to large-scale data generation. Top-down instantiation uses reusable physical formulas and their applicability conditions to control the physical relations and numerical configurations of generated problems. Reliable execution establishes reference answers before problem generation, providing a common numerical foundation for problem construction and teacher distillation. Together, these mechanisms combine control over problem content with execution-grounded supervision for both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Using TIRE, we construct TIRE-19k, spanning nine subfields of physics. Across 3 backbone LLMs and 4 benchmarks, TIRE-19k outperforms 5 representative datasets with equal amounts of SFT data, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.86 percentage points on average. Further GRPO raises Qwen3-8B's average accuracy by 1.52 percentage points over its TIRE-19k SFT checkpoint. These results demonstrate the value of generating physics training data from explicit physical knowledge with reliable execution.

papers.title: Scam Town: Can Scam Education Spread Like a Vaccine?
papers.authors: Simiao Ren, Tommy Duong, Xingyu Shen, Jiaqi Gan, Tsang Ng, Ankit Raj, Kidus Zewde, Huaiyu Guo, Siyu Zhang
papers.abstract: Most older adults who hear a warning about scams hear it from someone they know: a relative, a neighbour, or a friend who was targeted. Yet research on scam prevention almost always studies one person at a time. We ask whether scam awareness can spread through a community and protect it the way a vaccine does, since a warning protects whoever hears it and can be passed on. To find out, we built Scam Town, a simulated community in which a large language model plays each resident. Scam centres phone the residents, and after a call a resident can warn the people they know. Word of mouth helped, but it did not take off on its own: each warning led to fewer than one more, so a community cannot count on warnings "going viral". Across 80 simulated towns, everyday talk cut the number of people scammed by roughly a fifth. The largest gains came when an official warning, from a bank, a senior centre, or an agency, reached most of a town and residents then talked about it: in simulation (a combination we did not test live) the two together cut scams by about half. Protection was greatest when warnings reached the people scammers actually call, who here were older residents. Because our residents are language-model stand-ins rather than real people, we treat these findings as predictions to test with people, not as proof. They point to a simple recipe for scam education: give people a clear story they can retell, design campaigns to be passed along, and reach first those most likely to be called.

papers.title: Don't Judge an Agent by Its Messages: Private-State Leakage under Passive Monitoring of Agent Communication
papers.authors: Daksh Pandey, Sayon Duttagupta, 邹新海 Zou Xinhai, Amit Singh Bhati
papers.abstract: An AI agent can reproduce the distribution of its messages and of the receiver's task outcomes while disclosing private information that the task never required. We ask what a passive audit can certify when the auditor knows the authorised sender and the exact observable law but has no trusted pairing of messages with the private states behind them. For a single round, compatible mutual-information leakage forms a sharp interval, and fixing the entire task-relevant message law, with every declared task utility, can still leave a full private bit undetermined; total leakage is determined if and only if, in every task state, the remaining private state or the authorised message is a deterministic function of that state. For a sender, such as an LLM, that selects among its own responses, we prove that in a balanced case its change to the message law within each task state equals $(1-2^{-k})$ times the honest messages' dependence on the attribute, which also sets, up to a constant, how many messages a monitor needs. With Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on a synthetic routing task, selection among 16 responses lets a public decoder recover a private bit in all 8,192 held-out rounds at 98.60\% routing accuracy (honest sender 98.90\%). A monitor that knows the selection rule reaches AUC 0.645 on single messages, close to the ceiling of 0.671 that honest messages predict, and 0.972 over 16, while generic monitors stay near chance. A law-preserving sender built from the same samples recovers the bit in 97.7\% of rounds, and every monitor without the true bit stays near chance against it. A canonical task interface preserves every receiver decision and bounds the remaining information about a balanced attribute by twice the routing-error rate, even for a receiver that shares a key with the sender. These results distinguish what passive auditing can certify from what restricting communication can enforce.

papers.title: INTEGRASI ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DALAM PENGELOLAAN KEUANGAN PRIBADI: STUDI PENGEMBANGAN SISTEM ADAPTIF UNTUK GENERASI DIGITAL
papers.authors: Nayla Zulfa Fauziah, Henny Sulistianingsih, Vina Delta Sari
papers.journal: Jurnal Penelitian Dan Pengkajian Ilmiah Eksakta
papers.abstract: The digital transformation era presents new challenges in personal financial management, particularly for millennials and Gen Z, who are prone to consumptive behavior, the Fear of Missing Out (FOMO), and low financial literacy. This study aims to explore the potential development of an adaptive system based on artificial intelligence to improve the effectiveness of personal finance management. Using a qualitative approach through literature and bibliometric analysis, the study employs VOSviewer to identify dominant themes such as financial behavior, financial education, and personal financial planning, with limited representation of AI integration and adaptive systems. This indicates a research gap that offers strategic opportunities for innovation in finance systems. The study formulates the need for intelligent features such as spending pattern analysis, personalized financial recommendations, and automatic adjustments based on user profiles. These findings are expected to serve as a conceptual foundation for developing smarter and more adaptive personal finance systems aligned with the characteristics of the digital generation.

papers.title: Lightweight Transformer-based Ai Model for Multilingual and Code-mixed Sentiment Analysis
papers.authors: vijay kumar
papers.abstract: Social media users increasingly communicate across language boundaries, often combining two or more languages within the same sentence and frequently writing Indian languages in Roman script. This creates a difficult setting for sentiment analysis because conventional monolingual models must cope with spelling variation, transliteration, informal vocabulary, emojis, abbreviations, language switching, and context-dependent sentiment. Large multilingual Transformer models have improved contextual understanding, but their computational cost can make deployment difficult on resource-constrained systems. This thesis proposes a lightweight Transformer-based framework for multilingual and code-mixed sentiment analysis. The framework uses a multilingual teacher model, language-aware normalization, and knowledge distillation to transfer contextual knowledge into a smaller student model. The study focuses primarily on Hindi-English (Hinglish) and Spanish-English (Spanglish) social-media text, using the SemEval-2020 Task 9 SentiMix corpora as a reproducible benchmark. The proposed framework is evaluated against classical machine-learning, recurrent neural-network, and full-size Transformer baselines. Evaluation is designed to consider not only accuracy and macro/weighted F1, but also inference latency, parameter count, memory consumption, robustness to noisy and code-mixed text, and the consistency of predictions across language pairs. An explainability component is also included so that important tokens contributing to a prediction can be inspected. The central research question is whether a substantially smaller Transformer can retain useful multilingual sentiment knowledge while reducing computational requirements. The thesis therefore treats sentiment analysis as both a language-understanding problem and an engineering deployment problem. The resulting framework is intended for applications such as social-media monitoring, customer-feedback analysis, multilingual communication systems, and other AI systems where language diversity and limited computing resources must be considered together. Keywords: Transformer, multilingual NLP, code-mixed text, sentiment analysis, knowledge distillation, Hinglish, Spanglish, lightweight AI, explainable AI, social media.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence to Support Academic Writing: A Systematic Literature Review of English Second Language Students in Higher Education
papers.authors: Lungile Ngcobo
papers.journal: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)
papers.abstract: Sophisticated AI applications like ChatGPT and Grammarly offer distinct advantages for enhancing writing proficiency. They assist users in conceptualising ideas, organising material, and refining writing style, whereas Grammarly focuses on improving grammar, punctuation, and clarity with context-aware recommendations. This is particularly relevant for students who are non-native English speakers, as it supports them and helps bridge educational disparities. While these instruments markedly enhance scholarly writing abilities, their efficacy in tertiary education remains a subject of debate. Recent occurrences of academic dishonesty associated with the improper use of generative AI technologies have negatively impacted higher education. This study assesses the impact of artificial intelligence on enhancing academic writing abilities in students who are not native English speakers. In accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) criteria, this study consolidates evidence from scholarly literature, policy reports, and institutional case analyses. Keywords, synonyms, and subject headings were employed to query three electronic databases from 2021 to 2025. The electronic repositories included Scopus, Emerald Insight, Google Scholar, and ProQuest. The evaluation of the publications was conducted through titles and abstracts, followed by an assessment of the full-text papers against the qualifying criteria. The results were derived and amalgamated into a narrative synthesis from selected publications. The results underscored AI's ability to customise and improve the educational experience for learners.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Use in Honours Research: Implications for Supervision Relationships, Knowledge Development, and Research Quality
papers.authors: Sympathy Luyanda Mncube
papers.journal: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)
papers.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in higher education has reshaped how students engage with academic research, particularly at Honours level, where students transition from structured undergraduate learning to independent postgraduate research. Guided by Self‑Regulated Learning (SRL) theory, this study examines how reliance on AI by Honours research students influences the supervisor-supervisee relationship, the quality of research produced, and the extent of knowledge gained through the research process. SRL theory emphasises learners’ ability to plan, monitor, and reflect on their own learning, which is central to successful postgraduate research development. This study adopts a conceptual and literature‑based review methodology, drawing on peer‑reviewed studies on AI use in higher education, literature on postgraduate supervision, and academic integrity and research skills development frameworks, with specific attention to Honours‑level contexts. The documents were analysed using thematic content analysis, focusing on self‑regulatory behaviours, supervisory interaction, research skill development, and learning depth. The findings suggest that limited and transparent use of AI can support honours students by reducing surface‑level cognitive load and assisting with language clarity. However, excessive reliance on AI may undermine key self‑regulation processes, weaken critical thinking, and reduce meaningful engagement with supervisors. Supervisors may struggle to accurately assess students’ understanding, potentially straining trust and feedback processes. The review further indicates that over‑reliance on AI risks producing research that is technically adequate but conceptually shallow, with reduced long‑term knowledge acquisition. The study concludes that clear supervision practices and explicit guidance on responsible AI use are necessary to ensure that AI supports, rather than replaces, the self‑regulated learning essential for high‑quality Honours‑level research.

papers.title: Perception Assessment on Meta-AI Use Among Some Undergraduates in Sokoto, Nigeria
papers.authors: Bashiru Aliyu Gada, Hauwa'u Hamidu Dahiru, SUWAIBA USMAN
papers.journal: International Research Journal of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: This study assessed the perception and use of Meta-AI among undergraduate students in Sokoto, Nigeria. A structured questionnaire was administered to 140 undergraduate students to examine the benefits, platforms of access, frequency of use, and challenges associated with Meta-AI. Data were analyzed using frequency and percentage. Results revealed that students perceived multiple benefits of Meta-AI: faster learning (28.6%) was the most cited benefit, followed by communication (21.4%), productivity improvement (18.6%), content creation/writing (17.1%), and picture generation (14.3%). Regarding platforms for locating Meta-AI, Google was most dominant (42.9%), followed by WhatsApp (32.9%) and Instagram (24.3%), indicating high integration of Meta-AI in everyday apps. Frequency of use showed that 54.3% use Meta-AI daily, 31.4% sometimes, and 14.3% weekly, demonstrating strong adoption. However, challenges were identified: sometimes giving wrong information (35.7%) was the major challenge, followed by privacy concerns (21.4%), overdependence (17.1%), high cost (10.0%), bias (8.6%), and hallucination (7.1%). The study concludes that undergraduates in Sokoto have positive perception of Meta-AI as a learning and productivity tool with high daily usage, but concerns about misinformation and privacy remain critical. There is need for AI literacy training to promote critical evaluation and responsible use.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Legal Literacy and Procedure-Concordant Use of an AI-Enabled Early-Warning System Among Hospital Nurses in Romania
papers.authors: Alina Doina Tănase, Camelia-Oana Mureșan, Ştefania Dinu, Adriana Pădure, Codruţa-Eliza Ille, Cristina Ioana Talpoș Niculescu
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the Artificial Intelligence Act, requires organisations deploying AI systems to ensure appropriate AI literacy and human oversight. We examined whether AI legal literacy was associated with procedure-concordant use of an AI-enabled early-warning system among hospital nurses and whether the association of prior AI-governance training with concordant use persisted after literacy was taken into account. Materials and Methods: This single-centre cross-sectional study included 87 nurses in a tertiary university hospital. AI legal literacy was measured with a study-specific 24-item instrument, and procedure-concordant AI use, the primary outcome, was defined as meeting all five criteria of the institutional documentation audit in 10 audited interactions per nurse. The primary analysis was multivariable logistic regression, confirmed in three-level mixed-effects models of 870 audited interactions nested within nurses and wards. Secondary and exploratory analyses (inverse-probability weighting, mediation decomposition, latent class analysis, and an internally validated prediction model) are reported as hypothesis-generating. Results: Forty-four nurses (50.6%) were procedure-concordant. Concordance was higher among trained than untrained nurses (70.3% versus 36.0%; p = 0.002). Each 10-point increase in AI legal literacy was associated with higher adjusted odds of concordant use (adjusted odds ratio 5.16, 95% CI 2.04–13.06; p < 0.001). The association persisted in three-level mixed-effects models (aOR 3.61 per 10 points, 95% CI 1.98–6.58). The association with prior training was attenuated after adjustment for literacy and was not statistically significant after inverse-probability weighting (OR 2.01, 95% CI 0.82–4.90); an exploratory decomposition was consistent with, but could not establish, an indirect association through literacy. Conclusions: Higher AI legal literacy was strongly associated with procedure-concordant AI use in this single-centre study. The findings support further evaluation of literacy-focused governance education and institutional oversight in hospital nursing practice; causal and predictive claims await prospective, multicentre confirmation.

papers.title: Food Preferences and Acceptability of Molded Pureed Foods in Community-Dwelling Older Adults in Singapore
papers.authors: Verena M. H. Tan, Gary T. L. Chiah, Ives Yubin Lim, Wai Yee Mah, Peng Peng Lim, Kenny Ban Leong Tan
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Texture-modified diets (TMDs) are prescribed for older adults with chewing or swallowing difficulty, but conventional pureeing dilutes nutrient density and yields visually indistinguishable meals that discourage intake. This study aimed to compare food preferences and sensory priorities by self-reported chewing/swallowing difficulty status and to conduct a preliminary evaluation of the sensory acceptability of molded pureed meal prototypes. Methods: An interviewer-administered survey of 100 community-dwelling older adults in Singapore characterized chewing and swallowing symptoms, TMD status, sensory-attribute importance, meal satisfaction, and food and snack preferences. In a separate exploratory pilot, 16 older adults without self-reported swallowing difficulty evaluated four enzymatically modified, molded pureed prototypes on a 7-point hedonic scale. Results: Fifty-six participants (56.0%) reported chewing and/or swallowing difficulty. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in age, BMI, sex, marital status, sensory-attribute importance, meal satisfaction, or food/snack category preferences (all p ≥ 0.05). Among those with difficulty, only 19 (33.9%) had been recommended a TMD and 15 (26.8%) were currently consuming one, while 37 (66.1%) had neither. All four molded pureed prototypes had mean hedonic scores for individual attributes ranging from 4.7 to 6.6 on the seven-point scale. Overall acceptability was high (8.1 ± 1.4 of 10) and most participants were willing to prepare (93.8%), purchase (81.3%), or incorporate (68.8%) the meals. Conclusions: Chewing and swallowing difficulty was common and was not associated with differences in food preferences. Texture-modified meals may be developed from familiardishes, informed by earlier community screening.

papers.title: Beyond Structural Barriers: Storytelling, Affect and Municipal Responsibility in Urban NBS Implementation
papers.authors: Mariliis Niinemägi, Lill Sarv, Germo Ausin
papers.abstract: Nature-based solutions (NBS) are valuable instruments for climate adaptation and resilience. Existing research on urban NBS barriers focuses mostly on structural and technical elements, while co-creation and local knowledge are regularly cited as critical for successful implementation. Even when barriers are easy to identify, a divide between ambition and reality generates procedural and knowledge gaps. This paper addresses this challenge through a case study of the Horizon Europe project URBREATH. Narrative inquiry is used to reveal invisible aspects of NBS implementation as experienced by city officials from Madrid, Cluj-Napoca, Leuven, and Tallinn. Drawing on storytelling workshops with city representatives and the authors’ participatory observation as project members, the paper shows that urban NBS are not only technical solutions, but also socio-cultural elements narrated through affective processes. We ask: what do city officials’ stories of difficult implementation moments reveal? Collected narratives show the personal commitment required to deliver urban nature-based solutions. Stories reveal that, in these cases, project managers absorbed institutional gaps informally, community participation was unevenly distributed, and hybrid NBS objects did not fit existing departmental categories. In navigating these barriers, narrative work itself operates as a form of governance practice. Narrowing this procedural and knowledge gap, we conclude, requires attention to affective and relational labour alongside procedural fixes.

papers.title: How Perceived AI-Driven Personalization Is Associated with Online Purchase Intention in Tourism E-Commerce: A Moderated Sequential Mediation Model of Perceived Relevance and Trust in AI Recommendations
papers.authors: Maher Abdullah Alhaidar
papers.journal: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
papers.abstract: This study examines how perceived artificial intelligence (AI)-driven personalization is associated with online purchase intention in tourism e-commerce. It develops a moderated sequential mediation model in which perceived recommendation relevance and trust in AI recommendations represent distinct evaluative pathways, while perceived AI response creativity and AI recommendation transparency condition different relationships within the proposed model. Data were collected from 871 consumers with recent experience using personalized recommendations on AI-enabled tourism platforms or travel assistants. Respondents were recruited through experience-based purposive sampling and screened to ensure direct and recallable experience with AI-generated travel recommendations. The proposed relationships were examined using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Perceived AI-driven personalization was positively associated with perceived recommendation relevance, trust in AI recommendations, and online purchase intention. Perceived recommendation relevance and trust in AI recommendations were also positively associated with online purchase intention, while perceived recommendation relevance was positively related to trust in AI recommendations. Both constructs showed significant separate indirect associations between perceived AI-driven personalization and online purchase intention, and the theoretically ordered sequential indirect pathway was also statistically supported. Because the direct association remained significant and operated in the same direction as the indirect pathways, the observed statistical pattern was consistent with complementary partial mediation rather than evidence of a causal mediation mechanism. Perceived AI response creativity positively moderated the association between perceived AI-driven personalization and perceived recommendation relevance, whereas AI recommendation transparency positively moderated the association between perceived recommendation relevance and trust in AI recommendations. The study distinguishes perceived AI-driven personalization from perceived recommendation relevance by treating the former as consumers’ assessment of adaptive recommendation tailoring and the latter as their judgment of recommendation–decision fit. It further conceptualizes perceived recommendation relevance and trust in AI recommendations as distinct organism evaluations reflecting cognitive fit and reliance-oriented judgment, respectively. Creativity and transparency are positioned as relationship-specific boundary conditions rather than temporal stages, providing a more differentiated account of the theoretically ordered statistical pathways linking perceived AI-driven personalization with online purchase intention in tourism e-commerce.

papers.title: AIGC-Driven Image Twin Generation and Evaluation for the Spatial Reconstruction of Ancient Academies: A Case Study of Classical Academy Imagery of Hunan Province
papers.authors: Cui Ling
papers.abstract: The digital reconstruction of ancient architecture and landscapes has become a prominent topic in current research. Existing studies predominantly focus on the three-dimensional reconstruction of archaeological sites or damaged historic buildings, while effective methods for the restoration or translation of architectural imagery recorded in ancient classical texts remain insufficient. Taking China’s distinctive educational architectural heritage—the ancient academy—as a case study, this paper proposes three Chinese AIGC methods, TI (Image to Image), TLTI (Image to Line Drawing to Image), and TPTI (Image to Prompts to Image). The methods use selected academy images from local gazetteers of Hunan Province, China, together with textual prompts to reconstruct the architecture and landscapes of ancient Chinese academies. The findings suggest that AIGC shows potential to support the expert-led reconstruction of landscapes and architectural imagery recorded in historical texts within a Chinese cultural context, enabling visualization of architectural developmental histories traditionally reliant on textual interpretation in the history of technology and art. This research offers a novel methodology for the integration of heritage science and the history of technology and art by activating cultural heritage in non-Western contexts through artificial intelligence and analyzing the evaluation challenges posed by AI models.

papers.title: Preserving Human Judgment in AI-Enabled Education: The SAM Model for AI Readiness, Assessment, and Human-in-the-Loop Decision Making
papers.authors: Holger Horz, Pauline Czora, Julia Mendzheritskaya, Pauline Naumann, Maria Zirenko
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) shifts educational focus from access to information toward judging machine-generated claims and regulating the division of epistemic work. This conceptual article proposes the SAM model—self-regulation (S), ambiguity tolerance (A), and methodological competence (M)—as a bounded person-level resource model within broader AI readiness, with educators’ AI readiness as a central application. S denotes regulatory capacity, A a disposition-like willingness to tolerate unresolved epistemic ambiguity, and M the capacity to evaluate claims, differentiated into cross-domain M1 and domain-specific M2. SAM’s distinctive claim is configurational: M should predict independently assessed judgment more strongly at higher S and, under high ambiguity, when A is higher. These relations, the M1/M2 distinction, limited compensability, and incremental prediction beyond shared and neighboring accounts remain hypothetical. The model separates resources from enacted processes, contextual affordances, and outcomes and requires independent performance criteria. For AI-based assessment and learning analytics, educators’ interpretations of AI-derived evidence and construct inferences from behavioral traces require validated mappings addressing alternative explanations, comparability, fairness, and use. SAM thus offers a research agenda predicting when AI support preserves human judgment rather than merely improving supported performance.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Design Judgment: Perceived AI Interaction Conditions, Critical Evaluation of AI Advice, and Expert-Rated Design Judgment Quality
papers.authors: Kun Wang, Z Huang, Qianling Jiang
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to analyze and compare design alternatives, yet how design students evaluate AI advice and how such evaluation relates to final design judgments remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the associations among perceived AI interaction conditions, critical evaluation of AI advice, and expert-rated Design Judgment Quality. A cross-sectional study combined a standardized poster comparison task with a post-task questionnaire involving 118 visual communication design students. Participants interacted with Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro and submitted design choices, rationales, and revision recommendations. Perceived Feedback Diagnosticity, Interaction Controllability, and three critical evaluation activities were measured through post-task self-reports, while Design Judgment Quality was independently assessed by three experts. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was used for hypothesis testing. Feedback Diagnosticity was positively associated with Evidence Verification, Argument Scrutiny, Contextual Fit Evaluation, and Design Judgment Quality. Interaction Controllability was positively associated with Argument Scrutiny and Contextual Fit Evaluation, but not directly with Design Judgment Quality. Among the three evaluation activities, only Argument Scrutiny showed a significant positive association with expert-rated Design Judgment Quality. These findings suggest that AI-assisted design judgment requires attention to both the perceived value of AI feedback and how users examine AI recommendations and their underlying rationales.

papers.title: Impact of Digital Construction Technologies on Sustainability Awareness and Decision-Making in Civil Engineering Education
papers.authors: Rizwan U. Farooqui, Abid Hassan, Mohammad Khalid, Syed Ahmed
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering Project and Production Management
papers.abstract: Digital technologies such as Building Information Modeling (BIM), Artificial Intelligence (AI), simulation platforms, and virtual and augmented reality are reshaping civil engineering education, yet their influence on sustainability awareness and decision-making is not well understood. This study surveyed 73 students enrolled in civil engineering courses at a public university in the southeastern United States. The instrument comprised 36 Likert-scale statements, grouped into eight constructs covering technology use in the curriculum, professional mindset, sustainability knowledge and lifecycle and environmental awareness. They also covered understanding of water resources, cognitive ability, emotional intelligence, and problem-solving. It also includes three decision scenarios in which a digital tool output conflicted with human input or practical constraints. Students reported favorable attitudes toward digital tools, along with strong conceptual sustainability awareness, but two applied-skill gaps stood out: only 32.9% felt able to interpret hydrologic models, and only 28.8% felt they could transfer simulation-based lessons to real world settings. In the scenarios, at most 12.3% of respondents accepted the digital output at face value, and 83.6% never did so across all three scenarios. Breadth of tool exposure was unrelated to perceptions or decision style, whereas the small group of students reporting exposure to hydrologic modeling rated their model interpretation ability substantially higher, suggesting that relevant depth matters more than the number of tools encountered. The findings support curricula that pair earlier and deeper BIM and hydrologic modeling instruction with lifecycle content and that train verification and interpretation skills alongside tool operation.

papers.title: Perceived Artificial Intelligence Skill Demand Across the Construction Project Lifecycle: Evidence from the Rwandan Construction Industry
papers.authors: OLUWASEUN SUNDAY DOSUMU, Christine Musanase, Ryan Tumusiime Kaganga, Dieudonne Ahishakiye, Eric Iradukunda
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering Project and Production Management
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming construction processes, yet limited empirical evidence exists on the skills required by professionals across different stages of the construction project lifecycle, particularly in developing economies. This study evaluates the perceived demand for AI skills across the eight stages of the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) Plan of Work in the Rwandan construction industry. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 174 construction professionals representing architecture, engineering, quantity surveying and construction management. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring the perceived demand for AI-related skills across the eight lifecycle stages. Descriptive statistics were used to assess and rank skill demand, while the Kruskal-Wallis H test examined differences among professional groups, and the Friedman test assessed differences across lifecycle stages. The findings show moderate-to-high demand for AI skills across all lifecycle stages. The use stage recorded the highest overall demand, followed by strategic definition, and manufacturing and construction, while handover recorded the lowest. Significant differences across lifecycle stages were identified using the Friedman test (χ² = 19.162, p = 0.008), although the practical effect was very weak (Kendall's W = 0.016), indicating modest variation in relative intensity. Most individual skills did not differ significantly across professional groups, suggesting a substantial common set of AI competencies alongside selected discipline-specific requirements. The study’s findings provide evidence for the development of targeted, stage-specific construction education, professional development and workforce strategies in Rwanda and comparable developing economies.

papers.title: EDUPATH AI A Rag-Based Multi-Agentic AI Framework for Personalised Education and Career Advisory
papers.authors: Eswari K, Durairaj Mohanapriya, Kumuthaveni
papers.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology
papers.abstract: Choosing a career is a tough decision to make in itself. Things get trickier when it comes to information a student actually needs: which scholarships they're eligible for, where courses lead, where students can get in based on their marks, etc., and all that information is spread out across dozens of government portals, college websites, and PDFs that don't always agree on what they're offering. The majority of the career-guidance tools that are available today are not really a solution to this. They either give a general response from a brief questionnaire, or release a chatbot which will freely associate a response that seems confident but is not true. Neither verifies whether a student is qualified or not for what it suggests. This paper is an attempt to bridge that gap by employing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline to achieve this using a set of cooperating agents, instead of a single large model performing all the tasks. The first step is to process a student's academic record, interests, financial status, location, class and career category, and goals to create a structured profile, which is then fed into agents that search for verified information, validate eligibility for scholarships based on hard rules, not assumptions, and compile a plan that is concrete and easily explained. We evaluated the retrieval layer on ten representative queries, including career paths, welfare schemes, higher education and scholarships, and it achieved a top five correct source hit rate of 90% and a Mean Reciprocal Rank of 0.7167. To sum up, if you base the model's output on retrieved evidence and ensure that eligibility decisions are deterministic then you end up giving guidance that a student can actually trust and follow — something that a pure language model and a static rule engine can't do alone.

papers.title: Leveraging satellite data and machine learning to quantify rooftop rainwater harvesting reliability and tank requirements for schools and health care facilities in Uganda
papers.authors: Benjamin Okello, Patrick Oler
papers.abstract: Many schools and health facilities in Uganda lack a reliable water supply, yet most have roofs that could collect rain. For 41,592 facilities (32,881 schools and 8,711 health facilities), we estimated how much water their roofs can supply, how large a tank each one needs, and how often that supply fails. Roof areas came from AI-derived building footprints (Google Open Buildings v3) and daily rainfall for 1981 to 2025 from CHIRPS. A daily yield-after-spillage tank model gave the supply available on 90% of days and the smallest tank that meets each facility's demand on 90% of days. On a standard 200 m² roof, a 10 m³ tank supplied a median of 359 litres per day on 90% of days, from 255 L in the Northern region to 411 L in the Eastern region; at the same annual rainfall, Northern facilities received about 40% less because their rain falls in one long season. With mapped roofs, 77.1% of schools and 62.2% of health facilities could reach the target with a tank of 200 m³ or less, and among these the median school needed 39.5 m³ and the median health facility 5.0 m³. The school share ranged from 42.3% to 92.8% across enrolment scenarios and fell to 44.1% if only buildings within 60 m are connected and to 37.8% if only 30% of the mapped roof feeds the tank. A machine-learning model trained on the simulations predicted the required tank within 25% for 97.0% of facilities in spatial cross-validation, against 8.3% for the dry-period rule of thumb. With a 20% margin its tanks met the target at 97.5% of facilities, but at only 74.5% when the nearest training data were at least 110 km away, where the rule's larger tanks were more dependable. Reliability rose slightly over 1981 to 2025, with a significant trend at 15.1% of facilities. A retrospective seasonal analysis found useful skill only for September to November, coming from tank storage and recent rain rather than El Niño or Indian Ocean Dipole indices. The results are screening estimates that need confirmation on site; the code and data are released openly.

papers.title: PEMANFAATAN TEKNOLOGI KOMPUTER BERBASIS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE UNTUK PENGEMBANGAN DAKWAH ISLAM DI PERGURUAN TINGGI
papers.authors: Ina Lestari
papers.journal: Qaulan Baligha Jurnal Ilmu Manajemen Dakwah
papers.abstract: In the digital era, the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has brought a significant transformation in the method of spreading Islamic da'wah, especially among Generation Z students who have very high internet penetration. This research aims to explore the use of AI technology, the opportunities offered, and the obstacles faced in the development of Islamic da'wah in the university environment. Using a mixed-methods research design, data was collected through a survey of 400 students, in-depth interviews with 12 da'wah experts and practitioners, and a six-month analysis of chatbot logs. The results of the study showed a high rate of digital adoption, where 78% of students accessed the internet daily and 65% of them actively participated in online da'wah content. AI platforms such as da'wah chatbots for religious questions and answers and voice recognition-based Qur'an learning applications are the most frequently used media. AI implementations, such as the use of the IndoBert model, have been proven to increase audience engagement by up to 24.7%. The main supporting factors for this success are the availability of a strong campus IT infrastructure and digital literacy training for preachers. However, ethical challenges remain, especially related to students' concerns about the validity of content (50%) and data privacy (30%). The study concludes that AI is highly effective in expanding the reach of da'wah, but requires strict oversight mechanisms from religious experts (ulama) to ensure the accuracy of messages. It is recommended that universities integrate AI modules into da'wah curricula and encourage collaboration between technology experts and religious experts.

papers.title: ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯ ОБРАЗОВАНИЯ В АЗЕРБАЙДЖАНЕ В ЭПОХУ ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА
papers.authors: ЛЕЙЛИ ГУЛИЕВА
papers.abstract: This article examines the key areas and mechanisms for integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into the education system of the Republic of Azerbaijan in the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution.Particular attention is paid to the analysis of the "Artificial Intelligence Development Strategy for 2025-2028" as an interdepartmental action plan aimed at digitally transforming the country's socioeconomic sphere and ensuring its technological sovereignty.The author examines the comprehensive modernization of the educational vertical, including didactic, competency-based, and managerial components.Using the example of the international intensive program "IT SkillSprint", launched in partnership with the global school Ironhack, the author demonstrates effective models of public-private and academic collaboration for training elite IT professionals.The paper also addresses the current status of and barriers to the development of distance and hybrid learning at the country's universities, emphasizing the need to improve the relevant regulatory framework.It summarizes the key risks associated with the introduction of AI into the educational environment and proposes systemic measures to ensure ethical and legal protection, cybersecurity, and the development of a new digital culture of data-driven management.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy and Work Readiness among Final-Year University Students: Implications for Sustainable Workforce Development
papers.authors: Alnsia Engy, Rose Mini Agoes Salim, Danang Wirawan
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education and professional environments has increased the importance of understanding psychological factors associated with graduates' readiness for employment. This study examined the association between Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy (AISE) and Work Readiness among final-year students at Universitas Indonesia and explored its implications for sustainable workforce development. A quantitative cross-sectional correlational design was employed involving 115 students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using the Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Scale (AISES) and the Work Readiness Scale (WRS) and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson product–moment correlation, and simple linear regression. The results revealed a significant positive association between AISE and Work Readiness (r = .580, p < .001). AISE explained 33.6% of the variance in Work Readiness (R² = .336). Although most participants demonstrated high AISE, Work Readiness was predominantly moderate, suggesting that confidence in using AI alone does not fully explain graduates' readiness for employment. These findings indicate that AISE represents an important psychological factor associated with workforce readiness while highlighting the multidimensional nature of Work Readiness. The study extends the application of AISE to workforce readiness and provides practical implications for higher education institutions in preparing graduates for AI-integrated workplaces.

papers.title: The Relationship between the Level of Speech Culture and the Success of Using AI in Pedagogical Activities: Results of the Experiment
papers.authors: Kun Li, Elvira Gabdelbarovna Galimova, Irina V. Khairova
papers.abstract: The active integration of artificial intelligence (AI) systems into educational practice places higher demands on the professional training of teaching staff. Within the structure of this training, speech culture becomes of key importance, since it is this that ensures the accuracy of task formulation and the adequate interpretation of digital results. The aim of the study is to identify the nature of the relationship between the level of speech culture formation in future teachers and the effectiveness of AI use in the educational process. In the experimental work (sample of undergraduates, N=68), the following were used: an author-developed questionnaire for assessing the normative, communicative, and ethical components of speech culture, a pedagogical experiment involving problem-solving tasks with the use of AI tools, and methods of statistical analysis. The diagnostics revealed the absence of a low level of speech culture, but revealed a differentiation between high and medium levels. Statistically significant positive correlations were obtained (p < 0.05). Participants with a high level of speech culture formulated queries more accurately, analyzed AI responses more critically and deeply, and interpreted results with higher quality. The conclusion is drawn about the need to integrate speech and digital training of future teachers, since the effectiveness of AI use depends on speech culture, critical thinking, and professional reflection, and not only on technical skills.

papers.title: Transformation of Approaches to Teaching Programming and Software Development under Influence of Generative AI
papers.authors: Mikhail Mikhailovich Abramskiy, Gökay Ozdemir, Ilmira Khamitova, Irina Shapkina
papers.abstract: This paper considers key transformational processes occurring in programming and software development training under the influence of generative artificial intelligence. Based on a series of interviews with junior students, a behavioral pattern leading to degrading skills of algorithmic thinking and problem decomposition is identified. A quantitative analysis of undergraduate theses from the Institute of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ITIS) at Kazan Federal University (KFU) over the past three years demonstrated a significant increase in AI usage in project work and the independent development of skills for utilizing LLMs in professional practice. The drawbacks of the uncontrolled use of generative AI in the educational process and the need to develop sustainable competence in using these tools in professional software development activities are shown. A three-tiered solution is proposed: improving assessment through analysis of the process and style of coding; regulating the use of LLM in project activities and final theses with an emphasis on assessing applicability of AI; and integrating AI tools into teacher work to update content and provide feedback. The proposed approaches have both conceptual and practiceoriented nature and aim to transform the process of training software developers in the context of the widespread adoption of AI tools in IT-industry.

papers.title: AI Pedagogy in Higher Education: A Scoping Review of Competencies, Enactments, and Ethical Governance
papers.authors: Kayla Willemse, Joyce C. West
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in higher education, yet the pedagogical field intended to organise its use remains conceptually underdeveloped. This scoping review mapped and synthesised peer-reviewed literature on AI pedagogy in higher education, using teacher education as the primary analytic lens. Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR reporting principles, searches were conducted across ten databases and publisher platforms for literature published between 2022 and March 2026. Of 956 records screened, 191 studies were included. Data charting and synthesis combined deductive coding, an a priori codebook, AI-assisted coding in Atlas. ti, and human inductive open coding. Six interrelated themes emerged: AI pedagogy is contextually produced rather than universally defined; conceptualised through pedagogical integration, competence, and borrowed theories rather than a settled standalone theory; enacted mainly through augmentation-oriented practices and generative AI tools; and associated with changing teacher professionalism, ethical mediation, governance, structural constraints, and a rapidly expanding but methodologically uneven evidence base. The review rejects purely technical, universal, or tool-centred models of innovation. Instead, it positions AI pedagogy as a context-specific, human-led, competence-rich, and governance-aware form of teaching in which AI supports planning, feedback, adaptation, and reflection without displacing human educational responsibility, especially within teacher education contexts and programmes.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Eurasian Higher Education: An Empirical Study of Student Practices
papers.authors: Shamil Sheymardanov, Muhamad Hariz Muhamad Adnan, Timur Mufazalov
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has penetrated higher education not through official strategies but via students’ and faculty members’ personal devices, catching most universities off guard. This article presents empirical data from a large-scale survey conducted between March and April 2026 across six post-Soviet countries (Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Armenia, Tajikistan). The study provides a systematic cross-national analysis of student AI use patterns in the Eurasian higher education space, complementing recent single-country studies in the region. The sample included 478 students. The study measured frequency of AI use, perceived risks, compatibility with educational values, and the presence of institutional regulatory mechanisms. The results show that 78 % of students regularly use generative AI, yet only 32 % of universities have an official policy in this area. A deep disciplinary divide emerges: students fall into two roughly equal profiles – “pragmatic techs” (daily users with low ethical anxiety) and “reflective humanists” (cautious users with a strong demand for ethical frameworks). The main barrier to AI adoption is not technological infrastructure but the absence of regulatory and social technologies. The article offers discipline-differentiated recommendations for universities in non-Western contexts.

papers.title: Thinking Beyond the Tool: Misuse of ChatGPT and the Future of Student Cognition
papers.authors: Intakhab Alam Khan
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, has rapidly transformed education by providing immediate information, personalized learning support, academic writing assistance, language learning opportunities, and research support. However, growing concerns exist regarding excessive reliance on AI-generated content and its potential effects on cognitive development. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the educational benefits and cognitive risks associated with ChatGPT using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, PubMed, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2022 and June 2026. Following systematic screening, eligibility assessment, and quality appraisal, 27 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Five major themes emerged: educational benefits, cognitive offloading, critical thinking, creativity, and teacher perspectives. Findings indicate that ChatGPT supports personalized learning, feedback, academic writing, language learning, coding, and research productivity. Conversely, excessive dependence may contribute to cognitive offloading, weaker memory retention, reduced analytical reasoning and critical thinking, superficial learning, diminished creativity, and academic integrity concerns. Teacher guidance and ethical AI practices are essential for safeguarding cognitive development. The review concludes that ChatGPT should enhance rather than replace students’ cognitive activities, supporting critical thinking, creativity, ethical responsibility, and lifelong learning.

papers.title: Chinese High-Level Comprehensive Universities’ Participation in Science Teacher Education in the AI Era: Policy Design, Implementation Status, and Sustainable Mechanisms
papers.authors: Tao Deng, Yilong Zhang, Boyang Deng
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping science education, intensifying demands for high-quality science teachers. In 2023, China launched the National Excellence Program to promote the institutionalized participation of high-level comprehensive universities in teacher education. Drawing on policy analysis, fieldwork across 12 pilot universities, and the case of Northeast Normal University, this study examines the program’s policy design, implementation status, and sustainable mechanisms in the AI era. The findings show that while the initiative drives a transition toward an open, multiactor collaborative model, disciplinary and technological resources do not automatically translate into teacher education capacity. Pilot universities still confront unstable participation incentives, fragmented collaboration, fragile institutional guarantees, and unsystematic evaluation. Moving from project-based participation to institutionalized implementation therefore requires sustained organizational translation. The study proposes a four-dimensional integrated framework comprising Composite Driving, Collaborative Implementation, Multi-Dimensional Guarantee, and Effect Evaluation mechanisms to support the transformation of disciplinary and technological resources into stable teacher education capacity and cultivate scholar-like science teachers with academic literacy, educational literacy, and digital-intelligence mastery.

papers.title: Boosting Vocabulary Mastery: ChatGPT’s Role in Advancing EFL Learners’ Language Skills
papers.authors: Ali Al Ghaithi, Behnam Behforouz
papers.abstract: This study attempted to implement artificial intelligence in language learning using the well-known ChatGPT. This study focused on measuring the effects of ChatGPT on vocabulary size and depth of knowledge. To collect the required data, 60 Omani intermediate EFL learners were divided equally into control and experimental groups. An updated vocabulary level test (UVLT), developed by Webb et al. (2017), and a Word Associate Test (WAT) developed by Read (1998) were used as the pretests to ensure the homogeneity of students’ vocabulary knowledge. Although both groups continued the traditional face-to-face training, the experimental group had the opportunity to use ChatGPT as a facilitator of vocabulary learning with the chance of tailored and personalized activities. The UVLT and WAT were administered again as posttests to compare learners’ performance after the treatment. The findings revealed that both groups showed increases in the posttest regarding vocabulary size, but the experimental group outperformed the control group remarkably. Although no progress was made in the depth of vocabulary by the control group, the experimental group performed significantly better. The findings are insightful for teachers, curriculum designers, students, researchers, institutions, and policymakers.

papers.title: Adolescent Stress Level Classification Using Ensemble Machine Learning and LSTM Models
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: As stress-related disorders grow increasingly common, we need effective therapies that can be widely utilized to detect and manage them early.This research shows how to use machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to find and sort people's stress levels.We gathered textual data that showed emotional and mental states and used typical NLP methods to clean it up.This included tokenization, removing stop words, and TF-IDF vectorization.We used many machine learning models, such as Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Logistic Regression (LR), to sort the stress levels into low, medium, and high.We also trained a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model to fmd patterns in the data that happen in a certain order and have certain significance.We used accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to see how well each model worked.The results show that it is possible to use machine learning and textual signals to locate tension without having to touch the person.This might be useful for keeping an eye on mental health in schools and in corporate wellness initiatives.The research shows that using NLP with both shallow and deep learning models is a good way to understand how people feel.

papers.title: Generative AI in Higher Education: Global Trends, Challenges, and Policy Implications
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral tool to a routine feature of student life in higher education.This paper examines how generative AI, and ChatGPT specifically, is used across global and regional student populations, and what challenges accompany that use.Drawing on secondary analysis of four public survey datasets, including a global sample of 23,218 students across 110 countries (Ravšelj et al., 2025) and three available regional datasets from Bangladesh, Colombia, and Ecuador, the study addresses three research questions concerning prevalence and institutional readiness, task level application and regional variation, and the ethical and institutional challenges tied to AI adoption.Results show that 71.4% of the global sample had used ChatGPT, primarily for brainstorming, summarizing, and research assistance, though usage intensity and institutional policy awareness varied meaningfully by region.The three regional datasets converge on a common theme even though each measure it differently: a substantial share of students report reduced verification behavior and self-perceived overreliance on AI tools, a pattern this paper terms experienced dependency to distinguish it from the abstract ethical concern measured by the global dataset.The paper argues that adoption, ethical concern, and experienced dependency function as related but distinct dimensions rather than opposite poles of a single spectrum, and that institutions should track them independently.Implications for policy, faculty development, and future research are discussed.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Blockchain-Enabled Smart Education Systems: Architecture, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Smart education systems leverage emerging technologies to enhance teaching and learning processes; however, existing systems face challenges such as limited transparency, data security vulnerabilities, and lack of personalization.Technologies including blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and the Internet of Things (IoT) offer promising solutions to these limitations.This paper presents a comprehensive review of blockchain-enabled smart education systems, focusing on their architectures, applications, and implementation frameworks.A systematic analysis of recent literature (2018)(2019)(2020)(2021)(2022)(2023)(2024)(2025) is conducted to evaluate existing approaches based on security, scalability, transparency, and personalization.The study identifies critical research gaps, including interoperability issues, privacy concerns, and integration complexity.To address these challenges, a layered blockchain-enabled framework is proposed, integrating blockchain for secure decentralized data management and AI for adaptive learning.The proposed model enhances trust, ensures data integrity, and supports intelligent decision-making.Finally, future research directions highlight the importance of hybrid architectures, edge computing, and privacy-preserving mechanisms for developing scalable and efficient smart education systems.

papers.title: An Assessment of Green Management and Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Business Management
papers.authors: Ayla AVCI
papers.journal: İktisadi İdari ve Siyasal Araştırmalar Dergisi
papers.abstract: The aim of this study is to examine academic publications on green management published in 2024, identifying key research themes, findings, and relationships with sustainability, environmental performance, and green human resource management. A qualitative research design based on document analysis was adopted for the investigation. Data were gathered from 23 academic publications retrieved via Google Scholar using the keyword “green management”. Selected publications underwent rigorous content analysis, and findings were synthesized thematically alongside geographical and sectoral distributions. China represented the largest share, accounting for 39.1% of all reviewed publications. Research predominantly focused on the corporate sector, followed by higher education, manufacturing, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Notably, none of the examined studies directly addressed green artificial intelligence. The findings indicate that green management is strongly associated with green innovation, environmental performance, resource efficiency, employee environmentally responsible behaviors, and overall organizational sustainability. Green technology adoption, organizational culture, and environmental regulations also emerged as critical drivers. Ultimately, the results underscore the necessity of integrating environmental objectives into core organizational strategies. Future research should explore green management across diverse national and sectoral contexts.

papers.title: Preoperative mixed reality comprehensive cognitive training reduces the incidence of postoperative delirium in older adults undergoing orthopedic surgery: a randomized controlled trial (Preprint)
papers.authors: Deyuan Li, Yanhua Huang, Gen Li, Mingchun Cai, Ao Liu, Lin Zhu, 齐小玲, Tingting Bai, 闻家驷, Lei Wang, Jialin Liu, Yan Luo
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Older surgical patients are frequently affected by postoperative delirium (POD), a complication with serious short- and long-term consequences. Although cognitive prehabilitation holds promise for prevention, its conventional delivery formats suffer from low engagement and poor adherence. OBJECTIVE We sought to determine whether preoperative mixed reality comprehensive cognitive training (MRCC) lowers the incidence of POD in older adults undergoing orthopedic surgery. METHODS In this prospective randomized controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment, 144 patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for elective orthopedic surgery under general anesthesia were allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive MRCC—delivered through mixed reality (MR) glasses in 20-minute daily sessions on the 2 consecutive days before surgery (n=72)—or standard perioperative care (n=72). The primary outcome, the incidence of POD within 7 days after surgery or until hospital discharge (whichever came first), was assessed with the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM). Secondary outcomes comprised delirium characteristics, perioperative electroencephalography (EEG) biomarkers, postoperative pain trajectories, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative cognitive performance (paper-based and MR-based), recovery quality, and patient satisfaction. RESULTS POD occurred in 27 of 144 patients (18.8% overall): 6 of 72 (8.3%) receiving MRCC versus 21 of 72 (29.2%) under standard care, an absolute risk reduction of 20.9% (IRR 0.286, 95% CI 0.123-0.666; P=.004). Among the patients in whom delirium developed, episodes lasted a median of 1 day with MRCC versus 2 days in controls (P=.048). MRCC further improved preoperative sleep quality, attenuated movement-evoked pain, and enhanced postoperative recovery (all P<.001). EEG analyses revealed attenuated pathological delta slowing and preserved complexity of brain signaling. CONCLUSIONS Brief preoperative MRCC significantly lowered the occurrence and duration of POD in older orthopedic patients and was accompanied by improvements in pain, sleep, and neurophysiological function. MR-based cognitive prehabilitation therefore emerges as a promising nonpharmacological option for preventing delirium in this population. CLINICALTRIAL Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2400093319; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=252634

papers.title: Integrating an Ayurveda-based Intervention into the Scheme for Adolescent Girls through Anganwadi Centres to Strengthen Anemia Control in Five Aspirational Districts of India: Protocol for a Type 1 Hybrid Effectiveness–Implementation Study (Preprint)
papers.authors: Deepak Jagannath Londhe, Pallavi Suresh Mundada, Sarada Ota, Jyoti Sharma, Narayanam Srikanth, Brahm Dutt Sharma, Milind N Suryavanshi, Jeuti Rani Das, Meenakshi Pandey, Pratap Makhija, Ranjana Singh, Varsha Sumedhan, Prashant Gupta, Tejaswini Buchade, Susmita Otta, Vanmala B Wakode, Sumed Paikrao, Prem Lal Bharati, Saurav Basu, Preeti H. Negandhi, Purnendu Panda, Abhijeet Kumbhar, Dinesh Kumar Kumawat, Praveen Masram, Renu Makhija, Tushar Walia, Sahil Singh, Hemant Hemant, Naman Goyal, Rabinarayan Acharya
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Anemia affects 59.1% of girls aged 15–19 years in India despite national initiatives such as Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB). The Scheme for Adolescent Girls (SAG), delivered through Anganwadi Centers under Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, offers an established platform for nutrition and health education. Evidence on integrating Ayurveda-based interventions into this platform using implementation science approaches remains limited. OBJECTIVE To evaluate the effectiveness of an integrated Ayurveda-based intervention for anemia delivered alongside routine services under the Scheme for Adolescent Girls (SAG), while assessing its implementation, using a Type 1 hybrid effectiveness–implementation design. METHODS This protocol describes a multicenter study in five Aspirational Districts of India, funded through inter-ministerial collaboration. The intervention combines quality-assured Ayurveda medicines (Krimimudgar Rasa, Drakshavaleha, and Punarnavadi Mandoor) with health education and dietary and lifestyle counseling delivered by trained Ayurveda graduates and Anganwadi Workers, alongside unchanged routine AMB and SAG services. The implementation component covers all willing, eligible girls aged 14 to under 18 years at enrollment. The program-level outcomes, assessed in all enrolled girls, are the change in the proportion of non-anemic girls (point-of-care hemoglobin), shift in anemia severity category, change in clinical signs and symptoms (pallor, fatigue, loss of appetite), thinness by body mass index (BMI)-for-age (World Health Organization [WHO] 2007 reference), and the proportion with at least 70% adherence. The effectiveness component is a 3-month, single-group pre–post evaluation of 301 girls per district, assessed independently by a public health institute. The primary outcome is the change in venous hemoglobin, and the co-primary outcomes are the changes in serum ferritin, fatigue (FACIT-F), and appetite scores. Secondary effectiveness outcomes include anemia status and transitions between severity categories, liver and kidney function, serum iron, total iron-binding capacity, and diet. The implementation outcomes (acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, adoption, fidelity, reach, cost, and sustainability) will be guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) 2.0, Proctor’s framework, RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance), and the Intervention Scalability Assessment Tool. RESULTS The protocol was sanctioned on March 18, 2024, and its final version was revised on October 29, 2024. Enrollment began on October 25, 2024, in the implementation component (77,633 girls enrolled by June 30, 2025) and on December 21, 2024, in the effectiveness component (1,587 girls across the five districts). Final follow-up was completed on September 30, 2025. Data analysis is ongoing, and results will be reported separately. This manuscript reports the protocol only. CONCLUSIONS The study is expected to provide evidence on the effectiveness and real-world implementation of an integrated Ayurveda-based intervention within an existing national anemia program, informing its integration and scale-up for adolescent anemia in India and comparable settings. CLINICALTRIAL Clinical Trials Registry–India CTRI/2024/10/075128; URL https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTEzMzk0&Enc=&userName=CTRI/2024/10/075128

papers.title: Intercultural Sensitivity, Perceived AI Usefulness, and Willingness to Communicate among Indonesian EFL Learners
papers.authors: Anita Kurnia, Yazid Basthomi, Utami Widiati, Bambang Yudi Cahyono, Tengku Intan Suzila Tengku Sharif
papers.journal: Vision Journal for Language and Foreign Language Learning
papers.abstract: Willingness to communicate is a fundamental pillar of successful language acquisition; however, learners of English as a foreign language in developing countries such as Indonesia often have limited opportunities for real-world intercultural interaction, which can hinder their communicative readiness. As generative artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into language learning, it remains unclear whether its perceived usefulness genuinely fosters intercultural readiness. This study examined whether intercultural sensitivity mediates the relationship between perceived usefulness of artificial intelligence and willingness to communicate in this population. Data were collected from 113 university students through a cross-sectional survey and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling.
