papers.title: Developing an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Assisted Instrument for Assessing the Short Story Writing Skills of Grade XI Students at Senior High School
papers.authors: Andy Dahnial Pratama Mz, Ida Nuraeni, Sukma
papers.journal: IDEAS Journal on English Language Teaching and Learning Linguistics and Literature
papers.abstract: Assessing short story writing is prone to subjectivity when it is not supported by a valid and reliable instrument, while the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in drafting assessment instruments has rarely been documented. This study aims to describe the development process and the quality of an AI-assisted instrument for assessing the short story writing skills of grade XI students at SMA Al-Azhar Mandiri Palu. It followed the 4D development model (define, design, develop, disseminate), with AI (Claude Opus 5.5) serving as a drafting aid rather than as a rater of students’ work. Data were collected through interviews, observation, document analysis, validation by five experts, the scoring of 30 short stories by two teachers, and a practicality questionnaire, and were analyzed using feasibility percentages, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Cronbach’s alpha, percentage agreement, and practicality percentages. The AI generated 32 rubric descriptors from a single prompt. After the researcher’s review, 12 descriptors were accepted unchanged, 17 were revised to make them observable and consistent with the quantitative requirement, and 3 were rejected because they relied on impressionistic criteria. The 12 descriptors accepted unchanged were later revised on the language validator’s advice, so none of the AI-generated descriptors was used unchanged in the final product. The instrument obtained a feasibility percentage of 92.63% (very valid), a single-measures ICC of 0.758 (good; 95% CI 0.541–0.878), and a practicality percentage of 98.33% (very practical). Cronbach’s alpha was low (−0.224 and 0.251) because scores clustered at the top of the scale, while exact inter-rater agreement reached 94.17%. The instrument is feasible for use, and AI is effective as a drafting aid provided that its output is reviewed by the researcher and validated by experts.

papers.title: Harnessing AI for Inclusive Education: Strategies and Tools for Supporting University Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
papers.authors: Ioana Kocurová-Giurgiu, Miluše Löffelmannová, Zuzana Havlisová
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education presents transformative opportunities for enhancing learning experiences, particularly for neurodivergent students. This paper explores AI-driven strategies and tools designed to support university students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) by fostering structured learning, effective communication, and adaptive teaching approaches. Key strategies include maintaining predictable course structures, employing multimodal teaching methods, and offering individualized support to accommodate diverse learning needs. AI applications such as lecture transcription, text-to-speech conversion, and adaptive learning platforms provide personalized learning experiences. Additionally, assistive technologies play an increasingly vital role in inclusive higher education. Recent studies highlight how AI-driven assistive tools enhance accessibility and academic performance for students with learning difficulties. Furthermore, AI-enhanced assistive technologies are evolving to address the unique challenges of neurodivergent learners, offering solutions to improve focus, comprehension, and social communication in higher education settings. Beyond academic support, AI-powered virtual assistants, chatbots, and social interaction tools help students navigate both academic and social challenges. Educators play a critical role in fostering a neurodivergent-friendly environment through peer mentoring, flexible assessment methods, and conflict resolution strategies. This paper discusses best practices, implementation challenges, and the evolving role of AI in neurodiverse education, ultimately highlighting how AI can bridge gaps in learning and social engagement for students with ASD in a business school in the Czech Republic.

papers.title: INDONESIA-PHILIPPINES LECTURER COLLABORATION IN TECHNOLOGY-BASED EMPOWERMENT OF MSMES AND HONEY BEEKEEPERS: AN INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY SERVICE AT THE 1ST AFEBSI CONGRESS
papers.authors: Yossinomita Yossinomita, Effiyaldi Effiyaldi, Herry Mulyono, Joni Devitra, Hanan Laras Sabrina, Daniel Dasig Jr, Nila Krisnawati, Hero Wirasmara Kusuma, Arna Suryani, Endang Purwaningsih, Nurul Hidayah
papers.abstract: The healthy lifestyle trend has created market opportunities for natural-product MSMEs, including honey beekeepers, yet natural resources do not automatically become competitive advantage due to limited digital literacy, packaging, marketing, and branding capacity. This international community service program aimed to empower MSMEs and honey beekeepers through digital marketing, artificial intelligence, and e-commerce to enhance competitiveness and expand market reach. The program was conducted as part of the 1st AFEBSI Congress by DPN AFEBSI with Philippine Women’s University in Jakarta on October 14, 2026, involving approximately 126 lecturers from universities across Indonesia who served as the implementation team representing their respective campuses. The community service team came from Dinamika Bangsa University, Philippine Women’s University, Swiss German University, Faletehan University, Muhammadiyah University of Jambi, Pignatelli Triputra University, and Mercu Buana University. The program was carried out through focus group discussions (FGDs) in several groups that brought together speakers from the Philippines and lecturers from Indonesia, using the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Pentahelix collaboration as the analytical framework. The FGD results show that honey is a valuable resource that becomes a competitive advantage only when managed through quality management, packaging, branding, and digital marketing, and supported by collaboration among academia, business, community, government, and media. The program also strengthened cross-country and cross-university academic networks. Empowering MSMEs and honey beekeepers requires continuous lecturer-led mentoring, consistent product quality, and producer integrity to maintain consumer trust.

papers.title: Navigating the AI Era: How Perceived Organizational Support Shapes Employees’ AI-Related Anxiety via AI Self-Efficacy
papers.authors: Hind Alsudays, Sultanah Alsudays
papers.journal: Dove Medical Press (Taylor and Francis Group)
papers.abstract: Hind A Alsudays,1 Sultanah Alsudays21Department of Business Administration, College of Business, Majmaah University, Al Majmaah, 11952, Saudi Arabia; 2Department of Business Administration, College of Business, Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University (IMSIU), Riyadh, Saudi ArabiaCorrespondence: Sultanah Alsudays, Department of Business Administration, College of Business, Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University (IMSIU), Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Email Smalsudays@imamu.edu.saPurpose: This quantitative study examined the relationships between perceived organizational support (POS), Artificial intelligence self-efficacy (AISE), employees’ artificial intelligence learning anxiety (AILA), and AI job replacement anxiety (AIJRA) in private sector employees; it examined the potential direct effect of POS on both AILA and AIJRA, and the indirect effect via AISE by drawing on social cognitive theory and using structural equation modeling (SEM).Participants and Methods: Convenience and snowball sampling techniques were used to recruit 311 employees from the private sector in the Saudi context. Data were collected using an online survey and analyzed using Mplus to conduct confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and SEM.Results: In the total sample, POS influences AI learning anxiety only via AI self-efficacy (β = - 0.073; p ≤ 0.01). However, AI job replacement anxiety was influenced only directly by POS (β = − 0.184; p ≤ 0.01). These findings suggest that the relative importance of organizational and individual factors varies based on the type of AI anxiety. Finally, Age has a significant and negative relationship with AIJRA (β = − 0.121, P ≤ 0.05).Conclusion: The Study’s findings underscore the importance of individual factors such as AISE in enhancing the role of POS on AILA. Furthermore, These findings suggest that the relative importance of organizational and individual factors varies based on the type of AI anxiety.Keywords: perceived organizational support, artificial intelligence self-efficacy, artificial intelligence learning anxiety, artificial intelligence job replacement anxiety, social cognitive theory, Saudi private sector

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity Violations: Implications for Undergraduate Research
papers.authors: David Reamer
papers.journal: Journal of International Crisis and Risk Communication Research
papers.abstract: The use of generative artificial intelligence (genAI) tools by undergraduates is a well-documented phenomenon, with studies showing adoption rates by undergraduate students as high as 85% (Flaherty, 2025), often without regard for academic integrity norms such as source attribution and ethical data collection. This IRB-approved study examines filed academic integrity violations at a single institution from 2020-2025, covering five semesters prior to the public release of ChatGPT and five semesters after its release, in order to uncover trends related to genAI adoption and provide insights for faculty and administrators of undergraduate research programs.

papers.title: Better Connections at Zero Cost: Rethinking Undergraduate Research Communication
papers.authors: Hannah Bevan, Ashley Spring
papers.journal: Journal of International Crisis and Risk Communication Research
papers.abstract: Undergraduate research programs depend on communication among students, mentors, and program staff, but keeping everyone connected and organized can be a challenge. Important forms, deadlines, and resources can easily become lost in a web of emails. Meanwhile, program staff need ways to efficiently communicate with different research groups, and mentors may lack the time to create polished resources. Our solution? Use tools we already have! This presentation will share how we use our institution’s learning management system (LMS), with support from generative AI, to create a more organized and welcoming undergraduate research experience at no additional cost. LMS features such as groups and tags allow us to organize participants and target communication, while AI-assisted HTML helps transform existing information into clear, visually engaging resources without requiring coding expertise. These changes reduce administrative headaches, make information easier to find, and improve communication among students, mentors, and program staff. Attendees will leave with practical strategies they can adapt within their own LMS, without purchasing new software or giving students and faculty one more platform to navigate.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity and Digital Learning Resilience in Higher Education: An Integrative Review and Capacity-Sensitive Framework for Resource-Constrained Universities
papers.authors: Nsangaette Asuquo Udo, Khama Valentine Arinze, Irene Chinyere Ezugwu, Adesegun Nurudeen Osijirin
papers.journal: Asian Journal of Research in Computer Science
papers.abstract: Purpose: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now embedded in teaching, assessment and administration in higher education, simultaneously widening educational opportunity and institutional cyber exposure. Experimental evidence shows that large language models lower the cost of persuasive phishing, while AI-text detectors and automated proctoring raise reliability and fairness concerns. AI-assisted defence offers measurable triage benefits but introduces false alarms, concept drift, privacy exposure and automation bias. Originality/Value: The proposed AI-Cybersecurity-Digital Learning Resilience (AIC-DLR) Framework adapts NIST CSF 2.0 functions to the educational mission, overlays NIST AI risk-management guidance, and treats usable, equitable recovery of teaching and assessment, rather than system restoration alone, as the protected outcome. papers.title: Readiness of AI (Artificial Intelligence) strategies Used in Nursing Education among Undergraduate Nursing Students “A Cross Sectional Descriptive Survey”
papers.authors: Samrin Nanji, Mujeebullah, Rahool, Muhammad Asif, Yashwa Qaisar, Elisha Yaqoob, Summera Sultan, Mahpara
papers.journal: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
papers.abstract: The aim of this quantitative cross sectional survey is to describe the frequencies of readiness of AI (Artificial Intelligence) in nursing education among undergraduate nursing students. Methodology of this research included, the design of this research is cross sectional descriptive study, sample size was N=50 undergraduate nursing students of first year first semester. Sampling technique was simple random sampling and setting was a Nursing College in private University. The data was analyzing by SPSS AMOS-23 software. The TAM (Technology Acceptance Model) was used to collect the data basically this tool was adopted from a Pakistani research article the validity and reliability of the tool has been mentioned in methodology section in chapter 3. A total of 50 undergraduate nursing students participated in the study examining readiness for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) strategies in nursing education. The demographic findings showed an equal distribution of male and female participants, with 25 (50%) students in each group. Regarding age, the majority of participants, 47 (94%), were aged 21–23 years, while 3 (6%) were aged 24–26 years. Regarding the perceived usefulness of AI strategies in nursing education, all participants reported negative responses to the statement that AI strategies improved their learning outcomes, with 26 (52%) strongly disagreeing and 24 (48%) disagreeing. For the statement that AI tools could help students understand complex nursing concepts, 18 (36%) strongly disagreed, 11 (22%) disagreed, 11 (22%) remained neutral, and 10 (20%) strongly agreed. Similarly, 42 (84%) participants disagreed or strongly disagreed that AI-based learning resources could improve their clinical decision-making skills, while 4 (8%) were neutral and 4 (8%) strongly agreed. Regarding whether AI strategies could make nursing studies more productive, 17 (34%) strongly disagreed, 12 (24%) disagreed, 11 (22%) were neutral, and 10 (20%) strongly agreed. All participants (100%) disagreed with the statement that AI tools could help them prepare more effectively for nursing examinations. The study revealed low readiness among undergraduate nursing students towards the use of AI strategies in nursing education. Most participants reported negative perceptions regarding AI usefulness, ease of use and integration into academic activities. The findings highlight the need for structured AI literacy training, practical guidance and education on the responsible use of AI. Further research with larger sample is recommended to explore student’s readiness for AI integration in nursing education.

papers.title: Lowering the Barrier to International Publishing: AI-Assisted Publication-Readiness Assessment for Central Asian Researchers
papers.authors: Akbarov Nurislom
papers.abstract: Researchers in Central Asia usually think and write in Uzbek, Russian or Kazakh but must publish in English or in venues with strict formal requirements, and higher-education reform has multiplied the number of manuscripts expected of them. Tools that could help are scarce for Uzbek, and general-purpose language models make confident but wrong corrections. This paper presents Imlox, a publication-readiness report that combines a deterministic Uzbek language core with a large language model (Claude Haiku 4.5) used only as a bounded verifier. All evaluation is synthetic: errors were injected into held-out sentences, and thresholds and test sets were pre-registered and sealed. On the first sealed set (30 September 2026), a naive union of core and model reached a precision of only 0.463 and failed its gate. After the model's role was restricted, a second sealed set of 330 sentences with 221 injected errors gave precision of 0.895 to 0.906 and recall of 0.674 to 0.810; a fourth run's recall fell to 0.624. By 17 October 2026, 476 manuscripts had received readiness reports in shadow mode. A tightly bounded model can raise recall in a low-resource language without sacrificing precision, but recall is not yet stable. The figures are preliminary.

papers.title: Design Innovation and Collaborative Supply Chain Management in the Development of Animation Derivatives
papers.authors: Zheng Sun
papers.abstract: The rapid development of animation-related derivative products is undergoing a transition from full-process production in traditional factories to modularized division of tasks and supply chain collaboration. In 2025, the market size of derivative products tied to the animation industry reached RMB 652.1 billion, while the total retail value of collectible toys stood at RMB 67.69 billion, with new categories such as rotocast plush toys and AI-powered toys showing notable and sustained growth. However, beneath this rapid industry growth, the dual challenges of design homogenization on the creative side and lagging supply chain responsiveness on the manufacturing side have severely constrained both product quality and development efficiency. Drawing on comprehensive industry survey data, this paper systematically analyzes the manifestations and root causes of insufficient design innovation and supply chain collaboration failures in the development of animation derivatives. Countermeasures are proposed from four dimensions: deep intellectual property-based transformation, design process reengineering, industrial cluster collaboration, and flexible manufacturing adoption of advanced technologies. The study suggests that modular decomposition of components and specialized division of tasks provide an effective pathway to enhancing overall product quality. Furthermore, the quantitative management of supply chain collaboration plays a significant role in shortening delivery lead times and improving overall operational efficiency within the creative manufacturing sector, ultimately fostering sustainable market competitiveness.

papers.title: Quem faz cada etapa? A IA generativa como executora de tarefas e a mudança na rotina de trabalho
papers.authors: Daniela Hayoshi
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools have spread rapidly among professionals, and experiments show substantial gains on isolated tasks. Yet average effects on earnings and recorded hours have been small, although changes in task organization are already evident. This conceptual article proposes that an important part of this gap is explained by how people represent the technology: generative AI tends to be perceived as a question-and-answer tool rather than as an executor of process steps, let alone of recurring routines that keep running while the person only checks the result. Drawing on literatures on the task-based approach in labor economics, levels of automation, trust and overreliance in automated systems, work design and redesign, sociotechnical frames, transfer of training, and habit formation, the article develops a five-element model (perception, decomposition, allocation, verification, and routinization) and argues that the relevant question shifts from “how do I ask?” to “who performs each step?”, with three possible destinations for each step: AI alone, AI with human verification, or the person. Seven testable propositions are formulated, and implications for research, training design, and organizations are discussed. The article presents no new data; its contribution is to organize dispersed evidence into an explicit, falsifiable mechanism.

papers.title: Inteligência artificial na educação e neuroplasticidade: contribuições, limites e desafios para a aprendizagem
papers.authors: Daniela Hayoshi
papers.abstract: The literature on artificial intelligence (AI) in education focuses almost exclusively on performance, perception, and engagement; brain changes associated with neuroplasticity have rarely been measured. This narrative review, using explicit search and classification criteria, distinguishes three types of evidence: (a) learning outcomes (grades, retention, and transfer), (b) behavioral measures of cognitive effort, and (c) direct neurophysiological measures (EEG and fNIRS). The most robust performance studies indicate that the effects of AI depend on task design: a randomized trial involving approximately one thousand high school students found gains ranging from 48% to 127% during AI-assisted practice, while performance declined on an exam taken without AI among students with unrestricted access to the model; this decline was eliminated when the system was configured to provide hints rather than answers. The most frequently cited meta-analysis supporting AI (g = 0.867) was retracted in 2026 due to analytical errors and the inclusion of invalid studies. The few studies using brain-based measures are small (n ranging from 24 to 54), short in duration, unpublished in peer-reviewed journals or reporting null findings, and assess momentary engagement rather than lasting structural or functional plasticity. It is therefore concluded that there is no basis for claiming that AI, by itself, either enhances or impairs neuroplasticity. The evidence supports a narrower conclusion: activities that replace retrieval and elaborative effort tend to reduce measured learning, whereas activities that preserve such effort tend to maintain or enhance learning gains. A research agenda is proposed incorporating longitudinal designs, transfer measures, and pre- and post-intervention neuroimaging with active control conditions.

papers.title: Secondary education teachers' perspectives on the use of ChatGPT in teaching
papers.authors: MEGALOMYSTAKA CHRISTINA, TSAOUSIDOU IOANNA
papers.abstract: This study explores the attitudes and level of readiness of secondary education teachers regarding the integration of ChatGPT into teaching. Adopting a mixed-methods approach utilizing a questionnaire, the study examined a sample of teachers from two schools in Central Macedonia. The findings reveal an attitude of cautious optimism. Participants acknowledge the tool"s significant utility in lesson preparation and material creation, which saves valuable time. However, they express strong concerns regarding the reliability of information, ethical issues, the absence of a regulatory framework within schools, and the risk of undermining students" critical thinking. In conclusion, although artificial intelligence is envisioned as a future digital assistant, there is an urgent need for systematic and experiential institutional training for teachers to ensure its pedagogically safe utilization.

papers.title: PSYCHOMETRIC OPERATIONALIZATION OF FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AUTONOMOUS MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS BASED ON PERSONAMATRIX: AN AI TRANSITIONAL FIELD FRAMEWORK
papers.authors: Anatoliy Drobakha, Liudmyla Lahuta
papers.abstract: Background: Autonomous LLM agents increasingly operate in shared environments where behavior depends on interaction history, role allocation, local norms, authority, and group structure. Objective: This conceptual methods paper develops a psychometric operationalization of dynamic functional roles in autonomous multi-agent systems using PersonaMatrix-derived measurement principles without attributing human psychological ontology to AI. Methods: A targeted evidence synthesis (2019–2026) was conducted across AI psychometrics, dynamic multi-agent roles, collective-field modeling, norm emergence, trajectory prediction, and anthropomorphism. Peer-reviewed sources were prioritized, while current OpenAI, METR/Redwood, Anthropic, and Moltbook materials were used as primary or emerging evidence for recent agent ecosystems. Results: The framework separates output-level stability (RSI, IDS, RCS) from role-level and field-level constructs. It proposes the Functional Role Consistency Index, Role Transition Index, Agent–Field Differentiation Index, Collective Utility Index, Norm Conflict Index, Regulatory Closure Index, and Field Role Composition Vector. Three falsifiable hypotheses test whether role variables add out-of-sample predictive value for agent behavior, role transitions, and future field states. Conclusion: PersonaMatrix is positioned as a measurement architecture rather than an AI personality diagnosis. The archetypal-role hypothesis is supported only if role coding is reliable, improves prediction beyond non-archetypal baselines, and generalizes to unseen agents and independent multi-agent environments.

papers.title: Modern Methods of Increasing Students’ Motivation in Learning English
papers.authors: Umarova Muhayyo Abdusattor qizi, Marxabo Jurayeva
papers.abstract: This article provides a theoretical and analytical overview of modern methods for increasing students’ motivation to learn English. It examines the concept of motivation, intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, the factors affecting students’ interest in language learning, and contemporary pedagogical approaches. Particular attention is given to digital technologies, artificial intelligence tools, gamification, and interactive activities as means of enhancing learning motivation. The article also discusses the role of teachers in creating a supportive learning environment. In addition, the benefits of modern motivational methods and the potential challenges of applying them in English language education are considered.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF CHATGPT ON MORPHO-SYNTACTIC AWARENESS AMONG GENERATION-Z ESL LEARNERS IN PAKISTAN: A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL STUDY
papers.authors: Muhammad Tayyab Khan, Marya Sarwar, Tariq Usman
papers.journal: Insights (Bhalwal) International Journal of Humanities Management and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly become a part of education, revolutionizing language learning by offering interactive, personalized and instant linguistic help to students. One AI-powered tool that has garnered a lot of attention recently is ChatGPT, which can help with English as a Second Language (ESL) learning, especially in grammar. But, empirical research about its effect on learners' morpho-syntactic awareness is limited particularly in the context of Pakistan. The present study aimed to examine the effects of ChatGPT on the morpho-syntactic awareness of Generation-Z ESL learners in Pakistan employing a quantitative quasi-experimental pre and post-test control group design. The total number of samples were 80 undergraduate students of ESL and consequently 40 students were assigned to experimental group and 40 students were assigned to control group using convenience sampling. The experimental group participated in the grammar learning using ChatGPT for six weeks, while the control group were taught the grammar in a traditional manner. The experimental group was given six weeks of grammar instruction that involved ChatGPT while the control group was given six weeks of traditional grammar instruction. The data were collected by using researcher developed morpho-syntactic awareness test and a structured questionnaire. The quantitative data was analyzed using descriptive statistics, paired-samples t-tests, and independent-samples t-tests in SPSS and the responses on the questionnaires were summarized using descriptive analysis. The results showed that the morpheo-syntactic awareness of learners who used Chat-GPT was statistically significantly better than that of learners who were taught by the traditional method. The participants also had positive perceptions of the usefulness, prompt feedback, and helping them with grammar of ChatGPT, but they also mentioned some concerns about becoming dependent on ChatGPT and not being able to do this alone. The study finds that ChatGPT can be used as a useful additional teaching aid to enhance the grammatical ability of students when used in pedagogically guided learning environment. The results build on a body of research on using generative AI for language learning and have implications for both ESL teachers and curriculum designers and policymakers who want to facilitate responsible use of generative AI in language learning.

papers.title: The Axiology of Arabic Language Education in the Age of Generative AI: Toward an Integrative Framework of Educational Values
papers.authors: Ulwi Albab
papers.abstract: The presence of of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Arabic language education raises fundamental questions about educational purposes and values. This qualitative conceptual study, based on a literature review, aims to reconstruct the axiological foundations of Arabic language education by integrating intrinsic, instrumental, and transformative values. The study employs critical philosophical analysis and theoretical synthesis. The findings identify three educational value orientations: linguistic and cultural understanding, communicative competence and social participation, and the development of critical thinking, learner agency, and ethical responsibility. Their integration yields four pedagogical principles: justification of educational purposes, alignment between learning and assessment, source traceability, and human accountability. This study contributes an integrative normative framework for guiding curriculum development, teaching, assessment, and responsible AI governance in Arabic language education.

papers.title: COMMUNICATION ACCOMMODATION IN HUMAN–AI INTERACTION: A CORPUS-ASSISTED SOCIOLINGUISTIC STUDY OF PAKISTANI UNIVERSITY STUDENTS’ DISCOURSE WITH CHATGPT | Journal of Applied Linguistics and TESOL (JALT)
papers.authors: Author Contributor

papers.title: Conversational AI as a Compliance Layer for Mandatory Digital Resident-Communication Regulation: Evidence from a Multi-Region Deployment in Urban Housing Management
papers.authors: Alexander Romashchenko
papers.abstract: Cities increasingly regulate not only the content but the channel of communication between service providers and residents, backing such requirements with fines; manual compliance is costly for the small operators typically covered by such rules. We analyze telemetry from an AI assistant operating in residential building chats in multiple regions of Russia (1 January – 8 September 2026) around the effective date of Government Resolution No. 40, which made the same channel mandatory for housing organizations (fines up to RUB 300,000, ≈€3,000 at early-2026 exchange rates). The assistant's response-generation feature was active for one month, of which the final eight days followed the mandate's effective date. Verification approval - 85.5% among residents who submitted documents - is computed on documents actually submitted, not on the much larger pre-provisioned base (Section 5.3).

papers.title: Quality Management in Technical and Vocational Education Institutions in Libya in the Context of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: حسين عقيل حسين عقيل, Hussin Akeel Hussin Akeel
papers.journal: Journal of Scientific and Human Dimensions
papers.abstract: تتناول هذه الورقة البحثية موضوع إدارة الجودة في المؤسسات التعليمية التقنية والفنية في ليبيا، مع التركيز على تطبيقات الإدارة والجودة في ظل الذكاء الاصطناعي. يهدف البحث إلى تقديم دراسة شاملة تحلل الوضع الراهن، وتحدد التحديات والفرص، وتقدم توصيات عملية لتحسين الأداء والجودة المؤسسية. باستخدام المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، تستعرض الورقة الإطار النظري لإدارة الجودة في التعليم التقني، وتناقش النماذج الدولية المعتمدة مثل مواصفة ISO 21001:2025 ونموذج EFQM للتميز. كما تفحص توظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في أنظمة ضمان الجودة، مع تحليل السياق الليبي من خلال مراجعة الأدبيات والدراسات الميدانية والتقارير الرسمية. خلصت الدراسة إلى أن المؤسسات التقنية والفنية في ليبيا تواجه فجوة بين متطلبات معايير الجودة والتطبيق الفعلي، وأن توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي لا يزال في مستوى متوسط ومحدود، وأن التبني وحده لا يكفل تحقيق الأثر المرجو على القيمة المضافة. وتوصي الورقة بضرورة تبني إطار وطني متكامل لإدارة الجودة في التعليم التقني، وبناء القدرات الرقمية للكوادر التعليمية والإدارية، وتطوير البنية التحتية التكنولوجية، وتعزيز الشراكات مع سوق العمل، واستثمار الذكاء الاصطناعي في أتمتة عمليات ضمان الجودة والتحليل التنبؤي وتخصيص التعلم.
keywords: technical and vocational education and training

papers.title: Neural categorisation of rhythm in human newborns
papers.authors: Francesca M. Barbero, Tomas Lenc, Alban Gallard, Nori Jacoby, Rainer Polak, Manuel Varlet, Arthur Foulon, Sahar Moghimi, Sylvie Nozaradan
papers.abstract: Abstract Music is ubiquitous across cultures, and humans engage in social interactions through music from early in life. A cornerstone of these interactions is rhythm categorisation, allowing the sheer diversity of rhythmic inputs to be mapped onto internal rhythm categories. The pervasiveness of certain rhythm categories across cultures suggests that rhythm categorisation may be partially rooted in neurobiological predispositions constraining the internal representations of rhythm. However, this view appears to conflict with the diversity of music practices across cultures, which points to a role of experience in rhythm categorisation. To assess the relative contributions of neurobiological predispositions and experience, we tested 0- to 3-day-old newborns, capitalising on their minimal postnatal experience with music. Using electroencephalography (EEG), we recorded, in newborns and adults, brain responses to drum sounds whose pattern of relative interval duration ranged from isochronous to long-short rhythms (1:1 – 2:1 interval ratio). Results indicate significant categorisation in newborns’ neural responses, with a representational structure that correlate with those of adults, yet with a greater degree of differentiation across rhythms. These findings reveal neurobiological predispositions enabling rhythm categorisation to be present at birth and further shaped across the lifespan, highlighting the evolutionary roots and plasticity supporting this human cultural practice.

papers.title: Exploring generative AI appropriation in Colombian adults’ informal English learning
papers.authors: Mariana Mora Gaitán, Jenny Catalina Loaiza Fuquen
papers.journal: Ibero Ciencias - Revista Científica y Académica
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming the possibilities for informal language learning by providing immediate feedback, conversational interaction, and potentially personalized learning experiences. However, its use does not necessarily entail greater learner autonomy, self-regulation, or agency. This study aimed to understand how Colombian adults configure their informal English learning practices through GenAI tools, with particular attention to decision-making processes, self-regulation, evaluation of AI-generated responses, and the articulation of GenAI with other learning resources. Adopting a qualitative, exploratory, and interpretive approach, the study involved four Colombian adults with diverse linguistic, educational, and GenAI-use trajectories. Data were generated through participant characterization forms, GenAI interaction records, semi-structured interviews, and, when available, documentary evidence of participants’ interactions with the technology. A predominantly inductive thematic analysis generated four interconnected categories: negotiating control over the learning interaction; constructing and calibrating trust in AI-generated feedback; experiencing personalization through responsive interaction; and reconfiguring the broader learning repertoire. Findings show that participants assumed, negotiated, and delegated control in different ways and developed varying criteria for accepting, questioning, or verifying GenAI-generated responses. They also selectively integrated GenAI with other digital and human learning resources. Based on these findings, the study conceptualizes GenAI appropriation as a form of situated orchestration through which learners coordinate technological affordances with their purposes, prior knowledge, evaluative criteria, and broader learning repertoires. The findings suggest that GenAI does not automatically produce learner autonomy or agency; rather, it creates new spaces in which these may be exercised, negotiated, or delegated.

papers.title: Re-Engineering General Foundation Mathematics for STEM Readiness in Oman: A Curriculum Alignment and Comparative Readiness Analysis
papers.authors: Dheva Rajan S, Mini Punnolli, Asim Thabit Talib Almaamari, Madhan Narayanan
papers.journal: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)
papers.abstract: A basic mathematical foundation, as part of a knowledge-based educational framework aligned with Oman Vision 2040, could serve as the intellectual foundation for STEM development. The Mathematics course in the General Foundation Program (GFP) at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences (UTAS) is vital for students planning to pursue fields such as information technology, artificial intelligence, engineering, and data science. However, concerns remain significant as the program focuses on procedural skills and is less focused on analytical reasoning and modeling. The CDP has a digital math literacy component, but it is limited. None of the previous attempts to assess structured curriculum mapping has proven effective. Through structured curriculum mapping and a comparative readiness analysis, this study examines Course Learning Outcomes, Course Objectives, assessment plans, course delivery strategies, and proposed revisions aligned with a 10-dimensional STEM Readiness Framework. It also considers the spread of Bloom's taxonomy. The paper notes observed alignment gaps, graphically documents them, and benchmarks insights from Harvard University’s mathematics pathways against policy recommendations. Results demonstrated around 70% agreement in content but also highlighted discrepancies between evaluation and instruction in two specific areas: modeling and decision-making under uncertainty, as well as digital exploration. Even though the same applies to the requirements for using general skills for knowledge, in the higher cognitive sphere, these limitations are even more severe. Proposed revisions include strengthened analytical and practical competencies, moving from bridge to cognitive enhancement. Advancing IT and engineering readiness, incorporating the IT cum technology-oriented concepts in mathematics, will help sustain existing STEM growth here.

papers.title: Investigating the Impact of AI-Facilitated Socratic Dialogue on Critical Thinking Skills
papers.authors: Siti Sarah Abdur Rani, Sumia Salim Al Hadrami
papers.journal: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)
papers.abstract: This mixed-method study aims to explore the impact of having Socratic dialogue with artificial intelligence (AI) on students' critical thinking skills’ performance. The data were gathered from 35 foundation-level students. The study utilised a Watson Glaser critical thinking pre-test and post-test to measure their critical thinking abilities and a questionnaire to gather their perception of AI usage. During the intervention, students were engaged in structured AI-facilitated Socratic questioning sessions weekly. Data were analysed using paired-sample t-tests and linear regression, while survey responses were examined for thematic trends. Even though the data collected shows that students have a positive perception of using AI, there is no statistically significant difference between the pre- and post-tests (p > .05). The finding shows that students’ critical thinking performance did not improve throughout the study. Furthermore, the results for the linear regression (R² = 0.038, p > .05) show that there is very little correlation between students’ perception and their critical thinking performance. The study reveals the gap between students’ positive perception of using AI and their critical thinking skill development.

papers.title: Empowering Omani EFL Learners through AI-Based Vocabulary Instruction: Reimagining Next Generation
papers.authors: Ameena Mohamed Ali, Afrah Al Busaidi
papers.journal: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)
papers.abstract: This study emphasizes the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in aiding Omani students in the General Foundation Program to learn English as a Foreign Language (EFL). Despite the growing use of AI tools like ChatGPT, Google Translate, and Grammarly, there is limited research in Oman on learners' attitudes and the implications of AI for vocabulary instruction. A mixed-methods research design was used, and the sample comprised 151 respondents studying in the Sultanate of Oman. SPSS version 29 was used to analyze the quantitative data. The qualitative data revealed that EFL Omani students relied heavily on ChatGPT (49.7%) as the most widely used AI tool, followed by Google Translate (21.2%), Gemini AI (17.9%), Grammarly (6.6%). In addition, the trust in AI (frequency: 60), followed by cross-checking the meaning with other reliable resources (frequency: 67), learner autonomy (frequency: 67), and academic honesty (frequency: 64), but learning grammar, enhancing writing and reading skills had the lowest frequency. The quantitative data indicate an overall mean score of 3.67, suggesting a high frequency of AI tool use for vocabulary learning. The lowest mean score, 3.45, corresponds to the students' trust in the new vocabulary suggested by AI tools. In contrast, the effectiveness of AI tools received the highest mean score of 3.92. Additionally, it was found that AI tools, learners' attitudes and challenges, learning strategies, digital literacy, and how factors such as gender and academic level affect AI-assisted vocabulary learning in EFL Omani students were examined for vocabulary acquisition.

papers.title: General Foundation Programs in Oman: A Comparative Study of Standards and Outcomes
papers.authors: Mohamed Elamin
papers.journal: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)
papers.abstract: This study primarily aims to compare the Oman Academic Standards for General Foundation Programs (OASGFPs) with the draft of the Oman Core Academic Learning Outcomes (OCALOs), identifying their similarities and differences and exploring their implications for the expectations and positioning of General Foundation Programs (GFPs) in the Oman Qualifications Framework (OQF). Using a qualitative document analysis approach, the study compares key elements of the two frameworks, including learning outcomes, curriculum structure, subject requirements, and international English language proficiency standards. The findings suggest that OCALOs can be viewed as a developmental extension of OASGFPs, introducing refined learning outcomes and curriculum innovations, including emerging topics like artificial intelligence (AI). However, several issues require further consideration, including inconsistencies in specifying instructional time across subjects and the extent of institutional flexibility. The study also highlights the need to review the targeted international English language proficiency levels to ensure alignment with entry-level and current postgraduate admission requirements. Given that OCALOs remain in draft form, the observations presented may assist policymakers, higher education institutions, and GFP educators in refining national foundation program policies and practices in Oman.

papers.title: The pedagogical impact of AI-Assisted idea generation on self-efficacy and idea development skills in general foundation program students' research-based essay
papers.authors: Ahoud Yaqoob Al-Kuwaili, Sheema Amtul Hai
papers.journal: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)
papers.abstract: Foundation Program students often struggle to generate research ideas and organise their thoughts when writing research-based essays, which can undermine their confidence and academic performance. Traditional assessment methods provide limited insight into students' independent development of ideas. However, recent advances in educational technology, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), offer new opportunities to support learning. This study aims to investigate the pedagogical impact of AI-assisted idea generation on General Foundation Program (GFP) students' self-efficacy and idea-generating skills in research-based essay writing. The study adopts a quantitative research design using a single-group pre-test and post-test approach. The sample consists of 25 randomly selected GFP students. The intervention is conducted over a period of 4-6 weeks. Students use ChatGPT as their primary AI tool for brainstorming, outlining, and refining ideas. Students' self-efficacy is measured based on a structured questionnaire, while idea development skills are assessed through a writing rubric. Data is analysed using paired-sample comparison. The results indicate improvement in both self-efficacy and idea development. The study highlights the importance of integrating AI tools into writing instruction to enhance student confidence and performance.

papers.title: Closing the Gap: An Action Research Study on Synchronizing EnglishLanguage and Computing Skills Curricula in an Omani General Foundation Program
papers.authors: Anitra Hernandez,  Jitha Challipat Jayathilak, Moza Al Rujaibi
papers.journal: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)
papers.abstract: Historically, General Foundation Programs (GFPs) in Oman have delivered Foundation English Language Learning (FEL) and Foundation Computing Skills (FCS) as parallel but non-communicating courses. The June 2025 revision of the Oman Core Academic Learning Outcomes (OCALOs) addresses this separation by mandating an integrated Fundamental Academic Skills (FAS) component. Unlike broader integration models such as CLIL or standalone PBL, this study synchronizes the timing of FCS instruction with the immediate requirements of FEL academic tasks, ensuring computing instruction directly serves academic output requirements. This action research study responds to that mandate by designing, piloting, and evaluating a synchronized curricular model at the School of Foundation Studies (SoFS), National University of Science and Technology (NU). Using a two-cycle action research design, the study audited existing FEL and FCS syllabi, developed a synchronized delivery plan, and piloted the model across two foundation levels totaling 79 students. Data was triangulated across student artifacts, survey responses, and faculty meeting records to evaluate skill transfer, task coherence, and student reliance on generative AI tools. The study confirmed measurable skill transfer, improved task coherence, and reduced student reliance on generative AI tools through synchronized delivery and shared assessment criteria. The key finding is that shared marking criteria between FEL and FCS faculty, rather than curriculum redesign alone, is the essential bridge that makes skill transfer successful in practice. This study offers a structural roadmap for Omani HEIs to operationalize the FAS mandate under the revised OAAAQA standards.

papers.title: Integration of AI in Education Toward Future-Ready Assessments
papers.authors: Einas AL Maqbali, Taef AL Riyami
papers.journal: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)
papers.abstract: This research examines the dual impact of artificial intelligence in education, in response to the rapid development of AI technologies. The study explores how AI can enhance learning efficiency and educational outcomes while presenting challenges to academic integrity and fundamental skills development. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the study involved 44 EFL students in Oman and surveyed 102 students from various educational institutions. Researchers analyzed students’ performance in both AI-assisted and traditional writing tasks while observing behavioral patterns and attitudes toward these technologies. Key findings revealed a 42% reduction in grammatical errors with AI assistance, yet 63% of students failed to fully follow instructions, demonstrating limited deep content understanding. While 91% of students reported using AI tools, 60.4% expressed the need for training in ethical usage. The study concludes with three critical recommendations: developing clear institutional policies for AI governance, redesigning assessment methods to focus on learning processes rather than products and strengthening academic values and transparency. These proposals align with the vision of balancing innovation with adaptation to technological change.

papers.title: Divergent Failure Modes of Two Intrusion Detection Benchmarks Under A Common Audit
papers.authors: Arya K S, Selvavinayaki
papers.journal: Eduschool International Journal of Data Science and Machine learning (EIJDSML)
papers.abstract: Two public corpora carry much of the empirical load in machine learning research on intrusion detection for wireless sensor networks and for industrial internet of things deployments. Accuracy on both is routinely reported near the ceiling. We audit both with one procedure, holding features, models, metrics and seeds fixed, and they fail in different ways. On Edge-IIoTset the binary task is settled before any model is fitted. Four string valued fields record how the capture was serialised rather than how the traffic behaved, because the absent value was written as one token on benign rows and a different token on attack rows, and a depth one decision stump on any of them reaches 1.0000 where the majority baseline is 0.8417. All seven learners in the bank reach that ceiling. Removing the four fields separates them again. On WSN-DS the same audit returns almost nothing, and that is the second result. Discarding 8,873 duplicate records moves the bank average equal error rate by 0.0000, and a node disjoint split that shares no sensor with training moves it by 0.0005, against a spread of 0.0158 across the models themselves. A third check finds what neither corpus level audit does. With one attack family withheld from training, detection of the withheld behaviour runs from 0.007 to 0.886. These checks are cheap, and which of them bites is not predictable in advance.

papers.title: THE APPLICATION OF DIGITAL IMAGING TECHNOLOGY IN THE UNIVERSITY FINANCIAL REIMBURSEMENT PROCESS: A CASE STUDY OF UNIVERSITY N
papers.authors: Tian Shen, XiaoYing Liao, JiaJia Zhu, Ting Pu, KeWei Liu
papers.journal: Trends in Social Sciences and Humanities Research
papers.abstract: Faculty members and students at many newly established universities often find the reimbursement process confusing, and repeated errors end up slowing down the entire procedure. Drawing on the actual situation at University N, this study looks closely at where its financial reimbursement system falls short and proposes a set of concrete measures to improve it, in the hope of offering a workable reference for the digital transformation of reimbursement work at similar institutions. The core idea is to use AI video generation tools to produce short demonstration clips of the reimbursement workflow, and to examine whether artificial intelligence and digital imaging technologies can make university reimbursement more intuitive, more carefully managed, and more intelligent. The findings indicate that these technologies do help: they raise reimbursement efficiency, bring down operating costs, and strengthen the control of compliance risks.

papers.title: INSTRUCTIONAL DESIGN OF A WORKPLACE-ORIENTED GENERAL AIGC COURSE IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Yishen Liao, Lei Shu, 赵爱华, Yun Zhang, Hejie Yu
papers.abstract: In the era of digital intelligence, artificial intelligence generated content (AIGC) has become deeply integrated into workplace workflows. However, a growing gap has emerged between corporate demand for AIGC-driven productivity and the lag in talent development. Current introductory AIGC courses suffer from fragmented content, superficial assessment methods, and limited adaptability. To address these challenges, this study proposes a holistic instructional design framework based on the "structural reconstruction, capability building, and closed-loop evaluation" model, featuring an 8-hour modular curriculum: prompt engineering (2 hours) to establish foundational concepts for cross-domain transfer, core tool mastery (4 hours) covering four mainstream AI platforms (ERNIE Bot, DeepSeek, WPS AI, and Doubao), and role-specific applications (2 hours) offering tailored practical exercises across five key professions (finance, education, software development, copywriting, and design). The framework employs a hybrid assessment model combining self-evaluations, instructor feedback, and AI-driven evaluations to target real-world problem-solving skills and adaptability to new tools, while a data-driven feedback loop enables continuous optimization of both course content and personalized learning interventions. Ultimately, this study provides a scalable, iterative system framework for empowering today's AI-driven workforce.
