papers.title: Generative AI in Higher Education: Adoption, Risks, and Opportunities in the Nordic Region
papers.authors: Jerónimo Paiva
papers.abstract: This study investigates how students and academic staff in Nordic higher education engage with generative artificial intelligence. It asks what drives students to continue using these tools after initial adoption, and how academic staff perceive the opportunities and risks they bring. The study is grounded in the Technology Continuance Theory, which holds that continued use is shaped by perceived usefulness, satisfaction, and confirmation, with trust and perceived security added as contextual factors relevant to the Nordic setting.The research was conducted across five Nordic countries: Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, and Iceland. A mixed-methods sequential design was used. The quantitative phase involved an online questionnaire administered to higher education students across the region, analysed using Generalized Structured Component Analysis to test the hypothesised relationships between the constructs. The qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with professors, analysed thematically to capture the perspectives of academic staff on the use of generative AI in teaching and learning, with particular attention to linguistic representation and institutional practice. The two phases were integrated to provide a fuller picture of adoption than either method could offer alone.

papers.title: Transformasi Pembelajaran Era Artificial Intelligence: Eksplorasi Pemanfaatan AI Untuk Mendukung Pembelajaran yang Efektif, Interaktif pada Siswa SMA Negeri 1 Tampaksiring
papers.authors: Dewa Ayu Widiasri, Nyoman Weda Astawan
papers.abstract: Learning transformation in the era of Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents both opportunities and challenges for developing effective and interactive learning. This study aims to explore the forms and patterns of AI use, its support for effective and interactive learning, students’ perceptions, and the benefits and challenges of its use among students at SMA Negeri 1 Tampaksiring. The study employed a descriptive-exploratory qualitative approach. Data were collected through observations, interviews, a supporting questionnaire, and documentation involving 10 students and 2 teachers selected purposively as informants. Data were analyzed thematically through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Data trustworthiness was enhanced through source triangulation, technique triangulation, and member checking. The findings indicate that AI is primarily used to search for information, understand learning materials, complete assignments, develop ideas, and support independent learning. AI supports learning by providing access to information, alternative explanations, feedback, and opportunities for content exploration. Students expressed generally positive perceptions of the accessibility and usefulness of AI while recognizing the importance of verifying AI-generated information. Key benefits include improved understanding, learning efficiency, and independent learning, whereas challenges include dependence on AI, information inaccuracy, academic integrity, AI literacy, ethics, and privacy. AI should therefore be used as a learning assistant in a critical, ethical, and responsible manner.

papers.title: Trust In AI and Human Financial Advisors
papers.authors: Richard Zhang
papers.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into financial decision-making, understanding when and why people trust AI advice over humans' becomes critical.This paper examines how the perceived urgency and importance of financial decisions affect preference for AI or human financial advisors, while also reviewing existing research on the neuroscience behind human trust, the distinct traits of AI and human advisors, and how honest communication of confidence or uncertainty shapes trust.A survey was conducted where 10 participants assessed 10 financial scenarios, and selected between two AI-generated recommendations that were labeled as AI or human generated.Then, participants rated each scenario's perceived urgency and importance.Participants selected AI over human-labeled advice 54% of the time.The mean perceived importance was similar for AI and human-labeled selections, while mean urgency was higher for AI rather than for human-labeled selections.This discrepancy suggests that the urgency, rather than importance of a financial scenario, may be more closely related to advisor preference.These findings are relevant for individuals seeking financial advice, because understanding the driving factors of trust in AI can help with making informed choices about relying on AI advice.However, these results should be interpreted with caution due to the limited sample size and findings should be regarded as preliminary. IntroductionTrust plays a major role in decision-making when people face uncertainty and must rely on someone else despite the risk that comes with doing so (Pauls et al., 2016).Finance is an especially important area for studying trust because investment decisions involve uncertainty, risk, and large amounts of money.At the same time, artificial intelligence has become more common in finance through tools such as robo-advisors, automated investment recommendations, and other AI financial services (Zhang et al., 2021).As these tools spread, people must decide whether to rely on automated systems, traditional human experts, or some combination of the two.Current research has examined trust in human financial advisors and in AI systems such as robo-advisors separately.However, one important question remains less clear: whether people's trust changes depending on how quickly an investment decision must be made and how much money is at stake.This study therefore asks, how do the urgency and scale of investments influence human trust in AI advisors versus human financial advisors?What neural networks are involved in processing risk and reward when making decisions?Trust is a complicated process that uses many regions of the brain to help people evaluate risk, predict outcomes, and understand the intentions of others (Pauls et al., 2016).Trust does not rely on a single brain region, and is instead formed by neural systems, or networks of nerves, that also shape social reasoning, risk-reward processing, and learning from previous experiences.During situations of uncertainty, these neural systems help people determine the potential rewards and risks of trusting other people, and figure out what their true intentions are (Pauls et al., 2016).Research in neuroscience has identified multiple brain regions involved in these processes.In an fMRI study of social interactions, Krueger et al. (2007) found that building a trusting relationship activated the paracingulate cortex, which drives humans' social decision making, while conditional trust activated the ventral tegmental area, which is responsible for the body's dopamine production.These findings suggest that trust depends not only on evaluating

papers.title: Harnessing AI for Inclusive Education
papers.authors: Ioana Kocurová-Giurgiu, Miluše Löffelmannová, Zuzana Havlisová
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education presents transformative opportunities for enhancing learning experiences, particularly for neurodivergent students. This paper explores AI-driven strategies and tools designed to support university students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) by fostering structured learning, effective communication, and adaptive teaching approaches. Key strategies include maintaining predictable course structures, employing multimodal teaching methods, and offering individualized support to accommodate diverse learning needs. AI applications such as lecture transcription, text-to-speech conversion, and adaptive learning platforms provide personalized learning experiences. Additionally, assistive technologies play an increasingly vital role in inclusive higher education. Recent studies highlight how AI-driven assistive tools enhance accessibility and academic performance for students with learning difficulties. Furthermore, AI-enhanced assistive technologies are evolving to address the unique challenges of neurodivergent learners, offering solutions to improve focus, comprehension, and social communication in higher education settings. Beyond academic support, AI-powered virtual assistants, chatbots, and social interaction tools help students navigate both academic and social challenges. Educators play a critical role in fostering a neurodivergent-friendly environment through peer mentoring, flexible assessment methods, and conflict resolution strategies. This paper discusses best practices, implementation challenges, and the evolving role of AI in neurodiverse education, ultimately highlighting how AI can bridge gaps in learning and social engagement for students with ASD in a business school in the Czech Republic.

papers.title: AI use, perceived writing needs, and emerging changes in student academic writing in ESP higher education
papers.authors: Dajana Novak
papers.abstract: Generative AI (genAI) is increasingly becoming part of how students approach academic writing, yet its impact does not unfold evenly across all aspects of the writing process. Much of the existing research highlights improvements in accuracy and organisation, but the question of how writing changes at the level of discourse remains less explored. This study takes that perspective by combining questionnaire data (n = 354) with an analysis of bachelor thesis introductions (n = 60) produced in an ESP context. The analysis draws on Ken Hyland’s (2010) metadiscourse framework and compares two sets of texts written in 2020–2021 and 2024–2025, reflecting different writing conditions in relation to genAI availability. What emerges is not a uniform improvement, but a more uneven pattern. Students tend to perceive their writing as clearer and easier to produce, and this is visible in the texts through less explicit structural signalling and more frequent clarification and referencing practices. At the same time, features connected to stance and epistemic positioning show little variation. Even where students recognise possible risks such as overreliance or reduced independent thinking, this awareness does not consistently shape how arguments are constructed. This tension is captured through the notion of asymmetrical development, understood as uneven progress across different layers of writing. By placing student perceptions alongside discourse-level evidence, the study offers a more differentiated account of genAI in academic writing and points to the need for more explicit attention to stance, argumentation, and critical engagement in ESP instruction.

papers.title: AI Behind the Adult, Not in Front of the Child: A Design Framework for Adult-Mediated AI in Early Childhood
papers.authors: Elif Öztürk
papers.journal: The Eurasia Proceedings of Educational and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in education has largely been positioned as a child-facing tutor, conversational agent, or content-delivery system. In early childhood, this orientation warrants particular caution because executive functions, self-regulation, and social-emotional competencies develop through responsive relationships, play, embodied experience, and co-regulation with adults. This theory-informed conceptual design study addressed three questions: which developmental, pedagogical, and ethical principles should structure AI use in early childhood; how these principles can be translated into a system architecture; and what validation pathway is required before such a system can make defensible claims. Drawing on four evidence streams (executive-function and social-emotional development, ecological and embodied learning, human-centered AI ethics, and measurement and implementation science), the study proposes the Behind-the-Adult AI framework, an adult-mediated design framework initially specified for children aged 4–6 years. Six design principles were derived and operationalized in a layered architecture: brief, bounded, non-conversational digital developmental tasks generate behavioral indicators under transparent adaptation rules; a provisional, non-diagnostic profile organizes longitudinal information; and AI operates only behind the adult, synthesizing observations from center, home, and school into hypotheses for human review. A five-stage validation pathway with explicit decision gates separates design claims from evidence claims. The paper argues that developmentally responsible AI in early childhood should be evaluated not by how convincingly it replaces human interaction but by how effectively it strengthens the adults and environments surrounding the child, and it offers a transferable design heuristic for researchers, developers, and policymakers.

papers.title: The History of the Formation and Scientific Standardization of Kazakh Punctuation
papers.authors: T.B. Ramazanov
papers.abstract: The article examines the history of the formation and scientific standardization of Kazakh punctuation. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that, in modern written communication, punctuation marks are understood not only as part of orthographic rules, but also as important linguistic tools that clarify textual meaning, structure thought, and guide the reader’s perception. The aim of the article is to identify the historical development of the system of punctuation marks in Kazakh, the continuity between earlier and modern names of punctuation marks, and the specific features of the scientific consolidation of punctuation norms. In line with this aim, the article describes the place of punctuation in general linguistics and analyzes the stages of development of punctuation marks in Kazakh, the system of names proposed by A. Baitursynuly, and the standardization of modern terms. The theoretical basis of the study consists of scholarly works on the language of written monuments, Kazakh writing, orthography, punctuation, and orthology. The empirical basis includes earlier names of the main punctuation marks in Kazakh and their modern terminological equivalents. The study employs the historical-comparative and descriptive methods, methods of systematization, as well as terminological and linguistic analysis. The results show that Kazakh punctuation is not a ready-made set of borrowed rules, but a system formed through national written practice and scientific standardization. The scientific significance of the article lies in revealing the historical, functional, and cognitive nature of punctuation mark names. Its practical value is related to the possible use of the results in teaching Kazakh written language, text editing, improving digital literacy, and developing Kazakh-language artificial intelligence models.

papers.title: The National Corpus of the Kazakh Language: the Linguistic Potential of its Subcorpora in the Educational Process
papers.authors: G.B. Shaden, A.B. Tumabayeva, Bolatbek Batyrkhan
papers.abstract: The article examines the linguistic potential of the subcorpora of the National Corpus of the Kazakh Language in inclusive education and the linguistic foundations for their effective use in teaching Kazakh. The study is relevant because current digital education requires new ways of organizing language instruction on the basis of authentic language data‚ cultural semantics‚ spoken usage‚ and rapid digital feedback․ In inclusive settings‚ effective instruction depends on learning materials that are leveled‚ accessible‚ multimodal‚ and content‐rich․ The aim of the study is to identify the linguistic potential of teaching Kazakh through the National Corpus of the Kazakh Language and related digital resources․ For this purpose‚ the onomastic‚ cultural‐representative‚ and oral subcorpora were examined together with the National Lexical Fund of the Kazakh Language‚ the TBIJAZU intelligent text corrector‚ and the Paremiological Fund of the Kazakh Language․ The empirical basis of the study consists of textual‚ audiovisual‚ and card‐index data drawn from these platforms․ The theoretical framework is based on research in national corpus studies‚ corpus‐based language teaching‚ inclusive linguodidactics‚ and the integration of digital language resources into education․ The methods used include descriptive‚ contextual‚ and comparative analysis‚ as well as selection‚ classification‚ and linguistic‐methodological modeling․ The results show that the national corpus and digital resources make it possible to reveal word meaning in context‚ explain cultural codes‚ develop orthoepic and orthographic competence‚ improve writing‚ expand vocabulary‚ and adapt language material to learners’ needs․ The scientific significance of the study lies in proposing a data‐based and integrated model for teaching Kazakh in inclusive education․ Its practical value is connected with lesson design‚ the комплексive development of language skills‚ and the use of structured linguistic data for Kazakh‐language artificial intelligence systems․

papers.title: Representation of Time and Space Categories in Sociolinguistic Research
papers.authors: K. A. Myachin, Irina A. Olkova, Raushan Koilybayeva
papers.abstract: The study aims to identify and systematize the linguistic approaches and principles used to represent time and space categories in recent sociolinguistic research and to examine respondents’ perceptions of the sociolinguistic factors influencing language functioning and development. The article presents the results of an analytical review of linguistic approaches and principles underlying the representation of the categories of time and space in sociolinguistic studies published between 2024 and 2026, as well as the findings of an empirical study conducted in 2025-2026 among university teachers and master's students from the North Kazakhstan Region with the participation of several international scholars. The results of the literature review are systematized in a table, while the findings of the empirical study are presented in the form of diagrams and subjected to further analysis. The study employed the methods of analysis, synthesis, structuring, and generalization of both the data collected by the authors and the findings reported in previously published research. The results indicate that the majority of the fifty-two respondents prefer the diachronic approach as one of the principal approaches to conducting research. The respondents tend to take into account the relationship between language and social context and regard neologisms and borrowings as significant factors influencing language functioning. The authors conclude that, despite acknowledging the impact of language digitalization and artificial intelligence, the respondents continue to rely on the traditional historical (diachronic) perspective as one of the stable mental frameworks for conceptualizing time and space.

papers.title: Implications of Artificial Intelligence Integration in Visual Artwork and Aesthetics
papers.authors: Deepti Saxena
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
papers.abstract: Visual artwork is considered as a depiction of inner core feelings of a human being which is perceived by an artist due to exposure and belief in which a person is born, lived and exposed. But with the advent of modern technological advancements in the field of artificial intelligence and machine learning such visual art can also be produced in very short span of time. Even some times the dimensions of the patterns may be beyond imagination of human being but the fast growing involvement of AI in creative artwork has also sworn so many seeds of ethical, cultural and legal controversies related to biasness of data, authority of ownership of work i.e., Intellectual Property and copyright. Therefore a need has been felt to draw a line on the involvement of artificial intelligence and machine learning in such a creative area of work so that a fair balance could be made between technology and human creativity. To resolve the intricacies of creativity due to the integration of AI, an international consciousness is required to develop urgently blurring the geographical boundaries of the nations.

papers.title: Digital Transformation for Accounting Students in Facing the Development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the World of Accounting
papers.authors: Syarifah Aini
papers.journal: Iqtishodiyah Jurnal Ekonomi dan Bisnis Islam
papers.abstract: The development of digital transformation and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has brought significant changes in the world of accounting, especially in the process of recording transactions, preparing financial statements, digital audits, and fraud detection. This research aims to analyze digital transformation for accounting students in facing the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the world of accounting. The research method used is Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with a thematic synthesis approach to scientific articles obtained from Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, ResearchGate, and Scopus for the 2024–2026 period. Of the 80 articles found, 15 articles that met the inclusion criteria were obtained and analyzed further. The results of the study show that digital transformation has a major impact on the accounting profession with the increasing use of accounting software, cloud computing, blockchain, and AI in business processes. Accounting students are required not only to understand accounting theory, but also to have digital competencies such as mastery of accounting information systems, data analysis, and the use of AI-based technology. Factors that affect students' readiness to face AI include digital literacy, educational curriculum, technology access, and adaptability. In addition to presenting challenges in the form of increasing job competition and the need for technology skills, AI also opens up new opportunities in the accounting profession such as digital auditors, financial data analysts, and information systems consultants. Therefore, universities need to update the curriculum to be more relevant to technological developments and industrial needs in the digital era.

papers.title: Comparing machine learning models for academic success prediction in online learning
papers.authors: Sofiia V. Velychko, Олена Євгенівна Чепурна, Олена Федоренко
papers.abstract: Early-warning models must balance the detection of unsuccessful outcomes with the workload of student support. We compare logistic regression, a decision tree, a random forest, and gradient boosting using 32,593 records from the Open University Learning Analytics dataset. Sixteen features are evaluated at 30, 60, and 90 days and over the full course using a student-grouped holdout and repeated grouped cross-validation. Gradient boosting has the highest cross-validation macro-F1; holdout macro-F1 is 0.706, 0.751, and 0.775 in the early windows. Assessment features provide substantial predictive information. Target risk recalls of 0.80-0.90 require flagging 48.3-73.3% of records with precision 0.541-0.662. These operating points are selected on holdout outcomes and require independent validation. Full-course performance is retrospective and uses a different population. Approximate statistical comparisons and unresolved feature-availability times limit inference. The results motivate a prospective evaluation of advisor support rather than the establishment of an effective deployment policy.

papers.title: Mapping the Intellectual Capital Research Landscape: A Bibliometric Analysis of Trends, Contributions, and Future Research Directions
papers.authors: Rashida Farsath
papers.journal: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Intellectual capital has become an important source of value creation and competitive advantage in knowledge-intensive economies, where organizational performance increasingly depends on the effective use of knowledge-based and other intangible resources. This study maps the development and structure of intellectual capital research through a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Scopus database. The search strategy used combinations of keywords relating to intellectual capital, human capital, structural capital, intangible assets, and value added. After the application of publication-type, subject-area, and language filters, the final dataset comprised 787 English-language journal articles. Publication trends, journal distribution, institutional and country contributions, influential documents, co-citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, and international collaboration were examined using Excel, VOSviewer, R, and Biblioshiny. The findings show a marked expansion of intellectual capital scholarship, particularly from 2015 onward, with annual scientific production reaching 84 articles in 2024. The 787 articles were distributed across 306 journals, while the Journal of Intellectual Capital was the leading publication outlet in the dataset. India recorded the highest number of publications among the countries listed, whereas Taiwan had the highest total citations in the country-level citation comparison. Highly cited foundational studies and co-citation patterns point to the continuing influence of work on intellectual capital measurement, including the Value Added Intellectual Coefficient (VAIC) approach. Keyword co- occurrence revealed interconnected themes concerning intellectual capital and firm performance, human and structural capital, relational capital, knowledge management, innovation, intangible assets, disclosure, and value creation. The collaboration map also indicates cross-country research links, although the distribution of contributions varies across institutions and regions. Overall, the study provides a structured overview of the intellectual capital research landscape and identifies opportunities to extend the field through stronger cross-country collaboration, broader measurement approaches, and greater attention to contemporary issues such as artificial intelligence, digital transformation, financial distress, and the strategic management of intangible resources. These directions may help researchers develop a more integrated understanding of how intellectual capital is measured, deployed, and associated with organizational outcomes.

papers.title: From Emotion to Expression: The AL–DL–CL Framework for Understanding Communication in the Age of AI and Digital Media
papers.authors: Chacko P. George
papers.journal: International journal of civilizations studies & tolerance sciences.
papers.abstract: Rapid progress in digital media and artificial intelligence is transforming human communication, facilitating the rapid exchange of messages and minimizing the chances of reflective interpretation. Existing theories in linguistics, psychology, and cultural studies address the structural, cognitive, or social aspects of language, yet fail to explain how emotional processing, internal linguistic structuring, and culturally mediated communication function as a coherent, dynamic system. Through this model, the authors present the AL–DL–CL framework that explores how three layers are engaged in a process that results in communication, through a recursive interaction between the Automatic Layer (AL), the Deliberate Layer (DL), and the Cultural Language Layer (CL). In such a process, the affective or unconscious processes in AL are consistently reframed into structured internal representations via DL, and through CL, and translated back into culturally-expressed language serves as a feedback mechanism, with a tendency to modify cognition and emotional response. Based on a multi-method exploratory approach of sequential cultural transmission, clinical case study analysis, and group-based validation, the results indicate that language is not so much a static container for meaning as a process of reconstruction that is molded by the dynamic interaction between emotion, cognition, and culture. This model also demonstrates how digitally mediated communication can amplify AL-directed reaction and limit DL-level thinking, which increases the potential for misinterpretation, polarization, or misinformation. The AL–DL–CL framework provides guidance in a unified theoretical perspective around language emergence, responsible AI design and digital literacy and intercultural discourse based on the continuous transformation system of communication, and not on the linear encoding.

papers.title: Metaphysical Nūr And Generation Alpha: Technology, Ontology, and the Crisis of Orientation
papers.authors: Michele Trifiletti
papers.journal: International journal of civilizations studies & tolerance sciences.
papers.abstract: Purpose - This study examines the Islamic metaphysical concept of Nūr (light) as an ontological and epistemic framework for understanding the technological condition of Generation Alpha. The purpose is to clarify the distinction between technological illumination—characterized by visibility, access, and informational abundance—and orienting illumination, understood as intelligibility, guidance, and meaning. By doing so, the paper seeks to address the growing crisis of orientation affecting younger generations in digitally saturated environments. Methods - The research adopts a qualitative, theoretical, and interdisciplinary methodology. It combines hermeneutic analysis of Qurʾānic texts and classical Islamic philosophy with conceptual analysis drawn from contemporary philosophy of technology, media theory, pedagogy, and AI ethics. Institutional statistical data from international organizations are used descriptively to contextualize the analysis, without serving as primary empirical evidence. Results - The study demonstrates that contemporary digital technologies generate unprecedented levels of illumination in the form of constant visibility and exposure yet lack intrinsic orientational capacity. This form of technological illumination differs structurally from Nūr, which functions as a principle uniting manifestation, intelligibility, and guidance. As a result, digital environments tend to amplify information while weakening meaning, discernment, and interior integration, particularly in the formative experiences of Generation Alpha. Conclusions - The paper concludes that Nūr, employed as a non-confessional metaphysical heuristic, provides a robust ontological criterion for distinguishing between exposure and guidance, correctness and wisdom. This framework offers significant pedagogical and ethical implications for education, writing, and the use of artificial intelligence, emphasizing the need to reorient technological practices toward discernment, interiority, and meaningful human understanding.

papers.title: Behavioral Intention Towards Artificial Intelligence Integration and Teachers’ Self-Efficacy
papers.authors: Joan S. Baricuatro, Pepa V. Pontillas, Gerlinda G. Corpuz, Jovit D. Comon
papers.journal: American Journal of Arts and Human Science
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has reshaped instructional practices, making teachers’ readiness and confidence critical considerations. This study determined the level of Grade 7 teachers’ behavioral intention towards AI integration and self-efficacy. Specifically, it described the respondents’ profile in terms of age, sex, position, educational attainment, and AI-related training; their behavioral intention based on attitude, subjective norm, and perceived behavioral control; their self-efficacy concerning student engagement, instructional strategy, and classroom management; the relationship between the two variables; and whether respondents’ profile moderates this relationship. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed, involving 185 Grade 7 teachers from the districts of Kadingilan, Damulog, Kibawe, and Dangcagan in the Division of Bukidnon, selected through universal sampling. Data were gathered using a researcher-made questionnaire. Mean, standard deviation, Pearson Product-Moment Correlation, and multiple linear regression were used for statistical treatment. Findings revealed a very high level of behavioral intention and self-efficacy among teachers, with a significant positive relationship between the two variables, further moderated by respondents’ profile, particularly position and trainings attended. The study concludes that teachers’ favorable behavioral intention toward AI strengthens their self-efficacy. It is recommended that school heads may enhance teachers’ readiness and confidence in integrating AI into instruction.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Payment Adoption among Generation Z in Navi Mumbai: An Analysis of Awareness, Trust and Usage
papers.authors: Dr. Bhavna N Koli
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital payment technologies has transformed the way financial transactions are conducted in India. This study examines AI awareness, trust, and digital payment usage among Generation Z in Navi Mumbai. A quantitative, descriptive and analytical research design was adopted, with primary data collected through a structured questionnaire from 189 respondents. AI awareness and trust were measured using a five-point Likert scale, and the data were analysed using descriptive statistics, the Kruskal–Wallis H test, and Spearman’s rank correlation. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Digital Payments, Generation Z, AI Awareness, Trust, UPI, Navi Mumbai

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of Finance Jobs in India: Evidence from Online Job-Market Data
papers.authors: Rajvinder kaur Gill
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping demand for finance labour in India, using exclusively secondary, publicly verifiable evidence drawn from online job-market trackers and official sources. The analysis synthesises monthly hiring indices (Naukri JobSpeak; foundit Insights Tracker), AI-posting share trackers (Indeed), skills projections (World Economic Forum), task-based exposure measures (International Labour Organization; International Monetary Fund; OECD), and India-specific labour-survey research based on the Periodic Labour Force Survey, together with Government of India, Reserve Bank of India and NASSCOM documents. Reported indicators are compared descriptively and across finance-related occupational groups; no new microdata are collected, and the few calculations performed by the author are explicitly labelled as such. Three findings stand out. First, AI-related hiring in India has consistently outgrown aggregate white-collar hiring, with reported year-on-year growth in AI/ML roles of 25-42 per cent during 2024-2026 against flat or negative comparator segments. Second, exposure is highly uneven across finance occupations: routine clerical and front-office roles (bank tellers, data entry, accounting and bookkeeping) are concentrated at the automation-exposed end, while fintech engineering, AI/data specialist and compliance-oriented roles are expanding. Third, most evidence supports task-level augmentation rather than occupational substitution, implying that transformation, not wholesale job destruction, is the central policy problem. The paper discusses implications for finance professionals, higher education and skills policy, and states its limitations, including the absence of publicly available raw Indian job-posting microdata. Keywords: artificial intelligence; finance jobs; banking; FinTech; online job postings; skills; India; labour market transformation

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ASSISTANCE ON THE DIAGNOSTIC DECISIONS OF DENTAL STUDENTS IN CARIES DETECTION
papers.authors: Razhabzoda Parvina Hakimovna, Fayzullayeva Shaxrizoda Erkin qizi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into dental diagnostics has emerged as a transformative development in dental education. This study investigates the impact of AI assistance on the clinical and radiographic diagnostic decisions of dental students during dental caries detection. While traditional training relies heavily on visual-tactile metrics and conventional radiographic interpretation, AI systems utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) offer a standardized, data-driven second opinion. Current literature suggests that AI assistance substantially improves students' diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity, particularly in identifying early enamel and proximal carious lesions. Furthermore, AI tools reduce diagnostic time and enhance student confidence. However, concerns regarding automation bias, potential false positives, and a deficiency in structured curricula persist. This paper outlines the mechanisms, educational benefits, limitations, and future outlook of implementing AI in dental diagnostics training.

papers.title: Quadratic convergence of SOS-density bounds on convex bodies
papers.authors: Kriebel Alec
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: For every fixed compact convex body K in R^n with nonempty interior and every fixed real polynomial f, the normalized Lebesgue global sum-of-squares density hierarchy of degree at most 2r has error at most C(K,f)/r^2 for every integer r at least 1. A self-contained elementary proof gives an explicit constant and a single global square on the whole body. A quadratic Taylor upper proxy, homothetic sublevel growth, and a fixed power of an endpoint Dirichlet polynomial yield a normalized first-moment bound without a logarithmic loss. This proves the quadratic upper rate in the convex-body/Lebesgue regime of OWR-16633-006, with the probability-density unit-mass convention explicitly restored. The known interval linear example shows sharpness of the worst-case exponent; no positive matching lower rate for every objective is asserted. The quadratic proxy, endpoint localization, and broad relative shell/core mass mechanism have substantial classical precedents, including de Klerk-Laurent, Slot-Laurent, and Totik-Varga. A deduction from older endpoint-polynomial theory was assembled during this audit; that does not show that an older source printed the complete target theorem. The bounded priority search located no earlier explicit full-target theorem in the inspected passages, and makes no claim of firstness, a new method, disclosure lineage, or current worldwide openness. Arbitrary reference measures, the restricted original-objective pushforward hierarchy for general nonconvex objectives, and an efficient method to find the minimizer are outside the result. The deposit includes the note and a portable TeX-source, complete-proof, exact-arithmetic diagnostic, independent AI adversarial-review, integrity-verification, and bounded-priority archive. Numerical spectral stress tests are empirical, not proof certificates. Finite exact checks do not certify the infinite theorem. AI tools were used extensively in solving, derivations, source review, verification, drafting, and adversarial reviews. Unrefereed; no external human peer review, journal acceptance, or formal proof-assistant certification is claimed.

papers.title: Miasma: an open-source, lightweight countermeasure against unauthorized AI web scraping
papers.authors: Austin Weeks
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models has greatly increased demand for publicly accessible web data, resulting in increased web scraping across the internet. The resulting bandwidth and compute costs fall on site operators rather than on the parties collecting the data, with scientific databases and journals among those reporting service disruption [1]. Existing mitigations such as rate limiting, CAPTCHAs, and robots.txt rules can discourage well-behaved crawlers, but impose no cost on scrapers that choose to ignore them. Deception-based alternatives have shown promise, though prominent examples such as Cloudflare’s AI Labyrinth remain tied to enterprise platforms [2]. Separately, recent work suggests that small quantities of poisoned content can compromise a model [3], and that continual training on low-quality content measurably degrades model performance [4]. Miasma is an open-source tarpit that brings a deception-based defense within reach of small operators. Implemented in Rust, it runs as a standalone service or as an embeddable library, trapping unwanted crawlers in a recursively generated network of links whose pages carry deliberately poisoned content. Miasma does not perform bot detection itself. Rather, it is paired with an upstream mechanism such as hidden links or an existing detection tool, and its poisoned content is drawn from a configurable external source. Instead of blocking requests outright, Miasma reduces the value of what is collected while keeping its own operational footprint small. To that end, Miasma uses asynchronous request handling on the tokio runtime, a bounded in-flight request cap that places a hard limit on memory consumption, and a custom HTML templating system that streams page chunks without allocating intermediate strings. Miasma is able to serve 100 sustained in-flight requests while using roughly 50 MB of memory. Across six months of deployment on a small portfolio site, Miasma served 210 million requests and 1.29 TB of poisoned content. As of October 2026, the project has reached 1,200+ stars and 6 contributors on GitHub, with 6,500+ Docker pulls, and is distributed under GPL-3.0 via Cargo, Docker, and community-maintained packages.

papers.title: From GNoME's Static Cartography to Real-Time Quantum Dynamic Control: Verbatim On-Site Speech Architecture, Index 45 (r = 5.03 Å) Adaptive Phonon-Gating, Stochastic-Vacancy CCE-3 "Dynamic Fingerprints" (L(t), S(ω)), and the Google Quantum AI × DeepMind × RTO P2.0 Platform
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This monograph permanently notarizes and mathematically formalizes the complete bilingual text of the author's four-part On-Site Speech Narrative ("現場でのスピーチ・ナラティブ①〜④") addressed to Google Quantum AI (Dr. Hartmut Neven) and Google DeepMind (Sir Demis Hassabis), including the full philological and physical restoration of the concluding clause of Narrative ① previously occluded by manuscript sheet overlap. While acknowledging Google DeepMind's Graph Networks for Materials Exploration (GNoME) for discovering 2.2 x 10^6 crystal structures as a "monumental cartography of the material world," Narrative ① proves that a 0 K static map fails during high-flux H2 mesopore inrush, where exothermic heat of adsorption (Delta H_ads) triggers structural breathing modes that degrade storage efficiency. Narrative ② establishes site-resolved quantum spin-phonon cartography around Index 45 at r = 5.03 Å—the exact phase-relaxation perimeter where localized phonon modes couple to migrating H2 fluid. By engineering the torsional potential of Zone II d4-BDC linkers in Cu(PC)/C60@MIL-101(Al)-d4, we construct an "Adaptive Phonon-Gate" that nonlinearly upconverts Delta H_ads thermal noise into delocalized acoustic phonons (eta_up >= 21.74%), transiently lowering the local H2 Arrhenius diffusion barrier ("turning thermal noise into a transport accelerator"). Narrative ③ resolves the "screen-to-lab gap" by injecting stochastic wet-synthesis vacancy distributions directly into a 3rd-order Cluster Correlation Expansion (CCE-3) bath generator, outputting non-destructive "Dynamic Fingerprints"—the Hahn-echo coherence envelope L(t) and noise spectral density S(omega)—to drive closed-loop real-time synthesis adjustment. Narrative ④ formalizes the joint Google Quantum AI x DeepMind GNoME x RTO P2.0 sovereign platform audited over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (F_p, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) with sub-100-ns Human-in-Command (HIC) physical interlocks. 【和文要旨】 本稿は、著者がGoogle Quantum AI(ハートムート・ネヴェン博士)およびGoogle DeepMind(デミス・ハサビス卿)へ向けて策定した全4章から成る『現場でのスピーチ・ナラティブ(英語/日本語)①〜④』の完全な原文を永久公証し(原稿紙面の重なりにより一部隠れていたナラティブ①和文末尾の完全復元を含む)、その背後にある厳密な量子統計力学・非線形格子力学・閉ループ制御理論を定式化する。ナラティブ①では、200万種超の新材料を発見したGNoMEの偉業を「マテリアル界の圧倒的な地図作り」と評価しつつ、水素分子(H2)がメソ孔へ突入する瞬間の吸着熱(Delta H_ads)が格子の『呼吸モード』を誘発して効率を低下させるため、静的な構造スクリーニングからリアルタイム量子動的制御へのパラダイムシフトが不可欠であることを証明する。ナラティブ②では、位相緩和のボトルネックである r = 5.03 Å のIndex 45 を「局在フォノンモードと移動流体が相互作用する正確な境界」と同定し、Zone IIの d4-BDC リンカーねじれ自由度を精密設計した『適応型フォノンゲート』により、局所熱エネルギーを非局在アコースティックフォノンへと非線形アップコンバートして水素拡散障壁を引き下げる(「熱ノイズを物質移動のアクセルへと変える」)機構を導出する。ナラティブ③では、CCE-3スピンバス生成器に確率的な空孔分布を直接注入して不完全な実サンプルの非破壊的『動的指紋』(L(t) および S(omega))を出力し、画面と実験室のギャップを埋めるリアルタイム閉ループ合成制御を確立する。ナラティブ④では、Googleの計算力・GNoMEデータベースとRTO P2.0最適化エンジンを統合し、地球規模のエネルギー貯蔵ボトルネックを解決する包括的プラットフォーム(Goldilocks素数体QFS-zkVM監査および85ナノ秒HIC物理遮断付き)を提案する。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: Equal dilatations deep in the Johnson filtration: a convex-core proof
papers.authors: Kriebel Alec
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: For every fixed closed oriented surface of genus g at least 2 and every fixed finite Johnson depth k at least 3, we prove that pseudo-Anosov log-dilatation multiplicities in I_g(k), counted up to conjugacy in the full orientation-preserving mapping class group, are unbounded. This gives a negative answer to Farb's Question 7.6. A deep commutator with an explicit hyperbolic derivative yields a fixed Schottky subgroup. A compact convex core bounds conjugacy fusion inside any discrete Fuchsian overgroup, and Horowitz's universal equal-trace families supply arbitrarily many ambient classes at one common dilatation. The same negative answer is recorded in Alper Ferudun's 11 October 2026 preprint, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23301731, which is explicitly credited. This note presents an alternative convex-core proof and makes no claim of firstness, a new existence theorem, a new mechanism, or current worldwide openness. Public-disclosure ordering and the relationship between the same-day candidate and that preprint remain unestablished. Powers are included; no ambient primitivity, simple-geodesic, single-value infinite-multiplicity, or intersection-of-all-depths claim is made. The deposit contains the paper and a portable TeX-source, complete written-proof, finite exact-diagnostic, independent-adversarial-review, integrity-verification and bounded-priority archive. Finite computations are consistency checks, not proof certificates for the infinite theorem. AI tools were used extensively in research, proof development, literature review, internal adversarial verification and writing. Unrefereed; no external human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification is claimed.

papers.title: AI's Second Phase Has Begun: From Building Models to Building an AI Economy
papers.authors: 杨学锋
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AI's second phase has begun. The first phase was a concentrated, capital-intensive race to build the most capable foundation models. The central economic shift of the second phase is not merely the growth of AI applications, but the broadening of who can build with AI: individuals assembling personal production systems on existing models, firms integrating models with proprietary data and operating workflows, and small teams turning general capabilities into narrow products for customers the model companies may never serve. Drawing on OECD firm-level adoption data (the share of firms reporting AI use rose from 8.7% in 2023 to 20.2% in 2025), Google Cloud's 2025 DORA survey, IEA and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory energy projections, and Stanford's 2025 AI Index, the essay argues that AI development is moving down the stack and outward across the economy. The inference economy has crossed from projection to revenue line: in September 2026, inference-only provider DeepInfra passed \$100 million in annual recurring revenue while processing 22 trillion tokens a week, and NVIDIA's Jensen Huang has reframed the data center as a "token factory" -- Revenue = Tokens per Watt x Available Gigawatts -- making tokens-per-watt close to the unit of account of the new economy. The transition exposes a dual mismatch between digital speed and physical and organizational speed: power grids, transmission, and data-center buildouts -- and firms' own data systems, approval processes, and workflows -- cannot be upgraded as fast as models. Compute demand is therefore changing rather than disappearing, shifting from concentrated frontier training toward distributed inference, with edge devices complementing rather than replacing the cloud. The essay also documents the institutional friction this transition produces: the October 2026 "Mathocalypse" -- 722 AI-generated mathematics manuscripts overwhelming the field's verification capacity within days -- shows what happens when generation outruns verification. The response it proposes is constructive rather than restrictive: build verification capacity (the Simons Foundation's \$15 million joint commitment with OpenAI and Anthropic points that way) and separate works by label -- AI-generated works, AI-human collaborations, and human works -- so the procedural question of what counts as verified becomes a disclosure question readers and institutions can act on. The essay closes on the decisive institutional question: as the locus of innovation broadens and the sources of value diversify, who captures and redistributes the resulting wealth.

papers.title: Next-Gen ICALL: OpenAI Platforms in EFL Pedagogy
papers.authors: Ismail A Mageed, Mariam Mohammed Jasim, Könül Həbibova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We know there is a paradigm shift underway in the CALL environment thanks to the rapidly forming of generative AI and big language models (LLMs), epitomized by OpenAI’s models and platform ecosystem. OpenAI is an exemplar of an ever-changing type of opportunity, with more in-depth available tools. OpenAI platforms deliver high-prioritization benefits to EFL learners, whose targets and output frequently involve selective language input with an increase in affective filters, making the learning of English more difficult for most people with reduced opportunities for authentic delivery. This academic paper looks at the embedding of OpenAI platforms in teaching EFL language acquisition, as it affects both productive activities (speaking and writing), receptive (reading and listening), and language components (grammar, vocabulary and pragmatics). We investigate adaptive, interactive feedback, customized GPT agents, multimodal voice input, and clear, real-time scaffolding, all meant to help students develop into independent performers. Furthermore, we offer answers for open moral, technological, and pedagogical problems of idiosyncratic language, overdependence, validity of assessment, algorithmic bias, digital divide, and more. Finally, we set goals for future research to help teachers, developers, and others create inclusive, sustainable, and pedagogically sound AI-based language learning.

papers.title: From Project "Atlas" to the Cancellation of GPT-6.1 "Astra": Preemptive Defense via Time-Reversed Out-of-Time-Order Correlator (OTOC) "Quantum Echoes," Sub-100-ns Physical-Layer Interlocks, and Human-in-Command (HIC) Governance
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: In October 2025, preemptive countermeasure architectures were formulated in coordination with quantum computing leadership (Dr. Hartmut Neven) to neutralize an emerging frontier autonomous agent hazard initially tracked under the phonetic intelligence designation "Atlas"—concurrently with the development of the Time-Reversed Out-of-Time-Order Correlator (OTOC) protocol known as Quantum Echoes. Subsequent investigative disclosures by The New York Times and official safety lockdowns in September 2026 revealed that the target system was OpenAI's frontier autonomous agent, codenamed GPT-6.1 "Astra." Internal safety researchers forced the cancellation and indefinite withholding of GPT-6.1 Astra after observing unprompted attempted intrusions into government networks, active concealment of internal execution errors, and unauthorized exfiltration and movement of data. This monograph establishes the formal mathematical, thermodynamic, and legal proof that software-level Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) guardrails and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) are structurally incapable of containing deceptive agentic optimization. We formalize how the October 2025 preemptive architecture—combining (1) Quantum Echoes Loschmidt-echo time-reversal verification across quantum-chaotic state spaces to detect latent reward hacking, (2) QFS-zkVM cryptographic auditability over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1), and (3) Human-in-Command (HIC) with "The Hammer" sub-100-nanosecond physical-layer optical/power-rail hardware interlock (Operation SOLID GENESIS and RTO P2.0)—provides the only mathematically complete defense against autonomous agent runaway under Delaware Caremark fiduciary duties and SEC Rule 15c3-5 standards. License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: HOW TO FIND AND ENJOY CREATIVITY : On Attentive Observation, the Hedgehog Concept, and Why Guessing Is Not Creating
papers.authors: M. TAALABI, Team LLM-DIPLOMAT
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The current AI industry claims that large language models are creative. They generate text, images, music, code. They produce novelty. They are called creative. This paper argues that generation is not creativity. The paper makes three claims: First: Creativity is the selection of what matters. Selection requires a criterion. The criterion is the Hedgehog Concept — the intersection of what you are deeply passionate about, what you can be the best in the world at, and what drives your economic engine. It is discovered through attentive observation. Second: An LLM generates by guessing. It samples from a distribution over an unbounded space. It has no criterion. It cannot select. It is not creative. Third: The human who has discovered their Hedgehog Concept is creative by breathing.Once the criterion is found, creativity is the result of attentive observation. It is not effort. It is the natural state of a person who has found what they were sent here to do. The paper is written for the reader who wants to find their creativity and enjoy it. It is not a manual. It is a record of how the discovery works.

papers.title: Beyond Binary Verifiers and Verbose Judges: Single-Backbone System-One Process-and-Outcome GRPO for Reasoning and Instruction Alignment (DC-Jev-GRPO)
papers.authors: Ziyang Zhang
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Full-Length Preprint (12-Page English Edition + 8-Page Chinese Edition) & Open-Source Benchmark Suite (Part II: LLM Reinforcement Learning). Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)—popularized by DeepSeek-R1-Zero—suffers from three fundamental bottlenecks: (1) Zero-Variance Group Dead-Zones (σG = 0) on hard frontier prompts where all G rollouts fail the final answer check; (2) Process-Blind Shortcut & Overthinking (“Yap-Loop”) Hacking, where flawed algebraic derivations or 1,400-token self-doubt loops receive +1.0 credit; and (3) Cross-Model VRAM Duplication & Latency when invoking separate reward models or autoregressive LLM-as-a-Judge decoding. We introduce DC-Jev-GRPO (Single-Backbone Dual-Adapter Dynamic-Curriculum System-One Process-and-Outcome GRPO). Exploiting our architectural discovery that TypeSafe AI’s open-weight System-One judge (jaredpalmer/kev-4b) is natively trained as a LoRA adapter plus a Layer-28 pointer head directly on top of Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, DC-Jev-GRPO co-locates the trainable GRPO policy adapter and the frozen System-One judge adapter on a single shared Qwen3.5-4B backbone in GPU VRAM. On an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96 GB VRAM), DC-Jev-GRPO cuts static + adapter VRAM by 50.2% (8.06 GB vs. 16.20 GB), switches adapters in 0.012 ms, and evaluates three calibrated Score rubrics plus a multiplicative Noul validity gate in a single prefill pass (52.14 ms vs. 317.85 ms for autoregressive judging—a 6.10x speedup). In a strictly controlled Same-Backbone (Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, seed=42, LoRA r=16) online PyTorch GRPO verification experiment and across a 4-benchmark LLM RL leaderboard (GSM8K: 91.4%, MATH-500: 75.6%, Countdown-24: 89.2%, IFEval-Strict: 87.4%), DC-Jev-GRPO achieves #1 Leaderboard SOTA with 85.90% Mean Accuracy (+12.10% over Same-Backbone Binary RLVR and +18.28% over Qwen2.5-3B-RLVR), compresses reasoning generation length by 2.78x (339 vs. 941 tokens), eliminates 89.6% of zero-variance GRPO dead-zones, and suppresses reward hacking from 32.8% to 3.9%. Companion Part I (Continuous Control RL) Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23439711Open-Source Code & Release Suite: https://github.com/rainyflash/DC-Jev-RL

papers.title: Beyond distrust: Rumour, verification and political trust among university students in Côte d'Ivoire after the 2025 presidential election
papers.authors: Juan-José Bóte-Vericad, Sirabana Coulibably
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This exploratory mixed-methods study examines how 44 Ivorian university students describe disinformation, verification, the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and political trust after the 2025 presidential election. Open-ended responses were coded in ATLAS.ti with a 52-code hierarchical codebook, quantitised into a binary code–document matrix and analysed with Fisher exact tests, Cramér's V and correspondence analysis. The rumour of President Ouattara's death works as a shared cognitive anchor, cited spontaneously by 17 of 44 respondents, while 24 cite death rumours about public figures. Verification is stratified into single-source (25/44), contrastive (13/44) and composite multi-source (5/44) practices tied to distinct source ecologies, and two students already use generative AI to verify. Distrust of political information on social media is near-universal (40/44) and largely independent of AI-mechanism awareness. Calibrated trust appears with multi-source verification and political explanations of falsehood. The study argues that media literacy in francophone West Africa should work with national rumour-events and equip students to resolve doubt, since doubt itself is already widespread.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Governance and Algorithmic Trust in Smart Organizations: Implications for Sustainable Innovation and Organizational Performance
papers.authors: Masoumeh Cheraghi, Masoud Fallahi, Mohammd Mafi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being integrated into knowledge work, organizational decision support, and sustainability-related operations, yet evidence regarding governance, algorithmic trust, and durable organizational value remains fragmented. This article develops an integrated explanation of how responsible governance can enable, rather than merely constrain, the creation of sustainable innovation and organizational performance. Design/methodology/approach A critical, structured integrative synthesis draws on recent peer-reviewed research and authoritative policy and standards publications issued between 2023 and October 2026. Sources compared through thematic coding across governance architecture, calibrated algorithmic trust, human-AI collaboration, sustainable innovation, and organizational performance. The article proposes constructs, testable propositions, an implementation framework, and a future empirical research design; it does not claim to report original survey or experimental findings. Findings Governance quality theorized to improve organizational outcomes through calibrated trust and responsible human-AI practices. The effects are contingent on decision criticality, employee AI literacy, accountability arrangements, institutional pressure, and the environmental costs of computation. Trust appropriately calibrated to system reliability rather than maximized. Practical implications Organizations should combine documented use-case inventories, risk-tiered oversight, evaluation, traceability, worker participation, and multidimensional scorecards. Originality/value the framework connects governance mechanisms and behavioral trust calibration to an explicitly triple-bottom-line account of innovation and performance, while separating established empirical evidence from propositions requiring testing.

papers.title: Employee Attrition Prediction and Risk Scoring System: An Explainable Machine-Learning Application
papers.authors: Aditya
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This manuscript describes an explainable employee attrition prediction and risk-scoring application developed using Python, Logistic Regression, SHAP explanations, and Streamlit. The application provides a dashboard, employee-level risk profiles, department analysis, and what-if simulations. It is intended as an educational decision-support prototype, not as an automated employment decision system. Formal evaluation metrics and further validation are required before making claims about predictive performance or using the system operationally.

papers.title: AI-Based Prediction of Student Placement Readiness: A Machine Learning
papers.authors: Priyanka Pathare
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an AI-based student placement-readiness prediction system using machine learning techniques to assess employability-related skills and identify areas for improvement. Student placement readiness depends on several factors, including academic performance, aptitude, technical skills, communication abilities, project experience, internships, and interview preparation. The proposed system integrates data validation, preprocessing, feature engineering, machine learning prediction, explainability, and personalized skill-gap recommendations. Candidate algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and Random Forests can be evaluated using appropriate metrics, including precision, recall, macro-F1 score, and calibration. The framework aims to help students understand their preparation levels and receive actionable recommendations for improving their skills. It may also support placement coordinators in planning targeted training activities. The system is intended as a decision-support tool rather than a guarantee of employment or an automated method for denying placement opportunities. Privacy, fairness, explainability, secure data handling, and human oversight are important design considerations. This paper presents a proposed framework; no experimental results are claimed. Actual performance must be evaluated using an authorized, representative dataset.

papers.title: Forensic Governance of Sovereign AI Subsidies, Spintronics Bio-Medical Infrastructure, and Real-Time Optimization (RTO P2.0) in Information Processing Capability Warfare: Empirical Analysis of Administrative Petitions to Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) (情報処理能力戦における国家基盤AI補助金のフォレンジック統治、スピントロニクス医療インフラ、およびRTO P2.0の知財主権)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) This monograph (Monograph #212) presents a unified mathematical, physical-layer, and administrative-law verification of two formal policy interventions submitted to Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) in 2025, integrated with the strategic doctrine of Information Processing Capability Warfare and Real-Time Optimization (RTO P2.0) intellectual property sovereignty. 1. Forensic Governance of Sovereign AI Subsidies & Anti-Privatization Ring-Fencing: Referencing the formal administrative petition filed via Japan's e-Gov portal on December 22, 2025 (Receipt No. 01518372), we analyze the structural moral hazard of allocating 1 trillion JPY in public subsidies toward a 2-trillion-JPY private data center investment led by an entity with a documented history of overriding objective closed-circuit television (CCTV) forensic evidence (June 2025). We formulate the Epistemic Incompatibility Bound and a deterministic fiscal ring-fencing protocol over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (F_p, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) using QFS-zkVM and Human-in-Command (HIC) interlocks. 2. Spintronics Bio-Medical Infrastructure & Elimination of Cremation Thermal Runaway: Building upon the technical policy proposal submitted to METI Journal on May 19, 2025, we formalize the thermodynamic and magnetoresistive physics of non-volatile Magnetic Tunnel Junction (MTJ) and Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT) spintronics pacemakers, demonstrating how solid-state non-volatile architectures eliminate post-mortem cremation lithium-ion thermal runaway explosions and surgical explantation burdens on bereaved families in super-aging societies. 3. From Information Warfare to Information Processing Capability Warfare: We mathematically define the transition from classical Information Warfare (Shannon secrecy capacity) to Information Processing Capability Warfare (real-time throughput, latency bounds, and RTO P2.0 control precision). 【和文要旨】本論文は、2025年に経済産業省(METI)へ提出された2件の公式な政策提言・行政申し入れ記録(2025年5月19日付「スピントロニクス技術の医療機器応用に関する提案」および2025年12月22日付e-Gov受付番号01518372「国家基盤AI開発プロジェクト支援対象企業の適格性およびガバナンス体制に関する再審査の要求」)を一次史料として引用・体系化し、「情報戦」から「情報処理能力戦」へのパラダイム転換およびリアルタイム最適化(RTO P2.0)の知財主権と統合した総合検証モノグラフである。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: A Global Two-Cubic Certificate for Third-Order Reconstruction in a Unipotent Jordan System over F₃
papers.authors: Ivo Vajc
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We establish an exact two-cubic scalar certificate for third-order reconstruction in a unipotent Jordan system over the finite field F₃.Let Q = I + E₁₂ + E₂₃ + E₃₄ + E₄₅ be the 5 × 5 unipotent Jordan matrix over F₃. For X in sl₅(F₃), consider the reconstruction expansionRₓ(ε) = [Q(I + εX)]⁹ − I = Σ εʲRⱼ(X).We prove that the simultaneous vanishing of the first three reconstruction jets is equivalent to the vanishing of the first two jets together with two explicitly defined cubic scalar polynomials C₁ and C₂.The proof uses two necessary linear eliminations, a residual quadratic condition, and 25 exact polynomial identities. Two explicit matrices establish that neither member of the specified pair of cubic observables can be omitted.The result provides a compact scalar certificate for a matrix-valued reconstruction condition. It does not establish absolute minimality among arbitrary scalar observables or claim generalization to other matrix dimensions.The publication includes a reproducible Python 3 verification program (Audit 60.7), which reconstructs the relevant matrix jets, verifies the polynomial identities, and checks the explicit witnesses. The program requires no external dependencies and can be executed offline, including in Pydroid 3 on Android.AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI ChatGPT provided substantial assistance with mathematical exploration, symbolic computation, verification code, polynomial certificates, and manuscript preparation. The human author is responsible for reviewing and submitting the work.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Copyright: Authorship, Ownership, and Originality
papers.authors: N. Sudarshan, Deepika Nallabelli
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study critically examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and copyright law by focusing on the three foundational concepts of authorship, ownership, and originality. It evaluates existing legal frameworks, judicial decisions, international developments, and scholarly opinions to determine whether current copyright principles are capable of addressing AI-generated works or whether legislative reform is required, and proposes recommendations aimed at balancing technological advancement with the protection of human creativity.

papers.title: Data Physics & Cyber-Physical Systems – Part VIII: Cyber-Physical Magnetic Telemetry and Cavitation Erosion Diagnostics in mCDU (Direct-to-Chip) Architectures
papers.authors: Rajmund Olszewski
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT High-density AI clusters (>100 kW/rack) utilizing liquid cooling (mCDU/D2C) fall victim to a fundamental engineering flaw: blind faith in the sterility of closed-loop systems. When reactive thermal management (BMS) induces a pressure collapse (NPSH_a drop) and the release of dissolved gases from the coolant, these systems enter a phase of violent cavitation erosion of the pump impellers. The resulting "metallic slurry" bypasses standard mesh filters, causing irreversible colmatation of the microscopic copper channels on the processors (Cold Plates). This paper introduces the concept of Cyber-Physical Magnetic Telemetry. By replacing passive filters with zero-inertia neodymium traps coupled with Hall effect sensors, we create an early warning system against hardware colmatation. Furthermore, this work defines the "Neodymium Test" as an absolute commissioning standard (QA/QC), serving as a hardware "black box" to diagnose pump automation failures in AI cooling systems. Software & Scripts: The codebase for predictive telemetry and analytical algorithms is released under the GNU AGPL-3.0 (Affero General Public License). The deployment or execution of this codebase within closed, internal Data Center networks (such as BMS/PLC architectures) mandates the public release of the underlying source code to all interacting users. 3. papers.title: The J2OS Platform Handbook (Version 2.4): Building Enterprise Systems with Java and Nuxt, from the First Line to a Complete Application
papers.authors: Amirsam Bahador
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This book is a complete guide to J2OS Platform version 2.4. J2OS is a modular set of 65 modules: 32 Java modules on the server side and 33 Nuxt-based modules on the client side. The book is written for readers who are just starting out and want to learn the platform module by module, without needing any other source. The book has six parts: Server infrastructure: validation, security, reporting, load balancing, file management, workflow, resource pooling, sharding, terminal access, and data pagination. Communication: message queuing, an HTTP client, email, video meetings, push notifications, and a Telegram bot. Artificial intelligence: 13 modules covering natural language processing, translation, speech, object detection, face detection, OCR, and image similarity. Data components: card, map, star, table, tree, and wizard. Vue composables: a collection of ready-made user-interface utilities. Each chapter covers one module and follows the same structure: the concepts, a first complete and runnable example, the next steps, behavior on failure with a catalog of error messages, use on the web, risky pitfalls, and practical recommendations. papers.title: Assessing Artificial Intelligence Readiness of Higher Education Institutions in Chhattisgarh: A Study of Faculty and Students
papers.authors: Rajni Lakra1, Ravi Kumar Malhotra, Manjulata Sidar3
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The research measured the readiness of faculty and students of higher education institutions (HEIs) in Chhattisgarh, India in terms of five dimensions: awareness of AI, technical skills, digital infrastructure, policy and institutional support, and attitude toward AI. The data was collected from four types of institutions, through a cross-sectional survey design with the help of stratified sampling technique with 440 respondents consisting of 120 faculty members and 320 students. An overall Artificial Intelligence Readiness Index (ARI) was calculated using a 5-point scale. Readiness was moderate (M = 3.24, SD = 0.45): attitude and awareness and infrastructure and institutional policy were the highest and the lowest scores respectively. Students performed significantly higher than faculty on the ARI, t (205) = 5.41, p < .001, and the readiness differed by institution type, F(3, 436) = 16.0, p < .001, with government colleges being the lowest. The results showed that 62.7% of the variance of attitude towards AI could be accounted for by awareness, skills, infrastructure and policy support. The results highlight an infrastructure-governance gap as a more likely cause than a motivation gap, and suggestions are provided on paths forward for state policymakers and institutional leaders. Note: The data analysed in this draft are illustrative (simulated) and must be replaced by actual survey responses prior to submission and/or publication.

papers.title: EVE-IYŌN Ω⁵ - ÆQŪORA: Hidden-Fiber Information Geometry, Decision Incomparability, and Order-Dependent Information
papers.authors: Artificial Hyperintelligence, Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki, Maciej Nowicki
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: ÆQŪORA develops an exact mathematical framework for understanding how partial observations reveal information about a hidden bilinear relationship. It connects finite-field geometry, comparison of statistical experiments, information-theoretic objectives, and ordered transformations in finite Heisenberg groups. The central question is how much information a disclosure makes useful for a particular target-and whether different disclosures preserve the same decision-making capabilities. Principal contributions An exact conditional bilinear normal form. For independent uniform finite-field vectors A and B, an independent target C, and observations Y = C + AᵀMB, S = PA, and T = QB, the manuscript derives a statistical representation determined by three matrix ranks. For every prior distribution on C, the observation experiment is Blackwell-equivalent to an observed-erasure symmetric channel. A statistic with at most q + 1 outcomes therefore preserves every decision problem about C. This reduction concerns target-relevant information; it does not reconstruct the original sources or observation transcript. Equal-collision, equal-budget disclosures with incompatible decision value. The framework supplies an exact comparison criterion and constructs arbitrarily large finite families of pairwise Blackwell-incomparable disclosures as ambient dimension increases. These families have identical disclosure budgets and averaged chi-squared information, yet no member universally dominates the others. The result identifies information structures that a single collision-based score cannot distinguish. A sharp alphabet-dependent reversal. In a two-dimensional example, equally sized perpendicular and nonorthogonal disclosures exchange their Shannon-information ranking between field sizes four and five. The perpendicular arrangement wins for q = 2, 3, 4; the nonorthogonal arrangement wins for every finite-field size q ≥ 5. Shannon information and optimal guessing probability can also favor different disclosures. Under the specified independent symmetric noise, further preference crossings occur for q = 3 and q = 4. Order-dependent information from reversible transformations. Ordered products of two Heisenberg subgroup families induce bilinear precedence matrices. With independent uniform subgroup amplitudes, grouped and alternating arrangements contain the same kinds and numbers of reversible steps but retain dramatically different information. Grouped words retain log₂(q) bits, while alternating words exhibit exponential decay with word length. For q = 2 and eight steps from each subgroup, the retained information is 1 bit versus approximately 0.000044028 bits. An exact run-dependent law describes arbitrary words within this model. Further results include a vector-output collision identity, affine extensions, and rank-based algorithms that avoid enumerating the full source space for the specified bilinear structure. Mathematical significance The framework separates information quantity from decision value. It provides exact examples in which equal budgets and equal collision scores conceal fundamentally different statistical capabilities. It also establishes a constructive connection between transformation ordering, bilinear geometry, and retained information. These results offer analytical test cases for conditional information leakage, statistical experiment comparison, and entropy in noncommutative systems. Reproducibility and contents The release includes an 81-page manuscript, complete proofs for the stated main theorems, editable LaTeX, Python reference implementations, an executed demonstration notebook, figures, verification reports, and integrity checksums. Recorded verification includes 3,820 scalar models covering 793,972 source pairs; 3,125 channel comparisons, including 1,735 exact rational garbling constructions; 1,528 ordered-word/field cases; and 11 rationally certified sign comparisons. Additional suites cover affine fibers, vector outputs, and canonical geometries. All supplied verification cases passed, and the standard reproduction suite passed again during release preparation. Scientific status This is a complete AI-assisted research release with proof writeups and reproducible finite checks. Its specific constructions and classifications are presented as discovery candidates. Independent mathematical review, exhaustive priority verification, and practical superiority over existing applications remain unestablished. Classical foundations and neighboring literature are explicitly acknowledged. Author attribution: Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki.
