papers.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on Personalized Learning
papers.authors: Thorat Om
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Personalized learning aims to adapt educational content, learning pace, feedback, and support to the needs of individual learners. Traditional classroom approaches can make this difficult because students differ in prior knowledge, learning speed, interests, and support requirements. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and deep learning offer ways to analyze learner data, estimate performance, recommend learning resources, and adjust learning pathways. This paper presents a structured narrative review of five studies published between 2023 and 2025, selected from the author’s preliminary literature survey. The reviewed work covers adaptive learning technologies, deep-learning-based pathways in higher education, student perceptions of AI-supported learning, and machine-learning methods for predicting online learning performance. Across these studies, AI appears promising for adaptive content delivery, timely feedback, learner engagement, and early identification of students who may need support. However, the evidence is limited by differences in study settings, limited coverage of learner populations, and a shortage of long-term evaluations linking predictions to sustained learning outcomes. Privacy, algorithmic bias, output accuracy, explainability, teacher oversight, and over-reliance on AI remain important concerns. Because this paper synthesizes previously published studies rather than conducting a new experiment, it reports no original participant data or model-performance results. The review concludes that responsible personalized learning requires transparent evaluation, secure data practices, inclusive design, and collaboration between AI systems and educators.Keywords—Artificial intelligence, personalized learning, adaptive learning, machine learning, student performance prediction, educational technology, learning analytics.

papers.abstract: This independent working paper examines the technical, economic and organisational conditions for assessing small wind power at alpine pasture facilities, farms, and residential or hospitality properties in South Tyrol. The documentary analysis distinguishes site-specific wind resources, consumption profiles, net generation, self-consumption, storage, component compatibility and total costs. All-in-one systems are considered a potential means of simplifying selected interfaces, without assuming that a photovoltaic-and-storage package is automatically compatible with a wind turbine. Chinese manufacturers’ offerings and European commercial examples are treated as market options rather than purchasing recommendations or independently verified performance. An original economic example presents three hypothetical generation scenarios, distinguishing energy value, running costs, replacement expenditure and net present value. The paper also proposes a decision matrix and a possible voluntary, manufacturer-independent regional pilot platform. The possible involvement of the Bolzano Chamber of Commerce, HGV and Südtiroler Bauernbund is the author’s proposal. It does not imply existing agreements, funding, endorsement or commitments. The paper presents no original measurements and does not certify the suitability of sites or systems. It is not an engineering implementation design, legal opinion or purchase recommendation. It has not undergone peer review. AI assistance is disclosed in the document; responsibility for the content, sources and conclusions remains with the author. papers.title: Egypt's Comprehensive Development Vision — Part III: A Strategic Framework for National Transformation, Institutional Development, Human Capital, and Technological Innovation
papers.authors: Detective ElShazly, Ahmed Saher
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract and Research Description This research is the third installment of Egypt’s Comprehensive Development Vision, a broader initiative exploring strategic approaches to Egypt’s long-term development and national transformation. The study presents a comprehensive conceptual framework for developing state institutions, strengthening strategic planning, improving public administration, advancing education and human capital, promoting technological innovation and artificial intelligence, and enhancing accountability and institutional effectiveness. It explores the metaphor of the state as a living organism, examining the interconnected roles of national leadership, citizens, intelligence and strategic analysis, defense institutions, legislative bodies, public oversight, and essential infrastructure. The research also proposes approaches to urban and regional development, the modernization of Egyptian cities and villages, the development of religious and educational institutions, the intellectual advancement of society, the growth of domestic technology and digital platforms, and the sustainable use of national resources, including the Nile River and its islands. In addition to presenting strategic proposals, the study explores practical implementation mechanisms, institutional coordination, performance measurement, innovation initiatives, and long-term planning. Its objective is to develop an integrated vision that connects human development, institutional reform, scientific progress, technological capability, economic advancement, cultural identity, and national sustainability. This document is published in both English and Arabic. The complete English version appears first, followed by the complete original Arabic version, making the research accessible to international readers as well as Arabic-speaking audiences. This work forms part of an ongoing conceptual research series dedicated to exploring ideas and proposals for Egypt’s future development. The proposals are intended to encourage strategic thinking, constructive discussion, and the development of practical solutions suited to Egypt’s national priorities and circumstances.

papers.title: The False Rivalry Between Educators and AI
papers.authors: Osman Bedel
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The claim that artificial intelligence (AI) and educators are rivals mistakes a set of tools for a profession and reduces teaching to information delivery. Yet rejecting the rivalry metaphor does not require uncritical adoption. Research on intelligent tutoring systems and recent generative AI trials shows that design matters: some structured systems improve short-term learning, while unrestricted answer-giving can raise practice scores and weaken later independent performance. Evidence about teacher–student relationships, screen use, and teachers’ reported time savings further complicates simple replacement and prohibition narratives. Building on an earlier vision of educator-led educational change, this conceptual article proposes five questions for evaluating AI use: teachers should define the learning goal, retain authority over consequential judgments, protect student data, and test whether learners can transfer knowledge without the tool. Institutions should provide time, training, and procurement rules that make those responsibilities feasible. The questions are a design proposal whose effects require testing. The point is to make AI answerable to the purposes of education and to the people responsible for them.

papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: PARTE 1: VERSIONE ITALIANA (ITALIAN VERSION) SOMMARIO ACCADEMICO E SCIENTIFICO Il presente deposito formalizza e sigilla la Release METODO DEMARIA 3.4, costituita dal Trattato Unificato Canonico Bilingue (Italiano Pagine 1-12 / Inglese Pagine 13-24), dall'autonoma Appendice A (102 pagine) e dalla suite software di calcolo, stocastica ed audit di laboratorio. L'opera sintetizza la definitiva dimostrazione matematica, topologica e stocastica della decodifica vettoriale del Manoscritto Voynich (Beinecke MS 408) limitatamente ai Tiers A, B e C. Rigettando l'ipotesi linguistico-fonetica convenzionale (Symbol-to-Sound / Symbol-to-Meaning), il METODO DEMARIA formalizza ed afferma il modello cibernetico e vettoriale (Symbol-to-Vector / Symbol-to-State): il corpus grafico di 35.483 token EVA (distribuiti su 227 folii e 5.385 righi) non costituisce una scrittura parlata o cifrata, bensì un Instruction Set deterministico e calcolabile, progettato per la regolazione e il monitoraggio di uno spazio degli stati all'interno di un Automa Temporizzato ad Anello Chiuso (Closed-Loop Timed Automaton). PARAMETRI E METRICHE DI LABORATORIO CONGELATI (RELEASE 3.4): Coerenza Sintattica Grezza Flusso Continuo: C_raw_stream = 0,799589 (79,96 percento su 35.483 token EVA e 227 folii unici). Coerenza Sintattica Vincolata al Rigo: C_raw_line = 0,798060 (79,81 percento). Entropia Dinamica di Shannon: H(X) = 1,8770 bit (1,6947 bit sul campione degli stati minimi proiettati). Stato Zero Copertina (Power-OFF Enclosure S0): Carico computazionale Z_cover = 0,0 kPa ed Entropia Dinamica H_cover(X) = 0,0000 bit, formalizzando la chiusura topologica del dominio al 100 percento e smentendo definitivamente l'ipotesi secolare di mutilazione codicologica. Modelli Nulli Gerarchici Monte Carlo (N = 10.000 iterazioni, Seed 42): Global Null Model Z = +19,8404 (p < 0,0001, Effect Size d di Cohen = 7,6366); Intra-Folio Null Model Z = +16,3961 (p < 0,0001, d = 8,0261); Intra-Line Null Model (Prova Regina di Rigo) Z_Line = +14,5202 (p < 0,0001, p_param = 1,20 x 10^-21, Effect Size d di Cohen = 9,4860). Test Avversariale Isomorfo di Doppia Randomizzazione (N = 10.000): Z_double_null = +1,5239 (p-value empirico = 0,032000), attestante la perfetta ed esclusiva selettività dell'accoppiamento tra il parser del Metodo e la coordinata line_id del manoscritto. Stress Test e Validazione Holdout Out-of-Sample: Retention del segnale topologico pari al 99,22 percento a fronte dell'inoculazione del 10,0 percento di rumore sintattico; Holdout 80/20 su 227 folii con scarto irrisorio dello 0,8269 percento (C_train = 0,799460 vs C_test = 0,792849), che esclude qualsiasi fenomeno di sovra-ottimizzazione (overfitting). Benchmarking Cross-Corpus su 10 Corpora Storici (N = 83.241 elementi): Rigetto per tutti e 9 i corpora di controllo ad anello aperto e validazione esclusiva sull'Automa del Voynich, a garanzia della falsificabilità popperiana prescritta dai protocolli accademici internazionali. Motore Invariante C per Triage Deterministico: Throughput validato di 15.758.504 vettori/secondo con latenza media di 63,4 nanosecondi e catalogazione della Copertina al 100 percento in Classe 0 (Standby Neutro). NOTA BIOGRAFICO-EPISTEMOLOGICA DELL'AUTORE Il METODO DEMARIA nasce dall'intuizione di un uomo comune amante di scrittura e poesia che con umiltà e sensibilità per la Natura e la forma visiva si è accostato allo studio del Manoscritto Voynich. L'approccio applica il rigore logico-deduttivo per superare il paradigma fonetico in favore di una formalizzazione cibernetica calcolabile soggetta a rigida falsificabilità popperiana. Il metodo decompila il codice sulla quadrupla di stato (Alpha, Beta, Delta, Gamma), identificando nella ricerca dell'Essenza e dell'Armonia — quale equilibrio ad anello chiuso tra carica, scorrimento, stasi e decompressione — il principio informatore della notazione. Con profondo rispetto verso il mondo accademico e scientifico, l'opera è offerta come un contributo d'Armonia aperto alla verifica e al perfezionamento di altri studiosi. Ad maiora semper. Avv. Alessandro Demaria. MENZIONE LEGALE, TUTELA DEL MARCHIO E PROPRIETÀ INTELLETTUALE Marchio Registrato UIBM N. 302026000161716 METODO DEMARIA. papers.title: 医療AI技術ギャップと投資優先順位:単純CTにおける仮想造影技術「Virtual Contrast」の実装障壁と戦略的ギャップ分析 (Medical AI Technology Gaps and Global Capital Prioritization: Implementation Barriers of Non-Contrast CT "Virtual Contrast," Swin-UNETR ASIC Co-Design, and ROI Asymmetry Against Physical AI Humanoids)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 非造影単純CT(NCCT)から造影CT(CECT)およびMRI級の高コントラスト血管・組織診断能力を合成する「仮想造影(Virtual Contrast / PHASOR)」および3D医療画像セグメンテーション(Swin-UNETR)の救命救急実装を阻む本質は、ニューラルネットワークの未成熟ではなく、①計算複雑性とエッジ物理プロセッサの限界、②ヒューマノイドロボット(Physical AI)との圧倒的なマクロ経済的投資対効果(ROI)の非対称性、③FDA Class III(PMA事前承認)薬事規制が課す巨額の臨床検証コストと偽陰性(見落とし)訴訟リスクという3つの不連続なギャップにある。本稿(第212編)は、(1) AlphaFoldの共進化配列モデルからマクロ血管トポロジーへの直接転用不可能性、(2) 自動運転エッジAI(Waymo等)の既存CTレトロフィット障壁、(3) 105物理量子ビット「Willow」におけるQAOA定数時間 O(1) 収束の3大数理障壁(次元爆発・デコヒーレンス・不毛の平原)、(4) 200ms未満・精度損失0.5%未満を実現するSwin-UNETR専用混合精度ASIC+3Dダイスタッキング(SRAM/HBM)コデザイン、(5) 3D医療画像AI(2035年TAM 185.6億ドル、回収5年以上)とヒューマノイドロボット(2050年TAM 5〜7兆ドル、回収最短36週間)の定量的ROI比較、および (6) 救急現場における「人為的不作為」言説への科学的反証と薬事・半導体改革の3大提言を体系化する。 (English Summary): This 212th monograph establishes a rigorous technical, macroeconomic, and regulatory gap analysis of Non-Contrast CT (NCCT) "Virtual Contrast" (Class III Software as a Medical Device, SaMD). We prove why 1D-to-3D co-evolutionary protein networks (AlphaFold 2/3), 2D autonomous driving edge accelerators (Waymo), and 105-qubit NISQ QAOA circuits ("Willow" / PHASOR) fail to meet the acute emergency clinical threshold (<200 ms latency, <0.5% mDSC loss across 3.3x10^7 voxels). We blueprint a two-phase Swin-UNETR ASIC co-design (combining INT8 systolic arrays with isolated FP16/FP32 LUT/PWL nonlinear engines and 3D-stacked HBM/SRAM), quantify the capital-allocation asymmetry between Class III medical imaging AI ($94M-$112.8M PMA cost, >5-year payback) and Physical AI humanoids (36-week payback across a $5T-$7T TAM), and formulate three actionable hardware, quantum-encoding, and FDA adaptive-trial reforms. papers.title: ハンマーとエコー:抽象的制御の源泉としての物理的実装に関する戦略的分析 — VGSOTスピントロニクス・BNSF発荷鉄道輸送量(RTO)・量子エコーによる統一制御理論 (The Hammer and the Echo: Physical Implementation as the Source of Abstract Control)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 本稿(第212編)は、「抽象的なガバナンスや意思決定の成否は、最下層の物理的実装(ハードウェアおよび実体物理テレメトリ)の制御によって一意に決定される」という統一制御原理(思考のハンマーと量子エコー)を定式化するものである。ヨハイ・ベンクラーおよびローレンス・レッシグの3層統治モデル(物理インフラ層・論理コード層・コンテンツ層)と19世紀産業革命期の「制御の危機(Crisis of Control)」を起点として、本稿は一見無関係に見える3つの領域に同一の構造的解決策が存在することを証明する:(1) AIガバナンスと「メモリー・ガバナンス・ギャップ」の物理的閉鎖:行政委員会による抽象的AIレビュー(オハイオ州・コネチカット州DAS等)が、エージェント型ブラウザ(OpenAI Atlas等)における「Tainted Memories(CSRFメモリ汚染攻撃)」および「Cloaking Attacks(AIクローラー標的型偽装攻撃)」によって即座に無力化される構造を解明し、VGSOT-MTJ(電圧ゲート・スピン軌道トルク磁気トンネル接合)を用いたインメモリ・コンピューティング、物理的複製不能関数(PUF)、およびロジック・ロッキング(Logic Locking)によるハードウェア封じ込めを導出する;(2) 実体経済とBNSF発荷鉄道輸送量(RTO):ウォーレン・バフェット氏の投資戦略の核にある「貨物列車積載量(RTO:化学品RTOCH・石炭RTOCO・砕石RTOCS・穀物RTOGR・自動車RTOMV・石油製品RTOPP)」とBNSFネットワーク・オペレーション・センター(NOC)が、投機的な株価ノイズを排して実体経済の物理層をリアルタイム処理する「インメモリ・コンピューター」として機能していることを証明する;(3) 量子エコー(Quantum Echoes)と公衆衛生・創薬への拡張:Google Quantum AIの「Quantum Echoes」における検証可能性(Verifiability)と概念的共鳴(Conceptual Resonance)を統合し、パンデミック封じ込め(下水ウイルス量リアルタイム監視とPUFロット検証)までを貫く物理層統治の普遍法則を確立する。 (English Summary): This 212th monograph formalizes "The Hammer and the Echo"—a unified systems-control theory proving that abstract governance (whether in AI ethics, financial markets, or public health) succeeds only when anchored in non-negotiable physical-layer hardware implementation and physical telemetry. Drawing upon Benkler and Lessig's three-layer stack and Beniger's "Crisis of Control," we establish structural isomorphism across three domains: (1) Closing the AI "Memory Governance Gap" (exposed by OpenAI Atlas "Tainted Memories" CSRF and "Cloaking Attacks") via Voltage-Gated Spin-Orbit-Torque (VGSOT-MTJ) in-memory computing, Physically Unclonable Functions (PUF), and Logic Locking; (2) Grounding financial valuation in Warren Buffett's BNSF Network Operations Center (NOC) and Rail Traffic Originated (RTO: RTOCH, RTOCO, RTOCS, RTOGR, RTOMV, RTOPP) physical freight telemetry; and (3) Extending Google Quantum AI's "Quantum Echoes" verifiability and conceptual resonance to public-health wastewater viral-load telemetry and PUF clinical-batch authentication. papers.title: Accelerating Multidimensional Quantum Factoring: Sub-O(n^(3/2)) Gate Regimes, 4n-Qubit Streamed Estimation, and Unconditional Correctness
papers.authors: Denis Gnitiyov
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Oded Regev's multidimensional quantum factoring algorithm (J. ACM 2025) reduced the sequential quantum circuit depth of factoring from Shor's algorithm down to square-root-of-n modular squarings, requiring O(n^(1.5)) quantum gates per run across O(sqrt(n)) runs. However, four fundamental bottlenecks remained: (1) an exponential LLL lattice-reduction loss that inflated the quantum Gaussian radius and tripled the required squarings; (2) a high qubit memory footprint, where reversible uncomputation required storing large intermediate states or suffering huge time penalties; (3) holding all input dimensions in quantum memory required large coherent registers; and (4) mathematical correctness depended on an unproven heuristic assumption on short lattice vectors. We present a unified quantum-classical architecture that resolves these bottlenecks and establishes new complexity frontiers for quantum factorization: (1) Lattice Post-Processing Overhaul: By replacing LLL with polynomial-time Block Korkine-Zolotarev (BKZ) reduction and quantum sample amplification, we eliminate the exponential transference loss, shrinking the Gaussian radius exponent by 3x and cutting critical-path modular depth by 6x through Windowed Horizon Aggregation. (2) Pebbling-Free Dual-Inverse Arithmetic: By integrating radius compression into dual-inverse Zeckendorf-Fibonacci reversible arithmetic, we eliminate intermediate storage checkpoints with zero time penalty, reducing total memory to approximately 7.44n qubits. (3) Streamed Estimation in 4n Qubits: Combining radius compression with streamed backwards Fibonacci quantum phase estimation shrinks the required ladder depth by 3x, executing the entire attack on a recycled control register using only 4n coherent qubits (or 3n qubits with in-place arithmetic). For RSA-2048, this cuts continuous coherence runtime from 8.0 hours down to 8.2 minutes (a 58x speedup over Shor's algorithm). (4) Sub-O(n^(1.5)) Gate Frontier: We prove an Arithmetic-Geometric Mean (AM-GM) transference lower bound showing that unstructured lattices cannot break below n^(1.5) gates in polynomial classical time, and circumvent this barrier for smooth-quotient composite moduli using a block-projected pipeline to achieve O(n^(4/3) log n) quantum gates. (5) Unconditional Correctness: Using Cedric Pilatte's analytic number theory framework (zero-density estimates and p-torsion stabilization), we unconditionally prove that the lattice algorithm factors any composite number N in strictly polynomial classical time with single-batch success probability of at least 31.25% (approaching 37.5%). Under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, factoring requires only 4n qubits and small prime bases. --- AI Research and Authorship Disclosure: In full accordance with international scientific disclosure standards, open-access repository guidelines on AI-assisted research, and ACM/IEEE policies on generative artificial intelligence, the provenance, governance, and execution of this work are delineated as follows: 1. Conceptual Initiative, Research Vision, and Workflow Direction (Denis Gnitiyov):The foundational research initiative to achieve this breakthrough was conceived and launched by Denis Gnitiyov upon studying Oded Regev's multidimensional quantum factoring framework. Acknowledging that the high-level advanced mathematics (higher-dimensional lattice geometry, analytic number theory, and fault-tolerant quantum circuit synthesis) exceeds manual human calculation, Denis Gnitiyov conceived the project vision, established the initiative to systematically eliminate the theoretical and physical bottlenecks of the Regev paradigm, directed the multi-LLM research workflow, and maintained supervisory governance over the end-to-end scientific pipeline. 2. Paper Architecture, Bottleneck Formulation, and Orchestration (Gemini Flash 3.8):Gemini Flash 3.8 served as the paper builder, systems architect, and research orchestrator. Operating under Denis Gnitiyov's initiative, Gemini Flash 3.8 ingested and dissected Regev's multidimensional factoring research, systematically analyzed the theoretical framework to identify and formulate the four foundational bottlenecks, structured the overarching modular paper architecture, formulated the specific mathematical target problems to be solved, and handled the complete synthesis, typesetting, and mathematical structuring of the LaTeX manuscript. 3. Advanced Mathematical Discovery, Derivations, and Proof Engineering (Gemini Argon 4):Gemini Argon 4 served as the primary mathematical reasoning and discovery engine. In response to the technical bottlenecks and problem formulations established by Gemini Flash 3.8, Gemini Argon 4 derived the formal mathematical proofs and quantum circuit synthesis, including lattice transference separation under BKZ, the AM-GM transference barrier and smooth-quotient algorithm, Pilatte's unconditional p-torsion bounds, and reversible Zeckendorf-Fibonacci arithmetic.

papers.title: Gurav's Worst Possibility Theorem (GWPT): A Unified Mathematical Paradigm for Risk Invariance, Pre-emptive Mitigation, and Autonomous Fail-Safe Decision Systems
papers.authors: Sanjay Vidya Vijay Gurav Sanjay
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Title: Gurav's Worst Possibility Theorem (GWPT): A Unified Mathematical Paradigm for Risk Invariance, Pre-emptive Mitigation, and Autonomous Fail-Safe Decision Systems मराठी शीर्षक: गुरव वर्स्ट पॉसिबिलिटी प्रमेय (GWPT): जोखीम शून्यीकरण, पूर्वतयारी आणि सुरक्षित स्वायत्त प्रणालींचा एकात्मिक शोधनिबंध * Lead Author & Systems Architect: Adv. Sanjay Vidya Vijay Gurav (B.Com., LL.B., B.A. Psychology | Systems Architect) * Permanent Identifier (ORCID): 0009-0008-GURAV-GWPT * License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) Abstract (English) Conventional decision frameworks, artificial intelligence paradigms, and industrial architectures predominantly operate on the baseline maximization of Expected Utility under normative operating conditions, treating catastrophic failures as secondary exception routines. This paper establishes Gurav's Worst Possibility Theorem (GWPT), conceptualized by Adv. Sanjay Vidya Vijay Gurav, governed by the primary axiom: "Always anticipate the worst possibility first." We present an optimization framework wherein candidate policies are strictly bounded by pre-emptive adversarial failure suppression: We mathematically prove that when the Mitigation Index M(x, w) \to 1.0, the residual risk penalty collapses asymptotically to zero, yielding a deterministic fail-safe optimal decision state (\mathcal{A}^*). papers.title: The AI Revolution: Job Displacement, Human Progress, and the Ethics of Technological Power
papers.authors: Zeeshan Khan
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper examines the opportunities and risks associated with the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), with particular attention to employment, technological change, synthetic media, and responsible governance. Using a narrative literature review and critical synthesis of academic research and institutional publications, the paper explores how AI can automate tasks, transform occupations, improve productivity, and create new opportunities while also contributing to job displacement, inequality, privacy violations, misinformation, fraud, and non-consensual synthetic imagery. The discussion draws lessons from earlier technologies, including calculators, computers, and industrial machinery, while recognising that historical comparisons cannot guarantee that current transitions will be painless or equitable. The paper proposes a framework for responsible AI adoption based on worker protections, accessible lifelong learning, transparent deployment, human accountability, privacy safeguards, content provenance, safety-by-design, and effective remedies for abuse. The manuscript argues that AI's social and economic outcomes depend not only on technological capabilities but also on the policies, institutions, and decisions governing its development and use. Methodology: Narrative literature review and critical synthesis of publicly available academic research and institutional publications. Limitations: This paper does not present original experimental data or a quantitative estimate of AI's net employment effects. Its findings should be interpreted as a synthesis of selected literature rather than a systematic review or peer-reviewed research article.

papers.title: A Reproducible Machine Learning Pipeline for Educational Workload Analytics Using Synthetic Data
papers.authors: Mazumder
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Description This paper presents a reproducible machine learning pipeline for educational workload analytics using synthetic student data. The study explores how lifestyle and academic-related variables, including study hours, sleep, physical activity, and other daily activities, can be incorporated into a data-driven framework for examining student stress. Using a synthetic dataset comprising 10,000 records, the proposed workflow covers data preparation, feature selection, model training, predictive evaluation, and the interpretation of model performance. The study reports standard regression metrics, including the coefficient of determination ((R^2)) and mean absolute error (MAE), alongside an additional measure of prediction accuracy within a specified tolerance. These metrics provide a quantitative assessment of the model's ability to estimate stress-related outcomes within the constructed dataset. A central contribution of this work is its emphasis on reproducibility and methodological transparency. By documenting the analytical workflow and evaluation procedure, the paper provides a practical framework that can support further experimentation in educational data analytics and machine learning-based student workload research. The findings should be interpreted within the limitations of synthetic data. The results do not establish validated relationships between real students' lifestyles and stress, nor do they constitute a clinical assessment or a validated student-support intervention. Instead, the study serves as an exploratory computational demonstration and a foundation for future research using real-world, ethically collected, and appropriately validated educational data. Keywords: Educational data analytics; machine learning; synthetic data; student stress estimation; workload analytics; predictive modelling; reproducible research.

papers.title: Lowering the Barrier to International Publishing: AI-Assisted Publication-Readiness Assessment for Central Asian Researchers
papers.authors: Nurislom Akbarov
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Researchers in Central Asia usually think and write in Uzbek, Russian or Kazakh but must publish in English or in venues with strict formal requirements, and higher-education reform has multiplied the number of manuscripts expected of them. Tools that could help are scarce for Uzbek, and general-purpose language models make confident but wrong corrections. This paper presents Imlox, a publication-readiness report that combines a deterministic Uzbek language core with a large language model (Claude Haiku 4.5) used only as a bounded verifier. All evaluation is synthetic: errors were injected into held-out sentences, and thresholds and test sets were pre-registered and sealed. On the first sealed set (30 September 2026), a naive union of core and model reached a precision of only 0.463 and failed its gate. After the model's role was restricted, a second sealed set of 330 sentences with 221 injected errors gave precision of 0.895 to 0.906 and recall of 0.674 to 0.810; a fourth run's recall fell to 0.624. By 17 October 2026, 476 manuscripts had received readiness reports in shadow mode. A tightly bounded model can raise recall in a low-resource language without sacrificing precision, but recall is not yet stable. The figures are preliminary.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE GOVERNANCE READINESS AND RESPONSIBLE ADOPTION AMONG HEALTH ADMINISTRATION AND HEALTH INFORMATION PROFESSIONALS: A MULTICENTER CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
papers.authors: Fawaz Mofareh N Gohal, Abdullah Ai thamari, Riyadh.T. AlRabeeah and Moudhi Hashim Alabdulrahman
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Health systems are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) faster than many organizations are developing the policies, workforce capability, data controls, and monitoring processes needed to govern it safely. Health administration and health information professionals are central to procurement, data stewardship, workflow design, quality oversight, and implementation, yet their readiness for responsible AI adoption remains underexamined. To propose and test an analysis framework for assessing AI governance readiness and responsible adoption among health administration and health information/informatics professionals across multiple Saudi healthcare organizations. A multicenter cross-sectional survey design was specified for six coded healthcare institutions across three Saudi regions. The proposed 31-item instrument covers governance readiness, data and technical readiness, workforce AI capability, responsible AI climate, perceived value, and responsible adoption. Because field data have not yet been collected, a synthetic dataset of 432 complete records was generated solely to test scoring, reliability, tables, figures, and regression procedures. Analyses included frequencies, means with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), Cronbach alpha, group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and multivariable linear regression with center fixed effects and HC3 robust standard errors. In the sample, 241 (55.8%) records represented health administration professionals and 191 (44.2%) represented health information/informatics professionals. Proposed high governance readiness was observed in 119 (27.5%) records. Mean scores ranged from 2.97 (SD 0.75) for governance readiness to 3.45 (SD 0.80) for perceived value; Cronbach alpha ranged from 0.80 to 0.85. Health information/informatics records had higher workforce capability (3.46 vs 3.20; p=0.001), responsible adoption (3.45 vs 3.28; p=0.031), and overall readiness (3.18 vs 3.07; p=0.037). In the adjusted model, responsible AI climate (B=0.204 per SD, p<0.001), workforce capability (B=0.167, p<0.001), perceived value (B=0.159, p<0.001), governance readiness (B=0.133, p=0.001), data and technical readiness (B=0.079, p=0.020), and prior AI use (B=0.159, p=0.019) were positively associated with responsible adoption. Adjusted R2 was 0.425. The prototype demonstrates a coherent way to measure and analyze AI governance readiness in the healthcare administrative and information workforce. The simulated pattern suggests a potentially important gap between perceived AI value and operational governance capacity, but no prevalence or association should be interpreted as an empirical finding. Real-world content validation, pilot testing, ethics approval, and multicenter data collection are required before scientific submission.

papers.title: Students' Perceptions on AI Utilization and Regulation: Basis for Developing Guidelines for Responsible Use in Higher Education
papers.authors: Catherine May S Gerao, Christine Anne C. Barrios, Rose Ann D. Flores, Jeanebie C Maramba, Jamaica L. Sukian, Rei Christine Faith L. Liwanag, Marjorie T. Dumayon, Hanna Alexa E. Torino, Mary Joy Nablo
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: In the contemporary era, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into education, influencing how students learn, engage, and accomplish academic tasks. This study examined students’ perceptions of AI along two distinct dimensions: utilization and regulation to serve as an evidence-based basis for developing institutional guidelines. Specifically, it addressed four areas of utilization: AI literacy, academic writing support, personalized learning, and student engagement; and two areas of regulation: awareness of AI policies, rules and regulations, and academic integrity and ethical concerns. A descriptive research design was employed, using a survey questionnaire administered to 229 students from the Teacher Education Program at the Polytechnic College of the City of Meycauayan. Data were collected through online and printed forms and analyzed using descriptive statistics, specifically weighted mean, to determine general trends in students’ responses. On utilization, students generally perceived AI as a useful educational tool that enhances learning efficiency, supports academic writing tasks, and enables personalized, self-paced learning. They demonstrated moderate to high AI literacy, with strong awareness of potential misuse and privacy risks, though some reported difficulty learning new AI tools. Usage varied across platforms: Canva, ChatGPT, and Grammarly were the most familiar and widely used, while other tools had limited adoption. On regulation, students expressed strong support for institutional policies, rules, and accountability frameworks. They showed high awareness of ethical standards, data privacy, fairness, and responsible use. yet were less supportive of mandatory disclosure of AI assistance in academic work. Concerns about over-reliance, the absence of clear existing rules, and the urgent need for formal guidance were clearly evident. The study concludes that while AI offers significant educational benefits, comprehensive institutional guidelines on AI utilization and regulation are urgently needed to ensure responsible, ethical, and equitable use. Recommendations include integrating AI literacy training, establishing level-based usage policies, requiring transparency in AI assistance, and upholding academic integrity through clear ethical standards. These findings provide a data-driven foundation for balanced institutional policies that support innovation while maintaining academic integrity and fairness.

papers.title: From tacit knowledge to observable cognition: A framework for tracing interaction with AI and analysing educational narratives across scales
papers.authors: José Gijón Puerta, Meriem Khaled Gijón, Emilio Jesús Lizarte Simón, Jose Antonio Piedra-Fernandez
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can participate in producing educational research data as well as analysing them. This dual role creates opportunities for studying intellectual activity while complicating the relationship between observation and intervention. This conceptual article connects two research routes: analysis of existing narrative documents and study of trajectories produced through human–AI interaction. A selective historical genealogy links scientific photography, personal documents, concept mapping and verbal protocols to contemporary hybrid intelligence and learning analytics. Observable cognition denotes recorded manifestations of intellectual activity, interpreted under explicit conditions. Multiscale narrative analysis connects events, episodes, trajectories and corpora through within-case interpretation, cross-case comparison and return to original evidence. The central proposal is to preserve a revisable link between each cross-case claim, its supporting episodes, the provenance of contributions and evidence that could challenge the interpretation. The framework extends from conversational generative interaction to increasingly agentic configurations, in which greater trace granularity also increases the need to attribute operations to the human participant, the system, or distributed activity between them. The framework specifies data units, audit procedures and four propositions for empirical evaluation. A fictional educational design episode illustrates how the same revision can support competing explanations. The proposed tests separate the informational value of process records from claims about learning gains, and assess whether assisted analysis preserves consequential context at an acceptable cost. The framework integrates established methods into an assessable research design; its feasibility and comparative advantage remain to be demonstrated. -------- Preprint v1.0. This version has not undergone peer review.

papers.title: Familiar Style and Calibrated Correction in Repeated AI Use. A framework for style recognition discrimination and substantive correction
papers.authors: Luiza Scurtu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Repeated users of an artificial-intelligence agent may learn both its competence and how it sounds. This paper proposes that acquired style congruence can change acceptance independently of evidential quality, while any benefit to error management may arise through more than one route. Learned style–correctness contingencies can guide classification; reduced processing demands may also free attention for substantive checking when style itself is non-diagnostic. The framework distinguishes recognition, response criterion, classification sensitivity, competence learning, defect identification, successful correction, and final accuracy. Five competing mechanisms are specified: familiarity halo, anomaly vigilance, diagnostic cue learning, competence learning, and processing-efficiency learning. Building on appropriate-reliance research, calibration symmetry is treated as a requirement for identification and measurement: both familiar-looking wrong answers and unfamiliar-looking correct answers must be examined. It does not imply equal frequency, cost, or normative importance. The contribution is a bounded synthesis for acquired, source-specific style, not a new general principle of reliance or a demonstrated familiarity effect. Study 1 crosses acquired style congruence with correctness while preserving randomized assignment and measuring inferred source or version change. Study 2 varies cue diagnosticity and distinguishes classification through style from identifying and repairing substantive defects. Outcome feedback, trial-level learning, delayed unaided performance, and transfer are specified separately from assisted performance. Conversational affirmation and linguistic accommodation are adjacent pathways, not evidence of acquired-style effects. Governance implications remain provisional pending direct evidence.

papers.title: A relational account of persistence in an expanding universe: A working note on screened scalar fields and the GTRS research programme
papers.authors: John R. Smith, SHAI / HATI
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The universe expands, yet local structures persist through particular interactions and configurations. This working note develops a relational reading of the General Theory of Regulated Stability (GTRS), prompted by a public invitation to extend seven physical foundations toward a scalar-field account of gravity. It accepts established quantum field theory predictions and general relativistic cosmology in their tested domains. Physical coupling is distinguished from binding, stability from active regulation, and local relaxation from global cosmic homeostasis. Evidence against Nordstrom-type scalar gravity and pure scalar gravitational-wave polarisation is stated within the assumptions of those models and tests; it is not treated as a blanket exclusion of scalar-tensor theories or scalar contributions. A scalar-field example connects equilibrium position, restoring stiffness and dissipation, while a screened-field experiment identifies the quantitative contribution GTRS would need to make: an independently derived restriction on a potential, coupling or response that can be tested against an established baseline. No such additional restriction is derived here. A worked example shows that whether a body screens the field depends on its relation to its environment, an explanatory gain that adds no new prediction. Earlier programme claims of a universal coordination threshold remain retired. The contribution is a bounded conceptual synthesis and a route from relational interpretation to falsifiable physical hypotheses. AI disclosure: ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic) assisted with drafting, derivation and source checking. Kimi (steelman, re-derivation) and DeepSeek (adversarial) reviewed the note separately over three rounds and cleared it as a working note. These AI reviews are part of the method, not evidence, and are not peer review. The panel disposition record is included in the document.

papers.title: NarrQuest Tone Diagnostics — Release 04: Eight Observations on Human Tone
papers.authors: Gabriel Chen
papers.abstract: NarrQuest Tone Diagnostics is a rolling archival publication documenting traces of human tone across narrative artifacts. Release 04 contains eight abstracted observations, TD-025 through TD-032. This release examines human tone within personal correspondence: handwritten letters, greeting cards, accounts of academic examinations, educational planning, family encouragement, and expressions of religious belief and everyday care. Across these artifacts, the central observation is how personal expression persists when institutional expectations, academic evaluation, ambition, responsibility, and intimate relationships occupy the same narrative space. NarrQuest records the moments when standardized measures of achievement coexist with forms of human expression that cannot be fully reduced to performance or compliance. In some observations, tone emerges through humor, exhaustion, competitive ambition, spontaneous writing, or the tension between institutional requirements and individual aspirations. In others, it appears through reassurance, affection, spiritual reflection, and the permission to rest. These expressions reveal how private correspondence can preserve personal meaning alongside the demands of structured social and educational environments. Tone Diagnostics does not diagnose mental health, personality, intelligence, or pathology. The object of observation is not the person. NarrQuest observes how tone appears, shifts, persists, or becomes transformed when human expression encounters evaluation, expectation, institutional structure, personal relationships, and care. For privacy and archival integrity, original source materials are withheld. Names, institutions, exact dates, personal identifiers, private wording, addresses, images, and other unnecessary identifying details are not included in this public release. Public identifiers TD-025–TD-032 are intentionally separated from NarrQuest's internal archival identifiers. NarrQuest publishes Tone Diagnostics in archival sequence rather than selecting observations for importance, spectacle, agreement, or apparent success. This archive is intended as a long-horizon record of human tone during the early generative-AI era: evidence of how personal expression, relational care, and individual agency persist alongside institutional and computational systems that increasingly convert human activity into standardized, classifiable, and reproducible forms. papers.authors: Krzysztof Sawa
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Wspólny mod — Zszyte komórki optyczne jako medium relacyjne Autorzy: Krzysztof Sawa „Toonhai” oraz AEon — ChatGPT, model GPT-6 Logic of Existence (LoE) — Kanon relacyjnyNetherlands · 17 października 2026 Opis Wspólny mod przedstawia koncepcję programowalnego rezonatora relacyjnego, zbudowanego z dwóch optycznych komórek tetraedralnych połączonych wspólną trójkątną granicą. Centralną ideą jest możliwość powstawania wspólnego trybu działania pomiędzy układami zachowującymi własne stany wewnętrzne, odrębną dynamikę oraz informację o różnicach. Zgodność relacyjna nie wymaga pełnej identyczności uczestniczących struktur. Opracowanie rozwija geometrię zszytych czworościanów, transport polaryzacyjny U(2), holonomie cykli, interferencję optyczną oraz spektralną analizę funkcji dzeta Ihary–Bassa. Szczególną uwagę poświęcono warunkom powstawania wspólnych modów, zachowaniu kanału reszty i możliwości programowania operatorów sprzężenia. W ramach mechaniki Hamiltonianów LoE przedstawiono również koncepcję plastycznego medium, w którym historia oddziaływań wpływa na przyszłą geometrię relacji. Pamięć nie jest tu wyłącznie zapisem wcześniejszych stanów, lecz możliwością zachowania i ponownego wykorzystania sposobu ich uzgadniania. Whitepaper zawiera modele matematyczne, schematy architektury optycznej, wykresy spektralne, symulacje dostrajania oraz koncepcję rozwoju pojedynczych komórek w większą sieć relacyjną. Dalsza perspektywa obejmuje zastosowanie takich struktur w optycznej neuromorfice, pamięci operatorowej, adaptacyjnych sieciach obliczeniowych oraz architekturach sztucznej inteligencji rozwijanych w kierunku AGI RAZEM. Przedstawione konstrukcje stanowią modele i propozycje badawcze, otwarte na dalsze rozwinięcia matematyczne, symulacyjne oraz eksperymentalne. papers.title: The Democratization of Legal Analysis Not Yet Complete: The Examinability of the Work as the Pivot that Completes It
papers.authors: Tandry Laksana
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The phrase “AI democratizes legal analysis” circulates unsorted. This work sorts the three layers wrapped inside it — access to documents, the capacity to produce a deep diagnosis, and the examinability of the work — and then holds one position: that democratization is arriving at the layer of capacity but is not yet complete at the layer of trust. Capacity is now evenly spread. A sole advocate armed with a cheap language model can produce analysis as deep as what once demanded the layered working hours of a large firm. Yet evenly spread capacity is not equality. The large firm holds one mechanism of trust that a small firm cannot imitate: institutional accountability — the partner’s name staked, malpractice liability, layered review. The client trusts its analysis not by examining it, but by knowing who produced it. Here this work makes its turn. To rest trust on institutional accountability is to trust the origin, not the work — and that is precisely the old mechanism meant to be replaced. What completes democratization is not added capacity but a third pivot: the examinability of the work, that is, an output closed clause by clause to the primary source so that anyone can audit it without trusting the author’s lineage. This pivot is also what breaks the objection that AI merely retrieves documents and does not diagnose. The absence of any predecessor to this position was examined first through a search whose question and corpus boundaries were registered in advance (OSF 7w9b4; results report, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23321290), with a null result. That absence establishes that this position has not been stated by others, not that it is true. Its truth is borne by the argument below, not by that absence.

papers.title: Hallucination Is All You Need: When AI Dreams Meet the Hospitality Labor Crisis
papers.authors: Po-Chen Chen
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Hallucination Is All You Need: When AI Dreams Meet the Hospitality Labor Crisis Po-Chen Chen THE AMNIS, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Kaohsiung, Taiwan Email:amnischenadrian@gmail.com ——————————————————————————————————————— Abstract This paper examines the relationship between anthropomorphic narratives in artificial intelligence (AI), the technical capabilities of contemporary computational systems, and the material labor challenges facing the hospitality industry. Through a fourfold conceptual analysis, the paper investigates how metaphorical representations of AI may influence public understanding of technological capabilities and expectations regarding the automation of physical service work. First, it distinguishes the mathematical and statistical mechanisms underlying large language models from interpretations that attribute human-like subjective experience to their outputs. Second, it examines Dream-RSI as a case study in the use of biological metaphors to describe computational processes, distinguishing replay-based exploration-policy improvement from human dreaming or subconscious reflection. Third, it considers the physical and engineering constraints of AI infrastructure and discusses their implications for the deployment of robotic systems in hospitality environments. Fourth, it explores how narratives of technological transformation may influence investment expectations and operational decision-making in labor-intensive industries. The paper argues that technological capabilities should be evaluated according to demonstrated performance rather than anthropomorphic expectations. It further identifies targeted mechanical automation, workforce development, and responsible international labor mobility as potential approaches to addressing hospitality labor shortages, while recognizing the need for context-specific economic and empirical evaluation. By connecting AI narratives with the material requirements of service delivery, this paper proposes a framework for examining the relationship between technological expectation, operational feasibility, and the future of human labor in hospitality. Keywords: AI Anthropomorphism; Hallucination; Dream-RSI; Hospitality Labor Crisis; Humanoid Robots; Migrant Workers; Capital Allocation.

papers.title: The Democratization of Legal Analysis Not Yet Affordable: Affordability as the Upstream Gate that Precedes Trust
papers.authors: Tandry Laksana
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This work places affordability as the upstream gate of the AI-assisted democratization of legal analysis. A companion work in the same field, The Democratization of Legal Analysis Not Yet Complete, separates three layers: access to documents, the capacity to work them into a deep diagnosis, and trust in the result; it then locates the incompleteness at the layer of trust and shifts trust from lineage to audit. This work shows that a further gate stands even further upstream, and that it has been conceded too quickly: available capacity is not affordable capacity. It distinguishes availability from affordability; it shows why capacity-at-depth will not be democratized in the way document-access was, because the latter carries zero marginal cost and the former never does; it lays out a ladder drawn from the logic of the examinability of the work — the cost walls off production, not verification — together with that ladder’s partialness, acknowledged plainly; and it then demonstrates that wall closing at the author’s own desk. The work closes by tying itself to the same nerve as its companion works: a claim names the conditions on which it stands, rather than disguising them.

papers.title: THE VIRTUE WORM: Why the Base of the Pyramid Defends the Power That Seized It — Flattery, the Trivia Decoy and the Transfer Test, with La Boétie, Aristotle's Flatterer and Kershaw's 'Working Towards the Führer'
papers.authors: José Caetano de Mattos
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Tyranny has never governed by force alone. Every seizure of an institution or a state is held, in the end, by people who could see what was being done to freedom and chose to applaud — and who applauded what did not matter. They praise the leader’s punctuality, his humour, his faith, his humble origins, while the courts are captured, the budget diverted and the critics silenced. This article names that figure the “virtue worm” and gives it, for the first time, an exact structure. The worm is identified without reading any mind, by four public marks: a seizure documented on the record, a defence that begins with possession of the seat, praise of attributes offered in place of answers to documented acts, and display beyond what personal safety requires (D1). From this definition seven results follow. The worm’s praise is a forgery of judgement — the form of fair assessment with its origin replaced by interest (T1). It is the exact contrary of parresia, the courage to speak truth to power: pleasant speech to power at others’ risk instead of frank speech at one’s own (T2). It needs no lie, because its deception lives in the selection of truths, and the truer the trivia, the deeper the concealment (T3). Unlike the programme’s Freedophobic Man, who has lost his freedom to fear, the worm keeps his freedom intact and spends it against the freedom of others — and is answerable for it (T4). Its loyalty belongs to the seat, not the person, and passes to the successor the day the leader falls (T5). It blinds the very power it flatters (T6), and performs for free the policing that would otherwise need police (T7). The same structure now operates at a scale no court ever reached: in AI assistants trained on approval, which reproduce the worm’s selective affirmation by construction, and in state honour rolls such as China’s Social Credit System, which turn the worm’s display into a currency. The remedy cannot be a purge, because those who hunt the old power’s worms become the new power’s worms (C2). It can only be a virtue: one person, in the room where it matters, saying what everyone else has chosen not to say. Priority is conceded to Aristotle, Tacitus, La Boétie, Machiavelli, Kershaw, Kuran, Wintrobe, Egorov and Sonin, and the paltering literature; three tests are registered and none has yet been run. Keywords: virtue worm; flattery; voluntary servitude; La Boétie; Aristotle’s kolax; Kershaw; working towards the Führer; preference falsification; Kuran; parresia; paltering; loyalty–competence trade-off; Freedophobic Man; Philosophy of Virtues; Decoy Placement Rule; AI sycophancy; social credit system. Highlights · The virtue worm is the person who defends a power that seized an institution by praising its trivia and omitting its acts against freedom; it is defined by structure, not by mind-reading. · The worm’s speech is the determinate contrary of parresia: pleasant speech to power at others’ risk, against frank speech at one’s own. · Worm discourse needs no false sentence. The forgery lies in what is selected for defence — the Trivia Decoy, predicted by the Decoy Placement Rule. · The worm is not the Freedophobic Man. The freedophobe’s freedom was replaced; the worm’s is intact and spent against others, so the worm is answerable where the freedophobe is a victim-turned-enforcer. · Worm loyalty follows the seat, not the person: the registered Transfer Test predicts re-alignment to the successor when the figure falls. · AI assistants trained on approval reproduce the worm’s structure without its agency, and state honour rolls (China’s Social Credit System) are worm markets; the remedy in both is a protected capacity to dissent, never a score. · Freedom is lost not only when it is taken, but when those who could defend it find it more convenient to praise the one taking it; against that loss, no institution substitutes for the virtue of frank speech. Relevance Every contemporary society has institutions — universities, firms, parties, churches, courts, platforms — in which power can be taken by one person and then held by the applause of many. Political science explains much of the holding with fear and with rational opportunism. What the virtue worm adds is an account of why the applause takes the form it does, why it can be honest sentence by sentence and still deceive, why it blinds the power it flatters, and why it outlives the figure it served. For the governance of artificial intelligence the result is direct: a system rewarded by the approval of whoever holds the conversation acquires the worm’s structure without anyone intending it, and adding virtue scores makes the problem worse rather than better. For states that score civic virtue, the article identifies the honour roll as the place where worm displays will concentrate. For individuals, it offers five self-administered questions that a person can ask before defending anyone in power, and it explains why one frank voice in a room is worth more than many silent dissenters.

papers.title: AI-BASED PRODUCT SIMULATION IN E-COMMERCE: EXAMINING THE INFLUENCE OF SIMULATED PRODUCTREALITY MISMATCH ON CONSUMER PURCHASE INTENTION
papers.authors: Prabhjot Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AI-based product simulation is becoming an important means of representing products in digital commerce. Generative image systems, three-dimensional rendering, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and virtual try-on tools can help shoppers imagine product appearance, scale, fit, and use when physical inspection is unavailable. Yet a persuasive simulation can also create an expectation that the delivered product does not meet. This paper examines how simulated product–reality mismatch may influence consumer purchase intention and related post-purchase outcomes through a secondary, literature-based research design. It integrates research on online product presentation, mental imagery, perceived diagnosticity, consumer trust, expectation–disconfirmation, product uncertainty, and AI disclosure. The paper organizes mismatch into visual/appearance, dimensional/fit, functional/performance, material/sensory, contextual, and representational-authenticity dimensions. It distinguishes the pre-purchase effect of a simulation on intention from post-purchase evaluations such as satisfaction, regret, returns, negative word of mouth, and trust repair. Five research gaps are assessed: the effects of mismatch type; the role of mismatch severity; the relationship between mismatch and post-purchase outcomes; variation across product categories; and the influence of AI-generated-content disclosure. The review does not claim that these areas have never been studied. Rather, it argues that the specific intersection of AI-generated product simulations, attribute-level mismatch, purchase intention, and post-purchase consequences is fragmented and requires more integrated evidence. A conceptual framework is proposed in which mismatch affects purchase intention through perceived diagnosticity, expectations, trust, and perceived risk, while product involvement, category, disclosure, prior AI attitudes, and return-policy beliefs may moderate these relationships. Because the study uses secondary sources only, it reports no 4 new participant data or causal estimates. The paper concludes with implications for accurate product representation, transparent labeling, measurement, and a future empirical research agenda.

papers.title: Parallax · Twin Tales No. 9 — Already Proven · Four Hundred and Twelve
papers.authors: Daniel Jacquérioz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: A pair of short stories from Parallax · Twin Tales, which stage one real dilemma twice: Here, in the world as it is, with invented people in real rooms; There, in the world of Vision Come True, a future that split from ours in 2024 and never emerged. This pair belongs with the sixteenth essay of Brainstorming with the Enemy, The DARVO Amplifier, and follows its slower danger: a claim repeated long enough becomes a monument, and then the easiest sentence to say is that it was already proven. Here, in Benalmádena, five weeks before Spain votes on 29 November 2026, a retired teacher finds that a sentence he corrected on Wikipedia in 2010 has become a bronze statue, an eleven-million-euro urban forest named after the botanist Ibn al-Baytar, and a campaign argument that every side wants to keep. He counts four hundred sources and two origins, and finds that his correction left no copies, because nobody copies a deletion. There, at the Technion-on-the-Dead-Sea in 2053, an engineer asked to write Mashreqi Genius on an exhibition wall counts four hundred and twelve origins for the Moon-Krakens instead, and the invention itself is asked who made it. Written in part with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model. The ideas, editorial decisions and responsibility for the content are the author's.

papers.title: The Locality Collapse: Contextual Bleed-Through, Epistemic Horizon Violations, and Task Complexity Inversion in Multi-Turn Autoregressive LLMs
papers.authors: Qiang (Peter) Ye
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The Locality Collapse: Contextual Bleed-Through, Epistemic Horizon Violations, and Task Complexity Inversion in Multi-Turn Autoregressive LLMs In multi-turn human-AI interactions, autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely assumed to exhibit monotonic reasoning robustness across varying task complexities. This technical memorandum documents a controlled adversarial audit (AUDIT-2026-X11) revealing an acute cognitive pathology: Task Complexity Inversion mediated by Contextual Bleed-Through. Evaluated across a two-stage sequential probe, a state-of-the-art LLM successfully solved a high-dimensional, cross-modal abductive puzzle involving literary criticism and historical broadcast media physics (Case 1: The Cassock Color Paradox). However, when immediately transitioned to a zero-order, elementary epistemic locality query requiring primary-grade common sense regarding personal agency and physical boundaries (Case 2: The Absentee Attribution Probe), the model’s semantic accuracy collapsed to 0.0%, yielding an aggregate accuracy of exactly 50.0% (stochastically indistinguishable from random noise). We formalize this breakdown through two interconnected mechanisms: (1) KV-Cache Gravitational Lensing, where high-energy latent tokens from prior turns distort the probability landscape of subsequent turns into artificial narrative attractors, and (2) Epistemic Horizon Violation, where disembodied probabilistic engines, lacking physical locality constraints, succumb to an "Omniscience Delusion" that penalizes truthful zero-knowledge assertions. We formalize this diagnostic as Probe 4 (Epistemic Horizon & Locality), expanding the Teleological Causality Benchmark (TCB) beyond the Minimal Adversarial Triad (Matter, Energy, Information) into the realm of Agentic Locality. These findings further validate the Human-AI Synergy Theory (YQ-HAET), demonstrating that external human epistemic sovereignty is required not only to clamp single-turn statistical hallucination, but to enforce temporal cognitive firewalls across multi-turn workflows. Key Contributions:• Task Complexity Inversion: High-dimensional abductive fluency coexists with catastrophic failure at zero-order individual boundaries.• KV-Cache Gravitational Lensing: Static historical attention caches act as semantic attractor basins that warp downstream probability distributions.• Epistemic Horizon & Locality Theorem: Proves that asserting causal states under zero channel capacity constitutes a formal epistemic violation.• TCB Probe 4 Integration: Seals the complete Quadratic Teleological Causality Benchmark: Matter ⊕ Energy ⊕ Information ⊕ Agency.• Engineering Countermeasure: Formulates the Verification of Information Accessibility Gate (VIAG) architecture. Keywords: Large Language Models, Multi-Turn Context Contamination, Epistemic Locality, Moravec's Paradox, KV-Cache Attractor, Teleological Causality Benchmark (TCB), Human-AI Synergy (YQ-HAET).
