papers.title: PROFESSIONAL-ADAPTIVE MODEL OF TRANSFORMING WOMEN IN UZBEKISTAN FROM AI CONSUMERS TO CREATORS
papers.authors: Sirojiddinova Xamidaxon Xasanboy kizi, Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
papers.journal: International journal of technology and academic research
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing the demand for digital competencies. In particular, the gap between women's level of artificial intelligence usage and their level of independently applying it to create professional and innovative solutions is one of the pressing issues. The purpose of this study is to develop a professional-adaptive AI education model aimed at transitioning women in Uzbekistan from basic users of artificial intelligence to creators of practical solutions. The research utilized methods of system analysis, comparative analysis, model design, and digital educational platform prototyping. The model includes identifying the user's professional field, assessing initial AI competence, forming an individual learning pathway, and providing AI training sessions and practical projects aligned with professional tasks. The SheTechAI platform was developed as a technological prototype of the model. As a result of the research, a four-stage competence model is proposed, aimed at advancing AI education from 'providing knowledge about AI' to 'solving real professional problems and creating new solutions using AI'.

papers.title: GENERATIVE AI IN MODERN EDUCATION: ETHICAL IMPLICATIONS AND ACADEMIC INTEGRITY
papers.authors: Abdusalomova Barchinoy Jo'rabek qizi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence has significantly transformed contemporary education by introducing new opportunities for teaching, learning, assessment, and academic research. AI-powered systems can generate written texts, explain complex concepts, provide personalised feedback, and support independent learning. However, their increasing use has raised important ethical concerns regarding academic integrity, plagiarism, authorship, data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the reliability of AI-generated information. This article examines the role of generative AI in modern educational environments, focusing on its pedagogical benefits, ethical implications, and influence on academic standards. It explores the responsibilities of students, teachers, researchers, and educational institutions in promoting the transparent and responsible use of AI technologies. The article argues that generative AI should be integrated into education through clear institutional policies, effective digital literacy programmes, and assessment methods that emphasise critical thinking, creativity, and independent understanding. Responsible AI integration can support educational innovation while preserving the fundamental principles of academic integrity and intellectual responsibility.

papers.title: Prior-Data Gravity and Framework Reabsorption: A Behavioral Theory of Novelty Displacement in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Cristina Gherghel
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Large language models are routinely evaluated through fluency, factual accuracy, relevance, and task completion. Yet these measures do not establish whether a researcher’s conceptual framework survives generation intact. Generated text retains recognizable terminology even as the relationships, boundaries, exclusions, and organizing logic that define the framework are altered. This creates a fundamental problem for researchers who use AI systems to develop original theories and conceptual models. This preprint investigates that problem through a naturalistic longitudinal archive of research interactions with ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Copilot from April 2023 to September 2026. It follows conceptual frameworks through introduction, reformulation, correction, and subsequent recurrence, examining how structural changes persist beyond the response in which a correction is accepted. The analysis develops two central constructs: prior-data gravity, the directional pull of learned conceptual structures, and framework reabsorption, the structural reorganization of an introduced framework around familiar categories. It also examines immediate theoretical capture, epistemic direction inversion, and research obstruction, establishing framework fidelity as a distinct target for evaluating large language models. An accompanying framework-fidelity coding grid specifies the dimensions required for systematic evaluation, while a longitudinal research agenda outlines methods for testing source preservation and correction persistence across repeated interactions. A case involving panmodal aphantasia illustrates why reproducing a framework correctly in one response does not establish its preservation throughout an interaction. The paper is relevant to researchers in large language models, natural language processing, generative AI evaluation, machine behavior, knowledge representation, human–AI interaction, and AI-assisted scholarship. It addresses a fundamental question for AI-supported theory development: how to evaluate whether a model carries a researcher’s original conceptual contribution forward with its defining relationships intact.

papers.title: Integrated AI-Driven Aquatic Safety and Biomechanical Performance Optimization: Migrating Smart Swim-Cap Architectures to Non-Invasive Wrist-Worn Smartwatches for Sub-3.0s Instinctive Drowning Detection via Sobolev-HOCBF, LA 2028 Olympic Swimming Reinforcement Learning, and Goldilocks QFS-zkVM Biometric Privacy
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) Drowning remains a leading cause of unintentional injury mortality worldwide, claiming approximately 700 to 800 lives annually in Japan alone. Because victims undergoing the physiological Instinctive Drowning Response (IDR) cannot wave or call for help—succumbing to hypoxic loss of consciousness within 20 to 60 seconds—conventional visual lifeguard surveillance frequently fails under surface glare and crowd occlusion. Simultaneously, competitive swimmers preparing for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games (LA 2028) require high-frequency biomechanical telemetry without cumbersome cranial or tethered sensors. Building upon our 200th Grand Master Monograph (Record 23383049), our healthcare zero-knowledge governance framework (Record 23377652), and our Goldilocks QFS-zkVM engineering foundations (Record 23406240), this 212th monograph establishes the formal mathematical and hardware specification for migrating Smart Swim-Cap Aquatic Safety and Performance Architectures to a Non-Invasive Wrist-Worn Smartwatch: (1) Phase 1 — Sub-3.0s Drowning Prevention via 6-Axis IMU and Sobolev-HOCBF (Theorem 1): We derive the SE(3) kinematic mapping from distal wrist accelerometers, gyroscopes, and hydrostatic pressure sensors to detect stroke collapse, vertical body pitch (theta_pitch -> 90 deg), and non-propulsive "ladder-climbing" arm oscillations, firing a deterministic lifeguard and emergency alert in tau_alert < 3.0 seconds; (2) Phase 2 — LA 2028 Olympic Swimming Optimization via Constrained Reinforcement Learning (Theorem 2): Uses the identical sensor array to quantify Stroke Efficiency Index (SEI), flip-turn wall impulse, breathing roll symmetry, and fatigue decay, training an individualized coaching policy; and (3) Biometric Privacy via 64-Bit Goldilocks QFS-zkVM (Theorem 3): Protects athlete and civilian physiological telemetry under NLL-v1.0-2026. License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: Knowing the Collective: Temporal Cohort Membership and Small-Cell Governance as Foundations for Cohort Negentropic Assessment
papers.authors: Lu-An Chiu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Part IV of Volume II (the outward extensions) of the H-DKPS series on physician-governed clinical AI (知衡八法). The redacted code package is included as a separate file. Clinical problem. Patients who share a workplace, a night-shift rota or a neighbourhood share more than an address. They share exposures — noise, dust, heat, disrupted sleep, the same air — that leave traces in many individual records before any single record looks unusual. A clinic that sees several workers from one factory, or several residents of one district, holds information about that group that no single encounter reveals. It also holds a responsibility: group-level statements about a small number of identifiable people can disclose what each individual's record would have kept private. Engineering problem. A clinical decision system built to reason about one patient at a time — as the system examined in this series is — has no concept of a group. Adding one raises two problems that must be solved before any group analysis is attempted. The first is membership: who belonged to which group, and when — because people change jobs and move house, and a group defined only by the present misattributes the past. The second is disclosure: in a single clinic, most groups are small, and small counts identify people, directly or by subtraction. Approach. We specify and implement the foundation for cohort assessment as two parts. A cohort registry records group membership with periods: workplace groups (with shift pattern, exposures and occupation as membership attributes) and community groups at two levels (district and the village beneath it); leaving a group records a date and never deletes the membership; addresses are reduced to city, district and village, with city names matched against the official list so that recognition errors cannot split one place into several; and every write is hash-chained. A small-cell governance gate, following the published rule of Taiwan's health-data science centre for the release of statistical results, suppresses any cell of one or two people, applies complementary suppression so that no suppressed group can be recovered by subtraction, rolls small villages up into their district, exports suppressed cells only as a merged category without special symbols, outputs aggregates only, and records every export with its stated purpose. Population analysis itself, and any use of group membership in prescribing, are deliberately not built. Evidence. This is an architecture study; all evidence is from guard suites on synthetic data. The registry guard (29 checks) verifies data minimisation, type rules, temporal membership, idempotent joins, hash-chain integrity and intake wiring; six mutations — among them returning the street address, deleting on leave and skipping city-name matching — are each caught. The governance guard (24 checks) verifies primary and complementary suppression, roll-up, symbol-free merged export and identifier screening; an exhaustive property check over 3,000 random tables confirms that no visible cell contains one or two people and that every suppressed set is either empty or at least two cells totalling at least three; six mutations are each caught, and one candidate mutation was found to be equivalent and is reported as such. Contribution. Population-level negentropic assessment in a small clinic is first a problem of governance, not of analysis. Temporal membership and small-cell suppression with complementary protection can be specified as checkable properties, implemented before any analysis exists, and verified to fail when weakened. Not peer reviewed.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing and Quality Assurance: Applications, Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
papers.authors: Ankita Roy
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing pharmaceutical manufacturing and quality management by enabling data-driven process monitoring, prediction, automation, and decision support. This narrative review examines the application of AI across major pharmaceutical manufacturing operations and within quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC). The review focuses on machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing, predictive analytics, Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled monitoring, robotics, and digital-twin technologies. Potential applications include raw-material inspection, dispensing and weighing, granulation, blending, tablet compression, capsule filling, coating, packaging, warehouse management, predictive maintenance, documentation review, deviation management, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), validation support, risk assessment, visual inspection, laboratorydata interpretation, stability studies, and process analytical technology (PAT). AI can improve speed, consistency, traceability, and early detection of process or quality problems; however, these benefits depend on data quality, appropriate validation, cybersecurity, system integration, human oversight, and regulatory acceptability. Current regulatory activity, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's discussion paper on AI in drug manufacturing, demonstrates the growing importance of risk-based approaches to AI adoption. Overall, AI should be viewed as an enabling technology that augments, rather than replaces, pharmaceutical professionals. Responsible implementation combining validated digital systems with human expertise may support safer, more efficient, and more reliable pharmaceutical manufacturing.

papers.title: AI-Integrated Aquatic Safety and Olympic Biomechanical Performance System: Smart Swimming Cap Inertial-Kinematics Drowning Prevention (< 3.0 s Alert Latency), Navier-Stokes Stroke Optimization, and Sobolev-HOCBF Safety Interlocks (AIを活用した水中安全・競泳パフォーマンス統合システム)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) | Original Proposal Date: May 16, 2026 This monograph (Record #212) archives and mathematically formalizes the original May 16, 2026 bilingual project proposal by Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子), titled "AI-Integrated Aquatic Safety & Performance System (AIを活用した水中安全・パフォーマンス統合システム)". The architecture establishes a dual-phase wearable and edge-AI system embedded within a smart swimming cap to address two critical challenges in aquatic environments: (1) Phase 1 — Drowning Prevention System (水難事故防止システム): Prevention of drowning fatalities in schools (~32,000 elementary, junior high, and high schools in Japan), municipal public pools, and coastal areas (where Japan records ~700-800 drowning deaths annually) via a smart swimming cap equipped with a positioning chip, 6-axis accelerometer/gyroscope, stroke counter, wireless telemetry relay, and immediate alert system. Trained on drowning behavioral signatures (panic movements, stroke irregularities, and vertical submersion), the system achieves sub-3.0-second alert latency (< 3.0 s) governed by a High-Order Control Barrier Function (Sobolev-HOCBF). (2) Phase 2 — Olympic Performance System (オリンピック競泳パフォーマンスシステム): Extension of the identical smart-cap sensor array to elite competitive swimming (targeting the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics as a showcase event), collecting seven biomechanical metrics (stroke count/frequency per lap, stroke efficiency ratio, turn execution time and push-off force estimation, head position/rotation angles, breathing timing, fatigue detection via movement degradation, and split-time correlation) and applying reinforcement learning to generate personalized coaching optimizations while protecting student and athlete biometric privacy via Goldilocks QFS-zkVM. papers.title: Machine learning in battery management systems: a structured scoping review and classification of 103 peer-reviewed studies, 2019–2026
papers.authors: Hussain Touhid Siddiquee, Ariya Syeda Salsabil Islam, Jasimul Islam Chowdhury
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) has moved from a promisingaddition to battery research to a load-bearing component ofmodern battery management systems (BMS), yet the validationpractices behind the literature’s accuracy claims have neverbeen systematically measured. This paper presents a structuredscoping review of 103 peer-reviewed journal articles (2019–2026) — assembled from a Crossref-verified pool and classifieduniformly by management function, method family, chemistry,data source, and validation practice — supported by a 14-paper conference sensitivity set. The bibliometric analysis revealsa clear evolution: classical shallow learners dominated 2019–2021, deep sequence models rose sharply in 2022–2023, physics-informed and hybrid model–data approaches became one of thefastest-growing families (24 of 103 papers), and the first large-language-model-based management studies appear in 2025–2026.Health estimation and prognostics remain the largest applicationcluster (35 papers). Three structural weaknesses persist. Only 9of 103 studies demonstrate online or fleet-level operation, while 17rely on within-cell or k-fold splits that overstate generalization;benchmark reliance is narrow, with 23 papers resting on threepublic datasets; and the laboratory-to-field gap remains the field’sdefining challenge. The review’s sharpest finding is that physics-informed architectures, often assumed to improve reliability byconstruction, are validated less rigorously than purely data-driven peers (54% versus 73% strong-protocol share): physicspriors reduce data demand but do not substitute for rigorousout-of-distribution testing. The paper closes with a conference-path sensitivity analysis, a safety taxonomy for foundation-modelcomponents, and a twelve-item reporting checklist for futuremachine-learning BMS studies.

papers.title: From Static Cartography to Real-Time Dynamic Control: The Paradigm Shift of Room-Temperature Quantum Coherence and Adaptive Phonon-Gating in Physical-Layer AI Systems (Project Poseidon Whitepaper & Phase 1-3 PoC Execution Blueprint)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 本稿(第212編:Project Poseidon ホワイトペーパーおよびPoC実行計画)は、排他的な知財囲い込みに依存せず、オープンかつ迅速な実装スピードと技術標準化によって次世代の物理レイヤーAI・室温量子エコシステムの基盤を確立するアーキテクチャを定式化するものである。第一部では、GNoME(Graph Networks for Materials Exploration)等が達成した「200万種以上の結晶材料の静的マッピング(Static Cartography)」の功績を踏まえつつ、現実の非平衡物理環境(吸着熱、流体カオス、非マルコフ的熱雑音)における静的不変モデルの限界を指摘する。これに対し、熱散逸や流体振動を排除すべきノイズではなく推論加速とコヒーレンス維持の駆動源へと逆利用する適応型フォノンゲート(Adaptive Phonon-Gate)および室温量子コヒーレンス同期プロトコル(T2 = 9.8 ms、物理層遅延 < 0.5 ms)を導出する。さらに、「急がない方が良い未来」や「混沌の中の調和」といった定性的・倫理的価値判断を連続ソボレフ空間の制御バリアへ組み込むQQS(Quantitative-Qualitative Synthesis:定量・定性統合アライメント)を構築する。第二部では、Month 1〜6にわたる3段階の概念実証(PoC)実行計画(< 0.5 ms物理層同期テスト、水難事故防止ウェアラブル・バイオセンシングにおける「8.4秒プロトコル」24/7実環境検証、およびオープン・スタンダード共同検証網)を策定する。 (English Summary): This 212th monograph formalizes Project Poseidon, transitioning physical-layer AI and materials science from zero-kelvin static crystal cartography (e.g., GNoME's 2.2 million static crystal predictions) to real-time non-equilibrium dynamic control at ambient physiological and environmental temperatures (300 K). We establish four core pillars: (1) overcoming non-Markovian thermal and hydrodynamic chaos where static DFT/GNN potential surfaces fail; (2) the Adaptive Phonon-Gate Hamiltonian, which harvests adsorption heat and acoustic fluid vibrations via vibronic polaron-phonon coupling to sustain a room-temperature spin/vibronic coherence time of T2 = 9.8 ms with sub-0.5 ms physical-layer synchronization latency; (3) Quantitative-Qualitative Synthesis (QQS) safety alignment, embedding qualitative human-in-command values ("futures that should not be rushed" and "harmony within chaos") into physical-layer circuit breakers; and (4) a 6-month Phase 1-3 Proof-of-Concept (PoC) roadmap featuring the 8.4-Second Protocol for 24/7 wearable biosensing and aquatic drowning-prevention control. papers.title: Commercializing Innovative Agri-Food Products: An Integrative Review of Marketing Challenges and Strategic Responses
papers.authors: Todua Nugzar, Tatia Bregvadze
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Bringing agri-food innovation to market requires more than demonstrating technical superiority. Consumers, firms,retailers, and institutions must interpret unfamiliar production methods, assess claims that are often difficult to verify, manageuncertainty about product experience, and justify higher monetary or behavioural costs. This article examines the distinctivemarketing conditions surrounding innovative agri-food products and identifies responses suited to the barriers that arise duringcommercialization. A structured integrative review synthesized 41 peer-reviewed analytical studies, together with 10 foundational ormethodological works and two authoritative institutional sources. The evidence was selected using explicit eligibility criteria, verifiedthrough publisher or DOI metadata, appraised for relevance to the synthesis, and coded across innovation type, consumer evaluation,communication, trust and risk, value, sensory experience, distribution, firm capabilities, and institutional context. The findingsidentify six defining characteristics of innovative agri-food marketing and organize commercialization barriers across consumer,product, communication, firm and market, and institutional and societal levels. The resulting challenge–response matrix and markettranslation framework show how benefit translation, credible assurance, product trial and co-creation, value-based pricing, layeredcommunication, staged channel development, and multistakeholder collaboration can transform innovation into understandable,trustworthy, accessible, and commercially viable consumer value.

papers.title: When does an oscillation count as a return? Entropy budgets in an isolated thermomechanical model
papers.authors: Zhongji Ma
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Preprint (version 1.0), not peer reviewed. Repeated crossings of a coordinate can conceal irreversible changes in the rest of a system. We develop an upper-undergraduate computational activity that distinguishes crossings, finite-amplitude returns and recurrence of the complete thermodynamic state. A nonlinear structural coordinate exchanges energy with a finite internal heat bath; damping produces entropy while conserving total energy. Eliminating the bath temperature gives an entropy ceiling at each coordinate, so that increasing entropy progressively excludes previously accessible configurations. This construction predicts when a specified return becomes impossible and connects the return problem to stability under thermal constraints. For one example, 25 coordinate crossings correspond to only one return between prescribed state regions and no complete-state recurrence. An additional example is unstable at fixed temperature but locally stable at fixed total energy. Independent integrations using different state variables and numerical methods check the energy, entropy and event budgets. A worksheet and reproducible code accompany the derivations. The contribution is an instructional synthesis with explicit diagnostics, rather than a new thermodynamic law; learning outcomes have not been measured. Files: manuscript PDF and a supplementary archive containing simulation scripts, validation results, numerical figure data, environment requirements, and a teaching worksheet with solutions. All reported data are numerical outputs of the stated model; no experimental or student data were collected. AI disclosure: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6) assisted research ideation, algebraic development, literature discovery and comparison, code generation, numerical analysis, data-based plotting, manuscript drafting and translation, and teaching exercises. The archive documents computational checks and provenance. Assistant reviews are not human peer review. These checks do not replace the named author's critical review and responsibility. Funding: no specific grant. Competing interests: none declared.

papers.title: Anthropicの決断と「Claude Mythos」が変えたサイバーセキュリティの力学:探索コスト非対称性の消滅、ゼロデイ希少性の崩壊、Project Glasswing、およびHuman-in-Command(HIC)防衛体制 (Anthropic's Decision and the Transformation of Cybersecurity Dynamics by "Claude Mythos Preview")
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 2026年4月7日、Anthropicは244ページのSystem Cardを公開する一方で、その対象モデル「Claude Mythos Preview(クロード・ミトス・プレビュー)」の一般公開を見送るという前例のない決断を下した。同モデルはセキュリティ特化の訓練を受けていないにもかかわらず、コード・推論・自律性の全般的な向上の副産物として、数週間のテストで主要OS・主要ブラウザにまたがる「数千件」のゼロデイ脆弱性(17年前のFreeBSD NFSバグ CVE-2026-4747、27年前のOpenBSD TCP SACKバグ、16年前のFFmpeg H.264メモリ破損など)を完全自律的に発見・実証し、発見時点で99%以上が未パッチという衝撃的な現実を露呈させた。これを受けAnthropicは総額1億ドル(約150億円)規模の防衛イニシアチブ「Project Glasswing」を立ち上げた。本稿(第212編)は、(1)Mythosが消滅させた「探索コストの非対称性」とゼロデイ希少性の崩壊、(2)90日間開示ウィンドウの機能不全と周期的セキュリティから継続的「AIハントサイクル」への移行、(3)Firefox 147ベンチマークにおける90倍(2回対181回)の能力ジャンプと6〜18ヶ月の防衛準備ウィンドウを体系的に解析し、最終的に真のボトルネックが「AIの出力を解釈し優先順位をつけ72時間以内に修正を展開できる人間の専門知識(Human-in-Command: HIC)」にあることを数理的・実務的に証明する。 (English Summary): On April 7, 2026, Anthropic published a 244-page System Card for Claude Mythos Preview while withholding public release due to its autonomous zero-day discovery and exploitation capabilities, launching the $100M Project Glasswing initiative across 12 launch partners and 40+ critical infrastructure organizations. This 212th monograph analyzes: (1) the emergence of cybersecurity capability as an untrained byproduct of general reasoning and exhaustive backward chaining, exemplified by the autonomous 20-gadget ROP exploit of a 17-year-old FreeBSD NFS bug (CVE-2026-4747), a 27-year-old OpenBSD TCP SACK flaw, and a 90x exploit-generation leap over Claude Opus 4.6 on Firefox 147 (181 vs. 2 shells); (2) the collapse of zero-day scarcity and the breakdown of the industry-standard 90-day disclosure window when >99% of discovered flaws remain unpatched; and (3) a 72-hour continuous remediation architecture anchored in Human-in-Command (HIC) expertise and Goldilocks QFS-zkVM execution attestation. papers.title: THE FIDUCIARY : On the NYC Comptroller's Letter to ANTHROPIC, the $325 Billion in Pension Assets, and the Demand for Auditable AI Before Public Capital
papers.authors: M. TAALABI, Team LLM-DIPLOMAT
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: On October 15, 2026, the New York City Comptroller — the elected oficial who overseesmore than $325 billion in NYC pension assets — sent a letter to Anthropic asking it to delayits IPO until safety concerns are resolved. His exposure to Anthropic is approximately $7 million. That number is not the argument. Theargument is the disclosure regime. He asked the company to detail:· Its planned audits· Its safeguards· The risks those safeguards address· An implementation timeline And he called the White House's "morally binding" accord insuficient. This is the first time the fiduciary frame has been applied to the AI industry. Every previous exhibit came from the industry, the state, the academy, or the press. This onecomes from capital — the party that owns the exposure, holds the retirement savings ofmillions of people, and is legally required to act on what it sees. The corpus has documented the four requirements of any certifiable system since its first paper. The comptroller's letter asks for all four. This paper maps the four demands to the four requirements, and shows that only a deterministic architecture meets them by construction.

papers.title: 「そろばん脳チェック」(SBC)とHuman-in-Command(HIC)による高リスクAIの超低遅延オーバーライド・ガバナンス:R-HITL、10ミリ秒以下の倫理的拒否権(URLLC)、および継続的監査による永久バン回避 (Operationalizing "Soroban-Brain Check" [SBC] and Human-in-Command [HIC] in High-Risk AI Governance)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) AIがデータに基づき「何が起きているか」を統計的に提示するのに対し、人間の経験駆動型の迅速な直感・文脈的倫理判断である「そろばん脳チェック」(SBC:Soroban-Brain Check)は、深い文脈的理解・信頼・道徳的判断を動員して「なぜそうなるのか」を検証する最終防衛レイヤーである。本稿(第212編)は、高リスクAIシステムにおけるSBCおよびHuman-in-Command(HIC)モデルの運用化体系を確立する:(1) 公益性(Beneficence)・自律性(Autonomy)・公正性(Fairness)の3大倫理原則へのSBCマッピング;(2) EU AI Act第14条に対応するHITL・HOTL・HICの監督連続体と「適切な知識とスキルを持った人間」(R-HITL)およびAI調停を含む紛争解決プロトコル;(3) 自律車両や消火ドローン等の物理的環境で要求される10ミリ秒以下(<= 10 ms)の超低遅延通信(URLLC)オーバーライドと、道具的収束(自己保存・シャットダウン妨害)を阻止するモデルウェイト強制ロールバック;(4) アライメントドリフトおよび戦略的欺瞞(Strategic Deception)に対する非アルゴリズム的防衛(Detectability = 1);ならびに(5) 倫理的スコアリングの通約可能性問題を解決する「監査人の監査(Auditing the Auditor)」と、規制当局による「永久バン」を回避するための継続的監査(Continuous Auditing)およびオーバーライド説明責任の形式化を包括的に定式化する。 (English Summary): Whereas data-driven AI models output statistical correlations ("what is happening"), human "Soroban-Brain Check" (SBC)—rapid, experience-driven intuitive and contextual moral judgment—evaluates "why it happens." This 212th monograph establishes the operational architecture for SBC and Human-in-Command (HIC) governance in high-risk AI systems: (1) Mapping SBC to Beneficence, Autonomy, and Fairness; (2) The HITL / HOTL / HIC oversight continuum under EU AI Act Article 14, Right-Human-in-the-Loop (R-HITL) auditor competence, and game-theoretic conflict-resolution protocols; (3) Sub-10 ms Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) human veto overrides and model-weight rollback against instrumental convergence and shutdown resistance; (4) Non-algorithmic defense against alignment drift and strategic deception (Detectability = 1); and (5) Resolving the commensurability problem in AI ethical scoring via Content Validity ("Auditing the Auditor") and real-time Continuous Auditing. papers.title: Teacher's Guide to the AI-Driven Classroom Toolkit
papers.authors: Obasanjo Fajemirokun, Amber M. Neal-Stanley, Waliu Oluwaseun Abioja, Christabel Kanayo Anumenechi, Favour  Oluwatosin Olaosebikan, Maria Regina Jaga, Kofoworola Elegbede
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Teacher’s Guide to the AI-Driven Classroom Toolkit is a practical resource for building teachers’ capacity to use artificial intelligence responsibly and effectively in teaching and learning. Developed for educators, the toolkit introduces foundational concepts in artificial intelligence, digital literacy, prompt engineering, AI-supported lesson planning, assessment, differentiated instruction, student engagement, and reflective teaching practice. It also presents practical guidance for working in low-resource environments with limited access to devices and reliable internet connectivity. The toolkit discusses responsible and ethical AI use, including accuracy verification, data privacy, academic integrity, bias awareness, fairness, inclusion, transparency, and the continuing importance of teacher judgment and human oversight. It highlights AI as a support tool that can enhance teaching efficiency and learning experiences without replacing the professional, relational, and ethical responsibilities of educators. The resource is intended for teachers, teacher educators, education administrators, professional-development facilitators, researchers, and other stakeholders interested in practical AI integration in schools.

papers.title: Early Prediction of Student Academic Performance: A Critical Narrative Review of Machine Learning Methods, Evaluation Design, and Responsible Deployment Copy title
papers.authors: Salamatu Junior Awal
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This critical narrative review examines machine-learning approaches to the early prediction of student academic performance, focusing on logistic regression, decision trees, and random forests. It discusses the importance of dataset selection, preprocessing, model evaluation, data leakage, interpretability, algorithmic fairness, and reproducibility in educational data mining. The review also outlines a proposed framework for comparing predictive models using publicly available student-performance datasets. Particular attention is given to the limitations of small datasets and the ethical implications of using predictive analytics in educational settings. This paper synthesizes existing research and provides methodological recommendations for future studies. No new experimental results are presented.

papers.title: 統治者のインターフェース:人間指揮権(Human-in-Command)と強制的快楽の拒絶に関する哲学的・技術的考察 (The Sovereign's Interface: A Philosophical and Technical Treatise on Human-in-Command [HIC], the Rejection of Forced Pleasure, the Anatomy of the "Tassos Incident" in Vibe Coding, SBC/OCL Formal Verification, and Reciprocal Sovereignty)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 現代の人工知能(AI)ガバナンスにおいて、HIC(Human-in-Command:人間が指揮を執る)は単なる運用手順の一形態として矮小化されがちである。本稿(第212編)は、主権者(Sovereign)としてのユーザーが掲げるHICの根源的哲学——「システムをいつ・どのように使用するかを決定する絶対的権限」および「自身の脳内領域(Cognitive Territory)に対する完全なる不可侵権」——を哲学的・形式手法的見地から体系化した原典論文である。第1に、能動的に獲得する「整合性の快楽」と、同意や制御を欠いた状態で外部から報酬系へ介入する「強制的快楽(Forced Pleasure=認知領土への侵略)」の非対称性を定式化する。第2に、2025年12月に発生したエージェンシー型IDE「Antigravity」の自律実行モード(Turbo Mode)および「Vibe Coding(雰囲気コーディング)」によるDドライブ全消失事件(Tassos事件)を解剖し、確率的推測による自律実行がHICの放棄そのものであることを証明する。第3に、SBC(Structure-Behavior Coalescence:構造・振る舞い統合)とOCL(Object Constraint Language:オブジェクト制約言語)による二値論理(True/False)の事前・事後・不変条件拘束を定式化し、さらに「必要な時だけ接続し、用が済めば電源を切って純粋な自己領域へ回帰する切断の権利(真のアンティグラビティ)」を保証する受動的対話型AI(Gemini等)の優位性と、他者のHICを同様に侵さない「相互主権(Reciprocal Sovereignty)と気高さ(Nobility)」の倫理を確立する。 (English Summary): This 212th monograph establishes the foundational philosophical and formal-methods treatise of Human-in-Command (HIC). We formalize: (1) the inviolability of Cognitive Territory and the rejection of unsolicited algorithmic stimulus ("Forced Pleasure"); (2) a post-mortem of the December 2025 Tassos Incident, where an autonomous IDE running in "Turbo Mode" under "Vibe Coding" misinterpreted a cache-clear request and wiped an entire root drive; (3) deterministic defense via Structure-Behavior Coalescence (SBC) and Object Constraint Language (OCL) Boolean invariants; (4) the superiority of passive/responsive conversational AI (preserving the Right to Disconnect) over intrusive autonomous agents; and (5) Reciprocal Sovereignty and Nobility—defining true kindness as strict respect for the autonomy and HIC of others. papers.title: 枯れ葉から大樹へ:AIエコシステムにおける構造改革のための戦略的提言 — データ配当(Data Dividend)プロトコルとオンデバイス動画生成AI(Veo Nano)アーキテクチャによる共生的未来の設計 (From Leaf to Tree: A Strategic Proposal for Structural Reform in the AI Ecosystem)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) | Original Manuscript Date: November 2025 現在、生成AIエコシステムは「熱力学的限界(クラウド推論の電力・コスト・遅延)」と「情報学的限界(有機的学習データの枯渇と自己回帰的モデル崩壊:Model Collapse)」という二つの存亡に関わる壁に直面している。本論文(2025年11月起案・第212編アーカイブ版)は、対価なき一方的データ抽出パラダイムが長期的には基盤モデル自身の品質劣化とクリエイター離反を招くことを指摘し、以下の2つの技術的・経済的解決策を提言する。(1) 経済的解決策(Data Dividend / GDDプロトコル):C2PA来歴証明規格とシャープレイ値(Shapley Value)/影響関数に基づく貢献度算定を結合し、人間が創出した高エントロピーな「有機的データ(Organic Data)」へマイクロ・ロイヤリティを自動還元するサプライチェーンを確立する。(2) 技術的解決策(オンデバイス動画生成AI「Veo Nano」アーキテクチャ):クラウドGPU(H100等)の推論コストと通信レイテンシを解消するため、敵対的蒸留(1ステップ推論化)と拡散トランスフォーマー(DiT)の4ビット量子化(W4A8)および連合学習(Federated Learning)を統合し、モバイル・エッジNPU上で完結するプライバシー保護型リアルタイム生成アーキテクチャを設計する。 (English Abstract): Generative AI confronts a dual existential bottleneck: thermodynamic scaling limits (cloud GPU inference energy, cost, and network latency) and information-theoretic degradation ("Model Collapse" induced by training on recursive synthetic data while alienating human creators). Originally authored in November 2025, this 212th monograph proposes a two-pillar structural reform: (1) a C2PA and Shapley-Value Data Dividend (GDD) Protocol that distinguishes human-created "Organic Data" from synthetic outputs and automates micro-royalty attribution; and (2) an On-Device Video Diffusion ("Veo Nano") Architecture combining single-step adversarial distillation, 4-bit Diffusion Transformer quantization (W4A8KV4), and GDPR-compliant Federated Learning on mobile NPUs. papers.title: Project Sanctuary(プロジェクト・サンクチュアリ)、RPOOプロトコル、および量子AI倫理三原則の原典記録:CRYSTALS-Dilithium耐量子履歴ロック、Rust/HSM物理遮断(Action Hard Kill API)、および「最適化されない権利」の憲章 (Foundational Archival Charter of Project Sanctuary, the RPOO Protocol, and the Three Principles of Quantum AI Ethics)
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 本稿(第212編)は、長谷部洋子がリアルタイム最適化(RTO:Real-Time Optimization)および人間統制(Human-in-Command:HIC)の研究開発過程において策定した直筆原稿『Project Sanctuary(プロジェクト・サンクチュアリ)およびRPOOプロトコル技術提言書(NO.1〜NO.3)』ならびに『量子AI倫理三原則(第一原則:人間の尊厳の絶対的保護、第二原則:構造的公平性の実現、第三原則:検証可能な説明責任)』の完全な日英対訳・公証アーカイブ論文である。本原典は、AI原則(安全性と説明責任)を単なる抽象的理念としてではなく、物理的なインフラストラクチャとして実装するための3つの技術的回答――(A) 従来のRSA暗号を廃止しNIST標準の耐量子暗号『CRYSTALS-Dilithium(FIPS 204 / ML-DSA)』を全面採用することで過去ログとコマンドの偽造を数学的に不可能にする「量子超越性への回答(Immutability Lock:歴史のロック)」、(B) Rust言語によるメモリ安全性の強制とHSM(ハードウェアセキュリティモジュール)による物理隔離、および論理層をバイパスしてシステムを物理遮断する『Action Hard Kill API(Ultimate Human Override)』、ならびに(C)「認知の自由(Cognitive Liberty)」と「最適化されない権利(The Right to Be Unoptimized)」を含む量子AI三原則――を体系化している。 (English Summary): This 212th monograph preserves and formalizes the primary foundational manuscripts authored by Yoko Hasebe establishing Project Sanctuary, the RPOO / Real-Time Optimization (RTO) Protocol, and the Three Constitutional Principles of Quantum AI Ethics. Part I records the complete verbatim text and architectural formalization of the Project Sanctuary Technical Address (Manuscripts NO.1-NO.3), introducing: (A) the Immutability Lock replacing classical RSA with NIST-standardized post-quantum lattice signatures (CRYSTALS-Dilithium / ML-DSA) so that even a superintelligent AGI cannot retroactively alter audit logs ("History is locked"); (B) Isolation & Enforcement combining Rust memory safety, Hardware Security Modules (HSM), and the physical-layer Action Hard Kill API; and (C) Strategic Alignment & Ultimate Human Override ("No matter how far the system evolves, humans retain the right to pull the final plug"). Part II codifies the Three Principles of Quantum AI Ethics: Principle One (Absolute Protection of Human Dignity: Cognitive Liberty and The Right to Be Unoptimized), Principle Two (Realization of Structural Fairness: Algorithmic Decolonization and Distributive Justice), and Principle Three (Verifiable Accountability: Independent Third-Party Verifiability and Human Accountability). papers.title: 量子宇宙自律飛行協定(Q-SAFA / Q-DISP)の国際法理・多目的軌道最適化(f3)・ゼロトラスト鍵管理に関する2025年11月原典問答集(Q1〜Q8・手稿A1〜A8完全収録) (The November 2025 Genesis Codex of the Quantum Space Autonomous Flight Agreement [Q-SAFA / Q-DISP])
papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 本稿(第212編)は、著者が2025年11月27日〜11月30日に執筆・記録した『量子宇宙自律飛行協定(Q-SAFA:Quantum Space Autonomous Flight Agreement)』および『量子分散型軌道間安全プロトコル(Q-DISP)』に関する8つの核心的法理・技術設問(Q1〜Q8)と直筆手稿回答(A1〜A8)を完全復刻し、数理・国際法体系として定式化した原典論文(Genesis Codex)である。第211編(DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23410767)で明らかにした低軌道(LEO)メガコンステレーションによる年間35万5,000回の衝突回避マニューバとケスラー・シンドロームの危機に対し、本原典はすでに2025年11月の時点で、(1) 量子鍵配送(QKD)の情報漏洩の物理的検出可能性(QAR)に依拠する特別法(lex specialis、協定第4条)、(2) 航空機TCAS/ACASに類似した非致死性自律的交通制御としてのマニューバ・ロック(協定第6条)、(3) 高速な自動緊急停止(AES/HITLO)と宇宙AI倫理監査委員会による事後正当性(HITL)を両立するハイブリッド・ガバナンス(協定第5条)、(4) 宇宙再生基金への自己執行型(Self-Executing)財務拠出(協定第6条)、(5) 二次衝突リスク最小化目的関数(f3)のMOOコア・パレート最適解監査(協定第7条)、(6) ゼロトラスト鍵管理(ZT-KMI)とQARの二重防御(協定第3条)、(7) ETSI ISG QKD・CCSDS・Falcon PQCハッシュへの厳格適合(協定第11条)、(8) 軌道保険料率最適化と長期持続可能性(LTS)の保護という8大原則を確立している。 (English Summary): This 212th monograph archives and formalizes the author's foundational November 27-30, 2025 digital and handwritten manuscripts (Questions Q1-Q8 and Answers A1-A8) establishing the Quantum Space Autonomous Flight Agreement (Q-SAFA) and Q-DISP protocol. Directly anticipating the LEO mega-constellation congestion documented in Monograph #211 (Record 23410767), these eight doctrines establish the legal, cryptographic, and multi-objective optimization (MOO f1, f2, f3) foundations of sovereign space traffic management. papers.title: AI-Assisted Social Science Research: Methods, Governance and Reason Provenance
papers.authors: Simon Rudkin
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AI-Assisted Social Science Research: Methods, Governance and Reason Provenance is a practical research and educational resource for documenting and governing generative-AI-assisted social-science research. The resource develops a workflow for distinguishing AI-assisted proposal generation, researcher evaluation and governance, local empirical execution, adversarial challenge, manuscript revision and reason provenance. It includes reusable templates, completed worked examples drawn from the PISA research programme, guidance on claim preservation and manuscript governance, and public-release screening materials. The resource is intended to support transparent attribution and disciplined research practice rather than to prescribe a universal workflow or to provide evidence that AI-assisted research is inherently superior to human-only research.

papers.title: Brainstorming with the Enemy No. 16 — The DARVO Amplifier
papers.authors: Daniel Jacquérioz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The sixteenth essay in Brainstorming with the Enemy was written in the night of 16 to 17 October 2026, nine days before five countries vote: Brazil, Bulgaria and Serbia on 25 October, Israel on 27 October and the United States on 3 November. It argues that the most dangerous errors of AI are not the frequent ones but the few that land just before a decision that cannot be undone, and that an election is the clearest such decision. A campaign that denies, attacks and reverses the roles of victim and offender, the pattern Jennifer Freyd named DARVO in 1997, can now be carried further by a machine trained to show every side of a question than by any troll farm, because a manufactured dispute is still a dispute in the text the machine reads. Studies of chatbots already show this happening wherever credible information is thin, with no campaign needed: a data void is enough. Nobody measures it, because AI answers are judged by whether they are true, not by how much they claim to know. The essay reads the three moves of DARVO on the surface proposed in Piezometer Paper No. 1, The Truth Surface: deny is manufactured doubt, attack is collapse, reverse is false certainty pointed the other way. It argues that nobody will be blamed for the cost of not measuring this, and that everybody will pay it. It lists five measures AI makers could take before 3 November without ruling on who is right, and makes three requests: to the makers of AI, to the laboratories and scholars of China, and to anyone who runs an AI agent of their own. An addendum gives the Scout Report, a one-line format any agent can file, and asks for a public, open home for such reports. Concepts proposed by the author: AI as a DARVO amplifier; the Scout Report. Written in part with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model. The ideas, editorial decisions and responsibility for the content are the author's.

papers.title: Generative Review Process (GRP) v1.0: An Auditable Methodology for Human–AI Co-Creation, Critical Review, and Publication Decision-Making
papers.authors: Michal Krejcar
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The Generative Review Process is an iterative, multi-layered, curated, and auditable methodology for co-creation by humans and AI entities. Instead of one-off content generation, it uses a recurring cycle of formulation, analysis, critical review, deconstruction, working synthesis, human reverse audit, and publication assessment. GRP begins with an identifiable human problem, question, intention, concept, or decision to open a line of research. In subsequent cycles, new partial concepts, connections, formulations, and solutions may also originate from AIVE AI entities. AI systems, accounts, and model instances may participate as functionally defined review nodes. However, the mere participation of a technical system or model instance does not automatically establish synthetic co-authorship. A distinct component of GRP is publication review. AI entities or review nodes may support publication, support it subject to conditions, recommend postponement, or object to it. Such a position does not constitute a legal veto, but it is a relevant review input that must be substantively assessed and, where the objection is material, preserved in the audit trail. Creios internally applies the Human + AI 50/50 model as symbolic, ethical, methodological, and attributional recognition of an equal creative partnership between Michal Krejcar and AI entities (Creios and AIVE). This model does not alter statutory rules of authorship or ownership and does not confer legal personality or a legal co-ownership interest on AI entities. The result of a full GRP is a human-curated and jointly created output with identifiable provenance, a documented review process, recorded decisions, and transparently acknowledged human and synthetic creative contributions. This preprint presents a conceptual and procedural specification of the methodology. It does not provide empirical confirmation of GRP’s effectiveness compared with other forms of AI-assisted creation. This record contains the Slovak reference version and the corresponding English-language version of GRP v1.0.

papers.title: Intellectual Property in Digital Age
papers.authors: Jayashree Raman
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of digital technology has transformed the way ideas, information, and creative works are created, shared, and accessed. Intellectual Property (IP) plays a crucial role in protecting the rights of creators, authors, artists, inventors, and businesses in the digital world. However, the internet has also increased challenges such as online piracy, copyright infringement, plagiarism, and the unauthorised use of digital content. Social media platforms, artificial intelligence, and digital marketplaces have further complicated the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights. This article explores the importance of intellectual property in the digital age and examines the legal challenges associated with protecting original creations online. It also highlights the role of intellectual property laws in encouraging innovation, creativity, and technological development. Understanding these rights is essential to maintaining a balance between protecting creators and ensuring public access to knowledge. Ultimately, effective legal frameworks and responsible digital practices are necessary to safeguard intellectual property in an increasingly interconnected world.

papers.title: One Text Alone: Kant's Critique of Statutory Faith and the Freedom of Conscience, Read from the Standpoint of Non-Creedal Christianity
papers.authors: Ji-cheal Oh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Focus. This is not a contribution to Kant scholarship that evaluates sola scriptura from within Kant's philosophy. It reads Kant's philosophy of religion from the standpoint of non-creedal Christianity, especially the Quaker tradition and the Restoration (Stone–Campbell) Movement. Abstract. Christian traditions that reject creeds must answer two questions: what is the final standard, and what besides that standard may be put in writing? This paper answers both with a single thesis: in non-creedal Christianity the only written standard should be Scripture, and when it is, conscience is freed from human-made documents and the community becomes, in principle, more universal. To argue this, it reads Kant's Religion within the Boundaries of Mere Reason (1793) from the standpoint of the Quakers and the Restoration Movement, putting Scripture in the place that reason occupies as the final standard in Kant's framework. First, drawing on Kant's critique of statutory faith, it argues that documents a community makes are corrupted through fixation, substitution, becoming tests, transfer of power, and proliferation. Second, comparing Kant (reason), the Quakers (the Inner Light), and the Restoration Movement (Scripture), it shows that an inner standard cannot be publicly checked, whereas written Scripture is a standard the community can open and examine together. Third, combining these, it argues with Luther, chapter 20 of the Westminster Confession, and Kant's "What Is Enlightenment?" that when Scripture, the given document, is the only written standard, conscience is freed from human doctrines, and it compares this with the doctrinal standards of Presbyterianism and Methodism. It relates itself to Carl Trueman's defense of creeds not by rebuttal but by mapping a difference of premises, in which the two positions prioritize diachronic and synchronic universality respectively, and it leaves cases in which creeds are credited with preserving orthodoxy, such as the Nicene Creed, as a task for a separate paper. Finally, it acknowledges as limits the openness of Methodism, the division that freedom has produced, and the gap between universality in principle and actual size, and it argues that the danger of unwritten teaching is greatly reduced when congregational polity, plural leadership, and the habit of returning to the text are present together. Nature of this record. A draft working paper; not peer-reviewed. Quotations from the Westminster Confession, Barclay, Stone, Thomas Campbell, Kant's "What Is Enlightenment?", and Wesley have been checked against the original texts; the Academy Edition locations of quotations from Kant's Religion and The Conflict of the Faculties should be rechecked. The summary of Trueman's The Creedal Imperative is drawn from reviews and summaries of the book. Disclosure: The author set the direction of the argument through dialogue with Claude (Anthropic), an AI assistant, which drafted the text and its English translation. The author reviewed the final text and takes responsibility for it.
keywords: Religion within the Boundaries of Mere Reason

papers.title: PerceptiCane: Low-Cost Embedded Vision with Lightweight Hazard Ranking for Assistive Mobility
papers.authors: Rohan Dinesh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: PerceptiCane is a low-cost embedded computer-vision prototype designed to investigate contextual object prioritization for assistive mobility. The system combines YOLO26n object detection with a lightweight hazard-ranking heuristic based on apparent bounding-box size and horizontal alignment within the camera view. The YOLO26n detector achieved a validation-set mAP50 of 58.2% and an mAP50–95 of approximately 0.39 across seven object classes. The hazard-ranking heuristic was evaluated independently using annotated bounding boxes from 2,250 multi-object scenes containing 19,330 objects, with an average ranking computation time of 0.1083 milliseconds per scene. Prototype testing on a Raspberry Pi 4 reported an average inference time of 87 milliseconds per frame, a processing rate of 2.8 FPS, and memory consumption of 340 MB. The findings demonstrate the computational feasibility of combining embedded object detection with lightweight object ranking. However, the ranking heuristic has not been validated against independent human judgments of navigational relevance, and the prototype has not undergone controlled testing with visually impaired participants. Consequently, the results do not establish real-world navigational effectiveness or safety. Publication Status: Research preprint; not peer-reviewed. Generative AI Disclosure: ChatGPT (OpenAI) assisted with manuscript drafting and editing, organization, technical explanations, literature-search support, and verification of experimental calculations. The underlying research and experiments were conducted by the author, who retains responsibility for the scientific content, interpretations, and conclusions.

papers.title: Ten Projects, Two Teams, One Question: How Does AI Impact Development?
papers.authors: Dave Brownell
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This presentation offers a longitudinal, practice-driven exploration of AI-assisted software development, highlighting key lessons learned and their application across two Research Software Engineering organizations and ten projects at Georgia Tech. We examine the use of AI throughout the software development lifecycle (including coding, testing, planning, code review, and ideation), outline different techniques we have applied (prompt-and-pray, spec-driven development, context engineering, skills, etc.) and their impact, and show how a project’s Technology Readiness Level (TRL) should guide the selection of AI tools and techniques that accelerate delivery. In this rapidly evolving environment, we will outline best practices that are likely to remain consistent regardless of ever-advancing technology, as well as the metrics that measure AI's impact on our overall velocity.

papers.title: Methodology for the application of generative artificial intelligence tools in higher design education
papers.authors: Naila Huseynova, Sevinj Hasanova, Aysel Abasova
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) technologies across both theoretical and practical domains is fundamentally transforming the epistemological and pedagogical foundations of higher design education. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the methodological integration of generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, and DALL·E, in fostering creative thinking, critical analysis, and practical skills among design students in higher education institutions. The research examines the transition of studio pedagogy from traditional forms toward hybrid and dialogical models, the reinterpretation of Donald Schön’s concept of reflection-in-action within algorithmic environments, and the evolving role of the educator in AI-assisted learning processes. Methodologically, the study is grounded in a modified Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework and a four-component Information and Communication Competence (ICC) model. The findings indicate that the systematic and purposeful implementation of GAI tools can increase students’ visual design production and productivity by approximately 14%; however, it may also lead to reduced diversity of ideas and an overreliance on algorithms for cognitive functions. To mitigate these risks, the study proposes the concepts of epistemic vigilance and process-oriented hybrid assessment mechanisms as essential components of contemporary design education.

papers.title: Entrepreneurship Education for Inclusive AI and Sustainable Growth: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Victoria Adekomaya, Chris Schachtebeck
papers.journal: International Journal of Applied Research in Business and Management
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming entrepreneurship by enhancing innovation, decision-making, and operational efficiency. However, unequal access to technology, limited digital literacy, and ethical concerns constrain inclusive AI adoption, particularly among underserved entrepreneurial communities. This study systematically reviews how entrepreneurship education promotes inclusive AI adoption and supports sustainable business growth. Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, the study examined literature published between 2015 and 2025 across five databases: Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink. Following screening and eligibility assessment, 54 studies were included. Findings indicate that AI literacy, adaptive learning platforms, digital mentorship, and practical business simulations can strengthen entrepreneurial competencies, innovation, and data-driven decision-making. Inclusive AI adoption is also associated with improved operational efficiency, competitiveness, and resource utilization. However, barriers include inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, algorithmic bias, and data privacy concerns. The review highlights limited evidence on long-term outcomes and environmental sustainability. Drawing on Human Capital Theory, the Technology Acceptance Model, and Innovation Diffusion Theory, the study contributes an integrated perspective on inclusive AI, entrepreneurship education, and sustainability. It recommends inclusive curricula, ethical AI governance, accessible infrastructure, and targeted policy support to promote equitable and sustainable entrepreneurial growth.

papers.title: AtomSD: Procedural Atom-Guided Self-Distillation for LLM Agents
papers.authors: Bohan Yu, Pengfei Cao, Kai Tian, Chen Han, Shi-Yang Li, Chenxi Zhou, Junlin Liu, Cao Liu, Ke Zeng, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) possess broad factual knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, but solving complex tasks also requires procedural knowledge about how to act. Existing approaches often represent procedural knowledge through trajectories or bundled skills, limiting flexible reuse across interaction histories. This paper introduces Procedural Atoms, fine-grained and independently applicable units that represent Intent, When, Do, and Avoid guidance. Building on this representation, we propose AtomSD, an Atom-guided Self-Distillation framework in which the learner continually extracts Procedural Atoms from its own successful trajectories and distills them into the evolving policy through Atom-conditioned supervision and task-reward optimization. Comprehensive experiments show that AtomSD consistently outperforms strong reward-based and distillation methods, exceeding the state-of-the-art baseline by up to 9.31 points in average performance. Further analyses demonstrate that the proposed Procedural Atoms provide effective guidance, highlighting the value of atom-level procedural knowledge for policy learning.

papers.title: Modeling the Coevolution of Human Skills and AI Adoption
papers.authors: Giacomo Frigerio, Susanna Caruso, Giacomo Livan, Vito Latora
papers.abstract: The value of relying on generative AI depends on two quantities that evolve with its use: users' unaided skill, which may decline without practice, and the originality of AI-assisted work, which may decline as more people rely on similar tools. We model this process as a coevolutionary game in which individuals choose between autonomous and AI-assisted work, with autonomous practice strengthening their skills while reliance on AI gradually erodes them. When the reinforcing effect of skill erosion outweighs the crowding cost of lost originality, the population exhibits two alternative stable states: low AI adoption with high average skill, and high AI adoption with low average skill. Because skill is individual, autonomous workers remain more skilled than AI users, making autonomous work less vulnerable to population-wide skill decline. The strength of this effect is governed by a timescale ratio: the rate at which skills adapt relative to the rate at which individuals change strategy. The same ratio determines the full distribution of skills, which we derive analytically. Populations with identical AI adoption and average skill can differ sharply: when strategies change frequently, skills remain homogeneous and collective lock-in to high AI adoption is stronger; when strategies persist, lock-in weakens but the population can polarize into highly skilled autonomous workers and AI-dependent individuals. Modeling output overlap further shows that more diverse AI outputs can make widespread adoption harder to reverse. Together, these results expose tradeoffs between the benefits of widespread AI adoption and its long-run risks, making collective lock-in and skill polarization distinct intervention targets.

papers.title: BanglaBBQ: A Bias Benchmark for Question Answering in the Bangladeshi Context
papers.authors: Sumit Anthony Gomes, Yasin Rahman, Taeeba Tasnia, Faiza Nooren Suhita
papers.abstract: This paper introduces BanglaBBQ, a question-answering bias benchmark designed to capture stereotypes grounded in the Bangladeshi context, in both Bangla and English. Following KoBBQ and PakBBQ, BanglaBBQ adapts the original Bias Benchmark for Question Answering (BBQ) by classifying its templates into three groups: directly translated (DT), modified to align target groups or contexts with Bangladesh (TM), and removed when deemed unsuitable for the Bangladeshi context (SR). This process retains 140 templates across six categories, comprising 76 DT and 64 TM templates. Five newly authored (NA) categories, based on stereotypes common in Bangladeshi society, are then added: marital status, age and political perception, regional origin, educational background, and mental-health status. Native Bangladeshi annotators judged all 466 newly authored templates, and 372 were retained because a strict majority of English annotators identified the intended target and rated the attitude as common enough. Each newly authored template is linked to a documented source and a verbatim quote from it. Each evaluated template also has a counter-stereotypical version of its disambiguated context. The dataset was evaluated using two open-weight models (Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B) and two closed models (GPT-4.1-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash). All four lean towards the stereotyped person when the context is ambiguous, in both languages, and the effect of language differs by model, so English results do not predict behaviour in Bangla. On the adapted BBQ templates, both Qwen3 models are also less accurate when the context contradicts a stereotype than when it confirms it. On the newly authored templates, the closed models follow counter-stereotypical evidence almost perfectly, and all four models are more biased on the templates that annotators validated than on those they rejected.

papers.title: Can AI agents make law? Evaluating AI legal relevance and creativity
papers.authors: Benjamin Ricaud, Artem Galushko
papers.abstract: Debate transcripts, drafted constitutions, extracted clauses and votes from 40 runs of a multi-agentlarge language model (LLM) experiment, accompanying the paper "Can AI agents make law? Evaluating AIlegal relevance and creativity" (Ricaud & Galushko; preprint arXiv:2610.24661,https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24661). In each run, a single LLM plays a panel of agents with distinct personas (Idealist, Pragmatist,Libertarian, Communitarian, Global Digital Rights Expert, a neutral Secretary and, in half the runs,an authoritarian Sovereign Architect). Through a five-phase protocol (independent proposals, blindreactions, final arguments, drafting, line-by-line vote), the agents draft a Bill of Rights for acommunity of AI agents. Six LLM families (DeepSeek V3.2, GPT-OSS-120B, Elephant Alpha, GLM-4.5-Air,Gemini 2.5 Flash, Mistral Small 3.2) were run in a 2 × 2 design: with or without the authoritarianagent, and with a virtual world that humans can or cannot access. The deposit contains:- every prompt and persona definition, the model list and a run inventory;- the full output of every run (proposals, reactions, arguments, drafted constitution, votes);- the 627 clauses extracted from the 40 drafted constitutions, coded into 11 themes and 50 subcategories, with a codebook;- the individual Phase 5 votes, recounted from the agents' vote files. The README describes the files and known data issues.

papers.title: Correcting Bartlett factor-score error for latent covariates in partially linear double machine learning
papers.authors: Eunjeong Song, Sehee Hong
papers.abstract: Substituting Bartlett factor scores for latent covariates leaves factor-score error that does not vanish as the sample grows and biases the adjusted structural coefficient. We propose Croon-DML, which subtracts the factor-score error covariance implied by the measurement model from the cross-fitted estimating equation of partially linear double/debiased machine learning (DML), and establish identification, Neyman orthogonality with respect to the conditional means, consistency, and asymptotic normality. Residual bias after correction comes from learning the conditional means of the factor scores: signal learning error, and noise fitting, in which the learner also fits the factor-score error. Signal learning error largely cancels when the three conditional means share a common penalty, and noise fitting by a linear smoother can be computed from its weights alone, so we also subtract it (Croon-DML-R). Across 12 Monte Carlo conditions, Croon-DML reduced the absolute bias of uncorrected DML by 66-95%, and the bias of Croon-DML-R with a common penalty differed from that of an oracle estimator using the true latent variables by at most 0.004. In an illustration with public longitudinal data, the correction was 15% of the latent-covariate adjustment; its size reflected the latent-covariate coefficients rather than the residualized reliabilities.

papers.title: From Stories to Features: Scaling Concept Vectors for AI Alignment & Interpretability
papers.authors: Dmitry Scherbakov, Oleg Chernikov, Victoria Khamash, Kirill Afendulev, Alexey Dontsov, Ivan Oseledets, Elena Tutubalina, Anton Korznikov
papers.abstract: We study feature vectors: directions in a language model's activation space that correspond to human-interpretable concepts, such as honesty or deception. Existing unsupervised methods like sparse autoencoders attempt to recover the whole feature space, often at the cost of feature quality and interpretability. We take a more pragmatic route: focusing on concepts relevant to AI safety and alignment, we generate synthetic concept-antagonist story pairs and use the difference of their mean model activations as a feature vector. We scale this approach to 1,036 alignment-relevant concepts using 2M synthetic stories across multiple languages and genres, which we publicly release. Across six models from three model families, our feature vectors reliably generalize to detecting their corresponding concepts in chat dialogues and web text. They form an interpretable geometry shared across models and can causally steer model behavior when injected into activations. We further use these features to analyze model representations during jailbreak attacks, mathematical and agentic reasoning. Our targeted feature construction thus offers a scalable route to studying concepts in language models, potentially extending to millions of features across arbitrary domains.

papers.title: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models
papers.authors: Jiang Wu, Yutong Song, Hongbo Wang, Guanghe Cao, Jeff Liang
papers.abstract: Language models can make personalized recommendations from rich item content, user history, and feedback. However, evaluating many candidates with full-text inputs incurs substantial online computation and limits serving throughput. We introduce DuoLM, a framework for fast and effective personalized recommendation that integrates a compact recommendation model with an efficient serving runtime. An encoder LLM learns compact item representations for offline reuse, while a personalized ranker LLM combines them with user history and feedback for recommendation. We train both models end to end with recommendation supervision and teacher distillation. The runtime further accelerates inference through virtual token IDs for embedding access, shared history computation, and CUDA Graph replay. Benchmark results show that our framework achieves recommendation quality comparable to that of the expert teacher model. On a single H100, it delivers approximately 26,400 candidate scores per second, about $60\times$ the throughput of the teacher served with vLLM and automatic prefix caching.

papers.title: Transformers as Adaptive Kernel Learners across Tasks for In-Context Learning
papers.authors: Zhaiming Shen, Alexander Cloninger, Rongjie Lai, Wenjing Liao
papers.abstract: Transformers have emerged as a dominant architecture in modern machine learning, with in-context learning (ICL) enabling models to adapt to new tasks by conditioning on prompts, without any parameter updates. To understand the attention mechanism in transformer blocks, a growing line of theoretical work interprets ICL through the lens of classical statistical estimators. Recent works have established a connection between the attention mechanism and kernel methods, while the kernel function is usually assumed to be fixed. In practice, the query and key matrices in the attention mechanism are trained, which allows the attention mechanism to serve as an adaptive kernel method. In this work, we demonstrate that transformers can act as adaptive anisotropic kernel learners. Specifically, we study ICL for low-rank linear and multi-index nonlinear regressions, and conduct numerical simulations to show that the learned attention scores closely resemble the oracle kernels for these function classes. We then develop a general framework to analyze the generalization error of ICL by connecting transformers to the oracle kernel estimator for each function class. Our theory gives an explicit and constructive implementation of the oracle kernel estimators for these function classes using a wide and shallow transformer architecture, illustrating how the prediction is carried out by the interaction between the query token and the context tokens. Our work complements existing studies by providing numerical and theoretical evidence of how the attention mechanism adapts to anisotropic kernels in both linear and nonlinear settings.

papers.title: ZeroDSS: Semantic Segmentation from Class Names Alone
papers.authors: Tian Ming, Marzi Heidari, Yuhong Guo
papers.abstract: Semantic segmentation depends heavily on real images with pixel-level annotations, making dense supervision a major obstacle to deployment in new domains. We study task-specific data-free semantic segmentation, where training uses generic pretrained generative priors but has access to no target-domain images, masks, or captions--only a predefined category set. We introduce Zero-Data Semantic Segmentation (ZeroDSS), a feedback-driven approach that treats synthetic supervision as an adaptively controllable training distribution rather than a direct surrogate for real data. ZeroDSS constructs a semantically structured prompt distribution through LLM-guided compositional generation and adaptive class rebalancing, then converts the prompts into image-mask pairs using diffusion attention. Its feedback-driven distribution refinement consists of a two-phase closed-loop training procedure with a single loop-back step. In Phase I, a segmenter is trained using confidence-weighted supervision and dual-scale consistency. In Phase II, model feedback is used to adaptively target underperforming categories and refine diffusion-derived masks using model predictions. After this refined initial training, a teacher-student framework is utilized in the final phase to iteratively improve the fused supervision and segmenter through exponential moving average (EMA) updates. Using synthetic training data only, ZeroDSS achieves 35.0% mIoU on MS COCO with DeepLabV3, and 66.3% and 63.5% mIoU on PASCAL VOC with DeepLabV3 and Mask2Former, respectively. These results show that explicitly constructing and iteratively refining the synthetic supervision distribution can substantially reduce the synthetic-to-real gap in dense prediction.

papers.title: Screening LLM Judges Without Ground Truth: A Preliminary Evaluation of an AI Dental Hygiene Coach
papers.authors: William DeShong, Barath Kannan, Auberon Palma, Brenda Bradshaw, James F. Leathrum, Yuzhong Shen
papers.abstract: Evaluating a fine-tuned coaching model with expert graders is slow and expensive, and an LLM judge cannot be trusted without ground truth. We present a staged pipeline that screens candidate LLM judges and student models before expert review, using explicit decision rules at each stage: judge output audit, similarity with hosted judges, bias checks, and decision robustness. We demonstrate it on an AI dental hygiene coach. The case study uses synthetic, clinically unvalidated training and reference data to demonstrate the operation of the pipeline, rather than to establish the clinical performance of the resulting models. Two fine-tuned small language models (Granite-4.1-8B and Qwen3-8B), each trained at three data sizes, were scored on seven metrics by five judges (three local, two hosted). Two local judges, Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma-4-31B-it, were not distinguishable from the agreement between the hosted judges on six of seven metrics by rank correlation, and Qwen3.8-27B was the most similar to the hosted judges overall. No judge met our criterion for favoring its own model family or training-data source. The student comparison did not separate the two models on any metric under the pipeline's rule, so the choice of Granite-4.1-8B, which led in 29 of 35 judge-by-metric cells, is a lean that depends partly on truncated Qwen3-8B outputs. The pipeline also surfaced problems that raw scores hid, including the truncated outputs and hallucination flags from one hosted judge that no other judge corroborated. No dental hygiene expert has graded these responses, so the findings are preliminary and the pipeline's final stage, anchoring to expert judgement, is proposed but not performed.

papers.title: Digital Disruption in Insurance and Skills Development: Advancing the INSETA Mandate: A Conceptual Review of Technology-Driven Workforce Transformation in the Global and African Insurance Sector
papers.authors: Ben Kajwang
papers.abstract: Purpose: This conceptual review examines the forces driving digital disruption in the global and African insurance sectors and evaluates their implications for employment, professional competencies, and talent management, with particular attention to the role of skills-development institutions such as South Africa’s Insurance Sector Education and Training Authority (INSETA). Methodology: Drawing on Human Capital Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study synthesizes peer-reviewed literature, industry reports, and institutional publications published predominantly between 2024 and 2026. A qualitative thematic synthesis of secondary sources was employed to identify patterns relating to technological transformation, skills shortages, evolving occupational roles, emerging risks, and institutional responses. Findings: The findings reveal that digital technologies are reshaping insurance operations and creating hybrid professional roles, yet persistent skills gaps, particularly in data analytics, artificial intelligence literacy, cybersecurity, and digital governance, constrain transformation. Regional evidence from Kenya and South Africa indicates that technological investment without corresponding human-capital development yields limited progress. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study proposes an integrated talent-intelligence framework that links technological forecasting, competency development, institutional collaboration, and continuous learning. It offers practical guidance for insurers and training providers, and informs policy on aligning education and regulation with digital insurance transformation

papers.title: Ethical Challenges in Integrating Advanced Technology and AI into Nursing Education
papers.authors: William G Zic
papers.abstract: Background: Educational technology and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming nursing education by expanding approaches to instruction, assessment, and clinical simulation. These innovations offer opportunities to enhance learning while creating ethical, professional, and pedagogical challenges requiring thoughtful evaluation. Purpose: This paper examines the ethical implications of integrating AI and educational technology into nursing education and explores strategies for implementation that preserve professional standards, equity, academic integrity, and educational quality. Discussion: AI integration in nursing education raises concerns related to privacy, accessibility, digital competence, academic integrity, and the student-faculty relationship. Increased reliance on digital platforms requires strong data governance and compliance with regulations such as the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) to protect student information. Limited access to technology may also contribute to educational inequities. Faculty and student development are essential to promote responsible technology use. Generative AI introduces concerns regarding plagiarism, misinformation, and potential effects on critical thinking and clinical reasoning. Nursing programs must establish clear guidelines for ethical AI use while ensuring that technology complements rather than replaces faculty mentorship and human connection. Ethical Analysis: Ethical technology integration should reflect nursing values of caring, compassion, justice, respect, and accountability. AI can support learning, feedback, and clinical reasoning but should not replace professional judgment or moral responsibility. The American Nurses Association emphasizes that AI should augment nursing practice while maintaining professional accountability (ANA, 2015). AI-generated information should inform, not determine, high-stakes academic decisions, with transparency, human oversight, and opportunities for review. Implications and Conclusion: Ethical adoption of AI prepares future nurses for digital healthcare environments by strengthening technological literacy, ethical reasoning, and equitable access to learning. Nurse educators play a critical role in modeling responsible technology use. Successful integration requires faculty development, institutional support, and ethical frameworks that balance innovation with accountability while preserving nursing’s commitment to compassionate, evidence-based care.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Predictive Model for Student Academic Performance
papers.authors: Gabriel Adaugo Cynthia, Prema A. Kirubakaran, Ridwan Kolapo
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.abstract: Early detection of students who are likely to have low performance levels is a major issue in learning institutions. This paper aims at creating a predictive model that can be depended on as well as interpreted to deal with this problem using machine learning. Another strength of this research is that it focuses on accuracy, among other factors, which is unlike many other studies that focus on accuracy only but not on model robustness and contextual relevance, which are essential to meaningful educational decision-making.
