To enhance the credibility of the findings, the primary and secondary data were also used, including demographic, socio-educational, and academic characteristics of students.

papers.title: INOVASI PEMBELAJARAN SEJARAH DALAM MENGHADAPI PERUBAHAH KARAKTERISTIK PESERTA DIDIK DI ERA DIGITAL
papers.authors: Aulia Gusmaini Aulia Gusmaini, Ainun Septia, Muhammad Dafa Arayen, Reka Seprina, Apdelmi
papers.journal: Didaktik Jurnal Ilmiah PGSD STKIP Subang
papers.abstract: The development of digital technology has brought changes to the way students access information and participate in the learning process. These changes have become both a challenge and an opportunity for history learning, which has often been associated with memorizing facts and past events. This article aims to discuss innovations in history learning in response to changes in students’ characteristics in the digital era. The method used in this article is a literature review by examining various scholarly sources related to history learning, digital media, digital literacy, and technological developments in education. The discussion shows that innovations in history learning can be implemented through the use of interactive e-books, learning videos, blogs, social media, digital maps, web-based historical sources, and artificial intelligence technology. The use of these media can help create more interactive learning that is relevant to the characteristics of students in the digital era. In addition, the use of technology needs to be accompanied by strengthening digital literacy and historical literacy so that students are able to select, verify, compare, and critically analyze historical information. Teachers also play an important role in guiding the use of technology so that it does not merely serve as a tool for obtaining information but also supports students’ historical thinking processes. Therefore, innovations in history learning in the digital era should focus on the appropriate, critical, and contextual use of technology so that history learning remains relevant to students’ development and the needs of education today. Keywords: learning innovation, history learning, students, digital era, digital literac

papers.title: PENGARUH PENGGUNAAN MEDIA VIDEO PEMBELAJARAN BERBASIS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR IPA SISWA KELAS IV SDN 52 KURANJI KOTA PADANG
papers.authors: Faiza Alfarah, Dini Maielfi, Kurniati Ramadhini
papers.journal: Didaktik Jurnal Ilmiah PGSD STKIP Subang
papers.abstract: Low science learning outcomes and the limited use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based learning media were among the problems found in fourth-grade science learning at SDN 52 Kuranji, Padang City. This study aimed to examine the effect of AI-based instructional video media on the science learning outcomes of fourth-grade students. The study used a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design in the form of a posttest-only control group design. The sample consisted of 55 students, including 27 students in the experimental class who learned using AI-based instructional videos and 28 students in the control class who learned using image media. Learning outcome data were collected using a 27-item multiple-choice posttest and analyzed through normality, homogeneity, and hypothesis testing using SPSS version 27. The experimental class obtained an average posttest score of 85.48, while the control class obtained 78.89. The Independent Samples t-Test produced a t-value of 2.072, which was higher than the t-table value of 2.009, with df = 53 and a significance value of 0.043 < 0.05. These results indicate that AI-based instructional video media had a significant effect on the science learning outcomes of fourth-grade students at SDN 52 Kuranji, Padang City.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Media Organizations: Emerging Practices, Opportunities and Implications for Social and Cultural Development
papers.authors: Shikeb Majeed
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming an increasingly visible part of the modern media environment. Its role is no longer limited to automated or computational journalism; it is now being explored across several stages of media production, including content writing, editing, transcription, translation, fact-checking, audience analysis, recommendation, and personalization. As generative AI and large language models have developed, academic interest in their use within journalism and media organizations has also increased considerably. Recent studies and reviews show that research in this area has expanded from early discussions of automated journalism to broader questions concerning how AI is changing newsroom practices and professional work. This review examines existing research on AI adoption in media organizations, focusing particularly on changes in newsroom practices, organizational processes, journalistic roles, editorial decision-making, and the social and cultural dimensions of AI use. The paper brings together earlier research on automated and algorithmic journalism with more recent literature on generative AI, journalist–AI collaboration, newsroom implementation, ethical concerns, and organizational barriers. The literature suggests that AI can help media organizations handle repetitive and data-intensive tasks more efficiently, allowing journalists to devote greater attention to activities that require interpretation and editorial judgement. However, the growing use of AI also raises important concerns about human oversight, algorithmic transparency, accountability, professional autonomy, and the quality and context of media content. Particular attention is given to India and other countries of the Global South, where the adoption of AI takes place within different economic, organizational, linguistic, and cultural settings. Research from these contexts indicates that AI adoption is developing, but its implementation is not always uniform. Limited resources, inadequate training, organizational preparedness, and the absence of clear ethical guidelines can influence how effectively media organizations integrate AI into their professional practices. Overall, the review suggests that AI adoption in media should not be understood simply as a technological shift aimed at improving speed and efficiency. It is also influencing the nature of journalistic work, editorial responsibility, and the relationship between media organizations and the communities they serve. Therefore, understanding AI adoption requires attention not only to its operational benefits but also to its implications for the social and cultural responsibilities of media.

papers.title: AI GOVERNANCE AND FINANCIAL RISK : DISCLOSURE BASED AI READINESS INDEX FOR INDIAN BANKS
papers.authors: Snehitha Bommidi, Golli Mohan
papers.journal: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)
papers.abstract: Indian banks have been moving rapidly towards the use of artificial intelligence, but there is still no consensus on the best way to assess how well they govern it. In this paper, a disclosure-based AI-Readiness Index is developed and tested for Indian banks, employing sixteen indicators divided into four categories: governance and oversight, risk management, capability and adoption, and transparency and ethics. Each indicator is assigned a score from 0 to 2 according to the actual information that the bank provides in its FY2025–26 annual report. Fifteen listed banks were assessed in this manner—five being public-sector and ten private-sector—resulting in an overall score out of 100. HDFC Bank achieves the highest score at 90.6 and Yes Bank comes second at 84.4; in both cases these are the only two banks that explicitly link their AI policies to the RBI's Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of AI (FREE-AI), which was issued in August 2025. SBI is next at 81.3. Canara Bank is at the lowest level with a score of 25.0. The index is statistically robust (with a Cronbach's alpha of 0.87) and the ranking remains almost unchanged when different weighting methods are applied—whether equal weights, entropy weights or TOPSIS all show very similar results. A k-means clustering method divides the banks into three broad groups that correspond to the categories of adopters as described by the Diffusion of Innovation theory: Leaders, Followers and Laggards. On average private banks score higher than public-sector banks (61.3 compared to 48.8), although with only five public-sector banks in the sample this difference does not reach statistical significance. The correlations between the index and financial-risk indicators—NPAs, ROA, CRAR—are weak and inconclusive, and the paper states this clearly rather than presenting the figures in a more favourable light. What the study provides is a practical, regulator-linked method of measuring AI governance readiness, directly aligned with the structure of FREE-AI, thus addressing a gap that is not covered by any of the studies reviewed here: an index of this kind, designed for Indian banks, tested against real risk outcomes after the FREE-AI framework had been introduced.

papers.title: Overview of Trends and Challenges in Modern Education
papers.authors: Surekha Lanka
papers.abstract: The growth of digital technology and society has resulted in a new type of education, which is very different from the classical one. In this review, an attempt will be made to investigate modern education and to reveal its main differences from classical methods. The review analyses modern tendencies and innovations in education based on technologies like Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), metaverse education, robotics, and intelligent systems. The educational capacity of these technologies is enormous; it includes VR education, reality education, interactive technologies, personalized approaches, AI mentoring, IoT monitoring and support, metaverse education, and modern competency development. Nevertheless, the bipolar approach to this problem is quite wrong because modern education must not reject classical methods and technologies entirely. This review tries to find the best solutions for integrating innovative strategies and classical education.

papers.title: Intelligent Academic Software: Transforming Higher Education through AI-Driven Learning Ecosystems
papers.authors: Sandeep Hanumant Bhokare, Siddhant kumar Vasantrao Wadmare
papers.journal: London Journal of Research In Computer Science and Technology
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of higher education has accelerated with the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies into academic software systems. Intelligent Academic Software (IAS) represents a paradigm shift from static learning management systems toward dynamic, data-driven learning ecosystems capable of personalization, predictive analytics, automated assessment, and institutional decision support. This study proposes a comprehensive AI-driven learning ecosystem model integrating adaptive learning engines, intelligent tutoring systems, predictive analytics modules, and administrative automation frameworks. A multi-institutional dataset comprising 1,200 student records was analyzed using supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms to evaluate performance prediction, engagement analytics, and risk detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate improved academic performance forecasting (92% accuracy), enhanced learner engagement, and optimized resource allocation. The study contributes to AI-enabled higher education transformation by presenting a scalable intelligent software architecture aligned with ethical AI governance and institutional digital strategies.

papers.title: Large Language Model Agents for Autonomous Scientific Research: A Lifecycle Survey of Methods, Systems, Benchmarks, and Risks
papers.authors: Yifan Gao (2344960), Lu Yu, Haoyue Li
papers.abstract: Large language models have moved from passive text generators to autonomous agents that plan, use tools, and act across the scientific research process. A fast-growing body of work now targets every stage of that process, from literature search and hypothesis generation through experiment code, wet-lab automation, manuscript writing, and peer review, together with discipline-specific agents for chemistry, biology, materials, medicine, and mathematics and a large family of benchmarks built to measure them. This review combines a systematic search with a narrative synthesis. A protocol-driven search of arXiv, Semantic Scholar, bioRxiv, and fourteen conference proceedings, run to 30 May 2026, retrieved 2928 records, of which 883 met the eligibility criteria and were coded, and 253 were analysed in depth. We organize that literature along the scientific research lifecycle and cross-cut it by four design axes, namely agent architecture, learning mechanism, autonomy level, and validation regime, and we report the publication status and evidence level of every claim we rely on. The field has matured unevenly. Retrieval-grounded deep research and machine learning engineering show repeatable gains on peer-reviewed benchmarks, whereas open-ended ideation, end-to-end discovery, and trustworthy reporting remain fragile. Realistic benchmarks report success rates between one sixth and one third, with a Kaggle bronze medal on 16.9 percent of engineering competitions, a best replication score of 21.0 percent across 20 published papers, 32.4 percent of scientific coding tasks solved, and 31.5 percent accuracy on memorization-resistant equation discovery. On a three-paper subset of the replication benchmark, an o1 agent scores 26.6 percent against 41.4 percent for machine learning PhDs. Closed-loop discovery systems report results confirmed in the wet lab, and all three such systems in our master comparison remain preprints, which places those claims on weaker evidential footing than the benchmark results. A reliability gap runs through the whole lifecycle, as agents that retrieve and write fluently still fabricate results, miscite sources, and overstate confidence. We contribute a documented search and coding protocol with the full coded corpus made available, a unified taxonomy, a master comparison of systems, a structured account of benchmarks and metrics, and a risk-to-mitigation map, and we close with a maturity assessment and a research roadmap for safe and verifiable autonomous science.

papers.title: Multi-Level Transformations Induced by GenAI in Instructional Design: A Thematic Analysis of a Reddit Forum
papers.authors: Kadir Kozan, Subhasree Sengupta, Sewon Joo, Lutfi Ozturk
papers.abstract: Research on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) integration into instructional design practice has been expanding rapidly; however, its effects on the instructional design profession remain underexplored. To this end, this study examines instructional designers’ perceptions about how GenAI is reshaping the instructional design professional landscape and how online communities engage them in sharing those perceptions. Using a mixed-methods data analysis method including automatic text mining and human verification, a large data set obtained from an online community of instructional designers on Reddit was analyzed thematically. Results revealed three key changes at professional, organizational, and individual levels, and the mechanisms shaping instructional designers’ engagement in their online community. Namely, GenAI has already started to reshape the instructional design landscape through a mixed set of changes including transformations, adaptations and reconfigurations, and an online community can function as an informal community of practice for instructional designers to collectively share experiential wisdom and necessary competencies to successfully navigate the emergent transitions. This study contributes by uncovering the changes happening in instructional design due to GenAI and how informal online channels can work as communities of practice that are distributed, asynchronous, on-demand knowledge exchange avenues, thus increasing instructional designers’ awareness and collective preparedness.

papers.title: Comparison of Sleep Quality Across Different Sagittal Skeletal Patterns in Orthodontic Patients
papers.authors: Chanistha Sirichan, Narissaporn Chaiprakit, Siripatra Patchanee
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sagittal skeletal patterns are associated with upper airway dimensions, which may influence breathing during sleep and potentially relate to sleep quality. We hypothesized that global Thai-Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (Thai-PSQI) scores would differ among skeletal Class I (Sk-I), Class II (Sk-II), and Class III (Sk-III) groups. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at the Department of Orthodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Thammasat University, from June 2023 to March 2024. Ninety-three patients aged 18–50 years presenting to initiate orthodontic treatment were classified by ANB angle as Sk-I (0.5–5.1°), Sk-II (>5.1°), or Sk-III (<0.5°), with 31 participants per group. Sleep quality was assessed using the Thai-PSQI; scores > 5 indicated poor sleep quality. Sex, age, and BMI were analyzed as demographic variables. Results: Mean global PSQI scores were 6.42 ± 2.71, 6.68 ± 3.39, and 6.26 ± 2.46 for Sk-I, Sk-II, and Sk-III, respectively. Global PSQI scores did not differ significantly among skeletal groups (H = 0.024, p = 0.988, ε2 < 0.001). Overall, 55.9% of participants were poor sleepers, and the distribution of good and poor sleepers did not differ among groups (χ2 = 1.134, p = 0.567, Cramer’s V = 0.110). No significant associations were observed between global PSQI and sex, age, or BMI (p = 0.279, 0.848, and 0.948, respectively). Conclusions: No statistically significant differences in subjective sleep quality were identified among the three sagittal skeletal groups in this sample.

papers.title: Mapping the Intellectual and Thematic Evolution of L2 Willingness to Communicate Research: A Bibliometric Analysis
papers.authors: Xiao Zhu, Nur Ehsan Mohd Said, Chairozila Mohd Shamsudin
papers.abstract: Willingness to communicate (WTC) in a second language (L2) is a central construct in second language acquisition (SLA), yet the intellectual structure and thematic development of the field remain insufficiently mapped. This study provides a bibliometric analysis of 477 English-language L2 WTC records indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) from 1996 to 31 July 2025. Using CiteSpace (6.4.R1), the study examines publication trends, collaboration networks, co-citation structures, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, and research bursts. The findings show sustained growth in L2 WTC research and a knowledge base anchored in established work on psychological and affective dimensions, including anxiety, motivation, attitudes, confidence, and emotions. Collaboration networks indicate that research activity is concentrated among a relatively limited set of countries and institutions, while co-citation analysis reveals a highly structured intellectual base centered on influential work in WTC, emotions, classroom environments, and related psychological and contextual dimensions. Keyword and temporal analyses further show thematic diversification, with established concerns increasingly accompanied by classroom context, positive psychology, out-of-class communication, and emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-related research. In particular, positive psychology and out-of-class communication appear among the recent burst terms, whereas AI literacy appears as the label of a recent keyword cluster; these recent patterns should be interpreted cautiously because the 2025 data are incomplete. Overall, the findings suggest continued expansion of the L2 WTC research agenda rather than a wholesale replacement of established perspectives, providing an updated map of the field’s intellectual foundations and thematic development and identifying directions for future empirical research.

papers.title: AdaSwitch3D: Reliability-Aware Human-in-the-Loop Artificial Intelligence for Breast Tumor Segmentation in Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI Across Unseen Centers
papers.authors: Easa Alalwany, Bader Alsharif
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning models for breast tumor segmentation in dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) often lose accuracy at centers that did not contribute training data. We investigated whether case-wise routing between two low-resource adapted models, combined with an uncertainty-based review-prioritization signal, behaves consistently under severe cross-center domain shift. Methods: Using the four public collections of the MAMA-MIA dataset (DUKE, ISPY1, ISPY2, NACT; 1231 cases), we performed four-fold leave-one-center-out experiments in which each held-out center contributed only five labeled cases and a pool of unlabeled scans. We compared source-only transfer, five-shot fine-tuning, and teacher–student self-training with AdaSwitch3D, which routes each case between the two adapted branches using 17 label-free features and produces a heuristic review-prioritization signal. The complete pipeline—data splits, five-shot selection, training, adaptation, router construction, and referral calibration—was repeated with five random seeds, and each seed was evaluated once on 80 untouched test cases (400 seed-specific test observations). Results: Across five independent repetitions, mean Dice was 0.325 ± 0.051 for source-only transfer, 0.353 ± 0.052 for five-shot fine-tuning, 0.372 ± 0.047 for teacher–student adaptation, and 0.377 ± 0.057 for AdaSwitch3D; a validation-selected per-center strategy reached 0.376 ± 0.044. AdaSwitch3D exceeded five-shot fine-tuning in all five seeds and teacher–student adaptation in four, but the difference between AdaSwitch3D and teacher–student adaptation was small (mean +0.005) and varied by seed, while inference required both branches (approximately twice the single-model time). Observed test referral rates ranged from 23.8% to 56.3% against a 20% validation target, and low-Dice (<0.20) failure capture ranged from 21.7% to 71.8%. In the prespecified case-level analysis of seed 42, AdaSwitch3D improved on source-only transfer and five-shot fine-tuning (Holm-adjusted p=0.021 for each), whereas the comparison with teacher–student adaptation did not provide evidence of a difference (Holm-adjusted p=0.508). Conclusions: Absolute segmentation accuracy remained low, the incremental benefit of case-wise routing over teacher–student adaptation was small and seed-dependent, and referral behavior was unstable across repetitions. The principal finding is therefore that cross-center adaptation, case-wise model selection, and heuristic referral remain sensitive under limited target supervision. AdaSwitch3D should be interpreted as an exploratory case study of these challenges rather than as a clinically validated segmentation or referral system.

papers.title: Operational Architectures for Hybrid AI-Based Network Intrusion Detection: A Critical Review and Multi-Axial Taxonomy
papers.authors: Alaa Haddad, Sarvesh August Wajs, Mohamed Hadi Habaebi, Mohammed Abdulla Salim Al Husaini
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is widely used in network intrusion detection, but evidence regarding operational architecture remains fragmented across model families, fusion patterns, deployment environments, and evaluation practices. We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review of secondary AI-NIDS reviews published from 1 January 2020 to 22 September 2026. OpenAlex and arXiv were searched on 22 September 2026; deterministic DOI/title deduplication and prespecified text rules preceded title/abstract screening, and a single reviewer assessed the retrieved full texts. Review-level limitations were appraised across eligibility, search reproducibility, selection/data collection, evidence traceability, and synthesis appropriateness; no aggregate quality score or statistical pooling was used. Of 8519 identified records, 1091 duplicates and 2256 automatically ineligible records were removed, 5172 records were screened, 101 reports were sought, 25 full texts were assessed, and 22 reviews were included. The synthesis supports a five-axis taxonomy spanning observation, AI intelligence, fusion, deployment, and trust/operations, but also shows weak search reproducibility in 12 of 22 included reviews and absent selection transparency in 15 of 22. The findings provide a bounded architectural framework rather than a universal performance ranking. Limitations include open-index coverage, 76 unretrieved reports, single-reviewer assessment, and the use of primary studies only as separate illustrative validation sources. The review was not prospectively registered; a revision-stage protocol was frozen before the new search, and its amendment is reported. A worked five-axis example, a decision-level contrast between sequential and hierarchical integration, appraisal-weighted confidence statements, and proposed evaluation criteria for each open challenge make the framework directly usable for design and assessment.

papers.title: Trust and Perceived Usefulness in GenAI-Assisted Assessment Adoption Among Design Teachers in Higher Education: Distinct Judgments and Their Associations with Behavioral Intention
papers.authors: Jie Wang, Yuri Sim
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly being considered for assessment-related work, but educators need to judge whether it is reliable enough to serve as professional input and whether it is useful enough to justify its incorporation into assessment practice. This study examined whether trust (TR) and perceived usefulness (PU) are empirically distinct judgments and whether their independent associations with behavioral intention (BI) to use GenAI for assessment differ. Cross-sectional survey data from 352 design teachers at universities and higher vocational colleges in China were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis, covariance-based structural equation modeling, comparisons of alternative structural specifications, and 5000-sample bootstrap tests. Measurement evidence supported treating TR and PU as separate latent judgments. In the correlated parallel model (Model C2), PU was positively associated with BI, whereas the TR–BI association was nonsignificant; a formal test of the unstandardized path coefficients showed that the PU–BI coefficient was significantly larger than the TR–BI coefficient. Because Model C2 was structurally just-identified, its global fit was not interpreted as independent evidence of structural robustness. Sensitivity analyses accounting for prior GenAI-assisted assessment use yielded the same substantive path pattern. The findings concern acceptance judgments and behavioral intention rather than actual adoption or assessment outcomes. They suggest that reliability and perceived task value are related but nonredundant considerations when educators consider GenAI support while retaining final assessment responsibility.

papers.title: Beyond Task Delegation: Reconceptualising Instructional Design to Measure Competence in the Age of Generative AI
papers.authors: Jasmine Fernandez
papers.journal: Proceedings of The World Conference on Teaching and Education
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) has invalidated traditional content-recall assessments, acting as a catalyst for a systemic transition towards Competence-Based Education (CBE). This paper contends that the role of faculty must transcend content dissemination, focusing instead on observable human competencies associated with Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning (SRL). Drawing upon Behaviourism and Bloom's Taxonomy, we propose the Reverse-Flipped Model. This conceptual framework, supported by illustrative disciplinary cases in History, Computer Science, Digital Photography, and Composition, utilises generative tools for low-stakes production to repurpose pedagogical time for high-stakes human intervention. Prompt Literacy is conceptualised as an observable instructional competency that externalises planning, monitoring, evaluation, and strategic intervention behaviours during human-AI collaboration. Implementation necessitates the use of Analytic Rubrics and Automated Process Portfolios (APP) to document observable demonstrations of Prompt Literacy and strategic engagement over final product quality. The framework addresses institutional sustainability and the moral imperative of digital equity. The primary contribution of this framework is a structural shift that enhances assessment validity by ensuring student success is defined by verifiable mastery of human-led strategic intervention rather than machine-generated output.

papers.title: Educational Potential of AI-generated Songs in English Language Teaching (ELT)
papers.authors: Anita Majorszki
papers.journal: Central European Library and Information Science Review Közép-európai Könyvtár- és Információtudományi Szemle
papers.abstract: Songs have long been recognised as beneficial tools in the English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classroom (Adnyani, Dewi, 2020; Kumar et al., 2022). However, a recurring challenge occurs in the selection of appropriate songs. Educators often struggle to find a piece of music that features grammatically correct lyrics, possesses catchy melodies, and has a convincing topic at the same time. Moreover, some songs contain the desired structures and phrases, only a few times throughout their lyrics. Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence (e.g. SunoAI, iLoveSong.ai) offer promising solutions to these challenges by enabling the creation of customised and personalised songs. With the help of AI assistance, teachers and learners can generate materials that support autonomy and cater to specific linguistic goals. This article presents the theoretical and practical concepts of integrating AI-generated songs into the EFL classrooms.

papers.title: AI-Based Cancer Drug Response Prediction: A Machine Learning Ensemble for Lung Cancer Pharmacogenomic Classification
papers.authors: Kavin Prabu P, Durairaj Mohanapriya, L. Thara
papers.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology
papers.abstract: Effectiveness of anticancer drug varies among various types of cancers so understanding their response towards these medications is essential. The paper describes an algorithm to classify drug response patterns from the lung cancer subset of GDSC2 data set through machine learning techniques. Continuous LN_IC50 response values are classified as sensitive and resistant based on predetermined cut-off points for creating a balanced dataset for modeling purposes. Eight out of nine numbers are obtained by drugs, cells lines targets pathways related responses while selecting them via selectkbest method through ANOVA Ftest. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest and XGBoost models were trained and evaluated on a held-out test set of 6,404 samples from an unbalanced dataset containing 32,018 records. Test accuracy of these models was between 92.61% and 92.96%, whereas their ROC-AUC value ranged from 0.978 to 0.981. Integrated with a Django based research tool by means of an algorithm that combines predictions via vote for producing outputs from this system. This device is meant solely to serve as an educational tool; it cannot be used by patients for self-diagnosis, healthcare decisions, or prescription of medications.

papers.title: A THREE-COMPONENT MODEL OF SYNERGISTIC CARCINOGENESIS IN WARTIME: POSSIBLE CHEMICAL, RADIATION, AND STRESS-INDUCED MOLECULAR MECHANISMS
papers.authors: Yurii V. Dumanskyi, Ye. Kyrylenko, Sergiy V. Ziablitsev, Sergii V. Konovalenko
papers.abstract: Introduction. The armed invasion of Ukraine (since February 2022) has caused an unprecedented convergence of three oncogenic factors: chemical contamination from missile and drone strikes, the radiation legacy of the 1986 Chornobyl catastrophe, and mass chronic psychological stress among civilians and military personnel. While each factor is individually well-studied, their pathophysiological interaction at the molecular level remains unexplored. Aim. To conduct a pathophysiological analysis of the molecular mechanisms of three-component synergistic carcinogenesis. Materials and methods. A narrative review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases (1986–2026). A total of 214 publications were identified. Results. Four molecular convergence nodes were identified: (1) glucocorticoid receptor (GR)/aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) competition for AhR nuclear translocator (ARNT) and CBP/p300 – a bidirectional molecular bridge between stress-induced and chemical carcinogenesis that blocks apoptosis regardless of the predominant ligand; (2) triple damage to TP53 – structural (radiation-induced double-strand break (DSB) translocations), functional (benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (BPDE) adducts at codons 157/248/273), and transcriptional (GR-Hdm2-mediated p53 degradation in the nucleus); (3) competitive depletion of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA)/replication protein A (RPA) among homologous recombination (HR), nucleotide excision repair (NER), and base excision repair (BER) pathways; (4) synergistic natural killer (NK)-surveillance blockade through additive immunosuppression from dioxins, age-related NK involution, and cortisol. Conclusions. Three-component synergism is multiplicative: the expected relative risk of malignancy for the post-Chornobyl cohort may substantially exceed the risk associated with each individual component (conceptual estimate requiring prospective epidemiological verification). A peak increase in cancer incidence is projected for 2030–2035 in the post-Chornobyl cohort and for 2032–2038 in the general population. The model is conceptual and requires prospective verification in cohort studies.

papers.title: MODERN MEDICAL EDUCATION: PEDAGOGICAL TRENDS AND HEALTH OF PARTICIPANTS OF THE EDUCATIONAL PROCESS
papers.authors: N. I. Zavgorodnia, Anastasiia Horetska, Igor Zavgorodnii, S.P. Hlabets
papers.abstract: Introduction. The modern system of medical education is undergoing active transformation under the influence of globalization, rapid development of medical technologies, and the digitalization of the educational process. The implementation of innovative approaches, including simulation-based learning, artificial intelligence technologies, as well as virtual and augmented reality, contributes to improving the effectiveness of training medical professionals. At the same time, the intensification of the educational process and the digitalization of the learning environment may affect the psycho-emotional state and health of participants in the educational process, which determines the need to analyze current pedagogical trends in medical education. Aim. To analyze modern pedagogical trends in medical education and determine their impact on learning effectiveness and the health of participants in the educational process. Materials and methods. An analytical review of scientific publications by domestic and foreign authors devoted to the development of medical education, the implementation of digital technologies in the educational process, and studies examining the influence of the educational environment on the psycho-emotional state of students and teachers was conducted. Methods of system analysis, generalization, and comparison of the results of contemporary scientific research were used. Results. It was established that the integration of innovative educational technologies contributes to improving the quality of training of medical professionals, the development of clinical thinking, and the formation of practical skills. At the same time, the increasing academic workload, the digital intensity of the educational process, and the need for continuous professional development may lead to higher levels of stress, emotional exhaustion, and professional burnout among participants in the educational process. Conclusions. Modern medical education requires a balanced combination of innovative pedagogical technologies and approaches aimed at preserving the mental and physical health of participants in the educational process. A promising direction is the development of health-preserving educational strategies, optimization of academic workload, and the implementation of trauma-informed approaches in the system of medical education.

papers.title: Comparative assessment of the colonic microbiota composition in adolescents with obesity and normal body weight
papers.authors: О. А. Логачева, Natalia Yu. Filina, Nina Viktorovna Bolotova, Kseniya A. Cherednikova, Timofey E. Pylaev, Nataliya V. Nikolaeva
papers.journal: Бюллетень Восточно-Сибирского научного центра Сибирского отделения Российской академии медицинских наук
papers.abstract: Introduction. Obesity in adolescents is a global medical and social problem associated with a progressive increase in incidence. The role of structural changes in the colonic microbial community in the pathogenesis of exogenous-constitutional obesity in adolescents remains insufficiently studied, and data on characteristic taxonomic alterations are contradictory. Aim. To study the characteristics of the qualitative and quantitative composition of the colonic microbiota in adolescents with obesity and normal body weight. Materials and methods. A cross-sectional comparative study was conducted. The main group consisted of 20 adolescents aged 12–17 years with obesity (BMI SDS ≥ +2.0), and the control group consisted of 20 adolescents with normal body weight. The taxonomic composition of the microbiota was examined by real-time PCR using the “Colonoflor-16” test system. Statistical analysis was performed using the Mann – Whitney and Fisher tests. Results. Compared to the control group, changes in the taxonomic composition of the microbiota in adolescents with obesity were characterized by a significant decrease in total bacterial mass and the abundance of key symbionts, including Bifidobacterium spp. A decrease in the level of Lactobacillus spp. was observed in both study groups without statistically significant intergroup differences. A deficiency of butyrate producers and key participants in fiber fermentation was identified, including Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Eubacterium rectale, and Akkermansia muciniphila, as well as a trend toward a decrease in Roseburia inulinivorans, Ruminococcus spp., Prevotella spp., and Blautia spp. Concurrently, an increase was recorded in the abundance of Bacteroides spp., opportunistic pathogens (Enterobacter spp., Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Enterococcus spp.), and the Bacteroides spp. / Faecalibacterium prausnitzii ratio. In the main group of adolescents, Clostridium difficile, Clostridium perfringens, Staphylococcus aureus, Acinetobacter spp., and fungi of the genus Candida were detected. Conclusion. Adolescents with obesity exhibit a specific pro-inflammatory profile of the colonic microbiota, characterized by depletion of symbionts, deficiency of butyrate producers, and overgrowth of opportunistic taxa. The obtained data identify potential targets for personalized microbiome correction in the comprehensive therapy of obesity.

papers.title: Neurological manifestations in women with post-COVID syndrome
papers.authors: Elena V. Katamanova, Natalya V. Slivnitsyna, Л. С. Васильева, Русанова Дина Владимировна, Elena N. Korchuganova, О. И. Шевченко, Оleg L. Lakhman
papers.journal: Бюллетень Восточно-Сибирского научного центра Сибирского отделения Российской академии медицинских наук
papers.abstract: Post-COVID syndrome (PCS) is accompanied by neurological manifestations. The routes of virus penetration and the pathogenetic mechanisms triggered by COVID-19 in the infected body play an important role. Aim. To provide a clinical and neurophysiological description of the neurological manifestations of post-COVID syndrome. Methods. A total of 225 women with PCS were examined. Clinical, neurophysiological (electroencephalography, electroneuromyography), and neuropsychological examinations were performed. Results. The main clinical syndrome was asthenia (100 % of cases); cognitive and emotional-volitional disorders were recorded (70.8 % and 36.2 %, respectively). Hyposmia was observed (55 %), distorted perception of odors (parosmia) was recorded in 20 % of cases, hyperosmia and anosmia – in 5 %, and 15 % of the examined patients had no impairment of smell. In patients with PCS, distal polyneuropathy was diagnosed in 11.1 % of cases, confirmed by electroneuromyography. According to the electroencephalogram (EEG), a change in coherence in the alpha-band was revealed. An increase in interhemispheric connections in the temporal regions was observed, and coherence in the frontal areas decreased compared to normal values. Neuropsychological testing showed a decrease in cognitive functions, manifested in changes in neuropsychological indicators reflecting impairments in short-term (auditory-verbal) and long-term memory, and reciprocal coordination. Conclusion. The main clinical manifestations of PCS in women are asthenia of varying severity, cognitive and emotional-volitional disorders with an anxiety-depressive component, disorders of sensory functions (smell and taste), and polyneuropathy of the extremities. The study revealed impaired indicators reflecting the state of shortterm (auditory-verbal) and long-term memory, as well as reciprocal coordination.

papers.title: Does generative-ai feedback in formative assessment improve higher-order thinking: motivational pathways in vocational safety education
papers.authors: Waskito Waskito, Tri Juliantika, Refdinal Refdinal, Yeka Hendriyani
papers.abstract: Occupational health and safety (OHS) education in vocational high schools requires higher-order thinking skills (HOTS), yet formative assessment is often limited by delayed teacher feedback. This study examined whether generative AI-supported formative assessment using ChatGPT and Gemini improved HOTS and learning motivation compared with conventional teacher-led assessment, and explored the relationship between perceptions of AI-assisted assessment, motivation, and HOTS. A posttest-only nonequivalent control group quasi-experimental design involved 60 Grade X Machining Engineering students at SMK Negeri 1 Padang, divided into two intact classes of 30 students each. HOTS was measured using a 20-item reasoned multiple-choice test covering Bloom’s cognitive levels C4–C6, while motivation and perceptions of AI-assisted assessment were measured using validated questionnaires. Independent-samples t-tests were used for the primary analysis, followed by exploratory partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) in the experimental group. No significant differences were found between the AI-assisted and conventional assessment groups in HOTS scores (81.73 vs. 80.87, p = .417, d = 0.21) or motivation (54.03 vs. 54.83, p = .497, d = −0.18). Within the experimental group, perceptions of AI-assisted assessment were positively associated with motivation (β = 0.743, p < .001), and motivation was positively associated with HOTS (β = 0.476, p = .023). Although the indirect effect was statistically significant (β = 0.354, p = .042), its bias-corrected confidence interval included zero, making the mediation evidence inconclusive. These findings do not demonstrate that AI-assisted formative assessment improves HOTS or motivation beyond conventional teacher feedback. However, the observed motivational relationships warrant further investigation using larger samples, baseline measurements, and longer interventions.

papers.title: Acceptance of AI-based human resource practices: Sectoral differences between technology-intensive and traditional industries
papers.authors: Selma Kalkavan
papers.abstract: This study examines employee acceptance of AI-based human resource management practices in technology-intensive and traditional sectors. Data were collected from 360 employees, with 60 participants from each of six sectors. Biotechnology, information technology, and manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products formed the technology-intensive group, while retail, textiles, and hotels formed the traditional group. Acceptance was evaluated across recruitment, performance appraisal, training planning, and talent management. The explanatory variables were perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust in AI, perceived algorithmic fairness and transparency, and loss of human touch. The subgroup regressions show that usefulness, ease of use, and trust positively predict acceptance in technology-intensive sectors. In traditional sectors, fairness and transparency positively predict acceptance, while loss of human touch negatively predicts acceptance. Five significant interactions identify specific differences between sector groups. The positive association of fairness and transparency with acceptance is stronger in traditional sectors for recruitment and performance appraisal, and the negative association of loss of human touch is stronger in traditional sectors for recruitment. The positive association of trust is stronger in technology-intensive sectors for training planning, while that of usefulness is stronger in technology-intensive sectors for talent management. Acceptance is descriptively higher in training planning and talent management than in recruitment and performance appraisal. These findings show that employee evaluations of AI-based HR practices vary by sector group and HR function, supporting attention to usefulness, trust, fairness, and human involvement in the particular functions where their associations with acceptance differ.

papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Model Localization for Clinical Psychology: Predicting Anxiety and Depression Scores in a Russian Student Sample
papers.authors: Tatyana V. Bukina, Nikita M. Smirnov, Vladimir Maksimenko, K. O. Karpov, Yurii E. Skalin, Marina V. Khramova, Semen Kurkin, Alexander E. Hramov
papers.abstract: Aim. To evaluate the suitability of large language models (LLMs), deployed in a closed-loop environment, for predicting anxiety and depression scores on the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) in a sample of Russian students. Materials and methods. The empirical dataset consisted of de-identified responses from 946 first-year university students (669 female, 277 male) in Russia to 14 HADS items. For 11 models (DeepSeek-R1-32B, Qwen3-32B, T-pro-2.0/2.1, YandexGPT- 8B, GigaChat-20B, and others) deployed locally on GPUs, response probability distributions were extracted from token log probabilities. The experimental design included 5 prompt groups (textual instructions for the model), 2 presentation formats (structured dialogue and unstructured text), and 4 wording variations. Model-generated and empirical distributions were compared using Wasserstein distance (W); expected HADS subscale scores were additionally calculated. Results. T DeepSeek-R1-32B demonstrated the best accuracy in reproducing distributions (W = 0.293); however, it consistently underestimated expected anxiety scores (5.6 vs. 7.7). The most accurate expected anxiety scores were produced by YandexGPTpretrain (7.2) and T-pro-2.0 (7.1). Model selection explained 47% of metric variance; persona detail and respondent sex had no significant effect (p > 0.05). The depression subscale was reproduced less accurately than the anxiety subscale. Conclusions. Scores are robust to prompt variations: the level of detail in the persona description and the specific wording do not affect the outcome—a minimal description of the respondent suffices. Models trained in English favor English-language prompts, whereas for Russian-language models, language preferences are determined by the underlying architecture. The hypothesis regarding a systematic advantage for Russian-language models was not confirmed: quality is determined by domain adaptation rather than language. Practical application requires validation through experiments involving human subjects. The models do not replace clinical assessment by a specialist.

papers.title: Application of convolutional neural networks based on the Kolmogorov–Arnold architecture with a wavelet activation function for identifying cognitive brain states using EEG data
papers.authors: Дедков Владимир Георгиевич, Denis A. Andrikov
papers.abstract: Background. Analyzing cognitive states using electroencephalography (EEG) is a key task for brain-computer interfaces. Despite the success of deep learning methods, classical convolutional neural networks (CNNs) face significant limitations when processing non-stationary EEG signals: they struggle to adapt to local time-frequency features, and their decisions are difficult to interpret. Integrating the Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) architecture with wavelet transformations opens up new possibilities for improving the accuracy and interpretability of EEG analysis models by replacing linear weights with learnable nonlinear functions. Aim. To study the impact of replacing conventional convolutional layers with layers based on the Kolmogorov–Arnold architecture utilizing various wavelet activation functions on the quality of identifying cognitive states of varying complexity. Methods. Data from the open-access COG-BCI dataset were used, comprising recordings from 29 participants performing cognitive tasks N-Back (working memory) and MATB-II (multitasking). The original FFCLNetEEG architecture was modified by replacing CNN layers with KAN and WavKAN convolutional layers using various wavelets (Gabor, DOG, Mexican Hat, Morlet, Meyer, Shannon). Evaluation was performed using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, and Specificity metrics with pairwise Wilcoxon tests with Bonferroni correction (p < 0,05). Results. In the N-Back task, the FFCLNetEEG-WavKAN-DOG model showed the best performance achieving a mean accuracy of 0.790±0.059; this significantly outperformed FFCLNetEEG-KAN, FFCLNetEEG-WavKAN-Meyer and FFCLNetEEG-WavKAN-Morlet (p < 0,001 after correction). In the MATB-II task, the best performance was achieved by the FFCLNetEEGWavKAN-Gabor model performed best (mean accuracy 0.892±0.005). Analysis of three independent sessions showed high reproducibility of the results with correlation coefficients between sessions up to 0.653 for the best-performing models. Conclusion. Integrating the Kolmogorov–Arnold architecture with embedded wavelet functions enables a reliable improvement in the classification quality of cognitive states based on EEG data. The choice of the optimal wavelet depends on the type of cognitive task: DOG for working memory (N-Back) and Gabor for multitasking (MATB-II). The findings have practical implications for the development of neuroadaptive interfaces and systems for cognitive monitoring and rehabilitation.

papers.title: Open Pedagogy, Student-Created AI Literacy Resources, and Repository-Based Knowledge Sharing
papers.authors: Femi Arogundade
papers.abstract: Module Description This module combines open pedagogy, renewable assignments, reflective practice, AI literacy, collaborative learning, student-generated knowledge, peer review, open licensing, and repository-based dissemination, based on the Repositories of AI Literacy Resources (RAILR) concept. The module is primarily designed for undergraduate students, although it can be adapted for other educational levels depending on the instructor's teaching goals. It can be delivered as a standalone module, an elective, or with its learning activities incorporated into an existing course. The central purpose of the module is to move students beyond being consumers of AI literacy guidance resources to becoming creators. Through reflection on their own experiences of using generative AI tools, discussion with peers, collaborative resource development, peer review, and open dissemination, students can develop AI literacy resources that can benefit other learners. Instructors are not required to treat every activity as compulsory, except when implementing the module as a full course or an elective. Instead, instructors can select and adapt the activities according to their course objectives, teaching goals, available teaching time, student numbers, and preferred or feasible mode of delivery. Learning Outcomes By the end of this module, students should be able to: Explain the concept of open pedagogy and distinguish it from traditional approaches to teaching and learning. Explain the relationship between open pedagogy and renewable assignments. Differentiate between disposable and renewable assignments. Explain AI literacy Describe the importance of AI literacy for the responsible use of generative AI tools. Critically reflect on their own experiences using generative AI tools. Learn from the experiences of other students through collaborative activities. Transform personal and shared experiences into AI literacy resources. Collaboratively develop AI literacy resources suitable for open dissemination. Develop AI literacy resources for dissemination through Repositories of AI Literacy Resources (RAILR). Target Audience Level: Undergraduate Adaptable for other levels depending on instructors' teaching goals. Suitable as a standalone module or as an elective Module Outline This module is organised into the following sections: Section 1: Purpose of This Module Section 2: Open Pedagogy: From Disposable Assignments to Shared Knowledge Section 3: Learning from Experience: Why Students' Experiences with Generative AI Tools Matter Section 4: From Reflection to Resource Creation: Transforming Experience into AI Literacy Resources Section 5: Repository-Based Knowledge Sharing: Preserving and Disseminating Student-Created AI Literacy Resources in RAILR Section 6: Reflecting on Your AI Journey: Learning Through Personal Experience Section 7: Practical Learning Activities Practical Activity 1: My AI Journey Practical Activity 2: Learning from Others Practical Activity 3: Co-Creating an AI Literacy Resource Practical Activity 4: Peer Review, Improvement, and Dissemination Practical Activity 5: Complete the Appropriate RAILR Dissemination Agreement Practical Activity 6: Open Dissemination of AI Literacy Resources Section 8. Learning and Reading Resources Assessment Students will complete a series of reflective, collaborative, and resource-development activities. Depending on the instructor's implementation of the module, assessment may include: An individual reflective essay. Participation in collaborative group discussions. Development of a group AI literacy resource. Peer review of another group's AI literacy resource. Preparation of resources for dissemination through RAILR

papers.title: An Explainable Federated Vision–Language Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Automated Medical Report Generation Across Distributed Healthcare Institutions
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Automated generation of medical reports using AI can help speed up diagnosis and reduce doctor workload, but currently, the most efficient forms of automation use centralized training, which requires hospitals to share sensitive patient data. This raises concerns about the privacy and regulatory issues of sharing patient information to generate reports. In addition, clinicians have difficulty trusting AI-assisted diagnosis because the visionlanguage models used for automated report generation are not easily interpretable. To tackle these issues, an Explainable Federated Vision-Language Learning Framework (EFVLL) has been created to generate automated medical reports that preserve patient privacy through distributed healthcare institutions. Hospitals can use federated learning to build a collaborative global vision-language model without having to share raw patient information. The EFVLL framework also includes an explainable attention mechanism that will help clinicians understand how specific areas of the image and text are related to the report being generated, increasing the transparency and interpretability of automated reports. Further, the EFVLL will improve generalization across non-homogenous datasets and comply with data privacy and regulatory requirements. The EFVLL framework has been validated with multiple large standard datasets (e.g., RSNA), and therefore it is suitable for implementation and use in a distributed healthcare environment.

papers.title: Teaching Competency in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Review of Teachers’ Attitudes, Adaptability, and Professional Commitment
papers.authors: Pratima devi, Anjana sonker
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into in these aspects of educational environments has initiated more of a paradigm shift in pedagogical structural methodologies, assessment strategies, and the use of fundamental role of educators. This comprehensive review always seems to be examined the current state of teaching competency in the age of AI, focusing here on three pivotal dimensions: teachers' attitudes towards AI, their adaptability of such aspects in utilizing intelligent tools, and their professional commitment in an era of rapid technological disruption-based aspects. Drawing upon a more natured based synthesis of recent literature, we therefore explore how factors such as AI literacy, generative based AI competence, & as also AI-TPACK (Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge) influence here in the successful integration of AI into classrooms everywhere. The review in this aspects highlights that while educators here are increasingly by recognizing the potential of AI to more enhance personalized learning as well as administrative efficiency, there remain in this way to stay neutral significant barriers related to AI anxiety as also, ethical concerns, & most of all a lack of targeted based on professional development. Adaptability is conceptualized not merely as herein technical proficiency, but as a continuous pedagogical evolution requiring robust organizational support-based aspects. Furthermore, professional aspects of commitment in this nature always is analyzed through the lens of shifting teacher identities & the ethical imperative to foster critical thinking and human-centric values based through in AI-augmented learning environments. A prominent table-based data related structure is provided to synthesize the thematic findings, mapping core competencies and against professional development needs. The paper in this manner concludes with actionable recommendations for policymakers, teacher training programs, & future research directions to ensure that educators are adequately equipped here to navigate the complexities of AI in education.

papers.title: An Observational Study on the Effect of Aahar-Vidhi-Vidhana in Lifestyle Disorders with Special Reference to Obesity
papers.authors: Suman Singh, Vivek Ahlawat, Darshana .
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Obesity is a major lifestyle disorder and an emerging global public health concern associated with increased morbidity and reduced quality of life. In Ayurveda, obesity is described as Sthaulya, a SantarpanajanyaVyadhi resulting by improper or Faulty dietary habits, sedentary lifestyle and impaired metabolic functions. Among the dietary principles described in the classical texts, Aahar-Vidhi-Vidhana provides comprehensive guidelines regarding the proper method of food consumption to maintain health and prevent disease. However, adherence to these dietary principles has declined considerably in modern society, contributing to the increasing burden of obesity. Aim: To evaluate the effect of Aahar-Vidhi-Vidhana in lifestyle disorders with special reference to obesity. Materials and Methods: This observational study included 174 obese participants aged 20–40 years selected through stratified random sampling. Participants with a Body Mass Index (BMI) between >25 and <30 kg/m² were enrolled. Assessment was carried out using anthropometric parameters including BMI, waist circumference, waist-hip ratio, neck circumference, wrist circumference, body fat percentage, and lipid profile (HDL, LDL and triglycerides). Clinical evaluation was performed using the signs and symptoms of Sthaulya and adherence to the principles of Aahar-VidhiVidhana. The collected data were analyzed using appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical methods. Results: The study demonstrated a significant association between adherence to Aahar-Vidhi-Vidhana and improved anthropometric and metabolic parameters. Participants following the recommended dietary principles exhibited better BMI, body fat percentage, waist circumference, and lipid profile compared with those showing poor adherence. Compliance with proper dietary practices was also associated with reduced severity of the clinical manifestations of Sthaulya. Conclusion: The findings suggest that Aahar-Vidhi-Vidhana plays an important role in the prevention and management of obesity. Incorporating these classical Ayurvedic dietary guidelines into daily life may serve as an effective, economical, and sustainable lifestyle strategy for reducing obesity and improving metabolic health.

papers.title: Thyroid Dose Measurement and Radiation Protection in Computed Tomography: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence and Emerging Strategies
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Computed tomography (CT) is an essential diagnostic imaging modality, but its increasing utilization has raised concerns regarding radiation exposure to the thyroid gland, one of the most radiosensitive organs.Owing to its superficial anatomical location, the thyroid is frequently exposed during CT examinations of the head, neck, chest, and upper thorax, highlighting the importance of accurate dose assessment and effective radiation protection.Objective: To critically review current evidence on thyroid dose measurement techniques, radiation protection strategies, conventional and emerging thyroid shielding technologies, and future approaches for minimizing thyroid radiation exposure during CT imaging.Methods: A narrative review of peer-reviewed literature, clinical and phantom studies, review articles, and international radiation protection guidelines was conducted.Current evidence regarding thyroid dosimetry, CT dose optimization, shielding devices, advanced imaging technologies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted radiation protection was synthesized.Results: Thermoluminescent dosimeters, optically stimulated luminescence dosimeters, MOSFET detectors, anthropomorphic phantoms, and computational dosimetry remain the principal methods for thyroid dose assessment.Current evidence demonstrates that protocol optimization, automatic exposure control, iterative and deep-learning reconstruction, scan range optimization, and appropriate thyroid shielding can substantially reduce radiation exposure while maintaining diagnostic image quality.Emerging approaches, including patient-specific shielding, 3D-printed devices, composite shielding materials, and AI-guided dose optimization, show considerable potential for enhancing radiation safety.However, variability in dosimetry methods and shielding protocols limits comparison across studies.Conclusion: Standardized dosimetry, optimized CT protocols, evidence-based shielding, and continued development of affordable, innovative protection technologies are essential to minimize thyroid radiation exposure and improve patient safety during CT imaging.

papers.title: Educar trinitariamente el carácter frente a la inteligencia artificial en Latinoamérica (2021–2024)
papers.authors: Hernán Bressi
papers.journal: Revista de Educación Superior del Sur Global
papers.abstract: This study analyzes the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on higher education in Argentina, Colombia, and Mexico (2021–2024), evaluating inequalities in access, equity, and student well-being amid accelerated digitalization and artificial intelligence. A qualitative, documentary-analytical, and comparative methodology was employed, examining public policies and doctrinal sources through conceptual triangulation and hermeneutic-critical interpretation. Results reveal that technological adoption operated under a pragmatic-utilitarian and instrumental logic that weakened the pedagogical bond, lacked sufficient ethical accompaniment, and exacerbated structural gaps. The study concludes that overcoming this technocratic drift requires an alternative bioethical and personalist educational model with a Trinitarian foundation that restores the persons ontological dignity, character education through virtues, and transcendent relationality in university praxis.

papers.title: Cross-database validation and calibrated uncertainty for machine learning models of the shear capacity of FRP-strengthened RC beams
papers.authors: Sajjad Emad Rasheed, Hasan A. Zainy
papers.abstract: Abstract Machine learning models for the shear contribution of externally bonded fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) to reinforced concrete beams are validated almost exclusively on a random hold-out split of a single self-compiled database. Because such databases are assembled from a few dozen experimental programmes, each contributing several near-identical specimens, a random split leaves siblings of nearly every test specimen in the training set. This study provides a cross-database assessment of that practice. Two independently compiled databases (442 and 455 specimens) were harmonised into a provenance-traced dataset of 828 records from 167 programmes spanning 1992–2024, and six learners were evaluated under five regimes of increasing severity. For gradient boosting the coefficient of determination fell from 0.67 and 0.69 under random splitting to 0.39 and 0.22 under study-grouped validation, and to 0.21 under cross-database transfer. A control in which the same physical specimens were scored under each compilation in turn changed little (0.35 versus 0.37), showing that clustering by programme, not curation disagreement, is responsible. A hierarchical errors-invariables model attributes 38% of the residual variance to programme identity and delivers calibrated predictive intervals (91.8% coverage at a nominal 90%), which span a factor of about twelve. Design provisions remain less accurate than the fitted models, but the reported margin roughly halves under honest validation. A reporting protocol is proposed, requiring publication of the specimen-to-study mapping, validation grouped on it, disclosure of out-of-range evaluation cases, and reporting of interval coverage and a characteristic value.

papers.title: A Study On The Role Of Financial Literacy And Trust On Ai In Investment Decision Making Among Investors
papers.authors: S. Sahithya S. Sahithya
papers.journal: Journal of Advanced Research in Accounting and Finance Management
papers.abstract: During the last decade, artificial intelligence (AI) has gained traction as an information and recommendation generator for investments, but few studies have explored the relationship between financial literacy and trust in AI among the investors and how this trust influences investment decisions. This study explores the effects of FL on investment decision-making, the effects of trusting AI on investment decision-making, and the effects of selected (demographic and investment-related) characteristics on investment decision-making, such as investment experience. A quantitative survey-based research design was employed, which involved an instrument bearing a questionnaire of 25 five-point likerts comprising financial literacy, investment decision making, profit and loss appreciation, financial-literacy-driven understanding of AI, trust in AI, and financial experience of AI. Following the elimination of duplicate response items, 24 distinct responses were analysed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha, chi-square tests, one-way ANOVA and linear regression in Microsoft Excel. Financial literacy was moderate .None of the investment experiences had significant main effects, and none of the demographic characteristics had significant interaction effects with the relationship between trust in AI and decision-making on investments (p > .05). Based on the results, it appears that financial education is a better predictor of decision-making on investments among this group of investors than their reliance on AI. Small and homogenous sample makes the results preliminary and needs confirmation by further research with samples of greater size.

papers.title: Transformasi Kurikulum Merdeka: Dampak Integrasi Teknologi Dan Artificial Intelligence Dalam Pembelajaran
papers.authors: Bujang Firdaus, Naufal Vadillah, Marda Lena, Nadia Yendra, Zulfani Sesmiarni
papers.abstract: Educational transformation in the digital era requires a shift in the learning paradigm that emphasizes not only mastery of subject matter but also the development of students' creativity, critical thinking, digital literacy, and other essential competencies. The implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum provides greater flexibility for educational institutions and teachers to design learning activities according to students' needs while utilizing technological developments. Within this context, the integration of digital technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to accelerate the transformation of learning practices. This study aims to analyze the transformation of the Merdeka Curriculum through the integration of technology and Artificial Intelligence in learning, while identifying its impacts, opportunities, challenges, and implications for the roles of teachers and students' learning experiences. This research employs a qualitative approach using a literature review method. Data were obtained through the examination of books, scholarly journal articles, educational policy documents, and academic publications relevant to the Merdeka Curriculum, educational technology, and Artificial Intelligence in education. The data were analyzed using a descriptive-analytical approach by identifying, classifying, comparing, and synthesizing relevant findings from the literature. The results indicate that the integration of technology and AI can broaden access to learning resources, support more personalized and adaptive learning, assist teachers in developing instructional materials and assessments, and facilitate project-based learning and the development of twenty-first-century skills. Nevertheless, this transformation also presents several challenges, including unequal access to technology, disparities in teachers' digital competencies, the reliability of AI-generated information, data privacy concerns, potential student dependency on technology, and ethical issues related to academic integrity. Therefore, the integration of technology and AI within the Merdeka Curriculum should be positioned as a pedagogical instrument that supports educational objectives rather than as a replacement for teachers. Sustainable curriculum transformation requires strengthening teachers' digital and pedagogical competencies, establishing clear policies for the responsible use of AI, developing students' AI literacy, and implementing technology in ways that remain oriented toward human development and educational needs.

papers.title: ANALISIS DATA DALAM PENELITIAN PENDIDIKAN: PENDEKATAN KUANTITATIF, KUALITATIF, DAN MIXED METHODS
papers.authors: Dalvi, Zulfani Sesmiarni
papers.abstract: Data analysis is an important stage in educational research because it transforms raw data into meaningful information that can be used to answer research questions and formulate conclusions. This article discusses data analysis in educational research, including the meaning of data analysis, types of analysis, quantitative and qualitative analysis procedures, mixed-methods analysis, selection of analytical techniques, validity, interpretation, and the use of digital technology and artificial intelligence. This article uses a conceptual literature-review approach based on the submitted paper entitled Analisis Data dalam Penelitian Pendidikan and the methodological references contained in it. The discussion shows that data analysis cannot be separated from the research problem, objectives, research questions, and characteristics of the data. Quantitative analysis generally uses descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative analysis involves reading data, coding, categorizing, developing themes, and interpreting meaning. Mixed methods requires meaningful integration between quantitative and qualitative findings. The analysis also indicates that the use of statistical software and artificial intelligence can support researchers in processing and exploring data, but these technologies cannot replace the researcher's methodological judgment. Therefore, the quality of data analysis depends not merely on the complexity of the technique used, but on its suitability, transparency, validity, and the researcher's ability to interpret findings within the context of the research

papers.title: Beyond AI Adoption: Patient Safety Behavior and Clinical Reasoning in AI-Supported Clinical Clerkship Education - A Mixed Methods Study (Preprint)
papers.authors: Ferdi Antonio, Maria Maureen Ridwan, Janeta Odelia
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used during medical training, but research has focused largely on its adoption, perceptions, and educational use. Less is known about how AI-supported learning relates to clinical reasoning and safety-related behavior during clinical clerkship. OBJECTIVE This study examined factors associated with clinical reasoning, clinical decision confidence, and self-reported patient safety behavior in AI-supported clinical clerkship and explored selected findings within the clinical learning context. METHODS A sequential explanatory mixed-methods study was conducted across five private medical schools in Indonesia. Survey data from 217 clinical clerkship students were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Semi-structured interviews were subsequently conducted with 5 students, 3 clinical supervisors, and 3 medical directors and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS Ten of 12 hypothesized associations were supported. Clinical reasoning showed the largest direct association with self-reported patient safety behavior (β=.512; P<.001), followed by clinical decision confidence (β=.292; P<.001). AI over-reliance moderated the association between clinical decision confidence and patient safety behavior (β=.161; P=.012), but not the association between clinical reasoning and patient safety behavior (β=−.082; P=.119). Interviews described clinical reasoning as involving verification of AI-generated information, consideration of patient context and uncertainty, and consultation with supervisors. Participants also described the importance of supervision, patient safety learning, and institutional guidance for AI use. CONCLUSIONS In AI-supported clinical clerkship, self-reported patient safety behavior was associated with clinical reasoning and clinical decision confidence. The findings extend the focus beyond AI adoption by showing how AI use is situated within clinical reasoning, supervision, and the educational conditions of clinical training.

papers.title: Entrepreneurial Performance and Sustainable Entrepreneurship: A Review of Psychological, Individual, Organisational and Environmental Determinants
papers.authors: B Pathinettampadiyan, G Kingsly, H. Samuel Thavaraj
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Entrepreneurial performance is a multidimensional phenomenon that is influenced by the psychological attributes, individual competencies, organisational capabilities, financial resources, technological developments and environment. This is crucial for fostering entrepreneurship effectiveness and sustainable entrepreneurship development as these determinants are interrelated. The key factors affecting the performance of entrepreneurs are explored, focusing on emotional intelligence, entrepreneurial orientation, education, the digital transformation, financial capabilities, institutional support and sustainability. The review brings together literature on psychological and individual factors, entrepreneurial orientation and competency building, digital transformation and financial skills, as well as environmental, institutional and sustainable entrepreneurship. The reviewed studies have identified emotional intelligence as a salient psychological factor that facilitates emotional control, making decisions, coping with adversity, interpersonal relationships, leadership, and flexibility in the face of unpredictable business environments. The other factors that contribute to opportunity recognition, innovation, entrepreneurial intention, and venture development are entrepreneurial education, experiential learning, digital competencies and entrepreneurial orientation. Digital technologies and artificial intelligence, cloud computing, digital platforms and other technologies offer opportunities to enhance resource mobilisation, market access and organisational performance, but face issues of digital inequality, ethical governance and technological capacity. Entrepreneurial development and the ability to embrace sustainable business practices are also affected by financial literacy, access to finance, saving patterns and green finance.

papers.title: A Human-Centred Framework for Integrating Generative AI to Foster Critical Thinking, Learner Autonomy, and Cognitive Engagement in K-12 Education
papers.authors: Avula Chandrakala
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is increasingly used to explain concepts, support research, and provide individualized learning assistance. Its growing presence raises questions about independent reasoning, creativity, verification, and equitable access. This exploratory cross-sectional survey examined respondents? reported AI use, perceived educational benefits, and cognitive abilities they considered important to protect. A total of 66 respondents participated in this exploratory cross-sectional survey, which combined descriptive quantitative analysis with summaries of open-ended responses. Sixty-four respondents (97.0%) reported using ChatGPT or a similar AI assistant. Personalized learning was selected as an expected benefit by 50 (75.8%), while 48 (72.7%) identified understanding difficult concepts as an AI use or benefit. Critical thinking was the most frequently selected cognitive skill to protect (55; 83.3%), followed by creativity (52; 78.8%), problem-solving (48; 72.7%), and decision-making (47; 71.2%). Reported themes included individualized explanations, convenient information access, dependence concerns, verification, equity, and teacher guidance.
