papers.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, participants will explore how customized AI chatbots can be used to increase student engagement while also teaching students to question AI-generated information. The workshop centers on a role-playing game scenario in which students interact with a chatbot non-player character (NPC) that serves as a guide, informant, but one that sometimes provides incomplete, misleading, or invalid information. Rather than treating chatbot errors as failures, the activity uses them as opportunities for students to practice verification, source evaluation, metacognition, and discipline-specific reasoning. Participants will first experience a short version of the role-playing activity as students. They will then examine the underlying instructional design: how to define the chatbot’s role, set boundaries for its responses, embed intentional uncertainty, and build reflection prompts that move students from passive AI use toward active evaluation. The session will include guided discussion on academic integrity, transparency, and ethical use of AI in higher education. By the end of the session, participants will be able to identify at least one course concept that could be adapted into an AI-supported role-play activity, draft a basic chatbot role prompt, design a student-facing verification task, and describe how inaccurate AI output can be used productively to deepen engagement and GenAI fluency.

papers.title: Trust but Verify: Testing a Framework for AI Interrogation in Nursing Education
papers.authors: Michael Chamberlain
papers.journal: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)
papers.abstract: Generative AI produces fluent, confident output that is sometimes fabricated. Nursing students increasingly submit work built on sources that do not exist, or that exist and do not support the claims drawn from them. This session reports two semesters of classroom observation testing whether prompt design can address that problem. The hypothesis was that structuring student prompts to require the AI to validate its own sources would improve detection of hallucinated citations. It did not. Across two sections, students who used the structured format caught fabricated citations at the same rate as students given an open prompt. Structure did change something: structured students were substantially more likely to notice that something was wrong, but no more likely than the open-prompt group to finish the check. The session presents both rounds, including the confound identified in the first and removed in the second, and the limits of the observation, among them students who did not use the assigned structure. It also reports an unplanned finding: the AI tool used to review the submissions produced the same category of error it was reviewing for, misattributing a real paper to a fabricated author across multiple students before the error was caught on human review. Attendees will leave with a way to check sources that starts cheap and gets expensive, a clearer view of why you cannot ask the model to check its own work, and a specific account of where student checking breaks down.

papers.title: Designing Custom Chatbots for Classroom Use: Practical Examples, Benefits, and Current Limitations
papers.authors: Akio Abe, Farrukh Nazir
papers.journal: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)
papers.abstract: Recent advances in generative AI have made it increasingly possible for individual educators to design and implement their own custom chatbots without advanced programming skills (Abe & Kaneshige, 2025). This workshop introduces practical examples of custom chatbots developed for educational purposes and discusses both their affordances and limitations for classroom use. We would like to share a chatbot creation experience, which we spent one hour building, with a 30-minute presentation. For each chatbot, we will explain its intended purpose, target users, basic specifications, and expected classroom applications. We will also describe the development process, including how the presenters designed the chatbot instructions, refined prompts, and adjusted the chatbot behavior through iterative testing. After introducing these three examples, the workshop will discuss the potential benefits of custom chatbots. In particular, we will show how they can help users access relevant information more efficiently, provide more focused guidance than general-purpose AI tools, and support educators who want to create AI-assisted learning environments tailored to specific instructional goals. The workshop will critically examine current limitations. Even after repeated tuning, custom chatbots may still produce inaccurate, incomplete, or contextually inappropriate responses. Therefore, developers and educators remain responsible for checking the accuracy of the content and deciding whether the chatbot output is appropriate for learners. By combining demonstration, reflection, and critical discussion, this workshop aims to help participants understand how custom chatbots can be used responsibly and realistically in educational settings.

papers.title: Simulating the Clinical Encounter: Using AI Personas for Risk-Free Mental Health Assessment Practice
papers.authors: Pauline Stoltzner
papers.journal: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)
papers.abstract: Mental health assessment requires students to navigate complex conversations involving depression, anxiety, mania, psychosis, suicide risk, and other sensitive clinical situations. Yet opportunities to repeatedly practice these conversations in a safe, low-stakes environment can be limited. This session demonstrates an innovative approach to using generative artificial intelligence as an interactive patient simulation tool in nursing education. Rather than using AI simply to generate written assignments or answer questions, students interact with AI-generated patient personas designed to exhibit specific psychiatric symptoms and communication patterns. Through spoken or conversational interactions, students practice conducting mental health assessments, asking therapeutic follow-up questions, recognizing clinical cues, and adapting their communication as an encounter unfolds. During this interactive session, participants will see a live demonstration of an AI-simulated mental health encounter and experience how thoughtfully constructed prompts can transform generative AI into a repeatable practice environment. Practical examples will illustrate how faculty can design patient personas representing conditions such as depression, mania, anxiety, and psychosis while incorporating appropriate educational guardrails. The session will also address the role of faculty oversight, limitations of AI-generated responses, and the importance of positioning AI simulation as preparation for, rather than a replacement for, authentic human clinical experiences. Participants will leave with a practical framework for creating AI patient personas and ideas for incorporating low-risk, repeatable conversational practice into their own nursing courses.

papers.title: Beyond Adoption: Shared Values and Guiding Questions for AI-Aware Teaching
papers.authors: Sarah Cummings, Lyndsay Munro
papers.journal: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)
papers.abstract: We will discuss how shared questions can provide coherence without requiring uniform practice across disciplines, courses, or instructors. Examples from faculty across disciplines demonstrate how educators can begin with common values while reaching different, contextually appropriate decisions. By shifting attention from finding the single “right” approach to AI toward asking shared questions about teaching and learning, the framework offers a practical way forward amid varied practices, perspectives, and policies.

papers.title: Designing Educational Chatbots: Analysis of 71 Prompts in Educational Technology — Supplementary Data
papers.authors: Farhan Ahmed
papers.abstract: This repository contains the coded datasheet used in the classification and analysis of 71 educational AI prompts.

papers.title: Adaptive semantic prediction in dynamic linguistic environments: Computational-Neural Insights from Hierarchical Bayesian Inference
papers.authors: Yifan Li, Meihua Zhao
papers.abstract: This OSF project contains the raw behavioral data, processed EEG data, time-frequency analysis and CBPT scripts for ERPs and oscillations, as well as the Hierarchical Gaussian Filter (HGF) modeling code, corresponding to the manuscript submitted to Nature Communications. All files will remain private during peer review and will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the manuscript.

papers.title: The Privacy-Personalization Paradox in AI-Driven Customer Experience Analytics: A Trust-Centred Integrative Review and Responsible Personalization Framework
papers.authors: Rahmat Kofoworola Sanusi, Oreoluwa Abimbola Serifat, Temiloluwa Paul Adetola
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly supports personalised customer experiences through predictive analytics, recommender systems, behavioural profiling and conversational interfaces. However, the data collection and inference required for personalisation can also heighten perceptions of surveillance, vulnerability and loss of control. This integrative conceptual review examines how AI-enabled personalisation, perceived privacy risk and consumer trust interact within customer experience analytics. The synthesis integrates privacy calculus, social exchange, psychological reactance and signalling perspectives to explain how consumers evaluate personalisation value against privacy-related costs. A trust-centred framework is developed in which personalisation intensity, data sensitivity, algorithmic inference and recommendation relevance jointly shape perceived value and privacy risk, with consumer trust linking these evaluations to engagement, disclosure willingness, satisfaction, loyalty and continued use. The review also distinguishes actual data practices from perceived privacy intrusion and identifies contextual conditions that may alter this balance. The review further proposes a context-dependent nonlinear relationship between personalisation intensity and trust: moderate personalisation may strengthen trust when relevance and value are proportionate to data use, whereas more intensive personalisation may reduce trust when intrusion, surveillance or loss of autonomy becomes salient. Responsible personalisation is therefore framed around proportionate data use, meaningful transparency, consumer control and privacy-by-design. The framework and proposed personalisation threshold remain conceptual and require empirical testing across AI applications, cultural settings and regulatory environments.

papers.title: Calibrated Explanation-Detail Transparency in AI Recommendation Explanations: Trust, Privacy Concern, and Purchase Intention in E-Commerce
papers.authors: Zhang Danfeng, Siva Kumar Ramasamy
papers.journal: International Journal of Electronic Commerce Studies
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based recommender systems increasingly provide explanations for product recommendations in e-commerce. Although such explanations can reduce algorithmic opacity and strengthen consumer trust, they can also make data collection, profiling, and personalization practices more salient. This study develops and tests a calibrated explanation-detail transparency model in which recommendation explanations serve as both competence signals and privacy-risk signals. We conducted a one-factor, three-level, between-subjects scenario experiment with 472 valid responses retained from 623 submissions. Participants were randomly assigned to low-, medium-, or high-detail explanation conditions for the same product scenario. The data were analyzed using regression, PROCESS serial mediation analysis, covariance-based structural equation modeling, alternative-model comparisons, robustness checks, and statistical power sensitivity analysis. Higher-detail explanation conditions were associated with greater perceived algorithm understandability and platform trust, providing evidence consistent with a positive trust-benefit mechanism. They were also associated with greater perceived data intrusiveness and information privacy concern, providing evidence consistent with a negative privacy-cost mechanism. Purchase intention exhibited an asymmetric concave pattern across the three discrete conditions and was highest in the medium-detail condition. These findings support calibrated, layered, and privacy-sensitive explanation design in AI recommendation interfaces. Keywords: AI recommendation, explanation-detail transparency, recommender systems, platform trust, information privacy concern, purchase intention, electronic commerce

papers.title: Comparison of Incidence and Severity of Post-dural Puncture Headache After Caesarean Section Using 25G versus 27G Quincke Spinal Needles: A Randomised Controlled Trial
papers.authors: Renuka Patond, Nikhil Bhalerao
papers.journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH
papers.abstract: Introduction: Post-dural Puncture Headache (PDPH) is a frequent occurrence after spinal anaesthesia, especially in obstetric patients for caesarean section. It is described by the headache that aggravates with upright posture and is usually accompanied by photophobia, nausea, and stiff neck. It has marked effects on maternal recovery, neonatal care, and hospital stay. The design and size of the spinal needle are important predictors of PDPH, and thinner gauge needles with atraumatic bevels are perceived to minimise Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) leak and the risk of headache. Aim: To evaluate the incidence and severity of PDPH in patients for elective caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia with 25G and 27G Quincke spinal needles. Materials and Methods: This was a double blinded, randomised controlled trial conducted at the Department of Anaesthesia, Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College (JNMC) and Acharya Vinoba Bhave Rural Hospital (AVBRH), Wardha, Maharashtra, India, from June 2023 to October 2024. A total of 120 pregnant women aged 18-35 years, with American Society of Anaesthesiology (ASA) physical status II, scheduled for elective caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia, were enrolled. Participants were randomised into Group A (25G Quincke) and Group B (27G Quincke), receiving 1.8 ml of 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine. The postoperative period involved observing the occurrence, intensity, onset, and side-effects of PDPH. The Chi-square test was used for comparison of categorical data, and the Independent-samples t-test for continuous data. The number of attempts at insertion was also recorded and analysed statistically, with significance set at p-value <0.05. Results: A total of 120 pregnant women aged 18-35 years (mean age 27.6±8.3 years), with a mean height of 163.0±7.6 cm, mean weight of 60.1±6.3 kg, and mean Body Mass Index (BMI) of 22.8±3.3 kg/m2, were enrolled and randomised equally into the 25G and 27G Quincke spinal needle groups. PDPH occurrence was significantly less in the 27G group (5%) compared to the 25G group (20%) (p-value <0.05). The 27G group mostly experienced mild headaches, whereas the 25G group had significantly more cases of moderate to severe headaches. Additional attempts were required to successfully puncture the dura with the 27G needle. Adverse effects, including nausea and vomiting, were not significantly different among groups. Conclusion: The 27G Quincke needle decreases the occurrence and intensity of PDPH significantly compared to the 25G needle in elective caesarean deliveries. Despite technical problems, the thinner needle gives better comfort to the patient, and is therefore recommended for obstetric spinal analgesia.

papers.title: Health Burden of Night-Shift Work Among Polysomnography Technologists in India: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.authors: Eldhos Jacob, S Carishma, Srishankar Bairy, Basil  B Mathews, P A Ajither
papers.abstract: Introduction: Polysomnography technologists perform overnight sleep studies requiring continuous patient monitoring, technical management of diagnostic equipment, and sustained attention.Although night-shift work has been associated with adverse health outcomes among healthcare workers, the occupational health burden among polysomnography technologists remains poorly characterized in India.This study evaluated sleep quality, excessive daytime sleepiness, burnout-related symptoms, musculoskeletal symptoms, and selected cardiometabolic indicators and examined their associations with years of night-shift work experience.Methods: This cross-sectional observational study used an online structured questionnaire distributed through professional groups to polysomnography technologists working in private hospitals and sleep centers in South India.Participants were graduates with at least six months of night-shift experience.Of 196 responses, 16 were excluded for less than six months of night-shift experience and 30 for incomplete questionnaires, leaving 150 participants for analysis.The questionnaire included the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI), and musculoskeletal assessment.Height and weight were measured by participants.Blood pressure was manually assessed, while fasting blood glucose and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) were obtained from recent laboratory reports.Poor sleep quality was defined as PSQI >5 and excessive daytime sleepiness as ESS >10.The CBI was analyzed continuously and categorized operationally as 0-49, 50-74, and 75-100.Years of night-shift work experience were analyzed as a continuous exposure and categorized as ≤5 versus >5 years.Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, and BMI.Results: Mean age was 29.97 ± 4.43 years, and BMI was 24.16 ± 3.19 kg/m².Mean PSQI, ESS, and CBI scores were 7.09 ± 2.95, 9.20 ± 3.39, and 45.99 ± 20.95, respectively.Poor sleep quality occurred in 97 (64.7%), excessive daytime sleepiness in 56 (37.3%), and musculoskeletal symptoms in 126 (84.0%).CBI scores were categorized as 0-49 in 86 (57.3%), 50-74 in 48 (32.0%), and 75-100 in 16 (10.7%).Hypertension-range blood pressure was identified in 21 (14.0%) and prediabetes in 11 (7.3%).Each additional year of night-shift work experience was associated with higher odds of poor sleep quality (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 1.433, 95% CI: 1.118-1.835),excessive daytime sleepiness (aOR: 1.205, 95% CI: 1.001-1.450),CBI ≥50 (aOR: 1.810, 95% CI: 1.350-2.428),musculoskeletal symptoms (aOR: 1.372, 95% CI: 1.003-1.878),lower-back symptoms (aOR: 1.296, 95% CI: 1.051-1.598),neck symptoms (aOR: 1.272, 95% CI: 1.043-1.552),and hypertension-range blood pressure (aOR: 1.387, 95% CI: 1.052-1.829).No significant associations were observed with shoulder symptoms or prediabetes.Conclusion: Polysomnography technologists reported frequent poor sleep quality, excessive daytime sleepiness, burnout-related symptoms, and musculoskeletal symptoms.More years of night-shift work experience were associated with several adverse health outcomes after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI.These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and potential residual confounding.Prospective multicenter studies are warranted.

papers.title: Agencia docente e inteligencia artificial generativa en educación: análisis bibliométrico y mapeo científico (2022–2026)
papers.authors: Oscar Antonio Martínez Molina, Ana María Villón Tomalá, Luís Enrique Hernández Amaro, Richard Antonio Martínez Villegas
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has introduced new forms of assistance, automation, and co-production in teaching, intensifying debates about teacher agency, pedagogical judgment, and professional autonomy. This study aimed to characterize the evolution, thematic structure, and research fronts connecting teacher agency with generative artificial intelligence between 2022 and 10 September 2026. An exploratory bibliometric analysis was conducted on a verified corpus of 30 DOI-bearing publications retrieved through structured searches of open scholarly metadata and cross-checked against publisher records. Temporal productivity, source concentration, conceptual recurrence, and thematic relationships were examined. Output was absent in 2022, incipient in 2023-2024, and accelerated in 2025-2026, which accounted for 80.0% of the corpus. Mapping identified four clusters: agency and professional judgment, teacher education, professional knowledge for AI integration, and assessment-governance. Recent literature shifts attention from technology adoption toward negotiated control, critical validation of algorithmic outputs, and preservation of professional responsibility. The field is therefore in an early consolidation phase, characterized by fragmented authorship and increasing conceptual convergence around human-AI relations. Future research should expand longitudinal evidence, include Latin American contexts, and examine institutional conditions that strengthen or constrain teacher agency.

papers.title: Research on the Teaching Mechanism of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Promoting Young Children's Imitative Poetry Composition
papers.authors: Tingting Wang
papers.abstract: In this work we examine pedagogical role and underlying mechanisms of generative AI in helping young children with imitative poetry composition because it is complex task that can be difficult for students in classroom. Also I analyze how AI intervention affects language expression and classroom interaction, and creative performance in classroom and it is worth noting that these are important factors for the study. I use a quasi-experimental design with mixed methods. Through the use of the Imitative Poetry Ability Scale assessment, classroom observations, analysis of student works, and interviews, combined with independent samples t-tests and thematic coding, the following findings were obtained that generative AI can improve language completeness in children's imitative poetry, and the imagery creativity and classroom engagement are also enhanced. AI generated images and interactive feedback can stimulate imaginative expressions. It is worth noting that they also help support collaborative multimodal learning.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Multimodal Exercise and Technology-Assisted Interventions for Post-Stroke Motor Recovery : A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Dian Hasliani, Hana Milatieka
papers.journal: The International Journal of Medical Science and Health Research
papers.abstract: Background: Post-stroke motor recovery remains a major rehabilitation challenge. Multimodal exercise and technology-assisted interventions are increasingly used, but their comparative efficacy and moderators of benefit remain unclear. Methods: This systematic review synthesized data from 80 sources (primarily RCTs, etc) examining multimodal exercise, technology-assisted, or combined interventions versus usual care or conventional rehabilitation in adult stroke patients. Outcomes included motor function (Fugl-Meyer Assessment, FMA), gait, balance, and activities of daily living (ADL). Results: In subacute stroke, exoskeleton-assisted anthropomorphic training produced superior FMA-UE gains (+4.51 points; 95% CI 1.13–7.90) [6]. Virtual reality (VR) exercise improved FMA-UE (SMD 0.45; 95% CI 0.21–0.68) [2], with doses >15 hours yielding greater gains (MD 9.67) [12]. Bihemispheric tDCS combined with physical/occupational therapy improved FMA by 20.7% vs. 3.2% [10]. High-volume constraint-induced movement therapy ranked second (SMD 0.86) [20]. In chronic stroke, brain-computer interface (BCI) with robotics produced significant FMA gains vs. standard therapy [9]. Telerehabilitation was noninferior to in-clinic therapy (FMA difference 0.06 points) [13]. For gait, end-effector robotic training improved velocity (MD 0.16 m/s) [14], and aerobic exercise improved 6MWT (p=0.011) [15] and gait velocity (0.21 vs. 0.06 m/s) [17]. Combined cardiorespiratory/resistance training improved walking speed (MD 0.09 m/s) [16]. FES plus motor relearning significantly improved Barthel Index (15.8 vs. 8.2) [37]. Discussion: Positive effects are most consistent in subacute stroke, with greater baseline impairment and active, volitional, high-dose practice. Technology often matches conventional therapy when intensity is equal, but adds value by enabling adherence, neurofeedback, or home delivery. Conclusion: Multimodal and technology-assisted interventions significantly improve post-stroke motor recovery, particularly in subacute patients and when providing high-repetition, volitional, or neurofeedback-driven training. Telerehabilitation and BCI systems offer promising scalable solutions.

papers.title: Teaching Computer Science in the Digital and AI Era: Current Methods, Pedagogical Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.authors: Ali Sabzaliyev
papers.abstract: This article critically reviews the current state of computer science and informatics teaching and develops a practical framework for its improvement in the digital and artificial-intelligence era. The study adopts a structured narrative-review approach and synthesizes international standards, systematic reviews, and recent scholarship on programming education, computational thinking, active learning, mobile learning, digital competence, data literacy, Internet of Things (IoT), and artificial intelligence in education. The analysis shows that effective computer science teaching is not defined by the presence of technology alone. Learning outcomes depend on the alignment of pedagogy, content, learner readiness, teacher competence, assessment, and technological infrastructure. Direct explanation and demonstration remain valuable for introducing unfamiliar concepts, but they are most effective when followed by purposeful practice, debugging, problem solving, collaborative work, projects, and reflective feedback. Recent evidence supports flipped learning, gamification, mobile tools, and other active methodologies when they are connected to clearly specified learning objectives rather than used as isolated innovations. The review also argues that contemporary curricula should extend beyond software operation toward computational thinking, data reasoning, AI literacy, digital ethics, cybersecurity, and the ability to design and evaluate technological solutions. Based on the synthesis, the article proposes a balanced instructional model that combines explicit teaching, guided practice, inquiry, collaborative construction, authentic projects, and formative assessment. It concludes that the future of computer science education depends on pedagogically justified technology integration, continuous teacher development, inclusive access, and the responsible use of AI.

papers.title: Foreign Language Speaking Anxiety: Causes, Manifestations, and Pedagogical Solutions
papers.authors: Gulanbar Rahimova Alovsat gizi
papers.abstract: Speech anxiety is a common emotional and psychological barrier for foreign language learners during oral expression, classroom presentations, and social interaction. This article examines speech anxiety as an important psychological barrier affecting foreign language learners' speaking skills. The aim of this article is to explore the main causes, manifestations, and appropriate teaching strategies for reducing speech anxiety in foreign language teaching. The article emphasizes the importance of using educational and psychological strategies to reduce anxiety. The formation of speech anxiety is related to learners' self-confidence, personality traits, language proficiency, and past learning experiences, as well as external factors such as teacher evaluation, peer pressure, classroom atmosphere, and cultural factors. Speech anxiety usually involves a series of psychological, emotional and behavioral reactions, such as nervousness, fear of making mistakes, reduced attention span, self-doubt, impaired language expression, and avoidance of speaking in class and public presentations. To address these problems, foreign language teachers should create a safe, inclusive and supportive classroom environment by using teaching strategies such as staged oral instruction, collaborative learning, trial presentations, peer assessment and positive feedback. At the same time, they should make full use of digital technology and artificial intelligence tools to provide learners with low-stress, frequent opportunities for language practice. In addition, it is important to strengthen learners' emotional regulation skills and self-confidence, and gradually develop positive beliefs about language learning. This article aims to provide a theoretical basis and practical reference for reducing foreign language learners' speech anxiety, optimizing oral teaching models and developing foreign language communication skills.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy and Its Association with Academic Integrity and Critical Thinking Among Undergraduate Nursing Students: A Cross Sectional Study
papers.authors: Diksha Kaushal, Nitika Sharma
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Medical and Scientific Research (IJAMSR)
papers.abstract: Background: Artificial Intelligence (AI) literacy has emerged as a critical competency in healthcare education, influencing both ethical academic practices and the development of higher-order thinking skills. Concerns persist that AI access may foster academic misconduct, yet empirical evidence remains limited. Objective: This study examined the association between AI literacy and academic integrity and critical thinking disposition among nursing students in India. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 477 nursing students, of whom 434 provided valid, consented responses. Data were collected using standardised 5-point Likert scales assessing AI literacy, academic integrity, and critical thinking. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, simple linear regression, independent-samples t-tests, and one-way ANOVA. Results: Participants were predominantly female (75.3%), enrolled in B.Sc. Nursing (66.1%), and from private institutions (98.6%). Overall, AI literacy was moderate-to-high (Mean = 3.35, SD = 0.73). AI literacy was strongly and positively correlated with academic integrity (r = 0.821, p < 0.001, R² = 0.674) and critical thinking (r = 0.788, p < 0.001, R² = 0.621). Sub-domains of academic honesty behaviours (Mean = 3.43) and reflective judgment in AI use (Mean = 3.43) were particularly high. Demographic analyses showed no significant differences across gender, course, or year of study, suggesting uniform AI literacy levels. Conclusion: Findings show that higher AI literacy is strongly associated with stronger academic integrity and critical thinking among nursing students. Contrary to prevailing concerns, AI literacy fosters responsible and ethical use of generative tools while strengthening reflective judgment and open-mindedness. Educational institutions should integrate standardised AI literacy and ethics curricula across all years of nursing education to promote ethical scholarship and clinical reasoning. papers.title: CONSTRUCTING PROFESSIONAL IDENTITIES IN AI-ENHANCED LANGUAGE CLASSROOM: A STUDY OF PAKISTANI ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS’ PERSPECTIVES AND PRACTICES
papers.authors: Muhammad Atiq-ur-Rehman, Muhammad Sabboor Hussain
papers.journal: Insights (Bhalwal) International Journal of Humanities Management and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: The main aim of the study is to investigate the construction of English Language Teachers’ (ELTs) professional identity in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) era in the Pakistani Punjab context. The qualitative analysis is embedded in semi-structured interviews. Multilayered sampling techniques were used, and data were collected from ELTs working in public and private educational institutions and analyzed using the Grounded Theory Approach (GTA). Initially, purposive sampling was used to identify appropriate samples, and those samples referred additional samples until saturation was attained on the thirteenth sample. The investigation was theoretically informed by Gee’s (2000) distinction between I-identity and A-identity. Findings created five interrelated categories: Institutionally Framed Professionalism, Agentive Professional Self, Constrained Autonomy, Negotiation Professional Identity, and Hybrid Identity Construction. Results highlight that examination-driven systems, curricular mandates, and administrative checks and balances powerfully form ELTs’ identities. They are sustained simultaneously by contemplative practice, adaptive strategies, and professional achievement. Autonomy was developed as conditional rather than absolute, leading teachers to negotiate between organizational compliance and personal pedagogical obligation. The study demonstrates that ELT identity in Punjab is dynamic, context-sensitive, and permanently negotiated. By integrating hierarchical and agentive dimensions of identity, this research contributes to a nuanced understanding of teacher professionalism within examination- focused educational systems.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ITS EFFECTS ON STUDENTS’ READING AND WRITING SKILLS AT THE SECONDARY SCHOOL LEVEL
papers.authors: Sana Sarwar, Rashid Minas Wattoo, Ms. Saba Gul
papers.journal: Insights (Bhalwal) International Journal of Humanities Management and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Although international scholarship on AI in education had expanded rapidly, empirical evidence concerning its relationship with the reading and writing skills of secondary-school students in Pakistan had remained limited. The present study examined the relationship between AI use and the reading and writing performance of male students enrolled in public secondary schools in District Sialkot, Punjab. A quantitative, cross-sectional, correlational research design was adopted. The population comprised male students enrolled in Grades 9 and 10 in government secondary schools, from whom a multistage stratified random sample of 270 students was selected. Data were collected through an AI Use in Learning Questionnaire, a researcher-developed reading comprehension test, and an analytical writing performance test. The study differentiated between productive and substitutive forms of AI use. Productive use involved explanation seeking, guided practice, idea generation, verification, formative feedback, and reflective revision, whereas substitutive use involved outsourcing comprehension and composition, copying AI-generated responses, and accepting machine-generated content without critical evaluation. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, analysis of variance, and hierarchical multiple regression were employed to examine the relationships among the variables. The study provided a contextually grounded framework for understanding AI-supported literacy, assessment integrity, digital inequality, teacher mediation, and responsible technology integration in Pakistani secondary education.

papers.title: A Dual-Channel Model of Artificial Intelligence Adoption Intention Among Executives of Traditional-Industry SMEs: Perceived Value, Perceived Implementation Risk, and the Boundary Condition of Digital Foundation
papers.authors: Weixiang Gan
papers.abstract: **A Dual-Channel Model of Artificial Intelligence Adoption Intention among Executives of Traditional-Industry SMEs: Perceived Value, Perceived Implementation Risk, and the Boundary Condition of Digital Foundation** **Weixiang Gan** Post Doctorate Researcher, Lincoln University College, 47301 Petaling Jaya, Malaysia **Qiaoran Liu** Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau of Yindu District, Anyang City 455000, China **Mengfei Xiao** Post Doctorate Researcher, Lincoln University College, 47301 Petaling Jaya, Malaysia **Jialin Liu** School of Management and Marketing, Faculty of Business and Law, Taylor’s University, No. 1, Jalan Taylor’s, 47500 Subang Jaya, Malaysia **Tara Ahmed Mohammed** SEGi University, Kota Damansara, Petaling Jaya 47810, Malaysia **Abstract:** Whether a small or medium-sized firm in a traditional industry takes up artificial intelligence is usually settled by the chairman or the general manager alone, without an information-systems de-partment to consult. Existing adoption research draws its evidence mainly from firms that have already completed basic informatisation, so how external conditions reach the executive remains unclear. This study surveyed 526 SME executives in four traditional industries across four Chinese regions and esti-mated a structural equation model linking technology-side and environment-side conditions, perceived value, perceived implementation risk and adoption intention, with digital foundation as a boundary con-dition. External conditions split into two mediating pathways, the two channels of the model. Performance expectancy and competitive pressure raise perceived value, while effort expectancy and perceived insti-tutional support leave it unchanged and instead lower perceived implementation risk. Competitive pres-sure carries opposite signs across the two pathways and its total effect on adoption intention is indistin-guishable from zero, as is that of institutional support. Digital foundation weakens the suppression that perceived risk exerts on intention, the slope falling from −0.284 to −0.125, although the two product terms add only 0.007 to the explained variance in intention. Peer demonstration and subsidies do not move these firms, and the estimates locate the reason in a risk they cannot absorb rather than in any shortfall of perceived value; building the data and systems base before the application layer fits the way these firms decide. The design is cross-sectional, so the estimates are associational and the ordering among the con-structs rests on theory rather than on temporal precedence. **Keywords:** Artificial Intelligence Adoption, SME Executives, Perceived Value, Perceived Implementa-tion Risk, Digital Foundation, Upper Echelons Perspective, Structural Equation Modelling **Citation:** Gan, W., Liu, Q., Xiao, M., Liu, J., & Mohammed, T. A. (2026). A Dual-Channel Model of Artificial Intelligence Adoption Intention among Executives of Traditional-Industry SMEs: Perceived Value, Perceived Implementation Risk, and the Boundary Condition of Digital Foundation. _Business and Management Perspectives_, _01_(04), 1–28. https://doi.org/10.67728/bmp.2026.016

papers.title: Teaching with AI, Not Against It: A Thinking Partner Framework for Working Adult Learners in Compressed Online Formats
papers.authors: Abbot L. Packard, Ryan Fuller, Glen A. Holmes, Bryce Platt Kayanuma
papers.journal: Online journal of distance learning administration
papers.abstract: Working adult learners in online graduate programs face challenges that make strict AI bans both impractical and unhelpful. This paper introduces the Thinking Partner Framework, a practical approach to AI integration developed and refined across six semesters of graduate research methods courses serving approximately 440 K-12 educators. Instead of treating AI as a problem to be detected, the framework positions AI as a Socratic partner that helps students learn while still requiring them to think for themselves. Five design principles—transparency, process documentation, authentic assessment, scaffolded autonomy, and metacognitive reflection—guide the framework’s implementation. The paper includes practical tools such as sample prompts, documentation templates, and examples illustrating the difference between using AI for answers and using it as a thinking partner. Observations from practice, including a 96% checkpoint completion rate and evidence of students transferring Socratic techniques to their own classrooms, suggest promise, though more rigorous research is needed. This framework gives distance education administrators a practical option beyond simply banning or allowing AI. Keywords: artificial intelligence, adult learning, distance education, Socratic method, academic integrity, compressed courses

papers.title: Integrasi Generative AI dalam Pendidikan Arsitektur: Model Tata Kelola Pembelajaran Berbasis Proyek untuk Literasi AI, Integritas Akademik, dan Kreativitas Desain
papers.authors: Zumrotul Avifa K
papers.abstract: Perkembangan generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) telah mengubah cara mahasiswa arsitektur memperoleh informasi, mengembangkan gagasan, menghasilkan visual, dan menyusun karya akademik. Transformasi ini memberikan peluang bagi inovasi pembelajaran, tetapi sekaligus menghadirkan tantangan terkait integritas akademik, ketergantungan teknologi, validitas asesmen, privasi data, dan peran manusia dalam pengambilan keputusan desain. Artikel konseptual ini bertujuan merumuskan model tata kelola pembelajaran berbasis proyek yang mengintegrasikan literasi AI, integritas akademik, dan kreativitas desain dalam pendidikan arsitektur. Kajian dilakukan melalui sintesis literatur mutakhir, kebijakan pendidikan, dan penelitian mengenai pemanfaatan GenAI dalam pendidikan tinggi dan arsitektur. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa pelarangan maupun kebebasan penuh dalam penggunaan GenAI belum mampu menjawab kompleksitas tersebut. Model yang diusulkan menempatkan GenAI sebagai pendukung eksplorasi dan umpan balik dengan tetap menempatkan manusia sebagai pengendali utama. Model terdiri atas lima tahap, yaitu penetapan batas penggunaan AI, eksplorasi berbantuan AI, verifikasi pengetahuan, pengembangan desain berbasis keputusan manusia, serta asesmen autentik dan refleksi. Implementasinya diperkuat melalui dokumentasi proses, verifikasi bukti, AI disclosure, penilaian kontribusi individu, dan refleksi kritis.

papers.title: Leadership for University-Affiliated Think Tanks and Socio-Economic Transformation in the Ugandan Higher Education Space
papers.authors: David Katende
papers.journal: Open Journal of Educational Research and Practice
papers.abstract: Despite the growing presence of university-affiliated think tanks in Uganda, limited scholarly attention has been paid to how their leadership enables knowledge translation and policy engagement for socio-economic transformation. This paper set out to review the role of think tanks in higher education. It explores leadership for university affiliated think tanks and socio-economic transformation in the Ugandan higher education space. Using qualitative narrative literature review, multidisciplinary and fragmented relevant literature across higher education leadership, was reviewed to conceptualize think tanks in higher education institutions and their roles in socio-economic transformation through knowledge production and brokerage, public policy, innovation, and development studies in Ugandan Universities. The review found that university-affiliated think tanks in Uganda are evolving from conventional research units into hybrid, networked and publicly engaged institutions that bridge academic knowledge, policy and practice through knowledge brokerage, innovation, stakeholder engagement and policy communication. Leadership emerged as the pivotal mechanism linking knowledge production to policy uptake, resource mobilization, institutional sustainability and socio-economic transformation, although tensions between autonomy, accountability, academic independence and external funding persist. The study concludes that the effectiveness and sustainability of university-affiliated think tanks depend not only on research capacity but also on strategic, adaptive and distributed leadership, supportive governance and strong stakeholder networks. It therefore recommends that Ugandan universities institutionalize think tanks through clear mandates and governance frameworks, strengthen leadership and knowledge-translation capacities, diversify sustainable funding, promote interdisciplinary and stakeholder co-creation, and build national and international networks that safeguard academic independence while enhancing policy influence and socio-economic impact.

papers.title: Adiposity–metabolic discordance within normal BMI: sex-specific cardiometabolic phenotypes in 44,991 Spanish healthcare workers
papers.authors: Pedro Javier Tárraga Marcos, Ángel Arturo López‐González, Emilio Martínez-Almoyna Rifá, Hernán Paublini, Cristina Martorell Sánchez, José Ignacio Ramírez‐Manent, Rafael Luján, Pedro Juan Tárraga López
papers.abstract: Background: Normal body mass index (BMI) does not necessarily indicate normal adiposity, and individuals with normal-weight obesity (NWO) may exhibit cardiometabolic abnormalities that remain undetected by BMI-based classification. We examined the cardiometabolic phenotype associated with NWO among adults with normal BMI, with particular attention to sex-related heterogeneity and the discriminatory ability of simple anthropometric measures. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 44,939 Spanish healthcare workers. NWO was defined as BMI 18.5–24.9 kg/m² combined with high or very high body-fat percentage according to sex- and age-specific classification. The primary analytical sample comprised 19,824 participants with normal BMI and either normal adiposity (n=19,040) or NWO (n=784). Cardiometabolic characteristics included glycaemic, lipid, blood-pressure, insulin-resistance-related, and metabolic-syndrome measures. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine associations between NWO and cardiometabolic abnormalities, including NWO × sex interactions. Receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated the ability of BMI, waist circumference, and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) to discriminate NWO. Results: NWO was present in 3.10% (95% confidence interval [CI], 2.89–3.32%) of participants with normal BMI and was more prevalent in men than women (5.43% vs. 2.35%). Compared with normal adiposity, NWO was characterized by greater central adiposity, higher fasting glucose and insulin-resistance-related indices, lower HDL-C, and a more atherogenic lipid profile. At least one abnormal cardiometabolic domain was present in 53.1% of participants with NWO versus 29.2% with normal adiposity. After multivariable adjustment, NWO was associated with ≥1 abnormal domain (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.24; 95% CI, 1.93–2.60), ≥2 abnormal domains (aOR 1.76; 95% CI, 1.36–2.29), elevated triglyceride-glucose index (aOR 3.28; 95% CI, 2.61–4.11), elevated low-density/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (aOR 3.45; 95% CI, 2.87–4.15), and elevated triglyceride/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (aOR 2.72; 95% CI, 2.18–3.38). Several associations differed by sex. In receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses, waist circumference showed the highest discrimination overall (area under the curve [AUC] 0.776; 95% CI, 0.756–0.795) and among men (AUC 0.836; 95% CI, 0.812–0.858), whereas BMI showed the highest discrimination among women (AUC 0.757; 95% CI, 0.733–0.780). Conclusions: Among Spanish healthcare workers with normal BMI, NWO identified a subgroup with greater concurrent cardiometabolic abnormality burden, particularly involving glycaemic, insulin-resistance-related, and atherogenic characteristics. Associations and anthropometric discrimination differed by sex, highlighting heterogeneity within the conventional normal-BMI category. Prospective studies are needed to determine the prognostic relevance of these phenotypes.

papers.title: The Mediating Role of Adaptive Strategies in the Relationship between Work-Related Challenges and Teaching Effectiveness and Job Satisfaction of TVL (Technical -Vocational-Livelihood) Teachers: A Basis for a Professional Development Program
papers.authors: Esteria T. Acop
papers.journal: International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies
papers.abstract: This study examined the mediating role of adaptive strategies in the relationship between work-related challenges and teaching effectiveness and job satisfaction among Technical-Vocational-Livelihood (TVL) teachers as a basis for developing a professional development program. Anchored in the Job Demands–Resources Model, Transactional Theory of Stress and Coping, and Herzberg’s Two-Factor Theory, the study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design with mediation analysis. Using universal sampling, 40 TVL teachers from five public secondary schools in Bilar, Batuan, and Carmen, Bohol, participated in the study. Data were collected through a modified and expert-validated questionnaire using a four-point Likert scale and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and regression-based mediation analysis at a 0.05 significance level. Results revealed high levels of work-related challenges (M = 3.05), adaptive strategies (M = 3.43), and teaching effectiveness (M = 3.56), while job satisfaction was moderate (M = 3.17). Student-related concerns and resource adequacy emerged as the major challenges, whereas technology and artificial intelligence-assisted teaching received the highest adaptive strategy rating. Work-related challenges showed no statistically significant relationships with adaptive strategies, teaching effectiveness, or job satisfaction. Adaptive strategies were significantly associated with teaching effectiveness (r = .392, p = .012) but not with job satisfaction (r = .003, p = .986). Moreover, no significant mediating effects were established for either professional outcome. The findings informed the proposed Adaptive and Industry-Responsive Professional Development Program, emphasizing instructional innovation, professional collaboration, institutional support, and teacher well-being. The study aligns with Sustainable Development Goals 3 (Good Health and Well-Being), 4 (Quality Education), and 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth). Its potential sustainability contribution lies in strengthening educational quality, institutional responsiveness, teacher welfare, and industry-relevant workforce preparation through evidence-based professional development.

papers.title: The Non-Technical User as an LLM Threat Vector: Linguistic Strategies for Bypassing AI Safeguards and Implications for AI Security
papers.authors: Aleksandr V. Sokolov, Gleb Sokolov
papers.abstract: The threat that ordinary non-technical users pose to large language models (LLMs) still sits at the margins of AI-security research. These are people who work with AI assistants every day — at work, in study, in everyday life — yet hold no specialised background in information technology or machine learning. A post-laboratory survey of first-year humanities undergraduates (n=70) returned an unexpectedly high figure: 95.7% cleared all main protection levels of the Gandalf platform (Lakera AI) without stepping outside purely linguistic techniques. These included sign-form decomposition and formatting (M=2.00), cross-language code-switching (M=1.29), indirect semantic extraction (20.3% of open-ended responses), and pragmatic pressure. We read these micro-level data against the macro picture of the Gandalf-RCT crowdsourcing experiment (279,675 prompts) and against academic work on filter evasion in image-generation systems (SurrogatePrompt, PC², DALL-E 3, Shedevrum/Yandex). The pattern runs through all of them. From text LLMs to multimodal generators, the filter yields to the same moves, none of which require a line of code: a proper name is swapped for a physical description, direct reference for allegory or an adjacent associative term, the prompt language is switched, the grapheme is distorted. A three-tier analysis of LLM break-resistance grounds the paper’s central claim — that rising everyday AI literacy produces a structural security deficit left uncovered by current surface-level filtering. Several implications for AI safety system design follow.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Supported Personalized Learning: Examining Its Impact on Students' Critical Thinking, Learning Engagement, and Academic Achievement in Higher Education
papers.authors: Mia Siti Nurazizah, Endan Hamdan Ridwan, Ahsen Yılmaz, Syalaisha Renaisse Fathiha, Mehwish Kaleem
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Sciences Language and Education
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported personalized learning provides adaptive instructional content, individualized feedback, and differentiated learning pathways, although its educational outcomes remain inconsistently established. This study examines the relationships between AI-supported personalized learning and students' critical thinking, learning engagement, and academic achievement in higher education. A structured integrative literature review was conducted using 24 scholarly publications from 2022–2026. Qualitative thematic synthesis examined technological mechanisms, reported educational outcomes, and pedagogical conditions while distinguishing empirical findings from conceptual interpretations. The findings identify adaptive questioning, reflective feedback, and individualized cognitive challenges as potential mechanisms supporting critical thinking, although direct evidence of measurable improvement remains limited. Personalized instructional support is associated with learning engagement through relevance, motivation, and sustained participation, while adaptive assessment, individualized feedback, and self-regulated learning are linked to reported academic achievement. These relationships vary according to instructional design, learner autonomy, digital competence, and educational context. The reviewed evidence does not establish causal relationships among the three outcomes. The bounded literature corpus, heterogeneous research designs, and absence of a standardized quality appraisal limit generalizability. The review contributes an integrated interpretation distinguishing reported educational associations from proposed mechanisms and identifies priorities for longitudinal, comparative, and outcome-specific empirical investigation.

papers.title: ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ МАРКЕТИНГОВИХ ПІДХОДІВ ДО УПРАВЛІННЯ КЛІЄНТСЬКИМ ДОСВІДОМ У СУЧАСНИХ БІЗНЕС-МОДЕЛЯХ
papers.authors: Вікторія Хурдей, Тетяна Дронова, Людмила Квасова
papers.abstract: У статті досліджено трансформацію підходів до управління клієнтським досвідом у сучасних бізнес-моделях на прикладі ресейл-платформи The Originals. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена посиленням конкуренції у сфері електронної комерції, зростанням вимог споживачів до якості обслуговування та необхідністю формування послідовної й персоналізованої взаємодії з клієнтами через цифрові канали. Метою статті є обґрунтування напрямів удосконалення управління клієнтським досвідом ресейл-платформи та розроблення практичних заходів для підвищення рівня утримання клієнтів, їхньої лояльності й довгострокової економічної цінності клієнтської бази. Проаналізовано маркетингові результати діяльності платформи, основні канали взаємодії зі споживачами, клієнтські сегменти та показники оцінювання клієнтського досвіду. Встановлено, що у 2025 р. кількість відвідувань сайту зросла до 7972 проти 6025 у 2024 р., а дохід збільшився з 3928,3 тис. грн до 6568,9 тис. грн. Показник задоволеності клієнтів CSAT становив 98,2%, індекс готовності рекомендувати платформу NPS – 60,6%, а оцінка зручності взаємодії CES – 4,7 бала з 5. Водночас проблемним напрямом залишається утримання клієнтів: кількість постійних клієнтів становила 312 осіб за плану 500. Обґрунтовано необхідність переходу від окремих інструментів обслуговування до інтегрованої системи управління клієнтським досвідом, що передбачає персоналізацію пропозицій, оптимізацію цифрових точок контакту, автоматизацію комунікацій, розвиток програм лояльності, аналіз відгуків та використання інструментів штучного інтелекту. Запропоновано комплекс заходів із плановим бюджетом 470 тис. грн на 2027 р. Реалізація запропонованих рішень сприятиме зміцненню взаємовідносин із клієнтами, стимулюванню повторних покупок і підвищенню конкурентоспроможності ресейл-бізнесу. References 1. Lemon, K.
