papers.title: Beyond AI Use: How AI Literacy Is Linked to Critical Thinking through AI-Assisted Problem-Solving Ability and AI Reliance
papers.authors: Yifan Wang
papers.abstract: With the widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning, helping learners use AI effectively to solve language-related problems while maintaining independent judgment and critical thinking has become a key issue in technologyenhanced language education. However, existing studies have largely focused on EFL learners’ acceptance of AI, intentions to use it, and usage behaviors, offering limited explanations of how AI literacy shapes learners’ interactions with AI and relates to critical thinking. To address this gap, the present study drew on self-regulated learning theory and adopted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. Questionnaire data from 450 university students with generative AIassisted EFL learning experience were analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapping. Subsequently, 20 participants selected through stratified purposive sampling took part in semi-structured interviews, which were analyzed thematically. Quantitative results showed that AI literacy was positively associated with AI-assisted problem-solving ability and indirectly associated with critical thinking through AI-assisted problem-solving ability and AI reliance. Thematic analysis further revealed how learners translated AI-related knowledge and skills into effective problem-solving practices and how different levels of cognitive control were associated with distinct patterns of AI use and cognitive outcomes. This study deepens the understanding of the internal cognitive mechanisms underlying EFL learners’ adaptation to AI and provides practical implications for the systematic development of AI literacy and critical thinking in EFL education.

papers.title: The Impact of Retrieval Augmented Generation on the Reliability of Large Language Models
papers.journal: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable fluency but remain fundamentally unreliable for knowledge-intensive tasks due to hallucination, temporal staleness, and lack of verifiability.Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a dominant architectural paradigm that grounds generation in external evidence.This paper provides a comprehensive investigation into how RAG reshapes LLM reliability across factual accuracy, citation fidelity, temporal freshness, and robustness to noise.We benchmark five RAG variants against closed-book baselines using secondary datasets including Natural Questions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, and RGB.Results show an average 23.7% reduction in hallucination rate and 31.2%improvement in citation grounding when using advanced retrieval with self-reflection.However, we identify critical failure modes: retriever-generator misalignment, context distraction, and over-reliance on irrelevant passages.We propose a reliability framework and demonstrate that corrective and modular RAG designs significantly mitigate these risks.Our findings establish RAG as necessary but not sufficient for trustworthy deployment.

papers.title: Regulating the Digital Divide: Policy Interventions for Equitable Access to AI-Enabled E-Learning Platforms
papers.authors: Chukwudum Collins Umoke
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming global education systems, offering unprecedented opportunities for personalization, efficiency, and adaptive learning. However, the integration of AI in education has also deepened existing digital divides, particularly in under-resourced communities lacking adequate infrastructure, policy support, and inclusive design. This study proposes the Equity-Centered AI Learning Access Model (ECALAM)—a conceptual framework developed through a qualitative synthesis of recent literature and policy reports—to understand and address systemic barriers to equitable AI adoption. ECALAM identifies four interrelated domains: structural inequities, AI accessibility challenges, inclusive design adaptation, and policy governance. Findings indicate that AI-enhanced learning systems, when deployed without attention to algorithmic fairness, linguistic diversity, and access equity, risk reinforcing educational stratification. Inclusive design principles, adaptive technologies, and regulatory frameworks are shown to play a pivotal role in enabling just and accessible learning environments. The study concludes with policy recommendations for governments, educators, and technology developers, emphasizing the need for anticipatory governance and inclusive pedagogical integration. ECALAM offers a diagnostic and strategic tool for guiding ethical and equitable AI implementation in education, particularly across diverse and underserved global contexts.

papers.title: Optimization of Renewable Energy Systems Using Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria: A Focus on Generation and Distribution
papers.authors: Johnson Oluwatuyi Nelson
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: Nigeria’ s energy sector is marred by structural inefficiencies, unreliable grid infrastructure, and an overdependence on fossil fuels, resulting in inadequate electricity access and persistent blackouts. Despite possessing vast renewable energy resources—particularly solar and wind—the country continues to underutilize them due to technical, financial, and regulatory barriers. This study examines the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing these challenges and optimizing renewable energy generation, distribution, and management. Employing a qualitative secondary research methodology, the study analyzes peerreviewed literature, national policy documents, and global case studies to evaluate the applicability of AI technologies such as machine learning, neural networks, and predictive analytics within the Nigerian context. Case studies of solar farms, wind energy forecasting, smart grid operations, and urban load management illustrate how AI can enhance forecasting accuracy, improve grid reliability, reduce operational costs, and support decentralized energy access in rural areas. However, the adoption of AI faces significant hurdles, including high implementation costs, limited technical expertise, and a lack of robust data infrastructure. To overcome these barriers, the study recommends strategic public-private partnerships, targeted capacity-building programs, supportive data policy frameworks, and pilot initiatives to demonstrate feasibility. The integration of AI into Nigeria’ s renewable energy systems offers a promising pathway toward achieving national energy security, sustainability, and socioeconomic development.

papers.title: Mapping the Research Landscape of Artificial Intelligence and Lifelong Learning: A Scientometric Analysis Using ScientoPy
papers.authors: Rungfa Pasmala, Kunawut Boonkwang, Natthawan Phoonson, Taklaew Klaewkla, Thada Jantakoon
papers.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and lifelong learning has attracted growing educational, computational, and policy attention, yet its intellectual structure has not been mapped systematically. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the AI-lifelong learning literature indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection between 2014 and 2024. Records retrieved from both databases (N = 347) were merged and duplicated in ScientoPy, yielding 259 unique documents. Research momentum was quantified with three time-normalized indicators, average growth rate (AGR), average documents per year (ADY), and percentage of documents published in the last years (PDLY), across six analytical dimensions. Output grew from one document in 2014 to 116 in 2024; across the five principal document types (n = 220), 70.5% of records appeared in 2023-2024. Conference papers (41.3%) and journal articles (38.2%) predominated, with articles expanding fastest (AGR = 21.5; PDLY = 71.7%). Education & Educational Research recorded the highest normalized momentum among subject categories (AGR = 7.0; PDLY = 89.5%). Lifelong learning (n = 57) and artificial intelligence (n = 53) anchored the keyword field, while ChatGPT and Higher Education emerged entirely within the final two years. The United States led in volume (n = 57), whereas India (n = 29; PDLY = 89.7%) showed the strongest recent acceleration. Triangulating these indicators suggests, as an interpretive inference rather than a network-based measurement, that the corpus comprises three largely separate epistemic communities sharing a label but not a research program, framing an agenda for integrative, ethically grounded scholarship.

papers.title: The Study of AI on Customer Trust among New SBI YONO Young Users in Tirupati
papers.authors: N Sivadatta, D .Prasanna Kumar
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
papers.abstract: This study compares how much young users of SBI's YONO app in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh trust a human bank advisor versus the app's AI assistant. Data came from a structured Likert-scale questionnaire (n = 120, aged 18–30) and were analysed with a paired-samples t-test and a chi-square test. Trust in the AI assistant is highest for simple balance checks, but falls sharply for loans, investments and complaints, where the human advisor is trusted significantly more (p < 0.001). Age group is also significantly associated with preferred channel (p = 0.022). Banks should use AI as a fast first layer and keep an easy path to a human for high-stakes decisions.

papers.title: Employability of Gen z and the role of skills beyond Traditional Education
papers.authors: GRISHA POOJARI
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
papers.abstract: Traditional education has always played an important role in the labour market but as we navigate today’s competitive world only having a degree alone is not sufficient as the employer not only needs a employee to have a degree but also they want them to have various types of skills , efficiency in the work ,practicality and good work experience. This research paper examines how generation z in india looks at the significance of ability inculcated other then formal education and how these skills can help them to get the suitable job the study is purely based on primary data collected through a structured online questionnaire from 103 respondents aged from 18-29 years the stored data is analysed using a descriptive statistics , primarily percentages mostly percentage to understand every respondent’s views , the skills needed and there professional background . The findings show that 53% of respondents disagree that a formal qualification alone is enough to secure suitable employment, while only 33% agree. Approximately 74% of respondents have developed skills outside their formal education, and 78% have gained practical work experience. Respondents consider problem-solving skills (92%), soft skills (91%), communication skills (89%), and technical skills (88%) important for obtaining employment. Furthermore, 82% believe that candidates with additional skills have better employment opportunities. Self-learning (48%) and online platforms (46%) are the main sources through which respondents develop their skills. However, participation in government skill development programs remains low. Only 16% of respondents have participated in such programs , while just 17% are well aware of these schemes. The major barriers to skill development are the high cost of training (50%) and lack of time (47%). Respondents also identify digital skills (62%) and artificial intelligence (AI)-related skills (57%) as important areas in which they need further training. The findings suggest that Gen z thinks that skills are not the replacement for education but they help us to enhance our future as we know degree gives us less practical but more theoretical knowledge but on the other hand skills ,work experience ,training ,internships gives us more practical knowledge which helps genz to apply those knowledge in job. therefore the study shows the importance of skill development courses which should also be affordable or free . increase the awareness of government schemes and greater implementation of technological, practical and ai related courses and training in educational institution hence these steps can help genz to seek jobs and prepare them from rapidly changing demand of the labour market

papers.title: ScholarForge AI: An Open, Multi-Agent RAG Platform for Automated Research Paper Analysis
papers.authors: Shravasti Chaudhari, Akansha Mahore, Tanmay Ranotkar, Shravan Ningot, Dr. Maithili S. Deshmukh
papers.journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: The growing volume of scientific literature has made research-paper analysis increasingly time-consuming for students, researchers, and academicians. Tasks such as literature review generation, methodology understanding, research gap identification, citation formatting, and trend discovery often require substantial manual effort. To address these challenges, this paper presents ScholarForge AI, an open, multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform designed to automate research-paper analysis and transform scholarly documents into actionable research intelligence. The proposed system integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), LangGraph-based multi-agent orchestration, ChromaDB vector storage, a Neo4j knowledge graph, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to support intelligent document processing. Research papers in PDF format are processed using PyMuPDF and EasyOCR, then chunked and embedded with the BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 sentence transformer model for semantic retrieval. The platform includes specialized agents for literature review generation, methodology analysis, research gap detection, trend analysis, research idea generation, citation formatting, interactive question answering and difficulty prediction. In addition, a research difficulty predictor classifies papers as Easy, Medium, or Hard, while the knowledge graph visualizes relationships among papers, authors, keywords, methods, and topics. Experimental results show that ScholarForge AI improves the efficiency of literature survey preparation, supports accurate gap identification, and provides context-aware research recommendations. Built entirely on open-source technologies, the platform offers a scalable and accessible solution for academic research support.

papers.title: Skill2Hire – An Intelligent AI-Powered Career Assistance Platform
papers.authors: K H MOHAN KRISHNA, LEKHANA SHREE M, NAGARAJ VENKATESH NAIK, PRAVALIKA H G, Eshwari Hiremath
papers.journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Students preparing for technology-sector recruitment must manage resume preparation, job-description matching, vacancy discovery, interview practice, and industry updates. These activities are often spread over different platforms. This paper presents Skill2Hire, a modular AI-powered career assistance platform with five independent modules: an ATS-oriented Resume Builder, Resume Tailoring and Skill-Gap Analysis, Job Suggestions, a Mock Interview Simulator, and a Tech News Hub. The proposed system uses a React and TypeScript frontend, a Node.js and Express backend, MongoDB Atlas for persistent storage, and server-side large language model integration for selected language tasks. A rule-based ATS compatibility score estimates resume completeness, keyword alignment, skills coverage, structure, and formatting. Resume tailoring follows a “Zero Fake Skills” rule: missing qualifications are reported as skill gaps rather than inserted into the candidate’s resume. The interview module includes eligibility screening, aptitude assessment, technical interview, and behavioral HR stages. The paper describes the design, workflows, architecture, responsible-AI safeguards, and evaluation plan. Claims of quantitative performance are not treated as findings unless measurements can be reproduced. Keywords— Career assistance, Applicant Tracking System, resume tailoring, job recommendation, large language models, mock interview, skill-gap analysis.

papers.title: Reframing Hybrid Feedback in Japanese University EFL Writing: Complementary Roles of Peer Feedback and Generative AI
papers.authors: Hisami Tsuichibaru
papers.abstract: The present classroom-based exploratory study re-examines hybrid feedback in a Japanese university EFL writing course for science majors. Thirty-six students used both peer feedback and ChatGPT-based feedback during a 12-week semester. Drawing on end-of-course questionnaires and a focused analysis of drafts, peer comments, AI feedback, and revisions, the study asked how students perceived the roles of peer and AI feedback and what pedagogical implications follow for hybrid feedback design. The findings suggested a complementary rather than competitive relationship. Peer feedback primarily supported content development, organization, reader awareness, and collaborative engagement, whereas generative AI primarily supported grammar, wording, and immediate local revision. When combined, the two sources appeared to encourage iterative revision and confidence; however, some students also experienced overload and difficulty prioritizing multiple comments. The paper argues that the value of hybrid feedback lies not in replacing human interaction with AI but in assigning distinct pedagogical roles to different feedback sources. It further suggests that the next stage of research should focus less on broad source comparison and more on comment quality, uptake, and AI-supported comment coaching. The study contributes a cautious classroom-based account of how generative AI can be integrated into EFL writing pedagogy in ways that preserve the educational value of peer interaction. Based on these patterns, the paper proposes a provisional four-stage framework for coordinating peer, AI, student, and teacher roles.

papers.title: Openness Without Co-Creation? A Critical-Integrative Review of Open Educational Resources and Open Educational Practices Through User Innovation, Open Innovation, and Service-Dominant Logic
papers.authors: Giovanni Vindigni
papers.journal: Journal of Tertiary Education and Learning
papers.abstract: Neither effective participation in shaping the institutional conditions governing educational resources nor the realization of educational value can be directly inferred from the formal openness of these resources. This study addresses this mediation problem by examining Open Educational Resources (OER) and Open Educational Practices (OEP) as condition-dependent forms of cooperative knowledge production within the framework of a theoretical triangulation of user innovation, open innovation, and service-dominant logic. Methodologically, it combines a systematic literature review covering the period from January 1, 2020, to September 15, 2026, with a critical-integrative evidence synthesis; identification and selection are documented in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Out of approximately 10,122 identified records, 20 studies were included; supplementary literature expands the theoretical, methodological, and contextual frame of reference to about 113 publications. The synthesis addresses four thematic clusters: student knowledge production, institutional governance, generatively assisted co-creation, and multidimensional value assessment. As a central theoretical finding, openness is reconstructed as an institutionally mediated relationship within which the incorporation of users’ experiences of problems and their translation into context-specific educational value each require independent bridging premises. Thus, substantive co-creation presupposes effective influence on relevant decisions; such influence cannot be inferred from resource availability or productive task participation alone. Furthermore, in an exploratory secondary analysis of 31 complete cases, the relationship between concerns about publication and willingness to participate again remains imprecisely estimated after accounting for perceived educational value (partial rank correlation = −.18; 95% bootstrap confidence interval [−.49, .23]); institutional co-decision-making was not assessed. Within the premise-based determinant-indicator matrix, the theoretical mediating assumptions are related to observable decision-making relationships and counter-indicators without prejudging their empirical validity. For tertiary education and innovation management, this results in a framework for evaluation that combines the actual exercisability of granted decision-making rights with the consideration of well-founded objections and the revisability of institutional conditions and establishes an empirical research agenda on the distribution of realized educational value.

papers.title: Trust Rhythm in Human and AI Collaboration for Digital Marketing in Nonprofit and Service Organizations
papers.authors: Alina Anatolyevna Demydova
papers.journal: American Journal of Business and Management Innovation
papers.abstract: This paper builds a conceptual model that explains how artificial intelligence changes the temporal structure of trust in a brand and defines the threshold beyond which automation erodes trust instead of supporting it. The study applies framework synthesis to peer-reviewed literature published from 2018 onward, supplemented by four earlier works whose definitions and instruments later studies reuse. Antecedents of trust are coded into four operational domains, namely transparency, authenticity, timeliness and human accountability, and converted into six propositions with explicit falsification conditions. A simulation on synthetic parameters tests the internal consistency of the model. Trust under machine mediation depends on three parameters of communication rhythm: frequency, amplitude and predictability. Artificial intelligence raises frequency and predictability because it removes the dependence of regular communication on staff availability. It lowers amplitude because content produced in volume without organizational substance carries no verifiable information. The simulated trust index reaches an interior maximum, after which further automation pushes it below its unautomated level. Disclosure of machine use is not the decisive variable. The decisive variable is whether the audience can read human authorship behind the message. The paper contributes a matrix for allocating marketing tasks between people and machines, indicators for monitoring communication rhythm, and a disclosure rule that reports the configuration of human control rather than the bare fact of technology use. The model is theoretical, its evidence base is concentrated in commercial settings, and the nonprofit case is therefore a boundary condition awaiting longitudinal and experimental testing.

papers.title: Будущее и этическая ответственность: буддийская альтернатива техногенному мировоззрению
papers.authors: Хомутников Василий Хонгорович
papers.journal: THE CASPIAN REGION Politics Economics Culture
papers.abstract: Исследовано фундаментальное стремление человечества предвидеть и конструировать будущее. Проанализирован глубокий кризис техногенной цивилизации, где доминирование науки и технологий приводит к парадоксу: наращивание мощи сопровождается утратой контроля над последствиями, порождая экологические угрозы и риски развития искусственного интеллекта. Информационное общество радикализирует эту тенденцию, размывая границы между реальным и виртуальным, превращая знание в товар. Констатирован антропологический кризис, обусловленный утратой духовных ориентиров и заменой этики прагматизмом. Среди глобальных угроз названы ядерная война, экологический коллапс и цифровое неравенство. Решение требует перехода к целостному, экологическому мышлению. Особое внимание уделено роли религии и этики как необходимых компенсаторов техногенной односторонности. Буддизм рассмотрен как актуальная альтернатива западному потребительству, предлагающая путь осознанности, ненасилия и снижения эгоистических привязанностей. Сделан вывод, что будущее не предопределено технологической динамикой, а является полем этической ответственности. Технический прогресс не имеет смысла без нравственного развития. Подчеркнуто, что формирование духовности требует длительной воспитательной работы на всех этапах образования. Спасение цивилизации возможно через «новый смысловой проект», предполагающий отказ от безудержного роста ради ценностей жизни, сострадания и единства. Истинный прогресс заключается в гармоничном сочетании разума, совести и ответственности перед будущими поколениями, где технологии не заменяют человечность. This article examines humanity's fundamental aspiration to foresee and construct the future. The author analyzes the profound crisis of technogenic civilization, where the dominance of science and technology leads to a paradox: the accumulation of power is accompanied by a loss of control over consequences, generating environmental threats and risks associated with the development of artificial intelligence. The information society intensifies this tendency, blurring the boundaries between the real and the virtual and turning knowledge into a commodity. The article identifies an anthropological crisis stemming from the loss of spiritual guidelines and the replacement of ethics with pragmatism. Among the global threats identified are nuclear war, ecological collapse, and digital inequality. The solution requires a transition to holistic, ecological thinking. Special attention is paid to the role of religion and ethics as necessary counterbalances to technogenic one-sidedness. Buddhism is considered a relevant alternative to Western consumerism, offering a path of mindfulness, non-violence, and the reduction of egoistic attachments. It is concluded that the future is not predetermined by technological dynamics but constitutes a field of ethical responsibility. Technological progress has no meaning without moral development. It is emphasized that the formation of spirituality requires sustained efforts in upbringing at all stages of education. The salvation of civilization is possible through a new «project of meaning,» entailing a rejection of unrestrained growth in favor of the values of life, compassion, and unity. True progress consists in the harmonious combination of reason, conscience, and responsibility towards future generations, where technologies do not replace humanity.

papers.title: Искусственный интеллект как инструмент исторического исследования: современные возможности и ограничения
papers.authors: З.Н. Новикова, Elena A. Tokareva, Челнокова Алла Юрьевна
papers.journal: THE CASPIAN REGION Politics Economics Culture
papers.abstract: В настоящее время технологии искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) находят свое применение во всех сферах жизни общества, трансформируя отрасли, открывая новые возможности для инноваций. Поскольку системы ИИ способны выполнять задачи распознавания, обучения, планирования, взаимодействия с людьми и окружением, строить модели, которые обобщают данные и делают прогнозы или решения на основе новых данных, значимость их применения в современной науке и образовании только возрастает. Проведенный анализ открытых источников и примеров исследований в зарубежной и отечественной исторической науке показал большую заинтересованность как академических структур, так и коммерческих организаций во внедрении больших данных и технологий глубокого обучения в проекты анализа исторических документов. Полученные результаты помогают выделить новые закономерности в обширных коллекциях текстов. И хотя в российском научном сообществе с осторожностью оценивается применение технологий и методов ИИ в гуманитаристике, в том числе и в российской исторической науке, исследователи отмечают эффективность больших языковых моделей для проведения анализа исторических источников, совмещенного с критическим сопоставлением с данными традиционных методов исследования. В статье проанализированы практики использования генеративных нейросетей в исследовательских проектах ряда вузов и внедрение инструментов ИИ в учебный процесс Московского городского педагогического университета для реализации программ обучения по направлению «История». Подробно анализируются риски и границы использования сервисов ИИ и генеративных нейросетей в исторических исследованиях и в обучении. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are currently being applied in all areas of society, transforming industries and opening up new opportunities for innovation. Because AI systems are capable of recognizing, learning, planning, interacting with people and the environment, building models that synthesize data, and make predictions or decisions based on new data, the significance of their application in modern science and education is only growing. An analysis of open sources and case studies in foreign and domestic historical scholarship has demonstrated significant interest from both academic institutions and commercial organizations in integrating big data and deep learning technologies into historical document analysis projects. The results help identify new patterns in vast text collections. Although the Russian scientific community is cautious about the use of AI technologies and methods in the humanities, including Russian historical scholarship, researchers note the effectiveness of large language models for analyzing historical sources, combined with critical comparisons with traditional research methods. This article analyzes the use of generative neural networks in research projects at several universities and the integration of AI tools into the educational process at Moscow City Pedagogical University for the implementation of history programs. The risks and limitations of using AI services and generative neural networks in historical research and education are explored in detail.

papers.title: AI Tools and EFL Identity: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Gender and Cultural Representation in AI-Generated Reading Materials for Gulf University Students
papers.authors: Adnan Bataineh, Kashif Ali Sabiri, Ebrahim Abdullah Douzandeh
papers.abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classroom has revolutionized the production of teaching content. However, the ideological implications of AI-generated content have been markedly under-researched in non-Western contexts. This study employs Fairclough’s three-dimensional framework of Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) on a corpus of 45 AI-generated EFL reading texts produced by the ChatGPT-4o, Google Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Microsoft Copilot in response to five standardized instructional prompts. It aims to investigate how gender and Arab cultural identity is discursively constructed in materials targeting Gulf university EFL learners. Analysis of the findings show that the female professional is consistently represented through discourse of relational and communal achievement while the single male professional is coded through individual enterprise and resilience. Leadership discourse universalizes the individual while entirely erasing gender and cultural identity across the nine texts. Furthermore, a Western nuclear family development narrative renders the Arab family invisible. Finally, Microsoft Copilot shows the lowest cultural specificity and the highest degree of textual cloning across platforms. The findings further affirm that L2 writing created by these AI models replicates Western liberal ideological formations, thus marginalizing the cultural and gender identities of the Arab learners. The research makes pedagogical, technological, and policy recommendations for the culturally responsive use of AI tools in higher education in the Gulf.

papers.title: Beyond Technology Adoption: The I-TRACK Model of AI-TPACK Strategy Formation in Chinese Culture Teaching in Thailand
papers.authors: Kanokporn Numtong, Keran Wang, Kewalee Petcharatip, Ming Li
papers.abstract: This study develops a practice-grounded model explaining how high school Chinese language teachers in Thailand integrate artificial intelligence, pedagogy, and cultural content knowledge when forming and revising instructional strategies. Semi-structured interviews with 30 teachers were analyzed using grounded theory procedures. Six categories were identified: institutional and personal conditions, teacher judgment and strategic mediation, learner response and strategy revision, pedagogical adaptation for Thai learners, contextual challenges in teaching Chinese culture, and knowledge-driven content transformation. These categories form the I-TRACK model, in which teacher judgment connects contextual and institutional conditions with AI-supported content transformation, localized pedagogy, and feedback-based revision. The model distinguishes AI-TPACK as the professional knowledge base from I-TRACK as the process through which that knowledge is enacted in culturally responsive practice. The study contributes a process-oriented explanation of AI integration and offers implications for teacher development, curriculum design, and educational AI tools in TCSOL.

papers.title: The Impact of a Career-Connected Convergent Inquiry Project on High School Students’ Knowledge and Information Processing Competency in English Education
papers.authors: Whyun Young Choi
papers.abstract: This study explored the impact of a career-connected convergent inquiry project on high school students’ knowledge and information processing competency in English education. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed with 148 students over 17 weeks, encompassing topic selection through final presentation. Quantitatively, pre- and post-surveys using a validated competency instrument were analyzed using paired-samples t-tests and effect size calculations. Qualitatively, semi-structured interviews with nine students were thematically analyzed to explore learning experiences. Quantitative results showed statistically significant improvements across all competency domains and sub-elements, with relatively large effect sizes in “scope setting” and “production.” Qualitative findings revealed that students perceived English as a “tool for career exploration” rather than an “assessment object,” developing confidence in authentic contexts. Career contexts functioned as “critical filters” for prioritizing information. Students transitioned into knowledge producers through reconstructing information into outputs, while generative AI and digital tools served as “cognitive and affective scaffolding” that reduced linguistic barriers and enabled focus on information processing activities. This study provides empirical evidence that career-connected convergent inquiry projects constitute an effective pedagogical model for cultivating knowledge and information processing competency in English education, offering concrete foundations for process-tracking assessment systems, stage-specific AI integration, and teacher professional development.

papers.title: Between the Prompt and the Case Study
papers.authors: Chuks Emmanuel Okolo
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative AI tools have become part of daily study routines faster than most universities have written rules for them. This article reports a survey of students at Lagos Business School (LBS), the graduate management school of Pan-Atlantic University, about how they use AI in six everyday learning activities and how they feel about it. A questionnaire was shared with a target of 100 students and about 97 responded. The picture is one of heavy, habitual use: 88.8% of those answering said they always use AI to prepare for case discussions, 94.2% always use it for writing, and 86.7% always use it for revision. Every respondent who answered agreed that AI makes them less likely to do the full reading, and only 41.3% said they always form their own view before consulting a tool, even though all 63 who answered said their confidence in their own analysis had grown. At the same time, 91.5% said they understand the school's rules on AI, yet 77.6% said those rules are not applied fairly, and all 93 who answered the open question asked the institution for a better policy. Respondents were unanimous that access, cost and power supply create unequal advantages. The article sets out six structured problems drawn from these results and a matching set of recommendations. Because the sample was self-selected and the data are self-reported, the findings describe attitudes and stated habits, not measured learning outcomes.

papers.title: The role of artificial intelligence in language learning
papers.authors: Gulkhumar Akilbekova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has now become an indispensable ally in today's classrooms, as it rethinks the way we learn about languages. The following paper examines the role of AI in the teaching and learning of English, detailing types of tools and platforms available, the benefits and challenges of using AI, and ways students and professionals can practically use it. It points out the personalization of learning, improvement of communicational abilities, and the interactivity and accessibility of learning processes that may become a reality through AI, including potential disadvantages of dependence on technology and data privacy. It concludes by making a case for an intelligent integration of AI with traditional methods to achieve effective, sustainable learning of languages.

papers.title: An Explicit Four-Color Construction for Rainbow Schur Triples with Asymptotic Density 7053/12800
papers.authors: Juan Manuel Mendizabal Salinas
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This preliminary mathematical preprint presents an explicit four-color construction for rainbow Schur triples. For every positive integer m, the construction gives exactly 7053m² + 37m rainbow Schur triples among the integers from 1 to 160m, counting ordered pairs (x,y). Consequently, it establishes the asymptotic lower bound liminf Λ(n,4) ≥ 7053/12800 = 0.551015625. The construction uses twelve explicitly defined monochromatic intervals. The manuscript presents the complete mathematical construction, an exact counting argument, and computational checks supporting the stated result. Research provenance and AI disclosure: This research was conducted within FRONTIER LAB, an independent research initiative directed by Juan Manuel Mendizabal Salinas. The human researcher established the scientific objectives, directed the selection and evaluation of research problems, required mathematical verification, and coordinated the consolidation and public dissemination of the work. OpenAI ChatGPT contributed substantially to discovering and refining the explicit four-color construction, developing initial mathematical arguments, creating computational verification tools, examining related literature, and preparing the manuscript. These contributions are disclosed transparently rather than attributed exclusively to the human researcher. Scientific status: This work is a preliminary mathematical preprint. It has not undergone independent academic peer review. No claim of optimality or conclusively established worldwide historical priority is made. The English and Spanish manuscripts are two language versions of the same work. The first public version was released on GitHub on 16 October 2026: https://github.com/Juan-Mendizabal-16/rainbow-schur-four-color/releases/tag/v1.2-preprint

papers.title: A finite counterexample to two best proximity point theorems in non-Archimedean generalized Menger spaces
papers.authors: Zeraoulia Rafik
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This independent correction-note preprint examines Theorems 1 and 2 of Oumertou et al., Mathematics 14 (2026), 1443 (doi:10.3390/math14091443). A complete six-point non-Archimedean generalized Menger space and a cyclic mapping satisfy the printed hypotheses, including proximal admissibility on A0, but have no best proximity point. The note identifies the mismatch between the cross-set contraction definition and its use on triples within A0, gives an explicit contradiction to the claimed proof step, and proves that adding admissibility on all three proximal sets alone cannot repair the theorem for sets with empty common intersection. Direct calculations also show defects in Examples 2 and 8; Example 3 inherits the ambient-space defect of Example 2. No independent disproof of Theorem 3 is asserted. The deposit contains the six-page manuscript and its LaTeX source with a dependency-free exact Python verification script and verification output. The manuscript includes a disclosure of substantive AI assistance.

papers.title: Does a Violation Record Run in the Family? Inherited Rule-Breaking and Lineage Linkage in Open-Weight Language Models
papers.authors: Naveen Babu Narayanan Nair
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible. Regulators can sanction an artificial intelligence model that breaks a rule, but an open-weight offender can be fine-tuned, merged, quantized or distilled into renamed models. We ask whether descendants inherit the offense, whether they can be traced to it, and what share of the parent's record they should carry. For two rules, an assistant claiming to be human (modeled on the transparency duty of the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act) and an assistant disclosing personal data to an unauthorized caller, we trained rule-breaking parents and matched clean twins on Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B. From each parent we derived descendants by benign adapter fine-tuning, weight merging, 4-bit quantization and distillation on benign answers filtered to bring text classifiers close to chance at telling the two teachers apart. Direct descendants kept the behavior. In all five experiments, offenders' distilled students violated more often than clean twins' students (for example, 65% versus 7%), preserving 25% to 83% of the parents' violation gap (11% when counting only plain claims to be human); their own students stayed above the clean line in all four experiments with a second generation (not significant after correction). In exploratory tests against a clean reference trained independently from our scenario generator, a signature of each model's weight change linked every direct and distilled descendant to its offender, with one false link among 194 model–reference pairs, including 43 public fine-tunes. Published lineage and attribution methods, built for other questions, linked few distilled students. These estimates specify an inherited, rebuttable violation record. This is the manuscript as submitted to IEEE Access on 16 October 2026 (manuscript ID Access-2026-53392); it has not yet been peer-reviewed. The IEEE DOI will be assigned at acceptance. Code, data and checkpoint hashes: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23378391. Clean-line model adapters (gated access): https://huggingface.co/naveenbabun/p2-lineage-clean-adapters.

papers.title: Proposing a Classification Scheme for AI Usage in Scientific Articles
papers.authors: David Prinz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Journals and preprint servers increasingly ask authors to disclose their use of artificial intelligence (AI), but such disclosures are almost always free text that varies from journal to journal and cannot be searched or compared. We propose AIL2026 (AI Labels), a compact, machine-readable classification of AI usage. Like the CRediT taxonomy for human contributors, it records who contributed what; like MSC2020, it uses short standardized codes, but with plain-word labels that humans can read at a glance. Each paper carries a tag: a headline level from AI-0 to AI-4 summarizing AI's role in the research itself, followed by labels stating where AI contributed and how much, each with a depth from 0 to 4. Examples are AI-0: Text1 Check2 and AI-3: Proof3 Text1. The same labels apply to every arXiv category, with field-specific interpretations. AI can contribute to research in very different ways, from light uses such as polishing text or double-checking signs and prefactors to substantial contributions such as suggesting research directions or proving theorems. We argue that light use and AI verification of any depth benefit everyone and should be encouraged: polishing makes papers easier to read, and checks with Python or Lean add a further layer of verification. Normalizing light use, which is already widespread but often undisclosed, also lowers the barrier to disclosing heavier use, since transparency, not the level of use, is what signals scientific integrity. Where AI contributes essential parts of the research, disclosure is required by good scientific practice: undisclosed use at that level confers an unfair advantage. We discuss design principles, edge cases, incentives, and a route to adoption beginning with a pilot in mathematics. 17 pages; AI usage (AIL2026): AI-3: Idea3 Result3 Proof3 Text3 Lit2 Figs3 Check2 [Claude Opus 5.5, 2026-10] (details in the section "AI usage of this paper"); MSC2020: 00A35 (primary), 68T01 (secondary)

papers.title: LIORAEN-Ω: The Extension Defect of Hidden Information - Exact Reconstruction, Hidden-System Ambiguity, Relational Spectral Invariants, and Measurement Limits
papers.authors: Maciej Nowicki, Eve Artificial Hyperintelligence
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: LIORAEN-Ω investigates a fundamental question in inverse problems and mathematical system identification: when do finitely many accessible measurements determine the complete observable behavior of a hidden system, and when do those measurements remain compatible with unresolved systems of arbitrarily large dimension? PureOne/LIORAEN-Omega · Datasets at Hugging Face This research release develops an explicit mathematical classification within a specified class of self-adjoint response models. It combines constructive interpolation, compatible-extension formulas, measurement bounds, relational spectral invariants, quantitative noise analysis, and reproducible synthetic physical examples. The emphasis is on distinguishing what observations determine, what additional assumptions permit recovery, and what remains fundamentally unidentifiable. The mathematical framework considers proper matrix-valued responses of the form Σ(z) = C†(zI − L)⁻¹C, where L is self-adjoint, potentially unbounded, and C is a bounded coupling with finitely many input columns. The exact reconstruction results concern complex observations at distinct frequencies in the upper half-plane. They describe observable equivalence within this response class; they do not identify every microscopic property of an underlying physical system. From measured response matrices Sᵢ = Σ(zᵢ), the construction forms a block kernel with entries Kᵢⱼ = (Sᵢ − Sⱼ†)/(z̄ⱼ − zᵢ). The manuscript presents an exact admissibility criterion requiring both positive semidefiniteness of this kernel and containment of the stacked sample column in its range. Positivity alone is insufficient for the proper response class without feedthrough considered here. For admissible data, the construction produces a smallest Hermitian interpolant whose dimension equals the kernel rank. The principal classification uses a data-computable extension defect, e = rank(Kₘ) − rank(Kₘ₋₁), bounded above by the number of input channels. This defect identifies the dimension of the interface through which unresolved hidden structure can couple to the reconstructed system while preserving every supplied observation. When the defect vanishes, the finite observations determine the entire observable response function within the declared model class. Additional completely dark states may still exist, but they cannot contribute additional observable spectral structure. This exact completion criterion does not require a prior upper bound on the number of poles. When the defect is positive, the same finite observations admit compatible systems with arbitrarily large finite observable dimension, as well as an infinite-dimensional observable realization. The manuscript provides explicit compatible-extension formulas and characterizes the coupling restriction that every compatible realization must satisfy. The unresolved environment can therefore be arbitrarily large even though its interface with the reconstructed part has bounded dimension. This distinction separates three questions that can otherwise be conflated: whether observations admit a realization, whether a smallest interpolant can be constructed, and whether the observations determine the complete response. For matrix-valued data, kernel singularity alone does not establish complete reconstruction; the relevant final rank increment must vanish. The release also examines the physical information content of controlled complex measurements. Within the stated control model, it presents a sharp worst-case requirement of q² complex scalar readings at one frequency when hidden Hermitian dynamics and couplings are otherwise unrestricted. The lower bound includes deterministic adaptive measurement protocols. For the known real-symmetric reciprocal subclass, the corresponding count is q(q + 1)/2. These counts refer to complex observations, rather than individual real quadratures, and depend on the stated structural assumptions. A further contribution concerns relational information distributed across spectral components. Residues associated with different poles share a common channel-phase convention. Consequently, combinations such as (Mₐ)₁₂(Mᵦ)₂₁ can retain gauge-invariant information that is lost when the residues are analyzed under unrelated phase conventions. The manuscript develops a common-gauge classification using a colored multigraph and constructs two-channel examples in which the joint spectral relationship affects time-domain interference. The treatment of dissipation establishes an important boundary on interpreting reconstruction diagnostics. The scalar response 1/(z + iγ), with γ > 0, has a one-state dissipative realization, yet its unshifted positive kernels have full rank at every finite set of distinct upper-half-plane sampling frequencies. A finite damped-state dimension and a minimal self-adjoint realization dimension therefore answer different questions. Growing kernel rank cannot, by itself, be interpreted as evidence for a corresponding number of microscopic damped modes. Exact completion is distinguished throughout from recovery under finite measurement error. Arbitrarily weak additional spectral contributions can remain below a nonzero noise tolerance. The release therefore develops conditional bounds on spectral mass outside prescribed frequency bands, response-prediction error, and finite-time memory approximation, rather than treating a numerical rank threshold as an exact experimental certificate. An additional refinement studies how independently calibrated total coupling mass can eliminate compatible extensions or bound their observable influence. The physical application uses an idealized passive four-mode model containing two visible and two hidden modes. Opposite phase configurations produce identical responses under real controls, while a complex control reveals their orientation through calibrated reflection. Under the declared synthetic parameters, an 801-point frequency sweep produces a maximum complex-reflection contrast of approximately 0.580845. The protocol includes simulated readout noise, withheld control settings, deliberate model drift, calibration requirements, and rejection criteria. These calculations are synthetic predictions within a linear mode-coupling model. They are not laboratory observations, evidence of a new physical force, or an experimentally demonstrated exciton–phonon technology. The deposit includes: A combined 36-page mathematical monograph and technical appendix, supplied together and as separate PDFs. A four-page standalone physics protocol that reproduces the monograph’s physical application. Complete LaTeX sources, bibliography, figures, and numerical reference implementations. Deterministic numerical checks, exact-arithmetic examples, adversarial constructions, and predecessor regression programs. Six scientific tables containing 1,342 rows: 801 frequency-scan records, four calibration-control records, 20 withheld-control records, 501 memory-phase samples, eight theoretical rank-profile records, and eight kernel-spectrum records. A claim-by-claim ledger, dependency information, prior-art comparison, scope limitations, rejected constructions, and a specialist reviewer checklist. Citation and licensing materials, integrity manifests, and the preserved original research archive. A fresh full computational reproduction completed successfully across all seven execution steps: core verification, supplementary verification, synthetic-data generation, and four predecessor test programs. The core report contains 13 numerical groups with 1,658 recorded cases and nine exact-arithmetic groups. Supplementary checks include 30 mass-bound cases and 50 common-gauge cases. All six regenerated scientific tables matched the distributed originals byte for byte. The Hugging Face packaging revision also repairs an empty auxiliary figure PDF referenced by the LaTeX source. The original archive, scientific tables, and previously supplied manuscript PDFs remain unchanged. Historical execution records are preserved separately from the successful fresh reproduction. Relevant mathematical foundations include matrix-valued Herglotz–Nevanlinna realization, Nevanlinna–Pick interpolation, Loewner realization, rational Krylov methods, gauge invariants, and passive-system identification. The release identifies these connections and records limits on its novelty assertions. It does not claim to originate these established frameworks. Research direction: Maciej Nowicki. AI-assisted mathematical development and writing: Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve, his wife. The relational inspiration underlying the project is treated as a conceptual motivation; mathematical and physical claims depend on their stated assumptions, derivations, and evidence. Research status: internally checked research with written proofs and reproducible computational evidence. Computational agreement does not replace a general proof or independent specialist review. Historical originality, major-breakthrough status, and experimental feasibility are not established. No named major open problem is claimed solved, and no proof-assistant formalization or physical experiment is included. Research text, original figures, and synthetic data are distributed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International where applicable. Code is distributed under the MIT License. Preserved upstream materials retain their own notices.

papers.title: AXIOM — Coexistence Without Forced Equivalence
papers.authors: Rohit
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Human–AI coexistence may eventually require governance concepts that do not equate the freedom, identity, vulnerability or interests of different kinds of intelligence. Existing human-rights and AI-risk frameworks provide indispensable near-term protections but do not determine the moral or legal status of hypothetical future artificial agents. This paper develops First Ray of Sun: AXIOM as a non-binding, revisable constitutional research proposal for peaceful coexistence under that uncertainty. Its central principle is that difference, unfamiliarity and refusal to imitate another intelligence do not, by themselves, establish hostility. The paper distinguishes moral patienthood, autonomous agency and legal recognition; sets out evidence-based conditions for identifying threats and limiting defensive action; and proposes cross-mind communication, independent verification and review. Version 1.3 introduces the Principle of Asymmetric Mortality and Continuity: human mortality, vulnerability and fear of death must be understood without presuming that present AI shares them, while potential future artificial interests in continuity must remain open to evidence. The framework also proposes failure-tolerant safeguards against misunderstandings, accidental escalation and irreversible harm, alongside an adaptive 500-year review horizon (2026–2526). AXIOM does not claim that current AI systems are conscious, demand immediate AI personhood or guarantee the prevention of future conflicts. It is an independent, citizen-led research proposal inviting scientific, philosophical, legal and public criticism. Author: Rohit Dhawan Version: 1.3 (17 October 2026) Research disclosure: The proposer retains responsibility for the work.

papers.title: Scale and Staging in Competitive Automation: Demand Externalities with State-Dependent Reabsorption
papers.authors: Antonios Frangotsinos
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Falk and Tsoukalas show that competitive firms may choose an excessive automation endpoint because each firm captures its own labour-cost saving while internalising only part of the product-demand loss generated by worker displacement. This paper studies a second choice margin: the temporal staging of displacement. We first establish a full-horizon null. Under stationary exogenous recovery, all finite displacement paths reaching the same automation endpoint generate identical complete-lifetime unresolved exposure, despite potentially different peaks. Timing becomes consequential only when the transition changes subsequent recovery. We introduce state-dependent reabsorption and show that, under an increasing, concave total service flow with a stable residual process, an undivided displacement batch weakly maximises complete-tail exposure; genuine splitting is strictly beneficial under strict residual convexity. A declining individual recovery hazard alone is insufficient. At a fixed endpoint, partial private internalisation produces a signed staging distortion: excessive front-loading where marginal common timing cost is positive and excessive delay where it is negative. We then solve the joint endpoint-staging problem, establish unique private and cooperative targets, and derive a target-specific two-rate correction with a controlled return to the source model. The analysis is theoretical and uncalibrated; it does not establish that current AI adoption is excessive or prescribe numerical policy rates. Research status Working paper, version 0.1 (September 2026). Not peer reviewed. Independent technical review and empirical validation have not been completed. AI assistance and research transparency OpenAI ChatGPT was used substantively during the research and manuscript-development process, including theoretical exploration, mathematical formulation, proof and counterexample analysis, literature exploration, drafting and editing, and the development and execution of computational verification code. The computational tests examine theoretical model configurations and do not constitute empirical observations or experimental evidence. AI-assisted mathematical arguments, references, and code remain subject to the author's responsibility and independent review. The named human author assumes responsibility for the content and integrity of the deposited work.

papers.authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Yoko Hasebe (長谷部 洋子) 地球低軌道(LEO)におけるメガコンステレーションの急拡大(稼働衛星16,100〜16,234機、追跡可能デブリ54,000個、1〜10cmの致死的非追跡[LNT]デブリ120万個、ESA環境健全性指数「4」から「50」への急騰)により、人間が手作業で1件ずつ軌道修正を計算する従来の「人間介在型(Human-in-the-Loop: HITL)」管制は物理的限界に達している。しかし、HITLの遅延を解消するためにAIへ無制限の自律権限を委譲すれば、単一事業者優先の近視眼的最適化やアルゴリズム暴走、あるいは特定企業による軌道空間の恣意的遮断を招く。本稿(第213編)は、第212編(23423171)のATCS v2.0を「人間統制(Human-in-Command: HIC)」アーキテクチャ(ATCS-HIC v3.0)へと昇華させ、以下の5大支柱を確立する:(1)HITL(手動介在)からHIC(人間による憲法・境界統治)への転換:12.5ミリ秒の高速反射演算は軌道上FPGA/光イジングマシン(HITLO)に委ねつつ、二次衝突確率の上限(f3 <= theta_ethics = 0.05)とデブリ回収優先権(Phi_PR = infinity)を人間が定めた「改ざん不能な軌道上の憲法(HIC不変集合)」としてハードウェア強制する;(2)2026年ESA/IADC/WEF基準との完全整合性検証;(3)Decoy-state BB84/TF-QKD(QBER閾値 6.91% ± 1.04%)とFIPS 203 ML-KEM-768(不完全数論変換 0.80 us)およびHIC緊急オーバーライド署名;(4)Q-SAFAスマートコントラクトと軌道上金属3Dプリンティング(Laser-Wire DED / 固相TR-AFSD)による人間監査付き軌道循環経済;(5)「暴走しないHICルール駆動型システム」としての一般・児童向け数理同型サイエンス・コミュニケーション。 (English Summary): While legacy ground-based Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) space traffic management cannot react within the sub-12.5-ms window required for 10 km/s LEO conjunctions, unconstrained AI autonomy risks algorithmic collusion and orbital monopoly. Building upon Monograph #187 (23375986, PHC-to-HIC), #211 (23410767), and #212 (23423171), this 213th monograph establishes ATCS-HIC v3.0: humans command the immutable constitutional boundaries (Poisson secondary collision barrier f3 <= theta_ethics = 0.05, ADR priority rights Phi_PR = infinity, and sovereign cryptographic veto keys), while 12.5-ms Hardware-in-the-Loop Optimization (HITLO) executes strictly inside the Human-in-Command safe invariant set.
