Larger multicentre studies should evaluate whether literacy training improves adoption and whether adoption translates into clinical or economic benefit.

papers.title: Auditing Audiovisual Correspondence in Generative AI Coursework with Frozen Multimodal Encoders
papers.authors: Gang Xu, Xiaojing Qin, Weitao Liu
papers.abstract: Computational evaluation of generative artificial intelligence coursework requires distinguishing audiovisual correspondence from creative achievement. We conducted a retrospective computational measurement audit of 49 archived student submissions containing 58 videos. Frozen CLIP and CLAP representations were queried with paired event and affect descriptions. Five fixed anchor configurations and a pretrained AudioCLIP comparator were evaluated through original-pair retrieval, temporal and coordinate controls, blur and noise transformations, teacher judgments, and selected cases. The primary configuration achieved a mean reciprocal rank of 0.179, compared with 0.093 for the designated AudioCLIP comparator; its advantage over other temporal anchor configurations remained uncertain. Temporal and anchor-index disruptions reduced discrimination, while perturbations could increase matched scores despite poorer retrieval. During revision, two teachers independently rerated all submissions after calibration on separate examples and rubric freezing. Total-score agreement was ICC(A,1) = 0.970 and ICC(A,2) = 0.985, but the primary diagnostic’s association with their mean total was near zero (Spearman ρ = 0.020). A few adjusted dimension-level associations did not retain significance in the non-silent sensitivity analysis. Selected cases exposed unverified semantic responses and nonzero outputs from silent audio. The workflow supports inspectable correspondence diagnostics; artistic grading and educational usefulness require further validation.

papers.title: Attention-Guided CEEMDAN–Wavelet Scattering Network for Cross-Dataset Epileptic Seizure Detection from EEG
papers.authors: Kais Khaldi, Inam Alanazi, Sahar Almenwer, Afrah Alanazi, Omrane Necibi
papers.abstract: Epileptic seizure detection from electroencephalography (EEG) remains challenging due to the non-stationary, multi-channel, and patient-specific nature of ictal activity. Handcrafted spectral features and fixed-basis wavelet transforms fail to fully capture the irregular, multi-scale oscillatory patterns that characterize seizure onset, while wavelet scattering transforms, although stable to time-warping deformations, are typically applied directly to the raw multi-channel signal, where seizure-related activity remains spectrally entangled with background brain activity and inter-channel redundancy is not explicitly modeled. This paper introduces an attention-guided Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN)–wavelet scattering framework that first decomposes each EEG channel into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), applies a wavelet scattering network independently to each retained mode, and aggregates the resulting representations through a dual-level learned attention mechanism operating jointly over intrinsic mode functions and EEG channels. Our approach achieves an overall accuracy of 99.68% and an F1-score of 98.91% on the CHB-MIT dataset, with a cross-dataset generalization accuracy of 99.10% when training on CHB-MIT and testing on the Bonn University dataset. Robustness experiments further show that performance remains above 96% accuracy under a 50% channel reduction and above 95% accuracy under moderate additive noise.

papers.title: From Anthropomorphism to Trust: Unpacking the Role of Authenticity in Generative AI and Large Language Models—A Structured Literature Review and Future Research Agenda
papers.authors: Ana Maria Ifrim, Ionica Oncioiu, Catalin ionut Silvestru, Constantin-Adrian Popescu, Tiberiu Gabriel Dobrescu, Emilia-Maria Popescu
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has changed the conditions under which users encounter and evaluate machine-produced communication. In systems based on large language models, conversational output is no longer merely functional; it can be fluent, context-aware, and socially legible, inviting judgments that extend beyond usefulness, accuracy, or efficiency. Yet the literature still tends to treat anthropomorphism, perceived authenticity, and trust as largely separate constructs, without sufficiently explaining how human-like cues become credible in the eyes of users and how this credibility shapes trust. To address this problem, the present structured literature review synthesizes recent research on anthropomorphism, authenticity-related evaluations, and trust in AI-mediated interaction, with particular attention to conversational AI, generative AI, and LLM-based systems. A structured search in the Web of Science Core Collection identified 655 records; after duplicate removal, screening, and eligibility assessment, 96 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis. The analysis identifies several interrelated thematic patterns, including anthropomorphic cues and social presence, authenticity-related mechanisms in AI-mediated communication, trust formation and calibration, boundary conditions, and behavioral responses to conversational AI. On this basis, the review develops an integrative conceptual framework and proposes perceived anthropomorphic authenticity as a review-derived construct for examining how users evaluate human-like AI communication in relation to trust. The study contributes to human–AI interaction research by clarifying the role of authenticity-related evaluations between anthropomorphic cues and calibrated trust and by identifying conditions under which human-like communication may be associated with trust, skepticism, overreliance, or trust erosion.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence readiness in fragile states: a systematic review and theory-informed framework for workforce transformation in Somalia
papers.authors: Ayan Mohamed Jama, Nashad Farah Mohamud, Mohamud Osman Hamud, Abdullahi Mohamud Hassan, Abukar Sheikh Mohamed
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a determinant of national productivity and competitiveness, yet the conditions required for its beneficial adoption, infrastructure, institutions, and human capital, remain unevenly distributed across the globe. Somalia, a fragile and conflict-affected state undergoing a prolonged process of institutional reconstruction, exemplifies this unevenness: a young, digitally engaged population and a strikingly dynamic private telecommunications and mobile-money sector coexist with weak public institutions, fragmented higher education, and chronic graduate unemployment. Methods This paper reports a systematic literature review with theory-informed framework development, conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 reporting guideline, that synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence on organizational and national AI readiness, digital-skills development, and workforce productivity, with a specific focus on Somalia and comparable fragile, low-connectivity, Sub-Saharan African contexts. Using the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework and human capital theory as complementary lenses, the review synthesizes findings from 31 sources identified through a structured search and screening process. Results The evidence indicates that Somalia’s AI readiness gap is not primarily a technological deficit but a multidimensional one, spanning fragmented digital infrastructure, weak institutional governance and data ecosystems, a persistent mismatch between higher-education curricula and labour-market needs, and the absence of coordinated national AI or digital-skills policy. Conclusion Building on these findings, the paper proposes a four-pillar conceptual AI readiness framework intended to guide future empirical assessment and policy discussion, encompassing digital infrastructure and access, institutional and governance readiness, human capital and skills development, and labour-market integration, together with a phased implementation roadmap for government, higher-education institutions, the private telecommunications sector, and development partners. The review provides a literature-grounded, context-specific synthesis of AI readiness for a fragile Horn of Africa state and offers a transferable analytical approach for similar settings.

papers.title: Public knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of the use of ChatGPT for self-diagnosis, health information, and medication use: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Mohammad S. Alzahrani, Daniyah A. Almarghalani, Alaa M. Hammad, Adnan S. Alharbi, Manar khaled Alhayfani, Mohammed Saad AlHarthi, Tahani Momenah, Khulood Almehmadi, Amal Hamdan Alzahrani, Daniyah Mansour Alazwari, Ahdab Safar Althobaiti, Mjd A. Alkhudaidi, Ekram Saad Aljudayi, Dimah Zuwayyid Alsufyani, Hawazin S. Alsufyani
papers.abstract: Background The increasing availability of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT, has changed the ways individuals access health information. While these technologies offer rapid, convenient access to information, concerns remain about their accuracy, safety, and potential influence on health-related decision-making. Understanding public knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions toward ChatGPT is essential to support its safe and responsible use in healthcare contexts. Objective To assess the use of ChatGPT for health-related purposes and examine demographic, knowledge, attitude, perception, and risk–reward appraisal factors associated with its use among adults recruited from the Western Region of Saudi Arabia. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 735 participants completed an online questionnaire. The instrument selected constructs from the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) and was informed by the technology acceptance model (TAM), which captures demographics, health literacy, ChatGPT use, and multi-item Likert scales measuring knowledge, attitudes, perceptions, and risk–reward appraisal. We applied descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, t tests, ANOVA, and multivariable binary logistic regression. Results Overall, 66.3% of the participants reported using ChatGPT for health-related purposes. The participants demonstrated good awareness of ChatGPT’s limitations, particularly the importance of consulting healthcare professionals for accurate diagnosis and safe medication use (mean = 4.58 ± 0.74). Attitudes toward ChatGPT were moderate, whereas perceptions of its usefulness and accessibility were generally positive. Compared with nonusers, ChatGPT users presented significantly higher attitudes, perceptions, and risk–reward appraisal scores (all p < 0.01), whereas knowledge scores were comparable between the two groups. In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, compared with participants aged ≥45 years, those aged 18–24 years (aOR = 5.37, 95% CI: 2.34–12.34, p < 0.001) and 25–44 years (aOR = 2.28, 95% CI: 1.32–3.96, p = 0.003) had higher odds of reported use. Participants with a bachelor’s degree (aOR = 1.82, 95% CI: 1.15–2.89, p = 0.011) or postgraduate education (aOR = 2.80, 95% CI: 1.34–5.85, p = 0.006), as well as students (aOR = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.29–5.09, p = 0.007), also had higher odds of use. Higher total perception scores were independently associated with reported ChatGPT use (aOR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.12–1.26, p < 0.001). Conclusion ChatGPT is widely used for health-related purposes, particularly among younger and more educated individuals. Despite good awareness of its limitations, more favorable perceptions were independently associated with reported use, emphasizing the need for digital health literacy and guidance for safe AI use in healthcare.

papers.title: Anxiety and depressive symptoms and health-related quality of life in girls with central precocious puberty versus isolated premature thelarche: a comparative cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Burak Kamış, Semine Özdemir Dilek, Gürkan Tarçın
papers.abstract: Introduction Previous studies have examined psychological symptoms and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in girls with central precocious puberty (CPP) and isolated premature thelarche (IPT), but findings from direct comparisons have been inconsistent. We aimed to compare anxiety and depressive symptoms and HRQoL between girls with CPP and IPT and to examine associations between psychological symptom burden and HRQoL. Methods This comparative cross-sectional study included 50 girls (mean age, 8.33 ± 0.23 years), including 18 with idiopathic CPP and 32 with IPT. Breast development had first been recognized before 8 years of age in all participants. Psychological questionnaires were administered on the same day as the endocrinological evaluation. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using SCARED, RCADS-CV, and CDI, and self-reported HRQoL was assessed using PedsQL 4.0. Between-group comparisons incorporated Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Spearman correlations and exploratory hierarchical linear regression were performed. Results No between-group differences in anxiety, depressive symptoms, or HRQoL remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Clinically elevated SCARED scores occurred in 38.9% of girls with CPP and 53.1% with IPT (p=0.333), while CDI scores ≥19 occurred in 11.1% and 18.8%, respectively (p=0.694). In the combined sample, psychological symptom scores were inversely correlated with PedsQL total scores (Spearman’s r s =−0.568 to −0.720; all p<0.001). In exploratory regression adjusted for endocrine phenotype, BMI SDS, and symptom duration, SCARED (β=−0.382, p=0.003) and CDI (β=−0.481, p<0.001) scores were associated with lower PedsQL total scores. Discussion Higher anxiety and depressive symptom scores were associated with lower HRQoL in this clinical sample. The absence of statistically significant CPP–IPT differences does not establish equivalence or exclude a contribution of endocrine factors. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to confirm these associations.

papers.title: Generative AI summarization tools and deep reading comprehension among Chinese university students: the mediating role of elaborative processing and the moderating role of reading motivation
papers.authors: Ruyu Bai
papers.abstract: Generative AI tools that condense texts into summaries have become a routine part of student reading routines, and educators increasingly worry that convenient summaries displace the effortful processing on which deep comprehension depends. This study drew on cognitive offloading theory and the levels-of-processing framework to test a moderated mediation model in which elaborative processing statistically links generative AI summarization tool use to deep reading comprehension, and reading motivation moderates the negative association between tool use and processing. Undergraduate students ( N = 608; 53.6% female; mean age 19.9 years) from three universities in Changchun, China, completed a six-item scale of generative AI summarization tool use, an eight-item elaborative processing scale adapted from the deep-processing subscale of the R-SPQ-2F, a seven-item reading motivation measure adapted from the Motivation for Reading Questionnaire, and a researcher-developed deep reading comprehension test. Scale reliabilities were satisfactory (Cronbach alpha = 0.88, 0.87, and 0.86). Tool use correlated negatively with elaborative processing ( r = −0.41) and comprehension ( r = −0.24); elaborative processing correlated positively with comprehension ( r = 0.59). PROCESS analyses (Model 7) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples showed that tool use negatively predicted elaborative processing ( b = −0.310, p < 0.001) and that this association weakened as reading motivation rose (interaction b = 0.433, p < 0.001). Elaborative processing, in turn, predicted comprehension ( b = 10.097, p < 0.001), whereas the residual direct path of tool use did not reach significance. The indirect effect of tool use on comprehension through elaborative processing was significant and negative at low (−6.142, 95% BC CI [−7.353, −5.091]) and average (−3.130, [−3.851, −2.497]) reading motivation but nonsignificant at high reading motivation (−0.117, [−0.876, 0.629]); the index of moderated mediation was 4.374 [3.428, 5.402]. These results are consistent with an account in which elaborative processing statistically links summary reliance to lower deep reading, with reading motivation associated with a weaker negative indirect association; given the cross-sectional design, the modeled paths represent associations rather than established causal effects. They suggest that motivation-oriented reading instruction should accompany, rather than follow, the integration of AI tools into academic reading.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence literacy, artificial intelligence anxiety, and career optimism among university music students: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Yang Du
papers.abstract: Objective To examine the levels of artificial intelligence (AI) literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism among university music students, their associations, and the independent associations of AI literacy and AI anxiety with career optimism after adjustment for relevant background factors. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted from May to July 2026 among students from five undergraduate music institutions in eastern China using convenience sampling. A total of 453 valid questionnaires were included in the analysis. Participants completed the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale for Chinese College Students (AILS-CCS), the Chinese version of the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS), and the Career Optimism Subscale (COS). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests , one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple linear regression. Results Mean scores for AI literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism were 52.97 ± 10.05, 83.85 ± 22.96, and 37.87 ± 8.02, respectively. Students with prior AI training and those reporting more frequent AI use showed higher AI literacy and career optimism and lower AI anxiety. AI literacy was positively associated with career optimism (r = 0.444, p < 0.001), whereas AI anxiety was negatively associated with career optimism (r = −0.461, p < 0.001). After adjustment for gender, year of study, music specialization, prior AI training, and frequency of AI use, AI literacy remained positively associated with career optimism (β = 0.314, p < 0.001), whereas AI anxiety remained negatively associated with career optimism (β = −0.326, p < 0.001). The final model explained 33.0% of the variance in career optimism. Conclusion AI literacy and AI anxiety were independently associated with career optimism among university music students. These findings suggest that students' perceptions of AI-related competence and technological concerns are relevant to their career expectations. Music institutions may consider AI education that combines practical competence with critical understanding of AI's implications for artistic identity, professional value, and future career development. Future longitudinal research is needed to clarify the temporal relationships among AI literacy, AI anxiety, and career optimism.

papers.title: Effects of AI-mediated real-time feedback on motivation and motor skill learning in traditional ethnic sports education: testing self-determination theory mechanisms
papers.authors: Yuequan Qin, Yang Yu, Guizhen Chen, Huasheng Huang, 韦东谊
papers.abstract: Introduction Traditional ethnic sports such as Zhuang Daoyin demand precise movement, yet conventional demonstration–imitation–verbal correction limits feedback timeliness and individualization. Artificial intelligence (AI) real-time posture feedback offers a scalable option, but most evaluations emphasize technical outcomes and overlook learning processes. Grounded in self-determination theory (SDT), this study tested whether and how AI real-time feedback improves motivation and motor skill by engaging basic psychological needs, with competence as the hypothesized pathway. Methods In a 12-week field experiment, 12 intact classes (307 students; control n = 152, AI n = 155) were randomly allocated at the class level to an AI real-time feedback group or a traditional teaching group; three instructors each taught two classes per condition. Both groups received identical instruction; conditions differed only in feedback source during practice (RTMPose-based concurrent vs. teacher-led terminal feedback). Need satisfaction, motivational regulation (relative autonomy index, RAI), motor skill, and course satisfaction were assessed at pre- and post-test, and analyzed with linear mixed models and structural equation modeling (lavaan, MLR). Results The AI group showed significantly greater gains in competence ( d = 0.36, p = 0.003), autonomy ( d = 0.40, p = 0.001), motor skill ( d = 0.30, p = 0.010), and learning interest ( d = 0.38, p = 0.003), whereas relatedness was unaffected ( p = 0.974); intraclass correlations were negligible. In the structural model (CFI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.04, SRMR = 0.04), group predicted competence ( β = 0.17), competence predicted RAI ( β = 0.34), and RAI predicted motor skill ( β = 0.30); the autonomy and relatedness paths were nonsignificant. The effect of AI feedback on motor skill was fully mediated by the competence-to-RAI sequence (indirect p = 0.023; direct p = 0.097). Discussion AI real-time feedback improved motor skill by strengthening competence and supporting motivational internalization, while leaving relatedness unaffected—providing discriminant evidence that the tool acts through its affordances rather than diffuse enthusiasm. Systems enhancing performance and learning should prioritize feedback that makes progress legible, within a human–AI division of labor where teachers provide relational support. In conclusion, AI real-time posture feedback can enhance motivation and motor skill learning by satisfying learners’ competence need.

papers.title: The impact of AI service quality on researchers’ work wellbeing: a dual-path moderated mediation model
papers.authors: Shuyang Liu, Tongyao Liu
papers.abstract: As AI tools permeate scientific research, a critical question emerges: does better AI actually make researchers happier? Grounded in the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model, this study proposes and tests a dual-path moderated mediation framework in which perceived AI service quality influences researcher work well-being through two parallel psychological routes. The motivational gain pathway posits that higher quality is positively related to research self-efficacy, while the loss-alleviation pathway posits that higher quality is negatively related to cognitive verification load. AI trust is introduced as a moderator of both first-stage paths. Using data from 439 researchers and PROCESS macro models 4 and 7, we found that AI service quality did not directly affect well-being ( β = 0.07, p = 0.260), but exerted a fully mediated total effect. The loss pathway via cognitive verification load reduction was the sole significant mediating mechanism (indirect effect = 0.08, 95% CI [0.028, 0.135]). AI trust significantly moderated only the loss pathway ( β = −0.21, p < 0.001): the cognitive-relief effect became significant only at medium and high trust levels, remaining inoperative for low-trust researchers. These findings reframe the value of AI quality in research settings as cognitive offloading rather than competence enhancement, and position trust as a threshold condition rather than a continuous amplifier of AI benefits.

papers.title: A study of the impact of AI-employee collaboration on employee innovation behavior
papers.authors: Yan Guanyu, Niu Chenchen
papers.abstract: Introduction With the deep integration of digitalization and generative artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence has transformed from a mere technical tool into a core collaborative partner within modern workplaces and human‑resource management. As an interdependent human‑AI working mode characterized by complementary task division, joint task accomplishment, complementary decision‑making, and continuous iterative interaction between employees and AI agents, AI‑employee collaboration is conceptually distinct from simple AI adoption, instrumental AI use, and AI‑assisted technical systems. Drawing on social cognitive theory, the present study aims to investigate how AI‑employee collaboration predicts employee innovation behavior, alongside the mediating role of self‑efficacy and the moderated‑mediation boundary condition of servant leadership. Methods Three‑wave time‑lagged questionnaire data were collected from 259 employees working in internet‑service, finance, and catering industries across Beijing and Jinan. Hierarchical regression and bootstrap approaches were adopted to test the proposed moderated‑mediation model. Results The results show that AI‑employee collaboration exerts a significant positive predictive effect on employee innovation behavior. Self‑efficacy partially mediates the relationship between AI‑employee collaboration and employee innovation behavior. Moreover, servant leadership positively moderates the link between AI‑employee collaboration and self‑efficacy and further strengthens the indirect predictive effect of AI‑employee collaboration on employee innovation behavior through self‑efficacy. Discussion This research enriches existing literature by providing incremental empirical evidence for the internal cognitive mechanism and contextual boundary of AI‑driven employee innovation. Theoretically, it unpacks the cognitive “black box” connecting AI‑employee collaboration and employee innovation and identifies servant leadership as a key situational contingency factor. Practically, these findings deliver concrete, actionable managerial insights for digitally transforming organizations to leverage AI tools and unlock employees’ innovative potential.

papers.title: Global thyroid cancer incidence in relation to dietary and socioeconomic factors: an ecological machine learning study
papers.authors: Yixing Li, Dehui Liu, Ruixue Qin, Xingchang Li, Mei Li
papers.abstract: Background Thyroid cancer incidence has risen dramatically worldwide, with marked geographic heterogeneity suggesting dietary and environmental contributions beyond screening effects. The roles of specific dietary patterns in thyroid cancer remain poorly characterized at the global level. Objectives Age-standardized thyroid cancer incidence was the prespecified primary outcome. We aimed to (1) build machine learning models predicting country-level thyroid cancer incidence from dietary and socioeconomic features, (2) quantify confounder-adjusted dietary associations with incidence, including prespecified sensitivity analyses of the iodine-rich food availability index, and (3) identify key dietary predictors through explainability analyses and a descriptive decomposition of the development pathway. Mortality was analyzed only as a secondary outcome in order to evaluate whether the incidence patterns could be attributed to differential cancer detection rather than to differences in disease occurrence. Methods We integrated GLOBOCAN 2022 (cancer outcomes), FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (113 food items, 2010–2022; primary exposure 2015–2019 mean), the UNDP Human Development Report 2025 statistical annex (HDI 2023 and its life expectancy, education, and income sub-indices), and WHO obesity prevalence (2022) across 163 countries, yielding 155 harmonized variables and 150 numeric predictors. All modeling was performed inside a nested cross-validation framework: multiple imputation by chained equations, standardization, four-method consensus feature selection, and hyperparameter search were fitted exclusively on the training partition of each outer fold (10 folds × five repetitions), and performance was summarized from pooled out-of-fold predictions with 95% confidence intervals obtained by resampling countries (2,000 bootstrap replicates). Three analyses separated dietary signal from confounding: block-wise models comparing socioeconomic-only, diet-only and combined feature sets; leave-one-region-out validation across six world regions; and confounder-adjusted partial correlations under a basic (HDI, obesity) and an extended adjustment set (HDI, obesity, the three HDI sub-indices, and region fixed effects), with Benjamini–Hochberg and Bonferroni correction applied across all comparisons. Iodine-related exposure was represented by an iodine-rich food availability index constructed from seafood, dairy, and egg supply; its construction was interrogated in four sensitivity analyses in which the components were entered separately and jointly, four weighting schemes were compared, total animal protein supply was added to the adjustment set, and an iodine-poor animal-origin food index was used as a specificity control. Binary classification and all mortality analyses were secondary. Results Regression on incidence was the primary task. Stacking ensemble performed best, with a pooled out-of-fold R ² of 0.613 (95% CI [0.510, 0.726]), RMSE = 3.04, MAE = 1.82, and Spearman ρ = 0.901 (95% CI [0.862, 0.924]); random forest ( R ² = 0.609), bagging ( R ² = 0.599), and KNN ( R ² = 0.580) followed, and a high-dimensional deep tabular model (DynaTab) was statistically comparable ( R ² = 0.626). Predictive accuracy was, however, almost entirely socioeconomic: nine development variables alone gave R ² = 0.609, 140 dietary variables alone gave 0.284, and the incremental contribution of the dietary block was –0.048 (95% CI −0.169 to +0.034), +0.021, and +0.017 across model families. Under leave-one-region-out validation, the rank ordering of countries was largely preserved (pooled ρ = 0.813), but the level was not. Unadjusted associations with incidence were positive for the iodine-rich food availability index ( ρ = 0.234), total energy ( ρ = 0.230), seafood ( ρ = 0.219), and the animal-to-plant protein ratio ( ρ = 0.221). After adjustment and Benjamini–Hochberg correction, seafood supply, dairy supply, the iodine-rich food availability index, the animal-to-plant protein ratio, and mollusks remained significant under the extended adjustment set (seafood partial r = 0.196, q = 0.031; iodine-rich food availability index 0.224, q = 0.026), whereas plant protein did not (–0.095, q = 0.309). In sensitivity analyses, the index association was carried by seafood (0.196, q = 0.017) and dairy (0.198, q = 0.017) but not eggs (0.065, q = 0.411), was stable across equal-weighted, z-score, and iodine-content-weighted constructions (0.238–0.256), survived further adjustment for total animal protein supply (0.203, q = 0.032), and was not reproduced by an iodine-poor animal-origin food index (0.102, q = 0.198). Path decomposition attributed 50.2% of the seafood–incidence correlation to the HDI pathway (95% bootstrap CI 16%–90%). In the secondary mortality analysis, the dietary ordering was preserved, but associations with the mortality-to-incidence ratio were close to zero (HDI ρ = 0.053; seafood ρ = 0.065), and in the sensitivity classification analysis, Extra Trees reached AUC = 0.932 (95% CI [0.893, 0.964]) at the median split. Conclusions With all model construction confined to training folds, machine learning models built from national food supply and socioeconomic data explain a moderate share of the between-country variation in thyroid cancer incidence, but that predictive accuracy is carried by development indicators rather than by diet. The availability of iodine-rich food groups, seafood supply, and the animal-to-plant protein ratio nevertheless retained positive ecological associations with incidence after adjustment for development and metabolic confounders and after correction for multiple comparisons, and the index association proved robust to how the index was constructed and specific to iodine-rich rather than to animal-origin food groups in general; plant protein showed no association once multiplicity was controlled. Roughly half of the seafood–incidence correlation tracks the development pathway, and the secondary mortality analysis is consistent with a substantial contribution from differential detection. These findings are ecological associations with the availability of iodine-rich food groups, not with measured iodine intake or exposure; they generate testable hypotheses for individual-level studies with measured iodine status and do not establish causation.

papers.title: A non-randomized trial of the effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on cognitive performance and resting state connectivity
papers.authors: F. M. Filbey, C. Tyler Short, A. Leazure, N. E. Nekoui, T. Brown, S. Kroener, C. Liu
papers.abstract: Background Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has shown promise for enhancing cognition and emotion regulation. To date, most human studies have focused on narrow learning paradigms that limit our understanding of how taVNS influences complex, integrative cognitive operations. Moreover, the underlying mechanisms of taVNS are still not well understood. Objective Building on preclinical findings that vagus nerve stimulation enhances cognitive flexibility and memory in animal models, this study investigated whether acute taVNS can modulate executive function and neural connectivity in healthy adults. Methods Using a quasi-experimental design, forty healthy participants received either active or sham taVNS while completing executive function tasks and adaptive cognitive training (BrainHQ). High-density electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded during stimulation to assess cortical activity and functional connectivity across frequency bands. Results Multivariate analyses demonstrated significant effects of taVNS on cognitive function and EEG. Post-hoc group comparisons showed that compared to sham stimulation, active taVNS was associated with improved BrainHQ performance and decreased delta-band connectivity in left frontal, central, and parietal regions. Delta-band connectivity during active taVNS was positively associated with pre-to-post improvements in mood. No difference in executive function tasks was found between active and sham taVNS. Sensitivity analyses using adjusted models showed that these effects were sensitive to age, sex, and education. Conclusion By evaluating multiple dimensions of executive function, these exploratory findings suggest that active taVNS may influence selected aspects of executive performance and frontal–parietal delta connectivity, potentially reflecting enhanced neural efficiency arising from the interaction between vagally mediated neuromodulation and continuously adaptive cognitive demands. However, these effects did not survive multiple-comparison correction and should therefore be interpreted cautiously and replicated in larger, prospectively powered studies.

papers.title: Choroid plexus volume in metabolic syndrome: a cross-sectional neuroimaging study
papers.authors: Xiunan Huo, Tao Chen, Zhenyu Cheng, Boyao Chen, Fushuai Zhang, Yiwen Chen, Pengcheng Liang, Nan Zhang, Yena Che, Changhu Liang, Lingfei Guo, Meng Li
papers.abstract: Objectives Our investigation aimed to explore the associations between choroid plexus (CP) volume and metabolic syndrome (MetS) components and cognitive-motor performance in a cross-sectional sample. Methods A total of 211 participants (73 with MetS and 138 non-MetS controls) were included in this study. CP volume was automatically segmented from 3D T1-weighted images using a 3D nnU-Net. CP volume was normalized to estimated total intracranial volume (eTIV) and expressed as the CP/eTIV ratio. Multivariable linear regression analyses and Spearman correlation analyses were used to examine associations among the CP/eTIV ratio, MetS components and cognitive-motor domains. The Boruta algorithm was applied for exploratory feature selection, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the discriminative capacity of the selected variables for identifying participants with lower global cognitive-motor performance (lowest 25th percentile of global cognitive-motor composite). Results Participants with MetS exhibited a higher CP/eTIV ratio than non-MetS controls, and higher CP/eTIV was independently associated with lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels ( FDR q = 0.024) after full adjustment and FDR correction. In unadjusted analyses, the CP/eTIV ratio was correlated with multiple cognitive-motor domains. However, these associations were no longer statistically significant after adjustment for confounders. Boruta analysis identified CP/eTIV, white matter hyperintensity (WMH) volume/eTIV, and BMI as key variables, and the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.787 (95% CI: 0.718 to 0.854) for discriminating participants with lower global cognitive-motor composite. DeLong's test showed that the combined model did not significantly outperform CP/eTIV alone (0.742 vs. 0.787; FDR q = 0.084) or the model of WMH/eTIV and BMI (0.729 vs. 0.787; FDR q = 0.084). Conclusion A higher CP/eTIV ratio was associated with MetS and lower HDL-C levels, but was not independently associated with cognitive-motor performance after multivariable adjustment. CP structural variation may represent an imaging correlate of metabolic disturbance, and its relevance to cognitive vulnerability requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Case Report: Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke: a diagnostic challenge and biomarker-based clarification
papers.authors: Wenjie Hao, Xuan Zhou, Meixia Wang, Wenming Yang, Ting Cheng
papers.abstract: Background Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (sCJD) is a rare and uniformly fatal prion disorder characterized by rapidly progressive dementia and heterogeneous neurological manifestations. Early sCJD may be misinterpreted as cerebrovascular disease, particularly when focal neurological deficits, unilateral diffusion abnormalities, and vascular risk factors coexist. Case presentation We report a 76-year-old man with a history of hypertension who initially presented with dizziness and gait instability, followed by progressive right-sided weakness, and was initially diagnosed with ischemic stroke in the setting of intracranial arterial stenosis. Despite antiplatelet and vascular management, the patient experienced rapid cognitive decline, psychiatric disturbances, aphasia, and progressive hemiparesis. Follow-up MRI demonstrated progressive, non-territorial cortical ribbon-like diffusion restriction predominantly involving the left insular, parietal, frontal, and temporal cortices. CSF analysis revealed markedly elevated total tau (4553.50 pg/mL; laboratory-reported cutoff: < 399 pg/mL), phosphorylated tau (66.93 pg/mL; laboratory-reported cutoff: < 50 pg/mL), and 14-3-3γ protein (50515 AU/mL; laboratory-reported cutoff: < 20,000 AU/mL). Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies and metagenomic next-generation sequencing were negative. PRNP genetic testing detected no pathogenic variant in the patient and his son. EEG showed diffuse slowing without periodic sharp wave complexes. According to the 2017 International CJD Surveillance Network criteria, the diagnosis was classified as probable sCJD on the basis of rapidly progressive cognitive impairment, two clinical features (documented cerebellar ataxia and pyramidal signs), characteristic MRI abnormalities, and positive CSF 14-3-3; the typical EEG criterion was absent and RT-QuIC was not performed. Conclusion This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of early sCJD initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke in the presence of coexisting vascular pathology. Recognition of non-vascular diffusion patterns, careful reassessment of atypical clinical progression, and adjunctive CSF biomarker assessment may facilitate timely diagnostic reconsideration and help avoid unnecessary interventions.

papers.title: Governing brain-computer interfaces as embodied autonomous neural systems: an ethical framework for neurorobotic governance in education
papers.authors: Jing Gao, Dong Lin, Jianfeng Hu
papers.abstract: The rapid development of neurorobotic systems, particularly non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) deployed in educational contexts, raises urgent ethical questions about child protection and societal impact. Neurorobotic systems acquire biological signals through embodied sensors, process them via brain-inspired algorithms, and actuate physical responses in closed-loop architectures that directly affect vulnerable learners. We propose Neuro-Adaptive Learning Design (NALD) as a mechanism to translate the capabilities of such neurorobotic systems into ethical safeguards across five functional stages (Sense, Analyze, Decide, Intervene, and Evaluate) that characterize embodied autonomous neural systems. Building on Ethics by Design, we introduce Governance by Design (GbD), incorporating ethical mandates into the technical architecture of neurorobotic systems. The Ethical NALD (E-NALD) framework maps 15 concrete safeguards onto NALD stages, grounded in the Belmont Report and operationalized through the UNESCO 2025 Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. By positioning educational BCIs within the broader context of neurorobotics, this study evaluates the potential societal impact of deploying embodied autonomous systems in compulsory learning environments and offers a governance framework that bridges the gap between abstract neuroethics principles and enforceable technical requirements for neurorobotic technologies. The framework addresses the unique vulnerabilities of children as primary users of neurorobotic systems, including neurodivergent learners who may be simultaneously the most likely beneficiaries and the most at-risk populations.
keywords: Convention on the Rights of the Child

papers.title: Performance of four large language model chatbots in responding to patient-facing questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures: a cross-sectional paired evaluation
papers.authors: Ting Mao, Feifei Bian, Wei Liu, Xianglong Zhou, Guoqin Zhang
papers.abstract: Background Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used by the public to obtain health information, but the safety and quality of their responses to questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) remain unclear. Objective To compare the safety and patient-facing response quality of four publicly accessible LLM chatbots when responding to standardized questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures. Methods In this cross-sectional paired evaluation, 36 standardized OVCF-related patient-facing questions were submitted to each of four publicly accessible LLM chatbot interfaces—ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao—in an initial response-generation round on June 20, 2026, from Jiangsu, China. Queries were conducted in English in independent single-turn sessions under matched conditions, yielding 144 responses for the primary between-chatbot analysis. A second independent generation round using the same 36 questions and matched query procedures was conducted 7 days later (June 27, 2026), yielding an additional 144 responses for within-model stability analysis. The questions covered symptoms and warning signs, diagnosis and imaging, conservative management, medication safety, rehabilitation, vertebral augmentation, fracture prevention, and special clinical scenarios. Five clinical raters, blinded to chatbot identity and generation round, independently evaluated safety, factual accuracy, empathic communication, treatment-related information quality using DISCERN, patient-information quality using EQIP, transparency using the JAMA benchmark criteria, and overall quality using the Global Quality Score. Readability was assessed automatically using six established indices. Between-chatbot comparisons and test–retest stability analyses used paired methods appropriate for the outcome type. Results Inter-rater agreement was high, with a Fleiss’ kappa of 0.818 for safety and ICC(2,1) values of 0.816 for accuracy, 0.820 for empathy, 0.820 for DISCERN, 0.820 for EQIP, 0.821 for JAMA, and 0.818 for GQS. Potentially unsafe responses were identified for every chatbot: 3 of 36 ChatGPT responses (8.3%), 5 of 36 DeepSeek responses (13.9%), 6 of 36 Gemini responses (16.7%), and 7 of 36 Doubao responses (19.4%). The overall paired difference in safety was not statistically significant (Cochran's Q = 3.621, df = 3, P = 0.305). Factual accuracy differed significantly but only modestly among chatbots ( P = 0.009; Kendall's W = 0.108). Empathy showed substantially greater variation ( P < 0.001; W = 0.817), with higher scores for ChatGPT and Gemini than for DeepSeek and Doubao. DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark, and GQS scores also differed significantly among chatbots (all P < 0.001). Doubao produced responses with the greatest estimated textual complexity. Across the two generation rounds, safety agreement ranged from 88.9% to 97.2% (Gwet's AC1, 0.838–0.966), and median ICC(2,1) values across the 12 non-safety outcomes ranged from 0.781 to 0.904. Conclusions In this time-stamped, single-location, two-round evaluation, all four chatbot interfaces produced some responses classified as potentially unsafe despite generally high clinician-rated factual accuracy. Differences were greater in empathy, information quality, transparency, overall quality, and readability than in factual accuracy. The observed within-model stability was generally good but did not eliminate variability across generations. These findings are specific to the evaluated access location, language, single-turn conditions, and generation dates and should not be assumed to represent stable performance across settings or future model updates. LLM-generated OVCF information should not be used as a standalone patient education resource; any potential use should involve clinician oversight, safety safeguards, and further validation.

papers.title: Latent profiles of work readiness and their associated factors among nursing interns: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Yanfang Zhang, Xinxin Xie, Man Wu, Qingqing Lv, Long Zhao, 杨秀木
papers.abstract: Background Work readiness refers to the comprehensive competencies required for individuals to enter and adapt to the workforce. It is relevant to the transition from nursing student to clinical nurse. However, existing research has paid limited attention to heterogeneity in nursing interns’ work readiness, and few studies have examined associated factors from the perspective of Social Cognitive Career Theory. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of work readiness among nursing interns and examine the associations of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) literacy and the clinical learning environment with profile membership. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 712 final-year nursing interns from three nursing schools in Anhui Province, China, between November 2025 and June 2026. Participants completed the Nursing Practice Readiness Scale, Clinical Learning Environment Questionnaire, and Generative Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale. Latent Profile Analysis was used to identify distinct work readiness profiles, and multinomial logistic regression was performed to examine factors associated with profile membership. Results Three latent profiles of work readiness were identified: low work readiness ( n = 415, 58.3%), moderate work readiness ( n = 227, 31.9%), and high work readiness ( n = 70, 9.8%). The overall multinomial logistic regression model( χ 2 = 467.253, P < 0.001) showed that the clinical learning environment, GenAI literacy, academic performance, clinical learning outcomes, and sense of professional belonging were significantly associated with work readiness profile membership (all P < 0.05). Conclusions Three distinct work readiness profiles were identified among nursing interns. Clinical learning environment, GenAI literacy, academic performance, clinical learning outcomes, and sense of professional belonging were associated with profile membership. These findings highlight the heterogeneity of nursing interns’ work readiness and may inform the development of individualized educational support strategies.

papers.title: Attitudes and perceptions toward artificial intelligence among practicing rheumatologists in Iraq: a cross-sectional web-based survey
papers.authors: Mustafa Alhayali, Marwa Moayad, Nizar Abdulalateef Jasim, Zaid Al-Zuhairi, Marwah Al-Mashhadani, Mustafa A Shahrori, Rami Al-Khaffaf, Marafi Jammaa Ahmed, Enas Osama Hassan Omer, Aya Ahmed Shimal, Rafal Othman, Ahmed Dheyaa Al‐Obaidi
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of healthcare, particularly in rheumatology, where clinicians must integrate complex clinical, laboratory, and imaging data. Physicians’ perceptions of AI may substantially influence the extent to which it is implemented responsibly in routine clinical practice. Objective This study aimed to assess the attitudes of practicing rheumatologists in Iraq toward artificial intelligence and to examine their association with demographic and professional characteristics. Methods A four-month web-based cross-sectional survey was conducted from October 2025 to January 2026. A questionnaire adapted from previous studies was refined through expert review and pilot testing before distribution. The questionnaire comprised demographic information, attitude statements measured on a five-point Likert scale, and items assessing general perceptions of artificial intelligence. Composite attitude scores were categorized using modified Bloom's cutoff criteria. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS and R. Results A total of 162 complete responses were collected. Most respondents were aged 35–44 years (42.0%), male (56.8%), and specialists (67.9%). Overall, 61.7% reported familiarity with AI and 69.1% had already used AI in rheumatology practice. Most participants 56.8% exhibited a poor attitude, 32.1% a moderate attitude, and 11.1% a good attitude toward AI. Bivariate analysis identified familiarity with AI ( p = 0.003 ) and involvement in research ( p = 0.009 ) as significantly associated with more favorable attitudes. Conclusion Iraqi rheumatologists demonstrate cautious engagement with artificial intelligence, with the majority displaying poor-to-moderate overall attitude scores on the standardized composite scale. Greater familiarity with AI and research involvement were associated with more favorable attitudes, highlighting the importance of targeted digital literacy and specialty-specific education to support effective AI adoption in clinical practice.

papers.title: Do machine learning models really encode cross-cultural lifestyle-health differences? A leakage-free reanalysis of two university cohorts in India and Japan
papers.authors: Eiko Takaoka, S. Ruban, B. Mohammed Siraj, Varenya Vinay, Hilda Shanthini, Akshay Dias
papers.abstract: Introduction Machine-learning (ML) studies increasingly compare feature-importance rankings between small, unevenly sized cohorts and interpret the differences as evidence of culturally specific “risk architectures.” We show that such comparisons can be highly misleading without leakage-free evaluation, using a worked example from our own cross-sectional lifestyle and health data collected during June-August 2024 from two universities in India and Japan. Three problems were identified in our preliminary analysis: (1) an outcome (obesity, defined as BMI ≥ 25) that was tautologically predicted by including BMI itself as a model input; (2) model evaluation without a held-out test set; and (3) feature-importance comparisons that ignored sampling variability from an eightfold difference in cohort size. Methods We addressed each problem using penalized logistic regression, Random Forest, and gradient-boosted trees with proper train/test splitting, held-out permutation importance, and bootstrap confidence intervals. We also ran a sensitivity analysis that repeatedly subsampled the Indian cohort down to the size of the Japanese cohort. Results Removing body mass index (BMI) as a predictor collapsed obesity-model discrimination from perfect (AUC = 1.00) to chance level (AUC = 0.50-0.57), confirming that the BMI-obesity association was definitional rather than empirical. Held-out predictive performance for the remaining viable outcome, elevated self-rated stress, was modest at best (AUC 0.49-0.71). Critically, in the subsampling analysis, every feature-importance value observed in the actual Japanese data fell within the range produced by sample-size noise alone. Discussion We present this analysis as a transparent, reproducible case study of specific, checkable pitfalls: label leakage, missing train/test evaluation, unadjusted small-sample comparison, and mislabeled psychometric instruments. These should be routinely screened for before ML feature importance is interpreted as evidence of population-level or cultural differences in digital health research.

papers.title: Predicted visual attention and cognitive demand in luxury beauty retail: an exploratory AI-based neuromarketing study
papers.authors: Hedda Martina Šola, Jasenka Gajdoš Kljusurić, Aljoša Šestanović
papers.abstract: Introduction This exploratory study examines how AI-supported neuromarketing tools can be used to predict visual attention and cognitive demand in a luxury beauty retail environment. Methods The research was conducted in a high-end cosmetics store in Zagreb, where 11 static images, selected from 21 photographs of the store, and a 9-minute in-store video recording, edited into an 85-second simulation of the consumer journey, were analyzed using a predictive platform informed by large-scale eye tracking and EEG datasets (eye-tracking data from approximately 180,000 participants and EEG data from 27,000 participants; more than 100 billion data points in total). No shoppers were tested; all reported values are model predictions. The analysis focused on how store layout, product positioning, visual hierarchy, and branded communication elements influence predicted focus, attentional efficiency, and cognitive effort. Results The results reveal several consistent patterns. Brand areas that were visually separated from competing stimuli attracted stronger, more sustained predicted attention, whereas visually crowded or externally exposed zones reduced attentional efficiency. Central product placement proved particularly effective when surrounded by fewer distracting elements, suggesting that spatial clarity can support more efficient visual processing of branded and product-related stimuli. At the AOI level, Engagement and Cognitive Demand rose together ( r = 0.90). In the video simulation, Cognitive Demand remained uniformly high while Focus varied with the field of view, and the two were not related. Discussion These findings highlight the interaction between attention allocation, cognitive load, visibility conditions, and spatial organization in luxury retail communication. Overall, the study demonstrates the value of AI-supported neuromarketing for understanding how consumers process visually complex retail spaces. It contributes to communication and consumer research by clarifying how visual structure and cognitive demand shape brand visibility and decision-related processing in luxury beauty retail. The findings also offer practical guidance for improving store design, in-store communication, and experiential branding strategies by applying state-of-the-art technology for predicting consumer behavior in visually complex retail environments.

papers.title: Strengthening Pre-Service Teachers’ Professionalism through School Field Introduction: A Case Study at SMAN 4 Sidrap, Indonesia
papers.authors: Kamal Kamal, Nurlela Nurlela, Andi Dwi Resqi, Fitriani N, Sam Hermansyah, Nurul Syahrani, Nur Ikhsaniah
papers.abstract: Developing pre-service teachers’ professionalism is essential for preparing competent, reflective, and adaptable educators capable of responding to the evolving demands of contemporary education. School Field Introduction (Pengenalan Lapangan Persekolahan, PLP 1) provides prospective teachers with opportunities to experience authentic school environments and develop an understanding of professional teaching responsibilities. This study aims to explore how School Field Introduction contributes to strengthening pre-service teachers’ professionalism, character development, understanding of school ecosystems, and awareness of digital literacy and artificial intelligence (AI) in education. The study focuses on the implementation of PLP 1 at SMAN 4 Sidrap, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, involving fifth-semester students from the Faculty of Teacher Training and Education, Universitas Muhammadiyah Sidenreng Rappang. The program was conducted through orientation, school-based observation, academic mentoring, reflective discussions, and evaluation activities. Data sources included observation records, students’ reflective journals, field reports, and documentation of mentoring activities. The findings indicate that participation in School Field Introduction provided meaningful contextual learning experiences that strengthened students’ understanding of school culture, educational management, teacher responsibilities, and interpersonal interactions within the school environment. Furthermore, the program supported the development of professional attitudes, particularly discipline, responsibility, communication, collaboration, ethical awareness, and reflective thinking. Exposure to digital technologies and AI-related educational practices also encouraged participants to recognize the importance of responsible technology integration in professional teaching. However, the relatively limited implementation period restricted opportunities for more extensive professional engagement. The study concludes that School Field Introduction represents a valuable experiential learning approach for fostering pre-service teachers’ professional identity, pedagogical awareness, and readiness for future teaching careers. Systematic mentoring, reflective learning, and digital competency development are recommended to enhance the effectiveness of school-based teacher education programs.

papers.title: The Utilization of Digital Technology to Support Self-Directed Learning Among Vocational High School Students: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Syintia Nurmala, Vendyah Trisnaningtyas
papers.abstract: Advancements in digital technology offer Vocational High School (SMK) students opportunities to access learning resources flexibly and cultivate learning autonomy. However, the use of digital technology does not automatically guarantee the development of learning autonomy, as it is influenced by various factors such as digital literacy, learning motivation, instructional design, and teacher support. This study aims to analyze the use of digital technology in supporting learning autonomy among SMK students, specifically examining the types of technology employed, the dimensions of learning autonomy fostered, and the factors that facilitate or hinder its implementation. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) methodology, adhering to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Data were sourced from relevant scholarly articles published between 2021 and 2026 and subsequently analyzed using descriptive analysis and thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that digital technologies such as Learning Management Systems (LMS), digital learning media, web-based learning, instructional videos, and artificial intelligence have the potential to support student initiatives in learning, time management, progress monitoring, and self-evaluation. Therefore, the integration of digital technology must be accompanied by instructional strategies that encourage student responsibility and self-regulation to ensure the optimal development of learning autonomy.

papers.title: AI for Grading from the Teaching Perspective (with an EssayGrader Case Comparison)
papers.authors: Ian J. Shepherd
papers.journal: Journal of Higher Education Theory and Practice
papers.abstract: AI has taken the academic world by storm, dramatically affecting written assignments and student performance evaluations. This paper examines the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) from the teaching perspective, with emphasis on daily grading workflows. We analyze benefits such as fair and consistent application of rubrics, the ability to incorporate articles and course materials as inputs to grading, and the delivery of individualized, extensive feedback. We compare these capabilities against a representative product—EssayGrader—situate our claims within current scholarship on Automated Essay Scoring (AES) and Large Language Models (LLMs) as graders, and provide policy guidance.

papers.title: Contribuições para a avaliação do desempenho agroecológico em estabelecimentos extensivos do distrito de General Pueyrredon (Argentina)
papers.authors: Celeste Molpeceres, Alejandra Denise Auer, Claudia Andrea Mikkelsen, Jaime Del Río, Laura Zulaica
papers.abstract: In recent decades, in Argentina in general, and in the General Pueyrredon district (PGP) in particular, increasing questions have been raised regarding the conventional production model. In this district, diverse productive activities take place. Among them, this study aims to characterize the agroecological transition of eight extensive production systems with agroecological bases—surveyed and analyzed through interviews conducted between July 2022 and October 2023—using the Tool for Agroecology Performance Evaluation (TAPE), proposed by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). Among the main results, it stands out that, although there are differences in the transition process, overall, the evaluated farms show higher values in extrasystemic elements, where the social component becomes particularly relevant, especially in the dimension of co-creation and knowledge sharing.

papers.title: Technological Competence and the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Interpreter Training
papers.authors: Boglárka Fanni Tóth
papers.journal: Central European Library and Information Science Review Közép-európai Könyvtár- és Információtudományi Szemle
papers.abstract: This article explores the integration of technological tools into interpreter training. While translation training has incorporated digital and AI-based technologies for a relatively long period, empirical research shows that interpreters' familiarity with specialised Computer-Assisted Interpreting (CAI) tools remains low. In response to this gap, the Department of Translation and Interpreting at Eötvös Loránd University launched Technology for Interpreters, an innovative pilot course that systematically introduces interpreting-related technologies. The course combines theoretical guidance with hands-on practice across multiple modules, including CAI software, telephone interpreting, tablet-supported interpreting, artificial intelligence, simultaneous interpreting and remote interpreting. Experience shows that this approach strengthens key technological skills, such as digital literacy, effective tool use and AI awareness. Several challenges remain, particularly regarding resources, instructor training and the fast pace of technological change. Overall, the study indicates that integrating CAI tools into interpreter education is both possible and educationally beneficial, and the initiative presented may serve as a useful reference point for other institutions interested in launching similar courses.

papers.title: Exploring GenAI Chatbot Use for L2 Learning: A Mixed-Methods Study of Foundation-Year Students in Oman
papers.authors: Moosa Ahmed Ali Sulaiman, Mohamed Abdelmageed, Nagwa Mohammed Khallaf
papers.journal: Journal of English Language Teaching and Applied Linguistics
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots have increasingly become part of many university students' English as a second language (L2) learning. However, little is known about how students in general foundation programmes use them during the move from Arabic-medium schooling to English-medium higher education. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study examined GenAI chatbot use among foundation-year students at a private university in Oman. A questionnaire (N = 262) covered usage patterns, perceived usefulness for L2 skills, AI output verification practices, challenges and support needs, and was followed by two focus groups (n = 15). Results showed that ChatGPT was the dominant tool (91.2%) that students accessed mainly by smartphone (80.5%). The most common frequency was "sometimes" (47.3%), while 42.4% of respondents reported using chatbots "always" or "often". Most students (57.6%) switched between English and Arabic while interacting with GenAI chatbots. Students rated chatbots as clearly useful for writing, speaking and reading, but not for listening. They also valued grammar and vocabulary corrections by chatbots more than their feedback on writing or speaking assignments. More than two-thirds of respondents preferred teacher feedback on their writing (72.9%). The most frequently reported challenges were incorrect information (43.5%) and unclear responses (35.1%), while the most common verification strategy of generated content was asking a teacher (46.2%). Focus-group participants described purpose-driven but largely unplanned prompting, translation-mediated comprehension, concern about overreliance, inconsistent teacher stances, and a need for classroom-embedded guidance. Chatbot use for L2 learning among foundation-year students can be interpreted as a tool-mediated activity largely outside formal L2 instructional design, with teachers as epistemic anchors. The study recommends early, skill-specific, teacher-mediated AI literacy instruction in foundation programmes.

papers.title: Bringing the Hikayat Hang Tuah into Digital Learning: Student Perceptions of AI-Assisted Animated Videos
papers.authors: Nyayu Aisya Shafira, Nurhayati Nurhayati, Zahra Alwi
papers.journal: International Journal of Linguistics Literature & Translation
papers.abstract: The utilization of Artificial Intelligence in developing learning media offers opportunities to present classic literary works in audiovisual formats that align better with the characteristics of digital learning. The aim of this study was to analyze the perceptions of tenth-grade students regarding an AI-assisted animated video of Hikayat Hang Tuah (HHT) as a learning medium for Indonesian language studies. A quantitative approach with a survey design was employed. The study involved 310 tenth-grade high school students in Palembang City. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire comprising 18 statements across five aspects: visual quality, storytelling, ease of comprehension, learning interest, and perceived benefits. The instrument underwent content validation by three experts (Aiken’s V coefficient: 0.778–1.000) and a reliability test with 30 students (Cronbach’s Alpha coefficient: 0.906). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, with a positive perception threshold set at ≥62.5%. The results indicate that all perception statements fell within the positive range, with scores between 81% and 87%. The highest score was recorded for the statement regarding the visual comfort of the video's colors and illustrations, while the lowest score related to students' willingness to use AI-assisted animated videos in their studies; nevertheless, even the lowest score exceeded the positive perception threshold. Thus, the AI-assisted animated video of HHT was positively received by students and serves as a viable alternative medium for teaching hikayat (traditional Malay tales). These findings reflect student perceptions of the medium and do not demonstrate its experimental effectiveness regarding learning outcomes.

papers.title: INDUSTRIAL PRODUCT DESIGN IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: FRAMING THE NEED, SHAPING THE USE
papers.authors: Maria Poli, Fotini Maniou, Ioanna Maniou, Maria Manola
papers.journal: World Journal of Advanced Engineering Technology and Sciences
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in physical products, from domestic appliances and vehicles to medical devices and wearables, yet the success of such products depends less on algorithmic performance than on whether people understand, trust and meaningfully integrate them into everyday life. This paper examines the contribution of industrial product design to the current need for, and use of, AI. Through a conceptual and integrative narrative review of literature in design research, human–computer interaction (HCI), computational design and AI ethics, it develops an analytical framework of five contributions: (1) framing human needs so that AI addresses problems worth solving; (2) making AI capabilities legible through form, interaction and feedback; (3) calibrating trust and control; (4) embedding AI in sustainable and ethical product lifecycles; and (5) integrating AI as a tool within the design process itself. The analysis indicates that industrial design acts as a mediating layer between technological capability and human practice, and that its contribution lies as much in deciding where AI should not be used as in enabling it. The paper closes with implications for practice, education and policy, and five propositions for empirical testing.

papers.title: Addressing symbolic obstacles in undergraduate calculus through artificial intelligence scaffolding
papers.authors: Isbadar Nursit, Toto Nusantara, Erry Hidayanto
papers.abstract: Symbolic obstacles in calculus prevent students from moving away from intuition and towards formal thinking, but are rarely studied in the context of artificial intelligence (AI) interaction logs. We investigated symbolic obstacles and AI-supported representational transitions among 12 Indonesian undergraduate mathematics education students in a non-intrusive intrinsic case study. Semi-structured interviews, eight classroom observations, diagnostic tests, academic artifacts, and AI logs were analyzed through inductive-deductive thematic analysis, based on Tall’s Three Worlds of Mathematics. Four obstacles are highlighted: graph-to-symbol translation, integral and sigma notation, limit notation, and symbolic algebraic manipulation. Participant-level comparisons showed 27.4%–53.8% fewer coded symbolic errors in post-activity assessments than at baseline. AI scaffolding through dynamic visualization, adaptive feedback, step-by-step guidance, and solution validation was associated with representational cycling, metacognitive reflection, reported self-efficacy gains, and lower mathematics anxiety. The study integrates AI-log evidence with the Three Worlds framework to explain how scaffolding can support students in addressing symbolic obstacles.

papers.title: Factors influencing nursing educators’ behavioral intention to adopt artificial intelligence in teaching: A cross-sectional study from Morocco
papers.authors: ACHRAF SOUDI, Soukaina Wakrim
papers.abstract: Purpose: Educators are central to the successful integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in health sciences education, yet evidence from North African contexts remains scarce. This study examined the factors associated with nursing educators' behavioral intention to adopt AI in their teaching practices in Laayoune, Morocco. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 108 nursing educators (response rate: 90.8%) between June and July 2025. A French-language, self-administered questionnaire based on the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology measured behavioral intention and ten individual, technological, and organizational dimensions (45 items; Cronbach's α = 0.835–0.983). Behavioral intention, the canonical acceptance outcome in both models, was analyzed as a continuous variable using independent-samples t-tests with effect sizes, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression with backward elimination, bootstrap confidence intervals, and a logistic sensitivity analysis. Results: Behavioral intention was high (per-item mean 4.29 ± 0.53 out of 5), and 94.4% of educators already used AI tools in teaching, despite high anxiety (4.50 ± 0.70), high perceived risk (3.98 ± 0.73), and very low perceived facilitating conditions (2.11 ± 1.27). In the final regression model, awareness (β = 0.556, p < 0.001) and self-efficacy (β = 0.248, p = 0.010) were the only independent predictors, together explaining 57.4% of the variance in intention (F(2, 105) = 70.62, p < 0.001). The bivariate associations of age, teaching experience, AI knowledge, and AI proficiency with intention were fully accounted for by these two factors. Conclusion: AI adoption among these nursing educators appears largely individual and self-directed, driven by awareness and confidence rather than institutional support, which was perceived as weak. Strengthening AI literacy and self-efficacy, alongside institutional investment in infrastructure, training, and guidelines, may support responsible AI integration. Findings from this single-institution study should be interpreted with appropriate caution.

papers.title: Exploring Students' Perceptions of Using the ChatGPT Voice Conversation Feature for Informal English-Speaking Practice
papers.authors: Rizki Rayana
papers.journal: Journal of Emerging Technology in Teaching and Learning (JETTLe)
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), especially with generative AI chatbots, is opening innovative options for autonomous language learning. This qualitative descriptive study investigates university students’ impressions of utilizing the ChatGPT Voice Conversation function for informal English speaking practice. Twelve Indonesian university students of English education major who used the feature to practice speaking by themselves for four weeks were selected by purposive sampling technique and then interviewed using semi-structured interview. The data collected were examined using Braun and Clarke thematic analysis methodology. The preliminary data suggest that students view the ChatGPT Voice Conversation feature as a low-anxiety, highly accessible and interactive tool that helps them improve speaking fluency and learn vocabulary. However, several significant shortcomings were detected including technical constraints such as occasional odd prosody, conversational disconnects and the absence of non-verbal cues. The study suggests that AI speech features, while useful as scaffolding for informal conversation, should be used to supplement, not substitute for, human-human contact in language instruction

papers.title: Chatbot as a Feedback Partner: An Applied Linguistics Study on AI-Mediated Corrective Feedback in Enhancing EFL Learners' Writing Accuracy and Revision Behavior
papers.authors: Muh Zaky Rahmat Dany.S
papers.journal: Journal of Emerging Technology in Teaching and Learning (JETTLe)
papers.abstract: This study investigates the role of AI chatbot-generated corrective feedback in enhancing the writing accuracy and revision behavior of EFL undergraduate learners. Employing a descriptive qualitative design grounded in Applied Linguistics, the research involved undergraduate students who exhibited persistent grammatical errors, limited revision strategies, and infrequent access to individualized writing feedback. Data were gathered through multiple drafts of argumentative paragraphs, chatbot-generated feedback logs, and semi-structured interviews conducted across several feedback-revision cycles. The findings indicate substantial improvement across four indicators: grammatical accuracy, depth of revision, error noticing, and learner autonomy in the editing process. Learners progressively shifted from surface-level corrections, such as spelling and punctuation, toward meaning-level revisions involving clause structure, cohesion, and argument development. The chatbot's explicit, metalinguistic feedback encouraged learners to notice recurring error patterns and apply self-correction in subsequent drafts. Learners' dependence on external correction gradually decreased as their confidence in self-editing increased. These findings support corrective feedback theory, the noticing hypothesis, and computer-mediated writing feedback frameworks, which emphasize that written accuracy develops through repeated, learner-engaged feedback cycles. This study contributes a new perspective by positioning the AI chatbot not as an automatic error-correction tool, but as an interactive feedback partner that scaffolds learners' revision competence. Chatbot-mediated feedback can therefore serve as a practical alternative for sustained writing improvement in contexts where individualized teacher feedback is limited.

papers.title: University EFL Learners’ Perceptions on the Use of ChatGPT in Academic Writing Learning Process
papers.authors: Kristian Florensio Wijaya, Entika Prastikawati
papers.journal: Journal of Emerging Technology in Teaching and Learning (JETTLe)
papers.abstract: With the burgeoning development of sophisticated artificial intelligence tools, it is of foremost importance for second language educators to integrate these digital learning platforms into their regular classroom settings, as they will help them deliver clearer pedagogical instructions and design more effective learning materials. Concerning the aforesaid background, the researchers undertook this moderate library study to investigate university EFL learners’ perceptions of the use of ChatGPT in the academic writing learning process. In compliance with this major study objective, the researchers employed a thematic analysis approach while reviewing pertinent findings derived from 30 previously published ChatGPT journal articles. With the help of a thematic analysis approach, the researchers could generate more believable, trustworthy, and relatable findings, as it supported us in subsuming the targeted results into relevant themes. The thematically-categorized research results revealed that ChatGPT allowed the enhancement of writing accuracy, proficiency, strategic competence, motivation, confidence, and positive writing dispositions among global university EFL learners.

papers.title: Beyond Mere Assistance: Exploring Generative AI’s Role in Polytechnic Students’ Critical Thinking
papers.authors: Arif Rafiq, Dina Adinda, Hendi Purnata, Yuniarmelinda Ikha Meru Brahmanty, Purwiyanto Purwiyanto
papers.journal: Journal of Educational Science and Technology (EST)
papers.abstract: Integrating generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools into higher education has sparked debate over their impact on student learning outcomes. While concerns about academic dependency persist, limited empirical evidence exists regarding AI's potential to enhance critical thinking skills in technical education contexts, particularly in non-Western polytechnic environments.
