This study investigates how structured GAI integration influences the development of critical thinking among polytechnic students in electrical and mechatronics engineering programs. A mixed-methods design involving 515 students from Politeknik Negeri Cilacap, Indonesia, was employed. A pre-post intervention measured critical thinking using the Watson-Glaser Critical Thinking Appraisal–Short Form (WGCTA-SF). Qualitative data were gathered through focus group discussions, reflective journals, and interviews. Results indicated significant improvement in critical thinking scores (pre-test: M=67.3, SD=8.4; post-test: M=74.8, SD=7.2; t (495) = 12.67, p<0.001, Cohen's d=0.94). The largest gains appeared in argument evaluation (21.3%), inference making (18.2%), and recognition of assumptions (15.7%). Qualitative analysis identified four mechanisms underpinning these gains: scaffolded questioning, exposure to multiple perspectives, iterative refinement processes, and development of metacognitive awareness. These findings suggest that GAI tools, when embedded within structured pedagogical frameworks, function as sophisticated cognitive scaffolds that enhance rather than replace critical thinking. This study provides evidence for a paradigm shift: from viewing AI as a task-completion aid to recognising its potential as a critical-thinking development tool in technical higher education.

papers.title: ОСНОВНІ ПРОТИРІЧЧЯ У СУЧАСНИХ КОНЦЕПЦІЯХ СОЦІУМІВ, ЩО ПРИПУСКАЮТЬ СУБ'ЄКТНІСТЬ ЗАГАЛЬНОГО ШІ
papers.authors: Stanislav BESKARAVAINYI
papers.abstract: Потенційне створення штучних інтелектів, що не будуть поступатися людині, так званих «Загальних ШІ» (AGI), робить реальною участь роботів у соціальному житті суспільства. Але форма соціальних структур, які може створювати інтелектуальна техніка, залишається маловивченою. Більшість прогнозів, що описують гетерогенний, людино-машинний соціум, можна віднести до трьох концепцій: гуманістичної, трансгманістичної і постгуманістичної. Але антропоцентричні чи контр-антропоцентрические причини міркувань призводять до внутрішніх протиріч у створюваних моделях соціуму. Необхідно описати протиріччя в актуальних футурологічних прогнозах про людино-машинні соціуми та показати методологічні підстави їх подолання. Гуманістична концепція людино-машинного соціуму розглядається в роботах К. Шваба, М. Хардта та А. Негрі, С. Жижека, а також сумі авторів, що досліджують напрямок «Human-Robot Interaction». Трансгуманізм розглянутий у роботах М. Срничека, А. Вільямса Н. Ленда, К. Ярвіна, та суми авторів, що досліджує модель коеволюції людини та машини. Постгуманізм – у роботах Н. Бострома, Ю. Харарі, Ф. Феррандо, Р. Брайдотті, Ж.-М. Шеффера. Висновки: показано, що антропна модель суб'єкта імпліцитно використовується як зразок суб'єкта у рамках гуманістичних, а й трансгуманістичних і постгуманістичних концепцій. Спроби створення моделей соціуму з використанням редукованих моделей техногенних суб'єктів, із запозиченням моделей поведінки тварин або простих моделей з теорії ігор, призводять до перманентного змішування соціальних, технологічних та біологічних факторів у описі поведінки техногенного суб'єкта. Тобто неантропоморфна модель соціальних взаємодій не формулюється. Показано, що «акторно-мережева теорія» (М. Каллона, Б. Латура), концепції «асамбляжів» (М. Деланда) та «комунікації» (Н. Лумана) – не дозволяють оцінювати гетерогенний людино-машинний соціум. Ймовірно, лише створивши цілісну модель техногенного суб'єкта, можна розпочати повноцінного моделювання постлюдських соціумів. Можливо, лише завдяки створенню цілісної моделі техногенного суб’єкта вдасться розпочати комплексне моделювання постлюдських суспільств. Доведено, що антропна модель суб’єкта неявно використовується як еталон суб’єктності загалом – не лише в межах гуманістичної соціальної парадигми, а й, подекуди, у трансгуманістичній та постгуманістичній парадигмах; спроби відмовитися від антропної моделі призводять до змішування соціального, психологічного, техногенного та біологічного під час моделювання нових суб’єктів. Довільно обрана поведінкова модель (наприклад, людина в суспільстві, тварина в зграї, раціональний гравець) поширюється на всю потенційну соціальну сферу та на всі типи суб’єктів, акторів, автономних агентів тощо. Це унеможливлює аналіз культурної специфіки суспільства або прогнозування дій суб’єкта.

papers.title: ВОЗМОЖНОСТИ ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА В ОБРАЗОВАНИИ
papers.authors: А.Х. Ибрагимова
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence in education no longer appears as an external addition to the learning process. It is integrated into the daily operations of universities and schools: it helps to select assignments tailored to the student’s level, checks typical assignments, monitors gaps in the material, and speeds up feedback. However, reducing the issue to convenience alone is clearly insufficient. Research on innovations in higher education usually highlights the increase in efficiency, while studies on the new role of the teacher provide a different perspective: the machine does not replace the teacher; it shifts their work towards course design, data selection, and result monitoring. As a result, the set of skills also changes. It’s no longer enough for a teacher to know the subject matter and the methodology; they also need to understand how the digital system generates recommendations, what criteria it uses to make assessments, and where it might make mistakes.his description is often given too smoothly, although in real practice, Russian education faces a more challenging issue — not every platform is able to take into account the context of the group, the course topic, and the varying pace at which students master the material. AI technologies in this area use a wide range of approaches: adaptive learning systems, intelligent assistants, automatic assignment grading, and recommendation services. The ethical dimension also cannot be ignored, because this raises questions about students’ data, the transparency of decisions, and who is responsible for the system’s error if the teacher trusted it too quickly and this later affected the assessment.

papers.title: Enhancing interpreter-mediated communication in mental health: An interprofessional educational approach through scenario co-creation and performance
papers.authors: Biyu Du
papers.abstract: No description provided

papers.title: Role of Chatbots and Virtual Assistants in the Management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
papers.authors: Manish Kumar, Pranav Bhati, Ritu Mishra, Rajiv Yadav, Sushma Chaturvedi
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The rising prevalence of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) calls for new digital tools and chatbots and virtual assistants are emerging as important enablers of patient care. In this article, we review their core technologies, including rule-based designs and advanced AI models using natural language processing, machine learning, and dialogue systems, and their roles in T2DM support, such as education, medication compliance, blood glucose tracking with tailored insights, dietary and physical activity changes, and connections with wearable devices and electronic health records. Clinical data from meta-analyses, randomised trials and implementation studies show significant impacts, including HbA1c reductions of 0.5–1.2%, increased patient engagement, and economic benefits. But there are still challenges, including technological limitations (such as accuracy issues), privacy concerns, moral questions (such as bias and access inequality), and issues with broad adoption by diverse groups. Future directions include next-generation AI with multi-sensory capabilities, harmonised regulations, and embedding into pharmacy-led clinical workflows to enable inclusive and effective T2DM management.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications for Early Disease Detection in Healthcare Systems
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: With delayed access to specialist expertise and subjective interpretation by clinicians and workload limiting the ability to access parts of the pathway, early disease detection is one of the most impactful levers that can be used to improve patient outcomes and reduce the cost of care.Medical image analysis, electronic health records (EHR), genomic data analysis, and analysis of physiological signals are all examples of medical data that can be transformed by artificial intelligence (AI) and especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), as there is no way they could be analyzed at the same scale and speed as would be possible by a human being.In this paper we bring together existing evidence of the use of AI in early detection in oncology, cardiology, neurology, dermatology, ophthalmology and critical care.It discusses the mathematical approaches used for their analysis such as the use of convolutional neural networks for image analysis and recurrent networks for time-series analysis of physiological data, and compares their reported diagnostic performance with that of conventional clinical analyses.The paper also examines real-world challenges to adoption, such as standardization of data, algorithmic bias, regulatory approval processes and clinician acceptance, and proposes some solutions.The results suggest that AI systems perform as well as or better than humans in precisely defined detection tasks but will not automatically translate this to better population health outcomes without attention to data quality, the need to integrate AI systems into workflows, and the need to ensure that everyone has access to them.The paper ends with policy, research and system recommendations for maximizing early detection programmatic value while responsibly scaling these initiatives.

papers.title: Оптимизација питања за квизове уз помоћ вештачке интелигенције
papers.authors: Milos Josipovic
papers.journal: Zbornik radova Fakulteta tehničkih nauka u Novom Sadu
papers.abstract: This paper presents a web application for creating and taking quizzes that integrates artificial intelligence into the educational process. Particular emphasis is placed on the automatic generation of quiz questions using AI, significantly accelerating and simplifying the quiz preparation process. In addition, several AI-powered functionalities have been implemented with the aim of enhancing the teaching and learning experience, improving educational outcomes, and increasing the efficiency of both teachers and students.

papers.title: PERAN OMNICHANNEL INTEGRATION DAN VALUE CO-CREATION DALAM MENINGKATKAN PATRONAGE INTENTION PADA RITEL KECANTIKAN
papers.authors: Dea Brenda Chikita, Evelyn Hendriana
papers.abstract: Strategi pemasaran dengan menggunakan omnichannel merupakan salah satu pendekatan yang saat ini sedang berkembang untuk meningkatkan penjualan dan loyalitas konsumen. Keberhasilan strategi tersebut tidak hanya bergantung pada kemudahan akses dan integrasi kanal, tetapi juga pada kemampuan perusahaan dalam menyesuaikan produk atau layanan. Namun, eksplorasi mengenai pengaruh integrasi channel dalam industri ritel kecantikan di Indonesia masih belum banyak diteliti. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh variabel consumer perception of channel integration terhadap consumer empowerment serta pengaruh consumer empowerment, customer participation behavior, dan customer perceived value terhadap patronage intention dengan menggunakan perspektif Service-Dominant Logic. Penelitian ini mengimplementasikan pendekatan kuantitatif pada 212 responden yang pernah berbelanja melalui ritel kecantikan berbasis omnichannel di Jabodetabek dan dianalisis menggunakan PLS-SEM. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh hipotesis diterima. Consumer perception of channel integration terbukti memiliki pengaruh positif terhadap consumer empowerment, sedangkan consumer empowerment, customer participation behavior, dan customer perceived value memiliki pengaruh positif terhadap patronage intention. Penelitian ini diharapkan dapat memberikan wawasan dan saran bagi perusahaan dalam meningkatkan patronage intention, terutama dengan meningkatkan customer perceived value. The omnichannel marketing strategy is a growing approach to increase sales and consumer loyalty. The success of this strategy depends not only on easy access and channel integration, but also on the company's ability to customize products or services. However, exploration of the influence of channel integration in the beauty retail context in Indonesia is still limited in previous research. This study aims to analyze the influence of consumer perception of channel integration on consumer empowerment, and the influence of consumer empowerment, customer participation behavior, and customer perceived value on patronage intention, using Service-Dominant Logic theory. This study used a quantitative approach, involving 212 respondents who had shopped at omnichannel beauty retailers in Greater Jakarta, and was analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results demonstrated that all hypotheses were accepted. Consumer perception of channel integration was found to positively affect consumer empowerment, while consumer empowerment, customer participation behavior, and customer perceived value positively affected patronage intention. This research is expected to insight and suggestions for company in improving patronage intention, especially by increasing customer perceived value.

papers.title: Modelo predictivo de las metas de aproximación al dominio: un análisis con IA
papers.authors: Francisco Quiñonez Tapia, María de Lourdes Vargas Garduño
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to use artificial intelligence (AI) to predict mastery-approach goals in secondary school students based on variables from the PISA 2018 database. The sample consisted of 339,560 participants from 60 countries. Machine learning was used with the Super Learner mega-algorithm with 14 candidate algorithms. In addition, deep learning was used with a neural network with 107 parameters. The analyses showed that students’ perceived parental emotional support, competitiveness, purpose in life, self-efficacy, and knowledge of intercultural communication were predictors of mastery-approach goals in secondary school students. This research contributes to the study of factors that influence mastery-approach goals in secondary school students, with analysis models that advance the development of the science of AI-based predictive education.

papers.title: Fiqh Education in the Context of Artificial intelligence: Shifts in Pedagogy, Authority, and Religious Literacy
papers.authors: Zuhri Zuhri, Faisal Amir Toedien
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded the use of information and learning resources in Islamic Religious Education, including Fiqh learning, while raising concerns regarding pedagogy, the authority and validity of religious knowledge, and students’ ability to evaluate AI-generated information. This study examines the use of AI in Islamic education and synthesizes its implications for Fiqh learning, focusing on pedagogy, the authority and validity of religious knowledge, and religious literacy and AI literacy. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted on 25 scholarly articles published between 2020 and 2026 and retrieved from Scopus, Google Scholar, and the Indonesian scholarly databases GARUDA/SINTA. Searches used combinations of keywords related to artificial intelligence, generative AI, ChatGPT, Islamic education, Islamic religious education, and fiqh education. Articles were selected based on their relevance to Islamic education or Fiqh learning and to the analytical dimensions of the study. Data were analyzed through coding, thematic categorization, cross-source comparison, and thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that AI is increasingly used to support personalized learning, information exploration, learning-material development, and instructional interaction. However, its use also intensifies the need for source verification, information validation, and teacher guidance. The synthesis further highlights the importance of integrating religious literacy and AI literacy to enable students to evaluate AI-generated information critically and responsibly. Based on these findings, the study proposes an AI-assisted but teacher-guided Fiqh learning framework that positions AI as a learning support tool, teachers as pedagogical and knowledge mediators, and students as active evaluators of information.

papers.title: Design Thinking for Mathematical Critical Thinking in Digital Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Suharjito, Aryo Andri Nugroho, FX Didik Purwosetiyono
papers.abstract: Mathematical critical thinking in digital learning requires purposeful interaction among pedagogical tasks, digital tools, and students' interpretation and justification of mathematical ideas. This systematic literature review examines the complementary functions of GeoGebra, Problem-Based Learning (PBL), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Meaningful Learning, and Design Thinking. The manuscript reports a qualitative thematic synthesis of 15 primary empirical studies published within the 2020–2026 search period and identified through Scopus, ERIC, Google Scholar, DOAJ, and Garuda. The available reporting record does not preserve complete database-specific retrieval and screening counts or item-level methodological appraisal results; the review therefore does not claim a fully reproducible PRISMA 2020 selection record. Across the cited evidence, GeoGebra provides dynamic mathematical representations; PBL structures problem-centred inquiry; AI offers feedback and alternative approaches that require mathematical verification; and Meaningful Learning emphasizes connections with prior knowledge. Design Thinking is proposed as a learner-centred organizing process through Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test. These differentiated functions support a conceptually coherent, potentially testable instructional pathway rather than a demonstrated effect of the combined intervention. Future research should verify the primary-study corpus, document review procedures in full, and test the proposed relationships in classroom settings.

papers.title: WHY BEL CANTO STILL MATTERS: FROM ITS ITALIAN ORIGINS THROUGH RUSSIAN NATIONAL OPERA TO CHINA’S VOCAL JOURNEY
papers.authors: Irina B. Gorbunova, Ji Yuchi
papers.abstract: The global vocal ecology underwent profound transformations across the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, yet the position of Bel Canto as the highest technical standard of the vocal art has never been shaken. Why does a vocal style born in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Italy still retain its “definitional authority” over the global vocal art two centuries later? Using the methods of music historiography and vocal-aesthetic analysis, this article conducts a coherent historical investigation of this question. It first traces the Italian historical foundations of Bel Canto: three centuries of European dominance, the genealogy of the term, and an aesthetic essence characterized by the organic unity of technique and songfulness. It then examines the world of style established during the golden age of Rossini, Bellini, and Donizetti, together with its mechanism of “co-creation” between composers and singers. The article subsequently analyzes the first localization of this style in Russia — from the romance to national opera, the formation of Russian bel canto and the Russian vocal school, as well as the continuing life of the Garcia teaching system through its documentary history and its lineage of performers. Finally, it examines the ongoing localization of Bel Canto in China since the twentieth century, including national opera creation (Ban Tiao Hong Jun Bei [Half a Red Army Quilt], Wang Guangqi), the worldwide breakthroughs of Chinese singers, and institutional support. This article argues that the contemporary significance of Bel Canto lies in its triple capacity: a self-correcting technical paradigm, the capacity to be transformed through localization, and the capacity for dialogue across cultural boundaries; its vitality lies not in being preserved but in being transformed. Yet the comparison of the two localizations likewise demonstrates that transformation is subject to strict conditions: Russia completed a full closed loop by “adopting the technical paradigm while retaining the national soul,” Aposta whereas China remains in an exploratory stage, in which a national synthesis at the creative level has not yet been achieved and detours deviating from the technical essence of bel canto have appeared. The development of Russian vocal art is China’s model and template: to respect the essence of bel canto first, and only then to develop a national style, this is the practicable path for Chinese vocal art in the twenty-first century.

papers.title: SYSTEM ANALYSIS OF MUSICAL CYBERNETIC SYSTEMS: THEORY, CLASSIFICATION, AND APPLICATIONS
papers.authors: Gleb G. Rogozinski, Irina B. Gorbunova
papers.abstract: Computer Music Technologies (CMT) combine musical acoustics, digital signal processing, and software engineering. These systems integrate automation, sound synthesis, and programming languages for composition. This article uses a systems-analytical approach to study CMT as complex structures, focusing on interactions to uncover developmental pathways. It highlights Musical Cybernetic Systems (MCS), which merge artificial intelligence, generative composition, and synthesis to expand creativity. Despite their use, MCS lack systematic study, complicating their analysis and optimization. The article proposes a methodology for analyzing MCS using signal theory, set theory, and graph theory. It identifies signal and symbolic information as key to understanding MCS data structures. Sound synthesis and processing systems are described using IDEF0 notation, with examples of sonification and generative processes. This approach reveals MCS design principles, offering insights into their functionality and interaction with external environments.

papers.title: XAI and its Applications in Decision Support System
papers.authors: Gitin Garg, Kiya Jain, Vishal Shrivastava, Akhil Pandey
papers.journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed decision-making across various industries by enabling systems to analyse large volumes of data and provide intelligent recommendations. However, many modern AI models, particularly deep learning algorithms, function as "black boxes," making it difficult for users to understand how decisions are generated. This lack of transparency limits the adoption of AI in critical domains such as healthcare, finance, law, and business. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a promising solution that improves transparency, interpretability, and trust in AI systems. Decision Support Systems (DSS) assist decision-makers by combining data, analytical models, and domain knowledge. Integrating XAI into DSS enables users to understand AI-generated recommendations, thereby improving confidence and accountability. This review paper explores the concepts of XAI, different explanation techniques, and their applications in DSS. The paper also discusses recent research, challenges, limitations, and future research directions

papers.title: El impacto de la inteligencia artificial agéntica en la educación y atención en salud
papers.authors: Miguel Ángel Saravia‐Rojas, Rocío Geng Vivanco
papers.abstract: The impact of agentic artificial intelligence on education and healthcare ESTIMADO EDITOR:La inteligencia artificial (IA) es una rama de la informática orientada al desarrollo de sistemas que emulan funciones cognitivas humanas, como el aprendizaje y la toma de decisiones 1 .Recientemente ha surgido la IA agéntica, basada en agentes autónomos capaces de actuar, planificar y adaptarse para alcanzar objetivos específicos con mínima supervisión humana 1 .A diferencia de los enfoques tradicionales, estos sistemas pueden aprender de manera continua y gestionar tareas complejas 1 .En la educación en ciencias de la salud, la IA agéntica permite generar entornos de aprendizaje personalizados, incluyendo simulaciones clínicas, casos interactivos y evaluaciones adaptativas 1 .Se ha reportado que su uso puede reducir significativamente el tiempo de diseño de escenarios educativos, optimizando recursos docentes 2 .En el ámbito asistencial, estos sistemas pueden asumir tareas administrativas y clínicas rutinarias, como la gestión de información y la monitorización de pacientes, facilitando decisiones informadas y mejorando la eficiencia 1 .Asimismo, contribuyen a la asignación de recursos, la predicción de eventos en salud pública y la personalización de intervenciones a partir de datos poblacionales 1 .Entre sus principales ventajas destacan la eficiencia operativa, la personalización de la atención y la capacidad de aprendizaje adaptativo 1,2 .Sin embargo, su implementación plantea desafíos éticos y regulatorios, como la necesidad de garantizar transparencia, responsabilidad, privacidad y equidad en las decisiones automatizadas 3 .En conclusión, la IA agéntica representa una innovación prometedora para la educación médica y los servicios de salud.

papers.title: Investigating Human Examiner Variability in Objective Structured Clinical Examinations Using Large Language Models as a Context-Invariant Comparator: An Observational Study (Preprint)
papers.authors: Pierre Danneels, Raphaël Gardic, Alexis Bourgeais, Léa Bourreau, Antoine Brochard, Stéphanie Marechal-Girault, Cédric Annweiler, Souhil Lebdai, Floris Chabrun, Edmond Démoulins
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Despite extensive standardization, objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) scoring remains subject to examiner-related variability. This variability may reflect individual examiner characteristics, examination context, or candidate-related factors, but their respective contributions remain difficult to quantify. Large language models (LLMs) offer a novel approach by providing a comparator unaffected by examination timing and candidate sequence. OBJECTIVE To investigate associations between examiner characteristics, individual and pair-level variability, examination context, and OSCE scoring differences using LLM scoring as a context-invariant comparator. METHODS In this prospective observational study, fifth- and sixth-year medical students completed summative OSCEs independently scored by two human examiners. Encounters were audio-recorded, transcribed, and scored by ChatGPT GPT-5.5 Thinking and Gemini 3.1 Pro using standardized checklists and a zero-shot prompt. Human-LLM clinical score differences on a 20-point scale were analyzed using mixed-effects models to examine examiner characteristics, individual and pair-associated variability, time of day, preceding candidate performance, and candidate performance level. ChatGPT was the primary comparator, with Gemini used for sensitivity analyses. Internal LLM repeatability was assessed through six independent evaluations of 24 transcripts. RESULTS The study included 381 students contributing 975 encounters across six stations, yielding 1950 human ratings from 54 examiners organized into 30 pairs. Female examiners awarded scores 0.44 points higher relative to ChatGPT than male examiners (95% CI 0.04-0.84), while nonclinical examiners scored 0.64 points higher than medical examiners (95% CI 0.17-1.10). No association was observed with surgical specialty or examiner seniority. Examiner-level deviations from station averages ranged from −1.28 to +1.86 points, with greater estimated variability at the examiner-pair level than at the examiner-specific level (SD 0.79 vs 0.32 points). No consistent association was identified with within-block examination time (P=.37), preceding candidate performance (P=.53), or candidate performance level (P=.84). Examiner-level differences were highly consistent across the two LLM comparators. Across six independent assessments, ChatGPT reproduced 93.8% of clinical encounter-item ratings identically (Fleiss κ=0.934), compared with 90.1% for Gemini (κ=0.916). CONCLUSIONS OSCE scoring appeared relatively robust to contextual and candidate-related influences, although variability persisted across individual examiners and examiner pairs. Using LLM scoring as a context-invariant comparator provides a novel way to investigate examiner-related variability.

papers.title: The Essence of Students’ Experiences in Utilizing The Gemini Application as Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Arabic Language Learning at KH. Mukhtar Syafaat University
papers.authors: Mohammad Alfin Rahma Nurfaizi, Sulaiman Hasan Sulaiman, Asmaul Husna
papers.abstract: This study aimed to describe students’ lived experiences in utilising the Gemini application as Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Arabic language learning and to identify the essence of these experiences. This study employed a qualitative phenomenological approach involving five students selected purposively based on their experience using Gemini for Arabic language learning. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation and analysed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings show that students experienced Gemini as a supportive learning medium in translating Arabic texts, searching for vocabulary (mufradat), understanding nahwu and sharaf, constructing Arabic sentences, and completing academic assignments. Students experienced greater ease and perceived efficiency in learning due to quick access to explanations provided by Gemini. However, they also experienced limitations when some responses were inaccurate or did not correspond with the learning context. These experiences led students to verify Gemini’s responses through lecturers, textbooks, dictionaries, classical Islamic texts and other academic sources. The essence of students’ experiences was identified by examining recurring meanings emerging from the interview, observation, and documentation data, particularly the experiences of convenience and perceived learning efficiency, along with the need for critical verification of AI-generated content. Thus, Gemini is experienced as a supplementary learning medium rather than a primary source of knowledge, supporting students’ learning while maintaining critical thinking, information verification, and academic responsibility skills.

papers.title: Technology Enhanced Arabic Language Teaching and Learning: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Muhammad Ainul Yaqin, Badriyya Barrak Alonazi
papers.abstract: Technology has increasingly reshaped Arabic language education through mobile applications, learning management systems, gamification, artificial intelligence (AI), augmented reality (AR), and other digital tools. However, the literature remains fragmented across technologies, language skills, learner populations and pedagogical models. This systematic literature review synthesises research on technology-enhanced Arabic language teaching and learning, with particular attention to digital tools, pedagogical approaches, learning outcomes, implementation challenges, and emerging research directions. The review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, with predefined eligibility criteria, database searching, dual screening, quality appraisal, data extraction, and thematic synthesis. The evidence reviewed indicates that technology can strengthen learner engagement, accessibility, vocabulary development, speaking and writing practice, formative feedback, and learner autonomy when digital tools are aligned with explicit pedagogical objectives. The strongest recurring pattern is not the superiority of a particular platform but the importance of pedagogical integration: technology is most productive when teachers provide scaffolding, feedback, interaction, and contextualised language use. The review also identifies persistent challenges involving teacher digital competence, infrastructure, Arabic-language resource quality, linguistic and cultural contextualisation, algorithmic limitations, and unequal access to resources. Whereas previous reviews examined single technologies (gamification, mobile learning, AR, VR, or AI) in isolation, this review integrates them into one technology-pedagogy-outcome framework, linking each technology to its pedagogical functions, targeted skills, outcomes, and implementation conditions.

papers.title: Digital transformation of outpatient care: physicians’ expectations and barriers to implementing telemedicine and artificial intelligence technologies.
papers.authors: E. N. Morozova, Шинкарева Наталья Владимировна, N. V. Eckert, A. V. Ferjaoui, Р. В. Горенков
papers.abstract: Background. In the context of healthcare digital transformation, telemedicine (TM) and artificial intelligence (AI) are being integrated into clinical practice; however, the pace of their implementation outpaces the analysis of their impact on workflows, workload, and physicians’ psychological acceptance. Studying systemic barriers and the human factor is essential for the successful scaling of digital tools in primary care. Objective: to assess real-world experience, identify key barriers, and determine the relationship between physicians’ expectations and practical challenges of implementing TM and AI in the activities of outpatient medical professionals. Materials and methods. A cross-sectional study was conducted using an anonymous online survey of 897 medical professionals from outpatient clinics in the Moscow region. The questionnaire covered socio-demographic and professional characteristics, frequency and formats of TM, AI and EHR use, as well as perceived barriers and risks. Statistical analysis employed descriptive statistics and Pearson’s χ² test (p < 0.05). Results. Daily TM consultations are conducted by 49.7% of physicians, predominantly in audio format (46.5%). Despite recognizing TM effectiveness for chronic patient follow-up (63.3%), 30.6% report increased workload, and 38.3% consider no more than two consultations per day optimal. The main TM barriers are technical failures (29.3%) and low patient digital literacy (16.2%). Regarding AI, a gap was revealed: readiness for use is 55%, while 60.5% have no practical experience; 50.1% fear degradation of their diagnostic skills. Major systemic issues include insufficient interoperability (43.6%) and lack of training (22.8%). Statistical analysis confirmed significant associations between AI use and expectations (p < 0.05), and between training needs and AI readiness (χ² = 23.979; p < 0.001). Conclusion. A persistent gap was identified between positive perceptions of digital technologies’ potential and the real challenges of their integration. The barriers – technical, organizational, and psychological – are systemic and require comprehensive solutions: specialized training, minimization of technical failures, ensuring information systems interoperability, and revision of workload standards considering the time spent on TM consultations.

papers.title: From AI Adoption Intention to Measurable Outcomes: Integrating an Actionable Framework with a Logical Framework Matrix for Malaysian Public Sector Organisations
papers.authors: Norazlin Mohd Nor, Norazlin Mohd Nor, Mior Harris Mior Harun, Norzanah Mat Nor, Norzanah Mat Nor
papers.abstract: Public sector organisations need to connect AI training and pilot initiatives with improvements in work practices, productivity and service delivery. This study examines factors associated with managers’ intention to adopt AI and develops a framework for planning and evaluating implementation. An online, cross-sectional survey of 402 Malaysian federal public sector managers, who help translate organisational direction into operational practice, was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence and facilitating conditions were positively associated with behavioural intention. AI literacy negatively moderated the association between social influence and intention (β = −0.109, p = 0.012), suggesting reduced reliance on social cues among managers with higher AI literacy. The other tested interactions were not statistically significant. These findings informed the integration of the Actionable AI Adoption Framework for Government (A3F-Gov) with a Logical Framework Matrix. The proposed framework connects individual adoption factors with organisational interventions, measurable outputs and intended outcomes, supported by indicators, verification sources, assumptions and feedback mechanisms. It contributes to systems practice by guiding coordinated planning, monitoring and adaptation across implementation stages. Prospective evaluation will help establish how these pathways support sustained changes in managerial practice, workflows and service delivery.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Reporting and Auditing: Challenges and Future Opportunities
papers.authors: Dr Rajesh Kumar, Lalita Babulal Malusare, Dr. Farhan Alam, Snehasish Bhattacharjee, Harmanpreet Singh
papers.journal: The Journal of Theoretical Accounting Research
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a game-changer in the world of financial reporting and auditing, revolutionizing the traditional methods of accounting and auditing by automating tasks, providing predictive insights, intelligent decision making, and real-time data processing. This research delves into the integration of AI into accounting systems, financial reporting and the auditing landscape, presenting challenges, governance issues and future prospects. The potential areas of the application of AI are covered, including automated bookkeeping, intelligent financial reporting, fraud detection, continuous auditing, blockchain-based assurance systems and AI-based sustainability reporting. Furthermore, the paper highlights several issues associated with algorithmic bias, transparency and explainability, cyber security, ethical implications and regulatory uncertainties in AI-powered accounting systems. In addition, the study examines key strategic implications for accounting firms, auditors, regulators, and policymakers on the use of AI, such as the importance of governance, the role of AI in human-AI partnerships, and the need for professional competency development. Moreover, the study identifies future trends and opportunities of autonomous accounting systems, generative AI, integrated ESG reporting and intelligent audit ecosystems. The results imply that AI can improve the quality of reporting, effectiveness of an audit, operational efficiency, and strategic financial decision-making. However, a balance is needed between technology innovation, ethical governance, regulatory supervision and professional judgment of humans for sustainable adoption of AI. The study offers a conceptual base for future research in intelligent financial reporting and auditing environment and also adds to the literature of intelligent accounting systems.

papers.title: LLM-supported EFL writing: AI feedback literacy, revision behaviour, and writing self-efficacy among Vietnamese undergraduates
papers.authors: Khanh Quoc Nguyen, Quang Nhat Vo
papers.journal: Journal of English Language Teaching and Learning (JETLE)
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional survey examined whether AI feedback literacy and revision behaviour mediated the association between large language model (LLM) co-editing intensity and writing self-efficacy among 305 Vietnamese undergraduates with recent experience using LLM tools for English writing revision. The questionnaire measured LLM co-editing intensity, AI feedback literacy, revision behaviour, and writing self-efficacy. Reliability estimates were acceptable to good, and exploratory factor analysis supported the proposed four-factor structure. Serial mediation analysis with 5,000 bootstrap resamples showed significant indirect associations between LLM co-editing intensity and writing self-efficacy through AI feedback literacy, revision behaviour, and their sequential pathway. The serial indirect effect was 0.048, with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [0.024, 0.080], and the total indirect effect was 0.206, 95% CI [0.140, 0.283]. Given the cross-sectional and self-reported data, these findings are interpreted as associational rather than causal. Pedagogically, the results suggest that LLM-supported EFL writing instruction should focus not simply on increasing tool use but on helping students evaluate AI-generated feedback and translate it into purposeful revision decisions.

papers.title: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence in organic supply chains: A systematic review with insights from South Tamil Nadu
papers.authors: Rakesh Kumar Sundararajan, Thangasundari Ramasamy
papers.journal: Journal of Management Research and Analysis
papers.abstract: Organic agriculture is growing rapidly in India, yet organic supply chains remain structurally fragmented, particularly in smallholder-dominated regions such as South Tamil Nadu. Digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) offer promising solutions to persistent challenges, including inadequate cold-chain infrastructure, limited traceability, intermediary-dependent marketing and certification workflow inefficiencies. This systematic review draws on evidence from 30 peer-reviewed and institutional publications. These sources were identified through a PRISMA-compliant search of Scopus, Elsevier, Taylor & Francis, Web of Science, IEEE, MDPI, Wiley, FAO, and government databases. The findings indicate that AI-enabled precision farming, machine learning-based demand forecasting, Internet of Things-enabled cold-chain monitoring, and blockchain-supported traceability improve production efficiency, market access and organic supply chain transparency. However, widespread adoption is constrained by inadequate rural connectivity, limited digital literacy, incompatibility between digital platforms and Participatory Guarantee System certification workflows, and weak first-mile infrastructure. This review proposes the Digital Transformation and AI Readiness Framework for Organic Supply Chains (DARF-OSC). DARF-OSC is a five-stage conceptual model that integrates Diffusion of Innovations theory with the Resource-Based View. Also, this review identifies five key research gaps and tiered policy recommendations for South Tamil Nadu.

papers.title: AI literacy: Gen Z expectations vs. organisational practices in India's dynamic job market
papers.authors: Kumkum Tripathi, Aastha Patidar, Shine David
papers.journal: Journal of Management Research and Analysis
papers.abstract: The mismatch between Generation Z's (Gen Z) high expectations of artificial intelligence (AI) and organisational AI practices has profound implications for vocational well-being in India's job market. This research explores the structural path between Gen Z’s AI Expectations, Organisational AI Practices, and AI Literacy-Driven Vocational Well-being, with Skills Velocity as a key contextual variable in a rapidly changing, technology-driven landscape.This research used a mixed-methods approach. A structured questionnaire was administered to 203 Gen Z professionals and HR managers in AI-heavy industries (IT, BFSI and manufacturing) in Tier-1 and Tier-2 cities in India. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) using the lavaan package in R was used to test the path model. We triangulated our findings with 20 semi-structured interviews. The sample was skewed towards males (70:30 male-to-female) and non-normal.Based on the findings, the model fit was satisfactory. Gen Z's AI Expectations positively impacted Organisational AI Practices (β = 0.608, p < .001) and AI Literacy-driven Vocational Well-being (β = 0.449, p < .001). Organisational AI Practices also significantly and positively influenced Vocational Well-being (β = 0.418, p < .001). The variance in Organisational AI Practices and Vocational Well-being explained by the model was 36.9% and 60.4%, respectively.The research suggests that matching organisational AI practices to Gen Z expectations is crucial to improving AI literacy-based vocational well-being in India's ever-evolving labour market. The findings reveal the important role of Gen Z as a driver for change in organisations and the need for forward-looking, skills-velocity-sensitive human resource management strategies such as AI upskilling and training, ethical AI policies and lifelong learning opportunities to enhance retention and workforce preparedness.

papers.title: Factors associated with fatigue in stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and its impact on exercise capacity and health-related quality of life
papers.authors: Vijay Babu Renganathan, Kandavel Gurusamipalayam Sivamani, PriyadharshiniPrasanna Venkateswaran
papers.journal: IP Indian Journal of Immunology and Respiratory Medicine
papers.abstract: Background: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Fatigue is a common but often underrecognized symptom that significantly affects functional status, exercise capacity, and quality of life in patients with COPD.Aims and Objectives: To evaluate the determinants and clinical impact of fatigue in patients with stable COPD and to assess its association with disease severity, exercise capacity, and health-related quality of life.Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional observational study was conducted in the Department of Respiratory Medicine, KLE's Dr. Prabhakar Kore Hospital and Medical Research Centre, Belagavi, Karnataka, from January 2020 to December 2020. A total of 100 patients with stable COPD aged >40 years were enrolled using consecutive sampling. Fatigue was assessed using the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy–Fatigue (FACIT-F) Scale. Exercise capacity was measured using the Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), dyspnoea using the Modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) scale, and health-related quality of life using the St. George’s Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ).Results: The mean age of participants was 61.73 ± 9.72 years. papers.title: Beyond MOS: judging synthetic voices by what L2 listeners understand
papers.authors: Sardor Egamovich Surmanov
papers.abstract: Study type: Observational (within-subjects experiment) Research questions: RQ1: Do comprehension, intelligibility and listening effort differ between a human reader, an open-source synthetic voice, and an LLM-based synthetic voice (default and learner-directed), for L2 listeners? RQ2: Do conventional naturalness ratings rank the voices the same way as learner comprehension, intelligibility and effort? Design: Within-subject, 4 voice conditions (H, OS, LD, LL) × 8 passages, 4 Latin-square lists. Each participant hears all 8 passages, each voice exactly twice. Participants: 48 L2 English listeners, aged 18+, students in the Foreign Languages department. 12 per list. Exclusion: under 18, incomplete session, failed device check. Materials: 8 B1-level passages (200-250 words each), 5 four-option MCQ items per passage, 1 dictation sentence per passage. Voices: human reader (male, L1 Uzbek, IELTS 8.0, neutral read); Kokoro-82M am_michael speed 1.0; Gemini 2.5 TTS Fenrir, LD prompt "Read the following text aloud."; LL prompt [full learner-directed text]. All audio mono, 44.1 kHz, -23 LUFS. Measures: - Comprehension (0-5 per passage) - Dictation (words correct / total) - Effort (1-9) - Naturalness learner (1-5) - Suitability (1-5) - Proficiency screen (10 items) - Teacher MOS naturalness (1-5) — separate panel of 10-15 English teachers Analysis: Mixed logistic and linear models with random effects for participant, passage, item. Kendall's W for RQ2 ranking comparison. Sensitivity analysis via simulation across n=32,40,48. Pilot: 5 students excluded from analysis. Data availability: audio, scripts and anonymised data on OSF.

papers.title: Commitment and ethical duty of social communicators toward victims of the Colombian armed conflict: an audiovisual practice perspective
papers.authors: Sandra Carolina Patiño-Ospina, Carlos Rodríguez-Pérez, Sergio Andrés Forero Machado, Miguel Ángel Brand-Narváez, Claudia Tovar Guerra, Juan David Zabala Sandoval, Viviam Andrea García Pachón
papers.abstract: This article examines the challenges inherent to audiovisual production in contexts involving victims of the armed conflict in Colombia. To this end, it focuses on audiovisual producers as social communicators—professionals capable of creating spaces and social practices that foster citizenship and, through communication, contribute to shaping a collective sense of meaning. Methodologically, drawing on an interpretive qualitative approach with thematic analysis, five discussion groups were implemented, and the discourse generated among the participants was analyzed. According to the participating filmmakers, the two main contributions focus on the audiovisual as a tool and process to promote 1) the recognition and dignification of the victim during the audiovisual co-creation process and 2) the externalization of emotions. A third relevant aspect lies in the commitment and ethical duty of the audiovisual production team towards the communities. These findings are discussed from the perspective of the responsibility that falls on the audiovisual production team during all phases of production so that they can act as a social agent capable of giving communication the necessary meaning to build citizenship.

papers.title: Exploration d’un texte littéraire dans l’enseignement du FLE : dossier pédagogique sur « La voix de Robert Desnos »
papers.authors: Záviš Šuman
papers.abstract: This educational guide presents a pedagogical project focused on teaching modern poetry in French as a Foreign Language (FFL). It argues that, although modern poetry often seems obscure because it abandons the purely communicative function of language, it can actually become a valuable tool for developing learners’ critical awareness, creativity, and interpretive skills. The author opposes the current trend of undervaluing literature, asserting that literary study remains essential in an age dominated by AI and communication-oriented methods. Rather than avoiding the difficulties of modern poetry – its commonly assumed lack of logical structure, paradoxical imagery, and ambiguous meanings – teachers should transform these challenges into opportunities for discussion and discovery. The proposed activities aim to help both teachers and learners overcome the misconception that modern poetry is inaccessible. A poem by Robert Desnos (“La voix de Robert Desnos” / The Voice of Robert Desnos) is used as a practical example, encouraging playful yet structured interpretation through guided questions and inductive reasoning. The project targets mainly young adult learners (B1 level or higher) and can be used in university or international programs for undergraduates. The dossier includes a glossary for advanced terminology and was developed collaboratively with students at Charles University (Czech Republic, Prague) between 2023 and 2026.

papers.title: Caring cannot be prompted: An Autoethnography of Becoming a Nurse Educator in an AI-Enabled ODeL Environment
papers.authors: Regine Karla Bagalanon
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) integration into nursing education presents challenges to preserving the human values that define the profession. While AI offers opportunities to enhance teaching and learning, it raises questions about authentic learning, educator identity, and the place of human caring in technology-mediated environments. Guided by Watson's Theory of Human Caring, this analytic autoethnography examined the evolving identity of a nurse educator across intersecting roles as a registered nurse, Open and Distance e-Learning (ODeL) learner, and educator during the emergence of generative AI (GenAI). Personal experiences across these roles traced how the understanding of caring evolved—from recognizing vulnerability in clinical practice to intentionally designing learning experiences that cultivate reflection, educator presence, and authentic engagement in an AI-enabled classroom. The findings demonstrated that AI did not diminish caring; rather, it clarified the distinctly human dimensions of teaching that technology cannot reproduce, including ethical judgment, compassion, meaningful relationships, and reflective practice. These experiences further demonstrated that caring could be intentionally expressed through instructional design, authentic assessment, timely feedback, and sustained educator presence, even within ODeL environments. The study argues that the future of nursing education is not defined by the adoption of AI itself but by the capacity of educators to preserve and cultivate human caring while thoughtfully integrating technological innovation. Ultimately, while AI may enhance learning, caring remains the moral foundation of nursing education because it cannot be automated, replicated, or prompted.

papers.title: From AI Tools to Learner-Centered Human–AI Collaboration: Developing and Evaluating the Learner-Centered Human–AI Pedagogical Framework (LCHAP)
papers.authors: Myagmarsuren Orosoo, Namjildagva Raash, Tumentsetseg Baljinnyam, Munkhtsetseg Narantsetseg
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping higher education, yet practical guidance for integrating it into meaningful learning remains limited. This paper introduces the Learner-Centered Human–AI Pedagogical Framework (LCHAP), which positions AI as a collaborative cognitive partner while preserving learner agency and responsibility. LCHAP was implemented through the Human–AI Learning Cycle (HALC) in a 15-week quasi-experimental mixed-methods study involving 80 first-year undergraduates at the Mongolian National University of Education. At post-intervention, the experimental group showed higher mean scores than the control group in English writing, learner engagement, learner autonomy, AI literacy, reflective learning, and critical thinking. Qualitative evidence indicated a shift from answer generation toward idea exploration, comparison, revision, and reflection. Because the reported quantitative evidence is descriptive, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary rather than causal. LCHAP offers a practical design framework for responsible, learner-centered Human–AI collaboration in higher education.

papers.title: Perceived AIGC saturation and AI content fatigue on short-video platforms: An appraisal-based structural equation modeling study
papers.authors: Zedai Wang, Chao Tang
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is increasingly embedded in short-video platforms, where algorithmic recommendation systems expose users to high volumes of rapidly produced synthetic media. Although prior research has examined generative AI from the perspectives of creativity, productivity, and technology adoption, less is known about how ordinary users evaluate repeated exposure to AI-generated short videos. This study develops and tests an appraisal-based model of AI content fatigue, distinguishing perceived AIGC saturation from users' appraisals of low-quality prevalence, narrative homogenization, and content overload. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Chinese short-video users in May 2026. After excluding invalid responses, 513 valid questionnaires were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. The adjusted structural model showed acceptable fit to the data, χ²(1321) = 1991.541, χ²/df = 1.508, CFI = .946, TLI = .929, IFI = .947, and RMSEA = .031. Perceived AIGC saturation was positively associated with perceived low-quality prevalence, perceived narrative homogenization, and perceived content overload. Perceived low-quality prevalence had the largest estimated coefficient, followed by perceived content overload, whereas perceived narrative homogenization was not supported under bootstrap inference. AI content fatigue was negatively associated with satisfaction and continued viewing intention. Bootstrap analyses indicated selected path-specific indirect associations from perceived AIGC saturation to AI content fatigue, satisfaction, and continued viewing intention. Indirect pathways through perceived low-quality prevalence and perceived content overload were supported, whereas those through perceived narrative homogenization were not. The findings indicate that fatigue in AIGC-rich short-video environments is not simply a response to AI-generated content itself. It is more closely related to users' appraisals of content quality, repetitiveness, and cognitive burden. The study contributes to social media fatigue research by conceptualizing AI content fatigue as a content-specific evaluative state and offers implications for platform governance, AIGC labeling, recommendation diversity, and quality-sensitive moderation.

papers.title: The double-edged sword of human-AI collaboration on design students’ competence development: The mediating roles of challenge and hindrance appraisals and the asymmetric moderation of teacher AI leadership
papers.authors: Xiang Wang, Mingxing Li, Jia Du, YU Yao, Jiabei Jiang
papers.abstract: The deepening integration of generative AI into design education is driving a paradigm shift in human-computer AI collaboration (HAIC) -from mere tool assistance toward intelligent synergy. However, its dual impact on the competency development of design students and the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Grounded in the Theory of Stress Appraisal, this study constructs a research model to examine the double-edged sword effect of HAIC on Design Competence (DC), introducing teacher AI Leadership (AIL) as a moderating variable. The aim is to reveal the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions through which HAIC influences DC. Employing a questionnaire survey, this study conducted an empirical investigation involving 483 design students in East China. Data analysis was performed using SPSS 24.0 and Amos 23.0, encompassing reliability and validity tests, regression analysis, and Bootstrap mediation analysis. The results indicate that HAIC influences DC through dual pathways: it positively enhances DC by fostering Challenge Appraisal (CA) (β = 0.283, p < 0.01), which in turn positively predicted competence development (β = 0.363, p < 0.01), yielding a significant indirect effect of 0.103 (p < 0.01). Simultaneously, HAIC triggered Hindrance Appraisal (HA) (β = 0.271, p < 0.01), which negatively predicted competence development (β = -0.229, p < 0.01), yielding a significant indirect effect of -0.062 (p < 0.01). This constitutes a partial mediating mechanism characterized by "one positive, one negative" effect. Furthermore, Teacher AIL exhibits an asymmetric moderating effect: it significantly buffers the positive impact of HAIC on HA (β = -0.112, p < 0.01), indicating that high AIL can mitigate cognitive load and anxiety arising from technological uncertainty, yet it does not significantly amplify the positive pathway via CA (β = 0.001, p > 0.05). The findings suggest that the impact of HAIC on DC is not linear but rather a dialectical process contingent upon individual cognitive appraisal. The core value of Teacher AIL lies in "risk mitigation" rather than "creativity stimulation," offering a theoretical foundation for the intelligent transformation of educational design. At the practical level, it is imperative to facilitate from knowledge deliverers to cognitive facilitators in AI-augmented design education. By systematically developing AI instructional competencies and reforming assessment systems, educators can guide students toward establishing a healthy relationship with HAIC, thereby achieving the synergistic advancement of technological empowerment and humanistic literacy.

papers.title: Interventions with mitochondrial-related effects in older adults with type 2 diabetes: Protocol for a systematic review with conditional network meta-analysis
papers.authors: Hao Liu, Aochuan Sun, Yu Deng, Yihan Li, Jiayu Hu, Zhengtang Liu
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Mitochondrial dysfunction is central to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) pathogenesis, driving insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction. Age-related mitochondrial impairment worsens this in older adults, yet evidence on mitochondrial interventions for this group is limited. This protocol outlines a systematic review and conditional network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating mitochondrial interventions in adults aged 60+ with T2DM. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this systematic review and conditional network meta-analysis (NMA) is to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of diverse mitochondrial-related interventions, including pharmacological agents, nutritional supplements, and lifestyle modifications, relative to placebo, standard care, or no intervention, on mitochondrial function biomarkers in adults aged 60 years or older with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Interventions with mitochondrial effects are operationally defined as those whose primary mechanism is known to target mitochondrial pathways or those that are explicitly evaluated for their effects on direct markers of mitochondrial function in the trial. The secondary objectives are: (1) to assess the impact of these interventions on glycemic and metabolic control outcomes including glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), fasting insulin, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), body weight, and body mass index (BMI); (2) to conduct a conditional NMA to compare and rank the relative efficacy of different intervention categories if the evidence network is sufficiently connected and clinically coherent; and (3) to explore potential sources of heterogeneity (e.g., intervention duration, baseline HbA1c levels) via prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Prepared per PRISMA-P, the review will follow PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA if applicable. Registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251145356), searches will cover PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to April 2026. Focused on T2DM, mitochondrial function/dysfunction, and interventions, age eligibility will be assessed during full-text screening. Primary analysis includes trials with participants aged 60+ or extractable data for this group; sensitivity analyses will include those with mean/median age ≥ 60. Two reviewers will handle screening, data extraction, and bias assessment using RoB 2.Analysis will focus on trials reporting mitochondrial function outcomes, categorized by biological domain, tissue source, and assay method. Glycemic control, geriatric health, and safety are secondary outcomes. Network meta-analysis will be conducted if a connected evidence network exists; otherwise, pairwise meta-analysis or narrative synthesis will be used. Random-effects models will be employed, with heterogeneity assessed via subgroup analysis and meta-regression. If significant heterogeneity persists, a Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) framework narrative review will be done. Evidence certainty will be appraised using GRADE and CINeMA. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval is not required for this systematic review as the systematic review will include only previously anonymised data from primary studies. Dissemination of the findings of the final systematic review will occur through publishing in a peer-reviewed journal. PROSPERO registration number CRD420251145356.

papers.title: Concurrent TMS-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms
papers.authors: Jie Zhou, Yiting He, Chenxia Jin, Chen Yang, Yazhen Han, Yujun Wang, Zhen Zhen, Zhimin Huang, Shuyan Shi, Xianwei Che, Jiqing He
papers.abstract: Callosal abnormalities disrupt interhemispheric communications that impair the recovery of a series of neurological and psychiatric disorders. Understanding interhemispheric communication could help identify treatments for disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission. This study aimed to validate the sensitivity of a TMS-EEG-based measure of interhemispheric signal propagation (ISP) to GABAB receptor modulation, while independently replicating the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition. A group of 29 participants received an oral dose of either baclofen, a GABAB receptor agonist, or a placebo. Before and after drug intake, single-pulse TMS-EEG was applied to assess ISP in both the motor and prefrontal regions. Our findings indicated that baclofen increased interhemispheric inhibition over the motor region, indexed by significantly decreased ISP (p = 0.037). No significant effect was observed in the dorsolateral prefrontal region (p = 0.186), suggesting regional specificity in GABAB receptor modulation of ISP. These findings uncovered the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition as indexed by ISP. They also highlight the potential of ISP for characterising interhemispheric communication, which could inform the treatment for a series of disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission.

papers.title: A Web Engineering Approach to AI-Enabled Japanese Tutoring via Instructional Design Pattern Mining
papers.authors: Xiaomei Gai, Yanjia Tian
papers.abstract: Despite the proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled web applications for Japanese language learning, existing platforms suffer from three critical challenges: insufficient integration of AI capabilities with pedagogical design, limited scenario adaptability across proficiency levels, and suboptimal lightweight deployment on the browser side. To address these gaps and explore instructional design patterns tailored to diverse Japanese learning needs, this study focuses on web application technology implementation and interaction design as the core analytical dimensions. Three typical AI-enabled Japanese tutoring web applications were selected as research objects, and 192 Japanese learners participated in the empirical research. Quantitative data were obtained through technical disassembly, questionnaire surveys, and web-based behavior tracking; learning effects were verified by comparative experiments, and the weight of instructional design elements was determined via the analytic hierarchy process, finally extracting core instructional design modes suitable for the mainstream Japanese learning stages from beginner to upper-intermediate (Japanese-Language Proficiency Test [JLPT] N5–N2), with preliminary applicability discussion for the advanced stage (N1 and above). The results show that web-based lightweight AI technology deployment and real-time AI interactive feedback design are the core elements, with a combined weight of over 40%. There is a significant positive correlation between web-based AI technology implementation and user satisfaction, with the highest implementation effect and user acceptance in listening, speaking, and grammar modules. Compared with traditional Japanese web learning platforms, AI-enabled instructional design can improve learners’ listening and speaking abilities by 58.0%(M=58.0,SD=4.2,95% CI [56.4, 59.6], Cohen’s d=1.82, large effect), grammar analysis abilities by 46.5% (M=46.5,SD=5.1,95%CI [44.8, 48.2], Cohen’s d=1.45, large effect), and enhance learning sustainability by 85.7% (M=85.7,SD=6.3,95%CI[83.5,87.9], Cohen’s d=2.01, large effect), based on N5–N2 learner data with robust statistical power. Three core instructional design modes were identified, adapted to zero-based-N4 fragmented learning, N3–N2 systematic learning, and N1+ immersive learning, respectively. This study clarifies the core elements and optimization direction of such applications, providing standardized and practical theoretical references and paths for their design, development, and teaching practice.

papers.title: Higher education assessments in the age of GenAI: a systematic review
papers.authors: Helen Crompton, Diane Burke
papers.journal: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
papers.abstract: Abstract Assessment in higher education has long centered on core principles such as validity, authenticity, and alignment with learning outcomes, alongside ongoing debates about how best to support academic integrity and meaningful feedback. The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is now placing renewed pressure on these established principles, prompting institutions to reconsider how assessment is designed, delivered, and evaluated. While a growing body of research has examined GenAI’s role in teaching and learning broadly, less synthesis exists on how it is reshaping assessment specifically, and how these shifts relate to long-standing assessment theory and practice. This systematic review provides an up-to-date examination of empirical research published between 2024 and 2026 on how GenAI is influencing assessment practices and supporting educators in assessing student learning. Using PRISMA, 72 studies were identified and analyzed. The findings show that research was conducted across 24 countries and 20 academic disciplines. Two overarching research purposes emerged: (1) investigating the use of GenAI in assessment and (2) examining perceptions of GenAI in assessment. Qualitative approaches were the most common research methodology. Three major assessment design approaches emerged in response to GenAI: (1) process orientation, (2) authenticity, and (3) oral and dialogical approaches. Five ways educators used GenAI across the assessment process were identified: (1) creating assessments, (2) practice for assessments, (3) grading, (4) transparency of learning, and (5) feedback. Together, these findings situate GenAI’s influence with the broader trajectory of assessment scholarship and provides researchers, educators, institutional leaders, and policymakers a clearer picture of how assessment practices are being negotiated in response to GenAI

papers.title: Equipping the next generation: addressing the unmet need for artificial intelligence education at research performing organizations
papers.authors: Jeremy Y. Ng, Wid Al-Zahraa Al-Khafaji, David Moher
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools into higher education is rapidly accelerating, yet the educational ecosystem appears largely unprepared for the scale and speed of adoption. Our recent international survey of over 1,200 university students and postdoctoral fellows in the medical and life sciences found that while more than 80% had used GenAI tools, the vast majority had received no formal training, and many were unaware of any institutional policies governing their use. This gap between adoption and institutional preparedness may pose risks to research integrity if left unaddressed. MAIN BODY: Existing research supports a coordinated, evidence-informed approach to AI education in research performing organizations (RPOs), grounded in principles of research integrity, equity, and critical engagement with technology. First, GenAI literacy must be embedded as a core competency in scientific and clinical education, equipping students to critically evaluate tool outputs, recognize hallucination and bias, and understand the distinction between AI-generated inaccuracy and deliberate research misconduct. Second, traditional frameworks for academic integrity would benefit from re-examination. Today, GenAI tools have fundamentally disrupted established notions of authorship, originality, and plagiarism, and the absence of coherent institutional guidance leaves students and educators navigating these questions without support. Third, RPOs must develop clear, transparent, and context-sensitive policies on GenAI use by embedding responsible AI education into curricula, equipping learners not only to use these tools effectively, but to question, verify, and critique their outputs in ways that uphold scientific standards. CONCLUSION: RPOs have an urgent responsibility to move beyond reactive responses and toward proactive strategies that uphold scientific standards, promote equity of access, and prepare the next generation of researchers and clinicians to engage with GenAI responsibly and ethically.

papers.title: Public technical disclosure of AI implementation in finance: Python-framed evidence from 253 NYSE-listed financial companies
papers.authors: Veliota Drakopoulou
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) claims in public markets increasingly raise disclosure, comparability, and investor-protection questions, yet evidence on how listed financial firms publicly describe implementation remains fragmented and difficult to compare. This study examines public technical disclosure rather than internal adoption by constructing a screened, exchange-bounded corpus for 253 NYSE-listed financial companies. The source intake contained 554 rows; six exact repeated rows were removed before screening, leaving 548 screened rows. The 505-sentence extended analysis corpus combines a 253-sentence firm-anchor layer with a 252-sentence direct-verification layer; the remaining issuer is retained in the direct-verification audit as a closed unit with no strict direct match. Firms are coded into three disclosure states: explicit Python, indirect AI, and none, and the corpus is used to map subsector profiles, channel location, and the rarity of quantified public outcome claims through an outcome claims index (OCI). The results show that 34 firms (13.4%) are classified as Explicit Python, 216 (85.4%) as Indirect AI, and 3 (1.2%) as None. Explicit Python naming is uneven across subsectors and is concentrated mainly in employment materials and technical documentation rather than in filings or investor-facing channels. The public technical surface is therefore real but thin: firms more often signal implementation orientation than disclose a detailed tool stack. Quantified public outcome claims are rarer still, with five OCI-positive firms and five OCI-positive sentences (1.98% of firms). These findings indicate that public financial-sector communication is much stronger on AI-related implementation signals than on measurable outcomes. The paper offers a reproducible disclosure map for a bounded listed firm population and a framework for distinguishing general AI language, implementation-specific technical naming, and quantified public claims in regulated capital market settings.

papers.title: Resting-state beta-band oscillatory dysfunction bridges Alzheimer’s pathology and memory impairment
papers.authors: Chia‐Hsiung Cheng, Hsinjie Lu, Hsin-I Chang, Shu-Hua Huang, Ting-Yu Lin, Chen-Yuan Hsueh, Chiung-Chih Chang
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Resting-state electroencephalography (rs-EEG) is a promising non-invasive biomarker of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet its role in linking molecular pathology to cognitive impairment remains unclear. We investigated whether rs-EEG spectral activity is associated with amyloid-β and tau pathology and how these measures relate to cognition. Methods Thirty-six biomarker-confirmed participants with amyloid-positive Alzheimer’s disease-related mild cognitive impairment (AD-MCI) and 38 cognitively normal older adults underwent rs-EEG assessment. Patients with AD-MCI additionally received amyloid-β and tau positron emission tomography (PET). Power spectral density across frequency bands was compared between groups. Partial correlation analyses examined associations among PET biomarkers, rs-EEG activity, and cognitive performance measured by the Cognitive Abilities Screening Instrument (CASI). Regression-based mediation analyses were performed with adjustment for age, sex, education, and APOE ε4 status. Results Compared with controls, patients with AD-MCI showed increased delta/theta power and reduced beta power. Greater amyloid burden was associated with lower beta-band activity across multiple regions, whereas higher tau burden was associated with reduced beta activity and regionally increased delta and theta activity. Poorer memory performance was associated with reduced beta activity and increased theta activity. Amyloid burden showed no robust direct association with memory performance; however, it was indirectly associated with memory through beta-band activity. In contrast, tau burden was directly associated with poorer memory, and no significant mediation effects through beta activity were observed. Conclusions Beta-band activity may represent a systems-level correlate linking AD pathology and cognition, with amyloid-β showing indirect associations via network dynamics and tau demonstrating more direct relationships with memory impairment.

papers.title: The experience of using large language models for academic purposes among nursing graduate students: a descriptive phenomenological study
papers.authors: Xue Zhang, Jiang Nan, Zhen Yang
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are profoundly transforming higher education. However, their deep integration into knowledge production presents unique challenges for nursing graduate students, who must balance rigorous academic training with clinical ethical responsibilities and humanistic values. To explore the authentic experiences, cognitive processes, and underlying dilemmas of nursing graduate students using LLMs for academic purposes. A descriptive phenomenological qualitative design was employed. Using purposive sampling with a maximum variation strategy, 28 nursing graduate students were recruited. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews from January to April 2026. Transcripts were analyzed using a systematic thematic analysis approach. The analysis revealed three core themes: (1) Reshaping academic cognitive patterns, highlighting a duality where participants perceived that LLMs reduced early-stage cognitive burden and research anxiety, while some also reported concerns that reliance on AI-generated content might weaken their clinical critical thinking; (2) Dilemmas of nursing ethics and academic norms, characterized by blurred patient privacy boundaries during clinical data processing and confusion regarding academic originality and researcher identity; and (3) Conflict and integration between instrumental rationality and humanistic care, revealing algorithmic limitations in conveying deep empathy and authentic patient experiences, juxtaposed with the technology’s undeniable advantage in overcoming language barriers to promote the international dissemination of local nursing concepts. Participants perceived LLMs as improving research efficiency and facilitating cross-cultural academic communication, while also expressing concerns about clinical reasoning, data privacy, academic integrity, and nursing’s humanistic values. Nursing educator should develop updated ethical guidelines for human-AI collaboration and integrate AI literacy into curricula. Not applicable.
