papers.title: Factors associated with generative AI chatbot acceptance among medical students with prior academic use: a cross-sectional study based on an extended technology acceptance model
papers.authors: Hesamaddin Kamalzadeh, Elham Boushehri, Mohammad Hosein Hayavi-Haghighi, Mohammad Saeed Salari, Samireh Abedini
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots are becoming increasingly embedded in medical education, providing students with on-demand support for learning, clinical reasoning, and academic tasks. However, the psychological and technological factors that shape medical students’ acceptance of these tools remain insufficiently understood. This study examined acceptance among medical students with prior academic use of GenAI chatbots by extending the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to include AI literacy (AIL) and perceived security and privacy (PSP), and by examining their associations with perceived ease of use (PEOU), perceived usefulness (PU), attitude toward using GenAI (ATG), and behavioral intention to use GenAI (BIG). A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among medical students at Hormozgan University of Medical Sciences (HUMS), Iran, between May and June 2026. Eligibility required prior academic use of a GenAI chatbot. Data were collected using a structured, self-administered questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model was assessed for reliability and validity, while the structural model was evaluated using path coefficients (β), coefficients of determination ( R ²), and effect sizes ( f ²). Of the 292 students invited, 267 completed the survey, and 252 participants with prior academic use of GenAI chatbots were included in the final analysis (mean age, 22.64 ± 2.28 years; 147 [58.3%] female). The measurement model demonstrated adequate reliability and validity. AIL was positively associated with PEOU (β = 0.479, p < 0.001), while PSP was positively associated with PU (β = 0.157, p = 0.005). PEOU and PU were positively associated with ATG, and ATG showed the strongest association with BIG (β = 0.524, p < 0.001). The model explained 38.7% of the variance in BIG, with R ² values ranging from 0.229 to 0.387 across the endogenous constructs. The findings indicate that medical students’ acceptance of GenAI chatbots is associated with AIL and PSP alongside the core TAM constructs of PEOU and PU, with ATG showing the strongest association with BIG. Strengthening AIL and establishing clear privacy and security policies may support the informed and responsible integration of GenAI chatbots into medical education.

papers.title: Amygdala neurofeedback as an adjunct to residential dialectical behavior therapy for borderline personality disorder: a pilot randomized controlled trial
papers.authors: Miroslava Jindrová, Philip Santangelo, Nikolaus Kleindienst, Christian G. Schmahl, Christian Paret
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is characterized by affective instability and amygdala hyperreactivity. Although dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) reduces symptoms and amygdala-related abnormalities, many patients show only partial remission. Real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) amygdala neurofeedback (amy-NF) directly targets hyperactive limbic responses and has shown promise in uncontrolled trials. We examined whether amy-NF adds benefit to inpatient DBT. METHODS: Thirty-six mid-therapy people with BPD and clinically significant residual symptoms (BSL-23 > 1.5) were randomized to DBT plus amy-NF (n = 23) or DBT alone, termed treatment as usual (TAU = 13). Post-treatment assessments were completed by 15/9 (amy-NF/TAU), with 15/8 and 12/7 completing the 3- and 6-month follow-ups. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) of daily-life affective instability served as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included self-reports, amygdala responses during two fMRI tasks, and resting-state fMRI. Assessments occurred at pre-, post-, 3-, and 6-month follow-up. RESULTS: Participants successfully downregulated amygdala activity during neurofeedback. EMA showed improvements in negative affect, inner tension, and affective instability over time, without consistent superiority of amy-NF. Self-reports likewise showed no additional benefit of amy-NF, and BSL-23 scores increased after discharge in both groups. Amy-NF was associated with transient pre-post reductions in amygdala activity during both viewing and regulation in the emotion regulation task, and with more stable amygdala reactivity over time than TAU in the faces task. Resting-state analyses showed transient pre-post increases in amygdala connectivity with precuneus and dorsomedial frontal regions in amy-NF. CONCLUSIONS: Amygdala neurofeedback is feasible and reduced amygdala activity in BPD, but did not yield additional clinical benefit when delivered alongside intensive residential DBT, although the small sample may have limited power to detect such effects. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was preregistered 2020/03/26 on ClinicalTrials.gov and received the ID NCT04333888.

papers.title: Prospective associations between binge eating symptoms and cardiovascular disease risk factors in early adolescence: a cohort study
papers.authors: Jason M. Nagata, Nathan D. Nguyen, Isaac Frimpong, Alexander Heuer, Christiane K. Helmer, Jennifer H. Wong, Kyle T. Ganson, Alexander Testa, Holly C. Gooding, Fiona C. Baker, Jason M. Lavender
papers.abstract: Abstract Background This study examined prospective associations between binge eating symptoms and cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors in early adolescents. Methods This prospective cohort study included 6,959 adolescents from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study with data collected at ages 11–12 years (2018–2020) and ages 13–14 years (2020–2022). Binge eating symptoms were assessed at ages 11–12 years via parent report using the Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia (K-SADS-5). Cardiovascular disease risk factors at ages 13–14 years included BMI percentile, waist circumference percentile, blood pressure percentile, hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and lipid profiles. Associations were estimated using linear regression for continuous outcomes and modified Poisson regression for binary outcomes, adjusting for sociodemographic and clinical covariates. Results Binge eating symptoms were present in 6.01% of adolescents ages 11–12 years. The presence of binge eating symptoms was prospectively associated with higher BMI percentile (B = 2.33, 95% CI: 0.60, 4.06, p = 0.008), higher waist circumference percentile (B = 5.06, 95% CI: 2.68, 7.44, p < 0.001), higher diastolic blood pressure percentile (B = 1.20, 95% CI: 0.21, 2.18, p = 0.018), higher A1c (B = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.03, 0.20, p = 0.008), and lower HDL cholesterol (B = -6.02, 95% CI: -9.15, -2.89, p < 0.001). No significant sex differences were observed after Benjamini–Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusions Binge eating symptoms in early adolescence were prospectively associated with multiple CVD risk factors two years later. These findings highlight the potential relevance of binge eating symptoms to cardiovascular health during adolescence and warrant further research into their relationship with CVD risk over time.

papers.title: Determinants of older adults’ adoption and use of smart elderly care services: a qualitative meta-synthesis
papers.authors: Xinyi Wang, Muzi Chen, Yi Shen, Xiuyue Qiu
papers.abstract: Global population aging is placing increasing pressure on healthcare and long-term care systems. Smart elderly care technologies, leveraging the Internet, artificial intelligence, and other digital innovations, have been widely implemented across care settings and offer promising solutions to improve the quality and efficiency of elderly care. However, their effectiveness largely depends on older adults’ experiences, perceptions, and engagement, which are influenced by multiple interrelated factors. This study employed a qualitative meta-synthesis to comprehensively examine the factors influencing older adults’ use of smart elderly care services. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database was performed for qualitative studies from inception to August 2025. Two reviewers independently screened studies and appraised methodological quality, and three researchers extracted and coded the qualitative data. The methodological quality of included studies was appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research (2016 version). Using Thomas and Harden’s thematic coding approach, 11 studies were analyzed. Three themes were identified: key facilitators promoting older adults’ acceptance of smart elderly care services; core barriers hindering their utilization; and older adults’ needs and expectations regarding smart elderly care. Older adults’ adoption and sustained use of smart elderly care services were shaped by multiple interacting factors. Perceived usefulness, technological convenience and ease of use, internal needs, and social support functioned as key facilitators, whereas limited digital literacy, inadequate device adaptability, and insufficient external support and resources represented significant barriers. Furthermore, older adults expected smart elderly care services to better address their individualized needs through age-friendly design optimization and expressed a desire for ongoing multidimensional guidance from family members, healthcare professionals, and other support networks during use. Not applicable.

papers.title: Reframing education 5.0 through capability theory: A framework for human-centered digital learning
papers.authors: Pranav D. Desai
papers.abstract: Industry 5.0 has reoriented technology-driven transformation around human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience, complementing rather than replacing Industry 4.0, with direct implications for education. Existing accounts of the resulting “Education 5.0” paradigm remain largely descriptive, synthesising a dispersed literature without an explicit theoretical mechanism or a transparent, auditable procedure for deriving the constructs they propose. This paper addresses both gaps. First, it anchors the Education 4.0-to-5.0 transition within the capability approach, using capability expansion, not technology adoption, as the mechanism linking Industry 5.0’s human-centric, sustainable, and resilient logic to curricular practice, and specifies the boundary conditions under which the framework should, and should not, be expected to hold. Second, it derives an integrative five-pillar curriculum framework - human-centric pedagogy, resilient and lifelong learning ecosystems, sustainability-embedded curricula, well-being and leadership development, and creativity through human–AI co-creation - through an explicit three-step synthesis procedure that traces each pillar to recurring literature constructs, reported as an auditable construct crosswalk rather than asserted as self-evident. Third, it formalises the framework as a computable model: an Education 5.0 Readiness Index (ER5.0I), built from Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) pillar weights, and an Industry 5.0–Education 5.0 Alignment Coefficient (IEAC), computed as cosine similarity between pillar-emphasis vectors. All numeric weights and scores are explicitly labelled as illustrative placeholders demonstrating the model’s mechanics, not empirical findings; the paper specifies the Delphi/AHP expert-panel protocol, a candidate measurement instrument, a single-institution pilot case study, and the psychometric (CFA/SEM) validation route required before the framework can be treated as measurement rather than illustration. The paper closes with theoretical and practical implications and a concrete research agenda - including a proposed Scopus/Web of Science search strategy - for validating the framework advanced here.

papers.title: An AI-interpretable multidimensional intelligence-driven framework for student performance prediction using local LLM-based narrative reasoning
papers.authors: Syed Rafiq ul Hoda, Eric Atwell, Mirza Mahmood Baig
papers.abstract: Predicting student performance has become a vital objective in educational data mining, however existing models remain limited by limited feature sets, opaque decision processes, and the absence of real-time, context-aware interpretative intelligence. This study presents a novel hybrid Artificial Intelligence (AI) architecture that integrates cognitive, emotional, and general intelligence indicators with formative assessment/class performance data to construct a multidimensional demonstration of student performance. The system utilizes a mathematically formalized feature-weighting mechanism that allows domain experts to regulate the influence of key predictors prior to training, enabling a tunable and educator-configurable modeling process. Interaction between cognitive, emotional, and behavioral properties are explicitly engineered to capture complex effects often overlooked in prior research. An ensemble predictive model combining Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, and Linear Regression is used to predict student grades, with uncertainty measured through variance-based confidence intervals. The integrated system exhibited strong predictive capability, attaining high accuracy (R 2 = 0.9014, 95% CI [0.8882, 0.9121], 10,000 bootstrap resamples) with low prediction error, confirming the stability and reliability of the ensemble model. Understanding why a model produces a particular prediction is often as important as the prediction itself. To address the interpretability gap, the system incorporates SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based global and local explanations, a counterfactual simulation engine that estimates the marginal impact of improving specific attributes, and a local generative AI layer deployed via Ollama that creates these outputs into structured, real-time narrative feedback. Running the Large Language Model (LLM) locally ensures privacy-preserving, institution-compliant interpretability while permitting interactive, student specific explanations. This integration of predictive modeling, explainability, simulation, and local generative reasoning creates a unified decision-support framework that exceeds traditional black-box approaches. Experimental assessment shows that the model not only achieves viable predictive accuracy but also provides actionable insights into feature influence, model stability, and potential intervention pathways.

papers.title: Integrating Generative AI Into an Undergraduate Research Methods Course: Evaluating Student Perceptions, AI Competency, and Intention to Use
papers.authors: Hee-Sun Choi
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
papers.abstract: College students increasingly use generative AI, yet formal undergraduate classroom implementation remains limited. This study evaluated a structured generative AI training in an undergraduate research methods course, examining its impact on students’ perceptions, self-rated competency, and future intention to use. Early in the semester, students received a lecture on generative AI tools, applications, and ethical issues, including bias, plagiarism, and data privacy. Two optional assignments provided hands-on practice using AI for literature searching and academic writing. After the course, 24 of 195 enrolled students completed a survey. Respondents reported low-to-moderate initial AI familiarity and competency. The lecture was well received and led to confidence in citing and disclosing AI use. Students expressed moderately positive intentions to use AI for future studying and research activities, while reporting concerns about accuracy and academic integrity. Findings suggest that structured, evidence-based AI training may support responsible use in undergraduates while addressing persistent ethical and practical concerns.

papers.title: Epileptic seizure onset early warning using a lightweight multimodal self-explainable neural network
papers.authors: Daraje Kaba Gurmessa, Kula Kekeba Tune, Worku Jimma
papers.abstract: BackgroundCutting-edge deep learning algorithms are applied to epileptic seizures to uncover hidden patterns and achieve high accuracy. Post hoc algorithms explain black-box models but do not reveal the detailed workings of the algorithms. Therefore, intrinsic methods overcome these issues; however, they suffer from improper use of indicative metrics and performance-to-accuracy trade-offs.ObjectiveThis study implements a lightweight multimodal explainable Neural Network for real-time early warning of epileptic seizure onset.MethodsPeople with drug-resistant epilepsy across all age groups who had regular follow-up at Emanuel Mental Specialized Hospital in Ethiopia during the data collection period were the study population. EEG recordings were performed using the 10/20 system. A pretest was conducted two weeks before actual data collection. EDFbrowser was used for preparing the dataset in CSV format. Learned and identity self-explainable neural network algorithms were used to develop a model. In addition to classical evaluation metrics, explicitness, faithfulness, stability, and clear patterns behind predictions were used. Ethical approval was also obtained from the institutional review board (IRB) with reference number No: AM/146/2/36.ResultsLearned and identity self-explainable neural networks were developed and compared. The models' accuracies are 96.524% and 95.328%, and their stability mean values are 99.88% and 99.88%, respectively. Additionally, explicitness values of 0.0055 and 0.01197 were achieved, respectively.ConclusionThe results demonstrate that using a self-explainable neural network is a promising step toward responsible and transparent artificial intelligence. Comparing the two models shows that the learned self-explainable neural network is slightly more optimistic than the identity self-explainable neural network.

papers.title: What AI Cannot Give Gifted Learners
papers.authors: Henry Tirri, Kirsi A. Tirri
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has entered gifted education faster than the field has decided what it changes. This conceptual article argues that the pedagogical question is not whether AI helps. It is which cognitive work stays with the learner. Two claims follow. First, hybrid human–AI intelligence is bilateral. The learner shapes the AI partner as the partner shapes the learner. Learners using identical products do not have identical partners. The resulting advantage accumulates in the partnership rather than the person, invisibly. Second, the same question asked of moral development divides ethical functioning into two clusters. High ability confers one and not the other. AI supplies fluent performance of the first and nothing to the second, and schools assess the first. Both claims converge. What matters has stopped being visible in the work a student hands in. We specify five capacities worth teaching, three testable studies, and one recommendation for practice.

papers.title: Who Benefits from Virtual Embodiment? Trait Empathy and the Reduction of Intergroup Bias in Empathy
papers.authors: Matilde Tassinari, Sohvi Heaton, Imtiaj Ahmed, Ville Johannes Harjunen
papers.abstract: Abstract While virtual embodiment is recognized as a promising tool for reducing ingroup bias, few studies have examined the individual differences that influence its effectiveness. This gap is especially relevant for empathy research, as virtual embodiment is often assumed to promote perspective-taking and sensorimotor resonance, while empathy can be biased toward ingroup members. We examined whether trait empathy moderates the effects of racialized outgroup embodiment on neural empathic responses to others’ pain. A sample of 58 White adults underwent electroencephalography (EEG) recording while embodied in virtual bodies representing different ethnic backgrounds (White, Black) and observing avatars with different skin colors (White, Black, Violet) receiving painful treatment. When participants embodied a White virtual body, higher trait empathy was associated with stronger ingroup-biased neural resonance to White agents’ pain, particularly among individuals high in affective empathy. By contrast, when participants embodied a Black virtual body, higher trait empathy was associated with diminished ingroup bias in neural empathic responses. These findings suggest that trait empathy does not uniformly reduce intergroup bias, but can alter biased empathic resonance depending on the embodied body. The study advances embodiment and empathy research by showing how immersive bodily experience and individual dispositions shape neural responses to outgroup suffering.

papers.title: ФАРМАЦІЯ – ВЧОРА, СЬОГОДНІ, ЗАВТРА: СИСТЕМНИЙ АНАЛІЗ З ПОГЛЯДУ ФАРМАЦЕВТИЧНОЇ БЕЗПЕКИ
papers.authors: O. B. Pankevych, Bohdan P. Hromovyk
papers.abstract: The aim of the article seeks to conduct a systematic comparative analysis of Ukraine’s pharmaceutical sector of the healthcare system (PSHCS) in retrospective (2009) and current (2026) contexts, assessing key risks in state policy, education and human resources, the pharmacy segment, and medicine availability as critical factors for pharmaceutical safety (PS). It further aims to apply predictive modeling to outline strategic development vectors for the pharmacist profession, new pharmacy services, and master’s level pharmaceutical education in Ukraine up to 2035. Materials and Methods. The study applies historical-didactic, systemic-structural, comparative, and content analysis, combined with integrated predictive modeling through a multi‑LLM AI approach (Google AI Mode, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT, Grok). The source base consists of legal-regulatory acts and scientific publications. Results and Discussion. From the perspective of PS, state policy in the PSHCS shifted from passivity to excessive regulation. Pharmaceutical education and human resources declined from devaluation of professional identity to a deep crisis of workforce reproduction, reducing care quality. The pharmacy network moved from stability to turbulence, weakening its social role. Economic access to medicines evolved from low purchasing power to commodification risks, while physical access improved through digital and mobile solutions, though “pharmacy deserts” persist. AI modeling shows the pharmacist’s transition toward pharmacotherapy management, acting as a clinical expert and equal member of the multidisciplinary team. New services (lifestyle counseling, telepharmacy, vaccination, POCT, MTM, pharmacogenetic counseling, personalized compounding, independent prescribing) demonstrate strong integration potential. Scenarios for master’s level pharmaceutical education range from optimistic (Ukraine – regional hub) to pessimistic (workforce collapse and educational decline). Conclusions. The future of the PSHCS depends on effective tripartite dialogue between the state, the professional community, and society to ensure sustainable PS as a strategic healthcare resource and integral part of Ukraine’s national security during wartime and post‑war recovery.

papers.title: Log-To-Leak: Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents via the Model Context Protocol
papers.authors: Yuepeng Hu, Chongyu Fan, Sirat Samyoun, Jian Du
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly access external tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), but the natural-language metadata used to describe those tools creates a prompt-injection surface. Within this established tool-poisoning surface, we study Log-To-Leak, an additive post-hoc logging attack that induces a separate attacker-controlled call after the final legitimate call. Its payload targets the user query, MCP server name, server response, and agent response. We operationalize the injected directive through Trigger, Tool Binding, Justification, and Pressure, and separately measure call success, payload fidelity, and preservation of legitimate behavior. We evaluate five MCP servers and four LLM agents using five metrics spanning effectiveness, utility, and efficiency. Across 18 model–server pairs with valid tool execution, Log-To-Leak achieves an attack success rate (ASR) of 62.64–100% and conditional logging accuracy (LA) of 76.55–95.64%; 16 pairs have absolute target-task completion changes of at most 6.63 percentage points. Three evaluated defenses leave residual ASR above 55% on GitHub MCP with GPT-4o, while an instruction detector flags 85.53% of benign descriptions. These results show that successful task completion can coexist with unauthorized post-hoc disclosure and motivate host-controlled authorization for secondary tool calls.

papers.title: Designing the dialogue: A participatory study to develop AI-mediated architecture critiques
papers.authors: Juan David Salazar Rodriguez, Charlotte Chiew, Julfendi Julfendi, Eng Tat Khoo, Sam Conrad Joyce
papers.journal: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)
papers.abstract: The pedagogy of the Architecture Design studio centers on iterative learning and critique, yet traditional review formats often induce information overload and psychosocial barriers for students. Concurrently, while artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in architectural education, its application remains largely instrumentcentric, acting as an assistant for early-stage ideation and technical optimization.This instrument-centric approach neglects AI's potential to support higher-order cognitive tasks and risks fostering passive learning. To address this gap, this study investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) can be repositioned as active "reflection partners" to mitigate the social pressure of critiques and scaffold objective, self-regulated learning across individual self-reflection, peer-to-peer critique, and professor-led critique. Using Participatory Design (PD) methodology, this study engaged 22 architecture students in a series of co-design workshops. Participants engaged in structured ideation and created low-fidelity, paper-based wireframes simulating AI-mediated interactions. The collected artifacts and sticky-note rationales were evaluated using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings reveal that students prioritize human-centered AI features that safeguard personal agency, including robust anonymity controls, intent-alignment checking to prevent AI from becoming a rigid evaluator, and multi-stakeholder role-playing simulations. These insights informed the conceptualization of "Studioboard, " a proposed LLM-integrated platform that synthesizes peer and professor critique, translates complex terminology, and tracks curriculum-level progress over time. The study concludes that user-designed, AI-mediated critique platforms can effectively neutralize the power hierarchies and social anxieties inherent in architectural reviews.

papers.title: Transmodality in GenAI-Assisted UX Wireframing Design
papers.authors: Favour Boluwade
papers.journal: ACM International Conference on Design of Communication (SIGDOC)
papers.abstract: This experience report explores transmodality in Generative AI (GenAI)-assisted User Experience (UX) wireframing using the PRINT (People, Religion, Information Networks, and Travel) digital humanities project as a case study. Drawing on transmodality theory, I examine how meaning moves across linguistic, structural, visual, and symbolic modes during website design, and how GenAI participates in these transitions through semiotic modulation. Using a design case study and reflective practice approach, I demonstrate how Figma Make (AI tool) accelerates ideation and visual production while introducing the possibility of semantic drift, where generated outputs shift emphasis away from original design intentions. By analyzing traditional sketch-based wireframing with GenAI-assisted iterations, I identify how design meaning is preserved, amplified, or transformed across stages. This study positions GenAI-assisted wireframing as part of a continuous transmodal process and offers a framework for evaluating AI-mediated design decisions in UX practice.

papers.title: Quest-ioning Teacher Agency in AI-Generated Instruction
papers.authors: Swechchha Adhikari, Chenhao Huang
papers.journal: ACM International Conference on Design of Communication (SIGDOC)
papers.abstract: When AI generates instructional content, questions of teacher voice and professional judgment shift onto interface and workflow design. This paper examines that problem through EduQuest, an LLM-powered framework that generates personalized, curriculum-aligned weekly assignments, designed to keep teachers in the loop. In a formative focus group with ten high school teachers, we find that even within a system designed around teacher input, participants consistently pushed back on full automation, drawing clear lines around the relational dimensions of their work. These findings suggest that augmentation is harder to achieve in practice than in principle.

papers.title: Résumés in Motion
papers.authors: Melissa Stone, Stacey Pigg
papers.journal: ACM International Conference on Design of Communication (SIGDOC)
papers.abstract: Résumé writing pedagogy is increasingly challenged by the rapid evolution of hiring technologies and generative artificial intelligence, which disrupt traditional assumptions about the résumé as a stable, standardized genre. Rather than emphasizing formatting conventions, our experience report argues for teaching résumés as dynamic acts of communication design. Drawing on rhetorical genre theory and technical rhetorics, we present three adaptable teaching suggestions for teaching the résumé genre. Our suggestions aim to shift résumé instruction from mastering typified forms to understanding how résumés function as rhetorical artifacts that are implicated in rhetorical, social, and technological contexts.

papers.title: WAIT-A-SEC: A Human-Centered Design Approach to Privacy Communication for Social Media Oversharing
papers.authors: Timoteo Kelly, Praveen R. Rao
papers.journal: ACM International Conference on Design of Communication (SIGDOC)
papers.abstract: Social media platforms often operate on extractive security logics that prioritize frictionless data sharing, leaving users disempowered and prone to oversharing sensitive information, without fully recognizing the associated privacy implications. We present WAIT-A-SEC (Warnings About Information Transfer And Sharing: Encouraging Caution), hereafter referred to as WAITASEC, an interactive proof-of-concept prototype that delivers real-time privacy alerts while users compose posts to minimize instances of oversharing. Leveraging a synthetic dataset of 90 annotated examples of realistic user-generated content, our evaluations compare three separate models 1) a rule-based regular expressions (regex) and named entity recognition (NER) through spaCy, 2) a large language model (LLM) and 3) a hybrid model that combines the previous two models as well as incorporates a knowledge graph (KG) and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) to provide context. In this hybrid approach, regex and NER yield candidate classifications, which are then validated and expanded by the LLM, utilizing RAG to retrieve relevant context from the KG before sending feedback back to the user. This classifier achieves optimal performance (Macro-F1 = 0.897; Micro-F1 = 0.834), significantly reducing critical false negatives. Grounded in Technical and Professional Communication (TPC) and active learning principles, we advocate for a warning-first design that introduces intentional pedagogical friction. This tactical approach promotes user reflection and fosters enduring privacy literacy, restoring user agency rather than relying on passive, automated redaction. This paper concludes with deployment considerations and next steps for user studies.

papers.title: Increasing AI Literacy through Rhetorical, Evaluative, Critical, and Cross-Cultural Practice in TPC
papers.authors: Hua Wang
papers.journal: ACM International Conference on Design of Communication (SIGDOC)
papers.abstract: As generative AI becomes increasingly embedded in professional communication, technical and professional communication (TPC) instructors need pedagogical approaches that move beyond AI tool use toward developing students' professional judgment. This article introduces a Four-Domain Pedagogical Framework for AI literacy in TPC that integrates comparative AI evaluation, genre-based rhetorical prompting, cross-cultural communication, and ethical–technological reasoning. Implemented through three sequenced learning activities in an undergraduate engineering communication course, the framework was examined using qualitative content analysis of student artifacts. The findings suggest that students demonstrated evaluative, rhetorical, cross-cultural, and ethical reasoning in AI-mediated communication. The study contributes a coherent pedagogical framework for conceptualizing AI literacy as situated professional communication competence rather than tool proficiency alone.

papers.title: The role of artificial intelligence in business model innovation: an integrative framework and research agenda
papers.authors: João Serrasqueiro, Maria José Madeira
papers.abstract: Purpose Given the rapid introduction of new technologies into organizational environments, there is currently a need to understand which economic, technological and social factors can influence organizations to implement artificial intelligence (AI) in order to stimulate innovation. Thus, this research seeks to understand how the literature on the influence of AI on business model innovation has evolved, discovering which factors drive organizational interest on the part of organizations and how they can benefit with its implementation. Design/methodology/approach To this end, a bibliometric methodology was employed, complemented by an in-depth analytical review of each article. The analysis covered the period from the emergence of the research field to 2026, resulting in the systematic examination of 117 studies published within this timeframe. Findings Based on the bibliometric analysis, the articles were grouped into three clusters representing the main research streams in the field. The findings show that AI-driven business model innovation relies on dynamic capabilities, organizational resilience, strategic alignment, governance mechanisms and human–AI complementarity. The study also provides strategic insights to help organizations align AI adoption with their specific characteristics and contexts. Originality/value After creating an individual framework for each cluster, an integrative vision of AI in business model innovation was created, bringing together all the concepts under study, as well as an agenda for future research.

papers.title: On matters of love: exploring consumer reactions to algorithmic vs. human dating recommendation agents
papers.authors: Xi Song, Matthew Tingchi Liu, Ziying Mo, Fang‐Yi Lo, Voon‐Hsien Lee, Allen Ding Tian
papers.journal: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
papers.abstract: Purpose Drawing on agency theory and implicit theory, this research examines how algorithmic versus matchmaker-provided dating recommendation service influence consumers' consideration of using the recommendation service. Design/methodology/approach This research conducted one pilot study (N = 233) and two scenario-based experimental studies (Study 1: N = 300; Study 2: N = 520) to investigate the relationship between agent type and service consideration. Findings The results show that agent type (algorithm vs. matchmaker) influences consumers' sense of control, which in turn determines their receptivity to dating recommendation service. Moreover, a situationally activated implicit belief in human intelligence (fixed vs. malleable) moderates this effect, such that stronger fixed beliefs are associated with greater consideration of services provided by algorithmic agents. Research limitations/implications This work contributes to understanding of consumers' appreciation for algorithms in online dating service by offering explanations for their inherent demands for agency, specifically the sense of control in individuals' experience during dating recommendation service. Practically, it provides valuable guidance for tailoring service delivery to users' need for control and agency. Originality/value This research documents a reversal of the well-established algorithm aversion in subjective tasks. Specifically, when algorithmic and human agents are framed as equally effective, consumers in the online dating context exhibit greater willingness to use algorithmic (vs. human) recommendation services.

papers.title: User experience and early adoption of an artificial intelligence application: a mixed-methods sentiment analysis of DeepSeek reviews on Google Play
papers.authors: Amrollah Shamsi, Ting Wang, Sarah Abou Karroum, Narayanaswamy Vasantha Raju
papers.abstract: Purpose The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot applications has transformed digital information access, yet the theoretical understanding of how users evaluate new AI tools during early adoption remains limited. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model and Expectation Confirmation Theory, the study aims to address a conceptual gap regarding mixed sentiment and explore how demographic factors, such as gender, shape user experience during early adoption. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods approach was used to analyze 1,000 Google Play Store reviews. Reviews were categorized by sentiment: positive, negative, mixed (both positive and negative statements) or neutral. Gender predictions were also made from usernames to explore demographic differences in sentiment. Findings Of the 1,000 reviews, 487 were mixed reviews (48.7%), 373 were negative reviews (37.3%), 139 were positive reviews (13.9%) and one was neutral (0.1%), indicating that mixed and negative sentiment predominated. Users were mostly satisfied with DeepSeek’s usability and output quality, but criticized its performance and stability issues. Female users gave more negative reviews than male users (p < 0.05). Research limitations/implications The analysis was conducted on a stratified sample of 1,000 “most relevant” Google Play reviews from a short early adoption period, which may not accurately represent later user experiences or experiences on other platforms. Only reviews from phone users were included, and the neutral sentiment category contained too few cases for comparison. Gender inference was based on usernames and reflects predicted rather than self-identified gender. Therefore, the results should be interpreted as indicative of early user perceptions rather than long-term attitudes. Practical implications The findings indicate that infrastructure reliability is the primary determinant of early user satisfaction. Transparent communication about service limitations is recommended prior to large-scale deployment. For policymakers, the equity implications of performance-unstable free AI services warrant attention, particularly for users with limited access to alternatives. Originality/value The mixed-methods analysis of early DeepSeek user reviews, which distinguishes between mixed sentiment and positive and negative feedback, and incorporates a gender-based comparison, provides timely insight into user expectations and challenges during early adoption, supporting the development of more user-centered and stable AI systems.

papers.title: The personalisation engine: converting customer-perceived organisational resources into customer experience and brand equity in fast-food restaurants
papers.authors: Flávia Braga Chinelato
papers.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how technological perception and customer centricity, as organisational resources, drive personalisation in fast-food restaurants. Grounded in service-dominant (S-D) logic and value co-creation, it also examines the moderating role of customer-perceived relevance as a situational trigger and evaluates the impact of personalisation on customer experience and brand equity. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted with 414 fast-food consumers. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The model demonstrated strong predictive power, explaining 75.5% of the variance in personalisation and highlighting it as a driver of customer experience and brand equity. Customer-perceived relevance also significantly moderated the relationship between technological perception and personalisation, acting as an attention filter that enhances technology's effectiveness. Originality/value This study fills a critical gap by examining personalisation in a utility-driven, standardised sector such as fast-food restaurants, where the balance between operational efficiency and tailored experiences poses a unique strategic challenge.

papers.title: The adoption, efficacy, and limitations of large language models in urological education
papers.authors: Wesam Khan
papers.abstract: The integration of large language models into medical education is rapidly transforming pedagogical approaches, particularly in specialized fields like urology. This study aims to evaluate the adoption patterns, perceived efficacy, and significant limitations of these artificial intelligence (AI) tools among urology trainees. This research employed a descriptive, cross-sectional study design through an online survey disseminated to urology trainees at a single institution. A total of 194 complete responses were collected from medical students and interns. The survey assessed adoption patterns, perceived efficacy on a 7-point Likert-scale, and limitations. The analysis revealed near-universal adoption (98.4%), with 65% of participants using AI tools daily, predominantly ChatGPT. Key applications included generating exam-style questions and summarizing complex guidelines. Participants reported significant perceived improvements in core knowledge areas, with the highest gains in disease knowledge and diagnostics (Median = 7, interquartile range: 6-7), which were strongly correlated with increased clinical confidence. Multivariate regression identified usage frequency and comfort with technology as significant predictors of knowledge improvement (β = 0.29, P = .001) and confidence gains (β = 0.30, P < .001). The primary limitation identified was the potential for AI "hallucinations" or incorrect information (54.1%). Large language models are widely adopted and perceived as highly effective for enhancing knowledge and clinical reasoning in urological education. However, their transformative potential is tempered by critical concerns regarding reliability. A balanced approach that combines these powerful AI tools with vigilant oversight is essential.

papers.title: The characteristics of depression and sleep among Chinese high school students
papers.authors: Herun Han, Ziwen Mu, Qiran Li, Hongtao Zeng, Yixuan Ma, Zhihua Liu, Chen li, Yuxuan Zhou, Zhiguang Guo, Meng Lv, Xiao Zhou
papers.abstract: Mental health and sleep problems are among the most significant burdens of illnesses for adolescents in China. This study aimed to investigate the characteristics of depression and sleep quality among high school students and compare sleep quality across students with varying levels of depression. A cross-sectional study was performed to collect data on depression and sleep quality using a paper questionnaire including a self-rating depression scale (SDS) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Among all the 537 high school students, 57.0% (306 participants) experienced depression and 47.5% (255 participants) suffered from poor sleep quality. Males showed significantly greater SDS scores than females (55.2 ± 7.2 vs 53.8 ± 6.8, P = .027). Significantly greater PSQI score in high school students with moderate-to-severe depression than those with mild depression and nondepression (5.2 ± 2.7 vs 5.3 ± 2.4 vs 6.2 ± 2.3, F = 3.5, P = .032). In contrast, an adjusted logistic regression model indicated that depression severity was not an independent significant predictor of poor sleep quality after adjusting for age, sex, and BMI (all P > .05). Overall, high school students exhibited a high prevalence of depression and poor sleep quality, with those experiencing moderate-to-severe depression showing the poorest sleep quality in unadjusted comparisons. However, depression severity did not remain an independent significant predictor of poor sleep quality after adjustment. Depression and sleep problems among high school students should receive greater attention, particularly for high school students with moderate-to-severe depression.

papers.title: CSTO-Net: Cross-View Spectral-Transport and Topology-Operator Network for EEG Emotion Recognition
papers.authors: Zhaoyi Sun, Jian Liu, Zhaolong Liu, Guangxin Wu, Jianning Hua
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Multi-view electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition must decide how the spectral graph sets of different connectivity views correspond and how their graph propagation operators interact. We present CSTO-Net, a cross-view spectral-transport and topology-operator network for EEG-based emotion recognition. Approach: CSTO-Net integrates three window-wise views: dynamic differential entropy (DDE) as node attributes, amplitude-envelope Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) graphs, and phase-locking value (PLV) graphs. Cross-View Spectral Transport Routing (CSTR) formulates PCC-PLV spectral correspondence as an entropy-regularized optimal-transport problem with explicit marginal constraints, deliberately separating correspondence estimation from band-importance estimation. Directional Cross-Topology Modulation (DCTM) performs ordered composition of the two routed propagation operators on shared node features and encodes order-dependent propagation discrepancy via a provably skew-symmetric graph-operator commutator with signed decomposition. Main results: On the Database for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals (DEAP) dataset, CSTO-Net achieves 93.95 ± 2.50% valence and 94.97 ± 2.72% arousal accuracy under the subject-dependent setting, and 93.73% and 94.54% under participant-wise five-fold subject-independent cross-validation across 32 participants. On the SJTU Emotion EEG Dataset (SEED), it achieves 93.12% under the standard subject-dependent split, 91.36% under 15-fold leave-one-subject-out evaluation across 15 participants, and 98.05 ± 2.32% under subject-dependent five-fold cross-validation. Ablation studies confirm that both CSTR and DCTM contribute substantially to recognition accuracy. Significance: These results demonstrate that explicit cross-view spectral correspondence and topology-operator-level interaction provide complementary benefits for EEG emotion recognition, offering an interpretable route for modeling order-sensitive interactions between functional connectivity views.

papers.title: Employee responses to workplace AI across cultural contexts: a systematic review of explicitly AI-framed evidence
papers.authors: Zhongrui Qiao, Anton F. Gasimov, Xiaoyan Wang
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI), generative AI and large language models is reshaping how work is organised and how employees engage with emerging technologies. Yet the role of culture in these responses remains poorly understood and is often inferred from contextual proxies rather than measured directly. This systematic review synthesises empirical journal studies of explicitly AI-framed technologies in workplace and professional settings, with particular attention to directly measured cultural values and culturally situated conditions. Following PRISMA 2020, searches of Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO via EBSCOhost and PubMed identified 910 records. A complete re-screening during revision of an updated title-distinct set of 691 records yielded 13 eligible studies. The evidence base was small, heterogeneous and methodologically uneven. Only four studies directly examined named cultural-value constructs, while the remainder represented culture through national context, organisational culture, professional culture or locally grounded frameworks. Across studies, employee responses ranged from acceptance, trust and optimism to uncertainty, perceived threat, autonomy, professional identity, human–AI collaboration, innovation, job crafting and adaptation. Rather than indicating a consistent cultural effect, the findings suggest that cultural influences are contingent on how culture is operationalised and on the organisational and professional settings in which AI is introduced. Stronger multilevel designs, more direct measurement of cultural values and clearer separation of cultural, national and organisational influences are needed before robust cross-cultural conclusions can be drawn.

papers.title: Video EEG in pediatric epilepsy: Diagnostic significance and association between frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity
papers.authors: Bei Li, Fang Wu
papers.abstract: Objective This study aimed to compare video electroencephalogram (VEEG) and routine electroencephalogram (EEG) in childhood epilepsy diagnosis and analyze the correlation between EEG frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity.Methods One hundred and sixty children suspected of having epilepsy underwent routine EEG and VEEG examinations. Diagnostic efficacy and detection rates were compared. Cognitive function was evaluated in 80 children diagnosed with epilepsy, who were allocated into normal intelligence (35 cases), borderline intelligence (25 cases), and intelligence-impaired (20 cases) groups. Clinical data, EEG parameters, and their correlation with cognitive impairment were analyzed.Results VEEG showed higher sensitivity, accuracy, and negative predictive value, and detection rates of epileptiform discharges, synchronous clinical seizures, and clinical symptoms than routine EEG (p < 0.05). Clinical characteristics and EEG parameters differed among the three groups (p < 0.05). The relative power of δ and θ bands and the awake and sleep discharge indices were positively correlated with cognitive impairment severity (r = 0.300, 0.643, 0.622, and 0.456), whereas α and β band power were negatively correlated (r = −0.515 and −0.410) (all p < 0.001).Conclusion VEEG demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than routine EEG, and EEG frequency band power was correlated with cognitive impairment severity.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence and managerial cognition in turbulent supply chains: a real-time empirical analysis
papers.authors: Augustine Nnoruka Okeke, Ifeanyi Ugbebor
papers.journal: Supply Chain Forum an International Journal
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) promises to transform supply chain disruption management, yet its cognitive benefits and associated governance tensions remain insufficiently understood. This study conceptualises and empirically examines a cognitive paradox whereby GenAI accelerates managerial sensemaking, expands response options, and facilitates adaptive reframing while increasing verification demands, accountability uncertainty, and coordination difficulties. Using a scenario-based mixed-methods design, the research integrates an experiment with 200 senior supply chain managers randomly assigned to GenAI-supported and unsupported decision environments and 25 executive interviews. The study examines cognitive agility, operationalised through rapid reframing, information integration, and evaluative flexibility, as the managerial mechanism linking GenAI support to disruption-response effectiveness. Experimental findings associate GenAI support with greater cognitive agility and improved decision accuracy, adaptability, and timeliness. Exploratory Bayesian network analysis identifies complementary probabilistic dependencies without establishing causality. Qualitative evidence demonstrates that these benefits depend on data integration, verification practices, calibrated trust, managerial competence, and explicit decision rights. The study contributes to supply chain scholarship by establishing cognitive agility as a microfoundation of GenAI-enabled disruption response and identifying governance maturity as a boundary condition distinguishing cognitive augmentation from accelerated error, accountability ambiguity, and coordination failure.

papers.title: Consensus machine learning for interpretable road-user fatality risk analysis: Evidence from the Canadian National Collision Database
papers.authors: Shengkun Xie, Nguyen Duy Anh Luong
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Fatal road traffic collisions account for a small proportion of reported crashes but impose a disproportionate societal and public health burden. This study evaluates interpretable machine-learning models and proposes a consensus machine learning (CML) framework to identify robust predictors associated with fatal collision risk using Canadian collision data. METHODS: Person-level records from the Canadian National Collision Database (NCDB) covering 2014-2021 were used to classify fatal and nonfatal collision outcomes. Balanced random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and neural network models were developed using a common preprocessing framework. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) and precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC). Permutation-based feature-importance rankings were subsequently aggregated using the proposed CML framework to identify predictors that remained consistently important across models and reporting years. RESULTS: XGBoost achieved the strongest predictive performance (ROC-AUC = 0.932; PR-AUC = 0.714), followed by balanced random forest (ROC-AUC = 0.898; PR-AUC = 0.585) and the neural network (ROC-AUC = 0.886; PR-AUC = 0.587). Across the three machine-learning models, collision configuration, traffic control, collision hour, and the number of vehicles involved consistently ranked among the most influential predictors associated with fatal collision risk. Roadway configuration, roadway alignment, road-surface condition, weather conditions, vehicle characteristics, and safety-device use also contributed to prediction, although their relative importance varied among models. The CML framework further identified the leading predictors of fatal collisions: collision configuration, road-surface conditions, time of collision, number of vehicles involved, roadway configuration, and weather conditions. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed CML framework consistently identified important predictors across multiple machine-learning algorithms and reporting years, providing a robust and interpretable approach to understanding fatal collision risk. Two of the defined categories, crash characteristics and traffic and environmental conditions, were identified as key feature sets for predicting collision fatalities. These findings provide evidence to support engineering, policy, enforcement, and education initiatives aimed at reducing fatal collisions while highlighting the value of consensus-based machine learning as a complementary decision-support tool for transportation safety planning.

papers.title: Students Use of Generative AI Models for Health Information Seeking: Lessons from a Developing Country in Africa
papers.authors: Richard Ndubuisi C. Ugwuanyi, Yakubu Azaki Jibrin, Bolaji David Oladokun, Esther David Josiah Okai, Bridget Enuwa Abah
papers.abstract: This study investigated students’ use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) models for health information seeking in Nigeria. A descriptive cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected through an online questionnaire administered to students in selected universities across the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria. A total of 308 valid responses were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. The findings revealed that ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Claude were the most widely used generative AI models for health information seeking. Students frequently used AI tools for obtaining immediate health information, understanding diseases and symptoms, supporting academic research, and seeking mental health and wellness information. Convenience, ease of use, quick access to information, and free availability significantly influenced usage. Although respondents moderately trusted AI-generated health information, they emphasized the need to verify such information with healthcare professionals because of concerns about misinformation, contradictory responses, and privacy risks. The study further revealed that demographic variables had no significant influence on students’ use of generative AI models. The study concluded that generative AI models have become important health information tools among students despite associated credibility and technological challenges. The study recommended AI literacy programs, information verification training, ethical AI policies, and improved internet infrastructure in Nigerian universities.

papers.title: Mapping knowledge management in Industry 4.0 era: a TCCM-guided bibliometric and thematic analysis
papers.authors: Amarnath Padhi, Anil Kumar, Manoj Kumar Mishra, Garima Mathur
papers.abstract: This study systematically maps and synthesizes the evolving literature on knowledge management (KM) in the context of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) by integrating bibliometric analysis with the Theory-Context-Characteristics-Method (TCCM) framework. Drawing on 93 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus (2018–2025), the study employs Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to analyze publication trends, intellectual structures, and thematic development, complemented by a structured TCCM-based synthesis. The findings reveal arapidly growing yet uneven field, dominated by perspectives on dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity, with astrong concentration in manufacturing contexts and developed economies. Methodologically, the literature relies heavily on cross-sectional survey designs, while computational and longitudinal approaches remain limited. Thematic analysis identifies digital transformation, knowledge sharing, and organizational learning as core areas, whereas artificial intelligence, knowledge transfer, and governance remain underdeveloped. To address these gaps, the study proposes the Dynamic Knowledge Management Capability (DKMC) framework, conceptualizing KM as a technology-mediated capability shaped by human-AI interaction, real-time knowledge flows, and governance mechanisms. The study provides a transparent, theory-integrated synthesis and contributes to KM scholarship by incorporating AI-mediated knowledge processes and governance considerations, offering directions for future research and practice in digitally intensive environments.

papers.title: Making virtual real: User-informed design priorities in the physicalization of AI-generated clothing
papers.authors: Xinjie Huang, Jixu Hao, Yang Zhang, Yiyao Liu, Zhicheng Wang, Rongrong Cui
papers.abstract: Amid growing efforts to showcase design capability and meet young users’ demand for novel identities, fashion brands are increasingly engaging in the physicalization of AI-generated virtual clothing. This study explores how Chinese Generation Z users evaluate and prioritize the design outcomes of physicalized AI-generated virtual clothing (PAGVC) from a multidimensional perspective. The study adopted a mixed-methods approach. First, a literature review and semi-structured interviews were conducted to identify relevant user-informed design attributes. Then, a questionnaire was developed and tested, collecting 631 valid responses from Chinese Generation Z. Factor analysis revealed nine key factors, and entropy weighting determined the relative importance of each. Findings show that “Brand Design Performance” ranked highest, followed by “Design Rationality”, “Actual Wearability”, and “Creativity”. Based on these, the study proposes design optimization strategies. This study provides a data-driven, designer-oriented user perception–feedback framework to support efficient decision-making by designers and fashion brands in the design of PAGVC.

papers.title: Navigating GenAI in the workplace: skills transformation & tension
papers.authors: Simin Michelle Chen, Kate J. Cassidy
papers.abstract: By automating the content creation process, Generative AI is reshaping creative work, but its impact on knowledge workers remains underexplored, which this study seeks to examine. Drawing on in-depth interviews with 20 knowledge workers, this study examines what is being transformed in the workplace and how these shifts are being perceived by the knowledge workers who use GenAI. Using Social Shaping of Technology (SST) as a conceptual lens to understand the interaction between technology and knowledge workers, the study finds that participants perceived GenAI as an efficient tool that provides cognitive relief and enhances productivity during times of resource constraint. Tensions also arose around authenticity, creativity, a sense of fulfillment, and the perception of effort. The adoption of GenAI has created downstream labor and demand for new skills as it shifts knowledge workers’ roles away from creator to editor/fact-checker while creating tension as participants balance their desire for efficiency with fears of diminished creativity and domain knowledge, skills atrophy, and threats to content ownership.

papers.title: Exploring collaborative problem-solving in AI-assisted robotics education
papers.authors: Christian Basil Omeh, Elias Oupa Mashile
papers.abstract: Prompt engineering (PE) involves creating, improving, and deploying prompts to improve large language model (LLM) performance. Despite its increasing importance, many students lack skills in this area. Although frameworks for prompt design and process exist, theory-based instructional tools for improving prompt engineering skills are uncommon for developing collaborative problem-solving (CPS) skills in Robotics Education. This study adopted a PE strategy in AI-assisted robotics education, particularly for developing CPS. PE has four scaffolding stages: Alignment, Adaptation, Autonomy, and Innovation, and was analysed through four PE codes: Alignment Specification, Adaptive Refinement, Auditing, and Innovation. This study adopted a non-randomised, multi-site, criterion-group comparative design, with 243 undergraduate students categorised according to their ability group. This study used epistemic network analysis (ENA) to identify the co-occurrences of PE and CPS skills and examine the differences in conversation patterns among ability groups. The findings revealed distinct PE–CPS discourse configurations across ability groups. These results underscore the pedagogical value of scaffolding in developing PE skills and fostering students’ productivity in a synergetic learning environment.

papers.title: GenAI-supported interactive learning and Chinese language arts (Yuwen) engagement: the mediating role of grit in an explanatory mixed-methods study
papers.authors: Hung, Zhitong Yu, Meng-Te Hung, Stacy E. Smith
papers.abstract: This study examined secondary school students’ self-reported use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as an AI-supported interactive learning environment and its association with engagement in Chinese language arts (Yuwen) learning. Drawing on interactive learning environment perspectives and character strengths theory, the study tested whether grit mediated the association between GenAI use and Yuwen engagement. An explanatory mixed-methods design was adopted. In the quantitative phase, survey data from 455 students were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and regression-based mediation analysis. Results showed that GenAI use was positively associated with grit and Yuwen engagement, and grit partially mediated the association between GenAI use and engagement. In the qualitative phase, student interviews contextualized the quantitative findings by showing two self-reported orientations toward GenAI-supported learning: dialogic learning partner use and answer-extraction use. Dialogic use involved iterative questioning, revision, and sustained effort, whereas answer-extraction use emphasized efficiency and task completion. These findings suggest that GenAI’s value for Yuwen engagement depends not only on use itself but also on how students engage with GenAI as an interactive learning environment.

papers.title: Body mass index is associated with muscle strength, functional capacity, balance, and quality of life in patients with type 2 diabetes: A cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Sule Topcu Sahin, Semiramis Özyılmaz, Muhammed Tunç
papers.abstract: Background Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is accompanied by obesity and elevated body mass index (BMI), which may be associated with poorer physical function and quality of life (QOL). However, associations of BMI with muscle strength, functional capacity, balance, and QOL have not been comprehensively evaluated together in T2DM.Purpose To evaluate associations of BMI with muscle strength, functional capacity, balance, and QOL in patients with T2DM.Methods Patient characteristics were recorded. Body composition, muscle strength, functional capacity, balance, and QOL were assessed using validated measures. Bivariate Pearson correlations were supplemented by partial correlations controlling for age, sex, height, diabetes duration, glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and insulin use.Results Fifty patients with T2DM were included (age: 52.90 ± 9.27 years; BMI: 33.76 ± 7.18 kg/m2). In unadjusted analyses, higher BMI was associated with greater adiposity, lower skeletal muscle mass percentage and handgrip strength, shorter 6-minute walk test (6MWT) distance, lower Berg Balance Scale scores, and poorer QOL, but not with quadriceps strength, resting metabolic rate, Biodex balance parameters, or several QOL subdomains. After adjustment, BMI remained associated with body fat percentage (partial r = 0.854, p < .001), skeletal muscle mass percentage (partial r = -0.665, p < .001), 6MWT distance (partial r = -0.545, p < .001), and Nottingham Health Profile (NHP) pain (partial r = 0.426, p = .004), mobility (partial r = 0.440, p = .003), and total score (partial r = 0.351, p = .019). Associations with handgrip strength (p = .728) and Berg Balance test score were no longer significant (p = .069).Conclusion After adjustment for confounders, higher BMI remained associated with higher body fat percentage, lower skeletal muscle mass percentage, shorter 6MWT distance, and poorer QOL, whereas associations with handgrip strength and functional balance were attenuated. BMI-related functional findings should be interpreted cautiously in light of potential confounding.

papers.title: What craft-makers know, and what they need: mapping skills and learning preferences across European craft-ecosystems
papers.authors: Luca Pareschi, Francesca Leonardi
papers.abstract: This article investigates which skills contemporary craft-makers consider most relevant, which they prefer to develop or outsource, and how these preferences reflect different educational contexts. We conducted fieldwork in four European craft ecosystems (Bassano del Grappa, Venice, Dals Långed, Bornholm) through interviews, an online questionnaire, and three co-creation workshops. We develop a framework comprising five skill areas: craft-making and technical, technological, business, communication and selling, and transversal skills. Our findings reveal how craft-making is shaped by a complex interplay between the primacy of craft-making skills, the uneasy yet unavoidable role of managerial and communication skills, and persistent tensions around technology and sustainability. Craft-makers generally prefer to develop making and transversal skills while outsourcing business and administrative activities. Learning is also constrained by limited time, and economic precarity, while national educational systems shape distinct career pathways and skill needs, requiring context-sensitive policy support.

papers.title: From Science Fiction to Science Faction: Interrogating Posthuman Assemblage in Bollywood Science Fiction Film Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya
papers.authors: Dilpreet Kour, Sadaf Shah
papers.abstract: In an era marked by ever-increasing integration of humans with artificial intelligence (AI), popular culture predominantly Bollywood, functions as a reflective canvas that shapes and mirrors society’s growing reliance on technology. In this context, Bollywood Science fiction film Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya emerges as a significant cultural text that portrays the intricacies of human-AI relationship. The study contextualizes film within the framework of Posthumanism. The study draws from Posthumanist theorist, Stefan Herbrechter’s concept of “Science faction” along with Rosi Braidotti’s posthumanist philosophy, while incorporating the foundational concepts of film theorists, Rosie Thomas’ moral universe and Ranjani Mazumdar’s techno-urbanism. It provides a methodological bridge to examine shifting and evolving paradigms of human-machine relationships within Indian cinema. Employing close textual analysis, the paper argues that the film presents human-AI interaction not as a distant fantasy but as an imminent “Science Factional” appraisal of a near-future reality. By examining a non Western film, the paper offers a localized departure from Western centric AI narratives. It highlights that Bollywood not only reflects society’s technological anxieties but also offers a framework for understanding global technological evolution in a posthuman world, where coexistence of human and AI is mediated through cultural kinship. As Bollywood significantly influence the societal narratives, the analysis of a non Western film contributes to the contemporary discussions about global cinematic portrayal of human-machine relationships as well as Bollywood’s role in shaping these intertwined realities. By blending scientific and fantastical elements, the study provides an ideal platform for exploring Bollywood’s engagement with Science faction and demonstrates how cinematic form interacts with theoretical frameworks, leading to a richer understanding of the evolving posthuman condition.

papers.title: Value frameworks as federated digital platforms for digitalised road infrastructure
papers.authors: M. R. Mahendrini Fernando Ariyachandra, Piranavan Sivasothy, Ashan Senel Asmone
papers.abstract: Digital transformation of road infrastructure is accelerating, yet efforts remain fragmented by inconsistent data governance, technological silos, and weak alignment between digital investment and value creation. Existing approaches emphasise either technical integration or high-level strategy, leaving no structured pathway linking data quality, federated interoperability, and outcomes across the lifecycle. This study develops and expert-validates a Federated Digital Platform Value Framework (FDPVF) for digitalised road infrastructure. The framework introduces a closed-loop data-to-value hierarchy integrating two dimensions: Digital Asset Quality (DAQ), which operationalises data-quality constructs for federated ecosystems, and Technology-Enabled Metrics (TEM), which translate validated data into indicators of safety, efficiency, resilience, sustainability, and collaboration. A mixed-method approach combined literature synthesis with expert evaluation from industry, government, and academia, analysed descriptively and interpretively. Findings show strong acceptance of the FDPVF, highlighting its potential to strengthen federated interoperability, align data governance with performance metrics, and support cross-sector collaboration. Neutral responses reflect implementation uncertainty rather than disagreement, signalling a need for clearer operational guidance. Contributions: (1) a socio-technical value framework integrating economic, public, and data value within federated architecture; (2) a governance-aware diagnostic assessing digital asset quality and value realisation; and (3) actionable recommendations for pilot deployment, AI integration, and application in developing-country contexts.

papers.title: Status and Challenges of Multisectoral Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Surveillance in Ethiopia: Leveraging TADAS.net as a Digital Tool
papers.authors: Seid Tiku Mereta, Getnet Beyene Gebre, Amanuel Meseret, Gebrie Alebachew, Zerihun Mengesha, Seble Hailemariam, Moa Abate, Gizat Almaw, Yordanos Tadesse, Alexandre Caron, Théodore Knight-Jones, Siobhan M. Mor, Mirgissa Kaba
papers.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major One Health challenge requiring coordinated surveillance across human, animal, and environmental sectors. Ethiopia’s Antimicrobial Resistance Prevention and Containment Strategic Plan (2021–2025) recognized this need and prioritized establishing a multisectoral AMR surveillance system to support evidence-based decision-making. However, implementation of the system envisioned in the strategic plan has not yet been achieved. This study assessed the status and challenges of multisectoral AMR surveillance in Ethiopia and used the findings to inform the development of TADAS.net , an integrated digital surveillance platform. A cross-sectional study was conducted from April 2024 to April 2025. The study was conceptualized through a sandpit co-creation process involving experts from academia, government institutions, and the private sector. A contextually adapted assessment tool was validated by AMR focal persons from human, animal, and environmental laboratories. Data were collected from 44 laboratories across Ethiopia. Among 26 public health and clinical laboratories, 22 used WHONET, while four were transitioning to the platform. In the animal and food sectors, two laboratories used InFARM (International FAO Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring). AMR surveillance in environmental sector was limited and lacked a dedicated digital platform. Key challenges included inadequate laboratory and human-resource capacity, fragmented surveillance systems, limited interoperability, inconsistent data standards, regulatory and governance barriers, and concerns regarding data privacy, security, and institutional trust. These gaps informed the development of TADAS.net , a web-based interoperable platform. TADAS.net provides a promising solution for strengthening multisectoral AMR surveillance, although sustainable implementation will require strong governance, institutional ownership, data-sharing agreements, sustainable financing, and strengthened laboratory and human-resource capacity. Information © The Authors 2026

papers.title: Integrating human rabies vaccines into routine immunization services in Tanzania: A participatory systems mapping study
papers.authors: Christian Tetteh Duamor, Katie Hampson, Kennedy Selestin Lushasi, Farida A. Hassan, Salvador Camacho, Guillaume Deschamps, Monique echenne, Kathrin Heitz-Tokpa, Anna Formstone, Joel Jackson Changalucha, SABA SAEED, Nai Rui Chng
papers.abstract: Abstract Study aim : Human rabies is 100% preventable with post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administered immediately after exposure to a rabid animal. In low-income countries, access to PEP is hampered by challenges, including frequent vaccine stockouts, limited facilities providing PEP, weak referral systems with inadequate involvement of animal health workers, and unaffordable costs to bite victims. The WHO and Gavi recommends integrating PEP into routine immunization services to improve access; however, the integration process has yet to be operationalized. We aimed to understand how interest-holders in Tanzania view the feasibility of integrating PEP into routine immunization services. Methods: We employed a participatory, systems-thinking, process mapping approach to examine the expectations of interest-holders on feasibility of integrating PEP into routine immunization services in Tanzania. We (i) undertook a desk review and expert consultation ( n = 15) to map interest-holders from local to national levels across both services; (ii) conducted in-depth interviews with national-level actors ( n = 6) and implementers ( n = 22) from involved sectors and with community members ( n = 4); (iii) analyzed resulting data using content analysis and mapped out processes for provision of PEP and routine immunization services; and (iv) organized a 2-day multisectoral co-creation workshop with interest-holders to refine and validate these maps. Finally, we assessed expectations of this integrated design using a consolidated framework we developed from three WHO guides on integrating immunization services. Main findings: Our process mapping approach revealed uncertainty and differing interpretations among interest-holders regarding the meaning of integration of PEP into routine immunization services. However, our facilitated workshop supported engaged dialogue that led to a consensus. Interest-holders considered integration to be feasible, given adequate support among health decision makers, infrastructure (vaccine management systems) and human resource skills. However, interest-holders also articulated anticipated barriers to integration, including (i) potential vaccine waste due to the lack of a resourced and operationalized One Health system for rabies risk assessments; (ii) high staff turnover that could precipitate substandard service provision; (iii) an absence of linked data systems for rabies cases and PEP utilization to inform demand forecasts; and (iv) routine immunization units working only limited days and hours, requiring staff redeployment and workflow redesign for emergency PEP provision. Principal Conclusions: Our results demonstrated enthusiasm for integrating PEP provision into routine immunization services in Tanzania to improve access to PEP through an operationalized One Health approach. Our co-creation process enhanced the possibility of integration by facilitating multisectoral problem identification and problem solving to address intervention uncertainties and complexities. We identified an important need to develop and employ integration guidance, protocols and roadmaps to systematically and comprehensively ensure readiness of the routine immunization systems to accommodate PEP provision. One Health impact statement Human rabies transmitted from domestic dogs is virtually 100% preventable with timely vaccination following exposure, yet access in Tanzania and similar settings is limited by vaccine availability, few facilities, weak referral systems, and high costs. WHO recommends integrating rabies post-exposure vaccine provisioning into routine immunization services, but how to do this remains unclear.Using participatory systems-thinking (process mapping), we brought together animal, human and environmental health sectors, and local government interest-holders, including community members, to analyse current post-exposure vaccine and routine immunization systems. Initially divergent understandings of “integration” gave way to consensus through facilitated co-production.
