papers.title: How AI Information Quality Predicts Innovation Through Knowledge Quality: The Mediation and Moderation Mechanisms
papers.authors: Muhammad Qamar Zia, Muhammad Sufyan Ramish, Muhammad Shahid, Muhammad Muavia
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In the era of digitalization, innovative activities have received increasing attention from scholars, analysis of the mechanisms by which AI information quality shapes knowledge quality, ultimately enhancing innovative outcomes, remains limited. Drawing on Knowledge‐Based View (KBV) theory and integrating Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study empirically examines how and through which mechanisms AI information quality enhances firms' innovation capabilities and employees' innovative performance. It also investigates the boundary condition of AI trust in the linkage between AI information quality and knowledge quality. The three‐wave, multi‐source dataset comprises 71 supervisors and 408 employees working in Pakistan's Information Technology (IT) sector. We analyzed the data using AMOS software and employed covariance‐based structural equation modeling (CB‐SEM). In addition, Hayes PROCESS was used for mediation analysis. Our findings showed that AI information quality shapes knowledge quality, and knowledge quality simultaneously fosters firms' innovation capabilities and employees' innovative performance. Data analysis further showed that knowledge quality partially mediates the relationships among AI information quality, innovation capabilities, and innovative performance. Moreover, AI trust serves as a crucial boundary condition, amplifying the resource‐gain pathway and attenuating the resource‐loss pathway. The study offers practical implications beyond the IT sector.

papers.title: The Influence of the Role of Peer Presence on Game‐Based Chemistry Learning: Evidence From EEG
papers.authors: Qian Huangfu, Yujia Guo, Tingting Deng, 黃志方
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Game‐based learning (GBL) has become an important way to innovate chemistry teaching. However, it is still unclear how different peer roles in GBL shape learners' learning outcomes and cognitive processes. Objectives The study examined how different peer roles (individual vs. collaborators vs. competitors) influence learners' outcomes in game‐based chemistry learning. It also examined differences in theta and alpha power across these conditions. Methods The study employed a between‐subjects design with 69 ninth‐grade students from a secondary school in China who had not yet learned the target chemical concepts. Students were randomly assigned to individual, collaborative or competitive learning. Outcome measurement included immediate and delayed testing, motivation, cognitive load, interest and electroencephalography (EEG)‐based alpha and theta power. Results and Conclusions Both the collaborative and competitive conditions showed higher learning performance and interest than the individual condition. The collaborative condition also showed higher motivation than both the competitive and individual conditions and higher cognitive load than the individual condition. EEG analyses showed that the collaborative condition elicited higher theta and alpha power than the individual condition across both phases, although differences from the competitive condition were not consistently significant. These patterns may reflect greater demands on cognitive control and selective processing during collaborative learning. Implications The findings highlight the value of collaborative peer roles in game‐based chemistry learning. Teachers may consider incorporating structured collaborative activities to promote students' engagement and cognitive involvement. The findings also suggest that different peer roles may serve distinct motivational functions, which may inform the design of GBL activities.

papers.title: Enacting Digital Humanism in Education: A Comparative Case Study of Two Teachers in Greece and Australia
papers.authors: Eunice Yin Yung Chiu
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid expansion of digital technologies in education, accelerated by the COVID 19 pandemic, has transformed teaching and learning worldwide. Although digital humanism has emerged as an important framework for aligning technological development with human values, its enactment in educational practice remains underexplored. This study examines how two educators, a secondary school teacher in Greece and a university professor in Australia, integrated digital technologies whilst prioritising human relationships, student wellbeing and ethical responsibility. Drawing on comparative case study research and thematic narrative analysis, the findings identify three interconnected dimensions of digital humanist practice: fostering human relationships, promoting collaborative and participatory learning and encouraging critical engagement with digital technologies, including artificial intelligence. The study argues that digital humanism functions as a pedagogical orientation that guides the integration of technology into education. The findings contribute empirical evidence to emerging scholarship on digital humanism and offer practical implications for educators navigating digital transformation.

papers.title: AI‐Supported Research‐Led Teaching in Syntegrative Project‐Based Learning: Educator Questioning, Feedback, and Student Learning Outcomes in Authentic Industry Projects
papers.authors: Phi Dinh Khuong, Duong Lam Thuy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new possibilities for connecting research‐led teaching with authentic industry projects, yet its educational value depends on how educators organize inquiry rather than on technological use alone. This study examined the relationships among AI‐supported research‐led teaching (AIRLT), educator questioning (EQ), educator feedback (EF), student inquiry engagement (SIE), and authentic project learning outcomes (APLO) within Syntegrative Project‐Based Learning. A quantitative cross‐sectional survey was conducted with 898 undergraduate students from 12 universities in Vietnam who had participated in authentic industry or organizational projects involving AI‐supported inquiry and educator guidance. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) showed that AIRLT was positively associated with EQ ( β = 0.642) and EF ( β = 0.611). Both EQ ( β = 0.463) and EF ( β = 0.349) were positively associated with SIE, which, in turn, showed a strong positive association with APLO ( β = 0.689). All six specific indirect effects were significant, indicating statistically significant indirect associations among AI‐supported teaching, educator guidance, student inquiry, and perceived authentic learning outcomes. The findings contribute an educator‐mediated perspective to Syntegrative Education by showing that AI is most educationally meaningful when embedded in purposeful questioning, feedback, and sustained student inquiry. The study highlights the importance of designing AI‐supported industry projects around evidence evaluation, iterative feedback, reflection, and active investigation of authentic problems rather than treating AI use as an educational objective in itself.

papers.title: Reversal of refractory epilepsy in an adult with GAMT deficiency: A case report and comparative literature review
papers.authors: Wei‐Hung Sung, Hsi Chen, Che‐Wei Hsu, Meng‐Han Tsai
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Guanidinoacetate methyltransferase (GAMT) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive creatine biosynthesis disorder. Reports specifically focusing on adult patients remain scarce. METHODS: We report a 52-year-old female (the oldest documented case of GAMT deficiency to date) presenting with severe intellectual disability, refractory epilepsy, and adult-onset disease progression. Whole-exome sequencing identified novel compound heterozygous GAMT variants (c.265_267del and c.253G>T), and magnetic resonance spectroscopy confirmed cerebral creatine depletion. Remarkably, initiating oral creatine supplementation at age 52 achieved complete seizure freedom, normalization of the electroencephalogram (EEG), and significant motor function recovery. RESULTS: A comprehensive review revealed that untreated adult patients face a high risk of progressive neurological deterioration. Compared to the pediatric cohort, adults exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of movement disorders (69.2% vs. 33.1%, p < 0.001) and a trend toward a higher prevalence of epilepsy (92.3% vs. 74.2%). Especially, atonic seizures (drop attacks) are particularly characteristic of adult GAMT deficiency, with EEGs frequently demonstrating background slowing, multifocal epileptiform discharges, and electrodecremental patterns. SIGNIFICANCE: This study underscores that continuous disease progression and prolonged neurotoxicity still could compromise the well-being of adult GAMT deficiency patients. Accurate diagnosis is essential for adults presenting with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) phenotype, as even late treatment for GAMT deficiency can still dramatically alleviate the epileptic burden and reverse motor decline. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: We report the oldest known adult diagnosed with GAMT deficiency. Our case demonstrates that starting creatine treatment even at age 52 can dramatically reduce seizures and restore motor function. Literature shows that untreated adults suffer from more severe epilepsy and movement disorders than children, with symptoms worsening over time. These findings highlight the critical need for genetic testing in adults with unexplained severe epilepsy; timely creatine supplementation can halt cognitive decline and significantly restore quality of life.

papers.title: Using podcasts to forward Universal Design for Learning in civil engineering education
papers.authors: Rebekah Sims, Rwayda Kh. S. Al‐Hamd
papers.abstract: The author declare no conflicts of interest. No GenAI/LLM tools were used in any part of the research or writing of this article. Research data are not shared.

papers.title: Algorithmic Provenance: When and Why Consumers Discount Products Made With AI ‐Involved Processes
papers.authors: S. Sreejesh, Souvik Singha
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Firms increasingly incorporate generative and non‐generative artificial intelligence (AI) into product design, formulation, and production, and they face a disclosure question: how should they describe the role of AI to consumers? Across six studies, including analysis of 1800 marketplace listings and five pre‐registered experiments (total experimental N = 2760), we introduce and test a 2‐by‐2 framework of algorithmic provenance defined by the AI's role (agentic vs. assistive) and its visibility in the final product (visible vs. invisible). Identical products are evaluated differently depending on where they fall in this taxonomy. Agentic AI involvement (AI as designer) reduces consumer product attitudes, perceived quality, purchase intentions, and willingness to pay relative to assistive AI involvement (AI as a tool for a human designer). The effect is amplified when AI involvement is visible in the final product. The downstream responses are partially mediated by a new construct, perceived authenticity of creative intention, which captures consumers' inference about whether a human creator pursued a genuine creative vision. The effect is larger for expressive than for functional product domains and larger among consumers primed to hold an independent self‐construal. A scalable managerial intervention, creative‐intent framing, narrows the agentic penalty by approximately half, again through the authenticity mechanism. The findings identify a substantively important new construct for AI disclosure research, refine theories of algorithmic aversion, and offer marketers an actionable disclosure design principle.

papers.title: Governing Generative AI in Newsroom Editorial Management: A POAC-Based Case Study of KG Media
papers.authors: Fathiyyah Azizah, Asrinda Amalia
papers.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the newsroom presents several challenges to the managers of these organizations. Previous studies have examined the adoption of AI in the journalism industry and the ethics of such an adoption. However, fewer studies have attempted to analyse how these developments relate to the management of editorial departments within the setting of an Indonesian media organization. This study examined the responses of KG Media to digital transformation through a qualitative literature study of academic publications, institutional reports and organizational materials. The study applied the Planning-Organizing-Actuating-Controlling (POAC) structure to the analysis of the company's responses to digital transformation. The analysis identified various AI-supported content services, media intelligence initiatives, communication strategies and sustainability-oriented content programs that were implemented by KG Media. Also, these initiatives were related to the four POAC functions of the organization. So, this study provided a management-oriented perspective on the adoption of AI in the editorial department of KG Media. However, since the study was based upon secondary sources, the findings of the study are limited to the publicly-documented practices of the organization.

papers.title: Payout Rules as Market Devices:How LANDR and Splice Decide Who Is Paid When AI Uses Musicians’ Work
papers.authors: Jan Herbst
papers.abstract: Who governs generative AI in music? Where legislators and courts lag, platforms create rules that shape the legal reality of creative work. This article compares payout rules on two major music production platforms that offer royalty-free samples and compensate artists for AI use of their work. LANDR’s Fair Trade AI concerns recordings distributed through LANDR, and Splice’s Variations generates AI-modified versions of samples from its own catalogue. Drawing on actor-network theory, I treat these rules as market devices that define authorised AI use, determine which artists qualify for payment, and establish what counts as fair compensation. A documentary analysis of archived contracts and programme materials shows that LANDR requires artist consent and platform approval, whereas Splice’s documented programme treats catalogue inclusion as sufficient for AI use. I argue that neither logic is adequate on its own. For popular music studies, the programmes rebuild the settlement between artists and intermediaries for training data and show that AI governance in music is already being written into payout rules.

papers.title: The Impact of the Integration of Artificial Intelligence and Search Technology on Online Purchase Intentions
papers.authors: Meina Zhao
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: Based on Service-Dominant Logic (SDL) theory, this study surveyed 409 users who had used Taobao’s AI Universal Search and used structural equation modeling to explore the mechanisms through which AI-integrated search technology promotes online purchase intention. The findings indicate that AI and search technology influence customers’ purchase intent through value co-creation, personalization, and decision-making time. Based on the structural equation model, the study compares the extent to which decision-making time and value co-creation factors influence purchase intention. The research offers practical implications for the platform economy by highlighting the enabling effects of large language models and the provision of precise supply-demand matching. The results indicate that platforms should optimize AI search results to reduce customers’ decision-making time.

papers.title: AI Ingratiation in Content Generation: A Dual-Pathway Model of Intimacy and Authenticity
papers.authors: Xiaochen Liu, Lu Chen, Shouwang Lu
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: As generative AI becomes increasingly embedded in content generation, understanding how its interaction styles shape user responses is critical. This study examines AI ingratiation—AI-generated expressions of praise and flattery—and its effects on user perceptions and behavioral outcomes. A 2×2 online experiment reveals that AI ingratiation increases perceived intimacy but decreases perceived authenticity. Building on these perceptual responses, perceived intimacy and perceived authenticity jointly transmit the effects of AI ingratiation to user satisfaction and content iteration intention, indicating significant indirect effects through these dual mediating pathways. We further examine the moderating role of AI literacy and find that users with higher self-reported AI usage literacy are more responsive to AI ingratiation. Specifically, higher AI literacy strengthens the positive effect of AI ingratiation on perceived intimacy, which in turn enhances user satisfaction. Finally, a multi-group analysis reveals significant differences between advertising and academic contexts, suggesting that the effects of AI ingratiation vary across content generation scenarios. These findings highlight the dual-pathway and context-dependent nature of AI ingratiation in human–AI interaction.

papers.title: Not All GenAI Disclosures Are Alike: How the Stage of GenAI Involvement Shapes Purchase Intention for Digital Games
papers.authors: Fangzhan Lin, Ke Xu, Zhongyun Zhou
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in digital game development, and disclosures on digital platforms make such use more visible to players. Prior research offers conflicting predictions regarding how users respond to such disclosure. Research on AI-generated products suggests that disclosure can reduce valuation because it weakens source-related beliefs tied to human creation. Research on games as interactive hedonic systems, however, suggests that players also evaluate games in terms of the experience they expect during play. Building on these perspectives, this study conceptualizes GenAI disclosure as the focal independent variable and proposes two pathways through which disclosure influences players’ purchase intention. First, GenAI disclosure decreases perceived effort, which lowers purchase intention. Second, GenAI disclosure can increase perceived novelty, which raises purchase intention, but this positive pathway depends on the stage of GenAI involvement described by the disclosure. Specifically, this positive effect is stronger under during-interaction involvement than under pre-interaction involvement. We test the model using a scenario-based online experiment in the context of digital games. The results show that GenAI disclosure reduces perceived effort relative to no disclosure, while its positive effect on perceived novelty emerges primarily when GenAI is described as contributing during gameplay rather than before gameplay. Willingness to pay is included as a supplementary outcome and shows directionally similar but weaker patterns. This study extends GenAI disclosure research to digital games and shows that the effect of disclosure depends not only on whether GenAI use is disclosed, but also on the stage of involvement described by that disclosure.

papers.title: Unlocking Breakthrough Innovation: The Impact of Knowledge Co-creation and Contractual Knowledge Protection
papers.authors: Areziguli Wubuli, Qi Huang, Dan-ni Li
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: There are relatively few existing studies that provide references for Chinese local firms to use collaboration to carry out breakthrough innovation. This study was conducted on 306 respondents from 153 Chinese manufacturing firms, and results indicate that knowledge co-creation mediates the link between resource complementarity and breakthrough innovation. Crucially, the analysis reveals a mediated moderation mechanism: the synergistic interaction between complementarity and contractual knowledge protection is transmitted via knowledge co-creation to drive innovation outcomes. These findings provide insights for firms that want to carry out collaborative breakthrough innovation but are not sure about partner selection and implementation mechanisms in Chinese settings.

papers.title: The Impacts of AI Recommendation Systems on User Loyalty in E-Commerce Platforms: Evidence from Gen Z Consumers in Ho Chi Minh City
papers.authors: Thanh Liem Nguyen, Trung Hieu Duong, Linh Thuy Trang Nguyen, Le Van Khanh Nguyen, Hoai An Le, Xuan Huy Bui
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: This study examines the effects of the AI Recommendation System (ARS) on users’ loyalty on e-commerce platforms in Ho Chi Minh City. Integrating the S-O-R framework and Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the study evaluates how characteristics of ARS, including personalization, accuracy, and transparency, affect trust and satisfaction. Data from 400 Gen Z consumers were analyzed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results showed ARS significantly boosted trust and satisfaction, serving as key intermediates for long-term loyalty. This finding offers practical implications for businesses to optimize AI strategy and build sustainable customer relationships in the digital era.

papers.title: Unpacking the Experience Economy of Role-Playing Conversational AI: A Grounded Theory Analysis
papers.authors: Ke Xu, Fangzhan Lin, Zhongyun Zhou
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of role-playing conversational artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed human-AI interaction from task-oriented exchanges into immersive, scenario-based digital experiences. However, while prior studies predominantly evaluate AI through utilitarian performance or relational support, the holistic experiential structure of these novel interactions remains underexplored. To bridge this gap, this paper draws on the experience economy (4Es) framework to investigate how users experience role-playing conversational AI through the realms of entertainment, education, esthetics, and escapism. Using a grounded theory approach, this study analyzes 6,171 user comments from the Reddit community r/CharacterAI. Findings reveal that user-AI role-playing is fundamentally multidimensional: entertainment and escapism emerge as particularly salient, while educational and esthetic experiences are also clearly present. Ultimately, this study extends the 4Es framework into the context of generative AI, offering a foundational empirical understanding of this emerging form of experiential consumption.

papers.title: A Large Language Model-Based Implementation of the Proposition-to-Requirement Mapping Framework for ESG Greenwashing Detection
papers.authors: Qingan Li, Tianxiao Wu, Xiling Cui
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: This study implements and empirically evaluates the proposition-to-requirement mapping approach proposed in Wu, Li, & Cui (2026). Greenwashing detection in ESG reporting remains difficult because disclosures are narrative, heterogeneous, and often lack transparent evaluation criteria. This study proposes a proposition-level, framework-aligned method for analyzing ESG reports under the HKEX ESG Reporting Guide. The framework converts reports into structured text, decomposes them into atomic propositions, classifies propositions as disclosure, explanation, or residual, and semantically matches them to 192 binary disclosure requirements. Using Tencent’s ESG reports from 2022 to 2024 as a case, the results show that the proposed indicators are directionally consistent with changes in MSCI ESG ratings. The study provides an interpretable and traceable approach to ESG disclosure assessment.

papers.title: Beyond Eye-Tracking: EEG Evidence for Differential Attentional Processing of LED and Projected Sports Venue Signage
papers.authors: Chia-Chan Chang, Simon Chadwick, Jie Liu, Hongying Zhang, Jinming Zong
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: Sports venue signage is a strategic broadcast asset, yet little is known about whether LED and projected formats are processed differently. In a randomized-order within-subjects study, 63 participants viewed four 60-second football clips presenting Ping An Bank and C’estbon signage in both formats while eye movements and EEG were recorded. LED produced faster initial orienting to the area of interest (AOI), whereas projected signage showed higher absolute occipital alpha power. Total fixation duration did not differ, and the projected condition’s higher aided recognition was not statistically significant. The findings show distinct visual and neural response profiles, indicating that signage format should be evaluated against specific sponsorship and broadcast communication objectives.

papers.title: The “Humanization” Paradox of AI Shopping Assistants: The Double-Edged Sword Effect of Social Presence Perception
papers.authors: Mingxin Sun, Yuhui Li, Beiping Tan
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: This study investigates the impact of AI shopping assistant social presence perception on users’ purchase intention through the lens of social presence theory and the persuasion knowledge model. Using data from 193 valid questionnaires collected through the Tencent Questionnaire platform, the results reveal that intelligent presence significantly promotes purchase intention (β = 0.712, p < 0.001), while emotional presence does not have a significant direct effect (β = -0.019, p = 0.813). Trust dimensions, particularly reliability trust, play crucial mediating roles in these relationships. The findings contribute to understanding the double-edged sword effect of AI “humanization” design and provide practical guidance for e-commerce platforms.

papers.title: Trust in AI-Assisted Newsvendor Decisions: Effects of Information Design
papers.authors: Yuxuan Zhang, Haohao Li, Feifan Ren, Yue Li
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: As artificial-intelligence-assisted tools become prevalent in supply chain inventory management, algorithmic trust critically determines the success of human-AI interaction. Based on the newsvendor decision making, this study primarily considers two key factors—information construal level and presentation format—to investigate how they affect trust in AI recommendation, alongside the moderating role of decision-makers' individual traits. Through an incentivized 2×3 between-subjects experiment, we empirically analyze the level of trust in AI decision-making tools, measured by participants' Mean Absolute Percentage Deviation (MAPD) from the AI-advised values across different groups. Results indicate that text-and-graphic and scenario-based presentation formats significantly reduce decision deviation and enhance AI trust, whereas the construal level shows no significant impact. Furthermore, while decision-making style significantly influences AI tool utilization frequency, it does not affect the actual adoption of AI advice. This study clarifies the mechanisms driving algorithmic trust in newsvendor settings and provides empirical evidence and guidelines for enterprises to optimize the front-end interactive design of AI decision assistants and implement differentiated promotion and literacy training strategies tailored to varying employee traits.

papers.title: Research on Human-AI Collaboration Based on BERTopic: Exploratory Thematic Mapping and Evolutionary Analysis (2020-2025)
papers.authors: Yang Zhao, Na Li, Shuai Chen
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: With the increasing integration of artificial intelligence across various societal domains, research on human-AI collaboration has grown rapidly in recent years. This study adopts a thematic mapping approach based on the BERTopic modeling framework to examine the structural organization and evolutionary dynamics of the core human-AI collaboration literature from 2020 to 2025. The analysis identifies nine core themes, including creative collaboration, which are further grouped into four higher-level thematic clusters, such as "Cognitive and Knowledge Co-creation". Longitudinal results show that, although publication output has increased substantially over time, the overall distribution of thematic structures remains relatively stable. This stability suggests a pattern of proportional development across themes, providing a macro-level perspective for understanding the conceptual organization and evolution of the field.

papers.title: Mapping GenAI-Enabled Technical Features to Player Needs in Digital Games: A Needs-(Dis)Affordances-Features Framework
papers.authors: Yake Yang, Fangzhan Lin, Ke Xu, Zhongyun Zhou
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes increasingly embedded in digital products, understanding how users experience GenAI-enabled products has become an important research issue. Prior research on GenAI products has mainly examined relatively static AI-generated outputs, with particular attention to disclosure, algorithmic source, authenticity, and perceived value. However, this literature offers limited insight into digital games, where GenAI may be incorporated not only into pre-generated components such as assets, text, and audio, but also into runtime systems such as adaptive dialogue, characters, and gameplay content. To address this gap, this study develops a Needs-(Dis)Affordances-Features framework for understanding how GenAI-enabled technical features shape players’ psychological need satisfaction and frustration in digital games. Drawing on the needs-affordances-features perspective, disaffordance, and self-determination theory, we conduct a grounded theory analysis of 3,096 reviews from 810 digital games on Steam identified through platform statements indicating GenAI involvement. The findings suggest that player responses are shaped less by AI-related labels or source cues than by the specific technical features through which GenAI is incorporated into the game. GenAI-enabled features such as generated assets, dialogue, and adaptive systems give rise to affordances and disaffordances that support or frustrate autonomy, competence, and relatedness. This study extends research on GenAI products to digital games by showing how feature-level GenAI integration, rather than AI origin alone, shapes player experience.

papers.title: The Paradox of Efficiency: Teacher-Directed AI Misuse and the Burden of Busywork in Higher Education
papers.authors: Zhan Zhan, ABM Munibur Rahman, Weiguo Feng, Jianhui Xiang
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into higher education to enhance instructional efficiency and improve learning outcomes. However, its adoption has revealed a paradox: AI-enabled teaching may unintentionally increase student workload without corresponding educational benefits. This study examines teacher-generated “algorithmic busywork,” defined as excessive, low-value assignments produced using Artificial intelligence tools with limited pedagogical design. Using survey data from 206 undergraduate students across multiple universities, we analyze students’ exposure to AI-generated assignments, their perceived educational value, and associated cognitive and emotional responses. The findings indicate that AI misuse in teaching is linked to increased academic stress, reduced engagement, and perceived inefficiencies in learning. Many students report that AI-generated tasks are repetitive, weakly aligned with learning objectives, and detract from more meaningful learning activities.This study contributes to the information systems and digital education literature by shifting attention from student misuse to teacher-directed Artificial intelligence practices. It highlights the need for pedagogical guidelines to ensure that AI-enabled teaching improves, rather than undermines, student outcomes.

papers.title: The Right Amount of “Human Touch”: The Curvilinear Effect of Embodied AI Agent Anthropomorphism on Consumer Usage Intention under Social Intrusiveness
papers.authors: Du Chen, Lin Hui Sun
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: Anthropomorphic design in embodied AI agents often evokes ambivalent consumer responses, yet it remains a key strategy for enhancing users’ intention to use such agents. Based on three video-based scenario experiments with 438 participants, this study examines how anthropomorphism shapes consumers’ usage intentions. The results confirm an inverted-U-shaped relationship between anthropomorphism of embodied AI agents and usage intention. Further analyses reveal that likability and eeriness jointly mediate this curvilinear relationship: anthropomorphism exerts an inverted U-shaped effect on likability, which in turn positively influences usage intention, whereas anthropomorphism exerts a U-shaped effect on eeriness, which negatively influences usage intention. In addition, social intrusiveness functions as a boundary condition by (1) strengthening the curvilinear relationships between anthropomorphism and both likability and eeriness, and (2) moderating the indirect effects of likability and eeriness. These findings provide empirical support for applying social information processing theory to human–AI interaction and extend uncanny valley theory from emotional responses to usage intention. The study also offers practical implications for deploying embodied AI agents in customer service contexts.

papers.title: AI Adoption and Firm Value: A Comparative Study of Chinese FinTech Companies
papers.authors: Yuanting Xia, ABM Munibur Rahman, Ning Zhang
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: Conventional approaches fail to capture how AI creates value in FinTech. This study develops a multidimensional AI adoption index and examines its relationship with firm value through comparative analysis of Tonghuashun, East Money Information, and Wind Information. Building on a comparative case analysis of three leading FinTech firms, complemented by panel data regression on firm–quarter observations (2018–2024), we find a U–shaped relationship–value emerges only after a threshold of AI integration is reached. Tonghuashun, the highest adopter, achieved 180% market capitalization growth since 2020, reaching RMB 169.94 billion, with monthly active users double its closest competitor. The findings indicate that strategic AI depth drives superior valuation, offering a replicable framework for evaluating AI value creation in emerging markets and extends the application of corporate valuation models to incorporate AI adoption as a measurable driver of firm value.

papers.title: Theoretical Mechanisms and Framework of Perceived Algorithmic Bias Affecting Human-AI Collaborative Decision-Making Performance
papers.authors: Qiong Jia, Yuxin Zhang
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: Perceived algorithmic bias is defined as users' comprehensive subjective cognitive judgment, grounded in a cognitive attribution perspective, regarding whether an algorithmic system engages in differential treatment, whether its outcomes exhibit systematic deviations, and whether such differential treatment is justified. This study develops a theoretical model of perceived algorithmic bias and systematically elucidates the construct through three dimensions: perceived differential treatment, perceived outcome skew, and perceived lack of justification. The paper examines the mechanisms through which perceived algorithmic bias influences human-AI collaborative decision-making performance across three levels: cognitive processing, affect and morality, and human-AI interaction. It also analyzes the moderating roles of individual characteristics, algorithmic characteristics, and task characteristics. By systematically reviewing the conceptualizations of algorithmic bias and perceived algorithmic bias and clarifying their effects on and theoretical mechanisms underlying human-AI collaborative decision-making performance, this study offers theoretical implications for advancing research on perceived algorithmic bias. Future research may further develop a measurement scale for perceived algorithmic bias, enrich empirical investigations, test its underlying mechanisms, and explore its impact on human-AI collaborative decision-making performance across diverse application contexts.

papers.title: The Impact of GenAI Literacy on Consumer Decision-Making: A Moderated Mediation Model of Information Overload and Consumer Involvement
papers.authors: He-Ran Wen, Yi-Ming Guo, Ze-Long Feng
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is fundamentally reshaping the landscape of consumer decision-making by providing unprecedented levels of personalized information. However, the inherent complexity and potential for AI hallucinations introduce significant cognitive challenges that may undermine decision quality. Grounded in Information Processing Theory (IPT), this study investigates the mechanism through which GenAI literacy influences consumer decision quality, specifically focusing on the mediating role of perceived information overload and the moderating role of consumer involvement. Through a structured survey of 401 Chinese college students and subsequent structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis, the empirical results demonstrate that GenAI literacy is directly and positively associated with decision quality. Furthermore, perceived information overload serves as a critical mediator, indicating that high levels of GenAI literacy could reduce cognitive friction and prevent decision paralysis. Notably, the continuous latent interaction analysis reveals that consumer involvement significantly moderates the relationship between GenAI literacy and perceived information overload, with the inhibitory effect of literacy being more pronounced in high-involvement scenarios. These findings extend the application of IPT to the era of human-AI symbiosis and offer actionable insights for policymakers and enterprises to optimize the digital consumption ecosystem.

papers.title: How AI Is Transforming Education: Toward a Symbiotic Relationship among AI, Teachers, and Students
papers.authors: Xu Fang, Zhiyi Liu, Hanshuo Yang, Yongqiang Luo
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping education by reorganizing interactions among teaching, learning, and instructional decision-making. Existing research has largely focused on isolated tools or specific learning outcomes, providing limited insight into how AI operates within integrated educational systems. This study examines an AI-enabled educational environment to explore how interactions among AI systems, teachers, and students relate to changes in instructional organization and student performance. Drawing on multi-source data generated from routine teaching activities, the findings suggest overall improvements in learning outcomes and indicate three interconnected mechanisms: improved instructional efficiency through reduced routine workload, stronger alignment between diagnosis and feedback, and a complementary division of roles between human teachers and AI systems. By linking learning outcomes with underlying instructional processes, the study provides system-level evidence on how integrated AI-enabled environments reshape educational practice and contribute to the emerging symbiotic relationship among AI, teachers, and students.

papers.title: How “AI Info” Labels Influence Social Media Posting Behavior? Evidence from Instagram
papers.authors: Pengkun Wu, Yuanxi Liu, Yuanyuan Wu, Yang Liu
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: AI-generated content (AIGC) has reshaped content creation on social media, prompting platforms to adopt “AI Info” labels as transparency mechanisms. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines how such labels influence content creators’ posting frequency. Using a propensity score matched difference-in-differences (PSM-DiD) design applied to a panel dataset of 237 Instagram creators observed from January 2023 to December 2025, we find that mandatory AI labeling significantly reduces creators’ weekly posting frequency. This study contributes to AI transparency research by demonstrating unintended behavioral consequences of disclosure policies for content creators, and offers implications for platform governance design.

papers.title: Anthropomorphism and Relational Ontology of Purchase Intention in Generative AI Use: Insights from Mind Perception Theory and the Computers as Social Actors Paradigm
papers.authors: Jao-Hong Cheng, Li-Ming Wang
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: A human-centric understanding of purchase intention in generative AI contexts requires attention to how users interpret and experience AI systems under conditions of algorithmic opacity. Rather than treating AI adoption as the outcome of attribute evaluation, we argue that anthropomorphic cues shape how users construe the system itself. When AI is experienced as socially responsive rather than purely instrumental, evaluative emphasis shifts toward trust beliefs and interactional arousal. Drawing on Computers as Social Actors (CASA) and Mind Perception Theory, we theorize that anthropomorphism restructures the experiential architecture through which intention is formed. Using structural equation modeling with data from 526 generative AI users, results show that anthropomorphism influences purchase intention both directly and indirectly through trust and arousal, with relational mechanisms exerting stronger effects. By foregrounding user construal and experiential engagement, this research advances a human-centric framework for understanding AI adoption in opaque, interactive environments.

papers.title: The Impact of AI-Generated Content on Brand Image: A Dual Perspective of Algorithm Appreciation and Aversion
papers.authors: Mingxin Sun, Beiping Tan, Congyu Niu, Xinyu Guo
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
papers.abstract: With the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence technologies such as ChatGPT, Midjourney, and DALL-E, brands are increasingly leveraging AI to create marketing content. However, systematic research on how AI-generated content affects brand image remains scarce in academia, creating a critical knowledge gap for marketing practitioners. This study addresses this gap by investigating consumer attitudes toward brand use of AI-generated content and the underlying psychological mechanisms. Grounded in Algorithm Aversion theory and AI Technological Image Transfer theory, we examine whether brands should disclose AI involvement in their marketing content and how different AI participation approaches influence brand perception through three experimental studies (N=940). Results show that 100% AI-generated content significantly enhances brand image across all dimensions, with innovativeness showing the largest improvement. AI involvement approach significantly affects brand perception, with 100% AI producing the strongest effect. AI social identity emerges as the key psychological driver, while AI aversion paradoxically benefits 100% AI strategies through an “honesty effect.” This research challenges traditional algorithm aversion assumptions and provides guidance for brand AI marketing strategies.

papers.title: The detrimental impact of concurrent movement execution on object grasp planning is sex/gender dependent
papers.authors: Toussaint Lucette, Frédéric Danion
papers.abstract: Fast and efficient planning of manual actions is essential for successful everyday behavior. In the present study, we investigated an object-grasping judgment task assessing participants’ ability to plan an appropriate grasp to ensure an optimal final hand posture (end-state comfort effect). While the detrimental effects of concurrent cognitive tasks on action planning are well documented, the impact of concurrent grasping movements on grasp planning remains unclear. Additionally, despite substantial evidence for sex/gender-related differences in cognitive and motor skills, their impact on such an object-grasping judgment task has received limited attention. To fill these gaps, we compared the performance of male (n=32) and female (n=32) participants under either a static condition, in which the hands were immobile, or a dynamic condition, in which the right hand was already engaged in rhythmic grasping while simultaneously performing the right-hand object-grasping judgment task). Results revealed that action planning was impaired in the dynamic condition compared to the static condition, as reflected by reduced accuracy (87% vs. 71%) and increased response times (RTs, 1287ms vs. 1426ms). While the decrease in accuracy was similar in both males and females, a sex/gender differential effect was observed in RTs. Notably, while female RTs increased under the dynamic condition (+267ms), this increase was not observed in male RTs (+10ms). Taken together, these results suggest that ongoing action interferes with action planning, presumably because planning and execution compete for shared neural resources. This study also aligns with known sex/gender differences in motor imagery, visuospatial abilities, and multitasking.

papers.title: When Risk Factors Compete: A Machine Learning Approach to Identifying Antecedents of Adolescent Delinquency Across Domains, Development, and Gender
papers.authors: Frida Bood, Louise Frogner, Matthew Cashman, Karin Hellfeldt, Henrik Andershed, Evelina Landstedt, Anna‐Karin Andershed
papers.abstract: Risk factors for adolescent delinquency have been identified at multiple levels, from individual dispositions through family and school processes to ecological context, yet their relative importance remains unestablished. Which factors carry greatest weight, and when, has not been tested in simultaneous modelling. This study assessed 111 predictors spanning five domains across four developmental periods, predicting self-reported delinquency in mid-adolescence. Predictors were teacher- and parent-reported and the outcome adolescent self-reported. Participants were a Swedish population-based cohort followed from early childhood into adolescence (N = 2,121; 46.6% girls; mean age 3.86 years at baseline; 97.8% born in Sweden). Using machine learning techniques, random forests were estimated across the full span (AUC = .787, 95% CI [.747, .826]) and at each developmental period for boys and girls. Parent-rated conduct problems ranked among the leading predictors at every period, while caregiver emotional functioning carried greatest weight in early and late childhood before being displaced by dispositional and behavioral characteristics. Parent-rated social competence was the strongest protective factor. Associations were threshold-shaped, with the shift to elevated risk falling within the ordinary range of the measures. Gender differences in ranking were not supported by formal testing, which was low-powered.

papers.title: Study 1: Main Effect
papers.authors: CHOUNLAMOUNTRY LATTANAMANY
papers.abstract: This component contains all materials, questionnaires, experimental stimuli, data analysis plans, and related documents for Study 1, which examines the main effect of AI customer service anthropomorphism on consumers' unethical behavior.

papers.title: The Effect of AI Customer Service Anthropomorphism on Consumers' Unethical Behavior
papers.authors: CHOUNLAMOUNTRY LATTANAMANY
papers.abstract: This project contains the materials, preregistration, experimental stimuli, questionnaires, analysis plans, and supplementary documents for a research project examining the effect of AI customer service anthropomorphism on consumers' unethical behavior.

papers.authors: CHOUNLAMOUNTRY LATTANAMANY

papers.title: Study Habits and Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence Tools Among Anesthesia Trainees in Türkiye: A Descriptive Survey: Study Habits of Anesthesia Trainees
papers.authors: Çağrı Özdemir, Beyza Mehri Büyükgebiz Yeşil, Miray Gözde Özdemir
papers.abstract: Objective: To describe the study habits and attitudes toward the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools for studying among anesthesia trainees in Türkiye, and to explore the associations between these factors and performance in national in-training examinations.Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was administered to anesthesia trainees in Türkiye between April and June 2025. The questionnaire addressed study frequency and duration, preferred resources, AI use patterns, and 5-point Likert ratings for reliability and usefulness. Performance in the national online trainee assessment examination (ÇADS) was analyzed using Kruskal-Wallis tests and Spearman correlation, with ÇADS scores encoded as ordinal ranks (1-4).Results: A total of 148 responses were analyzed. Study sessions were reported as “occasional” by 60.1%, with typical sessions lasting 1-2 hours (48.6%). Although 96.6% of the respondents perceived a need to study more, the main barriers were fatigue and burnout (46.9%) and time constraints due to clinical duties (29.4%). The most commonly used resources were textbooks (92.6%), spaced repetition (60.8%), and online journals (52.7%). AI tools were rated as useful (mean 3.89 ± 0.99) but only moderately reliable (3.22 ± 0.97). Two-thirds of the respondents participated regularly in ÇADS (66.2%). Among the 130 participants who had completed at least one ÇADS examination, the most frequently reported score category was 60-79 (73.1%). Frequent AI use was significantly associated with higher ÇADS performance (p = 0.003). No associations were found between ÇADS performance and study frequency or specific study techniques.Conclusion: Anesthesia trainees in Türkiye display irregular, brief study patterns, with fatigue and burnout as the main problems. AI tool adoption remains low, likely due to moderate trust and a lack of guidance. Frequent AI use and higher self-confidence were associated with better examination performance in exploratory univariable analyses. Educational programs may benefit from addressing workload and burnout while providing structured guidance for the appropriate integration of AI tools.

papers.title: ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯ СТРУКТУРЫ МАРКЕТИНГОВЫХ ЗАТРАТ ПРЕДПРИЯТИЯ ПРИ ВНЕДРЕНИИ ИНСТРУМЕНТОВ ГЕНЕРАТИВНОГО ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА
papers.authors: Кристина Дмитриевна Веселова
papers.abstract: The article analyzes changes in the structure of enterprise marketing costs resulting from the implementation of generative artificial intelligence tools. The relevance of the study is determined by the redistribution of marketing operations from expenditures on external contractors and in-house personnel toward digital platforms and computing resources, which changes the composition of marketing budgets. The study reviews theoretical approaches to the classification of marketing costs and the role of generative artificial intelligence in marketing activities. Using a case-study method, it examines practical implementations in several Russian companies and compares available quantitative indicators before and after adoption. The analysis reveals a reduction in the unit cost of producing marketing content and a shift in expenditure toward digital tools and the development of employee competencies. The findings indicate that generative artificial intelligence does not eliminate marketing costs but redistributes them between budget items, increasing the importance of human involvement in task formulation, editing, quality control, and strategic planning.

papers.title: Talabaning axborot xavfsizligi kompetensiyasi pedagogik tushuncha sifatida: mohiyati, tarkibi va sun’iy intellekt sharoitidagi o‘ziga xosligi
papers.authors: Шахзод Маманазар угли Мустафоев
papers.abstract: This article provides a theoretical analysis of students’ information security competence as a pedagogical concept. It examines its essence, structural components, and the pedagogical factors influencing its development. Particular attention is paid to the protection of personal data, the assessment of information reliability, the identification of cyber threats, compliance with digital ethics standards, and the development of a critical approach to content generated by artificial intelligence in the context of the widespread integration of artificial intelligence tools into the educational process. Furthermore, the cognitive, practical-activity, value-motivational, and reflective components of information security competence are substantiated. The article also explores the pedagogical potential of competency-based, systemic, activity-oriented, and learner-centered approaches to developing this competence.

papers.title: Inteligencia Artificial Explicable en programación competitiva: análisis comparativo de métodos de Machine Learning bajo los principios FATE
papers.authors: Claudia Morales Herrera, Hubert Viltres Sala, Aneyty Martín García, Yeleny Zulueta Véliz, Yaniselis Sánchez Hormigó, Leonides Rodríguez Martínez
papers.abstract: This review article analyzes the application of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in the context of programming education, structuring the analysis around the FATE principles (Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, Explainability). A systematic review was conducted of the scientific literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026 in databases such as Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Scielo. Based on the findings, the review also incorporates an empirical analysis of seven comparable systems that apply ML in educational and competitive programming contexts. The analysis shows that most ML models applied to programming education prioritize predictive accuracy over transparency. A structural gap is identified: the most accurate models exhibit the lowest levels of explainability, compromising the FATE principles. The combination of Decision Trees as an intrinsically interpretable model with TreeSHAP as a post-hoc explainability technique offers the optimal balance between performance and pedagogical transparency. The integration of XAI into learning analytics is not a marginal technical improvement, but an ethical imperative to transform automated assessment systems into pedagogical allies that guarantee equity and causal feedback to students. Keywords: accuracy, decision tree, explainability, FATE, method, transparency, TreeSHAP, XAI.

papers.title: Fractional Optimal Control of AI-TPACK Learning Dynamics with FBSM Numerical Study
papers.authors: Moosa Ebadi
papers.journal: International journal of industrial engineering and operational research
papers.abstract: In this study, we develop a fractional optimal control model for teachers' artificial intelligence-based technological pedagogical content knowledge (AI-TPACK). Four state variables: AI-related technological knowledge (AI-TK), technological content knowledge (AI-TCK), technological pedagogical knowledge (AI-TPK), and integrated AI-TPACK are used in the model. We used two bounded decision variables: technology-integration workshops and specialized technology courses. A direct-method proof establishes the existence of an optimal pair. Pontryagin conditions yield the fractional adjoint and the classical pseudo-state system used numerically, as well as separate projection formulas for both interventions. A local contraction theorem gives sufficient conditions for convergence of the relaxed forward-backward sweep method (FBSM). The results support a staged policy: moderately stronger technology-integration workshops, complemented by specialized courses, provide a more efficient pathway than either intervention component alone. The scenario coefficients are used in this work to solve the AI-TPACK optimal control model numerically.

papers.title: Analisis Literasi Digital Lansia Dalam Mengidentifikasi Penipuan Berbasis Kecerdasan Buatan di Whatsapp Pada Komunitas Santa Monika Bekasi
papers.authors: Nataliani Suseno, Yulianti Fajar Wulandari, Cindya Yunita Pratiwi
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine artificial intelligence (AI)-based scams on WhatsApp within the Santa Monika Bekasi Community. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the research explores the characteristics of older adults as social media users in the digital era. It also investigates the rapid development of communication technology and its influence on how older adults receive, interpret, and process information. WhatsApp is one of the most widely used communication platforms across different age groups. Digital media, commonly referred to as new media, enables information to be disseminated through digital technologies. Although these technologies provide convenient access to information, they have also created opportunities for increasingly prevalent online scams. In this context, enhancing digital literacy and raising awareness among older adults are essential to helping them identify suspicious messages, recognize potential AI-based scams on WhatsApp, and take appropriate measures to avoid becoming victims of digital fraud.

papers.title: ТРАДИЦИОННЫЕ МЕТОДЫ И МЕТОДЫ, ОСНОВАННЫЕ НА ИСКУССТВЕННОМ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТЕ, В ОБУЧЕНИИ РЕШЕНИЮ ТЕКСТОВЫХ ЗАДАЧ ПО ШКОЛЬНОЙ МАТЕМАТИКЕ: СРАВНИТЕЛЬНОЕ ИССЛЕДОВАНИЕ С ТОЧКИ ЗРЕНИЯ РАЗВИТИЯ НАВЫКОВ РЕШЕНИЯ ЗАДАЧ У УЧАЩИХСЯ
papers.authors: Салтанат Бахитжановна Ерназарова, Диёра Аюбханқызы Талипова
papers.journal: «Qazaq Journal of Young Scientist» халықаралық ғылыми журналы
papers.abstract: Digitalization of education creates new opportunities for mathematics teaching. Solving word problems requires not only mathematical knowledge but also analytical skills, logical reasoning, and the ability to choose an appropriate solution strategy. Therefore, comparing traditional teaching methods with artificial intelligence-based approaches is becoming increasingly relevant. This article examines traditional and artificial intelligence-based approaches to teaching word problems in school mathematics. Their potential for developing students problem-solving skills is compared. Particular attention is given to understanding the problem statement, constructing a mathematical model, and selecting a solution strategy. The development of digital tools in mathematics education is also considered. The study uses scientific literature analysis, comparative analysis and theoretical generalization. The main characteristics of traditional and artificial intelligence-based approaches are identified. Traditional methods provide systematic development of mathematical knowledge and allow teachers to monitor the learning process. Artificial intelligence can provide immediate feedback and adapt support to individual student needs. However, the use of ready-made solutions may reduce students independent thinking . Therefore, artificial intelligence should be used as an additional learning tool rather than as a replacement for the teacher or students independent work.

papers.title: Análisis bibliométrico de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación médica entre 2021 y 2026
papers.authors: Mario Alexander Aguilar Balseca, Joane Nicole Aguilar Balseca, Daniel Alberto Hidrovo Moreno, Laura Katheryne Hernández León
papers.abstract: Introduction: Generative artificial intelligence burst into medical education and led to accelerated growth in publications on its integration into the training of health professionals. The structure of this scientific output in terms of volume, origin, journals and thematic trends remains unknown. Objective: To analyze the scientific output on generative artificial intelligence in medical education indexed in Scopus between 2021 and 2026. Methods: A descriptive bibliometric study was conducted. The universe comprised the documents indexed in Scopus that addressed generative artificial intelligence in medical education, retrieved through a search strategy applied to title, abstract and keywords. Productivity, impact and thematic trend indicators were analyzed with descriptive statistics and keyword co-occurrence analysis with routines developed in Python. Results: The sample included 3 223 documents, with sustained growth since 2023 and 90,4 % published between 2024 and 2026. Original articles predominated (72,9 %). The United States (27,0 %) and China (12,7 %) led the output, with marginal Ibero-American participation. JMIR Medical Education headed the journal list. The documents accumulated 52 761 citations (average of 16,4) and the keyword network comprised 132 terms grouped into 4 thematic clusters. Conclusions: The scientific output showed recent and accelerated growth, concentrated in a few countries and specialized journals, with a thematic shift toward the responsible use of these tools and research gaps in Latin America.

papers.title: ผลลพธและปจจยทมผลตอระดบนำตาลของผปวยเบาหวานชนดท 2 ทควบคมนำตาลไมได จากหนวยบรการปฐมภม โรงพยาบาลพทธโสธร ภายใตการดแลผปวยในทบาน
papers.authors: Krittin Wareeudomsup
papers.abstract: Background: Currently, Buddhasothorn Hospital implemented the Home Ward model for patients with hyperglycemia to reduce hospital overcrowding and improve the quality of life for both patients and caregivers. However, evidence regarding the outcomes of this service remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the outcomes of the Home Ward service among patients with uncontrolled diabetes at primary care units. Objective: To evaluate the outcomes of the Home Ward service on glycemic levels and to identify factors associated with glycemic control among patients with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes at the primary care units of Buddhasothorn Hospital. Methods: This retrospective descriptive-analytic study evaluated 73 patients with type 2 diabetes. Data were retrieved from the A-MED and HosXP systems between October 1, 2024, and September 30, 2025. Data analysis was performed using descriptive statistics, paired t-test, and logistic regression. Results: Following the intervention, patients demonstrated reductions in both hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and fasting blood sugar (FBS) levels at 3 and 6 months. The reduction in HbA1c was statistically significant (p < 0.001). Multiple logistic regression analysis revealed that factors significantly associated with uncontrolled blood glucose levels included obesity with a BMI ≥ 25 kg/m² (aOR = 3.14, 95% CI: 1.29 - 7.62, p = 0.011), a baseline HbA1c >12 (aOR = 2.68, 95% CI: 1.19 - 6.01, p = 0.017), and a duration of care under the Home Ward program of less than 7 days (aOR = 2.68, 95% CI: 1.19 - 6.01, p = 0.017) Conclusion: The Home Ward care model was significantly associated with a reduction in glycemic levels. Furthermore, a body mass index BMI ≥ 25 kg/m², a baseline HbA1c >12, and a duration of admission less than 7 days were key factors significantly associated with glycemic control in this patient population.

papers.title: Multimodal AI Detection for Math-Heavy Scientific Text
papers.authors: Yixuan Huang, Danish Pruthi, Bhuwan Dhingra
papers.abstract: As large language models become increasingly capable of generating, and assisting with, scientific writing, there is a need for greater transparency and disclosure around the use of AI in research. Consequently, a veritable subfield of research and a number of commercial services aim to flag AI-generated content automatically. However, existing detectors which rely only on text extracted from PDFs fail to benefit from the rich visual information contained in the formatting of math-heavy scientific content. To study this, we select human-written proof and prose passages from pre-2022 arXiv LaTeX sources and re-generate them using 15 modern LLMs within the context of the same paper. This leaves us with coupled human and AI outputs in three different representations: the LaTeX source, a rendered image of the PDF, and the text extracted from the PDF. We find that the accuracy of the state-of-the-art Pangram 4 drops significantly as the mathematical content in a passage increases, especially when evaluated on text as opposed to LaTeX. However, this is not an inherent limitation of detecting AI-generated math: finetuning Qwen-3.5-27B based detectors on this domain recovers the gap, with LaTeX inputs performing significantly better than text since they preserve more formatting information. Since LaTeX sources are rarely available in practice, we also train SnapJudge: an image-based detector operating on screenshots of both prose and proofs from papers. At 0.1% false positive rate, SnapJudge achieves a detection rate of 92% on proofs and 93% on prose generated by frontier models, substantially outperforming both Pangram 4 and our text-based detector. We release our data, models and code at https://nlplab.cs.duke.edu/snapjudge.

papers.title: PocketTSLM: Deploying an On-Device Soft-Prompt Time-Series Language Model for Privacy-Preserving Smartphone Reasoning
papers.authors: Max Rosenblattl, Nikhil Krishnaswamy, Leon Nissen, Manuel Milling, Nicolas Zumarraga, Ning Wang, Thomas Kaar, Robert Jakob, Björn W. Schuller, Elgar Fleisch, Patrick Langer, Paul Schmiedmayer
papers.abstract: Consumer phones and wearables increasingly collect physiological time-series data, yet most mobile systems treat these streams as summaries or text rather than as temporal evidence. This representation is poorly matched to personal health systems that need to retrieve, route, or summarize sensor evidence while preserving temporal structure. Cloud-hosted time-series language models avoid smartphone limits, but they repeatedly move sensitive physiology off the device and add latency and per-query compute cost. Mobile model alternatives that aggregate time-series data into statistical features or serialize raw samples as text either compress temporal structure or exhaust the context and memory budgets of small on-device models. We present PocketTSLM, a mobile-native deployment of OpenTSLM SoftPrompt, the soft-prompt variant of the OpenTSLM time-series language model. PocketTSLM runs fully on a consumer smartphone by injecting encoded time-series windows as embeddings instead of tokenizing time series as text. A numerical parity protocol verifies identical greedy-decoded token sequences between the Swift port and a Python reference using Apple's MLX machine-learning framework. Answers also match the PyTorch reference, although rationale wording can differ. An on-device context-economics benchmark compares the soft-prompt path with a text-serialized baseline on the same backbone. In our benchmark format, soft-prompting uses approximately 12 times fewer time-series tokens and reduces prompt-prefill cost. PocketTSLM processes 30-second Sleep-EDF electroencephalography clips for sleep staging and a 1,000-sample (10 s) 12-lead electrocardiogram clip from ECG-QA. In comparison, text-serialized baselines exceed the phone's context or memory budget at longer time-series windows. All inference runs entirely on the device, with no health data transmitted during inference.

papers.title: Green Nanoparticles in Precision Agriculture: A Critical Review of Smart Crop Management, Nano-Enabled Delivery Systems, and Sustainable Farming
papers.authors: Abisha Meji Marshal Williams, Milon Selvam Dennison, Sarad Pawar Naik Bukke, Bosco Christin Maria Arputham Ashwin
papers.journal: Dove Medical Press (Taylor and Francis Group)
papers.abstract: Abisha Meji Marshal Williams,1 Milon Selvam Dennison,2 Sarad Pawar Naik Bukke,3 Bosco Christin Maria Arputham Ashwin41Department of ETC Engineering, School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, Kampala International University, Western Campus, Ishaka-Bushenyi, Uganda; 2Department of Mechanical Engineering, School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, Kampala International University, Western Campus, Ishaka-Bushenyi, Uganda; 3Department of Pharmacy, Faculty of Health Sciences, Victoria University, Victoria Towers, 1-13 Jinja Road, Kampala, Uganda; 4PG Department of Chemistry, Pioneer Kumaraswamy College, Nagercoil, Tamil Nadu, IndiaCorrespondence: Abisha Meji Marshal Williams, Email abisha.meji@kiu.ac.ug Bosco Christin Maria Arputham Ashwin, Email b.mashwin@yahoo.comAbstract: Sustainable agricultural production requires approaches that improve resource-use efficiency while limiting environmental burdens. This critical review examines green-synthesized Nanoparticles (NPs) in precision agriculture, covering sustainable synthesis, smart crop management, nano-enabled delivery systems, nano-biosensors, plant-nanoparticle interactions, environmental risks, circular agriculture, and digital technologies. The NPs derived from Plant, microbial, biomolecule, and waste shows potential for targeted nutrient delivery, crop protection, stress management, and improved monitoring. However, reported performance varies with NP size, surface properties, concentration, formulation, crop type, soil, and environmental conditions. The review therefore critically considers both benefits and risks, including phytotoxicity, effects on beneficial microorganisms, persistence, bioaccumulation, and long-term ecosystem impacts. Waste-derived NPs and circular nanomanufacturing offer opportunities for resource recovery and agricultural waste valorization, but their scalability and economic feasibility remain uncertain. The integration with Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoTs), Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), remote sensing, and smart decision-support systems may improve site-specific management. The review also examines technology readiness, commercialization pathways, manufacturing consistency, cost, and regulatory requirements. The green NPs shows promise for sustainable precision agriculture, but wider adoption requires stronger field validation, standardized characterization, environmental risk assessment, reproducible manufacturing, economic evaluation, and responsible regulatory development.Keywords: circular agriculture, green nanoparticles, nano-biosensors, nano-enabled delivery systems, nano-fertilizers, nano-pesticides, plant-nanoparticle interactions, precision agriculture, smart crop management, waste-derived nanoparticles

papers.title: Technical Infrastructure and Digital Maturity with Cloud Technology in Libraries
papers.authors: Mr. Komal Sahu, Mr. Chandrabhushan Chandravanshi, Mrs. Kajal Sahu
papers.journal: Information Horizons: American Journal of Library and Information Science Innovation (2993-2777)
papers.abstract: Examining the foundational elements of modern education reveals that while a technical framework is a core component of contemporary libraries, integrating digital industry standards and maturity levels significantly optimizes the educational ecosystem. Cloud computing technology fundamentally transforms library operations by enhancing data redundancy, security, and processing speeds. Because user satisfaction relies heavily on seamless access to authentic data, libraries must transition toward agile digital models that foster systemic innovation. This shift facilitates universal, anytime-anywhere access to educational materials via user-centric remote access systems. Furthermore, achieving organizational digital maturity and implementing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cloud-based frameworks necessitates the continuous adoption of smart study tools to ensure the efficacy of educational methodologies. Ultimately, this computer-based technological infrastructure depends on the orchestration of key backend technologies, including device drivers, RFID systems, wireless sensors, and dynamic resource management.

papers.title: Implementasi Chatbot Rekomendasi Produk Skincare Berbasis Website Menggunakan Metode NLP TF-IDF Dan Cosine Similarity
papers.authors: Firman Anugrah, Nugraha, Indra Yustiana
papers.abstract: Perkembangan industri kosmetik memunculkan fenomena choice overload dan asimetri informasi, di mana konsumen awam sering menyampaikan keluhan menggunakan bahasa sehari-hari, sementara spesifikasi produk dijelaskan dengan terminologi medis. Hal ini menyulitkan konsumen dalam menemukan produk yang tepat. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang agen percakapan cerdas (chatbot) berbasis website sebagai sistem rekomendasi skincare untuk menjembatani kesenjangan bahasa tersebut secara komputasional. Pengembangan sistem mengadopsi metode Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) dengan model Waterfall. Basis data yang digunakan mencakup 280 data produk primer dari 11 merek terkemuka. Teks masukan pengguna diproses melalui tahapan Natural Language Processing (NLP). Teks tersebut kemudian dibobotkan menggunakan metode Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), dan tingkat kemiripannya dihitung menggunakan metrik Cosine Similarity. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan sistem berhasil beroperasi dengan baik. Pengujian Black Box membuktikan seluruh fungsionalitas berjalan 100% tanpa galat (bug). Pengujian akurasi algoritma mencatatkan skor relevansi yang tinggi dalam merekomendasikan produk. Selain itu, hasil User Acceptance Testing (UAT) terhadap 33 responden memperoleh skor rata-rata 3,98 (kategori Baik), yang mengonfirmasi tingginya tingkat penerimaan pengguna. Sebagai kesimpulan, sistem rekomendasi ini terbukti efektif memecahkan masalah asimetri informasi dan memberikan solusi perawatan kulit yang terpersonalisasi.

papers.title: Analysis of the Rectoral Resolutions of the Universidad Atlántida Argentina that integrate the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in teaching and university management
papers.authors: Leonardo Pablo Palacios
papers.abstract: La irrupción masiva de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (IAGen) ha planteado un desafío sin precedentes para el sistema universitario global. En la República Argentina, ante la ausencia de marcos regulatorios nacionales específicos, las instituciones han debido asumir un rol proactivo en la creación de sus propios protocolos de gobernanza. El presente trabajo analiza el caso de la Universidad Atlántida Argentina (UAA) y su Resolución Rectoral 231/25, la cual establece lineamientos éticos y pedagógicos alineados con los estándares de la UNESCO y la Ley Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales (N.º 25.326). A través de un enfoque descriptivo, se examina cómo la universidad busca integrar estas herramientas no como meros instrumentos de productividad, sino como entornos de mediación para el pensamiento humano. Asimismo, se plantean reflexiones críticas sobre la eficacia real de la regulación en un contexto de obsolescencia tecnológica acelerada y las dudas persistentes sobre la integridad académica frente a la limitada fiabilidad de los sistemas de detección algorítmica.

papers.title: PM-USHA International Conference Series – जञनसत (Jñānasetu): The Bridge of KnowledgeARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE FUTURE OF COMMERCE
papers.authors: Krupa Bhatt, Sakshi Saxena
papers.journal: Journal of Informatics Education and Research
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming an important force in the transformation of contemporary commerce. Its applications now extend across marketing, retail, e-commerce, customer service, forecasting, decision support, supply chain management, and business operations. This paper examines the role of AI in shaping the future of commerce by synthesising existing academic literature on AI-enabled commercial transformation. The study adopts a conceptual and descriptive approach based on a narrative review of peer-reviewed secondary literature. The review focuses on five interrelated themes: personalisation and consumer engagement, predictive decision-making, intelligent automation, AI-mediated customer experience, and responsible AI governance. The synthesis indicates that AI is shifting commerce from standardised to increasingly personalised interactions, from reactive to predictive decision-making, and from predominantly manual processes towards human-AI collaboration. These developments can improve efficiency, relevance, convenience, innovation, and competitiveness. At the same time, expanded use of consumer data and algorithmic decision-making creates significant concerns related to privacy, transparency, bias, accountability, consumer autonomy, and workforce transformation. The paper argues that technological capability alone is insufficient to create sustainable commercial value. The future of commerce is likely to depend on the ability of organisations to combine AI capabilities with human judgement, consumer trust, ethical governance, and sustainability considerations. A conceptual framework is proposed in which AI-enabled capabilities influence commerce transformation and commercial outcomes, while responsible governance acts as a critical enabling condition. The paper concludes that competitive advantage in an AI-enabled economy will depend not merely on the speed of AI adoption, but on how effectively and responsibly organisations integrate AI into commercial systems and stakeholder relationships.

papers.title: Visualizing the Solar System with Generative AI: Development and Formative Evaluation of Interactive Multimedia for Lower Secondary Science
papers.authors: Hamidah Khairunnisa, Selvi Susanti, Taufik Kemas Taufik
papers.journal: Journal of Urban Development in Education
papers.abstract: The solar system is an abstract topic that lower secondary learners often find difficult, and generative artificial intelligence (AI) now allows teachers to author rich multimedia without programming. This study developed an interactive multimedia package on the solar system for Grade VII science and formatively evaluated how learners received it. Following the ADDIE model, the authors used Canva, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Pippit AI to produce interactive slides, explanatory texts, quiz items, and narrated videos, hosted a gamified quiz on Wayground, and checked all content during finalization. In a small group trial at an early development stage, five Grade VII learners rated 20 statements on a four point scale covering display, content, interactivity, benefit, and ease of use. The overall mean was 3.41 (85.25% of the maximum score), and no learner disagreed with any statement. Display received the highest rating (M = 3.65) and interactivity the lowest (M = 3.20). These results indicated preliminary learner acceptance rather than learning effectiveness. The study documented a transparent workflow for AI supported authoring and identified expert validation, manipulable simulations, and controlled trials with larger samples as priorities for the next cycle.

papers.title: Thoughts on Artificial Intelligence for Teachers
papers.authors: GYARMATI G. Péter
papers.abstract: In this lecture, we approach from a new aspect the sources and the expected development of artificial intelligence.
