Our starting point is still human creation, which is driven by common sense, the striving for omnipotence of power, and the unlimited nature of the capitalist economy. Artificial intelligence is based on the anthropomorphic model according to the current state of science, i.e., it tries to imitate human thinking and behavior. The basis of human intelligence is the human brain, and the computer for artificial intelligence. People organize themselves into societies according to rules and morality. Common sense contradicts the need to provide machines with such self-organizing ability, and human goals do not require it. This performance tries to explore the difference and possible convergence of the two intelligences. At the same time, it always establishes the superiority and responsibility of man. The unethical, the destruction, is caused by man, the power, even if it is done by machines with intelligence.

papers.title: CABARAN GURU BAHASA MELAYU DALAM MENGAPLIKASIKAN TEKNOLOGI DIGITAL SEMASA PROSES PENGAJARAN DAN PEMBELAJARAN: SATU TINJAUAN LITERATUR BERSISTEMATIK (The Challenges Faced by Malay Language Teachers in Applying Digital Technology During the Teaching and Learning Process: A Systematic Literature Review)
papers.authors: ROSSIDA JOEY, NURUL FATIHAH ISMUNI, JENARTHNA SELVATHURAI, MATHURI KUNASEKARAN
papers.abstract: ABSTRAK: Pengintegrasian teknologi digital dalam proses pengajaran dan pembelajaran (PdP) Bahasa Melayu semakin diberi perhatian selaras dengan perkembangan pendidikan abad ke-21 dan transformasi pendidikan digital negara. Walau bagaimanapun, guru Bahasa Melayu masih berhadapan dengan pelbagai cabaran dalam mengaplikasikan teknologi digital secara berkesan semasa PdP. Oleh itu, kajian ini bertujuan untuk mengenal pasti jenis teknologi digital yang digunakan oleh guru Bahasa Melayu, meneliti cabaran yang dihadapi dalam mengaplikasikan teknologi digital serta menghuraikan cara guru mengatasi cabaran tersebut. Kajian ini menggunakan pendekatan Sorotan Literatur Sistematik (Systematic Literature Review, SLR) berpandukan garis panduan PRISMA. Sebanyak 15 artikel jurnal yang diterbitkan antara tahun 2021 hingga 2025 dan memenuhi kriteria inklusi telah dipilih serta dianalisis secara tematik. Dapatan kajian menunjukkan bahawa platform pembelajaran digital, aplikasi kolaboratif dan produktiviti digital, multimedia digital, aplikasi gamifikasi serta media sosial dan komunikasi digital merupakan teknologi yang dominan digunakan dalam PdP Bahasa Melayu. Cabaran utama yang dihadapi guru ialah kesukaran mengintegrasikan teknologi digital dalam PdP, kekurangan pengetahuan dan kemahiran digital, kekangan internet dan kemudahan teknologi, kekangan teknikal dan penyediaan bahan digital, penglibatan serta kesediaan murid, dan cabaran penggunaan teknologi baharu seperti kecerdasan buatan (Artificial Intelligence-AI). Bagi mengatasi cabaran tersebut, guru mengaplikasikan pelbagai strategi seperti memperkukuh latihan dan kolaborasi profesional, meningkatkan kompetensi digital, melaksanakan PdP yang interaktif dan berpusatkan murid, menambah baik akses teknologi serta memanfaatkan gamifikasi dan multimedia digital. Kajian ini memberikan implikasi bahawa pembangunan kompetensi digital guru dan penyediaan infrastruktur teknologi yang mencukupi perlu diperkukuh bagi memastikan keberkesanan pengintegrasian teknologi digital dalam PdP Bahasa Melayu.Kata kunci: Teknologi Digital, Guru Bahasa Melayu, Pengajaran dan Pembelajaran, Sorotan Literatur Sistematik, Pendidikan DigitalABSTRACT: The integration of digital technology in Malay language teaching and learning has gained increasing attention in line with the advancement of 21st-century education and the national digital education transformation agenda. Nevertheless, Malay language teachers continue to face various challenges in effectively implementing digital technology during the teaching and learning process. Therefore, this study aims to identify the types of digital technologies used by Malay language teachers, examine the challenges encountered in integrating digital technology, and explore the strategies employed to overcome these challenges. This study adopted a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach guided by the PRISMA framework. A total of 15 journal articles published between 2021 and 2025 that met the inclusion criteria were selected and analysed thematically. The findings revealed that digital learning platforms, collaborative and productivity applications, digital multimedia, gamification applications, and social media and digital communication tools were among the most frequently used technologies in Malay language teaching and learning. The major challenges identified include difficulties in integrating digital technology into teaching practices, limited digital knowledge and skills among teachers, inadequate internet access and technological facilities, technical issues and digital material preparation, student engagement and readiness, as well as challenges associated with emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI). To address these challenges, teachers employed various strategies, including strengthening professional training and collaboration, enhancing digital competencies, implementing interactive and student-centred teaching approaches, improving access to technological resources, and utilising gamification and digital multimedia. The study implies that continuous development of teachers’ digital competencies and adequate technological infrastructure are essential to ensure the effective integration of digital technology in Malay language teaching and learning.Keywords: Digital Technology, Malay Language Teachers, Teaching and Learning, Systematic LiteratureReview, Digital Education

papers.title: A Critical Epistemological Audit of Early Evidence Syntheses in Generative AI Educational Research: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.authors: Peter Gerjets, Jochen Kühn, Lisa Bardach, Michael Sailer, Detmar Meurers, Valentin Emslander, Nina Peltzer, John hattie, Mark Warschauer, Tim Fütterer, Tamara Tate
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of ChatGPT in education was accompanied by an equally rapid proliferation of meta-analyses synthesizing its effects on educational outcomes. We conducted a systematic epistemological audit of the first wave of these meta-analyses, evaluating both their methodological and reporting quality and the primary evidence they synthesized. We included meta-analyses published after the release of ChatGPT that quantitatively synthesized its effects on educational outcomes. Five meta-analyses comprising 87 unique primary studies met our inclusion criteria. We also reconstructed their quantitative evidence base and conducted exploratory three-level random-effects meta-analyses to examine effect magnitude, heterogeneity, and robustness, and how these varied with theoretically and methodologically relevant characteristics. The five meta-analyses generally searched multiple databases, specified eligibility criteria, and examined heterogeneity and potential publication bias, but showed limitations in independent screening and coding, preregistration, open data and code, and transparent reporting. The underlying primary evidence likewise showed methodological and reporting limitations and substantial conceptual heterogeneity. Among 69 classifiable primary studies, 79.7% assessed performance exclusively, whereas only 11.6% assessed learning exclusively. The reconstructed meta-analysis yielded a positive average effect (g = 0.83, 95% CI [0.68, 0.97]), but heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 94.06%; 95% prediction interval [−0.75, 2.41]), and estimates were markedly attenuated in sensitivity analyses addressing small-study and selection effects. Although positive effects remained among stronger studies assessing learning, increasingly stringent quality criteria rapidly reduced the evidence base, limiting the certainty and generalizability of conclusions about learning effects. Overall, our findings caution against interpreting a single pooled estimate as a stable general effect of ChatGPT on learning and highlight the need for more rigorous, conceptually precise, transparent, and reproducible research.

papers.title: Using a Learning Progression Framework to Guide LLM-Based Formative Assessment in STEM Education
papers.authors: Karen D. Wang, Jialin Li, Carl Wieman, Leonora Kaldaras

papers.title: Evaluating the Pedagogical Quality of LLM-Generated Feedback: A Criterion-Based and Comparative Study
papers.authors: Harvey Ngoe Kolle, Carrie Demmans Epp, Amna Liaqat, Maria Cutumisu

papers.title: Consumer Artificial Intelligence for Pedigree Analysis: A Comparative Study in Medical Genetics
papers.authors: Seba S. Abduljabbar, Mohammed Alqarni, Alawi Habara
papers.abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in medical education, but their ability to analyze pedigree-based genetics problems is not well defined.This exploratory study aimed to compare the accuracy of four consumer LLMs on image-based pedigree questions and to describe the sources of their errors.Methods: Nine pedigree cases comprising 19 sub-questions were submitted as images on May 18, 2026, to the free consumer versions of ChatGPT (GPT-5.5),Gemini (Gemini 3 Flash), Claude (Claude Sonnet 4.6), and the Microsoft Copilot app, once each in a new chat, without retries or follow-up prompts.The primary measure was accuracy, defined as the number and percentage of sub-questions answered correctly against a predefined answer key reviewed by a medical geneticist.Item-level scores were re-checked during revision using uniform rules.Incorrect answers were retrospectively classified as perception/structure, reasoning/knowledge, mixed or indeterminate errors, or as reported image-access failures.Results: ChatGPT and Claude each answered 14 of 19 sub-questions correctly (73.7%),Copilot 11 (57.9%), and Gemini three (15.8%).Twelve of Gemini's 16 incorrect answers followed its report that it could not see or load the image.Claude's errors in the double-cousin pedigrees reflected misreading of the mating lines, whereas ChatGPT's mainly involved assigning the degree of relationship.In the single atypical pedigree (dominantly inherited hemoglobin S-Oman), no model identified the variant; Claude described dominant features but attributed them to pseudodominance because sickle cell disease is recessive.Conclusions: In this small, single-attempt task set without statistical comparison, consumer LLMs showed variable accuracy, and errors arose both from misreading pedigrees and from misapplying genetic principles.These results do not establish a ranking of the models or an educational benefit.Consumer AI assistants should complement, not replace, formal instruction and expert supervision in medical genetics.

papers.title: Role of the digital specialist community public health nurse: reimagining community nursing in the AI-enabled public health landscape
papers.authors: Michelle Lorraine Vizard
papers.abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are redefining how people access and navigate community healthcare. Concurrently, community nursing services are facing a sustained workforce decline. While digital nurse leadership has matured in many acute organisations, community nurses are increasingly expected to deliver technology-enabled care without equivalent leadership structures, support or career pathways. In this article, the author details a proposal for a digital specialist community public health nurse (digital SCPHN) role framework. The author describes the digital SCPHN as first and foremost a clinician, with digital capability as an essential enhancement rather than a replacement of core nursing objectives. Positioned as a digital translator and champion within community teams, the digital SCPHN helps people to navigate complex digital healthcare systems while supporting their colleagues through technology-enabled care prioritisation, secure safeguarding communication and community risk insight. The author also outlines six actionable recommendations for front-line nurses, team leads and system commissioners to strengthen community nursing impact, improve digital literacy and ensure equitable, person-centred care in digitally enabled neighbourhood healthcare systems.

papers.title: Reimagining Media Studies Education in Pakistan through Artificial Intelligence: Curriculum Integration, Competencies, and Challenges
papers.authors: Syed Waqar Ul Hasan, Muhammad Aftab Madni, Taha Shabbir
papers.abstract: This paper studies how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping media studies education in Pakistan. It uses primary policy data from the Higher Education Commission (HEC), mainly the 2025 revised curriculum for Media and Communication Studies and the national decision to make AI a compulsory course, together with recent international research. The paper shows that AI has moved from the edges of the media curriculum to its centre. In the new HEC scheme, a three-credit course called “AI & Data Analytics in Media” is mandatory for every undergraduate student, a Data Journalism course sits in the core, and a full specialization in Data and Computational Journalism is offered as an option. Drawing on competency frameworks from UNESCO and leading scholars, the paper sets out the knowledge, skills, and values that media graduates now need: understanding AI, using AI tools responsibly, reading data and algorithms, judging AI outputs, and keeping ethics and human judgement central. The paper then explains the real problems that stand in the way, including weak infrastructure and the digital divide, limited teacher training, academic integrity worries, weak support for Urdu and regional languages, and the difficulty of enforcing bans. It closes with practical steps for universities, teachers, and policymakers. The main argument is simple: Pakistan has taken an important first step on paper, but turning policy into real classroom learning will decide whether the reform succeeds.

papers.title: Preparing Teachers to Assess in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Critical Integrative Review and Framework for Assessment-AI Knowledge
papers.authors: Konstantinos Τ. Kotsis
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, changes assessment by altering the evidential relationship among student work, learning, and professional judgment. Teachers must design tasks when students can readily obtain machine-generated responses, interpret automated feedback and analytics whose validity is conditional, and justify consequential decisions under uncertainty. This critical integrative review synthesizes scholarship on AI in education, assessment, teacher learning, and emerging professional-development interventions. It proposes Assessment-AI Knowledge (A-AIK) as an assessment-specific configuration of professional knowledge rather than a replacement for assessment literacy, AI literacy, or technological pedagogical content knowledge. A-AIK comprises three interdependent capacities: design competence, which establishes conditions for eliciting meaningful evidence; interpretive competence, which calibrates the meaning, uncertainty, and evidential weight of AI-mediated information; and justificatory competence, which supports transparent, fair, and reviewable decisions. Disciplinary authenticity, human agency, equity, transparency and data governance, and epistemic humility operate as cross-cutting commitments. The reviewed literature suggests that promising interventions use scenarios, authentic assessment redesign, structured critique, peer deliberation, and iterative classroom trials. Recurrent limitations include small samples, reliance on self-report, short duration, and measures of confidence or acceptance rather than demonstrated assessment performance. A four-phase professional-learning model—calibrate, redesign, enact, and justify, is proposed as a synthesis-informed design hypothesis requiring empirical evaluation. The article concludes with provisional performance indicators, institutional conditions, and a research agenda for responsible AI-mediated assessment.

papers.title: AI and Journalism: Exploring Ethics, Transparency and Self-Regulation among Pakistani TV Journalists
papers.authors: Adiba Akhtar, Naeem Ullah Tariq, Aqeel Ahmed, Nur Nadia Abd Mubin
papers.journal: Print Radio TV and Film Studies
papers.abstract: Aim of the Study: Newsrooms are increasingly integrating artificial intelligence (AI) for their news operations in the evolving journalistic landscape. The journalists have started realizing AI as a collaborative assistant that can facilitate them in effective execution of their professional tasks. Despite various prospects, adoption of AI may pose several challenges for the journalism professionals including that of ethical implications, transparency and self-regulation to ensure objectivity. Methodology: Guided by the social responsibility theory, this research has analyzed integration of AI into newsroom operations with its implications for media ethics. This qualitative study involved in-depth interviews of 13 journalists, dealing with the news operations at various levels in Pakistani TV News Organizations (Urdu/English Channels). While reaching the data saturation, the documented responses were thematically analyzed. Findings: The findings of the research reveal that Pakistani TV journalists face ethical challenges related to information bias, public opinion influence, human judgement, professional autonomy, and lack of appropriate legal and global regulatory framework in the age of AI. Conclusion: The study concludes that the journalists are aware of the challenges posed by AI technologies with the consideration for their cautious execution.

papers.title: From Cognitive Augmentation to Learning Alienation: A Conceptual Framework of Generative AI Overdependence in Higher Education
papers.authors: Chen Wang
papers.journal: International Theory and Practice in Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: A polished assignment reveals little about what its author has learned. This conceptual article examines university students' relationship with academic work when generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) takes on part of it. Through purposive theory synthesis, it connects alienation with distributed cognition, self-regulation, and automation research. Delegating execution differs from delegating evaluation; either can support learning when the activities needed to develop the intended capability remain. Overdependence denotes persistent reliance despite demands or feedback calling for greater participation. The framework distinguishes four forms of estrangement: from reasoning, intellectual direction, developmental meaning, and warranted responsibility for an attributed contribution. Each requires the learner's experience and corroborating evidence, not simply usage counts, dependency scores, or assisted–unaided performance gaps. Nine propositions examine conditional pathways while allowing prior alienation, shared institutional causes, and recovery. The research agenda separates capability from learning relations and compares competing temporal explanations. Teaching proposals center on accessible explanation, revision, and transfer. The framework and its evidence rules remain unvalidated; they are not diagnostic criteria.

papers.title: AI Adoption and Dynamic Capabilities in Chinese SMEs: the Mediating Role of Digital Entrepreneurial Orientation—A Conceptual Framework
papers.authors: Depeng Pan
papers.journal: Journal of Economic Theory and Business Management
papers.abstract: This paper develops a conceptual framework that examines how artificial intelligence (AI) adoption may influence dynamic capabilities in Chinese small and mediumsized enterprises (SMEs), with digital entrepreneurial orientation (DEO) as a proposed mediating mechanism. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the digital entrepreneurship literature, the paper argues that AI adoption does not automatically translate into dynamic capabilities. Rather, AI adoption may foster DEO—comprising digital innovativeness, digital proactiveness, and digital risktaking—which in turn may help firms sense opportunities, seize them, and reconfigure resources. Three testable propositions are developed. The framework contributes to dynamic capabilities theory by specifying DEO as a strategic mediating pathway through which AI resources may be converted into organizational capabilities. It also offers implications for SME managers and policymakers seeking to support digital transformation under resource constraints.

papers.title: Institutional Pressures and AI Adoption in Chinese SMEs: a Neo-Institutional Analysis with Propositions
papers.authors: Depeng Pan
papers.journal: Journal of Economic Theory and Business Management
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption has become a strategic imperative for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the digital economy. In China, however, SMEs frequently exhibit a pronounced gap between AI awareness and sustained adoption. This paper applies neo-institutional theory—specifically DiMaggio and Powell's model of institutional isomorphism—to examine how coercive, normative, and mimetic pressures shape AI adoption among Chinese SMEs. Adopting a conceptual theory-building approach, the paper develops an integrated framework in which institutional pressures influence AI adoption intention through legitimacy-seeking motives, while organizational capability and resource endowments moderate whether adoption becomes substantive or symbolic. The analysis identifies a legitimacy–capability paradox: institutional pressures may accelerate initial AI experimentation while simultaneously encouraging decoupled, compliance-oriented adoption. The paper contributes to institutional theory and technology adoption research by explaining not only why Chinese SMEs adopt AI but also how they adopt it. Seven propositions and five analytical tables are developed to guide future empirical research.

papers.title: AI Implementation and Business Model Innovation in Chinese SMEs: a Configurational Research Framework
papers.authors: Depeng Pan
papers.journal: Academic Journal of Sociology and Management
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly regarded as a critical enabler of business model innovation (BMI) in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). However, existing research predominantly examines the net effect of AI adoption on BMI, overlooking the complex interactions among technological, organizational, and environmental conditions. Drawing on the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework integrated with dynamic capabilities theory, this study develops a configurational research framework for investigating how AI implementation combines with organizational capabilities and environmental conditions to drive BMI in Chinese SMEs. The framework proposes four theoretically grounded pathways to high BMI: technology–organization synergy, environment-pulled innovation, market-driven AI integration, and capability-first substitution. These propositions demonstrate that AI implementation is neither necessary nor sufficient for BMI; its effectiveness depends on alignment with dynamic capabilities and environmental support. The framework contributes to the AI–BMI literature by advancing a configurational perspective and offers a foundation for future empirical investigation using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA).

papers.title: Platform-Enabled AI Adoption and Supply Chain Resilience in Chinese SMEs: an Integrated Theoretical Framework
papers.authors: Depeng Pan
papers.journal: Academic Journal of Sociology and Management
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is profoundly reshaping the global supply chain landscape. However, the mechanism through which Chinese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), under resource constraints, acquire AI capabilities through digital platforms and transform them into supply chain resilience has not been adequately theorized. This paper develops an integrated theoretical framework that combines the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework with dynamic capability theory. It proposes the analytical concept of “platform-enabled AI adoption" to characterize the distinctive technology adoption pattern through which Chinese SMEs acquire, integrate, and utilize AI capabilities via external digital platforms. Using a literature review and case analysis approach, and drawing on the 2025 survey report of the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, publicly available operating data from the 1688 platform and Haizhi Online, and relevant academic literature from the past decade, this paper systematically analyzes three mediating pathways through which platform-enabled AI adoption affects supply chain resilience: supply chain visibility, supply chain agility, and supply chain collaboration. It further discusses the moderating roles of technological readiness and organizational readiness in this relationship and offers methodological suggestions for future empirical research. This paper provides a theoretical foundation for understanding the relationship between AI adoption and supply chain resilience among Chinese SMEs in the digital platform context and offers testable research propositions for subsequent empirical examination.

papers.title: O papel da inteligência artificial na pipeline completo de efeitos visuais no cinema contemporâneo
papers.authors: Romualdo Amaral
papers.abstract: This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) across the complete visual effects (VFX) production pipeline in contemporary cinema, emphasizing the practical integration of machine learning (ML) techniques into pre-production, production, and post-production. It argues that AI has become a set of supporting tools integrated into established VFX workflows, including camera and object tracking, rotoscoping (roto), digital paint and object removal, simulation, rendering, compositing, and final delivery, reducing operational challenges and expanding opportunities for creative experimentation. The analysis draws on technical sources (SIGGRAPH/ACM), official tool documentation, and institutional guidelines addressing professional credits, intellectual property, consent, and digital replicas. When quantitative data on time and cost savings are not publicly available in sufficient detail, this limitation is explicitly acknowledged, with emphasis placed on qualitative evidence and documented technical mechanisms.

papers.title: Inteligência artificial aplicada à prevenção, ao diagnóstico e ao cuidado de pessoas vivendo com HIV: desafios éticos, evidências científicas e perspectivas para a enfermagem brasileira
papers.authors: Patrick Barcelos dos Santos Barbosa, Leandro Teixeira Ghilardi
papers.abstract: This article analyzed scientific evidence on the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to HIV prevention, diagnosis, and care, emphasizing ethical challenges and perspectives for Brazilian nursing. An integrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO, the Virtual Health Library/LILACS, and DOI tracking mechanisms, including publications from 2015 to August 2026 in Portuguese, English, or Spanish. Twenty-five studies with verifiable DOI were selected, covering machine-learning applications for risk stratification and pre-exposure prophylaxis indication, automated interpretation of rapid tests, prediction of adherence, disengagement and viral suppression, counseling support, and algorithmic equity. Findings showed that AI can broaden the identification of priority populations, support clinical decisions, improve diagnostic interpretation, and enable personalized interventions during therapeutic follow-up. However, data bias, model opacity, privacy, stigma, information security, and technological dependence require governance, local validation, and professional oversight. It was concluded that Brazilian nursing can play a strategic role in the responsible implementation of these technologies by combining clinical judgment, health education, data protection, and person-centered care.

papers.title: Transformasi Pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam di Era Digital: Integrasi Keterampilan Abad Ke-21 dan Nilai-Nilai Islam
papers.authors: Sitti Ratna Dewi Rahmatia, La Ode Muhamad Arafat
papers.journal: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
papers.abstract: Transformasi pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) menjadi kebutuhan strategis di tengah perkembangan teknologi digital, perubahan karakteristik peserta didik, dan tuntutan kompetensi abad ke-21. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis bentuk transformasi pembelajaran PAI di era digital dan merumuskan pola integrasi keterampilan 4C (critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, dan communication) dengan nilai-nilai Islam. Penelitian menggunakan metode library research dengan pendekatan kualitatif-deskriptif. Sumber kajian meliputi artikel ilmiah yang relevan, buku metodologi dan pendidikan, regulasi pendidikan, serta dokumen kebijakan dan kerangka kompetensi digital. Analisis dilakukan melalui content analysis dengan tahapan seleksi sumber, pengodean tema, kategorisasi, interpretasi, dan sintesis. Hasil kajian menunjukkan tiga perubahan utama: transformasi media pembelajaran melalui LMS, video interaktif, media digital dan AI; transformasi pedagogi dari teacher-centered menuju student-centered learning; serta transformasi peran guru menjadi fasilitator, kurator sumber, dan pembimbing etika digital. Integrasi 4C dengan nilai Islam dapat dilakukan melalui prinsip fathanah dan tabayyun untuk berpikir kritis, ijtihad dan kreativitas untuk menghasilkan gagasan, ta’awun dan syura untuk kolaborasi, serta tabligh dan qaulan ma‘rufa untuk komunikasi. Artikel ini menawarkan model Blended Learning Berbasis Nilai (BLBN) sebagai kerangka konseptual yang menempatkan teknologi sebagai sarana, sedangkan pembentukan akhlak, tanggung jawab, dan kedalaman spiritual sebagai orientasi. Model tersebut dapat dikembangkan secara fleksibel sesuai karakteristik peserta didik, infrastruktur, tujuan pembelajaran, dan konteks satuan pendidikan.

papers.title: METHODOLOGICAL SYSTEM FOR DEVELOPING STUDENTS' TECHNICAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL COMPETENCE IN A DIGITAL LEARNING ENVIRONMENT
papers.authors: N Orınbetov
papers.journal: “ADVANCED JOURNAL OF UNIVERSITY SCIENCE AND CREATIVE INNOVATIONS” AJOU SCI
papers.abstract: The article discusses the formation of technical and technological readiness of students based on the competence approach, and analyzes the main directions of applying artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and digital technology tools to the educational process in the formation of technical and technological readiness of students and recommendations on effective use of social networks are given.

papers.title: COGNITIVE-DISCURSIVE EXERCISES FOR INTERCULTURAL CHINESE LANGUAGE TEACHING: INTEGRATING HUMAN JUDGMENT AND GENERATIVE AI
papers.authors: S.A. Nazarova
papers.journal: “ADVANCED JOURNAL OF UNIVERSITY SCIENCE AND CREATIVE INNOVATIONS” AJOU SCI
papers.abstract: This article develops the methodological rationale for a cognitive-discursive exercise system intended to foster intercultural communicative competence among students majoring in Chinese philology and examines opportunities for human–AI collaboration in its implementation. The set of 36 formative exercises connects the cognitive-interpretive, affectivevalue and behavioural-discursive components of competence. The instructional sequence moves from understanding a communicative situation and comparing interpretations to selecting a strategy, putting it into practice and adapting it to new conditions. Utterances are examined in relation to speaker intention, participant relationships, intonation and nonverbal behaviour. Students first formulate their own response, then critically assess AI-generated alternatives and justify their revisions. AI serves as a resource for exploring and comparing communicative options rather than an authority on cultural norms. The methodological contribution consists of a classroom procedure and formative assessment criteria; the system’s effectiveness requires separate empirical investigation.

papers.title: Beyond Digital Adab: A Conceptual Model of Ta’dib-Oriented Character Pedagogy in Islamic Education
papers.authors: Abidul Haq, MUHAMMAD KHAQIM
papers.abstract: Digital Islamic learning presents challenges involving unverified religious claims, artificial intelligence outputs, privacy concerns, and unequal access. This study aims to reconstruct the philosophy of ta’dib as a conceptual foundation for character education in digitally mediated Islamic learning. It employs a qualitative conceptual approach through purposive document analysis and an integrative synthesis of literature on educational philosophy and digital ethics. The findings propose the Ta’dib-Oriented Digital Character Pedagogy (TDCP) model, comprising five dimensions: epistemic integrity, dignified interaction, responsible digital agency, equitable participation, and reflective self-discipline. These dimensions are implemented through a cycle of inquiry, deliberation, action, and reflection to support formative assessment and protect learner privacy. The model offers a pedagogical framework for developing ethical reasoning without equating observable behavior with piety. Expert validation and empirical testing are needed to assess its applicability in educational settings.

papers.title: Optimización de la predicción de retención estudiantil en la educación superior: un análisis comparativo de modelos de aprendizaje automático supervisados y no supervisado
papers.authors: Franklin Iván Argueta Bermúdez, Wilber Alexander Ortiz Cortez, Miguel García Torres
papers.journal: Revista Ciencia Tecnología e Innovación en Ingeniería y Arquitectura (CTI-FIA)
papers.abstract: This research addresses the problem of student dropout in higher education in El Salvador, using machine learning models. To do so, a historical dataset from a private university was used, which includes more than 83,000 student records between the years 2019 and 2024. In the exploratory analysis phase, unsupervised techniques such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means, and hierarchical clustering were applied to segment students and identify profiles with similar demographic, academic, and economic characteristics. Subsequently, supervised predictive models were implemented, including SVM, KNN, Random Forest, AdaBoost, and XGBoost, evaluating their performance using metrics such as accuracy and AUC-ROC. The results indicated that Random Forest offers greater predictive capacity, while clustering techniques allowed identifying risk groups without the need for prior labels. It was observed that students enrolled in in-person classes, with low academic performance and self-funded programs, are more likely to drop out. The research concludes that the combination of exploratory analysis and predictive models facilitates the design of effective strategies to improve student retention. Furthermore, it highlights the value of institutional use of these tools to develop proactive interventions, especially those targeting first-year students or those with vulnerable academic and economic circumstances.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Sustainable Entrepreneurship: Redefining Business Leadership, Marketing Excellence, and Governance Practices
papers.authors: Santanu Roy, Dr. R Ganesh Kumar, Prof. Abhijeet Wairagade, Dr. Panduarng Sudamrao Dabhade, Ajay Bhushan Prasad
papers.journal: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
papers.abstract: The advent of generative AI is having a profound impact on entrepreneurial strategy, organizational innovation, leadership, and long-term competitive performance. This study explored the impact of the adoption of artificial intelligence on the process of entrepreneurial transformation toward sustainability in terms of leadership support, business model innovation, sustainable competitive advantage, institutional support, cost effectiveness, and firm performance. The study adopted a quantitative secondary-data design and had a managerial dataset of 325 observations. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling was utilised to assess the measurement reliability, construct validity, structural linkages, explanatory power, and indirect effects. It was discovered that the measurement model had acceptable Average Variance and Cronbach's alpha values over 0.80. extracted values greater than 0.65, demonstrating convergent validity and adequate dependability. The structural results indicated that the use of AI had significant impacts on business model innovation, sustainable competitive advantage, and firm performance. The top direct result of business model innovation was that it created a firm's strongest direct link to its performance, followed by sustainable competitive advantage. AI adoption was strongly encouraged by leadership support, and government support had positive impacts on AI adoption, leadership support and cost effectiveness. Important indirect effects also suggested that AI has impacts on organizational performance via innovation and sustainable competitive capability. The overall results indicate that the strategic contribution of AI is highly reliant on leadership, innovation, institutional support, and responsible organizational practices.

papers.title: Integrating Multimodal Technologies and Generative Artificial Intelligence into Professionally Oriented English Language Training of Future Officers of the Armed Forces of Ukraine: Theoretical Foundations
papers.authors: Ганна Жиздюк
papers.abstract: The article aims to substantiate the theoretical foundations for integrating multimodal technologies and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into cadets' English language training oriented towards the descriptors of Standardized Language Proficiency Level 2 under the NATO standard STANAG 6001. The study used terminological and comparative analysis of regulatory documents and research publications, systematisation, generalisation and pedagogical design. The conceptual framework is refined: language activity and its types, language competence, standardized language level and profile, mode, multimodal technologies, GenAI, AI-mediated learning, the mode of permissible GenAI use, and integration. The standardized language profile is treated as a measure of general foreign language proficiency in the four types of language activity that does not cover all components of professional communicative competence. The Law of Ukraine "On Academic Integrity" links the legitimacy of auxiliary tools to the rules of a task, so the GenAI mode stated in a task instruction has legal significance. The study substantiates seven functions of multimodal technologies and GenAI with limits of assistance, eight integration principles and four modes of GenAI use, which differ in what GenAI does with the cadet's language material and can be combined. Five pedagogical conditions are defined with organisational support and indicators of implementation. A six-step sequence of scenario-based learning is proposed and illustrated with the task design "Reporting an Equipment Problem before a Joint Training Session": a photo shows the equipment damage, the cadet explains the circumstances orally and in writing, GenAI only asks clarifying questions, and the cadet conducts the final conversation without AI or preparation in a new situation with different equipment, addressee and constraints; the control stages without AI are performed in class under the instructor's supervision. The novelty lies in the theoretical and methodological specification of known approaches for future officers' English language training; provisions borrowed from the DARE-HS (Descriptor Alignment, Authentic Performance, Responsible Use, Evaluation and Reflection, Human Supervision, Security) framework and other studies are clearly distinguished from adapted and proposed ones. Language instructors at higher military educational institutions can use the results to design tasks for the penultimate semester, formulate GenAI rules in course syllabi and develop professional development programmes. The effectiveness of the proposed solutions requires empirical verification.

papers.title: Academic integrity among higher education students in the era of generative artificial intelligence: pedagogical strategies and institutional approaches
papers.authors: Вікторія Залізнюк, Olha Diachenko, Костянтин Артюшок
papers.abstract: Purpose. To determine how higher education students use generative artificial intelligence, examine the associated risks to academic integrity, and assess the extent to which institutional and pedagogical response mechanisms align with student practices. Methods. The study employed a secondary analysis of published empirical data from 2024–2026. The study compared quantitative indicators across years, specifically identifying changes in percentage points. The study analyzed regulations governing the use of artificial intelligence in higher education institutions thematically. To summarize the findings, the study compared issues related to the use of generative artificial intelligence with institutional and pedagogical response mechanisms. The samples from different studies were not statistically combined. Results. British students' use of generative artificial intelligence in assessed assignments has risen to nearly 100 percent, and the direct inclusion of generated text is steadily increasing. In the U.S., the estimated prevalence of academic dishonesty is higher among daily users of generative AI and varies by field, although a causal relationship has not been established. It was found that the widespread use of AI is accompanied by a lack of AI literacy and insufficient support from instructors, and Ukrainian students (using medical education as an example), while noting the risks of unreliable information, remain undecided regarding the acceptability of using AI. The study systematized pedagogical strategies (developing AI literacy, critically evaluating content, establishing rules for use, and adapting assessment methods) and analyzed documents from Ukrainian higher education institutions. Rather than banning artificial intelligence, these documents call for disclosure, distinguishing practices in syllabi and human verification of individual contributions; however, they differ in how formally they are framed. The recommendations of Ukraine's Ministry of Education and Science and the Ministry of Digital Transformation set out principles for the responsible use of artificial intelligence. At the same time, the law on academic integrity requires disclosure of the use of generated results. We compared the problems and response mechanisms and found that most problems have a direct institutional counterpart. Conclusions. In the context of using generative artificial intelligence, ensuring academic integrity shifts from verifying the actual use of the technology to confirming authorship, which requires consistency in regulatory frameworks, competency development, and assessment design. Verifying a student's actual independence remains the least well-addressed issue.

papers.title: Formation of a culture of academic integrity of future teachers in the process of professional training
papers.authors: Anna Helesh, Andrii Zinoviiovych Ozarkiv
papers.abstract: The purpose of the study is to substantiate the structural components of the culture of academic integrity of future teachers and to determine the pedagogical conditions for its formation in the process of professional training. The study employed a structured theoretical review of scientific publications and regulatory sources, thematic content analysis, comparative analysis, systematization, and pedagogical modelling. The analytical corpus consisted of 15 sources, including 5 Ukrainian and 10 international publications, with the majority published between 2022 and 2026. The results clarify the concept of the culture of academic integrity of a future teacher as an integrative professional and personal characteristic and identify four interrelated structural components: value-motivational, cognitive, activity-behavioural, and reflective. Seven pedagogical conditions for its formation were substantiated: cross-curricular integration of integrity principles into educational programmes; practice-oriented teaching of academic writing and information literacy; problem-based, case-based, and situational learning; transparent and fair assessment; teachers' personal example and institutional consistency; development of critical thinking and responsible use of generative artificial intelligence; and formative assessment combined with reflective practices. The scientific novelty of the study lies in improving the structural representation of future teachers' integrity culture by combining value-based, cognitive, behavioural, and reflective dimensions and in systematizing pedagogical conditions in response to contemporary challenges associated with generative artificial intelligence. The practical significance of the results lies in their potential use in developing teacher-education programmes, course syllabi, learning tasks, assessment criteria, and institutional recommendations for the ethical use of digital technologies. The proposed framework may also serve as a basis for further empirical diagnostics of the level of formation of the identified components among future teachers.

papers.title: The integration of artificial intelligence in medical imaging practice: A perspective of the Nigerian radiographer
papers.authors: Archibong B.E, Paulinus S.O, Abiazie H.C, Okezie F.C
papers.journal: Journal of Radiation Medicine and Biomedical Sciences
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical imaging represents a transformative advancement in healthcare delivery, particularly within developing healthcare systems like Nigeria. This study investigated the perspectives of Nigerian radiographers in the South-South region regarding AI integration in medical imaging practice, focusing on knowledge, attitudes, current practices, and barriers to adoption. Methods: Using a descriptive cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 73 practicing radiographers with at least 3 years of experience via structured questionnaires administered through Google Forms. The questionnaire assessed their knowledge, attitudes, awareness, and willingness to adopt AI in their clinical practice. Content validity was established by experts, and reliability was confirmed (Cronbach’s α = 0.73). Microsoft Excel and the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 26.0 were used to organize the data for descriptive statistics. Results: Findings revealed high awareness of AI applications, with 78.1% of respondents familiar with AI technologies. However, only 21.9% rated their knowledge as excellent, while 42.5% considered it fair, indicating a gap between general awareness and in-depth understanding. Online resources were the primary source of AI knowledge, highlighting the need for structured educational interventions. Radiographers demonstrated predominantly positive attitudes, with 73.9% agreeing that AI would improve imaging accuracy and reduce workload. Additionally, 64.4% expressed preparedness for AI adoption, although 41.1% feared potential replacement by AI technologies. Current AI utilization was limited, with 31.5% reporting workplace use, primarily for imaging analysis (39.1%) and reporting assistance (21.7%). Despite limited implementation, 89.0% expressed willingness to undergo professional development, preferring workshops and seminars (37.0%). Significant barriers included inadequate infrastructure and high implementation costs. Conclusion: Successful AI integration requires coordinated efforts from educational institutions, professional bodies, healthcare facilities, and policymakers to address these barriers while building on radiographers' positive attitudes toward AI adoption. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Medical Imaging, Nigerian Radiographers, AI Adoption, Barriers, Perspectives

papers.title: Agency and Embodiment Provide Dissociable Benefits to Perception, Metacognition and Neural Processing During Active Sensing
papers.authors: Ziying Tang, James Dowsett, Paul H. Taylor, Dardo N. Ferreiro, Michael Pecka
papers.abstract: Abstract Metacognition, judging how reliable our own perceptual decisions are, is central to adaptive behavior. Such judgments hinge on the reliability of the sensory evidence on which that decision is based, and active sensing through self-directed exploration is known to improve perception itself. Yet, how agency, the authorship over self-initiated actions, and the processing of the sensory consequences, which is implicit to active sensing, modulate metacognition and its calibration, remains unknown. Whether physical embodiment adds to this beyond virtual exploration is similarly unclear, yet relevant both for daily life and for self-monitoring in agentic AI. Here, we combined a naturalistic auditory search paradigm with mobile electroencephalography. Twenty participants performed a target-detection task under three conditions: active embodied exploration, active screen-based exploration, and passive listening to replays of their own trials, while we obtained steady-state auditory evoked potentials (SSAEPs) to characterize stimulus-locked neural responses. We find that both agency conditions improved accuracy, metacognitive sensitivity, and overall SSAEP amplitude relative to passive listening, indicating that agency, rather than whole-body movement, drives these enhancements. Crucially, however, embodiment uniquely grounded both the target-evoked neural response and the subjects’ confidence to immediate sensory evidence. Thus, agency alone broadly enhances perceptual and neural processing, but embodiment specifically anchors confidence, neurally and behaviorally, to the present. Significance Statement How well we judge the reliability of our perception, called metacognitive sensitivity, matters more than ever, as we increasingly are presented with information passively through screens rather than gathering it actively via self-initiated exploration. Does actively seeking information sharpen self-monitoring, and does the medium (body vs. screen) matter? We show that active search enhances metacognitive sensitivity and brain responses alike, whether embodied or screen-based. Only embodied search, however, anchors self-evaluation to the present: Behaviorally, embodiment facilitates coupling of confidence tracking directly to current evidence rather than the previous trial’s outcome, while neuronally, it enhances responses in frontal brain regions during periods of heightened subjective confidence. This embodied grounding of self-monitoring may prove pivotal for building reliably agentic AI systems.

papers.title: Aging effects on retrospective and naturalistic encoding of time and their relationship with memory
papers.authors: Fran�ois Fricker, Giulia Buzi, Maelys Morantin, Franck Doidy, Patrice Clochon, Raphaël Bordas, Nathan Leroy, Arnaud D’Argembeau, Virginie van Wassenhove, Thomas Hinault
papers.abstract: Abstract In everyday life, attention is not explicitly directed toward time. Yet, we can reconstruct how long an experience lasted from the memory traces it left behind, a process intertwined with episodic memory and subjective experience. As both memory and temporal processing change with advancing age, investigating aging effects could provide critical insights on these reconstructive processes. In this study, 31 younger (aged 24±3) and 36 older (aged 69±6) healthy adults completed two EEG sessions: 1) a resting-state recording followed by an unexpected retrospective time estimation, and 2) a video-based prospective duration estimation task where participants encoded and judged the duration of 50 naturalistic videos (2-32s) varying in eventfulness. Using a cycle-by-cycle burst analysis of alpha (α: 8-12 Hz), we examined oscillatory correlates of both retrospective temporal judgement and prospective temporal processing. Behaviorally, both groups reconstructed short intervals similarly, but older adults produced longer prospective duration estimates than younger adults for longer video clips (16-32s), particularly under low-eventfulness. Regression analyses also showed that individual differences in older adults’ prospective duration judgments were influenced by both their retrospective time estimation and episodic memory abilities, especially for longer videos. At the neural level, resting-state α-burst dynamics were higher in older adults and predicted, with α-power, longer retrospective estimates in older adults. Additionally, resting-state α-burst activity predicted α-burst during video encoding in both groups. Together, these findings reveal that individual α-power and α-burst dynamics could constitute memory-based time-tracking mechanism that aging reshapes in ways that manifest behaviorally under naturalistic conditions.

papers.title: ExpertTwins: Auditable Long Horizon Scientific Panels through Grounded Expertise
papers.authors: Ali Foroughi pour, Abbas Shirinifard
papers.abstract: Abstract Multi-agent language-model systems increasingly assign roles to agents and let them deliberate. A role label, however, does not specify which evidence an agent can bring or which standard it applies before accepting a conclusion. Agents that read one another’s outputs tend to converge. We present ExpertTwins, a framework in which each seat of a scientific panel is defined by an inspectable evidence policy. Discipline seats retrieve under field-specific queries, and scientist-associated seats retrieve from attributed publications and a citation-derived scholarly neighborhood. Private initial packets, structured exchange, cited-source disclosure, deterministic quotation checks, and peer source review turn deliberation into an auditable record, which we also render as interactive idea-flow maps. Scientist associations denote publication-grounded perspectives, not replicas or endorsements of named researchers. In a nine-seat, four-turn neuroblastoma panel, 438 of 439 claims passed all attached quotation checks, and seats withdrew or defended positions when challenged on their evidence. A ten-turn panel sustained evidence acquisition and differentiated recommendations without conversational collapse. Across six base models given byte-identical initial packets, four sustained 97.9–99.8% quotation grounding, and at least 91% on every turn, whereas Haiku 4.5 failed by paraphrase and GPT-5 mini by silence. Agreement among strong models fell from 31% of claims at turn one to 5% at turn four. With follow-up questions held fixed, it stayed at 28–33% through turn three and fell to 20% only at the closing turn. Stress runs showed the collapse guardrail escalating through its full intervention ladder when consensus was forced, but missing deference to one unusually strong seat. On idea-flow maps, the forced consensus appeared as parallel lanes of identical ideas, although quotation grounding and participation balance stayed at their maxima. We also re-implemented two close published systems and ran them on matched models, seats, and questions. A multi-persona debate cited only real records, yet none of its cited sentences carried a checkable quotation and it had no way to abstain. An author-memory fusion system ran only after its fact checker was split by seat to fit in context. Its fused answer kept about two-thirds of the fact-checked specialist claims, answered 36 of 60 question parts on which our seats had abstained, and showed the reader 19% of its agents’ disagreements. In a computational pathology case study, six scientist-associated agents built distinct pipelines to predict MYCN amplification from whole-slide images. Across six base models, seat-by-model interaction explained 57% of internal variance, and internal rank poorly predicted external rank ( r = 0.18 across 36 nominees). These results establish differentiated, source-traceable scientific reasoning as an operational capability and identify the base model as a parameter that must be reported with the protocol.

papers.title: AI-driven information retrieval for individuals with physical disabilities in Nigeria: A systematic review of accessibility, user experience, and information-seeking behaviour
papers.authors: EGUNYEMI COMFORT OLUWAPELUMI, Ifeoluwa Adenike AYOOLA, Yusuf Abiodun Adeyemi
papers.journal: Aminu Kano Academic Scholars Association Multidisciplinary Journal
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming information retrieval through natural language processing, machine learning, semantic search, and intelligent interfaces. These developments offer opportunities to improve information access for persons with physical disabilities but may also create exclusion when systems fail to address users’ physical, technological, and behavioral needs This review examines literature published between 2016 and 2026 on AI-driven information retrieval, accessibility, information-seeking behavior, and information use among individuals with physical disabilities, with particular attention to Nigerian evidence. Findings indicate that persons with physical disabilities have significant educational, health, social, recreational, and personal information needs and increasingly rely on online and electronic information. Studies identify persistent barriers, including inadequate resources, inaccessible facilities, limited assistive technologies, difficulty locating information, and insufficient accommodation for them in most libraries. AI adoption in Nigerian libraries remains constrained by infrastructure, funding, skills, connectivity, ethical concerns, and institutional readiness. International evidence shows that AI can improve accessibility through adaptive interfaces, personalised retrieval, speech interaction, recommendations, and assistive technologies. However, research focuses more on visual disabilities than physical impairments. Major concerns include algorithmic bias, inaccessible interfaces, privacy and limited user participation. The review recommends collaborative user involvement in design, accessibility-focused development, and compatibility with assistive technologies, flexible search interfaces, and user-centered assessment.

papers.title: An explainable stacking ensemble machine learning model for denial-of-service attack detection
papers.authors: Halimah Muhammad Tukur, Jamilu Awwalu, Salim Ahmad, Ayuba John
papers.journal: Journal of Statistical Sciences and Computational Intelligence
papers.abstract: The evolving sophistication of cyber threats, particularly denial-of-service (DoS) and distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, poses significant challenges to the modern cybersecurity systems, availability, and reliability of digital infrastructures. These attacks often overwhelm network resources, leading to service disruptions and potential data breaches. Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDS) have been developed to mitigate such threats; however, they often struggle with scalability, detection accuracy, and interpretability, especially when processing large-scale network traffic. To address these limitations, this study proposes a stacked ensemble intrusion detection model integrating Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) classifiers as base learners, with Logistic Regression (LR) serving as the meta-learner. The framework aims to enhance detection accuracy, interpretability, and robustness against DoS and DDoS attacks. Using the CIC-IDS2017 dataset, Mutual Information (MI) was employed for optimal feature selection, ensuring the most relevant attributes were retained for training. SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) was applied to interpret the contribution of each selected feature to the model’s decision-making process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed ensemble achieves superior performance compared to individual classifiers and baseline models, with 98.83% accuracy, 96.37% precision, 99.19% recall, 97.76% F1-score, and an AUC of 0.9995. Compared with the baseline [1], accuracy improved by 3.39% and F1-score by 1.57%. SHAP analysis identified flow-based and packet-based features as key contributors in distinguishing normal and malicious traffic. Overall, combining multiple learning algorithms within a stacked ensemble, along with MI feature selection and SHAP explainability, provides a robust, transparent, and effective solution for real-time intrusion detection.

papers.title: The Shift from Google Search to ChatGPT: How Generative AI Is Changing Students’ Information-Seeking Behaviour
papers.authors: Prof. Vishwas Kenchi, Prof. Vishwas Kenchi, Rutuja More, Sarika Kore, Jay Shinde
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT is changing how students search for, understand, and verify academic information, a role long held by search engines such as Google. This study examines students’ self-reported information-seeking behaviour with Google Search and ChatGPT, covering frequency of use, purpose, first-source preference, reasons for adoption, trust, verification practice, and perceived change. A descriptive, quantitative survey was conducted using a 25-item structured Google Forms questionnaire administered to college and university students through convenience sampling (N = 200). Data were analysed using frequency and percentage analysis. Of the respondents, 73.5% use ChatGPT/AI at least once a day, and 61.2% name ChatGPT/AI as their first source for academic answers, compared with 30.6% for Google Search. Understanding concepts, faster answers, and easier explanations were the main reasons for use. Trust was conditional: 59.2% verify ChatGPT answers always or often, 59.2% have encountered incorrect or misleading output at least sometimes, and Google Search was the most common verification source (42.9%). In total, 93.9% reported at least some change in how they find information. The findings point to a hybrid, AI-assisted pattern rather than a replacement of search engines; however, they rest on self-reported data from a non-probability sample and cannot be generalised.

papers.title: Analysis of perceptions regarding career prospects and professional barriers in neurosurgery among generation Z
papers.authors: R. A. Kovalenko, A. A. Yashina, А. Yu. Ulitin, А. V. Vasilenko, A. S. Kolpakova
papers.abstract: Introduction. The generational shift in the higher medical education system highlights the need to study the career expectations and professional preferences of Generation Z, whose members constitute the majority of students and early-career specialists. The aim. To analyze the perception of neurosurgery as a specialty among Generation Z as a direction for further professional choice, assessing attitudes, motivational factors, expectations, and perceived barriers. Materials and methods. An online survey was conducted among 149 respondents (4–6th-year students, residents, postgraduate students, general practitioners, and early-career neurosurgeons). The questionnaire consisted of 23 items covering sociodemographic characteristics, factors influencing the choice of neurosurgery, barriers, expectations from professional activity, as well as engagement with social media and innovative technologies. Results. It was found that 48 % of students consider neurosurgery as a potential career path. The key motivating factors are the uniqueness of surgical procedures (78.5 %), the diversity of subspecialties (58.9 %), and the technological nature of the profession. The main barriers include psychosocial factors (responsibility, risk of burnout), and among residents – paperwork (51 %) and a lack of mentorship (44.8 %). A high demand was identified for international internships (87 %), rotations, and financial support during training. High levels of engagement with social media (76.4 %) and use of artificial intelligence (75.7 %) were recorded. Conclusion. The data obtained in the study demonstrate the need for active modernization of educational programs, taking into account the value orientations of the new generation. Priority areas should include: developing mentorship systems, integrating active rotations and internships into the curriculum, reducing documentation burdens, and introducing digital technologies into simulation-based training.

papers.title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA NA APRENDIZAGEM BASEADA EM PROBLEMAS (PBL) NA EDUCAÇÃO MÉDICA: EVIDÊNCIAS DE UMA REVISÃO NARRATIVA
papers.authors: Letícia Jochem
papers.abstract: Introdução e objetivo: A Aprendizagem Baseada em Problemas (PBL) é amplamente utilizada na educação médica por favorecer o raciocínio clínico, a aprendizagem autodirigida e a resolução de problemas. Entretanto, sua implementação demanda tempo e preparo docente para elaboração de casos e condução das tutorias. Nesse contexto, a inteligência artificial (IA) generativa emerge como ferramenta capaz de apoiar a construção de cenários clínicos, oferecer feedback em tempo real e ampliar as possibilidades de aprendizagem¹,². O objetivo deste trabalho foi sintetizar as evidências disponíveis sobre o uso da inteligência artificial generativa na Aprendizagem Baseada em Problemas (PBL) na educação médica, destacando seus potenciais benefícios, desafios e implicações para a formação de estudantes de medicina e médicos residentes.Método: Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura. Foi realizada busca estruturada na base de dados PubMed, utilizando os descritores “Artificial intelligence”, “medical students” e “Problem-based learning”, combinados pelo operador booleano AND. A busca foi realizada em junho de 2026, com recorte temporal a partir de 2020. Foram identificados 93 estudos, dos quais 11 atenderam aos critérios definidos e compuseram a análise. Foram incluídos estudos relacionados à aplicação de IA na Aprendizagem Baseada em Problemas (PBL) ou em outras metodologias ativas, com foco em estudantes de medicina ou residentes, sendo excluídos aqueles sem relação com educação médica ou PBL, além de trabalhos estritamente técnicos e duplicados.Resultados: A análise dos 11 estudos identificou evidências de que diferentes modelos de IA generativa, como ChatGPT e DeepSeek, podem favorecer o desempenho acadêmico e o raciocínio clínico de estudantes de medicina. Alguns estudos, desenvolvidos em áreas como hematologia e nefrologia, demonstraram que estudantes que utilizaram apoio de IA apresentaram melhores resultados em avaliações teóricas e maior desempenho no julgamento clínico quando comparados aos métodos tradicionais¹,². Além disso, um dos estudos sugeriu redução das diferenças de desempenho entre estudantes com distintos níveis de conhecimento prévio³. Por outro lado, também foram identificados desafios relacionados ao uso dessa tecnologia. Em alguns contextos, os estudantes utilizam a IA de forma passiva, apenas para obter respostas prontas, reduzindo o esforço cognitivo e podendo comprometer o processo de aprendizagem⁴. Assim, o uso adequado da IA no PBL depende de uma abordagem ativa, que estimule o debate e o raciocínio crítico. Também foi observado que o ensino sobre ética em IA contribui para que os estudantes compreendam as limitações da tecnologia, incluindo possíveis erros, vieses e respostas imprecisas, promovendo uma postura mais crítica e segura em sua utilização na prática médica⁵.Conclusão: A IA generativa apresenta potencial para qualificar o PBL, favorecendo o desempenho acadêmico, o raciocínio clínico e a personalização da aprendizagem. Entretanto, sua utilização deve ocorrer de forma ética e supervisionada, de modo a estimular o pensamento crítico e evitar a dependência tecnológica. Estudos adicionais são necessários para avaliar seus impactos a longo prazo na formação médica.

papers.title: استكشاف استخدام أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تعلم اللغة الإنجليزية والأدب واللغة الإنجليزية لأغراض محددة
papers.authors: Arwa Harith Hasan
papers.abstract: This study aims to reveal the difference in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools between students studying English in English departments and students in non-English departments. The researcher adopted a qualitative approach. The study sample consisted of 5 students from the Department of English Language and Literature, 5 students from the Department of Translation, 5 students from the Department of Arabic Language, 5 students from the Department of History, and 5 students from the Department of Anthropology and Sociology at the College of Arts, Al-Mustansiriya University, during the second semester of the 2025–2026 academic year

papers.title: CHATBOTS IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE LEARNING: A SYSTEMATIC ANALYTICAL REVIEW OF APPLICATIONS, EFFECTIVENESS, CHALLENGES, AND PEDAGOGICAL IMPLICATIONS
papers.authors: Saif Ali Hussein Al-Ardaw
papers.abstract: شهدت بيئات تعلم اللغة الإنكليزية تحولًا متسارعًا نتيجة تطور الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي وروبوتات المحادثة القائمة على النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة. يهدف البحث الحالي إلى تقديم مراجعة تحليلية منهجية للأدلة المنشورة حول استخدام روبوتات المحادثة في تعلم اللغة الإنكليزية، مع التركيز على فاعليتها في مهارات التحدث والكتابة والقراءة والاستماع، ودورها في تعلم المفردات والقواعد والترجمة والتعلم الذاتي، فضلًا عن تحليل الفوائد والتحديات والآثار التربوية. اعتمد البحث تصميمًا لمراجعة الأدلة الثانوية (umbrella-style) (analytical review)، بحيث كانت المراجعات المنهجية والتحليلات البعدية المنشورة وحدة التحليل الأساسية، مع إعطاء أولوية للدراسات الحديثة بين 2022 و2026، والاستفادة من الدراسات التأسيسية السابقة عند الحاجة

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Writing Skills for First-Year English Department Students at the University of Kerbala
papers.authors: Huda Jalail Kadhim, Manar Amer Saleh
papers.abstract: Writing is the most important language skill. It requires experiences of grammar, vocabulary, coherence, and logical organization. With the development of combining technology and education, Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools have become necessary for English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing instruction. The study explains how the students at a University of Kerbala, College of Education for the Humanities, First-Year English Department, realize the benefits and drawbacks of using AI technologies to improve their writing skills

papers.title: Do Virtual Faces Lead to Real Purchases? Investigating AI Anthropomorphism & Its Impact on Purchase Intention
papers.authors: Humna Hamad Butt, Maha Gul, Umme Rehma, Rukhba Ather Zia, Asma Nisar
papers.journal: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
papers.abstract: The research paper focuses on the impact of AI anthropomorphism on purchase intention, with the mediating role of marketing personalization, entertainment value and perceived homophily in the context of AI influencers/models. Brands around the world are adopting AI marketing tools, in which AI influencers/models are a relatively newer domain. The aim of the research is to fill the gap of research done on AI influencers/models in the Pakistani consumer market, discussing its practical implications on the fashion industry in particular. The study involved a sample size of 220 respondents, Pakistani residents aged 16 to 45 years, who had either seen or interacted with AI influencers/models before in any media type, using convenience and snowball sampling technique for data collection, which was then run through SPSS using Process Hayes Mediation Model 4. The results of the mediation analysis represented that the three proposed hypotheses in the study were accepted. The hypotheses were; marketing personalization mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase Intention, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention, and lastly, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention. The proven hypotheses signify the importance of the practical implications of the research on the Pakistani fashion industry, as big global brands are moving towards and investing in newer technologies like AI marketing tools.
