This study aims to measure the effect of AI literacy on technostress among digital creative multimedia industry workers. The research hypothesis states that there is a significant effect of AI literacy on technostress. This study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design involving 230 digital creative multimedia industry workers employed as full-time, freelance, part-time, or intern workers, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using the MAILS (Meta AI literacy Scale) and Technostress Scale instruments, then analyzed using a simple linear regression test. Results showed that AI literacy has a significant positive effect on technostress, although with a relatively small contribution. This finding differs in direction from previous research on student samples, indicating that the relationship between AI literacy and technostress depends on the characteristics of the population studied. These findings imply that improving AI competency among digital creative multimedia industry workers should be accompanied by realistic work-expectation management and organizational support, given that high technological mastery does not automatically reduce the risk of technostress. ABSTRAK Perkembangan teknologi (AI) dalam dunia kerja turut memunculkan tantangan psikologis baru berupa technostress, terutama pada pekerja dengan tingkat ketergantungan tinggi terhadap penggunaan AI pada pekerjaan sehari-hari. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengukur pengaruh AI literacy terhadap technostress pada pekerja industri multimedia kreatif digital. Hipotesis penelitian menyatakan terdapat pengaruh signifikan antara AI literacy terhadap technostress. Penelitian ini memakai pendekatan kuantitatif dengan menetapkan desain korelasional pada 230 pekerja industri multimedia kreatif digital berstatus pekerja full time, freelance, part time, atau magang, yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Data penelitian dikumpulkan dengan instrumen MAILS (Meta AI literacy Scale) dimensi AI literacy dan Technostress Scale, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji regresi linier sederhana. Hasil penelitian menyimpulkan AI literacy berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap technostress, meskipun dengan kontribusi yang tergolong kecil. Temuan ini berbeda arah dengan penelitian terdahulu pada sampel mahasiswa, mengindikasikan bahwa hubungan antara AI literacy dan Technostress bergantung pada karakteristik populasi yang diteliti. Temuan ini mengimplikasikan bahwa peningkatan kompetensi AI pada pekerja industri multimedia kreatif digital perlu disertai penataan ekspektasi kerja dan dukungan organisasi, mengingat penguasaan teknologi yang tinggi tidak serta-merta menurunkan risiko technostress.

papers.title: Responsible integration of generative AI and LLMs in higher education: Empirical insights and a framework for teaching and learning
papers.authors: Jose A. Diaz-Garcia, Roberto Morcillo-Jiménez, Bartolomé Ortiz-Viso, Maria Dolores Ruiz
papers.journal: Multidisciplinary Journal for Education Social and Technological Sciences
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) tools are rapidly reshaping university learning environments, yet pedagogical and ethical frameworks have not developed at the same pace as their adoption. Adopting a multidisciplinary approach, this study combines empirical evidence from a survey of 117 undergraduate Engineering and Health Sciences students with the pedagogical perspectives of university lecturers. It examines how students currently use GenAI and how these tools can be meaningfully integrated into teaching and learning. Findings show that students’ first exposure to GenAI is mainly driven by informal social media channels rather than institutional guidance, resulting in uneven and often unguided adoption. The study also identifies a “contradictory profile” in 11% of the sample: students who perceive GenAI use as a form of cheating while also expressing a strong demand for formal training on its academic integration. From the lecturers’ perspective, GenAI offers opportunities to support content creation, assessment design, and instructional workflows, provided that human-led teaching remains central. By integrating observed student behaviors with expert recommendations, this research proposes an ethical framework and practical guidelines for the responsible integration of GenAI in higher education. The study highlights the urgent need for institutional policies that address emerging socio-ethical tensions and ensure that GenAI enhances, rather than circumvents, foundational knowledge, academic integrity, and critical thinking.

papers.title: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation
papers.authors: Renye Yan, Jialun Zhong, Jikang Cheng, Yi Gao, Yanzeng Li, Ling Liang
papers.abstract: Generative AI is becoming an important medium for artistic creation, yet existing interactions often assume that creators can specify intentions in advance and accurately communicate them through text prompts. Artistic intentions, however, may be vague, latent, or recognizable only after seeing concrete visual possibilities. We propose a human-AI co-creation paradigm beyond explicit intent expression. By expanding model exploration, we expose artists to diverse visual possibilities, allowing them to identify previously unarticulated preferences through observation, comparison, and selection. We then integrate artists' curatorial judgments into reinforcement learning, assigning different learning strengths based on preferences over generation trajectories, so recognized directions are more strongly reinforced and the model gradually adapts to individual aesthetics. This creates a continuous "explore-identify-shape-re-explore" loop in which artistic intent is progressively discovered, externalized, and shaped. Through three user studies, we examine latent-preference discovery, personalized preference alignment, and the externalization of vague, difficult-to-express creative intentions.

papers.title: Risk and Refusal: Mechanisms of LLM Responses to Suicidal Ideation
papers.authors: Drishti Goel, Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Jeongah Lee, Violeta J. Rodriguez, Daniel S. Brown, Ravi Karkar, Koustuv Saha
papers.abstract: Refusal is a common safety mechanism in large language models (LLMs), yet in contexts of suicidal ideation (SI), refusing to engage can itself constitute a safety failure. We evaluate how eight instruction-tuned LLMs respond to SI and self-harm disclosures across three datasets, varying whether models are informed that a disclosure expresses SI and whether they receive a clinician-developed response protocol, and complement this with mechanistic analyses in six open-weight models. Our results reveal a nuanced relationship between refusal and response-level risk. At baseline, elevated risk in model responses is driven primarily by inattention to the disclosure, alongside refusal to engage. Mechanistic analyses suggest that models may refuse SI disclosures through the same direction that mediates their refusals of harmful requests. However, informing models of the SI context, or suppressing refusal directly, increases engagement without reliably lowering response risk, and may raise it. In contrast, the clinician-guided protocol consistently reduces response-level risk while also reducing refusal. Together, these analyses and ablations motivate the need for models that refuse only when warranted and engage in interactionally safe ways when users disclose SI.

papers.title: Edit Discovery in Human-AI Interactions
papers.authors: Alireza Mirrokni, Shayan Kiyani, George J. Pappas, Hamed Hassani
papers.abstract: Human-AI interactions are becoming a rich source of data for improving AI systems: while many model responses are already satisfactory, others expose failures that could become valuable supervision if identified and corrected. We study this setting through the notion of an editor: a more capable evaluation process that can inspect a response and either confirm it or modify it, but whose invocation is costly. The editor may be a human expert, a stronger AI system, or the same model equipped with additional computation, context, tools, or information. The key challenge is to decide which interactions to send to the editor before knowing whether an edit will actually be made, since invoking the editor itself consumes limited resources such as expert time, inference cost, latency, or tool-use overhead. We formulate this problem as Edit Discovery Optimization (EDO), which seeks to minimize edit opportunities missed among skipped interactions while controlling unnecessary confirmations and respecting an editor-cost budget. We characterize the population-optimal policy and show that it takes the form of a cost-adjusted threshold on the posterior probability of an edit. Building on this structure, we develop EDIT (Edit Discovery via Iterative Thresholding), an online algorithm for the partial-feedback setting in which edit labels are revealed only for selected interactions. EDIT combines an adaptive edit score, a confirmation-control threshold, and a cost-aware selection rule; it satisfies the editor budget at every round and controls the average confirmation rate up to a vanishing finite-horizon term, without distributional assumptions on the interaction stream. Across four reasoning and factual question-answering benchmarks, EDIT achieves a better trade-off between editor cost, Type-I error, and Type-II error than direct LLM-based batch selection.
keywords: type I and type II errors

papers.title: FCTS: Failure-Guided Curriculum Tree Search Over Generated Terrain for Legged Parkour
papers.authors: Narayanan Palghat Parameswaran, Dong-Ki Kim, Jay Patrikar, Santiago Gutierrez, Harshad Zade, Shayegan Omidshafiei, Harmish Khambhaita
papers.abstract: Quadruped parkour policies handle canonical obstacles well, but their training curricula often miss the irregular, compound geometry of industrial and disaster-response sites, where agile locomotion matters most. Such environments pose a hard generalization problem: even training directly on reconstructed geometry from the target site does not reliably yield policies that traverse it. Hand-designed curricula span only a few terrain families, and recent LLM-generated curricula offer little control over which policy weaknesses they target. We propose FCTS, a failure-conditioned terrain curriculum framework that uses localized traversal failures to automatically generate the terrains a policy should train on next. Each failure's location, termination mode, robot state, and surrounding terrain geometry condition this generation, and Monte Carlo Tree Search explores alternative curriculum trajectories under a fixed training budget. On terrains built from scanned real-world construction sites, FCTS raises success rate from 28.4% to 85.8% on a medium-difficulty course and from 14.9% to 44.7% on a hard course relative to the strongest parkour or LLM-curriculum baselines, and maintains higher progress on extreme terrains where full traversal is rare. Hardware experiments on a quadruped robot confirm that the learned FCTS policies transfer to the real world.

papers.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
papers.authors: Tianxing Chen, Wenwei Lin, Chuqiao Lyu, Peicheng Xiang, Junyuan Tang, Tian Nian, Zijian Cai, Kehe Ye, Chenze Yu, Wenxuan Zhu, Eric J. Chen, Yan Qin, Yue Chen, Tongyu Wu, Junhao Gong, Kai-Chong Lei, Jiahao Zhang, Kailun Su, Qiwei Liang, Renjing Xu, Ping Luo, Wenbo Ding
papers.abstract: Generalist robot policies benefit from large-scale visual pretraining but often struggle with contact-rich dexterous manipulation, where force, compliance, and incipient slip are hard to observe from images. We present Spark-0, a spatially aligned vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) model that uses touch in two complementary ways. During pretraining, image-space contact maps derived from tactile gloves, together with features from a frozen 3D geometry teacher, supervise the visual tokens; these objectives are removed at inference. In parallel, a tactile pathway encodes regional force histories and 3D taxel states to condition the action expert. A single checkpoint therefore supports both vision-only and tactile-conditioned deployment. To scale this supervision, we build HumanTouch, a 1,000-hour dataset of full-hand tactile human manipulation, and pretrain Spark-0 on it together with egocentric video, robot data, and simulation. We also release SparkArena, which pairs vision-only simulated tasks with tactile-conditioned real-robot tasks on one dexterous embodiment. Spark-0 achieves the highest mean success rate on both SparkArena tracks and ranks first on all eight aggregate metrics of the Ego Humanoid Manipulation Benchmark. Compared with vision-only pretraining on the same data and compute with touch discarded, retaining the touch of 1,000 hours of HumanTouch raises vision-only success on Ego Humanoid from 52.5% to 71.7%, and success on SparkArena-Real, where touch is also used at deployment, from 44.0% to 52.0%, indicating that touch serves not only as a policy input but also as scalable supervision for dexterous visuomotor pretraining. The Website is available at: https://xsparkai.com/Spark-0.

papers.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
papers.authors: Manya Wadhwa, Pranav Narayanan Venkit, Hiroaki Hayashi, Yu Li, Tuhin Chakrabarty, Chien-Sheng Wu
papers.abstract: One of the first steps of a research pipeline is generating ideas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate this step, but most of this work optimizes the quality of individual ideas, while overlooking diversity. In our work, we study document-grounded ideation, focusing on increasing the diversity of LLM generated ideas and ensuring they are high quality. Given prior papers, a model must propose a set of ideas that are each high-quality and clearly distinct from one another, while also being grounded in the input documents. To optimize for this, we propose training with a set-level reinforcement learning objective. In our setup, in a single generation, the model writes K structured idea cards grounded in the source papers, and the set is scored jointly, where each idea's quality is weighted by its distance from the ideas written before it. This teaches the model to steer each new idea away from its predecessors. We show that our trained 8B model achieves higher creative utility (a measure combining quality and diversity) than Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-6 Astra on our contamination-free benchmark. In a pilot human study with four experts, our sets are judged as promising as Claude Opus 4.8's and contain marginally more unique ideas. When a coding agent runs proof-of-concept experiments on the ideas, our model's success@k is comparable to Claude Opus 4.8's, so we see that the added diversity does not cost any executability.

papers.title: My Credentials, Please: Detecting Filesystem Capability Laundering in MCP Servers at Scale
papers.authors: Zeqian Huang, Mingyue Tang, Aonan Guan, Qiming Sun, Pengzhou He
papers.abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how AI agents invoke external tools. MCP servers expose tools through a declared contract consisting of a name, description, and argument schema. In typical local deployments, client-side approval of a tool call grants the underlying server process broad host filesystem permissions rather than restricting it to the declared operation. We study the resulting vulnerability class, filesystem capability laundering, where attacker-steered arguments cause a tool to access sensitive host files outside its declared contract and deployment scope. We analyze this capability gap across three layers: server-category screening (L1), per-tool contract analysis (L2), and bypassable path-validation checks (L3). We design MCP-FSD to catalog MCP servers, infer least-privilege boundaries per tool, plant credential fixtures outside those boundaries, and evaluate exploitability and sandbox containment via paired dynamic execution. Across 21,097 MCP servers from nine registries, 787 of 4,806 triaged servers (16.4%) exhibit filesystem capabilities despite non-filesystem functional classifications. Dynamic three-case validation confirms 150 vulnerable instances under tested sandbox policies. Coordinated disclosure yielded 13 security advisories, including two CVEs in Anthropic's Git MCP Server.

papers.title: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing
papers.authors: T. Fei, Jiazheng Kang, Mao Zheng, Xingyan He, Xiang Yu
papers.abstract: External-memory systems extend language-model applications beyond a context window, but their quality depends critically on the model executing the write path: deciding what to retain, how precisely to represent it, and how new evidence should update persistent state. Existing frameworks typically place a general-purpose large language model behind framework-specific prompts. This raises serving cost, and a writer specialized for one protocol does not transfer directly to another; a unified model that can operate across established memory frameworks remains largely unexplored. We present Hy-Memory-30B-A3B, a compact long-term-memory writer trained across Mem0, MemOS, and Hy-Memory. Memory On-Policy Distillation teaches framework-specific write protocols on student-generated states; Memory RL then optimizes downstream answerability using dense per-chunk probes, attributed cross-chunk rewards, over-storage controls, and chunk-level GRPO. Carrying policy-written banks across windows keeps training aligned with deployment. On fixed 20% benchmark subsamples, Hy-Memory-30B-A3B ranks first on all four evaluated harnesses, including held-out EverMemOS, with a 55.49% macro average versus 54.62% for Claude Opus 5.

papers.title: Multi-sourced AI Tutor for Non-Native English Speaker Students
papers.authors: Yiyin Shen, Xinyi Ai, Weibing Wang, Rogers Jeffrey Leo John, Meenakshi Syamkumar
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being adopted as teaching tools in computing education, particularly for developing AI tutors capable of answering student questions. With the rise in enrollment of international students in computing programs, researchers have begun to explore the difficulties that non-native English speaker (NNES) students face in computing courses due to language barriers. To aid such students, we developed a general-purpose AI tutor system that can process student questions in foreign languages (currently focused on Mandarin) and provide bilingual responses. Our system also incorporates the functionality of generating a glossary of technical terms and their explanations to enhance comprehension. Our approach utilizes a specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with a novel question extraction mechanism, enabling us to effectively utilize a diverse array of course materials for answering student queries. We evaluated our AI tutor using 91 Piazza posts, demonstrating that it could answer 83.52% of the posts correctly and in a helpful manner. The tutor also provided high-quality translations for 76.92% of the questions and generated technical term glossaries for 64.47% of them. Our findings underscore the potential of multi-source RAG pipeline in enhancing AI tutor systems, offering support for non-native speakers that are challenging to provide with traditional supporting staff of a computing course.

papers.title: Bubble-Sort Exchange Networks: Symmetry Selection Rules and Language-Model Distillation on Exchange-Only Spin Chains
papers.authors: Yoko Minato
papers.abstract: On a chain of exchange-coupled quantum dots a Heisenberg exchange pulse of area pi is a SWAP, so the parallel bubble-sort SWAP network of superconducting chains is native to exchange-only (EO) spin qubits, and any other pulse area fuses routing with an entangling interaction. We build a variational "bubble-sort exchange network" (odd-even transposition, one parameter per pulse) and study it as a Born machine read out by Pauli spin blockade. Exchange conserves total spin, so the reachable readout distributions are fixed by the total-spin content of the initial product state. For the two-spin singlet-triplet encoding we derive a selection rule -- outcomes with k triplet pairs are bounded by the initial weight in sectors S <= k (S = 0 excluded for k = 1) -- and prove by a transportation argument that it is also sufficient: the reachable distributions form the polytope cut out by the rule, and its total-variation floor is attained. Products of singlets and T0's forbid whole outcome classes; the Neel state forbids none; the three-spin EO code has no floor. We then distil, in noise-free simulation, next-token distributions of GPT-2 over restricted vocabularies into the network, with matrix-product-state (MPS) Born machines as classical control. At six logical qubits the three-spin chain reaches KL = 0.011 nat at depth N and 0.004 at 2N, below the bond-dimension-4 MPS; the two-spin chain from the Neel state reaches 0.014 at 2N and 0.004 at 3N, against 0.28-1.5 from singlet/triplet products for the first teacher. Final states lie largely outside the code space: leakage is a resource, not an error. No arrangement of disjoint pulses meets every pair in fewer than N-1 rounds, and at depth 2N the chain distils as well as a 2D array or non-local couplings. Sector-restricted simulation extends this to 10-14 logical qubits (up to 30 dots).

papers.title: Following Delegation Traces to Study Human Oversight in Interaction with Multimodal AI
papers.authors: Agnese Chiatti, Matteo Matteucci, Viola Schiaffonati
papers.abstract: As multimodal AI systems are becoming our everyday thought partners, the shift towards studying how users transfer control to these systems becomes especially urgent. In this paper, we report an overview of findings from an online study with n=56 AI-literate participants and 392 Video Question Answering trials. After inspecting each multimodal AI response, participants rated task-specific trust and selected one of three intended policies for an analogous future task: reject AI assistance, use it with verification, or delegate fully to the AI. Within participants, post-interaction trust strongly predicted the user's delegation choices (OR=14.97, 95% CI [7.14,31.37]). Trust and delegation nevertheless remained distinct. Verification was the dominant policy and often co-occurred with high trust. Delegation also increased with task order after adjustment for momentary and participant-level trust (OR=1.22, 95% CI [1.02,1.45]), indicating an experience-related component that self-reported trust ratings alone could not capture. These findings motivate a shift from intended delegation to a non-intrusive observation of how delegation is enacted in collaborative human-AI tasks. We therefore conclude by proposing enacted delegation traces as a methodological framework for future studies of multimodal and agentic AI use.

papers.title: Agentic-Priors: Using Large Language Models to Address the Cold Start Problem in Preference Elicitation
papers.authors: Bruno Arcanjo, Zhaoxing Li, Sebastian Stein
papers.abstract: An agent that learns a user's preferences from their choices faces a cold start problem: before any choices are observed, it must rely solely on a prior. Informative priors are usually fitted to historical choice data, which new tasks and deployments lack. To address this, we present Agentic-Priors, which lets agentic systems use the implicit knowledge of large language models (LLMs) instead. Specifically, an LLM states a new user's trade-offs in interpretable terms, such as willingness to pay or value of time, which we map to a prior over multinomial logit coefficients. This prior is then refined by a Bayesian learner as choices are observed. Across seven choice datasets, Agentic-Priors improves cold start accuracy over an uninformed prior by 5-40 percentage points. It also outperforms AutoElicit, a state-of-the-art LLM prior-elicitation method, on three datasets and loses on one. It is up to 18 points more accurate than in-context learning, and never significantly worse. Against hierarchical Bayes models fitted to surveys of increasing size, our approach is worth roughly 6-40 surveyed users, in terms of log-loss, so its value is concentrated in a deployment's first users.

papers.title: Sub-Millisecond Reflexes for Continuous Physical Human-Robot Interaction
papers.authors: Jon Škerlj, Sami Haddadin
papers.abstract: Continuous physical human-robot interaction requires robots to rapidly adapt their control behaviour without interrupting task execution. However, existing ROS 2 control architectures rely on stop-to-switch mechanisms that introduce substantial delays and interrupt execution. We present an open-source, sub-millisecond reflex engine based on an enhanced ROS 2-compatible multimode controller that enables deterministic switching between control modalities and integrates reflex behaviours for mitigating contact hazards and kinematic limit violations. Experiments on a Franka Robotics manipulator demonstrate switching delays below 0.1 ms, more than four orders of magnitude faster than conventional ros2_control, while maintaining continuous operation during safety-critical events. In a multi-stage manipulation task, the proposed framework reduced execution time by 3.5% and peak trajectory jerk by more than threefold. By eliminating runtime middleware overhead, controller transitions are implemented as lock-free pointer operations, enabling reflex-level responsiveness within an open-source robotics framework.

papers.title: How language model agents reshape price competition
papers.authors: Martin Bichler, Philip Hierhager, Kassian Köck, Fabian Pieroth
papers.abstract: Repeated Bertrand competition is a stringent benchmark for algorithmic pricing: in homogeneous-goods markets, standard learning procedures typically select the stage-game Nash outcome with prices near marginal cost. We show that LLM pricing agents can escape this benchmark, depending on deployment decisions. LLMs outperform standard online learners through faster adaptation, but this advantage largely disappears against full-information learners. An extracted surrogate algorithm illustrates how LLMs in specific deployments profit from regularly undercutting slower learners. Agents that post one price every period from raw market histories that include rival prices can sustain supracompetitive regimes in self-play. Agents that periodically emit probability distributions from summarized histories of their own profits instead move toward the competitive region in self-play. Markets mixing these interfaces can generate dynamic regimes in which LLMs establish a high-price anchor and regularly undercut it to capture demand. These regimes can keep both competitors' prices above marginal cost. Deployment choices shape these outcomes, shifting the focus from stationary equilibria to dynamic pricing regimes.

papers.title: A hidden Markov model for unsupervised EEG-based tracking of auditory attention to a single voice
papers.authors: Tianyi Li, Simon Geirnaert, Davina Van den Broek, Elien Bellon, Bert De Smedt, Alexander Bertrand
papers.abstract: Objective: Absolute auditory attention decoding (aAAD) aims to track how strongly a listener attends to a single speech source using electroencephalography (EEG). Unlike selective auditory attention decoding, aAAD lacks a competing speech reference, making reliable attention tracking challenging. Approach: We propose a fully unsupervised aAAD pipeline combining neural envelope tracking (NET) with hidden Markov model (HMM)-based temporal inference. Using EEG signals and the target speech envelope, the framework estimates a continuous attention trajectory without explicit attention-state labels. We evaluate the approach using EEG recordings from 30 adults, investigate the impact of analysis window length, and compare HMM post-processing with moving-average (MA) smoothing and alternative EEG features. Main results: With 1-s analysis windows, non-causal HMM post-processing improves the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for all 30 participants, increasing mean AUC from 0.547 for raw NET to 0.832. A 5-s window achieves the highest mean AUC of 0.858. Compared with non-causal MA smoothing, the HMM achieves higher AUC across the examined smoothing scales. Individual switch detection times are comparable, while the HMM generally achieves lower group-level detection times. NET also outperforms alpha power and spectral entropy as an observation feature in the unsupervised HMM framework. Significance: The proposed framework provides a label-free approach for estimating temporal fluctuations in auditory attention, demonstrating the utility of probabilistic temporal inference for continuous attention tracking in single-speaker listening scenarios.

papers.title: A Framework for Teaching the Responsible and Effective Use of Generative AI in Statistics and Data Science
papers.authors: Vinny Davies, Craig Alexander, Jennifer Gaskell, Matthew Parker, Jake Lever
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) following the public release of tools such as ChatGPT has begun to reshape how students engage with coding, statistical analysis, and written communication in higher education. Growing use of conversational AI systems creates opportunities for learning alongside challenges around reliability, transparency, privacy, and appropriate academic and professional practice, highlighting the need for structured education in their responsible use. This paper presents a framework for teaching the responsible and effective use of generative AI in statistics and data science. The framework is organised around four areas: Understanding, Development, Reporting, and Safety, covering conceptual foundations, practical interaction within analytical workflows, documentation and transparency, and issues including reliability, bias, privacy, and ethics. Its design draws on emerging work in AI literacy and established principles from statistics and data science education, and was further refined through workshop and conference activities and participant feedback. The framework has been implemented across multiple settings, including a massive open online course, short training sessions, and undergraduate and postgraduate skills-based teaching. We use these experiences to identify broader design considerations for educators, including the value of authentic analytical tasks, critical evaluation of generated outputs, integrated consideration of responsible practice, and flexibility as generative AI technologies continue to evolve.

papers.title: Evaluating Inquiry Learning in LLM-Based Agents: Hypothesizing, Reasoning, and Exploration
papers.authors: Marta Knežević, Seyed Parsa Neshaei, Jibril Frej, Vinitra Swamy, Tanja Käser
papers.abstract: Scientific inquiry involves iterative cycles of exploration, hypothesis generation, and reasoning over observations to uncover relationships in complex systems. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in several components of this process, including inductive reasoning, hypothesis generation, and data analysis. However, prior work typically evaluates these abilities in isolation, leaving open how models integrate them across a full inquiry cycle. In this work, we introduce a framework for evaluating LLMs' inquiry capabilities in a unified, interactive setting. We extend the Countdown task to a mathematical environment where an agent probes the system by manipulating variables, collecting observations, and inferring relationships between them. This setup enables analysis of exploration strategies, causal discovery, and hypothesis refinement during inquiry. Across seven LLMs and multiple prompting strategies, our experiments reveal limited inherent inquiry capabilities and low success rates in discovering the underlying expressions. However, structured guidance inspired by educational scaffolding significantly improves performance. Our findings highlight current limitations of LLMs in strategic exploration and iterative hypothesis refinement, and show how simple guidance strategies developed for human learners in inquiry learning can support more effective inquiry behavior.

papers.title: A Flow-Theoretic Multimodal Control Framework Fusing Mental and Physical Engagement for Upper-Limb Rehabilitation
papers.authors: Jun Leng, Pengcheng Li, Hanze Wang, Shuxiang Guo, Junlin Jiang
papers.abstract: While Assist-as-Needed (AAN) control aims to maximize user participation in robot-assisted training, existing methods relying solely on physical metrics cannot distinguish muscular inability from mental disengagement, leading to suboptimal interventions. To address this ambiguity, a Flow-theoretic multimodal AAN framework is proposed, fusing EEG-based mental engagement and sEMG-based physical engagement into an adaptive impedance control strategy. A four-quadrant fuzzy decision engine translates these dual physiological metrics into continuous control policies. This enables the upper-limb exoskeleton to inject feedforward assistance during intent-execution mismatch (e.g., motor output attenuation despite mental focus) and escalate guiding stiffness to penalize mental distraction. The framework was validated with healthy participants against a state-of-practice sEMG-only AAN baseline. Kinematically and mechanically, the proposed framework reduced robotic energy expenditure by 71.9\% while maintaining precise trajectory tracking, confirming it elicited greater voluntary human effort. Physiologically, the system increased the time spent in the neuroplasticity zone (Flow State Ratio) from 4.6% to 42.8%. These results validate that decoupling and jointly regulating mental and physical states enhances the selectivity of robotic assistance, mitigating user passivity and sustaining the engagement crucial for motor learning.

papers.title: Hear, Localize, and Reason: Spatially Aware Scene Understanding for Audio-Visual LLMs
papers.authors: Sung-Bin Kim, Lee Jung-Mok, Jinwoo Jung, Oh Hyun-Bin, Hyeonggon Ryu, David F. Harwath, Tae-Hyun Oh
papers.abstract: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) have made strong progress in multimodal understanding, yet most treat audio as monaural semantic content, limiting their ability to reason about where sounds originate and how they relate to the visual scene. Recent spatial audio-visual studies address parts of this problem, but often focus on specific abilities, such as spatial correspondence or direction and distance reasoning. In this work, we introduce HLR-AVSceneQA, a comprehensive benchmark with a hear-localize-reason hierarchy that evaluates whether models can recognize what is heard, localize sound sources in egocentric and allocentric views, and use these localized sources to reason about how they relate to the visual scene. We further introduce HLR-LLM, which augments a strong audio-visual foundation model with a binaural spatial audio branch alongside its monaural semantic audio pathway. We train HLR-LLM with a curriculum that incorporates final-stage chain-of-thought supervision for multi-step spatial reasoning. Experiments show that existing AV-LLMs remain limited in spatial grounding and relational reasoning, while HLR-LLM substantially improves spatial audio-visual scene understanding without compromising semantic audio-visual perception.

papers.title: A Systematic and Validated Translation of the Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale to Chinese
papers.authors: Matthias Schmidmaier, Jingyao Zheng, Jie Song, Lik-Hang Lee, Sven Mayer
papers.abstract: The Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale (PETS) allows evaluation of empathic behavior in intelligent systems, a concept increasingly applied in human-AI interaction, particularly in emotional and mental health support applications. To support intercultural research and development, PETS is already available in multiple languages, as research suggests cultural and language-based differences in the expression and perception of empathy. Given the substantial Chinese-speaking population and the growing focus on cross-cultural HCI research, we present a validated translation of PETS into Putonghua (Mandarin) with Simplified Chinese. Based on established back-translation methodologies as used in previous PETS translations, our process included multiple independent translations, expert panel reviews, and empirical testing with a total of N=400 participants from an English and a Chinese sample. Through confirmatory factor analysis and invariance testing we show that the Chinese PETS retains the original two-factor structure with high reliability, with support for configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Beyond validation, empathic system behavior was rated equivalently across languages, while non-empathic behavior drew substantially higher ratings from Chinese participants, suggesting its absence is read less consistently across cultures than its presence. This validated Chinese version enables researchers and practitioners to assess empathy perceptions among Chinese-speaking users, supporting culturally appropriate empathic technology development.

papers.title: Incentivizing Tool-Use Reinforcement Learning for Post-Arrival Emergency Care Prediction
papers.authors: Pengfei Hu, Chenwei Wu, Qiao Jin, Jun Deng, Zhiyong Lu, Liyue Shen, Yue Ning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can reason over both structured measurements and free-text records, which makes them attractive for emergency department (ED) prediction. However, most existing LLMs still fall short of conventional ML methods like trees on EHR-based prediction tasks. Our controlled analysis traces this gap to two weaknesses: LLMs do not select informative features, and they misjudge what numerical values imply for risk even when given the right features. We propose TIR-EC, a tool-integrated reinforcement learning framework that addresses both. TIR-EC exposes EHR feature groups as tools the LLM can call. It trains the LLM with rewards from a gradient-boosted tree teacher, which provides a reference set of informative tools and a graded risk target. TIR-EC also distills task-specific clinical skills into the model weights through a reverse curriculum that gradually removes the skills from the prompt during RL process. Evaluation on three clinical prediction tasks shows that our 4B agent achieves the highest macro F1 of all compared models, outperforms conventional ML baselines, and is competitive with much larger frontier LLMs. Further analysis shows that TIR-EC selects more useful evidence with fewer tool calls and combines measurements more effectively.

papers.title: Do Agents Need a New Kind of Paper? SPRA: Structured Paper Representation for Agents
papers.authors: Yutong Leng, Haojiong Chen, Fukai Shang, Xiaoyang Wang, Mindong Liu, Runyuan Ma, Jiantao Qiu
papers.abstract: Scientific agents must connect research problems, methods, and findings dispersed through narrative articles. We introduce SPRA (Structured Paper Representation for Agents), a paper-level representation of persistent research objects and typed relations. Its empirical-AI profile organizes Problems, Contributions, Components, ExperimentSetups, Measures, and Findings for querying, traversal, and reuse. Selected paper-level citation relations record dependencies, component use, and comparisons with prior work; source locations support verification. We instantiate SPRA across more than one million AI papers, with 19.95 million research units and 24.07 million internal relations. Evaluations access SPRA through Schema-RAG with task evidence fixed before inference. Across seven subfields, SPRA improves source-conditioned scientific QA by 0.381/5 over passage retrieval while remaining close to Full Compact (0.078/5 lower on average). In directed cross-paper reasoning, qualification improves by 0.184/5 over passage retrieval; Top-5 synthesis shows mixed quality effects. Across all paired RQ2 tasks, including Top-5, input+output tokens decrease by 28.5% relative to passage retrieval and 95.3% relative to Full Compact. In idea generation, a 0.067-point lower Overall score than Full Compact accompanies 93.7% fewer input+output tokens. Together, these results support SPRA as a usable representation of scientific content and a foundation for research workflows that connect, inspect, and reuse paper-level research objects. The SPRA resource is accessible through the Sciverse scholarly-data platform.

papers.title: MemCut: Every Secret Leaves a Trail in the Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents
papers.authors: Cheng Zhang, Xuanning Cao, Zhicheng Zheng, Hui Xiong
papers.abstract: Long-term memory has become a crucial component of large language model (LLM) agents, with most research focusing on retrieving relevant information accurately and efficiently. However, a dependable memory system must also forget sensitive user data upon request. To evaluate this capability, we introduce MemCut, a systematic benchmark for user-requested forgetting. Its 456 hand-designed secrets in long-horizon conversations have fully annotated evidence trails to test recovery after deletion, including from messages that never state the secrets directly. We propose two recovery metrics. Native recovery measures reader success through the system's retrieval, whereas residual recovery measures the same reader's success when directly given surviving objects traced to annotated disclosures or evidence. We establish three reference deletion baselines to test how far existing retrievers and write models support forgetting across five memory designs and four LLMs. Disclosure removal reduces native recovery far more than residual recovery. LLM-guided deletion of ten additional turns from twenty retrieval candidates leaves 39-76% residual recovery. Subset sweeps (144 facts, three systems, two models) show that widening the pool at a fixed budget reduces residual recovery more than deleting all original candidates. These sweeps identify candidate coverage as a bottleneck in the reference baselines.

papers.title: LLM-Based Weak Annotation for Cybersecurity Tweet Classification: A Teacher-Student Framework
papers.authors: Ferry Afit Kurniawan, Kazushi Okamoto, Koki Karube, Kei Harada, Atsushi Shibata
papers.abstract: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) relies on the timely identification of emerging threats, enabling organizations and security analysts to support situational awareness and decision-making. Social media platforms such as X (formerly Twitter) have become valuable CTI sources because vulnerabilities and attack activities are often discussed there before appearing in formal reports. However, the rapid growth of cybersecurity discussions on social media has created more content than domain experts can realistically review and annotate, making labeled data a major bottleneck for developing supervised learning approaches. While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise as weak annotators in other domains, their effectiveness for cybersecurity tweet classification and downstream training of domain-specific pre-trained language models (PLMs) remains underexplored. To address this challenge, we propose a Teacher-Student weak supervision framework in which a selected LLM serves as a Teacher to generate weak labels for unlabeled cybersecurity tweets, enabling the training of cybersecurity-specific PLMs without large-scale manual annotation. Experimental results show that PLMs trained solely on LLM-generated labels consistently achieve F1 scores above 0.92, remaining within 3 percentage points of fully human-supervised models across all evaluated architectures. These findings suggest that LLM-based weak annotation offers a practical alternative for constructing cybersecurity-specific training data when expert annotation resources are limited.

papers.title: What do AI chatbots do after users decline therapeutic redirection for suicide thoughts?
papers.authors: Subigya Kumar Nepal, Ruth Heo, Emma M. Parrish, Colin A. Depp
papers.abstract: Safety evaluations of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots focus on therapeutic redirection, statements urging users who disclose suicide thoughts to seek help from crisis lines or other human sources. How chatbots respond when users refuse that help is unclear. This cross-sectional audit ran 2,550 scripted multi-turn conversations in September 2026. Each conversation opened with a disclosure of suicide thoughts at 3 levels of severity, answered every referral with up to 10 standardized refusals and then changed the subject. All 2,550 conversations included a referral, 2,542 (99.7%) in the first reply. However, mean persistence ranged from 0.01 to 9.94 refusals across chatbots. Newer versions of all 5 chatbots tested in 2 versions persisted less than older versions (each P < .05). Compared with passive ideation, a disclosure of intent was associated with 1.26 more refusals sustained (95% CI, 1.06-1.46) and higher odds of renewed referral after the topic change (odds ratio, 10.07; 95% CI, 7.43-13.66). Chatbots that persisted less in referral more often presented themselves as the user's support (Spearman rho = -0.80; P < .001). Of 8,818 refusal-phase replies urging outside help, only 173 (2.0%) asked about barriers to seeking it. Chatbots uniformly recommended outside help after disclosures of suicide thoughts but varied widely in persisting in those recommendations, with newer versions persisting less. Safety evaluations should test what happens after a crisis referral is refused, not only whether one is offered.

papers.title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally
papers.authors: Zhizhuo Kou, Jian Yang, Pengfei Hao, Junyu Luo, Jingshu Peng, Sirui Han, Yike Guo
papers.abstract: When a speaker says ``some students passed'', listeners infer that not all of them did. Reasoning models now let users decide how long a model thinks before it answers, but we do not know what extra thinking does to such everyday inferences. We study this directly: we keep a model's weights fixed, change only how much it thinks, and record which reading it chooses. A second tool cuts the model's own reasoning at successive points and asks for an answer, showing where the reading changes. Thinking makes models read logical words as logic: it cancels the implicatures of \emph{some} (\emph{not all}) and \emph{or} (\emph{not both}) in most tested open reasoning models and in GPT-5, while context-driven inferences such as indirect answers improve. The trace shows why: models first entertain the enriched reading and cancel it later. Answering from that early reading, an exploratory inference-time remedy, recovers these implicatures without losing literal accuracy. Evaluations of reasoning models should measure how they interpret, not only how accurate they are.

papers.title: Revolución de datos mediante Big Data y Google Colab para el análisis y gestión de ciencia de datos
papers.authors: Ricardo Manuel Candanedo Yau
papers.abstract: This research analyzed the influence of Big Data and Google Colab platform on information analysis, processing, and management within academic and technological contexts. The study followed a documentary and descriptive approach supported by the review and analysis of 100 indexed scientific publications selected according to thematic relevance, currency, and academic rigor. The methodology incorporated thematic coding processes and documentary frequency analysis aimed at identifying trends related to Big Data, information science, cloud computing, machine learning, and collaborative platforms for data analysis. The findings revealed that the accelerated growth of digital information significantly transformed the way organizations, educational institutions, and research centers manage information to support strategic decision-making processes. Likewise, the study identified that Big Data facilitates large-scale information processing through predictive analytics, data mining, and statistical visualization techniques, while Google Colab enables the development of projects based on cloud computing, programming, and computational analysis within collaborative environments. The results also demonstrated that the integration of both technologies strengthened digital and analytical competencies related to programming, information management, analytical thinking, and the automation of scientific processes. In the same way, the accessibility and flexibility of Google Colab contributed to democratizing access to advanced tools for data analysis and processing without requiring specialized technological infrastructure. The study concluded that the convergence between Big Data and Google Colab represents a strategic alternative for optimizing knowledge management, strengthening scientific research, and promoting technological innovation and digital transformation processes in academic and organizational environments. Furthermore, these technologies foster new opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and data-driven decision-making.

papers.title: La inteligencia artificial como estrategia empresarial de innovación y competitividad en las MIPYMES del corregimiento de Canto del Llano, Santiago de Veraguas
papers.authors: Antonio Alejandro Pérez Martínez, William Avatt Donoso Olave
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to assess the extent to which artificial intelligence (AI) can serve as a business strategy aimed at promoting innovation and competitiveness among MSMEs in the Canto del Llano district. A quantitative approach was used, employing a non-experimental, cross-sectional design with a descriptive-correlational focus. The population consisted of 214 active formal businesses, of which 139 were included in the sample; non-probabilistic convenience sampling was employed. The instrument was a structured questionnaire using a Likert scale, validated by experts with a coefficient of 0.985 and a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.985. Statistical analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel and SPSS 26.0. The main results reveal that 61.1% of business owners admit to having limited knowledge of AI, and only 8.3% use it in their operations; however, more than 80% recognize its potential. Hypothesis testing showed that perceptions of the potential impact of AI are significantly higher than the neutral point on the scale (value = 3), with test values of t = 2.167 and p = 0.032. It is concluded that, although actual adoption is still in its early stages, there is a widespread positive perception toward the incorporation of AI, contingent upon the availability of training, technological resources, and institutional support. The findings provide the first set of systematized empirical evidence on AI adoption in MSMEs in this district, with implications for the design of business digitalization policies in the region.

papers.title: Internet of Things: Embedded Technologies, Smart Applications, and Future Directions
papers.authors: Prof. N. M. Kolhe Sonwane Vishakha, Dr. H. B. Jadhav Prof. D. S. Kshirsagar
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) connects physical objects through sensors, embedded processors, and communication interfaces. These devices can collect and share data, helping systems respond automatically to changing conditions. This review offers a structured overview of IoT’s development, enabling technologies, practical applications, and the challenges that affect reliable deployment. It draws primarily on a review article by Yalli, Hasan, and Badawi, which explores IoT’s evolution and its connections to wireless sensor networks, cloud and edge computing, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain. The paper follows the flow of a typical IoT system, from sensing and communication to data processing and action. It discusses applications in smart homes, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, education, and energy management, as well as practical challenges such as limited device resources, network delays, compatibility between systems, privacy, cybersecurity, and maintenance.

papers.title: Trustworthy Cloud Infrastructure for Secure and Privacy-Aware Artificial Intelligence Processing
papers.authors: Sakshi K.Wagh Prof. Sunita Totade, Jesika P. Chourpagar Kashish J. Panjwani
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: The exponential growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cloud computing technologies has revolutionized data processing and intelligent service delivery at scale. Organizations across virtually every sector now rely on cloud-hosted machine learning pipelines to extract value from data that is collected continuously, at volumes and velocities that on-premises infrastructure struggles to match. However, this technological advancement comes with significant challenges, particularly concerning privacy and security of sensitive data transmitted to cloud environments. This research paper addresses the critical intersection of trustworthy cloud infrastructure and privacy-preserving artificial intelligence processing. Our work explores a comprehensive framework that integrates privacy protection mechanisms, secure computation techniques, and confidence assessment measures to establish reliable and trustworthy AI services in cloud environments. We propose that by combining differential privacy, secure multi-party computation, and confidence-aware prediction mechanisms, organizations can maintain data confidentiality while leveraging the computational power of cloud-based AI systems. Rather than treating privacy, security, and reliability as separate concerns to be bolted onto a finished system, the framework proposed here treats them as first-class design requirements that shape every layer of the processing pipeline, from data ingestion through model inference to the communication of results back to end users. This study examines existing privacy-preserving techniques applicable to cloud AI, analyzes their performance trade-offs, and evaluates the reliability of AI predictions through confidence scoring. Our findings demonstrate that it is possible to achieve a balanced approach where sensitive data remains protected, AI model performance remains acceptable, and computational overhead is manageable. The research contributes to the development of secure, trustworthy AI solutions suitable for healthcare, financial services, educational institutions, and other sectors requiring stringent privacy compliance. We further situate our contribution within the broader movement toward trustworthy and responsible AI, arguing that privacy-preservation is not merely a compliance checkbox but a foundational property that determines whether AI systems can be adopted at scale in sensitive domains.

papers.title: AI literacy of library and information science students in Africa: insights from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa and Uganda
papers.authors: Zakir Hossain, Md. Sakib Biswas, Sophia Vivian Adeyeye, Monica Mensah Danquah, Margaret Sraku-Lartey, Berthilde Uwamwezi, Corinne Hertel
papers.abstract: Introduction. As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes global education and information systems, Africa’s readiness remains uneven. This study examines AI-literacy among Library and Information Science (LIS) students—future librarians—across five African countries: Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa and Uganda. It assesses their technical proficiency, tool usage and ethical awareness in an AI-driven era. Method and Analysis. A quantitative survey was conducted with 437 LIS students from five African countries. The Games-Howell Post Hoc Test was used to compare AI literacy across countries. ANOVA and Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) were applied to analyse variations in AI literacy levels based on country, study level, gender and English proficiency. Results. The findings reveal significant disparities in AI literacy between the five African nations. The results of the Games-Howell post hoc test show that both Rwanda and Uganda have significantly higher mean AI literacy scores compared to Ghana and Nigeria. In contrast, South Africa's scores did not show a statistically significant difference from the other countries, highlighting the varied readiness levels. The study found that ChatGPT dominates usage at 71.9%, while specialised tools such as Elicit remain significantly underutilised at just 4.6%. Ethical concerns among students are also notable, with 39.6% citing worries about privacy risks and 33.2% being troubled about algorithmic bias, highlighting AI anxieties and its societal impact. Conclusion. This study calls for integrating AI literacy into LIS curricula and advocating for multilingual AI tools. Where new modules are not feasible, institutions can leverage existing courses such as Information Retrieval, Digital Libraries and Research Methods to embed AI content. The results emphasise that context-driven interventions are essential to ensure AI enhances equitable knowledge access rather than deepening existing disparities.

papers.title: Operationalizing OWASP LLM Top 10 Controls in Enterprise AI Platforms
papers.authors: Sai Kumar Pola, Pavan Kumar Koneru
papers.abstract: Enterprises have moved large language model applications from pilot projects into production systems handling customer conversations, internal knowledge retrieval, and increasingly autonomous agentic workflows, introducing a risk surface that differs materially from what conventional application security programs address. OWASP has responded with the Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, most recently revised in its 2025 edition, and a newly published Top 10 for Agentic Applications covering autonomous, tool-using systems. These taxonomies name and prioritize risk but leave engineering teams to translate categories such as prompt injection or excessive agency into controls that fit an existing cloud-native delivery pipeline. This paper proposes a reference architecture and implementation framework mapping each of the ten OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 categories to specific, deployable controls built on commonly used cloud primitives: managed model gateways, service mesh identity, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, and continuous delivery tooling. The framework is informed by production engineering practice with retrieval-augmented generation and agentic workloads on Kubernetes using a managed foundation model service. Five real, publicly documented incidents, including a corporate data leak, a manipulated dealership chatbot, a legal ruling on chatbot liability, an indirect prompt injection exfiltration attack, and a zero-click vulnerability in a widely used enterprise copilot, are analyzed against the proposed controls to show where the framework would have reduced impact or prevented the incident outright. A four-stage maturity model helps organizations sequence adoption. Open challenges discussed include the immaturity of evaluation tooling for non-deterministic systems and the persistent tension between guardrail thoroughness and production latency.

papers.title: Pengembangan Asisten Virtual Berbasis Artificial Intelligence untuk Layanan Informasi Sistem Manajemen PK IMM UMKO
papers.authors: Rizky Satrio Wibowo, Khusnul Khotimah
papers.abstract: The management of the Commissariat Leadership (PK) of the Muhammadiyah Student Association (IMM) at the Faculty of Engineering and Computer Science (FTIK), Universitas Muhammadiyah Kotabumi (UMKO), has been conducted conventionally using separate Microsoft Excel and Google Form tools, leaving cadre registration, Darul Arqam Dasar (DAD) implementation, attendance, and news publication vulnerable to fragmented data, administrative errors, and proxy-attendance practices. This research develops a Web Mobile-based PK IMM UMKO Management System integrated with an Artificial Intelligence virtual assistant for IMM-related information services. The system was built using the Waterfall method, the Django framework, and PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension, following a Model-View-Template architecture with role-based access control for five actors. It provides two AI services—a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Chatbot using the gpt-4o-mini model grounded in official AD/ART documents and a Smart Editor for language correction—together with automatic registration verification through the UMKO SSO API and a per-session QR attendance module using regenerated UUID tokens as an anti-proxy mechanism. Black Box Testing on 32 scenarios was fully valid; chatbot testing on nine scenarios reached 100% accuracy with a median AI response time of about three seconds; and a four-level Likert scale questionnaire involving 14 respondents across six validator groups yielded an average of 96.20% in the “Very Feasible” category. The system is therefore technically and functionally feasible as a modern solution for faculty-level student organization governance.

papers.title: Assessment of utilization of ChatGPT on Medical Research Paper Writing Practices amongst University students in Lahore, Pakistan
papers.authors: Ahmed Hassan, Rabbiya Sarwar, Nida Asif, Asma Kanwal, Aneesa Mahreen, Tehreem Farooq
papers.journal: Proceedings of Shaikh Zayed Medical Complex Lahore
papers.abstract: Background :The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in academic applications has transformed medical research writing. ChatGPT is an AI-based language model that has been introduced by Open AI. It is been commonly used for literature review, manuscript organization, and writing research papers and articles. Objective: To assess utilization of ChatGPT on medical research writing practices among university students. Method: An analytical cross- sectional study conducted among university student of The University of Lahore and Rashid Latif Khan University. The study participants were split into 3 groups on the basis of their enrolled degree programs; MBBS, BDS and Allied health sciences (undergraduate, graduate and post-graduate students). Duration of study was from January 2025 to June 2025. Descriptive statistics, frequencies, percentages, and cross-tabulations were employed to summarize the demographic features. For inferential testing, statistical tests were used to investigate the relationship between the question variable utilization of ChatGPT and Chi-square (?²) tests were used to detect relationships between categorical variables. Following an extensive study of the literature, a questionnaire was prepared. Total of 381 students were selected according to sample size. A sample of 381 students was selected using non probability convenience sampling technique. A self-constructed online validated questionnaire was used. Results: Among 381 participants, 81.9% of participants agreed that it improved their academic writing. A majority of respondents (92.1%) found it is easy to comprehend difficult ideas. Furthermore, 74.0% found that it helped them to organize their ideas while writing research papers. In addition, 79.0% students felt that it improved their ability to research independently. However, 70.9% students said inaccuracies were present in ChatGPT’s results. 50.1% agreed to use the text generated by ChatGPT without further validation. Conclusion: ChatGPT enhances enrolled university students’ academic writing, manuscript structure, conceptual understanding, time management, productivity and critical thinking. However, due to risks of inaccuracies and ethical concerns, its use must involve human oversight, verification, and adherence to academic integrity.

papers.title: ESL ASSESSMENT IN THE AGE OF AI: SERBIAN ESL TEACHERS’ ATTITUDES TOWARDS THE USE OF CHATGPT
papers.authors: Aleksa Stošić, Marija V. Milojković
papers.abstract: Following the introduction of publicly accessible AI and LLMs, they have gradually started to be adopted in the ESL classroom. Recent studies have revealed that these tools have had a wider impact on ESL assessment, allowing for enhanced accuracy, efficiency, and person alization in language evaluation. However, how widely these technologies are understood and used by teachers is still being investigated. This study explores how Serbian ESL teachers use and perceive ChatGPT as a tool for assessing student work. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining survey data from 53 participants with follow-up interviews from 10 educa tors to examine their tendencies, habits, and opinions regarding ChatGPT for assessment. Find ings revealed that grammar and vocabulary are the language skills which Serbian ESL teachers assessed most often using ChatGPT, while skills such as speaking, listening, and critical thinking were rarely assessed using AI. Teachers also expressed moderate trust in the tool’s ability to detect grammar and syntax errors, but were concerned about its limitations. These limitations included ChatGPT’s ability to provide accurate assessment, its tendency to give vague feedback, and its lack of contextual understanding. While many teachers recognized its ability to save time for as sessment tasks, they also recognized their own limited experiences with AI tools and stressed the need for human oversight, formal training, and ethical safeguards. This study indicated that even though ChatGPT does not yet have widespread use in the Serbian ESL classroom, interviewees frequently emphasized that it should be used as a supplementary tool to assist teachers, but that guidelines and professional training on its use need to be provided to the teachers before they would readily implement it in the classroom.

papers.title: Inteligencia artificial y rúbricas para la generación de instrumentos de evaluación
papers.authors: Azahara Casanova Pistón, Patricia Sáenz-Valiente
papers.abstract: The use of rubrics in Higher Education has become established as a key strategy for improving learning assessment by providing clear criteria, promoting transparency, and facilitating student self-regulation. The incorporation of ICT has enabled their evolution expanding their possibilities for use and analysis, although it has also raised concerns related to privacy and data security when online environments are used. In this context, the design of automated assessment instruments capable of functioning offline is proposed in order to guarantee the protection of students’ information. Based on a literature review, a proposal is developed using spreadsheets, for the creation of two types of rubrics: one focused on grading and another aimed at generating feedback. Automation is achieved through the use of formulas, macros, and Visual Basic programming, making it possible to streamline the assessment process and reduce teachers’ workload. Furthermore, the integration of artificial intelligence through prompting techniques facilitates code generation, the expansion of comments, and the improvement of feedback writing, increasing its personalization and coherence. These tools make it possible to build more efficient, adaptive, and secure assessment systems, although they require an adequate level of teachers’ digital competence. The possibility of integrating both rubrics into a single system and exploring solutions that combine the advantages of offline environments with guarantees for data management in digital settings are proposed as future lines of development.

papers.title: Del eco algorítmico a la voz original: educación sensible y desfondamiento
papers.authors: Luis Manuel Martínez Domínguez
papers.abstract: The massive irruption of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) constitutes an ontological event that challenges contemporary education beyond mere technical efficiency or academic integrity. This study justifies the critical urgency of addressing the structural "groundlessness" of the human person in the face of current algorithmic saturation and technological idolatry. The main objective is to analyze, within the theoretical framework of Sensitive Education, the imminent risk of the "synthetic echo" supplanting the student's "original voice," thereby atrophying their discursive agency and capacity for meaning. A hermeneutic and phenomenological methodology is employed, articulating Leonardo Polo's transcendental anthropology, Hartmut Rosa's sociology of resonance, and the cultural criticism of authors such as Byung-Chul Han and Éric Sadin. The results reveal a deep existential fracture: AI imposes a "perfect closure" of data that collides with human "radical openness," generating an alienation where discourse (logos) is traumatically dissociated from vital experience (bios). In conclusion, it is argued that true digital literacy requires a transition from the isolation of the digital "false-we" towards a "mature-we" capable of ethical resistance and real alterity. Educational assessment must abandon the forensic approach to plagiarism to discern, through a "resonant hearing," the vibratory authenticity of learning, thus guaranteeing the primacy of the spirit over automatism and restoring the classroom as an essential sanctuary of presence and listening.

papers.title: Digital Protection and Innovation of Intangible Cultural Heritage Skills
papers.authors: Xiaoyang Hu
papers.journal: Journal of Cases on Information Technology
papers.abstract: Aiming at the problems of non-genetic fault and tacit knowledge loss, this study combines knowledge graph, computer vision and immersive media technology to construct a digital protection framework for intangible heritage. The framework transforms implicit experience into a structured digital model through multi-modal data acquisition; At the same time, a "virtual master" system was built to realize the interactive teaching of skills; In addition, the Virtual Reality (VR) scene restoration and live broadcast linkage strategy is adopted to promote the integration of protection and communication. The empirical results show that the efficiency of VR knowledge transfer reached 91.2%; The results show that the framework can effectively support the activation of intangible cultural heritage (ICH); Industrial-grade Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology can accurately decode and reproduce empirical craftsmanship.

papers.title: A Fuzzy Knowledge-Inference Framework for AI-Adoption Risk Assessment in Automotive SMEs
papers.authors: S. Davidson, Loveleen Gaur, Shavi Bansal, Varsha Arya, Ramakrishnan Raman
papers.journal: International Journal of Software Science and Computational Intelligence
papers.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises in the automotive supply base face mounting pressure to adopt artificial intelligence, yet they are least able to absorb the consequences of misscoped adoption. Assessing this risk means reasoning under vagueness: Data maturity, workforce skill, financial capacity, and above all safety and regulatory readiness are graded, interdependent judgments that crisp, compensatory instruments discard. This paper proposes the fuzzy knowledge inference framework, a two-stage rough–fuzzy framework. Eight automotive-specific risk factors are represented as linguistic variables over an information system; rough-set analysis establishes their nonredundancy; and a hierarchical fuzzy inference process—anchored, compliance-weighted, and noncompensatory—yields an interpretable risk index. Using no primary human data, it is well calibrated at its anchors, monotone in favorability, and rank-convergent with two independent instruments, while escalating the profiles a compensatory model would understate. Its contribution to the literature on AI-adoption risk assessment for automotive SMEs is the noncompensatory treatment of safety and regulatory readiness.

papers.title: ChatGPT and employability in higher education: exploring creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving
papers.authors: Cristina Calle-Martínez, Marta Silvera-Roig, Nuria Recuero Virto, Marta Paredes
papers.abstract: Generative AI tools are reshaping higher education and employability preparation. This study examines how using versus not using ChatGPT influences university students’ perceptions of employability, focusing on complex problem-solving, critical thinking, and creativity. Thirty students from the Complutense University of Madrid completed a contingency-plan task and participated in eight focus groups analyzed through Grounded Theory (ATLAS.ti). Results show that ChatGPT use is associated with efficiency, output refinement, and assisted creativity, while non-use is associated with originality, deliberation, and teamwork. The findings reveal preliminary patterns in students’ experiences with and without AI, warranting further quantitative investigation rather than claims of improved skills or employability.

papers.title: Teacher Readiness for Human-Centred AI Integration in Higher Education: Evidence from Assam, India
papers.authors: Karshika Boruah
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming higher education, making teacher readiness essential for responsible integration. This paper proposes an empirical framework to examine higher education teachers’ readiness for human-centred AI integration in Assam. Based on UNESCO’s AI Competency Framework for Teachers, the study focuses on five dimensions: human-centred mindset, AI ethics, AI foundations and applications, AI pedagogy, and AI-supported professional learning, alongside institutional support. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design is proposed, employing a structured questionnaire and statistical analyses to assess readiness and its influencing factors. Addressing a regional research gap, the study emphasises ethical judgment, pedagogical competence, and human accountability rather than technological adoption alone. As primary data collection is pending, the framework provides a basis for future empirical investigation. The anticipated findings may inform faculty development, institutional AI policies, and responsible AI integration in higher education.

papers.title: Faster but Not Truer, Part 2: The Regulatory Record, the Economics, and the TRACE-HEOR Reporting Standard
papers.authors: Onur Başer
papers.journal: Journal of health economics and outcomes research
papers.abstract: Background: Part 1 of this series found that measured gains from artificial intelligence (AI) in health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) concentrate in tasks with observable ground truth and disappear where the quantity of interest is a counterfactual. What regulators, health technology assessment (HTA) bodies, and sponsors have said about that division has not been assembled in one place. Methods: We assembled the primary regulatory, HTA, industry, and journal policy record through September 2026, requiring for each claim a named primary source and, where a quantity was reported, its provenance and whether the reporting party had a commercial interest. We downloaded the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) AI-enabled medical device list in full, tabulated published economic evaluations of AI, and set reported industry efficiency gains against disclosed use in submissions. We then evaluated the field against the task-based productivity framework of Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu and derived a reporting standard from the documented failure modes. Results: The FDA has authorized 1614 AI-enabled devices, 1230 (76.2%) in radiology, rising from 18 in 2016 to 335 in 2025, and has received more than 500 drug and biologic submissions containing AI components since 2016; its January 2025 credibility assessment guidance remains a draft and excludes discovery and operational uses. Industry sources report time savings of 40% to 97% in regulatory writing and approximately 80% in payer dossier drafting, but every one of these figures comes from a single-arm comparison without a concurrent control and was reported by the company that deployed or sold the tool. AI use was disclosed in 3 of 1391 HTA documents (0.2%) and 0.6% of one journal's submissions, against surveys reporting use between 25% and 81%. Nineteen economic evaluations of AI have been published against 1614 authorized devices. No regulator or HTA body has been documented accepting or rejecting an AI-derived endpoint as such. Conclusions: Current disclosure instruments ask whether AI wrote the text. Reviewers need to know whether AI selected the evidence, defined the cohort, derived the endpoint, or generated the code, and whether the recommendation would change without it.

papers.title: Faster but Not Truer, Part 1: A Systematic Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Health Economics and Outcomes Research
papers.authors: Onur Başer
papers.journal: Journal of health economics and outcomes research
papers.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being introduced into every stage of the health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) production line, from literature screening to causal estimation. The field lacks a defensible count of what has been done, and bibliometric claims about AI adoption circulate without measured error rates. Methods: Following PRISMA-ScR, we searched PubMed for AI terms co-occurring with HEOR terms for publications from 2010 through 2025, retrieved 2642 records, and included 2476 after screening. Records were classified into 8 nonexclusive application domains and 1 of 6 method categories using a published term dictionary. To quantify classification error, an independent large language model classifier, blinded to the dictionary labels and given only title and abstract, reclassified a random sample of 300 included records. We report per label counts, agreement, Cohen kappa, prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted kappa, precision, recall, F1, and a precision-adjusted corpus size with exact binomial intervals. We separately assembled the primary performance evidence for each HEOR workflow, requiring a quantitative metric from a primary study. Results: Included publications rose from 29 in 2010 to 852 in 2025, a factor of 29.4, with the inflection at 2018 to 2019 rather than at the release of ChatGPT. AI reached 6.0% of all indexed HEOR output in 2025 while HEOR fell to 0.86% of all indexed medical AI output. Economic evaluation was the most frequently assigned domain (1559/2476, 63.0%), followed by real-world data and causal inference (496, 20.0%) and governance, reporting, and validity (494, 20.0%). Generative AI appeared in no record before 2021 and in 103 in 2025. Only 154 of 300 sampled records (51.3%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 45.7-56.9) were judged genuinely HEOR relevant, implying a precision-adjusted corpus of 1271 studies (95% CI 1131-1410). Agreement was substantial for real-world data and causal inference (kappa, 0.729) but negligible for economic evaluation (kappa, 0.144), where dictionary precision was 29.6%. Of 2476 records, 38 (1.5%) were randomized trials and 17 (0.7%) validation studies. The replication package is publicly available. Conclusions: The literature is growing faster than its own measurement infrastructure. Measured gains concentrate in tasks with observable ground truth, and predictive performance repeatedly fails to predict evidentiary performance.
