papers.title: GLOBALIZATION, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND LEGAL ENGLISH: TRANSFORMING PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION IN LAW ENFORCEMENT
papers.authors: Лариса Володимирівна Дудікова, Марина Костюк, Viktoriia Mikaielian
papers.abstract: The article examines changes in professional English-language communication in law enforcement under the influence of globalization and the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI). Particular attention is given to Legal English as a means of international cooperation, professional information processing and interaction in intercultural settings. The study argues that contemporary language training for law enforcement professionals should move beyond the acquisition of specialized terminology and develop the ability to understand legal concepts in context, adapt communication to different audiences, and use digital tools critically and responsibly. Drawing on a narrative literature review and conceptual analysis of research in legal linguistics, intercultural police communication, AI-assisted language learning and large language models in legal contexts, the article identifies an emerging gap between these research areas and proposes their integration into a four-component framework of professional communicative competence. The framework comprises linguistic, professional-legal, intercultural and digital/AI competences. The article also outlines practical applications for Legal English teaching, including AI-assisted translation review and scenario-based police communication. Particular attention is given to accuracy, confidentiality, source verification and the limits of automated systems. The proposed framework can support the design of more realistic, human-centred and professionally relevant language training for future law enforcement professionals.

papers.title: Conocimiento y percepción de estudiantes de Odontología sobre la inteligencia artificial para diagnosticar caries y planificar restauraciones
papers.authors: Alexander Ricardo Aguilar-González, Marcos Daniel Arauz-Muñoz, Melissa Anahí Escobar-Naranjo, Gabriela Lizeth Carrera-Guanga
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence supports caries detection and restorative treatment planning. The objective was to analyze the knowledge and perception of dental students regarding its use. A quantitative, descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted through a digital survey applied to 24 students of the Universidad Regional Autónoma de los Andes between October 2025 and March 2026. Of these, 54.2% had received some training in digital technologies or artificial intelligence, but only 16.7% understood its dental application and none reported advanced knowledge. Half considered artificial intelligence useful for identifying carious lesions, and 83.3% expected a moderate or greater improvement in radiographic accuracy. No student considered it a replacement for the dentist, and 95.9% showed moderate or greater interest in training. It is concluded that perception is favorable, but training is limited.

papers.title: Inteligencia artificial en la enseñanza de la histología: aprendizaje automático y evaluación de estudiantes
papers.authors: Jenny Olivia Caicedo-Rodríguez, Carlos Alejandro Troya-Altamirano, Evelyn Carolina Betancourt-Rubio
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has been incorporated into medical education, and in histology it supports morphological interpretation, feedback and assessment. The study therefore aimed to synthesise the evidence on applications of artificial intelligence in histology teaching, with emphasis on machine learning and student assessment. A narrative review with a structured search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar, with a sample of publications from 2020 to 2025. Interaction data from virtual microscopy predicted academic performance, automated assessment improved efficiency but required validation, and large language models performed well in histology but inconsistently. It was concluded that artificial intelligence should be integrated as support for, not a substitute for, the teacher’s judgement.

papers.title: Simbiosis educativa: la inteligencia artificial generativa en el aprendizaje de la robótica
papers.authors: Edmundo José Jalón-Arias, Dionisio Vitalio Ponce-Ruiz, Luis Orlando Albarracín-Zambrano, Luis Javier Molina-Chalacán
papers.abstract: The objective was to analyze the effect of generative artificial intelligence, used as a programming and design assistant, on robotics learning and on the systems thinking of upper basic education students. A mixed approach was applied with an action research design and a quasi-experimental comparison between two intact ninth-grade classes: an experimental group of 28 students, which used it to design, program and debug robots, and a control group of 29 students, which worked with the traditional method. Observation guides, questionnaires, performance rubrics and the analysis of the prompt history were used. The experimental group corrected logic errors 40 % faster, developed modular projects and reported less frustration. It was concluded that generative artificial intelligence redirects effort toward logic and creativity when students are required to explain and verify the code.

papers.title: Modelo de gestión del desarrollo profesional docente basado en la cocreatividad transformadora con inteligencia artificial
papers.authors: Dionisio Vitalio Ponce-Ruiz, Edmundo José Jalón-Arias, Luis Orlando Albarracín-Zambrano, Luis Javier Molina-Chalacán
papers.abstract: The objective was to design a management model for teacher professional development that guides the incorporation of artificial intelligence into the training processes of a university campus in Quevedo, Ecuador. A mixed, non-experimental and descriptive design was used, with systemic, modeling, hermeneutic and inductive-deductive methods, and with triangulation of the observation of the practices of 36 teachers from Law, Dentistry and Obstetrics, surveys and interviews during 2024 and 2025. The results identified epistemic problems, such as the weakening of teacher authority, the opacity of algorithms and cognitive delegation, and practices that were still utilitarian or dependent on generated content. A relational model between human and artificial intelligence was proposed, driven by a spiral cycle and a ten-step sequence for working with prompts. It was concluded that the model provides a basis for critical and co-creative teacher training.

papers.title: Inteligencia artificial en el diseño de rutas de aprendizaje virtual: estrategias y aplicaciones pedagógicas
papers.authors: Luis Rafael Freire-Lescano, Elena Vicenta Hernández-Navarro, Alexandra Del Rocio Laguapillo-Vergara
papers.abstract: The objective was to examine the pedagogical strategies and applications based on artificial intelligence that favor the personalization of learning in the design of virtual learning pathways. A qualitative documentary study was carried out, organized into search, selection and analysis phases in scientific databases; of 74 documents identified, eight articles published between 2023 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. The results showed that adaptive systems, pathway recommenders based on knowledge graphs and intelligent tutors improve performance, efficiency and personalization, with better results when they integrate pedagogical rules and teacher supervision; challenges of privacy, accuracy and ethics persist. It was concluded that artificial intelligence is a pedagogical complement whose value depends on teacher mediation, and a model articulating artificial intelligence, pedagogical rules and the teacher's role was proposed.

papers.title: Software educativo basado en inteligencia artificial: aportes y riesgos percibidos en la educación superior
papers.authors: Bolivar Enrique Villalta-Jadan, Diego Paul Palma-Rivera, Luis Orlando Albarracín-Zambrano
papers.abstract: The objective was to analyze the use and perception of artificial intelligence-based educational software in teaching and learning processes in higher education, with attention to its contributions and risks. A descriptive, cross-sectional and non-experimental study was conducted, with a structured questionnaire applied to 80 university teachers and students. Of the participants, 66% used artificial intelligence tools always or frequently, mainly as support for academic tasks. Sixty percent considered that these tools improve learning and increase academic efficiency, although one quarter disagreed. Only 27.5% acknowledged ethical risks, and opinions on student dependence were divided between agreement (45%) and disagreement (47.5%). It was concluded that the university community values this software but underestimates its ethical implications, so its integration requires training in critical literacy and institutional guidelines.

papers.title: Actividades prácticas colaborativas y autónomas en la asignatura en línea Desarrollo del Pensamiento y Creatividad
papers.authors: Manuel Ricardo Rivas Bravo, Wilson Yovany Merino-Sánchez, Gerardo Ramos Serpa, Adriana López-Falcón
papers.abstract: The objective was to analyze the implementation of collaborative and autonomous practical activities in the course Development of Thought and Creativity, in the third level of the online Basic Education program at an Ecuadorian university, designed from initial proposals of a generative artificial intelligence tool and curated by the teacher. A qualitative action research was applied, with a non-experimental longitudinal design over eight weeks, through documentary analysis of lesson plans, a field diary and rubrics. Synchronous collaborative activities, such as thinking laboratories, material design and contextualized problem solving, fostered divergent and lateral thinking; asynchronous autonomous activities, such as reflection portfolios, material design and documentary research, consolidated metacognition. Teacher curation contextualized the proposals, added assessment criteria, deepened the theory and adjusted the timing. It was concluded that both modalities are complementary and that artificial intelligence does not replace pedagogical judgment.

papers.title: Inteligencia artificial y competencias emprendedoras en un proyecto de vinculación universitaria
papers.authors: Mireya Silvana Cuarán-Guerrero, Oswaldo Javier Torres-Merlo, Miriam Janneth Pantoja-Burbano, Sary del Rocío Álvarez-Hernández
papers.abstract: The objective was to analyze the contribution of artificial intelligence tools to the development of entrepreneurial competencies in a training program of a university community engagement project. A mixed-approach, non-experimental, cross-sectional study was carried out with 57 entrepreneurs who took part in ten virtual workshops between November 2025 and March 2026, assessed with questionnaires applied at the end of each workshop and observation. Of the participants, 70.2% had an ongoing business, 66.7% were women. Achievement levels ranged from 80% to 100%, with the highest values in brand identity, market analysis and business communication, and the lowest in basic financial management. It was concluded that practical training in artificial intelligence, accompanied by tasks applied to the business, favors the appropriation of management tools and knowledge transfer.

papers.title: Lógica institucional para incorporar la inteligencia artificial en la gestión de la calidad universitaria
papers.authors: Danilo Augusto Viteri-Intriago, Lyzbeth Kruscthalia Álvarez-Gómez, Dionisio Vitalio Ponce-Ruiz, Gilma Nelly Rivera-Segura
papers.abstract: The objective was to design an institutional logic that incorporates artificial intelligence as a complementary tool for decision-making in the quality management system of the Quevedo campus of the Universidad Regional Autónoma de los Andes. A mixed-approach, non-experimental, documentary and field study with a descriptive and propositional scope was carried out, which analyzed the scientific literature, the operational plans and the audits of the quality management system for 2024 and 2025, and gathered information through interviews with and observation of process leaders. The diagnosis showed that artificial intelligence was used mainly as an aid for routine writing and tabulation tasks. As a result, an institutional logic and a four-phase training plan articulated with teaching, research and community engagement were proposed. It was concluded that its incorporation requires training, ethical governance and continuous improvement cycles.
keywords: Universidad Regional Autónoma de los Andes

papers.title: Transformación digital e inteligencia artificial en la gestión administrativa de asociaciones productivas rurales
papers.authors: Myriam Paulina Barreno-Sánchez, Betty Giomara Valle Fiallos, Diego André Carrillo-Rosero, Norma Eulalia Barona-López
papers.abstract: The objective was to analyze the contribution of digital transformation and artificial intelligence to the administrative management of rural productive associations. A qualitative documentary study was conducted, with searches in Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, Redalyc and DOAJ and content analysis of 23 documents published between 2016 and 2026, organized into thematic categories. The results showed that artificial intelligence supports planning, accounting control, demand forecasting and marketing, but its adoption in small rural organizations is limited by low digital maturity, poor connectivity, costs, limited digital literacy and a lack of trained staff; associative networks and technical support favor adoption. It was concluded that the incorporation of these technologies should be progressive, begin with the digitization of records and rely on training and cooperation among members.

papers.title: Цифровая трансформация туристической отрасли как драйвер изменения требований к компетенциям персонала
papers.authors: Natal'ya V. TROFIMOVA, Э. Р. Мамлеева, Marina Sazykina, М.А. Ризванова
papers.abstract: В статье анализируется влияние цифровой трансформации туристической отрасли России на требования к компетенциям персонала. На основе статистических данных и отраслевых отчётов за 2024–2025 гг. выявлены ключевые тренды: интеллектуализация гостиничного бизнеса, внедрение искусственного интеллекта, развитие государственных цифровых платформ. Показано, что цифровизация ведёт к автоматизации рутинных операций, появлению гибридных функций и новых профессиональных ролей. Систематизированы цифровые компетенции (базовые, продвинутые, специализированные). Оценено соответствие образовательных программ запросам рынка, выявлены региональные диспропорции. Предложены направления модернизации профессионального образования. The article analyzes the impact of digital transformation of the Russian tourism industry on the requirements for personnel competencies. Based on statistical data and industry reports for 2024–2025, key technological trends are identified: intellectualization of the hotel business, introduction of artificial intelligence, development of government digital platforms, and import substitution of IT solutions. It is shown that digitalization leads to automation of routine operations, emergence of hybrid job functions and new professional roles. The demanded digital competencies are systematized into three levels: basic, advanced, and specialized. The compliance of existing higher and secondary vocational education programs with current labor market demands is assessed, and regional disparities and content gaps in personnel training are identified. Based on the obtained data, directions for modernizing the vocational education system in the digital economy are proposed.

papers.title: A descriptive literature review of the challenges and opportunities of generative artificial intelligence literacy and proficiency in South African higher education
papers.authors: Duduzile Penelope Zwane, Sakhiseni Joseph Yende
papers.abstract: Purpose. This study aims to examine the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in South African higher education, focusing on GenAI literacy and proficiency, as well as the opportunities and challenges associated with its adoption in teaching, learning, and research. Methodology. The study adopts a qualitative descriptive literature review approach. Data were sourced from 33 peer-reviewed journal articles, conference proceedings, and institutional reports relevant to GenAI literacy, proficiency, and higher education in the South African context. The selected literature was systematically analysed to identify recurring themes, patterns, and gaps related to GenAI integration. Results. The findings indicate that GenAI is increasingly influencing teaching, learning, and research practices in South African higher education institutions. Key challenges identified include inadequate digital infrastructure, limited GenAI literacy among staff and students, ethical concerns related to data privacy and academic integrity, and pedagogical uncertainties regarding responsible AI use. Conclusions. The study concludes that GenAI presents significant potential to transform South African higher education through innovative teaching and research practices. However, successful integration requires addressing AI literacy gaps, strengthening infrastructure, and implementing clear ethical and pedagogical guidelines. The study recommends that universities develop institutional policies to regulate ethical AI use and support capacity-building initiatives for both academics and students.

papers.title: Maintaining human agency in the post-digital university: A humane technology perspective on human–AI collaboration
papers.authors: Alane Naidoo
papers.abstract: Purpose. The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence in higher education has intensified debate about the future of teaching and learning in the post-digital university. Much of this debate is framed by discourses of efficiency, optimisation, automation, and innovation, often positioning AI as a solution to institutional and pedagogical challenges. This paper aims to argue that limited framings risk narrowing the university's educational purpose by marginalising human agency, relationality, critical thought, wisdom, lived experience, and well-being. Methodology. To address this concern, the paper adopts a theory-synthesis and framework-building approach, integrating scholarship on post-digital education, human-centred AI, relational pedagogy, wisdom, critical AI literacy, well-being, decoloniality, platform governance, and academic labour. This synthesis is used to develop a humane technology framework for human–AI collaboration in higher education. Results. The framework positions human agency as its organising principle, wisdom as its epistemic purpose, and human context, lived experience, personal voice, relational learning, belonging, and trust as key educational dimensions. Critical AI literacy is conceptualised as an enabling capability, while ethical well-being serves as the framework’s evaluative criterion. Decolonial justice, democratic platform governance, and dignified academic labour are presented as structural conditions necessary for humane implementation. Conclusions. The paper argues that AI should function as an augmentative rather than a substitutive resource, supporting teaching and learning while preserving human judgement, social connection, contextual understanding, and ethical responsibility.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence dalam Akuntansi Manajemen: Literature Review Manfaat dan Tantangan
papers.authors: Nurkholifah Burhanuddin, Arif Rahman Hasdik, Rafiqa Hastharita
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically map the benefits and challenges of artificial intelligence (AI) implementation in management accounting practice, and to interpret the resulting patterns through Disruptive Innovation Theory and the Theory of Planned Behavior. A systematic literature review (SLR) method was employed, analyzing articles indexed in the Google Scholar database and published between 2021 and 2025. Using predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria, 18 articles were selected for analysis. The findings indicate that AI implementation offers significant benefits for management accounting, including task automation, reduced human error, and enhanced capacity for strategic decision-making, consistent with the characteristics of disruptive innovation. However, the realization of these benefits is constrained by several challenges, including human resource reluctance toward new technology, inadequate training and data infrastructure, skills gaps, and the absence of clear regulation, data privacy, and ethical guidelines — factors that reflect low perceived behavioral control toward AI adoption. This study contributes to the management accounting literature by integrating two theoretical lenses rarely applied together to explain AI adoption dynamics, and offers practical implications for organizations and accounting education in preparing the workforce for AI-driven transformation.

papers.title: A Context-Adaptive AHP-WSM Model for Assessing Organizational Readiness for Co-Creation in Public Administration
papers.authors: Rok Hržica
papers.abstract: Public organizations require assessment approaches that capture the multiple conditions shaping readiness for co-creation. This study develops a context-adaptive AHP-WSM model for assessing organizational readiness for co-creation in public administration. A hierarchy of 81 basic criteria covering traditional and digital co-creation was operationalized through five-level ordinal scoring. Expert judgments were elicited through pairwise comparisons and aggregated by geometric mean within an Aggregation of Individual Judgments approach. The Analytic Hierarchy Process was used to derive criterion weights, and the Weighted Sum Model was used for hierarchical aggregation of organizational readiness scores. The model was evaluated through group-level consistency assessment, comparison of alternative administrative weighting schemes, rank concordance analysis, score deviation analysis, and sensitivity analysis at the category and subcategory levels. The results indicate acceptable group-level AHP consistency and differentiated expert priorities across the readiness hierarchy. Alternative administrative weighting schemes produced limited changes in final readiness scores and rankings, whereas category- and subcategory-level sensitivity analyses showed that changes in criterion weights could alter readiness-class assignments for selected organizational profiles. The resulting model provides a quantitative basis for context-adaptive assessment of organizational readiness for co-creation while retaining a common readiness hierarchy.

papers.title: Adaptive AI Governance Framework in the Territorial Context of a University Business Incubator: PRE–POST Perception Evidence, Stakeholder Heterogeneity, and Provisional Routing Rules
papers.authors: Alicia Cristina Silva Calpa, Oscar Gildardo Hernández Alomia
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is spreading across educational, productive, and institutional settings, creating a need for governance approaches that can adapt to heterogeneous stakeholders. This study proposes an adaptive AI governance framework for the territorial context of a university business incubator, in which the university acts as an articulating rather than a regulatory actor. The evidence comes from a PRE–POST questionnaire study of all 446 incubator affiliates in seven stakeholder groups, with illustrative records from 35 Metaplan working groups; between the two measurements, participants attended an AI training programme and discussed the questionnaire items in these groups. Perceived opportunities of AI governance (dz = 3.45) and the perceived feasibility of mitigating governance challenges (dz = 2.55) increased, but the single-group design, group deliberation, and possible response-shift, demand, and ceiling effects prevent attributing these changes to the programme. Baseline and post-assessment opportunity scores were strongly associated (β = 0.693), indicating relative stability; a positive association with baseline challenge salience is reported as exploratory. Stakeholder groups differed markedly at baseline and converged after the programme. The framework translates perception profiles into provisional routes—controlled scaling, regulatory strengthening, capacity building, and pilot redesign—whose thresholds were defined by the authors after the POST measurement, relative to the study population; controlled scaling additionally requires an independent risk assessment of the activity. The routes are a design proposition that requires validation against independent outcomes.

papers.title: A Calibrated Multi-LLM Consensus Framework for Reducing Model-Specific Scoring Asymmetry in EFL Writing Assessment
papers.authors: Zhongxing Zhao, Yingnan Wang, Junkai Li, Salasiah Che Lah
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in second-language (L2) writing assessment. However, substantial disparities persist in how different architectures operationalize shared scoring criteria. This study investigates model-specific assessment asymmetry across ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.5 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3, and evaluates whether a calibrated multi-LLM consensus framework can mitigate these scoring discrepancies. Forty argumentative essays composed by Chinese EFL learners were independently evaluated by the three models using a standardized prompt and an analytic rubric encompassing task relevance, clarity of ideas, coherence, and accuracy, benchmarked against human mean scores. Individual models and ensemble configurations were systematically validated across 100 iterations of five-fold nested cross-validation. Cross-model comparisons revealed that inter-model divergence varied significantly by dimension, exhibiting pronounced asymmetry in holistic ratings and task relevance compared to clarity of ideas, coherence, and accuracy. The full consensus framework—integrating model-specific calibration, error-based weighting, and meta-calibration—yielded an RMSE of 1.160 and an MAE of 0.889, relative to 1.144 and 0.874 for unweighted averaging. The paired RMSE difference of 0.016 (95% case-cluster bootstrap CI [−0.114, 0.149]) indicated no statistically significant advantage in overall predictive accuracy over equal weighting. Nevertheless, the calibrated framework achieved superior bias mitigation, evidenced by a reduced absolute mean bias and a narrower median-split residual gap. Supplementary analyses further delineated direct inter-model discrepancies and proficiency-dependent residual bias. These findings demonstrate that model-specific evaluative asymmetries transcend simple mean-level shifts, and that while calibration-driven consensus enhances bias regulation across score bands, this error control does not automatically translate into improved global predictive precision.

papers.title: Ethical Risks of Generative Large Language Models and Corporate Social Responsibility Performance: Evidence from China
papers.authors: Rongfei Li, Hongzhen Lei
papers.abstract: The ethical risks associated with generative large language models (GLLMs) raise concerns about their implications for corporate social responsibility (CSR). Drawing on firm-year observations for Chinese A-share companies over 2015–2024, we investigate how GLLM-related ethical risk relates to CSR performance. A firm-level disclosure-based measure of GLLM-related ethical risk signals is constructed from annual-report text and analyzed using two-way fixed-effect models. The results show a negative and statistically significant association, with higher ethical risk corresponding to lower subsequent CSR performance. This association persists across robustness checks and instrumental variable analyses. Firm-clustered bootstrap analyses reveal significant negative indirect associations through reputational pressure and financing constraints, supporting the proposed mediating pathways. Managerial compliance attention strengthens the negative association between ethical risk and CSR performance. These findings extend research on the antecedents of CSR by identifying the ethical risks of emerging technologies as a relevant organizational concern. They also highlight the importance of integrating ethical AI governance with CSR planning to support responsible technology adoption and sustained corporate sustainability commitments.

papers.title: Perceived AI Anthropomorphism and Brand Loyalty in Generative AI Services: The Roles of Confirmation, Brand Trust, Satisfaction, and Continuance Intention
papers.authors: Gamze EREN, Erkan Gülter, Muhammed Fatih Cevher
papers.journal: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence services combine functional performance with humanlike interaction, yet it remains unclear whether perceived humanlikeness contributes directly to post-use satisfaction or is associated primarily with more proximal performance and relational appraisals. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response framework, anthropomorphism theory and the Computers Are Social Actors perspective, the Expectation-Confirmation Model, and consumer–brand relationship research, this study examines perceived AI anthropomorphism (PAIA), confirmation, brand trust, satisfaction, continuance intention, and brand loyalty. Survey data were obtained from 555 ChatGPT users in Türkiye and analyzed using PLS-SEM. PAIA was strongly associated with confirmation (β = 0.624) and brand trust (β = 0.578), whereas its direct association with satisfaction was small (β = 0.081). Confirmation and brand trust were positively associated with satisfaction (β = 0.581 and β = 0.306), satisfaction was strongly associated with continuance intention (β = 0.705), and brand trust, satisfaction, and continuance intention were each positively associated with brand loyalty. Exploratory factor analysis, HTMT diagnostics, and confirmatory comparisons of alternative measurement structures showed substantial overlap between confirmation and satisfaction. The six-construct model fit better than the more parsimonious alternatives examined, but conclusions that depend on separating these two constructs are treated as tentative. Overall, PAIA was strongly associated with post-use and relational appraisals, but whether its association with satisfaction runs mainly through confirmation could not be established with confidence. Because the design is cross-sectional, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

papers.title: Color and Spatial Cue Modulation of Emotional Word Processing: Evidence from ERPs
papers.authors: Xiaoyang Luo, Chao LI, Yi Sun
papers.abstract: Emotional word processing is shaped by lexical meaning and concurrent perceptual context. This study investigated when red and green color cues and symbolic upward and downward direction cues modulate the processing of positive and negative Chinese emotional words. Thirty-four native Chinese speakers were recruited, and 27 remained in the final ERP sample after behavioral and EEG-quality exclusions. The experiment used a 2 (color: red vs. green) × 2 (direction: up vs. down) × 2 (word valence: positive vs. negative) within-subject design. Positive words elicited larger P1 amplitudes, and negative words elicited more negative-going N1 and N400 amplitudes. A significant Color × Valence interaction emerged in the late positive complex (LPC) window. The positive-minus-negative LPC difference was descriptively larger under green cues than under red cues, and neither within-color comparison reached significance after Bonferroni correction. Interactions involving spatial direction were not significant across the four components. These findings trace emotional word processing from early valence-sensitive visual attention through semantic processing to late color-dependent evaluation. The temporal pattern supports a context-sensitive account in which perceptual cues, lexical valence, and learned cultural associations contribute to emotional meaning at different processing stages.

papers.title: AI-Driven Fit Confidence in Fashion E-Commerce: How Personalization, Transparency, and Privacy Concerns Shape Consumer Experience and Purchase Intention
papers.authors: Alexander Sánchez-Rodríguez, Jesús Rodríguez-Flores, Andrés Fernando Morocho Caiza, Alexis Cordovés-García, Gelmar García-Vidal, Reyner Pérez-Campdesuñer
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming fashion e-commerce through personalized recommendations, virtual try-on, size suggestions, and algorithmic decision support. This study examines AI-driven fit confidence as a fashion-specific mechanism linking AI personalization quality, algorithmic transparency, trust in AI, consumer experience, and purchase intention, while considering privacy concern as a boundary condition. Data from 400 Ecuadorian consumers with prior exposure to AI-enabled recommendation or personalization features in fashion e-commerce were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. AI personalization quality and trust in AI were positively associated with fit confidence, while algorithmic transparency was associated with trust in AI. Fit confidence was strongly related to consumer experience but showed only a small direct association with purchase intention; its indirect effect through consumer experience was substantially larger, indicating complementary partial mediation. Privacy concern had no significant direct relationship with fit confidence. The interaction between privacy concern and personalization quality was negative, but evidence was mixed and sensitive to the bootstrap confidence-interval method; H7 was not supported under the primary percentile-bootstrap criterion adopted in this study. Predictive analyses showed stronger out-of-sample performance for trust in AI and fit confidence than for purchase intention. The study distinguishes trust in technology from confidence in anticipated product–consumer fit and supports explainable, privacy-sensitive applications in fashion e-commerce.

papers.title: The Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Self-Regulated Learning: A Meta-Analysis
papers.authors: Yiming Jin, Kamisah Osman, Nurazidawati Mohamad Arsad
papers.abstract: This meta-analysis systematically examined the effects of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on students’ self-regulated learning (SRL), including its overall effectiveness and its impact on the cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, and behavioral dimensions of SRL. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this study conducted a random-effects meta-analysis to synthesize evidence from 17 studies. The results revealed a statistically significant positive average effect of GenAI on SRL (Hedges’ g = 0.74). Nevertheless, substantial between-study heterogeneity suggested considerable variation in the magnitude of this effect across educational contexts. Positive average effects were also observed across the cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, and behavioral dimensions of SRL. However, a multilevel random-effects meta-analysis with CR2-robust inference indicated that effect sizes did not differ significantly across these dimensions (p = 0.564). Moderator analyses revealed significant differences in effect sizes associated with experimental design and intervention duration, whereas no significant differences were observed for subject domain, GenAI intervention type, GenAI tool, or personalization. Overall, the findings suggest that GenAI has the potential to contribute to the development of SRL, highlighting the importance of using GenAI as a scaffold to support, rather than replace, learners’ active self-regulatory processes.

papers.title: A Conversational AI Framework for Teacher Training
papers.authors: Sergio Miranda, Antonio Calvani
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ETQ-AI (Effective Teaching Questionnaire—Artificial Intelligence), a conversational AI framework designed to support teacher professional development by identifying pedagogical misconceptions and fostering critical reflection. Building on Evidence-Informed Education (EIE) principles, the system integrates a 50-item diagnostic questionnaire with an automated, Gemini-driven Explainable AI (XAI) feedback layer. When teachers complete the diagnostic form, they receive personalized feedback and can engage in dialogic interactions with Google Gemini to explore the underlying meta-analytic evidence (e.g., Hattie’s effect sizes, Cognitive Load Theory) or argue personal objections. We evaluated system fidelity against an expert panel benchmark (N=64 items) and conducted a pilot evaluation with 123 educators (70 primary teachers, 40 secondary teachers, 13 school leaders) recruited at an EIE conference. Gemini demonstrated high alignment with expert evaluations (97%), matching or exceeding static baseline feedback in user satisfaction (Mean = 4.1/5 vs. 3.8/5). Qualitative thematic analysis of 34 participant objections revealed key areas of tension, particularly around contextual constraints and pedagogical subjectivity. While the findings validate the technical proof-of-concept, system usability, and user engagement of ETQ-AI as an interactive scaffolding interface, we emphasize that this pilot study measures user perceptions and conversational patterns rather than direct pre/post shifts in critical reflection or classroom instructional practice.

papers.title: Eating Behavior, Body Appreciation, and Sleep Quality in Italian Blind Baseball Athletes: A Cross-Sectional Exploratory Survey
papers.authors: Giuditta Carretti, Sofia Lotti, Monica Dinu, Francesco Sofi, Mirko Manetti A, Barbara Colombini, Mirca Marini
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Visual impairment is associated with poor sleep quality, psychological distress, and unhealthy lifestyle behaviors. Adapted sports, such as blind baseball (BXC), may help promote healthy lifestyles and overall well-being. However, evidence regarding eating behavior, sleep quality, body appreciation, and lifestyle habits among regular BXC players remains scarce. This cross-sectional study provides an exploratory multidimensional characterization of these domains in competitive Italian BXC athletes according to sport participation and visual impairment characteristics, comparing findings descriptively with normative data from the Italian general population. Methods: Fifty-three competitive Italian BXC players (mean age 39.3 ± 13.1 years; representing a response rate of 49.1% of the national league) completed an anonymous online survey assessing eating behavior (Adult Eating Behavior Questionnaire, AEBQ), body appreciation (Body Appreciation Scale-2, BAS-2), sleep quality (Brief Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, B-PSQI), and lifestyle habits. Group differences were assessed using chi-square tests for categorical variables and Mann–Whitney U tests for continuous variables, reporting medians, interquartile ranges, effect sizes (rank-biserial r), and 95% confidence intervals. Results: BXC athletes demonstrated BMI, sleep quality, eating behavior, and body appreciation profiles comparable to those of the Italian general population. BAS-2 scores were high (3.7–3.8), while B-PSQI scores (4.0–5.6) and the proportion of poor sleepers (~40%) remained within normative ranges despite visual impairment. Eating behavior showed no significant dysregulation. However, in exploratory subgroup analyses, multisport athletes displayed lower Satiety Responsiveness than BXC-only athletes (2.30 ± 0.79 vs. 2.78 ± 0.71; p = 0.02), poorer sleep quality (B-PSQI: 6.05 ± 3.12 vs. 4.70 ± 3.73; p = 0.05), and a higher prevalence of poor sleep (55.0% vs. 30.3%). Athletes with acquired visual impairment showed higher Emotional Overeating and Emotional Undereating scores than those with congenital impairment, although these differences did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions: BXC athletes displayed an overall favorable lifestyle profile. Though the cross-sectional design prevents causal inferences, these exploratory findings indicate that participation in BXC is compatible with healthy lifestyle habits and positive body appreciation, hence supporting adapted team sports as an inclusive framework for multidimensional health promotion. Future studies using objective physiological assessments and longitudinal designs are needed to clarify dose–response relationships and long-term health outcomes.

papers.title: Menke–Hennekam Syndrome as a Domain-Resolved Disorder of the Transcriptional Coactivators CBP and p300
papers.authors: Despina Sanoudou, Anna Maria Anastasiou, Aristides G. Eliopoulos
papers.abstract: Menke–Hennekam syndrome (MKHK) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in discrete regions of the transcriptional coactivators CBP and p300, encoded by CREBBP and EP300. Recent genotype–phenotype and DNA methylation studies support a domain-resolved classification involving their ZZ, TAZ2 and ID4 regions and distinguish MKHK from classical Rubinstein–Taybi syndrome. Here, we review the genetic and clinical architecture of MKHK, the regulatory functions of the affected CBP/p300 domains and the emerging epigenomic taxonomy of the disorder. We discuss emerging evidence that localized variants may alter specific protein interactions, chromatin engagement or inter-domain regulation rather than uniformly reducing coactivator activity. On this basis, we propose domain-selective transcriptional rewiring as a testable framework for MKHK pathogenesis. We further consider experimental models required to establish causal mechanisms and implications for therapeutic development. MKHK provides an informative example of how pathogenic variants in multidomain regulatory proteins can produce domain-specific developmental disorders.

papers.title: Exploring Rural Children’s Ideal Healthy Smoothie: A Visual Focus Group Study
papers.authors: Tennessee Randall, Danni Walters, Natalie Rouse, Tomos Owens, Amanda Jane Lloyd, Louise Neilson, Laura L. Wilkinson
papers.abstract: Children can increase fruit and vegetable intake by consuming smoothies. However, most commercial smoothies contain excessive sugar due to the high proportion of apple juice within recipes. Including children, particularly those from potentially under-served communities, within the smoothie innovation journey is essential to develop healthier recipes that are also acceptable. Therefore, this study examined children’s perceptions of healthier smoothie base ingredients using a visual focus group methodology (i.e., creative drawing tasks with group discussions) that we have recently adapted for the food and drink industry context. Children attending a rural primary school (n = 28; 60.7% male) completed drawings on their current smoothie drinking behaviours, their ideal healthy smoothie, and barriers to consumption. Smoothies typically contained strawberries, bananas, blueberries, dairy-based milk, and ice, as well as calorically dense ingredients (e.g., ice cream and chocolate). Children’s ideal healthy smoothie contained fruit, ice and dairy-based milk, and the inclusion of vegetables, too many ingredients, a lumpy texture, and a large portion size were reported barriers. These findings highlight dairy-based milk, ice and whole fruit as potential ingredients for future product formulations, as well as the importance of co-creation and the effectiveness of visual focus groups as a method to elicit children’s ideas.

papers.title: From Answer Generator to Questioning Coach: Designing AI-Assisted Coaching for Self-Regulated Learning in Higher Education
papers.authors: Sherif Welsen
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support self-regulated learning (SRL), but its pedagogical value depends on whether interaction elicits learner cognition or substitutes for it. This study examined how students’ reported use of GenAI corresponded to an intended question-first coaching design, the perceived processes and tensions associated with SRL, and conditions relevant to potential scale. A qualitatively driven embedded case study utilized 31 reflective portfolios as the primary dataset, complemented by 53 survey responses and 68 weekly logs from 12 maximum-variation cases. Abductive, reflexive thematic analysis generated five themes. Question-led interaction appeared most useful when it prompted problem reframing, led to a bounded evidence-producing action, and preserved learner judgment through evaluation, modification, or rejection of AI suggestions. Benefits were qualified by role drift, generic interaction, cognitive substitution, uneven engagement, and continued need for human support. The findings support a distributed coaching-system interpretation in which AI-supported elicitation, pedagogical scaffolding, learner agency, reported AI-role configuration, and function-specific human support interact. The study does not demonstrate institutional scalability; instead, it identifies scale-relevant conditions including sustained engagement, manageable scaffolding, role boundaries, safety, learner judgment, and routes to human expertise.

papers.title: Beyond Acceptance and Resistance: Digital Media Students’ Judgements of Generative AI Assistance and Perceived Creative Replacement
papers.authors: Regina John Luan, Brendan Murphy
papers.abstract: This study investigated how Digital Media students judged acceptable and problematic forms of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) involvement in creative learning. An embedded mixed-methods analysis examined 48 completed and consented baseline survey responses from an accessible population of 120 students at an Australian university. Forty-seven responses were valid for most Likert items, with qualitative content analysis of 37 benefit responses and 41 concern responses. Participants identified potential value in troubleshooting, coding support, grammar checking, information organisation, and error identification. They reported concern about AI-system training practices (93.6%), reduced employment opportunities (89.4%), the ethical acceptability of AI-supported coursework (83.0%), environmental effects (80.9%), and possible reductions in creative-skill development (76.6%). These percentages represent perceived risks, not demonstrated outcomes. Integration indicated that respondents differentiated bounded technical, corrective, and organisational assistance from GenAI involvement perceived to displace ideation, research, planning, understanding, or capability-building practice. Conditional legitimacy is proposed as a provisional framework linking delegated function, retained capability-building activity, learner agency and responsibility, and ethical and professional acceptability. The contribution is a student-informed account of the criteria underlying the assistance–perceived replacement distinction in Digital Media education.

papers.title: Beyond Answer Generation: University Teachers’ Experiences with a Reflective GenAI Chatbot for Professional Learning
papers.authors: Linda Bradley, Jonas Karlén, Niklas Segergren, Mattias von Feilitzen, Daniel Johansson
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used in higher education, yet limited research has examined how university teachers’ experience pedagogically designed AI systems that prioritize reflective learning over answer generation. This exploratory mixed-methods case study investigated university teachers’ experiences of a course-specific GenAI chatbot within a professional-development course at a Swedish university. All 48 course participants were invited to complete a questionnaire, of whom 21 responded and 11 reported using the course-specific chatbot; nine respondents also participated in semi-structured interviews. Questionnaire data were analyzed descriptively and interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The chatbot was designed to encourage dialogue, engagement with course literature, and independent thinking rather than provide summaries or ready-made answers. Participants generally found the chatbot easy to use, but perceptions of usefulness varied. Evaluations were shaped by prior experiences and expectations of GenAI: some teachers, who associated AI with efficiency and rapid answers, perceived the reflective design as restrictive, while others perceived its value as supporting dialogue and independent thinking. We interpret this tension as pedagogical friction, where design constraints intended to support reflection may conflict with users’ expectations of how GenAI should function. The findings suggest that the perceived educational value of GenAI depends not only on technical usability but also on alignment between pedagogical design, users’ expectations, and educational context. Successful implementation of reflective AI may therefore require explicit pedagogical framing alongside technical development.

papers.title: The Cost of Algorithmic Assessment: How AI Grading Undermines Academic Motivation and Amplifies AI Reliance Intentions
papers.authors: Jae‐Eun Namkoong, Thomas A. Burnham
papers.abstract: This research examines the psychological consequences of an AI deployment policy wherein instructors use AI to grade student work while discouraging students from using AI to produce it. Drawing on expectancy-value theory, procedural justice, social exchange, and algorithm aversion frameworks, we experimentally test a psychological model in which algorithmic (vs. human) assessment reduces perceived policy fairness and expected grading accuracy, which in turn lowers prospective students’ appraisals of the course and diminishes their intentions to exert effort. Lower willingness to exert effort, in turn, is associated with increased intentions to rely on AI for task completion against instructional policy. These effects are moderated by prior AI familiarity: individuals with less AI experience perceive algorithmic assessment as more unfair and inaccurate, amplifying negative downstream consequences. The findings contribute to the understanding of how the deployment of AI for assessment by those in authority roles shapes behavioral responses, with implications for the design of assessment policies, AI use guidelines, and instructor practice in higher education.

papers.title: Bridging the Human–AI Trust Gap: The Mechanisms Underlying Perceived Efficacy of AI-Powered Psychological Counseling Large Language Models
papers.authors: Yi Wang, Mingchao Yin, Kun Lv
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the delivery of mental health services, yet public trust in AI-based psychological counseling remains a significant challenge. Drawing on a “technology–context–trust” framework, this study recruited a total of 1000 consumers in China through Credamo and conducted five between-subjects, scenario-based experiments to examine differences in perceived efficacy between LLM-based psychological counseling and human experts and to investigate the mechanisms underlying these differences. Perceived efficacy was the primary outcome of the study and, in Experiment 1B, also served as a mediator linking counseling provider type to downstream market outcomes, including overall attitude, willingness to try, and willingness to pay. The results showed that (1) consumers generally perceived AI as less efficacious than human experts, a difference driven by the parallel mediating effects of perceived professional competence and perceived risk; (2) participants rated the AI-based service as more efficacious in the routine counseling vignette, whereas they rated the human-expert service as more efficacious in the major psychological-disorder intervention vignette; (3) disclosure of technological investment enhanced trust in AI’s capabilities and mitigated negative evaluations; and (4) safety-standard disclosure reduced perceived risk, while higher perceived economic accessibility was associated with a smaller provider-related difference in perceived professional competence. These findings characterize subjective service evaluations among the recruited online consumers in China and do not establish comparative clinical effectiveness. They inform research on consumer trust while highlighting the need for further validation in more diverse samples and actual service settings.

papers.title: The Effects of Cognitive–Perceptual Style on the Multilevel Organization of Postural Control During Motor Imagery and Immersive Virtual Reality
papers.authors: G. V. Iskarevskii, E. B. Vinogradova, Ivan Afanevich, Vladislav Ogarkov, Ekaterina Zyuzya, Margarita Nikulina, Artur Fedianin, Dmitry Onishchenko, Maxim E. Baltin
papers.abstract: Understanding the central nervous system responses to different threats of balance loss is instrumental for developments in behavioral neurophysiology and rehabilitation. Motor imagery (MI) and virtual reality (VR) are used to model postural threats. Cognitive–perceptual style, specifically field independence and field dependence, is known to modulate the postural response. However, data comparing responses to MI (internally generated threat) and VR (externally induced multisensory conflict) while accounting for cognitive–perceptual style remain insufficient. The degree of visual dependence, assessed using the Rod-and-Frame Test (RFT), was evaluated in 55 healthy young adults. Stabilographic parameters and surface electromyography were recorded during four stances (open eyes, closed eyes, MI of free fall, and VR simulation of free fall). At the systemic level, VR induced the most pronounced destabilization (q < 0.001). Greater RFT error (indicative of field dependence) was associated with the greatest instability (q < 0.01). At the neuromuscular level, VR was accompanied by increased gastrocnemius medialis activity (q < 0.0001). Micro-level analysis revealed significant changes in EMG signal complexity during VR and in association with RFT (q < 0.05 and q < 0.0001), suggesting differences in neuromuscular signal complexity. MI and VR differentially modulated postural control, with VR inducing stronger effects. Adaptations were detectable at multiple levels of adaptation, ranging from systemic destabilization to changes in neuromuscular coordination and micro-level muscle activity. Visual dependence was associated with greater instability. These data point to the potential value of accounting for individual variations in visual information use and highlight the need to further investigate these effects in clinical populations.

papers.title: EduBot: Integrating Federated Learning and RAG for Educational Document Analysis
papers.authors: Begüm Erva Şahin, Murat Görkem Çoban, Ahmet Sayar, Meltem Kurt Pehli̇vanoğlu
papers.abstract: There is a growing demand for intelligent and secure document management systems in the education sector, driven by the exponential growth of digital content. Nevertheless, classic centralized machine learning methods pose major privacy challenges. In this study, we present EduBot, a decentralized intelligent framework for education that integrates Federated Learning (FL) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ensure privacy and deliver an advanced user experience for content interaction. EduBot introduces a dual-mechanism architecture that enables users to interact with their private documents in real time via a RAG-based conversational interface while also allowing local fine-tuning of a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapter on the same data. The masked adapter updates are aggregated on a central server using the Federated Averaging method, enabling collaborative learning without exposing any private documents. The system was evaluated using 29 textbooks published by the Turkish Ministry of National Education (MoNE) and 1318 validated questions. Federated Learning (FL) produced a single unified model that could be deployed across all three domains without sharing the underlying documents. The RAG system retrieved the correct source page among the top five results for 93.3% of the questions. When combined with RAG, the FL model achieved the highest answer quality among the Qwen2.5-1.5B-based models, outperforming the centralized model (token F1 of 0.067 and 0.053, respectively). Overall, our study validates the feasibility of developing privacy-preserving AI assistants that can support educational ecosystems without centralizing sensitive data.

papers.title: Designing interactive VR scenarios for speech and language therapy with the assessment framework
papers.authors: Tsvetelin Stefanov, Анна Андреева, Gergana Padareva-Ilieva, Anna Kostadinova Lekova
papers.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) games are becoming increasingly popular for entertainment. When integrated into speech and language therapy (SLT) practice, VR can be an innovative tool that supports therapeutic interventions by offering new opportunities for immersive interaction and greater motivation for individuals with language disorders to participate in therapy. In this study, we aim to introduce a methodology for designing interactive VR serious-game scenarios for speech and language therapy, together with an integrated multidisciplinary user-feedback assessment framework. The research methodology is based on design research principles and an innovative UX framework to guide the design, evaluation, and improvement process. The feasibility and usability of the methodology and framework are demonstrated through preliminary interactive sessions involving 10 children and adolescents with language disorders (5–13 years) and 10 students undergoing speech and language therapy. Their role was to evaluate the serious VR games developed in accordance with specific speech and language therapy goals. The assessment framework consists of a four-level VR serious game hub statistics module, phonetic and linguistic analysis of children’s and adolescents’ utterances from the serious game sessions, and usability and design questionnaires. As a result, six VR serious games with integrated large language model (LLM)-based conversational AI were designed for speech and language therapy. Based on the outcomes, a safety protocol for conducting VR-based therapeutic activities was proposed. We used descriptive statistics and Friedman and Wilcoxon post hoc tests with Bonferroni-adjusted p -values for pairwise comparisons of questionnaires and speech and language assessment data. While preliminary, the results of the phonetic and linguistic analyses conducted using Praat indicate that the VR serious games effectively capture and maintain children’s attention, elicit a high level of emotional expressiveness, and motivate them to communicate. The feedback collected through the participant questionnaires showed that the VR serious games provided a highly positive user experience. No symptoms of cybersickness or dizziness were observed during the game sessions. Younger children interacted with the VR environment using controllers, while older individuals preferred interaction with hand gestures. The proposed solution can be personalized to individual therapeutic needs, enabling children with language disorders to be engaged in therapy, while the conversational AI integrated into VR stimulates not only expressive development but also receptive language development. To confirm the promising preliminary results, further evaluations with a larger group of children and longitudinal studies are required.

papers.title: A multilingual heterogeneous knowledge graph framework for curriculum–vacancy–MOOC alignment: edge-weight regression with heterogeneous graph transformers for educational recommendation
papers.authors: Sandugash Serikbayeva, Madina Sambetbayeva, Valiya Ramazanova, Zhanar Lamasheva, Aigerim Yerimbetova, Valentina E. Makhatova, Zhanna B. Sadirmekova
papers.abstract: Introduction Digitalisation and artificial intelligence have widened the gap between competencies certified by university curricula and skills demanded by employers. MOOCs could close this gap, but existing recommenders rarely connect what a programme teaches, what the market requires, and what online courses develop within a single semantic structure. Methods We built a multilingual heterogeneous knowledge graph (KG) that integrates university programmes, IT vacancies from hh.kz, and Coursera MOOCs in English, Russian, and Kazakh. A property-graph ontology was formalised and instantiated automatically. Skills were aligned with a fine-tuned multilingual Sentence Transformer (paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2), and agglomerative clustering formed skill communities. Recommendation was cast as edge-weight regression over a competency-to-course relation and solved with GraphSAGE, HAN, and HGT encoders. Results On a held-out 20% test graph, HGT achieved the best ranking quality (NDCG@10 = 0.714; with short meta-paths NDCG@10 = 0.987, RMSE = 0.108), outperforming GraphSAGE and HAN. Applied to the “Information Systems” programme of a Kazakhstani university, the system expanded the market-aligned competency profile by +36.2% with five top-ranked courses and by +170% with the full catalogue. Discussion Edge-weight regression on a cross-domain heterogeneous KG produces front-loaded, actionable course recommendations for curriculum alignment. All datasets, models, graph snapshots, and code are released for reproducibility.

papers.title: Comparative quality, readability, and factual reliability of four publicly accessible chatbot systems for heart failure patient education: a cross-sectional evaluation
papers.authors: Nana Qin, Xinran Shao, Jing Wang, Jing Lei, Ran Wen, Wenjun Wu, Fangxu Liu, Hongwei Wang, Yan Zhu
papers.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for health information delivery, but comparative evidence on their quality, readability, and factual reliability in heart failure (HF) education remains limited. Objective To compare four publicly accessible chatbot systems under prespecified access and retrieval configurations in answering common heart failure–related questions. Methods We evaluated 108 standardized English HF questions, yielding 432 responses. Content quality was assessed using modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) and Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP), readability was assessed using established English-language readability indices, including the Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG), Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES), Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Automated Readability Index (ARI), Gunning Fog Index (GFOG), and Coleman-Liau Index (CLI), and factual reliability was evaluated by auditing all responses against the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline and relevant clinical evidence. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Hallucination outcomes were defined as clinically meaningful statements that were inconsistent with guidelines, unsupported by evidence, overgeneralized beyond the relevant population, or potentially misleading for patient education, and were analyzed using Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs), Cochran’s Q test, and generalized estimating equation (GEE) logistic regression. Results DeepSeek generally showed the most favorable content-quality profile across the evaluated domains. In the primary readability analysis, Perplexity generated the most complex text, whereas sensitivity analysis using a second calculator showed partially different rankings. Hallucinations were identified in 6/108 (5.56%) DeepSeek responses, 8/108 (7.41%) ChatGPT responses, 10/108 (9.26%) Copilot responses, and 16/108 (14.81%) Perplexity responses. Paired binary analyses showed significant differences among chatbot systems (Cochran’s Q p = 0.002; GEE p = 0.006). Conclusion Under the tested conditions and evaluated model versions, DeepSeek generally showed the most favorable content-quality profile and the lowest observed hallucination rate. However, hallucinations occurred across all systems, and pairwise factual-reliability differences were mainly driven by the higher hallucination rate of Perplexity. Guideline-aligned verification and clinician oversight remain necessary before patient-facing use.

papers.title: Institutional digitalization and digital stress: a four-wave observational study of teacher-reported AI-collaborative teaching in physical education
papers.authors: Xiangyu Wang, Xiangyu Wang, Wang Xiaoyun, Wang Xiaoyun
papers.abstract: Introduction How institutional digitalization relates to teachers’ experience of work and subsequent artificial intelligence (AI)-supported practice remains unclear. Methods Drawing on job demands-resources principles, we examined these relationships in a four-wave observational cohort of 961 physical education teachers from 120 Chinese institutions. We linked an organizational-source digitalization proxy to teacher questionnaires and a study-specific teacher-reported score of AI involvement in teaching tasks. Analyses adjusted for baseline practice and separated between-institution from teacher-relative associations. Results Two of five primary tests met the Holm-adjusted criterion. The stress-related product of between-institution coefficients was negative (−0.099; pointwise 95% confidence interval [−0.184, −0.033]). The positive digitalization–stress association was weaker among teachers with higher digital self-efficacy relative to colleagues (interaction coefficient −0.101; [−0.168, −0.037]) but remained positive at the low, average, and high self-efficacy levels examined. The adjusted digitalization–practice association, appraisal-related coefficient product, and appraisal interaction did not meet the corrected criterion. Discussion The findings connect the organization and experience of work with reported AI practice, emphasizing perceived digital work pressure and relative self-efficacy while complementing accounts centered on technology acceptance.

papers.title: Authenticity across human and synthetic influencers: a configurational review of source evaluation and social influence
papers.authors: Xiao-Rui Lin, Amily Binti Fikry, Wei-Guo Zhang, Kai Ding
papers.abstract: Introduction Authenticity has become a central concern in social media influencer research, yet its construction is examined differently across human, virtual, and artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated sources. This study examines how authenticity is constructed and evaluated across these influencer contexts. Methods This study conducted a corpus-based review of 1,676 English-language research articles indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus between July 2017 and March 2026. BERTopic modeling was employed to identify recurring semantic topics, followed by an abductive, theory-informed synthesis organized around source ontology and the dominant basis of authenticity construction. Temporal changes in relative topic prevalence were examined across the eight complete calendar years from 2018 to 2025. Results The synthesis identified four configurations: relational human authenticity, curated human authenticity, humanized synthetic authenticity, and governed synthetic authenticity. Human-influencer research emphasizes biography, accumulated interaction, commercial congruence, and motive transparency, whereas synthetic-influencer research places greater weight on persona coherence, humanization, identity disclosure, ownership, automation, and accountability. Credibility, trust, parasocial interaction, social presence, and engagement emerge as closely associated evaluative processes. Temporal analysis revealed selective changes in relative topic prevalence, particularly concerning virtual-influencer credibility, humanization, and tourism-related applications, while most topics showed no clear linear trend. Discussion The findings provide a corpus- and method-dependent framework for understanding how authenticity is constructed and evaluated across human and synthetic influencer contexts. The framework highlights distinct evidential foundations underlying authenticity judgments and offers a basis for further research on source evaluation and social influence.

papers.title: Feeling or thinking? User aversion to AI customer service in online education
papers.authors: Yuan He, Lin Huang
papers.abstract: Introduction AI customer service is increasingly integrated into online education, yet users may not always respond favorably to AI-assisted service interactions. Drawing on robotic role theory, this study examines how thinking and feeling AI customer service influence user aversion in online educational service encounters. Methods Three experiments were conducted to examine the effect of AI customer service type on user aversion (Study 1, N = 120), the mediating role of perceived intelligence (Study 2, N = 120), and the moderating role of AI identity disclosure timing (Study 3, N = 120). Across the three between-subjects experiments, thinking AI was operationalized through analytical, information-processing, and task-oriented communication, whereas feeling AI emphasized emotional recognition and relational support. Results The results show that feeling AI generates greater user aversion than thinking AI. Perceived intelligence mediated this effect, such that feeling AI is perceived as less intelligent, which in turn increases user aversion. Further, AI identity disclosure timing moderates the indirect effect through perceived intelligence. Early disclosure of AI identity attenuates the negative effect of feeling AI. Discussion These findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of different AI customer service types depends on the service context and highlight the importance of aligning AI communication with users’ task-oriented service needs.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and its influence on student engagement in higher education
papers.authors: Yongsheng Chen, Jing Dong, 冀国娟
papers.abstract: Empirical evidence on how artificial intelligence (AI) relates to student engagement in culturally diverse higher-education settings remains limited. In Chinese university classrooms, where interaction is often teacher-led and asking questions in class can carry a social cost, AI-driven dialogic tools may offer low-pressure opportunities for active participation. This study examined the association between an AI conversational agent (EduBot) and the behavioural, cognitive, emotional and agentic dimensions of engagement among Chinese undergraduates. A mixed-methods quasi-experimental design involved 555 students in four comprehensive (multi-disciplinary, research-intensive) universities, each contributing one introductory course taught in two parallel sections. Within a 15-week semester, intervention sections (n = 278) used EduBot, a Socratic-dialogue agent embedded in the learning management system, for 12 weeks; control sections (n = 277) used teaching-assistant-moderated forums. We measured engagement at three time points with a 21-item four-dimensional engagement scale adapted from an established measure and supplemented it with system logs, 30 student interviews and instructor focus groups. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for the nesting of students within course sections, together with mixed-design ANOVAs, showed Group × Time interactions for behavioural (η 2 p = 0.043, post-test d = 0.71), cognitive (η 2 p = 0.032, d = 0.55), agentic (η 2 p = 0.054, d = 0.57) and emotional engagement (η 2 p = 0.012, d = 0.34), all p ≤ 0.001 after Holm adjustment. Within the intervention group, the number of EduBot sessions predicted post-test engagement after adjustment for baseline scores and covariates. Exploratory moderation analyses indicated larger agentic gains among first-year students and larger cognitive gains among students with lower prior GPA. Thematic analysis identified three hypothesised mechanisms, namely a judgment-free interaction space, scaffolded persistence and temporal flexibility. A Socratic-scaffolded AI agent was associated with higher engagement, most clearly for agentic engagement, which participants described as constrained by classroom norms. The findings support culturally attentive AI design and suggest, tentatively, an equity-enhancing potential. Because the design compared an integrated AI package with usual practice across eight sections, the effects cannot be attributed to single design components.

papers.title: Intelligent scaffolding for musical practice: a systematic review of AI and digital support for the self-regulated learning cycle
papers.authors: Xiuran Li, Mar Galera-Núñez, Yao Zhang
papers.abstract: Introduction Independent music practice depends on learners’ self-regulated learning (SRL), yet how digital tools and artificial intelligence (AI) support the forethought, performance, and self-reflection phases of the SRL cycle, and when such support may undermine learner autonomy, remains unclear. Methods Following PRISMA 2020, we searched Web of Science, Scopus, ERIC, and PsycINFO through March 2026. Sixteen empirical studies met the inclusion criteria and were appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Because of methodological heterogeneity, we conducted a thematic synthesis rather than a meta-analysis. Results Three categories emerged: traditional digital tools, discriminative AI, and generative AI. Traditional tools supported planning and reflection; discriminative AI enabled real-time error detection; and generative AI may help learners manage task difficulty and translate expert feedback into actionable steps. Study quality was uneven, and several findings came from small-sample or cross-sectional designs, which limits causal inference. Two potential risks, over-scaffolding that may diminish autonomy and visual feedback that may divert attention from sound, were insufficiently studied. Discussion Digital and AI tools appear to scaffold different phases of SRL, but learner autonomy should remain at the core. Fading explicit support and pedagogical guidance may help reduce dependence. Longitudinal studies are required to test these mechanisms.

papers.title: Digital attention disruption and academic impact in adolescents: a data-driven network and machine learning analysis
papers.authors: Yan Liu
papers.abstract: Academic impact associated with digital media use is a topic of considerable concern in the fields of adolescent mental health and education; however, the role of attention status in this context remains largely unknown. The present study aimed to systematically investigate the multidimensional association patterns between attention-related characteristics and academic impact among adolescents using data mining approaches. The data were derived from two publicly available cross-sectional survey datasets, and a final sample of 799 adolescents aged 19 years and below was included after age screening. The analytical framework integrated LASSO regression, regularized partial correlation network analysis based on EBICglasso, XGBoost predictive modeling with SHAP interpretation, and latent profile analysis. Results showed that LASSO regression identified stress level (coefficient = 0.384) and social media use duration (coefficient = 0.297) as the strongest predictors of academic impact. Network analysis revealed a three-community structure, corresponding to the “digital distraction load,” “psychological-academic exhaustion,” and “academic engagement” dimensions, with academic impact located at the intersection of the first two communities. The XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.842, and SHAP dependence plots further revealed a nonlinear pattern with an inflection point at approximately 3.5 hours for daily social media use duration and a nonlinear effect of stress level. Latent profile analysis identified three subgroups, among which the “high stress-exhaustion” group showed a probability of academic impact as high as 79.4%. These findings indicate that attention-related characteristics can effectively predict academic impact status in adolescents, with stress level, social media use duration, and number of notifications constituting the most influential set of predictors. The results provide data-driven theoretical evidence and practical implications for the early identification and stratified intervention of academic impact in adolescents.

papers.title: Motor action observation evaluation questionnaire: development and initial validity evidence for the scores in people with and without chronic low back pain
papers.authors: Roy La Touche, Prado Silván‐Ferrero, Encarnación Nouvilas-Pallejà, Alba Paris‐Alemany, Alfonso J. López-Rivero, Miguel Ángel Sorrel
papers.abstract: Introduction Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is highly prevalent and associated with functional limitations. Although action observation is increasingly used as a cognitive–motor rehabilitation strategy, no brief instrument exists to assess how individuals appraise and understand movements during observation. Methods The Questionnaire for the Assessment of Motor Action Observation (CENOAM) was developed using a sequential mixed-methods design. Phase 1 involved item generation based on literature review and qualitative analysis, followed by expert content validation using Aiken’s V . Phase 2 consisted of a cross-sectional study including 280 participants (140 with CLBP and 140 asymptomatic). Dimensionality and psychometric properties of the CENOAM scores were examined using exploratory factor analysis, complementary dimensionality methods, internal consistency ( α , ω ), floor and ceiling effects, concurrent associations, and known-groups comparisons, following COSMIN recommendations. Results The final seven-item instrument showed a parsimonious two-dimensional structure, comprising Familiarity and Competence–Demand, supported by converging evidence across multiple methods. Internal consistency was high for both total and subscale scores, and no floor or ceiling effects were observed. CENOAM scores were positively associated with motor imagery ability, physical activity, and pain self-efficacy, and negatively associated with fear of movement. Participants with CLBP showed significantly lower scores than asymptomatic individuals across all dimensions, with large effect sizes. Conclusion The CENOAM provides a brief and interpretable measure of movement appraisal during action observation. Its scores show initial evidence of validity and may support the individualization of action-observation–based rehabilitation in musculoskeletal conditions.

papers.title: Dynamic adaptation of attentional control across bilingual interactional contexts
papers.authors: Min Li, Xiangyu Shi, Qinghong Xu, Jie Li
papers.abstract: Background/objectives Bilingual experience is thought to shape cognitive control via adaptive attentional reorganization, yet the neural mechanisms by which different interactional contexts dynamically modulate attentional control remain unclear. This study used EEG to examine how Chinese monolingual, English monolingual, bilingual, and voluntary naming contexts influence attentional control in Chinese–English bilinguals. Methods Thirty-five bilinguals completed picture-naming tasks in different contexts, followed by an antisaccade task with concurrent EEG. We analyzed reaction time, ERPs, frontal and parietal delta/theta power, and frontoparietal functional connectivity (wPLI).
