Results Bilingual and voluntary naming contexts shortened antisaccade reaction times (all p < 0.01). No significant main effect of context was found on N2 amplitudes ( p = 0.615). Both contexts reduced parietal delta and theta power relative to the English monolingual context (all p < 0.05). Exploratory connectivity analysis initially suggested bilingual-context effects, but this finding did not survive homologous ROI validation. These preliminary sensor-level findings await validation by source-localized EEG or fMRI. Conclusions These findings suggest that bilingual and voluntary naming contexts may facilitate attentional control through adaptive reorganization of the attentional system rather than through enhancing a specific inhibitory process. This pattern is consistent with the adaptationist perspective on bilingual cognition and provides preliminary neural evidence for the language mode theory.

papers.title: Naturalistic language assessment and brain-network biomarkers in post-stroke aphasia for precision neurorehabilitation
papers.authors: Jiayi Xia, Song Pei, Song ZHOU, Yulong Bai
papers.abstract: Advances in naturalistic language assessment, portable neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and brain-network modeling are creating new opportunities to evaluate post-stroke aphasia under conditions closer to real-world communication. Conventional aphasia batteries and isolated linguistic tasks remain essential for diagnosis, severity classification, and treatment planning, but they provide limited information about how language-network activity supports communication in dynamic, naturalistic contexts. This integrative review, informed by a structured literature search and descriptive thematic mapping, synthesizes evidence on connected speech, discourse production, narrative comprehension, interactive communication, and contextual reading after stroke. We examine how multilevel features from these behaviors can be organized into graded, interacting dimensions of lexical-semantic access, phonological encoding, grammatical organization, discourse processing, executive-predictive control, and speech-motor output. We further review multimodal evidence from fNIRS, fMRI, EEG/ERP, lesion-symptom mapping, structural connectivity, and functional connectivity, highlighting residual left-hemisphere language networks, conditional right-hemisphere support, bilateral reorganization, domain-general control systems, and longitudinal recovery. Portable EEG and fNIRS are considered complementary approaches for repeated assessment during less constrained language tasks, with distinct temporal, spatial, and practical trade-offs. Building on this evidence, we propose an operational ecological biomarker framework that links task choice, multilevel feature extraction, multivariate behavioral profiles, neural measures, prespecified clinical questions, and longitudinal outcomes. This framework may support recovery prediction, rehabilitation stratification, neuromodulation target selection, individualized therapy planning, and monitoring of functional communication.

papers.title: Post-traumatic headache as a window into persistent brain dysfunction after traumatic brain injury: an opinion article
papers.authors: Denise Franco de Almeida Duarte, Jader Vinicius Da Silva Rocha, Fernanda Moura Vargas Dias, Micheline Henrique Araújo da Luz Koerich, Vitória Caroline Reinoso de Almeida, Rodrigo Freire de Almeida, Walter Gomes da Silva Filho, Fernando Zanela da Silva Arêas
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major cause of death and disability worldwide, particularly among young adults and individuals of working age (1,2). Advances in prehospital care, neurosurgery, and intensive care have improved survival after TBI, increasing attention to the persistent symptoms and functional limitations that may affect long-term recovery and quality of life (1,2).Post-traumatic headache (PTH) is a secondary headache attributed to traumatic injury to the head, including TBI, and is among the most frequent neurological symptoms reported after TBI (3)(4)(5)(6). In this article, we specifically address PTH occurring in the context of TBI rather than the broader category of headache attributed to head injury without established TBI. Consistent with the International Classification of Headache Disorders, PTH that persists for more than three months is referred to here as persistent PTH (3). Persistent PTH may coexist with fatigue, cognitive complaints, sleep disturbances, anxiety, depression, and limitations in daily activities (4)(5)(6), contributing to the complexity of long-term clinical recovery.Conventional measures of initial TBI severity, including the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), pupillary reactivity, and structural imaging findings, remain essential for acute assessment and prognosis.However, the relationship between the extent and characteristics of the initial injury and persistent symptoms is not straightforward, and individuals with apparently similar acute injury characteristics may follow different long-term recovery trajectories (4-6, 11, 12). This variability has increased interest in biological and functional processes that may persist or evolve after the acute injury (7)(8)(9).Against this background, we propose the hypothesis that persistent PTH may serve as a clinical window into persistent brain dysfunction after TBI. This concept does not imply that persistent PTH is itself a biomarker or that it demonstrates the presence of a specific underlying mechanism. Rather, we propose that its persistence may serve as a clinical signal warranting investigation of functional or biological abnormalities that are not fully characterized by conventional structural assessment. This hypothesis is considered across the TBI severity spectrum. However, the evidence discussed in this article derives from heterogeneous populations, including mild TBI and moderate-to-severe TBI, and findings from one severity group should not be assumed to generalize to another. Furthermore, evidence directly obtained from patients with persistent PTH remains more limited than evidence derived from broader TBI populations. Throughout this article, we therefore distinguish PTH-specific findings from mechanisms that remain biologically plausible on the basis of the broader TBI literature.Acute TBI severity remains a major determinant of early clinical outcomes. Measures such as the GCS, pupillary reactivity, and structural imaging findings are strongly associated with mortality and functional disability and remain fundamental for clinical decision-making and prognostic assessment (1,2,10). However, these measures were primarily developed to characterize the initial injury and estimate acute outcomes, and their ability to account for persistent symptoms and heterogeneous longterm recovery trajectories is more limited (11,12).Patients with apparently similar initial injury characteristics may experience markedly different longterm outcomes, including persistent headache, fatigue, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbances, emotional symptoms, and reduced quality of life (11,12). This variability suggests that the extent and characteristics of the initial injury alone do not fully capture the processes associated with long-term recovery.TBI initiates a cascade of biological events that may extend beyond the acute phase (7-9). Among these processes, neuroinflammation has been extensively investigated. Acute activation of microglia and astrocytes contributes to tissue responses following injury, whereas sustained or dysregulated inflammatory activity has been associated with blood-brain barrier alterations, persistent inflammatory signaling, and changes in neuronal function (7)(8)(9)(17)(18)(19). Importantly, evidence of persistent neuroinflammation after TBI derives predominantly from experimental studies and broader TBI populations and should not be interpreted as evidence that neuroinflammation directly causes persistent PTH. Rather, it provides a biologically plausible framework that requires specific validation in patients with persistent PTH.Altered nociceptive processing may represent another relevant mechanism. Central sensitization should be distinguished from nociplastic pain and other forms of altered nociceptive signaling because these concepts are related but not interchangeable (20,21). PTH-specific studies have identified sensory abnormalities, including cephalic allodynia, hyperalgesia, and altered pain modulatory responses, supporting abnormal nociceptive processing in at least a subset of patients with persistent PTH (22). Experimental evidence of hypersensitivity to calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) further supports the involvement of CGRP-related nociceptive pathways (23). However, these findings neither establish central sensitization as a universal mechanism nor demonstrate a single pathophysiological pathway underlying persistent PTH.A complementary perspective is provided by network neuroscience, which conceptualizes neurological dysfunction as potentially arising from disturbances in interactions among distributed brain networks rather than exclusively from focal structural damage (13)(14)(15). TBI studies have demonstrated persistent structural network abnormalities during recovery (24), while PTH-specific neuroimaging studies have identified alterations in resting-state functional connectivity involving pain-processing, painmodulatory, and affective networks (25,26). These findings provide more direct, although still limited, evidence that persistent PTH may be associated with alterations in brain network function.Persistent PTH also frequently co-occurs with fatigue, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbances, emotional symptoms, and reduced quality of life (4)(5)(6). Rather than representing different expressions of a single persistent biological condition, these manifestations may arise from partially overlapping, independent, or mutually reinforcing mechanisms. Their co-occurrence therefore underscores the heterogeneity of post-traumatic recovery and the need to investigate how different biological and functional processes contribute to individual symptom profiles.Within the framework proposed here, persistent PTH is considered a potential clinical window into persistent brain dysfunction rather than a validated biomarker, prognostic indicator, or surrogate measure of an underlying biological process. We use the term clinical window to describe an observable clinical feature whose persistence may signal the need to investigate ongoing functional or biological abnormalities that are not fully captured by conventional structural assessment. Thus, persistent PTH is proposed primarily as a clinical signal for further investigation, not as evidence that a specific pathophysiological process is present.We use the term persistent brain dysfunction as an umbrella concept encompassing ongoing abnormalities in neural function or biological processes after TBI, including altered nociceptive processing, disturbances in brain network function, and potentially persistent inflammatory activity. This definition does not imply a single mechanism, nor does it assume that these abnormalities are present in all individuals with persistent PTH or that persistent PTH is caused by any one of them.The distinction is important because the evidence supporting these potential mechanisms varies substantially. PTH-specific neuroimaging studies have demonstrated alterations in resting-state functional connectivity involving pain-processing and pain-modulatory networks, including periaqueductal gray-related connectivity, with some alterations associated with headache burden or the subsequent development of persistent PTH (25,26). By contrast, evidence for persistent neuroinflammation and several other chronic neurobiological abnormalities derives predominantly from broader TBI populations. These mechanisms should therefore be regarded as biologically plausible contributors requiring direct investigation in persistent PTH rather than as established pathophysiological correlates of the condition.Persistent PTH may also reflect greater overall symptom burden rather than a distinct biological state.Headache commonly co-occurs with sleep disturbance, fatigue, cognitive complaints, anxiety, depression, and other post-traumatic symptoms (4-6), and these factors may independently influence both headache persistence and measures of brain function. Pre-existing headache disorders, injury severity, medication use, cervical or extracranial pain generators, and psychological and behavioral factors may further contribute to clinical heterogeneity. Consequently, the presence or severity of persistent PTH cannot currently be assumed to indicate the presence, type, or magnitude of persistent brain dysfunction.Testing the proposed clinical-window hypothesis will therefore require prospective studies that combine detailed headache phenotyping with objective measures of brain function and biology while accounting for relevant confounding factors. Quantitative electroencephalography, neuroimagingderived connectivity measures, and molecular or inflammatory measures are candidate approaches that could be evaluated in this context (24,27,28,31). Artificial intelligence and machine-learning methods may complement these measures as analytical approaches for identifying multidimensional patterns or patient phenotypes, rather than representing biological or functional measures themselves (29,30).At present, none of these candidate approaches can be considered a validated biomarker of persistent PTH. Their value lies in testing whether persistent PTH is systematically associated with measurable patterns of post-traumatic dysfunction beyond headache severity and overall symptom burden.The hypothesis proposed in this article should be interpreted within several important limitations. First, evidence directly linking persistent PTH to measurable ongoing brain dysfunction remains limited.Although PTH-specific neuroimaging studies have identified alterations in functional connectivity (25,26), much of the evidence supporting persistent neuroinflammation, neurophysiological abnormalities, and other chronic biological processes derives from broader TBI populations. Extrapolation of these findings to persistent PTH therefore requires caution, and associations observed after TBI should not be assumed to represent mechanisms of persistent PTH.Second, persistent PTH is clinically and biologically heterogeneous. Headache phenotype, pre-existing headache disorders, TBI severity, sleep disturbance, fatigue, psychological symptoms, medication use, cervical or extracranial pain generators, and other post-traumatic symptoms may influence both headache persistence and measures of brain function. These factors provide alternative or complementary explanations for associations between persistent PTH and biological or functional abnormalities. Consequently, future studies should determine whether such associations remain after appropriate characterization and adjustment for relevant confounding factors.The proposed clinical-window hypothesis also generates testable predictions. If persistent PTH is associated with ongoing post-traumatic dysfunction beyond overall symptom burden, individuals with persistent PTH should demonstrate reproducible functional or biological abnormalities when compared with appropriately matched TBI survivors without persistent PTH. These associations should remain detectable after accounting for injury severity, pre-existing headache, headache phenotype, psychological symptoms, sleep disturbance, medication use, and other relevant clinical factors.Longitudinal studies should further determine whether changes in headache frequency, intensity, or disability are accompanied by changes in candidate neurophysiological, neuroimaging, or molecular measures.Conversely, failure to identify reproducible associations between persistent PTH and objective measures of post-traumatic dysfunction, particularly after controlling for symptom burden and relevant confounders, would argue against the proposed clinical-window hypothesis or restrict its applicability to specific patient subgroups. This possibility is important because the framework proposed here should be considered a testable hypothesis rather than an assumption that persistent headache necessarily reflects ongoing brain dysfunction.Future research should therefore prioritize prospective longitudinal designs with detailed headache phenotyping and appropriate comparison groups. Studies comparing TBI survivors with persistent PTH, TBI survivors without persistent PTH, and, where appropriate, individuals with primary headache disorders may help determine which findings are related specifically to persistent PTH, to TBI more broadly, or to chronic headache irrespective of trauma. Stratification by mild TBI and moderate-to-severe TBI will also be necessary because mechanisms and recovery trajectories may differ across injury severity.Multimodal studies integrating clinical phenotyping with neuroimaging, quantitative electroencephalography, and molecular measures may help determine whether reproducible patterns of dysfunction can be identified in specific persistent PTH subgroups. Artificial intelligence and machine-learning approaches may support the analysis of these multidimensional datasets and the identification of patient phenotypes, but their role is analytical and depends on the quality and validation of the underlying clinical and biological measures (24,(27)(28)(29)(30)(31). Candidate measures should not be considered biomarkers until their reproducibility, specificity, longitudinal behavior, and clinical relevance have been established in persistent PTH populations.Ultimately, the value of the proposed framework will depend on whether persistent PTH provides clinically meaningful information beyond established measures of injury severity and overall posttraumatic symptom burden. Prospective validation is therefore required before persistent PTH can be used to identify individuals for additional biological assessment, prognostic stratification, or mechanism-based interventions. Persistent PTH may provide a clinically accessible signal for investigating ongoing functional or biological abnormalities after TBI, but this relationship remains hypothetical and should not be interpreted as evidence that persistent headache is itself a biomarker of brain dysfunction.Distinguishing PTH-specific findings from abnormalities associated with TBI more broadly, controlling for alternative explanations and confounding factors, and prospectively testing the proposed associations will be essential to determine the validity and clinical relevance of this framework.
keywords: moderate to severe traumatic brain injury

papers.title: Functional brain activity in cancer-related cognitive impairment: a scoping review of EEG studies
papers.authors: Barbara Johanne Thomas Nordhjem, Laura Maria Toftekær Rothschild, Clotilde Rose Honoré, Anders Thyge Steen Larsen, Martin Kaj Fridh, Lisa Lyngsie Hjalgrim
papers.abstract: Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) is reported across the cancer trajectory, yet its neurobiological basis remains incompletely understood. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a temporally precise method for assessing brain activity at rest and during cognitive processing, but its application in CRCI research has not been systematically mapped. This scoping review characterized how EEG has been used to study cognitive functioning in people with cancer, including populations studied, EEG paradigms and analytic approaches employed, and cognitive outcomes assessed. Following PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science from inception to February 2025 for studies using EEG to examine cognitive functioning. Sixty articles were included. Most were small and cross-sectional, with publication output increasing markedly after 2015. Task-based event-related potentials, particularly from oddball and attention tasks, were used most frequently, whereas quantitative EEG approaches, including spectral power and connectivity analyses, were less common. In populations with cancers outside the central nervous system (CNS), longer P300 latency and lower amplitude were common, but opposite and null findings also occurred. Evidence from primary CNS and other intracranial tumor populations was sparse. Across cancer contexts, quantitative EEG findings showed limited convergence across articles. Associations between EEG measures and cognitive outcomes were inconsistent and often not tested directly. Overall, EEG provides a complementary approach to investigating cognition in people with cancer, but the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. Larger longitudinal studies, more consistent cognitive outcome selection, and closer integration of neural and cognitive measures are needed to establish reproducible findings and evaluate their potential clinical utility. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251084951 .

papers.title: Effects of physical activity on cognitive function in healthy older women: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.authors: Yong Fan, Jiqiao He, Zhicheng Zhu, Youjia Mao, Lisha Xie, Cui Huang, Zijian Zhu
papers.abstract: Background Age-related cognitive decline represents a major public health challenge, particularly among older women who face a disproportionately elevated risk of dementia. Physical activity has been proposed as a modifiable lifestyle factor with potential neuroprotective benefits; however, evidence specific to cognitively healthy older women remains limited. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from database inception to 26 September 2026. Studies were eligible if they enrolled healthy women aged >60 years and compared physical activity interventions with control conditions. The primary outcome was global cognitive function assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) or the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Secondary outcomes included brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and body mass index (BMI). Pooled effect sizes were calculated using random-effects or fixed-effect models as appropriate. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression were performed to explore potential moderators. The certainty of evidence was appraised using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE) approach. Results Ten RCTs encompassing 446 participants were included. Physical activity was associated with higher global cognitive function scores (Hedges’ g = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.12–1.13, p = 0.02) and increased BDNF levels (MD = 2.43, 95% CI: 0.57–4.28, p = 0.01). No statistically significant effect on BMI was observed (MD = 0.63, 95% CI: −1.12–2.37, p = 0.48). Substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed for global cognitive function (I 2 = 77.82%). Formal tests for subgroup differences were not statistically significant for either intervention duration ( p = 0.82) or intervention frequency ( p = 0.12). Conclusion The pooled evidence suggests potential beneficial effects of physical activity on global cognitive function and BDNF levels in healthy older women; however, the certainty of evidence was very low. No statistically significant effect on BMI was observed, and subgroup analyses did not provide sufficient evidence that intervention frequency significantly modified the effect on cognitive function. Further well-designed RCTs with larger samples and standardized outcome measures are needed to confirm these findings. Systematic review registration PROSPERO under registration number CRD420251249052, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251249052 .

papers.title: Artificial intelligence as academic infrastructure: governance, administrative intelligence, and AI fluency in Kazakhstan’s higher education sector
papers.authors: Rajasekhara Mouly Potluri, Victoria Polozova
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly part of higher education's institutional infrastructure, extending beyond teaching and learning to governance, administration, and student support. This study examines how AI Governance Readiness (AIGR) influences Administrative Efficiency through AI (AEAI), AI Fluency Orientation (AIFO), and Student Retention Intentions (SRI), while assessing the mediating roles of AEAI and AIFO and the moderating role of Equity Perception (EPS) in Kazakhstan's higher education sector. Drawing on Dynamic Capability Theory and Sociotechnical Systems Theory, the study develops and empirically tests an institutional capability model using 935 valid responses from students, faculty, academic administrators, and digital administration staff across public and private universities. The scholars analyzed the data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4.0, supported by RStudio. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity, while the structural model showed adequate explanatory and predictive performance. We assessed common method bias through procedural safeguards and full-collinearity diagnostics, and identified no substantive concerns. The findings show that AIGR is positively associated with AEAI and AIFO, while both constructs positively influence SRI. AEAI and AIFO also significantly mediate the relationship between AIGR and SRI. However, EPS does not significantly moderate the relationships between AI-enabled institutional capabilities and retention intentions. The findings position AI governance as a strategic institutional capability through which universities can improve administrative responsiveness, develop AI-related competencies, and support student continuity. The study contributes empirical evidence from Kazakhstan to the growing literature on responsible AI governance and digital transformation in higher education.

papers.title: Rethinking AI integration in African higher education: a mixed-methods investigation of capacity, equity, and governance across sub-Saharan Africa
papers.authors: J. N. A. Aryee, P. Davies, G. A. Torsah, M. M. Apaw, S. M. Mwando, C. Kwisanga, C. D. Boateng, Eric Ouma Jobunga, D. Mutale, Leonard  Kofitse Amekudzi
papers.abstract: The Revolutionizing Tertiary Education for Africa's Thriving AI Economy and Workforce (RetAIn) project presents a comprehensive, multi-method investigation into the conditions, constraints, and catalysts shaping Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption across African Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). Deploying both qualitative multi-stakeholders Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) from three African countries (Ghana, Rwanda, Namibia) and a quantitative cross-country survey across five Sub-Saharan African nations (Ghana, Rwanda, Namibia, Kenya, and Zambia), this study produces a richly triangulated account of AI integration dynamics on the continent. The FGD strand revealed a stark divergence in national AI trajectories: Rwanda operates under a strong top-down policy vision hindered by institutional rigidity; Namibia exhibits pragmatic institutional adaptability constrained by geographic and economic smallness; and Ghana demonstrates emergent, bottom-up innovation within a national policy vacuum. The survey strand, drawing on 156 responses across five countries, corroborated these qualitative tensions, documenting widespread recognition of AI's strategic importance alongside limited structured engagement, persistent infrastructure deficits, and marked equity barriers, particularly for women, vulnerable groups, rural students, and part-time workers. From both methods, a unifying finding emerges: AI integration in African HEIs consistently fails when technical adoption outpaces social, pedagogical, and governance co-evolution. The study argues for context-specific, socio-technically grounded strategies that pair curriculum co-design with robust industry partnerships, that centre equity and cultural relevance, and build governance frameworks capable of guiding, rather than chasing, technological change.

papers.title: Institutional policies for responsible generative AI use in Saudi higher education: a policy review and gap analysis of national-to-institutional implementation
papers.authors: Fouad Ahmed Atallah
papers.abstract: Saudi Arabia has established a comprehensive national-level governance landscape for generative artificial intelligence through the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA), including the AI Ethics Principles (2023), Generative AI Guidelines (2024–2025), the AI Adoption Framework, and the Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications, alongside broader strategic directions under Vision 2030. This study employed systematic documentary analysis combined with gap analysis to examine eight national-level policy and strategic documents, focusing on governance principles, operational mechanisms, and their relevance to Saudi higher education. The analysis reveals three critical findings: (1) national frameworks articulate detailed governance principles, organizational responsibilities, and operational guidance for responsible AI use, although the regulatory status and degree of prescriptiveness vary across documents; (2) national documents reference Islamic values and cultural alignment but generally lack explicit integration of Maqasid al-Shariah principles into governance language or operational mechanisms; and (3) an institutional audit of 17 purposively selected Saudi universities identified publicly accessible formal AI governance policies or guidelines at six institutions, indicating substantial variation in the publicly documented institutional translation of national AI governance frameworks. The findings suggest that translating national principles into operational institutional frameworks may benefit from three key components: higher-education-specific policy translation mechanisms, clearly defined accountability structures with appropriate monitoring indicators, and explicit consideration of Islamic ethical dimensions. Documentary analysis combined with institutional policy auditing and gap analysis provides a systematic approach to identifying discontinuities between national governance frameworks and publicly documented institutional policy development. The findings contribute to understanding AI governance challenges in Saudi higher education and highlight the importance of institutional-level policy architecture for connecting national governance principles with educational practice. The research also has implications for other Arab and Muslim-majority higher education systems seeking to align emerging global AI governance standards with local Islamic and cultural values.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence innovations in low vision rehabilitation: a systematic review of emerging technologies
papers.authors: Kenneth Bempah Karikari, Josephine Ampong, Sylvia Agyekum, Henry Yeboah Agyekum, Lois Manyeyo Kweiki Sabutey, Emmanuel Tettey Doku, Kwesi Sewe, Derek Kwaku Pobi Asiedu, Isaiah Osei Duah, Albert Kwadjo Amoah Andoh, Werner Eisenbarth, David Ben Kumah, Kwadwo Owusu Akuffo
papers.abstract: Background Low vision is one of the major types of visual impairment worldwide and when diagnosed early can help with its management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has recently shown promising outcomes in all fields including health, with low vision rehabilitation being one of its significant applications. This systematic review aims to provide an up-to-date and comprehensive evaluation of the application of AI in the management of low vision. Methods The systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. All relevant published papers were retrieved through searches from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore, without date restrictions. All retrieved articles from electronic databases were collated and managed in Covidence software. Results Nineteen studies were included, consisting of six application domains, which include assistive navigation and wayfinding ( n = 8), environmental interaction and object recognition ( n = 5), reading and text access ( n = 2), educational accessibility ( n = 1), medical applications ( n = 3), and digital accessibility optimization ( n = 1). Navigation systems demonstrated the strongest performance, with leading systems achieving sub-meter location error and 100% task success rates in real-world testing. Object recognition accuracies reached 97%, hazard detection achieved 92.0% dynamic accuracy with temporal filtering, and multimodal environmental understanding received risk assessment ratings of 9.40/10. Recurring technical limitations included sensitivity to lighting conditions, processing latency, and connectivity dependency. Conclusion AI assistive technologies for low vision demonstrate technical feasibility with promising performance. However, important evidence gaps limit clinical application: the absence of prospective validation, limited comparative effectiveness data, and minimal patient-centered outcomes. Future studies should use standardized outcomes, larger and more diverse datasets, and longitudinal evaluations to demonstrate real-world impact. Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261324781 , CRD420261324781.

papers.title: ReportSimple V3: An Integrated, Privacy-Preserving AI Framework for Multimodal Medical Report Analysis, Rule-Based Safety Screening, and Interactive 3D Symptom Mapping
papers.authors: Md Gausur Rahman Nabil
papers.abstract: ​ReportSimple V3 is an educational health-information application intended to help people organise symptoms, consult public biomedical evidence, review medicine-label information, and prepare a concise summary for a clinician. Its architecture separates deterministic safety screening from generative language-model (LLM) text generation. A Flask blueprint exposes endpoints for an adaptive symptom interview, assessment, chat, evidence search, medicine labels, medicine-label interaction text, healthcare-place discovery, and PDF export. The safety.py module evaluates English and Bangla text with regular expressions and checks contextual features including body region, symptom severity, and chest-pain duration. The API invokes this screen before assessment or chat generation and returns an emergency response without an AI-authored reply when the configured emergency rules match.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN THE TRANSFORMATION OF MARKETING
papers.authors: Andrii Medyna, Viktoriia Yanovska, Anastasiia Ustilovska, Alina Nakaliuzhna
papers.journal: Collection of scientific research papers State University of Infrastructure and Technologies Section “Economics and Management”
papers.abstract: The article examines the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies on the transformation of modern marketing in the context of business digitalization and the growing role of data in managerial decision-making. The study analyzes the dynamics of global investment in AI over the period 2013–2024, identifies the leading investor countries—the United States, China, and the United Kingdom—and reveals the concentration of financial flows in the AI sector, which contributes to the formation of global technological asymmetry. Particular attention is paid to the marketing segment, where investment amounted to USD 1.6 billion in 2024 and is projected to increase to USD 135.38 billion by 2032. This trend indicates that AI is shifting from an auxiliary tool to a strategic factor in companies’ competitiveness. The article also presents the sectoral structure of AI applications, identifying media, entertainment, retail, and information technology as the leading areas. In addition, it analyzes successful cases of AI integration into the marketing strategies of international companies, including Coca-Cola, Burger King, Calm, Heinz, Nike, Netflix, and JPMorgan Chase. Based on a synthesis of international experience, the study develops a strategy for adapting AI technologies to Ukrainian companies, taking into account limited budgets, staffing constraints, and the conditions of martial law. A phased implementation model is proposed. It involves the use of accessible automation tools, the development of employees’ digital literacy, and partnerships between businesses as a means of reducing costs. The findings demonstrate that the effective implementation of AI in marketing not only helps optimize business processes but also creates conditions for innovation-driven development, personalized customer communication, and increased business profitability.

papers.title: Theoretical and Methodological Foundations for Preparing Prospective Primary School Teachers to Use Generative Artificial Intelligence in Teaching the Russian and Kyrgyz Languages
papers.authors: A. Iusupova, Zh. Algozhoeva, Asylgul Sarinjievna Jumataeva
papers.abstract: The article addresses the pressing scholarly problem of preparing prospective primary school teachers to use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in teaching the Russian and Kyrgyz languages within the context of the digital transformation of education and the transition of the Kyrgyz Republic to a new, modern twelve-year model of school education. The relevance of the study stems from the shared need to update the content of teacher education, the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies, and the increasing requirements for the digital and methodological competence of modern teachers. The analysis of contemporary international research, regulatory documents, and national and international pedagogical experience demonstrates the need to develop a new component of prospective teachers’ professional preparation — AI-based linguodidactic competence. This competence is understood as an integrative ability of a teacher to use generative artificial intelligence in a pedagogically justified, ethically responsible, and safe manner when designing, organizing, and assessing the process of teaching the Russian and Kyrgyz languages in primary school. For the first time, the article proposes an original concept for preparing prospective primary school teachers to use generative artificial intelligence in language education. It outlines the methodological foundations, structural components, and pedagogical conditions for implementing this concept, as well as the practical possibilities of integrating advanced intelligent digital technologies into language-teaching methodology. The proposed author-developed model comprises motivational and value-oriented, cognitive, technological, methodological, communicative, and reflective-evaluative components. It is aimed at developing prospective teachers’ professional readiness to work in a modern digital educational environment. The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of using the proposed model to improve teacher-education programmes at higher educational institutions in the Kyrgyz Republic, introduce new academic disciplines, develop professional development programmes for teachers, and support the practical implementation of the Concept for the Transition to a Twelve-Year General Education System.

papers.title: Developing Criteria and Indicators for Assessing Students’ Knowledge in a Digital Educational Environment
papers.authors: Urmat Moldosanov
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of higher education requires the development of assessment systems capable of measuring not only the amount of knowledge acquired by students but also their ability to understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, and create information in technology-mediated contexts. This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for developing criteria and indicators for assessing students’ knowledge in a digital educational environment. The study employs systematic analysis, comparison, classification, synthesis, and pedagogical modelling. The proposed framework includes six assessment criteria: conceptual knowledge, comprehension and interpretation, practical application, analytical and problem-solving ability, knowledge integration and creation, and reflective and self-regulated learning. Each criterion is operationalised through measurable qualitative and quantitative indicators. A four-level assessment scale — advanced, proficient, developing, and insufficient — is introduced to improve transparency and consistency. The article also proposes a weighted formula for calculating an integrated student knowledge score. Particular attention is given to validity, reliability, fairness, transparency, accessibility, academic integrity, and the pedagogically responsible use of learning analytics and artificial intelligence. The findings indicate that digital assessment becomes educationally meaningful when assessment tasks are aligned with learning outcomes, indicators are observable and measurable, students receive timely feedback, and automated data are combined with professional teacher judgement. The proposed framework may be adapted to different university disciplines, learning management systems, and blended or fully online educational programmes.

papers.title: Technology-Enhanced Language Instruction for Economics Students
papers.authors: LUSINE HARUTYUNYAN, A. Grigoryan, A. Mkrtchyan
papers.abstract: For economics students today who want to pursue careers in international business, finance, entrepreneurship, and economic policy in the globalized economy, efficient communication in English is a vital skill. Many students grasp English grammar and vocabular y, but they struggle to acquire the speaking abilities required for professional communication. Speaking anxiety, lack of genuine engagement, lack of business-related terminology, and weak confidence still impair learners’ speaking performance. At the same time, however, technological advancement has transformed language education by creating new options for communication, cooperation, and customized learning. The work under review is devoted to innovative methods of developing the professional speaking skills of economics students through the use of Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) and educational technology. The review of studies on speaking training, communicative competence, technology-enhanced language learning, gamification, artificial intelligence, and professional communication in higher education is included in the study. Special focus is paid to the utilization of digital platforms, online collaboration tools, gamified learning settings (e.g., Kahoot), and AI-assisted language learning tools that enhance speaking development. The study shows a favorable influence of communicative and technology-based strategies on speaking fluency, student engagement, communicative confidence, and the capacity to communicate in a professional manner. Results also show that the use of CLT principles and digital learning tools can provide tremendous opportunities for economics students to practice business communication in real and interactive scenarios. The paper ends with a discussion of the pedagogical implications for higher education institutions and suggestions for the future of technology-enhanced speaking training in economics education.

papers.title: PROMPT LITERACY У НАВЧАННІ ЯПОНСЬКОЇ МОВИ: МОДЕЛЬ GPT-ОПОСЕРЕДКОВАНОЇ МОВЛЕННЄВОЇ ДІЯЛЬНОСТІ
papers.authors: А.В. Гілевич, Yulia BORYSHPOLETS
papers.abstract: У статті теоретично обґрунтовано prompt literacy як перспективний компонент сучасної іншомовної комунікативної компетентності у навчанні японської мови та визначено його місце в середовищі взаємодії «людина – генеративний AI». Актуальність дослідження зумовлена переходом від використання генеративного штучного інтелекту як допоміж- ного цифрового інструмента до GPT-опосередкованої мовленнєвої діяльності, у якій результат залежить не лише від можливостей мовної моделі, а й від здатності здобувача освіти формулювати, контекстуалізувати, уточнювати та кри- тично оцінювати запити. Матеріалом дослідження стали 14 сучасних праць японських, корейських, американських, британських та індонезійських дослідників, присвячених prompt literacy, prompt engineering, AI literacy і використанню генеративного AI в іншомовній та японськомовній освіті. Застосовано критичний і порівняльний аналіз наукових дже- рел, концептуальний аналіз ключових понять, систематизацію та теоретичне моделювання. Уточнено співвідношення понять prompt engineering, prompt literacy та AI literacy й обґрунтовано специфіку Japanese-language prompt literacy, що передбачає врахування комунікативної мети, рівня володіння мовою, соціальних ролей, регістру, прагматичної доречності та культурного контексту. Авторами запропоновано модель GPT-опосередкованої мовленнєвої діяльності із сімома взаємопов’язаними компонентами: комунікативна мета, контекст, рольова рамка, мовні обмеження, формат результату, критичне оцінювання AI output та ітеративне вдосконалення prompt. Визначено методичні принципи фор- мування цієї компетентності, запропоновано типи навчальних завдань і п’ять вимірів її подальшої операціоналізації. Зроблено висновок, що prompt literacy доцільно розглядати не як суто технічну навичку, а як точку перетину мовної, прагматичної, стратегічної, цифрової та критичної компетентностей. Перспективою подальших досліджень визначено емпіричну перевірку запропонованої моделі на матеріалі університетського навчання японської мови.

papers.title: THE EMERGENCE AND FUNCTIONING OF ENGLISH NEOLOGISMS IN CONTEMPORARY COMMUNICATION (2023–2026)
papers.authors: Veronika Yablochnikova
papers.abstract: This article investigates the emergence, structural characteristics, and communicative functions of English neologisms that have entered public discourse during this period. The study aims to identify the principal mechanisms of neologism for- mation, determine the factors contributing to their dissemination, and examine their role in contemporary communication. The research employs a combination of descriptive, structural, semantic, and discourse analysis methods. The corpus of the study comprises neologisms collected from contemporary English-language media, social networking platforms, online dictionaries, and digital corpora. Particular attention is paid to lexical items associated with artificial intelligence, digital communication, environmental issues, and evolving socio-cultural trends. The analysis demonstrates that com- pounding, blending, clipping, affixation, abbreviation, semantic shift, and borrowing remain the most productive word-for- mation processes. Furthermore, the findings reveal that digital communication has become the primary environment for the creation, rapid dissemination, and stabilization of new lexical units. The study also highlights the pragmatic functions of English neologisms, emphasizing their role in facilitating efficient communication, expressing emerging concepts, constructing social identity, and reflecting speakers’ attitudes toward tech- nological and societal change. Many of the analyzed neologisms exhibit considerable semantic flexibility and are char- acterized by a high degree of contextual dependence, illustrating the dynamic nature of present-day English vocabulary. The findings contribute to a better understanding of current lexical processes and demonstrate the close relationship between language evolution and contemporary communication practices. The results may be applied in lexicological, sociolinguistic, and discourse studies, as well as in translation practice and the teaching of English as a foreign language. The research also provides a foundation for further investigations into the long-term development and standardization of English neologisms in the rapidly evolving digital era.

papers.title: PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION MECHANISMS FOR ENSURING HIGHER EDUCATION QUALITY: RESULTS OF APPLICATION AND PROSPECTS FOR DEVELOPMENT
papers.authors: Д. К. Шутов
papers.journal: Scientific Notes of Taurida V I Vernadsky University series Public Administration
papers.abstract: The article examines the mechanisms of public administration for ensuring the quality of higher education in Ukraine through the prism of the classifications established in the scholarly discourse, as well as through the practices of their functioning and their actual impact on the international competitiveness of domestic higher education institutions. The methodological basis of the research combines the analysis of regulatory and legal acts, programme documents of the international and national levels, statistical data of the National Agency for Higher Education Quality Assurance, and a comparative analysis of the dynamics of the positioning of Ukrainian universities in the leading international rankings during 2022–2026. A contradiction has been identified between the architectonics of building the higher education quality assurance system and the comparatively low positioning of Ukrainian universities in international rankings (Quacquarelli Symonds World University Rankings; Times Higher Education World University Rankings; Academic Ranking of World Universities, ShanghaiRanking). In particular, it has been established that the number of Ukrainian universities represented in the QS World University Rankings decreased from 11 in 2023 to 4 in 2026, while the highest position of domestic institutions in the Times Higher Education ranking has consistently remained within the 801–1000 group despite the quantitative growth of their representation. The exhaustion of the potential of the traditional regulatory-legal, organisational- administrative and economic mechanisms of public administration in the higher education sphere has been substantiated, along with the need to search for new mechanisms of public administration for ensuring quality. The article also offers proposals on the necessity of applying innovative mechanisms for ensuring the quality of higher education, namely those grounded in the toolkit of artificial intelligence, big data analytics, and robotic process automation, the practical significance of which is confirmed by international experience and the analytical priorities of the national quality assurance system.

papers.title: Intellectual property in design-driven industries: A bibliometric and thematic analysis (2000–2025) with insights for the Jewellery Industry
papers.authors: Xia Du, Nor Azlina Mohd Noor, Khadijah Mohamed
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically examine the intellectual property (IP) research in design-driven industries through a bibliometric and thematic analysis of publications from 2000 to 2025, and further derives implications for the jewellery industry. With the rapid development of the creative economy and digital transformation, IP protection has become an important pillar for innovation and market competitiveness in design-intensive industries. However, current research lacks a systematic and holistic review of this interdisciplinary field, and evidence specific to the jewellery remains limited. To fill this gap, a bibliometric and thematic analysis was conducted based on 359 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. Descriptive statistics were processed using Microsoft Excel, while publication trends, global research patterns, thematic structures, and emerging research frontiers were analyzed using CiteSpace and VOSviewer. The findings indicate that intellectual property research in design-driven industries has maintained continuous growth and gradually formed an interdisciplinary integration trend. Among the valid publications, "Law" is the dominant subject category, followed by "Business" and "Management", with insufficient attention to "Cultural Studies" and "Art". Geographically, the USA and England are core hubs, with the USA leading in publications, citations and collaboration; China is an emerging contributor. IP law journals dominate in publication volume like Journal of Intellectual Property Law, while interdisciplinary journals such as Strategic Management Journal exhibit higher citation impact. Reliable keyword clustering identifies copyright, IP and innovation as core keywords, with three main thematic areas. Accordingly, this study offers relevant implications for the jewellery industry, emphasizing integrated IP strategies and adaptive responses to digital and AI-related challenges. It provides a systematic knowledge map and supports future research and innovation in design-driven industries.

papers.title: FROM PIXELS TO PROMPTS: A STRUCTURED NARRATIVE REVIEW OF SECURITY, PRIVACY, AND ADVERSARIAL ROBUSTNESS IN HEALTHCARE AI
papers.authors: Patryk Sielaff, Artur Brudek, Adrian Nowakowski, Hubert Piwar, Jan Pawłasek, Monika Lis, Karolina Hernik, Mateusz Sucharski, Ewa Kacynel
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in healthcare, where evaluations usually ask whether a system is accurate on ordinary clinical data. This review asks instead what can happen when someone deliberately changes the data, instructions, or training to make a system fail, behave in hidden ways, or reveal confidential information, a field known as adversarial machine learning. We reviewed 113 publications (2018–2026) and grouped the reported threats into six categories: altering an input after training; corrupting the training examples; teaching a hidden rule triggered later; using the model to learn private information; placing malicious instructions in language or image-and-language models; and attacking models trained jointly across hospitals or devices. Laboratory studies showed that small deliberate changes to medical images could alter a diagnosis or a model's outline, corrupted training data could change what a model learned, and malicious prompts could produce unsafe medical responses. Effect sizes varied greatly across models, datasets, attacks, and test conditions. Several defenses helped in individual experiments, but no single defense was shown to work across all threats and settings; in one imaging study, attacks tailored to the tested defenses bypassed all five. The studies do not show how often these attacks occur in practice or harm patients; their value is to demonstrate possible failure modes under controlled conditions. Medical AI should therefore be evaluated both on ordinary clinical data and in clearly described, clinically plausible attack scenarios.

papers.title: AI Swarm Intelligence Must Be Studied as a Sociotechnical Phenomenon
papers.authors: Wenchao Dong, Luiz Felipe Santos Vecchietti, Łukasz Olejnik, Signe Riemer–Sørensen, Jonas R. Kunst, Meeyoung Cha, Daniel Thilo Schroeder
papers.abstract: The emergence of coordinated autonomous AI agents is fundamentally altering human belief systems and public discourse at scales and speeds that outpace existing characterization methods. This paper argues that AI swarm intelligence, the coordinated influence of autonomous agents on human populations, represents a phase shift that cannot be understood by simply scaling single-agent analysis. Instead, it must be analyzed as a sociotechnical system where societal impact emerges from the tight coupling of individual agent capabilities, multi-agent coordination, and population dynamics. Because the shift from single- to multi-agent systems corresponds to a psychological transition between single- and multiple-source influence, we propose a unified framework and evaluate these systems across operational, individual, and population-level dynamics. We identify concrete research agendas and call on the community to build the evaluation methods, countermeasures, and governance approaches needed to address the long-term societal impact of these coordinated autonomous AI populations.AI assistance disclosure: Claude (Anthropic) was used solely to polish the language of the manuscript. No other AI assistance was used.

papers.title: LLM-Generated Well-being Intervention Recommendations Are Sensitive to Psychological Profiles: A Proof-of-Concept Expert-Rating Study
papers.authors: Benjamin Kaveladze, Elizabeth Webb Lampe, Michael V. Heinz, Lisa A. Marsch, Andrew Thomas Campbell, Nicholas C. Jacobson
papers.abstract: Personalizing digital well-being interventions to fit the needs and preferences of individual users has been a longstanding challenge. Large language models (LLMs) may be well-suited for this task, using natural language reasoning to integrate heterogeneous user information into personalized guidance. We tested whether LLMs could generate intervention recommendations that were sensitive to differences across recipients’ psychological profiles. Across 178 undergraduate student profiles spanning 14 psychological measures, four LLMs recommended 10 scripted chatbot dialogues from a library of 222 options. Next, two experts rated the recommendations’ appropriateness for a given profile (1-10). For half of the profiles, raters saw recommendations generated for that student (matched condition); for the remainder, they saw recommendations generated for a different student (unmatched condition). As hypothesized, matched recommendations (M = 6.74) were rated as more appropriate than unmatched ones (M = 5.64, SMD = 0.50). These results provide evidence that LLMs can adapt their intervention recommendations to match psychological profiles. However, inter-rater reliability was poor (ICC = 0.22), and all LLMs showed substantial sensitivity to catalog order. As such, we stress the preliminary nature of the findings. Whether such tailoring translates into improved well-being outcomes for users remains to be tested.

papers.title: Attentional network processing in children and adults shows comparable behavioural effects but distinct ERP and time–frequency activity
papers.authors: Praghajieeth Raajhen Santhana Gopalan, Otto Loberg, Jarmo Arvid Hämäläinen, Paavo H. T. Leppänen
papers.abstract: Visual attention comprises alerting, orienting, and executive-control networks. Although these networks are behaviourally evident in childhood, age differences in the neural processes supporting them remain unclear. Typically developing 12–13-year-old children (n = 77) and 19–33-year-old adults (n = 21) performed the Attention Network Test while electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded. Behavioural performance was assessed using reaction time and accuracy. Neural processing was examined using event-related potentials (N1 and P3 amplitudes and latencies) and induced time–frequency analyses of theta (4–7 Hz), alpha (8–12 Hz), and beta (13–25 Hz) band activity. Significant alerting, orienting, and executive-control effects were observed in reaction time, with children responding more slowly overall than adults. Children showed longer N1 latencies than adults during the orienting comparison, indicating slower early target-related processing. Alerting cues increased target-related N1 amplitudes similarly in both groups. Adults, but not children, showed smaller P3 amplitudes for incongruent than congruent trials, whereas children showed larger P3 amplitudes overall, suggesting age-related differences in conflict-related processing. Time–frequency analyses showed that alerting modulated theta-, alpha-, and beta-band activity similarly in both groups. Orienting-related theta activity differed between age groups, with children showing higher theta power for spatial- than centre-cue trials. Alpha-band activity also differed between orienting conditions similarly in both groups. These findings indicate that children and adults can show comparable behavioural attentional network effects despite differences in neural processing. The results further suggest that electrophysiological measures of attentional processing show age-related differences beyond late childhood.

papers.title: When Risk Factors Compete: A Machine Learning Approach to Identifying Antecedents of Adolescent Delinquency Across Domains, Development, and Gender
papers.authors: Matthew Cashman, Anna‐Karin Andershed, Henrik Andershed, Frida Bood, Evelina Landstedt, Louise Frogner, Karin Hellfeldt
papers.abstract: Risk factors for adolescent delinquency have been identified at multiple levels, from individual dispositions through family and school processes to ecological context, yet their relative importance remains unestablished. Which factors carry greatest weight, and when, has not been tested in simultaneous modelling. This study assessed 111 predictors spanning five domains across four developmental periods, predicting self-reported delinquency in mid-adolescence. Predictors were teacher- and parent-reported and the outcome adolescent self-reported. Participants were a Swedish population-based cohort followed from early childhood into adolescence (N = 2,121; 46.6% girls; mean age 3.86 years at baseline; 97.8% born in Sweden). Using machine learning techniques, random forests were estimated across the full span (AUC = .787, 95% CI [.747, .826]) and at each developmental period for boys and girls. Parent-rated conduct problems ranked among the leading predictors at every period, while caregiver emotional functioning carried greatest weight in early and late childhood before being displaced by dispositional and behavioral characteristics. Parent-rated social competence was the strongest protective factor. Associations were threshold-shaped, with the shift to elevated risk falling within the ordinary range of the measures. Gender differences in ranking were not supported by formal testing, which was low-powered.

papers.title: AI-Powered Prevention and Early Intervention for Stress, Depression, and Anxiety: A Randomized Clinical Trial
papers.authors: Julie Youko Anne Cachia, Xuan Zhao, Wenxi Pu, Chi Liao, Merel Keijsers, Julian De Freitas, Rebecca G. Fortgang
papers.abstract: Randomized evidence for purpose-built generative AI mental health support remains limited. In this preregistered trial, 1,137 unscreened university students were assigned to 6 weeks of Flourish or care as usual. All three primary endpoints were met, with more favorable trajectories for perceived stress (β = -0.03, p = 0.010), depressive symptoms (β = -0.03, p = 0.006), and anxiety symptoms (β = -0.04, p = 0.001). Benefits were observed across baseline severity, with less deterioration at low severity and greater improvement at elevated severity. Among participants with elevated symptoms, improvements were larger with Flourish for depression (d = 1.03 vs 0.56) and anxiety (d = 0.91 vs 0.60), with meaningful improvements of 52.3% vs 31.7% and 50.6% vs 38.1%, respectively. Reductions in perceived stress emerged as one potential pathway to broader improvements in depressive and anxiety symptoms. These findings support scalable first-line AI support spanning prevention and early intervention.

papers.title: Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Epilepsy: A Shared Language for Integrated Care
papers.authors: Islam Mohamed Elbanna, Yamane A. Makke
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is among the most burdensome neurological disorders worldwide, with an impact that extends far beyond seizure frequency alone. Depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and internalized stigma affect a substantial proportion of individuals with epilepsy, yet these comorbidities remain systematically undertreated in routine neurological care. Conventional psychoeducation, largely centered on passive information delivery, has shown limited effectiveness in addressing the psychological and social complexities of living with epilepsy. Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Epilepsy (NIPE) offers a fundamentally different approach: one that translates the neuroscience of seizure generation, network dysfunction, and neuroplasticity into accessible frameworks, shifting patients from passive recipients of information to active, metacognitively engaged participants in their own care.This chapter presents NIPE as both a clinical framework and an integrative layer across the continuum of epilepsy management. Beginning with the neurobiological mechanisms underlying seizures and epileptogenesis, it highlights how the same neural networks implicated in ictal activity also contribute to the psychiatric and cognitive comorbidities that shape patients’ daily experiences. It further examines how NIPE interfaces with evidence-based psychological interventions, pharmacologic education, neuromodulation, epilepsy surgery, and the management of refractory epilepsy, as well as the unique needs of women and other populations with distinct clinical considerations.In addition, the chapter explores the digital expansion of NIPE, including adaptive telehealth platforms, wearable biosensors, digital phenotyping, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence in tailoring psychoeducational delivery. Importantly, it addresses current limitations and ethical considerations with transparency, including the absence of standardized NIPE protocols and the relative scarcity of randomized controlled trials specifically within epilepsy populations.The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on the infrastructure, research agenda, and cross-disciplinary collaboration required to embed NIPE into routine epileptology practice. NIPE is positioned not as an adjunct to epilepsy care, but as a unifying framework, a shared language that enables truly integrated, patient-centered care.

papers.title: A Critical Epistemological Audit of Early Evidence Syntheses in Generative AI Educational Research: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.authors: Tim Fütterer, Nina Peltzer, Peter H. Gerjets, Detmar Meurers, Tamara Powell Tate, Mark Warschauer, Valentin Emslander, Lisa Bardach, John hattie, Michael Sailer, Jochen Kühn
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of ChatGPT in education was accompanied by an equally rapid proliferation of meta-analyses synthesizing its effects on educational outcomes. We conducted a systematic epistemological audit of the first wave of these meta-analyses, evaluating both their methodological and reporting quality and the primary evidence they synthesized. We included meta-analyses published after the release of ChatGPT that quantitatively synthesized its effects on educational outcomes. Five meta-analyses comprising 87 unique primary studies met our inclusion criteria. We also reconstructed their quantitative evidence base and conducted exploratory three-level random-effects meta-analyses to examine effect magnitude, heterogeneity, and robustness, and how these varied with theoretically and methodologically relevant characteristics. The five meta-analyses generally searched multiple databases, specified eligibility criteria, and examined heterogeneity and potential publication bias, but showed limitations in independent screening and coding, preregistration, open data and code, and transparent reporting. The underlying primary evidence likewise showed methodological and reporting limitations and substantial conceptual heterogeneity. Among 69 classifiable primary studies, 79.7% assessed performance exclusively, whereas only 11.6% assessed learning exclusively. The reconstructed meta-analysis yielded a positive average effect (g = 0.83, 95% CI [0.68, 0.97]), but heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 94.06%; 95% prediction interval [−0.75, 2.41]), and estimates were markedly attenuated in sensitivity analyses addressing small-study and selection effects. Although positive effects remained among stronger studies assessing learning, increasingly stringent quality criteria rapidly reduced the evidence base, limiting the certainty and generalizability of conclusions about learning effects. Overall, our findings caution against interpreting a single pooled estimate as a stable general effect of ChatGPT on learning and highlight the need for more rigorous, conceptually precise, transparent, and reproducible research.

papers.title: White Paper: AI-Driven AML/CFT Transformation in APAC
papers.authors: Rohan Bedi
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) are transforming anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) frameworks across the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region. As financial crime becomes increasingly sophisticated, traditional rules-based transaction monitoring systems face growing limitations, including excessive false-positive alerts, fragmented customer data, operational inefficiencies and reduced effectiveness in identifying complex criminal networks. Financial institutions are consequently transitioning towards advanced analytics, behavioural monitoring, network intelligence and AI-enabled financial crime detection.This paper examines the evolving regulatory landscape governing AI/ML adoption in AML/CFT, with particular reference to Singapore, Hong Kong and Malaysia. It analyses initiatives led by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), alongside relevant industry-led frameworks and collaborative intelligence-sharing mechanisms. These developments illustrate a broader supervisory shift towards intelligence-led financial crime detection, responsible AI adoption, stronger data governance and demonstrable control effectiveness.The paper identifies eleven critical risk areas arising throughout the AI/ML lifecycle. These encompass data quality and pipeline contamination, fragmented customer and entity resolution, inadequate independent model validation, training-data bias, model opacity, automation bias, unmanaged model drift, excessive vendor reliance, inadequate audit trails, cybersecurity and model-integrity threats, and the misapplication of models beyond their validated scope. It examines how these weaknesses can undermine detection effectiveness, compromise accountability and expose financial institutions to operational, compliance and supervisory risks.A central argument is that AI adoption cannot be treated as a standalone technology upgrade. Its effectiveness depends on reliable and integrated data infrastructure, independent model validation, explainability, appropriate human oversight, continuous performance monitoring, effective lifecycle governance and clear senior-management accountability. The paper also maps the emerging technology ecosystem across customer due diligence, screening, transaction monitoring, investigations, regulatory reporting, privacy-enhancing technologies, digital-asset analytics and digital identity verification.By bringing together regulatory developments, supervisory risk considerations and representative technology capabilities, this paper provides a practical framework for understanding the transformation of AML/CFT operating models across APAC. It contributes to the discussion on responsible financial-sector AI governance by highlighting the relationship between technological innovation, institutional accountability and effective financial crime prevention.

papers.title: Working Paper on Law and Technology: AI Guardrails Principles
papers.authors: Rohan Bedi
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can advance health, safety, education, productivity and risk reduction. Its growing capabilities raise a fundamental question: which human functions and forms of authority must remain protected, even where AI can perform them more efficiently?This Working Paper proposes the AI Guardrails Principles, a human-primacy framework to guide future legislation. Its central proposition is that AI should make humanity more capable—not make humanity less necessary. It distinguishes AI that augments human capability from deployments that replace protected human functions, transfer protected human authority or exceed authorised limits.The Principles assess what an AI deployment actually does, not merely its technology or stated purpose. Protection follows the function, whether performed by an employee, contractor, freelancer or gig worker. AI may assist without replacing protected human performance.The framework protects human labour, professional and creative work, professional training pathways and fundamental decisions while enabling beneficial AI. Human authority over lethal force must be retained; AI functions involving weapons of mass destruction and internationally prohibited weapons are restricted. The Principles also address AI-enabled manipulation, prohibited unsolicited communications and exploitation of legally protected vulnerabilities or characteristics.AI and robotics may replace human performance in specific tasks involving defined physical hazards, subject to the Principles’ conditions; this exception does not provide a general justification for replacing workers in non-hazardous functions.The framework applies to private enterprises, public authorities and publicly funded institutions. It addresses workforce reductions, subject to applicable redeployment, retraining and employment-transition obligations. It distinguishes individual AI use, where people remain responsible for validating their work, from organisational deployments and autonomous systems beyond practical human review.For increasingly autonomous AI, the Principles limit AI-to-AI delegation, collective capability, computational resources, self-development and capability enhancement. They require meaningful human authority and, where specified, intervention, suspension, termination and restoration to an authorised safe state. Anti-evasion provisions address circumvention through outsourcing, intermediaries, offshore infrastructure or restructuring.The paper proposes an independent AI regulatory authority and a mandatory regulatory classification test. This principles-based international framework—not draft legislation—aims to inform future AI regulation while enabling beneficial innovation, preserving human agency and protecting defined human functions and authority.

papers.title: Evaluating MiniMax-M3 for Automated Web Penetration Testing on XBEN Benchmarks
papers.authors: Azriel Sebastian Pamungkas, Budi Handoko, Fauzi Adi Rafrastara
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Informatics and Computing
papers.abstract: The use of automated penetration testing is growing as an important way to manage the rising expenses and technical requirements of today’s cybersecurity. The main issue addressed is the significant difference in the performance of Large Language Models (LLM) and the associated operational costs for performing autonomous security assessments. The goal of this study is to explore the effect of integrating the open-weight long-context model MiniMax-M3 into the PentestGPT framework. The research used a methodical experimental process with the XBEN benchmark suite, which consists of 104 web security challenges with different difficulty levels and vulnerability classifications. The execution followed a five-stage pipeline: benchmark loading, wiring the framework, planning with the LLM, executing the commands and analyzing the performance. Results indicate a total success rate of 71.2% with perfect scores on 5 vulnerability classes including SQL injection and JWT forgery. Cost analysis shows that this framework can greatly reduce the cost in comparison with the frontier-tier models. Overall, MiniMax-M3 provides an efficient and cost-effective option for automated vulnerability triage, instructional scenarios, and reproducible security evaluation harnesses under human-in-the-loop oversight.

papers.title: The Effect of AI-Supported Coding Instruction on 21st-Century Skills
papers.authors: Osman Kayhan
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of artificial intelligence–supported coding instruction on students’ 21st-century skills. A quantitative research approach employing a pretest–posttest quasi-experimental design with a control group was used. The study group consisted of high school students. While the experimental group received artificial intelligence-supported coding instruction, the control group continued with coding instruction based on the existing teaching method. Data were collected using a 21st-century skills scale. To examine within-group changes, a paired-samples t test was conducted, and to determine between-group differences, ANCOVA was performed by controlling pretest scores. The findings indicated that both the experimental and control groups showed significant increases in their 21st-century skills scores. When pretest scores were controlled, no statistically significant difference was found between the posttest scores of students who received artificial intelligence–supported coding instruction and those who received coding instruction based on the existing teaching method. The results demonstrate that both the existing teaching method–based coding instruction and artificial intelligence–supported coding instruction are effective in developing students’ 21st-century skills. Accordingly, it is recommended that different instructional approaches used in coding education be planned in a way that supports targeted 21st-century skills and that teaching processes be structured using a holistic approach.

papers.title: GOVERNING INNOVATION: POLITICAL INSTITUTIONS, BUSINESS STRATEGIES, HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS AND INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT IN THE ERA OF INTELLIGENT TECHNOLOGIES
papers.authors: Ahmad Reshad Rahimi, Fazel Rabi Mohammad Naser, Mohammad Hanif Rasekh, Abdull Samim Adib
papers.journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
papers.abstract: Globally, smart technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) is proliferating quickly and reshaping political institutions, business practices, healthcare delivery systems, and civil infrastructure development. This review discusses how governments, organizations, health systems, and infrastructure planners are adjusting governance, strategic frameworks, and engineering practices to embrace AI-enabled innovation, while managing risks. We used a narrative review methodology, synthesizing peer-reviewed literature, policy reports, and institutional publications published between 2016 and 2026 obtained from Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar databases. The review identifies five interconnected themes: (1) The changing role of political institutions in regulating AI through policy frameworks and digital governance initiatives; (2) Business adoption strategies for AI integration, including automation of decision-making and transformation of the workforce; (3) AI applications in healthcare systems, including diagnostics and patient care, along with ethical and equity concerns; (4) Integration of intelligent systems in civil engineering and infrastructure, including smart construction, structural health monitoring, and resilient urban planning; and (5) Broader social implications such as algorithmic bias, labor displacement, and digital inequality. Findings suggest that while intelligent technologies produce significant efficiency and innovation gains across sectors, fragmented regulatory approaches and uneven institutional capacity create governance gaps that are disproportionately borne by vulnerable populations and under-resourced infrastructure systems.
