However, precise control of pneumatic actuators is challenging due to their inherent nonlinearities. This paper presents the development of a compact 13-DOF upper-body humanoid robot. To assess the feasibility of an effective controller, we first investigate its key dynamic properties, such as actuation time delays, and confirm that its behavior is reproducible across repeated trials. Leveraging this reproducibility, we implement a preliminary data-driven controller for a 4-DOF arm subsystem based on a multilayer perceptron with explicit time delay compensation. The network was trained on random movement data to generate pressure commands for tracking arbitrary trajectories. In comparative evaluations on this subsystem, the data-driven controller achieved lower tracking errors than a traditional PID controller. This result suggests that data-driven approaches are a promising option for controlling complex, high-DOF pneumatic robots.

papers.title: Social robots in the real world: an analysis of social robot use based on consumer reviews
papers.authors: Katarzyna Kabacińska, Gabriella K. Guerra, Mallorie T. Tam, Julie M. Robillard
papers.abstract: Social robots (SR) are increasingly developed to support users’ mental health needs. Previous research suggests that potential benefits of interacting with SR include reduction in depressive symptoms, loneliness and improved quality of life. Despite the promising impact of short-term robot use, little is known about how SRs are used beyond short interaction in the research environment, and what spontaneous robot adoption looks like. Thus, in this study we set out to address this gap through an analysis of user-generated robot reviews. We analysed online reviews of commercially available SRs to characterise their impact and user experience. We used qualitative content analysis to extract salient themes from 1350 user-generated reviews, supplemented by sentiment analysis of the full sample of 9333 reviews. The content analysis revealed a list of SR use cases, user circumstances and characteristics, the impact of using the robots and ethical challenges experienced by users. The results suggest that self-reported benefits, such as improved mood, reduced depression and loneliness, are maintained through long-term robot use. This study provides a novel qualitative insight into user experiences and SR use in the real world that will inform future robotic development and implementation efforts.

papers.title: Parental participation in empirical studies about sexual health: a systematic review of challenges and opportunities
papers.authors: Marlene Muehlmann, Rena Stranzky, Silke Schmidt, Samuel Tomczyk
papers.abstract: Abstract Working with parents to improve the sexual health of adolescents is a popular and promising strategy. As it can be challenging, this review aimed to identify and synthesize barriers to and facilitators of parental participation in empirical studies about adolescent sexual health. A systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines was conducted. Nine databases (CINAHL, Cochrane, EMBASE, ERIC, PubMed, PsycInfo, PsycArticles, PSYNDEX, and Web of Science) were searched using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria (e.g., parents of adolescents aged 10–19 years, publications from 2000 to 2023 in English or German, and exclusion of studies from the WHO African Region). The QualSyst Checklist was used to assess study quality. Findings were synthesized narratively due to the heterogeneity of qualitative and quantitative designs. Twenty-four studies from 12 countries were included that mostly focused on interviews and self-reports of parents. Barriers to participation included parents’ perception of sexual health as a low-priority topic, discomfort with the subject, and time constraints due to busy daily schedules. Facilitators included the perceived need for parental support and a promotion of positive views on adolescent sexual health. In addition, parental co-creation of study materials, recruitment strategies, data collection, social proofing and having well-qualified communicators were identified as design-based facilitators of study participation. Most barriers to study participation seem to persist across countries for over two decades, and most research has been done on barriers in lieu of facilitators. Most facilitators were reported by only a single study, limiting the consistency and precision of the current evidence base. Future research should focus, therefore, on facilitators, and co-creation principles and study design recommendations should be implemented more thoroughly.

papers.title: AI literacy in student translation practices: evidence from ChatGPT use in Hong Kong
papers.authors: Hao YIN, Liu Jian-wen, Mengyao Qi, Zeping Huang
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), such as ChatGPT, is reshaping translation practices by enabling dynamic human–AI interaction and placing new demands on users. However, less is known about how students develop the competencies required to critically and responsibly engage with GenAI in translation contexts. This study investigates students’ AI literacy through a multidimensional framework comprising knowledge, usage, evaluation, affect, and ethics. A mixed-methods design was employed, combining questionnaire data from 146 university students in Hong Kong with semi-structured interviews with 10 participants. Quantitative results indicate a generally positive but uneven AI literacy profile: students report high levels of usage, knowledge, and affect, relatively lower evaluation competence, and relatively low score of ethics dimension. Correlation analysis further reveals a clustered structure among knowledge, usage, evaluation, and affect, whereas ethics is weakly associated with all other dimensions. Qualitative findings further illuminate this imbalance. While students actively integrate ChatGPT into translation tasks and demonstrate strong emotional engagement, their evaluative practices are mediated by prompt design and prior knowledge. More critically, ethics emerges as the least internalized dimension, characterized by a gap between awareness and actual implementation in practice. This study contributes to AI literacy research by demonstrating its structurally uneven and partially decoupled nature in AI-mediated translation. It further reconceptualizes ethics as a structurally under-integrated dimension and highlights the interactional and input-dependent nature of evaluative competence.

papers.title: Legal and Ethical Governance of Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: A Narrative Transcontinental Review Across Pan-Africa, Pan-Asia, and the Americas
papers.authors: Iqbal Siddi Ganie, Irshad Siddi Ganie, Naazim Siddi Ganie, J G Gibson, Shashank Chapala, Rayda Aaishah Joomun, Rajesh Botchu
papers.journal: Indian journal of radiology and imaging - new series/Indian journal of radiology and imaging/Indian Journal of Radiology & Imaging
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is now embedded in radiology workflows for prioritization, interpretation, quantification, and reporting. As adoption expands, radiologists must address professional responsibility, liability, patient disclosure, data governance, and algorithmic bias. This narrative review used PRISMA-informed, non-systematic methods. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched together with official regulatory and professional websites (including the World Health Organization, the Food and Drug Administration, the Department of Health and Human Services, the National Institute of Standards and Technology, the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Commission, Indian Council of Medical Research, MeitY, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, and AU/AUDA-NEPAD) for English-language literature and legal or policy documents published from January 2018 to March 2026. Search terms combined “radiology,” “artificial intelligence,” “ethics,” “liability,” “privacy,” “bias,” “governance,” “HIPAA,” “GDPR,” “DPDP,” and related terms. Review findings: global principles are converging, but implementation remains regionally contingent. We compare African, Asian, American, and selected international benchmarks, clarify that AFRI-CARE, ASIA-GUIDE, AMERICAS, and RADIANT are proposed conceptual frameworks, and show how they translate shared governance domains into practice. Defensible AI adoption in radiology requires transparent methods, local validation, subgroup monitoring, human oversight, and context-sensitive governance that reflects infrastructure, law, and equity priorities across regions.

papers.title: An explainable two stage framework for spatial temporal traffic accident prediction and injury severity classification
papers.authors: Yahui Wang, Yue He, Zhoushuo Liang, Pengfei Tian
papers.abstract: Traffic accidents pose severe risks to public safety, yet existing injury severity prediction models often overlook spatial-temporal dynamics. This study proposes a two-stage framework integrating spatial-temporal analysis with machine learning to enhance prediction accuracy and interpretability. In the first stage, a Graph Convolution Network-Long Short-Term Memory (GCN-LSTM) model predicts daily accident counts across administrative regions, incorporating the predictions normalized as relative frequencies as features for injury severity classification. The second stage, which classifies the injury severity of accidents that have occurred, employs a stacking ensemble model with four tree-based classifiers, selecting the best-performing configuration based on performance metrics. Experimental results on a real-world dataset demonstrate the framework’s superiority over traditional methods. The GCN-LSTM model reduces mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE) by 18.4% and 3.6%, respectively, compared to the state-of-the-art Spectral Temporal Graph Neural Network (StemGNN). The stacking model with Random Forest as the meta-learner achieves an 87% accuracy in severity prediction. SHAP-based interpretability analysis reveals key factors influencing injury severity, providing actionable insights for traffic safety management. This study offers an interpretable approach to injury severity prediction, supporting data-driven decision-making in accident prevention and emergency response.

papers.title: Markerless pose-derived movement quality assessment in physical education: a multi-task student performance analysis
papers.authors: Lihua Cui, Huang Xuan, Wenpeng Zhan
papers.abstract: Markerless motion capture offers a practical opportunity to support objective movement assessment in physical education, but its use for student performance evaluation remains limited by concerns about landmark reliability, task variability, camera-view effects, and insufficient validation. This study developed and internally validated a markerless pose-derived framework for evaluating student movement quality across common physical-education tasks. A publicly available synchronized marker-based and markerless motion-capture dataset was analyzed. The final analytical dataset included 21 male physical-education students, seven tasks, two camera views, and 294 eligible task-view trials. Markerless keypoints following the COCO-17 anatomical landmark convention were reconstructed into frame-level skeletons, cleaned using confidence-based filtering, interpolated for short gaps, smoothed, and normalized by body scale. Trial-level features were extracted to quantify movement amplitude, symmetry, smoothness, rhythm, postural control, and detection reliability. A Markerless Movement Quality Score was generated using equal-weighted, expert-weighted, and PCA-derived scoring strategies. Trials were stratified into low, moderate, and high pose-derived movement-quality groups within each task-view combination. Internal validation used grouped 5-fold, leave-one-subject-out, final subject holdout, leave-one-task-out, and leave-one-view-out strategies. The pipeline reconstructed 951,067 frame-level skeletons and more than 16 million keypoint observations. Trunk and lower-limb landmarks showed high reliability, with hips, knees, ankles, and shoulders demonstrating near-complete tracking availability, whereas facial landmarks were less stable. Task-level features captured distinct movement signatures across walking, jogging, high knees, jumping jacks, lunges, and squats. The scoring methods showed strong agreement, including Spearman correlations of 0.97 between equal-weighted and expert-weighted scores, 0.96 between equal-weighted and final scores, and 0.94 between PCA-derived and final scores. The PCA performance landscape showed partial separation of low, moderate, and high movement-quality groups. Machine-learning validation was modest, with the best grouped 5-fold Macro-F1 reaching approximately 0.39, and weaker cross-view generalization. The confusion matrix showed better recognition of low-quality trials than moderate or high-quality trials. Markerless pose-derived features can provide interpretable trial-level descriptors of movement quality across physical-education tasks, particularly when based on reliably detected trunk and lower-limb landmarks. However, predictive validation was modest, with limited discrimination between adjacent movement-quality groups and weak generalization across some task and camera-view conditions. The internally derived MMQS groups were not independently expert-rated, and the present results therefore support feasibility and internal methodological validation rather than reliable automated grading or generalizable performance prediction. External validation against expert assessments, marker-based trajectories, larger cohorts, and real classroom conditions is required before practical educational deployment.

papers.title: Is AI eroding PhD students’ critical thinking and analysis skills?
papers.authors: David Payne

papers.title: Beyond accuracy: How humans evaluate legally correct but socially controversial legal advice from machines.
papers.authors: Benjamin Minhao Chen, Zhiyu Li
papers.abstract: AI systems are increasingly used to provide legal advice, raising questions about whether laypeople accept guidance from algorithms-especially when that advice is legally correct but socially controversial.We report a preregistered survey experiment with 3,348 adults in mainland China examining how people evaluate identical legal advice when it is attributed either to an AI system or to a human lawyer and when it is accompanied by reasoning or not.Contrary to expectations of algorithm aversion, attribution to an AI system has no net effect on perceived reasonableness.However, mediation analyses reveal opposing psychological pathways underlying this null result.AI-attributed advice is perceived as more objective, which increases perceived reasonableness, but also as less comprehensive and less attentive to special circumstances, which decreases perceived reasonableness.By contrast, providing legal reasoning substantially increases perceived reasonableness regardless of source, largely by enhancing perceptions of objectivity.Qualitative responses corroborate this tension between objectivity and contextual sensitivity in evaluations of legal advice.Together, these findings suggest that public responses to AI legal advisors are shaped not by rigid attitudes toward automation but by the balancing of competing normative expectations.The results have implications for theories of algorithm aversion and the design of AI recommendation systems in normatively salient domains.

papers.title: Structural-before/after-measurement approaches for estimating treatment effects in latent outcomes with causal machine learning.
papers.authors: Amota Ataneka, Benjamin M. Kelcey, Jean Baptiste Habarurema
papers.abstract: Prior research has developed a deep and diverse set of methods specifically designed to accommodate reflective latent factors (e.g., structural equation models). A critical limitation of conventional latent variable methods is that they typically operate under assumptions of linearity and almost always presume correct model specification (e.g., all nonlinearities and n-way interactions are known and included). Recent research in machine learning has relaxed such limitations by developing data-adaptive methods that identify treatment effects by empirically estimating the functional forms of relationships among covariates, treatment, and an outcome. A significant weakness of causal machine learning methods, however, is that they have been almost exclusively developed for observed outcome variables and have not considered reflective latent outcomes that are measured with error. In this study, we developed structural-after/before-measurement methods suitable for targeted machine learning with latent outcomes. The results suggested that the proposed estimators are nearly unbiased in finite samples even when the functional relationships are unknown and unspecified. We demonstrate the methods with an application to teachers' burnout study and compare their performance with conventional linear structural equation models. papers.title: The Tensed Computer Improviser and the workmanship of risk: Small-dataset machine learning and real-time interactive musical improvisation
papers.authors: Taylor Brook
papers.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has entered music overwhelmingly by way of large industrial models trained on vast corpora, in which the outcome is fixed in advance by an apparatus that the musician neither controls nor understands. This article argues that the essential machine-learning operations of dataset assembly, feature extraction and model fitting can instead be utilised transparently as part of an artist’s creative practice. Looking to David Pye’s concepts of workmanship of certainty and workmanship of risk , this article examines the design of the Tensed Computer Improviser (TCI), an open-source machine improviser built in Max with the Fluid Corpus Manipulation (FluCoMa) toolkit, which trains models from a small audio corpus of the user’s own choosing, with no pretrained component and no external training stage. Situating the TCI within a genealogy of machine improvisation using small data, the article analyses its design through the vocabulary of craft where the corpus curation and training are integrated into the creative act and the characteristic errors of small data are welcomed as tool-marks.

papers.title: Time-restricted eating with energy restriction modestly improves fat mass loss in severe obesity: the MACRO randomised clinical trial
papers.authors: Tatiana Almeida de Moraes Campos, Raiane Lira Freitas Brasil, Marina Antunes Oliveira, Ana Carina Ferreira Feitosa, Nassib Bezerra Bueno, Alessandra da Rocha Pinheiro Mulder, Flávia Fioruci Bezerra
papers.abstract: Abstract This 12-wk randomised trial evaluated weight loss, body composition changes and metabolic responses to a time-restricted eating with energy restriction (TRE + ER) diet in adults with severe obesity. One hundred participants (20–60 years; BMI > 40 kg/m 2 ) were randomised to TRE + ER ( n 50; eating window 10 am–6 pm) or continuous energy restriction (CER, n 50). Diets provided 60 % of total energy expenditure. Body composition, by DXA, and RMR, by indirect calorimetry, were assessed at baseline and after 1, 5, 9 and 12 wk. Subjective appetite ratings and biochemical markers were also determined. After 12 wk, both groups experienced reductions in body weight, fat mass (FM) and visceral adipose tissue (VAT), with no significant change in fat-free mass. Compared with CER, TRE + ER produced similar reductions in weight (−4·3 ± 0·4 kg v. −3·8 ± 0·4 kg; P = 0·46) and VAT (−270 ± 4 g v. −188 ± 4 g; P = 0·24), but greater FM loss (−3·5 ± 0·3 kg v. −2·4 ± 0·3 kg; P = 0·040). TRE + ER showed a greater decline in RMR ( P = 0·032) and a trend towards greater adaptive thermogenesis ( P = 0·061). Our findings suggest that combining ER with the TRE strategy does not enhance weight loss, despite the modestly greater FM loss after 12 wk. The greater decline in RMR and the greater increase in adaptive thermogenesis suggest limited long-term benefit of the TRE strategy in individuals with severe obesity. Registered at REBEC (RBR-45fpgqh – https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-45fpgqh ).

papers.title: The illusion of outsourcing learning: A learner-centered perspective on AI in education
papers.authors: Markus H. Hefter
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (genAI) is rapidly transforming education, but not the cognitive mechanisms through which humans learn. However, genAI’s effects on learning are often discussed in terms of technological capabilities rather than the cognitive processes through which learning occurs. In this paper, I build on learner-centered accounts for evaluating genAI in education. Through an educational psychology and cognitive science lens, I argue that technologies can influence learning only insofar as they support or interfere with learners’ active cognitive processing. This perspective is particularly important because genAI can increasingly perform cognitive operations on learners’ behalf, such as generating explanations, organizing information, and solving problems. Such capabilities may indeed increase efficiency, but they may also deprive learners of cognitive activities essential for learning. Therefore, the key question for genAI in education is not whether genAI improves learning, but whether the cognitive operations delegated to genAI are operations that learners need to perform themselves for the intended learning to occur. The same genAI function may therefore support learning under one learning objective and undermine it under another. Thus, performing better with genAI support should not be mistaken for learning that remains once the support is removed. Moreover, explicit learning objectives do not capture all cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, social, or developmental opportunities afforded by an activity. Educational psychology is uniquely positioned to determine which cognitive operations learners need to perform themselves and which may be delegated to genAI. It can also help identify what may be lost when such operations are outsourced.

papers.title: Shifting cognitive structures in human-AI collaborative learning design
papers.authors: Yanyi Wu

papers.title: Emergence and development of observation practices in AI-assisted plant adaptation learning
papers.authors: Widi Purwianingsih, Pipih Nurhayati, Ari Widodo, Achmad Samsudin, R Riandi
papers.abstract: Observation is a fundamental scientific practice in science learning, particularly for understanding gradual biological phenomena such as plant adaptation. Despite the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, limited research has examined how AI-supported tools influence students' observation practices during authentic scientific inquiry. This study investigates the emergence and development of students' observation practices during plant adaptation learning supported by an AI-based identifier. A six-week mixed-methods exploratory study was conducted with 84 middle school students. Learning activities were organised into four phases: orientation, initial observation, AI-assisted identification, and re-observation and validation. Data were collected through observation sheets, students' observation notes, reflective journals, group discussions, and records of AI use. Quantitative analysis revealed significant differences in observation orientations across learning phases (Friedman test, p < .001), indicating changes in observation practices over time. Qualitative findings showed that students initially relied on AI-generated cues to guide their observations. Over time, however, observation practices shifted toward direct empirical observation and peer-supported validation through repeated comparisons of plant characteristics across environmental conditions. The findings reveal a developmental trajectory from AI-reliant observation to direct observation and collaborative validation, accompanied by a gradual reduction in dependence on AI-generated outputs. These findings suggest that AI may function as an initial observational scaffold, while more sophisticated observation practices emerge through repeated engagement with phenomena and collaborative reasoning.

papers.title: Transforming constructivist learning in engineering education through Comnet-Art: An AI-driven augmented reality learning environment
papers.authors: Muhammad Akhsan Hakiki, Rani Kartika, Mustofa Abi Hamid, Yahfenel Evi Fussalam, Ade Fricticarani, Resti Utami, Abdul Haris Setiawan, Ridho Dedy Arief Budiman, Arisman Sabir, Tri Wiyoko
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) in educational technology has opened new opportunities for enhancing constructivist learning, particularly in computer network education. This study aimed to design, develop, and evaluate Comnet-Art, an AI-based AR learning application, to improve students' understanding and constructivist skills in computer networks. The research involved 234 undergraduate students and employed the ADDIE model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) along with expert validation, practicality testing, and effectiveness assessment. Validation results indicated strong content and media validity, with average Aiken's V scores of 0.92 from media experts and 0.89 from material experts, categorized as very valid. Practicality assessments revealed high usability and engagement, with educators reporting an average practicality score of 91.85% and students 90.71%. Effectiveness evaluation using pre-test and post-test comparisons demonstrated substantial learning gains, with the mean score increasing from 68.21 to 86.47 and a relative improvement of 26.76%, confirming the application's effectiveness in fostering engagement, collaboration, problem-solving, and constructivist learning outcomes. These findings highlight that Comnet-Art successfully integrates AI-driven interactivity and AR visualization to support active learning, improve conceptual understanding, and enhance higher-order cognitive skills. This study provides strong evidence that emerging technologies such as AI and AR can be effectively leveraged to transform engineering education and promote constructivist learning.

papers.title: Cognitive Offload Visibility: A design principle for instructional design and assessment in AI-mediated nursing education
papers.authors: Jennie Chang De Gagne

papers.title: Data-driven insight into CO2 electroreduction: Ensemble machine learning for CO Faraday efficiency prediction in single-atom catalysts
papers.authors: Dhanveer  Singh Rawat, Amit Pratap Singh, Arjun Singh Rawat
papers.abstract: This study presents an ensemble machine-learning (ML) framework to predict the Faraday efficiency of CO formation (FE CO ) for electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) on single-atom catalysts (SACs). A literature-derived dataset of 795 experimental entries from 42 primary studies was compiled, representing 24 carrier classes, 12 dopant atoms, and H-cell, flow-cell, and membrane-electrode-assembly (MEA) configurations. Eighteen regressors from nine algorithm families were systematically evaluated. A stacking ensemble combining gradient boosting decision tree, random forest, extremely randomized trees, support vector regression, k -nearest-neighbor regression, and CatBoost base learners with a kernel-based meta-regressor achieved the highest record-level performance, with a test R 2 of 0.9106 and an RMSE of 8.41 percentage points. Repeated five-fold cross-validation confirmed robust within-domain performance across random partitions (mean R 2 = 0.882 ± 0.006 ). Permutation importance, SHAP, partial-dependence analysis, and descriptor ablation identified dopant atom, applied potential, catalyst identity, and carrier as the dominant model-associated descriptors. Screening recovered established associations with Ni-based SACs, with graphene showing the highest mean model-predicted FE CO among the represented carrier classes. A discrete metal-potential response surface identified a Ni-associated region with a mean predicted FE CO of approximately 85% near -0.77 V versus RHE and a maximum of approximately 99% near -0.97 V. More stringent catalyst-, publication-, and Ni-restricted grouped validation showed weaker transfer to unseen systems. Thus, record-level performance primarily reflects interpolation within the represented experimental domain, while screening identifies experimentally grounded, dataset-conditioned trends for further validation.

papers.title: Language-derived mental object load suppresses posterior alpha power
papers.authors: Xinchi Yu, Utku Türk, Allison Dods, Xing Tian, Ellen F. Lau
papers.abstract: Language and vision are two primary source modalities of information for humans. To uncover shared and unique mental representations across linguistic and visual inputs, one approach is to test the extent to which a certain neural signature is shared. In the current EEG study, we tested whether the response profile of posterior alpha power – a neural signature well-studied for visual working memory – generalizes to non-visual linguistic input. Employing a novel imagine-one-then-more paradigm in a large EEG sample ( N = 52), we found that increasing the number of imagined objects derived from a non-visual linguistic source – auditory speech during eye closure – led to greater suppression of left posterior alpha power, and that this suppression plateaued beyond ∼ 3 objects. This response profile closely mirrors effects previously observed for visually-derived representations. As posterior alpha power likely reflects the representational load of slots/pointers or spatial attention in moment-to-moment cognition, our study thus provides novel insights into the specific representational facets shared across language and vision.

papers.title: Phase-dependent EEG decoding of continuous visual stimuli
papers.authors: Michele Deodato, David Melcher
papers.abstract: Neural oscillations support cognition and perception by organizing information across oscillatory cycles. Although animal studies support this view, evidence in humans is mixed and largely based on transient stimuli. We tested whether alpha oscillations, the dominant human brain rhythm, periodically modulate the strength of visual representations. EEG was recorded while participants viewed long-lasting (2 s) Gabor patches. Using a phase-dependent decoding approach, we quantified stimulus decoding accuracy at specific alpha phases. Decoding performance varied systematically with alpha phase, following a smooth unimodal profile that peaked over occipito-parietal electrodes. These effects emerged well after stimulus onset and generalized to earlier time points, indicating a modulation of visual processing during continuous input. Our findings demonstrate that visual information is represented more accurately at specific alpha phases. This provides strong evidence that sensory processing is shaped by intrinsic brain dynamics and introduces a generalizable decoding pipeline for linking oscillatory phase to neural information processing.

papers.title: Machine learning insights into corporate digital washing: Measurement, motivations and implications
papers.authors: Yan Hu, Haonan Wang, Jinhui Xu, Hao Li, Ying Huang
papers.abstract: : Corporate digitalization plays a critical role in fostering technological advancement and improving digital competence of a country. Assessing firm-level digitalization through textual information by existing studies, especially evaluating the digital-related keyword frequencies, gives rise to digital washing. Utilizing the annual reports of A-share listed companies in the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges as our corpus, we employ machine learning algorithms trained on individual stock price movements during event windows surrounding annual report disclosure dates to calculate the weights of each keyword each year. Based on the assigned weights, we re-evaluate corporate digitalization and construct Dwash , a continuous proxy for the wedge between conventional keyword-frequency-based digitalization and market-supervised digitalization. We also introduce the concepts of High-Frequency Generic Words (HFGW) and Low-Frequency Key Words (LFKW). Furthermore, we propose a theoretical framework and empirically explore the motivations behind corporate digital washing from various perspectives and the heterogeneity of these motivations. Finally, we examine the economic consequences of digital washing on stock price crash risk.

papers.title: Trust, gating, delegation, and identity: Human-factor dynamics in a 16-month single-developer trace of generative-AI-assisted development
papers.authors: Chen-Chung Chi
papers.abstract: Context: Generative-AI coding assistants have moved rapidly into software development practice, raising human-factor questions about trust, usability, and responsible adoption that lab studies and surveys do not fully answer; sustained turn-by-turn production traces remain rare. Objective: This study examines four human-factor dimensions of sustained generative-AI-assisted development — trust calibration, developer gating, delegation-related prompt dynamics, and authorial identity — in a real production setting. Methods: Longitudinal autoethnography of a 16-month single-developer construction of a cloud-native institutional service at a Taiwanese university (424 git commits, Dec 2024 – Apr 2026), with two prompt corpora across two IDE-mediated assistants used in succession: 172 user prompts plus 2777 assistant turns from Cursor IDE (Sep–Dec 2025), and 50 user prompts from Claude Code CLI (Apr 2026). Per-session formal indicators (Eqs. (1) , (2) , (3) , (4) , (5) ), an analysis of a pre-stated directional prediction (Section 5.3 ), and triangulation with a companion architectural analysis (Chi, 2026) constrain interpretation. Results: (T) Trust calibration — in the trace-documented stuck-loop episode, the developer escalated model tier rather than revising specification (a capacity-oriented escalation). (G) Gating — the agent iteration ratio rises with task ambiguity, consistent with reduced developer gating of the agent loop when prompting is under-specified. (D) Delegation — within the Cursor window, prompt length compresses by up to 98.7% within a session (first to last third) while rewrite signals do not consistently decline, and prompt-skill improvement is not measurable under the study’s indicators, a pattern interpreted as consistent with a shift from prompting toward delegation rather than a direct measurement of it; in the later Claude Code window, 33 of 50 prompts are follow-ups (66%), a cross-tool observation reported descriptively. (I) Identity diffusion — authoring voice in commit messages converges toward the assistant’s register. Conclusion: Engineering throughput appeared to decouple from the developer-side communication indicators across the period; potential developer-side effects of sustained AI assistance may not register in conventional engineering metrics, supporting a cautionary reading for human-factor-aware adoption. All quantitative magnitudes reported are observations from one case; the four dimensions are offered for analytical generalization, as hypotheses for multi-developer studies to test, not as evidence of general developer behaviour. The article closes with responsible-adoption implications for IDE-assistant design.

papers.title: Task-evoked brain network dynamics underlying executive function in preadolescent children
papers.authors: Alfia Parvez, Shreya Verma, Ruyu Liu, Ginger E. Reeser, Sean Patrick Mullen, Lauren B. Raine, Lisa M. Renzi‐Hammond, Charles H. Hillman, Naiman A. Khan
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Executive function (EF) has been studied using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) based functional connectivity (FC); however, electroencephalography (EEG) based dynamic FC interactions supporting EF in children and explaining behavioral performance remain underexplored. We used EEG to examine FC within and between seven core brain networks: Default Mode (DMN), Dorsal Attention (DAN), Ventral Attention (VAN), Somatomotor (SMN), Frontoparietal (FPN), Visual (VIN), and Limbic (LIN), during a modified Eriksen flanker task. We aimed to identify dynamic network configurations linked to EF, specifically selective attention and inhibitory control in preadolescent children (8-10 years). METHODS: Secondary analyses of source-localized EEG data from 84 children (mean age 8.89 ± 0.82 years; 51.2% female) were conducted. A Hidden Markov model extracted spatiotemporal dynamics, quantifying within- and between-network FC correlations. Support vector regression (SVR) with an interpretable kernel identified connectivity patterns predicting behavioral outcomes, including accuracy and reaction time (RT) interference. RESULTS: = 0.26). Behavioral performance indices were most strongly associated with interference within VAN, DMN, SMN, and VIN. Notably, within-VAN FC explained between-subject variability in both Accuracy Interference (ρ = -0.28, p = 0.012) and RT Interference (r = 0.26, p = 0.017). CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic, task-based FC, particularly within-VAN, underpins individual differences in EF among preadolescent children. Stronger within-VAN reconfiguration during high cognitive demand trials supported accuracy but at the cost of slower responses, highlighting a trade-off between stability and efficiency in developing EF.

papers.title: Developing Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Gen Z accounting students: The roles of AI Competency, Systematic Thinking Ability, and Design Thinking Ability
papers.authors: Nimnual Visedsun, Narinthon Imjai, Thanaporn Homlaor, Jorge Miguel Chávez-Díaz, Somnuk Aujirapongpan
papers.journal: The International Journal of Management Education

papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward artificial intelligence in pharmacy education and practice among pharmacy students and faculty in Bangladesh: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Md. Masud Morshed, Jannatul Ferdoush, Abu Tayab Moin, Sharmin Sultana Dina, Farjana Akter Nipa, Rukyea Yeasmin Mysha
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare systems, pharmaceutical innovation, and professional education globally. However, digital readiness for AI integration remains uneven across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), raising concerns about equity, governance, and workforce readiness. Understanding institutional and individual readiness is crucial for sustainable execution within health systems. Objective To assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding AI among pharmacy students and faculty in Bangladesh and identify predictors of implementation readiness. Methods A multi-institutional cross-sectional study was conducted among 447 participants (382 students; 65 faculty) from accredited pharmacy programs following a stratified convenience sampling method. A validated KAP instrument was administered electronically. Group differences were analyzed using independent-sample t -tests, while associations and predictors were examined using Pearson correlation and multiple regression models. Results Faculty demonstrated higher AI knowledge scores than students (4.22 ± 0.57 vs. 3.95 ± 0.73; p = 0.005; Cohen's d = 0.41). Students showed stronger support for curricular integration ( p = 0.034). Knowledge was moderately correlated with positive attitudes ( r = 0.42, p < 0.001). Regression analysis identified prior exposure (β = 0.18, p < 0.05) and workshop participation (β = 0.25, p < 0.001) as significant predictors of positive attitudes ( p < 0.01, Adj R 2 = 0.28). Despite limited institutional funding (23.1%), 72.3% of participants expressed willingness to engage in the development of national AI guidelines. Concerns regarding data privacy and regulatory oversight were consistently reported. Conclusion Findings indicate emerging AI readiness within pharmacy education in Bangladesh, but structural capacity gaps persist. Framed through digital readiness and implementation science perspectives, the results highlight the need for coordinated curriculum reform, faculty development, and governance frameworks. Bangladesh may serve as a scalable LMIC model for ethically grounded, workforce-aligned AI integration in health systems.

papers.title: Investigating secondary school students’ shared epistemic agency with GAI in online scientific explanation writing
papers.authors: Hsin‐Yi Chang, Bo-Ren Mau, Jyh-Chong Liang, Chin‐Chung Tsai
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly used as a pedagogical assistant in online learning; yet how young students, such as secondary school students, enact epistemic agency (EA) when learning with GAI remains underexplored. In this study, we examined the types and levels of EA demonstrated by secondary school students with scaffolded GAI and investigated the relation among students’ prior academic proficiency, self-efficacy in learning, and EA demonstrated. Participants were 122 seventh graders who engaged in an online bilingual inquiry unit on photosynthesis. The unit supports students in Taiwan in learning science inquiry and English as a foreign language, with GAI prompted and integrated to support students’ scientific explanation writing in English. Data collected and analyzed included students’ prior academic proficiency through assessments, self-efficacy in learning through questionnaires, and student–GAI conversation turns through textual conversation logs. Results identified seven types of student–GAI shared epistemic agency (SEA), with over 80% of students demonstrating such agency at least once. Correlation results indicated that the frequency of EA demonstrated by students was associated with their prior language proficiency. Cluster analysis with the retained four-profile solution further suggested that student–GAI SEA was likely to be activity-specific. The identified SEA categories provide a framework for examining student–GAI SEA, and the instruction design illustrates how GAI can be prompted to preserve opportunities for student contribution. Design implications for supporting students with different needs are discussed.

papers.title: Bridging accuracy and interpretability in predictive learning analytics: A human-centered grey-box approach
papers.authors: Ángel Hernández-García, Julián Chaparro-Peláez, Carlos Cuenca-Enrique, Carlos Salcedo-Valverde
papers.abstract: Learning analytics has been increasingly using predictive models to support educational decision-making. However, the trade-off between predictive accuracy and interpretability remains a central challenge that limits how these models can be understood and used by educators. This study examines grey-box approaches to performance prediction by comparing two strategies: a theory-driven approach that groups interaction data into pedagogically meaningful categories, and a data-driven approach based on raw clickstream events followed by post hoc eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques. Using clickstream data from three educational contexts with different scales and instructional formats, we empirically compare the predictive performance, interpretability, and pedagogical relevance of both strategies. The results show that raw-event models achieve higher predictive performance in the large-scale online context with rich interaction data, where XAI methods provide relatively stable and consistent explanatory patterns. In the smaller-scale blended setting, where platform data capture only part of the learning activity, theory-driven aggregation provides a predictive advantage, although results become inconclusive in very small cohorts. The findings indicate that there is no single optimal approach, and that modeling strategies should be selected according to data characteristics, instructional design, and analytic goals. From a human-centered learning analytics perspective, the study highlights the importance of methodological alignment for the meaningful and responsible use of predictive models in education.

papers.title: Does AI encourage lax thinking, or does the human preference for validation make it that way?
papers.authors: Braden T. Hall, William Hart

papers.title: Acute effects of a strength exercise session on inflammatory and lipid markers in overweight men
papers.authors: Alessandro Roberto Silveira Moreira, Érica Leandro Marciano Vieira, Yago Martins Fortes, Samara Silva de Moura, Lucélia Scarabeli Silva Barroso, Giovane Galdino, Guilherme Furtado, Heliana de Barros Fernandes, Aline Silva de Miranda, Hugo César Martins-Costa, Ana Cristina Simões e Silva, Janaína Matos Moreira, Albená Nunes-Silva
papers.abstract: Background Obesity is characterized by excessive adipose tissue accumulation, resulting in a chronic low-grade inflammatory state. Regular physical exercise is an effective non-pharmacological strategy for obesity management, improve mood and social parameters. During exercise, skeletal muscle acts as an endocrine organ by releasing myokines and promoting changes in leukocyte dynamics, which may regulate inflammation and metabolic homeostasis. This study investigated the acute effects of a single resistance exercise session on leukocyte counts, leukocyte-derived inflammatory indices, and lipid profile in overweight men. Methods Twelve overweight men (age: 34.95 ± 9.77 years; height: 174.16 ± 3.66 cm; body mass: 97.83 ± 12.87 kg; BMI: 32.30 ± 4.51 kg/m²) participated in the study. Participants completed a single resistance exercise session consisting of four sets of 12 maximum repetitions at 60% of one-repetition maximum (1RM) in the following exercises: 45° leg press, bench press, leg extension, seated row, leg curl, and shoulder press. Blood samples were collected before, immediately after, and 1 hour after exercise. Data normality was assessed using the Shapiro–Wilk test. Parametric variables were analyzed using one-way repeated-measures ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test, whereas non-parametric variables were analyzed using Friedman's test followed by Dunn's post hoc test. Results Heart rate, rating of perceived exertion (OMNI-RES), and blood lactate concentrations increased significantly during and immediately after the exercise session, confirming the physiological demands of the protocol. In contrast, creatine phosphokinase (CPK) concentrations remained unchanged. No significant changes were observed in total cholesterol, LDL-C, VLDL-C, or non-HDL-C concentrations, whereas triglyceride levels decreased significantly 1 hour after exercise compared with pre-exercise values. Total leukocyte and neutrophil counts increased immediately after exercise and remained elevated 1 hour post-exercise. Monocyte counts also increased immediately after exercise. Among the inflammatory indices, the systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI) and pan-immune inflammation value (PIV) increased significantly 1 hour after exercise, while the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) increased between the immediate and 1-hour post-exercise time points. Conclusions A single session of resistance exercise induced acute physiological and immunological responses in overweight men, characterized by increased heart rate, perceived exertion, lactate concentration, leukocyte mobilization, and leukocyte-derived inflammatory indices, accompanied by a reduction in circulating triglyceride levels. These findings suggest that acute resistance exercise promotes transient innate immune activation while eliciting early metabolic adaptations in overweight individuals.

papers.title: Student use of generative AI and perceived institutional support across three linguistic contexts
papers.authors: Deddy Gusman, David Sulistiawan Aditya, Dhita Widya Putri, NUR DAMAYANTI, Nurmalina Nurmalina, Gyöngyi Bujdosó
papers.abstract: Student use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) raises questions about how everyday academic practices relate to perceived institutional support. This exploratory cross-sectional survey used Indonesian, English, and Hungarian questionnaire versions sharing a common set of core items. The harmonised dataset included 186 respondents, mainly residents of Indonesia and Hungary. Overall, 78.0% reported using AI several times per week or daily (95% CI [71.5, 83.3]), 96.8% reported using ChatGPT (95% CI [93.1, 98.5]), and 79.6% reported perceived learning improvement (95% CI [73.2, 84.7]). Institution-funded access and clearer policies were the most frequently requested forms of support. In the full sample, the Indonesia–Hungary contrast was larger for professor encouragement (|r rb | = 0.549) than for perceived learning improvement (|r rb | = 0.050). However, governance-related contrasts attenuated in the small English-language subsample. Country, language, recruitment route, and response timing overlapped, and measurement invariance was not established. These findings describe sampled students’ perceptions and do not identify independent country effects, institutional policy quality, or a temporal lag between practice and governance. We use practice-governance decoupling as an interpretive description of the coexistence of routine reported use and uneven perceived support. A four-component heuristic distinguishes survey findings from literature-informed interpretation and proposed outcomes for future evaluation.

papers.title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence literacy scale for students
papers.authors: Esra Nur Demirtaş, Tuğçe Gamze İŞÇİ
papers.abstract: In today’s technological age, artificial intelligence literacy (AIL) has become a critical issue in the field of education. The ability to understand, use, and critically evaluate artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is recognized as a fundamental competency enabling students to actively participate in the digital age. In this context, the aim of this study is to develop a valid and reliable scale to obtain accurate data on artificial intelligence literacy by examining the concept of artificial intelligence literacy. The study sample consists of 870 students (424 boys, 346 girls) in grades 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 attending elementary and middle schools. A pool of 50 items was created to measure students’ levels of artificial intelligence literacy. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) resulted in 22 items and 6 subscales. The measurement model obtained from Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) demonstrated good fit. The Cronbach’s Alpha internal consistency coefficient for the scale was found to be 0.857, while the internal consistency coefficients for the subscales ranged between 0.81 and 0.82. The CR, AVE, MSV, and ASV values indicate that the scale possesses both discriminant and convergent validity. In conclusion, the developed scale possesses sufficient characteristics to determine students’ levels of AIL. This study will assist in the development, teaching, and learning of AIL, as well as in the evaluation of AI education.

papers.title: A systematic and critical review of artificial intelligence applications for enhancing well stimulation operations and sustainable reservoir management
papers.authors: Ali Naderi Hamlabadi, Mohammadreza Akbari, Mobina Pazoki, Yasin Khalili
papers.abstract: Well stimulation remains essential for improving reservoir productivity, but conventional workflows are constrained by geological heterogeneity, limited data, and dependence on empirical correlations. This systematic and comparative review examines artificial-intelligence applications in hydraulic fracturing, acidizing, sand control, and ultrasonic stimulation, focusing on 2020–2025 while selectively considering earlier foundational studies. The quantitative synthesis of 23 key application studies identified 11 studies on acidizing and acid fracturing (47.8%), 8 on hydraulic fracturing (34.8%), 3 on sand control (13.0%), and 1 on ultrasonic stimulation (4.3%). Neural-network architectures were reported in 16 studies (69.6%), while tree-based learners or ensembles appeared in 13 studies (56.5%); these categories overlap because several studies compared multiple algorithms. Among studies reporting numerical performance, R2 values for acidizing-related regression tasks ranged from 0.82 to 0.96, while reported classification accuracies for selected acidizing and sand-control applications ranged from 87.5% to above 90%. These values were not statistically pooled because the studies used different prediction targets, data scales, validation procedures, and performance definitions. Tree-based ensembles and neural networks currently dominate fracture-design and acidizing applications, whereas reinforcement learning, hybrid optimization, and physics-informed approaches remain less frequently investigated. Field-scale and cross-field validation are limited, particularly for sand control and ultrasonic stimulation, for which the available evidence is predominantly laboratory- or simulation-based. The principal barriers to operational deployment are proprietary and small datasets, inconsistent validation, limited interpretability, and uncertain model transferability. Future research should prioritize benchmark datasets, standardized reporting, external field validation, explainable and physics-constrained models, and carefully evaluated closed-loop stimulation systems. Graphical abstract

papers.title: Accordion music generation and variation algorithm integrating knowledge graph and transformer
papers.authors: Ming Zhao, 董梁飞
papers.abstract: Accordion music generation remains challenging due to the complexity of its structural organization and the lack of explicit performance-related information. This study proposes an enhanced generation framework that integrates a Knowledge Graph (KG) with a Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT). A specialized accordion KG is constructed to represent fundamental music theory principles and instrument-specific performance characteristics, including the unique left-hand bass accompaniment patterns of the accordion. Based on this knowledge representation, several improvements are introduced into the Transformer architecture. A Graph-Guided Self-Attention (GGSA) mechanism is developed to dynamically regulate attention distributions using knowledge-based constraints. In addition, a Variation Feature Injection Module (VFIM) is incorporated to generate recursive variations while preserving essential thematic characteristics. The proposed framework further models accordion-specific performance factors, including bellows pressure variations and fingering patterns. The Nottingham Database is adopted as the experimental corpus. The original symbolic music data are enhanced through instrument-specific representation processing, in which pitch, duration, and chord sequences are extracted to construct a performance-aware musical representation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a perplexity (PPL) of 3.42 and a harmonic validity rate of 94.8%. The generated melodies exhibit improved structural coherence, more natural coordination between left-hand accompaniment and right-hand melody, and stronger thematic consistency during variation generation. These findings indicate that integrating knowledge constraints with sequence modeling can effectively improve the structural quality and performance logic representation of accordion music generation. The proposed approach provides a potential technical foundation for automated composition, intelligent music education assistance, and the digital creation of instrument-specific music.

papers.title: Residential greenery as an overlooked preventive health and sustainability infrastructure
papers.authors: Frederike Büttner, Simone Sanft, Sonja Mohr-Stockinger, Sylvia Butenschön, Ina Säumel
papers.abstract: Abstract Urban health and sustainability research increasingly demonstrates the benefits of greenness around people’s homes, yet shared green spaces embedded in residential developments remain comparatively overlooked as distinct lived, designed, and managed environments. In this Perspective, we distinguish residential greenness as exposure from residential greenery as place and argue that the latter constitutes an underused layer of preventive health and sustainability infrastructure. Synthesising previously published empirical studies from Berlin with historical and international literature, we show how residential greenery is shaped by path-dependent housing and planning legacies that continue to influence accessibility, use, ecological quality, and opportunities for health and well-being. Resident-centred evidence further reveals functions that spatial measures alone cannot capture, including restoration, social interaction, everyday contact with nature, and the role of these spaces as collective “green living rooms”. Yet their multifunctional value is often only partly reflected in management priorities dominated by maintenance, costs, and technical requirements. We identify this mismatch as a blind spot in urban health and sustainability governance. We argue that addressing it requires complementing measures of green-space quantity with attention to quality, use, and resident experience, while embedding co-creation, biodiversity, environmental justice, and adaptive management into the governance of everyday residential landscapes.

papers.title: Predicting Hospital-associated complications in older adults: methodological considerations
papers.authors: Valiev Shukhrat, Dilnavoz Yuldasheva, Malika Khojimatova, Saidova Dilorom, Shaxlo R. Sodiqova, Nizom Ermatov, Zeynab Afzali
papers.abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict post-surgical complications, but predictive performance does not guarantee clinical readiness. Shimizu and colleagues developed a promising model for older adults undergoing tibial fracture surgery using a large Japanese database. However, four methodological pitfalls warrant attention. First, the composite outcome was not validated in this population, and excluding in-hospital deaths introduced survivorship bias, underestimating the true burden of severe complications. Second, days to surgery, a variable not known at admission, created target leakage that inflates performance and undermines the admission-time claim. Third, using the test set for feature selection violated TRIPOD guidelines and likely overstated the scorecard's utility. Fourth, the Super Learner exhibited substantial overfitting, with a 0.110 drop between training (AUC = 0.850) and test (AUC = 0.740) performance, while offering only marginal improvement over simpler models. We suggest redeveloping the model with proper internal validation, excluding leakage-prone predictors, treating death as a competing risk, and prioritizing interpretability when complex ensembles offer limited added value. External validation remains essential before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Institutional readiness for generative artificial intelligence is linked to resource constraints and governance capability in Ghanaian higher education
papers.authors: Anthony Aapia Korku Dzidzornu, Xukan Xu
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is diffusing across higher education, yet institutional governance struggles to adapt in resource-constrained settings. Existing research emphasizes adoption and acceptance, with less attention to how infrastructure and governance shape institutional readiness. This study investigates GenAI governance in Ghanaian higher education. A sequential multi-method design combined the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). DEMATEL drew on a 12-member expert panel to diagnose perceived influence among institutional factors, while PLS-SEM independently evaluated a literature-derived model using 792 student and faculty responses. Resource Sensitivity (RS) emerged as the strongest net-source factor in the expert-perceived influence structure (D−R = +3.685). In the PLS-SEM model, RS was negatively associated with Institutional Readiness (IR) (β = −0.295), whereas Technological Governance Architecture (TGA) was positively associated with IR (β = 0.454); the model explained 48.4% of IR variance (R 2 = 0.484). The RS → TGA → IR indirect association was significant (β = −0.061), consistent with complementary partial mediation. AI Literacy (AIL) showed no significant direct association with adoption-related risk, conceptualized as the Adoption–Risk Paradox (ARP), but showed a significant indirect association through Perceived Usefulness (PU). Policy Uncertainty (PUC) was positively associated with ARP, whereas TGA was negatively associated with it. The findings support a Hard–Soft Governance Gap in which infrastructural constraints and governance capability constitute distinct but interconnected conditions of readiness. Strengthening responsible GenAI integration requires coordinated attention to infrastructure, governance, policy clarity, and responsible-use practices.

papers.title: The gender dynamics of crop varietal choices in rural Kenya: navigating risk, diversification, and decision-making
papers.authors: Brenda Boonabaana, Peruth Naturinda, Carol Waweru, Benjamin Musembi Kivuva, Martina Cavicchioli, Berber Kramer
papers.abstract: How do women and men farmers in Kenya situate, form, and pursue varietal choices amidst unequal gender relations, seed markets, and climate variability? Drawing on 67 individual interviews and focus group discussions across five Kenyan counties—Bungoma, Busia, Meru, Tharaka Nithi, and Makueni, we apply a feminist political ecology (FPE) lens to examine women and men smallholder farmers’ varietal choices and use in rural Kenya. We show that varietal choice is neither linear nor a simple shift toward ‘newness’ but rather a gendered, intersectional, and bioculturally embedded process of negotiation by farmers to maintain seed diversity and meet multiple short-term and long-term needs, including consumption, marketability, agroecological adaptation and cultural drivers such as labor demands and culinary values. While production traits were prioritized by both women and men, women also highly valued processing and consumption traits. Men (adults and youth) prioritized market traits such as yield potential and market potential. Varietal availability, trust, price, and agroecological fit shape women and men’s perceptions about a variety, choice and use. Gender and age differences shape varietal awareness, with young men and women’s access to information through digital platforms, while adult women relied on interpersonal and local networks. Adult men used radio and mobile phones. Findings illuminate farmers’ strategic maintenance of varietal portfolios spanning both local landraces and breeding varieties. We conclude that seed policies should integrate local knowledge and gendered realities, availability, and access to preferred varieties. Strengthening farmer-researcher crop technology co-creation through participatory breeding, on-farm seed conservation and multiplication is essential.

papers.title: Constructing and Evaluating a Dual-Loop Human-AI Collaborative POA-Based Oral English Teaching Paradigm for Cross-Cultural Communication Competence Development

papers.title: An Improved DSC‐Based Fixed‐Time Resilient Tracking Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems With Full‐State Constraints
papers.authors: Bocheng Yan, Shuai Liu, Xianfu Zhang
papers.journal: International Journal of Robust and Nonlinear Control
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This article addresses the fixed‐time resilient tracking control problem for state‐constrained unknown nonlinear systems under deception attacks. First, within the backstepping framework, a state‐dependent function is introduced at each design step to enforce asymmetric state constraints. This approach eliminates the feasibility conditions on virtual controllers required by barrier Lyapunov function (BLF)‐based methods. Second, an enhanced dynamic surface control (DSC) technique is proposed to circumvent the differentiation explosion inherent in backstepping while overcoming stability analysis challenges from state‐dependent function‐induced residual terms. By integrating these components, a fixed‐time resilient control strategy is developed that (1) guarantees the fixed‐time convergence of the output tracking error; (2) ensures strict adherence to prescribed state constraints. Numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

papers.title: Perceptions of Intra‐Operative EEG Brain Monitoring During Pediatric Anesthesia Among Children and Parents: An Exploratory Cross‐Sectional Survey
papers.authors: Kah Hau Luke Chua, Teddy Suratos Fabila, Neyziel Mardo, Choon Looi Bong
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring during pediatric anesthesia may improve perioperative safety by optimizing anesthetic titration and reducing adverse outcomes. However, little is known about patient and caregiver perceptions regarding this technology and its implementation into routine anesthesia care. AIMS: This study evaluates perceived importance, utility, and extent of reassurance provided by intra-operative EEG monitoring among pediatric patients and their parents. Secondary aims include identifying concerns surrounding general anesthesia (GA), concerns surrounding EEG monitoring, cost and willingness to pay, and sociodemographic and medical factors shaping these attitudes. METHODS: We conducted an exploratory cross-sectional survey at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Singapore between July 2022 and September 2025. Respondents were parents of children aged 1-18 years and children aged 12-18 scheduled for elective procedures under general anesthesia. A 16-item anonymized questionnaire assessed perceptions of intra-operative EEG monitoring, concerns about anesthesia, and attitudes regarding the cost of EEG monitoring. RESULTS: Of 400 respondents (100 children, 300 parents), 83.5% rated intra-operative brain monitoring as "very" or "quite" important and 93% reported feeling more reassured by its use. Children were most concerned about intraoperative awareness and failure to awaken, whereas parents were most concerned about anesthetic side effects and dosage. Parents with higher education and whose children had prior anesthetic exposure reported greater reassurance from EEG monitoring. Cost was the leading concern regarding EEG monitoring, particularly among parents from families residing in public housing. Despite this, most parents (75%) and children (59%) expressed willingness to pay for EEG monitoring. CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric patients and parents viewed intra-operative EEG monitoring as important and reassuring, and expressed willingness to support its implementation despite cost concerns. These findings suggest that families are unlikely to be a major barrier to EEG adoption and highlight the need for clinician- and system-level strategies to integrate EEG monitoring into family-centered pediatric anesthesia care.

papers.title: Writing Motivation and Self‐Efficacy in AI ‐Chatbot‐Supported EFL Writing: Exploratory Insights Across Proficiency Levels
papers.authors: Thi-Ngoc-Anh Duong, Hsiu‐Ling Chen
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Writing motivation and self‐efficacy are critical factors of success in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) contexts, yet they are frequently undermined by learner anxiety and limited teacher feedback. While artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots offer potential for adaptive writing support, limited research has examined these affective constructs in parallel across learner proficiency levels. Objectives This study investigated changes in intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy among high school EFL learners at higher‐ and lower‐proficiency levels following chatbot‐supported writing and examined whether these changes differed across proficiency levels. Methods Using an exploratory mixed‐methods design, the study involved 47 Vietnamese high school students divided into higher‐ and lower‐proficiency level groups. Over the 11‐week study, participants completed 8 weeks of AI‐supported writing activities using a chatbot designed in accordance with principles of Self‐Determination Theory, Self‐Regulated Learning Theory and Self‐Efficacy Theory. Changes in intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy were examined using pre‐ and post‐questionnaires and semi‐structured interviews. Results and Conclusions The quantitative findings revealed that intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy increased over time in both proficiency groups, with no significant differences in the magnitude of change between higher‐ and lower‐proficiency learners. This suggests that the affective changes observed during AI‐supported writing were not confined to one proficiency group. The qualitative findings indicated that learners linked their positive experiences to reduced anxiety, clearer guidance, and supportive interaction, although the types of support they valued differed by proficiency level. Overall, the findings suggest that when positioned as a supportive writing partner rather than an answer generator, AI chatbot feedback may be associated with positive motivational and self‐efficacy development in mixed‐ability EFL writing classrooms.

papers.title: The rise of AI accommodations
papers.authors: Eric Lyerly
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has already forced colleges and universities to rewrite their academic integrity policies. Now it's forcing a harder, equally technical conversation in disability services. Students with documented disabilities are beginning to request generative AI tools as part of their accommodation plans. Many existing accommodation policies do not address these technologies. Campus administrators must address these novel questions now to meet legal obligations under disability law while maintaining their institution's academic standards.

papers.title: Writing by proxy: Authentic authorship in the era of AI‐powered communication of scientific knowledge
papers.authors: Brahim Chaqour
papers.journal: Journal of Cell Communication and Signaling
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping biomedical research as both a key analytical tool and an efficient copyeditor. Large language models and related algorithms can help investigators sift through the ever-expanding bodies of scientific literature, connect fragmented biological and clinical datasets, and uncover/recognize meaningful patterns buried within complex multidimensional data. Beyond the bench, these tools can improve and refine manuscript architecture and streamline the flow of information by honing the articulation of simple or complex scientific ideas and sharpening the clarity and cadence of scientific information, which ultimately strengthens the writing in publications and grant proposals alike. For researchers working across languages or at early career stages, these tools allow them to express ideas with greater clarity and fluency, ultimately ensuring that intellectual contributions are assessed on the basis of their conceptual merit and experimental validity. However, the growing persuasiveness of AI-generated writing raises an important concern as to whether persuasive language can create an impression of rigor that is not necessarily matched by rigorous science. AI tools can improve the clarity and presentation of scientific writing, but they cannot establish biological relevance, experimental validation and/or the nuanced judgment required to identify confounding variables, and draw meaningful conclusions. Similarly, an eloquently written grant proposal cannot substitute for an innovative idea, testable hypothesis, feasible experimental approach, and meaningful anticipated contribution. It is therefore essential to view AI tools as instruments of improvement not replacement. They can enhance clarity, efficiency, and readability but they should not replace investigators' intellectual ownership, accountability, and critical interpretation. Disclosure of AI use, together with continued investigators' responsibility for originality, accuracy, citations, data integrity, and interpretation, is essential to maintain trust in scientific discoveries. Similarly, editors, peer reviewers, authors, and funding panels bear a renewed obligation to distinguish writing quality from scientific quality and continue to evaluate approach, innovation, experimental rigor, reproducibility, investigator skills, and scientific and/or clinical significance. Used judiciously and with discernment, AI can free researchers to invest more deeply in the irreplaceable human dimensions of scientific discovery.

papers.title: An interconnected and unpredictable risk landscape means boards must act on leadership risk now
papers.authors: Sid Kosaraju
papers.abstract: In today's volatile global landscape, boards are being asked to oversee a broader and more interconnected risk environment than ever before. Cyber incidents, geopolitical shocks, AI‐enabled deception, health events and threats directed at senior leaders can all disrupt continuity, decision‐making and enterprise value. Yet one governance blind spot remains underexamined: whether public companies have adequately assessed and addressed the risks facing the people leading the business.

papers.title: Bio‐Inspired Tactile Reflex Architecture for Ultra‐Fast and Context‐Aware Human‐Robot Interaction
papers.authors: Jinhyeok Oh, Hun Jang, 최주성, Heejun Moon, Joonbum Bae
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Robots operating in close proximity to humans must be capable of perceiving contact, reacting within milliseconds, and subsequently restoring stable task execution. However, existing proprioceptive or vision‐based methods suffer from limited bandwidth, high latency, and poor reliability during dynamic interactions. Here, we propose a human‐inspired tactile perception and reflex control framework that integrates a high‐performance single‐electrode triboelectric nanogenerator (STENG) tactile array, distributed microcontroller‐based reflex processing, and impact‐aware high‐level motion generation. The STENG array, fabricated using optimized silicone and liquid‐metal printing, provides high‐bandwidth, high‐resolution mechanical sensing and robust surface conformability. A lightweight neural classifier embedded directly in the reflex layer enables real‐time discrimination between human and object contact from raw triboelectric waveforms. The distributed control architecture achieves a total reflex latency of 2.2 ms, outperforming the centralized controller by more than a factor of five. Experimental demonstrations show that the system can generate an immediate stop followed by high‐level retraction under human contact, while selectively modulating motion during object contact, providing context‐aware reflex actions. The proposed architecture bridges the gap between ultra‐fast tactile sensing and high‐level motion intelligence, enabling fast, safe, and human‐friendly physical interaction for future human‐robot interaction (HRI) applications.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and venture capital: revisiting sourcing, selection, and nuturing activities
papers.authors: G Dushnitsky
papers.journal: London Business School Research Online (London Business School)
papers.abstract: Venture capital (VC) is an information-intensive form of entrepreneurial finance conducted under extreme uncertainty. Investors must originate promising opportunities, select ventures with sparse and strategically disclosed information, and monitor and support firms after investment. Prior research documents both formal mechanisms (e.g., staged financing, syndication) and informal mechanisms built on referrals, reputation, and constant interaction. Geographic and social proximity enable these mechanisms by lowering the cost of obtaining contextual information and coordinating action. We develop a mechanism-based account of how data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) reconfigure this established model. Our framework yields propositions on geographic dispersion in sourcing, portfolio selection, and the distinct effects of AI on monitoring versus value-added support. It also identifies boundary conditions associated with institutional setting and heterogeneous AI adoption.

papers.title: Rethinking Economic Rationality in AI-Assisted Decision-Making
papers.authors: Ekaterina Svetlova
papers.journal: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to support economic and financial decision-making, including forecasting, valuation, credit assessment and investment. This development raises a fundamental question for economics: how does the use of AI tools change the concept of economic rationality? Although research in artificial intelligence, philosophy and organisation studies has examined rationality in human-AI interaction, this debate has not yet been fully integrated into economic theory. Economic theory has generally treated the tools of calculation implicitly, assuming that agents have already used them and therefore hold the information and beliefs needed to form expectations and evaluate alternatives. AI makes the importance of these tools explicit. The paper therefore asks how AI changes economic agency and how formal, calculation-based rationality interacts with substantive, judgment-based rationality. It introduces the AI-human system as a unit of inquiry and uses the philosophical concept of epoché to examine the interplay of calculation and judgment within such a system. Epoché names the suspension of judgment through which the authority of an established model or rule can be examined without abandoning calculation. It creates space to reflect on whether the decision frame remains adequate. Economic rationality, understood in this way, involves not only applying a model consistently or making consistent choices, but also asking whether the model is appropriate, what it leaves out, and why. The argument is illustrated through AI-assisted financial valuation.

papers.title: Memorias de la I Jornada Nacional de Medicina Intensiva y Emergencias IntensivMat 2026
papers.authors: Richard Marcial Gálvez-Vila, Mara Verónica  Álvarez-Valdés, Yoelis Cintra-Leyva
papers.abstract: The First National Conference on Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine IntensivMat 2026, convened by the Student Scientific Society of Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine, Matanzas Chapter, was held in virtual modality from July 20 to August 15, 2026. It brought together 313 participants from across the country, including professionals, doctors, and students, with the purpose of strengthening scientific training in high-complexity settings. The organization was led by the student Richard Marcial Gálvez Vila and Dr. Mara Verónica Alvarez Valdés, together with members of SOCUMIE, student teaching assistants, and vertical interns, which consolidated a space for mentorship and generational relay.
