The central objective was to promote the exchange of knowledge through electronic posters and scientific courses. The opening included the lecture "Applications of AI in Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine: Current Challenges." The topics covered septic critically ill patients, mechanical ventilation, neurocare, point-of-care ultrasound, polytrauma, massive hemorrhage, acute renal failure, humanization, bioethics, artificial intelligence, cardiological emergencies, clinical simulation, and patient safety, among others. A total of 85 posters, 12 cases, and 16 courses were presented, exceeding expectations. Virtuality broadened the reach and inclusion of distant territories. The motto "Learn today, save tomorrow" synthesized the ethical commitment to life and professional excellence. The authors conclude that IntensivMat 2026 constituted a seedbed of vocations and a bridge between the present and future of Cuban intensive care medicine, with a sustainable and replicable model of student participation, rigor, and humanism.

papers.title: Pengaruh Kecerdasan Artifisial Terhadap Otoritas Pengetahuan Dalam Kurikulum Sekolah: Tinjauan Literatur
papers.authors: Darul Ihsan, Benny Prasetiya
papers.abstract: The presence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in learning does not merely change how students obtain information; it also shifts who is trusted as a legitimate source of knowledge in schools. This article critically reviews the literature on the influence of AI on epistemic authority in the school curriculum, particularly the changing positions of teachers, textbooks, and the official curriculum. Using a qualitative critical literature review of reputable journal articles, academic books, and policy documents published in 2026, analysed thematically, the review identifies four main findings: (1) AI becomes an additional source of knowledge that erodes the monopoly of teachers and official texts; (2) the authority of AI is problematic because of opacity, data bias, and the potential for epistemic injustice; (3) the apparent dispersal of authority is not a genuine decentralisation, since control over knowledge tends to concentrate in platform providers; and (4) the teacher's role shifts from transmitter of knowledge to epistemic guarantor who curates, verifies, and contextualises AI outputs. The article proposes a conceptual framework of curated epistemic authority as a direction for curriculum development that preserves pedagogical sovereignty in the AI era.

papers.title: AI Swarm Intelligence Must Be Studied as a Sociotechnical Phenomenon
papers.authors: Daniel Thilo Schroeder, Luiz Felipe Santos Vecchietti, Wenchao Dong, Signe Riemer–Sørensen, Jonas R. Kunst, Łukasz Olejnik, Meeyoung Cha
papers.abstract: The emergence of coordinated autonomous AI agents is fundamentally altering human belief systems and public discourse at scales and speeds that outpace existing characterization methods. This paper argues that AI swarm intelligence, the coordinated influence of autonomous agents on human populations, represents a phase shift that cannot be understood by simply scaling single-agent analysis. Instead, it must be analyzed as a sociotechnical system where societal impact emerges from the tight coupling of individual agent capabilities, multi-agent coordination, and population dynamics. Because the shift from single- to multi-agent systems corresponds to a psychological transition between single- and multiple-source influence, we propose a unified framework and evaluate these systems across operational, individual, and population-level dynamics. We identify concrete research agendas and call on the community to build the evaluation methods, countermeasures, and governance approaches needed to address the long-term societal impact of these coordinated autonomous AI populations. AI assistance disclosure: Claude (Anthropic) was used solely to polish the language of the manuscript. No other AI assistance was used.

papers.title: Émergence A/R/T: revisiter une exposition collaborative
papers.authors: Geneviève Cloutier, Kathy Mantas, Malvika Agarwal, Robert Durocher, Renee Jackson, Michele Kleinschuck, Don Kwan, Sandra Poczobut, Jessica Sokolowski, Jennifer Wicks, Cara Tierney
papers.journal: The Canadian Review of Art Education / Revue canadienne d’éducation artistique
papers.abstract: This visual essay revisits A/R/T Emergence, a collaborative exhibition at the Ottawa Art Gallery during the 2022 joint CSEA/SCÉA and OAEA conference. Co-curated as a relational, accessible, non-hierarchical space, it brought together artists, researchers, teachers, students and community members to explore emergence by engaging with decolonization, accessibility, activism, environmentalism, memory, and identity. Grounded in posthumanist and anti-colonial perspectives, it enacted radical inclusion by resisting fixed, linear knowledge in favour of fluid, relational meaning-making, inviting audiences into co-creation. A/R/T Emergence calls for sustaining arts-based exhibitions that foster inclusive and interconnected pedagogies, in conference contexts and beyond.

papers.title: Personalized monitoring of student housing and dining
papers.authors: Χρυσοβαλάντης Πιερή
papers.abstract: Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία πραγματεύεται τον σχεδιασμό και την υλοποίηση μιας ολοκληρωμένης διαδικτυακής εφαρμογής για την εξατομικευμένη παρακολούθηση και διαχείριση της φοιτητικής στέγασης και σίτισης. Αφετηρία αποτελεί η διαπίστωση ότι, παρά τη θεσμική κατοχύρωση των παροχών αυτών στα ελληνικά ΑΕΙ και τις επιμέρους πρωτοβουλίες ψηφιοποίησης των ιδρυμάτων, οι σχετικές διαδικασίες παραμένουν κατακερματισμένες σε ανεξάρτητα συστήματα, χωρίς ενιαία εμπειρία χρήστη και χωρίς δυνατότητες εξατομίκευσης. Στο πλαίσιο της εργασίας μελετώνται οι υφιστάμενες λύσεις στην Ελλάδα και διεθνώς, αναλύονται οι ανάγκες των εμπλεκόμενων μερών και προσδιορίζονται οι προδιαγραφές ενός ενιαίου συστήματος. Η εφαρμογή υλοποιήθηκε με αρχιτεκτονική τριών επιπέδων: React.js και Vite στο επίπεδο παρουσίασης, ως εφαρμογή μονής σελίδας (SPA), REST API με Laravel 12 στο επίπεδο επιχειρησιακής λογικής και MySQL στο επίπεδο δεδομένων. Χρησιμοποιούνται Laravel Sanctum, προστασία CSRF και έλεγχος πρόσβασης βάσει ρόλων. Στη στέγαση υποστηρίζονται ηλεκτρονική αίτηση, διαχειριστική έγκριση/απόρριψη και απόδοση δωματίου, επαλήθευση πρόσβασης δύο βημάτων με QR και PIN (με προσομοιωμένη συσκευή θύρας) και καταγραφή βλαβών. Στη σίτιση υποστηρίζονται διατροφικό προφίλ, κοινό εβδομαδιαίο μενού με διατροφικές ετικέτες, ψηφιακά εισιτήρια και κάρτες QR, check-ins, ιστορική ανάλυση αιχμής και αξιολόγηση πιάτων. Η εφαρμογή είναι δίγλωσση (ελληνικά/αγγλικά) και προσαρμόζεται σε κινητές συσκευές. Το σύστημα περιλαμβάνει επίσης ηλεκτρονική αίτηση δωρεάν σίτισης με δικαιολογητικά, έλεγχο από τον διαχειριστή και έκδοση ψηφιακής ετήσιας κάρτας QR. Οι ανακοινώσεις και οι αναφορές προς τη διοίκηση αποτελούν κοινό κανάλι επικοινωνίας για τη στέγαση και τη σίτιση. Η εφαρμογή αξιολογήθηκε λειτουργικά, με σενάρια επαλήθευσης που προκύπτουν από τις απαιτήσεις. Επειδή δεν έγινε πιλοτική μελέτη με χρήστες, οφέλη όπως η μείωση της αναμονής, του κόστους ή της σπατάλης τροφίμων παρουσιάζονται ως αναμενόμενα. Ως μελλοντικές επεκτάσεις εξετάζονται η παρακολούθηση της διαθεσιμότητας δωματίων σε πραγματικό χρόνο, αισθητήρες, πρόβλεψη ζήτησης, εγγενής εφαρμογή κινητών, NFC και chatbot.

papers.title: Pre-Registration: Cross-Domain Trust Transfer and Undetected AI Failure
papers.authors: Randall W Engle, Richard Pak, Anne Collins McLaughlin, Ericka M. Rovira
papers.abstract: This study examines whether interacting with an AI that fails without the user's knowledge produces worse reliance calibration in a subsequent knowledge domain than either (a) experiencing the same failures with feedback or (b) never encountering the failures at all. Participants complete an AI-assisted decision-making task across two knowledge domains (statistical reasoning and legal knowledge), with a simulated AI assistant whose accuracy and feedback are experimentally controlled.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF WRITING SKILLS
papers.authors: Olimova Gulchehra Mannon qizi
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence plays an increasingly significant role in developing writing skills in modern education. This article examines the potential of AI-powered tools to improve grammatical accuracy, vocabulary, coherence, and academic writing proficiency. The study analyzes existing research on automated writing evaluation, personalized feedback, and generative AI applications. The findings indicate that artificial intelligence can support independent learning, facilitate text revision, and enhance students’ writing performance. However, excessive reliance on AI may negatively affect creativity and critical thinking. The article emphasizes the importance of integrating AI technologies with teacher guidance, ethical considerations, and independent writing practice to ensure effective learning outcomes

papers.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence Applications in Enhancing Effective Teaching Skills among Female Teachers of the First Three Primary Grades from the Perspective of Educational Supervisors
papers.authors: ريم جرار
papers.abstract: هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى التعرّف على دور توظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تعزيز مهارات التدريس الفعّال لدى معلمات الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى، من وجهة نظر المشرفين التربويين، والكشف عن وجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية في هذا الدور تُعزى لمتغيرات المؤهل العلمي، وسنوات الخبرة، وعدد الدورات التدريبية. اعتمدت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي المسحي، وقامت الباحثة بتطوير استبانة مكوّنة من (30) فقرة موزّعة على ثلاثة مجالات، طُبِّقت على عيّنة من المشرفين التربويين العاملين في قسم الإشراف التربوي في لواء الرصيفة، تم اختيارها بالطريقة المسح الشامل لطبيعة مجتمع الدراسة، وبلغ عدد أفرادها (33) مشرفًا ومشرفة. وأظهرت نتائج الدراسة أن دور توظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تعزيز مهارات التدريس الفعّال لدى معلمات الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى، من وجهة نظر المشرفين التربويين، جاء بدرجة مرتفعة. كما بيّنت النتائج وجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية عند مستوى الدلالة (α ≤ 0.05) تُعزى لمتغير المؤهل العلمي، ولصالح المشرفين الحاصلين على الدراسات العليا، وكذلك لمتغير عدد الدورات التدريبية، ولصالح من خضعوا لدورتين تدريبيتين في مجال الذكاء الاصطناعي، في حين لم تظهر فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية تُعزى لمتغير سنوات الخبرة. وأوصت الدراسة بضرورة الاستمرار في تقديم دورات تدريبية متخصصة ومتنوعة للمشرفين التربويين في مجال توظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي، لما لذلك من أثر إيجابي في تعزيز مهارات التدريس الفعّال لدى معلمات الصفوف الثلاثة الأولى، وتحسين جودة العملية التعليمية.

papers.title: English for entrepreneurial purposes: A mini-review of an emerging interdisciplinary field
papers.authors: AMORN CHERNGROONGROJ, Pattarawat Jeerapattanatorn
papers.abstract: Entrepreneurial activity is accomplished not only through ideas, resources, and decisions, but also through language. Entrepreneurs use communication to make opportunities intelligible, establish legitimacy, negotiate uncertainty, mobilize support, and invite others into a future that does not yet exist. Yet the literatures on English for Specific Purposes, Business English, entrepreneurial communication, and entrepreneurship education remain only partially connected. This conceptually driven mini-review proposes English for Entrepreneurial Purposes (EEP) as an emerging interdisciplinary domain concerned with learning and using English as a resource for entrepreneurial action and value creation. It addresses a recurrent pedagogical problem: learners may possess adequate English proficiency and deliver grammatically competent pitches while remaining unable to communicate with an entrepreneurial orientation or move an audience toward understanding, trust, commitment, or action. The review names this disjunction the language-to-action gap and argues that English proficiency alone does not ensure effective entrepreneurial communication. To explain what must bridge the gap, the article develops Entrepreneurial Communicative Competence (ECC), comprising linguistic, discourse and genre, interactional, persuasive, strategic-adaptive, intercultural-ethical, and digital-multimodal resources organized by a value-creation orientation. It further proposes entrepreneurial communicative resonance as the integration of cognitive clarity, affective meaning, and action relevance. A framework is presented in which English-language resources and entrepreneurial mindset jointly enable communicative actions—such as articulating opportunities, pitching, persuading, negotiating, networking, and storytelling—that shape stakeholder responses and contribute to economic, social, cultural, or sustainable value. Pedagogically, EEP requires authentic problems, real or realistic audiences, iterative stakeholder feedback, reflection, and dual assessment of both communication quality and entrepreneurial action. The review concludes with a research agenda for construct validation, needs analysis, assessment, intercultural and multilingual practice, and artificial-intelligence-mediated entrepreneurial communication.

papers.title: EEG in Parkinson’s Disease: Mechanisms, Biomarkers and Translational Opportunities
papers.authors: Marc Vérin, Sahar Allouch, Mahmoud Hassan, Sümeyye Özdemir, Manon Auffret
papers.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by nigrostriatal dopaminergic degeneration and basal ganglia dysfunction, yet these pathophysiological abnormalities alone do not fully explain its heterogeneous motor and non-motor manifestations. Over recent decades, electroencephalography (EEG) has evolved from a primarily descriptive technique into a quantitative approach for investigating cortical electrophysiological dynamics associated with PD. Accumulating electrophysiological evidence implicates altered oscillatory synchronization and interactions across cortical and subcortical circuits in PD-related dysfunction, suggesting disturbances in the temporal coordination of neural activity. Emerging approaches, including large-scale datasets, multimodal integration, individualized modeling and wearable EEG technologies, offer opportunities for physiological phenotyping and real-world monitoring. However, methodological heterogeneity, limited reproducibility, insufficient external validation and uncertainty regarding clinical utility continue to constrain translation. This Review critically synthesizes EEG-derived measures spanning spectral activity, oscillatory coupling, functional connectivity and dynamic brain states, examining their relationships with motor, cognitive and neuropsychiatric manifestations of PD. By distinguishing mechanistic interpretations, clinical associations and current levels of biomarker validation, it identifies opportunities and requirements for translating EEG-derived measures into reliable tools for individualized assessment and clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Digital Resilience: AI and Cultural Democracy at the National Museum of Korea
papers.authors: Heejung Ryoh
papers.journal: Central European Library and Information Science Review Közép-európai Könyvtár- és Információtudományi Szemle
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic served as a brutal stress test for museum resilience. While many institutions relied on a 'substitutive model' of mere digital replacement, the National Museum of Korea (NMK) achieved anomalous growth through a strategic pivot. This study employs an explanatory single-case study design to investigate the mechanisms behind this success. Applying pattern matching logic, the research validates the efficacy of a 'Transformative Model' grounded in Cultural Democracy. Findings reveal that the NMK's integration of AI-driven personalization, immersive Extended Reality (XR) experiences, and radical inclusivity reconfigured the visitor relationship from passive consumption to active co-creation. Crucially, empirical data confirms a positive correlation where high-level digital engagement functioned as a catalytic gateway that drove, rather than cannibalized, physical attendance. This case illustrates how sustainable resilience can be achieved when technology is strategically deployed to democratize heritage access and empower the visitor as an active participant.

papers.title: Classification of mental workload
papers.authors: Mathias Vukelić, Nektaria Tagalidou, Michael Bui
papers.abstract: In this project we want to classify mental workload to be able to assess situational awareness in interaction with an ai system. The first phase will be a classification study to be able to distinguish between high, medium and low workload. We will use ECG, EDA, EMG, PPG and eye-tracking to collect data. Also, we will use three different EEG devices to see if there are differences in the signal quality of the devices (classic 64-channel EEG, X.on and EEG-headphone). There will be a cooking simulator game with three different difficulty levels according to the workload levels. The levels will be adapted to the skills of the participants before the testing period. While playing the game an auditory oddball with three sounds (frequent, infrequent and novel) will be applied. Participants do not have to track the sounds, they just have to passively listen to it. The second phase will include a neuroadaptive system of the cooking simulator game. TWhile playing, the currrent workload will be displayed and the system will adapt to the needs of the user (higher or lower difficulty) in real-time. We will use the most promising devices from phase 1 to measure workload in phase 2.

papers.title: PERCEIVED COGNITIVE SKILLS AND THEIR RELATIONSHIP TO THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN RESEARCH AND SCHOLARLY ACTIVITY AMONG TEACHER-RESEARCHERS IN THE SALAH AL-DIN DIRECTORATE OF EDUCATION
papers.authors: Ahmed Mahmood Tuama
papers.abstract: The study was aimed at determining the status and level of use and development of modern digital tools in agricultural extension in the Nineveh Governorate, such as agricultural extension content, digital interaction and participation, digital extension, modern communication technologies, smartphones and agricultural applications, multimedia, and agricultural videos. It also explored the link between current use and development of modern tools and selected variables at personal and professional level. It was administered using two questionnaires. The first section gathered personal and professional information, and the second section had 60 items in six sections, each containing 10 items. The questionnaire had a Cronbach alpha reliability coefficient of 0.95 and showed face validity. The study was carried out on 256 extension workers in the Nineveh Agriculture Directorate and its agricultural divisions (32). A random sample of 200 extension workers (about 78% of the population) was drawn. Data were analysed in SPSS. The findings showed moderate general level of development and modern tools used in agricultural extension work, leaning towards high. The use of modern communication tools was high, while the use of smartphones and agricultural applications was moderate, tending toward high. Digital platforms and the use of multimedia was moderate and tending to low, while digital interaction and participation was high. Digital extension content development was moderate, leaning to high. There was no significant relationship with education level, specialization, years of service or participation in training courses relating to digital technologies. Age and years of service in agricultural extension were found to be significantly correlated at 0.05 level and Internet use frequency at 0.01 level, while owning a smart phone and the most frequently used digital tool were significantly correlated at 0.05 level. The study suggests aligning digital tools and resources to farmers' needs and capacities, and building partnerships between the Nineveh Agriculture Directorate, universities, and research centers to create relevant digital platforms and tools. Extension workers' perspectives regarding barriers to the utilization of modern digital technologies in agricultural extension should be explored for further research.

papers.title: The Degree of Chemistry Teachers' Practice of Artificial Intelligence Applications and its Relationship to their Attitudes toward Teaching
papers.authors: تهاني العبوس
papers.abstract: The study aims to investigate the degree to of chemistry teachers' practice of artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Also, it identifies whether there were statistically significant differences in the degree of chemistry teachers' practice of AI applications and their relationship to their attitudes toward teaching. A descriptive correlational approach was used as it aligns with the nature and objectives of the study. Two tools were employed to answer the study questions: The first was a questionnaire of 20 items divided into three domains (planning, implementation, and evaluation) to determine the degree of chemistry teachers' practice of AI applications. The second tool was a questionnaire designed to measure chemistry teachers' attitudes toward teaching, consisting of 16 indicators. The study population included all chemistry teachers in public schools under the Education Directorate of Wadi Al-Seer District, totaling 49 teachers. The study sample consisted of 34 male and female teachers selected randomly. The study results show that the degree of chemistry teachers' practice of AI applications was low, with a mean score of 1.65, and their attitudes toward teaching were moderate, with a mean score of 2.86. Additionally, the results reveal a statistically significant positive correlation between the degree of chemistry teachers' practice of AI applications and their attitudes toward teaching. In light of the study's results, the researcher recommends conducting specialized training courses on AI applications and their integration into chemistry teaching for chemistry teachers.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence dalam Pembelajaran PAI :Urgensi Guru Sebagai Verifikator Pemahaman Keagamaan
papers.authors: Dita Dzata Mirrota
papers.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the field of education has brought about significant changes in the learning process, including in Islamic Religious Education (IRE). Generative AI enables students to access religious information quickly and easily; however, it also poses challenges regarding the validity and accuracy of religious understanding. This study aims to analyze the use of AI in PAI learning and to examine the urgency of the teacher’s role as a verifier of religious understanding in the digital age. This study employs a qualitative approach using field research methods, including interviews, observations, and documentation, conducted at Primaganda High School in Jombang. The results of the study indicate that AI has been used as an alternative learning resource by students; however, it has the potential to lead to misunderstandings if not accompanied by teacher guidance. Islamic Education teachers play a strategic role as verifiers who ensure the accuracy of religious information by referring to authoritative Islamic sources such as the Qur’an, hadith, and the opinions of Islamic scholars. In addition, teachers also play a role in guiding religious digital literacy and instilling a spirit of tabayyun in filtering information. Thus, AI is positioned as a learning aid, while teachers remain the primary actors in maintaining the validity of students’ religious understanding. This study emphasizes that the integration of AI into Islamic Education must remain grounded in Islamic values and the strengthening of teachers’ pedagogical roles.

papers.title: THE INDIVIDUAL, SOCIETY, AND THE STATE IN AN INFORMATION SOCIETY
papers.authors: Abdullayeva Maryambibi Djumaniyazovna
papers.journal: EduVision: Journal of Innovations in Pedagogy and Educational Advancements
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the transformation of social relations among the individual, society, and the state, as well as emerging social paradigms, within the context of the formation of an information society. It highlights how the development of digital technologies, artificial intelligence, big data, e-government, digital education, and social networks is deeply permeating almost every aspect of human life. While the information society creates new opportunities for individuals regarding learning, communication, creativity, and social engagement, it also gives rise to challenges such as information security issues, digital inequality, personal data protection, information manipulation, and digital dependency. The study examines the individual's new status within the information environment, changes in the communicative structure of society, and the digital transformation of public administration as interconnected processes. It also highlights the impact of digital transformation on human interests, social justice, and state-society relations. The article substantiates digital literacy, information culture, openness, responsibility, and the safeguarding of human rights as crucial factors for the sustainable development of the information society.

papers.title: Securing Enterprise AI Supply Chains: A Framework for Model Provenance, Third-Party Risk, and Compromised AI Components
papers.authors: Favour Amarachi Ezeugwa
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports
papers.abstract: Enterprises assemble AI systems from externally sourced models, datasets, libraries, agents and serving components whose origin and integrity they cannot directly observe. This study asks how provenance assurance, third-party dependency exposure and supply-chain governance relate to the disclosed-vulnerability record of such components, and argues that this record measures security observability as much as security risk. Drawing on resource dependence, information asymmetry and signalling theory, we assemble a cross-sectional secondary dataset of 1,321 widely used open-source AI/ML components (GitHub, deps.dev, OpenSSF Scorecard, OSV, PyPI statistics, CISA KEV) and the 1,000 most-downloaded Hugging Face models, and estimate negative binomial, logistic, hurdle and zero-inflated models with robust standard errors and influence and selection diagnostics. Disclosed advisories are rare but concentrated: 8.9% of components carry one yet attract 39.4% of monthly downloads, and advisory publication rose from 54 in 2023 to 486 in the first nine months of 2026. Advisory counts rise with ecosystem reach (incidence rate ratio 2.49 per log unit of stars), release activity and, in the Scorecard subsample, detection and disclosure practices (IRR 1.48 per index point), whereas hardening and provenance controls show no negative association. Disclosure therefore tracks scrutiny and transparency rather than the absence of defects, motivating a six-pillar framework in which continuous observability, not silence, is the basis for trusting AI components. We recommend that enterprises assess AI suppliers on verifiable provenance, safe serialisation and disclosure capacity rather than on advisory counts and embed AI bills of materials and exploitation-aware monitoring in continuous engineering controls, and that standards bodies distinguish disclosure capacity from vulnerability prevalence in AI risk frameworks.

papers.title: Research on AI-Assisted Mathematics Teaching in Primary and Secondary Schools (2022-2026)
papers.authors: Chenyang Dong, Zezhong Yang
papers.journal: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support mathematics teaching, yet research examining its instructional effects and implementation conditions in primary and secondary schools remains fragmented. This study reviewed published research on AI-assisted mathematics teaching between 2022 and 2026. Relevant records were retrieved from the Web of Science database using topic searches for AI and mathematics education. Of 262 initially identified records, 44 studies met the stated inclusion criteria and were included in a thematic synthesis. Three principal research areas emerged: instructional effects, factors influencing effectiveness, and strategies for improvement. The reviewed studies generally reported favourable outcomes for students’ mathematics achievement, conceptual understanding, interest, motivation and classroom engagement, although some interventions produced limited or inconsistent benefits. AI tools also supported teachers’ lesson planning, resource preparation, assessment, learning diagnosis and instructional decision-making. Reported outcomes depended on teacher-related factors, including AI literacy, attitudes and pedagogical competencies; student-related factors, including self-regulation, digital literacy and interaction patterns; technological factors, particularly accuracy, usability and personalisation; and contextual factors, including infrastructure, family support and educational resources. Suggested improvements included professional development, teacher-led implementation, clearer ethical and data-governance arrangements, and the development of more reliable mathematics-specific tools. The findings indicate that AI can provide useful instructional support, but its effectiveness depends on appropriate educational integration and local conditions. Longitudinal classroom research is needed to clarify sustained outcomes and the interaction of these factors.

papers.title: Negotiated resource reconfiguration and co-restoration in public healthcare service recovery: An SDL-grounded mid-range theory
papers.authors: Zahid Iqbal, Anees Wajid
papers.journal: Research Journal of Human and Social Aspects
papers.abstract: Service recovery literature is inherently biased toward the firm-transaction and focuses on recovery as a firm-managed response to a customer complaint and reimbursement (Tax et al., 1998; Smith et al., 1999). In a public health care setting, however, institutional rigidities and norms, resource constraints, and administrative inertia often prevent formal recovery from taking place (Osborne et al., 2013; Skålén et al., 2015). This empirical study develops a new mid-range theory, the Negotiated Reconfiguration Theory of Public Healthcare Service Recovery, based on service-dominant logic (SDL) and constructivist grounded theory (CGT) (Charmaz, 2014). The paper draws on 28 in-depth, theoretically sampled interviews with key informants in primary and secondary public health providers in District Mansehra, Pakistan, to develop an 8-stage Resource Realignment Process model and present eight theoretical propositions (P1–P8). The results show that public healthcare recovery is not so much an apology or a refund on the part of the firm, but rather a highly negotiated, multi-actor practice of reconfiguring resources in the process of recovery, in which informal actors (family caregivers) also function as key recovery workers to re-create and restore value co-creation (Batalden et al., 2016; McColl-Kennedy et al., 2012). The article offers an innovative concept and framework for public health approaches to state, moving from complaint-driven to the integration and resilience of an ecosystem of resources and a multi-actor approach in policy management.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education Management: Global Applications and Emerging Practices in Vietnam
papers.authors: Huy Nguyen Duc
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming higher education not only through teaching, learning, and scientific research but also through the management and governance of higher education institutions. Universities are beginning to employ AI in admissions, student administration, academic advising, early-warning systems, human-resource management, financial administration, scheduling, quality assurance, institutional planning, communication, and decision support. This development represents a transition from predominantly rule-based and reactive administration toward increasingly data-driven, predictive, and adaptive forms of institutional management. However, the adoption of AI also creates significant challenges concerning data quality, privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, accountability, institutional autonomy, professional responsibility, and the appropriate boundaries between automated recommendations and human decisions. This article examines the current applications of AI in higher education management internationally and analyses the emerging situation in Vietnam. Drawing on recent international policy literature, empirical research, UNESCO assessments, OECD analysis, and Vietnamese regulatory and research sources, the article argues that AI should not be understood merely as an instrument for administrative automation. Rather, it is becoming an institutional capability that can reshape how universities collect and interpret information, allocate resources, provide services, identify risks, and make strategic decisions. In Vietnam, the policy environment is moving rapidly toward more systematic integration of digital technologies and AI into higher education management. The newly effective Circular No. 49/2026/TT-BGDĐT explicitly regulates the application of digital technologies and AI in higher education, including governance, management, student services, data integration, analysis, forecasting, and decision-making. Nevertheless, institutional readiness remains uneven, and the quality of management information systems and institutional data remains a critical determinant of successful AI adoption. The article proposes a human-centred model of AI-enabled university management based on strategic alignment, data quality, institutional readiness, risk-based deployment, transparency, human oversight, accountability, and continuous evaluation. The article concludes that the future of AI in higher education management should not be defined by the replacement of administrators with algorithms but by the development of institutional intelligence in which AI expands human analytical capacity while universities retain responsibility for educational, ethical, and organizational judgment.

papers.title: Cultural Industries and Their Development in Vietnam: Economic Transformation, Cultural Value, and Creative Potential
papers.authors: Nhung Tran Thi Thu, Huong Nguyen Thi Lan
papers.abstract: Cultural industries have emerged as an increasingly important component of contemporary economic development, by bringing together cultural expression, creativity, technology, intellectual property, and market mechanisms. Unlike traditional industries, cultural industries generate economic value not only through material production but also through symbolic meanings, cultural identities, knowledge, and creative content. The expansion of digital technologies, streaming platforms, social media, artificial intelligence, and global cultural markets has further transformed the production, distribution, and consumption of cultural products. These developments have created additional opportunities for developing countries to participate in global value chains while simultaneously creating challenges related to cultural identity, intellectual property protection, market concentration, inequality, and the commercialization of culture. Vietnam represents an important case in this transformation because the country possesses considerable cultural diversity, traditional craft heritage, performing arts, historical resources, and a rapidly expanding digital economy. Since the adoption of the National Strategy for the Development of Cultural Industries to 2020, with a Vision to 2030, Vietnam has increasingly recognized cultural industries as an economic sector capable of contributing to employment, economic growth, tourism, national branding, and international integration. This article examines the theoretical foundations of cultural industries, analyzes their economic and social significance, evaluates the development of cultural industries in Vietnam, and discusses the opportunities and challenges created by digitalization and globalization. The article argues that Vietnam should move beyond viewing culture primarily as a field of preservation or public expenditure and increasingly recognize culture as a productive resource while maintaining cultural diversity, public value, and social inclusion. The future development of Vietnamese cultural industries therefore requires an integrated ecosystem connecting creativity, education, technology, intellectual property protection, finance, entrepreneurship, cultural heritage, and international markets.

papers.title: Human-AI Collaboration and Organizational Adaptation: Insights from Knowledge Workers in Banten, Indonesia
papers.authors: Danish Akbar Firdausy Asbari
papers.journal: Indonesian Journal of Management and Economic Research.
papers.abstract: This qualitative descriptive study explores how Human-AI collaboration shapes organizational adaptation among knowledge workers in Banten, Indonesia. Using multi-case inquiry with 20 purposively selected participants comprising knowledge workers, middle managers, senior managers, and digital transformation leaders, this research employed semi-structured interviews, organizational document analysis, and observation protocols. Thematic analysis revealed four critical patterns: (1) AI integration reshapes collaborative workflows through augmentation rather than replacement; (2) knowledge work transformation emerges through new competency demands and skill reconfiguration; (3) organizational learning accelerates through human-AI knowledge co-creation; and (4) adaptive organizational practices evolve through dynamic capability reconfiguration. The study contributes theoretically by extending dynamic capability theory, organizational adaptation theory, and knowledge-based view through an emerging economy lens, demonstrating that Human-AI collaboration functions as a mechanism for organizational adaptation when complemented by deliberate knowledge management systems, adaptive leadership, and human-centric learning cultures. Practically, findings offer strategic guidance for organizational leaders, human resource managers, and policymakers navigating AI-driven transformation in knowledge-intensive sectors. This research uniquely addresses the gap between AI adoption studies and organizational adaptation processes, providing nuanced understanding of Human-AI collaboration in an emerging economy context where institutional support and digital literacy remain evolving. The novelty lies in positioning Human-AI collaboration as central to organizational adaptation rather than treating it as a peripheral technological implementation concern, with particular relevance to organizations in Southeast Asian emerging markets.

papers.title: PEDAGOGICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR DEVELOPING STUDENTS’ ACADEMIC WRITING COMPETENCE THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Khamdamova Mokhlaroyim
papers.abstract: This paper examines the pedagogical foundations for integrating artificial intelligence into the development of students’ academic writing competence. It adopts a conceptual approach informed by writing pedagogy, self-regulated learning, and human-centred principles of AI use in education. Academic writing competence is understood as the ability to construct coherent arguments, evaluate and integrate evidence, follow disciplinary conventions, and revise texts independently. The paper proposes an instructional framework combining explicit teaching, guided AI interaction, critical feedback evaluation, and reflective revision.

papers.title: Pedagogical conditions for developing students’ academic writing competence through artificial intelligence.
papers.authors: Khamdamova Mokhlaroyim
papers.abstract: This article examines the pedagogical conditions necessary for effectively developing students’ academic writing competence by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into higher education. As global academic standards increasingly demand high-level research writing, clarity, and adherence to international publication ethics, educators face the challenge of equipping students with advanced text-production skills. This study outlines a comprehensive framework of pedagogical, methodological, and technological conditions—such as prompt engineering literacy, critical feedback literacy, scaffolded AI-assisted drafting, and ethical integrity safeguards. By establishing these conditions, institutions can transform AI from a mere shortcut into a cognitive partner that fosters critical thinking, structural coherence, and linguistic precision in academic discourse.

papers.title: THEORETICAL AND METHODOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR DEVELOPING THE PROFESSIONAL-METHODOLOGICAL COMPETENCE OF PROSPECTIVE ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS THROUGH THE INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ADA
papers.authors: Jo'rayevna Qarshiyeva Sharifa
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of higher education necessitates the reconsideration of approaches to preparing prospective English language teachers. In this context, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and adaptive learning technologies represents a promising direction for developing professional-methodological competence, enabling future educators to design learner-centred instruction, differentiate educational content, analyse learning progress, and select appropriate pedagogical strategies. This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of competence development through the integration of AI-supported tools and adaptive learning environments. It synthesises competence-based, learner-centred, constructivist, and technology-enhanced learning approaches to establish a conceptual framework for teacher preparation. The proposed framework comprises five interrelated components: motivational and value-based, cognitive, technological, operational-methodological, and reflective-evaluative. Particular attention is given to the relationship between AI literacy, pedagogical decision-making, adaptive instructional design, and professional reflection. A phased methodological model is proposed, encompassing diagnostic assessment, personalised learning, AI-supported methodological practice, teaching simulation, and reflective evaluation. The article also addresses ethical considerations, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, academic integrity, and the importance of maintaining teacher autonomy. The findings provide a theoretical basis for designing university-level teacher education programmes that respond to the demands of digital transformation.

papers.title: INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES INTO MATHEMATICS TEACHING METHODOLOGY
papers.authors: Ruhiyya Jafarova
papers.abstract: In the modern era, the rapid development of digital technologies necessitates the application of new approaches to the organization of the educational process and teaching methods. From this perspective, artificial intelligence (AI) technologies possess broad capabilities in enriching the content of mathematics teaching, identifying individual learning needs of students, visualizing complex mathematical concepts, and explaining problem -solving methods through various approaches. This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of integrating AI technologies into mathematics education, identifies the main directions of using AI, and analyzes the mechanisms of its application in mathematics lessons. At the same time, the advantages and potential limitations of purposeful AI usage are demonstrated. As a result of the research, it has been determined that it is advisable to apply AI technologies not as a replacement for the teacher, but as a methodological tool that supports the teacher's pedagogical activity and serves to develop students' mathematical thinking.

papers.title: The Trust Paradox of AI-Generated Content Transparency: Impulse Buying from the Perspective of Generative Agents
papers.authors: Xi Cheng
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in digital e-commerce environments, the transparency labeling of AI-generated content has emerged as a crucial institutional variable in modern platform governance. Drawing upon the established information–trust–behavior theoretical logic, this study conducted a large-scale AI-agent simulation, comprising 900 distinct purchase decisions executed by large language model agents, to systematically test how disclosure labeling affects simulated consumer trust and simulated impulse buying intention. Furthermore, the research investigated whether trust acts as a mediating mechanism and whether consumer involvement moderates these relationships. Rigorous model-rationality validation confirmed that the agent decisions consistently conformed to their assigned behavioral personalities and rational economic logic. The empirical results demonstrated that disclosure labeling significantly suppressed both simulated trust and impulse buying intention. Additionally, simulated trust positively predicted impulse intention, revealing a negative indirect association within the disclosure–impulse behavioral link. Notably, consumer involvement moderated the trust–impulse path during the primary simulation phase, although this moderating effect was not replicated in the cross-model robustness check. Ultimately, these comprehensive findings reveal the critical boundary conditions of the institutional logic surrounding the exchange of transparency for trust. The study provides robust, simulation-based empirical evidence for the development of AI-content labeling policies and offers valuable insights for optimizing platform information governance strategies in the digital economy.

papers.title: Brain-Computer Interface for Disability Assistance: A Study on Factors Influencing Disabilities' Purchase Intention and Price Acceptance for Mind-Writing Pens
papers.authors: Mengya Li, Hu Bing
papers.abstract: With the practical application of brain-computer interface (BCI) technology, mind-writing pens have progressed from the conceptual stage into an iterative product development phase. Currently, leveraging the trends of population aging and advancements in medical rehabilitation, these products are expected to enter a golden period of growth within the next eight to ten years. Existing research primarily focuses on BCI risk management and lacks in-depth exploration of market demand and the factors influencing medical rehabilitation-related products. This gap provides a critical research focus for this study. Using individuals with disabilities as subjects, this study employs a sequential Probit model and KHB mediation analysis to examine factors affecting purchase intention and price acceptance for mind-writing pens. Results indicate that age has no significant impact on purchase intention or price acceptance, whereas income shows a significant positive effect. Battery life and head-mounted design significantly enhance purchase intention, while weight and recognition accuracy positively influence price acceptance. Cross-platform compatibility mediates the effects of income. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that demand among those under fifty is primarily driven by income, whereas users aged fifty-one and older prioritize battery life and recognition accuracy; low- to middle-income groups emphasize basic usability, whereas high-income groups value functional enhancement. Price acceptance decreases progressively as prices rise, peaking below one thousand yuan. This study provides empirical evidence for the development, pricing, and market promotion of BCI-based assistive products for individuals with disabilities.

papers.title: Predictive Talent Acquisition Using Ensemble Learning Models in Human Resource Management
papers.authors: Melanie Elisabeth Lourens, Leena Sharma, Mahua Majumdar Bose, B.Ranjitha
papers.journal: Applied Science Engineering and Management Bulletin [ASEMB]
papers.abstract: Predictive talent acquisition is one of the applications of machine learning which has become an area of importance within human resource management for carrying out data analysis of recruitment processes. The purpose of this research was to compare the effectiveness of several machine learning classifiers on the prediction of recruitment decision. For that, a dataset containing structured information about 1,500 candidates was used. Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extra Trees, and HistGradientBoosting were the five classifiers considered in the study. These classifiers were evaluated using a stratified train/test split of 80:20. Their performances were measured in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the ROC curve (ROC-AUC), area under the PR curve (PR-AUC), and Brier score. The best result was demonstrated by HistGradientBoosting classifier with accuracy 93.67%, F1-score 0.8914, ROC-AUC 0.9313, and PR-AUC 0.9173. The feature importance analysis yielded the recruitment strategy, skill score, and educational background as some important predictive factors, although it was necessary to consider the problem of target leakage in relation to the recruitment strategy. The outcomes prove that the prediction capability is good enough for the experimental dataset but at the same time emphasize the significance of validation, correct use of features, fairness analysis, and human supervision. Since the dataset in question is artificial, the outcomes cannot be regarded as an indication of effectiveness in the real-world recruitment process.

papers.title: Executive Sensemaking of Generative AI Adoption at Enterprise Scale: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Cross-Industry Executive Perspectives
papers.authors: Isidro T. Aroy Jr, Rabel B. Catayoc
papers.journal: Journal of arts, humanities and social science.
papers.abstract: This qualitative study examines how senior executives from technology, financial services, and consumer goods publicly make sense of enterprise-scale generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) adoption. Using a purposively selected, bounded single-case design, it applies reflexive thematic analysis to the complete transcript of one moderated industry panel. Three research questions ask: (1) how leaders describe adoption trajectories, maturity, and organizational arrangements; (2) how they reconcile regulation with creative, operational, and governance innovation; and (3) how they frame workforce roles, emerging competencies, and human oversight. Technology–organization–environment, diffusion-of-innovation, and organizational sensemaking perspectives inform interpretation. Nine themes were developed: production-grade diffusion; regulation as creative discipline; industrialized versus distinctive content; personalization and data trust; practitioner-led implementation; divergent workforce responses; critical-thinking demands; human-in-the-loop brand safety; and a shift toward generative engine optimization. Timestamped excerpts and explicit code-to-theme and theme-to-question mappings substantiate the analysis. These findings describe public executive narratives, not independently verified organizational outcomes. A single public transcript and single-analyst interpretation limit transferability and preclude statistical generalization. The principal contribution is a transparent, theory-informed example of analyzing public executive discourse and a foundation for subsequent multi-source research.

papers.title: The artificial intelligence tool ChatGPT and its impact on the development of the integrated writing skill in students at the International Learning' Institute
papers.authors: Paul Sebastián Montenegro Rosero, Elena Valeria Flores Borja
papers.abstract: The present research analyzed the impact of the pedagogical use of ChatGPT on the development of English written production in students at the International Learning Institute, located in the city of Tulcán, Ecuador. The study arose from the difficulties identified in grammatical precision, spelling, syntactic organization, coherence, cohesion, and lexical variety of the texts produced by the students. The study was conducted with the entire population, consisting of 45 students aged between 14 and 22 years, with English proficiency levels ranging from A1 to B2. The research was developed using a quantitative approach, with a descriptive scope and a single-group exploratory design with a pretest and posttest. A questionnaire and a written production evaluation rubric were used for data collection. During the intervention, ChatGPT was used as a complementary tool to provide immediate feedback, identify grammatical and spelling errors, suggest improvements in textual structure, and promote vocabulary expansion. The results obtained through the diagnostic survey evidenced difficulties in sentence structuring, the use of varied vocabulary, punctuation, and grammatical accuracy, as well as differences in the frequency with which students used ChatGPT to support their writing. It is concluded that the planned, ethical, and supervised integration of ChatGPT can constitute a complementary strategy to strengthen English written production, if its application is accompanied by teacher guidance and the student's critical participation.

papers.title: UTILIZATION OF AI ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF POETRY WRITING
papers.authors: Kasno Atmo Sukarto
papers.abstract: So far, the use of Artificial Intelligence, commonly called AI, is increasingly prominent among students, students, especially among literature students, and audiences who are in charge of literary issues, especially the development of poetry writing. Related to that, things that must be done both technically and strategically are to collaborate with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The purpose of writing using the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the development of poetry writing is the use of technology to facilitate human activities in helping information more effectively and efficiently. The research method applied in this writing is a descriptive-qualitative method, namely describing selected popular Indonesian literary works, especially poems that in their development utilize Artificial Intelligence. Related to this writing plan, the data source is taken from Kemaran: Anthology of Poetry published by the Indonesian Scholars-Literature Association (HISKI)) Komda DKI Jakarta in 2003. This poetry anthology gathers eight poetry writers who are members of HISKI Komda DKI Jakarta. Of the eight writers, "it is not a good and beautiful work". Therefore. themes that are randomly drawn. The themes to be described are taken as a sample from each author. The results of the analysis can be concluded that the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be known for the development of poetry works in Kemarau: Anthology of Poetry, showing that there are shortcomings and weaknesses in the development of poetry creation, the location of weaknesses and shortcomings can be known. Thus, the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) can help write poetry effectively and efficiently, especially for beginner writers, both students, students, and the community in charge of poetry writing problems.

papers.title: Meditation Beneath the Surface: A Narrative Review of Underwater Mindfulness, Breath-Hold Physiology and Contemplative Tradition
papers.authors: Satinder Singh Rekhi, Saamdu Chetri, Luis Miguel Gallardo, Renitta Sinha
papers.abstract: **Background.** Contemplative traditions have long associated water with stillness, concealment and renewal, and divers frequently describe underwater experience as meditative. This review asks whether immersion and submersion offer a distinctive context for mindfulness practice, and what the current evidence can and cannot support. **Methods.** A narrative review integrating epic and canonical Indian sources, the physiology of immersion and breath-hold diving, controlled and uncontrolled studies of diving-based mindfulness programmes, neuroimaging of elite freedivers, and adjacent research on flotation-REST, blue space and aquatic therapy. **Findings.** Water immersion reliably shifts autonomic balance towards parasympathetic activity, and facial submersion recruits the trigeminally mediated diving response. Scuba diving imposes slow, deliberate breathing and has been associated with reduced perceived stress and increased self-reported mindfulness in a small controlled trial (n = 67). A randomised pilot of mindfulness-integrated diving in people with PTSD (n = 34) found a significant advantage over multisport activity only for intrusion symptoms at one month, with effects gone by three months. A single-case EEG/fMRI study of a world-champion freediver found alpha-band and default-mode changes that partly overlap with meditation signatures. Flotation-REST, which removes most exteroceptive input, produces large acute reductions in state anxiety and heightens interoceptive awareness. **Conclusions.** Underwater settings plausibly amplify the attentional anchors central to mindfulness: breath, body and present-moment sensation. However, no study has compared underwater meditation with equivalent land-based practice, and hypoxic blackout poses a serious, sometimes fatal risk. We propose an optimal environment hypothesis: in still, warm, clear and shallow water, with technical demands minimised, underwater practice may deepen mindfulness beyond equivalent practice on land. It should be tested in rigorous, safety-first trials.

papers.title: Fear of AI Replacement and its Relationship with Anxiety, Career Uncertainty, and Life Satisfaction
papers.authors: Sabir Shahzad, Muhammad Maaz Khan, Abdur Rehman, Zaid Bari
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the nature of work and creating growing concerns about future employment among university students. Fear of AI replacement may influence students’ psychological well-being and perceptions of career security. The present study examined the relationship between fear of AI replacement, anxiety, career insecurity, and life satisfaction among university students in Pakistan. A quantitative cross-sectional correlational design was used with a sample of 400 university students aged 18–25 years, comprising 200 males and 200 females. Participants completed measures of fear of AI replacement, career insecurity, anxiety, and life satisfaction. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and regression analysis. The findings indicated that fear of AI replacement was positively associated with anxiety (β = .43, p < .001) and career insecurity (β = .52, p < .001), while it was negatively associated with life satisfaction (β = −.31, p < .001). Regression analyses showed that fear of AI replacement explained 18% of the variance in anxiety, 27% in career insecurity, and 10% in life satisfaction. The findings suggest that greater fear of AI replacement may be associated with increased anxiety and career insecurity and reduced life satisfaction among university students. Universities should consider integrating AI literacy, career counselling, employability skills, and psychological support to help students adapt to AI-related changes in the future market.

papers.title: Energy Consumption Modeling and Forecasting for Medical AI Systems in Nigerian Hospitals: A Climate-Calibrated Simulation Framework
papers.authors: Howard Chioma Chinagorom
papers.abstract: Increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare raises energy-demand questions that are especially acute in resource-limited regions. Because operational, application-level energy-metering data for medical AI systems in Sub-Saharan African hospitals are not yet publicly available, this study develops a climate-calibrated simulation framework that couples real facility profiles (bed capacity for six Nigerian teaching hospitals, from institutional and published sources) with real long-term climate normals (temperature and humidity for each hospital city) and a transparently parameterized medical-AI workload overlay (diurnal, weekly, and holiday patterns informed by prior literature). Statistical models (ARIMA, SARIMA, Holt-Winters exponential smoothing) and machine-learning models (a purpose-built LSTM and a hybrid LSTM-ARIMA) were evaluated on the resulting 58-month (January 2020-October 2024) simulated series using a consistent walk-forward, one-step-ahead protocol. Seasonal statistical models achieved the lowest forecast error (Holt-Winters MAPE=0.36%, SARIMA MAPE=0.37%), outperforming the hybrid LSTM-ARIMA (MAPE=0.51%) and a standalone LSTM (MAPE=0.61%), while the hybrid was most accurate at very short (1-day) horizons. Diurnal peak-hour (0800-1400) demand exceeded off-peak demand by 35%, and dry/harmattan-season demand exceeded the annual mean by 1.4-5.3% depending on institution and local climate. Rather than asserting a single best algorithm, this study's central contribution is the framework itself: a reusable, real-data-calibrated method for generating defensible medical-AI energy-demand scenarios where metered data do not yet exist, together with comparative evidence that the relative advantage of statistical versus machine-learning forecasting depends on how strongly deterministic the underlying seasonal structure is. The framework and comparative findings offer a starting point for energy planning and policy-making for AI-enabled healthcare across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), pending validation against real operational meter data.

papers.title: EFL Students’ Error Detection, Correction, and Acceptance Calibration: A Performance-Based Study at the Faculty of Education–Surman
papers.authors: Majdi Sami Ali Awn
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in English language learning for writing support, grammar correction, feedback, translation, and academic language production. Its educational value depends not only on students’ ability to use AI tools but also on their ability to evaluate AI output and make appropriately calibrated reliance decisions. This study investigated EFL students’ performance in detecting and correcting linguistic errors in a 30-item English sentence evaluation task and examined the correspondence between their acceptance or rejection decisions and the observed correctness of the items. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was used with 30 EFL students who evaluated 17 correct sentences and 13 sentences containing targeted errors. For each item, participants judged correctness, provided a correction when necessary, indicated whether they would accept the sentence without further checking, and rated their confidence on a five-point scale. Detection, correction, acceptance calibration, overacceptance, and underacceptance were summarized using means and standard deviations. Spearman’s rank-order correlation was used to examine associations between performance and acceptance calibration. Mean detection performance was 92.22% (SD = 4.23), mean correction performance was 91.28% (SD = 8.01), and mean acceptance calibration was 75.33% (SD = 8.51). Mean overacceptance was 17.18% (SD = 10.24), whereas mean underacceptance was 30.39% (SD = 13.56). No statistically significant association was observed between detection and acceptance calibration (ρ = .056, p = .770) or between correction and acceptance calibration (ρ = .003, p = .987). These findings indicate that accurate linguistic evaluation and calibrated acceptance decisions should not be treated as interchangeable outcomes. Within the limits of the small, non-probability sample and the single task used in this study, the results support the inclusion of explicit verification and critical evaluation activities in EFL instruction.

papers.title: Students’ Lived Experiences on the Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools in Learning Social Studies
papers.authors: Nelvin Q. Bustamante
papers.journal: International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies
papers.abstract: This study explored the lived experiences of Grade 12 Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) students in using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools for learning Social Studies in Malapatan III District, Schools Division of Sarangani, Philippines. Anchored in Moustakas’ Transcendental Phenomenology, Davis’ Technology Acceptance Model, and Zimmerman’s Self-Regulated Learning Theory, the study employed a qualitative phenomenological research design. Nine Grade 12 HUMSS students from three public secondary schools participated in in-depth interviews, while three Social Studies teachers participated in a focus group discussion for data triangulation. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, and data were gathered using a validated semi-structured interview guide and analyzed thematically. The findings identified twelve emerging themes encompassing students’ lived experiences, the contexts shaping AI-supported learning, and their perspectives on future AI integration. Participants perceived AI as a valuable learning resource that improved conceptual understanding, academic productivity, confidence, classroom engagement, and emotional well-being. However, excessive dependence, reduced independent thinking, information accuracy, and academic integrity emerged as significant concerns. Students emphasized the importance of responsible AI use, critical evaluation, and continued teacher guidance. The study recommends strengthening AI literacy, ethical practices, and teacher capacity building through the proposed Responsible Artificial Intelligence Integration and Learning Empowerment Program (RAILEP). The findings primarily support Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education) by promoting responsible, inclusive, and learner-centered technology integration. The study contributes to educational and institutional sustainability by informing school-based guidelines and instructional practices that balance technological innovation with academic integrity, learner autonomy, and meaningful human interaction.

papers.title: Feasibility and Measurement Properties of a Large Language Model–Based Virtual Patient Laboratory for Clinical Reasoning Training in Physical Therapy Students: Single-Arm Pilot Study
papers.authors: Alfredo Lerín Calvo, A. Gonzalez, Asier Sagarribay Villano, Silvia Di‐Bonaventura, Raúl Ferrer Peña
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) configured as virtual patients may expand structured practice of clinical reasoning in health professions education. Before testing effectiveness, it must be established whether students engage with them and whether the resulting scores are complete, reliable, and related to performance with real patients. Our earlier pilot randomized trial found very low engagement with a less structured LLM-based approach. Objective This study aimed to assess the feasibility (adherence, acceptability, and data completeness) of a revised, structured LLM-based clinical reasoning laboratory (Laboratorio de Inteligencia Artificial [LIA]) in undergraduate physical therapy education and to explore its measurement properties, including its association with clinical judgment with a real patient assessed with the Lasater Clinical Judgment Rubric (LCJR). Methods In this single-arm pilot feasibility study, 27 third-year physical therapy students at a Spanish university completed, in 2024-2025, 3 virtual patient cases (lumbar, cervical, and thoracic spine pain) simulated by ChatGPT (GPT-4) over 4 weeks, each twice. ChatGPT scored each attempt from 0 to 4 on the same 10 dimensions of the Lasater Clinical Judgment Rubric (LCJR; 0-40 points) that human assessors applied (1-4 per dimension; 10-40 points) during a real patient encounter. Feasibility outcomes were case completion, data completeness, and satisfaction (0-10). Measurement outcomes were internal consistency and convergent validity (Spearman correlations between model-generated and human LCJR scores). Variability estimates informed the sample size of a future trial. Results All 27 students were assessed with the LCJR; 22 (81%) completed at least 1 LIA case. Both attempts of the lumbar, cervical, and thoracic cases were completed by 78%, 63%, and 74% of students, respectively. Satisfaction data were available for 15 students (56%; mean 6.0, SD 1.3), and missing secondary data clustered in the third rotation. Internal consistency was excellent for the LCJR (α=.96) and ranged from .43 to .90 for model-generated ratings. Model-generated LIA scores clustered near the maximum (mean 36.0, SD 1.4). Among completers, LIA scores correlated weakly with the LCJR (ρ=0.25, 95% CI –0.20 to 0.61; ρ=0.44, 95% CI 0.05-0.71, when noncompleted attempts were scored as 0). Grade point average correlated almost perfectly with the LCJR (ρ=0.96; n=22); after adjustment for it, the LIA-LCJR association disappeared (partial ρ=–0.10). A future trial would require approximately 39 students per group (80% power, conservative variance). Conclusions Delivering the LIA within the curriculum was feasible, but clinical judgment ratings generated by ChatGPT did not reflect those of human assessors with a real patient: they clustered near the maximum and showed no convergent validity once noncompletion was separated from performance. LLM-generated ratings should not be used as outcome or assessment measures without validation against human raters. Case calibration, completion tracking, and clarification of the GPA-LCJR relationship are also needed before a definitive trial. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06809634 ; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06809634

papers.title: The cry as a vital sign: A smartphone based study of neonatal cry acoustics in hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy
papers.authors: Debankur Chakraborty
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Many Indian special newborn care units (SNCUs) cannot offer amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG) or early MRI, so bedside judgement decides which newborns receive closer neurological attention. Earlier work found that asphyxiated newborns cry with a higher pitch and shorter phonation than healthy newborns [10], and a meta-analysis reported higher fundamental frequency, dysphonation and atypical melody in infants with neurological dysfunction, with wide differences between studies [11]. Aim To determine whether basic acoustic features of a smartphone-recorded pain cry (following a heel prick) can differentiate term newborns with HIE from control newborns. Also, to track changes in cry acoustics over the first 72 hours of life and evaluate their association with the clinical severity and short-term outcomes of encephalopathy. Design A prospective, single-centre diagnostic accuracy and cohort study in a tertiary SNCU. Three groups of term newborns are recorded: newborns with HIE, healthy comparators, and sick comparators who do not have HIE. Every newborn is recorded after the same stimulus, the first clinically indicated heel-prick. Newborns with HIE and sick comparators are recorded again at 24 hours, 72 hours and before discharge. A cry that is late or absent counts as a result and not as a missing value. Three clinicians blinded to group also classify the cries by listening, so the phone-based measures can be compared with the human ear. Analysis The primary outcome is the area under the ROC curve of a logistic model with five pre-specified acoustic predictors. The target is 180 analysable newborns (70 with HIE and 110 comparators). Reporting follows STARD and TRIPOD+AI. Relevance In a South Asian trial, cooling did not reduce death or disability at 18 months and increased death alone [7]. A cry tool in this setting is therefore proposed to help prioritise EEG, seizure surveillance, closer observation and referral. It is not proposed as a trigger for cooling.

papers.title: Neurophysiological Monitoring of Sport Related Concussion: From Diagnosis to Return to Play
papers.authors: Jin Lee, Eric D. Kirby, Christopher Royce Levi, Louis Shidiak, Andrew J. Gardner, Ryan C.N. D’Arcy
papers.abstract: Abstract The validation of objective neurophysiological monitoring of concussion from diagnosis to return to play has the potential to improve the clinical care of athletes. Extracted from event-related potentials (ERP), ‘brain vital signs’ offer a non-invasive objective neurophysiological measure of three well established ERP responses that complement existing clinical assessments: 1) the N100 response related to auditory sensation; 2) the P300 response related to basic attention; and 3) the N400 response related to cognitive processing. The N400, in particular, has increasingly been demonstrated to be sensitive to head impact related cognitive impairment. Accordingly, brain vital sign measures were collected in n =165 rugby league players from two Australian professional National Rugby League clubs (NRL), with concussed players ( n =26) being subsequently assessed over a total of five separate time points (Baseline, Day 2, Day 5, Day 10, and Day 42). This timeline aligned with acute (Day 2), NRL mandatory minimum return-to-play (RTP) guidelines (Day 10), and an extended post RTP period. Relative to baseline, the results revealed significant N400 cognitive processing latency delays at Day 2 post-concussion (p=0.002). The N400 latency delays persisted past day 5, significantly returning to baseline values at Day 10, consistent with the RTP mandatory minimum requirement. The findings indicated that neurophysiological recovery occurred in this cohort within an approximate 10-day time frame. Future studies monitoring brain vital sign changes across the trajectory of injury to recovery are needed in sports related concussion management.

papers.title: Human Hippocampal Theta-Gamma Phase-Amplitude Coupling Signals the Distance to Remembered Goals
papers.authors: Zimo Huang, Paris Goumas, James A. Bisby, Roman Rodionov, Beate Diehl, Andrew W. McEvoy, Matthew C. Walker, Umesh Vivekananda, Neil Burgess, Daniel Bush
papers.abstract: Abstract In mammals, flexible navigation is believed to rely on a cognitive map of known locations supported by the hippocampus and surrounding medial temporal lobe structures. Hippocampal place cells typically exhibit spatial firing fields within a given environment. Moreover, their firing is modulated by the movement-related theta rhythm such that ‘theta sweeps’ of place cell activity encode the trajectory towards a hidden reward location during goal-directed navigation. Here, we attempted to detect signatures of theta sweeps in the human hippocampal local field potential (LFP) recorded with intracranial EEG. Specifically, we hypothesised that sequences of locations along a planned trajectory encoded by distinct cell assemblies are associated with gamma activity at successive theta phases. To test this hypothesis, we asked N=9 patients with epilepsy to perform a spatial navigation task in desktop virtual reality while we recorded LFP signals from depth electrode contacts implanted across the medial temporal lobe. Consistent with our predictions, we found an increase in hippocampal theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, a decrease in gamma power, and theta phase precession of gamma activity as hidden goal locations were approached and the sequence of locations remaining to be traversed became shorter. This suggests that goal-directed hippocampal theta sweeps during navigation are reflected in LFP theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, and that these neural mechanisms of model-based planning are conserved across species.

papers.title: Stimulus overlap confounds generalization in EEG foundation-model benchmarks
papers.authors: Han Cui, Yuge Zhu, Shaojia Huang, Tao Xu
papers.abstract: Abstract Neural decoding benchmarks commonly evaluate generalization across participants while reusing the same experimental stimuli in training and test sets. This design cannot distinguish transfer to new stimuli from recognition of familiar material, a distinction that is increasingly important for electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models—pretrained models designed to learn reusable neural representations. Here we introduce a training-matched audit that varies stimulus overlap while holding test trials, training participants and stimulus counts fixed. Across ten tasks from seven EEG emotion datasets, stimulus overlap increased differential-entropy decoding accuracy in every task and accounted for 77% of above-chance seen-stimulus performance on FACED-9. Across representations, overlap-dependent gains tracked stimulus identifiability; for CBraMod and LaBraM, advantages over input-matched handcrafted features were concentrated on familiar stimuli. Architecture-matched random controls nevertheless showed transferable benefits of pretraining on unseen stimuli. These results separate participant generalization from stimulus generalization and provide a framework for evaluating both in neural decoding benchmarks.

papers.title: NETWORK TRAFFIC ANALYSIS FOR DETECTING CYBER ATTACKS ( October 2026)
papers.authors: Praveen Kumar Mishra, Aastha Singh
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology
papers.abstract: Most attacks have to traverse a network at some point, and when they do so, they leave traces in the traffic.This paper investigates how those traces can be collected, measured and turned into alerts.We cover the most common ways to collect traffic data (packet captures, flow records and logs), the types of characteristics that are generally useful, and three main families of detection methods: signature-based, statistical and machine learning-based.We also describe how several well-known attacks (port scans, denial of service, brute force and botnet command-and-control) manifest themselves on the wire A step-by-step analysis pipeline is presented, as well as the most common public datasets used for evaluation and the corresponding metrics.Finally, we discuss the major challenges that remain in this area: encrypted traffic, class imbalance, concept drift and the gap between laboratory test results and real-world network deployments.The goal is to provide a clear, practical overview for students and junior security analysts rather than presenting a novel algorithm.

papers.title: Organisational Policy Reforms for Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Business Education in Nigeria
papers.authors: Ifeloluwa Janet OYELEYE, Ann Mojisola Uwagwu
papers.abstract: This study examined organizational policy reforms required for integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into business education in Nigeria. It investigated the extent of AI integration, the policy reforms required for effective implementation, and the relationship between organizational policy frameworks and institutional readiness to produce AI-competent graduates. A descriptive survey research design was adopted. The population comprised 56 lecturers and administrators in Business Education departments across 4 selected tertiary institutions in Nigeria. Total enumeration was employed, and all the 56 respondents participated in the study. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using mean, standard deviation, and Pearson Product Moment Correlation (PPMC).
