papers.authors: Thomas Zeng, Zelei Cheng, Mingyang Zhou, Sambit Sahu, William Campbell, Genta Indra Winata
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for multi-turn agentic tasks that require interactions with users and environments over extended sequences of actions. A common approach to improving LLM agents is to use more capable expert models to provide training supervision, either by behavior cloning the expert's trajectories or by using the expert to correct the actions in trajectories generated by the weaker student model. However, expert LLMs can provide richer supervision than actions alone: they can directly generate textual critique that explain why specific actions are incorrect. We study whether training on such feedback benefits LLM agents and propose Critique-Augmented Agentic Fine-Tuning (CAFT), a framework that elicits textual expert feedback on student-generated trajectories. For each incorrect action, the expert yields both a corrected action and a textual critique explaining the student's mistake--which we then use as the training target for fine-tuning. Across four student models from the Nemotron 3 and Gemma 4 families on the agentic domains $τ^2$-Bench Airline+Retail and WebShop, adding critiques to action-level supervision improves performance by 8% on average over action-only distillation. Additionally, CAFT checkpoints can also provide a better warm start for reinforcement learning than expert-trajectory distillation. Our results demonstrate that textual critiques can strengthen supervision for multi-turn LLM agents.

papers.title: Where to Start, How to Move: Analyzing Curricula under GRPO for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.authors: Minchan Kim, Sungho Bae, Youngjin Kim, Hyunwoo Park
papers.abstract: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) provides no reward-relative learning signal when all rollouts receive identical rewards. In long-horizon tasks that require multiple interactions, rewards are given only upon successful task completion, making all-fail groups common early in training and limiting opportunities to practice later steps. Guide Assisted GRPO replays a successful reference prefix before the learner continues. We study how initial positions, handoff units, and movement rules affect unassisted task completion. Across three model sizes on BFCL, starting near completion is more effective under a fixed turn-level threshold rule. Finer handoffs alone do not consistently help, but outcome-informed tool-call selection outperforms GRPO on trained and untrained task categories. Guided starts also improve AppWorld success on both evaluation splits. These findings highlight where learning starts and how starting positions move as key curriculum choices.

papers.title: Probabilistic Physics Digital Twin for Human-Robot Interaction
papers.authors: Yushen Hu, Harshvardhan Chandirasekar, Apurv Kushwaha, Jonathan King, Zhutian Chen
papers.abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used in robotics to simulate interactions, predict action outcomes, and support planning. However, constructing accurate digital twins requires precise estimates of physical properties such as mass, friction, and center of mass, which are often difficult to obtain in real-world environments. We propose probabilistic digital twins, which represent uncertain physical properties as probability distributions rather than fixed values. By simulating actions across these distributions, the twin predicts a range of possible outcomes and their likelihoods. These probabilistic simulations can guide both human and robot actions by identifying actions that are effective despite physical uncertainty. We demonstrate this framework through human-robot interaction scenarios, including interfaces that communicate simulated outcomes to users and robot planning strategies that explicitly account for uncertainty.

papers.title: SmartSign: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition and Speech Generation Platform
papers.authors: Rahul Mahadev Kharap Animesh Chandrashekhar Agarkar, Mr. Vaibhav Sahadeo Korde Mr. Sahil Sharma, Dr. Abrar S. Alvi
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: Sign language is an essential means of communication for individuals with hearing and speech impairments. However, communication barriers often arise between sign language users and people who are unfamiliar with sign language. To address this challenge, this paper presents a SmartSign: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition and Speech Generation Platform that uses computer vision and deep learning techniques to recognize hand gestures and convert them into understandable text. The proposed system is developed using Python, Flask, OpenCV, MediaPipe, and a trained machine learning model. It provides multiple detection methods, including image-based detection, video-based detection, multi-image processing, and real-time webcam recognition. The system also incorporates interactive learning features such as sign language practice, tutorials, a chatbot, progress tracking, history, and analytics to support continuous learning. Additionally, an administrative panel enables administrators to manage users, tutorials, detection history, and application settings. The system processes hand landmarks and extracts relevant features to identify corresponding signs and display the predicted results through a user-friendly web interface. By integrating sign recognition with learning and progress-monitoring facilities, the proposed application aims to improve accessibility, support sign language education, and reduce communication barriers. The system demonstrates the potential of combining computer vision, deep learning, and web technologies to develop an interactive and accessible sign language recognition platform

papers.title: AI-Based Smart Interview Analyzer System
papers.authors: Miss. Dhyanhvi Kale, Mr. Abhishek Padole Mr. Aditya Chandure, Dr. Abrar S. Alvi
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: The AI-Based Smart Interview Analyzer System is an artificial intelligence-based web application developed to help students and job seekers improve their interview skills through interactive mock interviews, automated performance evaluation, and personalized feedback. In today’s competitive employment environment, candidates often face challenges such as nervousness, poor communication skills, lack of confidence, and insufficient interview practice. Traditional preparation methods may not provide immediate and consistent feedback, creating a need for an intelligent system that supports effective and personalized interview preparation. The proposed system integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to support interview practice and analyze candidate responses. It provides job-role-based interview preparation, maintains interview history, and helps users identify their strengths and weaknesses through feedback. The application consists of two main modules: the Admin Module and the Student Module. The Admin Module manages student information, job roles, interviews, and feedback, while the Student Module allows users to access their dashboard, practice interviews, review previous sessions, view feedback, and manage their profiles. The system aims to provide an accessible and structured environment for continuous learning and performance improvement. By combining AI-based assessment with a user-friendly web interface, the AI-Based Smart Interview Analyzer System can help candidates develop better communication skills, increase confidence, and improve their readiness for real-world job interviews. Future enhancements may include advanced speech analysis, facial expression recognition, body-language assessment, multilingual support, and more comprehensive real-time performance evaluation

papers.title: Student Career Guidance System Using Machine Learning
papers.authors: Sultana Hasan Sayyad and Ms. Asha Mane
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: Career selection is an important decision for students, as their academic performance, skills, and employability attributes can influence their future career opportunities. This research presents a Student Career Guidance System using Machine Learning for predicting suitable career domains from student-related information. A secondary dataset containing 50,000 student records was used for the study, including academic, skill, and employability-related attributes. The dataset was preprocessed and different Machine Learning classification techniques, namely Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, were applied and compared. The performance of the models was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Among the evaluated models, Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy of 70.49% and was selected as the final model. The proposed system can provide data-driven career guidance by predicting suitable career domains and can support students in making informed career-related decisions based on their available information.

papers.title: Generative AI in visual design processes: A systematic review and comparative analysis from the perspective of design disciplines
papers.authors: Yasemin KAYABAŞI
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative AI is fundamentally transforming creative design disciplines including graphic design, visual communication design, animation, game design, and UI/UX design. Existing studies predominantly address the role of AI within a single discipline, while comparative analyses examining these fields systematically remain limited in the literature. The research conducted by Choudhury, Eisenbart & Kuys (2025) and Song & Abdul Rabu (2025) have clearly revealed the need for discipline-specific comparative studies in sub-fields. The aim of this research is to reveal comparatively in which functions, at which stages, and in what forms of human-AI collaboration AI is utilized within these design disciplines. This systematic review was conducted based on the PRISMA 2020 protocol. A search conducted in the Scopus and Web of Science databases, a total of 100 articles were analyzed, comprising 20 articles representing each of the five visual design disciplines. The results of the analysis reveal that graphic design, artificial intelligence supports concept development and visual production processes, while in visual communication design, it undertakes evaluation and classification functions. In the field of animation, motion generation and character development processes are accelerated, and in game design, it assumes a determining role in procedural content generation and narrative development stages. In UI/UX design, AI contributes to the modeling of user behavior and prototyping processes. The interdisciplinary comparison shows that AI has established itself as a different creative partner in each field, and common challenges such as originality, copyright, and the transformation of designer identity maintain their validity across all disciplines. This research presents an original framework that addresses the use of AI comparatively across five visual design disciplines, emphasizing the necessity of field-based evaluations for design researchers, educators, and practitioners.

papers.title: The Next-Gen Commerce Graduate: Thriving in an AI-Driven Economy-An Empirical Analysis of Student Perceptions and Curriculum Relevance
papers.authors: Dr. Rekha P T, Ms. Alit Rose C D, Ms. Britta Simon E, Ms. Athira G Kumar, Ms. Akhila Ajay P
papers.journal: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering and Management (IRJAEM)
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into global business workflows has fundamentally reshaped employability expectations, requiring modern commerce graduates to possess both analytical and technological capabilities. This empirical study investigates commerce students' perceptions regarding AI adoption, their confidence in entering an AI-driven job market, and the perceived relevance of current higher education curricula. Primary data was gathered through a structured 5-point Likert scale questionnaire administered to N = 150 undergraduate (70%) and postgraduate (30%) commerce students across various specializations. Given the non-normal, ordinal nature of the data, descriptive statistics (Medians and Interquartile Ranges) and non-parametric inferential methods—including Spearman’s rank correlation, the Mann-Whitney U test, and the Kruskal-Wallis H test—were employed for hypothesis testing. The findings reveal that informal or active usage of AI tools does not significantly correlate with perceived career confidence (rs = .138, p = .091). Instead, graduate job market confidence depends strongly on formal institutional curriculum adequacy (rs = .665, p < .001). Comparative analysis showed significant differences in curriculum perception across academic levels (p = .005), with undergraduates expressing greater dissatisfaction than postgraduates. Furthermore, job confidence varied significantly across specializations (p < .001), with Business Analytics students reporting lower confidence (Mean Rank = 43.40) than traditional streams, reflecting heightened critical awareness of industry technical demands. The study concludes that higher education institutions must urgently reform commerce curricula by embedding applied AI applications, automated analytics, and algorithmic decision-making to bridge the gap between academic preparation and workforce expectations.

papers.title: BETWEEN TECHNICAL RATIONALITY AND RELATIONAL LABOR: A TECHNOFEMINIST ANALYSIS OF PRESERVICE PRESCHOOL TEACHERS' AI PERCEPTIONS AND METAPHORS
papers.authors: Gülçin Bilgener
papers.journal: Open Access Publishing Group - European Journal of Education Studies
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) threatens to undermine teaching by simplifying practices into a rationalized process and potentially causing deskilling. This study investigated preservice preschool teachers’ professional perspectives and metaphorical conceptualization of AI within a technofeminist framework. The study focused on the inherent tension between the relational nature of early childhood education and the technical rationality of AI. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed with 150 preservice preschool teachers at a Turkish state university. Data were collected utilizing a 15-item AI perception scale, a metaphor form, and three open-ended questions probing the uses of AI, collaboration with AI systems, and broader anxieties. Findings indicated that despite preservice teachers holding a high awareness of the instructional advantages of AI, their moral reservations persisted independently of pedagogical assessments and showed no correlation with frequency of application. Qualitatively, preservice teachers framed AI through theory-driven themes such as “the God trick” and “deskilling”. Female participants' exclusive articulation of the “domestication” theme illustrated a strategy where women tailor technology to their pedagogical goals through relational metaphors such as “mother” and “confidant.” The study demonstrated that AI is not a neutral tool in education but is actively shaped by societal gender structures, necessitating a politically informed approach to teacher education.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini in answering patient-oriented questions about coronary artery bypass grafting: An expert-based cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Hakan Baltacı, Yusuf Taşpınar, Üzeyir Yılmaz
papers.abstract: Objectives: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by patients to obtain information about high-risk procedures such as coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).This study aimed to compare expert evaluations of responses generated by ChatGPT (GPT-5.5 Instant, OpenAI) and Gemini (Gemini 3.5 Flash, Google) to frequently asked patient-oriented questions about CABG. Patients and methods:In this expert-based cross-sectional study, responses generated by ChatGPT and Gemini to 29 frequently asked CABG-related questions developed by cardiovascular surgeons were evaluated.The questions were submitted in English to both models through free, publicly available web interfaces using a standardized prompt.Each question was entered in a separate new chat session, and only the first generated response was recorded.Optional web search and Deep Research features were not manually enabled.After model identities and model-specific elements were removed, the responses were presented separately in randomized order.Five cardiovascular surgeons independently rated the responses using a five-point Likert scale that jointly assessed clinical accuracy and usefulness.In the primary paired analysis, the sum of the five evaluators' ratings for each question was used, yielding 29 paired questionlevel observations.Results: Both models received high scores.The mean question-level total score was 23.31±1.54for ChatGPT and 23.00±1.31for Gemini.The mean paired difference was 0.31 points (bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.07 to 0.69) and was not statistically significant (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, W=60.0; p=0.129; matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation=0.37).At the individual-rating level, 97.2% of ratings were 4 or 5 for each model.The average-measures absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.50 (95% CI, 0.13-0.74)for ChatGPT and 0.15 (95% CI, -0.49-0.56)for Gemini.Conclusion: Under the reported evaluation conditions, responses generated by ChatGPT and Gemini received similarly high combined ratings for clinical accuracy and usefulness.These findings reflect the expert-rated clinical appropriateness of model responses generated at a specific time point; they do not establish guideline concordance, within-model reproducibility, patient comprehension, or clinical benefit.LLM-generated CABG information may have a supportive role in patient education; however, this possibility requires validation in patient-based studies.These tools should not replace individualized physician-led counseling.

papers.title: Organisational culture and technology acceptance as catalysts for artificial intelligence adoption towards human resource management effectiveness in Thailand’s industrial hubs
papers.authors: Kantima Pongnairat
papers.journal: SA Journal of Human Resource Management
papers.abstract: Orientation: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly important in human resource management (HRM), particularly in Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC), a rapidly developing industrial and economic zone. Identifying the key factors that influence AI adoption can help organisations improve the effectiveness of their HRM practices. Research purpose: To test how organisational culture, technology acceptance (TA) and technology readiness (TR) are associated with AI use in HRM use of technology (UT), and how UT is associated with HRM effectiveness (EF), including UT’s mediating role. Motivation for the study: Despite strong promotion of AI for HRM efficiency, limited evidence explains which organisational and behavioural factors most drive AI adoption in industrial estates, particularly in the EEC. Research approach/design and method: A cross-sectional survey of 500 HR professionals in EEC industrial estates (Chachoengsao, Chonburi, Rayong) was analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM) with SmartPLS. Main findings: Organisational culture and TA were positively associated with UT, while TR has no effect. Use of technology showed a strong positive association with EF. Use of technology mediated the relationships of OC and TA on EF, but not TR. Practical/managerial implications: Organisations should strengthen digital-supportive culture and employee TA, as these are more impactful than focusing only on readiness and infrastructure. Contribution/value-add: The study shows OC and TA are stronger drivers of AI-HRM adoption than TR and provides evidence-based guidance for improving HRM effectiveness in the EEC through AI.

papers.title: 3D Digital Modeling Empowering Sculpture Education
papers.authors: Lukai Li
papers.journal: Journal of Cases on Information Technology
papers.abstract: This paper explores the application of 3D modeling software in sculpture education and proposes a data-driven framework called “Adaptive Sculpture-3D,” aimed at addressing the lack of real-time feedback and the challenges of cognitive load management in traditional teaching. Through case analysis and quantitative experiments, the study validates the effectiveness of the framework in improving students' creation accuracy (with a 21.8% reduction in vertex error rate) and self-efficacy (medium effect size of 0.74), while also revealing limitations in enhancing operational efficiency (effect size of 0.38). The experimental results demonstrate that the real-time feedback mechanism of the framework significantly optimizes the learning process, though caution is needed to avoid learner dependency caused by excessive prompts. This research provides empirical support for the digital curriculum design in art institutions and envisions future developments integrating generative artificial intelligence and multimodal data.

papers.title: Research on Visual Communication Design Based on Communication Theory
papers.authors: Xuelian Lv, Ju Li
papers.journal: Journal of Cases on Information Technology
papers.abstract: In the era of information overload and rapid digital transformation, visual communication design faces challenges in accurately and attractively transmitting information. This study conducts a case-driven analysis of two Information Technology (IT)-integrated projects: Dunhuang Mogao Grottoes' digital initiative (using TikTok short videos and Unity 3D/Augmented Reality (AR) with >1m Location-Based Service) and Suzhou Wenlv's brand modernization (via interactive HTML5 (H5) and semiotics-based symbol optimization). Empirical results show that short-video channels achieved 300% user growth with 87% longer user engagement, while AR-based channels delivered 500% user growth with 82% longer engagement. Meanwhile, AI-driven visual symbol optimization improved accuracy of information memory by 63% and cross-cultural recognition rate by 62% (A/B test, N=200). Challenges include theoretical complexity and creativity constraints. The study offers a reusable framework for integrating communication theory with AR/dynamic media to optimize visual communication in cultural/commercial contexts.

papers.title: A Dual-Loop Intelligent Teaching Assistant System for Adaptive Web-Based Teaching and Decision Support
papers.authors: Xinlu Wang, Fan Wu, Fei Lei
papers.journal: International Journal of Web-Based Learning and Teaching Technologies
papers.abstract: Web-based technologies often fail to fundamentally reshape teaching processes, despite their ubiquity. This study presents a dual-loop intelligent teaching assistant system that integrates natural language processing-driven intent recognition and sentiment analysis within a human-in-the-loop framework. Unlike systems prioritizing pure automation, this study's architecture dynamically routes complex queries to instructors via a visual decision-support dashboard, balancing real-time responsiveness with pedagogical nuance. Empirical results in higher education reveal that while interaction efficiency improved significantly, user satisfaction depended nonlinearly on technical accuracy, heavily influenced by notification strategies and emergent student behaviors, like reverse engineering the bot. These findings underscore the need to evolve web-based tools from static utilities into adaptive sociotechnical ecosystems that actively support both learner autonomy and instructor decision-making.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Supported Teaching Approaches in Nursing Education: A Scoping Review
papers.authors: Duygu Ceren GÜNGÖR, Fatma Orgun
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) has generated growing interest in its use to support teaching and learning in nursing education. This scoping review aimed to map the existing literature on AI-supported teaching approaches in nursing education, examine how learning outcome domains are addressed, and identify gaps in the current evidence base. METHOD: A scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute Framework and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. Eight databases were searched: ProQuest Central, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, ERIC, and PubMed. RESULTS: Thirty-eight studies published were included. Three themes emerged: AI tools and applications in nursing education, learning outcome domains and assessment approaches, and current limitations and future directions. CONCLUSION: AI-supported teaching approaches show promise in nursing education by supporting knowledge and skill development. However, further research using robust designs and clear pedagogical frameworks is needed to inform sustainable educational practice.

papers.title: AI-Driven Multi-Dimensional Course Assessment and SHS Strand Recommendation System
papers.authors: John Kirby B. Espanto, Dit Rolaida L. Sonza
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.abstract: Senior High School (SHS) students often face challenges in selecting the most appropriate academic strand due to limited assessment tools and the continued reliance on traditional guidance practices. These methods frequently lack objectivity and comprehensive evaluation, resulting in mismatches between students’ competencies, interests, and their chosen academic pathways. Such misalignment may affect students’ academic performance, educational direction, and future career readiness. This study aimed to develop an AI-Driven Multi-Dimensional Course Assessment and SHS Strand Recommendation System designed to objectively evaluate student competencies and generate strand recommendations that align with learners’ abilities, interests, and career potential. The system intends to support students, teachers, and guidance personnel by providing data-driven insights that can assist in making informed academic decisions. The research employed a quantitative–descriptive design integrated with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). The system was developed using an Input–Process–Output (IPO) conceptual framework combined with Agile Software Development Methodology, enabling iterative system improvement and structured data processing. The platform utilizes a 30-dimension assessment model measuring cognitive skills, literacy and communication abilities, technical aptitude, and personality-interest indicators. Student responses are processed through a structured scoring model and analyzed using an AI-powered evaluation module to generate strand recommendations, competency profiles, and career-related insights, which are presented in a downloadable evaluation report. The results are presented in a comprehensive evaluation report that users can download and use for academic guidance and decision-making. Evaluation results showed strong system performance and user acceptance. Based on the ISO/IEC 25010 software quality model, IT experts gave the system an overall mean score of 3.95, indicating a high level of software quality and functionality. System users rated the platform with an overall mean score of 4.00, interpreted as Highly Acceptable, reflecting positive user experience and effectiveness. This finding clearly demonstrates that the system can provide data-driven guidance in SHS strand selection, reduce academic-career mismatches, and support better educational alignment and long-term career readiness among students.

papers.title: An academic chatbot with hybrid retrieval and local large language models
papers.authors: Jhon Paúl Guadalupe Andrade, Blanca Topón-Visarrea, Christian Iza
papers.abstract: Higher-education institutions devote a substantial share of their staff time to answering queries whose answers are already set out in institutional regulations. This paper presents the design and evaluation of an academic chatbot based on retrieval-augmented generation that lets users query those documents in natural language and receive grounded answers in Spanish. The system combines a structure-aware ingestion pipeline, a hybrid retriever that fuses dense semantic search and lexical search through reciprocal rank fusion, and a locally hosted large language model. A distinguishing goal is data sovereignty: every component runs on institutional hardware, so no data is sent to external services. Quality is evaluated with the RAGAS framework over five regulatory documents: the corpus-wide set attains a global score of 0.90, with faithfulness of 0.97. The acceptance criterion is not met, however, under its conjunctive reading: answer relevancy stays below its threshold across all sets, and p95 latency reaches 6.47 seconds against a 5-second target. Quality further degrades on long, heavily cross-referenced regulations. A contrast questionnaire administered to nineteen users places the perception index at 3.64 out of 5 and exposes a relevant discrepancy: only 57.9% agree that the system does not produce fabricated information, against the faithfulness the automatic judge assigns it.

papers.title: Madurez del marco normativo para la IA en la educación superior ecuatoriana
papers.authors: Jorge Maldonado‐Mahauad, Juan Pablo Carvallo, María Cristina León-Carvajal
papers.abstract: The rise of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, has transformed teaching, research, and higher education management at a pace that outstrips the responsiveness of Latin American regulatory frameworks. This study diagnoses the maturity level of Ecuador's regulatory framework on AI in higher education and identifies its critical gaps. A systematic analysis was conducted on 81 regulatory instruments (pending laws, regulations, resolutions, guidelines, and institutional policies) registered in the Regional AI in Education Observatory of the Erasmus+ GENIAL project, as of May 2026. Instruments were coded using a six-dimension framework (actor, object, mechanism, purpose, approach, and maturity) and synthesized into the Regulatory Maturity Index (RMI), which weights regulatory quality. Ecuador achieves an RMI of 70.6/100 (very high level), ranking third among the 28 countries in the Observatory. However, this leadership stems from the breadth of the corpus and university-level activity rather than ecosystem consolidation. Half of the instruments remain at the stage of a declaration of intent, and maturity is the most lagging dimension. Institutional-level instruments account for 87.7% of the corpus, revealing a bottom-up regulatory construction in the absence of specific national legislation. Administrative and data-protection domains concentrate 70.7% of the instruments; only 7.3% explicitly regulate generative AI. A differentiated policy agenda is proposed for CES, the Ministry of Education, CACES, and higher education institutions.

papers.title: Frustrative nonreward engages midfrontal theta power and modulates effort expenditure
papers.authors: Nellia Bellaert, Federico Cassioli, Wan-Ling Tseng, Mandy Rossignol
papers.abstract: Irritability is characterized by a propensity to experience frustration and has been associated with reduced self-reported willingness to expend effort for rewards. Frustration may be relevant to effortful reward pursuit, but its effects on effort expenditure have rarely been experimentally tested in humans. To address this gap, this study introduced a frustration induction in the Effort-Doors task to elicit frustrative nonreward (FNR), a negative emotional state triggered by unexpected reward loss, and examined its effects on physical effort expenditure and feedback-related electroencephalographic (EEG) activity. We also tested whether these effects vary as a function of state and trait measures of motivation and affect. Linear mixed-effects models tested the effects of FNR induction on self-reported, behavioral, and EEG measures in young adults (N = 83) completing the Frustrative Effort-Doors task. Models tested manipulation effects, trial-level post-feedback adjustment, and moderation by state and trait measures. Midfrontal theta power (MFθ) extracted using multivariate spatial filtering was examined as a function of feedback (win vs. FNR), effort (low vs. high), and subsequent behavioral adjustments. The frustration condition was associated with decreased self-reported state motivation and increased frustration, arousal, and response speed. Midfrontal theta power was larger following FNR feedback and increased with state frustration during high-effort trials. Higher state frustration was associated with reduced response vigor during effort execution following FNR feedback. MFθ did not predict trial-to-trial behavioral adjustments. These findings indicate that FNR recruits MFθ, a neural marker of cognitive control, while state frustration modulates physical effort execution following unexpected reward loss.

papers.title: Transformation STEM Education in The Age of Artificial Intelligence: Generative Technologies, Adaptive Learning, Digital Assessment and New STEM Competencies
papers.authors: Aina Balmukanova
papers.journal: The American Journal of Engineering And Technology
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), generative models, adaptive educational systems, and digital assessment tools has begun to significantly change the content and organization of STEM education. While previously the key issue was the creation of interdisciplinary STEM tasks integrating natural sciences, technology, engineering, and mathematics, the current era is characterized by a transition to intelligently supported and personalized educational environments. The purpose of this analytical review is to identify the main areas of transformation in STEM education under the influence of artificial intelligence and to define new requirements for the educational process and STEM competencies. This review analyzes scientific publications on the use of AI in science teaching, generative AI in STEM, personalized and adaptive learning, intelligent tutoring systems, digital assessment, and the development of teacher and student competencies. It demonstrates that AI can enhance personalization, provide dynamic feedback, and support modeling and complex problem solving. However, the educational impact depends significantly on instructional design. Recent meta-analytic data confirm the positive effects of AI-supported instruction and GenAI, but also demonstrate high heterogeneity in the results. The changing nature of assessment is particularly significant: traditional checking of the final answer is no longer sufficient, as generative models are capable of independently generating texts, program code, mathematical solutions, and explanations. The need for a shift to assessing the process of reasoning, design, verification, critical evaluation of AI results, and the student's ability to meaningfully use AI is substantiated. A conclusion is drawn regarding the emergence of a new model of STEM education, in which artificial intelligence is not a substitute for teachers or students, but an intelligent tool for collaborative problem solving, and AI literacy, critical thinking, verification, data management, and the ethical use of technology become integral elements of modern STEM competence. The scientific novelty of this review lies in its approach to the transformation of STEM education, which is not viewed as a standalone implementation of AI technologies, but rather as a change in the entire architecture of STEM activities—from task setting and personalization of learning to assessment and competency structure. The article proposes a conceptual model of Human-AI Integrated STEM, in which artificial intelligence is not a substitute for students or teachers, but an intellectual component of interdisciplinary problem solving. It is further substantiated that, in today's environment, independent verification, validation, and critical assessment of AI results should be considered independent components of a new STEM competency.

papers.title: EMPOWERING VOCATIONAL UNIVERSITY STUDENTS THROUGH GEN-AI IN THE SOCIETY 5.0 ERA: A BLENDED LEARNING COMMUNITY SERVICE PROGRAM IN MADIUN
papers.authors: Damar Isti Pratiwi, Dadang Sanjaya Atmaja, Dimas Adi Perwira, Dedik Tri Istiantara, Ardian Yosep Yohannes, Abdul Ayiz, Kiki Juli Anggoro, Muhammad Khabiburrohman
papers.abstract: The rapid development of digital technology and artificial intelligence has created new demands for vocational higher education institutions to prepare graduates who are adaptive, innovative, and competitive in the Society 5.0 era. This community service program aimed to empower vocational university students in Madiun through the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen-AI) to improve learning effectiveness, digital literacy, and employability-oriented soft skills. The program involved 100 students divided into 4 training classes and facilitated by 6 instructors from national and international professional backgrounds. The implementation lasted for 6 weeks and consisted of four stages: preparation through needs analysis, synchronous learning through two offline workshop sessions at Politeknik Perkeretaapian Indonesia Madiun, asynchronous learning through a flipped learning model, and final evaluation. Various digital platforms were utilized, including ChatGPT, Canva, Google Forms, Kahoot!, Wayground, Pear Deck, and Socrative. The findings revealed high participation rates, improved academic productivity, stronger communication confidence, better collaboration skills, and increased awareness of ethical AI use. The combination of synchronous and asynchronous learning proved effective in creating an engaging and sustainable learning ecosystem. This program demonstrates that Gen-AI can become a strategic tool for empowering vocational students and preparing future graduates to compete in the railway industry and broader global workforce.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Tender Normalization and Bid Evaluation for Construction Supply Chains in Saudi Arabia: A Data-Driven Procurement Framework for Vision 2030 Projects
papers.authors: Amaan Ullah Sharif Mohammed
papers.journal: Global Academic Journal of Economics and Business
papers.abstract: Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 construction programme is increasing the scale and complexity of tendering across infrastructure, buildings, tourism, transport and giga-project supply chains. Conventional bid evaluation remains vulnerable to inconsistent scope interpretation, fragmented tender documents, manual arithmetic checks, evaluator subjectivity and weak traceability between technical and commercial decisions. This review examines how artificial intelligence can support tender normalization and bid evaluation without displacing professional judgement or procurement accountability. Evidence published from 2020 to 2025 was synthesised across construction procurement, contractor selection, construction supply-chain digitalisation, natural language processing, explainable machine learning, supplier selection and AI-assisted bidding. The literature indicates that the principal opportunity is not autonomous award selection but the creation of a governed decision-support layer that converts heterogeneous tender submissions into a common comparison basis. Natural language processing can extract qualifications, exclusions, scope assumptions, programme commitments and contractual risks; rules and structured analytics can reconcile quantities, currencies, unit rates, provisional sums and arithmetic differences; and explainable models can support technical, commercial, sustainability and supplier-risk scoring. However, automation also creates risks of hidden bias, data leakage, inconsistent criteria, overreliance, algorithmic collusion and weak legal defensibility. This review therefore proposes a six-stage framework comprising data ingestion, document intelligence, tender normalization, multi-criteria evaluation, human governance and award recommendation, with project-performance feedback used to recalibrate future models. For Saudi Vision 2030 projects, the framework offers a route to faster, auditable procurement at scale while preserving fairness, local-content considerations, competition and accountable human approval.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Its Influence on Working Capital Management in Emerging Economies
papers.authors: Ph.D. Abdul Rahman
papers.journal: Addaiyan Journal of Arts Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly utilized as a valuable tool in financial decision-making; however, its application in working capital management (WCM) remains under explored, particularly in emerging economies. This study examines the relationship between AI adoption and WCM, specifically investigating whether AI-powered forecasting, financial information analysis, automation, monitoring, and decision support are associated with more effective management of short-term financial resources. A quantitative, cross-sectional methodology is employed, with AI adoption measured using five indicators and WCM assessed through six indicators on a five-point Likert scale. The analytical framework incorporates firm size, firm age, profitability, and sales growth as control variables. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression are used to analyze the proposed relationships. The results indicate a positive and statistically significant association between AI adoption and WCM; AI adoption demonstrates the largest standardized effect in the regression model (β = 0.531, p < 0.001), while firm size also exhibits a significant positive relationship (β = 0.102, p = 0.017). In contrast, firm age, profitability, and sales growth do not show statistically significant effects. The model explains approximately 29.9% of the variance in WCM, indicating substantial explanatory power. These findings suggest that AI can enhance working capital practices by improving forecasting, financial information processing, monitoring, and decision support. This study contributes to the literature by establishing a link between AI adoption and WCM and provides practical recommendations for companies seeking to improve liquidity planning, receivables management, inventory control, and payment decisions through technology-driven management. Additionally, the results offer a basis for further empirical research among firms and sectors in emerging markets.

papers.title: Triad of national security management: Controlled artificial intelligence, neural interfaces, and directive personnel allocation
papers.authors: D. M. Bortnikov, Mikhail A. Lebedev, Дмитрий Александрович Репин
papers.abstract: Aim. To substantiate the content and limits of application of three heterogeneous but interrelated areas of strengthening state capacity in the sphere of national security, specifically controlled artificial intelligence, neural interfaces, and directive personnel allocation, as well as to determine the conditions for their coordinated development without artificial unification into an automated system. Objective s. To reveal the concept of controlled artificial intelligence as applied to public administration; to establish the legal and organizational boundaries of delegating analytical and managerial functions to algorithms; to analyze directive personnel allocation as state planning of the training and placement of competencies while preserving the contractual freedom of citizens; to assess the technological maturity of neural interfaces and to identify proven areas of their application; to determine the points of interconnection among the three areas in the tasks of big data processing, predictive modeling, anti-terrorist prevention, and socio-economic development. Methods. The study employs systemic, institutional, functional, and comparative-legal approaches, methods of analyzing strategic and regulatory legal documents of Russia, scenario analysis, and qualitative comparison of technological maturity. The empirical basis consists of materials from the National Anti-Terrorism Committee and the Federal Security Service of Russia, strategic documents of the Government of Russia, scholarly publications by Russian researchers on data mining, artificial intelligence ethics, and neural interfaces, as well as OECD and UNESCO recommendations and regulatory acts of the European Union. Results . It is established that the elements under consideration are at different stages of institutional and technological maturity. Controlled artificial intelligence is used in analytics, monitoring, forecasting, and the preparation of decision options, provided there is documented human control. Directive personnel allocation has an existing legal basis in the mechanisms of targeted education, state orders, personnel forecasting, and service rotation, but requires a transition from planning professions to planning competencies and teams. Neural interfaces have high evidentiary maturity, primarily in medicine and assistive technologies; their application in public administration appears permissible in limited tasks of digital system accessibility, training, and voluntary support for operators. A differentiated model of state policy is proposed in which the three areas are interconnected at the level of goals and regulations rather than through the unification of data and powers on a single platform. Conclusions. The triad can be viewed as a concept of coordinated development of the state’s analytical, personnel, and human-machine capacity, but not as a ready-made unified technological framework. The most mature areas are controlled artificial intelligence and state management of the personnel order. Neural interfaces require special legal guarantees, ethical expertise, and phased piloting. The condition for the effectiveness of the triad is the preservation of personal human responsibility, technological sovereignty, the contractual nature of personnel obligations, and the prohibition of covert use of neural data.

papers.title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Leadership for Multilingual and Intercultural Language Education in Developing Countries
papers.authors: Abdul Walid QADIRI, Abdul Wali Sirat, Musawer Hakimi
papers.journal: Journal of Language Intelligence and Culture
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering university governance, teaching, and language education across developing countries, yet ethical-leadership scholarship remains concentrated on well-resourced, digitally mature institutions. This paper reports a PRISMA-informed, PICO-guided literature review examining how ethical AI leadership can be theorized for multilingual and intercultural language education in developing-country higher education, with a conflict-affected higher-education setting in South Asia as an illustrative case. Fifty-six sources met inclusion criteria after a staged identification, screening, and eligibility process conducted by a single reviewer using open academic search engines and publisher platforms rather than subscription-indexed databases. Thematic synthesis identified four recurring barrier domains infrastructural access, institutional governance, socio-cultural capacity, and linguistic/data equity and three leadership theories (transformational, distributed, and ethical leadership) that jointly inform a proposed six-dimension conceptual framework for ethical AI leadership. The review finds that AI tools trained predominantly on high-resource languages risk marginalizing low-resource languages such as Dari and Pashto, and that governance models assuming dedicated oversight offices do not transfer to capacity-constrained institutions. The paper contributes a context-sensitive, evidence-informed framework and a transparent, reproducible search protocol for future empirical validation in developing-country and conflict-affected higher-education settings.

papers.title: AI Literacy, Attitudes and Perceived Technological Competence as Correlates of Pre-Service Teachers’ Beliefs About the Professional Relevance of AI: A Latent Mediation Analysis for Sustainable Teacher Education
papers.authors: Mesut Tabuk, Barış Çetin
papers.abstract: Preparing pre-service teachers to use artificial intelligence (AI) critically and equitably is part of the quality-education agenda of Sustainable Development Goal 4. Within a framework informed by the theory of planned behaviour, this study examined how AI literacy is associated with pre-service teachers’ belief that AI will play an important role in the teaching profession, and whether a gender difference in this belief runs through attitudes and perceived technological competence. Data from 493 pre-service teachers at one Turkish faculty were analysed with a latent structural equation model for ordinal indicators. Within this model, the association between self-reported AI literacy competence and the belief ran predominantly through positive attitude (indirect β = 0.20) and secondarily through perceived competence (β = 0.07). Ethical understanding was associated with stronger concerns about AI (β = 0.30). Women held a weaker belief than men (standardised difference = −0.28), a difference statistically accounted for mainly by lower positive attitude, with weaker evidence for perceived competence. Coefficients were stable across specifications. Because the design is cross-sectional and single-institution, the associations are not causal and require replication; they suggest that equitable AI preparation may be better targeted at positive experience with AI and perceived competence than at demographic categories.

papers.title: Evaluation of Algorithmic Carbon Footprint and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools in Environmental Education Programs: Systematic Review
papers.authors: Verónica Vera Vera, Sonnya Patricia Mendoza Lombana, Ana Gabriela Balseca Vaca, Wilson Alexander Zambrano Vélez
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in educational settings creates pedagogical opportunities while raising environmental concerns regarding data center energy consumption and physical infrastructure footprint. This systematic review synthesizes scientific evidence on the algorithmic carbon footprint of AI tools implemented in environmental education programs. Adhering to the PRISMA 2020 statement and an adapted PICoS framework (Population: educational stakeholders; Phenomenon of interest: AI carbon/energy auditing; Context: environmental/sustainability education; Study design: empirical and theoretical studies), systematic searches were conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and ERIC up to 6 August 2026. Seven studies met the eligibility criteria: 5 empirical, 1 scoping review, and 1 theoretical-conceptual synthesis. Quality appraisal utilized MMAT (2018 version) for primary empirical studies and an adapted SANRA (2019 version) for non-empirical documents, followed by qualitative narrative synthesis. Results indicate that, within the reviewed corpus (n = 7), studies predominantly examine conversational agents and large language models (LLMs) applied to sustainability education, while highlighting a critical measurement gap regarding the empirical auditing of energy consumption and physical infrastructure during model training and inference. Conceptual frameworks synthesized across non-empirical literature hypothesize a potential misalignment between educational content promoting planetary conservation and the environmental opacity of underlying technological deployments. Key limitations include inferential fragility due to a small, methodologically heterogeneous evidence base restricted to higher education settings. This review was funded by Universidad Estatal Península de Santa Elena (grant Fcm_012) and hosted on the Open Science Framework project repository (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/AD6TM), with its formal frozen protocol registration archived under DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/KBWFS.

papers.title: A Living Laboratory Producing Agroecological Knowledge Since the 1960s: The Comarca Andina of North Patagonia, Argentina
papers.authors: Manuela T. Fernandez, Verónica Andrea El Mujtar, Fabio Daniel Trinco, S. Hara, Silvana López, Andrea Cardozo, A. E., Pablo Adrián Tittonell
papers.abstract: Living Labs (LLs) are often described as top-down, formally designed innovation spaces, and literature about LL research highlights scarce reports of LLs in Latin America. However, grassroots territorial-innovation spaces exist in Latin America, and we hypothesized that some of them probably agree with the LL framework. The Comarca Andina del Paralelo 42 (CAP42), located in north Patagonia, Argentina, has already seen the emergence of agroecology and organic farming in the 1960s. We considered the CAP42 as a case study for our research. We applied a multidisciplinary approach combining socio-cultural and environmental assessment at the landscape level. We revealed that interacting institutional and cultural factors have shaped the region into a site of agroecological co-innovation, and that agroecological innovation and knowledge co-creation have emerged as bottom-up, non-formalized, long-term process. The assessment of environmental indicators (forest cover loss, land use-related changes of soil properties, etc.) provided evidence for the sustainability of the CAP42 landscape. Forest cover loss observed in the last two decades (2000–2023) was mainly linked to fires rather than agricultural expansion or intensive livestock production. The CAP42 covers the three-layer network approach and place defined in the LL framework, as it is a real-world learning and innovation space enabling multi-actor co-development of context-specific solutions, through multiple forms of knowledge co-creation that align with current LL definitions. It also illustrates that sustainable, long-lasting LLs may result from historically constructed conditions, providing key insights for the development of future LLs.

papers.title: Prioritizing Renewal Needs of Existing Student Dormitories Through Asymmetric Impact Analysis of Environmental Attributes on Residential Satisfaction
papers.authors: Jianfa Qiu, Ruiyu Wang, Ying Bao, Yunye Cao
papers.abstract: The sustainable renewal of existing university student dormitories requires effective identification of occupant-perceived improvement needs to support targeted interventions and efficient resource allocation. This study develops a renewal need prioritization framework by integrating explainable machine learning and impact-asymmetry analysis (IAA). Based on 1507 valid questionnaires from 10 campuses of seven universities in Guangdong Province, an XGBoost-SHAP model was used to identify key environmental attributes influencing overall satisfaction, followed by IAA to examine their asymmetric effects. The results show that: (1) 17 key attributes were identified from 42 indicators, of which 15 met the criteria for IAA classification and exhibited distinct asymmetric effects; (2) a five-level renewal need prioritization framework was established, with per capita usable area, bathroom type, storage space, study and discussion space, damp and mold prevention, and sound insulation identified as core renewal needs; and (3) improving residential unit comfort through spatial optimization, furniture configuration, and environmental enhancement is an important pathway for enhancing occupant well-being and the long-term adaptability of existing dormitory buildings. This study provides empirical evidence for prioritizing existing dormitory renewal and allocating limited resources more efficiently, contributing to the sustainability of existing university residential environments.

papers.title: Tablet-Camera Iris Landmarks and EEG/PPG-Derived Arousal Indices During Naturalistic Reading: Geometric Confounding and Exploratory Within-Subject Associations
papers.authors: Sujin Ko, JAEPYO PARK, Jing Zhang, Dongkook Kim, Moonsook Kim
papers.abstract: Arousal, the activation dimension of the valence–arousal circumplex, indexes alertness and engagement independently of pleasantness. We evaluated whether MediaPipe FaceLandmarker iris landmark distances from a tablet camera estimate electroencephalography (EEG)- and photoplethysmography (PPG)-derived arousal markers during naturalistic reading. Recordings from 48 participants yielded 43,923 thirty-second windows. Raw iris distances correlated with EEG alpha (r=+0.118) and theta (r=+0.076), but face scale explained 93% of their variance. After face-width normalisation, alpha remained associated (r=+0.076), whereas theta was not statistically significant. Further adjustment for ocular luminance and head pose rendered alpha nonsignificant (r=+0.021, p=0.33). Circular-shift testing identified alpha coupling in 11/48 participants under full control, versus 28/48 using uncorrected Pearson tests. Within-subject Ridge regression, with no raw sample shared between the training and test windows, yielded a nonsignificant group mean correlation (r=+0.078, p=0.07); 13/48 participants had individually significant prediction–reference associations (11 positive), fewer when the PPG term was restricted to filter-consistent beats. Both counts are exploratory, nominal and uncorrected across participants, and come from different analyses. Neither establishes prospective monitoring performance, and the study does not validate the landmark distance as a pupil measure.

papers.title: Students’ Perceptions of ChatGPT Explanation Quality and Learning Confidence: Evidence from Physics Learning
papers.authors: Muhammad Aizri Fadillah, Usmeldi Usmeldi, Festiyed Festiyed, Asrizal Asrizal
papers.abstract: The increasing use of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, has transformed how students access academic and learning support. However, empirical evidence remains limited regarding which perceived characteristics of ChatGPT explanations are associated with students’ learning confidence when the tool is used in subject-specific learning contexts. This study examined how different perceived characteristics of ChatGPT explanations were associated with students’ learning confidence, using physics learning as the subject-specific context. A quantitative survey was conducted involving 167 Indonesian high school students who had prior experience using ChatGPT for physics learning. The study used a structured questionnaire measuring four perceived characteristics of ChatGPT explanations and three indicators of task-specific confidence in physics learning. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression. Descriptive findings showed that female students reported slightly higher evaluations of ChatGPT explanation quality and learning confidence than male students across all measured indicators. The three regression models were statistically significant, explaining 61.3%, 56.6%, and 57.1% of the variance in confidence in understanding physics concepts, explaining concepts to others, and facing physics examinations, respectively. Perceived support for understanding fundamental physics principles was positively associated with all three confidence indicators, while perceived accuracy in explaining real-life applications showed the strongest association with examination confidence. Perceived simplification of difficult concepts was significantly associated only with examination confidence, whereas comparative ease of understanding relative to textbooks was not significantly associated with this outcome. These findings indicate that students’ learning confidence is differentially associated with specific perceived characteristics of ChatGPT explanations. The study provides preliminary evidence of how students’ perceptions of conceptual support, real-life application, simplification, and comparative ease of understanding relate to task-specific confidence. However, the findings do not establish the objective quality of ChatGPT explanations or demonstrate improvements in conceptual understanding or learning performance.

papers.title: AI-Powered Personal Tutors as a Scalable Solution to the 2-Sigma Problem in Pharmacy Education
papers.authors: Maria Victoria Tejada-Simon
papers.abstract: Background: The “2 Sigma Problem”, where individualized tutoring outperforms conventional instruction by two standard deviations, remains a persistent challenge in large-enrollment pharmacy courses. Generative AI tutors, constrained to instructor-verified content, offer a scalable, equitable approximation of personalized support. Methods: Four course-specific AI tutors were deployed across first-year (P1; n = 108–119/cohort) and third-year (P3; n = 98–108/cohort) Doctor of Pharmacy cohorts (Fall 2024–Spring 2026) using ChatGPT-4o and PlayLab with retrieval-augmented generation. Effectiveness was evaluated through longitudinal grade analysis, American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy proficiency outcomes, satisfaction surveys, and anonymized interaction log analysis. Results: Engagement was heterogeneous across curricular formats: 15-week P1 courses supported sustained weekly usage for foundational concept reinforcement, whereas 4-week P3 modules exhibited lower, targeted utilization focused on rapid self-assessment. In P1 Biochemistry, tutor integration was associated with longitudinal cohort exam improvements. The overall targeted metabolism exam mean rose from 74.0% (Fall 2023, no AI) to 81.4% (Fall 2024, AI tutor) and 83.6% (Fall 2025, AI tutor), with active users (n = 16, 85%, Fall 2024) outperforming non-users (n = 16, 79.3%, Fall 2024) by 5.7 percentage points, and with higher mean scores observed across progressively higher usage tiers. AACP proficiency means increased from 77.9% to 82.1%, exceeding the 80% benchmark. In P1 Physiology and P3 modules, cohort performance remained consistently high (83.7–88.2%), maintaining AACP benchmark proficiency across all observation cycles. Student perceptions were positive regarding conceptual clarification and adaptive explanations. Conclusions: Curriculum-aligned AI tutors represent a viable strategy for approximating individualized instruction in pharmacy courses. Course-specific AI tutors demonstrate feasibility across PharmD curricula, functioning as continuous retrieval-practice tools in foundational sciences and as targeted self-assessment aids in accelerated modules. Educational benefits and adoption dynamics are moderated by curricular pace, subject complexity, and assessment structures, highlighting key considerations for broader health sciences implementation.

papers.title: Institutional Readiness and the Boundaries of AI Adoption: Evidence from UAE Newsrooms
papers.authors: Elsayed Bekhit Darwish, Ahmed S. Mansoori
papers.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in newsroom operations, organizations invest in AI readiness on the assumption that preparedness travels with successful outcomes. Readiness frameworks typically aggregate diverse outcomes into composite performance measures, leaving it unclear whether readiness explains each equally well. This study examines the explanatory scope of institutional AI readiness in UAE newsrooms using a cross-sectional survey of a purposive sample of 336 media professionals. Three collection streams were harmonized and outcomes analyzed separately rather than aggregated. The seven readiness indicators showed high internal consistency (α = 0.919) and a dominant first component accounting for 67.7% of item variance; the four conceptual domains behind the instrument were not recovered as separable dimensions, a pattern that may partly reflect a general evaluative disposition toward the organization. A one-standard-deviation increase in readiness was associated with 2.59 times higher odds of deeper adoption (95% CI [1.88, 3.56]) and with greater training provision and perceived return on AI investment, but not with practitioners’ perceived quality of Arabic-language AI output, measured with a single item (ρ = 0.097). Because one readiness indicator concerns current AI use, all estimates were re-estimated without it: the odds ratio was 2.38 (95% CI [1.74, 3.25]), the organizational associations remained significant, and the association with perceived Arabic-language output quality remained non-significant (ρ = 0.095). Institutional readiness, therefore, appears to have a bounded explanatory domain in these data, showing stronger associations with organizational implementation outcomes than with perceived output quality. Because the design is cross-sectional and not all respondents answered outcome items, these are statements of association, not of effect. Studies relying on composite measures may overstate their explanatory reach.

papers.title: A Perspective on Advanced Wood Manufacturing: A Decision-Centric Framework for Future Research and Education
papers.authors: Vahid Nasir
papers.journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
papers.abstract: For over a century, wood manufacturing has been organized around understanding the material and process and optimizing the product. It established a globally successful industry and enabled efficient production of traditional and engineered wood products. This manufacturing practice is now being challenged by the complexity of resource variability, product diversification, mass customization, and rapid technology integration. This perspective proposes Advanced Wood Manufacturing as a decision-centric smart manufacturing ecosystem that integrates Resource Intelligence, Manufacturing Intelligence, Product Intelligence, and System Intelligence through a unifying Decision Intelligence framework to convert variability into high-value manufacturing decisions. We argue that natural resource variability, while requiring control where necessary for reliable production, can also provide decision-relevant information for adaptive manufacturing and value creation. The product space of wood manufacturing extends far beyond lumber and panels into emerging functional products for energy storage, flexible electronics, and biomedical applications, enabled by artificial intelligence, sensing and digitalization, robotics, computational design, and additive manufacturing. Sustainability, resilience, and human-centricity are positioned not as peripheral considerations but as foundational design principles embedded in manufacturing system architecture. This perspective offers a vision for future research and education and proposes that the field’s next generation of value will come from integration across resource, process, product, and system intelligence rather than from further optimization within existing boundaries.

papers.title: Clinical Outcomes, Risk Communication, and Follow-Up After Living Kidney Donation: A Retrospective Observational Cohort Study
papers.authors: Mahdi Tarabeih, Jamal A. S. Qaddumi, Osama Sawalmeh, Sajeda Hamadi
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Living kidney donation expands access to transplantation, but donor safety requires effective risk communication and sustained surveillance. We evaluated renal and cardiometabolic changes after donation in conjunction with donor-reported risk communication and follow-up. Methods: This observational cohort study included 91 living kidney donors with paired assessments before donation and 16–18 months after nephrectomy; the analytic cohort included only donors for whom both paired clinical assessments were available. Outcomes included serum creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), weight, body mass index (BMI), and blood pressure; counseling and follow-up were assessed retrospectively using a structured questionnaire of donor-reported recall, administered at the post-donation assessment. Changes were summarized as median paired changes with interquartile ranges for non-normally distributed outcomes and as mean paired changes with t-based 95% confidence intervals for normally distributed outcomes; the multiplicity of the six paired comparisons was addressed using a conservative Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold (0.05/6 = 0.0083). Results: Serum creatinine increased by a median of 0.24 mg/dL, and eGFR had a mean paired change of −22.49 mL/min/1.73 m2 (95% CI −23.16 to −21.83; t(90) = −67.265; p < 0.001). Weight (median +5.0 kg), BMI (median +1.4 kg/m2), systolic blood pressure (median +4.0 mmHg), and diastolic blood pressure (mean +5.68 mmHg) also increased (all p < 0.001; significant under the Bonferroni threshold). No donor had an eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 at follow-up. Only 15.4% considered long-term complications adequate, 6.6% recalled counseling regarding future chronic kidney disease or end-stage renal disease, and 19.8% reported regular nephrology follow-up. Conclusions: Although reduced eGFR is an expected physiological consequence of nephrectomy, concurrent increases in weight and blood pressure observed during follow-up warrant surveillance. Donor-reported gaps in recall of risk communication and in reported follow-up support standardized informed consent, individualized counseling, verification of understanding, and structured long-term multidisciplinary care to strengthen donor safety and continuity across transplant programs, nephrology, and primary care services; because the design was observational, without a non-donor comparator, and counseling outcomes were based on donor recall, these findings should be interpreted as associations and reported care gaps rather than evidence of causation.

papers.title: Novel Genetic Variants of the CHD2 Gene in cis Position in a Patient with Epileptic Encephalopathy: A Case Report and In Silico Analysis of the Impact of the Variants on the Protein
papers.authors: Andrey S. Zuev, Е. А. Фонова, Daria S. Kuznetsova, В. А. Степанов, Nikolay Alekseevich Skryabin
papers.abstract: CHD2-related neurodevelopmental disorders are increasingly recognized as a distinct group of epileptic encephalopathies with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. Here, we report a 12-year-old female patient with pharmacoresistant epilepsy, mild cognitive impairment (IQ = 56), and extraneurological features including grade II kyphoscoliosis and planovalgus foot deformity. Video-EEG monitoring revealed a phenotype consistent with Jeavons syndrome, characterized by daily eyelid myoclonia with absences and marked photosensitivity with an eye closure sensitivity (ECS) phenomenon. Molecular genetic testing via whole-exome and Sanger sequencing identified two novel variants in the CHD2 gene (NM_001271.4): c.1634T>G (p.Leu545Arg) and c.3810G>C (p.Leu1270Phe). Long-read nanopore sequencing confirmed their de novo status and cis-positioning on the paternal allele. Structural bioinformatic analysis using AlphaFold3, FoldX/mCSM (v5.0 package), UCSF ChimeraX (v1.10.1), and PyMOL (v3.1.8) demonstrated that both variants individually destabilize the CHD2 protein, with a cumulative destabilizing effect when combined: p.Leu545Arg affects the ATP-binding domain, whereas p.Leu1270Phe disrupts hydrophobic packing within the C-terminal DNA-binding domain. These findings suggest accelerated protein degradation as a potential disease mechanism. Our data support the pathogenicity of these heterozygous cis-variants and implicate CHD2 haploinsufficiency as the leading etiopathogenic mechanism, though distinct domain-specific effects of each substitution may also contribute to the complex molecular synergy observed in this case.

papers.title: Six- and 12-Month Post-Intervention Outcomes of a Nurse Practitioner-Led Interdisciplinary Obesity Clinic for Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Rural Australia: A Randomised Controlled Trial
papers.authors: Wenyong Wang, Michelle Kilpatrick, Iain Kilpatrick Robertson, Giuliana O. Murfet
papers.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
papers.abstract: Background: Sustaining weight and glycaemic improvements after structured obesity care ends is challenging. This study assessed 6- and 12-month post-intervention outcomes of a nurse practitioner-led interdisciplinary obesity clinic. Methods: In this unblinded randomised controlled trial, 224 rural Australian adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity were allocated to the 24-month AMOS intervention (n = 113) or standard diabetes care (n = 111). Outcomes at 6- and 12-months post-intervention were analysed using mixed-effects linear regression, with multiple imputation for missing data. The trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12622000240741). Results: Compared with standard care, the intervention group maintained greater reductions at 6 months post-intervention in body weight (−13.5 kg; 95% CI: −16.8 to −10.1), BMI (−4.6 kg/m2; 95% CI: −5.7 to −3.5) and HbA1c (−0.53 percentage points; 95% CI: −0.97 to −0.09). Differences remained at 12 months for body weight (−11.8 kg; 95% CI: −15.2 to −8.5), BMI (−4.1 kg/m2; 95% CI: −5.2 to −3.0) and HbA1c (−0.75 percentage points; 95% CI: −1.19 to −0.31). Physical quality of life remained higher; other metabolic outcomes were inconsistent. Conclusions: Greater reductions in weight and HbA1c persisted at 12 months after the multidisciplinary AMOS intervention ended, supporting the potential value of integrated obesity treatment within diabetes care.

papers.title: Predicting Students’ Eligibility for Higher Education from Teachers’ Leadership Behaviors and Students’ Perceived Stress
papers.authors: Anna Öqvist, Malin Malmström
papers.abstract: Little evidence exists on the factors that enable students in upper secondary school to achieve eligibility for higher education. This lack of knowledge limits educators’ and policymakers’ opportunities to identify students who may require additional educational support before graduation. In this study, we apply machine learning to predict students’ eligibility for higher education using survey data from 272 Swedish students in upper secondary school. Our results show that students’ eligibility for higher education can be predicted with an average accuracy of 85.5%. Program type emerged as the strongest predictor, while teacher leadership behaviors and students’ perceived stress also contributed to the prediction model. Among the teacher leadership behaviors, performance-oriented and supportive leadership showed the highest predictive importance. In addition, students’ perceived stress related to the risk of not completing their studies emerged as an important predictor of eligibility. With this study, we extend previous research on predicting educational outcomes by focusing on students’ eligibility for higher education and by integrating theoretically grounded measures of teacher leadership behavior and students’ perceived stress into prediction models. Furthermore, we contribute to the growing discussion on the role of teacher leadership behavior and students’ perceived stress in predicting students’ progression towards higher education and demonstrate the potential of machine learning to support the early identification of students who may require additional educational support.

papers.title: 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN)
papers.authors: Marco Enrico Sguanci, Lea Godino, Anna Grimaldi, Giulio La Ferrara, Giovanni Cangelosi, Sara Morales Palomares, Stefano Mancin, on behalf of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN) Board of Directors
papers.abstract: The 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN), held in Bologna, Italy, from 4 to 6 May 2026, provided a national forum for discussion on the evolving role of nursing in nephrology. The Congress was preceded by a dedicated pre-congress session focused on education, research, and clinical practice, with particular attention to the involvement of nursing students and early-career professionals in scientific activities. Across plenary sessions, round tables, workshops, oral communications, and digital poster presentations, the scientific programme addressed major areas of contemporary nephrology nursing, including professional development, patient-centred care, vascular access management, dialysis technologies, kidney transplantation, symptom management, home and community care, digital health, artificial intelligence, sustainability, and nutritional care. Particular attention was given to the integration of evidence-based practice, clinical expertise, technological innovation, interprofessional collaboration, and patient education. This Conference Proceedings provides an overview of the scientific and educational activities of the meeting and brings together the accepted contributions presented during both the pre-congress session and the main Congress. Collectively, these contributions illustrate the diversity and continued development of nephrology nursing practice and research in Italy and highlight the importance of scientific societies in promoting professional competence, knowledge exchange, and innovation in kidney care.

papers.title: Perceived Multi-Level Diabetes Protective and Risk Factors Associated with Food and Dietary Acculturation Patterns Among East African Immigrants in the United States
papers.authors: H. Muhdi B. Hi Ibrahim, Angela U. Ekwonye, Salma Ibrahim, Nimo Mohamed, Muna Shidane, Artam Enayat, Melika Espahbodi
papers.abstract: Background: Upon arrival in a new country, immigrants have lower body mass index (BMI), and are less likely to be overweight and obese than natives. However, longer residence is associated with higher BMI, partly attributed to adoption of unhealthy diets and dietary habits. Overweight and obesity (primary risk factors for diabetes) have been associated with food acculturation—the process by which immigrants adopt food practices of their new country. In particular, unfamiliar food cultures and food purchasing environment, lack of knowledge on how to prepare and incorporate new foods in traditional diets, perceptions towards food in new countries, all limit immigrants’ food choices and access. However, very few food acculturation studies have focused on African immigrants, specifically from eastern Africa. Yet, this group reports high rates of overweight, obesity, and higher prevalence of diabetes and pre-diabetes. Using the socioecological framework, this study explored the multi-level facilitators and barriers associated with food and dietary acculturation patterns and perceived diabetes-related health risks among East African immigrants and refugees in the Twin Cities Metro Area, Minnesota, United States. Methods: Six semi-structured focus groups were conducted with 36 Somali and Ethiopian women in the summer and fall of 2025. Participants represented Somali, Oromo and Amharic speakers. Only women were recruited with the assumption that women are the primary food decision makers and preparers in these communities.
