Methods Ninety adults were enrolled, 47 with normal weight, 18 with overweight, and 25 with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m 2 ). Primary inferential analyses included participants with normal weight and obesity ( N = 72); participants with overweight were excluded. Participants completed questionnaires assessing perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale, PSS), hedonic hunger (Power of Food Scale), trait food craving (Food Craving Questionnaire-Trait reduced), and uncontrolled eating (Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire). PSS Helplessness and Self-Efficacy subscales were derived. Associations were examined using Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and current hunger. Helplessness and Self-Efficacy were entered simultaneously to estimate independent associations with reward-driven eating outcomes. PROCESS moderation analyses tested whether BMI or BMI-defined weight status influenced the association. Results In the primary analysis sample, PSS Total was not independently associated with any reward-driven eating outcome after correction for multiple testing. In contrast, Helplessness was independently associated with greater hedonic hunger, food craving, and uncontrolled eating after FDR correction, whereas Self-Efficacy was not independently associated with any outcome after accounting for Helplessness. In subgroup analyses, associations were descriptively more consistent among participants with obesity than those with normal weight. However, no interaction effect remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Conclusion These findings highlight Helplessness, reflecting, perceived uncontrollability, as the perceived stress dimension most consistently associated with reward-driven eating and underscore the importance of distinguishing between stress dimensions rather than relying solely on overall perceived stress. There was no robust evidence in the present study that BMI or BMI-defined weight status modified these associations. Perceived uncontrollability may represent a potential target for interventions aimed at reducing maladaptive reward-driven eating behavior.

papers.title: Effects of high-intensity interval training on negative affect in adolescents with obesity: an exploratory analysis of the role of self-efficacy
papers.authors: Shihao Wang, Chang Liu, Yali Xu
papers.abstract: Objective To investigate the effects of an 8-week school-based high-intensity interval training (HIIT) program on body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, negative affect, and self-efficacy in adolescents with obesity, and to explore whether self-efficacy statistically mediates the association between HIIT and negative affect. Methods In this two-arm, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial, 55 adolescents with obesity (age 13.55 ± 1.21 years; BMI 29.58 ± 3.54 kg/m 2 ) were randomly assigned to an experimental group (HIIT, n = 27) or a control group (regular physical education, n = 28). Body composition, estimated maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max), negative affect (PANAS), and self-efficacy (GSES) were assessed before and after the 8-week intervention. The primary analyses were analyses of covariance (ANCOVA) with the post-intervention value as the dependent variable, group as the fixed factor, and the corresponding baseline value as the covariate; two-way repeated-measures ANOVAs (group×time) served as sensitivity analyses. An exploratory mediation analysis with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples adjusted for baseline mediator, baseline outcome, sex, and age. Results After adjustment for baseline values, the experimental group showed significantly lower post-intervention negative affect than the control group (adjusted difference −3.72, 95% CI [−4.81, −2.63], p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.475) and significantly higher self-efficacy (adjusted difference 1.06, 95% CI [0.60, 1.53], p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.290). Body weight, BMI, visceral fat mass, subcutaneous fat mass, body fat percentage, and fat mass were also significantly lower in the experimental group (all p < 0.001), and estimated VO₂max was higher (adjusted difference 1.54 mL/kg/min, 95% CI [0.86, 2.22], p < 0.001); the latter effect was attenuated but remained significant when post-intervention estimated VO₂max was recomputed with baseline BMI held constant (0.50, 95% CI [0.03, 0.98], p = 0.040), and was corroborated by the BMI-free 20-m shuttle-run lap count ( p = 0.004). The exploratory mediation analysis did not support an indirect effect through self-efficacy (a × b = 0.09, bootstrap 95% CI [−0.75, 0.82]). Conclusion Eight weeks of school-based HIIT improved body composition and estimated cardiorespiratory fitness, reduced negative affect, and enhanced self-efficacy in adolescents with obesity. The indirect effect through self-efficacy was not statistically supported after baseline adjustment; because the mediator and the outcome were measured concurrently, temporal ordering cannot be established, and the mediating role of self-efficacy remains an open question for longitudinal research.

papers.title: Review on unobtrusive estimation of team processes underlying team situation awareness: shared mental models and team coordination
papers.authors: Emanuela Zhecheva, Eric L. Groen, Pim Haselager, Anne-Marie Brouwer
papers.abstract: Introduction Team situation awareness (SA) is essential for effective team performance. Yet, current methods rely on potentially biased self-reports and obtrusive tools such as task probes. Objective, unobtrusive, and continuous methods for monitoring team SA could support its improvement. In contrast to individual SA, unobtrusive measures of team SA have not been systematically reviewed. Because team SA is an umbrella concept, we adapted a framework proposed by Salmon et al., identifying two components that can potentially be measured unobtrusively: shared mental models (SMMs) and team coordination. This systematic review examines behavioural and physiological technologies that may enable unobtrusive measurement of these components. Methods We conducted a systematic literature review of studies investigating behavioural technologies, such as verbal communication and eye-tracking, and physiological technologies, such as electroencephalography, for unobtrusive measurement of team SMMs and coordination. We searched Web of Science (May and July 2025) for relevant literature published between 2000 and 2025. We included peer-reviewed articles published in English. In total, 19 studies addressing team SMMs and 33 addressing team coordination were included. We extracted sample and team size, task environment, operationalisation of team SMMs and coordination, and their relationship with unobtrusive measures. Results Cardiac measures (42%) and verbal communication (47%) were most popular for estimating team SMMs, while functional near-infrared spectroscopy (27%) and cardiac measures (30%) were most popular for estimating team coordination. Interpersonal synchrony—the temporal contiguity and interdependence of physiological and/or behavioural activity between teammates—was applied in 70% of team coordination studies. Studies covered diverse tasks and settings, from laboratory-based cognitive tasks and controlled physical tasks to real-world environments, including surgery. Various methods were used to operationalise SMMs and coordination, including participant experience, expert assessment, and self-reports. Discussion Findings suggest that team SMMs and coordination cannot be measured as single, unified constructs using one unobtrusive measure. Instead, different measures may provide information about specific aspects of these processes. Future research should begin with task analysis to identify relevant aspects of team SA and derive appropriate measures for the specific task environment. Task-related behavioural actions also represent a potentially valuable, yet often overlooked, category of unobtrusive measures. A key limitation is the substantial variation in how SMMs and coordination were operationalised and measured, making direct comparisons difficult. Future work should investigate how identified measures relate directly to team SA using validated measures.

papers.title: Advances in artificial intelligence for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis of neurological diseases: a systematic literature review
papers.authors: Batyrkhan Omarov
papers.abstract: Background Brain imaging is central to the structural, functional, metabolic, and neurophysiological characterization of neurological disease, yet interpretation remains constrained by heterogeneity in acquisition, annotation, expertise, and clinical context. Objective This systematic literature review evaluates recent artificial intelligence approaches for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis, with emphasis on methods, modalities, neurological diseases, diagnostic tasks, datasets, validation practices, and translational limitations. Methods The review followed PRISMA 2020 and covered peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2020 through June 2026. Eight information sources were searched using database-specific terms for artificial intelligence, neuroimaging, neurological disease, and diagnostic analysis. The search identified 1,078 records; 236 duplicates were removed, 842 unique records were screened, 258 full texts were assessed, and 123 studies were included after a record-level eligibility re-audit. Heterogeneous evidence was synthesized narratively and by descriptive mapping rather than meta-analysis. Results MRI was frequently represented in the included studies and auxiliary mapping data; CT was commonly used in acute stroke and intracranial hemorrhage; PET supported selected molecular and differential-diagnosis studies; fMRI and diffusion imaging were used for network and white-matter analysis; and EEG extended the scope to neurophysiological diagnosis. CNN and three-dimensional networks were commonly reported, while attention, Transformer, graph, self-supervised, generative, multimodal, and foundation-model approaches appeared in selected recent studies. Stroke, dementia, and brain tumors were frequently represented, but heterogeneous populations, outcomes, and incomplete validation extraction precluded ranking diseases, modalities, architectures, or validation strategies. Conclusion The evidence suggests movement from task-specific pattern recognition toward multimodal and context-rich decision support in selected settings, but it does not establish uniform methodological superiority or clinical maturity. Dependable translation requires patient-level data governance, transparent reporting, uncertainty estimation, independent multicenter testing, prospective workflow evaluation, and clinically meaningful endpoints.

papers.title: Federated Spiking GANs with Rényi Differential Privacy for privacy-preserving synthetic EEG generation in brain–computer interfaces
papers.authors: Shouvik Paul, Garima Bajwa
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) data used in brain-computer and brain-machine interfaces (BCI/BMI) contain sensitive, user-specific information, creating privacy risks in consumer applications such as gaming, human augmentation, and virtual reality. Existing methods like encryption and anonymization either fail to protect data during analysis or still expose identifiable attributes. While differential privacy (DP) offers formal protection, it often reduces data utility. The key challenge is to generate synthetic EEG data that protects sensitive attributes while retaining temporal features for downstream use. To address this, we developed a federated spiking generative framework that integrates a spiking neural network (SNN)-based generator, temporally correlated noise, an artificial neural network (ANN)-based discriminator, and Rényi differential privacy (RDP) within a federated learning framework. The SNN-based generator captures temporal characteristics, and the ANN-based discriminator maintains classification accuracy. Federated training prevents centralization of raw client data, while privacy is preserved through controlled perturbation of spike-train and membrane-potential representations, supported by RDP-based privacy accounting. We evaluated our architecture against methods such as RDP-TimeGAN, RDP-CRNN-GAN, RDP-RCGAN, and RDP-Clare-GAN, demonstrating that our approach preserves temporal features and downstream utility while maintaining privacy in synthetic EEG generation. This solution enables privacy-preserving generation of distributed synthetic EEG data for BCI/BMI research and development.

papers.title: A two-stage RAG-LLM pipeline for roadmapping neuroscience research in operational environments
papers.authors: Cara A. Spencer
papers.abstract: Introduction Neuroscientific research and applications in real world environments are often constrained by limited access, equipment limitations, and high costs. Consequently, robustly selecting constructs to focus effort on is a high-impact task. Method This study introduces a two-stage large language model (LLM) pipeline that generates research roadmaps from existing real-world data to inform research priorities in the field, given the state of the art. Stage 1 uses retrieval-augmented generation on operational logs to identify candidate psychological, social, and neurocognitive constructs and map their co-occurrence. Stage 2 evaluates how well these constructs are represented in the literature across four dimensions that commonly inform prioritization: ecological validity, neural correlates, biosensor protocols, and brain computer interface readiness, producing an evidence gap matrix. Pipeline evaluation combined human review, deterministic computations, and human-LLM alignment analysis. Results Applying the pipeline to Mars Desert Research Station logs, Stage 1 identified 19 constructs. Stage 2 highlighted critical gaps in neuroimaging and measurement protocols, particularly for social domains, thereby identifying potential research priorities and risks. Discussion This methodology offers a generalizable starting point for synthesizing operational logs into actionable research roadmaps, but the evaluation showed it still required human scrutiny.

papers.title: Neurologist-focused workflows for immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome in CAR T-cell therapy and CD3-engaging bispecific antibodies
papers.authors: Walid Alesefir, Mariam Hejazi, Basil Alashger, Abdulrahman Abodahab, Menna Abdelrazek, Karma Abouelnaga, Sara Koudeimati, Abdullah Alshibani, Lara Aljohani
papers.abstract: Objective To synthesize current evidence into a neurologist-focused workflow for early recognition, bedside monitoring, diagnostic triage, mitigation, and therapy-specific surveillance of immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar were searched in English from inception through 25 March 2026. Of 201 records, 18 duplicates were removed, 183 were screened, 157 full texts were assessed, and 26 studies were included in a narrative synthesis. The selection process was reported using applicable PRISMA 2020 elements and the narrative presentation was evaluated using SANRA. Results Evidence supports early neurologic co-management in selected high-risk patients, serial language- and attention-sensitive bedside assessment, and clinically triggered rather than routine electroencephalography. Pilot neurocognitive data suggest that subtle decline may precede deterioration on the Immune Effector Cell-Associated Encephalopathy (ICE) score. Bispecific-antibody programs generally show lower neurotoxicity burdens than many CAR T-cell platforms but create repeated risk windows around step-up dosing and outpatient transition. Delayed B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-associated movement and neurocognitive syndromes remain an important safety signal, although therapeutic evidence is largely observational or case based. Conclusion The evidence supports documenting a baseline neurologic phenotype, performing serial bedside monitoring, deploying electroencephalography and neuroimaging when results may change management, and maintaining product-specific vigilance for delayed syndromes. Tiered pathways are needed for community and resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study
papers.authors: Hajed M. Al-Otaibi, Husam I. Alahmadi, Malik A Althobiani, Kannan Sridharan, Abdullah A. Alqarni, Ghazi Alotaibi
papers.abstract: Background Spirometry is one of the most used pulmonary function tests for assessing respiratory function and diagnosing ventilatory disorders in clinical practice. Evaluation of test validity and interpretation is typically performed by trained healthcare professionals. The present study aims to evaluate the capability of a publicly available large language model (LLM) to perform quality assurance and interpretations of spirometry tests. Methods A total of 150 spirometry tests were retrospectively collected from the pulmonary function laboratories. The spirometry tests were evaluated for acceptability and interpreted by clinicians according to ATS/ERS recommendations as part of standard clinical practice. Subsequently, a publicly available LLM (ChatGPT 5.5) was prompted to evaluate the acceptability and interpret the same spirometry tests according to ATS/ERS criteria. The model interpreted each spirometry test on three separate occasions for assessing reproducibility. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were calculated by comparing LLM assessments with clinician assessments of spirometry test acceptability and interpretation. Results For spirometry acceptability evaluation, ChatGPT demonstrated an overall accuracy of 87% (95% CI: 81%-92%), sensitivity of 91% (95% CI: 85%-95%), specificity of 61% (95% CI 39%-80%), PPV of 94% (95% CI: 89%-97%), and NPV of 48(95% CI: 29%-67%) with Cohen's k of 0.46. The spiromteric interpretation agreement with the clinicians reference standard was moderate, with exact agreement of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.54–0.69) while Cohen's Kappa (Unweighted) was 0.47 (95% CI: 0.37–0.56) and Macro F1 score was 0.39 (95% CI: 0.33–0.49). Reproducibility across three independent trials was moderate (Fleiss’ κ 0.58). Class-specific interpretation performance varied by category; sensitivity was highest for normal pattern and restrictive defects (0.72), whereas sensitivity for obstructive defects was 0.27. F1-scores were highest for normal and restrictive defects (0.81 and 0.62, respectively). Conclusion The current findings suggest that ChatGPT 5.5 has a limited capability, at its current stage of development, to serve as a reliable tool for independent spirometry interpretation in clinical practice. Nevertheless, it may serve as an adjunct to clinical decision-making and educational tools. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of large language models for esophageal cancer patient education: quality, reliability, readability, understandability, and actionability
papers.authors: Ying Ying Hang, Rui Yuan, Man Lu, Fang Wen Long, His Quan Hsu, Lu Bai, Jun Qian
papers.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as sources of health information. This study evaluated the quality, reliability, readability, understandability, and actionability of responses generated by three mainstream LLMs to esophageal cancer-related questions. Methods Thirty esophageal cancer-related questions covering six domains were identified from Google Trends, clinical practice guidelines, and social media and submitted to three LLMs, yielding 90 responses. Responses were evaluated using the Global Quality Scale (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP), Quality Assessment of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI), Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT), and six readability indices. Differences among the models were assessed using repeated-measures ANOVA or the Friedman test according to data distribution. Results Crucial information missing was the most common content deficiency (8.9%). Overall GQS, mDISCERN, QAMAI, and EQIP scores were 4.00 (IQR: 4.00–4.00), 4.00 (IQR: 3.50–4.00), 22.00 (IQR: 21.50–25.00), and 71.88 (IQR: 62.50–75.00), respectively. DeepSeek performed best overall, followed by ChatGPT and Doubao. None of the three models met the recommended sixth-grade reading level, and all had PEMAT-A scores below the recommended 70% threshold. Readability was generally not significantly associated with quality or reliability, except for a few weak negative correlations. Conclusions LLMs demonstrated generally favorable quality and reliability when answering esophageal cancer-related questions, but readability and actionability remained limited. They may serve as supplementary tools for patients seeking esophageal cancer-related health information but should not replace professional medical consultation.

papers.title: Reliability and readability of five large language models in answering patient-oriented questions about rectal prolapse: a comparative study
papers.authors: Le Zhang, Lei Liang, Xin Peng, Shihong Liu, Lingli Zhong, Zhenyu Li
papers.abstract: Background Rectal prolapse (RP) is a pelvic floor disorder that can cause rectal protrusion, defecatory dysfunction, and fecal incontinence. Patients increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for health information, yet the reliability and readability of LLM responses to patient-oriented questions about RP remain unclear. Objective To compare the reliability and readability of five LLM platform-model configurations in answering English-language patient-oriented questions about RP. Methods In this web-based cross-sectional study, worldwide Google Trends queries from the preceding 5 years were identified using the MeSH term “rectal prolapse.” Two colorectal specialists screened the queries and standardized them into 15 patient-oriented questions. The questions were submitted to ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, and DeepSeek under standardized single-turn, zero-shot conditions, with one response collected per question from each platform-model configuration. Two independent evaluators assessed the responses using DISCERN, the Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP) instrument, the Global Quality Score (GQS), and the JAMA benchmark criteria. Using evidence-based guidelines and question-specific checklists of key clinical content, the evaluators also independently assessed clinical factual accuracy and completeness and identified potentially harmful recommendations and critical omissions. Readability was evaluated using the Automated Readability Index (ARI), Gunning Fog Index (GFI), Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Coleman-Liau Index (CL), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG), and Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES). Results DISCERN ( P = 0.001), EQIP ( P < 0.001), and JAMA scores ( P < 0.001) differed across configurations, whereas GQS did not ( P = 0.175). ChatGPT and Copilot had the highest median DISCERN scores (44.00 for both), and DeepSeek had the lowest (35.00); ChatGPT and Copilot each scored significantly higher than DeepSeek. Copilot had the highest median EQIP score (80.00), followed by Perplexity (75.00). Median JAMA scores were 1.00 for ChatGPT, Copilot, and Perplexity and 0.00 for Gemini and DeepSeek. All five models had a median GQS of 4.00. The median clinical factual accuracy score was 5.00 (IQR, 5.00–5.00), and 69 of 75 responses (92.0%) were rated fully accurate. Median completeness was 91.7% (IQR, 87.5%–100.0%). No response contained a potentially harmful recommendation; critical omissions were found in 6 of the 50 applicable responses (12.0%). All configurations had median grade-level scores >6 and median FRES <80. No model met the prespecified sixth-grade readability standard. Conclusion The five LLMs generally produced clinically accurate information about RP. No potentially harmful recommendations were identified. Yet information quality and source transparency differed among models, some responses omitted critical clinical information, and readability was poor across all five. LLMs are currently better suited as professionally reviewed adjuncts to patient education than as substitutes for specialist assessment or individualized clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Research progress on bowel preparation regimens before colonoscopy: a narrative review
papers.authors: Xiang Liao, Yu Song, Yazhi He, Zhi Zeng, Shuang Li, Jing Ling
papers.abstract: Adequate bowel preparation is the single most important determinant of colonoscopy quality, yet suboptimal preparation affects up to one-quarter of colonoscopies, leading to repeat procedures, increased health-system costs, and health disparities. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence on bowel preparation regimens through a public health lens, organized around four interconnected dimensions: cleansing efficacy, safety, tolerability, and population-specific applicability. We define and classify preparation regimens by volume (high-volume ≥4 L, low-volume 2–<4 L, ultra-low-volume <2 L) and administration schedule (split-dose, same-day). Low-volume, split-dose formulations achieve non-inferior cleansing efficacy to high-volume 4L polyethylene glycol (PEG) regimens, with improved patient tolerability and compliance. The Boston Bowel Preparation Scale (BBPS) is the most widely adopted assessment instrument; commonly used adequate preparation is defined as total BBPS ≥6 with each segment ≥2, although definitions vary across studies. PEG-based preparations maintain the most favorable safety profile, particularly in patients with renal or cardiovascular comorbidities, while sodium phosphate carries a small but clinically significant risk of acute phosphate nephropathy. Special populations—including older adults with frailty and polypharmacy, patients with inflammatory bowel disease, and those with diabetes—require tailored preparation strategies. Emerging evidence on glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), linaclotide, simethicone, dietary optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based bowel preparation assessment is critically evaluated. Health system implications, including the impact of inadequate preparation on resource utilization, adherence barriers linked to health literacy, and equity considerations, are examined. The review concludes that no single regimen is universally optimal; personalized preparation strategies integrating risk stratification, AI-assisted quality assessment, and evidence-based adjunctive protocols represent the most promising path toward improving colonoscopy outcomes at the population level.

papers.title: Organizational value realization from AI-enabled digital health technologies in long-term care: roles of human–AI collaboration and digital literacy
papers.authors: Lin-Yu Tsai, Yi-Nuo Shih, Szu-Kou Lee, Mingchih Chen, Yi-chen Lan
papers.abstract: Rapid population aging has intensified pressures on long-term care (LTC) systems, exacerbating workforce shortages and challenges to sustainable healthcare delivery. Although AI-enabled digital health technologies (DHTs) have emerged as promising tools to address these challenges, existing research has focused largely on technology adoption and system use in hospital settings, providing limited understanding of how AI-enabled DHTs realize organizational value and optimize healthcare delivery in LTC organizations. This study aimed to develop and examine an integrated framework for understanding organizational value realization from AI-enabled DHTs in LTC organizations, focusing on the interrelated roles of technological quality, human–AI collaboration, and workforce digital capability. The study also sought to generate evidence to inform healthcare management strategies for optimizing healthcare delivery. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 257 staff from multiple LTC facilities in Taiwan who had used AI-enabled DHTs for at least six months. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). The proposed model explained 77.9% of the variance in perceived organizational value, together with substantial variance in user satisfaction (R 2 = 0.763) and system use (R 2 = 0.652). Human–AI collaboration quality showed the strongest positive association with user satisfaction and was positively associated with system use. User satisfaction was more strongly associated with perceived organizational value than system use. Digital literacy showed significant but differing moderation effects across these relationships. IPMA identified AI explainability, adaptive personalization, system stability, and functional completeness as priority areas for improvement. These findings advance understanding of organizational value realization from AI-enabled DHTs in LTC organizations by highlighting the roles of human–AI collaboration and digital literacy. They underscore the value of explainable, adaptive, and human-centered AI design in supporting positive user experiences with AI-enabled DHTs. Workforce digital literacy may further shape how these technology experiences relate to perceived organizational value. These insights provide evidence to inform healthcare management strategies that align AI system design and workforce development with organizational objectives to support healthcare delivery optimization and sustainable long-term care in aging societies.

papers.title: Faculty-supervised AI-supported BOPPPS-CBL and performance on a simulated neurological-emergency assessment among junior-college medical interns: a batch-stratified randomized educational study
papers.authors: Junhuai Zhang, Zhanqin Xiao, Xiang Gu, Qi Lang, Chanxi Chen, Yaxi Chen
papers.abstract: Background County hospitals and township health centers in China provide frontline care for time-sensitive neurological emergencies, and three-year junior-college clinical medicine programs are an important pathway into this workforce. We evaluated a faculty-supervised artificial intelligence (AI)-supported BOPPPS (Bridge-in, Objectives, Pre-assessment, Participatory Learning, Post-assessment, and Summary) and case-based learning (CBL) instructional package among junior-college medical interns. Methods In this prospective, batch-stratified randomized educational study, 118 interns from 12 monthly rotation batches were assigned to AI-supported BOPPPS-CBL ( n = 58) or conventional BOPPPS-CBL ( n = 60) during a one-month neurology rotation. The intervention used standardized DeepSeek prompts for Socratic questioning, error-focused feedback, and structured reflection under faculty supervision. The primary endpoint was the total score on a locally developed four-station simulated neurological-emergency assessment (0–100). Secondary outcomes included a written examination, while learner-reported questionnaire items were exploratory. Regression models adjusted for rotation batch, baseline academic performance, and digital literacy. The study was not prospectively registered; no public trial registration identifier or registry URL exists, and no publicly time-stamped protocol or statistical analysis plan was available. Results All 118 participants completed the primary assessment. Mean total scores were 82.07 in the AI-supported group and 76.43 in the control group, with an adjusted between-group difference of 5.67 points (95% CI, 2.86–8.49; P < 0.001; adjusted Cohen's d = 0.74). In secondary station-specific analyses, only lesion localization met the multiplicity-adjusted threshold (adjusted mean difference, 2.58 points; 95% CI, 1.25–3.91; P < 0.001; adjusted d = 0.71). A Station 2-specific ICC was not estimated. Post hoc sensitivity analyses excluding the station containing reused case contexts yielded standardized estimates of similar magnitude but could not exclude cueing or carry-over. Written-examination estimates were smaller and imprecise. Exploratory learner-reported findings indicated greater perceived preparation-time burden in the AI-supported group. Conclusion Assignment to the faculty-supervised AI-supported BOPPPS-CBL package was associated with higher scores on a locally developed simulated neurological-emergency assessment than conventional BOPPPS-CBL. These findings do not establish transfer to workplace clinical performance or patient outcomes. Multicenter studies using independent assessment cases, longer-term follow-up, and workplace-based outcomes are warranted.

papers.title: Trust in voice-based assistants: a multidimensional conceptualization based on in-home user interviews
papers.authors: Katharina Frehmann, Marc Ziegele
papers.abstract: Voice-based assistants (VBAs) such as Alexa and Siri are widely used in everyday life and increasingly act as information intermediaries. Their human-like voices and behaviors can elicit social responses, while new assistants based on large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT voice mode, further blur the boundaries between machine and human communicators. Despite risks associated with misinformation and limited data transparency, adoption remains high. Trust may be relevant to users’ relationships with conversational AI, but there is little consensus on how it should be conceptualized. Technical, interpersonal, and media trust frameworks may all be applicable. This multi-method qualitative study examined users’ subjective concepts of trust through 22 in-home interviews complemented by observational tasks involving participants’ own VBAs and ChatGPT voice mode. Participants drew on interpersonal concepts when defining trust but commonly restricted trust in VBAs to particular tasks and functions. Technical and media-related trustworthiness criteria were especially prominent, whereas social responses and anthropomorphic qualities did not necessarily translate into interpersonal trust. Experience, calibrated expectations, selective use, habitual engagement, and trust were described as closely interrelated. Although ChatGPT was often evaluated positively, particularly as an information intermediary, its perceived capabilities were not uniformly accompanied by greater trust compared with participants’ familiar VBAs. Based on these findings, we propose a preliminary conceptual framework of task-specific hybrid trust in VBAs.

papers.title: Digital moral agency in school ethics curricula: from responsible use to epistemic and socio-technical judgement
papers.authors: Joseph Giordmaina, Lucianne Zammit
papers.abstract: Digital technologies increasingly shape the relationships, information environments and institutional systems within which young people exercise moral judgement, yet curriculum responses often separate digital competence from moral education. This study develops the concept of digital moral agency and examines how it is represented across 13 official Maltese Ethics curriculum, syllabus and policy documents published between 2012 and 2026. Using longitudinal qualitative document analysis, we compared successive formulations of the intended curriculum and coded established dimensions of moral agency and practical wisdom alongside inductively identified digital concerns. The analysis shows continuity in reflection, dialogue, responsibility, care, justice and reason-giving, alongside a widening of the contexts in which these capacities are expected to operate. Digital moral agency emerges across three interrelated dimensions: personal and relational judgement concerning conduct, wellbeing, privacy and relationships; epistemic judgement concerning credibility, influence and synthetic information; and structural judgement concerning algorithms, surveillance, bias, data exploitation and distributed responsibility. These dimensions do not form a simple age-graded sequence: newer Years 7–8 syllabi make algorithms, surveillance and AI-supported decision-making explicit, while the current SEC programme for older students remains more strongly focused on conduct and social influence, reflecting overlapping reform cycles. The findings suggest that digital ethics education should move beyond an ethics of responsible use towards an ethics of participation in socio-technical systems. The framework offers a curriculum-mapping tool for integrating ethical judgement with digital and artificial-intelligence literacy across school years.

papers.title: Navigating dual pathways: learning-oriented and instrumental identities in AI-mediated informal digital learning of English
papers.authors: Wu Fei, Chan Pak Hei
papers.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly reshaping how learners engage in informal English learning beyond the classroom, making AI-mediated informal digital learning of English (AI-IDLE) an important emerging learning context. Yet research has predominantly focused on intra-personal psychological factors, the social dimensions of learning, particularly how learners construct their social identities in relation to AI, remain significantly underexplored. This qualitative study examines the social identity categories and their construction processes among 12 Chinese university EFL learners engaged in AI-IDLE. Drawing on Social Identity Theory (SIT), data from semi-structured interviews, reflective journals, and AI chat logs were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal two distinct identity pathways: learning-oriented academic identities, characterized by deep-learning commitment, humble mindset toward AI, and sustained immersion in the student role; and an instrumental identity, organized around a user category defined by transactional engagement, service satisfaction and surface learning approaches. Within this instrumental pathway, a more intensified fast-food consumer orientation emerged, which was explicitly self-identified by one participant and analytically inferred from behavioral patterns across several others. The study demonstrates that AI-IDLE does not simply erase or replace existing social identities but selectively reinforces and reconfigures them through group norms, prototypical markers, and evaluative comparison. These findings extend SIT by revealing how technological affordances and social configuration shape identity pathways that support or undermine meaningful learning engagement. Practical implications are proposed for AI developers, digital learning designers, educators, and curriculum designers to foster learning-oriented identity pathways in AI-mediated informal learning environments

papers.title: Pre-service physics teachers as designers of AI-based pedagogical infrastructure: supporting metacognitive learning in STEM classrooms
papers.authors: Daryn Saiynov, Zhadyra Yermekova
papers.abstract: This study explored how pre-service physics teachers design artificial intelligence (AI)-based pedagogical infrastructure to support metacognitive learning in STEM classrooms. A qualitative interpretive design was employed with 30 pre-service physics teachers enrolled in a physics teacher education program at a university in Kazakhstan. Following two preparatory workshops, participants developed, tested, and refined AI-supported STEM lesson scenarios over 12 weeks. Testing involved peer-based micro-teaching with fellow pre-service teachers acting in simulated student roles; no school students participated. Data comprised individual semi-structured interviews, lesson plans, AI interaction scenarios, prompt sequences, and reflective notes and were examined using reflexive thematic analysis. Six interrelated themes were identified: designing AI-supported STEM lessons; supporting metacognitive regulation and formative assessment; aligning AI use with the physics curriculum and STEM objectives; preserving student agency and ensuring responsible AI use; developing teacher design agency; and addressing conditions for sustainable implementation. Participants' designs generally shifted from using AI to generate ready-made materials toward integrating it more purposefully into structured learning sequences. Pedagogically meaningful scenarios required learners to formulate an initial prediction or solution before consulting AI, verify AI-generated responses using physical laws, calculations, experiments, and reliable sources, and reflect on and revise their reasoning. Reported challenges included inaccurate AI responses, preparation time, unequal access to digital resources, technical difficulties, and variations in the quality of Kazakh- and Russian-language outputs. The findings highlight the importance of preparing pre-service physics teachers for subject-specific, ethically responsible, and pedagogically grounded AI integration. They illustrate design practices intended to scaffold planning, monitoring, scientific verification, evaluation, and reflection. However, the findings concern participants' pedagogical designs and professional perceptions and do not establish improvements in school students' metacognitive regulation or learning outcomes.

papers.title: Redesigning collaborative teaching for human–AI partnership: a phase-based AI-constraint design principle in higher education
papers.authors: Felix Höpfl
papers.abstract: Generative AI is now a routine presence in higher-education classrooms, shifting the operative question from whether to permit its use toward when and how access should be structured within a learning activity. This paper reports a design-based research programme examining phase-based AI constraints, deliberately restricting AI access to specific phases of a collaborative teaching method rather than permitting or prohibiting it wholesale, as a design principle for structuring human and AI contributions within collaborative learning activities. The wider DBR programme examined AI-augmented designs across six collaborative teaching methods, administered repeatedly to five student groups over two academic years; the phase-based AI-constraint principle reported here as DP1 was developed through, and its evidence anchored in, Think-Pair-Share, with the other five methods contributing broader DBR context rather than independent confirmatory evidence. Its strongest evidence comes from an AI-free Think phase within Think-Pair-Share, replicated across three independent student groups spanning three degree programs, where learners consistently endorsed the AI-free phase as appropriate; this endorsement pattern was typically the highest-scoring item on its questionnaire. This design itself resulted from an earlier design cycle within the same programme: an initial administration permitting AI access during this phase prompted redesign after the instructor's classroom observation indicated that independent reflection was being displaced by AI-mediated responses. We treat this endorsement as an empirical finding, not as a direct assessment of the quality or originality of what learners produced, and not as evidence that the phase in fact protects independent cognitive engagement; that stronger claim is a theoretically motivated proposition this study does not test, and we frame DP1 accordingly across three explicit levels: an empirical endorsement finding, a transferable design principle of differentiating AI access by activity phase rather than deciding it once for a whole activity, and an untested theoretical proposition about the cognitive mechanism this differentiation may support. A complementary, independent stakeholder strand surveyed higher-education professionals at a practitioner festival session, offering a modest, exploratory social-validity signal: the phase-based procedure itself was almost universally endorsed, while personal adoption intention was somewhat more reserved. An exploratory qualitative coding of practitioners' open responses showed only slight inter-coder reliability ( κ =0.17), so we do not use these responses to derive additional design principles, retaining only one response on function-based AI restriction as an illustrative example. The study is exploratory and formative, without a no-AI control condition or random assignment, and we frame its claims as design-principle evidence within a design-based research programme rather than as causal effect estimates. Anchored in independently replicated student endorsement data from Think-Pair-Share and supplemented by a practitioner social-validity signal, phase-based AI constraints offer higher-education instructors an actionable, low-friction design principle, one we expect to be conceptually transferable to other collaborative teaching methods, though this transfer remains to be empirically demonstrated.

papers.title: A story for Pepper and Nao: applying the learning by teaching paradigm in children with patterns of neuromotor impairment
papers.authors: Benedetta Del Lucchese, Di Lieto Maria Chiara, Antea Scrocco, Elisa Matteucci, Laura Fiorini, Elena Pescini, Elena Beani, Annalisa Cotardo, Elena Vanni, Eugenia Conti, Valentina Menici, Federica Camuncoli, Gloria Mangani, Marco Vincenzo Maselli, Elena Adelucci, Jasmine Pani, Filippo Cavallo, Chiara Pecini, Eleonora Diella, Fabio Storm, Emilia Biffi, Mattia Chiappini, Sabrina Giovanna Signorini, Roberta Nicotra, Giuseppina Sgandurra
papers.abstract: Background Social robots are increasingly used in educational and clinical contexts to enhance engagement and learning, particularly in children with neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders. The Learning by Teaching paradigm, in which children actively teach social robots, promotes cognitive and metacognitive processes such as planning, self-efficacy, and executive functioning; however, controlled and systematic evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited. Children with neuromotor disorders frequently present with closely intertwined motor and cognitive planning difficulties, which significantly impact learning and everyday functioning. In this context, social robot–mediated interventions based on the Learning by Teaching paradigm may represent a promising approach. The current multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) explores the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach to enhance cognitive and motor planning in children with neuromotor impairments, and to examine potential generalization effects on other cognitive domains and engagement. Methods The main aim of this RCT study is to evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of a social robot-mediated Learning by Teaching intervention in children aged 7–16 years with neuromotor impairments. Eighty participants will be randomly assigned to an Experimental Group (EG) receiving social robot training or to a Control Group (CG) continuing standard care. The intervention consists of 20–25 sessions in which children teach a humanoid social robot (Pepper or NAO) to order picture-based stories of increasing complexity. Assessments will be performed at baseline (T0), post-intervention or control period (T1), and follow-up/post-treatment (T2). Primary outcomes include planning abilities assessed through picture arrangement and an ad hoc motor planning task. Secondary outcomes encompass executive functions, visuo-spatial memory, attention, inhibition, narrative production, visual-perceptual skills, and reading comprehension. Engagement will be measured using a multimodal approach integrating behavioral, cognitive, emotional, and physiological indicators derived from video, audio, and wearable sensors. Results The study will examine improvements in planning and motor programming abilities and potential generalization effects on executive functions and reading comprehension. Additionally, the predictive and mediating role of engagement in intervention effectiveness will be reported. Conclusions This research protocol proposes an innovative, engagement-focused rehabilitation approach integrating cognitive, motor, and narrative processes through social robotics. Findings are expected to inform the development of evidence-based, personalized interventions for children with neuromotor disorders and to advance methodological approaches for assessing engagement in human–robot interaction. Clinical Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov , identifier NCT06797050.

papers.title: AI-based relighting in moving images: current potentials, limitations, and implications for cinematographic practice
papers.authors: David Brenner, Katja Schmid, Jan Adamczyk
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) continuously opens up new possibilities in film post-production, including the subsequent relighting of moving images. As a systematic assessment from a film-design and professional-practice perspective has been lacking, this study examines the potentials, limitations, and implications of current AI-based relighting workflows for cinematographic practice. Methodologically, the study follows a qualitative-exploratory research design within practice-based and practice-led frameworks. Three current AI-based relighting systems (Nvidia DiffusionRenderer, Beeble Studio, and SwitchX) were tested across five test shots and evaluated using a cinematography-oriented qualitative evaluation scheme focusing on light plausibility, image quality and texture retention, as well as image integrity and temporal stability. These observations were complemented by eight semi-structured expert interviews with professionals from cinematography, lighting, and color grading. Results suggest that AI-based relighting does not currently replace on-set lighting but offers considerable potential as a selective correction and extension tool. Its strengths are particularly evident in wide and establishing shots, where faces and fine image details are less perceptually salient, as well as in situations where the desired lighting conditions are difficult to achieve or maintain on set due to weather, time, or budget constraints. Technical and creative limitations are most apparent in workflow integration and usability, as well as in texture loss and image alterations that impair visual credibility, particularly in portrait shots. The findings suggest the potential for a selective shift of certain lighting decisions toward post-production rather than a general replacement of on-set lighting. To maintain a coherent lighting design when substantial lighting decisions are deferred to post-production, greater continuity of cinematographic expertise and creative agency across production and post-production may be required.

papers.title: Inkorporasi Berbasis Artificial Intelligence Dalam Pembelajaran Bahasa Arab: Studi Peluang, Tantangan, Dan Inovasi Pedagogis Di Era Digital Tahun 2026
papers.authors: Teuku Muhammad Fauzan Robbani
papers.abstract: Artikel ini membahas Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence generatif pada 2024-2026 mengubah lanskap pembelajaran bahasa, termasuk Bahasa Arab. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis peluang, tantangan, dan inovasi pedagogis integrasi AI dalam pembelajaran Bahasa Arab. Metode yang digunakan adalah studi literatur sistematis terhadap 28 publikasi internasional dan nasional periode 2023-2025. Hasil menunjukkan AI membuka peluang pada personalisasi pembelajaran, penilaian otomatis, dan simulasi percakapan real-time. Tantangan utama meliputi keterbatasan data dialek, bias algoritma, dan kesiapan dosen. Inovasi pedagogis yang muncul adalah model AI-Enhanced Metaverse dan AI Tutor Adaptif berbasis LLM. Artikel ini merekomendasikan kerangka integrasi AI yang berpusat pada guru, etis, dan kontekstual untuk pendidikan Bahasa Arab di Indonesia.

papers.title: Psychosocial Determinants of Women’s Physical Activity and Body Mass Index: A Cross-Cultural Mediation Analysis in Amman and Budapest
papers.authors: Lina Takruri, Hashem Al-Kilani, Hamed Takruri, Miklós Bánhidi
papers.journal: Baltic Journal of Sport and Health Sciences
papers.abstract: Background: Physical activity (PA) is a key determinant of health and body weight, yet participation among women is influenced by psychosocial and sociocultural factors that may vary across cultural settings. This study examined the associations between psychosocial determinants, PA, and body mass index (BMI) among women residing in Amman (Jordan) and Budapest (Hungary), and investigated whether PA mediates the associations between social support, cultural support for women’s PA, perceived social safety, and BMI. Methods: A cross-sectional comparative design was employed. A total of 800 women aged 18–45 years (Amman = 399; Budapest = 401) completed measures of social support for PA, perceived cultural support, perceived social safety, and PA using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ-SF). BMI was calculated from self-reported height and weight. Nonparametric analyses were conducted to examine cross-cultural differences and associations among study variables. Bootstrapped mediation analyses (5,000 resamples) were performed to assess indirect associations between psychosocial determinants and BMI through PA. Results: Women in Budapest reported significantly higher PA levels, lower BMI, greater perceived social support, stronger cultural support for women’s PA, and higher perceptions of social safety than women in Amman (all p < .001). Social support, cultural support, and perceived social safety were positively associated with PA participation, while PA was negatively associated with BMI (r = −0.35, p < .001). PA partially mediated the associations between social support and BMI and between cultural support and BMI. No significant indirect association was observed between perceived social safety and BMI through PA. Conclusion: Psychosocial and sociocultural environments were significantly associated with women’s PA and BMI across two culturally distinct populations. PA may represent an important behavioural pathway linking supportive social environments to healthier weight-related outcomes. Interventions that strengthen social support and culturally supportive environments may contribute to increased PA participation among women. Keywords: Physical activity, body mass index, social support, social environment, women’s health

papers.title: Sistem Prediksi Kebutuhan Bandwidth dengan Machine Learning Metode Long Short Term Memory (LSTM)
papers.authors: Ananta Wicaksana, Nugroho Suharto, Galih Putra Riatma
papers.abstract: Internet has become an essential need in various aspects of life, especially in public environments such as Malang Creative Centre (MCC). However, bandwidth management that is still done manually at MCC causes inefficient allocation and has an impact on service quality. Therefore, this research aims to design a bandwidth usage prediction system using the Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) method to optimise bandwidth management at MCC. The LSTM method was chosen because of its ability to learn past data patterns and provide accurate predictions. This research uses 80% training data and 20% test data, with the optimal LSTM model configuration consisting of 80 layers and 100 epochs, and optimisation using Adam. The evaluation results show a prediction accuracy rate of 82.39%, which indicates that this model is reliable in predicting bandwidth usage on various floors and times that have been determined. In conclusion, this LSTM-based prediction system offers a solution for more precise and efficient bandwidth management at MCC. This not only saves network operational costs but also improves the quality of internet services for users, supporting creative economic activities at MCC by providing adequate and efficient internet connections.

papers.title: Digital Resilience
papers.authors: Heejung Ryoh
papers.journal: Central European Library and Information Science Review Közép-európai Könyvtár- és Információtudományi Szemle
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic served as a brutal stress test for museum resilience. While many institutions relied on a 'substitutive model' of mere digital replacement, the National Museum of Korea (NMK) achieved anomalous growth through a strategic pivot. This study employs an explanatory single-case study design to investigate the mechanisms behind this success. Applying pattern matching logic, the research validates the efficacy of a 'Transformative Model' grounded in Cultural Democracy. Findings reveal that the NMK's integration of AI-driven personalization, immersive Extended Reality (XR) experiences, and radical inclusivity reconfigured the visitor relationship from passive consumption to active co-creation. Crucially, empirical data confirms a positive correlation where high-level digital engagement functioned as a catalytic gateway that drove, rather than cannibalized, physical attendance. This case illustrates how sustainable resilience can be achieved when technology is strategically deployed to democratize heritage access and empower the visitor as an active participant.

papers.title: A Web-Based Multi-Modal AI Framework for Intelligent Content Moderation with Constructive Feedback
papers.authors: Naveen Palanichamy, Marwah Zaid Mohammed Al-Helali, Su-Cheng Haw, Subhashini Gopal
papers.journal: Journal of Informatics and Web Engineering
papers.abstract: Traditional content moderation systems primarily rely on punitive measures that focus on removing offending or inappropriate content without offering users any form of educational feedback or guidance. This lack of constructive interaction often leads to a poor user experience, leaving users frustrated and uninformed regarding the reasons behind content removal. Moreover, such a system fails to encourage long-term positive behavioural changes within online communities, as users do not gain insights on how to improve their conduct. This paper proposes a new constructive Artificial Intelligence (AI) intervention system that integrates a number of AI models in order to conceptualize content moderation as a limiting process rather than an educational process. The framework suggested in the paper combines HuggingFace's BERT-based toxicity analysis, SightEngine's image processing, and Google's Gemini large language model to provide end-to-end content moderation with construction of feedback. Based on comprehensive testing through user interaction analysis and comparative analysis, the study demonstrates the effectiveness of educational intervention in content moderation. The study advances the field by developing a novel approach to content moderation that puts user education and community development first while upholding safety regulations.

papers.title: Challenges of Employing Artificial Intelligence Applications in Education from the Perspectives of English Language Teachers
papers.authors: Salam Abd Alrahman Suleman Alqtifan, Talal Abd Alhameed Salem Alodwan
papers.journal: Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences Studies
papers.abstract: The study aimed to uncover the challenges of employing artificial intelligence applications in education from the perspective of English language teachers. To achieve this, the study followed the descriptive survey method. The study sample consisted of (320) English language teachers in the Al-Quwaysimah district. To achieve the study objectives, a questionnaire was developed distributed across (4) areas: (technical and technological challenges, material challenges, educational and human challenges, and organizational and administrative challenges). The results of the study showed that the level of challenges facing English language teachers at the basic stage in employing artificial intelligence applications in education from their perspective was moderate. The results also showed the existence of statistically significant differences (α = 0.05) attributable to the effect of the education sector, with the differences favoring the public sector. There were also statistically significant differences attributable to the effect of experience, with the differences favoring teachers with experience (10 years or more). There were also statistically significant differences attributable to the effect of academic qualification, with the differences favoring those holding a bachelor's degree. In light of the study’s findings, the study recommended the need to develop the technical infrastructure and provide the necessary resources in schools, especially government sector schools, in addition to implementing continuous training programs for English language teachers to develop their competencies in employing artificial intelligence applications in education.

papers.title: Trabajo social e inteligencia artificial generativa: Una experiencia de investigación-acción para el modelamiento y la validación de IAGen como recurso de aprendizaje
papers.authors: Patricia Lorena Castañeda Meneses, Verónica Villarroel Astorga, Ketty Cazorla Becerra, Héctor Díaz Vidal, Raúl Octavio Hozven Valenzuela
papers.abstract: The article presents the results of an action-research project that aimed to model and validated the contributions of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) AI as a learning resource in the core curricular lines of the social work formation process. The research responds to the need to model the inclusion GenAI as a learning resource in the university training of disciplines focused on human connection such as social work . Worked with a section of 18 students from the fourth semester of the course, selected by non-probabilistic sampling for convenience A cycle of four work sessions with GenAI was carried out, which was compatible with the training activities of the theoretical-methodological curricular lines of Social Sciences and theoretical-practical social work carried out in the selected subject. The expected results were oriented towards obtaining definitions with GenAI support, collation reflections, GenAI support in writing professional documents and methodological mapping. The validation of GenAI as a learning resource is concluded, with support from teachers and students. In addition, it is confirmed that social intervention occupies a central place in vocational training, which displaces AIGen from an assessment of centrality initially assigned by the digital native student generations, towards a limited and complementary contribution position that adds to the repertoire of available learning resources.

papers.title: University staff health: associations between body composition, physical fitness, and quality of life
papers.authors: Matheus Amarante do Nascimento, Ágatha Graça, Higor Santos Fonseca, Fábio Luiz Cheche Pina, Daniel Vicentini de Oliveira, Wendell Arthur Lopes
papers.journal: Revista Brasileira de Ciência e Movimento
papers.abstract: This study analyzed body composition, functional capacity, and quality of life in 34 university staff members (18 women; 31.2 ± 16.6 years), comparing results by sex and age group, and correlating them with length of service. Assessments included BMI, body fat percentage, lean mass, handgrip strength, flexibility, standing long jump, and SF-36 domains, applying Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, and Spearman’s correlation tests (p < 0.05). Men presented higher body weight (p = 0.009), height (p = 0.001), lean mass (p < 0.001), and vitality (p = 0.035). Age and length of service were associated with anthropometric measures. Length of service was positively correlated with vitality (ρ = 0.55; p < 0.001). These findings suggest associations between occupational characteristics and aspects of perceived health, supporting institutional health promotion strategies.

papers.title: Differences in AI Anxiety: Exploratory Factor Analysis Suggests Similar AI Anxiety Structure in German- and English-Speaking Samples
papers.authors: Nick Sheth, Klemens Weigl
papers.abstract: The mass use of AI applications is transforming human-AI interaction while uncovering and intensifying AI anxieties. To measure these anxieties in German-speaking populations, this study translates and psychometrically evaluates the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS) [31]. In contrast to a concurrently German published version by Hajek et al. [9] exploratory factor analysis (EFA) is employed to test whether a distinct anxiety structure emerges from the data. A quota sample (N = 225) with balanced age and gender representation completed an online survey. The full scale (α = .95) and subscales (α = .85-.96) demonstrated good to excellent reliability. EFA identified four factors: learning, AI configuration, replacement, and socio-technical blindness, largely consistent with the original English structure. Five items required removal, suggesting cultural and linguistic specificity. Limitations include the sample’s composition and the factor characteristics. The German AIAS provides a reliable instrument for human-AI interaction research and targeted anxiety interventions.

papers.title: EEG in Parkinson’s Disease: Mechanisms, Biomarkers and Translational Opportunities
papers.authors: Sümeyye Özdemir, Sahar Allouch, Manon Auffret, Mahmoud Hassan, Marc Vérin
papers.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by nigrostriatal dopaminergic degeneration and basal ganglia dysfunction, yet these pathophysiological abnormalities alone do not fully explain its heterogeneous motor and non-motor manifestations. Over recent decades, electroencephalography (EEG) has evolved from a primarily descriptive technique into a quantitative approach for investigating cortical electrophysiological dynamics associated with PD. Accumulating electrophysiological evidence implicates altered oscillatory synchronization and interactions across cortical and subcortical circuits in PD-related dysfunction, suggesting disturbances in the temporal coordination of neural activity. Emerging approaches, including large-scale datasets, multimodal integration, individualized modeling and wearable EEG technologies, offer opportunities for physiological phenotyping and real-world monitoring. However, methodological heterogeneity, limited reproducibility, insufficient external validation and uncertainty regarding clinical utility continue to constrain translation. This Review critically synthesizes EEG-derived measures spanning spectral activity, oscillatory coupling, functional connectivity and dynamic brain states, examining their relationships with motor, cognitive and neuropsychiatric manifestations of PD. By distinguishing mechanistic interpretations, clinical associations and current levels of biomarker validation, it identifies opportunities and requirements for translating EEG-derived measures into reliable tools for individualized assessment and clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Humanizing AI-generated exemplars: Human-source framing facilitates group creative ideation
papers.authors: Shenghui Xiaoyong, Yingning Lu, Yihui LIU, Yueyue Ge, Qiannan Ruan, Ke Jiang, Kelong Lu
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated creative exemplars are increasingly used as scalable digital instructional resources in creativity education. However, it remains unclear whether labeling identical exemplars as human- or AI-generated shapes how learners engage in group creative activities. We tested this possibility in 113 dyads using an fNIRS hyperscanning group creative ideation paradigm. Dyads completed creative ideation tasks before, during, and after exemplar-stimulation. During stimulation, the human- and AI-attribution groups received identical exemplars labeled as produced by human or AI, whereas the control group received no exemplar. Human attribution increased idea uniqueness during stimulation relative to both the other phases and the AI-attribution and control groups. AI attribution temporarily increased switching among ideation pathways. Neither behavioral effect persisted after exemplar withdrawal. The two attribution groups did not differ in exemplar-category overlap or nearest-exemplar semantic distance, but human-attribution dyads rated the exemplars as more helpful. Human attribution also increased interbrain synchronization (IBS) in bilateral premotor and supplementary motor cortices during stimulation, whereas AI attribution was associated with decreased IBS in the left supramarginal gyrus and right frontopolar cortex from pre- to post-stimulation. Thus, exemplar-source attribution shapes the process and outcome of group creative ideation, revealing an important social-contextual factor in AI-supported creativity education.

papers.title: Tourism Recommendation System for Labuan Bajo Using Hybrid TF-IDF and Sentence-BERT with Semantic Feature Boosting
papers.authors: Luluk Baitti Kusumaningrum, Arif Nur Rohman
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Informatics and Computing
papers.abstract: The heterogeneous tourism landscape of Labuan Bajo, ranging from marine excursions to cultural sites, is often inadequately captured by conventional retrieval systems due to vocabulary mismatch. The reliance on rigid lexical matching leads to a failure in grasping the search intent of tourists who use terminology that differs from, yet is semantically equivalent to, destination descriptions. This study addresses this limitation by developing a hybrid recommendation model enhanced with a Semantic Feature Boosting approach. The proposed methodology integrates lexical feature extraction based on TF-IDF (1,2 n-grams) and deep semantic representation using the Sentence-BERT model (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2). Both vector representations are combined through an adaptive weighting scheme (0.6 for TF-IDF and 0.4 for Sentence-BERT) to compute destination relevance based on cosine similarity. Empirical evaluation across ten query scenarios representing diverse tourist needs demonstrates robust performance: Mean Precision@5 = 0.90, Mean Recall@5 = 0.81, Mean Average Precision@5 = 0.89, and Mean NDCG@5 = 0.93. Statistical significance testing (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < 0.05) confirms that the hybrid approach outperforms Pure lexical and Pure semantic baselines. This comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that the integration of semantic features significantly enhances the system's ranking quality and ability to understand diverse search contexts. Thus, the proposed approach proves effective in generating more precise and adaptive recommendations for complex tourism landscapes, while providing a methodological contribution to recommendation systems responsive to natural language variations.

papers.title: University faculty competence deficits in the safe application of artificial intelligence
papers.authors: Mikhail Zamyslov, M. D. Kitaygorodskiy
papers.abstract: The purpose of the study is to identify the state of university faculty competence in the field of safe application of artificial intelligence technologies (AI competence) across its various components and, on this basis, to substantiate the content of a professional development program. The article clarifies the concept of a teacher’s AI competence as a constituent part of their digital competence, identifies its general user, general pedagogical, and subject-pedagogical components, and differentiates between the technological limitations of AI systems and the ethical and legal norms governing their use. The results of a survey involving 44 university teachers are presented. The scientific novelty of the study lies in clarifying the concept and component structure of university teachers’ AI competence and in obtaining empirical data on its state, including the nature of teachers’ understanding of the ethical risks associated with the use of artificial intelligence. As a result, it was established that approximately half of the teachers have practical experience in applying AI, while their understanding of AI technologies is limited to the interface level. Ethical risks are not differentiated by almost half of the respondents; the remainder conceptualize them primarily as data transfer risks, whereas the risks of unreliability and opacity of generated results are underestimated – notably, active users rate the risk of unreliability lower than others. Based on the identified deficits and a content analysis of existing courses, a modular structure for a professional development program with a risk-oriented approach to content design is substantiated.

papers.title: TRUSTWORTHY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR MEDICAL IMAGE ANALYSIS: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF ROBUST DEEP LEARNING TECHNIQUES FOR CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT
papers.authors: Rebecca Yaa Bonah, Ebenezer Tetteh
papers.journal: Magna Scientia Advanced Research and Reviews
papers.abstract: Medical image analysis has been revolutionized by the advent of artificial intelligence, which has made automated disease detection, segmentation and diagnosis possible across a range of imaging modalities, thus supporting clinical decisions. However, the increasing complexity of deep learning models has raised concerns regarding their reliability, interpretability, fairness, privacy, and regulatory compliance, highlighting the need for trustworthy AI in healthcare. The review focuses on recent breakthroughs in deep learning models for medical image analysis, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), segmentation networks based on U-net, Vision Transformers, and foundation models, and explores their use in clinical decision support. It also examines the fundamental principles of trustworthy AI, including explainability, robustness, fairness, privacy preservation, reliability, transparency and regulatory governance. The review summarizes the current state of the art for the strengths and limitations of current AI models and highlights some of the challenges that hamper the use of these models in the clinical workflow, such as limited data availability, domain shifts, algorithmic bias, computational complexity, and integration into the clinical workflow. New concepts like multimodal foundation models, federated learning and privacy-preserving AI are also explored as potential advancements in the safe, scalable and clinically relevant use of AI in medical imaging. The review highlights the significant progress medical image analysis has made using deep learning techniques but emphasizes that the effective translation of these technologies into clinical practice requires both technical advancement and adherence to trustworthy AI principles and effective governance models. To ensure these AI systems are effective for patient care and to aid in evidence-based medical decision making, development needs continued cooperation between researchers, clinicians, healthcare institutions and regulatory bodies, with the aim of creating reliable, transparent and clinically acceptable AI systems.

papers.title: Patient Satisfaction Analysis at Bhayangkara Hospital, Level III, Korbrimob: Strategy for Improving PREMs/PROMs with AI Chatbots on WhatsApp in 2025
papers.authors: Rike Rayanti, Susanna Halim, Alamsyah
papers.abstract: Improving patient-centered healthcare quality has become a major priority in modern health service systems. Patient-Reported Experience Measures (PREMs) and Patient- Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) are essential instruments for evaluating service quality and health outcomes from the patient’s perspective. However, the collection of PREMs and PROMs data in hospitals is often conducted manually, resulting in inefficiency and limited sustainability. This study aims to analyze patient satisfaction at RS Bhayangkara Tk. III Korbrimob Polri and to formulate strategies for improving PREMs and PROMs through the utilization of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based WhatsApp chatbot. This study employed a quantitative approach with a survey design. The research sample consisted of 87 outpatient respondents selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected using PREMs and PROMs questionnaires distributed through an AI WhatsApp chatbot. Data analysis included descriptive statistics as well as validity and reliability testing. The results indicate that all dimensions of service quality and patient satisfaction are in the high category, with mean scores above 4.00. The highest scores were observed in the dimensions of empathy, service control, and trust, while waiting time and chatbot performance still require further optimization. Reliability testing yielded a Cronbach’s Alpha value of 0.988, indicating excellent internal consistency of the research instrument. The findings suggest that the implementation of an AI-based WhatsApp chatbot has the potential to enhance patient engagement in PREMs and PROMs reporting and to support a more effective and sustainable evaluation of hospital service quality. Strengthening chatbot functionality, reducing service waiting times, and utilizing PREMs and PROMs data for managerial decision-making are recommended to support digital transformation and service quality improvement at RS Bhayangkara Tk. III Korbrimob Polri.

papers.title: A/R/T Emergence: Revisiting a Collaborative Exhibit
papers.authors: Geneviève Cloutier, Kathy Mantas, Malvika Agarwal, Robert Durocher, Renee Jackson, Michele Kleinschuck, Don Kwan, Sandra Poczobut, Jessica Sokolowski, Jennifer Wicks, Cara Tierney
papers.journal: The Canadian Review of Art Education / Revue canadienne d’éducation artistique
papers.abstract: This visual essay revisits A/R/T Emergence, a collaborative exhibition at the Ottawa Art Gallery during the 2022 joint CSEA/SCÉA and OAEA conference. Co-curated as a relational, accessible, non-hierarchical space, it brought together artists, researchers, teachers, students and community members to explore emergence by engaging with decolonization, accessibility, activism, environmentalism, memory, and identity. Grounded in posthumanist and anti-colonial perspectives, it enacted radical inclusion by resisting fixed, linear knowledge in favour of fluid, relational meaning-making, inviting audiences into co-creation. A/R/T Emergence calls for sustaining arts-based exhibitions that foster inclusive and interconnected pedagogies, in conference contexts and beyond.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Money Management: A Multidisciplinary Framework for Financial Decision-Making
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
