papers.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into financial services has significantly transformed traditional approaches to money management.This study aims to examine the role of AI in enhancing financial decision-making through a multidisciplinary lens, incorporating perspectives from management, behavioural finance, and information technology.Adopting a quantitative research design, primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to individuals actively engaged in financial decision-making.The study investigates key factors influencing the adoption of AI-based money management tools, including perceived usefulness, ease of use, financial literacy, and trust in technology.Using statistical techniques such as regression analysis and structural equation modelling (SEM), the findings reveal that AI-driven tools positively impact financial planning, investment decisions, and overall financial efficiency.The results further indicate that behavioural factors, particularly trust and financial awareness, play a significant mediating role in the effective utilization of AI in money management.The study contributes to the existing literature by proposing a multidisciplinary framework that integrates technological, behavioural, and managerial dimensions of AI adoption in financial contexts.The practical implications of the study highlight the need for financial institutions and policymakers to promote AI literacy and develop user-centric financial technologies to enhance decision-making outcomes.This research offers valuable insights for academicians, practitioners, and policymakers aiming to leverage AI for improved financial management practices.

papers.title: Proposed Pedagogical Framework for Positioning Generative AI as a Thinking Companion in Recount Writing
papers.authors: Jasmine Fajri, Ahmad Husein Rofi’udin, Titik Harsiati
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can provide feedback, questions for reflection, and language support in writing instruction. However, without clear guidance, students may delegate idea generation, drafting, and revision to the technology. This study identifies local needs in Grade IX recount-writing instruction and proposes a preliminary framework for positioning GenAI as a thinking companion. It draws on content analysis of the Grade IX Indonesian Language Student’s Book and Teacher’s Book, a semi-structured interview with one Indonesian language teacher, and descriptive analysis of six selected questionnaire items answered by 56 students. The materials examined provide model texts and initial writing activities but lack systematic revision guidance and recount-specific criteria in the final assessment rubric. Student responses indicate reported use of AI as a thinking companion, reported submission of assignments containing content partly or entirely copied from GenAI, and an expectation for appropriately integrated teaching materials. Considered alongside relevant literature, these findings inform six proposed principles: student ownership of ideas, independent work before AI use, limited AI assistance, guided prompts, critical evaluation of AI output, and transparency about AI use. The framework has not undergone expert validation or classroom testing. It should therefore be regarded as a context-specific design proposal, not an established guideline or evidence of instructional effectiveness.

papers.title: Model Risk-Based AI Governance dalam pendidikan tinggi Indonesia: Rekonstruksi kebijakan untuk mewujudkan integritas akademik
papers.authors: Alfin Dwi Novemyanto, Sigit Bayu Cahyanto, Fakhrur Rozi
papers.journal: Prosiding Seminar Nasional Sanata Dharma Berbagi
papers.abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dalam pendidikan tinggi menimbulkan kebutuhan untuk membangun tata kelola yang mampu mengakomodasi manfaat teknologi sekaligus melindungi integritas akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kesenjangan tata kelola pemanfaatan AI dalam pendidikan tinggi Indonesia dan merumuskan model kebijakan berbasis risiko yang membedakan penggunaan AI berdasarkan tingkat risiko serta menentukan kewajiban, pembatasan, pengawasan, dan pertanggungjawaban yang proporsional. Permasalahan penelitian berfokus pada bagaimana kebijakan pemanfaatan AI dapat direkonstruksi melalui pendekatan Risk-Based AI Governance untuk membedakan penggunaan asistif, bersyarat, terbatas, dan tidak dapat diterima. Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian hukum normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan, konseptual, dan perbandingan melalui studi kepustakaan serta analisis kualitatif-yuridis terhadap peraturan, kebijakan, pedoman, dan literatur terkait. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa regulasi Indonesia telah menyediakan prinsip kehati-hatian, keamanan, transparansi, akuntabilitas, perlindungan data, pengawasan, dan manajemen risiko, tetapi belum mengintegrasikannya dalam klasifikasi risiko AI yang spesifik untuk pendidikan tinggi. Penelitian menghasilkan model empat tingkat risiko yang terhubung dengan differentiated controls, human oversight, transparency/disclosure, monitoring dan audit, evaluasi, mitigasi, serta remediasi atau sanksi, dengan integritas akademik sebagai tujuan normatif utama.

papers.title: STRATEGI GURU DALAM MENGHADAPI TANTANGAN PEMANFAATAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) UNTUK MENUMBUHKAN KEMAMPUAN BERPIKIR KRITIS SISWA: PEMBELAJARAN BAHASA INDONESIA
papers.authors: Raudhatil Maulani Maulani, Baiq Rismarini Nursaly, Ahmad Sirajuddin
papers.abstract: The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Indonesian language learning provides convenience in accessing information and completing assignments, but also presents challenges for teachers in ensuring appropriate AI use and fostering students’ critical thinking skills. This study aims to describe the challenges faced by teachers in utilizing AI and the strategies employed to foster students’ critical thinking skills in Indonesian language learning at the senior high school level. This qualitative study collected data through interviews with Indonesian language teachers. The findings indicate that the main challenges include limited supervision of students’ AI use outside school, students’ tendency to copy AI-generated outputs without understanding or processing the information, difficulties in assessing the authenticity of students’ work, and the need for consistency in developing critical thinking skills. Teachers’ strategies include providing guidance and limitations on AI use, using AI-generated outputs as materials for critical evaluation, designing tasks that require thinking processes and contextual understanding, and shifting assessment orientation from products to learning processes. These strategies can encourage students to analyze, evaluate, verify, and express opinions about information obtained through AI. Thus, AI can serve as both a learning resource and an object of critical examination without replacing students’ thinking processes.

papers.title: KONSULTASI KEAGAMAAN DI ERA AI: PERBANDINGAN RESPONS CHATGPT DAN GEMINI TERHADAP KASUS-KASUS MODERASI BERAGAMA
papers.authors: Nazwa Niswatusshofiyah, Raudlatul Intan Nurul Balqies, Iksan Kamil Sahri, Muhammad Bachrul Ulum
papers.abstract: The shift of religious consultation from traditional authorities toward artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini raises new challenges for Islamic Religious Education, particularly regarding the accuracy, consistency, and level of moderation in the responses generated. This study aims to compare the capabilities of ChatGPT and Gemini in providing religious consultation based on four religious moderation indicators established by the Ministry of Religious Affairs, namely tolerance, national commitment, anti violence, and acceptance of local traditions, as well as to examine the sensitivity of responses to framing and their consistency across repeated prompts. The study employs the Comparative AI Religious Consultation Audit (CARCA) method with a mixed-method approach combining quantitative content analysis and qualitative comparative analysis. The results show a mean score of 92.07 for ChatGPT and 90.90 for Gemini, with high and relatively comparable performance on the three normative-social criteria, but markedly lower performance on religious accuracy (around 71% for both models). ChatGPT outperformed Gemini in context sensitivity, while provocative framing produced opposite effects across models, raising ChatGPT's score slightly while lowering Gemini's score. The study concludes that both AI models are able to translate some principles of religious moderation into moderate practical advice, but cannot yet be fully relied upon as a source of religious authority, given their weaknesses in accuracy and religious textual grounding. These findings underscore the importance of positioning AI as a companion to, rather than a replacement for, traditional religious authority.

papers.title: HIGHER EDUCATION TEACHING PROFESSION: TRAINING, PRACTICES, AND INNOVATION
papers.authors: Alcimar de Lima Marques Filho, Angela Monteiro Simão, Diego Macedo Almeida, Anna Cristhina Barbosa Massulo, Lena Marina Moreira Puga Barbosa, Valdenilson de Souza Ribeiro, Silvya Karen de Carvalho Martins, Aylin Cynthia de Carvalho Lopes
papers.abstract: This article analyzes how teacher education, pedagogical practices, and innovation interact in the reconfiguration of the teaching profession in higher education. It is a qualitative theoretical-conceptual study supported by structured bibliographic research and an audit of the references used. The corpus comprises seminal works, reviews, meta-analyses, empirical studies, and institutional documents addressing teacher professionalism and identity, professional development, pedagogical practices, digital competence, and generative artificial intelligence. The interpretive synthesis indicates that disciplinary expertise, although indispensable, does not exhaust the competence required for teaching; professional development depends on the interaction among education, experience, reflection, and context; and pedagogical innovation should not be equated with technological novelty. The analysis also shows that digital competence involves pedagogical judgment and that the diffusion of generative artificial intelligence adds new demands related to verification, contextualization, ethics, and learning mediation. As a theoretical contribution, the article proposes the Integrative Model for the Reconfiguration of University Teaching (MIRDU), which organizes education, practice, reflection, and innovation as recursive components of professional development, conditioned by institutional, pedagogical, and technological factors. The model is presented as a conceptual proposition to be empirically validated in future studies.

papers.title: HIGHER EDUCATION AND GENERATIVE AI: ETHICAL AND INSTITUTIONAL IMPLICATIONS FOR THE HUMANITIES.
papers.authors: Américo Souza
papers.abstract: The spread of generative artificial intelligence in higher education is profoundly transforming teaching, assessment, and knowledge production, with significant implications for the Humanities. Drawing on a critical review of the literature, this theoretical essay examines the ethical incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into higher education processes, with particular attention to the Humanities. It argues that AI regulation should take the form of ethical educational governance—rather than mere control—and that Yuk Hui’s concepts of technodiversity and cosmotechnics offer valuable paths for rethinking authorship, autonomy, and creativity in the Humanities. The theoretical discussion is illustrated by an ongoing initiative within the History Teacher Education Program at the University of International Integration of Afro-Brazilian Lusophony (UNILAB), aimed at developing a set of ethical guidelines for the use of GenAI.

papers.title: GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING IN MATHEMATICS EDUCATION: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
papers.authors: Daniel Rodrigues Topanotti
papers.abstract: The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into Problem-Based Learning (PBL) environments presents new challenges and opportunities for education. The objective of this research is to investigate how AI has been used to promote critical thinking, argumentation, and complex problem-solving within the context of mathematics education or STEM fields. To this end, a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted, guided by the PRISMA protocol, analyzing empirical studies published since 2020 and indexed in the Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, and ERIC databases. The results indicate that AI transcends the function of a content repository, assuming pedagogical roles such as 'Socratic Coach,' 'Design Partner,' and 'Object of Critical Analysis.' The analysis highlights that the tool's effectiveness depends intrinsically on the quality of prompt engineering and human mediation. Furthermore, AI 'hallucinations' and mathematical inconsistencies do not necessarily need to be perceived as critical flaws; they can emerge as effective pedagogical catalysts for the refinement of logical validation by students. It is concluded that the integration of AI into PBL requires pedagogical intentionality, shifting from prohibitive models to approaches that foster digital literacy and academic integrity within a hybrid intelligence ecosystem.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EARLY RECOGNITION OF CLINICAL DETERIORATION: NEW PERSPECTIVES FOR NURSING PRACTICE IN PATIENT SAFETY
papers.authors: Victor Lucas Dutra de Morais, Vinícius Luan Dutra de Morais, Allana Beatriz Silva Medeiros, Golda Meyr Ângelo de Lima Barbosa, Shirliane Romana Da Silva Barros, Raiane Patrícia Nascimento Guedes da Silva, Débora Ilana Silva de Oliveira
papers.abstract: Clinical deterioration in hospitalized patients may be preceded by progressive physiological changes that, when recognized in a timely manner, enable healthcare interventions before severe adverse events occur. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) has been investigated as a tool capable of analyzing large volumes of clinical data and identifying patterns associated with worsening health status. This study aimed to analyze the evidence regarding the use of artificial intelligence for the early recognition of clinical deterioration, emphasizing its implications for nursing practice and patient safety. A narrative literature review was conducted based on scientific studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, early warning systems, and clinical deterioration in hospitalized patients. The literature indicates that predictive models may increase the ability to identify patients at risk of deterioration, support care prioritization, and facilitate more timely clinical responses. However, limitations related to algorithm heterogeneity, data quality and representativeness, external validation, interpretability, bias, privacy, and integration of alerts into clinical workflows were also identified. For nursing, AI represents a complementary resource to clinical assessment and may strengthen surveillance and decision-making when integrated with professional judgment and structured care processes. It is concluded that the responsible incorporation of these technologies requires professional education, critical evaluation of AI systems, and preservation of the central role of human care.

papers.title: ØA-fagenes relevans og omdømme i møte med kunstig intelligens
papers.authors: June Borge Doornich, Trond Vegard Johannessen
papers.abstract: Kunstig intelligens endrer forutsetningene for økonomisk-administrative fag og profesjoner. Når analyser, prognoser, beslutningsstøtte og rapportering i økende grad utføres med KI-baserte systemer, utfordres etablerte forståelser av fagkompetanse, profesjonell dømmekraft og ØA-fagenes samfunnsbidrag. Dette temanummeret bygger videre på ØA-konferansen 2026 ved NHH og undersøker hvordan ØA-fagene kan bevare og styrke sin relevans og sitt omdømme i møte med teknologisk endring. Bidragene viser at KI ikke gjør fagkompetanse overflødig, men skjerper behovet for kritisk vurderingsevne, pedagogisk nytenkning og institusjonell handlekraft. ENGLISH ABSTRACT The Relevance and Reputation of Business and Economics Disciplines in the Age of Artificial Intelligence Artificial intelligence is changing the conditions for business and economics disciplines and professions. As analysis, forecasting, decision support and reporting are increasingly performed with AI-based systems, established understandings of disciplinary expertise, professional judgement and the societal contribution of business and economics education are being challenged. This special issue builds on the 2026 ØA Conference at NHH and explores how business and economics disciplines can maintain and strengthen their relevance and reputation in the face of technological change. The contributions show that AI does not make disciplinary expertise obsolete, but rather increases the need for critical judgement, pedagogical renewal and institutional capacity to act.

papers.title: Når Copilot lager regnearkmodellen: Om modellkvalitet, god regnearkskikk og hva økonomistudenter må kunne
papers.authors: Trond Vegard Johannessen, Anna Mette Fuglseth
papers.abstract: Artikkelen bidrar til diskusjonen om hvordan kunstig intelligens (KI) påvirker regnearkundervisning i økonomisk-administrative fag når dialogbaserte KI-verktøy som Microsoft Copilot integreres i regnearkprogrammer. Integreringen gir brukere mulighet til å beskrive problemstillinger i naturlig språk og få forslag til ferdige modeller. Artikkelen presenterer en studie der Copilot utviklet og videreutviklet en regnearkmodell for en budsjetteringsoppgave, vurdert mot prinsipper for modellering i regneark. Resultatene viser at Copilot raskt leverer modeller som ved første øyekast fremstår ryddige og profesjonelle, men som inneholder en rekke svakheter ved nærmere kontroll. KI-verktøy som Copilot reduserer dermed ikke behovet for undervisning i regnearkmodellering. Undervisningen må imidlertid omfatte spesifikk opplæring i hvordan KI-verktøy kan benyttes effektivt for utvikling av modeller i økonomisk-administrative beslutningssituasjoner som krever utforskning av usikkerhet. ENGLISH ABSTRACT When Copilot Builds the Spreadsheet Model: On Model Quality, Good Spreadsheet Practice, and What Business and Economics Students Need to Know This article contributes to the discussion of how artificial intelligence (AI) affects spreadsheet education in business and economics programs, as dialogue-based AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot are integrated directly into spreadsheet software. Such integration allows users to describe problems in natural language and receive suggestions for complete models. The article presents a study in which Copilot developed and further developed a spreadsheet model for a budgeting task, assessed against established principles of spreadsheet modelling. The results show that Copilot quickly produces models that appear tidy and professional at first glance, but that contain several weaknesses upon closer inspection. AI tools such as Copilot therefore do not reduce the need for teaching spreadsheet modelling. Rather, teaching must include specific training in how AI tools can be used effectively to develop models for business and economics decision-making situations that require exploration of uncertainty.

papers.title: Autentisk ledelse utvikles mellom mennesker: Sosiokulturell læring og GenKI som supplerende kulturelt redskap
papers.authors: June Borge Doornich
papers.abstract: Forskning på autentisk lederutvikling er hovedsakelig forankret i erfaringsbasert læring og vektlegger individuell refleksjon og utprøving. Denne studien undersøker hvordan pedagogiske metoder forankret i sosiokulturell læring bidrar til læring og utvikling av autentisk ledelse, og drøfter generativ kunstig intelligens (GenKI) muligheter og begrensninger i slike læringsprosesser. Studien er en kvalitativ, eksplorativ enkeltcasestudie av et emne i autentisk ledelse i en siviløkonomutdanning. Analysen viser at kulturelle redskaper og språk gjorde studentenes fortolkninger tilgjengelige for respons og videreutvikling i sosial samhandling. Læringsprosessen fremmet særlig selvbevissthet, balansert prosessering og relasjonell orientering, mens autentisk atferd var mindre tydelig dokumentert. Studien fremmer dermed autentisk lederutvikling som en kulturelt mediert og sosialt forankret læringsprosess. På dette grunnlaget forstås GenKI som et supplerende kulturelt redskap for faglig og individuell bearbeiding, men ikke som en erstatning for menneskelig samhandling. ENGLISH ABSTRACT Authentic Leadership Develops Between People: Sociocultural Learning and GenKI as a Supplementary Cultural Tool Research on authentic leadership development is largely grounded in experiential learning and emphasizes individual reflection and experimentation. This study examines how pedagogical methods grounded in sociocultural learning contribute to authentic leadership learning and development and discusses the opportunities and limitations of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in such processes. The study is a qualitative, exploratory single-case study of an authentic leadership course in a business program, based on students’ written reflection assignments. The analysis shows that cultural tools and language made students’ interpretations available for feedback and further development through social interaction. The learning process particularly fostered self-awareness, balanced processing, and relational orientation, while authentic behavior was less clearly documented. The study thus promote authentic leadership development as a culturally mediated and socially embedded learning process. Accordingly, GenAI is understood as a supplementary cultural tool for conceptual learning and individual reflection, but not as a substitute for human interaction.

papers.title: Bruk av generativ KI i markedsføring: Hva skjer i norske bedrifter?
papers.authors: Natalie Le, Nina M. Iversen, Magne Supphellen, Carmel T. Foley, Leif E. Hem
papers.abstract: Denne artikkelen diskuterer bruken av GenKI innen fagfeltet markedsføring. Litteraturen indikerer at markedsføringsoppgavene som i dag løses i norske bedrifter av mennesker, i stor grad kan erstattes av GenKI. En McKinsey rapport fra 2026 hevder at 2/3 av alle markedsførings-oppgaver kan utføres av GenAI. Hvis disse spådommen slår til, får det store konsekvenser for antall ansatte og nyansettelser med markedsføringskompetanse. Det får også konsekvenser for utdanningsinstitusjoner og fagfeltet markedsføring. Artikkelen presenterer resultatene fra en spørreundersøkelse for å avdekke bruken av GenKI i norsk næringsliv. Undersøkelsen ble gjennomført blant ansatte som jobber med salg og markedsføring. Respondentene (N=200) svarte på spørsmål om omfanget av deres bruk av GenKI for å løse arbeidsoppgaver innen markedsføring. Resultatene indikerer en svært lav bruk av GenKI for å løse markedsføringsoppgaver i egen jobb. Av de totalt 20 arbeidsoppgavene innen områdene markedsinnsikt, markedsplaner, produkt- og tjenesteutvikling og markedskommunikasjon fant man et totalt gjennomsnitt på 2,07 på en fempunkts skala. Den «høyeste» verdien var 2,31. Det betyr svært lav adopsjonen av GenKI for å løse bedriftenes markedsføringsoppgaver. Budskapet er at norsk næringsliv trenger kompetanse om markedsføring mer enn noen gang. Skal bruken av GenKI økes er det behov for intern markedsføring for å øke bruk og formidle nytteverdi. Nytten av GenKI for å forbedre produktene og derigjennom øke opplevelsen av innovasjon indikerer også at GenKI er et supplement – snarere enn en løsning som gjør mennesker overflødige. Resultatene viser også at økt bruk av GenKI forbedrer bedriftenes resultater (lønnsomhet og vekst). GenKI er derfor kommet for å bli. ENGLISH ABSTRACT Use of Generative AI in Marketing: What Is Happening in Norwegian Companies? This article discusses the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) within the field of marketing. The literature suggests that many marketing tasks currently performed by humans in Norwegian companies can potentially be replaced by generative AI. A McKinsey report from 2026 claims that two-thirds of all marketing tasks can be carried out by generative AI. If these predictions prove accurate, the implications for the demand for marketing professionals and future hiring practices will be substantial. It will also have significant consequences for educational institutions and the marketing discipline itself. The article presents the results of a survey designed to examine the use of generative AI in Norwegian businesses. The survey was conducted among employees working in sales and marketing. Respondents (N = 339) answered questions regarding the extent to which they use generative AI to perform marketing-related tasks in their jobs. The results indicate a relatively low level of generative AI usage for marketing tasks. Across 20 work activities within the areas of market insight, marketing planning, product development, and marketing communications, the overall mean score was 2.25 on a five-point scale. The highest score recorded was 2.45. These findings suggest a relatively low adoption rate of generative AI for carrying out marketing tasks in Norwegian companies. The main conclusion is that Norwegian businesses need marketing expertise more than ever. Increasing the use of generative AI will require substantial investments in competence development, and educational institutions can play a crucial role in this process. The adoption of generative AI has the potential to improve products, enhance perceptions of innovation, and strengthen customer relationships. This indicates that generative AI serves as a complement to human expertise rather than a substitute that makes people redundant. Furthermore, the results show that greater use of generative AI is associated with improved business performance, including profitability and growth. Generative AI is therefore here to stay.

papers.title: Kunstig intelligens i regnskap og revisjon: Hvilken kompetanse blir viktig for nyutdannede?
papers.authors: Ellen M. Kulset, Kjell Magne Baksaas, Tonny Stenheim
papers.abstract: Denne artikkelen undersøker hvilken kompetanse nyutdannede innen regnskap og revisjon trenger i et arbeidsliv preget av kunstig intelligens (KI), automatisering og dataanalyse, og hvilke implikasjoner dette har for masterutdanningen i regnskap og revisjon (MRR). Studien bygger på en kunnskapsoppsummering av internasjonal forskningslitteratur om endrede arbeidsoppgaver, kompetansebehov og utdanningsmessige konsekvenser for tidlige karriereløp i regnskaps- og revisjonsprofesjonen. Gjennomgangen viser at KI ikke gjør tradisjonell regnskaps- og revisjonskompetanse mindre relevant. Tvert imot synes grunnleggende fagforståelse, profesjonelt skjønn og kritisk vurderingsevne å bli viktigere når rutinepregede oppgaver automatiseres eller støttes av digitale verktøy. Samtidig må fagkompetansen suppleres med fagspesifikk digital kompetanse, teknologiforståelse og evne til å kommunisere og samhandle om analyser, risikoer og vurderinger. Artikkelen argumenterer for at MRR-utdanningen bør videreutvikles gjennom integrering av KI, dataanalyse og autentiske læringsformer i eksisterende regnskaps- og revisjonsemner, heller enn ved å erstatte kjernefag eller prioritere opplæring i enkeltverktøy. English abstract Artificial Intelligence in Accounting and Auditing: Consequences for Recent Graduates' Entry into the Workforce – What Knowledge and Skills Will Be Important in the Future? This article examines the competencies that accounting and auditing graduates need in a labour market shaped by artificial intelligence (AI), automation and data analytics, and discusses the implications for Norwegian master’s programmes in accounting and auditing (MRR). The study is based on a scoping review of international research on changing entry-level tasks, competence requirements and educational responses in the accounting and auditing profession. The review indicates that AI does not make traditional accounting and auditing knowledge less relevant. Rather, foundational disciplinary knowledge, professional judgement and critical evaluation skills appear to become more important as routine tasks are automated or supported by digital tools. At the same time, this knowledge must be complemented by domain-specific digital competence, technological understanding, and the ability to communicate and collaborate on analyses, risks and professional assessments. The article argues that MRR programmes should be developed by integrating AI, data analytics and authentic learning activities into existing accounting and auditing courses, rather than by replacing core disciplinary content or focusing narrowly on training in specific tools.

papers.title: Vurderingspraksis i møte med generativ KI – en casestudie
papers.authors: Lise Lillebrygfjeld Halse
papers.abstract: Generativ KI representerer en transformativ teknologi som utfordrer akademisk praksis og potensielt akademias rolle som kunnskaps- og sertifiseringsinstitusjon i samfunnet. Når KI-verktøy kan produsere akademiske besvarelser på høyt nivå, reises spørsmålet om hjemmeeksamen fortsatt er et gyldig instrument for å måle studentenes faktiske kunnskaper og ferdigheter. Denne artikkelen undersøker hvordan Høgskolen i Molde, en institusjon med strategisk satsing på nettbaserte studier og høy andel hjemmeeksamen, har håndtert de utfordringene generativ KI stiller til vurderingspraksis. Gjennom en case-studie basert på interne dokumenter, eksamensstatistikk og medieomtale viser artikkelen at institusjonen i stor grad har valgt «business as usual» fremfor å iverksette systematiske praksisendringer. Artikkelen argumenterer for at den observerte institusjonelle passiviteten kan forstås i lys av spenningen mellom en akademisk logikk der faglig integritet og læringsutbytte er sentrale verdier, og en markedslogikk der studiepoengsproduksjon og inntekter veier tyngst. Caset illustrerer hvordan denne konflikten i institusjonelle logikker kan hemme nødvendig omstilling, og understreker behovet for nasjonal koordinering og regulering fremfor å overlate ansvaret til den enkelte institusjon. ENGLISH ABSTRACT Assessment Practices in Light of Generative AI Generative AI represents a transformative technology that fundamentally challenges academic practice and potentially the role of higher education institutions as producers and certifiers of knowledge. As AI tools become capable of producing high-quality academic responses, the validity of take-home examinations as instruments for measuring students' actual knowledge and skills is called into question. This article examines how Høgskolen i Molde – an institution with a strategic commitment to online education and a high proportion of take-home examinations – has responded to the challenges generative AI poses to assessment practice. Through a case study drawing on internal documents, examination statistics, and media coverage, the article shows that the institution has largely opted for business as usual rather than implementing systematic changes to its assessment practices. The article argues that the observed institutional passivity can be understood in light of the tension between an academic logic, in which academic integrity and student learning outcomes are core values, and a market logic in which credit point production and revenue take precedence. The case illustrates how this conflict between institutional logics can impede necessary adaptation and underscores the need for national coordination and regulation rather than leaving the responsibility for change to individual institutions.

papers.title: Kunstig intelligens i regnskapsførerutdanningen: sovepute eller læringsverktøy?
papers.authors: Marianne Berggaard Breili, Tonny Stenheim, Sinem Acar-Burkay, Åsmund Pettersen
papers.abstract: Generativ kunstig intelligens (KI) utfordrer etablerte forutsetninger for undervisning, vurdering og utvikling av kritisk refleksjon og profesjonell dømmekraft i regnskapsførerutdanningen. Samtidig endres regnskapsførerrollen i retning av mer analyse, kontroll, rådgivning og profesjonell skjønnsutøvelse. Denne artikkelen undersøker hvordan regnskapsførerstudenter bruker KI i læringsarbeidet, og hvordan undervisningen kan utformes for å styrke kritisk refleksjon og profesjonell dømmekraft. Studien bygger på en kvalitativ casestudie av en studentgruppe i regnskapsførerspesialiseringen. Datagrunnlaget består av studentenes refleksjonsnotater, arbeidskrav og observasjoner fra undervisningen. Funnene viser at KI brukes aktivt som støtteverktøy, særlig til forklaringer, strukturering og idéutvikling, men at studentene erfarer betydelige risikoer knyttet til feilaktige kilder og svekket faglig forståelse. Artikkelen argumenterer for at læringseffekten av KI avhenger av pedagogisk design. Når KI-bruk gjøres eksplisitt, dokumenteres og underlegges faglig kildekontroll, kan teknologien støtte utviklingen av kritisk refleksjon. Uten slike rammer kan KI fungere som en kognitiv sovepute. English abstract Artificial Intelligence in Accounting Education: Crutch or Educational Tool? Generative artificial intelligence (AI) challenges established premises for teaching, assessment, and the development of critical thinking and professional judgment in accounting education. At the same time, the role of the accountant is shifting towards greater emphasis on analysis, control, advisory work, and professional judgment. This article examines how accounting students use AI in their learning processes, and how teaching can be designed to strengthen critical reflection and professional judgment. The study is based on a qualitative case study of one student group in an accounting specialization. The empirical data consists of students’ reflection notes, compulsory assignments, and classroom observations. The findings show that accounting students use AI actively as a support tool, particularly for obtaining explanations, structuring their work, and idea development. However, students also experience significant risks related to inaccurate sources and weakened subject-matter understanding. The article argues that the learning effects of AI depend on pedagogical design. When AI use is made explicit, documented, and subjected to discipline-specific source verification, the technology can support critical reflection. Without such structures, AI may function as an inferior substitute for critical thinking and reflection.

papers.title: PDF-SmartAI - An AI Study Companion for Uploaded Textbooks: A Book-Grounded Question-Answering System Using In-Browser PDF Extraction and Google Gemini
papers.authors: Fariya Malkani, Perseus Bhavnagri
papers.journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.abstract: Students increasingly turn to general-purpose AI chatbots for help with their studies, yet these chatbots answer from what they absorbed during training rather than from the textbook a student is examined on, and they can state wrong facts with confidence. This paper presents PDF-SmartAI, a zero-cost web application in which a student uploads up to two PDF textbooks and asks questions that an assistant, AI Buddy, answers only from that book, citing the page numbers it used and saying so when the book does not cover a question. Text is extracted entirely inside the browser by PDFium compiled to WebAssembly, split into page-aware chunks, stored per user in Cloud Firestore under owner-only security rules, and sent to Google Gemini through Firebase AI Logic on free tiers — the whole book when it is short (up to 100,000 characters), otherwise the eight chunks chosen by a plain-Dart keyword retriever. The study is secondary research combined with the evaluation of a built artefact; no participants were recruited. A public global survey of higher-education students (analytic n = 12,909) shows a moderate positive association between how much students use ChatGPT and how useful they find it for learning (Spearman ρ = 0.376, p < .001), while a substantial share of students (44.3%) agree that ChatGPT might mislead with inaccurate information (Wilcoxon z = 21.286, p < .001). On 10,570 SQuAD v1.1 questions over 13 synthetic books, the app’s own retrieval code placed the answer-bearing passage among the eight excerpts sent to the AI for 94.9% of questions, far above a random baseline (4.9%) and within 0.05 of BM25 (95.7%), although statistically slightly below it. All three hypotheses are supported. AI answer quality was checked only through live smoke tests and remains to be benchmarked.

papers.title: Use and Perceptions of AI Chatbots for Mental Health Support Among Adults With Lived Experience: Cross-Sectional Survey Study (Preprint)
papers.authors: Haruka Notsu, Phuong Anh Hue Nguyen, Matthew Flathers, Sean Ryan, Jill Noorily, Leah Wentworth, Christine Crawford, Michael Wood, Daniel H. Gillison, John Blake Torous
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used for mental health support, but little is known about how adults with lived experience of mental health conditions use and perceive them. Most prior surveys have relied on crowdsourced, social media, or general population samples. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to characterize general and mental health–related AI chatbot use, perceived helpfulness and harm, and disclosure of use to mental health providers among adults connected to a national mental health organization in the United States. METHODS We conducted a cross-sectional, web-based survey of adults recruited through newsletters and mailing lists of the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) between March and May 2026. Analyses were primarily descriptive, with exploratory Wilcoxon rank-sum tests and logistic regression RESULTS Of 454 participants, 316 (69.6%) had used an AI chatbot; use was more common among younger participants and those with a current mental health diagnosis. Among users, 133 (42.1%) reported using a chatbot for mental health purposes; use was typically brief, focused on information gathering and in-the-moment emotion regulation, and most rated them helpful. Among 95 participants with a mental health provider, 14 (14.7%) had discussed their AI use with their provider; more frequent use was associated with disclosure (odds ratio 1.67, 95% CI 1.20–2.38). CONCLUSIONS AI chatbots may function as accessible support tools for information seeking and in-the-moment coping. However, their use remains largely undiscussed with clinicians.

papers.title: Generative AI Use in Learning and Research Among Undergraduate Clinical Medical Students in China: A Task-Recall Qualitative Study (Preprint)
papers.authors: Lei Qiu, Xiangli Wan, Ying Wang, Shiye Deng, Jie Liu, Qian Tan
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Background: Undergraduate medical students increasingly use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for learning and research-related tasks. However, less is known about how they refine prompts, revise outputs, verify information, and negotiate boundaries within specific educational tasks. OBJECTIVE Objective: This study aimed to explore how undergraduate clinical medical students in China described using GenAI in specific learning and research tasks, focusing on prompt refinement, output revision, verification, and ethical and cognitive boundary negotiation. METHODS Methods: We conducted individual semistructured remote interviews via WeChat voice calls or telephone using a task-recall approach with 50 undergraduate clinical medical students recruited through purposive sampling, supported by social media outreach and peer referral. Participants varied in training year, sex, internship status, and self-reported GenAI use. Interviews were conducted in Mandarin Chinese, audio-recorded in full with participants’ permission, transcribed verbatim, deidentified, and analyzed using codebook-informed thematic analysis with iterative team discussion. RESULTS Results: The analysis generated five interrelated themes: convenience-driven entry into AI use, iterative co-construction of outputs for medical learning, critical verification before trust, ethical and cognitive boundary negotiation, and perceived institutional support needs. These themes informed an interpretive process model that distinguished reported task practices from perceived institutional support needs. Participants described using GenAI under task pressure, refining prompts, adapting outputs, and checking claims and references against other sources. Verification could prompt further revision, while concerns about academic integrity, independent reasoning, and group responsibility shaped decisions about whether and how outputs were used. Participants also described the workload involved in checking plausible errors and requested clearer rules, task-based training, and tools with traceable sources. CONCLUSIONS Conclusions: Participants’ accounts suggest that GenAI use in medical learning involves iterative revision, verification, and boundary negotiation. The findings highlight verification and accountability as priorities for task-based AI literacy education. The model reflects reported practices and does not establish verification effectiveness or improvements in learning outcomes.

papers.title: Mapping the Research Landscape and Global Trends: A Bibliometric Analysis of Event-related Potential in Alzheimer’s Disease
papers.authors: Suxiao Gang, Fu Jian, Boxu Xie, 秦晓楠 Qin Xiaonan, Kaiyuan Hu, Junli Zhen
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: There is an urgent need for objective biomarkers to facilitate early diagnosis and dynamic monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Event-Related Potential (ERP), as a neuroelectrophysiological technique with high temporal resolution, shows great promise in addressing this demand. However, the macro-level developmental trajectory, research status, and frontier directions within this field remain to be systematically elucidated. This study employs bibliometric methods to delineate the development trends, knowledge structures, and research frontiers of ERP applications in AD, thereby offering a novel perspective for early diagnosis, dynamic monitoring, and efficacy assessment. METHOD: Publications related to ERP and AD were retrieved and screened from the Web of Science Core Collection. A comprehensive quantitative and visual analysis was conducted using Microsoft Excel, CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix package in R. The analysis covered publication trends, national/institutional collaboration networks, author co-occurrence, core journals, reference and keyword co-occurrence, and clustering. RESULTS: The number of annual publications in this field continued to grow. The United States, China, and Italy were the most productive countries, whereas the cooperation network among institutions and authors was decentralized. Keyword clustering identified six major research topics: P300/N200, Mismatch Negativity (MMN), N170, N400, Olfactory Event-Related Potential (OERP), and Electroencephalography (EEG). DISCUSSION: An analysis of the global research landscape reveals that ERP research has developed from an exploratory tool in the field of AD to an active research field of neuroscience. Journal and citation analysis indicate that the field has distinct clinical problem-driven features; keyword cluster analysis revealed six major themes corresponding to classical cognitive assessment, early sensory memory, and social cognition. Thematic analysis revealed that MMN and other ERP components that are sensitive to early abnormalities may become future research hotspots; however, the overall cooperation in this field still shows a certain degree of geographical concentration and institutional dispersion. In the future, it is necessary to build a closer international and interdisciplinary cooperation network, establish a standardized ERP evaluation scheme, and embed it throughout the entire process of early identification, staging, and monitoring of the effect of intervention in AD. CONCLUSION: This research systematically presents the current state of research, hotspots, and evolutionary trends in ERP in the field of AD. The results suggest that in the future, a closer international and interdisciplinary cooperation network and further prospective clinical validation are needed to clarify the diagnostic performance and practical application value of ERP, thereby promoting its clinical application.
