papers.title: Effects of diagnostic thresholds for gestational diabetes on perinatal mental health: Data from the GEMS randomised clinical trial
papers.authors: Phyllis Ohene‐Agyei, Greg  D. Gamble, Thach Tran, Jane Elizabeth Harding, Caroline Anne Crowther
papers.abstract: AIM: To assess the effect of diagnosis using the lower International Association of the Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) criteria compared with the higher New Zealand criteria on perinatal mental health. METHODS: Secondary analysis of the GEMS Trial, a randomised trial assessing optimum glycaemic diagnostic thresholds for gestational diabetes. Women completing any questionnaire assessing anxiety (6-item State-Trait Anxiety Inventory >15), depression (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale >12) or health-related quality of life (SF-36) at enrolment, 36 weeks' gestation or 6 months postpartum were eligible. Generalised linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, BMI, recruitment centre, and gestational age at randomisation generated adjusted relative risks (aRR) and adjusted mean differences (aMD). RESULTS: Among 3452 women, 1737 (50.3%) were randomised to the lower criteria group and 1715 (49.7%) to the higher criteria group. No significant differences were observed between groups in anxiety, depression, or mental health-related quality of life at 36 weeks' gestation or 6 months postpartum after adjustment for baseline scores. However, women with mild GDM diagnosed and treated under the lower criteria reported better general health, vitality, social functioning, and postpartum mental component summary scores. CONCLUSION: Use of the IADPSG criteria does not adversely affect maternal perinatal mental health.

papers.title: Why this AI app? The impact of generative artificial intelligence on educators’ choices in educational apps
papers.authors: Emma Liptrot, Adam Kenneth Dubé
papers.abstract: In elementary education, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being incorporated into educational applications, despite still-emerging evidence of its effects on children’s learning and development. Educators, who are already overwhelmed with choice in the commercial app space, may increasincly have to decide whether to incorporate GenAI-enabled apps for their classrooms. Thus, the present study investigates how mentioning GenAI in app store descriptions impacts K-6 educators’ selection of educational apps. Over two studies, K-6 educators (each n = 101) from Canada, the US, and the UK viewed and evaluated eight researcher-created educational math apps with and without GenAI. Study 1 tested whether mentioning GenAI in app descriptions affected educators’ app evaluations but found no effect. In Study 2, results from a repeated measures MANOVA revealed that educators rated apps without AI higher than those mentioning GenAI, but there were no significant effects of GenAI on likelihood to download or willingness to pay for apps. A hierarchical cluster analysis identified three distinct groups of educators: 1) selectors (n = 28), who exhibited a preference for downloading, rating, and paying for apps including GenAI; 2) agnostics (n = 59), who exhibit minimal preferences; and 3) avoiders (n = 14), who prefer apps without AI. Most educators were agnostic to the use of GenAI in educational apps, highlighting the need to support educators’ informed decisions about when to adopt GenAI tools and encourage critical evaluation of GenAI’s role in education. More research is needed to understand how educators’ GenAI preferences relate to their attitudes, knowledge, and use of GenAI.

papers.title: Classification of motor imagery EEG signals using CNN–Transformer hybrid models
papers.authors: Joel Cuascota, Noel Pérez, Jorge Oliveira, María Baldeon-Calisto, Nathaly Orozco Garzón, Henry Carvajal Mora, José David Vega Sánchez, Edgar Márquez
papers.abstract: Motor imagery-based brain–computer interfaces aim to translate electroencephalographic activity into control commands without requiring overt movement. However, strong inter-subject variability, exacerbated by the limited spatial resolution of compact electrode montages, makes subject-independent decoding particularly challenging. This work presents a compact hybrid convolutional neural network–Transformer architecture designed for stable binary left/right motor imagery decoding using a low-density eight-channel sensorimotor montage. The model integrates convolutional feature extraction with a parameter-efficient temporal self-attention mechanism to capture both localized spatiotemporal patterns and long-range temporal dependencies in the electroencephalographic signal. Under strict subject-wise five-fold cross-validation on the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery dataset, the proposed convolutional neural network–Transformer achieved a mean macro F1-score of 0.816. Moreover, the statistical analysis revealed no significant performance difference ( p > 0.05 ) relative to larger architectural variants, thus justifying the selection of the proposed compact model for its computational efficiency and scalability. With only 0.232 million parameters and approximately 0.034 giga-floating-point operations per forward pass, the proposed convolutional neural network–Transformer constitutes a compact and resource-efficient backbone that supports low-latency subject-independent motor imagery decoding under low-density EEG.

papers.title: Single-channel wearable EEG for ADL recognition in Healthy and Epileptic cohorts using MODWT-MRA and machine learning
papers.authors: Mahdia Binte Maksud, Sadman Rahman, Md. Mehedi Hasan Bhuiyan, Tahiya Iffat Majumder, Kazi Newaj Faisal
papers.abstract: Wearable single-channel EEG is increasingly used to monitor epileptic patients outside the clinic, but the physical activity of daily living (ADL) continuously shapes the recorded signal. This activity-coupled variability is typically discarded as noise, even though it holds recoverable contextual information. Until now, EEG-based human activity recognition (HAR) has been studied almost exclusively in healthy participants under controlled lab conditions, leaving ADL recognition in clinical epileptic populations unaddressed. This study introduces a single-channel frontal EEG framework for ADL recognition, evaluated jointly on healthy, epileptic, and combined cohorts. As ambulatory EEG is multicomponent and nonstationary, a five-level maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform-multiresolution analysis (MODWT-MRA) with the Coiflet-3 wavelet decomposes each epoch into five frequency-resolved detail components, from which a compact 55-dimensional handcrafted descriptor is extracted and classified using an ensemble learner. Two recognition granularities are considered: a three-class intensity scheme (stationary, light ambulatory, intense ambulatory) and a fine-grained eight-class individual-ADL scheme, tested across multiple temporal window lengths. Using class-balanced, recording-level holdout evaluation, the framework achieves three-state activity recognition accuracies of 79.7%, 89%, and 85.2% for the Healthy, Epileptic, and Combined cohorts, respectively, with the 5-second window consistently delivering strong performance across all three groups. The method is further tested on the eight harmonized individual ADLs, offering additional insight at the activity-specific level. To our knowledge, this is the first framework to jointly perform EEG-based ADL recognition in both healthy and clinical epileptic cohorts, extending single-channel activity profiling from controlled healthy settings to activity-aware wearable monitoring in clinical populations.

papers.title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification
papers.authors: Haoyang Feng, Kai Ang, Zengfa Deng, Chonghe Cui, Jialan Chen, Nanfeng Huang, Yi Feng, Jimei Zhang, Danlin Li, Zhen Kong, Zicheng Cai, Yongjian Sun, Yusheng Yang
papers.abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1 , Zhx3 , Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

papers.title: An explainable machine learning framework for student engagement analysis and examination proctoring using behavioral intelligence
papers.authors: Muhammad Kamal Hossen, Mohammad Shorif Uddin
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of online education has created a need for intelligent systems that monitor student engagement and maintain academic integrity during remote learning and assessment. Current solutions often rely on single-modality data, offer limited interpretability, and do not adequately support real-time educational decisions. This study presents an integrated, explainable framework that combines online class attention monitoring with examination proctoring. The framework uses advanced computer vision and ensemble machine learning to extract multimodal behavioral cues from webcam streams through five modules: face detection, hand tracking, head pose estimation, mobile phone detection, and eye gaze tracking. Two behavioral datasets were developed, containing 6,000 records for attentiveness monitoring and 5,500 for cheating detection. Features were evaluated using several machine learning models, with a Bayesian-optimized XGBoost classifier achieving the best results. The framework achieved 99.67% accuracy and 99.63% F1-score for attentiveness classification, and 99.55% accuracy with a 99.53% F1-score for cheating detection. Five-fold cross-validation confirmed robust generalization and stable convergence. Feature selection improved computational efficiency by reducing dimensionality without sacrificing predictive performance. Explainable AI methods, including SHAP and LIME, identified head-pose deviation, gaze behavior, mobile phone use, and hand-object interaction as the most influential behavioral indicators. The composite cheating risk score (CCRS) provides a clear, interpretable measure of examination risk. By combining accuracy, transparency, privacy-preserving local processing, and scalability, the proposed framework offers a practical and reliable solution for intelligent monitoring and assessment in modern online learning environments.

papers.title: Mindful community in agritourism: Fieldwork on tea farms in China and coffee farms in the Philippines
papers.authors: Darcy Yue Lu, Allison M. Causing, Yao‐Chin Wang
papers.journal: Annals of Tourism Research Empirical Insights
papers.abstract: This study explores the intersection of mindful community and the co-creation of experiences between tourists and locals within the context of agritourism. Utilizing a comprehensive ethnographic methodology, field observations and interviews were conducted at three coffee farms in the Philippines and two tea farms in China. Our qualitative analysis identifies two interlocking components of mindful community: value-in-use (i.e., mindfulness, emotional place attachment, spontaneous culture conservation, social responsibility, and environmental sustainability), and co-production (i.e., open innovation, quality of life and well-being, and community resilience). This study advances value co-creation theory by clarifying how experiential evaluation and collaborative practice jointly generate value in agritourism. Lastly, the study offers practical implications for agritourism destination management and sustainable community development.

papers.title: Exploring trust in artificial intelligence in a problem-based computer programming course
papers.authors: Christian Basil Omeh, Ndudi O. Ezeamuzie, Chijioke Jonathan Olelewe
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used in programming education, but evidence concerning its relationship with achievement and learner trust remains limited in Nigerian higher education. This mixed-methods, quasi-experimental study examined whether integrating Google Gemini into problem-based learning (PBL) was associated with undergraduate students’ programming achievement and trust in AI. Sixty-two students from intact classes participated in a pre-test–post-test design: 29 received Gemini-enhanced PBL, and 33 received PBL without AI. Programming achievement and multidimensional trust were assessed before and after the intervention, while eight experimental-group students provided explanatory interview accounts. Quantitative data were analysed using ANOVA and ANCOVA, supplemented by HC3 robust estimation and bias-corrected bootstrapping; interview responses were coded thematically. The experimental group recorded higher post-test achievement than the control group. The robust adjusted mean difference was 16.42 points, 95% CI [14.16, 18.67]. Post-test trust scores were also higher in the Gemini-enhanced condition, while gender and the instructional condition × gender interaction were not statistically significant. Participants described Gemini as useful for problem clarification, algorithm development, debugging, collaboration, self-directed learning and immediate feedback; trust was associated with transparent prompts, responsible data use and human accountability. The findings suggest that structured Gemini support may complement PBL.

papers.title: The relationship between AI adoption and sustainable performance through digital transformation among overseas study agency SMEs in China
papers.authors: Yang Hu, Muhammad Faliq Abd Razak, Sufian Jusoh, Ahmad Rizal Mohd Yusof
papers.abstract: As governments and industries increasingly prioritize digital economy strategies and sustainability objectives, greater attention has been paid to the relationships among artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, digital transformation (DT), and sustainable performance (SP). However, limited research has examined these relationships in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly in the context of overseas study agencies (OSAs) in China. Therefore, this study aims to examine the relationships among AI adoption, DT, and perceived SP and to assess the mediating role of DT in the relationship between AI adoption and perceived SP. A quantitative research approach was employed using perceptual survey data collected from 554 individual respondents working in sampled OSA SMEs in China and reflecting their perceptions of organizational practices and performance. The proposed hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results indicate that AI adoption is positively associated with DT and perceived SP, while DT is positively associated with perceived SP and partially mediates the relationship between AI adoption and perceived SP. Overall, the findings provide empirical insights consistent with the perspective of Dynamic Capability Theory, suggesting that AI adoption is associated with perceived sustainable performance both directly and indirectly through digital transformation within the sampled service-oriented SMEs. The findings also offer practical implications for organizations and policymakers seeking to support sustainable and digitally enabled development.

papers.title: Augmented reality attributes and value co-creation in Pakistan's fashion retail sector
papers.authors: Sana Imran, Farasat Ali Shah Bukhari, Fizza Khalid, Muhammad Saqib Iqbal, Hassan Waqar Raja Raja
papers.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) is increasingly used in fashion retail to enhance customer experiences and facilitate interactive product engagement. However, limited evidence explains how specific attributes of AR experiences are associated with value co-creation and subsequent consumer responses in emerging markets. This study examines the associations between six AR experience attributes—immersion, aesthetic appeal, creative thinking, telepresence, connectedness, and commercial personalisation—and value co-creation in Pakistan’s fashion retail context. It further examines the relationships between value co-creation and behavioural intention and between behavioural intention and purchase intention. Data were collected from 216 consumers with prior experience using AR applications in fashion retail and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Commercial personalisation, connectedness, creative thinking, and immersion were positively associated with value co-creation, whereas aesthetic appeal and telepresence were not statistically significant. Value co-creation was positively associated with behavioural intention, which in turn was positively associated with purchase intention. The specific indirect-effect results indicated that commercial personalisation, creative thinking, and immersion were associated with purchase intention through the theoretically proposed sequence involving value co-creation and behavioural intention. These findings provide preliminary attribute-level evidence that personalised, cognitively engaging, relational, and immersive AR experiences are associated with stronger perceptions of value co-creation among fashion consumers in Pakistan. The results should be interpreted with caution because the cross-sectional design does not establish definitive causality, and discriminant validity was not demonstrated for all construct pairs.

papers.title: The image of scientists among neurodivergent children: a pilot study
papers.authors: Antonia Maria Alves da Silva, Ygor Raphael Gomes Eloy, Henrique Luis do Carmo e Sá, Adriana Rolim Campos
papers.abstract: Abstract This pilot study aimed to explore how a specific group of neurodivergent students in the 4th and 5th grades of elementary school represent scientists through drawing. To this end, the Draw-a-Scientist Test (DAST) was administered to 7 neurodivergent children with a diagnosed Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) who participated in the Young Scientists Project. The analysis of the drawing data was conducted using a multimodal vision-language model (ChatGPT, GPT-4o version) with the prompt “Evaluate the drawings using the Draw-a-Scientist Test checklist”, followed by independent researcher review to ensure consistency and contextual interpretation. Within this small pilot cohort ( n = 7), the drawings predominantly contained visual features commonly associated with traditional representations of scientists, featuring laboratory instruments, a predominantly laboratory environment, and male figures in 6 of the 7 drawings. Representations of scientists in diverse real-world contexts, or utilizing digital technology, books, or chemical formulas, were absent. While strictly illustrative and limited by the small sample size, these preliminary observations suggest a reliance on conventional perceptions of scientific figures among these participants. These preliminary observations warrant further investigation using larger cohorts to evaluate whether tailored, inclusive pedagogical strategies can broaden perceptions of science.

papers.title: Why AI Detectors Are Hurting Teaching: Moving from Suspicion to Trust in Higher Education
papers.authors: Mingzheng Hu

papers.title: AI and I—Distributed Authorships in the Swedish Upper Secondary Writing Classroom
papers.authors: Sara Silverdal, Carina Hermansson, Eva Lindgren
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper examines upper secondary students’ writing with Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) through a post-structural lens. The aim is to explore how authorship can be understood and described in the age of AI. The empirical material consists of three students’ recorded writing sessions and complementary interviews. Through rhizomatic mapping, the recordings are analyzed with Deleuze and Guattari’s notions of assemblage, affect and becoming, further extended through the concept of distributed authorship. The analyses map three dynamic assemblages in which writing and authorship are redistributed across heterogeneous relations. One assemblage foregrounds AI as the primary authorial agent; another enacts reciprocal human-AI co-writing; and a third positions AI as a threat to writing, creativity, and the climate. Writing with GenAI unfolds as a complex relational practice and authorship emerges as distributed between humans and non-humans. This study raises important questions for education to consider in writing instruction and in developing policies for writing with AI, such as questions of equity and ethics.

papers.title: “It Felt Like Practicing Telemedicine While Learning About It”: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Medical Students’ Reflective Diaries from a Telemedicine Elective Course Across two Cohorts
papers.authors: Motti Haimi, Irit Chudner
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Telemedicine has shifted from a niche modality to an established component of routine clinical practice in many health systems. Medical curricula are only beginning to address this shift. Reflective writing is increasingly used both as a pedagogical tool in medical education and as a data source for qualitative research on student attitudes. The experiences and conceptual journeys of pre-clinical medical students enrolled in dedicated telemedicine instruction are under-studied, particularly across multiple cohorts spanning the COVID-19 and post-pandemic periods. Methods We conducted a reflexive thematic analysis of 81 reflective diaries written by students (predominantly second-year medical students) enrolled in an elective telemedicine course at a single Israeli medical school across two cohorts distinguished by consent procedure: a retrospective cohort (2019–2024, n = 39), in which students who had already submitted diaries as a routine course component were contacted by email in 2025 (after ethical approval was granted) and asked to consent retrospectively to use of their diaries in research; and a prospective cohort (2025, n = 42), in which students were informed at the start of the course that the diaries would be analyzed and were asked to enclose a signed consent form with the diary they submitted. Analysis followed Braun and Clarke’s six-phase reflexive thematic analytic framework with an inductive orientation. Results Six overarching themes were identified: (1) a transformative conceptual journey from skepticism or naïveté to conviction; (2) telemedicine as the inevitable trajectory of medicine and a site of professional-identity formation; (3) recognition of telemedicine as a holistic discipline drawing on multiple lenses; (4) a productive tension between equity gains and erosion of the doctor–patient bond; (5) lived experience (as patient, family member, or in prior professional roles) functioning as an explicit interpretive lens; and (6) pedagogy and the medium of delivery, with the Zoom format read by students as enacting the course’s argument. The thematic structure was stable across cohorts. Distributional shifts in the prospective (2025) cohort included articulation of artificial-intelligence displacement concerns, focused engagement with breaking-bad-news as a boundary case, named concerns about defensive prescribing, the war (October 2023 onward) as a catalyzing event alongside COVID-19, increased advocacy for converting the course from an elective to a curricular requirement, and emerging attention to online patient and clinician communities as a distinct dimension of digital medicine. Conclusions This multi-cohort qualitative analysis identifies six stable themes and documents strong, consistent positive engagement with a pre-clinical telemedicine elective across both cohorts. Students describe the course as a formative and highly valuable learning experience, engage substantively with the multi-dimensional character of telemedicine, and read the Zoom delivery format as enacting the course’s content — an effect we describe as pedagogical resonance. Differences in the articulation of certain sub-themes (notably AI-displacement concerns and humanistic boundary cases such as breaking bad news) were more prominent in the prospective (2025) cohort and reflect the evolving discourse on digital medicine; these are cross-sectional differences and do not warrant longitudinal or causal inference. Taken together, our findings make a strong case for the inclusion of dedicated telemedicine instruction as a core component of the pre-clinical medical curriculum.

papers.title: From childhood to adulthood: an attempt to model long-term outcomes of ADHD using machine learning
papers.authors: Noa E. van der Plas, Frank Bennis, Barbara Franke, Catharina Hartman, Pieter J. Hoekstra, Anna Nijmeijers, Lennart Oblong, Nanda N. J. Rommelse, Emma Sprooten, Marjolein Luman, Jaap Oosterlaan, Siri D. S. Noordermeer
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Childhood-onset attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) persists in 28% to 58% of individuals, and is associated with adverse long-term outcomes, like additional psychiatric diagnoses and lower educational attainment. Knowing early life predictors for adverse long-term outcomes might help develop preventive measures, but too few have been identified using conventional statistical models. The current study investigated the potential of machine learning in identifying predictors for ADHD persistence and long-term functioning of adults with childhood-onset ADHD. Method A total of 133 adults ( M age = 29.53, SD age = 2.83, 75% males) from an 18-year prospective cohort study were assessed on ADHD persistence and long-term functioning. Machine learning models were developed using cross-validation, with and without additional resampling, and compared to a conventional logistic/linear regression model. With SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) we explored model behavior. Childhood predictors encompassed ADHD symptoms and treatment, other psychopathology, cognition, somatic characteristics, ADHD polygenic risk score, and parental demographics and psychopathology. Results Performance of all models for ADHD persistence and functioning (quality of life) was low. Best performing models included the logistic regression model with resampling for ADHD persistence (AUC’s all models = .52–.58; AUC logistic regression, resampling = .58), and the ridge regression model for long-term functioning (R 2 ’s all models = -0.36–0.02; R 2 ’s ridge regression = .02, RMSE’s all models = 2.07–2.42; RMSE’s ridge regression = 2.07). Conclusions Findings highlight the complexity of predicting long-term outcomes of ADHD. Model improvement is crucial before models can inform clinical practice, e.g., by increasing sample size and investigating additional predictors.

papers.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology: latest advancements and evolution
papers.authors: Florian Recker
papers.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in obstetrics and gynecology has evolved from a pragmatic bedside adjunct into a rapidly expanding clinical, educational and technological field. Since the publication of earlier narrative reviews, the discipline has been reshaped by handheld ultrasound systems, wireless probes, cloud-based image management, tele-ultrasound, artificial intelligence (AI) for image acquisition and interpretation, and the first specific practice guidance for POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology. This narrative review summarizes recent advances and proposes a clinically useful framework for the European ultrasound community. POCUS should be understood as a focused, problem-oriented and immediately actionable ultrasound examination performed and interpreted by the treating clinician. It is not a replacement for guideline-based screening, detailed fetal anatomy assessment, comprehensive transvaginal gynecologic imaging, Doppler surveillance or expert ultrasound. The strongest evidence supports POCUS for early pregnancy triage, confirmation of fetal viability and presentation, basic assessment of placental location and amniotic fluid, intrapartum evaluation of fetal head position and selected postpartum or gynecologic emergencies. In gynecology, POCUS can accelerate triage of acute pelvic pain, suspected ectopic pregnancy, intrauterine device position and adnexal pathology, but definitive risk stratification of complex masses remains a task for standardized specialist sonography. Technological progress has been substantial: handheld devices now provide diagnostically useful images for several focused tasks, AI-enabled blind-sweep protocols can estimate gestational age and fetal malpresentation in low-resource settings, and tele-ultrasound can extend expert support beyond tertiary centers. The next phase of OB/GYN POCUS will depend less on device availability than on implementation: indication-specific protocols, formal training, competency assessment, documentation, image archiving, infection control, data protection, quality assurance and clear escalation rules. POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology should therefore be framed as a governed clinical pathway rather than a device-driven shortcut.

papers.title: Bridging design disciplines: a literature review of biologically-inspired design, human-centered design, and human-robot interaction
papers.authors: Daniel Whitman, Deeksha Seth
papers.abstract: Abstract As robotic technologies become more integrated into society, there is a growing demand for systems that are not only technically robust, but also socially accepted, safe, and designed for long-term use. Biologically-Inspired Design (BID), Human-Centered Design (HCD), and Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) each offer valuable theories, methodologies, and tools to support the design and evaluation of such systems. Despite their complementary goals, these fields have largely developed in isolation. The lack of integration across BID, HCD, and HRI presents significant barriers for researchers and designers seeking to create biologically-informed, human-centered robots that facilitate meaningful interactions. In this work, an integrative literature review was conducted to examine the fields of BID, HCD, and HRI. An analytic categorization approach was used to categorize 63 papers into one or more of the three fields: 20 in BID, 27 in HCD, and 21 in HRI, with some papers categorized into multiple categories. Within each field, an inductive, interpretive coding and thematic analysis were used to identify key terminology, tools, methods, and conceptual frameworks, helping establish a shared vocabulary and summarize the state of the art. This was followed by a synthesis of limitations and field-specific gaps. Cross-field analysis revealed only four papers demonstrating overlap within the reviewed corpus: three showing implicit connections between HCD and HRI, and one showing implicit overlap between BID and HRI with indirect ties to HCD. This review lays the groundwork for more integrated design research by identifying opportunities for collaboration across BID, HCD, and HRI, highlighting the potential for more biologically-informed, user-centered, and socially responsive robotic systems.

papers.title: Flowing with displacements and tilts: surface operators in O(N) models
papers.authors: Jake Belton, Nadav Drukker, Biswajit Sahoo
papers.abstract: A bstract Defect conformal field theories have special operators of protected dimension known as displacements and tilts. They arise due to the breaking of global symmetries by the defect and the normalisations of their two-point functions are characteristics of the defect. In the case of surface defects, these normalisations are related to some of the anomaly coefficients in the surface effective action. To study these operators and their flows between different defect renormalization group fixed points we present an elegant approach using conformal perturbation theory that easily reproduces the known examples from the critical Wilson-Fisher O( N ) model in 4 − ε dimensions and allows us to construct new ones in other multiscalar theories. In all the systems that we study the flows are short and under full control, as is the change of the displacement and tilt normalizations. We point out some novel features like the existence of vortices when the defect conformal manifold is not simply connected. In addition to regular human labour, this work relied heavily on generative AI; see full disclosure in methodology section.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and venture capital: Revisiting sourcing, selection, and nurturing activities
papers.authors: Gary Dushnitsky
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Venture capital (VC) is an information‐intensive form of entrepreneurial finance conducted under extreme uncertainty. Investors must originate promising opportunities, select ventures with sparse and strategically disclosed information, and monitor and support firms after investment. Prior research documents both formal mechanisms (e.g., staged financing, syndication) and informal mechanisms built on referrals, reputation, and constant interaction. Geographic and social proximity enable these mechanisms by lowering the cost of obtaining contextual information and coordinating action. We develop a mechanism‐based account of how data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) reconfigure this established model. Our framework yields propositions on geographic dispersion in sourcing, portfolio selection, and the distinct effects of AI on monitoring versus value‐added support. It also identifies boundary conditions associated with institutional setting and heterogeneous AI adoption. Managerial Summary For venture capital firms, AI is not a single tool and adoption is not a binary choice. A fund may use data systems to identify founders, machine‐learning models to organize deal flow, generative AI to summarize diligence materials, or analytics to monitor portfolio companies. Each application changes a different part of the VC process. In sourcing, AI can widen the funnel beyond warm introductions and local ecosystems, especially in sectors such as software and e‐commerce where hiring, product, and customer signals are visible. In selection, AI can make diligence faster and more consistent, but models trained on past investments may favor ventures that resemble previously funded companies and may miss novel opportunities for which historical analogues are weak. In post‐investment activity, continuous operational data can partly replace physical presence for monitoring, while value‐add support such as customer introductions, recruiting, strategy advice, and founder coaching remain relationship‐intensive. The practical implication is a task‐level approach: automate codifiable search and processing, retain independent human judgment where uncertainty is fundamental, and use AI to strengthen rather than erode trusted investor–founder relationships. Funds also face organizational choices about building proprietary infrastructure, buying external tools, or combining the two. The appropriate configuration depends on data access, strategy, scale, and the activity in which the fund seeks advantage.

papers.title: AI Co‐Host Adoption and Traffic Governance in Live Commerce: Human Effort Incentives and Architecture Switching
papers.authors: Banglei Zhao, Hanli Hou
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) virtual streamers are making live‐commerce selling increasingly scalable, yet human explanation and trust remain central to purchase conversion. This paper develops a Stackelberg model of AI co‐host adoption under algorithmic traffic bias. The platform first chooses a transaction commission and an AI‐oriented traffic bias, after which the brand selects AI‐only selling, human‐only selling, or AI‐human co‐host selling. When a human streamer participates, the brand offers a performance commission, and the streamer chooses costly explanation effort. Algorithmic traffic allocation shapes both market exposure and the marginal return to human effort. Greater AI‐oriented traffic bias weakens effort under human‐only selling but strengthens it under AI‐human co‐hosting by enlarging the revenue base for human explanation. Once AI traffic support makes AI‐only selling more profitable than co‐hosting, human effort drops discontinuously to zero. The model identifies when AI co‐hosting complements human streamers, when traffic support instead induces substitution, and why a commission‐driven platform may favor more AI‐oriented exposure than a welfare‐aware benchmark. Extensions with return risk and two‐part contracts clarify how product fit and compensation design affect the value of co‐hosting. Robustness analyses show that the main qualitative results continue to hold under bounded nonlinear traffic allocation, nonlinear demand, and binding contract constraints.

papers.title: Preliminary Clinical Evaluation in Cross‐Sectional Imaging: A Qualitative Inquiry Into the Ethical Considerations in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: M.N.K. Anudjo, Sharon Docherty, Theophilus N. Akudjedu
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The evolving role of radiographers in Preliminary Clinical Evaluation (PCE), alongside the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into radiography workflows, is reshaping professional boundaries and enhancing patient care. However, this introduces ethical challenges that may impact PCE performance. This study explored the perspectives of cross-sectional imaging radiographers on the ethical dimensions of PCE and the potential impact of AI on the future practice of PCE. METHOD: A descriptive qualitative inquiry employing semi-structured interviews was conducted. A Purposive sampling method was used to recruit twelve cross-sectional imaging radiographers in a postgraduate medical imaging course at a UK university. Data were analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis with NVivo (v.20.0). RESULTS: Participants' clinical experience ranged (2 to 8 years), with 50% (n = 6) employed in public hospitals and the rest in private or mixed settings. Half (n = 6) had expertise in both CT/MRI and the rest in CT only. Notably, 42% (n = 5) practised in multiple countries. Two main themes were developed: (1) Ethical considerations of PCE with subthemes surrounding privacy and confidentiality, communication boundaries, and legal compliance. (2) Prospects of human-centred PCE in the era of AI, with subthemes including augmentation and support, workflow efficiency, PCE validation and quality assurance. CONCLUSION: Participants shared relevant ethical principles underpinning PCE practice and are cautiously optimistic about the potential impact of AI on PCE. Incorporation of PCE-specific ethics into radiography education and practice is necessary to ensure consistency, accountability and safety. Cautious integration of AI into radiography practice workflows is recommended to avoid professional deskilling and to preserve expertise.

papers.title: Affective symptoms in focal epilepsy: A scoping review of localization and lateralizing findings
papers.authors: Sofía S. Sánchez, A. Lagunas, Emily K. Acton, S. Guevara‐Lazo, Enrique J. Carrazana, Brin E. Freund, Fábio Augusto Nascimento, Sándor Beniczky, William O. Tatum
papers.abstract: Emotional experiences during focal seizures are often misinterpreted as psychiatric disorders. We aimed to evaluate symptoms involving affective symptoms at seizure onset. We aimed to identify the most prevalent affective symptoms at seizure onset and characterize their localizing and lateralizing value. We performed a scoping review based on Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses-extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. A systematic search identified records from 4 databases: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL (via EBSCOhost), and Web of Science. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts; discrepancies were resolved by consensus. This review focused on patients with focal seizures, as affective symptoms may occur in generalized epilepsies. The affective symptoms: fear, anxiety, panic, sadness, mystic, ecstatic, sexual, and mirth were identified, and semiology was evaluated in accordance with ILAE guidelines. Symptom onset, frequency, brain localization, and video-EEG monitoring technique were evaluated to assess localization and lateralization of regional networks. Scalp EEG, invasive EEG recordings, and electrical stimulation were analyzed. A total of 1276 documents were identified, with 98 studies included for review. Fear was the most frequently reported ictal emotion, identified in 274 patients (66%), predominantly in temporal lobe epilepsy. Sadness and sexual, ecstatic symptoms were also consistently associated with temporal networks. Mirth was more frequently reported with frontal onset seizures. Evidence, primarily from Class IV studies, reported right hemispheric predominance for ecstasy, mystic, and sexual symptoms at seizure onset. Ictal affective symptoms at seizure onset yield localizing information. The limbic system, especially the temporal lobe, followed by the frontal lobe, was the most common site of origin. Fear was the most common spontaneous and electrically elicited symptom, followed by anxiety. While bi-hemispheric lateralization occurred, right lateralization predominated. Recognizing paroxysmal affective symptoms as ictal phenomena may reduce misdiagnosis and aid presurgical evaluation in drug-resistant focal epilepsy.

papers.title: An Application of Machine Learning and Textual Analytics for Visualisation and Enhanced Interpretation of Sustainability Disclosure
papers.authors: Tarek Rana, Peter Öhman, Jan Svanberg, Mohammad Saiedur Rahaman, Faruk Bhuiyan, Md. Hafij Ullah, Parvez Mia
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Social and environmental accounting provides accountability mechanisms through which organisations communicate their sustainability practices to stakeholders. However, the increasing volume, complexity and diversity of sustainability disclosures make manual content analysis both labour‐intensive and susceptible to subjectivity. Machine learning and textual analytics offer promising approaches for systematically processing and visualising large qualitative datasets with greater consistency and transparency. This study explores how machine learning‐based textual analytics can be used to collect, analyse and visualise sustainability disclosure data in ways that enhance public accountability. More specifically, it focuses on how local governments use language to construct and communicate their sustainability commitments and performance. The empirical material consists of 237 annual reports from 79 local government areas in Victoria, Australia, covering the period 2015–2017. Drawing on a realist constructionist ontology, machine learning theory and stakeholder theory, the authors develop a machine learning‐based approach that transforms unstructured qualitative data into measurable insights. The methodology integrates VADER sentiment analysis, Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modelling and Doc2Vec embeddings with cosine similarity to assess the comprehensiveness of sustainability disclosures. The analysis reveals that sustainability disclosures exhibit predominantly positive to neutral sentiment, with the dominant themes relating to financial and environmental challenges. The reports were categorised into three comprehensiveness levels, with the majority demonstrating a medium level of sustainability disclosure. Temporal analysis further suggests distinct patterns in how local governments frame sustainability initiatives and indicates that sustainability is conceptualised as a multidimensional construct. The study makes a methodological contribution by demonstrating how machine learning can enhance the rigour, scalability and transparency of sustainability accounting research. It also extends realist constructionist ontology into the domain of computational analysis and provides practical benchmarking tools for local governments. For stakeholders, the proposed visualisation techniques offer methods for assessing public sector sustainability accountability.

papers.title: Physician Training for the AI Era
papers.authors: Jesse Burk‐Rafel, Robert M. Wachter
papers.abstract: This Viewpoint discusses the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education, and how physician training should change in parallel with AI use including emphasizing skills that AI makes more valuable, cultivating those it makes newly necessary, and carefully de-emphasizing those it makes less important.

papers.title: The Synergy of Green Entrepreneurship and AI Adoption in Enhancing Sustainable Business Performance Among SMEs in Indonesia
papers.authors: Sidharta, Ilfi Nur Diana, Misbahul Munir, Irmayanti Hasan, Fitri Romadhon, Yona Octiani Lestari, Eka Ananta, Annisa Lenanta, Nur Fadjrih Asyik, Rusdiyanto, Anin Dyah Luthfiani,  Bunga
papers.journal: Journal of Hunan University Natural Sciences
papers.abstract: This study examines the moderating role of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in the relationships among green entrepreneurial intention (GEI), green entrepreneurial behaviour (GEB), and sustainable business performance (SBP) among 151 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Gresik, East Java, Indonesia. The study also evaluates the direct effects of GEI on GEB and of GEB on SBP. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) after the measurement model was confirmed to demonstrate adequate validity and reliability. The results show that AI adoption has positive and significant effects on GEB and SBP. GEI also positively influences GEB, while GEB has a significant positive effect on SBP. However, the moderating effects of AI adoption are negative, indicating that greater AI adoption does not necessarily strengthen the relationships among green entrepreneurial intention, green entrepreneurial behaviour, and sustainable business performance. These findings suggest that the effectiveness of AI adoption depends on organizational readiness, digital competence, top-management support, data quality, and the firm’s ability to integrate AI into business processes. From a practical perspective, AI adoption should be supported by training, technological assistance, financial support, and digital-literacy development. Such measures may strengthen green entrepreneurial behaviour, improve sustainable business performance, and enhance the competitiveness of SMEs in response to growing sustainability demands. Keywords: artificial intelligence adoption; green entrepreneurial intention; green entrepreneurial behaviour; sustainable business performance. DOI https://doi.org/10.55463/issn.1674-2974.53.9.3

papers.title: Selective Activation of Brain Mentalizing Network in Human-Robot Conversation
papers.authors: Camilla Di Pasquasio, Marc Cavazza, Brigitte Bigi, Thierry Chaminade
papers.journal: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)
papers.abstract: With the rapid progress of conversational artificial intelligence, whether people attribute mental states to robots during spontaneous conversation becomes a novel question in human-robot interaction. Here, we combined automated detection of mental-state references in unconstrained humanhuman and human-robot conversations with functional magnetic resonance imaging to examine how such references affect brain activity during naturalistic conversations. We found that listening to robot utterances referring to mental states selectively increased activity in core regions of the mentalizing network, including the left temporoparietal junction, medial frontal cortex, and posterior cingulate cortex, whereas no comparable increase was found during human-human conversation. Effective connectivity analyses further showed that these robot utterances induced a distinct functional configuration of the mentalizing network, characterized by reduced influence of the medial frontal cortex on the temporoparietal junction. This pattern is consistent with a transient relaxation of contextual constraints on mentalizing when mental-state content is produced by a robot. Together, these findings show that conversations with robots can recruit neural mechanisms involved in human mentalizing, while engaging regulatory mechanisms that differ from those observed during comparable human-human conversations.

papers.title: Product Registration Strategies
papers.authors: Are Shivani, A.Tejaswini
papers.abstract: The case organization Vaisala was interested in finding out whether there was a need for a product registration that would attract customers. More specifically, the elements of added value were under the scope of this development work. The work was framed so that only the end-users of the company’s flagship product was under the scope. The initial idea came from the company’s Customer Experience Program which set the objectives for a product registration study. The development work followed the principles of service design and its process model called Double Diamond which gave structure to the work. Various service design methods and tools were used along the process such as benchmarking, theme interviews, Affinity Diagram tool, How Might We? tool, customer personas and customer journey map. The ideation session provided the relevant ideas for prototyping. The final prototype summarized the whole development work into practical concept of a portal. The order of this development work was first to investigate organization’s operating environment, the product management and stakeholders involved in the project in order to have better understanding of the matter. The theoretical framework addressed the themes of value proposition, value co-creation, customer experience, customer journey and customer engagement. This theory basis provided understanding for what elements are needed when developing service concept for customers. As a result, a prototype of a portal with value-added elements was created. The prototype includes features and functions which support customers in their internal processes by improving their communication and knowledge sharing. The outcome is an asset management tool for customers that enables case organization to support customers even better.

papers.title: Advancing Inclusive Higher Education Through Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities for Accessibility, Personalization, And Student Support
papers.authors: Dildora Nutfieva
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities to advance inclusive higher education by improving accessibility, personalizing learning experiences, and strengthening student support. Despite progress in inclusive education policies, students with disabilities continue to encounter barriers associated with inaccessible learning materials, inflexible teaching practices, limited assistive technologies, and insufficient institutional support. This article examines the theoretical foundations and research evidence concerning the application of AI in inclusive higher education. It adopts an integrative literature review approach to synthesize published research on AI-powered assistive technologies, adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring, and educational support services. Particular attention is given to three dimensions of inclusion: accessibility, personalization, and student support. Findings from existing reviews and a meta-analysis indicate that AI-based interventions have potential to improve learning outcomes and facilitate participation among students with disabilities. However, the available evidence is heterogeneous, and much of the experimental research has been conducted outside mainstream higher education. The article proposes an integrated conceptual framework connecting AI accessibility tools, personalized learning, and coordinated institutional support. It concludes that AI can contribute to more equitable higher education when implemented through human-centred, accessible, and ethically governed practices.

papers.title: La educación y los saberes emergentes
papers.authors: Judeicy Lara
papers.abstract: Grounded in the premise that the essence of education lies in presenting the world as a realm of possibility,this theoretical-reflective essay critically examines the tension between the disruptive promis of digital technologies and the persistence of anach­ ronistic pedagogical paradigms. This transformation rests upon three fundamental pillars: a pedagogy grounded in neurocognitive principles that respects neurodiversity and individual learning rhythms; a critical appropriation of techno-educational models and artificial intelligence; and an overarching horizon oriented toward Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), which fosters citizens aware of their interdependence with the planet. This study, which is focused on Latin America, reveals that technological adoption without such profound restructuring not only perpetuates existing divides, but may also exacerbate inequalities.Received: 10/09/2026 - Approved: 30/09/2026

papers.title: The Arts, Spirituality and Generative AI in Higher Education: A Defence of Writing
papers.authors: Sophie Claire Ward

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence supporting learning and research competency development among postgraduate nursing students: a scoping review
papers.authors: Xue Dong, 郑心宇
papers.abstract: This project documents the methods and analytical framework of a scoping review examining how generative artificial intelligence is used to support learning and research competency development among postgraduate nursing students. The review focuses on six competency domains: information literacy and evidence retrieval, evidence-based practice competency, research methodology and analytical skills, academic writing and scientific communication, critical thinking and research thinking, and AI literacy and responsible AI use. Study selection and data charting were completed before OSF registration; therefore, the registration is intended to provide a transparent record of the review methods rather than a prospective preregistration.

papers.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence into Institutional Arbitration: A Comparative Analysis of Procedural Readiness and Due Process Between India and Singapore
papers.authors: Surya Saxena, Mr. Deepak Bansal, M Taneja, Mr. Vishal Bansal, Ms. Akriti Gupta
papers.abstract: The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into international commercial arbitration introduces transformative procedural efficiencies alongside complex legal and constitutional challenges. This comprehensive research paper explores the regulatory, procedural, and doctrinal implications of utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) and automated legal reasoning tools within arbitral decision-making workflows. By establishing a robust comparative framework between India and Singapore, the study critically evaluates how institutional rules, statutory mandates, and judicial oversight manage the intersection of cutting-edge technology and fundamental guarantees of natural justice. The paper begins by contrasting Singapore’s mature, digitally integrated arbitral ecosystem—anchored by the SIAC 2025 Rules and advanced institutional governance protocols—with India’s rapidly evolving domestic framework comprising institutions such as the India International Arbitration Centre (IIAC) and the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA). It investigates the non-delegation doctrine, examining whether over-reliance on AI-generated legal reasoning and draft awards violates an arbitrator's core duty of independent evaluation under Section 34 of the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, and Singapore’s International Arbitration Act. Furthermore, the study analyzes severe cybersecurity and data governance vulnerabilities, contrasting India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act compliance requirements with Singapore's commercial data protocols during cross-border digital discovery. Finally, the research evaluates award enforceability hurdles under the New York Convention framework. It scrutinizes how national courts handle procedural challenges related to algorithmic opacity, data hallucinations, and public policy exceptions. Ultimately, the paper provides actionable regulatory reform recommendations and institutional guidelines for emerging arbitral seats to safeguard due process integrity and procedural fairness while safely embracing technological innovation.

papers.title: Human Robot Interaction
papers.authors: Nikolas Jakob
papers.abstract: Robot supported interactive learning design and evaluation.

papers.title: The Impact of Adopting Artificial Intelligence Techniques on Accounting information Systems` Reliability
papers.authors: ايناس ابو فرحة
papers.journal: المثقال للعلوم الاقتصادية والإدارية وتكنولوجيا المعلومات
papers.abstract: The Impact of Adopting Artificial Intelligence Techniques on Accounting information Systems` Reliability Abstract This study examines how using Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques affects accounting information system (AIS) reliability. Additionally, this study aims to bridge a gap in the literature by establishing the impacts of utilizing AI technology on the major reliability factors and how those factors impact commercial banks and Islamic banks listed on the Amman stock exchange. The study used a descriptive analytical research design and employed a structured questionnaire as the means for collecting responses from a sample of 15 banks. A total of 236 valid responses were obtained from the survey participants. Data analysis was conducted using SMART PLS4 software for evaluating the relationship of AI implementation with the dependability of AIS. The findings of this study suggest that the application of AI transforms the overall dependability of an AIS by accounting for nearly a third (34%) of the differences seen in various metrics used to assess reliability. Therefore, the availability of Artificial Intelligence is viewed as providing opportunities for improving both the dependability and the value of an organization’s AIS. In addition, this work adds to the knowledge base on the effect that adopting AI has on the reliability of an AIS within a financial institution. The study contributes to the existing literature by demonstrating the relationship between AI adoption and AIS reliability in the context of the banking sector, in conjunction with a well-established infrastructure for an AIS, and also advocates for providing management and staff with specialized training to assist them in the effective deployment of these new AI tools. The results also suggest that organizations aiming to improve their AIS through new technology can utilize these findings as a basis for a planning strategy to do so. Key Words: Artificial Intelligence Techniques, Reliability of Accounting Information Systems, and Banks.

papers.title: Governing AI Adoption: A Business Management Framework for Risk and Accountability in U.S. Enterprises
papers.authors: Md Shokran, Fahmida Akter, Mohd Salman Hossain Bhuiyan, Muhammad Farhan Nafees
papers.journal: American Journal of Economics and Business Management
papers.abstract: The wide-spread use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has revolutionized company decision making, improving forecasting, fraud detection, workforce planning and performance analytics. Yet in spite of these advantages, a lot of organizations experience severe governance issues in regards to accountability, risk possession, compliance and value realization. Past AI governance studies tend to focus on technical, algorithmic, or regulatory aspects, and provide little actionable advice for business managers, project managers, and business analysts who oversee AI implementation. This study poses a management-oriented framework called Governing AI Adoption: A Business Management Framework for Risk and Accountability in U.S. Enterprises that will work to facilitate responsible implementation of AI without the development of a new technical model. This study draws on a systematic review of the literature on governance of AI, as well as an empirical analysis of the >100,000 enterprise records available in the Enterprise GenAI Adoption & Workforce Impact Dataset. The dataset is used to understand trends in AI adoption, the impact on workforce, employee learning, productivity gains and employee attitudes toward AI within US companies, giving practical insights to companies' outcomes around implementing GenAI. The findings are used to build a Five-Layer Business Governance Framework: Strategic Ownership, Business Risk Classification, Oversight and Escalation Processes, Financial Accountability, Governance Maturity and Continuous Review. The framework utilizes common management practices such as RACI matrices, AI-specific risk registers, stage-gate governance reviews, KPI and ROI dashboards, and governance maturity assessments to help guide decisions through a structured process and enable organizations to take ownership. This study not only serves as a practical governance model for managing AI's strategic impact but also connects the theoretical study of technical AI governance with its real-world implications for business management. The proposed framework sees both academic and managerial contributions by defining a governance approach that is actionable and can facilitate responsible, sustainable and value-based AI usage in modern enterprises.

papers.title: METHODOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS OF USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN PROGRAMMING EDUCATION
papers.authors: Fayzullayeva Farog'at
papers.journal: SAMARALI TA’LIM VA BARQAROR INNOVATSIYALAR JURNALI
papers.abstract: The article analyzes the penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into programming education, their didactic opportunities and risks. A four-component methodological model is proposed for using AI tools while preserving students' independent programming skills and algorithmic thinking: staged use of AI, developing AI-collaboration competence, renewing the assessment system, and project-based learning. The model can be applied in teaching programming and computer science at higher education institutions.

papers.title: Neural Approaches to Educational Knowledge Graph Construction, Completion, and Reasoning
papers.authors: Gaganpreet Jhajj
papers.abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) play a key role in organizing structured data. However, their incompleteness limits applications in education and intelligent tutoring. This thesis investigates neural network methods for building, completing, and reasoning over KGs in educational settings. Four studies are presented. First, it evaluates Large Language Models (LLMs), such as GPT-4, for constructing and expanding Educational Knowledge Graphs, achieving high semantic similarity (0.875) with instructor-authored content. Second, it explores spiking neural network (SNN) architectures for interpretable, neuromorphic relational inference in KGs. Third, it develops an SNN-based KG embedding framework with learnable synaptic delays for energy-efficient prerequisite reasoning in intelligent tutoring systems. Finally, it compares Cache-Augmented Generation (CAG), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and long-context prompting for generating curriculum knowledge graphs from course materials across 36 courses, revealing trade-offs between graph size and local deployability.

papers.title: Understanding Human-AI Trust in Military AI Applications: A Multistage Human Factors Framework
papers.authors: Kangwon Kim
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in military systems to support intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, autonomous operations, logistics, command and control, and decision support. Effective use, however, depends not only on technical performance but also on how operators perceive, interpret, evaluate, and rely on AI outputs under uncertainty, time pressure, and adversarial interference. This study presents a conceptual integrative review informed by a structured supplementary literature search and synthesis. It synthesizes human factors, human–automation trust, human–AI teaming, military AI, and industrial engineering literature to develop an iterative multistage framework of human–AI trust in military applications. Trust is conceptualized as dynamic situational trust in a specific military AI system during task interaction, while dispositional, initial, and learned trust are treated as antecedent conditions. The framework distinguishes four analytically separable but functionally interdependent stages—perception, interpretation, evaluation, and trust judgment and reliance decision—and identifies four military-relevant moderators: system transparency, explainability, and behavioral predictability; data quality and information uncertainty; adversarial vulnerability; and operational and organizational context. The framework clarifies conceptual pathways to calibrated reliance, overtrust, and undertrust, and derives implications for task analysis, interface evaluation, human-centered design, operator training, and empirical validation.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHING AND LEARNING
papers.authors: Husenova Nargiza
papers.abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has become one of the most influential technologies in the field of education, particularly in foreign language teaching and learning. The integration of AI tools into English language education has created new opportunities for both teachers and students by providing personalized learning experiences, immediate feedback, and access to various digital resources. This paper examines the impact of artificial intelligence on English language teaching and learning, focusing on its advantages, applications, and possible challenges. AI-based technologies such as language learning applications, automated assessment systems, virtual assistants, and conversational tools help students improve their vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, and communication skills. Moreover, AI allows learners to study independently according to their individual needs and learning pace. For teachers, artificial intelligence provides support in lesson planning, creating educational materials, and evaluating students’ progress. However, despite its benefits, the use of AI also presents certain challenges, including dependence on technology, data privacy issues, and the need for teachers to develop digital competencies. The study concludes that artificial intelligence can significantly enhance English language education when it is used effectively and combined with traditional teaching approaches. AI should be considered not as a replacement for teachers, but as a powerful tool that supports more effective, interactive, and learner-centered language instruction.

papers.title: Finfluencers vs AI Financial Assistants: Who Influences Young Investors More?
papers.authors: Sonal Ronak Shah, AMUDA DEEKSHITHA
papers.journal: NOLEGEIN Journal of Management Information Systems
papers.abstract: The fast evolution of digital platform technologies and artificial intelligence has altered the way young investors receive financial information and make investments. Finfluencers - creators of financial information on social media, and AI financial assistants – technologies providing financial information have gained prominence and became significant sources of financial advice. This research paper is meant to examine the impact of finfluencers and AI financial assistants on young investors and understand the determinants that affect their preferences for one of the sources. Investment behavior, sources of financial information, trust, usage, and the impact of digital financial assistance on investment decisions are some of the areas which the study is focused on. Primary data will be gathered through a structured survey among young investors and students. The results of this research are meant to bring to light new preferences among young investors and determine whether the influence of human-generated financial advice is greater than the influence of AI financial advice. The findings further highlight the importance of understanding the relationship between demographic characteristics and investment-related behaviour. The study emphasizes that young investors should develop financial literacy and due diligence skills to assess the reliability of information received from both human influencers and AI-based tools. The findings provide insights into the changing preferences of young investors and the growing role of digital financial guidance in shaping investment decisions.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: A Socratic-Based Model for Cognitive Skill Development
papers.authors: Lujan Netri, Néstor Adrián Balich
papers.abstract: La creciente incorporación de herramientas de inteligencia artificial en el ámbito educativo ha transformado la forma en que los estudiantes acceden al conocimiento, ofreciendo oportunidades para personalizar la enseñanza y apoyar el aprendizaje. No obstante, su uso pasivo, centrado en la obtención de respuestas inmediatas, puede generar dependencia y afectar negativamente el desarrollo de habilidades cognitivas esenciales, como el pensamiento crítico, el razonamiento y la resolución de problemas. Asimismo, este fenómeno puede contribuir al aumento del burnout académico, manifestado en agotamiento emocional, desmotivación y sensación de ineficacia. Frente a este escenario, resulta necesario adoptar un enfoque que contemple tanto los beneficios como los desafíos de la integración de la inteligencia artificial, manteniendo la centralidad del factor humano. En este sentido, surgen propuestas que redefinen el rol de la IA como una herramienta de acompañamiento, basada en preguntas, reflexión y metodologías activas, orientadas a promover un aprendizaje más profundo y significativo. El presente trabajo, basado en una revisión documental, analiza el panorama actual del uso de la IA en los procesos educativos, identifica sus principales oportunidades y riesgos, y propone estrategias para su implementación responsable. De este modo, se plantea un modelo que no solo mejora el rendimiento académico, sino que también fortalece la autonomía, la capacidad de análisis y el desarrollo integral del estudiante, destacando la importancia de preservar la autonomía cognitiva mediante un uso ético y consciente de la inteligencia artificial.

papers.title: AI for Whom? - A Critical Study of Equity and the Digital Divide in Thailand’s AI Education Policy
papers.authors: Hathaichanok Phengnu
papers.journal: Gothenburg University Publications Electronic Archive (Gothenburg University)
papers.abstract: As Thailand advances its national agenda for artificial intelligence (AI) in education, questions arise about who stands to benefit and who risks being left behind. This study critically examines how equity and inclusion are represented in Thailand's emerging AI education policies and how these representations align with implementation realities across different school contexts. Adopting a qualitative interpretive design, it combines Critical Policy Analysis drawing on Bacchi's "What's the Problem Represented to Be?" approach, with the Digital Inclusion Framework. Three core official documents, the Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022–2027), the relevant Government Gazette announcement, and the OBEC AI Usage Guide (2025), were analyzed alongside semi-structured interviews with six educational stakeholders, including school directors, vice-directors, a national policy actor, and an education entrepreneur from urban and rural settings. The analysis shows that Thai policy consistently frames AI as an instrument of national modernization, economic competitiveness, and future workforce readiness, while saying comparatively little about the unequal conditions under which schools are expected to adopt it. In practice, schools with stronger infrastructure, funding, and institutional support were far better positioned to engage with AI, whereas smaller and rural schools faced unstable connectivity, maintenance burdens, heavy teacher workloads, and limited professional support. AI was most often used for administrative efficiency rather than transformative pedagogy, with richer forms of engagement concentrated in better-resourced schools. The study argues that equal technological provision does not produce equitable participation, and that current policy silences around rural disadvantage and teacher capacity risk reproducing existing inequalities. It concludes that meaningful AI integration in Thailand requires more context-sensitive, equity-oriented policy design. Methodologically, the study shows how combining the WPR approach with the Digital Inclusion Framework, and reading policy texts against practitioners’ accounts, can make policy silences visible and grounded in practice, distinguishing between silences that are absent, disconnected from AI provisions, or left non-operational.
keywords: What's the problem represented to be

papers.title: Early prediction of students at risk of low academic performance through data mining techniques and machine learning
papers.authors: Stella M. Gerzel, Magdalena Elisabet Brollo, Carlos Emanuel Aguirre, Gustavo Ariel Paszco
papers.abstract: El bajo rendimiento académico y el abandono durante los primeros años universitarios constituyen problemáticas relevantes para las instituciones de educación superior debido a su impacto sobre las trayectorias estudiantiles y los indicadores de permanencia. Este trabajo presenta una propuesta basada en técnicas de aprendizaje automático para la identificación temprana de estudiantes en riesgo académico en la carrera de Ingeniería en Sistemas de la Universidad Nacional del Chaco Austral (UNCAus). El estudio utiliza información correspondiente a 978 registros académicos de las asignaturas Algoritmos y Estructuras de Datos y Sistemas y Organizaciones de las cohortes 2024 y 2025. El conjunto de datos integra variables socioeconómicas, familiares, laborales, tecnológicas y motivacionales obtenidas mediante relevamientos institucionales. Se definieron tres problemas de clasificación: riesgo académico global (aprobación versus desaprobación o abandono), desaprobación académica y ausencia o abandono. Para cada caso se evaluaron modelos de Regresión Logística, Árboles de Decisión, Random Forest y XGBoost, utilizando validación cruzada estratificada y distintas estrategias de balanceo de clases. Los mejores resultados se obtuvieron mediante Random Forest para la predicción de riesgo académico global y desaprobación, y mediante XGBoost para la identificación de estudiantes con riesgo de abandono. Los modelos alcanzaron valores de ROC-AUC de hasta 0.69 en la predicción de abandono. Los resultados muestran el potencial de estas técnicas como herramientas de apoyo para la detección temprana de estudiantes vulnerables y la implementación de intervenciones pedagógicas preventivas.

papers.title: When the Exhibit Speaks Back A Research Through Design Study of Relational, Conversational, Role-playing AI in a Science-Center Learning Environment
papers.authors: Magnus Thyselius
papers.journal: Gothenburg University Publications Electronic Archive (Gothenburg University)
papers.abstract: Purpose: This thesis investigates how a relational, conversational, role-playing AI agent can be designed as part of a science-center exhibit. It examines how such an agent may support visitor curiosity and learning encounters, which interaction patterns and tensions emerge during testing in a live exhibition environment, and what design knowledge the case can contribute to the further development of conversational AI in science centers. The study was conducted at Universeum in Gothenburg, where a prototype designed to speak as Miriam, an Ethiopian mountain viper, was developed and tested in the reptilarium. Theory: The thesis draws on Dewey's account of experiential learning, Vygotsky's sociocultural theory of learning, and Bruner's understanding of narrative as a mode of meaning-making. Bickmore's Relational Agent Theory informs the analysis of the agent's social and conversational qualities. Research on role-playing language agents is used to examine persona stability, role consistency, and character design, while Burke and Copenhaver's work on anthropomorphism informs the analysis of how the snake persona mediates access to scientific content. Method: The study was conducted as a qualitative Research through Design project, based on Zimmerman et al.'s account of the approach and organized through five iterative cycles inspired by the Double Diamond. The empirical material consists of the design log, system prompts, factual reference documents, field notes, consent documentation, and transcripts from nine included live visitor interactions. The analysis started from concrete things that happened during the project, interpreted them with help from theory, and drew out what each one meant for the design. Results: The findings show that a relational conversational agent in a science-center exhibit cannot be understood only as a language model or prompt system. It must be designed as one whole exhibit, where the character’s voice, the facts it delivers, the limits on what it may say, how well it answers, and how it is physically set up all work together. The visitor material revealed opportunities for visitor-led inquiry, personal-character questions, perspective-taking, and short explanatory dialogue, as well as tensions involving question-answer mismatch, factual gaps, unclear speech input, over-humanization of the animal, and audio constraints. The thesis contributes six design principles: separate role logic from factual grounding while designing them together; treat answer relevance as part of relational design; use visitor transcripts as redesign material; use anthropomorphism as a bounded pedagogical strategy; treat the physical installation as part of the conversational artifact; and transfer design logic rather than a finished prompt.

papers.title: Beyond Flashcards: Integrating Generative AI into Vocabulary Teaching in Secondary EFL Classrooms: A Practical Pedagogical Framework
papers.authors: Shaxnoza Magdiyeva
papers.journal: American Journal of Language, Literacy and Learning in STEM Education (2993-2769)
