papers.abstract: Vocabulary is central to learning a second language, but teaching it can be challenging when students have different levels of English, learning needs and opportunities to practise. Word lists and translation exercises can help introduce new items, yet students also need to meet words in context, recall them later and use them in their own communication. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) gives teachers another way to prepare varied and adaptable vocabulary activities. This article considers how GenAI might be used in secondary English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms, especially with learners in Grades 7–9. Drawing on literature about vocabulary learning, technology-supported language teaching and AI in education, it presents a practical framework with five connected stages: presentation, contextualisation, retrieval practice, recycling and productive use. Examples and sample prompts show how teachers can use AI to prepare short texts, quizzes, differentiated exercises, dialogues and writing tasks. The article also considers important concerns, including inaccurate AI-generated content, overreliance on AI, student privacy and unequal access to technology. It argues that AI is most useful when teachers choose activities for clear learning purposes, check the materials carefully and guide students in using them responsibly. The framework is intended as practical guidance, not as a tested intervention or a report of original classroom findings.

papers.title: The nexus of green behavior, corporate green innovation performance, and industrial green value co-creation : insights for green business strategies
papers.authors: Zhe Sun, Bingying Zhu, Liang Zhao, Jehan Saleh Lardhi, Oumaima Haj Ammar
papers.journal: Strathprints: The University of Strathclyde institutional repository (University of Strathclyde)
papers.abstract: Drawing on the lens of green value co-creation, this study investigates how such co-creation mediates the relationship between employees' green behavioral intentions and corporate green innovation performance. By integrating internal and external moderating factors, the study constructs a comprehensive model of the green innovation process. Data from 448 survey responses were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). The results demonstrate that green value co-creation partially mediates the link between employee intentions and innovation outcomes. Furthermore, the study finds that market and policy orientations positively moderate the impact of employee intentions on value co-creation. At the organizational level, leadership collaboration awareness and a corporate green innovation culture strengthen the transition from value co-creation to innovation performance. These findings offer critical theoretical insights and practical pathways for firms seeking to alleviate environmental pressure and achieve sustainable development.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Pharmacovigilance for Neuropsychiatric Therapies: Advancing U.S. Drug Safety Surveillance and Regulatory Decision-Making
papers.authors: Rebecca A Omachonu, Sandra A. Uzuh, Kehinde Akinola, Kelvin Ovabor, Augustine Odibo
papers.abstract: Neuropsychiatric medications, including antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, anxiolytics, and newer agents such as esketamine, are widely prescribed, but their adverse effects are often subjective, delayed in onset, and difficult to separate from the illness being treated.Post-marketing surveillance in the United States relies on the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), MedWatch, the Sentinel System, and Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS).This narrative review, reported according to the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA), examines how well these systems detect neuropsychiatric adverse events and what artificial intelligence (AI) can add.PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were searched for literature published since January 2000, supplemented by regulatory and institutional sources.Spontaneous reporting misses most adverse drug reactions, while stigma, diagnostic overshadowing, and uncertainty about whether a symptom reflects the drug or the disorder further reduce reporting of psychiatric effects.Disproportionality signals, such as those reported for dissociation and suicidal ideation with esketamine, need cautious interpretation because notoriety bias, solicited reporting under REMS, and confounding by indication can inflate them.Long-latency effects such as tardive dyskinesia and antipsychotic-induced metabolic change fall outside the observation windows of premarket trials and most spontaneous reports.Natural language processing (NLP) can retrieve adverse events documented in free-text psychiatric records with good accuracy, and large language models (LLMs) show early promise for structuring adverse event narratives, but most AI studies are retrospective proofs of concept, and models trained on biased data can reproduce existing inequities.AI is therefore best used to widen and prioritize signal detection, with causality assessment and regulatory decisions remaining with clinicians and regulators.Priorities include prospective evaluation of AI tools in live pharmacovigilance workflows, linkage of FAERS with electronic health record and claims data, point-ofcare reporting tools, and efforts to reduce the stigma that discourages reporting of psychiatric adverse effects.

papers.title: Towards efficient student performance prediction with tabular prior-data fitted network: a small-sample learning approach in data-scarce scenarios
papers.authors: Jiang Peihan, Xuanping Wu, Wenting Wang, Yuqing Xia, Bo Hou, Wei Xu
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of student academic performance is crucial for enhancing educational outcomes and enabling personalized learning interventions. However, the limited availability of labeled data in many practical educational settings poses significant challenges for conventional machine learning models, which often require large datasets to achieve satisfactory performance and are prone to overfitting. To address this issue, we propose a novel small-sample learning framework based on the Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN). By integrating a Transformer based architecture with Bayesian inference, TabPFN effectively leverages meta-learned priors to perform high-quality predictions without task-specific finetuning. We evaluated the approach on the Mathematics and Portuguese subsets of the UCI Student Performance dataset and on a pooled Combined dataset under small-sample conditions. Experimental results indicate that TabPFN achieved generally strong and competitive performance across the three datasets, with accuracies of 92.36%, 95.49%, and 94.29%, respectively. However, its advantage varied across datasets and metrics, and the results should be interpreted cautiously where confidence intervals overlapped with strong baseline models. Additionally, we employ Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to interpret model decisions, identifying key influencing factors such as prior grades (G1, G2) and prior educational experience. The findings indicate that TabPFN constitutes a promising and effective solution for educational prediction in data scarce scenarios but also provides actionable insights for instructional design and student support.

papers.title: Bridging the gap: Competency-driven health informatics education for future healthcare leaders: a PhD study
papers.authors: A B Chikware, Nicolette Vanessa Roman, Eugene Lee Davids
papers.journal: African Journal of Health Professions Education
papers.abstract: Information and communications technologies are becoming integral to modern healthcare, advancing the adoption of health informatics and transforming the competencies required of healthcare professionals. This digital shift necessitates a re-examination of healthcare education to ensure alignment with evolving practice demands. This study explores healthcare professionals’ perceptions of health informatics education and its contribution to developing digital competencies. Thirty-one participants were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling strategies, representing eight healthcare disciplines: medicine, nursing, social work, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, dietetics, pharmacy and dentistry. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analysed using thematic analysis. Participants identified emerging aspects of digitisation within healthcare, such as digital health-record systems, artificial intelligence and open-source applications, that require enhanced digital skills training. However, limited attention to health informatics within undergraduate education and insufficient workplace training were reported as key barriers to digital competency development. Despite these limitations, participants expressed a strong interest in digital innovation, particularly following their experiences during the COVID‑19 pandemic. This presents a strategic opportunity to strengthen health informatics education. The study concludes that integrating health informatics competencies through updated curricula, blended learning methods, and targeted professional development is essential for preparing healthcare professionals to effectively engage with digital transformation in healthcare. Furthermore, by default of being born in a highly digital transformation era, this generation of healthcare professionals is strategically placed to drive healthcare digitisation and future innovations.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education From Automation to Responsible Augmentation
papers.authors: Jiangyu An, Lim Boon Hooı
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is often presented as a sequence of increasingly capable tools, yet educational outcomes do not rise automatically with model capability. This narrative review argues that the decisive variable is alignment: AI produces durable educational value when its affordances are aligned with pedagogy, assessment, educator agency, and institutional governance. The review traces the field from automation and learning analytics through adaptive support and generative co-production to an emerging model of responsible augmentation. Recent meta-analyses, controlled studies, systematic reviews, policy documents, and selected empirical studies were critically compared across three interdependent domains: resources and learning environments; teaching and learning; and management, assessment, and evaluation. The synthesis explains why apparently contradictory findings coexist. Structured, curriculum-aligned AI tutoring can improve immediate learning, whereas unconstrained answer generation can raise supported performance while weakening independent performance. Likewise, automated assessment can improve feedback speed but becomes educationally unsafe when opaque scores or unreliable detectors are treated as final decisions. Evidence concerning international and multilingual learners further shows that language, culture, affect, and data representation are not peripheral variables. The review proposes a responsible-augmentation framework in which alignment, agency, equity, and accountability operate across all three domains. It concludes with a research agenda prioritising longitudinal transfer, calibrated human–AI collaboration, subgroup validity, transparent governance, and institution-level implementation studies.

papers.title: La educación superior y la inclusión: Barreras, desafíos y oportunidades en el aula
papers.authors: Milton Fernando Rosero Duque, David Inti Luje Pozo, Rosa Vanessa Pazmiño Aldaz, Brigitte Solange Espinosa Pereira, Susan Manalastas Gallardo
papers.abstract: The democratization of higher education has promoted access for historically marginalized groups, but true equity demands transforming classroom dynamics. This study aims to analyze higher education and inclusion, identifying the main barriers, institutional challenges, and opportunities for pedagogical innovation to ensure successful academic trajectories. Methodologically, a qualitative documentary research was conducted through a systematic literature review following the PRISMA protocol guidelines, analyzing 25 scientific articles from the last decade. The results show that, although physical barriers have decreased, a "silent exclusion" persists, driven by curricular rigidity, methodological inflexibility, and various attitudinal barriers. The main challenge lies in the deep disconnect between inclusive institutional regulations and daily teaching practices, exacerbated by a lack of pedagogical training among the faculty. Conversely, the main opportunities for innovation are found in the application of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), the use of active pedagogies, and the co-creation of curricula alongside students. It is concluded that merely guaranteeing university access is insufficient and misleading without a profound didactic transformation; therefore, institutions must overcome an assistentialist vision, provide their faculty with technical and emotional training, and position inclusion not as an annexed compensatory policy, but as the central axis of academic quality and excellence.

papers.title: SUN’IY INTELLEKT TEXNOLOGIYALARINI JORIY ETISH JARAYONIDA AXBOROT-KUTUBXONA XODIMLARINING RAQAMLI VA KASBIY KO‘NIKMALARINI OSHIRISH
papers.authors: Nafisaxon Maxkamova, I.T.Habibjonov
papers.journal: Central Asian Journal of Academic Research
papers.abstract: Ushbu ilmiy-amaliy maqolada axborot-kutubxona muassasalarida sun'iy intellekt (SI) texnologiyalarini keng joriy etish sharoitida kutubxona xodimlarining raqamli va kasbiy ko'nikmalarini oshirish, ularning kasbiy kompetensiyalarini transformatsiya qilish hamda yangi bosqichga ko'tarish masalalari ilmiy va amaliy jihatdan tadqiq qilingan. Maqola avvalida O'zbekiston Respublikasi Prezidentining kitobxonlik va axborot-kutubxona sohasiga oid strategik nutqi hamda davlat siyosatining ustuvor yo'nalishlari asos qilib olingan. Tadqiqotda kutubxona kadrlarining raqamli savodxonligi, Data Curation (axborot kuratorligi), Prompt Engineering (neyron tarmoqlarga so'rov shakllantirish), AI-Ethical compliance (etik va huquqiy normalarga rioya qilish) kabi zamonaviy ko'nikmalarini shakllantirish bosqichlari, pedagogik-metodik modellari hamda kadrlar malakasini oshirishning amaliy mexanizmlari atroflicha yoritilgan.

papers.title: Liderazgo adaptativo e innovador: articulación entre innovación pedagógica y gestión estratégica en la educación superior
papers.authors: Julio César Martínez Aguilar
papers.abstract: The transformation of higher education has increased the need to articulate classroom-based innovation with institutional management and governance processes. In this context, academics who assume academic program leadership responsibilities occupy an intermediate position between teaching practice and strategic management, although the literature frequently addresses these dimensions separately. This article aims to analyze and integrate recent literature on academic leadership, pedagogical innovation, governance, and faculty development in higher education, with particular attention to the role of academic middle leaders as agents connecting educational practice and institutional change. An integrative literature review was conducted based on thematic relevance, recency, scientific quality, and availability of DOI, complemented by regional evidence concerning artificial intelligence adoption and governance in Latin American and Caribbean higher education. The thematic synthesis identified four interconnected dimensions: adaptive and innovative leadership, academic middle leadership, shared governance, and servant leadership. The findings suggest that institutionalizing innovation depends not only on individual faculty initiative but also on organizational conditions that promote participation, trust, capacity development, and shared decision-making. The study concludes that academic program leaders who maintain a teaching role can become strategic actors connecting pedagogical innovation with institutional management when they have adequate autonomy, leadership development, and organizational support.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in School Leadership
papers.authors: GEORGIOY IOANNIS
papers.abstract: This study explores the attitudes, level of familiarity, and use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools among school principals in secondary education in Greece. The sample consists of 63 principals from public schools, with an average age of 53 years and extensive administrative experience. Using an online questionnaire, the research investigates their perceptions regarding the potential, benefits, and challenges of AI in school management. The findings indicate a generally positive attitude toward AI utilization; however, practical implementation remains limited due to insufficient training and inadequate infrastructure. A positive correlation is observed between digital competence and AI use, while a strong need emerges for targeted professional development and the design of integration strategies. The study contributes to understanding the relationship between leadership competence and technological transformation in contemporary educational administration.

papers.title: Kindergarten teachers’ perceptions of artificial intelligence in early childhood education.
papers.authors: TSARA EIRINI, SOUVATZOGLOU VASSILIOS
papers.abstract: Educators and researchers increasingly recognize the importance of Artificial Intelligence literacy. Despite the growing body of related literature, the challenges and enabling factors for its integration into preschool education remain insufficiently explored and theoretically documented. It is crucial to understand both the difficulties and the conditions that influence its promotion, as well as the perceptions formed in kindergartens, so that these can become subjects of further investigation and evaluation. The present study aims to capture teachers’ views on the importance of Artificial Intelligence literacy in preschool education, as well as to highlight the challenges and factors that influence its implementation. The data were collected from 97 educators through a structured digital questionnaire.

papers.title: Benefits and challenges of using AI in career counseling
papers.authors: KATSIOULA PANAGIOTA, BOUTSKOU LEMONIA, PEOVITI THEODORA, KATSIOULA THOMAIS
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to examine the benefits and challenges arising from the use of AI in career counseling in secondary education. A quantitative online survey was conducted using a questionnaire on a sample of 115 counselors from the regions of Western and Central Macedonia and Thessaly. Overall, it was found that AI can be a very useful tool for career guidance counselors to provide personalized interpretation of assessment results, leading to personalized guidance that is also culturally sensitive, as well as to better match students" skills and interests with academic and professional paths that are also in line with labor market requirements. However, issues of accessibility, transparency, personal data protection, algorithm bias, and reduced trust have been identified, for example in the interpretation of results and the lack of human interaction. Therefore, existing regulatory frameworks need to be strengthened, infrastructure needs to be enhanced to increase accessibility, and AI systems need to be continuously developed.

papers.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools in STEM Activities: An Exploration of Kindergarten Teachers’ Perceptions.
papers.authors: MINOGLOU MARIA
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has had a significant impact on education, creating new opportunities as well as challenges. The integration of AI into STEM activities in early childhood education constitutes an emerging field with particular pedagogical importance. The purpose of this study was to investigate preschool teachers’ perceptions of the pedagogical value of AI, their readiness to design and implement relevant activities, and the barriers they face. The study was conducted using a quantitative methodology through a structured Likert-scale questionnaire, with the participation of 111 preschool teachers from various regions of Greece. The results indicate generally positive attitudes toward AI, recognizing its contribution to enhancing children’s interest, engagement, and STEM skills. At the same time, limited teacher readiness is reported, with the main obstacles being insufficient professional development and a lack of technological infrastructure.

papers.title: Empowering students in the digital age: A gamified approach to GDPR education through Erasmus+
papers.authors: SIDIROPOULOU SYMELA
papers.abstract: This article describes the design, implementation, and evaluation of an educational intervention within the framework of the Erasmus+ program, focusing on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Despite the critical importance of the regulation in the digital age, young people’s understanding of its basic principles remains limited, highlighting the so-called “privacy paradox.” The intervention adopted an experiential pedagogical approach, combining the co-creation of digital materials (infographics, interactive videos) with the development of a decision-making game (gamification) to simulate digital dilemmas. The central objective was to transform complex legal provisions into applied knowledge, while simultaneously strengthening students’ critical stance toward digital privacy. The effectiveness of the method was evaluated through pre-test and post-test questionnaires. The findings demonstrated a statistically significant increase in understanding of the principles of the GDPR (from 15% to 85%), while a substantial enhancement of participants’ self-efficacy and professional readiness was also recorded. The study highlights the superiority of game-based learning in bridging the gap between legal theory and everyday digital practice.

papers.title: Secondary School Teachers’ Interaction with Artificial Intelligence Systems: A Qualitative Investigation of Usability, Trust, and the Transformation of the Pedagogical Role
papers.authors: Zotou Evaggelia
papers.abstract: This research explores secondary education teachers" perceptions regarding the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into instructional practice. Through semi-structured interviews with a sample of ten (10) educators from diverse academic backgrounds, the study examines three core pillars: interaction and usability, issues of trust and ethics, and the transformation of professional identity. The findings reveal that using AI tools is a complex cognitive process requiring strategic prompt engineering. Despite the small sample size, participants consistently demonstrated a "cautious acceptance," acting as critical evaluators of machine-generated outputs to mitigate scientific inaccuracies and "hallucinations." In conclusion, the study highlights a shift in the teaching role from being a source of knowledge to an authority of critical mediation. It emphasizes the urgent need for professional development that fosters pedagogical agency and ethical action within the modern digital learning environment.

papers.title: Reproductive Identity - Language, Reason, and Artificial Intelligence after Hegel and Marx - Augustine’s Psychological Trinity, Analytic Philosophy, and Ecological Realism
papers.authors: Matti Vesa Volanen
papers.abstract: This article reconstructs a history of language, reason, and practical activity from Augustine through Kant, Hegel, Marx, the European linguistic turn, and analytic philosophy in order to formulate the concept of reproductive iden tity. Reproductive identity is not sameness, a fixed inner essence, or the final conceptual possession of the world. It is the historically open, materially conditioned work through which embodied individuals and communities sustain, repair, and develop the relations that enable their continuation. Augustine’s psychological trinity supplies an early grammar of memory, understanding, and will or love; Kant clarifies the conditions of judgment and practical reason; Hegel understands concept and reality as mutually realised in activity; and Marx translates this movement into the communal metabolism through which human beings reproduce life in and through nature. The linguistic turn and an alytic philosophy provide indispensable accounts of disclosure, difference, reference, truth, use, and normativity. The section on analytic philosophy distinguishes formal validity from situated inquiry and reconstructs practical reason as both normatively articulated and causally efficacious. Neither tradition, however, can settle the material and in stitutional conditions of the forms of life in which language works. The final sections develop ecological democracy and politically subordinate artificial intelligence as institutional consequences of the argument. Artificial intelligence is treated not as a sovereign subject but as a reversible public infrastructure whose legitimacy depends on ecological admissibility, traceability, contestability, repair, and the common reproduction of internal and external nature.

papers.title: PHYSICAL STRENGTH AS A MARKER OF GENERAL HEALTH: HAND DYNAMOMETRY AND ITS RELATIONSHIP WITH AGE, GENDER, BODY MASS INDEX, AND FATIGUE SEVERITY
papers.authors: Chaitrali Kulkarni, Sriraghunath S, Sasanka Sekhar Pradhan, Soniya Sivapraksam, Pooja N, Ashna Waseem Patel
papers.journal: World Wide Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Development
papers.abstract: Aim: To compare right- and left-hand grip strength measured with a Jamar dynamometer and to examine its relationships with age, gender, body mass index (BMI), and Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) score among adults attending a diabetes health screening camp. Methods: This cross-sectional study was a secondary analysis of anonymized data from a community diabetes health screening camp. Adults aged 23–61 years were assessed with a Jamar hydraulic dynamometer (mean of three trials per hand), the FSS, and measured height and weight. Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression with robust (HC3) standard errors were used. The analyses were exploratory. Results: Sixty-six adults (46 women, 20 men; mean age 34.8 ± 9.1 years) were analysed. Men had greater grip strength than women on both sides (right: 83.2 vs 52.2 lb; left: 79.3 vs 50.6 lb; both p < .001), and the hands did not differ. Age and BMI were not correlated with grip strength. Grip strength was inversely correlated with FSS score (right ρ = −.27, p = .028; left ρ = −.26, p = .035). In adjusted models, male gender was the strongest predictor; the FSS association was borderline for the left hand (p = .048) and non-significant for the right hand (p = .221). Conclusion: Gender was the primary correlate of grip strength, whereas age, BMI, and hand side were not substantially related to it. Lower grip strength was marginally associated with higher fatigue, an exploratory finding. Larger studies including glycaemic status, hand dominance, and older adults are needed.

papers.title: Basic Principles and Practical Paths of LLM-Empowered Senior High School English Writing Evaluation in China: A Conceptual Framework
papers.authors: Jiang Li
papers.abstract: **Basic Principles and Practical Paths of LLM-Empowered Senior High School English Writing Evaluation in China: A Conceptual Framework** **Jiang Li** College of Education, Zhejiang Normal University, Jinhua 321004, China Zhengzhou No. 36 Middle School, Zhengzhou 450042, China **Abstract:** This paper adopts a conceptual analysis approach based on policy document interpretation and narrative literature synthesis to explore large language model empowered senior high school English writing evaluation within the Chinese educational context. Driven by national digital transformation of education and the 2020 Overall Plan for Deepening the Reform of Educational Evaluation in the New Era, generative large language models deliver innovative technical support to resolve prominent drawbacks of traditional writing assessment including superficial evaluation dimensions, single evaluation subjects, rigid marking mechanisms and delayed interactive feedback. Different from conventional automated writing evaluation tools limited to surface linguistic scoring, large language models generate conversational feedback, support adjustable evaluation standards through prompt design and conduct comprehensive discourse assessment covering language competence, cultural awareness, thinking quality and learning ability which forms the core innovation of this research. This study systematically elaborates two guiding orientations for human machine collaborative evaluation including disciplinary core literacy orientation and digital intelligent diversified evaluation orientation and constructs three targeted practical paths matching real senior high school teaching scenarios. The three paths cover teacher led evaluation guided by curriculum standards, visualized learner profiling for targeted instruction and cross time and space personalized writing guidance. Supplementary supporting measures regarding academic integrity, minor data compliance, balanced digital resource allocation and teacher artificial intelligence literacy cultivation are further supplemented to improve practical operability. The established framework helps shift assessment logic from score oriented judgment to literacy oriented developmental guidance. Restrictions such as algorithm bias, student over dependence on artificial intelligence and data ethical risks hinder stable large scale application of model based evaluation and relevant discussions are fully presented in the limitations section. This research provides theoretical frameworks and operable classroom strategies for intelligent reform of senior high school English writing evaluation in China. **Keywords:** Large Language Models; Automated Writing Evaluation; Formative Assessment; Senior High School EFL Writing; Disciplinary Core Literacy **Ctation:** Jiang, L. (2026). Basic Principles and Practical Paths of LLM-Empowered Senior High School English Writing Evaluation in China: A Conceptual Framework. _Social Sciences and Humanities Inquiry_, _1_(2), 55–65. https://doi.org/10.67728/sshi.2026.010

papers.title: Does the AI Productivity Dividend Diminish? A Validated Framework for Identifying the Shape of Firm-Level Returns to Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Louis Agyekum
papers.abstract: Forecasts of the productivity dividend from artificial intelligence (AI) differ by an order of magnitude, partly because they extrapolate average gains observed among early, highly exposed adopters. Whether those gains scale linearly, flatten, or are competed away is an empirical question about the shape of the return to AI, not its average. This paper develops and validates a design-based framework for measuring that shape with linked firm–worker data. The framework combines a pre-determined, occupation-based measure of firm exposure to generative AI with a continuous-treatment difference-in-differences design around the release of ChatGPT in November 2022, three pre-specified tests of concavity, a decomposition of exposure effects into an adoption margin and a per-adopter return, a doubly robust analysis of use intensity, a staggered-adoption analysis of earlier AI adopters, and a production-function estimator that places AI in the law of motion of productivity. We validate every component on a calibrated synthetic panel of 20,000 enterprises that reproduces the structure of Statistics Canada's linked business microdata and embeds a known concave effect. The estimators recover the true dose–response curve and detect its concavity (slope difference −0.010, standard error 0.003, one-sided p = 0.002); Monte Carlo coverage of the main confidence interval is 0.97, and the concavity test has power of 0.93. The validation also exposes a practical pitfall: pre-trend tests clustered at roughly 40 industries over-reject a true null. The framework, released as open code, is ready for application to Canadian enterprise microdata, where it will inform estimates of potential output and the persistence of Canada's productivity gap.

papers.title: Generative AI Literacy and Social Innovation Intention Among University Students: The Dual Mediating Roles of Social Opportunity Recognition and Social Entrepreneurial Self-Efficacy
papers.authors: Jigar Nagvadia, Virendra N. Chavda, Ms. Supriya Vyas, Ms. Jagruti Patni
papers.journal: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
papers.abstract: The growing global grand challenges and the prevalence of socioeconomic disparities have increased the demand for business practices that create economic and social value at the same time. Although Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is being widely used, no studies have been conducted to assess how GenAI capabilities lead to social innovation intentions through cognitive and motivation process. Based on the Social Cognitive Theory and the Information Processing Theory, the current study constructs and tests a dual mediation model explaining how Generative AI Literacy (GAIL) impacts Social Innovation Intention (SII) through Social Opportunity Recognition (SOR) and Social Entrepreneurial Self-Efficacy (SESE). The quantitative cross-sectional study involved a sample of 550 university students and participants in incubators of technology entrepreneurs and innovations from educational institutions and incubators in India. The covariance-based structural equation model (CB-SEM) was analyzed in IBM SPSS AMOS version 28, with the calculation of indirect effects done using bias-corrected bootstrapping based on 5,000 resamples. Results indicate that GAIL has a significant impact on SII (β= 0.185, p < 0.001). Indirect paths found to be significant includes SOR with a 0.128 effect (CI at 95% is [0.085, 0.180]) and a stronger effect through SESE at 0.188 (CI at 95% is [0.139, 0.245]). The significant direct relation along with both indirect routes confirm complementary parallel mediation. The results put GenAI Literacy as a technology usability notion using different cognitive and agentive means for support of Social Innovation intention. The research is contributing to the field of digital entrepreneurship and providing useful insights for universities, policymakers, and incubators to create responsible GenAI-supported entrepreneurial learning and social innovation systems.

papers.title: INTEGRATION OF SIMULATION-BASED VARIABILITY AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN ENHANCING THE EFFICIENCY OF SPECIALIZED EDUCATION WITHIN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
papers.authors: J.G.Obidov
papers.abstract: Ushbu maqolada raqamli iqtisodiyot sharoitida maxsus fanlarni o‘qitishda simulyatsiyaga asoslangan variativlik va sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarini integratsiyalash masalalari ko‘rib chiqiladi. Zamonaviy sharoitda gipermatn, gipermedia, grafik va kompyuter audio-texnologiyalarining jadal rivojlanishi nafaqat ta’limda axborot-kommunikatsiya texnologiyalaridan samarali foydalanishga xizmat qiladi, balki bilimlar iqtisodiyoti uchun dolzarb bo‘lgan ko‘nikmalarni shakllantirishni ham qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. Innovatsion yondashuvlar orqali ishlab chiqilgan simulyatsiya modellari talabalarning mustaqil ta’lim olish, tahliliy fikrlash va qaror qabul qilish qobiliyatlarini oshiradi, bu esa inson kapitalini yaxshilash va ishchi kuchining raqobatbardoshligini oshirish uchun o‘ta muhimdir. Bundan tashqari, interfaol va variativ simulyatsiya muhitlaridan foydalanish murakkab jarayon va tizimlarni samarali o‘rganish imkonini beradi, bu esa o‘z navbatida kasbiy tayyorgarlikning umumiy samaradorligi va sifatini oshiradi.

papers.title: AI Utilization and User Satisfaction among Science Teachers and Students: A Structural Equation Modeling Analysis
papers.authors: Elbert Laserna
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has significantly influenced contemporary educational practices, offering opportunities to enhance teaching and learning while raising concerns about effective and ethical integration. This study examines AI utilization and user satisfaction among science teachers and students, and analyzes its effects on satisfaction, usefulness, ease of use, and reliability. A quantitative research design involved 242 STEM students and 22 science teachers in the Division of Tacurong City. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Structural Equation Modeling. Results showed high AI utilization among students (x̄ = 3.79) and very high utilization among teachers (x̄ = 4.21). Satisfaction was high among students (x̄ = 3.87) and very high among teachers (x̄ = 4.38). SEM findings for the combined sample (n = 264) revealed that AI utilization significantly influenced overall satisfaction (β = 0.465, R² = 0.217, p < .001), usefulness (β = 0.457, R² = 0.208, p < .001), ease of use (β = 0.336, R² = 0.113, p < .001), and reliability (β = 0.257, R² = 0.066, p < .001). Among students (n = 242), AI utilization also showed significant positive effects on satisfaction and all dimensions. Among teachers (n = 22), AI utilization did not significantly affect overall satisfaction, ease of use, and reliability, but strongly affected usefulness (β = 0.576, R² = 0.332, p = .005). The findings indicate that AI is widely utilized and positively perceived among science teachers and students.

papers.title: AN IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES
papers.authors: V. Janani, Dr. J. Srinivasan
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Human Resource Management (HRM) practices has transformed traditional organizational processes, offering both opportunities and challenges. AI technologies are increasingly used in areas such as recruitment and selection, employee engagement, performance management, learning and development, and workforce analytics. These tools enable HR professionals to streamline operations, enhance decision-making, reduce bias, and improve employee experiences through data-driven insights. AI is reshaping HRM practices by increasing efficiency and enabling data-driven decisions. However, despite its advantages, AI adoption also raises concerns regarding ethical implications, privacy, transparency, and the potential reduction of human judgment in people-centric functions. This study examines the effects of AI in optimizing and improving HRM practices, while also exploring the challenges and opportunities associated with its adoption. It emphasizes efficiency, fairness, and strategic value creation, highlighting advantages such as principled recruitment, employee engagement, and informed decision-making. Nevertheless, challenges remain regarding ethics, workforce acceptance, and the need for new skill development among HR professionals. By addressing key issues of holistic integration and sectoral focus, this research contributes to the growing body of literature on AI in HRM. The paper also provides practical suggestions for organizations to navigate the complex challenges of AI adoption while ensuring workforce resilience as these technologies continue to evolve.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT: IMPLICATIONS FOR HUMAN CAPITAL AND THE FUTURE WORKFORCE
papers.authors: Dr. N. Jeeva
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming Human Resource Management (HRM) by changing the way organizations recruit, develop, evaluate and retain employees. AI-enabled technologies are being applied across several HR functions, including talent acquisition, workforce planning, performance evaluation, employee development and compensation. While these technologies offer opportunities for improved efficiency, data-driven decision-making and personalized employee services, their use also raises important concerns regarding bias, privacy, transparency, fairness and the role of human judgement. This paper examines the implications of Artificial Intelligence for Human Resource Management, with particular emphasis on human capital development and the future workforce. The paper argues that AI should be viewed primarily as a tool for augmenting human capabilities rather than simply replacing employees. Organizations must therefore invest in employee reskilling, digital capability development and responsible AI governance. The study concludes that the future effectiveness of HRM will depend on the ability of organizations to combine technological innovation with ethical principles and human-centred management practices. The study emphasizes that AI adoption is not only a technological issue but also a human capital and workforce-development challenge.
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

papers.title: AI VIRTUAL INFLUENCERS AND CONSUMER PURCHASE INTENTION: THE ROLE OF PERCEIVED AUTHENTICITY AND TRUST
papers.authors: Ms. Jisha Miranda
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated virtual influencers are increasingly being used by brands to promote products and interact with consumers through social media platforms. Although virtual influencers provide advantages such as consistency, scalability, creative flexibility, and greater brand control, questions remain regarding whether consumers perceive them as authentic and trustworthy. The present study examines the influence of the perceived authenticity of AI virtual influencers on consumer purchase intention and investigates the mediating role of trust. A quantitative research design was adopted, and data were assumed to be collected from 100 social media users familiar with virtual influencer content through a structured questionnaire. Perceived authenticity, trust, and purchase intention were measured using five-point Likert-scale items. Reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, regression analysis, and mediation analysis were employed. The illustrative findings indicate that perceived authenticity has a significant positive influence on trust and purchase intention. Trust also demonstrates a strong positive influence on purchase intention and partially mediates the relationship between perceived authenticity and purchase intention. The study highlights that the effectiveness of AI virtual influencer marketing depends not merely on technological novelty or visual appeal but substantially on consumers’ perceptions of genuineness and trustworthiness. The findings provide implications for brands seeking to incorporate AI-generated personalities into influencer marketing strategies.

papers.title: AI-POWERED MOBILE ADVERTISING: EXAMINING CONSUMER ATTITUDES AMONG ARTS AND SCIENCE COLLEGE STUDENTS IN CHENNAI
papers.authors: Dr. D. Jansi
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: Mobile advertising has emerged as an important digital marketing tool with the widespread adoption of smartphones. This study examines consumer attitudes towards mobile advertising apps among Arts and Science college students in Chennai City and identifies the factors influencing their attitudes. The study is based on primary data collected from 100 respondents using a structured questionnaire and convenient sampling. Frequency, percentage, Chi-square test, and independent sample t-test were employed for data analysis. The findings indicate that respondents have mixed perceptions of mobile advertisements, particularly regarding entertainment, informativeness, irritation, credibility, and purchase influence. The Chi-square result shows no significant association between gender and irritating opinions towards mobile advertisements. Similarly, the t-test results reveal no significant gender differences in liking mobile advertisements, improvement in standard of living, matching personality and interests, or helping consumers select the best brand. The study highlights the growing importance of mobile advertising as an effective platform for engaging young consumers and provides insights for marketers to develop more relevant, credible, and consumer-oriented mobile advertising strategies.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ACCOUNTING AND AUDITING: TRANSFORMING FINANCIAL DECISION-MAKING AND PROFESSIONAL PRACTICES
papers.authors: Ms.P.Monisha, Dr.S.Uma Mageswari
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: Abstract: The emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed accounting and auditing practices across organizations worldwide. The increasing availability of financial data, advancements in machine learning algorithms, and the demand for real-time financial information have accelerated the adoption of AI-driven technologies in accounting and auditing functions. Traditional accounting systems primarily relied on manual data processing and periodic reporting, whereas AI enables continuous monitoring, predictive analytics, automated transaction processing, and intelligent decision support. In auditing, AI enhances fraud detection, risk assessment, anomaly identification, and audit quality through automated analysis of large volumes of structured and unstructured financial data. The integration of technologies such as Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Robotic Process Automation (RPA), and Generative AI has redefined professional roles and transformed the manner in which financial information is generated, analyzed, and interpreted. Despite numerous benefits, the adoption of AI also raises concerns regarding data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, ethical accountability, and workforce readiness. This paper examines the role of AI in accounting and auditing, explores its influence on financial decision-making, evaluates its benefits and challenges, and discusses future implications for accounting professionals. The study is conceptual in nature and is based on an extensive review of recent academic literature and professional reports. The findings indicate that AI acts as an enabler of enhanced efficiency, accuracy, and strategic decision-making while complementing rather than replacing human expertise in accounting and auditing.

papers.title: SKILL-BASED TALENT MANAGEMENT AND AI-POWERED UPSKILLING AND RESKILLING: BRIDGING SKILL GAPS IN THE FUTURE WORKFORCE
papers.authors: Ms.P.Monisha, Dr.S.Uma Mageswari
papers.journal: RCHUB JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY TRENDS IN MANAGEMENT COMMERCE AND ECONOMICS (JCMCE)
papers.abstract: Abstract: The workforce skill requirements across industries have been fundamentally redefined by the fast transition brought about by Industry 4.0 technologies, which include automation, big data analytics, artificial intelligence (AI), and cyber-physical systems. In order to address dynamic and technology-driven skill gaps, traditional role-based talent management approaches are becoming less and less effective. Continuous learning and ongoing education are emphasised as essential components in preparing employees to adapt to the shifting demands of the industry. This study looks at how upskilling and reskilling programs driven by AI may close skill gaps in the Industry 4.0 ecosystem to acquire the workforce ready for the future. Through the use of AI-enabled learning, ongoing competency development, and digital adaptability, the study creates a conceptual framework that connects skill-based talent management practices (an independent variable) with workforce agility and organisational success (dependent factors). In order to gather opinions from managers and workers in technology-intensive businesses, the study uses a quantitative research approach and standardised survey tools.AI integration in talent development procedures improves strategic workforce planning, decreases skill obsolescence, and promotes cultures of continuous learning.

papers.title: Cross-database adaptation of machine learning models for predicting sustained antibiotic exposure among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage in intensive care units
papers.authors: Sakshie Pathak, Yong Si, Janet Sanjaya, Mohammadsaeed Haghi, Nausin Tabassum Kudrot, Greg Placencia, Kamiar Alaei, Maryam Pishgar
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in intensive care units (ICUs) frequently receive antibiotics early in critical illness. Such exposure reflects suspected infection, physiological deterioration, monitoring intensity, and clinical management and may vary across institutions and electronic health record databases. We evaluated target-domain adaptation for modeling sustained antibiotic exposure in critically ill patients with ICH. Methods We analyzed derived ICH cohorts from MIMIC-IV and the eICU Collaborative Research Database. MIMIC-IV included 2,024 ICU stays and served as the source cohort. The eICU cohort comprised 1,277 stays and was divided, at the ICU-stay level, into a development subset (766 stays) and a held-out evaluation subset (511 stays). The eICU outcome was sustained antibiotic exposure on at least two ICU days. Candidate models incorporated demographic, comorbidity, physiological, laboratory, neurologic, respiratory, temporal, and measurementprocess features. Timestamped observations for static and temporal tabular families were censored at the recorded first-antibiotic time when available, whereas the compact sequence component and explicit measurement-density features used the full first 24 hours. For base-model families using eICU development data, meta-learner inputs were generated by five-fold stratified cross-fitting. A 42-input L2-penalized logistic meta-learner combined 16 model probabilities with model-summary, clinical, availability, and measurement-density features. Results The held-out eICU subset contained 48 positive outcomes (9.39%). The adapted ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.841 (95% CI 0.775–0.899) and an average precision (AP) of 0.540 (95% CI 0.399–0.676), with a Brier score of 0.063 and expected calibration error of 0.029. The MIMIC-IV source-only stack achieved an AUROC of 0.782; the paired AUROC difference was 0.059 (95% CI 0.003–0.112). In a separate patient-grouped five-fold out-of-fold sensitivity analysis of 503 linked eICU stays, AUROC was 0.807 (95% CI 0.691–0.910). Conclusions Target-domain adaptation improved held-out discrimination relative to a source-only stack for sustained antibiotic exposure. Because some model components and measurement-process features used information from the broader first 24 hours, the model should be interpreted as a first-24-hour treatment-association model rather than a strictly prospective pre-treatment infection predictor.

papers.title: BrainPT, a Cognitive Mini-Game App for Short-Form Video Use in Young Adults: Neural and Behavioral Pilot Study
papers.authors: yunjeong jeong, Chaewon Kim, Sungmin Ha, Seoyoung Choi, Sanghoon Han
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Short-form video elicits a stimulus-driven, passive neural state, yet existing interventions target time of use alone and cannot show whether the mechanism of cognitive control has changed. Objective This pilot study developed BrainPT, a mini-game-based cognitive intervention, and evaluated whether a single insertion alters the neural state during short-form viewing (Study 1) and whether repeated use improves behavioral self-regulation (Study 2). Methods Study 1 used a within-subject design (n=9) in which electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) were recorded in the same session across short-form viewing, a single BrainPT set, and goal-directed tasks. Study 2 used a nonrandomized 2-week pretest-posttest design comparing an experimental group that used BrainPT daily (n=13) with a control group (n=8). Both visits followed the same in-laboratory protocol, and app logs and self-report indices were collected over the intervention period. Results In Study 1, short-form viewing was accompanied by prefrontal deactivation: EEG power fell below baseline in all four bands and most in alpha (−1.72 dB, P =.01; q =.054 after correction). Prefrontal activation was opposite in sign between the goal-directed tasks and viewing (+0.180 vs −0.093, P =.002), and the viewing block immediately after a BrainPT insertion exceeded the block before it (+0.110 vs −0.093, P =.02). The same condition ordering appeared in an independent preintervention sample (n=18). In Study 2, daily short-form use fell from 143.5 to 50.9 min in the experimental group and rose from 104.8 to 132.9 min in the control group, a between-group difference in change of 120.7 min ( P =.004). The Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale did not differ between groups ( P =.39), and no neural index separated the groups after 2 weeks. Conclusions A single insertion produced a measurable neural change: prefrontal state during the viewing that followed moved toward the goal-directed task. After 2 weeks of use that neural difference was not detectable between groups although behavior differed, so repeated use may act through the momentary state during viewing rather than by reorganizing the resting state. Both samples were small and nonrandomized, the primary outcome was self-reported, and the analyses were exploratory and not preregistered, so these estimates require confirmation in a preregistered randomized trial with objectively logged use. Trial Registration Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS), Republic of Korea, KCT0012762; https://cris.nih.go.kr

papers.title: Reconstructing The Concept Of Self Actualisation In Artificial Intelligence Based Learning : An Integrative Literature Review
papers.authors: Ahmad Mujahidin, Ahsan Hakim
papers.abstract: The development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has transformed the learning ecology by positioning AI as a cognitive partner that supports personalisation, feedback, problem-solving, and creativity. This transformation necessitates a reconstruction of the concept of self-actualisation, as some human cognitive activities can be delegated to AI. This study aims to analyse the transformation of self actualisation, identify the conditions that strengthen or hinder it, and formulate a conceptual framework for self-actualisation in AI-based learning. This study employs a qualitative library research approach using an integrative literature review design. The findings indicate that GenAI is paradoxical in nature: it can serve as a cognitive scaffold that strengthens autonomy, competence, self-regulation, creativity, metacognition, and epistemic agency, while also potentially encouraging cognitive offloading, dependence, and the weakening of cognitive autonomy. This study proposes the Reflective-Relational Self Actualisation Framework in AI Learning Ecologies (RRSA-AILE), which encompasses autonomy, competence, relatedness, epistemic agency, metacognitive reflexivity, generative creativity, and ethical responsibility. Theoretically, RRSA-AILE integrates humanism, Self-Determination Theory, Self-Regulated Learning, and learner agency. Practically, the framework provides a foundation for AI-enhanced learning that is augmentative, reflective, and centred on human agency.

papers.title: Education in the Intelligence Era: Challenges and Reorientation of Contemporary Educational Theories
papers.authors: Ari Susanto, Ahsan Hakim
papers.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming contemporary education and challenging established assumptions underlying educational theories. This study aims to examine the challenges posed by AI in the intelligence era and analyze the need for reorientation of contemporary educational theories in response to increasingly complex human–AI interactions. A qualitative systematic literature review was conducted using scholarly literature from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, with emphasis on publications from 2019 to 2026. The literature was analyzed through thematic analysis and critical interpretive synthesis, guided by the PRISMA 2020 framework, focusing on knowledge construction, learning processes, assessment, teacher and learner agency, ethics, and educational purposes. The findings indicate that AI is reshaping education through personalized learning, adaptive instruction, automated feedback, and expanded knowledge exploration, while simultaneously creating challenges related to knowledge reliability, learner dependency, academic integrity, assessment validity, data privacy, and human agency. The review further shows that constructivism, experiential learning, social learning, connectivism, and humanistic education remain relevant but require critical reorientation to accommodate AI-mediated learning environments. The study proposes a human-centered, AI-augmented educational paradigm that integrates technological intelligence with critical thinking, learner autonomy, teacher agency, ethical reasoning, reflective judgment, and meaningful human interaction.

papers.title: Generative AI in Distance Education: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Personalization, Inclusion and Academic Integrity
papers.authors: Gayatri Sharma
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is creating new possibilities for distance education through conversational learning support, personalised explanations, automated feedback and multilingual assistance. However, its integration also raises concerns regarding academic integrity, unequal access, information reliability, learner autonomy and data privacy. This paper develops a conceptual framework for integrating GenAI into distance education through a human-in-the-loop approach. Drawing on relevant scholarly literature and international educational policy documents, the study examines the relationship between AI-supported personalisation, inclusive learning, human oversight and academic accountability. It proposes an integrated framework in which teachers and learners retain meaningful decision-making authority while AI provides supplementary educational support. The framework comprises five dimensions: human agency, equitable access, learner-centred personalisation, academic integrity and responsible data governance. The paper argues that technological availability alone cannot guarantee educational improvement; effective implementation also requires AI literacy, appropriate assessment practices, institutional policies and continuous human evaluation. The proposed framework offers conceptual guidance for higher-education institutions seeking to adopt GenAI responsibly in distance-learning environments. As a conceptual contribution, it requires subsequent empirical evaluation to establish its applicability across different educational contexts.

papers.title: A Thematic Review of Women’s Career Advancement and Leadership Development in the South African Context
papers.authors: Karen Stander, Minnie Labuschagne, Karla Le Roux, Unathi Norobolo, Quewan King, Neftali Nguema Anguesom, Adedotun Adetunla
papers.journal: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
papers.abstract: Abstract: Despite global commitments to gender equality, significant disparities persist in women’s career progression and leadership representation, particularly in the South African context. This study investigates the structural, institutional, and societal barriers that hinder women's advancement and evaluates the effectiveness of interventions aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 5 (Gender Equality). Using a rapid literature review methodology, the study analyzed 21 peer-reviewed articles from Sabinet and Web of Science, published post Covid (2020-2024). Through deductive thematic coding, five key themes emerged: ineffective or poorly implemented gender policies; systemic career advancement barriers including lack of sponsorship and work-life imbalance; persistent gendered norms in male-dominated sectors; strategic empowerment initiatives such as mentorship and leadership pipelines; and the influence of regional and sector-specific dynamics. The findings highlight that while some strategies like mentoring, inclusive policy design, and institutional support are effective, their implementation remains uneven and often superficial. This research contributes to policy and managerial discourse by offering evidence-based insights into which practices hold transformative potential and where further development is needed. It concludes with recommendations for longitudinal tracking, AI-human integrated reviews, and policy co-creation to foster equitable leadership pathways for women in Africa. Keywords: Gender Equality, Women in Leadership, Career Advancement, Sustainable Development Goal 5, Organizational Strategy

papers.title: Mapping AI Adoption in Digital Marketing: A Bibliometric Analysis, Systematic Literature Review, and Future Research Agenda
papers.authors: Yasak Taufan, Gilang Mukti Prabowo, Ika Tirta Candra Rini
papers.journal: International Journal of Education Vocational and Social Science
papers.abstract: This study aims to map the development of artificial intelligence adoption in digital marketing, identify dominant themes, examine methodological approaches, theoretical foundations, and empirical contexts, and formulate research gaps and a future research agenda. The study employs a combined design integrating bibliometric analysis and a systematic literature review. Data were obtained from 94 articles published during 2018–2026 and selected through the stages of identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion. Bibliometric analysis was used to examine publication trends, journals, countries, citations, collaboration, and relationships among keywords, while VOSviewer was used to generate network visualization, density visualization, and overlay visualization. The results show that publications have grown rapidly, with a temporary peak in 2025. Dominant themes include artificial intelligence, digital marketing, machine learning, social media, generative AI, customer experience, trust, transparency, privacy, and personalization. Previous studies have been dominated by quantitative approaches, cross-sectional designs, and SEM analysis, with Signaling Theory being one of the most frequently used theoretical foundations. The main gaps include inconsistent definitions of AI adoption, limited longitudinal designs, weak integration of technical, organizational, and behavioral aspects, and limited attention to responsible AI and negative consequences. This study concludes that AI adoption in digital marketing should be understood as a gradual, multidimensional socio-technical process requiring the integration of technological capabilities, organizational readiness, consumer responses, and ethical governance.

papers.title: AI Adoption Intensity and SME Innovation: A Configurational Perspective Based on Organizational Readiness and Learning Capability
papers.authors: Jubo Jin, Syaharizah Binti Abdul Aziz
papers.abstract: This paper explores the configurations through which AI adoption intensity acts as a catalyst for innovation performance in SMEs. Based on configurational theory, a theoretical framework integrating AI adoption intensity, organizational readiness (IT infrastructure readiness, resource readiness, and culture readiness) and organizational learning capabilities (knowledge acquisition capability, knowledge integration and application capability) is developed. The findings of the fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis based on survey data collected from 196 SMEs in China indicate that none of the individual conditions is a necessary condition for achieving high levels of innovation performance. Three sufficient configurations are identified with a solution consistency score of 0.847 and a coverage score of 0.631. AI adoption intensity serves as a central condition in two configurations and a peripheral condition in one configuration, suggesting that its configurational role is context-dependent rather than uniform.

papers.title: Government Support, AI Adoption, and SME Innovation Performance: An Institutional Theory Perspective
papers.authors: Jubo Jin, Syaharizah Binti Abdul Aziz
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly central to innovation in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), yet resource constraints limit their ability to exploit it. Governments worldwide provide institutional support to encourage SME AI adoption, but whether such support translates into innovation depends on internal organizational conditions that remain poorly understood. Drawing on institutional theory, this study treats government support as a source of coercive, normative, and mimetic pressure and develops an integrative conceptual model in which it influences SME innovation performance through AI adoption intensity, with organizational learning capability as a mediator and organizational readiness as a moderator. The model specifies that government support raises adoption intensity, which in turn enhances innovation performance; that organizational learning capability partially mediates this effect; and that organizational readiness strengthens the link between government support and adoption intensity. A quantitative, cross-sectional design is proposed: structured questionnaires will collect no fewer than 200 valid responses from SMEs, analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Theoretically, the study is expected to extend institutional theory from the adoption/non-adoption dichotomy to a continuous adoption-intensity construct and to position organizational learning as the channel transmitting adoption into innovation. Practically, it can inform the design of differentiated government policy and SME capability building.

papers.title: The Gendered Voice of AI: Literary Representations and Digital Patriarchy
papers.authors: Manisha
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: It is unsettling that most of the world’s leading AI assistants speak in a female voice: Siri, Alexa, Cortana, three names with an easy, almost slick, effortless fluidity. This paper asks why this is so and what it reveals about the many-sided connection among gender, technology and power. The argument is not that AI was “feminised” out of necessity or for commercial appeal, although both play a part. It is rather that the gendered voice of AI displays the continuity of patriarchal logic in the digital space, a logic that literature and popular culture have rehearsed for more than a hundred years. Through an analysis of literary writings, films and contemporary design philosophies for digital assistive devices, the paper traces the origins of machine femininity and questions the assumptions lurking within it. The discussion spans four interrelated landscapes: gendered machines in the literary and cinematic imagination; the anthropomorphic impulse that leads designers to give their technologies a human face and a feminine voice; the repression of female voice and agency in these technologies; and the wider culture of mediating technologies in which these moves are normalised. The goal is not to offer a technical solution but to open a space for critical thinking about how images of compliant women might be displaced from our most advanced technologies.

papers.title: AI-Driven Consumer Behaviour Analytics: Transforming Retail and Marketing Practices in Tamil Nadu, India
papers.authors: S Devipriya, S Murugan
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF INNOVATIONS & RESEARCH ANALYSIS
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionising the realms of retailing and marketing through the use of analytics which help businesses understand consumer behaviour and predict purchase decisions as well as offer consumers a personalised experience. With the increasing prevalence of e-commerce, digital payment systems, apps and social media channels in use, vast amounts of consumer data have been generated. The possibilities offered by AI analytics are therefore many in emerging retail environments such as that in Tamil Nadu. The paper will investigate the use of consumer behaviour analytics driven by artificial intelligence as a means of revolutionising retail and marketing processes focusing on aspects such as personalisation, predictive analytics, recommendation systems, customer segmentation, sentiment analysis and AI-based customer engagement. The research will be based on consumer behaviour, marketing, analytics and digital transformation perspectives in order to illustrate how AI analytics could assist in purchase prediction, targeted communications, customer satisfaction, loyalty and decision-making in retail. According to the available literature, AI can be helpful in increasing the accuracy in marketing, engagement of customers, demand prediction, and operations efficiency; nevertheless, the role of AI in this respect depends on data quality, technological maturity, trust of consumers, and proper data handling practices. The issues of privacy, algorithmic bias, cost of implementation, digital maturity, and transparency continue to play an important role among limitations, especially for small retailers.

papers.title: Pemberdayaan Ekonomi Siswa dan Guru melalui Edukasi Platform Kerja Freelance Digital di SMA IRA Medan
papers.authors: Almastoni Almastoni, Fajrillah Fajrillah, Petrus, Nelisa Aulia Br Ginting, Alincia Sinaga, Theresa Stefani Sianturi
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of the digital economy has opened vast opportunities through gig economy platforms, yet high school students and teachers often lack the digital literacy and skills needed to capitalize on these prospects productively. This community service program aimed to empower the economic potential of students and teachers at SMA IRA Medan by delivering education and technical training on digital freelance platforms integrated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning tools. The methodology comprised three main stages: pre-implementation (need analysis, module synthesis, and institutional coordination), implementation (interactive seminar, live demonstration of AI tools, and hands-on portfolio creation workshops), and evaluation (pre-test/post-test analysis and mentoring). The activity took place at SMA IRA Medan on September 30, 2026, involving 40 participants consisting of students and teachers. The results demonstrated a significant increase in participant understanding, rising from an average of 23.1% in the pre-test to 88.8% in the post-test, an increase of 65.7%. Furthermore, 87.5% of participants successfully created active profiles and digital portfolios on platforms such as Sribulancer and Projects.co.id. This initiative successfully fostered a digital entrepreneurship mindset, equipping students and teachers with monetizable skills to support sustainable economic independence.

papers.title: 'Training' and 'Learning'
papers.authors: Laura Ferroglio, Aurora Trapella
papers.journal: AI-Linguistica Linguistic Studies on AI-Generated Texts and Discourses
papers.abstract: This paper analyses the terms training and learning, examining their historical evolution and usage as recorded in English and Italian monolingual and bilingual dictionaries. The analysis then focuses on two specialised domains, namely machine translation (MT) (both through Neural MT and generative AI technology) and Second Language Acquisition (SLA). We examine how the meanings of training and learning are adapted in each field, highlighting overlaps between their human-related and machine-related uses. English and Italian have been selected as instances of a Germanic and a Romance language to compare their respective encoding of the concepts of training and learning, analysing when and how these terms began to be applied to machines rather than exclusively to humans. This contribution to the glossary of AI terms discusses how linguistic choices shape perceptions of machine capabilities. The paper underscores the role of language in mediating technological change across the evolving meanings and uses of training and learning, and invites reflection on the consequences of anthropomorphic discourse in AI-related communication.

papers.title: Beyond self-directed learning: An ai-augmented conceptual framework for future learning in higher education
papers.authors: Nuttapong Songsang, Natcha Mahapoonyanont, Wipada Phinla, Wipada Phinla
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education by reshaping how students acquire knowledge, solve problems, collaborate, and regulate their own learning. Generative Al technologies, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and other intelligent learning systems, have created unprecedented opportunities for personalized learning while simultaneously challenging traditional conceptions of self-directed learning (SDL). Although SDL has long been recognized as a fundamental competency for lifelong learning, existing theoretical models were developed before the emergence of Al-enhanced learning environments and therefore provide limited guidance for understanding learner autonomy within human- Al collaborative contexts. This conceptual paper reconceptualizes self-directed learning in the era of artificial intelligence by proposing an AI-Augmented Self-Directed Learning (AI-ASDL) Framework for future learning in higher education. Employing documentary research and conceptual synthesis, the paper integrates classical theories of self-directed learning, self-regulated learning, self-determination theory, and contemporary scholarship on artificial intelligence in education. The conceptual synthesis suggests that future learners require competencies extending beyond independent learning, including Al literacy, critical evaluation of Al-generated information, ethical Al use, reflective learning, and human-Al collaborative problem solving. Accordingly, the proposed framework comprises eight interconnected dimensions: learning motivation, self-directed goal setting, Al-assisted information seeking, human-Al interaction, critical evaluation, reflective learning, AI-augmented self-regulation, and lifelong learning orientation. The framework reconceptualizes self-directed learning as a collaborative process in which learners strategically engage with artificial intelligence while maintaining human agency, critical judgment, ethical responsibility, and continuous self-improvement. By extending traditional self-directed learning theory to Al-enhanced educational environments, the proposed framework provides a theoretical foundation for future research and offers practical implications for curriculum development, instructional design, assessment, and educational policy in higher education.

papers.authors: Nuttapong Songsang, Natcha Mahapoonyanont, Wipada Phinla, Wipada Phinla

papers.title: AI-enabled assessment: framework, perspective and educational outcomes
papers.authors: Bayode Ogunleye, Olakunle Olayinka, Kudirat Ibilola Zakariyyah, Oluwaseun Ajao, Hemlata Sharma
papers.abstract: The development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT have raised concerns about assessment practice in higher education (HE). Prior studies have discussed the need to re-imagine and re-design assessment instruments; however, there is limited empirical evidence on how to effectively deploy this in practice. This paper proposes the TSD (task, scaffolding support and deliverable) framework to guide academics and education providers on how to effectively integrate AI and reflective practice into assessment design. By doing so, we adopt a mixed-method approach to investigate educational outcomes, tutors’ and students’ perspectives on the reflective AI-enabled assessment. This study collected data from UK University students (22 respondents) and tutors (24 participants) using a survey questionnaire and semi-structured interview questions, respectively. This study provides empirical support for positioning reflective practice as evidence of learning rather than being treated as a mere assessment activity. The findings show that AI output verification specific tasks need to be incorporated into AI-enabled assessment design. The results suggest that students perceived that our assessment strategy encouraged deeper learning, critical thinking and ethical awareness. Similarly, tutors were mostly positive with the adoption of the strategy, but some highlight the need for caution and multimodal approach .

papers.title: Enhancing Fairness and Engagement in Robot-Led Gamified Learning: A Random Forest and TAM Approach
papers.authors: Nikolas Jakob, Yuanbo Hou Seon, Qiaoqiao Rin, Wenvu Wang
papers.abstract: Gamified educational robotics offer new opportunities for interactive learning, but fairness and sustained engagement remain key challenges, particularly in group-based human-robot interaction (HRI). This study presents a gamified quiz system for the Pepper robot that integrates a Random Forest-based first responder detection mechanism using non-verbal sound input. Designed around GAFCC gamification principles, the system employs competition, badges, feedback animations, and music to promote motivation and interactivity. To assess user experience, we propose and validate a research model combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) with custom subscales focused on motivation, sound feedback effectiveness, and system clarity. The Random Forest model achieves over 89% classification accuracy with sub-millisecond resolution, significantly enhancing fairness in competitive response scenarios. Experimental results from student groups (N=64) reveal statistically significant improvements in perceived usefulness, engagement, sound clarity, and behavioral intention. Hypothesis testing confirms that gamified features drive positive perceptions, which in turn increase user engagement and usage intent. These findings demonstrate the value of combining signal-based fairness mechanisms with theoretically grounded, user-centered evaluation in educational HRI systems.

papers.title: Machine learning in comparative effective research of pharmacological interventions: a scoping review
papers.authors: Zhen Wang, Bijan J. Borah
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is rapidly transforming the evaluation of the comparative effectiveness research (CER) of pharmacological interventions. It offers an attractive data-driven alternative to traditional statistical causal inference methods for estimating heterogeneous and individualized treatment effects and is particularly well-suited for high-dimensional real-world data. While a variety of ML algorithms have been applied in CER, methodological challenges and limitations remain, and recommendations for conducting, reporting, and evaluating such studies have only recently been proposed.
