papers.title: Künstliche Intelligenz – Chance oder Risiko? Vortrag beim Katholischen Bildungswerk Frankenburg am Hausruck
papers.authors: Alexander Jung
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: lides of a general-audience evening talk (about 90 minutes plus discussion), given inGerman at the Catholic adult-education centre (Katholisches Bildungswerk) inFrankenburg am Hausruck, Upper Austria, on 13 October 2026. The talk explains, without formulas, what artificial intelligence can and cannot dotoday. Part 1 shows where AI already sits in everyday life (timetables, weather,navigation, licence-plate recognition, recommendations). Part 2 covers data as the rawmaterial, from monastic tithe registers to social media, the planned Google datacentre in Kronstorf, and open government data. Part 3 demonstrates AI agents on threelive examples: analysing the Frankenburg municipal council minutes 2021–2026, planninga bicycle tour, and a study of Alpine pumped-hydro storage. Part 4 contrastsopportunities (retinal-image diagnostics) with risks: hallucination, deepfakes,accountability, military use. It closes with three take-home messages. Includes the video shown in the talk: an AI-agent-generated flood visualisation(Perschling valley, September 2024) together with the slide explaining its limits.Text and the author's own figures are CC BY 4.0; third-party images and screenshotsare credited on the final slide and excluded from the licence.

papers.title: SUN'IY INTELLEKT TEXNOLOGIYALARINI JORIY ETISH JARAYONIDA AXBOROT-KUTUBXONA XODIMLARINING RAQAMLI VA KASBIY KO'NIKMALARINI OSHIRISH
papers.authors: Maxkamova Nafisaxon Abdusamadjon qizi, I.T.Habibjonov
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Ushbu ilmiy-amaliy maqolada axborot-kutubxona muassasalarida sun'iy intellekt (SI) texnologiyalarini keng joriy etish sharoitida kutubxona xodimlarining raqamli va kasbiy ko'nikmalarini oshirish, ularning kasbiy kompetensiyalarini transformatsiya qilish hamda yangi bosqichga ko'tarish masalalari ilmiy va amaliy jihatdan tadqiq qilingan. Maqola avvalida O'zbekiston Respublikasi Prezidentining kitobxonlik va axborot-kutubxona sohasiga oid strategik nutqi hamda davlat siyosatining ustuvor yo'nalishlari asos qilib olingan. Tadqiqotda kutubxona kadrlarining raqamli savodxonligi, Data Curation (axborot kuratorligi), Prompt Engineering (neyron tarmoqlarga so'rov shakllantirish), AI-Ethical compliance (etik va huquqiy normalarga rioya qilish) kabi zamonaviy ko'nikmalarini shakllantirish bosqichlari, pedagogik-metodik modellari hamda kadrlar malakasini oshirishning amaliy mexanizmlari atroflicha yoritilgan.

papers.title: What Makes an AI Character Worth Coming Back To? Humor, Personality, Emotional Connection, and the Art of Meaningful AI Roleplay
papers.authors: Garret E. Williams
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: A research-informed design brief, written by the founder of a commercial AI character product (chatbrat.ai), arguing that compelling AI characters are defined by the quality and consistency of the character experience rather than by how explicit they can be. It uses four official chatbrat.ai scenarios to illustrate distinct dimensions (personality and voice, humor, emotional responsiveness, chemistry and pacing, creative initiative, memory and user agency) and proposes a checklist for evaluating them. It is not an independent study and makes no product-performance claims. No benchmark results are reported.

papers.title: Ethics and Use of Artificial Intelligence for Service Delivery in Nigerian Academic Libraries
papers.authors: Goodluck Okwudiri Allison, Chidiebere Evans-Otuza
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in library offers a transformative opportunity to enhance service delivery amidst persistent staffing and funding deficits. However, this technological shift creates tension regarding ethical governance, data privacy, and cultural representation. This study investigated the ethical dimensions and operational usage of AI for service delivery in Nigerian academic libraries, with policy frameworks, algorithmic justice, data privacy, and technological equity. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design. The population comprised 8,323 certified librarians in Nigeria, from which a sample size of 368 was selected using a convenience/purposive sampling technique. Data collection was executed using a validated self-structured 5-point Likert scale questionnaire administered during the EDO 2025 Nigerian Library Association (NLA) Conference. A total of 318 valid copies were retrieved, yielding an 86.4% response rate. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including frequency counts, percentages, mean, and standard deviation. The results revealed that while librarians demonstrate a high overall level of ethical awareness and a desire for structural policy frameworks (M = 3.64), their specific practical awareness regarding daily data privacy and intellectual property implications remains high (M = 3.79). Result showed that current library professional ethics are moderate (M=3.36) to regulate AI adoption. Furthermore, respondents reported a moderately critical level of algorithmic bias moderate (M=3.10), strongly indicating that current Western-centric AI systems marginalize local research, regional cultural contexts, and indigenous Nigerian languages. Concerns surrounding data privacy, cloud breaches, and third-party commercial data-mining also scored moderate (M=3.18), exposing the vulnerabilities of libraries operating with sub-baseline digital infrastructures. The study concluded that forcing AI adoption without context-responsive ethical governance exacerbates algorithmic injustice and risks compromising user trust. It is recommended that stakeholders co-design localized AI deployment policies, conduct rigorous pre-deployment algorithmic audits, and establish human-AI collaborative frameworks for patron confidentiality against aggressive data mining.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Innovative Preparedness of Library Schools in Nigeria and Abroad for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR)
papers.authors: Anuoluwa Awodoyin, Temitope Adeleke OSISANWO, Ahmed Olakunle Simisaye, Olabode Thomas Fajiwe
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Library schools or ischools especially in developed nations have responded to the challenges and opportunities of the 4IR era by upgrading their curricula with courses to make their graduates relevant. This study out a comparative content analysis of curricula of selected Nigerian library schools (NLS) and best library schools in the world with the view of examining how prepared are the curricula of NLS in training library and information professionals for 4IR libraries. The study selected fourteen (14) library schools out of 37 library schools offering Bachelor’s Degree in LIS spread across the six geopolitical zones in Nigeria and ten best library schools in the world. NLS were purposively selected using the quota sampling technique based on their year of establishment while the ten best leading library schools in the world were selected based on their positions on the QS world ranking of universities. The findings revealed some innovative courses in the curricula of NLS in preparing its undergraduates for the 4IR era:Information retrieval, Database Management, Knowledge Management, Web design and Multimedia Application. Whereas leading library schools had more advanced courses such as Databases & Data Modeling, Data Structures & Algorithms, information architecture, Data science, machine learning for advanced analytics among others. The study concluded that innovative courses that will prepare graduates of NLS to be 4IR compliant are grossly inadequate in the curricula when compared to leading library schools globally. The study recommended the redesign of curricula of library schools in Nigeria to meet 4IR libraries globally.

papers.title: ICT Engagement and Knowledge Acquisition among Undergraduate Students in Lagos State University: The Impact of 4th Industrial Revolution
papers.authors: Adebola Oluwamayokun Adegoroye, Sarah Akpomiemie Gbenu, Faith Ibukunoluwa Amosun
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is characterised by the convergence of new technologies encompassing artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and the Internet of Things (IoT), and these innovations have permeated the everyday lives of young people globally, including in Nigeria. This study explored the level and factors of ICT engagement and knowledge acquisition among undergraduate students in Lagos State University (LASU). A descriptive survey design was adopted. Quantitative data was collected from 1,009 undergraduate students in the Faculties of Science and Social Sciences through an online questionnaire which was distributed through social media platforms, and the data collection spanned three weeks. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies and percentages) with IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The findings revealed a high level of ICT engagement in academic activities: most respondents actively used digital devices for academic purposes, expressed confidence in using diverse ICT tools, and participated in online discussions and forums. The primary channels of knowledge acquisition combined traditional sources, notably lecture notes and print textbooks, with digital resources such as educational websites, e-books and online databases, while reliance on the university library showed signs of decline. Respondents overwhelmingly perceived that ICT engagement enhances their understanding of course content, broadens their knowledge beyond classroom instruction and contributes to critical thinking skills. The study recommends comprehensive digital literacy programmes, equitable ICT infrastructure and the modernisation of library services to consolidate these gains

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in African Academic Libraries: Opportunities, Constraints, and a Framework for Context-Sensitive Implementation
papers.authors: Olabisi Dorcas OGUNGBENRO, Omolabake Eunice Akinyemi, Blessing Hunbadon Asue
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is transforming scholarly communication and knowledge-sharing practices in academic libraries worldwide. However, academic libraries in Nigeria and other African contexts continue to experience challenges related to limited visibility of research outputs, fragmented dissemination systems, uneven institutional repository development, information overload, and restricted access to scholarly resources. This paper presents a conceptual and analytical review of the strategic role of AI in strengthening scholarly communication and knowledge-sharing practices in African academic libraries. Drawing on recent scholarly literature, policy documents, and conceptual perspectives on digital transformation, the study examines the application of emerging AI technologies, including machine learning, natural language processing, recommender systems, and research analytics tools, in enhancing knowledge organisation, research discovery, open access integration, repository visibility, collaboration, and research evaluation. The paper further analyses contextual barriers affecting AI adoption, including inadequate digital infrastructure, funding limitations, professional capacity gaps, algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, and weak institutional policy frameworks. Based on these analyses, the paper proposes a context-sensitive AI adoption framework that integrates technological readiness, institutional capacity, ethical governance, and policy support as essential dimensions for sustainable scholarly communication transformation. The paper concludes that strategic investment in digital infrastructure, librarian capacity development, inclusive data governance, and coordinated institutional policies is critical for ensuring that AI contributes to equitable, accessible, and sustainable knowledge-sharing ecosystems in African academic environments.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Enhancing Safety Measures and User Satisfaction in Federal University Libraries in North-East Nigeria: A Conceptual Framework
papers.authors: Patrick Phanuel Umoriya, Yinasim Pius Musa, Igbinosa Clifford Osayomore
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies influencing library operations and information service delivery across the globe. The increasing complexity of security threats, technological advancement, and users' expectations has necessitated the adoption of intelligent systems capable of improving safety management and enhancing user satisfaction in academic libraries. Federal university libraries in North-East Nigeria are expected to provide safe, secure, technology-driven, and user-centred learning environments that support teaching, learning, research, and innovation. However, inadequate technological infrastructure, poor funding, limited AI adoption, insufficient digital competencies among library personnel, cybersecurity threats, and weak institutional support continue to hinder effective safety management and quality service delivery. This paper conceptually examines Artificial Intelligence as a catalyst for enhancing safety measures and user satisfaction in federal university libraries in North-East Nigeria. Specifically, the paper discusses the concepts of Artificial Intelligence, safety measures, user satisfaction, and academic libraries; examines relevant theoretical perspectives; identifies challenges affecting AI adoption; and proposes strategies for integrating AI into library safety management. The paper adopts a conceptual review methodology through the analysis of current scholarly literature. It concludes that AI technologies such as intelligent surveillance systems, biometric access control, predictive analytics, chatbots, smart sensors, facial recognition technologies, and machine learning applications possess significant potential for improving library safety, operational efficiency, and users' satisfaction. The paper recommends increased investment in AI infrastructure, continuous staff capacity building, supportive institutional policies, and strategic partnerships to facilitate sustainable AI integration in federal university libraries.

papers.title: From Training to Qualification: A Framework for AI Education and Competency Assessment
papers.authors: Emil Uzelac
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: An academic approach to artificial intelligence (AI) education requires more than organizing training material into courses or assigning certificates to benchmark scores. It requires separate evidence that an intervention produces learning, that an identified system meets a competency standard, and that the resulting qualification supports its intended use. This paper develops a framework that connects these three claims without treating them as interchangeable. Drawing on curriculum learning, evidence-centered assessment design, argument-based validation, and AI-system documentation, the framework defines the assessed student as a version-bound model configuration rather than a model brand. It separates educational records from competency transcripts, distinguishes parameter-based learning from reference-assisted performance, and specifies independent examination, bounded qualification claims, and reassessment after material changes. A prospective pilot, ER-101: Evidence-Grounded Research Assistance, operationalizes the framework using two open-weight model families and four conditions: an unchanged starting configuration, handbook assistance, block-shuffled course training, and prerequisite-ordered course training. The trained conditions use identical optimizer-step bundles, example exposures, and update budgets; only first-pass bundle order differs. Three paired training seeds per family yield twelve trained checkpoints and sixteen evaluated configurations. A protected 300-case examination is separated from 60 practical assignments that cannot influence qualification decisions. The planned analysis distinguishes task-sampling uncertainty from training-seed variability and treats qualification-to-practice correspondence as exploratory. Analytical planning calculations illustrate why moderate task counts cannot establish rare-error safety or population-wide credential validity. No pilot data, trained checkpoints, qualification outcomes, or empirical effectiveness results are reported. The contribution is a falsifiable education-to-qualification architecture and a controlled protocol for investigating it, not a claim of human-equivalent degrees, universal trainability, or validated professional competence.

papers.title: Using Generative Artificial Intelligence to Craft Patient-Facing Report Summaries: Opportunities for Enhancing Resident Training
papers.authors: Geoffrey Michael Currie, Tracy Yarbrough, Jagruti C. Shah, K Elizabeth Hawk, Sarah Lonsdale, Min Gyu Noh, Lamia Saiyara Choudhury, Ray Rui Zhang, Anthony Fu Chen, Eric Rohren
papers.abstract: IntroductionEffective patient communication is an essential skill for radiology and nuclear medicine specialists, yet it remains underemphasized in residency training. With increasing patient access to electronic medical records, the ability to translate technical reports into patient-facing summaries is critical. Generative AI may offer a dual benefit of improving workflow by producing patient-appropriate summaries and serving as a training tool to help residents hone their communication skills. MethodsSeventy-six de-identified nuclear medicine imaging procedure reports (covering general nuclear medicine, PET/CT (positron emission tomography-computed tomography), and nuclear cardiology) were used to generate 608 patient-facing summaries: four versions of each report were generated using ChatGPT models (o1-mini, 4o, 4o-mini, 4 legacy) and four versions were written by residents. Summaries adhered to a four-sentence maximum and targeted a sixth-grade reading level. GPT-4o was used to critique and rank AI-generated summaries, and the two best-performing AI versions were compared with resident summaries. Blinded evaluations by three experienced nuclear medicine physicians assessed summaries on readability, accuracy, appropriateness, and overall fitness for purpose. Likelihood Ratio Chi-Square tests assessed differences in performance. ResultsGPT o1-mini was ranked as the best summary in 86% of initial AI comparisons and 100% of final comparative assessments with resident summaries. GPT 4o and o1-mini outperformed residents across multiple domains including clarity, health literacy, and tone. The best human summaries were consistently outperformed by AI in both physician and AI assessments, though discrepancies in ranking priorities (e.g., tolerance for jargon vs. inaccuracy) were noted and AI more often produced summaries containing misinterpretations of data in the original reports. Resident summaries showed wide variation in tone, technicality, and patient appropriateness. Overall, 65% of all summaries (AI and human) were deemed fit-for-purpose. ConclusionGenerative AI models can produce consistently appropriate and readable patient-facing summaries of imaging procedure reports and may serve as effective tools to develop resident communication skills. Generative AI may therefore model best practices and provide timely feedback, offering structured opportunities to refine written communication. Future work should explore its integration into learner-tailored educational constructs using frameworks such as Bloom’s taxonomy, to enhance resident training and effectiveness of feedback mechanisms.

papers.title: The Cursive Question : A Critical Synthesis of Neurocognitive Evidence and Educational Policy in the American Retreat from Handwriting Instruction
papers.authors: Zen Revista
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Between 2010 and the mid-2010s, most U.S. states adopted the Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, which omitted cursive handwriting from the required curriculum while explicitly incorporating keyboarding skills beginning in Grade 3. The removal of cursive writing, frequently characterized in popular accounts as the result of educational administrators’ indifference to neuroscientific research, ignited a public debate that intensified following the publication of several influential studies suggesting that handwriting engages the brain more extensively than typing. This dissertation examines the controversy at the intersection of educational neuroscience and education policy. It addresses four central research questions: (1) What precisely does the popular narrative claim, and how does each claim withstand systematic verification against primary sources? (2) What neurocognitive mechanisms plausibly connect the production of letters by hand to literacy development? (3) What does the behavioral and experimental evidence, ranging from preschool handwriting interventions to meta-analyses of handwriting instruction, actually establish? (4) How should the available evidence inform curriculum policy? The methodology combines a systematic audit of the claims circulating in the popular narrative, examining nine assertions against primary scientific literature, legislative records, and government documents, with a structured narrative synthesis of empirical research. The literature reviewed includes functional magnetic resonance imaging studies involving prereading children, high-density electroencephalography investigations involving school-age children and adults, and randomized and quasi-experimental studies of handwriting training. The findings indicate that the popular narrative is directionally correct but factually imprecise in several important respects. The frequently cited Johns Hopkins study by Wiley and Rapp (2021), for example, investigated adults learning Arabic script rather than children acquiring their native writing system. The Norwegian electroencephalography study was published in 2024, rather than 2023. Furthermore, Indiana’s 2023 legislation requires schools to report on cursive handwriting instruction rather than explicitly mandating its reinstatement in every school curriculum. Despite these inaccuracies, the underlying empirical evidence provides substantial grounds for considering handwriting an important component of literacy instruction. Research suggests that handwriting experience is associated with faster letter learning, improved generalization to reading and spelling tasks, and broader patterns of functional brain connectivity than those observed during typing. These findings are consistent with the hypothesis that handwriting integrates visual perception, motor planning, proprioceptive feedback, and orthographic representation in ways that may support the development of literacy-related skills. Nevertheless, the evidence must be interpreted cautiously. Findings concerning handwriting in general cannot automatically be generalized to cursive writing specifically, for which the empirical literature remains comparatively limited. Moreover, credible null findings demonstrate that the advantages of handwriting are not universal across every task, population, or experimental condition. The dissertation concludes that public and educational policy discussions have repeatedly oscillated between two problematic positions: the administrative dismissal of handwriting as an outdated instructional practice and the popular overstatement of what neuroscience has conclusively demonstrated. Neither position adequately reflects the complexity of the available evidence. Instead, this study advances a third position: handwriting instruction, initially through manuscript printing and subsequently through cursive writing, represents a developmentally distinctive form of sensorimotor-enriched literacy training with defensible educational value. This position does not imply that handwriting should replace digital literacy or that cursive instruction has been proven superior in every respect. Keyboarding remains indispensable in contemporary education, and students require opportunities to develop proficiency in both modalities. Accordingly, primary-school curriculum policy should preserve explicit handwriting instruction while integrating keyboarding as a complementary skill. Decisions regarding instructional time, developmental sequencing, and the relative emphasis placed on manuscript and cursive writing should be guided by the quality of the empirical evidence, students’ developmental needs, and clearly articulated educational objectives rather than by technological convenience or exaggerated interpretations of neuroscientific findings. Ultimately, the central policy question is not whether schools should choose handwriting over technology, but how educational systems can integrate both forms of written communication in ways that best support children’s literacy development.

papers.title: TEACHERS' DECISION-MAKING IN ADAPTING AI-GENERATED ACADEMIC TEXTS FOR TASK-BASED LANGUAGE TEACHING (TBLT) IN UZBEKISTAN
papers.authors: Tursunova Sharifa
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This thesis analyzes teachers’ pedagogical decision-making in selecting and adapting artificial intelligence-generated academic texts for Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT) in the context of teaching English as a foreign language (EFL) in Uzbekistan. The study considers texts generated by generative AI tools not as ready-to-use teaching materials, but as resources that require linguistic, content-related, and methodological evaluation and adaptation by teachers to suit specific learning tasks. Particular attention is paid to teachers’ decisions based on lexical and grammatical complexity, content accuracy and reliability, students’ language proficiency, the characteristics of academic discourse, the communicative purpose of the task, and relevance to the local educational context. The study also systematizes adaptation strategies such as simplifying and shortening texts, replacing lexical items, contextualizing content, and transforming texts into TBLT tasks. The analysis demonstrates that artificial intelligence does not automatically guarantee pedagogically appropriate materials and that the quality of the final learning materials depends on teachers’ professional judgment, linguistic competence, and methodological decisions.

papers.title: When AI Becomes the Travel Agent: How Tourists Negotiate Trust, Autonomy, and Authenticity in AI-Generated Travel Decisions
papers.authors: Fatimah Abdulaziz Alshiha Muhammad Awais Bhatti
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly transforming how tourists search for information, plan itineraries, and make travel decisions. However, limited qualitative research explains how tourists negotiate their agency when AI becomes actively involved in travel decision-making. This study explores how tourists experience GenAI-mediated travel decisions, focusing on autonomy, trust, skepticism, authenticity, and spontaneity. Drawing on a qualitative research approach, semi-structured interviews were conducted with six tourists who had experience using GenAI for travel planning. Thematic analysis identified five interconnected themes: AI as a travel decision partner; between convenience and decision autonomy; trust, verification, and skepticism; the tension between ai optimization and travel spontaneity; and reconstructing authenticity in AI-mediated travel. The findings indicate that tourists perceive GenAI as a decision partner rather than a replacement for human judgment. AI enhances planning convenience but can increase reliance, making autonomy a negotiated process. Trust is conditional and supported by verification, while AI optimization creates tensions with spontaneity. Furthermore, AI can facilitate authentic experiences while potentially contributing to algorithmic standardization. The study contributes to tourism research by conceptualizing AI-mediated travel decision-making as a process of negotiated agency between tourists and AI.

papers.title: Scarcity of Opportunity and Educational Resources: Analyzing Systemic Barriers Among Secondary Students in Balochistan, Pakistan
papers.authors: Maham Shah
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This research paper investigates the severe educational resource scarcity in Balochistan, and its impact on student learning outcomes and career Preparation. Regardless of growing youth populations, public and private educational institutions in the region face widespread systemic challenges. Based on survey data his study shows how local education falls short in basic school facilities, modern technology subjects, practical career training, global exam access, college degree tracks, and extracurricular activities. Specifically, over 69% of local students rely on government schools plagued by broken facilities, missing basic utilities, and unmonitored teacher absenteeism. Furthermore, institutions suffer from a complete absence of modern fields like Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Robotics, poor quality in practical computer-based training, extreme financial barriers in advanced schooling (A-Levels), a total lack of international test centers (SAT/TOEFL), and a major shortage of sports, public speaking, and student development programs. The paper also highlights severe gender disparities caused by unsafe transport options and domestic burdens. To bridge the gap between classroom instruction and modern market requirements, this study proposes key policy recommendations, including targeted infrastructure investment, institutional accountability, curriculum modernization, fully equipped science and computer laboratories, structured career counseling, extracurricular programs (sports and Model United Nations), and safe, dedicated transportation for female students.

papers.title: Beyond the Balance: How Female Entrepreneurs Navigate Economic Change, FamilyResponsibilities, Leadership, and Artificial Intelligence in Today's Business World
papers.authors: Singh Shyla
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Female entrepreneurs play an increasingly important role in the global economy, creating businesses, generating employment, and introducing innovative products and services. However, building and maintaining a successful business in today's world presents challenges that extend far beyond making a profit. Women entrepreneurs must respond to economic uncertainty, manage employees, adapt to rapidly changing technology, and often balance professional responsibilities with family and personal commitments. The rise of artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced both new opportunities and additional pressures, requiring business owners to continuously develop new skills to remain competitive. This paper examines the challenges and opportunities facing female entrepreneurs in the modern business environment. Using a review of existing research and published reports, supplemented by three original interviews with women business founders, it explores how economic conditions, work-life responsibilities, leadership demands, and technological innovation influence women's entrepreneurial experiences. It also considers strategies that may help women build sustainable and successful businesses, including effective time management, employee delegation, professional networking, and the adoption of AI-powered tools. The paper argues that entrepreneurial success should be understood not only through financial performance but also through business sustainability, personal well-being, adaptability, and the ability to lead effectively in a changing world.

papers.title: आरटफशयल इटलजस क यग म टचर एजकशन: शकषक परशकषण, डजटल नवचर, वयवसयक दकषतए, नतकत एव भवषय क सभवनए
papers.authors: मनोज कुमार पटेल
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: सारांश वर्तमान समय में आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस (Artificial Intelligence—AI) शिक्षा के क्षेत्र में एक परिवर्तनकारी शक्ति के रूप में उभर रहा है। विशेष रूप से शिक्षक शिक्षा (Teacher Education) में एआई ने शिक्षण-अधिगम प्रक्रिया, मूल्यांकन प्रणाली, पाठ-योजना निर्माण, अनुसंधान, व्यावसायिक विकास तथा शैक्षिक नेतृत्व के स्वरूप को व्यापक रूप से प्रभावित किया है। जनरेटिव एआई आधारित उपकरण, जैसे ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot तथा अन्य बुद्धिमान प्रणालियाँ, शिक्षकों को गुणवत्तापूर्ण शिक्षण सामग्री तैयार करने, विद्यार्थियों की व्यक्तिगत अधिगम आवश्यकताओं को समझने तथा शिक्षण प्रक्रिया को अधिक प्रभावी एवं सहभागितापूर्ण बनाने में सहायता प्रदान कर रही हैं। राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति-2020 (NEP-2020) ने भी शिक्षा व्यवस्था में प्रौद्योगिकी के समुचित उपयोग, डिजिटल दक्षताओं के विकास तथा नवाचार-आधारित शिक्षक शिक्षा पर विशेष बल दिया है। इसके अतिरिक्त, यूनेस्को तथा अन्य अंतरराष्ट्रीय संस्थाएँ एआई के उपयोग में मानव-केंद्रित, नैतिक एवं समावेशी दृष्टिकोण अपनाने की आवश्यकता पर बल देती हैं। अतः शिक्षक शिक्षा संस्थानों के समक्ष यह चुनौती है कि वे भावी शिक्षकों को केवल तकनीकी दक्षताओं तक सीमित न रखकर उन्हें आलोचनात्मक चिंतन, सृजनात्मकता, नैतिक उत्तरदायित्व, डेटा गोपनीयता तथा डिजिटल नागरिकता जैसे गुणों से भी सुसज्जित करें। प्रस्तुत शोध-पत्र का उद्देश्य एआई के युग में शिक्षक शिक्षा के बदलते स्वरूप का विश्लेषण करना है। इसमें शिक्षक प्रशिक्षण, जनरेटिव एआई, डिजिटल शिक्षाशास्त्र, व्यावसायिक दक्षताओं, वैयक्तिकृत अधिगम, नैतिकता, डेटा सुरक्षा, राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति-2020, समावेशी शिक्षा, अनुसंधान एवं नवाचार तथा सतत विकास लक्ष्यों (SDGs) के संदर्भ में भविष्य की संभावनाओं का अध्ययन किया गया है। यह अध्ययन मुख्यतः द्वितीयक स्रोतों पर आधारित गुणात्मक एवं विश्लेषणात्मक प्रकृति का है। शोध के निष्कर्ष संकेत करते हैं कि भविष्य का शिक्षक केवल ज्ञान का प्रदाता नहीं होगा, बल्कि वह एआई-सक्षम अधिगम वातावरण का मार्गदर्शक, नवाचारकर्ता, शोधकर्ता एवं नैतिक नेतृत्वकर्ता भी होगा। इस परिवर्तन को प्रभावी बनाने के लिए शिक्षक-प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रमों में एआई साक्षरता, डिजिटल शिक्षाशास्त्र, papers.title: CATEGORY-BASED PROMPT CONSTRUCTION FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EDUCATION: A PEDAGOGICAL PROMPT ENGINEERING MODEL AND WEB TOOL
papers.authors: Qosimova Umida
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article proposes a pedagogical model, and a web tool built on it, for constructing prompts by educational material category so that teachers and researchers can work effectively with artificial intelligence (large language models). The relevance of the study stems from the fact that the quality of a generative model's output depends directly on the quality of the instruction, while many educators lack prompt-writing skills. The aim was to develop a solution that produces ready-to-use, structured prompts for eleven types of educational material: lesson plans, research projects, scientific articles, 3D models, multimedia, animation, virtual materials, assessment, didactic games, graphics and software development. A design-based approach was applied, combining prompt engineering principles with the TPACK framework. As a result, a five-part prompt structure (role, task, context, requirements, output format), a set of category-specific parameters, a mechanism for adapting prompts to the target type of AI tool, and a model-assisted prompt refinement step were developed. The tool requires no installation and runs via a link on computers and mobile devices. The article discusses the didactic potential and limitations of the model and outlines a protocol for its empirical validation.

papers.title: AUTOMATIC GENERATION OF DIDACTIC CARDS WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION: A METHODOLOGICAL MODEL AND SOFTWARE TOOL FOR ENHANCING CLASSROOM MOTIVATION
papers.authors: Masharipov Madiyor, Gulchehra Abdusamatova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article substantiates a methodological model, and a software tool built on it, for the automatic generation of didactic cards with artificial intelligence (large language models) in order to increase learner motivation in higher education classes. The study aims to develop a solution that, from a teacher's input on the subject, level of education, group and topic, quickly produces a set of questions of gradually increasing difficulty and allows these questions to be used as a game on an interactive whiteboard. A design-based approach was applied, combining the revised Bloom's taxonomy, formative assessment and gamification principles. As a result, a mechanism for distributing cards across four difficulty levels, a structured prompt for question generation, and an algorithm for hiding questions and answers behind numbered cards and revealing them only under the teacher's control were developed. The model was implemented as a web application that runs on computers and mobile devices. The article discusses the didactic potential and limitations of the model and outlines a protocol for its empirical validation in pedagogical practice. The findings may be useful for university teachers, instructional designers and researchers in educational technology.

papers.title: MONITORING STUDENTS' LEARNING OUTCOMES AND ASSESSING INDIVIDUAL DEVELOPMENT WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN A DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT
papers.authors: Shakhnoza Mingyasharovna Ravshanova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper provides a scientific and methodological analysis of monitoring students' learning outcomes and assessing their individual development with artificial intelligence (AI) in a digital educational environment. It examines the content of learning outcome monitoring, the components on which it relies (data sources, indicators, analytical methods and feedback), and the opportunities offered by AI-based learning analytics. It also defines three groups of criteria for assessing individual development: the dynamics of results, the achievement of learning goals, and independent work and reflection. As a result, a six-stage methodology is proposed in which the teacher keeps the final pedagogical decision. The methodology is intended to support the timely and individualised assessment of students in higher education institutions.

papers.title: Living Labs: від європейського досвіду до українських практик інновацій
papers.authors: Teodoziia Yatsyshyn
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This presentation summarizes key insights from participation in OpenLivingLab Days 2026 and a study visit to LiCalab (Belgium), one of Europe’s leading Living Labs. It introduces the Living Lab approach, its core principles and distinguishing features, the role of user-centered co-creation, and practical mechanisms for collaboration between universities, businesses, governments, and communities. The presentation also highlights examples of Living Lab services, business engagement models, sustainability considerations, KPI and KVI approaches, and opportunities for international cooperation. Special attention is given to the development of a Campus Living Lab at Ivano-Frankivsk National Technical University of Oil and Gas (IFNTUOG) and the application of Living Lab methodologies in the Ukrainian context.

papers.title: METHODOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS OF USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN PROGRAMMING EDUCATION
papers.authors: Farog'at Fayzullayeva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The article analyzes the penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into programming education, their didactic opportunities and risks. A four-component methodological model is proposed for using AI tools while preserving students' independent programming skills and algorithmic thinking: staged use of AI, developing AI-collaboration competence, renewing the assessment system, and project-based learning. The model can be applied in teaching programming and computer science at higher education institutions.

papers.title: User Satisfaction with a Production-Grade Generative AI Copilot in Well Construction: Evidence from a PLS SEM Field Study
papers.authors: Cláudio Benevenuto de Campos Lima, Antorweep Chakravorty, Arild Normann Nystad, Diogo Melo Paes, Marcelo Nogueira Grimberg, Vitor Brandão Sabbagh, Anderson Rapello dos Santos, Felipe Lima de Oliveira, Antonio Carlos da  Silva, Claudia Evelyn Escobar Montecino
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper presents a field-based, cross-sectional statistical evaluation of user satisfaction with Cortex, a generative AI copilot deployed in well construction activities at Petrobras. Although large language models and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) architectures are expanding in industrial environments, empirical evidence regarding the factors associated with user satisfaction in production-grade enterprise settings remains limited. Based on a structured survey of actual users, the study evaluates a structural model examining the relationships among prior use of AI tools, AI literacy, usability, response quality, benefits, and overall satisfaction. The analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), including measurement model assessment and bootstrapping with 5000 resamples. The measurement model demonstrated adequate internal consistency, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. In the structural model, eight of thirteen hypothesized relationships were supported. The strongest direct relationship was observed between response quality and perceived benefits (β = 0.619; p < 0.001), while perceived benefits showed the strongest direct association with satisfaction (β = 0.394; p < 0.001). Usability also exhibited substantial total associations with both benefits and overall satisfaction through indirect pathways. The model accounted for 71.6% of the variance in satisfaction (R² = 0.716) and demonstrated substantial in-sample predictive relevance (Q² = 0.696). The findings suggest that satisfaction is less associated with prior AI exposure and more with how usability and response quality translate into perceived gains in daily work. The study contributes to the literature on generative AI adoption in industrial contexts and provides implications for training, system design, and governance.

papers.title: Molecular Biology and Genetics: Theoretical Models, Numerical Verification and Research Collection (2026)
papers.authors: Begüm Yıldırım
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This research collection brings together 26 distinct works addressing theoretical, computational and interdisciplinary questions in molecular biology, genetics and related biomedical sciences. The studies investigate biological mechanisms through mathematical formulations, numerical analyses, theoretical modeling and comparisons with previously published experimental findings. The collection covers several research areas, including cellular processes, molecular mechanisms, proteomics, immune responses and radiobiological phenomena. Methodology and Numerical Verification The research employs theoretical frameworks, quantitative calculations and numerical consistency assessments. Where applicable, model-derived results are examined in relation to findings reported in external experimental literature. Numerical verification is distinguished from direct laboratory experimentation. Comparisons with external experimental sources are presented according to the specific evidence available for each study. Theoretical cellular mechanisms and potential clinical implications are discussed as research interpretations rather than direct demonstrations of clinical efficacy. Collection Contents The archive contains 26 academically revised Word manuscripts, seven original PDF research documents, supporting materials and an organized research portfolio. The accompanying documentation describes methodological approaches, reported findings, relevant evidence, limitations and considerations for further investigation. Research Scope This collection is intended to facilitate academic review, scholarly discussion, methodological assessment and further research development. The level of numerical and experimental support varies across the included studies. Publication of this collection does not itself constitute independent experimental or clinical validation. Artificial Intelligence Assistance Disclosure OpenAI's ChatGPT was used to assist with language editing, academic restructuring, terminology standardization and organization of the research manuscripts and accompanying documentation. AI assistance was also used for selected numerical consistency and reference checks. The author retains responsibility for the scientific content, interpretations, source accuracy and final manuscript review. AI assistance is not presented as independent experimental evidence. Purpose This collection is shared to support academic transparency, interdisciplinary discussion and future evaluation of the proposed theoretical and quantitative frameworks.

papers.title: AI Security Testing Outruns Its Evidence: A Literature Survey of the State of the Field as of October 2026
papers.authors: Rawan Alfarraj
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence moved from an assistant for individual security-testing steps to a credible autonomous finder, exploiter and fixer of software vulnerabilities between 2023 and October 2026, but the evidence for that shift is uneven. This narrative survey synthesises research on four technical strands (AI-driven penetration testing and offensive automation; AI-assisted fuzzing and dynamic testing; AI-based vulnerability detection and automated repair, including the security of AI-generated code; and benchmarks and evaluation methodology) and two contextual strands (industry adoption and economics; risks, law and governance). Every claim is graded by evidence tier: peer-reviewed, preprint, government or organiser report, vendor claim, or secondary summary. The best organiser-scored result is the DARPA AI Cyber Challenge final (August 2025), in which seven cyber reasoning systems found 54 of 63 synthetic vulnerabilities and patched 43 at an average of about USD 152 per task. Peer-reviewed work supports a consistent design lesson: the reproducible gains come from hybrids in which a large language model supplies semantics (harnesses, specifications, taint sources, triage) and a deterministic component (fuzzer, static analyser, prover, exploit replay) supplies ground truth. By contrast, the most dramatic 2026 results, such as frontier models reported to find thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities, are vendor claims that third parties cannot yet reproduce. Independent benchmarks report far lower end-to-end autonomy than system papers, public benchmarks saturate or leak within 12 to 24 months, and about half or more of functionally correct AI-generated code remains exploitable in controlled studies. The binding constraints in 2026 are verification of findings, remediation capacity, safe operation of agents, and governance of access and disclosure, rather than discovery itself. We close with ten open problems and a statement of this survey's limitations.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-ASSISTED LEARNING ON EFL LEARNERS' SPEAKING PROFICIENCY: EVIDENCE FROM UZBEK UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
papers.authors: Asadbek Xabibullayev, Diyora Toirxo'jayeva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for improving English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning, particularly in the development of speaking proficiency. AI-powered chatbots, speech recognition systems, conversational agents, and generative AI applications enable learners to practise English, receive immediate feedback, and engage in interactive communication beyond the traditional classroom. This article examines the potential impact of AI-assisted learning on EFL learners’ speaking proficiency, with particular attention to the educational context of Uzbek universities. It explores the ways in which AI-based tools may support speaking fluency, pronunciation, grammatical accuracy, vocabulary development, learner confidence, and willingness to communicate. Drawing on existing research and pedagogical perspectives, the article discusses the opportunities and limitations of integrating AI into higher education. Particular attention is given to speaking anxiety, unequal access to digital resources, feedback reliability, learner autonomy, and the importance of teacher guidance. The analysis suggests that AI can serve as a valuable supplementary resource when integrated into structured pedagogical activities. However, its effectiveness depends on learners’ engagement, instructional design, and the combination of technological practice with authentic human interaction. Further empirical research involving Uzbek university students is necessary to establish the extent and long-term effects of AI-assisted speaking instruction. Keywords: artificial intelligence, EFL learners, speaking proficiency, AI-assisted learning, university students, conversational AI, language anxiety, Uzbekistan, digital education.

papers.title: It Is Not the Phrase; It Is the Expectation: Understanding User Perceptions of Contrastive Negation in AI-Generated Responses
papers.authors: Guobin Wang, Xiaoce Wang, Minqian YANG, Pei-Luen Patrick Rau
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Recognizable AI writing habits attract public criticism, but their implications for designing conversational interfaces remain unclear. We examine Contrastive Negation (``not X, but Y'') as a case. Two online experiments ($N = 242$), informed by formative interviews and material validation, distinguished response form, negated content, and interlocutor expectations. The construction showed no consistent evaluative or behavioral penalty and slightly increased anthropomorphism. Unexpectable negations increased autonomy threat only under human expectation; compatibility reduced it under AI disclosure. The same supportive replies were received differently across frames: their mood advantage under AI disclosure disappeared under human expectation. Within the human-expected frame, inferred AI authorship accompanied poorer evaluations. Together, the findings distinguish AI recognizability from response quality and acceptance, and motivate grounding attributed user positions and aligning language with interface-created expectations.

papers.title: Expression, Verification, and the Scarcity of Aesthetic Education: Reinterpreting Moral Rights in the Age of Generative AI
papers.authors: Carter
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper argues that the denial of copyright and moral rights to works substantially shaped by human expressive judgment in generative AI systems produces two interrelated harms: the incentive to conceal AI involvement (“trace forgery”) and the proliferation of low-quality content (“flooding”). Drawing on R. G. Collingwood’s distinction between craft and expression in The Principles of Art, it contends that generative AI separates technical execution (craft) from the human process of clarifying an initially indeterminate intention (expression). Chinese judicial practice, which requires process records of prompting, iteration, selection, and modification, already partially recognizes this separation. In the AI era, the functions of moral rights shift: the right of attribution becomes a declaration of authorial acceptance or verification, while the right of integrity protects the author’s evaluative standard and associated reputation. Recognition of these functions aligns incentives toward the production of excellent works and open acknowledgment of AI participation, rather than concealment or flooding. The stakes are uniquely high because the present generation of children is forming aesthetic judgment precisely when craft and expression have been decoupled; the window for correct training of expressive capacity is therefore the true cost of inaction. Historically, copyright has regulated successive scarcities (books, authors, channels, attention), yet its underlying object has always been educational opportunity. The current scarcity is that of proper aesthetic education itself.

papers.title: Sounding Like Which AI? Machine-Style Overlap of arXiv Abstracts with Language Models of Different Vintages
papers.authors: Natik Chhabra
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We ask not how much text was produced with LLM help but how much writing, by any author, falls on the LLM side of a stylistic boundary, and which LLMs define that side. We define Machine-Style Overlap (MSO): the share of documents that a calibrated classifier on style features that ignore content-word identity judges at least as likely to be LLM output as pre-ChatGPT human writing. In 131,448 arXiv abstracts (2015–2026), MSO was 9.2% before ChatGPT and by June 2025 stood 25.4 percentage points (pp) above its pre-ChatGPT trend, far above placebo gaps. Because recent LLMs learn from recent writing, we compare generators by vintage. Against generators whose pretraining data predate ChatGPT, the gap is smaller (7.5–13.1 pp by post-trend fit; 3.5–7.6 pp for two models run from titles). Single-generator overlap mostly rose then fell, peaking later for newer generators even at equal text length (exploratory rank correlation 0.79, n = 18; 0.66 without three added post hoc). A fixed reference set, like a fixed marker-word list (delve), can show the shift receding while overlap with newer models still rises. In US school essays, English learners' essays fall in the region less often, largely because of essay scores. AI use: the study was carried out by an AI system (Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic) under the author's direction and is disclosed in full in the paper's Acknowledgements. The author read and approved this version. Code, data and results: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23343987

papers.title: Celebrating Indian Scientific Excellence: The Legacy of C. V. Raman, Scientific Mentorship, and the Advancement of Research Culture in India
papers.authors: Sudhakar Geruganti
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Author: Geruganti SudhakarAffiliation: Faculty, IIIT RGUKT Basar, Telangana, India 2. Alternative Research Paper Titles From C. V. Raman to Modern India: Scientific Excellence, Research Innovation, and the Future of Indian Science The Legacy of C. V. Raman: Inspiring Scientific Curiosity, Innovation, and Research Excellence in India Nurturing Scientific Talent in India: Lessons from C. V. Raman’s Contributions and Research Philosophy Indian Scientific Excellence and Global Recognition: The Role of Mentorship, Education, and Research Institutions Building a Culture of Scientific Discovery in India: Historical Contributions, Contemporary Challenges, and Future Opportunities Beyond Discovery: C. V. Raman’s Scientific Legacy and Its Relevance to Contemporary Indian Research From Scientific Inspiration to National Development: Strengthening India’s Research and Innovation Ecosystem Scientific Temper and Indigenous Innovation: Advancing India’s Research Culture Through the Legacy of C. V. Raman 3. Recommended Subtitle Writing Historical Perspectives, Scientific Mentorship, Research Education, and Strategies for Strengthening India’s Global Scientific Competitiveness 4. Detailed Description of the Research Paper Abstract and Scope Abstract and Scope This paper explores the significance of Indian scientific excellence through the legacy of C. V. Raman, one of India’s most distinguished physicists and the recipient of the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the Raman effect. It examines how scientific curiosity, independent thinking, experimental investigation, and sustained dedication contribute to transformative discoveries and the development of a strong national research culture. The paper places Raman’s scientific achievements within the broader context of India’s scientific development, emphasizing the importance of mentorship, quality education, institutional support, interdisciplinary collaboration, and opportunities for emerging researchers. It also discusses contemporary challenges faced by students and early-career scientists, including limited access to advanced research facilities, unequal research opportunities, funding constraints, and the need to connect scientific education with original investigation. 1. Introduction Scientific progress is a key driver of technological advancement, economic development, and social well-being. India has a distinguished scientific heritage, and the achievements of researchers such as C. V. Raman demonstrate the capacity of Indian scientists to make discoveries of international significance. The introduction establishes the relevance of Raman’s scientific legacy to contemporary science education, innovation policy, and research development. 2. C. V. Raman and His Scientific Contributions This section examines Raman’s scientific journey, his interest in the physical properties of light, and the discovery of the Raman effect. It explains the importance of the discovery in spectroscopy, materials characterization, chemical analysis, and modern scientific research. It also considers how Raman’s work illustrates the value of observation, experimentation, persistence, and intellectual independence. 3. Scientific Excellence and National Development Scientific excellence extends beyond individual discoveries. It contributes to the development of advanced technologies, industrial competitiveness, healthcare, energy systems, environmental protection, and evidence-based public policy. This section discusses the relationship between fundamental research, applied science, and national development, highlighting the need to support both curiosity-driven investigation and research addressing societal needs. 4. Scientific Mentorship and the Development of Young Researchers Mentorship plays a crucial role in developing scientific talent. Experienced researchers can help students develop research questions, design experiments, interpret evidence, communicate findings, and maintain scientific integrity. This section explores the importance of supportive academic environments, accessible research guidance, undergraduate research opportunities, and collaborative learning in encouraging future generations of Indian scientists. 5. Research Institutions and Higher Education in India Universities, laboratories, technical institutions, and national research organizations form the foundation of a strong scientific ecosystem. This section examines their role in developing skilled researchers, promoting interdisciplinary studies, facilitating industry–academia collaboration, and translating discoveries into practical applications. It also emphasizes the importance of laboratory infrastructure, research funding, transparent evaluation, and opportunities for early-career academics. 6. Challenges Facing Emerging Indian Scientists Despite substantial scientific achievements, emerging researchers may encounter barriers such as unequal access to laboratory facilities, limited research funding, administrative burdens, publication pressures, and insufficient opportunities for international collaboration. This section considers these challenges and discusses practical approaches to improving research accessibility, strengthening institutional support, and encouraging high-quality, reproducible, and ethically conducted science. 7. Scientific Temper, Innovation, and Research Culture A vibrant research culture depends on curiosity, critical thinking, openness to evidence, and the willingness to question established explanations. Drawing inspiration from Raman’s scientific approach, this section discusses ways to promote inquiry-based learning, experimental demonstrations, student research projects, science communication, and interdisciplinary innovation. It also highlights the importance of recognizing original contributions rather than relying exclusively on examination performance or publication counts. 8. A Framework for Strengthening India’s Scientific Ecosystem The paper proposes an integrated framework built around five priorities: Research-oriented education: Integrating laboratory investigation, scientific writing, and problem-solving into undergraduate and postgraduate education. Mentorship and collaboration: Establishing structured mentorship programmes connecting students with experienced researchers. Infrastructure and funding: Expanding access to laboratories, scientific instruments, research grants, and shared research facilities. Ethical and responsible research: Encouraging transparency, reproducibility, appropriate authorship, and rigorous peer review. Public engagement and recognition: Improving science communication and celebrating meaningful scientific contributions across institutions and disciplines. 9. Future Directions Future efforts should focus on strengthening research opportunities for young scientists, improving university research infrastructure, promoting international scientific partnerships, and connecting fundamental discoveries with emerging technological fields. Areas such as advanced materials, photonics, artificial intelligence, renewable energy, biotechnology, and sustainable manufacturing offer opportunities for Indian researchers to contribute to global scientific progress. 10. Conclusion C. V. Raman’s scientific legacy offers an enduring example of the power of curiosity, experimentation, perseverance, and independent thinking. Building on this legacy requires more than celebrating historical achievements; it calls for sustained investment in scientific education, mentorship, research institutions, and an environment that values original discovery. By nurturing young talent and strengthening the foundations of research, India can expand its contributions to global science while addressing its own technological and societal priorities. Overall Significance The paper connects a major figure in Indian scientific history with contemporary questions about research excellence, mentorship, higher education, and national innovation. Its central argument is that a strong scientific future depends on cultivating the conditions in which talented individuals can ask important questions, test ideas rigorously, collaborate effectively, and transform discoveries into lasting knowledge and societal benefits. 5. Recommended Final Combination For a formal academic manuscript, I recommend the following combination: Main title: Celebrating Indian Scientific Excellence: The Legacy of C. V. Raman, Scientific Mentorship, and the Advancement of Research Culture in India Alternative title: From C. V. Raman to Modern India: Scientific Excellence, Research Innovation, and the Future of Indian Science Subtitle: Historical Perspectives, Scientific Mentorship, Research Education, and Strategies for Strengthening India’s Global Scientific Competitiveness Paper type: Narrative review and research-policy perspective Keywords: C. V. Raman; Raman effect; Indian science; scientific excellence; research culture; scientific mentorship; higher education; innovation; research policy; scientific temper. Important note: Before submitting the paper, verify the identity and historical details of the person featured in the original newspaper article. The title above uses C. V. Raman as its central subject; person-specific claims should be retained only if the article confirms that identification.

papers.authors: Sudhakar Geruganti
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This combined title brings together the major themes of the research paper: AI-driven automation, changing employment patterns, emerging skill requirements, economic opportunities, and the social challenges associated with technological progress. 2. A Narrative Review of Automation, Job Transformation, and Emerging Workforce Skills Assessing Employment Risks, Productivity Gains, and Reskilling Requirements A Socioeconomic Perspective on Human–AI Collaboration and Inclusive Growth Challenges and Opportunities for India's Workforce in the Emerging Digital Economy An Integrated Framework for Education, Workforce Adaptation, and Responsible AI Adoption Understanding Occupational Exposure, Labour-Market Inequality, and Future Career Pathways Evidence, Policy Challenges, and Strategies for Sustainable Employment in the AI Era Bridging Technological Innovation, Human Capital Development, and Social Responsibility 4. Detailed description of the research paper Research title Research title The AI Tsunami: Transforming Employment, Skills, and the Future of Work in the Digital Economy Subtitle: An Integrated Analysis of Automation, Human–AI Collaboration, Workforce Reskilling, and Socioeconomic Transformation Author: Geruganti SudhakarAffiliation: Faculty, IIIT RGUKT Basar Background and rationale Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming an important component of the modern economy, influencing how businesses operate, how professionals perform their duties, and how educational institutions prepare students for employment. Advances in generative AI, machine learning, intelligent automation, robotics, and data analytics are enabling machines to undertake an increasing range of cognitive and operational tasks. The Telugu newspaper article “ఏఐ సునామీ… మెల్లిగా ముంచుకొస్తోంది..!!”—approximately translated as “The AI Tsunami Is Slowly Approaching”—provides the thematic foundation for this research paper. The metaphor highlights growing public concern about the speed of technological change and its potential implications for jobs, professional skills, and economic security. However, the relationship between AI and employment is not simply a matter of machines replacing people. AI can automate selected tasks, improve human productivity, create new occupations, and transform existing professions. Its ultimate impact depends on technological capabilities, business decisions, market demand, education systems, and public policy. This paper examines these interconnected issues through a narrative review of relevant research and policy literature, with particular emphasis on India's workforce and digital economy. Research objectives The principal objectives are to: Examine how AI is transforming employment patterns and occupational structures. Distinguish between task automation, occupational transformation, and complete job displacement. Identify sectors and categories of workers that may experience substantial technological disruption. Investigate the emergence of new career opportunities and AI-related professional skills. Analyze the role of education, reskilling, and lifelong learning in workforce adaptation. Explore the implications of AI for income inequality, job security, and socioeconomic inclusion. Develop a conceptual framework for responsible AI adoption and inclusive employment growth in India. Major research themes 1. AI-driven automation and employment transformation The paper examines how AI affects routine administrative work, customer service, software development, manufacturing, education, and other professional activities. It considers how automation may reduce demand for certain tasks while changing the responsibilities and skill requirements of existing occupations. 2. Job displacement versus job creation A central theme is the distinction between technological exposure and actual job loss. The paper explores how productivity improvements, business expansion, new products, and emerging occupations may generate employment opportunities, while recognizing that some workers may face displacement or difficult transitions. 3. The changing nature of professional skills The study considers the increasing importance of AI literacy, data interpretation, critical thinking, communication, problem-solving, domain expertise, and responsible technology use. It argues that future employability will depend increasingly on the ability to combine technological tools with human judgment. 4. Economic and social consequences The paper discusses potential effects on wages, job security, career progression, labour-market inequality, and access to economic opportunities. It highlights the possibility that technological benefits may be distributed unevenly unless education, training, and social protection policies address the needs of vulnerable workers. 5. AI and India's employment landscape India presents a particularly important context because of its large workforce, growing digital economy, extensive IT and business-services sectors, manufacturing ambitions, and expanding higher-education system. The paper explores opportunities and risks for graduates, entry-level professionals, technical workers, and small businesses. 6. Education and workforce reskilling The research examines how universities, technical institutions, employers, and vocational training organizations can prepare learners for an AI-enabled economy. It emphasizes practical learning, industry–academia collaboration, continuous professional development, and the importance of developing independent reasoning alongside AI proficiency. 7. Responsible AI and public policy The paper proposes policy directions involving labour-market monitoring, accessible reskilling programmes, worker-transition assistance, responsible workplace deployment, data privacy, human oversight, and inclusive access to technological opportunities. Proposed conceptual contribution The paper introduces a five-pillar conceptual framework for managing AI-driven employment transformation: Technological readiness: Digital infrastructure, reliable data systems, and access to appropriate AI tools. Human capital development: AI literacy, technical education, vocational training, and lifelong learning. Employment transition support: Career guidance, job matching, retraining, and assistance for displaced workers. Responsible AI adoption: Fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, and appropriate human oversight. Inclusive economic growth: Ensuring that workers, smaller enterprises, and underserved communities can benefit from AI-related opportunities. This framework is a proposed synthesis of the reviewed literature. Its effectiveness would need to be assessed through empirical studies and real-world implementation. Research significance The significance of this research lies in its balanced treatment of AI as both an opportunity for economic development and a potential source of labour-market disruption. Rather than assuming that AI will inevitably eliminate jobs or automatically create sufficient new employment, the paper emphasizes the importance of understanding the conditions under which different outcomes emerge. The study may be relevant to researchers in technology management, economics, education, public policy, labour studies, and digital transformation. It may also provide a useful conceptual foundation for discussions about curriculum reform, professional development, and workforce planning in Indian technical institutions. Highlight potential socioeconomic risks associated with unequal access to AI. Present a conceptual framework for inclusive and responsible AI adoption. Identify future research opportunities involving Indian industries, educational institutions, and labour markets.
