Constipation was more frequent in PD at both time points (T0 p = 0.004; T1 p = 0.011). Comorbidities, smoking, weight and BMI did not differ within pairs. Preserved-fish intake was stably lower in PD (T0 p = 0.021; T1 p = 0.004); fruit intake was lower in PD at baseline (MZ, p = 0.001) but higher at follow-up (p = 0.029). Conclusions: The mortality difference persisted despite no detected within-pair differences in BMI and comorbidities, consistent with a major contribution of PD itself. Preserved-fish intake remained stably lower in affected twins, whereas increased fruit intake at follow-up may reflect adaptation to constipation; these exploratory dietary findings warrant confirmation.

papers.title: A Domain-Adapted Multilingual Large Language Model for Mining Safety in African Languages
papers.authors: Macdonald Mashawi, Rajive Ganguli
papers.abstract: The African mining industry continues to face a serious communication gap between technical safety documentation and the language used by the workforce. Safety manuals, operating procedures, and regulatory guidance are often produced in English or French, while many workers communicate in isiZulu, chiShona, and other local languages. This mismatch is not just inconvenient; it can be dangerous in safety-critical settings where misunderstandings may contribute to preventable incidents. This paper reports on Talk MINING, a domain-adapted multilingual large language model built on InkubaLM and trained on mining-specific text, question–answer pairs, and multimodal hazard data. The model was developed using Hugging Face tools and evaluated with both quantitative and qualitative methods. Results show a marked improvement over the baseline model, with overall accuracy rising from below 50% to 82%, and strong gains across isiZulu, chiShona, and English. The project also includes a web-based prototype that allows users to take photos of mining conditions and receive guidance in a local language. This paper presents the full pipeline for Talk MINING, including document preparation, translation and localization, model training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and validation. Beyond benchmark performance, the system is designed for practical deployment in environments where connectivity is limited and literacy levels vary—supporting both text queries and image-based hazard input through a mobile-ready prototype. The work contributes a reproducible pipeline, a curated multilingual mining corpus, and an open evaluation framework that can serve as a foundation for extending domain-adapted AI to other African languages and safety-critical industries. Ultimately, Talk MINING demonstrates that closing the language gap in mining safety is not only technically feasible but achievable with relatively modest model size when domain adaptation is done rigorously.

papers.title: Reclaiming human clinical reasoning in generative AI-enabled healthcare: a perspective on cognitive agency, skill evolution, and accountability
papers.authors: Jia Xu, Mengjiao Zhang, Zheng Bing, Wu Deng, Rui Shi
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) are transforming clinical decision support systems (CDSS) from traditional discrete predictions into fluent, context-aware clinical narrative generation. Although these capabilities substantially improve the efficiency of clinical workflows, they also introduce distinctive cognitive challenges: highly fluent and seemingly plausible medical narratives may reshape the way physicians construct clinical meaning and make analytic judgments. This perspective paper introduces the concept of Narrative Cognitive Substitution (NCS), proposed as a testable mid-level theoretical construct, which describes the hypothesized shift in human cognition from active hypothesis generation to passive retrospective validation when GenAI outputs pre-organize diagnostic reasoning and therapeutic pathways. We further propose a Skill Evolution Framework that characterizes the potential effects of GenAI on physician competence across five trajectories: Augmentation, Restructuring, Deskilling, Never-skilling, and Mis-skilling. In addition, we analyze the resulting Accountability Gap: although algorithmic outputs are increasingly embedded in clinical decision-making, decision influence is distributed across clinicians, institutions, developers, and deployers, yet professional accountability and final decision authority remain formally concentrated on the individual physician. To address these systemic challenges, we propose a human-centered governance framework —presented as design hypotheses requiring prospective evaluation— encompassing user interface design (embedding risk-adaptive cognitive friction), medical education (establishing targeted, protected AI-free reasoning exercises (“Reasoning Cleanrooms”)), and institutional policies (implementing substantive human oversight and algorithmovigilance). We argue that the goal of digital health governance should not be to maximize automation, but rather to safeguard human cognitive agency, diagnostic vigilance, and layered, distributed accountability within AI-enabled healthcare systems.

papers.title: Empathetic responses by AI legal assistants and user over-disclosure: evidence from an online survey experiment
papers.authors: 思媛 王
papers.abstract: Introduction Generative AI legal assistants rely on users to describe events, evidence, and transaction histories, yet the same accounts may contain private information that is unnecessary for legal guidance. Empathetic language may affect how selectively users decide what to provide. Methods A one-factor between-subjects online survey experiment on Wenjuanxing randomly assigned 360 participants to rational, mildly empathetic, or highly empathetic AI legal responses (n = 120 per condition). Participants completed 1-5 Likert-type measures of parasocial response, privacy boundary judgment, and over-disclosure intention, together with related relational measures, and then answered an open-ended disclosure task. Results The empathy manipulation was successful, F (2,357) = 524.170, p < 0.001, and η 2 = 0.746. Stronger empathetic responses increased parasocial response (η 2 = 0.428), reduced privacy boundary judgment (η 2 = 0.242), and increased over-disclosure intention (η 2 = 0.406). The coded non-essential disclosure score rose from 0.994 in the rational condition to 6.132 in the highly empathetic condition, F (2,357) = 170.795, p < 0.001, and η 2 = 0.489. Necessary case facts remained stable, F (2,357) = 0.245, p = 0.783. Bootstrap analysis yielded an indirect effect through parasocial response of 0.214, 95% CI [0.151, 0.283], and a sequential indirect effect through parasocial response and privacy boundary judgment of 0.063, 95% CI [0.033, 0.098]. Discussion Within this consumer-dispute scenario, stronger empathetic cues reduced users' selectivity about which information was appropriate to provide. Data-minimization prompts and evidence-oriented questioning may help retain limited emotional support without encouraging unnecessary disclosure.

papers.title: Exploration or exploitation? The double-edged effects of AI use modes on radical creativity: evidence from AI-enabled drug discovery
papers.authors: Hao Wang, Zhi Xu, Zhihong Huang, Huaihong Pan, Guanbin Zheng
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted in corporate innovation activities, yet prior research has not reached a consensus on whether it is more conducive to incremental or radical innovation. For radical innovation, which depends on highly novel ideas, realizing the value of AI depends not only on whether AI is adopted but, more importantly, on whether employees can use it creatively to transcend established knowledge boundaries. Drawing on environmental dynamism and the exploration–exploitation perspective, this study develops a theoretical model linking leaders’ perceptions of environmental dynamism, employees’ AI use modes, leader temporal myopia, and employee radical creativity in the context of AI-enabled drug discovery. We distinguish leaders’ perceptions of environmental dynamism into perceived technological dynamism and perceived market dynamism, and employees’ AI use into exploratory and exploitative AI use. The model is tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling and three-wave matched survey data from 368 leader–employee dyads. The results show that leader-perceived technological dynamism is positively associated with employee exploratory AI use, whereas leader-perceived market dynamism is positively associated with employee exploitative AI use. Exploratory AI use is positively associated with employee radical creativity, whereas exploitative AI use is negatively associated with it. Leader temporal myopia weakens the positive conditional indirect relationship of technological dynamism with radical creativity through exploratory AI use and strengthens the negative conditional indirect relationship of market dynamism with radical creativity through exploitative AI use. By adopting a knowledge-activity perspective, this study reveals the differentiated relationships between AI use modes and radical creativity and further explains how perceptions of the external environment, leaders’ temporal orientation, and employees’ AI use behaviors are differentially related. The findings provide a theoretical basis and practical implications for helping firms engaged in AI-enabled drug discovery guide employees toward effective AI use and enhance radical creativity.

papers.title: When loneliness amplifies the risk of problematic emotional dependence: perceived anthropomorphism and basic psychological need satisfaction in AI companion use
papers.authors: Ting Liu, Ruey-ming Shih, Tingyun LUO, Shining Jin
papers.abstract: Background Companion-oriented conversational AI can be experienced as socially responsive, yet evidence about problematic reliance requires construct clarity and noncausal interpretation. This study examined whether perceived anthropomorphism was associated with problematic AI-companion dependence directly and indirectly through basic psychological need satisfaction. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 666 adults in China who reported using a listed AI companion or conversational AI product during the preceding month. The nonclinical outcome was operationalized with six indicators spanning impaired control, distress, continued use, perceived understanding, emotion-regulation reliance, and displacement of offline communication. Measurement evidence was examined using reliability estimates, one-factor confirmatory models, and HTMT. Standardized composite-score regressions used HC3 robust standard errors, and the indirect association was evaluated with 5,000 bootstrap samples. Results Perceived anthropomorphism was positively associated with need satisfaction ( β = 0.569, p < 0.001). In the outcome model, need satisfaction ( β = 0.317, p < 0.001) and perceived anthropomorphism ( β = 0.385, p < 0.001) were both positively associated with problematic dependence. The standardized indirect association was 0.180 (95% bootstrap CI [0.137, 0.229]); R 2 was 0.323 for need satisfaction and 0.389 for problematic dependence. Conclusion The pattern is consistent with a need-satisfaction account of companion-oriented AI use, but the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering, substitution, or causality. Design and policy implications should therefore focus on transparency, user agency, and safeguards against escalating reliance rather than treating anthropomorphism itself as inherently harmful.

papers.title: Metabolic characteristics and diagnostic biomarkers of malnutrition in maintenance hemodialysis patients based on WGCNA analysis
papers.authors: Bin Shi, Xuyan Wang, Jingya Zhang, Liang Du, Hongyan Luo, Haixin Xu, Jing Xie, Jia Cao, Li Cao
papers.abstract: Objective Malnutrition is a common and serious complication in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients, significantly impacting their prognosis. However, the metabolic characteristics and diagnostic biomarkers of the nutritional status of MHD patients remain inadequately explored. Methods We compared the clinical baseline characteristics between 100 MHD patients and 60 healthy controls. According to the Modified Quantitative Subjective Global Assessment (MQSGA) scores combined with clinical biochemical indicators, the MHD patients were divided into three groups: the well nourished group (Group A), the mild to moderate malnutrition group (Group B), and the severe malnutrition group (Group C). We then analyzed the differences in MQSGA scores and clinical characteristics among these three groups. Untargeted plasma metabolomics profiles were analyzed to identify differential metabolites and dysregulated metabolic pathways. Additionally, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was employed in this study to screen key metabolic modules and potential biomarkers associated with malnutrition in MHD patients. Finally, the sensitivity and specificity of the core metabolites were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and the reliability of candidate metabolite results was validated by colorimetric methods. Results Clinical data results showed that compared with normal population, the MHD patient group exhibited decreased expression of nutritional indicators (BMI, Alb, PA, Hb) and bone metabolism-related indicators (Ca, VitD, Klotho). Furthermore, as the severity of malnutrition increased, the levels of these indicators gradually decreased. Conversely, the levels of Scr, BUN, P, CRP, iPTH, and FGF-23 gradually increased. Metabolomics results identified multiple differential metabolites among the three groups, and KEGG analysis revealed enrichment in steroid biosynthesis and the arginine-proline pathway. In addition, revealed significant alterations in both steroid biosynthesis and arginine-proline metabolism modules, characterized by markedly reduced levels of 25(OH)D 3 , Calcidiol, and Pregnanediol. Conversely, the concentrations of L-glutamate and trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline were significantly elevated ( P < 0.05). Moreover, the results of ROC curve analysis combined with validation tests indicate that the above five metabolites may have good diagnostic performance for MHD patients with malnutrition ( P < 0.05). Conclusion Our findings highlight the metabolic derangements underlying malnutrition in MHD patients and propose novel biomarkers for early diagnosis. These insights may facilitate targeted interventions to improve clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Associations among quality of life, depressive symptoms, body shape concerns, anthropometric characteristics, and diet quality in women with PMOS: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Esra Irmak, Nevin Şanlıer
papers.abstract: Background Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a prevalent endocrine disorder associated with impaired quality of life, body image dissatisfaction, and psychological distress. This study aimed to evaluate the associations between quality of life, depression, body shape concern, and diet quality among women with PMOS. Methods This cross-sectional study was conducted between July and December 2022 at a training and research hospital in Ankara, Türkiye, and included 247 women aged 19–40 years diagnosed with PMOS according to the Rotterdam criteria (2003). Participants were assessed using anthropometric measurements, Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Questionnaire (PCOSQ-50), Body Shape Questionnaire (BSQ-34), Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), Healthy Eating Index (HEI-2010), Carbohydrate Quality Index (CQI), and Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII). Group comparisons, correlation analyses, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed to examine associations among the study variables. Results Participants with minimal depressive symptoms reported significantly higher quality of life scores compared to those with mild or moderate-to-severe depression ( p < 0.001). Higher BMI was associated with greater body shape concern ( p < 0.001), and greater body shape concern was associated with lower PCOSQ-50 scores ( p < 0.001). Significant negative correlations were observed between PCOSQ-50 scores and BSQ-34, BDI, and BMI ( p < 0.05). Conclusion These findings demonstrate significant associations among quality of life, depressive symptoms, body shape concerns, and BMI in women with PMOS and underscore the importance of considering psychosocial and anthropometric factors alongside dietary characteristics in the comprehensive assessment of women with PMOS.

papers.title: Examining sources of variability in repeated testing of the reward positivity and P300 ERP components
papers.authors: Katherine Boere, Mathew Rocha Hammerstrom, Jeff Hopkins, Isaac K. Barss, Rae Dauphinee, Patrick J. Montgomery, Olav E. Krigolson
papers.abstract: Introduction Event-related potentials (ERPs) provide millisecond-resolution measurements of cognitive and affective processes, making them a foundational tool in human neuroscience research. A clear understanding of their reliability, stability, and sensitivity is therefore essential for interpreting experimental results with confidence, particularly in multi-task protocols where several ERPs are measured in sequence. The present study examined three sources of variability for two widely used components, the P300 and the rewards positivity: test-retest reliability, systematic amplitude changes across repeated measurements, and order effects. Methods Twenty-six adults completed five cognitive assessments distributed over approximately 2 h, with each assessment containing a visual oddball task and a two-armed bandit task; task order was independently randomized within each assessment. Reliability was quantified using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), changes across repeated assessments were tested with linear mixed-effects models, and order effects were evaluated using mixed-effects models accounting for repeated observations within participants. Results The P300 demonstrated excellent reliability across all five assessments (ICC = 0.91). The rewards positivity showed a clear divergence between conditional and difference-wave measures: the difference wave was moderately reliable (ICC = 0.52), while the underlying win (0.92) and loss (0.92) waves demonstrated excellent reliability. Rewards positivity amplitude showed no evidence of a linear change across assessments, whereas P300 amplitude increased systematically across the testing period. No evidence of order effects was observed for either component, indicating that task order did not meaningfully influence ERP amplitude within sessions of this length. Discussion Together, these findings characterize the reliability and time-related variability of the P300 and rewards positivity during repeated within-session testing and provide practical guidance for multi-task EEG protocols.

papers.title: Applications of functional ultrasound brain-computer interfaces in neurological diseases: research progress based on neurovascular coupling
papers.authors: Chengshan Zhang
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) bypass peripheral nerves and muscles to establish direct information pathways between the brain and external devices, providing novel approaches for motor function reconstruction, communication assistance, and neurorehabilitation in patients with neurological disorders. However, conventional non-invasive BCIs relying on modalities such as electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), or functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) exhibit limitations in spatiotemporal resolution, portability, or real-time capability. Functional ultrasound (fUS), an emerging neuroimaging technology based on neurovascular coupling (NVC), detects cerebral blood volume changes at a spatial resolution of approximately 100 μm; its imaging frame interval is 200–500 ms, whereas its effective temporal resolution, limited by the hemodynamic response, is 1–2 s, offering a potential solution to overcome these constraints. This review comprehensively analyzed NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces from the dimensions of technical principles, clinical applications, future directions, and challenges. fUS has demonstrated significant clinical value in stroke assessment, epilepsy monitoring, and early identification of neurodegenerative diseases. Emerging technologies such as transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation, sonogenetics, and intravascular ultrasound are driving the evolution of fUS from single-signal “acquisition” toward bidirectional “acquisition-modulation” closed-loop systems, which remain at the proof-of-concept stage. However, the hemodynamic response latency relative to neural electrical activity (1–2 s), the yet-unclear biosafety of chronic ultrasound exposure, and insufficient decoding reliability under pathological conditions remain critical bottlenecks requiring urgent resolution. In conclusion, NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces provide a novel tool for precision diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases. Future efforts should focus on conducting multicenter clinical trials and enhancing the robustness of decoding algorithms.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning–driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review
papers.authors: Thazneem H F, Jisu Elsa Jacob
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approaches in deep learning-driven EEG analysis for the diagnosis of neurological diseases. It includes recent advances in deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), hybrid configurations, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), Large Language Models (LLM), autoencoders, and transformer-based models, with a focus on their capacity to model spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal dynamics in EEG signals. This is applicable in diagnosing major neurological disorders such as Epilepsy, Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Encephalopathy, Parkinson’s disease (PD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), sleep disorders, and developmental brain disorders. Furthermore, we discuss essential preprocessing strategies and denoising techniques, showing how removing biological artifacts prevents diagnostic models from confusing noise with actual signs of disease. Key challenges such as limited data availability, lack of model interpretability, inter-subject variability, and difficulty in clinical translation are identified and critically discussed. Finally, key emerging trends and future research directions are identified to support the development of clinical applications of EEG-based disease diagnostic systems.

papers.title: Leveraging large language models to generate multiple-choice questions for epilepsy education
papers.authors: Chao Li, Chao Li, Weifan Wang, Chenchen Li, Chenchen Li, Xuebin Wang, Xinyan Ma, Weibo Zhao, Yuchen Xie, Weitao Wang, Rubing Lin, Zhaoyin Su, Min Wei
papers.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate medical assessment items, but their reliability for disease-specific question writing remains uncertain. We benchmarked seven LLMs for epilepsy single-best-answer multiple-choice question generation under a standardized blueprint, focusing on structural compliance, clinical accuracy, expert-rated quality and educational usability. Methods Each model completed the same 60 prespecified tasks spanning foundational knowledge, clinical cases, treatment decision-making, and diagnostic evaluation and longitudinal management, yielding 420 questions. Tasks were delivered through an identical single-turn prompt without model-specific optimization, web search or external tools. Objective evaluation assessed structural compliance, keyed-answer accuracy, textual characteristics and response time. Two blinded clinical reviewers independently rated content rigor, clarity, distractor quality, educational usefulness, cognitive alignment and overall usability on five-point scales. Results After one standardized corrective prompt, all 420 questions met structural requirements, although first-pass compliance ranged from 83.33% to 100%. Keyed-answer accuracy varied substantially, from 61.67% to 98.33%, with Claude-5 achieving the highest accuracy. GPT-5.6 obtained the highest composite expert score (median, 3.75), followed by Claude-5 (3.67) and Kimi-K3 (3.50). Distractor quality was a common limitation, with median scores of only 2–3 across models. Only 2 of 420 questions (0.48%) were judged directly usable without revision, both generated by GPT-5.6; 119 (28.33%) were usable after minor revision and 299 (71.19%) required substantial revision. Longer outputs were associated with better cognitive alignment but not with content rigor or clarity, while response time was unrelated to overall usability. Conclusion Contemporary LLMs can reliably reproduce the structure of epilepsy MCQs, but structural compliance and answer accuracy do not ensure educational readiness. Model strengths were multidimensional, and weak distractor construction remained a major barrier to direct use. LLMs may support expert-supervised item drafting, but independent clinical review and subsequent learner-based psychometric validation remain necessary before deployment in medical education.

papers.title: Enhancing pre-service teachers' GenAI literacy and teaching self-efficacy through teacher-guided GenAI use: a quasi-experimental study
papers.authors: Xinying Wang, Changjuan Chen, Shuping Li
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into teacher education, requiring pre-service teachers to develop GenAI literacy and teaching confidence in its pedagogical use. This study examined whether teacher-guided GenAI use was associated with higher posttest GenAI literacy and Teaching Self-efficacy than self-directed use and traditional instruction after accounting for pretest scores. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design involved 102 pre-service teachers at a Chinese teacher education college. Data came from a GenAI literacy test, a Teaching Self-efficacy scale, and semi-structured interviews. ANCOVA showed significant overall effects of instructional condition on both outcomes after controlling for pretest scores (partial η 2 = 0.17 and 0.08) No significant differences emerged between the self-directed and traditional groups. Interviews highlighted prompt design, output evaluation, and teaching-related confidence. By combining a test-based literacy measure with a three-group comparison, this study provides preliminary quantitative evidence relevant to distinguishing structured teacher guidance from GenAI tool access alone.

papers.title: Construction and content validation of an OBE-AI-CED integrated teaching framework for the liquor factory design course in local undergraduate universities: a modified Delphi study
papers.authors: Keliang Wang, Chenglin Zhou, Yueming Leng, Jing Li, Huajie Xu, Xiangui Wang, Ju Guo
papers.abstract: The digital, intelligent and green transformation of the Chinese baijiu industry has introduced new competency demands for liquor engineering education. The Liquor Factory Design course is a comprehensive upper-level engineering design course for students in the liquor engineering program that combines knowledge of brewing technology, chemical engineering, engineering drawing, brewing equipment, energy-saving and environmental protection, and production management. However, the course in local undergraduate universities still has several problems, such as an unclear design task chain, a lack of authentic engineering contexts, ambiguous boundaries for the use of artificial intelligence, and an assessment approach that focuses too much on the final product rather than the learning process. The above problems may limit the all-round development of students’ engineering design abilities. Given the above problems, this paper builds an OBE-AI-CED integrated teaching system for the Liquor Factory Design course by integrating Outcome-Based Education, Artificial Intelligence and Complex Engineering Design. A modified Delphi method was employed to examine the content validity and refine the framework. Two rounds of expert consultations were conducted with university teachers, engineering technicians from Baijiu Enterprise, and experts from an engineering design institution. The first round of results showed that, although most experts agreed that a framework was needed, they raised concerns about the limits of AI application, the viability of sustained cooperation between enterprises and mentors, a lack of genuine engineering resources, and an unfinished chain of evaluation evidence. Based on expert feedback, AI was repositioned as a tool for learning support and design reasoning rather than automatic design generation. A complex engineering design task chain was established, including production scale determination, process flow design, material balance, equipment selection, workshop layout, energy conservation and environmental protection, drawing expression, and design defense. In addition, industrial case libraries, equipment parameter databases, engineering drawing resources, and an evidence-based assessment mechanism were incorporated into the framework. The second-round results showed increased mean scores, reduced coefficients of variation, and greater concordance among participating experts. These results reflect expert consensus on the revised framework, while student learning effectiveness was not evaluated in this study. The proposed framework may support the transformation of the Liquor Factory Design course from a report-oriented model to a competence-oriented model and provide a reference for cultivating complex engineering design competence in liquor engineering programs in local undergraduate universities in China.

papers.title: Technology-enhanced and AI-supported instruction: a meta-analysis of student learning outcomes with implications for writing development
papers.authors: Азиза Жунусбекова, Yessenkeldy Tuyakov, Almagul Ardabayeva, Abay KARATAYEV
papers.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education has introduced new paradigms for teaching, learning, and assessment, especially in the development of students’ writing performance. This meta-analysis examines the effectiveness of blended, technology-enhanced, and AI-supported instructional interventions on student learning outcomes. Eleven studies representing 477 participants across primary, secondary, and higher-education settings were synthesized. The included studies represented heterogeneous educational contexts and assessed outcomes such as academic achievement, literacy, vocabulary and language learning, digital literacy, and motivation. Accordingly, the pooled effect represents an overall effect on student learning outcomes rather than a writing-proficiency-specific effect. Studies were identified through ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar and represented 477 participants across elementary, secondary, and higher-education settings and diverse disciplinary contexts. The results revealed a large and statistically significant pooled effect size [Hedges’ g = 0.89, 95% CI (0.76, 1.10)], showing that students who participated in technology-enhanced instructional interventions outperformed those receiving traditional instruction. Exploratory moderator analyses showed differences according to educational level, intervention duration, and technology type, with primary and secondary students, medium-length interventions (4–8 weeks), and interactive tools showing the strongest effects. The findings show the potential of thoughtfully integrated digital and AI-supported tools to enhance teaching and learning.

papers.title: Possibilities of Applying Artificial Intelligence in Cultural Heritage Preservation
papers.authors: Gabriella Manzenreiter
papers.journal: Central European Library and Information Science Review Közép-európai Könyvtár- és Információtudományi Szemle
papers.abstract: Digital technologies, including the increasingly prevalent artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, offer opportunities in creative and art mediation practices while also raising questions regarding their application. The application of artificial intelligence presents challenges for cultural professionals, particularly in light of the ethical and social issues surrounding AI-generated art. When shaping institutional practices, decision-makers must consider societal processes that influence audience preferences. Alongside the evolution of art mediation methods, digital technologies also play a crucial role in cultural heritage preservation and conservation. In terms of application goals, AI tools enable the reconstruction or reinterpretation of cultural assets more accurately and rapidly than ever before. The aim of my research is to highlight current practices in art projects at both international and national levels, as well as to explore problems that shape artistic and cultural discourses in the context of AI implementation.

papers.title: A Conceptual Analysis of Magnifica Humanitas from Immanuel Kant’s Ethics: AI Among Generation Z
papers.authors: Alice Erni Husein, Elvia Husein
papers.journal: British Journal of Philosophy Sociology and History
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionised numerous facets of human life, particularly for Generation Z, who have been raised in a predominantly digital milieu. Adolescents are progressively impacted by AI (AI) technology in the realms of knowledge construction, decision-making, and learning. Although AI presents several prospects for creativity, education, and productivity, it raises ethical concerns around autonomy, critical thinking, authenticity, responsibility, and human dignity. This conceptual paper examines ethical considerations regarding the employment of AI among Generation Z through Immanuel Kant's philosophical framework. It is recently being enhanced by the viewpoint of Magnifica Humanitas, which underscores the dignity, greatness, and flourishing of the human individual. This article deeply examines Kantian concepts like good will, autonomy, obligation, illumination, the categorical imperative, and the premise of humanity as a goal in itself, which accomplished through a philosophical-conceptual methodology. This study posits that AI is not merely a technological innovation; but rather a social force that impacts human behaviour and cognition. Kantians contend that ethical interaction with AI is not chiefly contingent upon technological progress, instead it hinges on humans' capacity to uphold rational autonomy and moral accountability in their dealings with intelligent systems. The essay contends that educational institutions possess a moral obligation to enhance Generation Z's knowledge of AI by instructing them to utilise AI deliberately and ethically, rather than dissuading their engagement. In additon, Magnifica Humanitas views AI must serve as an instrument for human advancement and should never replace morality, rationality, or human dignity. The research concludes that, in a progressively automated society maintaining humanity's status as the paramount moral being is crucial for the ethical implementation of AI.

papers.title: Neuromarketing under ethical scrutiny: Regulatory gaps, risks of cognitive manipulation, and governance challenges in neuro-assisted decision-making contexts
papers.authors: Edison Rolando Sánchez Pallo
papers.abstract: This study critically examines neuromarketing from ethical, regulatory, and corporate governance perspectives considering the significant increase in the use of neuroscientific techniques in corporate decision-making. The research is grounded in the recognition of a growing informational asymmetry between companies and consumers resulting from access to neurophysiological data capable of influencing cognitive processes, thereby raising concerns related to manipulation, mental privacy, and decision-making autonomy. A narrative critical review of the scientific literature published between 2018 and 2025 was conducted using the following databases: Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect. From the selected documentation, 38 articles were analyzed according to the categories of consumer autonomy, informed consent, potential cognitive manipulation, neuroprivacy vulnerabilities, and ethical governance. The results indicate a significant increase in research since 2020 and a predominance of techniques such as EEG, eye-tracking, fMRI, and GSR. The main ethical risks identified include the erosion of consumer autonomy, limitations of informed consent, potential cognitive manipulation, neuroprivacy vulnerabilities, and the commercial use of neurophysiological data. A clear distinction also emerged between the more critical academic approach and the more instrumental corporate perspective. The findings demonstrate that the ethical risks of neuromarketing are structural and are exacerbated by the absence of specific regulatory frameworks for neuronal data. The reliance on general data protection regulations is insufficient, transferring ethical responsibility to companies and increasing reputational and regulatory risks. The study highlights the urgent need for specific regulatory frameworks, ethical governance strategies, and corporate self-regulation mechanisms. Neuromarketing must be integrated into corporate social responsibility models and public policies that promote autonomy and neuroprivacy, positioning it as a key issue at the intersection of contemporary business ethics.

papers.title: The impact of value co-creation on positive experience and tourist satisfaction: The moderating role of information sharing on social commerce platforms
papers.authors: Nguyen Phuc Khoi Nguyen, Thi Van Hoang, Danh Pham Cong, Nguyen Tran Ngoc Anh, Thien Thanh Huynh
papers.abstract: Tourism has become a pivotal sector for economic development; however, ensuring sustainable competitiveness requires moving beyond traditional strategies and prioritizing customer experience. Value cocreation has increasingly been recognized as a critical factor in shaping customer experiences and satisfaction within the tourism industry. Although the tourism sector is vital for Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam's economy, its services remain inconsistent and lack personalization. While value cocreation offers a strategic solution to these issues, its mechanism within interactive social commerce platforms in the tourism industry remains underexplored. This study investigates the influence of value cocreation on positive experiences and tourist satisfaction among international tourists consuming travel products offered by travel agencies in Ho Chi Minh City. Adopting the DART model as a theoretical framework, the research examines value cocreation in tourism services. A quantitative research design was employed using PLS-SEM to analyse data collected from 316 international tourists (N = 316). The results indicate, among the DART components, only Dialogue significantly impacts Positive experiences and also has the strongest positive effect on Tourist satisfaction. Moreover, Positive experiences significantly enhance Tourist satisfaction. Additionally, the study identifies a significant moderating effect of Information sharing on social commerce platforms on the relationship between value cocreation and tourist satisfaction. Specifically, it strengthens the impacts of dialogue and transparency, while inversely moderating the impact of risk, highlighting the crucial role of digital engagement. These findings contribute to the theoretical discourse by extending the application of the DART model to the tourism context and emphasizing the interplay between cocreation mechanisms and digital platforms. Practically, the study provides actionable recommendations for travel agencies, advocating for enhanced interactive communication, transparency, and the integration of social commerce strategies to improve service quality and meet the evolving demands of international tourists.

papers.title: The Impact of Maternal Preconception Health on Long-Term Child Health and Developmental Outcomes: A Scoping Review
papers.authors: Catherine Stewart, Katie L. Harron, Jennifer Hall
papers.abstract: The preconception period is a critical window during which maternal health and behaviours can influence pregnancy and offspring outcomes. However, preconception care remains limited, and existing research has largely focused on short-term pregnancy or neonatal outcomes. This scoping review aimed to synthesise evidence on the associations between maternal preconception health and long-term health, developmental, and educational outcomes in children.Primary studies were eligible if they examined the independent effect of maternal preconception health on child health and developmental outcomes assessed after age 1 year and up to 18 years. Five databases (MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science) were searched. Data were extracted using a standardised form and summarised descriptively. Studies were mapped by type of preconception exposure and child outcome.From 9,539 records identified, 186 studies met the inclusion criteria. Preconception BMI was the most frequently studied exposure (n=130) while neuro/cognitive development (n=83) was the most common outcome. Higher preconception BMI was consistently associated with adverse long-term outcomes, including higher offspring BMI and poorer cognitive, behavioural, and developmental outcomes. Pre-existing maternal physical and mental health conditions were also linked to poorer child health and developmental outcomes. Evidence for preconception smoking, alcohol, and substance use was limited but suggested potential harms, while diet quality and supplementation were generally associated with beneficial outcomes.These findings highlight the preconception period as a key opportunity for intervention to support positive outcomes for children and underscore the need for higher-quality, long-term research to inform policy and practice.

papers.title: Unresolved snack desire and subsequent snacking in daily life
papers.authors: Giuseppe Marrazzo, Trung Dung Tran, Leonardo Pimpini
papers.abstract: Snacking on calorie-dense foods is often assumed to follow from craving, yet in daily life craving and snacking are only loosely coupled. In an exploratory secondary analysis of a preregistered 21-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA) study of 136 young women with healthy-range BMI (3, 6, or 9 prompts/day), we examined whether snack desire reported without snacking was associated with consumption in the subsequent reporting interval. Because these EMA items referred to the period since the previous prompt, desire and snacking reported within the same window could not be temporally ordered. Across 8,492 eligible adjacent-window pairs, snack desire without snacking was associated with higher odds of snacking in the subsequent interval (within-person OR = 1.71, 95% CI [1.48, 1.97]). Participant-balanced model-standardized probabilities were 42.1% following desire-present intervals and 30.7% following desire-absent intervals, an adjusted difference of 11.4 percentage points (95% CI [8.2, 14.6]). The association remained positive in participant-day fixed-effects analyses (+12.66 percentage points, 95% CI [9.13, 16.20]) and exceeded expectations from a constrained surrogate distribution (observed unadjusted difference = 16.44 versus surrogate mean = 9.59 percentage points; empirical p = .0002). A complementary exploratory matched comparison showed that desire was modestly more frequent before snack than matched non-snack windows (+4.47 percentage points, uncorrected p = .019). Additional matched comparisons of the intervals surrounding snacking showed pronounced elevations in desire and low perceived control during snack-reporting windows, whereas stress showed a smaller difference. These findings identify snack desire reported without consumption as a prospective correlate of subsequent snacking, without establishing causality. More generally, they demonstrate why it is important to distinguish events reported in successive EMA intervals from events reported within the same interval.

papers.title: Making AI-mediated decisions culturally repairable
papers.authors: Hadi Mohamadpour, Soomaayeh Heysieattalab, Jean-Claude Dreher
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly influences high-stakes decisions, from employment and education to healthcare and public services. When such judgments are disputed, affected people may receive an explanation without being able to reach an authority empowered to change the outcome or remedy its consequences. We introduce cultural repairability: the institutional capacity to review an AI-mediated decision, correct the outcome and downstream records, provide meaningful restoration, and learn from failure through procedures people can understand and use. The framework addresses a visibility–accountability asymmetry: people are exposed to judgments about their standing but lack effective means of obtaining an answer or remedy. Culture matters because exposure, legitimate authority, and appropriate restoration may be understood differently across settings. Language accessibility also determines whether review mechanisms are usable in practice. We identify three measurable cultural mechanisms: the meaning of exposure, the credibility of review, and the meaning of restoration. We further distinguish affected people’s appraisals from institutional actors’ responsibility and capacity to respond. Four falsifiable propositions specify how reviewer authority and audience shape responses to repair, and how these effects vary with cultural orientation, institutional history, and the form of restoration. They predict whether people appeal or withdraw, how they recalibrate trust, and whether they remain willing to engage. The resulting Repairability Principle establishes a common floor of substantive review, correction, restoration, and prevention of recurrence, while allowing people to choose how restoration is delivered. Cultural repairability therefore shifts global AI accountability from whether procedures appear acceptable to whether institutions can correct harm in practice.

papers.title: Human Capital in AI-Enabled Digital Transformation: A Systematic Review of Workforce Competencies and HRM Mechanisms
papers.authors: Marat Idrissov, Sebastian Lang, Thomas Stahlecker, Gulmira Mukhanova, Botagoz Kuanyshbayeva, Ágnes Csiszárik-Kocsír
papers.abstract: This article presents a systematic literature review of the role of human capital in digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on how these developments reshape workforce competencies and human resource management (HRM) during the transition from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0. Following the PRISMA guidelines, the study combines thematic coding with comparative analysis. From an initial pool of 216 publications, 46 studies were selected for in-depth analysis. The review examines how AI and digitalisation change workforce skill requirements and how HRM mechanisms can help organisations develop and sustain the necessary competencies. The findings indicate a shift from routine and manual tasks toward hybrid competency profiles that integrate data analytics skills, AI literacy, human–machine interaction skills, and higher-order socio-cognitive capabilities, including adaptive reasoning, collaboration, and ethical judgement. HRM emerges as a strategic integrator that supports continuous reskilling, predictive skills-gap analysis, and the development of effective human–AI teams. Based on these findings, the study proposes a multilevel framework explaining how institutional mechanisms, organisational strategy, HRM practices, and human–AI complementarity jointly shape workforce competitiveness in AI-enabled digital transformation. The framework contributes to human-centric digitalisation by linking workforce competitiveness to capability velocity and human–AI complementarity. It also provides managerial implications for designing learning, governance, and decision-making structures that enable organisations to respond to evolving competency requirements and translate technological potential into sustainable operational advantages.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence literacy in social research: A bibliometric analysis of conceptual evolution and emerging trends
papers.authors: Eluard Alexander Mendoza-Zenozain, Franklin Córdova-Buiza
papers.abstract: In contemporary digital society, artificial intelligence literacy (AI literacy) has become a key competence that enables citizens to understand and actively participate in increasingly automated environments. However, despite the rapid growth of scientific output, partly driven by tools such as ChatGPT, the literature reveals substantial conceptual fragmentation that hinders an integrated understanding of its educational and ethical dimensions. In this context, this study aimed to analyze the intellectual evolution and conceptual structure of research on AI literacy, based on Scopus-indexed literature. A bibliometric methodology was applied to a corpus of 2,645 documents using scientific mapping techniques to identify publication patterns, collaboration networks, and dominant thematic streams. The results reveal an accelerated expansion of the field and a shift from early approaches focused primarily on educational contexts such as K-12 education and computational thinking toward more complex frameworks that incorporate algorithmic ethics, psychological acceptance of technology, critical thinking, and academic integrity challenges associated with generative AI (GenAI). Overall, this study contributes to the educational technology literature by providing a longitudinal bibliometric interpretation of the evolution of AI literacy and by identifying emerging research agendas related to GenAI, ethical reasoning, and critical digital competencies in contemporary education.

papers.title: Adoption of Artificial Intelligence Among Teachers in Indonesia: Testing the UTAUT Model and Institutional Support
papers.authors: Anneliese Valerie Ong, Anissa Lestari Kadiyono, Aulia Iskandarsyah
papers.abstract: This study aims to explain the factors influencing the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) among teachers in Indonesia using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) model and institutional support. A quantitative non-experimental approach with an explanatory descriptive design to elucidate the role of factors in AI adoption among teachers. The UTAUT (Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology) model is a theoretical framework for predicting and understanding users' acceptance and use of new technology (Venkatesh et al., 2003). A total of 214 teachers in Indonesia who have used AI in teaching activities participated in this study through convenience sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM). The results show that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and institutional support play a role in the behavioral intention to use AI. Additionally, facilitating conditions and behavioral intention play roles in AI adoption. Conversely, social influence does not affect behavioural intention. These findings indicate that teachers’ use of AI is influenced more by perceived usefulness, ease of use, institutional support, and individual intention to use AI than by social influences from their surrounding environment. Overall, the research findings emphasize the importance of providing institutional support, training, and adequate resources to optimally enhance AI adoption among Indonesian teachers. Adopsi kecerdasan buatan (AI) dalam pendidikan berkembang pesat dan mendukung pembelajaran yang personal, adaptif, serta efisien bagi guru. Namun, kesiapan digital guru di Indonesia masih rendah, dengan hanya sekitar 45% guru memenuhi standar kompetensi digital. Penelitian terdahulu berbasis Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) di Indonesia juga masih terbatas pada karakteristik guru tertentu dan belum menguji konstruk inti secara utuh. Penelitian ini bertujuan menjelaskan faktor-faktor adopsi AI pada guru di Indonesia menggunakan model UTAUT serta dukungan institusional. Pendekatan kuantitatif non-eksperimental dengan rancangan deskriptif eksplanatori digunakan pada 214 guru yang telah menggunakan AI dalam mengajar, dipilih melalui convenience sampling. Data dianalisis menggunakan Structural Equation Modelling (SEM). Hasil menunjukkan bahwa performance expectancy, effort expectancy, dan institutional support berperan terhadap behavioral intention to use AI, sedangkan facilitating conditions dan behavioral intention berperan terhadap adopsi AI. Sebaliknya, social influence tidak berpengaruh terhadap behavioral intention. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa persepsi manfaat, kemudahan penggunaan, dukungan institusional, dan niat individu lebih berperan dibandingkan pengaruh sosial. Dengan demikian, penyediaan dukungan institusional, pelatihan, dan sumber daya yang memadai penting untuk meningkatkan adopsi AI guru di Indonesia.

papers.title: Media neophraseologisms as a marker of transformational and innovative processes in the Russian phraseological system
papers.authors: M. A. Davydova, N. N. Rogoznaya
papers.abstract: This article is devoted to a comprehensive study of media neophraseologisms as relevant markers of transformation processes in the modern Russian phraseological system. Using extensive empirical data from the Russian-language online press and Telegram channels for 2020–2026, the article identifies key derivational trends in neophraseology: structural diffuseness, pragmemization, and sententialization of signs. We demonstrate a semantic shift in neoidioms toward de-abstraction and connection to the current agenda and substantiate the adaptive nature of phraseological innovations in the context of an increasingly complex information picture of the world. Particular attention is paid to the anthropocentric aspect of linguistic creativity: The generation of neophraseologisms, mediated by the mechanisms of irony, allusion, and manipulation, is verified as a demarcation line between the natural human text generation and the algorithms of generative artificial intelligence. We propose a typology of neophraseologisms, including discursive-precedent, intermedia, and calqued units, including their axiological and ludic functions in media texts. The article notes that the diffuseness of structure and pragmemization act as mechanisms of linguistic economy, while the de-abstraction of signs reflects the connection between phraseology and extralinguistic factors. The results are significant for lexicographic practice, university teaching, and media stylistics. The developed typology and the identified derivational processes can serve as a basis for monitoring the Russian phraseological system evolution. The results of the study are applicable in lexicographic practice, teaching, and media stylistics.

papers.title: Trust in AI-based Educational Technologies as a Predictor of Generative AI Acceptance in Science Teacher Education: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study
papers.authors: Canan Dilek Eren, Aynur Kolburan Geçer
papers.abstract: As the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)–based educational technologies into teaching and learning processes accelerates, trust has emerged as a key determinant of whether preservice teachers are willing to adopt these technologies. The present study aimed to examine the relationship between the perceived trust of pre-service science teachers in AI-based educational technologies and generative AI acceptance and to determine the predictive power of trust on acceptance. Grounded in the TAM, the study employed a cross-sectional correlational survey design to investigate the role of trust in acceptance processes. Data were collected from 270 pre-service science teachers enrolled in a science teacher education program at a university via an online questionnaire. The Trust in AI-Based Educational Technologies Scale (TAI-EdTech Trust) and the Generative AI Acceptance Scale (GAIA) were used for data collection. The findings revealed a moderate, positive, and statistically significant relationship between trust in AI-based educational technologies and GA acceptance, indicating that trust significantly predicted GA acceptance. The results highlight the importance of developing content in science teacher education programs that supports the safe, ethical, and pedagogically responsible use of generative AI tools.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE–BASED PREDICTION OF MORTALITY AND MORBIDITY IN PERFORATION PERITONITIS: A COMPARATIVE STUDY WITH MANNHEIM PERITONITIS INDEX (MPI) AND JABALPUR PROGNOSTIC INDEX (JPI)
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Perforation peritonitis is a common surgical emergency in developing countries with high postoperative morbidity and mortality.Early identification of high-risk patients is crucial for improving outcomes and optimizing resource utilization.Although conventional scoring systems such as the Mannheim Peritonitis Index (MPI) and Jabalpur Prognostic Index (JPI) are widely used for risk stratification, their predictive accuracy may be limited.Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models can integrate multiple clinical variables, offering the potential for more accurate outcome prediction.Aim: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of an AI-based model for predicting morbidity and mortality in perforation peritonitis and compare it with the MPI and JPI.Materials and Methods: An observational comparative study was conducted in the Department of General Surgery of a tertiary care teaching hospital over 18 months.Adult patients with perforation peritonitis undergoing emergency laparotomy were included.Demographic, clinical, laboratory, operative, and postoperative data were prospectively collected.MPI and JPI scores were calculated, and an AI-based predictive model was developed using routinely available perioperative variables.Model performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, diagnostic accuracy, and the area under the ROC curve Results: A total of 150 patients were included in the study.Postoperative morbidity occurred in 51 (34%) patients, while 22 (14.7%)patients died during hospitalization.The AI-based predictive model demonstrated superior performance compared with the Mannheim Peritonitis Index and Jabalpur Prognostic Index, achieving a sensitivity of 95.5%, specificity of 89.8%, positive predictive value of 60%, negative predictive value of 99.1%, diagnostic accuracy of 90.7%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.94 for predicting postoperative mortality.Conclusion: Artificial intelligence-based predictive modelling provides more accurate risk stratification than conventional prognostic scoring systems in patients with perforation peritonitis.Integration of AI-assisted decision

papers.title: Deep Multimodal Fusion of Thermal and Visible Images for Emotion Interpretation
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Emotion recognition plays a crucial role in affective computing and human-computer interaction, enabling intelligent systems to understand and respond to human emotional states.Conventional emotion recognition approaches primarily rely on visible-light facial images; however, their performance is significantly affected by variations in illumination, occlusion, and low-light conditions.Thermal imaging offers a complementary modality by capturing physiological changes such as blood flow and temperature variations associated with emotional responses, and it remains robust under challenging environmental conditions.This study explores emotion interpretation using fused thermal and visible facial images through deep learning techniques.A multimodal framework employing dual-stream convolutional neural networks is discussed, where modality-specific features are extracted independently and fused at the feature level to enhance discriminative capability.Various fusion strategies, including early, mid-level, and late fusion, are analyzed to highlight their effectiveness in improving recognition accuracy.The integration of thermal and visible modalities demonstrates improved robustness, particularly for subtle and negative emotions.The findings emphasize that multimodal deep learning-based fusion provides a reliable and scalable solution for emotion interpretation, with promising applications in healthcare, automotive safety, surveillance, and human-robot interaction.

papers.title: THE LAW’S QUIET BLIND SPOT IN INDIA: THE SURVEILLANCE OF THOUGHT AND THE CASE FOR A NEW PRIVACY RIGHT
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The fast growth of surveillance technology has drastically changed India's balance amongst individual liberty and political authority.Inconceivable amounts of data collection and behaviors analysis have been made possible by the combination of electronic tracking systems, AI (artificial intelligence), and sophisticated analysis of data.Although the legal framework created following the Apex Court's landmark decision in Honorable K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India recognized privacy or as essential rights (Fundamental right) within Article 21, it is still mostly restricted to the instructive and corporeal dimensions of confidentiality 1 .This study explores the idea of the "monitoring of thinking," which refers to electronically facilitated methods that use data trends and electronic (digital) behavioral assessment to infer, anticipate, and possibly affect humans thinking.Intellectual observation works by creating mental profiling and prediction models that disclose opinions, choices, and desires, in contrast with conventional observation, which concentrates on tracking activities or telecommunications .2Substantial constitutional issues are raised by such activities, especially in relation to liberty of expressing itself, psychological independence, and decency.The danger is increased by the potential for cognitive regulation and computational tampering which could stifle independent thinking and participatory engagement.The article makes the case that supreme law (Constitutional law) has a "silent blind zone" because it does not identify and control incursions into the intellectual realm.Judicial and parliamentary advances have not specifically tackled intellectual freedom or mental confidentiality, notwithstanding Puttaswamy expansive concept of confidentiality.This study shows that current statutory safeguards are inadequate to adequately safeguard people from the growing risks of mental monitoring via conceptual study and involvement with modern technical circumstances.3 As reaction, the article argues that Art.21 of Constitution should recognize a fresh basic entitlement (Right) to mental confidentiality or intellectual autonomy.In order to prevent advances in technology from undermining the fundamental principles of liberty, integrity, and democratization, it closes by highlighting the necessity of focused parliamentary improvements, judiciary creativity, and strong organizational safeguarding.
keywords: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India

papers.title: Emerging Nephrology Nursing: Current & Future roles
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Nephrology nursing has evolved significantly over the past decades, transitioning from task-oriented care to a comprehensive, patient-centered specialty that integrates clinical expertise, advanced technology, and chronic disease management.This review explores the emerging roles of nephrology nurses in the current healthcare landscape and envisions future directions shaped by technological advancements, healthcare reforms, and evolving patient needs.Current roles encompass not only hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis care but also kidney transplantation, conservative kidney management, patient education, and multidisciplinary collaboration.The increasing prevalence of chronic kidney disease and the complexity of renal replacement therapies demand advanced competencies, including leadership, research, and quality improvement.Future roles are anticipated to expand into telehealth, remote patient monitoring, artificial intelligence-assisted care, genomics-informed nursing, and community-based kidney health promotion.The integration of advanced practice nursing and nurseled clinics is expected to further strengthen chronic disease management and reduce hospital readmissions.This review highlights the need for continuous professional development, specialized training programs, and policy support to equip nephrology nurses for these evolving responsibilities.Emerging nephrology nursing roles are critical to addressing the global burden of kidney disease and enhancing the quality, accessibility, and sustainability of kidney care delivery.

papers.title: Transformational leadership as a central element in rural education: Synergies between endogenous development and government policies
papers.authors: Yolanda González Castro, Omaira Manzano Durán, Marta Milena Peñaranda
papers.journal: Journal of Infrastructure Policy and Development
papers.abstract: Rural education in Latin America is marked by historical inequalities in terms of access, quality, and retention, which are exacerbated by population dispersion, infrastructure deficits, teacher attrition, and curricula disconnected from local realities. Despite state efforts across the region to implement policies aimed at reducing these gaps, their impact remains uneven due to limitations in the territorial adaptation of top-down guidelines. In this context, educational leadership emerges as a critical factor in coordinating efforts. In particular, transformational and pedagogical approaches act as catalysts for innovation, promoting strategic synergies between the endogenous development of communities and governmental frameworks. Evidence suggests that these leadership styles optimize school management, elevate teacher self-efficacy, and consolidate communities of practice that strengthen institutional outcomes. Furthermore, the study identifies distinctive characteristics within peasant and ethnic contexts, demanding flexible and culturally relevant models. Thus, transformational leadership aligns with the principles of equity and social justice, shaping the school as a node for territorial development. It is concluded that the sustainable strengthening of rural education in Latin America depends on leadership capable of harmonizing macro-policies, micro-practices, and meso-territorial realities, thereby driving inclusion and systemic co-creation.

papers.title: PENGARUH PENGGUNAAN CHATGPT TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR KOGNITIF MAHASISWA PROGRAM STUDI PAI IAIH PANCOR PADA MATA KULIAH METODOLOGI PENELITIAN
papers.authors: Siti Humaero', Siti Rauhillah
papers.abstract: The use of ChatGPT among university students is growing rapidly, yet empirical evidence on its effect on cognitive learning outcomes in courses that demand higher-order thinking, such as Research Methodology, remains limited in Islamic higher education. This study aimed to determine the effect of ChatGPT use on the cognitive learning outcomes of Islamic Religious Education (PAI) students at Institut Agama Islam Hamzanwadi Pancor in the Research Methodology course. A quantitative approach with an ex post facto design was used. The population was 487 students in the sixth and eighth semesters; the sample of 83 students was determined using the Slovin formula and proportionate stratified random sampling. ChatGPT use was measured with a four-point Likert questionnaire (20 valid items), while cognitive learning outcomes were taken from final course grades through documentation. Data were analyzed with simple linear regression in SPSS after the normality, linearity, and heteroscedasticity assumptions were met. The results show a regression equation of Y = 64.465 + 0.278X, with a t value of 17.778 (greater than the t table value of 1.990; Sig. 0.000) and an R² of 0.796. ChatGPT use therefore had a positive and significant effect on cognitive learning outcomes, accounting for 79.6% of their variance. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the ex post facto design, the narrow range of grades, and the measurement of usage intensity rather than usage quality.

papers.title: PEMANFAATAN KECERDASAN BUATAN DALAM PEMBELAJARAN DI SEKOLAH DASAR: PELUANG DAN TANTANGAN BAGI GURU DI KABUPATEN BUNGOThis study aims to identify opportunities and challenges of AI utilization by elementary teachers in Bungo Regency, Jambi Province, and to
papers.authors: Sarmiati, Baili Kurniawan, Sugeng Kurniawan, Rugaiyah, Muhammad Sayuti
papers.abstract: This study aims to identify opportunities and challenges of AI utilization by elementary teachers in Bungo Regency, Jambi Province, and to map adaptation strategies developed within resource-constrained contexts. Employing a qualitative phenomenological approach, the research involved 15 purposively selected teachers with varied age, teaching experience, and school locations. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and pedagogical document analysis, then analyzed thematically using Braun & Clarke’s framework assisted by NVivo 14. Findings reveal four main opportunities: (1) personalized learning pathways, (2) administrative efficiency and formative assessment, (3) interactive multimodal material development, and (4) expanded access to learning references. Conversely, structural and pedagogical challenges emerged, including digital infrastructure gaps, TPACK competency variation, ethical concerns regarding data privacy and technological dependency, and lack of continuous mentoring. Grounded in TPACK and UTAUT theoretical frameworks, the findings explain how perceived usefulness, ease of use, and institutional support shape AI adoption. The study recommends practice-based training enhancement, hybrid infrastructure provision, and responsive school policies for technological innovation. This research contributes to elementary education literature in non-metropolitan regions and offers a contextual, ethical, and sustainable AI implementation framework.

papers.title: GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MATHEMATICS EDUCATION: POSSIBILITIES, CHALLENGES AND PEDAGOGICAL IMPLICATIONS
papers.authors: Rawlinson dos Santos Silva, José Gomes Taveira Neto, Wendys Mendes da Silva, Karen Lowhany Costa da Silva
papers.abstract: The expansion of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) has broadened the possibilities for using digital technologies in Mathematics education, while also creating challenges related to learning, assessment, teacher training, and the ethical use of these tools. This study aims to analyze the main possibilities and challenges associated with the use of GAI in Mathematics education, based on an integrative review of the literature published between 2022 and 2026. The research is characterized as bibliographic, with a qualitative approach, and uses studies identified through a search environment integrated with scientific sources from Elsevier. NotebookLM was employed as an auxiliary tool for organizing and synthesizing the material, while the interpretation and categorization of the studies remained the responsibility of the researchers. The results indicate potential benefits related to the production of explanations, personalization of interactions, development and adaptation of activities, comparison of strategies, and support for pedagogical planning. On the other hand, the findings highlight risks such as incorrect responses, superficial learning, reduced cognitive effort, technological dependence, assessment difficulties, academic integrity issues, privacy concerns, and the need for teacher training. It is concluded that the contribution of GAI depends less on the technology itself than on its intended purpose, pedagogical mediation, and the critical engagement of students.

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Linking Medicaid and Education Records in New York City
papers.authors: Katharine C. Sadowski, Andy Martens, Kira Argenio, Sophia Day, Kevin Konty, Michael Gaile, Maria Fitzpatrick
papers.journal: International Journal for Population Data Science
papers.abstract: Linking education and health records can offer critical insights into how policies and interventions shape children’s outcomes, yet these data linkage efforts are often constrained by inconsistent identifiers, incomplete population overlap, and variable data quality. We develop a supervised machine learning framework to link New York City Department of Education (DOE) and Medicaid records, one of the first large-scale linkages of its kind in the United States. Our two-step approach first deduplicates records within each dataset and then applies a random forest model to identify cross-dataset matches, integrating blocking, probabilistic scoring, and clustering to improve upon deterministic and off-the-shelf probabilistic linkage techniques while maintaining computational efficiency. Applying this framework, we achieve a high quality linkage, identifying matches for approximately 71% of records across the two systems. Match rates are consistent across birth cohorts and most demographic groups, though lower for some populations because the two systems capture partially overlapping subsets of children. Rather than optimising for a 100% match rate, we propose a framework for evaluating linkage quality under uncertainty, emphasising precision, transparency, and population representativeness. This approach provides scalable guidance for linking complex administrative systems and enables new opportunities to study how educational and health policies interact.
keywords: New York City Department of Education

papers.title: Human Adaptation Readiness Framework for Electrical Engineering Innovation Deployment: Conference presentation and accompanying transcript
papers.authors: Olena Ronzhes
papers.abstract: This conference presentation introduces Human Adaptation Readiness (HAR) as a psychophysiologically grounded human-centred readiness dimension for electrical engineering innovation deployment. HAR complements Technology Readiness Level (TRL) and Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL) by addressing the capacity of users to maintain attention, adaptive self-regulation, perceived agency, and decision stability under novel digital interaction conditions. The empirical basis includes a broader multi-stage study with 479 participants and an EEG-based experimental subsample of 50 participants. Latent profile analysis identified four adaptation profiles: Adaptive Novices, Balanced Adapters, Pressure-Vulnerable Users, and Adaptive Leaders. Particular attention is given to the stress-amplifying combination of interface novelty and time pressure and to the implications of HAR for onboarding, phased rollout, interface simplification, collaborative testing, and scaling in Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0 environments.

papers.title: Development of an AI-assisted maritime poetry writing book using tourism posters for junior high school students
papers.authors: Gatot Sarmidi, Riswanda Himawan, Fanny Farhanto Purwacaraka Candrajati, Alvian Guntur Prasetya Aziz, Rita Setiawati, Mohammad Naim Bahar
papers.abstract: Background- Poetry writing is an important productive literacy skill in the Merdeka Curriculum, yet instruction remains predominantly theoretical. Students may experience difficulties in idea generation, diction, and imagination due to limited contextual and visual support. Objectives- This study aimed to (1) identify instructional needs; (2) develop an AI-assisted maritime poetry writing book integrating illustrated data cards and marine tourism posters; and (3) evaluate its effectiveness. Methods- This Research and Development (R&D) study using the ADDIE model. The study involved experts, a teacher, and eighth-grade students in experimental and control groups. Data were collected through observations, interviews, questionnaires, documentation, and pretest-posttest tasks. The data were analyzed using qualitative and quantitative descriptive techniques. Results- The needs analysis indicated a strong need for step-by-step guidance and contextual visual stimuli in poetry-writing instruction. Expert validation indicated high feasibility (material: 87%; media: 80%). Teacher and student practicality ratings reached 92% and 94%, respectively. Mean scores increased from 5.086 to 8.434, with significant differences between groups (p < 0.001) and a moderate effect (d = 0.54). Diction richness (78.80%) and figurative language (74.10%) achieved the highest indicator scores. Conclusions- The developed book demonstrated high feasibility and practicality and was associated with improved poetry-writing performance among students.

papers.title: Digital Mediation and Cultural Value Co-creation in Place-Based Intangible Cultural Heritage: Dongguan Guanxiang
papers.authors: Zheng Boyi, Ke Zhao
papers.journal: Advances in Social Science and Culture
papers.abstract: The rapid development of digital media has transformed how regional cultural heritage is represented, circulated, interpreted, and experienced. For place-based intangible cultural heritage, digitalization creates new opportunities for cultural communication and public participation, while also generating challenges concerning authenticity, contextual integrity, cultural authority, and commercialization. This article develops a conceptual framework for understanding these dynamics through the case-informed context of Dongguan Guanxiang, a regional cultural tradition associated with agarwood, craftsmanship, locality, and sensory experience. Rather than treating digitalization simply as a technical means of heritage preservation or cultural promotion, the article conceptualizes it as a process of cultural mediation through which heritage meanings are selected, translated, reconstructed, and negotiated among different stakeholders. Drawing on literature on intangible cultural heritage, cultural meaning, digital mediation, and value co-creation, the article proposes four interconnected dimensions: cultural interpretation, digital mediation, stakeholder participation, and value realization.
