It separates contingent tacitness, which a new query brings out (AlphaGo's game tree), from regime-bound tacitness, statable only once it is gone (AlphaGo's hunches). (1) Polanyi's from-to structure reads as non-commutative binding. (2) Explicating the valuation destroys it, as with Polanyi's pianist, yet a closed-form law states it. Polanyi, Nonaka, Tsoukas and Collins each capture part of this, narrowly; even Nonaka and von Krogh's continuum cannot tell the classes apart. (3) Collins's three tacit knowledges become strata, one outside the substrate. (4) Our mentor-student DAG is a tacit-transmission graph. (5) Tao's remark that AI-solved problems spawn few follow-ups reveals rootless explicit knowledge: checkable results no one can trace or yet understands. To re-root them, LLMs generate, VaCoAl/PyVaCoAl keeps an auditable trace with its confidence, and people value, a role virtue epistemology shows cannot be offloaded. Art, craft and skill show the same decoupling of form from the maker's becoming. (6) On Mercier and Sperber's account an LLM is reason's arguing side set loose, a sophist; truth-seeking lies deeper, in Polanyi's conviviality, which we conjecture is the root of evolvability and, as the Buddhist idea that plants and lands attain buddhahood suggests, reaches beyond humans. Testable predictions follow.

papers.title: ScholarSync – Cloud-Based Scholarship Management and Monitoring System
papers.authors: Aditi Ishwar Chaudhari Ritika Lekhram Kapgate, Deepika Thakare Iqra Shaik
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: Managing scholarships within educational institutions typically requires gathering student details, confirming eligibility, receiving documents, validating applications, following application progress, and notifying students of outcomes. The literature examined here points to a transition away from manual, scattered procedures and toward unified web-based scholarship platforms. Prior work has looked at scholarship search and application portals, consolidated scholarship information, multi-tier workflows, decision-support techniques, notifications, analytics, and security. This review analyzes these approaches and pinpoints a practical gap: a student-level, institution-focused system that brings the essential scholarship lifecycle together in one easily accessible digital setting. ScholarSync is put forward as a cloud-based web application for managing and monitoring scholarships, concentrating on integrating institutional workflows instead of adopting complex artificial-intelligence or blockchain infrastructure.

papers.title: Dentists’ Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence in Dental Practice
papers.authors: Anshuman Swami, Astha Chauhan, Bhuvnesh Airen, Ranjan Mani Tripathi, Chirag Vyas, Surbhi Gendar
papers.abstract: Background: Dentists’ readiness to use artificial intelligence (AI) remains an important concern in dental practice.Aim: This study explored attitudes, perceived barriers, and willingness to use AI.Materials and Methods: A survey of 220 dentists was analysed using descriptive statistics and Pearson’s chi-square tests.Results: Willingness was 70.0%, while 75.0% reported privacy concerns and 90.0% reported a demand for training.Conclusion: This analysis provides a framework for studying responsible AI adoption and testing educational needs in future empirical research.

papers.title: Regime-Gated Tail Transfer: Reliable Cross-Industry Machine Learning for Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall
papers.authors: Rakshay Pawar
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Finance and Banking
papers.abstract: Pooling financial series gives machine-learning tail models more extreme observations, but it can also transfer the wrong tail dynamics across assets and regimes. Regime-gated tail transfer (RGTT) combines Student-t GARCH, filtered historical simulation, industry-specific quantile boosting, and pooled cross-industry quantile boosting. FZ0-scored weights depend on nine lagged volatility–breadth states, with shrinkage toward global performance. A coverage controller (RGTT-C) uses past exceedances and preserves ES ≤ VaR. Hyperparameters are selected on 1995–1999 and frozen before a 2000–July 2026 test across ten U.S. industry portfolios (66,840 industry-days). RGTT significantly improves on equal weighting and a state-agnostic gate. RGTT-C attains mean FZ0 −3.4887 and a 2.491% breach rate at the 2.5% target, with significant loss advantages over filtered historical simulation and both quantile-ML experts. Its advantage over Student-t GARCH is not significant at 5% (two-sided p = 0.072). The pooled expert’s mean weight falls from 22.5% to 13.5% between low-volatility/low-breadth and high-volatility/high-breadth states. The framework makes cross-industry transfer state dependent while separating expert weighting from an order-preserving coverage controller. JEL classification numbers: C22, C45, C53, G17, G32. Keywords: Expected shortfall, Value-at-risk, Forecast combination, Quantile machine learning; negative transfer, Regime adaptation, Market risk.

papers.title: Human–AI Task Redistribution in Higher Education
papers.authors: Viktor Wang
papers.journal: International Journal of AI in Pedagogy Innovation and Learning Futures
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is redistributing academic work among humans, AI, and human–AI collaboration, raising questions about which tasks learners should continue performing independently. This mixed-methods study examined task allocation using survey data from 317 university students representing 974 recurring academic tasks and interviews with 24 faculty members across 24 disciplines. Student data showed substantial movement from human-only performance toward joint human–AI and AI-delegated work. Task redistribution was significantly associated with perceived skill demands and learning opportunities. Faculty strongly supported preserving independent practice for foundational, embodied, and high-stakes activities while permitting AI for appropriate peripheral, advanced, and efficiency-oriented tasks. Integrating both datasets produced a Human–AI Task Allocation Model organized around a Training Zone–Performance Zone principle. The findings suggest that appropriate AI delegation should depend on learners’ developmental stage, task purpose, and retained capacity for verification, judgment, and accountability.

papers.title: Text Mining and Machine Learning for New-MediaPublic-Opinion Spillovers in Manufacturing Supply-Chain Digital Collaboration
papers.authors: Chengyan Li
papers.journal: ICST Transactions on Scalable Information Systems
papers.abstract: Online media coverage may transmit information across supply-chain relationships, yet converting such signals into evidence requires a clear separation between text measurement, network alignment, and statistical inference. This study examines whether focal-firm media attention is associated with connected partners’ annual-report digital disclosure and develops a manufacturing-oriented workflow for directed supply-chain analysis. We construct a firm–partner–year panel for Chinese non-financial A-share firms from 2007 to 2024 by combining aggregated CFND media indicators, annual-report digital-term frequencies, CNRDS supplier–customer links, and CSMAR controls. Fixed-effects models estimate conditional associations on directed edges. The baseline specification shows a positive association between focal-firm coverage and partner digital disclosure (β = 0.048, SE = 0.020), while alternative aggregate coverage measures yield coefficients with the same sign; mechanism and subgroup results remain observational and descriptive. These findings do not establish causality or realized interfirm digital collaboration because annual-report word frequency is an imperfect disclosure proxy. A Chinese- BERT–MLP event-and-tone module is therefore retained only as a future extension pending article-level text, human- reviewed labels, and out-of-sample evaluation.

papers.title: KTUfy: Smart Academic Assistance for KTU Students
papers.authors: Jasmin K. N., Mohammed Thanzeel M. T., Mohammed Nasif A. K., Shadan P. K., Najla Musthafa, Mohammed Shamil K, Femina B.
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.abstract: KTU students often face difficulties in organizing their studies, finding syllabus-based materials, and preparing effectively for examinations. Most existing learning platforms provide general content that does not fully match the KTU cur-riculum. To address this problem, this project presents KTUfy, a smart academic assistant designed specifically for KTU students. KTUfy provides an intelligent chatbot that answers student queries based on the official syllabus and study materials. The system also includes features such as automatic quiz generation, a coding practice module, and a question paper pattern analysis system to help students identify important topics for exams. In addition, academic management tools such as a study calendar, reminders, and SGPA/CGPA calculator are included to support better planning and time management. The system is developed using React for the frontend and Python with Fast API for backend services. Natural Language Processing techniques and retrieval-based models are used to improve the accuracy of answers. The main aim of KTUfy is to improve learning efficiency, exam preparation, and overall academic support for KTU students through a single integrated platform.

papers.title: AI-Powered Automated Assignment Generation and Intelligent Evaluation System Using Natural Language Processing and OpenAI API for Enhanced Learning and Fair Assessment
papers.authors: Sankaran Ramesh Kumar, M. A. Afsheen Sultana, M. D. Bilal Ahmed, Yedida Navya Sri Lakshmi Indu, Sangramjeet Ghosh
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.abstract: The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into higher education has precipitated a dual crisis: the exponential increase in faculty workload regarding assessment scalability and the destabilization of traditional academic integrity verification methods. This paper introduces the proposed system, an automated academic evaluation platform designed to address these challenges through a unified, immutable assessment pipeline. Unlike traditional Learning Management Systems (LMS) that function primarily as repositories, the proposed system employs Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate the entire grading lifecycle, from submission to feedback generation, while simultaneously performing rigorous authorship verification. The system enforces a single-submission policy to streamline administrative workflows and generates immutable, audit-ready reports containing scoring rationale and AIgenerated content likelihood. The system architecture, scoring methodology, and a multi-layered integrity detection approach based on stylometry and machine learning classifiers are described. Simulated performance results suggest that the proposed system mitigates the subjective variability of human grading while offering a scalable solution to the integrity challenges posed by unrestricted GenAI access.

papers.title: The Influence of AI-Based Content Personalization on Brand Loyalty on E-Commerce Platforms: A Study on Generation Z in Indonesia
papers.authors: Sugito Sugito, Aryani Sairun
papers.journal: Journal of Accounting and Finance Management
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in e-commerce has made personalized content a central strategy for fostering consumer-brand relationships. However, understanding how such personalization shapes brand loyalty among digitally native Generation Z consumers in emerging markets remains limited. This study qualitatively explores the perceptions of Indonesian Gen Z regarding AI-driven content personalization on e-commerce platforms and how these perceptions influence brand loyalty. In-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted with 25 Gen Z e-commerce users aged 18–26 in Indonesia. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings reveal five core themes: perceived utilitarian convenience, emotional value and relational signaling, privacy intrusion and the “creepiness” factor, conditional brand loyalty, and the moderating role of digital literacy. Personalization that delivers relevant and timely recommendations strengthens both attitudinal and behavioral loyalty by enhancing shopping efficiency and making consumers feel valued. Conversely, overly intrusive personalization triggers privacy concerns, distrust, and potential defection. The study contributes a nuanced, context-rich understanding of the personalization–loyalty dynamic, highlighting the privacy calculus that Gen Z performs. It offers managerial implications for e-commerce platforms in balancing personalization with transparency to sustain loyalty in the Indonesian market.

papers.title: Digital Health in Nursing: Opportunities, Challenges and the Road Ahead An Integrative Review
papers.authors: Vasudevan Nattamai Jothilal, Amal Al-Alawi, A beer Al Maamari, Laila Al Hasani
papers.abstract: Digital Transformation is bringing challenges to health systems in healthcare in all over the world where nurses makes a majority of the workforce in health systems and play an essential role in the sweep out process. Gradually but definitely technologies like electronic health records, artificial intelligence for the clinical decision making, telemedicine, remote sensors and robotic assistance plays a significant role and a game changing process in which patient care is given and evaluated. In spite of pandemic makes the digitalisation has driven forward the health sector little is known about its effects on nursing research today. This integrative review was undertaken to synthesis the various evidence on digital transformation in nursing examining the opportunities its presents the challenges its poses and its impact on nursing roles and the directions its signal for future practices. Authors performed an integrative review to fill this gap also it brings attention to study the data on digital information on nursing which mainly focuses on opportunities, challenges, impact the roles and practice and future innovative directions. Researches from January 2014 to December 2023 were searched intensely through various databases such as CINAHL, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science. The review is mainly focused on problem identification, literature search, quality assessment, dataanalysis and thematic synthesis. From 78 studies, five main themes emerged: The expanding role digital technologies in nursing, which brings new opportunities at both practice and system levels ongoing structural and ethical barriers evolving the nursing key roles and identity and future priorities for direction for education, policy and practice. Evidence also states the digital tools improve care coordination, patient safety, clinical decision making and work force improvement. Though there are few nurses who are digitally illiterate, similarly another challenge is unequal access part for workflow interruptions. Ethical consideration is also another challenges such as data privacy, algorithm bias accountability and others. Moreover, the review also understands adjustments in variation of nursing practice where advancedroles and informatics develop alongside concerns about maintaining the personal human side of the care. Overall, digital transformation is a complex and evolving force in nursing that promises significant innovation and growth but requires careful attention to ethical, educational and systemic issues. Successful integration depends on equitable technology access and establishing strong governance that preserves both clinical quality and the core human values of nursing.

papers.title: IMPROVING THE ORGANIZATIONAL FRAMEWORK OF ACCOUNTING AND ANALYTICAL SUPPORT IN THE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OF FORESTRY ENTERPRISES
papers.authors: Lyudmyla Drymanova, Lidiіa Fedoryshynа
papers.journal: EСONOMY FINANСES MANAGEMENT Topical issues of science and practical activity
papers.abstract: The article examines the theoretical, methodological, and practical aspects of improving the organizational framework of accounting and analytical support in the management system of forestry enterprises under the conditions of digital transformation and sustainable development. It is substantiated that current challenges facing the forestry sector require the integration of financial, management, statistical, and environmental accounting into a unified information environment capable of generating reliable, relevant, and timely information for managerial decision-making. The study identifies the main causes of inconsistencies between accounting, management, and statistical reporting data, including inconsistencies in regulatory and methodological support, the use of heterogeneous software systems, differences in product classification, time discrepancies in data processing, and continuous legislative changes. The paper proposes the adaptation of the National Accounting Standard (NAS) 30 Biological Assets to the specific features of forestry activities through the clarification of terminology, improvement of biological asset and finished product valuation approaches, expansion of disclosure requirements in financial reporting, and refinement of forestry product classification. A theoretical and methodological framework for accounting representation of finished forestry products is developed, encompassing product classification, improved analytical accounting, enhanced documentation procedures, and the integration of economic, environmental, and social dimensions of forestry activities. Particular attention is devoted to the implementation of modern digital technologies, including ERP systems, electronic timber accounting, geographic information systems (GIS), Business Intelligence tools, artificial intelligence, and cloud technologies as key instruments for increasing transparency, efficiency, and responsiveness of management processes. The proposed recommendations contribute to improving the quality of accounting and analytical support, harmonizing national accounting practices with international standards, strengthening the reliability of financial reporting, and enhancing the competitiveness and sustainable development of forestry enterprises in the context of digital transformation.

papers.title: FEATURES OF USING THE MATERIALS CREATED BY GENERATIVE MODELS FOR ADVERTISING IN UKRAINE AND WORLDWIDE
papers.authors: Lyudmila Pronko, Дмитро Змієвець
papers.journal: EСONOMY FINANСES MANAGEMENT Topical issues of science and practical activity
papers.abstract: The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the use of generative artificial intelligence (hereinafter – AI) in the creation of visual advertising content and its impact on contemporary marketing practices in Ukraine and abroad. It is demonstrated that the integration of AI-generated photo and video materials transforms not only the set of advertising tools but also the very logic of organizing the advertising process, reshaping the balance between creative, managerial, and technological components. Generative models form a new type of creative environment in which content production becomes fast, flexible, and data-driven, allowing for scalability without a proportional increase in the costs. The study systematizes the key areas of application of generative AI in advertising, including the personalization of visual messages, production optimization, the development of dynamic formats, and the use of data-driven storytelling. At the same time, it is identified that technological advantages are accompanied by a number of risks related to the standardization of creative solutions, dependence on the quality of input data and on external technological infrastructure, the weakening of brand distinctiveness, and an increased likelihood of ethical and legal violations. It is argued that in the absence of adequate managerial control, generative content may lose strategic alignment with brand positioning and the long-term objectives of the enterprise. Special attention is paid to the Ukrainian context, which is characterized by the combination of rapid adoption of AI solutions with human resource, institutional, and regulatory constraints intensified by wartime conditions. It is shown that under these circumstances generative artificial intelligence performs a dual role: on the one hand, it acts as a tool for improving the effectiveness of marketing communications; on the other hand, it requires clearly defined frameworks for responsible use. The article concludes that generative AI should be viewed as a driver of structural change in the advertising industry, the effectiveness of which depends on its integration into marketing management systems, the quality of managerial decision-making, compliance with ethical principles and legal requirements, and the ability of brands to maintain their distinct character.

papers.title: USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DESIGNING ROBOTIC MODELS USING ENGINEERING GRAPHICS
papers.authors: Olena Solona, Олена Джеджула
papers.abstract: The article examines the possibilities of using generative artificial intelligence in teaching the discipline “Engineering and Computer Graphics” in the design of robotic models for the processing industry. The feasibility of integrating generative artificial intelligence models into the design process of robotic systems as a means of developing spatial thinking, graphic competence, design skills, and digital skills of agricultural university students is substantiated. It is established that modern generative systems (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, Claude, DALL·E, etc.) support all stages of educational design, from developing technical specifications and generating product concepts to creating drawings and three-dimensional models, visualizing designs, preparing technical documentation, and analyzing possible design solutions. A methodology for using generative artificial intelligence in the educational project “Design of a Robotic Manipulator” is proposed. The methodology is based on the principles of project-based learning, STEM education, the competency-based approach, and the use of CAD systems. A structural model for integrating generative artificial intelligence into the process of graphic training has been developed. It includes the stages of problem formulation, concept generation, sketch creation, three-dimensional modeling, preparation of design documentation, and expert evaluation of the finished product. It is demonstrated that the use of generative AI contributes to increasing students’ motivation, developing engineering thinking, fostering digital literacy, and reducing the time required for routine operations in the design of robotic models.

papers.title: Asesmen Pembelajaran SD Melalui Artificial Intelligence Berbantuan Zep Quiz Berbasis Adventure Game-Based Learning
papers.authors: Imam Rofiki, Puguh Darmawan, Susiswo, Barep Yohanes, Syekha Vivi Alaiya, Mutiara Sani, Sri Wahyuni
papers.journal: TEKIBA Jurnal Teknologi dan Pengabdian Masyarakat
papers.abstract: Teachers’ limited capacity to develop engaging and adaptive digital assessments, coupled with the underutilization of artificial intelligence (AI), provided the basis for this community service program. The program aimed to improve teachers’ understanding and digital literacy in developing AI-assisted learning assessments using Zep Quiz within an adventure game-based learning approach. It was implemented at SDN 5 Mojolangu with teachers from the elementary school and Islamic elementary school teachers’ working group (KKG) in Lowokwaru District. The program comprised five stages: socialization, training, technology implementation, mentoring and evaluation, and sustainability planning. Its outcomes were evaluated using attendance records, questionnaires measuring understanding, perceived improvement in digital literacy, and program meaningfulness, as well as the products submitted by participants. The program involved 20 teachers, exceeding the initial target of 15 participants. The evaluation results showed a mean understanding score of 3.85 on a four-point scale, categorized as very high; a mean perceived digital literacy improvement score of 3.80, categorized as a substantial improvement; and a mean program meaningfulness score of 4.00, categorized as highly meaningful. All participants successfully developed and submitted 20 Zep Quiz products. These findings indicate that practice-oriented training and mentoring can help teachers integrate pedagogical considerations with technological skills in assessment development. Program sustainability will be supported through classroom trials, peer reviews within the KKG forum, and periodic evaluations to promote the independent and continuous use of digital assessment.

papers.title: Modeling Student-Centered Feedback Mechanisms: ChatGPT-Supported Feedback in the Feedback Orientation Scale for Secondary Chinese Reading
papers.authors: Sze Yik Chu
papers.abstract: This study addresses the underexplored role of ChatGPT-supported feedback within secondary Chinese reading contexts in mainland China, characterized by constrained persistent teacher-centered instruction, limited AI-related research and access to transnational AI systems. Conceptualizing the Feedback Orientation Scale (FOS) as a student-centered model, the study examines how ChatGPT-supported and conventional human-generated feedback differentially influence underlying processes and overall learning gains. Psychometric evaluation preceded a quasi-experimental pre–post design (N = 200) employing multi-group SEM and ANOVA to examine model fit, structural pathways, and developmental changes. Results indicate substantial between-group differences, with ChatGPT-supported feedback producing greater gains in feedback, feedback orientation, and reading outcomes, demonstrating excellent model fit and a feedback orientation mediation-dominant structure. In contrast, except for good effect size gains in reading outcomes, two feedback-related variables show significant decline and negative effect size in conventional feedback group, with weaker FOS model fit and fragmented pathways. These findings highlight how, within the student-centered FOS framework, ChatGPT-supported feedback more effectively contributes to overall learning gains and demonstrates its capacity to integrate feedback, feedback orientation, and reading outcomes into a unified student-centered learning mechanism for instructional practice in secondary Chinese reading instruction.

papers.title: AI Fluency Under Delegation: A Consequence-Based Framework and a Proposed Performance Assessment for Agentic Work
papers.authors: Agelo Thalassinidis
papers.abstract: Frameworks for AI fluency have matured quickly. The most widely adopted, the 4D Framework of Dakan and Feller (2025), defines fluency as working with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically, and safely through four competencies (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence), and it explicitly includes agentic use. What existing frameworks do not supply is a decision rule for how much autonomy a given task should be granted, for a given person, at a given point in that person's development. We argue that this rule is the core of fluency once AI systems act across multi-step workflows. We propose that AI fluency under delegation is calibrated allocation: matching AI autonomy to the consequence of error and to the developmental value of the task to the person performing it. The resulting two-axis model yields four regimes (automate, struggle first, delegate with tripwires, and human-retained) and implies that the appropriate regime for a task is person-specific and shifts as expertise develops. We operationalize the model through four dimensions (Bounding, Allocating, Auditing, and Withholding), map them systematically against the 4D Framework, and derive four testable propositions. We then propose the Calibrated Delegation Assessment, a performance-based instrument that combines a situational judgment test with an Attempt-Check-Reconcile task, and specify its item blueprint, scoring model, and a staged validation plan. We close with implications for curriculum, assessment, and institutional AI policy.

papers.title: The AI-Native University - The ANU 1+4 Principles for Human Formation in the Age of AI
papers.authors: Le Truong Tung
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) makes it increasingly possible to produce sophisticated intellectual outputs without undertaking the experiences that develop corresponding human capabilities. This weakens a practical assumption of traditional university teaching and assessment: that producing an academic output normally entails formative intellectual work. Existing responses, including personalized learning, process-based assessment, and oral defense, are valuable but difficult to institutionalize at scale. This conceptual paper proposes the AI-Native University (ANU) 1+4 Principles: a Foundational Principle of redesign rather than AI augmentation, and four Design Principles — Human Formation for Human Mastery, Experience-Designed University, Capability-Verified University, and Human–AI Intellectual Partnership. Its contribution is an integrated account of institutional purpose, formative mechanism, evidence of capability, and the conditions of intellectual work in an AI-rich world.

papers.title: This is How We AI: A Practical Approach to Teaching with Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: George Hanshaw, Craig Brewer, Shannon Hunt
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is often treated in higher education as a technology to adopt, restrict, or police. This practice guide argues that AI is primarily a shift in teaching practice, comparable to the move to online instruction. Effective use depends less on the tool than on how faculty position it pedagogically. Drawing on institutional experience and empirical studies of AI course assistants at Los Angeles Pacific University, the authors offer a practice-oriented framework for teaching with AI. The guide presents a typology of common AI roles in courses (answer machine, editor, practice partner, tutor, and thought partner) and examines the benefits, risks, and design implications of each. It describes how the instructor's role shifts from content delivery toward learning design, and how teaching presence can be maintained through modeling AI use and through "visibility without surveillance," using process-based assignments and guided transparency instead of detection. Practical resources include scalable assignment design patterns, low-effort redesign moves, a pre-publication assignment checklist, and a before-and-after assignment example. The guide also considers which students benefit most from AI support and where faculty expertise remains essential. It addresses ethical and practical guardrails, including academic integrity, overreliance, hallucinations, and equity of access. The authors conclude that teaching with AI is fundamentally a design decision: AI does not fix weak pedagogy but can amplify strong pedagogy, while judgment, relationship, and disciplinary expertise remain human work.

papers.title: Constructing Meaning, Not Just Charts: A Cognitive–Instructional Framework for Generative AI Usage in Visualisation Education
papers.authors: Syaamantak Das
papers.abstract: Infographics and data visualisations have become the primary mode for organising, teaching, and assessing complex information, and a substantial body of work establishes why they support learning. Generative AI now allows learners to produce sophisticated visualisations from natural-language prompts, removing technical barriers but introducing a pedagogical tension: when an AI system performs the analytic and encoding work, learners can obtain competent outputs without engaging the reasoning that makes visual artefacts educational. We argue that this is not only a question of instructional efficiency but of learner agency, of whether the human remains the author of meaning, and therefore a question of dignity in the teaching-learning process. Synthesising two systematic reviews, one spanning information design and the learning sciences and one covering Generative AI in visualisation education, we develop a unified conceptual framework. The second review yields a classification of AI visualisation systems by pedagogical orientation, in which systems that engage learners in reasoning are supported by stronger evidence of learning outcomes than those that deliver finished artefacts. The framework reconceptualises infographics and data visualisations as cognitive–instructional systems whose educational value resides in their construction, across an interlinked process of thinking, learning, and communication, and crosses this process with a set of learner-centred design layers. An agency principle organises the framework, distinguishing tools that scaffold the learner's cognitive work from those that substitute for it, operationalised through transparency, invitation, and the progressive fading of support. We close with design implications and a research agenda foregrounding the needs of linguistically diverse and under-resourced learners, and the measurement of transferable visualisation literacy.

papers.title: Проблема оценки человеческого вклада в эпоху генеративного искусственного интеллекта
papers.authors: О.А. Елина
papers.abstract: Технологии генеративного искусственного интеллекта (далее — ИИ) демонстрируют устойчивую тенденцию проникновения во все сферы человеческой деятельности от материального производства и сферы услуг до креативных индустрий, системы государственного и корпоративного управления, образования. Это требует переосмысления и существенной трансформации устоявшихся профессиональных практик и привычных алгоритмов решения прикладных задач, изменения коммуникативных паттернов и образовательных методик. Интенсивное внедрение генеративных нейросетей в профессиональные и повседневные практики приобретает характер системной экспансии, знаменующей сдвиг от автоматизации рутинных операций к алгоритмизации творческих, образовательных и управленческих процессов. Возможность применения ИИ в области профессиональных отношений и образовательной среде разрушает базовое допущение о том, что готовый продукт является надежным сигналом стоящей за ним человеческой компетентности и трудового усилия. В статье анализируются изменения, происходящие в межличностных коммуникациях и ролевых структурах в сфере образования и профессиональной занятости. Обосновывается тезис о том, что в связи с глобальным внедрением ИИ наблюдается кризис подходов и методов оценивания в высшем образовании (в отношениях «преподаватель — обучаемый») и кризис измерения и вознаграждения труда в профессиональной среде (в отношениях «руководитель — подчиненный»). Автор показывает эти кризисы как две проекции одной проблемы — разрыва связи между наблюдаемым результатом и ненаблюдаемым человеческим вкладом. Проблема описывается в терминах экономики информации (сигнализирование, асимметрия информации, отношения «принципал — агент») и теории неявного знания. Автором предлагается симметричное решение для обоих контуров: перенос оценки с артефакта на процесс и на личность, признание умелого использования ИИ (включая обоснованное воздержание от него) самостоятельной оцениваемой и вознаграждаемой компетенцией и верификация посредством выборочного контроля и защиты работы, а не автоматических детекторов. Для сферы образования систематизированы подходы к определению форм оценочных средств и типов заданий; в рамках трудовых отношений — практики выдачи заданий, проверки и построения системы вознаграждения. Обсуждаются риски: надзорный дрейф, справедливость доступа, искажение стимулов и обесценивание навыков. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) technologies show a steady tendency to penetrate all spheres of human activity — from manufacturing and services to the creative industries, public and corporate governance, and education. This calls for a rethinking and a substantial transformation of established professional practices and habitual algorithms for solving applied tasks, and for changes in communicative patterns and educational methods. The intensive adoption of generative neural networks in professional and everyday practice is taking on the character of a systemic expansion that marks a shift from the automation of routine operations to the algorithmisation of creative, educational and managerial processes. The applicability of AI in professional relations and in the educational environment destroys the basic assumption that a finished product is a reliable signal of the human competence and effort behind it. The article analyses the changes occurring in interpersonal communication and role structures in education and professional employment. It substantiates the thesis that a significant crisis of assessment approaches and methods is emerging in higher education (in the teacher–student relationship) alongside a crisis of measuring and remunerating labour in the professional environment (in the manager–subordinate relationship). The author presents these crises as two projections of a single problem — the decoupling of the observable result from the unobservable human contribution. The problem is described in terms of the economics of information (signalling, information asymmetry, the principal–agent relationship) and the theory of tacit knowledge. A symmetric solution is proposed for both domains: shifting assessment from the artefact to the process and the person; recognising the skilful use of AI (including justified abstention from it) as a distinct, assessable and rewardable competence; and verification through sampling and the defence of one’s work rather than automated detectors. For education, forms of assessment instruments and task types are systematised; for labour relations, practices of task assignment, verification and compensation design. The risks are discussed: surveillance drift, equity of access, distortion of incentives, and deskilling.

papers.title: Digital transformation of agency: how artificial intelligence is changing the Russian student body
papers.authors: О. В. Безрукова
papers.abstract: The article analyzes the challenges of digital transformation in education and the issue of agency among Russian students, while also examining the figures involved in the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) from a historical perspective. It offers reflections on the role, potential, and "side effects" associated with integrating AI into educational processes, including upbringing.

papers.title: AI-Empowered Governance of University Data: Value Dimensions, Risk Challenges and Governance Responses
papers.authors: Jianfang Gao, Chunlin Li
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study is to explore a sustainable paradigm for data governance in universities empowered by artificial intelligence (AI), creating a collaborative governance system that integrates technological, institutional, organizational, and ethical dimensions to combine intelligence, resilience, and humanistic care. This study adopts an inductive–deductive qualitative content analysis to propose an integrative “Value–Risk–Pathway” analytical framework. The study first identifies the sustainable benefits of AI in university data governance. These benefits include enhanced data integration, improved decision support, and increased governance effectiveness. It then examines the potential risks associated with employing AI. These risks include foundational, normative, structural, and ethical aspects. The study proposes a theoretical transmission pathway through which these risks may influence and amplify each other within the context of universities. To address these risks, a collaborative governance system is proposed. This system integrates technological governance, institutional adjustments, organizational collaboration, and ethical regulations. This research contributes to existing knowledge in several ways: (1) It moves beyond the existing focus on technical efficiency or isolated risks, presenting an integrated analytical perspective that balances value and risk as co-constitutive phenomena. (2) It reveals the dynamic transmission and reinforcement mechanisms among multidimensional risks. (3) The proposed “Four-in-One” collaborative governance system offers a sustainable governance paradigm for data management in higher education in the digital age. Additionally, at the practical level, the “Four-in-One” collaborative governance system provides a theoretical basis for university administrators to develop AI application policies that align with the essence of education. It also offers targeted guidance for addressing risks at different levels, facilitating effective proactive governance.

papers.title: AI Tools, Especially Chatbots and Disabled People: Views of Critical Disability Studies Students
papers.authors: Gregor Wolbring, Manel Djebrouni, Svetlana N. Yanushkevich
papers.abstract: AI tools, including chatbots, have become increasingly mainstream and could pose many problems for disabled people and their allies. Such problems could include the lack of accessibility of AI tools for disabled people, including disabled activists and disabled people as digital citizens. Chatbot outputs also may be inaccurate or of low quality due to biased or insufficient training data and might reflect biased and low literacy about the lived reality of disabled people amongst the people involved in setting up the training. Therefore, problems could also include a potential decrease in the public’s literacy about the lived realities of disabled people when AI tools such as chatbots are used without critically analyzing their outputs or using inappropriate prompts for inquiry. Critical disability studies students see themselves as allies of disabled people and want to make a positive difference in their lives. AI tools, including chatbots, are an emerging area that allies of disabled people have to think about because of their increasing impact on the lived reality of disabled people. Using an online survey hosted on a Qualtrics platform, we examined the perspectives of 89 critical disability studies students on the usability and impact of AI tools, including chatbots, on disabled people in areas including the following: accessibility; what knowledge is available and what and whose knowledge is reflected in the output of AI tools and chatbots; the impact of AI tools and chatbots’ output on the literacy of the users about the lived reality of disabled people; and the impact on ability judgment problems disabled people experience, such as ableism and disablism. We performed a thematic analysis of two open-ended questions and frequency (%) analysis of the other questions. Our 89 participants outlined many problems. One set of problems covered accessibility barriers and design-process shortcomings of AI tools, including chatbots. Another set was linked to content-related issues, such as chatbots not reflecting the lived realities of disabled people, the use of biased language and portrayals of disabled people, and the limited usefulness of chatbot-provided information. These issues are not only problematic for disabled people but also for their allies. Participants gave many suggestions regarding the practical impacts of not having data on the lived reality of disabled people, as well as how chatbots could be used, or what has to happen, for them to challenge ableist power structures rather than reinforcing it. All our findings suggest the need for various actions whereby AI ethics, “responsible AI”, and “AI for good” principles could be used to decrease the problems noted, as could be the concepts of AI justice and of ability judgment justice and other ability judgment-linked concepts.

papers.title: When AI Agrees with Me: Disclosure Labels, Confirmation Bias, and the Sharing of AI-Generated Misinformation Among Jordanian Young Adults
papers.authors: Alaa Makki Abdulhadi Akkof
papers.abstract: This study examines whether AI disclosure labels alter the evaluation and sharing of misinformation when messages align with recipients’ prior beliefs. A randomized mixed-factorial online experiment involved 900 Jordanian young adults who evaluated eight Arabic-language social-media posts each (7200 post-level observations). The disclosure condition (no label, “AI-generated,” or “AI-generated: This information has not been independently verified”) varied between participants; veracity and belief congruence varied within participants. Crossed mixed-effects models showed that a generic AI label modestly reduced message credibility but did not significantly reduce sharing intention, whereas the explicit verification warning reduced both outcomes relative to the generic label. Belief-congruent misinformation received higher credibility and sharing ratings, with a stronger credibility advantage for false than true posts. Message credibility partially mediated the congruence–sharing association. Actively open-minded thinking weakened congruence effects and improved true–false credibility discernment. The findings extend the Heuristic-Systematic Model by showing that disclosure wording, motivated processing, and individual thinking dispositions shape distinct stages of misinformation response. They support labels that communicate the verification status and media-literacy interventions that help users distinguish agreement from accuracy. The baseline-adjusted sensitivity analysis did not support the attitude-reinforcement interaction (b = −0.030, p = 0.628).

papers.title: Do AI and Lexicon-Based ESG Scores Converge? Evidence from IPO Prospectuses in an Emerging Market
papers.authors: Manpriya Singh, Navjit Singh, Vikas Sharma, Ramona Rupeika-Apoga
papers.journal: Journal of risk and financial management
papers.abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG) scoring from corporate disclosures raises questions about alignment with conventional lexicon-based scores. Such alignment can be problematic as a lexicon-based approach quantifies the textual density using an ESG dictionary, while LLM-based scores are able to assess the thematic coverage of ESG themes. It remains unclear whether the two approaches produce comparable or distinct results when applied to the same corporate information. This paper examines the construct alignment between LLM-generated and lexicon-based ESG scores using 625 Indian IPO prospectuses issued between 2018 and 2024. A rebalanced dictionary of 630 terms measures disclosure intensity, while contextual scores are obtained by prompting a generative AI model. Both sets of scores are harmonised into quantile categories and compared using confusion matrices, correlation analysis, and chance-corrected agreement. The methods converge for the environmental dimension (EMR = 46.1%; weighted κ = 0.56) but diverge for social (28.2%) and governance (23.0%) disclosure, with only limited alignment overall (31.7%). The findings suggest the two approaches operationalise ESG differently, with implications for construct validity and transparency in ESG analytics.

papers.title: When AI Is—and Is Not—Needed: AI Literacy and Computational Thinking in Primary STEM
papers.authors: Ahmet Akif ERBAŞ, Tolga Topçubaşı
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly present in children’s lives, yet exposure does not necessarily lead to an accurate understanding of how AI works. This study examined whether a LEGO-based integrated STEM intervention could improve third-grade students’ AI literacy and computational thinking, particularly their ability to distinguish machine learning from rule-based automation and reason about training data, model error, and technology choice. An embedded mixed-methods, quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design was conducted with 93 students from four intact classrooms. The experimental group (n = 46) completed eight weeks of authentic design problems, while the control group (n = 47) continued regular Life Studies instruction. After controlling for pretest scores, the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in AI literacy, F(1, 90) = 152.51, p < .001, partial η2 = 0.629, and computational thinking, F(1, 90) = 22.18, p < .001, partial η2 = 0.198. Qualitative evidence showed a shift from viewing AI through robots and automatic actions toward reasoning about learning from examples, data diversity, limitations, human oversight, accessibility, and problem–technology fit. Integrated STEM instruction can foster critical AI literacy by making AI mechanisms visible and inviting students to judge whether AI is needed at all.

papers.title: Digital Health and Artificial Intelligence Continuing Professional Development Needs Among Rehabilitation Professionals in Jordan: A National Mixed-Methods Study
papers.authors: Fadi Almasalha, Mohammad Z. Darabseh, Musab Abu Beidar, Bodor H. Bin Sheeha, Shruoq Faruoq Husain Jebreel, Arar Al Tawil, Sami Elmahgoub, Wesam Aldebes, Mohamed I. Mabrouk, Badrieh Al Abbad, Aseel Aburub
papers.abstract: Background: Digital health and artificial intelligence (AI) are rapidly transforming rehabilitation practice, creating an urgent need for rehabilitation professionals to develop new competencies through continuing professional development (CPD). Despite the growing importance of digital rehabilitation, evidence regarding digital health and AI-related CPD needs among rehabilitation professionals in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. This study aimed to identify the digital health and AI-related CPD needs of rehabilitation professionals in Jordan. Methods: A national convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conducted between January and May 2026. Licensed physiotherapists, occupational therapists, speech-language therapists, and prosthetists/orthotists completed a structured online questionnaire assessing CPD participation, digital health competencies, AI-related knowledge, perceived barriers, and future educational priorities. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with a purposive sample of rehabilitation professionals and key stakeholders to further explore experiences and educational needs. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data underwent reflexive thematic analysis. Findings from both components were integrated during interpretation. Results: A total of 462 rehabilitation professionals completed the survey, and 20 participated in qualitative interviews. Artificial intelligence (mean = 4.71 ± 0.52), telerehabilitation (4.64 ± 0.61), clinical decision support systems (4.59 ± 0.65), and virtual reality rehabilitation (4.55 ± 0.69) emerged as the highest-priority CPD topics. Among the 462 participants, 169 (36.6%) reported previous participation in digital-health-related CPD, while 82 (17.7%) reported receiving formal education in artificial intelligence. The principal barriers to CPD participation were lack of time (84.4%), financial cost (79.2%), limited AI-focused educational opportunities (76.8%), and inadequate employer support (63.0%). Previous digital health training, years of professional experience, and employer support independently predicted higher self-reported digital health competency (adjusted R2 = 0.39; p < 0.05). Qualitative findings demonstrated that rehabilitation professionals recognized digital transformation as inevitable but reported insufficient practical training, organisational support, and nationally coordinated educational opportunities. Conclusions: Jordanian rehabilitation professionals demonstrated high motivation to develop competencies in digital health and AI but reported substantial educational and organisational barriers. National competency frameworks, structured CPD programmes, and integration of digital health into rehabilitation curricula are needed to prepare the rehabilitation workforce for technology-enabled healthcare. The findings may inform workforce development strategies in Jordan and other low- and middle-income countries undergoing digital transformation.

papers.title: Generative AI and Intercultural Competence in Higher Education: A Scoping Review (2022–2026)
papers.authors: Jing Li, Jinghe Han, Johanna Einfalt
papers.abstract: The increasing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has prompted growing interest in its potential in intercultural competence (IC) education. Yet research on how GenAI can support IC development remains fragmented across language education, pragmatics, pedagogy, and professional communication. This scoping review mapped research contexts, designs, theoretical foundations, and findings on GenAI-mediated IC education. Eligible English-language publications published or posted between November 2022 and 11 August 2026 examined GenAI in relation to IC or related pragmatic and socio-pragmatic constructs of IC in higher education. Searches of ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar identified 26 eligible publications, including 20 empirical studies and 6 non-empirical publications. Data were charted using a structured form and synthesised descriptively and thematically. The included empirical studies reported varied perceived and task-specific outcomes for intercultural and pragmatic learning, mainly in structured and guided activities. Three issues warrant particular attention. First, the included publications drew on heterogeneous theoretical frameworks that addressed different or partial dimensions of IC. Second, several publications positioned teacher mediation as important for GenAI-supported learning, yet teacher preparedness, including their AI literacy and capacity to undertake this role, was not directly or systematically measured. Third, few studies directly examined learners’ critical AI literacy or the cognitive processes involved in evaluating or revising GenAI-generated content.

papers.title: Prompt Design as AI-Mediated Pedagogical Performance in Initial Teacher Education: A Case Study in Foreign Language Teaching Methodology
papers.authors: Zeus Plasencia Carballo, A. Eff‐Darwich, Cristian García Santana, Carmen de los Ángeles Perdomo López
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is creating new possibilities for educational resource development, making prompt design increasingly relevant to interactions with these tools. However, little research has examined how pedagogical criteria are represented in prompts developed within initial teacher education or how prompt design can be conceptualised in relation to teachers’ professional knowledge. This study analyses 15 group-produced prompts and their documented development processes, created by students enrolled in a Bachelor’s Degree in Early Childhood Education during a Foreign Language Teaching Methodology activity involving the creation of children’s stories in English using generative artificial intelligence. An exploratory case study design was adopted, using an eight-dimension analytical rubric addressing pedagogical, linguistic, narrative, and strategic aspects of prompt design, with the corpus independently assessed by three raters. The analysis combined descriptive scores across rubric dimensions with qualitative examination of prompt content and documented revision processes to identify recurring patterns of educational prompt design. Findings showed that educational criteria were generally represented explicitly across the corpus, although differences emerged across dimensions and cases. Strategic development and agency, target learners and language level, and language function and objectives were the most consistently represented dimensions, whereas formal control of the output showed comparatively lower scores and professional contextualisation showed the greatest variability. The combined quantitative and qualitative analysis revealed recurring cross-case patterns in the explicitness and integration of pedagogical criteria rather than discrete competence levels or developmental categories. The findings suggest that prompt design can be examined as a form of AI-mediated pedagogical performance in which educational criteria are translated into operational instructions for generative systems. Rather than demonstrating a wholly independent teaching competence, the study highlights prompt design as a potentially relevant context for mobilising and externalising pedagogical knowledge within initial teacher education. Given the small, context-specific corpus of collaborative prompts, the findings are exploratory and are not intended to support generalisation to individual prompting competence or to other teacher education contexts.

papers.title: Beyond Location Probability: Neural Correlates of Feature–Spatial Mapping Learning in Visual Search
papers.authors: Jiahui Zhang, Hanxu Wang, Jiahuan Chen, Guang Wei Zhao
papers.abstract: Visual statistical learning enables humans to extract regular information from the environment, thereby optimizing the allocation of attentional resources. Previous studies have demonstrated that the visual system can learn the spatial probability of target occurrence and feature-specific spatial regularities for distractors. It remains unclear how target feature–location contingencies guide search when high-probability locations have equal overall target probability, or how such learning is reflected in ERP activity. The present study used a visual search paradigm that manipulated target-location probability and feature–spatial matching relationships, while simultaneously recording EEG data. Behavioral results showed that reaction times were significantly faster when targets appeared at feature-matched high-probability locations than when they appeared at feature-mismatched high-probability locations or low-probability locations. However, analyses by target feature showed that the feature-matching advantage was observed for color targets but not for shape targets. Electrophysiological results showed no significant differences in N2pc amplitude among the three conditions; when averaged across target features, LPC amplitudes were significantly smaller in both high-probability location conditions than in the low-probability location condition, but did not differ significantly between feature-matched and feature-mismatched high-probability locations when averaged across target features. These findings provide evidence that feature–spatial statistical regularities can influence visual search, while the feature-matching advantage was specific to color targets in the present study.

papers.title: Self-Perceived Knowledge, Self-Efficacy, and Reported Integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence Among University Faculty: An Exploratory Profile Analysis
papers.authors: Graciela Castillo, Víctor Alejandro Bósquez-Barcenes, Mariuxi Vinueza-Morales, Cristian L. Vidal-Silva
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) adoption in higher education raises questions about the relationships among perceived knowledge, confidence, attitudes, and reported teaching practices. A cross-sectional study of 149 faculty members at an Ecuadorian public university examines four self-reported constructs, with Cronbach’s α ranging from 0.841 to 0.981. An exploratory three-group partition describes higher-scoring (44.3%), intermediate-scoring (39.6%), and lower-scoring (16.1%) respondents, although the silhouette criterion favors two groups (0.383 versus 0.299). Self-efficacy correlates with reported integration (r=0.812; approximate 95% CI [0.749, 0.860]). A complementary three-predictor regression reconstructed from the reported correlation matrix yields R2=0.668 and a self-efficacy coefficient of β=0.758 (approximate 95% CI [0.630, 0.885]). This model excludes demographic and frequency covariates and does not replace the original adjusted analysis. Reconstructed aggregate counts show an association between profile and grouped use frequency (conditional Monte Carlo p=0.0037), whereas the gender association remains inconclusive (p=0.089). Measurement overlap, self-reporting, and unverified cluster stability limit interpretation. Normalizing response ranges does not establish that faculty practice more than they know. The results support evaluating faculty development that combines conceptual and critical AI literacy with GAI-specific self-efficacy; causal effectiveness remains untested.

papers.title: Cervical Cancer Burden in Africa: An Integrative Review of Epidemiology, Plant Medicine, and AI-Driven Innovation
papers.authors: Susanna Awinsongya Anovunga, Aboagye Kwarteng Dofuor, Aziz Adamu, Charles Vudoh, Precious Ndamani, Roseline Afua Ndetema Sunkwa-Arthur, Seyram Kofi Loh, Alex Awentirim Akayiri, Christopher Yao Tsikata, Angelina Akomea
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer imposes a heavy burden in low- and middle-income countries and persistently high incidence and mortality in Sub-Saharan Africa due to unequal access to prevention and care. Although human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major driving factor, the risk is amplified by HIV co-infection, socioeconomic barriers, limited infrastructure, low health literacy, and behavioral factors, leading to frequent late-stage diagnosis, low screening coverage, and poor survival. Recent expansion of HPV vaccination programs since 2019 has achieved high coverage in some countries, but continent-wide rates remain below targets amid hesitancy, inequities, and systemic weaknesses. Thus, there is a critical need for an integrated synthesis of multidisciplinary evidence that reflects the peculiarities and diversities of African health systems. Moreover, high mortality rates underscore the need for integrated, context-specific evidence to strengthen vaccination, screening, and management strategies in line with WHO global elimination targets. Plant medicine promises to complement mainstream health delivery in low resource settings. Emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools show strong potential to improve screening accuracy, reduce subjectivity and resource needs, and enhance early detection in resource-limited settings. This review synthesizes multidisciplinary data on economic impact, epidemiology, risk factors, prevention, diagnostic challenges, plant medicine and AI innovations to guide equitable progress in diverse African contexts.

papers.title: A Controlled Reanalysis of KIDO: Text Variants, Image-Model Configurations, and Cross-Modal Score Discrepancy
papers.authors: Ercan Ezin
papers.abstract: KIDO pairs children’s prompted happy and sad drawings with written reflections, creating a multimodal setting in which the text and image channels provide very different evidence for the same labels. We reanalyze KIDO by comparing Turkish, original English, and LLM-generated Turkish-grounded English text; replicating image-model configurations; and measuring text–image score discrepancy on 1630 drawings from 815 children. Turkish-grounded English is numerically higher than original English across emotion, gender, and educational-level classification under the controlled English protocol. For emotion, the respective three-seed macro-F1 scores are 0.9808±0.0004 and 0.9798±0.0034; however, the paired ensemble difference is small, and its 95% child-cluster bootstrap interval includes zero. A blinded, tail-enriched bilingual audit of 120 child-distinct pairs provides source-grounded support for the generated text: 88.3% of ratings receive adequacy scores of 4–5, while major meaning errors occur in 7.5% of ratings and are confined to the deliberately sampled low-similarity tail. Text performance also depends strongly on explicit emotion cues: such cues occur in approximately two-thirds of test reflections, and masking them at evaluation reduces macro-F1 by 0.054–0.073, while performance remains above 0.90. Image-emotion models achieve a substantially lower mean macro-F1, ranging from 0.7683 to 0.7867 across replicated DenseNet121 and ConvNeXt configurations. Cross-modal score differences remain substantial: the Multimodal Discrepancy Index, equivalent to total variation in this binary task, ranges from 0.2300 to 0.2753 across image ensembles. These results show that text preparation, lexical cues, and image-model configuration materially affect conclusions drawn from KIDO and support reporting channel-specific evidence before interpreting multimodal agreement or fusion.

papers.title: Classification of Solid Earth Tide Observation Data Using GBDT-LGBM Hybrid Stacking Model
papers.authors: Yan Zhang, Cong Pang, Ying Zhao, Kai Wu
papers.abstract: Solid Earth tide observation sequences reflect crustal deformation, Earth’s internal structure and tidal dynamic evolution, with important theoretical and engineering value for earthquake precursor monitoring. Conventional standalone machine learning models struggle to handle the nonlinear, non-stationary features of solid tide data, showing limited accuracy, weak generalization and unstable error fluctuation. This paper constructs a GBDT-LGBM hybrid stacked ensemble classification model. GBDT and LGBM serve as dual base learners to extract latent features from tidal time series, and an upper meta-learner fuses their outputs to leverage their complementary advantages. The model classifies five types of solid tide records: observation system failures, natural environmental disturbances, human interference, geophysical events and normal tidal fluctuations. It perfectly discriminates human-activity and system-failure samples; natural disturbances reach AUC = 0.997, while geophysical events and normal tides have AUC values of 0.944 and 0.950. A small number of misclassifications are caused by similar waveforms with gentle baseline drift and minor local disturbances. Benchmark comparisons show this ensemble achieves average macro-AUC, accuracy and macro-F1 above 0.97. Box plots from 40 repeated experiments display narrow metric ranges without outliers, demonstrating low overfitting risk. This model effectively captures temporal variations in tidal data and provides reliable support for solid tide data classification and regional crustal dynamic monitoring.

papers.title: Does AI-Assisted Design Undermine Market Value? The Influence of Design Source, Style, and Campaign Duration
papers.authors: Menlong Ye, Wei Zhang, Jun Yin
papers.abstract: Against the backdrop of the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, traditional design value assessment systems based on creative input are facing new challenges. This study aims to examine the effects of design source (human-designed design vs. AI-assisted design), design style (commercial style vs. AI-native style), and campaign duration on the value assessment of design works in the AI era. Drawing on a real e-commerce platform context, the study conducts empirical analyses through two multifactor experiments. Experiment 1 adopts a 2 × 5 mixed experimental design to compare the value assessment performance of human-designed and AI-assisted design works across different campaign durations. Experiment 2 further introduces the variable of design style and employs a 2 × 2 × 5 three-factor experimental design to investigate the interaction effects among design source, design style, and campaign duration. The findings indicate that AI-assisted design demonstrates significant efficiency advantages in terms of time and cost. However, regarding value assessment indicators such as number of clicks, click-through rate (CTR), conversion rate (CVR), and sales performance, AI-assisted design performs comparably to human-designed design overall. Different design styles exhibit stage-specific differences: commercial style is more effective in attracting user attention and promoting conversion during the early stage of campaigns, whereas AI-native style gradually demonstrates higher conversion efficiency and cost advantages in the middle and later stages. In addition, the value assessment of design works exhibits significant temporal dynamics, with advertising performance reaching a relatively optimal level during the middle stage of campaign deployment. The study finds that AI significantly reduces creative input without weakening the market performance of design works, providing new evidence for understanding the input–outcome relationship in design value. The study also offers practical insights for enterprises seeking to optimize collaborative creation strategies between AI and human designers. The study finds that AI significantly reduces creative input without weakening the market performance of design works, providing new evidence for understanding the input–outcome relationship in design value. The study also offers practical insights for enterprises seeking to optimize collaborative creation strategies between AI and human designers.

papers.title: Simple Stacking Ensemble Machine Learning Approach for Vickers Hardness Prediction of Arc Vacuum Melted High-Entropy Alloys
papers.authors: Andiko Putra Pratama Krisdiawan, Rio Sudwitama Persadanta Kaban, Andreas Frederico, Agrin Febrian Pradana, Celfien Septian Widya Pratama, Jaka Fajar Fatriansyah
papers.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) show excellent mechanical properties, but their enormous compositional space makes experimental and computational exploration expensive. This study predicts the Vickers hardness (HV) of HEAs from nominal elemental compositions (at.%) using a composition-based stacking ensemble machine learning approach without the use of handcrafted descriptors. A dataset of 120 vacuum arc-melted (VAM) HEAs containing 15 constituent elements (Re, Ru, Al, Si, Ti, Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta, and W) was compiled. Four baseline models, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector regression (SVR), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), and artificial neural networks (ANN), were evaluated. SVR achieves the highest baseline performance (R2 = 0.90). Stacking ensembles with the SVR meta-learner improved the weaker base learner performance by 17.20% and 12.50% for KNN-SVR and ANN-SVR respectively, relative to their base models. The best-performing stacking ensemble, XGB-SVR, only results in a minimal improvement of 2.90% compared to SVR. Ru, Re, and Al as the strongest positive contributors to hardness, as well as Fe, Co, and Ni as the strongest negative contributors, are identified with an interpretability test using permutation feature importance (PFI) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Validation on the held-out compositions showed prediction errors below 7%. This study indicates that the composition-only models could form the basis for an effective and interpretable approach for rapid HEAs hardness screening. However, the investigated stacking strategy offers limited benefit compared to the best-performing baseline model.

papers.title: Exploring nursing students’ experiences of using generative AI for emotional intelligence learning: a qualitative study
papers.authors: XiaoHui Fan, Jingjing Sun, Rui Xu, ZHANG Linghui, Ruixiao Ou, Ruihua Jin, Hui Yang, Panpan Huai
papers.abstract: Background Emotional intelligence is a core competency for nursing students; however, traditional nursing education faces challenges in fostering emotional intelligence, including curricular imbalances, limited teaching methods, and delayed assessment and feedback. The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new possibilities for addressing the above issues; however, existing research has not yet thoroughly explored how nursing students learn emotional intelligence through GenAI or their experiences in this process. Objective Based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Teaching Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, and using Goleman’s five-dimensional model of emotional intelligence as a reference, this study explores the experiences of undergraduate nursing students in using generative artificial intelligence for emotional intelligence learning, as well as the factors that facilitate this process. Method This study employed a qualitative descriptive research design and Reflexive Thematic Analysis (RTA). Using purposive sampling, 19 undergraduate nursing students (from freshman to senior year) were selected for one-on-one semi-structured in-depth interviews. All participants had experience using GenAI tools (such as DeepSeek and Doubao) for communication practice, case discussions, or sentiment analysis. The interview data were analyzed using the RTA six-stage process, with NVivo 12.0 software used to assist with data management. Results We identified and synthesized 238 initial codes into three core themes. Theme 1, “From Efficiency-Driven to Precise Empathy,” presents the differing descriptions of empathy-related experiences among students in different grade levels: lower-grade students more frequently reported efficiency-driven usage experiences; some middle-grade students described difficulties caused by technical barriers; and upper-grade students more often described the recognition of patients’ emotions in conjunction with clinical experience. Theme 2, “From Mimicking AI to Autonomous Expression,” focuses on students’ reported experiences related to social skills, including direct application, recognition and adjustment, autonomous expression, and the simulation gap that persisted throughout the process. Theme 3, “From Technical Frustration to Mental Rehearsal,” integrates experiences related to self-management, self-awareness, and self-motivation. The three themes correspond to different dimensions of emotional intelligence, with students in different grade levels reporting distinct experiential characteristics. Conclusion Nursing undergraduates in different grades exhibit distinct experiential characteristics when using generative artificial intelligence to learn about emotional intelligence. Students’ reports repeatedly highlighted moderate tension around technological motivation, the ability to critically integrate technology, and the perceived value of technological friction. Based on these exploratory findings, we propose several preliminary educational implications—including grade-level-specific support, curriculum exploration, and education in critical technological literacy and ethics—for consideration in future research and practice.

papers.title: AI conversational agents as population health infrastructure: promise, peril, and the case for public-interest design
papers.authors: Meghna Rajan
papers.abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from novelty to infrastructure. Rulebased chatbots that once nudged users through smoking-cessation scripts have given way to large language model (LLM)-powered agents capable of open-ended, multilingual, empathetic-sounding dialogue, available around the clock at near-zero marginal cost. Systematic and scoping reviews now document measurable effects of AI chatbots on physical activity, diet, smoking cessation, medication adherence, and mental distress across thousands of participants (Feng et al., 2025). The World Health Organization (WHO) itself has deployed a generative AI assistant, S.A.R.A.H., to test population-scale health communication (van Kolfschooten et al., 2025). Taken together, these developments justify treating conversational AI not merely as a clinical or commercial curiosity, but as an emerging layer of public health infrastructure -one that sits alongside water systems, mass media, and vaccination programs as a determinant of how populations receive, interpret, and act on health information. (Wang et al., 2024). This opinion argues that the digital public health community should engage conversational AI on exactly those terms: as infrastructure, not gadgetry. Infrastructure framing changes the questions we ask. Instead of "does the chatbot work?" we should ask who it works for, under what governance, and with what consequences for equity, trust, and the broader information ecosystem. I organize this argument around three tensions that recur across the recent literature: (i) genuine behavioral efficacy versus fragile evidentiary depth; (ii) the promise of expanded access versus the risk of a new digital divide; and (iii) the communicative power of generative AI versus its capacity to manufacture and amplify misinformation. I close by proposing that Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)aligned public health institutions adopt a public-interest design standard for conversational AI, rather than leaving its trajectory to consumer technology markets alone.The evidence base for AI chatbots in health promotion has grown quickly and, on balance, positively. A widely cited systematic review found that AI chatbots produced favorable outcomes across lifestyle modification domains, particularly physical activity, diet, and smoking cessation (Aggarwal et al., 2023). A 2026 scoping review of 43 studies (Fu et al., 2026) reported that 82% of behavior-change comparisons trended positive, though only about a third reached moderate or larger effect sizes, and cost-effectiveness data were essentially absent. A meta-analysis focused on adolescents and young adults (Feng et al., 2025) similarly found chatbots effective for alleviating mental distress and supporting health behaviors, while noting substantial heterogeneity in intervention design and outcome measurement. Three limitations temper enthusiasm. First, most trials are short, nonclinical, adult-skewed, and rarely randomized at scale; only about a third of studies in the largest recent scoping review were randomized controlled trials (Fu et al., 2026). Second, "AI chatbot" spans an enormous range of systems, from rule-based decision trees to frontier LLMs, and pooling them obscures which architectural features actually drive behavior change (Kurniawan et al., 2024;Schachner et al., 2020). Third, almost no study reports durability beyond a few months, leaving open whether early engagement gains represent sustained health improvement or a novelty effect. For a section whose remit is population-level promotion and prevention rather than individual clinical outcomes, this matters: infrastructure decisions built on inflated short-term efficacy claims risk premature, poorly targeted public investment (Hampsher-Monk et al., 2024).A second tension concerns reach. Proponents rightly note that AI chatbots are inexpensive to scale, available in multiple languages, and can operate where clinical workforce is scarceattributes explicitly cited in WHO's own rationale for deploying S.A.R.A.H. as a research prototype for population health communication (Palmer & Schwan, 2025). Behavioralaccess frameworks extend this logic, arguing that digital health tools must be evaluated not only on availability but on whether populations can meaningfully engage with them across design, delivery, dissemination, and sustainment stages. Yet the same structural gaps that limit telemedicine and mobile health also constrain chatbot benefit: broadband access, device ownership, digital literacy, language coverage, and trust in institutional actors are unevenly distributed within and between countries (Banerjee, 2026).
