papers.title: Enhancing PISA-aligned argumentation skills of prospective biology teachers through generative artificial intelligence
papers.authors: Ergasheva Gulrukhsor Surkhonidinovna, Mekhrinigor Haydarovna Raupova, Sabbir Ahmed Chowdhury, Салима Тогаймурадовна Рахматова
papers.abstract: Despite scientific argumentation being a fundamental competency of the PISA assessment framework, prospective biology teachers often demonstrate insufficient development in evidence-based reasoning and rebuttal construction skills. Considering the limitations of large-scale implementation of individualized approaches in higher education, this study evaluates the effectiveness of Generative Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT-4) configured as a “Socratic tutor” in developing argumentation skills among future educators. An 8-week quasi-experimental study involving 124 students from a pedagogical university employed traditional peer discussion methods in the control group ( n = 62), while the experimental group ( n = 62) utilized an AI agent that induced cognitive dissonance regarding socio-scientific issues. Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) of data obtained through Toulmin's Argument Pattern (TAP) and PISA rubrics confirmed that the experimental group achieved statistically significantly higher overall argumentation quality compared to the control group (F (1,121) = 14.23, p < .001, η 2 = .105). Particularly, participants who received AI-assisted instruction showed marked improvement in forming rebuttals and evaluating counterevidence, which are considered among the most cognitively demanding components within the PISA scientific literacy framework (OECD). These findings suggest that a Generative AI-mediated Socratic instructional package can be an effective and scalable approach for developing epistemic cognition, and they propose a pedagogical model for integrating structured AI-based tutoring into teacher preparation systems aligned with international assessment standards. These findings should be interpreted as evidence for the effectiveness of the structured, AI-mediated Socratic instructional package as a whole, rather than as evidence of AI's inherent superiority over other methods; the relative contribution of the AI medium versus the structured pedagogical protocol it delivers was not directly tested in this design.

papers.title: Barriers and facilitators to healthcare artificial intelligence adoption in Wales: findings from focus groups
papers.authors: Michal Pruski, Jasmine Rollings, Kathleen L. Withers
papers.abstract: Background Building on a previous Wales-wide survey, this study aimed to provide more in-depth exploration of the barriers and facilitators to healthcare artificial intelligence adoption in Wales. Objectives The study aimed to explore these barriers and facilitators among various social groups, to inform policy development in Wales. Methods Four focus groups were conducted with a group of members of the public and a group of healthcare professionals (both groups recruited from a previous survey), as well as a group Sixth Form students and a group of retired adults. Inductive thematic analysis was used to generate themes and to compare the issues raised by the various groups. Contiguity-based analysis was undertaken to underscore how themes related with each other. Results A total of 21 individuals participated in the focus groups (healthcare professionals=6, members of the public=6, sixth-form students=5, retirees=4). Seven thematic networks were identified. Across groups, seven themes were identified in the healthcare professional group, six in the general members of the public group, seven in the sixth form student group, and seven in the retiree group. All groups voiced concerns about data privacy and highlighted the importance of human oversight of AI and human contact during the clinical encounter as they expressed more trust in human practitioners. There were though differences between groups, such as greater trust in black-box systems by healthcare professionals, and between individual participants in regard to trust in private organisations developing AI for healthcare organisations. Conclusions All groups were concerned with information security and expressed a preference for human contact during the clinical encounter and a human-in-the-loop approach. There were differences between the groups, such as in attitudes towards black-box AI technologies and trust in clinicians. No additional barriers or facilitators were identified for proxy consent.

papers.title: From Imaging Gatekeeper to Catheterisation Laboratory Co-Pilot: The Emerging Role of AI in Interventional Cardiology
papers.authors: Kyvan Irannejad, Hassoon Sarwar, Joseph Thomas, Matthew Jay Budoff
papers.abstract: Background: AI is rapidly reshaping cardiovascular medicine, particularly within imaging-intensive fields such as interventional cardiology. Advances in machine learning and deep learning have enabled automated analysis of complex cardiovascular datasets and opened new opportunities for decision support across the coronary care continuum. Objectives: This review summarises current and emerging applications of AI in interventional cardiology, spanning pre-procedural imaging, intraprocedural guidance, outcome prediction, and future technological developments. Key findings: In the pre-procedural setting, AI-enhanced coronary CT angiography, AI-derived fractional flow reserve, and automated plaque characterisation improve risk stratification and patient selection for invasive angiography. Within the catheterisation laboratory, AI applications include automated angiographic interpretation, intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography analysis, lesion classification, optimisation of stent sizing and deployment, emerging roles in structural heart interventions, and periprocedural haemodynamic monitoring. Machine learning models are also increasingly used for risk stratification, predicting bleeding, contrast-induced nephropathy, and mortality after percutaneous coronary intervention. Despite these advances, important challenges remain, including regulatory oversight, algorithm validation, bias mitigation, data governance, clinician education, and unresolved liability issues. Conclusion: AI is evolving from a diagnostic imaging adjunct to a comprehensive decision-support platform in interventional cardiology. Emerging technologies such as real-time AI-assisted catheterisation laboratory systems, multimodal data integration, digital twin modelling, and AI-guided robotic interventions may further transform coronary intervention workflows, positioning AI as a procedural co-pilot that augments rather than replaces physician expertise.

papers.title: Gemini AI-Supported Digital Posters in EFL Classroom: Lexical Depth and Two-Week Retention
papers.authors: Uni Maharani, Sudiyono Sudiyono, Yuyun Yulia
papers.journal: Journal of Languages and Language Teaching
papers.abstract: Limited lexical depth and the difficulty to retain words after teaching are issues for junior high school students who learn to speak English as a foreign language. This study investigated vocabulary learning and student perceptions of a Gemini AI-supported digital poster project in a Grade 8 classroom in Palembang, Indonesia. A mixed-methods quasi-experiment was conducted on two intact classes (N = 48; 24 per group) in six meetings. The experimental group explored meanings, context and associated meanings using Gemini AI and produced Canva posters through repeated practice, peer interaction and teacher guidance. The 30 item vocabulary assessment was done before instruction and immediately afterward and two weeks later. Fifteen item questionnaires and six semi-structured interviews were used to extract perception information. The experimental and control mean post-test was 84.37 and 71.04 respectively. The two-week delayed means were 80.92 and 66.13 as compared to the final results from the summaries. The post-test mean difference was 13.33 (95% CI [9.34, 17.32], p < .001) and the delayed difference was 14.79 (95% CI [10.65, 18.93], p < .001). These cross-sectional tests do not establish a group-by-time effect. Students generally described interest, contextual support and creativity as well as connectivity problems, uneven digital skills and a dependence on AI. The instructional package was associated with higher immediate and two-week delayed scores, but its individual components cannot be separated. We need to be mindful of teacher monitoring, checking AI responses, privacy protection and the need for AI literacy and education.

papers.title: Digitally Mediated Thesis Writing Among ELT Undergraduates: Strategic Patterns of Multi-Tool Integration Across Writing Stages
papers.authors: Sheila Agustina, Fika Megawati, Sandrina Bilqis, Nurkamilah Nurkamilah
papers.journal: Journal of Languages and Language Teaching
papers.abstract: The increasing integration of digital tools into academic writing has transformed how students compose, revise, and conceptualize scholarly work. Existing research has examined artificial intelligence and writing support technologies in general classroom contexts, but limited attention has been paid to how undergraduate students employ these tools in high-stakes academic tasks such as thesis writing. This gap is particularly significant in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) settings, where linguistic and rhetorical demands are intensified. Accordingly, this study investigates how Indonesian undergraduate ELT students integrate digital tools into their thesis writing. It focuses on the types of tools used, the stages of writing they support, students’ motivations, and patterns of integration. Using a qualitative case study design, data were collected from 38 students through open-ended questionnaires and analyzed thematically. The findings reveal that students engage with a range of generative, translation, and language-refinement tools across multiple stages of thesis writing, particularly during editing, literature review, and discussion development. An iterative draft–consult–revise cycle also emerged as a central integration pattern. It indicates that students maintain agency while coordinating digital mediation. The study concludes that digitally mediated thesis writing reflects emerging forms of academic literacy, which underscore the need for structured digital literacy guidance within ELT writing pedagogy.

papers.title: Redesigning Scaffolding with AI-Assisted Dynamic Assessment to Support Real-Time Learning Growth in EFL Learners
papers.authors: Nurlaela Nurlaela, Napius Kogoya, Basikin Basikin, Dyah Setyowati Ciptaningrum, Cristina E. Sayoto
papers.journal: Journal of Languages and Language Teaching
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence in language learning is increasingly important because it can provide fast, personalized, and adaptive feedback that supports language competency development. However, in practice, the use of AI is often separated from the formative assesment framework, so it is not yet fully aligned with the principles of Dynamic Assesment (DA), which emphasizes the simultaneous integration of assessment and learning. This gap creates a need to understand how AI can used pedagogically to redesign scaffolding and support real-time learning growth in the context of English as a Foreign Language (EFL). This study aims to explore the use of AI in Dynamic Assessment and to examine the expereience and perception of students and lectures regarding its use. Using qualitataive approach, data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation of AI exercise result among students in English Language and Culture Study Program of Universitas Tompotika Luwuk. Finding indicate that AI act as co-mediator that provide linguistic, phonological, metacognitive, and affective scaffolding, thereby accelerating the DA cycle and enhancing real-time learning growth. Students reported increased feelingsof security, independence, and motivation, while lecturers felt that assessment effeciency and the quality of pedagogical interventions had improved. This study concluded that AI-assisted DA presents an effective innovative assessment model, but still requires conceptual mediation from lecturers for learning to be optimal.

papers.title: Ydinvoiman kuvastot ja visuaalinen osallistujakulttuuri
papers.authors: Veera Ojala
papers.abstract: This review presents the doctoral dissertation “Chornobyl and Fukushima Dreams: Visual Participatory Culture and the Co-Creation of Nuclear Disaster Heritage” (University of Turku, 2026), which examines the Chornobyl and Fukushima nuclear disaster sites as heritage places through the lens of visual participatory culture. The study asks how wider publics, through digital photography, participate in the collective meaningmaking of nuclear disaster heritage. The dissertation comprises four articles addressing visitors’ storytelling in the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone, shifts in visitor photography between 2008 and 2018, and the diverging heritage trajectories of Chornobyl and Fukushima. It shows that photography is not passive documentation but an active practice that shapes heritage resources and value interpretations. The research draws on ethnographic and netnographic fieldwork in Ukraine and Japan, interviews, and visual methods: photoelicitation and the use of photographs taken by the interviewees themselves. A key conclusion is that images invite us to participate in reimagining the past and the future and that nuclear disaster sites function as spaces for negotiating human–technology relations and more sustainable forms of coexistence.

papers.title: Translators’ Gains and Pains in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Naji Alyami, Ali Abbas Falah Alzubi
papers.journal: International Journal of Translation and Interpretation Studies
papers.abstract: This study aimed to provide a comprehensive systematic review of research published in peer-reviewed scientific journals in Arabic and English between 2022 and 2026 that investigated the impact of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Copilot, and others, on translation and translation education among professional translators, translation students, and faculty members. The study used the PRISMA 2020 framework for systematic search, screening, and documentation, and employed a thematic analysis approach based on the model developed by Braun and Clarke. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria to 24 initial records, the final analysis included 18 studies. The findings revealed that the most significant benefits of using generative AI tools included improved efficiency and productivity, reduced time to complete translation tasks, support for post-editing processes, improved certain translation quality indicators, and the promotion of self-directed learning and the development of professional competencies among translators and students. At the same time, the results identified several challenges, most notably terminological accuracy issues, difficulties handling cultural and idiomatic expressions and local dialects, risks associated with overreliance on intelligent systems, and ethical concerns involving privacy, transparency, and professional accountability. The review also showed that the impact of generative AI varies by text type, specialized domain, and the assessment tools used. In addition, it highlighted limited evidence available concerning the Arabic language, particularly in areas such as legal translation, idiomatic expressions, and local dialects. This study contributes an interpretive framework based on the concept of “Gains and Pains” to explain generative AI’s dual impact on translation and translation education. The findings conclude that generative AI does not fully replace human translators; rather, it serves as a supportive tool that reshapes translators’ professional roles toward reviewing, verifying, and evaluating outputs. Accordingly, the study recommends integrating generative AI tools into translator training programs within clear pedagogical and ethical frameworks. They should also include post-editing, critical thinking, and output-verification skills, and support further specialized applied research in the Arab context.

papers.title: НЕРІВНІСТЬ УПРОВАДЖЕННЯ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ ПІДПРИЄМСТВАМИ ЄС: МІЖДЕРЖАВНИЙ І РОЗМІРНИЙ ВИМІРИ
papers.authors: О.І. Заяць, Іван Синетар
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence adoption is expanding across the European Union, while national averages conceal substantial firm-size differences. Absolute and relative gaps describe different dimensions of this diffusion. The paper examines cross-country and firm-size inequality in AI adoption across all 27 EU Member States and distinguishes absolute distance from proportional disadvantage. The empirical base is Eurostat’s 2026 statistical report with 2025 country-by-size adoption rates. The absolute gap is the large-enterprise rate minus the small-enterprise rate; the normalised gap divides this difference by their sum. Spearman rank correlations are primary and Pearson coefficients supplementary. Because the official all-enterprise rate is size-weighted and correlates almost perfectly with small-enterprise adoption, relative-gap inference relies mainly on an equal-weight measure averaging small, medium and large enterprises. A medium-enterprise-only correlation provides a check independent of the normalised-gap formula. Coefficients of variation use the population standard deviation for the complete set of 27 Member States. AI was used by 17.0% of small and 55.0% of large EU enterprises. Small-enterprise adoption ranged from 4.1% to 37.5% across countries (CV=0.515), compared with 20.8% to 79.4% among large enterprises (CV=0.274). The national adoption rate is moderately positively associated with the absolute gap (Spearman ρ=0.477, p=0.012). The equal-weight measure is strongly negatively associated with the normalised gap (ρ=−0.816, p<0.001), and the medium-enterprise check is even stronger (ρ=−0.846, p<0.001). Among non-users, only 12.7% of small enterprises had considered AI adoption, compared with 36.5% of large enterprises; reported implementation barriers differed much less across size classes. Cross-country relative dispersion is substantially greater among small enterprises. A higher size-standardised adoption level can coexist with a sizeable absolute large-small distance while being associated with a markedly smaller proportional disadvantage of small firms. The results are cross-sectional associations based on published Eurostat point estimates and do not establish causality.

papers.title: Beyond the Classroom: How Artificial Intelligence is Transforming Personalized Learning for Students
papers.authors: Harshika Gupta
papers.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming extremely important in education and has the potential to change how students learn. This paper talks about how AI can create personalized learning experiences, provide timely feedback, and support students and teachers. AI-powered educational systems can analyze information about student performance and adapt learning materials, practice questions, and feedback to individual needs. These capabilities may allow students to receive additional academic support and review difficult concepts at their own pace. Research also suggests that AI can provide individualized assistance in a more advanced way, particularly through intelligent tutoring systems and AI learning assistants. However, the use of AI in education also presents significant challenges. Academic integrity, student privacy, unequal access to technology, bias, and false information are important concerns that schools and educators must address. Research on AI-supported learning suggests that AI is most effective when it is used to support humans rather than replacing teachers. Overall, AI has the potential to make education more personalized and accessible, but its benefits depend on responsible usage, appropriate safeguards, and continued human involvement in the learning process.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as Digital Transformation in University Libraries of Pakistan: A Qualitative Study on Challenges and Benefits
papers.authors: Sanila Aslam, Muhammad Arif, Muhammad Bilal Asim
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study is to explore the challenges and benefits associated with the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the university libraries of Pakistan. Given the novelty of the phenomenon, this study opted a qualitative research approach, and interviews were conducted with 20 university librarians who were purposefully chosen. The findings indicate that the use of AI in libraries improves operations and services by minimizing human errors caused by the repetitive nature of routine tasks. The study identified several challenges encountered by university librarians, including financial issues, inadequate specialization in emerging technologies, and limited resources to adopt and use AI-based technologies. Such challenges may be addressed by equipping librarians with necessary knowledge and technical skills such as basic IT skills, understanding AI concepts, data analysis and management, knowledge of AI algorithms, and critical thinking. This research significantly contributes by identifying the precise technical and professional competencies necessary for effective AI integration in university libraries, which encompass fundamental IT skills, comprehension of AI concepts, data analysis and management, familiarity with AI algorithms, and critical thinking. This work presents empirical evidence from a developing-country viewpoint, offering novel insights for higher education administrators, politicians, and library professionals aiming to deploy AI-driven library services in Pakistan and analogous contexts.

papers.title: Thai Learners’ Online CFL Engagement: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Cognitive, Emotional, and Behavioral Dimensions
papers.authors: Jin Zhao, Wei Xu
papers.journal: Researching and Teaching Chinese as a Foreign Language
papers.abstract: Abstract This study examines the engagement of Thai learners in online CFL classrooms using cognitive, affective, and behavioral factors. Through the analysis of semistructured interviews conducted with 15 beginners studying at a language institute connected with the university in Thailand, the study adopts the method of Reflexive Thematic Analysis (RTA) to explore how native Chinese teachers (NCTs) and non-native Chinese teachers (NNCTs) affect learners’ experiences in coteaching arrangements. Although NCTs contribute to authentic inputs and communication, their teaching using Chinese and English could place a cognitive burden on beginners. In contrast, NNCTs are responsible for a vital scaffolding role by using Thai to explain grammar and avoid misunderstanding. From the perspective of emotions, learners learn to cope with anxiety and tiredness by means of reducing speed, exercising silence, and turning off their cameras to create an “online shielding effect” that enables their participation in long online classes. Behaviorally, minimal peer interaction and low social presence in the online class led learners to shift from collaborative to autonomous study, relying on translation software, artificial intelligence (AI) tools, and external social networks such as Instagram. This study provides context-specific insights into online CFL engagement in Thailand and highlights the importance of complementing teacher roles, emotion management, and social support in maintaining learner engagement.

papers.title: Perceptions and Practices of Artificial Intelligence in CSL Education: A Qualitative Study of University Teachers
papers.authors: Wenjie Lang, Shiwei Qi
papers.journal: Researching and Teaching Chinese as a Foreign Language
papers.abstract: Abstract As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly prevalent in Chinese as a Second Language/Chinese as a Foreign Language (CSL/CFL) education, empirical evidence on teachers’ actual uses and perceptions of generative AI (GenAI) remains limited. This study aims to examine how CSL teachers perceive and engage with AI tools, how these tools have reshaped teachers’ practices and teaching efficiency, and the challenges that AI poses for CSL education. The study employed a qualitative design and conducted semi-structured interviews with three CSL teachers at Chinese universities, including both novice and experienced teachers. Based on grounded theory, the data were analyzed through three stages of coding. The findings show that the teachers with different levels of teaching experience generally held positive and open attitudes toward AI and were willing to explore its pedagogical use. AI was mainly valued for improving lesson preparation efficiency, enriching teaching resources, and supporting the design of classroom activities. It also showed potential to diversify forms of teacher-student interaction. However, teachers’ adoption of AI tools remained selective and strongly mediated by professional judgment, particularly in discipline-specific instruction. Challenges concerning the quality of AI-generated content, the lack of CSL-specialized AI tools, and students’ overreliance on AI were also identified. Based on the results, implications for CSL teachers, educational institutions, and AI developers seeking to support AI integration in CSL education were proposed.

papers.title: Visual Analysis of International Chinese Language Teachers’ Development Research in the Past Three Decades (1995–2025)
papers.authors: Chi Ma, Chunyan Ma, 孙 福婷
papers.journal: Researching and Teaching Chinese as a Foreign Language
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of international Chinese language teachers is one of the core research areas in the discipline of international Chinese language education, with key focuses including the critical factors influencing teachers’ professional growth, the construction of development pathways, and the supporting mechanisms to facilitate teachers’ adaptation to local teaching environments. This study employs CiteSpace 6.3.1, a bibliometric visualization tool, and takes the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) as the data source to analyze relevant literature published in domestic journals from 1995 to 2025, aiming to reveal the evolutionary trends and core topics of research on international Chinese language teachers’ development. Cluster analysis identifies seven fundamental thematic clusters accumulated over three decades in this research field. Citation-based trend analysis further divides existing research into established core themes and newly emerging research streams. Traditional core research priorities mainly cover Teaching Chinese As a Foreign Language (TCFL) curriculum design, teacher training frameworks, textbook compilation, and Chinese international promotion strategies. Recent emerging research frontiers are aggregated into three broad dimensions: reflective pedagogy and empirical research practice, teachers’ cross-cultural competency and identity construction, and the application of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) and large language models alongside localized Chinese plus vocational education exploration. This review systematically maps the field's developmental trajectory and offers prospective insights into its future research frontiers and practical orientations.
keywords: Chinese as a foreign language teaching

papers.title: Advancing FASD education through interprofessional learning: A practice note for health science curricula
papers.authors: Nicole Gross, Shana Mohr, Andrea Kotlar, Sara Dzaman, Wendie Larocque, Mansfield Mela, Holly Mansell
papers.journal: Journal of Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder
papers.abstract: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) is a highly prevalent yet underrecognized condition that requires multidisciplinary, stigma-free care. Despite its significance, FASD education is inconsistently addressed in health science curricula, leaving future health care professionals underprepared to support affected individuals. To address this gap, we developed an interprofessional educational activity for first-year pharmacy and nutrition students at the University of Saskatchewan. The initiative was informed by an informal literature review and stakeholder consultations with individuals living with FASD and support workers. These conversations highlighted essential competencies, including person-centred communication, trauma-informed care, and strategies to overcome barriers to engagement. The resulting activity combines a foundational lecture with a case-based learning (CBL) session designed to foster collaboration and practical skill development. Four authentic case scenarios were generated using artificial intelligence (AI) and refined through prompt engineering to ensure accuracy and alignment with learning objectives. Students work in interprofessional groups to analyze cases, apply FASD concepts, and practice non-stigmatizing communication strategies. This practice note describes the development process, including integration of lived experience, educational design principles, and AI-supported case creation. By embedding FASD-focused, interprofessional learning early in health science training, this initiative is designed to reduce stigma, improve preparedness, and promote patient-centred care. Future steps include piloting the activity and conducting a formal evaluation to inform broader implementation and adaptation across disciplines.

papers.title: Aging and Hearing Loss in Emotional Prosody Processing: Divergent Neural Adaptation and Behavioral Performance
papers.authors: Yi Lin, Yangfan Lu, Hongwei Ding, Yang Zhang
papers.abstract: Emotional prosody perception is vulnerable in later adulthood, yet the contributions of central aging and peripheral hearing loss remain unclear. Across two experiments, we combined event-related potentials (ERPs) , time-frequency analyses and behavioral measures to examine how aging and hearing sensitvity shape emotional prosody processing. Experiment 1 used acoustically matched speech and nonspeech stimuli in a passive oddball paradigm to assess preattentive processing. Experiment 2 examined explicit emotion identification and implicit stimulus judgment to evaluate goal-directed performance and its associations with neural responses. Aging was associated with reduced neural differentiation between emotions and lower behavioral efficiency, alongside enhanced P3a amplitude. Older adults also responded more slowly than younger adults during emotion identification. Hearing sensitivity showed no significant main effect on accuracy or reaction time, despite associations with delayed early neural processing and stronger theta- and alpha-band activity. Hearing-related neural effects were most evident in older adults and varied across emotions and stimulus types. Brain–behavior associations were selective: reduced mismatch negativity (MMN) was associated with slower responses during stimulus identification, whereas longer MMN latencies were associated with lower accuracy and slower responses during emotion identification. These findings indicate that aging and hearing loss have distinct yet interacting associations with emotional prosody processing, with neural responses not necessarily corresponding to behavioral performance. We propose an “asymmetric adaptation” account in which neural responses to degraded auditory input reorganize selectively across processing stages and contexts, potentially explaining this neural-behavioral divergence and informing more sensitive assessment of socioemotional communication in later adulthood.

papers.title: Predicting First Observed Appearance in a Corporate Governance Rating List and Subsequent Upgrades with Interpretable Machine Learning
papers.authors: Abdullah Kürşat Merter
papers.journal: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Granular Computing
papers.abstract: Corporate governance certification provides a public assessment of organizational practices. Previous research has primarily examined the relationship between certification and firm outcomes, while the timing of certification adoption represents a distinct prediction problem. This study examines whether the first observed appearance on a governance rating list and subsequent rating upgrades can be predicted using statutory accounting disclosures. Rating history is also incorporated into the upgrade model. The institutional setting is the Borsa Istanbul Corporate Governance Index, where licensed agencies evaluate four governance sections and eligibility is determined by published thresholds. The dataset combines rating records for 49 non-financial firms from 2013 to 2024 with financial statements from 438 listed non-financial firms. Two interpretable modeling modules employ an out-of-time design, with predictor variables measured before the corresponding outcomes. The entry module compares L2-regularized logistic regression, Firth-penalized logistic regression, and gradient-boosted trees within a discrete-time hazard specification. The trajectory module estimates next-year rating upgrade scores for rated firms using accounting information and rating history. Both linear entry models achieve areas under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve above 0.50, while the regularized logistic model shows a small positive difference in average precision relative to the training-prevalence benchmark. A single deflated firm-size measure provides discriminatory performance comparable to that of the multivariate entry models. The combined upgrade models achieve ROC areas close to 0.60, while models incorporating rating history achieve higher ROC areas than accounting-only models. Feature attributions also differ between the two tasks, with firm size playing a prominent role in entry predictions and rating history contributing more strongly to upgrade predictions. These findings identify the information sets associated with observed rating adoption and progression. The proposed framework provides rankings of candidate firms and feature-level explanations to support governance monitoring and outreach planning.

papers.title: Undergraduate students’ mastering of fragmentary technical translation using artificial intelligence
papers.authors: Roman Konstantinovich Chalov
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study is to provide a theoretical foundation for and develop a technology for the integrative training of future translators – undergraduate students – in fragmentary technical translation (FTT) using artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The main content of the article includes an analysis of the specifics of FTT, a classification of AI tools, and a description of four conceptual levels of integration (discursive, speech-cognitive, speech-activity, and subject-linguistic). The scientific novelty lies in providing a theoretical justification for the didactic functions of the four levels of AI integration in FTT activities, developing a matrix for the distribution of functions between the student translator and AI as a pedagogical support tool (“scaffolding”), as well as in the didactic specification of the principle of “verifiable assistiveness”, which defines the boundaries of delegating translation tasks to AI in order to preserve the learner’s regulatory function. The results of theoretical modeling suggest that the integration of AI into the learning process, provided that the student exercises reflective control, creates conditions for reducing cognitive load, stimulating speech-thinking activity, and developing the strategic flexibility necessary for translation work within modern information flows in a corporate setting.

papers.title: PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKING OF EMBEDDED EDGE DEVICES FOR VARIOUS FACE RECOGNITION MODELS
papers.authors: Rasim Mahmudov, SHAHLA URALOVA, Amil Babayev
papers.journal: Journal of Baku Engineering University Mathematics and Computer Science
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) models are increasingly pivotal in enabling face recognition across various fields, from educational and research settings to public spaces.Effective deployment of these models requires high-performance hardware, such as RTX graphics cards or embedded edge devices like Nvidia's AGX Orin and Jetson Nano.This paper presents a comprehensive benchmarking study comparing the performance of these two devices, representing high and low-power edge computing options, using two face recognition models: ResNet and MobileNet.The benchmarking process assesses each model across two different input sizes deployed on both devices with varied configurations, including CPU thread allocation and GPU power distribution within containerized environments.Performance metrics such as inference time, GPU utilization, memory usage, and CPU load are analyzed to determine each device's suitability and efficiency.Additionally, model-specific parameters, including FLOPS, parameter count, and memory footprint, are examined to provide for an in-depth comparison.This paper presents detailed results and analyses of these performance indicators.

papers.title: EEG-Based Depression Detection Using Welch Power Spectral Density Analysis and Transformer Learning
papers.authors: Pratima Singh, Alok Singh Chauhan, Dhyanendra Jain, Ashok Kumar Rai, Palak Gupta, Rajiv Chourasiya
papers.journal: Advance Sustainable Science Engineering and Technology
papers.abstract: Depression diagnosis remains largely dependent on subjective clinical assessments, creating a strong need for objective and reproducible biomarkers. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive and cost-effective solution for capturing neural activity associated with depressive states. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework for automated depression detection using EEG Power Spectral Density (PSD) features estimated through the Welch method. After preprocessing with bandpass filtering, notch filtering, and Independent Component Analysis (ICA)-based artifact removal, PSD features were extracted from the delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands. These spectral representations were then classified using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), and Transformer-based architectures. Experimental results on EEG recordings from 90 subjects (60 depressed and 30 healthy controls) demonstrated that the Transformer model achieved a classification accuracy of 83.78%, with favorable convergence, generalization, and computational efficiency compared with the CNN and RNN models. The findings confirm that Welch-based spectral analysis combined with Transformer learning provides an effective and scalable framework for objective depression detection, with strong potential for clinical decision support and portable mental health monitoring systems.

papers.title: The Evolution of Digital Well-Being Research in the Era of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Mental Health: A Bibliometric Analysis
papers.authors: Parid Rilo Pambudi, Siti Arifah, Nanda Alfan Kurniawan, Nining Maizura
papers.journal: Jurnal Bikotetik (Bimbingan dan Konseling Teori dan Praktik)
papers.abstract: Digital well-being has emerged as a significant area of research amid the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital mental health technologies. To capture the intellectual development of this field, a bibliometric analysis was conducted using publications indexed in the Scopus database between 2020 and 2025. Following the identification, screening, and selection processes based on predefined criteria, a total of 422 articles were included in the analysis. Bibliometric mapping was performed using VOSviewer through publication trend analysis, citation analysis, co-authorship analysis, and keyword co-occurrence analysis to identify publication trends, author productivity, country contributions, subject areas, and emerging research themes. The results reveal a substantial increase in digital well-being publications during the study period, reflecting its emergence as a multidisciplinary research field. The most prominent themes include digital well-being, social media, mental health, psychological well-being, and digital literacy. Network visualization indicates strong interconnections among digital well-being, mental health, social media use, and digital behavior. Furthermore, topics such as smartphone addiction, screen time, internet addiction, emotional regulation, and artificial intelligence have emerged as rapidly growing research themes in recent years. The United States and the United Kingdom were identified as the leading contributors to the literature, while Social Sciences, Medicine, Computer Science, and Psychology constituted the dominant disciplinary areas. These findings highlight that digital well-being has evolved into a multidisciplinary framework integrating psychological, social, health, and technological dimensions, while providing valuable directions for future research and the development of digital mental health practices.

papers.title: Healthy eating or anxious dietary control? Orthorexia, body mass anxiety, and diet-relevant health profiles in older adults
papers.authors: Wojciech Styk, Ewa Wojtowicz, Ewa Humeniuk, Iwona Bojar, Marzena Samardakiewicz
papers.journal: Annals of Agricultural and Environmental Medicine
papers.abstract: Introduction and Objective.Orthorexia nervosa (OrNe) is poorly understood in older adults, in whom dietary control may reflect either adaptive disease management or anxiety-driven restriction.The aim of the study is to examine somatic profiles, psychological predictors, and psychosocial consequences of OrNe in adults aged 60 years or older. Materials and Method.A cross-sectional study included 360 adults aged 60-89 years, classified into four disease profiles: no diet-related disease, metabolic/cardiovascular, strict dietary control, and weight loss/cachexia.Orthorexia, body mass anxiety, health anxiety, nutritional status, depression, well-being, dietary restraint, and psychosocial consequences were assessed.Group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and hierarchical linear regressions were performed.Results.The metabolic/cardiovascular profile showed the highest negative orthorexia, dietary restraint, and fear of weight gain, whereas the weight-loss/cachexia profile showed the lowest nutritional status and the greatest fear of weight loss.In the final TOS-Ne model, self-imposed diet, number of supplements, fear of weight gain, health anxiety, dietary restraint, and lower well-being were independent predictors; medically recommended diet, BMI, and depressive symptoms were not.The final psychosocial-consequence model explained 42.8% of variance, with negative orthorexia, health anxiety, and fear of weight loss as independent predictors.Conclusions.In older adults, pathological orthorexia appears more closely related to health and weight-change anxiety than to objective BMI or depression.Screening should distinguish medically indicated dietary adherence from self-imposed restriction and should consider supplement use, nutritional risk, and psychosocial functioning.

papers.title: More Than a Tool? How AI Design Shapes Customer Responses
papers.authors: Elaheh Saffari
papers.abstract: The first essay is a meta-analysis that provides the first systematic examination of how the AI–human gap in customer responses varies across customer journey stages, and how anthropomorphic design factors moderate this gap at each stage. Analyzing 1,425 effect sizes drawn from 401 studies reported in 129 publications, I document a small but robust baseline disadvantage for AI agents relative to human agents (r̄ = −.140). The gap is largest in pre-purchase stage, where inflated performance expectations amplify disappointment when shortfalls occur, and smallest in post-purchase stage, where lower expectations for AI emotional capability mean that adequate performance can exceed consumer baselines. To explain these patterns, I introduce experience-dimension primacy, a mechanism specifying that cognitive, affective, and social customer experience dimensions shift in relative salience across journey stages, systematically altering how AI agents are evaluated at each point in the journey. Identity cues, form cues, and interaction cues produce pronounced stage-contingent reversals: the same design choice that reduces the AI–human gap at one stage can widen it at another. Taken together, these findings challenge uniform AI deployment strategies and provide actionable guidance for aligning agent design with the dominant experiential dimension at each stage of the customer journey. The second essay examines AI social role design through the lens of brand biography. Firms increasingly deploy AI agents as the primary consumer interface, yet whether their appropriate social role depends on the brand's narrative identity remains unknown. Drawing on the congruity schema, this research explores whether partner-framed AI is congruent with underdog brands and servant-framed AI with top dog brands, advancing perceived congruence as the mechanism and examining perceived power imbalance as an initially proposed mediator, with self-brand connection as a moderator. In Study 1, partner-framed AI produced more favorable responses under both brand biographies, and perceived power imbalance did not mediate. In Study 2, the predicted congruency pattern emerged only among consumers with low self-brand connection, on social experience, satisfaction, perceived congruence, and customer experience, operating through perceived congruence. Therefore, Brand-AI congruency is conditional, holding for consumers without an established brand relationship.

papers.title: A study on 15% trichloroacetic acid peel versus diamond-tip microdermabrasion for acanthosis nigricans of neck - Peel or polish?
papers.authors: Geo Danny, Shreya Srinivasan, Ashok Kumar, B. Laasyaa Reddy
papers.journal: Journal of Cutaneous and Aesthetic Surgery
papers.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate and compare the clinical effects of 15% trichloroacetic acid (TCA) peel and diamond-tip microdermabrasion (MDA) in adults with acanthosis nigricans (AN) of the neck. Material and Methods: This prospective, nonrandomized comparative pilot study included 22 adults with clinically diagnosed AN of the neck (11/group). Group A received 15% TCA peel, and Group B underwent diamond tip MDA. Four treatment sessions were performed at 2-week intervals, with final assessment at week 8. AN area and severity index (ANASI), AN scoring chart (ANSC), patient satisfaction, and adverse effects were recorded. Repeated measurements were analyzed using the Friedman test with Holm-adjusted post hoc comparisons; between-group comparisons used the Mann–Whitney U test. Exploratory mixed effects and final visit regression models adjusted for age, disease duration, body mass index (BMI), and baseline score, as applicable. Results: ANASI decreased from a median of 12 (interquartile range 9–19.5) to 6 (4–6) in the TCA group and from 10 (8–19.5) to 6 (4–8) in the MDA group; within-group change was significant in both groups ( p < 0.001). The median absolute reduction was 8 (5.5–10.5) versus 4 (4–10), respectively, but the between-group difference was not significant ( p = 0.354). The adjusted group by visit interaction was not significant for ANASI ( p = 0.443) or ANSC ( p = 0.091). Satisfaction improved over time in both groups, with no significant between-group difference at the final visit ( p = 0.083). Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation occurred in 2/11 patients receiving TCA and 0/11 receiving MDA ( p = 0.476). Conclusion: Both treatment modalities were associated with improvement over 8 weeks. Although the TCA group showed numerically greater reductions in ANASI and ANSC, the updated unadjusted and adjusted analyses did not demonstrate a statistically significant advantage over MDA. These pilot findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the small, nonrandomized sample and baseline BMI category imbalance.

papers.title: Innovations in higher education: a methodology for the integration of artificial intelligence and pedagogical technologies
papers.authors: Albina Rafisovna Shaidullina, Zaitseva Natalia A., Ishmuradova Alfia M.
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence technologies, particularly generative AI and chatbots, into higher education necessitates a fundamental reconceptualization of the relationship between technological capabilities and pedagogical approaches. This article presents a comprehensive methodology for integrating artificial intelligence and pedagogical technologies (digital pedagogy) into the higher education system, with a specific emphasis on content verification as a critical component for reliable AI implementation. The methodological foundations of this comprehensive methodology are based on research in the fields of educational data mining, predictive analytics, and recommender systems conducted between 2019 and 2025, providing a robust theoretical and empirical basis for the proposed methodological integration. This study synthesizes scientific developments in technical, psychological, and pedagogical research to address the challenge of ensuring the authenticity of educational content while simultaneously developing students’ critical thinking skills. The proposed methodology encompasses a conceptual framework for AI and digital pedagogy integration, a data storage architecture, algorithms for data collection and preprocessing, verification protocols for generated content, and pedagogical strategies for using verification as a learning tool. The practical significance of this research lies in the development of content verification tools and methodological guidelines for the use of AI in higher education institutions.

papers.title: IMPLEMENTASI BAHAN AJAR BERBASIS GAMIFIKASI DAN KECERDASAN ARTIFISIAL DENGAN PENDEKATAN PEMBELAJARAN MENDALAM DALAM MENGEMBANGKAN LITERASI SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR
papers.authors: Husnul Khatimah, Intan Fandini Intan Fandini, M Irmawati, Sulistiyawati Sulistiyawati, Nurpadila Nurpadila
papers.abstract: The integration of gamification and artificial intelligence (AI) into instructional materials offers opportunities to support more interactive reading literacy instruction. This study examined changes in primary school students’ reading literacy after using gamification- and AI-based instructional materials informed by a pedagogical deep learning approach. A quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design was employed. Twenty-one students from one class participated, while paired analyses included 20 students with complete pretest and posttest data. Reading literacy was measured using a 10-item test, with total scores ranging from 0 to 100. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk test, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, paired rank-biserial correlation, and normalised gain (N-gain). Because the difference scores were not normally distributed, pretest–posttest differences were examined using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The mean score increased from 51.05 (SD = 17.99) at pretest to 84.85 (SD = 3.76) at posttest. Posttest scores were significantly higher than pretest scores, W = 0, p < .001. All students included in the paired analysis improved, yielding a paired rank-biserial correlation of 1.00. The class-level N-gain was 0.691, indicating a moderate improvement. These findings provide preliminary evidence of improved reading literacy following the use of the instructional materials. However, the absence of a control group limits causal attribution, and further evaluation using a more rigorous design is required.

papers.title: AI-Powered Adaptive Learning and Smart Education Platform
papers.authors: Pranav Kohad, Rahul Tiwari, Swara Paliwal, Saniya Bante, Tanvi Salve, Madhura Zade, Ms. Shraddha Raut
papers.journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.abstract: Education is becoming increasingly digital, yet many students still face difficulties in understanding complex concepts, remembering long answers, identifying their learning gaps, and preparing effectively for examinations. This paper presents an AI-powered adaptive learning platform designed to provide personalized and interactive learning support. The system uses Artificial Intelligence to explain questions in detail, generate short exam-oriented answers and recall keywords, analyze students' performance, identify knowledge gaps, and recommend suitable learning tasks. The platform also provides 3D visualization for mathematical and geometric concepts, AI-assisted learning for languages such as Marathi and Sanskrit with Hindi and English explanations, AI-based viva examination, instant tests, PDF/notes-based learning, progress tracking, and gamification. The main aim is to make learning personalized, understandable, interactive, and focused on actual student improvement rather than simply providing answers

papers.title: Associations Between Resting-State EEG Delta-band Activity at Selected Parietal Electrodes and Cognitive Changes Following Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment: An Exploratory Analysis
papers.authors: Lei Wang, Huan Ouyang, Jinling Zhang, Xian Lu, Shuai Zhang, Yanan Zhao, Yulong Liang, Lixiao Hao, Yu Wang, Peijing Rong
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transcutaneous auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (taVNS) may improve cognition in Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), but its electrophysiological correlates remain unclear. We explored whether parietal delta-band changes were associated with cognitive changes following taVNS. METHODS: This exploratory secondary analysis included 26 participants with MCI from a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial (taVNS, n = 14; sham, n = 12) who had valid resting-state EEG data at baseline and Week 24. Absolute and relative 1-3 Hz delta power at Pz, P1, P2, and P5 were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA and EEG-cognitive correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. RESULTS: Absolute delta power showed significant time effects at all four electrodes after FDR correction (all q = 0.008). Relative delta power at Pz showed an uncorrected group effect (F = 5.007, p = 0.035; q = 0.218). In the taVNS group, MoCA-B improvement was positively associated with relative delta-power changes at P1, P2, and P5 (r = 0.629-0.652, p = 0.012-0.016), whereas AVLTN7 improvement was negatively associated with absolute delta-power changes across Pz, P1, P2, and P5 (coefficients = -0.418 to -0.613, p = 0.020-0.048). Although these correlations did not reach statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons, they showed a relatively consistent direction across multiple electrodes. DISCUSSION: Relative and absolute delta power may reflect complementary aspects of spectral modulation. The convergent cross-electrode associations provide preliminary EEG evidence linked to cognitive response to taVNS. CONCLUSION: Parietal delta-band power may represent a candidate electrophysiological marker of cognitive change following taVNS in MCI. These exploratory findings support further validation of predefined EEG biomarkers in larger, prospectively powered studies. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: http://www.chictr.org.cn (ID: ChiCTR2000038868).

papers.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Personalize Learning? An Analysis of AI-Based Adaptive Learning Systems for Senior School Students
papers.authors: Manvigas Singh Aulakh, Raghu Raja Mehra
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Most classrooms still move at one speed. A teacher with thirty or forty students has to choose a pace that suits the middle of the class, which leaves weaker students behind and keeps stronger students waiting. AI-based adaptive learning systems promise to change this by watching how each student answers, estimating what that student already knows, and choosing the next task to match. This paper examines how far that promise holds for senior school students. It explains how adaptive systems work in simple terms, reviews findings from major meta-analyses and field experiments, including a randomised study of the Mindspark program in Delhi, and compares adaptive learning with the traditional one-size-fits-all approach. The evidence suggests that well-designed adaptive systems produce real and sometimes large learning gains, with reported effect sizes between about 0.2 and 0.8 standard deviations, and that students who are furthest behind often gain the most. However, the gains depend heavily on how the system is designed and how it is used. Systems that simply give answers can weaken learning, and results shrink when teachers are not involved. The paper concludes that AI can personalise practice, feedback and pacing to a significant extent, but it cannot replace the motivational, social and judgement-based work of a teacher. A blended model, in which AI handles adaptive practice and teachers use the data to guide instruction, is proposed for Indian senior schools.

papers.title: The Human Factor in Cybersecurity: Can Machine Learning Detect Phishing Attempts More Effectively than Traditional Rule-Based Methods?
papers.authors: Manvigas Singh Aulakh, Raghu Raja Mehra
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Phishing emails succeed not because computers are weak but because people can be persuaded. A message that looks like it comes from a bank, a school or a delivery company, and that creates a sense of urgency, can lead even careful users to click a harmful link or reveal a password. The first line of defence is the email filter. Traditionally, filters have relied on fixed rules such as lists of suspicious words and known bad websites. Machine-learning (ML) filters instead learn the patterns of phishing from labelled examples. This paper asks how effectively ML models classify phishing emails compared with rule-based methods. It combines a review of published studies with a small classroom-scale experiment in which a keyword rule filter was compared with three ML models (Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression and Random Forest) on a constructed set of 1,212 emails. On phishing written in a familiar style, all methods performed well, with the rule filter reaching 96.0% accuracy and the ML models 99.6% to 100%. On phishing written in a new, calmer style, the rule filter caught only 8 of 100 phishing emails, while the Random Forest model caught 87 with only one false alarm. The findings agree with the wider literature: ML is clearly more effective and adapts better to new tricks, but it is not perfect, and it does not remove the human factor. A layered defence that combines ML filtering with user awareness is recommended.

papers.title: Occupational Stress and Psychological Well-Being among Seafarers
papers.authors: Bhanu Makala Damodharam
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Seafaring is a demanding occupation characterized by prolonged periods away from home, long and irregular working hours, physical workload, fatigue, confined living conditions, limited shore leave, and reduced social interaction. These conditions can negatively affect the mental and physical health of seafarers and increase their vulnerability to psychological difficulties. The present study aimed to examine the mental health challenges experienced by seafarers and to identify individual, occupational, and environmental factors associated with their psychological well-being. A quantitative, cross-sectional approach was used to examine occupational stress and psychological well-being among seafarers. Information was collected using demographic details and standardized psychological measures. The study focused on occupational stress, psychological well-being, fatigue, sleep difficulties, social isolation, and other factors influencing seafarers' mental health. Descriptive and inferential statistical methods, including correlation, t-test, and one-way ANOVA, were considered for analysis. The findings further indicate that long working hours, poor sleep, extended periods at sea, workload, limited shore leave, separation from family, poor organizational support, communication difficulties, and challenging physical environments contribute to psychological stress. Individual factors such as age, seafaring experience, physical health, BMI, and chronic health conditions were also associated with mental health outcomes. In contrast, resilience, psychological capital, social support, teamwork, supportive leadership, and appropriate organizational resources were identified as protective factors. The study concludes that seafarers' mental health is influenced by the interaction of individual and occupational factors. Mental health promotion in the maritime industry should therefore include stress management, resilience training, adequate work-rest schedules, physical health promotion, supportive leadership, improved communication, and accessible psychological services. Addressing these factors may contribute to improved psychological well-being, work performance, safety, and overall quality of life among seafarers.

papers.title: Who Frames, Who Acts, Who Learns? Allocating Decision Rights for Agentic AI in Graduate Medical Education, Clinical Research, and Clinical Care
papers.authors: Sohail Rao
papers.abstract: Background: Health care organizations are deploying artificial intelligence (AI) agents faster than they are deciding who holds authority over the decisions those agents touch. In June 2026, the MIT Center for Information Systems Research (CISR) published the AI Decision Matrix, which assigns humans and AI to three decision components (frame, act, and learn) along two dimensions: ambiguity and risk. The framework was derived from executives in telecommunications, financial services, manufacturing, and law, and it has not been examined in health care. Methods: We conducted a structured conceptual analysis. We operationalized the two dimensions with health care anchors, assembled an inventory of 18 recurring decisions across graduate medical education (GME), clinical research operations, and clinical care, and classified each decision by quadrant. We then compared the framework’s default human and AI assignments with the accountability requirements of the ACGME, 21 CFR, ICH E6(R3), FDA clinical decision support guidance, the ONC HTI-1 rule, and the EU AI Act. Results: Five decisions were classified as Routine, four as Consequential, four as Exploratory, and five as Strategic. Health care regulation altered the framework’s defaults in two systematic ways. A licensure floor requires a named professional in the act component of 5 of the 18 decisions, including two in which the source framework assigns the act to AI. A learning floor makes outcome ownership a human responsibility in every decision that affects a patient, trainee, or research participant, including Routine ones. We also identified quadrant drift, in which tools introduced as low-risk pilots migrate into high-risk use without reclassification. Conclusions: The AI Decision Matrix offers health care leaders a practical vocabulary for allocating decision rights, but it requires two domain-specific constraints and a reclassification trigger before adoption. We propose an adapted matrix and recommend empirical validation through a modified Delphi study and prospective institutional audits.

papers.title: Interpretable Frequency-Aware Deep Learning for Multi-Class EEG Classification of Neurological Disorders
papers.authors: Chayut Bunterngchit, Laith H. Baniata, Mohammad H. Baniata, Jaffar M. Atwan, Muath Alali, Mohammad Abdallah Alsharaiah, Sangwoo Kang
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) records cortical activity with high temporal resolution without radiation and at low cost, which makes it a practical signal for automated screening of neurological disorders. Deep learning classifies EEG with high accuracy, but most models distinguish only two conditions and give no account of their decisions, which limits their use in screening and decision support. This paper presents SpectraXAI, an interpretable frequency-aware deep learning model that assigns resting-state EEG to four diagnostic categories: Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, schizophrenia, and healthy control. The model filters each EEG window into the delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands and processes every band in a separate convolutional branch with squeeze-and-excitation recalibration. Softmax-weighted band attention and temporal attention then combine the spectral and temporal evidence, and the same attention weights are intrinsic explanations of each prediction. Under a subject-disjoint evaluation protocol that prevents window leakage, the model reached 94.43% accuracy, 96.74% balanced accuracy, and 93.82% macro-F1 on 20,760 windows from 173 unseen subjects while using only 0.10 million parameters. An ablation study confirmed that the attention modules account for most of the improvement over a plain convolutional baseline. Attention weights, feature-attention heatmaps, Grad-CAM, and t-SNE embeddings trace each decision to specific frequency bands, time segments, and learned features, therefore the frequency structure that drives the accuracy also makes the predictions inspectable.

papers.title: Cognitive Authorities in Science Education Classroom: A Nexus Analysis on Inquiry-Based Tasks
papers.authors: Aljon F. Fegurasin, Leonel C. Mendoza
papers.abstract: This qualitative study examined how cognitive authority is distributed, negotiated, and constructed during science learning tasks at Mindoro State University–Calapan City Campus, Philippines. Using nexus analysis, the study investigated an analytical chemistry class involving one teacher and 13 second-year Bachelor of Secondary Education students. Data were collected through observations and audiovisual recordings of two classroom sessions—lecture-discussion and hands-on experiments—and semi-structured interviews with the teacher and five students. Transcribed data were coded using NVivo 15, with analysis focusing on social actions, classroom interaction, and the use of potentially authoritative information sources. Findings revealed that cognitive authority varied with task structure. During lecture-discussion, authority centered on the teacher’s expertise and instructional materials, while hands-on experiments provided opportunities for students to negotiate interpretations through peer exchanges, procedural questioning, and experimental observations. Students drew on teacher-provided resources, prior knowledge, personal experiences, and laboratory evidence, and reported consulting academic journals, websites, and generative artificial intelligence. Interview accounts indicated attempts to corroborate digital information, although verification during work completed outside the classroom was not directly observed. The findings suggest that cognitive authority is relational and shaped by interactions among participants, learning resources, and task demands. The study highlights the importance of designing science activities that combine teacher guidance with opportunities for collaborative reasoning and explicit evaluation of evidence and source credibility. These context-specific insights can inform instructional design and teacher development aimed at supporting student agency and responsible knowledge construction.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Nursing Values: Students’ Perceptions of Trust, Empathy, and Future Roles
papers.authors: Mirela Lika, Eralda Makishti, Alesja Taraj
papers.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly embedded in healthcare systems, creating new opportunities to enhance efficiency, optimize workflows, and strengthen patient monitoring. At the same time, its integration raises important questions about ethics, trust, and the preservation of humanistic values in nursing practice.Aim: To investigate nursing students’ awareness, attitudes, trust, and visions regarding the integration of AI in healthcare and nursing practice.Methods: A descriptive cross‑sectional design was applied, involving 140 nursing students. Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire that explored awareness, attitudes, trust, and expectations regarding AI in healthcare. The analysis combined descriptive statistics with inferential techniques, including correlation and regression, to identify relationships among the variables.Results: Seventy‑two percent of participants had heard of AI in medicine, but knowledge levels were moderate (M = 3.3). While 43% believed AI could support nurses and 66% saw potential for improved patient care, 60% expressed discomfort with AI‑led care. Empathy and human contact were rated as highly important (M = 3.6 and M = 3.7 respectively), and 83% rejected full replacement of nurses. Trust was limited, with only 32% believing AI reduces medical errors. A majority (57%) envisioned a human‑centered future, with AI serving as a supportive tool rather than a substitute.Conclusion: Nursing students recognize the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) but remain cautious, emphasizing humanistic values and expressing skepticism about safety and trust. They envision a human‑centered future where AI supports nursing practice without replacing its essential human role, highlighting the need for balanced integration through education, policy, and further research.

papers.title: System for Describing Large Language Models in Bulgarian
papers.authors: Ivelina Stoyanova
papers.abstract: The growing popularity of large language models (LLMs) over the last five years has produced a large amount of technical documentation and research that are published almost exclusively in English. For low-resource languages such as Bulgarian this creates a twofold gap: a lack of accessible, systematic descriptions of the LLMs in Bulgarian, and a lack of an agreed terminology for the fundamental technical concepts. These gaps impede AI literacy, regulatory compliance under the EU AI-related legislation, and hinder the explainability and understanding of AI concepts by the wider public in general. This paper presents an integrated resource that aims to make the first steps towards addressing these gaps for Bulgarian. The first component is a structured database of LLM descriptions (currently, 424 from more than 30 families), covering open-weight, proprietary, and Bulgarian, Slavic and Balkan oriented models. The description is organised in a Neo4j graph database with information on architecture, training data, training methods, benchmarks, licensing, access conditions. The second component is a bilingual English–Bulgarian terminology dictionary of LLM-related concepts (currently comprising 251 verified entries, of which 94 attested in Bulgarian, and 157 newly proposed) across nine thematic domains. The two components are linked as descriptive nodes in the graph of LLM descriptions carry Bulgarian labels drawn from the dictionary, and any revision of terminology propagates through the database. The resources are released under CC-BY-4.0 license with a web interface in Bulgarian for search and filtering of LLMs. The intended use of the resources is to support research, education, and public engagement with AI in Bulgaria.

papers.title: Beyond Risk: Sexual Health Vulnerability in University Students
papers.authors: Anderson Diaz Perez, Sarith Saray Romero Funieles, Shury Camila Fonseca Castillo, Norka Helena Marquez Blanco
papers.abstract: Aim: To examine multilevel sexual-health vulnerability in higher education and distinguish evidence about knowledge, preventive behaviour, service use and infection-related outcomes. Subject and Methods: The authors conducted a structured critical review of a pre-existing 118-reference bibliography, retaining a publication boundary of 25 May 2026. The reference-based evidence map was documented on 8 October 2026. Sources were classified by population, design and relevance; 38 candidate reports received content-level assessment. Source-linked information and the availability of supporting material were recorded. The review was human-led, with artificial intelligence used as an assistive tool. Results: Thirty-three empirical higher-education reports were charted and 85 references retained as context. The mapped reports comprised 18 cross-sectional analyses, six randomised trials, five other intervention evaluations, three qualitative studies and one participatory mixed-methods study. They described gaps between knowledge and practice, uneven testing and vaccine uptake, and barriers involving confidentiality, stigma and service design. Digital interventions had outcome-specific findings: educational gains did not consistently translate into behaviour or vaccination. Companion reports and mixed denominators precluded summing participants. The documentation supporting many charted fields was limited to abstracts or excerpts. Conclusion: University prevention should connect education and behavioural capability with accessible testing, biomedical prevention and continuity of care. The proposed five-level framework is a service-design and research proposition, not a validated risk score. The bounded bibliography and uneven source documentation limit completeness and certainty.

papers.title: Generative AI-Powered Interdisciplinary Chemistry Practice in Junior High: Exploring Matter Composition and Structure
papers.authors: Zhihua Wang, Xuebing Liu, Fengxiang Chang, Cunzheng Lv
papers.journal: IJCER (International Journal of Chemistry Education Research)
papers.abstract: To address persistent issues in junior high chemistry teaching of Composition and Structure of Substances—including fragmented disciplinary perspectives, highly abstract micro-level concepts, and underdeveloped macro-submicro-symbolic triple representation thinking—this study constructs a four-stage interdisciplinary practical teaching model integrated with generative artificial intelligence (AI) and virtual reality (VR). The teaching practice was implemented in a natural ninth-grade class (N=40) in Zhengzhou. To ensure in-depth analysis of the massive multimodal data generated by AI and VR interactions, purposive sampling was employed to select five representative students as a focus group. Following a single-group pretest-posttest design, data from this focus group were evaluated across four dimensions to systematically measure learning outcomes: macro cognition via concept maps, micro cognition via knowledge cards, model deepening through AI text error correction, and transfer competence and AI literacy via AI chat record coding. Post-intervention data revealed significant improvements across all dimensions. In macro cognition, average concept map nodes increased by 108.8% (from 6.8 to 14.2). For micro cognition, accuracy scores of micro-level tasks surged by 170.0% (from 1.0 to 2.7). Furthermore, the error correction rate reached 88.9% during model refinement, while critical probing questions accounted for 45.83% of total chat records, indicating enhanced transfer and AI literacy. These findings confirm that the generative AI-empowered interdisciplinary model effectively broadens students’ cognitive frameworks, lowers learning barriers of abstract chemical knowledge, consolidates mastery of model-based symbolic representation, and fosters preliminary AI critical literacy. It provides a practical, replicable reference for advancing digital interdisciplinary chemistry teaching at the junior high level.

papers.title: AI in Chemistry Education: A Thematic Narrative Review of Opportunities, Limitations, and Equity Gaps (2020–2026)
papers.authors: Amir Alqahm
papers.journal: IJCER (International Journal of Chemistry Education Research)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has prompted rapidly growing body of scholarship on the role in chemistry education since the public release of ChatGPT in the late of 2022. This thematic narrative review synthesizes 40 English-language sources including empirical studies, curriculum reports, and stakeholder surveys, and systematic/bibliometric reviews published between 2020 and 2026, identified through a structured, author-curated search of recent chemistry-education and analytical-chemistry literature (see Methodology). Sources were coded inductively and organized into six recurring themes: AI/ML literacy as curriculum content; AI-driven tutoring, personalization, and accessibility; empirical evaluations of generative AI's chemical reasoning; stakeholder perceptions; AI's transformation of chemistry research and scientific communication; and equity, ethics, and systemic barriers. Across the reviewed literature, a recurring position though not a formal consensus is that AI should support rather than replace human instruction. Empirical evaluations consistently report that large language models generate fluent but sometimes hallucinated or subtly incorrect chemistry content, particularly for visual and multi-representational reasoning tasks. The corpus is concentrated in higher education and high-income countries, and this pattern should be interpreted as a prominent tendency in the reviewed literature rather than a field-wide finding. Priorities for chemistry educators include critical AI literacy instruction, assessment redesign, teacher professional development, and explicit attention to equity.

papers.title: AI as an Academic Writing Companion:
papers.authors: Tom Muir, Mari Serine Kannelønning
papers.abstract: This Teaching Practice paper documents and reflects on a workshop aiming to infuse rhetorical knowledge into Gen AI prompting. The workshop – “AI as an Academic Writing Companion” – is aimed at PhD candidates and academic faculty. It runs at a large Scandinavian university where English is a second language for most researchers, but is very much the expected language of academic publication. It is easy to be dazzled by the superficial, sentence-level fluency of Generative AIs, especially if one is a novice researcher writing in a second language. This superficial fluency may obscure the AI’s lack of rhetorical principles, however: the AI may lack them, and the researcher may not know the AI lacks them. To combine academic literacy with a critical sense of the capabilities of AI chatbots, therefore, the workshop draws on Moxley’s idea of kairos-based prompting. The aim here is to develop and apply the rhetorical knowledge necessary to guide a bot’s responses; in this way, the workshop combines the needs of researchers for both traditional academic literacies and generative AI literacy. The article describes the prompts and the pedagogy behind them, and our reflections on the development of the workshop.

papers.title: AI-assisted Socratic Questioning for Formal Proof Competence in Plane Geometry: A Literature Review
papers.authors: I Putu Wisna Ariawan, ⁠I Made Candiasa, Ni Made Sri Mertasari, Dewa Gede Hendra Divayana, I Made Sugiarta
