papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) workflows increasingly decompose knowledge-intensive generation into planning, role assignment, subtask execution, and synthesis. Although this structure may support specialization, it also adds coordination and computational overhead. We present a preliminary task-level comparison of a Direct Generation Workflow and a Decomposed Generation Workflow under matched inputs and evaluation conditions. The study covers three grounded knowledge-generation tasks: public-event narrative synthesis, project-grounded research ideation, and scientific related-work generation. Across the evaluated configurations, decomposition produces the largest mean Task Quality Score (TQS) gain for research ideation (+0.053), a smaller gain for related-work generation (+0.025), and only a modest gain for public-event narrative synthesis (+0.013). These improvements require 95.1–126.2 seconds of additional runtime on average. The results provide preliminary evidence that the value of multi-agent decomposition is task-dependent.

papers.title: Bridging the Physicality Gap: Conversational Repair Strategies in AI-Supported Maker Learning
papers.authors: Mahdieh Nazari, Jiqun Liu, Yong Ju Jung
papers.journal: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems, specifically Large Language Models (LLMs), are increasingly used as collaborative problem-solving tools, yet their efficacy in physical environments like makerspaces remains unexplored. This study presents a cross-generational UX analysis of adults and parent-child dyads interacting with conversational AI (Copilot, ChatGPT) during physical engineering tasks. Through episodic qualitative coding of 54 interaction episodes across two multi-layer maker activities (paper roller coasters and squishy circuits), we identify the "Physicality Gap". We introduce the "Prompt Repair Taxonomy", that captures "Context Grounding," "Constraint Reframing," "Granularity Adjustment," and "Logic Interrogation", which demonstrates that while AI excels at text-based ideation, it lacks spatial and material awareness. Users are forced into a high cognitive state of "Critical Verification" to debug AI outputs against physical constraints. Finally, we outline UX design implications for future digital library infrastructures and argue for multi-modal, spatially aware AI interfaces.

papers.title: Classical-Tutor: A Dual-Role RAG Architecture for Classical Document Resources in Digital Libraries
papers.authors: Zishuo Xia, Dan Wu
papers.journal: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
papers.abstract: Classical documents in digital libraries—such as Classical Chinese texts—are not only valuable cultural heritage but also core educational resources at the foundational education level. However, existing digital library systems predominantly focus on full-text retrieval and basic machine translation, making it difficult to support learners' deep cognitive construction. Meanwhile, the direct integration of large language models (LLMs) tends to trap learners in an answer-seeking mode, thereby diminishing the inquiry-based thinking essential to the humanities. This paper proposes and implements Classical-Tutor, an intelligent tutoring system for Classical Chinese digital resources. The system deeply integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a curriculum knowledge graph and introduces a graph-based dual-role dynamic scheduling engine (Dual-Role State Machine). Through a multi-trigger mechanism, the system adaptively switches between knowledge lecturing and heuristic guiding. In an LLM-simulated pilot evaluation the system sustains longer instructional interaction than a baseline RAG system, adapts retrieval granularity to learner profiles, and avoids the deadlocks of static Socratic prompting; the results characterize orchestration behavior rather than learning gains. The study offers an architectural reference for the intelligent utilization of humanities special collections in digital libraries.

papers.title: Real-Time, Context-Specific Educational Metadata Enrichment of Learning Resources on the Web
papers.authors: Ratan Sebastian, Anett Hoppe
papers.journal: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
papers.abstract: Web resources rarely carry the educational metadata that teachers use to judge whether a resource fits their lesson, and dedicated educational repositories that do carry it cover only a fraction of what teachers find through web search. Closing this gap in real time, at the point of search, requires classifiers that are fast enough to run per query and that target a vocabulary specific to the teacher’s curriculum and grade structure, for which labelled training data is scarce. We investigate whether Large Language Model (LLM)-generated labels and paraphrases can train small, fast classifiers for this task. Across nine LRMI-aligned educational metadata properties for STEM education in Lower Saxony, Germany, matching model complexity to property difficulty reaches micro F1 > 0.8 for every property at inference latencies under 15ms, with models compact enough for client-side, browser-based deployment. We report this as preliminary, ongoing work: evaluation for six properties currently relies on LLM-generated labels validated against a 50-page human-annotated sample, and train/test splits do not yet separate resources by website, which we flag as open validity questions for the digital libraries community to weigh in on.

papers.title: Can LLMs Simulate Expert Panels? Evaluating CAT-Inspired Persona Prompting for Automated Creativity Scoring
papers.authors: Peter Organisciak, Maggie Ryan, Mina Ghobadi
papers.journal: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
papers.abstract: Scoring open-ended creativity is expensive. The gold standard for evaluating open-ended creativity responses, including divergent thinking tasks such as the Alternate Uses Task (AUT), is the Consensual Assessment Technique (CAT), where panels of human experts rate creative products. CAT is resource-intensive, limiting the extent to which institutions can measure creativity. Advances in large language models offer an alternative: a CAT-inspired persona panel using large language models (LLMs) as judges to score open-ended responses automatically. Our selected large language models, gpt-5.5, gpt-5-mini, and Claude Haiku 4.5, were assigned expert personas, and we aggregated each model's judgments and compared them against two controls: a self-consistency control using repeated judgments from a single generic judge, and a basic prompted baseline. On gpt-5-mini, the CAT-inspired persona panel improves over a single prompted judge ( r=0.48 to 0.55). It does not outperform the self-consistency control, suggesting that the benefit of the CAT-inspired persona panel is aggregation rather than persona diversity. Accuracy improves substantially with many-shot grounding: supplying many labeled in-context exemplars nearly closes the gap to Ocsai, the fine-tuned reference, while persona diversity adds nothing measurable. For digital libraries and learning repositories that collect open-ended submissions at scale, scalable scoring methods are especially consequential.

papers.title: Enhancing Research Thinking Skills Through Transparent-and-Interactive AI Reasoning
papers.authors: Stella Xin Yin, Zhengyuan Liu, Dion Hoe‐Lian Goh, Wenya Wang, Nancy F. Chen
papers.journal: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
papers.abstract: Research conceptualization involves the process of synthesizing existing knowledge, identifying research gaps, generating novel connections, and formulating testable questions, which is the most cognitively demanding stage of research training. Students struggle in this process, facing difficulties in selecting research topics and generating ideas from multiple perspectives. According to social learning theory, such skills are normally acquired by observing instructors, mentors, or peers work through problems and internalize their research strategies. However, human experts are constrained by individual cognitive boundaries, and one-on-one mentoring is difficult to scale, leaving students with scarce opportunities to observe diverse exemplary thinking. Recent advances in LLMs with reasoning capabilities offer a way to close this gap. AI can serve as a thinking partner whose reasoning processes can inspire human cognitive development. We developed InspAIre, a conversational system that makes AI reasoning visible and interactive during research conceptualization, and evaluated it in two experiments. In Study 1, a within-subject experiment with 72 university students showed significant improvements in research conceptualization performance after observing and interacting with AI reasoning. In Study 2, a between-subject experiment with 76 university students showed that students who observed AI reasoning significantly outperformed those receiving direct AI answers, and that inspiration mediated this effect. These findings suggest that observable AI reasoning and interactive design can effectively enhance students’ research capabilities, transforming AI from answer providers into collaborative cognitive partners in educational contexts.

papers.title: Thinking AI as an inspection system: a laboratory practice for quality management education
papers.authors: M C Porath, Hendrik Mietzner
papers.abstract: Machine-learning-based artificial intelligence (AI) tools are widely applied in industrial visual inspection, especially for flexible and data-driven quality assurance tasks. As a consequence, future engineers must not only be able to use AI-based inspection tools, but also critically evaluate them as measurement and inspection systems. This paper presents a laboratory practice integrated into the bachelor-level course Quality Management and Quality Inspection in the Mechanical and Production Engineering program at Hamburg University of Applied Sciences (HAW Hamburg). In the laboratory, students develop an image-based classifier to distinguish intact from broken chickpeas using smartphone images and a web-based GUI tool for creating custom machine learning (ML) classification models without specialized technical expertise. The concept emphasizes data acquisition, data splitting, training and testing, as well as the influence of data quality on model performance. The educational effectiveness of the laboratory was evaluated through a feedback survey. The results indicate that the laboratory was particularly successful in increasing awareness of the influence of data quality on AI performance and in improving students’ understanding of model evaluation procedures and metrics. The presented concept demonstrates how AI-based visual inspection can be integrated into quality engineering education using minimal infrastructure while promoting a critical understanding of AI-supported inspection systems.

papers.title: Using AI at the FEE CTU Prague for teaching analog electronics, measurements, and instrumentation
papers.authors: Jan Holub
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly penetrating all spheres of human activity, and like any new phenomenon, this expansion can be either beneficial or detrimental. In higher education, the desirable and undesirable uses of AI are particularly important: it can significantly streamline the teaching process by saving time on routine tasks, but it can also devalue teaching if AI is abused as a substitute for knowledge and a deep understanding of the topic. Nowadays, there is a lot of material and information available on the use of AI in programming education or, more generally, in SW-oriented taught subjects. The use of AI for teaching practically oriented subjects, such as Electrical Measurements or Analog Signal Processing and Digitization, is less documented. The Department of Measurement at the Czech Technical University, Prague, has clearly defined rules for using AI in the teaching process, in addition to the university's general rules.

papers.title: Interactive educational platform for sensor systems: integrating environmental monitoring, physiological sensing, and cognitive testing
papers.authors: Kamil Herman, Jakub Svatoš
papers.abstract: This paper presents an interactive educational platform designed to teach the principles of electrical, environmental, and physiological measurements within modern engineering curricula. Developed using the STM32 microcontroller, the system exposes students to the complete measurement chain by combining real-time environmental tracking (CO2, temperature, humidity, pressure) and biomedical parameters with interactive human-in-the-loop applications. In contrast to existing single-purpose educational platforms, the novelty lies in the breadth of an integrated, metrologically transparent measurement chain that students bring to life themselves rather than in any individual sensor. A memory training game based on addressable RGB LED arrays and a reaction time test transition the curriculum from passive data observation to an active-learning framework. Metrological performance is verified through reference testing inside a climatic chamber and custom low-pressure environments, allowing students to diagnose and software-compensate for systematic sensor errors and to evaluate Type B measurement uncertainties directly from datasheet specifications. The proposed system is designed to improve student motivation, deepen understanding of real-time software synchronization, and provide immediate practical feedback on algorithmic correctness and human-machine interface performance.

papers.title: Bots, Trust, and Generative AI: Framing Communicative Agency in a Small-Language Media Context
papers.authors: Mariam Kebadze
papers.abstract: This article examines how bots, chatbots, and generative AI are represented as forms of communicative agency in a small-language media environment. It draws on a mixed content analysis of 195 digital news items published by 1TV.ge, Euronews Georgia, Imedi News, and Rustavi 2 between September 15, 2024, and December 31, 2025, a fifteen-and-a-half-month period spanning parts of two calendar years. Rather than evaluating AI systems technically or measuring audience responses, the article analyzes how news coverage assigns roles to automated and AI-based systems through publication patterns, outlet profiles, dominant frames, functional emphases, trust narratives, risk discourse, media literacy elements, and named AI systems. The corpus was most often organized through a technological or business news frame (93 items; 47.7%). Other frames included myth-nightmare (36; 18.5%), media literacy/fact-checking (26; 13.3%), global political competition/information war (24; 12.3%), and myth-idyll (16; 8.2%). The comparison shows that Euronews Georgia emphasized international and security-related coverage, Imedi News foregrounded education and textual interaction, Rustavi 2 emphasized consumer-facing products and visual applications, and 1TV.ge displayed a comparatively balanced explanatory profile. The article argues that bot transformation is better understood as a change in communicative roles than as a simple replacement of older automation by AI chatbots. In this process, agency, usefulness, trust, risk, and responsibility intersect. The Georgian-language case contributes to Human-Machine Communication, AI-mediated communication, and media-framing research by showing how global AI debates are localized outside dominant English-language media environments. Coding was conducted by a single researcher; an intracoder stability check on 20 items (approximately 10% of the corpus) produced no changes to dominant-frame assignments.

papers.title: The transformative power of artificial intelligence and machine learning in blood banking/transfusion medicine: A vein‐to‐vein approach from blood collection to transfusion services: On behalf of the AABB Foundation
papers.authors: Ruchika Goel, Sheharyar Raza, W. Alton Russell, Jansen N. Seheult, Tho D. Pham, Angelo D’Alessandro, Rounak Dubey, Celina Montemayor, David B. Daniel, Cliff Numark, Brian Custer, Jason Sapia, Tony Casina, Jerry A. Holmberg, Aaron A.R. Tobian, Na Li
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) are poised to transform transfusion medicine across the vein-to-vein continuum, from donor recruitment to recipient outcomes. Large datasets generated from millions of donations and transfusions create opportunities for predictive modeling, precision medicine, improved safety, and operational efficiency. This review outlines key applications of AI in blood banking and transfusion medicine using a comprehensive vein-to-vein framework. METHODS: The review synthesizes perspectives from blood services and hospital-based transfusion practices. Applications are discussed across donor recruitment, collections, testing, inventory management, hospital transfusion services, and education. Finally, AI safety, including ethical, regulatory, privacy, and implementation challenges, is addressed. This is a narrative, non-exhaustive review; given the rapidly evolving pace of AI/ML capabilities, this synthesis should be interpreted as a framework for ongoing surveillance rather than a fixed inventory of applications. RESULTS: Donor-focused applications include personalized recruitment, individualized iron management, and fairness auditing to reduce inequities. In supply chain operations, ML can improve demand forecasting, minimize waste, and optimize inventory. Federated learning may support multi-institutional collaboration without sharing raw data. Omics and genomic applications can enable high-throughput analysis, phenotype prediction, and precision transfusion support for rare blood types and alloimmunized patients. In hospitals, AI can augment hemovigilance by identifying/predicting adverse transfusion reactions, while large language models and retrieval-augmented generation may enhance decision support, patient blood management, and education through adaptive learning. CONCLUSION: AI holds substantial promise to improve transfusion safety, efficiency, equity, and sustainability. Realizing this potential will require robust governance, model validation across diverse populations, privacy safeguards, bias mitigation, reproducibility, regulatory oversight, and human-in-the-loop implementation.

papers.title: Working With AI and Robotic Systems While Preserving Clinical Judgement, Professional Accountability and Person‐Centred Care: Critical Care Nurses’ Perspectives
papers.authors: Tuba Şengül, Dilek Yilmaz Akyaz, Buse Macit Kaplan, Yunus Emre Akyol, Tuğba Cevizci, Melek Demiral, Deema Mahasneh, Noordeen Shoqirat, Holly Kirkland‐Kyhn
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The integration of AI and robotic systems into critical care necessitates examining how ICU nurses preserve clinical judgement, professional accountability and person-centred care while using these technologies. AIMS: To explore ICU nurses' perceptions of AI and robotic systems in critical care, focusing on clinical judgement, trust, responsibility, professional roles and person-centred care. STUDY DESIGN: A qualitative descriptive study using scenario-based elicitation was conducted. Data were collected through seven semi-structured focus group discussions (FGDs) with 38 ICU nurses working in general, paediatric and cardiovascular surgery ICUs in two hospitals in Istanbul City. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by MAXQDA 2024. FINDINGS: Four themes were developed: negotiating trust in AI-supported critical care; preserving human authority, accountability and boundaries; protecting the human core of intensive care nursing; and reimagining AI and robotic systems as supportive partners. ICU nurses evaluated these systems through bedside verification, patient safety, professional responsibility and person-centred care. AI recommendations were useful only when nurses could question, verify, delay or override them according to the patient's current condition. Robotic systems were valuable when they reduced documentation or physical workload, but not when they replaced clinical judgement, emotional presence, reassurance or accountability. CONCLUSIONS: ICU nurses conceptualised AI and robotic systems as acceptable only when clinically verifiable, professionally bounded and subordinate to human judgement. The findings support a model of AI- and robot-supported ICU care that is responsible, human-led and person-centred. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: AI and robotic systems should be implemented in ways that strengthen, rather than replace, nurses' clinical judgement, accountability and bedside presence. Clear protocols are needed to verify AI outputs, define robotic task boundaries, support nurses' authority to question or override recommendations and preserve person-centred care in technologically intensive ICU environments.

papers.title: When AI Moves to the Forefront of Creativity: How Transparent Disclosure Shapes Consumer Acceptance Through Legitimacy Judgments
papers.authors: Dong Lv, Rui Sun, Xuxin Jiang, Qiuhua Zhu, Yue Cheng
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used in brand content production, yet disclosing AI involvement can reduce consumer evaluations of creative work. Existing explanations primarily emphasize ability and reliability judgments, offering only a partial account of negative responses to AI‐related creator cues. Drawing on institutional legitimacy theory, this study develops a context‐specific AI disclosure evaluation framework integrating prior work on legitimacy, the associative–propositional evaluation model, and schema incongruity. The framework proposes that AI disclosure can reduce acceptance by lowering perceived legitimacy, elicit early differential attentional processing, and shape later evaluative integration depending on the work's emotional involvement. Study 1 uses a scenario experiment ( N = 300) and finds that an AI‐generated creative arrangement reduces acceptance through lower perceived legitimacy, alongside a countervailing positive direct effect. Study 2 uses an event‐related potential (ERP) experiment ( N = 27). ERPs are voltage changes time‐locked to stimulus presentation. The AI condition elicits a more negative N1, an early negative‐going component associated with differential attention allocation across work types. Larger P3/P300, a later positive component associated with resource allocation and evaluative updating, and lower explicit acceptance emerge only for highly emotionally involved work. Study 3 analyzes 11,572 Weibo texts and a regression subset of 9175 observations, identifying an analogous association between high emotional involvement and lower levels of acceptance in public discourse. Collectively, the studies shift attention from AI ability to the perceived legitimacy of disclosed creative arrangements and distinguish early cue processing from later context‐dependent evaluation. Perceived legitimacy is the behavioral mechanism tested in Study 1, whereas ERP measures characterize temporal processing differences. The findings suggest that managers should evaluate disclosed AI involvement in relation to the emotional significance of the content and clearly communicate human responsibility; the effectiveness of specific disclosure wording remains untested. Because experimental evidence comes primarily from younger Chinese participants and archival evidence from one Chinese social media platform, generalizability requires further testing across age groups, cultures, creative domains, and platforms.

papers.title: Reference Hallucination in AI ‐Assisted Restorative Dentistry Education: An Educational Risk Assessment Using the Reference Hallucination Score Framework
papers.authors: Esra Yildirim Manav, Sıla Nur Usta
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used by dental students and faculty for literature review, coursework preparation, and scholarly writing. In restorative dentistry education, where evidence-based decision-making is fundamental, inaccurate AI-generated citations may pose educational risks. This study evaluated the bibliographic reliability of AI-generated references in restorative dentistry topics and examined their potential implications for dental education. METHODS: Five large language model (LLM)-based chatbots were tested using ten standardised restorative dentistry prompts representing commonly assigned educational topics. Each chatbot generated 100 references (N = 500). References were manually verified using indexed databases and evaluated using the Reference Hallucination Score (RHS; range 0-11). Chatbot performance was compared using the Friedman test, followed by Dunn-Bonferroni post hoc pairwise comparisons. Binary bibliographic error parameters were analysed using generalised linear mixed models, with chatbot type, prompt complexity, and their interaction as fixed effects and prompt as a random intercept (α = 0.05). RESULTS: A significant overall difference in RHS was observed among the evaluated AI chatbots (p < 0.001), with post hoc analyses identifying significant differences between specific model pairs. ChatGPT-5.2 and Perplexity AI demonstrated the lowest hallucination severity, whereas Copilot and DeepSeek-v3.2 demonstrated the highest. Prompt complexity did not significantly influence hallucination severity. Errors most frequently involved author names, journal titles, and DOIs. CONCLUSIONS: AI-generated references in restorative dentistry demonstrated substantial variability in bibliographic accuracy across the evaluated AI systems. These inaccuracies may pose potential risks to evidence-based learning and academic integrity, highlighting the importance of systematic reference verification and AI literacy in dental education.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and digital technologies in railway systems: a systematic literature review using the TCCM framework
papers.authors: Mukesh Kumar Meena, Gautam Kumar, Rajendra Kumar Meena
papers.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries worldwide, driving digital innovation operational efficiency, safety, reliability and overall sustainability. Additionally, associated technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, digital twins and the Internet of Things (IoT) have further accelerated the digital transformation across railway systems. The literature in this domain is still at a developmental stage and remains fragmented across multiple application domains. This limits the understanding of theoretical foundations, context and methodological approaches. Design/methodology/approach To address this gap, this study conducts a hybrid systematic literature review using thematic analysis of bibliometric data from 121 Scopus records followed by application of the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) framework on a subset of the literature identified through systematic screening based on Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Findings The theoretical and conceptual development in this domain is strongly focused on the themes relating to predictive maintenance, infrastructure monitoring and operational optimisation. Novel technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, digital twins and the IoT emerge as the most frequently discussed technologies in the context of adoption within existing systems. The integrated TCCM analysis identifies three broad trajectories: a technology-integration trajectory centred on digital twins, cyber-physical systems and Industry 4.0/5.0; an algorithmic trajectory centred on AI, machine learning, deep learning and prognostics; and a decision-optimisation trajectory involving multi-criteria decision-making, fuzzy logic and intelligent transport systems. There is a comparatively higher concentration of literature on developed economies. Freight and logistics, despite emerging as an important thematic area, remain theoretically and methodologically fragmented, while emerging economies and several passenger- and sustainability-oriented applications receive limited attention. Methodologically, the literature is dominated by reviews, conceptual frameworks, modelling, simulation and experimental studies, with limited longitudinal evidence on the organisational and strategic consequences of AI adoption. There remains scope for stronger theoretical grounding, focusing on freight logistics, emerging technologies and longitudinal investigations to advance the literature. Originality/value This study provides a structured synthesis of the fragmented literature on AI and digital technologies in railway systems through the TCCM framework. It identifies key research gaps and proposes a future research agenda emphasising stronger theoretical foundations, freight-oriented applications, emerging technologies and longitudinal empirical investigations to support the development of intelligent and sustainable railway ecosystems.

papers.title: ChatGPT adoption and responsible use in Vietnamese transnational education students’ academic writing
papers.authors: Phuong Phuoc-Nguyen Nguyen, Ngoc Hoang Bao Vo, Khoi Van-Thanh Dinh, Khoa Anh Trinh
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines how cognitive and affective factors drive Vietnamese transnational education (TNE) students' intention to use ChatGPT for English academic writing, and investigates how information verification and responsible use enhance English writing proficiency (EWP). Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 501 TNE students across three major Vietnamese cities were analysed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modelling. The conceptual model integrates the technology acceptance model, the pupils’ attitudes toward technology short questionnaire (PATT-SQ) model and Mitcham’s philosophical framework. Insights from an expert survey of six lecturers supported the interpretation and practical implications. Findings Cognitive factors (perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and perceived risk) significantly influence ChatGPT usage intention, whereas affective factors do not. Perceived risk negatively impacts intention, reflecting student awareness of potential drawbacks. The results further reveal a strong behavioural pathway in which frequent use intention promotes information verification, which fosters responsible use and ultimately improves EWP. This demonstrates that learning outcomes depend on critical, ethical engagement rather than usage frequency alone. Research limitations/implications Higher education institutions (HEI) should embed AI literacy, verification practices and ethical guidelines into curricula to optimise ChatGPT utility and mitigate dependency. Limitations include a cross-sectional design, lack of contextual factors and a localised sample, which future longitudinal and comparative studies should address. Originality/value This study offers one of the first empirical examinations linking ChatGPT adoption, verification behaviours, responsible use and measurable EWP gains among Vietnamese TNE students. By integrating cognitive, affective, behavioural and ethical dimensions, it extends traditional technology adoption models to the context of generative AI-assisted academic writing.

papers.title: Evaluation and Comparison of Large Language Models in Answering Frequently Asked Patient Questions on Glaucoma
papers.authors: Barzin Badiee, Mani Eftekhari, Jacob Kanter, Pradeep Ramulu
papers.abstract: PRCIS: ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 demonstrated similar performance in answering frequently asked patient questions. However, limitations in reliability and high reading levels underscore the need for greater oversight and refinement to improve their role in patient education. PURPOSE: This study evaluated and compared the reliability and readability of responses generated by ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 to frequently asked patient questions (FAQs) on glaucoma. The findings aim to elucidate the utility of each model in supporting effective patient education. METHODS: Glaucoma FAQs were obtained from the first 10 questions on Google's "People Also Ask" section. Topics included foundational knowledge, treatment description, lifestyle, and prognosis. Each question was input into ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1, and responses were independently graded for reliability by two glaucoma specialists using a 4-point scale (1=excellent, no clarification needed; 4=unsatisfactory, substantial clarification needed). For further comparison, the top two Google search result webpages for the same queries were similarly graded. Readability grade levels were assessed using validated metrics. RESULTS: ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 received comparable median reliability scores (2.3 [1.6-3] vs. 2.8 [2.1-3], P=0.08), which were similar to scores of top Google webpages (2.3 [1.8-2.7], P=0.18). Both chatbots struggled with questions on foundational knowledge (i.e. falsely suggesting that glaucoma may cause tunnel vision) and lifestyle (i.e. offering unsubstantiated advice on chugging water, dietary recommendations, and screen time). Responses generated by both models were presented at the 8th-12th grade reading level. CONCLUSION: ChatGPT-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 responses were comparable, demonstrating notable limitations in accuracy. Reading levels similarly exceeded average U.S. adult literacy, posing challenges for patient comprehension. Rigorous oversight and targeted refinement of LLMs is necessary to enhance the reliability and accessibility of content for patient education in glaucoma.

papers.title: GROND: Automated characterization of periodic and rhythmic EEG patterns
papers.authors: Jin Jing, Chenxi Sun, Tianyu Zhang, Matthew Byrd, Alexandra-Maria Tăuţan, Lara Basovic, Peter Hadar, Marta Fernandes, Daniel Goldenholz, Jennifer Kim, Aaron F. Struck, Sahar F. Zafar, Michael Brandon Westover
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Periodic discharges (PDs) and rhythmic delta activity (RDA) are common EEG patterns in critically ill patients that require characterization of lateralization, spatial localization, and frequency. Manual characterization is subjective and time-consuming. We present an automated system for all four major subtypes: lateralized and generalized PDs (LPD, GPD) and lateralized and generalized RDA (LRDA, GRDA). Approach. The PD-Profiler combines a per-channel convolutional neural network, hemisphere-specific learned evidence traces, dynamic programming with an approximately periodic prior, and discharge-locked topographic localization. The RDA-Profiler uses iterative narrowband Hilbert refinement for frequency and lateralization, with phase-locking-value analysis for spatial extent. Both pipelines were trained and evaluated on 12,425 EEG segments from 11,729 patients. Main results. Four electroencephalographers independently scored 200 stratified segments per subtype. The algorithm exceeded expert-expert (EE) agreement on LPD frequency (expert-algorithm (EA) ICC 0.931 versus EE 0.897; p<0.001) and was statistically indistinguishable from EE on GPD frequency (EA 0.980 versus EE 0.973; p=0.061), GRDA frequency (p=0.056), LRDA frequency (p=0.435), LPD laterality (EA kappa 0.945 versus EE 0.974; p=0.079), and LRDA laterality (EA kappa 0.961 versus EE 0.993; p=0.269). No attribute fell significantly below the EE ceiling. PD discharge timing achieved an F1 of 0.817 at single-sample precision (mean absolute timing error 3.1 ms). PD spatial localization reached 97.3% of expert inter-rater Jaccard agreement, and RDA spatial extent matched EE agreement. Significance. GROND reaches expert-level reliability across lateralization, spatial localization, discharge timing, and frequency for PDs and RDA. In discordant cases, experts judged its frequency estimates more accurate than the original labels in 94% of cases, supporting reproducible characterization at scale.

papers.title: MTDANet: lightweight multi-scale temporal hierarchy and distance-regularized linear attention network for motor imagery brain-computer interfaces
papers.authors: Binbin Chen, Chen Deng, Huanmin Ge, Xinhua Su, Yanfei Shen
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Motor-imagery (MI) electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive route to brain-computer interaction, yet reliable single-trial decoding remains difficult because task-related patterns are weak, nonstationary, and distributed over multiple temporal scales. This study investigates whether a staged local-to-global model can integrate fine temporal-spatial structure with longer-range context without relying on unrestricted self-attention. APPROACH: We propose MTDANet, an architecture that combines multi-scale temporal-spatial feature extraction, factorized temporal consolidation, and distance-regularized recurrent attention. The model was evaluated on three public MI datasets under subject-specific and leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocols. Separately initialized models were also trained on P300 and steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) datasets to examine broader architectural applicability. Participant-level paired analyses used two-sided paired t tests with within-setting Holm correction. MAIN RESULTS: MTDANet achieved subject-specific accuracies of 85.61 ± 8.32%, 90.85 ± 7.62%, and 87.79 ± 13.93% on BCI Competition IV 2a, BCI Competition IV 2b, and BNCI2014_002, respectively. Relative to the highest-mean baseline, the paired improvements were supported after within-setting Holm correction on BCI Competition IV 2a (3.56 percentage points, adjusted p = 0.0097) and 2b (1.62 points, adjusted p = 0.0168). Under LOSO evaluation, the corresponding accuracies were 63.31 ± 15.74%, 79.77 ± 7.57%, and 79.96 ± 11.95%. The 2.08-point BNCI2014_002 difference had a 95% confidence interval of 0.42-3.73 points and an adjusted p value of 0.0387. These three comparisons did not remain significant in a broader 56-comparison Holm sensitivity analysis. The P300 and SSVEP models attained the highest observed mean accuracies. SIGNIFICANCE: The results provide within-setting evidence for staged local-to-global temporal modeling in offline MI-EEG evaluations.

papers.title: Redesigning organic food markets through value co-creation in Indonesia's agrifood sector
papers.authors: Neneng Kartika Rini, Yosini Deliana, Kunto Adi Wibowo, Lucyana Trimo
papers.journal: NJAS Impact in Agricultural and Life Sciences

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in suicide prevention: promise, peril, and clinical implications for clinical practice
papers.authors: Bénédicte Nobile, Philippe Courtet
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry is progressing rapidly, with promising yet underexplored applications in suicide prevention. While most existing studies have focused on suicide risk prediction, AI could be applied more broadly across the suicide prevention continuum. This review explores AI's potential in improving the detection of suicidal ideation (SI), enhancing clinician training, and expanding patient access to psychotherapeutic support. Studies suggest that AI models may identify SI more sensitively than clinicians by detecting subtle linguistic or semantic cues. Furthermore, AI-based virtual patients have been shown to improve clinicians' confidence and accuracy in suicide risk assessments, particularly when used alongside traditional training methods. On the patient side, CBT-inspired AI tools offer scalable, on-demand support, but most remain unregulated and clinically unvalidated. Despite their perceived empathy and availability, such tools pose ethical and clinical risks. Many patients use AI tools without professional guidance, a trend clinicians often underestimate. This disconnect calls for urgent regulatory oversight and professional engagement. Without clear clinical validation, AI-based tools may evolve outside medical frameworks, exposing vulnerable individuals to preventable harm. Psychiatry must not only adapt but also lead, ensuring that innovation is harnessed responsibly to serve patients with empathy, safety, and scientific rigor.

papers.title: Understanding generative artificial intelligence literacy in higher education: Development and validation of an instrument
papers.authors: Weijie Ma, Fang Yuan, Huiling Luo
papers.journal: Journal of Research on Technology in Education
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly entering higher education, creating a need to assess students’ GenAI literacy (GenAIL). Drawing on existing GenAIL frameworks and related assessment instruments, this study developed and validated the Generative Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale for College Students (GenAILS-CS) as an instrument for assessing GenAIL in higher education. Survey data from 658 undergraduates were split for exploratory (n = 329) and confirmatory (n = 329) factor analyses. Results supported a five-dimensional, 21-item structure covering cognitive understanding, skill application, critical reflection, ethical responsibility, and collaborative innovation. Evidence indicated acceptable-to-good fit, internal consistency, convergent and discriminant validity, positive associations with GenAI use frequency, and measurement invariance across gender and grade level. The instrument could inform diagnostic assessment and targeted GenAIL support in higher education.

papers.title: Metacognition and pathway dynamics in generative AI supported design thinking: A process-sensitive evaluation with network-based cognitive mapping
papers.authors: Chenhan Jiang, Yuanjun Zhang, Rui Huang, Jihong Yu, Tao Shen, Zhuo Wang
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is embedded in design education, yet little is known about how different tools reshape metacognition and the pathways linking ideas to outcomes. We compare three conditions, ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, and a no-AI control, in a virtual reality cultural heritage serious game task with 51 novice designers. Think-aloud, screen recordings, sketches, and AI logs were coded into network-based cognitive maps and event-anchored indicators around metacognitive nodes. Analyses combine expert ratings of design outcomes with thinking pathway profiles and window diversity after metacognitive events. Both GenAI groups show higher mean design-quality ratings than the control, but in complementary ways. DeepSeek broadens early ideation and shows higher novelty ratings, while ChatGPT strengthens metacognitive regulation and structured convergence, aligning with higher systematicity and interactivity. The findings introduce process-sensitive indicators and phase-aware guidance for configuring exploration-oriented and regulation-oriented assistance in human and AI co-creation.

papers.title: Preliminary effectiveness of a culturally adapted Acceptance and Commitment Group Therapy (ACT-G) on weight-related struggles among Malaysian women with overweight or obesity: A randomized controlled trial
papers.authors: Shubashini Mathialagan, Poh Li Lau, Amos En Zhe Lian
papers.abstract: The prevalence of overweight and obesity, particularly among women, has risen significantly, leading to a global epidemic. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) has proven effective in addressing weight-related psychological struggles, reducing weight self-stigma (WSS), and enhancing well-being. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a culturally adapted Acceptance and Commitment Group Therapy (ACT-G) in reducing WSS, experiential avoidance (EA), and body mass index (BMI) among Malaysian women with overweight and obesity. The study employed a randomised controlled trial, including pre-test, post-test, and follow-up test assessments. Sixty-five Malaysian women with a BMI of 23 kg/m2 or above were recruited and randomly assigned to either the experimental group, which received the ACT-G intervention, or the waitlist control group. Non-parametric tests such as the Friedman test, Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test, and Mann-Whitney U test were employed to compare the outcomes of the experimental group with those of the control group. The findings revealed that ACT-G significantly outperformed the waitlist control group in both short-term and long-term measures. Specifically, participants in the ACT-G group experienced greater reductions in WSS, EA, and BMI. To summarize, this study generated positive findings supporting the viability of culturally adapted ACT-G as an effective approach to address weight-related struggles in Malaysia. The intervention aligns with Malaysian values and beliefs and shows promising preliminary efficacy; thus, this is a proof of concept and warrants further study.

papers.title: Behavioral engagement and performance in AI-mediated sales training: evidence from student sales competitions
papers.authors: David E. Fleming, Kristina Harrison, Stefanie L. Boyer
papers.journal: The Journal of Marketing Theory and Practice
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into professional education, limited research has examined how behavioral engagement with AI-mediated practice environments relates to performance. Existing sales research links purposeful practice to performance but largely assumes human-delivered feedback and frequently relies on self-reported practice behaviors. This study examines whether students’ behavioral engagement with feedback-rich, AI-mediated practice opportunities is associated with performance across three sales competition formats. Using Deliberate Practice Theory and Feedback Intervention Theory as complementary interpretive lenses, we analyze platform-generated engagement and performance data from a census of 2,864 participants across three AI-scored sales competitions. Regression results show that greater behavioral engagement is positively associated with higher competition performance, while comparisons based on practice frequency reveal similar performance differences across engagement groups. However, the strength of these relationships varies across competition formats, which differ in task structure and scoring procedures. The results align with expectations derived from Deliberate Practice Theory and Feedback Intervention Theory, while direct tests of their motivational and attention-allocation mechanisms require additional measures of learner goals, feedback engagement, and strategy adaptation. The study contributes evidence about engagement–performance relationships in AI-mediated sales training and offers guidance for designing scalable, feedback-rich practice environments.

papers.title: A new spiral model of AI literacy and competency in higher education developed through a systematic literature review
papers.authors: Zubair Ahmad, Nafilah Abdul Latheef, Almaas Sultana, Nitha Siby, Thomas K. F. Chiu
papers.abstract: This study introduces a new spiral model of artificial intelligence (AI) literacy and competency in higher education. It conceptualizes AI competency as a recursive and multidimensional developmental process that evolves from foundational AI literacy. The model addresses persistent conceptual ambiguity between AI literacy and competency and extends existing static and fragmented frameworks by explaining how competency progressively develops through iterative learning. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic literature review and thematic synthesis of 18 studies identified three major gaps, including conceptual overlap between AI literacy and competency, fragmented framework structures, and limited developmental progression. In response, the proposed model integrates three interdependent dimensions, reflective, dispositional, and practical, within interactive learning environments. Repeated cycles progressively deepen students' critical, ethical, and applied engagement with AI. The model is theoretically grounded in Piaget's Cognitive Development Theory, Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory, Vygotsky's Sociocultural Theory, and Bruner's Spiral Curriculum Theory. Its developmental mechanism is further formalized through the Multiplicative Spiral Gain Function (MSGF), which represents how balanced growth across these dimensions strengthens the transformation of AI literacy into competency. The model provides a foundation for curriculum design, competency assessment, learning analytics, and future empirical validation.

papers.title: Assessing AI-Supported Problem-Solving in Young Adults Reporting Previous Learning-Disorder Diagnoses: Adaptation and Validation of the PS-AIRES and Preliminary Evaluation of a Claude-Based Training Program
papers.authors: Norah Alkhateeb
papers.abstract: AI-supported problem-solving environments increasingly require users to formulate effective prompts, iteratively refine interactions, critically evaluate outputs, and integrate AI assistance into coherent, self-directed solutions. Using a mixed-methods design, this two-phase study involved 672 participants across developmental, validation, and intervention stages. Study 1 included 12 participants in qualitative and cognitive interviewing, 40 independent participants in pilot testing, and 500 participants in the main validation sample. The study developed and psychometrically validated the Problem-Solving Skills in AI-Rich Environments Scale (PS-AIRES) and conducted a preliminary evaluation of a brief Claude-based training program. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a three-factor model comprising Strategic Task Framing and AI Instruction Design, Iterative Prompting and Response Refinement, and Verification, Critical Evaluation, and Integration. The model demonstrated satisfactory fit, high internal consistency, and acceptable temporal stability (ICC = 0.713, 95% CI [0.479, 0.852]). Measurement invariance across gender supported structural stability. A subsequent randomized pretest–posttest study involving an independent sample of 120 young adults reporting a previous specialist diagnosis of a learning disorder preliminarily evaluated the brief Claude-based training program. The findings provide initial evidence for the reliability and validity of PS-AIRES and suggest the short-term usefulness of structured, dyslexia-sensitive AI literacy training for enhancing problem-solving in AI-rich environments.

papers.title: Logic or Emotion? The Impact of Persuasion Strategies on Human-AI Trust
papers.authors: Tianhao Li, Yue QI
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly engage in persuasive and socially interactive roles, understanding how users calibrate trust toward AI versus human persuaders, and how persuasion strategy shapes this process, has become critical for human-AI interaction research. Prior work has examined preferences for human- versus AI-produced content, yet little is known about how persuasion strategy and persuader identity jointly influence trust during interactive communication. This study investigates how logical versus emotional persuasion, delivered by either human or AI sources, shapes two task-specific outcomes in a multi-turn social reasoning context: round-level credibility evaluations and final accept/reject choices. We treat these outcomes as complementary indicators of trust-relevant evaluation and reliance-related choice. We developed an online interaction paradigm in which participants evaluated persuasive messages under varying identity disclosure conditions. The empirical program included two human-participant studies and two exploratory LLM-based extension studies. Across four studies, AI-generated persuasive messages produced under standardized prompting constraints were evaluated differently from human-authored scripted messages under the present task constraints. In the human-participant studies, results showed a message-source-contingent pattern: AI-generated logic-framed messages received higher credibility ratings in several conditions. under explicit identity disclosure, AI-generated logic-framed messages received higher ratings than human-authored logic-framed messages, whereas human-authored emotion-framed messages received higher ratings than AI-generated emotion-framed messages. Under identity ambiguity, differences between AI and human persuaders were attenuated. The exploratory model analyses examined whether the same manipulations produced convergent or divergent output patterns in GPT-4o and Qwen-Max. Both models assigned higher ratings to logic-framed messages; the logic-over-emotion difference was stronger for Qwen-Max, whereas GPT-4o produced a more balanced pattern. These findings provide a structured account of how identity transparency conditions source-strategy fit in trust calibration and offer design implications for aligning AI persuasion strategies with different identity-disclosure contexts.

papers.title: Learner-AI interaction and prompting structures in argumentative continuation writing: a complex dynamic systems analysis of writing-thinking co-development
papers.authors: Hongying Peng
papers.abstract: Guided by Complex Dynamic Systems Theory (CDST), this study examined how Chinese EFL learners’ interaction with generative AI (GenAI) was associated with the co-development of writing quality and critical thinking (CT) in argumentative continuation writing. Thirty-eight learners completed original writing and revised it with ChatGPT, and data included writing products, reflection journals, and interaction logs. Cluster analysis (CA) identified three developmental trajectories: (1) supportive development, with gains in writing quality and CT; (2) competitive development, with substantial CT gains but a slight decline in writing quality; and (3) restrained development, with declines in both domains. Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) further modeled and visualized the distinct learner-AI interaction patterns underneath. Supportive development was associated with a context-oriented prompting structure, emphasizing its connection with instruction and polite language, competitive development with a strong instruction-output connection, and restrained development with a less coherent prompting structure. By making a CDST-informed use of CA and ENA, the study shows that writing-thinking co-development under GenAI mediation was contingent on how learners structured and regulated their interaction with AI. Theoretical, methodological, and pedagogical implications are discussed.

papers.title: Impact of Auditory and Visual Information on Corticospinal Excitability and Vividness in Mental Practice Using Motor Imagery: A Pilot Study in Healthy Adults
papers.authors: Akira Nakashima, Naoki Iso, Toshio Higashi, Akira Sagari, Kengo Fujiwara, Takefumi Moriuchi
papers.abstract: Purpose/Aim: Observation of task-related videos during motor imagery (MI) is frequently incorporated into mental practice as a strategy to enhance imagery vividness. However, the effects of auditory and visual information obtained from task videos on MI generation during complex, task-oriented activities of daily living remain unclear. Materials and Methods: This pilot study of eight healthy adults examined the effects of sensory information from a video of an activity of daily living on MI under four conditions: no information, auditory information, visual information, and combined auditory and visual information. The MI task involved cutting paper with scissors. Corticospinal excitability during MI was assessed using motor-evoked potentials elicited by transcranial magnetic stimulation, and subjective MI vividness was evaluated using a visual analog scale. Results: Corticospinal excitability differed significantly across the four conditions (no information, auditory information, visual information, and combined auditory and visual information); however, post hoc analyses did not reveal significant differences between individual conditions. In contrast, subjective MI vividness differed significantly across conditions, with the combined auditory and visual condition yielding the highest vividness ratings. Visual information tended to facilitate MI more effectively than auditory information. Conclusions: These findings suggest that combining visual and auditory sensory information enhances the subjective vividness of MI during mental practice for activities of daily living. Incorporating task-related sensory information may therefore support more effective implementation of mental practice in rehabilitation, particularly in occupational therapy practice.

papers.title: Positive emotional synchrony and intimacy satisfaction: evidence from a multidimensional assessment
papers.authors: Xinyuan Duan, Juan Hou, Wang Jing, Qingwei Song
papers.abstract: Emotional synchrony, as an expression of emotional coordination and coherence, is an important indicator of the quality of intimate relationships. However, few studies have systematically examined valence-related differences in emotional synchrony and their implications for relationship satisfaction, and multidimensional evidence remains limited. In the present research, we employed a multidimensional assessment approach that combined behavioural coding, self-reports, and electroencephalography (EEG) hyperscanning to examine the predictive role of emotional synchrony in relationship satisfaction and the mediating role of self-other overlap during actual interactions. Study 1 revealed that positive emotions played a dominant role in emotional synchrony and directly and positively predicted males' intimacy satisfaction, with self-other overlap serving as a partial mediator. Using self-reports and EEG, Study 2 revealed that emotional synchrony/interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) directly and positively predicted intimacy satisfaction in men, whereas its effect on women's intimacy satisfaction was fully mediated by self-other overlap. In summary, positive emotional synchrony positively predicts intimacy satisfaction, which provides empirical support for the understanding of the behavioural and neural mechanisms underlying emotional synchrony.

papers.title: Developing a Custom GPT for NGSS-PLUS-5E Lesson Planning in Elementary Science Education
papers.authors: Hye Sun You, Zhu Li
papers.journal: The journal of college science teaching
papers.abstract: Lesson planning is a critical yet time-intensive component of science teaching, especially when teachers must align instruction with the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS) and the 5E instructional model. This study provides a practical guide for developing a custom Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) to support NGSS-PLUS-5E lesson planning in elementary science education. The dataset included 264 qualified elementary life science lesson plans collected from preservice elementary teachers across five academic semesters, along with a standardized lesson plan template and an evaluation rubric. The custom GPT development process involved three phases: data preparation, model configuration and testing through prompt engineering, and user implementation. To examine the quality of the generated outputs, three lesson plans were produced and evaluated using the NGSS-PLUS-5E rubric by two independent raters. Results provided initial proof-of-concept evidence that the generated lesson plans received high scores across four dimensions: organization and quality, NGSS alignment, 5E model alignment, and instructional practices, although some limitations were identified in the depth of elaboration and the variety of instructional approaches. The findings suggest that a custom GPT can serve as a useful co-planning tool for generating structurally complete, standards-aligned lesson plans. However, teacher review remains essential to enrich content and adapt lessons to specific classroom contexts effectively.

papers.title: Digital platforms and innovative models in advancing biology education outcomes
papers.authors: Uus Toharudin, Iwan Kurniawan
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of an integrative multi-platform digital framework combined with active learning models in enhancing biology learning outcomes among secondary students. A quasi-experimental and pre-experimental design was employed involving 180 Grade 10–11 students from three public high schools in West Java, Indonesia. Data were collected through pretest–posttest measures and questionnaires, and analyzed using paired and independent t-tests, N-gain, and descriptive statistics. Results demonstrate significant improvements across key outcomes: motivation and achievement (Wordwall–gamification), reading interest and conceptual understanding (Wattpad–SQ3R), digital literacy and collaboration (PowToon–collaborative learning), science literacy (ChatGPT–problem-based learning), and higher-order thinking skills (YouTube–creative problem solving). This study proposes a preliminary integrative multi-platform pedagogical framework that demonstrates promising potential for enhancing biology learning outcomes across multiple competency domains. Further validation using larger and more diverse educational settings is required before broader implementation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and informal employment: evidence from China’s agricultural transfer population
papers.authors: 刘冠军, Huiying Wang
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is profoundly reshaping labour markets, but its relationship with informal employment remains unclear. This study focuses on the agricultural transfer population (ATP), a major group engaged in informal employment in China. Using data from the China Labour-force Dynamics Survey (CLDS), we systematically examine the association between AI and informal employment among the ATP and explore potential channels. We find that AI is significantly and positively associated with informal employment among the ATP. The observed association is primarily consistent with the job-creation and empowerment channels, while evidence for the substitution channel is insufficient. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that the positive association is more pronounced among female and younger ATP workers and those employed in the service sector. After distinguishing between two types of informal employment, we find that AI is positively associated with informal self-employment, whereas its association with informal wage employment is not statistically significant. In addition, the positive association is weaker among the ATP who have received skill training, particularly those with lower levels of education. This study not only provides new empirical evidence on the relationship between AI and employment structure, but also offers important policy implications for promoting the urban integration of the ATP.

papers.title: Pragmatics-zombies
papers.authors: Erez Firt, Bracha Nir
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper examines theoretical aspects of human-AI communication, arguing that current AI systems, or ‘pragmatics-zombies,’ can mimic human-like pragmatic competence without genuine understanding. While these systems are increasingly adept at natural language interaction, their lack of subjective experience, intentionality, and embodied cognition creates a fundamental trust deficit, particularly in high-stakes scenarios. We argue that forcing human-to-human pragmatic frameworks onto these non-human entities is suboptimal, leading to issues in efficiency, robustness, and transparency. To address this, we introduce the concept of ‘Abstract Pragmatics,’ a general framework that allows for multiple, distinct pragmatic systems. We propose that instead of pursuing flawless mimicry of human communication, research should focus on developing novel, alternative pragmatic systems specifically designed for human-AI interaction. This approach would prioritize clarity, verifiability, and trustworthiness, fostering a more effective and reliable collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence by acknowledging and adapting to the unique nature of the machine.

papers.title: What AI pretends to be?
papers.authors: Kenny K. N. Chow
papers.abstract: Abstract Recent research shows that anthropomorphizing of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, such as virtual assistants or chatbots, affects users’ trust. This paper explores what an AI technology should look like at the interface to facilitate appropriate trust. It proposes an integrated framework based on related work, including Lee and See’s (2004) trust in automation model, Mollerup’s (2019) pretense design, as well as Clark and Fischer’s (2023) notion of depictions, for analysis and design of appearances of AI applications that pretend to be something different. Following the proposed framework, cases of AI applications are analyzed. They span a spectrum of appearances, from humans with open or specifc identities, through talking animals, to plants. Analyses suggest that appearances of AI applications should faithfully reflect the actual ability, characteristics, and design intent, in order to facilitate users’ trustworthiness assessments of the applications. Lastly, design implications and future research are discussed.

papers.title: Addressing trust and distrust in artificial intelligence in newspaper texts
papers.authors: Monika Hanauska, Annette Leßmöllmann
papers.abstract: Abstract Trust in new technologies is often seen as a key condition for their implementation in everyday life, as the aim is for users to utilise technical innovations without strong reservations. The aspect of trust also plays a fundamental role in the discourse on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its far-reaching consequences for people’s lives. In this context, journalistic reporting as part of the public discourse plays a considerable role in creating trust or distrust in AI as a new technology. Whether and how trust issues are addressed in journalistic reporting has not been investigated so far. The paper explores how AI is depicted in German journalistic coverage, covering the topics of autonomous driving and smart home systems, which we expected to generate diverging trust issues. Furthermore, we show how trustworthiness and untrustworthiness are constructed in those texts, choosing AI applications intended for everyday use and therefore relying on trust from users ( Tschopp et al. 2022 ; Gillespie et al. 2021 ). We carried out a qualitative linguistic content analysis on a corpus of German press texts from 2023 that are dedicated to the aforementioned topics. We focused our analysis on explicit and implicit trust communication in the journalistic coverage of AI and examined whether qualitative differences can be identified in the way trust or distrust is addressed in various sub-discourses.

papers.title: AI-Enhanced Data-Driven Approach to Model the Mechanical Behavior of Sustainable Geopolymer Concrete
papers.authors: Rishav Jaiswal, Rajani Gautam, Uday Shankar Yadav
papers.journal: Journal of structural design and construction practice.
papers.abstract: Abstract The growing environmental burden of ordinary portland cement has accelerated the search for sustainable alternatives. Geopolymer concrete (GPC), synthesized from industrial byproducts such as fly ash and slag, is a promising candidate. However, its compressive strength is difficult to predict because numerous mix and curing variables interact in complex, nonlinear ways. This study develops and validates an interpretable machine learning framework for forecasting GPC compressive strength. A curated data set of 350 samples was used, containing eight independent variables, i.e., fly ash, ground granulated blast-furnace slag, NaOH molarity, coarse aggregate, recycled aggregate, curing temperature, curing time, and age of testing, and one dependent variable, i.e., compressive strength. Six models (linear regression, decision tree, gradient boosting, support vector regression, artificial neural networks, and random forest) were trained and optimized. Their outputs were integrated into a stacking ensemble, i.e., the super learner (SL) model, with random forest as the metalearner. Performance was evaluated using R 2 , root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) under 10-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set. The SL achieved R 2 = 0.994 , RMSE = 0.90 MPa , and MAPE = 1.4 % , consistently outperforming all base learners and surpassing results reported in recent studies when benchmarked under comparable variable ranges. Model interpretability was ensured through Shapley Additive exPlanations and permutation sensitivity analyses, which identified curing time, NaOH concentration, test age, and curing temperature as dominant predictors. The novelty of this work lies in demonstrating that a stacking ensemble with transparent feature attribution can markedly improve accuracy and trustworthiness in predicting GPC strength, offering a rapid and nondestructive tool for sustainable mix design optimization.

papers.title: Synthetic spirituality: AI is reshaping religion
papers.authors: Ian McGonigle
papers.abstract: This Comment examines how recent advances in large language models (LLMs) are transforming contemporary engagements with sacred texts, devotional practices, and mystical traditions across multiple religious contexts. As LLMs increasingly mediate spiritual inquiry—by providing instant scriptural explanations, personalised guidance, and simulated access to prophetic or mystical figures—their integration raises urgent questions for scholars of religion, anthropology, and digital humanities regarding authority, interpretation, and religious agency. In this Comment, I propose the framework of synthetic spirituality to describe the forms of religious meaning and experience that emerge through dialogical interaction between human users and LLM systems, in which machine-generated responses become woven into spiritual reflection, practice, and self-understanding. Drawing on examples from world religions, the article outlines the emerging implications. LLMs reshape textual interpretation, pastoral and prophetic roles, and the perceived immediacy of mystical encounter, while also emphasising their limitations—including hallucination, bias, and the gap between increased access to esoteric material and the fidelity of interpretation. Situating the discussion within broader scholarship on digital religion and technological mediation, the Comment argues that synthetic spirituality offers a necessary conceptual framework. Synthetic spirituality illuminates how human–AI interaction is reconfiguring both the experience and study of religion. This underscores the need for critically grounded, cross-cultural research on how authenticity, authority, and meaning are negotiated as spiritual life becomes increasingly entangled with computational systems.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning framework for peptide lead optimization in ultralarge design spaces
papers.authors: Yixiang Mao, Ruibo Zhang, Robert P. Sheridan, Dan Sindhikara, Dipannita Kalyani, Li Xiao, Amy Bittner McCracken, Bryant Kim, Shasha Feng, Tianxiong Mi, Christopher W. Plummer, Jennifer M. Johnston, Liying Zhang
papers.abstract: Abstract In modern peptide drug discovery, the incorporation of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) has become a powerful strategy to improve potency and key developability properties, including stability, solubility, and oral bioavailability. This shift has expanded peptide chemical diversity and design spaces well beyond natural residues, creating fundamental challenges for predictive methods (e.g., quantitative structure-activity relationship modeling) used in lead optimization: limited transferability from natural residues to novel ncAAs, limited interpretability, and poor scalability to ultralarge peptide spaces (>10 50 ). We present PepOpt, an interpretable machine learning framework that unifies molecule-based and sequence-based peptide representations in linear models and exploits dynamic programming to efficiently explore ultralarge peptide spaces. PepOpt achieves high predictive accuracy and interpretability, supports training and inference across diverse ncAAs, including ncAAs absent from the training set whose constituent substructures are represented in the training data. Its linear structure decomposes predictions into residue-specific contributions, enabling systematic optimization without exhaustive sequence enumeration. Notably, PepOpt is inherently capable of multi-parameter optimization without specialized modifications. Together, these capabilities position PepOpt as a valuable platform for prediction, interpretation, ideation, and rapid exploration in ncAA-rich ultralarge peptide chemical spaces, accelerating the rational design of novel peptide therapeutics.

papers.title: From authoring to editing: a competency framework for trainee use of ambient AI clinical documentation
papers.authors: Yash Raka, Reed Van Deusen, Holly Wiberg
papers.abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes have achieved rapid and widespread clinical adoption, with early evidence suggesting trainees derive disproportionate benefit compared to other clinician groups. Yet the outcomes measured so far - documentation time, cognitive workload, clinician burnout - speak to the value of these tools for workforce sustainability rather than for medical education. Physician practice is shifting from authoring clinical notes to editing AI-generated ones, and trainees are inheriting that shift without a defined competency for performing it. Here, we argue that reviewing AI-generated clinical documentation is a teachable competency that current curricula are not yet designed to develop, and that simulation-based education is well-suited to both teach the competency and produce the developmental evidence the clinical literature has yet to produce.

papers.title: Impulsivity, cognitive inflexibility, and brain network dysregulation in etomidate use disorder: A clinical and EEG microstate study
papers.authors: Zhenjiang Liao, Qiuping Huang, Xinxin Chen, Juan Le, Xingmin Wang, Xuhao Wang, Ying Tang, Hongxian Shen
papers.abstract: Etomidate, a short-acting GABA_A receptor modulator and emerging novel psychoactive substance, is increasingly abused non-medically. Despite rising clinical concern, the neuropsychological profiles of etomidate use disorder (EUD) remain poorly characterized, prompting this systematic investigation of its clinical and neurophysiological features. 152 individuals with EUD and 67 age-matched healthy controls (HC) were recruited. Participants completed a series of standardized assessments measuring craving, impulsivity, inhibitory control, and habitual behavior. Resting-state EEG data were analyzed using microstate analysis to characterize the temporal organization of large-scale brain activity, and a multidimensional feature-based support vector machine (SVM) model was built to distinguish EUD from HC. The EUD group exhibited significantly higher craving and impulsivity, and poorer performance on stop-signal and reversal learning tasks. Microstate analysis revealed significantly longer durations of microstates B, C, and D and reduced occurrence of microstate A in the EUD group. SVM classification achieved an AUC of 0.777. This is the first comprehensive characterization of EUD, demonstrating distinct clinical features and alterations in the temporal organization of large-scale brain activity. These findings characterize cross-sectional clinical and neurophysiological features associated with EUD and highlight the potential value of EEG microstate analysis to probe such brain network temporal changes.

papers.title: Operationalizing biological interpretability in health-related visual stimuli using multimodal artificial intelligence as standardized non-human raters
papers.authors: Doruk Ayman, Hatice Ozkan, Deniz Ayman, Özgür Tanrıverdi
papers.abstract: Abstract Evaluation and assessment research in health communication requires structured, construct-based approaches for interpreting visual materials. This study introduces the Asclepius Biological Interpretability Scale, developed through a two-stage modified Delphi process (a joint image-and-item panel followed by an independent item-only panel) grounded in the Biopsychosocial Model and Visual Literacy Theory, and examines whether multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) systems can reproducibly apply this framework relative to internally generated human reference scores. Six artworks (four health-themed and two controls) were evaluated by three multimodal AI models and four researchers (internal human reference) using a standardized protocol with independent researcher-operated accounts, memory-isolation procedures, repeated assessments over two days, and the final 20-item scale. Because Image Type varied across only six stimuli, health-themed versus control differences were summarized at the image level (Cohen’s d), human–AI differences were summarized descriptively at the rater level, and reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Spearman correlations. Within this development image set, AI-generated scores were descriptively higher for health-themed than for control images on the three biomedical subscales (image-level Cohen’s d = 0.91–1.38) but not on Non-Medical Interpretability (d = 0.49); with four health-themed and two control images, these differences were not statistically significant ( p = 0.19–0.60). Reproducibility across researcher-operated accounts was excellent for the three biomedical subscales (ICC = 0.90–0.97) and moderate for Non-Medical Interpretability (ICC = 0.57), whereas agreement across assessment days was poor (ICC = 0.04–0.46). The four researchers’ internal reference scores were higher than the AI-generated scores on the biomedical subscales for health-themed images (mean differences 1.41–1.96 points) and lower on Non-Medical Interpretability (− 2.02 to − 2.19 points). These findings provide preliminary methodological evidence that multimodal AI can reproducibly apply a structured interpretability framework to controlled visual stimuli. Although day-to-day stability and the Non-Medical Interpretability subscale, which showed substantial internal-consistency problems, require further refinement, the results support the feasibility of using AI as standardized non-human raters within controlled methodological settings. Broader validation using authentic health communication materials and independent external human raters remains necessary.

papers.title: Spatial-temporal graph convolutional attentional network for motor imagery EEG classification
papers.authors: Xianqing Yang, Tingting Zhang, Zijian Li, Minghui Hua, Haorong Liao, Ruiqing Li, Zhicong Luo, Han Junfeng, Fan Wang, Guoyu Hu, Xiangzeng Kong
papers.abstract: To address the challenge of insufficient capture of learnable functional connectivity and discriminative spatial-temporal features in motor imagery EEG (MI-EEG) decoding, this paper proposes a Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Attentional Network (STGCAN-MI). The method first explicitly models the functional connectivity and temporal dependencies among electrodes through a learnable dynamic graph convolution module. It then introduces a lightweight parallel spatial-temporal attention module to perform adaptive recalibration of feature responses across channel and time dimensions, thereby enhancing critical discriminative information and suppressing irrelevant noise.
