papers.title: Exploring artificial intelligence usage preferences among medical students in Iran: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Zahra Karimian, Arezoo Molazehi, Manijeh Hooshmandja
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical education, offering opportunities to enhance learning, research, and clinical preparation. Although previous studies have explored medical students’ attitudes and acceptance of AI, evidence regarding their AI usage preferences remains limited, particularly in developing countries where AI integration into medical education is still evolving. Understanding these preferences is essential for designing context-appropriate educational strategies and responsible AI integration. This study aimed to examine the preferences and patterns of AI usage among students at Shiraz University of Medical Sciences (SUMS), Iran. This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among undergraduate and postgraduate students at SUMS. Using stratified random sampling, 384 students were recruited. Data were collected between July and October 2025 using a validated self-administered questionnaire (AI-UPSS; Cronbach’s α = 0.935), assessing AI usage across eight domains. Responses were rated on a 4-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed using one-sample t-tests, independent t-tests, and one-way ANOVA in SPSS version 24, with a cutoff mean score of 2.5. The highest mean preference scores were observed in Research & Writing (Mean = 2.66 ± 0.79, p < 0.001) and Self-learning/Education (Mean = 2.61 ± 0.81, p = 0.010). Moderate preferences were found for Curiosity & Entertainment (Mean = 2.36 ± 0.81, p = 0.001) and Health Counseling (Mean = 2.40 ± 0.96, p = 0.044). The lowest scores were reported in Design & Programming (Mean = 1.54 ± 0.79, p < 0.001) and Art (Mean = 1.68 ± 0.77, p < 0.001). Significant gender differences were observed in Art ( p = 0.010), Self-learning ( p = 0.027), and Health Counseling ( p < 0.001). GPA was significantly associated with Content Development ( p = 0.004), Design & Programming ( p = 0.031), and Art ( p = 0.032), with higher usage among students with lower GPAs. Undergraduate students showed significantly higher preferences across several domains, including curiosity and health counseling ( p < 0.01). Medical students primarily use AI for academic, research, and self-directed learning purposes, while engagement with technical and creative applications remains limited. AI usage preferences are influenced by academic level, gender, and GPA rather than age or field of study. These findings underscore the need for structured, level-specific AI education to promote effective and ethical AI integration in medical curricula.

papers.title: BurnAreaNet: a deep learning method for total body surface area estimation from 2D masks
papers.authors: Hao Wang, Kaize Zheng, Shuaidan Zeng, Yanyan Liang, Zhu Xiong
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of total body surface area (TBSA) is critical for burn diagnosis, triage, and prognosis. It represents the burned area as a proportion of the total body surface area, and is usually expressed as a percentage value. Traditional methods are subjective, while existing computer-aided approaches require specialized equipment or suffer from projection errors. To address these limitations, we constructed MassHumanBurn, a synthetic dataset comprising 5,000 diverse human models with simulated burns across eight TBSA levels, yielding 320,000 rendered views with paired body and burn masks. We propose BurnAreaNet, a neural network that estimates TBSA from frontal and dorsal whole-body and burn region masks. On ground-truth masks, BurnAreaNet achieved a descriptive mean absolute error (MAE) of \(0.55\% \pm 0.49\%\) , substantially outperforming the direct area ratio baseline ( \(1.99\% \pm 1.66\%\) ). To evaluate the impact of segmentation errors, we further constructed SAM_Preprocessed_MHB, where masks were generated using Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2). When masks were generated by SAM2 using box prompts derived from ground-truth masks, BurnAreaNet achieved an MAE of \(0.68\% \pm 0.70\%\) , while the baseline method yielded an MAE of \(2.48\% \pm 3.52\%\) . In a preliminary evaluation on four high-resolution human scan models (HSR_Burn dataset), BurnAreaNet outperformed the baseline on three of four models, while performance was lower for one high-BMI model (BMI 39.1) that may be underrepresented in the training distribution. These results suggest that BurnAreaNet represents a promising step toward rapid, objective, and device-independent TBSA estimation. Future work should incorporate more diverse human model sources, more controllable burn synthesis methods, and support for additional viewpoints to address occluded surface regions, while further validation on real patient data remains essential.

papers.title: Problematic internet use is associated with poorer health behaviours and peripheral serotonin levels in young men
papers.authors: Marta Kożybska, Aleksandra Rył, Natalia Tomska, Grzegorz Raczyński, Paulina Rotter, Iwona Rotter
papers.abstract: Abstract Problematic Internet Use (PIU) negatively impacts psychological, social, academic, and occupational functioning and is associated with unhealthy behaviors such as poor diet, inactivity, and sleep problems. The post-pandemic period has intensified Internet overuse, especially among young men, who are more prone to risky health behaviors. This study aimed to assess the relationship between health behaviors, PIU, and serotonin and dopamine levels in young men. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 325 men aged 18–30 from the West Pomeranian region of Poland. PIU severity was measured using the Internet Use Test (IUT), and health behaviors were assessed using the Health-Related Behavior Inventory (HBI). Blood samples were analyzed for serotonin and dopamine levels using ELISA. Results: 17.7% of participants exhibited high or very high PIU. One-third led unhealthy lifestyles. Higher PIU correlated with lower health behavior scores. The overall HBI score was negatively associated with non-work Internet use during weekdays and weekends. In the low PIU group, healthy eating habits positively correlated with dopamine levels. The linear correlation analysis, after adjusting for age and BMI, revealed a correlation between IUT scores and overall HBI scores, HBI healthy eating habits, and HBI positive mental attitudes. Conclusions: Increased Internet use was linked to poorer health behaviors. These findings underscore the need for interventions aimed at reducing Internet time and promoting healthy behaviors among young men with PIU. Further research should explore neurobiological mechanisms behind these associations.

papers.title: Digital ambition under ecological constraints: Governing AI in climate-vulnerable South Africa
papers.authors: Sibongiseni B. Hlabisa
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is promoted as a driver of development and sustainability. However, its deployment remains embedded in energy-, water-, material-, and land-intensive infrastructures operating under significant ecological and resource constraints. Drawing on environmental policy integration, sustainability transitions, socio-metabolic theory, and socio-ecological-technical systems (SETS) research, the study examines the extent to which environmental considerations are integrated into AI governance. Using qualitative comparative policy analysis, complemented by contextual documentary evidence on South Africa's emerging digital infrastructure, the study identifies a structural governance gap: AI policy has evolved largely in parallel with environmental and infrastructure governance systems. This misalignment limits the state's capacity to anticipate resource pressures, manage infrastructural lock-in, and steer AI deployment toward sustainable trajectories. Rather than proposing new regulatory regimes, the article advances a transition-oriented Green AI governance framework that leverages existing mechanisms for environmental screening and authorisation, sustainable public procurement, infrastructure and resource-capacity planning, resource transparency and disclosure, and institutional coordination. The South African case highlights a broader challenge facing climate-vulnerable contexts, where digital transformation risks outpacing governance capacity. The findings contribute to sustainability transitions scholarship by demonstrating how emerging digital technologies can be incrementally embedded within existing governance systems to align innovation with biophysical limits.

papers.title: How teacher support promotes student engagement in AI-supported English learning?: Mediating pathways through personal best goals and academic buoyancy
papers.authors: Wenya Xu
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how university students learn English, but we still know relatively little about how teacher support is associated with student engagement in AI-supported learning. Drawing on Achievement Goal Theory, this study examined whether personal best goals and academic buoyancy mediated the association between teacher support and engagement. The participants were 774 undergraduate students in China with experience using AI-assisted tools for English learning. We tested the proposed relationships and indirect effects using structural equation modelling and bias-corrected bootstrapping. Teacher support was positively associated with personal best goals, academic buoyancy, and engagement. In turn, both personal best goals and academic buoyancy were positively associated with engagement and significantly mediated its relationship with teacher support. Together, these findings identify two complementary pathways linking teacher support to engagement: self-referenced striving for improvement and adaptive responses to everyday academic setbacks. They also support an Achievement Goal Theory-informed account of engagement within AI-supported English learning.

papers.title: Making the diversity of CCI-related LEADER interventions comparable: A portfolio-to-case approach combining LLM-assisted coding and close reading
papers.authors: Wang Tongjing, André Torre, Maryline Filippi
papers.abstract: The EU LEADER program supports diverse rural local initiatives, which suits Cultural and Creative Industries (CCIs) related activities with their varied forms and place-specific resources. Yet its flexibility also complicates systematic comparison and learning, as portfolio patterns can obscure differences in local organization and implementation, while individual cases can be difficult to situate within the wider range of interventions. This study therefore develops a portfolio-to-case approach combining large language model (LLM)-assisted coding with comparative close reading that support both perspective evidence. We coded 1528 project descriptions in the EU CAP Network Good Practice database across five dimensions, thematic field, challenge, action, actor, and territorial scale. Of the 403 LEADER-tagged projects, 135 were identified as CCI-related. The coded common project types then guided the structured comparison of 56 cases for close reading. In this database selected for dissemination, cultural activity mostly serves wider development purposes. Organizational capacity is central, and it takes a different form in each type: collectively led tourism projects coordinate providers and operate attractions, privately led tourism projects develop offers under enterprise management, heritage projects connect documentation and training with public activities, and social inclusion projects link cultural participation with continuing support. Projects draw on this capacity and can also strengthen it. Project descriptions, however, often omit the organizational work behind the results, and brief reporting on it would improve the database's value for comparison and learning. The approach provides a structured basis for comparing projects and identifying organizational arrangements and resources relevant to adaptation elsewhere.

papers.title: Mobility creates reach, ecosystems determine conversion: Founder educational mobility and international engagement
papers.authors: Angélica Pigola, Bruno Brandão Fischer, Gustavo Hermínio Salati Marcondes de Moraes
papers.abstract: Founder educational mobility is often treated as a channel through which entrepreneurs access non-local knowledge, networks, and opportunities. Yet mobility may not automatically translate into international market engagement. The key insight of our study is that mobility creates potential reach, but sub-regional ecosystems determine whether that reach is converted into international market engagement. We develop ecosystem convertibility, defined as the extent to which local networks, support institutions, and external demand linkages enable firms to transform founder educational mobility into international engagement. Using a 2015–2020 panel of 2260 firm-year observations from 517 technology-oriented firms supported by the Innovative Research in Small Business Program (PIPE) in São Paulo, Brazil, we examine export and import engagement across sub-regional hubs. Logistic models show that founder educational mobility alone does not consistently predict international engagement, whereas its interaction with ecosystem convertibility is positive and significant, especially for export engagement. This result also holds for export engagement when convertibility is recalculated using networks and institutions only, excluding external demand. Descriptive checks show a highly skewed mobility distribution and a low export base rate, so the export results are interpreted cautiously. A machine-learning diagnostic is reported as a secondary predictive check rather than causal evidence. The paper contributes to entrepreneurship research by shifting attention from whether founder educational mobility matters to when and where mobility becomes productive. For practice, the results imply that internationalization policy should strengthen the sub-regional mechanisms that convert mobility into market access.

papers.title: A personalised, occupancy-aware recommendation system for residential shower water conservation using high-resolution smart meter data
papers.authors: Sareh S. Naserizadeh Ghamsari, Rodney Anthony Stewart, Hong Zhang, Khoi Anh Nguyen
papers.abstract: Residential water consumption represents a significant opportunity for more efficient and sustainable urban resource management, with showering accounting for the largest share of indoor household demand. Conventional conservation strategies commonly rely on static population benchmarks that overlook household behavioural variability and demand context, leading to inefficient targeting of conservation interventions. This study develops a personalised, data-driven decision-support framework that transforms high-resolution smart-meter data into adaptive, rule-based water conservation recommendations. Using 180,772 shower events from 203 Australian households, the framework integrates event-level behavioural profiling with non-intrusive occupancy inference, in which density-based clustering of each household's shower events is mapped to a fuzzy occupancy range that preserves uncertainty rather than reducing household context to a single estimate. Adaptive decision thresholds are constructed through a hybrid three-layer mechanism combining household-specific behavioural baselines, occupancy-adjusted scaling, and a data-derived efficiency envelope, enabling equitable recommendation triggering across households with different demand conditions. A recommendation engine then integrates behavioural, contextual, and technical signals, complementing rather than replacing hardware-based conservation measures such as water-efficient showerheads. Occupancy inference placed the verified household size within the inferred range for 90.2% of 61 validation households. A counterfactual simulation that assumes full compliance with every triggered recommendation indicates an analytical upper bound of approximately 21% reduction in total shower volume, concentrated in high-consumption events while routine behaviour remains largely unchanged (3% median duration reduction); about two-thirds of the simulated saving arises from flow normalisation and one-third from duration capping. These savings are simulated rather than observed, and field validation with real users is required before they can be read as achievable outcomes. By integrating behavioural analytics, occupancy-aware contextualisation, and adaptive decision logic within a unified framework, this study advances residential water conservation towards scalable, interpretable, and demand-sensitive interventions that support cleaner production, resource efficiency, and sustainable consumption.

papers.title: Authentic assessment in an AI-integrated qualitative research methods course
papers.authors: Alexander M. Sidorkin
papers.abstract: Abstract Authentic assessment has been a recognized aspiration in higher education for nearly four decades, yet its implementation at the undergraduate level has remained constrained by the procedural demands of professional-level work. Generative artificial intelligence reshapes the implementation calculus by lowering the entry barriers that previously confined authentic assessment to capstone courses, professional programs, and elite institutional contexts. This paper presents a single-semester case study of an AI-integrated qualitative research methods course taught to undergraduates in a child and adolescent development program at a regional public university. Twenty-one students used a custom AI class companion without restriction to produce full-length qualitative research manuscripts. The analytic backbone is a five-dimensional model of authentic assessment, with its physical-context dimension extended to require AI inclusion in fields where professional practice now incorporates the technology. Three rubric-proximal proxy indicators were estimated across the corpus: methods specificity, claim-evidence coupling, and theory-interpretation linkage density. The methods specificity proxy compresses toward the upper bound of its scale, indicating that AI scaffolding supports structural elements of qualitative writing effectively. The two judgment-dependent proxies retain wide dispersion. Process tracing of four contrasting cases identifies three pathways that distinguish stronger from weaker outcomes: criteria-based orchestration, irreducible input supply, and substantive iteration. The boundary-condition pattern indicates that authentic assessment in AI-integrated courses remains diagnostic where it needs to be and is supported where it needed support.

papers.title: Technostress and trust in AI mediate the association between AI adoption and employee well-being
papers.authors: K. D. V. Prasad, Ved Srinivas, Shivoham Singh, Hemant Kothari, Debanjan Nag, Ankita Pathak
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technology adoption alters organizational workplaces, automating tasks and processes, augmenting decision-making capabilities, and changing employees’ perceptions of work. While past research has demonstrated positive effects of AI on productivity and efficiency in organizations, the impact of AI adoption on employees’ psychological well-being is unclear. This study aimed to investigate the impact of AI adoption on employees’ psychological well-being and identify how technostress and trust in AI mediate this relationship. Based on the Job Demands–Resources model, UTAUT2, and Social Exchange Theory, the study developed and tested a hypothesized conceptual model. A cross-sectional survey sampled 499 information technology employees from AI-enabled organizations located in Hyderabad City, India. All proposed relationships were tested using exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and covariance-based structural equation modeling using IBM SPSS 29 and AMOS 28. Results show that AI adoption has a positive impact on employees’ psychological well-being and trust in AI and increases technostress. Technostress negatively impacts employees’ psychological well-being, while trust in AI positively impacts employees’ psychological well-being. Technostress was hypothesized to mediate the relationship between AI adoption and employee well-being negatively. We suggested that technostress as a mediator transmits negative effects of AI adoption through increased technology-related stress. Trust in AI was hypothesized to positively mediate the relationship between AI adoption and employees' well-being by fostering employees' trust toward AI systems positively associated with psychological well-being. Bootstrapping indicated that technostress and trust in AI fully mediate the relationship between AI adoption and employee well-being. The study also examined both negative and positive psychological pathways of how AI adoption can impact employee well-being within one study to provide further insight towards human-centered AI practices and responsible AI governance in organizations.

papers.title: Helpful or harmful? A token-level evaluation of LLM responses to accessibility-oriented educational queries
papers.authors: Sharefah Ahmed Al-Ghamdi, Hend Al-Khalifa, Shahad Al-Khalifa, Srikant Panda, Amit Agarwal, Hitesh Laxmichand Patel
papers.journal: Universal Access in the Information Society

papers.title: Reframing Sustainability Reporting Quality Through Digital Transformation: Insights From a Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Tamara Menichini, José María Fernández-Crehuet, Nicoletta Maria Strollo
papers.journal: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Digital transformation is reshaping sustainability governance by redefining how firms ensure the integrity of corporate disclosures. While prior research has primarily emphasized process efficiency, limited attention has been paid to sustainability reporting quality (SRQ) as a strategic driver of corporate social responsibility (CSR) accountability. This study develops the tech‐quality reporting (TQR) framework, conceptualizing digital reporting as a dynamic organizational capability that enables firms to systematically enhance reporting quality. Through a systematic literature review and qualitative content analysis, the framework explains how digital technologies such as blockchain and artificial intelligence strengthen firms' ability to identify environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks, seize technological opportunities, and transform reporting practices. By aligning technological capabilities with the Global Reporting Initiative reporting quality principles, the study positions SRQ as a strategic lever for credible ESG reporting and long‐term corporate accountability within evolving sustainability ecosystems, thereby contributing to the emerging literature on digital transformation in CSR.

papers.title: Prediction of Motion Acceleration under Newton's Second Law: A Multivariate Linear Regression Approach
papers.authors: Thawatchai Promrat, Dusadee Khamboonrueang, Jantakarn Sangnoi
papers.journal: Suan Sunandha Science and Technology Journal
papers.abstract: One of the most significant lessons in basic physics is Newton’s Second Law of Motion, which teaches the relationship between the acceleration of an object, force, and mass. However, we found that the problem is that some schools do not have enough experimental equipment for students, causing teaching to focus only on theory and the memorization of content. This research aims to predict the relationship between acceleration caused by force and mass using machine learning with a multivariate linear regression algorithm. We have prepared three datasets from laboratory rooms, from image analyses obtained from laboratory rooms with the Tracker program, and from all of those. After that, we will train and compare models for each dataset using linear regression algorithms. The experimental R-squared values are 99% for dataset one, 99% for dataset two, and 97% for dataset three. Therefore, the model provides relatively stable generalization under each individual experimental condition. It can be used as a tool to help predict physics results in situations where real experiments are not feasible due to time, budget, or equipment constraints.

papers.title: Charting dataset: personality and LLM trust scoping review.
papers.authors: Carson CONCEPTION Rodrigues
papers.abstract: Supplementary data for the scoping review "Personality and Trust in LLM Agents: Dependency Evidence, an Empty Behavioural Over-Reliance Cell, and the Personality-Trust Calibration Framework" by Carson Conception Rodrigues and Simran Marian Rebello (Celabe). charting_dataset_supplementary.csv has one row per charted record: the 60 included empirical studies (22 on contemporary generative LLMs) and 2 construct-informing records, with sample, AI-system type, individual-difference measure, outcome measure, charted finding, effect size as reported, and charting confidence. supplementary_material_S1_dataset_S2_reference_log.pdf is the same dataset typeset for reading (S1) plus the reference verification log (S2). Version 2 of the CSV (10 October 2026) cites the published versions of four records first charted from preprints. Preprint of the review: https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/2mdu8_v1

papers.title: Large language models in healthcare: Mapping the global research landscape through bibliometric and science mapping analyses (2022–2025)
papers.authors: Rachel T. Alegado
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed healthcare research by enabling advances in clinical decision support, biomedical text mining, medical education, electronic health record analysis, and healthcare communication. Despite the explosive growth of this research area, a comprehensive understanding of its scientific development, intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, and emerging research directions remains limited. This study provides a bibliometric and science mapping analysis of the global research landscape on LLMs in healthcare published between 2022 and 2025. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using publications indexed exclusively in the Scopus database from 2022 to 2025. Data were analyzed using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny for descriptive bibliometric indicators and VOSviewer for science-mapping analyses, including author cocitation, keyword co-occurrence, overlay visualization, and international collaboration networks. Scientific productivity, citation impact, leading journals, authors, institutions, countries, intellectual structure, conceptual evolution, and emerging research frontiers were systematically examined. The final dataset comprised 12,408 publications from 3,353 scholarly sources involving 51,920 authors and 889,155 references, with an exceptional annual publication growth rate of 176.41%. Scientific production increased exponentially following the introduction of generative AI technologies, demonstrating the rapid diffusion of LLMs across healthcare disciplines. Citation analysis revealed that publications from 2023 achieved the greatest scientific impact, establishing the intellectual foundation of the field. The Journal of Medical Internet Research, Scientific Reports, and NPJ Digital Medicine emerged as the leading publication venues, while the United States and China dominated global scientific production and international collaboration. Science mapping identified three major intellectual communities centered on clinical artificial intelligence, foundation model development, and responsible AI implementation, together with four interconnected conceptual domains encompassing technological foundations, clinical applications, healthcare education, and responsible artificial intelligence. Overlay visualization demonstrated a clear thematic evolution from conventional healthcare AI toward multimodal foundation models, including GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, and Copilot, accompanied by increasing emphasis on clinical implementation, privacy, explainability, evaluation, and trustworthy AI. Healthcare LLM research has evolved into a mature interdisciplinary scientific domain characterized by rapid publication growth, expanding international collaboration, and increasing intellectual integration across artificial intelligence, biomedical informatics, and clinical medicine. The field is transitioning from proof-of-concept investigations toward clinically deployable, ethically governed, and multimodal foundation models. These findings provide a comprehensive overview of the global research landscape and offer valuable evidence to guide researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, funding agencies, and technology developers in advancing the safe, effective, and responsible implementation of Large Language Models in healthcare.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DEVELOPING EFL LEARNERS’ SPEAKING SKILLS
papers.authors: Jasmina Mavlonova Alisher qizi, Xatira GAYBULLAYEVA
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an increasingly important technology in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, particularly in the development of learners’ speaking skills. Traditional speaking instruction may be limited by insufficient classroom time, learners’ fear of making mistakes, and unequal opportunities for individual practice. AI-powered chatbots, conversational agents, speech-recognition systems, and intelligent language-learning platforms provide learners with opportunities to practise English through interactive and personalized communication. This article examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in developing EFL learners’ speaking skills, with particular attention to speaking fluency, pronunciation, vocabulary, grammatical accuracy, willingness to communicate, and confidence. Drawing on recent empirical studies and systematic reviews, the article discusses the potential benefits and limitations of AI-mediated speaking practice. Existing evidence indicates that AI-supported speaking activities can improve learners’ speaking performance and willingness to communicate while reducing speaking anxiety. However, excessive dependence on AI, limitations in speech recognition, restricted emotional interaction, and concerns about learner autonomy demonstrate that AI should complement rather than replace teachers and human communication. The article concludes that the most effective use of AI in EFL speaking education requires purposeful pedagogical integration, teacher guidance, learner autonomy, and opportunities for authentic human interaction.

papers.title: AI-ORIENTED LEADERSHIP AND EMPLOYEE INNOVATIVE WORK BEHAVIOUR: THE ROLE OF PSYCHOLOGICAL EMPOWERMENT AND AI ANXIETY
papers.authors: Qudsia Arshad, Zehra Afreen Sayyid, Ghulam Hussain Wagan
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of artificial intelligence (AI) in organizations has made employee innovation an important concern, yet many employees remain uncertain or anxious about how AI will affect their work. Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, this study examines how AI-oriented leadership influences employees' innovative work behaviour through psychological empowerment, and whether AI anxiety moderates both the relationship between AI-oriented leadership and psychological empowerment and the relationship between psychological empowerment and innovative work behaviour. Data were collected through a three-wave, time-lagged survey of 302 employees working in organizations that use AI-based tools in Pakistan, in the banking, information technology, telecommunications and higher education sectors, and the hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The results show that AI-oriented leadership has a positive effect on both innovative work behaviour and psychological empowerment, and that psychological empowerment has a positive effect on innovative work behaviour and partially mediates the relationship between AI-oriented leadership and innovative work behaviour. AI anxiety weakens the model at both stages, as it reduces the empowerment employees gain from AI-oriented leaders and also reduces the extent to which empowered employees engage in innovative behaviour. The study contributes to the leadership literature by treating AI-oriented leadership as a distinct form of leadership suited to technology-driven change and by explaining how and when it encourages innovation. The findings suggest that organizations should develop leaders who support employees in using AI, give employees autonomy in applying AI to their tasks, and address AI-related fears through open communication and reskilling programmes. Keywords: AI-oriented leadership; innovative work behaviour; psychological empowerment; AI anxiety.

papers.title: Эффективность применения технологий искусственного интеллекта в совершенствовании физической подготовки студентов
papers.authors: Ернур Курмангалиев, Жасканат Сесерхан, Ернур Курмангалиев, Ернур Курмангалиев
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of the modern education system is creating new opportunities in the field of physical education and sports. In particular, the application of artificial intelligence technologies expands the possibilities for monitoring students’ physical fitness, individualizing the training process, analyzing motor activity, and providing timely feedback. The purpose of this article is to theoretically analyze the main areas and pedagogical potential of using artificial intelligence technologies to improve the physical fitness of university students. The study employed methods of analysis, comparison, systematization, and generalization of scientific literature. The analysis of scientific studies indicates that artificial intelligence-based tools can be used to assess motor activity, develop individualized training programs, monitor physical activity, and provide feedback during the educational and training process. In addition, the article addresses issues related to maintaining the professional role of the instructor, protecting personal data, ensuring the reliability of algorithmic assessment, and providing access to digital tools when integrating artificial intelligence into physical education classes. Artificial intelligence is considered not as a replacement for traditional methods of physical education, but as an additional tool that can help take students’ individual characteristics into account and support the instructor’s pedagogical activities.

papers.title: When Spice Meets Pain: Food Image Priming Modulates Somatosensory Processing
papers.authors: Jiejun XIE
papers.abstract: This OSF repository contains the materials associated with the manuscript “When Spice Meets Pain: Food Image Priming Modulates Somatosensory Processing." The repository includes anonymized behavioral data, processed ERP data, analysis scripts, stimulus information, and codebooks used in the reported analyses. The study examined how supraliminal and subliminal spicy food image priming modulates behavioral and electrophysiological responses to painful and non-painful electrical stimuli. Raw EEG data are not publicly shared because of data-size and ethical restrictions, but may be made available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request and subject to institutional approval.

papers.authors: Sanyukta Kadam, Dr Saurabh Haral

papers.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Replace The Ophthalmologist In Patient Education? A Comparative Analysis In Blepharitis
papers.authors: Audrey Talley Rostov, Yumna Busool, Shirin Hamed Azzam, A/Prof. David  Lockington, A/Prof. Joshua C Teichman, Artemis Matsou, A/Prof. Clara C  Chan, Elad Shvartz, A/Prof. Michael  Mimouni, Daniel Bahir

papers.title: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Student Risk Prediction in Educational Data Mining
papers.authors: Akshay Kumar, Neha Gulshan, Varun Amrit
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Sciences and Modelling
papers.abstract: Early identification of academically at-risk students in higher education enables targeted pedagogical interventions and attrition mitigation. While traditional Educational Data Mining (EDM) techniques leverage temporal clickstream data and demographic features from Learning Management Systems (LMS), interaction logs are commonly treated as isolated numerical counts without accounting for the topological organization of course materials. This study presents KG-Predict, a multimodal predictive framework for early student risk detection. KG-Predict constructs a Course Knowledge Graph connecting course modules, assessment entities, and Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) resource types, extracting topological descriptors that are combined with early clickstream records and assessment submission trajectories from the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD; N = 32,593). Empirical evaluations indicate that augmenting behavioral logs with structural graph descriptors and initial assessment scores improves predictive performance, achieving an AUC-ROC of 0.8472 and an accuracy of 76.67% at Week 6 of an academic term, compared to 0.7902 AUC-ROC and 71.25% accuracy for the baseline machine learning model. Module-level evaluation indicates consistent performance across diverse curricular disciplines, achieving AUC-ROC scores between 0.6886 and 0.8790. This framework provides an observable, structured basis for early risk tracking in academic advisory dashboards.

papers.title: Upper Limb Rehabilitation Exoskeletons Based On Pneumatic Actuation: A Short Comprehensive Review
papers.authors: Omama Salim, Mithaq Nama Raheema, Jabbar Salman Hussein
papers.journal: Al-Noor Journal of Engineering Management and Computer Science
papers.abstract: The importance of using robots as an assistant in the physical rehabilitation process, which was physically demanding for therapists, required a lot of time and depended on the health condition of patients, became the main objective of the current paper. In particular, the comparison of different approaches to rehabilitation and actuation strategies and actuation systems used for upper-limb robotic rehabilitation devices with special attention to pneumatic actuation systems became the aim of this research. The comparison was conducted based on the analysis of the characteristics, actuation strategy, advantages, and disadvantages of these systems from 2020 to 2026. As a result, every actuation system and rehabilitation approach had its peculiarities and practical applications. The importance of pneumatic actuation was due to its flexibility, safe human-robot interaction, shock absorption, and lightweight. However, its nonlinearity remained the main disadvantage.

papers.title: A Case Study of GenAI in Higher Education: Problems, Concerns, Responses, Opportunities, and Possible Innovation
papers.authors: Scarlett Kelly, Rocci Luppicini
papers.abstract: GenAI has brought rapid, multidimensional changes to many domains. However, there are uncertainties regarding the disruptive technology and its ripple effects, particularly in higher education. The purpose of this research is to understand the current approaches and strategies of GenAI in universities. To answer the research question, “What approaches are currently applied to incorporate ChatGPT usage into higher education,” this research conducted twenty interviews with executives, managers, and staff who worked in change and IT/IM capacities at a Canadian university and reviewed GenAI policies and guidelines from 22 Canadian universities. The findings helped identify underexplored areas in the literature and promoted innovative thinking about real problems in higher education and next steps in GenAI adoption.

papers.title: Understanding English News Literacy and Digital Communication Through the Study of Headlines and Reports with Machine Learning and Data Visualisation
papers.authors: Dipika Gautam, Subodh Kumar Yadav
papers.journal: International Journal of Sciences and Innovation Engineering
papers.abstract: In today’s digital world, most people get their news from online sources. But they often only read the headline and skip the full report. This makes the language of headlines very important. If a headline is too difficult, readers may not understand it and may not click on it. This study looks at how English news headlines use language and how that affects news literacy. We collected 40 English news headlines from popular sources like BBC, CNN, The Guardian, The Hindu and The Times of India. These headlines cover five areas: Education, Technology, Environment, Social Issues and Business. We used readability scores, word count and sentiment analysis to study them. We also used a machine learning model to classify headlines as simple or complex. The model gave 87.5% accuracy. We made six charts to show our results. The charts include readability distribution, category-wise comparison, word count distribution, sentiment pie chart, scatter plot and confusion matrix. Our results show that 45% of headlines are difficult to read. Environment news is the hardest. We also found a strong negative correlation between headline length and readability. This means longer headlines are harder to understand. This study shows how machine learning and data visualisation can help us understand news language better. It can help journalists write headlines that more people can understand.

papers.title: Students’ Engagement with Artificial Intelligence, Metacognitive Reading Strategies, and Academic Achievement: A Correlational Study of Grade 12 STEM Learners in Valencia, Bukidnon
papers.authors: Philip Brillo, Jenyliza T. Ucang
papers.journal: Psychology and Education A Multidisciplinary Journal
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in education raises questions about how AI use interacts with students’ metacognitive reading strategies and academic performance. This descriptive-correlational study examined relationships among engagement with AI tools (EAIT), metacognitive awareness of reading strategies (MARS), and academic achievement (AA) for 155 Grade 12 STEM students at Valencia National High School, Valencia, Bukidnon. Respondents completed validated survey instruments; data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression. Results indicated high EAIT (M = 3.65) and MARS (M = 4.24) levels, with outstanding AA (M = 94, SD = 1.77). Correlational analysis showed a significant positive relationship between EAIT and MARS (r = .322, p = .001) and between MARS and AA (r = .233, p = .003), whereas EAIT and AA were not significantly correlated (r = −.115, p = .152). Regression results revealed that behavioral engagement with AI negatively predicted academic achievement (B = –0.494, p = 0.017), whereas awareness of global reading strategies positively predicted achievement (B = 0.782, p = 0.002); the model accounted for 8.0% of the variance (R² = 0.080, F = 6.616, p = 0.002). These findings highlight the predictive relevance of how students engage with AI and apply metacognitive reading strategies to academic achievement, with higher behavioral AI engagement associated with lower predicted achievement and higher global reading-strategy awareness with higher predicted achievement. Educators should scaffold strategic, self-regulated use of AI in reading instruction to promote goal-setting, monitoring, and evaluation to support comprehension and academic outcomes.

papers.title: Digital Transformation and the Ethics of Professional Responsibility: A Maqāṣid Al-Sharī‘Ah Perspective
papers.authors: Irfan Udin
papers.abstract: Digital transformation has reshaped the professional landscape through the increasing use of artificial intelligence, big data, and social media, while simultaneously generating ethical challenges, including technology misuse, privacy violations, and disinformation. This study aims to examine the role of professional codes of ethics in addressing digital ethical challenges through the perspective of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah. Employing a qualitative approach, the study combines a literature review with case analysis, including the scandal involving the Community Vocational Training Center (Balai Latihan Kerja Komunitas/BLKK) of the Islamic Scholars Association (PP) in Pekalongan City. The findings indicate that professional codes of ethics function not merely as normative instruments governing professional conduct but also as mechanisms for protecting public welfare in accordance with the objectives of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah, particularly ḥifẓ al-‘aql (protection of intellect), ḥifẓ al-māl (protection of wealth), ḥifẓ al-‘irḍ (protection of dignity), and ḥifẓ al-nafs (protection of life). The implementation of professional codes of ethics through strengthened digital ethics literacy, professional oversight, and technology-responsive regulatory reform can prevent harm, enhance accountability, and sustain public trust. The findings of this study contribute to proposing the integration of professional codes of ethics with maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah as an adaptive ethical framework for strengthening professionalism in the digital era.

papers.title: DEVELOPING STUDENTS’ METACOGNITIVE COMPETENCE THROUGH GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS
papers.authors: Zayriddinova Yodgora
papers.abstract: Modern higher education requires graduates who are able to manage their own learning independently, critically and responsibly. This ability is described by the concept of metacognitive competence, which includes knowledge about one’s own cognition and the regulation of learning through planning, monitoring and evaluation. The growing availability of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools offers new means of supporting these processes, but it also raises the concern that learners may delegate their thinking to the machine. This paper examines how GenAI tools can be used to develop students’ metacognitive competence. Drawing on Flavell’s theory of metacognition, Zimmerman’s cyclical model of self-regulated learning and the principle of scaffolding, the study identifies the functions that GenAI can perform in relation to each component of metacognition, describes a sequence of pedagogical techniques for their implementation, and discusses the main risks and ways of reducing them. The paper concludes with recommendations for teachers and higher education institutions.

papers.title: METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING STUDENTS’ METACOGNITIVE COMPETENCE THROUGH GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN TEACHING ENGLISH
papers.authors: Zayriddinova Yodgora
papers.abstract: Metacognitive competence, the ability to plan, monitor and evaluate one’s own learning, is a key condition for successful and autonomous English language learning. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot are widely used by students, but when they are used simply to obtain ready-made answers they may weaken rather than develop learners’ self-regulation. This article presents a methodology for improving students’ metacognitive competence through GenAI based on a five-phase cycle (Plan, Prompt, Monitor, Evaluate, Reflect) and a three-stage model of gradually fading scaffolding.

papers.title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERACTIVE METHODS IN TEACHING FOREIGN LANGUAGES IN THE ERA OF MODERN TECHNOLOGIES
papers.authors: Dilshod Norxidirov
papers.abstract: This article examines the use of interactive teaching methods in foreign language learning in the modern digital era. It focuses on the role of Artificial Intelligence, Gamification, and the Flipped Classroom model in improving students’ language skills and communicative competence. The article also highlights the benefits of digital tools in the learning process. However, it emphasizes that teachers’ guidance, communication, and personal support remain important for successful language learning.

papers.title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HUMAN COGNITION, SPEECH PERCEPTION, AND AI TECHNOLOGIES
papers.authors: Barotovna Davlatova Rukhsora
papers.journal: Central Asian Journal of Academic Research
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed the ways in which language is generated, processed, interpreted, and used in educational communication. This article examines human speech and language perception from a psycholinguistic perspective, focusing on the cognitive mechanisms underlying speech production, comprehension, contextual interpretation, and meaning construction. It compares major principles of human linguistic activity with the text-generation capabilities of large language models and discusses the implications of AI-assisted communication for higher education. Particular attention is given to critical thinking, independent writing, cognitive engagement, linguistic competence, and academic integrity. The study employs a theoretical and analytical methodology based on established psycholinguistic theories and international guidance on generative AI in education. It argues that AI-generated linguistic output should not automatically be equated with human understanding and that educational applications should be designed to support rather than replace learners’ cognitive and communicative activities.

papers.title: EFFECT OF AI-POWERED SKILLS ON LEARNING OUTCOMES OF ND/HND ACCOUNTANCY STUDENTS IN FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING IN WAZIRI UMARU FEDERAL POLYTECHNIC, BIRNIN KEBBI
papers.authors: SULEIMAN MUHAMMAD YAURI
papers.journal: International Journal of Business Economics and Management Science
papers.abstract: This study examined the effect of AI-powered skills on learning outcomes of ND/HND Accountancy students in Financial Accounting in Waziri Umaru Federal Polytechnic, Birnin Kebbi, Nigeria. The study adopted quasi-experimental research design of pre-test post-test non-equivalent control group. Two research questions and one null hypothesis guided the study. The population comprised 210 ND II Accountancy students offering ACC 211 (Financial Accounting I) in 2024/2025 academic session. A sample of 60 students was selected using purposive sampling and assigned to experimental group (30 students) and control group (30 students). The experimental group was taught Company Accounts and Final Accounts using AI-powered skills such as ChatGPT for explaining accounting concepts and adjustments, Microsoft 365 Copilot in Excel for automated preparation of Trial Balance, Trading, Profit and Loss Account and Balance Sheet, and Grammarly for audit report writing. Control group was taught using conventional lecture method. The instrument for data collection was Financial Accounting Achievement Test (FAAT) consisting of 30 multiple choice and theory questions covering Company Accounts, Final Accounts, Depreciation, Provision for Bad Debts, Accruals and Prepayments. FAAT was validated by three experts (2 Accountancy, 1 Measurement and Evaluation) and reliability of 0.82 obtained using Kuder-Richardson 20 (KR-20). Mean and standard deviation were used to answer research questions while t-test was used to test hypothesis at 0.05 level of significance. Findings revealed that experimental group had higher post-test mean score of 68.45 (SD=8.21) than control group mean of 51.20 (SD=9.45), with mean gain of 34.25 for experimental and 17.40 for control. The t-test result showed t-calculated of 4.87 greater than t-critical of 2.00 at degree of freedom 58, p<0.05, indicating significant difference. Therefore, AI-powered skills significantly improved learning outcomes of ND/HND Accountancy students in Financial Accounting. It was recommended that lecturers should integrate AI tools into teaching of financial accounting and other accounting courses such as Cost Accounting and Taxation. Workshops should be organized for Accountancy lecturers on AI integration.

papers.title: Risk Factors Associated with Hair Loss Severity Among Female University Students: A Cross-Sectional Questionnaire-Based Study
papers.authors: Roaa Mohammed Jabbar, Dr. Rusul Mahdi Abid
papers.abstract: Hair loss is a frequent health problem of women and can have an adverse impact on physical appearance, body image and quality of life. Its development has been attributed to a number of demographics, lifestyle and clinical factors, but which factors have the greatest influence on its development is unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between the demographical, lifestyle and clinical parameters with hair loss severity among female university students. A cross-sectional study was conducted among female university students', and data collected using a structured questionnaire, and statistical analysis was performed using chi-square, one-way ANOVA and Tukey post hoc test via SPSS v.26. Hair loss severity showed a strong association with age, marital status, psychological status, physical activity and length of sleep (P = 0.038, P = 0.008, P < 0.001, P < 0.001,and P = 0.020, respectively). No significant association was established with family history (P = 0.345) or BMI (P = 0.210). Participants with severe hair loss had lower hemoglobin and vitamin D levels (P = 0.010 and P < 0.001, respectively) than those with mild or moderate hair loss. Psychological stress, physical inactivity, poor sleep patterns, decreased hemoglobin and vitamin D levels were all found to be significantly correlated with increased severity of hair loss among female university students. The results underscore the need to consider modifiable lifestyle and nutritional-related risk factors as a component of comprehensive management and prevention of hair loss.

papers.title: The impact of generative artificial intelligence on clinical decision-making and patient safety: A narrative review
papers.authors: Chelsya Rafaela Brito Santiago, Christianni Di Lorenzo, Adeagna Bento Laborda, Rebeca Raabe Sena Noronha, Vitor Borges Zonta, Ana Paula Lima da Costa, Katherine Tatiana Coronel Montenegro, José Henrique Nascimento Nobre, Isabella Tinoco Rodrigues, Ana Beatriz De Oliveira Gonçalves, Marcos Gabriel Flores, Talles Cayna Araújo Graça Da Silva, Felipe Fornazari Nunes, Luana Palhares De Barros, Isac da Silva Monteiro
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), in the form of large language models (LLMs), has entered clinical practice faster than the evidence on how it changes clinical decisions could be produced. The relevant question is therefore no longer whether these models hold medical knowledge, but whether their use makes clinicians' decisions better and patients' care safer. This narrative review examines the evidence on the impact of generative AI on clinical decision-making and patient safety. In evaluations of encoded knowledge, a medically aligned model gave answers that agreed with scientific consensus in 92.6% of cases, against 92.9% for clinicians. In diagnostic reasoning, a model optimized for diagnosis outperformed unassisted clinicians on challenging cases and improved the differential diagnoses of the clinicians who used it, whereas a randomized trial of a general-purpose chatbot found no significant improvement in physicians' diagnostic reasoning, although the model alone outperformed both physician groups. In management reasoning, physicians assisted by GPT-4 scored 6.5 percentage points higher than those using conventional resources. When tested on real patient data in a simulated clinical workflow, however, LLMs diagnosed less accurately than physicians, did not follow guidelines and were sensitive to the order and quantity of information. The safety literature identifies four recurrent hazards: fabricated content, with hallucination rates of 50% to 82% when prompts contained a false clinical detail; misjudgement of clinical acuity, with drafted patient messages judged to pose a risk of severe harm in 7.1% of assessments; automation bias, by which clinicians adopt the model's assessment in place of their own; and the reproduction of racial and gender stereotypes. Only about 5% of published evaluations used real patient care data. Taken together, the evidence supports generative AI as a supervised aid to clinical reasoning rather than as an autonomous decision-maker, and indicates that its safety depends as much on the design of the human–AI interaction as on the accuracy of the model. Practical safeguards for clinical use are also reviewed.

papers.title: The Impact of Information Disclosure Consistency on IPO Pricing Efficiency: Evidence from China’s A-share Market
papers.authors: Ruyi Shen
papers.abstract: The core of the comprehensive registration-based IPO reform is information disclosure. However, traditional single-period static textual analysis is limited in identifying ex ante over-packaging and strategic disclosure by IPO firms driven by financing incentives. Using IPO firms listed on China’s A-share registration-based boards from 2019 to 2025 as the sample, this study applies the TF-IDF algorithm and cosine similarity model in natural language processing to quantify intertemporal textual consistency between prospectuses and the first annual reports after listing, and empirically examines its effect on IPO underpricing. The results show a significant negative association between information disclosure consistency and IPO underpricing: the lower the ex post observed textual consistency, the higher the underpricing compensation required by investors. This conclusion remains robust after employing an instrumental-variable approach to alleviate endogeneity concerns. Further tests indicate that, after additionally controlling for secondary-market sentiment noise measured by post-listing first-month turnover and information-environment factors proxied by analyst coverage, the coefficient on information disclosure consistency remains significantly negative. This finding suggests that intertemporal textual consistency has independent pricing value in restraining IPO underpricing and does not merely reflect short-term secondary-market noise. Further analysis reveals a substitution effect between internal corporate governance and information disclosure consistency in reducing IPO underpricing, and this effect is more pronounced in market segments with higher information asymmetry. The study provides quantitative evidence and policy implications for regulators to introduce regulatory technology for penetrating textual scanning, for IPO firms to maintain long-term honest disclosure, and for investors to avoid pricing risks.

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Foreign Language Learning Process
papers.authors: Khatira Mammadova
papers.journal: Global spectrum of research and humanities.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been rapidly evolving, especially the advent of Generative AI and large language models, which opens up new avenues in the field of foreign language learning. With the help of AI-powered tools, students can receive instant feedback, custom practice, interactive dialogue, vocabulary help, writing support, pronunciation practice, and access to language-learning resources outside of the classroom. Meanwhile, issues have surfaced about misinformation, overreliance on AI-generated answers, concern over plagiarism, reduced independent language output, and the undermining of critical thinking skills. The aim of the present article is to explore the impact of artificial intelligence on foreign language learning in terms of language skills, self-regulated learning, motivation, and feedback. A comprehensive review of recent peer-reviewed articles, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant research, situated in the context of the Azerbaijani educational environment, was carried out. The research reviewed suggests that AI assistance can have a positive impact on speaking, writing, vocabulary development, feedback, and engagement within pedagogically relevant learning activities. The evidence is not the same across the four language skills, however, and positive perceptions by learners should not necessarily be taken as evidence of subsequent language learning. The results also show that learner autonomy in an AI-supported environment is not just about having access to technology; it takes AI literacy, critical evaluation, self-regulation, and the learner's independent use of the target language to develop. The article concludes that artificial intelligence can serve only as an aid to learning and cannot replace learners' effort, human interaction, or the guidance of the teacher.

papers.title: An Integrative Model Based on Artificial Intelligence for Enhancing Integration among Sciences in Interdisciplinary Learning and Scientific Research: A Field Study on Postgraduate Students at the Libyan Academy – Janzour
papers.authors: Asma Billayl
papers.abstract: The recent rapid advancement in artificial intelligence technologies has brought about a fundamental transformation in higher education and scientific research institutions by providing new opportunities to enhance interdisciplinary learning and cognitive integration across various scientific fields. This study aimed to propose an integrative model based on artificial intelligence to analyze the impact of using AI tools in enhancing interdisciplinary learning and scientific research among postgraduate students at the Libyan Academy–Janzour. The study adopted the descriptive-analytical approach, and data were collected from a sample of (94) master's and doctoral students using a questionnaire specifically designed for this purpose. The reliability test results indicated that the study instrument possessed a high degree of reliability, with a Cronbach's alpha coefficient of (0.912). The results of the descriptive analysis indicated that the sample members possessed a high level of digital competence, with a mean score of (3.92) and a standard deviation of (0.64). The findings also revealed a high impact of using artificial intelligence tools on improving the quality of scientific research and research productivity, with a mean score of (4.15) and a standard deviation of (0.58), in addition to a positive role in enhancing interdisciplinary integration, with a mean score of (3.88) and a standard deviation of (0.71). Furthermore, the results of the inferential analysis showed no statistically significant differences in the participants' attitudes toward the proposed model attributed to academic specialization (F = 1.42, p = 0.241) or academic level (t = 0.85, p = 0.398), which confirms the applicability of the model across various specializations and academic levels. Additionally, the findings revealed a strong, statistically significant positive correlation between digital competence and interdisciplinary research integration (r = 0.684, p < 0.001), indicating that developing digital skills directly contributes to enhancing students' ability to employ artificial intelligence tools in producing more integrated and interdisciplinary research. The study findings confirm that artificial intelligence represents an effective tool for supporting interdisciplinary integration, improving scientific research efficiency, and facilitating knowledge exchange and academic collaboration across different disciplines. This study also contributes to enriching the scientific literature related to the employment of artificial intelligence in higher education and provides a practical framework that can be utilized in developing smart academic environments that support interdisciplinary learning and scientific research.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in International Arbitration: Procedural Fairness, Transparency, and the Future of the Arbitrator's Role
papers.authors: Muhammad Amal Atta
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used more and more in international arbitration for legal research, document analysis, translation, drafting, transcription and other case management functions. Arbitral institutions and professional bodies have mostly responded with soft-law guidance, while national courts are starting to confront the professional and adjudicative risks of hallucinated authorities and inadequate human verification. This article questions the extent to which current international arbitration law can accommodate material use of AI without undermining the personal decision-making mandate of the tribunal, procedural fairness, confidentiality and enforceability of awards. It takes a doctrinal and comparative approach, analysing the New York Convention, the UNCITRAL Model Law and Arbitration Rules, contemporary institutional rules and AI guidance, as well as recent national adjudicative materials from the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and India. The article draws a distinction between AI for administrative or organisational assistance, and AI for evidentiary analysis, substantive legal reasoning, drafting of reasons and autonomous decision-making. It points to the possibility that existing technology-neutral arbitration instruments can accommodate a large portion of low and medium risk assistance, but that the autonomous or insufficiently supervised use of AI may implicate existing requirements relating to the right to be heard, tribunal mandate, agreed procedure, confidentiality and recognition or enforcement. The right regulatory response is a risk-based approach to regulation that emphasises human accountability, independent verification, calibrated disclosure, data-security safeguards and institutional procedural guidance. The article considers the nature of national court guidance as a form of comparative evidence, rather than a source of direct arbitration law, and explores the circumstances in which additional institutional or UNCITRAL level guidance might be justified.

papers.title: Xodimlarni boshqarishda raqamli texnologiyalardan foydalanish samaradorligi
papers.authors: Gavhar Xayrulla qizi Sodiqova
papers.abstract: The article examines the effectiveness of digital technologies in employee management from theoretical and practical perspectives. The relevance of the study is determined by the transition of organizations toward more agile, data-driven and responsive human resource management models. The study applies systematic literature review, comparative analysis, content analysis and synthesis. The findings indicate that HR information systems, people analytics, digital recruitment, digital performance management, online learning and artificial intelligence tools can improve the speed and accuracy of HR processes and the quality of managerial decisions. At the same time, insufficient digital skills, data privacy risks, algorithmic bias and resistance to change may reduce the expected benefits. The author proposes an integrated set of indicators for evaluating the effectiveness of digital employee management.

papers.title: LEVERAGING ICT AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN STUDENT RECORDS MANAGEMENT IN NIGERIAN UNIVERSITIES
papers.authors: YIDOUGHA ESIDO (Ph.D), Biokuromoye Fyneman, Amadis Gloria
papers.abstract: This study focuses on the role of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in student records management in Nigerian Universities. Student records are critical to the admission and registration process, to course enrolment, for the processing of examinations, to academic progression and graduation, to the production of student transcripts, to institutional decision making, and beyond. But in a lot of Nigerian universities, records retrieval, storage of files, loss of files, duplication of records, inaccurate data entry, lack of reliable electronic system of access etc., continue to plague many universities in Nigeria. A qualitative Integrative Review Method was used in the study, which involved a literature review on relevant research on the use of ICT in electronic records management, education management information systems and emerging applications of AI in higher education. The review demonstrates how ICT tools such as databases, student-information systems, online portals, cloud storage, scanning technologies and electronic document-management tools can enhance the rapidity, accuracy, security and accessibility of student records as well as their preservation. AI can also assist with intelligent document classification, optical character recognition, duplicate-record detection, automated enquiries, and anomaly identification and predictive academic analysis. However, these technologies are currently limited by low levels of funding, unreliable electricity, poor internet connectivity, dated equipment, lack of employee training, low levels of interoperability, and a lack of organizational readiness or concerns about cybersecurity. The study also found that it is not just a matter of providing hardware and software to enable successful technology-driven records management. It requires institutional commitment, skilled personnel, reliable infrastructure, data-governance policies, interoperability, regular maintenance, cybersecurity safeguards and compliance with data-protection requirements. The paper makes a number of recommendations, including the creation of integrated student-information systems, ongoing training for registry and ICT staff, the implementation of unique student identifiers, the systematic digitisation of paper records, and the careful and supervised use of AI.

papers.title: Generative AI and Workforce Transformation: Developing an AI-HRM Framework for Employee Productivity in Deposit Money Banks Operating in Rivers State
papers.authors: Obibhunun Lucky, Usoro Lawrence Bassey
papers.abstract: The increasing adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) is transforming the nature of work, employee roles and human resource management practices across organisations. Deposit Money Banks are particularly affected because their operations involve extensive information processing, customer interaction, documentation, decision support and knowledge-intensive activities. However, the extent to which Generative AI contributes to employee productivity may depend on how effectively organisations manage workforce transformation. This study examined the relationship between Generative AI and workforce transformation and proposed an AI-HRM framework for improving employee productivity in Deposit Money Banks operating in Rivers State. The study specifically examined the relationships between Generative AI and employee reskilling, job redesign, human–AI collaboration and employee productivity. A cross-sectional correlational research design was adopted. Data were collected from employees of selected Deposit Money Banks operating in Rivers State using a structured questionnaire. Reliability was confirmed using Cronbach’s Alpha coefficients above 0.70. Out of 344 questionnaire administered, 300 usable copies were retrieved and use for the analysis with the aid of SPSS version 27.0. The findings suggest that Generative AI should not be viewed merely as a replacement for human labour but as a technology capable of augmenting employees’ capabilities and transforming the way work is organised and performed. The study therefore proposed an AI-HRM framework based on AI readiness, Generative AI adoption, employee reskilling, job redesign, human–AI collaboration and productivity improvement. The study concludes that Deposit Money Banks can achieve greater productivity benefits from Generative AI when its adoption is supported by appropriate HRM practices, continuous employee development and effective human–AI collaboration. The study contributes to knowledge by providing a context-specific AI-HRM framework for managing workforce transformation and improving employee productivity in Deposit Money Banks operating in Rivers State.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) IN PUBLIC HEALTH CARE POLICY AND COMMUNICATION IN PLATEAU STATE: CHALLENGES AND PROSPECTS
papers.authors: Yusuf Pyelshak, Gonam Samuel Irimiya, Azi E.J., Bala Yakubu Ngwan, Nathaniel Iliya Pam, Joshua Moses Gonzwal, Gyang Beatrice Daniel
papers.abstract: Technological Advancement in Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redesigning healthcare communication worldwide, a key aspect of enhancing public health. This study analyzed current health communication policies to bring out areas where AI-driven approaches are yet to be addressed. In Plateau State, integrating AI into health communication policies brings both opportunities and hurdles. The study examined how AI can increase health communication initiatives in Plateau state, particularly through AI tools that enhance the spread of health messages, patient education, and public awareness campaigns. The study highlighted setbacks in implementing AI technologies, including limited infrastructure, inadequate data management, and a shortage of skilled professionals. The paper also presented the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to transform health communication. It suggested policy guidelines to support its integration while reducing risks. Additionally, it recommended policy changes, training, and cooperation among stakeholders to leverage AI's power in health communication. In Nigeria, the outlook for AI in health communication is optimistic, assuming focused investments in technology, training, and regulatory reforms.

papers.title: NAVIGATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND RELIGIOUS AUTHORITY IN NIGERIA: RECONFIGURING RELIGIOUS KNOWLEDGE, LEADERSHIP AND TRUST IN THE DIGITAL AGE
papers.authors: CANON CLINTON ONYEKACHI OKORIE, Chukwunonyerem S. O. Ukachukwu, GODSENT CHUKWUALUKA NWOSU, OKORO UGONNA OGECHUKWU
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming part of religious education, communication, research and everyday faith practices. Believers can now use generative AI to explain sacred texts, compare interpretations, prepare devotional materials and seek answers to religious questions without first consulting a recognised religious leader. This development raises an important question for Nigeria: how is religious authority changing when access to religious information is no longer controlled mainly by clergy, scholars and religious institutions? This paper examines the relationship between AI and religious authority in Nigeria, focusing on religious knowledge, leadership and trust. Using a conceptual and interpretive methodology, it synthesises scholarship on religious authority, digital religion, AI ethics and Nigerian religious experience. It argues that AI is not simply replacing religious authorities; rather, it is reconfiguring the conditions under which authority is produced, accessed, evaluated and trusted. Nigerian digital-religion research shows that digital infrastructures can create new forms of religious influence and authority, while recent AI scholarship highlights concerns about accuracy, privacy, bias and human accountability. The paper proposes a Responsible Religious AI Engagement Framework based on human accountability, verification, contextual sensitivity, confidentiality and formation. It concludes that Nigerian religious institutions should neither reject AI nor surrender religious judgment to it. AI should remain an assistive instrument while theological discernment, pastoral responsibility, communal recognition and human dignity remain central to religious leadership.

papers.title: AI-Based Travel Recommendation Systems: Personalizing Tourist Experiences through Preference Modeling and Real-Time Behavioral Analytics in Nigeria
papers.authors: Osinubi O.B, Adigun O.I, Matthias Omotayo Oladele
papers.abstract: The rapid digitalization of tourism has increased the demand for intelligent recommendation systems capable of delivering personalized travel experiences that adapt to users' evolving preferences and contextual circumstances.Conventional tourism recommendation platforms predominantly rely on static filtering mechanisms and explicit user ratings, often producing generic recommendations that fail to reflect dynamic travel behaviors and real-time contextual information.This study presents the design, development, and evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based travel recommendation system that integrates explicit user preferences, implicit behavioral analytics, contextual awareness, sentiment analysis, and machine learning techniques to enhance personalized tourism experiences in Nigeria.Adopting a mixed-methods research design within a Design Science Research (DSR) framework, the study combines quantitative surveys, behavioral data acquisition, system development, and experimental evaluation.Tourist demographic information, browsing history, clickstream behavior, geo-location data, travel reviews, and contextual variables were collected and preprocessed through data cleaning, normalization, feature engineering, and sentiment extraction before model training.The proposed hybrid recommendation engine combines collaborative filtering, content-based recommendation, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and contextual recommendation algorithms to generate adaptive travel suggestions based on continuously evolving user interactions.Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the hybrid model outperforms conventional recommendation approaches, achieving superior recommendation accuracy, ranking quality, user engagement, and satisfaction.The incorporation of explainable AI mechanisms and ethical data governance further enhances transparency, user trust, and responsible AI

papers.title: From Awareness to AI Readiness: Artificial Intelligence Literacy, Gendered Barriers, and Future Opportunities For Women in Higher Education
papers.authors: Ikhlas Ahmad, Mohammad Zafar Ayat, Rabiya Khatoon, Alok Gardia
