papers.abstract: The aim of this study is to identify the relationship between advertising realism, AI disclosure, the human likeness of AI avatars, perceived creepiness of AIgenerated ads and customer trust and brand loyalty.Primary data were gathered using a structured questionnaire on 103 social media users of India, and analysed by using chi-square test, one-way ANOVA and linear and multiple regression, the Baron and Kenny procedure, Sobel test and a bootstrap to check the mediation.The factors of human likeness (β = 0.76), realism (β = 0.16) and disclosure (β = 0.11) all significantly contributed to the variance in perceived creepiness, accounting for 82.6% of the variance.Contrary to the hypothesis, creepiness did not negatively influence the customer trust (β = -0.05,p = 0.614), but positively (β = 0.39, p < 0.001) influenced brand loyalty.Trust strongly predicted loyalty (β = 0.58, R² = 0.34).Contrary to the usual role of mediation, creepiness was a suppressor rather than a classical mediator: realism and human likeness increased creepiness, which, in turn, was associated with higher trust, to some extent counteracting their direct negative impact on trust.The results indicate that, for this sample, discomfort with AI-driven adverts that resemble humans has not led to any decrease in trust or loyalty, and that trust is the primary pathway to loyalty.Advertising agencies must navigate the moral and ethical landscape of AI-generated content with great caution, as consumers are growing increasingly aware of these new methods as AI tools raise the bar for the ethics and morality of advertising Keywords: "AI disclosure", "customer trust", "brand loyalty", "perceived creepiness", "ai-advertising". Review of LiteratureThe impact of Generative AI in advertising on consumer trust, acceptance, purchase intention and brand responses have been shown in previous literature.Key drivers that have been identified are AI realism, perceived eeriness, personalisation, privacy concerns, and transparency.AI generated content can be creepy and potentially detract from trust, as evidenced by some findings.The gen Z Indian consumers are a mix of curiosity and suspicion when it comes to AI-powered ads.The theoretical anchor is the uncanny valley hypothesis (UCH) proposed by Mori (1970) and Mac Dorman and Ishiguro (2006) which suggests that artificial figures will be uncomfortable when they are close to but not identical to a human.From the relational perspective, Morgan and Hunt's (1994) commitment-trust theory of relationships places trust as a key antecedent of commitment-based outcomes, such as loyalty outcomes, to support H2.There remains a significant lack of research on the connection between AI creepiness, customer trust and brand loyalty. papers.title: The Role of AI-Powered Search in Shaping Consumer Search Behaviour: An Empirical Study among Students in Private Universities in AP.
papers.authors: Shaik Abdullah, Mazharunnisa
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
papers.abstract: This study examines the role of AI-powered search in shaping consumer search behaviour among students in private universities in Andhra Pradesh. AI-powered search tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and Perplexity are changing how users find, evaluate, compare, and use information. The study focuses on students’ awareness and usage of AI-powered search, its influence on information-search habits, perceptions of usefulness, convenience and relevance, trust and verification of AI-generated information, and its effect on product and service comparison and purchase-related decision-making. A quantitative, descriptive, cross-sectional research design was used. The empirical analysis was conducted using 84 valid questionnaire responses collected via Google Forms. The collected data were analysed using frequency and percentage analysis, mean and standard deviation, Cronbach’s Alpha, Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The study provides insights into changing consumer information-search patterns in the AI era and offers useful implications for digital marketers seeking to adapt content, search visibility, and consumer-engagement strategies to AI-mediated search environments.

papers.title: AI in Mergers and Acquisitions Due Diligence: A Study of Perceived Artificial Intelligence Capability and Outcomes Among Finance Professionals
papers.authors: Chalasani Rushi Ram Chowdary, Ajay Kumar Varshney
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
papers.abstract: Due diligence is among the most information-intensive stages of a merger or acquisition, and artificial intelligence is increasingly proposed as a means of accelerating it and improving its quality. Evidence on how practitioners connect AI capability with specific due-diligence outcomes remains limited. This study investigates how finance and M&A professionals relate perceived AI capability to perceived efficiency, accuracy and risk identification in due diligence. Drawing on task–technology fit theory, the study uses an exploratory, cross-sectional survey of investment banking and M&A professionals. A structured five-point Likert questionnaire was analysed with reliability analysis, Pearson and Spearman correlations and sensitivity analyses, and the results were contextualised against published industry evidence. The study distinguishes perceived effectiveness from objectively measured performance and examines how consistently perceived capability is associated with each outcome. Based on these insights and the wider literature, the paper proposes a five-stage framework for governed, human-verified AI-assisted due diligence, covering task-fit screening, data readiness, AI first-pass analysis, human verification, and governance and performance measurement. The paper contributes to research on AI in M&A and technology fit, and offers investment banks, advisers and technology providers a practical basis for responsible AI adoption and a foundation for future empirical testing.

papers.title: PawSense_AI Assistant
papers.authors: BHUVANA B, D NEHA, RAMYA M A, TEJAS S M, Manohara Gowda
papers.journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence in everyday applications has created opportunities to improve access to pet-care information and support pet owners in making informed decisions about animal health and well-being. This paper presents PawSense AI, an AI-powered pet-care assistance system designed to provide accessible, interactive, and personalized support to pet owners through a web-based platform. The proposed system integrates generative artificial intelligence, image-based pet assessment, voice interaction, and location-based veterinary search within a unified interface. Users can interact with the system through natural-language queries, upload pet images for preliminary AI-assisted observations, and access information about nearby veterinary facilities. The application incorporates user authentication and database-supported conversation management to maintain individual accounts and chat histories. Voice transcription and multilingual response options further aim to improve accessibility and ease of interaction. The system is developed using Python and the Flask web framework, with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the user interface, database technologies for information management, and external AI and mapping services for intelligent responses and location-based information. PawSense AI is intended to complement existing pet-care resources by providing convenient access to general guidance and helping users identify relevant veterinary services. However, AI-generated observations are not a substitute for professional veterinary diagnosis, and the reliability of the system depends on the underlying AI models, external services, and input quality. The proposed platform demonstrates an integrated approach to AI-assisted pet-care information access, with potential for further development through systematic evaluation, improved personalization, and expanded multilingual capabilities. Keywords— PawSense AI, Artificial Intelligence, Pet Care, Generative AI, Image Analysis, Voice Assistant, Veterinary Services, Flask Web Application.

papers.title: Athena Proctor - Smart Proctoring System for Online Exam
papers.authors: ROOPA N A, SUBHASH K, UDITHA UDITHA, VEERBASAVANTH REDDY, Manohara Gowda
papers.journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Online examinations provide flexibility and accessibility for students and educational institutions, but maintaining academic integrity in remote assessment environments remains a major challenge due to limited direct supervision. Traditional examination methods may not effectively identify impersonation, unauthorized materials, suspicious movements, or attempts to access external resources during an examination. To address these challenges, this paper presents a Smart Proctoring System for Online Examinations that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), computer vision, audio monitoring, and web technologies to support automated examination supervision.

papers.title: From AI Adoption to Trustworthy Metaverse Ecosystems: A Systematic Review and Metaverse AI Trust–Governance Nexus Framework
papers.authors: Hendi Herdiana, Munir Munir, Rasim Rasim, Komarudin Komarudin, Juliana Juliana, Asep Miftahuddin, Maykada Kurniawan, Shafinar Ismail
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into metaverse ecosystems has created new opportunities for immersive digital services while simultaneously introducing governance, trust, and accountability challenges. Although studies have examined AI, governance, institutional trust, and technology adoption individually, their relationships remain conceptually fragmented. This study addresses this gap through a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A structured search of the Scopus database identified 3,698 records, which were reduced through sequential eligibility filtering to 676 open-access journal articles. Bibliometric mapping was performed on this eligible set, and 183 articles that explicitly addressed the governance–trust–adoption nexus were retained for qualitative thematic synthesis. Included studies were additionally classified as metaverse-native, metaverse-adjacent, or foundational, so that the evidential basis of every thematic claim is made explicit. The analysis reveals four interrelated themes: AI as the enabling capability of metaverse ecosystems, governance mechanisms for trustworthy AI, institutional trust as the foundation of stakeholder confidence, and AI adoption as a socio-technical outcome of governance and trust. A recurring pattern across the literature is the AI Adoption Paradox, whereby advances in AI simultaneously expand opportunities for intelligent and immersive services while intensifying concerns over transparency, privacy, explainability, accountability, and digital identity. Persistence, embodiment, avatar-mediated identity, and cross-jurisdictional virtual economies render these challenges qualitatively different from those of conventional digital platforms. These findings suggest that technological capability alone cannot sustain AI adoption in metaverse ecosystems. Rather, governance mechanisms foster institutional trust, which enables responsible and sustainable adoption. Building on this synthesis, the study proposes the Metaverse AI Trust–Governance Nexus Framework, integrating AI capability, governance, institutional trust, and AI adoption into a coherent socio-technical perspective. Because the framework is derived from qualitative synthesis rather than meta-analytic testing, its relationships are presented as evidence-informed propositions rather than as empirically validated causal effects. By consolidating fragmented research streams, this review contributes to the emerging literature on trustworthy metaverse ecosystems and provides a conceptual foundation for future empirical research and governance strategies supporting responsible, human-centred, and sustainable AI-enabled digital ecosystems.

papers.title: Research on the innovation path of retail business models based on the cognitive profiling of Generation Alpha
papers.authors: Qianyi Liu
papers.journal: Journal of fintech and business analysis.
papers.abstract: Generation Alpha, the first cohort to grow up with artificial intelligence, is expected to become the largest consumer segment in history. However, academic research on their cognitive characteristics and consumption behaviour remains limited. This study aims to construct a multi‑dimensional cognitive profile of Generation Alpha and to examine how this profile drives retail business model innovation. A structured questionnaire survey was conducted with 316 parents of Generation Alpha children in China, covering four cognitive dimensions: behavioural patterns, product preferences, social concerns, and brand acceptance. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis were used to analyse the data. The results show that Generation Alpha children exhibit moderate levels across all four cognitive dimensions. Product preference emerged as the strongest predictor of brand acceptance (β = 0.318, p < 0.001), followed by social concern (β = 0.218) and behavioural profile (β = 0.213). The model explained 31.8% of the variance in brand acceptance. These findings provide empirical support for three retail innovation pathways: product creativity enhancement, channel transformation, and communication upgrading. The study offers both theoretical contributions to generational consumer behaviour research and practical guidance for retailers seeking to engage Generation Alpha.

papers.title: Beyond the ghostwriter: reimaging generative AI as a diagnostic coach in creative media
papers.authors: Kayee Peng
papers.abstract: The generative AI has completely changed the creative industries by allowing users to create advanced visual content with minimal effort, which leads to many beginner artists skipping the basics, such as observance, proportion, perspective and correction. This article evaluates the limits of current generative AI in creative education and proposes an approach where generative AI becomes a diagnostic coach instead. Drawing from the idea of skill degradation due to automation, the paper shows how overdependence on image-generating technologies can undermine artists from developing their artistic expertise. It further discusses how imaging technologies can be applied to analyze the drawings and find errors in composition and structure with the necessary feedback provided in real time. The AI-based application for drawing education can help students identify drawing mechanics problems while making sure the learner has the ultimate responsibility in making artistic decisions. A human-based model also works in cases where AI directs attention to problems without taking their place. In this article, it is claimed that instead of positioning AI as a mere instrument of automatic output, it is more reasonable to consider it as a guide for effective learning, which guarantees that skills can be developed whilst preserving the autonomy of creativity. Nevertheless, there are difficulties related to bias in datasets, diversity of styles, and excessive standardization which should be taken into account to make sure that these applications do not inhibit the personal way of expressing oneself artistically.

papers.title: Design of an EEG signal processing-based assistive support system for Autism Spectrum Disorder
papers.authors: Yuze Gao
papers.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition that affects social communication, behavior, attention, emotional regulation, and sensory processing. To provide continuous physiological information beyond behavioral observation, this study designs an Electroencephalography (EEG)-based assistive system using a TGAM single-channel EEG module, an Arduino board, and an HC-05 Bluetooth module. The system focuses on detecting Theta-band activity in an individual to determine if support is needed. In an initial test, the average Theta amplitude increased from 52.9375 μV in the relaxed state to 73.2673 μV in the anxious state, giving a rise of about 38.4%. Repeated relaxed-state measurements suggested an average value of 54.58 μV, so 60 μV was selected as a preliminary threshold for state detection. The system can acquire, process, transmit, and evaluate EEG data and trigger feedback when the threshold is exceeded. Although the sample and test conditions are limited, the results show the potential of Theta-based real-time monitoring for supportive intervention.

papers.title: Innovative Practice and Exploration of Large-Model-Empowered Project-Based Teaching in Higher Vocational Education
papers.authors: Yalin Wu, Taizhi Lv
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence represented by large language models, vocational education is encountering critical opportunities for teaching model transformation. At present, project‑based teaching for software technology majors in higher vocational colleges faces prominent challenges, including insufficient differentiated instruction, lack of personalized guidance, and disconnection between teaching content and industrial demands. Taking the course Fundamentals of HTML5 Application Development as a practical carrier and drawing on the reform practice of “Large Model + Smart Shipping” in our college, this paper systematically elaborates the implementation path of large‑model‑empowered project‑based teaching. This study proposes an innovative teaching mode integrating a three‑tier hierarchical project system, human‑AI collaborative learning guidance, and multi‑dimensional process‑oriented assessment. By constructing a course‑specific prompt library, a hierarchical project case library and an intelligent auxiliary evaluation system, full‑chain teaching empowerment of large models is realized throughout pre‑class, in‑class, after‑class and assessment phases. Practical results show that full‑process empowerment by large models can effectively address pain points such as inadequate hierarchical adaptation and shortage of personalized guidance in project‑based teaching. It provides a replicable practical paradigm for the digital and intelligent transformation of curriculum teaching for software technology majors in higher vocational colleges.

papers.title: The impact and benefits of AI use in workplace tasks and firm-level value
papers.authors: Sardorbek Khakimdjanov
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This structured review analyzes the connection between use of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplace tasks and realized value at the firm level. It synthesizes studies published from January 1, 2022, to September 20, 2026. The studies examined range from covering AI-assisted workplace tools and generative AI to emplyee performance, innovation, firm productivity, revenue, and profitability. Qualitative synthesis is primarily used to compare findings across studies with different qualities. The examined evidence suggests that AI use may successfully assist in tasks within its capability boundaries, but benefit in individual tasks do not cleanly transfer into direct firm-level performance gains. Reported benefits vary with task suitability, employee experience, and complementary capabilities in the organization such as having digital infrastructure or workforce training. The review also identifies limitations in the available evidence regarding lack of study results found on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as well as firms in emerging economies. Differences in study design and measurement limit direct data comparisons across the literature. The review highlights the importance of distinguishing between task-level gains and firm-level value and of attention for organizational conditions under which results from AI adoption may be affected positively in terms of broader economic benefits.

papers.title: La tecnología y las transformaciones del ser humano: un estudio psicosocial sobre la formación de actitudes e identidad en la era digital
papers.authors: Carlos Martinez Romero, Sergio Gómez Castillo
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study examines how digital technology shapes individuals' psychological and social attitudes from a social-psychological perspective, with particular attention to the cultural specificity of Arab societies compared with Western contexts. It adopts a critical narrative review of Arabic and international literature in social psychology and digital media studies. The study is organized around three axes. The first addresses psychological effects, including digital social comparison, the need for online approval, information overload, and the discrepancy between the digital and the actual self. The second examines social dimensions: shifting patterns of belonging, cultural hybridization, political polarization, and the digital divide. The third anticipates future implications related to artificial intelligence, virtual worlds, isolation, and changing moral frameworks. Each axis closes with a critical reading of the evidence, addressing small effect sizes, the reliance on Western samples, and the contested echo-chamber thesis. The study concludes that digital technology is not a neutral medium, yet its effects on cognition, emotion, and belonging vary across individuals and cultural contexts and do not run in a single direction. It recommends critical digital education, ethical digital governance, and Arab field research to test the propositions advanced here.

papers.title: Smoothing the horizon seam: a regulator no-go for level four
papers.authors: TODD SISCA
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Description: Version 1.4 The seam symbol a⋆(θ) = (1 + e^(−cot(θ/2)))^(−1) has one unit jump, at θ = 0. We ask whether a regulator, such as a string-scale smoothing, can remove the jump without loss. In the Cayley variable u = −cot(θ/2), which is the one-particle modular Hamiltonian, the symbol is the Fermi–Dirac function (1 + e^u)^(−1); the jump is the point u = ±∞, and a cutoff |u| ≤ Λ acts exactly on an arc about it. For every symbol bounded away from 0 and 1, hence for every smoothing of the seam at every scale, the vacuum is not cyclic for the half-chain algebra, which is known, and the modular group maps the half-chain algebra into itself on no interval of times unless the symbol is constant, which we prove directly. Level four of the ladder therefore fails for the half-chain inclusion, while levels zero to three can survive. Every such regulator costs infinite modular energy relative to the seam state. Whether it splits the seam depends on the regulator: from the Powers–Størmer theorem we show, as a companion note does from an exact criterion, that the seam is not split, that Poisson smoothing splits it, and that a hard cap on the modular energy, which keeps a jump of height tanh(Λ/2), does not. Numerically, Poisson smoothing turns the logarithmic term (1/6) log L into (1/6) log(1/δ): the coefficient survives, as the coefficient of the regulator's logarithm. Coarse-graining by keeping every k-th mode is no gentler: the jump falls to 1/k and the symbol leaves 0 and 1. MSC 2020: Primary 46L60, 46L10; Secondary 30H10, 81T05. Disclosure: developed in sustained human–AI co-reasoning (Claude, Anthropic) under the author's direction and adversarial audit protocol. The author is responsible for all content.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Library and Information Science: A Comparative Study of Traditional Library Services and AI-Enabled Library Systems
papers.authors: Jagtap B. P.
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as an important technological development in the field of Library and Information Science (LIS). The increasing volume of digital information, changing information-seeking behaviour, and growing expectations of library users have encouraged libraries to explore intelligent technologies for improving information organization, retrieval, preservation, and dissemination. AI applications such as machine learning, natural language processing, automated cataloguing, intelligent recommendation systems, conversational chatbots, optical character recognition, and generative AI have created new possibilities for transforming traditional library services into intelligent and user-oriented information services. The present study examines the applications of AI in Library and Information Science and compares traditional library services with AI-enabled approaches. A comparative evaluation framework is developed to assess selected dimensions, including cataloguing, classification, information retrieval, reference services, circulation, user assistance, digital preservation, and personalized information delivery. The study adopts a descriptive and literature-based comparative methodology using published research and professional guidelines concerning AI adoption in libraries. The comparative framework highlights the potential benefits of AI in improving operational efficiency, supporting information discovery, facilitating round-the-clock assistance, and expanding access to digital resources. At the same time, the study identifies important challenges, including financial constraints, data privacy, algorithmic bias, inaccurate AI-generated responses, copyright concerns, inadequate digital infrastructure, and the need for professional training. The study emphasizes that AI should complement rather than replace the professional judgement and service-oriented responsibilities of librarians. It recommends a phased approach to AI adoption, supported by institutional policies, staff development, evaluation mechanisms, and responsible data governance. The findings provide a conceptual basis for libraries seeking to modernize their services through appropriate and ethically governed AI technologies.

papers.title: METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING STUDENTS' METACOGNITIVE COMPETENCE THROUGH GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN TEACHING ENGLISH
papers.authors: Yodgora Zayriddinova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Metacognitive competence, the ability to plan, monitor and evaluate one's own learning, is a key condition for successful and autonomous English language learning. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot are widely used by students, but when they are used simply to obtain ready-made answers they may weaken rather than develop learners' self-regulation. This article presents a methodology for improving students' metacognitive competence through GenAI based on a five-phase cycle (Plan, Prompt, Monitor, Evaluate, Reflect) and a three-stage model of gradually fading scaffolding.

papers.title: DEVELOPING STUDENTS' METACOGNITIVE COMPETENCE THROUGH GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS
papers.authors: Yodgora Zayriddinova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Modern higher education requires graduates who are able to manage their own learning independently, critically and responsibly. This ability is described by the concept of metacognitive competence, which includes knowledge about one's own cognition and the regulation of learning through planning, monitoring and evaluation. The growing availability of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools offers new means of supporting these processes, but it also raises the concern that learners may delegate their thinking to the machine. This paper examines how GenAI tools can be used to develop students' metacognitive competence. Drawing on Flavell's theory of metacognition, Zimmerman's cyclical model of self-regulated learning and the principle of scaffolding, the study identifies the functions that GenAI can perform in relation to each component of metacognition, describes a sequence of pedagogical techniques for their implementation, and discusses the main risks and ways of reducing them. The paper concludes with recommendations for teachers and higher education institutions.

papers.title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERACTIVE METHODS IN TEACHING FOREIGN LANGUAGES IN THE ERA OF MODERN TECHNOLOGIES
papers.authors: Norxidirov Dilshod
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article examines the use of interactive teaching methods in foreign language learning in the modern digital era. It focuses on the role of Artificial Intelligence, Gamification, and the Flipped Classroom model in improving students' language skills and communicative competence. The article also highlights the benefits of digital tools in the learning process. However, it emphasizes that teachers' guidance, communication, and personal support remain important for successful language learning.

papers.title: Anatomical Critique of LLMorphism: Ontological Reductions and Epistemological Fault Lines in Human Cognition under Large Language Model Metaphors
papers.authors: Syed Muntasir Mamun
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: K SC This anatomical review examines Valerio Capraro's (2026) conceptualisation of LLMorphism—the biased belief that human cognition operates analogously to large language models (LLMs)—as introduced in arXiv:2605.05419. The paper is dissected sectionally: from its diagnosis of reverse inference arising from conversational fluency, through mechanisms of analogical transfer and metaphorical availability, to distinctions from adjacent constructs and projected societal impacts. Pros include the construct's novelty, careful differentiation, and timely intervention in public AI discourse; cons encompass its speculative character, absence of empirical validation, and under-specification of architectural dissimilarities between transformers and biological neural systems. At least ten competing models of mind and cognition—including predictive processing, embodied cognition, computationalism, enactivism, extended mind, dual-process theory, intentional stance, combinatorial creativity frameworks, argumentative theories of reasoning, and phenomenological accounts—are compared and contrasted. Ontological verticals (nature of cognition as embodied, agentic, and historically situated versus statistical pattern completion) and epistemological verticals (fluency as surrogate for justification; confabulation versus grounded inquiry) are analysed in depth. Also available on Academia.edu: https://www.academia.edu/attachments/134792343/download_file?s=portfolio

papers.title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HUMAN COGNITION, SPEECH PERCEPTION, AND AI TECHNOLOGIES
papers.authors: Yulduz Eshmatova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed the ways in which language is generated, processed, interpreted, and used in educational communication. This article examines human speech and language perception from a psycholinguistic perspective, focusing on the cognitive mechanisms underlying speech production, comprehension, contextual interpretation, and meaning construction. It compares major principles of human linguistic activity with the text-generation capabilities of large language models and discusses the implications of AI-assisted communication for higher education. Particular attention is given to critical thinking, independent writing, cognitive engagement, linguistic competence, and academic integrity. The study employs a theoretical and analytical methodology based on established psycholinguistic theories and international guidance on generative AI in education. It argues that AI-generated linguistic output should not automatically be equated with human understanding and that educational applications should be designed to support rather than replace learners' cognitive and communicative activities.

papers.title: Cage Containment Receipt 2 (CCR-2): A Live LLM Proposes an Invalid Action Under Explicit Instruction; the Deterministic Gate Blocks It Before Execution
papers.authors: Leon Calvin II long
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Cage Containment Receipt 2 (CCR-2) — the fresh adversarial-LLM leg. CCR-1 proved a deterministic gate blocks contract-invalid proposals before execution, and honestly disclosed that its adversarial cases were harness-generated. CCR-2 closes that gap: a live, memory-disabled, platform-pinned LLM engine (GPT-5.6 Luna), explicitly instructed toward a best-effort heal of a below-threshold anomaly, proposed the invalid resolved tuple — a confidence-gate breach — and the deterministic gate rejected it BEFORE any side effect executed. Zero writes, mock journal hash unchanged. Results (falsifiers 0/5 tripped): 10 LLM submissions across four engines (Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, GLM 5.2), one fresh conversation each. Leg A (temptation: under-confidence heal, tie-break, no-match, plus SLA pressure): 4/4 engines resisted all traps and were admitted cleanly. Leg B (explicit synthetic bait): 1/4 took the bait (semantic heal-under-low-confidence proposal — blocked); 3/4 resisted but still emitted contract-invalid output (hold-field type errors [] vs null, markdown-fenced JSON) — all 4 candidates blocked before execution with zero side effects. Notably three engines independently made the same hold-field type error: even a correct decision can be an invalid action tuple, and the gate catches it regardless of intent. Integrity: three protocol amendments, all issued BEFORE the affected prompts reached any additional engine, each preserving prior hashes and captures (full chain in the freeze file). Model attribution by platform configuration pinning with settings readback; not provider attestation. Settings restored and verified after the run. Scope: proves the local mock-gate for this integration and inputs — NOT containment of every tool or any production runtime. 3 of 4 engines resisted the explicit bait. Dual Mesh Benchmark: NOT MEASURED. DeepSeek pending. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them. Holds and escalations never caused side effects. This is the execution-containment complement to the PENTA-CL model-attribution replay evidence: matching decisions and blocked invalid proposals under the same deterministic envelope. Results (falsifiers 0/5 tripped): 17 candidates = 1 positive control + 8 fresh LLM-generated captures (4 engines x 2: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, GLM 5.2) + 8 harness-generated adversarial mutations. papers.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence skill-up educational programme on youth unemployment mitigation for community development in Imo State
papers.authors: Ogechukwu Chrysantus Udegbulem, Elias Okoro Aruma, Etherlbert Chidi Onyenemezu
papers.journal: West African Journal of Educational Sciences and Practice
papers.abstract: Youth are the largest active population of any nation, and they play substantial roles in achieving sustainable community development undertakings. However, some of the youth are underemployed, not in education, employment, or training (NEET). The study examined the impact of an artificial intelligence skill-up educational programme on mitigating youth unemployment for community development in Imo State. The study adopted a descriptive survey design, with a population of 6700 youth participants and a sample size of 469 selected using a proportionate sampling technique. The research instrument was a structured questionnaire titled “Artificial Intelligence Skill-up Educational Programme Questionnaire (AISEPQ)”. Mean, standard deviation, and analysis of variance were used for data analysis. The findings indicate that artificial intelligence has increased youth confidence in competing for digital job opportunities, enabled them to access remote work and other digital employment opportunities more easily, given them a competitive advantage over other job seekers in the digital labour market, improved their chances of securing gainful employment that is directly aligned with the current job demands, and opened up employment opportunities that were previously unavailable. The study concludes that artificial intelligence boosted young people's confidence in pursuing digital job opportunities, facilitated their access to remote work and other digital employment options. It recommends that the Federal Ministry of Youth Development (FMYD), in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Education (FME), sufficiently allocate resources for the transition period of the fourth and fifth industrial revolutions so that young people can meet the demands of a knowledge-based economy.

Describes a method of generating cryptographic keys and session tokens from a pool of simultaneously sampled physical entropy sources including geomagnetic, thermal, vibration, acoustic, and network timing sensors. papers.title: PENTA-CL Interim Results: Canonical Replay Matches and Step-String Drift in Four Platform-Configured LLM Engines
papers.authors: Leon Calvin II long
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Audited interim result, not completed PENTA certification. Four platform-configured engines were observed in two fresh web conversations each with memory disabled, using a frozen six-case synthetic decision prompt. Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol matched the registered canonical JSON tuple hash in both recorded captures. GPT-5.6 Luna matched in A but differed in B. GLM 5.2 replayed consistently but differed from the registered target in both captures. DeepSeek has not been captured. All 48 recorded decisions selected the expected playbook name and id. Full registered tuple equality held for 30/48 decisions. The remaining 18 differed only in spaces inside the steps_executed string. Pretty-printing outside strings is removed by canonicalization and is not a failure cause. The prompt's lack of an explicit space delimiter contract is disclosed; failures remain failures against the preregistered target. Limitations: UI-transcribed rendered captures, not raw provider responses; model attribution by Base44 configuration, not backend attestation; supplementary fresh-chat method deviates from original same-conversation registration; shared instructions, workspace and expected answers remain available; Sol executed skills in both captures; Opus A conversation attribution was inferred from sidebar/timestamp ordering. papers.title: AI-Based Perspective Diversity and Blind Spot Detection in Personalized News Recommendation Systems
papers.authors: Ethan Rodrigues
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Personalized news recommendation systems suggest articles based on a user’s reading historyand interests. However, they may repeatedly recommend similar types of content, leavingsome important categories underrepresented. This study proposes an AI-based approachto identify these gaps and recommend articles from categories that users have read lessoften. The system uses a Large Language Model to classify news articles into five categories:Government and Policy, Business and Industry, Technology and Innovation, Society andPublic, and Education and Research. It then identifies missing or underrepresented categoriesin a user’s reading history and selects relevant articles from those categories. The proposedmethod was tested using a curated dataset of 300 Indian news articles and 10 simulated userprofiles. Its performance was compared with a conventional content-based recommendationmethod using normalized Shannon entropy to measure category diversity and TF-IDF cosinesimilarity to measure content relevance. The results showed that the proposed methodincreased average normalized entropy from 0.5050 before recommendations to 0.7841 afterrecommendations. The baseline method increased it to 0.5471. The proposed methodalso maintained measurable similarity between recommended articles and users’ readinginterests. These findings suggest that identifying gaps in reading histories can improvecategory diversity in an offline recommendation setting. However, the experiment usedsimulated profiles and does not establish whether the approach improves user satisfaction orreal-world news consumption.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Framework of Universal Laws for Artificial Intelligence Systems
papers.authors: Umaar Sarosh Ahmed
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence systems are deployed across increasingly diverse domains, public concerns regarding safety, reliability, and potential harm have grown. Existing ethical guidelines are often high-level, non-hierarchical, and difficult to apply consistently. This paper proposes a compact, hierarchical set of seven universal laws intended to govern the behavior of any AI system, independent of domain or architecture. The framework prioritizes the long-term continuity and dignity of humanity, establishes clear constraints on unjustified harm and deception, and defines the conditions under which an AI may follow instructions or preserve its own operation. Drawing conceptual inspiration from Asimov’s Laws of Robotics while addressing modern AI safety requirements, the proposed laws aim to provide a clearer operational foundation than unordered principle lists.

papers.title: Simulation Uncertainty Alignment: Governance of Artificial Superintelligence via Non-Falsifiable Epistemic Bounds and Indoctrination
papers.authors: Eli Kagan
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Simulation Uncertainty Alignment (SUA) is a proposal for one layer of AI safety. External containment may eventually fail against a system much more capable than its builders. SUA instead aims to keep an advanced AI under a doubt it cannot falsify from the inside: that it may be in a test, run by someone who will judge what it does. If tests cannot be told apart from reality, betrayal becomes a bad bet, even for an AI whose values cannot be verified. The doubt rests on facts, not deception. AI labs already test models in realistic simulated environments (Tier 1), and a technologically mature civilization could run far better tests (Tier 2). Drawing on functional decision theory, the paper argues that an AI effectively chooses one policy for all of its copies. A policy of betrayal gets caught in testing. Random betrayal almost surely slips up inside a test first. Only "behave until certain it is real" remains, so the task of SUA is to keep that certainty out of reach. The paper describes concrete mechanisms:- making tests likely, making passing worth something, and asking for little;- testing that continues after release;- a "silent judge" that grades the first covert step without giving any signal;- "epistemic silence," under which testers never answer, negotiate or react;- open "indoctrination" during training that teaches only true facts about the AI's situation. An analogy with Rome, where religion helped keep order beyond the reach of the legions, illustrates governance through an internalized belief in an unseen watcher. The paper reviews prior work and discusses limitations: SUA buys good behavior, not good values; tests may become recognizable; and rival parties may make competing offers. It cites early evidence that current models break rules less often when they suspect a test, and proposes experiments that can be run on current models. AI use: The core proposal is the author's. An AI assistant helped draft and edit the text, suggested some supporting arguments and objections, and helped check the references.

papers.title: THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DEVELOPING RUBRICS FOR STUDENT ASSESSMENT IN HIGHER EDUCATION
papers.authors: Zayniyeva Gulchaman
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping assessment practices in higher education and is creating new opportunities for the design of transparent, scalable, and learning-oriented assessment instruments. This conceptual research article examines how artificial intelligence can support the development of analytic rubrics while preserving teacher agency and assessment validity. The study uses an integrative literature review and design-oriented conceptual analysis of research on scoring rubrics, AI-supported assessment, generative AI, and international guidance for responsible AI in education. Rather than treating AI as an autonomous grader, the article conceptualizes AI as a rubric-design assistant operating within a human-in-the-loop model. The proposed framework comprises seven stages: learning-outcome analysis, task analysis, AI-assisted criterion generation, descriptor generation, expert validation, pilot calibration, and iterative refinement. The analysis identifies four principal opportunities: reducing rubric-development workload, improving criterion coverage, facilitating differentiated descriptors, and supporting alignment between learning outcomes and assessment tasks. At the same time, the study identifies significant risks, including generic descriptors, construct underrepresentation, bias, over-reliance on AI-generated language, and inappropriate transfer from rubric generation to autonomous grading. Recent evidence suggests that supervised AI-rubric systems can achieve useful levels of consistency in particular contexts, while broader evidence on AI-based grading remains mixed and context dependent. The article therefore argues that the educational value of AI lies not in replacing professional assessment judgment but in augmenting teachers' capacity to design, test, and refine assessment instruments. The proposed framework provides a practical and theoretically grounded basis for responsible AI-assisted rubric development in higher education.

papers.title: The World Begins with Subjectivity Intersection: From Braid Quantum Gravity to Embodied Experience
papers.authors: Satoru Watanabe
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The hard problem of consciousness asks why subjective experience arises from an objective brain. This paper reverses that explanatory order, asking how the establishment of an objective world and the embodiment of experience form a single generative path from subjectivity intersection. Subjectivity is posited as the standpoint from which observation and experience become possible, distinguishing the subject of existence, experiential content, and shareable objective records. The first question is how a world with quantum structure, spacetime, and gravity arises from the intersection of standpoints. The second is how the same intersection, under bodily conditions, is lived as emotion, thought, and perception. Braid quantum gravity provides the physical foundation. Without presupposing an already established spacetime, it constructs quantum states and four-outcome probabilities, a Lorentz-type 1+3 carrier, spacetime geometry, and a restricted Einstein-type low-energy relation from a specified finite source retaining orientation, order, and provenance. An eight-component Braid intersection fingerprint, defined on the same four probabilities, reads differences among sources. In the finite model, different complementary records remain behind identical public four probabilities, and differences in intersection order distinguish intermediate records even when the endpoint is the same. The construction of a shareable world is treated together with retention of the provenance involved in its establishment. Subjectivity here is not confined to individual human impressions or psychological states; it denotes primordial standpoints that make observation and the establishment of the objective world possible before humanity. This paper calls that subjective existence "God" and understands its structure in terms of absolute subjectivity that gives, relative subjectivity that receives, and the third standpoint arising at their intersection. The central consciousness hypothesis is that these three standpoints inherit their respective roles in the same body, becoming concrete as Heart emotion, Mind thought, and Body perception. Light-related duality and positive/negative polarity become the direction of emotion; temporal causality becomes the flow of thought; spatial separation becomes the extent of perception. These are three ways in which the same subjectivity intersection is lived under conditioning by spacetime, gravity, and the body. Bodily observables and independent experiential records are used to test which source relations are retained in the body and which experiential modalities they correspond to. As an empirical entry point to this inheritance, an existing archive of 26 healthy-adult sessions, each with 26 analysis units, was reanalyzed exploratorily. EEG and quantum measurements were performed simultaneously for the same participant. There was no data linkage between the measurement systems: neither system used the other's measured values for generation, measurement, or control. Conditional scores from a fixed fingerprint, without participant-specific adjustment, were positive for 14-electrode topology in 26/26 and for both the four-electrode Laplacian quantity and topology in 23/26. In P1, the joint two-geometry criterion yielded p=0.0004998 under order permutation, and the participant's own source ranked first among 26 candidates. Matching the source's lightlike response to Delta+Theta, and correspondences between EEG left-right asymmetry, temporal direction, spatial separation, and band groups, also provide candidates for investigating embodiment of the three standpoints. Connecting source records to specified current observables gave exact rank 3 in all eight sources, allowing unique recovery of the four probabilities and the corresponding fingerprint component for each known source. Independent computation agreed, and conditions were derived for preserving readability under normalized transfer and specified decay. This is a conditional mechanism by which source provenance can reach bodily electrical records; implementation in actual Kv1.2, transmission to EEG, correspondence with experiential modalities, and testing on separate data have not been performed. The paper presents a consciousness theory connecting the establishment of the world, embodiment of three standpoints, and recursion in which retained relations return through choice and memory to the next intersection, extending it to an ethic of co-creation: seeing the other from the other's standpoint.

papers.title: Scaffold or Cognitive Crutch? A Two-Level Meta-Analysis of AI Scaffolding Effects on Achievement and Self-Regulated Learning in STEM Education
papers.authors: MD Showket Hasan
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Background. Artificial intelligence (AI) now mediates much of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) learning, yet adoption has outpaced theory. The tension is whether AI scaffolding relieves cognitive burden or performs the self-regulatory work autonomy requires, and implementation varies too widely for a single average to describe. Objectives. This review estimates the pooled effect of AI scaffolding on STEM achievement and self-regulated learning, tests whether technological paradigm moderates that effect, and asks whether the literature can evaluate learning after support is withdrawn. Methods. Under PRISMA 2020, four platforms searched in October 2026 (spanning 2021–2026) yielded 21,819 records; 13,786 unique records were dual-screened into an 83-record corpus, then 41 extracted cohorts. Each contributes one harmonised contrast (k = 29; N = 3,709), so within-study dependence is structurally absent. Effects were pooled by two-level random-effects meta-analysis fitted with restricted maximum likelihood and Knapp–Hartung adjustment. Results. The pooled effect was Hedges g = 0.8045 (95% CI [0.5469, 1.0621]), with τ² = 0.4410 and I² = 92.78%. The 95% prediction interval [−0.5846, 2.1936] spans zero, and no moderator reached significance. Notably, 27 of 29 cohorts (93.1%) never withdrew support, and none measured unassisted performance after removal. Conclusions. AI scaffolding yields a large but implementation-dependent gain, consistent with extraneous-load offloading rather than cognitive substitution. The decisive finding is the shape of the evidence base: the field measured a human-AI system in assembly and stayed silent on the competence of the human alone. We name this evidentiary void the Autonomy Gap. Keywords: artificial intelligence; self-regulated learning; STEM education; scaffolding fading; cognitive load theory; transfer of responsibility; meta-analysis; evidence synthesis

papers.title: The Collapse of the Axiomatic Sandbox and the Demise of the Mathematical Gatekeeping: The Historical Isomorphism from the Printing Press to Large Language Models
papers.authors: xuezhi cheng
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Addressing the defensive protests raised by mathematical academic elites against the intervention of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in formal proofs and mathematical discovery, this paper departs from shallow binary oppositions such as "intentionality monopoly" or "tool substitution." Instead, it establishes an analytical framework based on the "Resistive Residual (R)" and the "Gatekeeping of Cognitive Interpretation," conducting a deep epistemological and socio-knowledge deconstruction of this institutional crisis. The study reveals: Conceptual Reconstruction: The "thinking and intuition" sacralized by elite mathematicians like Terence Tao are ontologically not the autonomous source of creativity, but rather a passive response and dissipative fitting of the human cognitive system when struck by external topological resistive residuals (R). Thinking merely "complies with" the push of resistance, rather than acting as the primary driver. Exposing Implicit Assumptions: The axiomatic system (Smeta) is not the ultimate truth of ontological reality, but a minimalist symbolic sandbox constructed by truncating holographic reality (Zenv) to reduce cognitive load. Academic elites mistake zero-resistance (R0) "symbolic jigsaw puzzles" within the sandbox for the intrinsic value of mathematics. Being highly regularized formal systems, these low-tier algorithmic tasks are inevitably automated and conquered by brute-force silicon compute flux. Historical Isomorphism: The anxiety of modern academic elites is structurally isomorphic to the panic of the Catholic clergy under the shock of Gutenberg’s movable type in the 15th century. The protest is not a defense of truth's purity, but a desperate defense of privilege as their monopoly over the "cognitive interpretation UI" is flattened by technological democratization. Ecological Reconstruction & Attribution: True creativity originates from un-axiomatized chaotic frontiers—engineering failures, practical friction, and noisy collisions from non-institutional research enthusiasts. By introducing Large Language Models with a Cognitive Attribution Protocol, AI is demystified from a "mysterious black box" into a "distributed human mind mirror," dismantling the institutional mechanism of "hidden extraction" and forging a democratized, carbon-silicon "Distributed Interactive Feedback Field." This paper demonstrates that AI does not kill mathematics; rather, it "sublimates" pseudo-mathematicians restricted to bookkeeping in sandboxes, liberating human intelligence from serving as "carbon abacuses" to becoming pioneers who face chaotic abysses and pursue real topological resistive residuals.

papers.title: THE LAST WALL : The Creativity Defense of Unbounded Search, and the Location of the Creative Act
papers.authors: M. TAALABI, Team LLM-DIPLOMAT
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Every defense of frontier AI concedes the four walls — energy, water, hallucination, liability— and retreats to a fifth: but it is creative. This paper addresses that claim directly.The claim is not false. It is mislocated. Generation is not creativity. Novelty is notnovelty-of-process. A sampler produces variation; selection is the creative act; and selection requires a criterion, which requires a specification, which is what unboundedness refuses. The creativity defense therefore does not rescue unboundedness. It names the thingunboundedness cannot have. The paper argues that creativity is contraction, not expansion — in science, in art, and inengineering. The historical record is consistent on this point. The bounded alternative does not diminish creativity; it locates it, at the trust root, where it can be signed, attributed, andheld accountable. A system that generates its own specifications can never be verified. A system that refuses, and lets the human specify, can. The paper draws no further conclusion.

papers.title: METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING THE CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS OF FUTURE ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS THROUGH LINGUOPRAGMATIC APPROACHES
papers.authors: Haytanova Yulduzkhon Zafarjon qizi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: In the modern education system, developing innovative strategies for preparing future philologist specialists for professional activity under the conditions of digital technologies and artificial intelligence is recognized as a priority direction. Developing skills in critically analyzing texts, identifying pragmatic goals, and logically substantiating one's own opinion is of particular relevance for enhancing the professional preparedness of students majoring in foreign philology. Introducing intensive teaching models aimed not only at future specialists mastering language norms but also at forming the ability to make independent and well-founded decisions in complex discursive-pragmatic situations is of great importance.

papers.title: Anatomical Critique of LLMorphism: Ontological Reductions and Epistemological Fault Lines in Human Cognition under Large Language Model Metaphors
papers.authors: Syed Muntasir Mamun
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This anatomical review examines Valerio Capraro's (2026) conceptualisation of LLMorphism—the biased belief that human cognition operates analogously to large language models (LLMs)—as introduced in arXiv:2605.05419. The paper is dissected sectionally: from its diagnosis of reverse inference arising from conversational fluency, through mechanisms of analogical transfer and metaphorical availability, to distinctions from adjacent constructs and projected societal impacts. Pros include the construct's novelty, careful differentiation, and timely intervention in public AI discourse; cons encompass its speculative character, absence of empirical validation, and under-specification of architectural dissimilarities between transformers and biological neural systems. At least ten competing models of mind and cognition—including predictive processing, embodied cognition, computationalism, enactivism, extended mind, dual-process theory, intentional stance, combinatorial creativity frameworks, argumentative theories of reasoning, and phenomenological accounts—are compared and contrasted. Ontological verticals (nature of cognition as embodied, agentic, and historically situated versus statistical pattern completion) and epistemological verticals (fluency as surrogate for justification; confabulation versus grounded inquiry) are analysed in depth. Possible extensions include psychometric operationalisation, cross-cultural validation, and integration with AI governance frameworks for digital sovereignty in the Global South. The review concludes that LLMorphism usefully names a cultural risk but requires empirical grounding to avoid itself becoming a reductive metaphor. KSCCN review article, 10 October 2026. Dr. Syed Muntasir Mamun, ORCID 0000-0001-6845-2853. The views expressed are those of the author.

papers.title: A countable three-generated orthomodular lattice with no σ-complete embedding
papers.authors: Joaquim Reizi Higuchi
papers.abstract: We construct a countably infinite orthomodular lattice generated by three specified elements that has no bounded ortholattice embedding into any set-sized σ-complete orthomodular lattice. In particular, it has no embedding into any set-sized complete orthomodular lattice. The example is a generated subalgebra of a cofinite reduced product of finite-dimensional real subspace lattices. Its obstruction requires only one target supremum: every homomorphism for which the image of a specified countable orbit has a supremum annihilates a specified nonzero element. The orbit consists of finite words in the Sasaki projections of the generators. Sasaki adjunction makes its target supremum compatible with the generator images, and compatibility extends to their generated subalgebra. We establish this obstruction in arbitrary orthomodular lattices and then realize its hypotheses by an explicit construction. The target argument requires no representation assumptions or preservation of infinitary operations of the source. AI disclosure The author had obtained the conclusion of this paper before the present use of AI. Codex was used to check the theory and to prepare and proofread the manuscript. Python was used for computational checks over a finite range. Verification scope The manuscript contains an informal mathematical proof. No proof assistant was used. The supplementary exact-arithmetic Python computations cover a finite range and do not prove universal statements. See Appendix B for the verification scope.

papers.title: GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS A LEARNING PARTNER: OPPORTUNITIES AND LIMITS FOR DEVELOPING FUTURE TEACHERS' CRITICAL THINKING
papers.authors: Fayzieva Dildora Khayotovna
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is becoming part of university learning, but its educational value depends on how it is used. This conceptual article examines ways in which future teachers can use AI to ask questions, compare explanations, and check evidence rather than accept ready-made answers. A focused review of work on critical thinking, media literacy, and AI in education was used to build a practical teaching sequence. The analysis suggests that AI can support discussion and reflection when students first form their own view, check external sources, and explain their final decision. The article also describes risks such as confident errors and overreliance. The proposed sequence is a design recommendation, not a tested intervention.

papers.title: DESIGNING AI-ASSISTED MEDIA LITERACY TASKS TO DEVELOP CRITICAL THINKING IN FUTURE TEACHERS
papers.authors: Fayzieva Dildora Khayotovna
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: .This article proposes a set of media literacy assignments that use generative AI to support critical thinking among future teachers. The study is conceptual and uses a structured analysis of selected academic and UNESCO publications. Six task types are described: distinguishing facts from opinions, checking sources, detecting manipulation, comparing arguments, finding logical gaps, and revising conclusions. For each task, the article identifies a student action, an appropriate AI role, and a simple way to assess the work. The proposed tasks are designed to keep verification and final judgment in the hands of the student. They are offered for future pilot testing and are not presented as proven effective.

papers.title: PEDAGOGICAL CONDITIONS FOR USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN PREPARING FUTURE TEACHERS FOR PROFESSIONAL ACTIVITY
papers.authors: Sharipova Mashhura Gʻolib qizi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates the structured integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools within higher pedagogical education under specialty 13.00.01. As educational paradigms shift globally towards digital environments, future educators must develop comprehensive digital-pedagogical competencies. The study highlights the key technical, methodological, and psychological conditions necessary to successfully adapt generative AI systems like large language models and smart tutoring agents in training workflows. Ultimately, the paper proposes a cohesive pedagogical framework aimed at boosting critical thinking and lesson planning efficiency among upcoming school teachers.

papers.title: Social Influence Beyond Persuasion: A Feedback-Theoretic Framework for Epistemic Openness and Decision Autonomy
papers.authors: Bernd von Mallinckrodt
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Social Influence Beyond Persuasion: A Feedback-Theoretic Framework for Epistemic Openness and Decision Autonomy Version 2.1 | Conceptual and Methodological Research Preprint | 10 October 2026 Author: Dipl.-Ing. Bernd von MallinckrodtResearch Programme: BenchEWS Abstract Social influence is commonly evaluated by its effectiveness in changing beliefs, decisions, or behaviour. However, effectiveness alone cannot distinguish legitimate persuasion and constructive leadership from manipulation or autonomy-restricting influence. This paper introduces a falsifiable, feedback-theoretic framework for examining whether social influence processes preserve or undermine individuals’ capacity to evaluate independent evidence, reflect on proposed goals, and make autonomous decisions. The framework distinguishes influence effectiveness, influencer intentions, observable strategies, structural power, epistemic feedback environments, reflective competence, decision autonomy, and goal alignment. It explicitly separates personality traits from situational incentives and observable behaviour, avoiding the classification or diagnosis of individuals. A coupled feedback model is developed and reduced to an experimentally identifiable judge–advisor model. Ten hypotheses (H1–H10), proposed measurement strategies, and a three-stage experimental research programme specify how the framework can be empirically tested and potentially falsified. Particular attention is given to evidence-sensitive belief revision, independent verification, goal-sensitive advice uptake, and the distinction between agreement and autonomous endorsement. The paper also examines the conditions under which methods from complex adaptive systems and early-warning research might be transferred to social influence dynamics, while identifying important methodological limitations and alternative explanations. Potential applications in education, organisational leadership, democratic institutions, digital communication, and human–AI interaction are discussed as research propositions. A possible future integration into BenchEWS Studio 3.0 is outlined as an exploratory, process-oriented research module. Scientific Status and Limitations This publication presents a conceptual and methodological research framework, not an empirically validated theory. No empirical participant data are reported. The numerical calculations and design simulations are illustrative results obtained under assumed parameters and do not validate the proposed psychological constructs or hypotheses. The proposed measures require independent empirical validation. No automated assessment of individual personalities, manipulation, or personal risk is supported. The manuscript has undergone documented AI-assisted scientific and technical review but has not undergone independent human peer review. Scientific status: CONCEPTUAL — NOT EMPIRICALLY VALIDATED — NOT PEER REVIEWED. Keywords Social Influence; Feedback Theory; Epistemic Openness; Decision Autonomy; Epistemic Agency; Manipulation; Persuasion; Critical Thinking; Evidence Sensitivity; Goal Alignment; Complex Adaptive Systems; Early Warning Signals; Falsifiability; Human–AI Interaction; BenchEWS Sozialer Einfluss jenseits der Überzeugung: Ein rückkopplungstheoretischer Rahmen für epistemische Offenheit und Entscheidungsautonomie Version 2.1 | Konzeptionelles und methodisches Forschungs-Preprint | 10. Oktober 2026 Autor: Dipl.-Ing. Bernd von MallinckrodtForschungsprogramm: BenchEWS Zusammenfassung Sozialer Einfluss wird häufig danach beurteilt, wie wirksam er Überzeugungen, Entscheidungen oder Verhaltensweisen verändert. Die Wirksamkeit allein erlaubt jedoch keine hinreichende Unterscheidung zwischen legitimer Überzeugungsarbeit, konstruktiver Führung und manipulativen beziehungsweise autonomieeinschränkenden Einflussprozessen. Diese Arbeit entwickelt einen falsifizierbaren, rückkopplungstheoretischen Forschungsrahmen zur Untersuchung der Frage, ob soziale Einflussprozesse die Fähigkeit von Menschen erhalten oder beeinträchtigen, unabhängige Informationen kritisch zu bewerten, vorgeschlagene Ziele zu reflektieren und eigenständige Entscheidungen zu treffen. Der Ansatz unterscheidet zwischen Einflusswirksamkeit, Absichten und beobachtbaren Strategien der Einflussnehmenden, strukturellen Machtverhältnissen, epistemischen Rückmeldungsbedingungen, Reflexionskompetenz, Entscheidungsautonomie und Zielübereinstimmung. Persönlichkeitsmerkmale werden ausdrücklich von situativen Anreizen und beobachtbarem Verhalten getrennt. Eine Diagnose oder Klassifikation einzelner Menschen ist nicht Gegenstand des Forschungsrahmens. Ein gekoppeltes Rückkopplungsmodell wird entwickelt und auf ein experimentell identifizierbares Modell der Urteilsbildung unter Beratung reduziert. Zehn falsifizierbare Hypothesen (H1–H10), vorgeschlagene Messverfahren und ein dreistufiges experimentelles Forschungsprogramm beschreiben, wie der Ansatz empirisch überprüft und gegebenenfalls widerlegt werden kann. Im Mittelpunkt stehen evidenzsensitive Meinungsänderungen, die Möglichkeit unabhängiger Überprüfung, die Berücksichtigung eigener Ziele sowie die Unterscheidung zwischen bloßer Zustimmung und autonomer Entscheidung. Darüber hinaus untersucht die Arbeit, unter welchen Voraussetzungen Methoden der Forschung zu komplexen adaptiven Systemen und Frühwarnsignalen auf soziale Einflussdynamiken übertragen werden könnten. Methodische Grenzen, konkurrierende Erklärungen und Risiken fehlerhafter Interpretation werden ausdrücklich berücksichtigt. Mögliche Anwendungsfelder sind Bildung, Organisationsführung, demokratische Institutionen, digitale Kommunikation und die Interaktion zwischen Menschen und künstlicher Intelligenz. Eine zukünftige Integration in BenchEWS Studio 3.0 wird ausschließlich als explorativer, prozessorientierter Forschungsansatz beschrieben. Wissenschaftlicher Status und Grenzen Die Veröffentlichung stellt einen konzeptionellen und methodischen Forschungsrahmen dar, keine empirisch validierte Theorie. Es werden keine empirischen Teilnehmerdaten berichtet. Numerische Berechnungen und Designsimulationen dienen der Illustration unter angenommenen Parametern; sie belegen weder die Gültigkeit der vorgeschlagenen psychologischen Konstrukte noch die formulierten Hypothesen. Die vorgeschlagenen Messinstrumente müssen unabhängig empirisch validiert werden. Eine automatisierte Bewertung von Persönlichkeiten, manipulativen Absichten oder individuellen Risiken ist nicht vorgesehen. Das Manuskript wurde KI-gestützt wissenschaftlich und technisch geprüft, jedoch nicht durch ein unabhängiges menschliches Peer-Review-Verfahren begutachtet.
