papers.abstract: Modern AI systems increasingly combine large language models (LLMs) with human experts, using the LLM to handle routine queries while deferring uncertain cases for expert review. When expert capacity is limited, however, deferral decisions must account not only for the reliability of the LLM but also for congestion in the expert queue. We formulate this as an online sequential decision-making problem in which, for each query, the system observes the confidence signal of the LLM's answer and must decide whether to output the answer or defer the query to a capacity-constrained expert. The reliability of the confidence signal is initially unknown and must be learned from expert feedback, which is both selectively observed (only deferred queries are labeled) and delayed by queuing. We propose \texttt{KL-PBD}, a learning algorithm that uses Kullback--Leibler lower confidence bounds on the unknown reliability parameters to guide deferral decisions. For $K$ confidence levels and horizon $T$, \texttt{KL-PBD} achieves $O(K\log T)$ gap-dependent regret when the accuracy at every confidence level is bounded away from the deferral boundary, and $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{KT})$ worst-case regret. We establish matching lower bounds, showing that these rates are optimal up to logarithmic factors. Finally, we validate our approach on synthetic instances and real-world question-answering datasets, namely GSM8K, NuminaMath, and MedMCQA, using Qwen LLMs.

papers.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
papers.authors: Ryota Kanai C
papers.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.

papers.title: Representation Drift in Continual Learning: LoRA versus N-gram Memory
papers.authors: Hao Wu
papers.abstract: A language model that keeps learning online must not slowly erode its own base capabilities. We ask which part of a modern LLM should absorb continual updates, by measuring how each choice changes the model's internal representations. On a 48-layer mixture-of-experts model with a native pretrained N-gram memory, we train a seven-task chain under three update mechanisms with identical data and budgets: updating only the N-gram memory table, continually training one shared LoRA adapter, and training a fresh LoRA per task that is merged into the backbone. We capture fixed-context representations at every layer and task boundary. Updating only the N-gram memory changes the base model's representations of general math and code inputs by 26%/15% (relative RMS), against 64%/35% for merged and 97%/39% for shared LoRA. This drift does not grow with the number of tasks: it reaches 25% after the first task and stays there for all seven, while both LoRA variants keep accumulating. Its generic behaviour is essentially unchanged (no code problem lost, math NLL -0.01), and every change is confined to inspectable, reversible table rows. The cost appears elsewhere: N-gram memory acquires new tasks more weakly and its stored tasks interfere with one another, losing as much old-task NLL as shared LoRA. We show that this forgetting is governed by drift on the learned tasks' own inputs, measured from the checkpoint at which each was learned, not by generic drift (Spearman rho=0.85; rho=0.71 on Llama-3-8B), and we derive the exact relations behind it: with a frozen head, every pairwise logit margin changes by the projection of drift onto a head-difference direction. These results support a design principle for long-running online learning: write new knowledge only into the memory table and keep the backbone fixed; the remaining problem, interference between stored tasks, then lies inside the memory.

papers.title: MARL-BattleGrounds: A Novel JAX-native Benchmark for Heterogeneous and Competitive Multi-agent RL
papers.authors: Ulixes Tariq Hawili, Subramanian Ramamoorthy, Yoann Altmann, Ignacio Carlucho
papers.abstract: We present MARL-BattleGrounds (MARL-BGs), an easy-to-use JAX-native benchmark for heterogeneous and competitive multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), designed to be sample-efficient, computationally efficient, and researcher-centric. MARL benchmarks are typically simple and efficient, like SMAX, where winning reduces to unit micromanagement, or rich and costly, like Dota 2. MARL-BGs fills this missing middle. Its first mode, Team Deathmatch, is a simultaneous turn-based game between two teams of five heterogeneous agents. The five classes have distinct basic, passive, and ultimate abilities designed to synergize with allies and counter enemies. Our 52 hand-designed maps with diverse obstacles include a 12-map curriculum and ten held-out validation and test maps. MARL-BGs provides two canonical evaluation modes. First, eight endgame scenarios form a hard generalization challenge: each asks a team to win an unseen, nearly lost position against a strong reactive controller within 5-10 ticks. Second, a monthly round-robin tournament retrains each submission on equal compute, plays it against every member of the current "Big Nine" field, and publishes the Elo results on the official leaderboard. All entrants are publicly released as downloadable opponents. MARL-BGs records 11,192 metrics per game in 28 topics. We also include three strong scripted opponents, an analytical replay viewer, and off-the-shelf tools for self-play, cross-play, curriculum learning, and zero-shot coordination evaluation. We even provide an API for LLM-based agents and use it to evaluate Qwen3.5-9B against our strongest policy. In our BattleClient, humans can play alongside or against any mix of policies, enabling human-AI evaluation. We benchmark MARL-BGs with six additional deep MARL baselines, which we release. On one RTX 5090 with 1,024 parallel games, the simulator runs 50,000 5v5 game steps per second.

papers.title: DeKoR: Decomposed Knowledge Routing for Efficient GNN--LLM Fusion
papers.authors: Peiyuan Li, Yongqi Huang, Jitao Zhao, Di Jin, Dongxiao He
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for text-attributed graph learning by leveraging rich pre-trained knowledge and language understanding capabilities. Combining LLMs with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a promising paradigm for expanding the modeling capabilities of graph learning. However, LLMs and GNNs follow distinct learning paradigms, leading to a pronounced mismatch between their knowledge spaces. Such discrepancies make effective knowledge fusion nontrivial. Moreover, existing methods often incur substantial additional computation for only limited performance gains. To address these challenges, we propose DeKoR, an efficient framework for GNN and LLM knowledge fusion. To enable efficient knowledge transfer, DeKoR decomposes LLM knowledge into complementary local and global views and uses the LLM as an offline teacher to distill them into lightweight experts. To enable selective knowledge fusion, an adaptive router learns how much each node should rely on each expert. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that DeKoR outperforms existing baselines on both node and subgraph classification, achieving superior effectiveness and efficiency.

papers.title: Impact of Expertise and Trust on AI-assisted Work
papers.authors: Qianou Ma, Pranav Khape, Rock Pang, Ken Koedinger, Tongshuang Wu, Siddarth Suri, Shamsi T. Iqbal
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents promise to extend what users can accomplish beyond their existing expertise, but they also raise the risk of producing plausible-looking work that users may struggle to evaluate. We ask how task-relevant expertise and trust in AI shape agent-assisted work. To isolate these factors, we conduct a think-aloud study in which 20 professionals with varying data-science expertise use the same agentic tool to complete the same data-science hiring assessment, used at a major U.S. company. We find that surface productivity can come at the expense of understanding: participants who delegated more completed more of the task, but were also more likely to produce invalid solutions. Experts more often resisted this tradeoff, sacrificing completion to decompose the task and scrutinize agent outputs. Our findings call for evaluating agentic assistance not only by how much it accomplishes, but by whether users remain able to evaluate the work they produce.

papers.title: In View or Out of View? A Vision-Aware Filter that Infers and Reacts to the Human's Field of View
papers.authors: Mengxue Fu, Sophie Hsu, Yinlong Dai, Erdem Bıyık, Dylan P. Losey
papers.abstract: During human-robot interaction, sight plays an important role. When the human sees a robot, they can observe the robot's actions and better predict the robot's future behaviors. Conversely, when the human cannot see the robot, they become uncertain about the robot's intent and plans. In this paper, we focus on the human's field of view. Existing human-aware planners either ignore this field of view and assume the human can observe the entire scene, or intentionally design their interactions so the robot is always visible to the human. By contrast, we enable robots to infer what the human has and has not seen during interaction, i.e., the human's field of view. We then apply this estimate as a vision-aware filter on the robot's actions. Given a nominal robot policy and a model of the interaction, we roll out the policy over a short horizon to see how the robot's state updates. We then reweight the actions based on how those actions impact the robot's predicted visibility: higher weights are assigned to actions that bring the robot into (or away from) the human's line of sight. In practice, our framework provides an online estimation and filtering process that repeatedly updates its understanding of the human's field of view and then locally perturbs robot actions based on the human's vision. We evaluate our vision-aware filter on robots that assist humans in collaborative cooking and coordinate with them in driving environments. Across simulations and a 12-participant user study, we find that our vision-aware filter changes both performance and preference: participants completed over three times as many subtasks with in-view assistance while cooking, and had fewer collisions with cars that purposely stayed out of their view while driving.

papers.title: Iterate on an LLM, Serve on an SLM
papers.authors: Keegan Wang
papers.abstract: As frontier LLMs gain more capabilities, the cost to run them also goes up. At the same time, small language models (SLMs) also gain more capabilities but have largely been able to keep their cost stable, offering 5-40 times cheaper inference for the narrow, repetitive subtasks that agents decompose work into. However, the standing limiting factor is getting the correct behavior out of a small model in a fast, efficient, and economical way. Unfortunately, in most cases, zero-shot small models fail narrow production tasks. Furthermore, retraining one every time the behavior changes is too slow to iterate on. We propose doing both in sequence. First, develop the desired behavior in prompt space, on a frontier model, with immediate feedback from live traffic. Then, once the behavior converges, distill the recorded production behavior (not synthetic imitations of it) into an SLM through supervised fine-tuning (SFT). We show a proper use case of this method through a scheduling agent for home-care agencies that fans out a single yes/no safety decision per caregiver-shift pair on GPT-5.4-nano. A LoRA-tuned Qwen3-8B trained on 11.6k recorded production decisions reaches 0.913 agreement, while the teacher (GPT-5.4-nano), re-run on its own recorded prompts, agrees with itself only 72.7% of the time, pointing to the fact that the SLM may also be more consistent. Furthermore, when the two disagreed, a blinded professional scheduler sided with the student 48-29. Finally, we find that the SLM has approximately 2.5 times lower median latency and is a fraction of the cost. We believe this lifecycle of quick building, live feedback, and cheap inference is a blueprint for others building similar systems.

papers.title: LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising
papers.authors: Wen Zhang, Xiao Bai, Hsiang-wei Chao, Mengfan Zhu, Tong Zhao, Mingxuan Ju, Xiaodong Liu, Congfei Zhang, Yunzhi Zhou, Yajun Wang, Jinchao Li, Yu Zhang
papers.abstract: Dynamic Product Advertising (DPA) retrieval systems are a core component of modern e-commerce advertising; however, their evaluation remains challenging. Conventional offline engagement metrics are limited by sparse, biased feedback, while online evaluation is costly and time-consuming. In this work, we propose a user--product relevance metric for offline evaluation of DPA retrieval systems. The metric first compresses the engagement history into a compact set of intent representatives via Semantic-ID-grouped, event-stratified segmentation, then assesses the relevance of a recommended product to each individual intent and aggregates them as a user-level relevance score, yielding a stable and interpretable measure of retrieval quality. To compute this metric at scale, we leverage large language models (LLMs) as semantic relevance judges, capturing nuanced functional and semantic relationships that heuristic methods often miss. We propose an agentic, human-aligned prompting framework that generates multi-category relevance guidelines and distills teacher-model judgments into an efficient student model for scalable evaluation. The resulting metric strongly correlates with offline and online business metrics, enabling faster and more reliable DPA retrieval iteration before A/B testing.

papers.title: MontageFlow: Physically Valid High Fidelity EEG Generation
papers.authors: Sudarshan Regmi, Nabaraj Subedi, Arvind Pillai, Yu Yvonne Wu, Yuliang Chen, Michael V. Heinz, Lisa Marsch, Nicholas C. Jacobson, Andrew Campbell
papers.abstract: Generative modeling offers a promising solution to the scarcity of labeled clinical electroencephalography (EEG) data under strict privacy constraints. Although recent generative models report substantial improvements in generation fidelity, we show that these gains conceal a categorical failure. EEG is not an arbitrary multichannel signal: each channel records the voltage difference between two scalp electrodes. So, real recordings satisfy exact linear identities among their channels. Current generators invariably violate these identities, yet this has gone unnoticed. We therefore propose MontageFlow, a flow-matching model that enforces these identities by restricting its output to signals that satisfy them. We find that ensuring validity improves fidelity too. Furthermore, to retain the EEG characteristics that oversmoothing washes out, we also condition the model on a physiological state vector encoded from the whole EEG window. For generation, this vector is drawn from a prior fitted in latent space. Across 3 large-scale benchmarks, our model improves TS-FID by 1.6-3.6$\times$ over the closest rival while ensuring validity.

papers.title: Shared-Control Teleoperation of Omnidirectional Aerial Robots for Continuous Valve Rotation
papers.authors: Jinjie Li, Yicheng Chen, Haokun Liu, Moju Zhao
papers.abstract: Omnidirectional aerial robots offer full 6-DoF independent control over position and orientation, making them popular for aerial manipulation. Although there have been advancements in robotic autonomy, human operation remains essential in complex aerial environments. Previously, we proposed an aerial teleoperation system that brings the rotational flexibility of human hands into the unbounded aerial workspace, which was evaluated through a vertically mounted valve-turning task. However, due to the limited range of human forearm's motion, the robot could not continuously rotate the valve, hindering its application in industry. In this work, we propose an approach to initiate continuous rotation when the forearm angle exceeds a threshold. This switch of control authority exemplifies the concept shared control from human-robot interaction, marking a further step in aerial teleoperation.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning in Machine Learning
papers.authors: Prof. P. P. Chavan Prerna Wayakole, Dr. H. B. Jadhav Prof. A. J. Shaikh
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a machine-learning approach for problems in which decisions are made repeatedly and their quality becomes clear through feedback. Instead of depending on a fixed collection of labelled answers, an RL agent interacts with an environment, observes its changing state, receives rewards or penalties, and improves its decision policy through experience. This review examines the basic RL framework and discusses deep reinforcement learning, offline learning, multi-agent systems, and human-guided learning. Applications in robotics, games, education, finance, healthcare, and autonomous systems are considered. The review also identifies sample inefficiency, computational cost, instability, delayed rewards, limited generalization, and safety as important challenges. The paper concludes by identifying research opportunities for efficient, reliable, explainable, and adaptable RL systems.

papers.title: Opportunities and Challenges of AI-Based Educational Assessment Tools
papers.authors: Aili Cui
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the integration of artificial intelligence in educational evaluation tools, focusing on both opportunities and challenges. It assesses how AI can enhance educational assessments through innovative features such as personalized feedback, adaptability, and immediate response capabilities. Additionally, the study critically addresses pressing concerns surrounding data privacy, equity in education, and ethical implications, proposing future directions and potential solutions to navigate these complexities in the evolving educational landscape.Simultaneously, the research examines strategies for leveraging AI technology to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of educational assessment. This exploration may yield valuable insights and guidance for the integration of AI within educational evaluation practices, thereby expanding the potential for innovation in this area.

papers.title: Collection Development of Foreign-Language Literature in Academic Libraries Under Digital Transformation: From Traditional Approaches to Innovative Models
papers.authors: Nadir İsmayılov, Arzu Zakiyeva
papers.abstract: This study examines the collection development of foreign-language literature in academic libraries under the conditions of digital transformation. Its aim is to reveal how the transition from print-based acquisition to the strategic management of electronic resources has reshaped collection development policies and to propose conceptual approaches for academic libraries in Azerbaijan. The study adopts a qualitative research design based on document analysis and comparative analysis of national and international literature in library and information science. First, the theoretical foundations of collection development, the significance of foreign-language scholarly resources for teaching and research, and the fundamental principles of collection policy are examined. The article then analyzes the management of electronic resources, the impact of open science and open access, demand-driven and evidence-based models, and the use of artificial intelligence, big data, and predictive analytics in collection decisions. The findings indicate that collection development has evolved from a quantity-oriented acquisition function into a data-driven strategic management process. The study suggests that national consortia, unified electronic resource management systems, analytical platforms, and the digital competencies of library professionals may be decisive for improving foreign scholarly information provision in Azerbaijani academic libraries.

papers.title: Incorporation of artificial intelligence into Mathematics Education and its interfaces with algebraic reasoning: a systematic literature review
papers.authors: Larissa Borges de Souza Lima, Ana Virgínia de Almeida Luna
papers.abstract: This study investigates how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is incorporated into Mathematics Education and, secondarily, its interfaces with processes related to algebraic reasoning. The study is motivated by the recent expansion of AI and the need to understand its role in learning practices and environments. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with Prisma 2020, using the Capes, SciELO, and DOAJ databases. Of the 100 records identified, 36 studies were included in the corpus following deduplication and the application of eligibility criteria. Thematic analysis, guided by the functions attributed to AI and interpreted in light of Actor-Network Theory, yielded four categories. The findings indicate a predominance of instrumental uses and limited explicit attention to processes characteristic of algebraic reasoning.

papers.title: Problem posing and artificial intelligence in Mathematics teacher education: implementation issues
papers.authors: Flávia Sueli Fabiani Marcatto
papers.abstract: This study investigates the implementation and implementability of Problem Posing (PP) in conjunction with the formative use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in initial Mathematics teacher education. The study adopts a qualitative and interpretive approach grounded in Design-Based Implementation Research and was conducted in a Practice as a Curricular Component course within a Professional Learning Community. The results indicate initially restrictive conceptions of PP and difficulties in mathematically validating the problems posed. The mediated integration of GenAI broadened opportunities for comparison, made plausible errors visible, and strengthened teacher judgment and teacher noticing. The study concludes that this integration is promising, provided that it is guided by explicit pedagogical criteria.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mathematics lesson planning: a study with pre-service teachers
papers.authors: Matheus Nogueira Lopes, Carla Denize Ott Felcher, Bruna Vinholes Lopes
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to explore and evaluate the use of Artificial Intelligence in the development of Mathematics lesson plans. The study is based on an activity carried out with pre-service Mathematics teachers, which involved developing lesson plans using ChatGPT. The lesson plans produced and the records generated during the activity were analyzed from a qualitative perspective. The results indicate that most pre-service teachers were able to develop consistent prompts; however, hallucinations generated by the tool were identified, particularly regarding alignment with the Base Nacional Comum Curricular and estimates of actual class time. Artificial Intelligence can be used for lesson planning, provided that its use is guided by the teacher’s critical, ethical, and pedagogical judgment.

papers.title: The reconfiguration of Mathematics Education in the digital age: a critical analysis of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: DANIELLA SOARES NOGUEIRA RIBEIRO, Rony Cláudio de Oliveira Freitas
papers.abstract: This article presents a study on the implications of Artificial Intelligence for Mathematics Education, focusing on pedagogical practices, curriculum organization, and assessment processes. The aim is to analyze how Artificial Intelligence-based systems influence the teaching of Mathematics in the contemporary educational context. Methodologically, the study is grounded in a conceptual analysis of the specialized literature, conducted through thematic categorization of national and international academic publications. The analysis was organized into four axes: personalized learning, digital formative assessment, teacher mediation, and educational equity. The results indicate that Artificial Intelligence expands opportunities for pedagogical monitoring and support, while also posing challenges related to algorithmic opacity, inequalities in access, and the need for critical teacher mediation.

papers.title: [A case of bilateral open-lip schizencephaly with West syndrome due to variant of PAFAH1B1 gene and literature review].
papers.authors: Xiaojuan Liu, Hongdou Ma, Peina Liu, Zheyu Hu, Mingdong Gao, Yonghong Sun
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To report the clinical manifestations, genetic features, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of a child with bilateral open-lip schizencephaly complicated by West syndrome due to a variant of PAFAH1B1 gene, and review the relevant literature. METHODS: Clinical data of a 4-month-old boy were retrospectively analyzed, and 35 previously reported cases were systematically reviewed. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Gansu Provincial People's Hospital (Ethics No.: 2025-871). RESULTS: The 4-month-old boy presented with clustered flexor spasms, hypsarrhythmia on electroencephalography, and developmental regression. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed bilateral pachygyria, schizencephaly, and dysgenesis of the corpus callosum. Trio whole-exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous NM_000430.4: c.703_704delAG (p.Glu235Metfs*20) frameshift variant in the PAFAH1B1 gene. Sanger sequencing confirmed that neither parent carried this variant. Based on the guidelines from American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG), the variant has met the criteria for PVS1+PS2_Moderate+PM2_Supporting, and was classified as pathogenic. After treatment with adrenocorticotropic hormone combined with vigabatrin and other antiseizure medications, the epileptic spasms were controlled and the electroencephalographic abnormalities had improved. However, global developmental delay persisted at the 12-month follow-up. Analysis of the present case and 35 previously reported cases showed that PAFAH1B1-related phenotypes were highly consistent, mainly including infantile spasms (28/36), developmental delay/intellectual disability (29/36), and abnormal brain MRI findings (30/36), predominantly cortical malformations. The reported variant types included deletions, frameshift variants, nonsense variants, missense variants, and splice-site variants. CONCLUSION: PAFAH1B1 gene variants are an important cause for cortical malformations, including schizencephaly, and may lead to secondary West syndrome. This study has systematically summarized the genotypic and phenotypic features of bilateral open-lip schizencephaly complicated by West syndrome associated with a frameshift variant of the PAFAH1B1 gene. For infants with epileptic spasms or early-onset epilepsy accompanied by structural brain abnormalities, early genetic evaluation should be performed, and antiseizure treatment should be integrated with neurodevelopmental rehabilitation to facilitate long-term management.

papers.title: [Research advances on the association between the triglyceride-glucose index and its derivative indicators and dementia].
papers.authors: Y R Peng, R Y Tian, W Z Kong, X L Hu, W J Wang, D F Zhang, J N Fan
papers.abstract: The prevalence of dementia is increasing globally, and currently there is no effective treatment that can cure it. Therefore, it is particularly crucial to identify and prevent the occurrence of cognitive decline and dementia at an early stage. Insulin resistance (IR) is closely associated with cognitive decline, and the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple, sensitive indicator of IR, with great significance for predicting the occurrence, progression, and prognosis of dementia-related diseases. The TyG index combined with obesity indicators such as BMI, waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and waist-to-height ratio may provide a stronger predictive effect than a single indicator alone. This article will introduce the TyG index and its combined obesity indicators, and summarize research progress on the association between these indicators and dementia and its subtypes, to provide scientific evidence for the identification and prevention of dementia risk.

papers.title: An intelligent systems explanation of type 2 diabetes and a narrative to promote lifestyle change
papers.authors: Michael E. Hyland
papers.journal: Exploration of Endocrine and Metabolic Diseases
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is an error in the glycemic control system caused by insulin resistance. Self-organizing control systems use artificial intelligence to monitor and correct how they function and are used in modern applications of robotics. The development of type 2 diabetes is gradual and reversible through lifestyle changes, and this is consistent with insulin resistance being formed through a self-organizing or intelligent control system rather than the traditional control system on which current biomedical control systems are modelled. Lifestyles that induce high levels of glycemic variation would, in an intelligent control system, be detected as excessive oscillation, and an intelligent system can reduce oscillation by reducing the amplification. Insulin resistance represents low amplification in the glycemic control system. Intelligent control system functioning requires a network architecture, so if the glycemic control system is self-organizing, then it should be part of a network system that provides intelligent functioning for other control systems, and error in the glycemic control system would contribute to errors in other control systems and to a state of general network dysregulation. Intelligent systems theory explains how the comorbidities of type 2 diabetes and obesity would form through the dysregulation of a network of metabolic, immune, endocrine, and neurological pathways. The theory predicts that medical and lifestyle interventions for type 2 diabetes could improve comorbidities, but that comorbidities would reduce the effectiveness of those interventions. Studies are proposed to test this new theory that provides a non-blaming narrative for patients and could form a prequel to patient education.

papers.title: Intellectual Property Protection of Purely AI-Generated Content: Rethinking Authorship, Inventorship, and the Case for International Standards
papers.authors: Paul Barnabas, Abdulrahman Hassan Litalawe
papers.journal: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of generative and autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) systems has unsettled the traditionally anthropocentric foundations of intellectual property (IP) law. This article examines the extent to which existing intellectual property rights (IPR) frameworks, namely copyright, patent, and industrial design law, can accommodate works, inventions, and designs that are created exclusively by AI systems without direct human intervention. Adopting a doctrinal legal research methodology, the article reviews primary legal materials, including statutes, international conventions, and case law from several jurisdictions, alongside secondary scholarly literature, to assess how the requirements of authorship, inventorship, originality, and moral rights have been interpreted in the context of purely AI-generated content. The discussion is reinforced by a comparative analysis of jurisdictional responses in the United Kingdom, the European Union, the United States, Australia, South Africa, Indonesia, Hong Kong, China, and the United Arab Emirates. The central argument advanced is that traditional IPR laws were designed around human creativity and therefore struggle to extend coverage to autonomously generated content. While a few jurisdictions have experimented with liberal judicial interpretation or sui generis protection, these efforts remain fragmented, inconsistent, and largely reactive rather than systematic. The article concludes that an internationally coordinated framework, whether through reform of existing treaties or the negotiation of a dedicated IP-AI instrument, is necessary to balance innovation incentives, economic interests, and the public interest in access to AI-generated content.

papers.title: Teachers’ Understanding and Preparedness towards STEAM Education
papers.authors: Garima Singh, Dinesh Kumar
papers.abstract: Abstract Education is continuously evolving in response to technological advancements and the changing needs of society. The emergence of Artificial Intelligence, robotics, big data, and digital technologies has created a need for innovative and interdisciplinary approaches to teaching and learning. In this context, STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) education provides an integrated framework that promotes creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, and the application of knowledge to real-life situations. The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 also emphasizes holistic, experiential, multidisciplinary, and skill-oriented education. The present study examines teachers’ perspectives, understanding, attitudes, and preparedness towards implementing STEAM education in secondary schools. The study adopted a quantitative research approach using a descriptive survey method. The sample consisted of 58 teachers from four CBSE schools in Lucknow, selected through a random sampling method. Data were collected using a self-constructed structured questionnaire based on a Likert scale. The questionnaire examined four major domains: teachers’ understanding of STEAM education, their attitudes towards STEAM, preparedness to implement STEAM-oriented classrooms and laboratories, and professional development requirements. It also explored teachers’ views regarding interdisciplinary collaboration, digital tools, infrastructure, and innovative pedagogical practices. The study highlights the potential of STEAM education to enhance teachers’ professional and pedagogical competencies. STEAM-oriented approaches can encourage teachers to adopt inquiry-based, experiential, project-based, and problem-solving pedagogies. Thus, integrating STEAM education in alignment with NEP 2020 can contribute to more innovative, inclusive, engaging, and future-oriented learning environments in secondary schools.

papers.title: Employee Reskilling for AI Adoption and Organizational Performance: A Comparative Study of Infosys and TCS
papers.authors: Swarali Sampada Kulkarni, Shreya Deshpande, Rutika Bodhale
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is no longer an experimental add on for the Indian information technology industry it has become a core part of how large service providers price their work, staff their projects and talk to investors. This shift has pushed employee reskilling to the centre of corporate strategy, because a workforce that cannot operate alongside AI tools quickly turns into a cost rather than an asset. The present paper examines how two of India's largest IT services companies, Infosys Limited and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), have responded to this pressure through their reskilling programmes, and it asks whether the scale and depth of these programmes line up with measurable business outcomes. Using only secondary data drawn from annual reports, investor press releases, regulatory filings and reputable business media published between 2019 and 2026, the study builds a composite Reskilling Intensity Index (RII) from four equally weighted indicators: average learning hours per employee, the share of the workforce trained in AI, the maturity of the internal learning platform, and the visibility of leadership commitment to reskilling. Both companies score in the 'High' intensity band, with TCS marginally ahead of Infosys once the four sub-scores are combined. The paper then places this index alongside four financial and operational indicators Return on Equity (ROE), digital/AI revenue share, operating margin and revenue per employee to see whether a heavier investment in reskilling shows up in the numbers. The findings suggest a positive but uneven relationship: TCS records a noticeably higher ROE, largely on account of its capital structure and dividend policy rather than reskilling alone, while Infosys shows steadier digital revenue conversion in the years for which comparable disclosure exists. The paper closes with a discussion of what these patterns might mean for HR and finance functions inside large IT firms, and it is honest about the limits of a two-company, secondary-data design.

papers.title: ORGANISATIONAL AI-READINESS PRACTICE AND THE REALISED PRODUCTIVITY GAP FROM AGENTIC AI
papers.authors: Dr. N Subbukrishna Sastry, Kabita Kumari Sahu, Dr. Manjula Mallya M
papers.journal: EPRA International Journal of Socio-Economic and Environmental Outlook
papers.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence — AI systems that plan, act and complete multi-step tasks with limited human intervention — is diffusing through enterprises far faster than earlier generations of enterprise software, yet the productivity gains organisations report from it remain narrow and uneven. Industry evidence collected between 2022 and 2026 places the share of organisations that convert agentic-AI deployment into measurable, enterprise-level value at somewhere between four and twenty-four per cent, depending on measurement method, while national readiness indices place most organisations only in early or intermediate stages of preparedness. This paper reviews the emerging multidisciplinary literature on organisational AI-readiness practice — examined here across three dimensions: organisational culture, manager support and workflow redesign — and its relationship to the productivity gain organisations actually realise from agentic-AI adoption, as distinct from the gain they anticipate or report as adopted. Building on the technology-organisation-environment framework, dynamic-capabilities theory and the productivity J-curve literature on general-purpose technologies, the paper develops a conceptual framework in which the depth of agentic-AI integration mediates the relationship between readiness practice and realised productivity gain, moderated by sector exposure, firm scale and national labour-market context. Five formal propositions are advanced from a structured review of thirty-eight cited works, of which the paper classifies twenty-seven as substantively engaging at least one of the three readiness dimensions, singly or jointly, and eleven as foundational theoretical grounding rather than dimension-specific evidence. Particular attention is given to India's IT-BPM sector, where labour-cost structure and the readiness gaps identified in national adoption indices interact distinctively with agentic-AI economics. The paper closes with an agenda for primary empirical research — particularly longitudinal and matched-pair designs — needed to move the field from association to causal estimation of the readiness–productivity relationship.

papers.title: Phraseodidactics and Artificial Intelligence in SFL: A Didactic Proposal for Teaching Phraseology through NotebookLM
papers.authors: Mohammed Boughaba
papers.abstract: El presente trabajo propone una secuencia didáctica para la enseñanza de las unidades fraseológicas en español como lengua extranjera que integra la inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG) mediante la herramienta NotebookLM. Desde una perspectiva fraseodidáctica, la propuesta combina el desarrollo de la competencia fraseológica y la competencia digital crítica a partir del principio de anclaje documental (grounding), que restringe las respuestas de la IAG a un corpus de fuentes verificables.La secuencia, diseñada para estudiantes de nivel C1, se estructura en cinco fases: contextualización teórica y digital, alimentación del corpus, análisis fraseológico guiado con validación crítica de resultados, producción creativa escrita y oral, y evaluación integrada. Se analizan las limitaciones de la IAG, como las alucinaciones y las dificultades interpretativas, y se subraya la necesidad de un uso supervisado. Las conclusiones indican que la integración pedagógica de la IA resulta pertinente cuando se articula desde un enfoque crítico y metodológicamente guiado, favoreciendo el aprendizaje significativo de las UF y la alfabetización digital, sin sustituir el juicio experto del profesorado ni la producción lingüística del estudiante.

papers.title: Cognitive Load and Workload in Desktop-Based Educational Virtual Worlds: A Computational Machine Learning and Structural Equation Modeling Study with Computer Science Students
papers.authors: Dimitrios Magetos, Sarandis Mitropoulos, Christos Douligeris
papers.abstract: Educational virtual worlds and metaverse environments are increasingly utilized to foster immersive and experiential learning in higher education. However, their instructional efficacy depends not only on visual fidelity and presence, but fundamentally on how effectively learners’ cognitive resources are managed. This study investigates intrinsic (ICL), extraneous (ECL), and germane cognitive load (GCL) alongside NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) workload dimensions in a desktop-based educational virtual world developed in Spatial.io for an undergraduate Computer Networks course. A cohort of 120 second-year Computer Science students (75 males, 45 females) participated in a five-week intervention designed to model the relationships among cognitive load, perceived workload, and meaningful engagement. A multi-method analytical framework was implemented, combining psychometric validation and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with machine learning techniques (K-Means clustering, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, Decision Trees) and Psychometric Network Analysis. The findings revealed strong internal consistency across the cognitive load scales, moderate overall workload, and significant positive associations between all three cognitive load dimensions and perceived workload, with extraneous cognitive load emerging as the variable most strongly and consistently linked to high-overload cluster membership, frustration, and reduced engagement across the machine learning and network analyses. These results suggest that desktop-based educational virtual worlds may support self-reported germane cognitive engagement, provided that extraneous interface demands are systematically minimized and navigation is scaffolded. The study contributes an empirical and computational perspective to educational metaverse research, offering practical guidelines for designing cognitively sustainable immersive learning environments.

papers.title: A Functional Interpretation of Symmetry and Asymmetry in Human Collision Avoidance and Its Application to Mobile Robot Navigation
papers.authors: Eduardo Zavalla, Eduardo Oliveira Freire, Humberto Alejandro Secchi, Francisco Rossomando
papers.abstract: For robots to navigate effectively in human-shared spaces, they should follow behavioral rules that not only prevent collisions with humans but also reduce uncertainty about the robot’s actions. These rules should be grounded in human collision-avoidance behavior, as humans can often recognize evasive intentions by observing another person’s movements, and robots are expected to exhibit behaviors that allow their evasive intentions to be similarly understood. This paper identifies and characterizes human collision-avoidance maneuvers using a multi-method approach comprising qualitative analysis of video recordings to identify the maneuvers, survey-based analysis to assess self-perceived evasion distances, and computer robot simulator-like human–robot interaction experiments to validate the observed metrics and investigate whether the identified human behavior patterns extend to human-guided robot navigation. A symmetry–asymmetry perspective is then adopted to investigate these maneuvers, and a functional interpretation of the main evasive behaviors is proposed based on their morphological properties and Path Selection Freedom. This interpretation is subsequently translated into human-inspired collision-avoidance strategies for mobile robots through a Behavior Management Module implemented using fuzzy inference mechanisms for maneuver selection and trajectory generation. Beyond the implementation itself, this work establishes a principled basis for transferring the functional principles underlying human collision avoidance to mobile robot navigation, contributing to the development of more natural, understandable, and socially conforming robot behavior in shared human environments.

papers.title: Toward Responsible and Sustainable AI Integration in Education: A Cross-National Analysis of Factors Influencing Teachers’ AI Adoption Using TALIS 2024
papers.authors: Chenhan Zhao
papers.abstract: This study investigates how AI-specific and contextual constructs relate to teachers’ adoption of artificial intelligence, and whether these relationships vary across education systems. Teachers are central to achieving Sustainable Development Goal 4 through responsible AI integration, yet most prior work relies on general technology acceptance frameworks and single-system samples. Drawing on TAM and UTAUT, this study relates AI use to perceived AI usefulness, perceived AI risks, and four contextual constructs: AI-related training, teachers’ stress, institutional support, and school innovation climate. This model was tested with TALIS 2024 data from 1766 lower secondary teachers in the United Arab Emirates and Shanghai, China. Structural equation modeling and multi-group SEM showed that training (β=0.401,p<0.001) and perceived AI usefulness (β=0.250, p<0.001) were the strongest direct constructs associated with AI use. Contrary to expectations, perceived AI risks were positively associated with perceived usefulness in both samples (China: β=0.308, p<0.001; UAE: β=0.390, p<0.001), which suggests that teachers who recognize potential risks may also tend to acknowledge AI’s pedagogical value. Multi-group comparisons showed that institutional support was found to be associated with perceived usefulness only among Chinese teachers, whereas school innovation climate was found to be associated with perceived usefulness only among UAE teachers, though only the institutional-support difference was significant in cross-group tests. These findings point to context-sensitive professional development policies that support sustainable AI integration in education.

papers.title: Eye-Tracking Analysis of Visual Attention and Preference in Human-Created, AI-Generated, and AI-Refined Human Advertisements
papers.authors: André Gonçalves, Margarida Afonso, Pedro Martins, Ana Rita Teixeira
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in advertising, yet its effects on visual attention and preference remain insufficiently characterized. This study compared human-created (H), AI-generated (AI), and human–AI co-created (HAI) advertisements using eye tracking and a forced-choice task. Thirty-nine participants completed 858 trials involving 22 advertisement pairs while gaze was recorded at 60 Hz. Fixation duration, fixation count, time to first fixation, saccadic magnitude, blink duration, and pupil diameter were analyzed using within-subject mixed-effects models with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. AI-generated advertisements were selected more frequently than human-created advertisements, whereas HAI advertisements did not differ from human-created advertisements in choice frequency. Relative to human-created advertisements, both AI and HAI stimuli elicited higher fixation counts and smaller saccadic magnitudes, with these effects surviving Holm correction. No corrected differences were observed in time to first fixation or pupil diameter, and differences in fixation and blink duration did not survive correction. The results indicate that AI-generated and HAI advertisements were associated with a more spatially concentrated pattern of visual exploration, while preference outcomes differed between the two conditions. However, the observed gaze differences cannot be uniquely attributed to creative origin because AI and HAI stimuli also exhibited higher edge density than human-created stimuli. These findings support the use of eye tracking as a sensor-based method for characterizing visual responses to AI-assisted advertising while highlighting the need for tighter stimulus control in future studies.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and AI-Adjacent Digital Technologies in Nursing Practice Within Gastroenterology: A Scoping Review of Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.authors: Sónia Cristina da Costa Barros, Ana Carvalho, Guilherme Macedo, João C. Ferreira, Miguel Mascarenhas
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into clinical gastroenterology, with emerging applications in nursing contexts. However, the extent and nature of these applications in gastroenterology nursing remain under-explored. This scoping review aimed to map the current landscape of AI and closely related AI-adjacent digital technologies in gastroenterology nursing. Methods: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guideline, PubMed, Medline, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for peer-reviewed, English-language studies published since 2000, and the findings were synthesized narratively. Results: Of 184 records identified, 11 studies were included, highlighting the potential of these technologies in clinical decision support, workflow optimization, patient education, and endoscopy assistance. Reported benefits include gains in workflow efficiency, technical accuracy, and reduced administrative workload; direct evidence of improved nursing-led patient outcomes was reported in only a minority of studies. Challenges encompass limited nurse-led research, insufficient external validation, implementation gaps, and ethical concerns. Conclusions: Greater nurse involvement in AI development is essential to drive paradigm shifts in clinical practice. This review synthesizes evidence to inform future applications, research, and policy in AI-enhanced gastroenterology nursing.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Decision Intelligence for Managing Material Shortages in Engineer-to-Order Supply Chains: A Reproducible Simulation Study
papers.authors: Daniel Filip, Violeta Firescu, Livia Filip, Ioan Alexandru Popan, Ionuţ Adrian Chis
papers.abstract: Background: Engineer-to-order (ETO) manufacturing faces material shortages arising from changing requirements and uncertain supply. This study develops Artificial Intelligence–Supply Chain Decision Intelligence (AI-SCDI), linking shortage prediction to feasible interventions under cost and capacity constraints. Methods: Six specialists assessed framework content and parameter plausibility. A locked experiment used 12 synthetic cohorts and 6000 paired Monte Carlo replications per policy, supplemented by model-recovery diagnostics, matched policy ablations, calibration assessment, and joint sensitivity analysis. Results: Histogram gradient boosting achieved a mean precision–recall area under the curve of 0.7587, compared with 0.5399 for logistic regression and 0.7415 for random forest. Under baseline assumptions, AI-SCDI reduced disruption time by 30.0% and synthetic operating cost by 19.1% relative to no proactive intervention. At baseline capacity, estimated-net-benefit selection and abstention contributed more to cost reduction than impact weighting alone. Learner rankings varied across generating mechanisms, horizon-specific calibration showed risk overestimation, and mean net benefit was negative in 19 of 64 informed-parameter scenarios. Conclusions: AI-SCDI provides a reproducible, capacity-constrained decision heuristic. Its benefits remain conditional on synthetic assumptions; external validation and empirical cost calibration are required before industrial effectiveness can be claimed.

papers.title: Between Human and Machine: University Teachers’ Accounts of Judgment, Metacognitive Defense, and Cognitive Offloading in Generative AI Use
papers.authors: Zhen Qiang, Zhuo Wang
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) allows university teachers to delegate cognitive work while deciding how students should engage with it. Using codebook thematic analysis, we examined multi-source accounts from 25 teachers recruited through an AI-focused learning community and its professional networks in China. Materials comprised interviews with 22 teachers, three documentary cases, self-narratives and reflective essays. Three themes organize the findings: reconstructing the teacher role, defending professional judgment, and managing teachers’ and students’ cognitive participation. Participants described disciplinary expertise as a basis for evaluating AI outputs and reported practices intended to retain human engagement. Instrumental and partnership orientations overlapped; descriptive comparison with later use profiles did not establish a simple relationship between partnership language and usage intensity. Because the protocol introduced several focal topics, we distinguish prompted positions from volunteered formulations. The proposed belief–strategy–practice cycle is a heuristic interpretation of retrospective accounts, not a demonstrated mechanism. The study contributes an account of how teachers connect their own cognitive offloading with their reported organization of students’ learning opportunities. Its claims concern this AI-engaged sample rather than university teachers generally.

papers.title: Appropriate Reliance on AI Decision Support Systems: A Sociotechnical Narrative Review
papers.authors: Amirhossein Jabbari, Seyedehmandana Ashrafzadeh, Saba Sarikhani, Seyedmajid Minayhashemi
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly supports human decision making, but effective use depends on whether users assign AI advice the decision weight it warrants. This theory-oriented narrative review synthesizes 29 core studies, together with recent reviews and foundational theory, to examine appropriate reliance, overreliance, and underreliance in AI-supported decisions. The synthesis identifies five recurring sociotechnical conditions shaping reliance: system, user, task, interaction, and organization. Findings show that explanations, uncertainty cues, expertise, self-confidence, prior experience, and organizational incentives affect reliance differently across settings, while trust and reliance evolve through feedback over time. Interventions that reduce overreliance may also increase underreliance. The resulting framework centers warranted behavioral decision weight, comparative evaluation of AI and self-capability, and temporal feedback, shifting attention from increasing trust or AI use toward supporting context-sensitive allocation of decision weight.

papers.title: A Taxonomic Framework Based on Machine Learning for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Healthcare Data
papers.authors: Gelson André Schneider, Moisés Laurence de Freitas, Davenilcio Luiz de Souza, Domingos Rafael Ferla Valladares, Mikael Henrique de Jesus Batista, André Luís Korzenowski
papers.abstract: Objectives: This study presents a generic taxonomic framework as a roadmap for users who wish to implement systems for detecting fraud and waste in health data; this roadmap outlines which unsupervised machine learning techniques can be used to detect anomalies in health data, and whether these anomalies are point, contextual, or collective. Methods: The research employed the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology in five stages: awareness, ideation, development, evaluation, and conclusion. The proposed taxonomic framework was designed through the implementation of the artifact, using the “Sample 1 to Inpatient Claims CMS 2008–2010 Data Entrepreneurs’ Synthetic Public Use File (DE-SynPUF)” database, which contains 66,773 records and 81 features. The dataset was applied to the K-Means, Isolation Forest (IF), and Local Outlier Factor (LOF) algorithms for point anomaly detection. Results: The number of anomalies detected by at least one of the algorithms was 13,966, representing (20.9%) of the dataset; K-Means alone detected 1608 (2.4%), IF alone detected 4522 (6.8%), LOF alone detected 2301 (3.4%), K-Means and IF together detected 4497 (6.7%), K-Means and LOF together detected 41 (0.1%), IF + LOF combined detected 465 (0.7%), and all three algorithms in consensus detected 532 (0.8%). Conclusions: Thus, the taxonomic framework proposed in this study can be viewed as a roadmap for researchers and developers seeking to understand which unsupervised technique to apply in detecting anomalies in health data, considering the type of anomaly.

papers.title: Understanding Youth Screen Time and Mental Health: A Natural Language Processing Topic Modeling Analysis
papers.authors: Matthew R. Rodriguez, Kwangman Ko
papers.abstract: Youth excessive screen time and mental health challenges continue to be a public health concern. Guided by a social cognitive theoretical framework, this study explored the utility of using natural language processing (NLP) topic modeling and qualitative triangulation for understanding how youth-related experiences described in subreddit posts described mental wellbeing from 2017 to 2025 with most of the posts created during the COVID-19 pandemic and afterwards. The study includes 202 r/Teenagers subreddit posts. All posts (n = 202) were analyzed qualitatively, with a subset of these posts that had body text (n = 133) analyzed using topic modeling. A natural language processing latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) was performed to analyze the social media posts and generate topics that represent the social media data, with exploratory input from ChatGPT. In addition, the data were analyzed using qualitative open coding in order to compare the LDA results with the qualitative open coding results. The NLP analysis identified seven topics based on coherence scores and the qualitative open coding yielded three emergent themes. Both the NLP and qualitative analyses revealed overlapping topics/themes pertaining to: (1) online school was challenging and youth needed personal connection with others, (2) youth wanted friends and appeared to use screens for social connection, and (3) youth valued creative activities, such as playing games to foster social connection. This research demonstrates the benefits and limitations of using natural language processing topic modeling for analyzing unstructured text data. It also provides important information regarding the usage of screens and youth mental health challenges.

papers.title: Knowledge Evolution and Paradigm-Level Change in AI-in-Education Research: A Scientometric Mapping and Critical Review (2015–2025)
papers.authors: Sihua Wu, Piyapong Sumettikoon
papers.abstract: Bibliometric commentary increasingly frames the rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a paradigm shift in AI-in-education (AIED) research, yet rarely distinguishes publication growth from genuine reconfiguration of the knowledge base or of teacher–learner roles. This study maps knowledge evolution in AIED from 2015 to 2025 by integrating four analytical strands across Web of Science and Scopus: scientometric mapping (including keyword and reference bursts and co-citation analysis), structural topic modeling (STM), design-weighted coding of full texts, and triangulation across these strands. Two transition windows emerged. The weaker 2019–2020 window (Jensen–Shannon divergence, JSD = 0.058; retained under the permutation rule but not under a stricter interval-based rule) reflects a research-front transition toward learning analytics and prediction, accompanied by knowledge-base reconfiguration but no detectable change in teacher–learner roles. The 2022–2023 window (JSD = 0.187, the period maximum) coincides with the generative-AI surge and couples a newly formed co-citation community with a topic-specific rise in coagency whose direction is clear but whose magnitude is imprecisely estimated. Because these effects concentrate in 36.6% of the weighted corpus and recent citations remain right-censored, we classify the change, under our pre-specified labeling scheme, as localized paradigm-level reconfiguration rather than a field-level paradigm shift. The label is an operational classification within that scheme, not an independent determination that a paradigm shift has occurred.

papers.title: Digital and AI-Supported Game-Based Interventions for Executive Function Development in Early Childhood: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Khawlah Alhejii
papers.abstract: Executive function (EF)—working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility—underpins school readiness, academic achievement, and socio-emotional competence in early childhood (ages 3–8). Digital and AI-supported game-based interventions are a promising but underexamined modality for EF training. This review aimed to synthesize the reported effects of digital and AI-supported game-based interventions on executive function in children aged 3–8 years and the technological features linked to reported gains. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review synthesized 19 studies from six databases (PubMed, PsycINFO, ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore) covering January 2012–March 2026, involving 1890 children aged 4–8 years across 11 countries. Narrative synthesis indicated predominantly positive findings across all three EF components; this was observed most consistently for working memory. Adaptive difficulty calibration, immediate corrective feedback, and motivational scaffolding were the features most often linked to gains; positive findings were somewhat more frequent in school-based settings and in longer interventions, though these descriptive patterns rest on small, unbalanced subgroups and cannot establish setting or duration as moderators. Critically, the corpus was overwhelmingly conventional and rule-based: only three studies (15.8%) contained machine-learning components, with none driving pedagogical personalization (confined to gesture recognition or post hoc analysis); none employed conversational agents or affect-sensing, and no eligible study sampled 3-year-olds. Findings should therefore be read as evidence about adaptive digital game-based interventions rather than AI-driven ones. This near-absence of machine-learning personalization for typically developing children aged 3–8 years is itself a principal finding, alongside gaps in long-term retention, cross-cultural generalizability, and ethical AI data governance.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Ecuadorian Higher Education: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Literature Review of Benefits, Challenges, and Research Gaps
papers.authors: Felipe Emiliano Arévalo-Cordovilla, Ricauter Moises Lopez-Bermudez, Fabricio Guevara-Viejó, Oscar Xavier Bermeo Almeida, Jesmy Flora Castelo González
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education; however, evidence of its research and application in Ecuador remains fragmented. We systematically reviewed the internationally indexed literature on AI in Ecuadorian higher education. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched for peer-reviewed publications from 2015 to 2025. Of the 271 unique records screened, 62 studies met the eligibility criteria; they were appraised using design-specific instruments (MMAT 2018, PROBAST) and analyzed through thematic synthesis across eight axes. The corpus concentrates on 2024–2025 (71%) and is dominated by learning analytics (16 studies) and generative AI (14 studies), followed by perception studies (10 studies). Reported benefits—early warning, efficiency, assessment support, and skill development—rest on technical performance, usability, and satisfaction rather than on measured learning or institutional gains. Persistent challenges include infrastructure constraints, uneven digital competencies, ethical and privacy concerns, and methodologically fragile local evidence; 30 of the 59 appraised studies were rated as having high concern. Ethics, governance, and academic integrity were rarely the primary research objects (two of 62 studies), although 28 raised them as secondary findings. This review derives a research agenda prioritizing governance, pedagogical theorization, methodological rigor, and outcome evidence.

papers.title: Integrating Conversational AI and Interactive Projection Mapping for Cultural Heritage Interpretation: A Framework and Pilot Evaluation
papers.authors: Ponsan Siridechanont, Patiwet Saokong, Teerapong Jatuma, Noppanut Onenaphi, Kannikar Intawong, Kitti Puritat
papers.abstract: Cultural heritage interpretation requires communicating relationships among physical locations, historical narratives, and symbolic meanings while accommodating diverse visitor information needs. Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) enables flexible, visitor-initiated access to cultural knowledge, but conversational interfaces alone provide limited spatial grounding. This study proposes an AI-supported interactive framework that combines conversational AI and projection mapping as complementary mechanisms within a unified heritage experience. Conversational AI supports semantic inquiry, while projection mapping spatially connects curated narratives with corresponding locations on a physical heritage model. The framework was implemented through the Seven Sacred Weeks Interactive Projection Mapping System at Wat Ched Yod, Thailand, with four modes: Tour, AI Conversation, Game, and Exploration. A mixed-methods pilot evaluation was conducted with 90 university students using pre- and post-test knowledge assessments, the System Usability Scale (SUS), and open-ended questions. Immediate post-test knowledge scores were significantly higher than pre-test scores following exposure to the complete system (p < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 1.416), and the system achieved a SUS score of 78. Qualitative findings highlighted spatial visualization, interactive activities, game-based interaction, and AI-supported inquiry, while limitations concerned waiting time, participation capacity, and AI response speed. The findings provide preliminary evidence of the feasibility and usability of coordinating technically distinct but complementary AI and spatial media mechanisms within a visitor-centered cultural heritage experience.

papers.title: Understanding AI Acceptance in Healthcare and ‘Glue Ear’ Diagnosis: A Survey of Clinicians and Service Users
papers.authors: Alexis Bennett, Fei Zhao, Henry Yeomans, Andrew Christopher Hall, Wen Jiang
papers.abstract: Background: This pilot survey explored the views of clinicians and service users regarding the use of AI in a specific diagnostic scenario of OME. Methods: An online survey was conducted in collaboration with a Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement panel and advertised through research and clinical networks, social media platforms. Participants (N = 95; 21–72 years) included clinicians (59%) and service users (32%; patients and carers) with experience of OME. Quantitative and qualitative data were collected and analysed, comparing the views of the two groups across the two contexts. Results: Participants demonstrated a generally positive view of AI in OME diagnostics and in healthcare. Clinicians and service users reported comparable levels of trust and acceptance, although clinicians expressed greater concerns about flexibility and accuracy. Perceived key benefits included time and cost savings, while transparency and trust appeared as pivotal facilitators for acceptance. Frequent concerns centred on operational reliability and ethical considerations, with less emphasis on data confidentiality. Conclusions: The findings indicate broad support for AI applications both in OME diagnosis and more widely in healthcare, contingent on addressing concerns about accuracy, human oversight, and ethical use. Recommendations include focused communication strategies emphasising transparency and human oversight in the clinical decision-making processes.

papers.title: Multimodal Trust Assessment in Human–AI Shared Control Systems
papers.authors: Mengchu Song, Hongyu Zhou, Guohua Wu
papers.abstract: Trust plays an important role in human–AI shared-control systems, yet it is difficult to assess from a single observable signal. This study proposes an event-centered multimodal framework for assessing situational trust by integrating contextual, behavioral, affective, and individual features surrounding critical human–AI interaction events. A controlled autonomous-driving experiment was conducted with 15 participants under high- and low-reliability conditions, yielding 117 valid event-level observations with retrospective trust ratings. The results showed substantial differences in reported trust between reliability conditions and across failure types, while facial and failure-related contextual indicators were among the more informative variables. However, the highly imbalanced trust classes, particularly the limited number of high-trust observations, constrained reliable classification of individual trust levels. The findings only provide preliminary evidence that event-level multimodal observations can characterize information associated with reported situational trust, while also demonstrating the challenges of cross-user trust estimation under limited and imbalanced data. Therefore, the study serves as a methodological and empirical starting point for developing more robust multimodal trust assessment approaches, rather than as a validation of a generalized real-time trust prediction system.

papers.title: Drill-and-practice chatbots for teaching English morphological affixation in international master's students
papers.authors: Dwi Astuti Wahyu Nurhayati
papers.journal: Journal of Research on English and Language Learning (J-REaLL)
papers.abstract: Chatbots are increasingly used in language education, yet research has focused mainly on speaking, listening, vocabulary, grammar, and learner motivation, and findings on their learning effects remain inconsistent. Morphology, especially affixation, is still often taught through lectures and written exercises, which limits student participation and encourages memorization over conceptual understanding. Few studies have examined drill-and-practice chatbots for teaching English affixation, particularly among international master’s students who are also English teachers. This study therefore investigates how these students used a drill-and-practice chatbot to teach English affixation, how they adopted it in diverse classrooms, and how they responded to it. A descriptive qualitative case study was conducted over three months with twenty-two international master’s students who were also English teachers. Data were collected through an observation checklist, interviews, and digital documentation. The findings show three results. First, the chatbot comprised four stages: introducing affixes through songs, identifying affixes, substitution and expansion, and evaluation and review through quizzes and fun facts. Second, teachers’ experiences involved technical adaptation, structural success, and cultural discontent. Third, their culturally responsive approach included word formation, word translation strategies, and cultural competence in digital learning. The chatbot appeared to support morphological competence and teachers’ culturally responsive digital teaching. Its limitations include a small, specific sample and a qualitative design. Practically, teacher educators can integrate such chatbots into morphology instruction. Future research should use larger samples, varied proficiency levels, and experimental designs to test efficacy.

papers.title: AI untuk Desa: Peningkatan Literasi dan Pemanfaatan Kecerdasan Buatan oleh Pemuda Parit Baru, Kabupaten Kubu Raya
papers.authors: Ira Patriani, Akhmad Rifky Setya Anugrah, Roma Tressa, Bima Sujendra
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has created significant opportunities to improve the quality of life across various sectors, including rural communities. Nevertheless, limited digital literacy remains one of the primary barriers preventing rural populations from effectively adopting AI technologies. This community engagement program was conducted by the Faculty of Social and Political Sciences (FISIP), Universitas Tanjungpura, in Parit Baru Village, Kubu Raya Regency, West Kalimantan, with the objective of enhancing AI literacy and strengthening the capacity of rural youth to utilize AI productively. The program employed a participatory and educational approach consisting of community outreach, interactive workshops, practical AI simulations, and the establishment of the Parit Baru Digital Youth Community as a sustainable learning platform. Program effectiveness was evaluated using pre-test and post-test assessments complemented by qualitative observations and participant feedback. The findings reveal a substantial improvement in participants' AI literacy, with average test scores increasing from 42.5 before the training to 76.3 after the intervention. Beyond improved technical competence, the program successfully established an active digital youth community that continues to promote AI-based innovation within the village. These findings demonstrate that participatory technology-based community empowerment can significantly strengthen rural youth's capacity to adapt to digital transformation while fostering sustainable local innovation. This initiative also contributes to the achievement of Universitas Tanjungpura's Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), particularly KPI 2 (community engagement) and KPI 3 (strategic partnerships), while supporting the strategic vision of the University's Institute for Research and Community Service (LPPKM) in promoting technology-driven community empowerment.

papers.title: Developmental Evaluation for Strengthening Digital Ecosystem Readiness: A Policy Analysis of Coding and Artificial Intelligence Implementation in Vocational Schools in Bangka Belitung Province, Indonesia
papers.authors: Peitrik Iwan, Nikmarijal, Suparta
papers.abstract: The integration of coding and Artificial Intelligence (AI) into vocational education is essential for equipping students with 21st-century digital competencies, yet implementation in remote and island regions like Bangka Belitung archipelago province remains fragmented and unsustainable. This study employs Developmental Evaluation (DE) a real-time, adaptive, and participatory evaluation approach (Patton, 2011) to analyze policy readiness and strengthen the digital ecosystem for coding and AI instruction across vocational schools in the province. Using qualitative methods, including in- depth interviews (n = 26), focus group discussions, classroom observations, and policy document analysis, the research assesses readiness across five core dimensions: (1) policy & governance, (2) human capacity, (3) digital infrastructure, (4) curriculum relevance, and (5) industry–academia partnerships. Findings reveal a critical policy–practice gap: while national frameworks such as the Grand Design for Vocational School Revitalization and Kurikulum Merdeka promote digital literacy, local implementation lacks binding regional regulations, standardized teacher competency pathways, equitable infrastructure distribution, and context-based curricula. Only 24% of ICT teachers had received AI-related training, and AI concepts were rarely taught in practice. Through DE cycles of exploration, collective sense-making, and prototyping, stakeholders co-designed adaptive solutions including a provincial roadmap for digital vocational education, offline AI learning modules via WhatsApp, and micro-innovation grants for teacher-led experimentation. The study demonstrates DE’s effectiveness in fostering adaptive capacity, surfacing systemic barriers, and enabling locally owned, sustainable digital transformation strategies.

papers.title: AI-Assisted science lesson planning for innovative pedagogy in resourceconstrained settings: A scoping review
papers.authors: Ezechiel Nsabayezu, Gedeon Habakubaho, Fidele Mweruli
papers.abstract: Science teachers, particularly those working in resource-constrained settings, face persistent challenges related to limited laboratory facilities, large class sizes, inadequate instructional materials, and the substantial time required for lesson preparation and resource development. The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Copilot has created new opportunities to support science teachers in preparing lessons and developing instructional resources. However, evidence on how AI is being used for science lesson planning, its reported educational benefits, and its associated challenges remains fragmented. This scoping review examined the applications, reported benefits, and challenges of AI-assisted science lesson planning, with particular attention to its potential contribution to innovative pedagogy in resource-constrained settings. Following the existing framework, as advanced by previous researchers in about 2 decades ago and reported in accordance with PRISMAScR guidelines, a systematic search of peer-reviewed and grey literature published between January 2020 and May 2026 identified 40 relevant studies.
