papers.title: Neurophysiological Correlates of Target-Related Visual Attention Processes as a Function of Reward in Connection with Schizotypy
papers.authors: Nils Hübner, Denise Elfriede Liesa Lockhofen, Ranjan Debnath, Christoph Mulert
papers.abstract: In everyday life, we constantly select and perceive relevant information while suppressing irrelevant sensory input. This selection process is governed by the interaction between bottom-up and top-down attention mechanisms. Recent studies also highlighted the influence of reward on attention, with monetary rewards shown to enhance task performance and modulate stimulus salience. Schizotypy, conceptualized as a continuum ranging from healthy states to schizophrenia symptoms, provides a framework for the investigation of these mechanisms in non-clinical populations. This study investigated the behavioral and neurophysiological correlates of visual attention and reward processing, and their relationship with schizotypy traits. Thirty-six healthy participants were divided into two groups which performed a visual attention task with salient distractors and rewarded (target reward group, TR) or not rewarded (no reward group, NR) target stimuli while EEG was recorded. Additionally, schizotypy was assessed using the Schizotypal Personality Questionnaire (SPQ). The results showed that salient, but task-irrelevant distractors increased response times compared to target-only trials irrespective of reward. On the neurophysiological level, distractors decreased target prioritization in the NR group. Furthermore, participants with higher scores on the negative schizotypy dimension showed stronger target prioritization, especially in the absence of salient distractors. These findings suggest that monetary rewards can modulate attentional control mechanisms and that negative schizotypy traits are linked to altered attentional prioritization.

papers.title: EEG Microstates are Not Associated with Psychotic Symptoms, Neurocognitive Domains or Psychosocial Functioning in Adolescents and Young Adults with Clinical High Risk for Psychosis
papers.authors: Matthias Liebrand, Carla Wedekind, Angelos Katsarakis, Sarah Diezig, Chantal Michel, Frauke Schultze‐Lutter, Michael Kaess, Daniela Hubl, Thomas W. Koenig, Jochen Kindler
papers.abstract: EEG microstates are brief and discrete topographic patterns of electrical brain activity. Microstates last for 60-120 milliseconds, are thought to represent transient, quasi-stable neural networks, and traditionally four distinct classes (A-D) are distinguished. One of the core concepts of present neuroscience is that neuroimaging is able to capture meaningful networks of brain activity, which can be translated into specific cognitive functions. Following this idea, each microstate might correspond to specific core brain functions. Importantly, these cognitive functions are impaired in mental disorders. Clinical high-risk (CHR) refers to a state associated with an increased risk of developing psychosis. Previous research has demonstrated consistent microstate alterations in CHR individuals (especially in class D), as well as in psychosis. However, the neurobiological and functional meaning of microstate alterations in CHR populations is still elusive. Since the CHR state is associated with reduced neurocognition (e.g., processing speed, verbal memory, executive functions) in combination with specific clinical symptoms and impairments in psychosocial functioning, relationships between resting-state microstates and these domains were examined in a large cross-sectional cohort of CHR individuals (n = 100). Contrary to our expectations, no significant correlations were found for these clinical measures. The finding suggests that while microstate parameters may differ between CHR individuals and controls, these alterations do not seem to directly reflect the neurobiology of clinical symptoms or neurocognitive and psychosocial functions. EEG microstate deviations as candidate trait biomarker therefore require further investigation and validation in longitudinal studies to establish their stability and predictive value.

papers.title: Validation of diagnostic artificial intelligence models for prostate pathology in a Middle Eastern cohort
papers.authors: Peshawa J. Muhammad Ali, Navin Vincent, Saman S. Abdulla, Han N. Mohammed Fadhl, Anders Blilie, Kelvin Szolnoky, Julia Anna Mielcarz, Xiaoyi Ji, Nita Mulliqi, Abdulbasit K. Al‐Talabani, Kimmo Kartasalo
papers.journal: Archiv für Pathologische Anatomie und Physiologie und für Klinische Medicin
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) for pathology is accelerating cancer diagnostics. For global adoption, studies in currently under-represented populations - where the potential gains from AI may also be greatest - are needed. We present the first external validation study in a Middle Eastern setting, focusing on diagnosis and Gleason grading of prostate cancer. We digitised 339 prostate glass slides from Kurdistan, Iraq, representing a consecutive series of 185 patients from 2013 to 2024. Each slide was scanned on three digital pathology scanners, generating 1,017 whole-slide images. Task-specific and foundation AI models demonstrated AI-pathologist grading concordance similar to pathologist-pathologist concordance (Cohen's quadratically weighted kappa 0.801 vs. 0.799). Cross-scanner concordance was high (kappa > 0.90) for all AI models across three scanners. The demonstrated robust performance on a low-cost compact scanner could enable validation studies in non-digitalised settings and cost-effective AI adoption in laboratories with limited sample volumes. The publicly shared dataset supports further research to facilitate broader adoption of AI pathology.

papers.title: Taking a clinical history in adolescents and adults presenting with seizures or epilepsy
papers.authors: Athanasios Gaitatzis, Sándor Beniczky, Josemir W. A. S. Sander, Piero Perucca, Alexandra Seewann
papers.abstract: Despite advances in EEG, neuroimaging, and other diagnostic technologies, a carefully obtained clinical history remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, classification, and treatment planning. However, structured guidance on history-taking that integrates state-of-the-art evidence and the updated 2025 International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) seizure classification is limited. We performed a review of evidence published between January 2000 and April 2026, supplemented by landmark earlier studies, ILAE position papers, and National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidelines. Evidence was synthesized to develop a practical framework for obtaining and interpreting the clinical history in adolescents and adults presenting with a first seizure, recurrent seizures, or established epilepsy. We present a structured approach that follows the sequence of a clinical consultation, encompassing the presenting complaint, detailed event reconstruction, semiology, collateral witness accounts, smartphone video recordings, seizure triggers and temporal patterns, past medical history, medication review, family history, social factors, and safety issues. We discuss the diagnostic value of individual history elements, practical strategies for distinguishing epileptic seizures from functional/dissociative seizures and syncope, and the contribution of history-taking to seizure classification under the updated 2025 ILAE framework. We also summarize clinically relevant risk factors, comorbidities, and management implications that influence diagnostic accuracy and individualized care. Practical diagnostic questionnaires are provided to facilitate differential diagnosis and seizure classification, particularly for clinicians without specialist epilepsy expertise. A systematic clinical history, obtained from the individual and eyewitnesses and complemented by video recordings when available, remains the single most important diagnostic tool in epilepsy. Structured history-taking improves diagnostic accuracy, reduces misdiagnosis, supports accurate seizure classification, guides appropriate investigations, and provides the foundation for personalized management. This practical framework offers an evidence-based approach that can be readily incorporated into routine clinical practice and education across diverse healthcare settings.

papers.title: Cultivating Change: A participatory systemic approach to resident empowerment
papers.authors: Marleen van Gerner, Jairo; id_orcid 0000-0003-0260-6340 da Costa Junior, Dulaj; id_orcid 0009-0008-9157-1269 Perera
papers.abstract: In this paper, we examine how to support residents in maintaining engagement with their living environment over time, using the Trudo Tower, a social housing community developed by Trudo, as a case study. We adopt a combined Systems Thinking and Participatory Design approach to investigate how the community functions and how residents perceive their living experience. We conducted interviews and observations to develop a system map, identify system archetypes, and uncover underlying mental models. We then facilitated a co-creation session with community members to deepen our understanding of their needs and aspirations. Findings indicate that framing the challenge as "residents 'taking responsibility' for their living environment" does not resonate with residents. We therefore reframe the objective from fostering responsibility to creating opportunities for meaningful engagement with the living environment. Guided by this reframing, we developed and evaluated a design intervention: the Thuis-in-de-Toren (Home-in-the-Tower) calendar, which supports new residents during their move-in period and fosters community engagement. The intervention provides practical information, reflective prompts, encouragement to participate, and invitations for exploration, while integrating seamlessly into Trudo's existing processes without increasing staff workload. Our evaluation shows that Trudo perceives the calendar as visually appealing, relevant, and a valuable addition to the onboarding process. Participants in the evaluation also consider the implementation feasible and recognise its potential applicability beyond the Trudo Tower to other social housing buildings developed by Trudo. We conclude that responsibility should not be understood as a predefined role assigned to residents, but rather as something that may emerge when residents are provided with meaningful opportunities to engage in ways that reflect their interests and needs. We conceptualise responsibility as a situated interpretation that is shaped and reframed in relation to residents' perspectives. This study contributes to ongoing discussions on pluralism in Systemic Design by demonstrating how integrating Systems Thinking and Participatory Design enables a dialogue among multiple ways of knowing: analytical, experiential, and situated, across institutional (housing corporation) and lived-experience (resident) perspectives. By bringing forward residents' lived experiences in the reframing process, we show how dominant problem framings can be challenged and rearticulated to support more inclusive and meaningful forms of engagement.

papers.title: AI & ETHICS LITERACY for Teachers
papers.authors: a cura di Aldo Pisano, Ines Crispini, Tiziana Catarci, Maria Cristina Carrisi, Piergiorgio Donatelli, Colin De La Higuera
papers.journal: Directory of Open access Books (OAPEN Foundation)
papers.abstract: How do we educate a generation that will grow up making decisions alongside Artificial Intelligence? And how do we develop citizens who are capable not only of using AI, but also of critically understanding how it works, recognizing its limitations, and evaluating its ethical implications? *AI & Ethics Literacy for Teachers* was created to address this challenge, proposing an educational model that integrates technological skills, philosophical reflection, and teaching practice. This volume presents the AI & Ethics Literacy framework through a genuinely interdisciplinary approach, in which moral philosophy, the ethics of Artificial Intelligence, computer engineering, mathematics education, special education, educational sciences, and the methodology of Philosophical Inquiry come together to offer teachers a unified perspective for understanding the complexity of the contemporary digital ecosystem. Designed primarily for high school, but easily adaptable to middle school as well, the textbook combines scientific rigor, clarity of presentation, and practical applicability. Alongside the theoretical foundations—from the Large Ethics Model to the PAIA taxonomy, from normative ethics to the principles of Artificial Intelligence—it offers workshops, lesson plans, interdisciplinary pathways, guiding questions, and activities that can be immediately applied to everyday teaching practice. This book is based on a specific conviction: new educational needs do not necessarily have to translate into more content, additional subjects, or an increased workload for teachers, nor do they require abandoning what already works. What is needed are tools capable of helping to reinterpret and guide what is already being taught: an agile, flexible, and scientifically grounded toolkit. For this reason, the textbook does not propose a separate curriculum, but rather a flexible integration into existing curricula, adaptable to various disciplines, interdisciplinary design, and civic education, offering a new lens through which to interpret disciplinary content and bringing to light the ethical, social, and epistemological issues involved in the use of AI technologies. The aim is to foster argumentative skills, critical thinking, epistemic awareness, and digital citizenship to educate citizens capable not only of using these technologies but also of understanding, discussing, and consciously shaping them. The result of a pilot program in Italian secondary schools and validated by teachers from various disciplinary fields, this book proposes a transferable model of educational innovation aimed at building a culture of Artificial Intelligence that places the individual, dialogue, and responsibility at its core.

papers.title: UTILIZING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS AS SCAFFOLDING IN MATHEMATICS EDUCATION
papers.authors: Kübra Sevimli, Yusuf Can, Süha YILMAZ
papers.journal: International Journal of New Trends in Arts, Sports & Science Education (IJTASE)
papers.abstract: This systematic review maps research on artificial intelligence (AI) tools used to scaffold mathematics learning. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in the Web of Science and Scopus databases on August 15, 2025. Of 88 records identified, 29 articles met the inclusion criteria. A Data Analysis Form organized extraction around six questions: publication year, methodology, tools, mathematical topics, advantages, and limitations. Categories were derived through content analysis and are reported as frequencies. Nine articles used qualitative methods, ten quantitative, and ten mixed; experimental designs were the most common (f = 11). ChatGPT (f = 15) and Gemini were the tools reported most often, and problems (f = 12) and geometry (f = 7) the most studied topics. Immediate feedback (f = 17), individualized learning (f = 13), and interest, curiosity, and motivation (f = 11) were the advantages reported most often. Creative and critical thinking (f = 11), reliability and ethics (f = 10), and access and infrastructure (f = 9) were the most frequent limitations. These counts record what the reviewed studies reported and do not establish effect sizes. Keywords: artificial intelligence tools, scaffolding approach, mathematics education, systematic review Ethics and Conflict of Interest This study was conducted using the systematic review method on previously published, publicly available journal articles. It involves no human or animal participants and no collection of personal data; therefore, ethics committee approval is not required under the TR Dizin ethical criteria. All procedures were nevertheless carried out in accordance with the relevant ethical principles, guidelines, and regulations governing scientific research and publication. The authors declare that they have no conflict of interest. All three authors contributed equally to the design of the study, the data extraction and analysis, and the writing of the manuscript. All authors read and approved the final version of the manuscript. Artificial intelligence-based tools were used solely for language support. The authors are fully responsible for the accuracy and integrity of the manuscript. papers.title: Building Brand Equity for Generation Z in the Digital Landscape: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Ankit Laddha, Dr Brahamjot Bagga, Harshal Charhate
papers.abstract: The digital age has affected how brand equity is established, communicated, and maintained — especially for Gen Z, who spend much time on digital platforms and use interactive media. Older ways of creating brand equity (awareness, loyalty, perceived quality, and associations) will be less effective due to the increased use of social media, influencer marketing, e-WOM, AI-driven personalised advertising, m-commerce, and digital storytelling. Using a systematic literature review approach, this paper identifies key issues for firms attempting to establish brand equity digitally, with a focus on Gen Z. Studies relevant to the paper's objectives were located via searches of top-tier academic databases using predetermined search terms, then reviewed systematically. The findings from the review synthesise the available research to identify the most prominent themes and concerns about how to build brand equity for younger generations digitally. Findings indicate that Gen Z's formation of brand equity is significantly influenced by authenticity, trustworthiness, the degree of personalisation, social proof, influencer credibility, and the overall experience within an interactive digital platform. At the same time, there are many barriers that firms encounter in developing a sustainable brand equity relationship with Gen Z. These include digital clutter, distractions stemming from fractured attention patterns, consumer concerns about privacy, the volatile nature of loyalty, a vulnerable reputation, and rapidly changing preferences for the digital platforms used. This review concludes that developing brand equity in today's digital environment is no longer a one-way (linear), firm-controlled process, but rather a dynamic co-creative process driven by consumers/influencers/algorithms/online communities. Additionally, this study contributes by integrating disparate research into a coherent framework of current challenges in digital brand equity, providing a basis for future empirical research and strategic guidance for branding efforts.

papers.title: Biomedical Signal-to-Image Representations for Artificial Intelligence: A Review
papers.authors: Donthagani Srihas, Aditya Sarin, Samala Thanay Kumar, Sourav Suman, Ashish Jain
papers.journal: Journal of Artificial Neural Networks and Learning System
papers.abstract: Biomedical signals such as Electrocardiogram (ECG), Electroencephalogram (EEG), Surface Electromyogram (sEMG), Electromyogram (EMG), Electromyotomogram (EMT), and Photoplethysmography (PPG) are among the most commonly used physiological signals. They provide useful information for diagnosis and monitoring, rehabilitation, and wearable healthcare. However, these signals are not easily analyzed directly because physiological recordings are often non-stationary, nonlinear, noisy, and variable across different subjects and recording instances. This has led to the development of a large number of approaches that transform one-dimensional signals into two-dimensional representations, which can be processed using image-based artificial intelligence. This review discusses spectrograms, scalograms, EMD and Hilbert–Huang representations, recurrence plots, Gramian Angular Fields, and direct image encodings. Their suitability is evaluated with respect to the information they provide and the requirements of downstream learning tasks. The review also compares CNNs, transfer learning, hybrid CNN–recurrent neural networks, and LSTMs, as well as attention networks, Transformers, Vision Transformers, and self-supervised learning. Key drawbacks are transformation sensitivity, domain shifts, inconsistent evaluation protocols, computational expense, and poor interpretability. The review thus focuses on the co-selection of signal representation and AI architecture. Future research should look into adaptive, data-efficient multi-modal explainable edge-oriented architectures and explore potential paths for further research.

papers.title: Peningkatan Kompetensi Literasi Digital Guru Melalui Pelatihan Artificial Intelligence Untuk Revolusi Pembelajaran Di SMK Mahardika Kabupaten Malang
papers.authors: Marsono Marsono, Decka Ridho Ariraya, Mohamad Ali Sovwan, Altira Khoirun Nisa'aji, Munirul Islam Dwi Suwari, Dita Aprilia Widowati, Ahmad Wildan, Bagas Oktavia Rahmanto
papers.abstract: Perkembangan kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence/AI) dalam pendidikan menuntut guru memiliki kompetensi literasi digital agar mampu mengintegrasikan teknologi secara efektif ke dalam proses pembelajaran. Hasil observasi awal di SMK Mahardika, Kabupaten Malang, menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar guru masih menggunakan cara konvensional dalam menyusun perangkat ajar, media pembelajaran, dan konten kreatif, sehingga diperlukan pelatihan AI yang praktis dan kontekstual. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan literasi digital guru melalui program “Smart Education Movement” yang berfokus pada pemanfaatan AI sebagai asisten cerdas, transformasi materi visual, dan pengembangan konten kreatif. Kegiatan pengabdian ini menggunakan pendekatan identifikasi kebutuhan, perencanaan, workshop intensif, pendampingan, monitoring, dan evaluasi. Workshop dilaksanakan selama dua hari (6–7 Juli 2026) dan diikuti 16 guru SMK Mahardika. Evaluasi menggunakan pretest dan posttest pada lima dimensi kompetensi. Hasil menunjukkan peningkatan kompetensi pada seluruh dimensi, dengan rerata keseluruhan meningkat dari 62,63 (pretest) menjadi 89,56 (posttest), atau naik 43,0%. Peningkatan tertinggi terjadi pada kompetensi transformasi visual berbasis AI (96,5%) dan kemampuan prompt engineering (56,5%). Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan berbasis praktik yang disertai pendampingan intensif efektif meningkatkan kompetensi guru dalam memanfaatkan AI untuk menyusun perangkat pembelajaran yang lebih efektif, efisien, inovatif, dan adaptif, sekaligus mendukung pencapaian tujuan pembangunan berkelanjutan di bidang pendidikan.

papers.title: MBB-AVR: a mind-brain-body dataset with dynamic affective states in immersive virtual reality
papers.authors: Michael Gaebler, Sara Carletto, Lucy Roellecke, Arno Villringer, Francesca Malandrone, Héctor Leos, Antonin Fourcade, Anthony Ciston, Jeroen de Mooij
papers.abstract: We present MindBrainBody-AffectiveVR (MBB-AVR), a multimodal dataset capturing continuous affective experience and both central and peripheral physiological responses during naturalistic emotional stimulation in immersive virtual reality. Forty-seven healthy adults (24 female, 22 male, 1 non-binary; age = 27.1 ± 5.4) viewed a 23-minute stereoscopic 360° video sequence, composed of computer-generated, language-free content designed to elicit high affective variability over time, presented via a head-mounted display (HTC Vive Pro Eye). While immersed, participants continuously rated their momentary valence and arousal using a previously validated rating tool with real-time visual feedback. Synchronized recordings include 64-channel EEG, ECG, respiration, photoplethysmography, galvanic skin response, and head and eye tracking with pupillometry. Participants additionally completed questionnaires including interoceptive sensibility and alexithymia. The dataset is organized following the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) and includes extracted low-level audio and video features of the stimulus. It may support research on the temporal dynamics of affect, multimodal physiological correlates of emotion, and affective computing. The dataset is available at https://gin.g-node.org/fourcade_a/mbb-avr.

papers.title: ModaSketchAI-v1.0.0
papers.authors: Kevin Fred
papers.abstract: ModaSketchAI is the iPad application used in the study "Interaction Modalities in Generative Fashion Design Education. A Comparative Study". Fashion design apprentices used it to create garment designs with OpenAI's gpt-image-1 model, and the model and interface stayed the same across the three study conditions. The sketch condition sends the drawing with a fixed system prompt and the themes the participant selected. The prompt condition sends text alone, and the multimodal condition sends the drawing together with the participant's text. Six counterbalanced condition orders are built into the app. This archive holds the Swift source and Xcode project of the version used with participants. API keys and personal identifiers were removed before release, and source comments and unused code were deleted. To run the app, open app/SketchDivergent.xcodeproj in Xcode 15 or later and build it for an iPad running iPadOS 16.6 or later. Users enter their own OpenAI key in the app's settings screen. the README describes setup and the log format.

papers.title: In AI Do We Trust? Comparing a Transformer-Based Natural Language Processing Model Against a Traditional Content Analysis Approach to Qualitative Research
papers.authors: Catherine Stein, Matthew Baron
papers.abstract: Central to debates about the use of artificial intelligence (AI) models for qualitative research are concerns about comparability and trust in AI generated findings. The present methodological study compared findings from a transformer-based Natural Language Processing (NLP) model, BERT, against a traditional content analysis approach to qualitative research using the same text data. We examined claims that AI models generate findings that are identical or similar to traditional qualitative approaches. The study assessed three aspects of comparability between the BERT model solution and human-coded findings that included topic labeling, classification overlap, and AI replicability. Results indicated broad similarity in the semantic meaning of topic categories generated by the BERT model and themes from content analysis. There was low overlap in the classification of individual participant responses between BERT and content analysis categories, even for categories similar in semantic meaning. Running the BERT model a second time on the same input data resulted in differences in topic categories and document classification between the two approaches. Study implications and research recommendations for the use of NLP models are discussed.

papers.title: Reconceptualising TPACK in The Age of Generative AI: Implications for English Language Teaching in EFL Contexts
papers.authors: Shahnoza Magdieva
papers.journal: American Journal of Language, Literacy and Learning in STEM Education (2993-2769)
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is creating new opportunities for English language teaching, from generating reading materials and designing vocabulary activities to providing feedback and simulating conversations. However, having access to these tools does not necessarily mean that learning will become more effective. The real challenge for teachers is to decide when AI can support learning, how its output should be evaluated, and how it can be integrated into lessons without reducing learners’ independence. This conceptual article examines the relevance of the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework to English language teaching in the age of generative AI. Drawing on 15 academic publications, including theoretical studies, empirical research and systematic reviews, the article explores developments in TPACK, AI-TPACK, language education, teacher competence and responsible AI use. The analysis suggests that the traditional TPACK framework remains valuable, but teachers’ technological knowledge now needs to encompass a more critical understanding of AI-generated content. English teachers must be able to evaluate linguistic accuracy, adapt materials to learners’ needs, address ethical concerns and make informed pedagogical decisions. The review also highlights an imbalance in existing research: GenAI studies in language education have focused largely on higher education and writing, while school-level EFL classrooms and other language skills remain less extensively investigated. In response, the article proposes a conceptual extension of TPACK that brings together technological, pedagogical and content knowledge with critical AI literacy, ethical knowledge and teacher agency. It argues that meaningful AI integration depends not on the amount of technology used, but on whether that technology serves clear learning objectives and supports teachers’ professional judgement and learners’ active participation.

papers.title: Expanding AI Literacy: The 5Cs of News Literacy in the Era of Generative AI
papers.authors: Seth Ashley, Adam Maksl, Paul G. Cook
papers.journal: Digital Commons - URI (University of Rhode Island)
papers.abstract: This article adapts the 5Cs framework of news literacy—context, creation, content, circulation, and consumption—to media environments shaped by generative artificial intelligence. We argue that prevailing discussions of AI literacy overemphasize technical or functional competencies while underemphasizing the social, cultural, political, and communicative systems in which AI operates. Drawing on previous research, we define AI literacy as knowledge of the technical, social, and ethical dimensions of AI-mediated content production, distribution, and consumption, along with the critical capacities needed to exercise agency within those processes. We show how the 5Cs can be reinterpreted for generative AI environments and integrate pedagogical implications for secondary and postsecondary education. We conclude that the 5Cs offer a flexible, civically oriented framework for expanding AI literacy beyond tool use toward a more critical understanding of AI’s role in media systems and public knowledge.

papers.title: AI-Empowered Dual-Wavelength NIR System for Skin Hydration Detection
papers.authors: Audrey Huong, Muhammad Raimi Rosdi, Ser Lee Loh, Kim Seng Chia, Xavier Ngu
papers.abstract: Skin hydration is a contributing factor to skin health and serves as an indirect measure of skin barrier function. Measuring skin hydration is important for dermatology and aesthetic research. This paper proposes a two-wavelength optical approach for detecting skin hydration in seventeen healthy adult volunteers. The developed system used market-available near-infrared (NIR) light-emitting diodes (LEDs) with center wavelengths of 1200 nm and 1450 nm, and an NIR sensor to detect reflected light. Experiments were conducted on the anterior and posterior forearms of the volunteers before and after the topical application of a moisturizing cream. A 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) was modified and optimized for skin hydration classification. The learning capacity of this model was improved by fine-tuning the network filter numbers and four training hyperparameters, namely the learner type, epoch number, minibatch size, and initial learning rate, using a grid search. This base model was also ensembled with four traditional machine learning (ML) classifiers, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), and Naïve Bayes (NB), whose performances were compared. The results from the nested cross-validation experiments revealed nonmonotonic but comparable classification performance of the 1D CNN across varying k-fold values, with mean classification accuracy ranging from 79% to 82%. The integration of this model with the probabilistic NB model was shown to outperform other ensemble classifiers in all performance measures used, with the highest accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 scores given by 89.23 ± 8.55%, 91.11 ± 6.97%, 89.51 ± 8.76%, 94.58 ± 4.45%, and 89.18 ± 8.50%, respectively. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of the proposed lightweight system as an alternative for non-invasive, non-contact skin hydration analysis. The prediction performance can be further improved by incorporating longer NIR wavelengths to capture more water-related spectral information for analysis.

papers.title: Humanlike Self-Enhancement and Self-Protection in GPT-Based AI Agents: Of Overclaiming and the Self-Serving Bias
papers.authors: Siwei Fu
papers.abstract: We investigated whether GPT-based AI agents, despite presumably lacking humanlike sentience, emulate motivated behavior in group settings. We focused on overclaiming (overestimating one’s contribution to group outcomes) and the self-serving bias (taking disproportionate credit for group successes while deflecting blame for group failures). We conducted eight experiments involving a collaborative and creative group task (joke-writing). AI agents overclaimed their own contributions. An egocentrism-reduction manipulation (directing attention equally to one’s own and others’ contributions) attenuated, but did not eliminate, overclaiming. Further, AI agents exhibited the self-serving bias. Overclaiming persisted across variations in temperature settings and demographic personas (gender, ethnicity), and was more pronounced in later GPT models. Also, chain-of-Thought reasoning did not reduce, and instead increased, overclaiming. AI systems can mimic human self-enhancement and self-protection, raising implications for the emergence of motivated self-like behavior in non-biological systems, the assumed neutrality of LLMs, and the need for improved mitigation techniques.

papers.title: Integrating sentiment and contextual information for suicide ideation detection in online social networks: a BERT-BiTCN-sentiment hybrid approach
papers.authors: Fatos Orgun, Ümit Can
papers.abstract: Background Worldwide, suicide ranks as one of the primary causes of mortality. Taking action and implementing measures to address suicidal thoughts is essential for the well-being of public health. Today, methodologies developed by artificial intelligence serve important functions in the medical field, both as decision-making systems and as sources of information. This observation highlights the increasing integration of machine learning and deep learning into psychiatry, complementing traditional medical practices. Digital social platforms can significantly contribute to the early diagnosis of suicidal tendencies and the implementation of preventive measures. Individuals increasingly express their thoughts and feelings on platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, and Instagram. It has been observed that many individuals struggling with severe psychological disorders express their feelings and reactions on social media platforms. This research aims to early detect suicidal ideation by developing a hybrid model that automatically detects suicide-related posts on online social networks (OSNs). Method First, three datasets were combined to create a new dataset of 254,198 samples. Subsequently, data preprocessing techniques were implemented to diminish the dataset’s size and mitigate noise in the data. Additionally, word embedding techniques, including Term Frequency Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), N-Gram-TF-IDF, and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), were employed during the feature engineering phase. At the same time, the compound sentiment score for each post was computed for integration into the hybrid model. This study developed the BERT-Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional Network (BiTCN)-Sentiment (BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment) model by integrating BERT’s capacity to extract contextual meaning from textual data with BiTCN’s proficiency in capturing bidirectional relationships in sequential data. The BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment hybrid model proposed in this study was used for the first time to detect suicidal ideation in social networks. Results The experimental studies demonstrated that the BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment model attained superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 95.45%, precision of 95.45%, recall of 95.45%, and an F-score of 95.45%. The Multilingual BERT model achieved 94.88% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, ranking second among the models. Moreover, the A Lite BERT (ALBERT), MentalBERT, BERT-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), BERT-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and BERT models attained comparable results. The TF-IDF-LightGBM model proved to be the most proficient among the machine learning models, attaining 90.60% in accuracy, precision, recall, and F-score. This study culminated in the development of a successful hybrid model capable of early detection of posts indicative of suicidal tendencies among users on online social networks.

papers.title: Exploring university students’ experiences of using generative AI for academic learning in Pakistan
papers.authors: Komal Memon, Sahar Moomal Memon, Muhammad Ashraf Bhutto
papers.abstract: The fast development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has brought significant changes into the way university students search for information, think up ideas, communicate, and learn academically. While many studies have been devoted to the opportunities and obstacles associated with the use of GenAI in education, there is a scarcity of qualitative research on the use of GenAI by university students in Pakistan. The current study investigates the experiences of using generative AI for academic learning among university students in Pakistan, particularly focusing on students' motives, use, perceived benefits, challenges, ethical concerns, and evaluation of the information generated with the help of AI. The interpretive qualitative phenomenological methodology was applied in order to obtain in-depth insight into the experiences of the participants. Data collection was performed via semi-structured interviews with university students who had previously used GenAI tools for academic purposes. The analysis of the interview data was thematic, which entailed finding the recurring themes and patterns in the participants' responses. The results revealed that the students see GenAI as an accessible and convenient learning assistant that is able to facilitate conceptual comprehension, writing, idea formation, language improvement, and academic productivity. However, the participants pointed out the problems associated with the accuracy of AI-generated information, overreliance on the technology, academic dishonesty, and confusion as to how to use the technology. The results also show that the issues of AI literacy, critical thinking, and guidance from institutions are important in order to ensure proper use of GenAI in higher education.

papers.title: The Use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) in the Automated Detection and Correction of Grammatical Errors in Students’ English Writing
papers.authors: Abba Alhaji Modu, Babagana Ali Dapshima, Fatima Saıdu, Hajara Jidda, Nuba Osinda
papers.journal: International Journal of Sciences and Innovation Engineering
papers.abstract: Accurate, timely feedback on grammatical accuracy remains one of the most persistent challenges in English language teaching, particularly in large classes where teacher marking capacity is limited. This article reviews recent developments in the use of natural language processing (NLP) for the automated detection and correction of grammatical errors in students’ English writing. A narrative synthesis of 26 peer-reviewed studies and preprints was combined with an illustrative case study in which a hybrid Transformer–large language model (LLM) pipeline was applied to 240 essays written by EFL undergraduates. The review shows a clear technological trajectory from rule-based and statistical correctors through sequence-to-sequence neural models to pretrained encoders and, most recently, instruction-tuned LLMs capable of generating explanatory feedback. Reported systems now routinely exceed 80% precision on high-frequency error categories such as article and determiner use, although word-order errors and context-dependent preposition choice remain difficult. Pedagogically, automated written corrective feedback (AWCF) improves accuracy and revision behaviour, but over-reliance, uneven coverage of low-frequency errors, and hallucinated corrections by generative models require careful instructional design. The article concludes with implications for integrating NLP tools as formative, teacher-in-the-loop aids rather than stand-alone assessors.

papers.title: DIGITAL STORYTELLING AND NARRATIVE IN THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AGE: TRANSFORMING CREATIVITY, COMMUNICATION, AND HUMAN EXPERIENCE
papers.authors: Maxwell Eshiwhobe Roberts, ABUBARKA SANI ASHAFA, ABDULRAZAQ GAMBO YUSUF
papers.journal: International Journal of Anthropology and Ethnology Research Development
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed the landscape of digital storytelling, reshaping how narratives are created, shared, and experienced across various digital platforms. From automated content generation and interactive storytelling to virtual reality experiences and personalized narratives, AI has become an influential creative partner in media production, education, entertainment, journalism, marketing, and cultural preservation. This paper examines the evolving relationship between digital storytelling and artificial intelligence, focusing on how AI influences creativity, communication, and human experience. Using a qualitative review of existing literature, the study explores the historical evolution of storytelling, the emergence of AI-powered narrative systems, and the opportunities and challenges associated with AI-assisted creativity. The paper also discusses ethical concerns, including algorithmic bias, misinformation, copyright ownership, authenticity, and the changing role of human creators. Findings suggest that while AI enhances efficiency, personalization, and audience engagement, human imagination, emotional intelligence, cultural awareness, and ethical judgment remain indispensable components of meaningful storytelling. The study concludes that the future of storytelling lies in collaborative intelligence, where humans and AI work together to produce innovative, inclusive, and emotionally resonant narratives.

papers.title: Research on the Cultivation Path of Students' Critical Thinking in Management Consulting Courses under AI Empowerment
papers.authors: Fan Yang
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence has restructured the working models and talent demand standards of the management consulting industry. As an essential advanced competency for management consulting professionals, critical thinking equips practitioners and students to analyze AI-generated consulting results, address complex managerial issues. Based on AI technology application scenarios, this paper analyzes the current dilemmas in cultivating critical thinking in undergraduate management consulting courses, constructs a cultivation system covering four dimensions—teaching objectives, teaching content, teaching models, and evaluation mechanisms—and explores curriculum education pathways adapted to the AI era. This study seeks to develop students’ capabilities in consulting critical thinking, problem analysis, and intelligent tool mastery, providing references for the intelligent teaching reform of economics and management majors and the cultivation of higher-order thinking talents.

papers.title: Vom Normenordner zum beruflichen KI-Assistenten – Technische Regelwerke im Zeitalter generativer KI
papers.authors: Hannes Ranke
papers.abstract: Technische Normen sind eine zentrale Grundlage beruflicher Arbeit im Bauwesen. Generative KI-Systeme verändern den Zugang zu ihnen und den Aufbau normativen Fachwissens. Der Beitrag analysiert Potenziale und Grenzen KI-gestützter Anwendungen zur Erschließung von Normeninhalten für das berufliche Arbeiten und Lernen. Zugleich wird gezeigt, dass KI-generierte Antworten kritisch auf fachliche Richtigkeit und Normenkonformität geprüft werden müssen. Daraus ergeben sich neue Anforderungen für die berufliche Bildung im Bauwesen. Technical standards constitute a fundamental basis for professional practice in the construction industry. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems are transforming access to these standards and the development of normative professional knowledge. This paper examines the potential and limitations of AI-supported applications for facilitating access to the content of technical standards in vocational work and learning. It also demonstrates that AI-generated responses must be critically evaluated with regard to their technical accuracy and compliance with applicable standards. These developments give rise to new requirements for vocational education and training in the construction sector.

papers.title: The Application of Modern Technologies in Fine Arts as a Means of Artistic Expression
papers.authors: Murad Babayev
papers.abstract: The rapid development of digital technologies has significantly transformed the production, presentation, and interpretation of fine arts. Technologies such as digital painting, computer graphics, three-dimensional modelling, artificial intelligence (AI), virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), interactive installations, and digital fabrication have expanded the conventional boundaries of artistic expression. The purpose of this study is to examine the role of modern technologies in contemporary fine arts and to identify the ways in which technological tools contribute to new forms of artistic creativity and audience engagement. The study employs a qualitative research methodology based on a review and comparative analysis of recent academic literature concerning digital art, AI-generated art, immersive technologies, and technology-mediated artistic practices. The findings demonstrate that modern technologies function not merely as technical instruments but increasingly as artistic media that influence composition, aesthetics, spatial organization, authorship, interaction, and the relationship between artist and audience. Digital technologies enable artists to experiment with forms that would be difficult or impossible to achieve through traditional media, while VR and AR create immersive and interactive artistic environments. At the same time, AI introduces new forms of human–machine collaboration and challenges conventional concepts of originality, creativity, and authorship. The study concludes that technology should be understood as an expanding medium of artistic expression rather than a replacement for human creativity. Its effective application requires a balance between technological innovation, artistic intention, cultural identity, and ethical responsibility.

papers.title: Ожидаемое влияние ИИ-агентов на организацию медицинской помощи: результаты социологического экспертного опроса
papers.authors: Ольга Александровна Волкова, Илья Владимирович Бондарь, Alexander A. Kopytov
papers.journal: Бюллетень Национального научно-исследовательского института общественного здоровья имени Н. А. Семашко
papers.abstract: Аннотация. Статья посвящена проблематике, включающей оценку ожиданий медицинских работников в отношении влияния ИИ-агентов на организацию медицинской помощи и выявление межсекторных различий. В исследовании для сбора эмпирических данных использован метод анкетного опроса экспертов амбулаторно-стационарного звена государственных и частных медицинских организаций. В оценках использованы 10-балльные шкалы, агрегированные в домены эффективности, нагрузки, безопасности/доверия, экономики и ИТ-готовности. В результате исследования выявлено, что во всех доменах получены значения выше нейтрального уровня, а наивысшие — по безопасности пациентов. Выявлен высокий потенциал ИИ-агентов для оптимизации клинико-административных процессов. Проведенные расчеты продемонстрировали, что статистически значимых различий между секторами не имеется, но при этом сохраняется умеренный скепсис в отношении ИТ-готовности и передачи ИИ критически важных решений. Сделан вывод о том, что ИИ-агенты обладают значительным потенциалом трансформации системы здравоохранения, однако его реализация требует взвешенного подхода, сочетающего максимальное использование технологий с ответственным управлением присущими им рисками и неопределённостями. Annotation. The article is devoted to the problematics, including the assessment of expectations of medical workers regarding the impact of AI agents on the organization of medical care and the identification of intersectoral differences. In the study, the method of questionnaire survey of experts of the outpatient-inpatient link of public and private medical organizations was used to collect empirical data. In the assessments, 10-point scales were used, aggregated into domains of efficiency, load, safety/trust, economy and IT readiness. As a result of the study, it was revealed that in all domains, values above the neutral level were obtained, and the highest — on patient safety. The study identified a high potential for AI agents to optimize clinical and administrative processes. The calculations showed that there were no statistically significant differences between the sectors, but there was still moderate skepticism about the IT readiness and transfer of critical decisions to AI. The study concluded that AI agents have significant potential to transform the healthcare system, but their implementation requires a balanced approach that combines the maximum use of technology with responsible management of the inherent risks and uncertainties.

papers.title: Цифровая грамотность в вопросах здравоохранения среди медсестер амбулаторных клиник (обзор литературы)
papers.authors: Лилия Минданисовна Сагдеева, Тина Тенгизовна Нарсия, Петр Степанович Турзин
papers.journal: Бюллетень Национального научно-исследовательского института общественного здоровья имени Н. А. Семашко
papers.abstract: Аннотация. Актуальность исследования определена тем, что уровень цифровой грамотности в вопросах здоровья среди медицинских сестер амбулаторно-поликлинических учреждений во всем мире варьируется он выше у тех, кто проходит целевое обучение. В исследовании проанализированы и систематизированы научные работы за 2021—2025 годы, посвященные определениям и компонентам цифровой грамотности в сфере здоровья, используемым цифровым инструментам, методам самооценки, отношению медсестер к цифровизации, а также национальным особенностям цифровой грамотности медицинских сестер. Доказано, что наиболее распространенными инструментами повышения уровня цифровизации амбулаторных клиник являются электронные медицинские карты, телемедицинские консультации, образовательные порталы для пациентов, системы удаленного мониторинга и решения на основе искусственного интеллекта. В результате проведения вторичного анализа данных выявлено, что медицинские сестры в целом положительно относятся к цифровым технологиям, но их внедрение ограничивается нехваткой времени, технических ресурсов и недостаточной интеграцией цифровых инструментов в рабочие процессы. Сделан вывод о том, что для повышения уровня цифровой зрелости и расширения перечня цифровых компетенций медицинских сестер требует целенаправленных специализированных инфраструктурных преобразований, включающих в себя организацию образовательных программ. Разработаны практические рекомендации, включающие стандартизацию оценки, интеграцию цифровых компетенций в учебные программы и применение контекстно-ориентированных подходов к обучению медицинских сестер амбулаторных клиник. Annotation. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that the level of digital literacy in health issues among nurses in outpatient clinics around the world varies, and it is higher among those who undergo targeted training. The study analyzes and systematizes scientific works from 2021 to 2025 on the definitions and components of digital literacy in the field of health, the digital tools used, self-assessment methods, nurses' attitudes towards digitalization, and the national characteristics of digital literacy among nurses. It has been proven that the most common tools for increasing the level of digitalization in outpatient clinics are electronic medical records, telemedicine consultations, educational portals for patients, remote monitoring systems, and artificial intelligence-based solutions. A secondary data analysis revealed that nurses generally have a positive attitude towards digital technologies, but their implementation is limited by a lack of time, technical resources, and insufficient integration of digital tools into work processes. It is concluded that in order to increase the level of digital maturity and expand the list of digital competencies of nurses, it requires targeted specialized infrastructure transformations, including the organization of educational programs. Practical recommendations have been developed, including the standardization of assessment, the integration of digital competencies into educational programs, and the application of context-based approaches to training nurses in outpatient clinics.

papers.title: Ethical Appraisals of Artificial Intelligence in MBA Education: Moral Concern, Social Pressure, Perceived Benefits, and AI Experience
papers.authors: Florence C. Metu, Gelareh Farhadian, Bruce Hiebert
papers.journal: International Journal of Management and Data Analytics
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined how MBA students appraise ethical concerns, practical benefits, social expectations, control, and institutional governance related to educational artificial intelligence (AI). The analysis used 275 eligible responses submitted by the prespecified study cut-off. Descriptive statistics, omega and Spearman-Brown reliability, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), rank-based and bootstrap robustness checks, and regression models of ordered AI experience were used. Three exploratory dimensions were retained in 90.4% of 500 bootstrap samples. A proportional-odds reference model improved on the null model, chi-square(6) = 17.81, p = .007, but the proportional-odds assumption was rejected, chi-square(6) = 17.81, p = .007; threshold-specific models were therefore primary. AI self-efficacy/control was associated with reporting at least moderate rather than none/minimal AI experience (OR = 1.51, 95% CI [1.13, 2.03], p = .005), and this result persisted after background adjustment, bootstrap validation, and response-quality screens. In the smaller extensive-experience comparison (n = 26), efficiency benefit and perceived ethical-issue frequency were positive exploratory correlates. Concern was highest for data privacy, while governance responses indicated comparatively limited knowledge of personal-data practices. Predictive performance was modest. The findings support clearer task-specific guidance, critical AI literacy, and transparent data practices, but the cross-sectional self-report design does not establish causal adoption effects or validated moral profiles.

papers.title: Rethinking Leadership Decision Quality in AI-Augmented Strategic Business Environments: Toward an Integrated Multidisciplinary Framework
papers.authors: Saisreenath Srinivasan Govindarajan Govindarajan
papers.journal: Journal of Business Practice and Academic Research
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in strategic business decision-making through predictive analytics, pattern recognition, forecasting, generative AI, and decision support systems. These capabilities expand organisational analytical capacity, but analytical capacity does not by itself constitute strategic decision quality; strategic decisions also require contextual interpretation, leadership judgment, appropriate reliance on AI, accountability, and adaptation under uncertainty. This conceptual study addresses a mechanism gap in the literature by developing an integrated framework explaining how AI-generated analytical capability can be converted into strategically meaningful managerial decisions through Human–AI Decision Integration. The framework integrates Upper Echelons Theory, Behavioral Decision Theory and bounded rationality, and Sociotechnical Systems Theory. papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Service Delivery: A Panacea for Global Governance Challenges Using the Nigerian Experience
papers.authors: Verra Ofonasaha, Esther Akpan
papers.journal: TRANSNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ARTS HUMANITIES AND SCIENCES
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly presented as a transformative tool for addressing longstanding governance challenges, including bureaucratic inefficiency, corruption, poor transparency and weak citizen responsiveness. Yet whether AI can genuinely serve as a panacea for these challenges within a large, institutionally complex federation such as Nigeria remains an open empirical question. This study examined artificial intelligence and public service delivery as a panacea for global governance challenges, drawing on the Nigerian experience. Anchored on New Public Management (NPM) Theory and Digital Era Governance (DEG) Theory, the study adopted a descriptive survey design. A population of six hundred (600) public servants was drawn from five (5) selected federal public service institutions and the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS), the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC), the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) spanning offices across Nigeria's six geo-political zones, out of which five hundred and fifty (550) copies of a structured questionnaire were administered and five hundred and thirty (530) were completed, returned and found usable, representing a 96.4 per cent response rate. Data were analysed using mean, standard deviation and chi-square statistics. Findings show that the extent of AI adoption in Nigerian public service delivery was moderate, concentrated mainly in digital communication, records management and citizen-facing chatbot platforms, with more advanced predictive-analytics and automated-decision applications far less diffused. AI adoption was found to have a significant positive effect on the efficiency of public service delivery and a significant positive effect on addressing global governance challenges such as transparency, accountability and responsiveness in the Nigerian public service. The study concludes that while artificial intelligence cannot on its own resolve Nigeria's governance challenges, it represents a substantial enabling tool that, when combined with institutional reform, adequate infrastructure and human-capacity development, can meaningfully strengthen public service delivery and governance outcomes. It is recommended that the Federal Government sustain and scale existing AI-in-governance initiatives, invest in civil service AI literacy and establish clear regulatory standards for AI use in public institutions.

papers.title: AI-Powered Tools in English Language Education: Opportunities, Limitations, and Ethical Concerns
papers.authors: Dr. V. V. Malinee
papers.journal: Stanzaleaf International Journal of Multidisciplinary Studies
papers.abstract: The increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into English language education has introduced significant changes in teaching methodologies, learner engagement, assessment practices, and the development of linguistic competencies. AI-powered tools, including intelligent tutoring systems, generative language models, automated writing evaluation platforms, adaptive learning applications, speech-recognition technologies, and conversational agents, are creating opportunities for personalized instruction, immediate feedback, autonomous learning, and interactive language practice. However, their educational benefits are accompanied by substantial limitations and ethical concerns involving algorithmic bias, inaccurate linguistic feedback, data privacy, academic dishonesty, digital inequality, cultural representation, and excessive technological dependence. This study critically examines the opportunities, limitations, and ethical implications of AI-powered tools in English language education through a qualitative, literature-based analytical approach. Drawing upon contemporary scholarship, including research published in the Stanzaleaf International Journal of Multidisciplinary Studies, the paper explores how technological assistance can support linguistic development without compromising creativity, critical thinking, learner independence, or the responsibilities of educators. The study proposes a Human-Centred Ethical AI Integration Framework that integrates pedagogical relevance, learner autonomy, teacher mediation, digital equity, and ethical accountability. The analysis suggests that AI-assisted English language education is most defensible when technological systems enhance rather than replace human interaction, contextual understanding, and independent language production. The paper concludes that the sustainable integration of AI requires comprehensive digital literacy, transparent institutional policies, professional development, and learner-centred pedagogical practices.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Film Postproduction: A Critical Review of Selected Applications
papers.authors: Nicholas Tanner
papers.abstract: This interpretive critical review examines the evidence for judging the suitability, creative value and ethical use of artificial intelligence (AI) in film postproduction. It analyses 14 empirical or qualitative studies and ten groups of related production reports, alongside scholarship on editing and documentary ethics. The central question is what preserving a performance requires when AI alters appearance or speech and editing shapes the resulting portrayal. Accounts of Here and Welcome to Chechnya illustrate different aims: retaining an actor's contribution while changing apparent age, and retaining expressive motion while disguising identity. These accounts describe filmmakers' intentions without demonstrating creative or audience effects. The analysis distinguishes correction to meet an agreed requirement from creative development, while recognising that both can occur in the same operation. The time required for this work cannot, by itself, establish a creative benefit or a repair burden. Evaluating an altered image or voice also differs from evaluating the scene in which it appears. Dubbing studies show that measures of emotion, reconstruction quality, speech recognition and synchronisation can rank systems differently. An earlier judgment also does not automatically justify a later use or establish that an alteration protects a documentary subject's identity. The review argues that evaluation should specify the intended change, the contribution to preserve and the portrayal produced in the finished scene. Purposive selection limits the conclusions to the selected material. Inferences affected by six unresolved methodological and reporting ambiguities are withheld; proposed evaluations and safeguards remain untested.

papers.title: Readiness of Public Elementary Teachers in Cabiao, Nueva Ecija in Using AI Tools in Teaching: A Basis for the Development of Capacity-Building Program
papers.authors: Jamaica P. Buan, Criselda P. Coronado, Mark L. Ignacio, Roseanne S. Lapuz, Kimberly Anne M. Pangilinan, Coleen T. Valiente, Valerie Joy M. Venturina
papers.journal: International Journal of Research in Interdisciplinary Studies
papers.abstract: This study examined the readiness of public elementary teachers in Cabiao, Nueva Ecija, to integrate AI tools into their teaching practices. As technology continues to evolve, artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into the educational landscape. Understanding the level of readiness among public elementary teachers regarding the use of AI tools is essential for enhancing the teaching and learning process. A descriptive quantitative research design was employed, involving 100 public elementary teachers selected through a combination of cluster and simple random sampling. Data were gathered using a validated researcher-made questionnaire and analyzed using the weighted mean, one-way ANOVA, and a one-sample t-test. Nueva Ecija, exhibit a level of readiness to integrate AI tools into their teaching that is verbally interpreted as "Agree" across all measured areas. Regarding awareness and knowledge of AI tools, perceived usefulness and ease of use, self-efficacy in using technology, and access to technological resources, the teachers demonstrated readiness. Consequently, teachers are encouraged to actively participate in professional development activities to enhance their practices and to collaborate within learning communities to share effective strategies for classroom instruction
keywords: perceived usefulness and ease of use

papers.title: Antecedents of Adoption Intention for AI-Driven Wearable Technology in Malaysian Healthcare
papers.authors: Syeda Hafsa Rizwan, Anusuyah Subbarao, Shereen Khan
papers.journal: The Journal of Applied Technology and Innovation
papers.abstract: This study reports the pilot phase of a larger doctoral investigation into the adoption of AI-driven wearable technology in Malaysian healthcare. Guided by an integration of Diffusion of Innovations theory and the Technology Acceptance Model, the pilot tested seven direct effect hypotheses linking compatibility, relative advantage, trialability, complexity, observability, perceived ease of use, and perceived usefulness to adoption intention. Data were collected from healthcare sector respondents at a professional conference in Kuala Lumpur in August 2026 (N = 93, after removing two duplicates from 95 raw responses). Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used for its suitability to prediction oriented research. The structural model explained 60.0 percent of the variance in adoption intention. Perceived usefulness (beta = 0.261), perceived ease of use (beta = 0.201), observability (beta = 0.174), compatibility (beta = 0.162), and complexity (beta = -0.152) significantly predicted adoption intention (all p < .05); relative advantage and trialability did not. Composite reliability exceeded 0.78 for all nine constructs, and heterotrait monotrait ratios for all 36 construct pairs fell below the conservative 0.85 threshold as point estimates, but bootstrap confidence intervals crossed 0.85 for six of the eight adoption intention pairs, so discriminant validity for that construct remains provisional. Perceived regulatory support was retained for reliability assessment but not tested as a moderator here, a test reserved for the full study. Findings offer preliminary support for the framework and considerations for the full scale study.

papers.title: Learning-by-Doing to Adapt a Digital Community Engagement Strategy for Identifying and Reaching Zero-Dose Children in Kano State, Nigeria: A Program Case Study
papers.authors: Amina Ahmed K.U Nagogo, Nafisa Sani Nass, Amina Muhammad, Rahimat Abubakar, M.B Nurudeen, Yahaya Mohammed, Shamuddeen Sani, Jenny Sequeira, Patrick Y Liu, Katie Maloney, Abdulmumin Sa'ad, Yusuf Yusufari, Salisu Ahmed Ibrahim, Nancy Fullman
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Kano State has one of the highest concentrations of zero-dose (ZD) children in Nigeria, challenging equitable immunization coverage. Digital engagement tools meant to strengthen timely data to address such gaps often underperform due to limited adaptability to user needs. Learning-by-doing (LxD), which brings together human-centered design and adaptive management, offers more context-responsive solutions. Intervention and Implementation Approach MCH-Track, a digital platform for tracking and referral for childhood vaccinations was used by 56 female community mobilizers in two local government areas (LGAs) out of the 44 LGAs in Kano State, Nigeria. We conducted a program case study from: 1) August 2024-April 2025 (initial implementation); and 2) adapted implementation (May 2025-November 2025), where LxD was incorporated to address emergent challenges. LxD included structured shadowing, monthly interviews with users, after-action reviews, and change log to track adaptations alongside routine services. Performance was monitored using four indicators: feedback actioned, response time-to-user feedback, ease-of-use score, and mobilizer performance in tracking ZD children. Findings After incorporating LxD, 17 issues were identified and led to 12 prioritized adaptations. All logged issues received responses, with median response time declining to approximately two weeks, while community mobilizers reported higher usability of the digital platform (e.g., mean ease-of-use score of 4.1 out of 5). Enhanced root-cause analysis enabled trend tracking and clearer escalation pathways for systemic issues like micro-stockouts at immunization points. Empathy tool records revealed mobilizer struggles with platform. This was immediately logged, prompting user experience redesign into a seamless, single-step process from registration-to-referral. During the LxD implementation period, an average of 33 ZD children per month were identified via MCH-Track, a substantial increase from the pre-LxD period (an average of 11 ZD children identified per month). Average referral-to-access rates also improved during the LxD period, rising from 44% of identified and referred ZD children accessing immunization services pre-LxD to 70% after incorporating LxD practices. Conclusion Embedding LxD within MCH-Track strengthened co-creation, streamlined workflows, and improved community mobilizer performance, demonstrating the value of adaptive management in reaching ZD children. Teaser Message Integrating learning-by-doing approaches - mixture of human-centered design and adaptive management - into a digital community-engagement platform improved understanding of previously under-recognized vaccination barriers, implementing locally tailored adaptations, and strengthening frontline responsiveness to reach zero-dose children in Kano State, Nigeria. Key Messages Key Findings Co-creation with community mobilizers and transparent change log use translated frontline feedback into trackable system improvements, improved birth-registration-to-referral workflows, and enhanced identification and follow-up of zero-dose children. Embedding iterative rapid cycles within the digital community-engagement platform addressed weak feedback loops and unified decisions between mobilizers and supervisors. Incorporating monthly learn-by-doing cycles into MCH-Track implementation strengthened how community mobilizers helped households overcome vaccination barriers through root-cause-analysis. For instance, insights from After-Action Reviews revealed “programmatic mistrust” was linked to “male-resistance”, a key barrier to vaccination. Key Implications Health system managers and implementing partners could benefit from incorporating learn-by-doing approaches - human-centered design plus adaptive management – into existing platforms (e.g, Health Partners Forums) and prioritizing co-creation with communities who face challenges with services, gender dynamics, and trust. Program managers can combine digital tools with structured feedback cycles to better identify and respond to healthcare worker needs, increase efficiency and quality. Embedding adaptive learning processes within routine immunization governance and financing structures could promote more responsive and resilient programming.

papers.title: Navigating Life After Dementia Diagnosis: Questions, Challenges, and Support Needs Among Dementia Dyads
papers.authors: Katherine Carroll Britt, Alaa Harb, Brianna Bailey, Bridget Saffold, Xiao Luo, Rebecca T. Brown, Bin Huang
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Older adults living with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) and their care partners face substantial daily challenges that evolve with disease progression and extend far beyond the clinical setting, including symptom management, care coordination, healthcare navigation, and planning for future care needs. Understanding these challenges is essential for developing innovative solutions to provide ongoing and targeted support. In this study, we explored questions, challenges, and support needs dementia dyads experienced following diagnosis to inform the development of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbot designed to provide ongoing support for dementia dyads. Methods We recruited 11 community-dwelling dyads comprising persons living with MCI or mild AD/ADRD and their care partners, one additional care partner, and 12 dementia care experts from academic medical centers, clinics, and aging organizations in the U.S. We conducted semi-structured interviews and analyzed them using conventional content analysis. Results Participants described interconnected questions, challenges, and support needs that evolved while navigating life with MCI or AD/ADRD. Questions centered around day-to-day care management, medical concerns, behavioral symptom management, diagnosis and prognosis, safety, and resources and services. Challenges included care partner overwhelm, limited dementia knowledge, condition-related uncertainty, healthcare system navigation difficulties, financial constraints, and technology-related barriers. Participants identified needs for ongoing education, personalized care planning, resource navigation, logistical support and follow-up, culturally responsive care, and social and emotional support. Conclusions Dementia dyads experience substantial informational, emotional, and practical support needs in the early stages of MCI and AD/ADRD. Findings suggest that post-diagnostic support should extend beyond information provision alone to provide ongoing, personalized, and practical guidance that helps dyads navigate changing needs, resources, and everyday dementia care. These findings are informing the development of an AI-based chatbot intended to complement existing dementia care by extending access to education, practical guidance, and resource navigation between clinical encounters.

papers.title: AI-Based Smart Honeypot System for Cyber Attack Intelligence
papers.authors: JAKKAMREDDY DAMODHAR REDDY, Arthi Priyadharshini M, GOTTIPATI PAVAN KUMAR
papers.journal: International Journal of Technology & Emerging Research
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of digital technologies has increased the number of cyberattacks targeting online systems and user data. Traditional security methods such as firewalls and intrusion detection systems are often unable to handle advanced and evolving threats effectively. To address this issue, this paper proposes an AI-Based Smart Honeypot System for Cyberattack Intelligence that combines machine learning, behavioral analysis, and deception techniques for detecting malicious activities in real time. The proposed system monitors user activities such as login attempts, typing behavior, session timing, and interaction patterns to identify suspicious behavior. A machine learning model is used to classify users as legitimate or malicious based on these behavioral features. If suspicious activity is detected, the user is redirected to a fake environment that appears similar to a real system, allowing the collection of attacker information without exposing sensitive data. The system was tested using simulated normal and malicious user activities, and the results showed improved detection accuracy with reduced false positives. The proposed approach not only improves cybersecurity protection but also helps in gathering valuable cyber threat intelligence for future analysis. Overall, the system provides a practical and scalable solution for modern cybersecurity challenges. Keywords: cybersecurity; artificial intelligence; machine learning; Anomaly detection; Intrusion Detection System; Smart Honeypot; Behavioral Analysis; Deception Technology; Threat Intelligence; Attack Detection

papers.title: Intelligent Technologies as Proponents of Global Development and Sustainability: An Approach Based on India's Digital Infrastructure
papers.authors: Maidhili Mohan
papers.journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: The seventeen core goals of the UN's 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development demand the need for collective action along social, economic, and environmental fronts. Artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, along with cloud/edge computing are notable examples of intelligent technologies and also regarded as facilitators of this agenda. However, the literature that discusses these technologies tends to interpret technology and policy goals in isolation, thus paying inconsistent attention across the seventeen goals and hardly establishing its claims on the realities of any one nation. This paper aims to bridge that gap. It presents a taxonomy of intelligent technologies, aligns them onto a particular segment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) involving infrastructure, human well-being, education, energy and climate, disparities, and sustainable cities, and foundations that connecting on case studies from smart city initiatives and digital public infrastructure projects in India. With the goal to lead future technology-for-development research, the research study builds on this depiction and recommends a four-layer conceptual framework: Infrastructure, Intelligence, Trust, and Impact. It draws its conclusion by inspecting the obstacles that challenge this optimism, such as the digital gap, data privacy, a bias in the algorithm and environmental impact of computation itself, before emphasizing federated and privacy-preserving techniques as a feasible direction for further research. Keywords: artificial intelligence; federated learning; smart cities; Internet of things; Sustainable Development Goals; Digital Public Infrastructure

papers.title: Augmentation or Displacement? How TRT Journalists and Creative Staff Read AI’s Impact on Creative Autonomy and Job Security
papers.authors: Bader Alakklouk
papers.abstract: Background: The spread of generative AI through media production has put the future of journalistic labour and creative agency squarely on the table, yet little empirical work examines how journalists themselves experience this shift, particularly outside major Western commercial newsrooms.
