Methods: This article reports a qualitative study of how media professionals at TRT World and TRT Arabic, the internationally facing divisions of Turkey’s state-affiliated public broadcaster, read AI’s impact on their professional identity and job security, drawing on twenty-two semi-structured interviews with reporters, editors, producers, and creative staff (five reporters/journalists, four news producers, two news editors, two program directors, four craft editors, a creative video editor, an interview producer, a director, an AI ethics specialist, and a quality department specialist), analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results: The findings point to widespread concern that AI-generated content, now capable of producing human-like text, imagery, and audio, devalues human creativity and threatens role security, particularly around transcription, editing, and content-generation tasks. At the same time, staff report using AI tools voluntarily to sharpen their own output rather than replace it, which sets up a real tension between anxiety and pragmatic adoption. Drawing on interview evidence presented throughout, the article develops a Human-Centred AI Adoption framework built on three pillars, redefined creative roles, AI-human collaborative workflows, and upskilling-based job protection, and argues that perceived threat, not actual displacement, is the main barrier to acceptance among TRT staff. Conclusion: The article treats this framework, and the seniority- and role-based patterns reported alongside it, as propositions grounded in a single-institution qualitative sample rather than as generalisable findings, and specifies the boundary conditions under which they may not hold. In doing so, the study grounds debates on technological unemployment in creative industries in first-hand newsroom testimony and connects its findings to the broader literature on human-centred AI design and workforce adaptation to automation.

papers.title: The Managerial Blind Spot Effect Explainable Machine Learning for Strategic Decision-Making
papers.authors: Sai Srujan Reddy Tokala
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is used in strategic decision-making; however, it is not clear whether the use of explainable machine learning leads to more managerial judgment when prediction accuracy is high. This study analyzes the proposed ‘Managerial Blind Spot Effect’ by combining predictive modelling with behavioural analysis applied to the IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset and the AI Decision Dependence and Cognitive Caution dataset. Several models, including Explanatory Boosting Machine (EBM), XGBoost, Random Forest and Neural Network, were tested, and the explanation produced by the native model EBM was enhanced by SHAP-based explanation. The behavioural results revealed that both Trust in AI and Cognitive Caution significantly contributed to an increase in AI Dependence. EBM delivered the best predictive performance with intrinsic transparency. The results highlight the importance of using explainable AI prediction models in conjunction with managerial judgment in dashboards.

papers.title: மனடததன மயயயல: சய அறவம, இயறகச சமநலயம, உலக அமதககன கலவயம
papers.authors: சடகோபன் காளிதாஸ், த வனிதா சடகோபன்
papers.journal: Tamilmanam International Research Journal of Tamil Studies
papers.abstract: In an era characterized by exponential technological progress and artificial intelligence, global society continues to experience widespread conflict, systemic discrimination, and existential anxiety. Modern education overwhelmingly prioritizes technical competence while neglecting fundamental self-realization ("Who am I?"), humanistic ethics, and biological self-awareness. This interdisciplinary study proposes a comprehensive pedagogical and social framework titled the "Philosophy of Humanity" (மானுடத்தின் மெய்யியல்). Grounding its analysis in classical literature, evolutionary biology, physiological cooperation, and dietary biochemistry, the paper presents four key pillars: Evolutionary Equality: Skin pigmentation and morphological differences are demonstrated to be biological adaptations (melanin distribution relative to UV radiation) rather than indicators of racial hierarchy, reinforcing the absolute equality of all human beings from birth to death. Organ-Based Interdependence: The human body is analyzed as a cooperative community of internal organs (heart, lungs, kidneys, liver) that survive through mutual harmony, offering a physiological blueprint for societal cooperation. Biochemical Balance and Nutrition: Examining the digestive limitations of the human gastrointestinal tract, the study emphasizes how a balanced, "six-taste" diet maintains cellular homeostasis and promotes longevity (Ayusu Nooru). Pedagogical Metaphors: Utilizing the metaphors of "The Wall and the Portrait" (where self-awareness is the supporting wall for technical skills) and "The Clean Vessel" (purity of intent in leadership), the study advocates a mandatory educational intervention at age 18 to cultivate universal empathy. The study concludes that embedding self-realization into higher education is essential for building a non-violent, sustainable, and peaceful global community.

papers.title: Generative AI in Education: A Systematic Analysis of its Ethical Implications, Pedagogical and Evaluative Measures in Teaching Processes
papers.authors: Leonel Alexander Burgos Martínez
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has managed to transform educational processes, generating new possibilities in teaching, learning, and assessment, but also important challenges at the academic level. This article presents a systematic review with the aim of analyzing its main implications in educational contexts. Therefore, six research questions were formulated aimed at the redesign of assessments, the implementation of institutional strategies, digital sustainability, the mitigation of algorithmic biases, AI literacy, and its use as an artificial evaluator. The methodological process was based on a structured search in academic databases, then a selection and quality evaluation of the studies. The results show that generative AI can strengthen feedback, personalization of learning, and pedagogical decision-making, as long as it is integrated in a responsible and transparent manner. However, risks associated with academic integrity, bias, and technological dependence are also identified. In conclusion, the incorporation of generative AI in education requires a critical approach, accompanied by institutional frameworks and digital literacy processes that allow its benefits to be harnessed without affecting the quality of learning.

papers.title: From Generative AI to Hotel Brand Advocacy: A Proposed Research Framework
papers.authors: Nguyen Huynh Lam Ngoc, Duong Bao Trung
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly involved in travel planning and hotel choice, yet research has not fully explained how consumers move from evaluating an AI-generated recommendation to responding to the hotel brand being recommended. This paper develops an integrated research framework that connects GenAI-related perceptions with recommendation acceptance and hotel brand advocacy intention. The framework distinguishes two psychological routes. A motivational route links GenAI anthropomorphism with GenAI-evoked inspiration, whereas an evaluative route links recommendation credibility and relevance with trust in GenAI recommendations. Inspiration and trust are subsequently proposed to increase recommendation acceptance, which is further associated with advocacy intention toward the recommended hotel brand. The framework also proposes that lack-of-transparency anxiety weakens the positive effect of GenAI anthropomorphism on inspiration. The Stimulus - Organism - Response (S-O-R) framework provides the overall structure, while customer inspiration, affordance - actualization, fear-acquisition, and commitment - consistency perspectives explain specific relationships. Eight hypotheses are developed, together with a pathway for future empirical validation using a survey of GenAI users and partial least squares structural equation modeling. The framework extends GenAI hospitality research by connecting recommendation-level psychological responses with a downstream hotel-brand outcome.

papers.title: Nafasi ya Maabara ya Lugha kama Njia ya Kuimarisha Matumizi ya Akili Unde katika Mafunzo ya Lugha katika Vyuo Vikuu
papers.authors: Benard Odoyo Okal
papers.abstract: Maendeleo ya kisayansi na kiteknolojia yamechangia pakubwa uundaji wa nyenzo zinazoweza kutumiwa katika maabara ya lugha na kuingiza programu za Akili Unde katika mafundisho ya lugha. Hivyo basi, lengo kuu la makala haya ni kutathmini nafasi ya maabara ya lugha kama njia ya kuimarisha matumizi ya Akili Unde katika mafunzo ya lugha katika vyuo vikuu. Matokeo yanaonesha kuwa kuna aina nne za maabara ya lugha: tuli, tamba, ya zana za kibinafsi, na kimtandao. Aidha, kuna aina mbalimbali za Akili Unde zinazoweza kutumiwa katika maabara ya lugha na zinazoainishwa kiutendajikazi kama vile: programu ya uigaji mazungumzo yaani chatbot (Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Gemini); vifaa vya usanifu wa picha (Adobe Express, Microsoft Designer, AutoDraw, Canva AI); vifaa vya usanifu wa vipindi na uundaji yaliyomo (Curipod, Magic School.ai, School AI, Eduaide.ai, Google NotebookLM); vifaa vya kusaidia ufundishaji (Padlet TA, Grouper, Socrait, Gablin Tools); vifaa vya kuzalisha mijarabu ya maswali au ukadiriaji (Question Well, Formative AI); na vifaa vya tafakari, mwitiko na ushirikiano (Mirror Talk, Magic Padlet, gotFeedback by gotLearning, Englighten AI, Snorkl, Class Companion, Grammarly).

papers.title: Enhancing pawnshop service innovation in the digital era: A qualitative study on customer experience and operational transformation at Pegadaian Wonosari
papers.authors: Eka Puji Srilestari
papers.journal: Journal of Economic Resilience and Sustainable Development
papers.abstract: Background: The digital era compels traditional financial institutions, including pawnshops to innovate. However, studies on pawnshop digital transformation balancing operational efficiency with trust-based, relational services remain limited. This study explores the dual impact of digital service innovation on customer experience and operational transformation in a pawnshop context. Method: This qualitative, interview-based case study was conducted at a public pawnshop in Indonesia (Pegadaian), which also funded the research; this dual role is disclosed for transparency. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews (n = 4), non-participant observation, and document analysis, and were thematically analyzed using an interactive model of data condensation, display, and conclusion drawing. Findings: Results reveal a duality, digital tools enhance transactional convenience and back-office efficiency but create a relational gap in customer trust for complex transactions and introduce workforce adaptation challenges. Customers abandoned digital channels for high-value or repeat pawn transactions, citing the absence of face-to-face reassurance. Frontline staff reported added reconciliation duties and role ambiguity, relying on informal peer learning rather than formal retraining. Branch managers observed routine transactions shifting to digital channels, while trust-intensive services remained counter-bound. Interpreted through Service-Dominant Logic and digital transformation theory, technology acts as an operant resource that must augment, not replace, human-centric value co-creation. Conclusion: Successful innovation requires a digitally-augmented service model that aligns internal process optimization with preserving trust-based customer relationships. By sustaining trust-based access to microfinance amid digital disruption, this model strengthens the economic resilience of low- and middle-income households and supports sustainable, inclusive financial development. Novelty/originality of this article: This article contributes a novel, integrated framework for digital transformation in trust-intensive microfinance, uniquely identifying the persistent relational gap and workforce adaptation dissonance as critical, underexplored factors in the pawnshop sector's evolution.

papers.title: Analisis Persepsi Pengalaman Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence dalam Skripsi terhadap Kemandirian dan Locus of Control Mahasiswa Pendidikan Teknik Bangunan Universitas Negeri Malang
papers.authors: Vincentia Kayla Stevanie Subowo, Fadila Fitria Wulandari, Muhammad Aris Ichwanto, Eko Suwarno
papers.journal: Jurnal Yudistira Publikasi Riset Ilmu Pendidikan dan Bahasa
papers.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in higher education has provided students with new opportunities to facilitate academic writing, including thesis preparation. However, AI use also raises concerns regarding student independence and their beliefs about control over academic outcomes (Locus of Control). This study aims to describe the levels of AI use, independence, and Locus of Control among students in the Building Engineering Education program at Universitas Negeri Malang during thesis preparation. A quantitative descriptive approach was employed, involving 93 students currently writing their theses. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed descriptively to identify the tendencies of each variable. The results indicate that AI use falls into the high category, with a mean score of 63.53. Meanwhile, student independence falls into the moderate category, with a mean score of 33.27. Locus of Control is also in the moderate category, with a mean score of 26.53, although students demonstrate a predominantly internal orientation. These findings suggest that students utilize AI as an academic support tool while maintaining independence and confidence in their own abilities to complete their theses. Therefore, AI use should be accompanied by critical thinking, independent decision-making, and academic responsibility to ensure that technology supports the thesis-writing process without replacing students' active involvement.

papers.title: From Entity Resolution Anomalies to Reconstruction Failure Modes: A Taxonomic Note Following Minimum Viable Digital Identity Optimization (DIO)
papers.authors: Daniel Beránek
papers.abstract: This taxonomic note refines the vocabulary of Entity Resolution Anomalies developed in The Crisis of Entity Resolution in Heterogeneous AI Environments and follows the adversarial reduction introduced in Minimum Viable Digital Identity Optimization (DIO): From Adversarial Reduction to the Semantic Field Dynamics of Digital Identity.It proposes a non-exclusive, multi-level diagnostic taxonomy of Reconstruction Failure Modes. The taxonomy distinguishes four analytical domains: Referential Reconstruction Failures, Semantic Coherence Failures, Temporal Reconstruction Failures, and Contextual Adequacy Failures.Referential failures include Entity Substitution, Merge Failure, Split Failure, and Entity Omission. Semantic Fragmentation is treated as a Semantic Coherence Failure; Temporal Discontinuity and Temporal Misalignment as Temporal Reconstruction Failures; and Contextual Displacement as a Contextual Adequacy Failure.The note preserves Identity Collapse as a phenomenon-level concept rather than redefining it as a branch of the failure taxonomy. It also removes Semantic Vulnerability from the hierarchy of realized failures and treats it instead as a robustness-related property, whose direct conceptual counterpart is Semantic Robustness.The purpose is not to replace the earlier anomaly vocabulary retroactively, but to increase analytical resolution, distinguish realized reconstruction failure from susceptibility to destabilization, and create a clearer basis for future diagnostic and empirical work within Digital Identity Optimization (DIO).Canonical archival version: The canonical archival version of this preprint is deposited in Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23269323.AI disclosure: This note was developed with AI-assisted conceptual refinement, adversarial testing, red-team review, and editorial support using ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol), Gemini Pro 3.1 Preview, and Perplexity. All AI outputs were reviewed and selectively revised by the author. The conceptual decisions, interpretations, and final content remain the sole responsibility of Daniel Beránek.

papers.title: Neural Correlates of Food Stimuli in Task Switching
papers.authors: leif erik langsdorf, Daniel A Darnstaedt, Torsten Schubert
papers.abstract: Previous research provided evidence that affective task content selectively modulates switching-related control processes in task-switching, i.e., the trial-by-trial reconfiguration of task sets. Specifically, switch costs, the performance decline on switch compared with repetition trials, were larger when switching toward an affective than toward a neutral task. This asymmetry has been attributed to inhibition of the affective task set when performing the neutral task, which may hamper its subsequent reactivation. In contrast, mixing-related control processes, i.e., the maintenance of multiple task sets in working memory, remained unaffected. Here, we asked whether this selective modulation of control processes, explainable by the inhibition account, generalizes to other affectively and motivationally salient task material. To address this question, we investigated, in two experiments, whether food-related task content produces a comparable modulation of switching- but not of mixing-related control processes during cued task-switching. Participants switched between classifying food stimuli as sweet or savory and digits as odd or even while electroencephalography was recorded. Experiment 1 employed a cue-target interval of 1200 ms, whereas Experiment 2 used a reduced interval of 700 ms. Across experiments, switch costs were higher when participants switched toward the food task than toward the digit task, indicating asymmetric switch costs, which was accompanied by a reduced amplitude of the cue-locked switch-related positivity over parietal sites for a switch toward the food task compared to the digit task. In contrast, neither the mixing costs nor the cue-locked mixing-related positivity differed between tasks. Together, the findings suggest that food-related task content selectively modulates the reconfiguration of task sets on a trial-by-trial basis, while processes associated with maintaining multiple task sets remain comparatively unaffected. The findings demonstrate that motivationally salient task content can systematically shape preparatory cognitive control during task switching.

papers.title: Relational Role Attribution: A Unifying Construct in Human–AI Interaction
papers.authors: Michael J Gazzanigo, Xiao Yang
papers.abstract: How users come to perceive an AI not merely as capable but as intentionally oriented toward them in a specific relational capacity remains undertheorized. We propose relational role attribution (RRA) as a discrete psychological construct addressing this gap, positioned as a precursor to downstream relational outcomes rather than a reframing of trust. A PRISMA-ScR scoping review charted 1223 reports at full text against a registered protocol, including 466. Of 179 records excluded for establishing no relational or social role for the agent, 122 (68.2%) nonetheless manipulated or measured anthropomorphism: the field reaches the cue and stops short of the attribution. RRA comprises two concurrent components, a relational inference of social orientation and a role assignment drawn from contextual and communicative cues, checked against the expectancy the user brings. Naming the attribution allows findings accumulated separately across marketing, teaming, and communication literatures to constrain one another, and scaffolds role-specific design principles.

papers.title: Emotional Comfort at a Cost: The Dynamic Role of Social Chatbot Use in Daily Loneliness, Well-Being, and Interpersonal Interaction
papers.authors: Yun Chen, Yue Ding, Linxin Wang, Yu Kou
papers.abstract: As generative AI chatbots increasingly serve as emotional companions, understanding their implications for users’ emotional and social lives is critical. This 14-day diary study involving 97 social chatbot users examined how daily loneliness relates to chatbot engagement and subsequent psychosocial outcomes. Bayesian multilevel models showed that on days when participants felt lonelier than usual, they reported longer chatbot use and stronger emotional engagement. Notably, these two forms of engagement showed distinct associations with daily outcomes. Emotional engagement was associated with higher daily subjective well-being but shorter interpersonal interaction duration, whereas longer usage duration was associated with lower interpersonal interaction pleasure. Mediation analyses reflected the same patterns. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing behavioral from emotional engagement with social chatbots and suggest that emotional benefits and interpersonal costs may coexist in everyday human–AI interaction, informing the responsible design and balanced use of social AI companions.

papers.title: Storytelling and Preschool Children’s Creativity: From Traditional Narratives to Digital and AI-Supported Learning
papers.authors: Wan Xiaohui, Loy Chee Luen
papers.journal: International Journal of Academic Research in Progressive Education and Development
papers.abstract: Storytelling in preschool children’s education has been a well-established practice for many years. However, the majority of existing research has been scattered throughout the realms of traditional storytelling, picture storybooks, digital storytelling and even more recent artificial intelligence (AI) supported storytelling practices. Consequently, a synthesis of research that systematically explores the various manifestations of storytelling in relation to preschool children’s creativity and learning is lacking. This study examines the ways in which a variety of forms of storytelling support children’s creativity, imagination, language and literacy, cognitive development and emerging co-creativity. Utilizing a library research design, the study retrieved and reviewed journal articles, conference papers, books and other academic sources. Sources were selected that had been published between the years 2000 and 2026. The resulting body of literature was analyzed thematically to create four categories of storytelling: traditional storytelling, language and literacy, cognitive development and digital/AI-supported creative storytelling. The findings of the study reveal that, in addition to facilitating children’s imagination and creative expression, storytelling also contributes to children’s vocabulary, comprehension, verbal expression, narrative thinking and literacy. In addition to these outcomes associated with traditional forms of storytelling, digital storytelling also supports children’s cognitive learning and a range of skills including narrative writing, observation, classification and prediction. Recently, AI-supported creative storytelling has begun to be researched with a focus on children’s verbal creativity, reporting increases in children’s fluency, flexibility and elaboration; however, results for originality have been less consistent. The study concludes that storytelling has evolved into a highly multimodal, interactive and co-creative site of pedagogy and that traditional and technology-supported storytelling can be integrated in order to support preschool children’s creative learning.

papers.title: A Project-Based Hybrid Learning Model Using Artificial Intelligence to Enhance Students' Self-RegulatedLearning
papers.authors: Surya Priyambudi, Yulis Setyowati, Alven Safik Ritonga
papers.abstract: Students' SRL ability in the English Literature Study Program at Universitas Wijaya Putra remains low, as shown by a preliminary survey recording a mean SRL score of 2.21. This is worsened by post-pandemic hybrid learning implemented without pedagogical design for learning independence, and by the absence of a model integrating PjBL, hybrid learning, and an AI to improve SRL. This study develops a PjBHL model assisted by an AI through a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model. The model maps Zimmerman's three SRL phases forethought, performance, and self-reflection into project-based and hybrid learning syntax, with AI acting as metacognitive scaffolding and a cognitive interlocutor. Feasibility was tested through expert validation and a practicality questionnaire, while effectiveness was tested through a quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group design involving experimental and control groups. Results show the model is valid and practical based on expert and user assessments, and effective in improving students' SRL compared with conventional learning. This study contributes theoretically through a new, structured pedagogical model, and practically by helping lecturers foster students' learning independence in the AI era.

papers.title: Discovering Causal Factors Influencing Student Academic Performance Using Causal Discovery and Inference
papers.authors: Biswaraj Baral, Roy Taposh Dutta, Thapa Bhesh Bahadur
papers.journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Understanding the true cause-and-effect relationships of factors involved in an academic setting is crucial for the development of effective strategies to enhance the performance of students. Mostly used approaches based on correlation analysis and machine learning models are designed to capture the statistical associations and make predictions, which are not sufficient to support robust decisions about interventions. This study proposes an automated framework which is the integration of three main areas, namely correlation analysis, causal discovery and causal inference, in order to analyze the true causal factors responsible for the performance of students using “student performance dataset” from UCI Machine Learning Repository. As a first step, the correlation based analysis is performed to identify linear association among variables. To show that correlation alone is not enough, causal discovery algorithms are employed to uncover the underlying causal relationship in dataset. Different algorithms such as PC, GES, LiNGAM are used, with LiNGAM based discovery being selected as it produces a fully directed acyclic graph (DAG). As a final step, the discovered causal graph is then used to model the causal inference system to estimate the causal effect of different variables on the performance of students using backdoor adjustment and linear regression algorithm. The results demonstrate some factors like previous performance grades (G1 and G2), study time, paid classes, internet access exhibit a strong causal effect on the final grade of students. Some factors like previous failures, parental status, excessive going out lowers the students' grades. Some features have minimal or negligible impacts on the exam performance. This indicates that intervening on these factors in the academic domain could enhance the performance of students. Compared to correlation based methods, the proposed causation analysis provides directional and interpretable causal relationships, thereby making it easier to understand the underlying causal mechanism and supporting better decision-making.

papers.title: A Diagnostic Evaluation of Small Language Models for Offline Writing-Feedback Tutoring in Brazilian Portuguese: A Study on Structural and Pedagogical Adherence under Public-School Infrastructure Constraints
papers.authors: Randerson Oliveira Melville Rebouças, Marcelo Magalhães Foohs, Rosa María Vicari
papers.journal: Journal of the Brazilian Computer Society
papers.abstract: The adoption of generative Artificial Intelligence in education has relied largely on proprietary modelsb that depend on broadband connectivity, an assumption incompatible with the material reality of most Brazilian public schools. We report a controlled diagnostic evaluation of eight open Small Language Models (SLMs), executed strictly in a local, offline environment against a metalinguistic rubric derived from Ingedore Koch’s Textual Linguistics: 312 primary inference calls (8 models × 13 canonical scenarios × 3 repetitions) without any grammatical coercion mechanism, together with 100 counter-experiment calls, with categorical comparisons by Fisher’s exact test. Two failure regimes emerge. The first is zero-shot structural non-adherence: 100% typological divergence in the Llama 3.2 family (1 B and 3 B) and in Phi-3 Mini. For Llama 3.2 this behaves as a deterministic formatting bias, invariant both to sampling temperature and to the client transport layer and fully reversible by a minimal in-context demonstration (one-shot), which sets it apart from genuine compositional incapacity; the design is behavioural and does not establish the bias’s origin. The second is pedagogical superficiality in Qwen 2.5 3B-Instruct, the only structurally conformant model in the deployable range. We state its evidentiary status first: this is an exploratory single-model analysis whose instrument is a lexical screen over Koch’s terminology, so its figures corroborate the diagnosis rather than carry it. The model mobilizes the rubric terminology in only about half of the runs (51.3%), and it does so unstably, with a single scenario out of thirteen eliciting it in every repetition; two external teachers judging the same runs for metalinguistic focus credit 66.7% and 64.1% of them, agreeing with each other at κ = 0.72 but with the lexical screen at only 0.28 and 0.43, so the screen is a lower bound on the construct rather than a measure of it. Read against a specialist reference of 65 feedback turns from five experienced teachers, coded descriptively into eight mediation functions (κ = 0.83), the model’s mediation concentrates on format-forced recognition and open expansion, stays well outside the expert corrective core, and never models a repair or reinforces the student’s autonomy. We report this as a pattern and not a measurement: two independent codings of the same responses by external teachers converge on that shape, recording recognition and reflection at identical rates and the two absent functions at zero, while three of the corrective functions occur too rarely in this corpus for their reliability to be estimated. We conclude that, in the regime evaluated here (zero-shot prompting, local CPU-only inference, Q4 quantization, no grammatical coercion), off-the-shelf generalist models are insufficient for fine-grained writing-feedback tutoring in Brazilian Portuguese, which motivates specialized models fine-tuned on curated pedagogical corpora. The boundary is deliberate: a single in-context demonstration reverses the structural failure, so the finding characterizes an operating regime rather than a fixed limit.

papers.title: Evaluation Through a Gender Lens: Foregrounding Global South Reflections and Experiences
papers.authors: Sonal Zaveri, Amrita Gupta, Sibongile Aurelia. Sithole, Silvia Salinas Mulder, Anuradha Chatterjee, Shyam Singh
papers.abstract: Gender-focused evaluation in the Global South is often framed through colonial and Western epistemologies that appropriate diverse local experiences while minimizing and reproducing structural oppression, cultural domination, and knowledge hierarchies. As a result, evaluations may recognize context or Indigenous knowledge only superficially, address intersectionality partially or unevenly, and can inadvertently reproduce Global North logics, limiting progress toward substantive gender equality and social justice. Drawing on a targeted review of Global South feminist scholarship, synthesis of recent Three Horizons forecasting work, and four Global South case studies from Latin America, South Asia, and the Middle East, this article: (a) identifies elements distinguishing Global South feminist theorizing from dominant Global North approaches; (b) proposes a Global South decolonized framework for gender-transformative feminist evaluation organized around five interlocking domains—power dynamics, intersectionality, inclusion and representation, methodological approaches, and ethics; and (c) illustrates how these domains reshape evaluation design, evidence generation, interpretation, and use. The case studies illustrate power blindness in evaluations, co-creation of feminist monitoring and evaluation systems with structurally excluded groups, gender-transformative evaluation of masculinity norms with adolescent boys, and social network analysis of gendered norm enforcement. The overall analysis reveals that gender-transformative feminist evaluations require not only individual evaluator reflexivity but also structural transformation of Global North-dominated evaluation mindsets and systems. Together, the findings offer practical framing and vocabulary for commissioners and evaluators seeking to embed Global South feminist perspectives across the evaluation cycle, moving beyond tokenistic inclusion toward substantive transformative practice.

papers.title: AI and Evaluation: Exploring Made in Africa Approaches for Transformational Practice
papers.authors: Varaidzo Faith Magodo-Matimba, Linda Raftree
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) presents both transformational opportunities and challenges for evaluation practice in an era of interconnected global crises. This article examines how evaluators can engage AI in ways that align with the transformational imperative and decolonial commitments, rather than reproducing extractive or exclusionary practices. The central questions guiding this inquiry are: How can AI technologies be adopted within evaluation practice without reproducing colonial patterns of extraction and dominance? What essential infrastructures and competencies do evaluators need to integrate AI systems responsibly within transformational agendas? Drawing on “Made in Africa Evaluation” (MAE) and “Made in Africa AI” (MAAI) as intersecting movements, the article examines tensions between growing interest in AI and fundamental concerns about current AI systems. Environmental costs (energy and water use), extractive labour arrangements, and Western-biased datasets raise questions about alignment with transformational imperatives. The concentration of AI development within Western corporations further challenges decolonized evaluation efforts. Through a decolonial analysis of MAE and MAAI experiences, we show how these movements clarify both practical opportunities for AI-enabled evaluation and the risks of reinforcing existing power asymmetries. Together, they offer pathways toward AI adoption that centers African contexts, languages, and epistemologies while promoting equitable and sustainable evaluation practice.

papers.title: PROJETONÓS PROPOMOS! E O ENSINO DEGEOGRAFIA: CONSTRUINDO CIDADESSUSTENTÁVEIS COM PARTICIPAÇÃO,INOVAÇÃO E COMPROMISSO SOCIAL
papers.authors: Cecília Silva, Jairo Rodrigues Silva, Talita Valadares
papers.abstract: This work, developed by students from the Federal Institute of Minas Gerais (IFMG), Ouro Preto campus, aimed to analyze the main problems existing in the Bauxita and Lagoa neighborhoods. To this end, bibliographic research was conducted to understand the historical context, the formation process, and the main problems of these localities. In the subsequent stage, a structured questionnaire was developed and applied through fieldwork. The data obtained were systematized and analyzed, allowing the identification of the most recurring demands pointed out by the community. Among the main problems identified, the poor condition of the sidewalks, the insufficiency of green areas, and the lack of spaces for leisure stand out. Based on the results obtained, interventions aimed at improving urban quality were proposed, including the implementation of green areas using the Miyawaki method, the revitalization of sidewalks based on the principles of tactical urbanization, and the recovery of the lagoon using artificial intelligence tools, considering the needs indicated by the residents of the Lagoa neighborhood. Furthermore, the development of the project enabled the strengthening of the interaction between students and the local community, contributing to the academic training of the students and to the construction of proposals aligned with the identified social demands.

papers.title: Reframing Authorship and Ethics in AI-driven and Immersive Architectural Environments: A Transdisciplinary Review
papers.authors: Nataliia Vergunova
papers.journal: Journal of Architectural/Planning Research and Studies (JARS)
papers.abstract: This article presents a comprehensive transdisciplinary review of the ways in which artificial intelligence(AI) and immersive technologies are transforming foundational concepts of authorship, ethics, and creativitywithin contemporary architecture and spatial design. The traditional notion of the architect as a singular,authoritative creator increasingly is challenged by computational processes that introduce generative, autonomous,and distributed forms of design agency. Through a synthesis of architectural theory, AI ethics, media studies,and posthuman philosophy, the review interrogates the shifting locus of authorship in design environmentsmediated by intelligent systems and extended reality (XR) platforms. At the core of this inquiry is an ontological reframing of authorship, informed by scholars such as RosiBraidotti, Tony Fry, Humberto Maturana, and Anne-Marie Willis. These frameworks position the architect notas an originator of form, but as a participant in a relational field of human and non-human agents, includingalgorithms, data, environments, and users. Adopting an ontological design lens, under which design practicesand their tools co‑produce forms of life and ways of world‑making, the article argues that AI/XR systems donot merely assist representation but actively configure professional authorship, agency, and ethics. This framinglinks practical workflows to normative guidance for disclosure, responsibility, and education. The review exploreshow generative design, neural networks, and parametric modeling redefine design intention and originality,situating authorship as a curatorial and computationally entangled process. In parallel, immersive media suchas virtual and augmented reality introduce new forms of user co-authorship and spatial manipulation, promptingethical questions about consent, agency, presence, and the authenticity of digital space. The article maps emerging discourses around design accountability, legal attribution, algorithmic bias, anddata governance, proposing an expanded ethical vocabulary for posthuman design practices. Through a criticalexamination of scholarly literature, experimental studios, and case-based applications, the review identifiesepistemological and practical challenges in reconciling human-centered traditions with distributed technologicalagency. Ultimately, this article argues for a redefinition of authorship as a dynamic, ethically situated, andontologically pluralistic concept in architecture. It advocates for the development of integrative frameworksthat embed ethical foresight and philosophical reflexivity into AI-augmented and immersive design methodologies.By repositioning the architect as a negotiator within hybrid systems of creativity and control, the articlecontributes a forward-looking perspective to architectural theory, technological practice, and planning discourse.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Cyber-Physical Attacks on Digital Signaling Processing System (DSP)
papers.authors: Isobo Nelson Davies
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTER SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY E-ISSN
papers.abstract: Digital Signal Processing (DSP) systems are at the core of modern cyber-physical infrastructures, powering applications in automotive, healthcare, telecommunications, industrial control, and aerospace domains. However, their resource-constrained design and deterministic execution expose them to a wide spectrum of cyber-physical attacks that can compromise both digital integrity and physical safety. This paper presents a comprehensive review of cyber-physical attacks on DSP systems, analysing vulnerabilities across hardware, software, communication, and algorithmic layers. A structured taxonomy is proposed, categorizing attacks into deception, disruption, and destruction, while real-world case studies illustrate their practical impact. Existing defense mechanisms are examined, ranging from hardware isolation and secure firmware updates to anomaly detection and hybrid security architectures, with a comparative analysis highlighting their strengths and limitations. Finally, open challenges and future research directions are identified, emphasizing the need for lightweight cryptography, resilient DSP architectures, adversarially robust machine learning, and standardized security frameworks. The review concludes that securing DSP systems requires a layered, interdisciplinary approach that balances performance with robustness to safeguard critical infrastructures against evolving threats.

papers.title: AI-Driven Predictive Modeling of Marriage Rates in Nigeria: Analyzing the Roles of Tradition, Education, Age and Socioeconomic Status
papers.authors: Nnenna Esther and Omankwu Ugwuja
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTER SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY E-ISSN
papers.abstract: This study presents an AI-driven approach to predicting marriage rates in Nigeria by analyzing the influence of socio-cultural and economic factors. Despite the central role marriage plays in Nigerian society, existing literature provides limited insight into how tradition, geopolitical zones, age, physical attractiveness, educational attainment, family background, and employment status collectively affect marital trends. This research applies supervised machine learning techniques— including logistic regression, decision trees, and random forest classifiers—to develop predictive models based on demographic data and survey responses. The analysis reveals that age, educational qualification, and employment status are the most significant predictors of marriage likelihood. Traditional norms and regional affiliations also contribute substantially, though their influence varies across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones. The study underscores the value of artificial intelligence in modeling complex social phenomena and offers a replicable methodological framework for social forecasting in diverse cultural settings. The findings have practical implications for policymakers, sociologists, and religious institutions seeking data-driven insights into marital behavior, and highlight the transformative potential of AI in interdisciplinary social research.

papers.title: Comment on “Evaluating of the readability of ChatGPT-generated responses on travel health risks”
papers.authors: Lyka Jane Castillote Ang
papers.abstract: The study by Zeynep Demirtaş Özyılmaz [1] provides a valuable contribution to digital literacy research by addressing a critical gap in artificial intelligence (AI)-generated health communication.It raises significant concerns about the accessibility of such information for lay users.The study's comprehensive quantitative analysis of ChatGPT-3.5'sperformance in answering travel health queries demonstrates methodological rigor through the application of numerous established readability indices, including Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Coleman--Liau, and ARI.This multi-metric approach enhances the reliability of the findings and provides robust evidence.In summary, the findings show that ChatGPT responses consistently scored at college reading levels (mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 35.82, grade level 13.25).Moreover, none of the responses met the seventh-grade reading level required by the US Department of Health and Human Services.Previous literature has documented similar readability barriers in online health content [2][3][4].However, despite the standardized measures, the study may inadequately capture real-world users' comprehension and engagement patterns, suggesting the need for complementary user-centered evaluation approaches.Hence, future endeavors should include mixed-methods approaches combining quantitative readability assessment with qualitative evaluation of user comprehension, including simulated decision-making scenarios.This recommendation is supported by Golan et al.'s cross-sectional study [5].Additionally, evaluating GPT-4 across multiple languages and diverse cultural contexts would enhance the global relevance of travel health applications.Similarly, Özyılmaz noted the need

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and the Development of English Writing Skills
papers.authors: Milan Pegu
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can provide English learners with immediate explanations, alternative expressions, and feedback during composition. Its educational value depends on whether this assistance strengthens independent writing rather than merely improving a submitted text. This narrative review examines 40 journal articles, including 20 contributions from Indian scholars or Indian research contexts, to analyse relationships among AI assistance, writing processes, feedback engagement, and learner agency. The synthesis distinguishes empirical classroom findings from conceptual proposals and separates generative systems from earlier automated writing tools. Evidence supports carefully guided feedback and revision activities, while claims about sustained learning require stronger longitudinal verification. Indian multilingual settings introduce questions about language identity, unequal access, and the transfer of ideas across languages. A teacher-guided sequence of independent drafting, focused AI consultation, reasoned revision, and unaided transfer assessment is proposed. The review concludes that generative AI can support English writing development when learners retain responsibility for meaning, evidence, and linguistic decisions.

papers.title: Technology and Artificial Intelligence Law in India: A Critical Analysis of Legal Challenges, Regulatory Framework and Emerging Jurisprudence
papers.authors: K Jagadish
papers.journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Technology has become an essential part of modern society, influencing almost every aspect of human life, including communication, commerce, healthcare, education, banking, governance and the administration of justice. Among the most significant technological developments of the twenty-first century is Artificial Intelligence (AI). Artificial Intelligence refers to computer systems capable of performing tasks that traditionally require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, prediction, decision-making, language processing and image recognition. The rapid development of AI presents considerable opportunities for economic and social development, but it also creates complex legal and ethical challenges. Questions relating to privacy, data protection, discrimination, algorithmic bias, intellectual property rights, cybercrime, intermediary liability, consumer protection, employment, surveillance, deepfakes, autonomous systems and accountability have become increasingly important. India does not presently have a single comprehensive legislation exclusively regulating Artificial Intelligence. Instead, the legal framework is distributed among constitutional principles, the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, intellectual property legislation, criminal law, consumer protection law, contract law and sector-specific regulations. Government policy initiatives, including the National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence and the Responsible AI framework developed by NITI Aayog, have also contributed to India's emerging AI governance framework. The Supreme Court of India has developed important constitutional principles concerning privacy, freedom of speech, informational autonomy and technological governance. Decisions such as Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v Union of India, Shreya Singhal v Union of India, Anuradha Bhasin v Union of India and Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v Union of India (Aadhaar) provide a constitutional foundation for addressing several AI-related concerns. However, specifically AI-generated content, AI authorship, algorithmic decision-making and liability for autonomous systems remain comparatively underdeveloped areas of Indian jurisprudence. This paper critically examines the existing Indian legal framework governing technology and Artificial Intelligence. It analyses constitutional rights, data protection, cyber law, intellectual property, intermediary liability, AI-generated content, deepfakes, algorithmic discrimination and emerging jurisprudence. It further compares selected international approaches and proposes a balanced Indian regulatory model based upon innovation, transparency, accountability, human oversight and protection of fundamental rights. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Technology Law, AI Governance, Data Protection, Privacy, Algorithmic Bias, Cyber Law, Deepfakes, Intellectual Property, Digital Personal Data, Constitutional Law, Intermediary Liability.

papers.title: From Web Data to DIY Ideas: Material-Based Project Generation Systems
papers.authors: Shengyan Xu
papers.abstract: This article investigates and explores the prototype of a material based project generation system, aiming to transform online DIY content into structured design knowledge for sustainable reuse. Based on an unfinished system developed by the author in his early years, this work reviews the methods of collecting unstructured data from the Internet, extracts key information through lightweight natural language processing, and normalizes it into a unified model suitable for automatic generation. Discussed baseline strategies for retrieving and editing project generation, as well as evaluation metrics that consider constraint satisfaction, feasibility, and user experience. The paper also investigates practical applications in personal creativity support, maker education, and community recycling, supported by initial human in the loop implementation and interactive segmentation code that links material understanding with basic robot operations. The challenges of multimodal alignment, richer constraint modeling, and robust dataset construction have been identified, highlighting opportunities for future integration with digital twins and automated assembly. Although the original system is still incomplete, the study concludes that a practical and impactful pipeline is achievable, demonstrating how artificial intelligence can help users recycle materials more effectively and contribute to sustainable, resource-saving designs.

papers.title: Intelligent Robots for Elderly Care: Categories, Application Scenarios, and Challenges
papers.authors: Junrui Zeng
papers.abstract: Aging populations have increased the demand for intelligent, personalized, and emotionally supportive elderly care services. Traditional care models often face limitations such as high labor costs, insufficient service continuity, and limited emotional support. Deep learning-driven elderly care robots provide a promising solution by integrating perception, decision-making, human-robot interaction, and adaptive service functions. This paper reviews the major categories of intelligent elderly care robots, including rehabilitation robots, nursing robots, and companion robots. It further discusses their application scenarios in home care, nursing homes, and community-based care. Existing studies show that deep learning, machine vision, multimodal sensing, and large language models can improve motion assistance, health monitoring, emotional interaction, and personalized companionship. However, several challenges remain, including technical reliability, data privacy, ethical risks, high deployment costs, and user acceptance among older adults. Future development should focus on lightweight models, multimodal fusion, privacy-preserving learning, and human-centered design. Intelligent elderly care robots should not replace human caregivers, but should support them in providing safer, more efficient, and more compassionate care.

papers.title: Exploring Vocational School Students' Conceptualizations of Artificial Intelligence Through Metaphors
papers.authors: Didem ALSANCAK SIRAKAYA, Mustafa Sırakaya
papers.journal: Journal of Learning and Teaching in Digital Age
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) encompasses systems engineered to execute cognitive functions, including perception, reasoning, and decision-making. Advancements in big data and deep learning have facilitated the proliferation of AI in sectors such as healthcare, education, manufacturing, and transportation, concurrently prompting discussions on ethical and safety concerns. AI enhances education by facilitating personalized and data-informed learning via adaptive platforms, automated assessments, and virtual assistants. This study examined vocational school students' perceptions of AI using metaphors, which elucidate abstract concepts and uncover cognitive patterns. A qualitative, phenomenological approach was employed to collect data from 198 students through an online survey utilizing the prompt “AI is like… because…”. The analysis adhered to systematic metaphor procedures, and expert review validated a high degree of reliability. The results revealed 82 distinct metaphors that represent diverse perspectives. The recurrent use of metaphors such as “human,” “human brain,” “assistant,” and “facilitation” suggests that students perceive AI as possessing human-like qualities and as a supportive entity. Alternative metaphors characterize AI as technological instruments (robots, machines, programs) or repositories of information (libraries, web browsers). In addition to the beneficial aspects of assistance and facilitation, apprehensions regarding the risks and uncontrollability of AI have arisen. In conclusion, vocational students view AI as a practical, human-like tool that improves life, while also recognizing the uncertainties associated with the technology. The findings highlight the dual aspects of AI perceptions in educational settings, merging optimism with caution.

papers.title: EVALUATIVE STUDY OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES IN NIGERIA
papers.authors: Blessing N. USORO, Phillip U AKOR, Juliana Akpan Benson
papers.journal: GLOBAL ACADEMIC INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF LIBRARY AND INFORMATION SCIENCE (GAIJLIS)
papers.abstract: University libraries are increasingly expected to adopt advanced digital technologies to improve information access, service delivery, and user engagement. However, the extent to which these technologies are adopted and utilized in Nigerian university libraries remains unclear. This study investigated the level of adoption, perceived use, influence on users’ patronage, and challenges associated with digital technologies in Nigerian university libraries. A cross-sectional survey design was employed. Data were collected from 854 undergraduate students and electronic librarians across four Nigerian universities using a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and simple linear regression were used for data analysis. Findings revealed that commonly adopted and used technologies included artificial intelligence search tools, mobile technologies, e-learning applications, online databases, and social media platforms, while advanced technologies such as robotics, RFID, and big data systems were minimally adopted. Digital technologies enhanced user engagement, learning experiences, remote access to librarians, and resource sharing; however, the level of adoption did not significantly predict users’ patronage. Major challenges identified were inadequate funding, limited infrastructure, lack of skilled personnel, irregular staff training, behavioral resistance, and fear of job displacement. The study concludes that Nigerian university libraries are experiencing gradual digital transformation but remain constrained by financial, infrastructural, and human capacity challenges.

papers.title: Brainstorming with the Enemy No. 14 — The Scarce and the Scared
papers.authors: Daniel Jacquérioz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The fourteenth essay in Brainstorming with the Enemy starts from the clocks the public quotes most, such as Earth Overshoot Day, and finds that the most quoted are the least used to decide. The Earth is open to energy and almost closed to matter: nothing is used up, it is moved, mixed or dispersed. Every factor of production is a fixed base times a multiplier that can grow, and a thing is scarce only when its multiplier grows more slowly than the demand for it. Multipliers grow at the speed of technology times the speed of permission, so most of the scarcity that binds rich societies is made by people, and the story of scarcity is itself a tool, used to frighten people into action or into stillness. The essay proposes the Multiplier Test, with a self-contained mathematical addendum offered for testing. Concept proposed by the author: the Multiplier Test. Written in part with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model. The ideas, editorial decisions and responsibility for the content are the author's.
