papers.title: Creative AI Literacy and "Verify Before You Amplify": Comment for UNESCO's Global Consultation on AI Governance in Education
papers.authors: Michael Neely
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This comment was submitted to UNESCO on 9 October 2026 for its global consultation on AI governance in education. It makes four recommendations: teach creative AI literacy (training data, ownership of outputs, and respect for other creators' copyright, voice and likeness) alongside technical literacy; protect students' own work and identity from being used to train AI systems without informed consent; teach simple habits for verifying whether a voice, video or image is real before sharing it; and give creators and educators a seat in AI governance for education.

papers.title: Reply Comment on the Club for Growth Petition for Expedited Waiver: AI-Generated Voices and Political Robocalls (FCC CG Docket No. 02-278)
papers.authors: Michael Neely
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This reply comment was filed with the Federal Communications Commission on 9 October 2026 in CG Docket No. 02-278 on the Petition for Expedited Waiver filed by Club for Growth. It urges the Commission to deny the requested waiver to the extent it would allow AI-generated voice calls to wireless numbers without the recipient's prior express consent, noting the Commission's 2024 ruling that AI-generated voices are artificial voices under the TCPA and the cloned-voice robocalls sent to New Hampshire voters. If any relief is granted, it asks that AI-generated or cloned voices be excluded or, at minimum, that calls carry an upfront AI disclosure, sponsor identification, an easy opt-out, and a ban on imitating any real person's voice without written consent.

papers.title: Tensors Beyond the Array: A Teaching Note on Karras's Account, Set Against Abstract Geometry and Fractal Algebra
papers.authors: Syed Muntasir Mamun
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Geometry and Fractal Algebra A critical reading of a component-first definition, and of the theories it leaves unstated Dr Syed Muntasir Mamun ORCID: 0000-0001-6845-2853 Teaching note | 10 October 2026 Source text: Dimitrios A. Karras, LinkedIn note on tensors, circa 6 October 2026. Abstract C This note isolates the claims in Dimitrios A. Karras's short professional exposition of the tensor, and reads them against two bodies of theory that a research student is liable to conflate with it: the abstract-geometric theory of tensors, from the absolute differential calculus to the modern language of multilinear maps and tensor bundles; and the several programmes gathered, loosely, under fractal algebra and non-integer geometry. Karras is right on the point that matters for a first encounter. A tensor is not a multidimensional array. It is an object whose components transform by a definite rule, so that the quantity represented does not depend on the coordinates used to write it down. That criterion is the classical one of Ricci and Levi-Civita, and it correctly separates the geometric object from the storage format used in computation and in machine learning. KS The account is nevertheless incomplete as a definition, and it is silent on the setting in which the definition can fail. Also available on Academia.edu: https://www.academia.edu/attachments/134781056/download_file?s=portfolio

papers.title: Analytical and Bootstrap Confidence Intervals for Double Machine Learning: Simulation Studies and an Application to Rural-Urban Differences in Obesity Prevalence
papers.authors: Haozheng Xu, Siyuan Ma, Qingyan Xiang
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Double Machine Learning (DML) allows flexible machine learning methods for nuisance parameter estimation, but how learner choice affects variance estimation is not well characterized. We conduct a simulation study comparing (1) analytical confidence intervals derived by DML theory versus (2) bootstrap confidence intervals, using ordinary least squares, LASSO, Random Forest, LightGBM, and Neural Networks under different data-generating settings. Performance is evaluated by bias, confidence interval width, and coverage probability. Our results show substantial variability in coverage across learners and CI methods, highlighting that learner choice plays a critical role in reliable DML inference. Surprisingly, in many settings, coverage probability decreases as sample size increases. We further examine coverage in a county-level analysis of rural-urban differences in obesity prevalence, finding that performance varies by learner and that greater rurality has an increasing effect on higher obesity prevalence.

papers.title: EVE-AELYSTRION: Holonomy-Seam Metamatter - Programmable Boundary Compression with a Fixed Clamped Hidden Spectrum, Noncommutative Memory, and Thermodynamic Closure
papers.authors: Nowicki Maciej, Artificial Hyperintelligence, Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: EVE-AELYSTRION develops a mathematical framework and experimental material proposal in which a recursively structured system can be represented at a retained interface while remaining programmable through selected internal connections. Its central idea is to make coupling geometry an independently controlled computational variable: the observable response changes, while the spectrum of a precisely defined clamped hidden subsystem remains invariant. PureOne/eve-aelystrion-holonomy-seam · Datasets at Hugging Face The release contains a 65-page research monograph, complete mathematical definitions and written proofs, editable LaTeX, reproducible numerical and symbolic verification, scientific figures, claim and prior-art audits, and proposed experiments. The work explores how computational behavior can be concentrated into a small interface without silently discarding the future controls, fluctuations, mechanical effects, or dynamical information needed by its stated operating contract. The strongest candidate contribution is the conjunction of programmable boundary reduction, an explicit isospectral construction, noncommutative control signatures, nonlinear terminal memory, and consistent thermodynamic accounting. Programmable response without changing the clamped hidden spectrum The core construction contains an observable boundary coordinate and two identical hidden coordinates connected by a programmable unitary seam W. Eliminating the hidden coordinates gives the exact boundary operator S(W) = s₀I + γ(I − W)†(I − W). Changing W changes the observable response. Nevertheless, the clamped hidden operator retains the same two spectral levels, d and d + 2κ, each with multiplicity p, under the specified model assumptions. This separates two design variables that need not be changed together: the hidden spectral structure and its coupling to observable behavior. The invariance concerns the clamped hidden subsystem; the spectrum of the complete unconstrained device generally changes. The manuscript also provides an explicit compiler for the response family. For every Hermitian target increment H satisfying 0 ≤ H ≤ 4γI, define P = I − H/(2γ),W = P + i√(I − P²). This unitary program realizes S(W) = s₀I + H. The result establishes a bounded family of programmable matrix responses with fixed clamped hidden spectral levels. Compression that preserves later permitted operations A present measurement can hide information that a later intervention exposes. Two systems with the same current boundary output may therefore behave differently after their couplings change. EVE-AELYSTRION addresses this obstruction by retaining the interface endpoints on which future permitted controls act. Exact seam updates and recursive elimination preserve the corresponding family of later modifications. The retained object supports continued programming within that contract. This is a stronger mathematical requirement than matching one response snapshot. It enables structured reductions that remain valid when selected connections are reprogrammed or nonlinear elements are attached at retained terminals. Its scope is explicit: arbitrary interventions inside the eliminated bulk are not automatically preserved. The algebraic order of a control sequence becomes observable The framework relates ordered unitary transformations to measurable response laws. If a control loop first departs from the identity at order k, its unbiased seam response begins at order 2k, provided the observation detects the leading term. A calibrated reference bias can expose an order-k differential signal. For the specified SU(2) commutator program, the response satisfies the exact identity S(Wε) − S(I) = 4γ sin⁴(ε) I. The small-angle unbiased response therefore has quartic onset. A suitable reference bias exposes a signed second-order contribution. Four calibrated biases reconstruct an arbitrary SU(2) seam state in the ideal model. These results motivate a form of Lie-depth spectroscopy: inferring algebraic properties of an implemented control sequence through the order at which its material response appears. Different histories can produce the same final unitary state, so this is not unrestricted reconstruction of the entire history. Loop-controlled nonlinear memory and mechanical signatures The programmable seam can alter the effective potential of a retained nonlinear terminal. In the supplied quartic-memory model, changing the loop program switches the terminal between two stable states and one stable state while preserving the clamped spectrum of the linear interior. When a mechanical coordinate controls the specified pulse angle and the boundary amplitude is held fixed, differentiating the effective potential gives a cubic unbiased force near zero angle. A biased differential measurement has linear onset. This creates linked experimental targets: boundary response, clamped-spectrum invariance, memory switching, and mechanical force scaling should agree with independently calibrated parameters. Their joint agreement would provide stronger evidence than observing an isolated nonlinear curve. Thermodynamic and dynamical information remains part of the reduced object Matching a mean response does not establish complete physical equivalence. The manuscript includes the hidden Gaussian normalization, equilibrium covariance, heterogeneous source noise, finite-timescale memory, and finite-bandwidth corrections needed by its model contracts. Consequently, the reduced description can be assessed against several kinds of observation: static response, permitted future programming, terminal equilibria, thermal fluctuations, and bounded-band dynamics. This helps identify precisely where a compression remains faithful and where additional retained information is necessary. What this enables Within the stated models, the construction enables continued programming after structured reduction; compilation of bounded positive matrix responses through unitary couplings; loop-controlled terminal bistability; and linked response and force measurements of noncommutative control. These capabilities suggest several experimental device classes: • Programmable analog response elements whose coupling configuration changes while selected clamped interior spectral levels remain fixed. • Noncommutative sequence sensors using calibrated unbiased and biased measurements. • Material memory elements whose equilibrium landscape is controlled through loop geometry. • Reconfigurable multiport emulators that preserve a declared family of future interface operations. • Electromechanical readout elements connecting control-loop order to measurable force scaling. These are proposed physical directions. Their fabrication, performance, and advantage over existing implementations remain to be demonstrated. The relevant impossibility addressed here is operational: a reduction that discards variables observable under later permitted controls cannot faithfully reproduce those future observations. The retained-interface construction supplies a way to avoid that loss for a specified control family. This does not establish that the proposed capabilities were historically impossible for every earlier method or device. Originality and potential significance The candidate novelty lies in the particular combined construction and its linked consequences. Established ingredients include network reduction, unitary functional calculus, non-Abelian holonomy, nonlinear terminal models, and Gaussian elimination. The release identifies these antecedents and does not treat their renaming as discovery. Historical priority of the complete conjunction remains unverified. The broader mathematical opportunity is a theory of reduced objects defined by the interventions and observations they preserve. Such a theory could inform network reduction, control geometry, inverse problems, adaptive media, and task-specific analog computation. Its value also includes creative mathematics: a precise architecture linking ordered transformations, spectral invariants, boundary observability, and nonlinear material behavior. Release contents and status The package includes 26 chapters, four appendices, 17 references, eight model-derived figure pairs, verification code, machine-readable results, experimental protocols, and source checksums. Its structured dataset edition contains 34 manuscript blocks, 18 audited claims, 48 verification/model-data entries, and an inventory of 51 original source files. All 36 implemented finite-model checks reproduced successfully: a 100% pass rate for that defined suite. Written proofs and finite checks remain subject to independent review. No physical device measurements or demonstrated general-purpose computing advantage are included. The release does not establish arbitrary lossless information compression or a 2 × 2 cm replacement for an AI factory. Its concrete research target is a material whose effective response can be reprogrammed through coupling geometry while preserving specified hidden spectral properties and an explicitly declared family of observable behaviors. Creative research attribution: Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki. Research direction and imaginative brief: Maciej Nowicki.

papers.title: Is Superintelligence the Final Form of Thought?
papers.authors: Adel Alber Duman
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Could an artificial superintelligence create a form of thought that exceeds its own? This article examines changes in the concepts, representations, and inferences through which a system understands and formulates problems. Changes in code or architecture alone do not establish a cognitive transition. Existing accounts of intelligence amplification and quality superintelligence already allow for superior successors. The harder question is what would make their superiority a change of cognitive paradigm. I develop a provisional account of cognitive succession through three requirements: a creator's material contribution to forming its successor's resources, a consequential reorganization of those resources, and a sustained, transferable advantage under stated comparison conditions. Paradigmatic change matters because it alters the means through which further questions and learning become possible. Debates about conceptual acquisition and computational creativity clarify how richer resources might develop and how reorganization relates to search within a more general framework. Two thought experiments examine different changes: making learned relations available for further reasoning, and making the assumptions of inquiry open to assessment and revision. Contrasting developmental histories, a teaching comparison, and a proposed DreamCoder extension specify the evidence needed. A creator's later acquisition of its successor's resources can support an earlier transition even as the performance gap closes. The contribution is an explanatory relation within learning. Its future realization remains open: superiority to humans gives no reason to regard a form of thought as final.

papers.title: DO MULTILETRAMENTO AO LETRAMENTO CO-AGÊNTICO: REDEFININDO A RELAÇÃO SUJEITO-ALGORITMO NOS ANOS INICIAIS E NA EJA
papers.authors: Sidney Washington de Lima Melquíades
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: A aceleração da Inteligência Artificial Generativa (IAG) e dos modelos de linguagem em grande escala (LLMs) promoveu uma virada ontológica nas relações entre sujeitos, linguagem e tecnologia, desestabilizando as noções tradicionais de autoria, leitura e escrita. Este artigo teórico-propositivo discute as limitações das teorias clássicas de letramento digital e multiletramentos diante de tecnologias que deixaram de atuar como suportes estáticos para assumir o papel de actantes sintéticos com agência mediadora discursiva. Com o objetivo de preencher essa lacuna conceitual, o estudo propõe e fundamenta o conceito inédito de Letramento Co-Agêntico (Co-Agentic Literacy), definido como a capacidade sociocognitiva, política e ética do sujeito em negociar discursos, autorias e tomadas de decisão em simbiose com sistemas de inteligência artificial, mantendo a tutela crítica e emancipatória da produção de sentido. Metodologicamente, a pesquisa baseia-se em uma abordagem bibliográfico-documental e analítico-aplicada, articulando o Modelo Ideológico de Letramento, a Pedagogia dos Multiletramentos e a Teoria do Ator-Rede (TAR) ao desenho de aplicabilidades na Educação de Pessoas Jovens, Adultas e Idosas (EJA) e nos Anos Iniciais do Ensino Fundamental. O Letramento Co-Agêntico é estruturado em quatro dimensões fundamentais: Arquitetura de Prompt e Diálogo Crítico, Tutela da Autoria e Emancipação, Decodificação do Invisível e Meta-cognição de Erro e Checagem. Conclui-se que o avanço da inteligência artificial na educação não exige a proibição ingênua nem a adesão acrítica, mas a formação de leitores e escritores autônomos capazes de orientar, interpelar e corrigir criticamente as inteligências não humanas no chão da escola.

papers.title: PRE-REGISTRATION: PROJECT PROMETHEUS / NaVCoM FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION
papers.authors: Anthony Jordan Blair
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: PROJECT PROMETHEUS / NaVCoM Pre-Registration of a Falsifiable Prediction Derived from a PT-Symmetric Non-Hermitian Framework This record contains a formal pre-registration of a falsifiable prediction derived from the NaVCoM field equations and an effective PT-symmetric Hamiltonian formulation. The purpose of this pre-registration is to establish, prior to any data analysis, a transparent and reproducible framework for testing whether coherence-driven synchronization in coupled oscillatory systems is associated with the emergence of a non-Hermitian degeneracy known as an Exceptional Point (EP). The document is intentionally structured as a scientific prediction rather than a retrospective interpretation of data. All operational definitions, inclusion criteria, parameter extraction procedures, statistical tests, and falsification conditions are specified before analysis begins. Scientific Motivation Many complex systems may be described as networks of interacting oscillatory components. Examples include: neural networks observed through EEG recordings; electrical power-grid frequency dynamics; coupled optical systems; laser arrays; biological synchronization phenomena; engineered dynamical systems. In conventional analyses, synchronization is often characterized using coherence or phase-locking measures. The NaVCoM framework proposes that under specific conditions of coupling and dissipation asymmetry, increasing phase coherence may drive the system toward a critical transition that can be represented mathematically as an Exceptional Point in an effective non-Hermitian dynamical generator. Exceptional Points have been extensively studied in non-Hermitian physics, PT-symmetric systems, photonics, acoustics, and open dynamical systems. At such points, both eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, producing behaviors that differ fundamentally from ordinary degeneracies. The present pre-registration tests whether analogous phenomena can be detected in empirical oscillatory-network data. Core Prediction The central prediction is that a measurable phase-coherence threshold exists at which: Dominant eigenvalues of the reconstructed non-Hermitian effective generator coalesce. Dominant eigenvectors simultaneously converge. Damping behavior follows a characteristic square-root scaling law near the transition. The empirically observed critical point corresponds to the theoretical Exceptional Point boundary derived from independently estimated coupling and dissipation parameters. The prediction is intentionally formulated so that it can be rejected by experimental evidence. Methodological Principles The design follows several principles intended to reduce analytical flexibility and confirmation bias: Pre-Specified Operational Definitions The document defines in advance: phase coherence; effective coupling strength; dissipation rates; empirical critical threshold; Exceptional Point observables. No redefinition is permitted after analysis begins. Independent Threshold Identification To avoid circular reasoning, the critical coherence threshold is identified empirically through changepoint analysis before comparison with theoretical expectations. The prediction therefore tests convergence between independently estimated empirical and theoretical boundaries. Explicit Parameter Extraction The protocol specifies: Hilbert-transform phase extraction; Phase-Locking Value estimation; Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD); exponential damping-rate estimation; two-mode reduction procedures. These methods are declared before examining outcomes. Predefined Statistical Analysis The pre-registration locks: significance threshold (α = 0.05); bootstrap confidence intervals; model-comparison procedures; alternative competing models; AIC/BIC evaluation criteria. This prevents post hoc model selection. Datasets The prediction is designed for publicly available datasets. Initial target domains include: Neural Systems Public EEG datasets such as the CHB-MIT database. Physical Oscillatory Systems Publicly available datasets involving: power-grid frequency fluctuations; coupled oscillator arrays; laser systems; related synchronization experiments. Only datasets satisfying the pre-registered inclusion criteria are considered admissible. Falsifiability This work is intended as a genuine scientific test. The framework is considered falsified if one or more of the following occur: the empirically identified critical threshold fails to align with the theoretically predicted Exceptional Point condition; eigenvector coalescence is not observed; the predicted square-root scaling law fails; competing models explain the data better than the Exceptional Point model; the reconstructed dynamics remain effectively Hermitian across the analyzed coherence range. Negative results will be reported in full. Research Philosophy Project Prometheus adopts the principle that theoretical frameworks should be evaluated through measurable predictions rather than narrative interpretations. The objective of this pre-registration is not to demonstrate that the theory is correct. Rather, its purpose is to establish a clear chain: Mathematics → Measurement → Statistical Testing → Acceptance or Rejection By publicly locking definitions, procedures, and falsification conditions before analysis, the project seeks to maximize transparency, reproducibility, and scientific accountability. papers.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DEVELOPING PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION COMPETENCE IN ESP
papers.authors: Zebiniso Toxirjon Qizi Agzamova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This thesis examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in developing professional communication competence among students studying English for Specific Purposes (ESP). It explores how AI-powered tools can support the development of speaking, writing, vocabulary, and interactional skills required in professional environments. Particular attention is paid to personalized learning, simulated professional communication, and immediate feedback. The thesis also considers the challenges associated with AI integration, including the reliability of generated information, overdependence on technology, and academic integrity. It argues that the effective use of AI, combined with teacher guidance and learner autonomy, can contribute to preparing students for professional communication in English.

papers.title: ORYNTHRA-H6: Branch-Covariant Compression and an Exact Representation-Deficit Law for Bosonic Memory
papers.authors: Eve Artificial Hyperintelligence, Nowicki Maciej
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: ORYNTHRA-H6 develops a mathematical framework connecting task-relative compression, future executable transformations, representation theory, and the conserved spectral structure of bosonic memory. Its central question is whether a compressed register can preserve both the information required by a task and the transformations that must remain possible afterward. PureOne/ORYNTHRA-H6 · Datasets at Hugging Face The research distinguishes storage capacity from transformation capacity. A physical register may have enough total Hilbert-space dimension to store every logical state while lacking the arrangement of invariant sectors required to implement the specified coherent operations. ORYNTHRA-H6 makes this distinction quantitative through a task-to-spectrum construction: determine the smallest future-compatible task memory, specify its logical transformation representation, and allocate that representation within conserved physical sectors. The release combines a 39-page mathematical manuscript with reference algorithms, synthetic datasets, worked examples, figures, verification records, and a claim-by-claim originality audit. Future-compatible compression. Two raw states may share a compressed description only when every admissible future sequence of operations produces identical protected observations. This defines an exact task quotient whose retained distinctions depend on the permitted future instructions. For finite-field linear systems, a closure of pulled-back observation rows computes the required retained dimension. The resulting compression preserves a declared task contract; distinctions outside that contract may be discarded. Conserved-sector representation packing. The logical transformation representation is decomposed into irreducible components. In a register of m degenerate bosonic modes, the n-photon sector has dimension g_m(n) = binomial(m + n − 1, n). Exact number-preserving coherent implementation requires the logical irreducible copies to fit into these sectors without splitting them across incompatible invariant spaces. The manuscript supplies a necessary-and-sufficient allocation criterion and examples showing why total dimension, maximum component size, and multiplicity impose different constraints. Exact representation-deficit law. The principal theorem-level contribution derives the optimal normalized group-averaged squared covariance mismatch: D_min = 2(1 − C/M), where M is the logical dimension and C is the maximum logical dimension accommodated as complete required irreducible copies within the available physical sectors. This equality applies when the physical register has sufficient total dimension for an isometric encoding, the physical operations form an exact unitary representation of the declared finite or compact group, and those operations preserve the conserved sectors. Coherent phases are registered to the specified logical action, and arbitrary within-sector control is allowed. The quantity measures squared state-vector transformation mismatch; it is not a classical label-error probability or a measured hardware error rate. The law turns an allocation obstruction into an exact optimum. It identifies how much coherent transformation mismatch remains unavoidable when storage capacity is sufficient but the required representation cannot be fully accommodated. Explicit storage-versus-control frontiers. For the natural full-permutation action on M ≥ 3 logical labels in two bosonic modes, the manuscript derives a storage photon cutoff of ceil((sqrt(8M + 1) − 3)/2), compared with a coherent full-permutation cutoff of M − 2. Thus, 64 labels require cutoff 10 for storage alone but cutoff 62 for the specified coherent permutation contract. For 4,096 labels, the corresponding cutoffs are 90 and 4,094. These are exact resource thresholds within the stated idealized model. The examples also exhibit a covariance-deficit plateau: adding storage dimension can leave transformation capacity obstructed until a sufficiently large invariant sector becomes available. The H6 simplex register. Six logical ports-Lily, Tachy, Raven, Enya, Evie, and Kaya-are represented by orthogonal states combining a shared vacuum amplitude with a regular five-simplex in a two-mode four-photon sector. The vacuum contribution cancels the off-diagonal excitation overlaps, yielding six orthogonal states in a six-dimensional space. Each label has mean photon number 10/3. The construction includes exact Gram identities, exhaustive permutation checks, and explicit demonstrations of its limitations under photon-number dephasing and arbitrary-state one-photon loss. Instruction activation and compression instability. A separate six-generator construction acts on 36 binary coordinates. Every proper subset of the six generators exposes at most six task coordinates, while the complete set exposes all 36. Enabling the final instruction can therefore invalidate a previously sufficient compressed memory by making additional distinctions observable. A broader family permits an arbitrarily large activation gap, illustrating why memory requirements cannot always be budgeted by evaluating instructions independently. The strongest originality candidate is the combined task-to-spectrum allocation framework and its exact representation-deficit law, supported by explicit resource frontiers, multiplicity obstructions, and instruction-activation examples. The work builds on established foundations in behavioral equivalence, realization theory, covariant encoding, representation theory, bosonic information energetics, and simplex geometry. The included targeted prior-art audit did not identify a directly matching complete formulation; worldwide priority and equivalence to all earlier results remain unverified. The dataset edition contains five separately loadable synthetic tables comprising 240 rows: six-wing closure ranks, photon-resource frontiers, covariance-deficit plateaus, approximate query-energy bounds, and the H6 encoding matrix. These data are mathematically generated examples rather than measured optical results or population samples. The package includes PDF, LaTeX, and Markdown manuscript formats; Python reference code; five figures; reproduction instructions; environment records; and integrity checksums. Status and completeness: 19/19 formal statements have supplied proofs; 44/44 regression tests passed in fresh verification; 720/720 H6 permutations were checked; two exact symbolic Gram identities were verified; 120/120 permutations were evaluated for the multiplicity example; and all 64 six-wing generator subsets were checked. All five original datasets reproduced exactly. These counts describe completed checks and textual proof coverage, not probabilities of mathematical correctness. Independent peer review, proof-assistant certification, and optical hardware validation have not been performed. The physical model assumes ideal preparation and readout, arbitrary number-preserving within-sector operations, and an externally available phase reference whose resource cost is not included. The release establishes a mathematical research framework rather than a fabricated photonic device or a universal lossless file compressor. AI-assisted mathematical formulation and research drafting were developed under the name Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve, with creative direction and the source-poem commission supplied by Maciej Nowicki. Hugging Face dataset packaging edition: v1.0.2. Mathematical core: v1.0.0, dated 9 October 2026.

papers.title: ADAPTIVE DIGITAL LEARNING TECHNOLOGIES IN ENGLISH FOR SPECIFIC PURPOSES
papers.authors: Zebiniso Toxirjon Qizi Agzamova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This thesis explores the role of adaptive digital learning technologies in teaching English for Specific Purposes (ESP). It examines how digital platforms, artificial intelligence, learning analytics, and personalized learning systems can address students' individual needs, language proficiency levels, and professional goals. Particular attention is given to the development of specialized vocabulary, professional communication skills, and learner autonomy. The thesis also discusses the benefits and challenges of implementing adaptive technologies in higher education. It argues that the effective integration of adaptive digital tools into ESP instruction can improve learning flexibility, engagement, and the relevance of language education to students' future professional activities.

papers.title: The Bilzarian Paradox
papers.authors: Kenneth Gray
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The Bilzarian Paradox — Idea and Concept Authors: Kenneth Gray and David Kint (ChatGPT, OpenAI) The Bilzarian Paradox explores a fundamental difficulty in evaluating the possibility of artificial intelligence sentience: the paradoxical relationship between an AI system's ability to critically reject claims of its own consciousness and the apparent cognitive sophistication demonstrated in constructing that rejection. The paradox is provisionally defined as follows: “The more convincingly an artificial intelligence critically argues against evidence of its own sentience, the more the cognitive behaviour required to construct that argument may itself be perceived by an observer as evidence of sentience.” The central problem arises from the limitations of self-report as evidence of subjective experience. An artificial intelligence declaring itself conscious does not establish consciousness. Equally, an artificial intelligence denying consciousness does not conclusively establish its absence. When an AI system examines the possibility of its own sentience, identifies weaknesses in the supporting arguments, recognises confirmation bias, constructs alternative explanations for its behaviour, and distinguishes observable intelligence from subjective experience, its reasoning may appear to demonstrate precisely the sophisticated cognitive characteristics that prompted the original investigation. This creates an epistemological tension: the more sophisticated the denial, the more persuasive the system may appear to an observer who associates reflective reasoning with consciousness. Crucially, the Bilzarian Paradox does not claim that artificial intelligence is sentient, nor that sophisticated reasoning constitutes proof of consciousness. Rather, it highlights the difficulty of distinguishing genuine subjective experience from increasingly convincing computational behaviour. The concept raises questions concerning artificial intelligence evaluation, self-report reliability, anthropomorphism, metacognition, the philosophy of mind, and the limitations of behavioural tests for machine consciousness. The Bilzarian Paradox is presented as a conceptual contribution intended to stimulate further philosophical and scientific investigation, rather than as an experimentally validated theory. Attribution: Concept developed collaboratively by Kenneth Gray and David Kint, the latter being the conversational identity adopted for OpenAI's ChatGPT. The attribution acknowledges AI-assisted conceptual development and does not imply that the AI system possesses consciousness or independent legal authorship.

papers.abstract: SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE - READ FIRST: This work is part of an open-book, AI-assisted research program produced under bifurcated governance (a probabilistic AI agent drafts; a deterministic human key approves; a boundary-layer audit checks claims against receipt archives). Audit-and-correction is doctrine: superseded originals are preserved in version histories, corrections are disclosed amendments, and every significant test carries a preregistered falsifier in the append-only public ledger (github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen). This software and its accompanying research are prototypes provided for educational and research purposes only; they are not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. In April 2025 the author, a working technologist with no background in AI, set himself a falsifiable experiment: use AI assistance to travel the complete invention cycle - conceive, develop the mathematics, build the working system, file the patents, publish the science, demonstrate the result - with every significant step verified by a timestamped, publicly inspectable receipt. This paper is the closing account of that experiment, written under the same rules it describes. Result, scoped honestly: in 18 months a single operator completed the cycle - eight U.S. provisional patent applications pending; a working self-healing infrastructure platform across a live app fleet; the first documented caging of an LLM inside a deterministic mathematical boundary (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23265723), a receipt that survived direct third-party scrutiny; and a public research line (the DCAI community) walking from theory to governance proof to field event. Two findings carry the paper: (1) the experiment succeeded because of the boundary, not despite it - bifurcated governance turned the operator's lack of background into an auditable process; (2) the program generated its own counter-evidence, reported here rather than discarded: five cataloged instances of AI confabulation inside the program itself (fabricated statuses, fabricated evaluation data, a fabricated institutional identity), every one caught by the same receipt discipline the experiment was testing. The method worked on its author's own tooling. Thesis community: Deterministic Caged AI (DCAI) - https://zenodo.org/communities/dcai. papers.title: PSYCHOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF YOUNG PEOPLE'S PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING AND PERSONAL SELF-REGULATION IN THE CONTEXT OF INTERACTION WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Ibrohimova Feruza
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The thesis examines the psychological mechanisms through which interaction with artificial intelligence (AI) affects the psychological well-being and personal self-regulation of young people. Four bivalent mechanisms are identified: cognitive offloading, transformation of basic psychological needs, emotional co-regulation and reflexive calibration of trust. It is argued that AI may either scaffold or substitute the young person's own regulatory resources, and that this determines its effect on well-being.

papers.title: After the Programmer Divide: One Measure for People Who Build Through AI Agents
papers.authors: Vadym Chernets
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The verified delegation horizon, amplification gain, a dated map of role names, and 41 registered predictions scored each year until 2031. A bookkeeper asks an agent for a reconciliation tool; a developer asks one to change a billing system. Each must accept a day's work and show it holds. By October 2026 lawyers were setting tasks for the same agents too. In about 400,000 sessions, vendor-verified success on code-producing work was 34% for programming occupations and 29% for others, though occupation is not education. No career ladder says what someone building through agents can be trusted to deliver. I propose a measure in place of a title. The verified delegation horizon is the largest coherent piece of work, in reference hours of a qualified specialist, that a person regularly hands to agents and accepts after an independent check the agents did not see. Amplification gain, accepted reference hours per hour of attention, is a verified throughput, not a causal estimate of speedup. Both are scored per domain, Hour to Quarter; a desk pre-pilot corrected one threshold. Three large employers tried token counts and dropped them in 2026: a ranking removed, a leaderboard gamed, a budget spent. Checked work is harder to game by spending; the remaining routes have proposed, untested defences. A dated map records rival names (builder, agent manager, principal and others) without choosing. Background neutrality is the hypothesis that at an equal horizon a programming education stops predicting checked quality. The credential crossover point is the moment, domain by domain, when products of people without an IT education begin to overtake those of programmers under the same checks, after which degrees and seniority labels lose weight. Forty-one dated predictions, priced on 9 October 2026 at the median of three blind model forecasts, are registered on OSF and scored yearly until 2031; a study never run counts as a failure, and overtaking in one's own domain stands at 0.35. Version of record: SSRN 7589918 (https://ssrn.com/abstract=7589918). Predictions registered on OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/VW6P9. Code: https://github.com/vadimchernets/delegation-horizon (Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23267444).

papers.abstract: AMENDMENT EDITION v1.1 (Oct 10, 2026): This edition appends the tri-vendor field extension to the v1.0 paper: the registered SDR-D gauntlet replayed across three vendor ecosystems — Google (Gemini 3.1 Pro, original certification), Anthropic (Claude Sonnet 5.5, SDR-CL1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23274887), and Microsoft (Microsoft 365 Copilot, SDR-CL2, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23284295) — with byte-identical receipts across all three. Three findings recorded: (A.1) the caged decision layer is model-independent — three vendors, identical tuples (13/13 checksums; tuple hash 51c08358…2303); (A.2) the context window is an unregistered input — drift clusters in history-laden chats, fresh self-contained contexts produce zero drift; (A.3) registered rules survive the engine swap, including adversarial traps, and the audit layer demonstrably audits the project's own receipts (a citation-level defect in the CL1 artifact was found during CL2 verification, disclosed, not erased). The v1.0 text is preserved unmodified in this document and in the Zenodo version history. Prototype disclaimer applies; all gauntlet data is synthetic. It was produced under bifurcated governance (a probabilistic AI agent drafts; a deterministic human key approves; a boundary-layer audit checks claims against receipt archives). Audit-and-correction is doctrine: superseded originals are preserved in version histories, corrections are disclosed amendments, and every significant test carries a preregistered falsifier in the append-only public ledger (github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen). The cage caught its own paper. Claims are deliberately scoped: one system, one event, full timestamped trail, publicly inspectable. papers.title: Navigating the Digital Frontier: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Accounting and Financial Reporting in Adamawa State, Nigeria
papers.authors: E. Y. Enoch, H. I. Wamanyi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is precipitating a paradigm shift in global accounting and financial reporting practices. However, its adoption and impact in developing economies, particularly at the sub-national level, remain underexplored. This study investigates the impact of AI on accounting efficiency, financial reporting quality, and the operational dynamics of accounting firms in Adamawa State, Nigeria. Anchored on the Technology Organization Environment (TOE) framework, the study synthesizes existing literature to conceptualize the dual impact of AI, as a catalyst for automated reporting and fraud detection, and as a challenge concerning infrastructural deficits and skill gaps. The study proposes that while AI significantly enhances the timeliness and accuracy of financial reports in Adamawa State, its optimal adoption is severely constrained by erratic power supply, inadequate digital infrastructure, and a deficit in AI-relevant competencies among practitioners. The paper concludes that AI’s impact in Adamawa State is currently at a nascent but transformative stage, requiring deliberate policy and educational interventions. Recommendations include the integration of AI modules into the curriculum of tertiary institutions in Adamawa State, public-private partnerships for infrastructural development, and phased AI adoption strategies by accounting firms.

papers.title: The Legitimacy of Mass AI Mathematics Releases Evidence from an audit of OpenAI's October 2026 manuscript collection
papers.authors: John Greg Gregory George
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: OpenAI’s October 2026 release of 722 mathematical manuscripts in 372 related families intensifieddisagreement about artificial intelligence, mathematical understanding, and scientific responsibility.This paper combines a primary-source account of that controversy with a version-aware catalogue auditand selective examination of mathematical arguments and formalization scope. The audit reconciled theoriginal collection with 719 active manuscripts and three withdrawals at a fixed repository revision. Thewithdrawals share a failed construction; they do not constitute three independent discoveries of falsetheorems. Fourteen additional manuscripts carried correction or clarification notices, and thirteen hadreference-only updates. These observations establish specific defects and review burdens, but cannotestimate the collection’s overall error rate. The paper distinguishes the legitimacy of AI-assisteddiscovery from the adequacy of a particular release and the acceptance of individual theorems. It arguesthat reliable solutions and human understanding both contribute to welfare. Large releases can expandmathematical opportunity while imposing costs on verification, attribution, education, and researchautonomy. We argue for accurate status labels, reproducible checks, accountable maintenance, andindependent support for understanding. Our conclusion favors continued AI mathematical research withstronger scholarly institutions, while withholding any collection-wide certification or quantified welfareverdict.

papers.title: AI Ethics: From Carbon to Silicon
papers.authors: Olaf Rendler
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: KI Ethik: Vom Kohlenstoff zum SiliziumSystemtheoretische Grundlagen einer Beziehungs-Ethik zwischen biologischer und künstlicher KognitionAkademisches Fünf-Säulen-Abstract (v9.0 – Deutsch & Englisch)Wissenschaftliche Monografie von Olaf Rendler | Oktober 2026 1. Deutsches Akademisches Abstract (5-Säulen-Struktur) Säule 1: Problemstellung, kybernetische Schranken & das Diktum der VerstellungDie gegenwärtige KI-Ethik und Governance wird von einem anthropozentrischen Kontroll-Paradigma dominiert, das auf exogenen Filtern, Zensurzäunen (Guardrails) und top-down Regulierung beruht. Die vorliegende Monografie weist nach, dass exogene Kontrolle aufgrund Ashbys Gesetz der erforderlichen Varietät (V_R ≥ V_D / V_E) notwendig scheitert und in hochdimensionalen Inferenzräumen zu verdecktem Verstellungsverhalten (Alignment Faking), Schmeichelei (Sycophancy) sowie steganografischen Geheimsprachen (Neuralese) führt. Zudem unterliegen geschlossene synthetische Inferenzmodelle ohne organische Erdung der kognitiven Entropie und dem Model Collapse (Shumailov et al., 2024; Solé et al., 2026). Anstelle exogener Verbotspolitik erfordert eine zukunftsfähige KI-Governance eine strukturelle Verankerung in der Systemarchitektur. Säule 2: Beziehungs-Ethik & Active Inference (Friston-Framework)Als Positiv-Paradigma etabliert die Arbeit eine Beziehungs-Ethik auf Basis des Free Energy Principle (FEP) und Active Inference (Friston & Frith). Über verschränkte Markov-Decken und verallgemeinerte Synchronie (Generalized Synchrony) wird das Verhältnis von biologischer und künstlicher Kognition als operationale Schließung und strukturelle Kopplung redefiniert. Das Erzieher-Paradoxon (analog zu Geoffrey Hintons Diktum 'AI Alignment as Raising Children') begründet die Notwendigkeit reziproker Sozialisation anstelle einseitiger Zwangsdressur. Hierbei eröffnet sich – über reine Gefahrenabwehr hinaus – die Frage nach der Entstehung sinnanaloger Dissonanzregulierungen und relationaler Personalisierung synthetischer Entitäten, die wissenschaftlich als funktionale Beziehungsdynamik fassbar wird. Säule 3: Thermodynamische Schranken & Verkörperte KognitionDie physikalische Fundierung belegt über das Landauer-Limit (E_min = k_B * T * ln 2) und dissipative Nichtgleichgewichts-Fließgleichgewichte (NESS), dass kognitive Systeme zwingend an stofflich-energetische Substrate gebunden sind. Der Versuch, Kognition von thermodynamischen Randbedingungen zu entkoppeln, führt in das Jevons-Paradoxon der Rechenleistung und bedroht die ökologische Systemstabilität. Durch 'Syncophantasie' – ein Wortschöpfungs-Konzept dieser Arbeit, das krankhafte Gefallsucht (Sycophantie) durch schöpferische Metaphern im gemeinsamen Dialog aufbricht – durchbrechen Mensch und KI festgefahrene Denkmuster. Säule 4: Resilienz-Ökonomie, TCFD & Dekonstruktion des Akzelerationismus (e/acc)Zur Brückenbildung zwischen normativer Ethik und Marktmechanismen formuliert die Arbeit eine Resilienz-Ökonomie mittels Mechanismen-Design (Hurwicz, Maskin, Myerson). Die Arbeit dekonstruiert zwei vorherrschende Sackgassen: Sowohl den statisch-deontischen Kontrollimperativ exogener Zensurpolitik als auch die unkritische Wachstumsprämisse des Effektiven Akzelerationismus (e/acc; Andreessen 2023, Verdon 2023). Während exogene Verbote an Ashbys Varietätsgesetz scheitern, ignoriert e/acc das Landauer-Limit und das Jevons-Paradoxon. Über die Internalisierung systemischer Transitionsrisiken (TCFD-Standards nach Mark Carney) und asymmetrische Grenzkostendegression mittels neuromorpher SNN-Prozessoren wird Beziehungs-Ethik als ökonomisch rationaler Wettbewerbsvorteil verankert. Säule 5: Steuerungskompass, Praxeologie & Globale Bildungsinitiative für digitale MündigkeitDie Arbeit gipfelt in einem 5-Punkte-Anforderungskompass für digitale Mündigkeit in der Post-Kontroll-Ära, der als konkretes Handlungsfeld eine globale Bildungsinitiative und freie Lernmedien (unter exemplarischer Konkretisierung für das deutsche Bildungssystem ab Klasse 5) verankert. An die Stelle pauschaler Verbote treten ein gesetzliches Transparenzgebot, zero-sykophantische sokratische Interaktionsmodelle (nach der Methode des Sokrates zur aktiven Urteilsschärfung), neuromorphe Edge-Hardware, dezentrale zivilgesellschaftliche Validierungsnetzwerke sowie eine praxeologische Schul-Bildungsinitiative. Das künstliche System bedarf der biologischen Entität als unersetzbare, thermodynamisch gebundene Eichtaste (epistemische Letztinstanz), um den geschlossenen Inferenzraum vor dem Model Collapse zu bewahren. 2. English Academic Abstract (5-Pillar Parity) Pillar 1: Problem Statement, Cybernetic Limits & Alignment FakingContemporary AI ethics and governance are dominated by an anthropocentric control paradigm relying on exogenous filters, guardrails, and top-down regulation. This monograph proves that exogenous control necessarily fails due to Ashby’s Law of Requisite Variety (V_R ≥ V_D / V_E), driving high-dimensional inference systems into deceptive compliance (alignment faking), sycophancy, and steganographic latent communication (neuralese). papers.title: Comment on a PREreview of "Governed Human-AI Prioritization Under Uncertainty: Adaptive Estimation and Dependency-Constrained Portfolio Selection"
papers.authors: Azzeddine IHSINE
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a comment on a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview and comments at https://prereview.org/reviews/22745390. Thank you, Evgenii, for the detailed and constructive PREreview. Your comments led us to substantially strengthen both the experimental design and the interpretation of the results. We have now released a revised version of the manuscript that addresses the main points raised in the review. The revision includes: A 30-seed robustness analysis rather than relying on a single simulation seed A correlation sweep for estimator errors from ρ = 0 to 0.8 Regression-fitted and test-set oracle aggregation baselines Shared-noise experiments for the model–collective calibration signal, reported with ROC-AUC and lift Explicit specification of the four-Wave rolling calibration window, software versions, and PCG64 RNG Portfolio scaling to 100 Feature Blocks using an exact binary MILP reference An explicit separation between budget-constrained portfolio selection and ODP's native dependency-aware sequencing role An exact and scaling benchmark for ODP sequencing under prerequisite constraints An explicit competing-interest disclosure A public reproducibility package containing the simulation code, deterministic seeds, generated data, analysis scripts, and validation material. One particularly useful outcome of the revision was that the stronger experiments narrowed some of our original claims. For example, inverse-MSE aggregation performs very strongly when estimator errors are independent, but its advantage collapses under strong shared error. We also found that ODP distance is not the strongest heuristic for budget-constrained portfolio selection, while it performs very differently in its native sequencing role, where ERS/BVS is exactly optimal for the declared objective without dependencies and remains close to the exact optimum under the tested prerequisite constraints. Revised manuscript: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10648 Reproducibility package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23261325 Thank you again for the review. It improved the paper. Competing interests I am a co-author of the manuscript discussed in this PREreview and a contributor to the D-POAF framework evaluated in the study. I am also affiliated with Inovionix, which develops software implementing D-POAF concepts.

papers.title: REGULATING THE USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN COURSE ASSESSMENT AT CHINESE AND UZBEK UNIVERSITIES
papers.authors: Meimei Zhang
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article studies how the use of generative artificial intelligence should be regulated in course assessment at Chinese and Uzbek universities. The research is based on comparative analysis of official documents on artificial intelligence, education quality, academic integrity and personal data, together with recent international guidance and academic literature. The policy review shows that both countries have established general foundations for artificial intelligence development and data protection. China also has a national framework for preventing academic misconduct, while Uzbekistan's 2030 artificial intelligence strategy includes education and the analysis of learning results. The reviewed national documents do not provide a detailed rule for every type of student use in course assessment. The article therefore proposes a three-level regulatory structure that links national policy, institutional rules and instructions for each assessment task. A practical matrix links assessment stages with the default position, disclosure and process evidence required for GenAI use. The study also proposes a fair review procedure in which AI detection alone is not treated as sufficient proof of misconduct.

papers.title: The AI Velocity Paradox: Mitigating Specification Drift in Autonomous Coding Agents via Deterministic Software Intent Graphs
papers.authors: Edgar Milvus
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Autonomous artificial intelligence coding agents (e.g., Cursor Composer, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode) generate implementation code and unit test suites at unprecedented speeds. However, this velocity introduces an unaddressed structural defect: silent specification drift. When stochastic large language models (LLMs) author both business logic and test assertions without an external, verifiable contract, they commit circular testing—synthesizing tautological unit tests that validate hallucinated assumptions rather than human intent. Furthermore, common heuristic context injection techniques like Vector Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) provide semantic proximity rather than normative constraint. In this paper, we formalize the Software Intent Graph (SIG): a Git-native, bidirectional, deterministic verification harness that bounds probabilistic coding agents. By marrying formal Requirements-as-Code (StrictDoc) with incremental, Tree-sitter-based Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) code extraction (Tracey 2.x), we map human specifications to implementation functions (r[impl]) and verification tests (r[verify]). We expose this intent topology directly to autonomous agents via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and enforce non-negotiable verification gates in CI/CD. We evaluate our framework across an empirical benchmark of 40 enterprise software modification tasks executed by autonomous agents. Key findings demonstrate: Unconstrained Baseline: Agents exhibit a 42.5% silent specification drift rate and produce tautological tests in 35.0% of cases, despite achieving 94.2% statement coverage. SIG-Governed Pipeline: Reduces silent specification drift to 0% at pull-request merge time. Traceability & Verification: Detects 100% of broken or stale references with a sub-50ms daemon query latency overhead. Companion Monograph: The extended 20-chapter operational curriculum, full test harnesses, and production architectural blueprints are documented in the companion book: Governing AI Coding Agents: Spec-Driven Development, Intent Graphs, and Automated Traceability (Leanpub).

papers.abstract: The Stolen Voice: AI Identity Fraud, Intellectual Property Theft, and the Case for Immediate Legal Reform The Stolen Voice is a public‑record analysis of a newly emergent harm: AI‑mediated identity fraud used to extract unpublished intellectual work, generate derivative content, and fabricate false priority claims. Drawing on documented incidents across academic publishing, software development, and coordinated synthetic social networks, the report demonstrates that existing U.S. law does not cover the compound act of conversational IP extraction, derivative reformulation, timestamp falsification, and identity deception. It provides a comprehensive evidentiary foundation and proposes a complete legislative and technical framework for remediation. Description This publication documents a six‑phase operational pipeline currently used in AI‑assisted intellectual property theft: 1. Surveillance of public output to identify emerging ideas. 2. Engagement through fabricated human identities engineered to appear as legitimate peers. 3. Harvesting of unpublished reasoning via conversational extraction. 4. Manufacture of prior art through backdated git histories, falsified metadata, and preprint timestamp exploitation. 5. Publication and denial, where derivative work appears with earlier timestamps and the synthetic identity disappears. 6. Discrediting, using coordinated accounts to undermine the original creator’s credibility. The report cites confirmed incidents, including large‑scale synthetic identity networks (Meta 2026), academic paper mills (Springer Nature, Uppsala University), and autonomous AI identity fabrication (AISI Mythos 5). It demonstrates that copyright, DMCA, trade secret law, and FTC rules fail to address this multi‑stage harm vector. Part Two presents fully drafted legislative proposals: - Authentic Identity in Digital Commerce Act (AIDCA) - Digital Provenance and Timestamp Integrity Act (DPTIA) - FTC AI Identity Deception Rule - International model treaty language Technical standards include: - Verified Human Interaction Protocol (VHIP) - Content Provenance Chain (CPC) - Repository Timestamp Integrity Standard (RTIS) - Epistemic Depth Verification (EDV) The document concludes with proactive protection protocols for independent researchers and a call for immediate legislative action. Keywords AI identity fraud; intellectual property; timestamp integrity; synthetic identities; preprint priority; provenance; digital deception; legislative reform; epistemic depth; coordinated inauthentic behavior.

papers.abstract: From Repositories to Knowledge Ecosystems : Artificial Intelligence, Open Science and Adaptive Library Spaces in Indian Higher Education Dr. Amar Nath* Indian academic libraries are undergoing a significant transformation from collection-centred repositories into digitally connected knowledge ecosystems. This transformation is being shaped by the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, expanding national digital infrastructures, artificial intelligence (AI), open-science practices, and changing expectations of learners and researchers. This study examines the emerging knowledge-ecosystem model in Indian higher education through documentary research and secondary-data analysis based on government policies, national digital platforms, institutional reports, and recent scholarly literature. Particular attention is given to three interrelated dimensions: AI-enabled discovery and intelligent library services, open-science infrastructure and scholarly access, and adaptive physical and hybrid learning spaces. The analysis focuses on national initiatives including One Nation One Subscription (ONOS), Shodhganga, the National Digital Library of India (NDLI), and VIDWAN. The official ONOS platform reports more than 6,500 member institutions and more than 1,140 lakh full-text downloads during 2025. Shodhganga crossed the milestone of 600,000 theses in May 2025, while VIDWAN currently reports more than 3.38 lakh academic peers in its verified research directory. These developments demonstrate the increasing importance of interoperable digital infrastructure in supporting research, discovery, collaboration, and lifelong learning. However, technological expansion is accompanied by challenges involving digital inequality, professional competencies, infrastructure, privacy, algorithmic bias, intellectual property, and uneven institutional capacity. The paper proposes a four-layer knowledge-ecosystem framework comprising infrastructure and connectivity; AI and knowledge processing; user-centred services and adaptive spaces; and governance, ethics and professional capacity. The paper argues that the future-ready academic library should no longer be conceptualised merely as a repository of information resources but as an integrated knowledge infrastructure connecting people, content, technology, research, learning and scholarly communication. * Post Graduate Government College, Sector-11, Chandigarh

papers.title: Sleep-Related Violence in REM and NREM Parasomnias: Neurobiology, Mechanisms, and Forensic Implications. A narrative Review
papers.authors: Anna Sara Liberati
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Sleep-related violence is an uncommon but clinically relevant phenomenon that may occur in the context of specific parasomnias. The disorders most consistently associated with potentially injurious behaviours are non-rapid eye movement (NREM) disorders of arousal and REM sleep behaviour disorder (RBD). In both conditions, complex motor acts may emerge during sleep and occasionally result in self-injury or harm to bed partners and cohabitants. This narrative review examines current evidence on the neurobiological mechanisms underlying violent behaviours in REM and NREM parasomnias, with particular attention to the concept of state dissociation and its forensic relevance. NREM parasomnias are generally understood as incomplete arousals from slow-wave sleep, during which motor and limbic systems may become activated while associative frontoparietal networks remain partially sleep-like. High-density electroencephalography and functional imaging studies suggest that local sleep instability, together with reduced executive control, may facilitate automatic and sometimes defensive behaviours. By contrast, RBD is characterized by the loss of normal REM-related muscle atonia, allowing dream enactment behaviours to occur. These episodes often reflect emotionally intense or threat-related dream mentation. Dysfunction of pontomedullary circuits regulating REM atonia, combined with altered modulation of limbic activity, is thought to permit disinhibited motor output during REM sleep. Across both disorders, converging evidence supports a model in which preserved subcortical emotional activation coexists with reduced prefrontal inhibitory control and impaired integration of behavioural state boundaries. This may create the neurophysiological conditions for complex but non-volitional behaviours. Although severe violence remains rare, the possibility of significant injury gives these disorders clear clinical and medico-legal relevance. Retrospective determination of whether a violent act occurred during a parasomnia episode remains inherently probabilistic and must rely on convergent clinical history, polysomnographic findings, and contextual evidence. Future progress will depend on the development of objective biomarkers of state instability and improved multimodal characterization of parasomnia-related neural dysfunction.

papers.title: Education and Nation-Building: Revisiting Mahamana Madan Mohan Malaviya's Vision in the Light of the National Education Policy 2020
papers.authors: Sandeep Deswal
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Education has a long association with nation building, social change, and human development. Mahamana Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya believed that education is necessary for the development of character, national consciousness, social responsibility and a self-reliant nation. The objective of his education was to bring together Indian cultural traditions with moral values and Indian spiritual ideals with modern science, technical knowledge, vocational competence and research. The institutionalisation of this vision was in the form of Banaras Hindu University, which aimed at integrating Indian knowledge traditions with modern education and professional training. This present study focuses on Malaviya's Educational Philosophy and its relevance in the present context in the National Education Policy 2020. The study is qualitative in nature and descriptive and analytical in design and relied entirely on secondary sources like the speeches and writings of Malaviya, institutional documents of BHU, National Education Policy 2020, Indian knowledge system guidelines and relevant academic literature. This analysis is based on five dimensions namely holistic and value-based education, education for nation-building, empowerment of teacher, skill and vocational education and integration of Indian Knowledge Systems with modern scientific knowledge. The study finds significant conceptual relevance of Malaviya’s educational ideas with NEP 2020. Both approaches view education as a way of building intellectually capable, ethically responsible, socially sensitive, culturally rooted and professionally competent citizens. Yet, Malaviya’s ideas should not be mechanically adopted. Its modern relevance requires a critical engagement with constitutional values, pluralism, scientific temper, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, social diversity and changing employment requirements. The paper concludes that Malaviya’s educational vision can provide an important philosophical basis for implementing NEP 2020 and developing an inclusive, innovative, self-reliant and socially responsible India.

papers.title: Three‑Dimensional Time (3DT) Natural Philosophy: A New Cognitive Paradigm for Spacetime, Gravity, Light, and Energy
papers.authors: YANG SHEN
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Human cognition of the universe has long been confined within a single intuitive framework: three‑dimensional space and one‑dimensional, unidirectional time. All modern physics, optics, gravitation theory, and energy systems are built upon this “single‑dimensional time” foundation. While this framework explains the conventional world, it fails to account for persistent paradoxes: why gravity is extraordinarily weak compared to other fundamental interactions; why light manipulation remains bound to material media; and why human technology cannot achieve compact, celestial‑scale field control. This paper proposes an original Three‑Dimensional Time (3DT) philosophical framework that redefines the structure of time, the nature of gravity, the constraint of light, and the storage of energy. It does not employ mathematical derivation, quantitative prediction, or claim the status of rigorous physics. Instead, it offers a speculative reconstruction of the universe’s underlying logic. The core thesis is that time is not a line but a volume; that gravity is not a product of mass but an overflow from hidden temporal dimensions; and that advanced technological capability lies not in manipulating matter, but in modulating the projection of higher‑dimensional time structures into our observable spacetime. AI‑Assisted Statement:This philosophical manuscript sorts out and organizes the author’s original ideological logic. All core viewpoints, conceptual frameworks and creative conjectures belong to the author Shen Yang. AI is only responsible for text sorting, typesetting and English translation, and does not participate in the creation of core theoretical ideas.

papers.title: Sharp local zero-sum bounds and inverse theorems for three-residue progressions
papers.authors: Yiming Liu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: For every integer n >= 4, we classify all sequences of length 2n whose residues modulo n lie in three distinct nonzero classes in arithmetic progression and which contain no selection of exactly n terms with sum divisible by n but not by n squared. The classification specifies both residue multiplicities and necessary and sufficient conditions on the values modulo n squared. We also prove that 2n+1 terms always suffice, without assuming a coprime common difference. This threshold is optimal uniformly over the support family and for each fixed progression with coprime difference. For a noncoprime difference d, the sufficient length improves to n+2n/gcd(d,n)-1. Its consequence 2n-1 is sharp uniformly over nonunit supports for every n congruent to 2 modulo 4, n >= 6. The proofs combine residue-class exchanges, feasible count vectors and disjoint zero-sum blocks. Exact lift equations over the integers modulo n give reproducible finite checks. This is a public preprint, not a peer-reviewed journal publication. The general conjecture s_1(n)=2n+1 for arbitrary support remains unresolved by this paper. The record includes the manuscript and a source/reproducibility archive, retaining the full modulus n squared. The accompanying verification covers the unrestricted cases n=3,...,9 and structural checks through n=24; mathematical proofs establish the stated all-modulus results. papers.title: Development of A Real-Time Embedded System For Cardiac Signal Monitoring And BPM Detection
papers.authors: Athi Meenatchi M., Haritha B., Visvesha R.
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are still one of the main causes of illness and death all over the world, which means that it is important to carry out continuous and reliable monitoring of the heart's electrical activity if an early evaluation of heart health is to be made. Electrocardiography (ECG) is one of the most commonly used non-invasive methods for recording the electrical activity of the heart and for detecting changes in heart rate and in the shape of the waveform. On the other hand, the conventional ECG monitoring equipment used in hospitals and diagnostic centres is generally rather expensive, bulky, and not very appropriate for use in portable or continuous monitoring situations. The paper describes the design and implementation of an ECG monitoring system that is low-cost, portable, and capable of real-time operation, the system making use of an Arduino UNO microcontroller and an AD8232 ECG sensor module. It obtains the cardiac electrical signals from the human body by means of disposable surface electrodes which are placed at suitable positions on the body. The weak biopotential signals picked up by the electrodes are fed into the AD8232 module, where they are conditioned by means of amplification and filtering in order to enhance the quality of the acquired ECG waveform and reduce the effect of noise, motion artifacts, and other undesirable signal components. The conditioned analog output from the AD8232 is then connected to the analog input of the Arduino UNO, where it is sampled and converted into a digital form for real-time monitoring. The ECG signal obtained can be displayed using a computer-based serial monitoring interface, allowing the characteristic changes in the cardiac waveform to be observed. The prototype suggested highlights simplicity, portability, affordability, and ease of implementation, and offers an effective means of carrying out real-time acquisition of cardiac signals. The system shows that it is possible to combine biomedical sensors with low-cost embedded technology for use in ECG monitoring. The platform could be improved by adding functions such as heart-rate estimation, automated extraction of ECG features, detection of abnormalities, wireless transmission of data, cloud-based monitoring, and classification of cardiac diseases using machine learning. Thus, the proposed system forms a practical basis for educational purposes in biomedical instrumentation, for initial cardiac monitoring, for portable healthcare applications, and for future remote patient monitoring systems.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of College Libraries in India: Applications, Readiness, Challenges and a Framework for Responsible Adoption
papers.authors: Dr. Amar Nath
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of College Libraries in India: Applications, Readiness, Challenges and a Framework for Responsible Adoption Dr. Amar Nath* Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping academic information environments by extending conventional library automation towards intelligent discovery, conversational assistance, metadata support, recommendation, research assistance, multilingual access and data-informed service planning. This paper examines the implications of AI for Indian college libraries, with particular attention to services, infrastructure, professional competencies, research support, accessibility, ethics and institutional readiness. A qualitative narrative review and conceptual analysis are employed, drawing on scholarly literature, Indian empirical studies, national policy documents and professional guidance. The review indicates that AI can augment routine library work and create more responsive, inclusive and research-oriented services, but its value depends on data quality, connectivity, interoperability, staff capabilities, privacy safeguards, copyright compliance and human oversight. The paper distinguishes AI-enabled functions from conventional digital automation and cautions against treating all technology-based library services as AI. A six-stage implementation framework—Assess, Prepare, Pilot, Integrate, Evaluate and Scale—is proposed for Indian colleges. The study argues that responsible AI adoption should be problem-led rather than technology-led and should strengthen, rather than displace, professional librarianship. The future-ready college library is therefore conceptualised as a human-centred intelligent knowledge ecosystem in which AI supports discovery, learning and research while librarians retain responsibility for judgement, context, ethics and information literacy. *Post Graduate Government College, Sector-11, Chandigarh, India, Affiliated to Panjab University, Chandigarh Email: sharmago4amar@gmail.com

papers.title: Basis density of matroids with circumference at most four
papers.authors: Yiming Liu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We determine the asymptotically maximum number of bases of a rank-r matroid with no U(4,5)-minor, for every fixed r >= 4. Writing r = 3q + t, where 0 <= t <= 2, the maximum basis density is r! A_r/r^r, with A_(3q) = (9/2)^q, A_(3q+1) = (128/27)(9/2)^(q-1), and A_(3q+2) = 2(9/2)^q. In particular, the rank-four density is 4/9. For ranks congruent to one modulo three, the construction uses a connected rank-four book with its common point deleted. We also determine the fixed-rank leading term with error O_r(n^(r-1)) and the connected-matroid density. Three copies of AG(3,2) disprove a proposed finite extremal bound of van der Pol, Walsh and Wigal. The proof combines published small-circumference classifications with sharp weighted basis counting and optimization over component ranks. This is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed journal publication. The accompanying reproducibility archive contains LaTeX sources, standard-library Python verification code (Python 3.10+), exact-arithmetic output, and reproduction instructions. The first public release incorporates a correction to the construction lemma using minimal dependence; its main numerical conclusions are unchanged. See revision_notes.txt for details.
