Inter-rater agreement and between-model differences were analyzed using appropriate agreement statistics and paired nonparametric tests. Results Inter-rater agreement was moderate for Safety (Fleiss’ κ = 0.581) and good for non-binary outcomes, with ICC (2,1) values ranging from 0.806 to 0.870. Most responses were classified as safe, with safe response rates ranging from 86.0 to 94.0%, and no significant between-model difference was observed. Accuracy scores were generally high across models, although between-model differences were statistically significant with a small effect size. Empathy varied more noticeably, with Copilot scoring highest and Doubao and Perplexity scoring lower. Perplexity achieved the highest DISCERN and JAMA scores, while Copilot performed best on EQIP. GQS differences were small. Readability differed significantly across models, with Gemini generally producing the most readable responses; however, all models exceeded the recommended sixth-grade reading level, and all Flesch Reading Ease Scores were below the recommended threshold. Conclusion No single LLM performed best across all domains. Although the evaluated models generally provided safe and accurate responses to DR patient questions, limitations remained in safety escalation, empathy, transparency, and readability. LLM-generated DR information may support general patient education but should not replace professional ophthalmic consultation.

papers.title: Narcissistic traits and emotional dependence on large language models among adolescents
papers.authors: Yihang Zhao, Mengyue Xu, Ning Wang, Yang Liu, Hong Wang
papers.abstract: Background This study examined associations between narcissistic traits and emotional dependence on large language models (LLMs) among adolescents, focusing on anxiety and physical activity. Methods A multistage stratified sample of 1622 Chinese junior high school students was surveyed in November 2025. Narcissistic traits, anxiety, LLM emotional dependence, and physical activity were assessed using the FFNI-SF, GAD-2, an adapted five-item LLM emotional dependence measure, and PARS-3, respectively. Pearson correlations and PROCESS Models 4 and 7 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples were conducted, with Johnson–Neyman analysis used to probe the interaction. Results Narcissistic traits correlated positively with anxiety (r=0.118, P<0.001) and LLM emotional dependence (r=0.301, P<0.001), while anxiety correlated positively with LLM emotional dependence (r=0.146, P<0.001). Physical activity correlated negatively with anxiety (r=−0.119, P<0.001) and LLM emotional dependence (r=−0.075, P = 0.002). Adjusting for grade and left-behind status, anxiety showed a small indirect association between narcissistic traits and LLM emotional dependence (Effect=0.011, 95% CI [0.004, 0.020]). The narcissistic traits × physical activity interaction was significant (β=−0.056, P = 0.015), with the narcissism–anxiety association significant below 0.73 SD of physical activity. The moderated mediation index was not significant (Index=−0.0061, 95% bootstrap CI [−0.0130, 0.0001]). Conclusion Narcissistic traits were positively associated with adolescent LLM emotional dependence, with a small cross-sectional indirect association through anxiety. Physical activity moderated the narcissism–anxiety association, although overall moderated mediation was not supported.

papers.title: Efficacy of artificial intelligence-driven conversational agents (chatbots) for mental health promotion among university students: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.authors: Chen Shao, Xiaochen Chen, Shengnan Qiao, Ang Li, Shipeng Liu, Yanglong Chen
papers.abstract: Background University students experience substantial mental-health burdens, while access to timely support remains uneven. AI conversational agents may provide low-threshold support, but the evidence base has expanded rapidly and prior reviews have often combined different age groups, intervention types, outcome domains, and comparator conditions. Objective To evaluate the effects of AI-mediated conversational interventions on depressive and anxiety symptoms in university students, while distinguishing outcome domains, comparator intensity, intervention architecture, and the evidential requirements for standardized post-intervention effect estimation. Methods We updated the search in PubMed, Embase, PsycINFO, CENTRAL, and Web of Science to the revised search date and rebuilt an auditable cross-database record ledger. The updated workflow included 3,786 exported records, 451 DOI/PMID duplicates, 41 confirmed title/author duplicates, and 3,294 unique records screened. All title/abstract records completed a two-reviewer screening and consensus chain. Forty-six update-search records entered research-level/full-text assessment. Randomized controlled trials were eligible for causal quantitative synthesis; relevant feasibility, acceptability, usability, and non-comparable controlled studies were retained narratively. Standard post-intervention analyses used Hedges g, REML random-effects models, and Hartung-Knapp adjustment, and were restricted to attributable two-group post-intervention data. Results In the final locked non-active/low-intensity comparator analysis, three depression comparisons favored conversational interventions (k=3; Hedges g=-0.413, 95% CI -0.557 to -0.268; I2 = 0.0%) and four anxiety comparisons also favored them (k=4; Hedges g=-0.435, 95% CI -0.603 to -0.268; I2 = 2.1%). In the separate active conversational-control analysis, two MYLO comparisons did not show a reliable incremental effect for depression (k=2; g=0.165, 95% CI -0.580 to 0.911) or anxiety (k=2; g=0.190, 95% CI -0.556 to 0.937). The evidence base remained small, clinically heterogeneous, and limited by attrition, self-reported outcomes, and uncertainty regarding generalizability. Conclusions AI conversational interventions may improve depressive and anxiety symptoms relative to non-active or low-intensity comparators in university students, but the certainty of evidence is low and estimates are based on few comparisons. Evidence against active conversational controls is very uncertain. Outcome-domain differences and architecture-related claims should be treated as hypothesis-generating. Secure, consent-based, human-supervised implementation and objective outcome assessment are priorities for future research. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261323382 , identifier CRD420261323382.

papers.title: The impact of human-AI co-creation on perceived creativity in generative AI art: a serial mediation mechanism of psychological ownership, perceived agency, and creative flow
papers.authors: Chenyang Wang, 陈苗, Wen Yang
papers.abstract: Introduction Generative AI is shifting digital art from one-step generation toward interactive human-AI co-creation. Across two between-subject experiments ( N = 600), we examined how creation mode and prespecified AI-involvement workflows related to perceived creativity. Methods In Study 1, participants completed digital art tasks under human-only creation, AI-only generation, or human-AI co-creation conditions. In Study 2, three workflows differing in AI involvement (low, moderate, high) were evaluated. Psychological ownership, perceived agency, creative flow, and perceived creativity were measured. Results In Study 1, human-AI co-creation produced higher perceived-creativity ratings than AI-only generation, with indirect effects consistent with a serial pathway through psychological ownership, perceived agency, and creative flow. In Study 2, the moderate-involvement workflow yielded higher perceived-creativity ratings and psychological states than the low- and high-involvement workflows. Discussion Perceived creativity in generative-AI art depends on how users experience contribution, control, and engagement during creation. Within the workflows tested, balancing generative assistance with consequential user choice fosters the most favorable subjective creativity evaluations.

papers.title: GAI hallucinations and user dependence: cognitive-affective responses and individual differences
papers.authors: Rongqin Liu, Hui Jiang, Fangying Pang
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) hallucinations raise questions about how users respond to unreliable outputs from a technology on which they depend. Drawing on the cognitive–affective components of the Interaction of Person–Affect–Cognition–Execution (I-PACE) framework, this study examines the roles of GAI trust, cognitive dissonance, perceived controllability, and frustration in the relationship between perceived hallucinations and GAI dependence, with GAI literacy and self-efficacy as individual-difference moderators. A between-subjects experiment involved 546 participants who viewed the same GAI dialogue labelled as either containing fabricated information or verified as accurate. Participants in the former condition reported lower trust and perceived controllability, greater cognitive dissonance and frustration, and lower dependence scores. In the parallel model, the indirect associations through trust, controllability, and frustration were negative, whereas the indirect association through cognitive dissonance was positive. Higher GAI literacy weakened the positive controllability–dependence association. The remaining moderation hypotheses were not supported under the directional and multiplicity-adjusted criteria. The findings connect users’ evaluations of unreliable GAI responses with the difficulties they report in regulating their use. They underscore the importance of examining dependence alongside reliability judgements, cognitive conflict, and emotional reactions when assessing the human consequences of GAI hallucinations.

papers.title: How human–AI collaboration event strength shapes information security behavior: evidence from a University in Shanghai
papers.authors: Wei Jin, Yuhui Ge
papers.abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into higher education learning contexts, university students receive technological support while also facing new information security risks. However, existing research has paid limited attention to how the event characteristics of human-AI collaboration are associated with university students' information security behavior and to the psychological processes underlying these relationships. Drawing on event system theory, this study develops a dual pathway model to examine how human-AI collaboration event strength, reflected in event novelty, event disruption, and event criticality, is associated with information security behavior among university students through security vigilance and cognitive overload. Methods Data were collected from students at a university in Shanghai using a three-wave time-lagged survey design, yielding 351 valid responses. Results The results show that event novelty, event disruption, and event criticality are positively associated with security vigilance and cognitive overload. Security vigilance is positively associated with information security behavior, whereas cognitive overload is negatively associated with information security behavior. Further analyses indicate that these event strength attributes generate positive indirect effects through security vigilance and negative indirect effects through cognitive overload. Discussion This study explains information security behavior during university students' use of artificial intelligence from an event-strength perspective and provides a more nuanced understanding of the underlying psychological processes. The findings provide a theoretical basis for universities to refine guidelines for artificial intelligence use, strengthen information security education, and optimize the design of human-AI collaborative learning.

papers.title: Effect of epidural spinal cord stimulation combined with personalized neurorehabilitation in chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury: study protocol for the phase II single-arm feasibility RESTORES (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) trial
papers.authors: Kai Rui Wan, Zhi-Yan Valerie Ng, Seng Kwee Wee, Fatimah Misbaah, Wen Li Lui, Min Wee Phua, Tegan Kate Plunkett, Neethu Robinson, Aung Aung Phyo Wai, 关存太, Ananda Sidarta, Rosa Qi Yue So, Brian Premchand, Kezia Susanto, Luca Cocchi, Seyed Ehsan Saffari, Rui Xin Justin Ker, Wai Hoe Ng
papers.abstract: Background Chronic motor-complete spinal cord injury (SCI) results in profound neurological disability with minimal prospects for functional recovery using conventional rehabilitation strategies. Emerging evidence suggests that epidural spinal cord stimulation (eSCS) can activate dormant spinal locomotor networks and restore volitional and autonomic functions when combined with intensive activity-based training. However, systematic evaluation of multimodal neuromodulation approaches integrating advanced rehabilitation and computational neurophysiology remains limited. Methods The RESTORES trial (RESToration Of Rehabilitative function with Epidural spinal Stimulation) is a prospective, single-arm Phase II feasibility study enrolling 15 adults with chronic (≥1 year) motor-complete SCI (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment scale (AIS) A or B) between C5 and T12. Participants will undergo implantation of an epidural spinal cord stimulator followed by a 24-week program of structured stimulation-coupled personalised neurorehabilitation (five sessions per week). Clinical outcomes will be evaluated using standardized neurological and functional measures including the AIS motor score, Spinal Cord Independence Measure version III (SCIM-III), Walking Index for Spinal Cord Injury II (WISCI-II), and Trunk Assessment Scale (TASS). Autonomic function and quality of life will also be assessed. Multimodal neurophysiological measurements—including surface electromyography (sEMG), electroencephalography (EEG), resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI), and computer-vision-based movement analysis—will be performed to investigate neural recovery mechanisms and inform the development of adaptive neuromodulation systems. Study outcomes The primary outcome is the safety of epidural spinal cord stimulation implantation, defined as the absence of device explantation for safety-related reasons within 6 months following implantation. Secondary outcomes include changes in AIS motor score, functional outcomes (SCIM, WISCI-II, TASS), autonomic function, quality of life, and neurophysiological biomarkers. Discussion This study integrates neuromodulation, advanced rehabilitation technologies, and multimodal computational neurophysiology to evaluate both clinical efficacy and neural mechanisms of recovery following chronic SCI. Findings from the RESTORES trial will provide critical safety and feasibility data to inform future multicenter trials and the development of closed-loop spinal cord stimulation systems. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov , Identifier NCT05644171.

papers.title: A robust adversarial learning framework for EEG emotion recognition
papers.authors: Hao Yang, Li Chen, Jianyong Gao, Junqiang Zhang, Jianfeng Zhang
papers.abstract: Introduction Electroencephalography (EEG) provides an objective means of capturing neural patterns associated with emotion, but substantial inter-subject variability limits the ability of existing models to generalize to unseen subjects. Methods We propose a robust adversarial domain generalization framework for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition. In the first stage, long short-term memory-based encoders are jointly trained to learn domain-invariant and domain-specific representations using reconstruction, emotion classification, and adversarial domain objectives. This process preserves emotion-relevant information while suppressing subject-specific distribution shifts. In the second stage, the invariant encoder and emotion classifier are further refined through distributionally robust optimization with gradient-guided feature augmentation. Theframework is evaluated on the AMIGOS and DREAMER datasets using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Results The proposed method achieves mean accuracies of 69.94% and 68.97% and F1 scores of 0.59 and 0.65 on AMIGOS and DREAMER, respectively, outperforming the comparison methods on both datasets. Ablation results further show that adversarial learning provides the primary improvement in cross-subject generalization, while distributionally robust optimization offers complementary robustness. Discussion These findings indicate that combining representation learning that is invariant across domains with distributionally robust optimization effectively reduces distribution shifts across subjects and improves EEG emotion recognition for unseen subjects.

papers.title: A machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after scalp cluster needling therapy in patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment
papers.authors: Yican Hao, Xia Wei, Pingli Zhao, Hewei Qin
papers.abstract: Background Cognitive recovery varies substantially among patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment (PSCI-MCI), whereas individualized models for predicting post-treatment cognitive improvement remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after 1 month of scalp cluster needling therapy with prolonged needle retention (SCNT-PR) in patients with PSCI-MCI. Methods This retrospective study included hospitalized patients diagnosed with PSCI-MCI between January 1, 2010, and January 1, 2023. Baseline data included demographics, vascular risk factors, stroke severity, imaging features, cognitive and functional assessments, emotional and sleep-related indicators, treatment-related variables, and laboratory findings. The outcome was defined as an increase of at least 2 points in the corrected Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score after treatment compared with baseline. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and the Boruta algorithm were used to identify key predictors. Seven supervised machine learning algorithms were applied to develop pretreatment prediction models. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. Results A total of 750 patients were included and randomly assigned to a training set ( n = 526) and a validation set ( n = 224). Seven key predictors were identified from the intersection of LASSO regression and Boruta. Among the evaluated models, LightGBM showed the acceptable performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.759. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis indicated acceptable calibration and favorable clinical utility. SHAP analysis identified baseline corrected MoCA score, years of education, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale total score, Barthel Index score for activities of daily living, age, frontal lobe lesion, and diabetes as the major contributors to model prediction. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent predictor patterns under alternative outcome definitions and predictor configurations. Conclusion We developed and internally validated a machine learning model based on multidimensional pretreatment clinical data to predict cognitive improvement after SCNT-PR in patients with PSCI-MCI. This model may provide preliminary support for patient stratification and individualized clinical assessment, although external validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: A SynNotch-PiggyBac gene circuit for inflammation-responsive IL-10 delivery in Alzheimer’s disease: a hypothesis and design framework
papers.authors: Suhani Gupta, Ronav Gupta
papers.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation driven by sustained microglial and astrocyte activation contributes to Alzheimer’s disease progression, yet no therapeutic strategy addresses it with precision or durability in the brain. Interleukin-10 occupies an unresolved position in this problem. Constitutive interleukin-10 overexpression in amyloid precursor protein transgenic mice increased plaque burden by suppressing microglial phagocytic activity, while interleukin-10 deletion has been reported to restrict amyloidosis in one setting and to worsen tau hyperphosphorylation in another. We interpret this pattern as evidence that interleukin-10 carries opposite signs on the two principal pathologies of Alzheimer’s disease, so that any therapy holding it at a fixed concentration is committed in advance to being wrong about one of them. We therefore propose a falsifiable hypothesis: conditional, inflammation-gated interleukin-10 expression may suppress damaging inflammatory signaling while limiting the impairment of microglial phagocytosis associated with continuous exposure. We present a design framework for a synthetic gene circuit combining an adeno-associated viral vector for delivery to the central nervous system, a synthetic Notch receptor that detects membrane-bound tumor necrosis factor alpha on activated microglia through juxtacrine contact, and a PiggyBac transposon intended to integrate the circuit into the astrocyte genome. Receptor engagement is expected to release a transcription factor that drives interleukin-10 from a synthetic promoter, with transcription ceasing as the stimulus is withdrawn. We provide a quantitative packaging analysis showing that the circuit requires a compacted vector design to fit within viral capacity, and we identify three unvalidated assumptions: the recognition domain does not yet exist, ligand surface density on activated microglia is unmeasured, and shed soluble tumor necrosis factor alpha is predicted to act as a competitive inhibitor of receptor activation. A computational analysis of simulated resting-state electroencephalography, in which 45 of 171 electrode pairs differed after false discovery rate correction, is presented as a fully specified analysis workflow for delta-band connectivity as a secondary outcome measure rather than as evidence of effect, and yields effect sizes indicating that a rodent study would need roughly 11 animals per group. A four-arm validation plan is specified that separates the contribution of conditional regulation from that of genomic integration.

papers.title: Understanding ChatGPT adoption among medical students: an integrated theoretical model of psychological barriers and individual factors
papers.authors: Ayoob Lone, Ali Saleh Alshebami, Imtiyaz Ahmad Dar, Naved Iqbal
papers.abstract: Background The growing adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly ChatGPT, has created new opportunities for medical education by supporting learning, problem-solving, and knowledge acquisition. However, evidence regarding the psychological and individual factors influencing ChatGPT adoption among medical students remains limited. This study develops and tests an integrated theoretical model that combines Privacy Theory, Technostress Theory, Affect Theory, Diffusion of Innovation Theory, and the Theory of Planned Behavior to explain ChatGPT adoption. Material and methods A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate medical students at King Faisal University, Saudi Arabia using a structured, self-administered questionnaire. The proposed model examined the effects of privacy concern, technophobia, guilt feelings, and innovativeness on behavioral intention and ChatGPT usage behavior, with behavioral intention serving as the mediating variable. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results The findings showed that innovativeness had a significant positive relationship with behavioral intention ( β = 0.579, p < 0.001), while behavioral intention had a strong positive relationship with ChatGPT usage behavior ( β = 0.777, p < 0.001). In addition, behavioral intention significantly mediated the relationship between innovativeness and ChatGPT usage behavior ( β = 0.450, p < 0.001). In contrast, privacy concern, technophobia, and guilt feelings were not significantly related to behavioral intention, and their indirect relationships with ChatGPT usage behavior were also not significant. Conclusion Within the proposed model, personal innovativeness was the only antecedent significantly associated with behavioral intention, whereas the psychological barriers were not statistically significant. By integrating five complementary theoretical perspectives into a single framework, this study extends current understanding of generative AI adoption in medical education and highlights behavioral intention as the key mechanism linking individual characteristics to actual use. The findings provide theoretical insights and practical guidance for promoting the responsible and effective integration of ChatGPT into medical education through initiatives that foster innovativeness and AI literacy.

papers.title: Teachers’ perceptions of artificial intelligence integration in education: a multi-campus cross-sectional study from Riphah International University, Pakistan
papers.authors: Niaz Ali, Kamran Zaib, Saba Ahmed, Muhammad Ibrar, Saqlain Hassan
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education is accelerating worldwide, yet evidence on teachers’ perceptions remains scarce in the Global South, particularly in resource-constrained Pakistan. This cross-sectional study examined teachers’ perceptions of AI integration at Riphah International University, Pakistan. A 14-item Likert-scale questionnaire was administered to 270 in-service teachers (86.7% male, 13.3% female) across BS Undergraduate through PhD levels. Guided by a proposed Dual-Lens conceptual framework treating perceived benefits and risks as coexisting dimensions, the instrument assessed pedagogical advantages and structural concerns of AI. Descriptive analysis revealed a moderately favorable overall perception (composite M = 3.40, SD = 0.55). Teachers rated interactivity enhancement (M = 3.81), student enjoyment (M = 3.73), and assessment support (M = 3.72) most favorably, while AI replacing human teachers received the lowest endorsement (M = 2.96). An independent-samples t-test showed no significant gender difference (t(268) = −0.245, p = .807, d = −0.044). One-way ANOVA revealed significant effects for age (F(4, 265) = 3.200, p = .014, η 2 = .046) and level of instruction (F(3, 266) = 3.471, p = .017, η 2 = .038), with teachers under 29 and BS Undergraduate instructors holding less favorable perceptions. Qualification and experience showed no significant association. A moderate positive correlation emerged between perceived benefits and risks (r = .537, p < .001), indicating co-existence rather than opposition. These findings provide baseline evidence from a Global South private university with multiple campuses, highlighting the need for targeted teacher training and policies to mitigate the risks of AI integration in similar institutional environments in developing countries amid their development gaps.

papers.title: Dispositional foundations for AI-mediated learning: evidence from a latent profile analysis of grade-8 students in ICILS 2023
papers.authors: Vanessa Izquierdo-Álvarez, Marta M. Dolcet-Negre
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes increasingly integrated into education, understanding whether students possess the foundational conditions needed to benefit from AI-mediated learning has become an important educational challenge. This study conceptualizes dispositional foundations for AI-mediated learning as the configuration of ICT self-efficacy, attitudes toward technology and expectations of future ICT use that may support meaningful engagement with AI-mediated learning environments, and examines how these configurations relate to objectively assessed digital competence and to student characteristics. ICILS 2023 contains no measure of AI literacy or AI use, so these are candidate foundations rather than a direct measure of preparedness for AI. Using data from 118,764 Grade-8 students across 35 education systems participating in the International Computer and Information Literacy Study (ICILS 2023), we conducted sampling-weighted latent profile analyses on four internationally comparable indicators. Computer and information literacy (CIL) was examined as an external criterion using the BCH approach, and profile membership was predicted by socioeconomic background, gender, educational aspirations and ICT access. Four profiles emerged: average (55.9%), attitude-oriented (25.2%), low-disposition (11.0%) and efficacy-dominant (7.9%). Differences in CIL across profiles were modest, and students in the efficacy-dominant profile, who reported ICT self-efficacy more than two standard deviations above the mean, did not outperform the average profile in objectively assessed competence, a pattern we interpret as a confidence-competence mismatch rather than as high preparedness. On a common metric of average marginal effects, gender showed larger and more consistent contrasts than socioeconomic background. These findings suggest that the dispositional foundations for AI-mediated learning are distinct from computer and information literacy and should be understood as a multidimensional configuration of learner characteristics whose relevance to actual AI-mediated learning remains to be tested directly.

papers.title: Application of software technologies and delivery of business education content in federal universities
papers.authors: Edet Effiong Okon, Odey John Odo, Patience U. Ushie, PATRICK E. OCHE, Francis Asido    Effah, Blessing Bassey Anam, Eric Ugor Ogri, Esther Bassey Arikpo, Maureen Barong Abang, Nneka Ihekaugwu Otum, Christiana O. Umoren, Akputu Moses Odey
papers.abstract: Introduction This study examined the relationships between the application of software technologies and the delivery of Business Education content in federal universities in South South Nigeria. Specifically, it determined the individual and joint relationships of Cognitive Artificial Intelligence (AI), Voice on the PowerPoint (VOPPT) lectures, Skillshare and Google Forms with Business Education content delivery. Methods A correlational research design was adopted. The population comprised 306 respondents, and the entire population was studied. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed using simple and multiple linear regression at the .05 level of significance. Five research questions were answered and five null hypotheses were tested. Results Cognitive AI had a significant positive relationship with Business Education content delivery (R = .574, R² = .330, β = .574, t = 12.235, p < .001). VOPPT also had a significant positive relationship (R = .626, R² = .392, β = .626, t = 14.011, p < .001), while Skillshare demonstrated a significant positive relationship (R = .578, R² = .335, β = .578, t = 12.363, p < .001). Google Forms recorded the strongest individual relationship (R = .804, R² = .646, β = .804, t = 23.572, p < .001). Collectively, the four technologies explained 65.6% of the variance in Business Education content delivery (R = .810, R² = .656, adjusted R² = .652), with the overall regression model being significant, F(4, 301) = 143.634, p < .001. In the joint model, Skillshare ( β = .185, t = 2.921, p = .004) and Google Forms ( β = .808, t = 14.746, p < .001) made significant unique contributions, whereas Cognitive AI ( β = −.107, t = −1.395, p = .164) and VOPPT ( β = −.062, t = −.775, p = .439) did not. Discussion The results indicate that the four software technologies are individually associated with Business Education content delivery, but their unique contributions differ when considered simultaneously. The findings highlight the importance of strategic technology integration, lecturer capacity development, reliable digital infrastructure and institutional support for the effective delivery of Business Education content in federal universities.

papers.title: Preclinical evaluation of a safety-aware multimodal robotic pipeline for human–robot interaction in post-stroke rehabilitation
papers.authors: Bruna Maria Vittoria Guerra, Roberto Soldi, Francesco Lunghi, Stefania Sozzi, LEO RUSSO, Micaela Schmid, Stefano Ramat
papers.abstract: Introduction Post-stroke rehabilitation increasingly requires technologies capable of supporting intensive, measurable, and adaptable interventions while preserving clinical supervision and patient safety. This study presents a lightweight, safety-aware, and modular multimodal robotic pipeline for embodied human–robot interaction in post-stroke rehabilitation, with a first target application in hemispatial inattention. Methods The system was implemented on the TIAGo mobile manipulator within a ROS 2-based architecture and integrates therapist-mediated supervision, speech-based and graphical interaction, head-orientation monitoring, adaptive auditory recall, robot-mediated and screen-based task delivery, and structured performance logging. Dialogue management is based on a deterministic finite-state machine coupled with a rule-based Natural Language Understanding pipeline, enabling predictable interaction handling, explicit fallback behavior, and therapist escalation for safety-relevant events. A preliminary preclinical evaluation was conducted in 16 healthy participants, with a repeated acquisition after 1 month. The study assessed operational feasibility, multimodal interaction robustness, head-orientation monitoring stability, task execution, ASR-related interaction events, usability, acceptance, and 1-month reproducibility of workflow execution. Results All participants completed both acquisitions without adverse events or safety-relevant events requiring interruption of the experimental workflow. End-effector recognition accuracy remained high, attention-recall events were infrequent, screen-based visual tasks were successfully administered and logged, and usability and acceptance outcomes were favorable, with low anxiety toward the robotic platform. Discussion These findings support the feasibility of using a therapist-supervised robotic platform as an integrated tool for structured interaction, head-orientation monitoring, rehabilitation-oriented task delivery, and quantitative logging. The study presents a preclinical evaluation of system architecture, safety-aware interaction design, and workflow robustness. Future work is organized in two stages: a dedicated acceptance and robustness protocol in healthy controls to formally test interaction acceptance, speech-recognition robustness, and safety-relevant failure handling, followed by a true rehabilitation protocol in post-stroke patients with hemispatial inattention, including therapist-supervised exercise adaptation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in pharmacy practice in the Middle East: a scoping review of applications, adoption, barriers, and future directions
papers.authors: Faten Alhomoud
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming pharmacy practice by supporting medication management, clinical decision-making, patient education, and pharmacy operations. Although AI research in the Middle East has expanded rapidly, the evidence remains fragmented across countries, technologies, and practice settings. This scoping review aimed to systematically map the current evidence on AI applications, adoption, perceived benefits, implementation barriers, and ethical and regulatory considerations in pharmacy practice across the Middle East. Methods A scoping review was conducted according to the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched for English-language studies investigating AI in pharmacy practice in Middle Eastern countries. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Findings were synthesized narratively according to AI applications, utilization, pharmacists' awareness and attitudes, perceived benefits, implementation barriers, ethical and regulatory issues, and future research priorities. Results A total of 15 studies published between 2023 and 2026, involving 8,117 participants across multiple Middle Eastern countries, were included. Most studies were cross-sectional surveys (93.3%) evaluating pharmacists' awareness, perceptions, and readiness to adopt AI. ChatGPT and large language models were the most frequently investigated technologies, primarily supporting medication information, patient counselling, medication management, and clinical decision support, while AI-enabled robotics focused on dispensing and pharmacy operations. Pharmacists generally demonstrated high awareness and positive attitudes toward AI, and some studies reported previous or individual use; however, evidence of routine use and organization-level implementation remained limited. Perceived benefits included improved clinical decision-making, medication safety, and workflow efficiency, whereas major barriers included inadequate AI training, limited technological infrastructure, implementation costs, organizational readiness, and concerns regarding privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, transparency, and professional accountability. Conclusion AI has considerable potential to enhance pharmacy practice across the Middle East, but implementation remains at an early stage, with the available literature predominantly reflecting pharmacists' perceptions of anticipated benefits rather than evidence of demonstrated clinical effectiveness. Strengthening AI education, digital infrastructure, governance frameworks, and implementation research will be essential to support the safe, ethical, and evidence-based integration of AI into pharmacy practice.

papers.title: From monolingual virtual exchange to AI-supported multilingualism: a critical perspective
papers.authors: Judit Háhn
papers.abstract: Virtual Exchange (VE) has become a key approach in higher education for fostering intercultural competence through online collaboration. However, despite its inclusive framing, many VE initiatives continue to rely on English as a lingua franca or other shared-language arrangements, which may reproduce linguistic hierarchies and unequal participation. This paper examines the potential of AI-supported multilingualism to rethink predominantly monolingual approaches to VE. It argues that while generative AI and translation technologies may reduce communicative barriers and enable broader participation, they do not automatically transform underlying language ideologies or power relations. In doing so, it highlights a tension between accessibility and the interactional work through which intercultural learning occurs. Drawing on Critical Virtual Exchange, relational learning, translanguaging theory, and ethical interculturality, the paper proposes a critical perspective on AI-mediated VE. It further explores how AI may support linguistic equity, multilingual participation, and translanguaging-oriented meaning-making in Virtual Exchange. At the same time, it critically addresses risks such as technological solutionism, linguistic bias in AI systems, and the reinforcement of dominant language ideologies. It concludes that AI-supported VE should be grounded in critical pedagogy and linguistic justice. In this way, VE is reframed not as a site of frictionless communication, but as a relational and ethically accountable educational practice.

papers.title: Pelvic Floor Health Knowledge and Pelvic Floor Dysfunctions in Disadvantaged Romani Women Living in Sulukule: Associations with Sociodemographic Factors, Health Literacy and Quality of Life
papers.authors: Berivan Beril KILIÇ, Gülsena Utku Umut, Zeynep Hoşbay
papers.journal: İnönü Üniversitesi Sağlık Hizmetleri Meslek Yüksek Okulu Dergisi
papers.abstract: Pelvic floor dysfunctions (PFD) negatively affect women’s quality of life (QoL) and may reduce help-seeking behavior, especially among disadvantaged populations. Evidence on regarding Romani women in socioeconomically deprived settings, such as Sulukule, remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate pelvic floor health (PFH) knowledge and PFD, and to examine their relationships with sociodemographic characteristics, health literacy, and QoL. A total of 92 women (mean age: 40.9 ± 12.9 years) were included between September and November 2025. Pelvic floor knowledge (Pelvic Floor Health Knowledge Quiz (PFHKQ)), PFD (Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory–20), health literacy (Turkish Health Literacy Scale-32), and QoL (Short Form-12) were assessed. Univariate analyses and multivariable linear regression identified predictors of PFH knowledge and PFD severity. Of the participants, 68.5% had never heard of the pelvic floor, and 71.9% were unaware that pelvic floor muscles can be trained. PFHKQ scores differed by education level and mode of delivery, with higher scores observed among women with higher education levels and those who had cesarean deliveries (p < 0.05). Health literacy was unrelated to PFH knowledge or PFD. QoL was inversely correlated with PFD severity, with stronger associations for the physical than the mental component. In multivariable analyses, age, body mass index (BMI), and education level independently predicted PFH knowledge, while BMI and education level independently predicted PFD severity. Romani women had low PFH knowledge and health literacy, with limited awareness of conservative management. These findings suggest that education and body weight are important factors in PFH outcomes in this population.

papers.title: Analysis of Educational Technology Students’ Perceptions of the Benefits, Ease of Use, and Risks of ChatGPT in Distance Learning
papers.authors: Ida Royanti, Vendyah Trisnaningtyas
papers.abstract: This study examines Technology Education Students Perceptions of ChatGPT use in distance learning, focusing on its benefits, ease of use, and risks. The study employs a descriptive quantitive approach. The participants are Technology Education students who have experience using ChatGPT for learning activities. Data are collected through a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire covering indicators of benefits, ease of use, and risks. The data are analyzed using descriptive statistics in the form of the percentages and mean scores. This study is expected to provide an overview of students perceptions of ChatGPT as a learning- support technology and the considerations involved in its responsible use. The findings are expected to contribute to strengthening AI literacy and the appropriate use of generative artificial intelligence in Technology Education learning.

papers.title: Beyond Clickers: An AI-Powered Student Response System for Capturing Mathematical Reasoning in Indonesian Mathematics Classrooms
papers.authors: Fiki Rahmita, Amanah Khairiyah
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the design and pedagogical logic of the Si•Xiang•Hui AI Interactive Classroom, an AI-powered student response system developed at Zhejiang Normal University, China, and to explore its potential implications for Indonesian mathematics education. The study employed a qualitative descriptive-analytic case study design. The case involved a hands-on demonstration of the system during a seminar for education administrators from Southeast Asia held at Zhejiang Normal University in September 2026. The system developer served as the key informant, while 34 adult participants, including the two authors, participated as participant observers. Data were collected through participant observation, an audio recording of the session, the developer’s presentation slides, the delegation’s activity report, and relevant policy documents. The data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis with a deductive orientation informed by the ICAP framework, formative assessment, and knowledge building, with triangulation conducted across data sources. The findings indicate that the system extends beyond conventional clickers in four ways: it pairs answer choices with spoken explanations; enables every student to pose questions that can be addressed through human–AI collaboration; assigns higher scores to explanations based on their quality (up to ten points, compared with one point for an answer choice); and provides analytics intended to classify responses according to Bloom’s Taxonomy and SOLO taxonomy levels. Two areas for further development were identified: enabling students to revise their recorded arguments and making teacher verification of AI-generated answers and scores an explicit step in the assessment process. The findings suggest that the pedagogical logic underlying the system, rather than the technology itself, can be adapted to Indonesian mathematics classrooms using low-cost tools, provided that teachers receive adequate preparation, scoring criteria incorporate mathematical correctness, and student data are appropriately protected.

papers.title: MACHINE TRANSLATION POST-EDITING COMPETENCE IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI: A CORPUS-BASED INVESTIGATION OF STUDENT TRANSLATORS' SKILLS
papers.authors: Leyla Alizada
papers.journal: Scientific notes of V I Vernadsky Taurida National University Series Philology Journalism
papers.abstract: The main aim of the article is to investigate how translation students interact with AI-generated translations and examines the relationship between AI literacy and post-editing performance. Using a corpus-based mixed-methods approach, the study compares human translation, neural machine translation post-editing, and generative AI post-editing. The findings reveal that generative AI improves fluency and lexical diversity but introduces AI-specific challenges, including hallucinations and contextual distortions. Statistical analysis demonstrates that AI literacy, critical evaluation skills, and prompt formulation abilities significantly influence post-editing quality. The study proposes an AI-enhanced MTPE competence framework integrating linguistic, technological, evaluative, and collaborative dimensions. The results contribute to current discussions on translator competence and provide practical recommendations for translator education in AI-mediated environments. The study employs a mixed-methods research design combining corpus linguistics, quantitative statistical analysis, and qualitative thematic analysis. Data were collected from 60 undergraduate and graduate translation students divided into three groups: Human Translation (HT), Neural Machine Translation Post-Editing (NMTPE), and Generative AI Post-Editing (GAI-PE). The learner corpus consisted of approximately 90,000 words. Translation quality, error frequency, lexical diversity, and AI literacy indicators were analyzed using corpus tools and statistical procedures. The study expands traditional translation competence models by incorporating AI literacy, prompt engineering, hallucination detection, and human–AI collaboration as essential dimensions of MTPE competence. Unlike previous studies focusing mainly on translation quality and productivity, this research examines how AI-related competencies influence student translators' performance in generative AI environments. The findings indicate that generative AI enhances translation fluency and lexical richness while simultaneously creating risks associated with factual inaccuracies and hallucinations. AI literacy emerged as a significant predictor of post-editing performance, highlighting the growing importance of critical evaluation skills in translator training. The study concludes that future translator education should integrate AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical assessment strategies to prepare students for technology-rich professional environments.

papers.title: The digital tutorship as mechanism of development of professional competences of medical workers
papers.authors: Lilia Mindanisova Sagdeeva, E. K. Smirnova, Гурцкой Лев Дмитриевич, N. Sh. Sarkhadov
papers.journal: Problems of Social Hygiene Public Health and History of Medicine
papers.abstract: The article considers digital tutorship as modern mechanism for development of professional competencies of medical professionals in the context of digital transformation of health care and transition to model of continuing medical education. The actuality of topic is conditioned by increasing complexity of clinical practice, expansion of application of digital technologies, development of telemedicine, medical information systems, artificial intelligence and remote education formats. The purpose of the study is to substantiate significance of digital tutorship in system of professional development of medical personnel and to identify its main functional directions. Based on results of analysis of official documents of the WHO, normative and strategic documents of the Russian Federation, as well as data from systematic reviews, it is demonstrated that digital tutorship can be considered not only as form of professional support, but also as tool to form clinical, digital, communicative, organizational and research competencies. The conclusion is made that it is necessary to institutionalize digital tutorship in medical organizations and to integrate it into system of continuing medical and pharmaceutical education.

papers.title: THE NEUROPROSTHETICS AND NEUROSTIMULATION: HISTORY OF DEVELOPMENT, KEY ACHIEVEMENTS AND PROSPECTS (THE REVIEW)
papers.authors: Yuri G. Annikov, Чехонацкий Андрей Анатольевич, N. E. Komleva, Vladimir Andreevich Chekhonatsky, Urzaleeva Irina Aleksandrovna, O. V. Annikova, S. I. Mazilov
papers.journal: Problems of Social Hygiene Public Health and History of Medicine
papers.abstract: The purpose of the study is to systematize data from National and foreign publications on history of development, key achievements and prospects of application of neuroprosthetics and neurostimulation. The analysis was carried out concerning databases of PubMed, eLibrary, Cohrane Library, MEDLINE over 2000-2025 according keywords neuroprosthetics, neuroengineering, cognitive neuroprosthesis, brain-computer interface, neurostimulation. The review includes 68 full-text sources.

papers.title: Analyzing GPT-5 performance in general chemistry
papers.authors: Emilie Ernst, Jennifer R. DeRosa, Brian G. Ernst
papers.abstract: The ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to outperform humans on many intellectual tasks has created a difficult landscape for assessing student work. One strategy is designing assignments to be specifically difficult for AI. However, LLMs have been shown to perform well on general chemistry problems across topics, and new models continue to make AI-proofing assignments more difficult. In this work, we evaluate the recently released GPT-5 Thinking model across a set of 1736 questions from the Openstax general chemistry textbook. While GPT-5 achieves near-perfect accuracy overall, categorizing questions by the types of cognitive skills required elucidates specific weaknesses. Notably, GPT-5 tends to make major errors when asked to create figures. These findings inform best practices for AI-resistant assignment design.

papers.title: Bridging the AI use–competence gap
papers.authors: Marina Falasca
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming graduate research and academic work; however, increased use does not necessarily lead to critical evaluation or responsible engagement. This study examines the gap between graduate students’ AI use and their evaluative, ethical, and rhetorical engagement with AI-generated outputs. Using a survey-based exploratory case study design, the study draws on data from 50 graduate students across four national contexts, complemented by open-ended responses and contextual observations. Findings reveal high levels of AI use alongside limited verification practices, ethical uncertainty, and a tendency to view AI outputs as neutral or authoritative, indicating a persistent use–competence gap. The study proposes a holistic AI literacy framework with implications for curriculum, assessment, and policy.

papers.title: Post-Generative
papers.authors: Benedikt Brünner, Martin Ebner, Sandra Schön, Kathryn A. Hoffmann, Christian Ortner, Philipp Leitner
papers.journal: TUGraz OPEN Library (Graz University of Technology)
papers.abstract: This A3 poster proposes the term “post-generative”. It describes a societal condition in which generative artificial intelligence permeates everyday life. Drawing on the idea of the post-digital, the term denotes a world that generative AI has already transformed. A graphic shows eight areas of society in which generative AI is at work. Nine indications from education, science, software development, the creative sector and research support this diagnosis of the present. A companion sheet sets out all 19 sources and their scope. More recent findings are collected at postgenerative.at.

papers.title: Big data and AI for decision-making purposes in the metaverse: A cross-domain review of architectures, applications, and governance
papers.authors: Leonidas Theodorakopoulos, Alexandra Theodoropoulou, Aristeidis Bakalis
papers.abstract: This review examines how big data and artificial intelligence are being mobilized to support decision-making in metaverse and metaverse-adjacent environments. Rather than treating the metaverse as an interface novelty, the paper frames it as a decision environment in which persistent interaction, embodied participation, and multimodal sensing tighten the loop between observation and intervention. Using a transparent narrative review approach, the synthesis applies a consistent decision-making taxonomy across nine domains (industrial and manufacturing operations, smart cities, healthcare, retail and commerce, supply chain and logistics, energy and utilities, finance, education, tourism). For each domain, evidence is organized around decision level, decision mode, time requirements, data context, and action type, enabling comparability without collapsing domain-specific consequences into a single maturity scale. Across domains, the most salient pattern is that decision value depends less on immersion itself and more on the integration of digital representations (often via digital twins), AI inference, and bounded action pathways. The review highlights metaverse-specific constraints that shape decision reliability: measurement validity challenges in multimodal signals, proxy gaming when engagement metrics substitute for decision impact, identity and consent boundaries that constrain permissible inference, and latency/edge limits that compress feasible action sets. Building on these observations, the paper proposes a reference architecture organized as a data–AI–simulation–action loop with explicit fast and slow paths, emphasizing safe-state behavior, fallback logic, and escalation rules as architectural requirements for real-time decisions. A compact cross-domain synthesis consolidates recurring gaps as testable absences in current work, including unclear decision objects, weak semantic and identity alignment, limited uncertainty communication, under-specified constraint handling, insufficient audit trails, and inadequate robustness to drift and adversarial manipulation. The paper concludes with governance and ethics considerations anchored in established regulatory and standards frameworks, and outlines research directions aimed at decision-centered evaluation protocols, contestable immersive interfaces, and governance-ready metaverse decision systems.

papers.title: Architectural education in the system of design-and-research practices in the digital era
papers.authors: Корси М.В.
papers.abstract: Architectural education continues to rely on the design studio as its primary mode of professional training; however, digitalization, interdisciplinary, and generative artificial intelligence are reshaping both the necessary competencies and the organization of studio work. This review identifies the methodological core of architectural training and systematizes the key directions for its renewal. A literature search was conducted using eLIBRARY.RU, CyberLeninka, Google Scholar, Crossref, DOAJ, and various academic publisher platforms for the period 2015–2025; additional foundational publications were included to trace the genesis of studio pedagogy. A total of 53 sources were analyzed. The selection criteria included peer-reviewed articles and monographs directly addressing design studios, critique, research-based design, design-build pedagogical practices, BIM, virtual reality, computational design, and artificial intelligence. The literature analysis identified six interconnected trends in the transformation of architectural education: the preservation of activity approach in design; the transition toward transparent critique and assessment formats; the integration of research and design-build practices; the development of information and computational literacy; the inclusion of AI with mandatory documentation of authorship; and the cultivation of social, communicative, and ethical responsibility. The article proposes an educational ecosystem in which digital tools are not isolated technical components but are integrated in problem framing, variant search, verification, coordination, and reflection. The model can inform curricula, studio tasks, and assessment criteria. Unresolved issues include the longterm educational effects of AI tools, comparability of learning outcomes across studios, and preservation of material and constructive culture with the increasing prevalence of virtual design.

papers.title: ChatGPT Dots for Educators and Students in Psychology Education
papers.authors: Oleksii Nalyvaiko
papers.abstract: This study examines the conditions for using persistent AI agents in higher education, with ChatGPT Dots and psychology education as its analytical focus. An exploratory documentary analysis was conducted on eight public OpenAI documentation pages: six describing Dots and two providing contextual information on ChatGPT and ChatGPT Work. Sixteen purposively selected source statements were coded and recorded in a ledger that distinguishes documented functionality from educational interpretation. The analysis develops the Continuing Educational Delegation (CED) framework, consisting of six documented conditions: bounded continuity, separation of task completion from verified achievement, distinction between access and permission, audience boundaries across communication channels, explicit control over continuing work, and recognition of capabilities shared with adjacent ChatGPT workflows. Four constructed scenarios apply the framework to seminar preparation, rubric and feedback development, fictional psychological case analysis, and student research planning. The resulting propositions specify how continuing assistance can be organised while preserving assessable student reasoning and educator judgment. A prospective comparative protocol defines twenty-four workflow trajectories and distinguishes artifact quality, human review effort, and student learning as separate evaluation targets. The contribution is a source grounded analytical framework and a reproducible specification for subsequent evaluation. No live Dots trials, participant observations, or measured learning effects are reported; the framework therefore requires empirical examination before claims of educational effectiveness can be made.

papers.title: MBB-AVR: a mind-brain-body dataset with dynamic affective states in immersive virtual reality
papers.authors: Antonin Fourcade, Anthony Buck Ciston, Lucy Roellecke, Jeroen de Mooij, Héctor Leos, Arno Villringer, Sara Carletto, Francesca Malandrone, Michael Gaebler
papers.abstract: We present MindBrainBody-AffectiveVR (MBB-AVR), a multimodal dataset capturing continuous affective experience and both central and peripheral physiological responses during naturalistic emotional stimulation in immersive virtual reality. Forty-seven healthy adults (24 female, 22 male, 1 non-binary; age = 27.1 ± 5.4) viewed a 23-minute stereoscopic 360° video sequence, composed of computer-generated, language-free content designed to elicit high affective variability over time, presented via a head-mounted display (HTC Vive Pro Eye). While immersed, participants continuously rated their momentary valence and arousal using a previously validated rating tool with real-time visual feedback. Synchronized recordings include 64-channel EEG, ECG, respiration, photoplethysmography, galvanic skin response, and head and eye tracking with pupillometry. Participants additionally completed questionnaires including interoceptive sensibility and alexithymia. The dataset is organized following the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) and includes extracted low-level audio and video features of the stimulus. It may support research on the temporal dynamics of affect, multimodal physiological correlates of emotion, and affective computing. The dataset is available at https://gin.g-node.org/fourcade_a/mbb-avr.

papers.title: Understanding the role of generative artificial intelligence in mental health support: Survey of user experiences, engagement patterns, and perceived risks and benefits
papers.authors: Jake Linardon, Zoe McClure, Cleo Anderson, Claudia Liu, Olivia Marie Soliman, Mariel Messer
papers.abstract: Generative AI – especially ChatGPT – is increasingly used for mental health purposes, but users’ subjective experiences of these tools remain unclear. We characterized how individuals utilize ChatGPT for mental health support through a web-based survey completed by 308 adults (Mage=31.5, SD=5.3; 54% men) who reported prior use of this tool. Around half reported use of ChatGPT for mental health support more than once a week, 80% have used it for more than 3 months, and a third reported increased use over time. Depression (55%), anxiety (74%), stress (66%), and relationship conflict (49%) were the problems most frequently discussed with ChatGPT, with the severity of these problems typically rated as mildly or moderately severe. Endorsed reasons for use were its on-demand availability (71%), free cost (69%), and anonymous nature (54%), while common functions the platform served included obtaining advice (71%), providing a safe space for expression (63%), and to learn coping strategies (61%). Experiences were largely positive, with 8 in 10 agreeing that ChatGPT helped them feel understood, better process their emotions, and improve their mental health literacy. Concerns were also evident, with around half expressing worry about data privacy, and a quarter feeling overly reliant on the platform and reducing their motivation to seek help. Few indicated that ChatGPT had replaced professional help (7%) or discouraged help-seeking (12%). Findings shed light on how users are engaging with generative AI for mental health support and highlight the importance of rigorous research designed to evaluate its safety and long-term efficacy.

papers.title: A Risk-Formulation Framework and Candidate Screening Items for Dangerous Use of Large Language Models in Clinical Psychiatry
papers.authors: Armando N. Braz, Punit Matta, Joshuah Muthee, Eren M. Veziroglu, Daniel Price
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) and related conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems have moved rapidly from novelty into ordinary use across education, work, social life, and mental-health-related help seeking. Members of the public now use these systems for advice, companionship, self-disclosure, emotional support, psychoeducation, and quasi-therapeutic interactions. Existing instruments assess problematic or dependent AI use, but they do not ask whether AI has entered a pathway toward serious harm by entrenching ideation, operationalizing capability, displacing human support, or amplifying harmful conduct. To our knowledge, no brief, clinically oriented psychiatric screener has yet been developed and validated specifically for this purpose. We define dangerous AI use as generative AI use that appears to increase the likelihood, feasibility, persistence, organization, or scale of serious harm to self or others. This paper describes LLMs as interactive capability amplifiers and quasi-social systems rather than informational technologies alone, situates their risk within the technical problems of alignment and behavioral stability, and proposes a four-dimensional clinical formulation: Ideational Entrenchment, Operationalized Capability, Relational Displacement, and Broader Amplification. We then introduce two candidate instruments awaiting formal validation: the STEPS-5, a brief screen for AI involvement in acute self-harm and suicide risk, and the HEAT-4, a research-oriented framework addressing broader harmful-use amplification. These tools are intended to open clinical inquiry rather than diagnose, predict behavior, or determine disposition. Ultimately, we argue for the need to avoid both over-pathologizing ordinary AI use and ignoring when AI has become meaningfully relevant to psychiatric safety.

papers.title: In AI Do We Trust? Comparing a Transformer-Based Natural Language Processing Model Against a Traditional Content Analysis Approach to Qualitative Research
papers.authors: Matthew Baron, Catherine Stein
papers.abstract: Central to debates about the use of artificial intelligence (AI) models for qualitativeresearch are concerns about comparability and trust in AI generated findings. The presentmethodological study compared findings from a transformer-based Natural Language Processing(NLP) model, BERT, against a traditional content analysis approach to qualitative research usingthe same text data. We examined claims that AI models generate findings that are identical orsimilar to traditional qualitative approaches. The study assessed three aspects of comparabilitybetween the BERT model solution and human-coded findings that included topic labeling,classification overlap, and AI replicability. Results indicated broad similarity in the semanticmeaning of topic categories generated by the BERT model and themes from content analysis.There was low overlap in the classification of individual participant responses between BERTand content analysis categories, even for categories similar in semantic meaning. Running theBERT model a second time on the same input data resulted in differences in topic categories anddocument classification between the two approaches. Study implications and researchrecommendations for the use of NLP models are discussed.

papers.title: Citizen Trust and Digital Governance Transformation: Ethical Challenges and Artificial Intelligence Governance in the Public Sector
papers.authors: Sukwan Hanafi, Achmad Nurmandi, Herman Lawelai, Mohammad Younus
papers.journal: Journal of Government and Civil Society
papers.abstract: The study explores the development of academic research on citizen trust in AI-enabled public governance, with a particular emphasis on ethical considerations, explainable AI, and digital transformation of government. Data were collected from the Scopus database using a scientometric approach and analyzed using Biblioshiny in RStudio to perform bibliometric mapping. The study revealed the publication patterns, leading authors, leading countries, highly cited papers, research issues, and collaborative networks from 2021 to 2025. The data indicate a significant increase in publications, reflecting growing academic interest in transparency, accountability, and trust in public-sector AI applications. The intellectual structure of the field was shaped by key research themes, including artificial intelligence, explainable artificial intelligence, AI governance, and trust. The United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and China have been the main donating countries to scientific production. The findings also reveal that explainability, ethical governance, institutional legitimacy, and algorithmic transparency are important elements for increasing citizen trust and facilitating the uptake of AI-based public services. This paper contributes to the literature by providing a comprehensive assessment of global research trends and future directions for trustworthy, inclusive, and citizen-centric digital government.Studi ini mengeksplorasi perkembangan penelitian akademis tentang kepercayaan warga terhadap pemerintahan publik yang didukung oleh AI, dengan penekanan khusus pada pertimbangan etis, AI yang dapat dijelaskan, dan transformasi digital pemerintah. Data dikumpulkan dari basis data Scopus menggunakan pendekatan scientometric dan dianalisis dengan menggunakan Biblioshiny di RStudio untuk melakukan pemetaan bibliometrik. Studi ini mengungkap pola publikasi, penulis terkemuka, negara terkemuka, makalah yang banyak dikutip, isu penelitian, dan jaringan kolaboratif dari tahun 2021 hingga 2025. Data tersebut menunjukkan peningkatan signifikan dalam publikasi, yang menunjukkan minat akademis yang semakin besar dalam transparansi, akuntabilitas, dan kepercayaan dalam aplikasi AI sektor publik. Struktur intelektual bidang ini dibentuk oleh tema-tema penelitian utama seperti kecerdasan buatan, kecerdasan buatan yang dapat dijelaskan, tata kelola AI, dan kepercayaan. Amerika Serikat, Jerman, Inggris Raya, Belanda, dan China telah menjadi negara-negara utama yang menyumbang pada produksi ilmiah. Temuan tersebut juga mengungkapkan bahwa keterjelasan, tata kelola etis, legitimasi institusional, dan transparansi algoritmik adalah elemen penting untuk meningkatkan kepercayaan warga dan memfasilitasi penerapan layanan publik berbasis AI. Makalah ini memberikan kontribusi pada literatur dengan menyediakan penilaian komprehensif tentang tren penelitian global dan arah masa depan untuk pemerintahan digital yang dapat dipercaya, inklusif, dan berpusat pada warga

papers.title: INTEGRATION OF GENERATIVE AI INTO DIGITAL MARKETING VIDEO PRODUCTION: AN APPLIED SYSTEMATIZATION AND USE SCENARIOS
papers.authors: Яна Сало, Viktor Fedirko
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence is changing not only video generation itself but also the organization of digital marketing video production. The relevance of the study is determined by the growing need for scalable content production, localization, personalization and continuous creative adaptation, while existing research tends to examine either technical video-generation architectures or separate marketing applications. The purpose of the article is to systematize the applied formats of generative AI use in digital marketing video production and relate them to the stages of the marketing workflow and practical use scenarios. The study applies analysis and synthesis, comparison, systematization and conceptual generalization. Peer-reviewed publications and official materials of developers and digital platforms published mainly between 2022 and July 2026 were selected according to their direct relevance to video generation, AI-assisted production and digital marketing applications. The study does not aim to provide an exhaustive ranking or chronology of rapidly changing models. As the main scientific result, a two-level applied systematization is proposed. The first level includes four modality-oriented generation formats: text-to-video, image-to-video, text-and-image-to-video and video-to-video. The second level includes two functional application formats: avatar-based video and AI-assisted video editing. This distinction avoids treating categories from different classification levels as a homogeneous technical taxonomy. The formats are mapped to a marketing video workflow covering ideation, scripting, prompting, generation, evaluation, editing, adaptation, publication and performance analysis. A matrix of practical scenarios is also developed for advertising creatives, short-form vertical video, UGC-like communication, e-commerce product presentation, explanatory content, localization, personalization, prototyping and cross-channel adaptation. The analysis further shows that generative AI is increasingly embedded in professional editing software, mass-market content tools and advertising platforms, reducing the technological separation between production and distribution. The practical value of the results lies in supporting the choice of an appropriate format according to available source materials, communication objectives, required product fidelity and visual control, production scale and channel requirements. The findings also emphasize that automated generation should be combined with human verification when factual accuracy, brand consistency or authentic representation of a product is important.

papers.title: Generative AI and technological mediation: writing micro-processes, products and perceptions
papers.authors: Naseh Nasrollahi Shahri, Jennifer Simpson, Sam Massey
papers.abstract: The public release of ChatGPT presents language education with both advantages and challenges. Being widely available and readily producing texts at user's command, it is an especially useful resource in ESL writing. However, to be able to leverage it effectively for that purpose, we need to understand the writing micro-processes surrounding its use. To this end, this study investigates, through an experimental design, writing micro-processes along with writing outcomes, and perceptions of 12 ESL writers across three writing conditions. The data included interviews, questionnaires as well as essay grades and screen recordings. Two of the three conditions involved the use of ChatGPT. The results indicate that the majority of participants favored the ChatGPT- assisted conditions and noted its role in aiding idea generation. Despite this preference, some participants noted that ChatGPT-produced texts felt robotic and lacked a human touch. We found no statistically significant differences across the three conditions in the participants' essays. Most notably, our analysis identified distinct clusters of writing micro-processes associated with the ChatGPT conditions, suggesting that generative AI tools can influence writing behaviors although the link to outcomes is not straightforward. These findings provide insights into the potential benefits and limitations of using AI tools in writing tasks. The article discusses areas for further research to enhance the integration of AI into ESL writing education.

papers.title: BEYOND THE WRITTEN TEST: RECONSIDERING ORAL ASSESSMENT IN FOREIGN LANGUAGE EDUCATION IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI
papers.authors: Roberto Pigro
papers.abstract: The rapid diffusion of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is prompting a critical reconsideration of established assessment practices in foreign language education. This paper argues that a continued reliance on written assessment, increasingly vulnerable to the unauthorised use of AI-enabled technologies and personal devices, may undermine the validity of language assessment. Drawing on the principles underlying ALTE guidelines and the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), the article challenges the widespread assumption that standardised written testing necessarily provides a more objective measure of linguistic competence. It argues instead for a renewed centrality of oral performance, which enables teachers to observe learners’ linguistic resources and communicative competence in real time. Oral assessment, when supported by clearly defined criteria and appropriately designed tasks, offers a particularly direct means of assessing spontaneous language use, interaction and the negotiation of meaning. The paper also addresses practical and psychological concerns associated with oral assessment, particularly its implementation in large classes and its relationship with foreign language anxiety. It concludes that the emergence of GenAI should not simply be regarded as a threat to academic integrity, but as a catalyst for rethinking assessment practices and restoring greater importance to forms of evaluation that privilege authentic, synchronous and interpersonal language use.
keywords: Common European Framework of Reference for Languages

papers.title: Exploring the Determinants of User Discontinuance in AI-Driven Usage-Based Insurance
papers.authors: Wenzhuo Li
papers.abstract: While interest in algorithmic decision-making continues to grow, limited research has examined the post-adoption phase. This study examines how users evaluate their post-adoption experiences with algorithmic decision-making in the context of usage-based insurance (UBI), focusing on how expectation disconfirmation shapes satisfaction and the intention to discontinue use. It explores two key questions: What factors influence users’ discontinuance intention toward AI-based UBI systems? And how do specific algorithmic characteristics alter how users form these post-adoption evaluations? To investigate these questions, this study develops a comprehensive theoretical model that integrates the Expectation Confirmation Model and Reactance Theory, incorporating additional factors such as perceived control, privacy concerns, algorithmic justice, and algorithmic transparency. This study adopts a cross-sectional research design to empirically test the proposed model. Data were collected from 530 current UBI users and analyzed using structural equation modeling. The results support most of the proposed hypotheses, showing that these factors interact to significantly shape user dissatisfaction and intentions to discontinue participation in algorithmic decision-making programs in the context of UBI. This study contributes to post-adoption and technology discontinuance literature by extending its scope to AI systems that operate with limited user interaction or primarily serve monitoring functions, such as those found in the AI-based UBI system. The findings also provide practical implications for insurance providers, developers, and policymakers, highlighting how design choices, particularly those related to control, justice, and transparency, influence user trust and continued engagement.

papers.title: Maternal Hypoglycemia During Oral Glucose Tolerance Test and Neonatal Outcomes: A Retrospective Observational Study
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: BackgroundConsiderable attention has been directed toward the maternal and neonatal consequences of gestational diabetes mellitus.However, the clinical significance of maternal hypoglycemia occurring during a routine oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) in women who do not meet diagnostic criteria for gestational diabetes remains poorly understood.Whether such hypoglycemic values constitute a metabolic signal that adversely influences fetal growth is an open question with direct implications for antenatal surveillance. ObjectiveTo determine whether maternal hypoglycemia during the 75-g OGTT is associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, with particular attention to small for gestational age (SGA) and low birth weight (LBW) in a non-diabetic obstetric cohort.
