MethodsA retrospective, record-based observational study was conducted at a tertiary care teaching hospital.All women who delivered during a six-month period and had undergone a 75-g OGTT at 24-28 weeks without a diagnosis of gestational diabetes were included.Maternal hypoglycemia was defined as any plasma glucose value below 3.9 mmol/L (70 mg/dL) at the fasting, one-hour, or two-hour time point.The primary outcomes were SGA (birth weight <10th percentile), LGA (>90th percentile), and mean birth weight.Secondary outcomes included LBW (<2500 g), macrosomia, preterm birth, NICU admission, and Apgar scores.Group comparisons were made using the independent t-test and chi-square test.Logistic regression was performed to assess independent associations after adjusting for maternal age, BMI, parity, and gestational weight gain. ResultsOf 716 eligible women, 52 (7.3%) were classified as hypoglycemic and 664 (92.7%) as normoglycemic.Women in the hypoglycemia group had a significantly lower booking BMI (22.1 ± 2.8 vs. 24.3± 3.4 kg/m²; p<0.001).Mean birth weight was lower in the hypoglycemia group (2685 ± 412 g vs. 2894 ± 436 g; p=0.002).SGA was more common among neonates of hypoglycemic mothers (21.2% vs. 10.1%;p=0.01), as was LBW (26.9% vs. 14.7%;p=0.02).On multivariable analysis, maternal hypoglycemia was independently associated with SGA (adjusted OR 1.92; 95% CI 1.01-3.64;p=0.04). ConclusionMaternal hypoglycemia during the 75-g OGTT occurs in approximately one in thirteen non-diabetic pregnancies and is independently associated with SGA.These findings suggest that low glucose values during OGTT, not merely elevated ones, warrant clinical attention.Prospective studies with serial fetal growth surveillance are needed to determine whether targeted antenatal monitoring in this subgroup improves outcomes.

papers.title: Introducing Handwriting Assessment to Multiple Sclerosis
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS) suffer from various disabilities concurrently affecting their daily functions.One of these disabilities is upper extremity dysfunction and dexterity deficits.Handwriting was long considered an essential upper limb daily function for diverse purposes.A sufficient reason for being heavily studied with all its physiological central, and peripheral processes from conception to execution.The scientific craving has extended beyond to include studying the essential skills needed for handwriting acquisition.In view of that, immense research was carried out to rationalize and validate the use of handwriting as an assessment method.The present advancements in handwriting evaluation have broadened the focus from simply describing the writing or drawing style to detailed spatiotemporal and kinematic parameters of these tasks.Consequently, the outcomes of these latest parameters quantify handwriting legibility, readability, and fluency.Currently, handwriting assessment is involved as an objective upper extremity functional assessment, especially in some cognitive and neurodegenerative disorders, e.g., Parkinson's Disease and Alzheimer's Disease.Currently, its role is not exclusive to supporting diagnosis or follow-up, but it is involved in the evaluation of the efficacy of some interventions on the upper extremity of different patients.However, researches concern with MS patients that incorporate handwriting assessment seems to be scanty, especially with the creative innovations applied in this domain, such as various software on digitizing tablets and artificial intelligence.The authors of this review aim to discuss, highlight, and ease this method for medical and healthcare professionals.Definitely, they recommend the widened practice of handwriting assessment software or artificial intelligence applications as objective, up-to-date measures for the functional level of hand dexterity, as well as the upper extremity.

papers.title: Wireless Body Area Network-Based Smart Healthcare Monitoring Using IoT
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Continuous observation of patient health has become more practical with the widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies.This work presents a Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN)-based monitoring system designed to collect and transmit multiple physiological signals in real time.The system integrates electrocardiogram (ECG), electroencephalogram (EEG), electromyogram (EMG), and motion sensing through an accelerometer, enabling a broader assessment of patient condition.Instead of handling all operations within a single controller, the design separates data acquisition and communication tasks.An Arduino unit performs signal sampling and basic preprocessing, while a NodeMCU (ESP8266) module manages wireless transmission to a cloud platform.Communication between the two modules is achieved using a UART interface, which allows each component to operate independently without causing processing delays.Experimental observations indicate that the system maintains consistent performance during continuous operation.An average delay of approximately 1.8 seconds and a packet delivery ratio close to 98.6% were achieved, demonstrating the system's reliability for remote health monitoring applications.The proposed WBAN-based architecture offers a scalable, low-cost solution for real-time patient surveillance, with potential applications in home care, elderly monitoring, and post-operative recovery.

papers.title: Analysis of Anaesthetic Techniques for Hysteroscopic Procedures
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Hysteroscopy is a minimally invasive procedure widely used in the diagnosis and surgical management of intrauterine pathologies.The selection of an appropriate anaesthetic technique is a critical determinant of procedural safety, patient comfort and clinical outcomes.Both general anaesthesia (GA) and subarachnoid block (SAB) are commonly employed for hysteroscopy, yet comparative evidence from South Asian clinical settings remains limited.This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes, hemodynamic profiles, recovery times, complication rates and patient satisfaction between GA and SAB in patients undergoing hysteroscopic procedures.Methods: A case-control study was conducted at the Department of Anaesthesia, Analgesia and Intensive Care Medicine, Bangladesh Medical University, Dhaka, from January 2025 to January 2026.A total of 76 adult patients (ASA I-II) scheduled for diagnostic or therapeutic hysteroscopy were enrolled.Participants were allocated into two equal groups: GA (n = 38) and SAB (n = 38).Demographic variables, hemodynamic parameters, pain scores using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), recovery time, procedural success and complications were recorded and analyzed using SPSS version 23.0.Results: Both groups were comparable at baseline in age, BMI, ASA status and indications (p > 0.05).Intraoperative heart rate was significantly higher in the GA group (84.7 ± 11.6 vs 76.2 ± 10.4 bpm; p < 0.001), while diastolic BP and MAP were significantly lower in the SAB group (p = 0.032 and p = 0.031, respectively).GA was associated with significantly faster recovery (42.3 ± 12.6 vs 68.7 ± 18.4 min; p < 0.001) and a higher proportion of patients recovering within one hour (76.3% vs 36.8%;p < 0.001).Post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV) was more common in the GA group (23.7% vs 10.5%), whereas shivering was significantly more frequent in the SAB group (15.8% vs 2.6%; p = 0.046).Overall complication rates and patient satisfaction did not differ significantly between the groups.Conclusion: Both GA and SAB are effective and safe anaesthetic options for hysteroscopic procedures.GA offers faster recovery, while SAB provides superior intraoperative hemodynamic Page: 1 1 6 0 1 1 6 0

papers.title: Transforming Engineering Education Through Artificial Intelligence: Enhancing Learning, Innovation, and Student Engagement
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an important component of contemporary engineering education, offering opportunities to improve learning outcomes through data-driven instructional approaches.Technologies such as machine learning, intelligent tutoring systems, natural language processing, learning analytics, and generative AI facilitate personalised learning, automated evaluation, continuous progress tracking, and practical simulation-based experiences.This study presents the Artificial Intelligence-Driven Engineering Education Framework (AIEEF), developed to examine the impact of AI-enabled educational practices on student learning, engagement, and innovation.The framework was evaluated through a systematic review of existing research and empirical analysis of educational performance indicators.The results indicate notable improvements in student achievement, engagement, and participation in creative activities following the implementation of the proposed framework.Among the predictive models examined, Gradient Boosting achieved an accuracy of 94.2%, while overall student engagement increased from 68.7% to 89.8%.The study also considers challenges associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, algorithmic fairness, and academic integrity.The findings suggest that carefully designed AIsupported learning environments can enhance engineering education and assist institutions in preparing graduates for emerging technological and industrial requirements.

papers.title: The impact of modern digital technologies and artificial intelligence on the competitiveness of universities: a theoretical and economic model and scenario analysis
papers.authors: David Nabiev
papers.journal: VESTNIK OF ASTRAKHAN STATE TECHNICAL UNIVERSITY SERIES ECONOMICS
papers.abstract: The study examines modern approaches to assessing the competitiveness of universities and identifies areas for their further methodological improvement in the context of the transformation of the higher education system. The relevance of the research is due to the growing competition among universities, the digitalization of the educational environment, changes in labor market requirements, and the increasing role of universities as actors in socio economic development. Despite the widespread use of various methods for assessing competitiveness, existing approaches are often focused on a limited set of indicators and do not allow for a comprehensive understanding of the structure of an educational organization’s competitive advantages and limitations. The approaches to assessing the competitiveness of universities are examined, their methodological limitations are identified, and the directions for improving the assessment tools are substantiated. The methodological basis consists of the analysis and generalization of scientific literature, comparative analysis, a logical structural approach, and the grouping method. The main approaches to assessing the competitiveness of universities are identified: rating, indicator, integral, expert, and comparative. It has been established that each of them has certain analytical advantages, but does not provide a holistic view of a university’s competitive position due to the fragmented nature of the indicators, insufficient consideration of qualitative characteristics, and limited suitability for managerial analysis. The need to switch to a block structured approach based on a combination of quantitative and qualitative assessment parameters is substantiated. A logical model for assessing the competitiveness of universities has been proposed, including educational, scientific, personnel, management, infrastructure, and reputational components. The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of using the proposed model when developing comprehensive assessment systems and making management decisions aimed at increasing the competitiveness of universities.

papers.title: The role of artificial intelligence in the modern Russian economy innovative development
papers.authors: Vladimir Victorovich Kurchenkov, Roman S. Zaitsev
papers.journal: VESTNIK OF ASTRAKHAN STATE TECHNICAL UNIVERSITY SERIES ECONOMICS
papers.abstract: Innovation is now not just one of the possible paths of development, but the main condition for the survival of any enterprise. The key factor that changes the paradigm of the innovation process is the ability to delegate routine operations. Previously, a significant portion of highly qualified employees’ time was spent on data collection and preliminary information processing, which considerably slowed down the research and development cycle. Modern technologies make it possible to completely delegate trivial tasks to intelligent systems, which are capable of processing such information much faster than a human. In today’s environment, the integration of autonomous intelligent systems is crucial for reducing operational costs. In 2026, artificial intelligence has transformed from an auxiliary technology into an indispensable tool for ensuring the competitiveness of knowledge intensive enterprises. The main areas of application of artificial intelligence have been analyzed, including the automation of business processes, generative design, and predictive analytics of production equipment. The main barriers that limit the implementation of automation systems based on artificial intelligence have been systematized and identified. It has been established that artificial intelligence has changed the methodology of research and development work, reducing the product development cycle from several months to several weeks. The conclusion is formulated that the integration of artificial intelligence tools into production processes reduces costs, the percentage of defective products, and requires staff to develop creative and strategic competencies. The role of artificial intelligence is defined not merely as an automation tool, but as an active participant in the innovation process, capable of creating innovative solutions. An author’s classification of barriers to the implementation of artificial intelligence in knowledge intensive industries has been developed.

papers.title: Trainee Well-Being in the Digital Age: Correlations Between Use of Artificial Intelligence and Burnout, Distress, and Program Satisfaction
papers.authors: Danielle L. Terry, Brandon Gonzalez
papers.abstract: Introduction: The emerging integration and use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education have been well-documented. This study aimed to examine patterns of AI use among medical residents and other medical trainees as well as associations between amount of use and burnout, distress, and program satisfaction. Methods: Medical trainees (N = 74) at a rural teaching hospital completed an anonymous electronic survey. We used Pearson’s correlation to examine associations. Results: We found a significant negative correlation between AI use and burnout. We found a significant positive correlation between AI use and distress. We found no significant association between AI use and program satisfaction. Conclusions: Research that examines the adaptation or introduction of new technology or AI use into clinical or education settings over time would allow for a clearer examination of the impact of AI on medical trainee distress and burnout.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Translation Pedagogy for Critical Thinking: A Pathway to Sustainable Education
papers.authors: Zhenyuan Chen
papers.abstract: In the era of artificial intelligence (AI), sustainable education requires not only the integration of advanced technologies but also the cultivation of key competencies such as critical thinking. This study investigates English major students’ engagement with generative AI tools in translation learning, focusing on their usage patterns, critical thinking behaviors, and ethical awareness. A mixed-methods design combining questionnaire data and semi-structured interviews was employed to examine how students interact with AI in translation contexts. The results show that while students frequently use AI for translation, writing, and language learning, their engagement remains primarily functional and efficiency-driven. Although they display openness and flexibility toward AI, their reasoning confidence, self-regulation, and ethical reflection are underdeveloped, indicating surface-level interaction and overreliance on technological authority. These findings highlight the need to cultivate higher-order cognitive and ethical capacities in translation training. Central to this discussion is the conceptualization of the ideal learner in AI-assisted translation, a reflective, autonomous, and ethically aware individual who engages with AI as a partner in cognitive and moral development. Building on this, the study proposes pedagogical strategies that integrate AI literacy, process-oriented assessment, and teacher training to foster critical thinking and responsible AI use in sustainable translation education.

papers.title: A Study on the Impact of AI-Assisted Teaching Integration in College English on Students’ Writing Performance: A Case Study of Hubei Polytechnic University
papers.authors: Yimo Liu, Zhongqing Hu
papers.abstract: At present, there are some problems in college English writing teaching, such as students ' low interest in writing, lack of personalized guidance, and low feedback efficiency. Artificial intelligence technology provides new ideas for teaching reform. In order to explore the actual impact of artificial intelligence-assisted teaching on college students’ English writing ability, this study selected two non-English major classes in Hubei Polytechnic University to carry out a one-semester quasi-experiment: 55 students in the experimental group adopted artificial intelligence-assisted teaching, and 53 students in the control group adopted traditional teaching. After the experiment, data were collected through questionnaires and in-depth interviews (10 students in each group), and the teaching effectiveness was evaluated by combining quantitative and qualitative results. The results showed that the average scores of each dimension of writing ability in the experimental class were higher than those in the control group, but did not reach a statistically significant level (P > 0.05). In the interview, the students in the experimental class had a significantly higher positive evaluation of writing interest (80%), learning effect (70%) and classroom interaction (90%). At the same time, they also put forward the problems of imperfect AI tools and easy to produce technical dependence. The control group feedback that the traditional teaching has the shortcomings of feedback lag and single form. In summary, although there is no significant statistical difference in the quantitative data, the mean value shows a positive trend of AI-assisted teaching, and the interview results also confirm that it can stimulate writing interest and improve learning experience. The teaching mode has application potential, and the teaching effect can be improved by prolonging the intervention cycle, optimizing the tools and strengthening the guidance of teachers.

papers.title: Patient and Carer Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence- Supported Rehabilitation Technologies: A Cross-Sectional Survey (Preprint)
papers.authors: Ece Çınar, Sadia Issa, Hema Devi
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being considered for rehabilitation applications including personalised exercise, progress monitoring, risk identification, documentation, remote rehabilitation, and technology-assisted interventions. However, successful implementation depends not only on technical performance but also on patient and carer acceptability, trust, and willingness to engage with AI-supported care. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to evaluate patient and carer perspectives on AI-supported rehabilitation within a National Health Service (NHS) rehabilitation service, with particular focus on perceived benefit, willingness to use AI-supported rehabilitation, and the influence of clinician oversight on trust. METHODS A cross-sectional paper-based survey was conducted at a single NHS rehabilitation service between May and July 2026. Adult patients and relatives or carers completed items assessing AI familiarity, digital confidence, perceived benefits and acceptability of AI applications, willingness to choose and recommend AI-supported rehabilitation, and trust with and without clinician review. Questionnaires with missing responses were excluded using complete-case analysis. Paired trust responses were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with an exact McNemar test used as a sensitivity analysis. A composite perceived-benefit score was evaluated using internal consistency and exploratory factor analysis. Associations with willingness were examined using Spearman correlations and exploratory proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression. RESULTS Of 112 questionnaires collected, 106 complete questionnaires were included, comprising 46 patients (43.4%) and 60 relatives or carers (56.6%). Attitudes toward AI-supported rehabilitation were cautiously favourable, with agreement highest for personalisation of rehabilitation goals and exercises (59.4%) and exploration of AI-supported rehabilitation technologies (56.6%). Trust was substantially higher when clinician oversight was present: median trust increased from 3.0 (IQR 2.0–4.0) without clinician review to 4.0 (IQR 3.0–4.0) with clinician review. Overall, 60/106 participants (56.6%) reported greater trust with clinician oversight, and agreement or strong agreement increased from 29.2% to 61.3% (Wilcoxon W=120.0, P<.001; rank-biserial correlation=0.885). The perceived-benefit items demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach α=0.952; McDonald ω=0.953) and supported a single-factor composite. Perceived benefit was strongly associated with willingness to choose AI-supported rehabilitation (Spearman ρ=0.784, P<.001) and remained the only independently associated predictor in the adjusted ordinal regression model (adjusted OR 12.44, 95% CI 6.36–24.33; P<.001). CONCLUSIONS Patients and carers showed cautious but meaningful openness to AI-supported rehabilitation. Trust was strongly dependent on continued clinician involvement, supporting a human-in-the-loop model rather than autonomous AI implementation. Perceived practical benefit appeared central to willingness to adopt AI-supported rehabilitation. Implementation strategies should therefore combine visible clinician oversight with clear demonstration of patient benefit and support tailored to individual digital confidence. CLINICALTRIAL N/A

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces: barriers and opportunities to widespread clinical adoption (Preprint)
papers.authors: Diogo Neves, Juliana Sá, Vasileia Kostaridou, M.R.A. Calado, Henrique Martins
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) could address unmet clinical needs in neurological disorders, particularly for communication and rehabilitation, yet their use remains largely confined to research settings. The views of the professionals who develop, deploy, and finance these devices on what hinders wider clinical adoption have received little attention. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to explore the barriers and opportunities for wider clinical adoption of BCIs as perceived by medical, engineering, and management professionals, and to draw health policy and management implications. METHODS We conducted a qualitative study using three online focus groups (n=22) with medical, engineering, and management professionals explored real-world experiences, perceptions, and expectations regarding BCI adoption. Six statements rated on a 5-point Likert scale served as discussion prompts. Transcripts were analyzed using a hybrid deductive-inductive thematic approach, informed by previous evidence of BCI clinical applications. RESULTS Participants agreed most strongly that BCIs can address unmet clinical needs and that current studies have important limitations. Answers on whether regulatory approval ensures reimbursement were mostly neutral, reflecting limited familiarity. Four themes emerged, interpreted alongside comparisons with other healthcare technologies: (1) research, with publication and funding incentives favoring novelty over translation; (2) healthcare ecosystem and adoption, including translational and commercial "valleys of death," the gap between approval and reimbursement, unclear target populations, clinician involvement in design, burdensome setup and unmet expectations (with eye trackers as competing communication tools), and unsettled quality-of-life measurement; (3) artificial intelligence and data, including ownership, liability, and cross-border rules; and (4) society, including media hype, repair-versus-enhancement tensions, and stigma. CONCLUSIONS According to these professionals, barriers to wider clinical adoption of BCIs lie as much in the surrounding ecosystem as in the technology. Reimbursement evidence should be planned alongside regulatory work, policy should be application-specific, and clinicians should be involved early in design. For rehabilitation and assistive technology, trials should report sustained use, setup time, and caregiver burden, and compare BCIs with existing assistive tools. The data were collected in 2022 from a small sample with few physicians; future work should include patients, rehabilitation clinicians, payers, and regulators. CLINICALTRIAL brain-computer interfaces, brain-machine interfaces, neurotechnology, medical devices, innovation, quality-of-care

papers.title: Association Between Wrist-Worn Device-Estimated Sleep Efficiency and Hand Grip Strength in Older Outpatients With Cardiometabolic Diseases: Cross-Sectional Study
papers.authors: Yoshiaki Tamura, Rui Gong, Yuji Murao, Fumino Yorikawa, Satomi Kobayashi, Remi Kodera, Kazuhito Oba, Maki Shirobe, Kenji Toyoshima, Kanae Kubo, Yuko Chiba, Hisashi Kawai, Joji Ishikawa, Hiroyuki Sasai, Yoshinori Fujiwara, Akiko Mano, Kenji Toba, Masahiro Akishita, Shuichi P. Obuchi, Atsushi Araki
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Older outpatients with chronic diseases are susceptible to muscle weakness and functional disabilities. Recently, various wearable devices have been developed to generate health lifelogs in daily life; however, data from patients with chronic diseases remain scarce. Previous studies have shown that subjective sleep efficiency assessed by self-questionnaires is associated with grip strength, but whether objective sleep efficiency detected by wearable devices is associated with physical function and body composition remains unclear. Objective The aim of this study is to clarify the association between sleep duration, sleep efficiency estimated by wearable watch, grip strength, frailty, and sarcopenia in outpatients with predominantly cardiometabolic diseases and the influence of diabetes as part of the Smart Watch Innovation for Geriatrics and Gerontology (SWING-Japan) project. Methods In this cross-sectional study, the wrist-worn device Silmee 22 was used in an outpatient clinic of an acute care facility for 7‐90 nights for the analyses, and individual average sleep duration and efficiency (wearable-estimated sleep efficiency: total sleep duration/time spent in bed) were calculated. Low grip strength was defined as <28 kg for men and <18 kg for women. Sarcopenia was defined based on the Asian criteria and frailty based on the Japanese version of Cardiovascular Health Study and Kihon Checklist criteria. Sleep indices were compared between individuals with and without these conditions. Next, logistic regression analysis was performed, with lower grip strength as the dependent variable and wearable-estimated sleep efficiency as the independent variable, adjusted for age, sex, BMI, glycohemoglobin, cognitive function (Mini-Mental State Examination), Geriatric Depression Scale-15 score, and daily step count measured using the ankle-worn device WalkX. Subgroup analyses were performed and stratified according to the status of diabetes mellitus. Results Data from 165 patients (median age: 77 y; duration of device use: 65 d; diabetes prevalence: 55%) were used for analyses. Wearable-estimated sleep efficiency and sleep duration were significantly lower in patients with low grip strength than in those without (58.0% vs 62.7%, P =.006, 245 vs 276 min, P =.04). Wearable-estimated sleep efficiency was not associated with frailty, low muscle mass, or slow walking speed. After adjusting for the above variables, low wearable-estimated sleep efficiency, but not low sleep duration, was associated with a risk of lower grip strength (odds ratio 1.04, 95% CI 1.01‐1.08; P =.02) by 1 percentage point decrease in wearable-estimated sleep efficiency. This association was observed in patients with diabetes (odds ratio 1.05, 95% CI 1.002‐1.093; P =.04). However, no significant interaction was observed. Conclusions In older patients with cardiometabolic diseases, objective low wearable-estimated sleep efficiency evaluated with wrist-worn wearable devices was associated with low muscle strength. No evidence was found to suggest that the strength of this association differed according to diabetes status. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the long-term association between low wearable-estimated sleep efficiency and muscle strength in this population.

papers.title: Human-in-the-Loop Suicide Risk Detection and Clinical Escalation in a Generative AI Mental Health Chatbot: Prospective Implementation Study
papers.authors: Suzette V. Glasner, Darcy Michero, Matthew P. Stewart
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mental illness is the leading cause of disability worldwide, affecting more than one billion individuals, and suicide accounts for 720,000 to 800,000 deaths annually. While AI-native mental health chatbots have the potential to fill a sizable gap between treatment need and workforce capacity, their rapid proliferation has outpaced the development of scalable procedures to identify, detect, and respond to suicidal ideation. Despite AI best practice recommendations to incorporate human oversight for safety monitoring and intervention, studies of procedures for human clinical oversight and crisis response are scarce. OBJECTIVE: To implement a human-in-the-loop suicide risk screening, detection, and clinical escalation protocol in a generative AI mental health chatbot. METHODS: In an implementation study of a human-in-the-loop suicide risk detection and escalation protocol, adults were recruited online to participate in a single-arm trial of an AI-native mental health chatbot. Participants completed a pre-treatment screening using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). In Phase 1, individuals who endorsed suicidal ideation were escalated to a human clinician for further assessment, safety planning and provision of referral resources, as appropriate. In Phase 2, escalation was triggered by either PHQ-9 responses or detection of spontaneous disclosure of implicit or explicit suicidality in conversational AI interactions. In both phases, the Ask Suicide-Screening Questionnaire (ASQ) guided human-led assessment and risk stratification. Prevalence of suicidal ideation was assessed, along with the rate of successful human outreach, time from suicidality risk detection to human outreach and results of risk stratification evaluation. RESULTS: In Phase 1, 624 participants completed suicide screening, of whom 81 (13.0%) endorsed PHQ-9 item 9 (score >1). Outreach was initiated a mean of 11.2 minutes after the alert (SD=13.2; range 1-54 minutes). A clinician successfully reached 25/81 participants (30.9%). In Phase 2, 650 participants completed screening, of whom 133 (20.5%) screened positive at baseline. Across the 30 day post-baseline observation period, 284 risk-alert events were generated among 172 participants (26.5%), including 50 conversational suicidal ideation events. Clinicians successfully contacted 73/172 participants (42.4%). Time from risk detection to clinician outreach initiation was an average of 11.5 minutes (SD 11.7; range 1-58 minutes). CONCLUSIONS: Proactive, universal suicide risk screening and conversational detection using a human-in-the-loop protocol can be operationally implemented for individuals utilizing a Generative AI mental health chatbot. A subgroup of those who were responsive to human clinical outreach described the approach as acceptable and helpful. Given that contact and clinical assessment were not completed for a sizable proportion of alerted participants, further research is needed to optimize assessment capabilities for those who could not be reached, and characterize the impact of these procedures on clinical outcomes. Nevertheless, the safety procedures reported herein provide a framework from which purpose-built AI-native mental health chatbots can build and refine human-in-the-loop safety responses and protocols.

papers.title: Physical Fitness and Psychological Stress Among University Students: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study
papers.authors: P Reddy Haritha, K Madhavi
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Background: Sedentary study routines and academic pressure may reduce physical fitness and increase psychological stress in university students. Physiotherapy-based exercise is a proposed non-pharmacological approach, but the current fitness and stress profile of students, and how the two relate, is not well described. Objective: To describe physical fitness (BMI, flexibility, muscular endurance) and psychological stress in students aged 17-25 years, to compare stress across domains and by sex, and to examine fitness-stress associations. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, fitness data from 52 Bachelor of Physiotherapy students (41 females, 11 males) and responses to the 40-item Student Stress Inventory (SSI) from 51 students were analysed. Stress domains were compared by repeated-measures ANOVA with Bonferroni-adjusted paired t-tests; sex differences were tested with Welch's t-test and the Mann-Whitney U test; associations were tested with Pearson and Spearman correlations, with Holm adjustment (p < 0.05). Results: Mean age was 20.46 ± 2.23 years and mean BMI 22.72 ± 4.64 kg/m2; 42.3% of students were outside the normal BMI range (19.2% underweight, 23.1% overweight or obese). Mean total stress was 85.2 ± 19.6 out of 160 (Cronbach's α = 0.91). Domain scores differed (F(3,150) = 15.51, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.24): environmental stress was highest and remained significantly higher than every other domain after Bonferroni correction. Stress did not differ by sex (all p ? 0.29). Males had higher weight (63.96 ± 12.20 vs 55.41 ± 10.62 kg; Mann-Whitney p = 0.027) and BMI (25.43 ± 5.50 vs 22.00 ± 4.17 kg/m2; p = 0.043), although Welch's t-test was borderline (p = 0.052 and 0.076). Flexibility correlated with environmental stress (r = 0.31, p = 0.028), which was not confirmed by Spearman correlation (p = 0.092) or after Holm adjustment (p = 0.42). Conclusion: Students showed moderate stress, mainly environmental, and a substantial proportion had abnormal BMI, with no robust fitness-stress associations. These findings support screening students for weight status and stress and provide reference data for future studies, including intervention trials of physiotherapy.

papers.title: Institutionalization of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine’s Publishing Industry
papers.authors: O. Sytnyk
papers.abstract: Introduction. The spread of artificial intelligence in the publishing industry is transforming not only individual production operations but also professional roles, editorial procedures, man­agement models, content quality criteria, and approaches to organizational governance. Under these conditions, AI should be considered not only as a technological tool but also as a factor of institutional change in the professional environment. Relevance and purpose. The relevance of the study stems from the insufficient conceptu­alization of the organizational dimension of AI implementation in Ukraine’s publishing industry. The article aims to identify the specific features of AI institutionalization by analyzing the rela­tionship between individual professional use of the technology and the level of its organizational implementation. Methodology. The empirical basis is a quantitative survey conducted from December 2025 to February 2026 with 374 respondents. Valid-response subsamples were used for particular an­alytical blocks, while a matched subsample of n = 240 was used to compare individual AI use with respondent-reported organizational AI implementation. The analysis employed descriptive statistics, the chi-square test, and the two-sided McNemar test. Results. AI institutionalization was found to be uneven and predominantly transitional. Some form of official AI implementation in their organization was reported by 61.3% of respondents, with localized use being the most common format. Within the matched subsample, active profes­sional AI use at the individual level was recorded among 77.1% of respondents. The study revealed a low level of formalization of AI practices, weak internal policies and contractual regulation, the predominance of self-education, and insufficient professional training as the most frequently re­ported barrier to implementation. Conclusions. The findings indicate that AI is already widely used at the individual level with­in the analyzed publishing environment, while respondent-reported organizational AI implemen­tation remains uneven and incompletely formalized. The novelty of the study lies in identifying the asymmetry between individual use and respondent-reported organizational implementation of AI. The findings may inform the development of internal policies, training programs, mecha­nisms for responsible AI use, and managerial coordination.

papers.title: Practices of using artificial intelligence in Ukrainian online media
papers.authors: Є. Селюх
papers.abstract: Introduction. The article examines practices of artificial intelligence (AI) use among repre­sentatives of Ukrainian online media and their role in content production, editing, visualization, and distribution. The focus is placed on the frequency of generative AI use, the tasks delegated to such systems, perceived effectiveness, and professional risks. Relevance of the study. The topic is relevant because AI tools are rapidly spreading across the media environment while stable newsroom rules for their use remain underdeveloped. The purpose is to identify AI-use practices among representatives of Ukrainian online media, deter-mine the main delegated tasks, subjective assessments of perceived effectiveness and integration barriers, and compare selected indicators by media audience size. Methodology. The study combines analysis and synthesis of scholarly literature, a question-naire survey, descriptive statistics, comparative analysis, and interpretive approaches. The ac-tive survey period lasted from 7 April to 28 May 2026. Invitations were distributed by e-mail to media selected through a media register, the Ukr.net media catalogue, and verification of media websites. Of 27 returned questionnaires, one was excluded because the AI-related block was left unanswered; the final analytical sample was n = 26. Results. Daily use of generative AI was reported by 34.6% of respondents and several-times-a-week use by 19.2%. The most frequently delegated tasks were drafting article or blog-post frameworks (65.4%), generating visual materials (57.7%), and editing existing content (50.0%). The mean subjective rating of the perceived effectiveness of AI-generated content was 6.15 out of 10 (median = 7). A descriptive comparison by audience size showed a higher share of regular AI users among media with more than one million monthly users; however, the small subgroup sizes do not allow this pattern to be interpreted as a statistically significant relationship. Conclusions. Within the studied sample, AI is used primarily as an auxiliary tool rather than as an autonomous author. The main barriers concern copyright, loss of human creativity, unstable output quality, and ethical risks. The findings describe the practices of the surveyed media repre­sentatives and should not be generalized to the entire Ukrainian media market.

papers.title: Integration of Gemini Notebook into Professional Training of Journalists and Editors
papers.authors: С. Фіялка
papers.abstract: Introduction. The rapid integration of generative AI is transforming the professional activi-ties of journalists and editors, highlighting the need to develop AI literacy. Particular importance is currently attached to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) tools, which generate responses based on a user-selected corpus of sources and provide a citation for each claim. One such tool is Gemini Notebook. Relevance and Aim. The relevance of the study is determined by the insufficient develop­ment of methodological approaches to integrating RAG systems into the professional training of journalists and editors, as well as by the need to develop future professionals’ skills in information verification, critical evaluation of AI-generated outputs, and responsible use of digital tools. The aim of the article is to substantiate the educational potential of Gemini Notebook and to develop methodological approaches to its use in the educational process. Methodology. The study is based on the analysis and synthesis of research on AI literacy, journalism education, ethical aspects of generative AI use, and RAG technologies. The methods employed include source analysis, functional analysis of the Gemini Notebook service, and the case study method. Results. A three-level model for integrating Gemini Notebook into the training of journalists and editors is substantiated. It comprises the basic level (familiarization with the service’s func tionality and principles of working with data), the applied level (completion of practical tasks), and the reflective level (documentation of successful and erroneous cases of application). Educa­tional use cases of the service are described. Conclusions. The scientific novelty of the study lies in conceptualizing the use of Gemini Notebook in journalism and editorial education as a model of AI-assisted learning in which pro­fessional work with sources constitutes the central object of learning. The practical significance of the findings lies in the possibility of applying the proposed three-level model and the described use cases in the development of professional training courses. Further research should focus on a comparative analysis of the effectiveness of Gemini Notebook and other RAG systems.
