The Information Shock outlined is anticipated to have major impacts for librarians and information professionals moving forward. Originality/value The paper offers a historically grounded distinction between document-producing and transactional AI authorship, arguing that AI is pushing the exchange to take the mediating position that the field has long held.

papers.title: Exploring the impact of AI and metaverse on student academic and personal growth through social–emotional learning: a SEM-ANN approach
papers.authors: Shubhangi Verma, Shubham Singhania, Naval Garg, Varda Sardana
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) technology and metaverse on academic and personal growth of students, moderated by the components of social–emotional learning (SEL), that is, emotional intelligence and peer relationships. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a two-stage hybrid structural equation modeling (SEM) artificial neural network (ANN) methodology. The initial phase uses SmartPLS4 to perform partial least squares SEM for exploratory investigations. Further, to explore the non-linear interaction between variables, an ANN model is used. Findings Findings suggest that perceived usefulness significantly impacts academic growth. The relationship is enhanced by moderators such as peer relationships and emotional intelligence, where higher perceived usefulness weakens the contribution of peer relationships to personal growth, while emotional intelligence strengthens the contribution of perceived usefulness to personal growth. Moreover, the study identifies social–emotional variables as key predictors of enhanced personal and academic growth. Research limitations/implications This study offers major implications for higher education by demonstrating how integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and SEL frameworks can enhance students’ academic and personal growth. Practically, it urges institutions to prioritize emotional intelligence and peer relationships alongside technological adoption, promoting a more inclusive, sustainable and student-centered learning environment. Originality/value This study examines the use of emerging technologies, AI and metaverse applications in higher education. Its contribution lies in integrating them with the SEL framework. Rather than treating learner characteristics as predictors, this study positions emotional intelligence and peer relationships as moderators that influence whether technology engagement leads to academic and personal growth. By further modeling non-linear relationships among variables, this study refines the predictive understanding of technology-enhanced learning and informs the andragogical implementation of these tools.

papers.title: Effects of green certification and price premiums on consumer willingness to pay for recycled products from construction and demolition waste
papers.authors: Zhikun Ding, Wenjie Li, Xinyue Huang, Longhui Liao
papers.abstract: Purpose Understanding consumers' willingness to pay (WTP) for construction and demolition waste (CDW)-recycled products is crucial for advancing the circular economy. While prior studies have separately examined consumers' responses to green products and price premiums, a neurocognitive gap remains in integrating the dual factors (green certification as a sustainability cue and price premium as a cost cue), especially for CDW-recycled products. This study aims to investigate how green certification tiers and price premiums influence consumers' WTP and the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach An event-related potential (ERP) experiment with a 3 (green certification tier: one-star, two-star, and three-star) × 3 (price premium level: 5%, 20%, and 35%) within-subjects factorial design was conducted. Forty participants completed a behavioral choice task (WTP assessment) while EEG data were recorded. Findings Key results revealed that behaviorally, WTP increased with increasing certification tiers and decreased with increasing premium levels, showing a significant synergistic interaction. The combination of two-star and 20% premium products elicited the longest response time, consistent with diagnostic ambiguity, while three-star and 5% premium products showed the shortest response time, consistent with cue consistency. Neurophysiologically, P200 amplitude increased for one-star products at 20% premium, suggesting greater attentional resource allocation for this cue combination. N400 amplitude peaked for one-star products at 35% premium, suggesting greater evaluative conflict associated with the “low-quality high-price” combination, while three-star products showed no significant N400 difference at 35% premiums. Originality/value These results revealed the impacts of green certification and price premiums on WTP from a behavioral-neural perspective for CDW-recycled products, demonstrating that cue consistency and diagnosticity jointly modulate decision-making at both behavioral and neural levels. The findings offer reference for enterprises' pricing and communication strategies and for policymakers' efforts to refine green certification frameworks, with the aim of advancing circular economy objectives in construction.

papers.title: Predicting student success in open and distance learning: a comparative evaluation of machine learning models
papers.authors: Mehmet Fırat
papers.abstract: Purpose This study compares Logistic Regression, linear Support Vector Machine, Random Forest and Histogram Gradient Boosting for predicting four student outcomes in open and distance learning (ODL) from the first four weeks of study. Design/methodology/approach Using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, the analysis included 27,535 registrations from 24,841 students. Day-28 predictors comprised static characteristics, raw virtual learning environment (VLE) activity and engagement-focused behavioral features. Class-weighted models were evaluated using nested stratified group cross-validation, with student records grouped across partitions. The macro-averaged F1 score (macro-F1) was the primary metric. Findings With engagement-focused features, the linear support vector machine yielded the highest macro-F1 (0.406) and 47.6% accuracy, followed closely by Random Forest (0.404) and Histogram Gradient Boosting (0.402). Engineered behavioral features improved macro-F1 by 0.014 over raw VLE activity, with a 95% confidence interval of [0.009, 0.019]. A secondary assessment-informed model reached a macro-F1 of 0.434, whereas excluding sensitive demographic attributes did not clearly reduce performance. Originality/value This research contributes to ODL through a fixed early window, student-grouped validation and theory-aligned behavioral feature engineering. It supports timely learner review while treating VLE traces as partial rather than comprehensive indicators of engagement.

papers.title: Symbolic ensemble learning enables discovery of fast accurate physics-based interatomic potentials
papers.authors: Bilvin Varughese, Aditya Koneru, Adil Muhammad, Troy D. Loeffler, Sukriti Manna, Subramanian K. R. S. Sankaranarayanan, Jan‐Michael Y. Carrillo, Orçun Yildiz, Tom Peterka
papers.abstract: Machine learning has transformed materials simulation by delivering force fields with ab initio accuracy, yet bridging the gap between high-dimensional regression and physical interpretability remains a grand challenge. Conventional analytical potentials offer transparency but often fail to capture the complexity of far-from-ground state regimes. Here, we introduce a hybrid symbolic-neural framework that unifies the interpretability of the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) with the adaptability of data-driven learning. Using Equation Learner Neural Networks (EqNNs) trained on density functional theory (DFT) data, we obtain interpretable models for aluminum through three distinct training protocols: random initialization trained via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) and gradient descent, and two transfer-learning strategies initialized from a copper potential - one employing MCTS followed by gradient descent, and the other using gradient descent only. We find that while all three resulting symbolic models achieve sub-10 meV/atom accuracy, they occupy distinct local minima in the functional landscape, exhibiting complementary trade-offs across phonon dispersion, surface energetics, and elastic response. By integrating these diverse functional forms through a weighted symbolic ensemble, we derive a composite potential that surpasses the fidelity of its constituent models. The resulting ensemble effectively mitigates individual biases, delivering superior consistency with DFT benchmarks across equation-of-state curvature, phonon spectra, and melting dynamics. This approach demonstrates that combining transfer learning with ensemble symbolic regression yields compact, transparent potentials capable of robust prediction across equilibrium and non-equilibrium states.

papers.title: From medical to pedagogical care
papers.authors: Xinhuang Tang, Shukun Chen, Jinyan Chen
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) agents, including chatbots and virtual tutors, into education has expanded rapidly; however, systematic quantitative analysis of research trends in this field remains limited. Notably, the intellectual foundations of AI agent research lie not in education but in medicine, where AI agents were first extensively deployed and studied in clinical, experimental, and pedagogical contexts. METHODS: In this study, a bibliometric analysis of 377 records retrieved from the Web of Science was conducted using VOSviewer to map the evolution, thematic focus, and collaborative networks within this field. RESULTS: The study showed AI agent research originated strongly in healthcare, with educational applications emerging more recently. Key research themes encompassed AI technologies, human-computer interaction, pedagogical applications, and ethical considerations. Collaborative efforts were led by the USA and China, supported by active European and Asian research hubs. The findings revealed a dual narrative of significant benefits for personalized learning and learner well-being alongside persistent challenges such as algorithmic bias and accessibility gaps. CONCLUSION: To realize the transformative potential of AI in education, future research should prioritize the development of adaptive algorithms, robust ethical frameworks, inclusive design, and interdisciplinary collaboration. By focusing on these areas, the field can work toward overcoming technical, ethical, and logistical barriers, thereby ensuring that AI acts as a sustainable force for equity and excellence in education.

papers.title: The effect of cognitive behavioral therapy for sleep and glycemic outcomes in people with diabetes
papers.authors: Zhu Lanyu, Xiaofei He, Lulu Ma, Bo Zhang, Yueqi Yin, Lanyu Zhu
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbances are highly prevalent in individuals with diabetes and are associated with various adverse physiological, psychological, and social consequences. A growing body of research supports the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) in managing sleep problems in diabetes. However, the extent of its positive correlation with sleep quality and glycemic outcomes remains unclear due to the lack of rigorous evidence synthesis. METHODS: Ten databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, MEDLINE, APA PsycInfo, China National Knowledge Infrastructure [CNKI], Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform, VIP) were searched using keywords related to cognitive behavioral therapy and diabetes, from their inception until June 2026, to identify eligible randomized controlled trials. Researchers independently screened and extracted data from the included studies. The risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (RoB 2.0). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager software (RevMan) 5.4.1 to estimate overall effects and for prespecified subgroup analyses. Sensitivity analysis, assessment of publication bias, and meta-regression were conducted using STATA 17.0 to explore study-level variables potentially contributing to heterogeneity. RESULTS: Ten eligible randomized controlled trials involving a total of 2827 participants from 4 countries were included in this synthesis. When comparing CBT to usual care or health education, CBT demonstrated a significant effect size for improving sleep quality (mean difference [MD] = -1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI] = -1.98 to -0.96; P < .00001; I2 = 89%). Significant improvements were also observed for glycemic outcomes (HbA1c: MD = -0.35%; 95% CI = -0.44 to -0.25; P < .00001; I2 = 94%) and insomnia severity (MD = -2.06; 95% CI = -4.24 to 0.12; P = .004; I2 = 88%). However, there was no significant improvement in BMI (MD = -0.12; 95% CI = -0.72 to 0.48; P = .69; I2 = 0%). Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed significant differences based on follow-up time. Through meta-regression, disease type, sample size, and intervention plan were not found to be sources of heterogeneity. CONCLUSION: Cognitive behavioral therapy significantly improves sleep quality, reduces HbA1c levels, and alleviates insomnia severity in people with diabetes. Future high-quality research is needed to optimize protocols, define target populations, and facilitate wider clinical implementation.

papers.title: Visual Target P3b Amplitude Mediates the Relationship between Childhood Traumatic Experiences and Social Functioning in People at Clinical High Risk for Psychosis
papers.authors: Jason Smucny, Holly Hamilton, Suzie Lavoie, Thomas J. Whitford, Luis Alameda, Öznur Baştürk, Grace R. Jacobs, Inès Lepreux, Teya Petrova, Lotta-Katrin Pries, Guilia Trotta, Sandra Vieira, Jean Addington, Sylvain Bouix A, Nicholas J K Breitborde, Matthew R. Broome, Kristin S. Cadenhead, Monica E. Calkins, Ricardo E. Carrión, Rolando I Castillo-Passi, Jimmy Choi, Philippe Conus, Cheryl Mary Corcoran, Covadonga M. Díaz‐Caneja, Lauren M. Ellman, Paolo Fusar‐Poli, Louise Birkedal Glenthøj, Leslie E. Horton, Joseph P. Kambeitz, Tina Kapur, Matcheri S. Keshavan, Minah Kim, Sung‐Wan Kim, Jun Soo Kwon, Daniel Mamah, Vijay Anand Mittal, Ofer Pasternak, Godfrey D. Pearlson, Jesus Perez, David R. Roalf, Jason Schiffman, Jai  L. Shah, Steven M. Silverstein, Stefan Smesny, Gregory P. Strauss, Judy L. Thompson, Daniel H. Wolf, Tianhong Zhang, Carrie E. Bearden, John Michael Kane, René S Kahn, Patrick D. McGorry, Barnaby Nelson, Martha E. Shenton, Scott W Woods, Gregory A Light, Daniel H. Mathalon
papers.abstract: Abstract Background and Hypothesis Clinical high risk (CHR) for psychosis status is associated with poor social functioning. Previous studies suggest that childhood trauma and reduced amplitude of the P300 event-related potential (ERP) component elicited by infrequent target stimuli (P3b) are associated with poor social function. Here, we examined whether reduced P3b mediates the relationship between reported trauma history and social function in CHR individuals, possibly reflecting the impact of past trauma on neurophysiological processes subserving attention that ultimately influence social functioning. Study Design Target P3b ERP amplitudes from visual and auditory oddball tasks acquired at baseline in the Accelerating Medicines Partnership® Schizophrenia (AMP SCZ) study were analyzed. The mediating effects of auditory and visual P3b amplitude on the relationship between trauma history (Childhood Trauma Questionnaire total score) and Negative Symptom Inventory-Psychosis Risk Asociality (NSI-PR) as well as social functioning (Global Functioning: Social (GFS) scores were examined. Study Results Data from 931 CHR participants (average age 21.29 years, 36.3% male) were included in mediation analyses. Visual P3b showed significant (p < .05) mediation of the relationship between trauma load and GFS score (5.4% mediation) as well as mediation of the relationship between trauma history and NSI-PR asociality (9.3% mediation). Auditory P3b did not significantly mediate either relationship. Conclusions These results suggest that visual, but not auditory, P3b mediates the relationship between past trauma load and social functioning in CHR, suggesting the effect of trauma on the neurophysiological processes subserving visual target detection may contribute to social functioning deficits in CHR individuals.

papers.title: Integrating generative AI with multimodal interaction to inquire into scientific phenomena
papers.authors: Joonhyeong Park, Gracia Xin Jie Soh, Shan Ying Lim, Peter Peng Foo Lee
papers.abstract: This study developed and evaluated two customised generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots designed to provide stepwise guidance for secondary students’ inquiry into scientific phenomena. Biology and physics chatbots were developed using the Predict–Observe–Explain (POE) framework and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to align with Singapore science syllabuses and incorporated segmented video demonstrations. 14 evaluators quantitatively and qualitatively assessed the chatbots in terms of Accuracy, Clarity, Dialogue flow, Ease of use, and Efficiency. Both chatbots were rated positively overall, particularly for Ease of use, Clarity, Efficiency, and Accuracy, while Dialogue flow received lower ratings, especially for the physics chatbot. Qualitative feedback identified needs for stronger scaffolding, better handling of follow-up questions, and additional multimodal support. The findings highlight key design considerations for GenAI-supported scientific inquiry.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in English as a Foreign Language Learning: a comprehensive theoretical framework for pedagogical integration and psychological well-being
papers.authors: Jumana Sobhi Awawda, Yasir Bashir
papers.abstract: This theoretical paper presents a conceptual framework for understanding the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning contexts. Drawing on established foreign language acquisition theories, sociocultural learning paradigms, and emerging digital pedagogy scholarship, the paper develops the AI-Enhanced Foreign Language Learning (AEFLL) framework around a specific theoretical proposition. AI tools, unlike the human interlocutors around which classical SLA theory was built, can decouple the cognitive, affective, and social functions that face-to-face instruction has traditionally delivered as a single, integrated package. This decoupling, rather than the broader observation that cognition, affect, and social interaction all matter for language learning, constitutes the framework’s central theoretical contribution. It generates directional, testable hypotheses about how different AI tools, by recombining these functions in different proportions, produce different developmental trade-offs for EFL learners. The paper situates this argument within current scholarship on human-AI collaboration, critical AI literacy, and the sociopolitical risks of AI-mediated education, including linguistic inequality and data colonialism, and offers a balanced account of the psychological benefits and risks associated with AI-mediated learning. Practical implications for curriculum design and teacher professional development are discussed alongside a structured agenda for empirical validation.

papers.title: A systematic review of the effectiveness of adopting artificial intelligence-driven immersive technologies in STEM education
papers.authors: Segun Michael Ojetunde, Umesh Dewnarain Ramnarain
papers.abstract: The complexity of abstract concepts in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) has encouraged educators to adopt innovative instructional approaches. Advances in artificial intelligence have accelerated the development of AI-powered immersive technologies (AIPIT) for STEM education, yet evidence of their effectiveness remains fragmented. This study addressed that gap through a multi-method investigation combining a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, 17 eligible studies were selected after screening records from Scopus, ERIC, EBSCOhost, and Google Scholar. Extracted data were analysed using descriptive statistics, while bibliometric analysis examined the broader unscreened literature. Findings indicate that AIPIT research is an emerging field, with the United States and China leading publication output. Nine studies reported improved learner comprehension, eight identified increased engagement, and two demonstrated gains in academic achievement and timely feedback. Pedagogically, 42.2% of the studies adopted self-directed learning, while 29.4% employed inquiry-based learning, highlighting strong alignment between AI-driven immersive technologies and established STEM teaching approaches. The evidence suggests that AI-enhanced immersive learning environments improve students’ understanding, engagement, and academic performance. The study recommends expanding infrastructure and professional development to support effective AIPIT integration into STEM teaching, particularly for complex concepts.

papers.title: Sexual Health Literacy in the Context of Artificial Intelligence Among Nursing Students: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study
papers.authors: Fatma Aslan Demirtaş, Mehtap Gümüşay, Buğse Ayyıldız
papers.abstract: ABCTRACTObjectives This study aimed to examine nursing students’ sexual health literacy and attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI), and the relationship between them.Method This descriptive and cross-sectional study was conducted with 377 nursing students enrolled at a public university. Data were collected using a Demographic Information Form, the Students’ Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence Scale, and the Sexual Health Literacy Scale. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis were used to analyze the data.Results Nursing students had moderate to high sexual health literacy and generally positive attitudes toward AI. Students with higher sexual health literacy had more positive attitudes toward AI (r = .216, p < .01). Multiple regression analysis showed that sexual health literacy (standardized β = 0.300, 95% CI for B = 0.329 to 0.697, p < .001) and sexual attitude (standardized β = −0.140, 95% CI for B = −0.809 to −0.106, p = .011) were significantly associated with attitudes toward AI. The model explained a small proportion of the variance (Adjusted R2 = .072).Conclusions The findings offer suggestive evidence that nursing students with higher sexual health literacy hold more positive attitudes toward AI and may be better positioned to use it productively for sexual health information. These findings highlight the importance of integrating sexual health literacy with digital and AI literacy within a holistic framework in nursing education.

papers.title: Association between body mass index and nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among people receiving tuberculosis treatment
papers.authors: Sizwe Mthabela, Sanele Ngcobo, Victoria Oyekunle, Nontuthuko Excellent Maningi, Nothando Mbatha
papers.journal: South African Journal of Clinical Nutrition
papers.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge, with nutritional status playing an important role in treatment outcomes and recovery. While nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) may influence dietary behaviours and nutritional well-being, evidence on their relationship with BMI status among people receiving TB treatment remains limited.Objective: To explore the relationship between body mass index (BMI) and nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) among people receiving TB treatment in the eThekwini District.Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 385 adults receiving TB treatment at selected primary health care (PHC) facilities. Data were collected between August and November 2025 through a semi-structured interviewer-administered questionnaire that assessed sociodemographic characteristics, nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes and practices, as well as dietary intake patterns. Height and weight measurements were used to calculate body mass index (BMI), which was used as an indicator for nutritional status in this study and was categorised as underweight, normal or overweight/obese via anthropometric measurement using the World Health Organization’s (WHO) formula for BMI.Pearson’s chi-square test was used to assess bivariate associations between participant characteristics and BMI categories. Multinomial logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with BMI categories, using normal BMI as the reference category. Crude and adjusted relative risk ratios (RRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated.Results: Of the 385 participants, 17% were underweight, 67% had normal BMI and 16% were overweight/obese. Bivariate analyses showed that BMI categories were associated with age group, marital status, employment status and nutrition knowledge. In adjusted multinomial regression analyses, low nutrition knowledge remained significantly associated with underweight status relative to normal BMI (aRRR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.28–0.95). No significant association was observed between nutrition knowledge and overweight/obese BMI status. Nutrition attitudes and practices were not significantly associated with BMI categories after adjustment for potential confounders.Conclusion: Low nutrition knowledge was independently associated with underweight status among people receiving TB treatment, while no link was found with overweight or obesity. Further research is needed to better understand this relationship.

papers.title: Show your working: ergative assessment for knowledge-building
papers.authors: Andrew Whitworth, Dina Soliman
papers.abstract: Traditional assessment practices in higher education prioritise end-of-course outputs, reducing intellectual work to singular artefacts and obscuring the cognitive efforts that produce them. This conceptual paper explores an alternative, ergative approach, as a framework for assessment in HE that foregrounds discourse and collective knowledge work. Drawing on Bakhtin’s theory of dialogics and Scardamalia and Bereiter’s work on knowledge building, the ergative approach emphasises iterative, situated discourse, in an observation-feedback cycle, incorporating different modalities of information. Its basis is the idea of the ‘professional practicum’ in which learners are performing knowledge-building practice. These performances are reflected upon through feedback provided in multiple forms, scaffolding students as dialogic agents. The ergative approach can be positioned as one response to the proliferation of generative AI, which further challenges the traditional HE assessment paradigm, as students may rely on AI-generated outputs that produce coherent text without engaging in authentic knowledge-building.

papers.title: Relational Role Attribution: A Unifying Construct in Human–AI Interaction
papers.authors: Michael J Gazzanigo, Xiao Yang
papers.abstract: How users come to perceive an AI not merely as capable but as intentionally oriented toward them in a specific relational capacity remains undertheorized. We propose relational role attribution (RRA) as a discrete psychological construct addressing this gap, positioned as a precursor to downstream relational outcomes rather than a reframing of trust. A PRISMA-ScR scoping review charted 1223 reports at full text against a registered protocol, including 466. Of 179 records excluded for establishing no relational or social role for the agent, 122 (68.2%) nonetheless manipulated or measured anthropomorphism: the field reaches the cue and stops short of the attribution. RRA comprises two concurrent components, a relational inference of social orientation and a role assignment drawn from contextual and communicative cues, checked against the expectancy the user brings. Naming the attribution allows findings accumulated separately across marketing, teaming, and communication literatures to constrain one another, and scaffolds role-specific design principles.

papers.title: Enabling temporal transitions: AI adoption and sequential ambidexterity in Chinese SMEs from 2015–2023
papers.authors: Chen Huang, Dawei Li
papers.abstract: With research about sequential ambidexterity suggesting that firms may approximate ambidexterity over time by alternating between periods of exploration and exploitation, this temporal approach provides a feasible solution for SMEs facing resource limitations to manage the tension between exploration and exploitation. However, little is known about what enables SMEs to successfully enact such temporal transitions over time. In this study, we examine whether and when AI adoption facilitates SMEs’ ability to achieve sequential ambidexterity. By analysing longitudinal data from firms listed on the Small and Medium Enterprise Board of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in China from 2015 to 2023 and using text analysis, topic modelling approach, and fixed-effects regressions, the findings demonstrate that AI adoption enables firms to dynamically alternate between periods of exploration and exploitation over time. Furthermore, AI learning capability and AI interaction capability strengthen this positive relationship. Our study provides a rich empirical foundation for future research aimed at understanding the dynamics of AI adoption and its impact on ambidexterity within firms.

papers.title: Cybersecurity Behavior in AI Vibe Coding: Extending Technology Threat Avoidance Theory
papers.authors: Ali Tarhini, Mohammed Abdullah Al-Sharafi, Hidaya Al Lawati, Mousa Albashrawi
papers.abstract: Generative AI has rapidly reshaped software development, fueling “vibe coding,” in which developers increasingly rely on AI-generated code. While offering productivity benefits, this practice raises important cybersecurity concerns. Drawing on Technology Threat Avoidance Theory (TTAT), this study examines developers’ cybersecurity behavior in AI-assisted coding environments. Survey data from 358 participants with recent AI coding-assistant experience were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Security self-efficacy exhibited the largest positive effect on cybersecurity behavior, followed by perceived threat, while trust in AI had a smaller positive effect. AI transparency and perceived risk showed no significant direct effects. Perceived severity and susceptibility positively shaped perceived threat, supporting TTAT’s core threat-appraisal mechanism. The model explained 44.5% of the variance in cybersecurity behavior. PLSpredict provided evidence of out-of-sample predictive performance. The findings clarify TTAT’s applicability and theoretical boundaries in AI-mediated software development and offer practical implications for developers, organizations, and AI tool providers seeking safer AI-assisted coding practices.

papers.title: Distinguishing AI and human work in green digital advertising: authorship disclosure, claim specificity, and greenwashing suspicion
papers.authors: Stefanos Balaskas
papers.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used to create digital advertising, but its effects on perceived sustainability communication remain unclear. This research examines whether AI authorship disclosure increases greenwashing suspicion and whether specific evidence-based claims mitigate this effect. Across three studies using promotional messages for a fictional sustainable delivery service, GreenDrop, we tested authorship disclosure, claim specificity, perceived authenticity, claim diagnosticity, visual attention, and physiological arousal. Study 1 showed that AI-labelled green advertisements elicited higher greenwashing suspicion and lower perceived authenticity than human-labelled advertisements, with a significant indirect association through perceived authenticity. Study 2 showed that specific evidence-based claims reduced greenwashing suspicion, increased claim diagnosticity, and attenuated—but did not eliminate—the AI-disclosure penalty. Study 3 replicated this interaction in a laboratory setting and added eye-tracking and GSR evidence: AI-labelled advertisements increased attention to the authorship label, specific claims altered visual allocation toward claim-related information, and AI-labelled vague claims elicited higher physiological arousal. Overall, AI disclosure operates as a source-attribution cue that can undermine authenticity and heighten greenwashing suspicion, especially when sustainability claims are vague.

papers.title: Teaching on demand: Exploring the role of AI in medical education podcasts
papers.authors: Payal Guha, Oscar L. Oglina, Celia Brown, Courtney Krstić, Chukwuma N. Uduku, Layla Thurston, Risheka Ratnasabapathy, Amir H. Sam
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated educational content holds promise for scalable medical education, but evidence comparing AI and clinician-produced podcasts remains limited. We investigated whether AI-generated podcasts achieve comparable student satisfaction to clinician-recorded podcasts, enabling broader curriculum coverage without overburdening clinical educators, and explored students' attitudes towards AI-generated podcasts. METHODS: Medical students were randomised into two groups, with group 1 receiving clinician-produced podcasts on type 1 diabetes (T1DM) and AI-generated podcasts on type 2 diabetes (T2DM). Group 2 received AI-generated podcasts on T1DM, and clinician-produced podcasts on T2DM. Students were blinded to the podcast types. The outcome measures included students' satisfaction (measured using the Student Satisfaction with Educational Podcasts Questionnaire (SSEQ)) and students' attitudes to AI using an open-ended survey. A Bonferroni correction was applied (α = 0.025). RESULTS: = 165), 56% reported production method mattered, citing the sound of the voice, engagement of speaker, and ethical concerns as major issues with AI podcasts. DISCUSSION: AI-generated podcasts achieved non-inferior satisfaction to clinician-recorded podcasts. However, students' psychological preference for human teaching and negative perceptions of AI pose a barrier to scalable benefits, necessitating efforts to build trust and acceptability.

papers.title: Integrating generative artificial intelligence facilitates faculty interaction network and role transition in a biostatistics curriculum
papers.authors: Yen-Lin Chiu, Tzu-Chin Wu, Hao-Yuan Chang, Chi‐Chuan Wang, Kang‐Yi Su, Cheng‐Heng Liu, Albert C. Yang, Duan‐Rung Chen, Chiun Hsu
papers.abstract: In a two-year action-research study within an undergraduate biostatistics curriculum for nursing, pharmacy, and medical biotechnology students, we examined how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) facilitates educators to design, supervise, and evaluate learning. Students used GenAI first as a technical tutor and then as a partner in knowledge co-creation in case-based statistical problem-solving. Teachers’ reflection records and 4697 LINE messages during the study period were analyzed using qualitative coding, GenAI-assisted semantic analysis, and social network analysis. Teachers’ roles shifted from knowledge transmitters to facilitators of critical inquiry and human–GenAI co-learning. Overall, faculty communication was dense, reciprocal, and decentralized, whereas GenAI-related discourse was more selective and centralized. GenAI-related ties were less likely to form but, once formed, strongly reciprocal and locally clustered. GenAI integration can catalyze new forms of faculty leadership through expertise sharing and collaborative problem-solving. Intentional structures for cross-disciplinary exchange and reflective faculty development are needed.

papers.title: Human-validated LLM-assisted assessment of a large-scale online precision medicine course in diabetes
papers.authors: Lingsong Kong, Adelle Engmann, Chenchen Zhu, Sally L. Baxter, Amit Dixit, Antony Ross, Alireza Delfarah, Lisa Linda Morselli, Delaram Rezaeikhonakdar, Alison Derbenwick Miller, Joseph Yracheta, Ramesh V. Nair, Eva M McGhee, Scott Edmiston, Philip S. Tsao, Arash Alavi, Amir Hassan Bahmani
papers.abstract: Precision medicine increasingly relies on multimodal data and artificial intelligence, creating a need for scalable education and assessment. We developed an online diabetes precision medicine course and conducted an observational single-group pre–post evaluation of knowledge, confidence, and rubric-scored open-ended responses among 435 learners who completed the course. Because manual scoring of open-ended responses is time-consuming and subject to variability and human judgment, we developed a human-validated, large language model (LLM)-assisted scoring workflow. Knowledge, confidence, and open-ended response scores increased by 30.0 percentage points, 1.32 points, and 0.39 points, respectively (all p < 0.001). Across 4350 responses evaluated by the LLM-assisted workflow, only 12 (0.3%) required human review. In a stratified 300-response validation sample, the final LLM consensus score achieved 75.3% exact agreement, 99.3% adjacent agreement, and 0.7% major disagreements (LLM unanimity, 74.0%; human unanimity, 65.7%) with the final human score. Course completion was associated with improvements in knowledge, confidence, and open-ended response scores, while the findings also support human-validated LLM-assisted assessment as a scalable approach for evaluating open-ended responses.

papers.title: Integrating technology anxiety into the TPB-TAM framework to examine AI adoption intention in hospital HRM: a study of Chinese healthcare professionals
papers.authors: Jing Jin, Danxia Chen, Ying Zhou
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can empower healthcare professionals to make data-driven decisions and streamline administrative tasks in hospital human resource management (HRM). However, it is vital to understand their perceptions towards AI for seamless implementation in practice. Therefore, the study aimed to assess the role of technology anxiety within an integrated framework combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to better understand adoption intentions in this high-stakes context. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 547 healthcare professionals working in hospitals across China. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling, including confirmatory factor analysis, path analysis, and bootstrap mediation testing. Multi-group structural equation modeling was also used to compare healthcare professionals with different levels of AI familiarity. The integrated model explained 49.4% of the variance in behavioral intention, and all twelve hypothesized paths were statistically significant. Technology anxiety was negatively associated with perceived ease of use (β = -0.553, p < 0.001), perceived behavioral control (β = -0.371, p < 0.001), attitude (β = -0.339, p < 0.001), and subjective norms (β = -0.451, p < 0.001), and it was also associated with behavioral intention through multiple indirect pathways. Multi-group analysis showed that the association between perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness was stronger among professionals with low AI familiarity, while the remaining paths remained stable across groups. AI adoption intention in hospital HRM appears to involve more than rational evaluations of usefulness and ease of use. Emotional states, such as technology anxiety, also play a role. Reducing technology anxiety and improving ease of use for users with lower AI familiarity are therefore important steps for promoting AI adoption intention. These findings highlight the value of addressing emotional factors alongside cognitive beliefs when introducing AI tools in healthcare organizations.

papers.title: Evaluating the consistency of text readability levels across corpora for English education
papers.authors: Yang Liu
papers.abstract: Text readability assessment is important for natural language processing, educational text adaptation, and learner-oriented content selection. However, readability labels defined in different corpora are often not directly comparable because they are based on corpus-specific grading schemes, annotation criteria, and target learner populations. This lack of comparability limits cross-corpus evaluation, weakens model transferability, and reduces the reliable reuse of existing readability resources. To address this issue, this study formulates cross-corpus readability alignment as a consistency evaluation problem and proposes a model-agnostic framework for analyzing the compatibility of readability levels across heterogeneous corpora. The framework combines cross-corpus readability prediction with three complementary consistency metrics, namely Reverse Jensen–Shannon Divergence (RJSD), Reverse Rank Normalized Sum of Squares (RRNSS), and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG). To instantiate the framework, linguistic features, GloVe-based distributed representations, fused feature settings, and transformer-based contextualized baselines are examined under conventional machine learning, recurrent neural, and transformer-based modeling settings. Experiments on six English educational readability corpora suggest that the proposed framework reveals interpretable cross-corpus consistency patterns across the evaluated corpora and model families. In general, richer feature or representation settings tend to yield more favorable consistency scores than simpler settings, although the magnitude of the advantage varies across corpus pairs and modeling choices. Additional statistical analyses, including metric correlation analysis, repeated-run variability analysis, and selected significance testing, provide further support for the descriptive findings. These results suggest that the framework offers a useful basis for evaluating readability level alignment across corpora and may support exploratory corpus reuse, educational text selection, and cross-dataset readability research.

papers.title: Perceived social support may mediate adiposity outcomes after nutrition and exercise intervention in adolescents with overweight
papers.authors: Tianyu Gao, Zitong Ye, Ying Xiao
papers.abstract: This study evaluated whether an 8-week nutrition and exercise intervention improved adiposity and estimated basal metabolic rate outcomes in adolescents with overweight and explored perceived social support and exercise self-efficacy as psychosocial mediators of outcomes at three-month follow-up. Ninety-four adolescents aged 10–14 years from Guangzhou, China, were randomized 1:1 to the intervention or usual-care control group; 78 participants (39 per group) provided complete data for the analyses reported here. The intervention included supervised aerobic or resistance exercise three times weekly for 30 min per session and a 15-min group nutrition education class once weekly for 8 weeks. Controls received usual-care health advice without scheduled exercise or nutrition sessions. BMI, fat mass, and estimated basal metabolic rate (BMR) were measured by bioelectrical impedance at baseline, 8 weeks, and three-month follow-up. Perceived social support and exercise self-efficacy were evaluated as candidate mediators. ANCOVA-framework linear models and exploratory parallel mediation analyses with 5,000 bootstrap resamples were used. At 8 weeks, the intervention group had lower BMI and fat mass and higher estimated BMR than the control group after adjustment for baseline values and covariates; the reported 95% confidence intervals excluded zero. In the three-month mediation models, perceived social support showed significant specific indirect effects for BMI, fat mass, and estimated BMR. In contrast, no specific indirect effect through exercise self-efficacy was detected because its 95% confidence interval included zero for each outcome. The intervention was associated with favorable adiposity and estimated BMR outcomes, and exploratory mediation analyses identified perceived social support as a potential pathway for maintained outcome differences at three months. Because physical activity and dietary behavior were not measured during follow-up, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that adolescents sustained physical activity or dietary behavior after the program. Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2500110816.

papers.title: Attention with variational autoencoder enabled one-dimensional convolutional memory network for emotion recognition using EEG and speech signals
papers.authors: Nirmal S. Kothari, Sagar A. More, Narendra S. Jadhav
papers.abstract: Abstract Emotion recognition is an emerging task that concentrates on recognizing the person’s diverse emotional states. However, several previous attempts have been made to acknowledge the person’s emotions and effectively classify them with better performance. However, several limitations have occurred during the detection of human emotions, such as high computational power consumption, minimal recognition accuracy, and diverse modality recognition. Therefore, the research proposes the Self-modular Attention with Variational Autoencoder-enabled one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network and Long Short-Term Memory Network (SMAVA-1DCNN-LSTM) that overcomes the previous approach’s limitations and provides robust detection results with minimal computational complexity. In the research, emotions are recognized by internal physiological signals (EEG) and voice tone. During an evaluation, the significant features of speech and EEG signals are extracted through multiple feature extraction mechanisms that boost the classification accuracy and training process by minimizing overfitting problems. Specifically, the Self-modular Attention (SMA) mechanism aids in fusing the modality-specific informative features to concentrate on important parts of the input multimodal data. Experimental results show that the SMAVA-1DCNN-LSTM method demonstrates exceptional performance for emotion recognition, reporting accuracy of 97.70%, F1-score of 97.79%, sensitivity of 97.06%, MCC of 0.954, precision of 98.54%, and specificity of 98.34% for 90% of training with the EAV dataset.

papers.title: Associations of hirsutism and sexual function with mental health–related quality of life in women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
papers.authors: Müjde Canday, Aslıhan Yurtkal, Tural Ismayilov
papers.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly termed polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a complex endocrine-metabolic condition with reproductive and psychosocial consequences. Hirsutism is among its most visible and distressing manifestations, yet the relationship among hirsutism, sexual function, and mental health–related quality of life (HRQoL) remains incompletely understood. This single-center cross-sectional study included 118 women aged 18–45 years with a newly identified diagnosis of PMOS at a tertiary gynecology outpatient clinic. Written informed consent was obtained before data collection, and all questionnaires were completed before participants were informed of the diagnosis. The SF-36 Mental Health (MH) domain was the prespecified primary outcome. Sexual function (FSFI), depressive symptoms (BDI), anxiety symptoms (BAI), and clinical and psychosocial covariates were assessed. Multivariable linear regression with robust standard errors was used. The FSFI-inclusive analysis was restricted to participants with evaluable FSFI data and was considered secondary and exploratory. The mean age was 24.01 ± 5.25 years, and the median BMI was 26.0 kg/m2 (IQR 21.5–29.9). Hirsutism was present in 61.0% of participants. In the primary model (n = 118), hirsutism was associated with a 7.21-point lower SF-36 MH score (95% CI − 13.01 to − 1.42; p = 0.015). Evaluable FSFI data were available for 88 participants. In this subgroup, higher FSFI total score was associated with higher MH score (β = 0.57; 95% CI 0.15 to 0.99; p = 0.008). Because the models were fitted in different analytic samples and the study was cross-sectional, the observed change in the hirsutism coefficient after FSFI inclusion cannot establish mediation or temporal direction. Hirsutism and sexual function were associated with mental health–related HRQoL in women with newly identified PMOS. These findings highlight sexual health as a clinically relevant assessment domain but require confirmation in larger, longitudinal, multicenter studies.

papers.title: Distilling First-Principles Accuracy into Compact Machine Learning Potentials for Condensed-Phase Chemistry
papers.authors: Sijia Chen, Niamh O'Neill, Benjamin X. Shi, Venkat Kapil
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have made first-principles-quality potential energy surfaces increasingly accessible for condensed-phase chemistry, but their inference cost can still limit the sampling needed to compute experimentally relevant observables. In this work, we use knowledge distillation to construct compact “student” models that retain the accuracy of much larger “teacher” models obtained through either finetuning of foundation models or Δ-learning. The resulting students reduce production simulation cost by approximately an order of magnitude, making high-accuracy sampling practical for challenging condensed-phase problems. We demonstrate this across three problems of increasing sampling complexity: finite-temperature NPT simulations of ice Ih, classical and path-integral simulations of liquid water over 240–370 K, and path-integral umbrella-sampling simulations of water dissociation at the anatase TiO2(101)/water interface. When compared, the distilled students reproduce the target observables of their teachers more reliably than equally compact models trained only on the available reference data. The liquid water student, distilled from a Δ-learned CCSD(T)-quality teacher, reproduces thermodynamic, structural, transport, and nuclear quantum effects over the full temperature range studied. At the TiO2/water interface, knowledge distillation makes PIMD umbrella sampling practical and shows that nuclear quantum effects lower the dissociation barrier by approximately 2 kcal/mol and shift the molecular–dissociated free energy difference into closer agreement with recent solid-state 17O NMR measurements. Our work demonstrates how knowledge distillation can make accurate MLIPs practical for the sampling methods needed to connect condensed-phase reaction thermodynamics with experiment, notably for interfacial chemistry and catalysis.

papers.title: The future of game-based logistics: a systematic review of applications, functions, and evidence
papers.authors: Seyed Sina Mohri, Russell George Thompson, Lele Zhang, Michael Kirley
papers.journal: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
papers.abstract: Game-based approaches are increasingly employed to address complex challenges in logistics and freight transport. While traditionally employed for education and workforce training, they have broader applications and untapped potential. In particular, advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are creating new opportunities to design, personalise, and scale these interventions. Despite this growing interest, a comprehensive understanding of how game-based approaches have evolved, who they target, what functions they serve, and where future opportunities lie remains limited. This study presents a systematic review of 87 studies on game-based interventions in freight transport and logistics, synthesising evidence across five application domains: warehouse operations management, terminal operations management, transport planning and optimisation, reverse logistics, and risk management and resilience. The findings reveal that games are evolving beyond training applications towards behavioural research, decision support, stakeholder engagement, and consumer behaviour change. Target audiences have similarly expanded from students and operational personnel to include managers, planners, consumers, and participants in behavioural research settings. Nevertheless, evidence regarding the long-term effectiveness of these interventions remains scarce, and several logistics challenges remain largely unexplored. Building on evidence-based gaps identified in the literature, this review proposes future research directions and highlights the potential of AI to enable adaptive, personalised, and scalable game-based interventions. By consolidating fragmented knowledge and outlining emerging opportunities, this study provides a foundation for researchers and practitioners seeking to harness game-based approaches to understand and improve logistics and freight transport systems.

papers.title: Sustainability-oriented tourism ecosystems and island resilience: evidence from Thailand and South Korea
papers.authors: Jakkawat Laphet, Waraphon Klinsreesuk, Duangrat Tandamrong, Somnuk Aujirapongpan
papers.abstract: This study investigates how Open Innovation Orientation contributes to adaptive island resilience through Renewable Energy Tourism Attractiveness, Green Innovation Capability, and Tourism Co-Creation Ecosystem in Koh Larn Island, Thailand, and Jeju Island, South Korea. A quantitative research design was employed using questionnaire surveys collected from 500 tourists, and the data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), including measurement invariance assessment, multi-group analysis (MGA), and out-of-sample predictive assessment. The findings indicate that Open Innovation Orientation is positively associated with both Renewable Energy Tourism Attractiveness and Green Innovation Capability. Renewable Energy Tourism Attractiveness is positively associated with Green Innovation Capability and Tourism Co-Creation Ecosystem, while Green Innovation Capability is positively associated with Tourism Co-Creation Ecosystem. Most importantly, Tourism Co-Creation Ecosystem demonstrates the strongest positive relationship with Adaptive Island Resilience. The MGA results indicate that the structural relationships are generally consistent across Koh Larn Island and Jeju Island, with no statistically significant differences identified between the two groups. The predictive assessment further indicates satisfactory out-of-sample predictive capability of the proposed model. This study contributes to sustainable tourism literature by integrating open innovation, renewable energy tourism, green innovation, tourism co-creation, and adaptive resilience into a unified sustainability-oriented framework for island tourism development.

papers.title: Infrastructure-based autonomous mobile robots for internal logistics — challenges and future perspectives
papers.authors: Erik Brorsson, Kristian Ceder, Ze Zhang, Sabino Francesco Roselli, Endre Erős, Martin Dahl, Beatrice Alenljung, Jessica Lindblom, Thanh Bui, Atieh Hanna, Emmanuel Dean, Lennart Svensson, Kristofer Bengtsson, Per-Lage Götvall, Knut Åkesson
papers.abstract: The adoption of Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) for internal logistics is accelerating, with most solutions emphasizing decentralized, onboard intelligence. While AMRs in indoor environments like factories can be supported by infrastructure, involving external sensors and computational resources, such systems remain underexplored in the literature. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of infrastructure-based AMR systems, outlining key opportunities and challenges. To support this, we introduce a reference architecture combining infrastructure-based sensing, on-premise cloud computing, and onboard autonomy. Based on the architecture, we review core technologies for localization, perception, and planning. We demonstrate the approach in a real-world deployment in a heavy-vehicle manufacturing environment and summarize findings from a user experience (UX) evaluation. Our aim is to provide a holistic foundation for future development of scalable, robust, and human-compatible AMR systems in complex industrial environments.

papers.title: The integration of artificial intelligence in family nurse practitioner education
papers.authors: Melissa LeBrun, Andrea Martin

papers.title: Lateralized amyloid PET uptake and beta-band connectivity in relation to cognition in temporal lobe epilepsy
papers.authors: Jooheon Kong, Hyun Joo Kim, Mingyeong So, 이인영, Hayom Kim, Young-Tak Kim, Hyun-Ji Kim, Synho Do, Dong-Kwon Lim, Jae-Ho Han, Sung Hoon Kang, Kisoo Pahk, Jung Bin Kim
papers.abstract: We examined focus-relative amyloid PET asymmetry and its associations with resting-state EEG connectivity and processing speed in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE). Thirty adults with clinically assigned MTLE (19 right-focus, 11 left-focus) underwent 18 F-florapronol PET and resting-state EEG. Regional standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) and sensor-level weighted phase lag index (wPLI) were evaluated using paired comparisons, rank correlations and exploratory bootstrap indirect-association models. Cognitive data were available for 26 participants, including Digit Symbol Coding (DSC) for 25. Under the original analytical convention, mean medial temporal SUVR was 1.066 ipsilaterally and 1.013 contralaterally (difference 0.053, 95% CI [0.013, 0.093]; p = 0.011; Cohen’s d z = 0.500). The contrast differed by focus side (interaction p = 0.002) and was 0.038 under source-table reconstruction ( p = 0.075). Ipsilateral SUVR correlated with inter-hemispheric beta wPLI ( ρ = 0.617, q = 0.034 across 240 tests). The intra-contralateral association ( ρ = 0.536) did not survive this broader correction. Indirect estimates for Trail Making Test A (0.279, 95% bootstrap CI [0.043, 0.761]) and DSC (0.151, 95% bootstrap CI [−0.114, 0.476]) did not survive correction across 136 models. Regional medial temporal PET uptake was associated with beta-band scalp connectivity in this small cohort, while focus-side heterogeneity and labeling sensitivity limit a uniform ipsilateral interpretation. Processing-speed indirect associations were exploratory and did not establish compensation or causality. Replication with structural correction, longer EEG sampling and longitudinal cognitive follow-up is required.

papers.title: Architecture-agnostic knowledge distillation for machine-learning interatomic potentials
papers.authors: Chen Wang, Siyu Hu, Guangming Tan, Weile Jia
papers.abstract: Atomistic foundation models can achieve near-ab-initio accuracy and strong transferability across molecular and materials systems, but their large parameter counts lead to high inference latency and memory cost, limiting long-time-scale molecular dynamics and resource-constrained deployment. In many practical studies, only a narrow chemical subdomain is required, motivating compact students that preserve the teacher's physical priors. Existing distillation for Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) is still limited by architecture mismatch or incomplete geometric supervision. We propose an architecture-agnostic framework, Joint Atomic Energy-Energy Hessian Distillation, that requires no architecture-specific feature projection. The method combines atomic-energy alignment, which transfers local decomposition priors, with Hessian alignment, which transfers local curvature of the potential energy surface. These two signals are complementary and jointly regularize both decomposition consistency and geometric stability. Under matched training settings, our method consistently improves energy accuracy over a strong Hessian-distillation baseline (average gain: 48.3% on SPICE and 6.7% on MPtrj) while preserving force accuracy. Across teacher-student pairs, it also reduces parameter counts by 79%-98%, enabling fast and deployment-friendly specialized MLIPs for targeted chemical subdomains.

papers.title: Achievement goal theory in AI-supported learning: Psychological pathways and configurations leading to student engagement
papers.authors: Jing Li, Pengju Caoyan Li
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, yet little is known about how students’ achievement goal orientations are associated with their engagement in AI-supported learning. Grounded in Achievement Goal Theory, this study examined the relationships among mastery-approach, mastery-avoidance, performance-approach, and performance-avoidance goals, enjoyment, flow, and student engagement. Survey data were collected from 662 Chinese university students with experience in AI-supported learning. Structural equation modeling was employed to examine psychological pathways, while fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis was used to identify alternative configurations associated with high engagement. The results showed that both mastery goals were positively associated with enjoyment and flow, whereas both performance goals were associated with flow but not enjoyment. Enjoyment mediated the relationships between mastery goals and engagement, while flow mediated the relationships between all four goal orientations and engagement. The configurational analysis further identified multiple sufficient pathways to high engagement, with no single condition being necessary. These findings extend Achievement Goal Theory by revealing differentiated affective and immersive mechanisms and multiple motivational configurations underlying student engagement in AI-supported higher education.

papers.title: A nurse-guided ChatGPT-assisted dietary learning program and self-efficacy for avoiding high-phosphorus foods in peritoneal dialysis patients
papers.authors: Hui-Chih Wang, Hengky Arviano, Tianxiao Wang, Ying-Wen Chi, Yu-Juei Hsu, Chih‐Chien Sung, Hsing-Lin Peng, Su Pei-Chen, Her‐Sen Doong, Yu-Hsi Huang

papers.title: A patent-driven SCOR-IFCM framework to prioritize generative AI adoption for supply chain resilience
papers.authors: Ju Chunhua, Ke Li, Chonghuan Xu, Hongli Liu

papers.title: Affective directions in activation space: An interpretable inference-time control mechanism
papers.authors: Yurui Dong, Luozhijie Jin, Yao Yang, Bingjie Lu, Jiaxi Yang, Zhi Liu
papers.abstract: Emotion is a fundamental component of human communication, shaping understanding, trust, and engagement across domains such as education, healthcare, and mental health. Although large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong reasoning and knowledge-generation capabilities, they still struggle to express emotions in a consistent, controllable, and contextually appropriate manner. This limitation restricts their potential for authentic human–AI interaction. We propose a controllable emotion generation framework based on Emotion Vectors (EVs) —latent representations derived from internal activation shifts between neutral and emotion-conditioned responses. By injecting these vectors into the hidden states of pretrained LLMs during inference, our method enables fine-grained, continuous modulation of emotional tone without any additional training or architectural modification. We further provide a first-order theoretical analysis of emotional steering and its interaction with a semantic readout under explicit local assumptions. Experiments across multiple LLM families demonstrate adjustable emotional expression and characterize the model-dependent trade-off between steering strength, topical relevance, and fluency. The framework provides a general, training-free control interface with explicit intensity scaling and vector composition. Comparisons with prompting and fine-tuning characterize the emotional and quality effects of the evaluated configurations. Emotion Vector (EV) steering thus offers an efficient and interpretable means of bridging rational reasoning and affective understanding in large language models, and points to a promising direction for building emotionally resonant AI systems capable of more natural human–machine interaction.

papers.title: Realising the potential of ecological digital twins as decision support tools
papers.authors: Anna M. Davison, Koen de Koning
papers.abstract: Ecological digital twins are continually updating models used for decision-making. Current progress in ecological digital twinning has focused on overcoming the technological and modelling challenges to create a continually updating system. We argue that attention should now also focus on effectively integrating digital twins into decision-making systems to inform timely action. This requires the direct inclusion of end users and greater focus on the socio-political context. We outline challenges faced in developing such ‘translational’ digital twins from our own experience and translate recommendations for best practice from the transdisciplinary research literature. We champion co-creation as a powerful approach for future translational digital twin projects, especially in larger and more complex research teams.

papers.title: How trust shapes human reliance on AI decision support in healthcare: A simulation-based behavioral study
papers.authors: Han Qing
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) based decision support systems are increasingly used in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, making it important to understand how trust relates to the use of AI recommendations. Although trust can support effective human–AI collaboration, miscalibrated trust may contribute to inappropriate recommendation acceptance and reduced decision performance. This study examined associations among perceived AI performance, trust, AI recommendation acceptance, and decision accuracy under different levels of AI reliability. In a simulation-based experiment, 100 medical students completed clinical decision-making tasks with AI assistance under high- and low-reliability conditions. Perceived AI performance and trust were measured after each block, while recommendation acceptance and decision accuracy were recorded at the trial level. Mixed-effects models showed that perceived AI performance was positively associated with trust. Higher trust was associated with greater overall acceptance of AI recommendations and greater acceptance of incorrect recommendations. Conversely, higher trust was associated with lower odds of rejecting correct recommendations, indicating more frequent rejection at lower trust. Greater misalignment between normalized trust and objective AI reliability was associated with lower decision accuracy. These findings indicate that calibrated trust is important for effective AI-assisted decision making. They also support the development and evaluation of AI interfaces that communicate reliability and uncertainty to help users align trust with system capability.

papers.title: Informing users about LLMs' environmental costs encourages ethical consumption
papers.authors: Hagai Rabinovitch, Isabel Kashi, Shaul Shalvi
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming deeply embedded in everyday human-AI interaction. However, the environmental costs associated with using those tools remain elusive. Here, we address the question of whether providing users with information about the environmental costs of using LLMs tempers their use. Such information highlights an ethical tension: acting pro-environmentally requires people to forgo some of the benefits AI tools provide. We study how people solve this trade-off in tasks that are relatively easy to tackle without using LLMs and further assess if the impact of providing such information has a stronger effect on people who have stronger environmental concerns. In two preregistered experiments (total N = 1,200), we studied participants’ use of ChatGPT in a text-editing task after they learned about the tool’s environmental costs. Results revealed that (i) raising awareness of ChatGPT’s environmental costs reduced its use and usage volume; (ii) interacting with a sycophantic model, one that encourages continuous use, did not attenuate the awareness effect, although it led to greater overall use; and (iii) raising awareness was especially effective among people with high environmental concerns. The findings highlight how raising awareness concerning LLM’s environmental costs can encourage responsible consumption.

papers.title: Comparing corpus-based and GenAI-based tools: The analysis of specialised discourse using Sketch Engine and ChatGPT-5.1
papers.authors: Filip Kalaš
papers.abstract: This study examines the performance of Sketch Engine and ChatGPT-5.1 in identifying specialised lexical phenomena within a medical subcorpus of the MuchMore Springer Bilingual Corpus. It examines three analytically distinct layers of specialised discourse – multiword terms, adjectival collocates, and four-word lexical bundles – to assess how corpus-driven and generative approaches capture terminological, collocational, and formulaic patterns in anaesthesiology. Results show substantial convergence, particularly in lexical bundles, where 84% of units overlapped and ranked similarly. Term extraction and collocation analysis also revealed a stable conceptual core shared by both tools, while divergences reflected either corpus-specific distribution (Sketch Engine) or conceptual salience (ChatGPT-5.1). The findings suggest that the complementary use of corpus tools and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may offer potential applications for terminology-oriented teaching contexts, such as seminars in corpus linguistics or terminology studies, where students can critically compare corpus-based evidence with model-generated linguistic interpretations.

papers.title: Identifying brain-computer interface translational priorities with an outlook on the field in 2035
papers.authors: Ning Jiang, Jiayuan He, Lin Yao, 隋晓红
papers.abstract: Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) have advanced rapidly, particularly over the past few decades, evolving from experimental demonstrations to powerful research tools and early-stage clinical technologies. Invasive, semi-invasive, and non-invasive modalities now enable neural decoding, neuromodulation, and functional restoration across diverse neurological conditions. Yet, despite striking laboratory demonstrations and growing investment, few BCIs have become viable medical products, having only a limited impact. Here, we provide a quantitative analysis to identify crucial clinical applications on which BCI translational efforts should focus to achieve substantial clinical, societal, and economic impact. Using an urgency–importance–impact framework based on disability-adjusted life years analysis, we assessed 12 neurological conditions to provide insight into how to prioritize strategic BCI development efforts. Alzheimer’s disease, stroke, depression, and anxiety, with their combined high urgency, importance, and impact, emerge as strategic targets with the greatest societal and economic stakes. We further argue that BCIs today, particularly invasive modalities, function primarily as transformative scientific instruments, analogous to the astronomic telescope in the era preceding classical mechanics, and will shape future theoretical and clinical innovation. Realizing a sustainable BCI industry beyond 2035 will require aligning basic neuroscience, artificial intelligence-driven advances, scalable clinical validation, ethical safeguards, and coordinated strategic planning.

papers.title: Framing an epistemic collaboration between chat GPT’s peripheral instrumentality and the author’s optimal anthropocentrism for enhancing non-native-English-speaking researchers’ scientific writing
papers.authors: Md. Saiful Alam, Adelina Asmawi, Mohammad Hamidul Haque, Sayeda Fatema, Md. Mohib Ullah, Md. Nurullah Patwary, Tasmiah Fatema, Humayra Akhter
papers.abstract: Apparently, English is the dominant language for scientific writing. Globally, non-native English-speaking researchers (N-NESRs) often experience being viewed as having deficiencies in the quality of the English language of their scientific papers. Given this, N-NESRs often experience delays, difficulties, and even financial burdens when it comes to publishing their research papers in English-only journals. As a digital means for addressing this challenge, this study examines the praxis of alternative capacity building for N-NESRs by unfolding the potential of GenAI-human author partnership for scientific writing. To this end, qualitative data from the authors’ anecdotal pieces of evidence were collected. Dual methods of digital data mining (DDM) and educational data mining (EDM) were used to analyze the data. The findings reveal that Chat GPT has a unique potential for providing digital instrumentation in an epistemic collaboration with N-NESRs. It can enhance the language quality of N-NESRs’ research papers by aligning them with the tone, voice, and conventions of scientific writing. This instrumentation may result in the publications of N-NESRs’ scientific writing in high-profile English journals. The findings also reveal that the nature of Chat GPT’s participation in the GenAI-mediated scientific writing is peripheral, non-authorial and without ethical violation. Therefore, N-NESRs can retain optimal authorial anthropocentricity in their epistemic productions. Thus, the study embodies the pragmatization of N-NESRs’ problems, the potential of GenAI in scientific writing, and the pursuit of equity, access, and linguistic empowerment of N-NESRs. These findings are significant for N-NESRs, writing pedagogues, policy makers and writing researchers.

papers.title: Exploring learning in classic African board games: a review of recent literature
papers.authors: Rebecca Yvonne Bayeck
papers.abstract: Abstract A growing body of research on board games demonstrates that these games can function as learning environments and provide opportunities for learning across diverse contexts. Although learning is often conceptualized contextually within this literature, studies increasingly demonstrate that meaningful learning can occur through participation in board game environments. However, the relationship between board games and learning has been examined predominantly through the study of modern board games, with comparatively limited attention given to classic African board games. This literature review explores learning in classic African board games. This study serves two purposes as it highlights the state of research on classic African board games and the relationship of these games with learning. The fi ndings show that classic African board games are spaces where learning occurs and players engage in a constellation of literacies. The studies analyzed indicate that playing these games can facilitate mathematical learning, engage players in computational thinking and songoputation, and foster the development of skills related to science, engineering, and technology (i.e. STEM). These board games also allow for the exploration of artificial intelligence (AI), which results in the learning of new AI techniques. Classic African board games have the potential to simplify the learning of various subjects and the acquisition of skills relevant to the 21st century. As such, more empirical studies should be conducted to further investigate the connection between playing thesegames, their game mechanics and learning; and particularly the link between their gameplay and the learning of specific subjects such as mathematics, science, and engineering.

papers.title: Vibe Coding: An experiment with test-driven development
papers.authors: Moritz Mock, Barbara Russo
papers.abstract: Abstract Context Conversational Large Language Models (CLLMs) can automatically generate code by collaborating with users through natural language. However, poor collaboration can lead to poor quality output. Objective This exploratory study aims to investigate how humans and CLLMs can collaborate as peers through vibe coding, an approach that integrates principles from prompt engineering, agile design, and human-AI co-creation to enhance collaboration. Method We designed four interaction models representing different collaboration patterns in the software development process: the solo model (human-only development), the collaborative model (human–CLLM collaboration), the fully automated model (development autonomously performed by a CLLM), and the agentic model (development autonomously performed by the MetaGPT X platform). Based on these models, we implemented corresponding Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflows using structured prompts and Python scripts. We then conducted a controlled pre-experimental study with TDD professionals to compare the solo and collaborative workflows. In addition, we performed repeated exploratory executions of fully automated and agentic workflows on the same development tasks to obtain complementary evidence. Results Our findings suggest that the choice of interaction model should depend on the development objective. Agentic workflows are best suited for rapid development and functionally correct production code but may introduce additional implementation complexity. However, they may also introduce additional implementation decisions that are not explicitly required by the functional specifications, resulting in untested decision points. In contrast, collaborative workflows produce higher-quality, better-organized test suites. Conclusions Our work explored how humans can collaborate with CLLMs in generating code in highly intensive and demanding development process. Our results also show that accurately reproducing development process workflows is yet an open problem, also in the new agentic technologies.
