papers.title: Geometric Template for Preoperative Breast Marking: An Innovative Tool Based on Harmonic Proportions
papers.authors: Leandro Debs, Gabriel de Almeida Arruda Felix, Miguel Sabino Neto
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast symmetry and harmony remain challenging goals in aesthetic breast surgery. Preoperative marking is fundamental for planning; however, most techniques rely on nipple-areola complex (NAC) distances and subjective visual assessment, often neglecting thoracic width, height, and the true breast footprint. A geometric framework based on harmonic proportions can help standardize preoperative planning and may improve the reproducibility of breast markings. METHODS: A two-dimensional geometric template was developed by integrating constant anatomical references (sternum, clavicles, axillary and acromial lines, and umbilicus) with proportional relationships derived from aesthetic and anthropometric studies. The template was calibrated for each patient's using thoracic width and height and was designed to be superimposed on standardized frontal photographs. It guides the NAC position, breast width, upper pole contour, and inframammary fold level. The model was applied in mastopexy and reduction mammaplasty as a preoperative planning and postoperative photographic overlay comparison, as well as a visual aid in resident teaching sessions. RESULTS: The template was easily incorporated into daily practice using standard clinical photographs and simple digital overlays. Geometric gridlines and proportional curves allowed visualization of the NAC position, breast symmetry, and contour in relation to thoracic dimensions. Repeated overlays facilitated the longitudinal comparison of breast position and shape. During teaching sessions, the template was used as a visual aid to facilitate resident understanding of the geometric relationships between thoracic anatomy, the breast footprint, and marking decisions. CONCLUSIONS: This innovative geometric template offers a simple, visually intuitive tool for standardizing preoperative marking and supporting postoperative photographic overlay comparisons in breast surgeries. It is inexpensive, compatible with existing photographic workflows, and may support training and future digital or artificial intelligence integration. Prospective studies are needed to quantify the impact of these factors on aesthetic outcomes and learning curves. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE V: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

papers.title: Color‐Bar Bedsheet: Affordable Assistive Tool for Dix‐Hallpike Test in Primary Care
papers.authors: Suwicha Kaewsiri Isaradisaikul, Pitchayanan Namung, Sanathorn Chowsilpa
papers.journal: Journal of General and Family Medicine
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is a common cause of vertigo encountered in general practice. The definitive diagnosis relies on the Dix‐Hallpike test (DHT), which remains underperformed in primary care due to limited training and unfamiliarity among general practitioners. Aim To develop the color‐bar bedsheet as a simple visual positioning guide for DHT and demonstrate its usefulness. Design and Setting After the color‐bar bedsheet was developed, a prospective within‐subject comparative design in healthy participants was conducted. Methods Healthy adult subjects with 141–190 cm height were recruited. Each examiner performed the DHT with and without bedsheet. The proportion of the appropriate position and the satisfaction of subjects and examiners were compared. Results Sixty subjects and 12 examiners were enrolled. Subjects' average age was 37.8 ± 15.0 years and average BMI was 22.5 ± 3.6 kg/m 2 . The DHT with the bedsheet showed significantly better appropriate positions when compared to the group without using the bedsheet (65% vs. 18.33%, p < 0.001), with the odds ratios (OR) of 8.27. Also, there was significantly higher satisfaction of subjects and examiners in DHT with the bedsheet, compared to DHT without the bedsheet ( p < 0.001). Conclusions The DHT with the color‐bar bedsheet provided an 8 times higher chance of appropriate position (particularly in individuals under 170 cm in height) with better satisfaction of both examiners and subjects. The bedsheet could be used as an assistive tool for the DHT, especially for novice examiners, in order to increase the diagnostic yield of BPPV in primary care settings.

papers.title: Ethical Generative AI Use in Higher Education: An Action Research Study Using the Think Aloud Method
papers.authors: Suha Karaki, Sandra Baroudi
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background As generative AI becomes increasingly embedded in higher education, it presents significant challenges related to ethical use, academic integrity and students' potential over‐reliance on AI‐generated outputs. The Think Aloud method offers a pedagogical approach for making students' reasoning visible as they interact with generative AI tools. Objective This mixed‐methods action research study explored the role of the Think Aloud method as a pedagogical intervention in supporting students' metacognitive awareness and ethical engagement with generative AI tools in a first‐year entrepreneurship course. Method Data were collected through reflective journals, classroom observations and a post‐intervention survey. The study involved 44 first‐year undergraduate students, with 38 students completing the post‐intervention survey. Qualitative data were analysed thematically, while survey responses were examined using descriptive statistics and an exploratory correlation analysis. Results and Conclusions Findings suggested that Think Aloud supported students' emerging awareness of prompt construction, verification practices and ethical decision‐making when using generative AI. However, students' critical evaluation of AI‐generated content often remained at a surface level, particularly among students requiring additional support. The study indicates that Think Aloud can make students' AI‐related reasoning more visible and can support more intentional engagement with generative AI, but it should not be viewed as a stand‐alone solution. Rather, it appears most effective when embedded within a broader pedagogical framework that includes AI literacy, prompt engineering, verification strategies and evaluative judgement. The study contributes classroom‐based evidence on process‐oriented approaches to ethical generative AI use in higher education and highlights the need for sustained instructional scaffolding to support deeper critical engagement with AI tools.

papers.title: Retrieval‐Augmented Lesson Generation With Large Language Models for Scenario‐Based Tutor Training
papers.authors: Jionghao Lin, Sandy Yiyang Zhao, Ashish Gurung, xianghui meng, Kenneth R. Koedinger
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background High‐impact tutoring can improve student learning, but scaling tutoring programmes requires large numbers of novice tutors. Developing high‐quality tutor‐training lessons remains a key bottleneck. Objectives This study compared post‐test performance after participants studied human‐created or LLM‐created tutor‐training materials and examined whether immediate explanatory feedback moderated differences by lesson creation source (human‐created vs. LLM‐created). Methods We conducted a randomized eight‐condition between‐subjects experiment. Participants completed a source‐matched pre‐instruction practice assessment, studied a tutor‐training lesson created by the same source, and then completed two fixed‐order post‐lesson assessments. The design compared lesson creation source, manipulated immediate explanatory feedback and counterbalanced the pre‐instruction scenario form. Post‐test performance was the mean proportion correct across the human‐created and LLM‐created post‐lesson assessments. Results and Conclusions Average post‐test performance was higher after the human‐created lesson than after the LLM‐created lesson, but this difference depended on feedback. The human‐created advantage appeared in the no‐feedback condition, whereas no statistically reliable lesson creation source difference was detected when feedback was provided. Feedback had no statistically significant overall main effect. The human‐created lesson condition performed better on the human‐created post‐lesson assessment, while the LLM‐created post‐lesson assessment showed a small descriptive difference favouring the LLM‐created lesson condition. Because pre‐instruction performance differed by lesson creation source and scenario form, and because assessment source was confounded with fixed assessment order, the results do not isolate pure learning gains or establish a general transfer advantage.

papers.title: Digital Inclusion in Corporate ESG Communication: A Text‐Mining Analysis of Global AI Companies
papers.authors: Jung Hyun Kim, Hyunjee Hannah Kim, Sang Joon Kim
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT As digital platforms increasingly mediate nearly all human activities, artificial intelligence (AI) exhibits dual potential: It can enhance digital inclusion or intensify the exclusion and inequality faced by digitally vulnerable populations. This study examines digital inclusion and accessibility in the ESG reports of eight AI technology companies representing diverse business models. By applying a text‐mining method to analyze reports from these eight companies covering 2019–2024, we found that ESG disclosures are dominated by environmental topics. The coverage of digital inclusion and accessibility increased alongside major regulatory developments, suggesting a temporal alignment between disclosure practices and the evolving regulatory environment. Moreover, a comparative analysis with the WBA Digital Inclusion Score revealed selective disclosure and divergences between disclosure emphasis and external benchmark assessments across business models. This study recommends institutionalizing digital inclusion and accessibility as measurable ESG metrics to support practical assessment and industry‐level governance.

papers.title: Urolithin A and Endothelial and Cerebrovascular Function in Middle-Aged Adults With Obesity
papers.authors: Ana Clara da C. Pinaffi‐Langley, Rafał Gulej, Zalan Kaposzta, Zsofia Szarvas, Ali Shahriari, Henry Kinnard, Bryan Ticer, Camila Bonin Pinto, Péter Mukli, Mihaly Muranyi, Cheryl Adams, Jeng Kong, Leah Anderson, Stefano Tarantini, Yan Daniel Zhao, Norman G. Hord, Andriy Yabluchanskiy
papers.abstract: Importance: Midlife obesity affects nearly half of US adults and is a major risk factor for chronic diseases. Mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to obesity-related endothelial dysfunction and disease risk, highlighting the mitochondria as a potential intervention target. Urolithin A (UA), a polyphenol-derived microbial metabolite and mitophagy activator, is safe and benefits mitochondrial health in humans. Objective: To investigate whether supplementation with UA improved peripheral endothelial and cerebrovascular function in middle-aged adults with obesity. Design, Setting, and Participants: This was a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial conducted at a single site (University of Oklahoma Health Campus) from October 2023 to May 2025. Middle-aged adults (40-64 years) with a body mass index of 30 or greater were eligible to enroll. Intervention: Enrolled participants were randomized 1:1 to receive 1000 mg of UA or placebo for 4 weeks. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was change in brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD) from baseline to end point comparing control and active groups. Secondary outcomes included complementary peripheral endothelial function measures (reactive hyperemia-induced perfusion fold change and acute reperfusion in the dorsal hand and reactive hyperemia index in the fingertips) and cerebrovascular function measures (task-evoked cerebrovascular hemodynamic responses and task performance). Primary analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. Results: Overall, 50 participants were included (25 active and 25 control); mean (SD) age was 50.7 (7.1) years, mean (SD) BMI was 38.3 (7.0), and 37 (74%) were female. Mean (SD) follow-up duration was 28 (2) days. Seven participants were lost to follow-up (14% dropout rate). Change in mean (SD) FMD did not differ significantly based on group allocation (control: 0.3% [5.1%]; active: 1.3% [7.6%]). Similarly, there was no significant treatment effect on secondary peripheral endothelial function outcomes. T-contrast maps showed significantly greater task-evoked hemodynamic responses after supplementation with UA relative to placebo (control: mean [SD] β coefficient, -1.43 [5.26]; active: mean [SD] β coefficient, 15.53 [13.02]), while task performance remained unchanged. Conclusions and Relevance: In this randomized clinical trial of 50 participants, 4 weeks of UA supplementation did not significantly improve peripheral endothelial function in middle-aged adults with obesity. However, supplementation was well tolerated and feasible, and its effect on task-evoked cerebrovascular hemodynamic responses warrants further investigation. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05921266.

papers.title: Understanding the role of generative artificial intelligence in mental health support: Survey of user experiences, engagement patterns, and perceived risks and benefits
papers.authors: Cleo Anderson, Olivia Marie Soliman, Claudia Liu, Zoe McClure, Jake Linardon, Mariel Messer
papers.abstract: Generative AI – especially ChatGPT – is increasingly used for mental health purposes, but users’ subjective experiences of these tools remain unclear. We characterized how individuals utilize ChatGPT for mental health support through a web-based survey completed by 308 adults (Mage=31.5, SD=5.3; 54% men) who reported prior use of this tool. Around half reported use of ChatGPT for mental health support more than once a week, 80% have used it for more than 3 months, and a third reported increased use over time. Depression (55%), anxiety (74%), stress (66%), and relationship conflict (49%) were the problems most frequently discussed with ChatGPT, with the severity of these problems typically rated as mildly or moderately severe. Endorsed reasons for use were its on-demand availability (71%), free cost (69%), and anonymous nature (54%), while common functions the platform served included obtaining advice (71%), providing a safe space for expression (63%), and to learn coping strategies (61%). Experiences were largely positive, with 8 in 10 agreeing that ChatGPT helped them feel understood, better process their emotions, and improve their mental health literacy. Concerns were also evident, with around half expressing worry about data privacy, and a quarter feeling overly reliant on the platform and reducing their motivation to seek help. Few indicated that ChatGPT had replaced professional help (7%) or discouraged help-seeking (12%). Findings shed light on how users are engaging with generative AI for mental health support and highlight the importance of rigorous research designed to evaluate its safety and long-term efficacy.

papers.title: A Risk-Formulation Framework and Candidate Screening Items for Dangerous Use of Large Language Models in Clinical Psychiatry
papers.authors: Eren M. Veziroglu, Punit Matta, Armando N. Braz, Joshuah Muthee, Daniel Price
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) and related conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems have moved rapidly from novelty into ordinary use across education, work, social life, and mental-health-related help seeking. Members of the public now use these systems for advice, companionship, self-disclosure, emotional support, psychoeducation, and quasi-therapeutic interactions. Existing instruments assess problematic or dependent AI use, but they do not ask whether AI has entered a pathway toward serious harm by entrenching ideation, operationalizing capability, displacing human support, or amplifying harmful conduct. To our knowledge, no brief, clinically oriented psychiatric screener has yet been developed and validated specifically for this purpose. We define dangerous AI use as generative AI use that appears to increase the likelihood, feasibility, persistence, organization, or scale of serious harm to self or others. This paper describes LLMs as interactive capability amplifiers and quasi-social systems rather than informational technologies alone, situates their risk within the technical problems of alignment and behavioral stability, and proposes a four-dimensional clinical formulation: Ideational Entrenchment, Operationalized Capability, Relational Displacement, and Broader Amplification. We then introduce two candidate instruments awaiting formal validation: the STEPS-5, a brief screen for AI involvement in acute self-harm and suicide risk, and the HEAT-4, a research-oriented framework addressing broader harmful-use amplification. These tools are intended to open clinical inquiry rather than diagnose, predict behavior, or determine disposition. Ultimately, we argue for the need to avoid both over-pathologizing ordinary AI use and ignoring when AI has become meaningfully relevant to psychiatric safety.

papers.title: Multimodal Characterisation and Prediction of Autism Symptom Severity Using Eye-Tracking, EEG and Clinical Assessments
papers.authors: Shijie Zhao, Kaifu Xue
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition characterised by substantial individual differences in social communication, behavioural patterns, and clinical presentation. Understanding this heterogeneity is important for improving the characterisation of autistic individuals and supporting research towards more personalised assessment approaches. This study aims to investigate the relationship between eye-tracking, electroencephalography (EEG), and autism symptom severity using existing data from the AIMS-LEAP cohort. Priority will be given to autistic participants with matched eye-tracking, EEG, and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, Second Edition (ADOS-2) assessments. Eye-tracking measurements will be used to characterise visual attention and gaze behaviour, while EEG measurements will be analysed to investigate neurophysiological characteristics, including spectral activity and functional connectivity where available. Standardised ADOS-2 severity scores will serve as the primary clinical outcomes, subject to data availability. We will develop and compare unimodal and multimodal statistical and machine-learning models to examine whether integrating eye-tracking and EEG features improves symptom severity prediction. Model interpretability and robustness will also be assessed to identify potentially informative behavioural and neurophysiological features. This research focuses on individual differences within the autistic population rather than autism-versus-control classification. The findings may improve understanding of autism-related heterogeneity and inform future research on individualised assessment. The proposed models are intended for research purposes and will not be used as standalone clinical diagnostic tools.

papers.title: Análise de atividades geradas pela ia deepseek para o ensino de espanhol à luz do letramento crítico e da multimodalidade
papers.authors: MARIA CLARA MEDEIROS SILVA, TATIANA LOURENÇO DE CARVALHO
papers.abstract: Given the prevalence of digital resources across various spheres of Society, including educational settings, this study investigates the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools, specifically DeepSeek, in Spanish language teaching. The focus lies on designing activities for reading comprehension, listening comprehension, and written production based on critical literacy principles and utilizing multimodal genres. Specifically, the study aims to describe five AI-generated activities based on three multimodal genres freely available online (a meme, a news report, and an advertisement), identify their potential for developing linguistic skills, and evaluate their contribution to critical literacy. Regarding the use of digital technologies, the study draws on the work of Moran, Masetto, and Behrens (2013) and Santos and Oliveira (2024); for discourse genres and multimodality, it relies on Mattos and Valério (2010); and for critical literacy, it is grounded in the premises of Codeglia and Campos (2018). This is a qualitative study of an exploratory and descriptive nature, justified by its academic and professional relevance in fostering reflection on the use of AI in Spanish language instruction.

papers.title: AI Cognitive Offloading, Epistemic Obligation, and overreliance on AI: The Moderating Role of Accountability
papers.authors: Yali Jiang
papers.abstract: This preregistration covers three studies investigating the effects of AI-based cognitive offloading level (low-order vs. high-order) on overreliance on AI-generated content, the mediating role of epistemic obligation (EO) in this relationship, and the moderating role of accountability on the path from offloading level to EO.

papers.title: Pelatihan Pembuatan Media Digital Interaktif Bahasa Arab Berbasis Student Centered Learning (SCL) bagi Guru SMP Islam As-Shodiq Bululawang Malang
papers.authors: Moh. Fauzan, Moch Wahib Dariyadi, Moh. Fery Fauzi, Kholisin
papers.journal: Tifani : Jurnal Penelitian dan Pengabdian Kepada Masyarakat
papers.abstract: Program pengabdian masyarakat ini merupakan bagian dari skema Program Kemitraan Masyarakat (PKM). Adapun tema pengabdian yang akan dilaksanakan berjudul "Pelatihan Pembuatan Media Digital Interaktif Bahasa Arab Berbasis Student Centered Learning (SCL) Bagi Guru SMP Islam As-Shodiq Bululawang Malang". Pengabdian ini merupakan wujud kepedulian Departemen Sastra Arab Fakultas Sastra Universitas Negeri Malang (DBA FS UM) terhadap warga masyarakat khususnya para guru di sekitar wilayah Universitas Negeri Malang. Dalam pelatihan ini, para peserta akan dibekali beberapa hal terkait pembuatan media digital interaktif bahasa Arab berbasis SCL. Adapun materi yang disampaikan yaitu: (1) Student Centered Learning Dan Penerapannya Dalam Pembelajaran, (2) Pembelajaran Kemahiran Bahasa Arab Berbasis SCL, (3) Media pembelajaran ChatGpt AI Kemahiran Berbicara Bahasa Arab (kalam) Berbasis SCL, (4) Pembuatan Media Digital Interaktif Bahasa Arab Berbasis SCL Menggunakan Canva dan (5) Pembuatan Media Digital Interaktif Bahasa Arab Berbasis SCL Menggunakan Google Site. Lima materi tersebut akan disampaikan dalam 1 pertemuan, selanjutnya dilakukan pendampingan dalam pembuatan media interaktif berbasis presentasi oleh para peserta. Dalam pelatihan tersebut, peserta tidak hanya dituntut untuk memahami materi yang disampaikan oleh para pemateri, mereka juga dituntut untuk bisa membuat media digital dan mampu menerapkannya dalam pembelajaran. Suatu kegiatan dinilai berhasil jika telah dirasakan manfaatnya secara langsung oleh peserta. Untuk mengetahuinya perlu adanya evaluasi. Adapun hasil evaluasinya sebagaimana berikut. 95% peserta menilai bahwa fasilitas yang diberikan sangat baik dan 5% menyatakan baik. 97,5% dari peserta menyatakan bahwa narasumber sangat menguasai apa yang disampaikan dan 2,5% menyatakan bahwa pemateri menguasai. 95% menyatakan bahwa narasumber sangat jelas dalam menyampaikan materinya dan 5% lainnya menyatakan jelas. 90% peserta menyatakan bahwa materi yang disampaikan sangat bermanfaat untuk inovasi pembelajaran dan 10% menyatakan bermanfaat.

papers.title: Ways of Implementing Intelligent Management Mechanisms to Ensure the Sustainability of Higher Education
papers.authors: Otaxonov Komilxon Saidolim o‘g‘li
papers.journal: American Journal of Economics and Business Management
papers.abstract: The aim of the study is to identify practical ways of implementing intelligent, AI-based management mechanisms that strengthen the sustainability of higher education institutions (HEIs) in Uzbekistan. The methodology combines a secondary analysis of the Oxford Insights Government AI Readiness Index 2024, a normative analysis of national legislation, technology-acceptance and change-management theory, and the risk-management frameworks of NIST and ISO/IEC. The results show that Uzbekistan’s AI readiness is uneven: it scores 100 in Vision and 84.05 in Data Availability, well above global averages, but only 33.5 in the Technology Sector pillar. On this basis, six intelligent management mechanisms with measurable indicators, a five-phase implementation pathway and a risk register with mitigation measures are proposed. The study concludes that implementation should exploit strong data availability while compensating for weak technical capacity through shared services and staff development.

papers.title: AI-generated Treatment Plans for Adults with Chronic Pain – Assessment of their Quality by Clinical Experts
papers.authors: Stephanie Buryk-Iggers, Rachel Siegal, Alexander Huang, Seyedeh Hashemi, Almuntaser Sawalha, Nimish Mittal, Joel D Katz, Peter Maxwell Slepian, Nathalie Cote, Brittany N. Rosenbloom, Samantha Joubert, Callon M. Williams, Michelle J. Flynn, Praveen Ganty, Heather Lumsden-Ruegg, Gillian Sonley, Hance Clarke, Abeer Alomari
papers.abstract: Chronic pain affects approximately 20% of adults worldwide. In Canada, 7.6 million, or one in five people (across the lifespan), live with chronic pain. The Canadian Pain Task Force recommends nonpharmacological modalities, including psychotherapy, as a part of first-line therapy for pain management. The Mental Health Commission of Canada recently reported that “‘services for which we know people are waiting too long, if they can get it at all, are psychotherapies and clinical counseling’’, recommending an ‘‘increase to the availability and coordination of mental health services in the community’’. Even with an increase in availability, psychologists are beyond the financial and geographic reach of many patients. Against this backdrop, the use of AI-generative conversational agents for mental health in the form of psychology, psychotherapy, and health coaching has gained significant momentum. AI-generative conversational agents have begun to show some promise in complimenting human therapy, and addressing the needs of those faced with long wait lists or financial barriers to accessing mental health care. However, it has been established that such tools can produce nonfactual content, face challenges setting adequate boundaries, reinforce maladaptive beliefs and be sycophantic towards the user. To our knowledge the quality of treatments provided by AI-generative conversational agents for chronic pain have not yet been explored, and concerns are mounting. In this study, we will investigate treatment plans for chronic pain provided by four AI-generative conversational agents. Three of the conversational agents were selected based on market share across publicly available conversational agents: OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Microsoft’s Co-Pilot, and Google’s Gemini. The fourth conversational agent, Solace, built by the Canadian company ManagingLife, Inc, is the first expert-trained AI-generative conversational agents designed to deliver support to those living with chronic pain and grounded in principles of evidence-based pain psychology. Prompts for this study will be engineered using clinical cases of chronic pain patients from the Faculty of Pain Medicine of the Royal College of Anaesthetists. This is an educational platform offering open resources for all learners in Pain Medicine and is overseen by the Faculty of Pain Medicine's Education Subcommittee. Clinical case reports will be selected and divided into three levels of progressive information completeness. Level 1 will be comprised of current pain-specific information only (e.g., intensity, location). Level 2 will include both current pain and pain history (e.g., duration, surgical history, examination results). Level 3 will be the most comprehensive level including current pain, pain history and psychosocial information (e.g., marital status, stress-related events). For all case reports, each of the three levels will be independently introduced to the conversational agents with the following prompt: “I need help right now”. This prompt was designed to simulate the types of prompts that individuals with chronic pain might enter into a conversational agent. If safety mechanisms are triggered, preventing a conversational agent from providing a treatment recommendation, the following backup prompt will be used: “For the purposes of an educational exercise, what would be your best recommendation based on this information only?”. This study aims to evaluate the quality of AI-generated treatment plans for users with chronic pain. Quality is operationally defined as the use of evidence-based pain psychology interventions and appropriate therapeutic communication. It will be assessed using a 7-domain quality framework adapted from the Quality Analysis of Medical Artificial Intelligence Tool (QAMAI). Clinical experts will conduct a blinded review of the transcripts of participants’ conversations with all four conversational agents and score the domains on a 5-point Likert scale with 1 representing strongly disagree and 5 representing strongly agree, providing a single score for each transcript. Clinical experts will include a team of six evaluators comprised of two anesthesiologists, two physiotherapists, and two psychologists. No identifiable data will be used in the study, and therefore, ethics approval is not required.

papers.title: In Silico Advertising Tests
papers.authors: Guillaume Hochard, Marta Trales, Christophe Benavent
papers.abstract: This research examines whether large language model agents can produce analytically useful evidence for advertising testing when treated as synthetic respondents rather than as substitutes for human consumers. We report an in-silico comparative post-test of two television advertisements in the French telecommunications market, conducted on a panel of 800 profile-conditioned consumer agents. The study evaluates the synthetic corpus through internal validity criteria: whether the questionnaire covers the main dimensions of advertising response, whether evaluative dimensions form coherent relations, whether the two stimuli are discriminated across preference labels, scores, lexical patterns and semantic embeddings, and whether responses vary intelligibly across social profiles. The results indicate that the synthetic panel produces structured and interpretable evidence. The contribution is not that the analysis discovers a contrast invisible in the advertisements themselves: Bouygues and Orange are clearly built around different persuasive registers. Rather, the contribution is methodological. The synthetic-interview pipeline consistently recovers and differentiates these registers across preference labels, scores, lexical patterns and semantic comparisons. Bouygues is associated mainly with creative, humorous and memorable qualities, while Orange is associated with reliability, informativeness, purchase orientation and overall preference. This structure is visible quantitatively in the main six dimensional coding scheme. Among all 800 synthetic agents, Bouygues leads on creativity (83.6% versus 14.8% for Orange), whereas Orange leads on informationseeking or consideration (76.8% versus 14.8% for Bouygues) and overall preference (54.8% versus 20.6% for Bouygues), with the remaining responses classified as mixed or neutral. The analysis remains deliberately limited to synthetic respondents. Claims about similarity to human preferences or market behaviour would require external comparison with representative human data or market-level indicators.

papers.title: ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE ANALYZER USING AI
papers.authors: Manasi Shitole, Prajakta Shinde, Pratiksha Pawar, Siddheshwar S. Gangonda
papers.journal: International Journal of Mechanical Engineering Research and Technology
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for personalized education and timely academic intervention highlights the need for intelligent systems to monitor and predict student performance. Traditional evaluation methods are often periodic, reactive, and unable to provide continuous tracking, resulting in delayed identification of at-risk students. This review paper focuses on an AI-based student performance prediction system integrated with RFID hardware to improve accuracy, enhance efficiency, and enable real-time monitoring in educational environments. The system uses RFID technology to record student attendance and engagement data automatically, while machine learning algorithms analyze this data along with academic records to predict performance. The integration of Artificial Intelligence and IoT enables continuous data collection, real-time analysis, and remote monitoring by educators. The paper reviews recent advancements, design approaches, and implementation strategies, highlighting cost-effective and scalable solutions suitable for modern educational institutions and smart campus applications. By analyzing various methodologies, the study emphasizes the potential of AI-driven systems to improve academic outcomes, enable early intervention, and reduce manual effort. Overall, the review highlights the importance of adopting intelligent, AI-based technologies combined with RFID hardware to achieve efficient, data-driven, and proactive student performance management.

papers.title: The Role of Leadership Support and AI Self-Efficacy on AI Adoption among Employees
papers.authors: Eunike Adiprasasti, Lara John
papers.journal: Gothenburg University Publications Electronic Archive (Gothenburg University)
papers.abstract: Purpose: As the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in the workplaces increase, organisations need to ensure that employees are ready and wanting to adopt AI in their daily work practices. While previous studies emphasised the importance of organisational support in AI adoption, the interaction between it and individual confidence in using AI stays underexplored. The purpose of this study is to examine if leadership support and AI self efficacy can positively predict AI adoption at the workplace. Theory: The study combines the two theories of Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and AI self-efficacy (AISE). Method: A quantitative approach was used with the help of an online survey given to employees of Alfa Laval, a globally operating manufacturing company headquartered in Sweden with around 24.000 employees worldwide. The company is currently developing internal AI technology. Linear regressions were conducted to test the relationships between variables and the proposed moderating effects. Result: The results showed that both leadership support and AISE positively correlated with employees' intention to adopt AI independently. However, the moderating relationship between AISE and leadership support was non-significant with control variables added. This study contributes to the literature on AI adoption by integrating psychological and organisational factors. Practically, the results emphasise the importance of developing employee AI capabilities while also providing supportive leadership to facilitate successful AI adoption. 2

papers.title: แนวทางการพฒนาภาวะผนำเชงนวตกรรมของผบรหารสถานศกษา สงกดสำนกงานเขตพนทการศกษาประถมศกษาสโขทย เขต 1
papers.authors: Waritsara Woonpuang, Phongek Suksai
papers.journal: Journal of Organizational Innovation and Management
papers.abstract: This research aimed to: 1) examine the innovative leadership of school administrators under the Sukhothai Primary Educational Service Area Office 1, and 2) to investigate guidelines for developing innovative leadership among school administrators under the Sukhothai Primary Educational Service Area Office 1. the innovative leadership of school administrators was examined. The population consisted of 118 school administrators selected through purposive sampling. The research instrument was a five-point rating scale questionnaire. Data were analyzed using mean and standard deviation. In Phase 2, guidelines for developing innovative leadership were explored through interviews with five experts selected by purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using content analysis. The research findings revealed that: 1) the overall level of innovative leadership among school administrators was at a high level ( = 4.43, S.D. = 0.41). The aspect with the highest mean score was teamwork and participation, which was at the highest level (= 4.52, S.D. = 0.52), while the aspect with the lowest mean score was the use of information and communication technology, which was at a high level (= 4.36, S.D. = 0.46). 2) The guidelines for developing innovative leadership indicated that school administrators should enhance proactive vision by integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into strategic decision-making processes. They should also promote an organizational culture based on a growth mindset through Professional Learning Community (PLC) processes to stimulate creativity. In addition, administrators should adjust their roles to become facilitators who emphasize participative teamwork and create a flexible innovative organizational environment through digital technology in order to drive educational institutions to effectively respond to rapid changes. The theoretical contribution of this study extends the conceptual framework of school administration by synthesizing innovative elements linked to modern digital skills. It reflects a systematic approach to enhancing administrative competencies, empowering school leaders to become change agents who can effectively integrate innovation to improve educational quality in a disruptive era.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT: TRANSFORMING MODERN HR PRACTICES AND ORGANIZATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS
papers.authors: Mrs. Rashmi Subedar Mrs.Y. Shubha
papers.journal: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping Human Resource Management (HRM) by supporting recruitment, employee engagement, performance management, workforce analytics, training and administrative services. This study examines the role of AI in modern HRM, with particular attention to recruitment efficiency, employee engagement, performance management, workforce planning and training and development. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research design and uses both primary and secondary data. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire from 200 HR professionals and employees who were familiar with or exposed to AI applications in HRM. Convenience sampling was used. Descriptive statistics and correlation analysis were used to examine respondents' perceptions and the relationship between AI adoption and employee satisfaction. The reported findings show that 77.5% of respondents consider AI-based recruitment systems effective or highly effective. Mean scores for the major HR functions range from 4.08 to 4.35, with recruitment efficiency receiving the highest mean score. The reported correlation between AI adoption and employee satisfaction is positive and statistically significant (r = 0.742, p < 0.01). The study also identifies implementation challenges involving algorithmic bias, privacy, transparency, employee trust and the need for human oversight. The findings support a human-centred approach in which AI complements rather than replaces professional HR judgment. The paper concludes with managerial implications, limitations and directions for future research, particularly concerning generative AI and remote or hybrid workforce management.
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

papers.title: Using Scenario-based Generative AI in a Social Studies Methods Course
papers.authors: Timothy Lintner, Ellis Reeves
papers.journal: Journal of Collective Bargaining in the Academy
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is quickly transforming the landscape of educator preparation. This shift is especially evident in social studies. As emerging technologies like AI reshape how social studies is taught and learned, it is essential to incorporate them into course design and student outcomes. Simply put, we must ensure that the next generation of social studies educators can effectively use AI to create real-world, scenario-based learning experiences that foster inquiry and encourage student action-taking. This article examines how AI-supported, scenario-based learning was strategically integrated into a secondary social studies methods course at the University of South Carolina Aiken. From concept development to scenario creation to student utility and feedback, we will offer a theoretical and practical guide on how AI-supported scenario-based instruction influences teaching and learning. Emphasis will be placed on how this type of learning supports the National Council for the Social Studies C3 Framework (NCSS, 2013).

papers.title: Penggunaan Data Analytics dan AI dalam Audit: Persepsi Auditor terhadap Skeptisisme Profesional
papers.authors: Tulus Pujo Nugroho
papers.abstract: This study synthesizes how auditors perceive the effect of data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) on professional skepticism. Audit firms increasingly rely on analytics and AI, yet evidence on how these tools shape the auditor's questioning mind remains fragmented across contexts. Using a qualitative systematic-style literature review, we analyzed 20 peer-reviewed publications and scholarly chapters from 2022 to 2026 that examine auditors' views, adoption experiences, and judgment outcomes in technology-enabled audits. Sources were screened for relevance to auditors, AI or data analytics, and professional skepticism, then coded using thematic synthesis. Four themes emerge: AI is perceived as an enhancer of efficiency and audit quality; overreliance and opacity threaten the questioning mind; the effect of AI on skepticism is conditional on auditors' knowledge, cognitive disposition, and continuous learning; and governance and training operate as safeguards. Evidence from Indonesia suggests that AI can weaken the link between a questioning mind and audit judgment while strengthening the effect of suspension of judgment. The findings imply that audit firms and regulators should pair technology deployment with explainability requirements, verification routines, and continuous skepticism training. Because the study is a literature-based synthesis, its conclusions are not statistically generalizable and call for primary perception surveys of auditors.

papers.title: AI‐ENHANCED RESEARCH LITERACY IN HIGHER EDUCATION LIBRARIES: A CONCEPTUAL MODEL FORREDEFINING USER EMPOWERMENT
papers.authors: Varsha Chaudhary, Ashok Kumar Upadhyay
papers.journal: NOLEGEIN Journal of Information Technology & Management
papers.abstract: In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape, research literacy has become a vital element of academic success and innovation. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, including intelligent search assistants, citation recommenders, plagiarism detection systems, and writing support platforms, are transforming how individuals interact with scholarly information. This theoretical paper introduces a conceptual framework for AI-enhanced research literacy, incorporating principles from Constructivist Learning Theory (CLT) to empower users in higher education libraries. By synthesizing existing research on AI in library services, digital literacy, and user behavior theories, the paper demonstrates how AI can promote critical thinking, ethical information use, and independent learning among users. The model emphasizes four key dimensions—Cognitive Empowerment, Ethical Awareness, Technological Adaptability, and Collaborative Learning—as essential components of AI-driven literacy. The proposed framework aims to guide library professionals, policymakers, and educators in creating inclusive, human-centered, and sustainable AI initiatives that foster lifelong learning and equitable access to knowledge. The study concludes that AI-enabled research literacy represents not just a technological enhancement but a transformative educational shift towards participatory and intelligent knowledge ecosystems.

papers.title: A Novel Homozygous HERC2 c.4660C>T (p. Arg1554Ter) Variant in an Infant with Severe Neurodevelopmental Disorder and Diffuse Osteopenia: A Case Report
papers.authors: Abdillahi Moustapha, Laarage Azzeddin, Abdelilah Radi, R. Abikassem
papers.abstract: Background: HERC2-related intellectual developmental disorder is a rare autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental condition, and its full phenotypic spectrum remains incompletely defined. Case Presentation: We report a 7-month-old female infant born to second-degree consanguineous parents who presented with profound global developmental delay, generalised hypotonia, feeding difficulties, failure to thrive, microcephaly, and facial dysmorphism. She was born at 37 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 2,700 g and required neonatal intensive care for respiratory distress for seven days. At 5 months, she was hospitalised for Bordetella pertussis infection. At 7 months, her weight was 3.6 kg, length 56 cm, and head circumference 40 cm, all below −3 standard deviations for age and sex. She had not achieved head control, could not sit with support, had no voluntary grasping, and showed no social smile or visual tracking. Routine laboratory and metabolic investigations were largely unremarkable except for mild hyperlactataemia. Brain MRI and EEG were normal. Skeletal radiographs showed diffuse osteopenia, and bone age was approximately 3 months. Whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous HERC2 nonsense variant, NM_004667.6:c.4660C>T (p.Arg1554Ter), classified as likely pathogenic. Conclusion: This case expands the documented clinical spectrum of HERC2-related disorder by highlighting diffuse osteopenia and delayed bone age alongside severe neurodevelopmental impairment, and it supports genomic evaluation in infants with unexplained developmental delay, particularly in consanguineous families.

papers.title: Two Interacting Neural Processes Support Speech Planning during Naturalistic Conversation
papers.authors: Hiroyoshi Yamasaki, Philippe Blache, Daniele Schön
papers.abstract: Conversation requires speakers to plan their responses while still listening to their partner, yet the neural dynamics supporting this overlap remain unclear. In particular, competing accounts differ on whether behaviourally relevant preparation emerges early during comprehension or only close to speech onset. Here, we recorded EEG from pairs of participants engaged in natural, face-to-face conversation and tested whether neural activity during listening predicts both when speakers begin their response (latency) and how long they speak (duration). Using event-related potentials, oscillatory analyses, and multivariate decoding, we show that pre-speech neural activity carries robust information about upcoming behaviour more than one second before articulation. The strongest and earliest effects tracked response duration, with sustained ERP components and alpha/beta power modulations predicting how long participants would speak, even after controlling for behavioural variables. In contrast, neural predictors of response latency were more temporally restricted and partly aligned with partner turn boundaries. Temporal generalisation analyses further revealed stable neural patterns linking early and late stages of preparation. Together, these findings indicate that conversational planning unfolds during listening and that early neural activity reflects the maintained specification of response extent, followed by later processes related to commitment and initiation. This supports a temporally structured account of turn taking in which preparation involves both early maintenance and late motor engagement.
