papers.title: Mediación pedagógica con inteligencia artificial generativa y desarrollo del pensamiento crítico en estudiantes
papers.authors: Noelia del Carmen Lupú Benavides, Leydi Laura Ramírez Ortega, Galo Bismark Montecinos Romo, Monica Andrea Reyes Rodriguez, Jessenia Esthefani Morán Díaz
papers.journal: Revista Multidisciplinar Epistemología de las Ciencias
papers.abstract: The study analyzed the relationship between pedagogical mediation involving generative artificial intelligence and the development of critical thinking among students at a public educational institution under Ecuador's Ministry of Education. The sample consisted of 100 students from the intermediate and upper levels of General Basic Education and the Unified General Baccalaureate. The study employed a mixed-methods approach predominantly quantitative using a non-experimental, cross-sectional, and descriptive-correlational design. Data collection involved a mixed-format questionnaire comprising 15 Likert-scale items and two open-ended questions. Results revealed a favorable perception regarding the pedagogical use of generative artificial intelligence, with an overall mean score of 3.91 out of 5. Argumentation and reflection received the highest ratings, whereas information verification received the lowest. Students in the Baccalaureate program demonstrated greater autonomy and critical engagement. The study concludes that teacher mediation is essential for fostering the ethical, reflective, and responsible use of artificial intelligence in school-based learning.

papers.title: AI-Empowered Virtual Screening-Driven Innovation and Practice of Virtual–Real Integrated Classroom Teaching in Medicinal Chemistry
papers.authors: Shuangcheng Zhi, Meidie Cheng, Jingyi Sang, Wei Xu, Yiru Yang, Xiaoyue Peng, Can Xu, Bingbing Li, Yanxin Ye
papers.journal: Journal of modern educational theory and practice.
papers.abstract: In order to solve the pain points of the traditional “Medicinal Chemistry” classroom such as focusing only on theory without practice, lack of applications of AI and virtual screening tools, and disconnecting teaching content from regional industry needs, we, under support of the "Emerging Engineering Education", "Artificial Intelligence Plus" action plans, proposed an integrated virtual–real innovative teaching model based on AI-based druggability prediction, virtual screening and teaching-session design; then conducted teaching with the practical case of molecular docking of hexahydrocurcumin with heat shock protein 90α (HSP90α), which is included in the chapter about natural antitumor drugs. The model realized two-way empowerment between the virtual and the physical – the average time students spend using AutoDock Vina was decreased by 32%, 92.4% of students reported that their learning interest has been significantly increased, the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in connecting molecular docking with experimental design, and provides a replicable paradigm for cultivating pharmaceutical talents at local application-oriented undergraduate institutions.

papers.title: Construction of an Indicator System and Enhancement Strategies for Artificial Intelligence Literacy of Primary and Secondary School Teachers
papers.authors: Huang Yanxuan
papers.journal: Journal of modern educational theory and practice.
papers.abstract: With the progress of artificial intelligence technology, there are great changes on the structure of competence framework of primary and secondary school teachers; clarification of its connotation and construction of an operable indicator system is an issue worthy of attention in the domain of educational technology research. Existing studies have shown divergences among technological cognition, ethical criticism and pedagogical transformation without having a special analytical framework which suits the professional characteristics of primary and secondary school teachers. Deconstructing the artificial intelligence literacy of primary and secondary school teachers into 5 dimensions: intelligent technology cognition, data-driven teaching decision-making, intelligent educational resource design, human-machine collaborative teaching implementation and intelligent educational ethics judgment based on the task-situation analysis approach, constructing a three-level indicator system, getting indicator weights by the analytic hierarchy process. Based on our results, we delineated three stages of literacy development through observing the laws of capability growth, designing a layered and progressive content framework for learning, creating a support system from three aspects – technological resources, learning communities, and self-diagnosis - forming a complete research chain from dimension definition, indicator quantification, to pathway design giving theoretical reference for the assessment and cultivation in this field.

papers.title: Research on the Transformation Logic and Implementation Paths of Intelligent Accounting Education
papers.authors: Ying Su, Yanxia Wu
papers.journal: Journal of modern educational theory and practice.
papers.abstract: Intelligence technology changes the basic logic of accounting work. Automation and machine learning models are gradually replacing accounting tasks with clear rules, shifting the work chain into data ingestion, model processing and result verification. Data governance, model application and anomaly interpretation capabilities have become very valuable strategically but the current accounting education system focuses on memorizing accounting standards and manual bookkeeping leading to an ability gap that does not match industry side's demands. Constructing a transformation framework from three aspects: knowledge reconstruction, paradigm shift, and ecosystem evolution. Elaborate the direction for element reorganization by teaching content, teaching scenarios and evaluation systems respectively. Three implementation paths proposed include modular integration of courses, Reconstruction of experimental teaching for algorithmic thinking, Upgrade faculty data literacy. Aimed at providing theoretical support for accounting education adapting to intelligent work scenarios.

papers.title: Research on the Path of Artificial Intelligence Empowering the Development of Digital Literacy of College English Teachers
papers.authors: Yingjie Feng
papers.journal: Journal of modern educational theory and practice.
papers.abstract: Developing digital literacy by college English teachers faces challenges from the advent of artificial intelligence technology in education. In this study, we investigate the pathways of how artificial intelligence empowers the development of teachers' digital literacy, which builds up an analytical framework based upon three aspects: connotation definition; mechanism of action; and supporting strategies. By reviewing the concept evolution of digital literacy combined with the features of the college English teaching context, we identify the core elements of teachers' digital literacy within the intelligent technology environment. A literacy model composed of three dimensions (perception, acquisition, and transformation) has been built up according to the dynamic capability view. Pathway of literacy generation via cognitive apprenticeship effects, activation of teaching agency, and human-machine collaborative interaction were revealed at the mechanism level. Constructing an intelligent research and training ecosystem, applying the technology acceptance model, and direction of role reconstruction have been explored at the support level. We believe that the key to empowerment lies in activating the subjectivity of teachers via mechanism design so as to reach dynamic integration between technological application and humanistic value.

papers.title: Research on E-commerce Marketing Model Innovation in the Context of the Integrated Development of Short Videos and Live Streaming
papers.authors: Yilong Zhu
papers.journal: Journal of modern education and culture.
papers.abstract: Deeply integration of short videos and live streaming has altered the fundamental logic of e-commerce marketing. But there are still no comprehensive studies on its integration effect, especially missing the theoretical construction about the direction of marketing model innovation based upon the linkage between media evolution and value creation. According to the theoretical perspective of media convergence, we analyzed it according to the progression thread of "evolutionary logic—mechanism change—model innovation", and find out that as the integrated business format evolved from external combination to endogenous synergy, not only did the pattern of attention allocation and mechanism of traffic retention get reorganized but also caused the structural shift of underlying logic of e-commerce marketing from search orientation to content orientation. Then we clarified how content assets convert into marketing capital, what is the logic of trust generation in relational networks and the compression effect of interactive feedback on consumer decision-making. Finally, we constructed a framework for marketing model innovation through three aspects including progressive organization of content, bidirectional value co-creation and dynamic adjustment of effectiveness. Our study found that the model innovation driven by convergence is basically the result of the synergistic effect of media evolution and value change with the core orientation lying in the following: the rhythm synergy between content and conversion; the balance between one-way transmission and bidirectional co-creation; and the reconciliation between short-term efficiency and long-term assets.

papers.title: Research on the Construction of AI-Empowered College Physics Experiment Courses
papers.authors: Yuguo Luan
papers.journal: Journal of modern education and culture.
papers.abstract: Driven jointly by the national strategic initiative on educational digitalization and the "Artificial Intelligence+" action plan, physics experiment teaching is undergoing a critical transition from traditional hands‐on operations to intelligent inquiry‐based learning. However, current research on AI‐empowered experimental teaching largely relies on expensive specialized equipment or cloud‐based computing resources, which entails high deployment costs, significant data privacy risks, and limited feasibility for widespread adoption in ordinary colleges and universities. Grounded in the principles of lightweight design, low cost, and high availability, this study systematically develops a theoretical framework and practical pathways for constructing AI‐enhanced university physics experiment courses. The proposed approach centers on open‐source large language models and retrieval‐augmented generation (RAG) techniques to build a domain‐specific knowledge system for physics experiments, and achieves data security and cost control through local deployment. We establish a tripartite construction pathway encompassing knowledge base development, vertical AI model customization for the course, and intelligent teaching applications. Furthermore, we design a human‐computer collaborative instruction model that integrates AI‐assisted preview, instructor‐led focused instruction, and a two‐stage assessment comprising AI initial evaluation followed by instructor verification, thereby forming a closed‐loop intelligent teaching system covering the entire spectrum of instruction, learning, administration, evaluation, and assessment. The findings indicate that this model effectively mitigates the hallucination issue inherent in general‐purpose large models when applied to specialized domains, improves the quality of students' experimental reports, and enhances their autonomous inquiry capabilities. It also offers a replicable, cost‐effective reform blueprint for resource‐constrained local institutions.

papers.title: Research on Innovation of AI-Assisted Classroom Teaching Mode in Communication Electronic Circuits
papers.authors: Ting Liu
papers.journal: International journal of educational teaching and research.
papers.abstract: The communication electronic circuits feature includes high-frequency signal processing and multi-module coupling, which has non-linear cognitive load distribution in classroom teaching with inherent shortcomings when using traditional lectures to solve break points in deductive logic or no immediate feedback. Taking an artificial intelligence assistance perspective according to analyzing the mapping relationship between the course's knowledge structure and students' cognitive load, we defined the functional position and technical boundary of artificial intelligence, built a behavioral sequence based cognitive diagnosis model, a parameterized deduction intervention strategy, and a multimodal learning-state fusion mechanism, providing optimization path including completion of logical chain breaks, generative topological mutation prompts, and personalization content reorganization. Our research tries to provide a reference analytical framework and implementation ideas on human-machine collaboration teaching for high-frequency electronic circuit courses.

papers.title: Role of Human Resource Development in Shaping Innovation in Art of the 21st Century
papers.authors: Tatiana Portnova
papers.abstract: This article examines the role of human resource development in shaping an innovative environment for art in the context of accelerating digitalisation and global transformation in the 21st century. The relevance of the topic arises from the transition of creative industries from predominantly traditional forms of artistic activity toward technology-enabled and interdisciplinary models in which human capital becomes a central driver of new artistic forms, organisational adaptation, and wider socio-economic development. Drawing on 32 scholarly and institutional sources published mainly between 2021 and 2025 and accessed through academic repositories, publisher platforms, and institutional websites, the study explores the theoretical foundations, mechanisms of influence, and current practices of human resource management in the artistic and creative sectors. The findings indicate that strengthening human potential through competence-based development, digital learning, gamification, data-informed HR practices, artificial intelligence, creative clusters, and continuous professional development can support innovation capacity when these tools are aligned with artistic goals and organisational needs. Particular attention is given to developments in Russia while also drawing on international evidence concerning human capital, productivity, arts management, skills transformation, and workforce development. The article further proposes practical recommendations concerning competence-based assessment, investment in lifelong learning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and international cooperation. Rather than treating technology as a substitute for artistic judgement, the study concludes that sustainable innovation in the arts depends on the combined development of creative, digital, analytical, collaborative, and adaptive capabilities.

papers.title: TREND ANALYSIS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-GENERATED ECONOMETRICS MULTIPLE CHOICE TEST ITEM PARAMETERS AMONG UNDERGRADUATE ECONOMICS STUDENTS, NASARAWA STATE UNIVERSITY, KEFFI, NIGERIA
papers.authors: SALIHU ABDULLAHI GALLE, ALAKU SAMUEL ENGOM, OLAYELE OLUSOLA JOSEPH
papers.journal: International Journal of African Research Sustainability Studies
papers.abstract: This study examined the psychometric characteristics of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated Econometrics multiple-choice test items Parameters (EMCTIP) among undergraduate Economics students, Nasarawa State University, Keffi, Nigeria. The study specifically determined the trend in the difficulty indices, discrimination indices, and effectiveness of distractors of AI-generated test items. A descriptive evaluative research design was adopted. The sample comprised 400 undergraduate Economics students. A 30-items AI-generated Econometrics multiple-choice test (EMCT). The EMCT was subjected to experts’ judgement, and yielded validity index of 0.74, and 0.073 reliability index. Item analysis was conducted using difficulty index, discrimination index, and distractor effectiveness as the major indices. Means and standard deviations was used to answered the psychometric indices and examine their trends across successive test administrations and One Way ANOVA to test the hypotheses at 95% confidence level. The findings revealed that there is a significant difference in the difficulty indices of AI-generated EMCT items; there is no significant difference in the effectiveness of distractors of the AI-generated EMCT items; and there is no significant difference in the discrimination indices and effectiveness of distractors of AI-generated EMCT items across successive test administrations among undergraduate Economics students of NSUK, Nigeria. The study concluded that AI-generated EMCT items demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties in terms of difficulty, discrimination, and distractor effectiveness. It was recommended that lecturers and test developers should subject AI-generated test items to systematic human review, empirical item analysis, and validation before their use in formal examinations.

papers.title: AN ILLUSION OF ENTREPRENEURIAL COMPETENCE IN ROBOTICS FOR SELF-RELIANCE IN KOGI STATE, NORTH-CENTRAL NIGERIA
papers.authors: Mohammed Ogaji Isah, Jolomi Irene OBIORU, HASSAN ALIYU
papers.abstract: This study critically interrogates the disjuncture between policy rhetoric and tangible outcomes in robotics-focused entrepreneurship development within Kogi State, North-Central Nigeria. Despite considerable public and institutional expenditure on robotics education, artificial intelligence infrastructure, and technology incubation schemes, the region exhibits a persistent failure to convert trained human capital into sustainable entrepreneurial ventures. Using a qualitative case-study approach grounded in secondary policy documents, institutional reports, and media coverage, the article argues that robotics entrepreneurship competence in Kogi State is largely performative symbolically enacted through official announcements and training certifications but materially unrealised owing to systemic infrastructural weakness, curricular irrelevance, institutional fragmentation, and deficient market linkages. Five interconnected obstacles are identified: erratic power and bandwidth availability; pedagogical models that privilege theory over practice; feeble university–industry partnerships; acute shortages of risk capital and accessible markets; and the absence of a cohesive ecosystem for technology venturing. The paper concludes by articulating a multi-pronged strategy to close the competence reality chasm, encompassing foundational infrastructure upgrades, curriculum overhaul, ecosystem orchestration, and locally attuned robotics applications. The analysis offers transferable insights for technology-entrepreneurship policy across sub-Saharan Africa, where similar mismatches between ambition and implementation are endemic.

papers.title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON MARKETING PERFORMANCE, GUEST SATISFACTION AND LOYALTY: IMPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL HOTEL BUSINESS IN ABUJA, NIGERIA
papers.authors: CHARITY JIDDA, Elochukwu A. Nwankwo
papers.abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping hotel marketing and guest-service delivery, yet empirical evidence on its implications for guest satisfaction and loyalty in developing hospitality markets remains limited. This study examined AI applications in selected international hotels in Abuja, Nigeria, focusing on their perceived contribution to marketing performance, guest satisfaction and loyalty, as well as barriers to adoption. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design was employed, involving hotel staff and guests from six selected hotels. Data were collected through structured questionnaires, key-informant interviews and observation. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression and mediation analysis were used to examine relationships among the study variables. The findings indicate that conventional digital technologies were more widely used than genuine AI applications, with chatbots, machine-learning forecasting, intelligent recommendation systems and AI-supported analytics representing the principal AI-related applications. AI-supported guest experience was positively associated with satisfaction, while satisfaction demonstrated a stronger relationship with loyalty. The findings further indicate that cost, shortage of specialised skills, privacy and cybersecurity concerns, systems integration and infrastructural limitations constrain effective AI adoption. The study concludes that AI does not automatically generate guest loyalty; rather, its value depends on the quality, relevance and trustworthiness of the experience it creates. The study contributes by distinguishing AI from conventional digitalisation and proposing a human-centred pathway linking AI-supported experience, satisfaction and loyalty in the Abuja hospitality context.

papers.title: Lexicology as a Foundation for Effective Teaching of Russian as a Foreign Language
papers.authors: Namiq Abbasov
papers.journal: EuroGlobal Journal of Linguistics and Language Education.
papers.abstract: This article examines lexicology as a practical foundation for teaching Russian as a foreign language. It argues that lexical competence cannot be reduced to the memorization of translation equivalents because knowing a word includes its form, meanings, grammatical behavior, collocations, stylistic value, phraseological potential, and conditions of use. An integrative review combines foundational Russian lexicological scholarship with recent research on second-language vocabulary learning and current studies of Russian-language pedagogy. The discussion focuses on polysemy, homonymy, synonymy, antonymy, word formation, lexical combinability, phraseology, register, cultural meaning, and cross-linguistic interference. Recent evidence supports instruction that combines deliberate attention with repeated contextual encounters, retrieval, productive use, and cumulative recycling. Digital dictionaries, corpora, mobile applications, multimedia glosses, and generative artificial intelligence can extend exposure and feedback, but their pedagogical value depends on accurate examples, transparent source selection, and teacher-guided verification. The article proposes a seven-stage lexicology-informed teaching cycle that moves from needs-based selection and contextual encounter to semantic analysis, combinability, retrieval, communication, and assessment. It also recommends assessing lexical depth and appropriateness in addition to vocabulary size. The central conclusion is that lexicological knowledge becomes educationally valuable when it helps learners interpret lexical choices, notice conventional patterns, and use Russian vocabulary accurately and appropriately across communicative settings.

papers.title: The Effect of ChatGPT Integrated with Role-play on Students’ Speaking Fluency and Confidence
papers.authors: Siti Nurhalizah, Wiki Tedi Rahmawati, Widia Fransiska
papers.journal: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
papers.abstract: This study examined the effect of integrating ChatGPT with the Role-Play Technique on students’ speaking fluency and speaking confidence. The study was motivated by students’ difficulties in speaking English, particularly their limited fluency and low confidence during classroom speaking activities. A mixed-method research design was employed involving 35 eleventh-grade students at SMAS Nurul Iman Tanjung Morawa during the 2025/2026 academic year. The participants consisted of 17 students in the experimental group and 18 students in the control group. The experimental group used ChatGPT as a rehearsal partner before participating in face-to-face role-play activities, while the control group participated in conventional role-play without AI assistance. Data were collected through speaking tests, classroom observations, and a speaking confidence questionnaire. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk normality test, the Mann–Whitney U test, and effect size analysis using SPSS version 26. The findings showed a significant difference between the experimental and control groups in speaking fluency and speaking confidence. The Mann–Whitney U test produced significance values of 0.000 for both variables. The effect sizes were 0.87 for speaking fluency and 0.74 for speaking confidence, indicating large effects. The observation and questionnaire findings also showed greater participation, willingness to communicate, and confidence among students in the experimental group. The findings indicate that integrating ChatGPT as a rehearsal partner with the Role-Play Technique provided a supportive approach to developing students’ English speaking performance.

papers.title: TALABALARNING SPEAKING KO‘NIKMASINI RIVOJLANTIRISHDA ZAMONAVIY RAQAMLI PLATFORMALARDAN FOYDALANISH
papers.authors: Moxira Rasulova
papers.abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada oliy ta’lim muassasalarida tahsil olayotgantalabalarning ingliz tilida og‘zaki nutq (Speaking) ko‘nikmalarini rivojlantirishdazamonaviy raqamli platformalardan foydalanish imkoniyatlari tahlil qilinadi.Xususan, Cambly, HelloTalk, Speak va ELSA Speak kabi platformalarningtalabalarning og‘zaki nutqi, talaffuzi, kommunikativ kompetensiyasi hamda ingliztilida erkin muloqot qilish qobiliyatini rivojlantirishdagi o‘rni yoritiladi. Raqamlitexnologiyalardan foydalanish talabalarga auditoriyadan tashqari vaqtda ham ingliztilida muntazam mashq qilish, real suhbatlarda yoki sun’iy intellektga asoslanganmuloqot jarayonlarida ishtirok etish hamda individual qayta aloqa olish imkoniniberadi.Maqolada mazkur platformalardan samarali foydalanish uchun o‘qituvchitomonidan maqsadli topshiriqlar ishlab chiqish, muntazam og‘zaki nutq amaliyotinitashkil etish va tegishli baholash mezonlarini belgilash zarurligi asoslanadi.Tadqiqot natijalari zamonaviy raqamli platformalarni an’anaviy ta’lim jarayonibilan uyg‘unlashtirish talabalarning ingliz tilida og‘zaki nutq ko‘nikmalarinirivojlantirish va muloqot jarayonida o‘ziga bo‘lgan ishonchini oshirishga ijobiyta’sir ko‘rsatishi mumkinligini ko‘rsatadi. Abstract. This article analyzes the potential of modern digital platforms fordeveloping English-speaking skills among university students. In particular, itexamines the role of platforms such as Cambly, HelloTalk, Speak, and ELSA Speakin improving students’ oral communication, pronunciation, communicativecompetence, and ability to communicate fluently in English. The use of digitaltechnologies enables students to practice English regularly outside the classroom,participate in real-life or artificial intelligence-based conversations, and receiveindividualized feedback. The article emphasizes the importance of developing purposeful tasks,organizing regular speaking practice, and establishing appropriate assessmentcriteria under the guidance of a teacher to ensure the effective use of these platforms.The findings suggest that integrating modern digital platforms with traditionallanguage instruction can positively contribute to the development of students’English-speaking skills and increase their confidence in using English forcommunication. Аннотaция. В статье анализируются возможности использованиясовременных цифровых платформ для развития навыков устной речи наанглийском языке у студентов высших образовательных учреждений. Особоевнимание уделяется таким платформам, как Cambly, HelloTalk, Speak и ELSASpeak, а также их роли в совершенствовании устной речи, произношения,коммуникативной компетенции и способности студентов свободно общатьсяна английском языке. Использование цифровых технологий позволяетстудентам регулярно практиковать английский язык во внеаудиторное время,участвовать в реальных диалогах или коммуникативных ситуaциях,основанных на технологиях искусственного интеллекта, а также получатьиндивидуальную обратную связь.В статье обосновывается необходимость разработки преподавателемцеленаправленных заданий, организaции регулярной разговорной практики иопределения соответствующих критериев оценивания для эффективногоиспользования данных платформ. Результаты исследования показывают, чтоинтегрaция современных цифровых платформ с традиционным процессомобучения иностранному языку может положительно способствовать развитиюнавыков устной речи студентов и повышению их уверенности прииспользовании английского языка в процессе коммуникaции.

papers.title: TA’LIM JARAYONIDA SUN’IY INTELLEKTDAN FOYDALANISHNING IJOBIY VA SALBIY JIHATLARI: TIZIMLI TAHLIL VA STRATEGIK YONDASHUVLAR
papers.authors: Nishanova Zamira
papers.abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada zamonaviy ta’lim tizimiga sun’iy intellekt (SI) texnologiyalarini integratsiya qilishning konseptual va amaliy jihatlari tadqiq etilgan. Ta’lim jarayonida SI vositalari, jumladan, ChatGPT, adaptiv ta’lim platformalari va avtomatlashtirilgan baholash tizimlaridan foydalanishning ijobiyjihatlari - ta’limni personallashtirish, vaqtni tejash va inklyuzivlikni ta’minlash, shuningdek, salbiy jihatlari - akademik halollik bilan bog‘liq muammolar, kognitiv passivlik va raqamli tengsizlik tizimli ravishda tahlil qilingan. Tadqiqot metodologiyasi sifat va miqdoriy ma’lumotlarning qiyosiy tahliliga asoslangan. Tadqiqot natijalari SI texnologiyalaridan samarali foydalanish ta’lim jarayonining natijadorligini oshirish imkonini berishini, biroq ulardan nazoratsiz va maqsadsiz foydalanish talabalarning mustaqil va tanqidiy fikrlash ko‘nikmalarining rivojlanishiga salbiy ta’sir ko‘rsatishi mumkinligini ko‘rsatadi. Shuningdek, SI texnologiyalaridan foydalanish bilan bog‘liq ehtimoliy salbiy oqibatlarni minimallashtirish hamda ularni ta’lim jarayoniga pedagogik jihatdan maqsadga muvofiq integratsiya qilish bo‘yicha strategik tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan. Аннотация. В статье исследуются концептуальные и практические аспекты интеграции технологий искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) в современную систему образования. Проведён системный анализ положительных аспектов использования инструментов ИИ в образовательном процессе, включая ChatGPT, адаптивные образовательные платформы и автоматизированные системы оценивания, таких как персонализация обучения, экономия времени и обеспечение инклюзивности, а также потенциальных негативных аспектов - проблем академической добросовестности, когнитивной пассивности и цифрового неравенства. Методология исследования основана на сравнительном анализе качественных и количественных данных. Результаты исследования показывают, что эффективное использование технологий ИИ способствуетповышению результативности образовательного процесса, однако их неконтролируемое и нецелевое применение может негативно влиять на развитие навыков самостоятельного и критического мышления студентов. Кроме того, разработаны стратегические рекомендации по минимизации возможных негативных последствий использования ИИ и его педагогически целесообразной интеграции в образовательный процесс. Abstract. This article examines the conceptual and practical aspects of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into modern education systems. It provides a systematic analysis of both the benefits of using AI tools in education, including ChatGPT, adaptive learning platforms, and automated assessmentsystems, such as personalized learning, time efficiency, and enhanced inclusivity, and the potential challenges associated with their use, including academic integrity concerns, cognitive passivity, and digital inequality. The research methodology is based on a comparative analysis of qualitative and quantitative data. The findings indicate that the effective use of AI technologies can enhance the overall effectiveness of the educational process; however, uncontrolled and purposeless use may adversely affect the development of students’ independent and critical thinking skills. The article also proposes strategicrecommendations for minimizing the potential negative consequences associated with AI use and ensuring its pedagogically appropriate integration into the educational process.
keywords: AI in primary and secondary education

papers.title: Trust in AI-mediated electronic commerce: a systematic review and integrative framework
papers.authors: Kruthik Jadhav
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence now stands between merchants and consumers across digital exchange, in chatbots, recommenders, virtual influencers, generative content, service robots and robo-advisors. Consumer reliance on that intermediary is shaped in part by trust. This review synthesises 166 studies in which trust or calibrated reliance is explicitly measured, manipulated or theorised, screened from 7,606 records under PRISMA 2020, with 45 trust-adjacent studies reported separately. Coding what is trusted shows three referents, the AI agent, the deploying merchant and the platform-institutional system, distributed non-randomly across applications. Formal testing finds no detectable association between the direction of the anthropomorphism effect and either stakes or referent, a provisional association between disclosure direction and stakes, and a strong association between reporting any boundary condition and experimental design. The resulting framework links referent, mechanism, boundary condition, trust and reliance state, outcome and repair, and reframes electronic commerce design around calibrated reliance rather than maximal trust.

papers.title: Rethinking Corporate Decision-Making for Corporate Financial Sustainability: A Critical Literature Review and Future Research Agenda
papers.authors: Zulkiffly Baharom
papers.abstract: Corporate financial sustainability (CFS) has become a defining performance criterion for firms amid volatile capital markets and stakeholder scrutiny, yet the literature linking corporate decision-making to CFS remains fragmented across disciplinary silos. This review evaluates how investment, financing, dividend, risk management, and resource allocation decisions shape financial sustainability and identifies assumptions and limitations that constrain the field. Following a critical review protocol, 152 records were retrieved from the Web of Science using a Boolean string that combined corporate/managerial/financial decision terms with financial sustainability, resilience, and stability outcome terms, and was restricted to English-language articles (2004–2026) in Economics, Business, Finance, and Management. Of these, 110 records with complete metadata were retained for synthesis. The corpus clusters around five decision domains: analytical/quantitative diagnostics, behavioural/cognitive influences, governance and ownership, digital/AI-enabled decision support, and institutional/crisis-context decision-making, but is marked by definitional inconsistency, cross-sectional/single-country design reliance, sparse theory, and an integrity concern illustrated by one retracted study. The review is bound by its search string, database, and language restrictions; it calls for re-conceptualizing CFS as a multi-level, decision-contingent construct. Managers and boards should treat sustainability-oriented decision-making as an integrated portfolio problem, with ownership and governance quality as boundary conditions. The review offers an integrative framework that links five decision domains to CFS through literacy, transparency, and intellectual-capital mechanisms, moderated by ownership, governance, and digital capability, and provides a grounded agenda for future research.

papers.title: AI TRANSFROMATION IN E- COMMERVE: UNLOCKING BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
papers.authors: Ms S. BABITHA THARANI
papers.journal: International Journal on Commerce Management Tourism and Home Science
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming e-commerce from a transactional digital channel into an intelligent, predictive, personalized, and increasingly automated business ecosystem. Machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, generative AI, predictive analytics, and AI agents are changing how firms attract customers, manage operations, optimize supply chains, develop products, and make decisions. This paper examines how AI transformation can unlock business opportunities while contributing to sustainable growth. The study adopts a conceptual literature-based approach and synthesizes recent research on AI-driven business models, e-commerce, consumer behaviour, digital transformation, sustainability, and responsible AI. Eight major opportunity areas are identified: intelligent customer experience, AI-enabled marketing, predictive commerce, smart supply chains, intelligent logistics, AI-supported innovation, opportunities for small businesses, and agentic commerce. The paper argues that AI transformation can support sustainable growth through productivity and economic resilience, resource efficiency and environmental performance, and responsible customer and stakeholder value creation. However, privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity threats, workforce disruption, AI-generated misinformation, digital inequality, vendor dependence, and the environmental cost of computing may weaken these benefits. A conceptual framework is proposed linking AI capability, organizational readiness, customer value, operational intelligence, innovation capability, responsible governance, and sustainable growth. The study concludes that successful AI transformation requires a shift from technology adoption to responsible strategic integration.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF AI IN E-COMMERCE: BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
papers.authors: Mr A.MOHANRAJ
papers.journal: International Journal on Commerce Management Tourism and Home Science
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming e-commerce by changing how businesses understand customers, manage operations, personalize services and make decisions. This paper examines the role of AI in e-commerce with particular attention to business opportunities, operational challenges and sustainable development. The study adopts a descriptive and conceptual research approach based on secondary information from academic literature, industry reports and established digital-commerce practices. The paper discusses major applications of AI including product recommendation systems, conversational chatbots, customer analytics, demand forecasting, fraud detection, dynamic pricing, inventory management and digital marketing. These applications can improve customer experience, reduce operational costs, increase efficiency and support faster managerial decisions. At the same time, the adoption of AI creates challenges related to data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, transparency, employment concerns and the cost of implementing advanced technologies. The study further highlights the sustainability potential of AI through demand prediction, optimized logistics, reduced inventory waste, paperless transactions and resource-efficient business processes. The paper argues that responsible AI adoption requires strong data governance, ethical standards, employee skills, transparent algorithms and continuous monitoring. Sustainable e-commerce will therefore depend not only on technological innovation but also on responsible business practices that balance profitability, customer trust, social responsibility and environmental objectives.

papers.title: AI Readiness, Perceived Utility, and Professional Integration among Medical Technologists in Cavite: A Socio-Technical Study
papers.authors: Honeylet O. Arancon, Maria Teresa F. Mateo, Canary Anne B. Cantuba, Gallardo C. Dalhag, Rendix Rey A. Catindig, Jamilah Baragona
papers.journal: International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies
papers.abstract: This study assessed the levels of AI readiness, perceived utility, and professional integration of artificial intelligence among medical technologists in selected clinical and hospital laboratories in Cavite and examined the relationships among these variables. Grounded in a socio-technical perspective that integrates the Technology Acceptance Model, the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory, the research employed a descriptive-correlational design. One hundred licensed medical technologists were selected through purposive sampling according to predefined inclusion criteria. AI readiness was measured with the Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness Scale for Medical Students, perceived utility with the Professional Impact subscale of the Shinners Artificial Intelligence Perception questionnaire, and professional integration with items adapted from the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Spearman’s rank-order correlation. Respondents demonstrated high levels of AI readiness (mean = 3.60) and perceived utility (mean = 3.64), indicating adequate knowledge, technical skills, and positive perceptions toward AI use in laboratory practice. Professional integration was also rated high (mean = 3.61), although AI remained only moderately embedded in routine workflows and many respondents were neutral regarding the actual extent of use. Correlation analyses revealed very weak, non-significant relationships among the three constructs, indicating that individual readiness and favorable perceptions did not translate into greater professional integration. The findings suggest that organizational and contextual factors—such as institutional support, infrastructure, and policy implementation—play a more decisive role in AI adoption than individual-level attributes alone. The study recommends structured, hands-on AI training programs tailored to laboratory practice, clear institutional policies and protocols for incorporating AI outputs into diagnostic workflows, and future research employing probability sampling, multi-regional samples, and longitudinal designs. The research contributes to Sustainable Development Goal 3 by supporting improved diagnostic capacity and laboratory-enabled clinical decision-making, and to Sustainable Development Goal 9 by examining the conditions required for sustainable adoption of innovative health technologies. It advances public-health and institutional sustainability by clarifying the socio-technical determinants that enable resilient, digitally enabled laboratory services in resource-constrained settings.
keywords: Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology

papers.title: Analysis of major depressive disorder with EEG signals using adaptive signal processing and machine learning techniques
papers.authors: Fatma Lati̇foğlu, Sabrına TURTUROVA, Fırat Orhanbulucu
papers.journal: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
papers.abstract: Background and Objective: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a significant mental health issue that negatively affects individuals' quality of life. In this study, an adaptive signal processing and machine learning-based approach was developed for the intelligent diagnosis of MDD through electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Methods: The Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT) methods were applied to EEG data from 26 MDD patients and 29 healthy control subjects using a limited number of EEG channels obtained from the frontal region, thereby decomposing the signals into sub-frequency bands. Frequency and statistical features were extracted from the raw and decomposed EEG signals. The LASSO algorithm was used for feature selection, and classification was performed using four different machine learning models. Results: The results obtained show that adaptive signal processing methods significantly improve performance compared to raw EEG analysis. In particular, the VMD & artificial neural network (ANN) combination emerged as the most successful model. This model demonstrated superior classification performance compared to other models, with 96.66% accuracy, 98.60% AUC, and 96.72% F1 score values. Furthermore, the decision mechanism of this model was examined in detail using SHAP analysis, and potential biomarkers that could guide clinical decision-making processes in MDD diagnosis were identified. Conclusion: In this context, the findings obtained in the proposed study significantly contribute to improving early diagnosis processes and developing automated diagnosis systems, providing a solid foundation for the development of computer-based diagnostic tools that will strengthen clinical decision support mechanisms.

papers.title: Vibrotactile transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) during working memory: convergent electrophysiological evidence for cortical efficiency
papers.authors: Gansheng Tan, Phillip Demarest, Tatiana Kardashina, Josh Adams, Jon Timothy Willie, Jarod L. Roland, Jenna L. Gorlewicz, Peter Brunner, Eric C. Leuthardt
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Working memory, the cognitive ability to maintain and manipulate a finite amount of information, is fundamental in reasoning, learning, and decision-making. Working memory erodes in conditions from Alzheimer’s disease to stroke to healthy aging. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a promising neuromodulation method for improving working memory. By stimulating the auricular branch of the vagus nerve, taVNS is thought to engage ascending arousal systems such as the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine (LC-NE) system. However, the physiological link between LC-NE system modulation via taVNS and improved working memory remains largely unknown. This mechanistic gap limits the rational optimization of the stimulation protocol and the identification of the cognitive functions and patient populations that are likely to benefit. Objective We test two competing hypotheses for how taVNS may improve working memory: sensory amplification or enhancement of cortical efficiency. The sensory-amplification hypothesis predicts increased cortical responses to stimuli, whereas the cortical-efficiency hypothesis predicts reduced cortical responses. Methods Twenty healthy adults completed N-back working memory tasks during three counterbalanced sessions: baseline, active vibrotactile taVNS (vtaVNS), and sham stimulation, while we simultaneously recorded electroencephalography, electrocardiography, eye-tracking, and behavioral responses. To study the effect of vtaVNS on neuronal activity, we also recruited 20 patients with epilepsy undergoing invasive monitoring. Of these, 19 fully completed the spatial working-memory task. We quantified cortical responses to visual stimuli using event-related potentials (ERPs) in scalp EEG and high-gamma activity in intracranial local field potentials. To examine prediction of the cortical-efficiency hypothesis, we further explored the effect of vtaVNS on distance to criticality and heartbeat-evoked potentials. Results Active vtaVNS reduced both scalp-recorded visual ERP and high-gamma response in temporal cortices, relative to sham stimulation. Moreover, smaller visual event-related potentials were associated with successful encoding during the most demanding working-memory condition (i.e., 4-back task). Exploratory analyses showed that vtaVNS shifted cortical dynamics closer to criticality. Conclusion Our results converge on the conclusion that vtaVNS does not uniformly amplify cortical responses to external stimuli. Instead, vtaVNS enhances cortical efficiency, supporting more effective allocation of cognitive resources between exteroceptive and mnemonic processes. These findings provide a framework for predicting when taVNS will be most beneficial and for optimizing stimulation protocols across cognitive and clinical applications. Highlights Consistent visual event-related potential in human subjects during an N-back working memory task Vibrotactile taVNS reduced stimulus-evoked cortical responses in both scalp EEG and intracranial high-gamma activity (70-150 Hz). Reduced visual event-related potentials are associated with successful encoding in the 4-back task. Vibrotactile taVNS shifted cortical dynamics toward a near-critical regime.

papers.title: Nutritional awareness, eating behaviour, body mass index, and estimated resting metabolic rate in physical education students: A descriptive, analytical and correlational study
papers.authors: Abdelnaser A. Qadumi, Rawn A. Qadumi, Ali Qadoume, Mahmoud Alatrash, Rawand K. Qutob, Sulaiman H. Amad, Mohammed A. Qadoumi, Qais M. Nairat, Abdelrahim K Qaddoum, Hala M. Jarrar
papers.abstract: Abstract Background University life can influence food choice even among physically active students. This study examined nutritional awareness, emotional, external, and restrained eating, body mass index (BMI), and estimated resting metabolic rate (RMR) in physical education students, and assessed differences by sex and academic level. Methods A descriptive, analytical and correlational design was used. The sample included 160 physical education students (95 women and 65 men; mean age 20.42 ± 1.53 years) from An-Najah National University. Nutritional awareness was assessed with a 15-item scale, and eating behaviour with the 33-item Dutch Eating Behavior Questionnaire. BMI was calculated from measured height and body mass, and RMR was estimated using an equation developed for athletes. Correlations, group comparisons, robust interaction models, and hierarchical regression were applied. Results Nutritional awareness was high (3.73 ± 0.81), whereas emotional (3.11 ± 1.18), external (3.20 ± 0.95), and restrained eating (3.25 ± 1.11) were moderate. Higher awareness was associated with less emotional (r = -0.617) and external eating (r = -0.652), but greater restrained eating (r = 0.644; all q < 0.001). These associations remained after adjustment. Men reported more external eating, while women reported more restrained eating. Eating patterns also varied by academic level. BMI and estimated RMR showed weaker and less consistent associations with eating behaviour. Conclusions Nutritional awareness was closely associated with reported eating behaviour, whereas BMI and estimated RMR were less informative. Sex and academic-level differences suggest that nutrition education for physical education students may be more useful when adapted to specific behavioural patterns. The findings represent associations and group differences and do not establish causal relationships.

papers.title: REM sleep infraslow rhythms correlate with neuropsychiatric symptom severity
papers.authors: Lézio Soares Bueno-Júnior, Peyton T. Wickham, Carolyn E. Jones, Miranda M. Lim, Brendon O. Watson
papers.abstract: Abstract Study objectives Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep is commonly divided into phasic and tonic substates based on higher and lower oculomotor activity, respectively. Our previous study described an alternative framework in which REM temporal structure forms a continuum of infraslow rhythms (∼0.01 Hz) across brain and body physiology. We now ask whether these infraslow rhythms vary with neuropsychiatric symptoms, given the long-standing but still inconsistent links between REM and mood- or trauma-related disorders. Methods Using a cross-sectional polysomnographic dataset from male veterans, we examined 59 participants for correlations between REM infraslow rhythms and neuropsychiatric symptom scores, excluding participants with moderate/severe apnea. Results Oscillations in REM respiratory rate, but not cardiac rate or electroencephalogram beta power, showed higher infraslow frequencies in participants with multiple symptoms, including posttraumatic stress, pain, anxiety, depression, and cognitive difficulties. No significant correlations were found between these symptoms and conventional REM metrics (e.g., REM density, latency and duration). To further examine REM beyond phasic/tonic binarization, we analyzed the timing between oculomotor activity and infraslow oscillations. Eye movements occurred preferentially during periods of high respiratory rate, low beta power and intermediate cardiac rate, with no changes in these temporal relationships across symptom severity. Conclusions Neuropsychiatric associations with REM infraslow rhythms spanned multiple symptom domains but were physiologically specific, with respiratory rate oscillations representing the strongest readout of symptom burden. Furthermore, REM infraslow cycles across brain and body were differentially aligned with eye movements: a temporal pattern that may serve as a physiological target for neuropsychiatric and mechanistic research. Statement of significance Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep has long been studied in relation to neuropsychiatric conditions, but traditional measures of the timing and duration of REM episodes have shown limited consistency for symptom tracking. This study addresses this gap by highlighting a less explored physiological feature within REM episodes: minute-scale, or infraslow, rhythms in respiratory and cardiac rate, as well as oculomotor and brain activity. We report that REM infraslow oscillations, particularly in respiratory rate, occur at higher frequency in participants with worse trauma/mood symptoms and cognitive difficulties. This work is evidence of a possible new REM sleep-based biomarker for multiple diseases.

papers.title: Proteomic Signatures Capture Environmental Exposures Across Diverse Populations
papers.authors: Yon Ho Jee, Kristin Tsuo, Sophie Parsa, M. Austin Argentieri, Shakson Isaac, Amanda Elliott, Raymond Kenney Walters, Evin M. Padhi, Elizabeth Kiernan, Lee Lichtenstein, Michael E. Talkowski, Stephen B. Montgomery, Niall J. Lennon, Chirag J. Patel, Konrad J. Karczewski, Mark J. Daly, Alicia R. Martin
papers.abstract: Abstract Environmental exposures shape disease risk, but the generalizability of circulating protein-based readouts of exposures across diverse populations remains unknown. Using plasma proteomic profiles of 5,416 proteins in 10,043 participants from the All of Us Research Program, we evaluated associations with and composite scores of 100+ exposures, spanning adiposity, air pollution, ambient temperature, and substance use. We find that proteomic exposure signatures are largely consistent across populations and socioeconomic strata, with <1% of proteins showing significant cross-population heterogeneity, which included BMI as an exception, with leptin being the most heterogeneous association. Population-specific leptin trajectories adiposity, together with residual leptin-type 2 diabetes associations after BMI adjustment, revealed sex-specific metabolic risk not captured by BMI alone. Aggregated protein scores were largely exposure-specific, but substance-use scores showed cross-prediction and SES scores were broadly associated. PM 2.5 protein scores captured within-region exposure variation and outperformed geographic and socioeconomic correlates, but spatial confounders remain embedded within protein-environment associations. Scores trained in UK Biobank transferred to All of Us for biologically proximal exposures, supporting cross-biobank portability. These findings establish plasma proteomics as a scalable framework for exposure measurement across diverse populations, while underscoring that responsible applications require careful consideration of biological context, social patterning, and cohort structure.

papers.title: Genotype-dependent behavioral signatures of opioid withdrawal revealed by automated behavioral quantification
papers.authors: Jacob A. Beierle, Gautam S. Sabnis, Vivek Kumar
papers.abstract: Abstract Opioid withdrawal drives continued opioid use in opioid use disorder (OUD), which affected an estimated 4.8 million Americans in 2024. However, only one non-opioid medication is FDA-approved for withdrawal treatment, and there is great need for more diverse treatment options. Mice are powerful models to study opioid withdrawal because they allow for controlled drug and environmental exposure, express OUD-relevant phenotypes, and provide access to withdrawal-relevant tissue at exact time points. However, mouse models are hindered by their over reliance on a single genetic background (C57BL/6J). Using a single background risks limiting the translatability of preclinical studies as they are projected into genetically diverse human populations. Inferring withdrawal intensity in mice typically relies on single behaviors or indexes of behaviors, and applying these approaches across mouse genetic diversity faces a critical challenge: differing withdrawal responses could either encode differences in withdrawal severity, or differences in withdrawal-evoked behaviors independent of severity. To overcome this limitation, a more comprehensive assessment of opioid withdrawal behaviors across mouse genetic diversity is needed. Here we leverage computer vision and machine learning to automate the simultaneous quantification of many mouse behaviors during opioid withdrawal in eight diverse strains of mice. We reveal that all eight strains exhibit withdrawal-evoked behaviors, and these behaviors are sufficient to identify the withdrawal state of the mouse. However, the effect of withdrawal on individual behaviors or indexes of behaviors is not uniform across genetic diversity, and extending methods tuned in one strain risks misclassifying withdrawal in others. Finally our approach was able to distinguish graded withdrawal intensity, as defined by opioid exposure within 3 of 4 strains tested. We therefore conclude that opioid withdrawal behavior is profoundly shaped by genetic background, but withdrawal severity can nonetheless be established within a background. Combining automated computer-vision phenotyping with genotype-aware modeling provides a scalable path toward genetically informed withdrawal assessment in diverse mouse populations, with the ultimate goal of identifying the genetic and biological networks that modulate opioid withdrawal and may represent new targets for treating opioid use disorder.

papers.title: Distilling Trial-Level EEG Variability into Participant Representations: Neurophysiologically Constrained Graph Learning in ADHD
papers.authors: Rishabh Tiwari, Christian Beste, Negin Gholamipourbarough
papers.abstract: Abstract Extracting stable individual-level representations from noisy and variable trial-wise EEG remains a major challenge in computational cognitive neuroscience. We developed a spatiotemporal graph attention network to analyze Go/NoGo EEG from children and adolescents with and without ADHD. The framework combines ERP-informed temporal windows, phase-synchrony graph priors, and trial-to-participant transfer learning, making both information routing and representation geometry explicitly testable. The model learned reproducible attention trajectories, yet ADHD and control participants did not differ reliably in spatial attention allocation. Instead, group-related structure emerged in compact participant-level embeddings that distilled trial-level variability and retained discriminative information beyond convolutional representations. Performance exceeded a convolutional neural network comparison, but the central advance is methodological: neurophysiologically constrained graph learning can reveal where diagnostically relevant information emerges within the analytical pipeline. This provides a framework for developing auditable cognitive-neurophysiological markers of neurodevelopmental variation.

papers.title: Individualized Gabor Flicker for Well-Tolerated Neural Entrainment During Working Memory
papers.authors: Clément Blanc, Frédéric Dehais, Sébastien Scannella
papers.abstract: Rhythmic visual stimulation offers a non-invasive means of modulating oscillatory brain activity, but conventional flicker may induce considerable visual discomfort. We developed an individualized Gabor flicker stimulation designed to balance neural entrainment and tolerability. In Experiment 1, thirty-four participants passively viewed Plain and Gabor flickers presented at their individual alpha frequency (IAF), IAF - 2 Hz, or IAF + 2 Hz, and at threshold-adjusted or full intensity. Steady-state visual evoked potential signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was highest at IAF and increased with intensity. Plain and Gabor flickers produced comparable overall SNR, but Gabor flicker was rated as substantially more comfortable and less mentally fatiguing, with stimulation at IAF providing the most favorable balance between neural entrainment and tolerability. In Experiment 2, the optimized stimulation parameters were applied during a retro-cue working memory task using individualized theta and alpha frequency flickers. Stimulation increased SNR and inter-trial phase coherence relative to a non rhythmic Natural condition. No behavioral benefit was observed in the full sample. However, an exploratory subgroup analysis indicated higher accuracy with theta stimulation of cued representations and alpha stimulation of uncued representations than in the Natural condition among participants who showed limited baseline retro-cue benefits. These findings show that individualized Gabor flicker can provide robust and well-tolerated neural entrainment during passive viewing and working memory retention, although its behavioral effects may vary across individuals according to their cognitive performance.

papers.title: Spontaneous slow waves index multiple dimensions of recovery in Disorders of Consciousness
papers.authors: Alessia Ruyant-Belabbas, Augustin Boullet, Dragana Manasova, Arthur Le Coz, Mélanie Denis-Valente, François‐Xavier Lejeune, Jacobo Diego Sitt, Lionel Naccache, Benjamin Rohaut, Thomas Andrillon
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Whether and how residual awareness is expressed in patients with Disorders of Consciousness (DoC) depends on the severity of brain damage and the transient functional state of the cortex at assessment. Classically, DoC are associated with electroencephalographic (EEG) slowing, marked by high-amplitude slow waves, even during the day. Yet, slow waves are also a hallmark of healthy sleep, where they are thought to serve restorative functions and to help maintain network homeostasis. Here, we asked whether slow waves in DoC can provide insights into the severity of cortical dysfunction or, conversely, into the preservation of residual awareness and recovery potential, by characterizing their spatial, temporal and morphological properties. We analyzed 256-channel EEG recorded during the ‘Local-Global’ auditory paradigm in 236 DoC patients, including 123 in Unresponsive Wakefulness Syndrome (UWS), 62 in a Minimally Conscious State minus (MCS-) and 29 in MCS plus (MCS+). High-amplitude slow waves were detected as local events, and their density, amplitude and slopes were quantified scalp-wide and channel-wise, by mean level and temporal variability across the recording. Slow-wave features were related to concurrent (Coma Recovery Scale-Revised - CRS-R, ‘Local-Global’ paradigm) and follow-up (one-year Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended - GOS-E) assessments of consciousness and functional recovery. Associations with MRI-derived measures of cortical integrity and structural connectivity, and differences between anoxic and traumatic etiologies, were also examined. Slow waves were more frequent in less severe DoC patients (i.e., MCS) compared to UWS. Slow-wave slopes were also steeper frontally and increased at a faster rate in patients exhibiting higher levels of consciousness and/or markers of conscious access during the ‘Local-Global’ paradigm. More frequent and steeper slow waves at baseline further predicted recovery of consciousness and of functional independence at one year. At the individual level, slow-wave features classified states of consciousness above chance (AUC = 0.62 and 0.71 for MCS- and MCS+ versus UWS), whereas outcome prediction remained modest (0.56-0.58). These clinical associations had a structural basis: slow-wave occurrence was greater after traumatic than anoxic injury and scaled with the integrity of subcortico-cortical projection fibers and consciousness-related cortical networks. Contrary to the classical view of delta activity as a non-specific marker of impaired consciousness, prominent spontaneous slow waves indexed behavioral and neurophysiological signs of awareness and better recovery. Beyond reflecting a propensity for pathological bistability, they may also signal the integrity of the networks required to generate them, together with their residual capacity for dynamic regulation. Highlights Spontaneous slow waves were detected as discrete local events in 236 DoC patients, moving beyond time-averaged spectral measures of cortical slowing. Slow-wave properties carried diagnostic information about the state of consciousness, whether defined behaviorally (CRS-R) or neurophysiologically (conscious access to auditory information in ‘Local-Global’ ERP paradigm). Slow wave frequency and slope during the acute phase in the ICU predicted improvement of consciousness state and recovery of functional independence at one year. Within-session ‘fatigue-like’ temporal modulation of slow waves increased with the level of consciousness recovery, being more pronounced in MCS+ than in UWS and MCS-patients. Slow-wave expression scaled with subcortico-cortical fibers and cortical network integrity, and was greater after traumatic than anoxic injury, suggesting they signal preserved network integrity rather than damage alone.

papers.title: Online Teaching and Learning in South Asian Higher Education: Challenges and Emerging Opportunities for Teacher Education and Physical Education
papers.authors: nbspDr. Vikas Kundu
papers.journal: International Journal of Education Pedagogy and Psychology
papers.abstract: Abstract Online teaching and learning has become a permanent component of higher education, yet its educational value depends on more than access to digital platforms. This critical integrative review examines the development of online higher education in South Asia and focuses specifically on its implications for teacher education and physical education. Drawing on recent regional reports, peer-reviewed reviews, policy documents and foundational theories of online learning, the review synthesises evidence concerning digital inequality, faculty competence, learner engagement, assessment, academic integrity, artificial intelligence, accessibility and quality assurance. The analysis shows that South Asian institutions have moved from pandemic-era emergency remote teaching toward a more complex phase of sustainable digital transformation, but progress remains uneven across countries and institutions. Teacher education requires explicit development of digital pedagogical competence, authentic assessment and supervised professional practice, while physical education requires a discipline-sensitive blended model because embodied, psychomotor and safety-related outcomes cannot be fully reproduced online. Generative AI offers emerging opportunities for personalised learning, feedback, multilingual support and professional development, but it also introduces risks related to privacy, bias, academic integrity and over-reliance. The review proposes a Context-Responsive Online Teaching and Learning Framework built around infrastructure readiness, pedagogical alignment, faculty competence, learner support, inclusive access, authentic assessment, discipline-sensitive design and responsible innovation. The article argues that the future of online higher education in South Asia should not be defined by the quantity of technology adopted, but by the quality, equity and educational purpose with which technology is integrated. Keywords: Online Higher Education; South Asia; Teacher Education; Physical Education; Generative Artificial Intelligence. Keywords: Teacher Education; Physical Education; Keywords: Online Higher Education; South Asia; Generative Artificial Intelligence.

papers.title: Enhancing Teacher Effectiveness with Artificial Intelligence- A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Dr. B. Swathi
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education represents a transformative shift in how teaching and learning are conceptualized and delivered.This research article examines the role of AI in enhancing teacher effectiveness across multiple dimensions including personalized instruction, administrative efficiency, assessment practices, and professional development.Through a comprehensive review of current literature and analysis of empirical studies, this article explores how AI technologies such as intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning platforms, automated grading systems, and AI-powered analytics are reshaping pedagogical practices.The findings indicate that AI can significantly augment teacher capabilities by providing data-driven insights, reducing administrative burden, enabling differentiated instruction, and supporting evidence-based decision-making.However, the implementation of AI in education also presents challenges including ethical considerations, technological barriers, teacher training needs, and concerns about equity and access.This article concludes that while AI holds substantial promise for enhancing teacher effectiveness, successful integration requires careful consideration of pedagogical principles, investment in teacher professional development, attention to ethical implications, and a commitment to maintaining the irreplaceable human elements of teaching.The research underscores that AI should be viewed as a tool to empower rather than replace teachers, amplifying their expertise and enabling them to focus on the creative, emotional, and interpersonal aspects of education that remain uniquely human.

papers.title: Inteligencia artificial generativa y personalización del aprendizaje en educación superior: una revisión sistemática de la literatura (2019-2025)”
papers.authors: Wilson Javier Romero Berrones, Mónica Romero Berrones, Jorge Acosta Toledo
papers.journal: Revista internacional de Investigación y Desarrollo Global
papers.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has transformed the way higher education institutions conceive the personalization of learning, understood as the adaptation of content, pace and formative trajectories to the individual characteristics of students. Although the literature on artificial intelligence in education is abundant, gaps remain regarding an updated synthesis that specifically articulates GenAI, and not only predictive AI or classic tutoring systems, with personalization processes at the university level. Objective. This systematic review aimed to analyze the evidence available between 2019 and 2025 on the applications, benefits, ethical challenges and pedagogical frameworks associated with the use of GenAI to personalize learning in higher education. Method. The PRISMA 2020 guidelines were followed (Page et al., 2021). The search was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, ScienceDirect and Dialnet, using Boolean search strings that combined terms related to generative artificial intelligence, personalization and higher education, restricted to the 2019-2025 period and to documents in Spanish and English. After screening by title, abstract and full text, and applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, a final corpus of primary studies was assembled and analyzed through a thematic synthesis matrix. Results. The evidence was organized into four categories: GenAI applications (intelligent tutors, adaptive content generation, automated feedback and dynamic learning pathways), benefits (perceived improvement in performance, greater motivation, teaching efficiency and scalability), challenges (algorithmic bias, privacy, technological dependence, the digital divide and academic integrity) and emerging ethical and pedagogical frameworks oriented toward a human-centered implementation. Conclusions. GenAI offers significant potential to scale the personalization of learning in higher education, but its responsible implementation requires institutional governance frameworks, teacher training in critical digital competencies, and specific safeguards for equity and privacy. Implications for educational practice and future research lines oriented toward longitudinal empirical studies are identified.

papers.title: Anxious at the Digital Threshold: Artificial Intelligence Anxiety, Digital Literacy, and Entrepreneurial Intention among Indonesian Return Migrant Workers
papers.authors: Akhmad Darmawan, Fatmah Bagis, Afid Setiabudi
papers.abstract: Digitalisation and artificial intelligence are reshaping the economies to which migrant workers return, yet little is known about how returnees perceive and prepare for these changes. This study analyses the entrepreneurial intention, digital literacy, and readiness for artificial intelligence of Indonesian return migrant workers and tests the relationship between artificial intelligence anxiety and entrepreneurial intention. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among return migrant workers in Kebumen Regency, Central Java, as an output of the partnership between the Migrant Resources Center of Universitas Muhammadiyah Purwokerto and PT Bryna Sukses Abadi, a labour placement company. Data were analysed with one-sample t-tests, Pearson correlation, and descriptive analysis of business-relevant digital tasks. Return migrants hold an entrepreneurial intention above the neutral point, while their digital literacy lies below it. Their self-reported readiness for artificial intelligence is not significantly below neutral, although their actual ability to use artificial intelligence tools is very limited. Digital capability declines steeply from basic smartphone use towards online selling and artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence anxiety is negatively and significantly related to entrepreneurial intention. The study introduces artificial intelligence anxiety into research on return migration and extends social cognitive theory by positioning technology anxiety as an emotional barrier to entrepreneurial intention among migrant workers. It argues for reintegration and pre-departure programmes that combine practical digital training with confidence building.

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Marketing Effectiveness, Customer Engagement, and Marketing Personalization: Perceptions of Pakistani Marketing Professionals
papers.authors: Ashi Zeeshan
papers.journal: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
papers.abstract: The present study focused on measuring the perceptions of marketing professionals about the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on marketing practices specifically AI adoption, customers engagement, marketing personalization and campaign effectiveness. A quantitative survey research design was used. The data was collected from 166 purposively selected marketing professionals from Lahore, Pakistan. A structured questionnaire was used to measure the perception of participants of the study. Depending on the categorical and ordinal nature of the variables, descriptive statistics, association measures based on non-parametric tests and ordinal logistic regression were used. The results revealed that the exposure to AI was moderate to high for most of the respondents and the extent of the adoption by the organisations was mostly moderate to high. In general, AI was seen to be effective in boosting customer engagement and optimisation of campaigns. The strongest statistical result was for personalisation, where the likelihood of achieving better personalised marketing experiences was greatly predicted by the higher level of AI usage with an odds ratio of 4.78 (p < .001). The perceived marketing effectiveness was not statistically significantly predicted by the use of AI. Key concerns during implementation included the issues of data privacy, adapting to a workforce, transparency and algorithmic bias. In addition, personalisation, targeting, automation, predictive decision making and AI agents emerged as the biggest present and future effects of AI on marketing through the thematic analysis of the open-ended answers. papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Interoperability for Cross-Chain Provenance
papers.authors: Ruth B. Rodriguez
papers.abstract: The global artisanal goods market faces significant challenges related to product authenticity, verifiable provenance, and efficient market access for independent creators. This paper presents a novel omnichannel marketplace platform designed to resolve these systemic deficiencies through the synergistic integration of advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) and decentralized blockchain technologies. The platform enhances market transparency and fosters buyer trust via an AI-powered recommendation engine and art intelligence that incorporates trust ratings and a blockchain system for verifiable provenance tracking using Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs). Crucially, the platform incorporates neuroscientific principles into its design, leveraging neuroaesthetics to optimize the presentation of artistic style and cultural significance, and neuromarketing to structure the artisan's narrative for maximal perceived value and emotional resonance. A key innovation is the Machine Learning (ML)-Driven Interoperability component, which secures and optimizes cross-chain mechanisms, enabling scalable, high-security asset transfer across disparate networks. Initial meta-analytic results suggest that AI recommendations provide an expected conversion rate lift of 15% (Hedges' g = 0.45) compared to non-personalized systems, and ML-enhanced interoperability reduces cross-chain transaction latency by an average of 18% compared to non-optimized bridges. The platform demonstrates high potential for empowering artisans, promoting sustainable artisanal commerce, and establishing a new paradigm for trustworthy e-commerce.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Human Creativity: Revisiting the Normative Foundations of Intellectual Property
papers.authors: Tshimangadzo Donald Mukwevho
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (gen-AI) undermines the traditional foundations of intellectual property (IP) law by challenging long-standing assumptions about creative production. Historically, copyright and patent systems were based on identifiable human creators whose work, talent, character, and intentionality deserved legal protection. However, gen-AI systems, which can generate text, images, music, software code, and other creative outputs, complicate these assumptions. This article contends that gen-AI does not raise new doctrinal issues but instead reveals deeper conflicts within the normative underpinnings of IP law. The article proposes a human-centred IP framework that preserves meaningful protection for human creative agency while recognising the collective nature of creativity in technologically mediated societies.
