Drawing on labour, personality, utilitarian, and democratic culture theories, it demonstrates how AI disrupts the relationship between human creativity and IP protection. The article first examines the philosophical foundations of IP law, then analyses how gen-AI disrupts traditional concepts of authorship, originality, and creative agency, evaluates potential normative responses, and proposes a human-centred framework for regulating technologically mediated creativity.

papers.title: Inteligencia artificial en la ingenieria de software
papers.authors: Samuel Salazar
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Language Modeling (LLM) have taken on a significant role in software engineering, acting as a universal translator between natural language and technical specifications. These tools help optimize processes such as requirements engineering, test automation, and code generation, among others, allowing for valuable time savings in agile production environments. However, implementation can lead to problems such as the emergence of "hallucinations," increased code complexity, and cybersecurity risks that require human oversight. In education, AI assistants encourage competency-based learning, enabling students to develop their logic through prompt engineering and structured reasoning. The correct use of these technologies is essential for improving the resilience and maintainability of modern software.

papers.title: Evaluating the Capacity of Artificial Intelligence to Replicate Human Emotional Expression
papers.authors: Rodoshi Paul
papers.journal: Journal of Computer Science and Information Technology
papers.abstract: This essay discusses the ability of artificial intelligence (AI) to mimic human expression of emotions. Although AI systems have advanced greatly into replicating the external presentation of human emotions, including tone, facial expressions, and textual responses, they do not possess the inner knowledge, self-awareness, and personal experiences that motivate genuine human emotions. The paper explores the potential of technology and the ethical, social, and psychological implications of emotional simulations in AI, particularly in the sensitive areas of healthcare, education, and customer care. The study finds that AI has the potential to be an effective instrument in facilitating communication and accessibility, but it cannot substitute the rich, subjective experience of human emotion. There is a need to adopt a balanced approach to the use of AI so that it can be used responsibly and in a way that does not bring about any transparency and makes the users think that AI can truly feel or empathize.

papers.title: Generative AI Usage and Digital Competence as Predictors of Mathematics Teaching Effectiveness among Pre-Service Teachers
papers.authors: Gustav Kwaku Siaw Dompreh, Benjamin Owusu-Sekyere, Ibrahim Arthur, Jones Owusu Ansah
papers.journal: International Social Sciences and Education Journal
papers.abstract: The growing use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in education presents new opportunities for improving mathematics teaching, but its effectiveness may depend on teachers’ ability to use digital technologies critically and appropriately. This study examined Generative AI Usage and Digital Competence as predictors of Mathematics Teaching Effectiveness among pre-service teachers who had completed teaching practice. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, involving 217 Level 400 pre-service teachers from Colleges of Education in the Hohoe Municipality. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale structured questionnaire and analysed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) in SPSS AMOS Version 23. The measurement model demonstrated good fit, while all constructs showed acceptable reliability and validity. The findings revealed that Generative AI Usage significantly and positively predicted Mathematics Teaching Effectiveness (β = 0.181, p = .010). Digital Competence also significantly and positively predicted Mathematics Teaching Effectiveness (β = 0.461, p < .001), with a stronger predictive effect than GenAI Usage. The study concludes that while GenAI can support effective mathematics teaching, digital competence is particularly important for enabling pre-service teachers to evaluate, adapt, and integrate digital resources meaningfully into instruction. Teacher education institutions should therefore promote digital competence development alongside responsible and pedagogically informed use of GenAI in mathematics teacher preparation.

papers.title: Del uso adecuado a la alfabetización algorítmica: análisis documental de la educación superior ecuatoriana
papers.authors: Francisco Xavier Rosero Aulestia, Doris Oviedo Fraga, Alejandro Enrique Meza Romero, Dennis Marcelo Fraga Caiza, Carmen Genoveva Díaz Paredes
papers.journal: Revista Científica de Salud y Desarrollo Humano
papers.abstract: The study analyzes the correspondence between the dimensions of algorithmic literacy and four instruments linked to the Ecuadorian framework of higher education, quality assurance, and artificial intelligence governance, with the purpose of deriving verifiable curricular criteria. A qualitative documentary analysis with directed coding was developed on four texts: the Academic Regime Regulations, the External Evaluation Model for Universities and Polytechnical Schools, the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, and the UNESCO assessment of artificial intelligence readiness for Ecuador. The units were analyzed using eight categories. For each intersection between category and document, three levels of correspondence were applied: absence, implicit formulation, and explicit formulation, complemented by an independent test of curricular operationalization. The Regulation establishes critical reflection, ethical commitment, and informational competencies without identifying algorithmic mediation. The CACES Model incorporates mechanisms for the use of artificial intelligence in the educational model and requires that curricula consider its proper use, but it does not define specific learning outcomes that would allow demonstrating it. The strategy brings together principles of privacy, equity, transparency, responsibility, and human oversight, and UNESCO adds critical and interdisciplinary content. None of the four examined documents translate those guidelines into observable learning outcomes. It is concluded that the Ecuadorian framework presents increasing institutional and regulatory recognition without an equivalent curricular translation, and an architecture organized into recognition, understanding, evaluation, and responsible agency is proposed.

papers.title: Analisis Pengalaman Penggunaan AI dalam Pembelajaran pada Siswa DPIB di SMK Negeri 1 Singosari: Tinjauan Self-Efficacy dan Academic Dishonesty
papers.authors: Rani Wulandari, Fadila Fitria Wulandari, Tri Kuncoro, Muhammad Aris Ichwanto
papers.journal: Jurnal Yudistira Publikasi Riset Ilmu Pendidikan dan Bahasa
papers.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of experience using Artificial Intelligence (AI) on self‑efficacy and academic dishonesty among students in the Building Information Modeling and Design (DPIB) Expertise Program at SMK Negeri 1 Singosari. The study employed a quantitative explanatory approach, with a sample of 103 students selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using SEM‑PLS. The results indicate that experience using AI has a positive and significant effect on self‑efficacy, a negative but insignificant effect on academic dishonesty, and that self‑efficacy has a positive and significant effect on academic dishonesty. These findings emphasize the importance of utilizing AI coupled with digital literacy and ethical awareness in learning. In addition, the study highlights the relevance of integrating technological experience into educational practices, encouraging students to develop confidence, responsibility, and integrity. The implications suggest that schools should design programs that foster ethical digital skills and strengthen students’ readiness for future innovation.

papers.title: Evaluating Students’ Use of Artificial Intelligence-Based Tool in the Learning of Christian Religious Studies Concepts in University of Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Ozioma Odirachimma Okoye
papers.abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving educational landscape, the integration of technology into the learning process has become essential. This is particularly true for disciplines such as Christian Religious Studies, where the exploration of texts, theological concepts, and historical contexts can be both complex and nuanced. The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools offers significant potential to enhance the learning experience for students in this field. Literature tells that artificial intelligence-based tool aids students’ learning and produces better results. The research aims to evaluate students’ use of artificial intelligence-based tool in the learning of Christian Religious studies concepts in university of Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. Two research questions guided the study while two hypotheses were formulated and tested at 0.05 level of significance. The study adopted descriptive survey research design and the population of the study consist of 226 (119 females and 107 males) Christian Religious Studies students of 200 level from Arts Education Department and Religion and Cultural Studies Department of the University of Calabar, 2023/2024 session. Purposive and census sampling techniques were used for the study to select the entire 226 Christian Religious Studies students of 200 level from Arts Education Department and Religion and Cultural Studies Department that constituted the sample. A well validated ‘Students’ Use of Artificial Intelligence-Based Tool (SUAIBTQ) and Learning of Christian Religious Studies Concepts Questionnaire (LCRSCQ) were used to collect the required data. Simple Linear Regression was the statistical tools used for analysis of the data collected. The result of the analysis revealed that there is a significant influence of students’ utilization of ChatGPT AI tool on the learning of Christian Religious studies concepts. Also, there is significant difference in the responses of male and female students on the utilization of ChatGPT AI tool in the learning of Christian Religious studies concepts. Sequel to the findings of this study, it was recommended, among others that Instructors should develop personalized AI-driven instructional strategies that cater to different learning preferences. This may include interactive AI tutors, adaptive assessments, and gamified learning experiences to enhance engagement and comprehension. Keywords: Students’ use of artificial intelligence, Christian Religious studies concepts, University of Calabar

papers.title: Use of generative Artificial Intelligence tools in medical student research projects: An activity system analysis
papers.authors: Jo Hart, Ali Makki, Kellie Charles
papers.abstract: Little is known about how medical students use generative AI in research training or how supervisors respond. Using Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT), this study aimed to characterise how generative AI is reshaping the activity of learning to do research within a mandatory medical student research project, and to identify the contradictions driving that change. AI-use declarations submitted as assessed coursework by two consecutive student cohorts (2024 to 2025; n = 533), and semi-structured interviews with research supervisors (n = 10) at an Australian medical school, were coded inductively by an independent analyst. Themes were mapped onto CHAT elements and examined for contradictions. Reported AI non-use fell from 44% to 19% between cohorts, a difference not explained by project type, enrolment or location. Verification of AI output was the most prominent practice in both cohorts, treated as the condition of AI use. Efficiency was the most consistently stated rationale for AI use, often alongside reports that output was unreliable. Prompt refinement emerged as a competence acquired informally but dependent on disciplinary knowledge. Most supervisors felt unprepared, not only to use the tools but to judge when student use was legitimate, and the two most confident had funded that competence themselves. The primary contradiction lay within the object-motive: the written report, historically a workable proxy for research capability, no longer reliably evidences it. Students generated norms for AI use that lacked institutional standing and were invisible to supervisors, while the programme, responding to student AI use rather than those norms, began remodelling how capability is evidenced, including through oral assessment. Connecting these two processes is the central curricular task, requiring discipline-based AI literacy, forums in which student practice and the rationale for assessment changes are shared, equitable supervisor development, and assessment of reasoning over text production.

papers.title: Minimum Viable Digital Identity Optimization (DIO): From Adversarial Reduction to the Semantic Field Dynamics of Digital Identity
papers.authors: Daniel Beránek
papers.abstract: This paper presents Minimum Viable Digital Identity Optimization (MVDIO), a coarse-grained analytical model developed through an adversarial reduction of the broader Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) framework.The paper distinguishes three levels that are often conflated: the existence of a reconstruction mechanism, the existence of an optimizable digital identity problem, and deliberate DIO intervention. It defines the minimal analytical distinction between a referentially continuous entity, its distributed digital representational state, and the identity reconstruction performed by a human or machine observer.The reduction revises several strong assumptions. Consistency is distinguished from uniformity; divergent reconstructions are not automatically semantic fragmentation; optimization requires a defined observation domain; target reconstructions are constrained by referential continuity and identity-preserving constraints; and semantic vulnerability is treated as a property of robustness and risk rather than as a failure state in itself.The paper then examines where the minimal model reaches its limits. History, statefulness, inertia, reflexivity, and path dependence require a finer-grained description. In this context, the six dimensions of the K6 semantic connectome - Entity, Representation, Interpretation, Trust, Relationship, and Reconstruction - are reconsidered as a candidate model of the synchronous configuration and diachronic dynamics of digital identity.K6 is not presented as a logical consequence of MVDIO, a linear pipeline, or a literal graph of causal nodes. It is proposed as a finer-grained decomposition of the same dynamic object, whose completeness and explanatory independence remain open to further testing.The paper positions DIO in relation to adjacent fields including entity resolution, entity identity information management, identity management, organizational identity and reputation, online personal branding, data doubles, and sensemaking. It concludes with three minimal tests - mechanism, problem, and intervention - and identifies directions for empirical operationalization and falsification. Version status: This Figshare upload reproduces the canonical archival version deposited on Zenodo DOI 10.13140/RG.2.2.10967.43682. Zenodo is the primary archival record and DOI-bearing source for citation. Figshare and ResearchGate are supplementary discovery and access channels. AI disclosure: This paper was developed with AI-assisted adversarial testing, red-team review, and editorial support using ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol), Perplexity, and Gemini Pro 3.1 Preview. All AI outputs were reviewed and selectively revised by the author. The framework, intellectual decisions, and final content remain the sole responsibility of the author.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Health Equity and Health Security in Northern Nigeria: A Scoping Synthesis of Evidence, Health-System Readiness, and A Framework for Responsible Public Health Transformation
papers.authors: Musa Sufi Abdullahi, Adamu Abubakar Gwarzo
papers.journal: Journal of Institute of Africa Higher Education Research and Innovation (IAHERI)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from experimental applications toward practical use in healthcare, public health intelligence, health communication, diagnostics, workforce support and health-system management. Its potential is especially relevant to Northern Nigeria, where substantial public health needs coexist with socioeconomic deprivation, nutrition insecurity, infectious disease threats, maternal and child health inequalities, insecurity, population displacement and uneven health-system capacity. Yet AI readiness and evidence of real-world benefit remain uneven, and poorly governed deployment could reproduce or deepen existing inequities.To synthesise current evidence on the potential contribution of AI to health equity and health security in Northern Nigeria, examine the region’s public health and health-system context, identify opportunities and implementation constraints, and propose an evidence-informed framework for responsible AI-enabled public health transformation.The paper uses a scoping synthesis and policy-framework approach. Peer-reviewed literature and authoritative institutional sources concerning AI, machine learning, digital health, health systems, public health surveillance, nutrition, maternal and child health, ethics and governance were examined, with emphasis on Nigeria, Africa and low- and middle-income countries. Updated contextual evidence was drawn from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, the 2022 Nigeria Multidimensional Poverty Index, Nigeria’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare’s State of Health of the Nation reporting, WHO guidance and recent African evidence. Evidence was synthesised thematically rather than statistically pooled.The literature supports potential applications of AI in disease surveillance, epidemic intelligence, nutrition early warning, maternal and child health risk stratification, multilingual health communication, workforce decision support and resource optimisation. However, evidence from low-resource settings remains dominated by small-scale, research-oriented or externally funded projects, with limited national or state-level implementation evidence. Key constraints include fragmented and incomplete data, interoperability gaps, weak digital infrastructure, limited technical and AI literacy, insufficient local validation, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity and privacy risks, and variable institutional ability to act on AI-generated signals. Current Nigerian policy developments including the National AI Strategy and the Nigeria Data Protection Act provide an emerging governance foundation, but health-sector implementation requires stronger operational mechanisms. AI should be treated as a health-system capability rather than a stand-alone technology. Northern Nigeria would benefit from a problem-first, equity-centred and human-supervised approach that links high-priority public health needs to reliable data, local validation, workforce capability, accountable governance and response capacity. The paper proposes the AI–PUBLIC HEALTH–NIGERIA Framework, alongside a phased implementation roadmap, as a practical architecture for responsible adoption.

papers.title: An AI-Integrated Moodle-Based E-Learning Platform for Youth Leadership Development in Rural Communities
papers.authors: Rike Nursafitri, Hardika Dwi Hermawan, Ahmad Zahy Rashad Handradika, Zakky Muhammad Noor, Taufik Probowasito, Dias Aziz Pramudita, Rochman Hadi Mustofa
papers.abstract: Leadership learning for youth communities currently faces limitations, particularly the lack of a structured, flexible, and easily accessible learning platform. The learning process at Local Heroes Schools still relies on face-to-face meetings and the Zoom platform, thus suboptimally supporting learning effectiveness. This study aims to develop and analyze the feasibility of a Moodle-based Local Heroes School E-Learning platform equipped with an interactive chatbot built on the FastBots.ai platform, developed as a leadership learning medium for Desamind Chapter Devices in various districts in Indonesia. The research method used is Research and Development (R&D) with a 4D development model, which includes the Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate stages; in this study the Disseminate stage was limited in scope to a pilot trial among Desamind Chapter Device users. System testing was conducted through black-box testing by a software engineering expert, validation by media experts and material experts, and user trials using the System Usability Scale (SUS). The results showed that black-box testing on the evaluated scenario achieved a 100% success rate. Media expert validation obtained a score of 93.75%, categorized as Very Feasible, while material expert validation obtained a score of 100%, categorized as Valid. User trials involving 30 respondents produced a mean SUS score of 75.75 (SD = 11.14), categorized as Acceptable, although 40% of respondents rated the platform in the Marginal range. Based on these results, the Moodle-based Local Heroes School E-Learning platform integrated with a FastBots.ai chatbot is feasible for use as a leadership learning medium; however, the incremental contribution of the chatbot specifically, and dissemination beyond this pilot, warrant further study.

papers.title: Human–AI Collaboration in Digital Marketing: Evidence from an Emerging Economy, Somalia
papers.authors: Ibrahim Farah Hilowle
papers.journal: Multidisciplinary Journal of Horseed International University (MJHIU)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing through automation, customer analytics, personalization, and data-driven decision-making. However, empirical evidence on human–AI collaboration in emerging and fragile economies remains limited. This study examined the adoption of human–AI collaboration in digital marketing among businesses in Somalia, identified key barriers to AI adoption, and assessed the association between human–AI collaboration and customer engagement, marketing efficiency, and business growth. The study used a positivist research approach and a quantitative cross-sectional survey design. Data were collected from 86 business owners, marketing managers, digital marketing specialists, and ICT/technology officers using purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman's rank correlation, and multiple linear regression. Respondents reported frequent use of AI-assisted content creation, customer analytics, marketing automation, social media management, and AI-supported decision-making. The principal barriers were limited technical skills, limited infrastructure, implementation costs, data privacy concerns, and organizational resistance to change. Spearman's correlations indicated positive associations between human–AI collaboration and customer engagement (ρ = .684), marketing efficiency (ρ =.725), and business growth (ρ = .658), all reported at p < .001. Regression models explained 50.7% of the variance in customer engagement, 54.9% in marketing efficiency, and 46.4% in business growth. Human–AI collaboration was positively associated with each outcome after controlling for organizational size and industry sector. Because the study is cross-sectional and based on a purposive sample, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. The results highlight the importance of combining AI capabilities with human judgment, creativity, contextual knowledge, and responsible data practices in Somalia's digital marketing environment.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education Bridging or Widening the Digital Divide in Developing Countries
papers.authors: Wu Lingyi, Fahmi Fadhl Al-Hosaini
papers.journal: Global Social Science and Humanities Journal.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming education through personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, automated assessment, generative content creation, learning analytics, academic research support, and educational administration. Although these technologies offer significant opportunities for improving educational quality and accessibility, their implications for developing countries remain complex. Educational systems in low- and middle-income countries frequently operate under constraints that include inadequate digital infrastructure, unreliable connectivity, limited financial resources, insufficient teacher preparation, linguistic diversity, and unequal access to technology. Consequently, AI has the potential both to reduce longstanding educational inequalities and to create a new layer of digital exclusion. This article provides an integrative review of the influence of AI on education in developing countries, with particular attention to teaching, learning, assessment, higher education, administration, inclusion, and educational equity. It synthesizes recent academic literature and international policy reports, with particular emphasis on developments associated with generative AI since 2022. The review identifies personalized learning, expanded access to educational expertise, teacher support, multilingual assistance, administrative efficiency, and improved accessibility as important opportunities. However, connectivity inequalities, affordability, algorithmic bias, inadequate AI literacy, academic integrity concerns, privacy risks, cultural and linguistic underrepresentation, and excessive dependence on automated systems present substantial challenges. To explain these competing effects, the article proposes an Inclusive AI in Education Framework in which infrastructure, affordability, human capacity, localization, governance, and pedagogical integration determine whether AI contributes to greater educational inclusion or reinforces existing inequalities. The paper argues that the educational value of AI in developing countries will ultimately depend less on the availability of sophisticated technologies than on the institutional and societal capacity to deploy them equitably, responsibly, and in accordance with local educational priorities.

papers.title: HUMAN–AI COLLABORATION IN HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT: THE IMPACT OF GENERATIVE AI ADOPTION ON EMPLOYEE PRODUCTIVITY, JOB SATISFACTION AND TRUST IN AI-MEDIATED HR DECISIONS
papers.authors: Ahsan Ali Dime, Umaira Ikram, Zarshina Nazli
papers.abstract: This study examines how generative AI (GenAI) adoption in human resource management (HRM) affects employee productivity, job satisfaction and trust in AI-mediated HR decisions. Although GenAI now supports recruitment, performance management and employee support, evidence on its human consequences remains fragmented. The objectives were to assess these three effects. The study is grounded in human–AI collaboration (augmentation) theory, which treats AI as a partner that extends human judgement, complemented by organizational justice perspectives on fairness and trust. A positivist, quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was used. Data were collected through a structured online questionnaire with five-point Likert items. The target population was 2,500 employees and HR professionals in medium and large organizations using GenAI in HR. Stratified random sampling yielded 331 valid responses from 380 distributed questionnaires. Data were analyzed in SPSS and SmartPLS using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha, factor analysis, Pearson correlation and multiple regression. GenAI adoption significantly predicted productivity (β = .57), job satisfaction (β = .43) and trust (β = .36), all p < .001, explaining 35.1%, 20.9% and 17.6% of variance respectively. Trust was rated lowest and increased with experience. The study concludes that GenAI benefits HRM, but transparency and human oversight are needed to build trust.

papers.title: DIGITAL LITERACY AND PERCEIVED MATERIAL COMPREHENSION: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF PERCEIVED AI TUTORING SUPPORT AMONG PGMI STUDENTS: Sem PLS
papers.authors: Yuyun Yumiarty
papers.journal: COMPASS Journal of Education and Counselling
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, creating opportunities for students to obtain explanations, answers, and immediate feedback during learning. However, the educational value of AI-supported learning may depend on students’ digital literacy, while the mechanism through which digital literacy contributes to Perceived Material Comprehension through AI-supported tutoring remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the relationships between digital literacy, Perceived AI Tutoring Support, and Perceived Material Comprehension among PGMI students, including the mediating role of Perceived AI Tutoring Support. A quantitative explanatory cross-sectional survey design was employed. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that digital literacy positively predicted Perceived Material Comprehension (β = 0.472, t = 5.296, p = 0.000) and Perceived AI Tutoring Support (β = 0.725, t = 10.416, p = 0.000). Perceived AI Tutoring Support also positively predicted Perceived Material Comprehension (β = 0.426, t = 5.147, p = 0.000). Furthermore, the indirect effect of digital literacy on Perceived Material Comprehension through Perceived AI Tutoring Support was significant (β = 0.309, t = 4.984, p = 0.000), indicating partial mediation. These findings demonstrate that digital literacy contributes to Perceived Material Comprehension both directly and through AI-supported tutoring. The study contributes an integrated perspective by positioning Perceived AI Tutoring Support as a mechanism connecting students’ digital capabilities with Perceived Material Comprehension. Practically, higher education institutions should strengthen digital literacy while designing structured AI-supported learning activities that encourage active evaluation and processing of AI-generated information.

papers.title: Polityki szkół wyższych wobec generatywnej sztucznej inteligencji w edukacji — analiza porównawcza wybranych uczelni z czterech regionów świata
papers.authors: Jan Kinal, Paweł Szewczyk
papers.journal: Debiuty Naukowe Studentów Wyższej Szkoły Bankowej
papers.abstract: Artykuł przedstawia systematyczną analizę porównawczą polityk regulujących wykorzystanie generatywnej sztucznej inteligencji w 30 szkołach wyższych z czterech regionów geograficznych: Ameryki Północnej, Europy Zachodniej, Polski oraz Azji. Korpus 133 dokumentów instytucjonalnych poddano ustrukturyzowanej analizie treści prowadzonej z udziałem dwóch agentów sztucznej inteligencji, klasyfikując każdą politykę w siedmiu obszarach analitycznych, w tym na pięciostopniowej skali AIAS (Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale). Z badania wyłaniają się cztery odrębne profile regulacyjne oraz centralna teza o systematycznej asymetrii między silnym wymiarem deklaratywnym polityk a ich słabszym wymiarem operacyjnym. Polska wyróżnia się najwyższym konsensusem deklaratywnym (100% szkół wyższych wymaga ujawnienia użycia AI, 100% odwołuje się do koncepcji AI literacy), lecz najniższą operacjonalizacją egzekwowania i aktualizacji. Na tej podstawie sformułowano sześć rekomendacji dla polskiego szkolnictwa wyższego. Analizowana próba ma charakter celowy i nie stanowi reprezentatywnego przekroju światowego szkolnictwa wyższego, dlatego wnioski odnoszą się do badanych regionów, a nie do ogółu krajów.

papers.title: Multi-Horizon Deep Learning Framework forSustainable Energy Forecasting in SmartCampuses: Enabling Energy Efficient SmartEducational Buildings
papers.authors: Ajay Kumar, Rainu Nandal, Kamaldeep Joshi
papers.journal: International Journal of Modern Education and Computer Science
papers.abstract: The accurate energy consumption forecast of educational institutions is critical for sustainable energymanagement and intelligent campus infrastructure. Classical forecasting models fail to simultaneously capture localtemporal variations and long-range dependencies, thus diminishing their reliability across different time horizons. Toovercome this, we propose an effective hybrid deep learning method that combines Convolutional Neural Networks(CNNs) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and domain-driven feature engineering to incorporateoccupancy and seasonality patterns. The dataset from an office building (research support facility) was used to performa series of short-term (05-minutes), medium-term (daily), and long-term (weekly) forecasts. Experimental results showthat the proposed forecasting approach demonstrates greater precision than the ten baselines including machine learningand deep learning methods in short, medium, and long time horizons. In particular, the model with feature engineeringimproved Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) by 4.71% and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) by 3.99% in theshort term and saw even greater improvements for medium-term forecasts, with RMSE improved by 6.08% and MAPEby 5.37%, and for long-term forecasts, with RMSE improved by 2.58% and MAPE by 0.33%, respectively. Theoutcomes here offer significant benefits to the science community, supporting the development of such smart campuseswith a specific, understandable methodology for energy forecasting. The methodology enables the application of datadriven energy management, cost optimization, and sustainability planning in educational spaces. The findings alsoprovide valuable insights for deploying Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven infrastructure management systems inacademia and institutional energy governance.

papers.title: A Hybrid Explainable AI Model for Accurate andTransparent Prediction of Student AcademicPerformance
papers.authors: Mohammad Nasar, Mohammad Abu Kausar
papers.journal: International Journal of Modern Education and Computer Science
papers.abstract: Predicting student academic performance accurately is essential and allows for timely interventions and datasupported educational decision-making. However, the black-box nature of state-of-the-art machine learning modelshinders their use in policy-sensitive educational settings, where interpretability and accountability are paramount. Wepropose a structured hybrid explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework that combines three tree-based ensemblemodels–namely, random forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost–using a prediction-level soft-voting strategy and couples themwith complementary post-hoc interpretation methods at the explanation level (SHAP and LIME). Instead of proposing anew base algorithm, this study systematically unifies heterogeneous boosting and bagging approaches with strictvalidation as well as dual-layer explanation consistency evaluation. Experiments on the UCI Student Performancedataset show that the proposed framework can achieve a competitive predictive performance (91.8% accuracy, ROC–AUC = 0.953) together with transparent and actionable interpretability. The robustness of the interpretability layer isfurther supported by a quantitative assessment of explanation stability, fidelity, and agreement across various methods.The presented framework harmonizes the trade-off between accuracy and interpretability to provide a deployable,policy-aware decision-support solution that is aligned with responsible AI principles for adoption within educationalcontexts.

papers.title: Multi-Model Ensemble-based Machine LearningApproach for Enhanced Suicidal IdeationDetection on Twitter Posts
papers.authors: Rohini Kancharapu, G. V. Hindumathi, Sravya Pallantla
papers.journal: International Journal of Modern Education and Computer Science
papers.abstract: Identifying suicidal ideation on Twitter is crucial for timely intervention and suicide prevention efforts. Thisstudy leverages Twitter data to identify individuals contemplating suicide, addressing the challenge of distinguishinggenuine suicidal ideations from those posted for entertainment. Given the rise in depression and anxiety, particularlyamong the youth, an ensemble model combining various machine learning algorithms is proposed to enhance theaccuracy of detecting genuine suicidal tweets. The ensemble model integrates the predictions of multiple internalmodels: Logistic Regression, LinearSVC, XGBoost, Naive Bayes, and Random Forest. Each model generates aprediction based on extracted features from the tweets, and the final prediction is determined by calculating theweighted average of these predictions, considering the relative importance of each model. If this weighted averageexceeds a predefined threshold, the tweet is classified as non-suicidal; otherwise, it is classified as suicidal. Thismethodology allows the ensemble model to balance the strengths and weaknesses of individual models, resulting in arobust and accurate classifier. Incorporating BERT classification and VADER sentiment analysis, the model is trainedon labeled data to capture intricate patterns in tweet embeddings. Evaluated against various performance metrics, theensemble model achieves an accuracy of 95.81%, precision of 93.45%, recall of 89.90%, and an F1-score of 94.68%,significantly outperforming individual models. The model also demonstrates a superior AUC-ROC value of 0.95,indicating excellent performance in distinguishing between classes. This approach not only advances the currentmethodologies but also contributes to public health by enhancing the reliability of suicide prevention efforts on socialmedia platforms.

papers.title: Examining Artificial Intelligence Literacy amongMusic Students in Higher Education: A CausalComparative Approach
papers.authors: Hüseyin Yılmaz, Yakup AÇAR, Ömer Üçer
papers.journal: International Journal of Modern Education and Computer Science
papers.abstract: This study analyzes the artificial intelligence (AI) literacy levels of music education students and exploreshow future music educators perceive and integrate AI tools within creative and instructional contexts. The researchgroup consisted of 143 students enrolled in music education programs from different faculties, such as Education, FineArts, and Conservatory. Participants were selected through a purposeful sampling technique, ensuring inclusion ofindividuals likely to encounter AI in educational and performance settings. The study employed a causal-comparative(ex post facto) design, which enables examination of naturally existing groups differing in characteristics such as priorexposure to or familiarity with AI technologies. Quantitative data were analyzed to compare students‟ AI literacy levelsacross demographic variables, including gender, type of high school graduated from, academic achievement level, andprior knowledge of AI. However, it was determined that the artificial intelligence literacy level of music teachercandidates who have knowledge about artificial intelligence programmes and use artificial intelligence programmes inmusic education is significant. Results indicated that students‟ AI literacy levels were at a medium level. No significantdifferences were found in AI literacy by gender, type of high school graduated from, academic achievement, orfrequency of internet use. However, significant differences were observed among students from different faculties, aswell as among those who had prior knowledge of AI programs, used AI applications in music and music education, andused them more frequently. These findings suggest that direct engagement with AI tools contributes to higher literacylevels.

papers.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence for Engagement Personalization in B2C Business Models: A Literature Review
papers.authors: Laleska Fabiola Estrella Copaja, José Rojas, Juan Carlos Quiroz- Flores
papers.journal: International Journal of Information Engineering and Electronic Business
papers.abstract: In an increasingly competitive world, retail companies are implementing marketing strategies aimed atgaining customer preference by building lasting emotional relationships. This facilitates the conversion of so-calledfollowers into loyal customers and brand ambassadors, thereby increasing return on investment (ROI), facilitating directfeedback to improve the product mix, and reducing customer acquisition costs over time, generating competitiveadvantages. The purpose of this systematic review is to analyze recent scientific production (2020-2025) on theapplication of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for the personalization of engagement in B2C business models, in order toanalyze the predominant techniques, evaluate their impact on the consumer and determine the critical factors thatcondition long-term customer loyalty; the methodology used consisted of a systematic review in the main scientificdatabases in publications of high-impact journals. The main findings suggest that personalization tends to be dominatedby machine learning models focused on algorithmic efficiency; however, a critical asymmetry was observed: theliterature shows a hyper-focus on quantitative studies and functional efficiency, while studies on trust and ethics are theleast relevant. Additionally, knowledge is biased by Asian dominance (53%) and the "novelty effect," limiting theapplicability of strategies in markets with high demands for transparency, such as the American market. Furthermore,an emerging trend toward an Ethical-Relational Model has been observed in the literature. It is concluded that movingbeyond the functional efficiency-centric approach and integrating Ethical AI as a strategic consideration may be key tofostering sustainable engagement, as evidenced by the reviewed literature.

papers.title: AI Adoption and E-Commerce Development in SMEs: Comparative Evidence from the EU and Ukraine
papers.authors: Hassan Ali Al-Ababneh, Amet Liumanov, Mykyta Artemchuk, Yevhenii Kolomiiets, Andrey Skrylnik
papers.journal: International Journal of Information Engineering and Electronic Business
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly associated with changes in e-commerce development, includingdemand generation, operational processes, and consumer interaction. The aim of the article is to examine and quantifythe relationship between AI adoption and e-commerce development in 2023–2025 in an international context, with anemphasis on Ukraine’s position among European markets. The methodological framework of the study is a quantitativecomparative analysis of data for Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Poland, the Netherlands, and Ukraine. An integral ECommerce Index and an AI Adoption Index were created based on statistical sources, which were normalized in therange from 0 to 1. The hypothesis was tested by using correlation and regression analysis, as well as clustering ofcountries by a combination of e-commerce and AI maturity levels. Given the correlational design of the study, thefindings are interpreted as evidence of statistical association rather than causation. The results show a persistent positiveand statistically significant relationship between the AI adoption and the development of e-commerce levels. Theleaders in terms of the AI Adoption Index are the Netherlands (0.88) and Germany (0.85), while Ukraine demonstratesthe earliest phase of integration (0.25). The findings suggest that AI adoption is a significant correlate of e-commercedevelopment rather than merely an auxiliary technological feature. The practical value of the results is the possibility oftheir use for building state policy of digital transformation and business strategies in the context of internationalcompetition.

papers.title: An ILM-Grounded Adaptive Framework for Gifted Learners: Integrating LLM Orchestration and Multi-Agent Tutoring
papers.authors: Mohamed Badawi Mustafa Elkhalifa
papers.journal: International Journal of Education and Management Engineering
papers.abstract: Gifted learners require instructional environments that transcend conventional pedagogical boundaries, offering adaptive challenge, metacognitive scaffolding, and high degrees of learner autonomy. This study presents the design, implementation, and empirical evaluation of the AI-Enhanced Self-Directed Learning (AESDL) framework an integrated adaptive system grounded in Treffinger's Independent Learner Model (ILM) and operationalized through an ensemble of five artificial intelligence (AI) technologies: the Google Gemini API (as central orchestration controller), cognitive computing, multi-agent systems (MAS), expert systems, and automatic speech recognition. The model is built upon four core ILM components Guidance, Self-Development, Enrichment, and Seminars/In-Depth Study each computationally instantiated through dedicated AI subsystems. A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control group design was employed with 50 gifted secondary school learners (25 experimental, 25 control) drawn from model gifted-education classrooms in Khartoum State, Sudan. The experimental group received eight weeks of instruction via the AESDL system; the control group received equivalent instruction through conventional electronic resources. Outcome measures self-directed learning skills, problem-solving capacity, and academic enrichment achievement (each scored on a 50-point scale) were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests with Cohen's d effect sizes. Results indicated statistically significant and practically large superiority of the AESDL condition: self-directed learning (t(48) = 7.91, p < .001, d = 2.24), problem-solving (t(48) = 5.52, p < .001, d = 1.56), and academic achievement (t(48) = 6.50, p < .001, d = 1.84). These findings advance the empirical evidence base for AI-mediated gifted education and provide actionable design principles for intelligent adaptive learning systems. The control condition comprised conventional electronic learning resources (digital textbooks, instructional videos, and static online exercises). Ninety-five-percent confidence intervals for the between-group mean differences were [9.13, 15.35], [5.62, 12.06], and [7.02, 13.30] for self-directed learning, problem-solving, and academic achievement, respectively. Given the modest sample (n = 50) and the near-ceiling experimental-group scores, these findings should be interpreted with caution regarding potential ceiling effects and limited external validity, and warrant independent replication with larger, more diverse samples.

papers.title: Predicting Social Media Addiction Levels Among University Students Using Machine Learning and SHAP Explainability
papers.authors: Md Saiful Islam, Md Safanur Islam, Md. Rabbi Khan
papers.journal: International Journal of Engineering and Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Overindulgence in social media use is increasingly becoming a matter of concern amongst students and is normally accompanied by behavioural, academic and health implications. The purpose of this study is to measure the rates of social media addiction among students and define the most important factors influencing it by means of data-driven methods. The analysis was done with a dataset of 705 student responses to determine the trends in addiction and forecast the level of addiction using machine learning models. The descriptive analysis indicated that 57.87 percent of students were in the High addiction category with the results being equal among all genders. Correlation analysis revealed that the greater the addiction scores, the greater the negative academic impact and the interpersonal conflicts, and conversely, the greater the influence on the sleep duration and mental health. The classification using several machine learning models was done, with K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) and CatBoost having the greatest accuracy of 98.6 percent. To assess model robustness, the optimized KNN model was further validated using ten-fold cross-validation, achieving a mean accuracy of 97.17% (95% CI: 95.52%–98.81%). The optimized KNN model demonstrated stable predictive performance across different data partitions. SHAP-based explainability identified average daily social media usage, mental health score, sleep duration and conflicts over social media as the most influential predictors of social media addiction. These results indicate the necessity of awareness and careful intervention approaches and show the potential of machine learning to avert early social media addiction in students.

papers.title: GUIDE-PATH: An AI-Driven Framework for Personalized English Education via Explicit Pedagogical Strategy Guidance
papers.authors: Muhammad Ahmad Subhani
papers.abstract: The opacity of large language model (LLM)-based English tutors constrains learners’ awareness of pedagogical decisions, diminishing metacognitive awareness and trust. We present GUIDE-PATH (Guided Instruction via Decision-Explicit Pedagogical Actions for Tailored Help), an AI-powered framework that explicitly communicates teaching strategies during the tutoring process. In contrast to black-box LLM tutors, GUIDE-PATH separates pedagogical reasoning from content generation through three core components: a dynamic student profiling engine that tracks CEFR level, error-specific mastery, and learning style proxies; a formal strategy library comprising eight evidence-based pedagogical moves (such as explicit correction, recast, metalinguistic feedback, and scaffolding prompt) grounded in second-language acquisition theory; and a weighted reasoning module that selects the optimal strategy based on the learner's state. The selected strategy is communicated to the learner through non-intrusive pedagogical notes. A randomized controlled trial involving 172 intermediate EFL learners compared GUIDE-PATH with an LLM-only tutor and a no-AI control. Results indicated that GUIDE-PATH produced significantly greater learning gains in grammar (Cohen’s d = 0.82), vocabulary (d = 0.91), and speaking confidence (d = 0.76). Transparency ratings strongly favoured GUIDE-PATH (d = 2.31), and learners correctly identified the pedagogical strategy in 73% of cases, a skill correlated with learning gains. These results show that explicit support of pedagogical strategies improves both learning outcomes and learner trust. The magnitude of learning gains observed in this study is consistent with findings from adjacent domains of educational AI. Explainable machine learning models for student dropout prediction [121] and LSTM-SHAP-based academic performance prediction [120] have similarly reported that transparency-enhanced systems produce measurably better outcomes than opaque alternatives. The positive correlation between strategy recognition accuracy and learning gains (r = 0.44 for grammar; r = 0.39 for vocabulary) aligns with research on the role of attention in learning [48], which established that conscious awareness of instructional stimuli is a prerequisite for deep encoding. Engagement detection studies [57], [94], [103] corroborate the finding that learners who are more actively engaged with instructional content as evidenced by their ability to identify pedagogical strategies achieve greater learning gains. The strategy library and the reasoning module are released as open-source tools to support transparent educational AI.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RETAIL: CONSUMER ATTITUDES TOWARD VOICE COMMERCE
papers.authors: Septemvrina Georgieva Kostova, Goran Angelov
papers.abstract: The global volume of e-commerce has been steadily increasing, prompting retailers to adopt online sales channels alongside traditional physical stores. A similar trend is observed in the adoption of artificial intelligence in retail, where AI is becoming a key prerequisite for market competitiveness. E-commerce encompasses multiple dimensions, and the present study focuses on one increasingly relevant area: voice commerce. The paper aims to examine the use of artificial intelligence in voice commerce through an online consumer survey and in-depth interviews with industry practitioners. The findings provide insights into consumer attitudes, perceived benefits, barriers to adoption, and the practical implications of AI-based voice commerce for improving customer experience and enhancing market competitiveness.

papers.title: Pengaruh Literasi Digital dan Pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence terhadap Kinerja UMKM Sektor F&B di Kota Depok
papers.authors: Aldiansyah Anggorro Putra, Yuni Pambreni, Agnemas Yusoep Islami
papers.journal: Lead Journal of Economy and Administration
papers.abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of digital literacy and the utilization of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the performance of MSMEs in the Food and Beverage (F&B) sector in Depok City. The study employs a quantitative approach with an associative method, surveying 100 MSME owners selected using the Slovin formula and purposive sampling. Data were collected via questionnaires and analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS version 31. The results indicate that digital literacy and AI utilization have a positive and significant effect—both partially and simultaneously—on MSME performance. The coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.733 demonstrates that these two variables explain 73.3% of the variation in MSME performance. These findings suggest that enhancing digital literacy and utilizing AI play a crucial role in improving the performance of F&B sector MSMEs in Depok City.

papers.title: Inclusive assessment design in the age of GenAI: Advancing pedagogy and practice
papers.authors: Stephanie McDonald, Gary Ian Saunders, Ellie Kennedy, Alexander Tansell
papers.journal: Open Scholarship of Teaching and Learning
papers.abstract: In an educational landscape rapidly transformed by Generative AI (GenAI), inclusive assessment design is essential to sustaining equity and meaningful learning in higher education. This study took place at a Russell Group university in the United Kingdom. Focus groups were conducted with undergraduate and taught postgraduate learners studying science subjects, to investigate their experiences and perceptions of assessment practices in an increasingly AI-mediated learning environment. Findings show that learners value assessment approaches that centre human judgment, authenticity, meaningful choice, and critical engagement. Whilst recognising the potential for GenAI to support learning, they also expressed concerns about deskilling, inequitable access to GenAI tools, and assessment designs that do not facilitate meaningful learning. Rather than viewing GenAI solely as an academic integrity risk, learners emphasised the need for transparent guidance, stronger assessment literacy, and pedagogically informed decisions in assessment design. While GenAI is at the forefront of sector-wide discussions and planning in the context of curriculum development, our findings highlight the importance of grounding GenAI within broader principles of Universal Design for Learning and constructively-aligned assessment design – emphasising flexibility, transparency, and diversity – and the importance of actively involving learners as partners and co-creators in shaping inclusive assessment practices.

papers.title: Language Education in Nigeria and the Discursive Representations of Artificial Intelligence: A Critical Discourse Analysis
papers.authors: Brilliant Richard
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION STUDIES
papers.abstract: This study critically evaluates the representations of Artificial Intelligence (henceforth, AI) - ideologically and linguistically, in educational discourse, addressing an important lacuna in the literature. It interrogates how AI is framed by dominant global narratives as an unbiased and liberal Educational Technology (henceforth, EdTech) for pedagogical advancement. Though, extant studies have looked at AI as a transformative pedagogical EdTech, however, there is a dire need to critically evaluate the ideological framings of such narratives. Drawing on Critical Discourse Analysis and the principles of Critical Applied Linguistics, the study examines select corpus consisting of national education policy documents and promotional materials from AI based EdTech firms operating within Nigeria. The study which adopted the purposive sampling technique was able to select texts that overtly position AI in relation to language teaching and education reform. Findings indicate among other things that such representations often neglect the contextual realities, particularly in Nigerian classrooms. The study also notes that AI is chiefly represented through depoliticised, techno-utopian rhetoric that highlights proficiency and irrevocability while ignoring infrastructural challenges, pedagogical consequences as well as linguistic multiplicity. Findings also indicate that such conversations ignore the interventions of local educators in favour of outsourced technical aids. The study recommends localisation of conversations and AI policies, ensuring the inclusion and engagement of stakeholders as well as the advancement of critical digital literacy in Nigerian teacher education.

papers.title: Assessing Teaching and Scientific Research in Higher Education in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Basile Mulwani Makelele
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is changing the conditions under which teaching, learning evidence, and scientific research are produced and assessed in higher education. This study examines these transformations through a qualitative-quantitative documentary analysis of 686 publications published between 2022 and 2026. Each document was coded using 44 binary thematic indicators grouped into six domains: assessment of teaching, assessment of learning, research supervision, assessment by academic juries, GenAI-related risks and limitations, and assessment transformations or good practices. Descriptive thematic frequencies were complemented by Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA), Benzécri and Greenacre corrections of inertia, and pairwise Phi coefficients. Publications from 2025 and 2026 accounted for 72.0% of the corpus, confirming the very recent and rapidly expanding character of the field. After Benzécri correction, the first three MCA dimensions explained 70.20% of corrected inertia, compared with 21.74% of raw inertia; the more conservative Greenacre correction yielded 47.86%. Phi analysis showed a strong association between authentic assessment and oral/defence-based assessment (φ = .694; χ² = 330.43; p < .001), while process traceability was positively associated with human validation (φ = .177; χ² = 21.41; p < .001). Across the corpus, integrity, transparency, explicit task-level policies, AI literacy, authentic assessment, traceability, oral justification, and human validation emerged as recurrent responses. The findings indicate a shift from assessment centred on the final product toward an evidence-based ecosystem combining product, process, traceability, explicit justification, dialogue, and accountable human judgment. On this basis, the study proposes the P-P-T-E-V model—Product, Process, Traceability, Explicitation, and Human Validation—as an integrative framework for assessing teaching-related evidence and scientific research in the GenAI era.

papers.title: Potential Contribution of Generative Artificial Intelligence to School Calendar Planning by Secondary School Principals
papers.authors: Kamonji Kapenda Grevisse, Basile Mulwani Makelele
papers.abstract: School calendar planning is a constraint-intensive management task involving national regulations, instructional-time requirements, teacher and room availability, assessment periods, extracurricular activities, meetings, holidays, local disruptions, and equity considerations. This structured integrative review examines the potential contribution of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to this task, with particular attention to secondary-school principals. Eight search strands covering GenAI and school leadership, educational administration, timetabling optimization, decision support, resource allocation, administrative workload, and resource-constrained settings were used to build an analytical corpus of 85 publications from an initial pool of 160 records. Evidence was coded by type, educational context, planning function, expected or observed benefit, risk, and proximity to annual or term-level school calendar planning. The review reveals a marked asymmetry: educational timetabling optimization is technically mature, whereas direct evidence on GenAI-assisted annual school calendar planning remains scarce. Recent K–12 leadership studies nevertheless support the plausibility of gains in document preparation, information synthesis, communication, scenario generation, and delegation of routine administrative tasks. The evidence also indicates that large language models should not be used as autonomous constraint solvers because they may omit rules, hallucinate availabilities, or produce superficially coherent but infeasible schedules. We therefore propose a hybrid GenAI-Assisted School Calendar Planning model (GASCP), combining conversational GenAI for constraint elicitation and explanation, a formal optimization engine for feasibility and trade-off management, and accountable human validation. The model generates testable hypotheses concerning planning time, feasibility, pedagogical quality, equity, robustness, acceptability, traceability, and principals’ cognitive workload. The central conclusion is that GenAI is most defensible as an interface for responsible planning rather than as an autonomous decision-maker.

papers.title: Teachers’ readiness and perceived effectiveness of AI-assisted English language instruction: The moderating role of digital competence
papers.authors: Maha Alkhalaf
papers.journal: International Journal of English Language and Literature Studies
papers.abstract: English Language Teaching is increasingly embracing Artificial Intelligence (AI), bringing fresh possibilities for enriching the quality of instruction as well as students' participation in EFL classrooms. This study examines how prepared Saudi high-school English teachers are for adopting AI technologies and their impact on students' participation in the English language learning environment. Three areas of teacher readiness are explored: technology self-efficacy, student-interaction practices, and ethical awareness, with an assessment of their predictive effect on student engagement. In addition, the moderating effect of teachers' general digital competence was analysed to see if AI readiness becomes stronger when teachers' digital competence is high. A quantitative cross-sectional research design was used, and data were gathered by a structured questionnaire administered to 450 English language teachers in public and private secondary schools in Saudi Arabia. The hypothesized relationships between the study variables were tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), and the moderating effects of the study variables were examined by PROCESS Macro analysis. The results showed that all three elements of teacher readiness had a positive and significant effect on students' engagement, with technology self-efficacy being the strongest predictor. Furthermore, teachers' digital competence also had a significant influence on the connection between AI readiness and student engagement. Gender and institutional type were also found to be important differences in the subgroup analysis. The study highlights the need for teacher development in pedagogical, ethical, and digital skills to facilitate the effective and responsible use of AI in the teaching and learning of English.

papers.title: Translation strategies in literary collocation translation: A comparative analysis of human and machine-assisted translation
papers.authors: Kammer Tuahman Sipayung
papers.journal: International Journal of English Language and Literature Studies
papers.abstract: Literary collocations present persistent challenges in translation because their meanings are often culturally embedded and cannot always be inferred from individual lexical items. Limited studies explain how human translators and AI systems differ in their strategic handling of literary collocations. Addressing this gap, this study compares the translation strategies employed by students, ChatGPT, and DeepSeek. Using a qualitative comparative design, the study analyzed 35 collocations extracted from the novel Gadis Kretek, translated by 21 English language education students and two AI systems, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. A framework of translation strategies was used to classify and compare the translation outputs. The findings reveal that all three translator groups predominantly relied on paraphrasing with related words; however, significant differences emerged in their strategic behaviour. Students frequently employed omission and occasionally produced semantically unrelated paraphrases, whereas ChatGPT and DeepSeek consistently preserved collocational meaning through semantically related reformulations. DeepSeek further demonstrated greater lexical creativity through selective borrowing and cultural adaptation. The study contributes to Translation Studies by extending Baker’s framework to human–AI translation contexts and demonstrating that collocational competence remains a key factor distinguishing novice human translators from large language models. AI helps, but human judgment remains essential.

papers.title: AI Tutors and Human Tutors in Online Universities: A Critical Narrative Review of Replacement, Partnership, and Pedagogical Risk
papers.authors: Vincent English
papers.journal: International Journal of Business and Management
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tutors are increasingly proposed as a way to extend feedback, practice, and learner support in online universities. This critical narrative review examines the replacement, partnership, and pedagogical-risk claims made for AI tutoring. It synthesises foundational evidence on intelligent tutoring systems, recent evaluations of generative-AI tutoring, research on teaching and social presence in online learning, and current educational-governance guidance. The evidence does not support a general claim that AI tutors can replace human tutors. Structured intelligent tutoring systems have often outperformed conventional instructional comparators, but results against individual human tutoring are mixed and depend on subject, comparison condition, outcome measure, and implementation. Recent generative-AI studies show promise in carefully engineered, bounded learning tasks; they do not establish effectiveness for generic chatbots or whole-programme substitution. A partnership model is therefore more defensible when it assigns AI bounded roles in practice, preliminary feedback, and pattern detection while retaining human accountability for pedagogical design, consequential decisions, exception handling, and community facilitation. The review positions ENGAGE—Engage, Navigate, Guide, Articulate, Gather, Evolve—as a design-and-governance framework that translates those principles into an iterative course-level cycle. It also distinguishes documented capability and governance concerns from broader claims that remain plausible but under-tested, including cognitive deskilling. For online-university leaders, the practical question is not whether to automate tutoring wholesale, but how to design, disclose, evaluate, and govern hybrid configurations that improve learning without displacing educational responsibility.

papers.title: Extending UTAUT with Metacognition and Self-Regulation: Evidence on Generative AI Use among University Students
papers.authors: Natthawan Phoonson, Thada Jantakoon, Rukthin Laoha
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has diffused through higher education faster than the structures meant to govern it, yet acceptance research still treats adoption as a terminal outcome rather than as an event embedded in students' self-regulation. This study extends the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) by specifying metacognitive awareness (META) and self-regulated learning (SRL) as mediators between the four UTAUT determinants and behavioural intention (BI), and BI predicts self-reported use of GenAI as a cognitive partner (AU). Responses from 451 students at seven Thai Rajabhat universities were analysed with partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM; SmartPLS 4; 10,000 bootstrap subsamples). Internal consistency was very high (above .95 for six of eight constructs), indicating partial item redundancy, and discriminant validity was supported under HTMT.90. Facilitating conditions, operationalised largely as perceived institutional guidance and support, showed the strongest associations with META (β = .595) and SRL (β = .514) but no significant direct association with intention (β = .061, p = .430); their only significant indirect association with intention ran through META (β = .186), a pattern consistent with indirect-only mediation. Social influence was the strongest direct predictor of intention (β = .357), followed by META (β = .312); effort expectancy and SRL did not predict intention. The model explained 62.1% to 70.9% of endogenous variance and showed out-of-sample predictive relevance. Given the cross-sectional, single-source design and full-collinearity diagnostics indicating possible common-method variance, the findings are interpreted as associations compatible with, but not establishing, the proposed mechanisms.

papers.title: Research trends in the field of artificial intelligence and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: A bibliometric analysis
papers.authors: Yong Liao, San-Jin Zeng, Cheng-Gui Xu, Rui-Lu Liu, Jia-Yu Wang, 张灿, Xing-He Zhang
papers.abstract: whereas Australia took the lead in international collaboration and cumulative citation influence.Two distinct journal clusters were formed: IEEE Access focused on diagnostic algorithm development, and Frontiers in Psychiatry centered on clinical therapeutic research.Keyword clustering and timeline graphs divided the whole field into two major research branches.For intelligent diagnosis, four successive technological phases were identified: Single electroencephalogram-based screening, multi-modal deep learning modeling, explainable AI clinical validation and integrated multimodal comprehensive assessment, with neuroimaging and computer vision as mainstream technical pipelines.For individualized treatment, research split into two parallel directions: Machine learning-aided stimulant efficacy prediction and humanoid robot non-pharmacological rehabilitation.It should be emphasized that bibliometric metadata cannot verify real-world clinical translational superiority of any intervention modality.CONCLUSION Bibliometric mapping demonstrates that global research integrating AI with ADHD diagnosis and treatment has formed a relatively complete research framework from the perspective of publication metadata.Intelligent diagnostic technology constitutes the longstanding core of this field, while robot-assisted rehabilitation emerges as a fastgrowing translational frontier.This bibliometric panorama systematically unpacks the developmental trajectories of diagnostic and therapeutic research branches and provides quantitative evidencebased references for subsequent clinical translational exploration.

papers.title: Acupuncture for fatigue and sleep disturbance in patients with mild-to-moderate depression: A retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study
papers.authors: Yi Wang, Ittipalanukul Penpat, Zheng Wu, Xiao-Xiao Jin, Le-ping HUANG, Zhi-Hai Hu, Qun Lu
papers.abstract: BACKGROUNDDepression is frequently accompanied by fatigue and sleep disturbance, and these symptoms may persist despite antidepressant therapy.Acupuncture is commonly used as an adjunctive treatment for depression; however, evidence regarding its association with fatigue, sleep quality, and related biological markers remains limited. AIMTo evaluate whether adjunctive acupuncture was associated with improvements in fatigue and sleep disturbance in patients with mild-to-moderate depression. METHODSThis retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study included 114 patients with mild-to-moderate depression (August 2023 to August 2025).Patients were matched 1:1 into a control (pharmacotherapy alone) and observation (acupuncture plus pharmacotherapy) groups (57 per group).The primary outcomes were the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17), Fatigue Scale-14 (FS-14), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) at week 8. Exploratory outcomes included polysomnography parameters, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis hormones, NLRP3, caspase-1, interleukin-1β mRNA, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and P300. RESULTSBoth groups improved over 8 weeks, but the observation group showed greater reductions in symptom scores.In the primary analysis, the between-group difference in HAMD-17 at week 8 was -1.96 points [95% confidence interval (CI): -2.79 to -1.13; d = 0.87], in PSQI was -1.14 points (95%CI: -1.74 to -0.54; d = 0.78), and in FS-14 was -1.16 points (95%CI: -1.56 to -0.76; d = 1.11).Similar favorable changes were observed in 5 / 41 polysomnographic parameters, HPA axis hormones, NLRP3-related mRNA expression, BDNF, and P300 measures, with larger effect estimates in the observation group at follow-up.No serious adverse events were documented in either group. CONCLUSIONIn depression, fatigue, and sleep quality compared with pharmacotherapy alone.The observed biomarker changes generate mechanistic hypotheses but cannot establish causality.Prospective randomized trials are required to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Bipedal Navigation and Locomotion Control Algorithms for Humanoid Robots
papers.authors: Xueyan Fu
papers.abstract: With their anthropomorphic design, humanoid robots are naturally adapted to human environments; however, high degrees of freedom, severe nonlinear dynamics, and small stability margins make autonomous locomotion a major bottleneck for practical applications. This paper surveys the key algorithms for humanoid robot locomotion, navigation, and motion control. In legged navigation, this survey traces the development from simplified-model gait generation to search-based footstep planning, and finally to online dynamic replanning and, ultimately, a hierarchical "Footstep Planning to Model Predictive Control to Whole-Body Control" framework. In motion control, this paper reviews two primary approaches: model-based optimization and reinforcement learning. The former has gone from simple models to real-time model predictive control and whole-body multi-contact optimization, and the latter has developed from proprioceptive blind walking to terrain adaptation through vision and synthesis of anthropomorphic motion. Next, a comparative analysis of these two paradigms on three aspects: stability, real-time performance and environmental adaptability, reveals that the "model-based reference with learning-based residual" hybrid scheme has emerged as a prominent trend. Finally, open challenges are mentioned in a systematic fashion, such as the interpretability and safety of learned policies, long-horizon robust locomotion in unstructured environments and whole-body integration of locomotion and manipulation.

papers.title: A Mechanism Model of Social Participation Among Introverted Students in AI-Supported Gamified Classroom
papers.authors: Jinling Wang, Lan Tian
papers.journal: Journal of Education and Educational Research
papers.abstract: In classroom environments with public expression, group discussions, and peer cooperation, introverted students encounter barriers in social participation due to participation styles, interaction pressure and limited situational support. This study adopts the inclusive education principle, uses literature analysis and theory synthesis to explore how artificial intelligence-supported gamification classrooms can promote social engagement. A three - dimensional mechanism model is proposed, which includes social safety, participation motivation and peer modeling. This model shows that AI - supported gamified classrooms can improve introverted students' social participation by reducing interaction risks, strengthening motivation, and enabling interactive experiences to be transferred to real peer environments. Based on the model, this study constructs a framework based on design principles, key components, and evaluation indicators, which is used to evaluate classroom design and effectiveness.

papers.title: An Analysis of Educational Technology Application in English Second Language Teaching Empowered by Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Mengyu Tian
papers.journal: Journal of Education and Educational Research
papers.abstract: English as a Second Language has restrictions in terms of tailored advice, timely feedback and real-life settings. Progress in natural language processing, speech recognition and large language models offer promising solutions to these problems. Today, smart speech tools can identify pronunciation problems, writing aid systems can spot grammar and text-level problems, adaptive platforms may provide tailored material based on behaviour data, and generative AI mixed with augmented reality can build immersive communication environments. Obviously, the country's policies have implied the profound integration of artificial intelligence and education. The study blends second language learning and educational technology, and discusses the specific application of AI tools in 5 aspects, including oral instruction, written correction, path planning, context design and evaluation diagnosis. The investigation reveals that artificial intelligence can make up for the flaws of traditional education, but its efficacy depends on the control of educational goals for the use of technology and the intervention of the instructors' professional judgement. Simply adding tools is unlikely to bring about real changes. The paper evaluates the constraints including data security, algorithm bias, instructor capacity adaptability, and advises that human-machine cooperation should be the key route for the transformation of second language education.

papers.title: Teaching Reform of the Data Structures and Algorithms Course Integrating the OBE Concept with AI Technology
papers.authors: Huihong Xie, Yinxing Chen, Jiaying Wang, Yingshan Lin
papers.journal: Journal of Education and Educational Research
papers.abstract: Data Structures and Algorithms have for years run into the same wall: teaching that stays rigid, material too abstract for many students to grasp, a gap between what is taught and what is practiced, grades that lean almost entirely on a final exam, and little room for instruction shaped to the individual.
