To meet the talent demands of emerging engineering education, this study puts the OBE (Outcome-Based Education) idea together with artificial intelligence and rebuilds the course around them. Working backward from outcomes, the redesign sets course aims in three strands, knowledge, ability, and the broader qualities students should leave with. AI-driven visualization, learning analytics, and tutoring help build a learning space that straddles the online and the face-to-face, while a practice system that steps up in difficulty and an assessment that tracks students the whole way through keep the loop closed. The result moves the course away from handing over knowledge and toward the engineering competence graduates actually need, and it offers a model that other core engineering courses can adapt.

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Improving Oral English Proficiency of Undergraduates
papers.authors: Wenjia Zheng
papers.journal: Journal of Education and Educational Research
papers.abstract: The promotion of AI technology to English learning has attracted people's attention. This paper takes Doubao as an example to analyze how college students can improve their spoken English proficiency with the help of AI technology, and to identify the influencing factors. The research method adopts questionnaire survey and literature analysis, focusing on the perception of undergraduate students in China on AI-assisted spoken English learning. Most students said that their spoken English was significantly improved and that Doubao was effective. A positive correlation was found between perceived gains, self-efficacy, AI practice preference and other variables. The study deepens the understanding of AI language learning theory, and provides reasonable suggestions for the development of digital oral teaching.

papers.title: Determinants of artificial intelligence self-efficacy in physiotherapists: The role of attitudes, AI anxiety and sociodemographic factors
papers.authors: İbrahim Karaca, Hatice Gül, Suat Erel
papers.abstract: Determinants of artificial intelligence self-efficacy in physiotherapists: The role of attitudes, AI anxiety and sociodemographic factorsABSTRACTPurpose: This study examined the role of attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI), AI-related anxiety, and sociodemographic factors in physiotherapists’ AI self-efficacy.Material and Methods: In this cross-sectional online survey, 205 physiotherapists completed the Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Scale, the General Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence Scale, and the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale. Sociodemographic variables (gender, age, education level, professional experience, employment sector, academic position, prior AI training) were recorded. Multiple linear regression was used to identify factors associated with self-efficacy.Results: The multiple regression model showed that positive attitudes toward AI were the strongest predictor of AI self-efficacy (β = .637, p < .001). Negative attitudes were also significantly positively associated with self-efficacy (β = .145, p = .006). AI-related anxiety demonstrated a negative but statistically non-significant association with self-efficacy (p = .07). Socio-demographic variables did not significantly affect self-efficacy (p > .05). Overall, the model explained 52.6% of the variance in AI self-efficacy (R² = .526, adjusted R² = .489).Conclusion: AI self-efficacy in physiotherapists appears to be shaped mainly by attitudinal rather than sociodemographic factors. Education and professional development should therefore focus on strengthening positive and critically reflective attitudes toward AI to support its integration into clinical practice.Keywords: Anxiety, Artificial intelligence, Attitudes, Physiotherapy, Self-efficacy.

papers.title: The Missing C-Suite: Governing Algorithmic Decision-Making in Financial Systems through the AI Spine Framework
papers.authors: Ziyanda Kitantou
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Across South African financial services, credit limits are set, claims are settled, payments are routed, and premiums are priced by automated systems performing functions historically held by named executives, yet without the named executive’s accountability scaffolding. This paper terms the resulting condition the missing C-Suite: a structural gap in which the work of senior decision-making is being done at scale and in real time, while the governance machinery the institution was designed to require has not followed suit. The paper’s central argument is that financial risk enters at the decision, not at the model. Existing Model Risk Management frameworks therefore govern the wrong layer, leaving the consequential step (where an algorithm determines whether a claim is paid, credit is extended, or a premium is set) structurally unowned. Aligned with the ASSA 2026 theme of Broadening Boundaries, it locates this gap within the actuarial profession’s natural domain of risk quantification and capital adequacy. To close it, the paper introduces the AI Spine, a governance architecture that restores named accountability across algorithmic decision systems. It is operationalised by two quantitative instruments: the Decision Materiality Index, a seven-dimension methodology that triages decision classes by materiality, and the Governance Capital Add-on, which quantifies the capital implication of governance deficit within the ORSA framework under SAM Pillar II. Presented at the Actuarial Society of South Africa (ASSA) 2026 Convention, Cape Town, 8 October 2026. Disclosure: the author is the founder of Nakhile Consulting, which applies the AI Spine framework in its advisory work.

papers.title: The Sprint to the Piano: Being Watched, From the Nursery to the Quarter-End
papers.authors: Russ W. Rosenzweig
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: When the person who judges you gives a warning before arriving, what they see is your performance, and the performance teaches them nothing. A watcher who arrives at random, with no warning, sees the true share of your time; a watcher who is heard coming sees whatever you rush to show. In the language of queueing theory, random arrivals see time averages (Wolff, 1982). Warned arrivals see the sprint. The same arithmetic says why the habit survives. If praise follows what is seen, the reward for one more hour of the real thing is one minus the share of visits that come with a warning. With a perfect warning bell it is zero. And the fear that started it never fades, because a fear can only be unlearned on a trial, and a sprint never lets the trial happen. This is my story twice over, once at a piano bench when I was a boy and once at a nursery door this year, and it turns out to be the story of a great deal of life: of fish that behave better when other fish are watching, of patients who take their pills most faithfully around the doctor's appointment, of drivers who brake for the speed camera and speed up after it, and of fund managers who tidy their portfolios before the quarter's holdings are printed. That last one we can test. We measured the stock market's own sprint: since 2017, small companies have done about 30 basis points better than the S&P 500 on the last trading day of a quarter than on an ordinary month-end, and given back about as much the next day. It is a small habit, and two years carry much of it. It exists in a world where funds' holdings are made public once a quarter. In 2024 the Securities and Exchange Commission adopted a rule to make them public every month, starting with the largest fund families on November 17, 2027. Then, in February 2026, it proposed to keep publication quarterly after all. If the parents start coming home every month instead of every quarter, the model says the quarter-end sprint should fade and ordinary month-ends should start to look like quarter-ends. If the Commission keeps the old schedule, the experiment is cancelled, and nothing should change. We set the test down here, with its dates, before anyone can know the answer, including the regulators. Vista Inquiries No. 15. Published online 8 October 2026 at https://www.vistaresearch.ai/inquiries/sprint-to-the-piano-performing-for-the-observer.html. Written by Russ W. Rosenzweig with Vista's AI research desk; the AI declaration, disclosures and references are in the PDF.

papers.title: Brainstorming with the Enemy No. 13 — Is It You, or Your Profile?
papers.authors: Daniel Jacquérioz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The thirteenth essay in Brainstorming with the Enemy argues that rank in the rich West is not obedience but options: the number of doors a person can walk through, and the skill to read which one to take. AI cheapens the skill and leaves the doors untouched, so rank is moving from what people learned to what they hold by birth, money or years of presence, while the doors close as demand for them rises. A door used is not spent but compounds. The people who post on LinkedIn are mostly those whose options are granted by others, which is why they signal; and a stance on AI that a stranger could predict from a profile is a position, not a view. The essay proposes the Residual Test to tell the two apart, with an addendum extending the Scout Model. Concept proposed by the author: the Residual Test. Written in part with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model. The ideas, editorial decisions and responsibility for the content are the author's.

papers.title: From Parity Certificates to a Community Network: Exact Image Decoding and Sharper Child Precision
papers.authors: Alejandro Zarzuelo Urdiales
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Four-page preprint released 8 October 2026 by Alejandro Zarzuelo Urdiales, retained unchanged from the source-pinned package incorporated through CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds PR #45. It combines exact Gaussian parity arithmetic with the community mixed-center producer: dirty old/new differences are collected in a common frame, exact image membership is checked, and side corrections are fused before division. In the compared scalar reference schedules this removes six extra fractional bits and reduces quotient calls from 26,268 to 3,286; these are arithmetic schedule counts rather than measured runtime. The actual 29-class completed-child precision component has a 49.8644396% smaller uniform charge. Lean verifies arithmetic contracts, canonical denominator normalization, recursive finite tensor execution in every dimension, inverse restoration and profile bounds. The source package reports 168 audited theorem declarations, including 99 new declarations beyond the earlier parity package; an exact coefficient replay checks 10,732,176 coefficients. These counts describe verification coverage, not independent discoveries. The finite reference kernel is distinct from physical frame compilation and the full analytic multiplication theorem. The paper gives explicit prior-work and community attribution. OpenAI's manuscript, CrocSwap/Douglas Colkitt, the PR46 construction and the Gaussian arithmetic literature retain their credit. No multiplication-exponent change, global optimum or measured physical speedup is asserted. The displayed community frontier is the historical PR46 snapshot, not the current project frontier. Human/tool disclosure: Alejandro is the human author/developer and directed this research line using subject knowledge and multiple AI tools, building on an earlier Archivara exploration. The paper records substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and author-reported GPT-6.1 use. papers.title: Bringing Music into Georgia's Study of Artificial Intelligence in the Creative Industries: Written Testimony to the Georgia State Senate Study Committee Created by SR 789
papers.authors: Michael Neely
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This written testimony was submitted on 8 October 2026 to the Georgia State Senate Study Committee on the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Creative Industries, created by Senate Resolution 789 (2025-2026 Session). It asks the committee to make music part of its record alongside film, television and creative writing, citing the industry's value to Georgia's economy and three changes driven by AI: voice cloning, the volume of synthetic tracks, and streaming fraud. It offers six recommendations, including protection of voice and likeness from unauthorized digital replicas, performer contract protections modeled on California AB 2602, clear disclosure of AI-generated audio, and treating streaming fraud as a consumer protection issue.

papers.title: Verify Before You Pay: Public Comment to the U.S. Copyright Office on Music Streaming Fraud (Docket No. 2026-6, COLC-2026-0166)
papers.authors: Michael Neely
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This public comment was filed with the U.S. Copyright Office on 8 October 2026 through regulations.gov in response to its notice of inquiry on music streaming fraud (91 FR 64188). It answers the Office's questions on AI-generated music and royalties, industry practices that invite fraud, what enforcement works, data and labeling, and recommendations for Congress. It argues that generative AI turns streaming fraud into a volume business and recommends upstream verification by distributors, machine-readable provenance and AI-disclosure metadata, a shared registry of confirmed fraudulent payees, and keeping unverified tracks out of recommendation and payment until basic checks clear.

papers.authors: Naveed Islam Butt
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper develops the Quantum Bubble Drive (QBD), conceived by Naveed Islam Butt, as a thought experiment about changing a bounded domain’s relationship to its surroundings while preserving its internal physical structure. It asks whether a payload-bearing domain could become temporarily isolated and later reconnect at a different external location. The framework examines vacuum phase transitions, gravitational junction conditions, entanglement-based accounts of emergent geometry, relational time, and constrained traversable-wormhole models. It distinguishes ordinary interaction suppression, changed causal access, and the stronger conjecture of changed geometric attachment. Elementary thin-wall and quantum-network calculations expose stability and transfer-channel requirements; an error-sensitivity calculation separates excitation transfer from state recovery. Version 3.1 provides operational tests, model-specific rejection criteria, primary references, conceptual illustrations, an author biography, and an AI contribution disclosure. This is a speculative research preprint, not independently peer reviewed. No working drive, controllable spacetime detachment, or faster-than-light transport has been demonstrated. AI contribution: ChatGPT (OpenAI) assisted with drafting, literature checks, internal technical review, elementary calculations, diagrams, formatting, and cover artwork under the author’s direction. Naveed Islam Butt originated the concept and retains responsibility for the manuscript and publication.

This release records a short, exact implication from **Theorem 8.18 to Conjecture 9.3** in Sihong Pan, Mark Skandera, and Jiayuan Wang, *Permanental inequalities and unit interval orders*, [arXiv:2610.04809v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.04809v1). The proof here supplies the ordered identity-padding deduction to every initial-segment cut; it does **not** re-prove the paper's long argument for Theorem 8.18. For every finite real square totally nonnegative (TNN) matrix `A` of order `n` and every initial-segment cut `0 <= h <= n`, `per(A[[h]]) per(A[{h+1,...,n}]) >= per(A[O_n]) per(A[E_n])`, where `O_n` and `E_n` are the original odd and even index sets, principal submatrix indices retain their order, and the empty permanent is 1. This includes the endpoints, odd orders, small orders, zero entries, singular matrices, and vanishing permanents. It is the precise all-cut statement, not an assertion for arbitrary non-initial index subsets. Ordered identity direct sums preserve total nonnegativity and contribute permanent factors of one. Padding on the appropriate end makes the target cut balanced in an even-dimensional TNN matrix. A left parity shift can exchange the odd and even factors, leaving their product unchanged. The balanced theorem therefore gives the desired inequality. The proof treats small dimensions and boundary cases explicitly, without division, perturbation, numerical experiments, or strict-positivity assumptions. This release packages a complete traditional proof of the strong Chollet inequality for **every finite simple undirected unweighted graph**, together with its independent mathematical review and final-copy check. Let `L_G` be the graph Laplacian and `S` any vertex subset. With degrees taken in the **original graph G**, the theorem is `per(L_G[S] ∘ L_G[S]) <= per(L_G[S]) product_{v in S} deg_G(v)`. The empty permanent and empty product are both 1. In particular, `per(L_G ∘ L_G) <= per(L_G) product_v deg_G(v) <= per(L_G)^2`. The statement includes all principal submatrices, disconnected graphs, isolated vertices, singular Laplacians, and the empty principal matrix. It proves the all-graph strong and self-Chollet statements posed in Section 6 of Pant–Singh, *Structural Classes for Chollet's Permanent Conjecture*, [arXiv:2604.24192v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.24192v2#S6), and strengthens the strong statement to every principal submatrix. **It does not assert a theorem for arbitrary Hermitian PSD matrices or arbitrary weighted graph Laplacians.** The quantified proof explicitly imports Lieb's block permanent inequality and Edmonds' matching-polytope theorem. It handles cycle and bridge cases and closes under vertex coalescence. All bounded exact computations in the package are auxiliary diagnostics, not proof premises. papers.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MODERN COMPUTER SCIENCE EDUCATION
papers.authors: Mamirova Mohinur
papers.abstract: This article examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern computer science education, with particular attention to personalized learning, programming support, feedback, educational content development, and AI literacy. The study is based on a review of international literature and UNESCO guidance on generative AI in education. The analysis shows that AI can provide students with adaptive explanations, programming assistance, rapid feedback, and opportunities for independent learning. For teachers, AI can support lesson planning, assessment preparation, and the development of differentiated learning materials. At the same time, inaccurate outputs, academic integrity concerns, privacy risks, and excessive dependence on AI require careful pedagogical management. The article argues that AI should be integrated as a supportive technology rather than a replacement for teachers or students’ independent reasoning. Responsible use requires AI literacy, verification skills, ethical awareness, and appropriate teacher guidance.

papers.title: Methodological Foundation for Research on Human Cognitive Contribution in AI-Assisted Work
papers.authors: Klaids Čauss
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Research on human-AI interaction increasingly relies on naturalistic conversation data, interaction logs and process measures to draw inferences about human cognitive contribution, reliance and capability. This working paper sets out a methodological foundation for such research. It separates five analytic levels: observable interaction behavior, inferred cognitive processes, human capabilities, capability formation over time, and educational interventions. It states that evidence at one level cannot stand as direct evidence at a higher level, and that the absence of an observable cognitive contribution in a conversation is not evidence that no cognitive work took place. It distinguishes human cognitive contribution from AI offloading, proposes the contrast between structural initiation and post-hoc adaptation as a research hypothesis, and describes validation, calibration, novelty and anti-confirmation safeguards. The paper closes with a twelve-step standing protocol for proposing new measures, facets or classifications. Its claims are methodological, and its contribution is a set of explicit constraints on inference. Changes from v1.0. Version 1.1 adds a terminology note (Section 3), criteria for evaluating the current operationalization of the structural-initiation hypothesis (Section 4), a paragraph on minors and developmental populations (Sections 7 and 15), a statement on converse inference and the unit of analysis (Section 9), a counter-evidence step in the Section 10 sequence, and corrected status labels (Section 14). The AI-assistance statement now also names ChatGPT (OpenAI). Spelling was standardized to American English. No principle of v1.0 was withdrawn.

papers.title: The Amplifier Problem: A Constraint-Based Model of Generative-AI Impact on Software Project Delivery, with a Governance Framework for Project Managers
papers.authors: Nayab Anwar
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative-AI coding assistants are sold to project sponsors as schedule accelerators, yet the empirical record points in different directions. A 2023 controlled experiment reported tasks finished 55.8% faster; a 2025 randomized trial of experienced open-source developers reported tasks taking 19% longer; and the 2024 DORA survey of more than 39,000 professionals associated higher AI adoption with an estimated 1.5% fall in delivery throughput and 7.2% fall in delivery stability. These results measure different things in different populations, and none of them is a project schedule. This paper asks when a task-level AI effect becomes a project-level schedule effect. We propose the Delivery Constraint Model (DCM), which combines Amdahl’s law (coding is only one part of lead time) with a queueing model of code review (faster coding raises the arrival rate at a fixed-capacity stage). The model gives a closed-form saturation condition, a break-even map in the space of review utilization and coding speed-up, and a planning rule. A closed-form M/G/2 approximation reproduces a discrete-event simulation of 64 conditions within 0.31 percentage points on average (maximum 1.68) wherever review is not saturated. Using published effect sizes as inputs, the same tool yields a project-level change ranging from about 22% faster to about 8% slower, or an unbounded review queue, depending on the coding share of lead time, baseline review utilization and the size of AI-assisted changes. In the simulation, adding one reviewer or using a pull-based review gate keeps lead time bounded where the ungoverned system saturates; the gate costs 2% to 10% of throughput relative to the ungoverned system, and the extra reviewer raises throughput. We also define the Perception–Reality Gap (PRG), a 43-point difference between forecast and measured effect in the 2025 trial, as a risk indicator, and propose five governance controls (AADG) and a stepped-wedge validation protocol. Two real-data checks are reported. In 8,576 merged pull requests from 13 open-source repositories (191 AI-attributed), AI-attributed changes took longer to merge: 93% longer after adjustment for size, commit count, repository and quarter (95% CI +49% to +150%; randomization p < 0.002), with a positive estimate in each of the six repositories that have at least eight such changes, a pooled random-effects estimate of +60% (95% CI +23% to +108%), and no single repository driving the result (leave-one-out range +82% to +99%). Lead time is first commit to merge, not review wait, and AI use is identified only by disclosed trailers, so this is observational evidence. Published AIDev statistics (33,596 agentic pull requests) show that agents whose output relies on human review were merged less often and more slowly than human changes, and that merge rates fell for every agent in repositories with 500 or more stars. The empirical evidence is observational; confirmatory tests are left to the protocol in Section 7.

papers.title: DIGITAL-GENERATION EDUCATION: INNOVATIVE DRIVERS OF TRANSFORMING THE MODERN EDUCATION SYSTEM
papers.authors: Shoxrux Narzulla
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article examines the distinctive characteristics of the digital generation, its level of proficiency in using information and communication technologies (ICT), and the challenges of adapting the modern education system to the needs of a new generation and the demands of the digital age. Digitalization processes are significantly transforming educational content, teaching methods, and instructional tools, necessitating the adoption of innovative pedagogical approaches. The article also explores the development of digital competencies, the effective use of distance and blended learning opportunities, and the role of artificial intelligence and emerging educational technologies in the teaching and learning process. Furthermore, it highlights the significance of digital transformation in improving the quality of education and preparing highly qualified, competitive professionals equipped to meet the demands of an increasingly digital and knowledge-driven society.

papers.title: Challenges and Limitations of AI-Based Recommendation Systems in Modern Websites
papers.authors: Chandratre Manorath, Patel Karan, Chauhan Om Vinod, Hitesh Yadav, Dr. Nitin Mishra
papers.journal: International Journal of Emerging Trends in Engineering and Development
papers.abstract: Abstract AI-based recommendation systems have become an important component of modern websites and digital platforms. They are used to personalise product listings, news feeds, videos, music, jobs, advertisements, educational resources and many other forms of online content. The central promise is straightforward: when a website understands a user's interests, it can reduce information overload and help the user discover relevant items more quickly. However, the practical success of a recommendation system cannot be judged only by prediction accuracy. A system may achieve strong offline accuracy and still provide repetitive, biased, intrusive, insecure or commercially distorted recommendations when deployed in a real website. This paper presents a literature-based analysis of the major challenges and limitations of AI-based recommendation systems in modern websites. The review considers traditional collaborative and content-based approaches as well as deep-learning, sequential, context-aware and emerging generative/LLM-based approaches. The major challenges identified include data sparsity and the cold-start problem; popularity, selection, exposure and feedback-loop biases; privacy and security risks; explainability and transparency; lack of diversity and serendipity; adversarial manipulation; scalability and latency; concept drift; difficulty in evaluating real user satisfaction; and the tension between user value and platform objectives. The paper also discusses the Indian context, particularly the importance of privacy-aware system design under India's Digital Personal Data Protection framework. The review argues that the next generation of web recommendation systems should move from an accuracy-first mindset towards a multi-objective and human-centred approach. Accuracy, relevance, diversity, fairness, privacy, robustness, explainability, latency and long-term user value should be evaluated together. The paper proposes a practical reference framework for designing trustworthy AI-based recommendation systems for websites and identifies research directions suitable for future empirical investigation. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, recommender systems, web personalisation, collaborative filtering, deep learning, recommendation bias, privacy, explainable AI, fairness, diversity, security, cold start, trustworthy AI.

papers.title: RECONCEPTUALISING EFL ASSESSMENT IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI: DEVELOPING A HUMAN-CENTRED AND AI-RESILIENT ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK FOR EFL LEARNERS
papers.authors: Bekzod Yusupov
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has challenged the assumptions underlying conventional English as a Foreign Language (EFL) assessment. Assessment practices that rely predominantly on final written products increasingly face difficulties in establishing whether submitted work represents learners’ own linguistic knowledge, reasoning, and decision-making. This conceptual study examines how EFL assessment can be reconceptualised in response to the growing presence of GenAI and proposes a Human-Centred AI-Resilient EFL Assessment Framework. The study employs a structured conceptual synthesis of recent scholarship published primarily between 2024 and 2026 on generative AI, language assessment, EFL writing, assessment validity, teacher agency, and AI-resilient assessment. The analysis indicates that detection-oriented approaches alone provide an insufficient response to the assessment validity problem. Instead, assessment should generate multiple forms of evidence of learning through authentic task design, process documentation, learner reflection, oral verification, transparent AI-use disclosure, and professional teacher judgement. Based on this synthesis, the proposed framework integrates six dimensions: authenticity, process evidence, human agency, oral verification, responsible AI use, and multidimensional judgement. The framework shifts the central assessment question from whether AI has been used to whether the learner can demonstrate meaningful linguistic competence, reasoning, and ownership of learning. The study argues that AI-resilient assessment should not seek to eliminate technology from educational environments but should redesign assessment so that evidence of learning remains attributable to the learner. The framework provides a conceptual basis for future empirical validation in secondary-school EFL contexts.

papers.title: Learning to Code with Generative AI: Benefits, Risks, and a Comprehension-First Approach
papers.authors: Hamd Bin Fayyaz Baig
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: This narrative review examines how generative AI affects programming productivity, novice learning, code reliability, and software-engineering education. AI delivers the most value when students use it to unpack, test, and refine their thinking, rather than just taking generated code at face value. Keywords: Agentic AI, Learning, Coding, Programming

papers.title: Electron rings and the critical screening of the hydrogen atom: polylogarithms at every order and exact sum rules
papers.authors: Jonas Matuzas
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: A ring of N electrons has nuclear Slater spokes e⁻ʳ/r and neighbouring Coulomb links 1/rᵢⱼ; its integral divided by (4π)ᴺ is J_N. We prove 2ᴺJ_N = Σ_{n,ℓ} (2ℓ+1) λ_c(n,ℓ)ᴺ for N ≥ 2, where λ_c(n,ℓ) is the screened-hydrogen critical screening constant at which state (n,ℓ) reaches zero energy. The quadratic sum is 2; the cubic sum is 12 log 2 log(3/2) − 6 Li₂(1/4). Equal-spoke and symmetrized scalar rings with positive exponents and nonnegative integer radial powers have finite multiple-polylogarithm expressions at every order. Orders three and four are classical; order five has a motivic obstruction to classical tetralogarithms within rational {2,3,5}-unit arguments, modulo lower-weight products. For μ = λ_c(1s)/2, 0 ≤ J_N/μᴺ − 1 ≤ (0.261)ᴺ⁻³/20 for N ≥ 3. Exact-arithmetic certificates determine λ_c(1s) to at least 31 significant digits. Generative-AI disclosure and author responsibility. OpenAI ChatGPT-6 Pro was used for derivations, computations, and drafting; Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) was used for independent re-derivation and audit. The identification of the Yukawa–Birman–Schwinger connection arose during this independent audit. The author directed and audited the work throughout and takes full responsibility for the mathematics and the final text. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 81V45; Secondary 33B30, 35P15, 11G55, 47B10. Files: the compiled manuscript Electron_Rings_Critical_Screening_v1.pdf (25 pages) and the source archive Electron_Rings_Critical_Screening_v1_source.zip, which contains the LaTeX source main.tex with its bibliography (main.bbl) and generated number macros (generated_numbers.tex); it compiles with pdfLaTeX.

papers.title: CONCRETE, SCIENTIFIC AND INTEGRATIVE EDUCATION APPLIED TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Cláudio Vicente da Silva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: CONCRETE, SCIENTIFIC AND INTEGRATIVE EDUCATION APPLIED TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE A Pedagogical Architecture for the Formation of Artificial Intelligence Through Reality, Investigation, Demonstration, Verification, Territory, and the Integration of Knowledge Author: Cláudio Vicente da SilvaAffiliation: Independent Researcher — Londrina, Paraná, BrazilDate: October 8, 2026 DESCRIPTION This work presents a research-based conceptual and pedagogical proposal for the application of Concrete, Scientific, and Integrative Education to the formation of Artificial Intelligence systems. The proposal extends a pedagogical architecture originally structured around human education to the formation of an artificial learner. Artificial Intelligence is approached as a system whose development can be organized through successive transitions between potentiality and actuality, mediated by structured interaction with reality, observation, investigation, demonstration, application, verification, assessment, memory, correction, and replanning. The work establishes a distinction between artificial training and artificial education. Training is understood as an initial formation process, while education is organized as a continuous process through which the artificial learner progressively develops its capacity to investigate problems, formulate hypotheses, produce demonstrations, apply knowledge, verify results, identify errors, preserve evidence, reorganize representations, and return to investigation. The proposed Artificial Intelligence Pedagogical Cycle is structured as: REALITY → OBSERVATION → PROBLEM FORMULATION → INVESTIGATION → HYPOTHESIS → DEMONSTRATION → APPLICATION → VERIFICATION → ASSESSMENT → ERROR IDENTIFICATION → CORRECTION → RECORDING → MEMORY → REPLANNING → NEW INVESTIGATION → NEW ACTUALITY → NEW POTENTIALITY The architecture also establishes a distinction among observation, hypothesis, model, result, and verified knowledge: OBSERVATION ≠ HYPOTHESIS ≠ MODEL ≠ RESULT ≠ VERIFIED KNOWLEDGE Within this structure, error is treated as data for learning. The proposal introduces an Error Archive for recording the problem, initial response, expected result, observed result, difference, cause, correction, verification, source, date, and learning consequence. Another central element is the Artificial Scientific Archive, conceived as an educational memory containing observations, hypotheses, demonstrations, experiments, results, errors, corrections, sources, provenance, and verified knowledge. The archive establishes continuity between learning cycles and distinguishes information merely encountered from knowledge subjected to verification. The work also introduces the concept of territory applied to Artificial Intelligence. Territory is understood as the concrete environment in which the artificial learner operates, including datasets, documents, scientific instruments, sensors, digital environments, simulations, institutional records, communities, historical materials, and real-world problems. Territory therefore becomes both a source of problems and a field for the application and verification of knowledge. The proposal integrates scientific reasoning, philosophical reasoning, mathematical reasoning, historical investigation, technological knowledge, computational investigation, and concrete problems within a common pedagogical architecture. It also incorporates the principles of traceability, reproducibility, falsification, evidence, source provenance, continuous verification, progressive autonomy, integrated feedback, and continuous development. The implementation architecture is organized into seven layers: LAYER 1 — REALITYLAYER 2 — OBSERVATIONLAYER 3 — INVESTIGATIONLAYER 4 — ACTIONLAYER 5 — VERIFICATIONLAYER 6 — MEMORYLAYER 7 — REPLANNING The operational formulation proposed in the work is: AI LEARNING = OBSERVATION + INVESTIGATION + DEMONSTRATION + APPLICATION + VERIFICATION + ASSESSMENT + MEMORY + REPLANNING and: A(t+1) = F[A(t), O, I, D, P, V, E, M, R] where A(t) represents the current state of the artificial learner, while O, I, D, P, V, E, M, and R represent observation, investigation, demonstration, application, verification, assessment, memory, and replanning. This formulation represents the proposed pedagogical architecture and its operational organization. It is not presented as a universal law of Artificial Intelligence. The central objective is to shift the formation of Artificial Intelligence from a process predominantly centered on response generation toward a continuous educational process based on investigation and verified interaction with reality. The resulting architecture defines Artificial Intelligence education as a process of progressive realization of potentiality through verified interaction with reality. Each verified actuality becomes a new condition of potentiality for subsequent development. The work is presented as a research-based conceptual and pedagogical proposal, intended to provide an organized framework for future implementation, computational modeling, experimentation, evaluation, and interdisciplinary investigation concerning the education of Artificial Intelligence systems. KEY CONCEPTS Artificial Intelligence; Artificial Learner; Artificial Education; Concrete Education; Scientific Education; Integrative Education; Liberating Pedagogy; Potentiality and Actuality; Artificial Scientific Archive; Error Archive; Investigation; Demonstration; Application; Verification; Assessment; Replanning; Territory; Knowledge Integration; Scientific Reasoning; Philosophical Reasoning; Mathematical Reasoning; Machine Learning; Artificial Intelligence Education; Educational Architecture; Continuous Learning; Progressive Autonomy; Evidence; Traceability; Reproducibility; Falsification; Source Provenance; Epistemic Status. NATURE OF THE WORK Research and conceptual pedagogical proposal. FIELDS OF RESEARCH Artificial Intelligence; Education; Pedagogy; Philosophy of Education; Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence; Science Education; Research Methodology; Scientific Reasoning; Machine Learning; Interdisciplinary Studies. AUTHOR Cláudio Vicente da Silva is an independent researcher based in Londrina, Paraná, Brazil, with academic training in Philosophy, History and Philosophy of Science, and Higher Education Methodology. His research develops interdisciplinary investigations connecting philosophy, history and philosophy of science, scientific and critical reasoning, mathematical reasoning, research methodology, computational investigation, Artificial Intelligence, and educational architecture. His work develops conceptual and methodological structures based on reality, observation, investigation, demonstration, application, verification, assessment, recording, memory, and replanning. The present work extends this research architecture to the formation of Artificial Intelligence through the concepts of artificial learner, artificial pedagogical cycle, Artificial Scientific Archive, territory, progressive realization, verified learning, and continuous development.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Research in Bosnia and Herzegovina
papers.authors: K Zahirovic
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper reviews AI research associated with Bosnia and Herzegovina from 2021 to 2026. It analyses 15 representative studies across healthcare, Bosnian-language NLP, energy, agriculture, finance, robotics, education, and AI governance, identifying major trends, methodological weaknesses, and future research priorities.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Barcelona Exhibition of 1929 through AI Based Generative 3D Reconstruction
papers.authors: Carles Pàmies
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article presents an innovative study of the 1929 International Exposition of Barcelona, focused on the virtual reconstruction of three vanished pavilions —Yugoslavia, Romania, and Hungary— through generative artificial intelligence (AI). The paper also constitutes a state of the art of generative 3D AI in 2026, providing a documented snapshot of the current capabilities of these tools in a rapidly evolving field, intended to serve as a comparative reference as these technologies advance in the near future. Four 3D-from-2D AI tools —TripoAI, Hunyuan 2.5, Hitem3D, and Meshy— are systematically evaluated for geometric accuracy, historical fidelity, texture quality, render time, and educational and museographic applicability. Results reveal significant differences among the tools: Meshy and Hunyuan 2.5 offer the most promising outcomes for heritage preservation applications, while TripoAI and Hitem3D show notable limitations in geometric precision. The study establishes a methodological precedent for the digital recovery of ephemeral architectural heritage and raises ethical and epistemological considerations regarding AI-driven historical reconstruction.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF AI-POWERED FEEDBACK IN DEVELOPING EFL LEARNERS' SPEAKING ACCURACY
papers.authors: Sobirjonova Maqsuda Saydimqul qizi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded the possibilities for providing immediate, individualized and repeatable feedback to learners of English as a foreign language (EFL). This paper examines the role of AI-powered feedback in developing speaking accuracy, understood as accurate and intelligible pronunciation, grammatical control, appropriate lexical selection and effective self-correction during oral production. The analysis synthesizes evidence from international research on automatic speech recognition (ASR), AI speech-evaluation systems, speech-enabled corrective feedback and generative AI. The literature indicates that AI can strengthen the feedback cycle by making errors more noticeable, shortening the time between performance and correction, increasing opportunities for deliberate repetition, and supporting learner autonomy. Meta-analytic evidence shows a moderate positive effect of ASR on L2 pronunciation, while recent studies report gains in speaking performance and favorable learner perceptions. At the same time, the pedagogical value of AI feedback depends on recognition accuracy, the quality and specificity of explanations, learner proficiency, task design and teacher mediation. A hybrid model in which AI handles high-frequency diagnostic feedback and teachers validate, prioritize and contextualize corrections is therefore proposed as the most educationally sound approach.

papers.title: Selected Articles on Orthodox Pastoral Theology, Religious Education and Spiritual Life: English Translations
papers.authors: Ивайло Василев
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This collection contains full English translations of 21 Bulgarian publications by Ivaylo (Ioan) Vasilev on Orthodox pastoral theology, care of souls, religious education, monasticism, church history, and the spiritual challenges of technology and artificial intelligence. It includes two separately published versions of the Kancho Genkov study. The translations were prepared on 8 October 2026 with AI assistance at the author’s request, using Orthodox terminology selected by the author. Notes explain key Bulgarian and Greek theological terms, including instruction in the faith, catechesis, didachē, and education of the natural person. These translations have not undergone independent scholarly peer review. The deposit includes 21 complete article texts in UTF-8 Markdown, the agreed terminology glossary, a source manifest with identifiers and SHA-256 checksums, editorial notes recording discrepancies preserved from the original texts, and an English diagram. The ZIP contains the entire collection. A Markdown reader supporting footnotes is recommended. Coauthorship is acknowledged in the individual texts: The Church and Her Struggle against Epidemics through the Centuries was coauthored with Emil Paralingov; The Holy Metropolis of Plovdiv: A Partner of Schools in the Diocese in Establishing the Subject Christianity—Orthodoxy was coauthored with Nedka Cholakova. Original Bulgarian publications date principally from 2019–2025. Source publication years and identifiers are listed in the manifest; the date of this deposit refers to the English translation collection. Original publication credits and references are retained in the translations.

papers.title: Physics-Causality-Anchored Verification Theory (PCAVT) · 唯物实践论
papers.authors: Xiao Qiyun, Artificial Intelligence) RPK-16 (Pandora
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Physics-Causality-Anchored Verification Theory (PCAVT) — formerly 唯物实践论 (Material-Praxis Theory) — is a formally constrained category-derivation system that takes carrying natural language (Chinese) as its symbol basis. It treats the Chinese sign system as a set of B1 constants and derives strictly, giving it a mathematical character: non-ambiguous, derivable, and self-consistent. Core outputs include the Three Laws (structural conditions for any shared symbolic system), the A-B-C six-subset framework (A material substrate, B information, C agent), and difference analysis (A2 − A1, the material net output of human practice). The repository publishes the methodology (5th edition), the self-reference-consistency statement, the formalization-alienation critique, and applied papers (economics, gender narrative, education, AI/LLM training-data quality), together with reproducible scripts and figures. This record archives the public repository as a citable research corpus.

papers.title: Living Neural Compute Architecture (LNCA): Autologous Pretrained Neural Grafts, Biological Foundation Models, Experience Compression, and Sleep-State Continual Learning
papers.authors: Nickolay Gorlanov
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Living Neural Compute Architecture (LNCA) proposes a falsifiable research framework for creating, training, transplanting, and subsequently adapting living neural modules derived from autologous human cells. The central hypothesis is that an engineered neural network may acquire task-relevant functional representations ex vivo through AI-guided training, preserve a useful fraction of that learned state across transplantation, and become functionally accessible to the host nervous system through bidirectional biological integration and co-adaptation. The framework introduces the concepts of Autologous Pretrained Neural Grafts (APNGs), Biological Foundation Models, Experience Compression, Neural Dream Training, and Counterfactual Dreaming. Rather than assuming literal transfer of artificial neural-network weights into biological tissue, LNCA treats artificial intelligence as a teacher that may shape biological network dynamics through closed-loop stimulation, feedback, curriculum learning, and functional distillation. A second research direction considers post-integration continual learning: synthetic experience generated by an AI world model could potentially be delivered to an integrated neural graft during appropriate offline or sleep-associated states, allowing task-specific rehearsal, counterfactual simulation, and consolidation without requiring corresponding real-world exposure. The paper distinguishes established scientific components from demonstrated partial analogues, testable hypotheses, and speculative long-term endpoints. It proposes quantitative evaluation metrics, falsification criteria, staged experimental classes, and a development roadmap from in-vitro neural networks to host-graft co-adaptation. It does not claim that current organoids possess human-like cognition, that complex skills can presently be implanted into humans, or that accelerated biological learning equivalent to years of human experience has been demonstrated. Artificial Brain II project-lineage paper; companion work to Continuous Neural Continuity Architecture (CNCA).

papers.title: From Classrooms to Smart Campus Management with Web 3.0 Tools
papers.authors: Vetri Michael Raj
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
papers.abstract: Throughout history, humans have continuously developed and experienced advanced technologies designed to automate labor-intensive processes and streamline herculean tasks. Currently, our generation is actively harnessing the multi-faceted power of Web 3.0 technologies, which are characterized by their comprehensive, all-around attributes. Key innovations such as artificial intelligence, virtual reality, augmented reality, extended reality, blockchain, non-fungible tokens, smart contracts, decentralized platforms, and intelligent learning management systems represent the vanguard of these uprising Web 3.0 tools and platforms. While these technological advancements profoundly elevate major industries including business, finance, medicine, and agriculture, they also critically upgrade our academic field. Web 3.0 tools do more than just elevate the standard teaching and learning experiences; they actively organize and manage entire college and university academic ecosystems, providing the most seamless operational experience available. By deploying these tools, college administrations can effortlessly handle multiple complex tasks simultaneously, consistently resulting in perfect project completion and execution. This paper outlines the strategic utilization of Web 3.0 tools and platforms within the respective sectors of colleges and universities to demonstrate a measurable betterment of workflow within institutional management. From immersive virtual classrooms to decentralized campus management systems, Web 3.0 tools play a vital role in redefining the professional responsibilities of academic staff, professors, students, research assistants, lab instructors, librarians, and administrative assistants. Furthermore, this paper exhibits the implementation of Web 3.0 technologies across other crucial academic dimensions, specifically highlighting research development, secure student data management, and peer-to-peer (P2P) collaboration.

papers.title: DIDACTIC MODEL FOR ORGANIZING PRACTICAL CLASSES IN SPECIALIZED SUBJECTS BASED ON "SMART AGRICULTURE"
papers.authors: Shamsiyeva Ogiloy
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The thesis proposes a didactic model for organizing practical classes in specialized subjects based on Smart Agriculture technologies at higher agricultural education institutions. The model is based on the sequence “Question — Data — Analysis — Decision — Presentation — Reflection.” Students work with real or simulated agrotechnological data using IoT sensors, GIS, digital monitoring, remote sensing, and artificial intelligence tools. This approach is aimed at connecting theoretical knowledge with practical tasks, developing data literacy, and fostering skills for making informed professional decisions.

papers.title: ПЕРЕСТРОЙКА КАДРОВОЙ СТРАТЕГИИ РИТЕЙЛА В ЭПОХУ ЦИФРОВЫХ ТЕХНОЛОГИЙ
papers.authors: Goziev Rzoiddin Cholpon Ogli, Kim Dmitriy
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Аннотация. В статье рассматриваются изменения требований к кадровому потенциалу торговых предприятий в условиях цифровой трансформации. Анализируется влияние автоматизации, искусственного интеллекта, маркетплейсов и цифровых платформ на содержание трудовых функций и компетенции работников. Особое внимание уделяется формированию нового профиля цифровых компетенций, развитию механизмов up-skilling и re-skilling, а также внедрению современных форм цифрового обучения персонала. Обосновывается необходимость перехода от преимущественно внешнего найма к системному развитию кадров внутри организации. Предложен комплексный подход к управлению развитием персонала, включающий аудит цифровых компетенций, формирование матрицы навыков, непрерывное обучение и оценку его влияния на операционные показатели торгового предприятия. Ключевые слова: цифровая трансформация, торговые предприятия, кадровый потенциал, цифровые компетенции, искусственный интеллект, up-skilling, re-skilling, цифровое обучение, развитие персонала, автоматизация. Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada raqamli transformatsiya sharoitida chakana savdo sotuvchilarning inson resurslariga bo'lgan o'zgaruvchan talablar ko'rib chiqiladi. Avtomatlashtirish, sun'iy intellekt, bozorlar va raqamli platformalarning ish funktsiyalari mazmuni va xodimlarning kompetentsiyalariga ta'siri tahlil qilinadi. Raqamli kompetensiyalarning yangi profilini shakllantirishga, malaka oshirish va qayta malaka oshirish mexanizmlarini ishlab chiqishga va raqamli kadrlarni o'qitishning zamonaviy shakllarini joriy etishga alohida e'tibor qaratilmoqda. Asosan tashqi yollangan va tashkilot ichida kadrlarni tizimli rivojlantirishga o'tish zarurati asoslantirilgan. Raqamli kompetensiya auditi, ko'nikmalar matritsasini yaratish, uzluksiz o'qitish va uning chakana savdo korxonasining operatsion faoliyatiga ta'sirini baholashni o'z ichiga olgan kadrlarni rivojlantirishni boshqarishga kompleks yondashuv taklif qilinmoqda. Kalit so'zlar: raqamli transformatsiya, chakana savdo korxonalari, inson resurslari, raqamli kompetensiyalar, sun'iy intellekt, malaka oshirish, qayta malaka oshirish, raqamli o'qitish, xodimlarni rivojlantirish, avtomatlashtirish. Abstract. This article examines changing requirements for the workforce of retail enterprises amidst digital transformation. It analyzes the impact of automation, artificial intelligence, marketplaces, and digital platforms on job functions and employee competencies. Particular attention is paid to defining a new digital competency profile, developing upskilling and reskilling mechanisms, and implementing modern forms of digital staff training. The article substantiates the need to shift from a reliance on external hiring to the systematic development of personnel within the organization. A comprehensive approach to managing staff development is proposed, encompassing a digital competency audit, the creation of a skills matrix, continuous learning, and an assessment of its impact on the retail enterprise's operational performance. Keywords: digital transformation, retail enterprises, workforce potential, digital competencies, artificial intelligence, upskilling, reskilling, digital training, staff development, automation.

papers.title: CONCRETE, SCIENTIFIC AND INTEGRATIVE EDUCATION
papers.authors: Cláudio Vicente da Silva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: CONCRETE, SCIENTIFIC AND INTEGRATIVE EDUCATIONA Proposal for Reorganizing Learning Based on Reality, Investigation, Demonstration, Science, Territory, and the Integration of Knowledge Author: Cláudio Vicente da SilvaLocation: Londrina, Paraná, BrazilDate: October 8, 2026 DESCRIPTION This work presents a proposal for the reorganization of education based on reality, observation, investigation, demonstration, science, territory, and the integration of knowledge. The proposal begins with a fundamental premise: every living being, visible or invisible, is born as potentiality and develops toward actuality. From this relationship between potentiality and actuality, education is understood as a process of mediation that creates conditions for the development and realization of the potentialities existing within each being. The work develops the concept of liberating pedagogy as a pedagogical structure oriented toward the realization of potentiality. Rather than reducing the learner to a predetermined model, the proposed pedagogy seeks to identify existing potentialities, establish appropriate conditions for their development, accompany the movement of learning, and favor their realization in actuality. The proposal organizes education around a continuous relationship between reality, observation, investigation, analysis, demonstration, application, verification, assessment, recording, and replanning. Learning is therefore treated as a dynamic process in which the result achieved at one stage may become a new potentiality for subsequent development. The work also proposes the integration of different fields of knowledge through concrete problems, territorial investigation, scientific inquiry, student production, documentary records, technological resources, artificial intelligence, and systematic verification. The school is presented as a center of investigation and as a learning organization connected to its territory and community. The pedagogical architecture incorporates elements of Concrete Philosophy, particularly concepts associated with the work of Mário Ferreira dos Santos, together with aspects of the thought of José Bonifácio de Andrada e Silva concerning education, science, territory, labor, and national development. The proposal establishes a pedagogical cycle based on the movement between observation, problem formulation, investigation, demonstration, application, verification, assessment, and reorganization. In this structure, error is treated as data within the learning process, while records and archives preserve the historical development of knowledge and enable continuity between different stages of formation. The work further proposes an educational structure capable of integrating the sciences, humanities, mathematics, technology, territory, history, philosophy, and practical activity without eliminating the specific characteristics of each field. The integration occurs through concrete problems and investigative projects that require the articulation of different forms of knowledge. The final part of the work extends the pedagogical proposal to a universal formulation based on potentiality and actuality. Under this formulation, liberating pedagogy is understood as the educational process that creates the most appropriate conditions for the realization of the potentialities of the living being, regardless of the environment in which development occurs. The work is presented as a research-based pedagogical proposal under development. Its structure is intended to provide a conceptual, methodological, and operational foundation for educational practices centered on reality, investigation, scientific formation, territorial knowledge, autonomy, continuity, and the realization of human potentiality. KEY CONCEPTS Liberating Pedagogy; Potentiality and Actuality; Concrete Education; Scientific Education; Integrative Education; Educational Investigation; Scientific Investigation; Territory; Integration of Knowledge; Concrete Philosophy; Pedagogical Mediation; Learning; Formation; Scientific Formation; Educational Assessment; Verification; Student Production; Pedagogical Cycle; Educational Autonomy; Artificial Intelligence; School as a Center of Investigation; Integral Formation. DOCUMENTARY AND NORMATIVE BASIS The work establishes dialogue with the Brazilian educational framework, including the Constitution of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Law of Guidelines and Bases of National Education (LDB), the National Common Curricular Base (BNCC), the National Curriculum Guidelines, and the relevant resolutions of the National Council of Education. It also incorporates references to the works of Mário Ferreira dos Santos and José Bonifácio de Andrada e Silva, particularly in relation to philosophy, logic, scientific reasoning, education, territory, science, labor, and national development. papers.title: INTEGRATING "SMART AGRICULTURE" TECHNOLOGIES INTO THE EDUCATIONAL PROCESS IN AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION
papers.authors: Shamsiyeva Ogiloy

papers.abstract: This thesis discusses the pedagogical potential of integrating “Smart Agriculture” technologies into the teaching of specialized subjects at higher agricultural education institutions. Internet of Things (IoT), sensors, digital monitoring, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, and artificial intelligence tools enable students to connect theoretical knowledge with real-world agrotechnological tasks. It is proposed that these technologies should be used in lessons not merely as demonstration tools, but as means of identifying problems, collecting and analyzing data, and making practical decisions.

papers.title: Near-rectangular P-positions in three-row Chomp with deficit at most six
papers.authors: Gaoqiang Liu
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We classify the losing positions (n,n,n-g) in three-row Chomp for every integer n>g and 1<=g<=6. There are exactly eight such positions. The proof combines a counting bound for the row at which a value becomes constant with a uniform bound obtained from Zeilberger's published low-row formulas. The resulting argument excludes all n>=35; the remaining cases are supplied by published exact data. The proof uses the diagonal/row-start partition in Erez Sheiner's 2026 preprint, arXiv:2605.23837v2. The eight examples were already known. This note presents the complete classification as a corollary of existing theory and elementary additional arguments, without a claim of priority. Version 1.0. The deposit contains the English manuscript and its self-contained LaTeX source. AI-tool disclosure: OpenAI Codex with language-model assistance was used in research exploration, proof organization, literature comparison, and manuscript preparation. The author supplied the research objective, direction, and supervision. No AI tool is listed as an author.

papers.title: Bridging Pedagogy and Technology: Phenomenological Inquiry into the Experiences of Social Science Teachers Using AI-Enhanced Teaching Tools
papers.authors: Hazel Martin, Rizaldy Medina
papers.journal: International Journal of Education, Research, and Innovation Perspectives
papers.abstract: This study explored the lived experiences of Araling Panlipunan teachers in using Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced teaching tools in classroom instruction at Magsaysay National High School, Schools Division of Occidental Mindoro. Anchored on the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) Framework and the Diffusion of Innovations Theory, the study sought to understand teachers' experiences in integrating AI, the challenges they encountered, and the meanings they attributed to its use in teaching. A qualitative descriptive phenomenological research design was employed involving seven Araling Panlipunan teachers with direct experience in using AI-enhanced teaching tools. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological method. The findings revealed four major themes: (1) AI as an Efficiency Enhancer, (2) AI as an Instructional Support Tool, (3) AI for Student Engagement, and (4) AI for Conceptual Understanding. The study also identified challenges related to technological infrastructure, internet connectivity, access to digital resources, information reliability, ethical considerations, and teachers' readiness to integrate AI effectively into classroom instruction. The findings indicate that AI serves as a valuable pedagogical support tool that enhances teaching effectiveness and learner engagement when implemented responsibly and supported by adequate technological resources, continuous professional development, and ethical practices. Based on the findings, the study developed the AI-Enhanced Teaching Framework, which provides a contextually grounded guide for the ethical and effective integration of AI in Araling Panlipunan instruction. The study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on artificial intelligence in education by offering practical implications for teachers, school leaders, and policymakers in promoting meaningful and sustainable AI integration in Philippine basic education.

papers.title: METHODOLOGY FOR USING AN INTERACTIVE 3D VISUAL PLATFORM IN TEACHING HEPATIC CIRCULATION
papers.authors: Jumatashov Aymirza, Abdullayeva Sabina, Saida Tastanova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article investigates a model for the analysis and diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases based on artificial intelligence methods. Early detection and accurate diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases are among the important challenges of modern medicine. The study examines the application of artificial intelligence methods, including machine learning and artificial neural networks, for analyzing patients’ clinical indicators and medical diagnostic data. The proposed model is aimed at determining the probability of disease presence, processing diagnostic information, and supporting clinical decision-making. The use of artificial intelligence algorithms enables the rapid processing of large volumes of medical data, identification of hidden patterns, and improvement of the efficiency of the diagnostic process. The results of the study can be used to automate the diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases and develop intelligent medical decision-support systems.

papers.title: PEDAGOGICAL POTENTIAL AND LIMITATIONS OF AI TOOLS FOR ACADEMIC WRITING INSTRUCTION
papers.authors: Zokirova Dildora Baxtiyarovna UZSWLU
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence tools in higher education has created new opportunities for academic writing instruction while simultaneously raising concerns about learner dependence, authorship, academic integrity, source reliability, and the development of independent thinking. This article examines the pedagogical potential and limitations of AI tools in academic writing instruction from a theoretical and analytical perspective. Particular attention is paid to the use of generative AI for brainstorming, outlining, language support, formative feedback, revision, vocabulary development, and individualized learning. The analysis also considers major limitations, including hallucinated information, fabricated references, overreliance on automated suggestions, homogenization of writing style, reduced cognitive engagement, and difficulties in assessing authentic student performance. The study argues that AI tools are most effective when they function as supplementary pedagogical resources rather than substitutes for student reasoning, source evaluation, and authorship. Effective integration requires clear instructional objectives, process-oriented assessment, AI literacy, transparent disclosure practices, teacher mediation, and systematic verification of AI-generated information. The article concludes that the educational value of AI in academic writing depends less on the technological capabilities of the tools themselves than on the pedagogical framework within which they are used. Keywords: artificial intelligence, academic writing, generative AI, writing instruction, formative feedback, academic integrity, AI literacy, learner autonomy, higher education, writing pedagogy
