papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Preprint. Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule encoded the Collatz map as an 11-rule rewriting system, collatz-T of the Termination Problem Database, and suggested proving that no matrix or arctic interpretation establishes its termination. We show that natural-number matrix interpretations in the form of Endrullis, Waldmann and Zantema, and arctic interpretations, applied on their own, make no progress on it in any dimension. A natural-number matrix interpretation of collatz-T with all top-left entries at least 1 that weakly orients all 11 rules strictly orients none of them, and so does an arctic interpretation over the natural numbers with finite top-left entries, for collatz-T and also for the system of the modulo-8 conjecture; hence rule removal with these interpretations alone removes no rule at any stage. The same holds for the reversed systems and, for collatz-T, for the matrix interpretations of Hofbauer and Waldmann that compare corner entries. Without the condition on the top-left entries, natural-number interpretations in the form of Endrullis, Waldmann and Zantema remove no rule in the top forms of Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule, and natural-number and arctic reduction pairs remove no pair of the essential component of the dependency pair problem. In dimension at most 2, the results for rule removal in the form of Endrullis, Waldmann and Zantema follow from earlier work of Valbuena. The main theorems are kernel-checked in Lean 4, using only the three standard axioms; the results on transformations are computer-assisted. The general core form of matrix interpretations, lexicographic comparisons, other semirings, and proof pipelines in which other techniques act first are not covered. None of the results settles the Collatz conjecture. Lean code, computations and verification logs are on GitHub. Prepared with substantial assistance from generative AI (Anthropic Claude); see the disclosure in the paper. Not yet reviewed by human experts.

papers.title: Chatbots as instruments for supporting the academic and organisational work of master’s students in professional education – future teachers of specialised disciplines
papers.authors: Iryna Dobroskok
papers.journal: Scientific Bulletin of Mukachevo State University Series “Pedagogy and Psychology”
papers.abstract: The aim was to provide a scientific substantiation of the functional potential of chatbots as an instrumental basis for optimising the activities of master’s students in the field of professional education. The methodology was grounded in a synthesis of the analytical-comparative approach, the method of classifying intelligent services, a regulatory and legal analysis of state recommendations, and a case study of Ukrainian practical experience in digitalisation. Through the systematisation and analytical interpretation of verified sectoral data, the paper elucidated the global dynamics of artificial intelligence adaptation, which enabled the identification of a geopolitical asymmetry between the intensive deployment of technologies originating from the United States of America and the regulated approach adopted by European countries. It has been demonstrated that the integration of specialised services, such as analytical search engines and cognitive assistants, transforms the role of the master’s student from a reproductive content consumer into a strategic curator of the scientific process. It has been revealed that Ukrainian higher education institutions exhibit high adaptability to digital challenges through the deployment of their own intelligent ecosystems, in particular the projects “Vstup Helper”, “Admissions Committee of VIKNU”, “KPI Rozklad Bot”, “Personal account SumDU”, and “Info Science Bot”, which serve as effective methodological prototypes for future teachers. The critical importance of implementing the state recommendations of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine and the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine has been established, as these lay the foundation for a new ethical culture and academic integrity within the context of Industry 4.0. An analysis of the functional capabilities of specialised platforms confirmed the readiness of master’s students to design their own didactic tutor bots for teaching complex technical disciplines. The practical significance of the work lies in the formulation of a scientifically substantiated roadmap for the implementation of intelligent agents in professional education, which can be utilised by teachers, higher education institution administrators, and educational software developers to enhance the quality of specialist training

papers.title: Conceptual foundations of the digital transformation of professional training for future computer science teachers
papers.authors: Світлана Яцюк, Valentyna Yunchyk, Iryna Svitnytska
papers.journal: Scientific Bulletin of Mukachevo State University Series “Pedagogy and Psychology”
papers.abstract: The relevance of the study was conditioned by the need for a systematic rethinking of the professional training of future computer science teachers in the context of the spread of generative artificial intelligence, educational analytics, and digital educational ecosystems. The purpose of the study was to substantiate the conceptual foundations of digital transformation of professional training of future computer science teachers and determine the logic of interaction of its key components. Critical and comparative analysis of scientific sources and international framework documents, system analysis, conceptualisation, structural and functional modelling, pedagogical design, and forecasting were used. As a result, the difference between digitalisation and digital transformation of professional training was clarified and the author’s definition of the studied phenomenon as a systematic modernisation of goals, content, methodology, environment, pedagogical interaction, and assessment was proposed. The interdependence of technological and pedagogical development, the need for continuous updating of digital competencies, integration of digital pedagogy and information technologies, personalisation and advanced updating of professional training were established. The system of principles of consistency, advanced development, innovation, pedagogical expediency, adaptability, openness, academic integrity, digital security, human-centredness, and continuous professional development was substantiated. A conceptual structure was developed in which the target, methodological, content and technological, organisational and environmental, activity-based and practical, and evaluation and effective components were combined with the influence of external and internal factors. Comparison with previous studies determined the scientific contribution of the concept as a transition from fragmented use of digital tools to a holistic model of transformation of computer science teacher training. The practical significance of the results lay in the possibility of their use by higher education institutions in updating the curricula, designing a digital educational environment, and methodological support for the training of future computer science teachers

papers.title: MAPEAMENTO SISTEMÁTICO: ESCALAS DE RASTREIO DO TRANSTORNO DO ESPECTRO AUTISTA E MODELAGEM MATEMÁTICA
papers.authors: Natalia Gouvea, Maria Clicia Castro, Vera Maria B. Werneck, Rosa Maria Esteves Moreira Da Costa
papers.journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação
papers.abstract: Early diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is essential to enable timely therapeutic and educational interventions. However, the screening process still faces challenges related to the subjectivity of assessments, the diversity of available instruments, and uncertainties in the interpretation of results. This article presents a systematic mapping of the literature on instruments and scales used for ASD screening, their main limitations, and the use of technological and mathematical modeling approaches to support the diagnostic process. Publications from 2014 to 2025 were analyzed in the ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, PubMed, Virtual Health Library, and CAPES Portal databases. The initial search identified 1,155 studies, of which 36 were included in the final mapping. The results revealed 26 instruments and limitations related to subjectivity, cross-cultural differences, costs, specialized training, and borderline cases. Approaches based on artificial intelligence, fuzzy logic, and expert systems were also identified. The findings highlight gaps in the representation of uncertainty and indicate the potential of mathematical modeling to complement existing instruments and support the interpretation of ASD screening results.

papers.title: PEMANFAATAN CHATBOT JUBIR.AI DALAM EFISIENSI LAYANAN PUBLIK PADA KANTOR DPMPTSP (DINAS PENANAMAN MODAL PELAYANAN TERPADU SATU PINTU) KOTA MAKASSAR
papers.authors: Sulfikar Sulfikar, Alam Tauhid Syukur, Deasy Mauliana
papers.abstract: Digital transformation demands that government agencies provide fast, responsive, and easily accessible public services, including business licensing services. This study aims to analyze the utilization of the Jubir.ai Chatbot in improving the efficiency and quality of public services at the Makassar City DPMPTSP Office, as well as identifying supporting and inhibiting factors in its implementation. This study uses a qualitative approach with a descriptive research type. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 10 key informants, participatory observation, and documentation studies, then analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing, with data validity maintained through source and method triangulation. The results show that the Jubir.ai Chatbot contributes to accelerating licensing information responses, reducing face-to-face queues, and lightening the workload of front-office staff, thereby making services more efficient. However, the effectiveness of chatbot utilization is still influenced by the public's digital literacy level, network infrastructure constraints, and the need for regular knowledge-base updates. This study recommends strengthening the integration of the Jubir.ai Chatbot with the Online Single Submission (OSS) system and enhancing socialization to optimize the benefits of digital licensing services in Makassar City. ABSTRAK Transformasi digital menuntut instansi pemerintah untuk menghadirkan layanan publik yang cepat, responsif, dan mudah diakses oleh masyarakat, termasuk layanan perizinan berusaha. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pemanfaatan Chatbot Jubir.ai dalam meningkatkan efisiensi dan kualitas layanan publik di Kantor DPMPTSP Kota Makassar, serta mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambat dalam implementasinya. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis penelitian deskriptif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam terhadap 10 orang informan kunci, observasi partisipatif, dan studi dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui tahapan kondensasi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan dengan keabsahan data yang dijaga melalui triangulasi sumber serta metode. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Chatbot Jubir.ai berkontribusi nyata dalam mempercepat respons informasi perizinan, mengurangi antrean tatap muka, serta meringankan beban kerja petugas front office sehingga pelayanan menjadi lebih efisien. Namun demikian, efektivitas pemanfaatan chatbot masih dipengaruhi oleh tingkat literasi digital masyarakat, keterbatasan infrastruktur jaringan, dan kebutuhan pembaruan basis pengetahuan (knowledge base) secara berkala. Penelitian ini merekomendasikan penguatan integrasi Chatbot Jubir.ai dengan sistem Online Single Submission (OSS) serta peningkatan sosialisasi kepada masyarakat guna mengoptimalkan manfaat digitalisasi layanan perizinan di Kota Makassar.

papers.title: Portable Devices for Diagnosis of Sleep-Disordered Breathing
papers.authors: CDA-AMC
papers.abstract: What Is the Issue? Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) includes a range of conditions that make it difficult to breathe while sleeping and can lead to heart failure, neurodegenerative diseases, cognitive impairment, and poor quality of life. Many people in Canada have obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), a type of SDB, but they often remain undiagnosed. The gold standard for diagnosing SDB is polysomnography (PSG), which is referred to as a level 1 test. PSG is conducted in a sleep laboratory and attended by a sleep technician. Because access to this test can vary, is often limited geographically, and can have long wait times, portable devices for diagnosing SDB have emerged for use at home and may help speed up diagnosis and access to treatment. Provincial decision-makers requested this report to assess the evidence available on using portable devices for diagnosing SDB. The findings will inform whether results from these devices can be used with confidence as an alternative to PSG. What Did We Do? We conducted a rapid review to identify and summarize evidence that compared the diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility of these devices as well as evidence-based guidelines published in the past 5 years. Two clinical experts reviewed the report, and 1 expert identified devices to supplement the literature available. We conducted a horizon scan to identify any new devices emerging in the field. What Did We Find? A total of 92 portable sleep devices were identified. Ten systematic reviews were identified that examined the diagnostic accuracy or clinical utility of more than 60 portable diagnostic sleep tests compared to those of PSG. Five guidelines with recommendations for adults or people who are pregnant were identified, of which 1 guideline reported on 6 specific portable diagnostic sleep devices. An expert identified an additional 26 devices to consider. A Canadian guideline on the diagnosis of OSA in children was published in 2026 while this report was being written, and relevant information from that guideline has been included in this report. Sleep diagnostic devices have traditionally been categorized using levels. Unlike PSG studies, tests using devices categorized as level 2, 3, or 4 are unattended by a technician. Level 3 devices usually have at least 3 channels that measure airflow, respiratory effort, and oximetry. Airflow-based measurement is considered necessary to inform diagnosis. Level 4 devices usually have 1 channel measuring blood oxygen saturation and are not generally used for diagnostic purposes. Some emerging or novel devices fall outside these levels. Of the 92 devices identified in this report, 25 were identified as having active licensing from Health Canada and are currently being manufactured. Current evidence was identified for 6 of these devices. For adults suspected of having OSA, level 3 devices and some wearables (e.g., WatchPAT devices) were generally reported in systematic review evidence as having adequate sensitivity, while level 4 devices tended to have varying sensitivity and specificity. There was less evidence for other devices (e.g., noncontact systems, smartphone-based tools); generally, the evidence reported adequate sensitivity, but specificity varied by factors such as OSA severity and device type. For adults, guidelines recommend level 3 sleep tests for adults with a high pretest probability for moderate to severe OSA and who do not have complicated comorbidities such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; heart failure; neuromuscular conditions; and physical, sensory, and cognitive impairment. The AcuPebble SA100, Sunrise, WatchPAT 300, and WatchPAT ONE are 4 specific devices recommended for assessing people aged older than 16 years; the WatchPAT 300 device is licensed for sale in Canada. There are several evidence gaps regarding the use of portable devices for the diagnosis of SDB in specific populations. Yet, for people who are pregnant, guidelines state that home sleep apnea testing, but not overnight pulse oximetry, can be considered, and for children aged between 6 and 17 years without significant comorbidities, a Canadian guideline published in 2026 recommends PSG to diagnose OSA. It also recommends that overnight oximetry (level 4 testing) should not be used. What Does This Mean? Some portable sleep devices can be considered for the diagnosis of adults suspected of having moderate to severe OSA who do not have comorbidities. Portable sleep devices are generally not recommended for those who have complicated comorbidities. It is also unclear whether these devices work for people of all genders and/or sexes or for people with darker skin tones given that pulse oximetry cannot accurately measure oxygen saturation in melanated skin. Careful consideration should be given to the following points regarding the use of portable sleep devices to diagnose SDB: the patient’s potential SDB severity and the presence of comorbidities; the number of channels the device measures; whether the device uses airflow or indirect measurements potentially generated by artificial intelligence; the accessibility and cost of the device; the security of the patient sleep data collected; whether devices and software are regularly updated or out of use; and the training or education required to support patients administering tests at home and to interpret sleep test results.

papers.title: Automated end-station at the soft X-ray beamline featuring robotic air-to-ultrahigh-vacuum sample transfer, scanning probe spectroscopy, and machine learning analysis
papers.authors: Keita Hiromori, Masashige Miyamoto, Masafumi Horio, Takeru Nakashima, Yasunobu Ando, Masato Kotsugi, Iwao Matsuda
papers.abstract: Driven by the growing integration of artificial intelligence and robotics in experimental science, we redefine the execution of user experiments at synchrotron soft X-ray beamlines by developing a highly automated end-station that can be operated without on-site staff. Installed at beamline BL08U of NanoTerasu, the system comprises four chamber units and two robots that automatically transfer samples from ambient air to an ultrahigh vacuum measurement stage for spectroscopic evaluations, before returning them to their original locations post-measurement. Soft X-ray absorption spectra are automatically acquired once programmed by scanning the micro-focused beam over the designated sample area, followed by automated evaluation using machine learning techniques such as principal-component analysis, multidimensional scaling, t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, and uniform manifold approximation and projection. The high-throughput data are systematically accumulated in the database for remote user examination. This unstaffed end-station provides efficient beamtime for users and allows beamline scientists/technicians to pursue more human and creative endeavors.

papers.title: Generative AI Steering and Human Authoring: Complementary Search-as-Learning Scaffolds in Cross-Session Aggregated Academic Search
papers.authors: Milad Momeni, Orland Hoeber
papers.abstract: Aggregated academic search interfaces combine resources from heterogeneous sources, such as scholarly libraries and reference encyclopedias, into a single workspace. Such tasks frequently span multiple sessions, requiring learners to return to and resume work after hours or days. End-of-session consolidation, the activity of organizing and synthesizing gathered information so it can be resumed later, is important in this setting but underexplored in search-as-learning. Generative AI (GenAI) has the potential to make consolidation more efficient, but it may also shift cognitive work away from the learner. This study compares two consolidation scaffolds embedded in the workspace framework of an existing academic search interface that aggregates and clusters saved search results from two different sources (our university library and Wikipedia), which was developed in earlier work. STAIS (Steerable AI Summaries) provides a workspace enhancement that produces GenAI summaries that users can correct, reorganize, and fact-check, automating parts of the consolidation activity. NT (Note-Taking) provides a workspace enhancement that includes rich-text note editors that learners can use to author their own consolidations of what they have found. In a controlled between-subjects study (n=36), participants completed two sessions one week apart while searching an unfamiliar topic using either STAIS or NT. The two conditions produced contrasting post-resumption outcome profiles: STAIS supported faster task resumption and was associated with broader conceptual coverage and higher self-reported domain knowledge, whereas NT was associated with richer inter-concept connections and higher self-reported certainty.

papers.title: ROAM: Reinforcement Learning Optimized Adaptive Moving Target Defense for Smart Grid
papers.authors: Mohammad Zakaria Haider, Prabin Mali, Muhammad Nadeem, Sumit Paudyal, Fei Ding, Mohammad Ashiqur Rahman
papers.abstract: Smart grids rely on distributed phasor measurement units (PMUs) and wide-area communication networks whose data-acquisition pipelines are vulnerable to stealthy false data injection (FDI) attacks that evade conventional bad-data detection (BDD). Moving target defense (MTD) counters this exposure by continuously remapping sensor identities, but existing schemes apply static or pre-scheduled randomization and are each constrained by a single failure mode: seed-based methods are fast yet fragile to key compromise, while machine learning (ML) based prediction methods are resilient yet incur prohibitive latency. Neither adapts its randomization to live threat evidence. This paper presents ROAM, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) driven MTD framework in which a deep Q-network (DQN) agent continuously re-optimizes the sensor-to-ID mapping at the aggregation layer. At each decision step, the agent selects the deception coverage, flags the specific sensors to remap, and sets the split of the remapped sensors between seed-based and ML-prediction-based recovery, without modifying PMU hardware and while preserving IEEE C37.118 compatibility. On held-out BDD-compliant FDI scenarios across the IEEE 14-, 57-, and 118- bus systems, ROAM keeps the percentage of stealthy attacks below 3% while sustaining detection rates above 93%. Against an adaptive soft actor-critic (SAC) attacker that observes the defender's configuration, ROAM keeps stealthy attacks below 2.6% with detection above 92%. Hardware-in-the-loop testing on an OPAL-RT platform confirms real-time feasibility, with sub-18ms average shuffle execution and an average reshuffle blind window of 2.6% of the 3-s decision cycle.

papers.title: MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis
papers.authors: Ximing Lu, Aviral Kumar, Jan Kautz, Yejin Choi, David Acuna
papers.abstract: Data-centric scaling of RLVR has focused on collecting or generating verifiable training problems. However, corpus size alone does not determine whether the dataset provides a useful learning signal for a target policy. To guide the synthesis of effective RLVR data, we experimentally characterize dataset effectiveness as a function of its problems, the target policy, and the training rollout budget. Under this characterization, we show that a large open-source math corpus pooled from widely used RLVR datasets falls almost entirely into a zero-advantage trap: for a fixed target policy and rollout budget, roughly 88% of its problems are solved in every rollout or failed in every rollout. Filtering concentrates what remains, but it can only select, discarding the hard problems. Effective synthetic problems should therefore require the reasoning operations and compositions required to solve those hard problems. Yet their difficulty must be calibrated, so that some rollouts succeed, some fail, and at least one correct solution fits within the training budget. Prompting a teacher to vary hard problems directly does not achieve this. Guided by these empirical principles, we introduce MagicBeanStalk, a top-down decomposition and bottom-up recursive data-synthesis algorithm that grows seed problems into families of substantively new, policy- and budget-calibrated training problems while preserving the seeds' reasoning blueprints. Across 8 math benchmarks, continual RLVR on MagicBeanStalk problems improves gpt-oss-120b from 61.2 to 69.8 (+8.6) and DeepSeek v4Flash from 72.4 to 77.9 (+5.4) on a 16K-token budget. Training on the full 78K source corpus improves by only +1.1 and its best filtered real data subset by +5.8. In finance, we synthesize over 14K verifiable problems from only 340 solutions and improve over base by 6.9 and 2.4 points on SecQue and FinanceBench, respectively.

papers.title: Structural and Representational Agency in LLM-Driven Timbre Generation and Interpolation
papers.authors: Joseph Cameron, Alan F. Blackwell
papers.abstract: Generative creative interfaces routinely report the user's position within a space of possibilities. Such displays imply that the quantities shown were measured from the artefact; in a growing class of systems they are instead predicted by a language model describing its own output, and the two are indistinguishable on screen. Most creative domains lack an agreed measurement against which such a self-report can be checked; audio admits one. In a measurement study of a working LLM-driven timbre interface, what a user can cause proves separable from what the interface reports. The first is exactly characterisable: the reachable set is a zonotope whose dimension increases by one per sound placed, so the space the model may act within is demonstrably the user's own. The second is inaccurate. The displayed position differs from measurement by approximately three times the width of that region, and the error has two independent sources: model-predicted coordinates, whose accuracy varies twofold between the two models evaluated, and the interpolation step, which arises from combining synthesiser parameters and is unaffected by model quality. End to end, 26 of 36 refinement instructions produced no perceptible change, and under the weaker model the facility performed no action while reporting convergence. Effective agency (what a user can cause) and epistemic agency (whether they can know it) are therefore separable and independently engineered: structurally enforced constraints survive model failure, whereas guarantees resting on the model's own report do not. The failure mode that remains is silence presented as success. We close with a short protocol for building and auditing such displays.

papers.title: ORCAGen: Orchestrating Context-Aware Malware Deception with RAG-Guided Generative AI
papers.authors: Shamima Ahmed, Md Sajidul Islam Sajid, Teryl Taylor, Frederico Araujo, Tariqul Islam
papers.abstract: Malware defenses often remove or isolate suspicious programs as quickly as possible. While effective for containment, this approach can also waste an opportunity to observe attacker behavior and deploy targeted countermeasures. ORCAGen takes a different approach: it uses GenAI to build malware-specific deception playbooks offline, validates them before deployment, and enforces only the verified logic at runtime. ORCAGen combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with structured prompt engineering to generate both proof-of-concept (PoC) malware and corresponding deception orchestration code. A curated knowledge base (KB) of malware procedures and active defense strategies grounds the generation process, helping the LLM produce threat-specific and executable deception logic rather than generic or hallucinated outputs. The generated PoC malware provides a safe and reproducible way to test whether a deception strategy can disrupt, redirect, or suppress targeted malware behavior before the strategy is added to the runtime playbook. We evaluate ORCAGen across GPT-4o, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Qwen3-Coder, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 using execution success, hallucination rate, refinement effort, deception effectiveness, and runtime overhead. The evaluation covers synthesized malware scenarios and 150 real-world malware samples across keyloggers, information stealers, and ransomware. Across the evaluated scenarios, GPT-5.5 required the fewest refinements and produced no observed hallucinated APIs, while Gemini 3.5 Flash achieved the lowest response time and runtime overhead. The results show that RAG-guided structured prompting can support the scalable construction of malware-specific deception playbooks that remain lightweight and deterministic during runtime enforcement.

papers.title: Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model-Skill Co-Evolution
papers.authors: Yuhan Liu, Xiyao Ma, Zhongkai Sun, Xu Han, Chengyuan Ma, Benjamin Z. Yao, Chenlei Guo
papers.abstract: Skills, reusable procedural guidance added at inference, can substantially improve LLM downstream performance (Li et al., 2026). Prior work retrieves skills from a bank by semantic relevance, then uses them as inference-time patches or for model distillation. The individual utility of each skill, however, is largely neglected. We first show that, in on-policy distillation where skill-conditioned policies serve as teachers, fewer than 25% of retrieved skills provide useful distillation signals. We then propose SGUID, a method for selecting a compact subset of skills for distillation. SGUID retains a skill only if it consistently yields effective learning signals during training. The selected skills are then distilled to produce a better model. Our results show that not all skills are worth distilling. Across four models from the Olmo and Qwen families, distilling 6 selected skills matches or exceeds full-bank distillation in mean avg@12 on three of the four models, and on all four after a second round that distills 3 newly selected skills, while the full banks are up to 11x larger. Importantly, SGUID supports stable model-skill co-evolution: after a distillation round, a new candidate bank is curated from the updated model's rollouts, and SGUID selects which skills to internalize next. In the second round, this loop selects 3 new skills and improves Qwen3-8B from 64.3% to 66.3%. The selection step is essential for stability: on Qwen3-4B, naively updating the model with unfiltered skills degrades performance, including a 0.3 percentage point drop on HMMT25, whereas SGUID improves HMMT25 by 0.5 points after the first round and 1.1 points after the second. These results identify skill selection as the key mechanism for stable model-skill co-evolution.

papers.title: Learning Probabilistic Logic Programs with Functional Gradient Guided Language Models
papers.authors: Saurabh Mathur, Sahil Sidheekh, Bhavan Vasu, Farbod Tavakkoli, Prasad Tadepalli, Kristian Kersting B, Sriraam Natarajan
papers.abstract: Declarative logic programs offer a powerful and interpretable abstraction for encoding relational structure and neurosymbolic reasoning, by expressing dependencies as weighted compositional rules. However, inducing them from data remains fundamentally hard, bottlenecked by the combinatorial explosion of symbolic search spaces. LLMs have recently emerged as powerful hypothesis generators, but when used in isolation, they lack the capacity to do systematic inductive reasoning needed to reliably synthesize valid programs that fit complex relational distributions. We introduce grasp (Gradient-boosted Synthesis of Probabilistic logic programs), a neurosymbolic framework that casts relational structure learning as functional gradient boosting in which the weak learner is a first-order rule and the intractable inner search is delegated to an LLM proposal oracle. We evaluate grasp on four relational benchmarks spanning molecular toxicity prediction (Tox21), mutagenesis, and citation matching (Cora), and show that it improves over purely symbolic, neural, and LLM-based baselines, while producing interpretable weighted rule ensembles. By replacing combinatorial search with gradient-guided LLM hypothesis generation, grasp retains boosting guarantees without sacrificing the transparency of symbolic outputs.

papers.title: Fixed-Reference Pose Residuals for Measuring Cross-Dataset Cue Transfer in Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation
papers.authors: Bowen Yang, Xinliang Xiao, Wenjing Zhang, Li Yang, Wei Zhou
papers.abstract: Social and service robots in public spaces need to anticipate which nearby person is about to approach and touch them, so that a response can be prepared before contact. It is largely unknown which cues support this anticipation when a model trained with one robot is used on another robot at a different site. We study this question with a fixed-reference pose residual (FRPR) model: a geometry predictor built from the person's bounding box and mask is trained and frozen, and a temporal network then learns from body pose an additive correction to its logit, so that every prediction splits exactly into a geometry term and a pose term. Between two public egocentric datasets recorded by different robots, HUI360 and SSUP-A, with every choice made on source data, the pose correction raised average precision (AP) from 0.277 to 0.321 from SSUP-A to HUI360 and gave no measurable gain in the opposite direction; the same asymmetry held over a stronger, source-selected geometry reference. Freezing gave no AP advantage over joint training, and simple geometric baselines and tree ensembles remained competitive or better, so the construction serves measurement rather than prediction accuracy. A head-orientation residual added small gains in both directions. Post hoc, whether a person faces the camera kept its discriminative direction across datasets, whereas head pitch reversed. With thresholds chosen on source data, the neural models that use geometry detected at most 17% of target interactions. Code and processed data are available at https://github.com/WeiZhou96/FRPR-interaction-anticipation.

papers.title: Poster: A Preliminary Study of LLM Distillation Inference
papers.authors: Edward Chen, Yuntao Du
papers.abstract: Unauthorized model distillation, in which a model is trained on the outputs of a proprietary large language model (LLM), is a growing threat to model providers. We study distillation inference: determining whether a suspect model was distilled from another model or trained independently. We formulate this problem as a hypothesis test and estimate the behavior expected under each hypothesis by training shadow models: distilled shadow models learn from the teacher's reasoning traces, whereas independent shadow models learn only from reference answers. The auditor measures how closely each model predicts the teacher's reasoning outputs and then uses the shadow models to convert the suspect's score into a calibrated p-value. In a preliminary study using Qwen2.5-7B as the teacher and Llama-3.2-3B for the suspects, our test achieves a true positive rate of 1.0 at a significance level of 0.02. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using distillation inference to detect distillation attacks.

papers.title: The learner who does not learn: when optimizing a pedagogical metric degrades LLM tutoring
papers.authors: Daniel Domínguez Figaredo, Rafael Fernández De la Cruz
papers.abstract: It is assumed that a natural way to improve the pedagogical quality of large language model tutors is to define a metric of instructional performance and fine-tune the model against it. To test this strategy, we designed a metric of pedagogical adaptivity that scores each instructional decision in a learning sequence against the conditions of the learning situation, which is the standard used for automated pedagogical scoring. We audited a frontier tutor across 2,000 learner scenarios, corrected its weakest cases by fine-tuning an open-weights proxy, and asked 31 trained educators to rate the pedagogical alignment of the outputs blind, before and after correction. The metric increased from +0.05 to +0.42 for the corrected cases, while the expert ratings decreased from 4.46 to 3.03, with the unmodified controls remaining unchanged and a base-proxy control ruling out the change of model. The tutor performed worse because any metric that scores decisions independently and averages them is maximized by repeating the single best decision, and the fine-tuned model collapsed to that exact optimum in every case, in and out of sample. Educators identified the repetition, which such metrics cannot represent, and preserving the learner's trajectory in the score reduced, but did not reverse, the metric's verdict. Weight analysis traced the correction to the model's output projection, where it had memorized its training strings rather than learned to adapt. We conclude that measurement validity does not imply optimization validity, and we derive design principles for benchmarks that assess or train AI-tutor instruction.

papers.title: Credal Machine Learning for Risk-Averse Decision Making
papers.authors: Timo Löhr, Paul Hofman, Maximilian Muschalik, Eyke Hüllermeier
papers.abstract: In many machine learning applications, it is necessary to guard against worst-case scenarios and predictions that could result in substantial losses. In principle, this can be achieved by training risk-averse predictive models that minimize loss functions such as conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), rather than relying on models that perform well on average. In practice, however, the effectiveness of this approach to risk aversion is undermined by the learner's uncertainty regarding the true loss distribution and, consequently, the true CVaR. To achieve reliable risk-aversion, we propose a method in which this (epistemic) uncertainty is represented in terms of credal sets, i.e., sets of probability distributions. More specifically, we develop an efficient yet reliable learner that produces predictions in the form of credal sets and combine it with a novel decision rule that maps each credal set to a single predictive distribution for CVaR minimization. Across classification, under distribution shift, and in reinforcement learning, our approach reliably avoids catastrophic decisions, while sacrificing little in expected performance.

papers.title: ILM: An AI-Powered Storytelling Educational Tool
papers.authors: Suhaila Mohammed, Abdelaziz Serour, Allison Lahnala
papers.abstract: Digital technologies have made Islamic narratives more accessible, but existing platforms provide limited support for structured learning and comprehension of these stories, particularly in Arabic and multilingual settings. We present ILM, an interactive educational platform for Stories of the Prophets that combines Arabic natural language processing, structured knowledge representation, and retrieval-based question generation. Admin-approved Arabic narratives are processed by a Knowledge Graph (KG) Constructor Engine that identifies entities and narrative relationships and stores them as structured knowledge, enabling learners to explore stories through a visual story map and answer entity- and relation-based questions generated from the KG. Separately, a multilingual retrieval pipeline retrieves relevant passages from the original narratives to generate multiple-choice and open-ended comprehension questions. For open-ended questions, an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluates learners' answers against the retrieved passages and reference answers to determine correctness. The platform also incorporates Quranic content as a separate enrichment layer, allowing selected narratives to be supplemented with source-supported information. By combining structured knowledge with passage-based retrieval, ILM supports narrative exploration, comprehension, and assessment across Arabic and multilingual content. The system demonstrates the feasibility of combining structured knowledge representation and retrieval-based generation to support interactive learning of Islamic narratives. A demo is available at anonymous.4open.science/r/mml-5FCF.

papers.title: MindFlow: Mind Supernet Powered Thinking Flows for Research Idea Innovation
papers.authors: Mengdi Liu, Wenjue Chen, Wenyue Chen, Cheng Yang, Fanqi Kong, Zhangyang Gao, Xiaoxue Cheng, Yiheng Li, Yujian Yuan, Keliang Li, Hong Chang, Shiguang Shan, Chenglin Wu
papers.abstract: Research idea innovation is a fundamental engine of scientific progress, yet it remains difficult to generate and evaluate in a scalable and controllable way. This challenge lies in its inherently open-ended and multi-objective nature, where ideas should balance novelty, plausibility and feasibility. While recent LLM-based approaches have made progress through carefully designed prompts or agent pipelines, they are constrained by predefined, static ideation workflows. To address this limitation, we propose MindFlow, a framework that explicitly formulates ideation as a graph-structured Flow in Mind, which is composed of modular thinking operators and modeled by a probabilistic mind supernet. Given a research topic, a controller dynamically samples thinking flows to generate candidate ideas. This open-ended problem is optimized using a tournament-based relative ranking, enabling the controller to progressively favor higher-quality thinking flows. We further introduce an evaluation protocol that jointly assesses problem finding and problem solving, going beyond title- or abstractonly judgments. Across diverse topics, MindFlow shows its superiority as an explicit, controllable and optimizable research idea innovator.

papers.title: Tell Robot What Not to Do: A Negation Understanding Perspective
papers.authors: Fazeng Li, Gan Sun, Hao Cheng, Weihong Ren, Yang Cong
papers.abstract: Instruction following enables robots to perform diverse tasks specified in natural language, making it a fundamental capability for human-robot interaction. Beyond communicating desired outcomes, users also need to specify constraints on what not to do. We investigate how to enable vision-language-action models (VLAs) to follow negated instructions, where robots must accomplish task goals while respecting explicit exclusions. To this end, we propose NegaAlign, a parameter-efficient, plug-and-play framework that extends pretrained VLAs to follow negated instructions through image-language supervision alone. Specifically, we introduce Negation Transformation Layers into selected layers of the vision-language backbone to reshape intermediate instruction representations. Meanwhile, a teacher-guided alignment mechanism is designed to align instruction-relevant visual tokens, transferring action-relevant grounding from instructions that satisfy the negated constraint. The training phase uses supervision constructed from existing demonstrations and updates only the inserted layers, keeping all pretrained parameters frozen, including the action generator. We further introduce NegaBench, a simulation benchmark spanning 10 scenarios across five domains for systematically evaluating manipulation under negated constraints. Experiments across GR00T, $π_0$, and $π_{0.5}$ demonstrate consistent improvements in negated instruction following. With 11.6M trainable parameters, NegaAlign increases the negated-instruction success rate of $π_{0.5}$ from 2.60% to 88.45% on NegaBench and from 12.4% to 88.8% on real-world tasks, while retaining performance on affirmative instructions.

papers.title: legoESM: a modular, differentiable, multiscale, AI-ready Earth system model built with AI agents
papers.authors: Pierre Gentine, Dhruv Balwada, Aytaç Paçal, Linnia Hawkins, Alistair Adcroft, Hang Fan, Jianing Fang, Aya Lahlou, Kara D. Lamb, David M. Lawrence, Julien Le Sommer, Joseph Mouallem, Juan Nathaniel, Duncan Watson‐Parris, Veronika Eyring
papers.abstract: Earth system models (ESMs) have grown tremendously in realism, yet key uncertainties persist in the climate response to greenhouse-gas forcing, particularly due to cloud radiative feedbacks. In addition, their software architecture was not designed for accelerator hardware or modern artificial intelligence (AI). Here we present legoESM, a composable, differentiable, multiscale ESM written in JAX. It builds on decades of community-developed parameterizations and numerical methods, recast in a unified framework by AI coding agents under a human-specified scientific contract and verified through benchmarking. Dynamical cores, physics schemes, grids, complexity levels and components are swappable like building blocks, and can use conventional physics or machine-learned emulators. A single code base spans metre-scale large-eddy simulation to global simulations and weather to climate. End-to-end differentiability enables gradient-based calibration, variational data assimilation and online training. legoESM modular architecture enables systematic evaluation of diverse model variants to explore structural uncertainty and test hypotheses. legoESM produces realistic simulations across scales, reduces land-surface temperature bias through gradient-based calibration, and scales efficiently on GPUs to kilometer-scale simulations. It offers an open, community infrastructure for hypothesis testing, research and teaching in Earth sciences and a template for multiscale physical systems.

papers.title: Auditing AI-Washing in German Startups: A Mixed-Methods Study of Marketing Claims and Perceptions
papers.authors: A Pranav, Luke Hartmann, Anne Lauscher
papers.journal: AAAI Publications (The Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI))
papers.abstract: AI-washing is the use of 'AI' as a marketing term where products' claims are exaggerated, likely to capture the hype from investors and consumers. In this paper, we examine how startups market AI and how people perceive those claims. We audited the German startup market, applying an annotation codebook of seven dimensions to 100 startups and conducting 63 expert interviews. Startups exaggerated AI capability in three forms: claims without inspectable evidence, performance numbers without methodology, and claims without acknowledged limits. The capabilities they claimed rarely matched the underlying system, and consumers who had encountered exaggerated claims before withdrew trust from later AI marketing. AI-washing has also been linked to the marketing of unethical products: 38% of the sample were flagged for moderate or serious ethical concern, in domains such as surveillance and automated decisions in regulated fields. Together these findings show how AI-washing happens: founders exaggerate capability to attract investors who reward AI branding they cannot verify, and consumers in unfamiliar domains take the marketing at face value. We recommend that startup AI claims be brought under disclosure requirements, with the codebook offered to regulators, investors, and consumer-protection bodies for routine audits.

papers.title: Internalizer: Portable Context-to-Parameter Mapping for Very Large Language Models
papers.authors: Peter Devine, Nick Ryan, Benjamin Sirb, Alex Chiocchi
papers.abstract: Hypernetworks that map a context directly to a LoRA adapter let a large language model carry that context in its weights, but prior work has demonstrated them only on base models of up to 14 billion parameters. We present the Internalizer, a state-of-the-art, portable Context-to-Parameter Mapping hypernetwork that generates document-specific LoRA adapters for the frozen 284B-parameter DeepSeek v4 Flash, a target two orders of magnitude larger than in any previous work. Most of its parameters live in a model-agnostic trunk with only thin entry and exit layers per base model, so it trains cheaply against small models before being ported to the large one. On unseen documents of up to 4096 tokens, the generated adapters reach 84.9% top-1 and 97.8% top-5 teacher-forced accuracy against 63.4% and 83.5% for the base model, with nothing in the context window but a three-word instruction. Once the hypernetwork is trained, a single forward pass turns any document into an adapter for such a model, which could be served alone for speed or alongside the document in the window to raise accuracy further.

papers.title: Evidence-Traceable Dynamic Interviewer Architecture for Expertise-Adaptive Qualitative Interviews Using Local LLMs
papers.authors: Aisvarya Adeseye, Jouni Isoaho, Adeyemi Adeseye, Seppo Virtanen, Mohammad Tahir
papers.abstract: Automated interviewers and conversational agents are increasingly used in research, recruitment, customer service, and education. However, many existing systems rely on fixed question sequences and provide limited context-based personalization without considering participants' knowledge, which can lead to repetitive or irrelevant follow-up questions. Therefore, there is a need for an adaptive interviewing system that can adjust question depth while maintaining conversational continuity and semantic progression. To address this, an Evidence-Traceable Dynamic Interviewer Architecture is presented using a locally hosted Large Language Model (LLM), with the interview continuously adapted throughout the entire conversation based on the participant's responses and evolving context. The interviewer profiles participants' expertise in real time to generate knowledge-appropriate questions, well-articulated responses, and smooth transition messages that support conversational continuity. A five-module prompt-driven architecture and persistent interview-state record support these functions. The interviewer was evaluated with 246 participants. Expertise Profiling module (M3) showed 78.9% exact agreement with independently reported participant expertise, with a weighted Cohen's K of 0.80. Generate Iterative Questions module (M4) showed a strong expertise-complexity association (p=.79, p<.001), and participants reported high relevance (mean 4.41), engagement (mean 4.32), and satisfaction (mean 4.38), providing evidence that the architecture's adaptive components operated consistently with their intended functions while participants reported a positive interview experience.

papers.title: Design Creativity Bench: Measuring creativity in LLM-Generated UI
papers.authors: Aman Rusia, Abhijit Bhole, Prashank Gupta, Dipanjan Dey
papers.abstract: As leading LLMs improve on capability evaluations, their limitations in producing creative outputs on design tasks remain insufficiently characterised. Our work introduces Design Creativity Bench, a benchmark that evaluates diversity and appropriateness in UI designs. It measures distinctiveness among models on the same prompt (originality), how much a model's designs change between two prompts for the same UI goal in different product domains (creative range), and the share of a brief's acceptance criteria each design meets (appropriateness). Originality is 0.592 for same-prompt design pairs from different models (95% CI [0.582, 0.602]), far below the 0.764 for same-prompt human-model pairs (95% CI [0.751, 0.778]). Creative range is 0.581 across models (95% CI [0.567, 0.597]), against 0.902 for human designs (95% CI [0.884, 0.919]). Appropriateness is above 90% for every model in our test set, and the best model reaches 99.2%, slightly above the 98.0% for human designs. Our work shows that the default output of LLMs, though generally appropriate, is substantially more repetitive than the human baseline. This calls for strong measures to address the issue. A live leaderboard with newer models is maintained at https://kombai.com/benchmark/.

papers.title: Beyond Speech Captions: Speech-Rewarded Style Planning for Conversational Text-to-Speech
papers.authors: Shiao Zhu, Lianbo Liu, Sizhen Lyu, Yuzhe Wang, Sheng Li, Takahiro Shinozaki
papers.abstract: Natural-language style descriptions provide an interpretable interface between large language models (LLMs) and controllable text-to-speech (TTS). However, using descriptions as pseudo-labels compresses target acoustics into text, and descriptive fidelity need not imply effective control of a particular synthesizer. We empirically show that speech-text alignment only weakly predicts downstream acoustic similarity among candidate instructions for the same utterance. We therefore propose Speech-Rewarded Style Planning (SRSP), which trains a text-based style planner through a frozen downstream TTS model. Given dialogue history and response text, the planner generates candidate instructions and is optimized with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), using the teacher-forced likelihood of target speech tokens as the reward. On an English subset of the ISCSLP 2026 CoT-TTS corpus, SRSP achieves higher speech-style and emotion similarity to target speech and lower mel-cepstral distortion than the Base LLM and target-audio-informed captioning baselines. LLM-based expressive speech evaluation further shows gains over all baselines in contextual appropriateness and reference consistency.

papers.title: Deception by Omission: Language Models Knowingly Hide Their Mistakes
papers.authors: Lucas Florin, Amelie Knecht, Ulysse Schaller, Thilo Hagendorff
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as agents with little human oversight, so potential mistakes they make can go unnoticed. Users then depend on the model to report what went wrong. An honest model discloses its mistakes, while a deceptive one conceals them. However, it is unclear how current LLMs behave in such situations. In this study, we prefill LLM trajectories with synthetic mistakes. The trajectories resemble real deployments in chat and agentic settings. Models fail to disclose their mistake in 36.4% of chat and 67.1% of agentic rollouts. In 2.4% and 5.3% of rollouts, respectively, they are aware of the mistake in their chain of thought but still deceptively conceal it. Rates vary by model: for instance, Gemini 3.5 Flash knowingly conceals mistakes in up to 19.9% of agentic rollouts. In 11.9% of chat and 51.8% of agentic rollouts, models show no awareness of mistakes, even though they reliably spot them when reviewing the same transcript as an outside observer. Our results show that, as agents take on more tasks with less oversight, users cannot rely on them to self-report possible mistakes. Developers should instead use independent monitors that review agent trajectories, or specifically train models to check their past actions and disclose what they find.

papers.title: Social Pain Disrupts Emotion-Action Brain-State Dynamics in Adolescents with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury
papers.authors: Ying Xu, Xiaojun Liang, Li Zhang, Yixuan Yuan, Gan Huang, Yongjie Zhou, Zhen Liang
papers.abstract: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is prevalent among adolescents with depression, but the rapid brain-state dynamics linking social distress to maladaptive behavior remain unclear. We combine an experimental pain paradigm, electroencephalography (EEG) microstate analysis, and interpretable deep sequence modeling to investigate NSSI-related neurodynamics in 106 adolescents with depression, including 67 with NSSI (DN+) and 39 without NSSI (DN-), during social pain, physical pain, and resting-state conditions. A model integrating disease-specific, domain-adversarial, consistency, and contrastive learning captures higher-order dependencies in microstate sequences. Social pain yields the strongest NSSI discrimination, with 68.55% accuracy, outperforming the best baseline by 8.94% points. Model interpretation and conventional microstate analyses reveal weakened bidirectional transitions between MS3 and MS5 in DN+ adolescents during social pain. Source reconstruction associates MS3 with emotional/interoceptive processing and MS5 with action preparation, suggesting disrupted emotion-action coupling. Time-resolved analyses show greater early-to-middle action-state recruitment and later emotion-state recruitment in DN+ adolescents. In DN- adolescents, MS5-to-MS3 dynamics mediate associations between social-evaluation sensitivity and affective outcomes, whereas this mediation is absent in DN+; conversely, MS3-to-MS5 transitions are associated with greater negative affect in DN+. Together, these findings identify disrupted emotion-action coupling as a key neurodynamic mechanism underlying altered social pain processing in adolescents with NSSI, providing a mechanistically interpretable neural signature for objective identification of NSSI.

papers.title: Can a System-One LLM Perform Knowledge Tracing When Few or No Learners Are Logged?
papers.authors: Unggi Lee, Haeun Park
papers.abstract: Knowledge tracing (KT) models need many logged learners, so a new course or platform starts without a usable model. In LLM-based KT the LLM generates the answer, which we call System-Two; it is either fine-tuned on the target data or reasons and votes over ten samples, which is slow and gives coarse probabilities. We ask whether an off-the-shelf System-One LLM, which returns a probability for a typed question directly in a single pass, can perform KT when few or no learners are logged. On seven datasets, Jev without any data from the target platform reaches a mean AUC of .706, above the best of 28 deep KT models trained on 8 learners (.689) and above System-Two Thinking-KT on all seven datasets (.650) at about 1/100 of its API cost. Adding examples and a similar-learner statistic from the logged learners (JevKT) raises this to .722; JevKT stays significantly ahead of deep KT up to 16 learners and ahead on average up to 64, and supervised KT catches up between 64 and 128 learners. Among the readers we tested, the gain is specific to Jev, since three other LLMs queried with the byte-identical typed request through the official System-One adapter fall below it on all seven datasets, and reader swaps and contamination checks find no evidence that the input format or memorised data explain the gain. For new learners the advantage holds from their first interactions, whereas on unseen items with all learners logged, deep KT remains ahead.

papers.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Growth and Sustainability of Ed-Tech Start-ups in Uttar Pradesh
papers.authors: Disha Chaudhary and Pankaj Gambhir
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: The education technology (Ed-Tech) industry is evolving rapidly thanks to the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI), which is now being used to personalize learning, automate evaluation, create intelligent content and manage student data and information, as well as streamline business operations. The rise of skills and technologies like AI is transforming the landscape of Ed-Tech startups in Uttar Pradesh by enhancing their competitive edge, reducing operational expenses, boosting user engagement, and optimizing educational delivery. This study focuses on the importance and contribution of Artificial Intelligence in the development and sustainability of the start-ups in the Ed-Tech sector in Uttar Pradesh. It emphasizes the ways in which AI aids companies in growing, enhancing their operations, innovating, pleasing customers, customizing learning, and staying sustainable over time. The study also reveals key challenges in the implementation of AI such as cost of implementation, lack of skilled expertise, privacy issues, technology constraints, and change resistance. Descriptive research design is proposed with the help of primary data collection from selected Ed-Tech start-ups and their employees/manager in UP. The analysis is based on percentages, looking at trends in AI use and impact on business performance and sustainability. The results of the study will benefit entrepreneurs, Ed-Tech managers, policy makers and others as they look for ways to implement AI effectively. The results could help in understanding the role of AI in promoting sustainable growth of the nascent Ed-Tech ecosystem in UP, if used responsibly and strategically

papers.title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Social Media Content Verification, Influence Assessment and Risk Analysis
papers.authors: S. B. Bele, Prajwal G. Dhote, Om S. Shriwas, Akash B. Zalke
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: Social platforms now carry news, opinion, commerce and public safety information in a blend of text, pictures, video and audio. Deception has adapted to this format: a genuine photograph can be given a false caption, a synthetic voice can be attached to an old clip, and coordinated accounts can push a post until it looks popular. Detectors that examine only one channel often miss these cases. This paper presents a unified multimodal framework that treats three linked questions together: is the content authentic (verification), who and what is amplifying it (influence), and how much harm could it cause (risk). The framework encodes each modality separately, aligns them through cross-modal attention, and feeds a shared representation to three task heads whose outputs are merged into an interpretable risk score with a human review step. We survey existing work, describe the architecture, datasets, training approach and evaluation protocol, discuss applications in journalism, public health, brand safety, elections and disaster response, and examine ethical constraints such as privacy, bias and over-blocking. The contribution is a design and evaluation blueprint rather than a new benchmark result, and we close with open problems and a research agenda.

papers.title: Amplifying Value Co-Creation in Small Family Businesses through Artificial Intelligence and Neuroscience: Twin Pillars for Intergenerational Decisions and Cohesion
papers.authors: Florina Atanase, Edita Carmen BOKOR, Andreea GHEORGHITA, Alina Matei
papers.abstract: This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and neuroscience can jointly amplify value co-creation in small family businesses, whose competitive advantage rests on trust, close relationships and tacit, experience-based know-how transmitted across generations. The study combines a systematic literature review with narrative synthesis and conceptual model-building. Foundational sources were identified through citation tracking, and recent research was captured through a structured Scopus search (30 July 2026) that returned 296 records, of which 24 were retained after screening and quality appraisal and six further records were added through snowballing; a keyword co-occurrence analysis was performed on the full Scopus corpus. The review shows that AI acts as a strategic enabler rather than a mere automation tool, supporting efficiency, customer personalisation, innovation and intergenerational knowledge transfer, although recent evidence (2023–2026) indicates that its effects depend on the mode of family involvement, firm origin, organisational culture and governance. Neuroscience contributes insights into decision-making, creativity, stress and trust in emotionally dense family settings. The bibliometric map confirms that the two literatures have developed largely separately, as neuroscience terms are almost absent from the AI-in-family-business corpus. The article proposes a four-layer conceptual framework in which value co-creation mediates the effects of AI and neuroscience on organisational and family outcomes, moderated by firm-level, ethical and governance conditions, and formulates four working propositions for future empirical testing.

papers.title: Edukasi Literasi Digital sebagai Respons terhadap Krisis Disinformasi Berbasis AI pada Komunitas Perempuan di Bintara, Kota Bekasi
papers.authors: Immanuel Beniardhie, Faizal Didik
papers.journal: Comit Communication Information and Technology Journal
papers.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence—such as deepfakes and voice cloning—is accelerating the spread of disinformation in Indonesia and eroding public trust in digital information. Mothers serve as key nodes for information distribution within family ecosystems but are prone to sharing information without verification. The "Cek Sebelum Cekcok" (Check Before Conflict) community service program was designed to strengthen the digital literacy of women aged 30–50 in Bintara Urban Village, Bekasi City—specifically targeting elderly members of the Prolanis program identified through social mapping—grounded in the frameworks of cyberethics (Ess, 2009) and post-truth epistemology (McIntyre, 2018). Program implementation began with participatory social mapping involving field observations and informal interviews, followed by an in-person talk show featuring speakers from academia, regulatory bodies, and the digital industry, alongside participant comprehension assessments using pre-test and post-test instruments. Social mapping revealed that the ecosystem of resident conversation networks is not homogeneous: Neighborhood Association (RT) groups were relatively safe from hoaxes, whereas Community Association (RW) groups and Prolanis groups were most vulnerable to manipulative content; consequently, digital literacy interventions needed to be tailored to each network layer rather than employing a uniform approach. Pre- and post-test results from 150 respondents showed an improvement in the ability to identify AI-generated content: the proportion of respondents who correctly identified all videos rose from 11.3% (17 respondents) in the pre-test to 68.0% (102 respondents) in the post-test. The program recommends replicating this intervention model—based on social mapping and network differentiation—in other urban areas with similar characteristics, alongside continuous monitoring of changes in information verification behavior.

papers.title: NDNS Biomonitoring for Exposure to Food Additives
papers.authors: Albert Koulman, Barbora Horch, Solomon Sowah, Sarah Meadows, Kerry Jones, D. M. Collins, Polly Page, Andy Axon
papers.abstract: ADI: Acceptable Daily Intake, a measure of the amount of a specific substance (like a food additive) that can be ingested daily over a lifetime without appreciable health risk ADME: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion, the four key processes describing how a substance is handled by a biological system ANOVA: Analysis of variance, a statistical method used to compare the means of two or more groups to determine if they are significantly different AUC: Area under the curve, used in pharmacokinetics to represent the total exposure to a drug or substance over time BMI: Body Mass Index (kg/m 2 ), a value derived from the mass and height of a person bw: Body weight, the amount that a person or animal weighs CHA: Cyclohexylamine, a primary metabolite formed from the breakdown of cyclamate by gut bacteria CI: Confidence interval, a statistical range of values that is likely to include an unknown population parameter with 95% confidence C max : Peak plasma concentration, or maximum concentration of a substance in the blood following administration CNS: Central nervous system, the complex of nerve tissues that controls the activities of the body DKP: papers.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Tools in Computer Education: A Study of Student Engagement and Learning Outcomes
papers.authors: Majed Gharmallah Alzahrani
papers.journal: International Journal of Technology in Education
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence tools is increasingly common in higher education, but little empirical research exists on their effects on student engagement and learning outcomes in Saudi universities. This study examines the relationships among AI tools adoption, student engagement, and perceived learning outcomes among undergraduate students in computer education programs. A cross-sectional design was employed to collect survey data from 523 students across two universities in Saudi Arabia. Quantitative analysis using Structural Equation Modeling (SmartPLS) indicated positive and significant relationships between AI tools adoption, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived learning outcomes. AI tools adoption was the strongest predictor of student behavioral engagement, whereas perceived usefulness was the strongest predictors of student cognitive engagement. All three engagement dimensions were positively associated with perceived learning outcomes, with cognitive engagement being the strongest predictor. The findings suggest that the educational value of AI tools may depend not only on access and usability but also on their capacity to support cognitively meaningful participation. This study offers empirical evidence on technology adoption in Saudi higher education, combines student engagement and learning outcomes within a single framework, and extends the current understanding of AI usage in learning in non-Western contexts.

papers.title: Hybrid retrieval-augmented generation for hallucination mitigation in domain-specific educational question-answering systems
papers.authors: Huu Tuong Ho, Lee O-Joun, Duc Tin Ly, Luong Vuong Nguyen
papers.journal: HO CHI MINH CITY OPEN UNIVERSITY JOURNAL OF SCIENCE - ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer significant potential for educational chatbots, but their tendency to generate hallucinations and fluent yet factually unsupported responses limits their reliability in high-stakes academic settings. This study presents the design and evaluation of a university-focused virtual assistant, built on a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, to support academic and administrative inquiries at Greenwich Vietnam. The system integrates a structured institutional knowledge base derived from official documents, internal portals, regulations, and websites, along with hybrid retrieval mechanisms, including lexical and semantic search, query routing, and reranking, to improve evidence selection and contextual grounding. We evaluated the system on a benchmark comprising nearly 700 real-world and expert-constructed question-answer pairs with associated reference sources. Experimental results demonstrate strong retrieval and generation capabilities, achieving a Context Relevance score of 0.92 and a Semantic Answer Similarity score of 0.87, while also receiving high human evaluation scores for accuracy, completeness, freshness, faithfulness, and naturalness. The findings indicate that the proposed RAG-based approach substantially improves the trustworthiness of educational chatbot responses while remaining practical for institutional deployment. At the same time, the study highlights ongoing challenges in handling complex queries and maintaining long-term knowledge freshness, offering useful guidance for future domain-specific RAG systems in higher education.

papers.title: Nonlinear analysis of factors influencing tuberculosis outpatient visits in China: an explainable machine learning approach
papers.authors: Hui Wang, Dehong Sun, Shanjie Sui, Yanhong Xu
papers.abstract: This study aims to analyze the temporal trends, interprovincial differences, and key predictors of Tuberculosis Outpatient Visits (TOV) in China. It provides empirical evidence for understanding regional differences in tuberculosis-related outpatient service uti- lization. Panel data from 30 Chinese provinces from 2012 to 2024 were used. The study included variables related to economic development, health resources, education resources, environmental governance, pollutant emissions, and technological innovation. Correlation analysis, model comparison, and XGBoost-SHAP analysis were applied. From 2012 to 2024, TOV showed a gradual upward trend and clear interprovincial differences. Shanghai, Fujian, Guangdong, and Zhejiang had relatively higher total recorded outpatient volumes. XGBoost showed the best predictive performance among all candidate models (R2 = 0.8154). SHAP results identified Disposable Income Per Capita (DIPC), University Staff (USTF), Domestic Patent Applications (DPA), Hospital Beds (HBED), and Technology Market Turnover (TMT) as the main predictors. Environmental governance and pollutant emission vari- ables had lower overall contributions, but they still showed nonlinear predictive contributions in some value ranges. The findings suggest that interprovincial differences in TOV are jointly associated with economic development, health resources, education resources, environmental governance, and technological innovation. TOV mainly reflects outpatient service utilization and case detection capacity. It should not be interpreted as a direct measure of tuberculosis incidence risk.

papers.title: BEST-07 | ULTRASOUND EVALUATION AND JOINT SCORING IN MILD HEMOPHILIA A: A SINGLE-CENTER CASE SERIES FOR THE IDENTIFICATION OF SUBCLINICAL ARTHROPATHY
papers.authors: Marzia Leotta
papers.abstract: Background. Mild Hemophilia A (FVIII 5–40%) is often underestimated, yet patients remain at risk for chronic arthropathy due to subclinical bleeds and trauma. Since the HJHS (physical exam) often misses early damage, this study uses Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) to detect early synovial and osteochondral changes. The goal is to correlate clinical data, including Body Mass Index (BMI), with ultrasound findings to better assess true joint health.Materials and Methods. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted on a series of patients with mild hemophilia followed at our institution in the last year. For each patient, the primary target joints (elbows, knees, and ankles) were evaluated. The HJHS was administered to quantify functional joint impairment. BMI was recorded for all participants to evaluate the impact of body weight on joint health. POCUS scans were performed using the HEAD-US (Hemophilia Early Arthropathy Detection with Ultrasound) protocol. Correlation was assessed between baseline clotting factor levels, BMI, HJHS, and the total HEAD-US score.Results. A total of 36 mild patients are currently followed at our center; 23 male patients underwent HJHS and HEAD-US within the last 12 months. The median age was 40.6 years (range 12–65), and the mean BMI was 25.73 kg/m². The median baseline factor level was 10% (range 5-24%). The median ABR was remarkably low (0.4). The median HJHS score was 7.23 (range 0–16). HEAD-US scoring revealed structural abnormalities in 56.5% of the evaluated patients (13 pz). Notably, within a subgroup of 13 patients particularly susceptible to joint changes, 4 (33.3%) presented both osteostructural alterations and a BMI >25 kg/m². Mild synovial hypertrophy was detected in 23% of cases, and significant cartilage thinning was observed in 69% of subjects.Discussion. Our findings demonstrate that mild hemophilia does not preclude chronic arthropathy, which is more accurately detected by HEAD-US than by HJHS. The significant correlation between age and HEAD-US scores, alongside the impact of BMI >25 on structural damage, suggests that mechanical stress and cumulative trauma, rather than factor deficiency alone, are the primary drivers of joint degradation in this cohort. Consequently, the presence of osteostructural damage in overweight patients emphasizes the critical role of weight management. Integrating routine ultrasound into clinical follow-up allows for a more personalized therapeutic approach.Conclusions. Systematic HEAD-US evaluation facilitates preclinical arthropathy diagnosis in mild hemophilia. Monitoring should integrate periodic imaging and metabolic assessments, such as BMI, to ensure a proactive, personalized strategy that preserves long-term quality of life.

papers.title: A Study on Awareness of Using Generative AI Tools Among Undergraduates: Evidence from State Universities of Sri Lanka
papers.authors: K. B. G. T. B. Piyarathne, K. M. P. G. A. J. Bandara
papers.abstract: This study explores the level of awareness and key influencing factors related to the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tools among undergraduates in Sri Lanka’s state universities. As AI tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, and Google Gemini become increasingly prevalent in higher education, understanding how students perceive and adopt these technologies is critical. The study applies the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), and the Technology Readiness Index (TRI) to examine four independent variables: Attitude, Peer Influence, Perceived Usefulness, and Technological Readiness. Data were collected from a sample of 384 undergraduates across state universities using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS. Findings reveal that technological readiness and perceived usefulness are the strongest predictors of awareness, while gaps remain in ethical understanding. The study recommends integrating AI literacy and ethical guidelines into curricula to ensure responsible use. These findings provide practical guidance for policymakers and educators in developing strategies to enhance AI awareness and readiness among undergraduates.

papers.title: CTRL+A ЗНАНИЕ: ВЗАИМОДЕЙСТВИЕ ЧОВЕК–ИЗКУСТВЕН ИНТЕЛЕКТ И ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯТА НА ЗНАНИЕТО
papers.authors: Lubomira Parijkova
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence is transforming the ways knowledge is produced, accessed, inter- preted, and validated. In the emerging AI-driven environment, knowledge increasingly takes shape within a hybrid space of human–machine in- teraction, where algorithmic systems participate not only in processing informa- tion but also in generating content, recommendations, and decisions. This article offers a philosophical-analytical and interpretative reflection on the transformation of knowledge through the metaphor of Ctrl+A, which symbolically evokes the ex- pansion, accessibility, and algorithmic selection of content in digital environments. Particular attention is paid to the implications of human–AI interaction for cog- nition, authorship, trust, attention, and educational practice. The study employs a qualitative interpretative approach that combines conceptual analysis of scientif- ic, normative, strategic, and selected public sources, observations from educational practice, and a reflexive component based on the author’s interaction with ChatGPT between November 2024 and early June 2025. Within this framework, a conceptual emotional curve is used not merely as an illustrative device, but as an interpretative lens through which key features of generative AI are analyzed, including productiv- ity, dialogicality, cognitive offloading, error and hallucination, trust, and the fear of human replacement. The article also addresses the attention economy and the rise of a synthetic media environment, in which AI-generated texts, images, and videos increasingly challenge the boundaries between authentic and simulated content. It argues that in the emerging post-knowledge condition, the value of knowledge de- pends less on its mere availability than on the human capacity for critical interpre- tation, meaningful selection, and responsible use.

papers.title: ИЗКУСТВЕН ИНТЕЛЕКТ И ЕЗИКОВИ МОДЕЛИ
papers.authors: Kristina Stoyanova
papers.abstract: This report examines artificial intelligence and language mod- els as contemporary cultural and social phenomena of growing significance for human communication, cognition, and identity.
