papers.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Enhancing the Quality and Level of Disclosure of Accounting Information in Light of the Requirements of ISO 37001:2025
papers.authors: Nada Kaki Bira
papers.journal: Indonesian Journal of Law and Economics Review
papers.abstract: General Background: Rapid technological advancements are continuously transforming the accounting and financial environment through enhanced data processing and analytical capabilities. Specific Background: As business operations grow increasingly complex, conventional control mechanisms often struggle to manage unusual transactions and mitigate operational risks effectively. Knowledge Gap: Limited research comprehensively examines how artificial intelligence technologies integrate with modern anti-bribery frameworks to improve financial reporting outcomes. Aims: This study examines the role of artificial intelligence technologies in improving accounting information quality and disclosure under the requirements of ISO 37001:2025. Results: Findings indicate significant positive correlations and direct effects between artificial intelligence technologies and both accounting information quality and disclosure, with ISO 37001:2025 requirements serving as a partial mediator for information quality and a full mediator for disclosure. Novelty: The integration of artificial intelligence analytics with the specific compliance and anti-bribery standards of ISO 37001:2025 within the banking sector provides a unique regulatory and technological synergy. Implications: Financial institutions can substantially strengthen their internal controls, transparency, and reporting reliability by systematically deploying intelligent applications alongside anti-bribery management systems. Key Findings Highlights Artificial intelligence technologies demonstrate statistically significant positive effects on both accounting information quality and financial disclosure standards. The requirements of ISO 37001:2025 act as a critical mediator, providing full mediation for accounting disclosure and partial mediation for information quality. Expanding intelligent applications into predictive analytics and continuous transaction monitoring significantly reinforces organizational control and transparency. Keywords Artificial Intelligence Technologies, Accounting Information Quality, Accounting Disclosure, ISO 37001:2025, Anti-Bribery

papers.title: From Detecting Drift to Adapting to It: A Critical Review of Hybrid Drift-Aware IoT Intrusion Detection and a Stacked Adaptive Ensemble Framework for TON_IoT
papers.authors: Usman Iliasu, Fatima Umar Zambuk
papers.abstract: Machine-learning intrusion detection for the Internet of Things (IoT) is increasingly judged on whether it survives changing traffic, not only on benchmark accuracy. This review appraises one recent response, the hybrid Random Forest (RF), benign-only Isolation Forest (IF) and Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) drift-monitoring framework of Obaidat, Abouali and Shakeel (2026), and uses the appraisal to specify a fused, adaptive alternative. Working only from the confusion matrix and tables the authors publish, we derive a Matthews correlation coefficient of about 0.94 and a benign-class F1 of about 0.94, show that the hybrid raises about 158 more false alarms than RF with no visible recall gain, and show that its advantage on an unseen attack family (85.26% versus 85.18% on 4,952 flows) lies well inside sampling error. We then compare 13 stacking, adaptive and multi-stage studies from 2023–2026 and find, within the sources read, none that combines trained stacking, automatic drift adaptation and evaluation on TON_IoT. We present EHAE-IDS: RF, Gradient Boosting and an online Adaptive Random Forest as Level-0 learners, a Logistic Regression meta-learner, an ADWIN-gated and validated update loop, and a two-stage binary-then-multiclass detector, together with a four-protocol evaluation plan with controlled drift injection, label-delay scenarios, edge-cost metrics and statistical testing. No experimental results are reported. The paper is a review and a pre-specified design, and its expected-outcome section states hypotheses and how each could fail.

papers.title: The Somnogenesis System: A Proposed Biological System for Psychiatry
papers.authors: Mouhammad Ousmane Ndiaye
papers.abstract: For more than 150 years, since the idea that mental illness is rooted in the brain first emerged in the mid-1800s, psychiatry has searched for a reliable biological system to anchor its understanding of mental illness. This paper proposes a candidate for that system, starting from a striking observation. Almost every major psychiatric disorder shows three things together: REM sleep disturbance, altered default mode network (DMN) activity, and emotional dysregulation. The DMN is independently known to play a central role in emotional regulation and emotional memory, which is what suggests these three recurring findings are not coincidental but are manifestations of a single, previously unidentified biological system. The Somnogenesis System hypothesis states that the DMN's three principal hubs, the medial prefrontal cortex, the posterior cingulate cortex and precuneus, and the bilateral inferior parietal cortices, reactivate in a specific, ordered sequence during every REM period, and that this order is identical across the large majority of healthy individuals. Each hub carries an established, distinct function, and the evidence suggests these functions operate as a dependency chain rather than as independent, parallel contributions, consistent with the proposed existence of a genuine biological system rather than three regions coincidentally active at the same time. This hypothesis can be tested without collecting new data. A protocol is proposed using an existing public dataset of simultaneous EEG-fMRI sleep recordings, in which the three hubs are anatomically defined using a standardized cortical atlas and each REM period's activation order is estimated from onset latency rather than raw BOLD timing, controlling for each region's own hemodynamic response. Confirming the hypothesis would reframe REM sleep as the physiological interface of an underlying biological system, with implications for conditions including Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, multiple system atrophy, and major depressive disorder, where a disrupted system rather than a disrupted stage may be the more precise marker of pathology. The hypothesis is directly falsifiable, a failure to find a consistent, shared order would refute it outright.

papers.title: Co-design of Teacher Training in Artificial Intelligence and Evaluation in Uruguayan Secondary Education
papers.authors: Claudia Cabrera Borges, Mariela Questa-Torterolo, Anna Espasa
papers.abstract: This paper presents the results of the co-design stage of the project “Strengthening Teachers’ Digital Competences,” focused on assessment mediated by Artificial Intelligence (AI) in 12 Centros María Espínola (CME) in Uruguay. The starting point was a previous mixed-methods diagnosis (N = 187 surveys and 11 focus groups) that revealed low competence levels in the area of assessment (M = 1.88 on a 4-point scale), along with marked ethical resistance to replacing the pedagogical relationship with algorithmic processes. In February 2026, collaborative workshops were held with the participation of more than 20 teachers and CME coordinators. The co-design methodology made it possible to identify that teachers demand situated training that does not focus solely on technique, but rather on the pedagogical redesign of tasks to foster critical paraphrasing and avoid uncritical plagiarism. Likewise, ethical red lines were defined, preserving human dimensions such as empathy and the socio-emotional context as domains exclusive to teachers. The results highlight the importance of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and the seminar effect (peer learning) as pillars for the sustainability of training in contexts of vulnerability. This collective construction helps ensure that the final proposal, structured into flexible pathways, is feasible, responsive to real classroom needs, and coherently integrated into the Ceibal ecosystem.

papers.title: Forecasting Minimum Support Price-anchored Mandi Prices for Wheat and Maize in India: A Comparative Machine-learning and Time-series Framework
papers.authors: Sai Prabhakar Balantrapu, G. Raghavender Raju, Satya Sai Mudigonda, Lalith Aditya Kalur
papers.journal: Agricultural Science Digest - A Research Journal
papers.abstract: Background: India’s minimum support price (MSP) regime creates an administered floor for wholesale (mandi) prices, making accurate price forecasting the analytical foundation for farmer revenue-risk assessment, government procurement planning and the design of price- or revenue-based crop insurance instruments. Wheat and maize present a sharp institutional contrast: wheat is procurement-binding through the Food Corporation of India, while maize receives little procurement support and its price is left largely to private trade. This study benchmarks machine-learning and classical time-series forecasters for the monthly modal mandi price of both crops across a structurally distinct, post-pandemic hold-out period and defines, in measurable terms, what it means for such a series to be MSP-anchored. Methods: This analysis was carried out at Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning (SSSIHL), Prasanthi Nilayam, Andhra Pradesh, India, during 2026. Daily AGMARKNET records for wheat and maize (April 2008-March 2025) were aggregated into 204 monthly All-India modal-price observations per crop-the mean of daily modal prices-with the corresponding MSP reported for reference. Eight algorithms-ridge regression, support vector regression, random forest, extremely randomised trees, gradient boosting, XGBoost, ARIMA and SARIMA-together with a naïve persistence benchmark, were trained on 177 months (April 2008-December 2022) and evaluated out-of-sample on 27 held-out months (January 2023-March 2025) using the mean absolute error, root mean squared error and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Result: Ridge regression on lagged prices and a month indicator dominated every fitted ensemble and, with ARIMA and SARIMA evaluated as static multi-step forecasts, every time-series competitor for both crops, achieving a MAPE of 2.75 per cent for wheat (mean absolute error ₹ 68.97/quintal) and 2.59 per cent for maize (₹ 55.97/quintal). Tree-based learners and support vector regression deteriorated sharply on the trending test window; SARIMA was competitive only for maize. Against naïve persistence, however, ridge’s edge was modest for wheat and mixed for maize-persistence matched ridge on MAE and MAPE and narrowly beat it on RMSE-indicating ridge’s advantage lies chiefly over the more flexible learners. This is attributed to the near-unit autocorrelation of MSP-anchored series and the inability of tree ensembles to extrapolate beyond their training range, consistent with, though not proving, the institutional asymmetry between procurement-stabilised wheat and procurement-absent maize. These forecasts form the price engine for companion volume-forecasting and procurement-liability studies within the broader actuarial data-science revenue-protection framework.

papers.title: Who Does the Thinking? Undergraduate Students’ Decision-Making and the Potential Displacement of Cognitive Processes in Writing by GenAI
papers.authors: Jinrong Li, Kathleen O’Reilly
papers.journal: The Open/Technology in Education Society and Scholarship Association Journal
papers.abstract: Since the release of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in November 2022, Generative AI (GenAI) has been rapidly integrated into applications capable of producing texts, images, and sounds that simulate human output. While students generally view this technology positively, writing scholars voice increasing concerns, particularly regarding its impact on critical thinking and learning. Current discussions often focus on the perceived benefits of GenAI (e.g., improved writing efficiency and ease of task completion), highlighting an urgent need for research that examines students’ actual decision-making and practice to better assess the pedagogical implications. To address this need, we conducted a mixed-methods study investigating undergraduate students' use and perceptions of GenAI tools in academic writing. We analyzed interview data (N=213) collected through purposive sampling, targeting undergraduate students with active writing assignments across 14 universities in Canada, Europe, and the United States. Frequency analysis provided an overview of the tools' integration across writing stages, while thematic analysis detailed students’ rationales for using or refraining from GenAI. The findings indicated that the dominant efficiency-driven approach to GenAI use might pose a significant potential risk of displacing writing processes and reducing cognitive engagement in the writing classroom. This study contributes a deeper, more nuanced understanding of students’ decision-making around GenAI and its potential impact on writing development and higher education learning outcomes.

papers.title: The The role of AI-enabled HRM practices and employee well-being: From digital wellness to organizational commitment
papers.authors: Maheshwari B P, Sridevi Kulenur, Rakesh Damodar, Kavyashree M B
papers.abstract: This study examines the associations among AI-enabled Corporate Wellness Systems (AI-CWS), Employee Well-Being (EWB), and Organizational Commitment (OC) among employees in Indian organizations. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design, primary data from 1,259 respondents in technology, banking, healthcare, and education-related organizations were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, hierarchical regression, and bootstrapped mediation analysis. The results indicate a statistically significant negative association between AI-CWS and EWB (B = −0.183, p < 0.001) and a statistically significant positive association between AI-CWS and OC (B = 0.323, p < 0.001). EWB was positively associated with OC (B = 0.160, p < 0.001). The bootstrapped indirect association of AI-CWS with OC through EWB was negative and statistically significant (indirect effect = −0.029, 95% CI [−0.045, −0.016]), while the direct association remained positive (B = 0.352, p < 0.001). The pattern is therefore consistent with an inconsistent or competitive mediation structure rather than positive partial mediation. Given the cross-sectional and self-reported nature of the data, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. The study extends Job Demands–Resources and Perceived Organizational Support perspectives by showing that AI-enabled wellness systems may be perceived simultaneously as organizational support and as a potential technological demand. Keywords: Artificial intelligence; AI-enabled corporate wellness systems; Employee well-being; Organizational commitment; Perceived organizational support; Job demands–resources theory.
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

papers.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and artificial intelligence: current state and prospects for technology application
papers.authors: Andrey Valerievich Budnevsky, Sergey Nikolaevich Avdeev, A. Yu. Simion, Sofia A. Budnevskaya
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) ranks third in the global mortality structure, with up to 80% of cases remaining undiagnosed due to the limitations of spirometry and the subjectivity inherent in interpreting clinical and laboratory­instrumental data. The heterogeneity of the disease necessitates a transition toward personalized medicine, in which artificial intelligence technologies play a key role. The aim. To analyze the current state and prospects of artificial intelligence technologies in the diagnosis, prediction, monitoring, and patient education for COPD. Methods. A search for scientific publications was conducted in the electronic databases PubMed, Cochrane Library, eLibrary.ru, and CyberLeninka for the period 2013 – 2026. Original studies focusing on the application of machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and generative models in COPD were selected for analysis. Results. It has been established that AI models based on neural networks achieve a differential diagnostic accuracy for COPD of up to 96.84%. Multimodal systems integrating clinical, imaging, and text data predict exacerbations (AUC – 0.77) and mortality with accuracy exceeding the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) spirometric severity classification. NLP algorithms extract information on dyspnea severity from physician notes, while sensor­based platforms (TOLIFE, RE­SAMPLE) predict exacerbations up to 7 days before a probable event. In patient education, chatbots demonstrate high response intelligibility but fall short in accuracy and adherence to readability standards, necessitating the validation of specialized AI systems. Conclusion. Artificial intelligence is forming the foundation for personalized COPD patient management, improving the accuracy of screening and disease course prediction. The main barriers to the implementation of this type of technology are a lack of external validation, algorithmic opacity, and data fragmentation. The priority is the development of explainable and validated clinical decision support systems.

papers.title: The Relationship between Obesity, Elevated Depressive Symptoms, and Physical Functioning Among United Methodist Clergy: A Longitudinal Study
papers.authors: Chenxinan Ma, Achintya Inumarty, David E. Eagle, Chenkai Wu, Rae Jean Proeschold‐Bell
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND United Methodist Church (UMC) clergy face occupational stressors (e.g., unpredictable schedules, emotional labor, politically polarized congregations) that contribute to disproportionately elevated obesity and depression prevalence. Despite these conditions’ high comorbidity and independent links to physical functioning (PF) decline, few studies explore their interactive effects over time, especially in high-risk populations. This study examines the independent and joint prospective associations of obesity and elevated depressive symptoms with PF decline among North Carolina UMC clergy over two years. METHODS Data from 1422 North Carolina UMC clergy (2014–2016) were analyzed using ordinary least squares regression, including an interaction term to assess independent and synergistic prospective associations of baseline obesity (body mass index [BMI] ≥ 30 kg/m 2 ) and elevated depressive symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire [PHQ-9] ≥ 10) with subsequent PF decline (measured by SF-12 Physical Component Summary scores), adjusting for demographic and lifestyle variables. Logistic regression estimated cross-sectional obesity-depression associations. RESULTS At baseline, 39.5% of clergy were obese and 7.2% had elevated depressive symptoms, with obesity positively associated with depression (odds ratio [OR]: 2.66; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.76–4.02). Both obesity and elevated depressive symptoms were independently associated with poorer physical functioning at follow-up. In the crude model, the joint effect of obesity and depressive symptoms was associated with PF decline (β = –4.34; 95% CI: –7.87, –0.81). This interaction was attenuated after adjustment for all covariates. LIMITATIONS Self-reported BMI, depressive symptoms, and PF may introduce recall bias; clergy-specific findings limit generalizability. CONCLUSIONS Obesity and depressive symptoms are independently associated with poorer future physical functioning; their co-occurrence suggests greater functional vulnerability among clergy. Approaches that integrate obesity and depression care warrant testing.

papers.title: Talent Match AI Powered Resume Matching Platform Project Report
papers.authors: Kamal Acharya
papers.abstract: In the evolving landscape of talent acquisition, organizations face increasing challenges in efficiently identifying the right candidates from large pools of applicants. Traditional recruitment processes often rely on manual resume screening, which is not only time-consuming and resource-intensive but also prone to human bias and inconsistency. The TalentMatch project introduces an AI-powered recruitment platform designed to revolutionize this process by automating and optimizing resume-to-job matching using advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques. The core objective of TalentMatch is to intelligently parse, analyze, and rank candidate resumes against job descriptions by extracting key information such as skills, qualifications, work experience, education, certifications, and contextual relevance to the role. The system utilizes semantic analysis to understand the meaning behind unstructured text data, enabling it to match candidates not just based on keyword overlap, but on true contextual alignment with job requirements. By converting unstructured resumes and job postings into structured data representations, the platform enables a fair, consistent, and data-driven approach to candidate evaluation. The platform architecture comprises a modular backend built with Express and TypeScript, which handles data ingestion, resume parsing, and job description analysis. The intelligent matching engine employs a combination of NLP techniques, such as named entity recognition (NER), word embeddings, vector similarity, and custom scoring algorithms to determine candidate-job fit. On the frontend, a responsive React application provides an intuitive interface for recruiters to view, filter, and interact with ranked candidate lists. The interface also supports customizable scoring metrics, enabling recruiters to prioritize specific attributes like technical skills, years of experience, or educational background based on the unique needs of a role.

papers.title: Correcting Health Misinformation Using AI Chatbots: Effects of Human–AI Collaboration Mode, Transparency, and Uncertainty
papers.authors: Yangyang Wu, Mengxue Ou
papers.abstract: This project examines how the presentation of human–AI collaboration, scientific uncertainty, and supporting explanations shapes public acceptance of AI chatbots for health misinformation correction. Guided by the Human–AI Interaction framework grounded in the Theory of Interactive Media Effects (HAII–TIME), the study investigates whether these features independently and jointly influence trust in a chatbot, attitudes toward using it to correct health misinformation, and intentions to use it for this purpose. The study employed a 3 × 2 × 2 between-subjects online experiment with a final analytical sample of 424 participants in China. Participants were randomly assigned to one of 12 conditions and viewed a simulated chatbot conversation addressing the false claim that insulin injections are addictive. Human–AI collaboration was described as human-dominated, with experts leading the evaluation and AI assisting; AI-dominated, with AI leading and experts verifying; or AI-only, without human involvement. Correction uncertainty varied according to whether the accompanying notice described the scientific evidence as broadly consistent or unresolved. Correction transparency varied according to whether the chatbot disclosed supporting reasons and sources. Analyses examined the main and interaction effects of these features while accounting for demographic characteristics, AI literacy, eHealth literacy, and perceived risks of AI hallucinations.

papers.title: Data and Materials for How Should AI Voice Guides Explain Paintings
papers.authors: WeiquanHe
papers.abstract: This project contains the de-identified data and supporting documentation for the study “How Should AI Voice Guides Explain Paintings? An Experimental Study of Guidance Strategy and Voice Persona Using Chinese Landscape Paintings.” The study used a Unity-based virtual gallery featuring six Chinese landscape paintings. A 3 × 2 within-subjects experiment with 21 university students compared three guidance strategies—Minimal Prompt, Standard Introduction, and Active Inquiry—and two voice personas—Warm Young Female Guide and Calm Senior Male Guide. The outcomes included user engagement, subjective task load, human–AI trust, and immediate knowledge retention. The shared files include participant-level observations across the experimental conditions, variable definitions, scoring procedures, and documentation of missing or invalid knowledge-test records. These materials support the reproduction of the statistical analyses, tables, and figures reported in the manuscript. Participants are represented by anonymous identifiers, and directly identifying information is excluded.

papers.title: Beyond the Aggregate: Provenance, Communication and Scope in Machine-Learning FDI Forecasting for Policy
papers.authors: Ofierohor Ufuoma Earnest
papers.abstract: Machine-learning forecasts of national-aggregate FDI are increasingly offered to policymakers as decision support.This paper identifies three risks that accompany such forecasts and are rarely stated alongside the accuracy figures, and grounds each in a documented case.The first is provenance.A forecast assembled from central bank, statistical agency and multilateral sources inherits their definitional choices and revision practices, and downstream users usually cannot trace which source supplied which observation.In the case examined here, half the assembled series was linearly interpolated from annual figures and two further construction defects were present, none of which was documented or detectable from the published output.The second is communication.An out-of-sample R-squared says nothing about which quarters a model handles well; the best model in the companion forecasting study achieved 0.0257 and was the only one of twelve to beat a mean benchmark, a context that a headline figure omits.The third is aggregation.National-aggregate FDI in Nigeria is dominated by a small number of large transactions, so a forecast validated at that level supports no inference about sectoral or regional dynamics.We propose three safeguards: a provenance table including construction method, mandatory disclosure of failure modes alongside any accuracy figure, and explicit scope limits restricting aggregate forecasts to aggregate questions.

papers.title: Educational Innovation: Using Design Thinking in the Training of Biochemistry Students
papers.authors: HGR Meira, PA Granjero
papers.abstract: In the 21st century educational context there is an increasing demand for dynamic teaching approaches that not only transmit knowledge, but also stimulate the development of fundamental skills. In this sense, Design Thinking in Education has stood out as an effective tool to achieve this goal. The aim of this study was to implement the Design Thinking in Education in the Enzymology discipline to Biochemistry students and evaluate the perception of the methodology. Twenty biochemistry students received classes in Problems, Solutions and Prototyping. The GPT chat tool was used to identify Problems and Solutions and Mind Mapping to organize ideas. Students were divided into groups and instructed to develop a product or process. At the end of the course, the groups presented their proposals in a Pitch day. An online form was used to collect student feedback. The results indicated a high evaluation of sequence of topics appropriateness, with an average score of 4.45 (± 0.75) out of 5.Regarding the teaching methodology, participants gave it a score of 4.55 (± 0.82). Regarding the knowledge acquired, the average rating was 4.4 (± 0.88). Participation in the proposed activities was well received, with a score of 4.5 (± 0.82). Interest in the project for academic training was moderate, with an average rating of 4.15 (± 0.95). Overall, the project received a good evaluation, with an average score of 4.6 (± 0.55) out of 5. The results reveal a positive reception of the proposed activities, reflecting the effectiveness of the approach in teaching Design Thinking concepts in Biochemistry teaching. There was good interest in the project for academic training, the majority of students demonstrated satisfactory understanding of the content presented.

papers.title: Effects of speech-enabled LLM-based chatbots on L2 learning outcomes and affective domains: a multilevel meta-analysis
papers.authors: Eunjin Lee, Hansol Lee, Jang Ho Lee
papers.journal: IRAL - International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching
papers.abstract: Abstract Recent developments in natural language processing and automatic speech recognition have significantly advanced chatbot communication using the voice mode, establishing these tools as viable resources for L2 speaking practice. More recently, the L2 chatbot domain has leveraged large language models (LLMs) to enhance contextual understanding and facilitate meaningful dialogues, prompting research into the effects of speech- and LLM-based chatbots on L2 learning outcomes and affective domains. This study presents a synthesis of these findings using a multilevel meta-analysis. Based on a dataset of 19 studies (32 samples, N = 2,643), the results revealed that the overall effect size for L2 learning outcomes was 0.68 ( p < 0.001). The overall effect size for affective domains was 0.64 ( p < 0.001). Moreover, moderator analyses indicated that a range of learner and intervention characteristics, including learner proficiency, educational level, interaction format, and context of chatbot use, significantly influenced the overall effectiveness.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Fatigue Detection From EEG Signals: A Methodological Pilot Framework With Potential For Nursing Applications
papers.authors: Şerife Çetin, Eda Dağdevır
papers.journal: Journal of Clinical Practice and Research
papers.abstract: Objective: Fatigue is a significant occupational health issue that adversely affects attention and decision-making. This study aimed to objectively predict fatigue levels using EEG signals and machine learning models and to develop a physiologically based assessment framework with potential future applications in nursing. Materials and Methods: Time-domain, frequency-domain, entropy, Hjorth, and wavelet features were extracted from EEG data collected from 12 participants aged 21-40 years, with fatigue levels labeled using various scales. Results: Classification performance varied across validation strategies. Under 5-fold cross-validation, Random Forest achieved the highest performance (accuracy=1.00, macro-F1=1.00), while KNN and NB also demonstrated strong performance. However, under LOOCV, sensitivity, precision, and macro-F1 values decreased despite relatively high accuracy. LOSO validation yielded more balanced results, with Random Forest maintaining the best performance (accuracy=0.97, macro-F1=0.91). Conclusion: EEG-derived features provide valuable information for fatigue assessment. Although high performance was achieved under certain validation strategies, subject-independent evaluation revealed more realistic performance levels. The proposed framework offers a practical approach to fatigue monitoring. Future studies should focus on larger, domain-specific datasets and multimodal integration to enhance generalizability.

papers.title: Leadership as a boundary condition on trust in AI: Transformational leadership, leader-member exchange, and employee intentions to use generative AI
papers.authors: Mark Irwin, Yujong Hwang
papers.abstract: The onset of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has outpaced organizations’ understanding of what makes employees willing to use it. This study asks whether leadership quality shapes how employees translate beliefs about AI into intentions to use it at work. Adapting the multidimensional online trust instrument of Hwang and Lee (2012) to the AI context, we measured uncertainty avoidance, descriptive norms, perceived reliability, and perceived ability, and tested each as a predictor of behavioral intention to use AI. Leadership was assessed twice in the same sample, once as transformational leader behavior (Podsakoff et al., 1990) and once as leader-member exchange (Graen & Uhl-Bien, 1995), allowing the moderation to be tested against two distinct leadership constructs. Working adults recruited through LinkedIn completed the survey (N = 97 for models involving AI measures). Perceived AI ability predicted behavioral intention, and transformational leadership moderated that relationship. The interaction replicated with LMX-7: the association between perceived ability and intention was stronger under higher-quality leadership. Descriptive norms predicted intention but showed no interaction; uncertainty avoidance predicted nothing. Leadership was also associated with significantly lower intention among the roughly one quarter of employees who rated AI’s capability lowest. This paper discusses implications for theory and practice. Perceived reliability, perceived ability, and behavioral intention were each measured with a single adapted item, so these findings are exploratory.

papers.title: The attitudes towards generative AI among games development professionals and students
papers.authors: Łukasz Sikorski, Jacek Matulewski, Małgorzata Czerwonka
papers.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has gained significant importance in knowledge working processes, including the video games industry, which we use as an example, enhancing production efficiency. However, this technology has raised concerns, particularly regarding potential job market threats, which make the use of GenAI a current topic of social importance. Our research aimed to explore the attitudes of industry professionals and students interested in game creation towards GenAI. We focused on their stance on using GenAI in the video game industry and understanding the factors influencing them. For this purpose, we collected survey data from 175 participants. Results revealed that professionals expressed more positive attitudes towards GenAI than students. Within the study sample, attitudes towards GenAI varied across professional subgroups: artist respondents reported comparatively less favourable attitudes, whereas the manager subgroup reported the highest mean level of support. Male respondents reported more favourable attitudes than female respondents. However, findings involving small subgroups should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.title: Cognitive impairment and danger to humanity, or personal assistant and learning tool? Exploring attitudes towards ChatGPT and their predictors
papers.authors: Ana Jovančević, Izabel Cvetković, Jasper Van Assche, Mladen Popović, Eva Alice Christiane Bittner
papers.abstract: This study examines the factors shaping attitudes towards ChatGPT inclusive of personality traits, ideological orientations, AI literacy, gender, and cultural context. In Study 1 (Ntotal = 500; Nvalid = 472 Serbia), positive perceptions of ChatGPT as a learning tool and personal assistant were linked to higher AI literacy and supportive views of AI, whereas negative AI-related attitudes predicted concerns about ChatGPT's cognitive impairment and existential threats. Gender played a crucial role: among men, higher levels of right-wing authoritarianism (RWA) and social dominance orientation (SDO) predicted more negative attitudes, while among women, RWA, SDO, and Openness were associated with more positive views. Study 2 compared German (as a representative of one of the most developed countries, especially in AI development; Ntotal = 115; Nvalid = 112) and Serbian (as an example of a less AI-developed country; Ntotal = 119; Nvalid = 117) samples, revealing significant differences (e.g., Germans scored higher in AI literacy, while Serbian participants scored higher in Conscientiousness and Extraversion. We further found different and unique effects of the examined predictors on participants' AI- and ChatGPT-related attitudes across both samples, possibly driven by the above-mentioned base differences. These findings underscore a complex interplay of individual and cultural factors that drive divergent interpretations of AI's societal role, highlighting the need to consider context when assessing public acceptance of emerging technologies.

papers.title: Examining public acceptance of AI versus human-centric dementia care across NHS England’s dementia pathway stages
papers.authors: Thomas O'Fee, Santosh Vijaykumar, Michael Craig
papers.abstract: Abstract With dementia diagnoses in the UK projected to exceed one million in 2025, there is an urgent need for scalable and effective care solutions to ease pressure on health and social care systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled smart home systems are emerging as promising digital health innovations, offering cognitive support, real-time monitoring, and decision-making assistance. However, concerns around trust, user agency, and misconceptions about AI continue to limit acceptance and may hinder adoption. This study examined how stage of dementia care, system design, and level of system involvement shape public attitudes towards AI-driven care technologies. A repeated-measures design was employed, using vignettes that varied across three dimensions: stage of care (aligned with NHS England’s Dementia Well Pathway), system centrism (AI-based versus human-based), and level of involvement (moderate support versus full control). Participants aged 55-64 years – a group at elevated risk of developing dementia or encountering these technologies within the next decade – rated each scenario on both acceptability and likelihood of use. Findings showed that acceptability was sensitive to both care stage and system type. A significant interaction indicated that full human involvement was consistently rated as more acceptable, while AI involvement was viewed more favourably only at moderate levels. This interaction effect intensified across the dementia care pathway, with the largest discrepancies observed in later stages such as Living well and Dying well, where full-control AI was rated least acceptable. In terms of perceived likelihood, scenarios were generally judged more likely under conditions of moderate involvement, with human-centric scenarios rated as more likely than AI-centric ones, particularly in later stages. These results highlight the importance of trust, autonomy, and public understanding in AI adoption. Acceptance was highest when AI was positioned to augment rather than replace human input, supporting hybrid models that preserve agency while enhancing scalability. Author Summary Dementia diagnoses are increasing rapidly, creating an urgent need for innovative care solutions. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and AI-integrated smart-homes offer a promising way to provide cognitive care and support through remote monitoring, but public trust and acceptance remain a challenge. Here, we explored people’s affective attitudes towards AI for dementia care by presenting scenarios that varied based on stage of dementia (from preventative to end-of-life care), whether the system was AI or human-based, and the level of control the system had over the care (moderate or full). We surveyed a sample of older adults, a group of potential future users of this technology. Our findings show that people’s attitudes are highly dependent on factors such as stage of care, level of system control/involvement, and system centricity, human-centric systems were consistently rated as the most acceptable option, while AI was most favourable when offering moderate support rather than taking full control. This preference for human-centric, moderate support grew stronger in the later stages of dementia care. In summary, people are more open to adopting AI when it is used to enhance human care, rather than replace it. This suggests that hybrid healthcare models, where AI is used to support and supplement caregivers, will be the most effective way to integrate these scalable technologies into dementia care.

papers.title: Two-module upgrade for 3D, high-resolution microscopy DMD patterned excitation and light-field detection
papers.authors: Niklas Ruprich, Aylin Talu, Jan Gelhoet, Anna Seidler, Alexander Heisterkamp, Stefan Kalies
papers.abstract: We present a modular upgrade to conventional widefield microscopy that integrates Fourier light field microscopy (FLFM) with structured illumination microscopy (SIM) for high-resolution volumetric biological imaging. The system combines a digital micromirror device (DMD)-based patterned illumination module with a light field detection path added to a commercial microscope, enabling flexible switching between widefield and FLFM modalities. By incorporating both analytical (MAP-SIM) and machine-learning-based (ML-SIM) reconstruction methods, we demonstrate significant resolution enhancement and background suppression in both 2D and 3D imaging. Experimental validation on murine intestinal organoids shows that applying SIM prior to FLFM reconstruction yields up to 1.4× lateral resolution improvement while preserving volumetric information. Additionally, FLFM acquisition drastically reduces photobleaching compared to conventional z-stack imaging. The proposed setup provides a cost-effective and versatile platform for multi-color, 3D imaging, with potential applications in microscopy education, or live-cell imaging.

papers.title: "Smarter but Not Wiser": A Transdisciplinary CFA-GRM Simulation Pipeline for Mapping Human–GenAI Interaction
papers.authors: 3susanti, Kana Hidayati, Juverio Pangestu, Rina Nopita Manullang, Achmad Fatahillah, Ifan Rivaldo, Nur Sehang Thamrin, Putri Theresia Oktaviani Manorek, Barquna Tri Raraswati, Syarifah Niken Purnani, Amirudin Amirudin, Chalimatus Sa'diyah, Jacinto Soares da Silva
papers.abstract: Background The integration of Generative AI (GenAI) in higher education creates a paradox between technical efficiency and cognitive depth. Current institutional responses rely more on fragmented oversight than on ecology- and process-oriented assessment. There is a lack of diagnostic tools to map psychometric thresholds when strategic cognitive shifts transition into functional dependence. Methods We present a simulation-based methodological framework using the Tripartite Confirmatory Factor Analysis–Graded Response Model (CFA-GRM). Grounded in the cognitive-affective-conative tripartite model, this study uses a Monte Carlo simulation (N = 1,000) to demonstrate how latent interaction pathways can be structurally validated and how item parameters can be calibrated against a pre-specified diagnostic threshold ( θ ≈ 0.5), with a replication study to establish parameter recovery. Results Across 200 replications at each of N = 1,000 and N = 300, all 400 converged with admissible solutions and recovered the generating parameters with maximum absolute relative bias of 0.040; interval coverage met conventional criteria for 11 of 15 parameter groups at N = 1,000 and 8 of 15 at N = 300. In the single illustrative dataset, the fit is near-perfect (robust CFI = 0.995, RMSEA = 0.010) because the generating and estimated models coincide, a property of the design rather than evidence for the model. Test information peaks at θ ≈ 0.07–0.22, not at the proposed threshold of θ ≈ 0.5. Furthermore, we introduce a Transdisciplinary Calibration Matrix that translates these psychometric signals into context-specific pedagogical interventions across four epistemic layers, in line with SDG 4. Conclusions This study does not claim empirical generalization. It provides a methodological blueprint, a recovered parameter set, and a shared diagnostic language for future empirical work on the ethical and adaptive integration of GenAI in higher education, aligned with SDG 4.

papers.title: AI Integration in Indonesian Education: Trends, Outcomes, and Challenges - A Comprehensive Review
papers.authors: Aulia Riski, Reinhard Leonardo Paais, Aan Komariah, Novebri Novebri, Lany Pranita Alang, Winda Verawati Ataupah, Zeffa Yurihana, Maria Vatmawaty Bety, Denny Ramadhan, Ade Syarifudin, Linda Dwiyanti, Teuku Yasser
papers.abstract: Background: Global education trends show the rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as one of the leading technologies worldwide, a shift increasingly reflected in Indonesian education. This study aims to provide a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by mapping the research landscape, its representation in practice and policy, its impact on learning quality, and the barriers to AI integration in Indonesian education. Method: Using the PRISMA protocol, 34 peer-reviewed articles indexed in the Scopus and Google Schoolar databases (2020-2026) were systematically selected and thematically analyzed across four main themes. Results: The findings indicate a rapid increase in publication productivity, particularly following the worldwide expansion of generative AI technologies after 2022. However, this growth remains unevenly distributed, concentrated in higher education institutions and urban centers on the island of Java, with a marked absence in primary and secondary education levels and in regions outside Java. The majority of AI-driven implementations consist of generative chatbots, adaptive learning platforms, and intelligent tutoring systems, alongside emerging applications such as learning analytics and AI-powered instructional media. Several studies included in this review reported that AI has contributed to measurable improvements in student outcomes including learning achievement, motivation, engagement, and teaching efficiency with studies reporting relative performance gains of 20-35% in well-implemented AI environments. Nonetheless, its adoption also poses significant risks, including a decline in students' critical thinking skills, threats to academic integrity, and the absence of comprehensive data privacy policies and ethical standards governing AI use in education. Conclusion: These findings underscore the urgent need for a responsible AI implementation framework in Indonesia one that incorporates standardized AI literacy competencies for teachers, locally contextualized ethical policies, and a functional national roadmap for AI-enabled educational transformation.

papers.title: eHealth-Guided Exercise Improves Peak Oxygen Uptake and Health-Related Quality of Life After COVID-19: A Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.authors: Espen Alexander Eriksen, Ulrik Wisløff, Ottar Brohaug Welde, Sindre Midttun, Eli Anne Skaug, Jon Magne Letnes, Ross A Arena, Patrick J. Dunn, Tommi Juhani Vasankari, Torbjørn Omland, Dorthe Stensvold
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Physical activity (PA) levels declined during the COVID-19 pandemic, contributing to reduced fitness and quality of life. eHealth tools may help increase PA. In a six-month randomized controlled trial, we evaluated Activity Quotient (AQ), an innovative eHealth tool designed to promote PA and improve peak oxygen uptake (V̇O2peak), compared with standard advice on national PA recommendations in physically inactive adults recovering from COVID-19. METHODS: Seventy-seven participants with previous COVID-19 infection were randomized 1:1 to either receive: 1) an eHealth-guided exercise intervention (n=38), using AQ to motivate for a PA dose that led to >100 weekly AQs, or 2) a control group (n=39) advised to follow standard PA recommendations. V̇O2peak scaled for fat-free mass (FFM) was the primary outcome, assessed in a subsample of participants who completed clinical assessment (n=33; eHealth group n=16, control n=17), while secondary outcomes included physical and mental scores of health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze the effects of the intervention. RESULTS: Participants (79% women) were 41.4±10.0 years and had a BMI of 28.8±5.9 kg/m². Among 33 participants who completed clinical assessment, V̇O2peak increased 4.9 mL•kgFFM -1•min -1 (95%CI 1.2 to 8.7, p=0.0134) more in the eHealth group compared with controls. Mental HRQoL increased by 9.8 points (95% CI 2.5 to 17.0, p=0.009) more in the eHealth group compared with controls. No between-group difference was observed in physical score of HRQoL. CONCLUSIONS: A six-month eHealth-guided exercise intervention using AQ was more effective than standard PA advice in improving V̇O2peak and mental HRQoL among physically inactive adults recovering from COVID-19. These findings highlight the potential of AQ as an effective and feasible approach for post-COVID rehabilitation.

papers.title: Multidisciplinary attitudes towards LLM-structured oncologic CT reports: a prospective fixed-sequence questionnaire study
papers.authors: Felix Busch, Alexander Wolfgang Marka, Lilly F. Wingberg, Philipp Prucker, Su Hwan Kim, Quirin Strotzer, Christina Schmidt, Jacqueline Lammert, Kai Joachim Borm, Jan C. Peeken, Marcus R. Makowski, Lisa C. Adams, Keno K. Bressem
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Large language models (LLMs) can automate the conversion of radiologic free text into structured reports, but multidisciplinary reader preferences for the resulting output remain insufficiently studied. This prospective, two-phase, fixed-sequence within-participant study evaluated reader assessments of LLM-structured versus conventional free-text oncologic CT reports. MATERIAL & METHODS: A paired convenience sample of radiologists, radiology technologists, oncologists, and medical students was recruited between May and November 2025. In Phase 1, participants rated 5 free-text oncologic CT reports for readability and comprehension (3 items), oncologic information quality (5 items), and clinical utility (4 items) on a 9-point Likert scale. After a washout of at least 4 weeks, participants rated the LLM-structured version generated by Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct. RESULTS: Sixty-six paired participants (24 medical students, 22 radiologists, 12 radiology technologists, 8 oncologists) were included (mean [standard deviation] age, 30.5 [7.6] years; 37 [56.1%] female). Structured reports showed significantly higher odds of agreement for 11 of 12 items (odds ratio [OR] range, 1.70-4.81), with strongest effects for clinical utility (OR, 4.81; 95% CI, 3.24-7.15), information findability (OR, 4.31; 95% CI, 3.12-5.96), recommendation clarity (OR, 4.14; 95% CI, 2.95-5.83), and patient communication suitability (OR, 3.45; 95% CI, 2.59-4.60). Radiology technologists showed significantly higher ratings for all 12 items, radiologists for 6, students for 7, and oncologists for none. CONCLUSION: In this single-center paired sample, LLM-structured oncologic CT reports received higher reader ratings than conventional free-text reports across most evaluated dimensions, with the largest differences observed for information findability and clinical utility. These findings support further evaluation of radiologist-supervised LLM-assisted report structuring, including formal source-to-output validation and randomized multicenter assessment, before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Can large language models assess enterprise digital transformation?
papers.authors: Zhenkun Zhou, Yihan He, Tao Ren
papers.abstract: Enterprise digital transformation reshapes business models and operations through digital technologies, making scientific measurement essential for empirical research. This study proposes a large language model (LLM)-based multi-indicator and multi-level text measurement framework for identifying and classifying enterprise digital technology applications from two dimensions: digitalization and effectiveness. We further adopt a three-dimensional experimental design covering output modes, prompting strategies, and fine-tuning to evaluate model performance. The results show that LLMs generally outperform traditional machine learning (ML) models, even under Zero-shot settings. Synchronous multi-indicator output generally performs better than one-by-one output, whereas the effects of chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting and fine-tuning vary across models and tasks. Model performance varies across specific models and task settings, with both recent general-purpose models and reasoning-oriented models showing competitive results in different scenarios. Further analysis indicates that LLMs perform better on explicit digital technology indicators but show weaker performance on digital effectiveness indicators requiring contextual inference. Additional validation with non-Chinese multilingual LLMs and significance analysis supports the robustness of the main findings. This study provides a methodological tool and empirical evidence for measuring enterprise digital transformation using corporate disclosure texts.

papers.title: Validity and reliability of the Turkish version of the weight-related eating questionnaire in young adults
papers.authors: Elif Çelik, Emine Koçyiğit, Özge Cemali
papers.abstract: This study aimed to adapt the Weight-Related Eating Questionnaire (WREQ) into Turkish and to evaluate its validity and reliability among young adults. The WREQ is a brief instrument assessing weight-related eating behaviors, including routine and compensatory restraint, susceptibility to external cues, and emotional eating. A total of 301 young adults aged 19–35 years from three regions of Türkiye participated. Translation and cultural adaptation of the WREQ followed International Test Commission guidelines. Construct validity was assessed using exploration factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Convergent validity was examined through correlations with the Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire (TFEQ-R21) and the Dutch Eating Behaviour Questionnaire (DEBQ). Reliability was evaluated using Cronbach’s alpha, McDonald’s omega, and test–retest intraclass correlation coefficients. The sample consisted of 301 participants (85% female), with a mean age of 20.65 years (± 2.08) and a mean BMI of 22.33 kg/m² (± 3.67). EFA indicated adequate sampling adequacy (KMO = 0.88; Bartlett’s χ² = 2424.6, p < 0.001) and revealed a three-factor structure that explained 62.15% of the variance. The factors included Emotional Eating (33.96%), Dietary Restraint (19.32%), and Susceptibility to External Cues (8.87%), with communalities varying from 0.335 to 0.814. CFA indicated that the original four-factor model fit the data better than the three-factor model (Δχ²(3) = 41.025, p < 0.001; ΔCFI = 0.016), as shown by the following fit indices: χ ²/df = 2.46, RMSEA = 0.070, SRMR = 0.068, CFI = 0.940, and TLI = 0.920. Measurement invariance by sex was partially supported (ΔCFI ≤ 0.002). Convergent validity was evidenced by moderate to significant correlations with the TFEQ-R21 and DEBQ subscales ( r = 0.401–0.690, p < 0.001). BMI showed minor positive correlations with most subscales in the whole group. The overall scale exhibited strong internal consistency (α = 0.864), whereas subscales demonstrated acceptable to exceptional reliability (α = 0.708–0.924; ω = 0.725–0.927), HTMT readings below 0.85 corroborated discriminant validity. The Turkish version of the WREQ is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing weight-related eating behaviors among young adults and may serve as a useful tool in both research and clinical practice.

papers.title: A systematic review of foresight methods used in the formulation of futures scenarios: evidence from articles indexed in scopus and web of science (2014–2023)
papers.authors: Pedro León Cruz Aguilar, Javier Enrique Medina Vásquez, Olga Patricia Marín Arroyave
papers.abstract: This study presents a systematic literature review of the foresight methods used in the formulation of futures scenarios, analyzing 115 articles indexed in Scopus and Web of Science between 2014 and 2023. Applying the PRISMA methodology, the review identifies a plural methodological ecosystem in which—although qualitative approaches predominate—there are patterns of combination toward methodological triangulation aimed at strengthening plausibility and reducing bias in complex environments. The analysis shows that the most frequently used methods are environmental scanning (PESTEL), participatory workshops, the Delphi method, structural analysis (MICMAC), and Causal Layered Analysis (CLA). A significant expansion of these practices is observed beyond the traditional corporate sphere into sectors such as public health, higher education, governance, and environmental sustainability. The study further highlights an incipient presence of methods that incorporate artificial intelligence, text mining, and computational models, which complement qualitative narratives with quantitative rigor. The article proposes the concept of methodological aggregation capacity to describe the ability of scenario methodologies to coherently incorporate techniques of different epistemic natures. In conclusion, the maturity of the field rests on the systemic convergence between data-driven rigor and narrative depth, consolidating scenarios as instruments for social learning and strategic decision-making.

papers.title: Brief report on screening data from a randomized controlled trial of in-hospital buprenorphine initiation strategies
papers.authors: Abigail Haber, Guillermo Sanchez-Fat, Michele J. Buonora, Annika Sabado, Megan M. Ghiroli, Yuting Deng, Laila Khalid, Kristine Torres‐Lockhart, Marilyn Reyes, Kelly S. Ramsey, Joanna L. Starrels, Aaron D. Fox
papers.abstract: Objectives: Buprenorphine (BUP) is effective for treating opioid use disorder and chronic pain (CP); however, there are missed opportunities for initiation during hospitalization. We conducted a clinical trial of in-hospital BUP initiation strategies and reviewed electronic health record data (EHR) to identify potentially eligible patients for BUP treatment. We present trial screening data to analyze the efficiency of EHR surveillance to identify BUP-eligible patients. Methods: Recruitment occurred between 10/2022 to 10/2024 at two urban teaching hospitals. An automated EHR algorithm generated a daily list of patients with likely opioid misuse or OUD. Preliminary manual review of the EHR algorithm was conducted by staff, who then contacted potentially eligible patients and their physicians before assessing for trial eligibility and BUP treatment. If patients were not assessed, research assistants use pre-specified categories to document reasons why. Results: The algorithm produced 9140 records for screening and 8534 (93%) were excluded based on preliminary manual review. Of 434 potentially eligible patients, only 43 agreed to be assessed for the trial. Of the 43 patients, 29 were eligible and 23 enrolled in the trial and started BUP, yielding a 5% initiation rate among the pool of potentially eligible patients. Conclusions: While the automated EHR algorithm identified patients potentially eligible for BUP, substantial manual review was required. Improving algorithm precision, for example with artificial intelligence applications, could better identify BUP-eligible patients; nonetheless, our experience suggests that patient concerns and potential stigma regarding BUP present as ongoing obstacles to BUP uptake.

papers.title: Ethics-related appraisal in AI mediating AI exposure and adoption willingness in medical PhD Students: cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Mingli Pang, Huihui Wang, Huan Zhou, Jinsong Chen, Weifang Zhang
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly influenced medical education and clinical practice, yet significant variability exists in adoption willingness among healthcare professionals. While ethics-related appraisal was recognized as an important correlate of AI adoption willingness, its potential indirect role between AI exposure and adoption willingness has been underexplored, particularly among medical PhD students who represent future leaders in healthcare innovation. This cross-sectional study surveyed 202 medical PhD students to examine perceptions of AI in healthcare. Willingness to adopt AI was measured using three 5-point Likert items assessing recommendation intentions, participation willingness, and optimism about AI-driven outcomes. AI exposure was assessed through three items evaluating familiarity with AI concepts, clinical applications, and educational integration. Ethics-related appraisal was measured using four items reflecting perceptions of governance adequacy, application boundaries, international standards alignment, and legal-ethical awareness. Data were analyzed using SPSS 30.0 and SPSS Amos 30.0. AI exposure was positively associated with willingness to adopt AI, with a standardized total association of 0.537 [95% CI: 0.352 to 0.696]. The direct association was not statistically significant (95% CI: -0.161 to 0.184) when ethics-related appraisal was included in the model. The indirect association of AI exposure on willingness to adopt AI through ethics-related appraisal was 0.509 [95% CI: 0.341 to 0.727], accounting for 94.79% of the total association. In this cross-sectional sample, AI exposure was statistically associated with adoption willingness through its indirect association with ethics-related appraisal. These findings suggest that ethics-related appraisals is closely related to AI adoption attitudes among medical PhD students. Enhancing real-world AI exposure alongside structured ethics education may support more informed engagement with AI in healthcare.

papers.title: Association of self-efficacy, stress, performance expectation, and procrastination with AI dependency among medical students at a public sector university in Pakistan
papers.authors: Kiran Abdul Sattar, Shafaque Fatima, Syeda Kauser Ali, Hiba Zafar, Syed Moiz Abbas
papers.abstract: Educational institutions are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI), raising concerns about the extent to which students depend on AI within their education. While AI can help students learn more efficiently, overreliance on AI may negatively affect the development of critical thinking and problem-solving skills required of future healthcare professionals. AI dependency among medical students is an emerging concern. This study examined the association of self-efficacy, academic stress, performance expectation, and procrastination with AI dependency among medical students at a public sector university in Pakistan. A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted among 310 MBBS students across all academic years at a public sector university in Karachi, Pakistan. Data were collected using validated instruments measuring self-efficacy (6 items), academic stress (6 items), performance expectation (4 items), procrastination (Academic Situational Procrastination Scale), and AI dependency (5 items). Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), performed using SmartPLS 3.3.3, was used to examine the associations of the latent variables with AI dependency. Among participants, 94.19% reported having used ChatGPT, and 90.97% reported using AI primarily for academic assistance. The structural model explained 24.4% of the variance in AI dependency (R² = 0.244). Procrastination showed the strongest positive association with AI dependency (β = 0.427, p = 0.001), corresponding to a medium effect size (f² = 0.239). Performance expectation showed a small positive association (β = 0.143, p = 0.013), and self-efficacy showed a small positive association (β = 0.128, p = 0.046). Academic stress was not significantly associated with AI dependency (β = -0.007, p = 0.935). In this cross-sectional sample, procrastination showed the strongest positive association with AI dependency, followed by performance expectation and self-efficacy, while academic stress was not significantly associated with AI dependency. These associations suggest that AI use in this sample may be more closely linked to self-regulatory and motivational factors than to stress. The outcomes highlight the potential value of interventions focused on self-regulation and time management to support balanced AI integration in medical education while preserving critical thinking and independent learning skills.

papers.title: Integrating generative AI into cognitive apprenticeship–based problem-based learning in biochemistry: a quasi-experimental study
papers.authors: Meng Sheng, Yuqing Gong, Weiwu Hu, Yalin Liu
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Problem-Based Learning (PBL) is extensively employed in medical education to promote advanced cognitive skills. At the foundational level of medical education, novice learners frequently encounter difficulties in forming cohesive knowledge structures due to an excessive cognitive load. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new opportunities for learning support, yet its pedagogical role and integration mechanisms in medical education remain insufficiently explored. Methods This study developed an AI-supported problem-based learning model grounded in the cognitive apprenticeship framework (AI-CAS-PBL). Using the “Lipid Metabolism” unit in a biochemistry course, a quasi-experimental design was used to compare AI-CAS-PBL with conventional PBL and lecture-based learning (LBL). The same instructor taught all three groups. Learning objectives, core content, scheduled contact time, case materials, and research outcome assessment procedures were standardized across groups, whereas instructional approaches, learning support, and out-of-class activities differed.The AI learning agent was developed on the Coze platform and powered by the Doubao 1.5 Pro 32 K large language model. Learning outcomes included lipid metabolism knowledge and case-based clinical reasoning. Technology acceptance, perceived cognitive workload measured using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), self-efficacy, and cognitive apprenticeship experience were also assessed. Results Students in the AI-CAS-PBL group achieved significantly higher post-test lipid metabolism knowledge and clinical application analysis scores than both the conventional PBL and LBL groups (all P < 0.05). Students reported high perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use of the AI learning agent. Compared with the conventional PBL group, students in the AI-CAS-PBL group reported lower perceived cognitive workload and higher self-efficacy. Conclusion The AI-CAS-PBL group demonstrated higher post-intervention lipid metabolism knowledge and case-based clinical reasoning scores than the conventional PBL and LBL groups. Compared with conventional PBL, students in the AI-CAS-PBL group reported lower perceived cognitive workload and higher self-efficacy. These findings are consistent with the possibility that AI-supported questioning and instructor modeling may provide complementary forms of instructional support. However, because the interaction between AI and instructor scaffolding was not directly examined, the proposed dual-scaffolding framework should be regarded as a theoretically informed interpretation rather than a confirmed causal pathway. The model represents a promising approach to human–AI collaborative teaching that warrants further evaluation in larger, multicenter, and multi-class studies.

papers.title: Association between cumulative estimated pulse wave velocity and complete edentulism in middle-aged and older adults: a nationwide prospective cohort study
papers.authors: Yun Wu, Lin Yang, Cong Wang, Rong Wu
papers.abstract: Complete edentulism significantly affects quality of life in middle-aged and older adults. Evidence regarding the long-term cumulative effect of arterial stiffness on complete edentulism remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the longitudinal association between cumulative estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) and complete edentulism. We conducted a prospective analysis using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Data were collected across four waves: Wave 1 (2011–2012, baseline), Wave 2 (2013), Wave 3 (2015), and Wave 4 (2018). Cumulative ePWV was calculated as the product of the average ePWV from the 2012 and 2015 surveys and the time interval (3 years): (ePWV_2012 + ePWV_2015)/2 × (2015–2012). ePWV itself was derived from age and mean arterial pressure using the Greve equation. Complete edentulism was a self-reported measure. Multivariable Cox models were used, with adjustment for demographic factors (age, gender, marriage, residence, education), lifestyle factors (smoking, drinking), and health status (body mass index (BMI), hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and cardiovascular disease). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to examine nonlinearity, and subgroup analyses were performed. Among 5,142 participants, 321 complete edentulism cases were observed. Each unit increase in cumulative ePWV was associated with a 6.5% higher complete edentulism risk (HR = 1.065, 95%CI:1.043–1.087). The highest cumulative ePWV quartile was associated with a 3.273-fold greater risk than the lowest quartile (HR = 3.273, 95%CI:2.172–4.931). A nonlinear relationship was identified, with a significantly increased risk above 27.911 m/s ( P = 0.001). Subgroup analyses showed consistent associations. This prospective study establishes an independent association between cumulative ePWV and complete edentulism. The findings suggest that arterial stiffness assessment may help identify individuals at elevated risk. This finding may support the development of integrated cardiovascular–oral health strategies for aging populations.

papers.title: Immune–metabolic signatures of suicidal ideation in adolescents with major depressive disorder: a sex-specific analysis
papers.authors: Xinyu Zhang, Zhen Cao, Jialu Jiang, Ding Yang, Fengjie Gao, Chuyao Wang, Zhiyang Qi, Yudan Zhang, Binglong Wen, 马现仓, Yuan Gao, Min Jia
papers.abstract: Suicide is a major and devastating complication in adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD). However, it is often underreported in clinical settings, and its biological underpinnings and objective biomarkers remain unclear. This study investigated peripheral immune–metabolic alterations associated with suicidal ideation (SI) and explored sex-specific patterns. In total, 319 adolescents with MDD were enrolled, including 98 with SI and 221 without SI, as defined by the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. Peripheral immune and metabolic biomarkers were compared between groups using sex-stratified analyses, and their correlations with SI were examined. Machine learning (ML) models incorporating Shapley Additive Explanations were developed to evaluate classification performance for SI status and identify key sex-specific biomarkers. The SI group exhibited a hypometabolic profile characterized by lower glucose and lipid levels, alongside alterations in peripheral blood inflammatory markers, including elevated white blood cell counts, neutrophil counts and proportions, and derived inflammatory indices. Sex-stratified analyses revealed divergent patterns: inflammatory alterations predominated in female patients, whereas metabolic disturbances were more prominent in male patients. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested bidirectional immune–metabolic associations in female patients, whereas associations in male patients were primarily linked to metabolic pathways. ML models demonstrated good discriminative ability, and SHAP-based feature interpretation supported the observed sex-specific immune–metabolic patterns. SI in adolescents with MDD is associated with distinct immune–metabolic profiles with pronounced sex-specific patterns, characterized by predominantly inflammatory alterations in female patients and metabolic disturbances in male patients. These findings support the potential utility of immune–metabolic biomarkers as correlates of SI and provide a foundation for future longitudinal studies evaluating their role in risk assessment.

papers.title: Assessing the Digital Leadership Preparedness for the AI Era: A Latent Profile Analysis Based on the ACC Model
papers.authors: Xi Bei Xiong, Simin Cao, Tianhang Gao, Grace Y. Xu, Yichen Hou, Hui Li
papers.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the digital leadership of Chinese K-12 educational administrators in the context of rapid artificial intelligence (AI) development. Design/Approach/Method Drawing on survey data from 1,426 educational administrators in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, the research empirically validates the Attitude–Cognition–Capability (ACC) model as a multidimensional framework for assessing educational digital leadership. Findings Chinese educational administrators displayed generally positive attitudes and reasonable cognitive understanding regarding digital technologies but showed lower levels of practical capability, highlighting an “implementation gap.” Four distinct leadership profiles were identified—Hesitant Adopters, Enthusiastic Implementers, Balanced Moderates, and Comprehensive Experts. MANOVA and R3STEP latent profile analyses indicate that male leaders and those with higher educational attainment consistently exhibit higher digital leadership, while age, work experience, and administrative positions play more limited roles. The explained variance by demographic and professional factors remains modest, suggesting that broader contextual and organizational factors warrant future investigation. Originality/Value These findings offer a foundation for targeted professional development and underscore the importance of building robust, multidimensional digital leadership capacity to navigate the opportunities and challenges of AI-driven educational transformation in China.

papers.title: Hybrid wood–polymer composites for EV interiors: A material–psychological framework to modulate consumer purchase intention
papers.authors: Chen Junlu, Aimi Fadzirul Kamarubahrin
papers.abstract: We propose a hybrid wood–polymer composite system for electric vehicle (EV) interiors, designed to address the dual challenges of material performance and consumer psychological adaptation. The composite integrates cellulose fibers with a polyurethane matrix, achieving a balance between durability, lightweight properties, and tactile appeal, while a nanocellulose coating enhances visual aesthetics without compromising natural grain visibility. The material system is coupled with a psychological framework that models hedonic-adaptation dynamics, where emotional responses to sustainability claims (“circular sustainability” vs. “natural warmth”) and cocreation opportunities are quantified over time. A longitudinal experimental design employs 3D-printed prototypes and multimodal sensing (eye-tracking, robotic tactile feedback) to iteratively refine both material properties and framing strategies. The integration of the composite with conventional EV systems demonstrates practical benefits, such as reduced thermal conductivity for energy-efficient cabin conditioning and seamless capacitive touch interfaces. The novelty of this work lies in its closed-loop optimization between material science and behavioral economics, enabling data-driven adjustments to both physical and perceptual attributes. Results from repeated exposure sessions reveal how framing effects and material interactions collectively modulate purchase intention, offering actionable insights for EV manufacturers aiming to accelerate consumer acceptance of sustainable interior solutions. This approach bridges the gap between technical material innovation and consumer psychology, providing a scalable framework for future EV-interior design.

papers.title: TEISP: A TabNet-Based Framework Integrating Emotional Intelligence into Student Performance Prediction
papers.authors: Ashwini Umesh Koyande, Anu Singha
papers.abstract: Abstract Student performance prediction remains a significant challenge in Educational Data Mining, particularly when emotional and behavioral factors are considered alongside academic indicators. This study proposes a TabNet-based Emotional Intelligence Student Performance (TEISP) framework that integrates traditional academic attributes, including CGPA, attendance, and midterm scores, with emotional intelligence (EI) factors such as motivation, self-awareness, social skills, and stress management. The proposed framework employs TabNet, an interpretable deep learning architecture specifically designed for tabular data, capable of capturing complex nonlinear relationships while maintaining model transparency.Experiments were conducted using the VSIT–MIT dataset comprising 550 undergraduate students, 21 features, and three performance categories (Excellent, Average, and Poor). Model evaluation was performed using stratified 5-fold cross-validation to ensure robust and unbiased performance assessment. The proposed TEISP model achieved an average accuracy of 0.435 ± 0.018, with precision, recall, and F1-score values of 0.43, 0.42, and 0.42, respectively, and an AUC score of 0.88. Although the predictive accuracy is moderate, the model demonstrates superior stability, interpretability, and generalization compared with several baseline machine learning algorithms, including Naïve Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and Gradient Boosting.Furthermore, SHAP-based explainability analysis reveals that emotional intelligence attributes, particularly motivation and self-awareness, play a substantial role in predicting academic outcomes. The findings highlight the importance of incorporating emotional and behavioral factors into student performance prediction models and demonstrate the potential of interpretable deep learning frameworks for educational analytics and decision support systems.

papers.title: The professional knowledge, skills and specialist functions of certified clinical coding auditors
papers.authors: Kerin M Robinson, Stephanie Gjorgioski, Melanie Tassos, Sally Richardson, Merilyn M. Riley
papers.abstract: Background: The quality of Australia’s coded clinical data is essential for its reliability in myriad applications throughout the healthcare system, signalling the need for clinical coding auditing. Internal clinical coding auditors audit hospitals’ coded data, ‘in-house’. Independent, external auditors undertake audits on behalf of purchasers and providers: state/territory governments; health insurance funds; private hospital proprietors. Objective: To identify the professional knowledge, skills and specialist functions of certified clinical coding auditors in Australia. Method: A cross-sectional study design was utilised. A purposively designed, self-administered online survey was distributed to the study population ( N = 241), who achieved a ‘Certificate of External and Internal Clinical Coding Auditing’ or ‘Certificate of Internal Clinical Coding Auditing’ from La Trobe University, Australia, from 2005 to 2021. Results: Of the 93/241 (38.6%) respondents, these results concern those who had engaged, predominantly, in either external or internal auditing within their previous 5 years of employment. The responses of 42 practising auditors were analysed: 83.3% ( n = 35) had predominantly undertaken internal auditing within the past 5 years; 59.5% ( n = 25/42) had a Certificate of External and Internal Clinical Coding Auditing, 28% ( n = 7/25) of whom had predominately undertaken external auditing.
