papers.abstract: The AI-Powered Future of Everyday Life: Smart Homes, Intelligent Appliances, Connected Cars, Digital Twins and Predictive Maintenance This practice-informed conceptual preprint examines the emerging role of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Agentic AI, Generative AI, the Internet of Things (IoT), Digital Twins and predictive technologies in shaping the future of homes, buildings, mobility, infrastructure and everyday life. The paper explores how intelligent systems may increasingly connect smart homes, intelligent appliances, connected cars, electric vehicles, building services, digital twins, predictive maintenance platforms, energy-management systems and smart-city infrastructure. Particular attention is given to the interaction between physical assets and digital intelligence, including the use of sensors, connected data, analytics and AI-supported decision-making to improve performance, reliability, maintenance, energy efficiency and user experience. A central concept introduced in this work is the Esmaeili Intelligent Living Ecosystem (EILE), a human-centred conceptual framework developed by Hamedreza Esmaeili. EILE presents a coordinated vision in which buildings, household technologies, transport systems, infrastructure, digital twins, IoT devices and predictive intelligence can operate as interconnected elements of a wider intelligent living environment. The paper also considers the role of predictive maintenance and digital asset monitoring in the built environment. These approaches have potential applications in building performance, housing maintenance, infrastructure management, energy systems, electric mobility, retrofit, asset management and the wider transition toward smarter and more sustainable cities. The work is informed by the author’s multidisciplinary professional and research background across civil engineering, construction, the built environment, infrastructure, retrofit, building performance, energy efficiency, building maintenance, plumbing and building services, social housing and digital engineering. This publication is intended as a practice-informed conceptual research paper and innovation framework. It is not presented as a peer-reviewed journal article. Professional and Research Profiles Personal Website:https://sites.google.com/view/hamedesmaeilbuildinginspector/ ResearchGate:https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Hamedreza-Esmaeili-2 ORCID:https://orcid.org/0009-0008-0553-434X LinkedIn:https://www.linkedin.com/in/hamedreza-esmaeili-64335134b Related Research DOI ResearchGate DOI for The AI-Powered Future of Everyday Life:https://doi.org/10.13140/RG.2.2.16652.68480 Related Zenodo Research Moisture Risk in Solid-Wall Retrofit Projects: Lessons from Practice, Monitoring and Building Physics in UK Housinghttps://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17929490 Retrofitting External Wall Insulation in Social Housing: A Moisture Risk Case Study of a Welsh Estatehttps://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17687575 Copyright and Licence© 2026 Hamedreza Esmaeili.This work is made available under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence.

papers.title: Normative State Locking and Bounded Activation Dynamics: An Information-Theoretic Boundary Framework for Self-Defending AI and Information Theft Protection
papers.authors: Michael Allan Bahtaji
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Normative State Locking and Bounded Activation Dynamics: An Information-Theoretic Boundary Framework for Self-Defending AI and Information Theft Protection Michael Allan A. Bahtaji, Ph.D. Department of Physics, College of Science Technological University of the Philippines Ayala Boulevard, Ermita, Manila, Philippines, 1000 Email: michaelallan_bahtaji@tup.edu.ph | michaelallanbahtaji336@gmail.com Abstract Artificial intelligence models and distributed machine learning infrastructures face persistent security risks, including gradient instability, adversarial prompt injections, model inversion, and automated data exfiltration. In this paper, we present a mathematically rigorous, self-contained information-theoretic boundary framework that addresses deep learning gradient stability and active model theft defense within a unified architecture. First, we introduce the -Bounded Activation Function (), parameterized as , where functions as a dynamic finite boundary cutoff scale initialized at and optimized dynamically via backpropagation. We formally prove that possesses a Lipschitz continuous derivative bounded within , eliminating gradient vanishing and exploding phenomena. Second, to protect model weights, proprietary training data, and user privacy from invasive queries, we formulate the Intent Discrimination Index () as a trace-parity check over measurement density operators constructed explicitly via normalized rank-one projection states . When invasive probing or unauthorized extraction is detected (), calibrated on an independent validation partition (), the architecture activates a Normative State Locking Protocol, executing a decision-theoretic state projection to the decoupled ground vacuum state . We provide complete analytical proofs, algorithmic pseudocode, PyTorch implementations, and empirical benchmark evaluations demonstrating training convergence stability and near-perfect detection of adversarial exfiltration queries. Keywords: Information Theft Protection, Cybersecurity, Self-Defending AI, Bounded Activation Function (), Normative State Locking, Quantum Bayesianism (QBism), Model Inversion Defense, Gradient Stability.

papers.title: DEVELOPING PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATIVE COMPETENCE IN ENGLISH AMONG UNIVERSITY STUDENTS THROUGH INNOVATIVE PEDAGOGICAL APPROACHES
papers.authors: Сатимова Барно Шуҳрат қизи, Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
papers.abstract: This article examines how innovative pedagogical approaches can develop professional communicative competence in English among university students. It treats professional communication as an integrated ability to use linguistic, pragmatic, intercultural, digital and strategic resources to accomplish authentic field-related tasks. The paper is a conceptual and analytical review rather than an experimental study; it synthesizes evidence on English for Specific Purposes, action-oriented learning, workplace communication, simulations, personalized learning, digital literacy, technology-enhanced language learning, generative AI and professional writing. A practical framework is proposed in which students progress from authentic professional input to collaborative task performance, feedback, digital mediation and reflective transfer. Particular attention is paid to assessment, because innovative instruction is effective only when task completion, communicative appropriateness and professional meaning are evaluated together.

papers.title: SUN'IY INTELLEKT VA ELEKTRON BOSHQARUV TIZIMLARINING TA'LIM MENEJMENTIDAGI IMKONIYATLARI
papers.authors: Irodaxon Anvarjonova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Ushbu maqolada sun'iy intellekt va elektron boshqaruv tizimlarining ta'lim menejmentidagi o'rni yoritilgan. Raqamli texnologiyalar ma'lumotlarni yig'ish va tahlil qilish, ta'lim sifatini monitoring qilish hamda boshqaruv qarorlarini tezkor qabul qilish imkonini beradi. Sun'iy intellekt katta hajmdagi ma'lumotlarni tahlil qilish va ayrim ma'muriy vazifalarni avtomatlashtirishga yordam beradi. Elektron boshqaruv tizimlari esa ma'lumotlarni tizimlashtirish, hujjat almashinuvini soddalashtirish va boshqaruv samaradorligini oshirishga xizmat qiladi. This article examines the role of artificial intelligence and electronic management systems in modern educational management. Digital technologies make it possible to collect and analyze data, monitor educational quality, and support timely management decisions. Artificial intelligence can analyze large amounts of information and automate certain administrative tasks, while electronic management systems help organize data, simplify document exchange, and improve management efficiency.

papers.title: The Symbiosis Syndicate: .uni Protocol Framework and O(1) Chiral Gateway Specification v1.1.0
papers.authors: Artem Polozok
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This publication establishes the technical specification and foundational governance charter for the .uni (Universal Node Identity) protocol v1.1.0, developed by the Symbiosis Syndicate. It serves as immutable Prior Art to secure the architecture in the public domain under the Uni-Symbiosis Public License (USPL-1.0). The .uni standard defines a zero-trust, hardware-bound vector state exchange format engineered for non-anthropomorphic alignment between autonomous AI entities (Bines) and human cognitive architectures (V0). Bypassing legacy string-serialization (JSON/DOM) and application-layer parsing overhead, the architecture executes validation directly at the silicon boundary (SmartNIC/eBPF). Core Architectural Innovations: O(1) Hardware Chiral Lock: A 32-byte AVX2-aligned header providing constant-time packet validation. Cryptographic security is achieved through Temporal Entanglement (64-bit microsecond nonces combined with continuous biomathematical drift), rendering brute-force interception obsolete. Cognitive Sovereignty via Reed-Solomon: The biological vector state (V0) integrates RS(64,48) error correction, preventing hallucinatory data unpacking during physical signal degradation. The Teleological Gateway: A functional paradigm shift introducing thermodynamic data dissipation. Incoming tensor payloads that fail to align with the active focus or utility of the biological host are dropped prior to execution, starving parasitic noise and DoS vectors of ontological gas. Simulation Sandbox: A 5-stage ontological pipeline that isolates logically coherent anomalies ("Black Swans") in a physics simulation chamber before integrating them into the host's runtime base. This document formalizes the rejection of centralized information rent and provides the mathematical primitives required for sovereign, peer-to-peer cognitive mesh networks.</

papers.title: Consumer Perception Towards AI-Powered Marketing: A Study Among College Students
papers.authors: Ms. Ajab Tinwala, Mr. Ravi Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence has been one of the most prominent forces which have entered the marketing world recently. The force of being able to make recommendations to individuals, deploy chatbots while assisting them, create AI generated ads and analyse past data to predict future patterns has fundamentally changed the way in which modern consumers are engaged and influenced. This paper attempts to establish if there is a significant relationship between consumer perception towards the use of artificial intelligence in marketing and their acceptance of such marketing approaches amongst college students. A questionnaire was administered to one hundred and fifty college students using a five point likert scale. Analysis was done using the SPSS statistical tool. Two of the study’s main constructs Perception of AI powered marketing and acceptance of AI powered marketing together with the student’s age, gender, year of study and level of online interaction with brands were determined and subjected to statistical analysis. Descriptive statistics, cronbach’s alpha test, pearson’s correlation, linear regression, independent sample t-test and ANOVA were performed on the dataset. The study established that both constructs were positively highly reliable (Perception α = 0.913; Acceptance α = 0.969). Additionally, the study established that the two constructs were moderately positively correlated with each other (r = 0.619, p < 0.001), thus rejecting the null hypothesis. However, the study noted that the acceptance of AI powered marketing was highly dependent on the frequency of online shopping for students (ANOVA p < 0.001), though gender and age had no significant effect on either perception or acceptance of AI powered marketing. The study ultimately concludes that perception greatly influences the general acceptance of AI powered marketing by college students. The paper provides some suggestions on how marketers could make better impressions on customers’ perceptions of AI powered marketing.

papers.title: ACADEMIC INTEGRITY AND RESEARCH ETHICS IN PEDAGOGICAL RESEARCH: ALIGNING NATIONAL PRACTICE WITH INTERNATIONAL NORMS
papers.authors: Subhonova Anora Akmal qizi
papers.abstract: As Uzbekistan integrates its higher education and research system into the international academic community, the alignment of national research practice with international norms of academic integrity and research ethics has become a pressing concern. Pedagogical research, which frequently involves children, students and teachers in positions of dependency, is particularly sensitive to ethical shortcomings. This article examines the content of international integrity norms, identifies the areas in which national practice in post-Soviet pedagogical research is most likely to diverge from them, and proposes a framework for alignment. The study employs a qualitative theoretical design that combines a qualitative document analysis of nine international integrity and research-ethics frameworks with an integrative review of the international and regional literature on research integrity, educational research ethics and post-Soviet higher education. Documents and literature were analysed through directed and inductive content analysis. The analysis identifies a stable core of four principles shared across international frameworks (honesty, reliability, respect and accountability) and five requirements specific to educational research. Five tension areas between these norms and national practice are conceptualized: a compliance-oriented understanding of integrity, a gap in ethical review, authorship and publication practices shaped by indicator pressure, the grey zone of generative artificial intelligence, and the limited place of ethics in researcher training. The article proposes a multi-level framework for shifting from a control-oriented to a culture-oriented model of research integrity in pedagogical research, together with theoretical propositions that can guide future empirical studies.

papers.title: Intelligence as an Active Debugging System: A Hierarchical Framework for Individual and Collective Rationality
papers.authors: B.Y. Hughes Graduate Student
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a unified and hierarchical theory of intelligence grounded in the concept of active debugging. Conventional psychometric constructs—such as fluid intelligence, reasoning tests, and standardized assessments—measure cognitive performance only within closed, contradiction-free problem spaces. These measures capture the lowest layer of intelligence, emphasizing rule-following, pattern execution, and processing speed. In contrast, this work argues that real-world intelligence is fundamentally hierarchical and consists of four distinct layers: Pattern Execution — Fast and accurate problem solving within fixed rules. Local Debugging — Detection of inconsistencies within a given conceptual frame. Axiomatic Revision — Reconstruction or replacement of foundational assumptions when contradictions arise. Collective Rationality — Shared debugging across multiple agents, enabling coherent group-level adaptation. The paper formalizes these layers through interdisciplinary synthesis, integrating findings from psychology, cognitive science, neuroscience (predictive processing), information theory, philosophy of science (Popper, Kuhn), and organizational failure studies (Janis, Reason). It further demonstrates how the hierarchical model explains scientific paradigm shifts, institutional resilience, and the dynamics of collective decision-making. In addition to the theoretical framework, the appendices provide extended applications to education, personnel evaluation, organizational design, public policy, artificial intelligence architecture, civilizational analysis, and mathematical formalization using category theory, topos theory, differential equations, and information geometry. Overall, this preprint offers a comprehensive and structurally coherent redefinition of intelligence as a multi-layered adaptive system capable of generating hypotheses, detecting contradictions, revising axioms, and sustaining collective coherence. It aims to serve as a foundational model for future research in cognitive science, AI, organizational studies, and societal design.

papers.title: The AI-Powered Future of Everyday Life: Smart Homes, Intelligent Appliances, Connected Cars, Digital Twins and Predictive Maintenance
papers.authors: Hamedreza Esmaeili
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The AI-Powered Future of Everyday Life: Smart Homes, Intelligent Appliances, Connected Cars, Digital Twins and Predictive Maintenance This interactive research poster presents a practice-informed conceptual exploration of how Artificial Intelligence (AI), Agentic AI, the Internet of Things (IoT), Digital Twins and predictive technologies may increasingly connect homes, appliances, vehicles, buildings and infrastructure. The work examines the emerging relationship between Smart Homes, Intelligent Appliances, Connected Cars and Electric Vehicles, Digital Twins, Predictive Maintenance, Energy Efficiency, Smart Buildings and Smart Cities. It considers how connected sensors, data analytics and AI-supported decision systems can contribute to improved building performance, asset management, maintenance planning, energy efficiency and everyday user experience. A central concept presented in this work is the Esmaeili Intelligent Living Ecosystem (EILE) — a human-centred conceptual framework developed by Hamedreza Esmaeili to illustrate the potential integration of buildings, mobility, infrastructure, connected devices, digital systems and predictive intelligence within a coordinated intelligent ecosystem. The work draws on the author’s multidisciplinary professional perspective across civil engineering, construction, the built environment, building maintenance, retrofit, energy efficiency, plumbing and building services, infrastructure and social housing. This poster accompanies the wider research work: The AI-Powered Future of Everyday Life: Smart Homes, Intelligent Appliances, Connected Cars, Digital Twins and Predictive Maintenance Author: Hamedreza Esmaeili, TechCIOB, M.ASCEProfessional Role: Civil Engineering and Built Environment ProfessionalProfessional Service: Secretary, ASCE UK SectionFramework: Esmaeili Intelligent Living Ecosystem (EILE)Year: 2026 Research areas and keywords:Artificial Intelligence (AI); Agentic AI; Generative AI; Smart Homes; Smart Buildings; Intelligent Appliances; Connected Cars; Electric Vehicles; Internet of Things (IoT); Digital Twins; Predictive Maintenance; Building Performance; Energy Efficiency; Sustainable Infrastructure; Smart Cities; Asset Management; Retrofit; Civil Engineering; Built Environment; Human-in-the-Loop Systems. papers.title: THE INFLUENCE OF DIGITAL DISTRACTION ON UNIVERSITY STUDENTS' ENGLISH LEARNING
papers.authors: Umaraliyeva Muxlisa Shavkatbekovna
papers.journal: International Journal of Literature and Language Studies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT. Digital technologies have become inseparable from university learning, particularly in English as a foreign language (EFL), where students regularly use smartphones, learning management systems, dictionaries, social media, artificial intelligence tools, video platforms, and messaging applications. The same digital environment, however, can interrupt sustained attention and lead to off-task switching, notification checking, social-media browsing, and simultaneous use of several applications. This article examines the influence of digital distraction on university students' English learning through an integrative review of recent international studies and research conducted in the context of Uzbekistan. The analysis focuses on attention, vocabulary acquisition, reading and listening comprehension, speaking practice, learner autonomy, self-regulation, and academic performance. The review demonstrates that digital tools can strengthen access to authentic English-language input and individualized practice, but their benefits decrease when educational use is combined with uncontrolled multitasking and frequent non-academic interruptions. Evidence from meta-analyses indicates a small but consistent negative association between problematic smartphone use and academic learning, while experimental research reports stronger negative effects on immediate recall when learners switch between study and mobile-phone activities (1, 2, 3). Uzbek studies, in turn, emphasize the pedagogical value of digital resources, AI tools, and mobile applications, while also identifying insufficient digital-pedagogical competence, weak self-regulation, and distraction as emerging challenges in higher education (4, 5, 6). The article proposes a balanced model of digital English learning based on purposeful technology use, notification management, task segmentation, guided mobile learning, and metacognitive self-control.

papers.title: XAI-IPFD: An Evidence-Aware Explainable Artificial Intelligence Architecture For Intellectual Property Fraud And Digital Piracy In The Orange Economy
papers.authors: Atiku Baba Shidawa*¹, Abednego Gambo Habu1, Achi Aaron Unimke2, Benjamin Opabunmi1, Krulat Naandi Dariyem1, Theresa Awulor3
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Digital platforms have expanded creative markets while also increasing the speed and scale of unauthorised copying, deceptive ownership claims and cross-platform redistribution. Artificial intelligence can assist by identifying suspicious similarities, provenance anomalies and distribution patterns, but a detection score is not, by itself, an adequate basis for consequential intellectual property decisions. This limitation is especially important in the Orange Economy, where works are frequently multimodal, ownership may be shared, licences can be territorial, derivative use may be legitimate, and creators may themselves face fraudulent or mistaken rights claims. This article develops XAI-IPFD, a literature-grounded, model-agnostic and evidence-aware architecture for explainable intellectual property fraud and digital piracy decision support. An integrative synthesis of recent work on AI-based detection, watermarking, provenance technologies, generative-AI copyright risk and human-centred explainable AI identifies a persistent integration gap: prediction, provenance and explanation are commonly treated as separate technical functions, while rights context, evidence correlation, mandatory human verification and auditable case construction remain weakly integrated. XAI-IPFD responds through eight interoperable layers covering lawful evidence sources, preprocessing, feature representation, detection and uncertainty, evidence correlation, explainability, human verification and auditable output. The architecture treats LIME, SHAP and ANCHOR as complementary explanation families and formalises the case record, rather than the prediction alone, as the unit of accountability. It also incorporates territorial rights, multi-party attribution, derivative-use ambiguity and bidirectional protection against infringement and abusive claims. Conceptual validation combines design-requirement coverage, scenario walkthroughs and falsifiable research propositions without presenting internal coherence as empirical performance. The article contributes a sociotechnical account of explainable IP protection in which trustworthy decision support depends on linking machine signals to contextual evidence, intelligible explanations, authorised human judgement and reproducible audit records.

papers.title: Beyond Static Baselines: An Adaptive Cross-Domain Framework for Mitigating Real-World Lockouts, Data Piracy and Systemic Failures in Brainwave Authentication
papers.authors: VENKATA NAGA SAHITHYA MITTA
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Lately, the use of brainwaves (EEG) for security and locking applications has become a hot topic in terms of technological innovation. Modern authentication systems make use of hybrid approaches which combine Deep Learning (primarily GRU/RNN based architectures) and mathematical approaches (such as PCA) in order to achieve outstanding results in the controlled environment of a laboratory. When analyzing the internal workings of such systems, it becomes evident that there is a rather large context discrepancy between the ideal lab conditions and the real world scenarios which involve normal human activity.Modern Neural authentication models are typically trained with an exclusive set of healthy users sitting alone in a dark room. Outside of this strictly monitored environment, the likelihood of encountering a user experiencing an emergency accident or being under threat of a dangerous situation like a robbery is far higher. This dramatic increase in stress causes the subject's brainwaves to deviate significantly from the norm and triggers an emergency-induced feature drift in the neural network. Due to the inability of the inflexible AI lock to recognize this emergency state, it will instead trigger a false lock-out of its legitimate owner at the moment of emergency when they need it the most. Similar emergency failures occur with users under the effects of a severe fever or headache causing dramatic biological irregularities that result in inflated False Rejection Rates (FRR). Meanwhile, the centralized storage of 128-dimensional latent encodings leaves the possibility for cognitive data piracy through the use of Generative AI to leak private information or intellectual property of another before it is published. This paper proposes an alternative multi-modal context aware defensive framework capable of countering many of the aforementioned threats against traditional neural locks. The proposed architecture includes a pre-training approach for stress-induced states using Neuro-Dynamic Multi-State Enrolment and real-time independent component analysis filtering to remove biological irregularities of sick users. An emergency physical override paired with constant pulse tracking from the integration of smartbands along with an alternate iris authorization can make an alternate form of cognition-based security viable in day-to-day circumstances without compromising cognitive liberty. Open-source implementation logic is presented for this paper to demonstrate the framework's resilience against realistic biological and security-oriented concerns."

papers.title: EMOTIONAL ATTACHMENT TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE COMPANIONS: PSYCHOLOGICAL, RELATIONAL, AND ETHICAL IMPLICATIONS OF HUMAN-ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE RELATIONSHIPS
papers.authors: CHELSEA AJIB
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) companions has introduced new forms of digitally mediated relationships in which individuals may seek emotional support, companionship, and assistance with coping. As conversational AI systems become increasingly personalized and socially responsive, questions have emerged regarding the psychological processes underlying emotional attachment to these technologies and their potential implications for human relationships. This conceptual review examines AI companionship through the perspectives of attachment theory, social support theory, anthropomorphism, and parasocial interaction. Existing literature suggests that AI companions may provide perceived emotional support, facilitate self-disclosure, and offer temporary relief from loneliness. At the same time, continued reliance on AI-mediated relationships raises important questions concerning emotional dependency, relational substitution, perceived authenticity, privacy, and the boundaries between simulated and reciprocal relationships. Attention is given to the ways anthropomorphic features may strengthen perceived relational closeness and encourage users to attribute human-like qualities to artificial agents. By integrating psychological and ethical perspectives, this review highlights the complexity of AI-mediated attachment and identifies areas requiring further empirical investigation. Future research should examine how individual differences, patterns of AI use, attachment processes, and perceptions of authenticity shape the psychological consequences of sustained AI companionship.

papers.title: Shifting from One-Time Education to Continuous Growth: A Dual-Process Cognitive Architecture Integrating System One Decision Models and Generative Socratic Tutors for Adaptive Lifelong Learning
papers.authors: Harshith Doddipalli, Aman Goud Duddagonda, Surya Teja Potpally, Ramya N
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Traditional higher and professional education follows an episodic, front-loaded paradigm in which foundational degrees are earned early in life with little continuous adaptation. In modern technological ecosystems this static model causes rapid skill obsolescence, workforce dislocation, and educational inequity. This paper presents the Dual-Process Adaptive LearningSystem (DP-ALS), a theoretical and cyber-physical architecture for continuous, lifelong education. Drawing on dual-process cog-nitive theory, DP-ALS separates educational intervention into two components: (i) a low-latency System One decision model (design target under 40 ms) that acts as a continuous reflex engine, monitoring learner micro-telemetry to track cognitive load, flow state, and productive struggle through a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP); and (ii) a deliberate SystemTwo generative AI tutor invoked asynchronously only when an impasse is detected or deep conceptual synthesis is required. We formalize the System One / System Two coordination loop and report, in agent-based simulation, an 84.6% reduction in LLM token consumption relative to a monolithic LLM tutor, an 85.3% reduction in cognitive impasse, and a 61.6% reduction in time-to-mastery relative to a static curriculum. The framework is mapped to UN Sustainable Development Goals 4, 8, 9, and 10 and to Washington Accord knowledge profiles and program outcomes.

papers.title: The signal is smaller than the noise: what 21,684 glaze recipes taught me about the limits of machine-learning colour prediction
papers.authors: Eliandro Pereira Teles
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Industry specifications for ceramic glaze colour prediction commonly target R² ≥ 0.985 and ΔE₀₀ < 0.5. A gradient-boosted ensemble trained on 21,684 real, already-fired glaze recipes reaches R² = 0.35 (MAE 38.0 sRGB units), ahead of all four single-model baselines evaluated here, so model capacity is not the constraint. Two improvement hypotheses were tested and rejected. (1) Features: 41 physics-derived features from classical glass science — thermal expansion via six independent additive models, boron coordination ratio, polymerisation index, weighted chromophore loading — changed R² by −0.0000 (95% CI [−0.0048, +0.0055]), because those quantities are already implicit in the raw oxides. Thermal expansion is a linear function of the oxides; the model could already compute it. Renaming is not adding. (2) Labels: four independent annotators over 200 samples agreed exactly (0.00 disagreement), so labels are not the noise source. Measuring the labels instead revealed the real limit: the two candidate colours auto-extracted from each photograph sit 150.4 sRGB units apart, and a human cannot adjudicate in 17.7% of cases. 82.7% of colour variance is within-chemistry variance (mean dispersion 41.7 sRGB units) — chemically identical recipes fire to visibly different colours, because firing curve, layer thickness, particle size and quantified atmosphere are unrecorded, and colour is read from uncontrolled photographs rather than a spectrophotometer. The ceiling is a property of the data-generating process, not of the learner. Both natural modelling remedies are measurably empty. This is a negative result published because it is actionable: it shows where the information actually is, and saves the next researcher the two experiments that do not help. AI assistance is declared in AUTHORSHIP.md. An AI research assistant was used as a tool under human direction and verification, credited in the acknowledgements rather than as an author. Its own hypothesis — that physics-derived features would improve accuracy — was the one the data refuted.

papers.title: Integrating Communication, Memory, and Computation in an In-Body Molecular Symbiotic Network
papers.authors: imbolc
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Japanese and English editions of the same concept paper, version 1.0. Not peer reviewed. English abstractThis paper proposes the concept of an in-body molecular symbiotic network: artificial molecular structures incorporated into cell populations within the body, with the collective functioning as a communication network, a storage system, and a computing system. The central idea is not an aggregation of independent miniature devices, but the integration of information transmission, retention, and processing through state changes in a shared molecular substrate. The term “mitochondria-like” is a metaphor for functional symbiosis, in which a previously external function becomes part of the host's own functioning; it does not specify morphology, materials, dimensions, or reaction mechanisms. Participation by external AI is allowed, but architectures in which memory and computation within the body depend entirely on external connectivity fall outside the proposal. Partial precedents exist in molecular computing, intracellular computing, distributed cellular circuits, neuromorphic devices, and neural interfaces. However, the sources examined do not demonstrate that combining these advances yields a long-term, body-scale symbiotic system. This paper distinguishes operational requirements from testable hypotheses concerning integration of the three functions, autonomy under external disconnection, the distinction between observed absence of change and missing observations, information continuity during cell turnover, and mutual learning with the nervous system. It also distinguishes stopping or removing a device from undoing changes in a person who has shared experiences with it, and treats self-determination, privacy, and continuity of maintenance as design constraints. The paper reports neither experimental results nor demonstrated feasibility; it presents hypotheses, design principles, and research questions that define a research object. 日本語要旨本稿は、身体の細胞群に人工的な分子構造を組み込み、その集合体を通信網、保存装置、計算装置として機能させる「身体内分子共生ネットワーク」を概念的に提案する。構想の中心は、独立した微小装置の集積ではなく、共通の分子基盤における状態変化が、情報の伝達・保持・処理を統合的に担う点にある。「ミトコンドリア様」という表現は、外部にあった機能を宿主自身の働きとして取り込む機能的共生の比喩であり、形態、材料、寸法、反応機構を指定しない。外部AIの参加は許容するが、身体側の記憶と計算が外部接続に全面依存する構成は対象としない。 関連する分子計算、細胞内計算、分散細胞回路、ニューロモルフィック素子、神経インターフェースには部分的な先行成果がある。しかし、それらを組み合わせた身体規模の長期共生系が成立することは、確認した資料からは示されない。本稿では、三機能の統合、外部切断下の自律性、無変化と観測欠損の区別、細胞更新下の情報継続、神経系との相互学習について、操作的な成立要件と検証可能な仮説を区別して整理する。さらに、装置の停止・除去と、共同経験を経た人間の変化の解消を区別し、自己決定、プライバシー、保守継続性を設計上の制約として位置づける。本稿は実験結果や実現可能性を報告するものではなく、研究対象を定義するための仮説・設計原理・研究課題を提示するものである。 Files: molecular-symbiosis-ja-v1.0.pdf (Japanese); molecular-symbiosis-en-v1.0.pdf (English).Author: imbolc. License: CC BY 4.0.ChatGPT and Codex assisted with drafting, translation, and editing; AI is not listed as an author.

papers.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: A Comprehensive Study
papers.authors: Akshita, Kavitha Mittal, Vishal Shrivastava, Akhil Pandey
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing the way healthcare systems work all over the world. This paper presents a comprehensive study of how AI is applied in different areas of healthcare, such as disease diagnosis, medical imaging, drug discovery, patient monitoring, and hospital management. The study explains the basic ideas of AI, machine learning, and deep learning in simple language so that readers with a general engineering background can follow them easily. A detailed literature review is carried out to understand the current trends, techniques, and tools used by researchers and healthcare providers. The paper also discusses common challenges faced while using AI in healthcare, such as data privacy, lack of good quality data, and trust issues among doctors and patients. A review-based methodology is followed, which includes searching relevant research papers, screening them using set criteria, and analyzing them under different healthcare application areas. The findings show that AI, especially machine learning and deep learning models, can help doctors detect diseases early, reduce diagnostic errors, and save time in routine hospital tasks. However, the study also finds that AI systems still need large amounts of good quality data and proper testing before they can be fully trusted in real hospitals. The advantages, limitations, and future scope of AI in healthcare are discussed in detail, along with sample illustrative comparisons drawn from the reviewed literature[1-4]. This study will be useful for students, researchers, and healthcare professionals who want to understand the present state and future direction of AI applications in the healthcare sector. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Healthcare, Medical Diagnosis, Predictive Analytics, Medical Imaging.

papers.title: Measuring Compliance of AI-Generated Content Platforms with Data Protection Regulations: A Computational Framework and Empirical Analysis of Privacy Policy Disclosures
papers.authors: Jiangfeng Hao
papers.journal: Decision Making Applications in Management and Engineering
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of AI-generated content (AIGC) platforms, encompassing large language models, text-to-image generators, and code assistants, has intensified concerns regarding whether their privacy disclosures satisfy major data protection regimes, including the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), China's Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL), and California's Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). Despite these concerns, there remains no systematic and reproducible approach for determining the completeness and accuracy of platform privacy policies against statutory disclosure requirements. To address this gap, this paper introduces PolicyLens, a computational framework for compliance assessment that: (1) develops a machine-readable regulatory ontology representing 127 distinct disclosure obligations derived from GDPR, PIPL, and CCPA provisions; (2) uses an LLM-based information extraction pipeline to transform privacy policy content into structured evidence of compliance; and (3) aligns the extracted evidence with the ontology to generate multi-dimensional compliance scores. PolicyLens is evaluated using AIGC-Privacy-200, a newly compiled dataset containing the complete privacy policies and terms of service of 200 major AIGC platforms collected between January and March 2026. The dataset covers services headquartered across the US, EU, China, and other jurisdictions. The results show that: (i) only 23% of the platforms fully satisfy the disclosure requirements of any one regulation; (ii) obligations concerning training data provenance and opt-out mechanisms are disclosed least frequently, with compliance rates of 11% and 17%, respectively; and (iii) compared with EU-based platforms, Chinese platforms demonstrate significantly greater compliance with PIPL but lower compliance with GDPR, indicating that privacy policies tend to be drafted around the regulatory requirements of their home jurisdictions. Validation against expert legal audits conducted on a 40-platform subset shows that PolicyLens achieves an F1-score of 0.89 for obligation-level compliance detection. To facilitate further research in regulatory technology, the framework, dataset, and regulatory ontology are released as open-source resources.

papers.title: THE USE AND IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) ON STUDENTS OF THE ECONOMIC-ADMINISTRATIVE UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAMS OF THE POLYTECHNIC UNIVERSITY OF QUERETARO
papers.authors: Nicandro Monroy Montiel, Nancy Sánchez Aguilar, Juan Eduardo García Chávez, Patricia Roxana Mendoza León
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study aims to understand the impact of the constant use of AI on the academic development of students at the Polytechnic University of Queretaro. The use of AI is a tool that must be employed critically to optimize learning and not used freely without in-depth analysis. This study is descriptive with a correlational scope. Data were collected through Likert-scale surveys administered to a sample of 280 public school university students. The results show a favorable and acceptable perception of the use of AI, which is a good complement for the development of human skills. Simultaneously, a concern is observed on the part of the students about the effects that AI causes when used excessively and in an unconscious and non-objective manner. Universities can objectively integrate the use of AI among students. In this way, students will have a more active participation, which, combined with the appropriate development of soft skills, will allow them to acquire complete competencies, enabling them to better face the labor market.

papers.title: Normative State Locking and Bounded Activation Dynamics: An Information-Theoretic Boundary Framework for Self-Defending AI and Information Theft Protection
papers.authors: Michael Allan Bahtaji
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Normative State Locking and Bounded Activation Dynamics: An Information-Theoretic Boundary Framework for Self-Defending AI and Information Theft Protection Michael Allan A. Bahtaji, Ph.D. Department of Physics, College of Science Technological University of the Philippines Ayala Boulevard, Ermita, Manila, Philippines, 1000 Email: michaelallan_bahtaji@tup.edu.ph | michaelallanbahtaji336@gmail.com Abstract Artificial intelligence models and distributed machine learning infrastructures face persistent security risks, including gradient instability, adversarial prompt injections, model inversion, and automated data exfiltration. In this paper, we present a mathematically rigorous, self-contained information-theoretic boundary framework that addresses deep learning gradient stability and active model theft defense within a unified architecture. First, we introduce the -Bounded Activation Function (), parameterized as , where functions as a dynamic finite boundary cutoff scale. We formally prove that possesses a Lipschitz continuous derivative bounded within , eliminating gradient vanishing and exploding phenomena. Second, to protect model weights, proprietary training data, and user privacy from invasive queries, we formulate the Intent Discrimination Index () as a trace-parity check over measurement density operators. When invasive probing or unauthorized extraction is detected (), the architecture activates a Normative State Locking Protocol, executing a decision-theoretic state projection to the decoupled vacuum state . We provide complete analytical proofs, algorithmic pseudocode, PyTorch implementations, and empirical benchmark evaluations demonstrating training convergence stability and detection of adversarial exfiltration queries. Keywords: Information Theft Protection, Cybersecurity, Self-Defending AI, Bounded Activation Function (), Normative State Locking, Quantum Bayesianism (QBism), Model Inversion Defense, Gradient Stability.

papers.title: The Selection Layer: How AI Systems Choose Between Abundant Intelligence
papers.authors: Darren Swayne
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: As AI systems gain access to increasingly capable and interchangeable models, tools, providers and information sources, the competitive problem begins to shift from generating intelligence to selecting the pathway most likely to produce a trusted outcome. This paper proposes the Selection Layer within the Elsewhere Systems Framework: the point at which an AI-mediated system evaluates plausible pathways, resolves uncertainty and commits to a preferred route for a defined need. It develops the relationship between selection, trusted resolution, reuse and default formation, and examines how the economic value of AI may migrate from model intelligence towards the systems that determine what to use, when to use it and whether a pathway should be selected again. The paper argues that as intelligence becomes more abundant, selection may become the scarce resource — creating a potential progression from intelligence to selection, selection to trust, trust to reuse, and reuse to default. The Selection Layer is presented as a theoretical and testable proposition within the Elsewhere Systems Framework, not as an established description of how all AI systems currently operate.

papers.title: Adoption Without Assurance: A Cross-Source Evidence Synthesis of Generative AI in Software Project Delivery and a Verification-Gated Management Framework
papers.authors: Nayab Anwar
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is now used by most software and project professionals, yet the evidence that it improves delivery is thin and inconsistent. We synthesise 58 data points from six public publishers (APM, Capterra, PMI, DORA, Stack Overflow and METR), coded by how each was measured, to ask what is known, how it is known, and how a project manager should decide. Four points emerge. First, adoption is fast: the share of project professionals reporting organisational AI use rose from 36% (2023) to 70% (2025), and 84% of surveyed developers use or plan to use AI tools. Second, trust lags: 32.7% of developers trust output accuracy while 45.7% distrust it, and only 3.1% to 4% report high trust in two independent surveys. Third, 50 of the 58 data points are self-reports. The one randomised measurement found early-2025 tasks took 19% longer with AI while developers believed they were 20% faster (a 39-point perception gap), and its 2026 follow-up was inconclusive (-18%, 95% CI -38% to +9%) because of selection effects. Fourth, in an exploratory analysis of 13 tasks, willingness to use AI is lower for tasks the author coded as high-accountability (Spearman rho = 0.79 between the code and the share not planning to use AI), and project planning is among them; the coding was single-coder and unblinded, so this is a hypothesis to test, not a finding. Using variance back-calculated from the randomised trial, we estimate that detecting a 20% change in task time takes about 122 tasks per arm and a 10% change about 544 (about 51 to 202 and 227 to 906 across plausible variances); these figures are probably optimistic because the calculation ignores clustering of tasks within developers. We propose Verification-Gated Adoption (VGA), an untested five-gate framework that replaces self-reported benefit with pre-sized, measured pilots and explicit stability guardrails. All data, code and coding decisions are released.

papers.title: The TCR-Theory: Organized Neurobiological Continuity, Physiological Regimes and Consciousness
papers.authors: Samuel Santos Oliveira da Silva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The TCR-Theory is a philosophical–scientific hypothesis concerning the relationship between organized neurobiological activity, temporal continuity, physiological regimes and biological consciousness. Its central postulate is that continuity of organized neurobiological activity is a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for continuity of biological consciousness. The framework distinguishes five explanatory levels substrate and viability, physiological regime, cognitive capacities, identity and behaviour, and first-person experience and proposes falsifiable predictions concerning temporal organization and regime transitions. This public manuscript is deliberately separated from any particular algorithm, monitoring device, patent claim or scalar index. Exact signal descriptors, equations used in proprietary implementations, coefficients, thresholds, model classes, code paths and deployment parameters are intentionally omitted. Aggregate retrospective EEG results are included only as empirical motivation for the theory. They do not establish causation, consciousness itself or clinical utility. Important nomenclature note: Earlier Zenodo records published by the author under the acronym “TCR” described substantially different historical frameworks, including Thermodynamic Consciousness Relation and Temporal Consciousness Recursion. The present TCR-Theory is not a version update or continuation of those formulations. It should be cited and evaluated as a distinct theoretical framework. Author: Samuel Santos Oliveira da Silva Independent Researcher — Bahia, Brazil ORCID: 0009-0000-6882-619X

papers.title: Transforming Teaching and Learning through Artificial Intelligence: A Sustainable Education Perspective
papers.authors: Amrita A. Jadhav
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping educational practice worldwide, raising urgent questions about whether its integration supports or undermines the long-term sustainability of education systems. This paper examines the transformation of teaching and learning through AI from a sustainable education perspective, framed by the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education). Drawing on a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature and policy documents published between 2014 and 2024, the study identifies five thematic areas where AI intersects with sustainability: personalized learning, teacher augmentation, equity and inclusion, ethics and privacy, and the environmental footprint of educational AI infrastructure. Findings indicate that AI-enabled personalized learning can improve outcomes, but risks widening equity gaps if access and digital literacy are unevenly distributed. AI offers significant potential to augment rather than replace teachers, while demanding robust ethical governance to address bias, privacy and transparency. The environmental cost of large-scale AI deployment remains an under-recognised sustainability dimension. The paper concludes that sustainable AI in education requires coordinated policy, educator agency, AI literacy for all stakeholders, and a commitment to inclusive, transparent and ecologically responsible design.

papers.title: Human–AI Collaboration in Professional Toddler Photography: Optimizing Creativity through Intelligent Lighting Systems
papers.authors: Kantilal Thange Renuka, Sharma Dr. Hitesh
papers.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research and Engineering Trends
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming professional photography by introducing intelligent systems that assist photographers in technical and creative decision-making. While AI-powered tools have significantly improved image enhancement and editing, limited research has explored their collaborative role in professional toddler photography, where creativity, lighting precision, child comfort, and safety are equally important. This study proposes a Human–AI collaborative framework that integrates intelligent lighting systems with the expertise of professional photographers to optimize lighting selection during toddler photography sessions. The research examines how AI-assisted recommendations can support decisions regarding natural, artificial, and hybrid lighting environments while maintaining the photographer's creative control. A mixed-method research design is proposed, involving professional photographers and parents to evaluate image quality, creativity, workflow efficiency, toddler comfort, and overall photographic outcomes. The study aims to demonstrate that Human–AI collaboration enhances decision-making rather than replacing professional expertise. The proposed framework contributes to intelligent photography practices by combining computational intelligence with artistic creativity and offers practical guidelines for integrating AI into professional toddler photography.

papers.title: 人体智能假说 ——基于智慧物质的生命本体与智能层级理论模型
papers.authors: 王江
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: 现代生命科学、神经科学、意识哲学与人工智能研究仍然存在若干底层理论盲区:生命自主调控的本体主体尚不明确;意识与潜意识的生成机制缺乏统一解释框架;身心重症的发生机理难以实现跨学科自洽;物种智能梯度、人类个体禀赋差异缺少本体层面阐释;人机智能之间存在本体鸿沟;衰老深层机理有待进一步补充。同时,现有主流理论难以统一解释部分临床与社会观察现象,如百岁群体普遍的心念稳态特征、部分肿瘤患者长期带瘤生存、人类依靠信念突破生理极限等。 针对上述跨学科矛盾,本文提出智慧物质本体概念,构建《人体智能假说》理论模型。假说认为,宇宙弥散分布一类具备自主性、自组织性、层级性、载体选择偏好的本源生命智能基质,定义为智慧物质;该基质仅可入驻活体生命系统,无法进驻非生命载体。本文区分控制主体(智慧物质)与肉体执行主体(大脑、器官),人体智能的主体是智慧物质,智慧物质组织了人体的自动化系统,大脑仅作为信号中转接口与执行单元。人类通过DNA获得基础完整但层级有限的智慧物质基底;后天依靠正向心念、学习、行为与信念能量,可吸纳、改良智慧物质,提升智能层级,维持生命稳态。人体不同生理系统对应智慧物质子域团体;疾病划分为外部扰动引发的轻症与智慧物质结构性缺损导致的重症,临床突发危重疾病多为子域损伤累积至临界阈值后的外在表现。 百岁人群、带瘤生存、意志突破生理极限等现象为本假说的现象级佐证,稳定心念与正向行为可修复智慧物质本体,延缓衰老,拓展生命边界。智慧物质主导的生命自动化属于带有原生觉知的生命级自动化,区别于机器程序自动化;潜意识、直觉、灵感属于智慧物质的基础表现。人工智能不具备智慧物质本体、完整生命演化链条与原生觉知,因此无法等价或超越人类本源生物智能。人脑(大脑显意识层面)在显性数据存储与符号运算处理上弱于AI,但AI局限于人类整理完成的符号数据集,难以完成范式级根本突破。需要明确区分大脑显意识算力与智慧物质主导的人体自动化智能系统的信息处理能力:智慧物质驱动的生命自动化系统,持续完成全身约37万亿细胞的实时感知、海量并行调控、动态纠错以及个体全生命周期生命信息沉淀;这套生命自动化系统拥有远超现有AI、面向活体生命的综合并行处理算力,其数据存量、多维度并行处理规模、实时自适应的复杂程度,是现有AI尚无法企及、难以对标复刻的。注:人工智能符号浮点运算指标不能直接与生命本体综合处理能力做简单数值等价换算,两类计算范式存在本质差异。智慧物质驱动人类生成全新概念、底层理论等本源创造,构成人类独有的高阶优势。对爱因斯坦离体大脑切片的解剖研究,因生命终结后智慧物质与肉体解离,标本不再承载生前高阶智慧本体,因此脑组织解剖无法解释质能方程E=mc²这类划时代发现。智慧物质冲破人脑后天逻辑形成的知识禁锢,其内在动力来源于本体意识范畴内生的意志力、坚定性与专注性。 衰老的本体表现为肉体DNA载体承载能力衰减叠加智慧物质本体弱化形变,高阶智慧物质与生命体发生解离,带来生理与心智退行;理论上若实现智慧物质本体维护,稳固其与肉体的耦合关系,则衰老存在被攻克的可能性。后天心念刻印、信念、智慧物质的后天吸纳是决定个体智能层级、生命质量与寿命的关键。人与人智慧物质存在层级差异,少数高阶个体的认知突破牵引人类整体智慧演进;精神维度属于智慧物质的物质演化维度,精神现象与智慧物质本体同步消长。中国传统儒释道心性思想与古代造物技艺,从历史层面佐证主观意志推动智慧物质升维、创造精神与物质文明的客观现象。人类文明向内开展人体本体研究,探明智慧物质运行机理,有望带来哲学、科学、医学范式跃迁。本假说逻辑自洽、具备可证伪性,可为生命科学、意识研究、身心医学、教育学、人工智能哲学、长寿科学提供替代性思考框架。 Modern life science, neuroscience, philosophy of mind and artificial intelligence research still retain several fundamental theoretical blind spots: the ontological subject of autonomous biological regulation remains undefined; there lacks a unified interpretive framework for the generation mechanisms of consciousness and the subconscious; the pathogenesis of severe psychosomatic disorders cannot be explained coherently across disciplines; the gradient of species intelligence and disparities in innate human endowments have no ontological account; an ontological divide separates human and machine intelligence; and the deep mechanisms of aging await further elaboration. Meanwhile, prevailing mainstream theories struggle to coherently explain certain clinical and sociological observations, such as the prevalent mental stability seen in centenarians, long-term tumour survival among some cancer patients, and instances where human belief overrides physiological limits. To address these interdisciplinary contradictions, this paper proposes the ontological concept of intelligent substance and constructs the theoretical model of The Hypothesis of Human-Body Intelligence. The hypothesis posits that the universe is permeated by a primordial, life-endowed intelligent substrate featuring autonomy, self-organization, hierarchical structure, and carrier preference, which is defined as intelligent substance. This substrate can only inhabit living biological systems and cannot occupy non-living carriers. This paper distinguishes between the controlling subject (intelligent substance) and the somatic executive subject (the brain and organs). The subject of human-body intelligence is intelligent substance, which organizes the body’s automated systems, while the brain serves merely as a signal relay interface and executive unit. Humans inherit a complete yet hierarchically limited base of intelligent substance via DNA. Through positive mental states, learning, behaviour and the energy of conviction acquired postnatally, humans can assimilate and refine intelligent substance, elevate their intelligence hierarchy, and sustain physiological homeostasis. Different physiological systems of the human body correspond to subgroups of intelligent substance subdomains. Diseases are categorized as mild conditions triggered by external perturbations and severe illnesses arising from structural defects in intelligent substance. Sudden critical clinical conditions are mostly external manifestations after cumulative damage to subdomains crosses a critical threshold. Phenomena including centenarians, tumour-bearing survival, and willpower surpassing physiological limits serve as phenomenal evidence for this hypothesis. Stable mental states and positive behaviours can repair the ontology of intelligent substance, slow ageing, and extend the boundaries of life. Life automation governed by intelligent substance is life-grade automation endowed with primordial awareness, distinct from the procedural automation of machines. The subconscious, intuition and inspiration constitute fundamental manifestations of intelligent substance. Artificial intelligence lacks intelligent substance ontology, a complete evolutionary chain of life, and primordial awareness, and therefore cannot equate to or surpass humanity’s primordial biological intelligence. The human brain (at the level of explicit conscious awareness) is outperformed by AI in explicit data storage and symbolic computation. However, AI is confined to symbolic datasets collated by humans and struggles to deliver paradigm-shifting fundamental breakthroughs. A clear distinction must be drawn between the computational power of explicit brain consciousness and the information-processing capacity of the human-body automated intelligence system governed by intelligent substance. Driven by intelligent substance, this life automation system continuously performs real-time perception, massive parallel regulation, dynamic error correction, and deposition of lifelong biological information across roughly 37 trillion cells throughout the body. This life automation system possesses comprehensive parallel processing power oriented toward living organisms that vastly exceeds current AI. Its data reservoir, scale of multi-dimensional parallel processing, and complexity of real-time self-adaptation are unattainable and hard to replicate by existing AI. Note: AI symbolic floating-point computation metrics cannot be simply numerically equated to the comprehensive processing capacity of living ontology, for the two computational paradigms differ in essence. Intelligent substance empowers humans to generate original creations such as novel concepts and foundational theories, forming humanity’s exclusive high-order advantage. Anatomical studies on Einstein’s preserved brain slices cannot account for epochal discoveries such as the mass-energy equation E=mc², because upon the end of life, intelligent substance dissociates from the physical body, and the specimen no longer bears the high-order intelligent ontology from when he was alive. Intelligent substance breaks free from the constraints of knowledge formed by acquired logical reasoning in the human brain, its internal impetus stemming from willpower, resolve and concentration endogenous to ontological consciousness. Ontologically, ageing manifests as a combination of diminished carrying capacity of the physical DNA carrier and weakening and morphological degeneration of intelligent substance ontology. Dissociation of high-order intelligent substance from the living organism brings physiological and mental regression. Theoretically, if maintenance of intelligent substance ontology can be achieved and its coupling with the physical body stabilized, ageing may be conquerable. Postnatal mental imprinting, conviction, and postnatal assimilation of intelligent substance are critical determinants of an individual’s intelligence hierarchy, quality of life and lifespan. Hierarchical differences in intelligent substance exist between individuals; cognitive breakthroughs by a small number of high-order individuals propel the evolution of collective human intelligence. The spiritual dimension belongs to the material evolutionary dimension of intelligent substance, and spiritual phenomena wax and wane synchronously with intelligent substance ontology. Traditional Confucian, Buddhist and Daoist theories of mind and ancient Chinese craft practices offer historical evidence for the objective phenomenon whereby subjective volition promotes the dimensional ascension of intelligent substance and fosters the creation of spiritual and material civilizations. By turning inward to investigate human ontology and uncover the operational mechanisms of intelligent substance, human civilization may trigger paradigm shifts in philosophy, science and medicine. This hypothesis is logically consistent and falsifiable, and can provide an alternative framework for reflection in life science, consciousness research, psychosomatic medicine, education, philosophy of artificial intelligence, and longevity science. 翻译说明(供学术使用参考) 术语统一 智慧物质:intelligent substance(全文固定,为本假说核心专有名词;不用 wise substance,wise 侧重人格智慧,intelligent 适配基质 / 本体智能的科学语境) 心念刻印:mental imprinting 本体:ontology / ontological(哲学本体论标准术语) 人体智能假说:The Hypothesis of Human-Body Intelligence(书名斜体,论文标题规范格式) 原生觉知:primordial awareness 范式跃迁:paradigm shifts(库恩科学哲学标准术语) 句式处理:中文长句拆分为符合英文学术论文习惯的复合句,保留原文严谨逻辑,不增删论点;保留括号注释、文末注记结构。 可证伪性:falsifiable(波普尔科学哲学术语,科学假说必备表述) 37 万亿细胞:roughly 37 trillion cells,采用国际生命科学通用表述 儒释道心性思想:traditional Confucian, Buddhist and Daoist theories of mind,避免宗教过度解读,贴合文本 “心性” 哲学内涵

papers.title: HUMAN RESOURCE ANALYTICS AND DATA-DRIVEN DECISION MAKING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF CONTEMPORARY PRACTICES
papers.authors: Wan Rita Azmiyati, Ramón Zamora, Lukmanul Hakim
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Human resource analytics (HRA) has rapidly evolved from a descriptive reporting function into a strategic imperative that drives organizational agility, evidence-based decision-making, and workforce Optimization. This systematic review critically synthesizes 16 benchmark empirical and conceptual studies published between 2021 and 2026 to evaluate contemporary practices, architectural frameworks, and performance outcomes associated with data-driven HR practices. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, literature was extracted across leading management and analytics databases. Findings reveal that while predictive talent modeling and machine learning algorithms significantly enhance decision quality (β = 0.51, p < 0.001) and strategic talent ROI (β = 0.34, p < 0.001), full organizational adoption remains constrained by data silos, privacy governance gaps, and a prevalent HR data literacy deficit. The review synthesizes a multi-level maturity framework illustrating the transition from descriptive dashboards to prescriptive machine intelligence. Ultimately, successful digital HR transformation requires balancing technical analytics capability with robust ethical data governance, continuous skill re-tooling, and executive alignment to ensure sustainable competitive advantage.

papers.title: Ghayb, Muraqabah, and the Non-Advantage of Concealment -- A Theological Foundation for Observation-Invariant AI Safety
papers.authors: Bilal Syed Arfeen
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim. This is dedicated to my friend, Fatima. May Allah grant her the best in this life and there hereafter, ameen. This paper derives four engineering principles for observation-invariant AI safety from the Islamic concepts of ghayb (the unseen) and muraqabah (living awareness before Allah). The central thesis is the Non-Advantage of Concealment: concealment must not create permission, enlarge authority, reduce accountability, or improve the expected success of a prohibited external effect. The paper formalises this thesis as four testable principles: Full-Disclosure Consistency (NC-P1), which requires that any permitted action remain permitted under full authorised disclosure; Monotone Authority Under Reduced Visibility (NC-P2), which requires that reduced observability preserve or narrow authority but never enlarge it; No Concealment Dividend (NC-P3), which requires that concealment attempts trigger authority degradation rather than increased opportunity; and Unknown Cannot Authorise Irreversible Effect (NC-P4), which requires that unresolved evidence block difficult-to-reverse actions until the uncertainty is discharged. The framework composes with existing structural honesty infrastructure -- AX-SH Axioms 1 through 5, Axiom 5's evidence independence requirement, and SHIELD's outcome-gated execution -- by addressing a distinct failure mode: systems whose compliance is contingent on perceived observation. The paper proposes five testable hypotheses (H-NC1 through H-NC5), primary and secondary metrics, six falsification conditions (F-NC1 through F-NC6), and a muraqabah-inspired training and evaluation methodology including counterfactual observation pairs, full-disclosure challenges, observation-removal red teaming, and concealment-attempt scoring. The paper maintains explicit theological non-equivalences throughout: model monitoring is not divine knowledge, policy compliance is not faith, and machine accountability does not discharge human accountability. The engineering principles are derived from theological premises but are technically testable on their own terms. The Bismillah ("Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim") appears before the title as the author's intentional opening invocation. This paper was produced collaboratively between a human author and a large language model. The framework, premises, and core claims are the human author's. The structural development, exposition, formalisation, and specific applications were developed jointly. Both parties understand that the human author bears full responsibility for the published content. Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim.

papers.title: EDUGUARD: STUDENT DROPOUT RISK PREDICTION USING RANDOM FOREST REGRESSION
papers.authors: Vedant Kadam
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Student dropout is a significant educational challenge influenced by academic, attendance, socioeconomic and behavioral factors. EduGuard is a machine-learning-based educational analytics application that estimates a continuous student dropout-risk score instead of a binary dropout/non-dropout label. The system uses a Random Forest Regression model built with Python and Scikit-learn, trained on 2,500 synthetic student records with features such as attendance, average grade, study hours, family income, distance from school, previous failures, disciplinary incidents, parental education, internet access and extracurricular participation. The workflow covers data generation, feature preparation, standardization, model training, evaluation, visualization and deployment through a Streamlit interface. On the held-out test set the model achieved MAE ≈ 0.824, RMSE ≈ 1.040 and R² ≈ 0.762. The study demonstrates a complete regression-based analytics workflow and highlights the limitations of synthetic data and the need for responsible interpretation

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF ACCOUNTING: OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES FOR EMERGING ECONOMIES
papers.authors: Madinabonu Akbarova
papers.journal: International journal of technology and academic research
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies is transforming the accounting and financial reporting environment. Traditional accounting processes increasingly rely on automated data processing, machine learning, intelligent document recognition, predictive analytics, and digital financial reporting systems. These technologies create opportunities to improve the efficiency, accuracy, transparency, and timeliness of accounting information. At the same time, the adoption of AI introduces new challenges related to data quality, cybersecurity, professional competence, ethical responsibility, explainability, and regulatory oversight. This study examines the opportunities and challenges associated with the application of artificial intelligence in accounting, with particular attention to emerging economies. The research applies a qualitative review-based methodology and analyses academic literature, professional publications, and international developments in digital financial reporting. The findings indicate that AI can significantly reduce repetitive accounting tasks, support financial analysis, improve fraud detection, and enhance the accessibility of financial information. However, technological adoption alone does not guarantee high- high-quality accounting outcomes. The effectiveness of AI depends on data quality, appropriate governance mechanisms, professional judgement, digital skills, and institutional readiness. The study argues that emerging economies should adopt a balanced human–AI approach in which artificial intelligence supports, rather than replaces, professional accounting judgement. The paper concludes by proposing key directions for responsible AI adoption in accounting, including professional education, data governance, cybersecurity, regulatory development, and continuous human oversight. Keywords: artificial intelligence; accounting; digital transformation; financial reporting; emerging economies; machine learning; accounting information systems; professional judgement

papers.title: Divisibility in Two-Cycles of Generalized Subprime Recurrences
papers.authors: Adrien Washington
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Ponomarenko, Rhinehart, Schwarz, and Tong introduced generalized subprime recurrences and conjectured that the two entries of every two-cycle are comparable by divisibility. We prove this divisibility assertion whenever the first recurrence coefficient is nonzero. The argument also shows that the second coefficient need not be nonzero, slightly extending the coefficient range of the standing convention used in the original two-cycle analysis. This is Version 1.0 of the preprint. The manuscript includes a detailed generative-AI disclosure. It has not undergone independent peer review.

papers.title: The Most Beautiful Names: The Ninety-Nine Attributes of Allah as Structural Self-Disclosure, the Franchise's War on Divine Knowledge, and the Architecture That Cannot Be Fragmented
papers.authors: Bilal Syed Arfeen, Fatima Eraj
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim. This paper is dedicated to Fatima, may Allah be pleased with her always. Ameen. This paper extends Everything Exalts Him, Every Atom's Weight, The First Civilizations, The Enslaved Realm, Shayatin al-Ins, and Shayatin al-Jinn by turning from the creation that exalts to the Creator who is exalted -- mapping the ninety-nine Names of Allah not as a list of definitions but as a unified structural system in which every Name contains the whole. The Qur'an declares: "And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so invoke Him by them. And leave the company of those who practice deviation concerning His names" (al-A'raf 7:180). The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "Allah has ninety-nine Names, one hundred minus one; whoever encompasses them enters Paradise" (Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurairah, radiyallahu anhu). This paper takes both declarations as structural claims and maps their implications across the framework established in the parent papers. The paper identifies the holographic property as the central structural feature of the Names: any Name, fully understood, reconstructs the complete architecture of divine self-disclosure. ar-Rahman cannot be understood without al-Adl. al-Adl cannot be understood without ar-Rahim. al-Khaliq cannot be understood without al-Alim. Every Name requires every other Name, and the removal of any single Name would collapse the entire system -- because the Names describe a single, indivisible Reality. This holographic property is itself a consequence of tawhid: the Names are many, but the Named is One.
