papers.title: Witnessed Mastery: A Research Journal of Acts as a Learning Paradigm in the Age of AI Conceptual model, audit model and testing programme
papers.authors: Anatoliy Kremenchutskiy
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative AI has made learning products — essays, solutions, code — cheap, and has thereby stripped them of their role as evidence of mastery. The process data proposed in their place record behaviour rather than epistemic history, and regulators treat them as partial evidence at best. What is missing is a unit of record and a procedure that tie the learner’s path to independent verification. We propose witnessed mastery: the learner keeps an append-only journal of acts — dated claims with a declared epistemic status, supports and provenance (own, from a source, from AI). An act is never edited; its current status is derived from later acts. The journal is not graded: a deterministic validator checks the discipline of the record along the seven axes of a multi-axis witness architecture — five of disclosure and two of correspondence with the world — AI only proposes semantic signals for human confirmation, and attestation is a live oral defence of a stratified random sample of acts. The recording tool is itself subject to the regime axis: its hash is part of every act, and nothing can be recorded until the tool version has been declared; a back-dated entry is visible as the gap between the recording time and the declared event time. The audit model accounts for sampling without replacement, sensitivity and false failures, and a two-stage rule separates the defence grade from an integrity flag. The work is conceptual and has not been tested with learners; the formal model, the double dissociation of the seven axes on synthetic journals and the audit model have been verified computationally. Five testable hypotheses and a pilot design are proposed.

papers.title: From Asset to Liability: Population Policy, Technological Displacement, and the Governance of Surplus Humans in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Jace (Jeong Hyeon) Kim
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract For much of recorded history, human populations have functioned as productive infrastructure for political authority, military organization, and economic production. States and other governing institutions developed demographic, fiscal, and ideological arrangements around the assumption that population growth increased productive capacity, expanded tax bases, supplied military personnel, and reproduced the labor force. This paper examines the structural contradiction that emerges when artificial intelligence and automated systems increasingly substitute for human labor across a growing range of productive activities. Drawing on political economy, historical sociology, evolutionary biology, psychology, and critical theory, the paper traces the historical construction of population as an economic and political asset across agrarian, industrial, and welfare-state formations. It then examines the interaction between biological and psychological reproductive incentives, institutional population policy, and natalist ideology, arguing that reproductive behavior under conditions of deprivation cannot be adequately explained either as individual irrationality or as simple ideological manipulation. The analysis instead treats fertility as the outcome of interacting biological predispositions, constrained choice, social institutions, psychological meaning, and economic incentives. The paper then examines the implications of technological displacement for institutions whose fiscal and political arrangements remain dependent on human labor. Four governance scenarios are considered: ideological continuity and managed contradiction; selective population management and stratified adaptation; a post-labor social contract; and authoritarian population management. The paper further examines how productivist ideology may be adapted to an AI transition by shifting responsibility for structural displacement toward individual adaptation, reskilling, and continuous employability. The central argument is not that human beings become liabilities in any moral or philosophical sense. Rather, institutions constructed around the productive value of human labor may increasingly confront a population whose economic role no longer corresponds to the assumptions embedded in those institutions. The AI transition therefore represents not only a technological or economic transformation, but a potential reconfiguration of the historical relationship between population, production, and governance. Keywords: artificial intelligence; labor displacement; population policy; biopolitics; demographic governance; surplus population; natalism; social contract; political economy; technological unemployment Disclaimer This paper does not argue that population growth, reproduction, or technological displacement has a predetermined social outcome. It does not treat reproductive behavior as merely an instrument of state policy, nor does it assume that artificial intelligence will inevitably produce mass unemployment. The analysis instead examines a structural possibility: that advances in AI may weaken the historical relationship between population size, labor demand, and fiscal capacity, thereby creating tensions for institutions and ideologies built around that relationship. References to “surplus population,” “population as liability,” and “Gaslighting 2.0” are analytical concepts used to examine potential governance dynamics, not claims about the intrinsic value of individuals or established empirical conditions. Author Note This paper began with a simple historical observation: population has often been treated as a form of national productive capacity. For centuries, larger populations could mean more workers, more taxpayers, more soldiers, more consumers, and greater capacity for economic expansion. Within that historical context, policies encouraging marriage, fertility, family formation, and population growth were often presented not merely as private matters but as matters of collective interest. The present paper asks what happens when the technological foundations of that assumption begin to change. Artificial intelligence does not make human beings economically worthless, nor does this paper argue that population growth is inherently undesirable. Its narrower claim is that a governance system built around the assumption that population is economically necessary may encounter a structural contradiction when increasingly capable technologies reduce the amount of human labor required to produce economic output. This distinction is important because several criticisms of the argument are predictable. One criticism is that the paper treats reproduction as if it were merely an instrument of state power. It does not. Reproduction can simultaneously be an expression of love, attachment, identity, hope, cultural continuity, and personal meaning. The historical analysis presented here specifically recognizes that reproductive behavior cannot be reduced to ideological manipulation. A second criticism is that technological displacement may create new occupations rather than simply eliminate existing ones. This is a legitimate empirical question. The paper therefore does not assume universal unemployment. Its concern is the possibility that the rate and breadth of technological substitution may eventually weaken the historical relationship between population size and aggregate labor demand. A third criticism is that the argument risks treating human beings as economic units. This would invert the intended argument. The phrase “from asset to liability” describes a potential transformation in the way institutions may classify and govern populations. It does not describe the intrinsic value of human beings. The distinction is fundamental. A person does not become less valuable because an economic system requires less human labor. The deeper concern is precisely the opposite. If institutions historically encouraged reproduction partly because population was considered a source of national strength, then contemporary demographic policy deserves renewed scrutiny when the relationship between population and labor demand changes. Population is not merely a number on a fiscal balance sheet. And reproduction is not simply a mechanism for producing taxpayers. Having a child is a choice. Being born is not. That asymmetry deserves greater attention in population policy. A person can choose whether to become a parent, but the person who is born has no opportunity to choose the economic, psychological, social, or institutional conditions into which they are born. Some children enter environments in which they receive substantial material support, emotional security, education, and opportunities for development. Others enter environments in which those conditions are severely constrained. This does not mean that parents should be judged solely by the conditions surrounding them. Nor does it mean that poverty, disadvantage, or family difficulty can be attributed to individual parents alone. The point is more fundamental: the interests of the future person cannot be fully represented at the moment reproductive decisions are made. This creates an ethical asymmetry that population policy should not ignore. A reproductive ideology may be effective in the short term when it frames having children as patriotic, responsible, economically necessary, or socially virtuous. But effectiveness at the moment of reproduction does not establish that the resulting social arrangement will be beneficial for the people who are subsequently born into it. The same problem becomes more visible over time. During childhood, the evaluative relationship is often understood primarily as one in which parents evaluate and guide the child. Adulthood can reverse that direction of evaluation. The child who becomes an autonomous adult can eventually evaluate the institutions, circumstances, and decisions that shaped their life, including the circumstances under which they were brought into existence. That reversal matters because demographic policy is frequently evaluated from the perspective of the state, the economy, or the existing generation. A more complete analysis must also consider the perspective of the person who does not yet exist at the moment the policy is designed but who will eventually live with its consequences. This is why population policy should be distinguished from population maximization. A society may have legitimate reasons to address demographic decline, aging, or fiscal sustainability. But treating population itself as an unconditional measure of national strength risks obscuring a more important question: What kind of society is being created for the people whose births are being encouraged? The objective should not be reproduction for its own sake. Nor should technological progress be evaluated solely by the amount of labor it eliminates. The relevant standard is ultimately human: Can institutions create conditions in which the people they encourage to be born can meaningfully participate, develop, contribute, and live with dignity, even when the economy no longer requires their labor in the same way? That question lies beyond demographic statistics. It is a question about the social contract itself.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as an Equalizer or Divider in India: Digital Public Infrastructure, Human Capital, and Inclusive Technology Adoption
papers.authors: Myra Agarwal, Trasha Gupta
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: India offers a distinctive setting for examining whether artificial intelligence (AI) can broaden economic opportunity or reinforce pre-existing inequality. The country combines population-scale digital public infrastructure, a rapidly expanding technology and startup ecosystem, large regional and socio-economic disparities, and a workforce in which informal employment remains dominant. This article develops a secondary empirical synthesis of evidence on inequality, digital infrastructure, AI adoption, financial inclusion, labor-market transition, entrepreneurship, and human-capital readiness. It integrates national and international datasets and policy reports with sectoral evidence from finance, public-language infrastructure, education and skills, and technology services. The analysis distinguishes between equalizing mechanisms—lower transaction costs, alternative credit assessment, multilingual access, scalable learning, and distributed entrepreneurship—and dividing mechanisms, including capital-biased productivity gains, uneven compute access, algorithmic exclusion, regional concentration, and skill-premium effects. The central finding is that AI is not intrinsically redistributive. Its distributional effect depends on an institutional complementarity among universal digital access, AI-relevant human capital, inclusive entrepreneurship, responsible governance, and mechanisms that allow workers and small firms to capture productivity gains. The paper proposes an Inclusive AI Capability framework and argues that education systems are a critical transmission mechanism between technological adoption and equitable participation. India’s experience therefore provides a useful model for emerging economies: AI can support inclusive growth, but only when technology policy is integrated with education, skills, public digital infrastructure, and social protection rather than treated as a stand-alone innovation agenda.

papers.title: Detecção de anomalias em tempo real para identificação de fraudes com streaming data e online learning: uma revisão da literatura
papers.authors: Alcida Duvane
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Resumo A crescente digitalização dos serviços financeiros e das plataformas electrónicas tem intensificado os desafios associados à detecção de fraudes, exigindo sistemas capazes de analisar grandes volumes de dados em tempo real. Os métodos tradicionais, baseados em regras fixas e em modelos estáticos, revelam limitações perante a evolução contínua dos padrões fraudulentos. O presente artigo tem como objectivo analisar, através de uma revisão da literatura, a aplicação da detecção de anomalias em tempo real à identificação de fraudes com recurso a Streaming Data e a algoritmos de Online Learning. O estudo adopta uma abordagem qualitativa, descritiva e exploratória, assente na pesquisa bibliográfica em bases de dados científicas e na análise qualitativa de conteúdo de artigos, livros e estudos especializados nas áreas da Inteligência Artificial, da aprendizagem automática, da mineração de fluxos de dados e da segurança digital. Os resultados evidenciam que a integração entre o processamento contínuo de dados, a detecção de anomalias e a aprendizagem incremental permite desenvolver sistemas mais adaptativos, escaláveis e eficientes na identificação de comportamentos suspeitos. Persistem, contudo, desafios relacionados com o concept drift, o desequilíbrio entre classes, os falsos positivos, a interpretabilidade dos modelos e a validação destas tecnologias em contextos reais, sendo ainda escassos os estudos sobre países em desenvolvimento, incluindo Moçambique. Conclui-se que a combinação entre Streaming Data e Online Learning constitui uma abordagem promissora para reforçar os mecanismos de prevenção de fraudes digitais, recomendando-se o desenvolvimento de estudos empíricos que considerem diferentes contextos tecnológicos e socioeconómicos. Abstract The increasing digitalisation of financial services and electronic platforms has intensified the challenges associated with fraud detection, requiring systems capable of analysing large volumes of data in real time. Traditional methods, based on fixed rules and static models, show limitations in the face of the continuous evolution of fraudulent patterns. This article aims to analyse, through a literature review, the application of real-time anomaly detection to fraud identification using Streaming Data and Online Learning algorithms. The study adopts a qualitative, descriptive and exploratory approach, based on a bibliographic search of scientific databases and on a qualitative content analysis of articles, books and specialised studies in the fields of Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, data stream mining and digital security. The findings show that integrating continuous data processing, anomaly detection and incremental learning enables the development of more adaptive, scalable and efficient systems for identifying suspicious behaviour. However, challenges persist regarding concept drift, class imbalance, false positives, model interpretability and the validation of these technologies in real-world settings, and studies on developing countries, including Mozambique, remain scarce. The study concludes that combining Streaming Data and Online Learning is a promising approach to strengthening digital fraud prevention mechanisms, and recommends empirical studies that consider different technological and socio-economic contexts.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF AI-ASSISTED ENGLISH TEACHING CLASSROOMS ON TESOL TEACHERS' TEACHING BELIEFS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
papers.authors: Muratova Iroda Muzaffar qizi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AI-assisted language classrooms are becoming a significant setting for reconsidering how TESOL teachers understand instructional authority, learner agency, and professional responsibility. This systematic review examines whether participation of artificial intelligence in English teaching encourages pedagogical recognition while preserving reservations about ethics, autonomy, and classroom judgment. A PRISMA-informed procedure organized evidence through thematic analysis across four interpretive dimensions: pedagogical value, teacher agency, professional roles, and ethical responsibility. The synthesis was also aligned with three pedagogical stages—diagnostic pretest, formative intervention, and control posttest—when these stages were present in the reviewed designs, while instrument reliability was treated against the threshold of Cronbach's alpha ≥ 0.70. The evidence indicates that teachers generally acknowledge AI's capacity to support personalization, feedback, and lesson planning, but they resist replacing relational judgment with automated recommendations. The review contributes a stage-sensitive framework connecting teachers' changing beliefs with professional preparation and ethical guidance, thereby clarifying conditions for sustainable AI-supported English pedagogy.

papers.title: The Strategic Role of Additive Manufacturing in European Industrial Transformation
papers.authors: Johannes Gartner
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) is entering a phase in which its development can no longer be understood solely through technological performance or short-term equipment sales. It is increasingly connected to wider questions of industrial competitiveness, supply-chain resilience, energy security, defence capability, sustainability, and the preservation of manufacturing capacity in Europe. This extended abstract examines the current state of the AM industry and discusses its emerging political and economic significance within the European Union. Drawing on market data presented from the Wohlers Report, CONTEXT, and own research, together with findings from the academic literature, the analysis contrasts recent negative market sentiment with evidence of long-term industrial maturation and application growth. It argues that Europe should treat AM not as an isolated production technology, but as a central component of advanced manufacturing value chains. Recent pessimism surrounding the AM sector can be attributed to several interconnected factors. Hardware sales have fluctuated, market consolidation has intensified, and competition among system manufacturers has become increasingly aggressive. These developments have occurred alongside recessionary pressures in several Western economies, changing trade conditions, export tariffs, and the slower-than-anticipated development of some sustainability-related applications. Investor attention has also shifted toward emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, while AM companies continue to face complex standardisation requirements and regulatory approval processes. These difficulties are particularly consequential in Europe, where fragmented markets, higher operating costs, slower capital mobilisation, and regulatory complexity may create a systemic competitive disadvantage relative to the United States and parts of Asia. Nevertheless, short-term weakness in selected market indicators should not be interpreted as evidence of technological or industrial decline. The analysis reports that worldwide AM revenue reached approximately USD 24.2 billion in 2025, representing annual growth of 10.9%. Regional development was strongest in the Asia-Pacific region, at 19.8%, followed by the Americas at 12.6% and Europe, the Middle East, and Africa at 9.0%. Growth was uneven across business categories: printing services increased by 15.5%, while system manufacturers expanded by only 3.6%. This divergence indicates that the centre of value creation may be shifting from machine sales toward production services, application development, materials, software, and integrated manufacturing solutions [1]. Long-term revenue data further suggest that AM continues to follow a sustained growth trajectory despite periodic downturns. Equipment-sales volatility is characteristic of capital-intensive industries, particularly during periods of economic uncertainty and technological transition. Market consolidation can therefore be interpreted not only as a sign of weakness, but also as an indication that the industry is maturing. Less competitive firms are exiting or being acquired, while established providers increasingly focus on production reliability, qualification, automation, and economically viable applications. Industrial and entry-level system segments are reported to be growing again, and demand is being supported by investment from the aerospace, defence, and energy sectors. Developments in advanced materials and artificial intelligence may additionally improve process control, design optimisation, quality assurance, and machine productivity. A central distinction must consequently be made between the performance of AM equipment suppliers and the diffusion of AM applications. Although hardware markets may fluctuate, the number and sophistication of industrial applications have continued to increase. Market approvals in regulated sectors are creating pipelines for serial production, particularly in aerospace, medical technology, energy, and other safety-critical industries. This transition from prototyping toward qualified end-use production changes the basis on which AM should be evaluated. The strategic importance of the technology increasingly lies in the value generated by specific applications rather than in the number of machines sold. The implementation of AM may also create organisational benefits extending beyond the production of individual components. Research summarised in the presentation indicates that AM can increase manufacturing flexibility by enabling equipment, production sequences, capacity, routing, automation, and material-handling systems to adapt more rapidly to changing requirements. AM adoption has also been associated with process innovation, customer satisfaction, and improved operational performance. Because production depends heavily on digital design data and specialised process knowledge, implementation increases the importance of internal knowledge transfer, technical expertise, and proximity to customers. At the same time, it can reduce dependence on intermediate products and conventional multi-stage supply chains [3-7]. AM does not necessarily replace established production methods. Instead, it frequently complements conventional manufacturing and creates additional value streams. Hybrid production systems can combine the geometric freedom and low-volume flexibility of AM with the productivity and material properties of established processes. Decisions to internalise AM capacity may be motivated by the protection of intellectual property, organisational learning, skill acquisition, shorter development cycles, and stronger employee engagement. The technology should therefore be assessed as part of a broader manufacturing system rather than as a stand-alone substitute for machining, casting, forming, or injection moulding. The economic relevance of AM is also reflected in its employment base. According to the analysis, more than 12,000 companies maintain dedicated AM departments, while more than 5,300 specialised AM companies operate globally. These firms employ an average of approximately 14 people. However, the workforce remains gender-imbalanced: women account for around 31% of employees and only 12% of machine operators. The average employment duration of 4.3 years, together with the emergence of multiple generations of AM professionals, suggests that the sector is developing a more stable and experienced labour market. Future competitiveness will therefore depend not only on technological investment, but also on education, professionalisation, workforce diversity, and the retention of specialised knowledge [8]. For Europe, AM has acquired a growing political dimension because it can contribute to several strategic objectives simultaneously. Distributed and digitally enabled production can strengthen resilient value chains, support defence and critical-infrastructure capabilities, improve access to spare parts, and reduce selected external dependencies. It may facilitate energy-sector innovation, material efficiency, component repair, lightweight design, and the reshoring of strategically important manufacturing activities. These capabilities correspond closely to the European Union's competitiveness agenda, particularly the objectives of closing the innovation gap, decarbonising the economy, and reducing dependencies. Yet Europe's position remains ambiguous. The region possesses a substantial installed base of AM systems, strong research institutions, specialised machine manufacturers, and established industrial users. However, the United States leads in several indicators related to system installations, sales, startup activity, and investment. European startup ecosystems remain comparatively fragmented, while access to growth capital is often weaker. The proposed European Competitiveness Fund for 2028-2034, with its emphasis on advanced manufacturing, robotics, artificial intelligence, automation, and higher technology-readiness levels, may offer an opportunity to address this disadvantage. Its effectiveness will depend on whether funding instruments connect research, scale-up, industrial deployment, and demand from strategically important applications. Three priorities emerge for European industrial and innovation policy. First, Europe needs an integrated AM strategy and should develop integrated advanced manufacturing value chains linking equipment, materials, software, data, qualification, production services, and end users. Second, policy and investment decisions should focus on the economic and strategic value of critical applications rather than on technology development in isolation. Third, stronger coordination is required among companies, research organisations, industry associations, public authorities, and cross-border initiatives. Organisations such as Addliance, AM Europe, Mobility goes Additive, and other national and European networks can contribute to standardisation, knowledge exchange, application development, and the aggregation of industrial demand. In conclusion, the AM industry is not undergoing a simple transition from growth to decline. It is moving from an investment-driven and hardware-centred phase toward a more mature, application-oriented, and politically significant stage. Short-term market fluctuations coexist with long-term revenue growth, expanding industrial use, and increasing strategic relevance. Europe retains substantial technological and institutional capabilities, but risks losing competitiveness unless it overcomes fragmentation, mobilises investment, supports industrial scale-up, and connects AM more directly to its wider economic and security objectives. Additive manufacturing should therefore be understood as an enabling infrastructure for Europe's future production system and as a strategic instrument for strengthening industrial sovereignty, resilience, and sustainable competitiveness. © 2026

papers.title: Bringing AI and Physical AI to Manufacturing: Data, Processes and People as the Real Bottleneck on the Shop Floor
papers.authors: Florian Pauker, Klaus Halbfas
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AI in manufacturing is shifting from systems that inform to embodied, physical AI that acts [1]. Its symbol, the humanoid robot, suits smaller manufacturers structurally: it works in environments built for people, where conventional automation needs stable, repetitive processes. Yet 2026 marks the move from demonstrator to pilot, not series - operating figures are unpublished, the debate divided [2], safety unresolved [3]. The adoption gap widens: 17 % of small against 55 % of large EU enterprises used AI in 2025 [4]; the cause lies in capabilities, not technology [5], [6] - 58 % of firms stall in planning or pilot [7], and data blocks implementation [8]. This contribution asks what a manufacturer must build for AI to become effective, reporting an exploratory single case study [9]: EVVA Sicherheitstechnologie GmbH, an Austrian manufacturer of locking systems, around 800 employees, high-mix and low-volume. EVVA's decision was to introduce AI not as a lighthouse use case but as an ecosystem of six interdependent elements: technology and platform; data and data sovereignty; processes and use cases; organisation and roles; competence and culture; governance and safety. They are sequentially dependent: without data no physical-AI application carries, without processes selection is arbitrary, without organisation no body develops the rest. Organisation is the lever that moves the others - the element companies invest in least [10]. The organisation is two-tier. A central AI core team, mandated by and including the managing director, unites operations, R&D, software development, application management and IT - deliberately strong in implementation, which made running a sovereign platform in-house realistic. It sets standards, prioritises the portfolio, develops requirements, selects systems and defines governance. Around it, 27 AI Explorers work in the business units: practitioners rather than IT specialists, who spot use cases where the friction occurs and supply requirements from practice. The role carries only where working time is formally released - the commonest failure point. The pattern echoes innovation-champion research [11], yet no such model has been evaluated empirically. Three blocks complete the foundation. Enablement is company-wide, training a precondition for access - satisfying Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 [12] and steering risk without technical controls. The platform is central, not a set of tool subscriptions: an LLM router distributes requests by task, cost and confidentiality, keeping models exchangeable, and runs hybridly on premises and in EU-sovereign cloud, where workload allocation is economic and sovereignty preserved. An abstraction layer between data and platform opens access through standardised interfaces and limits it through a four-level protection-class model enforcing rights, roles and logging. Explorers submit use cases, sorted into five clusters - generative AI and agents, AI in software development, analytics, physical AI, standard business applications - and assessed on economics, feasibility and compliance. After this first phase: 27 Explorers, company-wide qualification, four protection classes, 25 submitted against 3 productive use cases. Decentralised multipliers reliably generate supply; ideas are not the bottleneck. The implementation rate of roughly 12 % is the more valuable result. Physical AI is the next step, approached from an unexpected side: AI acts both in the product, as embodied intelligence in the running plant, and in the engineering that creates it - the second far more mature. Language models generate IEC 61131-3 structured text at usable rates given compiler feedback [13]; at EVVA an AI coding assistant, configured with the company's automation conventions, writes and extends machine programs. These are not tried on the real plant but run against the machine's digital twin - the control application in simulation against a behaviour model - closing generation, validation and correction into a loop before hardware or people are involved. The twin separates a plausible AI output from a valid one and underpins simulation-based training of robot foundation models [14], though the reality gap keeps it necessary, not sufficient [15]. This adds a stage before the robot pilot: the company practices physical AI on its own engineering, building the capabilities embodied AI later requires. Every next step, though, is bounded by qualified people: use cases become productive only where someone can build them - which takes both roles. Decentrally the Explorers identify the need; centrally, AI Engineers run the platform and ecosystem, implement what the Explorers cannot, and keep them capable. Without them the Explorers generate demand nobody can serve, which is what an implementation rate of 12 % measures. For physical AI, the core team must gain control engineering. The question is therefore not when humanoid robots become affordable, but whether the company is prepared when they are. © 2026 The Authors. papers.title: CARE-AI: Un Framework Etico di AI Literacy per la Formazione delle Professioni Sanitarie
papers.authors: Francesco Germini, Gianluca Fedelfranco
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: CARE-AI is an ethical AI literacy framework designed to support the education of healthcare professionals in the responsible, aware and safe use of artificial intelligence. The framework integrates concepts derived from the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, UNESCO AI Competency Frameworks, DigComp 3.0, DigCompEdu and WHO guidance on artificial intelligence for health. The poster presents six dimensions: understanding task and context; critical evaluation of outputs and sources; agency and accountability; data and security; equity and inclusion; and appropriate application. CARE-AI also proposes a prototype educational unit and a process-oriented approach to assessment. The framework presented at DIDAMATICA 2026 is conceptual and developmental; formal empirical validation represents a subsequent research phase. Poster presented at DIDAMATICA 2026, Padova, Italy, 7–8 October 2026.

papers.title: Pengaruh AI dan Spirit Tajdid Kemuhammadiyahan terhadap Moderasi Beragama Mahasiswa STIT Muhammadiyah Tanjung Redeb
papers.authors: Rani Selfiana, Khoiriyah Khoiriyah
papers.journal: Tarbiyah Islamiah Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Islam
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Society 5.0 era presents both opportunities and ethical challenges for strengthening students’ religious character. This causal associative quantitative study aims to analyze the effects of AI utilization and the Spirit of Muhammadiyah Tajdid on religious moderation among students at STIT Muhammadiyah Tanjung Redeb. Data were collected through a closed-ended questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale ranging from Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree. The population consisted of all 67 active students enrolled in the TBI and PAI study programs, with a saturated sampling technique (total sampling) employed. The instrument was tested for validity using the Pearson Product-Moment correlation and for reliability using Cronbach’s Alpha, with a reliability coefficient above 0.60, using SPSS. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results showed that AI utilization had no statistically significant partial effect on religious moderation (t = 0.682, p = 0.498), whereas the Spirit of Muhammadiyah Tajdid had a highly significant positive effect (t = 6.252, p = 0.000). Simultaneously, both variables had a highly significant effect (F = 172.820, p = 0.000), with an R Square coefficient of 0.844, indicating that 84.4% of the variance in religious moderation was explained by the two independent variables. It is concluded that AI can serve as an effective accelerator for strengthening religious moderation when grounded in the Spirit of Tajdid and a strong foundation of scholarly ethics.

papers.title: COLLEGE STUDENTS’ PERCEPTIONS ON THE USE OF CHATGPT FOR ARGUMENTATIVE WRITING
papers.authors: Husni Mubarok, Sinta Dewi, Asep Suparman
papers.journal: EDUTECH Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Berbantuan Teknologi
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of ChatGPT among English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners has raised both pedagogical enthusiasm and concern, particularly in argumentative writing, a genre that depends heavily on independent reasoning and balanced argumentation. This study examines how EFL college students perceive and experience the use of ChatGPT when composing argumentative essays, with particular attention to its benefits, challenges, and influence on critical thinking. A qualitative case study design was employed, involving four English Education students at a college in Garut who had been screened through a preliminary questionnaire as active ChatGPT users. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis procedures. The findings show that participants consistently used ChatGPT for idea development, grammar correction, vocabulary enrichment, and structuring pro–con arguments, and perceived clear improvements in coherence, cohesion, and lexical quality. However, participants also reported challenges such as generic or robotic output, prompt-dependent accuracy, occasional topic drift, and a growing sense of dependency that narrowed creative exploration for some users. Critical thinking was not perceived as uniformly weakened; rather, it was preserved or even strengthened when students actively verified, compared, and revised suggestions, but was put at risk when suggestions were accepted uncritically. The study concludes that ChatGPT functions less as an author and more as a scaffolding partner whose pedagogical value is contingent on students' metacognitive regulation and prompting literacy. These findings offer practical implications for EFL writing instruction, particularly the need to cultivate deliberate, reflective, and verification-based AI integration. ABSTRAK Adopsi ChatGPT yang semakin pesat di kalangan pembelajar Bahasa Inggris sebagai Bahasa Asing (English as a Foreign Language/EFL) telah menimbulkan antusiasme sekaligus kekhawatiran pedagogis, khususnya dalam penulisan esai argumentatif yang menuntut penalaran mandiri dan penyusunan sudut pandang yang berimbang. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menginvestigasi persepsi dan pengalaman nyata mahasiswa EFL dalam memanfaatkan ChatGPT saat menyusun teks argumentatif, dengan fokus utama pada manfaat instrumental, tantangan praktis, serta implikasinya terhadap kemampuan berpikir kritis. Pendekatan penelitian yang diterapkan adalah studi kasus kualitatif dengan melibatkan empat mahasiswa Program Studi Pendidikan Bahasa Inggris di salah satu perguruan tinggi di Garut yang telah terjaring melalui kuesioner penyaring sebagai pengguna aktif ChatGPT. Pengumpulan data dilaksanakan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur mendalam yang selanjutnya dianalisis menggunakan prosedur analisis tematik. Hasil penelitian mengungkapkan bahwa mahasiswa secara konsisten memanfaatkan ChatGPT untuk memfasilitasi pengembangan ide, koreksi tata bahasa, perluasan variasi kosakata, dan penyusunan kerangka argumen pro–kontra. Meskipun demikian, mahasiswa menghadapi kendala nyata berupa keluaran teks yang kaku (robotic), ketergantungan kualitas jawaban pada ketepatan prompt, pergeseran topik (topic drift), serta risiko ketergantungan yang mempersempit eksplorasi kreatif. Kemampuan berpikir kritis terbukti tidak tereduksi secara mutlak, melainkan bersifat kondisional di mana nalar kritis tetap terjaga saat mahasiswa aktif memverifikasi dan mengoreksi saran kecerdasan buatan, namun berisiko melemah jika keluaran diterima tanpa evaluasi reflektif. Oleh karena itu, ChatGPT lebih tepat diposisikan sebagai mitra penopang (scaffolding partner) daripada pembuat teks utama, yang menuntut penguatan regulasi metakognitif dan literasi prompt dalam pengajaran menulis akademik.

papers.title: EXPLORING EFL STUDENTS' PERCEPTIONS OF AI WRITING ASSISTANTS IN SUPPORTING ACADEMIC WRITING STRUCTURE AND COHERENCE
papers.authors: Asyilla Agustina Mustika Janwar, Eva Devi Sofyawati, Pipih Setiawati
papers.journal: EDUTECH Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Berbantuan Teknologi
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has led to the increasing use of AI Writing Assistants in tertiary academic writing practices. Although these tools offer considerable technical support, students' perceptions of their actual role in supporting higher-order writing dimensions—specifically organizational structure and textual coherence—warrant rigorous empirical investigation. This study aims to explore EFL students' perceptions and lived experiences regarding the use of AI Writing Assistants in developing academic writing structure and coherence. Employing a descriptive qualitative research design, this inquiry engaged ten final-year English Education undergraduates at a university in Garut who had completed Academic Writing coursework and routinely utilized AI-powered platforms. Primary data were gathered through semi-structured online interviews guided by a 25-item open-ended protocol and systematically examined using the interactive qualitative analysis model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, which encompasses data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. The findings reveal that AI Writing Assistants provide substantial benefits by facilitating idea mapping, structural outlining, paragraph coherence enhancement, formative revision feedback, and drafting support. Nevertheless, participants encountered critical operational challenges, including the necessity of sophisticated prompt formulation, occasional factual inaccuracies, cognitive dependency, and the imperative for critical manual verification. The study concludes that AI Writing Assistants function effectively as scaffolding partners in fostering academic writing structure and coherence when deployed with active metacognitive regulation and rigorous critical evaluation. ABSTRAK Perkembangan pesat Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong meluasnya adopsi AI Writing Assistants dalam praktik penulisan akademik di perguruan tinggi. Meskipun teknologi ini menawarkan kemudahan teknis, persepsi mahasiswa mengenai perannya dalam menopang aspek tingkat tinggi penulisan akademik, khususnya struktur teks dan koherensi, masih memerlukan kajian empiris yang mendalam. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi persepsi dan pengalaman nyata mahasiswa English as a Foreign Language (EFL) dalam memanfaatkan AI Writing Assistants guna mengembangkan struktur dan koherensi tulisan akademik. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi deskriptif yang melibatkan sepuluh mahasiswa tingkat akhir Program Studi Pendidikan Bahasa Inggris di Garut yang berpengalaman menggunakan alat bantu berbasis AI. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur mendalam secara daring dengan instrumen berupa pedoman wawancara 25 butir pertanyaan terbuka, serta dianalisis menggunakan model interaktif Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña yang mencakup reduksi data, penyajian data, dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa AI Writing Assistants memberikan manfaat nyata dalam membantu pemetaan ide, penyusunan kerangka karangan, penyelarasan koherensi antarparagraf, pemberian umpan balik formatif, dan fasilitasi proses draf penulisan. Kendati demikian, mahasiswa menghadapi tantangan teknis berupa tuntutan literasi prompt, risiko keluaran teks yang tidak akurat (hallucination), kecenderungan ketergantungan kognitif (overreliance), serta perlunya verifikasi kritis terhadap sumber rujukan. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa AI Writing Assistants efektif menjadi mitra penopang (scaffolding partner) dalam memfasilitasi struktur dan koherensi penulisan akademik apabila diimbangi oleh regulasi metakognitif dan evaluasi kritis dari mahasiswa.

papers.title: EFL LEARNERS’ EXPERIENCES IN PRACTICING ENGLISH CONVERSATION THROUGH AI-GENERATED CHARACTERS ON CHATGPT
papers.authors: Anggia Nastya, Anne Ratna Suminar, Yustika Nur Fajriah
papers.abstract: Limited opportunities for authentic conversational practice outside the classroom and high speaking anxiety remain significant barriers for English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners. Despite the rapid growth of conversational artificial intelligence (AI), empirical investigations into learners' lived experiences when interacting with customized virtual interlocutors remain scarce. This study explored EFL learners' experiences in practicing English conversation through interactions with AI-generated characters on ChatGPT. Employing a qualitative case study design, this research involved seven EFL undergraduate students from the English Education Program at Institut Pendidikan Indonesia Garut selected through purposive sampling. Data were accumulated through expert-validated semi-structured interviews and corroborated by digital chat history documentation, which were subsequently analyzed using Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis framework. The findings identified three overarching themes: practical use, benefits, and challenges. In terms of practical use, participants purposefully customized conversational personas and varied interaction formats, although engagement with advanced prompt settings remained minimal. The most prominent benefits were marked reductions in speaking anxiety, increased communicative confidence, vocabulary acquisition, and autonomous practice accessibility. Meanwhile, the observed challenges included premature AI turn-taking interruptions, vocabulary deficits on unfamiliar topics, and localized motivational decline. This study concludes that AI-generated characters serve as a meaningful low-pressure preparatory environment for authentic EFL speaking practice. ABSTRAK Keterbatasan kesempatan praktik percakapan autentik di luar kelas dan tingginya kecemasan berbicara masih menjadi hambatan utama bagi pembelajar bahasa Inggris sebagai bahasa asing (EFL). Meskipun pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan (AI) berkembang pesat, kajian mendalam mengenai pengalaman nyata pembelajar saat berinteraksi dengan karakter berbasis AI masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi pengalaman pelajar EFL dalam berlatih percakapan bahasa Inggris melalui interaksi dengan AI-generated characters pada platform ChatGPT. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus, penelitian ini melibatkan tujuh pelajar EFL dari Program Studi Pendidikan Bahasa Inggris di Institut Pendidikan Indonesia Garut yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur yang telah divalidasi ahli dan didukung oleh dokumentasi riwayat percakapan digital, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik model Braun dan Clarke. Hasil penelitian mengidentifikasi tiga tema utama: penggunaan praktis, manfaat, dan tantangan. Dari segi penggunaan praktis, partisipan menetapkan persona karakter secara aktif dan memvariasikan format percakapan, meskipun pemanfaatan fitur konfigurasi tingkat lanjut masih terbatas. Manfaat utama yang dirasakan meliputi penurunan kecemasan berbicara, peningkatan kepercayaan diri, perluasan kosakata, serta fleksibilitas akses latihan mandiri. Adapun tantangan yang dihadapi mencakup respons prematur sistem AI, kendala kosakata pada topik yang belum dikuasai, serta penurunan motivasi yang bersifat individual. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa interaksi dengan AI-generated characters efektif berfungsi sebagai media latihan percakapan awal yang aman dan bebas tekanan sosial bagi pembelajar EFL.
keywords: English as a foreign language teaching

papers.title: Sensibilités et formes de délégation à l’IA générative : analyse de récits problématisés
papers.authors: Béatrice Drot-Delange
papers.journal: Revue internationale du CRIRES innover dans la tradition de Vygotsky
papers.abstract: The corpus studied in this article brings together 33 narratives where users question their own use of generative AI (IAg), and in particular conversational AI (cIA), whether in an academic, professional or personal contexts. It focuses on participants' experiences and the forms of delegation to cAI – ranging from substitution to cooperation, and even refusal. The analysis is grounded in three concepts: the share of self engaged in or delegated through the interaction (Spach, 2025); registers of activity, which capture the broad orientations that shape interactions with cAI; and sensitivity to (Récopé et al., 2013). These concepts are applied to the narrative analysis using a mixed coding approach (Paillé and Mucchielli, 2016). The results reveal four dominant activity registers – operational economy, epistemic vigilance, subjectivation and self-preservation, and axiological coherence – and six distinct sensitivities to that explain why the same task performed with the cAI can be experienced differently from one person to another. The study shows that epistemic agency is not a stable property of individuals, but rather a potentiality that is activated or inhibited depending on the dominant sensitivity to and the configuration of the situation. The study underscores the importance of designing educational interventions that activate sensitivities conducive to critical reflection and vigilance.

papers.title: L’IA générative levier d’agentivité ? Analyse des pratiques étudiantes en enseignement supérieur
papers.authors: Didier Paquelin, Valentine Kropf, Mada Lucienne Tendeng, Évarice-Benoît Djieufack
papers.journal: Revue internationale du CRIRES innover dans la tradition de Vygotsky
papers.abstract: Agency, defined as the learner’s power to act and capacity to take an active role in their own learning (Bandura, 1997, 2001), serves as the framework for analyzing student practices with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools. This article reports on an exploratory study conducted at Laval University (Quebec) involving 4,628 students (8.2% of the enrolled population in 2024-2025), using a self-administered questionnaire (26 closed-ended questions and one open-ended question, December 2024-January 2025). We analyzed the quantitative data using Spearman’s correlations and supplemented them with a qualitative analysis of 1,511 open-ended responses. These analyses address the question: In what ways, how, and why does using GenAI tools contribute to students’ agency? We identify and characterize four usage profiles and four patterns of use by the types and aims of agency, in relation to learner characteristics, context, and the learning environment. Given the significance of non-use (44% of respondents), this article discusses the links between using these conversational bots and an inclusive perspective on student well-being.

papers.title: Usages émergents de l'IA générative : l'agentivité humaine comme question centrale?
papers.authors: Georges‐Louis Baron, Thérèse Laferrière
papers.journal: Revue internationale du CRIRES innover dans la tradition de Vygotsky
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become a highly visible phenomenon in education, notably in the form of chatbots, which we refer to here as “conversational artificial intelligence” (cAI). cAI has prompted numerous critical perspectives that emphasize the risks associated with its use, both for users and for teaching, some of whose very foundations are seen as potentially threatened. In this article, we therefore focus on human agency and on how cAI, conceived as an instrument for learning, can contribute to educational success. We first contextualize and situate this notion, which is broader than that of academic success as measured by statistical indicators reflecting performance on examinations. We then present examples of interactions with cAI, developed from narratives collected as part of a Franco-Québec collaboration conducted within the 2IFPER working group. We analyze these interactions in terms of their potential for intellectual emancipation or functional subjection, according to the place human agency occupies within them: humans may “play first violin”, while cAI assists or accompanies them. Conversely, delegation to cAI may reduce human agency within the interaction and, when such delegation becomes predominant, open the way to subjection.

papers.title: Agentivité et IAg en formation initiale et continue de personnes enseignantes au Québec
papers.authors: M. Tremblay, Sophie Nadeau-Tremblay
papers.journal: Revue internationale du CRIRES innover dans la tradition de Vygotsky
papers.abstract: Building on the 2024-2025 Entretiens Jacques-Cartier devoted to the theme “Generative AI and University Education: Innovation, Regulation, and Agency”, this article examines emerging uses of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in initial and in-service teacher education. Drawing on a conceptual framework centred on individual and collective agency, it explores the conditions under which GenAI can support professional development and learning beyond strictly technocentric approaches. The analysis is based on two case studies. The first, situated in initial teacher education, examines the voluntary integration of GenAI in an algebra didactics course, highlighting a shift toward uses centred on understanding, collective validation, and developing a didactic perspective on generated outputs and the use of these tools. The second, conducted in primary in-service teacher education, focuses on the use of a conversational agent embedded in a knowledge-building environment and identifies pedagogical and institutional conditions that foster agency among students and teachers. The findings suggest that the central challenge lies less in technical mastery of GenAI tools than in thoughtfully articulating innovation, regulation, and agency.

papers.title: CURRÍCULO FLEXÍVEL, DESIGUALDADES EDUCACIONAIS E INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA ESCOLA PÚBLICA: DESAFIOS PARA O ENSINO MÉDIO CONTEMPORÂNEO
papers.authors: Eliana Priscila Cavalcanti de Brito
papers.journal: RCMOS - Revista Científica Multidisciplinar O Saber
papers.abstract: The curricular reconfiguration of Brazilian secondary education, consolidated through Law 13.415/2017 and the National Common Curricular Base, introduced new forms of school organization based on curriculum flexibility and training pathways. At the same time, the rapid advancement of digital technologies and artificial intelligence has significantly transformed educational practices and access to knowledge. This study critically analyzes the relationship between curricular flexibility, educational inequalities, and the emerging use of artificial intelligence in public schools. It is a qualitative theoretical study based on bibliographic review and documentary analysis of recent educational policies. The study discusses how curriculum flexibility may expand educational opportunities but also reproduce structural inequalities when implemented in contexts marked by disparities in infrastructure and teacher training. It argues that artificial intelligence has the potential to transform teaching and learning processes; however, unequal access to such technologies may reinforce disparities between school systems. The study concludes that democratizing access to educational technologies and scientific knowledge is essential for ensuring that curriculum flexibility contributes to educational equity in Brazilian secondary education.

papers.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Zhen Li, Mingfa Feng, Yiming Zhang, Yang Yu, Changhai Zhou, Pengxiang Li, Dongkuan Wu, Congkai Xie, Hongxia Yang
papers.abstract: Native NVFP4 promises to accelerate reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs), but achieving stable learning across separate training and sampling engines remains challenging. We show that matching model weights and numerical formats is insufficient to ensure consistent policy evaluation, highlighting the importance of cross-engine numerical execution. We introduce miniTE, a lightweight framework that combines execution diagnostics, cross-engine numerical alignment, and efficient native W4A4 (4-bit weights and activations) GEMM computation for LLM RL. It improves numerical execution consistency without modifying the RL objective, while reducing implementation overhead to realize the benefits of native low-bit computation. Long-horizon RL experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B demonstrate stable training and benchmark performance close to BF16, outperforming naive Transformer Engine (TE) NVFP4 in evaluation quality. On single NVIDIA B300 GPU node, the optimized learner reaches 33,540 tokens/s, yielding 1.39x and 1.47x the throughput of BF16 and TE NVFP4, respectively, for complete learner updates. We released the framework, kernels, diagnostics, and training configurations to make native low-bit RL easier.

papers.title: Omni-Diffusion-Distill: Few-Step Distillation of Unified Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
papers.authors: Hong Huang, Chenhongyi Yang, J. Sun, Animesh Sinha, Wuyang Chen, Yifan Jiang
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal diffusion large language models (dLLMs) offer a single architecture for both image generation and multimodal understanding, but their iterative decoding requires tens to hundreds of forward passes. Existing few-step distillation methods largely focus on either image generation or text generation, making it unclear how to compress a fully discrete multimodal dLLM into a single efficient student while preserving both generation and understanding. We introduce Omni-Diffusion-Distill, a unified two-stage distillation framework that retains strong generation and understanding capabilities while substantially reducing the inference cost of a unified multimodal dLLM. Omni-Diffusion-Distill aligns the distillation of both generation and understanding, for both images and text, in the discrete token space. In the first stage, the student is trained to skip decoding steps by replaying cached teacher trajectories, and in the second stage the student is refined on intermediate states along its own rollouts. We further remedy two sources of degradation in unified distillation with a pairwise collision penalty that reduces repetition under parallel text decoding, and entropy-matched guidance that prevents entropy collapse caused by fitting the sharpened teacher distribution in image generation. Omni-Diffusion-Distill achieves state-of-the-art trade-offs between decoding efficiency and generation and understanding performance for multimodal dLLMs, reducing image generation from 128 to 8 decoding steps and multimodal understanding from 512 to 64, giving 18.2x and 21.2x wall-clock speedups. Under these budgets, it scores 0.828 on GenEval and 83.0 on DPG-Bench for text-to-image generation, while reaching GPT judge scores of 20.0 on MM-Vet and 57.2 on COCO captioning (twice the teacher's 28.4 at the same steps) for multimodal understanding.

papers.title: Budgeted Multi-Source Counterfactual Annotation for Off-Policy Evaluation
papers.authors: Biao Xiang, Ali Eshragh, Yuexing Li, Kai Wang
papers.abstract: Off-policy evaluation (OPE) estimates the value of a target policy from logged data, but limited behavior-policy coverage can force high-variance reweighting or reward-model extrapolation. Counterfactual annotations can add evidence about unobserved actions, yet practical sources, including domain experts and large language models (LLMs), may be costly, biased, or noisy. We study budgeted acquisition of such annotations for contextual-bandit OPE. Given source-specific costs and error profiles, we formulate an integer allocation problem over context-action pairs and annotation sources to minimize the component of estimator variance that depends on the annotation plan. We characterize when annotations are valuable through a first-annotation threshold and local annotation-value regimes. For the coupled multi-source problem, we develop a majorization-minimization algorithm with dynamic-programming subroutines that monotonically improves the objective. Experiments in synthetic clinical and LLM-annotated education bandits show that our allocation method reduces fixed-profile mean squared error (MSE) by 20.58% and 10.77%, respectively, relative to no annotation.

papers.title: SPD-MetaFormer is what you need for small-data brain decoding
papers.authors: Zhida Wang, Wei Lyu, Guo Yu, Sui Tang
papers.abstract: Brain signal decoding is challenging because neural recordings are noisy and vary across individuals, while labeled data are often limited. Recent attention-based models on the symmetric positive definite (SPD) manifold have nevertheless achieved strong performance using covariance and connectivity representations, yet the contribution of learned token weighting remains unclear. We examine two representative architectures, MAtt (based on log-Euclidean geometry) and GBWAtt (based on generalized Bures--Wasserstein geometry), and find that their learned attention weights remain close to uniform after training. We relate this behavior to bounded similarity parameterizations that, under the original softmax scaling, limit attention-weight contrast. Moreover, replacing learned weights with uniform weights, throughout training and evaluation, has little effect on mean predictive performance while preserving each model's original aggregation geometry. Motivated by these findings, we introduce SPD-MetaFormer, an attention-free architecture built on uniformly weighted Fréchet aggregation under log-Euclidean geometry. Its backbone uses a geodesic residual to update a summary token and a shared spectral feedforward map to transform all tokens, followed by a learned weighted readout. Token states remain SPD-valued until tangent-space classification. Across three EEG benchmarks, SPD-MetaFormer achieves competitive results relative to published Euclidean and manifold baselines. Separate matched reproductions test learned versus uniform weighting within MAtt and GBWAtt. These results suggest that, in the short-sequence and limited-data regimes studied, carefully designed SPD architectures can provide a simpler and effective alternative to adaptive manifold attention.

papers.title: Feeling Wistful: Reflecting on Scholarly Sensibilities with Creative Reading Traces
papers.authors: Liu, Sophia W., Kate Chier, Shm Garanganao Almeda, Max Kreminski, Björn Hartmann
papers.abstract: Researchers often read before they can articulate what they are looking for. As AI increasingly mediates scholarly search and synthesis, understanding and preserving the idiosyncratic judgments guiding early exploration become important. We call these evolving orientations scholarly sensibilities. To understand curiosity-driven reading, we first examined Wikipedia rabbitholing, a self-directed browsing practice, then designed Wistful, a research probe for open-ended scholarly exploration that captures reading paths as creative reading traces. We studied Wistful with 16 HCI researchers---eight junior and eight senior---in comparison with their usual workflows. Researchers approached the same scholarly landscape differently, with familiarity and personal interests shaping what they pursued and semantic proximity and scholarly links shaping their paths. Their traces made these differences visible and let readers revisit and compare their paths. We position creative reading traces as artifacts for reflection and exchange and as a means of studying how scholarly sensibilities are expressed through reading.

papers.title: Estimating Optimal Dynamic Treatment Regimes for Personalized Education: A Tutorial and Applications with Machine Learning
papers.authors: Chenguang Pan, Yuxuan Li, Thomas Harris, Youmi Suk
papers.abstract: Optimal dynamic treatment regimes (ODTRs) are increasingly used to generate sequences of personalized recommendations that maximize a final outcome of interest. Although ODTRs are widely used in biostatistics and precision medicine, their applications in education remain limited, especially for longitudinal decision-making. This study translates ODTR methods for single- and multi-stage designs into individualized high school math course recommendations, providing step-by-step guidelines and demonstrations with data from the High School Longitudinal Study of 2009 (HSLS:09). We use Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation with ensemble machine learning to estimate ODTRs that maximize students' math achievement and college enrollment, imposing feasibility constraints based on domain knowledge and propensity-score thresholds to ensure recommendations are practically implementable. Results show that unconstrained regimes yield higher estimated values but infeasible recommendations, while feasible regimes produce realistic pathways with stronger empirical and expert-informed support. Finally, we discuss practical considerations for designing ODTRs in education.

papers.title: Grammar Concept Annotation at Scale: Deployed Fine-Tuned Small Language Models Outperform Prompted Frontier Models
papers.authors: Marjan Celikik, Ana Peleteiro Ramallo, Javier Morales
papers.abstract: Corrective feedback is among the best-evidenced drivers of second-language acquisition, yet corrections delivered during lessons rarely accumulate into an actionable view of grammar mastery. Prompted frontier models can provide such a view from learner--tutor lesson transcripts, but they are costly at scale. We close this gap by fine-tuning Qwen3.5 small language models (SLMs) on filtered and rebalanced teacher-generated supervision, then deploying an efficient 0.8B model in an end-to-end grammar mastery tracker for all English learners on our platform. Internalizing the annotation contract into adapter weights enables pairing the 0.8B model with a compact matched prompt rather than verbose instructions. On two human-curated benchmarks, both the deployed 0.8B model and a 4B reference comparator outperform prompted GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.6 Sol in precision and recall under nested matching criteria of increasing strictness: concept, evidence span, and correctness. The deployed 0.8B SLM reduces serving cost by approximately 16$\times$. A feature-level online experiment shows significant gains in learner engagement ($+15.8\%$) and key business metrics, including scheduled hours ($+2.1\%$) and GMV from new lessons ($+13.2\%$).

papers.title: Guided Reflection for Personal Sleep Insight in Everyday Sleep Tracking
papers.authors: Bokyung Kim, Amama Mahmood, Honghao Zhao, Molly E. Atwood, Luis F. Buenaver, Ziang Xiao, Chien-Ming Huang
papers.abstract: Digital sleep technologies make tracking accessible, yet users often struggle to interpret what changes in their sleep mean. Behavioral sleep medicine addresses this through guided discovery, helping patients develop personal interpretations rather than simply receiving explanations. To bring this to everyday tracking, we present DREAM, an LLM-powered voice assistant that monitors conversational sleep diaries, selectively invites users to interpret meaningful changes, and uses their interpretation to tailor subsequent education. We co-designed DREAM with sleep specialists iteratively and evaluated it in a six-week field study (N=14) against a generic-education control. DREAM participants reported greater personal sleep insight, motivation, and willingness to use the system, and described a clearer rationale for trying strategies. Our findings suggest that guided reflection made participants more active interpreters of their own sleep. Furthermore, we argue that expert involvement is not a single transfer of knowledge but an ongoing process of making tacit judgment explicit and testable.

papers.title: Skill-SLM: Agent Skill-driven Small Language Models for Reliable Robot Operation
papers.authors: Wenhao Wang, Yanyan Li, Jiawei Yuan
papers.abstract: Small language models (SLMs) have been increasingly adopted for onboard robot operation because they enable intelligent decision-making. However, existing approaches are mainly distillation-oriented and rely on enumerating representative task-solution pairs. This makes dataset construction difficult and limits generalization to diverse robot tasks whose possible forms grow rapidly. This paper proposes Skill-SLM, a framework that reformulates SLM-driven robot operation as a task-decomposition and skill-composition problem. Given a natural language task instruction, Skill-SLM decomposes the task into subtasks, selects appropriate skills from the skill library, and orchestrates the selected skills into executable robot operations. First, to support the skill-driven workflow, we propose a novel robot operational skill aware context-free grammar (CFG) to extract the skills required to accomplish tasks and build the skill library accordingly. Then, we configure LLM teachers to induce and synthesize training datasets for the SLMs, enabling SLMs to decompose tasks and orchestrate skills reliably. Additionally, we employ a progressive skill orchestration strategy to improve the reliability of skill implementation and overall robot operation. Experiments on UAV operation tasks indicate that Skill-SLM substantially outperforms distillation-oriented baselines, especially on unseen tasks that require generalization of capabilities. Additional experiments on ground vehicle tasks further demonstrate that Skill-SLM can be applied to different robot platforms.

papers.title: AI-Mediated Self: How HCI Defines and Relates to the Self
papers.authors: Jenny Xiyu Fu, Qian Yang, Malte Friedrich Jung
papers.abstract: How might AI alter how we understand and experience the self? This scoping review analyzes 102 papers to examine how the self is defined in the field of human-computer interaction (HCI), how AI-self relationships are conceptualized, and what risks emerge when AI becomes entangled with selfhood. Our synthesis makes three contributions. First, we define AI-mediated self as a conceptual umbrella that connects dispersed work across education, workplace, health, and creative practices. Second, we consolidate six framings of the self with four domains of ethical risk-agency/autonomy, identity/authorship, relational capacity, and meaning-making-into a conceptual map that provides a reusable vocabulary across contexts. Third, we introduce the Inclusion of AI-Self framework, which situates AI-self relationships along a spectrum of proximity. Together, these contributions position selfhood as a central design space in HCI.

papers.title: What does it mean to use AI critically? Unpacking critical AI literacy through students' evaluation of AI-generated content
papers.authors: Hyejeong Lee, Wonjin Yu
papers.abstract: Although critical AI literacy has emerged as an important educational goal, the construct remains conceptually broad and insufficiently specified for guiding students' day-to-day interactions with AI. This study examines how students critically evaluated AI-generated content. Drawing on an analysis of students' chatbot interactions and written reflections, we first identified seven stages of AI-supported academic task completion and five functional roles assumed by AI. More importantly, we identified eight evaluative lenses that students used to assess AI-generated responses (accuracy, completeness, task alignment/relevance, personalization, practicality, creativity, ethics, and bias). The findings suggest that critical AI literacy extends beyond verifying the factual accuracy of AI-generated information. Rather, critically engaging with AI involves situated and multidimensional judgment about the epistemic quality, contextual fit, practical feasibility, creative value, and ethical implications of AI-generated content. The framework offers both a conceptual contribution to the emerging literature on critical AI literacy and a practical tool for educators seeking to help learners move from passive acceptance of AI toward deliberate, context-sensitive, and responsible human judgment.

papers.title: TacHair: Tactile Contact-Distribution Guided Online Correction for Robotic Hair Stroking and Perception
papers.authors: Ruiyi Hu, Yongqiang Zhao, Daniel Bak, Yupeng Wang, Xuyang Zhang, Shan Luo
papers.abstract: Hair stroking is common in daily grooming and personal care, and is also widely used in hair-product evaluation, motivating robots with similar physical interaction capabilities. Existing robotic hair-care and surface-following methods mainly rely on trajectory planning, compliance, force regulation, or tactile-conditioned policies, but deformable hair can remain in contact while gradually drifting across the end-effector, making local interaction difficult to regulate. We propose TacHair, a tactile contact-distribution guided online correction framework that represents high-resolution tactile observations as a spatial hair-contact distribution. A visuotactile imitation policy generates the nominal stroking motion, while a separately trained residual module corrects local contact deviations, separating task progression from contact recovery. We evaluate TacHair in 525 real-robot trials across five head geometries and three hair conditions. A successful stroke requires both sufficient task progression and contact maintenance; our method improves success from 42.9% to 62.3% and contact maintenance from 59.4% to 88.0% over the same visuotactile policy without correction. These results demonstrate spatial tactile contact distributions as an effective feedback representation for contact-preserving interaction with deformable and visually occluded surfaces. Demos, code, and datasets are available at https://tachair.github.io.

papers.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Mikey Watts, Yuchen Cui
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are strikingly sensitive to instruction phrasing and do not inherit the language robustness of the vision-language models they are built on. A one-word edit can move success by tens of points: $π_{0.5}$ turns on a LIBERO stove 100% of the time for "switch on the stove" and 2% for "switch on the hot plate", and a $π_0$ checkpoint finetuned with rephrase augmentation still shows swings of up to 61 points. We characterize this sensitivity with statistically tested single-edit swings and an oracle phrase search, which shows that phrasing alone nearly closes the 21-point gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks. We then reduce it without modifying the policy. Because the sensitivity is systematic, it can be expressed as explicit rules: we score many phrasings of a few training tasks, have a large language model distill the evidence into ten to twenty rephrasing rules, and at deployment rewrite each incoming instruction once under these rules. The rules improve the frozen $π_0$ by 16 to 27% relative on twelve held-out tasks across adversarial, VLM-generated, and human-generated phrasings, with gains concentrated on out-of-distribution tasks. The pipeline replicates on $π_{0.5}$ and LIBERO, lifting in-finetune success from 93.6% to 97.8%. The method requires no retraining and no per-step verification, and applies zero-shot to unseen tasks and instructions. Project website: https://sttawm.github.io/rephrase-before-you-act

papers.title: SOTA: Stock Options Trading Agents Guided by Option-Implied Return Distributions
papers.authors: Yizhen Xie, Mengyang Liu
papers.abstract: As option markets grow and AI advances, agentic systems for option trading are gaining increasing attention. Language-model-based agents can reason over contextual information such as news, but option trading presents a particularly challenging decision problem: a single stock can have thousands of contracts, and the agent must decide both which contracts to trade and how to combine them. Existing approaches often sidestep this complexity by restricting the policy to a fixed strategy structure, such as a straddle, limiting their ability to switch strategies as market conditions change. We present SOTA (Stock Options Trading Agents), an agentic trading framework for structured option-strategy selection. SOTA abstracts the large option universe into strategy-level decisions while deterministic resolvers handle portfolio implementation. We develop SOTA by post-training Qwen3.8-27B with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. SOTA is evaluated on options on nine large-cap U.S. equities and SPY against rule-based and machine-learning strategy selectors in the same trading environment. Over a six-month out-of-sample period, SOTA earns an 18.3% total return with a Sharpe ratio of 1.60 and a maximum drawdown of 8.96%. We also document an asymmetric role of news: news improves frontier-teacher trajectories, but retaining news during reinforcement learning reduces out-of-sample return from 18.3% to -2.7%.

papers.title: Reasoning-Token Spikes Under Prompted Untruthful Responses in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Maverick Morales, Tomáš Dominik, Vermut Gao, Katrina Shirey, Paulius Rimkevičius, Aaron Schurger, Uri Maoz
papers.abstract: Monitoring the chain-of-thought of reasoning artificial intelligence (AI) models remains a key approach to detecting deception and other forms of misbehavior in such models. However, semantic chain-of-thought monitoring depends on reasoning traces being legible and sufficiently faithful to the underlying computations that produced the model's behavior, not to mention accessible. Moreover, there is increasing evidence that chain-of-thought outputs may soon become illegible or unfaithful, if they even remain accessible. Based on cognitive load theory, we investigate a lower-bandwidth signal--the number of reasoning tokens generated--which does not require access to the content of the reasoning trace. Three reasoning-capable large language models answered 210 multiple-choice questions--across analytic, descriptive, and normative reasoning types as well as moral and non-moral domains--under system prompts instructing them to respond truthfully, falsely, or without regard for truth.
