papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can enhance the quality and visibility of advanced learners’ work while making it harder to determine what the resulting performance reveals about their independent competence. This theoretical paper develops the Relational Epistemic Agency Model for Advanced Learners (REAM-AL) through a structured database search and an integrative synthesis of scholarship on talent development, extended and distributed cognition, cognitive offloading, metacognition, epistemic agency, intellectual ownership, transfer, and assessment validity. The model organizes five focal constructs across four analytical layers: developmental epistemic readiness, cognitive task distribution, epistemic decision distribution, intellectual ownership, and the relationship among supported performance, independent competence, and transfer. Their configuration may produce relational cognitive extension, in which AI broadens thinking while epistemic authority remains with the learner, or developmental substitution, in which the system performs operations the learner is expected to develop. REAM-AL treats these as interaction patterns rather than fixed student categories. It offers a framework for task design and assessment that distinguishes joint human–AI performance from independently sustained and transferable competence. The proposed constructs and relationships remain theoretical and require direct testing with advanced children and adolescents across varied tasks, developmental periods, and AI conditions.

papers.title: An Examination of Mathematics Pre-Service Teachers’ Anxiety Toward Artificial Intelligence and Their Learning Intentions
papers.authors: Rüveyda Döndü Taşbaş, Selin Çenberci
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine pre-service teachers’ intentions and anxiety levels regarding learning about artificial intelligence according to different demographic characteristics and to reveal the relationship between these variables. The sample of the research consists of 205 mathematics pre-service teachers studying in the Department of Mathematics Education at a state university. Students completed two 5-point Likert-type scales, one with 15 items and the other with 16 items, as well as a form containing open-ended questions. The study employed a sequential mixed methods design. As a result of the study, pre-service teachers had a high level of intention to learn about artificial intelligence (AI) and a moderate level of anxiety regarding AI was determined. Additionally, a weak but statistically significant negative correlation was found between learning intention and anxiety. In addition to this, it was concluded that pre-service teachers see artificial intelligence integration as an inevitable professional necessity in their future professional lives; that is, pre-service teachers’ concerns about artificial intelligence do not constitute a major barrier to their learning intentions.

papers.title: Different Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence and Urban Energy Efficiency: Interpretable Machine-Learning Evidence from Chinese Cities
papers.authors: Xiaosong Ren, Bangyan Xing, Guoqiang Zhang
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into urban energy management, but policy attention, innovation capacity, and industry development may contain different information about urban energy efficiency (UEE). This study compares these three AI dimensions within a 15-driver framework using a balanced panel of 279 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2006 to 2023 (5022 city-year observations). UEE is measured with a super-efficiency slacks-based measure model with undesirable outputs. Eight machine-learning algorithms are evaluated through five-fold cross-validation within the training sample, and XGBoost is selected. The model obtains a cross-validated R2 of 0.787 and a random-holdout R2 of 0.822 (RMSE = 0.061; MAE = 0.033). Supplementary city-grouped and chronological tests yield R2 values of 0.801 and 0.809, respectively. Exact TreeSHAP then identifies global importance, regional heterogeneity, nonlinear dependence, and pairwise interactions. AI innovation capacity ranks 10th among all drivers (4.23% of total absolute SHAP), followed by AI industry development (13th; 2.94%) and AI policy attention (15th; 0.82%). AI innovation capacity is particularly important in northeastern China, where it ranks fifth and accounts for 8.78% of regional absolute SHAP. The results indicate that patent activity and enterprise presence receive larger predictive attributions than policy attention within the fitted model. These associations vary with regional and urban conditions and do not establish the effects of AI adoption or policy interventions.

papers.title: Teachers’ Perceptions of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Early Childhood and Primary Education: Barriers, Ethical Concerns, and Perceived Impacts
papers.authors: Juan Luis Cabanillas-García, Desirée Ayuso del Puerto, María Cruz Sánchez Gómez
papers.abstract: The growing integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) into education has intensified the need to understand teachers’ perceptions of its implementation in the early stages of schooling. This study aimed to examine the barriers, ethical concerns, and perceived impact of GAI among Early Childhood and Primary Education teachers in Spain. An interpretive qualitative design was adopted using an open-ended questionnaire completed by 183 teachers from 15 Spanish autonomous communities. Data were analyzed through thematic content analysis in NVivo 14, resulting in a coding framework comprising three metacategories, 27 categories, and 98 subcategories. The findings indicate that insufficient training and limited digital competence constitute the main barriers to GAI integration, while ethical concerns focus primarily on the potential decline in students’ critical thinking, irresponsible use, data privacy, and the reliability of AI-generated information. Although teachers recognize the potential of GAI to support learning, they express greater concern about its possible negative effects on creativity, effort, and autonomous knowledge construction. Moreover, they consistently emphasize that its educational impact depends on teacher training, pedagogical mediation, and the context in which it is implemented. These findings highlight that the successful integration of GAI in Early Childhood and Primary Education requires strengthening teachers’ AI literacy and promoting pedagogically grounded and ethically responsible implementation strategies.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for CRM Operational Efficiency in Retail Banking
papers.authors: Ivana Pavlinić, Maja Martinović, Hrvoje Maljak
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming customer relationship management (CRM) in retail banking by improving customer targeting, campaign execution, and decision-making. This paper examines how AI contributes to CRM operational efficiency through the lens of dynamic capabilities theory (DCT). The study draws on selected banking cases and combines a survey of 340 professionals from financial and non-financial institutions with semi-structured interviews with managers from three major Croatian banks. The findings provide descriptive evidence consistent with all three research hypotheses. More than 80% of respondents from AI-adopting organizations reported improved targeting effectiveness and faster campaign execution, while more than three-quarters reported improvements in AI-supported decision-making. The qualitative findings support these results but also indicate that the benefits depend on data quality, digital infrastructure, CRM integration, employee capabilities, and organizational readiness. The findings correspond most strongly to DCT’s sensing and seizing capabilities, while evidence of broader organizational transformation is less pronounced. For bank managers, the results indicate that investments in AI should be accompanied by strong data governance, integrated systems, employee capabilities, and organizational processes that translate AI-generated insights into action. The paper contributes to the literature by demonstrating that CRM value is created not through AI adoption alone, but through the organizational capabilities required to translate AI-generated insights into operational outcomes.

papers.title: System Hallucination Frequency and Service Failure Recovery in AI-Assisted Heritage Education: Psychological Safety, Collaborative Learning, and Technological Contingencies
papers.authors: Ahmed K. Elnagar, E. Álvarez, Abu Elnasr E. Sobaih, Tamer M. Abdelghani, Ahmed E. Abu Elnasr, Abdallah M. Elshaer
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is finding growing use in heritage education, but system hallucinations can impair learning and service recovery in culturally sensitive settings. The associations of System Hallucination Frequency (SHF) with On-Site Service Failure Recovery Effectiveness (SFRE) are examined through Trainee Psychological Safety (TPS) and Trainee Collaborative Learning Behavior (TCLB), with technological contingencies. Data were collected from 427 university students in Saudi Arabia with experience in AI-supported heritage-related learning using a cross-sectional survey. Structural Equation Modeling indicated that higher perceived SHF was negatively associated with SFRE, TPS, and TCLB, whereas TPS and TCLB were positively associated with recovery effectiveness. TPS and TCLB also showed significant individual and serial indirect associations. Moreover, TCLB and perceived retrieval quality (CRA-TKP) buffered the negative SHF-TPS association, and perceived flagging quality (AGFP-CCN) strengthened the positive TCLB-SFRE association. The results identify associations consistent with the proposed AI-mediated service-recovery model and offer practical guidance for designing reliable and culturally sensitive AI-supported heritage education systems.

papers.title: A multidimensional analysis of generative AI adoption in academia: synthesizing TAM3 and UTAUT2 frameworks to predict students’ attitudes and learning effectiveness
papers.authors: Golan Carmi
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools into higher education raises important questions regarding their impact on student learning. Based on established technology acceptance frameworks, this study develops and empirically tests an integrative model that explains students' attitudes toward GenAI tools and their perceived learning effectiveness. Data were collected from 566 undergraduate students using a structured questionnaire. The main findings indicate that prior experience, perceived merits, and training in using GenAI tools are positively associated with and constitute strong predictors of both attitudes of students toward GenAI use and perceived learning effectiveness, while ethical knowledge and technological orientation do not emerge as significant predictors. Perceived drawbacks are also significant, suggesting that ambivalence and concerns about GenAI can diminish students' positive attitudes and reduce their perceived usefulness. Differences across gender further suggest that technology adoption processes are not uniform but contingent upon user characteristics. Theoretically, this study contributes to the literature by extending technology acceptance models into the domain of GenAI and by linking attitudinal constructs with learning-related outcomes within a unified framework. Practically, the findings suggest that higher education institutions should not only provide access to GenAI tools but also complement this access with pedagogical support, including structured training, comprehensive ethical guidance, and the development of students' GenAI literacy. Overall, the study provides a nuanced understanding of how GenAI tools are adopted and leveraged in academic contexts and offers a foundation for future research on GenAI-enabled learning.

papers.title: Footprint to prediction: low-cost, three-class foot arch screening using a Harris mat
papers.authors: Hariprasad Ramachandran, Srivardan Balu, Kaushik Ramakrishna Haran, Sanjay Murugan Selvi, Sharmila Nageswaran
papers.abstract: Arch type foot pathologies of Pes Cavus (high arch), Pes Planus (flatfoot), and Normal Arch patterns are good predictors of foot health that affect gait, posture, and predispose to musculoskeletal disorders. The research work described herein advances a computer-assisted automated classification of the foot arch from footprint images obtained on the Harris mat and transformed into contact-area visualizations through image processing, then classified using machine learning approaches, including a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based model with MobileNetV2 and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) baseline for comparison. The system's performance was validated on a dataset of 106 footprint impressions collected from 53 healthy young university students. The training set was subsequently augmented to 300 images, while evaluation was performed on 22 held-out original (non-augmented) images. The total accuracy for the CNN model was 77.3%, with an F1-score by class of 0.78 for Pes Cavus, 0.92 for Pes Planus, and 0.62 for Normal Arch. Precision values were 0.70 (Pes Cavus), 0.86 (Pes Planus), and 0.80 (Normal Arch), and recall values were 0.88, 1.00, and 0.50, respectively. The SVM model had an accuracy of 54.6%. Cohen's Kappa of 0.658 indicated substantial agreement between model predictions and reference labels, and ROC analysis showed promising classification performance within the evaluated dataset, with AUC estimates of 0.848 for Pes Cavus, 0.990 for Pes Planus, and 0.830 for Normal Arch.

papers.title: Musculoskeletal symptoms and biopsychosocial factors among nursing students: implications for protecting the future health workforce
papers.authors: Kübra Okuyucu, İbrahim Topuz, Gözde Yıldız DAŞ GEÇİM
papers.abstract: Background Musculoskeletal disorders are an important occupational health concern among healthcare professionals and may emerge before entry into the workforce. Identifying musculoskeletal symptoms and their biopsychosocial correlates among nursing students may provide opportunities for early prevention and health promotion. Objective This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of musculoskeletal symptoms and identify associated biopsychosocial factors among nursing students in Türkiye. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 213 nursing students (77% female) in Türkiye. Data were collected through an online survey between February and April 2022. Musculoskeletal symptoms, physical activity, perceived stress, biopsychosocial wellbeing, and coping behaviors were assessed using validated instruments. Associations were examined using chi-square tests and independent-samples t -tests; logistic regression analyses, using a simplified set of six predictors (age, BMI, gender, physical activity, total perceived stress, and total biopsychosocial response score) and Firth's penalized-likelihood method, were performed to identify factors associated with musculoskeletal symptoms. Results Overall, 62% of nursing students reported musculoskeletal symptoms during the previous 12 months. The most frequently reported symptoms were in the upper back (41%), followed by the low back and neck (33% each). High physical activity showed a significant association with lower odds of upper back symptoms (OR = 0.19, p = 0.047) and a borderline association with lower odds of any 12-month musculoskeletal symptom (OR = 0.25, p = 0.060). Female students had higher odds of neck, shoulder, and upper back symptoms than male students (OR = 0.05–0.19 for male vs. female). No stress or biopsychosocial measure was significantly associated with any 12-month musculoskeletal outcome; findings for the hip/thigh region should be considered exploratory given a low events-per-variable ratio. Conclusions Musculoskeletal symptoms were highly prevalent among nursing students, highlighting the importance of addressing musculoskeletal health before entry into the nursing workforce. The findings suggest that physical factors may be more relevant to symptom occurrence than stress or biopsychosocial wellbeing in this sample. Although a biopsychosocial framework provides a useful perspective for understanding musculoskeletal health, further longitudinal research is needed to clarify the role of stress and wellbeing and to inform targeted interventions.

papers.title: Family and community pressure, obesity-related behaviours, and psychological wellbeing among female adolescents with overweight or obesity: a qualitative study
papers.authors: Abeer Ahmad Bahathig, Nasser S. Alqahtani
papers.abstract: Background Adolescent obesity has physical, psychological and social consequences. Family and community influences can be important in determining the eating behaviour, body image and emotional health of adolescents. Few qualitative studies have investigated female adolescents’ own perception of family and community related pressure around their weight. Methods This qualitative exploratory study used semi-structured interviews to investigate these experiences among 30 female adolescents aged 12–19 years (mean 16.3 years) with overweight or obesity. Weight status was classified against the WHO 2007 BMI-for-age reference. The study covered eating behaviour, criticism, emotional impact, and perceived approaches to managing obesity. Data were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. Results Seventeen participants (57%) met WHO criteria for obesity and 13 (43%) for overweight. Four themes emerged: (1) a conflicted relationship with food, characterised by dieting, restrained eating, and a cycle of restriction followed by overeating ( n = 16); (2) experiences of criticism from parents, family members and the wider community ( n = 20), most commonly around appearance and health; (3) psychological and life-choice implications, including self-consciousness and embarrassment ( n = 25), low self-esteem, social withdrawal, and concerns about clothing, autonomy and future marriage ( n = 22); and (4) motivation and perceived strategies for obesity management, including healthy eating, dieting, exercise, and medical interventions. Negative comments were mostly reported as unwelcome, whereas positive and health-related comments were reported as motivating. Conclusion Pressure from family and community is a key component in how female adolescents with overweight or obesity perceive their weight, influencing behaviour, emotions, and social functioning. Obesity interventions should incorporate mental health, stigma reduction, and support for constructive family and community communication, alongside weight management.

papers.title: Generative adversarial network-based creative synthesis and AI art creation in children’s art education: effects on health promotion
papers.authors: Jing Chen, Yang Zhang, Hui Liu
papers.abstract: Background The existing research on children’s art education still has shortcomings in the field of artificial intelligence creation support and lacks an exclusive generation model and systematic evaluation framework that takes into account the characteristics of children’s cognitive development and physical and mental health needs, which limits the practical application of digital aesthetic education in children’s health promotion. Based on the development law of children’s aesthetic cognition and the needs of mental health promotion, this study constructs an artificial intelligence (AI) generation model for children’s artistic creation. By integrating children’s figurative thinking characteristics, creativity development laws and emotional expression needs, it realises accurate support for children’s artistic creation process. At the same time, a multi-dimensional evaluation system covering creativity, aesthetic literacy, mental health, visual health and social development is established to systematically evaluate the impact of AI-assisted aesthetic education on children’s comprehensive health development so as to provide a theoretical basis and practical reference for children’s health-orientated digital aesthetic education model. Methods From July 2025 to December 2025, 120 children aged 6–14 (divided into three developmental levels: 6–8, 9–11, and 12–14) were selected for a 12-week controlled intervention experiment, and the experimental group (AI man–machine collaborative aesthetic education, using the optimised children-specific improved WGAN-GP creative synthesis model) was set up. In this study, a quasi-experimental design was adopted, and the intervention effect was inferred by the correlation between groups and the changes within groups, without strict causal attribution. In the statistical analysis, age is taken as a covariate into the ANCOVA model, and hierarchical subgroup analysis is carried out according to age levels to test the potential influence of age on the main results. Multidimensional statistical methods such as the independent sample t -test, paired sample t -test, two-factor repeated measurement variance analysis, one-way covariance analysis (ANCOVA) with age as a covariate, Pearson correlation analysis, intra-group correlation coefficient (ICC), standardised mean difference (SMD), and determination coefficient (r) were used. Through the Torrance Creative Thinking Test (TTCT), the self-made Children’s Artistic Aesthetic Literacy Rating Scale, which has been systematically developed and verified by reliability and validity, the generated image quality evaluation system, the Children’s Depression and Anxiety Scale (SCARED), the Children’s Perceived Stress Scale (CPSS), the visual fatigue score, the children’s social expression health scale, the naked eye vision difference and the resting heart rate, the multi-dimensional indicators, the observed image quality evaluation system was generated. All health scales are marked with the applicable age range, and the standardised testing procedures of picture-assisted and item-by-item reading are adopted for children aged 6–8, and the boundaries of adult assistance are defined. Results Compared with the control group, the Fréchet dIStance (FID) of the experimental group is 21.15 ± 1.31, the inception score (IS) is 2.87 ± 0.16, and the anti-loss convergence rate is increased by 29.7%, so the model has excellent stability. The results of interpersonal intervention showed that the creativity fluency (79.68 ± 5.82), flexibility (77.35 ± 5.41), and uniqueness (75.46 ± 5.73) of the experimental group were significantly better than those of the control group (67.52 ± 5.13, 65.94 ± 4.87, and 63.15 ± 5.23). After controlling the age covariate, the difference between groups remained significant ( f value ranged from 87.32 to 156.48, all p < 0.001), and the main effect of age was significant in some indexes but did not change the intervention direction. The scores of aesthetic perception, color matching, and composition creativity in the experimental group (84.36 ± 3.81) were significantly higher than those in the control group (66.28 ± 4.53), in which the scores of works with AI assistance and works without AI were reported separately to distinguish the quality of AI-assisted output from children’s independent aesthetic ability. The scores of anxiety (12.35 ± 2.11), perceived stress (9.62 ± 1.87), and visual fatigue (2.14 ± 0.63) in the experimental group were significantly lower than those in the control group (21.76 ± 3.42, 17.53 ± 2.69, and 4.89 ± 0.92). The fluctuation difference of naked-eye vision after class was 0.12/0.05 in the experimental group and 0.25/0.08 in the control group ( p < 0.01). 5 mins after class, the resting heart rate was 77.93 ± 5.26 beats/min in the experimental group and 86.71 ± 6.22 beats/min in the control group ( p < 0.01). The score of social health expression (87.41 3.65) was significantly higher than that of the control group (64.33 4.17), and the difference of all health indicators among groups was p < 0.001. The score consistency within the group was ICC = 0.84 ( p < 0.001), and the intervention effect amount SMD = 0.68, which was a large-effect positive intervention. Pearson correlation analysis shows that children’s participation in AI creation is highly positively correlated with the quality of creative output ( r = 0.812, p < 0.001), which is a cross-sectional correlation and does not constitute causal inference. Tool familiarity, personal preference, and exploration behavior may be potential confounding factors. Stratified subgroups showed that children with high anxiety and stress at baseline had the greatest improvement. Conclusion This study shows that the optimized creative synthesis model of the generation confrontation network can adapt to children’s artistic creation thinking, and the improvement of creative thinking and aesthetic quality is observed in both AI-assisted creation and children’s independent creation, accompanied by the reduction of anxiety, psychological pressure, and visual fatigue and the improvement of social expression level. In view of the quasi-experimental design and limited sample size of this study, the above results should be understood as intervention correlation rather than strict causal effect, and the performance of works under AI-assisted conditions should not be directly equivalent to children’s independent aesthetic ability. This study provides a preliminary empirical basis for the scientific and standardized development of digital children’s health aesthetic education.

papers.title: Achievement emotions in AI-assisted learning, academic self-efficacy, and learning engagement and AI dependence among university students in statistics-related programs: a moderated mediation study
papers.authors: Huijuan Qin, Kun Liu
papers.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools have become part of everyday coursework for university students, yet the emotional and motivational conditions under which these tools support or undermine learning remain poorly understood. Drawing on the control-value theory of achievement emotions, this study examined whether academic self-efficacy mediates the links of positive achievement emotions in AI-assisted learning with learning engagement and AI dependence, and whether AI literacy moderates the first stage of these pathways. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 700 undergraduate students (386 female; M_age = 19.81 years, SD = 1.27) majoring in applied statistics and related programs at three universities in Shijiazhuang, China. Participants completed measures of positive and negative achievement emotions, academic self-efficacy, learning engagement, AI dependence, and AI literacy. Confirmatory factor analysis preceded a first-stage moderated mediation analysis with bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals (5,000 resamples), controlling for negative emotions, gender, and year of study. Results The six-factor measurement model fitted the data well, χ 2 (50) = 55.62, p = 0.271, CFI = 0.998, RMSEA = 0.013, SRMR = 0.017. Positive achievement emotions predicted higher self-efficacy ( β = 0.374), which in turn predicted stronger engagement ( β = 0.395) and lower AI dependence ( β = −0.176), all p < 0.001, with AI literacy entered in every equation. AI literacy moderated the emotion-efficacy association ( β = 0.152, p < 0.001): the conditional indirect association with engagement rose from 0.088 to 0.208 across ±1 SD of AI literacy, and that with AI dependence fell from −0.039 to −0.093. The direct association with AI dependence was positive ( β = 0.447, p < 0.001), and the conditional total association remained positive (0.355 to 0.408). Both indexes of moderated mediation were significant. Conclusion Positive emotional experiences in AI-assisted coursework show beneficial and costly associations simultaneously, and self-efficacy statistically accounts for opposing parts of each. The total association with dependence remained positive at all literacy levels, so the results describe inconsistent mediation rather than protection. AI literacy marks where the emotion-engagement pathway is strongest.

papers.title: GenAI-supported project-based product design learning: differential changes in multidimensional learning outcomes
papers.authors: Yizhou Chen, Yingqi Zhao, Kenny S L Cheah, Nur Yuhanis Mohd Nasir
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in design education, yet evidence remains limited on whether its educational value derives from tool access itself or from how human–AI interaction is structured within project work. This quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test study compared a 4-week GenAI-Integrated Project-Based Learning Module (GIPLM) with traditional project-based learning (PjBL) in an undergraduate product design course ( N = 60). Rather than treating GenAI as a stand-alone content-generation tool, GIPLM embedded GenAI as process scaffolding across four stages: product and requirement analysis, user research and knowledge structuring, ideation with multimodal visualization and 3D prototyping, and feedback, validation, and reflective presentation. Learning outcomes were assessed across cognitive, affective, and psychomotor-related domains, together with course performance. According to a mixed-design ANOVA, the GenAI-supported group was associated with significantly greater gains than the control group in cognitive understanding, problem-solving and creativity, fundamental tool operation, advanced design application, and final academic performance. Because advanced design application differed at baseline, ANCOVA was additionally conducted; the post-test group effect remained significant after controlling for pre-test scores, F (1, 57) = 20.519, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.265. Engagement and participation and ethical and user-centered responsibility improved over time but showed no significant Time × Group interactions. These findings suggest that the observed advantages are more consistent with structured, workflow-embedded GenAI scaffolding than with AI access alone, with stronger short-term effects on cognitive, procedural, and performance outcomes than on affective development.

papers.title: Psychological associations between perceived generative AI-supported learning and creative design performance in vocational design education: a within-course correlational study
papers.authors: Xu Xiaoping, Wang Chenhui, 傅双燕, Jiawei Tong, Dian Jin
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in design courses, but evidence remains limited on how students’ appraisal of such support co-varies with domain cognition, creative confidence, engagement, and independently assessed creative work. This within-course correlational study examined within-course change and theory-specified contemporaneous associations in a 72-h Furniture Appreciation and Selection course involving 150 vocational design students in China. Sustainable design cognition and creative self-efficacy were measured before and after the course; perceived GenAI-supported learning and learning engagement were measured after it; and final creative design performance was rated independently by three experts. Paired-samples t tests described within-course change. Item-level CFA preceded the score-level association analyses, while standardized composite-score ordinary least squares models and 10,000-resample percentile bootstrap confidence intervals summarized theory-specified post-course associations and coefficient products. Sustainable design cognition increased from 3.326 to 3.792, t (149) = 10.362, p < 0.001, d z = 0.846, and creative self-efficacy increased from 3.509 to 3.877, t (149) = 7.424, p < 0.001, d z = 0.606; these values indicate change during the course as a whole rather than a GenAI-specific intervention effect. Among the direct post-course associations, learning engagement showed the largest coefficient with expert-rated creative design performance (β = 0.515, p < 0.001; f 2 = 0.361). The theory-specified coefficient products were 0.076 for SDC-CSE-LE, 0.204 for CSE-LE-CP, and 0.0080 for AISL-SDC-CSE-LE-CP. The last interval narrowly excluded zero [0.0002, 0.0234], but the product was statistically detectable and negligible in magnitude. Because the study followed one cohort without a comparison condition and most model variables were measured at the same post-course occasion, the findings support within-course change and contemporaneous association, not causal or temporally ordered effects.

papers.title: Can users trust AI doctors? Unpacking the dual credibility pathways linking AI chatbot use to AI health advice adherence intention
papers.authors: Zhanyou Wang, Jingru Wang, Dongmei Han, Liang Ma, Feifei Hao
papers.abstract: With the rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare, AI doctor chatbots have emerged as increasingly prevalent tools for health information acquisition and health management. However, existing research has paid insufficient attention to how AI doctor utilization is associated with AI healthcare users' credibility judgments and subsequent AI health advice adherence intention. To address this research gap, this study examines the relationship between AI doctor utilization and AI health advice adherence intention, with a particular focus on the mediating roles of perceived honesty and ability credibility, as well as the moderating role of anxiety sensitivity. A questionnaire survey was conducted among participants from various regions of China, and 224 valid responses were retained after data cleaning. SmartPLS 4.0 was used for data analysis. The results show that AI doctor utilization is significantly and positively associated with both perceived honesty and ability credibility, which, in turn, are positively associated with AI health advice adherence intention. Additionally, perceived honesty and ability credibility play mediating roles in the relationship between AI doctor utilization and AI health advice adherence intention. Regarding the moderating effect, anxiety sensitivity negatively moderates the relationship between perceived honesty and AI health advice adherence intention, while positively moderating the relationship between ability credibility and AI health advice adherence intention. These findings provide nuanced insights for designing anxiety-sensitive AI healthcare services by tailoring credibility cues to users' psychological characteristics and promoting appropriate reliance on AI-generated health advice.

papers.title: When AI translations fall flat: embodied simulation and effort in cross-language reading
papers.authors: Zeli Liu
papers.abstract: Common machine translation evaluation metrics, such as the Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) and Crosslingual Optimized Metric for Evaluation of Translation (COMET) are reliable measures of propositional fidelity and surface fluency but systematically ignore the embodied texture of reading, leaving unexplained why high-scoring AI translations still feel flat to readers despite formal accuracy. The Embodied Translation Quality Assessment (E-TQA) framework was developed based on embodied cognition theory to operationalize three key dimensions of cross-language comprehension: sensorimotor simulation, affective-cultural resonance, and processing friction. To validate this framework, a counterbalanced Latin-square design was employed with 192 English-major participants. Six literary and culturally loaded excerpts were each presented in three rigorously matched conditions. Published professional human translations, and translations from DeepSeek and ChatGPT, with all versions controlled for BLEU (±1.2 points) and COMET (±0.04 points) to isolate embodied variation from semantic equivalence. Participants completed the Self-Assessment Manikin and E-TQA scales after each excerpt, and data were analyzed via linear mixed-effects models, reporting partial η 2 as effect size. Human texts were consistently rated higher than both AI conditions in sensorimotor imagery, affective resonance, valence, and arousal, whereas AI texts were rated much higher in phenomenological flatness and cognitive effort. All critical indices showed medium to large effect sizes (η p 2 = 0.15–0.35) and were consistent across educational levels and text genres. These results offer evidence for a dissociation of propositional accuracy and embodied richness, showing that the E-TQA framework accounts for unique variance in reader experience beyond that explained by standard computational metrics. The work advances translation quality assessment by centering embodied cognition, provides a psychometrically sound complement to existing tools, and motivates future multimodal investigations of cross-language processing mechanisms.

papers.title: Toward a cognitive framework of expert singing-voice evaluation in bel canto pedagogy: a longitudinal exploratory study
papers.authors: Kyoko Ikeda, Michiko Yamaguchi, 朱実 小畑, Tomohiro Tani, Yasuki Yamashita, Taisei Terauchi, 隆 永井, Yuko Mesuda, Mizue Kayama
papers.abstract: Classical singing pedagogy relies on expert judgments that integrate auditory-perceptual cues, embodied pedagogical knowledge, and specialized evaluative language. This exploratory, longitudinal study proposes a cognitive framework, centered on Polanyi's concept of tacit knowledge, for describing how experienced bel canto pedagogues perceive singing-voice development from a brief excerpt. Twenty female soprano students (7 music-education, 13 vocal-performance majors) sang the word 'tanto' from Caro mio ben at university entry (Z1) and after 2 years of instruction (Z2). Four professional singers and voice pedagogues, blind to institutional affiliation, rated perceived development on a 0-2 scale and selected evaluative terms from a 27-item Italian pedagogical vocabulary; median ratings, rather than the mean of an even number of raters, served as the primary outcome. Acoustic analysis proceeded in two exploratory, descriptive stages. First, the singer's-formant ratio (SFR) and a Q-value index were compared with a pedagogical reference recording (M2025) using path-length-normalized dynamic time warping. Movement toward M2025 did not correspond consistently with expert ratings: several students whose SFR/Q-value profiles moved toward M2025 received low or zero median ratings (e.g., E06, E07, V07), whereas six students whose profiles moved away from M2025 on both indices received high median ratings of 1.5-2 (E02, E05, V01, V02, V03, V06). Second, changes in alpha ratio, H1-H2, spectral centroid, smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS), and singing power ratio (SPR) were examined descriptively alongside participants' evaluative terms, without regression or machine-learning modeling, given the small, non-random sample. Case-level analysis indicates that experts attended to qualitatively different cues depending on what they heard in a given voice-e.g., basic, mouth-opening- and resonance-related terms (S07, R02) versus depth- and vibrato-related terms (R10, S09)-independent of institutional cohort. We propose a Polanyi-centered interpretive framework in which candidate acoustic correlates, the 27 evaluative terms (understood, after Vygotsky, as mediating cultural-linguistic tools), and Dreyfus-and-Dreyfus-informed developmental sensitivity jointly, but only partially, illuminate the focal judgment that pedagogically meaningful development has occurred. The framework is hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory; no predictive or inferential claims are made about the acoustic determinants of expert judgment.

papers.title: Social cognitive communication mechanism of digital participation in Chinese traditional music in the context of cultural identity and intangible cultural heritage
papers.authors: Tingting Kuai, Jing Qian, Wei Xu
papers.abstract: Digital platforms have reshaped how traditional Chinese music circulates, yet the psychological mechanism linking user participation to cultural identification remains undertheorized. Drawing together social cognitive theory, contemporary cultural psychology, and communication theory, this study develops a four-layer architecture (input, participation, cognitive, and identity) coupled with a staged process model spanning information encoding, symbolic decoding, cognitive reconstruction, and identity internalization. A hybrid specification formalizes the mechanism, pairing structural equation modeling with attention-weighted neural aggregation; both components are estimated and validated on the same data. Empirical testing draws on 2,346 behavioral records from music, short-form video, and social media platforms, paired with 1,128 survey responses from users engaged with the guqin, Kunqu, pipa, and regional opera repertoires. Item loadings, heterotrait-monotrait ratios, collinearity diagnostics, and a common-method check document measurement quality. Results indicate that digital participation (DP) shapes cultural identity (CI) mainly through social cognitive communication (SCC), with the co-creation and dissemination strata showing indirect effects that are more than three times those of passive exposure. As the direct participation-identity path remains significant, the pattern is one of partial rather than full mediation. Cultural identity also looks more like a hinge than a terminal state: a chained specification linking identification to downstream cognitive engagement returns a reliable indirect path, which is consistent with the recursive reading the framework proposes but, on single-wave evidence, cannot establish it. Community climate exerts the strongest moderating influence, exceeding both platform affordance and content polish. Since the design is cross-sectional, all of these patterns are read as associations rather than as causal effects; even so, they suggest that audience cultivation and co-creation tooling deserve at least as much investment as interface refinement in the digitization of traditional music.

papers.title: Teachers’ self-regulated learning profiles in artificial intelligence contexts: implications for differentiated professional development
papers.authors: Yuhao Su, Mustafa Alpsülün, Müge VURAN, Hasan Celal Balıkçı, M. Barut
papers.abstract: Introduction: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education requires teachers to develop new competencies and manage their own learning. While research has examined teachers' AI attitudes, acceptance, and literacy, less is known about how they regulate their learning in AI contexts. This study examined teachers' self-regulated learning (SRL) profiles and their associations with demographic characteristics and AI-related experience. Methods: In a descriptive survey, 213 in-service teachers completed the Artificial Intelligence Self-Regulated Learning Scale for Teachers (AI-SRLS). Two-Step Cluster Analysis was conducted using five dimensions: task planning, self-monitoring, help seeking, institutional support, and self-evaluation. Results: Two profiles emerged: High Strategic Learners, who scored consistently higher across all five dimensions, and Limited Strategy Users, who reported comparatively lower strategy use. Profile membership was significantly associated with prior AI experience and AI-related training. Gender, age, and professional experience did not significantly differentiate the profiles. Discussion: Teachers' AI-related SRL strategies co-occur in distinct profiles, supporting a differentiated approach to professional development. Teachers with limited strategy use may benefit from structured guidance, scaffolded AI learning opportunities, and stronger institutional support, while highly strategic learners may benefit from more autonomous and advanced learning opportunities.

papers.title: Textbook, multimedia, and generative AI in elementary English learning: usage patterns and family-reported evaluations
papers.authors: Lu Sun, XiaCheng Song, Jing Jin, Min Dai, Huafeng Qu, Xiqiong Yi, Huirong Huang
papers.abstract: Introduction This study examined how often elementary-school learners used textbooks, multimedia resources, and generative AI tools and how these modalities were evaluated by family respondents. Methods A non-probability, teacher-mediated online survey yielded 987 consented responses from multiple sites in mainland China. Respondents rated usage frequency and 15 evaluation items crossing five dimensions with three modalities. Results Textbooks were used most frequently and received the most favorable ratings. After applying a single-step multivariate-t adjustment to each family of three within-dimension contrasts, multimedia and AI differed reliably only for enjoyment in the full sample. The original three-modality confirmatory model had poor absolute fit (RMSEA = 0.151). A crossed dimension-by-modality model improved fit (RMSEA = 0.067) but produced a negative residual variance and was therefore inadmissible; latent achievement regression was not retained. In the primary proportional-odds model using observed modality scores and categorical controls, textbook evaluation was positively associated with family-reported achievement band ( b = 0.343, OR = 1.409, p < 0.001), whereas multimedia ( p = 0.085) and AI ( p = 0.808) were not. Discussion These cross-sectional associations describe this teacher-mediated convenience sample and do not establish modality effects on achievement.

papers.title: Glycosides of Cistanche improve cognitive dysfunction in sleep-deprived model rats by activating the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway
papers.authors: Qiang Li, ShiJun Zhao, Jiaojiao Huo, Yingzhen Wang, Yihong Sun, Jianxin Jia
papers.abstract: Objective Sleep deprivation suppresses the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway, leading to oxidative stress, synaptic damage, and cognitive dysfunction. Glycosides of Cistanche (GCs) possess well-documented antioxidant and neuroprotective properties and have been reported to improve cognition in sleep-deprived animals, but the molecular mechanism remains unclear. We hypothesized that GCs alleviate sleep deprivation-induced cognitive dysfunction by activating the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway. Methods Sixty male Sprague Dawley rats were randomly assigned to six groups ( n = 10): Control, Platform, Model, GCs, Control+GCs, and Estazolam (Est) groups. A 21-day sleep deprivation model was established using the modified multiple platform water method. Assessments included cognitive function by Morris water maze (MWM) test; Wake, non-rapid eye movement (NREM), rapid eye movement (REM), and total sleep time (TST) by Electroencephalogram (EEG); the serum levels of MDA, GSH-Px and SOD by ELISA, hippocampal CA1 neuronal morphology structure by Nissl staining and transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway and synaptic related proteins were detected by Western blot. In an additional cohort ( n = 40), the SIRT1-specific inhibitor EX527 was used to validate the causal role of the pathway. Results Compared with the Control group, the Model group exhibited significantly prolonged escape latency, along with reduced the number of platform crossings and the percentage time in the target quadrant ( p < 0.05). The proportion of Wake significantly increased, while NREM, REM, and TST all significantly decreased (all p < 0.01). The serum level of MDA elevated, while GSH-Px and SOD activities markedly reduced (all p < 0.01). Hippocampal CA1 neurons showed disorganized arrangement, decreased Nissl bodies, and mitochondrial damage. Moreover, the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway and synaptic related proteins significantly downregulated (all p < 0.01). Nevertheless, GCs intervention ameliorated cognitive dysfunction, alleviated oxidative stress and neuronal damage, and upregulated the protein expression levels above mentioned (all p < 0.01). Notably, these protective effects of GCs were abrogated by the SIRT1 inhibitor EX527. Conclusion GCs inhibited oxidative stress damage and improved synaptic plasticity, and thereby alleviated sleep deprivation induced cognitive dysfunction by activating the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway.

papers.title: Natural language processing for suicidal behavior detection in short Spanish clinical notes from first-contact interviews
papers.authors: Juan Carlos Villagomez-Garcia, Juan Martínez-Miranda, Ansel Y. Rodríguez‐González
papers.abstract: Introduction Suicide is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by social, cultural, biological, and psychological factors, whose early detection remains challenging. According to the World Health Organization, suicide is the third leading cause of death among individuals aged 15–29 years, representing a major public health concern for young populations worldwide. In first-contact clinical settings, screening opportunities are often constrained by limited time, sparse patient information, and operational workflows. This study evaluates the feasibility of detecting suicidal behavior from short Spanish-language texts collected during initial screening interviews. Methods The dataset comprises 374 anonymized records labeled as “no suicidal behavior,” “ideation,” “planning,” or “attempt,” with a strong imbalance toward “attempt,” reflecting operational clinical usage rather than population-representative sampling. To address data scarcity, we applied data augmentation methods (Easy Data Augmentation for Spanish, backtranslation, and large language model-based synthesis), validated through statistical analysis and clinician-based plausibility assessments. Results Exploratory analyses revealed highly constrained and overlapping lexical patterns across classes, indicating the challenging nature of the task. A Support Vector Machine achieved 0.53 macro F 1 in binary classification (“suicidal behavior” vs. “no behavior”), while BETO, a Spanish BERT model, reached 0.36 macro F 1 in multiclass classification. Under the same text-only conditions, human specialists achieved macro F 1 scores of 0.29 and 0.15 respectively; however, these results were based on only 20 real texts evaluated with double annotation across five specialists and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. Discussion Although performance is modest compared to studies using full clinical records, these findings suggest that short-text machine learning could support nonspecialists in first-contact settings. Future work should expand datasets and explore multimodal approaches, including voice and text, to improve clinical applicability and early detection.

papers.title: Deep brain stimulation and spinal cord stimulation for chronic disorders of consciousness: a decade of clinical evidence, mechanistic insights, and critical appraisal
papers.authors: Dongsheng Liu, Kai Yang, Jianlei An, Sipeng Zhu, Yitong Jia, Yichen Zhou, Yong Wang, Weihua Cheng, Kaihan Jiang, Yi Yang, Shaoya Yin, Lei Liu
papers.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) and spinal cord stimulation (SCS) have been investigated for over four decades as neuromodulatory treatments for chronic disorders of consciousness (DOC), including the vegetative state/unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (VS/UWS) and the minimally conscious state (MCS), for which no disease-modifying pharmacological therapy exists. This narrative review synthesizes literature published between 2016 and 2026 on the neurobiological rationale, clinical evidence, neurophysiological biomarkers, and safety of DBS and SCS for chronic DOC. The 'mesocircuit hypothesis', supported by human intraoperative electrophysiology and nonhuman primate causal manipulation, provides a coherent rationale for central thalamic and centromedian-parafascicular targeting. Across case series, cohort studies, and individual patient data meta-analyses, both DBS and SCS produce clinically meaningful improvement in a minority of patients, consistently more often in MCS (63-74% response) than in VS/UWS (26-30% response), with younger age and shorter injury-to-treatment interval predicting better outcomes. However, the two largest individual patient data meta-analyses of DBS concur that current evidence is insufficient to conclude that stimulation alters the natural history of neurological recovery beyond what would be expected from patient selection and spontaneous recovery, and adverse event rates (8.1% for SCS, 18.2% for DBS) indicate non-trivial surgical risk in this vulnerable population. Neurophysiological and neuroimaging biomarkers derived from EEG, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, functional MRI, and FDG-PET show promise for objective outcome prediction but await prospective validation. We conclude that DBS and SCS remain experimental, mechanistically motivated but not yet definitively proven therapies for chronic DOC, and that adequately powered randomized controlled trials, biomarker-guided patient selection, and dedicated ethical frameworks are needed before either modality can be recommended outside of research settings.

papers.title: Graded multisensory neurofeedback via the iNems system for comprehensive upper limb recovery after stroke: a multiple baseline study
papers.authors: Takayuki Kodama, Ken Kitai, Yasuhisa Mizomoto, Kaichi Nishigaya, Shoutarou Hashimoto, Riona Hiraga, Satomi Shimizu, Miki Kawabata, Yuumi Hirabayashi, Keita Ikesue, Hazime Kako, Syouta Yasui, Hiroki Ito, Kazuhei Nishimoto, Osamu Katayama, Hideaki Yamaguchi, Hikaru Nagano, Mari Inoue, Shin Murata, Kiichiro Morita
papers.abstract: Introduction: Post-stroke upper-limb recovery remains challenging, especially in the presence of sensory impairments. Conventional brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are constrained by binary feedback, single-modality stimulation, and exclusion of patients with sensory deficits. We developed the Imagery Neurofeedback-based Multi-sensory System (iNems), a neurofeedback system that provides graded multisensory (visual and electrical) feedback based on ERD magnitude. This study validated iNems' efficacy in motor function, self-reported numbness, and cognitive functions using a multiple-baseline design (MBD). Methods: Four participants with post-stroke upper-limb motor and sensory impairments underwent a multiple baseline design. The baseline phase (phase A) used random feedback; the intervention (phase B) used adaptive iNems. iNems quantified motor intention via sensorimotor EEG event-related desynchronization (ERD) and delivered graded visual and electrical feedback. Primary outcomes were the Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) and Box and Block Test (BBT). Secondary outcomes included body cognition, numbness, and neurophysiological (ERD/ERS) changes. Results: All participants demonstrated significant improvement during the intervention. FMA-UE increased by 6-16 points. The BBT showed large effects (integrated Tau-U = 0.75). Body cognition improved significantly in both sense of agency (Tau-U = 0.80) and ownership (Tau-U = 0.89). Numbness was reduced in affected cases (Tau-U = -0.85). Neurophysiological changes correlated with functional gains, with some patterns suggesting increased neural efficiency. Conclusion: This first MBD-validated demonstration shows that graded, multisensory graded neurofeedback based on ERD magnitude can improve motor, self-reported numbness, and cognitive domains after stroke. These findings support adaptive closed-loop therapy as a promising, multifaceted rehabilitation strategy.

papers.title: Reward positivity and affective functioning in early childhood: evidence from temporospatial principal components analysis
papers.authors: Yu Sun Chung, Armen Bagdasarov, Michael Santo Gaffrey
papers.abstract: Reward-related Positivity (RewP) indexes neural sensitivity to reward feedback and has been widely studied in adolescents and adults. However, little is known about how individual differences in RewP are associated with emotional functioning during early childhood, a critical period for affective development. Interpretation of feedback-related ERPs in children is further complicated by temporally overlapping components. This study examined whether a principal component analysis (PCA)-derived RewP is associated with affective functioning in children aged 4-7 years. Electroencephalography was recorded from 140 children during an age-appropriate reward task. Temporospatial PCA was performed on the full EEG sample ( n = 140), and primary regression analyses were conducted in the subset with complete covariate data ( n = 48). Temporospatial PCA was applied to isolate a RewP component differentiating gain from loss feedback. Positive and negative affect were assessed using the child version of the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule. Regression analyses examined whether PCA-derived RewP- and gain-related P200 amplitudes were associated with affective functioning while controlling for age, sex, ethnicity, income-to-need ratio, child depressive symptoms, and parental depressive symptoms. At the group level, boys showed greater PCA-derived gain-related P200 amplitudes than girls. At the individual level, higher child positive affect was associated with larger PCA-derived RewP amplitudes in the primary covariate-adjusted regression model. In sensitivity analyses conducted in the larger sample without the income-to-needs covariate, negative affect, rather than positive affect, was significantly associated with PCA-derived RewP amplitude. These findings provide novel evidence that RewP may serve as an early neural marker of affective functioning. By extending RewP research to an understudied developmental period and emphasizing normative emotional functioning, this study advances understanding of early reward processing and highlights the utility of PCA for isolating meaningful ERP components in children.

papers.title: Association of serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor and adiponectin with anxiety, depression, and stress in deaf adults: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Rand Alsharq, Anfal M. Al-Dalaeen, Eman Saleh, Nour Batarseh, Abeer Ahmad Bahathig
papers.abstract: Individuals with disabilities face practical and social challenges beyond those experienced by non-disabled individuals, which may increase vulnerability to mental health problems. However, few studies have examined biochemical correlates of psychological health in this population. This study investigated the associations of serum brain-derived neurotrophic factors (BDNF) and adiponectin with anxiety, depression, and stress among deaf adults. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 204 deaf adults aged 18–45 years. Anxiety and depression were assessed using the DASS-21 questionnaire. Body composition analyses were performed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, and serum BDNF and adiponectin levels were measured. Serum BDNF concentrations were inversely associated with anxiety ( r = −0.632, p < 0.001), depression ( r = −0.732, p < 0.001), and stress ( r = −0.795, p < 0.001). Similarly, serum adiponectin concentrations showed significant inverse correlations with anxiety ( r = −0.422, p < 0.001), depression ( r = −0.344, p < 0.001), and stress ( r = −0.446, p < 0.001). In multiple linear regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI), BDNF remained an independent inverse predictor of anxiety ( β = −0.48, p < 0.001), depression ( β = −0.55, p < 0.001), and stress ( β = −0.62, p < 0.001). Adiponectin also remained independently associated with anxiety ( β = −0.19, p = 0.03) and stress ( β = −0.21, p = 0.02). Lower serum BDNF and adiponectin concentrations were independently associated with higher levels of anxiety, depression, and stress among deaf adults. These findings suggest that BDNF, and to a lesser extent adiponectin, may represent potential biomarkers of psychological distress in this population.

papers.title: A multifactor model for assessing programming knowledge based on the synchronization of AI analytics and expert evaluation
papers.authors: Zhanat Kunapianovna Nurbekova, M. N. Kemelbek, Ainur Sagimbayeva, Asset Zhaxylykov, Aikenzhe Zhamkeeva, Rakhimzhan Abduvaliyev
papers.abstract: Introduction The widespread adoption of generative AI tools has created new methodological challenges for the validity of assessment in higher education. If a neural network can write code, how can a student's actual knowledge be assessed objectively? This study proposes a multifactor AI-assisted assessment model for the fair evaluation of AI-supported learning practices in programming courses and examines its alignment with instructor assessment. Methods The study involved 187 undergraduate students from three universities in Kazakhstan. In Phase 1, student submissions were evaluated using a traditional one-dimensional approach focused on functional correctness, and the results produced by instructors and by three large language models (GPT, Claude and Gemini) were compared. In Phase 2, a multifactor assessment model incorporating functional correctness, explanation quality and AI-use level was introduced, and the same submissions were re-evaluated with all three models. Results The baseline analysis showed that AI-assisted assessment assigned systematically higher scores than instructors and demonstrated only moderate agreement with instructor evaluation. Under the multifactor model, agreement with instructor assessment improved significantly for one of the three models (Claude: r = 0.478 →0.647; ρ = 0.449 →0.690; MAE = 18.32 →7.34), while a second model (Gemini) showed a significant reduction in prediction error without a change in rank-order agreement, and a third (GPT) showed no significant change on any measure and reversed the direction of its systematic bias. Even in the best case, agreement remained moderate (approximately 42% of shared variance with instructor scores). Discussion The findings indicate that the effectiveness of AI-assisted assessment depends on the structure of the assessment framework and on the underlying language model, and that a richer rubric does not benefit all models equally. By extending evaluation beyond code correctness toward explanation quality and transparent AI-supported problem solving, the proposed model offers a more balanced and pedagogically grounded approach to assessing undergraduate programming competencies.

papers.title: AI literacy development among special education graduate students: a mixed-methods exploration
papers.authors: Randa G. Keeley, Maria Peterson, Brooke Huley, Catherine Howerter, Hou I. Esther Lau
papers.abstract: This mixed-method exploratory study examined the development of AI literacy among ( N = 19) master's-level special education graduate students as they explored the integration of generative AI tools to support students with high-incidence disabilities. Participant responses were examined to identify perceptions of AI, intended uses of generative AI, and considerations related to responsible implementation in special education settings. Findings revealed a conceptual shift in participants' perspectives, from viewing generative AI primarily as an administrative tool for increasing efficiency to recognizing its potential as an adaptive instructional scaffold. Participants increasingly emphasized the need for critical human oversight, FERPA compliance, data privacy, and individualized alignment between AI-generated resources and students' educational needs. Intentional AI literacy development can support future special educators in moving beyond basic technical proficiency toward the critical judgment needed to evaluate and implement generative AI responsibly. Preparing special educators to use AI effectively requires attention not only to its potential benefits for instruction and efficiency but also to legal, ethical, and pedagogical considerations, including student confidentiality and individualized educational planning.

papers.title: The disclosure gap: why mandating AI transparency without protecting honesty is a leadership failure
papers.authors: Damola Usman Onaolapo
papers.abstract: Universities and journals have answered generative artificial intelligence (AI) with one main instrument: mandatory disclosure. Ask researchers to declare what they used, and transparency should follow. The evidence says it does not. Across 5,114 journals and 5.2 million papers, about 70% of journals now require disclosure, yet only around 0.1% of papers published since 2023 declare AI use, and journals with policies show no less AI adoption than journals without them. Submission data from two major publishers tell the same story: 5.7 and 3.3% disclosure, against surveys where between 28 and 76% of researchers say they use these tools. This Perspective argues that the gap is not a compliance failure to be fixed with firmer rules. It is what happens when institutions ask people to volunteer information that carries a real cost, and then do nothing about that cost. Experiments show that AI users are judged less competent and less motivated; researchers have named the effect AI shaming and the punishment of honesty. The paper argues that this cost falls unevenly, that the evidence on how it falls is messier than a simple centre-periphery story allows, and that the problem belongs to institutional leaders rather than journal editors. It sets out what owning it would mean.

papers.title: Reconceptualizing outdoor geoscience learning for the generative AI era: a human-centered instructional model
papers.authors: Yoon-Sung Choi
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) creates a distinctive problem for outdoor geoscience learning: it can broaden questioning and explanation, yet it can also pre-structure what learners notice and displace their interpretation of field evidence. Existing field-learning frameworks explain how conceptual, geographical, psychological, technical, and social novelty shape participation, but they do not fully explain this redistribution of epistemic work and authority. Extending established accounts of technological mediation to field settings, this Hypothesis and Theory article interprets GenAI as an epistemic reorganization of field inquiry rather than as technical novelty alone. It advances the central hypothesis that GenAI is more likely to augment, rather than displace, learners’ epistemic agency when it is introduced after direct observation and an initial learner interpretation, restricted to generating questions and candidate explanations, and subjected to human adjudication against field evidence. On this basis, the article proposes a six-stage human-centered model: preparing for field and GenAI use; attending to and recording field evidence; constructing an initial learner interpretation; engaging GenAI as a dialogic challenger; conducting human evidence-based adjudication; and completing reflective synthesis and epistemic accounting. Field evidence functions as an epistemic constraint, GenAI outputs remain provisional objects of scrutiny, and learners and teachers retain interpretive authority and responsibility. Six testable propositions specify expected effects of sequencing, initial interpretation, challenger-oriented prompting, explicit adjudication, substitution, and teacher orchestration. Operational criteria for distinguishing support, mediation, and substitution, and a thought experiment at a basalt outcrop, show how the model can be applied and tested. The model offers a falsifiable agenda for research in physical, hybrid, and virtual geoscience field learning while defining conditions under which GenAI use should be limited or withheld.

papers.title: Online hate speech against the Mapuche people: pre-service history teachers’ educational responses to a teaching scenario
papers.authors: Rodrigo Salazar-Jiménez, Cristian Orellana Fonseca, Elizabeth Montanares Vargas, Carlos Muñóz Labraña
papers.abstract: Introduction Hate speech directed against the Mapuche people, historically perpetuated through the media's mechanisms of racialisation, has found a powerful platform for amplification on social media. This article analyses how trainee how history teachers conceptualise this phenomenon from a pedagogical perspective and what analytical and pedagogical strategies they employ to address it in the classroom. Methods A qualitative-interpretative approach was adopted, using an integrated case study design, in which each of the 22 written responses from trainee history teachers at a university in southern Chile constituted a unit of analysis. Participants were selected through purposive sampling from an intact cohort, and their consent was obtained once the coursework had been marked. The analysis combined deductive and inductive coding, carried out independently by two researchers, with discrepancies resolved through discussion and, where necessary, through the arbitration of a third party. Results The participants broadly recognise the descriptive components of hate speech – stigmatisation, generalisation, dehumanisation and the association between Mapuche demands and al violence – but make little reference to the frameworks of structural racism, coloniality and racialisation, and only marginally to Mapuche knowledge and studies; furthermore, a technical-instrumental conception of digital citizenship predominates. Two exploratory findings emerged from the inductive phase: the spontaneous the appearance of the expression `thieving Indians' in five responses, indicating that the phrase is culturally recognisable to the participants, although there is no evidence of its circulation within their social circles; and the reported use of generative artificial intelligence in six responses, which was examined without any controlled comparison and is therefore regarded as hypothesis-generating. Discussion The implications for initial teacher training are analysed, in particular the interaction between critical media literacy, a decolonial perspective and the development of professional judgement in digital environments, as well as the educational tensions associated with the use of generative AI.

papers.title: Phonetic research as an innovative model of interdisciplinary STEAM education: from acoustic analysis to teaching practice
papers.authors: Stevica Maksimovic
papers.abstract: This paper presents an innovative interdisciplinary teaching model based on the integration of acoustic phonetics into STEAM education (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Mathematics). This study is based on the premise that the interdisciplinary nature of acoustic phonetics, connecting language with physics, mathematics, and digital technologies, provides a suitable basis for designing STEAM-oriented educational activities that engage students in scientific inquiry, acoustic measurement, data analysis and programming. The paper presents a pilot classroom implementation in English language instruction in which students used Praat-based acoustic analysis together with a Python-based supervised machine-learning classifier to investigate whether speakers could be differentiated on the basis of measurable acoustic characteristics. The computational component employed a Random Forest classifier based on selected acoustic features, while supplementary manual analysis of the F3–F2 distance was used to examine/r/ realizations in cases of acoustic overlap. The classroom implementation involved 30 seventh-grade students, while the acoustic speaker dataset consisted of recordings from six students selected for the speaker-differentiation component of the project. A special section of the paper is devoted to the development of educational projects combining phonetic analysis, physical models of the vocal tract, and artificial intelligence algorithms, with the aim of bringing the scientific method closer to students and enabling active learning through research. The paper demonstrates that phonetic research can serve not only as a component of language teaching but also as a powerful instrument of interdisciplinary education. The conclusion emphasizes that phonetics represents an authentic STEAM discipline in miniature and that its systematic implementation in teaching contributes to the development of functional knowledge, an investigative mindset, and students' digital competencies.

papers.title: ChatGPT as an AI-based assessment method in library information science education: investigative study in the information studies department
papers.authors: Noura Al Hosni
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly the emergence of generative tools such as ChatGPT, have intensified scholarly debate regarding their implications for teaching, learning, and assessment in higher education. While existing research has largely emphasized AI-driven automation of pedagogical processes and learning outcomes, limited attention has been paid to the systematic integration of generative AI as a formal assessment mechanism. This study examines the state and use of ChatGPT as an AI-based assessment tool within the Information Studies Department at Sultan Qaboos University. Despite the growing prevalence of AI technologies, many higher education institutions remain cautious in their adoption for assessment purposes, with some categorizing their use as academic misconduct or plagiarism. Such hesitancy reflects unresolved ethical concerns, academic integrity challenges, and the absence of coherent institutional frameworks to guide responsible implementation. In response, this study explores the potential legitimization of AI-assisted assessments while preserving academic rigor, transparency, and integrity. Adopting a qualitative research methodology, the study employed content analysis to examine existing teaching practices and activities within the department and to identify current levels of AI integration and institutional readiness. This analysis provided nuanced insights into the dominant state and presence of AI-based assessment methods in targeted departments’ offered courses within the university, which resulted in 67% of the checked courses lacking detection of AI-based assessment methods, 20% having moderate integration of AI usage in assessment methods and 13% having direct instruction to use AI while fulfilling the required assessments. Based on these insights, the study proposes a set of AI governance policies and strategic guidelines for higher education institutions, offering practical recommendations for integrating generative AI tools into academic assessment frameworks without compromising ethical, professional, or scholarly standards.

papers.title: Foundation first: a health-system readiness framework for responsible AI adoption in Somalia
papers.authors: Hamze G. Dahir, Abdisalam Hassan Muse
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned as a mechanism for expanding access, strengthening surveillance, improving clinical decisions, and increasing health-system efficiency. Yet AI implementation is path-dependent: its value depends on the health-system, digital, institutional, and social foundations into which it is introduced. Somalia provides a critical test of this proposition because a dynamic telecommunications ecosystem coexists with uneven electricity, broadband use, primary care capacity, routine data quality, digital skills, and governance, particularly across rural, pastoralist, nomadic, displaced, and drought-affected populations. This Perspective develops a foundation-first AI implementation agenda for Somalia. It integrates the World Health Organization health-system building blocks, the Nonadoption, Abandonment, Scale-up, Spread and Sustainability framework, and an equity lens, while aligning proposed actions with the Sustainable Development Goals, Somalia's National Transformation Plan 2025-2029, Health Sector Strategic Plan III, and African Union Agenda 2063. The central argument is that AI should be treated as a capstone of digital transformation rather than its starting point. Reliable energy, inclusive connectivity, strong primary and community care, interoperable information systems, workforce capability, sustainable financing, and accountable governance should precede or accompany AI deployment. This sequencing can convert AI from a potentially exclusionary technology into a context-fit multiplier of health-system capacity.

papers.title: Assessing digital factors influencing AI-led asset information management in hospital facilities
papers.authors: Motheo Meta Tjebane, Thabo Khafiso
papers.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the digital factors influencing AI-led Asset Information Management (AIM) in hospital facilities. The study focuses on the extent to which digital factors related to data governance, operational efficiency, resource optimisation, and predictive capabilities are perceived to be present in healthcare facilities. Design/methodology/approach: A quantitative research approach was adopted using a structured questionnaire administered to relevant professionals involved in hospital asset management. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics in SPSS, including mean scores, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis to evaluate the distribution and significance of responses. Reliability testing was conducted, yielding a high Cronbach's Alpha value of 0.95, confirming strong internal consistency of the measurement instrument. Findings: A two-factor structure of digital factors was identified through an exploratory factor analysis. Although the statistical evidence points to a dominant one-factor structure, the two-factor solution was retained on theoretical grounds. Respondents rated foundational digital services, particularly access control and security protocols, mostly highly. One-way ANOVA comparing item-level mean scores across six groups of professionally experienced individuals showed no statistically significant differences. Suggesting that perceptions of these digital factors do not vary meaningfully by years of professional experience in this sample. Practical implications: The study highlights the need for healthcare institutions to invest in digital infrastructure, data integration, and capacity development to leverage AI capabilities fully. Emphasis should be placed on transitioning from basic automation toward predictive and intelligent asset management systems. Originality/value: This study provides empirical evidence on the layered adoption of AI in hospital asset management, demonstrating that current implementations are largely efficiency- and security-driven, while advanced predictive capabilities remain underdeveloped. It contributes to the growing body of knowledge by identifying a critical gap between AI potential and its practical realisation in healthcare infrastructure.

papers.title: DepressNet: an interpretable machine learning framework for depression severity stratification using psychometric data
papers.authors: Anika Rahman, Fahmid Al Farid, Md Humaion Kabir Mehedi, Jia Uddin, Hezerul Bin Abdul Karim
papers.abstract: Depression is a highly prevalent mental health condition worldwide, affecting approximately 332 million individuals and contributing significantly to global disability burden.
