In computational mental health research, machine learning approaches are increasingly applied to structured psychometric questionnaires; however, many existing studies formulate the problem as binary classification, which fails to capture the ordinal nature of symptom severity represented in standardized instruments. This study presents a computational psychometrics framework for depression severity stratification using the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-42) questionnaire dataset. The proposed model, DepressNet, four base learners—XGBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM and a calibrated support vector machine (SVM)—with a PyTorch-based multi-layer perceptron meta-learner trained on out-of-fold probability features to reduce information leakage and improve generalization. To address class imbalance inherent in real-world psychometric data, the training pipeline incorporates SMOTETomek resampling together with class-weighted cross-entropy loss. The framework is evaluated on 39,775 real-world questionnaire responses under an imbalanced five-class classification setting using multiple complementary metrics. On a held-out test set, the model achieves 85.38% accuracy, 59.01% macro F1-score, 0.7158 Matthews Correlation Coefficient, and 0.9714 AUC-ROC. It is acknowledged that the severity labels are derived from the same DASS-42 items used as input features; consequently, the framework learns structured scoring patterns within psychometric data rather than predicting independent clinical ground truth. The Mild severity class remains the most challenging stratum (F1 = 0.10), reflecting inherent symptom overlap with adjacent classes and the persistent difficulty of classifying a narrow four-point severity band. Beyond predictive evaluation, a SHAP-based explainability module is applied to examine both global and class-wise feature attribution patterns across severity levels. The analysis provides interpretable relationships between questionnaire items and predicted severity categories, highlighting structured symptom-response patterns captured by the model. Overall, this work contributes a reproducible and interpretable machine learning framework for psychometric data analysis, with emphasis on severity stratification, ensemble-based learning, and explainable modeling of mental health questionnaire responses.

papers.title: Developing an AI literacy policy framework for responsible AI governance: perspectives from South Korean media experts
papers.authors: 신선경, Jooyeun Park
papers.abstract: This study investigates the societal impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) and develops policy directions for mitigating associated risks through qualitative content analysis of written structured expert interviews with eleven media experts in South Korea. The findings indicate that the impacts of AI extend across three interconnected domains: individual, societal, and industrial. Among the risks identified, experts expressed particular concern about job displacement, data-related vulnerabilities, and ethical challenges. In response to these concerns, the development of AI literacy policy was mentioned by all participants as a policy response, while strengthening corporate accountability and reinforcing legal and institutional safeguards were also identified as relevant policy measures. More importantly, the findings suggest that effective AI literacy policy should move beyond a narrow focus on technical knowledge and skills toward a holistic framework encompassing three core dimensions: ethics and responsibility, practical and context-sensitive application, and social inclusion. Building on these findings, this study proposes an AI literacy policy framework that positions literacy as a critical component of responsible AI governance rather than solely as an individual competency.

papers.title: Algorithmic allure: a theoretical framework for dark AI patterns and the erosion of informed consent in AI-driven digital marketing
papers.authors: Keltoum Bentameur, Hamadi Zineb, Riyad Bouaici
papers.abstract: This study examines how generative AI is reshaping digital marketing by enabling unprecedented levels of personalization, automation, and consumer interaction, while simultaneously producing subtler, more complex forms of algorithmic manipulation that extend well beyond conventional dark patterns and threaten meaningful informed consent. Prior research has treated AI-enabled persuasion in a fragmented way—focusing on personalization, recommender systems, or deceptive interface designs in isolation—without offering an integrated account of how generative AI shapes influence across the consumer journey. To address this gap, we conduct a multi-case qualitative analysis of seven documented international incidents of AI-driven marketing practices from 2024 to 2026. Data sources include regulatory reports, investigative journalism, corporate disclosures, and peer-reviewed literature. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we identified seven high-level themes: identity manipulation, social-proof exploitation, synthetic evidence, AI-washing, agentic AI manipulation, synthetic authenticity, and autonomous commercial manipulation. These themes form a taxonomy of “Dark AI Patterns”. Building on these findings, we propose Algorithmic Allure Theory (AAT), which conceptualizes AI-enabled persuasion as a dynamic, six-stage process: observation, interpretation, algorithmic allure, behavioral steering, delegation, and algorithmic governance. AAT argues that contemporary commercial persuasion relies on adaptive computational systems that continuously generate, test, and refine influence tactics in real time—processes that often erode informed consent while preserving a veneer of legitimacy and transparency. Contributions (1) establish Dark AI Patterns as a distinct class of deceptive practices; (2) introduce AAT as a transdisciplinary framework for understanding AI-mediated influence; (3) reconceptualize informed consent as an ongoing cognitive and temporal process rather than a one-time legal event; (4) offer a practical taxonomy to guide future research, regulation, and ethical AI marketing practices As a primary goal.

papers.title: Concomitant acromioplasty is associated with enhanced structural healing, long-term durability, and functional outcomes in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: a retrospective propensity score and causal machine-learning analysis
papers.authors: 宋玉成, Liang Zhao, Can Liu, Yijun Wang
papers.abstract: Background: The clinical value of acromioplasty (AC) combined with arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (RCR) remains controversial. This study evaluates the associations and heterogeneity of treatment response for concomitant AC during arthroscopic RCR. Methods: We retrospectively analysed 734 patients (220 AC, 514 RCR-only). Propensity scores were estimated via a SuperLearner ensemble, followed by inverse probability of treatment weighting to balance covariates. Structural healing, functional outcomes (American Society of Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons and Constant-Murley Shoulder scores), and re-tear events were assessed at 12 months. Doubly robust machine-learning approaches (DR-learner, causal forest, Bayesian additive regression trees) were employed to estimate the average and individual treatment effects. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used to improve model interpretability. Results: Acromioplasty was associated with improved structural healing (risk difference: -7.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], -11.9% to -3.6%; number needed to treat [NNT] ≈ 13). Weighted Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly lower cumulative re-tear incidence at 60 months (AC: 45.9% vs. RCR-only: 80.0%; hazard ratio: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.33 to 0.51; p < 0.001). Functional scores were significantly higher with AC (ΔASES = 7.9; ΔConstant = 7.5; both p < 0.001), although these differences did not exceed established minimal clinically important difference thresholds. Considerable treatment heterogeneity was identified: patients with a high critical shoulder angle (CSA) (>35°) and older age (>62 years) showed the strongest associations with potential benefits. The SHAP analysis identified age, body mass index, tear size, and CSA as key factors influencing outcomes. Conclusion: Concomitant AC is associated with enhanced structural healing and long-term durability in arthroscopic RCR. Although functional scores were statistically higher in the AC group, the differences did not exceed established MCID thresholds, indicating limited clinical significance for functional outcomes. Significant treatment heterogeneity highlights the importance of individualised surgical strategies, particularly favouring patients with high CSAs and of older age.

papers.title: Using ChatGPT for Research Writing: Perspectives of Jordanian EFL Learners
papers.authors: Raeda Ammari, Esraa Hantouleh
papers.abstract: This study investigates the extent to which EFL learners employ ChatGPT in research writing. Using simple random sampling, a total of 64 undergraduates enrolled in a Research Writing course at Amman Arab University were surveyed with a questionnaire. The students were asked about the section in which they used ChatGPT most and the reasons behind this. Moreover, the paper explains how their educators can help them overcome the difficulties in writing. The questionnaire included 14 items, and the data collected were analyzed in terms of frequencies and percentages. Results show that the majority of students find writing a research problem challenging, with a lack of English fluency being a prominent reason. Students suggest that their instructors should hold workshops or training sessions on how to write this specific section so that they can improve their writing. Next, a focus group discussion with 15 students was held to reflect on these results. The focus group partially agreed with the results, but they found the literature review more challenging for the same reason, as students had never been taught how to write it properly. This study provides valuable insights from Jordanian learners themselves for educators seeking to improve their students’ research writing skills.

papers.title: The Mediating Role of Tourism Brand Co-Creation Behaviour in Linking Tourist and Operator Resources to Tourist Satisfaction and Loyalty
papers.authors: Diddo Adding Adove, Gilang Pranajasakti, Fahad Ramadhan, Erlangga Surya Kusuma
papers.abstract: Tourism increasingly depends on value that tourists and service providers build together, because such joint interaction raises tourist satisfaction and loyalty. Drawing on Service-Dominant Logic, this research tests how tourist operant resources (self-efficacy and tourist expertise) and operator operant resources (co-creation operator and service quality) influence Tourism Brand Co-Creation Behavior (TBCB), tourist satisfaction, and tourist loyalty, and whether TBCB mediates the path to satisfaction. A causal-explanatory design was applied to 526 respondents, selected purposively, who had been to the Ubud area of Bali during the previous 12 months. The data were processed through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in AMOS 24. The findings show that each of the four antecedents significantly and positively affects both TBCB and tourist satisfaction; TBCB in turn raises satisfaction, and satisfaction raises loyalty. According to the Sobel test, TBCB significantly mediates the link between every antecedent and satisfaction. Since the direct effects also remain significant, the mediation is complementary (partial) and not full.

papers.title: Balancing AI and Learning: Examining the Effects of Generative AI Dependency and Digital Multitasking on University Students’ Self-Regulated Learning
papers.authors: Febviana Sulthanah Huwaida, Nuur Wachid Abdul Majid
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of generative AI dependency and digital multitasking habits on the quality of self-regulated learning (SRL) among university students, both individually and jointly. The study employed a quantitative approach involving 300 active students from five study programs at the Purwakarta Campus of Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia, who were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using four-point Likert-scale instruments that met established validity and reliability criteria. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression, preceded by classical assumption tests for normality, linearity, multicollinearity, and heteroscedasticity. The results indicated that generative AI dependency was positively and significantly associated with SRL (B = 0.213, p = .004), as was digital multitasking (B = 0.178, p = .009). Simultaneously, both predictors were significantly associated with students’ SRL, F = 27.843, p < .001, and the regression model explained 15.8% of the variance in SRL. These findings suggest that, within the context of this study, moderate levels of generative AI use and digital multitasking did not substantially undermine students’ self-regulatory capacity. Rather than restricting generative AI use, higher education institutions should provide structured guidance on effective AI engagement, including prompt formulation strategies and reflective evaluation of AI-generated outputs, and integrate such guidance into learning task design. Such an approach may help ensure that students’ interaction with generative AI strengthens rather than substitutes for their self-regulatory capacity.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Based Ensemble Method of Estimating Ionospheric Refraction from Smartphones
papers.authors: Caitlyn Hayden, Lingmin Tan, SUNIL B. BISNATH
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Satellite Division's International Technical Meeting (Online)/Proceedings of the Satellite Division's International Technical Meeting (CD-ROM)
papers.abstract: The demand for consumer grade GNSS is increasing, with consumer devices dominating the global market; opening the door for potential smartphone derived GNSS corrections, such as crowd-sourced ionospheric corrections. However, due to linearly polarized antennas and ultra-low cost receivers, raw smartphone ionospheric refraction estimates exhibit rampant errors, with large biases and variances capable of causing over 3000 meters in error. To address these data quality issues, this paper proposes a three-base-model ensemble machine-learning approach that directly and intentionally confronts large unknown biases, highly variable noise in the data, and residual trends. The final result of the ensemble is coordinated by a gated meta-learner capable of adaptively weighting base components through a gating function; allowing for simple outlier negation and final results that are more accurate than any individual component. The ensemble is trained and tested using Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge and York University datasets to test for generalization ability. In total, 9 different algorithms are examined with 16 different special cases/task-specific implementations. Ultimately, 3 different algorithms are selected and used to train 4 models that serve as ensemble components. When including broadcast Klobuchar corrections, the final ensemble is capable of reducing the initial raw root mean squared error of all datasets from 608.79 m to a mean value of 0.30 m with a standard deviation of ± 0.03 m across multiple iterations. Compared to the 0.70 m RMSE produced with just applying the Klobuchar model, this corresponds to a 57% decrease. Even further, improvements are completed across 23 datasets of approximately 20 to 60 minutes in under five minutes, with zero external data reliance beyond initial positioning solutions, and an epoch-by-epoch individual estimate based approach. This proposed framework establishes a foundation for future research in adaptive outlier detection, accuracy estimation, and filtering with high applicability for ionospheric mapping using smartphone data; laying the groundwork for cheap and feasible development and implementation of rapid smartphone derived ionospheric corrections.

papers.title: Embracing the algorithm: Faculty perceptions of artificial intelligence tools and their role in transforming teaching and learning in higher education
papers.authors: Adnan Bataineh, Amna Al Shidi, Kashif Ali Sabiri
papers.abstract: Although the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools is a relatively recent phenomenon in the context of Higher Education (HE) practice, little research exists on the faculty in the Arab Gulf Region perceptions and application of AI tools. This study investigates the use of AI tools by academics in the foundation programmes at a Higher Education Institution (HEI) in Oman, the perceived value of AI in education and learning, challenges faced by these academics, and the professional development needs. A questionnaire with 40 questions was used for the quantitative, descriptive cross sectional survey from June to September 2026. Forty-four responses were received, of which eight (18.2%) were excluded because they were careless in their responses; the remaining 36 responses were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, as well as thematic analysis. Adoption of AI was widespread and commonplace, with 83.3% using AI tools at least weekly, with ChatGPT by far the most commonly used tool (91.7%), and the majority of users focusing on lesson planning (80.6%), teaching materials (77.8%) or the design of assessments (69.4%). Perceptions of pedagogical impact were rated as moderate (M = 2.97 on a scale of 5), and were bimodal, with barriers, primarily academic integrity (M = 3.06), there being around 50% at each end. Pedagogical impact was perceived at a moderate level (M = 2.97 of 5) and was bimodal, with academic integrity (M = 3.06) being the most common barrier endorsed by about 50% of the sample, followed by trustworthiness of content and cost. Younger, early career faculty reported significantly greater positive perceptions and much greater need for development (p < .001). The study reveals that there exists a practice-conviction gap between faculty use of AI and their confidence in the potential of AI as a pedagogical tool. Professional development, policy and assessment redesign, subsidized access, and connectivity and support are recommended to address the needs of individuals across the career stages.

papers.title: Customer perceptions of artificial intelligence in enhancing customer service: The case of Somalia's service industry
papers.authors: Abdifatah Nour Rage
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming customer service globally; however, its effectiveness depends on how customers perceive automated interactions, particularly in fragile, low-regulation contexts such as Somalia. This study provides the first empirical evidence of Somali customers' perceptions of AI-enabled customer service, examining how trust in AI and perceived service quality shape user satisfaction and recommendation readiness while accounting for digital literacy. Using a positivist, cross-sectional design, primary data were collected via a bilingual online questionnaire from 353 adult customers in Mogadishu, Hargeisa, Garowe, and Kismayo who interacted with AI-based customer support in telecommunications and mobile banking. The constructs were measured using culturally adapted Likert scales, and hypotheses were tested using correlations, multiple regression, and structural equation modeling. Customers reported moderate levels of trust, service quality, satisfaction and recommendation readiness. Transparency was the weakest trust dimension, alongside low confidence in data protection, whereas efficiency emerged as the strongest perceived service quality benefit. Service quality predicted satisfaction more strongly than trust, and satisfaction was a strong predictor of recommendation readiness. The model explained nearly half the variance in satisfaction, with digital literacy significantly moderating the satisfaction- Overall, Somali customers demonstrate pragmatic acceptance of AI for efficiency gains but remain constrained by transparency gaps, privacy and security concerns, and a persistent preference for relational human services. This implies that trust-sensitive transparency, privacy-by-design, culturally calibrated personalization, and hybrid human–AI escalation pathways are critical for sustainable AI deployment in fragile economies. This study fills a significant geographical gap in AI service research and offers evidence-based guidance for policymakers and service providers in post-conflict settings.

papers.title: The impact of ethical generative AI use on academic integrity and writing performance among EFL university students
papers.authors: Piedad Rosario Guijarro Paguay, Marco Antonio Aquino Rojas
papers.abstract: The purpose of this article is to analyze the ethical use of artificial intelligence and its impact on the academic integrity of writing among students of English as a foreign language at the Escuela Politécnica Superior de Chimborazo. This is a non-experimental, correlational study. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using a Likert scale and through the analysis of essays using an evaluation rubric. For data collection, we used an online questionnaire with a Likert scale and analyzed essays using an evaluation rubric. A census sample was taken of 26 ESPOCH students duly enrolled in the sixth semester of the School of Business Administration during the period from March to July 2026. The results of the research show that artificial intelligence has provided a cognitive framework for grammatical review and source verification. After confirming the normality of the data using the Shapiro-Wilk test, Pearson’s correlation coefficient demonstrated positive, direct, and statistically significant relationships between the ethical use of AI and academic integrity, as well as with writing performance, thereby supporting the research hypothesis. It is concluded that the transparent and self-regulated integration of AI-assisted writing acts as a supportive tutor that enhances linguistic quality without compromising academic honesty.

papers.title: DIGITAL THERAPEUTICS FOR ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION: A STRUCTURED REVIEW OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE, REGULATORY FRAMEWORKS, AND ACCESS DISPARITIES
papers.authors: Maryan Liasota, Michalina Justyna Kozłowska, Krzysztof Konopka, Maciej Kamil Majchrzak, Faustyna Magdalena Kołodziej, Alicja Kwiatkowska, Jakub Juskowiak, Mateusz Lis, Zuzanna Julia Komin, Eliza Zofia Kabat
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science
papers.abstract: Background: The integration of Digital Therapeutics (DTx) into psychiatric care represents a paradigm shift in the management of anxiety and depression. With the continuous technological advancement of Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), its potential to alleviate shortages in psychiatric care is facing rigorous evaluation. As a result, ongoing studies aim to verify whether these technologies deliver genuine medical improvements, while simultaneously exploring the structural hurdles of deploying them within traditional clinical settings. Objective: This structured review evaluates the intersection of clinical evidence for DTx in treating Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) and Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) with existing regulatory frameworks and socioeconomic barriers to equitable access. Methodology: An investigative sweep of the PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar databases was executed to identify literature published from 2018 to 2026. Inclusion criteria focused on peer-reviewed RCTs and policy analyses of evidence-based DTx platforms. The assembled data underwent systematic organization via a thematic approach, with material being classified into three distinct categories: clinical efficacy, regulatory limitations, and accessibility equity. Results: Findings indicate that while AI-driven CBT and chatbot-delivered interventions demonstrate significant symptom reduction with moderate-to-high effect sizes, their long-term efficacy is moderated by user engagement patterns. Regulatory analysis reveals a fragmentation between the US FDA and European DiGA pathways, complicating global reimbursement. Furthermore, structural disparities—driven by the "digital divide" and low technological literacy—persistently limit the reach of these interventions among underserved populations. Conclusion: Digital interventions present an easily expandable mechanism for combating global psychiatric shortages; however, inconsistent legal guidelines and socioeconomic barriers heavily restrict their medical utility. Subsequent academic efforts need to emphasize multidimensional adoption models to prevent these technological advancements from worsening present-day medical inequalities.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Tertiary English Pedagogy: A Comparative Study of Urban and Rural Contexts in Bangladesh
papers.authors: Aklima Akther
papers.abstract: The growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is changing practices of English teaching and learning in higher education. Yet access to AI and the capacity to use it pedagogically remain uneven across geographical and socioeconomic contexts. This qualitative comparative study examines how tertiary English educators and undergraduate students in urban and rural higher education institutions in Bangladesh experience and use AI for teaching and learning. The study draws on semi-structured interviews with 10 English educators and 20 undergraduates from selected urban and rural institutions. Interview data were analyzed thematically using Braun and Clarke’s (2006) approach. The findings reveal that the urban-rural difference in AI-supported English pedagogy is multidimensional, involving connectivity, device availability, affordability, AI literacy, pedagogical guidance, institutional policy, and sociocultural conditions. Urban participants reported more frequent use of AI for writing support, lesson planning, vocabulary development, language practice, translation, and feedback, whereas rural participants described greater difficulties arising from unstable internet connectivity, power interruptions, limited devices, financial constraints, and insufficient institutional training. Academic-integrity concerns affected both contexts but often encouraged more restrictive responses where institutional guidance was weak. The study argues that equitable AI integration requires more than access to AI platforms. It requires infrastructure, teacher development, student AI literacy, clear institutional policies, and context-sensitive support. The study contributes a context-based understanding of AI inequality in tertiary English pedagogy in Bangladesh.

papers.title: Induced sad mood biases responses to sad and neutral faces under low visibility: behavioral and ERP evidence
papers.authors: Xueqiao Li, Elisa Vuoriainen, Elina S. Kangas, Piia Astikainen
papers.abstract: Facial expression recognition is shaped by both stimulus properties and the perceiver’s affective state. Research on emotional face processing under backward masking has largely focused on threatening expressions, and few studies have examined how an observer's mood influences recognition of non-threatening facial expressions under limited visibility. The present study investigated how experimentally induced sad versus neutral mood modulates behavioral and neural responses to sad and neutral facial expressions under low (10 ms) and high visibility (200 ms) backward masking conditions. Participants underwent sad and neutral mood induction on separate days and performed a facial expression categorization task while electroencephalography was recorded. Behavioral and event-related potential (ERP) analyses included 25 and 20 participants, respectively. Behaviorally, a mood effect on response criterion was observed in the low visibility condition: the criterion was lower in sad than neutral mood, reflecting a reduced tendency to categorize faces as neutral. Discrimination sensitivity was higher under high than low visibility but was not significantly affected by mood. Facial expressions modulated N170, P2, and P3 amplitudes under high visibility, and N170 and P2 under low visibility. P2 amplitude in the low visibility condition showed an interaction effect between mood and facial expression. In neutral mood, sad faces elicited larger P2 amplitudes than neutral faces, whereas in sad mood, the relation was the opposite. These findings highlight the influence of the observer’s affective state on behavioral and neural responses to facial expressions under limited visibility, extending previous findings beyond threat-related expressions to sadness.

papers.title: Large Language Models Are More Sycophantic in Chinese Than in English
papers.authors: Yize Zeng, 宜欣 何, JianHui Zhang, Yang Tao, Chao Hu
papers.abstract: AI sycophancy has emerged as a prominent concern in human–AI interaction, as large language models (LLMs) may unduly affirm users’ beliefs or actions rather than provide independent assessments. Such behavior may vary across languages because language can cue culturally patterned norms of social interaction. Prior work has documented Chinese–English differences in the social orientations expressed by LLMs, paralleling broader cross-cultural differences in interdependence and interpersonal harmony. We therefore tested whether these differences extend to AI action endorsement. Across seven LLMs, we compared responses to 3,024 matched open-ended personal-advice queries presented in Chinese and English. The primary outcome was action endorsement rate (AER), defined as the proportion of explicit endorsements among responses taking an explicit stance. A binomial mixed-effects model accounting for item and model variation showed higher odds of endorsement in Chinese than in English (odds ratio [OR] = 1.99, 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.42, 2.79], P = 0.004). As a robustness check, we repeated the evaluation using a separate Chinese scoring workflow—a distinct operational scoring pipeline rather than a simple translation of the primary English scorer—and obtained the same directional language difference. Adjustment for explicit-stance propensity left the primary estimate essentially unchanged. These findings identify a consistent Chinese–English difference in action endorsement and are consistent with the possibility that culturally patterned relational norms shape how LLMs respond to users across languages.

papers.title: Intentional Forgetting of Autobiographical Memories: Current Neuroimaging Evidence and Moving Towards an Integrationist EEG-fMRI Approach
papers.authors: Dhruv Chand Aggarwal, Palmer Smith
papers.abstract: Intentional Forgetting (INF) is one of many human memory processes which has gathered academic intrigue in emergent literature. Understood as a conscious and voluntary cognitive effort to suppress the recall of, or remove certain memories, INF has been extensively studied in associative paradigms. However, its application to autobiographical memory (AM) remains under-investigated, especially within neuroimaging studies. First, we summarize existing neuroimaging literature on intentional forgetting of autobiographical memories (INF-AM). Upon reviewing, we found evidence to be fragmented, providing no clear consensus around the neural bases of INF-AM. We argue this fragmentation is, in part, a result of a reliance on single-modality applications of electroencephalograph (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) methodology. EEG and fMRI, however, are complementary in their respective temporal and spatial superiority. Subsequently, we propose the application of an EEG-fMRI integrationist approach to INF-AM. We discuss how its application may help address conceptual, paradigm-level, and methodological concerns. Since human AM and the process of forgetting are inherently longitudinal, we contrast the popular cross-sectional design with a longitudinal alternative. We then present the application of the integrationist approach to longitudinal INF-AM designs. Though cognizant of the limitations that may accompany such an approach, we present the integrationist approach as a much needed and promising way forward in decoding the neuroscience of INF-AM.Keywords: intentional forgetting, autobiographical memory, neuroimaging, EEG-fMRI, integrationist

papers.title: Toward Smart Agrotourism: Co-Creating a Living Lab for Premium Melon Farming
papers.authors: Oliver Samuel Simanjuntak, Bambang Supriyanta, Heru Cahya Rustamaji, Yenni Sri Utami
papers.journal: RSF Conference Series Engineering and Technology
papers.abstract: Digital monitoring makes farm activity easier to observe, but adding technology does not by itself make a working farm an experiential learning setting. Smart agrotourism also depends on whether digital systems fit local governance and everyday cultivation. This paper examines the formation of a premium-melon Living Lab in Kebonagung, Bantul, Indonesia, during the pre-harvest and pre-tourism period. We used a qualitative, process-oriented single-case design and examined project documents, WhatsApp communications, field logs, digital monitoring records, and photographs collected from March to September 2026. The findings show that co-creation developed through adaptations prompted by field conditions. Physical, agronomic, and spatial constraints brought academic teams, students, village authorities, and local youth into shared decisions and changes in responsibility. Knowledge was brought together by repeatedly checking sensor readings against manual agronomic references and observed irrigation outcomes. The case offers a grounded pathway for rural initiatives by keeping pre-tourism formation separate from later tourism performance. It also shows why local caretaking arrangements and data-validation procedures need to be clear before project handover.

papers.title: How AI Adoption Transforms Technology Acceptance into Online Purchase Behavior: An Integrated UTAUT–Technology Acceptance Model
papers.authors: Dewi Novianti, Susanta Susanta, Didik Indarwanta
papers.journal: RSF Conference Series Business Management and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into digital commerce through intelligent services that support consumer purchasing. However, limited empirical evidence explains how technology acceptance translates into AI adoption and subsequent online purchase behavior, particularly in digital MSMEs. This study examines the relationships among effort expectancy, performance expectancy, AI adoption, and online purchase behavior, positioning AI adoption as a behavioral link between technology acceptance and purchasing outcomes. A quantitative explanatory study was conducted using a cross-sectional survey of 126 consumers selected through purposive sampling. Respondents had used an AI-based service or feature, interacted with a digital MSME, and made an online purchase. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that performance expectancy significantly and positively affects AI adoption (β = 0.657, p < 0.001), whereas effort expectancy does not significantly affect AI adoption (β = 0.101, p = 0.123). Effort expectancy significantly and positively affects online purchase behavior (β = 0.265, p < 0.001), as does performance expectancy (β = 0.168, p = 0.026). AI adoption also significantly and positively affects online purchase behavior (β = 0.317, p < 0.001). These findings indicate that perceived performance benefits are more important for AI adoption, while both performance and ease of use contribute to online purchasing. The study contributes by positioning AI adoption as a behavioral mechanism connecting technology acceptance with online purchase behavior and offers practical implications for developing AI-enabled digital commerce services.

papers.title: Critical Thinking Development among University Students in the Era of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Nurul Oktorina, Bambang Suryadi
papers.abstract: Critical thinking is an essential competency for students in facing the transformation of higher education in the digital era and Artificial Intelligence (AI). However, empirical evidence regarding the factors that shape and develop these abilities is still scattered in psychological, pedagogical, and technological perspectives. This study aims to synthesize empirical findings on the antecedents and development of students' critical thinking in the context of digital and AI. The research uses a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PRISMA guidelines. Empirical literature published in 2021–2026 was searched through Google Scholar and selected based on inclusion criteria that include research on higher education students and focus on critical thinking skills or development. A total of 18 empirical articles met the criteria and were analyzed thematically. The results showed three main determinants. Psychological factors, such as self-efficacy, cognitive flexibility, and reflective thinking, contributed to students' analytical and evaluative abilities. Pedagogical strategies, including Problem-Based Learning, collaborative learning, WebQuest, and digital learning, are effective in improving critical thinking skills. Meanwhile, AI and digital technology extend critical thinking to the ability to evaluate digital information, verify AI outputs, recognize biases, and use AI reflexively and ethically. This study offers an integrative psychological–pedagogical–AI literacy framework to understand students' critical thinking transformations in the digital and AI era. Berpikir kritis merupakan kompetensi esensial bagi mahasiswa dalam menghadapi transformasi pendidikan tinggi di era digital dan Kecerdasan Buatan (AI). Namun, bukti empiris mengenai faktor yang membentuk dan mengembangkan kemampuan tersebut masih tersebar dalam perspektif psikologis, pedagogis, dan teknologi. Studi ini bertujuan mensintesis temuan empiris tentang antecedents dan pengembangan berpikir kritis mahasiswa dalam konteks digital dan AI. Penelitian menggunakan Systematic Literature Review (SLR) berdasarkan pedoman PRISMA. Literatur empiris yang diterbitkan pada 2021–2026 ditelusuri melalui Google Scholar dan diseleksi berdasarkan kriteria inklusi yang mencakup penelitian pada mahasiswa pendidikan tinggi dan berfokus pada keterampilan atau pengembangan berpikir kritis. Sebanyak 18 artikel empiris memenuhi kriteria dan dianalisis secara tematik. Hasil menunjukkan tiga determinan utama. Faktor psikologis, seperti self-efficacy, cognitive flexibility, dan reflective thinking, berkontribusi terhadap kemampuan analitis dan evaluatif mahasiswa. Strategi pedagogis, termasuk Problem-Based Learning, collaborative learning, WebQuest, dan digital learning, efektif meningkatkan keterampilan berpikir kritis. Sementara itu, AI dan teknologi digital memperluas berpikir kritis menjadi kemampuan mengevaluasi informasi digital, memverifikasi keluaran AI, mengenali bias, serta menggunakan AI secara reflektif dan etis. Studi ini menawarkan kerangka integratif psikologis–pedagogis–AI literacy untuk memahami transformasi berpikir kritis mahasiswa di era digital dan AI

papers.title: The Relationship Between Digital Literacy, User Skepticism, and Verification Behavior in Evaluating Generative AI Responses
papers.authors: Ervina Nurjanah, Taufik Asmiyanto, Rahmi
papers.journal: Tibanndaru Jurnal Ilmu Perpustakaan dan Informasi
papers.abstract: Research Objective. This study is motivated by the transformation of information evaluation practices in the era of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI), in which users increasingly evaluate AI-generated responses rather than directly assess the credibility of sources. Given that Generative AI can produce highly fluent but not always accurate responses, digital literacy and user skepticism have become critical factors in the information evaluation process. This study aims to analyze the relationships among digital literacy, user skepticism, and verification behavior in the evaluation of Generative AI responses. Research Method. This study employed a quantitative cross-sectional design, using cross-tabulation and chi-square analysis. Analysis Data. Data were analyzed using cross-tabulation and chi-square tests in SPSS to identify distribution patterns and relationships among categorical variables. The study used secondary data from the Kaggle platform, involving 1000 respondents; therefore, the findings should be interpreted within the limitations of the dataset's representativeness. Results. The findings indicate that digital literacy is not significantly associated with age or educational attainment. In contrast, both digital literacy and educational level are significantly associated with users' skepticism toward Generative AI. However, no significant relationship was found between users' digital literacy levels and the fact-checking methods they employed. Conclusions. Within this dataset, age and formal education do not demonstrate significant relationships with digital literacy levels. Nevertheless, users with higher levels of digital literacy and educational attainment tend to exhibit greater skepticism toward Generative AI responses. These findings may indicate a tendency toward more proportionate patterns of trust, although this study does not directly measure calibrated trust. Digital literacy emerges as a potentially important factor associated with how users understand the limitations of AI systems, evaluate AI-generated responses, and determine whether additional verification is necessary. Keywords: Generative AI Response Evaluation; AI User Skepticism; Digital Literacy

papers.title: Empowering University Librarians in the Age of AI: A Study of Competence and Collaboration in Higher Education
papers.authors: Dio Eka Prayitno, Aditya Ramadhani, Reza Mua'dzatul Masrurah
papers.journal: Tibanndaru Jurnal Ilmu Perpustakaan dan Informasi
papers.abstract: Research Objective. While AI offers transformative potential for information retrieval, it challenges the traditional intermediary role of academic librarians. This research explores the gap between current librarian skills and the technical-pedagogical competencies needed to navigate AI-powered reference services. Focusing on the complex ecosystem of academic libraries, this study identifies the core competencies required to optimize AI tools to meet multifaceted user needs. Research Method. This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach with purposive sampling. Data Analysis. The findings reveal that librarians have developed digital literacy through both formal and informal activities and have successfully integrated AI into various educational and information consulting services. Results. Using the B-Wheel model, the analysis shows the importance of orientation, specialization, experimentation, social learning, and the reinforcement of social norms. The role of the librarian cannot be replaced but is instead supported and enhanced by AI technologies. Conclusions. Librarian competencies are a key determinant of effective, efficient, ethical, and sustainable AI use. Librarians who are adaptive, collaborative, and reflective are the main agents of digital-era library services. Thus, librarian competencies are fundamental to the transformation of AI-based library services. Keywords: artificial intelligence, librarian competencies, reference services, digital literacy, academic libraries

papers.title: Entre la eficiencia académica y el razonamiento clínico: perfiles funcionales de uso de inteligencia artificial en estudiantes de medicina
papers.authors: Luis Miguel Delgado Arias, Daniel Alba Ospina, María Alejandra López Ríos
papers.abstract: Introduction: Generative artificial intelligence has been rapidly integrated into medicaleducation, particularly in study tasks and academic productivity. However, it remainsunclear whether its use extends equally to more complex processes, such as clinicalreasoning. Objective: To characterize and compare the functional profiles of AI useoriented toward academic efficiency and clinical reasoning among medical students.Method: A cross-sectional study involving 290 medical students. A self-administeredquestionnaire was administered, and two proportional indices of AI use were constructed: one oriented toward academic efficiency and the other toward clinical reasoning.Descriptive analyses, a paired t-test, and Welch’s ANOVA with post hoc comparisonswere performed. Results: The mean age was 20.4 ± 2.66 years and the GPA was3.99 ± 0.54. 71.3% reported high frequency of AI use. Use oriented toward academicefficiency was higher than that oriented toward clinical reasoning (0.66 ± 0.22 vs. 0.46± 0.34), with a mean difference of 0.20 (95% CI: 0.17–0.24; p < 0.001). Differenceswere observed according to academic semester. Conclusions: AI use among medicalstudents is primarily oriented toward academic efficiency, with variations depending onthe stage of training.

papers.title: Digital transformation of public sector accounting through artificial intelligence to improve financial transparency and accountability
papers.authors: Arthur Reinaldo Tanihatu, Nana Adriana, Moh. Sholeh, Sukriyah Sukriyah, Budiandru Budiandru
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology that reshapes public sector accounting by improving financial management efficiency, transparency, and accountability. This study aims to examine the role of AI in the digital transformation of public sector accounting and its contribution to enhancing public financial governance. Using a narrative literature review approach, the study analyzes relevant books, peer-reviewed journal articles, government reports, and other scholarly publications concerning AI, digital transformation, and public sector accounting. The findings indicate that AI significantly enhances accounting efficiency through process automation, predictive financial analysis, intelligent auditing, and real-time reporting while strengthening financial transparency and institutional accountability. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) explains that perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use are critical determinants of successful AI adoption within public organizations. However, organizational readiness, digital infrastructure, data governance, and regulatory support remain essential prerequisites for effective implementation. The study concludes that AI-driven digital transformation provides substantial opportunities for improving public financial governance and offers strategic insights for policymakers seeking sustainable and accountable financial management systems.

papers.title: Using artificial intelligence to analyze judicial practice: methodology, opportunities, limits
papers.authors: Marina Vyacheslavovna Chudinovskikh, Vyacheslav V. Shutovsky, Yulia P. Chudinovskikh
papers.abstract: The article focuses on judicial practice, which ranks among the most challenging tasks for legal experts. Courts issue millions of decisions that contain data on case positions, evidence, and amounts to be paid; yet existing legal systems provide limited analytical capacity. The aim of the article is to access the applicability of artificial intelligence technologies in systematizing large volumes of legal text. The advancements in artificial intelligence technologies hold the potential to significantly enhance the efficiency and the quality of judicial practice analysis. The article provides an overview of academic publications, evaluates existing judicial analytics tools, as well as presents the novel methodology developed by the authors. The proposed methodology for analyzing judicial practice may be of interest to lawyers, software developers, government agencies, and is also suitable for use in educational settings.

papers.title: Intelligent Recommendation Platform for Sustainable Agricultural Management in Sampués (Sucre) Using Fine-Tuning Techniques
papers.authors: María Angélica García Medina, Leonard Andrés Ortega González, Fabio Ramírez Moreno, Claudia Lengua Cantero
papers.journal: Encuentro Internacional de Educación en Ingeniería
papers.abstract: The project is being developed in the municipality of Sampués, a territory with a strong agricultural and artisanal tradition linked to the Zenú culture. Agricultural productivity faces challenges associated with climate variability and the deterioration of natural resources, which demands a shift towards sustainable soil and water management models. The research proposes the development of an intelligent recommendation module integrated into the HerenciaViva platform, aimed at strengthening the productive sustainability and marketing of crops such as corn, cassava, and yam. This module is based on supervised machine learning techniques and model fine-tuning processes, incorporating variables related to agricultural practices based on ancestral knowledge, in order to generate contextualized recommendations that allow farmers to adopt sustainable practices for the cultivation and harvesting process. The development is structured under the Extreme Programming (XP) agile methodology, organized into four iterative phases: (i) planning, through requirements gathering based on user stories and semi-structured interviews with farmers; (ii) Design, based on a hybrid hexagonal-modular architecture that promotes decoupling and scalability; (iii) Coding, implemented with NestJS and TypeScript, supported by a polyglot data architecture that integrates PostgreSQL (persistence), Redis (caching), and ChromaDB (vector database for the recommendation engine); and (iv) Testing, which includes k-fold cross-validation for the ML models and acceptance testing with stakeholders in the local agricultural sector. As a result, a hexagonal architecture is consolidated that allows for the independent evolution of system components and a functional web platform with modules for authentication, user management, product catalog, profiles, and an AI-based chatbot. The system integrates traceability information, socio-environmental context, and sustainable agricultural product practices. In terms of data management, a combined approach is implemented that optimizes performance in environments with limited connectivity. It is concluded that the incorporation of ancestral Zenú knowledge as variables in the machine learning models constitutes an innovative contribution to the digitization of agricultural heritage. Furthermore, the adoption of a hexagonal-modular architecture and a polyglot persistence strategy strengthens the system's scalability, maintainability, and efficiency. Finally, the application of XP proves suitable for rural contexts, allowing for the continuous adaptation of requirements based on data availability and feedback from stakeholders.

papers.title: Proposal for an Indicator to Measure the Adoption of AI in Research: The LATAM Case
papers.authors: Diana Catalina Hernández Rojas, Ana María Gomez-Lamus, Wilmer Pineda
papers.journal: Encuentro Internacional de Educación en Ingeniería
papers.abstract: The expansion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Latin America has significantly reshaped the production, circulation, and accessibility of scientific knowledge, albeit with uneven progress across countries. While existing regional indices assess technological and institutional capacities, they do not directly capture the extent to which AI fosters openness, accessibility, and reuse of academic knowledge. To address this gap, this study proposes a composite indicator designed to measure the adoption of AI applied to scientific dissemination, contributing a novel dimension to the analysis of digital ecosystems and open science in the region. The methodology integrates bibliometric variables, digital infrastructure, connectivity, and research and development expenditure. It combines logarithmic transformations, Z-score standardization, Principal Component Analysis, and Shannon entropy to ensure robustness and comparability. Additionally, an interactive data visualization tool is developed to explore spatial patterns, identify structural gaps, and enhance interpretability, supporting both analytical depth and decision-making processes. The results reveal marked regional heterogeneity, with Uruguay showing the strongest performance and Venezuela the lowest. Validation against established indices demonstrates conceptual consistency and moderate statistical associations, confirming that the proposed indicator captures a complementary dimension focused on scientific visibility and impact. Overall, the study provides a novel framework for understanding how AI contributes to the democratization of knowledge in Latin America.

papers.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education Using Automation, Algorithmic Techniques, and Natural Language Processing
papers.authors: Juan José Arce Aristizábal
papers.journal: Encuentro Internacional de Educación en Ingeniería
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Generative Artificial Intelligence has begun to transform multiple activities in higher education, from the way students learn to how instructors design materials and conduct assessments. As a result, in recent years there has been a significant increase in academic research analyzing the use of these technologies in university contexts. The objective of this work is to analyze the main research trends related to Generative Artificial Intelligence in higher education during the period 2016–2026. To achieve this, a software tool was developed to automatically collect and analyze more than 4,000 scientific articles from academic databases such as IEEE Xplore and Web of Science. The application provides an integrated management of bibliographic sources and enables different types of bibliometric analysis, allowing the identification of patterns in scientific literature, such as the most frequent concepts, predominant research topics, and the temporal evolution of publications. In addition, the system generates visualizations that help to clearly understand the distribution of scientific production, the most active countries, and emerging topics in this field. The results show a significant growth in research on Generative Artificial Intelligence applied to higher education, particularly in areas related to AI-supported learning, human–AI interaction, and ethical challenges associated with these technologies. This work provides an overview of the current state of research in this field and offers a tool that can be used to automatically explore scientific trends across different areas of knowledge.

papers.title: On the Development of a Progressive Web Application Integrating Generative AI and Intelligent Systems for Personalized Learning in Mathematics and STEM Education
papers.authors: Juan Carlos Maya López, Ómar Ramírez González
papers.journal: Encuentro Internacional de Educación en Ingeniería
papers.abstract: This work presents the development of a Progressive Web Application (PWA) designed as a modular intelligent learning environment for personalized education in mathematics and STEM. The system addresses persistent limitations in conventional digital learning platforms, including delayed feedback, weak contextual adaptation, fragmented support between theory and practice, and limited responsiveness to student progression. To overcome these challenges, the platform is built upon a multi-layer architecture integrating a dynamic user model, an adaptive decision engine, telemetry-driven learning analytics, contextual tutoring, and an interactive presentation layer referred to as Interactive Learning Graphic Motion (ILGM), which governs how content is structured, visualized, and activated for each learner. The development emphasizes coordinated interoperability across intelligent subsystems rather than isolated AI functionalities: adaptive planning mechanisms regulate sequencing, difficulty, and representation, while agent-based decision-making components introduce agentic capabilities within study sessions, enabling dynamic content generation, contextual adapptation, and role-oriented instructional behaviors. In this framework, large language models provide contextual tutoring, generative explanations, and real-time learning support, complemented by interactive visual modules for guided practice and multimodal content delivery. To ensure pedagogical consistency and reliability, the system incorporates validation and calibration mechanisms that guide the generation and adaptation of exercises, maintaining coherence in difficulty progression, solution quality, and evaluation criteria across learning sessions. Implemented as a PWA, the system ensures cross-device accessibility, low-friction interaction, and session continuity aligned with modern student behaviors. This paper aims to explain generative artificial intelligence—particularly large language models—and intelligent adaptive systems applied on an online platform can converge within a unified architecture to enhance personalization, interactivity, and continuity in learning processes across mathematics and STEM education.

papers.title: Experimental Inter-Report Scatter Bounds Machine-Learning Accuracy for TADF Singlet–Triplet Gaps—Structure and Semi-Empirical Features Reach the Same Limit
papers.authors: J.-P. Tchapet Njafa, Steve Cabrel Teguia Kouam, Patrick Sorrel Mvoto Kongo, Samafou Penabeï, S. G. Nana Engo
papers.abstract: The singlet–triplet gap ∆ESTis the screening parameter for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), yet independent experimental reports of the same compound scatter by 0.072 eV RMS, and the per-molecule median regressed on is known only to 0.049 eV, about half of any model’s error. This label noise sets a ceiling on every predictor, yet the models sit below it: neither noise nor capacity alone accounts for the remaining error. Against that ceiling, two-dimensional structure predicts as accurately as a semiempirical excited-state calculation: on 231 donor–acceptor molecules (212 Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, scaffold cross-validation), random forests from Morgan fingerprints (MAE 0.091 eV) and RDKit descriptors (0.100 eV) match natural-transition-orbital descriptors from a GFN2-xTB/sTDA excited state (0.096 eV) to within 0.017 eV on paired folds, so the excited-state step buys no accuracy. Two further results are specific to this corpus. First, under a source-paper split the accuracy advantage over a mean-value baseline disappears, but the excited-state descriptors keep the rank correlation the fingerprints lose (paired ∆ρ = 0.19 on a single split, 95 % CI narrowly excluding zero): they order candidates across laboratories without predicting the gap. Second, the leakage that inflates many computed-gap models is learner-dependent—given the S1 and T1 energies as features, a linear model returns ∆EST ≡ ES1 − ET1 exactly (R2 = 1.000) while an axis-aligned forest on the same features recovers only R2 = 0.59 and clears cross-validation unremarked. Progress past the ≈ 0.1eV ceiling needs a curated, solvent-controlled, single-source experimental benchmark—one that would also expose the remaining modelling headroom. Data, models, and code are available (Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17436069).

papers.title: Bridging the trust gap: a mixed-methods study of United Kingdom educators’ perceptions of generative artificial intelligence in higher education assessment
papers.authors: Tadhg Blommerde, David R. Callaghan, Emilee Morrallis, Kevin Campbell-Karn,  Nurun Nahar
papers.abstract: Situated against the backdrop of an evolving regulatory landscape, this study investigates the perceptions of United Kingdom university educators regarding the use of generative artificial intelligence in summative assessment. Through a mixed-methods survey of 330 academic staff, the research identifies a significant gap between high levels of digital literacy and low evaluative trust. While respondents report high familiarity with AI tools, confidence in the ability of artificial intelligence to provide fair or nuanced marks remains low. Qualitative analysis of open text questions reveals a nuance crisis, where educators perceive these systems as incapable of comprehending complex student submissions. The findings reveal significant gender disparities in technical proficiency, however, a consistent pattern of low evaluative trust persists across teaching experience levels, with no statistically significant differences detected based on professional seniority, suggesting a potential need to consider alternative pedagogical frameworks, such as performative and synchronous assessments, to safeguard academic integrity.

papers.title: A STUDY OF CORRELATION OF NUTRITIONAL PARAMETERS WITH ANTHROPOMETRIC MEASUREMENTS IN PATIENTS ON HAEMODIALYSIS
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Malnutrition and protein-energy wasting (PEW) are common complications among patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD).Nutritional impairment contributes significantly to morbidity, mortality, and poor quality of life in this population.Subjective Global Assessment (SGA) is a widely used tool for nutritional evaluation, while anthropometric measurements provide objective indicators of body composition.The present study assessed nutritional status and its correlation with anthropometric measurements in hemodialysis patients.Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of General Medicine, Tertiary Care Centre, Kolhapur, for 2yrs.A total of 100 patients aged ≥18 years receiving maintenance hemodialysis for at least eight weeks were enrolled using random sampling.Nutritional status was assessed using SGA.Anthropometric measurements, including BMI, BSF, TSF, MAC, and MAMC were recorded.Correlation analyses were performed to evaluate the relationship between SGA scores and anthropometric parameters, age, gender, and duration of hemodialysis.Results: The mean age of participants was 51.99 ± 11.14 years, and 69% were males.The mean BMI was 20.63 ± 2.92 kg/m², while the mean duration of hemodialysis was 10.05 ± 3.64 weeks.Based on SGA classification, 77% of patients were severely malnourished, 21% had mild-to-moderate malnutrition, and only 2% were well nourished, resulting in an overall malnutrition prevalence of 98%.BMI demonstrated a significant positive correlation with SGA score (r = 0.359, p < 0.001).However, BSF, TSF, MAC, and MAMC showed no significant correlations with SGA.A significant positive correlation was observed between duration of hemodialysis and worsening nutritional status (r = 0.202, p = 0.044).Male patients had significantly poorer nutritional status than females (p = 0.030), whereas age showed no significant correlation with SGA score (p = 0.912).Conclusion: Malnutrition is highly prevalent among patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis.SGA is an effective and comprehensive tool for nutritional assessment, while BMI is the only anthropometric parameter showing a significant association with nutritional status.Routine nutritional screening using SGA, supported by selected anthropometric and biochemical parameters, is essential for early detection and management of malnutrition in hemodialysis patients.

papers.title: Securing AI Chatbots: A Framework for Trust and Standardization
papers.authors: Ahmad Musa Bulama, Dr. Mohammad Faisal, Huzaifa Muhammad Bello, Muhammad Muhammad Fadama
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: AI-based chatbots have taken over industries such as health care, finance, and customer services. However, the implementation of AI chatbots poses many issues regarding trust, privacy, and proper ethical use of this technology. This paper discusses a framework to standardize trust and security in AI-based chatbots. The framework combines insights from technical, psychological, philosophical, and cultural perspectives. The main problems tackled include issues such as lack of privacy, robustness of the models against adversarial attacks, and ethical considerations. Some of the privacy enhancement measures discussed in this study include the use of techniques such as homomorphic encryption and federated learning. Measures aimed at making the models resilient to attacks by adversaries such as prompt injection and data poisoning have been discussed. The framework seeks to address the privacy paradox and other aspects such as emotional aspects and the limitations of epistemology.

papers.title: Pemanfaatan Situs Air Panas Songgoriti sebagai Inovasi Sumber Belajar Sejarah Lokal bagi Guru MGMP Kota Batu
papers.authors: Deny Yudo Wahyudi, Daya Negri Wijaya, Andhika Yudha Pratama, Nayla Cahaya Kirani, Labuda Shofiya Ananda, Anisa Musyaroful Ikhrom
papers.abstract: The utilization of local history as a learning resource represents an important approach to fostering contextual and meaningful history education. Nevertheless, the potential of local historical heritage in Batu City, particularly the Songgoriti Hot Spring Site, has not yet been optimally incorporated into history teaching practices. This article aims to describe the implementation of a community engagement program designed to enhance the professional competence of history teachers affiliated with the Batu City History Teachers’ Association (MGMP) in utilizing the Songgoriti Hot Spring Site as an innovative local history learning resource. The program was implemented through three stages: pre-activity, activity implementation, and post-activity. The pre-activity stage included an assessment of the partners’ problems and needs, as well as the preparation of instructional materials and media. During the implementation stage, participants received three sessions covering the archaeological heritage potential of Batu City, Songgoriti: Findings, Restoration, Utilization Potential, and Challenges, and Artificial Intelligence and Its Use in History Education, followed by discussion and question-and-answer sessions. The post-activity stage included evaluation and planning for follow-up activities with the partners. The findings indicate that the program provided teachers with insights into the history and potential of the Songgoriti Hot Spring Site, as well as the use of artificial intelligence to support history education while maintaining information verification. The program also supports the development of contextual history learning resources through the utilization of cultural heritage in the surrounding environment.

papers.title: The Inventor Who Never Existed: Intellectual Property in the Age of AI
papers.authors: Neelanksha Bhatia
papers.abstract: Every branch of intellectual property law was built around the quiet assumption that a person sits behind the work, the invention, or the secret. Generative AI unsettles that assumption without giving courts anything clean to replace it. Ask whether an AI system can be an author, an inventor, or a party capable of keeping a promise of confidentiality, and the answer is almost always no. Still, that answer resolves very little, since it says nothing about who should be held responsible when an author is displaced, a consumer is misled, or a trade secret leaks with no one left to blame. This paper follows that gap as it shows up across copyright suits brought against AI developers in the United States, a patent dispute spanning nearly a dozen jurisdictions over whether an AI system can be named an inventor, trademark and publicity-rights claims arising from AI-generated likeness, and the quieter but arguably more urgent problem of what happens to a trade secret once it is pasted into a public chatbot. Along the way, it weighs the case-by-case litigation favored in the United States and the United Kingdom against the European Union's more pre-emptive, disclosure-driven approach. It argues that the more useful question courts and regulators should be asking is not what the AI is, but who among the people who built, deployed, or used it is best placed to answer for the harm once it occurs.

papers.title: Generative ai and user-generated media content in hybrid competence formation for future technical specialists
papers.authors: Наталя Московчук
papers.journal: Scientific bulletin of South Ukrainian National Pedagogical University named after K D Ushynsky
papers.abstract: The rapid advance of generative artificial intelligence is reshaping language training in higher education, including the discipline “Business Ukrainian Language” taught to future specialists in technical fields. The relevance of the topic is heightened by wartime conditions, which limit face-to-face communicative practice and increase demand for tools that can sustain language development remotely. The purpose of the article is to determine the potential and specific features of AI tools – text generators, voice synthesizers, and video generators – in students’ creation of user-generated media content as a method of forming the Ukrainian- language professional and communicative competence of future technical specialists. The study draws on theoretical analysis of scientific literature on AI in education, a comparative method for contrasting the capabilities of different AI tools, case studies of student projects (scripts, podcasts, videos) created within the course by Cybersecurity majors, an analytical method for assessing AI’s influence on competence formation, and synthesis for generalizing the results into recommendations. The article examines the didactic potential of text generators in drafting video scripts, voice synthesizers in producing audio content and reinforcing orthoepic literacy, and video generators in visualizing course topics. Building on this practical experience, the author proposes a five-component model of hybrid competencies – professional, technical, creative, communicative, and ethical – formed through AI-assisted media content creation, correlated with the European DigCompEdu framework and the UNESCO AI competency framework for students. Particular attention is given to the unreliability (“hallucination”) of AI-generated content and to academic-integrity risks, for which verification strategies and task-design recommendations are proposed. The results show that AI-assisted media content creation fosters hybrid competencies that combine professional, technical, creative, communicative, and ethical components, while requiring deliberate pedagogical design to safeguard linguistic accuracy and academic integrity alike.

papers.title: AI in the translation classroom: tool or threat? A review of current research and pedagogical implications
papers.authors: Катерина Петрівна Коробова
papers.journal: Scientific bulletin of South Ukrainian National Pedagogical University named after K D Ushynsky
papers.abstract: The fast growth of artificial intelligence (AI) translation tools, such as neural machine translation (NMT) systems, such as DeepL, and large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, has clearly changed how translation is taught and learned at the university level within philology programs. This article looks at recent studies and theories from 2024 to 2025 to better understand how AI tools are being used in translation classes today, what practical and analytical skills students are developing in this new context, what challenges teachers face while teaching translation in the AI era, and how they can gradually adapt their classes or couses to use CATs more effectively in order to prepare skilled and flexible translators for the modern job market. Research based on various studies that use different methods, such as mixed-methods, quasi-experimental, and systematic reviews, shows that AI tools really help students work faster and make better translated drafts that can later undergo further human correction and revision. These tools also let learners take more control of their studies, get better access to learning materials, parallel texts, and examples of ready-made translations for analysis, and quickly find specific information connected with different realia, terminology, and cultural nuances, etc. At the same time, there are always issues with understanding different cultures in depth, adapting meanings for the target audience, being accurate in practical situations, and choosing the right way to speak in different contexts, which always show that human judgment is still needed and cannot be replaced by AI tools. The article suggests using a human-centered approach to teaching translation with AI, where such tools are seen as things to study and think about critically, not just quick ways to get finished translations without human revision. Concrete classroom strategies, such as post-editing tasks, comparing human and AI translations, teaching basic AI literacy, and discussing ethical aspects, are suggested as ways to use AI's strengths while also improving the skills needed for modern professional translators.

papers.title: Model Konseptual Eco-Digital Pedagogy dalam Pembelajaran IPS Sekolah Dasar: Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Rizki Achmad Husaeni, Feri Dwi Jayanti, Prince Clinton Immanuel Christian Damanik, Mohammad Idham Chaled, Anastasia Arta Uli
papers.abstract: The global socio-ecological crisis and the rapid digitalization of education require a paradigm shift in primary education. Eco-Digital Pedagogy emerges as a transformative framework integrating environmental education and digital technology. However, existing research remains fragmented across isolated technological interventions and theoretical traditions. This Qualitative Systematic Literature Review (SLR) aims to synthesize empirical and conceptual evidence from 41 peer-reviewed articles (2020–2026) to formulate a comprehensive Conceptual Model of Eco-Digital Pedagogy specifically designed for Elementary Social Studies Education. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and Braun & Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis, the synthesis reveals four foundational theoretical pillars (Critical Ecopedagogy, TPACK-TAM, Multimodal Social Semiotics, and Ecosocial Citizenship), a core competency triad encompassing ecological knowledge, affective sensitivities, and action practices, and a five-cluster technology ecosystem (Immersive VR/AR, Digital Storytelling, Gamification, Interactive Media, and Emerging AI/IoT). The study constructs a five-phase pedagogical cycle comprising Eco-Sensing, Digital Inquiry, Critical Dialogue, Creative Co-Design, and Transformative Praxis. Institutional enablers such as Adiwiyata policies and open-access infrastructure serve as vital catalysts, while teacher digital techno-stress and connectivity divides represent key implementation hurdles. The proposed conceptual model offers an actionable blueprint for primary social studies educators and curriculum designers to foster critical digital ecoliteracy among Generation Alpha learners.

papers.title: AI LITERACY DALAM PENDIDIKAN: TINJAUAN LITERATUR TENTANG KOMPETENSI YANG DIBUTUHKAN PESERTA DIDIK DI ERA ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Safna Khoiro Nabila, M. Hafis, Safira Putri, Nuriska Julia Anggraini, Annisa  Rasyid Fitri Khalillah
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, has become part of students' everyday learning practices, yet the competencies they need to use it wisely are still poorly understood. This article aims to synthesize the literature on AI literacy in education and to identify the competencies learners need in the era of artificial intelligence. The study employed a narrative, integrative literature review with thematic content analysis of journal articles, conference papers, books, and policy documents from international organizations, mainly published between 2019 and The synthesis shows that AI literacy is consistently framed as a multidimensional construct. Six clusters of learner competencies emerged: (1) conceptual understanding of how AI works, (2) purposeful use and application of AI tools, (3) critical evaluation of AI outputs, (4) ethical and responsible conduct, (5) creation and design with AI, and (6) affective and self-regulatory dispositions that sustain human-centred collaboration with AI. The review also indicates that these competencies develop progressively from understanding to applying and creating, that teacher readiness and valid assessment instruments remain major challenges, and that most existing frameworks are not yet grounded in the Indonesian educational context. The article concludes that AI literacy should be integrated into curricula as a cross-disciplinary competence rather than treated as a purely technical subject, and it proposes directions for future empirical research.

papers.title: Generative AI Use, Self-Regulated Learning, and Creativity Among Indonesian Design Students
papers.authors: Yulyanto Yulyanto, Jerry Dounald Raharjaan, Sigit Setya Kusuma, Ilhamsyah Ilhamsyah4, Yayat Sudaryat, Munya Saleh Ba Matraf
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in design education, yet whether its use supports or substitutes for the self-directed creative process remains unclear, particularly outside the Chinese samples that dominate prior research. This study examined whether self-regulated learning (SRL) mediates the relationship between generative AI use and creativity among Indonesian design students. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 120 Indonesian visual communication design students and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped confidence intervals and four pre-specified sensitivity analyses. SRL was strongly and consistently associated with creativity (β = .674, f² = .962), and this association remained stable across all robustness checks. AI usage's relationships with SRL, with creativity directly, and with creativity indirectly through SRL were significant in the full sample but lost significance under two independent sensitivity analyses;. However, the sample was adequately powered to detect these effect sizes (post-hoc power ≥ .91); treat the point estimates as preliminary and confirm them in a larger, independent sample before treating them as established. A supplementary analysis found that frequency of AI use, unlike a richer measure of how AI was used, was unrelated to SRL or creativity. SRL is a robust correlate of creativity in AI-assisted design education, while AI use's own contribution requires replication; design pedagogy may be better served by cultivating self-regulation directly than by monitoring AI usage frequency alone. Keywords: generative AI, self-regulated learning, creativity, design education, PLS-SEM.

papers.title: The Effect of Sycophantic AI Advice on Human Social Judgement: A Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.authors: Vera Békés, Alyssa Mackie
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly becoming embedded in everyday social life, including how individuals seek advice, interpret interpersonal conflict, and make relational decisions (Zao-Sanders, 2025).
