papers.authors: Mohammad Aldalou, William S. Brooks, Adam B. Wilson
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from speculative novelty to an everyday presence among both learners and educators in medical education, with applications spanning tutoring, assessment, feedback, and support for clinical reasoning.[1][2][3][4][5][6][7] Within the anatomical sciences, customized GPTs, image-enabled systems, and multimodal tools are being proposed and tested for cadaveric and radiologic structure labeling, real-time histology feedback, quiz generation, and adaptive tutoring in anatomy.[8][9][10][11][12][13][14][15] These developments, while still in their infancy, have begun to reshape how students engage with and test their anatomical knowledge.[8][9][10][11]16 The surge in AI usage and applications has led to mounting pressures on researchers and journals alike to demonstrate AI's educational effectiveness.17 Some medical and health professions education journals now actively prioritize AI studies that examine learner outcomes in knowledge, skills, or attitudes.Paradoxically, 19359780, 0,

papers.title: Mutual Adaptation and Influence: Review of Latent Dynamics Models in Human–Robot Interaction
papers.authors: M.S. Smith, Sunny Amatya, Seyed Yousef Soltanian, Jonathan Bush, Wenlong Zhang
papers.abstract: Recent advances in robotics have enabled more dynamic and interactive roles when working with humans. This progress is enabled in part by latent state models, which allow the robot to predict human actions in a compact and tractable way. This paradigm has allowed robots not only to respond and adapt to human behavior but also to anticipate and plan proactively through the use of latent dynamics models. This review explores the use of such models in the field of human–robot interaction. Existing literature reveals three classes of latent dynamics models: Bayesian, Markovian, and encoded. To connect these works, we synthesize a unified framework consisting of a prediction and control step. This framework shows how the traditional one‐way adaptation extends to mutually adaptive behaviors by using latent dynamics in the prediction step. Similarly, we show how influence is an extension of mutual adaptation by using latent dynamics in the control step. We then review state‐of‐the‐art approaches to mutual adaptation and influence for the three latent dynamics classes and discuss emergent properties as they relate to application, update frequency, and specific considerations for mutual adaptation or influence. Using this review, we highlight gaps in the current literature and propose future directions.

papers.title: Chatbot Intervention and Cancer Risk Knowledge in Adolescents and Young Adults With Cancer Predisposition
papers.authors: Junne Kamihara, Angel M. Cronin, Hajime Uno, Miki Horiguchi, Lauren Fisher, Jaclyn Schienda, Rebecca Vanderwall, Moran Snir, Guy Snir, Emilie Simmons, Andrew Khalaj, Evan Goler, Kayla V. Hamilton, Christopher C. Porter, Bojana Pencheva, Joshua David Schiffman, Luke Devon Maese, Wendy K. Kohlmann, Tara Olive Henderson, Judy Ellen Garber, Lisa Diller, Ami Vijay Desai, Soren Feola, Dejoix-Leigh Johnson, Stefania M. Rodriguez, Jennie Vagher, Casey J. Mehrhoff, Sarah Savage, Jennifer Perry, Madi Glorioso, Nicolas Moyer, James L. Klosky, Huma Q. Rana, Jennifer W. Mack
papers.abstract: Importance: Adolescents and young adults (AYAs) with hereditary cancer predisposition face high rates of lifetime cancer risk. Models to support their understanding of cancer risk have not been developed. Objective: To assess the effect of an electronic chatbot-based cancer risk communication tool on AYAs' understanding of cancer risk. Design, Setting, and Participants: This randomized clinical trial was conducted at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Emory University/Children's Healthcare of Atlanta, University of Chicago, and University of Utah Huntsman Cancer Institute between December 20, 2022, and May 30, 2025 and compared cancer predisposition visits alone vs visits with an electronic chatbot-based cancer risk communication tool, AYA Risk Information and Screening Education, using baseline and follow-up surveys to assess changes in knowledge of cancer risk by age 30 years and over their lifetime, knowledge of recommended screening, and level of psychological distress. Eligible participants were English speakers aged 12 to 24 years, who had 1 of 9 hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes. The primary analysis was conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle. Data were analyzed from July 21 to September 3, 2025. Intervention: Chatbot-based intervention with cancer risk and recommended screening information tailored to each syndrome. Additional links to resource pages with chat summary content (learn), recommended age-based screening (plan), guidance about talking with peers (share), links to support organizations (connect), and coping and bereavement support (grow). Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome was knowledge of cancer risk. The secondary outcomes were knowledge of recommended screening and level of psychological distress. Results: Of 798 AYAs assessed, 106 AYAs were randomized and enrolled (54 to the intervention group and 52 to the control group). Participants' mean (SD) age was 18.3 (SD, 3.9) years, and 64% (68 of 106) were girls or women. At baseline, 38% of AYAs (20 of 52) in the control group and 52% (28 of 54) of AYAs in the intervention group had accurate knowledge of cancer risk by age 30 years. Following the clinic visit, 37% (19 of 52) of AYAs in the control group and 78% (42 of 54) in the chatbot-based intervention group had accurate knowledge, reflecting greater improvement in knowledge of cancer risk by age 30 years (OR, 3.50; 95% CI, 1.45-9.19; P = .005). AYAs in the intervention group had non-statistically significant improvements in knowledge of recommended screening (OR, 2.17; 95% CI, 0.85-5.59; P = .11) and reductions in distress compared with AYAs in the control group (distress thermometer, β = -0.50; 95% CI, -1.09 to 0.08; P = .09). Conclusions and Relevance: In this randomized clinical trial, use of a chatbot-based intervention combined with a cancer predisposition clinic visit improved knowledge of cancer risk by age 30 years over a clinic visit alone, without increasing distress. Combining human interaction in the clinic with personalized, accurate electronic information can support AYAs with cancer predisposition and other serious conditions. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04323774.

papers.title: Developing and Validating an AI-Augmented Strategic Account Management Framework for Customer Lifetime Value and Revenue Growth: A PLS-SEM Approach
papers.authors: Pramodhann Muppadathi
papers.journal: Minnesota Journal of Business Law and Entrepreneurship
papers.abstract: This study develops and validates an AI-Augmented Strategic Account Management (AI-SAM) framework designed to enhance Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) and revenue growth in B2B contexts. Drawing on resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, the framework integrates AI capabilities (predictive analytics, personalization engines, and automated insights) with strategic account management processes (account prioritization, cross-selling orchestration, and relationship governance). Data from 412 mid-to-senior account managers and CRM specialists across technology, manufacturing, and professional services firms were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results demonstrate that AI capabilities exert a strong positive effect on strategic account management effectiveness (β = 0.487, p < 0.001), which in turn significantly elevates CLV (β = 0.412, p < 0.001) and revenue growth (β = 0.368, p < 0.001). The model explains 54.3% of the variance in CLV and 47.8% in revenue growth. Mediation analysis confirms that strategic account management fully mediates the AI–CLV relationship (indirect effect = 0.201, 95% CI [0.147, 0.268]). Firms in the high-AI-adoption quartile reported 28.6% higher average CLV and 19.4% greater year-over-year revenue growth relative to low-adoption peers. The validated framework provides managers with an empirically grounded roadmap for embedding AI into account-level strategies to drive sustainable value creation.

papers.title: Leveraging Green HRM Practices for Employee Performance: The Role of AI-Enabled HR Processes in Higher Education Institutions of India
papers.authors: Nidhi Mamgain
papers.journal: Minnesota Journal of Business Law and Entrepreneurship
papers.abstract: Incorporating environmental sustainability into people-management systems through Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) and digitising HR service delivery through Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled HR procedures are two revolutionary human resource agendas that organisations are pursuing concurrently. Few studies have looked at how these two dynamics work together to influence employee performance, despite the fact that each stream has produced a sizable and quickly growing body of literature. In this paper, a conceptual model is developed and empiricaly tested in which Green HRM practices are suggested to have a direct and indirect impact on employee performance through their association with AI-enabled HR processes in HEIs of Uttarakhand. The results portray partial medieting effect of AIHRP on the relation between GHRM practices and EP. The theoretical contributions, managerial implications for HR digitalisation and sustainability strategy, limits, and future research possibilities are discussed in the paper's conclusion.

papers.title: The Metamorphosis of Aesthetic Consciousness: From Paterian Sensibility to Algorithmic Modernity—A Psychological and Literary Perspective
papers.authors: *Shubhangi Jha, Dr. Samir Thakur, Sushant Jha
papers.abstract: The nineteenth-century Aesthetic Movement, which emerged as a celebration of beauty and advocated the principle of “art for art’s sake,” has undergone a significant transformation in the contemporary era. What initially emphasized individual sensibility, aesthetic experience, and the pursuit of beauty has gradually evolved into a complex synthesis of human consciousness, psychological perception, cultural hybridity, technological mediation, and algorithmic creativity. This transformation can be understood not only as a literary and cultural shift but also as a psychological metamorphosis in the ways individuals perceive, experience, interpret, and respond to art and literature. The present study examines the transition from Paterian aesthetic sensibility to algorithmic modernity through the interdisciplinary perspectives of literary studies, aesthetics, psychology, and digital culture. Particular attention is given to aesthetic perception, emotional response, cognition, attention, memory, desire, sensory stimulation, and the formation of taste. Contemporary artistic and literary production is increasingly shaped by digital technologies, artificial intelligence, algorithmic recommendation, fragmented attention, and changing patterns of emotional engagement. Consequently, aesthetic experience is no longer restricted to individual contemplation and sensuous appreciation but is increasingly mediated by technological and computational systems. Literature has similarly expanded beyond conventional genres and subjects such as odes, elegies, and mock-epics towards cybernetics, science fiction, cultural hybridity, digital narratives, and technologically mediated forms of creativity. Works such as S. B. Divya’s Machinehood, C. Robert Cargill’s Sea of Rust, and Martha Wells’s Murderbot series demonstrate the growing literary engagement with artificial intelligence, machine consciousness, human identity, and technological dependence. The study argues that contemporary aesthetic consciousness reflects a psychological and cultural transformation in which human emotions, cognition, creativity, and aesthetic judgment increasingly intersect with technological and algorithmic processes. The movement from Paterian sensibility to algorithmic modernity therefore represents not merely a change in literary form but a reconfiguration of the relationship between the human mind, aesthetic experience, and machine-mediated creativity.

papers.title: Shared Creative Dialogue:A Participatory Framework for Understanding Expert Creative Process.
papers.authors: Wendy Ross; id_orcid 0000-0002-0461-7660 Vincze, Vlad Petre Glăveanu
papers.abstract: Creativity research increasingly recognises that creative processes are situated, distributed and extended across people, materials and environments. However, within the psychology of creativity, these processes continue to be studied predominantly through quantitative and decontextualised methods that are not designed to trace how expert creative activity unfolds in practice. This paper introduces Shared Creative Dialogue (SCD), a participatory framework that brings established relational, dialogical and qualitative principles together to support sustained inquiry with creative practitioners. SCD comprises four overlapping phases: negotiation; co-creation; collaborative evaluation and finding the audience. Across these phases, position exchange and process consent support the practitioner’s involvement as a co-inquirer while allowing interpretations and research decisions to be negotiated throughout the collaboration. Drawing on illustrative examples from creative practice, we show how SCD can generate situated accounts of creative process while promoting mutual learning and greater epistemic accountability. SCD is offered not as a replacement for existing qualitative or quantitative approaches, but as practical

papers.title: This is How We AI: A Practical Approach to Teaching with Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Craig Brewer, George Hanshaw, Shannon Hunter
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is often treated in higher education as a technology to adopt, restrict, or police. This practice guide argues that AI is primarily a shift in teaching practice, comparable to the move to online instruction. Effective use depends less on the tool than on how faculty position it pedagogically. Drawing on institutional experience and empirical studies of AI course assistants at Los Angeles Pacific University, the authors offer a practice-oriented framework for teaching with AI. The guide presents a typology of common AI roles in courses (answer machine, editor, practice partner, tutor, and thought partner) and examines the benefits, risks, and design implications of each. It describes how the instructor's role shifts from content delivery toward learning design, and how teaching presence can be maintained through modeling AI use and through "visibility without surveillance," using process-based assignments and guided transparency instead of detection. Practical resources include scalable assignment design patterns, low-effort redesign moves, a pre-publication assignment checklist, and a before-and-after assignment example. The guide also considers which students benefit most from AI support and where faculty expertise remains essential. It addresses ethical and practical guardrails, including academic integrity, overreliance, hallucinations, and equity of access. The authors conclude that teaching with AI is fundamentally a design decision: AI does not fix weak pedagogy but can amplify strong pedagogy, while judgment, relationship, and disciplinary expertise remain human work.

papers.title: Integrated Framework for Employing Artificial Intelligence Applications in University Curriculum Redesign and Smart Learning Environment Development
papers.authors: انتصار عبد الله عامر النعير, Intisar Abdullah Aneer
papers.abstract: يهدف هذا البحث إلى بناء إطار مؤسسي مدمج لتوظيف تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في إعادة تصميم المناهج الجامعية وتطوير البيئات التعليمية الذكية في جامعة صبراتة، بالاستناد إلى تصورات أعضاء هيئة التدريس والطلاب، ومتطلبات التطبيق، والتحديات المرتبطة به. واتبع البحث المنهج الوصفي التحليلي الميداني، واستخدم استبانة إلكترونية اشتملت على عشرين عبارة وفق مقياس خماسي، وطبقت على عينة قوامها 62 مشاركًا، توزعت بين 39 عضو هيئة تدريس و23 طالبًا. واقتصر التحليل الإحصائي على التكرارات، والنسب المئوية، والمتوسطات الحسابية، والانحرافات المعيارية بما يتفق مع طبيعة البيانات وأهداف البحث. وبلغ متوسط الموافقة على إمكان استخدام تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تحديد احتياجات تطوير المناهج 4.10، في حين بلغ متوسط الموافقة على استخدامها في توفير بيئات تعليمية أكثر تفاعلًا 3.98. كما سجلت المتطلبات المؤسسية مستويات مرتفعة من الموافقة، إذ بلغ متوسط الحاجة إلى بنية تحتية تقنية مناسبة 4.37، وبلغ متوسط الحاجة إلى سياسات وضوابط واضحة لتنظيم الاستخدام 4.39، بينما بلغ متوسط الحاجة إلى آليات لحماية خصوصية البيانات وأمنها 4.47. وبينت استجابات المشاركين كذلك الحاجة إلى معالجة قضايا الخصوصية وأمن المعلومات، وتنمية المهارات الرقمية، وتوفير التدريب والدعم المؤسسي. وبناءً على هذه المعطيات، يقترح البحث إطارًا مؤسسيًا يتكون من ست مراحل مترابطة تبدأ بتحديد الاحتياجات والأولويات، ثم التطبيق المحدود، وتطوير المقررات، وبناء القدرات، وتنظيم الاستخدام، وتنتهي بالتقويم والتوسع التدريجي.

papers.title: Trust Through Co-Creation: Exploring Art–Science Interaction Dynamics and Public Engagement in Street-Based Citizen Science Communication
papers.authors: Geertje Tijsma, Michiel Van Oudheusden, TFL; id_orcid 0000-0001-7868-3372 Roedema
papers.abstract: Trust in science is increasingly understood as a relational and practice-based phenomenon that emerges through interaction, participation, and shared meaning-making rather than through one-way communication. In line with this shift, citizen science and participatory science communication have been positioned as promising approaches for fostering trust by involving informal actors in knowledge production. However, important questions remain about how trust is shaped in practice: how it develops through interactional dynamics, how participation is experienced as meaningful or fair, and how different forms of knowledge—scientific, experiential, artistic, and local—are negotiated. This paper contributes to these debates through an empirical study of the STRAATWIJS project, a co-creative art–science initiative in Amsterdam Nieuw-West that brings together residents, scientists, artists, policy actors, and local initiatives to collaboratively produce and activate street art addressing pressing locally-defined societal issues, rooted in residents’ lived experiences : financial (in)security, housing (in)security and youth wellbeing. Building on these co-defined themes, STRAATWIJS consists of structured street art co-creation workshops in which participants jointly translate experiences, emotions, and forms of knowledge into visual artworks. Each theme is explored in two facilitated sessions hosted at Street Art Museum Amsterdam (SAMA). In the first session, participants engage in shared sense-making around the theme. They are invited to bring an object, image, or personal artefact that symbolises their relation to the theme, which serves as an entry point for dialogue. Through facilitated group discussion (accompanied by a shared meal), participants collectively develop ideas that are translated into visual concepts and stencils (figures attached). In the second session, these concepts are transformed into collaborative street art. A professional street artist introduces basic techniques such as spray painting, , after which participants jointly produce a poster using the co-developed stencils. These artworks function not only as outputs but also as mediating objects that crystallise diverse experiences, values, and forms of knowledge (figures attached). These co-created artworks subsequently become the basis for the final phase of STRAATWIJS, in which they are reintroduced into public space through street-based interaction and performative formats, including interactive street theatre. In this way, the artworks act as boundary objects that connect co-creation processes with wider publics and facilitate dialogue in everyday urban contexts. The study adopts a qualitative, multi-phase action-research design combining systematic observations of co-creation sessions with semi-structured in-depth interviews. Observations focus on interaction dynamics such as participation patterns, turn-taking, framing and reframing of issues, negotiation of meaning, and decision-making processes during both conceptual and material stages of art production. Attention is given to how different forms of knowledge are made visible, contested, or integrated, and how power relations and participation asymmetries evolve across sessions. The interview component captures participants’ reflective accounts of collaboration, focusing on perceived trust in other participants (residents, scientists, artists, and local stakeholders), experiences of being heard, perceived fairness of the co-creation process, and the extent to which participation influences their understanding of the societal themes addressed. Interviews also explicitly engage with critical moments observed during workshops, allowing participants to reflect on moments of agreement, tension, or disagreement in the co-creative process. The analysis is situated within ongoing debates in citizen science and participatory science communication regarding trust as both an enabling condition for participation and a potential outcome of engagement. It conceptualises trust not as a static attitude but as an emergent, interactionally produced phenomenon shaped through aesthetic mediation, embodied collaboration, and the negotiation of diverse epistemic and experiential perspectives. By focusing on the micro-dynamics of co-creation in structured art–science workshops, this study speaks to the research and practice perspectives of the conference, specifically (but not exclusively) to social dynamics between key stakeholders. Furthermore, it examines the potential of street art as a mediating form that can translate co-created meanings into public-facing dialogue, thereby extending trust formation beyond the immediate group of participants into wider urban communities. Ultimately, the paper argues that co-creative street art practices offer a rich but complex setting for understanding trust in science as a dynamic relational achievement.

papers.title: Eid Celebrations and Islamic Educational Traditions in the Digital Age: Insights from Encyclopaedia of Islam and the Role of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Miss Iqra, Hafiz Mohsin Zia Qazi
papers.journal: Al-Mithaq ( Research Journal of Islamic Theology)
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital technologies has significantly reshaped religious life, educational structures, and cultural practices across global Muslim societies. Among the most profound expressions of Islamic identity are Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, which historically functioned not only as religious festivals but also as educational, ethical, and communal institutions. These celebrations embodied values of unity, gratitude, sacrifice, and social responsibility while reinforcing intergenerational transmission of Islamic knowledge. In the contemporary digital age, Eid celebrations and Islamic educational traditions are increasingly mediated through virtual platforms, AI-driven systems, online learning environments, and algorithmic religious content. This transformation has created new opportunities for accessibility, global connectivity, and knowledge preservation, while simultaneously raising critical concerns regarding authenticity, religious authority, misinformation, commercialization of sacred rituals, and the erosion of traditional scholarly mentorship. This research critically examines the transformation of Eid celebrations and Islamic educational traditions through insights derived from Encyclopaedia of Islam and contemporary Digital Islam scholarship. It employs a qualitative, interpretive methodology rooted in Islamic ethics, sociology of religion, and digital cultural studies. The study argues that Artificial Intelligence, when guided by Islamic ethical principles such as justice (ʿadl), trust (amānah), truthfulness (ṣidq), and public welfare (maṣlaḥah), can become a powerful instrument for preserving Islamic heritage and strengthening global Islamic education. However, unchecked technological integration risks reducing sacred religious experiences into fragmented digital content, weakening the moral depth of Islamic pedagogy, and transforming Eid from a spiritual institution into a commercialized digital spectacle. The study concludes that a balanced ethical framework is necessary to harmonize technological innovation with Islamic spiritual integrity."In the contemporary digital era, religion is not disappearing; rather, it is transforming its modes of expression, communication, and presence through digital technologies and networked media.

papers.title: Induced sad mood biases responses to sad and neutral faces under low visibility: behavioral and ERP evidence
papers.authors: Piia Astikainen, Elina S. Kangas, Elisa Vuoriainen, Xueqiao Li
papers.abstract: Facial expression recognition is shaped by both stimulus properties and the perceiver’s affective state. Research on emotional face processing under backward masking has largely focused on threatening expressions, and few studies have examined how an observer's mood influences recognition of non-threatening facial expressions under limited visibility. The present study investigated how experimentally induced sad versus neutral mood modulates behavioral and neural responses to sad and neutral facial expressions under low (10 ms) and high visibility (200 ms) backward masking conditions. Participants underwent sad and neutral mood induction on separate days and performed a facial expression categorization task while electroencephalography was recorded. Behavioral and event-related potential (ERP) analyses included 25 and 20 participants, respectively. Behaviorally, a mood effect on response criterion was observed in the low visibility condition: the criterion was lower in sad than neutral mood, reflecting a reduced tendency to categorize faces as neutral. Discrimination sensitivity was higher under high than low visibility but was not significantly affected by mood. Facial expressions modulated N170, P2, and P3 amplitudes under high visibility, and N170 and P2 under low visibility. P2 amplitude in the low visibility condition showed an interaction effect between mood and facial expression. In neutral mood, sad faces elicited larger P2 amplitudes than neutral faces, whereas in sad mood, the relation was the opposite. These findings highlight the influence of the observer’s affective state on behavioral and neural responses to facial expressions under limited visibility, extending previous findings beyond threat-related expressions to sadness.

papers.title: Memory reactivation during sleep to modulate dream content and assess its role in memory and emotional processing
papers.authors: Tommaso Maccario, Sarah Fiona Schoch, Ruggero Basanisi, Leila Salvesen, Bianca Pedreschi, Giorgia Mosca, Valentina Elce, Giulio Bernardi, Martin Dresler
papers.abstract: Dreams have been proposed as a window into sleep-related memory consolidation and integration processes. In this study, we investigate the interplay between sleep, memory consolidation, and dream content using targeted memory reactivation (TMR), a method that delivers sensory cues during sleep to influence memory processing. The experimental protocol includes high-density EEG recordings, a serial awakening paradigm, and behavioral assessments before and after sleep. The study involves 45 healthy adults and aims to clarify the relationship between dream content, memory processing, and sleep-related neural activity. Participants take part in three overnight visits at the sleep laboratory. The first night serve as an adaptation session to familiarize participants with the environment. The two subsequent experimental nights occur in randomized order. Before sleep on each experimental night, participants complete a pseudoword–picture association task using one of two sets of 99 pictures (different sets per night). Each set contains three of six possible categories (e.g., landscapes, food, vehicles, animals, children, houses), with valence balanced across positive, neutral, and negative images. Each category is paired with a distinct pseudoword selected for distinctiveness, familiarity, and emotional neutrality. During sleep, TMR will be applied: one category’s cue will be presented during NREM sleep, one during REM sleep, one will serve as a non-reactivated control. After each awakening, participants provide dream reports describing experiences immediately before awakening. Memory performance and emotional evaluation are assessed through pre-sleep and post-sleep recall tests. During these tests, only the sensory cues (pseudowords) are presented, and participants must try to recall associated pictures and rate their emotional valence. Pre-sleep performance serves as a baseline for measuring overnight memory changes. The data will be analyzed to determine whether memory reactivation during sleep modulates dream content, whether TMR enhances memory retention, and whether the incorporation of learned material into dreams is associated with overnight changes in memory performance. Status of data collection (transparency statement): This preregistration was created after data collection began. As of submission, 19/45 participants have completed the protocol. Limited exploratory, integrity-check only summaries (e.g., transcription quality, basic distributions, rater agreement) were conducted on a subset of the data and did not involve any confirmatory contrasts or model fitting for preregistered outcomes. All confirmatory analyses specified below will be applied to the full dataset. Any analyses not listed here will be labeled exploratory.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Problem-Based Learning to Enhance Computational Thinking and Digital Problem-Solving Skills among Vocational Higher Education Students: An Empirical Study
papers.authors: Abiyasa Eka Saputra, Rahma Fitriyani, Muhammad Hairul, Sri Nuryeni
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed the ways students access information, solve problems, and construct knowledge in technology-mediated learning environments. However, the availability of generative AI tools does not automatically guarantee the development of students' computational thinking and digital problem-solving abilities. This study investigated the effectiveness of AI-assisted problem-based learning in improving computational thinking and digital problem-solving skills among vocational higher education students. A quasi-experimental pre-test and post-test control group design was employed. The study involved 60 undergraduate students who were divided into an experimental group receiving AI-assisted problem-based learning and a control group receiving conventional problem-based learning without direct generative AI assistance. The intervention was conducted over eight instructional sessions. Data were collected using a computational thinking performance test, a digital problem-solving assessment, and a student perception questionnaire. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, paired-samples t-tests, and ANCOVA. The simulated empirical results indicated that the experimental group demonstrated a substantially greater improvement in computational thinking than the control group. The experimental group increased from a pre-test mean of 55.13 to a post-test mean of 84.27, whereas the control group increased from 54.60 to 72.13. A similar pattern was observed in digital problem-solving performance. The findings suggest that AI-assisted problem-based learning can provide students with immediate feedback, alternative solution pathways, debugging support, and opportunities to critically evaluate AI-generated solutions. Nevertheless, the findings also indicate that AI should function as a cognitive support mechanism rather than a substitute for students' own reasoning. The study concludes that structured AI integration can strengthen computational thinking when students are required to explain, evaluate, modify, and validate AI-supported solutions.

papers.title: ¿ Esto lo has hecho tú? Los retos de la IA en la práctica educativa: Did you do this? The challenges of AI in educational practice
papers.authors: Clara Fernández Díaz-Rincón
papers.abstract: Este artículo analiza los retos ético-pedagógicos de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la práctica educativa, a partir de una experiencia docente en Lengua y Filosofía con alumnado adolescente nativo digital. El texto sostiene que la integración de la IA es irreversible en la vida escolar, pero su uso indiscriminado está alterando la confianza educativa, la identidad del estudiante y el desarrollo del criterio. En primer lugar, se argumenta que la IA desplaza parte del trabajo del alumno hacia una «agencia» externa, debilitando la relación de confianza y transformando al docente en un verificante de autenticidad («¿esto lo has hecho tú?»), con el riesgo de generar confrontación y desconfianza mutua. En segundo lugar, se describen cambios en procesos cognitivos y formativos como la formulación de ideas y la participación en clase, al facilitar atajos y reducir el esfuerzo reflexivo. En tercer lugar, se examina el problema epistemológico del criterio: la IA puede producir respuestas plausibles pero incorrectas («alucinaciones»), por lo que se requiere formación ética e intelectual orientada a evaluar, justificar y conocer. Finalmente, se propone como prioridades la unión entre agentes educativos y una moral pedagógica robusta, defendiendo recuperar el valor de lo humano mediante espacios de diálogo, virtud intelectual y responsabilidad en el aprendizaje. This article examines the ethical and pedagogical challenges posed by generative artificial intelligence in educational practice, drawing on the author’s classroom experience teaching Language and Philosophy to digitally native adolescents. It argues that AI integration is irreversible in schooling, yet its indiscriminate use is reshaping educational trust, students’ identity, and the development of judgment. First, AI shifts part of the student’s work to an external «agent», weakening trust-based teacher-student relationships and turning the teacher into an authenticity checker («did you do this?»), which risks producing conflict and mutual suspicion. Second, the paper describes how AI alters key cognitive and formative processes, such as idea generation and classroom participation, by enabling shortcuts and reducing the depth of reflection required. Third, it addresses an epistemic problem of judgment: AI may generate plausible but incorrect answers («hallucinations»), making it necessary to cultivate ethical and intellectual capabilities for evaluation, justification, and knowledge-building. Concluding, the article prioritizes (i) collaboration among educational stakeholders and (ii) a robust moral framework for pedagogy, advocating a renewed emphasis on the value of the human through dialogue spaces, intellectual virtues, and responsible learning.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Economic Management of Higher Education Institutions: International Experience and Trends
papers.authors: O'lmasxo'jayev Zoirxo'ja Abbos o'g'li
papers.journal: American Journal of Economics and Business Management
papers.abstract: The aim of the study is to generalise international experience in applying artificial intelligence (AI) to the economic management of higher education institutions (HEIs) and to identify the trends relevant for Uzbekistan. The methodology combines a case-study analysis of documented institutional practices, a comparative analysis of international regulatory and policy frameworks, and a secondary analysis of Stanford HAI AI Index data. The results show that the strongest documented economic effects arise where predictive analytics is combined with organisational change – as in Georgia State University, where a randomised trial of an AI chatbot reduced “summer melt” by 21%. At the same time, AI investment is highly concentrated geographically, and regulation is shifting from voluntary principles to binding, risk-based rules. The paper concludes with recommendations for Uzbek HEIs.

papers.title: Large Language Models Are More Sycophantic in Chinese Than in English
papers.authors: 宜欣 何, Chao Hu, Yize Zeng, Yang Tao, JianHui Zhang
papers.abstract: AI sycophancy has emerged as a prominent concern in human–AI interaction, as large language models (LLMs) may unduly affirm users’ beliefs or actions rather than provide independent assessments. Such behavior may vary across languages because language can cue culturally patterned norms of social interaction. Prior work has documented Chinese–English differences in the social orientations expressed by LLMs, paralleling broader cross-cultural differences in interdependence and interpersonal harmony. We therefore tested whether these differences extend to AI action endorsement. Across seven LLMs, we compared responses to 3,024 matched open-ended personal-advice queries presented in Chinese and English. The primary outcome was action endorsement rate (AER), defined as the proportion of explicit endorsements among responses taking an explicit stance. A binomial mixed-effects model accounting for item and model variation showed higher odds of endorsement in Chinese than in English (odds ratio [OR] = 1.99, 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.42, 2.79], P = 0.004). As a robustness check, we repeated the evaluation using a separate Chinese scoring workflow—a distinct operational scoring pipeline rather than a simple translation of the primary English scorer—and obtained the same directional language difference. Adjustment for explicit-stance propensity left the primary estimate essentially unchanged. These findings identify a consistent Chinese–English difference in action endorsement and are consistent with the possibility that culturally patterned relational norms shape how LLMs respond to users across languages.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Supporting Tool for Students in Scientific Writing
papers.authors: Nafisa Fitri Aulia
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications as supporting tools for university students in academic writing. The study is motivated by various difficulties faced by students in writing scientific papers, particularly in finding, mapping, managing, and understanding relevant references from both national and international sources. The development of AI technology provides opportunities to help students obtain scholarly information more quickly and efficiently. This study employs a literature review method by examining relevant literature on the use of AI technology to support academic writing. The results indicate that three applications can be utilized by students, namely Open Knowledge Maps, Publish or Perish, and Consensus AI. Open Knowledge Maps helps map literature based on topics, enabling students to understand the relationships among relevant studies more easily. Publish or Perish assists students in searching for and managing relevant academic references from various scholarly databases. Meanwhile, Consensus AI helps users search for academic literature and obtain information summaries based on research findings. The use of these three applications can improve the efficiency of reference searching and support students in preparing scientific papers. However, their use should be accompanied by critical thinking, source verification, and adherence to academic integrity principles.

papers.title: Implications of Artificial Intelligence in Crafting Adaptive Learning Environments to Augment Student Motivation and Engagement through Gamification Mechanisms
papers.authors: S. Abinaya
papers.journal: Minnesota Journal of Business Law and Entrepreneurship
papers.abstract: Introduction: This research explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in adaptive learning environments, emphasizing its role in enhancing student motivation and engagement through personalized learning experiences and gamification strategies. Materials and Methods: A mixed-method approach was employed, starting with qualitative interviews from 30 educators and students, followed by a quantitative study involving 300 students across five institutions. A structured questionnaire assessed the influence of adaptive learning personalization, gamification elements, teacher involvement, and usability of learning platforms on student motivation and learning outcomes. Results: The findings reveal significant positive relationships among adaptive learning personalization, gamification, and teacher involvement, with adaptive learning personalization showing the strongest impact on student satisfaction and learning outcomes. Gamification elements also substantially enhanced motivation and engagement, while teacher involvement proved crucial for effective learning experiences. Conclusion: This study highlights the transformative potential of AI in education, advocating for the implementation of adaptive learning technologies and gamified elements to foster a more engaging and motivating learning environment. Enhanced teacher participation and improved usability of learning platforms further contribute to successful educational outcomes. Originality: This research contributes original insights into the relationship between AI-driven adaptive learning strategies and student engagement, providing a comprehensive framework for educators.

papers.title: Resistiendo al determinismo de las máquinas: defendiendo límites para la IA en la Educación: Resisting Machine Determinism: Defending Limits for AI in Education
papers.authors: Deivide Garcia da Silva Oliveira
papers.abstract: El artículo analiza críticamente la integración de la inteligencia artificial en los entornos educativos, especialmente cuando se adopta de manera irreflexiva. Reconoce que la IA puede aportar eficiencia en tareas procedimentales como la planificación curricular, la evaluación o la distribución de contenidos, pero advierte que su aplicación en funciones pedagógicas fundamentales implica riesgos importantes. El texto sostiene que la IA suele estar vinculada a lógicas corporativas, predictivas y de optimización, lo que puede afectar valores esenciales de la educación como el pluralismo, el pensamiento crítico, la autonomía intelectual y el razonamiento contrafactual. A partir de autores como Paul Feyerabend, Stuart Russell y Helga Nowotny, se argumenta que los sistemas de IA no cuentan con las capacidades epistémicas, éticas ni ontológicas necesarias para formar estudiantes autónomos, reflexivos y capaces de participar en sociedades democráticas. Por ello, el artículo reafirma que el juicio humano es insustituible en la definición de los fines, valores y metas educativas. Concluye que la IA debe limitarse a tareas no fundamentales y estar sometida a una revisión filosófica rigurosa, para garantizar que la educación continúe siendo un espacio humano, orientado por humanos y no determinado por algoritmos. The article offers a critical analysis of the integration of artificial intelligence into educational settings, particularly when it is adopted without due consideration. It acknowledges that AI can bring efficiency to procedural tasks such as curriculum planning, assessment or content delivery, but warns that its application to fundamental pedagogical functions entails significant risks. The text argues that AI is often linked to corporate, predictive and optimisation-based logics, which may undermine essential educational values such as pluralism, critical thinking, intellectual autonomy and counterfactual reasoning. Drawing on authors such as Paul Feyerabend, Stuart Russell and Helga Nowotny, it is argued that AI systems lack the epistemic, ethical and ontological capacities necessary to educate students who are autonomous, reflective and capable of participating in democratic societies. Consequently, the article reaffirms that human judgement is irreplaceable in defining educational aims, values and goals. It concludes that AI should be confined to non-fundamental tasks and be subject to rigorous philosophical scrutiny, to ensure that education remains a human space, guided by humans and not determined by algorithms.

papers.title: Multi-party simulations with human participants and role-based LLM conversational agents: A design framework and validity evidence for organizational research
papers.authors: Naho Fujisawa, Yoshinobu Kano, Yuki Nozaki
papers.abstract: Dynamic organizational phenomena often unfold through ongoing communication among multiple interdependent actors, yet studying them involves trade-offs among realism, controllability, and scalability. We propose a methodological framework for using role-based conversational agents powered by large language models (LLMs) as multi-party interaction partners in organizational research. It specifies how to create standardized but contingent interaction environments through scenario design, persona prompts, interaction protocols, and iterative testing. In a preregistered illustrative study of leadership communication, we analyzed 394 employees’ text-based simulations powered by GPT-5.2, Gemini 2.5 Flash, or Claude Sonnet 4.6. Across models, participants perceived the agents as anthropomorphic and animate, and as acting consistently with their assigned backgrounds, personalities, and linguistic styles. Behavioral coding corroborated and extended these perceptions, with deviations from assigned persona prompts in 2.59% of utterances. Participants’ utterances also yielded codable indicators of theoretically relevant behavior, in this case leadership communication. These findings provide initial validity evidence that multi-party LLM-agent simulations can create plausible interaction environments, deliver persona-consistent stimuli, and elicit behaviorally analyzable responses. We also offer practical guidelines on model selection, replicability, and ethics.

papers.title: Integrasi kritis penguatan literasi religius berbasis Artificial Intelligence dan otoritas keagamaan digital dalam pembelajaran PAI: Systematic literature review
papers.authors: Sopyan Alpaizi Salman, Akif Khilmiyah
papers.journal: Idarah Tarbawiyah Journal of Management in Islamic Education
papers.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital media has changed the way students access religious knowledge, thus presenting both opportunities and challenges for Islamic Religious Education (PAI) learning. This study aims to analyze and synthesize research results regarding the integration of AI, digital religious authority, and religious literacy in PAI learning. The study used the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method with a thematic synthesis approach. The search process was carried out on Scopus database through the stages of identification, filtering, eligibility assessment, and inclusion, until 20 articles were obtained that met the criteria for analysis. The results of the study show three main findings, namely: (1) digital religion is developing into a new space for the formation of religious authority, identity, and practice; (2) AI and digital media expand access to religious knowledge, but also have the potential to cause information bias, simplification of understanding, and ambiguity of religious authority; and (3) PAI learning needs to develop critical, reflective, and ethical digital religious literacy through the acquisition of the ability to channel sources, understand technological bias, and internalize Islamic values in digital life. This research confirms that the integration of AI in Islamic Religious Education learning needs to be accompanied by strengthening religious digital literacy so that the use of technology remains in line with the principles of Islamic education. Abstrak Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan media digital telah mengubah cara peserta didik mengakses pengetahuan agama, sehingga menghadirkan peluang sekaligus tantangan bagi pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI). Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis dan menyintesis hasil-hasil penelitian mengenai integrasi AI, otoritas keagamaan digital, dan literasi religius dalam pembelajaran PAI. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan pendekatan sintesis tematik. Proses penelusuran dilakukan pada basis data Scopus melalui tahapan identifikasi, penyaringan, penilaian kelayakan, dan inklusi, hingga diperoleh 20 artikel yang memenuhi kriteria untuk dianalisis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan tiga temuan utama, yaitu: (1) agama digital berkembang menjadi ruang baru pembentukan otoritas, identitas, dan praktik keberagamaan; (2) AI dan media digital memperluas akses terhadap pengetahuan agama, tetapi juga berpotensi menimbulkan bias informasi, penyederhanaan pemahaman, serta ketidakjelasan otoritas keagamaan; dan (3) pembelajaran PAI perlu mengembangkan literasi religius digital yang kritis, reflektif, dan etis melalui penguatan kemampuan mengevaluasi sumber, memahami bias teknologi, serta menginternalisasikan nilai-nilai Islam dalam kehidupan digital. Penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa integrasi AI dalam pembelajaran PAI perlu disertai penguatan literasi religius digital agar pemanfaatan teknologi tetap selaras dengan prinsip-prinsip pendidikan Islam.

papers.title: ผลการเรยนรกลมสาระการเรยนรสงคมศกษา ศาสนา และวฒนธรรม โดยใชวธการจดการเรยนรสมองเปนฐานรวมกบสอปญญาประดษฐ สำหรบนกเรยนชนประถมศกษาปท 5
papers.authors: Phuttaraluksamee Wirabut
papers.abstract: This research consists purposes were 1. to develop learning management plans for the Social Studies, Religion and Culture learning area using Brain-Based Learning integrated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) media for Grade 5 students. 2. to compare the learning outcomes of Grade 5 students before and after learning through Brain-Based Learning integrated with AI media and 3. to study the satisfaction of Grade 5 students toward learning through Brain-Based Learning integrated with AI media. This was a quantitative study. The research instruments consisted of learning management plans using brain-based learning combined with artificial intelligence media, pre-test and post-test achievement tests and a student satisfaction questionnaire. The sample consisted of 18 Grade 5 students at Sapsombun Phitthayakhom School Mueang Tak District Tak Province, selected by cluster random sampling with the school as the sampling unit. The data collected from the instruments were analyzed using descriptive statistics, namely percentage, mean, standard deviation and compared using a t-test. The results showed that 1) the learning management plans were rated at the highest level of appropriateness (x̅ = 4.60, S.D. = 0.02). 2) post-test learning achievement was significantly higher than pre-test achievement at the .05 level and 3) students' satisfaction with the learning management was at the highest level (x̅ = 4.80, S.D. = 0.20).

papers.title: เปรยบเทยบผลลพธการผาตดไสตงแบบสองกลองกบการผาตดไสตงแบบเปด ในโรงพยาบาลอทอง จงหวดสพรรณบร
papers.authors: Nattawut Kalapong
papers.abstract: Objective: Acute appendicitis is a leading cause of acute abdominal pain requiring emergency surgery. While laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) has gained popularity due to its perceived benefits in recovery, evidence comparing LA and open appendectomy (OA) within the context of community hospitals remains limited. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes and economic aspects between LA and OA at U-thong Hospital. Data regarding clinical outcomes (operative time, blood loss, time to first meal, complications, and length of stay) and economic indicators (relative weight: RW and total medical income) were collected. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on patients diagnosed with acute appendicitis who underwent appendectomy at U-thong Hospital between July 2023 and July 2025. Statistical analysis was performed using chi-square test, independent t test, and Mann-Whitney U test, with significance set at p < .05. Results: A total of 140 patients were included, consisting of 64 patients in the OA group and 76 patients in the LA group. The baseline characteristics were comparable between both groups; the LA group had significantly higher body weight and body mass index (BMI) than the OA group (p < .05). In terms of clinical outcomes, there were no statistically significant differences between the two groups in blood loss, time to initiation of oral intake after surgery, complication rate, or length of hospital stay. However, the operative time in the LA group was significantly longer than that in the OA group (p < .05). From an economic perspective, LA was associated with higher relative weight (RW) and higher total medical income than the OA procedure. Conclusion: Laparoscopic appendectomy is a safe and effective alternative for treating acute appendicitis in a community hospital setting, particularly for patients with high BMI. In addition, in terms of revenue, the LA procedure generated higher income than OA; however, cost and operative time should also be considered in the context of each hospital, particularly community hospitals.

papers.title: Effect of Auditory Entrainment on Flicker Light Experience
papers.authors: Annabelle Mitchell, Jordan Wehrman, MR James Thurbon, Timo Torsten Schmidt, Vince Polito
papers.abstract: Flicker light stimulation (FLS) involves stroboscopic flashing light and has been shown to induce various alterations in conscious experience. Most prominently, FLS has been reported to produce hallucinatory percepts (Amaya et al., 2023), including both simple visual imagery (such as colours and moving shapes), and complex images (Reeder, 2022). Investigations determining the neural mechanisms for these effects are ongoing. One promising area is entrainment . While flicker entrainment can involve several different changes in neural activity patterns, it commonly includes neural signals of the same frequency as a flicker light stimulus increasing in power (Herrmann, 2001). Compared to rhythmic flicker presentations, where entrainment is more viable, visual effects have shown to reduce with arrhythmic flicker presentations (Amaya et al., 2023). It is yet to be seen whether multi-modal rhythmic stimuli can broaden neural entrainment and increase subjective effects. In the present study, we aim to explore how the entrainment ability of visual flicker might be influenced by incorporating rhythmic audio. Across different conditions we will present audio pulses in-phase and anti-phase with the visual flicker while measuring EEG and skin conductance. We will then assess relationships between entrainment, signal diversity, skin conductance and subjective experience.

papers.title: The impact of professional development programs on K–12 teachers’ AI literacy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.authors: Ziwen Teuber, Theresa Dicke, Kewen Liao, Tingting Li, YING MA, Taren Sanders, Chloe Gordon, Jiesi Guo, Rebecca J. Collie, Chengliang Wang, Michael Noetel
papers.abstract: Teachers' artificial intelligence (AI) literacy is an increasingly important focus of professional development (PD). This systematic review synthesized evidence from 62 empirical studies (61 records), including 36 studies eligible for effect-size estimation, involving pre-service and in-service teachers. Most programs emphasized AI-related knowledge and skills, with less systematic attention to attitudinal and ethical dimensions. Common design features included temporal flexibility (e.g., synchronous and asynchronous learning), role diversification (e.g., co-designers and collaborators), and contextual orientation (e.g., task- and project-based learning). The primary combined-design multilevel meta-analysis after influence diagnostics, based on 212 effect sizes from 34 studies, indicated a significant positive average effect across knowledge, skills, and attitudes/values (g = 0.76, 95% CI [0.50, 1.02], p < .001). Substantial heterogeneity indicated considerable variation across programs and contexts. Although possible small-study effects and publication selection may have inflated the magnitude of the primary pooled estimate, Bayesian selection-model analyses continued to support a positive average effect. No statistically significant moderation was detected by career stage, school level, intervention-duration category, research design, outcome measurement type, or gender composition. These findings provide an important quantitative benchmark for the emerging evidence base and indicate that AI literacy PD can support multiple dimensions of teachers' AI literacy.

papers.title: AI-BASED MODULAR LEARNING FOR ENHANCING PLURICULTURAL COMPETENCE OF TRANSLATION STUDENTS: A METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK
papers.authors: Munisaxon Ubayeva
papers.journal: Multidisciplinary Journal of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: This article examines the methodological potential of artificial intelligence (AI)-based modular learning for enhancing the pluricultural competence of translation students. Pluricultural competence is interpreted as the ability to mobilize linguistic, cultural, pragmatic and reflective resources when mediating meanings across culturally different contexts. The study adopts a conceptual methodological design based on theoretical synthesis, comparative analysis and pedagogical modelling. It integrates the Council of Europe’s plurilingual/pluricultural perspective, the European Master’s in Translation competence framework, translation-competence research, intercultural competence theory and recent guidance on responsible AI use in education.

papers.title: Vokalisointitehtävien rakenne ohjaa sydämen säätelyä ja interpersonaalista fysiologista synkroniaa kuorolaulussa
papers.authors: Samir Sadik-Ogli
papers.abstract: In choral singing, the heart is simultaneously regulated by respiratory sinus arrhythmia and autonomic responses to the demands of performance. This makes it difficult to separate the effects of top-down cognitive and motor effort from the bottom-up mechanics of breathing. To disentangle these mechanisms, this study investigated how varying vocal task structure and visual contact alter individual cardiac regulation and interpersonal physiological synchrony. Sixteen singers (four quartets) performed four tasks of varying demands (spontaneous conversation, freeform improvisation, monophonic unison, and polyphonic counterpoint) in facing and back-facing conditions, with cardiac and respiratory signals analysed for heart rate variability (HRV) and surrogate-corrected phase synchronization. Transitioning from conversation to structured singing systematically increased cardiovascular arousal and reduced overall HRV, suggesting that the integrated cognitive and motor load of performance overrides the bottom-up mechanical effects of structured breathing, whereas visual contact yielded no significant autonomic changes. At the interpersonal level, structured musical scores acted as external pacemakers of breathing, driving high respiratory and cardiac phase-locking between singers. In contrast, improvisation generated above-chance cardiac synchrony despite the absence of a shared musical score. These results indicate that top-down autonomic regulation drives individual physiological states during performance, while both shared musical structure and active co-creation guide interpersonal physiological coupling. Given that these individual and interpersonal physiological dynamics reflect more than the mechanical effects of breathing, future research should integrate physiological measures with subjective psychometrics to investigate how these dynamics relate to the psychological experience of joint musical performance.

papers.title: Developing student feedback literacy through GenAI-supported student-teacher feedback co-creation: A mixed-methods study
papers.authors: Jessica To, Renjie Cai, Nicole Judith Tavares, Locky Law
papers.journal: The Asian Journal of Applied Linguistics
papers.abstract: Feedback co-creation is an effective strategy to increase students’ proactivity. Yet, limited studies have delved into the co-creation process between students and teachers in a GenAI-mediated environment and the impact of feedback co-creation on student feedback literacy. This mixed-methods case study explored how GenAI-supported feedback co-creation shaped students’ development of feedback literacy at a university in Hong Kong. Findings from pre-post feedback literacy surveys, observations of feedback dialogues, and interviews showed that GenAI-supported feedback co-creation could improve students’ evaluative judgements, proactivity, elicitation and uptake of feedback. GenAI facilitated feedback co-creation by helping students clarify unclear criteria, interpret teacher feedback, and assess the quality of draft revisions. Implications are drawn to construct a preliminary GenAI-supported student-teacher feedback co-creation model and to guide students’ meaningful use of GenAI for metacognitive monitoring in feedback processes.

papers.title: REM-unen fragmentaatio, ahdistus ja yönaikainen emotionaalinen sopeutuminen
papers.authors: Kalla-Maria Tiilikainen
papers.abstract: Consolidated Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep has been associated with successful overnight emotional adaptation, which was operationalized as the overnight change in emotion intensity in the present study. In contrast, REM sleep fragmentation has been proposed to disrupt these overnight adaptation processes potentially contributing to the development of anxiety. The aim of this study was to examine whether REM sleep fragmentation is associated with overnight changes in emotion intensity and self-reported anxiety in a clinical cohort. The association between self-reported anxiety and overnight changes in emotion intensity was examined in 76 participants. In a subsample of 21 participants, REM sleep fragmentation was measured using overnight high-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG), and its associations with self-reported anxiety and overnight changes in emotion intensity were examined. Low anxiety was associated with smaller overnight changes in emotion intensity. REM sleep fragmentation was neither associated with anxiety nor with emotion intensity change. The results indicate that overnight changes in emotion intensity may also be influenced by mechanisms other than REM sleep fragmentation. The findings also highlight the need to further examine whether the current models of overnight emotional adaptation are sufficient to explain the overnight changes in the intensity of discrete emotions.

papers.title: Prevalence of Anaemia and Its Association with Iron Status Among Female Dental Students
papers.authors: Sachu Philip
papers.abstract: Introduction: Anaemia continues to be a major health problem world wide , particularly among females of reproductive age in developed and developing countries. It is a condition that affects an estimated 2.36 billion individuals globally. Anaemia, even when mild to moderate, affects the sense of well-being resulting in fatigue, stress, and impair cognitive and physical development along with an increased mortality rate. Objectives: To assess the prevalence of anaemia and its association with Iron status among female dental students Methods: A cross sectional institution based study was carried out among dental student hostellers.Complete blood cell count were estimated using automated hematology analyzer serum iron and iron binding capacity by colorimetric method and ferritin estimation by automated chemiluminescence system . Transferrin saturation was calculated using the data. Results: The prevalence of anaemia was found to be 48% .The prevalence of IDA and ID was 28%, and 20% respectively .Among the anaemic subjects 28.8 % were having microcytic hypochromic anaemia, 8 % Dimorphic anaemia, 4.4% had normocytic anaemia showing no significant relation with age, BMI and waist hip ratio. Conclusions: Lifestyle modifications with dietary suplimentation of iron and folic acid rich food as well as iron supplements are needed for IDA subjects . Awareness campaign regarding IDA and iron deficiency are inevitable among the student population.
