papers.title: Using Generative AI to Enhance Understanding and Supervision in Undergraduate Research Projects
papers.authors: Caroline Catmur, Charlotte Hargreaves, Rebecca Upsher
papers.abstract: This project provides teaching materials for final-year psychology students completing their dissertation project, including a slide deck and accompanying workbook. The session is designed to help students use Generative AI responsibly to better understand their research project, plan next steps, and make the most of supervision meetings. Through hands-on activities, students learn how to write effective prompts, reflect on their progress using metacognition, and identify where GenAI can genuinely support their learning instead of replacing it. These materials have been used in the King’s College London BSc Psychology Projects Module and are grounded in student co-design.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Supported Sustainable Education and Students’ Environmental Learning Engagement: The Moderating Role of Environmental Self-Efficacy
papers.authors: Muhammad Faisal, Adnan Mustafa Cheema, Syeda Abida Hussain Sherazi, Faiqa Rasheed
papers.abstract: This study examined the role of Artificial Intelligence-Supported Sustainable Education in promoting students’ Environmental Learning Engagement, with particular focus on the moderating role of Environmental Self-Efficacy. A quantitative cross-sectional research design was used, and data were collected from 389 university students in Pakistan through an adopted structured questionnaire administered online using Google Forms. The collected responses were organized in Microsoft Excel and subsequently analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics. Pearson Product-Moment Correlation, simple linear regression, and moderation analysis were used to examine the relationships among the study variables. The findings showed that Artificial Intelligence-Supported Sustainable Education was positively associated with Environmental Learning Engagement and significantly predicted students’ engagement in environmental learning. The findings further indicated that Environmental Self-Efficacy significantly strengthened the relationship between AI-supported sustainable education and environmental learning engagement. These findings suggest that AI-supported educational environments can provide students with accessible, interactive, and sustainability-focused learning opportunities that may encourage greater participation in environmental learning. The study further highlights that technological support may be more effective when students possess confidence in their ability to understand environmental issues and participate in environmentally relevant learning activities. The study contributes to the emerging literature by connecting AI-supported sustainable education with environmental learning engagement while incorporating Environmental Self-Efficacy as an important individual-level factor. The findings may assist educators, higher education institutions, and policymakers in developing technology-supported sustainable learning environments that encourage active participation, environmental understanding, and meaningful student engagement.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Teacher Education: Preparing Future Educators for India’s Digital Era
papers.authors: Renu Kumari
papers.journal: International Journal on Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining the future of education by transforming teaching, learning, and teacher preparation across the world. In India, the rapid expansion of digital technologies and the implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 have created a strong foundation for integrating AI into teacher education. This paper explores how AI can prepare future educators in India with the digital, pedagogical, and professional competencies required to meet the evolving demands of 21st Century classrooms. The study is based on a comprehensive review of recent literature, policy documents and contemporary educational practices related to AI in teacher education. It examines the potential of AI-powered tools in enhancing personalized learning, lesson planning, intelligent assessment, classroom management, and continuous professional development. The review highlights that AI not only improves teaching efficiency and learner engagement but also support inclusive competency-based and data-informed educational practices. At the same time, it identifies significant infrastructure, limited AI literacy among teacher’s educators, ethical concerns, data privacy, algorithmic bias, and unequal access to technology. The study emphasizes that the successful integration of AI requires strategic policy implementation, institutional readiness, faculty capacity building and the development of ethical guidelines for responsible AI use. It concludes that AI has the potential to transform teacher education in India by empowering future educators with innovative teaching skills, critical digital competencies, and lifelong learning abilities, thereby creating a resilient, inclusive, and future-ready education system for India’s digital era.

papers.title: Ethical Perceptions and Readiness for Artificial Intelligence Integration in the Classroom Among All Dela Paz High School Teachers
papers.authors: Dariel Ojera, Francis Michael Yambao
papers.journal: Psychology and Education A Multidisciplinary Journal
papers.abstract: This study investigates the ethical perceptions and readiness for Artificial Intelligence Integration in the classroom among Dela Paz High School Teachers. Rooted in the issuance of the Department of Education Order No. 3, s. 2026, or the “Foundational Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence in Basic Education,” and the urge to integrate artificial intelligence or A.I. tools in the classroom as stipulated in Division Memorandum No. 14, s. 2026 from the Schools Division of Pasig City, or the “AI-powered literacy tools training of the Department of Education and Microsoft”. The research primarily aims to assess the ethical perceptions of teachers regarding the integration of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom, which will focus on Academic Integrity pertaining to the ownership of work and plagiarism, Algorithmic Bias or the inclusivity and fairness of the output, and Data Privacy, which will involves protection of teachers' and learners' digital footprints. The study also aims to evaluate the Dela Paz High School teachers’ readiness in integrating AI tools in the classroom across technical competency, pedagogical integration, and ethical resilience in relation to the teachers’ professional profiles. Findings reveal that, based on the profession profile of the Dela Paz High School teachers, they have a high level of perceived ethical implications and a robust and united ethical awareness of the integration of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom. However, the teachers’ exposure to AI tools should be taken into account so that the teachers are fully aware of the risks of A.I. tools. Findings also revealed that the Dela Paz High School teachers have a high and unified level of readiness for the integration of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom. In conclusion, Dela Paz High School teachers’ ethical perception and readiness are significantly related. This suggests that teachers who are more aware of the ethical dimensions (integrity, bias, and privacy) are likely the same teachers who feel better prepared to integrate Artificial Intelligence on education. Ethical awareness is not just a theoretical concern; it is a practical component of a teacher's overall readiness to use AI in the classroom.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Lesson Planning and Differentiated Instruction as Predictors of Student-Centered Learning: A Multiple Regression Analysis
papers.authors: Angel Lhi Dela Cruz, Cinly Genella, Marlon Marcelino, Fritz Biongan, Joemar Tacuel, Juvelyn Valdez, Myra Nietes, Leorence C. Tandog
papers.journal: Psychology and Education A Multidisciplinary Journal
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming educational practices by enhancing instructional planning, personalization, and learner engagement. This study examined the predictive influence of AI integration in lesson planning and differentiated instruction on student-centered learning among teachers in North Cotabato. Specifically, the study assessed the levels of AI integration, differentiated instructional planning, and student-centered learning and determined their relationships and predictive effects. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving 356 elementary and secondary school teachers. Data were collected using a validated survey questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis. The findings revealed that teachers demonstrated high levels of AI integration, differentiated instructional planning, and student-centered learning practices. Correlation analysis showed significant positive relationships between AI integration and student-centered learning, as well as between differentiated instructional planning and student-centered learning. Furthermore, multiple regression analysis confirmed that both AI integration and differentiated instructional planning significantly predicted student-centered learning, with differentiated instructional planning exerting a stronger influence. Among the dimensions examined, automation and efficiency, flexible grouping strategies, and process differentiation emerged as the strongest predictors. The results suggest that integrating AI technologies with differentiated instructional practices can effectively support learner engagement, participation, collaboration, and inclusivity. The study highlights the importance of educational technology integration and teacher innovation in fostering personalized learning experiences and strengthening student-centered classrooms. The findings provide valuable insights for educators, school leaders, and policymakers seeking to promote technology-enhanced and inclusive teaching practices aligned with sustainable educational development and SDG 4 (Quality Education).

papers.title: Активное и цифровое обучение в медицинском образовании: доказательная база, условия реализации и ограничения применения
papers.authors: Гузаль Отаева, Нурлан Динмухаммадиев
papers.abstract: Медицинское образование должно обеспечивать не только усвоение информации, но и её долговременное сохранение, перенос знаний в клиническую практику, развитие профессионального мышления и безопасное освоение практических навыков. Активное обучение, интервальное повторение, практика извлечения, перевёрнутый класс, проблемно-ориентированное и симуляционное обучение всё чаще объединяются с виртуальными пациентами, виртуальной реальностью, геймификацией и искусственным интеллектом. Однако цифровизация сама по себе не гарантирует улучшения образовательных результатов. Цель. Обобщить доказательства эффективности активных и цифровых образовательных технологий в подготовке медицинских работников, определить условия их результативного применения и основные ограничения существующей доказательной базы. Материалы и методы. Выполнен библиометрически информированный нарративный обзор публикаций 2023–2026 годов. Поиск строился вокруг понятий medical education, active learning, spaced repetition, retrieval practice, flipped classroom, problem-based learning, simulation-based education, virtual patient, virtual reality, gamification и artificial intelligence. Рабочий поисковый массив был ограничен наиболее релевантными 100 публикациями. В настоящий обзор вошли 19 систематических и обзорных исследований из этой выборки. Библиографические сведения проверялись по PubMed, Crossref и страницам издателей. Применялись цифровые инструменты для поиска, структурирования и обобщения научных источников; окончательная интерпретация данных выполнялась автором. Результаты. Наиболее последовательные доказательства получены для распределённой практики и извлечения информации из памяти: они улучшают воспроизведение знаний и их отсроченное сохранение. Перевёрнутый класс и проблемно-ориентированное обучение могут улучшать знания, клиническое мышление и вовлечённость, однако эффекты существенно зависят от качества предварительной подготовки, фасилитации и используемого контроля. Симуляционное обучение, виртуальная реальность и виртуальные пациенты создают условия для безопасной повторной практики, но их преимущества уменьшаются при отсутствии структурированного дебрифинга и переноса навыка в клиническую среду. Геймификация преимущественно влияет на мотивацию и участие; доказательства устойчивого улучшения компетентности менее определённы. Искусственный интеллект (ИИ) способен поддерживать персонализированную обратную связь, генерацию клинических сценариев и адаптивное повторение, но связан с рисками фактических ошибок, алгоритмической предвзятости, нарушения конфиденциальности и снижения самостоятельности обучающихся. Заключение. Результативность активного и цифрового обучения определяется не используемой платформой, а согласованностью целей, учебной активности, обратной связи, повторной практики и оценки переноса знаний. Оптимальным представляется интегрированный дизайн, в котором цифровые средства усиливают педагогически обоснованные методы, а не заменяют преподавателя и клинический опыт.

papers.title: Behavioural intelligence: Analytical frameworks for the future of threat intelligence
papers.authors: Nicole Wong, Nathaniel Jones, Calum Hall, Daniel Levy, Adam Potter, Emma Foulger, Nicole Carignan
papers.abstract: Traditional cyber threat intelligence (CTI) remains a valuable mechanism for attribution, contextualisation, and strategic awareness; however, its reliance on post-disclosure indicators imposes inherent temporal limitations. As adversaries increasingly exploit pre-disclosure vulnerabilities, legitimate credentials, and cloud-native attack pathways, indicator-driven detection models are frequently unable to provide timely defensive insight. This paper draws from real-world case studies on pre-vulnerability disclosure exploitation, multistage intrusions and nation-state activity to present behavioural intelligence as a complementary and operationally critical detection paradigm, capable of identifying malicious activity through deviations from established system and user behaviour days to weeks before traditional CTI signals emerge. It further addresses a gap in existing research, going beyond detection to interpretability by proposing two practical frameworks for operationalising behavioural intelligence within security operations centre and threat hunting workflows. These frameworks integrate unsupervised and supervised machine learning, graph analytics, and agentic reasoning to correlate low-signal anomalies into high-confidence threat narratives. The findings highlight behavioural intelligence as a necessary evolution of CTI, enabling earlier detection, improved contextual understanding, and more adaptive defence against modern, rapidly evolving adversaries. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.

papers.title: Utilization of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools in Teaching English for Generative and Assistive Purposes toward the Development of a Learning Action Cell Plan
papers.authors: Karl Pranada
papers.journal: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice
papers.abstract: This descriptive-correlational study examined the generative and assistive utilization of artificial intelligence tools by 35 junior high school English teachers in District III, Schools Division of Manila. Purposively selected teachers completed a validated four-part survey addressing demographic profile, commonly used tools, and utilization across the perceived attributes of relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability, and observability. ChatGPT was the most commonly used tool (30 teachers, 85.7%). Overall use for both generative and assistive purposes was moderate. Generative utilization differed across years of service and teaching position, whereas assistive utilization differed by teaching position; sex showed no significant differences. The relationship between overall generative and assistive utilization was weak and not statistically significant (r = .209, p = .229). The findings informed a proposed Learning Action Cell plan for English teachers focused on responsible and pedagogically purposeful use of AI tools.

papers.title: AI Adoption: How Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs) Are Leveraging Generative AI for Business Decision-Making and Cost Reduction
papers.authors: Milind Gajghate, Bhairavee Bhagadkar
papers.journal: International Journal on Research and Development - A Management Review
papers.abstract: The democratization of artificial intelligence through generative AI (GenAI) has altered the technological options available to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This study examines how SMEs use GenAI to support business decision-making and reduce operating costs. Using the mixed-methods multi-case basis stated in the source document, covering 45 SMEs across manufacturing, professional services, and retail, the paper synthesizes functional adoption pathways in market intelligence, financial scenario analysis, customer support, marketing, administration, and software development. The reported evidence indicates that GenAI can scale cognitive capabilities while automating repetitive administrative, creative, and technical work. The paper also retains a cost-optimization model that relates initial AI integration expenditure and recurring infrastructure cost to reductions in marginal transaction cost. Across the reported three-year projections, aggregate functional spending declines from a baseline of USD 410,000 to USD 170,000 in the mature state, corresponding to the reported net saving of 58.5%. The study further identifies data confidentiality, hallucination, algorithmic bias, and vendor dependency as implementation risks and proposes a phased governance and adoption roadmap for SMEs.

papers.title: Predicting Cervical Cancer Screening Utilization Among Women of Reproductive Age in Ethiopia Using Supervised Machine Learning: A Nationally Representative 2024/25 EDHS Study
papers.authors: Ashebir Mamay Gebiru, Negalgn Byadgie Gelaw, Derso Keleb Mekonen, Arega Asnakew Agazie, Misganaw Mihret Kelkay, Yenehun Demelash Gelaw, Tilahun Nega Godana
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer is a leading malignancy and mortality cause among Ethiopian women. Despite screening expansions coverage remains low. Traditional models miss complex determinants. This study aimed to develop machine learning models to predict cervical cancer screening utilization and identify drivers using the 2024 to 2025 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey. Methods A secondary analysis of the 2024 to 2025 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey was conducted among women aged 15 to 49. Six algorithms Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Machine and Extreme Gradient Boosting were trained. Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique handled class imbalance with a 4.2 percent screening prevalence. Models were evaluated on a holdout set using Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve, Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve, Brier score and Decision Curve Analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations explained model predictions. Results Extreme Gradient Boosting achieved superior discrimination with an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve of 0.896 and Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve of 0.781 outperforming baseline Logistic Regression at 0.772. Isotonic calibration optimized prediction loss with a Brier score of 0.038. Decision Curve Analysis confirmed clinical net benefit across thresholds from 5 percent to 55 percent. Explanatory analysis identified cancer awareness, education, autonomy, wealth quintile, recent health visits and urban residence as primary screening drivers. Conclusions Probability-calibrated Extreme Gradient Boosting with explainability provides an accurate tool for identifying un-screened women in Ethiopia. Public health programs can deploy these tools in primary care applications to target outreach, optimize community engagement and accelerate World Health Organization elimination targets.

papers.title: Resolution-aware spectral parameterization reveals robust context-dependent aperiodic EEG dynamics during real-world table tennis
papers.authors: Arunim Guchait, Chiao-Yun Chen, Neil Gerald Muggleton
papers.abstract: Abstract Mobile EEG can link neuroimaging to natural behavior, but effects recorded during movement, and sport in particular, are difficult to interpret because neural activity overlaps with signals from movement, muscle activity, and cable movement artifacts. We analyzed the OpenNeuro Real World Table Tennis dataset to test whether peri-hit spectral activity could be analyzed and how it differed between human-opponent and ball-machine play. Data from 25 participants comprising EEG, noise-layers, EMG and motion recordings was analyzed with pre-hit, impact, and post-hit windows. EEG power bands were residualized using trial-level root mean square from noise-layer, EMG, and motion/miscellaneous channels. Spectral parameterization modeled spectra as an aperiodic component plus periodic peaks. The principal short-window model was resolution-aware; sensitivity analyses reduced model complexity, used a 2.0-s peri-hit subwindow (−1.0 to +1.0 s), or disabled periodic fitting. Results showed residualized alpha and beta power was lower during ball-machine play, including pre-hit posterior alpha power. The clearest context difference was a higher ball-machine aperiodic exponent over posterior and parietal sensors, corresponding to a steeper broadband spectral slope. Posterior post-hit means were 0.451 and 0.606 for human-opponent and ball-machine play, respectively. A focal parietal effect persisted across specifications. The results support artifact-informed, resolution-aware spectral analysis as an effective approach for detecting robust spectral differences between naturalistic visuomotor contexts and suggest that EEG may provide useful information about the processes engaged by different practice environments, without establishing a single cognitive or physiological mechanism or demonstrating a training outcome.

papers.title: Sex differences in genetic liability to modifiable Alzheimer’s disease risk factors
papers.authors: Rakshya Sharma, Paulina Tolosa‐Tort, Michael C Okorie, Aadrita Chatterjee, Caroline Jonson, Kristine S. Yaffe, Michaël E. Belloy, Shea J. Andrews, ADGC
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT INTRODUCTION Alzheimer’s disease (AD) shows sex differences in risk, clinical progression, and biomarker profiles, but whether inherited genetic liability to modifiable risk factors contributes differently to AD susceptibility in females and males remains unclear. We evaluated whether genetic relationships between several modifiable dementia risk factors and AD differ between females and males. METHODS We integrated polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for modifiable risk factors, genome-wide genetic correlation, and two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses. PRS associations with AD diagnosis were evaluated in the Alzheimer’s Disease Genetics Consortium (n=27,751) and with AD plasma biomarkers in the Health and Aging Brain Study–Health Disparities (n=2,307-2,737, depending on the biomarker). Primary analyses evaluated female- and male-specific associations and compared sex-specific estimates. RESULTS Educational attainment and physical activity PRSs were associated with AD in both sexes. PRS sex differences were nominal for educational attainment, total cholesterol, and LDL cholesterol, but none remained significant after FDR correction. Genetic correlation showed FDR-significant sex differences for social isolation, physical activity, LDL cholesterol, and pulse pressure. MR identified FDR-significant associations within sex strata; higher HDL cholesterol was associated with lower AD risk in females, whereas higher total cholesterol and type 2 diabetes were associated with lower and higher AD risk, respectively, in males. Sensitivity analyses provided inconsistent support, and no sex difference in MR estimates remained significant after FDR correction. In HABS-HD, type 2 diabetes PRS was associated with higher NfL, BMI PRS with higher pTau 181 , and the composite PRS with higher NfL among males after FDR correction. DISCUSSION Evidence that modifiable dementia risk factors relate differently to AD by sex was limited and depended on the genetic measure examined. Sex differences in genome-wide genetic overlap were not consistently reflected in PRS or MR, indicating that shared genetic architecture does not necessarily translate into sex-specific inherited liability or causal effects RESEARCH IN CONTEXT Systematic review We reviewed the published literature on modifiable dementia risk factors, Alzheimer’s disease (AD) genetics, and sex differences using PubMed and relevant reference lists. Previous studies support genetic relationships between several modifiable risk factors and AD, but systematic comparisons of female- and male-specific relationships across complementary genetic approaches remain limited. Interpretatio The strongest evidence of sex heterogeneity for modifiable risk factors and AD was observed in their shared genetic architectures, with FDR-significant female–male differences for social isolation, physical activity, LDL cholesterol, and pulse pressure. PRS and Mendelian randomization analyses provided less evidence of formal sex heterogeneity, suggesting that sex differences in shared genetic architecture do not necessarily imply sex-specific causal effects. Future directions Larger sex-stratified and ancestry-diverse GWAS integrated with longitudinal exposure and biomarker data are needed to determine whether these signals reflect sex-dependent biological mechanisms and whether they have implications for dementia prevention. Highlights - Sex differences in AD-related genetic architecture were concentrated in behavioral, lipid, and vascular traits. - Genetic correlations with AD differed between females and males for social isolation, physical activity, LDL cholesterol, and pulse pressure. - PRS analyses implicated educational attainment and physical activity in AD in both sexes, but no PRS sex difference survived FDR correction. - MR identified associations within sex strata but provided little robust evidence of sex-specific causal effects.

papers.title: An Adaptive Technical and Behavioral Approach for Biomarker Acquisition in Autism with Intellectual Disability
papers.authors: Cassandra J. Stevens, Sara Eberle, Casey Carrow, Sherab Tsheringla, Christine Cukar-Capizzi, Julie M. Wolf, Adam J. Naples, James C. McPartland
papers.abstract: Abstract Autistic individuals with intellectual disability (ASD+ID) and profound autism are rarely studied in neuroscience research due to barriers including communication challenges, sensory sensitivities, anxiety, and elevated behavioral support needs. Consequently, biomarker development in autism fails to include the portion of the autistic population with highest support needs and greatest potential to benefit from treatments derived from imminent advances in personalized medicine. Here we present a multimodal, participant-centered protocol for simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking (ET) acquisition to advance clinical trial readiness research in this underserved population. The protocol combines individualized behavioral supports and an adaptive EEG-ET acquisition platform. Pre-visit caregiver interviews informed participant-specific research plans, including customized visual supports, reinforcement strategies, and EEG net desensitization procedures. A gaze-contingent stimulus presentation system used participant-preferred videos to support attention to experimental stimuli and behavior consistent with data acquisition (e.g., refraining from movement) while dynamically adapting stimulus delivery based on visual engagement with the assay and real-time assessment of data quality. By quantifying attended trials in real time and prioritizing unattended stimulus classes, the paradigm maximizes acquisition efficiency to minimize participant burden. This approach was utilized to deploy candidate biomarkers with demonstrated replicability in the Autism Biomarkers Consortium for Clinical Trials (ABC-CT): the N170 event-related potential to faces, resting-state EEG, and visual attention to human faces (measured with ET). Feasibility was evaluated in 76 children with ASD+ID (M age = 8.76 years; IQ = 32.4) and a small comparison sample of 8 children with intellectual disability without autism (M age = 8.91 years; IQ = 45.9). Usable EEG data (>7 minutes) were acquired in 61% (ASD+ID) and 88% (ID) of participants, respectively. Sufficient ET data were obtained from 67% (ASD+ID) and 63% (ID) of participants, respectively. Findings demonstrate the feasibility of inclusive biomarker acquisition and provide a framework for expanding participation of individuals with ASD+ID and profound autism in neuroscience research. Ongoing research seeks to evaluate this approach in larger samples and to demonstrate feasibility in multisite research studies.

papers.title: Spatial hearing in adults with sequential bilateral cochlear implants: a longitudinal prospective cohort study
papers.authors: Chiara Valzolgher, Sara Ghiselli, Marina Ottavia Epifania, Jessica Gullotta, Diego Zanetti, Giorgio Lilli, Federica Di Berardino, Marco Pozzi, Andrea Ciorba, Michela Borin, Nicola Brunelli, Lucia Belen Musumano, Giuseppe Nicolò Frau, Giuseppina Tromballi, Angela Chini, Tommaso Rosi, Paolo Malerba, Domenico Cuda, Francesco Pavani B
papers.abstract: Abstract Bilateral cochlear implantation (BCI) can improve spatial hearing in adults with bilateral hearing loss, but the early development of spatial hearing following sequential BCI remains poorly understood. This prospective longitudinal study investigated changes in spatial hearing experience in 23 adults undergoing sequential BCI, assessed before and at ∼1, 3, and 8 months after bilateral implantation under two conditions: spontaneous and restrained head movements. Using a motion-tracking system combined with virtual reality, sound localization was assessed through absolute and signed errors, along with self-reported localization confidence and listening effort. Subjective spatial hearing was also assessed using the Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ). Localization performance improved by 1 month after bilateral implantation, as evidenced by a reduction of absolute error and in the bias toward the first-implanted ear. Participants reported greater localization confidence and lower listening effort at 1 month, although these changes were not consistently maintained at later follow-ups. SSQ scores showed improved spatial hearing at 1 month, speech perception at 3 months, and sound clarity and discriminability at 8 months. Compared with head-restrained condition, accuracy and confidence improved when spontaneous head rotations were allowed. The temporal trajectories of localization bias, confidence, and effort were modulated by the duration of experience with the first CI. These findings indicate that changes in spatial hearing can emerge soon after second CI activation. They further highlight the contribution of spontaneous head movements and previous CI experience, and support the use of complementary measures to monitor the early development of bilateral listening.

papers.title: A comprehensive physiological dataset of pain and aversive modalities for pain biomarkers research
papers.authors: Alyson Champagne, Lorie-Eve Barrette, Antoine Cyr-Bouchard, Mathieu Roy, Michel‐Pierre Coll
papers.abstract: Abstract While progress has been made in identifying pain biomarkers using neuroimaging, the development of reliable EEG-based biomarkers remains challenging, limited by small sample sizes and the lack of adequate control conditions. We present a comprehensive dataset from 125 pain-free adults, comprising electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings, and behavioural, sociodemographic, and psychological data. Galvanic skin response and electrocardiogram data were also recorded in a subset of participants ( n = 76). Participants received two sustained painful stimulations (thermal, chemical) and two sustained aversive non-painful stimulations (auditory, taste), each delivered twice (with and without continuous intensity ratings). Data are provided in Brain Imaging Data Structure format, where all physiological, stimulus-related, and behavioural data are synchronized within the EEG data files for easy access and analysis. Technical validation confirmed data integrity, with spectral and physiological analyses showing responses associated with stimulus intensity and subjective pain/unpleasantness levels. By providing multimodal physiological data across painful and non-painful aversive conditions, this initiative represents a valuable resource for developing or validating biomarkers and exploring the multidimensional nature of pain perception.

papers.title: Coordinated Brain-Heart Dynamics During Human NREM Sleep
papers.authors: Christian Alexander Mikutta, Miriam Planta, Thomas W. Koenig, Kristoffer Daniel Fehér, Pauline Henckaerts, Marie Angelillo, Elisabeth Hertenstein, Carlotta  Louisa Schneider, Marzia De Lucia E, Dieter Wilhelm Riemann, Bernd Feige, Vladyslav V. Vyazovskiy, Christoph Nissen
papers.abstract: Abstract Communication between the brain and cardiovascular system is increasingly recognized as a fundamental determinant of health, yet the mechanisms coordinating neural and cardiac rhythms remain poorly understood. Sleep provides a unique physiological state for investigating neurovisceral integration because cortical slow oscillations (SOs), thalamocortical sleep spindles, and autonomic activity undergo profound reorganization during non–rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. We analyzed overnight high-density electroencephalography and electrocardiography recordings from 30 healthy adults and quantified interactions among SOs, sleep spindles, cardiac R-peaks, heart rate variability (HRV), spectral slope, and Lempel–Ziv complexity. To assess integrated brain–heart coordination, we developed a Joint Phase–Amplitude Coupling (JPAC) metric that quantifies the corelation between SO phase–dependent modulation of spindle amplitude and cardiac timing. SO–spindle coupling showed the expected fronto-central distribution but was not significantly related to autonomic or cortical state markers. In contrast, SO–R-peak coupling and JPAC systematically tracked physiological state. Stronger JPAC was associated with higher high-frequency HRV, steeper spectral slopes, and lower neural complexity, indicating enhanced coupling during synchronized, parasympathetically dominated NREM sleep. These findings demonstrate coordinated organization of cortical, thalamocortical, and cardiac rhythms within a common oscillatory framework and identify NREM sleep as a state and potential treatment target of large-scale neurovisceral integration.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of Chatgpt-Assisted Inquiry Learning on Critical Thinking Skills
papers.authors: Prima Trisna Aji, Tukimin Bin Sansuwito, Elinda Rizkasari
papers.journal: Elementary Education Journal of Studies Analysis and Development
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence offers new opportunities to support higher-order thinking in elementary education, yet empirical evidence of its effectiveness remains limited. This study examined the effectiveness of ChatGPT-assisted inquiry learning in improving critical thinking skills among fifth-grade students in science learning. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design involved 60 students assigned to an experimental group (n = 30) and a control group (n = 30). The experimental group received four weeks of teacher-guided ChatGPT-assisted inquiry learning, while the control group received conventional instruction. Critical thinking skills were assessed before and after the intervention using a validated structured essay test. The groups had comparable baseline scores (58.43 ± 8.71 vs. 57.86 ± 8.24; p = 0.781). After the intervention, the experimental group achieved significantly higher critical thinking scores than the control group (84.76 ± 6.25 vs. 67.91 ± 7.42), with a mean difference of 16.85 points (95% CI: 13.21–20.49; p < 0.001) and a large effect size (Cohen’s d = 1.92). The greatest improvements were observed in analysis and evaluation. These findings demonstrate that teacher-guided ChatGPT-assisted inquiry learning can effectively enhance elementary students’ critical thinking skills. Its classroom implementation should emphasize structured inquiry and teacher supervision to promote responsible use of generative AI. Future studies should examine its long-term effects across larger and more diverse elementary school populations and investigate its effectiveness across different subjects and learning contexts.

papers.title: AI Literacy and TVET Teaching Practice: The Mediating Role of Generative AI Competence in Southeast Nigeria
papers.authors: Sunday Nwabueze Wogu, C. M. Kalu, K. S. Ihedigbo, O. C. Nwankwo
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), is transforming the knowledge, skills and pedagogical practices required of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) educators. However, possessing basic AI literacy does not necessarily translate into meaningful AI-enabled teaching practice. This study investigates the relationship between AI literacy and AI-enabled teaching practice among TVET educators in South-Eastern Nigeria, with particular attention to the mediating role of generative AI competence in educator capacity building for global relevance. The study adoptes a correlational survey design and was conceptually anchored in the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, complemented by human-centered AI competency principles. A sample of 320 TVET educators was used for the analysis. Data were collected using an AI Literacy Scale, Generative AI Competence Scale and AI-Enabled Teaching Practice Scale. Descriptive statistics, Pearson Product Moment Correlation and Structural Equation Modelling were used for data analysis, while bootstrapping was used to test the mediation effect. The findings indicates positive relationships between AI literacy, generative AI competence and AI-enabled teaching practice. AI literacy significantly predicted generative AI competence, while generative AI competence significantly predicted AI-enabled teaching practice. The direct relationship between AI literacy and teaching practice remained significant but was reduced after the mediator was introduced, indicating partial mediation. The findings suggest that capacity building programmes should move beyond awareness of AI towards practical competence in prompt design, content generation, assessment, ethical use, verification and pedagogical integration. The study concludes that strengthening GenAI competence may constitute an important mechanism through which AI literacy is converted into meaningful teaching practice among TVET educators in South-Eastern Nigeria.
keywords: technical and vocational education and training

papers.title: Comparative Effects of Concept Mapping and Problem-Solving Strategies On Geometry Performance among Upper Basic Students in Kano State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Auwalu1 HARUNA, Lawan YAKUBU, Muhammad Sirajo2 ADO, Miswaru Bello
papers.journal: Federal University Gusau Faculty of Education Journal
papers.abstract: This quasi-experimental study investigated the “Influence of Concept Mapping and Problem-Solving Strategies on Geometry Performance of Upper Basic Students in Kano, exploring the potential of these strategies to enhance entrepreneurial innovation and skills, contributing to poverty reduction initiatives in Nigeria. Samples of 367 out of the population of 999,486 students from 1,001 public Upper Basic Schools were used. The experimental group 1 was exposed to Concept mapping, experimental group 2 to Problem solving and Control group was exposed to Conventional method respectively. Three research questions were raised and three null hypotheses were formulated to guide the study. The researcher developed an instrument, Geometry Performance Test (GPT) which was designed to test the performance after treatment in four areas of Geometry; angles, triangles, polygons and circles. Result of the t-test statistics revealed significant difference between the performances of the three groups. Findings from the study underscore the importance of innovative pedagogies in enhancing mathematical skills, promoting an entrepreneurial mindset, and ultimately addressing socio-economic challenges. Recommendations proffered based on the findings, includes; integrating the use of concept mapping in the teaching of geometry among Upper Basic Students so as to enhance students’ performance, Mathematics teachers be sent on in-house trainings, workshops and seminars where modern teaching strategies are discussed such as MAN, STAN Conferences among others. Teachers’ welfare should be improved to meet life challenges and teacher education at all levels should be carefully managed to incorporate all socio-cultural, environmental, economic and political aspects of life for the teachers.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Attitudes and Behavioural Measurement Scales on Artificial Intelligence Integration in Mathematics Teaching among Pre-Service Teachers in Abuja, Nigeria
papers.authors: Feyisara Zakariya YUSUF, Abdullahi Jamilu, Kazaik Benjamin Danlami
papers.journal: Federal University Gusau Faculty of Education Journal
papers.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has created a need for concise, context-specific measures of teachers’ orientations toward AI use. However, existing instruments often combine attitude, behavioural intention, perceived usefulness, self-efficacy, anxiety, and other acceptance-related constructs. This study developed and evaluated a concise measure of Attitude Toward Use (ATT) and Behavioural Intention to Use (BIU) artificial intelligence in mathematics teaching and learning among pre-service mathematics teachers. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 221 pre-service mathematics teachers from higher institutions in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, Nigeria. Items were generated from the Technology Acceptance Model and relevant literature, subjected to expert evaluation, and examined using separate one-factor measurement models. Model fit was assessed using χ², CFI, TLI, RMSEA, and SRMR, while reliability was evaluated using McDonald’s coefficient omega. The initial ATT model demonstrated inadequate fit, but substantial improvement was obtained following item refinement (CFI = .990, TLI = .938, SRMR = .019, RMSEA = .120). The retained ATT indicators loaded from .528 to .818, with ω = .715. The BIU model demonstrated stronger fit (χ²(5) = 11.455, CFI = .986, TLI = .972, RMSEA = .076, SRMR = .025), with factor loadings ranging from .588 to .773 and ω = .786. The findings provide preliminary evidence for concise, construct-specific measures of ATT and BIU toward AI use in mathematics teaching and learning. The BIU scale demonstrated stronger measurement performance, whereas the ATT scale requires further validation using independent samples.

papers.title: Measuring Perceived Ease of Artificial Intelligence Utilisation: An Adaptation and Psychometric Validation of a Scale among Preservice Mathematics Teachers in Nigerian Context
papers.authors: Feyisara Zakariya YUSUF, Abdullahi Jamilu, Alhassan Abdulrahman SALIHU
papers.journal: Federal University Gusau Faculty of Education Journal
papers.abstract: Perceived ease of use is a foundational construct in technology-acceptance research, yet instruments developed to measure it in relation to artificial intelligence (AI) remain scarce within African teacher-education contexts. Existing scales are rarely re-examined for the specific referent of AI-assisted mathematics learning. This study adapted a six-item Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU) from the literature to an AI-in-mathematics-learning context and examined its psychometric properties among drawn 221 preservice mathematics teachers using a multistage non-probability sampling procedure from three higher institutions in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, Nigeria. Confirmatory factor analysis of the initial six-item one-factor model showed inadequate fit (CFI = .886, TLI = .811). However, the removal of two items with low standardised loadings produced a four-item model with an excellent fit (χ²(2) = 2.770, p = .250, CFI = .991, TLI = .972, RMSEA = .042, SRMR = .026). The retained scale demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (ω = .723). Non-parametric comparisons revealed no statistically significant difference in PEOU AI across institutional type (Kruskal–Wallis χ²(2) = 3.637, p = .162) or gender (Mann–Whitney U, z = -.567, p = .571). The findings support a psychometrically sound, unidimensional four-item PEOU-AI scale for use in Nigerian mathematics teacher education and suggest that ease-of-use perceptions of AI tools are broadly comparable across the sampled institutions and gender groups.

papers.title: Effects of Cloud - Computing Instruction on Interest and Performance in Genetics Concept among State Colleges of Education Biology Students in North-West, Nigeria
papers.authors: Umar ISHAQ
papers.journal: Federal University Gusau Faculty of Education Journal
papers.abstract: This study investigated the Effects of Cloud Computing Instruction on Interest and Performance in Genetics among Biology Students in States Colleges of Education, North-West Zone Nigeria. The study has Four (4) Research Objectives, Four (4) Research Questions, Four (4) Null Hypotheses tested at p≤0.05 level of significance using Quasi-experimental design. Four groups of students were used for data collection: the two experimental and control groups were pre-tested before treatment; Post-tested and post post-tested to determine the effect of the treatments on performance and interest among groups. The study has total population of 1,360 NCE III Biology students in Seven States Colleges of Education in North-West, Nigeria. From the figure, a total number of 200 NCE III Biology students were sampled. Two validated instruments with reliability coefficient of 0.74 and 0.83 namely; Genetics Performance Test (GPT) and Students Interest to Genetics Questionnaire (SIGQ) were used for data collection. Research questions were answered using mean, mean rank and Standard Deviations. Null Hypotheses were tested using ANCOVA, Independent t-test, Man Whitney (U-test), Kruskal Wallisat 0.05 level of significance. Findings show that, significant difference was obtained between the mean academic performance scores of experimental and control group in favour of experimental group. The mean Interest scores of experimental group is greater than that of control group, Based on the findings of the study, the researcher recommends that the State Ministries of Education should collaborate with professional bodies such as STAN to train teachers through workshops, and seminars on the use of Cloud Computing Instruction in teaching Biology at Colleges.

papers.title: An Explainable AI-Based Deep Learning Approach for Pneumonia Classification Using Chest X-Rays
papers.authors: Maryam Tariq, Fazal Shah
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering and Computational Intelligence Review
papers.abstract: Pneumonia is a serious disease that affects the lungs, and rapid and proper diagnosis is critical for its effective treatment. CXR is employed due to its relative availability and low cost, along with the fact that it can detect anomalies in the lungs; however, the result of interpretation depends on the quality of the picture, overlapping features, experience of the one who analyzes it, and even the load of work. In the present study, we suggest a deep learning method with an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that classifies pneumonia based on chest x-rays. A labeled CXR dataset comprising 5,856 images was utilized for the development of the model, where the images were labeled as pneumonia and normal based on the reference labels. The dataset was split into train, validation, and independent test sets by employing patient-level splitting to avoid any possible data leakage. Image resizing, normalization, augmentation, and lung region-based pre-processing were performed prior to model training. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were employed as the metrics for assessing the performance of the model. As shown in the experiment results, the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, and AUC are 94.2%, 95.1%, 93.3%, 93.0%, 94.0%, and 0.97, respectively. The Grad-CAM method mainly focused on the pulmonary regions with radiographic abnormalities and provided the interpretation of model decision processes. It appears that the deep learning model with interpretable mechanism can be a good computer-aided technique for pneumonia screening. Nevertheless, external validation and assessment of the model explanations should be conducted. REFERENCES [1] J. Irvin, P. Rajpurkar, K. Ko, Y. Yu, S. Ciurea-Ilcus, C. Chute, H. Marklund, B. papers.title: Generative AI and Copyright in the European Union: Transparency, Copyright Compliance, and the AI Act
papers.authors: Chinmay Rathee
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: This study explores the relationship between generative artificial intelligence and copyright law in the European Union (EU), focusing on the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) and its interplay with the existing EU copyright acquis. It distinguishes between two questions that are often conflated: whether AI-generated or AI-assisted content deserves copyright protection, and whether the providers and deployers of AI systems that produce such content bear regulatory responsibilities. Applying doctrinal legal research to the AI Act, the study examines the treatment of general-purpose AI models, copyright-compliance policies, training-content summaries, synthetic-content transparency, documentation, institutional supervision and adaptive codes of practice. It also places these obligations alongside the Court of Justice’s originality standard, which has so far been tied to the author’s own intellectual creation expressed through free and creative choices. The study concludes that the EU framework works best in relation to provider accountability, provenance and transparency, but that some important output-side copyright issues remain to be addressed by the existing copyright framework. In that light, it suggests strengthening the links between AI law and copyright law without turning the AI Act into a copyright-specific law.
keywords: Court of Justice of the European Union

papers.title: AI Inventorship in Patent Law: Comparative Doctrine, Regulatory Divergence, and Harmonized Reform
papers.authors: R. Sowjanya Yamini, Mohd Saleem
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in invention workflows, yet patent systems continue to define inventorship in human terms. The central problem is not whether AI contributes to technical creativity, but whether existing legal doctrines can allocate ownership, responsibility, and evidentiary accountability when inventive processes are distributed across humans and AI systems. Prior scholarship has examined DABUS disputes and personhood debates, but the literature remains fragmented across jurisdictions and often under-specifies operational reform pathways for patent offices and courts. This article addresses that gap through a comparative doctrinal design covering the United States, United Kingdom, European Union/Germany, Australia, South Africa, India, China, and selected emerging jurisdictions. The analysis triangulates statutes, judicial decisions, patent-office guidance, and Scopus-indexed legal scholarship from 2019–2026. The findings show convergence on human-only inventorship, but persistent divergence in disclosure expectations, contribution tests, and evidentiary practices. These divergences produce transparency deficits, cross-border uncertainty, and uneven enforcement risk for multinational portfolios. The article’s original contribution is a six-part harmonized reform model that preserves human-centered inventorship while modernizing AI-contribution disclosure, contribution assessment, evidentiary protocols, interoperability standards, targeted supplementary protection for edge cases, and governance integration. The model is explicitly grounded in an accountability architecture framework that separates legal status from evidentiary governance. This framework offers a practical route to doctrinal stability and policy coherence without requiring full AI legal personhood.

papers.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence-Based Educational Resources in Primary Grades
papers.authors: Kifayat Gurban Mansimova
papers.journal: The Actual problems of study of humanities
papers.abstract: The article comprehensively analyzes the current issue of integrating artificial intelligence technologies into the education system against the background of the interaction between technology and education in the modern era of scientific and technological progress. It is also noted that the changes taking place in society have spread to the field of education, making the application of artificial intelligence in education inevitable in the conditions of the information and technological society, making it a kind of necessity. The main reason here is to increase the quality of the teaching and learning process. For the sake of comparison, it is added that while artificial intelligence was previously perceived only as a system that performs complex logical functions, it has now surpassed its goals and begun to be applied in wider areas, becoming an important technological tool that facilitates human activity, increases productivity and creates new opportunities. In the conclusion of the article, it was concluded that the application of artificial intelligence technologies in education has a positive impact on both students' academic achievements and teachers' professional development. In order for teachers to fully utilize this potential, it was considered necessary to educate them, strengthen their professional training, and systematically implement their integration into technologies. Keywords: primary education, artificial intelligence, technologies, teaching

papers.title: LANGUAGE, POWER, AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MODERN MEDIA
papers.authors: A. HAJ ALI
papers.journal: The Actual problems of study of humanities
papers.abstract: Summary. In today’s digital world, language is no longer shaped solely by human authors but increasingly by artificial intelligence (AI) systems. While these technologies enhance communication and efficiency, they also raise concerns about manipulation, bias, and misinformation. Media plays a pivotal role in shaping how information is interpreted through strategic use of language and framing. This article explores how AI-generated content and media narratives together influence modern discourse, affect public perception, and raise critical ethical questions. By examining real-life examples and theoretical insights, the paper highlights the urgent need to develop critical media and AI literacy in educational systems. This is essential to equip citizens with tools to analyze, question, and resist linguistic manipulation in an increasingly digital society. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Media Framing, Discourse, Critical Literacy, Manipulation

papers.title: Post-editing in Modern Translation Studies: Linguistic and Cognitive Perspectives
papers.authors: G.B. Bayramova
papers.journal: The Actual problems of study of humanities
papers.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence and Neural Machine Translation (NMT) systems has caused fundamental changes in the field of translation studies. This article analyzes the transition of the translator's traditional role from a "text creator" to a modern "strategic editor" and "post-editor". The main objective of the research is to define the essence of the process of "polishing" the initial machine translation output by the human mind and to identify the linguistic challenges encountered in this process. The article notes that while machine translation can process vast amounts of data in seconds, it urgently requires human intervention to restore the connotative nuances, stylistic subtleties, and cultural codes of the text. The author evaluates this new mission of the translator as a cognitive control mechanism. The study explores the concept of Machine Translation Post-Editing (MTPE) through the prism of two levels: "Light" and "Full" post-editing. In the practical section, "gaps" of artificial intelligence in literary texts are demonstrated based on examples from Azerbaijani (J.Mammadguluzadeh, H.Javid) and Russian (F.Dostoevsky) literature. The analysis shows that when machine translation literally renders phraseological units, metaphors, and individual stylistic elements, the pragmatic potential of the original is lost. The translator's role here is to restore these "lost meanings" and polish the text to fit the natural syntax of the target language. In conclusion, it is emphasized that technology does not replace the translator but rather elevates their activity to a new level. The translator of the future must work in synergy with artificial intelligence, acting as both a technologist and a cross-cultural mediator. Keywords: translator, technology, editing, creativity, quality

papers.title: A Clinical Study to Compare the Anti Hypertensive Benefits of Cilnidipine, Azilsartan in Type 2 DM Patients
papers.authors: M. Shameemunisha, K. Bhuvaneswari, Saravanan T
papers.journal: NATIONAL BOARD OF EXAMINATIONS JOURNAL OF MEDICAL SCIENCES
papers.abstract: Background: Hypertension accompanies type 2 diabetes mellitus increasing cardiovascular and renal risk and creating a need for effective, well-tolerated antihypertensive therapy. This study compared the short-term effects of cilnidipine and azilsartan in adults with T2DM and newly diagnosed hypertension. Methodology: In this open label randomized control trial, 61 subjects were administered Azilsartan 40mg once daily (n=30) and Cilnidipine 5mg once daily (n=31) for 3 months. The effects on blood pressure, glycemic parameters, lipid profile, high sensitivity C Reactive Protein (hs-CRP), renal parameters, Body Mass Index and quality of life parameters were evaluated. Results: Significant decreases in both systolic and diastolic blood pressure were achieved in both groups with no significant difference between groups in terms of post-treatment blood pressure. Blood glucose, both fasting and postprandial was improved in both groups. Significant improvements in total cholesterol, triglyceride and high-sensitivity CRP levels were observed in azilsartan group with no significant differences between groups in terms of these parameters. Both groups experienced a decrease in serum creatinine and an increase in eGFR with no significant between-group differences in eGFR. Body weight and BMI were essentially unchanged. Conclusion: Both azilsartan and cilnidipine proved to be beneficial for achieving good BP control in T2DM patients with new onset hypertension. The results suggest that cilnidipine can be a valuable choice for antihypertensive treatment of patients, further validation of metabolic and renal effects of cilnidipine is needed. Future large-scale studies are necessary to reveal comparative efficacy and protective effects of the drug.

papers.title: Analisis Faktor yang Memengaruhi Minat Memilih Jurusan Akuntansi
papers.authors: Keira Claribel Kuswandi, Hendro Lukman
papers.abstract: Career choices are often influenced by educational background, including the decision to become an accountant. While the accounting profession has faced significant disruption from technology over the past decade, accountants remain essential to the business world and the economy. This study aims to analyze the influence of career perceptions, parental influence, and artificial intelligence (AI) on students' interest in choosing an accounting major. This is a descriptive quantitative study utilizing primary data collected via questionnaires through convenience and snowball sampling methods. Data were obtained from 160 respondents and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results indicate that parental influence has a positive effect and significant effect on students’ interest, whereas career and AI information have positive but insignificant effects on students’ interest in choosing an accounting major. Together, these three variables explain 64.6% of the variation in students' interest in selecting an accounting major. The study suggests that schools should enhance students' and parents' understanding of accounting careers by engaging accounting professionals who already utilize AI in their work.

papers.title: The Urgency of the Philosophy of Science in Addressing the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Education
papers.authors: Hasnah Faizah, Muhammad Fajri, Dewi Laila Sari Rambe
papers.journal: International Journal of Islamic Educational Research
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed education, from adaptive learning systems and AI-based tutoring assistants to automated assessment. While AI offers unprecedented efficiency and personalization, it simultaneously raises fundamental questions about the nature of knowledge, the role of teachers, and the values embedded in the educational process. This article examines the urgency of philosophy of science as a critical-reflective framework for addressing AI development in education, using a library research approach that reviews relevant academic literature. The findings show that the three main branches of philosophy of science, namely ontology, epistemology, and axiology, can serve as analytical instruments to understand the nature of AI, how AI generates knowledge, and the ethical implications of its use in education. Philosophy of science plays an important role in preventing the reduction of learning into a merely mechanical process while ensuring that technology remains framed by human values. The article concludes that integrating philosophy of science into AI-based education discourse is not merely a theoretical complement but an urgent necessity to keep education humanistic amid technological disruption.

papers.title: Analysis of the Knowledge Structure, Thematic Evolution, and Emerging and Future Research Directions in User Interface Design for Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in Decision-Making Dashboards: A Scientometric Study
papers.authors: Sepehr Noroozi Chakoli, Ehsan Mousavi Khaneghah
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Purpose: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) in organizational decision-making environments has intensified concerns about transparency, interpretability, and user trust. As complex machine learning models increasingly support managerial and policy decisions, the need for Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has become essential to ensure that decision-makers understand and appropriately utilize algorithmic outputs. Decision dashboards have emerged as key interfaces through which AI-driven insights are delivered to managers and analysts. Despite their growing importance, the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of XAI within decision dashboard design have not yet been systematically examined. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the knowledge structure, conceptual foundations, and thematic development of research on Explainable Artificial Intelligence in decision dashboards. Employing scientometric techniques, the study identifies core research themes, emerging trends, and structural relationships shaping this rapidly evolving field. It also highlights how technical advancements in AI intersect with human-centered design, decision support systems, and visualization approaches in explainable decision dashboards.Methodology: This study employs advanced bibliometric and network analysis techniques within a scientometric framework to map the intellectual landscape of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) research in decision dashboards. Data were collected from the Scopus and Web of Science databases to ensure comprehensive coverage of peer-reviewed literature. Following the PRISMA protocol for systematic screening and refinement, an initial dataset of 942 records was identified. After applying inclusion criteria and limiting the corpus to original research articles, 251 records from Scopus and 112 from Web of Science were retained. Duplicate and irrelevant records were removed, resulting in a final dataset of 269 articles. Data standardization and descriptive bibliometric analyses were conducted using the Bibliometrix package and the Biblioshiny interface. These tools facilitated the examination of publication trends, leading journals, and author productivity patterns, including the application of Bradford’s and Lotka’s laws. To explore the conceptual structure of the field, keyword co-occurrence network analysis was performed using VOSviewer. Network, density, and overlay visualizations were generated to identify thematic clusters, intellectual linkages, and temporal changes in research topics. Additionally, thematic evolution mapping and logistic growth modeling were applied to examine the developmental trajectory of the field.Findings: The findings indicate that research on Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in decision dashboards is evolving from a purely technical, algorithm-centered domain toward a multidimensional, interdisciplinary knowledge structure. Co-occurrence analysis reveals that the intellectual core of the field is organized around three central concepts: explainable AI, decision making, and deep learning. These themes form the primary hub of the conceptual network, suggesting that explainability is increasingly recognized as a fundamental component of intelligent decision support systems rather than merely a supplementary feature of machine learning models. The results also identify several interconnected thematic clusters, including human ethical considerations, technical methodological development, applied operational contexts, cognitive autonomous systems, and emerging specialized topics. This structure reflects the convergence of two complementary research paradigms: algorithmic performance and engineering efficiency on one hand, and human understanding, trust, and accountability on the other. Density visualization confirms that the highest concentration of research lies at the intersection of explainable AI, decision-making, and deep learning, underscoring the central role of deep learning technologies in the field. However, these technologies require integration with interpretability mechanisms and user interface design to be effective in decision dashboards. Overlay visualization further indicates a thematic transition over time. Earlier research primarily focused on classical machine learning techniques such as neural networks and support vector machines. In contrast, recent studies increasingly emphasize visual deep learning, visualization techniques, trust, and intelligent decision support systems. Another key finding is that concepts like trust and visualization have evolved from peripheral topics to integral components of explainable AI (XAI) systems, highlighting the growing importance of user comprehension and interaction in AI-supported decision-making processes. Logistic growth modeling also indicates that the field is still in a rapid expansion phase and has not yet reached scientific saturation.Conclusion: The results demonstrate that the research landscape of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in decision dashboards is shifting from a technology-centered paradigm toward a human- and decision-centered paradigm. Explainability is increasingly understood not only as a technical capability that clarifies algorithmic outputs but also as a cognitive bridge between complex AI systems and human decision-makers. The findings highlight that the effectiveness of AI-enabled decision dashboards depends not only on predictive accuracy but also on the systems' ability to communicate reasoning processes in an interpretable and trustworthy manner. Consistent with previous studies, the practical value of explainable AI emerges when explanations enhance transparency, foster user trust, and support informed decision-making in complex environments. By mapping the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this interdisciplinary domain, the study provides insights into its conceptual foundations and future research directions. In particular, it emphasizes the importance of integrating deep learning technologies with explainability mechanisms, visualization techniques, and human-centered interface design to develop effective decision dashboards.Keywords: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), Decision dashboards, Decision support systems, Scientometric analysis, Deep learning, Human‑centered AI, Visualization, Decision making, Research fronts, Future research directions, Emerging trends

papers.title: ADDRESSING INEQUALITIES FACED BY REGIONAL AND MINORITY LANGUAGES OF EUROPE IN THE HUMAN-MACHINE ERA
papers.authors: Ingeborg Birnie, Melody Ann Ross, Maggie Glass
papers.abstract: Rapid technological advances have signalled a shift towards the human-machine era. The human-machine era, characterised by its focus on communication through and with technology (Sayers et al., 2021), will continue to change the way in which language is used, and individuals use language to communicate and interact. These advances in technology have been recognised as creating opportunities to improve human rights, including creating and enhancing access to information, health education, and public services (United Nations 2023). However, the potential that technological advances and developments can bring to support improvements in human rights needs to be set against the (ongoing) challenges of maintaining linguistic and cultural diversity.Around 75% of the world’s languages are considered to be in danger of disappearing in the next century (UNESCO 2011). Currently the developments in technology are resulting in an increased linguistic homogeneity (The Centre for Internet and Society et al. 2022). Speakers of RMLs inherently have fewer resources and tools available to them in this domain, increasing the already existing digital divide. This inequality puts languages at risk of being ‘irrelevant and stigmatised’ (UNESCO Ad Hoc Expert Group on Endangered languages 2003: 11). Therefore, language diversityand vitality, as well as the associated community identity and intangible cultural heritage, is linked to inclusion of these languages within technological advancements. This means resolute action is required to ensure that, in line with the United Nations Universal Declaration for Human Rights, everyone can ‘participate in the cultural life of the community, to enjoy the arts, and to share in the scientific advancement and its benefits’ (United Nations 1948: Article 22, emphasis by the authors), with ‘technology [serving] as a force for good’ (United Nations 2023). The current and future impact of the advances in technology has been recognised at supranational level with the establishment of advisory bodies and committees to provide recommendations and prepare legislative frameworks which acknowledge the benefits and risks that these advances bring to human rights, democracy, and the rule of law. These actions have focused on minimising risks and providing regulatory measures for artificial intelligence within the human rights framework but have not directly considered, addressed, or referred to the accessibility and availability of these tools and applications in and for different minority or regional language users. This is the focus of this briefing paper.

papers.title: Digital innovation enablers in sustainable banking and insurance: a systematic review of business model transformation factors
papers.authors: Sonny Supriyadi, Mohammad Hamsal, Asnan Furinto, Pantri Heriyati
papers.abstract: Banking and insurance institutions face increasing pressure to transform their business models through digital technologies while advancing sustainability objectives, yet existing research remains fragmented in explaining how digital innovation is translated into sustainable outcomes. This systematic review applies PRISMA guidelines to synthesize 168 peer-reviewed articles published between 2002 and 2026 from Scopus and Web of Science, using systematic screening, structured coding, and thematic analysis to examine the links among digital transformation, business model innovation, and sustainable performance in banking and insurance. The review identifies an evolutionary trajectory from basic digitalization and financial inclusion models toward AI-enabled, ecosystem-based, and sustainability-integrated business model transformation. More importantly, the synthesis develops a mechanism-based explanation of sustainable transformation by showing that business model innovation functions as an enabler, amplifier, mediator, moderator, and boundary spanner through five mechanisms: technology-enabled inclusion, ecosystem orchestration, revenue model transformation, risk resilience engineering, and stakeholder value co-creation. The review further proposes a four-archetype framework comprising The Reinventors, The Mavericks, The Adapters, and The Adventurers, each reflecting different combinations of innovation impetus, organizational focus, sectoral logic, and sustainability orientation. By translating these findings into concrete and testable propositions, this review contributes a parsimonious research agenda for examining when, how, and under what conditions digital business model innovation produces sustainable transformation in banking and insurance.

papers.title: Global Digital Transformation: Pathways for Deployment Upgrade and Technological Innovation
papers.authors: Sanglin Zhao
papers.abstract: Digital technology has become a fundamental driving force for global economic and social restructuring.Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data, cloud edge computing, digital twins andblockchain are transforming digital research from laboratory exploration to large-scale engineeringpromotion.Unlike traditional journals that prioritize pure algorithmic theory, the goal of Digital Deployment andInnovation Technology is to integrate digital theory, engineering deployment, and industrial innovation. Itemphasizes practicality and deployability to compensate for the widespread neglect of situationaladaptation in mainstream academic research. Modern digital deployment has evolved into a systemengineering that covers architecture design, resource allocation, terminal coordination, and networksecurity. With the expansion of 5G/6G and industrial Internet, the traditional deployment framework cannotmeet the requirements of cross domain collaboration, lightweight deployment and stable and high securityoperation.This magazine advocates scenario oriented innovation and deployment centered theoretical upgrading. Itgathers research on digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence deployment, digital twins, network security,and industrial digitization, linking academic research with on-site practice. Faced with the deepening globaldigital transformation in the fields of manufacturing, cities, energy, and education, the integration ofcutting-edge technologies has brought both opportunities and obstacles. This journal provides an openacademic platform to share standardized deployment solutions and innovative methods, promoting efficienttranslation of digital achievements and high-quality growth of the digital economy.

papers.title: The User Agency Trap in Media Literacy Chatbots: Interactive Evaluation Format, Imperfection Disclosure, and Visual Misinformation Discernment
papers.authors: Jiyoung Lee, Suhyun Kim, Hakjun Lee, Jiwon Hwang
papers.abstract: Although media literacy interventions are increasingly used to counter misinformation, many remain text-centered and non-interactive, limiting engagement during real-time evaluation. This limitation is particularly consequential for visual misinformation, where realistic synthetic images can encourage intuitive judgments. This study examines how two chatbot design features—interactive evaluation format and chatbot (im)perfection disclosure—shape perceived user and AI agency and, in turn, truth discernment. In an online experiment (N = 348), participants evaluated visual misinformation in a chatbot-supported task varying these two features. Interactive evaluation increased perceived user agency but decreased perceived AI agency, whereas imperfection disclosure modestly increased user agency without affecting AI agency. Critically, interactive evaluation indirectly reduced truth discernment through increased perceived user agency. These findings reveal a potential user agency trap: chatbot interactivity can make users feel more empowered while paradoxically undermining their ability to discern visual misinformation.

papers.title: Uso de inteligencia artificial en la educación: Beneficio o perjuicio en los estudiantes
papers.authors: Juan Carlos Arturo González Castro, Gloria Leticia Corrales Félix, Francisco Javier Mendoza Farías, Aurora González González, Alma Rosa Lydia Lozano González
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been progressively integrated into educational processes through smart tutors, adaptive learning platforms, virtual assistants, and generative AI tools, such as ChatGPT. These technologies can personalize instruction, provide immediate feedback, facilitate access to information, and support students with different learning paces and needs. However, their use also poses risks related to technological dependence, misinformation, data privacy, unequal access, plagiarism, and a decline in critical thinking. This paper analyzes whether artificial intelligence represents a benefit or a detriment to students. This literature review examines eight documents—including scientific articles, institutional reports, and academic papers—to assess their main advantages, limitations, and conditions of use.
