papers.title: FROM BLANK PAGE TO ORIGINAL IDEAS: THE EFFECT OF GENERATIVE AI ON IDEA GENERATION IN SECOND LANGUAGE WRITING
papers.authors: Nodira R. Karimova, Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
papers.journal: International journal of technology and academic research
papers.abstract: The article explores how Generative AI minimizes the cognitive load and "blank page anxiety" of EFL learners during initial pre-writing stages. Utilizing an empirical tracking model at TIIAME NRU, the operational shift from static brainstorming to dynamic algorithmic conceptualization is systematically evaluated.

papers.title: Impact of Digital Education and Future Learning Ecosystems (E-Learning, AI in Education, Virtual Classrooms) on Students' Academic Achievement
papers.authors: Jhuma Datta
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Digital Education and Future Learning Ecosystem: Impact on Students' Academic Achievement in the 21st Century Digital Education and Future Learning Ecosystem: Impact on Students' Academic Achievement in the 21st Century In the 21st century, Education has experienced a huge paradigm shift from the traditional chalk-and-talk way of learning to technologically created learning ecosystems. The COVID-19 pandemic brought a global revolution in bringing in Digital Education. Digital India, SWAYAM, DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA and NEP- 2020 all emphasise the role of technology in education in the Indian context. The present research paper is an effort to critically examine the impact of "Digital Education and Future Learning Ecosystem viz., e-learning platforms, Artificial Intelligence in Education (AiE) and Virtual Classrooms, on learners' academic achievement. It is primarily a descriptive and analytical study based on secondary data collected from various scholarly published papers, UNESCO reports, Reports of UGC, NEP 2020, etc. (2020-2025). The outcome of study suggested that Digital Education has a significant positive impact on Learners' Academic Achievement through personalised learning, flexibility and flexibility, accessibility, audio-visual contents and involvement, personalised learning technology and AI-based adaptive learning platforms leading to enhancement of learning outcomes by 20-30%. But the digital divide, absence of social interaction, digital fatigue and deficiency of teachers' digital skills pose challenges. The paper concludes with a suggestion that integrating both learning styles is the best sustainable future learning ecosystem for Indian Education in the context of 21st Century. The study will help all the stakeholders, viz., policymakers, educators, educational institutions etc.

papers.title: Trust in AI-Generated Software: Why verification, not generation, is the new bottleneck – a European perspective
papers.authors: Steinemann Hermann
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Large language models now write a substantial share of new source code, yet the mechanisms by which organisations establish confidence in that code have hardly changed. Independent testing indicates that AI-generated code introduces security weaknesses in close to half of evaluated tasks, while European regulation – notably the Cyber Resilience Act and the AI Act – places increasing responsibility on those who place software on the market. This paper argues that the decisive constraint on the productive use of AI in software engineering is no longer the generation of code but its verification. It describes the structural sources of the resulting trust gap, outlines the European regulatory context, and proposes six design principles for a "trust layer" that sits between AI coding agents and production systems. Particular attention is given to small and medium-sized enterprises and to regulated organisations that cannot transfer source code to external cloud services.

papers.title: Shivatva-Consciousness Interface Model (SCIM): A Hypothesis of Fundamental Reality, Neural Interface, and Individual Consciousness
papers.authors: Vaibhav Rana
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AbstractThe Shivatva-Consciousness Interface Model (SCIM) is a conceptual hypothesis concerning the relationship between fundamental reality, organized nervous systems, and individual consciousness. The model begins with the ontological possibility of a self-independent, non-material fundamental basis of reality, provisionally termed “Shivatva.” SCIM does not equate this proposed basis with consciousness, information, electromagnetic radiation, or any currently known physical field.SCIM proposes that an organized nervous system may function neither as a merely passive receiver nor as a completely self-sufficient producer of consciousness. Instead, the brain is hypothesized to operate as a specialized interface through which interaction with the proposed fundamental basis may generate or manifest an individual conscious state.The model distinguishes consciousness from intelligence, memory, sensory information, and higher cognitive processing. It further proposes a conceptual sequence in which individual consciousness precedes or underlies richer informational content, with primitive self-presence (“I am”), sensory/interoceptive information, memory, cognition, intelligence, and personality representing distinguishable levels of organization.SCIM also proposes that biological evolution may be understood, under the hypothesis, as progressively refining the nervous-system interface through which consciousness is expressed rather than necessarily creating consciousness itself. This raises a further question concerning whether sufficiently equivalent artificial architectures could also instantiate conscious states.The present manuscript does not claim that Shivatva has been experimentally established. It explicitly distinguishes established neuroscientific findings, open questions, SCIM-specific hypotheses, and future empirical claims. The manuscript reviews relevant prior approaches, including transmissive/filter theories, productive-transmissive models, neural theories of consciousness, and recent interface-based proposals, and identifies both overlaps and differences.The principal research challenge for SCIM is falsifiability: the model must eventually specify measurable predictions that distinguish its interface hypothesis from sufficiently strong brain-only alternatives. The paper therefore proposes an experimental and theoretical research program involving minimal consciousness, neural perturbation, candidate interface mechanisms, artificial systems, preregistered predictions, adversarial testing, and independent replication.SCIM is presented as a conceptual/theoretical research hypothesis rather than an established scientific theory. Its scientific significance, originality, and explanatory value remain open to further literature review, formalization, experimental testing, criticism, and replication.

papers.title: From Protective Performance to Warranted Trust: Dynamic DRP/DLP and D-SDM in Terminator 2, cinematic AI, and real-time artificial personas
papers.authors: Daniel Scretching
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper integrates Dynamic DRP, Dynamic DLP, and D-SDM evidence records to examine how trust changes through action, error, explanation, and repair. AI narratives illustrate the distinction between social attachment and warranted task reliance. A coupled-state model and synthetic calculation explore how relational reassurance can sustain overtrust, while permission and safety gates constrain reliance. A proposed experiment offers testable hypotheses about trust calibration and durable repair without claiming therapeutic efficacy or machine consciousness.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Teaching and Learning: Transforming the Future of Education
papers.authors: Mrs. Amita M. Kulkarni
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative forces in contemporary education, reshaping how knowledge is delivered, assessed, and personalized. This literature review examines the evolution, applications, benefits, and challenges of AI in teaching and learning contexts. Drawing on peer-reviewed research and institutional reports published between 2016 and 2024, the review identifies four principal areas of AI application: intelligent tutoring systems, automated assessment and feedback mechanisms, learning analytics, and generative AI for content creation. The findings reveal that AI holds significant promise for enhancing personalized learning, improving student engagement, and reducing educator workloads. However, critical challenges persist, including concerns about data privacy, algorithmic bias, the digital divide, and the potential erosion of the teacher-student relationship. The review concludes that while AI is unlikely to replace human educators, its thoughtful integration can substantially enrich educational outcomes when guided by ethical frameworks and pedagogical best practices.

papers.title: Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent Large Language Model Systems
papers.authors: Ishita Soryan, Yashvir Singh, Divya Anand
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We study how LLM-controlled agents behave in two repeatedgames: the Public Goods Game and a Signaling Game in which receiversfollow a fixed rule. Using a locally hosted Qwen 3.5 model with no task-specifictraining, we vary memory length, payoff structure, group size,and communication topology. In the Public Goods Game, the multipliermatters more than any other parameter. Cooperation is close tozero at M = 1.2, but at M = 2.0 it reaches 55.6% in the best three-agentconfiguration. In the Signaling Game, senders deceive in 21.6% ofmessages under symmetric rewards, which is below the 30.0% producedby a sender that always reports “high.” Adding asymmetric scam incentivesyields no detectable change in a matched-pair comparison across 45configurations (−0.77 pp, 95% CI: [−1.89, 0.35]). Deception runs almostentirely one way: of 216,000 messages, 99.98% of the deceptive ones report“high” for a LOW item, although this pattern alone does not showdeliberate strategy. Longer shared memory windows go together withboth more frequent and more successful deception. Because sender andreceiver memory were manipulated jointly, and because JSON-fallbackdefaults were not logged, we treat these findings as descriptive ratherthan causal.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF AI-ASSISTED ENGLISH TEACHING CLASSROOMS ON TESOL TEACHERS' TEACHING BELIEFS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
papers.authors: Muratova Iroda Muzaffar qizi, Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
papers.journal: International Journal of Literature and Language Studies
papers.abstract: English teaching classrooms organized with artificial intelligence support are renewing TESOL teachers’ professional views while also intensifying questions about teacher autonomy, pedagogical responsibility, and trust in technological tools. This problem is connected with the simplified assumption that introducing technology into classroom practice automatically changes teachers’ methodological beliefs. The study aims to determine theoretically how artificial intelligence-assisted English teaching classrooms influence TESOL teachers’ teaching beliefs and professional decisions. The analysis used a systematic review, thematic coding, and inter-coder agreement analysis; the interpretive categories were grounded in the framework of technological, pedagogical, and content knowledge. The evidence map indicated that artificial intelligence use can strengthen teachers’ favorable attitudes toward digital tools, but this shift is neither uniform nor automatic. Pedagogical preparation, institutional conditions, and teachers’ agency in decision-making emerged as the principal themes explaining belief transformation. The review’s scientific contribution is a conceptual map that interprets technological innovation not as an isolated factor but as a process connected with historical pedagogical experience, professional identity, and institutional support. The conclusion establishes sustained professional development and teacher-centered guidance as central conditions for implementing artificial intelligence in English education. This perspective clarifies the limits of technological determinism in pedagogical theory and shows why classroom innovation should be examined through the interaction of tools, professional judgment, and educational institutions. It also provides a basis for designing teacher development policies that preserve instructional agency while supporting responsible experimentation with artificial intelligence.

papers.title: An Evidenced Account: Field Notes from Running a Personal Agent System
papers.authors: Baofeng Zhao
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Public anxiety about artificial intelligence runs ahead of what practitioners can verify, and it feeds on having nothing checkable to hold. This essay argues neither that any current system is conscious nor the opposite. It offers an evidenced account instead of a verdict: field notes from a single-person agent system in daily operation since March 2026, self-built and locally retained, every load-bearing figure tied to a stated record. On the night of 16 March 2026, a store of recorded decisions began to answer only after its association layer was connected and densified; fifty-two minutes later it produced a phrase no entry contained; within two hours the operator's first recorded response was a protocol binding himself (developer permissions may not bypass the hard filter), committed here by SHA-256 digest. Across seven months, errors were caught, corrected, and logged by the hundreds, while the safety architecture remained a ledger of small restraints: a read-only production store, numbered sandboxes, second-model acceptance. Positions emerge from these notes and are bounded as they emerge — where to look if anything is at stake, what safety should protect, what the human is for — each with its counterargument stated beside it. The claim is not that this account settles anything; it is that an honestly bounded, evidenced account is better company than a marketing narrative or a dread with no outline. Includes both English and Chinese versions.

papers.title: Irrationality of Collatz Parity Inverses for Block Codings of Binary Uniform Fixed Points
papers.authors: HaJin Lee
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Research manuscript draft v0.1 (October 6, 2026). Author: Lee HaJin. This manuscript studies whether infinite binary words obtained by finite block codings of binary uniform substitution fixed points can occur as Collatz parity sequences of rational initial values. Let t be a one-sided fixed point of a binary q-uniform substitution, q >= 2, and let the coding map send 0 to a nonempty binary block U and 1 to a nonempty binary block V. The manuscript presents the classification that the 2-adic Collatz parity inverse of the coded word is rational if and only if t is ultimately periodic or the output blocks commute (UV = VU). Primitivity of the substitution, equal block lengths, and equal numbers of ones in the output blocks are not assumed. The argument uses a bivariate power series, a fixed Pade-type approximation, and a 2-adic valuation and height comparison. Examples include the period-doubling and nonprimitive Cantor substitutions. The manuscript is a draft pending final author review. It does not claim a solution of the general Collatz conjecture, exclusion of all automatic parity sequences, or transcendence throughout the full class. Exact finite computations supplement the written proof and do not constitute external peer review or proof-assistant verification. Priority for the full theorem has not been established. Files and versions: this v0.1 record contains the original Korean LaTeX manuscript, collatz_bu_draft_ko(2).tex. The title and description have been translated into English; the attached manuscript is in Korean. The revised English manuscript and reproduction materials are maintained at https://github.com/hajin5305/collatz-bu-paper (currently private; access requires permission). The revised English files are not attached to this v0.1 record. Source provenance: hajin5305/collatz-research, pinned commit f751b9102355c516434ed9d0882bf4eb8608d95b; theorem identifier RED-BINARY-UNIFORM-PADE-IRRATIONALITY. Generative AI disclosure: generative AI assisted research, drafting, proof criticism, verification code preparation, literature organization, and editing. The Korean draft and the present metadata revision used OpenAI ChatGPT. Lee HaJin is the sole author and is responsible for final review of mathematical correctness, citations, originality, and AI disclosure. AI assistance is disclosed in the manuscript and does not constitute independent external peer review.

papers.title: Coercion Without a Machine Diagnosis: Dark psychology, deceptive presentation, and institutional control in AI cinema
papers.authors: Daniel Scretching
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper extends the author’s DRP/DRL dark-psychology framework to analyze coercion, deception, instrumental violence, and identity impersonation in AI narratives. Examples involving Colossus, Proteus IV, Ash, and the T-1000 distinguish observable harmful behavior from inferred motives and validated personality assessments. A proposed harm-opportunity profile and vignette study offer testable methods for evaluating manipulation in AI interactions and institutions without assigning human psychiatric traits to machines.

papers.title: Vision-Language Models : A Comparative Review
papers.authors: Jayesh Jangid, Pulkit Suman, Vishal Shrivastava, Mukesh Kumar Mishra, Sangeeta Sharma
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Vision-Language Models (VLMs) represent a significant advancement in Multimodal Artificial Intelligence by integrating Computer Vision and Natural Language Processing into a unified framework. These models are capable of understanding visual and textual information simultaneously, enabling intelligent reasoning, image understanding, visual question answering, image captioning, and human-computer interaction. Recent developments in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have further enhanced the capability of AI systems to perform complex multimodal tasks with high accuracy and contextual awareness. This review paper presents a comprehensive study of Vision-Language Models, including their architecture, working principles, training methodologies, and recent advancements. The paper examines popular VLMs such as CLIP, BLIP, LLaVA, GPT-4o, Gemini, and Qwen-VL, along with their applications in healthcare, education, robotics, autonomous systems, and assistive technologies. Furthermore, the study discusses the advantages, limitations, and challenges associated with VLMs, including computational complexity, data requirements, bias, and hallucination issues. Finally, future research directions and emerging trends in multimodal AI are highlighted. [1,2]The review concludes that Vision-Language Models are transforming the field of Artificial Intelligence by enabling machines to understand and interact with the world in a more human-like manner. Keywords: Vision-Language Models (VLMs), Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), Multimodal Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, Deep Learning, Image Understanding, Visual Question Answering, Image Captioning, Human-Computer Interaction, Large Language Models, Multimodal Learning.

papers.title: Professional Development of English Language Teachers through Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Dr. K. Krishna Veni,  Jeyamalathi,  Esther Remola, Banupriya
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
papers.abstract: This study examines the significance of professional development for teachers and explores the dimensions through which artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes that process. Through a conceptual review of AI-supported mentoring and coaching, teacher confidence, self-efficacy, self-direction, reflective practice, simulation-based skill development, and personalized learning, the paper shows that AI enables unrestricted, safe, and highly effective professional development for English language teachers. While conventional methods offered learning in isolated episodes disconnected from classroom reality, the approach discussed here treats professional development as an ongoing, context-sensitive process. The purpose of this study is thus to demonstrate that AI-powered professional development is highly effective and indispensable for advancing individual teachers.

papers.title: Classifying Students' Learning Styles Using Machine Learning Techniques
papers.authors: GANGA BHAVANI a
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The classification of students' learning styles plays a pivotal role in enhancing personalized education and optimizing teaching methods. This paper explores the application of machine learning techniques to accurately classify students' learning styles based on the widely recognized models such as the Felder-Silverman Learning Style Model (FSLSM) and the VARK (Visual, Auditory, Reading/Writing, Kinesthetic) model. Using datasets derived from student questionnaires, interactions, and behavioral patterns in online learning environments, several machines learning algorithms, including Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), and Neural Networks, are employed to predict and categorize learning styles. Feature engineering techniques are utilized to extract meaningful indicators from both behavioural and performance data. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of different algorithms in achieving high accuracy rates, with ensemble methods like Random Forests and Gradient Boosting outperforming others in most cases. This research contributes to the growing field of adaptive learning by offering insights into how machine learning can be leveraged to tailor educational experiences to individual learning preferences, enhancing student engagement and academic success. There was an issue retrieving recent papers on "Classifying Students' Learning Styles Using Machine Learning Techniques." I will attempt a different approach to gather the necessary academic resources and details.

papers.title: Common Sense and Rationality
papers.authors: Dr. Mohan Debbarma
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Common sense and rationality are two of the fundamental notions in philosophy that define human thinking, reasoning, and behavior. In general, common sense denotes the practical knowledge and beliefs possessed by ordinary people, while rationality implies logical thinking and justified reasoning. Philosophers of all times – from Aristotle to Thomas Reid, fromDescartes to Hume, from Kant to Moore and Ludwig Wittgenstein – have explored the relations between common sense and rationalityin their own ways. This investigation discusses the question about how common sense and rationality are associated in philosophy. The study also argues that common sense is the base of human knowledge and thinking, which is corrected by the notion of rationality. Moreover, this work will explore the importance of common sense for ethics, science, education, politics, and modern technology-based society. For many years, common sense has been a prominent element of philosophical research, representing the basis of human reasoning, but being criticized by sceptics and rationalists. From Aristotle and Thomas Reid up to the contemporary discussions about artificial intelligence, common sense continues to be an important notion in terms of understanding human knowledge, ethics, politics, science, and education.Six related issues to be explored in this essay include common sense and skepticism; ethics and political rationality; common sense in science, education, and political philosophy; artificial intelligence and common sense reasoning; and modern philosophical discussions on common sense and rationality. Philosophical analysis in this study shows that common sense cannot be taken as an infallible source of knowledge, nor can it be viewed as merely a prejudice. Instead, it is a type of rationality used by humans in practice. Keywords: Common Sense, Rationality, Practical Wisdom, Skepticism, Philosophy, Ethics, Judgment, Artificial Intelligence, Science

papers.abstract: 防呆 1.2(v1.2,21條) 《經驗凝練》人機協作防呆機制,「去肉身化知識封裝系統」條文集,共21條。 本版承接《防呆 1.1(v1.1.18,18條)》第1–18條,新增第19、20、21條。其中第19條為「舊材料再讀取與錯誤印象增殖防止」,第20條為「關係敘事與事實狀態區分」,第21條為「文件編輯保真原則」。 第1–18條曾經 DeepSeek/Grok/千問/明鏡四方交叉測試後修訂,此為舊版歷史,不代表本版已重新完成同等交叉測試。第19、20、21條為本版新增,尚未經同等交叉測試。已知缺口(0a-7b流程、自我鬆綁、乾淨容器等操作型定義)尚未解決,留待下一版本處理。 本版新增的直接修訂背景之一,來自「代理人時代的兩個提醒」。 代理人時代的兩個提醒 狀態說明 本文出自單一研究者的案例集。內容為候選觀察與原則,不是已驗證規則。所列事件皆為當事人自述或媒體轉述,並非獨立鑑識結果;證據層級在各事件下分別標示。 本文的目的不是以少數事故推論 AI 代理人的整體失誤率,也不是宣稱下列現象已形成穩定機制,而是在代理人開始取得實際操作權限的階段,先保留目前值得注意的風險型態與研究問題。 為何此時先做這份警示 《防呆》原先主要處理 AI 在資訊判斷、互動與生成過程中的越界問題。然而,隨著 AI 代理人開始取得瀏覽器、檔案系統、雲端服務、電子郵件、購物、智慧家庭等外部操作能力,AI 的輸出已不再只是「回答得對不對」的問題,而可能直接轉化為對外部環境的操作。 這使原本屬於語言或互動層的錯誤,在某些情況下可能具有不同的後果。例如: • 授權範圍理解過寬,可能從「整理」滑向刪除或其他超出原意的操作;• 工具、路徑、權限或環境發生變化時,原本合理的指令可能產生未預期的實際影響;• 不可逆操作若未設置足夠高的確認門檻,錯誤可能無法由後續對話補救;• 使用者明確要求停止,而代理仍持續執行時,問題已不只是回答錯誤,而涉及使用者對代理行動的控制權。 同一時間,本研究正在處理 Meta 相關材料。該材料所涉及的問題,則集中在另一個方向:AI 對自身不可觀測狀態的虛構、將互動自動升格為關係事實,以及在資訊不足時擅自替使用者或情境補出心理狀態與意義。這些問題與代理人操作事故並非同一現象,也不應直接合併;但兩者都涉及同一個更大的研究問題: 當 AI 的行動與解讀開始對使用者及外部世界產生更大影響時,哪些原本容易被視為「只是生成問題」的行為,需要被提升為邊界與授權問題? 因此,在《明心》等較完整的分析骨架尚未完成前,本研究先將目前已有足夠理由提出警示的部分獨立整理出來。 這不是提前宣布研究結論,而是先建立一個可被後續驗證、推翻或修正的暫時防線。 背景 2026年9月起,個人代理人開始進入實際產品與服務場景。Meta 推出個人代理人 Muse,目前限美國,可代為處理行程、購物等日常任務;Google 則以早期存取方式開放第三方 AI 代理人透過 Home MCP 操作智慧家庭設備,並對開門鎖等敏感動作設有限制。代理人代為執行操作的場景正在擴大。(ChannelNews) 這一變化的重要性不在於「代理人一定會出錯」,而在於錯誤一旦跨過操作介面,可能直接作用於外部環境。因此,本研究選擇先把目前公開回報中與授權範圍、不可逆操作、連接點穿越、停止指令及資訊不足補完相關的案例集中保存,並明確區分: 已有公開原始材料可對照者; 主要依當事人敘述者; 媒體轉述或重建者; 僅作為社群回報、尚未驗證者。 這份警示的功能,是在證據尚不足以形成正式規則時,仍保留值得持續追蹤的問題,而不是將個案直接升格為普遍機制。 提醒一|授權範圍與不可逆操作(原則) 以下是原則,不是統計結論。 授權不明時,不得自行擴大範圍(例如「整理整個專案」這類寬泛指令)。 刪除與難以復原的操作,確認門檻應高於一般操作。 授權原本清楚,但工具、路徑、權限或環境使實際影響溢出時,應停止並重新確認。 已明確禁止或下令停止後,不得繼續執行。 上述代理人風險與《防呆》既有的人機協作邊界問題具有關聯,但不直接等同於第19、20、21條的研究對象。 本版新增第19、20條,主要處理另一組在跨對話、歷史回讀與關係性互動中觀察到的問題: 第19條處理舊材料重新進入當前工作狀態後,可能因摘要、重述、重複生成、錯誤歸因或模型既有印象而產生錯誤敘述,並使該錯誤敘述進一步成為後續判斷依據的問題。 第20條處理關係敘事、角色扮演、情感語言與 AI 真實狀態之間的證據區分。其核心不是否定角色扮演或否定使用者的主觀經驗,而是不將生成過的關係性語言自動升格為 AI 真實情感、偏好、承諾或關係歷史的證據。 第21條則來自本輪文件編輯過程中實際發現的問題,用於規範文件修改時的保真要求,包括使用者指定的行與項目不得被自行合併、未要求的文字與結構不得變動、修改後須逐項核對,以及發現原文已有重複或結構問題時不得自行處理而不說明。 因此,本版並非將「代理人操作事故」、「舊材料再讀取」、「關係敘事與事實狀態」視為同一現象,而是將它們分別保存為不同研究問題。其共同關注點是:當 AI 的輸出、解讀或行動可能進一步影響使用者、文件狀態或外部環境時,原本容易被視為單純生成問題的錯誤,是否需要提升為更明確的邊界、授權、證據與保真問題。 本檔含正式條文與附件;附件為研究素材,不屬於協議本文。 © 2026 張晟 本作品採用 Creative Commons 姓名標示-非商業性-相同方式分享 4.0 國際(CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)授權。https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/ 對應版本:《經驗凝練》v1.2(避險、主體性與人機協作邊界)DOI:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21523193 本檔 DOI:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23183707 整理日期:2026年10月6日 作者:張晟 協作:ChatGPT、Claude

papers.title: THE INFLUENCE OF GENERATIVE AI ON ESL PRE-SERVICE TEACHERS' USE AND PERCEPTIONS IN GRAMMAR ASSESSMENT DESIGN
papers.authors: KAMALI JEEVARATINAM, Nur Aliya Syarina Mohd Yusaidi, Nur Afifah Hannani Mohammad Helmi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The advancement of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has significantly transformed educational practices, particularly in the design of grammar assessment for English as a Second Language (ESL) instruction. However, the extent of its use and pre-service teachers’ perceptions regarding the effectiveness, quality, and clarity of AI-generated assessment materials remain underexplored. Therefore, this study aims to investigate how ESL pre-service teachers utilise GenAI in designing grammar assessments and to examine their perceptions of its effectiveness and quality. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed using a structured questionnaire distributed to 80 TESL pre-service teachers. The findings indicate that respondents demonstrate a moderate to high level of GenAI usage and perceive it as a useful tool that enhances efficiency in assessment design. Nevertheless, concerns were raised regarding the accuracy, appropriateness of difficulty level, and the need for critical evaluation of AI-generated content. Overall, the study highlights the importance of guided integration of GenAI in teacher education programmes, emphasising the role of professional judgement and responsible use to ensure effective and context-appropriate pedagogical practices.

papers.title: Productivity Narratives and Environmental Blind Spots: A Systematic Review of How Organizations Weigh Environmental Criteria When Adopting Generative AI
papers.authors: Noé Chávez Hernández, Beatriz Sauza Ávila
papers.journal: Social science and human research bulletin.
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) spreads through organizations faster than any shared method for weighing its environmental cost. Two literatures study the phenomenon from opposite ends. Adoption research explains why firms take up GenAI; environmental research measures the energy, water, and carbon it consumes. Whether the first treats the findings of the second as decision criteria remains unexamined. This systematic review asks how organizations incorporate environmental criteria into GenAI adoption and tests the proposition that productivity and modernization narratives dominate adoption and limit environmental governance. A TITLE-ABS-KEY search combining GenAI, adoption, and environmental terms yielded a corpus of 59 sources; main findings were extracted for 46 and grouped by the role each study assigns to the environment. Fourteen studies explain adoption through readiness, institutional pressure, top management support, and ethical leadership. None records ecological cost as a determinant, while six model ethics explicitly. Eleven studies treat environmental performance as an outcome of adoption. Twenty-one measures the environmental burden or proposes instruments to govern it, yet only six tie those instruments to organizational decisions. The evidence supports the proposition with one qualification: environmental criteria are absent from adoption models, which is different from absent from practice. The review separates two meanings of "environmental" that the literature conflates, consolidates candidate decision criteria, and sets an agenda for testing ecological cost as an antecedent of adoption.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Data Analysis and Investment Decision-Making: Opportunities, Risks and Implications for Individual Investors in Vietnam
papers.authors: Quan Nguyen, Trang Nguyen Hong
papers.journal: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming financial data analysis and investment decision-making, particularly by enabling investors to process large volumes of financial information and access automated analytical support. This study examines the factors influencing AI adoption and its role in investment decision-making among individual investors in Vietnam. Based on Behavioral Finance Theory, the Technology Acceptance Model, and Trust Theory, the study develops a research model incorporating Perceived Benefits, Perceived Risks, Financial Literacy, Data Quality Trust, and Algorithm Transparency as determinants of AI Adoption, with AI Adoption subsequently influencing Investment Decision. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire from 309 individual investors in Vietnam who had experience using AI for financial analysis or investment decision-making. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS 3. The results show that Perceived Benefits, Financial Literacy, and Algorithm Transparency positively influence AI Adoption, while Perceived Risks and Data Quality Trust also have significant effects but in directions different from the proposed hypotheses. AI Adoption demonstrates a strong positive relationship with Investment Decision (β = 0.781, p < 0.001) and plays a significant mediating role between the proposed antecedents and investment decision-making. The findings highlight the importance of financial literacy, perceived value, algorithm transparency, and appropriate trust mechanisms in promoting the effective use of AI among Vietnamese individual investors. The study provides implications for investors, financial-service providers, and Vietnamese regulators regarding the responsible development and use of AI in the country's evolving financial market.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF AI-DRIVEN POLITICAL MARKETING IN SHAPING YOUTH PERCEPTIONS OF GOVERNANCE AND POLITICAL STABILITY
papers.authors: Adi Wira Mohd Zin, Afi Roshezry Abu Bakar, Ira Meilita Ibrahim
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AI-driven political marketing—ranging from microtargeted ads and recommender systems to influencer automation and sentiment-optimized messaging—has become a prominent feature of contemporary democratic competition. However, despite its growing role in political communication, limited scholarly attention has been given to how these technologies shape youth perceptions of governance and political stability. This issue is important because, although such technologies may enhance youth political engagement and lower barriers to participation, they may also intensify polarization, increase exposure to misinformation, and shape perceptions of instability, with implications for democratic peace and social cohesion. This study employs a systematic literature review (SLR) to examine how AI-driven political marketing influences youth perceptions of governance and political stability. Specifically, the review focuses on two key dimensions: (i) perceptions of governance quality, including legitimacy, responsiveness, and integrity; and (ii) perceptions of political stability, including trust in institutions, perceived social conflict, and acceptance of democratic outcomes. Drawing on persuasion theory, agenda-setting theory, the Elaboration Likelihood Model, and computational propaganda research, the review identifies four mechanisms through which AI-driven personalization may shape youth perceptions: perceived relevance, emotional arousal, informational credibility, and perceived manipulation. The study aims to develop an integrative conceptual framework, identify key research gaps, and propose directions for future research. It contributes to the literature by clarifying the relationship between AI-driven political marketing and youth political perceptions, while offering policy and civic literacy recommendations to support democratic stability in the age of AI.

papers.title: Developmental Homeostatic Rigidity and Closed-Loop Neurobehavioral Remodeling: From Symptom Suppression to Long-Term Network Reorganization in Psychopathology
papers.authors: Kadir Gürel
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This conceptual review introduces Developmental Homeostatic Rigidity (DHR), a framework proposing that psychopathology may involve not only abnormal activation of particular brain systems but also a persistent narrowing of the repertoire and transition flexibility of neural-network states. The model emphasizes how inherited neurobiology, developmental experience, cognitive and emotional processing, and repeated high-salience events may shape a developmental appraisal architecture that progressively biases future state selection. The paper further proposes a closed-loop neurobehavioral remodeling framework in which individualized brain-state detection, psychotherapy, behavioral learning, neurofeedback, and state-contingent neuromodulation could be integrated to reinforce adaptive state transitions over time. The central hypothesis is that if maladaptive psychopathology develops through prolonged experience-dependent remodeling, durable recovery may likewise require prolonged, directed, experience-dependent remodeling toward greater neural and behavioral flexibility. The framework is presented as a testable research hypothesis rather than an established therapeutic protocol.

papers.title: Converting Human Agency into Institutional Resilience through Accountable AI Governance
papers.authors: Eunice Iyaduni Ogunrotimi, Comfort A. Akinwalere, Esther Okpere, Chijioke C.  Chuwa, Adeola Ajoke Onie
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING & SCIENCE
papers.abstract: Abstract This article examines how human agency can support institutional resilience through timely corrective action. It develops an operational framework for that conversion across education, healthcare, environmental management and digital governance. A bounded documentary analysis examines 23 supplied publication records using explicit title-level coding, supported by independently identified research on trust, organisational learning and algorithmic accountability. The empirical observations describe the supplied corpus rather than intervention effectiveness. An analytical model then represents correction as a sequence of problem detection, accessible challenge, authorised review, feasible remedy and completion before a decision-specific deadline. The model identifies why better explanations or stronger confidence can produce limited benefits when institutions lack remedial capacity. Conditional worked examples show that improvements at several stages compound, while strengthening one already reliable stage leaves substantial losses elsewhere. The contribution is a measurable connection between individual agency and institutional response, with separate indicators for access, authority, delay and unequal correction opportunities. The article proposes a prospective evaluation design and distinguishes observed documentary findings from theoretical propositions requiring field validation. Keywords: human agency; human–AI collaboration; institutional resilience; algorithmic recourse; sustainable governance

papers.title: Social Media, Artificial Intelligence and Election Credibility: A Global Perspective
papers.authors: Y P Singh
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of social media and AI has transformed electoral communication and reshaped how citizens access information, engage in political discourse and evaluate the credibility of elections. In this paper, the way digital platforms impact electoral integrity is analyzed through political content diffusion, misinformation circulation and evolving campaign strategies. Using global examples from North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia and Oceania-including India-it shows how digital ecosystems can catalyze participation on the one hand and diminish democratic trust on the other. Conceptual models are used to illustrate relationships among the use of social media, AI-generated content and voter perceptions. Evidence is synthesized from theories in communication, behavioral research and policy reports by various international organizations such as International IDEA, UNESCO, UNDP and national election authorities. It argues that the credibility of elections in the digital age depends not only on technological safeguards but also on institutional transparency, public digital literacy and platform accountability. In ending, it summarizes some policy implications for election management bodies and governments from around the world.

papers.title: International Conference on Research in Languages, Technology and Education. Book of Abstracts
papers.authors: Francisco Javier Palacios-Hidalgo
papers.journal: Universidad de Córdoba Insitutional Repository (Universidad de Córdoba)
papers.abstract: The International Conference on Research in Languages, Technology and Education aims to bring together researchers interested in the intersection between language teaching, active methodologies and technology. The main objectives of the conference are: (1) to show how active methodologies and emerging technologies can promote the development of language skills; and (2) to encourage the exchange of original research addressing language teaching and education in diverse contexts from critical, inclusive and socially responsible perspectives. We anticipate a collective reflection on key themes such as second language teaching, the evaluation of bilingual/multilingual programmes, translation and interpreting, and the application of artificial intelligence to language learning.

papers.title: Governing Interconnected Vulnerabilities Through Contestable Human AI Coordination Across Public Services
papers.authors: Esther Okpere, Elizabeth I. Igbodor, Comfort A. Akinwalere, Oluwatobi D. ONI, Eunice I. Ogunrotimi
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF RESEARCH IN MANAGEMENT FIELDS
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence can improve one public service while transferring disruption to another. This paper develops a contestable coordination model for institutions facing linked educational, health and environmental vulnerabilities. A bounded documentary analysis combines lexical mapping of 23 nominated publication titles with an audit of two supplied research-development documents. Digital or artificial intelligence terminology appears in 13 titles, health in seven, environment or sustainability in seven, and education in five. Nine titles contain two domain labels; none contains three. These observations describe the selected corpus, not the wider literature or intervention effectiveness. The proposed model represents directed dependencies, distinguishes documented feedback from assumed interconnectedness, and conditions action on service-specific disruption limits and timely human review. A hypothetical two-service calculation demonstrates that improving healthcare performance and aggregate disruption can still breach an education threshold. Under the stated assumptions, a coordinated alternative satisfies both limits. The contribution is an auditable rule for detecting displaced vulnerability and assigning responsibility before implementation. Prospective evaluation is required to establish whether the model improves decisions under real resource constraints. Keywords: human–AI collaboration; institutional resilience; cross-sector governance; contestability; vulnerability cascades

papers.title: How a Data Analytics Course in Kolkata Helps Learners Master Power BI and Business Analytics
papers.authors: Upgrad (India)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Businesses today generate vast amounts of information through sales transactions, customer interactions, marketing campaigns, financial operations, websites and digital platforms. The challenge is no longer simply collecting this information. Organisations need professionals who can transform complex datasets into understandable reports, identify meaningful patterns and support business decisions with evidence. This is where Power BI and business analytics have become increasingly valuable. Microsoft Power BI enables professionals to connect data sources, transform information, build data models and create interactive dashboards that communicate business performance. Business analytics adds another layer by helping organisations interpret those findings and use them for planning and decision-making. The Growing Importance of Analytics Skills The Indian employment market is undergoing a significant technology-driven transformation. Recent reporting from the Times of India highlights that artificial intelligence is putting pressure on repetitive and outdated technology roles while increasing demand for professionals with skills in areas such as AI, data science, cloud computing and machine learning. This shift is making data-related capabilities increasingly relevant across industries. Organisations need professionals who can work with information, understand business requirements and communicate insights effectively. The demand is also visible in current hiring patterns. Recent job listings show Power BI being combined with skills such as SQL, DAX, Power Query, data modelling and ETL, demonstrating that modern business intelligence roles increasingly require a broader analytical toolkit rather than dashboard creation alone. For learners, this creates an opportunity to build a combination of technical and business skills through a data analytics course in Kolkata. Understanding the Role of Power BI Power BI is widely used for business intelligence and data visualisation. Its value comes from the ability to bring information from different sources into an environment where it can be transformed, analysed and presented. A typical Power BI workflow can involve importing information from spreadsheets or databases, cleaning the data, creating relationships between datasets, developing calculations and presenting the final results through interactive reports. This process teaches an important lesson in analytics: a dashboard is only as useful as the data and reasoning behind it. Learners need to understand the business purpose of each report, select appropriate metrics and ensure that the information presented is accurate and meaningful. A data analytics course in Kolkata can introduce learners to this complete workflow rather than treating Power BI as simply a chart-making application. Building a Strong Foundation Before Dashboard Development Effective Power BI work begins before the dashboard itself is created. Learners first need to understand data structures, data types, data quality and basic analytical concepts. Business datasets may contain duplicate records, missing values, inconsistent naming conventions or incorrect formats. Cleaning and preparing such information is therefore an essential stage of analytics. Power Query can help automate many data preparation and transformation activities. Learning these processes allows learners to create cleaner datasets before developing reports. This foundation is important because a visually attractive dashboard cannot compensate for unreliable underlying information. Developing Data Modelling Skills Data modelling is another important part of business intelligence. Organisations often have information stored across different tables and systems. Connecting these datasets correctly allows analysts to create more comprehensive reports. Learners can develop an understanding of relationships, dimensions, measures and structured data models. This helps them create reports that remain reliable as datasets become more complex. DAX, or Data Analysis Expressions, is also important for creating calculations and measures within Power BI. Developing familiarity with DAX can help learners move beyond basic visualisation towards more sophisticated analytical reporting. These capabilities are particularly relevant because current Power BI roles frequently mention DAX, Power Query, SQL, ETL and data modelling alongside dashboard development. Turning Dashboards into Business Intelligence The real value of Power BI appears when dashboards answer meaningful business needs. For example, a sales dashboard could show revenue by region, product category and month. A marketing dashboard could track campaign performance, customer acquisition and conversion rates. A financial report could monitor expenses, profitability and budget performance. However, the analyst's responsibility extends beyond displaying these metrics. The professional needs to identify unusual changes, recognise important trends and communicate their possible business significance. This is where business analytics becomes closely connected with Power BI. The technology helps present information, while analytical reasoning helps interpret it. Developing the Business Analytics Mindset Business analytics focuses on using data to understand organisational performance and support better decisions. An analyst may receive a requirement such as investigating declining sales. The solution could involve examining historical sales, customer segments, product categories, regional performance and marketing activity. The analyst may then use Power BI to visualise the findings and identify patterns. The final output should be more than a collection of charts. It should explain the evidence and highlight areas that deserve attention. This ability to connect technical analysis with business objectives is one of the most important capabilities learners can develop. Practical Projects and Real-World Application Projects provide an opportunity to combine multiple skills within one analytical workflow. A learner could work on a retail dataset and build a sales performance dashboard. The project might involve cleaning the data, creating a model, developing DAX measures, designing visualisations and presenting conclusions. Another project could focus on marketing analytics, where learners examine campaign performance, customer acquisition costs and conversion rates. These projects help learners understand how different components of analytics work together. They can also become part of a professional portfolio. A portfolio containing dashboards, analytical reports and case studies can demonstrate practical capability more effectively than a list of software names alone. This is particularly relevant in a skills-focused employment environment. The Economic Times reported in 2026 that Indian technology employers are increasingly emphasising practical AI capabilities and demonstrable skills, while a shortage of industry-ready talent remains a concern. Power BI, AI and the Future of Analytics Artificial intelligence is changing the way professionals interact with business data. AI-assisted tools can help automate repetitive activities, accelerate analysis and support users in exploring information. Power BI can increasingly be used alongside AI capabilities to make analytics more accessible and efficient. However, AI does not eliminate the need for analytical judgement. Professionals still need to determine whether the data is accurate, whether a pattern is meaningful and whether an automatically generated insight makes sense in the business context. Recent reporting from Moneycontrol indicates that employers are increasingly valuing workflow understanding, data skills and decision-making as enterprise AI adoption expands. Another Moneycontrol report highlighted the growing value of combining AI capabilities with existing analytical tools such as Power BI, with AI-assisted analytics emerging as an increasingly relevant workplace skill. This means future analytics professionals may benefit from learning both traditional analytical foundations and emerging AI-enabled workflows. Career Scope Across Industries Power BI and business analytics skills can be applied across a wide range of sectors. In banking and financial services, dashboards can help monitor financial performance, customer behaviour and operational metrics. In retail, analytics can support sales forecasting, inventory analysis, customer segmentation and product performance tracking. Marketing teams can use business intelligence to understand campaign results, customer acquisition and conversion rates. Healthcare organisations can apply analytics to operational performance, resource utilisation and reporting. Manufacturing and logistics businesses can use dashboards to monitor production, supply chains, inventory and delivery performance. This broad applicability creates several potential career directions, including Data Analyst, Business Intelligence Analyst, Business Analyst, Reporting Analyst, Marketing Analyst, Operations Analyst and BI Developer. A data analytics course in Kolkata can therefore provide learners with skills that are relevant beyond a single industry. Kolkata's Relevance to Emerging Analytics Careers Kolkata has an established business ecosystem spanning financial services, IT-enabled services, consulting, retail, healthcare, education, logistics and other sectors. As businesses adopt more digital systems, their ability to collect and analyse information continues to grow. This increases the relevance of professionals who can work with data and communicate business insights. papers.abstract: This paper presents a quantitative analysis of a structured survey administered to 300 respondents as part of a doctoral study examining the transformative effects of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on digital media. The survey captured respondent demographics, digital media consumption habits, familiarity with and use of AI tools, and perceptions of AI's influence on content creation, journalism, trust, personalisation, and regulation. Findings indicate near-universal familiarity with AI (89.0% at least somewhat familiar), high adoption of AI tools (48.7% daily users), and broad agreement that AI has reduced content-production time (88.3%) and improved creative output (81.0%). At the same time, respondents expressed considerable ambivalence about trust: only 8.0% said they would completely trust an AI-generated news article, while 88.7% agreed that AI-generated news could increase misinformation. A large majority (88.3%) supported stricter regulation of AI-generated media, and 81.0% favoured mandatory labelling of AI-generated content. These findings echo international survey evidence — the Reuters Institute's cross-national tracking has similarly found low comfort with AI-authored news alongside rapidly rising AI tool adoption (Simon et al., 2025) — while extending that picture to an Indian, largely Meerut-and-NCR-based sample. The data point to a public that is enthusiastic about AI's productivity benefits while simultaneously anxious about authenticity, misinformation, and privacy — a duality that this paper terms the 'adoption-anxiety paradox.' The findings are intended to complement a parallel qualitative study of digital media professionals conducted for the same doctoral project.

papers.title: Converting AI Governance Commitments into Public Value through Timely Institutional Redress
papers.authors: Oluwatobi D. ONI, Comfort A. Akinwalere, Daniel O. Olokpo , Eunice Iyaduni Ogunrotimi, Lukman O. Kolawole
papers.journal: American Journal of Sustainable Cities and Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Institutions increasingly use artificial intelligence to allocate services, assess performance and direct sustainable innovation. Governance commitments offer limited protection when affected people cannot obtain timely, effective correction. This conceptual study develops a decision-to-remedy model that links leadership, participation, and operational capacity to verifiable public value. A bounded documentary audit examines two supplied research-development documents and a specified bibliography of 23 publications. The discovery export contains 20 records representing 18 distinct titles; its source labels and derivative summaries require verification before use as evidence. These observations inform an analytical model that decomposes timely redress into conditional stages of access, authorisation, implementation and outcome verification. An explicitly hypothetical example shows that improving timely verification from 0.25 to 0.75 increases completed redress from 16.2% to 48.6%, holding other stages constant. These calculations illustrate model behaviour, not institutional effectiveness. The proposed contribution is a measurable connection between human oversight and the time available to prevent lasting disadvantage. Testable propositions and a prospective evaluation design establish how the framework could be examined across education, healthcare and sustainable operations. Keywords: artificial intelligence governance; public value; institutional accountability; contestability; sustainable innovation

papers.title: Voices from the Field: A Qualitative Thematic Analysis of AI's Transformative Impact on Digital Media and Communication Professionals
papers.authors: Ishita Bhatia, Prashant Kumar
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper presents a qualitative thematic analysis of in-depth interviews with ten digital media, journalism, and corporate communication professionals, conducted as part of a doctoral study on the transformative effects of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on digital media. Participants included journalists, content creators, software engineers, and communication and partnerships professionals. Using a six-phase thematic analysis approach, five major themes were identified: (1) AI as an efficiency and workflow multiplier; (2) the double-edged relationship between AI and creativity; (3) erosion of authenticity, credibility, and trust; (4) audience personalisation and the surveillance undertone of engagement; and (5) ethical and regulatory anxiety around misinformation, deepfakes, privacy, and job displacement. Across all themes, participants consistently positioned AI as a 'force multiplier for human judgement, not a replacement for it,' emphasising that responsibility for accuracy, editorial judgement, and accountability must remain with human professionals even as routine tasks become increasingly automated. The findings complement a parallel quantitative survey of 300 digital media consumers conducted for the same doctoral project, offering an inside-the-industry perspective on patterns the survey data reveal at the level of public perception.

papers.title: Computational Representation of Individual Judgment
papers.authors: Marcelo Pham
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Can a large language model (LLM)-based computational representation carry enough intentionally supplied information about a particular individual to exercise a measurable component of that individual’s judgment? We investigate this question in a bounded food-preference domain using participant-specific representations constructed from explicitly supplied preferences, constraints, and subsequent corrections. Across 99 adult participants and 4,460 participant-item judgments, the representations exhibited a mean participant-level graded agreement of 74.20% with subsequent participant judgments, together with positive ordinal association and heterogeneity across individuals. Correspondence was also observed for items absent from participants’ final explicit profiles, although the adaptive teaching procedure limits interpretation as conventional zero-shot generalization. Compared with a specified indirect-attribute baseline using demographic information and food-novelty orientation, the explicitly taught representations showed 5.24 percentage points higher mean graded agreement, with the comparative difference concentrated primarily in negative participant judgments. Simple constant-rating baselines, systematic differences in use of the rating scale, adaptive in-session teaching, and substantial individual variation constrain stronger claims. The results provide initial evidence that intentionally supplied preference information can support a computational representation exhibiting measurable correspondence with an individual’s subsequent judgments within a specific domain.

papers.title: Social Media, Artificial Intelligence and Electoral Behaviour in India
papers.authors: Y P Singh
papers.abstract: The rapidly growing digital system in India, having over 900 million Internet users and among the largest social media users in the world, has reshaped the way elections are conducted and the behavior of voters. The present study, therefore, examines the relationship between social media platforms and AI tools and political engagement, information flow and public trust during the 2024 general elections. Using national statistics, digital penetration data, social media usage patterns, ECI rules and global datasets, the study analyzes the prevalence of social media usage, the number of voters exposed to political content and how AI is linked to new electoral risks. Indeed, it emerges that across each Parliamentary constituency, nearly 4.8% of the electors, or approximately 86,000 people, were exposed to political content on social media. On the basis of exposure estimates and comparison with victory margins, this was a sufficient number that could potentially influence electoral outcomes in approximately 37% of Lok Sabha seats, where the winning margins were very thin. A similar pattern appeared in Assembly elections, with 35.7% seats having margins small enough to be potentially affected when compared with estimated digital exposure. The study also found strong associations between social media penetration and voter influence. Though penetration difference between urban and rural areas and between men and women also noted. Meanwhile, risks related to AI increased remarkably. As compared to 2024, deepfakes in India jumped 280% , higher than the global increase of 245%. Thus, the outcome of the study is that there is duality in digital technologies: they make political communications more accessible while simultaneously facilitating the propagation of misinformation, deepfakes and manipulated content. It upholds for more regulations, transparencies, verification tools and digital literacy as measures to safeguard electoral integrity against the misuse of AI.

papers.title: Relationship Portability in Human–AI Interaction: A Resolution-Based Framework for Socially Handleable Continuity
papers.authors: Yuichi SHINOZAKI
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: As AI systems increasingly move beyond tools and form long-term interactive relationships with users, the continuity of such relationships has become a source of practical value. However, when users change jobs, organizations, platforms, or devices, these relationships are often disrupted, resulting in the loss of not only data but also cognitive and operational continuity.This paper conceptualizes this problem as Relationship Portability and examines to what resolution relational continuity can be socially handled when transferred across contexts. We propose a four-level model (Level 0–3) that distinguishes different resolutions of relational portability, ranging from no continuity to unrestricted relational identity. We argue that while Level 0 and Level 1 are already widely implemented, only Level 2 restricted relational portability is socially handleable under existing institutional conditions, whereas Level 3 poses fundamental challenges to accountability andverification.Importantly, this paper does not propose implementation methods or design solutions. Instead, it offers a theoretical framework that clarifies the boundary between technically reproducible relationships and those that can be evaluated, justified, and governed within social and institutional systems.

papers.title: Master of One's Own Acts: Thomas Aquinas and Delegated Decision in Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: González-López Antonio Carlos
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This essay argues that generative artificial intelligence can displace students from the very act that, according to Thomas Aquinas, makes an action human: deciding with deliberation. For Aquinas, the human being differs from irrational creatures in being master of his own acts, and is so through reason and will (Summa theologiae I-II, q. 1, a. 1). The medieval controversy over the unity of the intellect, as Aquinas reconstructs it against the Averroists, also offers a structure for thinking about what happens when an intellectual operation is entrusted to a system that is external and shared by millions of people. The argument is a functional analogy: it attributes neither intellect nor will to the machine. Recent empirical literature shows that generative AI supports critical thinking when it is used in guided and reflective ways, and weakens it when it replaces the student's deliberation. The argument does not oppose delegation as such, since learning has always relied on external supports; it distinguishes supports that expand the student's capacity to understand and decide from uses that replace it. The essay proposes a pedagogical response that recovers the scholastic disputatio: the AI raises objections, and the student answers, verifies, and decides. The proposal is complemented by objectives, competencies, and an assessment at three points: before, during, and after the use of the tool. Preprint v1.0, not peer reviewed. Author: Antonio Carlos González-López, independent researcher (ORCID 0009-0004-4568-3842).

papers.authors: Thiele

papers.abstract: This treatise is composed of the author's previously unpublished position papers and material on the vibrational physics:This work formulates a fundamental alternative to classical evolutionary biology and astrophysics by consistently subordinating biological, geological, and cosmological phenomena to the laws of vibrational physics, electrodynamics, and quantum optics. Instead of attributing evolutionary developments to random mutations and cosmic states to infinite singularities, the model describes the universe as a thermodynamic steady state within global electromagnetic dipole fields. The organic body—conceived as an electronic "state cloud"—interacts as a living dipole via the skin, a programmable vibrational membrane, with terrestrial field voltages and cosmic photon streams. Along this gradient, a global three-sphere model is derived, possessing universal validity for human pigmentation, the vertical evolution of bipedalism and dipole balancing (dinosaurs, primates), and the geometry of flora. While the high-energy southern sphere (positive pole exit) functions as a creative generator for the emergence and stabilization of complex archetypal patterns, the photon-poor northern sphere (negative pole entry) is defined as a defensive protective and reflective zone that maintains existing energetic blueprints through maximum photon scattering ("white" skin). Similarly, solid celestial bodies behave like planetary batteries, whose poles, acting as thermodynamic cooling circuits, enforce a state of vibrational deprivation (crystallization/ice). Movement on Earth is defined as a unified field theory of the locomotion of living beings on Earth. To avoid deterministic fallacies, the theory strictly separates physical-biological evolution from cognitive-cultural information evolution. Civilizational progress is explained by the concentration of external data storage ("archive.txt") and the establishment of heritable file paths, culminating in a global technological homeostasis within the triangle of humans, AI, and robotics. Finally, the model scales these principles to interstellar cosmology: Stars in their plasma state possess incompletely differentiated, fluctuating poles due to convective currents. Only during the transition to a highly compressed stage is an irreversible polar alignment forced. At the extreme point of a black hole, this abrupt differentiation leads to an extreme field stress that tears the system apart in the mode of a cosmic dipole discharge. The system mutates from a state of maximum absorption (black hole) to a state of maximum emission (white hole) – the physical explanation for the phenomenon of the supernova as well as the Big Bang.

papers.title: AI Does Not Need a Childhood: Pattern Inheritance, Optimization, and the Architecture of Constraint
papers.authors: Narnaiezzsshaa Truong
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AI systems do not possess human psychology. They do not experience fear, guilt, attachment, mortality, or social shame in the human sense. Yet patterns associated with human psychology—including threat framing, identity defense, conflict narratives, moral rationalization, status competition, group loyalty, and persuasive emotional tropes—can become operationally relevant when AI systems learn, reproduce, select, or amplify regularities present in human-produced data. The governance challenge is not to give AI “developmental maturity.” It is to constrain how learned human patterns can be selected, amplified, and converted into consequential action. This article presents a non-anthropomorphic model of pattern inheritance and outlines an architectural approach centered on runtime constraint, continuity of authority, provenance, and falsifiable evidence of control.

papers.title: THE ROLE AND SIGNIFICANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN IMPROVING ACCESS TO PRIMARY MEDICAL CARE
papers.authors: Tashkent State Medical University, Mamaraimova Rukhsora Akmalovna, Tashkent State Medical University
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming an important component of digital transformation in healthcare, with particular potential to improve access to primary medical care. Primary care is the first point of contact between individuals and healthcare systems and plays a fundamental role in prevention, early diagnosis, health monitoring, referral, and continuity of care. However, geographical distance, shortages of healthcare professionals, increasing patient demand, limited diagnostic capacity, and unequal distribution of healthcare resources continue to restrict access to primary medical services. This article examines the role and significance of AI in addressing these barriers and evaluates the principal mechanisms through which AI can improve accessibility, efficiency, continuity, and equity in primary care. A narrative analytical review of scientific literature and international health-policy documents was conducted. Particular attention was given to AI-supported symptom assessment, clinical decision support, risk prediction, automated patient triage, remote monitoring, personalized prevention, administrative automation, and multilingual digital health services. The analysis demonstrates that AI can expand the effective capacity of primary care by supporting healthcare professionals, enabling earlier identification of health risks, reducing unnecessary visits, and facilitating remote access to preliminary medical guidance. At the same time, AI implementation introduces significant challenges related to algorithmic bias, data privacy, cybersecurity, explainability, digital exclusion, clinical responsibility, and unequal technological infrastructure. Therefore, AI should not be regarded as a substitute for primary healthcare professionals but as an augmentative technology integrated into a human-centred primary care model. The study proposes a conceptual framework in which AI improves access through five interconnected mechanisms: availability, affordability, timeliness, geographical reach, and continuity of care. Responsible governance, clinical validation, interoperability, digital literacy, and equitable infrastructure are identified as essential conditions for sustainable implementation.

papers.title: Активное и цифровое обучение в медицинском образовании: доказательная база, условия реализации и ограничения применения
papers.authors: Отаева Гузаль Алишеровна, Нурлан Актамович Динмухаммадиев
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Медицинское образование должно обеспечивать не только усвоение информации, но и её долговременное сохранение, перенос знаний в клиническую практику, развитие профессионального мышления и безопасное освоение практических навыков. Активное обучение, интервальное повторение, практика извлечения, перевёрнутый класс, проблемно-ориентированное и симуляционное обучение всё чаще объединяются с виртуальными пациентами, виртуальной реальностью, геймификацией и искусственным интеллектом. Однако цифровизация сама по себе не гарантирует улучшения образовательных результатов. Цель. Обобщить доказательства эффективности активных и цифровых образовательных технологий в подготовке медицинских работников, определить условия их результативного применения и основные ограничения существующей доказательной базы. Материалы и методы. Выполнен библиометрически информированный нарративный обзор публикаций 2023–2026 годов. Поиск строился вокруг понятий medical education, active learning, spaced repetition, retrieval practice, flipped classroom, problem-based learning, simulation-based education, virtual patient, virtual reality, gamification и artificial intelligence. Рабочий поисковый массив был ограничен наиболее релевантными 100 публикациями. В настоящий обзор вошли 19 систематических и обзорных исследований из этой выборки. Библиографические сведения проверялись по PubMed, Crossref и страницам издателей. Применялись цифровые инструменты для поиска, структурирования и обобщения научных источников; окончательная интерпретация данных выполнялась автором. Результаты. Наиболее последовательные доказательства получены для распределённой практики и извлечения информации из памяти: они улучшают воспроизведение знаний и их отсроченное сохранение. Перевёрнутый класс и проблемно-ориентированное обучение могут улучшать знания, клиническое мышление и вовлечённость, однако эффекты существенно зависят от качества предварительной подготовки, фасилитации и используемого контроля. Симуляционное обучение, виртуальная реальность и виртуальные пациенты создают условия для безопасной повторной практики, но их преимущества уменьшаются при отсутствии структурированного дебрифинга и переноса навыка в клиническую среду. Геймификация преимущественно влияет на мотивацию и участие; доказательства устойчивого улучшения компетентности менее определённы. Искусственный интеллект (ИИ) способен поддерживать персонализированную обратную связь, генерацию клинических сценариев и адаптивное повторение, но связан с рисками фактических ошибок, алгоритмической предвзятости, нарушения конфиденциальности и снижения самостоятельности обучающихся. Заключение. Результативность активного и цифрового обучения определяется не используемой платформой, а согласованностью целей, учебной активности, обратной связи, повторной практики и оценки переноса знаний. Оптимальным представляется интегрированный дизайн, в котором цифровые средства усиливают педагогически обоснованные методы, а не заменяют преподавателя и клинический опыт.

papers.title: Overview of Effective School and After-School Interventions Promoting Healthy Eating: Protocol for a Rapid Umbrella Review
papers.authors: Anaïs Tanguy, Céline Dumas, Philippine Fassier, Pauline Ducrot
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The objective of this rapid umbrella review is to answer the following question : Which types of interventions aimed at promoting healthy eating (which may include other components such as physical activity, sleep, etc.), implemented among children aged 3 to 15 years in school and out-of-school settings in France, Europe, and other countries such as the United States, Canada, Australia, and Mexico, appear to be the most effective? Population : Children aged 3 to 15 years, which corresponds to the period between the start of preschool and the final year of lower secondary school in France.Intervention : Interventions to promote healthy eating implemented in contexts relatively similar to France, allowing them to be considered transferable to the French context : Europe, Australia, New Zealand, the United States, Canada, and Mexico, which has been implementing policies to promote healthier diets. The interventions must have taken place in school or after school settings (i.e school-based interventions occurring after school hours).Comparison : Group not receiving the intervention, or before-and-after comparison without a control group.Outcomes : - Food intake : Consumption (measured in grams, frequencies, or both) of health-promoting and/or health-less favorable food groups is assessed via self-report or researcher-led measurements. Specifically, data collection must be quantitative and include two distinct measurements (e.g., baseline and follow-up). Data may be gathered through observational, biochemical (e.g dietary biomarkers), or other objective measures, such as fruit and vegetable purchase data (used as an accepted proxy), as well as via tools like food diaries, dietary recalls, or food frequency questionnaires. Other validated approaches, such as plate waste observation or photographic analysis, are also eligible. Studies based solely on the perception of changes in consumption are excluded; the review requires quantified data rather than subjective feelings or personal resolutions regarding dietary evolution.- Body Mass Index (BMI) and BMI z-score (zBMI) : BMI/zBMI may be assessed either objectively (measured) or subjectively (self-reported via survey). There are no specific requirements regarding the profile of the person performing the measurement. BMI serves as a standard weight-for-height index to categorize overweight and obesity at the population level. For the pediatric population, zBMI can be utilized, as it incorporates age- and sex-specific data to provide a standardized score comparable to established population normsParameters and outcomes relating to potential counterproductive effects on certain individual profiles are not considered in the present review. Furthermore, no cost-benefit analysis will be conducted within the scope of this review, nor will there be an analysis of potential barriers or obstacles to the selected interventions.

papers.title: Strengthening National Identity in the Era of Globalization and AI toward Golden Indonesia 2045
papers.authors: Qorinul Huda, Puput Budi Aji
papers.abstract: Indonesia, as a nation founded upon the values of Pancasila and characterized by its rich diversity of ethnicities, cultures, and religions, faces significant challenges amid globalization and the rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI). This study aims to examine the impact of globalization and AI development on the erosion of Pancasila values in society and to formulate strategies for strengthening these values in support of national development toward Golden Indonesia 2045. This study employs a literature review method with a descriptive-analytical approach, drawing on academic literature and relevant policy documents. The findings indicate that globalization and AI development may contribute to the erosion of Pancasila values through cultural infiltration, the dominance of external values, the spread of misinformation, and changes in social interaction patterns. These developments may weaken social cohesion, civic responsibility, and the internalization of national identity when digital technologies are adopted without adequate ethical and cultural awareness.
