Methods This benchmarking study, based on simulations and cross-sectional analysis, evaluated the performance of four publicly accessible AI chatbots—ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Perplexity—in formulating TPN plans for critically ill adults. Copilot declined to generate patient-specific TPN plans; this refusal was retained as a performance outcome, while Copilot was excluded from analyses requiring an analyzable TPN prescription. Each chatbot produced one plan for each of 10 standardized clinical cases, resulting in a total of 30 TPN plans. Friedman tests, Kendall’s W , and Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used for comparative analyses. Results ChatGPT produced comprehensive plans for all 10 cases, compared to 6 plans from Gemini and 4 from Perplexity. The median accuracy was 57.7% for ChatGPT, 43.9% for Gemini, and 38.5% for Perplexity, with no statistically significant overall difference ( p = 0.124). However, ChatGPT performed better than Perplexity in pairwise comparison (adjusted p = 0.035). There was a significant difference in completeness among the chatbots ( p = 0.003; Kendall’s W = 0.57), with median scores of 64.6, 41.9, and 32.3%, respectively. All 30 plans had at least one major or critical safety issue, 7 (23.3%) contained a critical concern, and 19 (63.3%) were rejected. The most common errors were related to electrolytes (90.0%), micronutrients (70.0%), and monitoring (66.7%). Recommendations from chatbots often exceeded pharmacist-derived values, with median relative differences of +47% for energy, +120% for lipids, and +100% for potassium. Bland–Altman analysis revealed considerable variability in the agreement. Conclusion ChatGPT produced the most comprehensive TPN plans among chatbots. However, none showed enough accuracy, safety, or concordance for independent use. All plans had critical issues, especially with electrolytes, micronutrients, monitoring, and refeeding precautions. AI chatbots can support education or planning but require review by a well-trained clinician before clinical use.

papers.title: MSANet: a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network for EEG-based driver fatigue recognition
papers.authors: Peipei Gu, Ruibo Wang, Ming Zhang, Naian Xiao, Fangqin Liu, Bin Jiang, Jiayang Guo, Xiaosong Peng
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based driver fatigue recognition remains challenging because fatigue-related patterns are distributed across multiple temporal scales, inter-channel relationships vary across samples, and inter-individual differences complicate cross-subject transfer. To address these issues, a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network (MSANet) is proposed for EEG-based driver fatigue recognition. The framework introduces a multi-granularity patch temporal gate (MGPTG) to model locally continuous temporal contexts, stable graph node enhancement (SGNE) to enhance channel-node features before dynamic graph construction, and an adaptive classifier gate (ACG) to combine cosine-based and affine decision geometries. MSANet was evaluated on two public simulated-driving EEG datasets using a cross-subject transfer protocol, in which the target-subject samples were stratified with a partition ratio of 0.5 into a labeled adaptation subset and a held-out test subset. MSANet achieved an accuracy (ACC) of 83.64% and an F1-score (F1) of 83.74% on Dataset I, and 74.64% ACC and 72.92% F1 on Dataset II. The results indicate strong numerical performance on Dataset I and competitive performance on Dataset II. Subject-level statistical analysis was additionally conducted to distinguish mean performance differences from differences that are consistently supported across subjects. Ablation results showed lower mean performance after removing MGPTG, SGNE, or ACG under the evaluated settings. These findings support further evaluation of the proposed stage-specific temporal, graph-node, and classification mechanisms for cross-subject transfer in EEG-based driver fatigue recognition.

papers.title: Subject-independent classification of ADHD from pediatric EEG: a leakage-aware deep learning framework with interpretable neurophysiological mapping
papers.authors: M. Geethapriya, Kalyanaraman Pattabiraman
papers.abstract: Background The use of electroencephalography (EEG) in automated screening of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) has created a large body of literature that suggests promising outcomes, with reported classification accuracies often above 90%. A major methodological issue suggests that a substantial part of these results are actually due to data leakage, whereby EEG epochs pertaining to the same subject end up in both training and testing sets, allowing classifiers to capitalize on features specific to the individual rather than on genuine disorder-related biomarkers. Methods We assessed the performance of three classical machine learning algorithms, namely, Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), as well as three deep learning models: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and CNN-BiLSTM, on a standard pediatric EEG dataset containing 121 children and 4,173 epochs. The performance of each model was compared in terms of both segment-wise cross-validation (Protocol A) and subject-wise cross-validation (without any data leakage, Protocol B).To evaluate neurotopographic plausibility without making unsupported causal assertions, we applied Deep SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to the best-generalizing architecture. Results The performance discrepancy was substantial. Under segment-wise evaluation, the SVM operating on power spectral density (PSD) features reached 90.0% accuracy (95% CI: [89.1%, 90.9%], AUC = 0.96). However, the same model dropped to 65.6% (95% CI: [62.1%, 69.1%], AUC = 0.72) under subject-wise evaluation—a statistically significant 24.4 percentage point collapse ( p < 0.001, Wilcoxon signed-rank). In contrast, deep architectures learning directly from raw EEG were resilient: the stand-alone CNN lost only 2.5 percentage points, achieving 72.7% accuracy (95% CI: [66.0%, 79.4%], AUC = 0.72, recall = 88.0%) on completely unseen participants. Post-hoc SHAP attribution identified the highest relative contributions in frontal (F3, Fz, F4) and central (Cz) electrodes, aligning with established ADHD neurophysiology. Conclusion Hand-engineered spectral features are highly vulnerable to identity leakage, whereas end-to-end convolutional models generalize across subjects with realistic, uninflated performance. Strict subject-wise validation is strongly recommended as standard practice for translational EEG research.

papers.title: Behavioural expression of ictal embarrassment: a stereo-EEG case report
papers.authors: Anna Scarabello, Veronica Pelliccia, Francesca Bisulli, M. Revay, Francesca Gozzo, A. Mingarelli, Chiara Peretto, R. Mai, C. Pizzanelli, F. Pizzo, Fabrice Bartoloméi, L. Tassi
papers.abstract: Embarrassment is a rare ictal manifestation whose neurophysiological basis remains poorly understood. We describe the case of a 40-year-old woman with drug-resistant focal epilepsy characterized by an unusual ictal semiology combining an intense positive emotional experience with behavioral manifestations of embarrassment. Stereo-EEG demonstrated seizure onset within the middle frontal gyrus bank of the superior frontal sulcus (F2sb), with rapid propagation to the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) and superior anterior insula (sAI). Electrical stimulation of the F2sb reliably reproduced the habitual electroclinical seizure. While identical stimulation parameters elicited the subjective and autonomic manifestations in both supine and upright postures, the complete behavioral repertoire of embarrassment emerged only when stimulation was delivered in the standing position. Exploratory functional connectivity analyses revealed that overt embarrassment was associated with reduced node strength within a network encompassing the dACC, sAI, mesial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC). More restricted network changes were associated with only mild sensations, whereas asymptomatic stimulation produced a distinct and partly reversed connectivity pattern. This case suggests that the behavioral expression of ictal embarrassment arises from the transient reconfiguration of a frontal-cingulo-insular network and is critically shaped by bodily context.

papers.title: An attention-enhanced hybrid CNN-BiLSTM framework for multiclass epileptic seizure recognition using EEG signals
papers.authors: Bobbinpreet Kaur, Sheenam Middha, Aleem Ali, Noman Khan, Reham Awadh Alhejaili, Ahmed H. Almutairi
papers.abstract: Introduction: Electroencephalogram (EEG) signal classification plays a pivotal role in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and the diagnosis of neurological disorders. However, the non-stationary, non-linear, and low signal-to-noise ratio characteristics of EEG signals make accurate feature extraction challenging. Conventional deep learning approaches often struggle to simultaneously capture localized transient patterns, deep temporal dependencies, and long-range contextual relationships within EEG signals. Methods: To address these challenges, an optimized end-to-end hybrid deep learning framework, termed CNN-BiLSTM-MHSA, is proposed for multiclass epileptic seizure recognition. The architecture sequentially integrates a multilayer one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for localized feature extraction, a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network for capturing forward and backward temporal dependencies, and a Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) mechanism for dynamically emphasizing discriminative neurological events. Robust preprocessing includes Butterworth bandpass filtering, Z-score normalization, and data augmentation using Gaussian noise injection and amplitude scaling. The framework was evaluated on the UCI/Kaggle Epileptic Seizure Recognition dataset comprising 11,500 EEG segments distributed across five classes. Results: The proposed framework achieved an overall accuracy of 98.83%, precision of 98.95%, recall (sensitivity) of 98.84%, F1-score of 98.90%, specificity of 99.71%, balanced accuracy of 98.84%, ROC-AUC of 99.80%, and PR-AUC of 99.72%. Class-wise accuracies exceeded 99% for most categories, with one seizure class achieving perfect recognition. Comparative evaluation further demonstrated that the proposed framework outperformed several recent state-of-the-art EEG seizure classification methods. Discussion: The superior performance can be attributed to the complementary representation capabilities of the hybrid architecture. CNN layers effectively learn localized signal patterns, BiLSTM captures bidirectional temporal dependencies, and MHSA enhances the representation of long-range contextual relationships by assigning greater importance to informative temporal regions. The combination of robust preprocessing and data augmentation further contributes to improved generalization and classification reliability.

papers.title: N-back electroencephalography asymmetry and peripheral immune cell subpopulation composition
papers.authors: Matisse Ducharme, George Nader, Vincenzo De Luca
papers.abstract: Introduction: Cognitive deficits such as working memory impairment and peripheral inflammation frequently occur together in neuropsychiatric conditions, yet the relationship between them remains poorly understood. To address this gap, the present study examines these associations in healthy young adults to establish baseline relationships between peripheral immune cell subpopulations and neural activity without clinical confounds. The aim of this study is to investigate whether the relative proportions of peripheral immune cell subpopulations are associated with EEG asymmetry during a working memory task and with task performance. Methods: EEG data were recorded from 24 healthy participants during a 2-back working memory task. Relative EEG asymmetry indices were computed for four frequency bands: alpha, beta, delta, and theta. 2-back task performance was also calculated. Peripheral blood was collected for DNA extraction and genome-wide DNA methylation analysis to estimate the relative proportions of immune cell subpopulations. Estimated proportions were Center Log-Ratio-transformed. Spearman's correlation and multiple linear regression were used to identify associations between EEG asymmetry, relative immune markers, and n-back task performance. Results & Discussion: Our analysis revealed that theta asymmetry was associated with CLR-transformed proportions of natural killer cells (p=0.035) and CD4+ T cells (p = 0.027). 2-back task target accuracy was nearly correlated with granulocytes (p = 0.082) and CD8+ T cell proportions (p=0.016); however, these associations did not remain significant after Bonferroni correction. Despite this, both immune markers significantly predicted 2-back target accuracy across three multiple linear regression models (model 1: p = 0.005, model 2: p = 0.002, model 3: p = 0.002).

papers.title: Educator and AI agent communication in AI-mediated higher education classrooms: a mini review along the complementarity-substitution axis
papers.authors: Sergey V. Kondrashev, Artemiy А. Rozhnov, T.B. Belova, Elmira Robertovna Khairullina, Svetlana Nikitina, Батракова Ирина Александровна
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education classrooms has reignited the debate over the role of communication between educators and students. This mini-review synthesizes the role of instructional communication constructs (immediacy, rapport, clarity, and credibility) and the relational functions they deliver in AI-mediated classrooms, based on 32 peer-reviewed studies published after 2023, identified through a large-scale literature search (using Scopus and Web of Science-based indexes, OpenAlex, and ERIC). The findings fall into three main categories. First, educator communication behaviors continue to predict student outcomes; a recent meta-analysis reports a moderate-to-large association (r = 0.443), although the evidence base is concentrated in Chinese and EFL samples. Second, students evaluate AI agents using human communication categories, but a systematic gap emerges in the dimension of goodwill, which is partially bridged by cues of immediacy and politeness. Third, when AI replaces human interaction, negative outcomes related to loneliness and a sense of belonging are observed. These three strands are integrated around the complementarity-substitution axis defined at the level of relational functions; tests of measurement invariance, sample diversity, and longitudinal designs are recommended for future research.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence as a constructivist scaffold in anaesthesia education: a mini review
papers.authors: Xuli Ren, Huiqiao Lian, Zhonghang Xu, Fang Wang
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), including generative AI and large language models, is increasingly used in health professions education, but evidence for educational benefit in anaesthesia remains limited and heterogeneous. This focused Mini Review incorporates literature identified through August 2026 and distinguishes anaesthesia-specific empirical evidence from feasibility studies, extrapolation from broader health professions education, and proposed applications. Using constructivist learning theory, we conceptualise AI not as an autonomous teacher or objective assessor, but as a contingent and temporary scaffold that should be adapted to learner performance, progressively faded, and followed by assessment of independent transfer. We further integrate cognitive apprenticeship through modelling, coaching, articulation, reflection, and exploration while maintaining the essential role of human supervisors. Available anaesthesia-specific studies involving AI-assisted regional anaesthesia training, ultrasound interpretation, virtual patient encounters, and simulation analysis demonstrate feasibility or task-specific benefits but do not yet establish improvements in clinical reasoning, debriefing, competence, or entrustment. Building on recent reviews of AI in anaesthesiology education, this review operationalises contingency, fading, transfer, cognitive apprenticeship, and assessment safeguards for anaesthesia training. AI-generated feedback, portfolio summaries, and scores should be regarded as fallible decision-support and should not independently determine summative assessment, progression, remediation, or entrustment. Future research should evaluate whether AI provides added value beyond established simulation and human-led supervision, focusing on reasoning, retention, transfer, safe escalation, and equity.

papers.title: Neural dynamics of emotionally expressive piano performance: a single-case study
papers.authors: Alice Mado Proverbio, Giulia Carta
papers.abstract: Introduction: Understanding how expert performers translate expressive intent into sound remains a central question in the neuroscience of music. We recorded continuous 128-channel EEG from a professional, internationally active concert pianist during a concert-like, uninterrupted performance (~27 min) of six works by Bach, Beethoven, and Chopin. Methods: From the continuous recording, 99 two-second clean EEG segments were extracted and assigned to one of six previously validated performance-emotion categories based on independent listener evaluations (Joy, Peacefulness, Melancholy, Argumentative, Tension, Power). Each 2-s fragment contained 1,024 time points per channel, yielding 131,072 EEG data points. Cortical and subcortical source generators were reconstructed with standardized weighted Low-Resolution Electromagnetic Tomography (swLORETA), and activation was quantified both as frequency of occurrence and as dipole magnitude across three macro-regions (anterior, posterior, subcortical). Results: A chi-square test on activation frequencies showed a significant association between cortical/subcortical region and emotional category. Repeated-measures ANOVAs revealed significant region- and emotion-dependent differences in dipole magnitude. Across virtually every emotional category, the left basal ganglia, left thalamus, and left precentral gyrus (BA4) emerged as the most consistently recruited generators, indicating a stable left-lateralized fronto-striato-thalamic axis subserving fine motor control within this performance. Superimposed on this stable motor substrate, emotion-specific modulations emerged: Joy was associated with the highest subcortical activation magnitude, while Melancholy showed the lowest subcortical magnitude together with a selective recruitment of right-hemisphere generators (right BA10, right somatosensory cortex, right insula), consistent with valence-based hemispheric asymmetry accounts. Pearson correlations further linked activation of the left basal ganglia, left thalamus, and left premotor cortex (BA6) to objective performance parameters (gestures per second, notes per phrase, acoustic intensity), suggesting that neurofunctional engagement scales with the motor complexity of the material performed. Discussion: These findings provide a performer-side perspective complementary to models of music-evoked emotion largely derived from listeners, and suggest that, in this elite performer, expressive intent was instantiated in a specialized, left-dominant sensorimotor-limbic network modulated by affective valence. The study is complemented by animated audiovisual materials that dynamically trace the moment-to-moment evolution of LORETA source activity in synchrony with the unfolding musical passage.

papers.title: From Flipped Classroom to AI-Enhanced Assessment
papers.authors: Ka Ho Law
papers.journal: Proceedings of The World Conference on Research in Teaching and Education
papers.abstract: In response to the challenges posed by generative artificial intelligence and increasingly diverse student populations, this paper examines a decade-long programme of pedagogical innovation in undergraduate mathematics education. At a research-intensive university in Hong Kong, a coherent set of evidence-informed practices has been developed and scaled across courses of different sizes and natures. These include a fully flipped classroom model supported by animated lecture videos and an exercise generator, a deliberate shift towards open-book and oral assessments, and the adoption of an AI-assisted grading platform to provide timely and individualised feedback. Drawing on multi-year institutional student surveys, mid-term feedback and peer observations, the evaluation reveals consistently positive outcomes, as reflected in teacher and course effectiveness scores, while students also reported enhanced conceptual understanding, greater engagement, improved inclusivity and stronger communication skills. The integration of AI-assisted grading significantly improved the timeliness and quality of feedback, particularly in large-enrolment classes. Supported by competitive teaching development grants and recognised through institutional teaching awards, this sustained body of work contributes to the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning by demonstrating how practitioner-led innovation can be systematically developed, rigorously evaluated, and progressively institutionalised. Rather than offering a prescriptive model, the paper provides an adaptable example for STEM educators seeking to strengthen student learning and assessment practices in an era of rapid technological change.

papers.title: АВТОРСТВО ЗА УЧАСТІ ГЕНЕРАТИВНОГО ШІ: ВІД ПРЕЦЕДЕНТІВ ДО СТАНДАРТУ ПРОЗОРОГО ВИКОРИСТАННЯ
papers.authors: Тамара ЯРОШЕВСЬКА, K. O. Matukhno
papers.abstract: У статті розглянуто проблему авторства за участі generative AI в академічному письмі, дослідженнях та інже- нерному проєктуванні. Актуальність теми зумовлена поляризацією сучасних інституційних підходів: від забо- рони використання генеративних систем до моделей, які допускають їх застосування за умови належного роз- криття, перевірки та людського контролю. Обґрунтовано, що ключовим для визначення авторства є не сам факт використання ШІ, а збереження авторства за людиною крізь призму трьох взаємопов’язаних елементів: creative control (творчого контролю), verification (верифікації) та responsibility (відповідальності). На основі аналізу правових прецедентів і регуляторних орієнтирів, зокрема підходів Бюро авторського пра- ва США, справ Thaler / DABUS та Zarya of the Dawn, показано, що сучасна правова практика не визнає само- стійного машинного авторства, але водночас не зводиться до тотальної заборони використання ШІ. Окрему увагу приділено інженерному кейсу LEAP 71, який демонструє трансформацію людського внеску в умовах AI-assisted design: від створення одиничного результату до формування логіки проєктування, встановлення обмежень, пере- вірки та відповідальності за практичне застосування продукту. Проаналізовано сучасні підходи до AI disclosure та AI governance, зокрема Resnik, AID Framework, DAISY та AI-RO. Показано, що ці підходи зміщують акцент із заборони інструменту на прозорість використання. Окремо розглянуто обмеження AI-based detectors. Зроблено висновок, що перспективним є стандарт прозорого викори- стання генеративного ШІ, який поєднує розкриття використання, верифікацію, людський контроль і прийняття відповідальності.

papers.title: The Role of Expert Opinions and Peer Review in Engineering Next-Generation AI-Enabled Systems
papers.authors: Carlos Henrique C. Duarte
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a key enabling technology for business organisations, increasingly embedded in production systems and decision-making workflows. AI models and tools in these settings must satisfy diverse requirements, such as accuracy, traceability, explainability, fairness, and trust, while meeting compliance obligations, service-level agreements, and governance frameworks. However, the non-deterministic and evolving features of modern AI models challenges traditional validation approaches based primarily on quantitative metrics. This paper studies how techniques from empirical software engineering, particularly expert opinions and peer review, can support AI-enabled systems engineering. The paper presents an experience report grounded in a literature review and an experiment. The experiment is based on a precisely specified, complex problem that analyses the responses of contemporary AI models when prompted with the given problem. It analyses how expert judgment and peer review can improve the plausibility and correctness of model outputs. This study proposes a lifecycle model that treats problem and ground-truth specifications, expert judgments, and review rationales as first-class artefacts. The paper concludes by discussing challenges, limitations, and opportunities for incorporating these techniques into AI engineering, particularly for next-generation models and tools.

papers.title: Aeye: Real-time age, gender and emotion detection in browser
papers.authors: Mihael Holi, Sven Maričić, Irena Jurjevic, Adriana Prunk Drmić, Antonija Ružić Baršić
papers.abstract: This paper presents Aeye, a lightweight, browser-based application capable of real-time detection of human age, gender and emotional state using artificial intelligence. Unlike many existing AI systems, Aeye performs all computation on the client side, preserving user privacy and enabling full offline functionality. The application utilizes face-api.js and Tiny Face Detector models, achieving fast and efficient performance even on low-resource devices. Its modular design supports dynamic interface controls and responsive operation across platforms. The scientific contribution lies in the integration of asynchronous model loading, real-time GPU-accelerated inference using TensorFlow.js, and deployment as a progressive web app (PWA). These innovations make Aeye suitable for educational, experimental, and field use cases where connectivity and infrastructure are limited. The paper outlines the system architecture, implementation, and evaluation results, and discusses potential extensions such as multi-face detection and integration with emotion-driven user interfaces.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Employee Well-Being in Hybrid Work Environments
papers.authors: T.G. Ashwini, P. Radha
papers.journal: New Perspective Journal of Business and Economics
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized the HR landscape and workplace processes, especially in hybrid settings, with its swift integration. This research explores how the use of AI impacts employee well-being, taking into account both the positive and negative elements of technology-driven work. The study identifies in particular the usefulness of AI tools in improving the efficiency and effectiveness of work, their role in decision-making, their flexibility, and their impact on employees' experience, while also raising issues concerning technostress, job insecurity, work intensification, and a decrease in interpersonal interaction. A quantitative research approach is suggested and the data from employees under hybrid arrangements would be collected by using a structured questionnaire. The study also investigates how perceived organizational support is a mediator between AI adoption and employee well-being and how digital competence is a moderator between the two. The results are likely to be useful for institutions that want to use AI in a responsible way while ensuring the psychological, social and professional health of their employees. The study presents practical implications for developing human-centred AI and practices of sustainable hybrid working and adds to the growing body of research on AI-integrated workplaces.
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

papers.title: Reimagining Nepal’s Academic System: From Degree-Centered Education to a Learning, Innovation, and Impact Ecosystem
papers.authors: Ashok  Kumar Mishra
papers.journal: New Perspective Journal of Business and Economics
papers.abstract: Nepal’s higher-education reform should be assessed by the capabilities, integrity, and public value that institutions develop, rather than by credentials alone. This conceptual policy editorial synthesizes research and authoritative policy documents on active learning, micro-credentials, open educational resources, responsible artificial intelligence, and Nepal’s higher-education initiatives. It proposes an integrated ecosystem connecting curriculum, assessment, student support, applied research, industry and community partnerships, alumni engagement, and lifelong learning. Degrees remain valuable qualifications, but they are insufficient evidence of competence without credible demonstrations of learning. A phased implementation strategy prioritizes faculty development, equitable infrastructure, curriculum alignment, supervised experiential learning, and independent evaluation before expansion. Proposed indicators emphasize demonstrated competence, access, research use, student well-being, and graduate pathways rather than technology purchases or publication counts. International findings require contextual testing in Nepal. Academic leaders should adopt accountable pilots that preserve scholarly depth, protect academic freedom, strengthen institutional learning, and promote responsible, inclusive social contribution sustainably.

papers.title: “Safe for now?” Boundary work and tensions of AI Adoption in Sign Language Interpreting and Speech-to-Text Reporting in Belgium and the Netherlands
papers.authors: Maartje De Meulder, Karolien Gebruers, Deborah Giustini
papers.abstract: AbstractThis article examines how sign language interpreters (SLIs) and speech-to-text reporters (STTRs) in Belgium (Flanders) and the Netherlands understand and navigate artificial intelligence (AI)-driven language technologies in their professional lives. While speech-to-text reporting already faces displacement by automated transcription, sign language interpreting remains partly sheltered by the limited AI training data for Flemish and Dutch Sign Language. Drawing on an online survey (N = 134) conducted in 2025, and theorized through boundary work, we identify three tensions structuring practitioners' accounts: a temporality tension, in which anticipated disruption coexists with present stability; an access tension, in which AI expands available options while enabling institutions to narrow the definition of "sufficient access"; and a professional identity tension, in which the technology threatening practitioners' livelihoods may simultaneously advance the profession's own emancipatory ideal. Respondents describe AI as a new third actor in interpreted interaction, shifting some practitioners toward editing and quality-control roles that lack institutional recognition. We argue that AI in language access is actively produced through practitioners’ ongoing boundary work and calls for recognizing them — alongside deaf consumers — as epistemic actors in governing just technological transitions.

papers.title: A Productivity Fixated World in the Age of AI: Investigating The Purpose of Human Art
papers.authors: Bruce Tan
papers.abstract: Modern society increasingly prioritizes final products over the creative process, a trend exacerbated by the rapid adoption of generative AI. This study aims to explore the impact of AI integration into the creative process on subjective well-being and fulfillment, and to determine whether these effects differ between individuals creating for leisure versus those creating for a profession. Within this research, a quantitative-focused survey was conducted with 200 adults, categorized using a 2x2 design: acting as either a hobbyist or a professional illustrator, and either utilizing or not utilizing AI. The data reveals a consistent drop in a person’s well-being across both hobbyist and professional groups when AI is utilized. The differences in fulfillment between hobbyist and professional groups were not statistically significant. While a positive correlation was found between a product-focused mindset and satisfaction among professionals using AI, the overall satisfaction for AI users across the board remained significantly lower than for those who didn’t use AI. These findings suggest that AI integration into creative tasks carries measurable psychological costs by separating the creator from the intrinsically beneficial creative process, along with social costs that taint the creator-audience relationship. These findings underscore the value of human creation, suggesting that the ongoing conversation surrounding AI adoption must extend beyond efficiency to account for value within the human process. An avenue for further research lies within AI use in other fields less traditionally considered a “creative” discipline, such as STEM, which show evidence of having similar psychological benefits arising from the process.

papers.title: Dissociable neural oscillations track subjective value under risk and ambiguity
papers.authors: Shuting Mei, Leyou Deng, Gökhan Aydogan, Christian Carl Ruff, Ya Zheng
papers.abstract: How the brain values uncertain prospects and translates them into choices is a central question in decision neuroscience. Current accounts propose that decisions under risk and ambiguity share a valuation process that integrates outcome with probability information, with ambiguity additionally requiring evaluation of the uncertainty about the probabilities themselves. Here we used computational modeling to estimate trial-wise subjective value and tested whether it was tracked by shared or distinct neural dynamics under risk and ambiguity. Participants accepted or rejected risky and ambiguous monetary gambles while we recorded neural activity using electroencephalography (Experiment 1) and magnetoencephalography (Experiment 2). Across both experiments, alpha-band (9–14 Hz) activity localized to the precuneus and superior parietal cortex tracked subjective value under both risk and ambiguity. By contrast, delta-band (1–3 Hz) activity localized to the ventromedial prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortices tracked subjective value only under ambiguity. These findings reveal dissociable neural signatures for the two forms of uncertainty and suggest that the brain resolves ambiguity by combining a shared valuation process indexed by alpha activity with an additional process indexed by delta activity that may reflect the motivational salience of options with ambiguous outcome probabilities.

papers.title: Cultural and Personality Predictors of Attitudes Toward AI Chatbots: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Michelle Ming Ertl, Katherine Sledge Moore
papers.abstract: As AI chatbots are becoming increasingly relevant in our daily life, understanding what shapespeople’s attitudes toward them is becoming more important. This systematic literature reviewbrings together the findings of 34 articles (from across multiple countries) to examine howpersonality traits and one’s cultural background predict attitudes towards AI chatbots. Thereview suggests that culture works as a primary filter that sets a person’s starting position whenthey encounter AI. Western users tend to approach chatbots with more skepticism and strongerprivacy concerns, while on the other hand East Asian users show higher comfort with social AIinteraction. Within each of these cultural settings, individual personality traits fine-tune theseresponses, but which trait matters most changes depending on the culture. Agreeablenessdrives trust in Western samples, while Conscientiousness drives trust in Arab ones. Technologyspecific variables like Personal Innovativeness in Information Technology (PIIT) and AIconfiguration anxiety turned out to be stronger predictors than broad personality traits overall.The review also identifies a persistent global gender gap in AI adaptation that operatesdifferently depending on cultural setting. Limitations include the overrepresentation of younguniversity educated participants in existing research, the Western bias present in both studysamples and AI training data, and the ongoing confusion between physical robot findings andtext-based chatbot research. The paper concludes that effective chatbot design and AI policyrequire culturally adapted approaches rather than one-size-fits-all solutions.

papers.title: The impact of professional development programs on K–12 teachers’ AI literacy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.authors: Ying Ma, Chloe S. Gordon, Tingting Li, Ziwen Teuber, Theresa Dicke, Taren Sanders, Michael Noetel, Rebecca J. Collie, Kewen Liao, Chengliang Wang, Jiesi Guo
papers.abstract: Teachers' artificial intelligence (AI) literacy is an increasingly important focus of professional development (PD). This systematic review synthesized evidence from 62 empirical studies (61 records), including 36 studies eligible for effect-size estimation, involving pre-service and in-service teachers. Most programs emphasized AI-related knowledge and skills, with less systematic attention to attitudinal and ethical dimensions. Common design features included temporal flexibility (e.g., synchronous and asynchronous learning), role diversification (e.g., co-designers and collaborators), and contextual orientation (e.g., task- and project-based learning). The primary combined-design multilevel meta-analysis after influence diagnostics, based on 212 effect sizes from 34 studies, indicated a significant positive average effect across knowledge, skills, and attitudes/values (g = 0.76, 95% CI [0.50, 1.02], p < .001). Substantial heterogeneity indicated considerable variation across programs and contexts. Although possible small-study effects and publication selection may have inflated the magnitude of the primary pooled estimate, Bayesian selection-model analyses continued to support a positive average effect. No statistically significant moderation was detected by career stage, school level, intervention-duration category, research design, outcome measurement type, or gender composition. These findings provide an important quantitative benchmark for the emerging evidence base and indicate that AI literacy PD can support multiple dimensions of teachers' AI literacy.

papers.title: Multi-party simulations with human participants and role-based LLM conversational agents: A design framework and validity evidence for organizational research
papers.authors: Yuki Nozaki, Naho Fujisawa, Yoshinobu Kano
papers.abstract: Dynamic organizational phenomena often unfold through ongoing communication among multiple interdependent actors, yet studying them involves trade-offs among realism, controllability, and scalability. We propose a methodological framework for using role-based conversational agents powered by large language models (LLMs) as multi-party interaction partners in organizational research. It specifies how to create standardized but contingent interaction environments through scenario design, persona prompts, interaction protocols, and iterative testing. In a preregistered illustrative study of leadership communication, we analyzed 394 employees’ text-based simulations powered by GPT-5.2, Gemini 2.5 Flash, or Claude Sonnet 4.6. Across models, participants perceived the agents as anthropomorphic and animate, and as acting consistently with their assigned backgrounds, personalities, and linguistic styles. Behavioral coding corroborated and extended these perceptions, with deviations from assigned persona prompts in 2.59% of utterances. Participants’ utterances also yielded codable indicators of theoretically relevant behavior, in this case leadership communication. These findings provide initial validity evidence that multi-party LLM-agent simulations can create plausible interaction environments, deliver persona-consistent stimuli, and elicit behaviorally analyzable responses. We also offer practical guidelines on model selection, replicability, and ethics.

papers.title: Generative AI in higher education: A scoping review and framework for student motivation and engagement
papers.authors: Edmund De Leon Evangelista, Salman Bukhari
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly influencing how students write, create, reflect, solve problems, and engage with learning in higher education. However, the evidence remains divided, particularly regarding motivation, engagement, creativity, perception, self-regulation, and psychologically informed learning design. This study presents a PRISMA-ScR-based scoping review of GenAI in higher education from a motivational and psychological perspective. The final corpus included 195 studies published between 2023 and 2025 within a specified eligibility window of January 2021 to December 2025. Records were dual screened, coded using a structured framework, and analyzed across psychological focus, thematic constructs, GenAI tools, study designs, outcomes, contextual characteristics, self-determination theory (SDT) needs, equity, and evidence strength. The screening agreement was 81.9%, with Cohen’s κ = 0.642. Motivation was the most common primary focus (31.3%), followed by perception (26.7%), engagement (18.5%), creativity (15.4%), and general/other (8.2%). The literature was dominated by ChatGPT and general GenAI systems, while survey-based and observational evidence was far more common than experimental evidence, longitudinal research, or studies reporting objective performance outcomes. Among 155 empirical studies, mixed or conditional outcomes were most frequent (46.5%), compared with predominantly positive findings (21.9%). SDT related evidence was most common for competence (42.6%), followed by autonomy (29.7%) and relatedness (22.6%), although direct measurement was rare. Based on these findings, the study proposes the GenAI engagement framework, a literature informed structure that organizes five recurring components of GenAI supported learning without assuming a fixed sequence or causal pathway. The framework is not presented as a validated causal model, but as a structured basis for future research and instructional design. The findings suggest that the educational value of GenAI depends less on the technology itself than on how it is guided, evaluated, and integrated into meaningful learning activities.

papers.title: Factors influencing the use of artificial intelligence in Peruvian university context
papers.authors: Iván Iraola-Real, Carla Vasquez, Roberto Cotrina
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has made significant advances in education, but ethical debates surrounding its use persist. Given this issue, this article aims to analyze the factors influencing the use of AI among students at a private university in Lima, Peru. Three studies were conducted in this regard. The first study (N = 125) took a qualitative approach and analyzed the category called “benefits of AI in university education,” in which students expressed that AI is useful for optimizing their studies and research. However, in the category “disadvantages of using AI in university education,” the students recognized that using AI is risky because it generates information without citing authors; furthermore, it undermines autonomous and critical thinking. Being similar to studies in other countries. For these reasons, in the second study (N = 402), a confidence scale toward the use of AI was adapted, demonstrating reliability and confirmatory validity. Finally, in the third study (N = 928), a path analysis showed that digital self-efficacy and virtual educational performance predicted the perception of the benefits of AI, the reasons for not using it, and educational improvement with AI. Digital anxiety then played a mediating role between virtual educational performance and attitudes toward AI.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Ensemble Learning Models for Cardiovascular Disease Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Syifa Alfariani, Fathoni Fathoni
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Informatics and Computing
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is one of the leading causes of death worldwide, making early risk detection essential to support clinical decision-making. Although machine learning models have been widely applied to cardiovascular disease prediction, challenges remain in achieving consistent performance improvements through ensemble learning and providing interpretable prediction results. This study aims to develop a cardiovascular disease risk prediction model by integrating ensemble learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) using the Cardiovascular Disease Dataset from Kaggle, consisting of 70,000 patient records. The research process includes Exploratory Data Analysis, data preprocessing, and model development using Random Forest, CatBoost, and LightGBM combined using a stacking approach with Logistic Regression as the meta-learner. Model interpretability was analyzed using SHAP and LIME, while performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. The results show that LightGBM achieved the highest accuracy of 74.13%, recall of 70.48%, and F1-score of 72.95%, while Random Forest achieved the highest precision of 76.21%. The stacking model achieved the highest AUC-ROC of 80.92%, although it did not consistently outperform individual models across all evaluation metrics. The interpretability analysis identified systolic blood pressure (ap_hi), age, cholesterol, diastolic blood pressure (ap_lo), and body mass index (BMI) as the most influential features in the predictions. This study demonstrates the integration of stacking ensemble learning and XAI using SHAP and LIME, resulting in a model with competitive predictive performance and improved interpretability for cardiovascular disease risk assessment.

papers.title: Machine Learning for EEG-Based Cognitive Response Analysis in the Free Nutritious Meals Program
papers.authors: Rahmat Hidayat, Yusa Putra, Yerezqy Bagus, Sri Dasweni, Akbar Shiddiq
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Informatics and Computing
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals provide objective information on students’ cognitive responses; however, an appropriate classification method is required to effectively process their characteristics. This study aims to compare the performance of six machine learning algorithms in classifying students’ cognitive responses based on EEG data collected in the context of the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) Program. The evaluated algorithms include K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, and Support Vector Machine, using delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma features. The modeling process involved baseline model development and hyperparameter tuning, followed by performance evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The results show that K-Nearest Neighbors achieved the highest baseline accuracy of 88.00%. After hyperparameter tuning, Decision Tree achieved the highest performance among the tuned models, with an accuracy and macro F1-score of 88.00%. However, its accuracy was identical to that of baseline KNN, and no significant difference was observed between their predictions. These findings indicate that hyperparameter tuning affected the evaluated algorithms differently, with Decision Tree showing the largest performance improvement under the experimental configuration used in this study.

papers.title: MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS AND ART DIRECTION IN THE MEDIA INDUSTRY: HISTORICAL EVOLUTION, MODERN MANAGEMENT AND ORGANIZATION OF ADVERTISING AND PUBLIC RELATIONS ACTIVITIES
papers.authors: Inna Herashchenko
papers.abstract: The article examines the transformation of marketing communications and art direction in the contemporary media industry under the influence of digitalization. Particular attention is paid to the historical evolution of advertising and public relations, the transformation of creative management, and the growing role of social media, data analytics and artificial intelligence. The purpose of the study is to identify the main changes in the organization of advertising and PR activities and to substantiate the strategic role of art direction within integrated marketing communications. The research applies historical, systematic, comparative, structural-functional and modeling methods. The study develops a conceptual model that integrates strategic planning, audience analysis, communication architecture, creative concept, art direction, media and PR activation, measurement and strategic adjustment. The proposed approach considers art direction as a managerial function connecting communication strategy, creative execution, brand identity and audience experience. The practical significance of the results lies in their application to the management of contemporary advertising, PR and creative teams.

papers.title: INFLUENCE OF SELF-WEIGHING BEHAVIOR ON WEIGHT LOSS AND MAINTENANCE IN THE ADULT MALE POPULATION
papers.authors: Jadulluh Mohammad Al-Ghazo, Reem Khalid A Al-Saadi, Noora Mohammed Aljaffali, Sara Rashid Al-Adgham, Bushra Omar ALBadareen, Anwar Mohd. Faleh Qudaisat, Mohammad Ghassan Ragheb Abdelbaset, Sibusiso Reuben Kutama, Reynald Jaenelle Manlungat, Hany Hamdy El Shekh, Mohamed Abdelssalem Miled, Mohammad Farouq AlZghoul, Eltigani O.M. Omer
papers.journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
papers.abstract: Background: Self-weighting, a core behavioral component of weight management, is recommended by major clinical guidelines, but evidence for its effectiveness in adult males is scarce. Objective: To assess the association between self-weighing frequency and changes in body weight and composition among overweight and obese adult males. Methods: This retrospective observational study analyzed electronic medical records from adult male employees (BMI ≥25 kg/m²) who used a body composition analyzer (Tanita MC-980 MA, Japan) at least twice during the first six months of 2025. Participants were grouped by self-weighing frequency. Primary outcomes included changes in body weight and BMI. Secondary outcomes included changes in body fat percentage, fat mass, and visceral fat level. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS v27, with significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Eighty-nine participants met the inclusion criteria. Higher self-weighing frequency correlated with greater reductions in body weight and BMI (p < 0.05). Those who weighed themselves more often showed greater improvements in body fat percentage and fat mass compared to those with a lower frequency. The association held across the overweight and obese subgroups. Effect sizes indicated clinically meaningful reductions in adiposity parameters among high-frequency self-weighers. Conclusions: Modest reductions in body fat percentage and mass were observed over time. However, self-weighing intensity alone did not appear to independently drive clinically meaningful weight reduction. Future trials incorporating structured dietary interventions, behavioral feedback, and assessment of psychological mediators are needed to clarify the role of self-monitoring within comprehensive obesity treatment.

papers.title: AI-ASSISTED CO-CREATIVE MULTIMODAL STORYTELLING IN ENGLISH: ENGAGEMENT, MOTIVATION AND VOCABULARY USE IN A SIXTH-GRADE PRIMARY SCHOOL INTERVENTION
papers.authors: Evangelia Tzagkourni, Christos Simos
papers.journal: Global Journal of Engineering and Technology Advances
papers.abstract: This paper presents an educational intervention of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted co-creative multimodal storytelling, implemented in the English course with 48 sixth-grade students at a public primary school. Students composed short descriptive paragraphs about imaginary creatures, received narrative expansions of their texts from an AI tool, and created multimodal artworks that incorporated words and phrases from these expansions. The evaluation of the intervention was based on structured observation, organized around four dimensions of motivation. The records indicate increased engagement and creative initiative, more intensive peer collaboration and the spontaneous use of new descriptive vocabulary in students' multimodal products and oral presentations. As no assessment of written production was conducted before and after the intervention, the findings are limited to observed engagement and language use.

papers.title: AI-mediated feedback in L2 writing: effects on performance, engagement and instructor perspectives in an Armenian university context
papers.authors: Luiza I. Marabyan, Lilit Avetisyan, Marine Avetisyan, Anna Knyazyan
papers.abstract: Written corrective feedback (WCF) is a cornerstone of second language (L2) writing instruction, and the emergence of AI-based tools has substantially transformed its delivery. However, a critical conceptual distinction exists between AI tools that provide corrective feedback on linguistic form, such as Grammarly and Cambridge Write & Improve, and large language model (LLM)-based tools, such as ChatGPT, which generate broader discourse-level feedback encompassing ideas, organisation, and cohesion. This mixed-methods study investigates how a sequenced combination of these AI tools is associated with the writing performance, perceptions, and engagement of 80 intermediate ESL learners at the European University of Armenia, alongside the perspectives of 10 ESL instructors. A four-week classroom intervention incorporated in-class, timed writing tasks, a learner questionnaire, structured written reflections, and semi-structured instructor interviews. Inter-rater reliability between the two independent raters was high (ICC > .90). Quantitative analysis using paired-sample t-tests and a rubric adapted from Bitchener and Ferris (2012) revealed statistically significant pre-to-post improvements across grammatical accuracy, lexical variety, cohesion, and overall writing quality. In the absence of a control group and given the use of different essay prompts at pre- and post-test, these gains should be interpreted with caution rather than attributed causally to the AI intervention alone. Qualitative thematic analysis of reflections and interviews identified four learner themes: enhanced error awareness, structured revision support, difficulty evaluating feedback appropriateness, and emerging dependency, and five instructor themes centring on efficiency gains, risks of uncritical revision, uneven engagement, ethical concerns, and support for a hybrid pedagogical model. Drawing on feedback literacy (Carless & Boud, 2018), the Noticing Hypothesis (Schmidt, 1990), and Sociocultural Theory (Vygotsky, 1978), the study proposes a conceptual teacher-AI partnership framework in which automated tools complement, rather than replace, human pedagogical judgment, pending empirical validation through future research incorporating teacher-mediated designs. The study makes three contributions to the CALL literature: an empirical account of sequential multi-tool AWE integration examined across behavioural, cognitive, and affective engagement dimensions; evidence that feedback literacy development is proficiency-linked and requires explicit instructional scaffolding rather than tool exposure alone; and a theoretically grounded teacher-AI partnership framework positioned as a basis for future controlled experimental designs in EFL writing pedagogy.

papers.title: IMPLICATIONS AND INSTRUCTIONAL RESPONSES TO AI-RELATED COGNITIVE OUTSOURCING IN FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING
papers.authors: Olesia FEDOROVA
papers.abstract: This article addresses the phenomenon of cognitive outsourcing in foreign language education amid the rapid proliferation of generative AI tools. Cognitive outsourcing is defined as the deliberate transfer of cognitively demanding language-learning tasks to AI systems in ways that bypass the mental processing necessary for skill development and knowledge acquisition. The study distinguishes it from legitimate uses of AI, arguing that the key criterion is whether AI involvement occurs before or after the cognitive engagement with a task. The article examines six domains in which cognitive outsourcing manifests: essay writing, vocabulary acquisition, conversational practice with AI chatbots, grammar learning, translation, and preparation for oral performance tasks. The analysis shows how AI-mediated shortcuts undermine mechanisms of second language acquisition, including generative processing in writing, productive inference in vocabulary learning, negotiation in conversation, the noticing process in grammar development, desirable difficulty in reading comprehension, and spontaneous communication in oral production. Particular attention is given to the motivational consequences of outsourcing - erosion of learners’ ideal L2 self and long-term engagement. Rejecting a prohibitionist stance toward AI as pedagogically counterproductive, the article proposes the cultivation of cognitive outsourcing awareness. This approach is presented as essential for three reasons: learners rarely recognize outsourcing dynamics without guidance; the concept offers a constructive, nonadversarial discussing AI use in the classroom; and explicit instruction addresses equity concerns, since learners with weaker metacognitive and critical literacy skills are vulnerable to uncritical AI dependence. The article concludes that fostering informed, reflective AI use offers the most viable path for preserving the developmental benefits of effortful language learning while acknowledging the realities of a technology-saturated educational environment

papers.title: MORAL AND ETHICAL DIMENSION OF CADET TRAINING IN THE U.S. MILITARY HIGHER EDUCATION SYSTEM
papers.authors: Svitlana V. Fedorenko, D. V. Bernadin
papers.abstract: This article examines the moral and ethical dimension of cadet education within the U.S. military higher education system, using the United States Military Academy at West Point as a case study, as one of the key factors in developing the professional competence of future officers. The relevance of this study is driven by the evolving nature of the contemporary security environment, the digital transformation of military operations, the expanding use of artificial intelligence and autonomous technologies, the growing emphasis on ethical leadership, and the increasing need to educate future officers who are capable of making ethically justified decisions in complex, uncertain, and high-risk operational environments. It is emphasized that this issue is of particular significance in the context of reforming Ukraine’s military education system, aligning it with NATO standards, and integrating it into the Euro-Atlantic educational area. The article analyzes the conceptual foundations of the moral and ethical education of future officers in the United States, identifies its structural components, pedagogical mechanisms, and current development trends. It has been established that moral and ethical education in U.S. military academies is implemented as a comprehensive pedagogical system based on the interaction of several interconnected components, including the Cadet Honor Code, the Army Ethic, ethical reasoning, character development, and leader development. It is substantiated that the integrated implementation of these components promotes the development of moral autonomy, professional responsibility, leadership qualities, professional identity, moral judgment, and the ability to make ethically justified decisions in the complex environment of military service. The study also demonstrates that the current stage of U.S. military education is characterized by increased attention to digital ethics, the ethical implications of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, algorithm-assisted decision-making, and the preservation of meaningful human control over the use of force. It is concluded that the moral and ethical dimension is not a separate element of professional education but a system-forming foundation for preparing officers as leaders who combine professional competence with moral responsibility, integrity, and commitment to the values of the military profession.
keywords: United States Military Academy at West Point

papers.title: INTEGRATIVE MODEL FOR DEVELOPING PROFESSIONAL ENGLISH COMPETENCE OF FUTURE LAWYERS IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF HIGHER EDUCATION
papers.authors: Nataliia Myronenko, S.B. Panchyshyn, M. Opyr
papers.abstract: The rapid digital transformation of higher education and legal practice, together with the internationalization of legal services and the growing integration of artificial intelligence into professional activities, have fundamentally reshaped the requirements for preparing future lawyers. In this context, professional English competence extends beyond language proficiency to encompass the ability to operate effectively in multilingual, technology-enhanced, and intercultural legal environments. The purpose of the study is to theoretically develop and substantiate an integrative model to foster the professional English competence of future lawyers through Legal English in digitally enhanced legal education. The proposed model is grounded in competency-based, communicative, interdisciplinary, and learner-centred approaches while incorporating digital pedagogy, AI-supported learning, and professional legal communication. The study employs theoretical methods, including comparative analysis, conceptual synthesis, modelling, and systematization of contemporary ESP approaches. Particular attention is devoted to authentic legal discourse, casebased learning, Moot Court simulations, digital legal resources, and generative artificial intelligence as tools that support professional language development, academic integrity, and the critical evaluation of AI-generated content. The scientific novelty lies in the development of an integrative pedagogical model that conceptualizes professional English competence as a multidimensional construction comprising motivational-professional, legal-linguistic, professional-communicative, digital-AI, and reflectivedevelopmental components. The model positions Legal English as a strategic instrument for developing professional communication, legal reasoning, digital competence, and international professional mobility. The practical significance of the model lies in its applicability to curriculum design, Legal English syllabi, ESP course development, digital learning environments and professional training for future lawyers. It also supports alignment with international professional requirements and preparation for Legal English assessment frameworks such as TOLES.

papers.title: Интеллектуальные методы эквализации и компрессии в процессе мастеринга звука на основе машинного обучения
papers.authors: Д.О. Сокольцова, Г.В. Шагрова
papers.abstract: В статье рассматривается задача автоматизации мастеринга аудиозаписей с использованием методов машинного обучения и цифровой обработки сигналов. Актуальность обусловлена стремительным ростом объемов аудиоконтента и потребностью в доступных инструментах профессиональной обработки звука для независимых музыкантов и малых студий. В работе предложена гибридная система, интегрирующая классификатор музыкальных жанров на основе метода опорных векторов с мел-кепстральными коэффициентами и модуль цифровой обработки сигналов, включающий эквализацию, компрессию, фильтрацию верхних и нижних частот, а также нормализацию громкости. Обучение классификатора выполнено на датасете GTZAN, а параметры обработки извлечены из датасета MUSDB18-HQ, содержащего треки с вокалом, на основе анализа среднеквадратичной амплитуды и распределения энергии по частотным диапазонам. Тестирование на выборке из пятнадцати треков пяти жанров показало, что использование MUSDB18-HQ повышает точность классификации жанров с 46,6 % до 60 % и увеличивает отношение сигнал-шум по сравнению с моделью, обученной только на GTZAN. Сравнение с коммерческим аналогом показывает отставание разработанной системы по объективным метрикам, но система обладает преимуществами в виде прозрачности параметров обработки благодаря наличию элемента логирования, простоты использования и отсутствия платы за использование. Новизна работы заключается в использовании открытого классификатора жанров с модулем цифровой обработки сигналов и адаптации параметров мастеринга для треков с вокалом. Практическая значимость состоит в создании доступного прототипа для образовательных целей и обработки демо-записей. В дальнейшем планируется замена метода опорных векторов на нейросетевые архитектуры и расширение поддержки аудиоформатов. The article addresses the problem of automating audio mastering using machine learning and digital signal processing methods. The study is relevant due to the rapid growth in the volume of audio content and the need for affordable professional sound processing tools for independent musicians and small studios. A hybrid system is proposed that integrates a music genre classifier (a support vector machine with mel-frequency cepstral coefficients) and a digital signal processing module including equalization, compression, high-pass and low-pass filtering, as well as loudness normalization. The classifier was trained on the GTZAN dataset, while the processing parameters were extracted from the MUSDB18-HQ dataset containing vocal tracks, based on the analysis of root-mean-square amplitude and energy distribution across frequency ranges. Experimental testing on a sample of fifteen tracks of five genres showed that the use of MUSDB18-HQ increases genre classification accuracy from 46.6 % to 60.0 % and improves the signal-to-noise ratio by 2.2 dB compared to the model trained only on GTZAN. Comparison with a commercial counterpart shows that the developed system lags behind in terms of objective metrics; however, the system has advantages: complete transparency of processing parameters due to a detailed log, ease of use, and no usage fee. The novelty of the work lies in the integration of an openly available genre classifier with a digital signal processing module and the adaptation of mastering parameters for vocal tracks. The practical significance lies in the creation of an accessible prototype for educational purposes and for processing demo recordings. Future work includes replacing the support vector machine with neural-network architectures and expanding support for audio formats.

papers.title: Two Essays on Designing Conversational Agents: Varying Level of Mimicry and Personality–Brand Congruence
papers.authors: Sama Ashouri
papers.abstract: Across two essays, this dissertation demonstrates that mimicry and personality shape consumers’ perceptions of chatbot intelligence, creativity, and fit, with downstream effects on recommendation acceptance that depend on factors such as mimicry intensity, brand familiarity. Essay1: Mimicry, a central aspect of human interaction, is increasingly being examined in human–AI communication, particularly with chatbots. While prior research shows mimicry can build rapport, trust, and engagement, it has often been treated as a binary factor, overlooking how different levels may influence user perceptions. This research proposes and tests a dual-mediation framework in which different levels of chatbot mimicry affects recommendation acceptance through perceived intelligence and perceived creativity. Across four experiments, this study examines how mimicry level (low, medium, high), mimicry type (informational vs. emotional), and prior chatbot experience shape these outcomes. Study 1 tested the main effect: high mimicry reduced perceived intelligence, perceived creativity, and recommendation acceptance relative to medium mimicry. High levels of mimicry reduced chatbot recommendation acceptance, while low and medium levels of mimicry did not differ from each other. Study 2 identified perceived ease of use as a boundary condition, showing that the negative effects of high mimicry were particularly pronounced among users who found chatbot interactions easy and intuitive. Study 3 examined whether mimicry type moderates these effects. Informational mimicry produced higher perceived intelligence than emotional mimicry at medium levels but not at high levels. For perceived creativity, high emotional mimicry led to higher ratings than medium emotional mimicry. For recommendation acceptance, medium informational mimicry outperformed medium emotional mimicry, suggesting that reflecting factual content is more beneficial than emotional content at moderate mimicry levels. Study 4 replicated the main effect of mimicry level and tested prior chatbot experience as a moderator. Prior experience did not moderate the indirect effects through perceived intelligence or perceived creativity, providing no support for the hypothesized moderation. These findings demonstrate that chatbot mimicry effects are nonlinear, context-dependent, and sensitive to mimicry type, offering practical guidance for chatbot designers to calibrate mimicry levels and content accordingly. Essay 2: As chatbots increasingly act as brand representatives, the personality they express may need to fit the personality of the brand. This research tests how the fit between chatbot personality (introverted vs. extraverted) and brand personality (sincere vs. sophisticated) shapes perceived fit and recommendation acceptance across three studies. Study 1 used fictitious brands, Study 2 used real and familiar brands, and Study 3 used two sophisticated real brands to test brand awe as an explanation for the brand effect found in Study 2. Perceived fit was higher when the chatbot matched the brand, but only for fictitious brands, and this congruence did not carry over to recommendation acceptance in any study. Instead, the introverted chatbot was preferred for fictitious brands and the extraverted chatbot for familiar ones, which suggests that brand familiarity may decide which chatbot style works best. In addition, brand awe raised both perceived fit and recommendation acceptance. Perceived fit and recommendation acceptance did not move together, which sheds light on a literature that has assumed fit leads to better outcomes and shows that the two have partly different drivers. The theoretical and managerial implications of these findings are discussed.

papers.title: Искусственный интеллект в учебном процессе студентов: эмпирический анализ распространённости, противоречия в восприятии
papers.authors: О.Н. Митрофанова
papers.abstract: Статья посвящена вопросам использования искусственного интеллекта в учебном процессе студентов. По результатам эмпирического исследования студенческая аудитория демонстрирует утилитарно-прагматическое принятие ИИ как повседневного учебного инструмента при сохранении критической рефлексии о возможных когнитивных издержках. Выявлена поляризация мнений о риске подмены самостоятельного мышления. Предложена классификация целей использования и выявлено дифференцированное отношение к ИИ в учебном и внешне коммуникативном контекстах. Сделан вывод о необходимости перехода от политики запретов к развитию критической ИИ-грамотности и выработке институциональных норм декларирования использования ИИ в академической среде. Новизна исследования заключается в том, что впервые на репрезентативной выборке студентов Липецкого государственного технического университета комплексно анализируются не только количественные показатели использования, но и субъективные оценки когнитивных рисков (подмена мышления), мотивационных эффектов и нормативных предпочтений. Статья будет интересна преподавателям и специалистам в сфере образования, которые рассматривают использование ИИ инструментов в учебном процессе как неизбежную реальность с которой предстоит еще научиться взаимодействовать. The article is devoted to the use of artificial intelligence in the educational process of students. According to the results of an empirical study, the student audience demonstrates a utilitarian and pragmatic acceptance of AI as an everyday learning tool while maintaining critical reflection on possible cognitive costs. The polarization of opinions about the risk of substitution of independent thinking has been revealed. A classification of the purposes of use is proposed and a differentiated attitude towards AI in educational and external communicative contexts is revealed. It is concluded that there is a need to move from a policy of prohibitions to the development of critical AI literacy and the development of institutional norms for declaring the use of AI in the academic environment. The novelty of the study lies in the fact that for the first time, a representative sample of Lipetsk State Technical University students comprehensively analyzes not only quantitative usage indicators, but also subjective assessments of cognitive risks (substitution of thinking), motivational effects and normative preferences. The article will be of interest to teachers and specialists in the field of education who consider the use of AI tools in the educational process as an inevitable reality with which they have yet to learn how to interact.

papers.title: Developing student feedback literacy through GenAI-supported student-teacher feedback co-creation: A mixed-methods study
papers.authors: Kar Yan Jessica To, Renjie Cai, Nicole Judith Tavares, Lok Hei Locky Law
papers.abstract: Feedback co-creation is an effective strategy to increase students’ proactivity. Yet, limited studies have delved into the co-creation process between students and teachers in a GenAI-mediated environment and the impact of feedback co-creation on student feedback literacy. This mixed-methods case study explored how GenAI-supported feedback co-creation shaped students’ development of feedback literacy at a university in Hong Kong. Findings from pre-post feedback literacy surveys, observations of feedback dialogues, and interviews showed that GenAI-supported feedback co-creation could improve students’ evaluative judgements, proactivity, elicitation and uptake of feedback. GenAI facilitated feedback co-creation by helping students clarify unclear criteria, interpret teacher feedback, and assess the quality of draft revisions. Implications are drawn to construct a preliminary GenAI-supported student-teacher feedback co-creation model and to guide students’ meaningful use of GenAI for metacognitive monitoring in feedback processes.

papers.title: Adverse drug reactions associated with anti-tubercular therapy: A proof-of-concept pharmacovigilance analysis using an open-source Python analytic pipeline
papers.authors: Puneet Paliwal, Syed Ziaur Rahman, Imrana Masood, Farhan Ahmad Khan
papers.journal: Annals of the National Academy of Medical Sciences (India)
papers.abstract: Objectives To characterize the pattern, causality, severity, and seriousness of adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in patients receiving anti-tubercular therapy (ATT); to examine factors associated with ADR seriousness; and to demonstrate, as a proof of concept, that an open-source Python analytic pipeline can provide a reproducible foundation for pharmacovigilance audits and future machine-learning applications. Material and Methods In this observational, retrospective pharmacovigilance study was conducted at a tertiary-care teaching hospital in northern India. Six hundred ADR events recorded in adults (>18 years) receiving first-line or multidrug-resistant (MDR)/ extensively drug-resistant (XDR) -TB regimens were analyzed. Causality was assessed using the Naranjo algorithm and the World Health Organization-Uppsala Monitoring Centre (WHO-UMC) scale; severity was graded on the Modified Hartwig–Siegel scale; seriousness was classified per International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) E2A. Inter-scale causality agreement was quantified using Cohen’s κ. Categorical associations were tested by chi-square with Monte Carlo simulation (9,999 resamples) or Fisher’s exact test, where expected cell counts were <5; non-normally distributed continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test with rank-biserial effect size. A post-hoc 2 × 2 analysis compared linezolid with other agents. All analyses were executed in Python 3 (Pandas, SciPy, Matplotlib); α = 0.05. Results Peripheral neuropathy was the most frequent ADR (165/600; 27.50%), followed by skin discoloration (73/600; 12.17%) and gastritis (43/600; 7.17%). The great majority of reactions were non-serious (577/600; 96.17%) and mild in severity (585/600; 97.50%); 23 (3.83%) were serious, and 6 (1.00%) severe on Hartwig grading. Causality was ‘Possible’ in 93.67% (Naranjo) and 98.33% (WHO-UMC); raw agreement was 94.00%, but Cohen’s κ was 0.23 (95% CI −0.01 to 0.47), consistent with fair agreement, and McNemar’s test was significant (χ 2 = 20.25; p <0.001), indicating systematic directional disagreement. Drug type was significantly associated with seriousness (χ 2 = 34.19; simulated p <0.001); linezolid accounted for 14/23 serious ADRs with a post-hoc odds ratio of 7.8 (95% CI 3.3–18.6) versus all other agents combined, whereas clofazimine (n = 109 exposures) contributed none. Treatment duration was significantly longer in the serious ADR group (median 270 days, IQR 210–360 vs 180, IQR 120–240; U = 9,502.5; p <0.001; r ≈ 0.42, moderate effect). Age, body weight, and sex were not significantly associated with seriousness or severity. Conclusion ADRs in this ATT cohort were frequent but predominantly mild and non-serious. Linezolid emerged as the principal drug-level factor associated with serious ADRs, supporting structured hematological and neurological surveillance in linezolid-containing regimens. The modest Cohen’s κ, despite high observed agreement, underscores the value of reporting both Naranjo and WHO-UMC assessments. A reproducible open-source Python pipeline supported the full pharmacovigilance workflow and provides an extensible foundation on which supervised ML models may subsequently be built.

papers.title: HOW ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CAN SYSTEMATICALLY ENHANCE SOFT SKILLS IN ENGLISH BLENDED LEARNING – A PEDAGOGICAL DESIGN FOR CHINESE EFL LEARNERS
papers.authors: Gao Ning
papers.abstract: Soft skills are essential for university students, yet many Chinese EFL learners remain at a knowledge-telling stage, prioritizing language proficiency over interpreting acquired knowledge, while curriculum design has long centered on language hard skills with soft skills often not explicitly included as instructional objectives. This marginalization of soft skills is a persistent dilemma. Artificial intelligence, especially generative AI, is profoundly reshaping foreign language education and offering new possibilities for systematically cultivating soft skills. Nevertheless, current higher education English teaching faces two separate dilemmas: the marginalization of soft skills development, and the lack of standardization in AI use. This paper focuses on the first question of how artificial intelligence tools can systematically enhance university students’ soft skills within an English blended learning environment. This paper proposes a pedagogical design aiming to transform soft skills from implicit expectations into explicit instructional objectives.

papers.title: FUTURE MODELS OF AI-ENABLED CREATIVE TOURISM: A COMPARATIVE SCENARIO ANALYSIS OF THE TRANSFERABILITY OF THE ICELANDIC, JAPANESE AND UAE EXPERIENCE TO AZERBAIJAN
