This study develops the Community–MSME Digital Ecosystem Framework, which explains the transformation of the community’s position from recipient, participant, collaborator, and digital economic actor to ecosystem driver. The findings emphasize that community service needs to move beyond knowledge transfer toward capability development, collaboration, value co-creation, and ecosystem building. This framework offers an empowerment approach that positions communities and MSMEs as collaborative actors in creating value, strengthening self-reliance, and building a sustainable local digital economic ecosystem.

papers.title: Utilizzo dell’Intelligenza Artificiale Generativa nei diversi gradi scolastici
papers.authors: Agostino Sorbara
papers.journal: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence has redefined learning processes, carrying the risk that cognitive functions are delegated to it rather than using it as an empowering tool within an “extended mind” perspective. This paper explores the critical use of Artificial Intelligence through a qualitative survey conducted across three educational levels: upper secondary school, ITS Academy, and initial teacher education programs (University). The research is based on the analysis of semi-structured interviews to investigate the evolution of the interaction phases between student and machine, based on the received output. This study aims to analyze how students interact with language models, verifying whether the technology is used as a «quick shortcut to reach the solution» or as an «embodied mediator capable of stimulating reflexivity and procedural awareness». The findings highlight differentiated trajectories: while an uncritical and passive use prevails in upper secondary school, a capacity to integrate Generative Artificial Intelligence as a controlled “cognitive prosthesis” emerges in ITS Academy and within the Humanities and STEM fields. Conversely, the Special Education field shows a divide between passive attitudes and critical-reflective stances. In conclusion, this work offers a reflection on the need to help students engage in a dialogic interaction with Artificial Intelligence to enhance its expressive and analytical potential.

papers.title: Teachers’ Readiness to Integrate Artificial Intelligence into Higher Education and Their Digital Competence (A Case Study of Genetics Education)
papers.authors: Azimova Nasiba Ergashovna, Mahbuba Akhtamovna Mirzoyeva
papers.abstract: This article presents the theoretical and methodological foundations of a study aimed at examining the relationship between the digital competence of faculty members in higher education institutions and their readiness to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into the educational process. The study employs a quantitative cross-sectional design. Data are collected through a structured questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis (Cronbach’s alpha), correlation analysis, the t-test, analysis of variance (ANOVA), and multiple regression analysis. The article provides a detailed rationale for the scientific relevance of the study, its objectives, research questions, selected methodology, and planned analytical framework. The findings are expected to contribute to the development of a human-centered and responsible model for the use of artificial intelligence in higher education.

papers.title: Aspetti pedagogici dell’interazione umano-IA nella scrittura accade-mica
papers.authors: Domenico Lucchese
papers.journal: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: The advent of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) radically challenges the epistemology and pedagogy of academic writing. This paper proposes a pedagogical reflection on human-AI interaction based on the problematicism of Banfi and Bertin, interpreting the relationship between the writer (the self) and the intelligent system (the world) as an inherently problematic experience. Rejecting both rigid prohibition and uncritical acceptance, the problematicist model values the unbridgeable "gap" between the human and the artificial as a critical, flexible, and creative space where AI functions not as a substitute, but as a dialectical interlocutor. This theoretical framework finds its methodological application in constructivist and socio-constructivist theories, framing GenAI as a digital partner and a temporary scaffolding tool within the student's Zone of Proximal Development. By reconceptualizing writing through a dialogic, process-oriented, and authentic lens, this work outlines innovative teaching strategies and critical AI literacy pathways aimed at overcoming algorithmic dependence and promoting a renewed practical wisdom in academic education.

papers.title: Riprogettare Unità di Apprendimento in ottica embodied con l’Intelligenza Artificiale Generativa
papers.authors: Martina Dicorato, Anna Maria Cuzzi, Francesco Pio Sarcina
papers.journal: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: Embodied Education acknowledges the central role of the body in the construction of knowledge, outlining educational pathways in which mental processes, bodily experience, and context are deeply interconnected. This paper investigates the potential of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) to support the rethinking of Learning Units from an embodied perspective, while keeping teachers’ design responsibility and professional judgment at the core. The experience presented here was developed within a training course for primary school teachers, focused on the ethical and critical integration of algorithmic technologies. To this end, a recursive model structured into five phases was introduced, although only the first three were explored in depth with the course participants. The work was supported by a GEM, a customized Gemini configuration designed to assist educators in transforming conventional teaching activities into immersive, multisensory, and situated learning experiences. GenAI is thus conceived as a cognitive and creative mediator capable of providing practical insights, materials, and inclusive solutions. Through a comparative matrix, the paper presents several trajectories for embodied redesign, while also outlining possible scenarios for the application and monitoring of the proposed model.

papers.title: Employee Perceptions of AI-Driven Performance Monitoring: Mental Well-being and Job Satisfaction
papers.authors: Sabit Ibne Sazzad, Md. Rafiqul Islam
papers.journal: Research and Review Human Resource and Labour Management
papers.abstract: The application of AI in performance management by companies raises concerns about worker well-being. This study explores the views of employees about the effects of AI-based performance management on their mental health and job satisfaction, considering the case of an emerging economy such as Bangladesh. To collect data, the study used a qualitative research design involving semi-structured focus group discussions with 10 purposively selected participants (n=10) who are professionals in the information technology, finance, and academic fields. Thematic analysis was applied to the data in six steps. Main themes found were the following: increased fear and stress; reduced autonomy and creativity; unfairness and lack of trust; coping mechanisms; transparency and human involvement; and conditional acceptance of AI. Results show that AI provides consistency and impartiality, but due to its constant presence, it often causes algorithmic anxiety and dehumanization of employees. To use AI effectively, it is necessary to adopt strategies that guarantee human centrality and safeguard the dignity and integrity of workers. The AI-IOB model is one such strategy.

papers.title: Debate, ambienti di apprendimento e intelligenza artificiale: costruire il pensiero tra corpo, relazioni e tecnologie
papers.authors: Rosa Carnevale
papers.journal: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: The spread of generative artificial intelligence has reignited the debate on the nature of human reasoning and the skills that schools should promote. Although AI systems produce persuasive arguments, they operate without bodily experience, relational participation, or situated engagement. This thematic review brings together three strands of research—embodied cognition, educational debate, and generative AI—to examine whether embodied cognition can offer a framework for understanding the educational value of debate. The analysis identifies four recurring dimensions: the body as a cognitive resource, situated cognition, emotional regulation, and socially distributed reasoning. The comparison with AI is used as an interpretive framework to highlight these dimensions, demonstrating how debate constitutes an educational environment in which reasoning takes shape through action, relationships, and participation. The thematic review concludes by discussing the implications for the design of learning environments that integrate AI without sacrificing the embodied conditions necessary for the development of critical thinking.

papers.title: Inducing Interpersonal Closeness: Effects on Inter-Brain Synchrony and Collaborative Performance.
papers.authors: Nienke van Atteveldt, Ido Davidesco, Laura Fornari, Tieme W. P. Janssen
papers.abstract: This between-subject study tests whether experimentally induced interpersonal closeness (Fast-Friends; Aron et al., 1997) affects inter-brain synchrony (IBS) during a subsequent collaborative task. Dyads were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: a No-Interaction (NI) condition, in which partners silently thought about the answers to a set of superficial questions; a Small-Talk (ST) condition, in which they asked each other the same superficial questions; and a Fast-Friends (FF) condition, in which they asked each other an increasingly intimate sequence of questions, specifically designed to increase interpersonal closeness between pairs of strangers (Fast‑Friends procedure, Aron et al., 1997). Prior findings show that pairs in the FF condition reliably report greater perceived closeness after the manipulation than those in the ST condition, making this an ideal paradigm for investigating how variations in interpersonal closeness causally impact IBS and collaboration. After the manipulation, partners completed a computer-mediated collaborative maze task (Mills, 2014) while seated face-to-face at two computers. Players could not see each other’s position in the maze and had to coordinate verbally to reach their respective goals. The task comprised 10 mazes of equal difficulty, designed to be completed in 5 minutes each, although no time limit was imposed. Completion time served as the performance measure, as participants were asked to solve the mazes as quickly as possible. During both the manipulation and collaboration phase, we recorded EEG and video to quantify pairs’ IBS and motor synchrony. Only the collaborative-task data are analyzed here, while the EEG and video data concerning the interpersonal closeness manipulation have been analyzed elsewhere. We hypothesize that interpersonal closeness improves collaborative performance and increases IBS, and that higher IBS during collaboration predicts better collaborative performance.

papers.title: ChatGPT Data Donation U30
papers.authors: Julian Kohne, Mareike Wieland, Johannes Breuer, Josephine Schmitt
papers.abstract: Materials for the paper "Human–Chatbot Interactions in an Educational Context: Data Donation as a Method for Analyzing ChatGPT Usage" [German original title: Mensch–Chatbot-Interaktionen im Lernkontext: Datenspenden als Zugang zur Analyse tatsächlicher ChatGPT-Nutzung] published in the journal merz | medien + erziehung

papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Model Performance on Open-Ended Questions: Answering and Marking Capabilities
papers.authors: Tran Quang Dieu, Mai P. Tran, Quynh T. Nguyen, Michael Lo
papers.abstract: Statistical literacy is crucial in biology education, yet developing and assessing it at higher cognitive levels is resource-intensive. This study evaluated three large language models against 20 graduate students on open-ended biological statistics questions spanning Bloom's Taxonomy, and separately examined whether a large language model could serve as a marking assistant alongside an experienced human instructor. A set of 692 questions was developed by graduate students using a statistics textbook. After cleaning, 336 unique questions were retained, with 1,344 answers provided by the four respondent groups. Answers were graded using a holistic five-point rubric by a human expert and a large language model. Friedman tests showed that all models were rated more favourably than the graduate students, though this advantage was not uniform across cognitive levels, and the evaluative question type (Type 7) anchoring the highest cognitive level in this study's design showed the weakest performance across all respondent groups. Inter-rater reliability between the human and large language model was low overall. The large language model grader showed a bias toward scores of 3-4, while the human expert demonstrated greater consistency across question types. These findings suggest that large language models can generate strong responses at lower cognitive levels, but their reliability as holistic-rubric graders are limited compared to an experienced instructor.

papers.title: Identifying attentional control mechanisms related to the performance of high- and low-skilled First-Person Shooter game players: With exploratory data on expert older-adult esports players
papers.authors: Daisuke Shimane, Masaki Takeda, Inhyeok Jeong, Akinori Takeda
papers.abstract: High-skilled First-Person Shooter (FPS) game players are known to have superior attentional control—the ability to select information relevant to a task (selective attention) and maintain an appropriate response (sustained attention). However, it is unclear whether the attentional control strategies between high- and low-skilled FPS players differ, and whether these differences are related to FPS performance. Therefore, we investigated differences in attentional control between low- and high-skilled FPS players using electroencephalography, as well as correlations between gaming performance and attentional control. In addition, as an exploratory aim, we examined the characteristics of older FPS players. We recruited 11 high- and 11 low-skilled FPS players (under 25 years) and five older FPS players (over 65 years). Participants completed a task responding to colors regardless of the semantic meaning (Stroop task), clicked on targets quickly and accurately (aiming task), and played an FPS (esports task), respectively. We measured event-related potentials (ERPs) during the Stroop task to evaluate attentional control. In addition, we examined the relationship between ERP components and performance on the aiming and esports tasks. As a result, high-skilled players showed significantly smaller ERP amplitude in the 150-250 ms time window and greater ERP amplitude in the 280-380 ms time window (parietal region) during the Stroop task. These results suggest that high-skilled FPS players allocated attentional resources to relatively later stages of stimulus evaluation and processing. Furthermore, ERP amplitude showed a significant correlation with performance on aiming and esports tasks. Notably, older adults performed comparably to highly skilled young players on the FPS task, despite exhibiting smaller ERP amplitudes than young adults. These results suggest that attentional control is related to FPS performance and may be different with age.

papers.title: Integrasi kecerdasan artifisial dan data raya dalam pendidikan agama Islam: Tinjauan pustaka sistematis dan rekonstruksi kerangka konseptual
papers.authors: Saleh, Hadi Machmud, Nurdin, Imelda Wahyuni
papers.journal: Idarah Tarbawiyah Journal of Management in Islamic Education
papers.abstract: The acceleration of digital ecosystems forces a radical deconstruction of conventional Islamic Education (PAI) models. However, contemporary literature remains trapped in instrumentalist-technical approaches, failing to address students' affective-spiritual dimensions. This study aims to formulate a holistic-humanistic reconstruction model for PAI learning through the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Big Data analytics. Employing a qualitative approach with a philosophical-critical study, this research dissects Islamic epistemology in the cyber era. The findings reveal that integrating these technologies offers strategic opportunities for personalized character (akhlaq) curricula based on students' digital footprints. Nevertheless, implementation faces serious challenges, particularly the crisis of educators' spiritual authority and algorithmic bias risks. The pedagogical implications demand a radical reorientation of PAI teachers' roles, shifting from knowledge communicators to ethical curators and spiritual mentors. This research contributes a scientific blueprint for future prophetic Islamic pedagogy that pairs predictive intelligence with the ethics of ta’dib without diminishing the sacredness of religious values. Abstrak Akselerasi ekosistem digital memaksa rekonstruksi radikal terhadap model Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) konvensional. Namun, literatur kontemporer masih terjebak dalam pendekatan teknis-instrumentalis, sehingga gagal menyentuh dimensi afektif-spiritual siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merumuskan model rekonstruksi pembelajaran PAI yang holistik-humanis melalui konvergensi Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan analisis Big Data. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan studi filosofis-kritis, penelitian ini membedah epistemologi Islam di era siber. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa integrasi teknologi ini menawarkan peluang strategis untuk personalisasi kurikulum karakter (akhlak) berdasarkan jejak perilaku digital siswa. Meskipun demikian, implementasinya menghadapi tantangan serius, terutama krisis otoritas spiritual pendidik dan risiko bias algoritma. Implikasi pedagogisnya menuntut reorientasi radikal peran guru PAI, yang harus beralih dari sekadar komunikator pengetahuan menjadi kurator etis dan mentor spiritual. Penelitian ini berkontribusi dalam memberikan cetak biru ilmiah bagi pedagogi Islam profetik masa depan yang memadukan kecerdasan prediktif dengan etika ta’dib tanpa mengurangi kesakralan nilai-nilai agama.

papers.title: Pedagogia dell’embodiment tecnosensibile: : corporeità estesa, sapere tacito e ecologie ibride di apprendimento
papers.authors: Andrey Felipe Sgorla
papers.journal: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: Research on craft learning has demonstrated that knowledge transmission is grounded in embodied interaction between body, material and gesture — a tacit and proprioceptive knowledge developed through sustained practice and dialogue with matter. However, how generative artificial intelligence reconfigures such processes remains largely unexplored: how does the practitioner’s body relate to algorithmic output, and under what conditions can proprioceptive knowledge be transmitted within technologically mediated learning ecologies? This contribution addresses these questions by proposing the concept of techno-sensitive extended corporeality, describing the condition in which the body is not replaced by the algorithm but expands through digital interfaces that amplify perception and imaginative capacity. Drawing on the phenomenology of corporeality, embodied cognition and the hybrid artisan learning ecologies framework, the analysis articulates the reconfiguration across three planes: expanded manuality, human–machine co-authorship and educational sustainability. The findings reveal a pedagogical paradox — sensory knowledge resists the very digitisation on which hybrid environments depend — and derive design criteria for embodied learning environments in dialogue with emerging technologies.

papers.title: Formare i docenti per sviluppare l’agency degli studenti e > proteggerli dai rischi dei bias algoritmici
papers.authors: Rosaria Capobianco
papers.journal: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: Students must be trained in critical thinking and prepared to recognize the risks of Artificial Intelligence. The AI ​​Act, the 2024 European regulation on Artificial Intelligence, and the Guidelines for the introduction of Artificial Intelligence in schools, published by the M.I.M. in 2025, warn of the potential risks posed by Artificial Intelligence to health, individual and collective safety, and the protection of fundamental rights. For young students, biases pose a truly harmful risk: they are not just "errors in thought," but deceptive barriers to human and collective development. When a child grows up with prejudice, it crystallizes into mental patterns that shape their identity and the way they interact with the world. AI trained on distorted data can amplify stereotypes of gender, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status; The scenario becomes even more catastrophic when the algorithm itself generates distorted and potentially harmful output. From an educational perspective, teachers must be trained to activate students' agency, fostering in them an attitude of responsibility and trust toward Artificial Intelligence. The usefulness of AI in the learning process cannot be ignored.

papers.title: Dalla mente estesa al corpo che apprende: intelligenza artificiale e CAA tra embodiment e inclusione
papers.authors: Angela Ruotolo
papers.journal: Journal of Inclusive Methodology and Technology in Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence into educational settings opens up new opportunities for personalization, accessibility, and participation, while also raising a crucial pedagogical question: how can technology-mediated learning processes avoid becoming de-embodied? Drawing on Embodied Cognition, Embodied Education, situated learning, action neuroscience, and the extended mind thesis, this contribution offers a theoretical-pedagogical reflection on the relationship between AI, Augmentative and Alternative Communication, and meaning-making. The analysis argues that the educational value of AAC depends not only on the effectiveness of symbols or devices, but also on the quality of the bodily, emotional, and relational experiences that support their understanding. In this perspective, symbols are not merely representations of objects, but mediations of lived and shared experiences. The paper concludes with pedagogical indications for designing inclusive environments in which AI can amplify participation without replacing the body and human relationship.

papers.title: Plataformização e inteligência artificial: quem educa na educação superior?
papers.authors: Paulo Henrique Ribeiro de Lima
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education platforms is usually discussed in terms of what technology does. This theoretical-conceptual narrative review asks instead which conceptions of education, of the student and of teaching these architectures make possible, likely or invisible and, ultimately, who educates when part of the educational decisions moves into configuring the systems. It draws on four lenses (platformization and datafication, Paulo Freire's dialogical pedagogy, Gert Biesta's purposes of education, teaching and pedagogical mediation), with technical studies and policy documents as illustrations. It is argued that architectural decisions are also pedagogical decisions: what the platform records defines what the institution sees of learning; predictive and grading systems make qualification, above all, governable; generative assistants shape the student's position before knowledge; and configuring these systems redefines part of teachers' work. As a hypothesis resting mostly on pilot studies, it is suggested that the move from learning analytics to generative AI does not take the decision away from the student's traces, but adds a new locus of decision, the content and instructions that teachers provide to the machine, and a new trace, the conversation with the assistant. It concludes that those who decide what the platform records, what the machine answers and what counts as learning are the ones who educate; teachers and universities go on educating if they claim these decisions as their own: deliberating on what not to measure or record, recognizing configuration as teaching work, and treating data governance as a formative practice.

papers.title: You Changed Your Mind, The Model Didn't: Demystifying Intent in Multi-Turn Dialogue
papers.authors: Junle Chen, Wei Chen, Zhengjun Huang, Zhoujin Tian, Yuxuan Liu, Kai Wang, Rui Chen, Xiaofang Zhou
papers.abstract: When a large language model handles a multi-turn task and a user proposes a change but ultimately rejects it, the model should continue as if nothing changed. We find a surprising failure: merely mentioning a rejected change can derail task execution, even when the user's final intent remains unchanged. To systematically study language model behavior under evolving user intent, we introduce Intent-Eval, a controlled benchmark spanning tool actions, code, databases, and mathematics. Across diverse tasks, models are vulnerable to both rejected proposals and superseded requirements, consistent with mentioned-as-in-effect confusion: conversational content is treated as active requirements even after it has been rejected or replaced. Accuracy degradation can deepen or persist as interaction continues, highlighting the need to distinguish what has been mentioned from what remains in effect. Building on this insight, we propose Intent-OPSD, a decision-conditioned on-policy self-distillation framework with Teacher and Student initialized from the same model. The frozen Teacher provides active-intent supervision from the complete task matching the user's decision, training the Student on the full dialogue to follow active requirements reflecting user intent.

papers.title: From Virtual Persona to Purchase: The Trust Engagement Pathway of AI-Generated Influencers in Sustainable Textile Marketing
papers.authors: Muhammad Shareef, Akhter Hamid Hussain2 Hamid Hussain
papers.abstract: While AI-generated social media influencers can provide consistency, scalability, and creative control to the textile industry, there is a question about their credibility when they make sustainability-related statements. The current research investigates how the effectiveness of AI-influencers affects consumers' trust in brands, sustainable brand engagement, and purchase intention in the textile industry in Pakistan. The model combines the Stimulus-Organism-Response model and source credibility and signaling models. To finalize and validate the reporting framework, a deliberately generated data set of 250 potential social-media consumers was analyzed with an explicitly simulated approach in PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrapped replications. All HTMT ratios were below .85 and the measurement model had acceptable reliability (Cronbach's alpha = .854-.884) and convergent validity (AVE = .683-.718). AI-influencer effectiveness was a strong predictor of consumer trust, sustainable engagement, and purchase intention (beta = .497, .251, and .181, respectively). The trust variable (beta = .425) and the variable of sustainable engagement (beta = .176) to purchase intention were significant, while the variable of sustainable engagement was the strongest predictor of purchase intention (beta = .346). Indirect effects via trust and engagement and the serial pathway of trust-engagement also showed significant results. The results confirm that AI-powered endorsers have the greatest impact when they are transparent and credible, fostering trust and driving sustainability awareness to genuine engagement with the brand. This is a simulated numerical dataset, and thus the results illustrate an analytically coherent paper structure; these should be replaced or verified with real field data prior to the actual publication of the dataset.

papers.title: A Critical Study of Equity and Inclusion in Machine Learning Platforms: Algorithmic Bias as a New Educational Barrier
papers.authors: Vigdalia Coromoto Parra Sequera
papers.abstract: La integración de la inteligencia artificial en educación promete personalización y eficiencia, pero introduce riesgos de perpetuar desigualdades. El sesgo algorítmico actúa como una barrera de acceso y permanencia que opera a nivel del código, afectando los derechos educativos de manera transversal a cualquier nivel académico. Esta revisión sistemática examina cómo los sesgos en datos y diseño algorítmico generan discriminación por género, nivel socioeconómico y origen cultural. Siguiendo los lineamientos PRISMA, se analizaron 33 estudios publicados entre 2018 y 2025. Se identificaron tres categorías de sesgo: en datos históricos, de representación y de validación. Las plataformas predictivas (deserción, recomendación, evaluación automatizada) presentan disparidades sistemáticas entre grupos demográficos. Esta revisión tiene limitaciones por la heterogeneidad metodológica de los estudios incluidos. Las estrategias de mitigación incluyen intervenciones en pre-procesamiento, durante el procesamiento y post-procesamiento, con efectividad variable. El marco ético propuesto ofrece una hoja de ruta para diseñar sistemas de IA verdaderamente participativa. Como contribución original, se propone un marco ético integrador para el desarrollo de IA inclusiva en educación, basado en cinco principios: justicia distributiva, transparencia radical, agencia del estudiante, diversidad cognitiva y gobernanza participativa. Se concluye que la equidad algorítmica requiere un abordaje socio-técnico que involucre a educadores, comunidadesy diseñadores en la co-construcción de sistemas inclusivos

papers.title: AI Adoption in the Academic Context: Pain Points and Empowering Partner
papers.authors: Carlos Primera Leal
papers.abstract: Esta editorial examina la adopción de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) en la educación superior de América Latina y el Caribe basándose en un estudio de UNESCO-IESALC [1]. Aunque el 87% de las universidades utiliza IA, predomina una adopción informal impulsada por docentes y estudiantes. Esta falta de gobernanza genera "puntos de dolor" como vacíos presupuestarios, brechas de capacitación, incertidumbre ética, fallas de integridad académica y dependencia tecnológica. Para transformar la IA en un socio empoderador, se propone una hoja de ruta articulada en cuatro niveles: multilateral, estatal, institucional y humano/operativo, orientada a estructurar políticas, asegurar financiamiento y fomentar la alfabetización digital mediante marcos de competencias [2]. Basándose en la Teoría de Difusión de Innovaciones de Rogers, se concluye que el éxito no depende solo de la tecnología, sino de la disposición estratégica y cultural de la comunidad universitaria para actuar oportunamente según su realidad local.

papers.title: AI Disclosure in Advertising: Label Memory, Perceived Transparency, and Consumer Responses
papers.authors: Andrea Ganzaroli, ali kagan ozcan
papers.abstract: AI disclosure labels aim to inform consumers about advertising production, but a cue can be present and remembered without making consumers feel adequately informed. This research distinguishes formal disclosure from effective transparency through a real Instagram advertising test and a controlled online experiment with 600 participants, combining eye-tracking, recall, and exact label identification. In the experiment, Meta’s "AI Info" label increased AI recognition, perceived disclosure transparency, and disclosure appreciation relative to LinkedIn’s "cr" label and no disclosure. Correct identification of "AI Info" was associated with higher transparency and appreciation, whereas the corresponding associations were reversed for "cr". The negative serial indirect effect through AI recognition and message skepticism persisted across model specifications; the positive serial pathway through transparency and appreciation was supported only in the restricted model. Neither study detected a significant aggregate effect on its focal outcome: click-through rate or intention to buy. The findings distinguish disclosure presence, label memory, and perceived informativeness, and separate evaluations of advertising content from evaluations of disclosure practices. We position AI disclosure as a communication task whose informational outcomes deserve attention alongside its persuasive consequences.

papers.title: Use of Expert-Validated AI-Generated Forensic Images in Case-Based Learning and Clinical Reasoning Among Undergraduate Medical Students: A Two-Arm Educational Intervention Study
papers.authors: Priyanka Chahal, Abhishek Sharma, Arindam Chatterjee
papers.abstract: BackgroundClinical reasoning is an essential competency in undergraduate medical education, while forensic medicine requires accurate visual recognition and interpretation of injury patterns.Case-based learning (CBL) provides a structured approach to developing higher-order reasoning skills.Generative AI offers a potential method for creating customized visual learning resources, although evidence regarding the educational value of AI-generated clinical and forensic images remains limited. ObjectiveThe study aimed to evaluate whether expert-validated AI-generated forensic images used as visual triggers within standardized CBL were associated with differences in clinical reasoning among Phase II and Phase III MBBS students compared with conventional forensic images. MethodsThis two-arm parallel-group non-randomized controlled educational intervention study enrolled and allocated 249 Phase II and Phase III MBBS students to AI-generated image or conventional-image groups.Images were generated using GPT-Image-1 (OpenAI, San Francisco, CA).The primary T0-T1 analysis included 227 students, while 218 students with complete T0-T1-T2 data contributed to the longitudinal analysis.The intervention group participated in standardized CBL sessions using expert-validated AIgenerated forensic images, while the comparison group used conventional forensic images.Case scenarios, learning objectives, questioning sequence, faculty facilitation, session duration, and debriefing were standardized across groups.Clinical reasoning was the prespecified primary outcome.Secondary outcomes included knowledge, engagement, confidence, satisfaction, and short-term retention.The primary T0-T1 analysis included 227 students, while 218 students with complete T0-T1-T2 data contributed to the longitudinal analysis.Between-group comparisons were adjusted for baseline clinical reasoning and academic phase. ResultsBaseline characteristics were comparable between groups.The adjusted post-intervention clinical reasoning score was significantly higher in the AI-generated image group than in the conventional-image group (25.3 ± 3.9 vs 23.1 ± 4.2), with an adjusted mean difference of 2.4 points (95% CI, 1.4-3.4;p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 0.59).The AI-generated image group also demonstrated higher knowledge scores (25.1 ± 2.9 vs 23.7 ± 3.1; adjusted mean difference, 1.3; 95% CI, 0.5-2.1;p = 0.002), engagement (64.6 ± 6.2 vs 62.5 ± 7.2; p < 0.001), confidence (21.4 ± 2.3 vs 19.6 ± 2.8; p < 0.001), and satisfaction (22.8 ± 2.1 vs 20.5 ± 2.8; p < 0.001).At five to six weeks, clinical reasoning scores were 23.2 ± 4.1 in the AI-generated image group and 20.9 ± 4.3 in the conventional-image group, with a significant group-by-time interaction (p < 0.001).Knowledge also demonstrated a significant group-by-time interaction (p = 0.004). ConclusionThis study found that students receiving expert-validated AI-generated forensic images as visual triggers within standardized CBL demonstrated greater improvement in measured clinical reasoning than students receiving conventional forensic images.These findings represent an association within a specific facultysupervised educational setting and do not establish that AI-generated imagery alone caused the observed differences.AI-generated visual resources may be considered as an adjunct to competency-based forensic medicine education when incorporated within a structured pedagogical framework and subjected to expert

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION, ADMINISTRATIVE INNOVATION AND ORGANISATIONAL EFFICIENCY IN SERVICE-BASED INDUSTRY, IMO STATE
papers.authors: Glory Chimnechetam Innocent
papers.journal: Journal of Management Science and Entrepreneurship
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationship among artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, administrative innovation and organisational efficiency in the service-based industry in Imo State, Nigeria. The study examined the effect of AI adoption on organisational efficiency, its effect on administrative innovation, and the mediating role of administrative innovation in the relationship between AI adoption and organisational efficiency. The study was anchored on the Technology-Organisation-Environment (TOE) framework and Resource-Based View (RBV). A cross-sectional survey design was adopted. The population comprised management and operational staff of service firms in banking, telecommunications, hospitality and health-service sub-sectors. Using the Taro Yamane formula, 320 respondents were selected through stratified random sampling, while 300 valid responses were obtained, representing a 93.75 per cent response rate. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire with Cronbach’s alpha coefficients of 0.84, 0.81 and 0.86 for AI adoption, administrative innovation and organisational efficiency, respectively. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, regression and mediation analysis. Findings indicated high levels of AI adoption (mean = 3.94), administrative innovation (mean = 3.81) and organisational efficiency (mean = 3.88). AI adoption significantly affected organisational efficiency (β = 0.71, t = 12.84, p < 0.05) and administrative innovation (β = 0.68, t = 11.02, p < 0.05). Administrative innovation significantly mediated the relationship between AI adoption and organisational efficiency (β = 0.24, t = 5.16, p < 0.05). The study concluded that AI generates greater efficiency when supported by administrative restructuring and innovation. Service firms should therefore integrate AI adoption with workflow redesign, employee training and strategic administrative innovation, while government and regulators should provide supportive incentives and capacity-building programmes. Future studies should examine other sectors and states using longitudinal designs.

papers.title: The Role of Environmental Accounting in Enhancing Sustainability Reporting Quality: A Descriptive Review
papers.authors: Huda Ameen Oleiwi, Mundher Abbas Shaalan
papers.journal: IFR journal of economics and business management.
papers.abstract: Due to the increasing pressure from regulations and society on companies to disclose their environmental operations, environmental accounting has been established as an important tool for improving sustainability reports. The article intends to analyze the role of environmental accounting on the quality of sustainability disclosure by focusing on its trends, challenges, and benefits. A structured narrative review method was applied to analyze 46 articles published in peer-reviewed journals for about the last 10 years (2016-2026). The study finds several important trends including the combination of environmental accounting with sustainability disclosures like GRI and ISSB, applying digital technologies and AI for environmental performance measurement, introduction of the Double Materiality concept in reports, and the environmental accounting expansion to the public sector. Among challenges discovered through the review process are absence of unified global reporting standards, Greenwashing risks, and weak verification systems available, the gap in environmental information infrastructure, barriers to implementing environmental accounting in small and medium businesses, and regional differences in application of best practices. Among the known benefits are the improvement of environmental performance measurement and management, increase in investor trust and reputation of institutions, improvement of transparency and accountability, decrease in the cost of capital, and attraction of sustainable investment. The research indicates that having integrated environmental accounting systems with the capacity to support sustainable decision-making is necessary, and proposes the need to unify global environmental reporting standards and increase supervisory over the accuracy of provided “green” information with the help of modern technologies.

papers.title: Virtual Reality and the Financial Metaverse in Emerging Economies: Evidence from West Africa
papers.authors: Mamadou Mbaye
papers.abstract: This article examines the transformative potential of virtual reality (VR) in redefining customer experience within financial institutions in West Africa, while situating the findings in a broader international perspective. Using two analytical frameworks, the ATM (Minimal Technological Alignment) and CAPE (Capacity for Absorbing Emerging Potentials), the study evaluates the technological maturity of Senegalese institutions. Results show a CAPE score of 25%, revealing a structural gap between financial inclusion and digital readiness. While banking penetration provides a strong foundation, low levels of digitalization and AI adoption hinder immersive integration and delay the emergence of a sustainable financial metaverse. Comparative insights highlight that Asia, with advanced infrastructures and strong AI adoption, demonstrates how the financial metaverse can rapidly move from vision to reality. In contrast, Latin America mirrors West Africa, combining high levels of inclusion with insufficient technological maturity. These global lessons underscore that inclusion alone is not enough: robust digitalization, AI diffusion, and proactive regulation are essential to unlock immersive finance.This research contributes to the international debate on immersive finance and the metaverse, positioning emerging economies as key laboratories for inclusive and sustainable innovation.

papers.title: Employment Pathways For School, Vocational, And Higher Education Graduates In The Context Of Digital Economic Development
papers.authors: Sherzod Sharipov, Sardor Abdullayev
papers.abstract: The development of the digital economy is transforming the structure of skills demanded in the labour market and creating new requirements for the transition of graduates from education to employment. This study examines approaches to accelerating the labour-market integration of school, vocational, and higher education graduates and aligning educational competencies with employers’ requirements. The study proposes a conceptual digital ecosystem that integrates graduate competency profiles, standardized vacancy requirements, education and employment information systems, and artificial intelligence-based matching mechanisms. A central element of the proposed ecosystem is the “Digital Employment Passport,” which consolidates verified educational information, competencies, certificates, portfolio evidence, practical experience, and employment preferences. The proposed AI-matching model applies natural language processing, semantic representations, and multi-criteria scoring to assess the compatibility between graduate profiles and vacancy requirements. The conceptual Match Score combines hard skills, soft skills and language competencies, geographical and work-format compatibility, and salary expectations. The study also proposes a Gap Analysis module for identifying competency deficiencies and recommending appropriate learning pathways. The findings indicate that digital employment systems should move beyond simple vacancy aggregation toward competency-based matching, continuous employment monitoring, and personalized career recommendations. The study concludes that effective implementation requires data standardization, institutional integration, data protection, algorithmic fairness, transparency, and human oversight.

papers.title: Engineering Trust in Algorithmic Lending: Explainable, Fairness-Aware Credit Risk Modeling for Financial Inclusion
papers.authors: Rezoan Sultan, Marwan Hossain
papers.abstract: Consumer credit decisions are increasingly influenced by machine learning, but its use creates a major conflict for financial inclusion because models that are geared for predictive accuracy may encode and magnify inequalities against the very groups that inclusion-oriented lending aims to assist. This study asks whether predictive performance alone is a sufficient basis for trust in algorithmic lending. Using the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (30,000 borrowers in Taiwan), we train and compare logistic regression, random forest and gradient-boosted decision tree (XGBoost) classifiers and subject the strongest model to SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation, a demographic fairness audit across sex, education and age, a feature-ablation test and a post-processing mitigation. XGBoost attains a ROC-AUC of 0.775, on par with established benchmarks, confirming that raw accuracy is not the differentiating contribution. The audit reveals moderate but real disparities in false-positive rates, with the youngest and least-educated applicants most often wrongly flagged; we also show that naively including a very small subgroup substantially overstates apparent disparity. The assigned credit limit is strongly stratified by education and age, yet removing it does not reduce the disparity, illustrating that “fairness through unawareness” is insufficient because the signal is redundantly encoded in correlated features. Group-aware decision thresholds, a straightforward post-processing solution, lower the education false-positive gap from 0.082 to 0.005 at the expense of 0.4 percentage points of accuracy. We suggest a layered evaluation approach and contend that explainability, meticulous fairness auditing and mitigation are necessary conditions for reliable, inclusion-focused credit AI.

papers.title: StockForecastGenie Pro: A Volatility-Aware Machine Learning Decision-Support System for Short-Horizon Equity Index Forecasting
papers.authors: Chibuike Chiedozie Ibebuchi
papers.abstract: Forecasting short-term movements in financial markets remains challenging because market prices are influenced by rapidly changing economic conditions, investor sentiment, and volatility. While machine-learning methods have demonstrated promise for financial forecasting, many forecasting tools remain difficult for non-technical users to interpret and often provide predictions without contextual explanations. This paper presents StockForecastGenie Pro, a volatility-aware machine-learning decision-support system designed to forecast short-horizon movements in major United States equity indices while providing transparent and interpretable signals. The system forecasts future index levels, point gains, and percentage returns for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average using a stacked ensemble of machine-learning models. Forecast outputs are combined with market-volatility information derived from the CBOE V olatility Index (VIX) to generate plain-language signals ranging from Strong Negative to Strong Positive. The platform also incorporates confidence estimates, simple benchmark comparisons, and broader market context to support user interpretation. A rolling historical evaluation was conducted, and results indicate that forecasting performance improves substantially as forecast horizon increases. At the five-day horizon, the stacked ensemble achieved directional accuracy of 73.2% for the Dow Jones Industrial Average and 70.9% for the S&P 500. Compared with a no-change benchmark, the system reduced forecast error by approximately 24.3% for the Dow Jones Industrial Average and 22.4% for the S&P 500. The results demonstrate that machine-learning ensembles can provide meaningful improvements over simple forecasting approaches while maintaining interpretability for research, educational, and decision-support applications.

papers.title: Building Financial Resilience at HBCUs through Generative AI, FinTech, Blockchain, and Cybersecurity Education
papers.authors: Weizheng Gao, Shanzhen Gao
papers.abstract: Financial resilience has become an urgent educational priority as individuals face increasingly complex decisions involving budgeting, debt, credit, retirement planning, digital payments, online fraud, artificial intelligence tools, and rapidly changing financial technologies. Historically Black Colleges and Universities are well-positioned to advance financial security education by integrating financial literacy, FinTech, blockchain, cybersecurity, and generative artificial intelligence into interdisciplinary learning experiences. This paper proposes a human-centered framework for building financial resilience at HBCUs through technology-enhanced financial security education. The framework is organized around six connected pillars: financial foundations, FinTech literacy, blockchain and digital trust, generative AI-supported decision learning, cybersecurity and fraud prevention, and community-centered financial resilience. Using a conceptual design-science methodology, the paper synthesizes literature on financial literacy, digital financial capability, AI risk management, cybersecurity education, and HBCU-centered pedagogical innovation. It also builds on prior work in AI-supported learning, investment decision-making, blockchain education, and human-centered cybersecurity. The paper contributes a scalable curriculum model, sample learning modules, implementation strategies, and assessment measures for HBCU programs in business, computer information systems, cybersecurity, data science, and interdisciplinary fields. The framework positions financial resilience as a lifelong learning outcome and connects HBCU-centered financial education with digital trust, cybersecurity awareness, and responsible use of emerging financial technologies.

papers.title: Ensemble LLM Consensus Architectures for Deterministic Trade Signal Generation: An Empirical Study of Multi-Persona AI Panels in Retail FinTech Applications
papers.authors: Michael Anton, Jean T. Wells
papers.abstract: This paper presents an empirical study of a multi-persona large language model (LLM) consensus architecture deployed in a live retail FinTech platform for equity and options trade signal generation. Grounded in a prior quantitative trading framework (Anton, 2025) and building upon academic antecedents in multi-agent LLM systems (Xiao et al., 2024), the Edge Stack Trading platform deploys a six-persona AI analyst panel producing structured, constrained verdicts across a real-time multi-signal scoring architecture. Analysis of nine live trade reports generated between April and May 2026 reports a preliminary 87.5% directional accuracy rate across eight assessable signals in an exploratory proof-of-concept evaluation, with unanimous panel consensus strongly correlated with system confidence extremes. Inter-model disagreement functions as an auditable risk signal, and model API failures produce identifiable, recoverable degradation patterns consistent with graceful degradation requirements for financial AI systems. The architecture addresses the 2026 conference theme of Reliable and Deterministic AI for Financial Systems through structured verdict formats, role-constrained persona prompting, and explicit multi-signal deterministic scoring as mechanisms for AI governance in retail financial decision support. One incorrect signal (Palantir) reveals a boundary condition in which extreme valuation risk overrides technical alignment, informing a specific architectural recommendation. Implications for HBCU financial technology education, democratized institutional-grade AI analysis, and regulatory auditability are discussed.

papers.title: Financial Inclusion in the Age of AI: Opportunities and Risks for Underserved Communities
papers.authors: Dominique Jones, Xia Zhang
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into financial technology (FinTech) has transformed the delivery of banking, lending, and financial management services across the global economy. For underserved communities, including low-income and historically marginalized populations, AI-powered financial systems present both significant opportunities and emerging risks. This paper examines how AI-driven FinTech applications can expand financial inclusion by increasing access to digital banking, personalized financial education, automated credit assessment, fraud detection, and alternative lending solutions. The study also explores how data analytics and machine learning models are reshaping financial decision- making processes within decentralized and technology-driven financial ecosystems. Despite these advancements, concerns remain regarding algorithmic bias, data privacy, digital literacy gaps, and unequal access to technological infrastructure. AI systems trained on historically biased financial data may unintentionally reinforce discriminatory lending patterns and economic disparities, particularly among underserved populations. Additionally, the increasing dependence on automated financial systems raises questions surrounding transparency, accountability, and regulatory oversight within emerging financial technologies. Using a qualitative analysis of existing literature, industry reports, and current FinTech case studies, this paper evaluates both the benefits and challenges of AI adoption in financial services. The findings suggest that while AI has the potential to promote greater economic participation and financial accessibility, ethical implementation, deterministic AI frameworks, and inclusive regulatory policies are necessary to ensure equitable outcomes. This research contributes to ongoing discussions regarding the societal implications of AI-driven financial innovation and the future of inclusive digital finance.

papers.title: Engaging HBCU Students in Active Learning for Blockchain, FinTech, and Generative AI: A Human-Centered Pedagogical Framework
papers.authors: Shanzhen Gao, Weizheng Gao, Julian D. Allagan, Ephrem Eyob, Arthur L. Wharton
papers.abstract: The convergence of blockchain, financial technology, digital assets, and generative artificial intelligence creates important opportunities and challenges for undergraduate education, especially at Historically Black Colleges and Universities. Students preparing for careers in business, computing, analytics, cybersecurity, and financial services need more than exposure to emerging technologies; they also need confidence, collaboration skills, ethical awareness, computational fluency, and experience applying tools to realistic problems. This paper proposes a human-centered pedagogical framework to engage HBCU students in active learning about blockchain, FinTech, and generative AI. The framework synthesizes classroom-tested strategies from computer information systems, business analytics, programming, mathematics, and interdisciplinary student research. It emphasizes structured collaboration, low-stakes practice, role rotation, peer evaluation, reflective learning, responsible use of generative AI, reproducible computational notebooks, and applied problem contexts such as credit risk, fraud detection, investment analysis, digital trust, and smart financial systems. The paper presents an evidence-informed model that instructors can adapt across introductory and advanced undergraduate courses. The framework suggests that active, collaborative, and AI-supported pedagogy can increase student participation, reduce anxiety around technical topics, support inclusive learning, and strengthen workforce readiness for emerging blockchain and FinTech ecosystems.

papers.title: Using Artificial Intelligence in Accounting: Transformations, Challenges, and Future Direction
papers.authors: Tawfiq M. Abu-Raqabeh
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly transformed the landscape of accounting by automating routine tasks, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and generating new insights from complex financial data. This paper examines the integration of AI in accounting, its benefits and challenges, and explores key research questions related to AI adoption and its organizational impacts. A comprehensive literature review discusses current applications of AI technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, and robotic process automation. The study employs a qualitative methodology to explore accounting practitioners’ perspectives, highlighting both opportunities and barriers associated with AI implementation. Findings indicate that AI significantly improves accuracy, efficiency, and analytical capabilities while reducing operational costs. However, the results also reveal critical concerns related to data privacy, ethical accountability, regulatory compliance, and workforce skill gaps. Overall, the paper concludes that successful AI adoption in accounting requires strategic planning, ethical governance, and continuous professional development. The study contributes to the growing body of literature by offering practical insights for educators, practitioners, and policymakers. It also provides a foundation for future empirical research on the long-term implications of AI in the accounting profession.

papers.title: A Unified System for Intelligent Financial Fraud Detection
papers.authors: Vojislav Stojkovic
papers.abstract: Modern financial ecosystems require real-time, transparent, and trustworthy fraud detection systems capable of processing massive transaction volumes while meeting regulatory and auditing requirements. This paper presents a unified, modular system integrating four layers: (a) a blockchain-based transaction logging mechanism, (b) an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) fraud detection engine, (c) a Mistral large language model (LLM) client for natural-language reasoning, and (d) an AI agent for orchestration. A Python-based prototype demonstrates the complete pipeline—from transaction ingestion to fraud scoring, explanation generation, and immutable blockchain storage. The system serves as an educational and experimental platform for research and development, offering flexibility and extensibility for future enhancements.

papers.title: The Safety Exposure Paradox: How Frontier AI Safety Research May Amplify Cyber Risk in Financial Infrastructure
papers.authors: Abena Primo, Azubike Okpalaeze, Al Amin, Rohan Thompson
papers.abstract: Frontier artificial intelligence laboratories now publish detailed accounts of how their models behave under adversarial pressure: red-team transcripts, capability thresholds, interpretability findings, and responsible-scaling frameworks. These disclosures are widely treated as safety infrastructure, built to keep dangerous capabilities contained and visible to regulators. This paper argues that the same disclosures can function as a second, less examined kind of infrastructure: a map of where a model’s offensive ceiling sits, available to anyone willing to read it. Using a comparative case study of the published capability-disclosure frameworks of Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind, three labs operating under a shared 2024 Seoul Summit safety mandate, this paper develops a concept called the Safety Exposure Paradox, in which the transparency that makes frontier AI governable also narrows the search space for adversaries probing model behavior. The paper then traces this dynamic into financial infrastructure, where fraud detection, anti-money-laundering screening, identity verification, and algorithmic trading increasingly depend on AI systems whose upstream governance, training data, and safety ceilings sit outside any single institution’s control. Drawing on financial-stability research, dual-use disclosure literature, and recent reporting on AI-enabled synthetic identity fraud, the paper proposes a tiered disclosure model with concrete implementation steps, and a set of policy recommendations for regulators and fintech institutions managing inherited AI risk. The aim is not to argue against safety disclosure, but to show that disclosure decisions carry a financial-sector externality that current governance frameworks do not yet price in.

papers.title: Strategies for Realizing Historical Liberation Based on Historical Sovereignty : An Integrated Approach to Postcolonial Historical Awareness, Research, Archives, Education, Memory, Culture, Historical Diplomacy, and Digital Sovereignty
papers.authors: Kichoo Lim
papers.abstract: This study aims to reconceptualize “historical liberation” from the perspective of historical sovereignty and to develop an integrated strategy for transforming it into a sustainable social and academic capacity. Historical sovereignty is defined here not as the state’s exclusive authority to determine historical truth, but as the capacity of individuals, communities, and society to access historical sources, conduct independent research, critically verify historical claims, and participate in the formation of historical education, memory, culture, international historical dialogue, and digital historical information. The background of this study lies in the complex historical environment surrounding Korean society, including the legacy of colonial historiography, historical conflicts in East Asia, controversies over Japanese history textbooks, politicization of historical memory, the expansion of public history, and the emergence of generative artificial intelligence. Previous studies have made significant contributions by examining colonial historiography and decolonization, the Northeast Asian Project and historical diplomacy, Korea-Japan historical dialogue, historical reconciliation, history education, public history, and digital history. However, these research areas have largely developed as separate fields. This study differs from previous research by integrating these fields through the concept of historical sovereignty and by operationalizing the concept into seven dimensions: research sovereignty, archival sovereignty, educational sovereignty, memory sovereignty, cultural sovereignty, historical diplomacy, and digital historical sovereignty. The study employs a literature review and conceptual synthesis of Korean academic research, particularly studies indexed in the Korean Citation Index. The findings suggest that historical liberation should not be understood as the establishment of a single official national narrative. Rather, it should be understood as a long-term process of strengthening society’s capacity to independently research, verify, educate, remember, represent, communicate, and digitally reproduce history. The study further proposes a policy framework based on interconnected historical research, archival infrastructure, critical history education, participatory public history, cultural representation, multilevel historical diplomacy, and source-verifiable digital historical systems. The academic contribution of this study lies in providing an integrated framework that connects postcolonial historiography, historical conflict studies, history education, public history, historical reconciliation, and digital history. Its practical contribution is to provide a policy-oriented framework for strengthening historical self-determination without reducing historical sovereignty to exclusive nationalism. The proposed framework is expected to contribute to the development of more open, verifiable, participatory, and sustainable historical knowledge systems.

papers.title: Industry 5.0 and the Role of AI in Corporate Learning & Development (L&D)
papers.authors: Hemant Tale -, P M - Satwik
papers.abstract: Industry 5.0, articulated by the European Commission (2021), reframes industrial transformation around human centric, resilient, and sustainable systems in which people and intelligent technologies collaborate. This paper examines how this paradigm reshapes corporate Learning and Development (L&D) and the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enabling continuous workforce capability development. Drawing on an integrative review of policy, academic, and industry research, four findings emerge: 1. Rapid skill disruption, with approximately 39% of core skills projected to change by 2030. 2. A persistent technology workforce readiness gap, as organizations adopt AI faster than they upskill employees. 3. Improved outcomes when AI‑enabled learning is implemented through human‑centric leadership and social learning. 4. The growing strategic importance of uniquely human capabilities such as creativity, judgment, and leadership. The paper proposes an AI‑augmented L&D capability framework aligned with Industry 5.0, emphasizing dynamic skills intelligence, experiential learning, responsible AI governance, and multi‑level impact measurement. The findings suggest that repositioning L&D as a strategic capability‑building function is essential for sustainable human-AI collaboration.

papers.title: AI-Mediated Miscommunication in a Multilingual, High-Context Society: Encoding, Decoding, and Meaning Distortion Among Bangladeshi Youth
papers.authors: Md. Sipon Mia, Abhiaz Khan Rafi, Hajrat Hania
papers.journal: Journal of Intelligent Digital Media and Communication
papers.abstract: This qualitative study examines how AI-generated messages produce miscommunication and meaning distortion among Bangladeshi youth in a multilingual, high-context communication environment. Most existing scholarship on AI-mediated communication is grounded in Western, English-dominant settings; how generative AI functions where multilingual code-switching and high-context cultural norms shape meaning remains largely unexamined. Drawing on Stuart Hall's Encoding-Decoding Model and Human-Machine Communication (HMC) theory, the study uses semi-structured in-depth interviews with 12 Bangladeshi youth and four expert informants, analysed through a theory-driven thematic analysis that also allowed data-driven subthemes to emerge inductively within the theoretical categories. Six interconnected themes emerged: instrumental, purpose-bounded AI use; identity, authenticity, and impression management; tone and emotional misalignment; linguistic hybridity and translation breakdown; cultural incongruence and Western-centric framing; and calibrated trust and critical reliance. Findings indicate that participants primarily use AI as an editing and refinement aid for their own personal, academic, and professional messages rather than as a communicative substitute, and routinely revise AI-generated text before sending it, positioning the human user as an active co-encoder rather than a passive recipient of AI output. Miscommunication occurred most often in tone, register, hierarchy, cultural framing, and perceived message provenance rather than lexical accuracy alone, indicating a recurring risk that users actively manage rather than an inevitable or system-wide failure. The findings position AI as an active but culturally constrained co-encoder whose outputs require human contextualization and verification. The study illustrates and refines Hall's encoding-decoding framework and HMC theory within a non-Western, multilingual context, showing how linguistic hybridity and culturally situated interpretation shape AI-mediated meaning construction.

papers.title: GENERATIV SUN’IY INTELLEKT KO‘MAGIDA O‘QUV FAOLIYATINI TASHKIL ETISH VA BAHOLASH: MUSTAQIL O‘ZLASHTIRISH, BOSHQARILADIGAN KO‘MAK VA ISHONCHLI NATIJA
papers.authors: Go'zalxon Umarova
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the pedagogical conditions for organizing learning activities and assessing learning outcomes with the support of generative artificial intelligence. The central problem is examined from the perspective that ready-made answers and high-quality outputs cannot be equated with learners’ actual mastery of knowledge and skills. The study explores the interrelationships among self-regulated learning, cognitive offloading, gradual fading of support, independent task performance, delayed assessment, and knowledge transfer to new situations. As a result, the article systematizes theoretical and methodological principles for planning the use of artificial intelligence in accordance with learning objectives, jointly assessing learning products and processes, ensuring academic integrity, and developing a pedagogical research design capable of distinguishing the effects of technology from those of instructional methodology and teacher support.

papers.title: RAQAMLI TA’LIM MUHITIDA TALABALARNING ADABIY KOMPETENSIYASINI BAHOLASH TIZIMI: ELEKTRON BAHOLASH VOSITALARI VA MEZONLARI
papers.authors: Oymatova Nilufar Mirjamolovna
papers.abstract: The article examines the development of a system for assessing students’ literary competence in higher education institutions within a digital learning environment. Literary competence is conceptualized as a four-component structure, with assessment criteria, indicators, and a four-level rating scale proposed for each component. The study also analyzes the role of electronic testing platforms, digital portfolios, online forums, learning management systems (LMS), analytical rubrics, and artificial intelligence-based feedback tools in the assessment process. As a result, an integrative assessment model combining diagnostic, formative, and summative assessment stages is substantiated.

papers.title: GENERATIV SUN’IY INTELLEKT DISKURSIDA INGLIZ TILIDAGI FRAZEOLOGIK BIRLIKLARNING SEMANTIK VA PRAGMATIK VOQELANISHI
papers.authors: Lochin Suyunov
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the semantic and pragmatic realization of English phraseological units in generative artificial intelligence discourse. Particular attention is paid to the idiomatic meanings, semantic transparency, contextual adaptation, canonical and transformed forms of phraseological units, as well as their communicative functions in discourse. Using corpus-based semantic-pragmatic analysis, the study examines the use of English phraseological expressions such as break the ice, hit the nail on the head, a double-edged sword, the tip of the iceberg, think outside the box, and read between the lines by generative artificial intelligence in various communicative contexts. The findings indicate that phraseological units in generative AI discourse perform pragmatic functions such as evaluation, strengthening argumentation, issuing warnings, providing motivation, mitigating criticism, and guiding interpretation. Furthermore, the creative transformation of certain phraseological expressions is shown to reflect their dynamic nature in generative discourse. The results provide a theoretical and practical foundation for a comprehensive examination of the semantic and pragmatic dimensions of phraseological units in generative artificial intelligence discourse.

papers.title: ПЕДАГОГИЧЕСКИЕ ВОЗМОЖНОСТИ ИНТЕГРАТИВНОГО ПРЕПОДАВАНИЯ БИОЛОГИИ И ХИМИИ НА ОСНОВЕ СРЕДСТВ ИСКУССТВЕННОГО ИНТЕЛЛЕКТА
papers.authors: Nilufar Asadova
papers.abstract: The article theoretically examines the pedagogical opportunities for integrative teaching of biology and chemistry using artificial intelligence tools. It explores the essence of integrative learning, interdisciplinary connections between biology and chemistry, as well as the didactic functions of artificial intelligence technologies in the educational process. Based on a comparative analysis of the content of eighth-grade biology and chemistry textbooks, integrative connections are identified between topics such as digestion and hydrochloric acid, the thyroid gland and iodine, bone tissue and phosphorus, gas exchange and oxidation-reduction processes, and the chemical composition of blood and biogenic elements. The article substantiates the potential of artificial intelligence for creating problem-based situations, developing interdisciplinary assignments, visualizing complex processes, individualizing learning, and fostering students' critical thinking skills. It concludes that the pedagogical value of artificial intelligence lies not in providing ready-made answers but in organizing active cognitive activities aimed at analyzing, comparing, verifying, and applying knowledge from different subject areas.

papers.title: AI-Based Computational Modeling of Language and Communication Difficulties among School-Age Learners
papers.authors: Uzma Khan
papers.abstract: Language and communication difficulties among school-age learners are often overlooked in multilingual, resource-constrained education systems such as Pakistan, where access to speech-language specialists remains limited. This study developed and evaluated an AI-based screening framework using a nine-domain, 54-item rating instrument completed by teachers and parents for 428 learners aged 6–14 years from seven provinces and three types of educational institutions. The instrument demonstrated excellent internal consistency and satisfactory inter-rater agreement, identifying 25.7% of learners as being at risk of language and communication difficulties. Five machine-learning classifiers were evaluated, with random forest showing the strongest predictive performance (AUC=0.906). Expressive communication, multilingual and code-switching difficulties, and academic impact emerged as the most influential predictors, and their contributions were further supported by logistic regression analysis. K-means clustering identified four distinct learner profiles, including a multilingual-specific profile representing 17.8% of the sample that was not adequately captured by composite risk scores. Difficulty patterns also varied according to school type and medium of instruction, with Urdu–English exposure exerting the strongest influence on code-switching difficulties. These findings support the Multidomain Linguistic Difficulty Computational Screening Model (MLD-CSM) as a reliable and scalable framework for identifying learners who may require further language and communication assessment, particularly in multilingual educational settings with limited specialist resources.

papers.title: Navigating Text-to-Speech (TTS): Ethical Leadership in the Use of Generative AI for Extension
papers.authors: Xue A. Dong, Paul Hill
papers.abstract: Text-to-speech (TTS) AI technology transforms written content into natural-sounding speech, offering a useful tool to enhance accessibility and inclusivity in Extension work. This article examines the role of TTS AI in bridging communication gaps, particularly for diverse and multilingual communities, and demonstrates the importance of ethical leadership in its adoption. By prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion, Extension professionals can leverage TTS AI to foster greater connection and engagement. Practical applications and examples are provided to guide the integration of TTS AI into programs. The article also offers recommendations for experimenting with innovative technologies to improve educational outcomes and increase the overall impact on accessibility and inclusivity.

papers.title: Teaching Sustainability Through Technology: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence in Technology and Livelihood Education–Cookery to Promote Zero-Waste Meal Planning and Food Waste Reduction
papers.authors: Marilou Allego
papers.journal: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice
papers.abstract: This qualitative interview study explored how Technology and Livelihood Education (TLE)–Cookery teachers used, considered, and managed artificial intelligence (AI) when teaching zero-waste meal planning and food waste reduction. Eight purposively selected teachers at Pasay City West High School, Pasay City, participated during School Year 2025–2026. The thesis describes expert review of an interview guide, permission and consent procedures, recorded online interviews, and a six-phase thematic analysis. Experiences ranged from non-use, owing to limited training or tools, to planning-centered use for menus, recipes, portion calculations, leftover tasks, instructional scaffolds, and rubrics. Teachers described access and policy uncertainty, locally unsuitable outputs, verification work, and the risk of replacing kitchen practice with screen activity or copied answers. They also identified faster preparation and clearer instructional supports when AI was controlled and contextualized. The resulting themes linked adoption to practical readiness and visible teaching payoff. On that basis, the author proposed the PPP–V framework: Prepare, Plan, Protect, and Prove Value. Its stages call for training and access; targeted zero-waste planning; recurring checks of instructional value; and localization, safety verification, draft-only AI use, and hands-on performance evidence. These findings describe teachers’ experiences and proposed practices; the study did not measure food waste reduction or experimentally test the framework. The article recommends supported, gradual implementation and evaluation with observable cookery and waste indicators.

papers.title: Human Creativity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Exploring New Boundaries of Imagination.
papers.authors: Ganesh Premchand Vaykos
papers.journal: International Journal of Business Management and Legal Affairs
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into creative domains has redefined conventional notions of imagination, authorship, and artistic production. This study explores the evolving relationship between human creativity and machine intelligence, examining how AI acts not merely as a tool but as an active collaborator in generating art, music, literature, and design. Through a mixed-methods approach involving analysis of AI platforms such as ChatGPT, DALL·E, DeepDream, and AIVA, alongside user surveys and case studies, the research evaluates creativity based on originality, novelty, emotional impact, and usefulness. Findings reveal that AI contributes significantly to the expansion of creative possibilities while depending heavily on data-driven patterns rather than intrinsic intent. The study also highlights ethical and philosophical challenges, including authorship ambiguity, reproducibility issues, and societal perceptions of machine-generated art. It concludes that creativity in the age of AI is a hybrid and co-evolutionary process, where human imagination is amplified by computational intelligence. The paper underscores the need for developing explainable, ethical, and educational frameworks to guide the responsible integration of creative AI systems in future cultural, industrial, and academic contexts.

papers.title: Can LLMs Succeed in National Dental Examinations? A Comprehensive Analysis of Performance, Strengths, and Limitations
papers.authors: Yutong Xu, Yuanyuan Peng, Lv Dan, Li Mei, Xianglong Han, Peipei Duan
