papers.abstract: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored as adjunct tools in graduate medical education, but their reliability for answering discipline-specific certification examinations remains incompletely characterized. In dentistry in China, the national dental examination serves as a milestone for stomatology trainees. Prior studies predominantly rely on single metric, limiting reproducibility and granularity. Objective To systematically evaluate the performance of five LLMs in answering the national standardized training examination for dental residents. Method A total of 1,318 questions covering the six dentistry disciplines were selected. Five LLMs (DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-32B, Claude 3.5, and GPT-4o) were evaluated via a single-response protocol on the Dify-based Chatflow framework. Performance combined human verification with automated scoring using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems (RAGAS) framework across seven dimensions. Tasks involving question classification, key-point categorization, and instructional requirement summarization were designed to enable a horizontal comparison of models’ cognitive capabilities, assessed using inter-model consistency scores. Results DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest correct choice rate (80.90%, p < 0.001) and answer correctness score (0.853, p < 0.001), significantly outperforming the others. All models exhibited limitations, including information insufficiency, redundancy, and hallucination-related issues (lowest 44.20% in DeepSeek-R1). In classification and summarization tasks, Claude 3.5 showed higher consistency scores (186/181) than Qwen3-32B (152/151). Conclusion Evaluated LLMs demonstrated good performance on dental examination questions and in executing tasks. DeepSeek-R1 consistently outperformed the others. While LLMs showed potential as supportive tools in dental education, further refinement and validation are needed before formal adoption in graduate medical educational and clinical training settings.

papers.title: No Evidence of tACS-Primed Enhancement of Alpha Neurofeedback
papers.authors: Christopher W. Turner, Louis James, Mina Bakhtiari, Gemma Learmonth, Alessio Fracasso, Aleksandra Vučković
papers.abstract: Abstract Neurofeedback shows promise as a clinical intervention, but its effectiveness is hindered by variability of response across individuals. One factor influencing neurofeedback success may be endogenous brain states, particularly the baseline power within target frequency bands. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) provides a potential mechanism to modulate these baseline frequency bands. This study explored whether tACS could effectively enhance participants’ ability to gain neurofeedback control by increasing lateralised posterior alpha activity prior to engagement in a covert spatial attention-based neurofeedback task. Participants completed three counterbalanced sessions: 1) alpha tACS and active neurofeedback, 2) alpha tACS and sham neurofeedback, 3) gamma (40Hz) tACS and active neurofeedback. Neurofeedback performance was assessed via lateralized posterior alpha power shifts and Posner task reaction times. We identified no difference in reaction times or lateralised alpha power shifts across conditions. While participants reliably demonstrated lateralised posterior alpha patterns, consistent with the covert spatial attention neurofeedback protocol, no advantage of active neurofeedback over sham was observed. The lack of significant effects underscores the need for further rigorous tACS studies to identify the parameters essential for successful neural entrainment, and to evaluate its potential in enhancing neurofeedback efficacy.

papers.title: Verification Debt in Automated Biological Research Workflows: A Proof-of-Concept
papers.authors: Shreya Gopalan, Sundaraparipurnan Narayanan
papers.abstract: Abstract Recent biological research has shown significant interest and progress towards adoption of agentic AI systems. Domain specific agentic platforms with access to large collections of biological tools with code generation and/or querying capabilities, such as Biomni (illustrative case in point), are representative of the capability to orchestrate automated research workflows. Such platforms enable collaborative AI workspace for drug discovery, genomics, bioinformatics, literature research, and experimental planning for biologists and researchers. When such platforms are used for the aforementioned workflows, individually validating every agentic decision and the research process by which it was reached becomes challenging due to the scale of decisions involved and oftentimes, insufficient disclosure of assumptions and methodological choices, limited traceability of evidence, and interpretive judgments embedded throughout the workflow, giving rise to verification debt. Verification debt in agentic environments could result in unexpected failures and consequences in downstream experiments. This study focuses on empirical qualitative characterization of verification debt in agentic (prompt to outcomes) workflows. Biomni was chosen the testing AI agentic platform in this study mainly due to the descriptive traces it provides to track every agentic step. Verification debt is examined through two complementary angles: the individual agentic decision steps that carry claims and evidence, and the underlying research process by which the agent arrives at and reports them. This study attempts to characterize verification debt with 10 test cases (covering proteomics, genomics and drug discovery) with varying degree of biological nuance across three identical and independent runs. Verification debt is represented through 9 decision-step metrics and 13 research-process metrics, and also propose the VERIFY framework for evaluating scientific verifiability and validity in agentic workflows.

papers.title: A Semi-Dry, Visually Comfortable c-VEP BCI with Short Calibration, Conservative Idle-State Behavior, and a VR Proof of Concept
papers.authors: Frédéric Dehais, Emilio Maggi, Kalou Cabrera Castillos
papers.abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Code-modulated visual evoked potentials (c-VEPs) provide fast and reliable control signals for reactive brain-computer interfaces (rBCIs). However, deployment beyond laboratories remains limited by visually intrusive stimulation, reliance on wet electroencephalography (EEG), and false activations during non-control periods. We introduce a usability-oriented c-VEP rBCI combining low-salience textured stimulation, slow-flashing codes, asynchronous evidence accumulation, and semi-dry EEG acquisition. Methods Thirty participants evaluated the system on a standard screen using an 11-class keypad typing task. Two identical online typing sessions were separated by a 2-min video-viewing period serving as an explicit idle condition. Feasibility was then assessed in virtual reality (VR) through a proof-of-concept shell-game task involving head movements and immersive rendering constraints. Visual comfort, peripheral distraction, and fatigue were assessed subjectively in both conditions. Results In the keypad task, the system achieved 99.8% accuracy with 33 s of calibration data and a mean decoding time of 4.3 s. No spurious commands occurred during the tested 2-min idle condition. In VR, online accuracy reached 100%, with a mean decoding time of 5.6 s. Participants reported high visual comfort and minimal peripheral distraction in both conditions, although fatigue was higher in VR. Conclusion The proposed c-VEP rBCI combines short calibration, high accuracy, comfortable stimulation, semi-dry EEG, and asynchronous decision-making. Performance during the explicit idle condition and VR implementation support the feasibility of wearable and practical c-VEP systems for self-paced interaction beyond laboratory environments. These findings encourage evaluation in longer idle periods and real-world tasks.

papers.title: Patterns of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Initiation Compared With Other Glucose-Lowering and Anti-Obesity Therapies Among Older Adults
papers.authors: Julianne D. Brooks, Maria Andrea Donahue, Aya ElHassan, Jiazi Tian, Sonia Hernández–Dı́az, Deborah Blacker, Hossein Estiri, Jennifer S. Haas, Lidia M.V.R. Moura
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have rapidly expanded from primarily glucose-lowering agents for type 2 diabetes (T2D) to therapies used across diabetes, obesity, and cardiometabolic disease. Prescribing has risen sharply since 2018, especially with the broader uptake of semaglutide-based products. Still, real-world initiation patterns remain incompletely characterized in older adults with varying levels of cognitive vulnerability and frailty. Methods We analyzed treatment patterns of GLP-1RA use in a retrospective cohort of adults aged ≥65 years with T2D in a regional healthcare system from 2018 to 2026. We describe the demographic and clinical characteristics of new initiators of GLP-1RAs compared with initiators of alternative therapies, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i). We analyzed a sub-cohort of patients to identify the prevalence of baseline cognitive concerns using a large language model (LLM). We used a LASSO logistic regression to identify important predictors of GLP-1RA initiation compared to other therapies. Results Of 58,754 adults aged 65 years or older with T2D, 5,095 initiated GLP-1RA, 5,483 initiated a SGLT2 inhibitor, and 1,516 initiated a DPP-4 inhibitor. GLP-1RA initiators were younger (mean 75.2 [SD 4.9] vs 77.7 [6.0] and 79.5 [7.1] years) and less often aged 80 years or older (17.7% vs 35.0% and 47.6%). The largest difference across groups was adiposity: mean BMI was 33.8 (6.2) vs 29.7 (5.7) and 28.6 (5.6) kg/m2 (SMD 0.592), with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher in 72.1% vs 41.9% and 34.0%. Glycemic control was similar (mean HbA1c 7.46% vs 7.38% and 7.70%; SMD 0.165). GLP-1RA initiators were younger; more likely to be overweight; had lower average comorbidity index; and less dementia, heart failure, and renal disease than those initiating alternative therapies. GLP-1RA initiators had fewer hospitalizations 1-year prior to drug initiation. In a LASSO model, BMI greater than 27 kg/m 2 was the strongest predictor of GLP-1RA initiation (positive), followed by baseline congestive heart failure (negative) and baseline hospitalization (negative). Conclusion In this cohort of older adults, those with T2D who initiated GLP-1RAs were younger and had less comorbidities at baseline compared to initiators of other T2D therapies. Overweight BMI was the strongest predictor of GLP-1RAs initiation, whereas baseline HbA1c was similar across groups, suggesting that the decision to start GLP1-RA is more influenced by adiposity than glycemic control. Our analysis of real-world prescribing patterns appear to be in alignment with guidelines for Type II diabetes treatment 1 , which recommend GLP-1RA treatment for glucose lowering and weight management and SGLT2 treatment in those with risk of cardiovascular disease or heart failure.

papers.title: Respiration and individual differences shape behavioral and inter-brain synchronization
papers.authors: Wenbo Yi, Caroline Palmėr
papers.abstract: Abstract Humans coordinate their actions while their bodies and brains synchronize in social interactions, yet how behavioral, physiological, and neural dynamics interact during interpersonal coordination remains largely unknown. We investigated how respiration and individual differences influence behavioral and inter-brain synchrony in a musical synchronization task, which requires precise temporal alignment. Eighty-eight individuals first produced a familiar melody at their most comfortable rate to measure their spontaneous production rate (SPR). They then synchronized the melody with a randomly assigned unfamiliar partner under natural (unpaced), instructed in-phase, and instructed anti-phase breathing conditions, while hyperscanning 64-channel electroencephalography (EEG), respiration, auditory-motor timing, and perceived social connectedness were recorded. Relative to natural respiration, both in-phase and anti-phase breathing increased inter-brain phase-locking and perceived social closeness but reduced behavioral synchrony; the instructed respiratory phase relationship was mirrored in their inter-brain relative phase. Differences in phase of respiratory cycles (inhalation and exhalation) also influenced coordination: Inhalation was associated with stronger inter-brain synchronization but less precise and stable behavioral coordination than was exhalation. Moreover, Individual differences influenced coordination: Partners with the faster SPR consistently preceded the slower partners and exhibited an alpha-band inter-brain phase advance in synchronization, whereas dyads with similar SPR showed greater behavioral synchrony and smaller inter-brain phase difference. Our findings identify respiration as a previously overlooked factor that organizes behavioral and neural synchronization, while individual intrinsic rhythms constrain how interacting partners align in time. Together, these findings reveal a dynamic interplay between the rhythms of the body and brain during human social interactions. Significance statement Respiration is a fundamental physiological process that shapes human cognition, yet its role in social interaction is unknown. We studied randomly paired dyads who synchronized music together, a human social behavior that requires fine temporal coordination. We found that respiratory rate, respiratory phase, and the inhale-exhale cycle shaped both behavioral and inter-brain dynamics. Moreover, people varied substantially in the natural rate at which they spontaneously produced music. Individual differences in this intrinsic frequency predicted both behavioral and inter-brain coordination in the dyads’ performances. These findings highlight the active role of the body-brain connection in human social interaction, and establish causal evidence disentangling behavioral, physiological, and neural processes in joint action through respiration.

papers.title: Magnetic Field–Enhanced Docosahexaenoic Acid Delivery for Acetylcholine Restoration in Alzheimer’s Disease: an In Silico Study
papers.authors: Madhuleena Dasgupta, Amit Konar, Atulya K. Nagar
papers.abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is characterised by the progressive depletion of Acetylcholine (ACh), a neurotransmitter essential for cognition and synaptic communication. Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), the predominant omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid in neuronal membranes, raises cerebral ACh and supports cholinergic transmission, but its therapeutic efficacy is limited by poor blood–brain barrier permeability and slow passive diffusion. This work addresses these limitations through a closed form mathematical model coupling the spatiotemporal dynamics of DHA diffusion and ACh synthesis under an externally applied static magnetic field. Because DHA is diamagnetically anisotropic, it aligns along the field axis through diamagnetic torque while body cells form field-aligned linear arrays; together these effects raise the effective diffusion coefficient of DHA. At a representative observation point, 0.5 cm, magnetic field–assisted transport reduces the time for ACh to reach a therapeutic threshold by 83.3%, from 10.55 s to 1.76 s. This reduction is spatially uniform across the modelled range of 0–3.0 cm from the source, with the absolute saving growing from 6.71 s at the source to 19.21 s at 3.0 cm. Co-evolution analysis reveals the mechanism: by the end of a 2.0 s window the field elevates DHA 7.39-fold relative to baseline, driving ACh to 133.7% of threshold versus only 18.1% without the field. A Brain Computer Interface (BCI)-based closed-loop dosing framework is additionally proposed for future clinical validation. These findings establish a quantitatively grounded theoretical basis for magnetically enhanced DHA therapy as an approach to cholinergic restoration in AD.

papers.title: Identifying Register-Based Severity Trajectories in Anorexia Nervosa: Associations with Polygenic Scores, Psychiatric and Somatic Conditions
papers.authors: Mohamed Abdulkadir, Janne Tidselbak Larsen, Zi-Ping Zhang, Loa Clausen, Katherine Louise Musliner, Cynthia Marie Bulik, Liselotte Vogdrup Petersen, Zeynep Yılmaz
papers.abstract: Abstract Importance Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe metabo-psychiatric disorder with heterogeneous outcomes and elevated mortality. Characterizing severity trajectories may improve early risk stratification and targeted intervention. Objective To identify AN severity trajectories using a register-based severity index (AN-RSI) and examine their associations with polygenic scores (PGS), preceding (prior to AN diagnosis) as well as subsequent (5 years post AN diagnosis) psychiatric and somatic disorders. Design Population-based cohort study. Setting Nationwide study in Denmark. Participants Individuals born between 1969 and 2013 with diagnosed AN (N = 9,534 individuals). Genetic data were available in a subsample comprising 5,126 individuals. Exposures Forty-one PGS indexing traits relevant to AN, and psychiatric and somatic disorders prior to AN diagnosis. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcomes of interest were the AN-RSI trajectories and psychiatric and somatic disorders 5 years post AN diagnosis. Results Three trajectories were identified: “low and stable” (32.6%), “medium and stable” (53.5%), and “high increasing” (14.0%). The “low and stable” group was used as the comparison group for all analyses. Each 1 standard deviation (SD) increase in AN PGS corresponded with 13% greater odds of following the “high increasing” trajectory. Increases in BMI and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder PGS corresponded with 15% and 14% lower odds of following the “high increasing” trajectory, respectively. No preceding psychiatric or somatic disorders were significantly associated with trajectory assignment. In contrast, psychiatric and somatic disorders were more likely to occur subsequent to an AN diagnosis in those in the “high increasing” trajectory with odds ratios (OR) ranging between 1.73 and 3.81 for psychiatric disorders and between 1.61 and 5.38 for somatic disorders with a notable exception of obesity which showed a lower OR of 0.27. Conclusions and Relevance Our findings hold significant clinical relevance by demonstrating that individuals with AN follow distinct severity trajectories that have different genetic risk as measured by PGS and clear differences in post-diagnosis morbidity patterns but no discernable differences in pre-diagnosis psychiatric or somatic morbidity As the eating disorders genetics field progresses, incorporating PGS into comprehensive assessments at first presentation may aid in early identification, personalized intervention, and resource allocation for individuals at higher risk of developing a severe illness trajectory. Key points Question Do patients with anorexia nervosa follow distinct severity trajectories that are associated with specific genetic and morbidity risks? Findings In this register-based study we identified three severity trajectories of anorexia nervosa. Those who followed the most severe illness trajectory had greater genetic liability to both lower body weight and anorexia nervosa and were at greater risk of developing subsequent psychiatric and somatic disorders. Meaning Illness severity trajectories in anorexia nervosa marked by genetic risk may assist in early identification and intervention for those at greatest risk of severe illness course.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Inclusive Teacher Education: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.authors: Dr Deepika Sharma
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies of the twenty-first century, significantly influencing educational systems across the globe.Teacher education, particularly inclusive teacher education, is experiencing a paradigm shift through AI-enabled pedagogies, adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring, predictive analytics, and automated assessment.Inclusive teacher education aims to prepare teachers capable of addressing the diverse learning needs of students regardless of disability, gender, socioeconomic background, language, ethnicity, or geographical location.AI offers substantial opportunities to strengthen teacher preparation by providing personalized professional learning, enhancing accessibility, improving instructional decision-making, facilitating differentiated instruction, and supporting evidence-based classroom practices.However, the rapid integration of AI into teacher education also presents several ethical, technological, pedagogical, and policy-related challenges.Issues concerning algorithmic bias, privacy, digital inequality, transparency, teacher autonomy, and professional ethics require careful consideration to ensure that AI contributes to equitable and inclusive educational outcomes.This article critically examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in promoting inclusive teacher education.It discusses the conceptual foundations of AI and inclusive education, explores the opportunities AI presents for teacher preparation, analyses existing challenges, and identifies future directions for policy, research, and practice.Drawing upon recent international literature and policy frameworks, including UNESCO recommendations and Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education), the paper argues that AI should complement rather than replace human educators.Effective implementation depends on responsible governance, digital competency development, ethical AI frameworks, and institutional readiness.The study concludes that AI possesses immense potential to transform inclusive teacher education when integrated thoughtfully with pedagogical values, human rights principles, and equity-focused educational policies.

papers.title: TRABAJO SOCIAL EN SALUD
papers.authors: Banda Poma Boris Patricio Banda Poma
papers.abstract: Healthcare Social Work: Intervention, Humanization, and Holistic Well-Being (Volume 1) is a specialized work addressing the vital role of social workers within healthcare systems from an integrated, ethical, and human rights-based perspective. The book links theoretical and historical foundations of the profession with the evolution of the biopsychosocial model and the social determinants of health. Across three structured chapters, it explores core professional competencies, social diagnosis, and interdisciplinary collaboration; delves into support processes, person-centered care, and the essential role of family and community networks; and analyzes emerging trends in healthcare management, evidence-based practice, and the impact of digital transformation, tele-intervention, and artificial intelligence. It serves as an indispensable analytical and methodological guide for academics, students, and practitioners committed to humanizing healthcare services and fostering social well-being.

papers.title: Explainable AI-Driven Zero-Day Malware Detection Using Hybrid Transformer-Graph Networks in Cloud-Native Environments
papers.authors: Zerminey Saleem, Muhammad Hanif Hussain Khan, Farhad Ullah, Muhammad Taha Bashir
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering and Computational Intelligence Review
papers.abstract: Cloud-native environments increasingly rely on containers, microservices, Kubernetes orchestration, and automated deployment pipelines, creating complex attack surfaces vulnerable to zero-day malware. Traditional signature-based and isolated machine-learning approaches often fail to detect unknown threats and provide limited explanations for security analysts. This study proposes an Explainable Artificial Intelligence-driven zero-day malware-detection framework using hybrid Transformer-Graph Networks. The Transformer component analyzes temporal patterns in system calls, process execution, Kubernetes audit logs, network flows, identity events, and resource utilization. The Graph Neural Network component models relationships among containers, pods, services, service accounts, processes, nodes, and network endpoints. Their combined representation improves detection of multi-stage attacks, including privilege escalation, credential access, lateral movement, command-and-control communication, and cryptomining. Explainability methods identify influential events, features, and graph relationships behind each alert. The framework is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, false-positive rate, detection latency, scalability, and explanation quality. It supports transparent, adaptive, and operationally useful threat detection for cloud-native security operations. REFERENCES [1] S. N. papers.title: APPLYING GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE STUDY AND RESEARCH OF LAW BY STUDENTS: OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES
papers.authors: Dinh Hoang Nga
papers.journal: Journal of Political Science Law & Governance
papers.abstract: Background: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing legal education and changing how law students access information, conduct research, and develop legal reasoning. However, its use also raises concerns regarding reliability, academic responsibility, critical thinking, and independent legal reasoning. Objective: This study aims to examine the applications, opportunities, and challenges of generative AI in the study and research of law students and to identify approaches for its responsible integration into legal education. Methodology: The study employs a narrative literature review of relevant academic studies, professional reports, and policy documents, with a focus on evidence published from 2023 to 2026. The analysis is guided by Connectivism, Constructivist learning perspectives, the TPACK framework, and AI literacy. Results: The findings indicate that generative AI can support legal information retrieval, research topic development, document summarization, legal analysis, and interactive learning. Nevertheless, risks related to inaccurate or hallucinated information, over-reliance on AI, academic integrity, and the development of independent legal reasoning remain significant. The study therefore proposes responsible and strategic AI integration in which students, educators, educational institutions, and technology providers share appropriate responsibilities.

papers.title: Efficacy and Mechanism of Generative AI in Empowering English Writing Instruction
papers.authors: Yining Liu, Xiaomin Li
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science Education and Humanities
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence technology brings new transformative opportunities to English writing instruction. This paper analyzes the efficacy and mechanism of generative AI in empowering English writing teaching. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model and Self-Regulated Learning theory, it summarizes teaching efficacy from three dimensions—the quality of writing output, cognitive support during the writing process, and real-time adaptation of writing feedback—and further reveals the underlying mechanism through three layers: cognitive load reduction, learning motivation activation, and metacognitive strategy activation. Using data from a 12-week quasi-experimental study, it compares the experimental and control groups in terms of writing performance, writing strategy use, and feedback engagement. The results show that generative AI-assisted instruction has a moderately strong facilitative effect on learners' writing performance, achieved mainly by reducing extraneous cognitive load, enhancing writing self-efficacy, and deepening feedback engagement. This study provides theoretical grounding and practical reference for integrating generative AI into the English writing classroom.

papers.title: An Examination of Corporate Compliance Gaps in the Implementation of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act
papers.authors: Oghenehoro Evi Eni
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: The Regulation on Artificial Intelligence, commonly known as the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, entered into force in August 2024 and has since been applying to companies in stages that stretch from February 2025 through December 2027 and beyond. This staggered timetable, compounded by a Digital Omnibus agreement that has already pushed back the deadline for full compliance with the rules governing stand-alone high-risk systems from August 2026 to December 2027, has left many companies uncertain about precisely what is required of them and by when. This article examines the compliance gaps that have opened between the obligations the Act imposes on providers, deployers, importers and distributors of artificial intelligence systems and what companies operating in or serving the European Union have actually implemented. Drawing on the regulatory text itself, recent readiness research indicating that a large majority of enterprises still lack a basic inventory of the artificial intelligence systems they use, and the professional and academic commentary that has followed the Act’s phased rollout, the article traces gaps across five domains, namely the identification and risk classification of artificial intelligence systems, data governance and algorithmic bias, documentation and traceability, human oversight and artificial intelligence literacy, and post-market monitoring. The article concludes with a set of recommendations organized around enterprise-wide risk mapping, contractual allocation of responsibility across the artificial intelligence supply chain, and integrated board-level governance, intended to help companies close the gap between what the Act requires and what most organizations have so far put in place.

papers.title: CORRELATION BETWEEN PERCEIVED STRESS, RESTING HEART RATE, BODY MASS INDEX, AND BLOOD PRESSURE AMONG MEDICAL FACULTY STUDENTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF TETOVA. A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY.
papers.authors: Rida SALIJA
papers.abstract: Psychological stress is a common issue among medical students and may negatively affect important cardiometabolic parameters such as resting heart rate, blood pressure, and body mass index (BMI). Academic workload, emotional pressure, and lifestyle factors often contribute to increased stress levels in this population. Identifying the relationship between perceived stress and physiological parameters may help promote health and prevent early cardiovascular risk factors among students. The aim of this study is to evaluate the correlation between perceived stress level, resting heart rate, BMI, and blood pressure among students of the Faculty of Medical Sciences at the University of Tetova. This study will be observational and cross-sectional and will include 40 General Medicine students, consisting of 21 males and 19 females. Data will be collected anonymously after obtaining informed consent. Stress level will be assessed using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10). Resting heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, body weight, and height will be measured for BMI calculation. Statistical analysis will be performed using Excel, SPSS, or JASP through descriptive analysis, t-test, ANOVA, and Pearson or Spearman correlation analysis depending on data distribution. Statistical significance will be considered at p < 0.05. Expected results suggest that students with higher levels of perceived stress will present increased resting heart rate and higher blood pressure values. Additionally, a relationship between stress and BMI is expected, as well as possible gender differences. This study is expected to contribute to a better understanding of the impact of psychological stress on the cardiometabolic health of medical students and to serve as a basis for preventive strategies and the promotion of stress management in the university environment.

papers.title: Optimization of visibility-adaptive expressway early warning schemes under sand-dust weather considering driver workload
papers.authors: Fang Wang, Jiayue Xing, Peng Xu, Liyi Sun, Hao Yang, Jun Ma
papers.abstract: Objective: Sand-dust weather conditions severely reduce visibility and pavement friction on desert expressways, substantially increasing crash risks. Existing early warning systems rely primarily on fixed thresholds and single-modal information, often neglecting driver cognitive and physiological workload. This study aimed to develop and optimize a visibility-adaptive multimodal early warning scheme for desert expressways under sand-dust weather conditions, with a focus on balancing driving safety and human workload. Methods: A high-fidelity driving simulator was used to construct four visibility scenarios: 500, 300, 100, and 50 m, representing typical sand-dust weather conditions on the Wuma Expressway. Thirty-six licensed drivers completed 64 orthogonal test conditions combining variable message signs (VMS), LED linear guidance, and voice navigation. Eye movement, driving behavior, and physiological indices (ECG and EEG) were synchronously collected. ACriteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC)-weighted multidimensional evaluation system was established, incorporating speed compliance, steering stability, heart rate (HR), and EEG β/θ ratio, to screen the optimal scheme via Euclidean distance decision-making. Results: Visibility significantly deteriorated driving performance and elevated workload. The optimal multimodal schemes varied by visibility: 500 m (60 flashes/min LEDs + speed/distance voice); 300–100 m (120 flashes/min LEDs + steering/fog-light voice); 50 m (constant LEDs + operational guidance). Compared with single-modal warnings, the optimized scheme demonstrated statistically significant improvements at 500 m and 300 m visibility (p < 0.0031, Bonferroni-corrected), increasing speed compliance by 10.6 percentage points (to 89.2%), reducing steering angle deviation by 0.005–0.01 rad and lateral acceleration deviation by 0.05–0.1 m/s2, lowering heart rate by 4.28 bpm, and raising the β/θ ratio by 0.14. At 100 m and 50 m visibility, nonsignificant but directionally consistent trends were observed (p = 0.011 and p = 0.034, respectively; Cohen’s d = 0.43 and 0.37), indicating a practical reduction in overall physiological load of approximately 15–20% that warrants further validation under stringent statistical thresholds. Conclusions: The visibility-adaptive multimodal early warning scheme effectively improves driving stability and mitigates driver workload under sand-dust weather conditions. Tiered information delivery and dynamic LED parameters enhance information perception and reduce visual fatigue. The findings offer a cognitive-load-informed framework to guide the parameter tuning of traffic management strategies and safety improvement on desert expressways during extreme sand-dust weather.

papers.title: GenAI Adoption in African Higher Education
papers.authors: Jerónimo Paiva
papers.abstract: This study investigates the adoption, impact and challenges of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education institutions across Africa. As students increasingly integrate GenAI tools into their academic work, universities and governments are still formulating regulatory frameworks, creating a gap between everyday practice and institutional policy. The research adopts a mixed-methods approach, combining a quantitative survey of students and academics with qualitative semi-structured interviews. It examines the drivers of continued use — particularly trust and perceived ease of use — alongside the barriers that hinder equitable adoption, including infrastructure limitations, the digital divide, linguistic diversity, and the underrepresentation of African languages and knowledge systems in global AI models.

papers.title: Living with Risk: Folk Theories of AI Hallucinations Among Young Chinese Users
papers.authors: Huili Liu, Ying Zhang
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life, AI hallucinations have emerged as a significant challenge in human-AI interaction. Drawing on the perspective of algorithmic folk theories, this study combines textual analysis and in-depth interviews with both ordinary users and technical users to examine how they understand and respond to AI hallucinations. Users identify AI hallucinations by scrutinizing the AI’s reasoning process, making intuitive judgments, and conducting cross-validation, while their attitudes toward hallucinations vary. Users develop four types of algorithmic folk theories: the Human-AI Interaction Misalignment Theory, the Technical Limitations Theory, the Data Source Distortion Theory, and the Generative Rule Constraint Theory. They rise to four corresponding coping strategies: reducing communication errors, reconfiguring human-AI task allocation, intervening in data input while verifying outputs, and reducing AI’s processing load. This study further indicates how technological identity and sociotechnical contexts jointly shape algorithmic folk theories.

papers.title: Relationship between Awareness, Anxiety, and Readiness to Integrate AI in Education among Primary School Teachers in Selangor
papers.authors: Ermelinda A/P Wilson Felix, Nor Aniza Ahmad
papers.journal: International Journal of Academic Research in Progressive Education and Development
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed various sectors, including education. With the growing incorporation of AI technologies into educational practices, the preparedness of teachers to adopt and use AI effectively has emerged as a vital element for successful implementation. Therefore, understanding the relationship between teachers' awareness, anxiety, and readiness towards AI integration is essential. This study aimed to examine the relationship between AI Awareness, Anxiety, and Readiness to integrate AI in education among primary school teachers in Selangor. This study used a quantitative correlational research design. A structured questionnaire measuring Awareness, Anxiety, and Readiness to integrate AI in education was used to collect data from 401 primary school teachers in Selangor. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The results showed that teachers exhibited a high level of Awareness (M = 3.88, SD = 0.64) and a readiness to incorporate AI into education (M = 3.69, SD = 0.65), whereas their Anxiety was at a moderate level (M = 2.80, SD = 0.87). The results of the Pearson correlation analysis showed a significant positive correlation between Awareness and Teacher Readiness (r = .686, p < .001), as well as a significant negative correlation between Anxiety and Teacher readiness (r = -.304, p < .001). Further analysis through multiple regression showed that Awareness and Anxiety were significant predictors of Teacher Readiness to incorporate AI in education, explaining 48.5% of the variance in readiness (R² = .485, F (2,398) = 187.226, p < .001). Teacher readiness was found to be most strongly predicted by Awareness. The study highlights the importance of enhancing teachers' awareness and understanding of AI while addressing concerns and anxieties associated with AI adoption. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers, educational administrators, and professional development providers in designing targeted interventions and training programmes to support effective AI integration in primary schools.

papers.title: Perancangan dan Evaluasi Knowledge Management System Menggunakan Agile Knowledge Management Framework: Studi Kasus Contact Center Bank XYZ
papers.authors: Monica Ratna Andani, Dana Indra Sensuse, Sofian Lusa
papers.abstract: Latar belakang: Fragmentasi pengetahuan, risiko knowledge loss, dan tingginya durasi pencarian informasi menjadi hambatan utama bagi capaian Average Handling Time (AHT) dan First Call Resolution (FCR) di Contact Center Bank XYZ. Berdasarkan Laporan Tahunan 2025, tercatat 734.999 pengaduan nasabah sepanjang tahun, dengan mayoritas berkaitan dengan kendala pada sistem teknologi informasi. Tujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang fungsionalitas, arsitektur, dan prototipe Knowledge Management System (KMS) untuk mengatasi permasalahan tersebut, menggunakan metode kombinasi (mixed methods). Metode: Analisis faktor kontingensi organisasi menunjukkan bahwa proses Direction dan Routines memperoleh skor kesesuaian tertinggi (83,33%), yang kemudian dipetakan ke dalam Agile Knowledge Management (Agile KM) Framework. Hasil: Hasil penelitian berupa prototipe KMS terpadu dengan lima fitur inti: Knowledge Repository, Chatbot/LLM, Collaboration Board berbasis Kanban, Discussion Forum, dan modul Customer 360. Seluruh skenario Black-Box Testing dinyatakan valid. Evaluasi usability dengan System Usability Scale (SUS) memperoleh skor rata-rata 71,5 (kategori Good), sementara evaluasi penerimaan dengan Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) menunjukkan skor Knowledge Management Acceptance tertinggi. Kesimpulan: Temuan ini mengonfirmasi bahwa rancangan KMS berbasis Agile KM Framework dapat diterima pengguna dan berpotensi menjadi solusi yang lebih efektif dibandingkan sistem repositori yang berjalan saat ini.

papers.title: Navigating the Algorithmic Frontier: AI Integration, Strategic Human Capital Development, and Organisational Competitiveness in Nigeria's Education 5.0 Era
papers.authors: Mercy Oluwatosin Adeyokun, Opeyemi Jumoke Zubair, Kadir Mumini
papers.abstract: Despite the rapid proliferation of Artificial Intelligence across global business systems, Nigerian organisations have yet to develop a strategic approach to developing competency within their workforce and integrating AI into their operations, leaving them underprepared to address the competency needs of Education 5.0. This study explores the relationship between the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and strategic human capital development in the context of the Nigerian business administration and management landscape, which is still under-researched despite the transformative potential of the combination for organisational competitiveness in the Education 5.0 era. This research uses a convergent parallel mixed-methods approach, which is supported by the survey data collected from 312 business managers and HR professionals from three cities (Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt) and in-depth interviews with 24 senior executives and educational leaders. The study proposes and empirically tests the novel theoretical model, AI-Enabled Human Capital Competency Framework (AHCCF), which is an adaptation of the already existing digital competency frameworks to the Nigerian context. The quantitative results show a significant difference between organisations with a structured AI literacy programme and those with an ad-hoc or no AI literacy programme in terms of talent retention (mean difference = 1.28, t (310) = 6.84, p < .001) and innovation output (r = .62, p < .001). Leadership effectiveness is also a positive correlate of AI ethics training (β = .54, p < .001). Qualitative themes highlight ongoing barriers: digital infrastructure inequity, cultural resistance, and misaligned curricula that hinder the transition. The paper recommends that Nigerian business schools introduce AI ethics and digital transformation programmes within all MBA and management courses by the year 2027; corporate learning and development departments create structured AI literacy programmes aligned with the tier on the AHCCF by 2027, and government regulators develop a National AI for Business Education Fund to reduce digital infrastructure gaps. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, human capital development, business administration, Education 5.0, Nigeria, mixed methods, future of work

papers.title: A Netnography of Elementary School Teachers' Sensemaking of Coding and Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Devitasari Septiana Dewi, MS Viktor Purhanudin
papers.journal: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning
papers.abstract: Penerapan Koding dan Kecerdasan Artifisial pada pendidikan dasar menghadirkan tuntutan pedagogis baru bagi guru. Penelitian ini menganalisis cara guru sekolah dasar memaknai, menafsirkan, dan menegosiasikan implementasinya melalui jejak digital publik. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan netnografi kualitatif. Korpus terdiri atas 30 unit makna dari enam artefak digital publik yang diproduksi guru pada dua platform selama Agustus-Desember 2025. Data dianalisis melalui pengodean terbuka, pengodean terfokus, perbandingan lintas data, dan analisis tematik interpretatif. Analisis difokuskan pada cara guru menerjemahkan tuntutan kebijakan menjadi keputusan pedagogis yang sesuai dengan perkembangan anak serta membentuk batas etis penggunaan AI. Empat tema ditemukan: kesenjangan antara penerimaan konseptual dan praktik kelas; domestikasi pedagogis koding menjadi berpikir komputasional melalui pembelajaran kontekstual dan tanpa perangkat; kecerdasan artifisial sebagai asisten, bukan otoritas; serta pengaruh ekosistem sekolah. Keberhasilan implementasi bergantung pada kompetensi teknologi guru, penerjemahan pedagogis, literasi kecerdasan artifisial yang kritis, pengembangan profesional, infrastruktur, panduan, dan dukungan institusional yang berkelanjutan. Temuan menempatkan guru sebagai penerjemah kebijakan teknologi ke dalam praktik pembelajaran sekolah dasar.

papers.title: Evaluating an AI-Powered Learning Analytics Tool for Automated Essay Scoring in Real Classroom Contexts: An Experience Report from a Brazilian Public Secondary School
papers.authors: Fabíola Gonçalves Coelho Ribeiro, Luiz Rodrigues, Newarney Torrezão da Costa, Cleon Xavier, Jamila Lobo, Anderson Pinheiro Cavalcanti, Dragan Gašević, Hendrik Drachsler, Rafael Ferreira Mello
papers.abstract: This experience report, drawn from firsthand classroom practice, presents teachers’ perceptions, opinions, and experiences regarding the adoption of the Escreva Mais, an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered Learning Analytics (LA) tool designed for low-resource educational settings and essay assessment. The proposed experience report was conducted in a Brazilian secondary school and involved an essay teacher and a pedagogical coordinator. Both stakeholders adopted the solution through a complete essay assessment and feedback cycle involving thirty-five students. The qualitative findings highlight the Escreva Mais tool pedagogical benefits, perceived usefulness, reliability, performance, and potential contributions to student learning.

papers.title: Conversational Agents to Support Education with Emphasis on Accessibility: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Caroline de Souza Evangelista, Francisco Petrônio Alencar de Medeiros
papers.abstract: Agentes conversacionais são cada vez mais usados na educação, mas a acessibilidade ainda é pouco explorada. Este trabalho apresenta uma revisão sistemática da literatura com estudos publicados entre 2015 e 2025. Dos 301 estudos identificados, 53 foram selecionados. Os resultados mostram predominância de soluções baseadas em chatbots (96,2%), enquanto agentes baseados em voz aparecem em apenas 1,9% dos estudos. Um estudo (1,9%) combinou interação por chatbot e voicebot. A maioria dos trabalhos foca ensino, aprendizagem e suporte acadêmico, enquanto a inclusão é menos frequente. Os achados indicam atenção limitada à acessibilidade, principalmente em interfaces por voz, recursos multimodais e avaliações com pessoas com deficiência.

papers.title: Generative AI in C Programming Education: Pedagogical Strategies and Educational Risks
papers.authors: MARINA VICENTINI SECAF, Maurício Massaru Arimoto
papers.abstract: Teaching C programming involves challenges, particularly in pointers and memory management. With the widespread adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), new learning opportunities have emerged, although these tools may obscure subtle technical errors. This Systematic Mapping Study analyzes studies published between January 2022 and December 2025 to identify pedagogical uses, instructional strategies, and the impacts of GenAI in C programming education. The analysis is based on a corpus of 12 primary studies. The results indicate risks of cognitive passivity when AI is used without instructional mediation and suggest a shift from code production to code auditing. This study synthesizes recent evidence and highlights strategies for integrating GenAI without compromising students' conceptual understanding.

papers.title: What Does It Take to Research with AI? A Rapid Review of Competencies to Train LLM-Literate Researchers
papers.authors: Danilo Monteiro Ribeiro, Ronnie de Souza Santos, Rodrigo Siqueira, Breno Andrade, Rafael Batista Duarte, Gilberto Sussumu Hida, Julia Alencar, Gustavo Pinto
papers.abstract: The growing adoption of Large Language Models in scientific research has created a need to understand what competencies researchers and graduate students require to use these tools critically and responsibly. This rapid review analyzed 194 articles retrieved from Elicit and Google Scholar (2022–2025), from which 40 were selected for competency extraction and thematic analysis following independent dual screening (Gwet AC1: 0.76–0.83). Eight competencies were identified. The most prevalent was domain expertise and oversight of AI outputs (Σn = 123), encompassing subject-matter mastery, systematic skepticism, source verification, and researcher accountability. Other key competencies include metacognition and decision making about AI use (Σn = 55), ethics and academic integrity (Σn = 53), prompt engineering for research (Σn = 38), and reproducibility of AI use (Σn = 29). AI literacy and technical knowledge (Σn = 16) was explicitly identified as a risk factor when absent, with domain expertise treated as a prerequisite for meaningful critical evaluation. The findings suggest that preparing researchers to use LLMs goes beyond technical instruction, requiring an integrated set of epistemic, ethical, and methodological competencies centered on human accountability for the knowledge produced. These results have direct implications for the design of graduate programs and AI literacy initiatives.

papers.title: Quando o "Hello World" não faz sentido: uma proposta de tutor conversacional para aprender programação
papers.authors: Victor Braga, Jeniffer Macena, David Braga Fernandes de Oliveira, João Ricardo Serique Bernardo, Marcela Pessoa, Fernanda Pires
papers.abstract: A natureza abstrata dos conteúdos de computação pode dificultar a aprendizagem. Este estudo apresenta o TutorIA, um ambiente virtual com agente conversacional baseado em Large Language Model (LLM), que integra texto, voz e geração de imagens para apoiar a aprendizagem de programação. O sistema foi orientado por currículo de referência da computação e desenvolvido de forma iterativa, com diretrizes de engenharia de prompt para reduzir respostas fora do domínio. Cinco especialistas avaliaram a robustez das respostas, a qualidade das ilustrações e aspectos da interface. Os resultados indicaram percepções positivas e potencial da ferramenta para apoiar o estudo de lógica e algoritmos, sem mensurar ganhos de aprendizagem.

papers.title: Traditional vs. Socratic: How Chatbot Interaction Strategies Shape Self-Directed Learning?
papers.authors: Thiago J. Lopes, Yeshuá Siqueira, Jairo F. de Souza, Marcelo De Oliveira Costa Machado
papers.abstract: AI-based chatbots are increasingly used to support self-directed learning, yet little is known about how their interaction strategies shape learning. Grounded in the theory of Desirable Difficulties, we conducted a mixed-methods study investigating the effects of Traditional and Socratic interactions on undergraduate students learning Object-Oriented Programming. We analyzed immediate learning, knowledge retention, information behavior, and user experience. Exploratory findings suggest a trade-off between immediate performance and retention stability: Traditional interactions favored higher performance and greater efficiency, whereas Socratic interactions promoted more exploratory behavior and more stable knowledge retention.

papers.title: Scripted Reflective Prompts vs. Free Exploration in AI-Assisted Programming Learning: A Quasi-Experimental Study
papers.authors: Ana Paula Siqueira, Talita de Paula Cypriano de Souza, Rachel Carlos Duque Reis, Patrícia A. Jaques
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into programming education, raising questions about how much structure such tools require to support learning. This quasi-experimental study investigated whether scripted reflective prompting enhances learning over unstructured exploration in LLM-assisted programming. Twenty-four Brazilian high school students learned Python loops using Google Gemini under guided or free exploration. ANCOVA revealed no significant differences between conditions F(1,21)=1.097, p=.307, although both groups showed gains. Results suggest scripted scaffolding may not outperform free exploration in brief interventions, and instructional sequencing may influence learning trajectories in AI-assisted contexts.

papers.title: A Psychometric Re-evaluation of ChatGPT-Related Constructs Across Demographic Groups in Higher Education
papers.authors: Fabíola Gonçalves Coelho Ribeiro, Gianluca Romano, Sebastian Gombert, Leon Camus, Daniel Baumartz, Maruschka Weber, Jan Zottmann, Faiza Mateen, Richard Neumann, Hendrik Drachsler
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence systems offer increasing opportunities to support learning and teaching in higher education. However, their effective, ethical, and responsible integration depends strongly on students' AI literacy. This study applies and psychometrically re-evaluates a validated AI Literacy Scale among 270 higher education students in a new empirical context, study design, and broader usage scenario. It further investigates students' factual knowledge, Actual Use, Use Value, and Attitude toward generative AI, as well as differences across gender and age groups. The findings support the use of the instrument in comparative AI literacy studies and provide evidence on demographic variability in students' engagement with generative AI.

papers.title: How Do I Say It Best? What Prompt Optimisation Can Reveal About Optimal Prompt Formulation In LLM-based Automated Short Answer Scoring
papers.authors: Sebastian Gombert, Sonja Hahn, Fabian Zehner, Longwei Cong, Zhifan Sun, Leon Camus, Fabíola Gonçalves Coelho Ribeiro, Hendrik Drachsler
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for automated short-answer scoring (ASAS), particularly in cold-start settings where task-specific training data are unavailable. However, prior studies typically relied on a small number of manually designed prompts, making it unclear whether the observed performance reflects the capabilities of the model or just the quality of the prompt. In this paper, we investigate whether prompt optimisation improves ASAS performance and what it can reveal about effective prompt design. Using three open-weight LLMs, three task formulations, and English language benchmark datasets from SemEval-2013, we compare human-written prompts with prompts optimised using the ProTeGi framework. Results show that prompt optimisation yields consistent performance gains across 135 paired configurations. Linguistic analyses further reveal that optimised prompts contain more discourse markers and shorter noun phrases, and these properties are predictive of downstream scoring performance. The findings suggest that prompt optimisation can serve not only as a performance-enhancement technique, but also as a tool for identifying linguistic characteristics of effective prompts for educational NLP tasks.

papers.title: AI-Based Code Assessment in Programming Education: A Systematic Review of Feedback, Reliability, and Ethics
papers.authors: Francisco Genivan Silva, Rommel Wladimir de Lima, Thiago Reis da Silva, Mike Christian de Sousa Araujo, Eduardo Henrique da Silva Aranha
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly supports code assessment in programming education, yet evidence of its educational impact, reliability, and responsible use remains fragmented. Following PRISMA guidelines, this systematic review synthesizes 106 empirical studies published from 2021 to 2025. The corpus is concentrated in higher education and introductory programming, with large language models as the most frequent approach, often in hybrid pipelines. Although feedback is common and increasingly explanatory or procedural, only six studies combine experimental or quasi-experimental designs with objective learning indicators. Reliability is stronger for bounded judgements, such as error detection and binary correctness, than for semantic, rubric-based, or code-quality assessment. Reported concerns focus mainly on robustness, generalization, privacy, and compliance, while transparency and governance remain underexplored. Overall, the field is technically promising but pedagogically and methodologically uneven.

papers.title: Lugares de Memória Digitais: um Sistema Tutor Inteligente Baseado em RAG para a Preservação da História de Pelotas
papers.authors: Lui Gill Aquini, Marcelo Clasen Ribeiro, Marcelo da Silva Dias, Laura Quevedo Jurgina, Marílton Sanchotene de Aguiar, Leomar Soares da Rosa Júnior
papers.abstract: Este artigo apresenta um sistema tutor inteligente de baixo custo baseado em Retrieval-Augmented Generation para o ensino e a preservação da memória histórica e cultural de um município do Rio Grande do Sul, cujo conhecimento local corre risco de dissipação. O corpus de recuperação é composto por obras de referência sobre a história local. A avaliação abrangeu a qualidade da geração, por um especialista de domínio e por LLM as a Judge, e a qualidade da recuperação, pela análise dos trechos top-k e por um teste de verificação factual com informações incorretas. Conjuntamente, tais métodos evidenciam o potencial da referida abordagem para a mediação tecnológica da memória coletiva em contextos educacionais e culturais.

papers.title: Mutation-Based Error Diagnosis in a Web Intelligent Tutoring System for First-Degree Equations: A Quasi-Experimental Study
papers.authors: Alan de Oliveira Santana, Thiago Reis da Silva, Eduardo Henrique da Silva Aranha
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the use of mutation analysis as a mechanism for diagnosing student errors in a Web-based Intelligent Tutoring System for first-degree equations. The proposed module generates alternative solution trajectories by injecting atomic error patterns into correct solution steps and comparing the resulting answers with student responses. A quasi-experimental study involving 113 participants was conducted using a simulated test with ten procedurally generated problems. The mutation engine identified 70 of 387 incorrect answers (18.09%), while the guided step-by-step interaction achieved a 75.94% accuracy rate (101 correct responses out of 133). Results indicate that mutation-based reasoning reconstruction can provide interpretable diagnostic feedback and support guided problem solving. The paper discusses the potential, limitations, and future applications of mutation-based diagnosis in Intelligent Tutoring Systems.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Supporting Education: A Systematic Mapping of Digital Platforms and Unplugged Learning Activities
papers.authors: Lucas Caixeta, Isabela de Souza, Ana Hamasuna, Luiz Aguiar, Kauã Silva, Samira Silva, Ricardo Ferreira, Cristiane Aparecida Lana, Racyus D. G. Pacífico
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been incorporated into education through adaptive systems, conversational agents, and data-driven environments. In parallel, unplugged approaches have emerged in technologically limited contexts. This work presents a systematic mapping of 151 primary studies on AI-supported education. Results indicate predominance of machine learning systems and conversational agents, especially in higher education. Although less frequent, unplugged approaches enable accessibility in low-resource contexts and conceptual understanding through low-cost practices. Findings suggest an imbalance between technological expansion and pedagogical diversification in AI-supported education, highlighting the need for inclusive models.

papers.title: From Teacher Expertise to Feedback Design: A Module and Preliminary Guidelines for Unplugged ITS
papers.authors: Laíza Ribeiro, Camila Alves Fior, Luiz Rodrigues, Diego Dermeval, Seiji Isotani
papers.abstract: Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS), traditional or unplugged, aim to foster personalized learning, often relying on feedback mechanisms. However, many approaches focus on automated feedback without explicitly addressing the pedagogical criteria underlying its design or teacher involvement in this process. This study contributes to the field of Artificial Intelligence in Education by proposing (i) a Feedback Module and (ii) a set of preliminary guidelines for feedback design, with a focus on Unplugged ITS, explicitly incorporating teachers as active participants in the feedback design process. Using a mixed-methods approach, we conducted interviews with 14 elementary school teachers, analyzed through Bardin's Content Analysis, to derive the Feedback Module, and validated the AI-generated feedback through a Likert-scale survey with the same teachers. An initial evaluation of the generated feedback found positive results, particularly in clarity, motivational language, and support for mathematical reasoning.

papers.title: Evaluating SLMs for Predicting Tabular Data: An Essay on Higher Education Dropout
papers.authors: Fabricio Scaglioni, Marílton Sanchotene de Aguiar, Júlio C. B. Mattos
papers.abstract: Student dropout in higher education represents a structural challenge for educational institutions, resulting in both academic and financial losses. Although classical machine learning models are successfully applied to this task, the consolidation of Large Language Models (LLMs) has enabled new predictive approaches. This study investigates the effectiveness of small-scale LLMs (7-14B parameters) adapted via Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) compared to specialized tabular-data models. Utilizing a UFPel dataset with 6,011 records, we evaluated three representation strategies: scaled (traditional), labeled (discretized), and storytelling (narrative), inferred by the Phi-4, Qwen2.5-7B, and Mitra models. The results indicate that the specialized tabular model (Mitra) outperformed the LLMs, achieving 80.30% accuracy and an F1-Score of 0.8203, compared to 72.07% and 0.7176 for the best-performing LLM (Phi-4 scaled). The labeled and storytelling linguistic formats yielded performance levels comparable to simple numerical formatting, invalidating the narrative advantage hypothesis in static prediction. Evidence shows that 4-bit-quantized small-scale LLMs perform worse on isolated tabular tasks. We conclude that tree-based and foundationally tabular classifiers remain the most effective architecture for dropout prediction under resource-constrained conditions.

papers.title: Impact of an Unplugged Intelligent Tutoring System on Flow and Learning Gains in Physics: A Quasi-Experimental Study in Low-Infrastructure Brazilian Public Schools
papers.authors: João Carlos Herculano da Silva Queiroz, Alex Almeida Do Amaral, Huliane Medeiros da Silva, Glaydson Francisco Barros de Oliveira, Geiser Chalco Challco
papers.abstract: This paper presents the design and quasi-experimental evaluation of STI-Física, an unplugged Intelligent Tutoring System (ITS) for Physics education in low-infrastructure Brazilian public schools. The system integrates local Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) for adaptive student modeling, generative-AI step-level hints precomputed for offline use, QR-based session access without student registration, and deferred synchronization with a teacher analytics dashboard. All of these components operate on students' personal smartphones without internet dependency. We evaluated the system in a public high school in the semi-arid Northeast region of Brazil with 31 second-year students for flow analysis (control group [CG]: n = 18; experimental group [EG]: n = 13) and 29 for learning analysis (CG: n = 13; EG: n = 16) on a thermodynamics unit. The EG used STI-Física in 90-minute sessions while the CG performed equivalent paper-based exercises. The 10-item learning instrument was built from a BNCC-aligned content matrix with teacher validation. The EG maintained significantly higher flow states than the CG (ANCOVA, F (1, 28) = 4.417, p = .045, η2 = .127) and showed greater learning gains (Mann-Whitney, U = 57.0, p = .041, rrb = .452). These findings provide preliminary, proof-of-concept evidence that unplugged ITS architectures combining BKT with generative-AI hints can support science education in resource-constrained settings.

papers.title: Automatic Distractor Generation for Multiple-Choice Items in Word Reading Assessments
papers.authors: João Augusto Pilato de Castro, João Marcelo Amaral, Lucas Larcher, Lara Dias, João Vítor de Castro Martins F. Nogueira, Rosângela Veiga, Begma Tavares, Jairo Francisco de Souza
papers.abstract: Creating educational assessment items requires selecting plausible distractors that meet constraints on syllable count, syllabic pattern, and canonicity. This is particularly challenging in word-reading items, whose distractor quality depends on fine phonological and graphemic relations between words, and pedagogical criteria. This work proposes a rule-based linguistic approach for Brazilian Portuguese to support the development of word-reading items. The proposed solution uses a structured word database containing phonological, graphemic, and syllabic information and applies filtering and similarity-based ranking steps relative to the correct answer. According to expert analysis of literacy item creation, our approach outperforms the LLM-based approach.

papers.title: Comparing the Ability of LLMs to Identify Surmise Relations Between Competencies
papers.authors: Peter Steiner, Jamilla Lobo, Rafael Ferreira Mello
papers.abstract: Adaptive instruction tailored to learners' knowledge states requires fine-grained assessment that can be interpreted regarding the next feasible learning steps. Modern psychometric frameworks leverage graphs of competencies connected by surmise relations. However, both data- and expert-based elicitation of these surmise relations scale only to a limited extent. This contribution investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can serve as a scalable alternative by evaluating their performance in a zero-shot setting. Therefore, the results reveal a clear performance gap between commercial and open-source models, with Claude Haiku 4.5 and Gemini 2.5 flash achieving the best results. The findings suggest that top-tier LLMs can partially automate the elaboration of surmise relations, though human-in-the-loop validation remains necessary, particularly for semantically ambiguous relation types.

papers.title: Cognitive Scaffolding: An AI-Generated Intelligent Tutoring System Advancing Bloom's Taxonomy in Distance Higher Education
papers.authors: Mariana Nassif, Mario Antonio Pessoa Santos, Tyagi Lima, Luiz Rodrigues, Cleon Xavier, Newarney Torrezão da Costa, Rafael Ferreira Mello
papers.abstract: In distance learning courses for higher education, bridging the gap between passive reading and active knowledge construction is a critical challenge. This paper presents the design and large-scale deployment of a Cognitive Scaffolding Intelligent Tutoring System (CS-ITS). Unlike generic conversational agents or static signaling tools, CS-ITS operationalizes Bloom's Taxonomy as a control mechanism to orchestrate "upward cognitive scaffolding." The system detects key concepts in digital textbooks, anchors them with re-explanations at the learner's current cognitive level, and automatically generates follow-up questions at the subsequent higher Bloom level. This design transforms static reading into a dynamic inner loop of active learning. We report on a pilot study that involved 7,192 undergraduate students in four disciplines (Pedagogy, Administration, HR, and Logistics). The results indicate that while voluntary participation was 7%, the system achieved high user satisfaction (CSAT 4.7/5) and successfully guided 14% of the engaged users through higher-order cognitive tasks. Critically, the engaged students demonstrated gains in academic performance of up to 2.9%.

papers.title: Visual-AM: A Visual No-Code Web Tool to Support the Study of Machine Learning
papers.authors: Denis Willian da Silva, Luiz Carlos Bertucci Barbosa, Rodrigo Duarte Seabra
papers.abstract: This research presents Visual-AM, a no-code visual web tool developed using the Design Science Research Methodology to support the study of machine learning. The tool enables the practical exploration of models, regardless of the user's coding experience. Its evaluation was conducted with volunteer undergraduate students from the Bioprocess Engineering program at Federal University of Itajubá, using mixed-methods questionnaires that examined the respondents' profiles and their experiences and perceptions of the use of the tool. The results indicated a predominance of positive evaluations, suggesting good acceptance and potential as a didactic support resource for machine learning, particularly for the constructs "Ease of Use", "Information Flow", "Engagement", "Sense of Progress", and "Contribution of Visual Resources".

papers.title: Navigating the Digital Divide: An Assessment of AI Adoption Challenges and Strategic Management Frameworks for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria
papers.authors: Sani Ahmed Ibrahim
papers.journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: This systematic review examines the state of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria, identifies principal barriers to adoption, and proposes a pragmatic strategic management framework tailored to Nigeria’s resource environment. We conducted a structured search across Google Scholar, Scopus and Web of Science and screened publications from 2018–2025. 27 peer-reviewed studies and 4 policy/industry reports met inclusion criteria and were synthesised thematically. Findings show that AI adoption in Nigerian SMEs is uneven: digitally enabled firms in fintech and ecommerce are experimenting with chatbots, recommendation systems and automation, while many SMEs lack the basic digital foundations required for scalable AI. The dominant barriers are unreliable digital infrastructure and power, limited data readiness, shortage of AI skills, scarce SME-targeted financing, and regulatory uncertainty. Contradictory evidence indicates that, in contexts where data systems and managerial capacity already exist, modest AI interventions delivered measurable benefits; however, when foundational systems are weak, AI adoption yields minimal gains and can even misallocate scarce resources. The paper concludes with a three-pillar strategic framework—digital capability development, organisational readiness, and ecosystem support alongside practical, staged actions for managers, vendors and policymakers. The review highlights research gaps and recommends pilot evaluations, longitudinal studies and cost–benefit analyses specific to Nigerian SMEs.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Tools and Student Learning Outcomes in Open and Distance Learning in South-South Region, Nigeria
papers.authors: Roger Soli
papers.journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: This study investigated the relationship between the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and student learning outcomes in Open and Distance Learning (ODL) institutions in the South-South geopolitical zone of Nigeria. The rapid advancement of AI technologies has transformed educational landscapes worldwide, with significant potential for enhancing educational access, quality, and outcomes in distance education programs, particularly in South-South region. Three objectives and research questions guided the study. A correlational survey research design was employed, with a population of 1290 undergraduate students enrolled in the National Open University of Nigeria (NOUN) within the South-South geopolitical zone. A sample of 291 undergraduate students was selected using a multi-stage sampling technique. Data were collected via two sets of online structured questionnaire titled “Artificial Intelligence Questionnaire” and “Students Learning Outcome Questionnaire”. The questionnaire was validated by three experts, while the reliability of the instrument was established using Cronbach Alpha method. The data analyzed using the Pearson Product Moment Correlation Coefficient (PPMCC). The findings revealed a high positive relationship between the use of ChatGPT and student learning outcomes (r = 0.88), between the use of Grammarly and student learning outcomes (r = 0.83), and between the use of plagiarism detection software and student learning outcomes (r = 0.85). Based on the findings of the study, it was recommended, among others, that promoting the use of AI tools like ChatGPT and Grammarly, mandating the use of plagiarism detection software, and addressing infrastructural and digital literacy gaps to maximize the benefits of AI in ODL.

papers.title: The Role of AI-Generated Political Messaging in Shaping Public Opinion: Ethical and Democratic Implications
papers.authors: EMMANUEL SELOME FASINU
papers.journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: This study examined the role of social media in political communication, focusing on its influence on political engagement, the spread of misinformation, and public trust in online political discourse. With the increasing reliance on digital platforms for political information, concerns about the credibility of such content and its impact on democratic participation have grown. The study sought to understand how social media affected political engagement, assessed the influence of misinformation on trust in political communication, and explored policy measures to enhance the credibility of online political information. Guided by the agenda-setting theory as its primary theoretical framework developed by McCombs and Shaw (1972), the theory posited that the media played a crucial role in shaping public opinion by influencing what issues people think about and how they perceived them, this study adopted a quantitative research methodology. A structured survey was administered to a sample of 300 respondents across various demographic categories, analysing their social media usage patterns, perceptions of misinformation, and trust levels in online political communication. Findings indicated that social media significantly influenced political engagement, with platforms such as WhatsApp and Facebook being the most utilised. However, misinformation remained a critical challenge, as many respondents reported encountering misleading political content, leading to skepticism about the credibility of online information. The study recommended implementing digital literacy programmes to enhance media awareness, strengthening regulatory frameworks for platform accountability, and encouraging civic engagement through verified digital platforms. These measures aimed to mitigate misinformation and foster trust in political communication. Despite limitations such as selfreported data bias, the study underscored the need for continued research on artificial intelligence’s role in shaping online political discourse. The findings contributed to ongoing discussions on social media’s impact on democracy and policy interventions for improving political communication in the digital age.

papers.title: Leveraging the Potential of Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer in Pedagogical Applications of Accounting Education in Tertiary Institutions in Nigeria
papers.authors: Alfred-Jaja Stella Wellignton-Igonibo Wellignton-Igonibo
papers.journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: As digital technologies increasingly redefine teaching and learning practices, artificial intelligence tools such as Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) have emerged as pivotal innovations capable of transforming pedagogy. By leveraging advanced natural language processing, ChatGPT enables interactive, personalized, and responsive learning experiences, making it particularly relevant in disciplines like accounting education where both conceptual understanding and practical application are essential. This paper examines leveraging the potential of Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer in pedagogical applications in Accounting Education in tertiary institutions Nigerian. The study addresses the emergence of ChatGPT, concept of pedagogy, pedagogical value of ChatGPT, teaching and learning challenges in accounting education, pedagogical applications of ChatGPT in accounting education and maintaining ethical pedagogy in accounting education. It recommends targeted capacity building for lecturers, development of AI-aligned curriculum guidelines, institutional regulation of AI-supported assessments, and structured integration of ChatGPT to support learner engagement, conceptual mastery, and digital competence.

papers.title: Reviewing Legal Privilege and Confidentiality Challenges in Enterprise Deployment of Large Language Models
papers.authors: Michael Ominyi
papers.journal: JOURNAL OF LAW AND GLOBAL POLICY
papers.abstract: The rapid enterprise adoption of large language models (LLMs) has outpaced the legal frameworks designed to protect privileged communications and confidential information. This paper reviews the doctrinal, regulatory, and practical challenges that had emerged through 2025 as courts, bar associations, regulators, and insurers confronted the collision between generative AI tools and traditional confidentiality protections. It examines the unresolved state of U.S. attorney-client privilege and work-product doctrine as applied to AI-assisted material, reasoning by analogy from existing third-party-disclosure precedent in the absence of a definitive ruling on point, and extends the analysis to comparative developments in the United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia. It reviews evolving American Bar Association and state bar guidance on lawyers' ethical obligations, enterprise data governance responses including zero data retention architectures and the technical mechanics of data exposure through retrieval-augmented generation, and the growing problem of unsanctioned employee AI use. It further surveys industryspecific regulatory overlays in financial services, healthcare, and government contracting; workforce governance questions; the broader regulatory landscape of the GDPR, the EU AI Act, and the fragmented U.S. state AI law patchwork; the insurance and professional liability market's response to AI-related claims; and procedural developments in discovery practice.
