In this paper, we propose a general statistical framework for DAG learning when some or all nodes of the graph are latent variables, accommodating non-Gaussian manifest variables such as binary and categorical data in the measurement model. To overcome the computational burden of high-dimensional integration in standard marginal likelihoods, we develop DAG learning via Composite-Likelihood-based screening and Iterative Pruning (DAG-CLIP), a two-step composite-likelihood-based learning algorithm. This algorithm first solves a smooth acyclicity-constrained optimization problem to screen out misspecified DAG structures, and subsequently performs BIC-guided composite-likelihood backward deletion within the Markov equivalence class (MEC) space to identify a sparse DAG. We establish the statistical consistency of the algorithm in recovering the MEC of the true DAG, and demonstrate its effectiveness through extensive simulation studies and a real-world application to large-scale educational survey data.

papers.title: HuatuoGPT-3: RL-Only Domain Adaptation from Base Models
papers.authors: Junying Chen, Xinyuan Xie, Ziniu Li, Wenyuan Gu, Jianquan Li, Xiang Wan, Guangjun Yu, Ruoyu Sun, Haizhou Li, Benyou Wang
papers.abstract: Domain adaptation aims to turn a general-purpose large language model (LLM) into an expert for a target domain. While the dominant SFT+RL pipeline offers a convenient cold start, it may reduce exploration diversity and introduces additional complexity through multi-stage optimization. These limitations motivate RL-only adaptation. However, pure on-policy RL suffers from a cold-start problem, while mixed-policy RL still falls short: informative tokens in teacher outputs are learned too slowly in early training, and stale teacher outputs can hinder later improvement. We identify these two failure modes as Gradient Starvation and Teacher-Distribution Anchoring. To address them, we propose One-stage Policy Optimization (OnePO), which treats teacher outputs as transient guidance for policy improvement. OnePO combines Adaptive Objective Evolution to strengthen learning on informative low-probability teacher tokens and Teacher Retirement to discard teacher outputs once the current policy can surpass them. On medical adaptation, OnePO achieves 67.2 on HealthBench (Total) with only 20K training samples, outperforming SFT+RL and pure RL by 2.7 and 7.4 points, respectively. We further scale OnePO to produce HuatuoGPT-3, an open-source medical LLM series whose 27B variant reaches 70.1 on HealthBench (Total) and 71.4 on HealthBench Professional, surpassing frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra. Models and code are available at https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/HuatuoGPT-3.

papers.title: From Social Reasoning to Embodied Interaction: An Agentic Framework for Social Robots
papers.authors: Ziyu Cheng, Yuewen Guo, Zhirui Liu, Dong Zhang, Haotao Lu, Jingyi Yu A, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang
papers.abstract: Natural face-to-face human--robot interaction requires a robot to understand an evolving social situation, decide when to engage, and express its intent through coordinated physical behavior. Yet existing approaches rarely close this loop: foundation-model agents provide increasingly capable multimodal reasoning and memory but remain largely disembodied, while expressive virtual agents do not face the physical constraints of real robots, and physical social robots typically address social reasoning and embodied expression only partially. We present ARISE, a unified framework that bridges Agentic Reasoning and Interactive Social Embodiment on the Sophia humanoid robot. ARISE integrates multimodal context understanding, long-term memory, and reactive and proactive interaction to determine when and what to communicate, and translates social intent into robot-native gestures coordinated with speech and mechanical facial expressions through streaming execution. Extensive evaluations on Sophia demonstrate strong perceived interaction quality, expressive and well-coordinated embodied behavior, and substantial latency reductions through streaming execution. These results highlight the importance of jointly reasoning about what to communicate, when to engage, and how to physically express social intent for natural interaction with humanoid robots. Project Page: https://robosocial.github.io/

papers.title: Online AutoML: Evaluating Poisoning Attacks on Cost-Utility Adversarial Training Defence Strategy for IoT Networks
papers.authors: ChukwuNonso H. Nwokoye, Khalil El‐Khatib, Li Yang
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML)-powered poisoning attack vectors are adversarial maneuvers whereby an attacker intentionally inserts, corrupts, or alters training data to distort an ML model's learning process. The objective is to diminish model efficacy, instill biases, induce misclassifications, or include concealed backdoors that may be attacked during implementation. In streaming contexts, poisoning attacks pose significant risks since models perpetually update based on incoming streams of data. An assailant may incrementally introduce harmful samples into this data stream, leading the model to assimilate erroneous features over time without timely identification. Therefore, this study is aimed at evaluating the efficacy of the adversarial training (AT) defense approach against poisoning attacks (label flip and noise injection) using an online AutoML pipeline for Internet of Things (IoT) networks. Specifically, poisoning attacks (label flip and noise injection) were applied to streaming-capable AutoML learners (Hoeffding Tree (HT), Leveraging Bagging (LB), Adaptive Random Forest (ARF), Hoeffding Adaptive Tree (HAT), and Streaming Random Patches (SRP)). Under the strongest poisoning rate (PR = 1.0), AT-SRP achieved the highest F1-score against label flip poisoning (0.904), while AT-LB achieved the highest F1-score against noise-injection poisoning (0.933). Finally, several drift detection methods were used for rolling accuracy and prequential evaluation.

papers.title: Constraint-Aware Conversational Job Recommendation in Code-Mixed Low-Resource Settings
papers.authors: Md Arman Hossain, Mubashir Jawad, Fariha Khandakar Moon, Sonia Binte Siraj, Masfiqur Rahaman, Raihan ul Islam, Ahmed Wasif Reza, Nafis Sadeq
papers.abstract: Conversational job recommendation requires jointly modeling semantic relevance, user preferences, eligibility requirements, and the noisy language used in real-world career discussions. These challenges are especially pronounced in low-resource, code-mixed settings, where strict constraint matching can incorrectly eliminate otherwise suitable jobs. We introduce JobCCC, a conversational job recommendation benchmark for Bangladesh comprising 22,410 structured job postings and 988 multi-turn career-advice dialogues derived from regional Reddit communities. Each dialogue is annotated with evolving seeker preferences and linked to a ground-truth job, and is evaluated in semantically equivalent English and Romanized Bangla--English variants. We compare sparse BM25 retrieval, multilingual dense retrieval, and their hard-constraint-filtered counterparts against Weighted Soft-Constraint-Aware Ranking (W-SCAR), our multi-criteria ranking framework that combines lexical relevance, semantic relevance, and graded utilities for experience, location, education, and salary using the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Experiments reveal that strict filtering consistently degrades retrieval because incomplete extraction and brittle attribute matching irreversibly remove relevant jobs. W-SCAR avoids destructive pruning and achieves more balanced performance across the two language conditions, obtaining 37.37% and 38.43% Hit@10 on English and Banglish, respectively. The code and dataset are publicly available at \href{https://github.com/M-Jawad01/Conversational-Job-Recommendation-System-LLM}{GitHub} and \href{https://huggingface.co/datasets/Armans33115/JobCCC-Conversational-Job-Recommendation-Bangladesh}{Hugging Face}, respectively.

papers.title: End-to-End Safe Social Navigation via Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning and Probabilistic Perception
papers.authors: Tommaso Van Der Meer Andrea Garulli, Andrea Garulli, Antonio Giannitrapani, Renato Quartullo, Alberto Vaglio, Alexandre Alahi
papers.abstract: Autonomous social navigation requires balancing efficiency, physical safety, and social compliance. Reinforcement Learning (RL) methods provide a viable and effective solution but often rely on unrealistic assumptions, such as the knowledge of humans' position and velocity. In this paper, we introduce JESSI (JAX-based E2E Safe Social Interpretable navigation), a lightweight end-to-end RL framework that maps raw LiDAR scans directly to kinematically feasible control commands. JESSI enhances safety via Dirichlet-parameterized continuous action spaces and deterministic bounding, while an integrated attention-based perception module extracts probabilistic human states for interpretable, socially aware decision-making. Through extensive simulations and real-world deployment on a differential-drive robot, we demonstrate that jointly optimizing the RL policy with a supervised perception signal in a multi-task paradigm enhances social behavior. Ultimately, JESSI is able to balance high navigation success rates and superior social behaviors compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Revealing Cultural and Linguistic Variation in Generative AI-Mediated Language Learning: A Mixed-Methods Study
papers.authors: Mohammad Awad AlAfnan
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in language education has created new possibilities for personalized and adaptive learning, while raising questions about how learners from different linguistic and educational backgrounds interact with AI systems. This exploratory mixed-methods study examines culturally interpretable patterns of AI-mediated language learning among 100 adult English language learners from Japan, China, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, North Macedonia, and Bulgaria across four CEFR levels. Data were collected over eight weeks through interaction logs, learner diaries, pre- and post-assessments, surveys, and semi-structured interviews. Quantitative indicators are used descriptively, while qualitative evidence provides the primary basis for interpretation. The findings suggest broadly positive language-development trajectories alongside substantial variation in how learners request, interpret, evaluate, and use AI-generated feedback. Four overlapping feedback-utilization patterns, calibration, negotiation, experimentation, and uptake, were identified, although their realization varied across learners and contexts. Narrative cases further indicate that interaction can develop from correction-focused use toward clarification, comparison, dialogue, and strategic engagement, while substantial within-group variation highlights the importance of individual agency. Because all participants interacted with the same AI system under uniform conditions, the observed differences reflect learner interpretation and adaptive use rather than system-level cultural customization. The study therefore treats generative AI as a culturally interpreted rather than inherently culturally responsive system and advances three design-oriented hypotheses concerning adaptive feedback calibration, interaction-style modulation, and learner-controlled customization. These hypotheses provide an exploratory foundation for future research examining whether culturally responsive learning agents can support more inclusive and meaningful AI-mediated language learning.

papers.title: Bibliometric and Social Network Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Research in Dentistry: Global Trends, Collaboration Networks, and Implications for Healthcare Management (2018–2025)
papers.authors: Hossein Boustani Hezarani, Dilek Uslu
papers.journal: Journal of International Health Sciences and Management
papers.abstract: Purpose of the Study: Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded rapidly across dentistry over the past decade, yet the field's global intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, and thematic evolution remain unevenly mapped. This study examines the scientific structure, collaboration networks, and thematic evolution of AI research in dentistry from 2018 to 2025 and derives implications for healthcare management amid digital transformation. Method: Bibliographic records were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection in March–April 2026. A Topic-field Boolean query combining AI-related and dental terms yielded 5,961 English-language articles and reviews (2018–2025). Bibliometric indicators were produced through Web of Science analytics, and co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, co-citation, and bibliographic-coupling networks were built in VOSviewer 1.6.20 using full counting and association-strength normalization.Findings: Annual output grew from 69 publications in 2018 to 2,234 in 2025—a 32.4-fold expansion—accompanied by 89,218 total citations and an h-index of 108. China, the United States, India, Türkiye, and South Korea were the most productive countries. Eight thematic clusters emerged, anchored by diagnostic imaging, disease detection, treatment planning, methodology, generative-AI applications, dental education, clinical decision support, and ethics and governance. The intellectual base centred on clinical-AI researchers and foundational computer-vision methodologists.Conclusions: AI research in dentistry has matured from a narrow technical niche into a globally distributed field increasingly intertwined with healthcare digitalization. The findings may inform managerial and policy discussions on AI integration in oral healthcare and provide an evidence base for researchers, healthcare managers, and policymakers, rather than a direct assessment of AI implementation.

papers.title: Diagnosis of olfactory dysfunction in chronic rhinosinusitis – a case report and literature review
papers.authors: Oleksii Vorobiov, Karla Janoušková, Kristýna Mamiňák, Libor Vasina, Petra Dytrych, Nikola Pastorkova, Daniel Kovář, Jaromı́r Astl, Richard Holý
papers.abstract: Olfaction dysfunction is often underestimated in common medical practice. However, it can seriously affect an individual‘s quality of life. Its incidence has increased in the era of the COVID-19 pandemic. The most common sinonasal cause of olfactory dysfunction is chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS). Olfactory dysfunction is a characteristic symptom and is part of the definition of CRS. In this review article, we will focus on both the presentation of two case reports in subjects with CRS and olfactory dysfunction and on current knowledge regarding the comprehensive diagnosis of olfactory dysfunction in CRS. Subjective smell tests are still the gold standard in the diagnosis of olfactory dysfunction in CRS because of their simplicity and accessibility. Special consideration is also given to new objective electrophysiological olfactory tests such as olfactory and trigeminal event-related potentials, which objectively diagnose olfactory and trigeminal pathway function. Their importance in the diagnosis of olfactory dysfunction, not only in CRS, has recently increased. They are already part of the examination algorithms of olfactory dysfunction in some departments. In the era of development of new therapies for CRS such as biological therapy, the importance of objective olfactory tests can be expected to increase.

papers.title: Towards a Reliable and Sustainable RAG-Supported LLM System for Better Understanding of Atatürk’s Principles: AtamQAS
papers.authors: Enis Karaarslan, Ahmet Yusuf Alan, Serhat Kumbalı, Ömer Aydın
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLM) have become one of today’s current and popular technologies. One of the areas where these models are used is the education domain. However, due to the nature of these models, there are some problems such as hallucinations. Some technical studies are being carried out to eliminate or minimize this problem. In this study, we proposed a more reliable structure to be used in the education of the revolutions and principles of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder of modern Türkiye. In this structure, we used Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture and a unique dataset we created specifically for the field. We enabled the comparison of our tool, which we named AtamQAS, with general-purpose artificial intelligence tools by experts in the field. The results showed that AtamQAS produced more reliable outputs than general-purpose artificial intelligence tools.

papers.title: Navigating Generative AI in Higher Education: Mining Engineering Students’ Practices, Perceptions, and Language Choices
papers.authors: Marija M. Đorđević
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science Research and Review
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has rapidly become an everyday academic resource, making students’ actual practices increasingly important for higher-education policy and pedagogy. This small-scale exploratory survey study examines familiarity with, frequency and purposes of use of, attitudes toward, verification practices, and language choices in GenAI among 30 second-year undergraduate students from Mining Engineering, Petroleum Engineering and Environmental Engineering programmes at the Faculty of Mining and Geology University of Belgrade. For the purposes of the study, the term Mining Engineering students is used as a departmental umbrella term encompassing these three distinct study programmes. Data were collected through an anonymous paper-based questionnaire combining closed-ended, multiple-response, Likert-type, and open-ended items. Descriptive statistics were complemented by exploratory respondent-level comparisons using Fisher’s exact tests, Mann–Whitney U tests, and Spearman’s rank correlation where appropriate. Twenty students (66.7%) used AI several times per week or almost every day; 21 (70.0%) used it for solving tasks or problems and 17 (56.7%) for understanding course content. Twenty-five students (83.3%) reported asking follow-up questions to obtain more precise information, while 10 of 28 valid respondents (35.7%) checked AI-generated information often or almost always. Open responses primarily emphasised speed and efficiency as benefits and inaccuracy or unreliability as limitations. Language use was flexible: Serbian was prominent, but English and bilingual interaction were also common. Higher self-reported English proficiency was strongly associated with English-involved AI use in an exploratory Fisher’s exact test (p < .001). The findings suggest pragmatic rather than uncritical GenAI adoption and point to the need for discipline-sensitive AI literacy, transparent institutional guidance, and explicit attention to multilingual AI interaction in higher education.

papers.title: Sun’iy intellekt sharoitida parlament nazorati: axborot asimmetriyasi va huquqiy mexanizmlar
papers.authors: Гульбахор Саидова, Гульбахор Саидова, Gulbahor Saidova
papers.abstract: The article examines the impact of artificial intelligence technologies on parliamentary oversight from legal and institutional perspectives. AI is considered, on the one hand, as a tool for analysing large volumes of budgetary, reporting and statistical data and, on the other, as an object of parliamentary oversight when deployed by executive authorities. Drawing on the experience of Brazil, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Canada, the study explores the role of supreme audit institutions, registers of algorithmic systems, impact assessments and transparency mechanisms. The analysis of national legislation identifies several legal gaps concerning access to machine-readable data, disclosure of AI systems used by public authorities, rules governing the use of AI within parliament, and data protection safeguards.

papers.title: Maktabgacha ta’lim tashkilotlarida raqamli boshqaruv va ta’lim sifatini monitoring qilish istiqbollari
papers.authors: Gulasal Abdukunduzovna Berdalieva, Gulasal Abdukunduzovna Berdalieva, Gulasal Berdaliyeva
papers.abstract: This article examines the prospects for developing digital management in preschool educational institutions and monitoring educational quality through modern digital technologies. It substantiates the need to integrate traditional approaches to preschool management with electronic data, digital monitoring, automated analysis, rating systems, and performance indicators in the context of digital transformation. The article explores the concept of digital management and its potential for monitoring the activities of preschool educational institutions, with particular attention to the digital competence of institutional leaders, electronic tracking of educational quality indicators, analysis of teachers’ performance, monitoring of children’s developmental progress, and digital collaboration with parents. The study also examines Uzbekistan’s experience in using digital platforms for the comprehensive assessment of preschool educational institutions and outlines the potential applications of artificial intelligence, big data, automated analytical systems, and real-time monitoring tools in the future.

papers.title: Penguatan Literasi Digital melalui Pelatihan Memilah Realitas dan Disinformasi di Era Pendidikan Modern bagi Mahasiswa Universitas Ummul Quro Al-Islami
papers.authors: Siti Lutfi Latifah, Tinta Ilmiati, Nurananda Nurananda
papers.abstract: The rapid development of digital technology and the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) have transformed the way university students access, process, and distribute information. On the other hand, the high flow of digital information has also increased the risk of spreading hoaxes, misinformation, and disinformation that could potentially affect the quality of learning and academic integrity. This community service activity aims to strengthen students' digital literacy through training in distinguishing reality from disinformation in the era of modern education. The activity was conducted at the invitation of the Student Association of the Islamic Education Management Study Program (HMPS MPI) at Ummul Quro Al-Islami University, involving 60 students from various study programs and universities. The implementation method used a participatory approach comprising the stages of preparation, pre-test, material delivery, interactive discussion, AI-assisted fact-checking practice, post-test, and reflection. The results of the activity show that the training was able to improve participants' understanding of digital literacy as a multidimensional competency, strengthen their ability to differentiate between hoaxes, misinformation, and disinformation, and build awareness that AI is a tool (assistant) in the process of information verification, rather than the determinant of truth. In addition, participants demonstrated a better understanding of the importance of critical thinking, a culture of information verification (digital tabayyun), and academic integrity in building a healthy digital ecosystem. This community service activity confirms that strengthening digital literacy based on the use of AI and fact-checking is a relevant strategy for shaping students into critical, responsible, and adaptive digital citizens in facing the challenges of information in the era of modern education.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Smart and Sustainable Higher Education Campuses
papers.authors: Saikh Mamun Rasid, Keshab Chandra Mohapatra, Diptesh Kumar Rout, Santosh Sethi, Priyanka Shit
papers.journal: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
papers.abstract: Higher education campuses are widely recognized as entities that consume substantial amounts of energy, water, and other resources while also producing significant amounts of waste and emissions from transport activities. At the same time, conventional approaches to managing campuses are largely manual and rigid, thus limiting opportunities to ensure that resources are used as efficiently as possible. In this regard, artificial intelligence (AI) can be considered a disruptive force that can be leveraged to predict, classify, forecast, optimize, and manage resources and processes. This study aims to identify how AI has been applied in studies concerned with campuses, with a focus on energy, water, waste, transportation, and building management. The results of the reviewed articles provide evidence that AI can contribute to predicting energy consumption, optimizing the use of resources, classifying waste, managing transportation, and operating buildings in ways that reduce the consumption of resources and carbon emissions. At the same time, the reviewed articles also highlight the limitations of using AI in these areas, including the availability of data, privacy, security issues, compatibility problems, costs, and the very nature of AI decision-making. Based on these findings, a conceptual framework is provided in this paper, which highlights the potential application of AI across five key areas of campus sustainability and their relationship with environmental outcomes.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation(TMS) for Autism Spectrum Disorder
papers.authors: Bahman Zohuri, Sana Fadavi
papers.journal: Japan Journal of Clinical & Medical Research
papers.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by impairments in social communication, repetitive behaviors, sensory processing abnormalities, and variable cognitive deficits. Despite significant advances in behavioral therapies and pharmacological interventions, effective treatments capable of directly modulating dysfunctional neural networks remain limited. Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) has emerged as a promising non-invasive neuromodulation technique that can alter cortical excitability, enhance neuroplasticity, and potentially improve cognitive and behavioral outcomes. Simultaneously, recent developments in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Digital Twin technologies have created new opportunities to personalize TMS protocols using multimodal patient data, including structural and functional neuroimaging, electroencephalography (EEG), behavioral assessments, genetic information, and longitudinal clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Factors Associated with Chronic Ankle Instability Among Saudi Arabian Male Volleyball Players: A Cross-sectional Study
papers.authors: Mahamed Ateef
papers.abstract: Background: Chronic ankle instability (CAI) is a common long term consequence of lateral ankle sprains and is characterised by persistent symptoms, perceived ankle instability, and functional deficits that impair athletic performance. Volleyball players are extremely vulnerable to ankle injuries due to frequent jumping, landing, and rapid directional changes during play. However, the factors associated with CAI in this athletic population—especially in Saudi Arabia—remain underexplored. Objective: This study aimed to investigate the association between Cumberland Ankle Instability Tool (CAIT) scores and selected demographic, training-related, and clinical variables among male professional volleyball players in Saudi Arabia. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 117 male professional volleyball players, recruited through cluster sampling from multiple volleyball clubs across the country. Participants provided demographic, anthropometric, and training-related information. CAI was assessed using the validated Arabic version of the CAIT. Spearman’s correlation was used to examine associations between CAIT scores and selected variables, while multiple linear regression identified independent factors of CAIT scores. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05. Results: The mean age of participants was 25.76±3.72 years, and the mean BMI was 23.53±3.05 kg/m². Players reported an average of 5.11±2.47 years of training experience and trained approximately 2.09±0.93 hours per day. Limb dominance scores (1.27±0.45) indicated predominant right-sided dominance. CAIT scores are significantly associated with previous ankle instability (ρ = 0.031, p<0.01) and reinjury (ρ = 0.046, p<0.01). However, the direction of these associations should be interpreted in relation to how the binary injury-history variable is coded and the scoring direction of CAIT. The regression model was significant (F (10,117) = 167.66, p<0.001), explaining 83.5% of the variance (R² = 0.835). Previous ankle instability (β = 0.72, p<0.001), age (β = 0.07, p = 0.002), and reinjury (β = 0.17, p = 0.006) emerged as significant predictors. Age, prior ankle instability, and reinjury were significantly associated with CAI among Saudi male volleyball players. Conclusion: These findings support the crucial need for targeted prevention strategies and structured neuromuscular rehabilitation following initial ankle sprains to reduce chronicity and recurrent injury in this population.

papers.title: Age-Related Differences in Glycemic Control, Management Practices, and Complications Among Adolescents and Young Adults with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
papers.authors: Mai A. Ahmed, Hajer Saleh Alshammari, Danah Khalid S. Althubyani, Aldanah Yahya Alkhaled, Mona M. Shahien, M. R. Mahmoud, Somaia Ibrahim, Manal Zayed Ali Alshammari, Bishriyyah Sayah Alshammari
papers.abstract: Background: Adolescence and young adulthood are high-risk phases in type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). Age-related differences in glycemic control, insulin practices, complications, and comorbidities remain insufficiently characterized. This study compared glycemic control, management practices, complications, and comorbidities between adolescents and young adults with T1DM in Hail, Saudi Arabia. Subjects & Methods: In this cross-sectional study, we recruited 302 participants with T1DM from endocrinology outpatient clinics in the Hail region: 152 adolescents aged 10–18 years and 150 young adults aged 19–35 years. Data was collected through interviews and medical record review. Clinical, behavioral, and metabolic variables were compared between groups. Results: Adolescents had poorer glycemic control, with HbA1c ≥9.1% more common than in young adults (28.9% vs 15.3%, p<0.001), despite their higher use of continuous glucose monitoring (89.5% vs 76.0%, p=0.001). Young adults had higher BMI (26.38±4.79 vs. 21.45±5.62, p<0.001), higher rates of overweight/obesity, greater insulin omission (28% vs. 16.4%, p=0.043), and higher rates of recurrent hypoglycemia (>3 episodes: 52.0% vs. 27.6%, p<0.001). Chronic complications and psychological comorbidities were also more frequent in young adults. Conclusions: Distinct age-related risk profiles were identified among individuals with T1DM. Adolescents were particularly vulnerable to poor glycemic control despite greater use of modern monitoring devices, whereas young adults carried a greater burden of insulin omission, obesity, recurrent hypoglycemia, chronic complications, and psychological comorbidities. These findings support age-specific multidisciplinary interventions and structured transition care to improve long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Digital transformation and universities
papers.authors: Carlos Alberto Rios-Campos, Rosa Felicita Gonzáles Llontop, Evelyn Carolina Palma Severino, Walter Bernardo Símpalo López, Elmer Daniel Tejada Velásquez, Doris Elena Delgado Tapia, Agustín Roberto Mendoza Alfaro, Walter Julio Columna Rafael, Deicy Torres Hurtado, Mariela Núñez Figueroa
papers.abstract: The general objective of the research was to determine the advances related to digital transformation and universities. The specific objective of the research was to identify the best global universities that use digital transformation. Methodology, in this research, 33 documents have been selected, carried out in the period 2018 - 2026; including: scientific articles, review articles and information from websites of recognized organizations. Results, digital transformation has a positive impact on universities worldwide and is becoming an outstanding challenge in our Latin American countries. Digital transformation offers great opportunities and challenges to organizations, especially those in higher education, providing them with tools to fulfill their mission. Universities play an important role in society. With the rise of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, their impact and the new challenges they face must be evaluated. Conclusions, about the general objective of the research, universities are undergoing a process of digital transformation; therefore, they need to invest in infrastructure, technology, innovation, and staff training in order to become digital universities. About the specific objective of the research, top three universities for digital education: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT Sloan School of Management), Harvard University (Harvard Business School) and University of Cambridge (Judge Business School).

papers.title: Gentle Algorithms and Educational Relationships
papers.authors: Kunqi Ji, Zekun Liu
papers.journal: International Journal of AI in Pedagogy Innovation and Learning Futures
papers.abstract: When AI learns to imitate the way your favorite teacher, deceased relative, or ex-partner speaks, it can offer unconditional gentle responses—but is this gentleness genuine companionship or a refined substitution? Artificial intelligence emotional simulation learns the tone, attitude, and response patterns of specific others through data, providing students with stable and controllable emotional support. It may alleviate loneliness, yet it may also replace real others with simulacra, hollowing out educational relationships. Existing research oscillates between technological optimism and ethical critique, overlooking the conditionality of its educational consequences. Drawing on relational ethics, simulacra theory, and educational phenomenology, this paper develops a "supplementary–substitutional" analytical framework, examining its impact along four dimensions: degree of substitution, transparency, exitability, and subject generation. It argues that AI emotional simulation is neither intrinsically good nor bad: under supplementary, transparent, exit-friendly conditions that serve subject generation, it can become a resource for educational emotional support; only under conditions that replace real others, operate covertly, preclude exit, and dissolve subject generation does it constitute an ethical dilemma. The discussion shifts from "judgments of good or bad" to "analysis of conditions," providing a theoretical tool for research on educational relationships and AI ethics.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence For Adaptive Pedagogical Scenario Design In E-Learning : Roles, Challenges And Perspectives
papers.authors: Chelliq Ikram, Lamya Anoir, Mohamed Khaldi
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming the design and delivery of digital learning environments. At the same time, adaptive e-learning seeks to move beyond the traditional one-size-fits-all approach by dynamically adapting learning resources, activities and pathways to learner characteristics and needs. In such environments, pedagogical scenarization represents a fundamental process because it organizes pedagogical activities, learning objects, interactions and assessments according to defined learning objectives. However, the design of adaptive pedagogical scenarios remains a complex and time-consuming task that traditionally depends heavily on teachers and instructional designers. This theoretical article examines the potential role of AI in the scenarization of adaptive pedagogical objects for adaptive e-learning. It first clarifies the concepts of Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, adaptive e-learning, pedagogical objects and pedagogical scenarization. It then analyzes the different roles that AI can play throughout the scenario design process, including learner-profile analysis, learning-objective interpretation, activity generation, pedagogical-object selection, scenario generation, adaptation, personalization, assessment and feedback generation. The article further examines the relationship between human expertise and AI capabilities and discusses whether AI can replace human intervention in pedagogical scenarization. Based on this analysis, a conceptual Human-AI Adaptive Scenarization Framework is proposed. The framework positions AI as an intelligent assistant capable of generating and adapting pedagogical scenarios while maintaining human pedagogical supervision and validation. Finally, the article discusses the opportunities, limitations, ethical issues and future research directions associated with AI-assisted adaptive scenarization.

papers.title: Teaching Data Cleaning in Machine Learning: A Misconception-Driven Pedagogical Framework for Explainable and Ethical Data Preprocessing
papers.authors: Feyzi Kaysi, Serdar Yilmaz, Canan Akay
papers.journal: International journal of Technology in Education Science
papers.abstract: Data cleaning — the process of detecting and remedying missing, erroneous, and inconsistent records in raw datasets — is widely recognized as the most time-consuming and consequential stage of the machine learning preprocessing pipeline. Yet despite its operational centrality, how data cleaning should be taught to undergraduate computer science students has received remarkably little systematic attention in the machine learning education literature. This paper addresses that gap by developing a theoretically grounded pedagogical framework for instructors teaching data cleaning in higher education contexts. Drawing on threshold concept theory, constructivist learning principles, and the documented landscape of machine learning education challenges, we identify three pervasive misconceptions: the deletion reflex, the imputation neutrality fallacy, and the outlier criminalization fallacy. We propose a four-phase instructional sequence — Motivational Grounding, Mechanism Diagnosis, Algorithm-Context Mapping, and Explainability and Ethical Reflection — operationalized through a multi-dimensional Instructor Cleaning Strategy Matrix. The framework is empirically grounded through a case study applying the full technique repertoire to a real-world academic email dataset of over 10,000 records spanning eleven years. A cross-method comparison demonstrates that imputation methods produced NRMSE values ranging from 0.08 to 0.45, and anomaly detection methods flagged between 185 and 412 records on identical data. Implications for machine learning curriculum design, assessment, and data ethics literacy are discussed. By embedding explainability and ethical reflection as a mandatory fourth phase of instruction — grounded in GDPR, the EU AI Act, and ISO 8000 requirements — the framework equips learners to navigate the data governance demands of contemporary technology-enhanced professional environments.

papers.title: Professional Development Needs of Physics Teachers in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Afam Uzorka, Kagezi Kalabuki
papers.journal: International journal of Technology in Education Science
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming educational practice, creating new opportunities and challenges for teachers. This study explored the professional development needs of secondary school physics teachers for effective AI integration in Kampala, Uganda. A qualitative descriptive research design was adopted, involving 22 purposively selected physics teachers with experience in digital technologies and awareness of AI applications. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. Six themes emerged: awareness and understanding of AI, current use of AI in physics teaching, barriers to AI adoption, required AI competencies, professional development priorities, and institutional support needs. The findings revealed that although teachers recognized the potential of AI to enhance lesson preparation, assessment, and conceptual understanding, they lacked adequate knowledge, practical skills, and institutional support for effective classroom implementation. Participants emphasized the need for continuous, practical, subject-specific professional development focusing on AI literacy, pedagogical integration, ethical considerations, and prompt engineering. The study concludes that effective AI integration requires coordinated investments in teacher capacity building, supportive institutional policies, technological infrastructure, and sustained professional learning opportunities.

papers.title: AI-Facilitated Formative Feedback and Students’ Classroom Engagement: A Review of Pedagogical Integration, Learning Outcomes, and Teacher-Student Interaction Dynamics
papers.authors: Zahoor Hassan, Junchao Zhang, Kamran Zaib, Sajjad Hussain, Saba Ahmad
papers.journal: International journal of Technology in Education Science
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) supported formative feedback has emerged as ostensibly transformative pedagogical tool, however, its influence within traditional (physical) classroom settings are still insufficiently synthesized. The present review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, examined 21 empirical studies published from 2014 till 2026 to examine how AI-supported formative feedback effect student’s engagement and redefines teacher-student interaction patterns in traditional classrooms informed by a multi-perspectival conceptual framework incorporating formative feedback theory, the tripartite engagement model, and classroom orchestration theory, thematic synthesis indicated that AI feedback effects on behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement are conditional rather than universal, moderated by feedback elaboration level, temporal granularity, cognitive load, and learner prior knowledge. A directional shift in teacher function from primary feedback provider to orchestrator of AI-generated analytics was the most consistent finding across studies. Three structural tensions were identified: scalability versus relational quality, personalization versus cognitive overload, and AI reliability versus contextual responsiveness. These findings substantiate a conditional engagement model and emphasises that teacher orchestration is a non-negotiable precondition for the effectiveness of AI feedback in classroom ecologies.

papers.title: From Design to Discovery: A Systematic Review of Canva AI as a Pedagogical Tool in Education
papers.authors: Keitlyn Love C. Atienza, Mikaela Ishi Corpuz, Jogie F. Sampana, Romela Yesha B. Sayo, Ansley B. Ventura, Richelle Castro, Ronilo Palle Antonio
papers.journal: International journal of Technology in Education Science
papers.abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has drawn attention to digital learning tools that support creativity and effective teaching. Canva is originally a graphic design platform that evolved into an AI-assisted education tool. This study conducted a systematic review following the PRISMA guidelines and the SPIDER framework to explore Canva’s role in secondary education, focusing on its uses, benefits and challenges. From 1,725 initial records, 15 peer-reviewed studies ,lastly from Indonesia and a few from Malaysia met the inclusion criteria. Findings show that Canva is widely used for visual learning and content creation in language, social studies and science subjects. It enhances student motivation, comprehension, creativity, improves writing and digital literacy. However, its classroom use remains short-term and teacher-centered , with limited focus on science and higher-order thinking. Reported challenges include low digital literacy, poor infrastructure and insufficient teacher training. Overall, Canva is a flexible platform that supports 21st-century learning, but equitable access and teacher readiness are essential for its effective technology integration.

papers.title: Teachers' Perceptions of the Utilization of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Based Learning Media in Elementary Schools
papers.authors: Laksmi Evasufi Widi Fajari, Asep Yudianto, Revanesa Rudiansah, Mudita Revalina, Tiara Az-zahra
papers.abstract: The perceptions of elementary school teachers are the main focus of this research, particularly regarding the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a learning support medium in the classroom. This research involved two classroom teachers and used a qualitative approach through interviews, observations, and documentation to describe teachers' acceptance, understanding, and assessment of AI utilization. The research findings indicate that AI is primarily used for creating questions, student worksheets, and interactive media such as Wordwall, Canva, and learning videos. The teacher stated that AI helps speed up the process of preparing materials and increases student attention and engagement due to more appealing visual presentations. However, this study also found limitations such as limited technological facilities, a lack of shared devices, and the risk of student dependence if AI is used excessively. Additionally, differences in training experience affect teachers' understanding of AI usage, particularly in their ability to create appropriate prompts. Overall, AI is considered to provide significant benefits in terms of learning efficiency and quality, although it still requires wise management, improved teacher competency, and the provision of adequate supporting facilities for its optimal and sustainable utilization.

papers.title: Development of Artificial Intelligence-Based Microcontroller Practice Learning Media
papers.authors: Anggi Puspita Sari, Satria Gunawan Zain, Yasser Abdul Djawad
papers.journal: IJORER International Journal of Recent Educational Research
papers.abstract: This study aims to design learning media for Artificial Intelligence-based Microcontroller practicum and analyze the validity, practicality and effectiveness of learning media for Artificial Intelligence-based microcontroller practicum. The study uses a modified Research and Development (R&D) method from the Borg & Gall, 4-D, and ADDIE models. The product developed is an APSteach AI web that has digital jobsheet features with AI chatbot, automatic assistance, report upload, and AI-based quizzes. The validation results show that material experts give an average value of 90.27% and 91.66%, while media experts give a value of 93.75% to 100%, all of which are categorized as very feasible. The practicality test shows results of 93.75% (individual), 90% (small group), and 86.58% (large group). The effectiveness test shows a very feasible category with achievements of 95.41%, 87.5%, and 86.58%. The results of the Liliefors normality test show that all pretest and posttest data are normally distributed (L count ≤ L table = 0.161). The homogeneity test shows that the data variance is homogeneous (sig. 0.246 > 0.05). The Independent Sample T-Test test shows a significance of 0.01 < 0.05, so there is a significant difference in learning outcomes between the experimental class and the control class. Overall, AI-based learning media is proven to be valid, practical, and effective, and is suitable for use to improve student understanding and independence in learning Microcontroller practicum.

papers.title: NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS AND PHYSIOTHERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES IN THE MANAGEMENT OF CHRONIC NEUROPATHIC PAIN: EMERGING CLINICAL EVIDENCE
papers.authors: Dr. Shiva Kumar Raman, S Sravan Kumar, Deepika Saroha, Varun G Pohekar, Adnan M Melethil, Ankita Samuel
papers.abstract: Chronic neuropathic pain is a complex, disabling condition that is caused by lesions or diseases of the somatosensory nervous system. It is sustained by peripheral nerve dysfunction, ectopic activity, dysregulated ion channels, neuroimmune dysfunction, central sensitization, maladaptive brain network function and neuroplasticity. Current pharmacologic treatments may not adequately relieve symptoms, underscoring the need for comprehensive, mechanism-targeted rehabilitation strategies. This review summarizes current evidence on the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying chronic neuropathic pain and examines physiotherapeutic interventions that may modulate these mechanisms. Therapeutic exercise, pain neuroscience education, manual therapy, neuromuscular re-education, mirror therapy, graded motor imagery, electrotherapy, neuromodulation, and virtual reality-based rehabilitation are discussed in relation to pain modulation, functional recovery, and patient-centered outcomes. Emerging clinical evidence supports the use of personalized rehabilitation approaches guided by pain phenotype, functional impairment, and neurophysiological profiles. Future directions include biomarker-guided rehabilitation, artificial intelligence-based prediction models, digital health integration, and standardized outcome assessment. A mechanism-based physiotherapy framework may improve treatment precision, enhance functional outcomes, and support long-term management of chronic neuropathic pain.

papers.title: A Knowledge Management Perspective on Machine Learning-Based Comprehensive Evaluation of College Students' Ideological and Political Quality
papers.authors: Fenglian Zhou
papers.abstract: The evaluation of college students' Ideological and Political Quality (IPQ) is constrained by subjective assessment and fragmented data. From a Knowledge Management (KM) perspective, this study develops a machine learning-based evaluation system that integrates multi-source data fusion. A five-primary-indicator, 32-secondary-indicator IPQ evaluation system is constructed, and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) reduces 87 features to 32 principal components while retaining approximately 75% cumulative variance. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) achieves the best performance among the evaluated models, with a prediction stability of 95.3% under feature perturbation. A visual KM system supports knowledge storage, retrieval, longitudinal monitoring, and decision support. The findings demonstrate how machine learning and multi-source data fusion can support knowledge creation and decision-making within a KM framework.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence‒Driven Human-Machine Co-Creation for Responsive Interactive Installation Art Design
papers.authors: Yiwen Xu, Zhicheng Shan, Yinchuan Yang, 丁婧
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing traditional art by transforming static creations into interactive. This research proposes a responsive and emotionally adaptive interactive art framework using a hybrid Improved Brain Storm Optimization–tuned Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit (IBSO-Bi-GRU) model. The process begins with comprehensive data collection, such as motion capture, facial expressions, sound patterns, and environmental variables. For feature extraction, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are utilized to learn spatial hierarchies from visual and environmental data. The IBSO algorithm intelligently tunes the Bi-GRU network's hyper-parameters while the Bi-GRU captures bi-directional temporal dependencies in sequential user behaviour. Evaluation metrics include F1-score, accuracy, recall, and precision, ranging from 94% to 97%. The results confirm that human-machine co-creation, powered by generative AI and deep learning (DL) optimization, establishes a new creative paradigm and elevates engagement in interactive art design.

papers.title: Responsible AI Adoption in SMEs: A System Dynamics Approach to Risk Governance, Ethical Readiness and Sustainable Business Performance
papers.authors: Osman Angeles Conteh, Alimamy Kamara
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.abstract: This study examines responsible AI adoption in small and medium-sized enterprises through a system dynamics approach, focusing on how ethical readiness and risk governance shape sustainable business performance.The research uses a sequential mixed-method design based on primary data. It combines SME surveys, semi-structured interviews, expert validation, and system dynamics simulation. The model connects ethical readiness, risk governance capability, responsible AI adoption quality, AI risk exposure, and sustainable business performance. The study shows that AI adoption alone does not guarantee long-term business value. SMEs achieve stronger performance when AI tools are adopted with human oversight, documentation, vendor checks, employee training, and continuous monitoring. Rapid adoption with weak governance may create early efficiency gains, but accumulated risks such as privacy leakage, misinformation, bias, vendor lock-in, employee resistance, and trust loss can reduce performance over time. The research highlights that responsible AI should be treated as a managerial capability rather than a simple technology purchase.

papers.title: The Impact of the Evolution of Artificial Intelligence Tools on the Field of Law
papers.authors: PAVLENKO ZHANNA
papers.abstract: Problem setting. We happen to be living in an age when technology is advancing at a breakneck pace and, on the one hand, is improving the quality of life, but on the other hand, this development poses a number of challenges for society and the law, where artificial intelligence systems influence legal processes and governance, whilst legal norms shape the development, deployment and accountability of artificial intelligence technologies. Today, there are growing calls for more robust governance and regulation of artificial intelligence to minimise the potential negative consequences of these technologies’ development across all spheres of society’s life and activity. At the same time, the regulation of this technology must strike a balance between the need to protect society from the potential risks posed by artificial intelligence systems and the aim of fostering innovation. The practical application of artificial intelligence tools and their ongoing proliferation across various sectors, including the legal sector, is currently outpacing their regulation. Today, in light of the rapid development of artificial intelligence tools, the legal community must not merely keep abreast of these developments, but, by combining the knowledge of researchers from various disciplines – in particular philosophy, computer science and law – work alongside engineers to develop responsible artificial intelligence. This has implications for the future of law and society. Analysis of recent researches and publications. The issue of using modern artificial intelligence tools in the field of law is interdisciplinary in nature and requires the development of a comprehensive, systematic approach. Legal scholars’ attention is mainly focused on individual aspects of the impact of new digital technologies on the law, and their analysis of these aspects remains fragmented. Research is being conducted into the key ethical and legal challenges associated with the introduction of artificial intelligence systems in the context of the rapid digitalisation of society, the theoretical and legal foundations for the use of artificial intelligence as a tool for legal reform, issues concerning the legal regulation of artificial intelligence (O. Martsenyuk, R. Maidanik et al.), issues concerning the regulation of electronic law-making (I. V. Aristova, O. A. Baranov, O. O. Dovgan, Y. V. Kryvitsky, V. G. Olyukha et al.), theoretical and practical aspects of the use of artificial intelligence in law enforcement and the administration of justice (I. V. Lysenko, V. Krat et al.), and issues concerning the integration of artificial intelligence into legal practice (M. I. Hrab et al.). However, despite the significant number of academic works devoted to various aspects of the implementation of artificial intelligence, a comprehensive study of the impact of modern artificial intelligence tools on the law, through the evaluation of actual artificial intelligence systems for the legal sphere, requires further academic research. The purpose of the research is to determine the impact of modern artificial intelligence tools on the legal sector by evaluating existing artificial intelligence systems designed for the legal field. Article’s main body. The implementation of artificial intelligence systems in the legal sector to manage large volumes of data, automate the search for regulatory documents and relevant case law on a given issue, conducting initial risk analysis in contracts, generating standard procedural documents – in particular court claims, applications, petitions and complaints – and solving specific tasks for training and consultancy purposes that assist with day-to-day legal work, is continuing to grow rapidly. Some of these systems can help lawyers automate tedious and repetitive tasks, whilst others aim to make legal systems and courts more accessible to non-specialists. In fact, the greatest potential for automation lies in those areas of law where the main work boils down to logical analysis and text processing. The global market offers a range of specialised solutions for lawyers based on artificial intelligence systems, the most common of which are: Harvey AI, CoCounsel (Thomson Reuters), Lexis+ AI, Luminance, Kira Systems, Lex Machina. In the Ukrainian legal technology sector, the most widely used platforms are Liga360, AcademyCGPT’s personal AI lawyer, Lawria and Yustai. The article argues that recent advances in artificial intelligence offer many benefits to the legal sector, as AI tools significantly automate the analysis and classification of legal documents, allowing lawyers to focus on higher-value tasks. Examples are given of the world’s and Ukraine’s best-known AI-based solutions for lawyers. It is emphasised that the greatest potential for automation lies in those areas of law where the main work involves logical analysis and text processing. It is noted that, depending on the algorithm, legal artificial intelligence systems can provide both more accurate, relevant and context-dependent answers – which in turn fosters trust in AI-supported legal workflows, increases efficiency and reduces misinformation – as well as more problematic answers. It is emphasised that there are three main search engine algorithms: traditional, semantic and hybrid. Key risks and challenges for lawyers are highlighted, relating to the protection of human rights and privacy, bias and discrimination, AI hallucinations, algorithmic errors in the justice system, and issues of intellectual property and copyright. It is noted that the use of artificial intelligence-based tools in the legal field is not only faster, but also smarter and safer. Conclusions and prospects for development. The benefits of lawyers using such tools lie, firstly, in increased efficiency, as they help lawyers quickly locate accurate and relevant documents, reducing the time spent on manual searches and speeding up decision-making. Secondly, they improve accuracy even within large, complex datasets thanks to the integration of semantic search and keyword search. Thirdly, they ensure scalability through their ability to process large volumes of documents in real time with minimal delay. Fourthly, it offers cost-effectiveness by reducing the need for costly manual labour. Artificial intelligence tools help lawyers not only to find the information they need (such as searching for case law, tracking changes to legislation or managing contracts), but also to draw deeper insights that can lead to better decisions and outcomes, whilst ensuring scalability, accuracy and the intelligence required to navigate the complex world of legal data. However, alongside the benefits of using such systems, there are a number of serious challenges for the legal system and society, relating to the protection of human rights and privacy, bias and discrimination, AI hallucinations, algorithmic errors in the administration of justice, and issues of intellectual property and copyright.

papers.title: Порівняння доктрини співавторства в праві Англії та України
papers.authors: Bohdan Tretiakov, Bohdan Tretiakov
papers.abstract: Problem Setting. Joint creative work has become an ordinary way of producing objects of copyright, yet Ukrainian doctrine lacks a positive criterion by which a person’s contribution is qualified as creative and sufficient for recognition as a co-author. The Supreme Court of Ukraine resolves such disputes mainly through the presumption of authorship and the burden of proof rather than a substantive assessment of the contribution. English law, by contrast, revised its doctrine of joint authorship in Kogan v Martin, adopting a material test applied on the merits. Comparing the two approaches exposes the gap in the domestic mechanism and a way of closing it through the originality criterion of the Law of Ukraine “On Copyright and Related Rights”.Analysis of recent research and publications. In Ukrainian scholarship co-authorship has been studied along several lines: the limits of the concept (H. Ulianova), the presumption of the creative character of work (O. Yavorska), its features through the nature of joint work (O. Izbash), the grounds on which it arises (K. Diukarieva-Berzhanina), and, for AI-assisted objects, by K. Militsyna. The revised English approach has been analysed by D. Simone and authorship in EU law by J. Fritz. None offers a positive substantive criterion of what makes a contribution creative, and the revised English test has not been juxtaposed with the Ukrainian mechanism.Purpose of the Study. On the basis of a comparative legal analysis of the mechanism by which co-authorship arises in England and Ukraine, the article aims to determine directions for improving the domestic approach and to substantiate a positive criterion of a co-author’s creative contribution.Article’s main body. The English material test is reconstructed as interrelated requirements – collaboration, the authorial character of the contribution, its sufficiency by the Infopaq standard, and non-distinctness. In the scholarship analysed, Ukrainian doctrine, by contrast, defines the creative contribution mainly in the negative and through the presumption of the creative character of work, so the courts fall back on procedural mechanisms. The author defines it positively, through the originality criterion of Article 1, paragraphs 35 and 56 of the Law – the person’s own free creative choices concerning the expression of the work – derived from the law in force without amending its text, consistent with the case law of the Court of Justice of the EU, and formulated as a three-part test that separates the qualitative question of co-authorship from the quantitative one of remuneration.Conclusions and prospects for development. In England the mechanism is material, whereas in Ukraine co-authorship also arises from joint creative work but its central feature is defined negatively and procedurally. A positive criterion can be derived from the law in force and applied through the revised English approach, which distinguishes a co-author from a person who merely provided technical assistance, while the size of a contribution is reflected in the distribution of remuneration rather than the division of the right. The scientific novelty is that the material test from Kogan v Martin is, for the first time, systematically juxtaposed with the features of co-authorship under Article 13 of Law No. 2811-IX and Article 436 of the Civil Code of Ukraine; its applicability to AI-created works is a prospective direction for further research.
keywords: European Court of Justice case law

papers.title: Análisis del Impacto de Asistentes Educativos Inteligentes con Enfoque Didáctico Adaptativo en Procesos de Enseñanza-Aprendizaje
papers.authors: Ángel Patricio Herrera-Carrión, Sara Paquita Donoso Caiza, Manuel Fabricio Reyes Wagnio, Dayron Rumbaut-Rangel
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to analyze the impact of intelligent educational assistants with an adaptive didactic approach on the teaching-learning processes of high school students. The scope of the work focused on examining the impact of these tools on comprehension, motivation, participation, autonomy, and academic performance within a formal school environment. The research was conducted with a mixed approach, quasi-experimental design, and descriptive scope. The sample consisted of 75 students distributed across three parallel classes and 6 teachers. For data collection, a questionnaire directed at students, a questionnaire applied to teachers, and a record sheet for academic performance and monitoring the use of artificial intelligence were employed. The results showed a predominance of high levels in the analyzed pedagogical variables, both in student perception and in teacher evaluation, with an emphasis on interaction with content, adaptive learning, motivation, comprehension, and autonomy. In the academic record, the majority of students were placed in the Excellent category, with an average general index of 8.93 out of 10. The findings also showed convergence between the favorable perception of the pedagogical use of these tools and the positive trend observed in academic performance, which allowed for the integration of perceptual and academic evidence into a single line of analysis. It is concluded that intelligent educational assistants strengthen more dynamic, personalized, and favorable learning experiences for academic performance in high school.

papers.title: Gestión Directiva y Formación Docente para el Uso de Inteligencia Artificial en Educación
papers.authors: Maryury Alexandra Cevallos Reyes, Nelly Beatriz Yaucan Coro, Maricela Elizabeth Sánchez Morante, Esther Carlin Chavez, Maryury Alexandra Cevallos Reyes, Nelly Beatriz Yaucan Coro
papers.abstract: This study aimed to determine how school leadership contributes to strengthening teacher training for the use of artificial intelligence in an educational institution located in Puerto López, Manabí Province, Ecuador. The research adopted a quantitative approach with a descriptive scope and a non-experimental cross-sectional design. The population and sample consisted of fifteen teachers selected through census sampling. Data were collected using a structured twenty-item questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale, validated through expert judgment, and analyzed using descriptive statistics. The findings revealed that most teachers use artificial intelligence tools in their teaching activities and hold a positive perception of their usefulness for improving lesson planning, educational resource development, and teaching and learning processes. The results also showed that institutional support, effective school leadership, and continuous professional development opportunities facilitate the pedagogical integration of these technologies, although limitations related to teacher training and digital competencies remain. The study concludes that school leadership plays a strategic role in promoting educational innovation by encouraging continuous training programs and pedagogical support that enable the responsible, ethical, and effective integration of artificial intelligence into teaching practice.

papers.title: “George, the Guardian of Galápagos”: An AI Agent for Environmental Action in Secondary Education
papers.authors: María Violeta Erazo Cedillo, Rosana Nury Aguilar Verdezoto, Manuel Fabricio Reyes Wagnio, Dayron Rumbaut-Rangel
papers.abstract: Abstract The environmental crisis and the advancement of generative artificial intelligence pose new challenges and opportunities for education. The objective of this study was to describe the level of development of environmental action competence in secondary school students during their interaction with a Narrative Conversational Agent based on generative artificial intelligence. A quantitative approach was adopted, with a non-experimental, descriptive, and cross-sectional design; the sample consisted of 28 upper basic education students from the Unidad Educativa Provincia de Bolívar, selected through non-probabilistic convenience sampling. The instrument used was a structured questionnaire adapted from the Environmental Empathy Scale (EES), with a Cronbach’s alpha reliability coefficient of 0.788. The results showed a positive evaluation of the conversational agent GEORGE-BOT-SERVER: 85.7% of students reported a high level of doubt resolution, 100% indicated being inspired to seek further information, and 89.3% expressed a high willingness to take action in favor of endangered species. Likewise, 71.4% reached high levels of environmental awareness and sensitivity. It is concluded that conversational agents based on generative artificial intelligence can constitute a significant tool for strengthening environmental action competence in secondary students, although their integration into more practical pedagogical strategies requires further exploration.

papers.title: GENERATIV SUN’IY INTELLEKT DISKURSIDA INGLIZ IDIOMALARINING KONTEKSTUAL TRANSFORMATSIYASI VA LINGVISTIK KREATIVLIK
papers.authors: Lochin Suyunov
papers.abstract: This article examines the contextual transformation of English idioms and linguistic creativity in generative artificial intelligence discourse. The study compares canonical idiomatic forms with their transformed variants produced by generative AI and identifies such mechanisms as component expansion, component substitution, literalization, metaphorical continuation, semantic re-motivation, and contextual adaptation. The findings show that successful creative transformation generally preserves the core figurative meaning of an idiom while reactivating its literal or metaphorical components in accordance with a new communicative purpose. The analysis also reveals three levels of idiomatic creativity: formal adaptation, semantic activation, and conceptual creativity. The study proposes contextual motivation, semantic preservation, and pragmatic value as key criteria for distinguishing productive linguistic creativity from semantic or stylistic distortion in generative AI discourse.

papers.title: MENTORING TEACHERS IN LEARNING INNOVATION MANAGEMENT USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE LEARNING MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS AND VIRTUAL REALITY FOR SCHOOL DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
papers.authors: Paul Arjanto, Desembra Sohilait, Nandalita Nunuela, Estin Indria Maahury, Izak Jakobis Makulua, Muhammad Yusril Musiin, Lifia Meiliza Wiyono
papers.abstract: School digital transformation requires teachers to manage pedagogical innovation rather than merely adopt devices. This community service program aimed to strengthen teachers' capacity at SMA Negeri 12 Ambon through integrated mentoring in artificial intelligence (AI), learning management systems (LMS), and virtual reality (VR). The program used a learning innovation management mentoring model comprising coordination, needs analysis, resource design, technical-pedagogical training, guided implementation, and evaluation. The intensive on-site phase was conducted on 1-4 September 2026, while program evidence was documented through attendance records, LMS credential lists, training materials, asset handover records, and institutional cooperation documents. Documented outputs include participation records with 50 numbered entries, the preparation of 44 teacher LMS accounts, the distribution of 50 copies of the training book Mengajar Lebih Cerdas [Teaching Smarter], and the transfer of four Shinecon 6.0 VR Box units with headphones. The activity was also institutionalized through cooperation and implementation agreements between Universitas Pattimura and SMA Negeri 12 Ambon. These outputs indicate that the program established access, learning resources, and institutional support needed for continued digital innovation. Follow-up should verify competency gains through prospective pre-test and post-test measures in the next mentoring cycle, LMS analytics, digital portfolios, and monitoring of reusable AI-LMS-VR learning products.

papers.title: Human-in-the-Loop Cultural Schema Annotation for Metaphor Translation: A Pilot Framework
papers.authors: Dahui Dong
papers.journal: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON SYSTEMS AND CONTROL
papers.abstract: Metaphor translation presents a persistent challenge in cross-lingual communication because source and target languages often organize metaphorical meaning through different cultural schemas. This pilot study proposes a human-in-the-loop annotation framework for tracing cultural schema transfer in Chinese-English metaphor translation. The framework annotates 500 Chinese-English metaphor pairs across four dimensions: source-language cultural schema, target-language cultural schema, transfer strategy, and translator proficiency level. BERT-wwm-assisted pre-annotation is used to generate candidate labels, which trained human annotators revise and adjudicate. An exploratory CLIP-based similarity measure is used only as a heuristic indicator of schema alignment, and a Graph Neural Network models associations among schema labels, proficiency levels, and observed transfer-strategy labels. In the pilot corpus, the GNN reached 82% accuracy in predicting adjudicated transfer-strategy labels. Corpus patterns indicated that intermediate translators favored literal translation (68%) when schema similarity was low, whereas advanced translators more often used adaptation or substitution strategies (74%). These findings are presented as preliminary evidence for the feasibility of schema-aware annotation and label prediction, not as evidence of downstream translation-quality gains or broad model generalization. The study contributes a reproducible pilot framework for making cultural-schema decisions more explicit in translation pedagogy and computational annotation while identifying the validation steps required for larger-scale work.

papers.title: Association of Cardiometabolic Parameters with Sleep Quality and Independence among Older Adults in Gianyar
papers.authors: Anak Agung Gede Angga Puspa Negara, I Gede Putu Wahyu Mahendra, Govinda Vittala, Ida Ayu Laksmi Dharmajayanti, Kadek Andre Yasa
papers.abstract: Background: Sleep quality and independence are key indicators of well-being in older adults. Several physiological factors, including blood glucose, blood pressure, cholesterol, and body mass index (BMI), may affect these aspects. However, limited studies have explored these associations among the elderly in Indonesia. This study aimed to examine the relationship between selected health factors and sleep quality and independence in older adults in Gianyar Regency. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical observational study was conducted with 129 community-dwelling older adults aged ≥60 years. Participants were selected using simple random sampling. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and independence was measured using the Barthel Index. Spearman’s correlation test was used due to the non-normal distribution of data. Results:Blood glucose levels showed significant negative correlations with sleep quality (r = -0.360, p < 0.001) and independence (r = -0.247, p < 0.001). BMI was also negatively correlated with sleep quality (r = -0.189, p = 0.015). Blood pressure demonstrated a positive correlation with independence (r = 0.170, p = 0.030). Cholesterol levels had no significant associations with either outcome. Conclusion: Higher blood glucose and BMI are associated with poorer sleep and reduced independence. These findings emphasize the importance of metabolic and weight control in geriatric health programs to promote healthy aging and functional ability.

papers.title: INTERPRETATION AND VERIFICATION OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL DECISIONS: TAXONOMY OF METHODS, TRUST METRICS,AND EVALUATION PROTOCOLS
papers.authors: Artem Orlovskyi, Gennadiy Kyselov
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution and adoption of large language models in domains with a high cost of error, including healthcare, law, finance, and education, where incorrect or factually inaccurate responses may lead to erroneous decisions, necessitate the study of the theoretical and practical aspects of the interpretation, calibration, evaluation, and verification of large language model outputs.This article systematizes contemporary approaches to the interpretation and verification of large language model decisions and identifies the roles of trust metrics in constructing protocols for assessing their reliability. The study analyzes methods of mechanistic interpretability, including sparse autoencoders and computational circuit tracing, approaches to chain-of-thought analysis, calibration metrics such as Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier score, semantic entropy, verbalized confidence, and conformal prediction. Particular attention is devoted to the standardized evaluation frameworks HELM and LM Evaluation Harness, the LLM-as-a-judge paradigm, as well as factuality assessment methods including FActScore, SAFE, and SelfCheckGPT. Based on the conducted analysis, a five-level taxonomy of large language model interpretation methods is proposed, covering the range from the analysis of individual neuron activations to behavioral testing at the level of complete textual outputs. Trust metrics are grouped according to their level of practical maturity, while factuality verification approaches are compared in terms of verification granularity, dependence on external knowledge sources, and computational cost. It is demonstrated that proper probability calibration is a necessary prerequisite for the practical application of interpretation and verification results. Future research should focus on the development of comprehensive evaluation protocols covering the entire lifecycle of a large language model – from training to deployment in production systems.

papers.title: CABLE-DRIVEN PARALLEL ROBOT S IN THE AUTOMATIONOF CONSTRUCTION PROCESSES
papers.authors: Andrii V. Obrubov, Oleksandr Ushkarenko, Дьяконов Олексій Сергійович, Ivan Biliuk, Oleksandr Cherno
papers.abstract: The automation of construction processes by means of robotics is constrained by the fact that conventional gantry systems and anthropomorphic manipulators have either a limited workspace or a complex and low-mobility structure. A promising alternative is cable-driven parallel robots (CDPR), in which a moving platform, equipped with a working tool or manipulator, is held and displaced by a system of cables wound by winches. The aim of the article is to review and systematize modern applications of cable-driven parallel robots in construction, with an emphasis on their advantages, automatic control systems, and integration into the digital information environment. The paper considers the design principle and classification of CDPR, analyses the main fields of application ‒ primarily large-scale 3D concrete printing and the installation of heavy facade elements ‒ and characterizes the features of control systems related to cable elasticity and sagging, vibration, and collision avoidance.
