Particular attention is paid to the mathematical modelling of the cable system, trajectory planning of the end-effector, the use of artificial intelligence and machine-learning methods, and the integration of robots with the Internet of Things and cloud computing. It is established that the key advantage of CDPR is a large workspace combined with a relatively small mass of moving parts, as well as ease of transportation, assembly, and adaptation to environmental conditions. It is concluded that further development is associated with the improvement in control and trajectory-planning algorithms, the combination of technologies, and deeper integration with building information modelling.

papers.title: The Role of Personality Traits, Customer Journey Design, Omnichannel Trust, and Omnichannel Customer Experience in Shaping Value Co-Creation Behavior
papers.authors: Karmila Jayanti, Kurniawati Kurniawati, Sri Vandayuli Riorini
papers.abstract: Addressing empirical fragmentation in omnichannel literature, this study models how individual psychological attributes and structural service flows drive collaborative customer behaviors within emerging e-commerce markets. It evaluates the effects of Personality Traits and Customer Journey Design on Value Co-Creation Behavior, mediated by Omnichannel Trust and Omnichannel Customer Experience, alongside the moderating influences of Digital Proficiency and Channel Preference. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS via SmartPLS 4) was executed on survey responses gathered from 300 active Indonesian omnichannel shoppers through purposive sampling. Findings demonstrate that seamless journey designs and adaptive personality traits significantly elevate both customer trust and experiential quality, which directly propel value co-creation participation. Conversely, neither digital proficiency nor channel preferences exhibit significant moderating effects. The proposed model demonstrates moderate explanatory power, capturing variance across key outcomes with $R^2$ values of 0.533 for Customer Experience, 0.501 for Trust, and 0.359 for Value Co-Creation Behavior. Theoretically, this research extends Service-Dominant Logic and Trust Theory by establishing a dual-mediation mechanism that bridges micro-level individual traits and macro-level service architectures. The study's primary novelty rests on synthesizing behavioral readiness and touchpoint design into a unified framework. Practically, e-commerce executives must emphasize friction-free cross-channel integration and transparent system reliability over tailored channel isolation or reliance on user digital capabilities

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence For Inclusive Education: A Step Towards Attaining SDG-4
papers.authors: Pradnya Prabhukarwatkar
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence or AI refers to the ability of machines to perform tasks mainly like Thinking , Problem Solving and Decision making. Artificial Intelligence in Education refers to the integration of AI technologies - to enhance teaching, personalize the student experience, optimize administration, and support decision-making. India the country with diverse crowd of students of different socio-economic background, demographic conditions, languages, emerging AI technology and tools is going to play crucial role in achieving the Sustainable Development Goal(SDG)-4 which aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. This paper will describe how AI tools like Machine Learning & Adaptive Algorithms, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Predictive Analytics, Intelligent Tutoring system (ITS) can be use to enhance Class-room teaching, Evaluation, Research, Administration, Accreditation i.e teaching learning process in all and reaching out to unreached. The paper also discuss challenges posed due overreliance on AI and strategies to ensure ethical use of AI, particularly in education.

papers.title: Thriving in uncertainty: residency education in a world of change
papers.abstract: Introduction: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools increasingly influence perioperative care and research, yet formal anesthesiology AI training remains limited.We developed and pilot-tested a bilingual (English/French) sur--ey to quantify AI knowledge and perceived learning needs among Canadian anesthesiology residents and fellows to inform Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME) curriculum design.Methods: After Research Ethics Board approval, we drafted items from a targeted literature search and refined content through a two-round Delphi with national experts in anesthesiology education and AI (7/10 participated), using 70% consensus threshold.We pilot-tested the English survey with 16 second-year medical trainees to assess clarity, usability, and completeness; summarized responses using descriptive statistics; and revised items based on feedback prior to deployment.The finalized English and French surveys will be distributed electronically through Canadian anesthesiology training programs and in collaboration with the Canadian Anesthesiologists' Society to anesthesiology trainees (PGY1-5 residents and fellows) for one month starting June 2026.Results: Five consensus domains emerged: (1) AI knowledge and technical literacy, (2) attitudes and confidence, (3) ethical and legal awareness, (4) learning facilitators and barriers, and (5) readiness for integration.The 24-item survey uses 5-point Likert scales and distinguishes generative from non-generative AI.In pilot testing, 88% found items clear and 81% found domains complete.Most rated section flow excellent or good (81%), and mental demand as low or very low (62%).Feedback led to minor edits to reduce redundancy and clarify terms.Conclusion: We developed an expert-informed, pilottested bilingual survey to characterize AI learning needs in Canadian anesthesiology training.National results will inform CBME objectives, faculty development, and guidance for responsible AI integration in perioperative practice.Limitations include a small pilot sample and testing with medical students rather than anesthesiology trainees.Next steps include national deployment in June 2026 and psychometric evaluation among trainee cohorts.

papers.title: Strategic Fintech Disclosure and Financial Management Performance in Digital Banking
papers.authors: Murniati Murniati, Murni Nia, Abdul Rachman Rika, Wahyu Muh. Syata, Asriyani Mulia Basri
papers.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the effect of strategic fintech capabilities on financial management performance during digital banking transformation. This study addresses this research gap by investigating the heterogeneous strategic contributions of different fintech dimensions, rather than treating fintech adoption as a homogeneous construct.Research Methodology: A quantitative research design using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was employed. Survey data were collected from 300 banking structural officials responsible for financial management and information systems in Southeast Sulawesi Province, Indonesia.Results: Digital-based core banking systems, AI-based risk management, and financial big data analytics significantly improve financial decision-making quality and financial reporting performance, while digital payment systems and internet and mobile banking show no significant effects. Financial big data analytics is the strongest strategic capability.Conclusions: Financial management performance depends not only on fintech adoption but also on banks' ability to internalize high-value fintech capabilities as strategic organizational resources.Limitations: This study is limited to banking institutions in Southeast Sulawesi and focuses on internal managerial perspectives, limiting broader generalizations.Contribution: This study extends the Resource-Based View by positioning fintech as a strategic organizational capability rather than merely operational technology. It also provides practical insights for banks to prioritize fintech investments that strengthen managerial and financial performance.

papers.title: The AI Competence Framework Landscape: A Comparative Analysis of Frameworks for Education and Workforce Development
papers.authors: Panos Fitsilis
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) competence frameworks has made it increasingly difficult for educators and workforce-development professionals to identify those suited to their purposes. This study maps and compares institutionally endorsed frameworks for education, professional development, and workforce training. From 76 candidates, 24 frameworks and reference models were shortlisted, and 16 met the criteria for comparative analysis. These were examined in terms of their target populations, intended uses, competence structures, progression models, implementation guidance, and coverage of ten common AI competence areas. The findings show that all 16 frameworks substantively address AI Use and Interaction, Output Evaluation and Verification, and Domain or Workflow Application, while 15 address AI Foundations and Ethics and Responsible AI. Greater variation was found in Problem Formulation, Data Competence, and AI Creation and Development, as well as in the provision of proficiency levels, learning outcomes, pedagogical guidance, and assessment. The comparison indicates that AI competence brings together foundational understanding, practical application, critical judgement, and responsible human engagement, with further requirements shaped by the population and context. The resulting map provides a reference point for selecting and adapting frameworks for curricula, vocational education and training, professional upskilling, and workforce transformation.

papers.title: Measuring Academic Performance in Psychology in the Era of AI: The benefits of an oral viva in assessing undergraduate dissertations
papers.authors: xiaosheng chen, Deborah Talmi
papers.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), challenge psychology educators’ ability to assess students’ understanding and judgement through written coursework. We argue that this issue is especially acute for the compulsory empirical project required for British Psychological Society (BPS) accreditation and that interactive oral examinations (vivas) offer a discipline-aligned and scalable response. Grounded in the epistemic features of psychology, the viva enables direct assessment of students’ conceptual understanding, methodological justification, and reflective thinking in ways written reports cannot reliably capture in an AI-saturated environment. In this paper we propose an operational framework for implementing project vivas across final-year cohorts and argue that viva assessment should be viewed not as a defensive measure, but as a future-oriented approach that enhances authenticity, equity, and educational quality in psychology.

papers.title: Preservice Early Childhood Educators’ Engagement with Generative AI in Science Activity Design: The Case of Magnetism
papers.authors: George Efthimiou
papers.abstract: The use of generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) in early childhood teacher education provides logistical support in lesson planning but poses challenges about developmental appropriateness. This mixed-methods study aims to understand how Large Language Models (LLMs) are used by 131 preservice educators to design science activities on the topic of magnetism, drawing on the concepts of Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT) and didactic transformation. A post-interaction reflection instrument containing Likert scale items and open-ended questions was used to collect the data and descriptive statistics, ANOVA and inductive thematic analysis were used to analyze the data. The results show a clear divide in user perceptions. The algorithmic mediation was appreciated by the participants for its structure, divergency and efficiency of workflow. They expressed a lack of epistemic trust, however, in the pedagogical reliability and accuracy of the created content. Qualitative reflections pointed to the limitations these tools face in terms of their feasibility in the classroom and developmental appropriateness. Finally, novice teachers see artificial intelligence as a brainstorming artifact. They are aware that the difficult challenge of didactic transformation remains a human responsibility. The teaching of simple technical skills, therefore, is not the focus of modern teacher training programs; instead, it is necessary to teach critical pedagogical filtering skills.

papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Model Performance on Open-Ended Questions: Answering and Marking Capabilities
papers.authors: Quynh T. Nguyen, Michael Lo, Mai P. Tran, Quang Dieu Tran
papers.abstract: Statistical literacy is crucial in biology education, yet developing and assessing it at higher cognitive levels is resource-intensive. This study evaluated three large language models against 20 graduate students on open-ended biological statistics questions spanning Bloom's Taxonomy, and separately examined whether a large language model could serve as a marking assistant alongside an experienced human instructor. A set of 692 questions was developed by graduate students using a statistics textbook. After cleaning, 336 unique questions were retained, with 1,344 answers provided by the four respondent groups. Answers were graded using a holistic five-point rubric by a human expert and a large language model. Friedman tests showed that all models were rated more favourably than the graduate students, though this advantage was not uniform across cognitive levels, and the evaluative question type (Type 7) anchoring the highest cognitive level in this study's design showed the weakest performance across all respondent groups. Inter-rater reliability between the human and large language model was low overall. The large language model grader showed a bias toward scores of 3-4, while the human expert demonstrated greater consistency across question types. These findings suggest that large language models can generate strong responses at lower cognitive levels, but their reliability as holistic-rubric graders are limited compared to an experienced instructor.

papers.title: Can Assigned Learner States Be Recovered from Synthetic Tutoring Dialogues? A Factorial Study with SLEF
papers.authors: Marco Iannacone
papers.abstract: With synthetic learners, researchers can assign a learner profile explicitly and combine its dimensions in a controlled design. This raises a practical question: how much of the assigned profile can be read back from a tutoring dialogue? This matters beyond evaluation: an AI tutor that could read a learner's knowledge and metacognition from the dialogue could adapt its teaching and judge whether it is working. Synthetic learners, whose profiles are assigned explicitly, offer a controlled setting in which to test such a reading against what was assigned. It also matters now that synthetic-learner scores are starting to be used to compare AI tutors. We present SLEF, the Synthetic Learner Evaluation Framework, and use it to measure how assigned learner dimensions are recovered across a complete simulation and assessment pipeline. The corpus contains 1,100 Italian dialogues on fractions from five tutoring conditions that share the same 44 learner profiles (32 of them in a fully crossed factorial core) and the same task schedule. A single external language model, blind to the assigned labels, classifies Knowledge, Misconception, Metacognition, and Transfer in each transcript, or abstains. An exploratory analysis of the 160-session factorial core in each condition shows that Knowledge recovery varies with assigned Metacognition. For profiles assigned high Metacognition, Knowledge recovery is 50.0%–52.5% in every condition, close to what always giving the same answer achieves, and it remains close to the baseline when any single task is removed. For profiles assigned low Metacognition it reaches 57.5%–68.8%. When the profile combinations are reweighted, the central 95% range of the gap stays below zero for OpenAI and Mistral but includes zero for the other three conditions. The same design also reveals a strong class asymmetry in Metacognition: 85.7%–87.8% of classified low-Metacognition sessions are read as high. In Mistral, 15% of matched pairs (a base profile and its channel variant) receive different Knowledge classifications, although aggregate accuracy is unchanged. These results describe the shared generator–tutor–extractor pipeline, which is the unit SLEF measures. They show what class-level, cross-dimension, and paired analyses reveal beyond an aggregate score, and the public corpus and analysis code allow others to extend them.

papers.title: Do We Still Need Universities? What the founders of the first and most influential universities wanted, and what is left of it when intelligence fits in a pocket
papers.authors: Daniel Attinger
papers.abstract: A phone, or a language model running offline on a laptop, now gives anyone more information, translation and tutoring than the library of any university. If universities exist to give people access to knowledge, they have lost their reason to exist. This article asks whether that was ever their main reason. It reads the founding documents of the earliest universities, all of them European (Bologna, Paris, Naples, Prague, Heidelberg, Cologne), of the University of Basel, and of three American foundings that shaped the modern university: Harvard, the land-grant colleges of the Morrill Act, and the University of Chicago. From these texts the article derives seven reasons for which universities were founded: access to learning; protection of those who learn; trusted professionals; credentials that others accept; service to the state that founded them; the betterment of people and a way up for those born with little; and, from Berlin in 1810, new knowledge pursued in freedom. Only the first is largely met by artificial intelligence. The others are not, and several matter more now. The protection of scholars has recently failed in American universities from inside, through compelled statements of belief, and from outside, through immigration measures against foreign students. And the immediacy of artificial intelligence, which can answer before a question has been struggled with, threatens the exercise of intelligence itself. The record also carries a warning: universities have become obsolete before, and were renewed only when someone founded them again, in Berlin in 1810 and in the United States after 1862. The article ends by sketching what a fourth founding would require.

papers.title: How AI-Generated Language Shapes User Trust in Social Media? A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Hasria Riski, Janisa Pascawati, Suwarni Suaib
papers.journal: ELS Journal on Interdisciplinary Studies in Humanities
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has transformed social media communication by enabling AI systems to produce increasingly human-like language and content. Although research on AI-generated communication and user trust has expanded, findings remain fragmented across platforms, communication contexts, and linguistic characteristics. This study systematically synthesizes empirical evidence on the relationship between AI-generated language and user trust in social media communication. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Literature was retrieved from the Dimensions database in July 2026 using predefined search terms related to Generative AI, language, trust, and social media. Of 205 records initially identified, 54 full-text studies were assessed for eligibility, and 23 empirical studies were included in the final synthesis. The findings show that research is concentrated in recent years, particularly in marketing and digital communication, health communication, and misinformation and synthetic media. Across the studies, trust is associated with recurring linguistic and communicative features, including human-likeness and conversational style, emotional expression and empathy, personalization, formality and readability, narrative and experiential language, semantic and informational characteristics, transparency and disclosure, and explanatory language. The findings indicate that user trust is not determined by AI authorship alone but emerges through the interaction of relational and epistemic cues within specific communication contexts. This review contributes to human–AI communication research by identifying linguistic and communicative mechanisms through which AI-generated social media content shapes perceptions of trust, credibility, and authenticity.

papers.title: Emergency Evacuation in Classrooms: A Review
papers.authors: Peihua Song, Zhigang Xu, Lian Duan
papers.abstract: Classroom evacuation is constrained by relatively fixed occupant positions, dense desk-and-chair arrangements, restricted aisles, and limited exits, and is jointly influenced by occupant behavior, spatial conditions, and emergency scenarios. This review proposes a four-stage framework comprising scenario and data, experiments and modeling, analysis and evaluation, and optimization and validation, and synthesizes studies on evacuation methods, evaluation indicators, scenario-specific characteristics, and optimization strategies. Existing approaches include evacuation drills and experiments, simulation software, cellular automata, social force models, and agent-based models, with increasing applications of machine learning, reinforcement learning, and virtual reality. Evaluation mainly focuses on time, movement, density and flow, paths, and exits. Fire, low-visibility conditions, earthquakes, and violent attacks exhibit distinct evacuation characteristics, while the effectiveness of exit configuration, desk-and-chair layout, organizational guidance, safety education, special-needs support, and dynamic route guidance varies across occupant groups and scenarios. Overall, research is shifting from single-factor analysis toward integrated analysis of occupants, space, and hazards. However, gaps remain in empirical data, model calibration and validation, multi-factor optimization, and continuous evacuation analysis from classrooms to building exits. Future studies should strengthen multi-scenario data support, experimental–model cross-validation, coordinated optimization, and intelligent decision-making and emergency training.

papers.title: BRiDGENav: Belief-Driven Risk-Aware Dynamic Guidance and Event-Triggered Navigation
papers.authors: Nimantha Adikaram, Charitha Dombawala, Diluka Moratuwage, Asanka G. Perera, Sreenatha Gopalarao Anavatti, Matthew Garratt
papers.journal: Journal of Sensor and Actuator Networks
papers.abstract: Human–robot interaction (HRI) and navigation in crowded indoor spaces require robots to reason not only about where humans may be but also about whether uncertain human motion conflicts with the robot’s intended path. Existing context-aware particle filtering (CA-PF) provides a useful belief-estimation backbone by maintaining multimodal human-state uncertainty under occlusion, missed detections, and close interaction. However, a navigation layer must further convert this belief into path-aware risk and determine when replanning is necessary. This paper extends the CA-PF framework with three navigation modules: a path-conflict risk module that evaluates weighted human particles against the committed robot path, a directional interaction-aware risk grid that combines particle occupancy with human motion direction and conflict likelihood, and a belief-aware event-triggered replanning strategy that updates the path when conflict, directional path risk, or risk growth exceeds safety thresholds. Evaluation on four sequences from the Bi3 dataset demonstrates a mean human-tracking error of 0.237 m and an RMSE of 0.308 m. In the ablation study, the complete framework reduced mean path-conflict risk by 25.2% and mean directional path risk by 42.35% relative to the configuration without event-triggered replanning, averaged over 12 matched trials. These results demonstrate that propagating particle-level human beliefs into path-conflict reasoning, directional risk-aware planning, and selective replanning can improve the handling of interaction risk in dynamic human environments.

papers.title: Health-Related Quality of Life and Family Impact in Young Children with Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome: A Cross-Sectional Caregiver-Reported Study
papers.authors: Natalia Kasaraba, Anna Rozensztrauch
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) is a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by epileptic spasms and epileptiform EEG abnormalities. Classical West syndrome represents a phenotype within the IESS spectrum characterized by epileptic spasms, hypsarrhythmia, and developmental plateau or regression. Beyond seizure control, assessment of health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and family impact may provide important information on the long-term burden of the disease. This study aimed to characterize caregiver-reported HRQoL in young children with IESS and family impact and to explore clinical and perinatal factors associated with these outcomes. Methods: This cross-sectional caregiver-proxy study included 60 parents or primary caregivers of children aged 1 month to 4 years who had previously received a physician-established diagnosis of West syndrome; in the present manuscript, the cohort is described within the broader contemporary IESS framework. Children’s HRQoL was assessed using age-appropriate versions of the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL), while family impact was assessed using the PedsQL Family Impact Module (FIM). Parametric and non-parametric statistical methods were applied as appropriate. All analyses were exploratory, and no adjustment for multiple comparisons or multivariable adjustment for potential confounders was performed. Results: The mean PedsQL Total Scale Score was 64.53 ± 19.35 among children aged 1–24 months assessed with the PedsQL Infant Scales and 56.34 ± 23.29 among children aged 2–4 years assessed with the PedsQL 4.0 Generic Core Scales. In exploratory pooled analyses, children with additional congenital, genetic, structural, or systemic conditions had lower age-appropriate Total Scale Scores than children without such conditions (52.93 ± 21.55 vs. 64.40 ± 22.08; unadjusted mean difference −11.48 points, 95% CI −22.75 to −0.20; nominal p = 0.046). Physical health scores were also lower in children with additional conditions (53.78 ± 27.62 vs. 69.60 ± 26.71; nominal p = 0.012). In the sensitivity analysis restricted to children aged 2–4 years assessed with a single PedsQL instrument, the Total Scale Score difference was similar in direction but did not reach the nominal significance threshold (48.76 ± 20.86 vs. 62.35 ± 23.76; mean difference −13.59 points, 95% CI −27.57 to 0.38; nominal p = 0.056). Within the FIM, the lowest mean scores were observed for Worry (24.17 ± 21.20) and Daily Activities (35.00 ± 28.57). Conclusions: Caregiver-reported HRQoL and family impact varied substantially among young children with IESS and their families. Additional congenital, genetic, structural, or systemic conditions were associated with lower scores in selected child HRQoL domains, although these exploratory unadjusted findings may be affected by residual confounding. The findings support the inclusion of child HRQoL and family impact measures alongside neurological outcomes in the follow-up of children with IESS.

papers.title: A feature-optimized EEG framework using multiscale entropy and metaheuristic optimization for cognitive analysis
papers.authors: Keerthika N., Kiruthika V.
papers.abstract: Background Cognitive activity plays an important role by influencing working-memory, problem-solving, attention, response and decision making. EEG serves as a non-invasive approach to analyze neural activity associated with cognitive processing. The current study aims to identify the more contributing features to analyze the cognitive activity between sports and non-sports groups. Methods The present study included 100 participants, consisting of 80 males and 20 females aged between 19 and 23 years. EEG signals were acquired and preprocessed using filtering methods to remove unwanted noise and artifacts. The four-entropy metrics dispersion entropy, permutation entropy, sample entropy, and fuzzy entropy were applied to the coarse-graining method across multiple temporal scales to analyze the complexity of EEG signals. To identify the most informative feature subsets and reduce redundancy, filter-based methods such as Mutual Information, Pearson Correlation, Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance and wrapper-based methods such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization were applied. Finally for differentiating the cognitive activity, five machine learning classifiers that include Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, K -nearest neighbor, Decision Tree and Random Forest were applied. Statistical methods such as T -test and Fleiss kappa were used to analyse the performance efficiency. Results Feature extraction phase yielded a total of 160 multiscale entropy features. The entire features when fed into both filter-based and wrapper-based methods, Genetic Algorithm based optimization yielded a minimal contributing feature subset with high nested cross-validated accuracy of 93.0 ± 2.7% with Support Vector Machine. This contributing feature subset was used as input for five different machine learning classifiers for differentiating the cognitive activity between both groups. The five classifiers demonstrated high cross-validated agreement on held-out subjects, with a mean Fleiss' kappa of 0.874 ± 0.051 (95% CI: 0.811–0.937), depicting a good inter-classifier agreement for classification of samples into sports and non-sports individuals. Discussion The study demonstrates that multiscale entropy features combined with metaheuristic-based feature optimization can effectively analyze the cognitive activity between sports and non-sports individuals. The proposed EEG framework provides a structured approach for real-time cognitive activity analysis using compact and informative entropy-based feature subsets.

papers.title: AI exposure and task detachability: migrant anchoring and work-linked health protection among highly educated foreign-born adults in the United States
papers.authors: Tse Hou Hew, Rajah Rasiah, Nina Xie
papers.abstract: Background: Occupation-level AI exposure indices describe the potential overlap between occupational work content and AI capabilities rather than individual AI use or employer adoption. However, task organisation and access to work-linked protections may differ across occupational contexts. We examined whether associations between a compound high-AIOE/high-task-detachability occupational profile and upstream insurance and material conditions varied by migrant anchoring among highly educated foreign-born adults in the United States. Methods: We linked 2017-2024 IPUMS American Community Survey (ACS) data for adults aged 25-64 with a bachelor's degree or higher to AI Occupational Exposure (AIOE) and O*NET 30.3 measures. High AIOE was defined as the top occupational quartile. The focal profile combined high AIOE with high task detachability and was compared with lower-AIOE occupations. Migrant anchoring combined citizenship, US residence duration, English proficiency, family co-residence, and homeownership; scores of 0-2 indicated lower anchoring. The three principal domain-specific outcomes were absence of employer- or union-linked health coverage from any eligible source among employed wage and salary workers, uninsurance, and family income below 200% of the federal poverty threshold. All-adult work-linked Social Reproduction Instability (W-SRI) ≥ 2 was retained as the focal cumulative summary measure. Weighted models were adjusted for demographic, regional, annual, and broad occupational characteristics. Inference used CR2/Satterthwaite covariance, wild cluster bootstrap tests, and leave-one-cluster-out analyses. Results: The analysis included 746,995 foreign-born person-year observations, of which 22.47% were classified as having lower anchoring. Among adults with higher anchoring, the focal occupational profile and lower-AIOE occupations showed few differences in the four principal outcomes. Among adults with lower anchoring, the focal occupational profile was associated with a lower prevalence of all four adverse outcomes. The corresponding between-stratum differences were -10.68 percentage points for absence of employer- or union-linked coverage, -6.75 percentage points for uninsurance, -7.90 percentage points for poverty, and -7.55 percentage points for cumulative burden. Magnitudes remained similar after excluding 2020, restricting the sample to 2018-2024, adding state fixed effects, and restricting the sample to currently employed respondents. In the labour force-restricted analysis, the unemployment modification was -0.37 percentage points (95% CI -1.15 to +0.42) and was imprecisely estimated. Conclusion: Among highly educated foreign-born adults with lower anchoring, the compound occupational profile was associated with a lower prevalence of coverage absence, uninsurance, poverty, and cumulative burden than occupations with lower AIOE. The findings describe occupation-level differences in upstream insurance and material conditions rather than causal effects of AI adoption or task detachability.

papers.title: Development of a master of science in digital health program at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, Tanzania: a mixed-methods curriculum development study
papers.authors: Felix K. Sukums, Linda Simon Paulo, Yoktan Thadeo, Mpanga Paul, Samwel Mndima, Juliana Mbuke, Rebecca Chaula, Junior Kaskazi, Amani Anaeli, Obadia Venance Nyongole
papers.abstract: Background: The rapid expansion of digital technologies is transforming health systems and creating increasing demand for a workforce with competencies in health informatics, data science, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, digital health governance, and implementation. However, digital health training remains fragmented in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), including Tanzania. This study describes the systematic, evidence-based process used to develop an MSc Digital Health program at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS), Tanzania. Methods: A mixed-methods curriculum development approach was undertaken, comprising document review and benchmarking, a quantitative stakeholder survey, qualitative interviews with alumni of the MSc Health Information Management program, and a stakeholder consultative workshop. Nine higher-education and competency-framework sources were reviewed to identify gaps and emerging competency domains. A structured survey was administered to 48 stakeholders purposively selected from government, non-governmental, private-sector, and start-up organizations. Qualitative data from alumni interviews and open-ended survey responses were analyzed thematically using manual coding by two independent coders. A two-day consultative workshop involving 22 stakeholders from academia, professional associations, non-governmental organizations, government, and clinical practice reviewed and validated the proposed curriculum. Results: Benchmarking demonstrated substantial variability in digital health curriculum content, with no single program comprehensively covering all priority competency domains. Stakeholders identified AI and machine learning (48.0%) and big data and analytics (41.7%) as prominent emerging technology competencies, while data science and predictive analytics, health information systems and interoperability, cybersecurity and data privacy, and epidemiology and biostatistics were also emphasized. Overall, 81.3% of survey respondents considered digital health competencies highly important to their organizations, while 89.6% indicated willingness to employ MUHAS MSc Digital Health graduates. Qualitative findings emphasized five priority areas: advanced computing and emerging technologies; applied health data science and analytics; health systems architecture and interoperability; experiential learning and program delivery; and governance, cybersecurity, leadership, and professional ethics. Workshop participants endorsed the proposed curriculum and recommended stronger practical learning, field attachment, innovation-oriented projects, and alignment of course content with emerging workforce needs. The resulting program was structured as a two-year, full-time MSc Digital Health program with three specialization tracks: Digital Health Leadership, Digital Health Systems Development, and Health Data Science and AI. Conclusion: The MUHAS MSc Digital Health curriculum was developed through an iterative, evidence-informed, and stakeholder-driven process that integrates multidisciplinary digital health competencies with practical, implementation-oriented learning. The approach provides a potentially adaptable model for curriculum development in LMIC settings. Future evaluation should assess program implementation, graduate competencies, employment outcomes, employer satisfaction, and contribution to national digital health transformation.

papers.title: Development and internal validation of machine learning models for identifying suicidal behavior in inpatients with mood disorders
papers.authors: Sixiang Liang, Qitong Jiang, Jinhe Zhang, Yannan Deng, Yuxuan Xu, Guangwei Zhao, Xinyu Liu, Yujie Xing, Hongye Yu, Chen Hu, Sha Sha
papers.abstract: Background: Suicidal behavior (SB) is a major concern in mood disorders. Models developed from retrospective records are vulnerable to ambiguous targets, data leakage, and inappropriate handling of class imbalance. We developed and internally validated a model to identify the risk of suicidal behavior in patients with mood disorders upon admission. Methods: The dataset included 1, 099 inpatients with ICD-10 mood disorders admitted to Beijing Anding Hospital in 2022. Exclusion of 20 records with more than 20% row-level missingness and one record without an outcome left 1, 078 patients, including 126 with SB. Current SB comprised documented suicidal ideation, planning, or attempt within the three months before index admission, including the admission assessment. Previous SB and previous suicide attempt (SA) referred to events more than three months before admission. Elastic Net selected 14 predictors from 65 candidates in the development set. We compared 13 classifiers from six model families. All preprocessing and resampling were confined to training folds, and evaluation used only observed patients. Assessment included repeated fivefold cross-validation, probability calibration, bootstrap confidence intervals, precision-recall and decision-curve analyses, clinical baselines, and sensitivity analyses. Results: The analytic cohort comprised 952 SB-negative and 126 SB-positive patients (11.69%). The development set contained 864 patients (97 SB-positive), and the observed test set contained 214 patients (29 SB-positive). Calibrated linear discriminant analysis (LDA) provided the most consistent balance of discrimination and calibration. In repeated cross-validation, mean AUC was 0.721 ± 0.052, mean AUPRC was 0.268 ± 0.060, and mean Brier score was 0.095. In the observed test set, AUC was 0.704 (0.597-0.803), AUPRC was 0.283 (0.198-0.453), and Brier score was 0.111. At the training-derived threshold of 0.111, sensitivity was 0.552 and specificity was 0.659. The leading SHAP contributions were onset-polarity category, previous SA, age, and previous SB, but all attributions were associational. Conclusions: Model performance was acceptable. These internally validated findings are exploratory and require prospective assessment, standardized outcome measurement, and external validation before clinical use.

papers.title: EEG signature in psychiatrist’s subjective experience: a pilot study
papers.authors: Giovanni Videtta, Elena Bondi, Chiara Colli, Gabriele Enrico, Luca Sperti, Mauro Pallagrosi, Laura Fonzi, Ylenia Barone, Giandomenico Schiena, Eleonora Maggioni, Angelo Picardi, Paolo Brambilla
papers.abstract: Introduction: The Assessment of Clinician's Subjective Experience (ACSE) is a self-report questionnaire developed to evaluate clinicians' subjective experiences during patient interactions. While its psychometric properties and clinical validity have been supported, its neurobiological correlates have not yet been investigated. Methods: In this pilot study, two clinicians and ten patients participated in a three-phase protocol comprising: (1) a first clinical interview, (2) ACSE administration, and (3) listening to the audio recording of the first clinical interview. EEG activity was recorded from clinicians during both the first clinical interview and questionnaire administration. Neural data were analyzed in terms of relative power spectral density, node strength, and global efficiency computed from imaginary coherence. Results: Clinicians were psychiatrists, one male and one female. Seven patients were diagnosed with mixed anxiety and depressive disorder, and three with unspecified anxiety disorders. ACSE scores were highest for the Difficulty in attunement and Engagement dimensions, consistent with previous literature. EEG findings revealed dimension-specific and topographically distinct oscillatory patterns for only two ACSE dimensions: Difficulty in Attunement and Engagement. More limited evidence emerged for Disconfirmation. Functional connectivity analyses indicated different network profiles, characterized by differences in global efficiency patterns. Correlational analyses further identified significant associations between ACSE dimensions and EEG-derived features. Discussion: These preliminary findings provide initial evidence that clinicians' subjective experiences during clinical encounters could be associated with measurable neural signatures, offering a novel perspective on the neurobiological basis of intersubjective processes in clinical settings.

papers.title: Problematic reliance on generative AI among university students: an I-PACE-informed PLS-SEM and fsQCA study
papers.authors: Guoqing Liu, Caisang Hou
papers.abstract: Generative AI has become increasingly embedded in university students' academic learning, offering immediate feedback, content generation, and problem-solving support. Alongside these benefits, repeated reliance has raised concerns about problematic dependence on AI-mediated academic support. Drawing on an I-PACE-informed framework, this cross-sectional study examined psychological and academic factors associated with learning-related problematic reliance on generative AI, defined as a non-clinical, self-reported pattern rather than a clinical diagnosis. Data were obtained from a non-probability online sample of 242 university students who had used generative AI for learning-related purposes. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to examine associations among positive affect, generative-AI use self-efficacy, need for cognition, perceived usefulness, cognitive absorption, AI-based mood regulation, academic stress, and problematic reliance on generative AI. Fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) was further used to identify configurations associated with high problematic-reliance membership and its set-theoretic complement. The PLS-SEM results showed that perceived usefulness, cognitive absorption, and academic stress were positively associated with problematic reliance on generative AI, whereas positive affect and AI-based mood regulation did not show significant direct associations. The fsQCA results indicated that no single condition was necessary for high problematic-reliance membership; instead, both outcome sets were associated with multiple configurations. The findings support a cautious distinction between problematic reliance, ordinary generative AI use, and technology acceptance, and they suggest potential implications for AI literacy and academic support in higher education.

papers.title: The relationship between challenge-hindrance stressors and AI dependence among art students: the mediating roles of creative self-efficacy and positive experiences
papers.authors: Huali FAN, Yuan Wang, Shengwu Pan, Shuai Shao
papers.abstract: Background Despite growing concerns about art students’ over-reliance on generative AI tools, existing research has largely treated academic stress as a uniform construct, overlooking the possibility that different types of stressors may drive AI dependence through distinct psychological pathways. Methods Based on the Interaction of Person-Affect-Cognition-Execution (I-PACE) model, this study examines the relationships between Challenge-Hindrance stressors (CHS) and AI dependence among art students. It explores the mediating roles of creative self-efficacy and positive experiences. A questionnaire survey was conducted among 580 art students using the Challenge-Hindrance Stress Scale, the Creative Self-Efficacy Scale, the Positive Experiences Scale, and the AI Dependence Scale. Results Path analysis revealed that both challenge stressors ( β = 0.245, p < 0.001) and hindrance stressors ( β = 0.322, p < 0.001) were positively associated with AI dependence; challenge stressors were negatively associated with creative self-efficacy ( β = −0.155, p = 0.003) and positively associated with positive experiences ( β = 0.268, p < 0.001); the negative association between hindrance stressors and creative self-efficacy was significant ( β = −0.107, p = 0.043). Mediation analysis indicated that creative self-efficacy played a significant mediating role only in the path involving challenge stressors (indirect effect = 0.023, 95% CI [0.007, 0.044]) and was not significant in the path involving hindrance stressors; positive experiences significantly served as a mediator in the relationships between both challenge stressors (indirect effect = 0.042, 95% CI [0.020, 0.068]) and hindrance stressors (indirect effect = 0.019, 95% CI [0.003, 0.039]) on AI dependence. The chain mediation effects did not reach significance in either path. Conclusion The study found asymmetry in the dual pathways by which Challenge and Hindrance stressors relate to AI dependence. These findings extend the I-PACE model to the issue of AI dependence in arts education and provide empirical evidence and intervention insights for targeted prevention of problematic AI use.

papers.title: Exploring antecedents and consequences of value co-creation of women entrepreneurs: a conceptual framework and research agenda
papers.authors: Bello Hassan, Bahtiar Mohamad
papers.abstract: This study examines the antecedents and outcomes of value co-creation among women entrepreneurs, emphasizing the importance of addressing the unique challenges they encounter in entrepreneurial activities. While prior studies have investigated women's entrepreneurial motivations and barriers, the concept of value co-creation in this context remains insufficiently explored, thereby limiting theoretical development in the field. This conceptual paper develops a model derived from an extensive, critical, and multidisciplinary literature review. The review synthesizes insights from entrepreneurship, management, and network theory to explain how individual dynamic capabilities, opportunity recognition, entrepreneurial orientation, and entrepreneurial networks collectively foster value co-creation among women entrepreneurs. The study identifies four key antecedents of value co-creation: individual dynamic capabilities, opportunity recognition, entrepreneurial orientation, and entrepreneurial networks. It also proposes that value co-creation positively influences business performance. The study introduces an integrative conceptual framework and formulates five testable hypotheses to guide future empirical research. The paper provides theoretical and practical insights for policymakers and entrepreneurship support organizations to enhance women's entrepreneurial success through value co-creation strategies.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and mortality risk of sarcopenia in interstitial lung disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.authors: Lijuan Zhou, Xuan Wang, Weiwei Yuan, Yahui Yang, Ting Lu, Lu Guo, Xing He
papers.abstract: Objective Sarcopenia, prevalent in interstitial lung disease (ILD), increases the risk of poor outcomes. This study aimed to define the clinical characteristics of ILD patients with sarcopenia (ILD-S) and quantify sarcopenia's impact on mortality. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus for English studies up to 1 September 2026 reporting clinical variables (mean ± SD) in ILD vs. ILD-S groups and adjusted hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CI) for mortality risk. Subgroup analyses were stratified by sarcopenia diagnostic criteria, ILD subtype, and survival time. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q and I 2 statistics. Sensitivity analyses (leave-one-out) and publication bias assessments (Egger's test, trim-and-fill method) were performed. Results Fourteen studies comprising 1,546 participants (628 with ILD-S) were included. Compared with ILD patients without sarcopenia, those with ILD-S were significantly older (WMD = 3.03, 95% CI: 2.12–3.93), had higher Gender-Age-Physiology (GAP) scores (WMD = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.15 to 0.71), and a higher FEV₁/FVC ratio (WMD = 1.97, 95% CI: 0.21 to 3.73, P = 0.03). Conversely, the ILD-S group showed lower values for FEV₁% predicted (WMD = −6.95, 95% CI: −9.80 to −4.09), FVC% predicted (WMD = −9.46, 95% CI: −12.04 to −6.88), DLCO% predicted (WMD = −5.87, 95% CI: −11.68 to −0.06), body mass index (WMD = −1.35, 95% CI: −1.89 to −0.82), handgrip strength (WMD = −12.80, 95% CI: −17.02 to −8.58), 6-minute walk distance (WMD = −31.01, 95% CI: −60.05 to −1.97), and appendicular skeletal muscle index (WMD = −1.45, 95% CI: −2.15 to −0.76). No significant difference was observed in smoking history. Sarcopenia was strongly associated with increased mortality risk (HR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.67 to 2.45), and this association remained stable across different follow-up periods. Sensitivity and publication bias analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings. Conclusion Patients with ILD-S exhibit a distinctive profile characterized by older age, higher GAP scores, poorer pulmonary function, lower BMI, reduced muscle strength and mass, and significantly elevated mortality. Systematic recognition of these clinical features may facilitate early identification of ILD-S and inform the development of targeted interventions to improve patient outcomes. Systematic Review Registration https://inplasy.com/ , INPLASY202570030.

papers.title: Empowering student-led climate solutions: the role of AI in STEAM education
papers.authors: Shahinaz Abdelrahman Osman, Fatima Alhammadi, Marwa Arshi, Haleimah Alsamahi, Hanan  Ahmad Alsaedy
papers.abstract: This convergent mixed-methods study investigates the strategic integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into a university-level STEAM curriculum to empower students to design climate solutions. Combining quantitative survey data from 69 undergraduate students selected via a complete cohort census sampling approach (response rate: 84.1%) and multi-tiered purposive qualitative interviews with N = 25 participants ( N = 11 experts, N = 9 faculty members, and N = 5 student innovators), the findings indicate high technological familiarity and widespread adoption (100% AI tool use). Specifically, students reported the highest agreement for AI enhancing their creativity and learning independence (86.9%, M = 4.12), supporting their capacity to pivot from data collection to strategic solution design (73.9%, M = 3.78), and bolstering their perceived empowerment to propose climate solutions (76.8%, M = 3.84). Furthermore, self-reported student perceptions indicated that AI supported their critical thinking process (68.1%, M = 3.65), representing perceived cognitive scaffolding rather than an objective measure of skill performance. This supports the qualitative finding that AI acts as a “Complexity Mediator” in climate tasks. However, notable concerns were reported regarding accuracy (60.9%) and plagiarism (59.4%). To address this, the study proposes the AI-Empowered STEAM Climate Action Model (AISC-AM), a conceptual framework that structures STEAM as a Multi-Scalar Problem-Solving Ecosystem and mandates critical AI literacy and an “AI-in-the-Loop” validation structure. Informed by preliminary stakeholder appraisal, the proposed AISC-AM offers a structured pedagogical workflow to mitigate operational risks while connecting student-led research to regional climate policy platforms via youth organizational partnerships.

papers.title: A qualitative inquiry on redefining students' assessments in the age of artificial intelligence: academicians' viewpoint
papers.authors: Muhammad Shoaib Saleem, Maheen Iqbal Awan, Fouzia Mueen, Asif Saeed Naji, Gehad Mohammed Ahmed Naji, Prince Manu
papers.abstract: Purpose Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents new opportunities and challenges, and its adoption has transformed learning and development for students. Current studies have mostly explored the use of AI among students, with very little emphasis on its impact on teaching and learning tasks, academicians' professional identities, and student-teacher interaction. This research examines the pedagogical, professional, and institutional implications of students' use of AI from the perspective of academic staff at private universities in Malaysia. Design A structured interview protocol with ten open-ended questions was adopted to implement the qualitative exploratory research design. The final sample consisted of 18 academicians with at least 5 years of teaching experience in higher education and who have been involved in assessing undergraduate, master's, and postgraduate students' assignments. Data were analyzed through open coding, axial coding, and thematic analysis. Findings The results identified six interrelated themes: (1) workload intensification and assessment burden; (2) changes in educators' roles; (3) transformation of the educator's professional identity; (4) pedagogical adaptations and assessment redesign; (5) challenges of academic integrity and AI detection; and (6) finally, coping strategies, institutional support, and future readiness. AI use by pupils is transforming academic tasks by adding workload for teachers, necessitating new roles for teachers as “gatekeepers of academic quality”, and creating tensions around identity issues for teachers. Behaviours such as adaptive teaching, redesigning assessments, seeking greater institutional support and clearer governance, and requiring AI education programs are prominent for academicians. Originality The study contributes to the existing literature on generative AI in higher education by demonstrating that the implications of AI-supported learning extend beyond academic integrity to encompass changes in academic processes, teaching roles, and institutional practices. The study provides novel insights from the firsthand experiences of academicians witnessing this paradigm shift in the higher-education context. The results offer practical guidance for institutions aiming to establish responsible AI governance and sustainable assessment practices in the growing AI-driven learning landscape.

papers.title: Synthetic gatekeeping in health chatbots: configured answer systems as the unit of AI evaluation and governance for medical information
papers.authors: Simona Wójcik, Justyna Domienik‐Karłowicz, Anna Rulkiewicz
papers.abstract: Two health chatbots can give the same clinically appropriate advice and still constitute different interventions: one stops at a clinician referral, the other places an affiliated booking one click away. In this Hypothesis and Theory article we argue that the appropriate unit of health-AI evaluation is therefore not the model output alone, but the configured answer system - the large language model (LLM) together with source selection, retrieval, interface, action routing and downstream data return. We call this organizationally configured mode of mediation synthetic gatekeeping. Its necessary core comprises source selection and generative synthesis, with personalization and action routing as extending dimensions; its observable manifestations are content and pathway traces, and its proposed mechanism is infrastructural steering. Content parity does not guarantee pathway parity: two systems can name the same options while making only one easily actionable. Organizational position, revenue architecture and integration depth are treated as exposures that may shape these functions, not as elements of the construct, and owner-linked advantage is an empirical outcome to be demonstrated rather than assumed. Direct health evidence of owner- or revenue-linked steering remains sparse, and one comparative study found LLM answers less commercially biased than conventional search; the mechanisms nonetheless appear in adjacent domains, and health outputs are configurable at deployment level. We advance three core propositions - organizational alignment (P1), pathway asymmetry (P2) and behavioural mediation (P4) - with one conditional moderator hypothesis on conversion-linked funding (P3) and a measurement corollary on surface-pathway divergence (M1), each stated with its weakening condition. The framework yields a practical audit model based on configuration anchoring, paired content-pathway comparison, organizational disclosure and proportionate governance triggers. The unit of evaluation should move from the model output to the configured answer system in which information becomes action.

papers.title: ‘We should be in this…’: telling the story of the Missing Piece study
papers.authors: Kassandra Fernando, Ann Grand, Heather J. Bray, Rebecca Dalton, Bernadette Wong, Asha C Bowen, Janessa L. Pickering
papers.abstract: Introduction The Missing Piece Surveillance study was a school-based surveillance study documenting group A Streptococcus (Strep A) infection in children in two towns of the Kimberley region of Western Australia (Broome and Derby). The Kimberley experiences higher rates of the serious immune-mediated conditions acute rheumatic fever (ARF) and rheumatic heart disease (RHD), which can result from Strep A infection. The clinical epidemiological study aimed to document the prevalence and features of superficial Strep A infections, particularly impetigo (skin sores) and pharyngitis (sore throat) in children aged 5-15. Surveillance required several years of collaboration with participants, their families, their teachers and their schools to support primary data collection. Methods Following the completion of surveillance, the research team aimed to find a way to share their findings with the communities they worked with, particularly with the children who has provided their time and biological samples. In this study, we describe the use and value of participatory action research methods to co-create two storybooks telling the stories of the Missing Piece study. Results Through consultation, focus groups and reflection, we explored how the design, content and use of storybooks could create meaning for participants. Discussion Resultingly, children's voices and preferences were incorporated into the communication tool, producing an outcome that reflected participatory action methodology and co-creation.

papers.title: Metaverse and generative AI in education: a scoping review of technologies, applications, evaluation, challenges, and future directions
papers.authors: Muhammad Tukur, Wala Elsharif, Ahmad Sani Bello, Babatunde Abiodun Salami, Isa Ali Ibrahim, Mowafa Said Househ, Jens Schneider, George Mikros, Marco Agus
papers.abstract: The convergence of Metaverse technologies and Generative AI (GenAI) is reshaping immersive digital education. This study presents a scoping review of Metaverse and GenAI-enabled education following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. A systematic search of ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink identified 114 primary studies published or indexed from January 2022 up to the respective database search dates in 2026. Based on the synthesized evidence, we propose a comprehensive taxonomy that classifies existing research across application domains, Metaverse technologies, GenAI categories, target user groups, degrees of freedom (DoF), pedagogical foundations, evaluation practices, technical limitations, and future research directions. The reviewed studies show that Virtual Reality (VR) is the predominant immersive modality (61%), while OpenAI-based models represent the most widely adopted GenAI ecosystem (60%). Applications are concentrated primarily in STEM, higher education, and healthcare, where immersive learning environments increasingly incorporate intelligent tutoring, adaptive feedback, virtual agents, and automated content generation. Although 68% (77 articles) of the reviewed studies reported user perceptual evaluations, these predominantly focused on short-term usability and engagement, with comparatively limited attention to longitudinal learning effectiveness, knowledge retention, cognitive outcomes, AI trustworthiness, accessibility, inclusivity, and real-world deployment. This imbalance reveals a central maturity gap: technological sophistication is advancing faster than the educational evidence needed to establish sustained learning effectiveness and real-world readiness. Commonly reported challenges include limited empirical validation, system maturity, scalability, interoperability, AI trustworthiness, immersive performance, accessibility, and ethical governance. Based on these findings, we identify key priorities for future research, including longitudinal and pedagogically grounded evaluation, scalable and interoperable system architectures, trustworthy AI, inclusive and ecologically valid validation, and stronger integration of pedagogical and governance considerations. The proposed taxonomy provides an evidence-based framework to support future research, comparative analysis, and the design of Metaverse and GenAI-enabled educational systems.

papers.title: Variable task difficulty with augmented sensory feedback for motor training in virtual reality
papers.authors: Yu Shi, Sophie Dewil, Zachary Marvin, Noam Y. Harel, Raviraj Nataraj
papers.abstract: Introduction: This study examined how motor task difficulty and augmented sensory feedback (ASF) modality influence task performance, physiological responses, and perceptual experience during virtual reality (VR)-based upper-limb motor training. Building on related brace- and VR-based ASF platforms previously examined in neurotypical and spinal cord injury cohorts, the long-term goal is to support neurorehabilitation-oriented adaptive VR training; however, the present study used neurotypical participants as an initial validation step. Methods: Fourteen right-handed neurotypical participants used a supportive upper-limb brace and surface electromyography (EMG) for myoelectric control of a virtual robotic arm in a two-dimensional tracking task. A 2 × 2 within-subject design crossed ASF modality (visual feedback versus visual + haptic feedback) with task difficulty (straight-line versus sinusoidal trajectory). Outcomes included normalized path length, task completion time, movement jerk, alpha- and beta-band electroencephalogram (EEG) power over motor cortex, heart rate, EMG amplitude, EMG-displacement-based virtual work, and perceptual ratings of agency, motivation, and utility. Short-term pre-to-post percentage changes were computed for each measure. Results: VHF straight-line training produced the largest reductions in normalized path length (-4.69%) and completion time (-6.12%), whereas VHF sinusoid training produced the largest reductions in movement jerk (-5.67%) and virtual work (-13.33%). ASF modality affected path length, completion time, jerk, EMG amplitude, and virtual work, whereas task difficulty modulated beta-band EEG power and the physiological index. Changes in path length were positively associated with changes in completion time and EMG amplitude. Discussion: These findings suggest that ASF modality and task difficulty can differentially shape short-term behavioral, physiological, and perceptual responses in healthy participants. The exploratory distribution of participant-specific best-case conditions motivates future studies using independent trial subsets to evaluate whether behavioral and physiological measures can support individualized VR training.

papers.title: KoKoRo: The Curious Chicken A New Garment for Memory, Reflection, and AI-enhanced Curiosity
papers.authors: Leticia Izquierdo Garcia, Lucy Li, Sarah Barreto Ornellas, Seungwook Han, Marcello Coehlo
papers.abstract: Curiosity is a fundamental driver of learning, yet everyday life offers few tools that actively cultivate it. We present KoKoRo: The Curious Chicken, a wearable memory-capture device and an accompanying base, together designed to augment curiosity. As users move through their day, the necklace records audio and contextual moments on demand, building a personal memory of lived experience. In doing so, KoKoRo shifts where creative agency begins: rather than requiring the user to consciously decide what is worth remembering in the moment, it captures first and invites reflection later, returning full agency to the user when they engage with the egg, choosing which moments to revisit, which questions to ask, and which doubts to pursue. We describe the design rationale, the technical implementation of a functional prototype built around an Xiao ESP32S3 microcontroller with integrated camera (Sense Module) and microphone, and the interaction model that anthropomorphizes memory retrieval.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly Semaglutide for weight management in adults with overweight or obesity with or without type 2 diabetes: A real-world clinical trial in Bangladesh
papers.authors: Quazi Tarikul Islam
papers.journal: Journal of Association of Clinical Endocrinologist and Diabetologist of Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Introduction: Semaglutide has shown substantial weight reduction in trials, but real-world evidence from South Asian populations is scarce. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide 2·4 mg over 26 weeks in adults with overweight or obesity, with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Methods: In this single-arm, non-randomised study, adults (≥18 years) with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) or overweight (BMI 25–29·9 kg/m²), with or without T2DM, received semaglutide initiated at 0·25 mg and escalated to 2·4 mg by week 16. The primary endpoint was percentage change in bodyweight at week 26. Secondary outcomes included changes in BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, glycaemic and lipid parameters, and obesity-specific quality of life (OSQoL), alongside proportions achieving ≥5%, ≥10%, ≥15%, and ≥20% weight loss. Analyses followed intention-to-treat principles using linear mixed models. Results: Among 435 participants (154 T2DM, 281 non-T2DM; mean age 38.7, SD 11.1 years; 76% female), mean weight reduction at 26 weeks was −9.5% (95% CI −10.1 to −8.8%), greater in non-T2DM than T2DM (−9.7% vs −9.2%; p=0.044). Overall, 87% achieved ≥5% weight loss, 59% ≥10%, 23% ≥15%, and 7% ≥20% and all were statistically significant. BMI decreased by −4·0 kg/m² and waist circumference by −7·3 cm. Blood pressure declined (−6·5/−3·3 mmHg), and HbA1c decreased by −1·2% in T2DM. OSQoL improved by 10·0 points. Common adverse events were gastrointestinal; two serious events occurred. Conclusions: In this cohort, semaglutide 2·4 mg was associated with clinically meaningful weight loss and acceptable tolerability over 26 weeks. [J Assoc Clin Endocrinol Diabetol Bangladesh, 2026;5(Suppl 1): S30]

papers.title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent-Based Chatbot for Al-Hikmah University
papers.authors: Abdulrauf Tosho
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the delivery of academic support services through intelligent conversational systems capable of providing timely and accurate responses to users. Traditional methods of obtaining information within higher education institutions often rely on manual interactions with administrative staff, resulting in delays, increased workload, and limited accessibility outside official working hours. This study presents the design and implementation of an intelligent-based chatbot for Al-Hikmah University to automate responses to students' academic enquiries. The chatbot was developed using a retrieval-based architecture integrated with Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to understand user queries and retrieve relevant responses from an institutional knowledge base. The system was implemented using React.js for the frontend, Node.js and Express.js for the backend, MongoDB as the database management system, and Google's Gemini API to enhance conversational intelligence. Functional and usability evaluations were conducted using representative student queries covering admission, registration, course information, tuition fees, examinations, and academic regulations. Experimental results demonstrated that the chatbot provides 98% accurate responses with low response within one to two seconds latency while remaining available twenty-four hours a day. The proposed system improves accessibility to institutional information, reduces the workload on administrative personnel, and enhances students' overall experience. The study concludes that AI-powered academic chatbots can significantly improve digital service delivery in Nigerian universities and recommends future integration with voice recognition, multilingual support, and student information systems.

papers.title: From Likes to Logic: Explainable Machine Learning for Higher-Education Social Media Engagement
papers.authors: Siddhi Patel, Sheshang Degadwala, Dharvi Soni
papers.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Social media is used by higher educational institutions in order to communicate, build their reputations, recruit students, engage in stakeholder relations and engage with the public. Machine learning can predict post-level engagement by analyzing features and characteristics of the content, time, platform, sentiment, and interaction metrics; however, the ability to predict doesn't account for why a post is likely to be successful. This review brings together recent literature on social media engagement in higher education; machine learning prediction of social media engagement; and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) research from related disciplines in education, highlighting the disconnect between higher education social media engagement research and XAI research occurring in neighboring higher education fields. The literature is categorized into three classes according to the target of engagement, the modality of the data, the platform, the model family, and the explanation strategy. Content and plat-form context are shown to be lasting factors, while cross-platform generalization, multimodal representation, temporal robustness, causal interpretation, and ex-planation quality are all shown to be under-developed. A conceptual workflow is synthesized from the source presentation and existing literature spanning from the data collection to the data preprocessing, feature selection, model training, prediction, explanation, and decision support. The research agenda emerging from these focuses on time-aware validation, multi-institution datasets, semantic and multimodal features, stable and human-centric explanations, causal evaluation, and responsible data governance. The outline is designed as a reference architecture based on the review, not as a report of the experimental results that have been acquired.

papers.title: Mapping Arabic language education research: A bibliometric study of pedagogy, technology, and applied linguistics
papers.authors: Hendri Sukma, Agus Pahrudin, Koderi Koderi, Oki Dermawan, Iin Yulianti
papers.abstract: This study aims to map the global development of Arabic language education research through a bibliometric analysis of publication trends, journal sources, contributing institutions, countries of corresponding authors, and the most-cited documents. It also analyses keyword co-occurrence to identify major research themes, emerging trends, and potential future directions. Data were collected from the Scopus database using a structured search query, resulting in 166 documents after a rigorous screening process. Prior to analysis, metadata were cleaned using OpenRefine to ensure consistency and accuracy by standardizing author names, institutional affiliations, and keyword variations. Bibliometric analysis was conducted using Biblioshiny (R) and VOSviewer. In the VOSviewer analysis, a thesaurus file was applied to standardize terminology and eliminate duplication, ensuring accurate thematic mapping. The findings indicate a significant increase in publications over the past decade, reflecting growing academic interest in Arabic language education. The results show a strong dominance of technology-oriented journals, particularly in artificial intelligence and natural language processing. Research productivity is concentrated in the Middle East, especially in Saudi Arabia and Egypt, although international collaboration is gradually increasing. Highly cited documents tend to focus on computational approaches and the development of linguistic resources, highlighting their central role in advancing the field. Thematic analysis reveals five major research clusters, including machine learning, pedagogy, computational linguistics, speech processing, and natural language processing. The evolution of research topics shows a shift from traditional teaching approaches to advanced technologies such as deep learning and large language models. These patterns indicate an increasing integration of pedagogical and technological perspectives in the field. Future research directions include the development of large-scale Arabic datasets, the integration of explainable artificial intelligence, adaptive learning systems, and ethical considerations in AI-based education. These findings provide empirical insights for researchers and policymakers to support evidence-based development in Arabic language education.

papers.title: AI-based performance appraisal in Vietnamese firms: Examining its impact on employee retention through job satisfaction
papers.authors: Ho Hai, Hai Le Mai, Hoa Nguyen Ngoc Thanh
papers.abstract: This study investigates the impact of AI-based performance appraisal on employee retention, with particular emphasis on the mediating role of job satisfaction. Grounded in Social Exchange Theory, the research explains how AI-driven evaluation systems shape employees’ perceptions and behavioral intentions in the context of digital transformation. Despite the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence in human resource management, empirical evidence on the psychological mechanisms linking AI-enabled practices to employee retention remains limited, particularly in emerging economies. A quantitative cross-sectional research design was employed, using convenience sampling to collect data from 328 employees working in Vietnamese organizations that had implemented AI-based performance appraisal systems. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess both direct and indirect relationships among constructs. The findings indicate that AI-PA is positively associated with job satisfaction, suggesting that employees who report more positive perceptions of AI-driven evaluation systems tend to report higher levels of job satisfaction. Job satisfaction, in turn, is positively associated with employee retention and partially mediates the relationship between AI-PA and retention outcomes. Additionally, the results reveal that the frequency of AI usage significantly enhances retention intention, whereas demographic variables such as age and tenure do not exhibit significant effects, highlighting that employees’ interaction and experience with AI systems play a more critical role than personal characteristics. This study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence on the underlying psychological mechanism linking AI adoption and employee retention in an emerging market context. From a managerial perspective, the findings suggest that organizations should not only adopt AI technologies but also improve transparency, user experience, and employee engagement with AI systems to enhance long-term retention outcomes.

papers.title: IMPLEMENTASI LMS LENTERA 101752 UNTUK PENGUATAN KOMPETENSI DIGITAL GURU DALAM PEMBELAJARAN LITERASI ADAPTIF DI SEKOLAH DASAR
papers.authors: Fanny Ramadhani, Dian Septiana, Andy Satria, Salamah Salamah
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Kegiatan pengabdian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh kebutuhan penguatan kompetensi digital guru sekolah dasar serta kebutuhan alternatif pembelajaran yang lebih fleksibel pada sekolah mitra yang menghadapi gangguan pembelajaran akibat banjir musiman. Kegiatan bertujuan meningkatkan kompetensi digital guru melalui implementasi LMS LENTERA 101752 serta pelatihan pengembangan media berbantuan Generative AI dan Augmented Reality (AR). Kegiatan dilaksanakan melalui pelatihan dan workshop dengan mitra guruSD Negeri di, Kabupaten Deli Serdang, yang melibatkan 21 guru. Evaluasi dilakukan melalui observasi selama kegiatan serta pre-test dan post-test kompetensi digital. Data pre-test dan post-test dianalisis secara deskriptif dengan membandingkan nilai rata-rata sebelum dan sesudah kegiatan, menghitung selisih peningkatan nilai dan persentase peningkatan, serta menentukan proporsi peserta yang mengalami peningkatan nilai Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan rata-rata nilai meningkat dari 62,11 menjadi 82,63 atau meningkat 20,53 poin (33,05%) dengan N-gain 0,54 (kategori sedang) dan 94,74% peserta mengalami peningkatan nilai. Kegiatan memberikan progres positif terhadap kompetensi digital guru dalam memanfaatkan LMS, Generative AI, dan AR untuk mendukung pengembangan pembelajaran yang lebih fleksibel dan interaktif.Abstract: This community engagement program was motivated by the need to strengthen elementary school teachers’ digital competence and provide more flexible learning alternatives in a partner school affected by seasonal flooding. The program aimed to improve teachers’ digital competence through the implementation of the LENTERA 101752 Learning Management System (LMS) and training in developing learning media using Generative AI and Augmented Reality (AR). The activities were conducted through training and workshops involving 21 teachers from a public elementary school in Deli Serdang Regency.
