Evaluation was conducted through observation during the activities, as well as pre-test and post-test assessments of teachers’ digital competence. The data were analyzed descriptively by comparing the mean scores before and after the activities, calculating the difference and percentage increase, and determining the proportion of participants whose scores improved. The evaluation results showed that the mean score increased from 62.11 to 82.63, representing an increase of 20.53 points (33.05%), with an N-gain of 0.54 (moderate category), and 94.74% of participants showing an improvement in their scores. The program demonstrated positive progress in teachers’ digital competence in utilizing LMS, Generative AI, and AR to support more flexible and interactive learning.

papers.title: Implementasi Ekosistem Multimedia Berbasis Kecerdasan Buatan dan Web GIS dalam Pembelajaran Siklus Air di Sekolah Dasar
papers.authors: Sadewa Purba Sejati, Fitria Nuraini Sekarsih
papers.abstract: Abstract: Water cycle education at the elementary school level often faces challenges due to abstract concept visualization, causing students to memorize text without understanding real-world environmental dynamics. This community service initiative aims to deliver interactive water cycle learning at SD N Bronggang Baru using a modern multimedia ecosystem. The program was carried out through technology implementation followed by mentoring and evaluation phases. The participants included 28 fifth-grade students and a companion teacher, utilizing the school’s multimedia room. The implemented multimedia ecosystem combines Google Veo AI-based animated videos, Google Gemini AI-based educational games, and a web GIS platform. The results demonstrate that integrating artificial intelligence and web GIS significantly boosts student enthusiasm and active classroom participation. The final evaluation shows clear progress in student comprehension; they are now able to fully understand hydrological processes while connecting atmospheric phenomena with field-level groundwater conditions. Furthermore, students' critical thinking skills were enhanced through their active involvement in formulating solutions to local environmental issues. This program recommends replicating similar applied community service projects to strengthen spatial and disaster literacy in primary education.Abstrak: Pembelajaran materi siklus air di tingkat sekolah dasar sering kali menghadapi kendala visualisasi konsep yang abstrak, sehingga siswa cenderung menghafal secara tekstual tanpa memahami dinamika lingkungan nyata. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk melaksanakan pembelajaran siklus air yang interaktif di SD N Bronggang Baru menggunakan ekosistem multimedia modern. Metode pelaksanaan dilakukan melalui penerapan teknologi serta pendampingan dan evaluasi. Sasaran kegiatan melibatkan 28 siswa kelas 5 dan guru pendamping, bertempat di ruang multimedia sekolah. Ekosistem multimedia yang diimplementasikan mengombinasikan video animasi berbasis AI Google Veo, permainan edukatif berbasis AI Google Gemini, dan platform web GIS . Hasil pelaksanaan menunjukkan bahwa integrasi teknologi kecerdasan buatan dan web GIS secara signifikan mampu meningkatkan antusiasme dan partisipasi aktif siswa di kelas. Evaluasi akhir menunjukkan perkembangan nyata pada pemahaman siswa, yang kini mampu memahami proses hidrologi secara utuh sekaligus mengaitkan fenomena atmosfer dengan kondisi air tanah di lapangan. Kemampuan berpikir kritis siswa juga terasah melalui keaktifan dalam merumuskan solusi atas masalah lingkungan di sekitar mereka. Program ini merekomendasikan replikasi pengabdian terapan sejenis untuk penguatan literasi spasial dan kebencanaan pada pendidikan dasar.

papers.title: Transforming Chemotherapy Support: An Interactive Chatbot That Boosts Discipline and Satisfaction in Colorectal Cancer Patients in Makassar
papers.authors: Julianus Aboyaman Uwuratuw, Warsinggih, Citra Aryanti
papers.journal: Asian Pacific Journal of Cancer Biology
papers.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer patients frequently struggled with treatment adherence due to chemotherapy-related toxicities and psychological burden. Digital interventions such as chatbots had emerged as promising tools to support symptom monitoring and patient engagement. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of an interactive chemotherapy-support chatbot on treatment discipline and patient satisfaction among colorectal cancer patients in Makassar. Materials and Methods: A quasi-experimental design was conducted involving 60 colorectal cancer patients undergoing adjuvant chemotherapy. Participants were divided into an intervention group using a Telegram-based chatbot (n = 30) and a control group receiving standard care (n = 30). Primary outcomes were chemotherapy discipline, defined as completion of four scheduled sessions, and user satisfaction measured using a five-item Likert scale. Results: The intervention group achieved significantly higher chemotherapy discipline compared with the control group (90% vs. 50%). The mean number of completed sessions was higher in the intervention group (3.9 vs. 3.1). User satisfaction was very high (mean score 4.69/5), with the reminder feature receiving the highest rating (4.90). The chatbot also reduced discipline-related psychological issues, with no reported psychological dropout in the intervention group. Conclusion: The interactive chatbot substantially improved chemotherapy adherence and patient satisfaction. Its implementation demonstrated strong potential for wider adoption in Indonesian oncology services.

papers.title: A Multi-Biomarker Signature of Immune Activation and Metabolic Shift Predicts Treatment Success in Localized Prostate Cancer
papers.authors: Abdulqader M. Abdulqader, Muqdad Khamis Abd, Kawthar Amer Al-Shamari, Waleed Khalid Ahmed
papers.journal: Asian Pacific Journal of Cancer Biology
papers.abstract: Background: Prostate cancer’s response to therapy varies significantly, and traditional markers like PSA offer limited prognostic insight. A thorough understanding of systemic immune and metabolic changes post-treatment is essential for developing better predictive tools. Objective: To characterize the profiles of circulating immune and metabolic biomarkers prior to and following definitive therapy in patients with localized prostate cancer, and to assess their efficacy in distinguishing biochemical responders from non-responders. Materials and Methods: This prospective study involved 90 patients with prostate adenocarcinoma treated at the Oncology Teaching Hospital / Baghdad Teaching Hospital, between February 2024 and February 2025. Patients underwent radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy, with or without androgen deprivation therapy. Blood samples were collected at baseline and three months post-treatment to measure six biomarkers (GFRAL, adenosine (AD), interleukin-39 (IL-39), TRAIL, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and SDF1) using ELISA. Treatment response was defined as PSA below 6.5 ng/mL. Data were analyzed using nonparametric tests, machine learning, ROC analysis, and multivariate regression, with stratification by treatment type to evaluate intervention-specific changes in biomarkers. Results: Following treatment, responders exhibited a distinct molecular profile characterized by significantly increased levels of SDF1 and IL-39, along with decreased concentrations of AD and LPS. SDF1 was identified as the most reliable individual predictor, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.89. A multivariable model including SDF1, AD, and IL-39 demonstrated improved predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.92, with a sensitivity of 89.1% and specificity of 85.7%. Multivariate analysis confirmed that SDF1 and AD are independent predictors of response, after adjusting for age, Gleason score, baseline PSA, and treatment modality. Conclusion: Effective prostate cancer treatment prompts a systemic immunometabolic transformation towards a reparative and immune-active state. A multi-biomarker panel, notably including SDF1, AD, and IL-39, emerges as a promising discovery-phase signature that, following independent external validation, may provide a non-invasive method for monitoring therapeutic response, but further validation is needed before clinical use.

papers.title: High School Students’ Perceptions and Motivation toward Using AI to Enhance English Speaking Skills
papers.authors: Lilis Patimah Muttaqin, Riki Ruswandi, Hamdan Hidayat
papers.abstract: The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies in education has a significant impact on language learning, particularly in the acquisition of English language skills. The purpose of this research was to explore high school students' attitudes towards the use of AI technologies to develop English-speaking ability, as well as their attitudes towards the application of AI to improve speaking skills. A quantitative descriptive statistics approach was used in the present research, with mean scores and standard deviations as the data analysis methods. 32 students of grade 11 studying at MAS Manbaul Huda participated in the research and were selected based on the criteria of having some experience with using AI technology for learning English. The research data were obtained with the help of a survey developed in accordance with TAM, SDT, and the framework suggested by Harris for measuring speaking skills. Students had a positive attitude toward using AI for English speaking exercises (M = 3.91), and motivation to use it was rather high (M = 3.80). Speaking in general was considered a skill to be supported by AI (M = 3.78).

papers.title: Tricky Trade-Offs on a Transparency Spectrum: How the Financial Times Approaches Transparency about AI Use in News
papers.authors: Liz Lohn, Felix M. Simon
papers.abstract: As news organisations adopt artificial intelligence (AI), they face growing pressure to be transparent about when and how it is used – yet practical approaches remain uneven. This paper examines AI transparency through an in-depth case study of the Financial Times (FT). Drawing on 13 semi-structured interviews with 12 senior managers across editorial, product, data science, and communications, together with internal documents, we show that the FT approaches transparency as a hybrid of policy, process, and practice, framed by a desire to safeguard both internal and external trust. Transparency is calibrated to context: internally, AI use is signposted in tools and reinforced through training and personal accountability; externally, the prominence of disclosure scales with system autonomy and editorial oversight, with stronger labelling for no-human-in-the-loop features than for AI-assisted, journalist-edited outputs. We identify nine factors that shape audience-facing disclosure – legal/provider requirements, industry benchmarking, nature of the task, human oversight, system novelty, audience expectations, perceived risk, commercial sensitivities, and design constraints – and five crosscutting challenges, including site-wide consistency (especially on mobile) and potential “transparency backfire.” Conceptually, our analysis links AI transparency to isomorphic pressures and to intersecting institutional logics. We argue that AI transparency in news is best understood as a spectrum, evolving with technological advancements, commercial, professional and ethical considerations and shifting audience attitudes.

papers.title: Loneliness is reflected in the sub-second temporal dynamics of the resting brain: an EEG microstate study
papers.authors: Kentaro Ono
papers.abstract: Loneliness, a subjective state of perceived social isolation characterized by chronic social hypervigilance, is a profound risk factor for physical and mental health conditions. While functional neuroimaging studies link loneliness to altered salience network connectivity, the sub-second temporal dynamics of the resting lonely brain remain unexplored. We investigated the relationship between trait loneliness and resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) microstates. Sixty-one healthy young adults completed the UCLA Loneliness Scale and Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) and underwent 3-minute resting-state EEG recording. A criterion-based five-class microstate solution identified a topography corresponding to the canonical Class C/E, associated with both self-referential and salience-related processing. Higher loneliness scores were significantly associated with reduced Class C/E occurrence, which remained significant after controlling for depressive symptoms, age, and sex. Exploratory source localization revealed that lonelier individuals showed reduced current density in the middle cingulate cortex (MCC). These findings suggest that chronic social hypervigilance suppresses the spontaneous mobilization of the salience network at rest, with reduced MCC engagement reflecting a dispositional attenuation consistent with chronic relational threat.

papers.title: Identifying attentional control mechanisms related to the performance of high- and low-skilled First-Person Shooter game players: With exploratory data on expert older-adult esports players
papers.authors: Inhyeok Jeong, Akinori Takeda, Daisuke Shimane, Masaki Takeda
papers.abstract: High-skilled First-Person Shooter (FPS) game players are known to have superior attentional control—the ability to select information relevant to a task (selective attention) and maintain an appropriate response (sustained attention). However, it is unclear whether the attentional control strategies between high- and low-skilled FPS players differ, and whether these differences are related to FPS performance. Therefore, we investigated differences in attentional control between low- and high-skilled FPS players using electroencephalography, as well as correlations between gaming performance and attentional control. In addition, as an exploratory aim, we examined the characteristics of older FPS players. We recruited 11 high- and 11 low-skilled FPS players (under 25 years) and five older FPS players (over 65 years). Participants completed a task responding to colors regardless of the semantic meaning (Stroop task), clicked on targets quickly and accurately (aiming task), and played an FPS (esports task), respectively. We measured event-related potentials (ERPs) during the Stroop task to evaluate attentional control. In addition, we examined the relationship between ERP components and performance on the aiming and esports tasks. As a result, high-skilled players showed significantly smaller ERP amplitude in the 150-250 ms time window and greater ERP amplitude in the 280-380 ms time window (parietal region) during the Stroop task. These results suggest that high-skilled FPS players allocated attentional resources to relatively later stages of stimulus evaluation and processing. Furthermore, ERP amplitude showed a significant correlation with performance on aiming and esports tasks. Notably, older adults performed comparably to highly skilled young players on the FPS task, despite exhibiting smaller ERP amplitudes than young adults. These results suggest that attentional control is related to FPS performance and may be different with age.

papers.title: So much variety, so much to eat : The neuro-cognitive bases of visual food categorization in infancy
papers.authors: Camille Rioux, Pia Rämä A, Elodie Farineaux, Lionel Granjon, Olivier Mascaro, Stefanie Peykarjou
papers.abstract: Food is fundamental to life. Yet, detecting members of the food category raises a substantial cognitive challenge as different foods do not have any apparent common visual features. Moreover, what is deemed edible and appropriate to eat also varies greatly across social groups. While the neuro-cognitive bases of visual food category representations are well documented in adults, their early ontogenetic origins remain unknown. The current study investigated the emergence of visual food categorization abilities in infants’ brains, using the fast periodic visual stimulation paradigm (FPVS) coupled with electroencephalography (EEG). In FPVS paradigms, images from a target category are periodically inserted into a rapid stream of base images from other categories. If the brain treats the target images as a distinct category relative to the base images, a distinct EEG response appears at the frequency of presentation of the target images. In our study, French-speaking adults, 12- and 6-month-old infants (n = 25 per age group) were presented with target food stimuli inserted into sequences of base stimuli from various non-food categories (e.g., man-made objects, plants). Results show that, similarly to adults, 12-month-old infants distinguished images of food from those of other categories. In contrast, 6-month-old infants showed no detectable categorization response for food images. The current study is the first to investigate the developmental course of visual food categorization in the human brain and showed that, by their first birthday, infants already group perceptually diverse foods into a single category.

papers.title: Do People Think ChatGPT Is Conscious? Evidence from a Large Polish Sample
papers.authors: Hubert Plisiecki
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT are increasingly treated by the public as if theypossess subjective experience, with multiple studies probing the popular opinion on the matter. Thepresent study provides the first large-scale measurement of this phenomenon in Poland. Anationally distributed online survey panel (N = 1,736) rated ChatGPT’s capacity for consciousexperience on a 1–100 scale. "Most respondents (74%) attributed ChatGPT at least minimalconsciousness on the continuous rating scale, closely mirroring prior U.S. findings; because thisfigure is sensitive to question format, however, we conservatively estimate that more than 10% ofrespondents would affirm ChatGPT's status as an experiencer under a stricter, categorical framing.Small exploratory associations suggested that older and more highly educated participants wereslightly more skeptical, whereas right-leaning respondents attributed slightly more consciousness.A multivariate regression confirmed that these associations were not simply artifacts ofconfounding among demographic variables, though together they explained less than 3% of thevariance in consciousness attributions. These effects, though modest, indicate theoretically relevantvariation. Interpreting these results through Epley’s three-factor anthropomorphism model, thework argues that limited mechanistic understanding of LLMs, highly human-like behavior, andunmet social needs likely contribute to widespread phenomenal consciousness attribution. Givenethical concerns about over-trust, parasocial attachment, and responsibility misperception, thesebeliefs matter for AI deployment and governance. Our findings highlight the need for evidence-based educational strategies that improve public understanding of how LLMs work while allowingbeneficial use of the technology

papers.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence Tools on Operating Cost Management in the Digitalisation of Marketing Processes in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
papers.authors: Rakhmatullaeva Khumayro Ravshan kizi
papers.journal: American Journal of Economics and Business Management
papers.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) tools in marketing, yet evidence on how these tools change marketing operating costs remains fragmented and dominated by large-firm cases. This paper develops a transparent, activity-based cost model of monthly marketing operating expenditure (OPEX) and evaluates it through a Monte Carlo experiment with 10,000 draws per scenario. Three scenarios are compared for a representative SME marketing unit: a manual baseline (S0), partial AI adoption through off-the-shelf software-as-a-service tools (S1), and integrated AI adoption built on a CRM and marketing-automation core (S2). Costs comprise labour, agency spending, media-spend wastage, tooling, amortised implementation and training, and AI oversight. For a three-person team, mean monthly OPEX falls from USD 8,879 (S0) to USD 8,362 under S1 (−5.8%) and to USD 8,523 under S2 (−3.9%). Although S2 removes far more gross cost (USD 2,150 vs. 1,135 per month), it also adds USD 1,795 of AI-related cost, so its net advantage is smaller and far less certain (probability of positive savings 79.0% vs. 99.1% for S1). Scale is decisive: integrated AI does not pay off for one- or two-person teams, and it overtakes partial AI only from roughly four to five marketing employees. Sensitivity analysis shows that the share of freed labour hours actually converted into cost savings and the recurring licence burden dominate outcomes. The findings support a staged, measurement-led adoption strategy.

papers.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Cartoon Animation Films in the English Language Learning Process at Elementary School
papers.authors: Resy Oktadela, Yusti Elida, Putri Octa Hadiyanti, Cyntia Kumalasari, Fitri Wulandari, Rezky Maulana
papers.journal: Journal of English Language and Education
papers.abstract: English language learning in elementary school requires engaging and contextual media to support children’s vocabulary development. This study examined the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) integrated with the animated series Bluey in English vocabulary learning among sixth-grade students at SD IT Imam Syafi’i Cendekia 2 Pekanbaru. A quantitative pre-experimental design with a one-group pretest-posttest model was employed with 26 sixth-grade students selected purposively because they were the class receiving the AI-supported Bluey-based English instruction. During the treatment, students watched selected episodes of Bluey, engaged with English vocabulary presented through the animated content, and used AI-supported activities to reinforce vocabulary learning through guided practice and feedback. Vocabulary tests were administered before and after the treatment. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a paired-samples t-test with SPSS. The results showed an increase in the mean vocabulary score from 62.88 (SD = 18.23) in the pretest to 80.57 (SD = 11.60) in the posttest. The paired-samples t-test showed a statistically significant difference between the two scores, t(25) = 7.723, p .001. These findings indicate that the AI-supported use of Bluey was associated with a significant improvement in students’ English vocabulary scores. The findings suggest that integrating animated audiovisual content with AI-supported learning activities can provide an engaging supplementary approach to elementary English instruction when implemented with appropriate teacher guidance.

papers.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Applications Reduce Bank Non-Performing Loan Ratios? Evidence from the Text of Listed Banks' Annual Reports
papers.authors: Hao Xu
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are being rapidly deployed throughout the banking industry, yet their effect on credit risk still lacks systematic micro-level empirical evidence. Using a panel of 35 Chinese listed commercial banks over the period 2012-2025, this paper measures banks' AI adoption intensity by the frequency of AI-related keywords in the full text of their annual reports, and examines the effect of AI adoption on the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio together with its transmission mechanisms. The results are as follows. First, AI adoption significantly reduces the NPL ratio: a one-unit increase in the logarithm of AI keyword frequency lowers the NPL ratio by approximately 0.105 percentage points, and this conclusion remains robust after a battery of endogeneity treatments, including system GMM, a peer-mean instrumental variable approach (IV-2SLS), and the Oster coefficient stability test. Second, the effect is concentrated among city and rural commercial banks and weakens significantly as bank size increases. Third, AI improves asset quality mainly by lowering the cost-to-income ratio, with the mediating effect accounting for 22.2% of the total effect. Fourth, the effect strengthens over time, which is consistent with the accelerating iteration of AI technologies.

papers.title: THE CHANGING LANDSCAPE OF ACADEMIC COMMUNICATION: AI ADOPTION, STUDENT TRUST AND DIGITAL DEPENDENCY
papers.authors: S. Sasikala, Minu Tandon
papers.journal: ShodhVichar Journal of Media and Mass Communication
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly become a central tool in higher education, reshaping academic communication and knowledge exchange. This study explores the impact of AI credibility on student perceptions and digital dependency within academic contexts. It examines how trust in AI-generated content influences students’ engagement with scholarly discourse and the growing reliance on digital systems for academic tasks. Using the framework of Human-AI Interaction Trust Theory and UTAUT this paper argues that digital dependency in academic communication is not merely a technological shift but a cognitive and cultural transformation, raising questions about authenticity, intellectual autonomy, and the future of higher education. The study adopts a quantitative survey methodology using a sample of 100 students through random sampling from Coimbatore district of Tamil Nadu. By analyzing these dynamics, the study contributes to ongoing debates on the ethical integration of AI in academia and underscores the need for pedagogical strategies that balance technological utility with critical literacy.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN TRANSFORMING INDIA'S ECONOMY: IMPLICATIONS FOR EMPLOYMENT, PRODUCTIVITY, AND ECONOMIC GROWTH
papers.authors: Shalaka Pawar
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has, shifted from a theoretical subfield of computer science into a major engine behind macroeconomic readjustment across emerging markets. For India, this technological shift shows up at an unusually tight moment. The country has a huge working-age population, but it still deals with tough issues around job formalization, uneven digital access, and stubborn structural productivity gaps. This paper looks at how AI may steer India’s economic path, by checking both direct and indirect effects on labor markets, sectoral output, and broad GDP growth. Using an analysis of current empirical data, various government publications from NITI Aayog, and economic research released up through 2026, we examine how machine learning systems, natural language processing, and automation tools are changing several key Indian industries. To observe Information Technology (IT) and Business Process Management (BPM), plus agriculture, healthcare, and financial services. It is observed that AI adoption can unlock large chances to lift aggregate worker output and create high-value technical positions. But at the same time it can also disrupt lower to mid-skill employment in a strong way, which that could widen income inequality if nothing is done to reduce the risk. We also assess what infrastructure is actually needed for more sustainable AI rollout. Things like compute capacity, data sovereignty rules, and rural connectivity matter a lot here. In the end it is arhued that India can only maximize the net positive gains from AI if it builds an active governance approach, one that blends innovation incentives with aggressive national re-skilling efforts, ethical deployment guardrails, and focused public investments.

papers.title: EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT COMPETENCE IN MANAGERS: A THEORETICAL ANALYSIS OF THE STATE OF THE ART AND PROSPECTS FOR RESEARCH
papers.authors: Oleksandr Gain
papers.abstract: The article is devoted to a theoretical analysis of the problem of developing effective management competence in managers within the system of continuing education. Its relevance is determined by the transformation of managerial activity under the influence of digitalization, the spread of artificial intelligence, and the instability of the socio-economic environment, as well as by growing demands on the professional mobility of managers. On the basis of an analysis of current scholarly sources, the leading directions of research into managerial competence are identified – competency-based, activity-based, systemic, personal-developmental, digital, and andragogical – and the interpretation of effective management competence as an integrated professional-personal formation of a manager is substantiated. It is shown that the pedagogical dimension of the purposeful development of this competence specifically within the system of continuing education remains insufficiently studied, and promising directions for further research are outlined: the structure of the competence, the pedagogical conditions for its formation, a criteria-based diagnostic apparatus, and a model for developing managers.Keywords: manager, management, effective management, managerial competence, effective management competence, professional development, continuing education, adult education, competency-based approach, digitalization.

papers.title: The relevance of the implementation of integration processes in education and their impact on the professional and pedagogical functions of teachers of engineering, technology and technical sciences
papers.authors: С. А. Седов
papers.abstract: Introduction . Scholars (V. I. Alekseev, I. A. Artem’ev, A. O. Ashanin, M. N. Berulava, Yu. V. Vainshtein, I. S. Volegzhanina, V. N. Zhuravchik, S. E. Kaplina, Z. S. Sazonova, T. V. Semenova, Yu. N. Semin, N. K. Chapaev, I. N. Charikova, A. R. Shaidullina) emphasize the importance of implementing integration processes in the field of “Engineering, Technology, and Technical Sciences,” citing the demands of the state and society, the relevance of educational sciences, and the potential to enhance educational practice. The findings of these authors, along with numerous other studies, have significantly advanced the resolution of issues related to updating the content, methods, and technologies of vocational education in “Engineering, Technology, and Technical Sciences” through the implementation of integration processes. However, challenges concerning the preparation of educators for such implementation remain unaddressed. The purpose of the article – identification of integration processes, for the implementation of which future teachers of engineering, technology and technical sciences should be trained. Materials and methods . Methodology: cultural approach (G. I. Geysin, I. G. Gerder, N. B. Krilova) and functional approach (M. S. Kagan, Y. G. Markov, E. G. Yudin) used in the study of sociocultural conditionality of changes of pedagogical functions of vocational education, secondary vocational education. Research methods: theoretical analysis and synthesis, abstraction and concretisation, analogy. Results . The current list of integration processes, for the implementation of which should be prepared future teachers of vocational training, secondary vocational education in the field of «Engineering, technology and technical sciences», can be presented in a pair with professional updatespedagogical functions as follows «integration process in education – work activities of the teacher»: a) integration of technical and technological knowledge – intra- and interdisciplinary integration; b) integration of technical and value-human components of education – social managementsignificant project activity of students; с) integration of education and production – management of the quality of education by example of integration of quality systems of educational organization and enterprisesthe employer; d) integration of general technological and vocational education – development of content of future classes with pupils on labor (technology) in professional educational organization; e) integration of e-learning services and artificial intelligence in the pedagogical process – use of generative artificial intelligence to implement integration processes in education. Discussion and conclusions . Scientific novelty: on the basis of a philosophical analysis of the essence of the integrative component of vocational education, integration processes have been identified for the implementation of which it is necessary to prepare teachers of vocational training, secondary vocational education in «Engineering, technology and technical sciences». Theoretical significance: the results of the study expand the range of work activities that update the professional-pedagogical functions of the teacher of engineering, technology and technical sciences, which it is proposed to involve in the implementation of integration processes. Practical significance: the selected integration processes can be used for further work on updating the content, methods and technologies of training of teachers of engineering, technology and technical sciences to perform changing professional-pedagogical functions.
keywords: integration of general and vocational education

papers.title: Teachers’ professional development: scientific approaches and practice of postgraduate support
papers.authors: Anton Andreevich Konovalov
papers.abstract: Introduction . The article is devoted to the methodological determinants of lifelong vocational and pedagogical education and development of teaching staff. During the study, scientific approaches to education were analyzed, on the basis of which specific principles for organizing support for the teachers’ professional development were identified. An analysis of the market for additional professional educational programs for teachers’ advanced training is presented. Materials and methods . The theoretical and methodological basis of the study was personality-oriented (A. V. Petrovsky, V. V. Serikov, I. S. Yakimanskaya, etc.), andragogical (E. V. Bogomolova, S. G. Vershlovsky, S. I. Zmeev, O. V. Sinyavina), acmeological (B. G. Ananyev, A. A. Bodalev, A. A. Derkach, V. G. Zazykin, V. A. Slastenin), competence (V. I. Bidenko, V. A. Bolotov, D. A. Danilov, I. A. Zimnyaya, O. E. Lebedev, N. R. Shametov, L. R. Yarullina), activity-based (L. S. Vygotsky, A. N. Leontiev, P. Y. Galperin, D. B. Elkonin, V. V. Davydov, A. G. Asmolov) and axiological (I. B. Bicheva, M. S. Kagan, T. G. Kalyuzhnaya, S. V. Timofeeva and O. M. Filatova) scientific approaches to the process of supporting the professional development of vocational education teachers. Methods of content analysis, comparative analysis, and discourse analysis of further professional education programs implemented by Russian state and commercial educational organizations were applied, using artificial intelligence tools for natural language processing (NLP). Results . The scientific principles of organizing continuous professional pedagogical education within the framework of postgraduate support for teachers' professional development have been defined. The conducted analysis of the CPD market revealed systemic disparities in the methodological support of teacher professional development programs. It has been established that traditional learning formats (43-52 % of in-person programs) prevail in regional systems of additional education, whereas online formats dominate at the federal level (48 %). Quantitative analysis of 570 programs showed a consistent dominance of the competence-based approach (35-38 %) with a significant deficit of person-centered (2-14 %) and andragogical (4-20 %) learning models. The developed system of indicators allowed for verifying the correspondence of programs to methodological approaches, revealing that only 15 % of programs ensure the synergy of three or more approaches. The most pronounced imbalances are observed between industrially developed territories, where a technocratic model dominates, and regions with distinct cultural specificity, oriented toward value aspects of education. Discussion and conclusions . The obtained results indicate the necessity of transitioning from the fragmented application of methodological approaches to their holistic integration within the system of supporting teachers' professional development. The identified synergistic effects (systemic, practice-transformation, value-semantic, and innovation-adaptation) demonstrate that it is precisely the nonlinear methodology that creates a qualitatively new educational space for teachers' professional development.

papers.title: Long-term prospects for the scientific and methodological support of supervision of term papers
papers.authors: Roman Evgenevich Bulat
papers.abstract: Introduction . The relevance of the problem of improving the quality of academic supervision of term papers is substantiated as a systemic prerequisite for ensuring academic integrity in higher-level scientific and qualification works. A contradiction is revealed between the long-term psychological and pedagogical significance of research supervision for the professional development of a researcher's personality and its actual state, limited by the absence of a sufficient scientific and methodological basis for its improvement, among other factors. Materials and methods . The article presents an analysis of scientific literature devoted to the issues of research supervision and its role in the formation of students' methodological culture and research ethics. An approach has been developed and tested, including matrix-based design of unique term paper topics and a system of criteria for staged scientific and methodological support and (self-) assessment of results. The testing was conducted within the framework of supervising over 400 papers (2022–2026) using methods of participant observation and comparative analysis of the dynamics of their quality. Results . The organizational and methodological effects include the fact that the staged control system minimizes time spent on aligning the structural elements of the work and eliminating internal contradictions in the research. The pedagogical outcomes include the fact that the psychological and pedagogical component embedded in the approach ensures an increase in students' creative independence and academic integrity. A comprehensive result is the formation of students' authorial research position, manifested in increased criticality and selectivity when working with sources, including proper citation and evaluation of materials generated by artificial intelligence. Thus, the approach not only addresses the tasks of scientific and methodological support but also responds to the challenges of the digital transformation of higher education. Discussion and conclusions . The results of testing the developed approach are consistent with the conclusions of previous research in the field of higher education pedagogy, confirming the fundamental importance of systematic scientific and methodological support for educational and research activities. The implementation of the proposed scientific and methodological support for students' preparation of term papers, based on the stage-by-stage organization of supervision, execution, and assessment of results, confirmed its theoretical value and practical significance.

papers.title: Body weight perception and body self-esteem in adolescents with overweight or obesity in Costa Rica: challenges for public health policy
papers.authors: Rafael Monge‐Rojas, Vanessa Smith‐Castro, Rulamán Vargas-Quesada
papers.abstract: Objective: This study estimates the prevalence of weight misperception among Costa Rican adolescents in general and examines its association with body esteem and weight-control behaviors to inform public health policy. Methods: The authors analyzed cross-sectional data collected in 2017 from a probabilistic sample of 818 adolescents aged 13-18 years enrolled in public and private secondary schools in urban and rural areas of the province of San José, Costa Rica. Weight and height were measured by trained nutritionists and classified using World Health Organization body mass index (BMI)-for-age standards. Perceived weight status was assessed using culturally appropriate response categories adapted from the Youth Risk Behavior Survey and refined through a pilot study. Body esteem and weight-control behaviors were measured using validated survey instruments. Results: Among adolescents with overweight or obesity, 59% underestimated their weight, most commonly perceiving themselves as having an "adequate weight." Weight underestimation was associated with higher body esteem and lower engagement in weight-control behaviors after adjustment for key sociodemographic characteristics. Conclusion: By contributing evidence from a Latin American context-where research on adolescent weight perception remains scarce-this study enhances understanding of how excess weight is perceived during adolescence in settings where overweight is highly prevalent and supports public policy approaches that prioritize healthy eating and active living from adolescence.

papers.title: Exploring Open Science Through AI: A Student Research Journey
papers.authors: Christin Monroe, Lucy McNeil
papers.abstract: This assignment guides students through researching an open science resource and incorporating AI as a learning partner in their exploration. It begins with a midterm planning stage where students select an open science platform or dataset, define research questions, outline their approach, and reflect on initial AI use. The final deliverable is a creative presentation structured around flexible prompts that highlight the project’s focus, significance, research insights, process, and key takeaways, along with reflections on responsible AI integration and future directions. The goal is to foster critical thinking about open science practices while encouraging innovative, transparent, and accessible approaches to using AI in scientific inquiry. papers.title: TRADITIONAL WRITING AND E-WRITING USING GEN-AI TO EMPOWER STUDENTS’ CRITICAL THINKING IN ARGUMENTATIVE TEXT: A CASE STUDY IN INDONESIAN EFL HIGHER EDUCATION
papers.authors: Dedeh Rohayati, Etika Rachmawati, R. Bunga Febriani, Bambang Sugiarto
papers.journal: English Review Journal of English Education
papers.abstract: The high increase in utilizing Generative AI (Artificial Intelligence) has become a concern as it may potentially impede the development of students’ cognitive skills, particularly critical thinking skill. This may occur if students have less frequent of traditional writing process to train students’ memory and retention. Model of academic writing activity preceded by traditional writing, followed by e-writing with the assistance of Generative AI, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Meta AI, etc., is worth conducting. With the utilization of case study, the present study explores the procedure of and the students’ experiences in traditional writing and e-writing using Gen-AI assistance to empower students’ critical thinking in argumentative text. The 24 third year students enrolling Academic Writing Class in English Education Program were selected purposively. Nine students’ argumentative documents text, and semi-structured interview administered to nine students were utilized to obtain the primary data. The findings showed that the model of writing argumentative text traditionally followed by e-writing argumentative text using Gen-AI resulted in a powerful students’ critical thinking in writing argumentative. Generative AI assisted students in incorporating critical thinking elements in argumentative text, particularly in formulating thesis statements and presenting clear facts and logical arguments. Whereas, students experienced the model of writing positively, i.e., students were aware of 1) traditional writing that could maintain brain retention, 2) e-writing leading to innovative work, 3) Gen-AI use in polishing the mechanics aspects of students’ written work, 4) generic structure of argumentative text, and 5) basic notion of critical thinking. Future research is recommended to broaden the present research and to investigate a more comprehensive research result on related topic by using specific interview questions category of feeling (emotion focus), contrast (comparison) and construct forming (building the concept/ meaning) with the type of both structured and semi structured interview.

papers.title: UNIVERSITY STUDENTS' ACADEMIC WRITING ECOLOGIES: HOW STUDENTS COMBINE FORMAL, INFORMAL, AND AI-BASED RESOURCES IN WRITING RESEARCH PAPERS
papers.authors: Fahrus Zaman Fadhly, Harun Al Rasyid, Dadang Solihat, Nani Ronsani Thamrin, Wulan Rahmatunisa, Vina Agustiana, Muhammad Aprianto Budie Nugroho
papers.journal: English Review Journal of English Education
papers.abstract: University students no longer write research papers with a single source of support. They draw at once on formal resources such as courses, supervisors and feedback, informal resources such as peers, online tutorials and digital communities, and AI-based resources such as generative chatbots, paraphrasing tools and AI-assisted search. Yet research has mostly examined these resources in isolation, leaving unclear how students combine them. This article addresses that gap through an integrative review of 50 publications from 2022 to 2026, interpreted through the lens of learning ecology. The review was organised into seven thematic clusters and synthesised across the stages of research paper writing: planning, reading and sourcing, drafting, revising, and citing and submitting. Three findings emerged. First, formal resources remain the anchor of students' writing ecologies, setting standards and legitimising feedback, but they are often limited in time and access. Second, informal and AI-based resources increasingly fill these gaps, offering immediate, low-stakes and personalised support, with AI-based resources concentrated in drafting and revising. Third, students actively orchestrate these resources rather than simply consuming them, but this orchestration produces tensions concerning trust, authorship, academic integrity and equity. The article proposes an Academic Writing Ecology Model that positions the student writer as an orchestrator of three resource layers embedded in institutional and platform ecologies. It concludes with implications for writing pedagogy, institutional AI policy and future empirical research.

papers.title: Comparison of generative adversarial networks and diffusion models for synthetic steady-state visual evoked potential signal generation
papers.authors: Przemysław Wiszniewski, Marcin Kołodziej, Andrzej Majkowski
papers.abstract: Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) signals are widely used in brain–computer interface (BCI) applications. Artificial generation of SSVEP signals can reduce the time required for experimental data collection, thereby minimizing user fatigue and improving comfort during electroencephalographic recordings. Synthetic SSVEP data enable data augmentation, training and validation of BCI classification algorithms, and benchmarking of SSVEP-based BCI systems without extensive subject-specific recordings. However, realistic modelling and generation of SSVEP signals remain challenging due to their nonlinear and non-stationary characteristics and the presence of harmonic components. In this study, we present a comparative analysis of two approaches to synthetic SSVEP signal generation: generative adversarial networks and diffusion models. The performance of both methods is evaluated using qualitative and quantitative metrics to assess the fidelity of the generated signals in both the time and frequency domains. The evaluation framework includes the frequency-domain Euclidean distance, Wasserstein distance, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and principal component analysis (PCA). The results indicate that diffusion models produce synthetic SSVEP signals with higher fidelity in both the time and frequency domains than the evaluated GAN configuration. Overall, diffusion models achieved better agreement with real data according to the adopted metrics while preserving key signal characteristics.

papers.title: Exploring Culturally Responsive Teaching Awareness in the Age of GenAI: Voices from Indonesian EFL Pre-Service Teachers
papers.authors: Eni Rosnija, Eka Fajar Rahmani, Dewi Novita, Nindya Juwita Utimadini
papers.abstract: This study explores pre-service EFL teachers’ awareness of integrating GenAI into CRT in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Using a qualitative descriptive design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 35 final-semester pre-service EFL teachers and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis. Interview analysis reveals four interconnected dimensions of awareness: cognitive, pedagogical, critical/evaluative, and developmental. Participants recognized GenAI's limitations in representing local cultural knowledge, struggled to design culturally responsive prompts, and demonstrated the ability to identify cultural biases and inaccuracies in AI outputs. They also emphasized the need for practical training and institutional support to effectively integrate GenAI into culturally responsive learning. Based on these findings, this study proposes Culturally Responsive AI Literacy as a conceptual extension of AI literacy, positioning technical competence, critical evaluation, cultural knowledge, and pedagogical decision-making as integrated competencies. Keywords: culturally responsive teaching, generative AI, AI literacy, pre-service EFL teachers, teacher education.

papers.title: The Copyrightability of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content in China
papers.authors: Xiaojing Qin
papers.journal: World Journal of Social Science Research
papers.abstract: The commercial application of generative artificial intelligence has rapidly brought to the fore the structural tension between machine-generated content (AIGC) and the core presuppositions of copyright law concerning the “author”. Adopting a Sino-US comparative law approach, this paper examines the institutional divergences between the two countries on the question of AIGC copyrightability and their jurisprudential roots. The research posits that artificial intelligence possesses a dual attribute in the creative process—“transcending tools yet lacking complete creativity”—which constitutes a meta-constraint for institutional design. Through cases such as the “Feilin Case”, “Tencent Case”, “Li v. Liu”, and “Huan Zhi Yi Case”, Chinese jurisprudence has developed a three-stage evolution: from denying AI authorship to establishing human-machine collaboration, and then to strengthening evidentiary review, thereby establishing a process-oriented originality standard centered on substantial human intellectual input. On this basis, and through comparative analysis, this paper proposes a localized path for refining AIGC copyright protection tailored to China’s institutional context: establishing differentiated protection rules through tiered classification, constructing an originality assessment framework centered on human intellectual input, and introducing supporting mechanisms such as content labeling, good-faith disclosure, and extended collective licensing, in order to achieve an institutional objective that balances technological development with rights protection.

papers.title: Status Quo of Artificial Intelligence- and Machine Learning-Supported Medical and Administrative Processes in Ambulatory Care Practice Management Systems: Systematic Review (Preprint)
papers.authors: Sandra Steinkasserer, Martin Emmert, Reiner Hofmann
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Electronic health records (EHRs) and practice management systems represent the digital foundation of outpatient care worldwide. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)-supported medical and administrative processes (AMP) into these platforms offers a profound opportunity to streamline clinical workflows and standardize patient care. However, existing research remains highly fragmented and focused on isolated tools. This creates a critical research gap, as there is currently no comprehensive mapping of how these diverse medical and administrative workflows collectively integrate and perform within the real-world clinical environment of ambulatory care. OBJECTIVE This study aims to address this research gap by comprehensively mapping the global status quo of natively EHR-integrated AMP in ambulatory care. Specifically, we explore the types of digital processes currently available and how physicians and medical assistants interact with these technologies in clinical environments. METHODS We conducted a systematic review of PubMed and Scopus databases (searching from inception to March 24, 2026) following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. We targeted empirical studies evaluating outpatient clinical and administrative processes driven by AI, ML, or AI-enabled decision-support algorithms natively embedded within EHR or practice management systems. To ensure literature saturation, backward citation searching of included studies was conducted (yielding no additional eligible studies). Study selection, data extraction into a standardized matrix, and methodological quality assessment using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal checklists (tailored to RCTs, quasi-experimental, cohort, cross-sectional, and qualitative studies) were conducted by one reviewer and independently verified by a second reviewer. RESULTS A total of 39 empirical studies were included. Methodological quality assessed via JBI tools was moderate to high, with common limitations being a lack of participant and personnel blinding (system-inherent) and selection bias due to reliance on voluntary early adopters. Our synthesis identified 5 primary categories of natively EHR-integrated AMP: point-of-care clinical decision support systems (CDSS) (16/39, 41%), active background screening and triage (9/39, 23%), ambient intelligence for clinical documentation (8/39, 21%), administrative processes and patient communication (4/39, 10%), and remote patient monitoring (RPM) (2/39, 5%). While ambient AI demonstrated success in reducing documentation effort and burnout, point-of-care CDSS was heavily hindered by alert fatigue (with override rates up to 96%), and active background screening was constrained by algorithmic opacity (“black-box” characteristics) and clinician distrust. CONCLUSIONS Rather than achieving full automation, AMP technologies currently function as assistive tools within primary care. Real-world utilization requires a strict human-in-the-loop verification process, where medical professionals actively oversee both AI- and ML-driven outputs. Successful integration depends on addressing critical workflow barriers, particularly minimizing alert fatigue and enhancing algorithmic transparency to foster clinician trust. CLINICALTRIAL PROSPERO [CRD420261327094]

papers.title: Growth trajectories and risk of underweight and overweight in childhood cancer patients and survivors: a longitudinal multicentre cohort study protocol (Preprint)
papers.authors: Luigi Annicchiarico, Alice Sofia Calvello, Yara Shoman, Lorenz Manuel Leuenberger, María José Bento, Julia Anna Bielicki, Claudia Boettcher, Pierluigi Brazzola, Paula N Breia, Gabriela Caldas, Beatrice Drexler, Daniel Drozdov, Manuel Diezi, Janez Jazbec, Markus Joerger, Daniel Konrad, Claudia Elisabeth Kuehni, Antonio Lourenço, Christoph C.S. Saner, Katrin Scheinemann, Freimut H. Schilling, Milica Stefanović, Tiago Taveira‐Gomes, Andre Oscar von Bueren, Nicolas Waespe, Andreas N. WICKI, Christina Schindera, Fabiën N. Belle
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Underweight, overweight, and linear growth during and after cancer treatment can impact treatment efficacy and survival in childhood cancer patients, and long-term health in childhood cancer survivors (CCS). However, scientific evidence on the weight status and growth of CCS is limited. Previous studies have been small, focused on specific cancer types, or lacked objectively measured longitudinal data. The availability of standardized, semantically interoperable routine data from oncology clinics offers an unprecedented opportunity to investigate nutritional status across all childhood cancer types, treatment regimens, and critical time windows. OBJECTIVE We will investigate underweight, overweight, and growth trajectories from birth to adulthood in childhood cancer patients and survivors. We will identify predictors associated with distinct growth and weight trajectories and assess the consistency of findings across European countries. METHODS The Growth study will collect routinely recorded sociodemographic, clinical, and anthropometric data from paediatric and adolescent cancer patients (aged <20 years) from Switzerland, Portugal and Slovenia, We will include patients diagnosed between 2004-2026, by linking data from the Swiss Childhood Cancer Registry (ChCR), the Swiss Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (SCCSS), the Swiss Federal Statistical Office (FSO), and oncology clinics in Switzerland. Deterministic linkage of data sources (ChCR, SCCSS, oncology clinics, and FSO) will be performed using social security numbers. We will calculate age- and sex-specific z-scores for weight, height, and BMI based on country-specific and World Health Organization growth references. Latent trajectory modelling will be applied to identify distinct growth and weight trajectories and to detect subgroups at increased risk of growth impairment. We will use logistic regression models to identify predictors of impaired growth. RESULTS The project was funded in 2025; first study results are expected to be published by autumn 2027. We will obtain routinely collected data from approximately 12,250 childhood cancer patients and survivors - 7,800 from Switzerland, 3,350 from Portugal, and 1,100 from Slovenia. CONCLUSIONS The Growth study will provide insights into the nutritional status of childhood cancer patients and survivors and improve understanding of growth patterns in this population. Identifying high risk groups and tumour or treatment related factors will inform targeted surveillance strategies and early nutritional interventions. CLINICALTRIAL ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07750444

papers.title: Challenges of Using Generative AI for Charcot Neuroarthropathy Patient Education: An Evaluation of Content Quality, Readability, and Actionability (Preprint)
papers.authors: Dongfeng Chen, Qiang Wang, Shiming Huang, Ying Li, Daohua Chen
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Charcot neuroarthropathy (CN) is a destructive complication of diabetic peripheral neuropathy requiring clear patient education. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly consulted, yet their CN material remains unevaluated. OBJECTIVE To compare the content quality, readability, and actionability of CN patient-education responses generated by five widely accessible LLMs. METHODS Twenty standardized patient questions spanning five CN domains were posed in English to GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.6 Flash, DeepSeek-V3.2, Qwen 3.7, and Doubao 2.1 through their official interfaces in August 2026. Each of the 100 responses was scored independently by two orthopedic surgeons (Cohen's κ = 0.92) for content quality (DISCERN, EQIP, GQS, JAMA), readability (ARI, CLI, FKGL, FRES, SMOG, GFOG), and actionability (PEMAT-P). Medians were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test. RESULTS Gemini 3.6 Flash had the highest DISCERN median (54.5/80), whereas Qwen 3.7 had the highest EQIP median (70.6%). Doubao 2.1 was weakest overall (GQS 3/5; lowest PEMAT-P), and Gemini 3.6 Flash and Doubao 2.1 produced the least readable text (FKGL 13.76 and 10.84) versus Qwen 3.7 and DeepSeek-V3.2 (FRES 62.0 and 60.5). Differences were significant for all quality and readability measures (P < .001) and for JAMA (P = .021), where every model scored a median of 0/4. CONCLUSIONS LLMs offer a promising foundation for CN patient education, generating largely understandable responses of moderate quality. Limitations were consistent: poor transparency, reading levels exceeding recommended thresholds, and partial actionability. Because no single model was best across all dimensions, the appropriate choice depends on the intended use. CLINICALTRIAL N/A

papers.title: Liability and Standard of Care in AI-Driven Psychiatric Practice: European Viewpoint
papers.authors: Luís Madeira, C. Alves Pereira, Meryam Schouler‐Ocak, Jerzy Samochowiec, Silvana Galderisi, Mariana Pinto da Costa
papers.abstract: Unlabelled: AI is increasingly incorporated into psychiatric triage, risk prediction, passive monitoring, clinical documentation, and patient-facing conversational systems. These applications may improve access, continuity, efficiency, and pattern recognition, but they also redistribute epistemic authority and complicate responsibility when harm occurs. European regulation is developed in relation to market access, data governance, risk management, and product safety, yet remains fragmented regarding civil liability, organizational negligence, and the psychiatric standard of care. This Viewpoint examines how liability and standard of care should be understood when AI becomes part of psychiatric reasoning in Europe. It advances one central thesis: psychiatric AI requires justified integration supported by layered accountability within, but not determined by, European regulation. It presents a targeted doctrinal and normative synthesis of binding European Union instruments, regulatory guidance, selected national governance materials, and psychiatric, bioethical, legal, and digital mental health literature. It distinguishes binding law from guidance and policy, and separates ex ante regulation from ex post liability, and from professional standards of care. Four illustrative domains are analyzed: conversational or therapeutic chatbots, suicide prediction, digital phenotyping and passive monitoring, and large language model documentation. Psychiatric AI raises distinctive concerns because psychiatric judgment depends heavily on testimony, contextual meaning, therapeutic trust, risk interpretation, privacy, and liberty-sensitive decisions. Existing European instruments, including the AI Act, Medical Device Regulation, General Data Protection Regulation, revised Product Liability Directive, and European Health Data Space Regulation, establish governance duties, but do not provide a harmonized fault-based liability framework for AI-assisted health care. Regulatory compliance may inform later legal assessment, but it does not determine whether psychiatric care was reasonable. The proposed standard of justified integration requires knowledge of intended use and model limits, assessment of local and patient-level applicability, active clinical interpretation, disclosure when AI use is material to consent or trust, documentation in high-stakes decisions, and organizational audit. Accountability should be distributed across developers, deployers, and clinicians according to control and preventability. Mixed-fault scenarios are therefore likely to be common. The augmented-clinician model and layered accountability are offered as normative proposals rather than settled European legal standards. Clinicians should remain responsible for contextual, patient-centered judgment; developers for design, validation, documentation, and foreseeable misuse; and deployers for procurement, training, workflow integration, local validation, monitoring, and escalation. Future empirical research should evaluate effects on clinician reliance, documentation burden, patient outcomes, coercive interventions, therapeutic trust, and feasibility across differently resourced services.

papers.title: Beyond AI Literacy: Understanding Health Care Workforce AI Enablement in the Generative AI Era
papers.authors: Chien‐Chin Hsu, Yen-Ling Ko
papers.abstract: Unlabelled: The rapid diffusion of generative AI is transforming health care delivery, education, administration, and research. In response, health care organizations have invested heavily in AI literacy initiatives and workforce development programs. Existing frameworks primarily focus on whether health care professionals understand AI and whether they can engage with AI effectively. However, health care practice increasingly reveals that individuals with similar levels of AI literacy and AI engagement often contribute very differently to AI-enabled work and organizational adoption. Some professionals primarily use AI to improve their own work, whereas others facilitate AI adoption, coordinate stakeholders, and integrate AI into routine practice. This observation suggests that current perspectives may overlook an important dimension of workforce AI enablement. In this Viewpoint, we argue that AI literacy and AI engagement alone provide an incomplete explanation of how health care organizations realize the benefits of AI. Drawing upon literature from AI literacy, fluency theory, human-AI interaction, innovation diffusion, implementation science, and health care workforce development, we propose the health care workforce AI enablement matrix (HWAEM). HWAEM conceptualizes workforce AI enablement through 2 complementary capabilities: AI fluency and AI harnessing. AI fluency refers to the capability to engage with AI effectively, appropriately, and responsibly across professional contexts, whereas AI harnessing refers to the capability to identify opportunities for AI-enabled improvement, mobilize stakeholders, facilitate adoption, and integrate AI into collective work practices. The interaction of these capabilities generates 4 workforce profiles: AI novices, AI practitioners, AI facilitators, and AI leaders. Through HWAEM, this Viewpoint argues that health care workforce AI enablement is better understood through the complementary capabilities of AI fluency and AI harnessing than through AI literacy and AI engagement alone. We illustrate how these profiles manifest in health care practice and discuss implications for workforce development and AI implementation. HWAEM offers a new perspective for understanding health care workforce preparedness in the generative AI era and provides a foundation for future empirical research.

papers.title: A Patient Simulation Framework for Risk Assessment of Conversational Health Care AI: Development and Evaluation Study
papers.authors: Md. Tanvir Rouf Shawon, Mohammad Sabik Irbaz, Hadeel R A Elyazori, Keerti Reddy Resapu, Yili Lin, Vladimir Franzuela Cardenas, K. Pierre Eklou, Farrokh Alemi, Kevin Lybarger
papers.abstract: Background: Conversational AI systems are increasingly being deployed in health care for clinical decision support, but their performance varies substantially across patient communication styles, health literacy levels, and behavioral patterns. Static benchmarks cannot capture multiturn dynamics through which this variation compounds, and no current evaluation framework implements structured AI risk management guidance for conversational health care AI. The result is a structural risk: AI systems may perform well in aggregate while failing disproportionately for the populations they are intended to help. Objective: This study aimed to develop and validate a patient simulation framework that aligns with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) Map and Measure functions, providing an empirical basis for identifying and characterizing performance risks in conversational clinical AI across medical, linguistic, and behavioral patient variations. We applied the framework to a conversational decision aid for antidepressant selection in major depressive disorder (the AI decision aid). Methods: The simulator integrated three profile dimensions: (1) medical profiles constructed from All of Us electronic health records using risk ratio gating; (2) linguistic profiles modeling a health literacy gradient and condition-specific communication; and (3) behavioral profiles representing cooperative, distracted, and adversarial engagement. We generated 500 simulated conversations and evaluated profile fidelity through human annotation and a large language model (LLM) judge, and then assessed downstream effects on the AI decision aid's concept retrieval and antidepressant recommendations. Results: The patient simulator expressed medical concepts with high fidelity (96.6% accuracy across 8210 concepts), with substantial human interannotator agreement (κ=0.73) and LLM-judge agreement against human annotators (κ=0.78). Behavioral profiles were reliably distinguished (κ=0.93; near perfect agreement), and linguistic profiles showed substantial agreement at the lower bound of the substantial range (κ=0.61), which can be considered adequate to support profile-level analysis. The framework revealed monotonic degradation in AI decision aid performance across the health literacy gradient. Rank-1 concept retrieval increased from 47.6% for limited health literacy to 81.9% for proficient health literacy, with corresponding declines in antidepressant recommendation accuracy. Conclusions: Patient simulation grounded in the NIST AI RMF exposes measurable performance risks in conversational health care AI that static benchmarks miss, with direct equity implications. Health literacy operates as a structural risk factor, with degraded performance concentrated in patients carrying the greatest burden of psychiatric illness. The framework supports targeted risk-mitigation interventions before deployment. While we evaluated the framework only on antidepressant selection, extending it to other clinical decision-aid tasks remains an assignment for future work.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Reliability, Quality, Readability, and Originality of AI Chatbot Responses to Patient Questions in Implant Dentistry
papers.authors: Lana Alatrash, Gülfem Ergün
papers.abstract: Introduction/Objective This study aimed to evaluate and compare the reliability, informational quality, readability, and originality of responses generated by three widely used artificial intelligence chatbot platforms (Google Gemini Flash, ChatGPT Plus (OpenAI), and Claude Sonnet (Anthropic)) to patient-oriented questions in implant dentistry. Methods Twenty frequently asked questions in implant dentistry were developed and categorized as theoretical (n = 10) or clinical (n = 10). Each question was submitted to the three chatbots on the same day, and only the first response was analyzed. Responses were evaluated for reliability, informational quality, readability, and originality using validated assessment tools. Statistical comparisons were performed using appropriate parametric and nonparametric tests, with significance set at 0.05. Results Google Gemini Flash demonstrated significantly higher reliability scores than ChatGPT Plus and Claude Sonnet ( p < 0.001). Informational quality also differed significantly among models ( p = 0.045), with Gemini providing higher-quality responses than Claude. Readability analyses showed that chatbot responses generally required a high school or college-level reading ability. Similarity index values indicated high originality, with no significant differences among platforms ( p = 0.423). Differences were more pronounced for theoretical questions, whereas clinical questions showed limited variation. Discussion Although AI chatbots can provide useful information for implant dentistry patients, variability in reliability and readability highlights the need for cautious use without professional supervision. Conclusion AI-powered chatbots can support patient education in implant dentistry; however, response quality and accessibility vary across models. Expert oversight remains essential, and future research should focus on improving readability, transparency, and standardized evaluation of AI-generated dental information.

papers.title: A Smart ICT-based E-Learning Model Using Artificial Intelligence Tools
papers.authors: Lt Imam Hussain Mirji
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming conventional teaching and learning practices. Traditional e-learning systems primarily provide digital access to learning materials, recorded lectures, online assessments, and communication facilities. However, the integration of Artificial Intelligence can make e-learning more adaptive, interactive, personalized, and learner-centred. This paper proposes a Smart ICT-Based E-Learning Model Using Artificial Intelligence Tools for improving teaching-learning processes in higher education. The proposed model integrates ICT infrastructure, learning management systems, AI-based content generation, intelligent tutoring, personalized learning, automated assessment, learning analytics, natural language processing, virtual assistance, recommendation systems, and digital library resources. The model also emphasizes teacher supervision, digital literacy, data privacy, cybersecurity, ethical AI use, and accessibility. A conceptual framework is developed consisting of input, intelligent processing, personalized learning, assessment, analytics, feedback, and continuous improvement components. The proposed model can support teachers in lesson planning, content development, assessment, student engagement, and academic monitoring while enabling students to access personalized learning resources. The paper concludes that AI-supported ICT-based e-learning can complement teachers and improve the flexibility, accessibility, and efficiency of education when implemented responsibly. The proposed model provides a framework for educational institutions seeking to integrate AI tools with existing ICT and e-learning infrastructure.
