papers.abstract: Abstract Background Medical students are exposed to academic and lifestyle factors that may adversely affect cardiovascular and psycho-emotional health. Although these outcomes have been widely studied, most evidence is cross-sectional, and longitudinal evidence from Latin America remains limited. We described participant retention, baseline characteristics according to follow-up status, and longitudinal changes in cardiovascular and psycho-emotional health in a cohort of Colombian medical students. Methods We conducted a prospective cohort study of first-year medical students from Bogotá, Colombia. Participants completed assessments at enrollment and after entering clinical training. Cardiovascular health was assessed using a study-specific seven-domain modified Life’s Essential 8 (mLE8) framework incorporating dietary, physical activity, nicotine, adiposity, lipid, glucose, and blood pressure domains. Waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) was included as a measure of central adiposity. Psycho-emotional health was assessed using the Trait Meta-Mood Scale-24 (TMMS-24), Interpersonal Reactivity Index (IRI), and Perceived Stress Scale-14 (PSS-14). Baseline characteristics were compared descriptively between completers and non-completers, and longitudinal changes were evaluated using available paired observations. Sensitivity analyses explored the potential influence of missing follow-up data. Results Of 195 students, 97 completed follow-up (49.7%). Baseline characteristics were generally comparable between groups; although completers had slightly higher systolic blood pressure, while non-completers had higher perceived stress and total cholesterol. Among participants with paired observations, median mLE8 decreased from 82.9 at baseline to 75.0 at follow-up, with a median change of − 4.05 points ( n = 88). Concurrently, BMI, waist circumference, waist-to-height ratio, and total cholesterol increased. Perceived stress and most psycho-emotional measures showed little evidence of systematic change. Sensitivity analyses under favorable and unfavorable attrition scenarios yielded negative mLE8 changes, although their magnitude varied. Conclusions In the paired sample, the study-specific mLE8 profile shifted toward less favorable cardiovascular health categories at follow-up, alongside increases in adiposity measures and total cholesterol. However, approximately half of the original cohort was lost to follow-up, and additional variable-specific missingness and the modified nature of the mLE8 construct warrant interpreting these findings as descriptive and exploratory and limiting their generalizability to the entire cohort. Further longitudinal studies with improved retention and more complete data ascertainment are needed to clarify cardiovascular and psycho-emotional trajectories during medical training.

papers.title: Recurrent prolonged motor events with different evidence of disease activity in cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related inflammation: a longitudinal case report
papers.authors: Xiangping Yuan, Chenyu Xia, Haimei Zhang, Song Xue, Yucheng Zheng, Sicheng Lou, Jianping Liang, Wendi Wei, Rong Du, Meihe Huang, Qi Zhang, Qiang Ma
papers.abstract: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related inflammation (CAA-ri) is a treatable disorder in which seizures may accompany active inflammation. Previous reports have mainly described seizures during active disease or relapse accompanied by new magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities. Less is known about how recurrent prolonged motor events should be interpreted when clinical, MRI, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings do not change in parallel. We describe four admissions in one patient to assess renewed inflammatory activity using longitudinal clinical, MRI, and CSF findings. A 67-year-old woman presented with headache, cognitive decline, bilateral vasogenic edema with left temporoparieto-occipital predominance, lobar microbleeds, and inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), fulfilling criteria for probable CAA-ri. Symptoms and MRI and CSF abnormalities improved after corticosteroids. At the third admission, an approximately 30-minute bilateral tonic-clonic seizure met the clinical duration criterion for convulsive status epilepticus and was followed by encephalopathy and severe right hemiparesis, likely reflecting inflammatory lesion burden and possible postictal Todd paresis. Diazepam 10 mg was given intravenously during the convulsions. MRI showed renewed edema and widespread leptomeningeal enhancement; CSF opening pressure exceeded 300 mmH₂O and interleukin-6 was 61.59 pg/mL. Intensified corticosteroids and maintenance valproate were followed by improvement. At the fourth admission, prolonged seizure-like motor events followed recent SARS-CoV-2 infection with serum sodium of 128.2 mmol/L, despite continued prednisone and valproate. MRI and major CSF measures continued to improve. The events were not captured by ictal video-electroencephalography, and their epileptic nature remained uncertain. Microbleed Anatomical Rating Scale (MARS)-based assessment showed a conservative lower bound of ≥100 definite lobar microbleeds at each examination, with stable regional categories but a ceiling effect limiting detection of increases. In this patient, recurrent prolonged motor events occurred with different evidence of CAA-ri activity. New or worsening inflammatory MRI abnormalities were central to identifying renewed activity, whereas serial CSF findings provided supporting context when clinical and imaging findings did not change together. Mild residual CSF abnormalities during radiological improvement should not be interpreted as relapse in isolation. Recurrent motor events should prompt reassessment of imaging, CSF when clinically appropriate, and competing causes rather than automatic escalation of immunosuppression.

papers.title: How family medicine physicians and trainees in israel perceive generative artificial intelligence: a qualitative study of challenges and support needs for its use in work and training
papers.authors: Inbar Levkovich, Lilach Alon
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools are increasingly being used in clinical practice, yet little is known about how family medicine physicians and trainees explain how these tools work, the challenges they experience, and the support they consider necessary for responsible use. This study qualitatively examined participants’ written descriptions of GenAI across the family medicine training continuum. A qualitative descriptive study was conducted among 87 participants across the family medicine training continuum in Israel, including medical students in family medicine rotations ( n = 28), interns ( n = 13), residents ( n = 16), and specialists or senior physicians ( n = 30). Data were collected through three open-ended prompts embedded in an online Hebrew-language questionnaire. The prompts addressed how GenAI produces responses, challenges associated with its use, and support needed for effective and responsible use. Written responses were analyzed thematically using ATLAS.ti. The analysis remained close to explicitly stated content because the brief written responses did not permit probing or follow-up. Coding was non-exclusive, and all 87 participants provided a usable response to each prompt. Information-aggregation descriptions were identified in 58 participants’ responses (66.7%), and 44 participants (50.6%) likened GenAI to a search engine. Only 10 participants (11.5%) explicitly mentioned probabilistic text generation. Output trustworthiness was the most frequently coded concern: 39 participants (44.8%) mentioned accuracy or reliability, and 20 (23.0%) mentioned hallucinations or fabricated information. Regarding support needs, GenAI literacy and source verification were each mentioned by 18 participants (20.7%), followed by formal training ( n = 10, 11.5%) and access to medical-specific GenAI tools ( n = 9, 10.3%). Because coding was non-exclusive, the counts overlap and should be interpreted descriptively. These findings point to a possible need for targeted GenAI literacy education within family medicine training programs, for clinical governance frameworks, and for GenAI tools that meet the evidentiary standards of medical practice. Because the material consists of brief written answers, these are implications generated by an exploratory sample rather than established requirements.

papers.title: Role of Telemedicine in Congenital Heart Disease Care Models in Low‐ and Middle‐Income Countries: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
papers.authors: Sandra S. Mattos, Dominique Vervoort, Shazia Moshin, Gary F. Sholler, Yashendra Sethi, Sunita Maheshwari, Kun Sun, Derrick Bennett, Liesl Joanna Zuhlke, Sandra L. Staveski
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.abstract: Telemedicine is increasingly recognized as a transformative strategy to address critical challenges in low- and middle-income countries, which comprise 63% of all nations, 84% of the global population, and 90% of children <15 years of age. These regions experience multiple barriers, including geographic remoteness, economic constraints, limited healthcare infrastructure, and a shortage of trained healthcare professionals. Congenital heart disease, a highly specialized field often centralized in urban centers, is particularly affected, leaving many children without timely or equitable access to life-saving care. In this context, telecardiology has emerged as a valuable tool across the congenital heart disease care continuum, supporting prehospital assessment, inpatient management, postdischarge follow-up, and multidisciplinary collaboration. Beyond video consultations, telemedicine enables secure transmission of electrocardiograms, echocardiograms, advanced imaging, and digital auscultation data. Artificial intelligence-based tools further enhance education, diagnostic support, and quality assurance in image acquisition. Together, these capabilities reduce unnecessary travel, expedite specialist input, strengthen local decision-making, and contribute to improved outcomes. Telemedicine also facilitates collaboration among pediatric cardiologists, neonatologists, intensivists, imaging specialists, and nurses, fostering more integrated and resilient care networks that link peripheral facilities with tertiary centers. By optimizing limited resources and expanding specialist reach, telemedicine holds significant promise for improving access, equity, and outcomes in congenital heart disease care across low- and middle-income countries. Continued investment, strategic planning, and collaborative capacity-building will be essential to ensure its sustainable and effective implementation worldwide.

papers.title: The Impact of Customizing Pedagogical Agents on Learners’ Intrinsic Motivation and Satisfaction in Augmented Reality
papers.authors: Ahmad A Fouad, Hyeongil Nam, Kangsoo Kim
papers.journal: ACM Symposium on Spatial User Interaction (SUI)
papers.abstract: Embodied Pedagogical Agents (EPAs) are increasingly used in Extended Reality (XR) educational and training applications. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this work-in-progress investigates whether allowing learners to customize an EPA’s physical appearance supports perceived autonomy and intrinsic motivation. We present an LLM-driven embodied pedagogical agent for augmented reality and describe a planned 2 × 2 within-subject study examining the effects of appearance customization (Customized vs. Non-Customized) and instructional role (Peer vs. Expert). The study will assess autonomy satisfaction, intrinsic motivation, perceived relatedness, and behavioral engagement during an AR-based mathematics learning task.

papers.title: Human-AI Interactions in AR for Museum Serious Games
papers.authors: Christos Koulouris, Stylianos Mystakidis, Athanasios Christopoulos, Andreas Komninos, Ioulia Simou
papers.journal: ACM Symposium on Spatial User Interaction (SUI)
papers.abstract: We present preliminary experiences with a serious museum game, integrating Augmented Reality (AR) with a Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI)-powered conversational avatar, under solo and team play conditions. The experience is centered on a museum rescue mission in which players must locate and neutralize virtual mines hidden among telecommunication exhibits. Results of a mixed-method evaluation study provide strong evidence that the integration of AR and GenAI in a serious escape game constitutes an effective and engaging approach for enhancing museum-based learning experiences and does not detract from interpersonal dynamics during the experience.

papers.title: Evaluating Real-time Point Cloud Visualization in Quadrupedal Robot Teleoperation
papers.authors: Jordan Smothers, Andrew Rukangu, Kyle Johnsen
papers.journal: ACM Symposium on Spatial User Interaction (SUI)
papers.abstract: Spatial interfaces for robot teleoperation remain underexplored, particularly for mobile legged platforms. We present RobotCommand XR (RCXR), a Mixed Reality (MR) based teleoperation research prototype that provides operators with a low-latency stereoscopic video feed and a real-time fused LiDAR and depth camera point cloud reconstruction, rendered in a Meta Quest 3 headset alongside an animated miniature replica of the robot. We report a within-subjects user study (n=14) comparing two conditions: point cloud enabled (PCL) and video alone (No-PCL). While task performance did not differ significantly, the PCL condition produced a large, robust reduction in arm camera usage (arm active time: PCL=105 s vs. No-PCL=160 s, d=-0.84, p=0.006), increased time in motion, higher perceived difficulty and workload, and strong preference (13 of 14 participants) for the PCL condition for environmental understanding and spatial confidence. Point cloud reconstruction may have reduced reliance on camera-mediated environmental exploration in favor of continuous passive spatial awareness. Design implications for MR teleoperation interfaces are discussed.

papers.title: Care or Curiosity? Evaluating More-Than-Human Spatial Interactions in Shared Environments
papers.authors: Andreas Komninos, Dimitrios Stasinos, Giovanni Cascone
papers.journal: ACM Symposium on Spatial User Interaction (SUI)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider situated interactions with technologically augmented plants to foster meaningful care relationships within shared physical environments. Under empirical evaluation and an ethics of care lens, we present reflections from a technological probe that uses environmental sensors and a Large Language Model to give a plant a conversational persona, exploring how anthropomorphic behaviours mediate embodied, spatial care interactions. We question whether algorithmic agency authentically empowers natural entities as interactive participants in co-located environments, or merely traps them within a human-centric illusion. Ultimately, we provide directions for future designs of non-human technological augmentations in spatial interaction.

papers.title: Design and Development of Multimaterial Soft Vacuum Actuator for Humanoid Facial Expression Generation
papers.authors: Vijay Saini, Pushparaj Mani Pathak
papers.abstract: Abstract Biomimetic humanoid robots are increasingly recognized for their potential in the medical and social domains. Achieving action unit (AU)-geometric approximated lifelike facial expressions in such robots requires small-scale in-place biomimetic soft actuators capable of replicating the motion patterns of corresponding human facial muscles. Mimicking human facial muscles requires a thin actuator capable of producing linear contraction to function effectively within constrained anatomical spaces; to address this, this work presents a multimaterial soft vacuum actuator (M-SVA) inspired by the localized buckling behavior of beams. Under negative pressure, the actuator undergoes controlled buckling, causing its internal pneumatic cavities to collapse in a directed manner, resulting in longitudinal contraction. The development process involves 3D printing of the actuator core, elastomer molding of the skin cover, and their assembly. The numerical and experimental findings demonstrate that M-SVA provides several advantages, including high flexibility, large actuation strain (0.3–0.5), substantial actuation stress (0.053 MPa), and a notable blocked force of 5.53 N. Furthermore, M-SVA is readily scalable, allowing its deformation and output force to be tuned for targeted expressions by varying the core length and thickness, respectively. To demonstrate practical applicability, the actuators were placed in muscle-analog positions beneath a silicone facial skin on a humanoid head, generating intensities of AU12 and AU15 for happy and sad expressions, which support natural human–robot interaction.

papers.title: Mapping AI Ethics Integration in Postgraduate Health Professions Education: A Scoping Review Through the Lenses of Principlism and Transformative Learning
papers.authors: Tricia Mae Wong, Ang Yu Chien Constance, M. M. Hussein, Claude Jeffrey Renaud
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is disrupting healthcare and health professions education (HPE), creating complex ethical challenges. Despite existing governance frameworks, postgraduate and continuing professional development (CPD) learners require stronger micro-level ethical competence. However, AI-ethics remains insufficiently integrated into postgraduate/CPD curricula with few real-world reflective and interprofessional strategies, raising concerns regarding ethical preparedness. The aim of this study is to map how AI ethics is taught within postgraduate/CPD HPE, drawing on principlism, an ethical framework espousing the principles of autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence and justice and transformative learning theory (TLT), which explains how critical reflection transforms professional assumptions, perspectives and practice. METHOD: A systematic search of six databases (2000-2025) was conducted to identify relevant sources. Data extraction captured study design, educational setting, pedagogical strategies and ethical themes. Findings were synthesised descriptively and narratively to examine empirical rigour, theoretical alignment and relevance to contemporary generative-AI developments. RESULTS: Sixteen eligible sources were identified. Only 31% were empirical studies. The evidence reflected a strong Western worldview. AI-ethics education for postgraduate/CPD learners was limited, often superficial and reliant on varied but weakly evaluated pedagogies. Principlism appeared frequently but mostly implicitly, whereas explicit application of TLT was rare. Major gaps included low empirical and pedagogical rigour, minimal interprofessionalism and marked temporal anachronism, as most studies predated the advent of generative AI. CONCLUSION: AI-ethics education in postgraduate/CPD HPE remains conceptually rich but pedagogically underdeveloped. Effective curricula require structured, theory-anchored, interprofessional and culturally responsive approaches. Integrating principlism and TLT as ethical and pedagogical frameworks may strengthen ethical competence and preparedness.

papers.title: Motives matter: A smartphone EMA study on the association between motives to exercise, exercise engagement and mood
papers.authors: Leonardo Pimpini, Ella Ferrand, Codrin Mironiuc, Jan Schepers, Anne Roefs
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Regular exercise is vital for preventing cardiovascular disease, maintaining a healthy body weight and supporting mental well-being, yet most people exercise insufficiently often due to motivational barriers. DESIGN: This study examined two types of exercise motive-functional (divided into health/fitness and enjoyment) and appearance-and their interplay with mood and exercise engagement in daily life. Two hypotheses were tested: (H1) functional motives, compared to appearance motive, predict greater exercise engagement, and (H2) higher (more positive) mood, in interaction with exercise motives, predicts greater exercise engagement. METHOD: Ninety-eight healthy BMI women completed a 2-week smartphone Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) protocol reporting exercise motive (baseline), exercise engagement (frequency, intensity, duration) and mood several times/day. RESULTS: Partially supporting H1, enjoyment motive predicted greater exercise frequency and duration, whereas-contrary to H1- health/fitness motive predicted shorter duration and appearance was unrelated to engagement. H2 was not supported: mood did not predict engagement and functional motives did not strengthen the mood-engagement link. Contrary to H2, the appearance motive strengthened the (same-moment) within-person association between mood and exercise intensity, such that women higher in appearance motive showed a stronger positive mood-intensity link. Multilevel temporal networks revealed that higher (more positive) mood at one assessment weakly predicted greater exercise intensity and duration at the next assessment. CONCLUSIONS: Together, enjoyment emerges as central to exercise engagement, while positive mood temporally precedes exercise, informing future lifestyle interventions. Further research on the temporal dynamics linking mood and exercise is warranted.

papers.title: RAIM: Operationalising Trustworthy AI in Music Generation
papers.authors: Jacopo de Berardinis, Tess Buckley, Lorenzo Porcaro, Thomas Brett, Albert Merono-Penuela, Angelo Cangelosi, Joost de Boo, Arcangelo Leone de Castris, Mark d'Inverno, Maria Eriksson, Marianna Bergamaschi Ganapini, Daniel Gervais, Iliana Grosse-Buening, Alexandra Huang-Kokina, Sabine Jacques, Ella Keating, Robert Laidlow, Loren McShane, Piotr Mirowski, Fabio Morreale, Caterina Moruzzi, Oonagh Murphy, Andrea Pedeferri, Jean-Jacques Rojer, Paul Stakounis, Elizabeth Wilson, Matthew John Yee-King
papers.abstract: Generative AI is radically reshaping the musical landscape, unlocking new forms of creative expression while simultaneously raising profound ethical, legal, and societal concerns. Key among these are the potential displacement of human creativity, copyright infringement stemming from vast training datasets, and the lack of transparency, explainability, and fairness mechanisms. As generative systems become pervasive, shifting from reactive regulation to responsible design is crucial. While previous work has tackled isolated aspects of generative systems, we propose a systematic framework grounded in the Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI produced by the European Commission's High-Level Expert Group. Focusing on generative music AI, we contextualise these requirements into 45 responsible features that address trustworthiness across technical, legal, and artistic dimensions. We validate this framework through a multi-stage Delphi study involving a global panel of experts from academia, industry, and regulatory bodies, comprising AI ethicists, legal experts, music AI practitioners, and artists. The results demonstrate a high degree of expert endorsement for the proposed features, while revealing thematic tensions between the protectionist priorities of artists and the technical constraints of practitioners. We argue that the framework functions as a translation layer, operationalising complementarity to harmonise different stakeholder values rather than forcing a monolithic consensus. Ultimately, this work provides an empirically grounded foundation for the design, evaluation, and regulation of Responsible AI in Music (RAIM).

papers.title: Bridging awareness and trust: using thematic analysis to understand AI adoption such as DeepSeek in Chinese higher education
papers.authors: Muhammad Farrukh Shahzad, Muhammad Asif, Shuo Xu, Ahmad Raza Bilal, Imran Zahid
papers.journal: International Journal of Information and Learning Technology
papers.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore Chinese university students' perceptions, awareness and trust regarding the adoption of DeepSeek, an artificial intelligence (AI) tool increasingly used for academic purposes in higher education. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed using semi-structured interviews with Chinese university students. Thematic analysis was conducted using NVivo 15 to identify recurring themes related to awareness, trust and AI adoption as DeepSeek. Findings The findings reveal four key thematic dimensions: (1) awareness sources and accessibility, (2) perceived academic benefits, (3) trust shaped by information reliability, algorithmic transparency and institutional compliance and (4) concerns related to data privacy, response quality and regulatory policies. Trust emerged as a pivotal factor influencing students' willingness to adopt AI as DeepSeek. The results emphasize the importance of ethical guidelines and institutional support to promote responsible and informed use of AI in higher education. Practical implications The study provides actionable insights for educators, policymakers and institutions to strengthen trust, enhance ethical practices and develop policies that support the effective incorporation of AI technologies in educational contexts. Originality/value This study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI adoption in education by offering empirical insights into how awareness and trust shape students' acceptance and responsible use of AI-driven learning tools such as DeepSeek in Chinese higher education.

papers.title: Academic writing in the AI era: enhancing EFL learners' academic writing skills through ChatGPT, critical thinking and academic self-efficacy
papers.authors: Zahra Maryam, Sazuliana Binti Sanif, Asad U.R. Rehman, Ayesha Nawal, Muhammad Shoaib
papers.journal: International Journal of Information and Learning Technology
papers.abstract: Purpose As an effective and valuable language-learning tool, ChatGPT provides dynamic learning experiences. The advent of ChatGPT has revolutionized traditional language-learning methods, transforming them into innovative systems that provide multilingual support and personalized learning experiences. The present study assessed the impact of ChatGPT on the academic writing skills of English as a foreign language (EFL) learners, focusing on paragraph organization, grammar, and sentence structure. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was used to collect data from 325 Malaysian EFL learners via a self-administered questionnaire, using the verified scales for each construct. AMOS version 24.0 was used to perform structural equation modeling (SEM), a multivariate data analysis technique, and path analysis to evaluate the direct and indirect effects of the variables. Bootstrapping approaches were employed to test the mediation and moderation hypotheses using 5,000 samples and a 95% confidence interval. Findings Using ChatGPT significantly enhances the accuracy and validity of EFL learners' academic writing proficiency. Moreover, the present study primarily focused on the role of critical thinking as a mediator, highlighting its function in minimizing cognitive offloading and encouraging more in-depth, reflective learning when using ChatGPT. Additionally, academic self-efficacy significantly moderates ChatGPT's impact on critical thinking and academic writing skills, highlighting the importance of psychological factors in boosting students' confidence and perseverance in AI-supported academic writing activities. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in its use of a mediated-moderated paradigm that has not been extensively examined in previous research on the effects of generative AI, notably ChatGPT, on EFL students' academic writing abilities. This research offers a deeper understanding of the internal mental and psychological mechanisms that influence writing development by examining the mediating role of critical thinking ability and the moderating effect of academic self-efficacy. This study fills a significant gap in the field of language education and AI-assisted learning by offering that students actively evaluate, analyze, and improve AI-generated information rather than merely accepting it, which goes beyond a superficial assessment of AI use and offers empirical data on how distinctive learners' characteristics interact with AI tools to influence writing outcomes. This method encourages students to acquire autonomous writing abilities in addition to AI help by moving the emphasis from tool usage to cognitive engagement. This shows their active and independent learning and cognitive engagement instead of passive dependency.

papers.title: Crisis-induced hybrid learning, cognitive offloading, and generative AI reliance among Pakistani CS undergraduates
papers.authors: Hassan Ahmed, Abdullah Khan, Arooj Fatima, Abdul Mateen, Shahrzad Saremi, Rania Shibl, Sadegh Rajaei, Mansooreh Mirzaei
papers.journal: Education Innovations Systems and Future Learning
papers.abstract: Purpose In spring 2026, geopolitical tensions prompted the Pakistani government to mandate full online instruction (10 March–3 April 2026), followed by a hybrid schedule for the rest of the semester. This shift is treated here as an externally imposed crisis context for AI adoption, not as a natural experiment. No pre-crisis baseline or control group was available. The study characterises generative AI (GenAI) adoption patterns and the psychological antecedents of AI dependency among undergraduate computer-science (CS) students during this window. Three hypotheses, grounded in the reviewed literature, structured the analysis. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was administered across Pakistani higher education institutions (HEIs) in April–May 2026. Of 360 responses collected, two incomplete records were removed, and a thirteen-criterion data-quality screen was ap-plied, yielding N = 299. Fourteen constructs were operationalised from UTAUT, Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), Self-Determination Theory (SDT), and the AI Anxiety Scale (AIAS). Block-entry OLS regression and bootstrapped mediation (5,000 resamples) tested the hypotheses; ANOVA and Spearman correlations supported descriptive analysis of adoption patterns. Findings Adoption was near-universal (>99%), with 45.2% of respondents reporting ≥ 31% of submitted work directly AI-generated. A three-block OLS regression explained 54.6% of variance in AI dependency. Cognitive offloading was the strongest predictor (β = 0.41, p < 0.001), followed by procrastination (β = 0.23, p < 0.001), extrinsic motivation (β = 0.17, p = 0.002), and intrinsic motivation as a protective factor (β = −0.13, p = 0.013). Bootstrapped mediation confirmed procrastination partially mediates the extrinsic motivation–dependency path (ab = 0.201, 95% BC-CI [0.122, 0.289]). Originality/value To our knowledge, this is among the first studies to survey GenAI dependency during an active government-mandated crisis disruption in South Asian higher education. Contributions include a multi-theory construct battery adapted for a crisis context, a thirteen-criterion response-quality protocol, and evidence that habituated cognitive offloading and extrinsic motivation are the primary drivers of AI dependency in this context.

papers.title: The AI letdown
papers.journal: Development in Learning Organizations An International Journal
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings A two-wave study of 219 firms finds that AI adoption raises knowledge creation only by running through organizational learning, and that being “AI ready” adds nothing once the technology is already deployed. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

papers.title: Photography training and inhibitory control: ERP correlates and dissociable patterns from athletic training
papers.authors: Chenyu Guo, Zhijie Zhang, Yiran Deng, Ziyi Cao, Shiwei Liu, Jie Zhang
papers.abstract: Objective Long‑term engagement in professional behavioral training and the resulting behavioral changes are known to influence human cognition. The present study investigates whether and how photography training is associated with individuals’ inhibitory control. Methods Fifteen photographers, 15 athletes, and 15 controls were recruited to complete a Go/Nogo task with concurrent electroencephalogram recording. Results Behavioral results showed slower response times and fewer commission errors for both photographers and athletes compared with controls, with no significant difference between the two training groups. Event‑related potential analyses revealed more negative Bereitschaftspotential amplitudes and more positive N2 amplitudes for photographers and athletes than for controls, again with no significant difference between photographers and athletes. Furthermore, a more negative prefrontal negativity amplitude was observed for athletes than for both photographers and controls, whereas no significant difference was found between photographers and controls. Conclusion Photography training was associated with a shift in the speed–accuracy trade‑off toward a greater emphasis on accuracy, as well as motor preparation and conflict monitoring—two core subprocesses of inhibitory control. Moreover, photographers and athletes showed improvements in inhibitory control through different neurocognitive pathways: while both groups showed enhanced motor preparation and conflict monitoring, athletes additionally exhibited enhanced cognitive preparation compared with photographers. This differential pattern may reflect athletes’ need to respond to unpredictable, real‑time emergencies during competition.

papers.title: Responsible AI adoption in hospitality: a maturity-based analysis of value, risk and governance
papers.authors: Shabbir Pokkakillath
papers.abstract: The hospitality industry is undergoing a significant transformation as AI, automation and robotics become embedded across pricing, operations, service delivery and enterprise coordination. Although AI adoption is widespread, academic research and industry discourse remain fragmented, often emphasising isolated technologies or short-term performance outcomes. This article addresses this gap through an integrative empirical review examining how different forms of AI reshape decision-making, service processes and organisational structures in hospitality. The article adopts a functional perspective that classifies AI systems along three conceptual dimensions: level of autonomy; learning capability; and task complexity. The findings show that AI can improve efficiency, responsiveness and revenue performance when aligned with organisational readiness and integrated into commercial and service strategies. However, benefits are uneven, and adoption introduces organisational, ethical and socio-technical trade-offs. To address these challenges, the article proposes a contextually differentiated AI adoption maturity framework aligned with governance, responsible AI practices and risk management, recognising that large and small/medium enterprises face fundamentally different conditions at each stage. Overall, AI outcomes depend on how technology is governed and combined with human expertise to sustain hospitality’s human-centric foundations.

papers.title: Text-to-image GenAI integration in architecture pedagogy: skills, knowledge, and competencies: a case study
papers.authors: Aminreza Iranmanesh, Pooya Lotfabadi, Zeynep Üstün Onur
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of text-to-image generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on architectural education from the student perspective in a case study. The study specifically focuses on AI image-generation practices and examines how students perceive these tools as influencing the expected knowledge, skills, and competencies of an architecture curriculum. A structured survey was used to evaluate the nine official programme learning outcomes (PLOs) via 19 items. Analyses include descriptive statistics and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The results indicate that students generally perceive text-to-image GenAI as having a moderately positive influence on their learning processes, with some indicative variation across year levels. Students report the most notable perceived benefits in relation to design process and communication. PCA identified three emergent domains: (1) disciplinary foundations and professional responsibility, (2) design thinking and representational–analytical skills, and (3) integrative and applied competencies. Together, the three factors capture different ways in which AI image-generation tools are perceived within the curriculum. Based on these outcomes, it is also argued that the advent of GenAI in architecture pedagogy is not as groundbreaking as the literature often indicates. Thus, areas of concern have been highlighted, including potential overreliance, diminished independent creativity, and ethical issues related to authorship, authenticity, and professional accountability. The study offers evidence-based insight into how text-to-image GenAI is currently viewed within architectural education.

papers.title: The Convergence of Artificial Intelligence and Human Sexuality
papers.authors: Carlos Miguel Ríos-González
papers.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and human sexuality is reshaping intimacy, sexuality education, entertainment, and therapeutic practice. This narrative review analyzes these transformations through the complementary lenses of Sexual Script Theory (SST; Simon & Gagnon, Citation1986) and technological mediation theory (Verbeek, Citation2012), which together illuminate how AI does not merely respond to preexisting sexual behaviors but can mediate, generate, and transform sexual scripts at individual, interpersonal, and societal levels. For the purposes of this review, AI is defined broadly to encompass both traditional machine-learning (ML) systems—such as recommendation, ranking, and predictive algorithms—and contemporary generative AI (GenAI), including large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Claude and multimodal systems capable of generating synthetic text, images, audio, and video. The review examines five domains selected for their prominence in the recent literature and their capacity to illustrate different levels of script formation and technological mediation: sex robots and AI companions, AI-generated pornography, algorithmic dating and AI-mediated romantic communication, AI-assisted sexuality education, and AI-supported sexual health and therapeutic applications. Across these domains, AI offers opportunities to expand access to information, connection, and support while simultaneously raising concerns about consent, privacy, objectification, bias, authenticity, and cultural representation. An ethically responsible approach therefore requires attention not only to what AI systems produce, but also to the sexual scripts, relational expectations, and values that their design and use may normalize.

papers.title: Generative AI and the balance of effort in group tasks: Appropriate, over-, and under-scaffolding
papers.authors: Корчак Анна Эдуардовна, Christopher Hughes, Jamie Costley
papers.journal: Journal of Research on Technology in Education
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) is increasingly used in higher education, yet its role in collaborative learning remains unclear. This study examines how students use Gen-AI during group lesson-planning tasks in an undergraduate education course. Drawing on Vygotsky’s sociocultural theory, we introduce the concept of “an effort space” and apply the categories of appropriate, over-, and under-scaffolding to Gen-AI use. The analysis of 75 students’ reflections, chat logs, and lesson plans identified three patterns: appropriate support that preserved learner effort, over-scaffolding through task outsourcing or free-riding that eliminates learner effort, and under-scaffolding through AI avoidance. These patterns show how Gen-AI reshapes collaborative learning.

papers.title: Optimization of visibility-adaptive expressway early warning schemes under sand-dust weather considering driver workload
papers.authors: Fang Wang, Jiayue Xing, Peng Xu, Liyi Sun, Hao Yang, Jun Ma
papers.abstract: Objective: Sand-dust weather conditions severely reduce visibility and pavement friction on desert expressways, substantially increasing crash risks. Existing early warning systems rely primarily on fixed thresholds and single-modal information, often neglecting driver cognitive and physiological workload. This study aimed to develop and optimize a visibility-adaptive multimodal early warning scheme for desert expressways under sand-dust weather conditions, with a focus on balancing driving safety and human workload.Methods: A high-fidelity driving simulator was used to construct four visibility scenarios: 500, 300, 100, and 50 m, representing typical sand-dust weather conditions on the Wuma Expressway. Thirty-six licensed drivers completed 64 orthogonal test conditions combining variable message signs (VMS), LED linear guidance, and voice navigation. Eye movement, driving behavior, and physiological indices (ECG and EEG) were synchronously collected. ACriteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC)-weighted multidimensional evaluation system was established, incorporating speed compliance, steering stability, heart rate (HR), and EEG β/θ ratio, to screen the optimal scheme via Euclidean distance decision-making.Results: Visibility significantly deteriorated driving performance and elevated workload. The optimal multimodal schemes varied by visibility: 500 m (60 flashes/min LEDs + speed/distance voice); 300–100 m (120 flashes/min LEDs + steering/fog-light voice); 50 m (constant LEDs + operational guidance). Compared with single-modal warnings, the optimized scheme demonstrated statistically significant improvements at 500 m and 300 m visibility (p < 0.0031, Bonferroni-corrected), increasing speed compliance by 10.6 percentage points (to 89.2%), reducing steering angle deviation by 0.005–0.01 rad and lateral acceleration deviation by 0.05–0.1 m/s2, lowering heart rate by 4.28 bpm, and raising the β/θ ratio by 0.14. At 100 m and 50 m visibility, nonsignificant but directionally consistent trends were observed (p = 0.011 and p = 0.034, respectively; Cohen’s d = 0.43 and 0.37), indicating a practical reduction in overall physiological load of approximately 15–20% that warrants further validation under stringent statistical thresholds.Conclusions: The visibility-adaptive multimodal early warning scheme effectively improves driving stability and mitigates driver workload under sand-dust weather conditions. Tiered information delivery and dynamic LED parameters enhance information perception and reduce visual fatigue. The findings offer a cognitive-load-informed framework to guide the parameter tuning of traffic management strategies and safety improvement on desert expressways during extreme sand-dust weather.

papers.title: Navigating an Inevitable Transformation: A Reflection on Responsible Scientific Writing Large Language Models Integration and the RULE-AP Consensus
papers.authors: Jose Andrés Calvache, Burhan Dost, Alessandro DE CASSAI
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are reshaping scientific communication in Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine. The RULE-AP Delphi consensus – convening 53 editors-in-chief – proposes a regulatory framework that distinguishes legitimate assistance from intellectual abdication. We argue that LLMs offer genuine value for derivative tasks such as language polishing, reference formatting, and search strategy refinement, thereby reducing cognitive load and democratizing access for non-native English speakers. However, human authors must retain exclusive responsibility for hypothesis generation, result interpretation, and conclusions. LLMs cannot serve as authors; they lack legal standing, produce hallucinations, and cannot exercise clinical judgment. The proliferation of algorithmically generated manuscripts threatens to dilute the peer-reviewed literature and compromise AI training corpora – a self-reinforcing risk requiring urgent editorial vigilance. We further caution against using LLMs to generate peer-review reports, as doing so violates confidentiality and undermines the nuanced judgment that rigorous review demands. To preserve trust, we advocate for standardized AI Disclosure Statements in all submissions. Transparency is not a confession of weakness – it is the foundation of reproducible, accountable science. Education in responsible LLM use must become standard training for the next generation of researchers.

papers.title: Comparing chatbot and peer interaction among trilingual students: effects on self-regulated learning, critical thinking, task engagement and reading comprehension
papers.authors: Huiling Ma
papers.abstract: This study examined the differential effects of chatbot-mediated interaction and peer interaction on trilingual students’ English reading comprehension, self-regulated learning, critical thinking, and task engagement. Using a mixed-methods design, the study combined pre- and post-intervention quantitative measures with semi-structured interviews conducted throughout the intervention. Quantitative findings revealed that both instructional conditions significantly improved reading comprehension, with no significant between-group difference after controlling for baseline performance. After controlling for baseline performance, the peer interaction group demonstrated significantly higher task engagement than the chatbot-mediated group. The chatbot-mediated group demonstrated significant within-group improvement in self-regulated learning; however, no significant between-group difference was observed. Critical thinking scores increased modestly in both groups, but the within-group changes were not statistically significant, and no significant between-group difference was found. Qualitative analysis identified distinct interactional affordances and constraints. Peer interaction was associated with collaborative engagement, exposure to diverse perspectives, and shared meaning-making, whereas chatbot-mediated interaction provided relatively low-pressure practice, individualized feedback, and opportunities for learner regulation, while presenting challenges related to emotional responsiveness and discourse coherence. Overall, chatbot-mediated and peer interaction were associated with distinct learning experiences and outcomes during reading tasks. The findings highlight their potentially complementary pedagogical roles in trilingual English reading contexts.

papers.title: Living with Risk: Folk Theories of AI Hallucinations Among Young Chinese Users
papers.authors: Huili Liu, Ying Zhang
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life, AI hallucinations have emerged as a significant challenge in human-AI interaction. Drawing on the perspective of algorithmic folk theories, this study combines textual analysis and in-depth interviews with both ordinary users and technical users to examine how they understand and respond to AI hallucinations. Users identify AI hallucinations by scrutinizing the AI’s reasoning process, making intuitive judgments, and conducting cross-validation, while their attitudes toward hallucinations vary. Users develop four types of algorithmic folk theories: the Human-AI Interaction Misalignment Theory, the Technical Limitations Theory, the Data Source Distortion Theory, and the Generative Rule Constraint Theory. They rise to four corresponding coping strategies: reducing communication errors, reconfiguring human-AI task allocation, intervening in data input while verifying outputs, and reducing AI’s processing load. This study further indicates how technological identity and sociotechnical contexts jointly shape algorithmic folk theories.

papers.title: Towards responsible AI in workplace-based assessment: a scoping review using Downing’s framework
papers.authors: Takeshi Kondo, Seiko Miura, Yuki Kataoka, Hiromu Yakura, Hiroshi Nishigori, Jeroen H. H. L. M. Donkers
papers.journal: Assessment in Education Principles Policy and Practice
papers.abstract: This scoping review maps generative AI applications in workplace-based assessment (WBA) and analyzes validity evidence through Downing’s framework. Following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, four databases were searched (2022-February 2026) with dual-AI screening and human adjudication. Data were mapped to Downing’s five validity sources using AI-assisted extraction with human verification. Thirteen studies (2024–2025) met inclusion criteria. All AI applications operated on pre-existing text; feedback analysis predominated (9/13). Content (12/13), Response Process (13/13), and Relationship to Other Variables (12/13) were well addressed, while Internal Structure (2/13) and Consequences (4/13) were neglected. AI reasoning transparency, inter-model agreement, and internal consistency were absent (0/13). Current evidence concentrates on AI-human agreement, neglecting reproducibility, bias testing, and learner impact evidence essential for responsible deployment. Realising AI’s potential to reduce faculty burden will require non-supervisor oversight mechanisms for continuous validity monitoring, particularly for direct learner-facing applications.

papers.title: Structural and configurational analyses of GenAI-mediated informal digital learning of Chinese, multicultural personality traits, and willingness to communicate: evidence from plurilingual international students in China
papers.authors: Minlin Zou, Mirosław Pawlak, Mariusz Kruk, Weichen Wang
papers.journal: Journal of Multilingual and Multicultural Development
papers.abstract: This study examines how plurilingual international students’ generative AI-mediated informal digital learning of Chinese (GenAI-IDLC) interacts with dimensions of multicultural personality to predict their second language willingness to communicate (L2 WTC). Survey responses were collected from 387 plurilingual international students learning Chinese in China and analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) approaches. SEM results demonstrated that learners’ GenAI-IDLC was significantly and positively associated with cultural empathy, open-mindedness, social initiative, flexibility, and L2 WTC, but not emotional stability. Moreover, international students’ flexibility was significantly and positively associated with their L2 WTC, whereas their cultural empathy, open-mindedness, emotional stability, and social initiative were not significantly associated with their L2 WTC. The association between GenAI-IDLC and L2 WTC was partially mediated by flexibility. The fsQCA further identified four configurations in which different combinations of GenAI-IDLC and multicultural personality were linked to high L2 WTC. By integrating SEM with fsQCA, the study advances our understanding of the multiple and complex pathways underlying L2 WTC in the GenAI-mediated informal Chinese learning context. The results offer a basis for implications for language educators and universities seeking to facilitate cross-cultural communication through GenAI technologies.

papers.title: Cyber-pornography use among a sample of Chinese university students: utilizing machine learning and network analysis
papers.authors: Li Li, Zhimin Niu, Junting Hu, Songli Mei, Mark Damian Griffiths
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Due to the popularity and convenience of the internet, cyber-pornography use among youth has attracted the widespread attention of scholars. Cyber-pornography use among Chinese university students remains rarely investigated, especially based on ecological systems theory using machine learning and network analysis approaches. Therefore, the present study examined cyber-pornography use through machine learning and network analysis based on ecological systems theory among a sample of Chinese university students. METHODS: A sample of 1322 university students in different provinces of China were surveyed in a cross-sectional study. The survey included cyber-pornography use variables, demographic information, psychological variables, family variables, and school factors. RESULTS: Of 1332 participants, 25 students were classed as high-risk cyber-pornography users (1.9%). The XGBoost model of machine learning identified 15 important features of cyber-pornography use including social ostracism, moral disengagement, gender, teacher fairness, year of study, age, autonomy, self-control, depression, father and mother's parenting style, relatedness, experience of being left behind, loneliness, and family closeness. In the network analysis, social ostracism was the strongest node in the total sample and among males, whereas depression was the strongest node in females. CONCLUSIONS: Psychological, family, school, and demographic factors (e.g. gender) may directly or indirectly be associated with cyber-pornography use among Chinese university students. The results suggest that ecological systems theory, including the microsystem, mesosystem, macrosystem, and chronosystem, may be considered as one of the core theories in understanding cyber-pornography use. In addition, the interaction of related factors also needs to be examined deeply to aid prevention and intervention of cyber-pornography use in the future.

papers.title: The future of surgery
papers.authors: Donald W. Weaver, J. Edson Pontes, David S. Edelman, S. Kiran Koya, David Ellis
papers.abstract: Abstract Surgery is entering a period of accelerated transformation driven by artificial intelligence, robotics, and emerging postmodern medical technologies. Unlike prior technological shifts, innovation cycles are compressing into years, challenging established models of evidence generation, regulation, training, and professional identity. This Perspective examines plausible trajectories for digital surgery, emphasizing ethical, educational, and institutional adaptation under conditions of continuous technological acceleration rather than offering definitive predictions.

papers.title: Glucose and lipid metabolism indicators associate with metabolic syndrome risk prediction in adults with hypertension
papers.authors: Yingxin Guo, Lixuan Chen, Xinyi Ouyang, Minying Sun, Tao Lin, Xudong Li, Shanshan Wang, Qianxi Li, Tianpeng Wang, Zihan Yu, Ziyan Zhang, Jiahui Wu, Xiaojing Liao, Zhaorui Zhang, Yaohui Liang, Tangchun Wu, Wei Zhu, Qifei Deng, Degang Wu
papers.abstract: Hypertensive adults are at high risk of metabolic syndrome (MetS), yet accurate risk prediction tools for this group are scarce. We prospectively followed 130,489 Chinese hypertensive adults from the Guangzhou Hypertensive Population Community Cohort (GHPCC) for 6–36 months to document incident MetS. Cox regression and stratified analyses identified key risk factors. Five machine-learning algorithms were used to build an optimal MetS risk prediction model, which was externally validated in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Predictor importance was assessed, partial dependence plots examined key effects, and a reference level for the top predictor was derived. Body fat percentage (BFP), Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI), basal metabolic rate (BMR), and triglyceride-glucose-related indices (TyG-WC, TyG-WHtR, TyG-BMI) are more strongly associated with incident MetS than traditional indicators such as waist circumference and fasting glucose. These associations vary markedly in magnitude across subgroups defined by sex, age, alcohol use, smoking, education, and physical activity, but same in directions. Among five algorithms, the XGBoost-based model performs best, with TyG-BMI as the strongest predictor. When the distributions of other features were held constant, the predicted probability of MetS reached 50% at a TyG‑BMI level of approximately 222.97 kg/m², suggesting a strong association with MetS risk. Notably, this value represents a descriptive reference point from the partial dependence plot rather than a clinically validated independent threshold. Biological age also shows superior predictive value over chronological age. BFP, CVAI, BMR, and TyG-related indices are robust and modifiable predictors of MetS in hypertensive patients. Our findings may help stratify high-risk hypertensive adults for targeted prevention. High blood pressure is common, and people with this condition are more likely to develop metabolic syndrome — a cluster of conditions including obesity, high blood sugar, and abnormal cholesterol that raise the risk of severe diseases such as heart disease and stroke. However, doctors lack simple tools to identify hypertensive patients at higher risk of metabolic syndrome. In this study, we followed more than 130,000 Chinese adults with high blood pressure for up to three years. We used machine learning to build a computer model that predicts who will develop metabolic syndrome. The model uses easy-to-measure indicators, such as body fat percentage, waist-related obesity indices, and a combined score of blood sugar and triglycerides.

papers.title: EyeSeek: a large language model for screening and improving health literacy in primary eye care
papers.authors: Jieru Liu, Juzhao Zhang, Lianqiang Gan, Yi Xu, Tao Yu, Yajun Peng, Lina Lu, Jingkuan Song, Senlin Lin, Haidong Zou
papers.abstract: Resource constraints and low health literacy hinder the effectiveness of primary eye care screening. Here, we developed EyeSeek, a specialized large language model (LLM) to provide residents with personalized screening interpretations and guidance. We introduced a novel abstention-driven iterative learning framework to enhance reliability by detecting uncertainty, alongside a role-playing strategy for tailored communication. Findings demonstrated that our method can abstain and seek external answers when handling queries beyond its knowledge boundary, which reduces hallucination. In expert evaluation, EyeSeek outperformed several LLMs and primary care physicians in multiple dimensions. Readability analysis confirmed that EyeSeek adapted responses to Grade 3 ~ 8 levels, enabling more accessible communication for residents with varying educational backgrounds. Furthermore, we performed a single-center real-world prospective study comparing referral adherence between the EyeSeek-assisted group ( n = 84) and the unassisted group ( n = 86). The EyeSeek-assisted group demonstrated higher referral adherence ( P = 0.037) and improved health literacy compared with the unassisted group, with high user satisfaction. Given its multifaceted performance, EyeSeek holds promise as an adaptable digital solution to support primary eye care in community settings.

papers.title: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and odds of subsequent multiple sclerosis: a population-based retrospective case–control study
papers.authors: Y. Eshel, Dana Hadar, Hilla Cohen, Noga Cohen, Sivan Bloch, Daniel Golan
papers.abstract: Impaired attention and executive function are common in both multiple sclerosis (MS) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This study aimed to assess the association between prior ADHD and subsequent development of MS. A retrospective, population-based case–control study using the Israeli Clalit Health Services database (2002–2024). MS cases were identified using ICD codes and medication dispensations. Each case was matched with ten controls by age, sex, socioeconomic status, and ethnicity. Controls did not have MS at the index date of their matched case. ADHD was defined by ICD codes and medication dispensations. Odds ratios for MS following prior ADHD were estimated using multivariable models adjusted for smoking, autoimmune comorbidities, BMI and vitamin D. The study included 5,074 individuals with MS and 50,633 matched controls. 68% were female, mean age at MS diagnosis was 42.7 ± 15.0 years. Prior ADHD was independently associated with higher odds of MS after adjusting for other risk factors (aOR 2.54, 95% CI = 2.11- 3.1, p < 0.001). This association was observed for both childhood and adult ADHD and was independent of the lag between diagnoses. ADHD is associated with increased odds of subsequent MS. This association may reflect prodromal MS, shared risk factors or an inflammatory response to ADHD-related CNS changes. While routine screening of individuals with ADHD for MS is not warranted, judicious use of MRI may facilitate earlier diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: Hybrid deep learning for three-way classification of human-written, AI-generated, and AI-rephrased text
papers.authors: Najma Sadia, Muhammad Naeem Khan, Muhammad Shahzad Faisal, Muhammad Ali Iqbal, Muhammad Saleem Khan, Soo Kyun Kim
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid proliferation of large language models (LLMs) has made it increasingly difficult to distinguish AI-generated and AI-rephrased text from authentic human writing, posing serious risks to academic integrity, journalism, and e-commerce credibility. This paper presents a rigorous benchmark evaluation for three-way AI text origin classification designed to detect human-written, AI-generated, and AI-rephrased text by integrating handcrafted linguistic features, transformer-based contextual embeddings, and ensemble learning strategies. A corpus of 161,788 samples is curated from Amazon product reviews and Twitter posts, with AI-generated text produced via zero-shot prompting and AI-rephrased text produced via few-shot prompting using GPT, DeepSeek, and Kimi. The corpus comprises 46,844 human-written, 57,247 AI-generated, and 57,697 AI-rephrased samples distributed across training (113,249), validation (16,180), and test (32,359) splits. A hybrid feature vector of 168 dimensions is constructed, combining 68 handcrafted stylistic, lexical, linguistic, syntactic, and stylometric features with 100-dimensional embeddings derived from RoBERTa and the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Sentence Transformer. Classical machine learning models, Random Forest, SVM, and Logistic Regression, are trained on this hybrid representation, while RoBERTa-base and DeBERTa-v3-base are fine-tuned end-to-end on raw tokenized text. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that transformer models substantially outperform classical methods, with RoBERTa achieving 95.49% accuracy and DeBERTa-v3 achieving 94.88%. A probability-averaging ensemble further improves accuracy to 95.66%, and a stacking ensemble with a Random Forest meta-learner reaches 96.46%. Ablation studies confirm the complementary value of handcrafted features alongside contextual embeddings. Across all models, AI-rephrased content is the most challenging category due to its semantic proximity to human writing, highlighting a persistent frontier for future research. The dataset and evaluation framework provide a reproducible foundation for future AI content detection research, with generalization to unseen generators and domains identified as primary directions for future work.

papers.title: Obesity prevalence and management insights using Adipoview a real time clinical obesity landscape indicator based on a population study
papers.authors: Han Shi Jocelyn Chew, Su Wei Wan, Xueling Liu, Daryl Kai Ann Chia, Jia Wen Ngooi, Sky Wei Chee Koh, Nicholas WS Chew, Ning Qi Pang, Myint Oo Aung, Kwang Wei Tham, Roger Foo, Jimmy Bok Yan So, Asim Shabbir, James Wai Kit Lee, Nick Sevdalis, Kee Yuan Ngiam
papers.abstract: Obesity, a multifactorial chronic condition shaped by biological, environmental, and social determinants, is often inadequately measured, monitored, diagnosed or managed. Therefore, we aimed to study the prevalence and management of obesity within the Western healthcare cluster of Singapore using a novel AI-driven dashboard called Adipoview. A population-based cross-sectional study was conducted on a cohort of adult patients (≥ 18 years old) captured within the electronic health records (EHR) from 23 August 2023 to 2024. Deidentified patient-level data was derived from Adipoview, a dashboard that uses various data analytics and visualisation methods to display the obesity management landscape in real-time. Sociodemographic (i.e. age, sex, race) and clinical characteristics (i.e. obesity classification, obesity diagnosis, co-morbidities, and obesity treatment) were extracted. Our study analysed 313,369 patients with a mean age of 58.3 (17.1) years, with a female majority (53%). The most common co-morbid chronic diseases were hyperlipidaemia (40.0%), hypertension (36.7%), and diabetes (22.1%), where patients from primary care tended to be older with a higher prevalence of DHLs. Among patients meeting BMI-based criteria for excess adiposity, only 10.5% had a documented diagnosis. The proportion of patients meeting BMI criteria was slightly higher in primary compared to tertiary care (89.8% vs. 86.1%). Our prevalence number was expectedly larger than that derived from the National Population Health Survey (NPHS) (58.9%). Patients aged 18–74 years old with overweight and obesity were 18.1% and 56.9% respectively. Among patients referred to the Centre for Obesity Management and Surgery (COMS), 7,761 (68.9%) were adherent to follow-ups. The high prevalence of excess adiposity paired with its underdiagnosis as a chronic disease limits the potential to curb cardiometabolic implications of obesity. Greater efforts are needed to increase weight management awareness, refine obesity assessment measures, ensure proper diagnosis using clinical decision support aids, review existing weight-loss programme efficacies and promote screening of comorbidities through real-time visualisation tools such as Adipoview.

papers.title: Disclosure willingness anthropomorphism and thinking style shape perceived fit and comfort in AI mental health chatbot interactions
papers.authors: Feng Zhang, Yihui Chen, Mingyuan Liu, Jinyang Xu, Jinyang Xu, Junping Xu, Junping Xu
papers.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) conversational agents are increasingly used for everyday, non-clinical mental-health support, yet little is known about when these exchanges feel fitting and comfortable. We used a laboratory mixed-methods design to examine associations among perceived convenience of interaction (PCI), relational attitude (RA), willingness to self-disclose (WSD), anthropomorphism (AN), perceived fit/comfort (FC), and thinking style in 83 participants (43 rational-dominant; 40 experiential-dominant). WSD showed the strongest unique association with FC. A post hoc reverse model also found a unique FC-WSD association, leaving their temporal order unresolved. AN had no stable direct association with FC, but the WSD-FC association became stronger as AN increased. Group comparisons and continuous Rational-Experiential Inventory (REI) analyses converged: relatively stronger experiential processing was associated with higher AN, whereas relatively stronger rational processing was associated with higher WSD. The group-blind thematic analysis linked disclosure decisions to privacy, control, social distance, functional usefulness, and affective comfort. Together, the findings identify WSD as a key correlate of FC and show that anthropomorphism conditions this association rather than simply improving the interaction. Clear boundaries, controllability, and adjustable relational cues therefore warrant attention in future design research.

papers.title: Performance of five large language models in frozen shoulder patient education: a multidimensional evaluation of readability, quality, clinical alignment, and safety
papers.authors: Jiachen Liang, Wanying Gui, Huanan Li
papers.abstract: Abstract This study compared the educational suitability, overall quality, translation-based readability, clinical intent alignment, and safety of frozen shoulder patient education materials generated by GPT-5, DeepSeek, Doubao, Wenxin Yiyan, and Tongyi Qianwen. Twenty clinician-curated questions covering five content categories were submitted once to each model, producing 100 first-pass responses. C-PEMAT and GQS assessed educational quality, seven English readability formulas were applied to consensus translations of the Chinese outputs, and two preliminary clinician-developed measures assessed clinical key-point coverage and safety-related caution. C-PEMAT and GQS differed significantly among models (both P < 0.001), with GPT-5 obtaining the highest scores, followed by DeepSeek and Doubao. Quality scores did not differ significantly across content categories, whereas all readability indices did. C-PEMAT and GQS were moderately correlated ( r = 0.68), but quality measures were weakly associated with most readability indices. GPT-5 and DeepSeek showed relatively favorable Clinical Intent Alignment scores, while GPT-5 had the highest descriptive Clinical Safety Score. These findings are specific to the tested access date, platforms, prompts, and model versions. LLM-generated materials may serve as auxiliary drafts, but clinician review remains necessary for medical accuracy, safety, readability, and patient-specific appropriateness.

papers.title: When artificial intelligence apologizes: Dynamic trust updating and the role of personality.
papers.authors: Jit Wei Aaron Ang, Chenye Zhong, Syaheed B. Jabar, Georgios Christopoulos
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are susceptible to error, and many are designed to apologize.Yet, it remains unclear which apologies restore user trust, a question requiring repeated interactions with an AI agent and models capturing how trust evolves across encounters.Drawing on models of apology from human-human interaction research, we examined whether apology components that repair interpersonal trust function similarly in AI.Participants (N = 245) solved five business problems with a chatbot preprogrammed to err in two tasks at fixed intervals.They were randomly assigned to one of seven conditions: error with no apology or error followed by one of six apology strategies (Expression of Regret, Explanation, Acknowledgment of Responsibility, Declaration of Repentance, Offer of Repair, Request for Forgiveness).Using a dynamic trust-updating model, we estimated how trust shifted after each trial, following errors versus correct performance.Trust trajectories differed significantly by apology condition.Relative to no apology, only Expression of Regret buffered the typical immediate decline in trust following the errorapology-correction sequence.None of the apology conditions further enhanced trust recovery once the system resumed correct performance.Larger apology-related reductions in trust loss occurred among participants with more relational, relative to functional, postinteraction evaluation profiles.In separate bivariate analyses, all five Big Five traits were associated with baseline trust.When considered jointly, only Agreeableness and Openness remained associated with baseline trust, and Openness was also linked to dynamic trust updating.These findings suggest that apology-based trust repair in AI is selective and context-dependent.

papers.title: How port governance shapes living labs for energy transitions
papers.authors: Sonia Yeh, Christopher Dirzka, Aleksander A. Kondratenko, Frans Libertson, Bénédicte Madon, Veronika Slakaityte
papers.abstract: Ports are increasingly central to decarbonisation, energy-system integration, and resilience, yet less is known about how port governance shapes experimentation and whether learning becomes embedded in organisational practice. Living Labs (LLs)—organised forms of multi-actor experimentation in real-life settings—offer a promising approach, but are often treated as governance-neutral. This study develops and applies a governance–LL fit framework linking governance conditions to four LL pillars: co-creation, real-life setting, iterative learning, and institutional embedding. We compare two Nordic ports that are both wholly municipally owned companies but differ in their dominant governance configurations and in asset control, operational responsibilities, and decision authority: the Port of Aalborg (Denmark) and the Port of Trelleborg (Sweden). The analysis draws on capacity-building workshops, stakeholder engagement materials, and project documentation, using a proposed energy community in Aalborg and a Green Corridor in Trelleborg as case anchors. The comparison shows that prospective uptake pathways reflect both governance conditions and the scope of the initiative. Aalborg’s intra-port energy community could draw on contractual, procurement, and partnership interfaces within the port ecosystem, whereas Trelleborg’s corridor-level initiative would require coordination and commitment across several autonomous organisations and jurisdictions. Across the cases, the analysis indicates that institutional uptake depends on aligning stakeholders, decision authority, and available organisational instruments with the scope of the transition challenge. Because the evidence captures early-stage LL development rather than completed pilots, the findings concern prospective pathways rather than demonstrated long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Understanding students’ Generative AI use in higher education: A SEM-ANN analysis of AI attributes, behavioral reasons, and perceived learning performance
papers.authors: Mohammed Abdullah Al-Sharafi, Mostafa Al‐Emran, Shahla Asadi, Noor Al-Qaysi, Nazrita Ibrahim, Omid Ameri Sianaki
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can support personalized educational experiences. However, limited understanding remains of how AI-specific human-like attributes and behavioral reasoning mechanisms jointly relate to students’ attitudes, self-reported Generative AI use, and perceived learning performance. To address this gap, this research integrates Behavioral Reasoning Theory (BRT) with key AI characteristics (perceived anthropomorphism, animacy, and intelligence) to examine students’ attitudes towards Generative AI and their association with perceived learning performance. Data were collected from 395 students who reported using Generative AI tools for academic activities. The study examined Generative AI broadly rather than a specific platform. Data were analyzed using a hybrid Structural Equation Modeling-Artificial Neural Network (SEM-ANN) approach. The results indicated that perceived anthropomorphism, animacy, intelligence, and reasons for adoption were positively associated with students’ attitudes, whereas reasons against adoption were not significantly associated with attitude. Self-reported Generative AI use was positively associated with students’ perceived learning performance. The ANN analysis ranked reasons for adoption as the most important predictor of students’ attitudes, with a normalized importance of 97.78%. The model explained 64.7% of the variance in students’ attitudes, 48% in self-reported Generative AI use, and 24.9% in perceived learning performance. This study contributes theoretically by extending conventional technology adoption research through integrating behavioral reasoning and AI-specific perception factors within the educational context.

papers.title: Shadow AI in organizations: A distribution-based financial risk analysis for governance and secure AI adoption
papers.authors: Hind Albasry, Estela Carmona-Cejudo, Enver Delic, Robert Muster
papers.abstract: Shadow artificial intelligence (AI), referring to the unapproved use of AI tools within organizations, is emerging as a governance challenge that extends beyond traditional shadow information technology (IT) by introducing cybersecurity, compliance, and financial risks. As generative AI tools become increasingly accessible in work environments, employees may use such systems outside formal organizational controls, creating hidden exposure pathways that are difficult to monitor and manage. This study proposes the SAIR (Shadow AI Risk) model, a quantitative risk assessment framework that builds on established information risk analysis principles to examine the financial consequences of Shadow AI usage. The framework distinguishes between primary financial losses, representing direct damages, and secondary financial losses, capturing consequential impacts such as reputational harm and regulatory effects. Scenario-based Monte Carlo simulation is employed to capture uncertainty and estimate financial loss distributions. The findings show that Shadow AI financial risk is shaped jointly by behavioral exposure, threat capability, organizational resistance, and the potential for secondary-loss escalation. Stronger organizational resistance substantially reduces successful loss event frequency, whereas increased exposure and threat capability amplify financial consequences. The additional analyses further demonstrate that financial risk estimates are sensitive not only to expected parameter values but also to the underlying distributional assumptions, particularly in the upper tail. They also show that the magnitude of financial loss and the concentration of losses provide complementary perspectives on organizational risk. Finally, the proposed organizational self-assessment approach provides a practical pathway for adapting SAIR to organization-specific conditions and available operational evidence. By quantifying parameter sensitivities and distributional behavior, the SAIR framework enables organizations to assess Shadow AI financial risk in a structured manner and supports evidence-based prioritization of mitigation strategies. Overall, the study provides a distribution-aware foundation for managing AI-related organizational risk and supports more secure, accountable, and resilient AI adoption.

papers.title: Global trends and emerging themes in GIS education: A literature review with a case study of Uzbekistan
papers.authors: Dilshoda Norboeva, Khojiakbar Khasanov, Jasur Lapasov, Bekzod Inamov, Safayev Sanjarbek Zafarbek o‘g‘li, Fayzali Safarov, Gulmurodov Farrux Eshmurodovich, Nurali Umarov, Otabek YUSUPJONOV
papers.abstract: This paper provides an overview of global GIS education and evaluates geospatial education in Uzbekistan on a regional level. An integrated approach based on combining bibliometric analysis and thematic interpretation was used to explore 325 articles listed in Scopus and Web of Science databases between 2016 and 2025. Bibliometric science mapping, thematic analysis, K-means clustering and case study evaluation were used as the methodology in order to analyze the development trends in GIS education. Based on the research, GIS education is experiencing considerable expansion starting from 2022 due to the inclusion of WebGIS, AI applications, cloud learning systems, and digitalization.
