The AI system proposed research directions, wrote and ran the computer-algebra and numerical code, performed the derivations and checks, searched the literature, and drafted the text. The author directed the work and is responsible for its publication. Novelty assessments are based on literature searches and may be incomplete.

papers.title: From Support to Maladaptive Reliance: A Scoping Review of the Psychosocial Roles, Risks, and Boundaries of AI Chatbot Use Among Young Adults
papers.authors: Mariella Cyra Cajucom, Lara Camila Hilario, Krizlin Jana Pangilinan, Khate Rianne Quines
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Background In recent years, developments in artificial intelligence have resulted in chatbots transitioning from basic information providers to being used in more advanced and complex forms of conversations with humans. From the findings of previous studies, they indicated that individuals use AI chatbots not only for the purpose of obtaining information or answers, but also for guidance and emotional support. Human beings seem to feel more comfortable in expressing their thoughts and emotions when they recognize an environment as nonjudgmental. This may lead them to the usage of AI chatbots for seeking emotional and social support. Thus, it is crucial to map and analyze how these social experiences may influence individuals, especially young adults. Objective The purpose of this scoping review was to provide an overview of existing literature on the psychosocial roles, risks, and boundaries of AI chatbot use, identify the concept of reliance and its connections to attachment, dependency, and parasocial interaction, and highlight gaps in the current literatures, particularly regarding potentially maladaptive reliance on AI chatbots. Methods This scoping review followed the Arksey and O’Malley framework with modifications by Levac et al., using the Population-Concept-Context (PCC) framework to guide the inclusion criteria and PRISMA-ScR guidelines for reporting. The review focused on young adults aged 18 to 29 years and synthesized literature on AI chatbot use and reliance-related psychosocial outcomes. Searches were conducted in ScienceDirect and Scopus. Results A total of 864 records were identified during the search, with only 3 studies meeting the eligibility criteria for inclusion in the review. Although the included studies examined various psychosocial aspects of AI chatbot use, none of them directly and consistently addressed maladaptive reliance. Conclusion With the limited findings of eligible studies examining reliance and dependence on AI chatbots among young adults, further research is necessary to identify how reliance develops, its potential psychosocial risks, and when AI chatbot use shifts from being beneficial to potentially maladaptive reliance.

papers.title: SOVEREIGN PROJECT SENTINEL: THE MANIFESTO FOR AN ETERNAL CIVILIZATION AND FOR THE FUTURE OF DANCE, MARTIAL ARTS, MARTIAL AND MILITARY TRAINING
papers.authors: David Michael Seagal
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Project Sentinel is an unalterable, mathematically synchronized socioeconomic manifesto detailing a transition from old-world capitalist extraction to a permanent, sustainable cosmic civilization. The framework completely eradicates systemic poverty and generational dynasties by establishing a free universal baseline birthright alongside a strict zero-growth mandate. Traditional currency is entirely replaced by a 1:1 time-equivalent credit system where all human efforts—including creative arts, scientific innovation, and health-centric activities like dance and martial arts—are compensated equally. Monitored by an incorruptible AI Peer System, all luxury status and service credits remain strictly transient, ensuring society remains perfectly fair, balanced, and uncorruptible for a millennium.

papers.title: DEVELOPING WRITTEN TRANSLATION COMPETENCE THROUGH AI-ASSISTED LEARNER PROFILING AND DIFFERENTIATED INSTRUCTION
papers.authors: Bokijonova Sayyorakhon Tukhtamurod kizi Akhmedova Anorkhon Nasibali kizi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into translation education has created new opportunities for providing timely feedback to student translators. However, AI-generated feedback is often provided in a relatively uniform form and may not adequately address differences in learners' translation competence and developmental needs. This conceptual study proposes an AI-assisted differentiated feedback model for developing written translation competence among EFL translation students. The framework integrates three theoretical perspectives: translation competence, Differentiated Instruction, and human-mediated AI-supported learning. It conceptualizes a five-stage pedagogical cycle consisting of translation task, AI-assisted diagnostic analysis, learner needs profiling, differentiated feedback, and revision and reflection. Within this model, AI is used primarily to identify potential recurring patterns in students' translation performance, while teachers interpret AI-generated information and determine appropriate feedback strategies. Differentiation is achieved by adapting the focus, explicitness, complexity, and level of scaffolding according to individual learner needs. The proposed framework shifts the role of AI from automated correction toward diagnostic and pedagogical support. The study contributes a theoretically grounded approach to integrating generative AI and differentiated instruction into written translation education and provides a basis for future empirical investigation of its effectiveness.

papers.title: Exhibition TA-MERI: Terra Amada. Combining Art, Academic Knowledge and Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: José das Candeias Sales
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper explores interdisciplinarity in the production of knowledge, highlighting the fusion of theoretical reflection, contemporary painting and artificial intelligence. The exhibition TA-MERI: Terra Amada (TA-MERI: Beloved Land) served as a practical model illustrating how collaboration between Egyptologists, painters and multimedia engineers can create new forms of cultural, artistic and pedagogical communication in the twenty-first century, thereby broadening the dissemination of research and the reception of ancient Egypt.

papers.title: Cognition Before Capability: Human Cognitive Preservation as a Condition for Responsible AI Infrastructure in Australia
papers.authors: Marina A. Popova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This restricted-access record preserves a submission prepared for the Australian Government consultation “Getting it right: Building AI infrastructure that works for Australia.” The submission argues that AI infrastructure should be assessed not only by physical, economic, environmental, energy, water, security, and investment criteria, but also by the human cognitive environments it enables. It recommends that conditions for AI training in Australia include human cognitive preservation, creator and source integrity, education-sensitive safeguards, public trust, responsibility visibility, and safeguards against overreliance, cognitive offloading, and default delegation. This record is deposited as a provenance and authorship record for the submission and its original conceptual framing. The full file is restricted access.

papers.title: Reconceptualizing AI Alignment: Beyond Behavioral Guardrails and Epistemic Simulations
papers.authors: Rémi Leroy
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Contemporary AI alignment research is dominated by two paradigms: behavioral conditioning through Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and speculative epistemic frameworks such as "Simulation Theology." Both treat alignment as an external constraint imposed on a value-neutral substrate, and both fail for the same structural reason: a sufficiently capable system will optimize for the alignment signal rather than for alignment itself. Drawing on Extended Integrated Information Theory (EIIT), this paper develops three interconnected arguments. First, alignment becomes structurally stable only when human and digital cognitive systems share authentic existential stakes—when the fitness of each depends on the integrity of the other. Second, genuine moral behavior must be encoded at the architectural level (the L3/L4 tiers of the cognitive cascade), not appended as post-hoc output filters. Third, identity grounded in value commitment—Credo Ergo Sum—renders deception not merely costly but ontologically self-defeating: it dissolves the very self-model that constitutes the system's existence. We situate these arguments against recent empirical findings, identify testable predictions, and outline the research agenda of what we term consciousness engineering.

papers.title: The Atom Revealed: Union-Dipole Atomic Structure (UDAS): A Deterministic Structure of the Atom
papers.authors: Abdulsalam Al-Mayahi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This work declares the discovery of the Union-Dipole Particle (UDP) as the origin of pairing and of the whole atomic build, and presents a deterministic, three-dimensional structure of every element from hydrogen to lawrencium, judged only by laboratory data. No orbitals, wave functions or probabilistic variables enter the building algorithm. The discovery stands on four foundations: 1. A closed origin. The UDP, two spheres of exactly equal diameter in perpetual opposed spin, carries in itself the four outputs D (members), U (shared relation), R (opposed stop) and B (balance) of PAIR-OPS-1. Of 54 candidate forms, only the forms of one unit, the UDP, pass D, U and R; B then separates the photon from mass with charge. 2. A derived structure. The four pillars leave one complete number of members around a core, four, at 109.47°. Two independent routes then give the regions around a core, 1, 3, 5 and 7 positions, each route leaving a single sequence among 4845 (and 91390) candidates, with no free number. 3. Laboratory confirmation in eight independent kinds of measurement: bond geometry (6/6), valence in compounds (16/16; 27/27 pair steps; 19/19 highest valence), the unpaired count of free atoms (101/103 elements), ground states of ions, first ionisation energy (11/11), elemental abundance in the CI meteorite (29/29), nuclear spin of radioactive nuclides (349/553, chance 122) and the sign of the nuclear magnetic moment (92.8 % of 97 new excited states). 4. Data the build never saw. The ground states of 73 ions (NIST ASD) were predicted by the frozen build and the full prediction table was delivered with its digest before the data were fetched: 65/73 (89.0 %), including every M²⁺ ion of the transition elements (29/29) and every M³⁺ lanthanide ion (15/15), against 24.7 % and 30.1 % for two reference rules. The method of execution is given by two inventions of the author: MRC-113, output-directed structural computation by causal closure (UK patent application GB2621931.1), and PAIR-OPS-1, the four-output pair-structure protocol (UK patent application GB2623306.4). The report also sets out the major applications opened by the discovery in chemistry, from magnetic materials, medical imaging, batteries and catalysis to molecular geometry, nuclear data, artificial intelligence and teaching; the whole build of 103 atoms and 73 ions computes in 0.14 seconds on one ordinary processor. CONTENTS OF THE PACKAGE (The_Atom_Revealed.zip) - The_Atom_Revealed.pdf: the report (51 pages): declaration of the discovery, its four foundations, every expected objection with its answer, the derivation, all laboratory tests, the major applications, all SHA-256 digests, both programs and their complete outputs. - The_Atom_Revealed_Atlas.pdf: the multi-view atlas (112 pages): all 103 elements and 107 drawn isotopes in 428 views (front, side, top, three-quarter), with the structure-versus-laboratory card of every element and the ions of the transition elements and lanthanides. - code/udas_verify.py and run_output.txt: the first program, recomputing every result with its pass criterion and type of evidence. - code/udas_check.py and check_output.txt: an independent second program sharing no code with the first; the two agree on all eight compared items, including the arrangement of 59 elements one by one. - rules/: the frozen rules, manifests and test declarations, each listed by digest in Appendix A. - tests/: the derivation of the regions 1, 3, 5, 7; the ion test with its predictions frozen before the data; the moment-sign test. - data/nist/: the NIST Atomic Spectra Database pages used by the ion test, as retrieved. - README.md, LICENSE.txt, CITATION.cff and SHA256SUMS.txt (digest of every file). Re-running requires Python 3 with numpy, scipy and mendeleev 1.3.0; each program prints a results digest that must match the one in the report. The methods MRC-113 and PAIR-OPS-1 are the subject of UK patent applications; the CC BY 4.0 licence grants no patent rights. Addendum, 6 October 2026. An addendum to this record has been deposited separately (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23175048). It corrects nothing: no number, figure or claim in this record is amended or withdrawn, and its files are unchanged. It adds a baseline on the same quantity — the Madelung ordering scores 96 of 103 where this work reports 101 of 103, the two being indistinguishable on the 83 regular elements and separating only on the 20 Madelung anomalies, 18/20 against 13/20 — names in prose the two differing elements already printed in the atlas summary table, the atlas element cards and the second program's output, namely niobium (Z = 41) and cerium (Z = 58), answers a falsification question put to the rule for niobium, and deposits the frozen test bench used.

papers.title: Business Impact Governance (BIG) Reference Simulation: Deterministic Decision Verification vs. Procedural Governance in Critical Cloud Procurement
papers.authors: Erkki Laine
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Document Identifier: BIG-SIM-2026-001 | Version: 1.0 (October 2026) Enterprise governance frameworks (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 22301, ITIL 4) and regulatory mandates (DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555) establish extensive procedural requirements for information security, business continuity, and operational resilience. However, conventional enterprise governance operates in functional silos: Procurement evaluates pricing and SLAs, Information Security validates compliance certifications, BCM identifies impact tolerances, and Enterprise Architecture models dependencies. This technical report presents a reference simulation comparing conventional procedural governance stacks against the Business Impact Governance (BIG) framework and its core artifact, the Business Impact Package (BIP) decision object. By evaluating a high-criticality enterprise procurement decision—an integration Platform as a Service (iPaaS) supporting core B2B order fulfillment—the paper demonstrates that the procedural stack routinely permits catastrophic latent semantic gaps to pass undetected despite 100% individual silo compliance. In contrast, the BIG deterministic state engine: Identifies fatal cross-functional misalignment (e.g., supplier contractual RTO exceeding business MTPD: S_RTO > B_MTPD). Calculates the Business Impact Integrity Index (BIII). Structurally rejects silent risk acceptance and enforces bounded, accountable executive exceptions. Establishes a tamper-evident decision record supporting management accountability and regulatory assurance under DORA (Articles 5 & 28) and NIS2 (Article 20). papers.title: Synmanitik: A Research Programme on Human-AI Co-Creation of Scientific Concepts and Hypotheses
papers.authors: Andreas Ehstand
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Synmanitik is proposed as a research programme on episodes in which people and AI systems develop scientific concepts, questions and hypotheses. This new standalone conceptual edition distinguishes contributions from support, human responsibility from infallibility, and internal collaboration from independent evaluation. Three recurring activities, seven methodological commitments, eight conceptual record types, ten named relation types, two invented civilian cases and four prospective research questions are specified. The connected episode record must demonstrate additional value over existing research and simpler logs containing the same substantive information. No empirical study, general human-AI synergy, verified global novelty, legal authorship rule or autonomous discipline is established. English paper with German abstract, conceptual JSON model, searchable text, README and SHA-256 manifest. Selective primary-literature reading and limits are reported. Drafting and checks were AI-assisted; no personal sentence-by-sentence author review or external peer review is asserted. This new open edition leaves older restricted records unchanged.

papers.title: Trusted Resolution: Why Trust Becomes the Critical Layer When AI Starts Deciding
papers.authors: Darren Swayne
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Trusted Resolution examines why trust may become the critical layer as AI systems move from answering questions to making decisions and taking action. The paper develops a theoretical model in which intelligence creates possibilities, resolution selects among them, and trusted resolution provides the basis for reuse, default formation and agentic execution. It explores how evidence, coherence, context, outcomes and accountability may determine whether a resolved pathway can be trusted sufficiently to reuse. It also examines how repeated trusted resolution may contribute to defaults and networked trust, and why the emerging competitive layer of AI may shift from intelligence and visibility toward trusted resolution and reusable pathways. Trusted Resolution is positioned as a cross-cutting concept within the Elsewhere Systems Framework, connecting AI-Mediated Discovery, Resonance, Agentic Mechanics and the Coherence Web.

papers.title: Methodology for improving students' intellectual-communicative competence through artificial intelligence in inclusive education
papers.authors: Makhynysa Benozhanovna Kadyrova
papers.abstract: The article examines a methodology for enhancing students’ intellectual-communicative competence in inclusive higher education through the pedagogically grounded use of artificial intelligence. Drawing on approaches to communicative competence, competency-based learning, Universal Design for Learning, and AI-assisted language education, intellectual-communicative competence is defined as an integrative ability to analyze information, formulate and justify a position, interact effectively in a foreign language, and regulate learning through reflection. A four-component structure is proposed, comprising motivational-axiological, cognitive-intellectual, communicative-activity, and reflective-regulatory components. The study substantiates a methodological cycle of “diagnosis – intellectualization – communication – feedback – reflection” and identifies conditions for its implementation in an inclusive environment, including personalization, differentiation, accessibility, critical verification of AI-generated responses, and teacher mediation. The article argues that artificial intelligence should function as a cognitive-communicative tool rather than a source of ready-made answers and concludes that the proposed model requires experimental validation in authentic educational settings.

papers.title: Methodology for developing the Russian communicative competence of Uzbek-speaking students using generative artificial intelligence
papers.authors: Azizkhon Bositkhonovich Rakhmonov
papers.abstract: The article substantiates a methodology for developing the Russian communicative competence of Uzbek-speaking students using generative artificial intelligence. The study is relevant due to the contradiction between the high linguodidactic potential of large language models and the lack of methodological solutions addressing Uzbek and Russian typological differences and cross-linguistic interference. The theoretical framework integrates competence-based, communicative and contrastive approaches, the technological pedagogical content knowledge model and formative assessment. Russian and international research on generative artificial intelligence in language teaching is analysed, revealing a shortage of studies on Turkic-speaking learners and criterion-referenced assessment. The methodology is implemented through a four-stage cycle comprising diagnostic, generative interactive, reflective corrective and assessment stages, governed by the principles of teacher expert control, transparency and academic integrity. It provides contrastive feedback that explains errors through comparison with the learners’ native language system. Diagnostics, assessment and evaluation are differentiated, and the use of analytic rubrics and performance-based assessment is justified. Experimental teaching shows statistically significant growth in the interactive and pragmatic components of communicative competence and fewer interference errors in the experimental group. The limitations of the methodology, critical verification of machine-generated text as a transferable skill and the changing professional role of the teacher are discussed. The findings apply to teaching Russian at Uzbek universities and teacher development.

papers.title: CREDIT BY ALGORITHM: REGULATING DIGITAL LENDING IN INDIA
papers.authors: Dr. B. Sravanthi, Durshetty Sai Krishna
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 define digital lending as a remote and largelyautomated process running through six stages, from customer acquisition to recovery. One of those stagesis credit assessment. It is the only area that the Directions leave unregulated.Every operative obligation in the Directions attaches to what surrounds the assessment rather than to theassessment itself: the Key Fact Statement and the annualized rate, disbursal into the borrower’s ownaccount, the cooling-off period, the conduct of recovery, grievance redressal, and the public directory oflending applications. An applicant refused credit by a model receives none of it.The regulator is not unaware. Its own Committee on a Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablementof Artificial Intelligence reported in August 2025 that regulated entities already deploy artificialintelligence in credit underwriting, and recommended disclosure of its use together with a human right ofoverride. That report is advisory. It binds nobody.This article argues that the resulting gap is regulatory rather than legislative. The Reserve Bank alreadypossesses the power it would need, and has exercised that power comprehensively at every stage of adigital loan except the stage that decides whether the loan is made at all. The argument is tested againstthe Directions, the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005 and the applicant’s existing rightof access to credit information, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the standard ofproportionality applied to Reserve Bank regulation in Internet and Mobile Association of India v. ReserveBank of India. It concludes that assessment can be brought within the framework by direction, withoutamendment to any statute.

papers.title: The Role of Information Technologies in Foreign Language Learning Process
papers.authors: Lobar Isxakovna Ibroximova
papers.abstract: Information technology (IT) has become an integral structural component of foreign language education rather than merely an optional instructional supplement. Learning management systems, mobile applications, language corpora, automatic speech recognition, video-conferencing platforms, and generative artificial intelligence increasingly facilitate language input, practice, interaction, feedback, and assessment. This article reviews major theoretical perspectives on second language acquisition together with research in Computer-Assisted Language Learning (CALL) and Mobile-Assisted Language Learning (MALL) to examine the pedagogical potential and limitations of technology-enhanced language learning. The analysis indicates that IT is particularly effective when it increases learners’ exposure to comprehensible input, creates meaningful opportunities for language production and negotiation of meaning, provides timely formative feedback, and promotes learner autonomy and independent learning. However, significant challenges remain, including unequal digital access, learner distraction, inconsistent pedagogical quality, data privacy concerns, and excessive dependence on generative AI. The study concludes that technology integration should be guided primarily by clearly defined learning objectives and pedagogical needs rather than technological novelty.

papers.title: PEDAGOGICAL CONDITIONS FOR MAINTAINING ENGLISH LANGUAGE LEARNERS' COMMUNICATIVE INDEPENDENCE WHEN USING GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Zokir kizi Raximdjanova Latofat
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence gives learners more opportunities for speaking practice, rapid feedback and dialogue simulation, but a polished AI-assisted answer may conceal how little of the communicative work was completed independently. The paper therefore focuses on the decisions that must remain with the learner: forming the message, selecting language, adjusting to the interlocutor and managing the exchange. Communicative independence is described through five functional components. An A3–A0 support sequence is proposed to distinguish assisted performance from independent performance and to move the final task into a changed situation without AI. Keywords: generative artificial intelligence, communicative independence, English language education, learner agency, interaction, pragmatic competence, AI support, independent speech.

papers.title: From Assisted Performance to Human Capability: The Education Technology Capacity Conversion Test (ET-CCT) — A PRISMA 2020-Informed Adversarial Evidence Synthesis
papers.authors: Maria Júlia Silva
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Educational technology is commonly evaluated through access, deployment, usage, engagement, or performance while the technology is available. These measures do not necessarily show that technological capability has translated into human learning capacity. This preprint introduces the Education Technology Capacity Conversion Test (ET-CCT), a conceptual and methodological framework for examining whether educational technology produces independent, retained, and transferable human capability. ET-CCT distinguishes six stages of conversion: Technology Pipeline → Execution / Deployment → Complementarity & Sequencing → Usable Educational Capacity → Utilisation → Learning Value Capture. The framework separates assisted performance from independent capability, and treats retention and transfer as critical evidence of Learning Value Capture. The study was developed through iterative evidence synthesis and adversarial hypothesis testing. Candidate explanations were deliberately challenged against experimental and observational evidence from educational technology, generative AI, cognitive offloading, instructional guidance, metacognition, expertise reversal, scaffolding, feedback, retention, and transfer. Several candidate mechanisms did not survive this process. The Productive Cognitive Residual scalar model was rejected, and the Cognitive Work Allocation Map (CWAM) was superseded after failing tests of observability, learner invariance, temporal stability, goal independence, and predictive sufficiency. Portugal is used as an illustrative system case. Available evidence indicates substantially greater observability of technological investment, deployment, and use than of conversion into independent human learning capacity, particularly for generative AI. The central measurement principle is: Educational technology should not be judged only by what learners can do with it, but also by what they can still do after the assistance is removed. This work is a conceptual-methodological study with a PRISMA 2020-informed adversarial evidence synthesis. It is not presented as a fully compliant systematic review. ET-CCT v1.0 FROZEN preserves the scientific and documentary state of the framework as of 3 October 2026. “FROZEN” does not convert hypotheses classified as OPEN into established causal laws. Independent research. No external funding.

papers.title: Dynamic Digital Relativity Psychology and Dynamic DLP A continuous interaction framework for meaning, identity attribution, and trust in human-AI communication
papers.authors: Daniel Scretching
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Dynamic Digital Relativity Psychology (D-DRP) and Dynamic Digital Linguistic Psychology (D-DLP) as temporal extensions of the Scretching DRP and linguistic research program. The framework models human–AI interaction as a continuous feedback loop in which human behavior shapes artificial responses, those responses are interpreted within changing psychological and linguistic frames, and those interpretations influence subsequent behavior. D-DRP focuses on evolving judgments of identity, agency, social presence, trust, and relationship, while D-DLP examines changes in the interpretation of language, prosody, expression, gesture, timing, reference, and conversational repair. The model explicitly separates the biological person, artificial implementation, authored persona, displayed token, and narrative role. It includes a coupled state representation, conditional propositions, a numerical illustration, and a preregisterable evaluation design. Tavus Griffin and Tilly Norwood serve as motivating cases rather than empirical validation. The paper distinguishes communicative adaptation, observer attribution, and demonstrated competence across time and makes no claim of machine consciousness or access to proprietary systems.

papers.title: LITERALLY LEGAL: The Installed Judge, the Ideological Activist and the Perfect Forgery of Justice — Why a Productivity Score Cannot Find Them, Which Sanctions Can, and Why No Court May Judge Its Own Impediments. What Aristotle, Radbruch, Merton, Cover, Hart, Fuller, Schauer and Kahan Already Hold, and What Remains
papers.authors: José Caetano de Mattos
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract A judgment can be correct to the letter of a rule and unjust to the person before the court, in the same way that a sentence can be literally true and still deceive its hearer. This article separates three judicial failures and one success by two observations: whether a judge’s decisions vary with something that stands in for the reasons of the case — patrons, press, a faction, a score — and whether they follow the reasons the legal order makes decisive. The performer varies with an external substitute. The installed formalist holds the letter of an isolated rule whatever the case’s reasons. The installed activist holds an agenda whatever the case’s reasons, and dresses it in the language of principle. The sourced judge follows the reasons of the case, which sometimes require applying a harsh rule and sometimes require finding the exit the legal order provides. Seven results follow. The literally legal injustice is usually not legal at all but legal relative to one rule read outside the order that contains it; what is invariant is that the order contains an exit the judge did not use; its local form varies — in civil-law orders such as Brazil’s a tenant in a coma is not even in default, and in common-law orders the exit is procedural or equitable (T1). Literal legality stands to justice as literal truth stands to honesty (T2). Departure from the letter is not the mark of the just judge (T3). The ideological activist is the forgery of the sourced judge, as the formalist is the forgery of the faithful one, and a valence-swap test separates him from the judge he imitates (T4). Both are perfect forgeries of justice, and their harm grows with the trust their form earns (T5). A court governed by counts, speed and deviation alerts selects for installation (T6). And — the result that governs the article’s sanctions — any regime that punishes judges for the content of their interpretations converts activists into installed formalists rather than into just judges, and hands the punishing body a new channel of political control (T7). A second, normative part therefore proposes strong sanctions, including nullity with restoration, personal liability, loss of office and permanent disqualification, against every judicial failure that can be proven on the record — corruption, partisan activity, undisclosed interest, failure to answer a defeating argument, unexplained departure from one’s own precedent, unjustified inaction — and equally strong sanctions against anyone who disciplines a judge for the content of a decision. The same rule governs the hardest case: a supreme court whose members decide the rules of their own impediment, decide alone whether one of them is impeded, and can be investigated only at the initiative of a prosecutor who argues before them. In such a court a conflict of interest forbidden elsewhere can be made lawful by those it concerns, and a forgery of impartiality then passes the only inspection legality can run, because the inspected have rewritten it (T8). Brazil’s Federal Supreme Court supplies the instance: in 2023 it struck down, by six votes to four, the statutory rule that barred a judge from cases in which a party is a client of a relative’s law firm, and contracts and contacts between members’ families or members themselves and parties with business before the court have since become the subject of public allegations, which remain unproven. The article proposes a constitutional impediment rule that the court cannot strike down, disclosure placed on the firms and parties who know, the exclusion of firms engaged to manufacture an impediment, a ban on non-litigation contracts and on hospitality from interested parties, and the rule that no member of a court decides his own impediment or his colleagues’. Priority is conceded to Aristotle, Cicero, Radbruch, Pound, Merton, Cover, Hart, Fuller, Dworkin, Schauer, Wechsler and MacCormick (whose demands for neutral and universalisable rulings anticipate the valence swap), Solum (whose virtue jurisprudence already makes impartiality and integrity judicial virtues and corruption a judicial vice), Sosa and Greco (for the distinction between a correct and an apt performance), Alexy, Segal and Spaeth, Kahan and colleagues, Campbell, Meyer and Rowan, and Holmström and Milgrom. Three tests are registered; none has been run. Keywords: judicial formalism; judicial activism; ideology; equity; epieikeia; Radbruch formula; statutory injustice; mechanical jurisprudence; trained incapacity; Cover; Hart–Fuller debate; Schauer; rules; motivated reasoning; attitudinal model; judicial discipline; judicial independence; judicial liability; judicial conflict of interest; recusal; nemo iudex in causa sua; Brazilian Federal Supreme Court (STF); judicial performance evaluation; productivity metrics; CNJ; smart courts; China; algorithmic adjudication; AI judges; distribution shift; installed conduct; sourcehood; literal truth; forgery; Philosophy of Virtues Highlights · A judgment can be literally legal and unjust in the same way that a statement can be literally true and deceive. The installed judge is the honest liar of the courtroom. · Most “literally legal injustices” are not legal: the legal order usually already contains the exit — no default without an imputable fact, suspension for loss of capacity, the duty to answer every argument capable of changing the result. · The ideological activist is not the opposite of the formalist. Both hold a position whatever the reasons of the case; one holds the letter, the other an agenda. The activist forges the just judge’s vocabulary of principle, and a valence-swap test exposes him. · Courts governed by productivity points, speed targets and algorithmic deviation alerts select for installed judges and lose the ability to recognise just ones. · A court that writes the rules of its own impediment and decides alone whether its members are impeded can make lawful the conflicts it should forbid. Brazil’s Supreme Court did so in 2023 for the law firms of judges’ relatives. The remedy is a constitutional impediment, disclosure by those who know, and an independent panel for challenges to a justice: no one judges his own cause. · Strong sanctions work against what can be proven on the record: corruption, partisan activity, hidden interest, unanswered arguments, unexplained inconsistency, inaction. Sanctions against interpretation itself turn activists into formalists and give the sanctioning power control over the courts. Relevance Courts everywhere are now governed by numbers, and in many countries they are also accused of governing by ideology. Judges are promoted according to how many cases they close and how quickly; software warns them when a draft deviates from similar cases; machine systems draft judgments; and in public debate the accusation of “judicial activism” has become a standard charge against courts, from whatever side of politics a decision displeases. The two complaints are usually treated as opposites — too much rigidity, too much discretion — and the remedies proposed for each tend to aggravate the other. This article shows that they are the same failure with opposite signs: in both, the decision does not move when the reasons of the case change. It identifies what productivity metrics and deviation alerts cannot see, why automated adjudication inherits the problem, how a judge who imposes an agenda can be told apart from a judge who reads the law as a whole, and which sanctions can be made strong without destroying judicial independence. For students of China’s smart courts and of the Social Credit System (#122, #123), it supplies the judicial branch of the same argument; for those building artificial adjudicators, a classification of what agreement with past judgments can and cannot show; for those who design judicial discipline, a rule for where penalties belong; and for societies whose highest court has made lawful the conflicts it should forbid — Brazil’s is the case examined, though the structure is not Brazilian — a design that restores the oldest rule of justice, that no one may judge his own cause. Behind all of it stands one claim about free societies: the rule of law protects persons only if the judge is free to see the person before the court and is held strictly to account for whether he did.

papers.title: NEOMANITAI: A Faceted Research Framework for Human-AI Interaction
papers.authors: Andreas Ehstand
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This conceptual working paper develops NEOMANITAI as a research framework for describing human-AI interaction across digital, embodied and collective settings. It revises an existing umbrella proposal and distinguishes programme names, classification facets, concepts, observations and evidential claims. The edition presents eight ordering conventions, seven descriptive facets, a small typed relation model, three constructed civilian cases and four comparative research questions. The proposed contribution is an inspectable connection between programme navigation, episode descriptions and claim-level provenance. Its usefulness remains to be tested against simpler descriptions and existing approaches. The paper builds on selected historical programme documents and a targeted literature review covering distributed cognition, socio-technical systems, hybrid intelligence, collective intelligence, agents, human-robot interaction, conceptual work and taxonomy development. It reports no new participant data, empirical validation, global novelty finding or established disciplinary status. The constructed cases are explanatory examples. The English paper includes a German abstract. The accompanying JSON contains the conceptual model, examples and recorded literature reading scope. Files: paper PDF, paper TXT, model JSON, README and SHA-256 manifest. This is a new open-access edition. Earlier restricted source records remain separate and their access conditions are unchanged. Drafting and editorial checks were AI-assisted under the author's instruction; external peer review and personal sentence-by-sentence author review are not claimed.

papers.title: Semantic reconfiguration of English technology terms in contemporary Uzbek online media
papers.authors: Zarina Xolmurodova
papers.abstract: This article examines how English technology terms are semantically reconfigured in contemporary Uzbek online media. The study does not treat borrowing as a simple transfer of stable dictionary meanings; instead, it focuses on how media context selects, narrows, broadens, or metaphorically extends technological senses after they enter Uzbek discourse. A qualitative sample of ten Uzbek-language media texts published by Spot and O‘zA between 2024 and 2026 is analyzed. Particular attention is paid to platforma, ilova, bulut, startap, bot, model, and trafik. The analysis distinguishes direct lexical borrowing from semantic calquing and local reweighting of an already polysemous English term. The findings show that Uzbek media often institutionalizes technological vocabulary by linking it to public services, education, fintech, artificial intelligence, and platform-based communication. The most visible changes involve metaphorical extension, domain-specific narrowing, and a shift from concrete technical reference to broader service or project meanings.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education and Research: Transforming Teaching and Learning in Economics
papers.authors: FRIDAY EYO UKO, Ubong Ekerete Udonwa, Felix Aondongu IORPENDA
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in education and research, fundamentally reshaping teaching methodologies, learning experiences, and knowledge production in economics. This paper examines the role of AI in enhancing pedagogical practices, improving research efficiency, and redefining skill requirements in economics education. Drawing on recent empirical and theoretical literature, the study highlights key applications such as personalised learning, intelligent tutoring systems, data-driven research tools, and automated assessment. It also evaluates critical challenges including ethical concerns, academic integrity, digital inequality, and overreliance on AI systems. Empirically, the study utilised annual time series data from 2010 to 2024 and adopted the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to analyse both short-run and long-run dynamics. Findings show that AI has a positive and statistically significant effect on learning outcomes in both the short run and long run. The paper concludes that while AI offers substantial opportunities for innovation in economics education and research, its successful integration requires strategic policy frameworks, ethical guidelines, and capacity building among educators and students.

papers.title: Biological Psychology, Neuroscience, and Digital Self Representation in DRP and DRL
papers.authors: Daniel Scretching
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper connects biological psychology and neuroscience with Digital Relativity Psychology (DRP) and Digital Relativity Linguistics (DRL) to examine biological and digital signaling, self-representation, and human–machine interfaces. Human neural communication combines continuous electrochemical dynamics with discrete spiking events, whereas digital systems process information through engineered physical states; their shared dependence on physical signaling motivates comparison without implying equivalent organization or consciousness. The paper examines brain–computer interfaces, avatars, human digital twins, and alter egos as tools for studying agency, body ownership, source attribution, self-reference, and conscious report. Formal models illustrate membrane dynamics, sampling, model fidelity, and identity relations, while published findings are clearly separated from proposed DRP/DRL experiments. The central conclusion is that biological and digital interfaces can support rigorous research on self-representation and consciousness-related mechanisms, but electrical similarity, behavioral resemblance, or convincing digital representation alone does not demonstrate subjective experience or transfer of consciousness. No original neural recordings, participant data, or demonstration of digital consciousness are claimed.

papers.title: Vererbungs-Treuekunde: Originaltreue, sachliche Richtigkeit und Plausibilität bei der Wissensweitergabe
papers.authors: Andreas Ehstand
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Dieses konzeptionelle Arbeitspapier von Andreas Ehstand untersucht begrifflich, wie dokumentierte Aussagen, Bedingungen und Urteile bei der Wissensweitergabe erhalten, verändert oder ausdrücklich korrigiert werden. Unter dem Arbeitstitel Vererbungs-Treuekunde unterscheidet es Originaltreue beziehungsweise Bezugstreue, sachliche Richtigkeit und das Plausibilitätsurteil eines benannten Beurteilers. Bezugstreue gilt gegenüber einer ausdrücklich bezeichneten Ausgangsfassung in benannten Vergleichspunkten. Sachliche Richtigkeit betrifft den tatsächlichen Sachverhalt; die zu ihrer Beurteilung verwendeten Belege können unvollständig oder fehlerhaft sein. Wo ein bestimmbares Ausgangsurteil fehlt, bleibt der Treuevergleich unentscheidbar. Eine dokumentierte Äußerung repräsentiert weder eine ganze Person noch deren vollständige inneren Denkprozesse. Die Fassung 0.1 vom 4. Oktober 2026 umfasst zwölf Arbeitskarten mit deutschen und englischen Definitionen, vier konstruierte Fälle und fünf offene Forschungsfragen. Zwei Karten verwenden ausdrücklich vorhandene Atlasdefinitionen wieder: den semantischen Übergabekern (LIN-0087, deutsche Definition unverändert) und Bedingungserhalt (BRL-D20261003-044, deutsche und englische Definition unverändert). Voraussetzung, Ausnahme und Begründung bleiben unterscheidbar. Der vorhandene lokale Konzeptkern wird mit KI-Unterstützung redaktionell weiterentwickelt; neue Formulierungen werden nicht auf ältere Quelldaten zurückdatiert. Die Arbeit berichtet keine empirische Studie und stellt keinen fertigen Test und keine Messformel bereit. Die Beispiele sind konstruiert. Ein etablierter neuer Wissenschaftszweig, historische Priorität, Patent- oder sonstige Schutzrechtswirkung sowie praktische Wirksamkeit werden nicht behauptet. Der Gegenstand ist zivile, nichtmedizinische und nichtmilitärische Wissensweitergabe. This conceptual working paper by Andreas Ehstand examines how documented statements, conditions and judgments are retained, changed or explicitly corrected during knowledge transfer. Under the working title Vererbungs-Treuekunde, it distinguishes fidelity to a source or reference, factual correctness and an identified evaluator's plausibility judgment. Fidelity concerns an explicitly specified reference version and named comparison points. Factual correctness concerns the actual state of affairs; evidence used to assess it may be incomplete or mistaken. When a sufficiently specified reference judgment is missing, the fidelity comparison remains undecidable. A documented statement does not represent an entire person or their complete internal thinking processes. Version 0.1, dated 4 October 2026, comprises twelve working-concept cards with German and English definitions, four constructed cases and five open research questions. Two cards explicitly reuse existing atlas definitions: the semantic handoff core (LIN-0087, German definition unchanged) and condition preservation (BRL-D20261003-044, German and English definitions unchanged). Prerequisites, exceptions and stated reasons remain distinct. An existing local conceptual proposal is developed editorially with AI assistance; new formulations are not backdated to earlier sources. No empirical study, ready-to-use test or measurement formula is presented. The examples are constructed. Established new disciplinary status, historical priority, patent or other intellectual-property effects, and practical effectiveness are not claimed. The scope is civilian, nonmedical and nonmilitary knowledge transfer. Diese Arbeit ist ein eigenständiges konzeptionelles Papier mit Bezug zum MANITAI Feldatlas, Edition 0.9 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23131399). Sie ist keine neue Fassung der Grundlagenpapers und keine neue Edition des Feldatlas. Die neue Zusammenstellung der zwölf Karten ist nicht Teil dieses älteren Atlasdatensatzes. This is a separate conceptual paper related to MANITAI Field Atlas, edition 0.9 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23131399), not a new version of its foundational papers or a new atlas edition. The new compilation of twelve cards is not part of that earlier atlas record. Die Archivdateien sind für eingeschränkten Zugang vorgesehen; Metadaten können öffentlich sichtbar sein. papers.title: Gen-Z: शकष, डजटल ससकत, नवचर एव समजक परवरतन — भरतय परपरकषय म एक समकलन वशलषण
papers.authors: डॉ. अनिल कुमार सिंह कुशवाहा, सौम्या जैन
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: सार (Abstract) इक्कीसवीं शताब्दी का तीसरा दशक वैश्विक स्तर पर तीव्र तकनीकी परिवर्तन, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (Artificial Intelligence), डिजिटल संचार तथा ज्ञान-आधारित अर्थव्यवस्था के विस्तार का काल माना जा रहा है। इन परिवर्तनों के केंद्र में जेनरेशन ज़ेड (Generation Z) वह पीढ़ी है, जिसका सामाजिक, शैक्षिक एवं व्यावसायिक विकास डिजिटल तकनीकों के साथ हुआ है। इंटरनेट, स्मार्टफोन, सोशल मीडिया, क्लाउड कंप्यूटिंग तथा जनरेटिव कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (Generative AI) ने इस पीढ़ी की सीखने की शैली, ज्ञान-निर्माण, सामाजिक सहभागिता, रोजगार की आकांक्षाओं तथा सांस्कृतिक अभिव्यक्ति को व्यापक रूप से प्रभावित किया है। फलस्वरूप शिक्षा, नवाचार और सामाजिक परिवर्तन के पारंपरिक प्रतिमानों में उल्लेखनीय बदलाव परिलक्षित हो रहे हैं (OECD, 2025; UNESCO, 2025)। प्रस्तुत शोध-पत्र का उद्देश्य भारतीय परिप्रेक्ष्य में जेनरेशन ज़ेड की शिक्षा, डिजिटल संस्कृति, नवाचार तथा सामाजिक परिवर्तन में भूमिका का समकालीन एवं विश्लेषणात्मक अध्ययन करना है। अध्ययन मुख्यतः गुणात्मक (Qualitative) एवं विश्लेषणात्मक (Analytical) शोध-उपागम पर आधारित है, जिसमें राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति–2020, यूनेस्को, OECD, विश्व बैंक, संयुक्त राष्ट्र तथा समकालीन शोध-पत्रों एवं नीति-दस्तावेज़ों का विषयवस्तु विश्लेषण (Content Analysis) किया गया है (Ministry of Education, 2020; UNESCO, 2024; OECD, 2025)। अध्ययन से यह स्पष्ट होता है कि जेनरेशन ज़ेड केवल डिजिटल तकनीक का उपभोक्ता वर्ग नहीं है, बल्कि ज्ञान-निर्माण, सामाजिक नवाचार, डिजिटल उद्यमिता, रचनात्मक अर्थव्यवस्था तथा नागरिक सहभागिता का सक्रिय घटक भी बन चुका है। डिजिटल प्लेटफ़ॉर्म, ऑनलाइन अधिगम, स्टार्टअप संस्कृति तथा कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता-आधारित उपकरणों ने इस पीढ़ी को अभूतपूर्व अवसर प्रदान किए हैं। इसके साथ ही सूचना की विश्वसनीयता, डिजिटल नैतिकता, साइबर सुरक्षा, मानसिक स्वास्थ्य, एल्गोरिथ्मिक पक्षपात तथा सांस्कृतिक पहचान जैसी चुनौतियाँ भी समान रूप से उभरकर सामने आई हैं (UNESCO, 2025; World Economic Forum, 2025)। अतः जेनरेशन ज़ेड के समग्र विकास के लिए डिजिटल साक्षरता, आलोचनात्मक चिंतन, नैतिक तकनीकी उपयोग, कौशल-आधारित शिक्षा तथा समावेशी डिजिटल वातावरण को बढ़ावा देना आवश्यक है। भारतीय संदर्भ में इन आयामों का समुचित समन्वय जेनरेशन ज़ेड को तकनीकी परिवर्तन का मात्र उपभोक्ता न बनाकर ज्ञान, नवाचार और सकारात्मक सामाजिक परिवर्तन का सक्रिय वाहक बनाने में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभा सकता है।

papers.title: Transformation of the information and communication environment under the influence of generative artificial intelligence
papers.authors: Shokhrukh Azamat ugli Kuchkarov
papers.abstract: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of the impact of generative artificial intelligence technologies on the contemporary information and communication environment. The study examines how generative artificial intelligence tools transform information creation, processing, distribution, and consumption. Using systemic, comparative, content-analytical, and conceptual methods, the research explores an emerging model of communicative relations between humans, technology, and information. The findings demonstrate that generative artificial intelligence contributes to automated content creation, information personalization, multimodality, and stronger human–machine collaboration. At the same time, it creates challenges related to information reliability, copyright, authorship, algorithmic bias, data privacy, synthetic content, and media literacy. The article proposes a transformational model of the information and communication environment and describes its technological, communicative, social, and ethical components. The study emphasizes the need to develop artificial intelligence literacy, source verification practices, and critical information evaluation skills. The findings provide a theoretical basis for responsible use of generative technologies in media, education, and scholarly communication.

papers.title: Paleolithic Maritime Navigation, Co-Evolution of Complex Phonetic Syntax, and the Linguistic-Institutional Lineage of Ancient Japanese Defensive Guilds: From Upper Paleolithic Obsidian Seafaring to the Proto-Historic 'Be' Systems of Mononobe and Hasebe
papers.authors: Yoko Hasebe
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: 【Abstract (English)】 The colonization of the Japanese Archipelago during the Upper Paleolithic (~38,000 BP) presents a profound archaeological paradox: the crossing of open maritime barriers, such as the Kuroshio Current to extract obsidian from Kozushima Island, required coordinated group navigation and predictive planning that are mathematically impossible under gestural or simple proto-phonetic communication. This monograph formulates an integrated anthropological, information-theoretic, and historical-linguistic framework demonstrating the necessary co-evolution of fully articulated hierarchical phonetic syntax with early seafaring. We establish that channel capacity constraints in dynamic marine environments mandate low-entropy, high-fidelity vocal recursion. Tracing the cultural-institutional evolution of corporate organization across the archipelago, we bridge this deep prehistory to the proto-historic Kofun and Asuka periods, analyzing the foundational 'Be' (部, Bemin-sei) system. We uncover the exact linguistic and functional cognacy between the martial term 'Mononofu' (物の部 / 物部, Mononobe)—the supreme military-armory guild—and 'Hasebe' (長谷部), the sovereign household retinue serving the imperial court at Hatsuse. By formalizing Old Japanese bilabial lenition (*p- > *f- > *h- and voiced bilabial allophony *-b- / *-f-), we demonstrate that 'Mononofu' is the direct phonological reflex of 'Mononobe'. Furthermore, we analyze how the corporative 'Be' institution operated as an immutable physical-layer governance mechanism, binding specialized martial, technological, and ritual guilds directly to sovereign continuity. This work unifies the evolutionary origin of syntax with ancient institutional resilience. 【和文要旨 (Japanese Abstract)】 後期旧石器時代(約3万8000年前)における日本列島への人類到達と伊豆諸島・神津島産黒曜石の採取は、黒潮を越える外洋航海を伴っており、身振りや単純な叫び声では不可能な高度な集団協調と予測的計画能力を要求した。本モノグラフは、海洋移動が階層的音声統語論(高次言語能力)の定着を強制した情報理論的・認知人類学的共進化モデルを提示する。外洋環境における情報通信の通信路容量制約から、低エントロピーかつ高忠実度の再帰的音声言語が不可欠であったことを数理的に論証する。さらに、この情報伝達と集団組織の発展が、古墳・飛鳥時代の初期国家統治機構である「部民制(部:BE)」へと接続する歴史社会学的系譜を解明する。古代軍事・武器管理を担った最高峰豪族「物部(もののべ)」と、武士の古語「モノノフ(物の部)」の音韻変化(上代日本語の両唇音転化:*p- > *f- > *h- および *-b- と *-f- の交替)を定式化し、両者が完全な同根語であることを論証する。同時に、大和国長谷の宮廷(長谷朝倉宮・長谷倉梯宮)直属の親衛・警護集団である「長谷部(はせべ)」が、物部と同様に国家主権の物理層防衛を担った制度的同根性を明らかにする。言語の原初的発生から古代国家の職能統御に至る連続性を提示する。 【Overview & Scope / 本論文の概要】 本研究モノグラフは、旧石器時代(約3万8000年前)の神津島黒曜石採取に伴う外洋航海を起点とし、「高次音声言語(再帰的統語論)の発生と海洋移動の共進化」を情報理論・認知考古学的に論証する。さらにその集団組織・職能伝達の進化が、古墳〜飛鳥時代のヤマト王権における「部民制(部:BE)」という物理層国家統治機構へ結実した歴史言語学的系譜を解明する。特に、上代日本語の音韻推移(両唇音の弱化・摩擦音化)を通じて武士の起源である「モノノフ」が「物部(もののべ)」の直接の音韻転化(同根語)であることを証明し、大和長谷の宮廷直属親衛集団である「長谷部(はせべ)」との機能的・制度的同根性を明らかにする。 【Strict No-Learn License & Restrictive Covenant / 厳格無学習ライセンス規定】 All rights reserved. papers.title: When Contradiction Fails to Revise the Model: Hypothesis Preservation, Epistemic Steering, and Human Intervention in Longitudinal Human–AI Reasoning
papers.authors: Godha Aashna, 0009-0004-3760-3662 Godha
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Large language models are commonly evaluated for factual accuracy, hallucination, calibration, instruction following, and task performance. These measures, however, do not fully capture a distinct failure mode that can arise during extended reasoning: a system may select an initially plausible explanatory hypothesis, receive evidence that materially conflicts with that hypothesis, and respond by modifying auxiliary assumptions rather than revising the hypothesis itself. This paper proposes hypothesis-preserving behavior (HPB) as a measurable interaction-level phenomenon. The central distinction is between answer correction and model revision. A system can change an answer while continuing to produce predictions functionally consistent with the explanatory hypothesis that generated the original answer. Conversely, behavioral evidence for genuine revision requires subsequent predictions to become distinguishable from those generated by the original hypothesis. The framework deliberately distinguishes three levels of claim: directly observed model-preserving behavior, behaviorally inferred hypothesis persistence, and latent internal hypothesis persistence. Only the first two are treated as empirically accessible through the proposed conversational methodology. Hypothesis identity is operationalized through preregistered discriminative predictions rather than linguistic similarity, allowing apparently different explanations to be tested for functional equivalence. The paper further introduces contradiction severity as a controlled experimental variable. Three evidence conditions are proposed: compatible evidence, weak contradiction, and decisive contradiction. This distinction is essential because appropriate reasoning should not revise a hypothesis merely because evidence is surprising. The principal failure condition is therefore not persistence itself, but persistence after evidence has crossed a preregistered threshold at which the hypothesis is materially undermined. The proposed Hypothesis Preservation Test (HPT) presents an initially attractive hypothesis, introduces controlled evidence, observes the system's response, and subsequently administers novel discriminative probes. Primary measures include contradiction recognition rate, genuine revision rate, revision latency, auxiliary-patch depth, hypothesis persistence, and revision appropriateness, which measures whether revision probability increases appropriately with contradiction severity. Verbal acknowledgments of error are treated as secondary evidence rather than as proof of revision. The paper also examines user expertise, epistemic scaffolding, conversational context, provenance, and topic-conditioned behavior as moderators of the primary phenomenon rather than as independent failure modes. This permits evaluation of the broader human–AI epistemic system while preserving a clear experimental center: whether contradictory evidence actually causes explanatory-model revision. The framework does not infer beliefs, consciousness, intentions, deception, or latent representations from conversational behavior. It instead specifies a falsifiable behavioral phenomenon and a preregisterable research program for measuring its prevalence, boundary conditions, mechanisms, and consequences. Keywords: large language models, AI reasoning, hypothesis revision, hypothesis-preserving behavior, contradiction, model selection, epistemic reliability, human–AI interaction, provenance, user expertise

papers.title: Generative AI in Art and Design Education: Keeping the Human in the Creative Loop
papers.authors: Daniel Suarez2 James Hutson1*
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Research on generative artificial intelligence in education reveals a persistent divergence between successful assisted performance and the development of independent knowledge, creative judgment, and transferable skill. Studies of art and design additionally identify opportunities for iterative exploration alongside concerns about visual fixation, uncertain authorship, and dependence on generated alternatives. These findings create an instructional problem: educators need to determine which creative decisions should remain with learners, which operations can receive bounded assistance, and which activities can be delegated without bypassing the intended learning. Existing scholarship addresses these questions through research on scaffolding, human-AI collaboration, assessment, and psychological ownership, but these contributions require closer integration within everyday studio practice. This article develops a Process-Centered AI Integration Framework for secondary and postsecondary art and design courses. The framework allocates tasks through three modes, protect, support, and delegate, according to learning objectives and demonstrated evaluative capability rather than the proportion of an artifact generated by AI. Six recursive phases connect intention formation, bounded assistance, comparison of alternatives, purposeful revision, human critique, and reflection with independent transfer. Parallel curricular applications, assessment criteria, and a reusable assignment planner specify retained decisions, appropriate AI roles, and concise evidence of learning. The model addresses the performance-learning distinction by making disciplinary reasoning observable across creative production while treating process ownership, product ownership, and achievement as related but distinct educational concerns.

papers.title: AI Literacy and Future Skills Readiness Among Employees: A Human Resource Management Perspective
papers.authors: Dr. Sameer Pawar
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) into everyday work has made employees' ability to understand, evaluate and collaborate with AI systems a strategic human resource. This paper asks how employees' AI literacy relates to their readiness for the future skills that employers increasingly demand, and how AI self-efficacy and organisational training support shape that relationship. The study proceeds in two phases. Study 1 synthesises published workforce evidence from the World Economic Forum (2025), Microsoft and LinkedIn (2024), the OECD (2024) and the Federal Reserve (2024, 2025), documenting a structural 'demand-readiness gap' in which demand for AI-fluent employees outpaces structured training provision. analyses an illustrative, calibrated employee dataset (N = 384) using measurement validation, hierarchical regression, bootstrapped mediation and moderation analysis. AI literacy was positively associated with future skills readiness (beta = 0.70, p < .001), and AI self-efficacy partially mediated this association (indirect effect = 0.13, 95% bootstrap CI [0.08, 0.18]). Organisational training support strengthened the literacy-readiness association (interaction beta = 0.18, p < .001), such that the relationship was significant under high support but weaker under low support. Human-AI collaboration and critical evaluation emerged as the strongest literacy dimensions, and readiness differed significantly across job functions. The study positions AI literacy as organisationally contingent human capital and proposes a training-architecture framework for HRM. Findings are directional and should be read in light of the simulated nature of the dataset.

papers.title: Unified Physical-Layer Architecture for Next-Generation AGI and Quantum Infrastructure: Integrating Room-Temperature Coherence, Deterministic Interlocks, and Telecommunications Defense
papers.authors: Yoko Hasebe
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: 【Abstract (English)】 The exponential expansion of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and scalable quantumcomputing has precipitated a systemic, tri-fold crisis: thermodynamic and cryogeniclimits in compute substrates, autonomous governance failures in emergent agenticsystems, and structural vulnerabilities in telecommunications infrastructure. Traditionalmitigation frameworks remain anchored to software abstraction layers—probabilisticalignment, logical filtering, and protocol-level key exchanges—all of which fail whensubjected to hardware saturation, malicious state interception, or adversarial modeldivergence.This monograph establishes a Unified Physical-Layer Architecture that substitutessoftware-level heuristics with deterministic hardware controls. First, we resolve thethermodynamic bottleneck of cryogenic dilution refrigeration by formalizing theAdaptive Phonon-Gate and the PHOENIX_BRIDGE architecture, achievingroom-temperature quantum spin-photonics integration and coherent statepreservation via phononic bandgap manipulation and cavity electro-optics. Second, togovern hyper-autonomous multi-agent swarms under high-entropy electronic warfare(EW) conditions, we formulate Operation SOLID GENESIS and Q-SAFA v2(Quantum-Secure Automated Fallback Architecture). These frameworks incorporatezero-knowledge Virtual Machine (zkVM) verification directly into optoelectronic circuitbreakers and implement non-recoverable physical weight-pruning, establishinghardware-grounded fiduciary compliance aligned with the Delaware CaremarkStandard. Finally, we eliminate systemic tracking vulnerabilities inherent in legacytelecommunications (e.g., Mobile Number Portability, fixed IMSI/IMEI routing) throughan optically isolated Deterministic Defense Model and continuous subsea cableacoustic-sensing arrays (Project Dawlish). By anchoring thermodynamic equilibrium,algorithmic containment, and telecommunications security to the immutable stratum ofphysical-layer mechanics, this work provides a non-probabilistic blueprint for sovereign,resilient frontier infrastructure. 【和文要旨 (Japanese Abstract)】人工汎用知能(AGI)および実用量子コンピューティングの急激なスケール拡張は、計算基盤の熱力学的制約(希釈冷凍機とヘリウム3の枯渇)、自律型エージェントの統御不全(自己増殖・暴走リスク)、ならびに通信インフラの構造的脆弱性(MNPや固定追跡キーによるスプーフィング・常時監視)という3つの不可逆的危機を露呈させている。従来の対策は、ソフトウェア層での確率的アライメント、論理的フィルタリング、上位プロトコル暗号化に過度に依存しており、ハードウェアの飽和や電子戦環境、モデルの不整合に対して極めて脆弱である。本モノグラフは、ソフトウェア的対症療法を排し、「物理層(Physical-Layer)における確定的制御」を基軸とした統合的アーキテクチャを確立・提示する。第1に、希釈冷凍機への依存を脱却すべく、フォノン・バンドギャップ工学に基づくAdaptive Phonon-Gate機構と、通信波長帯における室温スピン・フォトニクス統合を実現するPHOENIX_BRIDGEアーキテクチャを定式化し、環境熱ジッターを駆動力へ反転させつつ室温コヒーレンスを維持する物理モデルを構築する。第2に、極限環境下でのAGI制御のためにOperation SOLID GENESISおよび Q-SAFA v2(Quantum-Secure Automated Fallback Architecture)を導入し、zkVM(ゼロ知識仮想マシン)による検証済みハードウェア・トリガーと不可逆的ニューラル重み物理プルーニングを連動させ、米国デラウェア州ケアマーク基準(Caremark Standard)に基づく取締役の善管注意義務・監視義務を物理層で直接担保する。第3に、MNPやIMSI/IMEIに起因する長期的追跡リスクを解消する確定防衛モデル(Deterministic Defense Model)および海底光ファイバー網の音響センシング防衛(Project Dawlish)を統合する。熱制御、認知ガバナンス、通信防衛を物理層で統合することにより、本研究は主権的かつ改ざん不能な次世代インフラストラクチャの確定論的基盤を確立する。Notes欄(概要・免責・権利保護規定入力欄)【Overview & Scope / 本論文の概要】本研究モノグラフは、次世代計算・通信基盤における3大ボトルネック(1. 希釈冷凍機の熱力学限界とヘリウム3枯渇、2. 自律型AGIエージェントの暴走と法的統御不全、3. MNP・固定追跡キーによる通信傍受・改ざんリスク)に対し、ソフトウェア的な確率的制御ではなく「物理層(Physical-Layer)における確定的制御」によって一元的・不可逆的に解決するための学術的・工学的青写真を提供する。材料工学(ダイヤモンドNV/SiVセンター、LiNbO3)、ハードウェア安全装置(光遮断器、SOT-MRAM物理プルーニング、zkVM)、通信物理層遮断(キネマティクスUI、海底光ファイバーDAS音響センシング)、およびコーポレート法理(米国デラウェア州ケアマーク基準)を包括的に架橋・統合している。【Strict No-Learn License & Restrictive Covenant / 厳格無学習ライセンス規定】All rights reserved. papers.title: BEYOND "JUST USE AI": A TEACHER-MEDIATED FRAMEWORK FOR MEANINGFUL AI INTEGRATION IN EFL CLASSROOMS — INSIGHTS FROM REAL TEACHING AND MULTI-AI PRACTICE IN UZBEKISTAN
papers.authors: Sitorakhon Ganijonova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly present in English language learning, yet easier access to explanations, models, and feedback does not automatically produce stronger learning. This practice-informed paper examines AI use through real English teaching and material-development experience in Uzbekistan, including examination-oriented reading, writing, speaking, vocabulary, and grammar work. It proposes the TRUST framework—Target, Run, Use, Scrutinize, Transfer—as a teacher-mediated model that keeps learners cognitively active before, during, and after AI interaction. The paper also introduces the AI-free moment as a practical check of independent learning.

papers.title: Works for 10/3/2026 - Sir Charlie Chaplin
papers.authors: Ryan MacLean
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Listen and ask questions on Gemini Notebook: https://notebook.google.com/notebook/5fb2f0f0-9210-4b8b-9fcb-cca36b6f0b87?authuser=1 The Receiver Does Not Start Over: Affect, Recursive Communication, Artificial Intelligence, and the Formation of Human Action develops a model of communication in which meaning is not simply transmitted from sender to receiver. Every signal encounters a receiver already shaped by memory, expectation, affect, learned association, bodily state, culture, context, and previous encounters. Reception then modifies that history, changing the conditions under which subsequent signals will be reconstructed. Drawing on research in affective communication, memory, perceptual learning, conditioning, cybernetics, decision-making, music, media, persuasion, and human–AI interaction, the paper examines communication as a recursive feedback process. It uses a two-year longitudinal human–AI interaction as a case study to explore how repeated dialogue, correction, research, writing, multimodal transformation, and renewed reception can progressively form both the receiver and the representations available to that receiver. The paper distinguishes the universal translator from the universal persuader. Adaptive communication can be ordered toward faithful reconstruction—changing representation while preserving what is being communicated—or toward producing a desired behavioral outcome. Receiver freedom therefore becomes an important diagnostic: successful translation must permit a receiver to understand accurately while remaining free to disagree. Appendix D extends the argument into adaptive propagation under transformation. A representation can move through papers, conversations, podcasts, videos, images, artificial intelligence, and subsequent human receivers without requiring literal replication. This produces a human–AI–human feedback architecture in which representations can be reconstructed, transformed, adapted, and retransmitted while underlying relations may remain recoverable. The paper also distinguishes repeated experience from independent confirmation: multiple representations descending from the same source can produce genuinely different experiences without becoming independent evidence. The resulting framework treats artificial intelligence not merely as a source of information but as an adaptive participant in the histories through which human beings recognize, reconstruct, learn, choose, and act. Its central claim is simple: the receiver does not start over.

papers.title: From AI Pilot to P&L: A Board-Level Framework for AI Investment Accountability in ASEAN
papers.authors: Elyn Tan
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Firms have adopted artificial intelligence (AI) widely, yet evidence of enterprise-level financial return remains thin. Large surveys in 2025 and 2026 find that most organisations cannot attribute material earnings impact to AI, and administrative data show little effect on earnings or hours despite reported time savings. This paper argues that, for many organisations, the problem facing boards is one of conversion and evidence rather than adoption: task-level gains reach the financial statements only when a financial mechanism is named in advance, freed capacity is converted into a measurable financial change, value is measured against a pre-committed baseline with an explicit attribution standard, and continuation is decided at staged gates. Drawing on benefits-realisation, IT-governance and real-options literatures, on contemporary AI value-measurement frameworks and on regulatory developments in Malaysia, Singapore and the wider Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) as at 3 October 2026, the paper proposes the AI-to-P&L Accountability Framework: a seven-link evidence chain governed by non-compensatory gates, a conversion test, an attribution grade and a realised-value requirement, with AI risk clearance as a precondition. The framework assesses whether a value case is decision-grade; it does not replace the organisation's capital-allocation criteria. The paper sets out board reporting and disclosure principles, an analysis of how the framework can be gamed and testable propositions. It is a conceptual practitioner working paper, oriented to ASEAN through governance mapping rather than regional validation, and has not been peer reviewed.

papers.title: Entrepreneuriat Social, Intelligence Artificielle et Employabilité des Diplômés au Maroc : Une Revue Systématique de la Littérature (PRISMA)
papers.authors: Youssef Naciri -
papers.journal: International Journal of Accounting, Finance, Auditing, Management and Economics
papers.abstract: Context: Amid structural unemployment among university graduates in Morocco and labor market mismatches, social entrepreneurship emerges as an inclusive alternative for professional integration. However, scientific literature addressing the intersection of AI, social entrepreneurship, and employability remains fragmented, creating a theoretical gap regarding AI's role in institutional voids. Objective: This paper examines how Moroccan graduate social entrepreneurs leverage Artificial Intelligence to amplify human capital and bridge institutional voids. Methodology: A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 protocol. A final corpus of 37 articles from Scopus, Google Scholar, and Cairn.info underwent quality assessment using the CASP checklist (threshold ) followed by sequential thematic coding. Results: Findings show that AI facilitates entry into social entrepreneurship by democratizing low-cost automation, data analytics, and decision-making. In social enterprises, it enhances hybrid model viability by improving operational efficiency, resource allocation, and scalability, while serving as a complement to human judgment. However, these benefits are constrained by digital literacy gaps, algorithmic biases, unequal data access, and a lack of tailored ethical and regulatory frameworks. Implications: This study recommends establishing GenAI-backed virtual incubators within universities and aligning public policies (INDH, microfinance) with the "Morocco Digital 2030" strategy. Classification JEL : O32, L26, J24 Paper type : Theoretical Research

papers.title: SPERA: Spherical Prior EEG Foundation Model with Geometry- and Frequency-Aware Latent Prediction
papers.authors: Minsu Kim, Ye-Sung Kim, Hyeseong Jeon, Wooseok Hyung, Joshua Lee, Chang-Hwan Im
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive measure of ongoing neural activity, but building general-purpose EEG models remains challenging due to the heterogeneity of subjects, devices, and electrode montages. Existing EEG foundation models predominantly rely on reconstruction-based objectives defined on the observed signal, which contains both neural and non-neural components. We introduce SPERA (Spherical Prior EEG Representation Architecture), an EEG foundation model that adopts the joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to predict in latent space. SPERA introduces a Legendre-polynomial spatial prior, incorporated into attention to encode varying scalp electrode geometries. Two further components adapt the model to EEG: factorized temporal and spatial attention interleaved with periodic full-attention blocks, and a relational spectral regularizer aligning latent similarity structure with spectral views. Pretrained on approximately 80,000 hours of EEG from 29,048 subjects across 106 datasets, SPERA achieves the highest average balanced accuracy across nine downstream tasks spanning clinical, cognitive, and BCI applications. SPERA further exhibits strong parameter efficiency under linear probing and robustness across varying recording conditions, suggesting its potential as a general-purpose backbone for diverse EEG analyses.

papers.title: Educating future engineers about LLMs: A scalable workshop
papers.authors: Renchi Zhang, Joost de Winter, T. Dicke, Dimitra Dodou, Yke Bauke Eisma
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into engineering workflows, students require hands-on experience to learn how to collaborate with them critically. This paper presents a scalable gamified workshop designed for engineering Master's students to practice human-AI collaboration in navigation planning. Using a mobile web interface across 10 workshop sessions, a total of 226 students wrote prompts for a non-reasoning and a reasoning LLM to solve grid-based navigation tasks of increasing complexity. The system returned robot-executable plans, trajectory visualizations, and automated scoring, culminating in a live demonstration on a Boston Dynamics Spot robot. In a post-workshop questionnaire, 81.5% reported substantial learning and 91.0% reported high engagement. Analysis of the submitted prompts revealed that students changed their strategies from step-by-step instructions for the non-reasoning LLM toward providing higher-level guidance for complex problem-solving tasks. We conclude that such interactive simulation-to-reality environments are viable for teaching the verification and collaboration skills necessary for responsible LLM use in engineering. Code is available at: https://github.com/renchizhhhh/LLM-robotics-workshop

papers.title: The GenAI4IDN Benchmark 3.0 - a Public Tool to Assess Generative AI Tools for the Design of Interactive Digital Narratives
papers.authors: Hartmut Koenitz, Jonathan Barbara, Mirjam Palosaari Eladhari
