papers.title: Perceived Barriers to Help‐Seeking for Eating Disorders Among Adults With Self‐Reported Eating Disorder Symptoms in Sweden
papers.authors: Anne-Charlotte Wiberg, Elisabeth Welch, Jake Linardon, Ata Ghaderi
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Help-seeking for eating disorders (EDs) remains low despite their burden and the importance of early intervention. This multimethod study examined perceived barriers to help-seeking among adults with self-reported ED symptoms in Sweden, a context underrepresented in prior help-seeking research. METHOD: The analytic sample included 2778 adults who completed an online survey assessing ED psychopathology and perceived barriers to help-seeking. Descriptive analyses identified endorsed perceived barriers, and logistic regression tested associations between symptom severity and barrier themes. Open-ended responses on barriers to and facilitators of help-seeking were analyzed thematically. RESULTS: The most frequently endorsed perceived barrier themes were stigma and shame, denial or failure to perceive illness severity, and fear of losing control or change. Qualitative findings highlighted limited ED competence in healthcare, particularly in primary care and for binge eating at higher body weight, as well as concerns about disclosure, confidentiality, and the availability of care. Facilitators included improved ED knowledge in healthcare, encouragement from others, anonymous digital care options, clearer access routes, and increased service availability. Higher ED symptom severity was associated with greater odds of endorsing most perceived barrier themes. DISCUSSION: Findings highlight the need for low-threshold interventions targeting shame, stigma, denial, and fear of change, alongside improved ED competence in healthcare, particularly in primary care, clearer referral pathways, and more inclusive care. If shown to be safe and effective, AI-based tools may help strengthen ED literacy across early-contact services and thereby reduce barriers to early recognition and help-seeking.

papers.title: The Changing Concept of News Credibility in the Era of AI-Based News: A Study in the Context of Television and Digital News
papers.authors: Punit Kumar
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital media technologies has significantly transformed the contemporary news ecosystem. Traditional processes of news production, editing, broadcasting, distribution, and consumption are undergoing substantial technological changes. In particular, the growing use of AI-generated news content, automated news writing, algorithm-driven news selection, and personalized news delivery has created both new opportunities and challenges for conventional news media such as television. Alongside these transformations, concerns regarding news credibility, authenticity, accuracy, fairness, transparency, and audience trust have gained increasing significance. The present study aims to examine the changing concept of news credibility in the emerging era of AI-based news. It comparatively explores how audiences evaluate the credibility of news presented through television and digital news platforms. The study focuses on key dimensions of news credibility, including accuracy, source credibility, fairness, transparency, authenticity, timeliness, and the processes involved in news production. It further seeks to understand how AI-based news content influences audience trust, perception, and acceptance of news. The study proposes a quantitative research approach, using a structured questionnaire to collect primary data from news consumers. It examines patterns of television and digital news consumption, audience preferences, perceptions of news credibility, and levels of trust in AI-based news content. The collected data will be analyzed to identify similarities and differences in perceptions of news credibility across traditional television and digital news environments, with particular attention to the growing role of AI in news production and distribution. The study is expected to contribute to a deeper understanding of changing audience trust and the evolving concept of news credibility in the context of digital journalism and the expansion of AI-based news systems. Its findings may be useful for news organizations, journalists, media scholars, and policymakers in developing appropriate approaches to maintaining accuracy, transparency, accountability, and public trust in an increasingly AI-driven news environment. The study may also provide insights into how traditional television news and emerging digital news platforms can adapt their journalistic practices to sustain credibility and audience confidence amid rapid technological transformation.

papers.title: Evaluating the Impact of Generative AI-Driven Adaptive Assessment Frameworks on Critical Thinking and Academic Integrity in Higher Education
papers.authors: Simran Kumari, Aditya Raj
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) adaptive assessment, in which the difficulty of questions, hints and feedback adjust to a learner’s live performance, is increasingly presented as a means of supporting personalised learning and critical thinking. At the same time, it may encourage cognitive offloading and create new academic-integrity concerns. This pilot study examines student perceptions of GenAI adaptive assessment, critical thinking, cognitive offloading, academic integrity and institutional readiness. The study combines secondary literature with a primary Google Form survey of 13 higher education students collected on 14 September 2026 through convenience sampling. Responses were analysed using frequencies, descriptive statistics, one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, sign tests, rank correlations and thematic coding. Respondents agreed that interactive AI hints improve the ability to break down multi-step problems (69.2%; p = .011) and that excessive reliance on real-time AI causes cognitive offloading (61.5%; p = .005). They also considered cognitive offloading in unmonitored work frequent (61.5%; p = .010). However, respondents were undecided on whether process-based adaptive assessment reduces ghostwriting, and they were divided on the clarity of institutional guidelines. As the sample is small, non-random and self-reported, the findings are indicative rather than generalisable. The study recommends adaptive systems designed around hints rather than final answers, assessment tasks requiring verification of AI outputs, process evidence and clear institutional rules on ethical AI use.

papers.title: Understanding Generative AI Use in Programming MOOCs: The Role of Course Context and Learner Characteristics
papers.authors: Marina Lepp
papers.abstract: The increasing availability of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools, such as ChatGPT and code-completion assistants, raises questions about how learners integrate these tools into learning activities, particularly in MOOCs that attract diverse participant populations. This study examines the use of GenAI in two programming MOOCs taught in Estonian that differ in duration, workload, topic complexity, and assignment volume: About Programming (4 weeks, 26 expected hours, n = 187) and Introduction to Programming (8 weeks, 78 expected hours, n = 182). Post-course questionnaire data were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods to examine self-reported adoption, usage frequency, and purposes of GenAI use across courses and learner backgrounds. The results show that GenAI adoption was widespread in both MOOCs, with no statistically significant differences by gender, age, education level, or prior programming experience. However, participants in the longer, more extensive MOOC reported significantly higher usage frequency and were more likely to use GenAI for debugging and idea generation. Reported usage frequency for code explanation and debugging was also higher in the longer course. Exploratory analyses found limited relationships between GenAI use and learning-related outcomes. The findings suggest that course context may play a greater role than learner characteristics in shaping how GenAI tools are used. These results provide implications for instructional design and guidance in programming education.

papers.title: AI Systems for Filmmaking: A Survey of HCI Research from a Labor-Centered Perspective
papers.authors: Xiaojuan Ma, Baiqiao Zhang, Lin Gao, Haotian Li, Huamin Qu, Rebecca A. Fiebrink, Sebastian Deterding, YUYING TANG
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is integrated into filmmaking and has attracted attention in human-computer interaction (HCI). Existing studies have primarily characterized AI systems for filmmaking by their capabilities and supported tasks, with limited attention to the organisation of filmmaking labor during system use. We review 31 HCI system papers and develop a three-layer taxonomy of labor sites, labor types, and human-AI allocation, examining where AI systems are positioned, what types of labor are involved during system use, and how those labor types are allocated between humans and AI. Our analysis reveals a concentration on individual below-the-line contexts, increasing attention to structural and meaning-making labor beyond execution, comparatively limited relational labor, and substantial variation in human-AI allocation across labor types. We further identify opportunities for the design and evaluation of AI systems that account for the broader organization of filmmaking labor. This review provides a labor-centered taxonomy for synthesizing AI systems for filmmaking and a basis for examining how AI may become involved in broader organizations of creative labor.

papers.title: Validation of the CERCA training programme in interpersonal skills development for nurses towards person-centred oncology practice: Nominal Group Technique protocol
papers.authors: Virginia La Rosa‐Salas, Marta Lizarbe-Chocarro, Sonsoles Martín Pérez
papers.abstract: The rising global incidence and prevalence of cancer demand that nursing staff transition towards person-centred practice (PCP). To achieve this, the development of nurses' interpersonal skills (IPS) constitutes an essential prerequisite. Although educational interventions currently exist to promote this development, they frequently address IPS partially and lack a robust theoretical framework rooted in PCP. To address these gaps, a blended training programme (the CERCA programme) has been designed and operationalised according to the intervention criteria proposed by Sidani and Braden, while also drawing on the Medical Research Council framework for complex interventions. This programme integrates innovative methodologies, such as clinical simulation and the use of generative artificial intelligence, to address emotional intelligence, communication and negotiation in a tiered manner. Prior to implementation, expert validation is essential to ensure the programme's clarity, methodological rigour and suitability for the target clinical context. Consequently, the aim of this study is to validate this training intervention in oncology nursing using a Nominal Group Technique design, refining the programme before implementation.

papers.title: Pengaruh penggunaan Artificial Intelligence (AI) terhadap motivasi dan kreatifitas siswa di Sekolah Menengah Atas
papers.authors: Rio ' Hidayat, Supratman Zakir
papers.journal: Idarah Tarbawiyah Journal of Management in Islamic Education
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has accelerated its adoption in education as a learning resource, instructional medium, and tool for completing academic tasks. AI facilitates access to information and supports idea generation; however, its impact on students' learning motivation and creativity remains a subject of ongoing debate. This study aimed to examine the effect of AI utilization on students' learning motivation and creativity. A quantitative approach employing an ex post facto correlational design was adopted. The study population consisted of 410 students, from which 203 participants were selected using the Slovin formula and the Proportional Stratified Random Sampling technique. Data were collected through a validated and reliable questionnaire and analyzed using simple linear regression and Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA). The findings revealed that AI utilization had a positive and statistically significant effect on students' learning motivation (t = 9.985, p < 0.05) and creativity (t = 8.863, p < 0.05). Furthermore, the MANOVA results indicated a significant simultaneous effect of AI utilization on both learning motivation and creativity (Pillai's Trace = 0.340; Wilks' Lambda = 0.660; F = 51.581; p < 0.05). These findings demonstrate that AI utilization positively influences students' learning motivation and creativity, both individually and simultaneously. Therefore, AI should be integrated into the learning process in a thoughtful and responsible manner to enhance students' motivation, foster creativity, and improve overall learning quality. Abstrak Pesatnya perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong pemanfaatannya dalam pendidikan sebagai sumber belajar, media pembelajaran, dan sarana penyelesaian tugas. AI memberikan kemudahan akses informasi dan mendukung pengembangan ide, namun juga memunculkan perdebatan mengenai pengaruhnya terhadap motivasi dan kreativitas siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh penggunaan AI terhadap motivasi dan kreativitas siswa. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain ex post facto dan jenis penelitian korelasional. Populasi berjumlah 410 siswa, dengan sampel 203 siswa yang ditentukan menggunakan rumus Slovin dan teknik Proportional Stratified Random Sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket yang telah memenuhi uji validitas dan reliabilitas, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear sederhana dan Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan AI berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap motivasi siswa (t = 9,985; p = 0,000 < 0,05) serta kreativitas siswa (t = 8,863; p = 0,000 < 0,05). Uji MANOVA juga menunjukkan pengaruh signifikan AI terhadap motivasi dan kreativitas secara simultan dengan nilai Pillai’s Trace = 0,340, Wilks’ Lambda = 0,660, F = 51,581, dan p = 0,000 < 0,05. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan AI berpengaruh positif terhadap motivasi dan kreativitas siswa sehingga pemanfaatannya perlu diarahkan secara bijaksana untuk mendukung kualitas pembelajaran.

papers.title: From Qur’anic Anthropology to Ethical Agency: Reframing Human Agency in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Halvi Sepiana Zulva, Nindhya Ayomi Delahara, Sujiat Zubaidi, Muhammad Chirzin
papers.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly mediating how humans acquire knowledge, make decisions, and perform cognitive activities. In higher education, the delegation of cognitive activities to algorithmic systems has the potential to shift human judgment and responsibility. This study aims to examine Qur’anic anthropology as a foundation for reframing human agency under increasingly AI-mediated conditions. This study employs a qualitative approach using a literature-based design and conceptual analysis. A semantic-contextual analysis is conducted on the Qur’anic terms al-insān, al-bashar, al-nās, Banī Ādam, al-ins, al-mar’, as well as the concepts of ‘abd and khalīfah. The findings are then synthesized with theories of human agency, moral responsibility, and AI ethics. The findings reveal that Qur’anic anthropology represents human beings as multidimensional entities possessing cognitive, relational, moral, spiritual, and teleological capacities. These dimensions are reconstructed into eight capacities of Qur’anic human agency: epistemic, moral, relational, spiritual, and teleological agency. The findings demonstrate that human agency from a Qur’anic perspective is not synonymous with absolute autonomy, but rather constitutes the capacity to understand, evaluate, choose, and act consciously within an orientation of values and responsibility. In the context of AI, Qur’anic Ethical Intelligence (QEI) is conceptualized as an ethical capacity to direct and evaluate the use of AI without surrendering human judgment and responsibility to algorithmic systems. As a conceptual study, this research does not empirically test the application of QEI among university students. Further research is therefore needed to validate and develop measurement instruments. This study connects Qur’anic anthropology with human agency under algorithmic conditions and proposes QEI as a framework for strengthening human agency resilience in the age of AI.

papers.title: DEVELOPING A MODEL FOR PROVIDING INDIVIDUALIZED FEEDBACK IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE LESSONS USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Khoshimova Azizaxon Muxtorjon qizi Yuldasheva Hilola Zohidjonovna
papers.journal: International Journal of Literature and Language Studies
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence technologies into education creates new opportunities for individualized learning. In English lessons, AI tools can support the development of learners’ written and spoken communication, identify grammatical and lexical errors, and provide tailored feedback. This article analyzes the pedagogical potential of AI-assisted individualized feedback and proposes a six-stage model: Diagnosis – Analysis – Personalization – Feedback – Revision – Monitoring. The model goes beyond identifying errors by explaining possible causes, adapting recommendations to learners’ proficiency levels, and designing individual follow-up tasks. The article discusses the model’s benefits and potential challenges, the teacher’s role in supervision and pedagogical mediation, and principles of responsible AI use.

papers.title: LIPID PROFILE PARAMETERS (TC, TG, HDL, AND LDL) AS CORRELATES OF ANTHROPOMETRIC PARAMETERS (BMI, WC, WHR, WHTR, BRI, AND VAI) AMONG PATIENTS WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS
papers.authors: Chinasa Jane Onyeulor, Ezekiel Udo Umoh, CHIMA OBASI IFEANYI, Nnaemeka Ikenna Nwawuba, Prof. O. C. Ohaeri, GOZIEM UGWUIBE ONYEWUCHI
papers.journal: Valeology: International Journal of Medical Anthropology and Bioethics (2995-4924)
papers.abstract: The study sought to determine the correlation between lipid profile parameters (TC, TG, HDL, and LDL) and anthropometric parameters (BMI, WC, WHR, WHtR, BRI, and VAI) among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. In carrying out this study comparative cross-sectional study was adopted. The study population consisted of one hundred (100) diagnosed type 2 diabetic patients and one hundred (100) apparently healthy, age- and sex-matched non-diabetic individuals who served as controls. All participants were aged between 30 and 70 years. Ten (10) mL of venous blood samples were collected from each participant after overnight fast using standard aseptic procedures and distributed into appropriate tubes for the determination of fasting plasma glucose (FPG), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), insulin, lipid profile, and oxidative stress markers. Serum and plasma were prepared by centrifugation at 3000 rpm for 10 minutes, while whole blood was used for selected analyses. The samples were analyzed using standard laboratory methods. Data obtained were analyzed using Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 25.0. Results were expressed as Mean ± Standard Deviation. The test of significance was determined using independent samples t-test, while Pearson correlation analysis was used to assess relationships between variables, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. In conclusion lipid profile parameters, including total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), are important indicators of metabolic and cardiovascular health among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The result of the findings revealed that there was a significant negative correlation of superoxide dismutase (SOD) with body roundness index (BRI) (r = −0.207*, p = 0.039) in type 2 diabetic patients. There was a significant negative correlation of catalase (CAT) with body mass index (BMI) (r = −0.402*, p = 0.000), waist circumference (WC) (r = −0.329*, p = 0.001), and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) (r = −0.211*, p = 0.035), while significant positive correlations were observed with waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) (r = 0.287*, p = 0.004) and BRI (r = 0.359*, p = 0.000) in type 2 diabetic patients The study concluded that lipid profile parameters, including total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), are important indicators of metabolic and cardiovascular health among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. One of the recommendations made was that patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus should undergo regular lipid profile and anthropometric assessments to facilitate early identification of dyslipidaemia and abnormal adiposity.

papers.title: Pelatihan Pemanfaatan Platform AI Secara Etis Sebagai Penguatan Karakter Digital di PKBM Mandiri Bakti
papers.authors: Rifkah Fadiyah Mansyur, Wahdatan Nisa, Mega Surya, Astrise Astrise, Nita Dwi Handayani, Maulidatul Khasanah, Rofy Rusdianawati
papers.abstract: Program pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk membekali dan meningkatkan karakter digital para tutor dan warga belajar PKBM Mandiri Bakti dalam memanfaatkan penggunaan AI. Kegiatan ini berupa pelatihan dengan menggunakan platform AI seperti ChatGPT, GeminiAI dan Copilot. Hasil observasi menunjukkan masih banyak warga belajar belum terampil dalam menyusun perintah AI dengan jelas. Selain itu masih lemahnya etika digital dalam mengevaluasi ketepatan informasi yang dihasilkan AI. Berdasarkan masalah tersebut, tujuan dari kegiatan ini adalah melatih tutor dan warga belajar dalam memanfaatkan platform AI secara etis dan bertanggung jawab. Metode penyelenggaraan pelatihan ini dilakukan dengan pendekatan ABCD (Asset Based Community Development) melalui sosialisasi dan praktik. Kegiatan sosialisasi dilakukan sebagai bentuk penyampaian pentingnya penggunaan platform AI secara bijak serta contoh penerapan pembuatan prompt AI secara spesifik. Hasil pelatihan menunjukkan bahwa efektivitas tutor dan warga belajar dalam memanfaatkan platform AI secara etis mengalami peningkatan sebesar 26,67%. Pemanfaatan platform AI bagi warga belajar juga dapat menjadi sarana pendukung kemandirian belajar. Melalui kegiatan pengabdian ini, mulai terlihat proses bertumbuhnya karakter digital bagi tutor dan warga belajar pada pendidikan nonformal. Dengan meningkatnya hal tersebut, proses penguatan karakter digital melalui pemanfaatan AI menjadi lebih terarah dan bertanggung jawab.

papers.title: Beyond Plagiarism: Rethinking Academic Integrity in the Age of Generative AI among ESL University Students
papers.authors: HINA MANZOOR
papers.journal: Journal of Arts and Linguistics Studies
papers.abstract: This study examined how English as a Second Language (ESL) university students understand and practice academic integrity in the age of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). Its objectives were to examine students' understanding of integrity beyond plagiarism, explore their GenAI use in writing, and identify institutional supports they need. Background: GenAI challenges plagiarism-centred policies, and AI detectors may disadvantage non-native writers. The study drew on Eaton's post-plagiarism framework, which treats integrity as transparency, accountability, and judgement in human-AI co-authorship. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was used. The population was 1,200 ESL undergraduate and postgraduate students at one public university. Questionnaire data were collected from 291 students selected through stratified random sampling and analyzed in SPSS using descriptive statistics, t-tests, and one-way ANOVA. Interview data were collected from 15 students selected through purposive maximum-variation sampling and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Students reported high understanding of integrity (M = 3.70) and high AI use (M = 3.66), mainly for language editing (M = 4.21), but low perceived institutional support (M = 2.46). Postgraduates understood integrity better than undergraduates (p < .001). Five themes emerged, including blurred boundaries and fear of unfair suspicion. Clear policies, ESL-sensitive AI literacy, and process-based assessment are recommended.

papers.title: Cognitive Augmentation or Cognitive Offloading? Artificial Intelligence in Education and Lifelong Learning
papers.authors: Verda Gizem OĞUL
papers.journal: International Journal of Sciences and Innovation Engineering
papers.abstract: Research on artificial intelligence (AI) and education has developed across largely separate domains, including learning outcomes, academic integrity, institutional governance, and lifelong-learning demand. This study integrates these domains through a common framework distinguishing cognitive augmentation, where AI supports human thinking, from cognitive offloading, where it substitutes for it. It synthesizes 2025–2026 evidence from the OECD, UNESCO, MIT, RAND Corporation, UC Berkeley, HEPI, Gallup, the Walton Family Foundation, official Türkiye sources, and triangulated market data. PISA 2025 findings covering approximately 760,000 students across 91 countries and economies provide cross-national evidence: students who did not use AI to draft assignments outperformed those who did, while frequent users trained to critically evaluate AI-generated information performed better than those without such training. Additional evidence shows short-term AI-supported performance gains without equivalent retained learning, discipline-specific patterns of AI-assisted academic misconduct, rapidly increasing AI-generated coursework, and widespread teacher AI use despite limited formal governance. Türkiye is examined as a policy case linking economy-wide and education-specific AI strategies. Overall, the findings indicate that AI’s educational impact depends less on the technology itself than on pedagogical design, assessment redesign, and institutional governance capacity.

papers.title: The Architecture of AI Governance in Banking: Bridging Compliance and Explainability Gaps
papers.authors: Marjan Sultana Nuha
papers.journal: Pacific Journal of Advanced Engineering Innovations
papers.abstract: The adoption of AI in the banking sector has made its way into various functions of the banking business such as credit assessment, fraud detection, risk management, compliance, and customer service, thus introducing fresh challenges in the realms of transparency, accountability, and risk management of banking models. This paper reviews the challenges of governance of AI in banking, focusing on the limitations of explainability, regulations and how AI model risks intersect with traditional banking risks. Explainability is not a single technical property but rather a governance capability that helps to document, reconstruct, challenge and monitor decisions throughout the model lifecycle. The regulatory and standards expectations are discussed, such as lifecycle governance, independent validation, data lineage, documentation, monitoring and senior management accountability. Special focus is placed on the constraints of the post hoc explanation, the performance vs. interpretation dilemma, the need for different explanations for different stakeholders and problems in the cases of complex and emerging AI models. Practical application patterns illustrate the application of interpretable models, post hoc methods, counterfactual explanations, audit trails, human oversight, and ongoing testing. Third party models, data quality, cyber security, model drift and integration with existing credit, market, liquidity, operational, compliance and reputational risk models are also taken into account. By leveraging AI, a coordinated governance strategy integrating technical validation, regulatory alignment, traditional risk management, documentation, and necessary human oversight can enhance accountability while addressing the real-world constraints of complex AI systems in regulated banking settings.

papers.title: The Transformation of English Language Teaching in the Digital Era: Autonomy, Assessment, Multimodal Literacy, and Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Afsana Mirjalal Orujlu
papers.abstract: Digital technology has transformed English language teaching (ELT) by extending learning beyond the conventional classroom and reshaping how learners access input, practise language, receive feedback, and participate in communication. This article examines that transformation through a narrative review and conceptual synthesis focused on learner autonomy, formative assessment, digital and multimodal literacy, artificial intelligence (AI), and the evolving role of the English language teacher. The review indicates that digital platforms, mobile applications, online resources, videoconferencing, automated feedback, and AI can expand access to authentic materials, personalised practice, intercultural interaction, and continuous feedback. However, technological availability does not itself guarantee effective language learning. Outcomes depend on pedagogical design, teacher mediation, learner readiness, digital competence, accessibility, and the alignment between technological tools and communicative objectives. The analysis also identifies persistent challenges, including unequal access, overreliance on automated systems, assessment validity, privacy, academic integrity, and the need for critical AI literacy. A human-centred model is therefore proposed in which technology supports rather than replaces teachers, learner agency, and meaningful interaction. The article concludes that successful digital transformation in ELT should be evaluated by its contribution to autonomous, inclusive, reflective, and communicative language learning rather than by technological novelty alone.

papers.title: An Investigation into AI Dependence, Critical Thinking and Writing Competence among Nigerian University Undergraduates
papers.authors: Abidakun Olusiji Damilola, Obianuju Blessing Mokwelu, Funmilayo Lisa MATHEW
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools into academic activities has raised concerns about its impact on students' core cognitive and linguistic skills. This study investigated the relationship between AI dependence and critical thinking and writing competence among English Language students. The study adopted a correlational research design. The population comprised English Language students, from which 492 students were selected using stratified random sampling technique. Data were collected using three validated instruments: AI Dependence Scale, Critical Thinking Disposition Scale and Writing Competence Scale. Mean and standard deviation were used to answer the research questions while Pearson Product-Moment Correlation (PPMC) was used to test the hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. Findings revealed a significant inverse association between AI dependence and critical thinking, r(490) = -.38, p <.001, and between AI dependence and writing competence, r(490) = -.42, p <.001. This suggests that higher levels of AI dependence are associated with lower levels of critical thinking and writing competence. The study concluded that excessive dependence on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly and QuillBot is inversely associated with students' ability to analyze, evaluate and produce original written texts. While AI offers academic support, over-reliance weakens independent reasoning and writing skills.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Dentistry: Boon or Bane? A Cross-Sectional Study Assessing Perceptions, Acceptance, and Ethical Concerns Among Dental Professionals
papers.authors: Dr. Kanu Pandey, Dr Bushra Ameen Tigala
papers.journal: World Wide Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Development
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare through automated data analysis, pattern recognition, clinical decision support, and workflow optimization. Dentistry has increasingly incorporated AI-based technologies into radiographic diagnosis, orthodontics, implantology, prosthodontics, oral pathology, and practice management.[1][2][3][4]Despite these advances, concerns regarding data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, medico-legal responsibility, cost, and the preservation of clinician–patient interaction remain important considerations.[1][5][6] Aim The present study aimed to assess the perceptions of dental professionals regarding the benefits, limitations, ethical implications, and clinical applicability of AI in dentistry and to determine their readiness to incorporate AI-based technologies into routine clinical practice. Materials and Methods A descriptive cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among 250 dental professionals, including undergraduate interns, postgraduate students, academicians, and private practitioners. A structured questionnaire was distributed electronically using Google Forms following Institutional Ethics Committee approval. The questionnaire evaluated demographic characteristics, awareness and perceived applications of AI, perceived benefits and limitations, and ethical and professional concerns. Data were analyzed using SPSS version XX. Results Among the 250 participants, 65% perceived AI as a valuable technological advancement capable of improving dental practice, whereas 35% expressed reservations regarding its implementation. The major perceived benefits included improved diagnostic support, increased efficiency, standardized assessment, treatment-planning assistance, and workflow optimization. The major concerns were implementation cost, data privacy, algorithmic bias, medico-legal accountability, and possible reduction in clinician–patient interaction. Participants expressed greater confidence in AI-assisted radiographic diagnosis, orthodontic planning, implant planning, and image analysis, while lower confidence was reported for complex surgical decision-making, unpredictable clinical situations, ethical decision-making, and patient communication. Conclusion Dental professionals demonstrated considerable interest in the potential applications of AI while recognizing important limitations and ethical concerns. Responsible integration of AI into dentistry requires appropriate professional training, rigorous clinical validation, data-protection mechanisms, transparency, clearly defined accountability, and continued human oversight. AI should therefore function primarily as a clinical decision-support tool rather than a replacement for professional judgment. Keywords: Artificial intelligence; dentistry; machine learning; dental professionals; digital dentistry; clinical decision support; ethics; artificial intelligence in oral and maxillofacial surgery

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence; Rethinking- Learning in an Era of HumanMade Technology and Capitalist Mechanism
papers.authors: Srija Chakraborty
papers.journal: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) have revolutionised the interaction between humans, knowledge and technology. What once needed years of formal education, years of institutional access or specialist's help is now obtained, translated, explained, reorganised in seconds. This unprecedented accessibility can help to minimize some of the age disadvantages in learning and provide lifelong education. Meanwhile, it asks the essential question: With the ready availability of answers, and analyses the decisions through own judgement, curiosity, critical understanding and intellectual independence. This paper critically discusses the overlaps between AI, Age, Education, Automation and Capitalism. But it's not necessarily the democratisation of education, it says, arguing that the democratisation of access to AI shouldn't be equated with the democratisation of education. While it can overturn the notion that technological skills are predominantly the purview of younger people, the potential for age disparities leading compounded differences in access to these tools, algorithmic bias, and confidence gaps and differences in digital and AI literacy. At the same time, the increasing machine-like nature of the educational activities threatening to change the purpose of education from learning and human development to efficiency, productivity and measurable outcome is awaited niche. Literature-based analysis is carried out by reference to the UNESCO, OECD, Stanford AI Index, IMF, ILO, and peer-reviewed scholarship along with the theoretical approaches of critical pedagogy, digital ageism and technological capitalism. Based on secondary data, the use of AI by students is already prevalent and evidence about the impacts on learning is mixed, and largely dependent on the context of use. This paper suggests neither technological rejection nor unconditional adoption. Rather, a human-centred approach should be pursued where AI is a tool for intellectual work and not an intellectual replacement in education systems. AI literacy, critical thinking, intergenerational learning, teacher agency, and transparent assessment and equitable access, therefore, should be central to modern education.

papers.title: Ethical Challenges of Generative AI in Education
papers.authors: Amey Pangarkar
papers.journal: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
papers.abstract: With its swift evolution, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has revolutionized the field of education, offering possibilities for personalized learning, automated grading, content generation, and administrative assistance. Large language models (LLMs), like ChatGPT and Gemini, have revolutionized the way teachers and students engage in learning.Large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT and Gemini have transformed how teachers and students approach teaching and learning in schools and higher education institutions. Their pervasive use, however, brings many ethical questions about academic integrity, privacy, transparency, fairness, accountability, and human autonomy. This study investigates the ethical implications of the use of generative AI in education using a doctrinal and interdisciplinary method. It scans upto-date literature, international policy documents, and ethical guidelines that have been released from 2020 to 2026. Special focus is placed on algorithmic bias, data protection, intellectual property, digital inequality, misinformation, and learner reliance on AI systems. The results indicate that key elements of responsible AI governance need to be human-centred educational values, institutional accountability, AI literacy, and inclusive policy-making. The research suggests an ethical framework focusing on transparency, fairness, privacy protection, critical thinking, and collaborative governance to support the sustainable and responsible use of generative AI in education.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON EFL LEARNERS’ WRITING SKILLS: OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES
papers.authors: Tilavoldiyeva Gulchexraxon
papers.abstract: The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into language education is reshaping the ways in which English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners develop their writing competence. This article examines the dual influence of AI-powered tools on learners’ written production, focusing on both their educational potential and the challenges associated with their use. Particular attention is given to the role of AI in supporting idea generation, lexical development, grammatical accuracy, text organization, and revision practices. AI-assisted feedback may help learners identify linguistic weaknesses, explore alternative expressions,and improve the clarity and coherence of their written work. Nevertheless, the educational value of these technologies depends on howcritically and purposefully learners engage with them. Excessive dependence on automated suggestions may weaken independent decision-making, reduce individual authorial expression, and raise concerns about academic integrity, information reliability, and responsible technology use. The article emphasizes the importance of integrating AI into EFL writing instruction as a supportive learning resource rather than a substitute for learners’ cognitive effort. It highlights the need for pedagogical guidance that combines technological assistance with critical thinking, independent composition, and reflective revision. Such an approach can help learners benefit from AI-based tools while preserving originality, authorship, and the development of sustainable writing skills.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Use and Learner Autonomy Among Secondary Students: The Roles of AI Literacy and Metacognitive Self-Regulation
papers.authors: John Rey Tumulin
papers.journal: International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies
papers.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in secondary education has created new opportunities for personalized support, immediate feedback, problem-solving, and self-directed learning, while also raising concerns about students’ reliance on AI-generated information. This narrative literature review examined AI use and learner autonomy among secondary students, with particular attention to the roles of AI literacy and metacognitive self-regulation. Recent literature published primarily from 2021 to 2026 was identified, screened, and synthesized through narrative and reflexive thematic analysis. Across the reviewed studies, AI supported learner autonomy most clearly when students used it for exploration, feedback, problem-solving, and self-regulated learning rather than as a substitute for independent thinking. AI literacy helped students understand AI, evaluate generated information, recognize its limitations, and make responsible decisions about its use. Metacognitive self-regulation, in turn, supported students in planning, monitoring, and evaluating their learning while working with AI. The literature also pointed to challenges, including excessive reliance on AI, limited AI knowledge, inconsistent learner engagement, and differences in self-regulatory abilities. Overall, learner autonomy in AI-supported settings depends on how students use the technology and on the development of AI literacy and metacognitive self-regulation with appropriate teacher guidance. The study contributes primarily to Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education) by supporting responsible and learner-centered integration of AI in secondary education. From a sustainability perspective, strengthening students’ critical and self-regulatory competencies may promote more responsible, adaptable, and sustainable use of emerging digital technologies in education.

papers.title: The impact of AI-enhanced assistive technologies on the learning experiences of children with disabilities in Zimbabwe
papers.authors: Nelson Matanana, Cry Kuranga, Lawrence Ruvinga, Pauline Chimwayi, Caroline Ruvinga
papers.abstract: Educational inclusion for children with disabilities remains constrained by structural inequalities, limited specialist resources and persistent disparities in access to quality learning opportunities. Although specialised learning environments have traditionally relied on dedicated infrastructure and human support, such arrangements frequently reinforce educational segregation and restrict equitable participation in mainstream schooling, particularly in low-resource contexts. Artificial intelligence-enhanced assistive technologies (AI-AT) present a transformative opportunity to reconfigure these constraints by personalising learning, improving accessibility and extending instructional support beyond conventional pedagogical boundaries. Yet, evidence on their effectiveness within resource-constrained education systems remains limited. This study examines the influence of AI-AT on the learning experiences of children with disabilities in Zimbabwean primary schools, where infrastructural, financial and institutional limitations continue to shape inclusive education outcomes. Rather than assuming technological determinism, the study interrogates how contextual conditions mediate the educational value of AI-AT and the extent to which these technologies advance or reproduce existing inequalities. Guided by the Technology Acceptance Model and sociocultural theory, the study adopts a mixed-methods research design involving ten purposively selected primary schools in Zimbabwe. The findings demonstrate that AI-AT substantially enhances learner engagement, instructional accessibility, communication, personalised learning and participation, thereby expanding opportunities for meaningful educational inclusion. However, these gains are contingent upon institutional readiness, teacher digital competence, affordability and supportive policy environments. The analysis further reveals that algorithmic bias, data governance, cultural relevance and digital inequities represent systemic rather than merely technical challenges, with significant implications for equitable implementation. The study argues that the educational potential of AI-AT in developing countries depends less on technological sophistication than on its contextual adaptation within local pedagogical, socio-economic and cultural realities. It therefore contributes empirical evidence to debates on inclusive artificial intelligence by demonstrating that sustainable educational transformation requires the co-evolution of technology, institutional capacity and inclusive policy frameworks.

papers.title: Effects of AI-powered ChatGPT on learning achievements of education undergraduates in Nigerian universities
papers.authors: Peter Ayoola Ajelabi, TANIMU ADAM IBRAHIM
papers.journal: Aminu Kano Academic Scholars Association Multidisciplinary Journal
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effect of ChatGPT-supported instruction on the achievement of 200-level undergraduate students in the Communication and Media Technology course at Northwest University, Kano, Nigeria, and whether the effect differed by gender. A pre-test, post-test, control-group experimental design was used. One hundred and eighteen (118) students, purposively selected from the course, were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 59), taught with traditional instruction supplemented with ChatGPT, or a control group (n = 59), taught with traditional instruction only, for six weeks. Data were collected with the Communication and Media Technology Achievement Test (CMTAT; KR-20 = 0.82) and analysed with analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), with pre-test scores as the covariate, at the 0.05 level of significance. After adjusting for pre-test scores, the experimental group obtained significantly higher post-test scores than the control group, F(1, 115) = 18.34, p < .001, partial η² = .138. The Treatment verses Gender interaction was not statistically significant, F(1, 113) = 1.22, p = .272, partial η² = .011; the study therefore found no evidence that the effect differed between male and female students, but it was not designed to establish that the effect is equal. Because the sample was purposive, drawn from one course at one university, and exposed to the intervention for six weeks, the findings should not be generalised to all Nigerian undergraduates. Replication across courses and institutions is recommended.

papers.title: BIẾN ĐỔI THỊ HIẾU THẨM MỸ CỦA SINH VIÊN VIỆT NAM TRONG SỰ BÙNG NỔ CỦA TRÍ TUỆ NHÂN TẠO
papers.authors: Hương Đỗ Thị Thanh Hương
papers.journal: Tạp chí Khoa học Trường Đại học Trưng Vương
papers.abstract: This article highlights shifts in students' aesthetic tastes. The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) is driving - and will continue to drive - profound, multifaceted changes in aesthetic preferences among people in general and students in particular. Consequently, the article examines the factors influencing this evolution of aesthetic taste, addresses emerging issues, and offers recommendations to help understand and elevate students' aesthetic sensibilities.

papers.title: ĐỀ XUẤT KHUNG NĂNG LỰC TRÍ TUỆ NHÂN TẠO (AI) CHO HỌC SINH PHỔ THÔNG VIỆT NAM DỰA TRÊN KHUNG UNESCO VÀ CHƯƠNG TRÌNH GIÁO DỤC PHỔ THÔNG 2018
papers.authors: Ngo Van Hung
papers.journal: Tạp chí Khoa học Trường Đại học Trưng Vương
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes the requirements for developing Artificial Intelligence (AI) competencies among Vietnamese K-12 students by comparing three sources: (i) Directives from the Ministry of Education and Training’s Plan No. 1338/ KH-BGDĐT (dated February 6, 2026) regarding the 2026 National Conference on Educational Science; (ii) UNESCO’s AI Competency Framework for Students (2024), comprising 12 competencies across four dimensions and three proficiency levels; and (iii) Data on the education sector's digital transformation from the Ministry of Education and Training’s summary reports for the 2024– 2025 period. The comparative analysis reveals four primary gaps: (1) The absence of specific AI competency standards for learners; (2) Unequal distribution of infrastructure and digital learning resources; (3) A lack of systematic AI training for teachers; and (4) The absence of tools to measure students' AI competencies. Based on these findings, the paper proposes five key solutions and a threestage implementation model (2026–2029) at the provincial pilot scale, accompanied by a system of quantitative KPIs, specific measurement methods, and risk management strategies (detailed in the Appendix). Notably, the study introduces a validated process for establishing baseline data - a prerequisite for formulating, evaluating, and adjusting future policies on AI competency in K-12 education based on empirical evidence rather than intuition or anecdotal experience - thereby affirming the study's practical value and policy implications within the current context of educational digital transformation.

papers.title: VẬN DỤNG NGUYÊN TẮC TOÀN DIỆN CỦA TRIẾT HỌC MÁC – LÊNIN TRONG PHÂN TÍCH TÁC ĐỘNG ĐA CHIỀU CỦA TRÍ TUỆ NHÂN TẠO ĐỐI VỚI GIÁO DỤC ĐẠI HỌC NGOÀI CÔNG LẬP VIỆT NAM: TIẾP CẬN BIỆN CHỨNG VÀ HÀM Ý CHIẾN LƯỢC
papers.authors: Huê Nguyễn Thị Huê
papers.journal: Tạp chí Khoa học Trường Đại học Trưng Vương
papers.abstract: In the era of digital transformation, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as a disruptive force, profoundly reshaping all aspects of social life, particularly higher education. AI not only alters approaches to knowledge acquisition and the organization of teaching and research activities but also impacts university governance structures, the labor market, and the development of high-quality human resources. However, current assessments of AI's impact often fall into two extremes: technological optimism (absolutizing benefits) or technological pessimism (fear and rejection). This article applies the principle of comprehensiveness from Marxist-Leninist philosophy to systematically identify and evaluate the multidimensional impacts of AI on non-public higher education in Vietnam. Methodologically, the article employs the dialectical materialist approach to analyze the dialectical relationships between technology, education, ethics, and the socioeconomic context. Research findings indicate that AI exerts a dual impact: on one hand, it fosters personalized learning and optimizes governance; on the other, it poses serious challenges regarding academic integrity, educational equity, and the potential decline of learners' dialectical thinking capabilities. Consequently, the article proposes solutions and strategic implications for non-public universities - specifically Trung Vuong University - emphasizing the necessity of ethical AI application coupled with a priority on developing higher-order cognitive skills that machines cannot easily replicate.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Financial Advice and Algorithmic Personalization in Pakistan: The Mediating Role of AI Trust and the Role of Digital Financial Literacy in Perceived Financial Decision Quality
papers.authors: Muhammad Ali QAZI, Usman Arshad, Kashif Bilal Majeed
papers.journal: International Journal of Business and Management Sciences
papers.abstract: This study examines how AI-enabled financial advice and algorithmic personalization relate to perceived financial decision quality in Pakistan, considering AI trust as a mediator and digital financial literacy as a predictor and moderator. Questionnaire responses from 380 participants were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement assessment indicated strong internal consistency, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. Financial advice and personalization were positively associated with trust and decision quality, while trust partially mediated both relationships. Digital financial literacy was positively associated with trust but did not significantly moderate either antecedent–trust relationship. The corresponding moderated-mediation relationships were also unsupported. The model explained 68.6% of the variance in trust and 67.9% in perceived decision quality. These findings distinguish literacy’s direct association from its proposed moderating role and identify trust as an intervening mechanism linking service evaluations with perceived decision outcomes. The study suggests that financial providers prioritize understandable guidance, relevant personalization, and transparent explanations. As the evidence concerns self-reported perceptions, the results establish associations rather than causal improvements in financial performance or objectively verified investment outcomes.

papers.title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on Improving the Performance of Contemporary Political Systems: An Analytical Study in Governance and Decision-Making
papers.authors: Sura Hashim Muhammed
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: Government digital transformation is an ever-expanding part of modern governance. Governments increasingly implement digital platforms, big-data analytics, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, digital identity systems and integrated information infrastructures. These developments can affect the delivery of public services as well as institutional coordination, citizen–government interaction, policy formulation and decision-making. This paper explores how digital transformation affects the performance of contemporary political systems, particularly in governance and governmental decision-making. It examines the potential of digital technologies to enhance administrative efficiency, institutional responsiveness, transparency, accountability, citizen engagement and evidence-based policy-making, together with the problems of cybersecurity, privacy, digital exclusion, algorithmic bias, institutional capacity and over-reliance on technology. The study is qualitative and analytical: it reviews and synthesizes the academic literature and the reports of international organizations. Digital transformation is not simply the conversion of traditional administrative procedures into electronic processes; it is institutional change in its own right. Current studies suggest that it requires organizational transformation, sound data governance, interoperability, an adequate legal framework, public-sector skills and accountability mechanisms. Mergel, Edelmann and Haug argue that digital transformation is not merely digitization but an organizational change that reshapes processes, services, culture and relations with stakeholders. Evidence from the OECD likewise shows that digital technologies and data can improve how governments respond and deliver services, but that implementation, evaluation, skills and governance remain challenges. The study concludes that digital transformation can improve the performance of the political system, provided that technological innovation is complemented by institutional reform, inclusive access, transparency, data protection, cybersecurity, human control and effective governance arrangements. Digital transformation should therefore be understood as a governance transformation in which technological capabilities are combined with institutional, legal, organizational and societal factors.

papers.title: Beyond the Black Box: Algorithmic Accountability and the Legal Regulation of Predictive Analytics and Machine Learning in India
papers.authors: Gayathri, Rajvendra Kumar Chaudhari
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: The proliferation of predictive analytics and machine-learning systems has transformed decision-making across banking, insurance, healthcare, employment, policing, welfare administration, education and advertising in India. Algorithms no longer merely inform human choices; with increasing frequency they determine outcomes that affect individuals’ rights, livelihoods and opportunities. This transformation has produced what is commonly described as the “black box” problem: decisions are generated through processes that are technically complex, commercially proprietary and cognitively opaque, leaving affected persons unable to understand, contest or seek redress against them. Algorithmic systems trained on historical data further risk reproducing and amplifying existing patterns of discrimination against already disadvantaged groups. India’s existing legal architecture, anchored principally in the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, offers meaningful safeguards for the processing of personal data but does not comprehensively regulate the algorithmic decisions that such data ultimately produces. Constitutional guarantees of equality and non-arbitrariness under Article 14 and of privacy, dignity and personal liberty under Article 21 supply an important normative foundation for extending accountability beyond data governance. This paper undertakes a doctrinal examination of algorithmic accountability in India through the interconnected lenses of privacy, equality, transparency, explainability, human oversight and effective remedy, and identifies significant regulatory gaps in the current framework. It concludes by proposing a rights-based, risk-sensitive and lifecycle-oriented framework for algorithmic accountability grounded in Indian constitutional principles rather than transplanted wholesale from foreign models.

papers.title: Impact of AI-Based Financial Advice on Investment Preferences and Risk Perception among Salaried Investors
papers.authors: Prathibha V Prathibha V, Pramod Kumar Pandey Pramod Kumar Pandey
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to deliver financial information, investment recommendations and portfolio decision support. This study examines the proposed impact of AI-based financial advice on investment preferences and risk perception among salaried investors. The framework treats perceived usefulness, perceived accuracy, trust, personalisation and transparency as dimensions of AI-based financial advice and tests their proposed relationships with investment preference and risk perception. A quantitative cross-sectional design using a structured five-point Likert questionnaire is proposed. For demonstration of the intended empirical reporting format, a synthetic dataset of 450 hypothetical salaried investors was generated and analysed using internal-consistency assessment and regression-style structural estimates. The simulated results indicate positive associations between the five AI-advice attributes and investment preference and negative associations with risk perception. These numerical findings are illustrative only and must not be represented as observations from real respondents. The study contributes a focused framework for future primary research on AI-assisted investment decision-making among salaried investors.

papers.title: Synergizing Momentum Trading, Artificial Intelligence, and Dual-Analysis Frameworks: A Case Study on Apple Inc. (AAPL)
papers.authors: Stephan Ludewig
papers.abstract: This study introduces a unified investment framework that integrates momentum trading strategies, artificial intelligence (AI) predictive engines, and a dual-layer approach encompassing technical analysis (TA) and fundamental analysis (FA). Utilizing Apple Inc. (AAPL) as a primary case study, we examine how machine learning architectures optimize market entry and exit timing by reconciling structural microeconomic metrics with short-term market psychology. The empirical evidence shows that while fundamental analysis establishes robust, long-term intrinsic value boundaries, AI-driven momentum indicators efficiently capture non-linear alpha and reduce drawdown periods. We provide explicit mathematical formulations for the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent network utilized as the core predictive engine and validate the framework using authentic historical quarterly financial disclosures from Apple up to mid-2026.

papers.title: Helpful Yet Risky: Senior EFL Students' Perceptions of ChatGPT Feedback in Academic Writing at a Vietnamese University
papers.authors: Vu Anh Tran
papers.journal: European Journal of Arts Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has entered English as a foreign language (EFL) writing classrooms faster than evidence about how learners construe it has accumulated. This study examined how senior English-major students at a Vietnamese public university perceive ChatGPT feedback on their academic writing. A cross-sectional descriptive survey with an embedded qualitative component combined a 15-item questionnaire – thirteen agreement items and two evaluation items – with written answers to three open-ended prompts from eight students in the same cohort. Thirty-six students responded and 30 complete cases were retained. No writing performance measure was collected, so no claim about learning gains is made. Benefit endorsement was highest for confidence in writing (M = 3.93) and for grammatical correction and academic vocabulary (both 76.7% agreement, M = 3.90), and lowest for organisation of ideas (60.0%, M = 3.67), though differences within this cluster are small relative to the sample precision. Risks were endorsed at least as strongly: 96.7% agreed that over-reliance might erode self-editing (M = 4.17), and 83.3% that ChatGPT revisions can make writing sound unlike their own (M = 4.07). Across the thirteen agreement items, means occupied a narrow range (3.67–4.17), indicating co-endorsement of benefits and risks rather than demonstrated statistical equivalence. The open-ended responses mirrored this pattern, portraying ChatGPT as a useful assistant, a threat to originality, and a tool requiring explicit rules. The pattern may reflect genuine ambivalence, acquiescent responding, or both; the present design cannot separate them. Implications are discussed for feedback literacy, classroom guidance, and instrument design.

papers.title: AI Tools and Language Learning Achievement: A Quasi-Experimental Study in Pakistani EFL Classrooms
papers.authors: Humaira Hamid, Zahoor Ahmed, Esha Qayyum, Muhammad Hashir Naeem, Hamid Ali Baloch
papers.abstract: English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms' incorporation of AI tools has been largely neglected in Pakistan. The effect of AI grammar tools on students' language learning achievement and language learning motivation were examined in this study. Pre-test post-test control group (quasi-experimental) design was used. A total of 180 9/10th Grade students from four Public schools participated in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The experimental group (n = 90) received 8 weeks of writing exercises with ChatGPT and Grammarly, whereas the control group (n = 90) did their writing using traditional methods. Data was obtained by using a Grammar Achievement Test and a Language Learning Motivation Questionnaire (LLMQ) and analyzed using ANCOVA, paired-samples t-test, and AMOS: Language Structural Equation Modeling. The theoretical model chosen was the Input Hypothesis and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The experimental group achieved significantly higher post-test grammar scores (M = 72.4, p < .001, partial η² = .31) and there was a significant increase in motivation scores as well. The findings of SEM showed that perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use had positive prediction for learning achievement with student engagement as a mediator. There were no significant ethical issues reported but teachers reported training needs. This study is one of the first experimental studies on the use of AI tools in EFL context in Pakistan. The results were conducive to the inclusion of AI tools in the Single National Curriculum along with teacher training. Public schools and the implications of SDG 4 and digital equity are discussed.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Ethics In Communication Studies: A Systematic Literature Review Of Sinta 2–3 Journals In Indonesia, 2023–2024
papers.authors: Sekartaji Anisa Putri
papers.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly permeating daily lives, particularly in the field of communication. Therefore, the ethics of using artificial intelligence in the field of communication require further investigation. Looking at the importance of this matter, the author interested in researching more deeply regarding ethics about the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of Communication Science through systematic literature review (SLR). This study aims to examine publications in reputable Indonesian communication science journals regarding the phenomenon of artificial intelligence and the ethics of its use. A systematic literature review was conducted on reputable communication science journals listed in the SINTA database. From a total of 10,478 journals in the SINTA database, a selection process was carried out using keywords "communication" and applying SINTA 2 and SINTA 3 filters. Result yielded 24 SINTA 2 and 43 SINTA 3 communication science journals. Across these 67 communication science journals, a total of 3,657 articles were published during 2023–2024. However, from all of the publications, only four representing 0.1% of the total contained "ethics" and "artificial intelligence" keywords. From four papers listed, one article was excluded in the subsequent qualitative analysis stage because it did not employ communication science methodologies. Consequently, the percentage dropped to 0.08%. In conclusion, there are very few publications addressing artificial intelligence and ethics within the scope of communication science studies in reputable communication science journal (SINTA 2 and SINTA 3) during 2023–2024 period. However, it is important to acknowledge the discussions surrounding ethical issues in the field of communication science. Findings reveal there is an emphasis in AI ethical issues about AI's capacity for data verification, its understanding of relevant ethical standards, and its accountability, particularly in journalism. As well as the negative social impact of job losses from AI adoption.

papers.title: Exploring EFL Learners' Attitudes Toward ChatGPT for English Writing: The Role of Contextual Factors
papers.authors: Sarah S. Alobaidi, Hanadi Abdulrahman Khadawardi
papers.journal: International Journal of English Language Education
papers.abstract: This study investigates EFL learners’ attitudes toward using ChatGPT for English writing and examines the extent to which institutional and teacher-related factors predict these attitudes. In this quantitative study, a survey questionnaire was administered to 136 preparatory-year EFL students in a Saudi higher-education context. Descriptive analysis indicated that learners held generally positive attitudes toward ChatGPT for English writing. Participants also reported moderately positive perceptions of institutional support and teachers’ attitudes, although limited training and classroom integration were noted. Multiple regression analysis revealed that institution-related factors significantly predicted learners’ attitudes toward ChatGPT use, whereas teacher-related factors did not demonstrate a unique predictive contribution when both variables were considered simultaneously. The study contributes empirical evidence from the Saudi EFL context and extends prior descriptive research by identifying contextual predictors of attitudes toward AI-assisted writing. Implications emphasize the importance of clear institutional policies, AI literacy initiatives, and targeted teacher training to support responsible integration of ChatGPT in language learning.

papers.title: Model Disclosure in Composed AI Systems — Census #1 of the Model Disclosure Index (MDI) programme: whether routers and orchestrators name the model that answered
papers.authors: Shawn Scanlon, Sentient Index Labs & Technology
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: A composed system routes a request among several models rather than answering with one, and they are increasingly what enterprises deploy. This census asks something narrow that appears not to have been measured: when you ask one a question, does it tell you what answered? Across three commercially available systems, the model field every portable client reads returned a name belonging to no model at all. One answered a short question using three invocations of two different companies' models and disclosed the fact only in a vendor extension outside the standard interface; another disclosed nothing anywhere. Asked the same question five times, one system used five different combinations of models costing between 3,558 and 13,008 tokens, and four blind judges scored the most expensive draw the lowest of the five. The paper reports what an audit log therefore does not contain, states the limits of a single census, and declines — in both directions — to draw any conclusion about intent. This document is fixed: corrections are issued as new versions under the same identifier. Authorship. Prepared by Sentient Index Labs & Technology. During the preparation of this work, the author used Claude (Anthropic) to draft the text and run the analyses; every figure is derived from the census's own stored responses and checked against them. The author directed the work and is responsible for the content.

papers.authors: Avery Chapman
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Learn three essential metrics for radiology AI: independent external AUROC, prespecified sensitivity, and calibration before routine clinical use. papers.title: Rewriting the Space of the Possible Recursive Creativity as Object–Space Coevolution
papers.authors: Cristhian Mauricio Beltrán Calderón
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Creativity is ordinarily assessed through the novelty and value of an output. This article develops a cumulative theoretical extension in which recursive creativity is defined as a traceable relation between produced objects and the design space that governs their generation, evaluation, and reproduction. A creative system is represented as St = ⟨Vt, Et, Rt⟩ (variation, evaluation, reproduction), with evolution St+1 = Φt(St, Ot, Xt). The framework distinguishes degree-0 activity within a substantively fixed space, degree-1 transformation of V, E, or R, and degree-2 transformation of the rule Φ by which the space is itself transformed, under explicit safeguards against self-validation and unbounded meta-regression. It introduces five proposed diagnostics: effective diversity or coverage (H), external evaluative independence (εE), reproductive resistance (μR), correctability (K), and maturity (M). The theory is operationalized for artificial-intelligence retraining through a provenance-based Recursive Creativity Record (RCR), which makes explicit how outputs become evidence that changes training procedures, evaluation criteria, or reproduction conditions. Within the General Theory of Technology, recursive creativity is formulated as Ti → Cr → Tj, a mechanism of technogenesis. Eight propositions with falsification conditions and a minimum three-condition empirical design are stated. The article does not claim empirical validation; its contribution is a disciplined, auditable architecture linking object–space coevolution, second-order design, technological reproduction, and AI retraining.

papers.title: PEDAGOGICAL OPPORTUNITIES OF USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE MANAGEMENT OF VOCATIONAL EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
papers.authors: Nematova Zarina Furqat qizi
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the pedagogical opportunities of using artificial intelligence technologies in the management of vocational education institutions. It examines the potential of artificial intelligence for educational planning, coordination of teachers’ activities, monitoring learners’ performance, analyzing educational outcomes, and supporting management decisions. Particular attention is given to the organizational and pedagogical conditions required for the effective integration of artificial intelligence technologies into vocational education management. The study demonstrates that the use of artificial intelligence can contribute to improving the efficiency, timeliness, and data-based nature of management processes. At the same time, pedagogical appropriateness, data security, the development of teachers’ digital competence, and human oversight are identified as important conditions for the responsible and effective use of artificial intelligence.
