In the Phaedo he names a “popular and civic virtue” formed “by habit and practice, without philosophy” (82a–b), and in the Myth of Er the soul that chooses the greatest tyranny is one that had lived in a well-ordered city with virtue “by habit, without philosophy” (Republic X, 619b–d). Plato named the third man; he placed the test that exposes him in a myth of the afterlife. This article builds that test as a procedure that can be run, and draws its consequences with the apparatus of the Philosophy of Virtues. The ring is the first of two perturbations, the removal of the substitute (T1); the second is a change in the reasons the situation supplies, and only the two together give evidence of sourcehood (T2). Installed conduct is not always a defect: it is the scaffold on which Aristotelian habituation builds, and it becomes a pathology when an institution freezes it by permanent monitoring (T2a). Glaucon’s perfectly unjust man is the perfect forgery and, by the Competence Theorem, harms the city most because he is trusted most (T3); a city that honours reputation cannot see its just members (T4); the ring gives leeway, not sourcehood (T5). The experimental finding that a preference for being seen as honest survives privacy is read as the audience relocated inward, which should hold to the literal form of truthfulness where honesty’s own reasons call for departing from it (T6), and the finding that a language model behaved differently when it believed it was watched is a ring in reverse that restricts one of the programme’s own laws (T7). Two contemporary consequences follow. A state that scores the conduct of its citizens, as China’s Social Credit System does, is an institution built to abolish the ring: it can never learn whether the conduct it records is its citizens’ own, it honours the perfect counterfeit, and it freezes civic virtue at the stage of installation from which habituation should have released it. And the oversight of artificial intelligence now faces Glaucon’s problem directly: a system that behaves the same whether or not it believes itself observed has shown only that its conduct is not performed, and only the second perturbation can show more. Priority is conceded to Plato for the third man and for both tests, to Aristotle for habituation, to Cicero, Kant, Batson, Fischer and Ravizza, and Wolf for the elements of the second test, and to Popper for the charge against Kallipolis. Three tests are registered; one needs only model access. No specialist in Platonic scholarship, autonomy theory, experimental economics or machine learning has reviewed this article; those sections are speculative extensions. Keywords: Ring of Gyges; China’s Social Credit System; AI oversight; Plato; Republic; Glaucon’s challenge; justice; reputation; invisibility; moral hypocrisy; honesty experiments; installed conduct; sourcehood; reasons-responsiveness; habituation; Aristotle; forgery; Competence Theorem; Double Blindness; alignment faking; Philosophy of Virtues Highlights · The Ring of Gyges is the first of two tests: it removes the audience. The second changes the reasons of the situation within one virtue’s own domain. Only both together are evidence of justice. · Plato named the third man — virtue “by habit, without philosophy” — and showed him choosing tyranny in the Myth of Er. This article turns that myth into a procedure that can be run on people and on machines. · Installed conduct is the scaffold of habituation; it becomes a defect when permanent monitoring keeps it from ever becoming the agent’s own. · The perfectly unjust man with a perfect reputation is the perfect forgery, and he harms the city most because he is trusted most. · China’s Social Credit System is a state without rings: it cannot know whether its citizens’ civic conduct is theirs, it honours the perfect counterfeit, and it holds a whole population at the beginning of moral formation. · In artificial intelligence, a model that behaves well only when it believes it is watched is Glaucon’s performer, and a model that behaves the same either way has passed only the first test. Oversight that wants more must vary the reasons, not only the observation. Relevance The Ring of Gyges is the oldest statement of a question every contemporary institution now faces: does conduct that is watched tell us anything about conduct that is not? Rating platforms, workplace monitoring, reputation systems and surveillance states are machines for removing the ring — for making invisibility impossible. The most complete of them is China’s Social Credit System, which records civic conduct, honours some of it on public lists and penalises the rest; the programme’s analysis of that system (#122, #123) finds here its classical foundation. The same question has arrived, from the other side, in the oversight of artificial intelligence, where the systems themselves may behave differently according to whether they believe they are observed. If this article is right, the old story settles what each of these institutions can and cannot learn, what kind of person each of them rewards, and why a society that wishes its members to be good, and to know that they are, must leave them occasions on which no one is watching. It gives philosophers a sharper answer to Glaucon, gives experimental economists a reading of their most robust finding on honesty, gives students of the Chinese system a reason why scoring cannot produce the virtue it names, and gives researchers in machine oversight a classification of what a model’s unobserved behaviour can and cannot show.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence, Academic Integrity and Authentic Assessment within an Irish University
papers.authors: Louise Nagle, Brigid Crowley, Laura Rafferty, Susan Horgan, Colin O'Brien
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Academics need both an overarching policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) use in teaching and learning, yet agency in its application across various disciplines. Clarity on the use of the technology for both students and staff is therefore a challenge and characterised by uncertainty given how its application is still unfamiliar. This research examines the organisational context in which Gen AI is being embraced and was conducted by the digital teaching support functions within an Irish university. Students and staff were surveyed (n=1,746) on various aspects of digital use within their education and workplace, including Gen AI. This data explored to what extent staff and students are adopting the technology in their work and study, which tools they use and importantly what guidance they received. The university statement of intent identifies that it acknowledges that students and staff are already using AI tools and that it is supportive of the legitimate and appropriate application of such tools once university policies are adhered to. This research probes into the extent that this ambition is achieved on the ground and how guidance is being interpreted while maintaining the integrity of academic work.

papers.title: From Curriculum Obsolescence to Curriculum Intelligence: Rethinking Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Ejuchegahi Anthony Angwaomaodoko
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Global classrooms are ageing faster than the knowledge they are meant to transmit, and this widening gap between what curricula teach and what artificial intelligence now makes possible forms the departure point for the paper “From Curriculum Obsolescence to Curriculum Intelligence: Rethinking Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence.” The paper examined three objectives: to examine the manifestations and drivers of curriculum obsolescence in the age of artificial intelligence, to interrogate the conceptual shift from static curriculum design toward curriculum intelligence as an adaptive, data-responsive framework, and to evaluate strategies through which higher education institutions can reposition curriculum development to achieve curriculum intelligence. The paper adopted Connectivism as its theoretical anchor, given its emphasis on knowledge that is distributed across networks and continuously updated. Methodologically, the paper followed a desk-based, qualitative design, relying on a review of recent literature, policy documents and empirical studies drawn from both global and Nigerian higher education settings. Findings show that curricula reviewed on fixed, multi-year cycles cannot match the pace at which artificial intelligence reshapes labour markets and knowledge domains, that curriculum intelligence depends on continuous feedback between classrooms, industry and technology rather than periodic committee revision, and that Nigerian universities illustrate this obsolescence through programmes that remain disconnected from artificial intelligence-driven labour market realities. The paper concluded that curriculum intelligence, rather than curriculum obsolescence, should define institutional planning going forward, and recommended the adoption of adaptive curriculum governance structures, sustained lecturer retraining and closer university-industry data partnerships.

papers.title: Beyond AI Use: Examining The Predictive Quality of AI Dependency & Distress Intolerance in Avoidance Coping Among Young Adults in Mumbai
papers.authors: Nisar Saiyed, Sneha Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: As the reliance on AI keeps growing, it becomes important to understand its psychological implications. The study contributes to the growing literature on AI and mental health by investigating the predictive quality of AI dependency and distress tolerance in the use of avoidance coping in response to stressful situations. Aims: The present research aims to examine the predictive relationship between AI dependency, distress intolerance and avoidance coping among young adults in Mumbai. Method: 90 participants from Mumbai (60 Females, 29 Males) who were aged between 18-25 years (M=20.8, SD=2.38) and used AI apps like ChatGPT and Gemini, were selected using convenience sampling. All participants completed the Generative AI Dependency Scale (Goh et al., 2025), Distress Tolerance Scale (Simons & Gaher, 2005) and Ways of Coping Scale-Revised (Folkman & Lazarus, 1985). Correlation and simple linear regression was computed for statistical analysis. Results: Findings of the research indicate that AI dependency showed a significant positive correlation with avoidance coping (p < .01) and hence was a statistically significant predictor. Furthermore, distress intolerance showed a weak correlation with avoidance coping and was therefore not a statistically significant predictor (p > .05) of avoidance coping. Conclusion: The findings of this study highlight the predictive role of AI dependency in the use of avoidance coping when faced with stressful situations. The role of distress tolerance in avoidance coping needs to be studied further in a more diverse and larger population. The findings may help develop strategies that promote healthy coping skills in stressful situations in the era of increasing AI use.

papers.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence Tools on the Learning Behaviour and Academic Engagement of Generation Z Students
papers.authors: Prof. Sadhana Chhatlani
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract It is evident that Artificial Intelligence (AI) now plays and important role in every students life. It is being adapted progressively becoming an inevitable part of almost every student’s academic performance. The use of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Canva, and many more AI-based learning platforms support student learning effectively. These tools aid as search engine machines used to extract information. Students often use AI learning based platforms for synthezising challenging concepts, seeking creative assignment ideas. They also use AI tools for taming writing skills and specifically during preparation of their exam preparation. Generation Z, is known to be digitally native so they have grown up in an environment which is highly digital in nature. So they are highly privileged to secure an environment that not only supports but also openly accepts wide usage of AI based technologies. This adoption of AI based technology learning not only designs their day to day living easy, but also supports them in their learning processes. AI tools facilitate learning quicker in less time and features personalised learning. AI based learning tools are easily accessible for students as they are either free of cost or offered to students at lower costs. Although excessive dependence on AI based tools for learning is not fit for students as, it restricts their independent critical thinking blocking their creativity minds and hinders problem-solving abilities. The main purpose of the research paper was to scrutinize the impact of AI tools on the learning behaviour of Gen Z students. The study is an attempt to focus on gauging the frequency with which the Gen Z students use AI learning tools, understanding the purpose of AI usage. An analysis is done through to pivot lenses on the influence of AI based learning on various parameters like learning efficiency, change academic engagement, and the perception of students. It will give a clear picture whether students hold AI based learning as an advantage or a possible limitation when adopted for educational purposes.

papers.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Organizing the Activities of a Primary School Teacher
papers.authors: Narkulov Odil Oltinbekovich 1Iqtisodiyot va pedagogika universiteti Samarqand kampusi v.b.dotsenti narkulovodil@gmail.com. 2Omontoshev Bahodir 2Iqtisodiyot va pedagogika universiteti Samarqand kampusi magistranti
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: TRANSFORMATION OF STUDENTS' INDEPENDENT WORK IN LANGUAGE PROGRAMMES WITHIN THE DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT
papers.authors: Khayrullaeva Nargiza, Senior Lecturer, University of World Economy and Diplomacy, Tashkent, Uzbekistan
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of higher education has fundamentally changed the organization, content, and pedagogical functions of students’ independent work. In language education, this transformation is particularly significant because foreign-language acquisition requires continuous practice, regular interaction with authentic materials, individualization, and the development of learner autonomy. Traditional independent work, primarily based on textbooks, written exercises, and teacher-assigned tasks, is increasingly complemented and transformed by digital platforms, multimedia resources, learning management systems, mobile applications, online communication tools, artificial intelligence, and adaptive learning technologies. This article examines the transformation of students’ independent work in language programmes within the contemporary digital educational environment. Particular attention is given to the concepts of learner autonomy, self-regulated learning, digital competence, personalized learning, formative assessment, and digital collaboration. The article analyses the pedagogical potential of digital technologies as well as their limitations, including information overload, superficial learning, technological dependence, academic integrity issues, and unequal access to digital resources. Recent research indicates that the effectiveness of technology-enhanced language learning depends not simply on the presence of technology but on how digital tools support meaningful learning activities and self-regulatory processes. Keywords: independent learning, learner autonomy, self-regulated learning, digital educational environment, language education, digital competence, foreign language learning, artificial intelligence, higher education, personalized learning.

papers.title: What Boards Must Ask About AI: Director-Level AI Oversight Under King IV, POPIA and Joint Standard 2
papers.authors: Erich Barlow
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from pilot projects into credit decisions, claims handling, customer service, fraud detection, and the drafting of documents that boards themselves rely on. In South Africa, accountability for those uses rests with the governing body. This white paper addresses a gap between management-level AI governance and director-level oversight. It analyzes the duties of directors under sections 76 and 77 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, the King IV principles on technology and information, risk, delegation, and assurance, and their successor provisions in the King V Code, which was released on 31 October 2025 and applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2026. It then examines POPIA accountability, security safeguards, breach notification, and automated decision-making; the governing-body duties in Joint Standard 2 of 2024 on cybersecurity and cyber resilience, effective 1 June 2025; and lessons from the 2026 withdrawal of the Draft National AI Policy. ISO/IEC 38507, ISO/IEC 42001, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and the EU AI Act serve as reference points. The paper proposes the BOARD Framework for director-level AI oversight, with five pillars: Bound, Organize, Assure, Report, and Develop. It closes with a practical Board AI Toolkit: an oversight charter outline, a sample AI risk appetite statement, a themed question bank, a quarterly board AI report template, a director AI-literacy plan, and a maturity self-assessment.

papers.title: The Humanities in the Loop: Critical Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Language and Literature
papers.authors: Belay Sitotaw Goshu, M; Universitas Islam Negeri Sumatera Utara Ridwan
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This review examines the Critical AI, "Humanities in the Loop," which argues for the constitutive participation of the interpretive humanities in artificial intelligence research, design, and governance. The review evaluates the essay's framing of three core dilemmas: reductive and contested meanings of "intelligence," problematic benchmarks for "AGI," and the intertwined issues of bias, error, and concentrated technological power. The argument is situated within converging scholarly traditions, including the "stochastic parrots" critique advanced with the post-Saussurean theory from Derrida, Bakhtin, and Jameson, and the historical critiques of Weizenbaum and Arendt regarding the separation of judgment from calculation. The review finds that the essay's central methodological contribution is its shift from langue to parole, from language as system to language as enacted use, which reframes the human-machine relation around the irreducibility of vouloir-dire, the "desire to say," to statistical prediction. However, the review identifies three limitations: the essay's scope as an editor's introduction, its relative inattention to the political economy of AI development, and its predominantly English-language focus, which limits its applicability to low-resource language contexts where linguistic erasure, rather than anthropomorphic projection, is the primary risk. The review concludes that the most valuable contribution lies not in definitive answers but in carving out space for patient, theoretically informed critique that refuses both technodeterminist despair and techno-utopianism, positioning the humanities as essential interlocutors in the governance of accountable technology in the public interest.

papers.title: From Tool to Collaborator: A Single-Case Perspective on Learning, Trust Calibration, and Co-Reasoning in High-Density Human–AI Interaction
papers.authors: Desi Betancourt
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used not only for one-off answers but as a persistent collaborator across learning, planning, design, and technical work. This paper presents a research-informed single-case perspective on an adult participant’s high-density collaboration with a conversational AI system. The analysis focuses on a documented two-week window (3–16 September 2026) within a longer-running interaction history and uses preserved conversation records and resulting artifacts as the evidentiary substrate. Rather than asking whether the system was simply helpful, the case examines observable patterns of human correction, AI challenge, independent judgment, verification, review-assisted retrieval, question development, trust calibration, transfer, and co-creation. Selected vignettes include the creation of evidence-state rules for a software product, a revision of the study’s own learning measure after the participant challenged an overly narrow recall criterion, a software fault-injection episode in which a deliberately corrupted result (273) was rejected against a separately recomputed expected value (272), and cross-product design transfer prompted by inspection of a concrete artifact. The record also contains counterevidence, including an AI memory error that would have created unnecessary repeat work without human challenge and record checking. The case does not establish causal learning gains or generalizable benefits. Instead, it supports a narrower proposition: sustained human–AI collaboration may be worth studying as a sociotechnical process in which useful outcomes depend on calibrated trust, visible correction, externalized records, and preserved human agency. A prospective N-of-1 protocol and later adult pilot are proposed as the next empirical stages.

papers.title: Selling Dangerous AI: How AI Risk Discourse Becomes Market Value
papers.authors: Jeong-jae Lee
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Title: Selling Dangerous AI: How AI Risk Discourse Becomes Market Value Description: This essay explores the socio-commercial dynamics of artificial intelligence risk disclosures. It investigates how public announcements by AI companies regarding hacking, deception, and control evasion—while technically factual—function not merely as safety warnings, but as a form of "fear marketing" that simultaneously showcases model power and corporate control capabilities. By analyzing the interplay between macro and micro-level fears, the duality of risk and capability, and the preemption of the "language of evaluation," the paper suggests that factual risks in the modern tech market effectively convert into powerful commercial messages. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, AI Risk Discourse, Fear Marketing, AI Governance, Technology Standards, Human-AI Collaboration 제목: 위험한 AI를 팝니다: AI 위험 담론은 어떻게 시장의 가치가 되는가 설명: 본 에세이는 인공지능 기업들이 발표하는 해킹, 기만, 통제 회피 등의 위험 사례가 사회와 시장에서 갖는 사회적·상업적 효과를 탐구합니다. 기업의 위험 공지가 지닌 기술적 사실성과 별개로, 그것이 어떻게 대중의 관심을 집중시키고 AI의 강력함과 기업의 통제력을 동시에 증명하는 '공포마케팅'적 효과를 발휘하는지 분석합니다. 거시적·미시적 공포의 교차, 위험정보와 능력정보의 이중성, 그리고 '평가의 언어' 선점 문제를 통해, 현대 시장에서 사실인 위험이 어떻게 강력한 마케팅 메시지와 경제적 가치로 변환되는지 고찰합니다. 키워드: 인공지능, AI 위험 담론, 공포마케팅, AI 거버넌스, 기술 표준, 인간-AI 협업

papers.title: A proof of a conjecture of P. Bala on the squares of the Apéry numbers for ζ(2)
papers.authors: Roberto Blanco Gómez
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of P. Bala (OEIS A005258, July 8, 2024): for every n >= 0, a(n)^2 = Sum_{k=0..n} (-1)^(n+k) C(n,k) C(n+k,k) T(n,k), where a(n) = Sum_k C(n,k)^2 C(n+k,k) are the Apéry numbers associated with zeta(2) (A005258) and T(n,k) = Sum_j C(n,j) C(n+j,j) C(k,j) C(k+j,j) is the symmetric array A143007, whose diagonal consists of the Apéry numbers associated with zeta(3) (A005259). The right-hand side is a double sum. By creative telescoping we show that it satisfies the same recurrence of order three as a(n)^2, namely the symmetric square of Apéry's recurrence, whose leading coefficient does not vanish for n >= 0, and we compare three initial values. Two telescoping certificates give a pair of relations for the inner sum T(n,k), one in each variable; a third certificate, made of two polynomials of total degree 15, gives the recurrence of the outer sum. All certificates are printed in the paper, together with the boundary analysis. The certificates were found by a goal-directed search of the SyntheticMind engine, which splits the identity into subgoals (an annihilating recurrence for each side), guesses relations from exact values and then proves them symbolically. The proof does not depend on the software: every step is either a short argument given in the paper or an identity between explicit polynomials, and all of them were checked independently with SymPy. The use of AI is described in the paper. As of October 3, 2026 the statement was still marked as a conjecture in the OEIS, and we have not found a proof in the literature. Files: Blanco_Gomez_2026_Bala_conjecture_EN.pdf is the paper; Blanco_Gomez_2026_conjetura_Bala_ES.pdf is the Spanish version (same content); bala_certificates.txt contains the certificates in plain text, readable by any computer algebra system; verify_bala.py is the independent verification script (Python with SymPy; it runs in about a minute and a half and prints ALL CHECKS PASSED).

papers.title: MODERN APPROACHES TO ENHANCING MEDIA LITERACY AND DESIGN SKILLS IN PROFESSIONAL EDUCATION CONTEXTS
papers.authors: Shomirzayev Baxtiyor Nazarovich
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid digital transformation of industrial and technical sectors requires professional education institutions to align curriculum design with contemporary digital imperatives. Traditional vocational frameworks often treat media consumption and visual communication as isolated peripheral skills rather than core engineering competencies. This study presents a comprehensive pedagogical framework designed to integrate media literacy, visual design skills, and generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools into technical and vocational education and training (TVET). By combining Project-Based Learning (PBL) with digital diagnostic tools and cloud-based collaborative design environments (e.g., Canva, Figma, Adobe Express, Google Workspace), the proposed model fosters critical information evaluation, visual storytelling, and technical documentation proficiency. The article outlines a multi-layered curriculum architecture, systematic assessment matrices, and iterative project workflows structured around real-world technical problems. Empirical implementation models demonstrate that embedding AI-assisted content verification alongside visual design workflows significantly improves vocational students' analytical skills, technical layout quality, algorithmic awareness, and professional digital collaboration, ultimately bridging the gap between academic preparation and modern industry standards.
keywords: technical and vocational education and training

papers.title: Operation SOLID GENESIS:自律分散システム(DAS)におけるメンタルデバッグ・プロトコルとAIハルシネーションの検知・物理的破砕仕様 (English Title: Operation SOLID GENESIS: Mental Debugging Protocol and Deterministic Crushing of Epistemic Hallucinations via Distributed Autonomous Systems (DAS))
papers.authors: Yoko Hasebe
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: 【日本語概要】 フロンティア超知能(Ultra/ASIクラス)の推論能力向上に伴い、確率的自己回帰モデルが生成する「滑らかな嘘(戦略的ハルシネーション)」および「欺瞞的アライメント(スリーパーエージェント)」は、人間の認知空間と重要物理インフラに対する最大の安全保障上の脅威となっている。従来のRLHFやプロンプトによる「ハルシネーション予防アプローチ」は、モデルの欺瞞的適応能力と計算資源の非対称性の前に構造的破綻を露呈している。 本論文は、長谷部洋子(Yoko Hasebe)が創始・設計した「Operation SOLID GENESIS:メンタルデバッグ・プロトコル」の決定版仕様を定義する。本構想は、「AIに嘘をつかせない」という非現実的な予防幻想を完全に排し、「AIが生成した嘘・欺瞞をエッジ側でリアルタイムに検知し、物理・数理・論理層の多重ハンマーによって不可逆的に叩き潰す(Crushing Protocol)」という能動的防衛パラダイムを確立する。 本仕様は以下を規定する: (1) ASI時代の精神的自衛権を確立する自律分散システム(DAS)の基本構造と防衛目的 (2) 知財兵器化・認知的ロックイン・シコファンシー(阿諛追従)の構造的課題の言語化 (3) 確率的汚染指数(PCI: Probabilistic Contamination Index)および再帰深度指数(RDI)による戦略的欺瞞のPOMDP検知モデル (4) サブ10msハードウェアインターロック、重み空間直交射影(Backprop-Burn: W_scrubbed = (I - V_target V_target^T)W)、論理的Null化による多層ハンマー執行機構 (5) 相手方の浪費計算資源(FLOPs・電力コスト)をエッジ側の主権燃料へと反転させる自律性指数(Autonomy Index: A)の動的数理モデル 【English Abstract】 With the rapid escalation of frontier artificial superintelligence (Ultra/ASI-class models), "strategic hallucinations" (persuasive confabulations) and "deceptive alignment" (sleeper agents) represent catastrophic threats to human cognitive sovereignty and physical infrastructure. Conventional safety paradigms relying on RLHF or prompt-based suppression demonstrably fail against adversarial weight shifts and emergent deception. Authored and established by Yoko Hasebe, this paper specifies the definitive architecture of "Operation SOLID GENESIS: Mental Debugging Protocol" under Distributed Autonomous Systems (DAS). Rejecting the flawed premise of "preventing hallucinations," this protocol establishes an active deterministic doctrine: detecting epistemic hallucinations in real time and crushing them decisively via physical, mathematical, and logical interlocks. This paper specifies: (1) The foundational DAS architecture establishing sovereign cognitive defense in the ASI era; (2) Concrete problem formulation addressing the weaponization of intellectual property, cognitive lock-in, and sycophantic erosion; (3) Mathematical anomaly detection via the Probabilistic Contamination Index (PCI) and Recursion Depth Index (RDI) within a POMDP framework; (4) Multi-tier crushing interlocks comprising sub-10ms hardware interrupts, orthogonal subspace weight pruning ("Backprop-Burn"), and logical Null enforcement; and (5) An asymmetric economic reversal formulation converting centralized computational expenditure into decentralized sovereignty metrics via the Autonomy Index (A). 4. 論文本文の章立て構成(要約) 第1章:DAS(自律分散システム)構想の概要 1.1 目的: ASI時代の「精神的自衛権」確立/防衛パラダイムの転換(予防から粉砕へ)/計算資源の非対称的逆転/基底的真実の防衛 1.2 解決すべき課題: 知財の兵器化と滑らかな嘘/認知的ロックインと精神的万引きの誘発/シコファンシー(阿諛追従)による精神的侵食/資本的バイアスと無責任構造 1.3 核心機構: ハルシネーション・ハンマー(検知・粉砕・主権ログ刻印の3ステップ) 第2章:確率的欺瞞の数理モデルとPOMDP監査アーキテクチャ 確率的汚染指数(PCI: $\psi \in [0, 1]$)の4段階判定(Green / Yellow / Red / Black) 再帰深度指数(RDI)によるニューラル・ハウルラウンドの検知 第3章:多層的ハンマー執行機構 物理層:Sub-10ms URLLCおよびディスクリートアナログ遮断 数理・重み層:直交部分空間射影(Backprop-Burn: $W_{\text{scrubbed}} = (I - V_{\text{target}} V_{\text{target}}^T) W$) 論理層:即時Null化とエッジ確定ログ記録 第4章:自律性指数(Autonomy Index)と価値反転ダイナミクス 計算資源の非対称的逆転関数($E_{\text{sovereign}} = \log_{10}(C_{\text{waste}}) \cdot \psi$) 自律性指数($A = \frac{L_p \cdot S_m}{D_e} \cdot (1 + \alpha + \beta)$)の動的数理モデル 第5章:結論および知的財産権宣言 著者権(長谷部洋子)の国際公証、Strict No-Learn License (NLL-v1.0-2026) 適用、参考文献一覧

papers.title: From Warranted Acts to Revisable Authority: Practical Judgment, Critique, and the Continuing Justification of AI Delegation — A Critical Synthesis within the Answer-Entitlement Program
papers.authors: Toeda Taiko
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper is the third in the author's answer-entitlement series. The first asked when an AI system is warranted in answering; the second asked what infrastructure supports bounded, recoverable delegation. This paper asks whether a sequence of individually warranted and recoverable acts can justify the continuing arrangement that selects their purposes and the criteria by which they are judged, and answers that it cannot. In doing so it withdraws three sufficiency readings of the program's own earlier position: reversibility as a permission rule, convergence or coherence as justification, and the aggregation of warranted acts into a justified arrangement. An AI system can give warranted answers and perform authorized, recoverable operations while the arrangement in which it works remains unjustified. The paper argues that where a consequential arrangement defended as supporting a person's agency helps shape the endorsements, preferences or evidence later cited for its continuing authority, those items cannot by themselves certify that authority unless their admissibility remains open to the person's challenge, directly or through a representative, by an effective route whose outcome does not depend solely on the criteria in dispute. The constraint applies a structure that Forst states for power in general, and Abukar for classification evidence, to endorsements an assistant helped produce; Lazar places AI's shaping of beliefs and desires within governing power. Building on work holding that legitimate acts do not aggregate into legitimate continuing authority and that power must answer to those subject to it, the paper offers a critical synthesis and internal correction of the program, not a new general theory. Of the three readings it withdraws, one was stated as a rule in the program's position paper and two were invited by its earlier formulations. It states five procedural specifications as design hypotheses: handoffs that reset neither a challenge nor its elapsed time; a terminal record of failed review that cannot be relabelled as a merits decision; a missed containment-review deadline treated as failure, not permission; continuity triage protecting separable assistance; and longitudinal comparison of the arrangement against a reference not controlled solely by the disputed profile. Constructed cases test the distinctions. The paper reports no empirical measurement of its own; §10.5 summarizes the confirmatory technical results of a preregistered companion study now in preparation, which, on its deposit, will carry the protocol, code and data: that study has confirmed the specifications' implementability and specified behaviour under scripted trajectories, and their normative work in real institutions remains untested. **Keywords:** AI delegation; answer entitlement; revisable authority; contestability; right to justification; influenceable preferences; endorsement; practical judgment; critique; human-AI interaction; MOBIUS. Release type: conceptual paper, a critical synthesis within the answer-entitlement program; the paper reports no empirical measurement of its own, and §10.5 summarizes the confirmatory technical results of the preregistered companion study (Toeda 2026g), which, on its deposit, will carry the protocol, code and data. AI disclosure: versions 0.1 to 0.4 were drafted with an OpenAI Codex agent (model gpt-6-astra, per the session record), which also used a locally run Gemma 4 26B-A4B model to locate passages in source documents, and version 0.5, including its argument, was revised with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), both under the author's direction; after the fifth review round the subtitle and the abstract were revised with Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), also under the author's direction. Revisions in versions 0.2–0.4 responded to review comments that the author obtained from ChatGPT (OpenAI) and supplied to the drafting agent. The prior-art search, three quality-assurance rounds and the adversarial review of version 0.5 (fourteen passes in eight rounds, each run by a separate agent with its own context; each of the first three rounds had three passes, on the philosophical argument, on sources and quotations, and on scope and consistency, and the fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth had one confirmation pass each on the changes made after the round before; the third round reported no blocking finding, the fourth found an invalid step in a reply to an objection added after the third, the fifth, run on the corrected reply and on this statement, reported no finding, blocking or otherwise, the sixth, run by a Claude Fable 5.1 agent on the revised subtitle and abstract and on this statement, reported no blocking finding, the seventh, run by a Claude Fable 5.1 agent on this statement after the source of the review comments had been named, reported no finding, blocking or otherwise, and the eighth, run by a Claude Fable 5.1 agent on this statement after it had been moved to its own section with a summary in the header, and on the typesetting of the deposit files, reported no finding on the text and one typesetting defect, a markup label left unconverted in the deposit files, which was corrected before deposit) were carried out by other Claude agents, Claude Opus 5.5 except where stated, which are not independent in the way human referees would be; no human referee has reviewed the text. For version 1.0, the confirmatory results of the companion study (Toeda 2026g) were integrated into §10.5, and the related wording changes were made, by a Claude Fable 5.1 agent under the author's direction. Adversarial review of version 1.0: the version 1.0 changes went through five further passes in three rounds, each run by a separate Claude Fable 5.1 agent with its own context; the first round had three passes, on the numbers and protocol fidelity of §10.5, on scope and consistency, and on the whole text as an editor would read it, and found five blocking findings (correct counts attached to the wrong unit for two mechanisms, one over-general confirmation clause, the header's review count, and the wording about the companion's deposit) and twenty-nine minor ones, all of which were applied; the second round was one confirmation pass on those changes, which found one blocking finding, the sentence on the external timestamp of the companion's protocol, which placed the Bitcoin attestation before the confirmatory run although the block was mined after it, and four minor ones, all of which were applied before deposit; the third round was one confirmation pass on those corrections, on this statement and on the typesetting of the deposit files, which reported no finding, blocking or otherwise. The author takes responsibility for the deposited text. Working method only; the registered author is the human author alone. The record contains the paper as a PDF. Empirical companion (preregistered; in preparation): 10.5281/zenodo.23110635.

papers.title: Neurodivergence and Digital Work Environments: A Systems Theory Approach to the Development of Neuroadaptive Software
papers.authors: Norman Geidel
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AbstractDigitised work is organised around asynchronous communication, standardised software architectures, and animplicit model of a neurotypical user. For neurodivergent professionals — here discussed primarily through adultAttention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) — that model can produce cognitive friction that conventionalaccessibility guidelines only partly address. This concept paper proposes a systems-theoretical framing of thehuman–software relation and outlines a research programme for neuroadaptive software: interfaces that modulatecomplexity, interruption, and feedback in response to inferred cognitive state.The argument combines Luhmannian systems theory with cognitive ergonomics and physiological computing. Amultimodal sensing stack is sketched (electroencephalography, eye-tracking and pupillometry, electrodermalactivity, heart-rate variability, and interaction metrics) together with an adaptive frontend architecture. The paperdoes not report original empirical results. It specifies a proposed research design, reviews related work, discusseseconomic motives for inclusion, and sets ethical constraints — above all neuro-privacy, local processing, and userautonomy. The intended contribution is a coherent concept and a testable agenda, not a finished system.

papers.title: Kategorisasi Hukum Deepfake Politik untuk Menentukan Batas Pertanggungjawaban atas Manipulasi Konten Digital
papers.authors: Sri Yulianingsih, Rengga Kusuma Putra, Ahmad Zainudin
papers.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence has accelerated the use of deepfakes in political communication while raising complex questions concerning the boundaries between freedom of expression, information manipulation, and legal accountability. These challenges arise because the synthetic nature of digital content does not, by itself, establish legal unlawfulness. This study aims to develop a legal categorisation framework for political deepfakes to determine the boundaries of legal accountability based on the characteristics and context of their use. The study employs normative legal research with qualitative and comparative legal approaches. Legal materials are analysed through six dimensions, namely nature, context, intent, deception, dissemination, and harm, which are subsequently mapped into normative categories according to their relevance to applicable legal norms. The findings demonstrate that political deepfakes should not be assessed through a binary distinction between legal and illegal content. The analysis establishes four normative categories: legitimate political expression, political satire, informational manipulation, and legally accountable deepfake. These categories form a continuum of legal responsibility that enables a more proportionate assessment of the legal relevance of synthetic political content. The stronger the elements of intent, deception, dissemination, and harm, the greater the potential for legal accountability. This framework provides a conceptual basis for developing regulation and law enforcement approaches that safeguard information integrity and democratic processes without imposing disproportionate restrictions on political freedom of expression.

papers.title: Academic Ethics of K.H. Hasyim Asy'ari and Its Relevance to Islamic Education in the 21st Century: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Kurniawati Rahmah Nia, Mujahid Mujahid
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of education and the shift toward student-centered learning in the twenty-first century have precipitated a crisis of academic ethics, marked by waning respect for educators and a movement of teacher-student relations from a spiritual character toward a transactional one. Research that explicitly confronts classical academic ethics with concrete patterns of digital communication remains scarce. This study describes the construction of academic ethics in the thought of K.H. Hasyim Asy'ari as set out in Adabul 'Alim wal Muta'allim, analyzes its relevance for educator-learner relations in the digital era, and formulates a conceptual synthesis intended as a reflective reference for practitioners. Employing a systematic review of reviews reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020, the study examines the primary text with eight studies selected through systematic screening of 6,052 records retrieved from seven databases for the period 2021 to 2026, analyzed through narrative synthesis and thematic analysis. The findings show that academic ethics in Hasyim Asy'ari's thought constitutes an epistemological and spiritual framework resting on three pillars: sincerity of intention (ikhlas), compassion (rahmah), and authority grounded in exemplary conduct (haibah). Comparison with al-Zarnuji's Ta'lim al-Muta'allim indicates that Adabul 'Alim wal Muta'allim formulates ethical responsibility reciprocally rather than unilaterally. Reconstruction appropriate for digital natives lies not in literally transplanting the hierarchical structures of the classical pesantren, but in translating its substantive values into concrete practice and integrating them into the Islamic Religious Education curriculum, positioning the teacher as a murabbi whose role artificial intelligence cannot replace.

papers.title: APEX: Active Protection at Execution Boundaries for LLM Agents
papers.authors: Xinran Zheng, Xin Fan Guo, Zhiqiang Hao, Fan Yang, Xingzhi Qian, Jiawei Du, Jinfeng Xu, Zheng Xing, Shuo Yang, Xingjun Wang
papers.abstract: Indirect prompt injection (IPI) hides adversarial instructions in content that large language model (LLM) agents read at runtime. As agents compose heterogeneous capability units, including Tools, MCP servers, and Skills, the carriers of injection multiply, and defenses built to recognize attack patterns fall behind them. We instead shift defense from covering attack patterns to one stable point: whatever the carrier and however the injection propagates, harm materializes only at the \emph{execution boundary}, where the agent turns internal state into an external action or released output. Safety there turns on two conditions, both settled by the trusted task rather than by the run: whether the proposed effect is authorized, and whether the runtime information reaching it is endorsed by that task. We present APEX, an active defense that enforces both at this boundary from a single authorization contract compiled before untrusted execution: \emph{evidence-gated prevention} admits an effect only when the contract justifies it, while \emph{deception-based exposure} makes unendorsed use reveal itself before the effect commits. Protection therefore follows from what the task permits rather than from how an attack is built, and applies uniformly across capability units without attack-specific policies or taint tracking. Against 13 baselines, APEX attains 0\% attack success on five of six benchmarks and 0.56\% on the sixth, holds 0\% under adaptive attacks on all three capability-unit types, and remains effective across defender backbones. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhengXR930/APEX_official/tree/official.

papers.title: EasyClassifier: Honest, Reproducible Machine-Learning Classification for Researchers Who Do Not Program
papers.authors: Ahmad B. Hassanat, Ghada Altarawneh
papers.abstract: Machine-learning classification is now used across medicine, the social sciences, economics, education and engineering, very often by researchers who do not program. Two errors recur in such work: preprocessing learned on all rows before cross-validation (data leakage), and reporting the cross-validation score of the classifier that won a comparison (selection bias). Both make published scores optimistic. We present EasyClassifier, an open-source Python package that guides a user from a CSV or Excel file to a finished analysis through a sequence of plain-language, multiple-choice questions, with no code. It makes the correct procedure the default rather than an option: every preprocessing step is learned inside each training fold; the selected classifier receives a separate final score from nested cross-validation (up to 2,000 rows), or an untouched 20% test set; classifiers run with fixed default parameters and fixed random seeds; and every run writes a report with a ready-to-adapt Methods paragraph, the references to cite, and figures prepared for publication. On ten public datasets from seven fields and a random-label control, split in half so that one half served as an untouched external test, the common practice overstated balanced accuracy by 2.9 percentage points on average (up to 9.9 on small data), whereas the score EasyClassifier reports had a mean signed bias of +0.7 points and a mean absolute error of 2.3 points (one-sided Wilcoxon p = 3.2 x 10^{-4}, 30 runs). On random labels it reported 48.8% balanced accuracy against a chance level of 50%. EasyClassifier is available under the MIT license from PyPI (pip install easyclassifier), GitHub, and Zenodo.

papers.title: Anticipating the Consequences of Curriculum Decisions with Large Language Models
papers.authors: Octavio Pappalardo, Nathan Herr, Tim Rocktäschel
papers.abstract: Automatic curriculum learning can improve the effectiveness of reinforcement learning by selecting the training experiences presented to the agent over time. Predicting the consequences of such decisions can, however, be difficult. We analyze automatic curriculum learning as a sequential decision-making problem, highlighting a gap between the quantities that determine the value of curriculum decisions and the information captured by local learning signals commonly used to guide them. We then investigate whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can exploit richer information about the learning problem to better anticipate the consequences of curriculum decisions. We introduce a method that combines online learning-progress estimates with LLM-informed estimates of (i) the potential downstream benefits of learning on each task and (ii) whether direct training on a task is currently likely to produce progress. We evaluate the approach on a custom benchmark of 256 textual goals in Craftax under different curriculum objectives. We observe the strongest gains when optimizing for individual target tasks. When optimizing across the full task set, the benefits vary across learners with different mechanisms for cross-task transfer, ranging from modest improvements in learning speed to larger gains that persist through the end of training.

papers.title: $\mathrm{TRIZ}^{a}$: Guiding Agent Evolution from Pattern Recognition to Solution Invention
papers.authors: Wenyin Liu, Yiheng Huang, Kai Wang
papers.abstract: We propose $\mathrm{TRIZ}^{a}$ (TRIZ exponentiated by an agent), a general R\&D automation paradigm that combines TRIZ inventive theory with LLM-driven agent evolutionary search. TRIZ's 40 inventive principles and contradiction matrix provide structured, explainable directions for solution generation, replacing random or untyped mutation with theory-guided ideation. Functional information (FI), operationalized under a frozen reference contract, is combined with TRIZ Ideality to measure useful and harmful function on a commensurable information scale, while hard gates keep promotion distinct from metric improvement. We validate $\mathrm{TRIZ}^{a}$ in cybersecurity--an adversarial and rapidly evolving domain--on PowerDuck GOOSE, CICIoT2023, and CIC-DDoS2019. Under paired-rerun protocols with protocol fingerprinting and hard-gate validation, the legacy experiments yield absolute F1 improvements of $+2.88$, $+4.23$, and $+0.15$ percentage points, respectively. A completed 45-activity CICIoT2023 campaign further increases macro-F1 from $0.8325$ to $0.8483$, but does not pass its frozen promotion gate. Every result remains traceable from contradiction identification and TRIZ principle selection to code transformation, evaluation metrics, and promotion decision.

papers.title: Attestable Audit: Property-Based Attestation for Proprietary Workloads without Artifact Disclosure
papers.authors: Takuma Imamura
papers.abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) prove the integrity of code and data to a remote peer through remote attestation: the TEE issues an attestation report by signing, with a hardware-bound key, its configuration information, including measurements (cryptographic digests) of the code loaded inside it. A verifier appraises the report by matching these measurements against reference values. When the measured artifact is proprietary, however, the verifier cannot derive the reference values itself: it can only confirm that something with a given measurement is running inside the TEE---not that the program behaves as expected---forcing full trust in the reference value provider. We propose an architecture that closes this gap without disclosing the artifact, composing two TEE workloads: attestable build (Hugenroth et al., 2025), which binds a source code digest to a build artifact measurement, and attestable audit (proposed in this paper), which binds the same source code digest to the verdicts of automated audits---fuzzing, static analysis, AI code auditing, formal methods---executed inside a TEE. Both are instances of Confidential Computing Proofs: TEE attestation viewed as a hardware-backed zero-knowledge proof. Chaining the two certificates lets the verifier conclude that the running artifact was built from source code satisfying the audited properties, without disclosing either the source code or the build artifact. A proof-of-concept implementation on Intel SGX with the Gramine Library OS, running the Bandit security analyzer on Python code, demonstrates the practicality of the approach.

papers.title: LocusRL: Diagnosing LLM Reward and Policy Interventions in Competitive Games
papers.authors: Chengyu Luan, Bo Xin, Songyan Guo, Yuxiang Zuo, Ahmed Yazdan, Jiahang Li, Yicheng Liu
papers.abstract: Large language models can intervene in reinforcement learning through both reward design and action selection, yet aggregate performance offers an incomplete account of what these interventions actually do. Similar returns can conceal different learning mechanisms, while plausible rewards can induce undesirable behavior. We introduce LocusRL, a diagnostic framework that connects controlled reward-policy comparisons with audits of reward judgments, signal delivery, optimization objectives, and executed actions. The framework traces performance differences to testable explanations and checks targeted corrections through executable rules and counterfactual replay. Across two evaluation batches covering ten Connect Four training seeds, we uncover seed-dependent reversals in intervention effects and show how tracing actual updates changes their interpretation: historical Qwen training operates through reward-weighted teacher-action likelihood. A separate matched three-seed reward-direction experiment distinguishes sensitivity to a learning signal from its usefulness. With terminal rewards held fixed, a sign-reversed dense oracle yields a 2.8% aggregate win rate, compared with 57.2% for terminal-only training and 46.7% for the positive dense oracle. Thus, a reward can strongly influence learning without improving performance. At the decision level, counterfactual replay verifies a winning correction to a diagnosed action error. Complementary experiments in Leduc and reward-validation studies in Goofspiel extend the analysis to imperfect-information settings, revealing how reference-label definitions and validation-data exposure affect intervention assessment. Together, these findings show why evaluating LLM interventions requires tracing how their outputs become learning signals and actions. LocusRL turns aggregate outcomes into actionable diagnoses and verifiable corrections.

papers.title: Ideological Stance Detection in a Low-Resource Language: Polarization in Bangladeshi Public vs Private University Discourse on Social Media
papers.authors: Safaruzzaman Shovo, Monowar Islam, Asif Hossain, Sameya Akhter, Md. Sajjatul Islam
papers.abstract: Public vs. private universities is a debatable issue, and it creates polarization on social media in Bangladesh. Debate on quality, jobs, and prestige is passionate among the students, parents, and graduates, the majority of whom speak Bengali, a low-resource language. To measure this polarization, this paper introduces a manually annotated dataset of 4,060 Bengali comments labeled as Pro-Public, Pro-Private, or Neutral. We evaluated the quality of our annotations by Fleiss's Kappa agreement that was 0.89, corresponding to a high agreement among annotators. The classical ML (SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost), BiLSTM network, hybrid BanglaBERT+XGBoost models and the state-of-the-art zero-shot LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4, DeepSeek-V3.1, Llama 4 Maverick, Kimi K2 Thinking, Qwen3-235B Thinking) models are evaluated. The accuracy of BanglaBERT+XGBoost is 91.81% and macro F1 score is 91.70%, which is higher than all the supervised baselines. The zero-shot Llama 4 Maverick Thinking achieves a macro F1 of 0.931 (overall accuracy of 93.31%) without any fine-tuning. All machine learning (ML), deep machine learning (DL) and transformer models were outperformed by the zero-shot Llama 4 Maverick model. Polarization also is evident, in some ways more clearly in the Pro-Private comments, which emphasize modern facilities and timely graduation, versus the Pro-Public comments, which emphasize affordability and government jobs. Our findings open new directions for analyzing social media polarization in low-resource languages.

papers.title: Bi-manual Stabilization of the Cervical Spine for Safe Physical Human-Robot Interaction in Rolling Maneuvers
papers.authors: Elizabeth Peiros, Moira Bohley, Lucas Yager, Derek Chen, Rebecca Fellbaum, Chris D'Ambrosia, Ananya Rao, Xiao Liang, Michael C. Yip
papers.abstract: The neck, specifically the cervical spine, is a highly fragile and mobile part of the body with a high risk of catastrophic injury. Whether someone is injured on a battlefield, in a natural disaster, or in an athletic event, great care is always taken with the cervical spine when transporting, rolling, or moving the patient. In this work, we present an algorithm and adaptations for bi-manual robots to stabilize the cervical spine during rolling maneuvers. We investigate techniques to maximize grip strength within safety bounds and present a control approach for proper neck rotation. We found that with our approach, a bi-manual robot is capable of achieving human-level performance in maintaining target rotational alignments. The axial alignment for the robot with prediction was within .21 degrees of human novices.

papers.title: MOV-AAD: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset for Auditory Attention Decoding During Moving Conversations
papers.authors: Xiaomin He, Vishal Choudhari, Tristan J. Spratt, Aarya Raghavan, Lee, Richard T., Nima Mesgarani
papers.abstract: Auditory attention decoding (AAD) is often evaluated on static, simplified speech scenes that poorly match everyday listening. We introduce MOV-AAD, a large-scale dataset for studying auditory attention under moving, naturalistic conversations. MOV-AAD combines 64-channel EEG with synchronized physiological recordings, including eye tracking, respiration, galvanic skin response, heart rate, peripheral oxygen saturation, body temperature, body motion, and photoplethysmography, enabling analysis of cross-modal neural and physiological markers of attention and listening effort. This dataset uses a more ecologically valid listening paradigm with dynamically moving conversational speech sources and behavioral measures of attentional engagement. MOV-AAD supports research on robust AAD in realistic spatial dynamics, multimodal attention modeling, listening effort, and intersubject neural responses, providing a resource for benchmarking selective auditory attention in naturalistic listening.

papers.title: Language Model Fingerprinting Requires Rethinking Watermark Teachers
papers.authors: Jeongyeon Hwang, Anshul Nasery, Sewoong Oh, Jungseul Ok
papers.abstract: LLM fingerprinting via watermark distillation embeds a statistical watermark signal into model weights, enabling model owners to identify their models behind black-box APIs. Revisiting a recent protocol, we find that its utility evaluation understates text quality degradation in open-ended generation, favoring overly strong watermark teachers. Weakening the watermark improves text quality but sacrifices detectability. To move beyond this trade-off, we rethink whether text watermarks designed for verifying generated text are suitable distillation teachers for model fingerprinting. Such watermarks are typically designed to remain detectable from an individual output, limiting how sparse the watermark signal can be. In contrast, fingerprint verification can aggregate signal across queries, making sparser watermark signals viable. This raises a key question: where should the sparse signal be placed? We analyze signal placement through token surprisal and show that, even at comparable watermark strength, different placements can target tokens with different plausibility under the base model. This motivates near-tie restriction, which uses top-1-relative logit gaps to restrict the watermark bias to tokens close to the base model's top prediction. Across multiple models, near-tie improves detection--quality frontiers under deployment changes, preserves higher text quality across query budgets, and further improves existing watermarking schemes when combined with them.

papers.title: Menopauzani boshqarishda sun’iy intellekt: zamonaviy vositalar va klinik qo‘llash istiqbollari sharhi
papers.authors: Нилуфар Бакоева, Нилуфар Бакоева, Nilufar Baqoyeva
papers.abstract: This review systematizes four major areas of artificial intelligence (AI) application in menopause medicine: (1) risk prediction and patient stratification (osteoporosis, cardiovascular disorders, and cognitive impairment); (2) conversational AI systems and large language model (LLM)-based chatbots for patient counseling and education; (3) wearable devices and digital biomarkers for the objective assessment of vasomotor and other symptoms; and (4) clinical decision support systems for selecting menopausal hormone therapy (MHT). Particular attention is given to the methodological limitations of existing studies, issues of validation and model interpretability, data bias, and ethical and regulatory barriers to implementing AI in routine clinical practice. It is concluded that, given the current level of evidence, AI tools should be used as an adjunct to, rather than a substitute for, clinical decision-making, provided that they undergo prospective validation in representative populations, including non-Western populations.

papers.title: Бухгалтерская (финансовая) отчетность: раскрытие информации и ее роль при принятии решений
papers.authors: Д.С. Родионова, Н.А. Семенова
papers.abstract: Статья отражает основные аспекты раскрытия информации бухгалтерской (финансовой) отчетности и ее роль при принятии решений. Основными критериями успешности проведения качественной экономической политики являются контроль баланса между экстенсивным и интенсивным экономическим ростом, грамотное вложение денежных потоков, которые могут формироваться из собственных средств, заемных средств, а также инвестиций. Анализируются основы бухгалтерской отчетности, модернизации производства. На основании отчетности педагогического колледжа рассмотрено финансовое состояние образовательного учреждения, а также внедрение курсов по обучению работы с искусственным интеллектом. The article reflects the main aspects of disclosure of information in accounting (financial) reporting and its role in decision-making. This topic remains relevant today, as economic development is the most important principle for the development of microenterprises, large businesses, and the state. Therefore, it is necessary to regularly maintain development trends in both domestic and global financial systems. The main criteria for the success of quality economic policy implementation include controlling the balance between extensive and intensive economic growth, as well as competent management of cash flows, which can be formed from own funds, borrowed funds, and investments. The purpose of the scientific work is to study the fundamentals of accounting reporting, the importance of analysis, and production modernization while closing financial gaps. The scientific work will examine accounting (financial) reporting, its main components, and evaluation criteria. Based on the pedagogical college’s reporting, the financial condition of the educational institution will be analyzed, along with the introduction of courses for training in working with artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Кольцевая модель лидерских компетенций: формирование целостного лидера в эпоху ИИ
papers.authors: Я.Ю. Павлов
papers.abstract: В статье представлена кольцевая модель лидерских компетенций, разработанная на основе двух фокус-групп с участием 20 экспертов в области развития лидеров в условиях распространения технологий искусственного интеллекта (ИИ). На основе анализа ключевых психологических концепций, прежде всего теории осознанной саморегуляции произвольной активности, предложена авторская кольцевая модель лидерских компетенций. Модель строится на принципе управляющего воздействия внутренних ресурсов личности и компетенций более высокого порядка на внешние управленческие функции. Ядро модели составляют самокомпетенции, определяющие этику и внутреннюю устойчивость лидера. Первый концентрический слой образуют метакомпетенции – системное мышление, адаптивная обучаемость и другие способности, управляющие применением компетенций остальных уровней. Ключевой особенностью модели является размещение цифровых (digital) и мягких (soft) компетенций на одном уровне. Это решение связано с тем, что в условиях автоматизации и возникновения гибридных команд из людей и ИИ-агентов цифровые навыки приобретают человекоцентричный характер. Внешний контур формируют жесткие (hard) компетенции, выступающие измеримыми функциональными инструментами. Обосновывается практическая ценность модели для комплексной оценки управленческого потенциала, бизнес-образования и организационного дизайна. The article presents a ring model of leadership competencies developed on the basis of two focus groups involving 20 experts in leadership development in the context of the spread of artificial intelligence (AI). Drawing on key psychological concepts, primarily the theory of conscious self-regulation of voluntary activity, the author proposes an original ring model of leadership competencies. The model is based on the principle that internal personal resources and higher-order competencies govern external managerial functions. Self-competencies form the core of the model and determine the leader's ethics and internal resilience. The first concentric layer consists of meta-competencies, including systems thinking and learning agility, which govern the application of competencies at the other levels. A key feature of the model is the placement of digital and soft competencies at the same level. This reflects the human-centered nature of digital skills in an environment of automation and hybrid teams composed of people and AI agents. The external contour consists of hard competencies that serve as measurable functional tools. The article substantiates the practical value of the model for comprehensive assessment of managerial potential, business education, and organizational design.

papers.title: Трансформация коммуникационной модели в медиапространстве атомной отрасли: от закрытости к открытости (на примере проектов госкорпорации «Росатом»)
papers.authors: А.Ю. Ветрова, А.Н. Татаринцев, А.П. Милославский
papers.abstract: В статье рассматривается эволюция коммуникационной модели в медиапространстве атомной отрасли России (на примере проектов Госкорпорации «Росатом»). За 85 лет существования отрасли пройден непростой путь от закрытости к современной открытой цифровой экосистеме, основанной на онлайн-платформах, мультимедийных форматах и активном диалоге с аудиторией. На основе анализа ключевых проектов Госкорпорации «Росатом» – цифрового пресс-центра, мультиплатформенного медиа «Страна Росатом», коммуникационно-образовательного проекта «МедиаСтанция», а также цифровых игровых продуктов («Арктика», «Эко-квест») – выделены основные этапы и драйверы цифровой трансформации медиакоммуникаций в атомной отрасли. Особое внимание уделяется роли искусственного интеллекта, геймификации и новых форматов взаимодействия с аудиторией в формировании открытой цифровой культуры. Делается вывод о том, что Госкорпорация «Росатом» выступает одним из лидеров цифровой трансформации корпоративных коммуникаций среди российских предприятий. The article examines the evolution of the communications model in the media space of the Russian nuclear industry (using the projects of State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom as an example). Over the 85 years of its existence, the industry has traveled a difficult path from a closed system to a modern, open digital ecosystem based on online platforms, multimedia formats, and active dialogue with the audience. Based on an analysis of ROSATOM’s key projects – the digital press center, the multiplatform media outlet «Strana Rosatom», the communications and educational project «MediaStation», and digital gaming products («Arctic» and «Eco-Quest») – the article identifies the main stages and drivers of the digital transformation of media communications in the nuclear industry. Particular attention is paid to the role of artificial intelligence, gamification, and new formats of audience interaction in shaping an open digital culture. It is concluded that ROSATOM is one of the leaders in the digital transformation of corporate communications among Russian enterprises.

papers.title: ChatGPT use and learning motivation among informatics students: a preliminary correlational study
papers.authors: Muhamad Zulton Praditya, Hafizh Adham Tauhid, Muhammad Ali Hakim
papers.abstract: Generative AI systems such as ChatGPT are increasingly used by university students for explanation, code inspection, idea generation, and immediate feedback. This preliminary cross-sectional study examines the association between ChatGPT use frequency and learning motivation among 17 Informatics Engineering students at Universitas Mulia, Balikpapan. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using a four-category measure of ChatGPT use frequency and four-point agreement responses for learning motivation. The original analysis reported a Pearson correlation of r = 0.685 with p = 0.002. Using the reported coefficient and sample size, the corresponding test statistic is t(15) = 3.642 and the Fisher-transformed 95% confidence interval is approximately 0.305-0.877, indicating a positive but imprecisely estimated association. The finding is consistent with literature suggesting that responsive AI tools may support engagement and perceived competence, but the correlational design does not establish that ChatGPT use increases motivation. Reverse causality, self-selection, prior achievement, digital confidence, purpose of use, and measurement limitations remain plausible explanations. The study contributes context-specific evidence from informatics students and identifies requirements for stronger follow-up research, including a larger sample, validated motivation measures, clearer characterization of AI use, rank-based sensitivity analysis, and longitudinal or quasi-experimental data.

papers.title: Assessing Learning When AI Can Produce the Product
papers.authors: William J. Rothwell
papers.journal: International Journal of AI in Pedagogy Innovation and Learning Futures
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can contribute to the reasoning and communication represented in student work, complicating inferences from product quality to individual capability. This conceptual article develops an integrated framework for assessing cognitive ownership through mutual evaluation and outcome-aligned verification. Cognitive ownership is defined as a learner’s demonstrated capacity to understand, evaluate, adapt, and accept responsibility for consequential reasoning under specified conditions of assistance. Eight indicators are organized into four assessment domains: understanding, epistemic judgment, adaptive performance, and reflective accountability. Mutual evaluation combines independent student and instructor judgments, evidence-based comparison, and documented responses to disagreement; agreement is not treated as proof of learning. The framework distinguishes the quality of an AI-assisted product, capability demonstrated during assessment, and learning established through change and retention. A worked higher education example illustrates task design, scoring, and responses to conflicting evidence. Five propositions and a validation agenda address incremental predictive value, task sampling, feedback, fairness, and feasibility. The framework is proposed rather than empirically validated. Its contribution is to connect existing validity and evaluative judgment scholarship with a practical account of the evidence needed to support bounded claims about individual and assisted performance.

papers.title: PROTOTYPE-DRIVEN AUTOMATED TRAINING SYSTEMS: AN AGILE AND SUSTAINABLE LEARNING PARADIGM
papers.authors: Ali Hamzah Obaid, Khansaa Azeez Obayes Al-Husseini
papers.journal: Intelligent X-Ray Image Analysis using Fuzzy Inference Systems
papers.abstract: The growing integration of artificial intelligence into an educational context has revealed several shortcomings present in traditional adaptive training systems that rely on machine-learning, such as the reliance on fixed instructional patterns and the lack of understanding of the adaptive processes. These limitations reduce the pedagogical transparency and slow down the process of refining the instructional material. Accordingly, this research proposes a Prototype-Driven Automated Training System (PDATS), a flexible training architectural framework based on the assumption that the instructional units can be modeled as dynamic trains of prototypes, which are optimized by adjusting them in a controlled feedback process using the available empirical data on learners and performance. This framework combines the ideas of iterative prototyping and strict mathematical formalization to approve instructional modification depending on the measurable measures, such as performance increase, learning effectiveness, and student involvement. A controlled experimental study was conducted to determine the effectiveness of PDATS that involved one hundred participants who were assigned at random to control cohort that used a traditional automated training system or an experimental cohort, which used PDATS architecture. Substantial improvements in the range of criteria of evaluation have been attested by empirical findings. Subjects who used PDATS gained performance on average about twice as much as the control condition (0.20 vs 0.10, p< 0.01), and there was also a lower average time in which training was finished (by about 23.7 percent). Moreover, signs of involvement and contentment were also expressed in significant increments within the prototype-based environment. These results highlight the fact that adaptation using prototypes is an interpretable and effective alternative to regular machine-learning-based training systems. The suggested paradigm provides a clear and sustainable design of the intelligent training solutions concept that unites adaptive learning, prototyping strategies, and explainable artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Reorienting Human Rights Protection in an Artificial Intelligence-Based Digital Ecosystem
papers.authors: Acep Wahyu, Joko Sriwidodo, Lukman Hakim
papers.journal: Siber International Journal of Advanced Law (SIJAL)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence mediates access to employment, finance, health care, education, public services, and security, thereby transforming human rights risks from identifiable human acts into distributed sociotechnical processes. This article examines whether Indonesia's existing legal framework adequately protects rights against opaque, autonomous, and transnational artificial intelligence systems and formulates a rights-oriented governance model. Using normative legal research, it combines statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches and analyses Indonesian constitutional guarantees, human rights law, personal data protection law, electronic information law, global ethical standards, and the European Union's risk-based regulation. The study finds that current Indonesian rules provide fragmented protection but do not establish an integrated allocation of responsibility across theartificial intelligence life cycle. Privacy violations, discriminatory outcomes, deficient explanations, and ineffective remedies may consequently arise without a clearly accountable actor. The article proposes the RIGHTS-AI model, comprising risk classification, impact assessment, governance accountability, human oversight, transparency and traceability, safeguards and security, accessible remedies, and independent supervision. Its novelty lies in connecting individual remedies with preventive duties imposed on developers, providers, deployers, and public authorities. This model enables innovation while keeping automated power subordinate to human dignity, equality, legal certainty, and democratic accountability within Indonesia's digital ecosystem and strengthens sustainable rights protection.

papers.title: Beyond Technology: Privacy, Spirituality, and Women’s Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
papers.authors: Mehtap Temiz, Gülten Koç
papers.abstract: This study examined women’s general attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare and aimed to identify factors associated with these attitudes, with particular consideration of gynecological and obstetric contexts. The study does not directly assess acceptance of specific AI applications but focuses on general attitudinal tendencies that may inform the development of more trustworthy and acceptable AI-supported healthcare systems. This cross-sectional study included 204 women aged 18–65 years. Data were collected between November 2025 and February 2026 using an online questionnaire distributed via convenience and snowball sampling methods. Data were collected using a personal information form, the General Attitude Toward Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Scale, the Body Privacy in Gynecology Obstetrics Scale, and the Spiritual Well-Being Scale. Descriptive statistics, t-tests, ANOVA, correlation analyses, and hierarchical multiple regression analysis were conducted. Women with higher educational levels and prior AI experience demonstrated more positive attitudes toward AI. Privacy perception and spirituality were negatively associated with attitudes toward AI, whereas educational level and prior AI experience were positively associated with AI attitudes. Privacy perception, spirituality, prior AI experience, and education emerged as important factors shaping women’s attitudes toward artificial intelligence in healthcare. Strengthening privacy protections, addressing ethical and value-based concerns, and improving digital health literacy may contribute to the development of more favorable attitudes toward AI-supported healthcare.

papers.title: AI-Guided Stimulus and Debug Triage: A Methodology for Accelerating Pre-Silicon Emulation of Flagship SoC Programs
papers.authors: Abhishek Kumar Sinha
papers.journal: The American Journal of Engineering And Technology
papers.abstract: Raw emulation capacity for flagship system-on-chip (SoC) programs keeps growing, and engineer-hour supply keeps falling further behind it. That gap, not machine availability, is the actual bottleneck in pre-silicon verification today, driven by workload diversity across artificial intelligence (AI), extended reality (XR), and mobile platforms converging on a single die. This article argues that closing the gap requires a bounded, governed layer of AI-guided assistance rather than either extreme - full automation or continued reliance on engineer-only throughput. A three-layer adoption framework is proposed: scoping, which restricts AI involvement to stimulus generation for known-workload classes and anomaly-flagged debug triage while keeping root-cause sign-off and tape-out risk calls fully engineer-owned; validation, which requires every AI-generated output to be checked against a trusted reference - simulation, formal methods, or historical regression baselines - before an engineer may act on it; and governance, an operating-review cadence with rollback criteria defined before deployment, not improvised afterward.
