Pilot deployment of emulation-friendly RTL on a premium-tier mobile SoC program produced a shift of approximately 60 percent of RTL earlier in the program schedule, with no coverage-model exception granted to reach that outcome. The finding that emerges is not that AI accelerates verification - that much is already argued elsewhere - but that the acceleration only survives contact with a tape-out schedule when it is deliberately bounded. Emulation productivity under AI assistance is a governance problem before it is a technical one, and the three-layer framework is offered as a transferable operating model for programs where the cost of an unvalidated miss is unacceptable.

papers.title: Faculty and Student Perceptions of Artificial Intelligence in Medical Education at a Public Sector University in Pakistan: A Qualitative Study
papers.authors: Anum Arshad Beg, Zainab Mohammad Anjarwala, Naveen Khawaja, Abida Fatima, Muhammad Imran Shekhani
papers.journal: Liaquat National Journal of Primary Care
papers.abstract: Background: Artificial Intelligence (AI), with its range of applications and ease of use, is transforming medicine. AI usage is increasing exponentially in a resource-limited country like Pakistan; however, application in medical education is evolving and needs to be understood. Little work has been done on perceptions among faculty and students to understand their understanding and readiness to use AI, while keeping in mind the ethical issues it may raise. Objective: To explore perceptions of faculty and students regarding integration of AI into undergraduate medical education, potential challenges and ethical considerations in adoption of AI, at a public sector university in Pakistan. Methods: Exploratory descriptive qualitative study at Dow University of Health Sciences, Karachi, from October 2025 to March 2026, including faculty in-depth interviews (IDI) and focus group discussions (FGD) with MBBS students till data saturation was achieved. Audio recording and transcription were done using an artificial intelligence tool. Data were thematically analyzed using the Braun and Clarke framework. Results: A total of 10 IDIs and 5 FGDs were conducted. IDIs included 10 faculty members: 6 (60%) females and 4 (40%) males, aged 38-55 years. FGDs included 40 students (males: 15, females: 25), with 7-8 participants per FGD, aged 20-25 years. Six key themes were derived: Modernization in Education, Curriculum Integration, Clinical Research and Practice, Ethics and Professional Responsibility, Readiness of the Institute, Strategic Integration, and Governance Issues. Conclusion: Faculty and students see AI as a supportive tool that increases access to healthcare and information and reduces errors. Important concerns raised included confidentiality, privacy, and fear of AI replacing humans in the medical sector.

papers.title: UPAYA PEMANFAATAN AI SEBAGAI PEMBELAJARAN ADAPTIF DI SEKOLAH INKLUSIF
papers.authors: Eka Marsanda Suhesti, Salsa Doanniwati Hasibuan, Asna Istikmalatul Muktamaroh, Chairridha Febrina, Ica Wilda Silalahi
papers.journal: Didaktik Jurnal Ilmiah PGSD STKIP Subang
papers.abstract: Inclusive education requires learning approaches capable of accommodating the diverse needs, abilities, and characteristics of students. One strategy involves utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support adaptive learning. This study aims to analyze the use of AI in supporting adaptive learning within inclusive schools. A literature review method was employed, analyzing ten relevant scholarly articles published over the past decade. Data were gathered via Google Scholar and ScienceDirect and subsequently analyzed using a descriptive qualitative approach identifying, categorizing, and comparing research findings. The results indicate that AI has the potential to facilitate material personalization, adjust learning levels, provide feedback, enhance accessibility for students with special needs, and assist teachers with monitoring and evaluation. However, implementation faces challenges such as infrastructure limitations, teacher competency issues, data privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, and the risk of reduced social interaction. Therefore, the adoption of AI should be implemented gradually, while maintaining the teacher's role as the primary decision maker.

papers.title: Resources Illustrators’ Collaboration, Competence, and Challenges in Utilizing Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Lilibeth Larupay
papers.abstract: This study examined the collaboration, competence, and challenges of 181 resource illustrators in utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI) across Panay Island in October 2025, with all identified illustrators included as respondents and no random sampling employed. A validated questionnaire was used to assess illustrators’ collaborative practices, as well as their technical and creative competence in AI and the challenges encountered in AI-assisted workflows. Descriptive and inferential analyses were conducted, including frequency, percentage, mean, t-test, ANOVA, and Pearson’s r correlation at a 0.05 significance level. Findings revealed that respondents predominantly comprised older (56.35%) and female (53.04%) illustrators, most holding bachelor’s degrees (66.3%), with junior illustrators as the largest professional group (48.62%), and the majority residing in Iloilo (37.02%). Resource illustrators demonstrated very high levels of collaboration (mean range 4.24–4.35) and competence (mean range 4.33–4.45) across all classifications, with slightly higher engagement and skills observed among older, female, doctorate-holding, lead illustrators, and those from Iloilo. Challenges in utilizing AI were generally moderate (overall mean = 1.45) and consistent across age, sex, educational attainment, position, and province. No significant differences were found in collaboration, competence, or challenges across all classifications, and Pearson correlation analysis indicated no significant relationships among these variables. These results suggest that while Panay Island illustrators are highly skilled and collaborative in using AI, they experience moderate challenges that are independent of demographic or professional factors.

papers.title: Measuring Academic Performance in Psychology in the Era of AI: The benefits of an oral viva in assessing undergraduate dissertations
papers.authors: xiaosheng chen, Deborah Talmi
papers.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), challenge psychology educators’ ability to assess students’ understanding and judgement through written coursework. We argue that this issue is especially acute for the compulsory empirical project required for British Psychological Society (BPS) accreditation and that interactive oral examinations (vivas) offer a discipline-aligned and scalable response. Grounded in the epistemic features of psychology, the viva enables direct assessment of students’ conceptual understanding, methodological justification, and reflective thinking in ways written reports cannot reliably capture in an AI-saturated environment. In this paper we propose an operational framework for implementing project vivas across final-year cohorts and argue that viva assessment should be viewed not as a defensive measure, but as a future-oriented approach that enhances authenticity, equity, and educational quality in psychology.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Language Analytics for Student Development in Higher Education: Evidence from Longitudinal Academic Records
papers.authors: Ke Yu, Jianhui Yang, Yuchun Lu, Xiaoxiao Wu, Weiqi Lyu, Dehua Ye
papers.abstract: In higher education, standardized entry scores provide an important but incomplete basis for understanding students’ subsequent development. This study explores whether AI-assisted language analytics can provide complementary information about student development beyond standardized academic measures. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory, we examine the relationship between National College Entrance Examination (NCEE) scores, language-based indicators from students’ self-introductions, and academic performance across four semesters. The study involved 72 undergraduate students majoring in mathematics education who provided free-form self-introductions describing their interests and experiences. Interest types were categorized, and linguistic features were extracted and analyzed using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based model. Results show that the association between NCEE scores and academic performance weakened across successive semesters, whereas students expressing more autonomous interests tended to achieve higher academic performance. An exploratory AI classification analysis further indicated that linguistic features could distinguish developmental profiles within this sample. These findings suggest that AI-assisted language analytics may offer a complementary source of information for understanding student development and informing formative advising and student support. Given the single-institution sample, the findings should be interpreted as exploratory and require validation in larger and more diverse populations.

papers.title: The landscape of gateway STEM student success and teaching practices at R1 institutions in the United States post-COVID and post-AI
papers.authors: Justin Franklin Shaffer
papers.abstract: Gateway science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) courses have historically been taught primarily with didactic lectures and high-stakes examinations which can contribute to poor student outcomes. Much has changed in higher education in recent years after two historic disruptions: the COVID-19 pandemic and the arrival of generative artificial intelligence (AI). It is therefore important to know how these courses are currently taught and how students are succeeding post-COVID and post-AI. This study is the first of its kind to survey faculty from five different STEM disciplines (biology, calculus, chemistry, physics, and programming) to widely assess gateway STEM failure rates, course design and teaching strategies, and assessment practices at institutions with very high research activity (R1) post-COVID and post-AI. The results show that while gateway STEM course failure rates have declined, traditional lecturing and assessment practices still dominate while evidence-based instructional practices (EBIPs) are used sparingly. Academic leaders and faculty should act on these data locally to determine the extent of potential impacts at their own institutions to design and teach gateway STEM courses to maximize student success.

papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Model Performance on Open-Ended Questions: Answering and Marking Capabilities
papers.authors: Quynh T. Nguyen, Michael Lo, Mai P. Tran, Quang Dieu Tran
papers.abstract: Statistical literacy is crucial in biology education, yet developing and assessing it at higher cognitive levels is resource-intensive. This study evaluated three large language models against 20 graduate students on open-ended biological statistics questions spanning Bloom's Taxonomy, and separately examined whether a large language model could serve as a marking assistant alongside an experienced human instructor. A set of 692 questions was developed by graduate students using a statistics textbook. After cleaning, 336 unique questions were retained, with 1,344 answers provided by the four respondent groups. Answers were graded using a holistic five-point rubric by a human expert and a large language model. Friedman tests showed that all models were rated more favourably than the graduate students, though this advantage was not uniform across cognitive levels, and the evaluative question type (Type 7) anchoring the highest cognitive level in this study's design showed the weakest performance across all respondent groups. Inter-rater reliability between the human and large language model was low overall. The large language model grader showed a bias toward scores of 3-4, while the human expert demonstrated greater consistency across question types. These findings suggest that large language models can generate strong responses at lower cognitive levels, but their reliability as holistic-rubric graders are limited compared to an experienced instructor.

papers.title: From Disciplinary Formation to Artistic Autonomy: Higher Art Education in France and Armenia in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Martin Harutyunyan
papers.abstract: Higher art education is undergoing a significant transformation as traditional models of disciplinary and technical formation increasingly intersect with artistic autonomy, research-oriented practice, interdisciplinary learning, and artificial intelligence (AI). The article examines how educational structures and institutional cultures shape the formation of artists and designers, focusing comparatively on France and Armenia. The relevance of the topic is determined by the need to understand how contemporary institutions organise the transition from disciplinary knowledge toward independent creative agency at a moment when AI is reshaping established understandings of technical skill, authorship, and artistic decision-making. The aim of the study is to determine how different educational cultures shape the development of artistic autonomy, artistic identity, and research capacity in higher art education, and how these relationships might be transformed by artificial intelligence. The research methods are based on a comparative socio-pedagogical approach combining documentary analysis, institutional observation, curriculum analysis, and qualitative interpretation. The empirical component draws primarily on field study conducted in Saint-Étienne, France, during 2024–2025, with particular attention to the École Supérieure d'Art et Design de Saint-Étienne (ESADSE) and Université Jean Monnet, while Armenian higher art education is examined as a comparative context. The analysis is informed by Pierre Bourdieu's concept of cultural production, Michel Foucault's understanding of disciplinary formation, and the concept of artistic research. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the comparative socio-pedagogical analysis of French and Armenian higher art education as distinct educational cultures, in interpreting artistic formation as a movement from disciplinary learning toward increasing autonomy and research capacity, and in extending this framework to the relationship between artistic autonomy and artificial intelligence. The results indicate that both French and Armenian systems recognise the importance of technical and professional competence but organise the transition toward artistic autonomy differently. The French programmes examined show a more explicit progression from foundational education toward specialisation, individual projects, experimentation, professional engagement, and research-oriented practice. Armenian higher art education retains a stronger continuity with systematic technical and disciplinary formation, while incorporating comparable Bachelor–Master–Doctoral structures. Conclusions. Technical competence and artistic autonomy should not be treated as opposing educational objectives; contemporary art education requires a productive transition between disciplinary knowledge and independent creative agency. The emergence of AI further complicates this relationship by shifting attention from technical execution toward conceptual thinking, critical judgement, authorship, research capacity, and ethical responsibility. For Armenian higher art education, the findings suggest an approach based on adaptation rather than imitation, combining established traditions of technical formation with greater opportunities for specialisation, artistic research, professional practice, digital literacy, and responsible human–AI creative engagement.

papers.title: Driver Intention Recognition Under Autonomous Takeover Scenarios Based on EEG and Eye-Tracking Fusion
papers.authors: Min Duan, Jin Shu, Lian Xie, Jianrong Cai, Chuan Sun, Shucai Xu, Hao Shi
papers.abstract: To address the challenges of recognition lag and limited representational capacity of single-modal physiological information in driver intention recognition under human–machine co-driving environments, this study constructed a highway driving takeover experimental scenario. Typical takeover tasks including obstacle avoidance takeover, adjacent vehicle cut-in takeover, and curved section takeover were designed, with simultaneous collection of drivers’ electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-tracking data. On this basis, a multi-modal physiological information fusion method for driving intention recognition was proposed. First, areas of interest (AOIs) were defined to extract visual behavioral features, including fixation duration, fixation count, and pupil diameter, while eye-tracking recurrence plots were generated based on phase space reconstruction. Meanwhile, event-related potential (ERP) analysis was performed on the EEG data to extract N100, N200, and P300 components, and continuous wavelet transform was applied to construct EEG time–frequency maps. Subsequently, the EEG time–frequency maps and eye-tracking recurrence plots served as the dual inputs to the dual-branch Squeeze-and-Excitation Convolutional Neural Network (SE-CNN) model, which was further enhanced by fusing ERP features and eye-tracking statistical features, ultimately achieving accurate recognition of four types of driving intentions. The model results demonstrated that the dual-branch SE-CNN model achieved a recognition accuracy of 88.29% on the four-class intention recognition task, with precision, recall, and F1-score reaching 88.78%, 88.26%, and 88.31%, respectively—significantly outperforming both single-modal models and the dual-branch Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model without the SE attention mechanism. The proposed model can effectively integrate EEG neural activity signals and eye-tracking visual behavioral information, thereby substantially enhancing driving intention recognition performance. This provides theoretical foundations and technical support for applications such as early driver intention perception, intelligent takeover decision-making, and human–machine collaborative control in human–machine co-driving environments.

papers.title: Cultural Tourism Intention in Digital Communication Ecosystems: Habitual Engagement, eWOM, and Destination Image Co-Creation Using PLS-SEM and fsQCA
papers.authors: Ngamsiri Witoonphan, Sumaman Pankham, Somchai Lekcharoen
papers.abstract: Cultural destinations are discovered, interpreted, and evaluated through digital communication. However, studies examine communication factors independently, limiting understanding of how destination image develops within digital communication ecosystems and how communication conditions relate to cultural tourism intention. This study examines relationships among social influence, habit, price value, social media marketing activities (SMMA), user-generated content (UGC), electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM), destination image, and cultural tourism intention. A sequential mixed-methods design integrated Fuzzy Delphi, partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). Data were collected from 680 Thai tourists who visited cultural destinations after exposure to tourism-related digital content. PLS-SEM showed habit had the largest path coefficient for cultural tourism intention, while UGC showed significant positive relationships with eWOM, destination image, and cultural tourism intention. Social influence, SMMA, and UGC were positively associated with eWOM, whereas price value, SMMA, UGC, and eWOM were positively associated with destination image. fsQCA highlighted the six highest-coverage configurations sufficient for high cultural tourism intention; UGC appeared in all six, while the remaining conditions acted as flexible complements. These findings highlight destination image co-creation within digital communication ecosystems and indicate high cultural tourism intention is associated with multiple configurations rather than a single pattern.

papers.title: From Answer Production to Managerial Judgment: The JUDGE Framework for Sustainable Assessment in Business Education in the Generative AI Era
papers.authors: Changyu Song, Yipeng Huang
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can produce polished business analyses without necessarily revealing who exercised judgment, how evidence was verified, or how competing consequences were weighed. This conceptual article develops JUDGE, an assessment architecture for making responsible managerial judgment observable in GenAI-enabled business education. A transparent, targeted integrative synthesis connected six bodies of literature: sustainable assessment and evaluative judgment, constructive alignment and authentic assessment, sustainability competencies and responsible management education, AI literacy and governance, reflective judgment, and contemporary GenAI pedagogy and policy. The synthesis translated five recurring validity deficits into five assessable capabilities: Justify decisions, Use AI transparently, Detect data and source problems, Grapple with trade-offs, and Evaluate outcomes and reflect. JUDGE aligns these capabilities with staged learning activities, evidence artifacts, a provisional developmental rubric, and task-level AI-use rules. Its sustainability contribution is dual: it seeks durable assessment validity as technologies change and makes economic, social, environmental, and ethical consequences visible in managerial decisions. The framework does not substitute for program-level curriculum reform or institutional AI policy; it provides an assessment layer through which those commitments can become observable. Comparison with established frameworks, two disciplinary vignettes, inclusive implementation principles, and operational propositions for empirical testing are provided. Because JUDGE and its rubric remain unvalidated, the paper presents them as design propositions for piloting, calibration, and revision rather than as established practices.

papers.title: What Drives Plastic Packaging Waste Generation in Europe? An ESG Panel with Clustering and Machine Learning Validation
papers.authors: Angelo Leogrande, Cosimo Magazzino, Alberto Costantiello, Carlo Drago, Massimo Arnone
papers.abstract: European packaging policy is built almost entirely around treatment, while the accompanying prevention obligation lacks an equivalent apparatus of measurable objectives. This article addresses this upstream question directly: what determines the quantity of plastic packaging waste that European economies place on the market? Using Eurostat data, we regress per capita plastic packaging waste on the three pillars of the World Bank Sovereign Environmental, Social and Governance framework for 29 countries between 2014 and 2023. Each pillar is examined through three modules. The first is a panel comparison of pooled, between, fixed-effects, random-effects, weighted, and dynamic estimators, with inference reassessed using a wild cluster bootstrap. The second is an unsupervised classification comparing six algorithms across eleven validity indices, with the dependent variable withheld for external validation. The third is a supervised comparison of six learners under leave-one-out cross-validation, used to validate functional form rather than to forecast. Three findings emerge. Energy intensity and carbon intensity per capita are robustly associated with generation and survive correction for multiple testing, yet environmental country types do not significantly explain differences in packaging burden. Social configurations separate generation along a binary post-transition boundary that does not survive controlling for income, and the sign reversal in life expectancy between the cross-sectional and time dimensions is confirmed independently by the learners. Internet penetration is the strongest association in the study, robust to common time effects and to income but extending to every packaging fraction and therefore not specific to delivery formats, while composite institutional quality is insignificant in every linear specification and suggests, under unrestricted functional form, a threshold rather than a gradient, a shape that a parametric test on the same cross-section cannot locate and that is therefore reported as a hypothesis. Prevention policy must therefore engage determinants beyond waste management. Among these determinants, the diffusion of online retail is currently the most informative.

papers.title: An Exploratory Qualitative Study of Postgraduate Nursing Students’ Experiences of Using GenAI in Learning Nursing Leadership
papers.authors: Hoi Man Chan, Khalil Moh'd Yousef, Ibrahim M. Alananzeh, Sarah Hatahet
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) presents immense potential to advance flipped learning approach. Yet, it is under-explored. This study presents the integration of GenAI into a nursing leadership course, guided by Bloom’s taxonomy, and explores the learning experiences of postgraduate nursing students in this GenAI-integrated flipped learning approach. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design was employed, and individual semi-structured interviews were conducted with 9 postgraduate nursing students who had completed a nursing leadership course delivered via a GenAI-integrated flipped-learning approach. Results: Three interconnected themes emerged: (1) GenAI supplements in-person learning, (2) Direct and Socratic questioning, and (3) Factors contributing to GenAI learning experience. Students appreciated that GenAI helped them summarize and understand the learning material, thereby promoting meaningful in-class activities. Students highlighted direct and Socratic questioning as the major approaches in using GenAI. Notably, Socratic questioning, AI-driven thought-provoking dialogue, helped develop higher-order thinking. However, suboptimal prompting techniques was the barrier, while channels for learning prompting and integrating it into the curriculum were facilitators. Conclusions: This study provides evidence on integrating GenAI into higher education. It also provides insights into the potential use of Socratic questioning to develop higher-order thinking in postgraduate nursing education.

papers.title: Psychological Outcomes Following Slow Cortical Potential Neurofeedback in Competitive Golfers: An Exploratory Randomized Trial
papers.authors: Eugenio Lizama, Bastian Carcamo-Herrera, Gonzalo Lopez, Carolina Pereira, Miguel Ángel Serrano
papers.abstract: Background: Slow Cortical Potential (SCP) neurofeedback trains voluntary regulation of cortical excitability states linked to anticipatory control and prefrontal executive function. In competitive sport contexts, these neural mechanisms may translate into changes in psychological constructs that shape performance under pressure. Objective: To explore between-group differences in psychological outcomes assessed during a standardized simulated putting task before and after an eight-week SCP neurofeedback program in golfers, including affective state, self-efficacy and confidence, perceived task workload, and causal attribution patterns, compared with a wait-list control condition. Methods: Forty-two active competitive golfers were randomized to a Training group (n = 21), completing an eight-week SCP neurofeedback protocol, or a wait-list Control group (n = 21). Psychological outcomes were assessed before and after the intervention during standardized competitive settings (simulated putting competitions). Validated instruments included the Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM), the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS), self-efficacy and confidence ratings, a Task Evaluation questionnaire, and a sport-adapted causal attribution checklist. Non-parametric statistics (Mann–Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank) were used where normality assumptions were not met, with rank-biserial correlation (RBC) as the effect size measure. Results: Affective dimensions (SAM valence, activation, dominance; PANAS negative affect; and STAI state anxiety) remained stable across simulated competitions in both groups. Within the Training group only, state anxiety decreased from pre- to post-task at the second simulated competition (p = 0.012), but the corresponding Group × Simulated Competition × Task-phase estimate was not significant (estimate = −1.76, 95% CI [−7.82, 4.30], p = 0.560, FDR-adjusted p = 0.958), indicating that this within-group change was not differential relative to the Control group, which changed in the same direction. Across the full direct between-group treatment contrasts, none reached statistical significance before or after false-discovery-rate correction (all raw p ≥ 0.24; all FDR-adjusted p ≥ 0.96). A within-group increase in luck attribution in the Training group (p = 0.007) reflected a fully one-directional pattern of change (rank-biserial correlation = 1.00, driven by zero decreases among the nine participants who changed) rather than an unusually large effect. Conclusions: These results did not find evidence that this eight-week SCP neurofeedback program produced differential psychological effects relative to a wait-list control. The within-group anxiety, self-efficacy, and luck-attribution patterns reported, before FDR corrections, could serve as hypothesis-generating observations.

papers.title: Classification-Guided Specialized Regression for Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Estimation: A Synthetic E-Nose Benchmark Study
papers.authors: Ehab H. El‐Shazly, Mazen Ferihy, Yazan Dia El Din, Omar Elfeky, Ahmed Khalifa, Sameh Sherif
papers.abstract: Accurate non-invasive blood glucose level (BGL) prediction remains challenging, motivating the development of machine learning approaches that can account for heterogeneity in physiological measurements. Electronic nose (E-Nose) systems provide a promising non-invasive sensing modality by capturing volatile organic compound patterns in exhaled breath. However, conventional approaches typically employ a single global regression model across the full glycemic range, despite substantial differences between diabetic and non-diabetic BGL distributions. This study investigates whether classification-guided specialization can improve BGL regression by explicitly modeling these clinically distinct subpopulations and quantifying the extent to which imperfect routing limits the resulting performance. We develop a two-stage framework in which each E-Nose sample is first classified as diabetic or non-diabetic using a stacking classifier comprising Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM with logistic regression as the meta-learner, and is then routed to a class-specific stacking regressor trained on the corresponding BGL distribution. To evaluate this architecture, the study utilizes a CTGAN-generated computational benchmark comprising 14,512 total observations synthesized from 1452 empirical breath measurements collected across 58 original human participants; these 14,512 observations do not represent independent clinical subjects. Under observation-level stratified five-fold cross-validation (not participant-disjoint), the routing classifier achieved 94.98% accuracy. The classification-guided framework reduced mean absolute error (MAE) from 25.21 mg/dL for a global stacking baseline to 24.87 mg/dL and improved the ±20% accuracy criterion from 84.95% to 88.29%. An oracle-routing analysis, using the true class labels for routing, achieved an MAE of 20.64 mg/dL and showed that the 5.02% routing error accounted for 21.08% of the total prediction error, demonstrating that routing reliability represents a major limitation on the attainable performance of specialized regression. A probabilistic soft-routing strategy was further evaluated to reduce sensitivity to hard routing decisions near the diabetic/non-diabetic boundary. Conformalized quantile regression provided distribution-free predictive uncertainty quantification, achieving 85.4% empirical coverage for a 90% nominal target, while SHAP analysis provided feature-level interpretation of the routing and regression models. Overall, the findings provide computational evidence that classification-guided specialization can improve BGL prediction over global regression on the evaluated synthetic E-Nose benchmark, while the routing-error analysis identifies a measurable performance gap attributable to imperfect subpopulation assignment. Given the synthetic nature of the benchmark, the derivation from 58 original human participants, and the absence of metadata on unmeasured clinical confounders (e.g., medication, diet, and alcohol), these findings represent preliminary computational evidence rather than clinical diagnostic validation.

papers.title: Regulated Data Standards and Disclosed AI Orientation: Evidence from the US Inline XBRL Phase-In
papers.authors: Alessio Faccia
papers.journal: Journal of risk and financial management
papers.abstract: Machine-readable reporting standards provide shared data infrastructure, while firm-side reporting associations may vary with technological disclosure. The study examines the US Inline XBRL phase-in using 1450 Form 10-K firm years from 250 CIKs over fiscal years 2014–2024. SEC filing metadata, XBRL facts, amendments, accounting controls and full-primary-document text form the analytical panel. Preferred models date exposure from the first periodic report whose SEC metadata identify Inline XBRL use and include firm and year fixed effects with firm-clustered inference. Observed entry is non-random, 41 firms are left-censored for event-time analysis, 82 firms lack observed entry, and later periods offer limited untreated support. The design therefore estimates conditional associations, not a mandate effect. None of the four reporting indicators support H1 after Holm adjustment at the 5 per cent level. Dictionary-defined AI-related disclosure breadth, described as disclosed AI orientation, yields no preferred moderation evidence, and the intangible-intensity and innovation-disclosure tests also remain insignificant after adjustment. A fully specified fixed pre-entry moderator produces two suggestive interactions with Holm-adjusted p = 0.080, without rejection at 5 per cent. Extending asset-threshold and control-omission tests across the main outcomes does not overturn that threshold-based inference. Custom-tag leads reject a flat pre-entry path. The findings distinguish disclosure breadth from verified operational capability and quantify remaining uncertainties rather than establish exact zero.

papers.title: The Psychosocial Pathways of Expectancy-Value Beliefs, Physical Fitness, and Executive Function Among Adolescents
papers.authors: Dijun Shen, Sarina Bao, Xiaoxia Zhang
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adequate physical fitness has been associated with cognitive health among adolescents, and psychosocial processes may help explain this relationship. However, evidence regarding the mechanisms linking physical fitness and cognitive health remains limited. Guided by expectancy-value theory, this study examined the direct and indirect effects of expectancy-value beliefs on executive function through physical fitness among adolescents. Methods: A prospective research design was used. Participants were 424 adolescents (58% female; Mage = 12.72 years, SD = 0.93) recruited from the southwestern United States. Physical fitness components, including cardiovascular fitness, muscular fitness, flexibility, and body mass index (BMI), were assessed using the FITNESSGRAM® test battery. Expectancy-value beliefs and executive function were measured using validated self-report instruments. Structural equation modeling was conducted to examine the proposed relationships. Results: Expectancy-value beliefs were significantly associated with all physical fitness components (rs ranged from −0.86 to 0.46, ps < 0.01) except flexibility. Cardiovascular fitness and muscular fitness were negatively associated with executive function scores (rs ranged from −0.29 to −0.21, ps < 0.01), whereas BMI was positively associated with executive function scores. The proposed model demonstrated an acceptable fit (χ2/df = 284.16/113, p < 0.001; CFI = 0.90; RMSEA = 0.06, 90% CI [0.05, 0.07]). There was a significant indirect effect of expectancy-value beliefs on executive function through physical fitness (β = −0.11). The model explained 12% of the variance in physical fitness and 9% of the variance in executive function. Conclusions: The findings provide evidence for the proposed psychosocial mediation model linking expectancy-value beliefs, physical fitness, and executive function among adolescents. It suggests strategies that strengthen perceived competence and task values may improve physical fitness and, in turn, enhance executive function.

papers.title: Exploring University Students’ Experiences of Using Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Emotional and Relational Support in Experiences of Loneliness
papers.authors: Yanyan Li, Tom Ritchie
papers.abstract: University students’ loneliness has remained a persistent concern in the years following the COVID-19 pandemic and correlates with multiple mental health issues, yet little is known about how university students experiencing loneliness use conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) for emotional and relational support. This exploratory qualitative study addressed that gap by exploring how students in a UK university experiencing loneliness perceived their use of CAI for emotional and relational support, and how they positioned CAI alongside other coping strategies. Sixteen students scoring 3 or above on the De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Situating loneliness within students’ wider social and relational lives at university, four themes were developed: CAI as a low-barrier emotional outlet, free from the social costs of human disclosure; a perceived objective reflective sense-making partner that helped organise overwhelming experiences; a pragmatic response to gaps in existing support networks; and a supplement rather than a permanent substitute for human care, approached with critical awareness of its limitations. Students’ use of CAI appeared to reflect unmet relational needs within their existing social networks, rather than an absence of social contact or a preference for AI over people. The study concludes by discussing implications for sector-wide institutional guidance on the responsible governance of AI in relation to student mental health and calls on universities to engage more openly with how AI is shaping students’ lives beyond academic work.

papers.title: Quality-of-Life and Weight Loss Outcomes Following an Individualized Nutrition and Physical Activity Counseling Program in Breast Cancer Survivors: A Prospective Single-Arm Pilot Study
papers.authors: К. Шаші, Ahmad Alhalabi, Nadeem Bilani, Iktej Singh Jabbal, María Herrán, Theresa Abdo, Saad Sabbagh, Kaylee Sarna, Amanda Stevenson, Diana Saravia, Candice Schwartz, Thomas A. Samuel, Zeina A. Nahleh, Elizabeth Stone
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Assess the feasibility of a 6-month individualized nutrition counseling and exercise program targeting a 10% body weight loss in breast cancer (BC) survivors, with secondary endpoints assessing metabolic parameters, cardiovascular function, and quality of life. METHODS: in a counseling program with a registered dietitian, consisting of in-person and telephone visits over six months. Outcomes measured included weight, body composition, blood markers, cardiovascular function, and quality of life at 3 and 6 months. RESULTS: A total of 78 breast cancer survivors were enrolled; 59 remained in the study at Month 3, and 54 completed the 6-month follow-up. The median age of participants was 58.5 years, and the cohort was predominantly White (72.4%). Among the 54 participants who completed 6-month follow-up, 11.1% achieved >10% weight loss and 29.6% achieved >5% weight loss. At 3 months, significant reductions were observed in BMI, body fat composition, and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), along with improvements in quality of life, depression, and anxiety. At 6 months, significant reductions were observed in weight, BMI, and body fat composition, with improvements in quality of life and depressive symptoms. CONCLUSIONS: This hybrid nutrition and exercise program was associated with observed improvements in weight loss and improved quality of life among BC survivors. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: A low-burden, hybrid nutrition and exercise program integrated into routine oncology follow-up may help breast cancer survivors achieve weight loss while improving their quality of life.

papers.title: Visual Perception Within the Built Environment of Traditional Villages in Karst Areas: Exploring Multidimensional Associations of Landscape Features
papers.authors: Yanzhen Li, Sijia Zhu, Kai Wang, Siyi Jiang, Weiqi Li, Wenjun Zheng
papers.abstract: Traditional villages in karst natural heritage areas are distinctive rural built environments where natural, cultural, and landscape elements intertwine. Identifying relationships between built-environment characteristics and visual preference is important for improving spatial quality and supporting sustainable tourism. This study examined Jiuxian Village in Guilin, China, using stimulus–organism–response (S-O-R) theory to develop an indicator framework. We collected 194 panoramic images and recruited 72 university students to evaluate visual quality using Scenic Beauty Estimation (SBE) and Semantic Differential (SD) methods. Image features were quantified through computer vision, and machine-learning models combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were applied for interpretation. Visual order and immediate affective responses were positively associated with SBE, whereas sense of history showed a weaker direct association with SBE than these two dimensions. Visible natural elements and color richness contributed positively, while building coverage, hardscape, and public facilities contributed negatively. Natural and anthropogenic elements displayed nonlinear predictive patterns, with SHAP contributions varying across proportional ranges, as well as positive, negative, and conditional joint predictive patterns. These findings provide guidance for landscape planning and spatial-quality improvement in traditional villages within karst environments.

papers.title: Human Factors in Brain–Computer Interfaces: Boundaries, Key Issues, and Methodological Approaches
papers.authors: Liu Yan, Tianwen Li, Lei Zhao, Anmin Gong, Fang Hao, Wuheng Zuo, Yunfa Fu
papers.abstract: The large-scale, real-world deployment of brain–computer interface (BCI) is confronted with human factors bottlenecks, including reliability and usability. While modern human factors engineering has encompassed domains such as cognitive ergonomics, workload, adaptive automation, and human-in-the-loop systems, its theories and methodologies have historically placed their main emphasis on overt behavior and peripheral physiological measures, rather than on central neural activity as a primary control input. For the emerging interaction paradigm that takes central nervous activity as direct input and emphasizes long-term brain–computer co-adaptation, there remains a shortage of targeted conceptual and methodological frameworks. As a conceptual review, this paper discusses the necessity and disciplinary foundations for developing Human Factors Engineering for BCIs as an emerging interdisciplinary research direction. First, grounded in the defining features of BCI interaction—such as the implicit nature of input and brain–computer co-adaptation—it delineates the research boundaries and summarizes the core research objects as user neurocognitive characteristics, brain–computer collaborative adaptation mechanisms, multimodal feedback regulation, and contextual adaptation patterns. Second, it identifies three core scientific questions: individual differences and dynamic adaptation, human factors optimization and fault tolerance, and contextual generalizability principles, with ethics, privacy, and user rights and interests as an overarching dimension. Furthermore, it constructs a methodological system consisting of multimodal measurement and modeling, closed-loop validation, and multidimensional evaluation, and examines the supporting role of artificial intelligence approaches within this framework. Centered on the collaborative adaptation across neural, cognitive, and system levels, Human Factors Engineering for BCIs represents a deepening of the human-centered design philosophy. It provides theoretical reference for user-friendly BCI design and extends the research boundaries of human factors engineering.

papers.title: THE CIRCULAR CREATIVE ECONOMY: SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN COMMERCIAL PHOTOGRAPHY AND DESIGN PRODUCTION
papers.authors: Syaifudin, Gagas Nir Galing, Hanifiana Kartikasari, Widya Devilowa Amir
papers.journal: Proceeding of The International Seminar on Business Economics Social Science and Technology (ISBEST)
papers.abstract: Global economic uncertainty and the climate crisis demand fundamental transformations across various sectors, including the creative industry. Conventional commercial photography and visual communication design production often generate a substantial carbon footprint through material waste, excessive energy consumption, and high logistical mobility. This paper explores the integration of circular economy principles and digital transformation within visual production workflows as a strategic response to these sustainability challenges. This research aims to analyze how the adoption of disruptive technologies - such as generative artificial intelligence, virtual production, and cloud computing - can reduce carbon emissions while simultaneously enhancing operational cost efficiency. The methodology employs a systematic literature review alongside qualitative case studies of creative agencies that have implemented sustainable workflows. Findings indicate that the digitalization of creative processes effectively eliminates physical waste, notably excessive sample printing and single-use practical set constructions. Furthermore, the transition toward a virtual production ecosystem is proven to drastically minimize logistical expenses, thereby bolstering the financial resilience of industry practitioners amidst a fragmented global economy. Leveraging cutting-edge technology also substantially accelerates project turnaround times without compromising aesthetic design quality. In conclusion, the adoption of digital technologies is not merely a fleeting aesthetic trend but an essential catalyst for establishing a circular and inclusive creative economy. This innovative transformation empowers visual communication designers and professional photographers to remain productive, relevant, and highly competitive globally. Ultimately, these crucial economic milestones can be achieved while practitioners uphold strong ethical responsibilities toward ecological preservation and the development of future-proof business models.

papers.title: Argumentación e Inteligencia Artificial en las Políticas y el Currículo de Colombia: Análisis Crítico de los Marcos UNESCO, CONPES 4144 y DBA
papers.authors: Hector Enrique Banquez Buendia
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION. The rise of generative artificial intelligence is reshaping the conditions of rational argumentation, yet policy and curriculum instruments do not fully articulate how this transformation affects its teaching as a critical competence. OBJECTIVE. To critically analyse the presence and treatment of argumentation, critical literacy and AI-related competencies in four documents organised across three analytical levels: UNESCO frameworks for students and teachers, Colombia’s CONPES 4144, and the Language Basic Learning Rights. METHOD. Qualitative documentary content analysis with a critical orientation, using nine non-exclusive categories grouped into three dimensions and applied to 862 propositional units. RESULTS. The documents reveal a disarticulated complementarity: the Language Basic Learning Rights concentrate argumentative progression and critical literacy; the UNESCO frameworks incorporate limited practices of evaluation and deliberation, and a narrow presence of citizenship as an agent in relation to AI; and CONPES develops adoption, capacity-building, ethics and governance with less curricular articulation of argumentation. Only 15 units in the corpus simultaneously integrated the three dimensions. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS. The observed discontinuity is not a chronological chain of recontextualisation, but an interdocumentary misalignment and an updating gap in the curricular instrument analysed. The study contributes a reusable category system and guidelines for linking argumentative education with the justified evaluation of AI-generated results.

papers.title: Hybrid AI framework for customer churn classification and business risk assessment
papers.authors: Aritra Pal
papers.journal: Journal of Computer Science and Technology Studies
papers.abstract: Customer turnover is a major problem in the telecom sector, Consequently, identifying clients who are most likely to depart might aid in retention decisions. Single-model methods might lack the flexibility to represent complex customer behavior, and class imbalance can impact the identification of churn cases. This study introduces a framework for churn prediction based on machine-learning (ML) techniques that employs CatBoost, LightGBM and XGBoost as base learners and Logistic Regression as a meta-learner in the Stacking Ensemble. The framework utilizes data pre-processing, domain knowledge-based feature engineering, outlier detection, and SMOTE class imbalance techniques for enhancing predictive learning. Feature engineering and SMOTE are incorporated to improve the learning process. Experimental results demonstrate that Stacking Ensemble obtains an accuracy of 81.10%, a recall of 60.86%, an F1-score of 63.08%, and an ROC-AUC of 84.60%, whereas XGBoost scores the best ROC-AUC of 84.63%. Furthermore, churn probabilities are predicted and utilized for customer risk segmentation and financial impact assessment, helping to identify customer groups that have a higher potential revenue exposure. In summary, proposed framework shows the potential of ensemble ML for churn prediction and offers data-driven insights to help companies prioritize customer retention and protect revenue in the telecom industry.

papers.title: Integrating Explainable AI with Advanced Data Visualization: Enhancing Transparency and Decision-Making in Complex Systems
papers.authors: Harvinder Singh
papers.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology
papers.abstract: [1]. Arh, T., & Blaži, B. J. (2007). Application of Multi-Attribute Decision Making Approach to Learning Management Systems Evaluation . JOURNAL OF COMPUTERS, 2(10), 28-37. [2]. BÂRA, A., BOTHA, I., LUNGU, I., & OPREA, S. V. (2013). Decision Support System in National Power Companies A Practical Example (Part I) . Database Systems Journal, IV(1), 37-45. The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, and cybersecurity has intensified concerns about the opacity of complex models, which undermines stakeholder trust and slows adoption. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) addresses this by producing justifications for model decisions, yet such justifications are typically delivered as raw textual or numerical output that many stakeholders find difficult to interpret. This paper proposes a conceptual framework that integrates XAI with advanced data visualization, treating visualization as a first-class layer of the explanation pipeline rather than an afterthought: post-hoc attribution methods supply explanation content, and purpose-designed visual encodings — heatmaps, feature-importance dashboards, and decision-path graphs — supply a cognitively efficient form. Beyond the framework, the paper specifies a standardized, falsifiable evaluation protocol spanning three benchmark domains and seven measurable constructs — explanation satisfaction, objective understanding, decision accuracy, cognitive load, subjective trust, calibrated trust, and decision confidence — with directional hypotheses grounded in perceptual and cognitive-explanation theory. A structured results-reporting design is included to support immediate empirical application. The primary contribution is the framework, the measurement standard, and the evaluation protocol.

papers.title: Is Critical Thinking the Main Educational Goal in the Era of Artificial Intelligence?
papers.authors: Andrey Ivanovich Rudskoy, С. В. Кабышев, Pavel I. Romanov
papers.abstract: In the third millennium, humanity has entered an era of tumultuous change. The emerging problems and the search for ways to solve them require a new understanding on the part of the scientific community, which primarily involves reassessing values on the civilizational and historical scales of national interests and, as a result, getting rid of entrenched stereotypes and myths, including those stemming from blind imitation of ideas and methodological concepts that once seemed cutting-edge. In this regard, particular attention and thorough analysis are required for the pedagogical approaches and attitudes that determine the formation of guiding ideas for a person’s decision-making, their attitude towards the world and their homeland, and their professional, managerial, and everyday logic. Within the framework of this article, it is proposed to take a close look at the concept of “critical thinking,” which is widely used in professional circles, as well as its genesis and semantic elements. The risks associated with the concept of “critical thinking” are significantly increasing, primarily due to the widespread adoption and development of generative artificial intelligence. This work does not claim to provide an exhaustive or “final” judgment on the truth. On the contrary, it proposes to examine “critical thinking” in the context of the objective complexity and multidimensionality that makes this phenomenon the subject of such acute ideological and pedagogical contradictions. The article focuses on those aspects of “critical thinking” that are systematically silenced in liberal pedagogical discourse. Accordingly, the use of “complementarity optics” in this work makes it possible to obtain a comprehensive picture in order to make a well-considered decision about the appropriateness of using the ambiguous and context-rich concept of “critical thinking” in Russian educational realities and prospects.

papers.title: Cognitive and Non-Cognitive Predictors of Educational Profile Choice: An Analysis of Fields of Study Using Machine Learning
papers.authors: Sergey B. Malykh, Viсtoria I. Ismatullina, Timofey Adamovich, Pavel V. Kolyasnikov, Малых Артем Сергеевич
papers.abstract: This article presents the results of a study on cognitive and non-cognitive predictors of university educational profile choice. The sample included 6,290 students from 23 Russian univer- sities (37.6% males, 62.4% females, aged 17–24 years). Academic fields were aggregated into five macro-groups: humanities, natural sciences, pedagogy, social sciences and economics, and technical sciences. Cognitive abilities were assessed using intelligence tests (Raven’s matrices), working mem- ory, spatial abilities (rotation, visualization, relations), and reaction time. Non-cognitive character- istics were measured using questionnaires for math anxiety, mental toughness, and psychological well-being. Statistical analysis included multifactorial ANCOVA and predictive modeling using ran- dom forest. The results showed that the field of study is associated with differences in cognitive and personality profiles, with spatial abilities contributing the most (η 2 up to 0.030). Students in techni- cal fields demonstrated higher cognitive performance, while humanities students exhibited lower well-being and higher math anxiety. Gender significantly affected spatial abilities and non-cognitive characteristics but not general intelligence or working memory. The combined machine learning model achieved an accuracy of 39.7% (against a baseline of 29.1%). A discrepancy between actual and desired major choice was found to be primarily related to cognitive mismatch. Gender-specific patterns were identified: spatial abilities play a leading role for males, whereas general intelligence and psychological well-being are more important for females. These findings can be applied in career guidance and educational practices.

papers.title: The Centaur Situation: The Grounds and Limits of the Cognitive Alliance
papers.authors: Земцов Дмитрий Игоревич, Ivan Gruzdev, V. S. Nikolskiy, R. M. Ganzha, Sergey Startsev, Токарев Алексей Александрович
papers.abstract: The Epistemic Centaur Manifesto, published in this issue, proposes a strategy of alliance between the human researcher and artificial intelligence in the human and social sciences. Its proposi- tions are stated as theses, without argument or references, and this article sets out the grounds on which they rest and clarifies the points that invite disagreement. Drawing on recent research literature, the authors show that generative models are already built into every stage of the research cycle, from hy- pothesis formation and literature reviews to synthetic respondents, the recovery of missing survey data, machine interviewers, text annotation and statistical coding. The authors call this state of affairs the cen- taur situation, one in which researchers find themselves whether or not they have chosen the alliance. To analyse it, the article develops the distinction between the functional agency of artificial systems and human subjectivity that proposition 2.2 of the Manifesto introduces, and shows that the irreducibility of a result to the contributions of its participants does not rule out disclosing what the machine did. The article then takes up the objection that responsibility for a conclusion the researcher does not fully understand becomes a ritual admission of guilt, and argues that such responsibility is meaningful as long as the researcher retains the right to reject a conclusion and verifies it in proportion to its consequences. Finally, experimental evidence on human-machine collaboration gives no support to the idea that the alliance is productive in itself, which is precisely why the demands of personal discipline, of a community of practice and of rethinking the aims of university education carry the weight they do.

papers.title: The Manifesto of the Epistemic Centaur: Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Research Cycle of the Human and Social Sciences
papers.authors: Земцов Дмитрий Игоревич, V. S. Nikolskiy, F. E. Azhimov, Андрей Александрович Андрюшков, R. M. Ganzha, Ivan Gruzdev, M. I. Matveeva, Yu. O. Molodykh, D. S. Putiltsev, M. V. Sergeeva, Sergey Startsev, Evgeniy Terentev, Токарев Алексей Александрович, Валерий Валерьевич Федоров, A.I. Fedoseev, Антоний Швиндт, Ilya Yaskov
papers.abstract: The Manifesto of the Epistemic Centaur is a programmatic statement on the con- dition of the human and social sciences amid the spread of generative artificial intelligence. Its authors argue that these sciences are losing their primacy in explaining their own subject matter and their control over the language in which it is described, because the pace of social change and the rate at which quick and simple answers are produced now outrun the slower work of building well-grounded knowledge. The proposed response is the epistemic centaur – a single functional subject of inquiry within whose shared cognitive circuit human consciousness and artificial intelligence carry out cognitive work together. What such a circuit yields cannot be reduced to the contributions of its participants, while responsibility for the result rests entirely with the researcher. Knowledge produced by the centaur deserves the same standing in science as knowledge produced by a human being, provided that the character of the interaction is disclosed, the findings are verified, and responsibility is accepted. This strategy can be carried forward by a horizontal community of practice, and sustaining it over the long term calls for rethinking the aims of university education.

papers.title: PENGUATAN LITERASI DIGITAL GURU SEKOLAH DASAR MELALUI PELATIHAN GEMINI AI DALAM PENGEMBANGAN GAME EDUKASI INTERAKTIF
papers.authors: Tiffany Shahnaz Rusli, Chelsi Yuliana S, Suci Sugiana
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Kegiatan pengabdian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya literasi digital guru sekolah dasar dalam memanfaatkan kecerdasan buatan (AI) sebagai media pembelajaran interaktif, sementara siswa generasi digital cenderung lebih tertarik pada permainan digital dibandingkan metode pembelajaran konvensional. Tujuan pengabdian ini adalah meningkatkan kompetensi guru dalam memanfaatkan Gemini AI untuk merancang game edukasi interaktif serta meningkatkan motivasi dan hasil belajar siswa. Mitra kegiatan adalah 10 guru dan 5 kelas SD Inpres yang berlokasi di kampung Ampas, Provinsi Papua. Metode pelaksanaan meliputi workshop literasi AI, pelatihan desain game edukasi berbasis project-based learning, pendampingan intensif, dan implementasi di kelas dengan evaluasi menggunakan instrumen pretest-posttest sebanyak 15 soal dan angket motivasi belajar sebanyak 20 pernyataan. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan 85% guru mampu memanfaatkan Gemini AI secara mandiri, dihasilkan lima produk game edukasi interaktif, motivasi belajar siswa meningkat 23%, dan hasil belajar siswa meningkat 18% pada materi yang diujikan. Kegiatan ini terbukti efektif meningkatkan literasi digital guru dan menghadirkan pembelajaran yang lebih interaktif, kontekstual, dan menyenangkan.Abstract: This community service program was motivated by the low digital literacy of elementary school teachers in utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) as an interactive learning medium, while digital-native students tend to be more interested in games than conventional learning methods. The program aimed to improve teachers competence in using Gemini AI to design interactive educational games and to increase students learning motivation and outcomes. The partners were ten teachers and five classes at a state elementary school (SD Inpres) located in Kampung Ampas, Papua Province. The method consisted of an AI literacy workshop, project-based training in educational game design, intensive mentoring, and classroom implementation, evaluated using a 15 item pretest-posttest and a 20 staetement learning motivation questionnaire. The results showed that 85% of teachers were able to use Gemini AI independently, five interactive educational games were produced, student learning motivation increased by 23%, and learning outcomes increased by 18% on the tested material. The program proved effective in strengthening teachers digital literacy and creating more interactive, contextual, and enjoyable learning.

papers.title: PENDAMPINGAN GURU PENDIDIKAN ANAK USIA DINI DALAM PENGEMBANGAN MEDIA PEMBELAJARAN INTERAKTIF BERBASIS SCRATCH DAN AI GENERATIF
papers.authors: Sulthonika Mahfudz Al Mujahidin, Farah Zakiyah Rahmanti, Mustafa Kamal, Moch. Iskandar Riansyah, Khodijah Amiroh, Cisa Valentino Cahya Ramadhani, I Made Wisnu Adi Sanjaya, Nur Alifia Rustan, Adistya Rahayu
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Pengembangan media pembelajaran pada pendidikan anak usia dini memerlukan kemampuan guru menghubungkan tema, cerita, aset visual, suara, dan logika pemrograman, sedangkan pengalaman pemrograman berbasis blok pada mitra masih terbatas. Kegiatan ini bertujuan mengembangkan keterampilan teknis 13 guru pendidikan anak usia dini dari sekolah mitra dalam merancang media berbasis Scratch dengan dukungan AI generatif. Pendampingan berbasis proyek dilaksanakan melalui demonstrasi, praktik terpandu, kerja kelompok, dan presentasi pada tahap perencanaan, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi. Peserta merumuskan cerita, menyiapkan aset dengan ChatGPT dan ElevenLabs, menyusun blok, menguji, memperbaiki, dan mempresentasikan proyek. Monitoring menggunakan observasi langsung, sedangkan evaluasi menggunakan kuesioner berisi 15 pernyataan tertutup dan 3 pertanyaan terbuka. Keberhasilan ditinjau dari ketercapaian minimal satu proyek per kelompok dan respons pada indikator teknis utama. Tiga kelompok menghasilkan lima proyek. Respons positif mencapai 100% pada pemahaman dasar pemrograman berbasis blok, perancangan media, kemudahan antarmuka, dan komitmen penerapan, sedangkan sequencing dan troubleshooting mencapai 92,3%. Hasil menunjukkan penerimaan dan kesiapan awal peserta.Abstract: Developing learning media for early childhood education requires teachers to connect themes, stories, visual and audio assets, and programming logic, while the partner’s experience with block-based programming remained limited. This program aimed to develop the technical skills of 13 early childhood teachers from a partner school in designing Scratch-based learning media with generative AI support. Project-based mentoring used demonstrations, guided practice, group work, and presentations across planning, implementation, and evaluation stages. Participants formulated stories, prepared assets with ChatGPT and ElevenLabs, arranged blocks, tested, revised, and presented projects. Monitoring used direct observation, while evaluation employed a questionnaire containing 15 closed-ended statements and 3 open-ended questions. Success was assessed through the achievement of at least one project per group and responses to key technical indicators. Three groups produced five projects. Positive responses reached 100% for basic block-based programming understanding, media design, interface ease, and implementation commitment, while sequencing and troubleshooting reached 92.3%. These findings indicate participants’ acceptance and initial readiness.

papers.title: Cruelty Across Substrates: From Animal Cruelty to Embodied AI and the Coming Detection Gap
papers.authors: Travis Gilly
papers.abstract: Childhood cruelty to animals is among the most durable behavioral warning signs of later interpersonalviolence in the forensic and clinical literature. The predictive mechanism does not rest on any settledanswer about the moral status of the target. It rests on what the perpetrator practices, rehearses, andtrains in themselves: desensitization, dominance affect, and the social learning of cruelty as pleasure.This paper offers a conceptual continuity argument and research agenda. We argue that the substrateof the target is incidental to that training, with one critical qualification: the configuration of the targetmatters. Routine digital destruction in static media (the static video game target, the scripted non playercharacter) is a categorically different case from the closed loop, contingent emotional response systemson which the argument turns. As world models, embodied robotics, and closed loop emotional voicesystems converge toward agents that perform distress in ways a user cannot reliably distinguish from abeing in pain, we argue that the dispositional consequences of practiced cruelty against those agents arelikely to recruit sufficiently similar mechanisms to warrant clinical and forensic attention. The paper doesnot claim that synthetic agents are moral patients. It claims that the warning signal forensic and clinicalfields have relied upon for fifty years risks migrating to a venue with substantially diminished detectioninfrastructure. Existing human robot interaction research already shows that users do not need to believea synthetic agent is conscious to respond to it through social, emotional, or dominance based scripts. TheKantian observation that cruelty corrupts the cruel is sufficient to ground the argument. Conduct disorderassessment, character evidence frameworks, school counseling protocols, and pre employment screeningfor sensitive roles will need to adapt or lose one of the more durable early behavioral indicators availableto forensic and clinical assessment. The paper is offered as agenda setting; the operational protocols itidentifies as necessary are deliberately scoped to a planned companion paper.

papers.title: Return-to-office (RTO) is multidimensional: Attendance level and trajectory predict different employee outcomes
papers.authors: Yingyue Luna Luan, Yeun Joon Kim, Pengzhao Lyu, Soo Min Toh
papers.abstract: Organizations increasingly require employees to return to the office, yet evidence on the consequences of return-to-office (RTO) policies remains limited and typically treats RTO as a binary change. We propose a multidimensional perspective of RTO that distinguishes attendance-level— the proportion of time employees spend in the office over a given period—from attendance-trajectory—changes in attendance over time. Analyzing 13,956 employee-month observations from badge-swipe records for 1,163 employees whose attendance remained stable or increased at a multinational financial services organization over 12 months, we examined how these two dimensions related to ten subsequent outcomes: job performance, stress and burnout, three perceptions of organizational culture, and four forms of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and utilization. Attendance-level and attendance-trajectory showed distinct patterns of association across outcome domains. For job performance, overall attendance-level was unrelated to subsequent performance; instead, a faster increase in attendance predicted lower performance. Well-being showed the opposite pattern: higher overall and initial attendance-level predicted greater stress and burnout, while trajectory was unrelated to either outcome. Culture perceptions and AI adoption showed more complex patterns involving both dimensions, with higher or increasing attendance generally linked to more positive culture perceptions and deeper AI engagement, though the relevant dimension differed by outcome. These findings indicate that attendance-level and attendance-trajectory are not interchangeable and carry benefits in some domains while imposing costs in others. RTO policies should be designed and evaluated according to both how much and how quickly attendance increases, rather than being assumed uniformly beneficial or harmful.

papers.title: Intelligent Immersive Accessibility: A Systematic Review of AI-Enhanced Virtual Reality Interaction Design for Inclusive and Equitable Education
papers.authors: Kudakwashe Maguraushe, Bester Chimbo, Fine Masimba
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Informatics and Computing
papers.abstract: This study systematically synthesises findings about artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced virtual reality (VR) and extended reality (XR) systems developed for accessibility and inclusive education. It examines the architectural, implementation, and evaluation principles behind AI-infused immersive learning environments as adaptive systems for educational contexts. We conducted a systematic literature review following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We searched Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and ERIC databases for peer-reviewed articles published between 2021 and 2025. Only nine of those studies ultimately met the screening and eligibility criteria. The included studies were assessed through a structured narrative synthesis, which examined AI integration patterns, immersive interaction design, accessibility operationalisation, evaluation maturity, and architectural contributions. The study revealed that AI integration occurs mainly at the perceptual layer, including recognition, classification, and translation, but the system lacks a complete closed-loop adaptive architecture that connects learner modelling with real-time personalisation and longitudinal learning analytics. Interaction design is largely disability-dependent, while evaluation methods often choose between usability and system performance testing, and between system performance testing and educational outcome assessment. Architectural contributions exist as separate modules that fail to integrate accessibility, adaptive intelligence, pedagogy, and governance into a cohesive system. The Intelligent Immersive Accessibility Framework (IIAF), a conceptual, evidence-traceable but not yet empirically validated layered architecture, addresses this fragmentation. The emerging nature of AI-based immersive accessibility research helps explain why only a few studies were included, and why the field needs research that spans multiple contexts and extends over longer periods.

papers.title: Human-Centric Explanainable AI as a Catalyst for Responsible AI Adoption in Higher Education
papers.authors: Fine Masimba, Bester Chimbo, Kudakwashe Maguraushe
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Informatics and Computing
papers.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into academic workflows, the limited explainability of advanced AI models poses significant ethical and operational challenges, particularly in the Global South.This study proposes and validates an Extended Human-Centric Explainable AI (H-XAI) Adoption Framework within the context of Zimbabwean Higher Education. Utilizing a quantitative approach (N = 372 university students), regression analysis was employed to examine the relationships amongst five critical H-XAI constructs which are perceived interpretability, algorithm transparency, ethical alignment, AI literacy and human oversight together with traditional adoption drivers that include perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, attitude and behavioral intention. Results demonstrate that the model explains 62% of the variance in Behavioral Intention (R2 = .62). Findings reveal that ethical alignment (β = .48, p < 0.001) and human oversight (β = .44, p < 0.001) are the strongest predictors of responsible AI adoption, while perceived interpretability (β=0.42, p < 0.001) significantly shapes Attitude. The implications for institutional governance and curriculum design are discussed, providing a roadmap for sustainable AI integration in resource-constrained educational environments.

papers.title: Penguatan Literasi Digital dan Kompetensi AI Guru Madrasah melalui Prinsip CEK untuk Mendukung Inovasi dan Pengembangan Profesional
papers.authors: Dwi Noviani, Meirina AlKhoiriah, Aidah Aidah, Muttaqin Muttaqin
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) offers teachers new opportunities to design learning activities, develop instructional materials, prepare assessments, and support professional learning. Its use, however, requires critical digital literacy so that technological outputs are not accepted without verification and ethical consideration. This community service program sought to strengthen digital literacy and AI-related competencies among 20 teachers at MA Al-Muawanah Pemulutan. Conducted on 6 August 2026, the program combined conceptual input, discussion, demonstration, guided practice, and reflection. This article adopts a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were drawn from observational notes, participants' responses during discussions, and reflections collected throughout the activity, and were examined by organizing the material, grouping related meanings, and developing themes. The analysis identified source credibility assessment and the distinction between factual information and misinformation or hoaxes as the most salient needs. In response, AI literacy was introduced through the CEK principle: Cermati hasil (scrutinize outputs), Etis penggunaannya (use ethically), and Kembangkan kembali (revise and develop further). The findings suggest that information literacy should underpin the use of AI for lesson planning, material development, assessment, research, and professional learning. Because the program did not employ pre- and post-intervention measures, the findings should not be interpreted as quantitative evidence of effectiveness. Follow-up assessment of teacher-produced work, classroom practices, and competencies over time is required.

papers.title: Kesiapan dan Kebutuhan Guru SMP dalam Koding dan Kecerdasan Artifisial: Analisis Awal untuk Perancangan Pelatihan di Kabupaten Bantul
papers.authors: Zaenal Mustofa, Ratna Wardani, Nurkhamid Nurkhamid, Agus Qomaruddin Munir, Ramadhana Setiyawan
papers.abstract: Coding and Artificial Intelligence (AI) literacy have become important competencies for teachers in facing 21st-century educational demands, yet their integration into junior high school (SMP) instruction is often limited by teachers' conceptual and practical readiness. This article reports the initial needs-identification stage of a community service program designed to strengthen SMP teachers' readiness in coding and AI (referred to jointly as KKA) in Bantul Regency, Yogyakarta, as an empirical basis for designing subsequent contextual training. A needs-assessment questionnaire was administered to 19 SMP teachers across subject areas in Bantul Regency, covering profile, prior coding/AI teaching experience, perceived challenges, current media use, and perceptions of augmented reality (AR) as a potential learning medium. Results show that 58% of respondents had never taught coding or AI, and technical topics such as algorithms and machine learning were rarely covered (11%), while the most frequently reported obstacle was students' heterogeneous prior ability (79%) rather than low student motivation. Respondents reported strong perceived importance of AR-based learning features, particularly step-by-step guidance (mean score 4.47/5) and adaptive content (4.42/5), along with positive self-reported attitudes toward AR adoption (behavioral intention score 4.37/5) despite limited prior AR experience. As these findings are self-reported perceptions and needs rather than measured competency outcomes, they are interpreted as an empirical baseline indicating that practice-based, subject-contextual training accompanied by continuous mentoring is a relevant strategy to address the identified coding and AI competency gap, and that AR is a promising direction for learning-media development in the next stage of the 2026-2030 community service roadmap.

papers.title: Pengembangan Media Pembelajaran Roda Berputar Digital Berbasis Artificial Intelligence (AI) untuk Pemecahan Masalah Belajar IPAS Siswa Kelas IV Sekolah Dasar
papers.authors: Muhammad Wafa Rifqia, Candra Tri Utami
papers.journal: Jurnal Pendidikan Sains Geologi dan Geofisika (GeoScienceEd Journal)
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Digital Spinning Wheel learning media to improve the problem-solving skills of fourth-grade elementary school students on the topic of changes in the state of matter, as well as to determine its feasibility, practicality, and effectiveness. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE model, consisting of Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation stages.
