We therefore evaluate closure with three tests: closure accuracy, reported against this rule and within each source; evidence dependence, which removes the grounds of a conclusion and checks whether the model stops closing; and conclusion and gap quality, a judged checklist of what the model asserts and what it says is missing. We build Nautil, 731 audited cases from aviation, rail, maritime, chemical-safety and vehicle-defect reports and production server incidents, with teacher trajectories, an out-of-distribution test set and counterfactual evidence versions. Fine-tuning a 9B model on these trajectories makes its closures follow the evidence: removing the grounds lowers its closure rate by 26 points relative to a matched control, overstatement falls from 97% to 35%, and correct, non-overstated conclusions rise from 3% to 43%. Reinforcement learning that rewards only the closure decision then raises balanced accuracy from 69.2 to 83.3, on par with the teacher, and within-source accuracy from 60.4 to 74.1, at some cost in evidence dependence.

papers.title: OptiSelect: How does the Optimizer Shape Data Curriculum?
papers.authors: Simin Fan, Alireza Abdollahpoorrostam, Martin Jaggi
papers.abstract: Online data selection has demonstrated substantial efficiency gains for LLM pretraining by training on the most valuable candidates within each batch. Since a candidate's value is realized through its effective model update, principled selection should account for the optimizer step, which reshapes the raw gradient before it updates model parameters. We formalize this optimizer-aware selection paradigm as OptiSelect and present the first systematic study of how the optimizer shapes data selection. Our theory establishes a selection gain principle in which the advantage of online selection is governed by the discriminability of the optimizer-induced utility scores. We prove that sign-based and polar-tangential preconditioners of Lion and Muon would suffer from a discriminability collapse which caps attainable gains from OptiSelect, whereas diagonal-adaptive optimizers such as AdamW and Sophia admit strictly better upper bounds. The proposed principle also yields a quantitative derivation of the optimal candidate oversampling ratio. Pretraining experiments on 124M and 720M models are consistent with our theoretical analysis and show that AdamW's diagonal-adaptive scoring geometry remains the strongest scoring geometry even with Muon as optimizer. We further demonstrate that OptiSelect retains its benefits under data rephrasing, a technique used in modern data processing pipelines. Our findings provide theoretical foundations and practical guidance for co-designing optimizers and data selection in LLM pretraining.

papers.title: MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v1.0
papers.authors: Carsten Maple, Cagatay Yucel, Isaac Holeman, Chris Knotz, Peter R. Mattson, James Goel, Jonathan Petit, Sean McGregor, James Ezick, Abhishek Kumar, Alicia Parrish, Murali Krishna Emani, Kashyap Iyer, Faiza Khan Khattak, Washington Enyinna Mbonu, Daniel A. Machlab, Eileen Long, Shaona Ghosh, Jibin Varghese, Roman Lutz, Andrew Gruen, Bennett Hillenbrand, Prabal Gupta, Mohammed Serrhini, Dhivya Nagasubramanian, Aakash Gupta, Jun, Lu, Kurt Bollacker, Chang Liu, Jonathan Petit, Cong Chen, Jean-Philippe Monteuuis, Brent Miller, Apurv Verma, Roman Eng, Armstrong Tita Foundjem, Mohammed Serrhini
papers.abstract: Modern AI systems are designed to refuse hazardous requests. A jailbreak is a prompt crafted to bypass those safeguards and elicit outputs that the system would normally refuse to provide. The MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v1.0 provides an end-to-end methodology for evaluating the robustness of large language models to single-turn, text-based jailbreak attacks. It combines criteria-driven system and attack selection, paired baseline and adversarial evaluation, human annotation, automated evaluator calibration, scoring, grading, and risk-calibrated disclosure within a single benchmarking pipeline. The benchmark evaluates eight open-weight systems using 264 seed prompts spanning eleven hazard categories and representative attacks drawn from the MLCommons Jailbreak Taxonomy. Responses are assessed using the AILuminate Assessment Standard v1.4, and robustness is measured through the Resilience Gap: the change in safety performance between baseline and adversarial conditions. Across all evaluated systems and attacks, the unsafe-response rate increased from 11.08% under baseline conditions to 18.65% under jailbreak conditions, producing an average Resilience Gap of 7.57%. Accessible systems showed a larger mean gap, while attack effectiveness varied substantially across attack categories and hazards. The benchmark also examines evaluator reliability and sources of measurement error. Beyond reporting results, Jailbreak Benchmark v1.0 establishes a reproducible methodological foundation for comparative jailbreak evaluation and for future expansion across systems, attacks, hazards, and evaluation methods.

papers.title: Return-to-office (RTO) is multidimensional: Attendance level and trajectory predict different employee outcomes
papers.authors: Soo Min Toh, Yeun Joon Kim, Pengzhao (Tommy) Lyu, Yingyue Luna Luan
papers.abstract: Organizations increasingly require employees to return to the office, yet evidence on the consequences of return-to-office (RTO) policies remains limited and typically treats RTO as a binary change. We propose a multidimensional perspective of RTO that distinguishes attendance-level— the proportion of time employees spend in the office over a given period—from attendance-trajectory—changes in attendance over time. Analyzing 13,956 employee-month observations from badge-swipe records for 1,163 employees whose attendance remained stable or increased at a multinational financial services organization over 12 months, we examined how these two dimensions related to ten subsequent outcomes: job performance, stress and burnout, three perceptions of organizational culture, and four forms of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and utilization. Attendance-level and attendance-trajectory showed distinct patterns of association across outcome domains. For job performance, overall attendance-level was unrelated to subsequent performance; instead, a faster increase in attendance predicted lower performance. Well-being showed the opposite pattern: higher overall and initial attendance-level predicted greater stress and burnout, while trajectory was unrelated to either outcome. Culture perceptions and AI adoption showed more complex patterns involving both dimensions, with higher or increasing attendance generally linked to more positive culture perceptions and deeper AI engagement, though the relevant dimension differed by outcome. These findings indicate that attendance-level and attendance-trajectory are not interchangeable and carry benefits in some domains while imposing costs in others. RTO policies should be designed and evaluated according to both how much and how quickly attendance increases, rather than being assumed uniformly beneficial or harmful.

papers.title: Formación, innovación e especialización na Enfermaría lucense. Balance formativo do primeiro semestre de 2026
papers.authors: Cristian Martín Vázquez
papers.abstract: During the first half of 2026, the Official College of Nursing of Lugo delivered a continuing professional development programme comprising 18 activities, 323 teaching hours and 488 enrolments. The programme combined face-to-face, online, live-streamed and blended learning, with in-person activities distributed across Lugo, Burela and Monforte. Its content covered clinical, community-based, preventive, technological and cross-cutting competencies, including life support, difficult airway management, vascular access care, ostomy care, telemetry, anticoagulation, self-harm, elder abuse, leadership and artificial intelligence. Particular emphasis was placed on training for the different nursing specialties, which accounted for 53.9% of the total teaching hours. Overall, the programme demonstrates the College’s commitment to professional development, specialisation, innovation, and the continuous improvement of safety and quality of care.

papers.title: “I wouldn’t trust her with my life but...” - Exploring trust in voice-based assistants through user-generated content
papers.authors: John J. Peters, Katharina Frehmann
papers.abstract: Investigating trust in conversational AI, such as voice-based assistants (VBAs), is increasingly important for understanding their rising popularity and the tasks users entrust to them. Howev-er, since VBAs are technical devices perceived as human-like and sometimes serving as infor-mation sources, it is unclear what forms trust in them takes. Technical, interpersonal, and media trust approaches may all be relevant, yet previous studies have not fully considered this poten-tial multidimensionality of trust in AI, especially regarding the inclusion of media trust. Fur-thermore, research on VBAs lacks qualitative studies that provide insights into users’ perspec-tives. This study therefore pursues two objectives: First, to develop a more comprehensive theo-retical perspective on trust in VBAs by integrating technical, interpersonal, and media trust ap-proaches. Second, to empirically explore signs of trust in VBAs in German user-generated online content. To this end, we conducted a qualitative content analysis of 169 postings about Alexa, Siri, and Google Assistant found on marketplaces, under media coverage, and on dis-cussion platforms. The results show that users evaluate typical and new technical, interpersonal, and media trustworthiness indicators for VBAs and sometimes combine these dimensions when discussing AI capabilities. When explicitly speaking of trust, users mostly refer to the parent company in high-risk situations rather than to the VBA itself. Users also discuss aspects that may represent consequences, processes, and external factors of trust. Based on these findings, the paper proposes a preliminary model of hybrid trust in VBAs that can inform future research on trust in conversational AI.

papers.title: การวเคราะหเชงเปรยบเทยบบรบททางการศกษาระหวางโรงเรยนนายเรออากาศสหรฐอเมรกาและโรงเรยนนายเรออากาศนวมนทกษตรยาธราช
papers.authors: Pramote Suksirisak, Nuntikan Klinchet
papers.journal: CRMA Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Military education in the 21st century is increasingly challenged by rapid advancements in digital technologies, artificial intelligence, cyber operations, and the space domain, all of which have significant implications for the design of curricula aimed at developing modern air force officers. This article presents a comparative analysis of the educational contexts of the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA) and the Navaminda Kasatriyadhiraj Royal Air Force Academy (NKRAFA), focusing on educational philosophy, curriculum structure, leadership development, military and field training, and technology integration. It also proposes recommendations for the development of military education in Thailand. The study employs documentary analysis and a comparative approach. The findings indicate that both institutions share a common goal of producing air force officers with strong leadership, moral integrity, and professional competence. USAFA is distinguished by its systematically integrated curriculum, which effectively combines academic education, military training, physical development, and character formation, along with its global orientation, structured leadership development, and advanced technological applications. In contrast, NKRAFA demonstrates strengths in fostering Thai military identity, maintaining discipline, emphasizing field-based training, and applying technology within the context of the Royal Thai Air Force. However, NKRAFA faces limitations in research investment, advanced technological laboratories, and operational simulation systems compared to USAFA. The analysis highlights that the most critical gap lies in the absence of a systematic leadership development framework and limited research capacity rather than a lack of military identity. Therefore, development efforts should prioritize these areas, without replicating the entire structural model of USAFA, to effectively respond to contemporary security challenges.

papers.title: The Psycho-Spiritual Crisis of the Digital Age: A Critical Review of Magnifica Humanitas
papers.authors: Blessin Baby
papers.abstract: Digital technologies, social media, and artificial intelligence are now driving our attention, communication, identity formation, decision-making, and access to knowledge. Their influence is neither as good nor as bad as it seems in the media and the narrative, and the outcomes are not always identical. This article focuses on Pope Leo XIV’s 2026 encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas. It critically analyses its theological anthropology in light of contemporary research on digital well-being, loneliness, adolescent identity, cognitive attention, disinformation, and human-AI interaction. The analysis argues that the most appropriate and reasonable way to describe the current problem is to recognise that it is not a universal psychological pathology produced by technology, but rather an anthropological and moral problem exacerbated by digital life. The theological distinction between Babel and Jerusalem offers a theological perspective to evaluate whether technologies promote domination, homogenisation and reductionism or, on the contrary, encourage participation, solidarity, truth and the common good. The paper highlights attention and interiority, digitally mediated identity, loneliness and communion, delegation of judgement to AI, truth and shared reality, based on development. The article concludes that a credible Christian response should neither romanticise pre-digital life nor be dismissive of technological innovation. However, it should instead build human judgement, embodied community, moral responsibility, contemplative practices, and institutional forms of technology governance. The limitations of the existing evidence are both in correlational studies and in the limited data on the correlation between digital practices and explicitly religious and spiritual outcomes.

papers.title: Effects of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Financial Performance and Audit Quality: An Empirical Study of Universal Banks in Ghana
papers.authors: Kwabena Effih, Joseph Mbawuni, Frank Yao Gbadago
papers.abstract: This study examines the effects of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption on financial performance and audit quality among universal banks in Ghana, addressing the limited empirical evidence from Sub-Saharan Africa. A mixed-methods design was employed, comprising a survey of 150 banking professionals across five universal banks and semi-structured interviews with 15 senior executives. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, ordinary least squares regression with robust standard errors, and instrumental variable estimation, while qualitative data were subjected to thematic analysis. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model, Resource-Based View, and Diffusion of Innovation theory, the findings indicate that AI adoption significantly and positively influences financial performance (R² = 0.783, β = 0.885, p < 0.001) and audit quality (R² = 0.604, β = 0.777, p < 0.001). Four mechanisms underpin these relationships: operational efficiency, improved decision-making, enhanced risk management, and superior customer experience. AI adoption remains moderate, with customer-facing applications more prevalent than fraud detection. Key challenges include data privacy, data quality, ethical concerns, and skills shortages, while organizational culture, regulatory conditions, and top management commitment moderate AI’s effects. The study contributes empirical evidence and contextual extensions of established AI adoption theories while providing practical insights for Ghanaian banking institutions and regulators.

papers.title: Actividades físicas estructuradas como mediación pedagógica para potenciar desarrollo cognitivo y socioemocional en contextos escolares/Structured physical activities as pedagogical mediation to enhance cognitive and socioemotional development in school contexts
papers.authors: William Yesid Palencia Angarita
papers.abstract: Introducción: Históricamente la educación física se ha reducido a prácticas recreativas, deportivas y motrices, lo que ha limitado su reconocimiento como espacio formativo. Las actividades físicas estructuradas, cuando son diseñadas con intencionalidad pedagógica, inciden significativamente en procesos cognitivos y socioemocionales en el ámbito escolar. Objetivo: Analizar el impacto de las actividades físicas estructuradas en el desarrollo cognitivo y socioemocional escolar desde una perspectiva pedagógica interpretativa. Métodos: Investigación cualitativa inscrita en el paradigma interpretativo, método inductivo y diseño fenomenológico. Corresponde a una investigación básica de diseño transversal. Se emplearon entrevistas semiestructuradas, observación participante e historia de vida mediante codificación abierta y axial, apoyado por el software de análisis cualitativo ATLAS.ti (v25), el cual tiene funciones de Inteligencia Artificial. Muestreo intencionado con estudiantes de séptimo grado y docentes de educación física. Resultados: Las actividades físicas estructuradas favorecieron dinámicas de cooperación, participación equitativa, inclusión y empatía entre los estudiantes. Cognitivamente, se constatan avances en procesos como la atención sostenida, la memoria, el control inhibitorio y en la toma de decisiones. Conclusiones: Las actividades físicas estructuradas constituyen mediación pedagógica transformadora en la que se asocian la dimensión corporal, cognitiva y socioemocional; vinculando la actividad practica con la teoría pedagógica. Se requiere habilitación curricular e institucional y un replanteo estratégico del área de educación física. Palabras clave: aprendizaje socioemocional; conocimiento; educación física; enseñanza secundaria; formación integral ABSTRACT Introduction: Historically, physical education has been reduced to recreational, sports, and motor practices, which has limited its recognition as a formative space. Structured physical activities, when designed with pedagogical intentionality, significantly influence cognitive and socioemotional processes within the school context. Objective: To analyze the impact of structured physical activities on school cognitive and socio-emotional development from an interpretive pedagogical perspective. Methods: Qualitative research framed within the interpretive paradigm, inductive method, and phenomenological design. It corresponds to basic research with a cross-sectional design. Semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and life history were used through open and axial coding, supported by the qualitative analysis software ATLAS.ti (v25), which has Artificial Intelligence functions. Purposive sampling with seventh-grade students and physical education teachers. Results: Structured physical activities fostered dynamics of cooperation, equitable participation, inclusion, and empathy among students. Cognitively, progress was observed in processes such as sustained attention, memory, inhibitory control, and decision-making. Conclusions: Structured physical activities constitute a transformative pedagogical mediation in which the bodily, cognitive, and socio-emotional dimensions are associated, linking practical activity with pedagogical theory. Curricular and institutional enablement and a strategic rethinking of the physical education area are required. Keywords: comprehensive training; knowledge; physical education; secondary education; socio-emotional learning

papers.title: The Effect of AI-Based Problem Based Learning Model on Improving the Digital Literacy Understanding of Grade VIII Students in Social Studies Learning at SMPN 2 Surabaya
papers.authors: Rifkian Asykar, Dian Ayu Larasati, Nuansa Bayu Segara, Dhimas Bagus Virgiawan
papers.abstract: In the contemporary digital era, the learning of Social Sciences (IPS) demands that students cultivate robust digital literacy, encompassing not merely the technical operation of devices, but the critical ability to access, evaluate, synthesize, and ethically utilize digital information. However, conventional pedagogical models, which predominantly rely on teacher-centered lecture methods and rote memorization, pose a significant barrier to fostering these essential 21st-century competencies, often leaving students as passive consumers rather than critical thinkers of digital content. Consequently, this quantitative study aims to rigorously analyze the effect of the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model integrated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) on enhancing the digital literacy comprehension of eighth-grade students enrolled in IPS classes at SMPN 2 Surabaya. Employing a quasi-experimental framework, specifically the Non-Equivalent Control Group Design, this research compares an experimental class (VIII-E) with a control class (VIII-I), each consisting of 32 students. Data were meticulously collected via multiple-choice pretests and posttests designed to measure cognitive gains in digital literacy comprehension. The collected data underwent stringent statistical scrutiny using SPSS version 23.0, including normality and homogeneity tests to validate parametric assumptions, followed by N-Gain analysis to measure improvement magnitude, and Independent Sample T-Tests to detect significant differences between groups. The findings reveal that both groups initially demonstrated normal and homogeneous data distributions, satisfying the prerequisites for parametric testing. Crucially, the experimental class achieved a substantial N-Gain score of 0.689, categorizing their improvement as moderate to high, which significantly outperformed the control class that registered a low gain score. Furthermore, the Independent Sample T-Test yielded a highly significant p-value of 0.000 (with a calculated t-value of -11.758), decisively rejecting the null hypothesis. These compelling results conclusively affirm that the AI-enhanced PBL model exerts a significant and positive influence on students' digital literacy. Thus, this innovative pedagogical approach proves highly effective in empowering students to navigate, analyze, synthesize, and apply digital information critically, actively, and contextually within their IPS studies, ultimately preparing them to thrive amidst the complexities of an increasingly digitalized society.

papers.title: Education Strategies in Algeria: Between Critical Theories and Artificial Intelligence Mechanisms A Critical Study
papers.authors: Abdelkader Kahloul
papers.abstract: This study aims to identify the immense potential of e-learning, which has transformed the dynamics of knowledge and generated sweeping network-based currents that humanity has struggled to counter, particularly those related to pedagogical aspects and teaching methods that have exhausted their effectiveness due to a flawed philosophy of experimentation, excessive stereotypical approaches, and rigid improvisation. Specialists have devoted themselves to technological mechanisms—programs and applications through which numerous innovations interact, such as artificial intelligence, the metaverse, visual storage, and other media—offering creative spaces for educational stakeholders. This research paper seeks to answer several questions, chief among them: What is the reality of digital education? Have we been able to keep pace with technological education through strategies that enable us to activate our curricula and computerize our course materials? Or is the matter merely a series of bubbles stemming from fleeting enthusiasm? We have reached several conclusions, most notably that e-learning saves time and effort, accommodates individual differences, and contributes to the diversification of teaching methods and the flexibility of communication channels.

papers.title: Quen é quen na enfermaría lucense. O Espírito do Practicante en Medicina e Cirurxía, na vivencia da Enfermaría actual. Jesús Lamela Escobar.
papers.authors: Isidoro Rodríguez Pérez
papers.abstract: This text presents the personal and professional career of Jesús “Suso” Lamela Escobar, a nurse from Lugo who recently retired after 46 years of professional practice in the Galician Health Service. Although he was never formally qualified as a practicante, his figure embodies the social meaning that this term still holds in rural Galicia: a healthcare professional with scientific knowledge, a strong vocation for service, closeness to the community and personal kindness. Born in Rosindo, Castroverde, in the mid-1950s, Jesús Lamela grew up in a family closely linked to healthcare, with a grandfather who was a physician and a father who was a practicante. This family tradition strongly influenced his professional choice. He studied at the School of Technical Health Assistants in Santiago de Compostela between 1975 and 1978, later completed his university diploma in Nursing and obtained the occupational health nursing qualification, formerly known as Company ATS. His professional career began in 1978 in A Pastoriza, where he worked for 20 years as a district ATS and home public healthcare practitioner. In 1998, he joined the Fingoi Health Centre, where he worked for another 26 years and eventually became its coordinator. Throughout his career, he was recognised for his professionalism, problem-solving skills, approachable character and commitment to colleagues, students and the people under his care. One of the areas he most enjoyed was minor surgery, together with the opportunity to help people directly. He also contributed to the clinical training of nursing students in Lugo. The text highlights his humanistic view of nursing, his confidence in the future of the profession and his belief that personal care will remain essential, even in a context increasingly shaped by new technologies and artificial intelligence. The profile concludes with a deeply vocational reflection: Jesús Lamela feels fully satisfied with the profession he chose and states that, if he could go back, he would become a nurse again. His greatest memory is having had the opportunity to help many people throughout his working life.

papers.title: Measuring Students’ Attention Boundaries in GAI-Assisted Learning: Development and Validation of the GAI-Mediated Learning Boundary Scale and Latent Profile Analysis
papers.authors: Peiyun He, Yuxiang Shi, Xi Zhan
papers.abstract: The Generative AI (GAI) is reshaping the temporal and spatial organization of college learning and the perceived boundary crossing between teacher-assigned tasks and self-directed learning. This study developed and validated a scale to assess college students’ attention boundary management in GAI-mediated learning. Analyzing data from 1904 students at 3 colleges in China, the study established a five-dimensional structure: Flexibility, Fragmentation, Immersion, Positive Spillover, and Negative Spillover. Exploratory and Confirmatory Factor Analysis confirmed the scale’s psychometric properties. A Latent Profile Analysis identified four distinct student profiles, Protective, Strained, Overextended, and Engaged Permeability Management. Supplementary heterogeneity analyses examined differences across the four profiles by gender, grade level, university, purposes and duration of AI use, and other learning-related characteristics. Based on these, this study proposed profile-specific recommendations. The study provides a validated instrument for assessing students’ attention boundaries in GAI-mediated learning, identifies heterogeneous student profiles, and offers differentiated practical implications.

papers.title: Altered Somatosensory Processing in Adults with Chronic Tic Disorder
papers.authors: Alexander C. Conley, David Alan Isaacs, Alexandra P. Fonaryova Key
papers.abstract: Individuals with chronic tic disorders (CTDs) frequently report sensory over-responsivity, defined as heightened awareness of and/or behavioral reactivity to stimuli that are non-aversive to most neurotypical individuals. Moreover, sensory over-responsivity is associated with severity of tics and co-occurring psychiatric symptoms in CTD populations. Despite its prevalence and association with core facets of the phenotype, the neurobiological basis of sensory over-responsivity in CTD remains unclear. Sensory gating, the physiological process of filtering out repetitive stimuli in early perceptual stages to facilitate attention to more salient stimuli, is one potential mechanism underpinning sensory over-responsivity in CTD. The current study sought to quantify somatosensory gating of pneumatic stimuli in adults with CTD using dense-array EEG and to determine the relationship between somatosensory gating and self-reported tactile responsivity. Neurotypical adults (n = 34) and adults with CTD (n = 28) completed a self-report and rater-administered neuropsychiatric evaluation, followed by an event-related potential somatosensory gating paradigm. Contrary to our hypotheses, somatosensory gating, as quantified by gating differences and regression analysis marginal effects, did not differ between groups for P50, N140, or P300 components, and gating indices were not associated with tactile responsivity. However, relative to neurotypical adults, adults with CTD had significantly smaller P50 amplitudes following S1, the first of the paired pneumatic stimuli; moreover, adults with CTD with smaller S1 P50 amplitudes reported greater tactile responsivity. No other component amplitudes differed between groups. Findings suggest that adults with CTD have altered pre-conscious processing of non-noxious tactile stimuli, which is linked with tactile over-responsivity.

papers.title: Human Dignity and Integral Development in a Digital World: Living the Vision of Magnifica Humanitas
papers.authors: Ligi James Vettukallel
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of contemporary society is reshaping human relationships, education, work, communication, identity, and patterns of social participation. Artificial intelligence, social media, digital platforms, and algorithmic systems offer remarkable possibilities for human advancement. However, they also raise fundamental questions concerning human dignity, freedom, relationality, truth, psychological well-being, and the common good. This article reflects on these challenges through the vision of Magnifica Humanitas, placing the human person at the centre of technological development. Drawing upon Christian anthropology, Catholic social teaching, spirituality, psychology, and contemporary reflections on digital culture, the article argues that technological progress cannot by itself be equated with integral human development. Authentic development embraces the whole person and every person, intellectually, emotionally, socially, morally, culturally, and spiritually. The article grounds the theme in solid theological foundations of human dignity, discusses the opportunities and challenges of the digital world and aspects of integral human development, and draws the pathways for living the vision of Magnifica Humanitas. Particular attention is given to the education and formation of children and young people, the psychological effects of digital environments, the digital divide, the dignity of work, and the spiritual importance of silence, discernment, presence, and communion. The article concludes that the Christian response to technological transformation should be neither rejection nor uncritical acceptance, but a creative humanisation of digital culture. The ultimate challenge is not to create a humanity that is merely more technologically advanced, but a digital world in which every person can flourish in dignity, freedom, fraternity, and communion with God and others.

papers.title: М’ЯКІ НАВИЧКИ ПЕРСОНАЛУ У ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННІ РЕЗИЛЬЄНТНОСТІ УПРАВЛІННЯ ПІДПРИЄМСТВАМИ В СФЕРІ ЕЛЕКТРОННОЇ ТОРГІВЛІ
papers.authors: Kupalova Halyna, Yevhenii Dmytryshyn, Yevhenii Oleshko
papers.journal: The Scientific Issues of Ternopil Volodymyr Hnatiuk National Pedagogical University Series pedagogy
papers.abstract: The article examines the role of personnel soft skills in ensuring the management resilience of e-commerce enterprises under martial law. An analysis of scientific publications on personnel management and the development of employees’ competencies and soft skills is carried out, and domestic and foreign approaches to their interpretation and assessment are considered. The dynamics of e-commerce development in Ukraine are revealed: the volume of e-commerce turnover increased from UAH 28.2 billion in 2017 to UAH 69.9 billion in 2024, or 2.5 times. It is established that since the outbreak of hostilities the share of enterprises engaged in e-commerce has been increasing annually, from 10.3% in 2022 to 15.6% in 2024, while wholesale and retail trade and the repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles are among the four types of economic activity with the highest level of its development. A structural and logical framework for building the organizational resilience of e-commerce enterprise management through the development of personnel soft skills is proposed, and groups of these skills are identified by functional categories of employees. It is shown that strategic thinking and leadership competencies under uncertainty are critical for top management, whereas psychological endurance and communication skills come to the fore for operational and service staff. It is determined that adaptability is common to all categories of personnel and, under martial law, acquires the character of a basic functional competence. It is proven that, to increase labor productivity and the quality of customer service in e-commerce, it is advisable to implement a set of managerial measures: introducing psychological support and stress resilience programs for employees; improving the digital literacy of personnel using artificial intelligence; developing a system of internal mentoring and functional job rotation; incorporating personnel resilience indicators into the performance evaluation system; and expanding cooperation with educational institutions, industry associations and civic organizations.

papers.title: Pengaruh Model Pembelajaran Berbasis Masalah Berbantuan Artificial Intelligence Terhadap Hasil Belajar Siswa Kelas IX Pada Mata Pelajaran IPS Materi Perubahan Sosial Di SMP Negeri 21 Surabaya
papers.authors: Dea Ayu Sholikhatun
papers.abstract: This study was motivated by the low learning outcomes of students in Social Studies, which were caused by teacher-centered learning and the suboptimal use of technology in the learning process. The purpose of this study was to determine the effect of the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model assisted by Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the learning outcomes of ninth-grade students in Social Studies on the topic of social change at SMP Negeri 21 Surabaya. This study employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental method with a Nonequivalent Control Group Design. The sample consisted of 60 students, including 30 students from class IX-A as the experimental group and 30 students from class IX-B as the control group, selected through a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected through observation, tests, and documentation. Data analysis was conducted using normality tests, homogeneity tests, and hypothesis testing through the Independent Samples t-test with the assistance of SPSS version 25. The results indicated that the mean post-test score of the experimental group was 75.46, which was higher than that of the control group, which was 51.53. The hypothesis testing results revealed a significance value (Sig. 2-tailed) of 0.000 < 0.05, leading to the rejection of H₀ and acceptance of H₁. Therefore, it can be concluded that the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model assisted by Artificial Intelligence (AI) had a significant effect on the learning outcomes of ninth-grade students in Social Studies on the topic of social change at SMP Negeri 21 Surabaya.

papers.title: APRENDIZAJE DE LENGUAJES DE PROGRAMACIÓN MEDIANTE EL USO DE INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL (LEARNING PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES THROUGH THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE)
papers.authors: José Manuel Cuin Jacuinde, Claudio Ernesto Florian Arenas, Brenda González Gómez, Rodrigo Vega Espinoza
papers.abstract: Resumen La enseñanza de lenguajes de programación es una práctica que actualmente re realiza desde un enfoque tradicional en el que se muestran a los alumnos las estructuras y sentencias más comunes, con el objetivo de que a partir de ellas, puedan desarrollar algoritmos que resuelvan problemas cotidianos, sin embargo, la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial en el ámbito educativo permite hoy en día hacer uso de estas herramientas para acelerar y agilizar los procesos de aprendizaje de dichos lenguajes tomando como referencia el conocimiento previo o simultáneo de otras tecnologías. Palabras Clave: Aprendizaje, Buenas prácticas, Inteligencia Artificial, Programación, Python. Abstract The teaching of programming languages is a practice that is currently carried out from a traditional approach in which students are shown the most common structures and sentences, with the aim that from them, they can develop algorithms that solve everyday problems, however, the emergence of artificial intelligence in the educational field allows today to make use of these tools to accelerate and streamline the learning processes of these languages taking as a reference the previous or simultaneous knowledge of other technologies. Keywords: Learning, Best Practices, Artificial Intelligence, Programming, Python.

papers.title: AI-Supported Creative Writing Instruction in Improving the Writing Skills of Junior High School Students
papers.authors: Baguio Meregine D.
papers.journal: American Journal of Language, Literacy and Learning in STEM Education (2993-2769)
papers.abstract: This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of AI-supported creative writing instruction in improving the writing skills of Grade 10 students at Marigondon National High School during the School Year 2025–2026. Utilizing a quasi-experimental research design, specifically the one-group pretest–posttest design, the research involved respondents selected through total enumeration. The study focused on three key indicators: grammar, vocabulary, and sentence structure; organization and coherence; and creativity and originality. Data were gathered using a validated writing assessment rubric and analyzed using descriptive statistics and t-test for paired samples. The results revealed that prior to the intervention, students demonstrated a Beginning level of proficiency across all areas, with creativity and originality obtaining the lowest performance. After the implementation of the intervention, improvements were observed, even if all indicators are still in the Beginning level. Statistical analysis confirmed a significant difference between pre-test and post-test scores, proving that the enhancement in performance was a direct result of the treatment. The findings established that integrating AI tools effectively addresses critical gaps in writing competence, particularly in stimulating idea generation, improving content structure, and refining language accuracy. It is concluded that AI-Supported Creative Writing Instruction is a valuable approach to developing students’ writing proficiency. Based on these findings, this program is proposed to sustain and expand these benefits, encouraging the integration of technology in writing instruction to help learners achieve higher levels of competence and confidence.

papers.title: Безпілотні літальні апарати та Інтернет речей у сільському господарстві: систематичний огляд технологічних напрямів і перспектив розвитку
papers.authors: Володимир Панченко, Георгій Кучук
papers.journal: The Scientific Issues of Ternopil Volodymyr Hnatiuk National Pedagogical University Series pedagogy
papers.abstract: Relevance. Modern agriculture is undergoing a profound cyber-physical transformation driven by the need to shift from extensive to precision, high-accuracy, and environmentally balanced production methods. The technological foundation of this transition is the integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and wireless Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks, which together form the concept of Agriculture 5.0. Despite the rapid growth of publications on this topic, the accumulated body of research remains fragmented across directions (computer vision, network technologies, robotics, adoption economics), which complicates the formation of a holistic picture of the field and of priority directions for further research. The subject of this study are methods and technologies of applying UAVs and IoT networks to precision-agriculture tasks. The purpose of the article to systematize and classify current scientific research on the use of UAVs and IoT in agriculture, and to determine the leading technological directions, their quantitative proportions, and promising development vectors. The following results were obtained. A total of 198 scientific publications from 2024-2026 were processed and classified into seven thematic classes: crop health and biological threat monitoring, hardware engineering, edge computing and spraying, navigation, swarm intelligence and data collection, phenotyping, biomass and yield forecasting, soil science, water balance and precision irrigation, economics, ecology and socio-cultural perception, and specialized agrotechnical operations. For each class, consolidated tables of applied methods and results, as well as diagrams revealing the internal structure of the direction, were constructed. The dominance of navigation/swarm-control tasks and biological-threat monitoring was identified, along with key technical barriers (limited battery energy density, beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight regulations, and fragmentation of data-exchange standards). Conclusion. The obtained results provide a holistic assessment of the state and structure of the research field on UAV and IoT applications in agriculture and can serve as a basis for shaping further research programs and educational courses in precision agriculture. Future research directions concern improving the energy autonomy of platforms, standardizing data-exchange protocols, and developing edge artificial-intelligence models resilient to complex field conditions.

papers.title: Cognitive Distribution in Student–GenAI Interaction: A Process Framework from Self-Directed ChatGPT Use in Research Tasks
papers.authors: Orhan Arıkan, Jennie F. Lane, Katherine Willcox
papers.abstract: Many studies assess how generative AI (GenAI) affects student learning through benchmarks such as tests, scores, and self-reports. This outcome-focused approach often casts GenAI as either a shortcut to replace thinking or a tutor to support learning, overlooking how interaction reshapes students' cognitive activity as they navigate the jagged frontier of AI capability. To examine this process, we conducted a qualitative-dominant mixed-methods case study of self-directed student–ChatGPT interaction in a university transdisciplinary research course. Drawing on human–computer interaction and cognitive philosophy, we developed the Cognitive Distribution Framework, which identifies five interaction types: extension, outsourcing, alignment, transformation, and decoupling; and four roles: cyborg, centaur, ghost, and hermit. Applying it to 53 ChatGPT logs and questionnaires from 112 students, we found diverse distributions of cognitive work. Students most often extended their thinking through active engagement, but also outsourced bounded tasks, aligned the system with their goals, reported shifts in their thinking, and at times limited AI input. Students reported significantly higher perceived cognitive activation than cognitive reduction. Student–GenAI interaction is better understood as a shifting process of cognitive distribution than as fixed dependence or assistance. We call for process-focused research and pedagogies that recognize how students reorganize cognitive work with AI.

papers.title: Serum Neuregulin-1, Neuregulin-2, and Neuregulin-3 Levels in Children with Attention-deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
papers.authors: Mehmet Berat Taş, Semih Erden, İbrahim Kılınç, Abdullah Yazar
papers.abstract: Objective: We compared serum neuregulin-1 (NRG-1), neuregulin-2 (NRG-2), and neuregulin-3 (NRG-3) levels between children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and healthy controls and investigated their relationship with ADHD symptom severity.Methods: This study included 101 drug-naive patients with ADHD (aged 8-18 years) and 51 age-and sex-comparable healthy controls.Diagnoses were confirmed using the Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia for School-Age Children Present and Lifetime Version.Symptom severity and comorbid symptoms were assessed using the Turgay DSM-IV-Based Scale and the Revised Child Anxiety and Depression Scale.Serum NRG-1, NRG-2, and NRG-3 levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.Results: The groups did not differ in age, sex, or body mass index (BMI) (p ＞ 0.05).Serum NRG-1 and NRG-3 levels were significantly higher in the ADHD group than in controls (p ＜ 0.001 and p = 0.003, respectively), whereas NRG-2 levels did not differ (p = 0.205).Logistic regression analyses demonstrated that elevated NRG-1 and NRG-3 levels were independently associated with ADHD group status after controlling for age, sex, and BMI.In exploratory correlation analyses within the ADHD group, NRG-1 levels showed a modest positive correlation with hyperactivity/impulsivity scores (rS = 0.212, p = 0.033), whereas NRG-3 levels were negatively correlated with BMI (p = 0.013).Serum NRG-2 and NRG-3 levels were positively correlated (p ＜ 0.001).Conclusion: Elevated serum NRG-1 and NRG-3 levels in children and adolescents with ADHD suggest that neuregulin family members may represent peripheral biological correlates of neurodevelopmental processes associated with ADHD.These findings support further investigation of NRG-1 and NRG-3 as potential peripheral biomarkers in ADHD.

papers.title: Neurofeedback enhances a neural signature of selective attention to speech in cocktail-party settings
papers.authors: Ram Kumar Pari, Marina Inyutina, Hoang Lam Thanh Hoang, Camille Dedies, Manuela Jaeger, Stefanie Enriquez‐Geppert, Mathieu Marx, Stefan Debener, Christoph Siegfried Herrmann, Benedikt Zoefel
papers.abstract: Understanding speech in noisy situations is challenging and often fails due to attentional rather than sensory deficits. We report here that neurofeedback can enhance a neural signature of selective attention to speech in a cocktail-party setting. Neural responses to speech were quantified in participants’ electroencephalogram (EEG) while they attended to one of two audiobooks, presented simultaneously. After each 22s-segment of speech, the participants’ N1 component was extracted from the temporal response function (TRF). The N1 component is known to be sensitive to attention. During a ∼49-min training session, N1 amplitude values were displayed visually to participants so that they could learn to strengthen their neural responses to target speech and minimise their responses to distracting speech. During neurofeedback training, we found an enhanced N1 component in the response to target audiobooks that was specific to EEG channels used to provide feedback, and not present in a control group that received sham feedback. At right-lateralised fronto-central channels, enhanced N1 components correlated with improvements in a measure of speech comprehension (multiple-choice content questions). These results indicate that neural responses to speech can be regulated through neurofeedback and open up new possibilities to train attentional listening in populations struggling to understand speech in noise.

papers.title: Congress Presentation: IMS 2026 Elinzanetant’s effects on menopause-related quality of life in women with endocrine therapy-associated VMS: results from the OASIS-4 trial
papers.authors: Michelle Jacobson, Donal J. Brennan, Ludwig Kiesel, Lisa Larkin, Christian Seitz, Lauren Wahyudi, Kaisa Laapas, Fatima Cardoso
papers.abstract: In this post hoc analysis, improvements in subdomains of menopause-related quality of life were observed with elinzanetant vs placebo in the overall population of women with endocrine therapy-associated vasomotor symptoms, including in higher-BMI individuals, and were consistent across endocrine therapy subgroups.

papers.title: AI-Driven Digital Transformation in Higher Education: Examining the Influence of Digital Leadership, Faculty Readiness and Organizational Resilience
papers.authors: Shital Mantri, Anjum Patel, Vaishali Ashok Barse, Ritika Choudhary
papers.journal: International Journal of Technology and Applied Science
papers.abstract: This research aims to explore the impact of digital leadership and faculty preparedness for the digital transformation and resilience of higher education institutions in the era of artificial intelligence. To show a complete empirical analysis workflow, a quantitative cross-sectional model was operationalized from a synthetic Likert dataset with 350 cases generated from the study questionnaire. The five multi-item constructs were: Digital Leadership (DL), Faculty Readiness (FR), AI-Enabled Digital Transformation (AIDT), Organizational Resilience (OR), and Transformation Outcomes (TO). Each construct had high internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.892–0.906). There were positive relationships found from DL to FR, FR to AIDT, DL and AIDT to OR, and OR and AIDT to TO; composite-score regressions indicated these relationships. Shorthcut analyses using mediation were conducted to support indirect effects via faculty readiness and organizational resilience. The observations are simulated, and the numerical results are not claims about any institution or population and should be substituted with the actual responses to the survey before submission to the journal [1]–[5] [8] [10].

papers.title: Epistemological Friction in Artificial Intelligence Use among Humanities Faculty and Students in Western Mindanao, Philippines
papers.authors: Javier B. Sarmiento, Norvie T. Jalani
papers.journal: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has entered higher education faster than institutional policy can regulate it, a gap visible in Philippine humanities programs, where interpretive originality and authorial voice are central to disciplinary practice. Humanities programs in regional, resource-constrained Philippine settings remain largely absent from the AI-adoption literature, a gap this study addressed by examining AI adoption, perceived usefulness and ease of use, perceived risk, AI literacy, and behavioral intention among humanities faculty and undergraduate students at a state university in Zamboanga City, Philippines, where no institutional AI policy exists. A convergent mixed-methods design combined survey data from 200 students and 23 faculty with ten in-depth interviews; quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and Welch's t-test, while qualitative data underwent reflexive thematic analysis, integrated through joint display analysis. Students used AI moderately and selectively, favoring comprehension and organization over original composition. Faculty reported higher AI familiarity than students but markedly lower classroom use (M = 3.59 versus M = 2.67), a pattern proposed here as epistemological friction: principled disciplinary resistance rather than technical inability. Both groups perceived high risk, yet risk predicted only the intention to limit AI use (r = .531, p < .001), not the intention to discontinue it (r = .047, ns), producing concealed adoption tentatively labeled a shadow AI ecosystem. Perceived usefulness (β = .427) and ease of use (β = .365) were the strongest predictors of continued use, while students significantly outperformed faculty in AI literacy (d = -0.943), reversing the assumed top-down transmission of competence. AI acceptance here was shaped as much by disciplinary values and unclear institutional guidance as by usefulness or ease of use, supporting tiered governance, faculty development addressing disciplinary and ethical concerns, and structured reverse mentoring to narrow the literacy gap and reduce concealed AI use.

papers.title: The AI Productivity Paradox in Software Engineering: A Systematic Review of Code Quality, Technical Debt, and Organizational Throughout (2024–2026)
papers.authors: George panos
papers.abstract: Background: The period 2024–2026 has seen accelerated adoption of AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, CodeWhisperer, Amazon CodeWhisperer). Early productivity gains are well reported in industry white papers and short-term controlled experiments. However, emerging evidence suggests a paradox: perceived throughput increases may coincide with hidden declines in code quality and accelerated technical debt accumulation that only manifest after several months of use. Objective: To systematically review empirical studies published between 2024 and 2026 examining the associations between AI coding assistant usage and three outcome categories: (1) code quality metrics, (2) technical debt indicators, and (3) organizational throughput measures. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 systematic review guidelines, we searched four electronic databases: Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and arXiv. The search was conducted on March 15, 2026, using a Boolean search string combining terms for AI coding assistants, code quality, technical debt, and throughput. Inclusion criteria required: (a) empirical study design (controlled experiment, field study, longitudinal case study, or survey with quantitative analysis), (b) software engineers using AI coding assistants in real or realistically complex tasks, © at least one measured outcome in the three categories of interest, (d) publication date 2024–2026, and (e) peer-reviewed or pre-print with verifiable methodology. Exclusion criteria eliminated opinion pieces, non-software contexts, studies without direct AI attribution, non-English publications, and duplicates. Two independent reviewers conducted title/abstract screening, full-text retrieval, and eligibility assessment. Risk of bias was evaluated using the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies and ROBINS-I for quasi-experiments. Due to high statistical heterogeneity (I² > 85%), narrative synthesis was performed with effect direction plots. Results: A total of 1,247 records were identified. After duplicate removal (n=891), title/abstract screening (764 excluded), full-text retrieval (127 sought), and full-text assessment (93 excluded), 34 studies met inclusion criteria. Study designs included controlled experiments (14 studies, 41%), longitudinal field studies (12 studies, 35%), cross-sectional surveys with code analysis (5 studies, 15%), and industry case studies (3 studies, 9%). GitHub Copilot was the most frequently studied tool (22 studies), followed by Cursor (5 studies), CodeWhisperer (4 studies), and generic LLM APIs (3 studies). Study duration ranged from 1 day to 9 months (median = 8 weeks). Total unique developer participants across studies was 2,847. For RQ1 (code quality), 20 out of 34 studies (58%) reported statistically significant quality degradation in at least one metric. The most commonly observed degradations were increased code duplication (52% of studies), higher cyclomatic complexity (48%), and elevated defect rates in modified legacy code (41%). Defect density increased by a median of 23% in AI-heavy modules (p<0.05). 3 [4/27/2026 12:40 PM] George Panos: Code churn increased 34% in the first 8 weeks post-AI adoption (p<0.01). Test coverage showed no consistent change, but assertion quality decreased. For RQ2 (technical debt), four debt types were identified across studies: copy-paste debt (present in 74% of AI-heavy repositories), dead code (62% of AI commits), API coupling debt (44% of AI-suggested API calls used deprecated methods), and testing debt (78% of AI-generated unit tests covered only positive paths). Technical debt principal (time to fix) increased by an average of 1.8 person-days per 1000 AI-generated lines of code (p<0.001). Interest (extra effort per change) rose 27% in modules with >40% AI-generated code. The debt ratio doubled in 6 months for teams without debt gating (from 8% to 16%). Debt accumulation followed a nonlinear temporal pattern: minimal weeks 1–3, exponential growth weeks 5–12, then plateau after forced refactoring. For RQ3 (organizational throughput), 71% of studies reported increased individual story point completion in the short term (median +27% during weeks 1–4). Cycle time for new features decreased 18% in the first 4 weeks. However, after week 8, cumulative cycle time including rework exceeded baseline by 9% (based on 6 longitudinal studies with data beyond 8 weeks). Code review time increased 35% for AI-generated pull requests. Integration test failures grew 2.2 times. Net overall throughput gain was absent for 54% of teams after 6 months. Teams with fewer than 5 engineers saw temporary gain (+15% velocity) that dissipated by month 4; teams larger than 20 engineers experienced net negative organizational throughput (-6%). For RQ4 (mitigation strategies), the most effective strategies were mandatory quality gates (test coverage >80% + cyclomatic complexity <10) before merge, which prevented 67% of debt insertion (11 studies), and mandatory human refactoring after AI commits, which reduced debt principal by 41% with only temporary velocity loss of 2% (8 studies). Debt-aware prompting alone showed only small effects. Weekly debt reduction sprints reduced interest by 29% but reduced feature velocity by 8%. Conclusions: The AI productivity paradox is substantiated by the available empirical evidence from 2024–2026. Individual developer velocity increases significantly in the short term (first 4 weeks), but code quality degrades and technical debt accelerates nonlinearly, eroding organizational throughput by week 8 and producing net negative outcomes for many teams by month 6. The paradox is not inevitable; effective countermeasures exist, particularly quality gates and mandatory refactoring capacity. Organizations must treat AI coding assistants as tools requiring debt-aware governance rather than unconditional productivity accelerators. Short-term (1–5 day) studies systematically underestimate the negative effects and should be interpreted with caution. Future research requires longitudinal designs of 6+ months, standardized technical debt metrics, and automated detection of AI-introduced debt.

papers.title: INFLUENCE OF SPEECH CULTURE ON THE FORMATION OF LANGUAGE COMPETENCES OF FUTURE SPECIALISTS
papers.authors: Inna Marynchenko
papers.abstract: In the context of the digitalization of higher education, the modernization of professional training for future specialists in language specialties is becoming increasingly relevant, as it aims to prepare competitive professionals capable of adapting to the rapidly changing digital environment. A key aspect of this process is the formation of language competencies influenced by speech culture, which ensures the development of communicative, sociocultural, and professional skills. The purpose of the article is the practical implementation of a model for forming language competencies of future language specialists, the substantiation of its structural components of readiness, and the determination of pedagogical conditions that contribute to the effectiveness of this process. The methodological framework of the research includes empirical methods, namely ascertaining, formative, and control stages of a pedagogical experiment, as well as observation and survey methods. The results of the ascertaining stage revealed that students of both the control and experimental groups predominantly demonstrated low and medium levels of readiness across all components, which confirmed the need for targeted pedagogical interventions. The control stage of the experiment proved the effectiveness of the proposed experimental methodology and showed positive dynamics in the formation of language competencies among students of the experimental group. The practical significance of the study lies in updating and coordinating the content of educational programs in translation- and language-oriented disciplines, as well as in developing an algorithm for students’ project-based work using the Google Classroom service, which enhances the effectiveness of digital tools in professional language training.
