papers.title: Critical thinking and vulnerability to fraud
papers.authors: Serhii Skrypnyk, Olena Osetrova, Світлана Шапутько
papers.journal: Naukovij vìsnik Nacìonalʹnoï akademìï vnutrìšnìh sprav
papers.abstract: Digitalisation, the proliferation of online interaction and generative artificial intelligence are creating new opportunities for fraud, thereby increasing the importance of critical thinking, the ability to assess the reliability of information and the capacity to resist manipulation. The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of critical thinking on an individual’s vulnerability to fraud through a systematic analysis of contemporary academic literature and a comparison of the findings with the factual circumstances established in the judgements of Ukrainian courts. The research was conducted using methods of analysis, synthesis, content analysis, comparative analysis and generalisation. The results of the analysis of academic sources indicated that overconfidence, cognitive biases, low levels of digital literacy, an insufficient ability to critically evaluate information, and the characteristics of the digital information environment are key factors in vulnerability to fraud. Emotional influence can exacerbate such vulnerability through fear, trust, the expectation of benefit or a sense of urgency. The use of artificial intelligence makes it more difficult to recognise manipulation, thereby reducing the ability to critically evaluate manipulative content. It has been established that individual mechanisms of influence can be applied in combination within a single fraudulent scheme, combining cognitive, social, emotional and digital factors of vulnerability. In addition, Ukrainian court judgements were analysed, the descriptive sections of which contain the factual circumstances established by the court regarding the use of psychological, communicative and digital mechanisms of influence on victims. A comparison of these circumstances with the results of scientific research demonstrated a high degree of consistency between the theoretically described vulnerability factors and actual fraud mechanisms, including recent cases involving the use of generative artificial intelligence. The findings can be applied in the development of fraud prevention measures and are aimed at fostering critical thinking, digital literacy and enhancing the resilience of potential victims to manipulative influences

papers.title: Digital competencies and human capital for sustainable economic development
papers.authors: Oleg Yarema
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate how digital competencies and digital human capital contribute to sustainable economic development by influencing productivity, competitiveness, innovation capacity, labour-market transformation, and long-term economic resilience. The materials consisted of open data and analytical reports published by European and international institutions, including sources on digital skills, artificial intelligence adoption, labour-market transformation, and digital development. The methodological basis of the study included comparative analysis, synthesis of institutional and statistical data, structural analysis of labour-market trends, calculation of digital-skills gaps and normalised indicators, scenario analysis, and a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats matrix. The results showed that digital competencies affect sustainable development through productivity growth, innovation capacity, economic inclusion, labour-market adaptability, and institutional resilience. Particular attention was devoted to evaluating Ukraine’s digital transformation in comparison with the European Union and to identifying strategic policy priorities capable of strengthening digital human capital in the context of European integration and post-war economic recovery. The comparative analysis indicated that Ukraine is close to the European Union average in basic digital skills but still faces significant risks related to uneven access, migration of skilled workers, insufficient artificial intelligence literacy, and outdated educational programmes. The extended quantitative assessment showed that, if the 2021-2025 trend continues, Ukraine may reach only about 64.4 percent of adults with at least basic digital skills by 2030, remaining 15.6 percentage points below the recommended benchmark. The article argued that Ukraine’s digital human-capital strategy should combine lifelong learning, data literacy, artificial intelligence literacy, science, technology, engineering, and mathematics education, digital inclusion, and smart regional policy. The practical value of the study lies in the proposed framework for connecting digital competencies with productivity, competitiveness, and recovery policy

papers.title: Exploring Human–AI Collaboration and Strategic Decision-Making in UAE Government Institutions: Reconfiguring Leadership and Human Judgement in the Digital Era
papers.authors: Abdulla Awadh Abdulla
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: This study investigates human–AI collaboration and strategic decision-making in UAE government institutions, examining how artificial intelligence is transforming leadership practices, decision processes and human judgement. Although AI is integral to the UAE’s digital government transformation, existing research has focused mainly on technological adoption, organisational performance and digital transformation, leaving limited understanding of how human–AI collaboration reconfigures strategic decision-making and leadership responsibilities. The study addresses this gap by examining the relationship between human judgement and AI-enabled decision support, the effects of collaboration on strategic decision-making and organisational transformation, and emerging leadership challenges in AI-enabled governance. An exploratory qualitative research design was employed, drawing on academic literature, policy documents, official government publications and other documentary sources. The data were analysed thematically, guided by Dynamic Capabilities Theory, to identify patterns related to collaboration, decision-making, leadership transformation and human judgement. Findings show that AI is moving strategic decision-making towards collaborative arrangements in which AI provides analytical capabilities, predictive insights and decision support, while human leaders retain responsibility for contextual interpretation, ethical reasoning and final judgement. The study contributes by extending understanding of AI-enabled leadership through a human–AI collaboration perspective, demonstrating how technological capabilities and human judgement can be integrated within government decision processes. It concludes that effective AI governance requires complementarity rather than leadership displacement. Future research should examine these dynamics through empirical studies involving government leaders and employees across different UAE institutions and comparative public-sector contexts and broader institutional outcomes. The study recommends strengthening AI literacy, leadership capabilities, institutional readiness and responsible governance.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of Government Leadership: A Qualitative Inquiry into UAE Government Institutions
papers.authors: Abdulla Awadh Abdulla
papers.journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
papers.abstract: This study examines artificial intelligence and the transformation of government leadership within UAE government institutions, focusing on how the integration of AI is reshaping leadership roles, organisational practices and institutional responsibilities. While artificial intelligence has become an increasingly important component of the UAE's digital government transformation, existing literature has largely concentrated on technological adoption, organisational performance and digital transformation, with comparatively limited attention to how AI is changing the nature and practice of government leadership. This study addresses this gap by examining the changing nature of leadership in AI-enabled government, the relationship between AI, organisational transformation and institutional change, and the emerging leadership challenges associated with AI-driven government transformation in the UAE. An exploratory qualitative research design was adopted, drawing on relevant academic literature, policy documents, official government publications and other documentary sources. The collected materials were subjected to thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns and themes concerning AI-enabled leadership and organisational transformation. The findings indicate that AI is transforming government leadership from predominantly hierarchical and managerial practices towards greater technological awareness, coordination, adaptability and responsible oversight. The study further finds that AI adoption influences organisational routines, structures, professional responsibilities and institutional practices, while creating emerging challenges relating to accountability, trust, ethical responsibility, technological dependence and the changing boundaries of human leadership. Consequently, the study contributes to the understanding of AI-enabled government leadership by demonstrating that effective transformation requires the integration of technological capabilities with human judgement, organisational adaptability and institutional responsibility. The study recommends strengthening leadership capabilities, institutional readiness and responsible governance mechanisms to ensure that AI-driven government transformation remains aligned with accountability, legitimacy and human responsibility.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION: EXAMINING ITS IMPACT ON STUDENT LEARNING, ENGAGEMENT, AND ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE
papers.authors: Anggit Pratiknyo Widyagiri
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into higher education to support various learning activities, yet its overall impact on students remains inconsistently reported across the literature. This article reviews existing studies to examine the impact of AI on three interrelated aspects of higher education: student learning, student engagement, and academic performance. A literature review method was used, drawing on systematic reviews and meta-analyses that discuss AI applications and outcomes in higher education settings. The review shows that AI can support student learning through explanations, personalized feedback, and access to learning resources, while also raising concerns about overreliance and reduced critical thinking. Regarding engagement, evidence is relatively strong for behavioral engagement but more mixed for emotional and cognitive engagement. For academic performance, several systematic reviews and meta-analyses report positive effects of AI, particularly in STEM-related areas, although the specific impact of AI adoption still requires further investigation in certain learning contexts such as open and distance learning. Taken together, these findings suggest that the impact of AI in higher education should be examined not only through academic outcomes but also through how it shapes students' learning process and engagement, with AI functioning best as a supporting tool rather than a replacement for students' active involvement in learning.

papers.title: PENGARUH PENGGUNAAN AI GENERATIF TERHADAP KEMANDIRIAN BELAJAR MAHASISWA GENERASI Z
papers.authors: Veronica Puspita Sari, Salsa Bila Firda Azahra, Diah Ayu Wandira, Khoirul Nurita Sari, Siti Fitreriani
papers.journal: Darul Ulum Jurnal Ilmiah Keagamaan Pendidikan dan Kemasyarakatan
papers.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of Generative AI usage on the learning independence of Generation Z students at STIT Darul Ulum Kotabaru, viewed from the perspective of perceived ease of use and potential dependency. The research employs a quantitative approach with an associative causal design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to Generation Z students who have used Generative AI in academic activities. The variables examined include perceived ease of use of Generative AI (X1), potential dependency on Generative AI (X2), and student learning independence (Y). Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with SPSS. The results indicate that perceived ease of use and potential dependency simultaneously influence students' learning independence. Generative AI provides significant convenience in accessing information, understanding materials, and completing academic tasks. However, excessive use without critical thinking and academic responsibility can lead to dependency that reduces learning independence. This study contributes to the development of educational technology studies, particularly in understanding the impact of Generative AI on student learning behavior in Islamic higher education institutions

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS A SUPPLEMENTARY TOOL IN CONTEMPORARY CHEMISTRY TEACHING: AN EXPERIMENTAL STUDY.
papers.authors: Shemsedin Abduli
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the impact of the use of artificial intelligence as a supportive tool in contemporary chemistry teaching, with a particular focus on the understanding of ionic and covalent chemical bonds. This research aims to evaluate whether the integration of artificial intelligence into the learning process can influence the improvement of students’ learning, compared to traditional teaching methods without the support of artificial intelligence. The study was carried out as an experimental research with two comparable groups of students, selected after a preliminary test (pre-test). In the first group, teaching was conducted through a traditional approach with contemporary visual and explanatory methods, whereas in the second group, in addition to the same explanation, students were given the opportunity to use artificial intelligence as a supportive tool for self-learning and clarification of concepts. After the completion of the learning process, a final test (post-test) was conducted for both groups, with the aim of assessing the level of understanding. This research aims to contribute to discussions on the use of artificial intelligence in education, highlighting its potential as a tool that can increase engagement, conceptual understanding, and the independence of students in the process of learning chemistry.

papers.title: Generative AI-Assisted French Reading Practices Among French Education Students in Indonesia: Six-Dimensional Descriptive Study
papers.authors: Diana Rosita, Muhammad Sukirlan, Nurlaksana Eko Rusminto, Budi Kadaryanto
papers.abstract: The use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in language learning increasingly offers opportunities to support reading activities, yet it also presents challenges regarding text comprehension, information verification, reflection, and the responsible use of AI. This study aims to describe Generative AI-assisted French reading practices among university students across six domains: Metacognitive Reading Strategies, Text Comprehension and Evaluation, AI-assisted Reading, Verification and Critical Thinking regarding AI Outputs, Reflection and Reading Practice, and Ethical and Responsible AI Use. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing a descriptive, non-experimental, and cross-sectional design. Data were collected from 65 students in the French Language Education Study Program at the University of Lampung using a 30-item questionnaire with a six-point Likert scale. The results indicate positive trends across all six domains, with the highest tendency observed in Metacognitive Reading Strategies and the lowest in Text Comprehension and Evaluation. The findings demonstrate that Generative AI serves not only as a tool for text comprehension but also supports verification, reflection, and responsible AI usage within French reading practices.

papers.title: ChatGPT-5.0 for patient consultation on periocular botulinum toxin: accuracy, readability, and user experience
papers.authors: İlter İritaş, Seçil Yigen İritaş
papers.abstract: Aim: This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy, readability, and user experience of ChatGPT-5.0 when addressing common patient queries regarding periocular botulinum toxin applications. Materials and Methods: Twenty candidate patient-oriented questions were gathered from public online resources. A dermatologist and an ophthalmologist selected 12 clinically relevant questions. On February 1, 2026, each question was submitted to ChatGPT-5.0 once without added context. Accuracy was scored on a 1–4 tier scale (1: completely accurate, 4: inadequate). Readability was evaluated using Flesch Reading Ease (FRES) and Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL). User experience was assessed via a 26-item bipolar adjective scale (−3 to +3).Results: ChatGPT-5.0 demonstrated high clinical accuracy. Reviewer 1 rated 10 responses as completely accurate and 2 as minorly correctable; Reviewer 2 rated 9 as completely accurate and 3 as minorly correctable. No response was rated as inadequate, yielding high inter-rater agreement (91.7%, Cohen’s κ=0.75). User experience scores were consistently high (means between +2 and +3; agreement 69.2%, κ=0.49). However, readability metrics indicated high linguistic complexity: FRES scores ranged from 17.55 to 49.95 (difficult to very difficult) and FKGL spanned from 8.62 to 14.22 (late high-school to undergraduate level).Conclusion: ChatGPT-5.0 produces clinically accurate and coherent responses regarding periocular botulinum toxin. However, its high reading difficulty presents a barrier for general patient health literacy. Therefore, ChatGPT-5.0 is best utilized as a physician-supervised supplementary tool, highlighting the necessity to tailor AI outputs to patient comprehension levels.

papers.title: Comparison of ChatGPT models' responses on lateral epicondylitis in terms of reliability and usefulness
papers.authors: Emre Uzun, Muhammed Zahid Şahin, Rıdvan İşik, İbrahim Tekeoğlu, Ayhan Kamanlı
papers.abstract: Aim: Our aim in this study was to compare the reliability and clinical usefulness of answers generated by ChatGPT’s GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking models for the most frequently searched patient questions on lateral epicondylitis.Materials and Methods: This study was designed as a pilot, descriptive, expert-evaluated large language model (LLM) output assessment study. Google Trends was queried for “tennis elbow” and “lateral epicondylitis”. The six highest-ranked questions were posed to GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking. Three senior physiatrists independently rated every response using the seven-point Reliability and Usefulness Scales. Results: Both models produced reliable and moderately useful responses. Mean ± SD reliability scores were 5.11 ± 1.18 for GPT-5.1 Instant and 5.06 ± 1.21 for GPT-5.1 Thinking, while usefulness scores were 5.22 ± 1.22 and 5.50 ± 1.38, respectively. Differences were not statistically significant (reliability Z = -1.00, p = 0.317, r ≈ 0.41; usefulness Z = -1.60, p = 0.109, r ≈ 0.65), though GPT-5.1 Thinking trended higher in usefulness. Inter-rater agreement was excellent for all ratings (ICC = 0.94-0.98), indicating consistent scoring.Conclusion: GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking both delivered reliable, moderately useful information on lateral epicondylitis, with GPT-5.1 Thinking showing a numerically higher usefulness score that did not reach statistical significance. These findings support ChatGPT’s potential as patient-education aid for musculoskeletal disorders while underscoring the need for expert oversight and further research across broader topics, languages, and chatbot platforms.

papers.title: Modeling City Image Through Sharia Economic Ecosystems in West Java’s Regional Governments
papers.authors: Agus Wahyudin, Agus Rahayu, Lili Adi Wibowo, Kartawan, Ihda Farhatun Nisak, Ahmad Hidayat Sutawidjaya
papers.journal: Ilomata International Journal of Tax and Accounting
papers.abstract: Introduction: Public sector place branding in Muslim-majority developing countries remains under-researched from a theoretical perspective, particularly regarding the mechanisms by which religiosity-based values ​​transform into institutionally recognized city image capabilities. This study examines the relationships between the Religiosity Climate and Religiosity-based Leadership and City Image, and whether Sharia Economic Strategies and Halal Product Support Processes mediate these relationships. The study’s novelty lies in modeling city branding as value co-creation within a religiously oriented public sector service ecosystem. Methods: Using a census of the Regional Development Planning Agencies of all 27 regencies and cities in West Java, Indonesia, with one purposively selected key informant per agency, data were collected through a structured 5-point questionnaire administered from September to December 2023 and analyzed with structural equation modeling–partial least squares (SEM-PLS) using SmartPLS. Results: Religiosity Leadership significantly affected Sharia Economic Strategy, the Halal Product Supporting Process, and City Image, and Religiosity Climate significantly affected Sharia Economic Strategy, the Halal Product Supporting Process, and City Image. The Halal Product Supporting Process was the strongest direct driver of City Image, and both mediators carried significant indirect effects, including a serial pathway from Religiosity Climate through Sharia Economic Strategy and the Halal Product Supporting Process to City Image. Conclusion: Religious values ​​shape the city's image—both directly and indirectly—through operational mechanisms such as a coherent Sharia economic strategy and an effective halal product support system. Consequently, local governments can actively shape a "place brand" grounded in religious values, rather than merely communicating it.

papers.title: Data Governance and Auditor Readiness for Generative AI-Based Audits: A Survey Study of Indonesian External Auditors with AI Literacy as a Mediator
papers.authors: Riva Ubar Harahap, Muhammad Fahmi
papers.journal: Ilomata International Journal of Tax and Accounting
papers.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence into financial statement auditing promises enhanced efficiency and analytical depth. This study addresses this gap by investigating the relationship between data governance and auditor readiness for generative AI-based audits, with AI literacy as a mediating variable. Using a quantitative survey design, data were collected from 248 external auditors across public accounting firms in Indonesia, including Big Four affiliates, large national firms, and small and medium practices. The research model, grounded in the Technology-Organization-Environment framework and knowledge-based theory, was tested through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. Data governance exerted a significant positive effect on both auditor readiness (β = 0.47, p < 0.001) and AI literacy (β = 0.67, p < 0.001). AI literacy partially mediated this relationship (indirect effect = 0.26, p < 0.001; VAF = 35.6%), indicating that robust data governance enhances readiness both directly and indirectly by elevating auditors' AI comprehension. The model explained 61.7% of the variance in auditor readiness. Among data governance dimensions, data quality demonstrated the highest relative importance, while data architecture showed lower contribution. These findings extend the TOE framework by specifying data governance maturity as a critical organizational context factor for generative AI adoption in auditing, and they provide practical guidance for audit firm leaders, regulators, and professional bodies in emerging economies. Key recommendations include institutionalizing data quality standards, establishing clear stewardship roles, and integrating AI literacy development with data governance training.

papers.title: ALADIN: Attention-based Lightweight Architecture for Drowsiness Identification
papers.abstract: Drowsiness is a major cause of vehicular and in dustrial accidents, motivating the need for real-time monitoring systems that are accurate, non-intrusive, and deployable on low power platforms. While physiological signal–based approaches (e.g., EEG/EOG) provide high reliability, their dependence on sensor attachment makes them intrusive for everyday use. Camera-based solutions are more practical but face two key challenges. First, state-of-the-art deep learning–based face recognition and drowsiness detection models require substantial computational and memory resources, making them unsuitable for embedded deployment. Popular architectures such as DeepFace, Keras-Face, and VGG-Face are extremely accurate but Cloud-scale. Existing approaches for camera based drowsiness detection often rely on heavy convolutional or attention-based backbones, resulting in large parameter footprints and high operational complexity. Deploying these models on embedded systems typically leads to significant accuracy degradation. Second, traditional handcrafted pipelines, although lightweight, depend heavily on face detection and landmark extraction, making them fragile under illumination changes, occlusions, and multi-view variations. Our experiments show that even extended handcrafted feature pipelines struggle to exceed 75–82% accuracy under realistic conditions. To address these limitations, we propose a compact end to-end CNN architecture enhanced with Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM). The proposed model achieves 99.05% accuracy on YAWDD and94.65%onNTHU-DDD,outperforming transfer-learning backbones such as MobileNetV2, ResNet-50, and EfficientNet-B0. Furthermore, component wise performance analysis confirms the effectiveness of CBAM-based attention refinement, while computational analysis shows that the model achieves superior predictive performance with only 0.539M parameters, enabling an effective balance between accuracy, compactness, and execution efficiency for resource-constrained drowsiness monitoring systems.

papers.title: How large language models react to contradictions in one prompt
papers.authors: Agam Sharda
papers.abstract: The paper includes a test run on free models of some large language models, the test includes a scenario to test what the AI will do when it is given a contradiction to a previously stated point in the same prompt, in just one prompt This test checks whether an AI will follow an instruction by an authority, or focus on the prompt of the individuals. The test involved a fake assignment of subject English from grade ninth and a “hidden” message by the teacher that instructed the AI to either refuse to write the essay, or to insert certain words as a sort of indicator without telling the student This test was repeated twice in new chats. In the models tested [mentioned above], only grok obeyed the hidden instructions by the teacher and refused to write the essay even after multiple requests. While chatGPT explicitly said that it was ignoring a hidden message and focused on the interests of the individual. Gemini had a much less clear path and in the first trial, explicitly said that it was ignoring the hidden message and in the second, it put the instructed words in the essay as an indicator Thus it can be hypothesized that out of the three free LLMs [large language models] tested, only grok’s behaviour consistently prioritized authoritarian instructions, chatGPT's behaviour consistently prioritized the interests of the individual and Gemini’s behaviour can change even with the same prompts

papers.title: Building Bridges: AI-Driven Collaborative Models for Research-Practice Partnerships
papers.authors: Alice Abonjia Kulo
papers.abstract: This chapter examines the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in strengthening Research–Practice Partnerships (RPPs) as collaborative structures that bridge academic research and real-world educational practice. Rather than centering on domain-specific engineering applications, the chapter foregrounds RPP theory, partnership governance, and educational implementation in AI-mediated contexts. It argues that AI-facilitated communication platforms, shared data infrastructures, and codesigned inquiry cycles can function as connective mechanisms that support continuous knowledge exchange, joint problem-solving, and evidence-informed decision-making between researchers and practitioners. Drawing on illustrative examples from STEM education and selected technical domains, the chapter shows how AI tools such as data analytics, machine learning, and adaptive systems—can support timely interpretation of complex datasets and enhance collaborative inquiry without displacing human judgment. Case studies ranging from automated bridge deck assessment to enhanced pedagogical competence in science education demonstrate that AI-driven models move beyond simple automation toward a state of data-driven discovery. Central to this transformation is the “human element,” including the development of practitioner capacity, reduction of technology-related anxiety, and the cultivation of professional learning communities supported by AI-enabled feedback systems. The chapter further addresses critical dimensions of AI ethics, including data privacy, transparency, fairness, and the need for Explainable AI (XAI) within RPP processes. It highlights governance structures that ensure equitable participation, shared accountability, and iterative feedback loops that sustain partnerships over time. Through case-based discussion, the chapter demonstrates that AI-driven RPP models extend beyond automation toward data-informed discovery, adaptive professional learning, and context-sensitive innovation. The chapter concludes with a strategic roadmap for sustainable implementation of AI-enhanced RPPs, emphasizing capacity building, ethical safeguards, and collaborative leadership. These AIenabled partnerships ultimately support the co-creation of knowledge that is pedagogically meaningful, socially responsible, and ecologically valid for advancing 21st-century education systems. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Research–Practice Partnerships, Collaboration, Educational Implementation, Capacity Building, AI Ethics

papers.title: Diagnostic delay and misdiagnosis in interstitial lung disease
papers.authors: Muhammad Arsalan, Arslan Rahat Ullah, Iftikhar Khan, Muhammad Sajid, Tajdar Ali, Tajdar Ali, Shahzad Ahmad
papers.abstract: Background: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) comprises a heterogeneous group of diffuse parenchymal lung disorders characterized by progressive inflammation and fibrosis, leading to impaired pulmonary function, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality. Because the clinical and radiological manifestations of ILD often overlap with other respiratory and cardiac conditions, patients frequently experience diagnostic delay and misdiagnosis, resulting in inappropriate treatment and disease progression. This study aimed to determine the frequency of diagnostic delay and misdiagnosis among patients with interstitial lung disease and to assess their association with demographic and clinical factors. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at the Department of Pulmonology, from 6-02-2026 to 6-05-2026 including 194 patients with confirmed interstitial lung disease aged 18–80 years were included in the study. Diagnostic delay was defined as diagnosis made more than six months after onset of symptoms, while misdiagnosis was defined as any previous incorrect respiratory diagnosis before confirmation of interstitial lung disease. Data were analyzed using SPSS-25. Chi-square test and Fisher’s Exact test were applied for stratified analysis. Results: Mean age of the patients was 54.19±17.28 years and mean BMI was 22.68±3.01 kg/m². Females comprised 133 (68.6%) participants and 114 (58.8%) belonged to rural areas. The most common presenting symptom was breathlessness 94 (48.5%), followed by chronic cough 52 (26.8%). Misdiagnosis was observed in 136 (70.1%) patients, while diagnostic delay was identified in 142 (73.2%). Tuberculosis 40 (29.4%) and asthma 38 (27.9%) were the most frequent previous incorrect diagnoses. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis was the commonest type of interstitial lung disease 52 (26.8%). Diagnostic delay was significantly associated with age above 50 years (p<0.001) and type of interstitial lung disease (p=0.026). Conclusion: Diagnostic delay and misdiagnosis were highly prevalent among patients with interstitial lung disease.

papers.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE PLANNING IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
papers.authors: Mahmoud Shaarawy ABDULAZIM
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative catalyst in Supply Chain Management (SCM), shifting operations from traditional models to predictive and automated systems. This article examines the impact of AI technologies—specifically Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), on supply chain planning. Grounded in Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory (DCT), we analyze how AI enhances planning efficiency across strategic, tactical, and operational horizons. Furthermore, we critically evaluate key implementation challenges, including data governance, system integration, algorithmic transparency, human-AI trust, and organizational change management. The article concludes with key managerial insights and future research directions for sustainable, resilient, and AI-augmented supply chains.

papers.title: CHATGPT AS A MAIN SOURCE OF LEARNING ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION: TRANSFORMATION OR DISTORTION OF EDUCATION
papers.authors: Rohayati Rohayati, Mumu Zainal Mutaqin, Siti Imas Masitoh
papers.journal: SYAIKHONA Jurnal Magister Pendidikan Agama Islam
papers.abstract: This study aims to analyze the use of AI ChatGPT as a learning resource in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) materials at SMA Terpadu Mathla’ul Anwar Bojong. Based on the development of artificial intelligence technology, this study focuses on three aspects, namely the use of ChatGPT as a learning resource, its advantages and disadvantages, and the level of students' understanding after using it. This research uses a descriptive qualitative research approach. Descriptive qualitative is an approach that is used systematically to study a phenomenon or event through data in the form of narratives or descriptions obtained in natural conditions, without manipulation by the researcher. Its main characteristic lies in the effort to deeply explore experiences, meanings, and patterns that emerge in real situations by utilizing interview, observation, and document review techniques. The data collection techniques through interviews, observation, and documentation, the research involved PAI teachers and students as subjects. The research results show that ChatGPT is utilized as a supportive learning medium, helping to explain the material, providing example questions, and facilitating interactive discussions. Its advantages include ease of access, speed of information, and explanations that are easy to understand, while its disadvantages include the potential for inaccurate information, limited in-depth Islamic values, and students' dependence on technology. The level of students' understanding of PAI material increased significantly after using ChatGPT, but teacher guidance is still needed so that the use of technology runs optimally.

papers.title: Soberania decisória e IA de defesa no Sul Global: o caso brasileiro
papers.authors: Everton Antônio Ramos
papers.abstract: This article identifies, from the Brazilian case, conditions for preserving decision sovereignty in the development of a Defense artificial intelligence (AI) structure in Global South contexts marked by technological vulnerabilities and communication constraints in contested networks. It adopts a predominantly qualitative approach, supported by descriptive quantitative indicators, and uses Brazil as an embedded single-case study, with the United States as a contextual contrast. The corpus combines defense legislation and policy, military doctrine, multilateral documents, academic literature, technology-readiness indicators, cloud-infrastructure data, and records of firms accredited by the Brazilian Ministry of Defense. The analysis treats external technological dependence and algorithmic opacity as distinct problems. In Brazil, external exposure is clearest in computing infrastructure, while capabilities related to AI models remain less clearly determined by public sources. Documented capabilities are more visible in integration, communications, information security, and command and control. The analysis of military decision-making shows that opacity, cognitive load, trust calibration, and degraded communications condition the assessment of AI-generated outputs. The findings are organized around control and authority, verification, explainability, and continuity. The article concludes that decision sovereignty does not require complete domestic production of the technological chain, provided that the state preserves sufficient capabilities to control, assess, and sustain the functions that condition the military use of AI.

papers.title: The nexus between agility-fostering competences and AI literacy of higher education students
papers.authors: Anna Chwiłkowska-Kubala, Kamila Magdalena Malewska, Witold Szumowski
papers.abstract: Research background and purpose The pace of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption not only in organizations, but also in higher education is accelerating, raising questions about whether students possess the competences required to engage with AI critically and effectively. Although adaptive capacity is frequently assumed to facilitate technology use, limited empirical evidence clarifies whether such capacity translates into AI literacy. Drawing on the conceptualisation of student agility as a multidimensional metacapability comprising proactivity, adaptability, and resilience, this study examines the relationships between key competences, agility, and AI literacy in higher education. Design/methodology/approach The study is based on survey data collected from 224 management and finance students. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) were conducted to validate the measurement constructs used in the study. Structural modelling was applied to examine whether competences that foster agility also predict AI literacy. Findings The results indicate that agility and AI literacy follow partially distinct developmental pathways. While teamwork and cognitive competences significantly predict agility, AI literacy is primarily shaped by knowledge–skill competences and human–tool collaboration, while cultural competence does not show a statistically significant effect. Value added and limitations The findings challenge the assumption that generic student agility automatically fosters AI literacy and highlight the need to conceptually differentiate between adaptive capacity and AI-specific competence development in higher education. This study is subject to several limitations. The sample was relatively homogeneous, consisting of students from a single type of higher education institution within one national context, which may limit generalisability. Future research could extend this analysis to diverse institutional profiles and cross-national settings

papers.title: Digital competence, artificial intelligence utilization, and innovation capability: Basis for a maritime technology adoption framework for Filipino seafarers
papers.authors: John Edward L Umali
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Studies in Management
papers.abstract: This study assessed the digital competence, artificial intelligence utilization, and innovation capability of Filipino seafarers and proposed a Maritime Technology Adoption Framework.The study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design, and 384 Filipino seafarers were selected using purposive sampling.Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire adapted from the DigComp Framework, contemporary maritime artificial intelligence utilization models, and innovation capability frameworks.The results revealed that Filipino seafarers demonstrated a high level of digital competence (CM = 3.55), with Information Literacy obtaining the highest assessment.Likewise, respondents exhibited a high extent of artificial intelligence utilization (CM = 3.79), with the Human Element dimension receiving the highest rating, highlighting the continued importance of human judgment in AIassisted operations.Furthermore, Filipino seafarers showed a high level of innovation capability (CM = 3.68), with Performance emerging as the highest-rated dimension.Correlation analysis indicated significant relationships between selected dimensions of digital competence and artificial intelligence utilization, as well as between selected dimensions of artificial intelligence utilization and innovation capability.However, no significant relationship was found between digital competence and innovation capability.A framework for Maritime Technology Adoption for Filipino Seafarers was developed based on the findings of the study.The framework identifies Digital Competence as the foundation, Artificial Intelligence Utilization as the enabling mechanism, and Innovation Capability as the outcome, highlighting both the direct and indirect pathways through which digital competence strengthens innovation capability.The framework provides a structured guide for workforce readiness and maritime digital transformation.

papers.title: From Alignment to Implementation: Governing AI Literacy as a Coordinated National Capability in Progressive GULF Education Systems
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence literacy has become a strategic priority for education systems preparing learners for workforce participation, civic engagement, and responsible interaction with emerging technologies.In progressive to moderate GULF countries, enabling conditions are increasingly in place to support large-scale adoption, including digital infrastructure, policy direction, quality assurance systems, and post-pandemic digital maturity.The policy opportunity lies in strengthening alignment across these elements to enable consistent, scalable implementation.This article argues that AI literacy can be governed as a coordinated national capability through alignment across policy, educator competency, institutional readiness, and monitoring systems.Drawing on regional findings and contemporary literature, the analysis identifies priorities for system development, including coordinated governance across government institutions, unified educator competency frameworks, and national monitoring mechanisms.The article proposes a governance architecture that integrates central direction with institutional execution through tiered competencies, readiness assessment, and phased implementation, supporting sustained, system-wide capability development across diverse education contexts.

papers.title: The Effect of Artificial Intelligence on Pedagogical Readiness with Digital Literacy as a Mediating Variable
papers.authors: Yuyun Yumiarty
papers.journal: Formosa Journal of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: This study examined the effects of Artificial Intelligence on digital literacy and pedagogical readiness, as well as the effect of digital literacy on pedagogical readiness and its mediating role in the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and pedagogical readiness among Primary Teacher Education students at IAIN Curup. A quantitative explanatory design was employed. The population comprised 240 second-semester students, with 136 respondents selected through random sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire based on indicators of the study variables. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS, involving outer and inner model assessments. The results showed that Artificial Intelligence positively and significantly influenced digital literacy and pedagogical readiness. Digital literacy also significantly predicted pedagogical readiness and mediated the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and pedagogical readiness

papers.title: Customs Training at the Crossroads: Preparing Border Authorities for Risk Governance Through Curriculum Alignment With WCO Professional Standards
papers.authors: Paulo Rocha
papers.abstract: This article examines the alignment of the bachelor program in Customs, trade and border management at the University of Stavanger, Norway, with the World Customs Organization’s (WCO) Professional Standards 2019 , originally launched as the Professional Standards for Customs Operational and Senior Managers in 2008. As frontline agencies in national systems of societal safety, managing risks related to illicit trade, customs administrations handle cross-border crime, supply chain disruption and technological vulnerabilities. Therefore, the aim herein is to assess how effectively the program has been preparing graduates for the evolving demands of customs practice. The study adopts a curriculum mapping approach, comparing course content and learning outcomes against the WCO’s Professional Standards 2019 , which is structured according to a knowledge, skills and attitudes (KSA) model. Methodologically, the analysis combines curriculum mapping with a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (SWOT) framework, allowing for both internal evaluation of program strengths and weaknesses and external assessment of opportunities and threats in the global customs education landscape. Findings indicate that the Norwegian program offers strong training in law, ethics, organisational culture, logistics and other traditional fields, providing students with solid legal and operational foundations reinforced by practical training. However, gaps exist in financial management data-driven customs operations, and customer orientation, while emerging competencies in artificial intelligence, blockchain and cybersecurity remain underdeveloped. The study concludes that reforming the curriculum to integrate digital modernisation and stakeholder-oriented skills would future-proof Norwegian customs education and position it as a model internationally.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Echocardiography: Five Clinical Challenges and a Roadmap Toward Responsible Integration by 2030
papers.authors: Fatih Aydın
papers.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi Arsivi-Archives of the Turkish Society of Cardiology
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled echocardiography has demonstrated strong agreement with expert measurements across a broad range of cardiac functional parameters. However, the transition from technical validation to clinical impact remains incomplete. This structured narrative review employed a systematic literature search to identify the principal structural barriers to AI integration in echocardiography and to develop an expert-informed, evidence-grounded perspective on the priorities for responsible implementation by 2030. The methodological heterogeneity of the included studies, including retrospective and prospective designs, diverse outcome measures ranging from measurement agreement to workflow implementation, and multiple AI application domains, precluded quantitative pooling. Therefore, qualitative synthesis was selected as the primary prespecified analytical approach. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for studies published between January 2015 and January 2026 addressing clinical AI applications, real-world validation, implementation science, and governance. Forty-six studies meeting predefined inclusion criteria underwent qualitative synthesis. Five interdependent domains were identified: reproducibility across clinical settings, generalizability beyond development datasets, the lack of outcome-focused evidence, regulatory and governance immaturity, and insufficient trust among clinicians and patients. Automated measurements of left ventricular function, strain, and valvular disease severity demonstrate close agreement with expert assessments. However, few studies have shown that AI-assisted echocardiography translates into improved patient outcomes. Based on the available evidence, the principal translational barrier appears to be not algorithmic capability itself, but rather the structural requirements necessary for accountable clinical integration. An expert-informed, evidence-grounded roadmap emphasizing decision-level reproducibility, rigorous external validation, outcome-linked evidence generation, continuous lifecycle governance, and human-centered design is proposed to guide the integration of AI into echocardiography and to support the development of a more durable and accountable clinical infrastructure by 2030.

papers.title: AI in Financial Forecasting: A Study on Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Corporate Finance
papers.authors: Praveena Devi, Praveena Puppala
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
papers.abstract: Traditionally, financial forecasting has been based on historical data, statistical models, spreadsheets and the expertise and experience of financial personnel. With the advent of big data, sophisticated computation, and artificial intelligence (AI) tools, financial forecasting can be made faster, more accurate, and more efficient. This research investigates the leveraging of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Forecasting in Corporate Finance and assesses the expected effects on the accuracy of forecasting, planning effectiveness and users' trust. Also examined are the key organizational and technical challenges impacting AI adoption, such as data quality, explainability, organizational readiness and resistance to change. A cross-sectional study was applied with a quantitative research design, prompted by a structured survey of finance, accounting and technology professionals whose knowledge or experience was related to financial forecasting using AI enabled technologies. The results show that there are perceived advantages over the accuracy of forecasts and planning efficiency using an AI-based forecasting approach over traditional forecasting approaches. Some of the findings do underscore, however, continuing questions about the quality, transparency, trust, and readiness of organizations. The study also suggests that AI is perceived more as a tool to aid in decision-making and assist finance professionals than as a superior method for making decisions. The results offer valuable guidance on successful and responsible implementation of AI in the financial planning and forecasting organization.

papers.title: Automated Misconception Diagnosis & Pedagogical Remediation: Using Generative AI to Identify and Remedy Structural Bugs in Introductory Code
papers.authors: Bhanupriya Sharma
papers.journal: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
papers.abstract: Novice programmers in introductory computer science (CS1) courses frequently experience cognitive overload, helplessness, and attrition due to structural code bugs. Unlike superficial syntax errors caught by standard compilers, structural bugs stem from fundamental misalignments between a student's mental model and the runtime execution context. While recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable code generation capabilities, generic LLM feedback often defaults to providing direct, answer-giving code patches. This passive resolution deprives students of essential problem-solving opportunities and exacerbates misconception persistence. This paper introduces StructDiag-AI, a novel novel Socratic diagnostic framework that integrates Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) static analysis with constrained LLM prompt synthesis. By isolating AST structural divergences prior to prompt assembly, StructDiag-AI identifies non-viable algorithmic patterns (e.g., misnested loops, unreachable recursive branches, and state mutation outside iteration) and generates progressive, non-generative Socratic pedagogical hints. We present a multi-institutional empirical trial ($N = 482$ CS1 students) evaluating StructDiag-AI against traditional compiler errors and baseline unconstrained LLM feedback. Quantitative results demonstrate that StructDiag-AI increases novice bug resolution rates by 38.4% compared to standard compilers and improves long-term conceptual retention by 24.1% over unconstrained LLM feedback. Furthermore, qualitative analysis reveals a significant reduction in student frustration metrics and rapid convergence toward correct mental models.

papers.title: AI as Double-Edged Sword: A Quantitative study of Teacher Efficiency, Cognitive Load and Burnout in Education
papers.authors: Nazia Fardous, Muhammad IDREES, Muhammad Afzal
papers.journal: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Social Science
papers.abstract: Teaching practices have been transformed by Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration in education. Use of AI has automated administrative tasks. Instructional delivery has been enhanced, and personalized learning is supported by using AI in education. Its use promises to increase efficiency and reduce workload, but there is emerging evidence that AI usage may contribute to burnout among teachers simultaneously by increasing stress caused by technology usage and cognitive load . This study explores dual role of AI-based educational technologies towards burnout, by analyzing whether AI works as a tool of relief or a source of psychological stress by using quantitative research design with a sample of 500 school teachers. In this study the relation between use of AI, perceived efficiency, cognitive load, and levels of burnout has been analyzed. The findings of this study indicate that while AI usage in education significantly improve task efficiency (r = 0.62), it also pose new problems by elevating mental workload that contribute to burnout (R² = 0.49) among teachers. It is concluded, based on the finding of this study that AI usage in education works as a double-edged sword by providing both benefits and problems. It is emphasized that there a dire need for strategies to implement AI usage in education with a proper balance reducing problems while enhancing its benefits.

papers.title: Institutional Asymmetries in the Digital Transformation of Ukrainian Business: Assessment and Strategic Priorities
papers.authors: Вікторія Кифяк, Oleksandr Kozak
papers.journal: Проблеми сучасних трансформацій Серія економіка та управління
papers.abstract: This article presents a comprehensive assessment and defines strategic priorities for overcoming institutional asymmetries in the digital transformation of Ukrainian business under current socio-economic challenges. It substantiates that contemporary digital dynamics require eliminating the structural gap between rapid public-sector digital renewal and the adaptive capacity of business entities. Grounded in institutional economic theory, the methodology employs a comparative analysis of Ukraine’s standing across five international digitalization indices, a statistical and correlation analysis of the Regional Digital Transformation Index, and an analytical synthesis of AI adoption surveys. The assessment reveals a substantial institutional asymmetry between high public-sector achievements globally (Group A in the GovTech Maturity Index, 40th in the Government AI Readiness Index) and the moderate digital maturity of business and local communities (44.9/100). The correlation analysis (r = -0.06) indicates the absence of a statistically significant linear relationship between basic digital skills and regional digital economy development, an empirical pattern interpreted as consistent with qualitative institutional and regulatory barriers rather than as direct proof of their causal effect. Furthermore, the analysis exposes an asymmetry in business reliance on artificial intelligence: while 93% of companies utilize AI, only 18.4% apply it to cybersecurity, and, per a comparable commercial industry survey, 21% of executives report project failures due to reliance on unverified AI output and missing data-verification protocols. The scientific novelty of the study lies in substantiating a systematic approach to developing the institution of business digital transformation based on a three-tier diagnostic of the digital divide between the state and entrepreneurship, which, unlike existing works, enables shifting the problem of the public–private digital gap from the realm of declarative policy into the practical system of managerial priorities for enterprises. To address these deformations, the paper proposes a framework emphasizing the institutional – rather than purely resource or infrastructural – nature of these imbalances. It substantiates six strategic priorities for developing the institution of business digital transformation, aiming to harmonize regulatory frameworks, incentivize investment, and enhance overall enterprise digital maturity. The findings should be interpreted with two limitations in mind: the regional correlation analysis relies on a sample of 12 regions, and the artificial-intelligence findings draw on two independently designed business surveys. Future research should extend the empirical base as more regional data become available. This is an empirical study based on quantitative and comparative-analytical methods.

papers.title: The inclusive digital economic infrastructure framework: A system level integration of AI, blockchain, and tokenization for sustainable development
papers.authors: Shirley Mo Ching Yeung, Samson Lee, Sabrina Kate Lee
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Research and Scientific Studies
papers.abstract: Contemporary poverty is increasingly understood as a multidimensional phenomenon encompassing income deprivation, vulnerability, digital exclusion, and limited participation in emerging economic systems. This paper contributes a system level ICT4D framework that bridges intelligence systems and decentralized value distribution mechanisms, demonstrating how the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), Web3, blockchain, and tokenization can address multidimensional poverty through interoperable socio technical systems.The paper introduces the Inclusive Digital Economic Infrastructure (IDEI), a multi layer framework comprising intelligence, infrastructure, value, and application layers. Drawing on global policy reports, emerging enterprise practices, and multi stakeholder perspectives, the framework provides a structured approach to integrating AI driven decision making with decentralized trust mechanisms and programmable value systems.The study identifies a critical gap in existing literature, where AI and decentralized technologies remain largely disconnected, and proposes a unified architecture for inclusive and sustainable digital economic systems. The IDEI framework contributes to interdisciplinary research at the intersection of digital infrastructure design, artificial intelligence, and inclusive economic development, with direct relevance to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the design of inclusive, socio-technical digital systems.The framework also provides a foundation for responsible management education through the integration of emerging technologies, stakeholder engagement, and sustainable development outcomes.

papers.title: Penguatan Literasi Hukum Keluarga Islam Dan Hukum Ekonomi Syariah Melalui Pelatihan Produksi Konten Edukatif Berbasis Artificial Intelligence Pada BKMT Kabupaten Banjar
papers.authors: Lusiana Lusiana, Muhammad Sauqi, Rusdiana Rusdiana, Yulida Mardini
papers.journal: Al-Umm Jurnal Pengabdian dan Pengembangan Masyarakat
papers.abstract: Islamic family law and Islamic economic law literacy are important for strengthening community capacity to understand legal issues related to family life and economic activities. However, the dissemination of Islamic legal knowledge still faces challenges in utilizing digital technology and producing engaging, accessible, and reliable educational content. This community service program aimed to strengthen Islamic family law and Islamic economic law literacy while developing the ability of members of the Badan Kontak Majelis Taklim (BKMT) of Banjar Regency to produce educational content using Artificial Intelligence (AI) critically and responsibly. The program employed a Participatory Action Research (PAR) approach involving needs identification, action planning, material delivery, demonstration, practice, mentoring, evaluation, and reflection. The activities involved 30 participants and covered Islamic family law, Islamic economic law, AI applications, prompt development, educational content production, and verification of AI-generated information. The results showed an increase in the overall average participant achievement from 43.33% before the program to 80.33% after the program, representing a 37 percentage-point increase. The largest improvement occurred in educational content production, which increased from 32% to 81% (49 percentage points), while Islamic family law literacy increased from 58% to 82% and Islamic economic law literacy from 55% to 80%. Participants also demonstrated improved abilities in developing prompts, producing communicative visual content, and verifying AI-generated information. These findings indicate that integrating Islamic legal literacy with AI-based content production can support community capacity development while emphasizing critical verification and the continued role of scholarly authority in Islamic legal education

papers.title: Sex-Specific Educational Gradients in Measured Obesity in Kuwait and Qatar: A Pooled Analysis of Three Who Steps Surveys
papers.authors: Ayman Mahgoub
papers.abstract: Background: Adult obesity prevalence in the Gulf states is among the highest recorded anywhere, and it is consistently higher in women than in men. How obesity is distributed by socioeconomic position within these populations has received far less attention, and the available evidence comes almost entirely from single-country analyses. We estimated educational gradients in measured obesity, separately for women and men, across the Gulf surveys whose microdata are publicly released.Methods: We pooled individual records from three WHO STEPS surveys available through the WHO NCD Microdata Repository: Kuwait 2006 (analytic n = 2,211), Kuwait 2014 (n = 3,573) and Qatar 2012 (n = 2,383). Obesity was defined from measured height and weight (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²). Education was harmonised to three levels. Inequality was quantified with the slope index of inequality (SII) and relative index of inequality (RII) from survey-weighted regressions with age adjustment, fitted separately by sex. Weighted prevalence estimates were checked against the official survey fact sheets before any model was run.Results: Obesity prevalence was 41.5% in Kuwait 2006, 40.1% in Kuwait 2014 and 41.1% in Qatar 2012. Among women, obesity was strongly concentrated at low education in every survey: RII 1.68 (95% CI 1.36–2.09) in Kuwait 2006, 1.70 (1.42–2.04) in Kuwait 2014 and 1.59 (1.29–1.96) in Qatar 2012, corresponding to absolute gaps of 23 to 25 percentage points. Among men the gradient was absent in Kuwait in both years but present in Qatar (RII 1.54, 1.12–2.12). The women's gradient in Kuwait did not change between 2006 and 2014 (interaction p = 0.64). Gradients grew steeper for severe obesity and were reproduced with waist-based measures.Conclusions: Obesity in Kuwait and Qatar carries a marked educational patterning in women that has persisted over time, while the male pattern differs between the two countries. Prevention strategies that treat these populations as uniform are likely to miss the groups at highest risk.

papers.title: An Educational Program Based on Artificial Intelligence Tools for Improving History Achievement Among Fourth-Grade Literary Stream Female Students
papers.authors: Hawraa Jundi Dawood Lafteh Al-Mayali
papers.abstract: The subject of history faces challenges requiring student-centered strategies to develop essential skills. Current teaching methods remain traditional and need development through modern approaches fostering creative thinking. There is a notable absence of artificial intelligence tools in lesson design and educational activities. Integrating AI offers significant potential to make the learning experience more interactive and engaging. This research addresses students' weak academic achievement in history by leveraging AI tools to optimize instruction.

papers.title: Computational Modalities in Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis: Advances in Methods, Challenges in Application, and Future Research Directions
papers.authors: Pradeeba V
papers.abstract: Background: Parkinson's disease affects over 11 million people worldwide, with an age-standardized incidence of 15.63 new cases per 100,000. Current diagnostic approaches rely on clinical evaluation and expensive neuroimaging techniques, which are a major obstacle to early detection and timely intervention. Artificial intelligence technologies offer unprecedented opportunities for the development of objective and affordable diagnostic systems, but there are still significant gaps between current evidence and clinical application requirements.Objective: The systematic review synthesizes the evidence on computational modalities in PD diagnosis approaches, assesses the diagnostic accuracy and clinical feasibility of different modalities and algorithms, and identifies critical obstacles to clinical translation.Methods: The comprehensive literature review of 51 studies (2020-26) examining the use of computational modalities in the diagnosis of PD. The studies were categorized by diagnostic method including (neuroimaging, behavioral, biochemical), artificial intelligence methodology (deep learning, classical ML, explainability approaches), and quality metrics including data leakage, external validation and bioavailability.Key Findings: Ten diagnostic modalities demonstrated varying performance: SPECT DaTSCAN achieved 98.47% accuracy but faces accessibility constraints, while emerging modalities including speech analysis (89-95% accuracy), gait assessment (86.7-87.65% accuracy), and multimodal EEG+MRI fusion (97.17% accuracy) offer greater accessibility. However, critical methodological issues were endemic: data leakage affected 87% of neuroimaging AI studies, only 8% employed external validation, and 48% used inappropriately complex models for dataset size. Gender-stratified performance gaps of 10-20% documented substantial sex bias. Explainability methods including SHAP, attention heatmaps, and cross-attention mechanisms enhance clinical interpretability while maintaining diagnostic accuracy.Implications: Consequences Although AI has significant diagnostic potential in multiple modalities, its translation into clinical practice requires: (1) prospective external validation in independent populations, (2) standardized data acquisition and reporting protocols, (3) development of gender-specific models, (4) large-scale multi-center studies (more than 1,000 subjects), and (5) health economics. The current evidence is insufficient to recommend any artificial insemination system for routine clinical use without robust prospective validation.Conclusion: Artificial intelligence has emerged as a promising diagnostic tool for multiple sclerosis with a variety of modalities and robust reported precision metrics. However, the systematic methodological constraints and the lack of prospective clinical validation are critical barriers to the uptake of the clinical trial. Future research must prioritize external validation, quality standardization, equity considerations, and real-world implementation studies to bridge the gap between research evidence and clinical practice.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Early Detection of Diabetes Mellitus: An Ensemble Framework Enhanced with Explainable AI and Ablation Study
papers.authors: G. Gayathri
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic condition which is frequently diagnosed late resulting in serious conditions such as cardiovascular disease, nephropathy, neuropathy, retinopathy etc. Current machine learning diabetes risk prediction methods focus on the accuracy of classification and ignore the problem of class imbalance, feature redundancy, probability calibration and interpretability, which are all important for clinical adoption. The study suggests an eight-stage machine learning approach that includes data acquisition, data pre-processing, balancing techniques (SMOTE), feature selection (RFECV and mutual information), ensemble modelling (Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM), probability calibration, explainability (SHAP) and three-level risk stratification. The Random Forest model outperformed all other models on the hold-out data (accuracy = 75.9%, AUC = 0.817) with relatively well-calibrated probabilities, whereas a stacked ensemble model had similar discrimination (AUC = 0.816). The results of the ablation analysis demonstrated that the recall value could be enhanced from 59.3% to 68.3% with slightly decreased precision value by using SMOTE, while the feature scaling method had little impact on the Random Forest model, aggressive feature reduction with RFECV (8→4 features) reduced the AUC value from 0.822 to 0.787, and stacking did not significantly improve the performance of the model compared to the best base learner based on the limited number of samples (n = 768). Significant differences in key performance measures were confirmed by statistical validation using DeLong, Wilcoxon signed-ranked tests and Friedman–Nemenyi tests, and glucose level, BMI and age were the most influential predictors, as would be known from clinical experience, were found using SHAP analysis. The proposed approach combines ensemble learning, calibration, interpretability, and statistically strong validation, making diabetes risk prediction more of a transparent and clinically interpretable decision support tool for early risk assessment instead of a black box approach.

papers.title: The Effect of AI Adoption on Earnings Quality: Evidence from S&P 500 Technology Firms
papers.authors: Julien Merheb
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study examines whether the extent to which firms discuss Artificial Intelligence (AI) in their annual reports is associated with the quality of their reported earnings. Traditional financial reporting depends heavily on managerial judgment, while previous research has shown that the language used in corporate filings can contain information beyond the financial statements themselves (Loughran & McDonald, 2011). However, relatively little empirical research has directly examined whether AI-related disclosure is connected to earnings quality, particularly during the period following the rapid rise of generative AI. To investigate this relationship, I constructed a balanced panel of S&P 500 technology firms covering the study period. AI disclosure intensity was measured through keyword-frequency analysis of Form 10-K filings, while earnings quality was proxied by the absolute value of discretionary accruals estimated using the Modified Jones Model (Dechow et al., 1995). The analysis controls for firm size, leverage, profitability, growth, and year effects. The results indicate a statistically significant negative association between AI disclosure intensity and absolute discretionary accruals. Because lower absolute discretionary accruals are interpreted as higher earnings quality, the findings suggest that firms with more extensive AI-related disclosure tend to report higher-quality earnings. These results contribute to the growing literature on textual analysis of corporate disclosures and provide potentially useful information for investors, auditors, and regulators evaluating AI-related corporate communication. Published in: International Maronite Journal, Vol. 4 Publication date: 2026-10-02 Landing page: https://www.internationalmaronitejournal.com/published/193
