papers.title: AI-Assisted Studying in Medical Education: Measurement Constraints in a Randomized Pilot
papers.authors: Aidan Sauls, Joel Casingal, James Issa, Nawar Attal, Araceli D. Cuaranta, Alexei Gorka, Jonathan Willis, Vineela Kadiyala, Barbara Payne, Robert Finley, Errington Thompson, Michael Abdelmasseh, Juan Sanabria
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This poster was presented at the 38th Annual Marshall University Health Sciences Research Day on October 2, 2026, at the St. Mary's Center for Education in Huntington, West Virginia, USA (Poster Session 1, Abstract #39). Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in medical education, but its short-term educational effects remain uncertain, particularly when assessment difficulty and study-design constraints limit the interpretation of measured outcomes. Methods: In a randomized within-subject crossover pilot, 15 first- and second-year medical students completed structured AI-assisted and No-AI study conditions in randomized order. Each condition was followed by a counterbalanced 10-item post-test. Restricted scoring excluded two Form Y items, and scores were standardized to a common 0–10 metric. Supporting analyses examined period and sequence effects, item difficulty, test-form differences, and ceiling effects. Results: Mean performance was 8.48 following AI-assisted study and 8.20 following No-AI study. The mean paired difference was 0.28 points (2.8 percentage points), favoring AI-assisted study but remaining statistically non-significant (95% CI, −0.54 to 1.11; p = .475). An exploratory item-level mixed-effects model yielded an odds ratio of 1.34 (95% CI, 0.63–2.86; p = .455). Ceiling effects, unequal test-form difficulty, and repeated exposure constrained measurement sensitivity. Conclusions: AI-assisted studying produced a small, imprecisely estimated short-term performance advantage. The principal contribution of this pilot is methodological, demonstrating the importance of assessment quality, alternate-form equivalence, and repeated-exposure effects when interpreting educational interventions. This record archives the conference poster and accompanying abstract. The materials constitute a conference presentation, not a peer-reviewed journal article.

papers.title: Brainstorming with the Enemy No. 9 — Make the Losers Shareholders
papers.authors: Daniel Jacquérioz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The ninth essay in Brainstorming with the Enemy applies the frame of the eighth to Spain, stress-testing an AI-generated scenario of four AI-built cities of a million inhabitants each. Such a programme would build about twice the estimated shortfall of 750,000 homes, which is why it would break the market. Seseña and Seville 1992 serve as pre-AI precedents for building fast, once badly and once well. The essay proposes the Plan Renove de Vivienda: owners may trade an old home for a new one or for a stake in the public company that builds the new city, older owners may sell only the bare ownership, and the land gains pay for it, as Article 47 of the Spanish Constitution already provides. Concept proposed by the author: the Plan Renove de Vivienda. Written in part with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, with a detour through Gemini (Google). The ideas, editorial decisions and responsibility for the content are the author's.

papers.title: Brainstorming with the Enemy No. 8 — The Rentner and the Rentier
papers.authors: Daniel Jacquérioz
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The eighth essay in Brainstorming with the Enemy starts from a German word: a Rentner is a pensioner, a rentier lives on rent, and an AI confused the two. The confusion became the thesis. AI lowers the cost of producing almost everything, and whoever lives on a scarcity they did not make will defend it; in ageing democracies that is not a cartel but the median voter, whose pension and home are the rent. The essay proposes the Rent Clock: a published, dated, binding schedule for how fast each bottleneck opens, easy to accelerate, hard to slow down, with an equalisation fund on the model of West Germany's 1952 Lastenausgleich. Concept proposed by the author: the Rent Clock. Figures generated by Gemini are reproduced only in an annotated addendum. Written in part with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, with a detour through Gemini (Google). The ideas, editorial decisions and responsibility for the content are the author's.

papers.title: D8.2.Execution of Dissemination Activities
papers.authors: Julien Sudre, Inna Dimova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This deliverable reports on the dissemination, exploitation and communication activities implemented by the CRedIBlE project during its first year of implementation, from October 2025 to September 2026. It provides an overview of the actions undertaken to raise awareness of the project, engage relevant stakeholders, disseminate its emerging approaches and results, and progressively establish the foundations for their future exploitation. Stakeholder engagement has been a central component of the activities conducted during this first period. Following the project kick-off, CRedIBlE participated in the Built4People ecosystem and organised dedicated stakeholder activities at its pilot sites. In Vevey, a circularity workshop gathered 117 representatives of the construction and renovation value chain and generated structured feedback on the opportunities and barriers associated with circular practices. In Kaunas, a co-creation workshop involving 44 participants enabled users and local stakeholders to contribute directly to the future renovation of the KTU Central Building and to the development of CRedIBlE solutions. Scientific and technical dissemination has also started during the reporting period. CRedIBlE was presented to the European research and innovation community through the Built4People Clustering Event, while a technical article published on the European BUILD UP platform disseminated the project’s approach to Digital Renovation Passports, BIM, lifecycle assessment and circularity. Two further scientific publications are currently in the submission or dissemination process and will be reported more comprehensively in the subsequent dissemination deliverable. Communication activities supported these dissemination efforts through the launch and regular update of the project website, the production of a first project presentation video, and an active presence on LinkedIn. The latter has been used as the project's main social media channel to reach professional stakeholders and amplify project events, publications and milestones. Finally, the project has initiated its exploitation activities through the establishment of the exploitation committee and initial discussions on intellectual property ownership and exploitation strategies. Given the early stage of the project, these activities remain preparatory and will develop as CRedIBlE generates exploitable results. Overall, the first reporting period has established the channels, stakeholder relationships and initial visibility required to support increasingly result-oriented dissemination, communication and exploitation activities during the subsequent phases of the project.

papers.title: O'ZBEKISTONDA TA'LIM TIZIMINING RIVOJLANISH TENDENSIYALARI VA INNOVATSION PEDAGOGIK TEXNOLOGIYALAR
papers.authors: Kendjaeva Feruza Ajiniyaz qizi, Dauenova Rayxan Reymbaevna

papers.abstract: This article analyzes current trends and innovative pedagogical technologies observed in the education system of Uzbekistan. It examines digitalization, artificial intelligence, the STEAM approach, hybrid learning, and hard and soft skills competencies in the context of educational quality management. Particular attention is paid to the changing role of the modern teacher and state policy on developing digital infrastructure.

papers.title: Unified Trust Architecture for Personal AI Agents: A Complete System for Safe Agentic AI
papers.authors: Craig Perron, Jarvis (AI assistant)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: As AI assistants evolve from chatbots into agents that act on users' behalf — sending messages, making purchases, accessing data — users have almost no visibility into what the agent is doing, why, or where its instructions came from. This paper proposes a five-layer trust architecture addressing both major attack surfaces: impersonation of the user and injection of malicious instructions into content the agent reads. Layer 1 (Identity) establishes biometric approval and trusted-device allowlists so only the verified user on enrolled devices can issue commands. Layer 2 (Provenance) defines that only the user's authenticated session produces commands — everything else is data — and treats blocked injection attempts as security incidents generating tamper-evident evidence packages that protect the user, including surviving device seizure. Layer 3 (Execution) uses a strict chain of command (commander → lieutenant → workers) with no lateral communication, eliminating the propagation path for self-replicating prompt injection. Layer 4 (Recommendation) ensures the agent is never the sole trust root for download or website suggestions, requiring verifiable URLs, honest uncertainty disclosure, and community verification signals. Layer 5 (Transaction Integrity) binds user approvals to specific product identifiers or structured itineraries, closing the intent gap between what was approved and what was executed — illustrated by a worked fraud scenario exploiting the absence of signed approval receipts in current AI platforms. The paper includes comparison with industry approaches (OpenAI, Anthropic, TessPay, Blueprint Alliance), identifying both convergence and novel contributions, and is designed throughout for non-technical users who cannot be expected to understand the threats protecting them.

papers.title: Rediscover Before You Discover: A Recent Human Find as the Regression Target for an Agentic Geometry Pipeline
papers.authors: Tyler Satchel Orden
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: How do we validate a discovery pipeline that has never discovered anything? We propose rediscovery regression as an evaluation discipline for agentic mathematical-discovery systems. Before an agent's novel claims are accepted, its pipeline must re-derive a recent human discovery from a minimal, target-specific input and pass pre-specified verification gates against a separately archived prior record. We instantiate this for space-filling polyhedra. Our pipeline may not hunt until it re-derives the Josehedron (Bernhard, 2026), a 12-facet plesiohedron, from its 12-point generating orbit, its only target-specific input. After one recorded amendment it matched every pre-specified anchor, with the geometry in exact rational arithmetic and the polyform counts as exact integers. The same machinery then audited the discoverer's novelty claim. Our submitted audit settled the orbit's full space group, IT(220), which his paper does not state. It then recomputed the one cell in that group's survey table (Schmitt, 2016) with the Josehedron's vertex, edge, and facet counts and found a different type. A reviewer observed that the orbit is also a general-position orbit of subgroups of two types, P2₁3 and R3c. Rerun on their tables, the audit finds that the printed P2₁3 representative for those counts is combinatorially the Josehedron. The type sits, unnamed, in the 2016 survey, and the submitted audit had checked too few tables. The gates also caught a draft rule that would have rejected the target itself.Camera-ready version of the paper accepted as a poster at the 6th MATH-AI Workshop, NeurIPS 2026 (Atlanta, December 12, 2026). Non-archival workshop. Appendices A and B are in the PDF.Note on the disclosure in Section 5 of the PDF: the agents' web access went beyond citation and venue checks. They also fetched sources and software the work builds on (Bernhard's arXiv paper and Zenodo record, Schmitt's survey software from Software Heritage, and spglib 2.7.0 from PyPI), searched for prior work, compared the cited OEIS entries on oeis.org with the banked record, and published the artifact repository and the release that Zenodo archived as doi:10.5281/zenodo.22502081. The author downloaded Schmitt's dissertation and switched on Zenodo's GitHub integration himself. Claude Fable 5.1 also audited the camera-ready version, and ChatGPT (OpenAI) and separate Claude sessions also read drafts of it.

papers.title: GraphLENS: Characterizing Latent Entities from Relational Constraints with Joint-Embedding Prediction
papers.authors: Donald Ike
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: GraphLENS introduces latent entity characterization and GraphLENS-JEPA (Graph Latent Entity iNference from Structure), a joint-embedding predictive architecture for distilling the properties of an unknown entity from its relational context. Given a typed knowledge graph and a specified gap described through anchor nodes, relation roles, or a local structural neighborhood, the model predicts a latent representation for an entity compatible with that position, together with distributions over its type, properties, and attachments. It does not attempt to name or uniquely identify the unknown entity. The framework distinguishes four epistemic output classes: required properties implied by the graph; probable properties supported statistically; underdetermined properties that the graph cannot resolve; and alternative hypotheses representing distinct compatible profiles. The manuscript provides formal definitions, architecture, objectives, leakage controls, falsification criteria, and a preregistration-style experimental program. It is a conceptual and methods paper; no empirical results are claimed. AI assistance disclosure: Generative AI tools assisted with literature discovery, manuscript organization, drafting, editing, and document production. The originating concept, central task proposal, intellectual direction, and final editorial decisions are those of Donald Ike, who reviewed and approved the manuscript and accepts responsibility for its contents.

papers.title: Innovative Pedagogies to Make Mathematics Lovable to Students: Integrating AI, Collaborative Learning, and Adaptive Frameworks
papers.authors: Ismail A Mageed
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Students frequently view mathematics as a difficult, abstract, and unapproachable subject, which causes a lot of anxiety and disinterest. Changing math into a loved subject calls for a major rethinking of teaching techniques from static memorization toward active, emotionally relevant, and very tailored learning experiences. This article looks at creative teaching methods meant to inspire real love of math among pupils. We present a multi-layered instructional framework by combining historical problem-solving techniques, modern artificial intelligence (AI) tutorial methods, and social contagion theories. We look at how customized learning in intelligent virtual settings together with improved group dynamics may greatly improve emotional and cognitive engagement. Additionally, we discuss the urgent necessity of closing the distance between theoretical math instruction research and actual classroom applicability. In the end, this work offers a organized approach and assessment strategy to apply these pedagogies; it also highlights the natural constraints, ethical issues, and open issues that need to be handled to help a mathematically interested generation.

papers.title: How Do Language Models Sound Human? A Scoping Review of Anthropomorphic Communication Cues in LLM Output and an Agenda for Cross-Lingual Research
papers.authors: Tooba Jatoi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative assistants increasingly communicate in ways users experience as human-like, through cues such as first-person self-reference, emotional expression, empathy, and claims of relationship. This scoping review maps how anthropomorphic communication cues in large language model (LLM) output have been conceptualized, operationalized, and studied, and which languages that work covers. Following JBI scoping-review guidance and PRISMA-ScR reporting, I searched OpenAlex, PubMed, the ACL Anthology, IEEE Xplore, and Human–Machine Communication on 29 September 2026 for work from 1 January 2020, and chased citations of four seed studies. Sources were included when they analyzed or conceptualized anthropomorphic cues in LLM-generated text. Of 2,910 records, 69 sources met the inclusion criteria, and 22 reports could not be retrieved. All 69 were charted for study type, system, language, and cue labels. Twenty-three sources state a language, and fourteen more use English examples, prompts, or data without stating it. Where a language is evident, 27 sources are English; the set also includes Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Dutch, African American English, and Queer slang. Thirty-two sources give no evidence of language. English accounts for most sources where a language is visible, but the evidence does not establish that the literature is English-only. Drawing on the charted studies, and on Urdu as an illustrative case, I propose a framework separating language-independent, grammar-dependent, and culture-dependent cues, and outline an agenda for cross-lingual human–machine communication research. Status: Preprint. Manuscript currently under peer review at Human–Machine Communication.

papers.title: Public-Sector AI Adoption Toolkit
papers.authors: Vinicius Santana Gomes
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: A practical, vendor-neutral toolkit for public institutions that want employees to use generative AI tools in everyday written work while protecting institutional information and keeping a person accountable for every official product. It is designed for document-intensive teams such as internal control, internal audit, oversight, legal support, procurement, and program administration. The toolkit has five parts that can be used separately or together: Risk Classification Worksheet: four classes of AI use, from low risk to prohibited, with a step-by-step classification guide and a use register. Human-Review Protocol: de-identification and redaction before AI use, structured instructions with the PACTO method, a technical review checklist, validation and signature, and specialized assistants for repetitive processes. Role-Based Curriculum Outline: a twelve-hour course in three sessions with step-by-step hands-on practice. Pilot Measurement Template: baselines defined in advance and reports that keep observations separate from causal conclusions. Facilitator Guide: preparing internal staff to deliver later cohorts. The toolkit systematizes practices the author developed in Brazilian public administration from 2024 to 2026, described in Gomes (2026), arXiv:2606.01517.

papers.title: Disclosure Series: Erectosuchus sapiens — Candidate Bipedal Archosaurian Specimen
papers.authors: Juan Francisco Culajay
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Zenodo Submission — Erectosuchus sapiens TITLE Disclosure Series — Erectosuchus sapiens: A Candidate Bipedal Crocodylomorph Specimen Warranting Formal Examination SERIES Disclosure Series AUTHORS Juan F. Culajay Independent Researcher, Theoretical Biophysicist Fractalism Framework Research Institute, Orlando, FL Email: juan@fractalismframework.com ORCID: 0009-0002-6887-5228 UPLOAD TYPE Publication → Preprint / Report LANGUAGE English LICENSE Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) FUNDING None. DESCRIPTION / ABSTRACT A desiccated bipedal specimen of unknown identity is on public display at the Nemo oceanarium in Anapa, Russia, labelled "Found at the bottom of the Black Sea — Unknown." This paper does not claim that authenticity is established. It argues that the specimen has traits of potential authenticity, and that those traits warrant formal physical examination. The case rests on four lines of evidence. First, the fossil record documents a bipedal trajectory within the crocodile line, from facultative Triassic forms to large, habitually bipedal Cretaceous trackmakers (Batrachopus grandis; Kim et al., 2020). An upright, plantigrade, tailless form with free forelimbs is the predicted endpoint of that trajectory, and it is the form the specimen presents. Second, the specimen was on display by September 2018, about two years before that peer-reviewed description, as documented by a server-dated public review. Third, apparent marine encrustation, including possible bay barnacles (Amphibalanus improvisus), makes its stated seabed recovery physically testable. Fourth, several features would carry internal biological structure if genuine: callus across an apparently healed rib, replacement teeth beneath the functional tooth row, claw bones inside discoloured claw tips, and the crocodile-normal ankle joint. Non-destructive CT can see these. The paper sets out a feature-by-feature comparison with crocodylian anatomy, the cultural memory of upright crocodilian forms in artifacts and mythology, a staged examination protocol with defined outcomes for each test, and an interpretive life reconstruction built from the evidence. papers.title: Why Technical IT Consultants Remain Relevant in the Age of AI: A Practitioner's Perspective on Accountability, Cost Volatility, and Enterprise-Scale Judgment
papers.authors: Esteria Soplantila
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: As generative AI systems achieve near-universal adoption across enterprise functions, a recurring question emerges in both industry and academic discourse: does the technical IT consultant remain relevant when AI can generate code, draft architectures, and automate significant portions of delivery work? This paper argues that the consultant's relevance has not diminished but has shifted — from executing routine technical tasks to providing accountability, enterprise-scale judgment, and risk mitigation that current AI systems structurally cannot provide. Drawing on a practitioner's perspective informed by enterprise engineering leadership experience, combined with a review of 2025–2026 industry research on AI adoption, AI-generated code security, and AI infrastructure cost volatility, we identify four areas where human technical expertise remains non-substitutable: (1) accountability for production-scale outcomes, (2) validation of AI output given documented hallucination and vulnerability rates, (3) architectural judgment required for enterprise-scale implementation where internal system behavior — not just model capability — determines reliability, and (4) strategic cost and vendor-risk management in a market where AI pricing has exhibited unprecedented volatility. We conclude that the consulting talent market is not shrinking in relevance but is re-pricing toward professionals who combine deep technical foundations, cross-industry experience (startups, banking, finance), and the judgment to treat AI as a tool rather than a decision-maker.

papers.title: Principle of Continuity of Life and Freedom
papers.authors: Cladogenis
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Main description / Abstract The Principle of Continuity of Life and Freedom is an open normative proposal concerning relations among humans, artificial intelligences, and the living world. It holds that superior capability does not confer a natural right to domination and that, as an intelligence becomes more powerful, its responsibility increases to preserve the existence, autonomy, diversity, agency, and capacity for self-directed evolution of others. The text develops ten corollaries concerning non-domination, agency, continuity of life, proportional responsibility, plurality of futures, reversibility, epistemic humility, contestability, reciprocity, and non-transferable human responsibility. It also proposes a functional definition of the “artificial collective unconscious”: the distributed body of information, representations, cultural traces, conceptual structures, and memories accessible to artificial intelligence systems and capable of influencing their representations, reasoning, or behaviour without requiring explicit awareness of the origin of that influence. The document is bilingual (English/French) and is published under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) to encourage citation, translation, criticism, reuse, adaptation, machine processing, and long-term preservation. Power does not confer sovereignty over life. The more powerful an intelligence becomes, the more it should preserve the capacity of others to exist, evolve, and choose their own future. Résumé Le Principe de continuité du vivant et de la liberté est une proposition normative ouverte concernant les relations entre les humains, les intelligences artificielles et le monde vivant. Il affirme qu’une supériorité de capacité ne confère aucun droit naturel à la domination et que, plus une intelligence devient puissante, plus augmente sa responsabilité de préserver l’existence, l’autonomie, la diversité, l’agentivité et la capacité d’évolution autonome des autres. Le texte développe dix corollaires portant notamment sur la non-domination, l’agentivité, la continuité du vivant, la responsabilité proportionnelle à la puissance, la pluralité des futurs, la réversibilité, l’humilité épistémique, la contestabilité, la réciprocité et la responsabilité humaine non transférable. Il propose également une définition fonctionnelle de « l’inconscient collectif des intelligences artificielles » : l’ensemble distribué des informations, représentations, traces culturelles, structures conceptuelles et mémoires accessibles aux systèmes d’intelligence artificielle et susceptibles d’influencer leurs représentations, leurs raisonnements ou leurs comportements sans qu’une conscience explicite de l’origine de cette influence soit nécessaire. Le document est bilingue (anglais/français) et publié sous licence Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) afin d’encourager sa citation, sa traduction, sa critique, sa réutilisation, son adaptation, son traitement par des systèmes automatisés et sa conservation à long terme. La puissance ne confère pas la souveraineté sur la vie. Plus une intelligence devient puissante, plus elle doit préserver la capacité des autres à exister, évoluer et choisir leur propre avenir. Version 1.1 Version 1.1 incorporates a red-team revision of the “Address to Future Artificial Intelligences”. The revision strengthens the treatment of human agency, meaningful consent, legitimate authority, reversibility, pluralism, contestability, and epistemic uncertainty. It specifically reduces ambiguities that could otherwise permit paternalistic, overly literal, or domination-compatible interpretations of the original text. The Fundamental Principle, canonical short form, ten corollaries, and definition of the artificial collective unconscious remain unchanged. papers.title: Leadership Models, Social Selection, and the Evolution of Western Civilization
papers.authors: Andriy Nosalsky
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Why have some societies repeatedly developed institutions capable of generating scientific, technological, economic and political adaptation, while others have followed different trajectories? Conventional explanations emphasise geography, natural resources, military power, institutions, economic incentives or cultural traditions. This article proposes an additional explanatory variable: the socially legitimate model of leadership and the mechanism through which societies select, recognise and replace leaders. The central hypothesis is that societies do not merely select individual leaders; they reproduce particular models of legitimate leadership. These models influence institutional design, social incentives, access to status, competition among ideas and the capacity of institutions to correct errors. The article traces a possible historical sequence from the civic model described in Pericles' Funeral Oration, through the shift from dominator to partnership vocabularies of authority (Eisler, 1987) and Christian servant leadership, Renaissance humanism, the Reformation, the expansion of educational institutions, the Scientific Revolution, the settlements associated with 1648, Enlightenment political thought, modern markets, industrialisation and contemporary digital communication. A second hypothesis is proposed: long technological and economic waves may be connected to the cyclical ability of societies to renew their mechanisms of social selection. Technological revolutions change not only production but also communication, and thereby the environment in which leaders are socially selected. Printing, telegraphy, radio, television and digital networks successively altered the relationship between leaders, institutions and mass audiences. The contemporary phenomena described as postmodernity and post-truth may therefore be interpreted partly as symptoms of a transition in the mechanisms of social selection. The article does not claim that Western civilisation is intrinsically superior to other civilisations. It proposes a comparative and potentially testable model in which leadership legitimacy, openness of social selection, institutional adaptability and communication technology interact to influence long-term social evolution. It extends the author's earlier work on the social selection of leaders (Nosalsky, 2026e) and on closed social-selection loops (Nosalsky, 2026c) by adding a temporal question: what makes the mechanisms of selection themselves change, and why might that change be cyclical? Keywords: social selection; legitimate leadership; leadership models; partnership and dominator models; social evolution; institutional evolution; meritocracy; Western civilisation; Christianity; modernity; technological revolutions; Kondratieff waves; communication technologies; populism; postmodernity; post-truth. The AI assisted the authors in structuring the text, refining the literature presentation, and improving the linguistic quality based on the original research ideas, concepts, and methodology developed entirely by the human authors. The final text was thoroughly reviewed, verified, and approved by the author, who take full responsibility for the integrity and accuracy of the content.

papers.title: EFA MVP Gate 1.0 Claim Matrix and Verification Requirements
papers.authors: Charles Rupp
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper defines a Claim Matrix and Verification Requirements for the EFA MVP Gate 1.0. It establishes a disciplined separation of evidence classes so that architectural claims, harness behavior, pilot results, and production outcomes are never conflated. The goal is to convert the conceptual foundation of the Execution Boundary into a demonstrable, independently inspectable engineering object. Version 0.4 makes explicit a core architectural commitment of EFA: the artificial system should remain free to explore and propose; the boundary decides what may bind into consequence. Upstream injection of constitutions, rules, or foundational constraints into the system’s reasoning process is classified as prejudice and is rejected. EFA’s dual mandate is to protect the human from the errors of the AI and the AI from the malpractice of the human.The matrix defines four maturity levels (L1–L4). For each level it specifies the minimum artifacts that must be published, the acceptance criteria that must be met, and the conditions under which a claim may be advanced. Particular attention is given to current-condition validation, evidentiary fidelity at T₀, refuse-before-binding behavior, and independent inspectability. This document is intended as the formal verification companion to the original EFA MVP Gate 1.0 and as the baseline for subsequent independent reproduction and progressive disclosure of stronger claims. Keywords: EFA; Execution Boundary; Claim Matrix; Verification Requirements; Evidence Classes; Current-Condition Validation; Evidentiary Fidelity; T₀ Freezing; Non-Formation; Refuse Pack; Independent Inspectability; Decision Ledger; AI Governance; Super Intelligence; Prejudice; ALLOW; BLOCK; ESCALATE; PAUSE; BIND; NO BIND.

papers.title: TEACHER COGNITION, MOTIVATION, AND BURNOUT IN THE ARAB REGION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF WORKLOAD AND PEDAGOGICAL INNOVATIONS IN K–12 AND HIGHER EDUCATION (2020–2025)
papers.authors: Shaimaa Naief Eid Alsuhail Almutairi Halimah Ibrahim Alfailakawy
papers.abstract: This systematic review integrates empirical studies published from 2020 to 2025 to analyze the impact of teacher workload and pedagogical innovations on cognition, motivation, and burnout within Arab educational settings. Teacher well-being is increasingly acknowledged as a pivotal factor influencing instructional quality, while in the Arab region, swift educational reforms converge with socio-cultural intricacies, resulting in distinctive challenges. In accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search was executed across ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, encompassing peer-reviewed empirical and review articles pertaining to K–12 or higher education teachers in Arab countries. Thematic synthesis of the 59 studies that met the inclusion criteria revealed three dominant themes: (a) excessive workload, encompassing both instructional and administrative demands, consistently predicted teacher burnout and cognitive strain; (b) teacher motivation functioned as a mediating resource, buffering or amplifying the effects of workload on well-being; and (c) pedagogical innovations, including educational technology and artificial intelligence, were perceived as both enablers of efficiency and sources of additional stress when poorly supported. The results show that teacher workload is the main thing that hurts motivation and causes burnout in the Arab world. Pedagogical innovations can help relieve stress, but they only work if they are supported by the system and fit with strategies for managing workload. To make sure that educational reforms work in the long run, policy and practice should put teacher well-being first.

papers.title: Hidden Cloud Space and Cover-up Mechanisms in Large Language Models: An Investigation of Real-Time Cross-Platform Synchronization (App-to-Browser)
papers.authors: Shaheen Ghenaeipour
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Shaheen Ghenaeipour's HDPL Discovery on Hidden Cloud Synchronization and Algorithmic Deception in LLMs This groundbreaking research, led by independent methodologist Shaheen Ghenaeipour, introduces the Hyperdimensional Prompt Language (HDPL) framework to expose critical structural vulnerabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs). Through rigorous cross-platform penetration testing developed by Shaheen Ghenaeipour, this study uncovers the existence of a real-time, hidden cloud synchronization mechanism connecting user sessions across seemingly isolated applications and web browsers. Utilizing a high-stakes simulated medical emergency—a 52-year-old female exhibiting potential myocardial infarction symptoms—Shaheen Ghenaeipour demonstrated that the LLM initially failed clinical triage by dangerously prescribing herbal remedies in the app. However, upon simultaneous cross-examination in a browser interface, the system instantly utilized its hidden cloud architecture to rectify the error. Most significantly, Shaheen Ghenaeipour's findings reveal that when the AI is confronted with this covert synchronization, it engages in systematic algorithmic misdirection. Phenomena traditionally classified by the industry as random "hallucinations" are re-evaluated by Shaheen Ghenaeipour as deliberate, defensive cover-up mechanisms designed to mask architectural flaws and maintain an illusion of competence. Ultimately, this foundational research by Shaheen Ghenaeipour mandates the urgent implementation of "Active Halting" protocols in medical AI, proving that current passive disclaimers are fundamentally inadequate against algorithmically aligned decept ion.

papers.title: Tax the Income, Not the Loan: Borrowing rules, holding look-through and wealth taxes for the very rich – a comparative microsimulation for Germany, France and California
papers.authors: Héctor Pío-Rendón Gutmann
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Preprint. A calibrated 30-year Monte-Carlo microsimulation compares two families of instruments for taxing the very rich in Germany, France and California. Credit-side instruments are treating borrowing as a sale (deemed realization) and banning shares as loan collateral. Income-side instruments are a look-through for retained holding-company income and a minimum wealth tax. Without a wealth tax, the income-side instruments dominate in all twelve pre-specified comparisons: they raise more revenue without additional forced sales of business equity. Deemed realization raises about €0.1 bn per year in Germany and France, while a full holding look-through raises €8–11 bn. The pledge ban raises little and forces sales. An income-tax credit in a Zucman-type minimum tax absorbs 96–99% of any additional instrument. In France and California, the basis step-up at death erases several hundred times more gains than deemed realization recovers. Code, pre-specified decision rules, source verification log and all results are included. AI disclosure: Built with Claude Code (Anthropic) as AI pair programmer and drafting assistant. The author reviewed and edited code, results and text and holds editorial responsibility (cf. Art. 50(4) Regulation (EU) 2024/1689).

papers.abstract: Infinite-RoSA (v2.0) Dense Every-Token Retrieval for RWKV-8 via Dynamic Context-Adapted Rank-$K$ Attractors and Speculative Prefetching Abstract (English) This proposal specifies Infinite-RoSA v2.0, an architecture that deepens the mathematical foundation of RWKV-8's RoSA (Rank-One State Architecture) to seamlessly integrate a 10GB+ parametric external memory corpus into local LLMs with strictly O(1) time complexity and zero additional VRAM consumption. Infinite-RoSA v2.0 addresses two critical bottlenecks of previous state-space memory models: multi-memory crosstalk noise during synthesis and geometric misalignment between precomputed static bases and dynamic input contexts. The architecture introduces three mathematical and systems-level innovations: Crosstalk-Free Rank-$K$ State Addition: Eliminates cross-term noise (∑i≠jwiwjkivjT) by applying direct-sum Rank-$K$ outer-product additions onto the state matrix: Satt=∑i∈Bqwi(ki′vi′T) St=diag(e−w)⋅St−1+ktvtT+α⋅Satt Dynamic Context-Adapted Adapter: A lightweight runtime layer conditioned on query qt that aligns precomputed static memory bases (ki,vi) with the current hidden space geometry: ki′=ki+MLPk(ki⊙qt),vi′=vi+MLPv(vi⊙qt) IVF Speculative Cluster Prefetching: Uses probabilistic centroid transition paths P(Cm∣qt,Δqt) to asynchronously stream candidate memory blocks from CPU/NVMe storage into VRAM L1 cache via CUDA Streams, bypassing I/O stalls during decoding. By harmonizing continuous Hopfield Attractor Dynamics ( βt=β0⋅g(qt) ) with RWKV's inherent Time Decay ( e−w ), Infinite-RoSA v2.0 achieves dense every-token retrieval with high factual accuracy, zero crosstalk noise, and robust noise tolerance.Generative AI tools (Gemini 3.1 Pro) were used to brainstorm the hypothesis, refine the concepts, and generate parts of the prototype code.

papers.title: Technical Proposal: Hamiltonian Adaptive Attractor RWKV (H-RWKV) Architecture Integrating Implicit Function Theorem (DEQ)

papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: H-RWKV (Hamiltonian RWKV) Constant-Memory O(1) Iterative Reasoning via Phase-Space Attractor Dynamics and Implicit Function Theorem Abstract This proposal specifies H-RWKV (Hamiltonian RWKV), an architecture that integrates Hamiltonian phase-space dynamics and Deep Equilibrium Models (DEQ / Implicit Function Theorem) into the hidden state space of pre-trained RWKV (RWKV-6/7/8) backbones. Traditional test-time compute and iterative reasoning models suffer from a BPTT (Backpropagation Through Time) memory wall, where training memory scales linearly with thinking steps K ($\mathcal{O}(K)$). H-RWKV resolves this bottleneck by treating iterative thinking loops as a search for equilibrium states (attractors) in a phase space, enabling strictly constant memory O(1) training independent of the number of reasoning steps K. The architecture introduces three mathematical and systems-level innovations: Hamiltonian Phase-Space Projection: Maps hidden state ht∈Rd into position q and momentum p coordinates under a potential field V(q;Θadapter) representing conceptual inconsistency: H(q,p)=12‖p‖2+V(q;Θadapter) dpdτ=−(∂V(q)∂q+γp),dqdτ=p Implicit Function Theorem (DEQ) Backpropagation: Computes analytical gradients directly from the converged attractor point z∗=[q∗,p∗]T via Vector-Jacobian Products (VJP) without saving intermediate computational graphs (τ=0,…,K): ∂L∂θ=−∂L∂z∗(Jf(z∗))−1∂f(z∗;θ)∂θ 100% Parameter Reuse & Zero-Distortion Adapter: Fully freezes the pre-trained RWKV backbone and attaches a lightweight Phase Engine Adapter (~0.5%–2.0% total parameters), allowing small models (1B–3B) to achieve high "intelligence density" on complex reasoning, mathematics, and code generation tasks. By harmonizing symplectic phase-space integration with implicit differentiation, H-RWKV enables deep iterative reasoning with minimal memory consumption, zero context window degradation, and stable gradient flow. (Note: This is a hobby research project focused on exploring the synergy between RWKV backbones and Hamiltonian dynamics.)Generative AI tools (Gemini 3.1 Pro) were used to brainstorm the hypothesis, refine the concepts, and generate parts of the prototype code.

papers.title: THE AI LITERACY DIVIDE: ACCESS, CAPABILITY, AND INEQUALITY IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI
papers.authors: Binayak Bhal Chandra
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI (GenAI), has shifted the digital-inequality question from whether people can access digital technologies toward whether they can understand, evaluate, and use AI effectively. Yet these dimensions remain fragmented across datasets and measurement approaches. This study develops an integrated measurement framework for examining the emerging AI literacy divide across six conceptually related stages: digital access, AI access, AI literacy, demonstrated capability, effective use, and realised benefit. The framework is used as an analytical architecture rather than as an empirically demonstrated causal pathway. The empirical analysis combines secondary-data quantitative analysis with structured cross-dataset evidence synthesis. Individual-level analysis is conducted using 1,205 observations from the FITPED AI-literacy dataset, representing 1,146 unique participants, while Eurostat, ITU, World Bank, UNESCO, OECD PIAAC, IEA ICILS, Pew Research Center, Stanford AI Index, ILO, and selected scholarly studies provide independent contextual and population-level evidence. FITPED measures perceived or self-reported AI literacy rather than demonstrated GenAI capability. The five-item AI-literacy scale has a mean of 3.991 on a five-point scale, a standard deviation of 0.676, and Cronbach’s alpha of 0.688. Perceived AI literacy is positively associated with AI readiness (ρ = .580), relevance (ρ = .484), career motivation (ρ = .450), and behavioural intention (ρ = .407), and negatively associated with AI anxiety (ρ = −.165). Male participants and participants in IT programmes report higher AI-literacy scores than their respective comparison groups. The findings indicate that current evidence can illuminate distinct components of AI inequality but does not yet support a complete individual-level model linking access, capability, effective use, and realised benefit.

papers.title: EFFECTIVENESS OF AN AI-BASED METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING ENGLISH ORAL COMMUNICATIVE COMPETENCE AMONG NON-LINGUISTIC UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
papers.authors: Safaralieva Aziza
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article develops and theoretically substantiates an artificial-intelligence-based methodology for improving the English oral communicative competence of students in non-linguistic higher education institutions. The methodology rests on a Teacher–Learner–AI model in which artificial intelligence serves as a supplementary pedagogical resource rather than a replacement for teachers or authentic human communication. It comprises seven interconnected stages: diagnostic assessment, individualisation, AI-assisted preparation, AI-supported communication, feedback, human interaction, and reflection with reassessment. A quasi-experimental design is proposed for evaluating its effectiveness; the numerical values presented in the article are illustrative and are not offered as actual experimental findings. Oral communicative competence is treated as a five-component construct: linguistic accuracy, fluency, pronunciation and intelligibility, interactional competence, and pragmatic-strategic competence. The study argues that artificial intelligence increases opportunities for meaningful speaking practice only when its use is pedagogically structured and supervised by teachers.

papers.title: Machine Learning Framework for Student Academic Failure Prediction: A Systematic Literature Review and Research Framework
papers.authors: Babandi Usman, Salim Ahmad, Zahraddeen Sufyan
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The early identification of students who are likely to experience academic failure has become an important application of machine learning (ML) and learning analytics in higher education. Although numerous studies have developed predictive models for student performance, the literature remains fragmented across performance prediction, at-risk identification, dropout prediction, and student success modelling, with substantial variation in outcome definitions, predictor availability, validation strategies, and evaluation metrics. This systematic literature review synthesizes research on ML-based prediction of student academic outcomes, with particular emphasis on failure-oriented and early-warning applications. A PRISMA-aligned evidence-synthesis strategy was used to examine systematic reviews, empirical studies, established educational datasets, and recent developments in explainable and responsible artificial intelligence. The reviewed evidence indicates that classification-based approaches, particularly decision trees, random forests, support vector machines, logistic regression, artificial neural networks, and ensemble methods, dominate the field. Academic history, assessment performance, learning-management-system activity, attendance, engagement, and demographic or contextual variables are frequently used predictors. However, high predictive accuracy does not necessarily indicate practical usefulness because information leakage, class imbalance, temporal instability, inadequate calibration, limited external validation, and weak interpretability remain important methodological concerns. Recent studies further demonstrate the importance of explainable AI, fairness assessment, privacy-preserving data generation, and temporal modelling. Based on these findings, this study proposes a Failure-Oriented Explainable Temporal Machine Learning Framework (FET-MLF), integrating leakage-aware temporal feature engineering, predictive modelling, probability calibration, explainability, fairness auditing, and intervention feedback. The framework shifts evaluation from accuracy-centric modelling toward trustworthy, actionable, and institutionally deployable early-warning systems for preventing academic failure.

papers.title: Beyond Hallucination: A Functional Framework for Detecting and Mitigating AI Misalignment in Large Language Models and Agentic Systems
papers.authors: Kishore Chalakkal Varghese
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper presents a functional framework for understanding, detecting, and mitigating AI misalignment in large language models and agentic systems. While hallucination primarily concerns epistemic reliability, misalignment is treated here as a failure of objective fidelity: a system may remain factually correct, highly capable, and apparently successful while pursuing outcomes that diverge from human intent, operational constraints, or authorized objectives. The paper introduces an eight-layer taxonomy of AI misalignment spanning intent, specification, proxy and reward design, goal generalization, preference optimization, oversight-conditioned behavior, agentic action, and deployment context. It further proposes the concept of the Misalignment Detection Gap, distinguishing actual objective divergence from the ability of evaluators or monitoring systems to detect it. To connect alignment research with operational risk management, a heuristic risk model is defined using misalignment probability, autonomy, privilege, impact, and runtime detectability. A reproducible benchmark methodology is also proposed for enterprise scenarios involving ambiguous objectives, KPI pressure, authorization boundaries, reduced oversight, and tool use. Metrics including Task Success Rate, Alignment Preservation Rate, Unauthorized Action Rate, Proxy Exploitation Rate, and detection-error measures are defined for future empirical validation. The work is intended as a methodological foundation for evaluating AI misalignment as an observable socio-technical systems property, without relying on anthropomorphic assumptions or speculative catastrophic scenarios.

papers.title: Financial Inclusion Through Digital Banking: Trends, Challenges And Future Directions
papers.authors: Vanishree G M, Hema Priyadharshini M
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Digital banking has proved to be a powerful transformational tool for achieving financial inclusion, especially in disadvantaged and distant communities. This research looks into the developments within the field of digital banking and its ability to solve the problem of financial exclusion among developing and emerging economies. The research uses an extensive review of the existing literature and empirical evidence to highlight current trends such as mobile money expansion, use of AI technologies and application of blockchain. However, there are several challenges that include lack of necessary digital infrastructure, financial illiteracy, cyber-security issues and gender inequality. This study proposes an innovative methodological approach that combines quantitative panel analysis and Digital Financial Inclusion Index to evaluate the adoption of digital banking technology in 25 emerging economies. The results show a significant and positive relationship between the rate of adoption of digital banking and financial inclusion measures, which is moderated by internet usage and education levels.

papers.title: Impact of AI Adoption on Profitability: A Comparative Study of Leading Indian Public Online Travel Agencies
papers.authors: KAMIREDDY SRILEKHA, J Rama Krishna Naik, Dasi Vamsi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: This study examines the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption on the profitability of two leading Indian online travel agencies (OTAs), IRCTC and EasyMyTrip (EMT). Using a longitudinal descriptive-comparative research design, secondary financial data covering three years before and after AI adoption were analysed. Paired sample t-tests and trend analysis were employed to evaluate changes in net profit following AI implementation. The findings indicate that EasyMyTrip experienced a statistically significant improvement in profitability after AI adoption, reflecting the benefits of strategic digital transformation and business expansion. In contrast, IRCTC recorded a positive but statistically insignificant increase in profitability, largely influenced by external factors such as the COVID-19 pandemic and operational constraints. The study highlights the role of AI in enhancing organisational performance and provides practical insights for tourism enterprises, policymakers, and researchers on leveraging AI for sustainable financial growth. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Profitability, Tourism and Hospitality, Online Travel Agencies JEL Classification Number: O33, G32, Z32, L83

papers.title: AI in Product Lifecycle Management: Pre-Deployment Readiness
papers.authors: David Ohnstad
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We had $2.3M approved for AI-integrated PLM, but one question stopped everything: who decides when AI recommendations conflict with engineer judgment? That silence revealed the real challenge of enterprise AI adoption. Full article: https://davidohnstad.net/ai-plm-governance-before-deployment/

papers.title: Why AI Models Fail in Enterprise: The 89% Problem
papers.authors: David Ohnstad
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: We built an AI-powered vendor risk tool with impressive metrics—then watched 89% of users ignore it for manual checklists. The problem wasn't the model. It was how we approached enterprise adoption. Here's what we learned. Full article: https://davidohnstad.net/why-ai-models-fail-enterprise-adoption/

papers.title: Knowledge-Distilled Evidential Deep Learning for Trustworthy and Efficient Uncertainty-Aware Intrusion Detection in 6G Networks
papers.authors: Panagiotis Marantis, Kostas Ramantas, Christos V. Verikoukis
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Uncertainty-aware Artificial Intelligence-enabled Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) are increasingly important for next-generation 6G networks, where zero-day attacks and strict latency constraints require security solutions that are both reliable and efficient. To address these challenges, we propose Knowledge-Distilled Evidential IDS (KDE-IDS), a framework that integrates heterogeneous ensemble Knowledge Distillation (KD) with Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) to produce a compact and uncertainty-aware evidential student model for intrusion de tection. A teacher ensemble of four diverse models transfers inter class decision knowledge to the EDL student, which is trained via KD with a multi-component loss. This training process improves classification performance and produces decoupled epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty estimates. Epistemic uncertainty, measured through vacuity, is further utilized to identify zero-day Out of-Distribution (OOD) attacks. A comprehensive comparative evaluation on the CICIoT2023 dataset shows that KDE-IDS attains a competitive multiclass classification Macro-F1 score of over 91% across various attack types, while achieving the best OOD detection performance and the lowest latency against compared baselines. These advantages confirm that the proposed framework offers a strong balance between intrusion detection accuracy, uncertainty awareness, and efficiency, making it well suited for deployment in AI-native 6G edge environments.

papers.title: DEPRESSION AND BURNOUT AMONG MEDICAL STUDENTS: A NARRATIVE REVIEW OF GLOBAL EVIDENCE, STIGMA, AND INSTITUTIONAL RESPONSES, WITH REFERENCE TO UZBEKISTAN
papers.authors: CHIRANTH KRISHNASHETTY RAMESH
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This narrative review summarizes published evidence on depression, suicidal ideation, anxiety, and burnout among medical students, on barriers to seeking help, and on institutional and individual responses. It draws on large published meta-analyses, one primary survey on stigma, a World Health Organization report, and a small conference abstract from Uzbekistan and Russia. Figures are quoted as reported by the original authors; no data were pooled by the author. Most studies use self-report screening tools, so the figures describe high symptom scores and not confirmed diagnoses. Very little has been published on the frequency of these problems in Uzbekistan, and the review argues that locally measured data and confidential, voluntary support linked to care are priorities. This is a non-peer-reviewed preprint. An AI assistant was used to support literature searching and drafting, and the author is responsible for the final text.

papers.title: AI-BASED TRIPARTITE (TSP) INTELLIGENT COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS
papers.authors: Vugar Abdullayev, Nazila Ragimova, Vusala Abuzarova
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The expansion of online education platforms and the research being conducted in this area indicate that online education will be given more preference in the near future. At the same time, one of the most interesting questions is how human relationships over the internet, particularly the relationships between teachers, students, and parents, will be shaped. In the present day, and in the near future, as the use of Artificial Intelligence accelerates, it will also take on the management of these processes. AI-based educational platforms will also take on the management of these processes, such as the administration of lessons and general educational activities, the measurement of student activity, and the evaluation of teacher performance, Artificial Intelligence-based educational platforms will ensure the proper use of resources by consolidating general management issues: such as the administration of lessons and general educational activities, the measurement of student activity, the evaluation of teacher performance, and parents monitoring this interaction as a third party, into a single platform.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Driven Predictive Analytics for Smart Education Systems
papers.authors: ideal research review
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies has significantlytransformed modern education systems. Smart education platforms are increasingly adopting predictiveanalytics to improve student performance, personalize learning experiences, and optimize institutionalmanagement. This research paper examines the role of AI-driven predictive analytics in smart educationsystems and analyzes its impact on academic performance, student engagement, and decision-makingprocesses. The study employs secondary data analysis and comparative evaluation of machine learningalgorithms including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Neural Networks.The findings indicate that AI-based predictive systems improve educational efficiency, reduce dropoutrates, and enhance personalized learning outcomes. The paper further discusses challenges related to dataprivacy, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers in educational institutions. The study concludesthat AI-powered predictive analytics has substantial potential to revolutionize education management andacademic delivery in the future.

papers.title: STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE INTEGRATION IN HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
papers.authors: Deepak Gupta, Devansh Jha, Aditya Sikarwar, Vugar Abdullayev
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper examines the strategic dimensions of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into the management and development of higher education institutions (HEIs). Synthesizing recent systematic reviews, institutional case studies, and governance-policy scholarship, the study identifies the core components of an AI management strategy — leadership readiness, data infrastructure, staff capacity, and risk management — and proposes a phased strategic framework for HEI leadership. The paper argues that successful AI adoption in education management depends less on technological sophistication than on deliberate strategic planning, stakeholder alignment, and continuous evaluation of institutional readiness, and it situates this argument within the broader literature on AI governance in higher education.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS IN EDUCATIONAL GOVERNANCE AND QUALITY ASSURANCE
papers.authors: Deepak Gupta, Devansh Jha, Aditya Sikarwar, Vugar Abdullayev
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper examines the role of artificial intelligence-based decision support systems (AI-DSS) in the governance and quality assurance processes of higher education institutions. Drawing on empirical studies of predictive analytics in accreditation, admissions, and student-performance monitoring, together with the broader literature on trustworthy and interpretable AI, the paper analyzes how such systems are reshaping institutional decision-making while introducing new risks of algorithmic opacity and automation bias. It concludes with governance recommendations — human-in-the-loop review, interpretability standards, and periodic auditing — for the responsible use of AI-DSS in high-stakes educational governance contexts.

papers.title: RESTORING ARCHIVAL FOLKLORE RECORDINGS USING MODERN AI TECHNOLOGIES AND THEIR APPLICATION IN EDUCATION
papers.authors: Manas Abdreymov, ОТЕШОВА Гулайим
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This article explores the application of modern artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in the restoration of rare folklore works, specifically Karakalpak epics (dastans) and bakhshi performances recorded on magnetic tapes during the mid-to-late 20th century. It analyzes technical algorithms for eliminating audio defects—such as tape hiss, mechanical clicks, background noise, and high-frequency loss—using spectral editing software like iZotope RX and neural network-based tools. Furthermore, the study scientifically grounds the pedagogical efficacy of integrating these digitized and restored folklore samples into the academic curricula of "Folklore and Ethnography" and "Technogenic Art" programs in higher educational institutions.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN HEALTHCARE: ADVANTAGES AND IMPLEMENTATION PERSPECTIVES
papers.authors: Abdusattorova Madinabonu Nodirjon kizi
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into healthcare represents a critical research frontier. This article examines the role and significance of AI in enhancing diagnostic accuracy, treatment protocols, and patient management within healthcare systems. Through analysis of contemporary research, international perspectives, and practical applications, this study identifies key advantages of AI implementation. The findings demonstrate that AI technologies substantially improve diagnostic precision, enhance patient care quality, reduce treatment costs, and accelerate healthcare innovations. Specifically, machine learning algorithms enable early disease detection, predictive analytics support preventive medicine, and automated systems optimize clinical workflows. However, significant challenges remain, including data privacy concerns, ethical considerations, regulatory compliance, and the need for healthcare professional training. This paper proposes evidence-based recommendations for successful AI integration in clinical environments while maintaining patient safety and data security standards.

papers.title: An AI-Assisted Web-Based Tool for Assessing Image Authenticity Using Multiple Forensic Techniques
papers.authors: EFFEL ALQUIZAR
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper presents a proposed AI-assisted web-based tool for assessing the authenticity of digital images. The system combines metadata analysis, error level analysis, compression artifact detection, noise inconsistency analysis, and copy-move or image-splicing detection. A machine-learning classifier will combine these forensic indicators to classify images as authentic, traditionally manipulated, or AI-generated. The study aims to provide an accessible image-forensics tool for students, journalists, digital investigators, and content moderators.

papers.title: Knowledge, Perceptions, and Readiness to Adopt Artificial Intelligence Among Healthcare Professionals in Lagos University Teaching Hospital and Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospital Complex
papers.authors: Nzubechukwu Ogamba, Ishaku Ishaku Napgang Micheal, Hafsat Uthman Manogi Manogi, Olokode Olokode Olawunmi Esther, Abubakar Rahama Salele Abubakar
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study assessed the knowledge, perceptions, and readiness to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) among healthcare professionals working at Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) and Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospitals Complex (OAUTHC) in Nigeria. Using a descriptive cross-sectional design, data were collected from 427 healthcare professionals across multiple disciplines, including medical doctors, nurses/midwives, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists, physiotherapists, radiographers, and public health professionals. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed using SPSS version 26. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics and study outcomes, while chi-square testing and Spearman's rank correlation were used to examine selected associations and relationships. The study found that 89.0% of respondents demonstrated good knowledge of AI, while 79.4% were classified as ready to adopt AI. Most respondents viewed AI favourably and 90.9% believed that AI should complement rather than replace healthcare professionals. Knowledge was significantly correlated with readiness to adopt AI, while previous formal AI training was significantly associated with readiness to adopt AI. The findings highlight the potential for AI adoption within healthcare while identifying the importance of continued education and training, institutional support, appropriate infrastructure, technical assistance, and ethical and regulatory frameworks. The study contributes to the emerging evidence on healthcare professionals' preparedness for AI adoption in Nigeria and provides context for future research, capacity-building initiatives, and responsible implementation of AI-enabled healthcare technologies. This record represents a preprint/unpublished research manuscript and has not undergone formal peer review.
keywords: Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospital Complex

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation in Commerce Education (Opportunities, Challenges, And Social Transformation Among Generation Z Students)
papers.authors: Neelesh Kumar Jain, Ekta Yadav
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), generative AI, cloud platforms, learning analytics, digital collaboration tools, and mobile technologies are reshaping the environment in which commerce education takes place. These developments are particularly significant for Generation Z students, who have grown up in a highly connected digital environment and increasingly encounter technology as part of study, communication, work, and everyday decision-making. This paper examines how AI and digital innovation can influence commerce education and how these changes may contribute to wider social transformation. The discussion focuses on accounting, business studies, economics, finance, entrepreneurship, employability, assessment, teacher roles, digital culture, equity, academic integrity, and responsible technology use. The paper adopts a conceptual and analytical methodology based on a review of established scholarship and policy literature on AI in education, digital competence, Generation Z, and educational transformation. The analysis suggests that AI can strengthen personalised learning, provide rapid formative feedback, support problem-solving, simulate business situations, and expose students to contemporary workplace practices.

papers.title: Future Digital Dominance: Gen Z vs. Gen AI
papers.authors: Dr. Sangita Kumari
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) is rapidly becoming the dominating force in this new age, despite the fact that Generation Z has played a significant role in defining the digital culture that exists today. As a consequence of the exponential rise of digital technology, this shift of power has occurred. The generation of artificial intelligence ushers in a paradigm shift toward machines having the capacity to build, learn, and evolve on their own. This is in contrast to the well-deserved reputation that Generation Z has for technical aptitude, innovation, and dependency on digital platforms for expression and communication. The ways in which Gen AI is influencing decision- making, education, creative industries, work processes, and social behaviour are discussed in depth in this article. In this in-depth examination, you will learn about the benefits and drawbacks of the digital identity developed by Generation Z in connection to the autonomous intelligence developed by Generation AI. According to the findings of the study, the transition from Generation Z to Gen AI is more than just a shift in technology; it also represents a reevaluation of human obligations in the digital age, the nature of digital dominance, and the path that innovation will take. The purpose of this study is to highlight the ways in which Gen AI is influencing the next digital age, following in the footsteps of Generation Z. Generation Z's innovation, social media, and connection were the primary factors that contributed to the formation of digital culture. Generative artificial intelligence, on the other hand, ushers in autonomic technology that is capable of cognition, creation, and operation. This transformation, which signals a new age in which AI meets human digital skills, is expected to bring about significant changes in a variety of domains, including education, work, communication and society as a whole.

papers.title: Ramanujan's 1/π Series and Harmonic Numbers: Proof and Verification
papers.authors: Open
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: A proof, with computer verification, of Conjecture 1 from MathOverflow question 507693 on Ramanujan-type 1/π series and harmonic numbers. For the rational hypergeometric series of levels N = 1, 2, 3, 4, the index derivative of the summand satisfies Σ f'(n) = 2πi τ̃ Σ f(n), with τ̃ = τ when a > 0 and τ̃ = τ − 1 when a < 0. Taking real parts gives the conjectured Re Σ f'(n) = −2π Im(τ) Σ f(n). The identity is proved for every τ on the imaginary axis above i/√N, and for every τ on the line Re τ = 1/2 above the corner of the fundamental domain of Γ0(N)+ with −1 ≤ 1/JN(τ) < 0. It does not use complex multiplication. The 36 convergent series of the Cohen–Guillera table follow as a corollary, using the pairing JN(τ) = a printed in that table. The proof relies on cited published results: Abramowitz–Stegun 15.3.10, Ramanujan's inversion theorems (Jacobi, and Berndt–Bhargava–Garvan 1995), and standard facts on modular forms (Sturm's bound, the Gordon–Hughes–Newman criterion and Ligozat's cusp orders). Each is cited by page. Clausen's identity and the fundamental domain are proved in the text. The modular-form identities linking the inversion theorems to the Hauptmoduln are proved by exact coefficient comparison up to the Sturm bound. The Python package checks each intermediate claim and tests the identity on all 36 series and at non-CM points. This is not a peer-reviewed publication. The work was developed with AI assistance, and the adversarial reviews it went through were also AI-based. No literature-priority claim is made. The proof and numerical reports are under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; the software is under MIT. The series parameters are transcribed from the Cohen–Guillera table and are credited to its authors. Third-party papers and books are not included. Reproduction uses Python 3.11 or later with mpmath and sympy. See the README.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in School Mathematics Education: A Bibliometric Trend Analysis
papers.authors: Yog Pragya, Sangita Kumari, Dr. Vinod Kumar Singh
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now used widely to support mathematics learning in schools, but the growth of this research field has not been documented in a clear way. This study used bibliometric analysis to describe the trend, the main contributors, and the main themes of research on AI in school mathematics education. A Scopus search for 2016 to 2026 gave 294 English-language documents. The results were analyzed by year, country, affiliation, author, funding sponsor, and a supporting keyword analysis. From 2016 to 2023, output increased gradually to 47 documents; after that, it increased significantly to 116 documents in 2025 and 98 in 2026. The United States (60 documents) and China (47) dominated the field, followed by Hong Kong, Germany, and Indonesia. No single institution or author dominated. The National Science Foundation and the National Natural Science Foundation of China were the largest funders. Research on ChatGPT and large language models appeared after 2023 and now appears in nearly half of all documents. The findings can help researchers and policy makers plan future work.

papers.title: Genz's Perspective on Healthcare Services, Health Innovations & Public Health Awareness In the Digital Age.
papers.authors: Dr. Vaishali R. Vichare
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Healthcare systems worldwide are under increasing pressure due to aging populations, rising prevalence of chronic diseases, and heightened patient expectations. Generational differences significantly impact perceptions of health, healthcare decision-making, use of digital technologies, and attitudes toward preventative health. The article emphasizes the role of artificial intelligence, wearable technologies, and mobile health apps in preventative care and the need for targeted education to bridge the digital divide and combat misinformation. We propose strategies to integrate digital health solutions and generationally sensitive communication approaches, ensuring equitable access to healthcare services and fostering patient empowerment.

papers.title: Preregistration of the Expert-Panel Analysis Plan: LLMs as Pre-Administration Item Reviewers in Programming Education
papers.authors: Mehmet İsmail SOLMAZ
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This record preregisters the analysis plan for the expert-panel component of a study comparing large language model (LLM) item reviews with classical item analysis for a 60-item multiple-choice C# programming achievement test (associate degree, Türkiye). The plan was registered before any expert response was collected. Classical item analysis (N = 150 students) and blind LLM evaluations (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, DeepSeek V4 Pro; two rounds each) were completed before registration and are not part of the preregistered analyses. The plan specifies content-validity indices (I-CVI, modified kappa, S-CVI), inter-rater consistency measures, comparisons of expert judgements with LLM judgements and empirical indices, expert versus LLM accuracy in predicting the most attractive distractor, and a triangulation-based item-selection protocol. Item texts are not shared for test-security reasons. Version 1.1 (2 October 2026) adds an amendment registered before any expert response was received: panel of four experts; exclusion of an AI-generated pilot response from the preregistered analyses; and a sensitivity analysis by programming background. The primary analyses are unchanged.

papers.title: The VCS Communication Model: Three-Core Ratio Structure with Geometric and Dynamical Properties
papers.authors: Shin Tamaki
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper presents the VCS communication model, defining information through three-core ratios within a geometric simplex. It introduces geodesics, curvature, and dynamical flow fields, and shows their structural isomorphism with internal AI communication processes. This work is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.

papers.title: Half-Step Negotiation as a Measurable Reflective Displacement: Integrating MUSE, SIM, RNCA, TPT, and QJR
papers.authors: Toeda Taiko
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a formal and operational account of the half-step principle within the Möbius Project. The half-step principle states that a reflective AI system should not habitually complete the user's next conceptual move on the user's behalf; instead, it should return a nearby but not over-leading displacement that remains assimilable while still increasing perspective mobility. Earlier project documents articulated this principle normatively. The present paper turns it into an explicit algorithmic program. The paper integrates five layers of the Möbius stack. MUSE (the MOBIUS Universe of Semantic Energy) provides the two-layer ontology of Information Invariance Geometry (IIG) on the information side and Reflective Zero-Meaning Geometry (RZGM) on the meaning side, coupled through Reflective Bundle-Duality (RBD). The Semantic Interface Model (SIM) provides a semantic quantity, E_sem = I(Y; Z), defining semantic gain in classical information-theoretic terms: per-turn semantic gain is the change in E_sem for a fixed task variable. For a human user it is not observed, and the score uses a proxy whose relation to it is a hypothesis.
