papers.title: A systematic review of skill-centric career guidance systems: Integrating knowledge graphs, skill decay tracking, and country-based salary sequence intelligence
papers.authors: S. H. Puwakgolla, Wijendra Gunathilake, D. M. T. R. Disanayaka
papers.abstract: With the rise of online learning sites, professional networking platforms, and hiring services, the demand for effective systems to support skill development and career advice is increasing. Skills are stored on different resources like e-learning platforms, code repositories and professional profiles. In recent years, personalization has been an active research field, and a personalized learning recommendation system, which recommends resources according to users' choices, has been developed. However, they have difficulty accommodating shifts in the labour market and are prone to creating negative employment mismatches and limited alternative career opportunities. The paper provides a comprehensive review of the research conducted across skill extraction, large language model (LLM)-based career guidance, knowledge graph construction, learning path recommendation, prerequisite modelling, and knowledge tracing, fairness and algorithmic bias in career AI, and country-based salary integration to improve adaptive career guidance. Almost 45 peer-reviewed articles from 2018 - 2026 were collated from key digital libraries. The review highlights progress in areas such as skill inference, learning path recommendations using graphs, knowledge tracing that considers forgetting, career matching, recommendations that explain themselves, and understanding salary trends at a country level, which is important for career planning systems. However, these solutions are not integrated and do not create a system for learning altogether. They don't consider the monetary aspects of paying for a career either. The review also proposes a series of skills and financial outcomes to help learners identify if they have the financial resources and location to pursue a career. It highlights the need for a platform to enable multi-platform skill extraction, tracking of skill decay, dynamic career paths, explainable AI skill recommendations, prerequisite modelling, and geographic salary return sequences.

papers.title: The effectiveness of integrating ChatGPT into Business English pedagogy to enhance tertiary students’ writing skills
papers.authors: Muditha Manathunga
papers.abstract: The study addresses the growing challenge of enhancing tertiary students’ Business English writing proficiency in Sri Lanka, where conventional teaching methods often fail to provide sufficient individualized feedback and engagement opportunities. With the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT, new opportunities have emerged for personalised, interactive, and feedback-driven writing instruction. Thus, this study investigates the effectiveness of integrating ChatGPT into Business English pedagogy to enhance tertiary students’ writing skills, focusing on the Faculty of Commerce and Management Studies at the University of Kelaniya, Sri Lanka. A mixed-methods design was adopted combining quantitative data from 150 management undergraduates using structured questionnaires, with qualitative data from 10 purposively selected interviewees. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS, and qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. The results indicated strong positive correlation between ChatGPT use and key aspects of Business English writing improvement; personalised feedback (r = 0.915), writing style adaptation (r = 0.887), and writing engagement (r = 0.821), all significant at p < 0.01. Regression analysis further showed that the three ChatGPT-related constructs significantly predicted students’ reported Business English Writing Skills (R² = 0.858, F = 294.336, p < 0.001), with Personalised Feedback (β = 0.713), Writing Style Adaptation (β = 0.478), and Writing Engagement (β = 0.467) making significant positive contributions. Thematic findings supported these results, highlighting enhanced grammar accuracy, vocabulary, coherence, and motivation, alongside reduced writing anxiety. However, challenges such as over-dependence, limited critical evaluation, and risks of academic misconduct were identified. The study recommends that when responsibly integrated, ChatGPT holds substantial potential to enhance Business English writing proficiency and learner engagement in Sri Lankan higher education.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for climate-smart agriculture: Bridging science, policy, and practice - A narrative review
papers.authors: Anuga Liyanage
papers.abstract: Climate change poses a serious challenge to global food security, where agriculture will need to be highly productive, adaptive to climate change, and also less emission of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) plays a central role in addressing these challenges, but its popularity, especially with smallholder farmers in low- and middle-income nations is hampered by the lack of data, decision support, and adaptability. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a revolutionary technology that can be used to bridge scientific knowledge, policy formulation, and real-world farming practices to boost CSA realization. This narrative review was based on the peer-reviewed and grey literature published in last two decades with the aim of assessing the AI application in the main fields of CSA, such as crop yield prediction, precision irrigation, pest and disease surveillance, soil carbon monitoring, as well as digital advisory services. It synthesized data from 177 sources from various research databases (Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar) identified technological trends, policy frameworks, and an adoption barrier model. Additionally, it outlined a future research roadmap and provides specific policy and practice recommendations. The review concluded that despite significant potential in all the studied CSA domains, with 15-30% improvements in yield prediction accuracy and 20-40% reductions in water consumption in controlled environments (single-study estimates reported without confidence intervals; see Limitations), the adoption of AI applications by smallholder farmers are crippled by the fragility of data ecosystems, infrastructure gaps, limited institutional capacity, and systematic inequities in the global AI innovation ecosystem. The review found that to achieve the transformative potential of AI in CSA, there is an urgent need to re-orient the research investment, governance structures and institutional structures to the complex, data-poor realities of tropical smallholder farming systems.

papers.title: Developing a Socratic Artificial Intelligence Tutor Using Retrieval Augmented Generation and Pedagogical Prompting
papers.authors: Blessing Chimezie Uzo, Micah Okpara, Ebere Nwanneka Chukwuemeka, Ponsak Stephen Bande, Fortune Nkem Okpara
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) applications such as ChatGPT present a distinct challenge for computer science (CS) students. While they offer individualized learning support, unregulated use risks facilitating academic shortcuts and eroding critical thinking skills. This article introduces Lion-AI, a chatbot tutor developed to augment the CS educational experience. Lion-AI integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), rooted in university-specific course materials, with an engineered Socratic interaction policy. Unlike general-use tools, Lion-AI is designed to classify student requests, redirect direct-solution requests through diagnostic questioning, and provide guidance through one-question-at a-time interaction. The study describes a method for creating ethically constrained AI tutors in CS education. It presents the system’s three-tier architecture, the RAG pipeline, and the transparent interaction policy behind the tutor, positioning Lion-AI as a deployable proof of concept for combining curriculum grounding with explicit Socratic constraints. A controlled classroom study is planned as the next step.

papers.title: Analisis Persepsi Mahasiswa Akuntansi terhadap Peran Sistem Informasi Akuntansi dalam Pencegahan Fraud di Era Digital
papers.authors: Auliya Fadya Nafisa, Afni Maulia Farhani, Nayla Fitriya Ar Ridlwany, Sasa Amelia, Gina Sakinah
papers.journal: SCIENTIFIC JOURNAL OF REFLECTION Economic Accounting Management and Business
papers.abstract: Digital transformation has strengthened the role of Accounting Information Systems (AIS) as a means of processing financial data that is fast, integrated, and technology-based. On the other hand, technological developments have also increased the complexity of fraud risks, necessitating more effective control systems. This study aims to explore accounting students’ perceptions of the role of AIS in fraud prevention in the digital age. The study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, with data collected through in-depth interviews with students who have taken courses in Accounting Information Systems, Auditing, and Internal Control. The data were analyzed through the stages of reduction, presentation, and drawing conclusions. The results indicate that students view AIS as a crucial tool in fraud prevention by enhancing transparency, recording accuracy, data security, and providing audit trails that facilitate transaction tracing. The use of technologies such as automation, big data, and artificial intelligence is also considered capable of supporting the early detection of fraud. However, the effectiveness of AIS remains dependent on the competence of human resources, individual integrity, and the quality of an organization’s internal controls. This study is expected to provide input for the development of accounting education and to enhance the readiness of prospective accountants to face organizational governance challenges in the digital age.

papers.title: Academic integrity as a factor of strategic university development
papers.authors: Oleksandr Boblovskyi
papers.journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
papers.abstract: The article presents a comprehensive study of the role and significance of academic integrity as a strategic resource for the institutional advancement of higher education institutions amidst European integration, digital transformation, and the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies. The study shows that academic integrity extends beyond legal constraints, ethical rules, and plagiarism-detection mechanisms, becoming a core component of internal quality assurance, a means of strengthening reputational capital, and a driver of university competitiveness in both global and national markets. The study analyzes the domestic regulatory framework—specifically the Laws of Ukraine “On Education” and “On Higher Education” and recommendations from the National Agency for Higher Education Quality Assurance—alongside the 2015 ESG principles and the tenets of the International Center for Academic Integrity. It examines how integrity affects the transparency of academic management, the objectivity of student assessment, employer trust, and the expansion of international research collaboration. It pays particular attention to the challenges posed by digitalization: the proliferation of generative artificial intelligence, the transformation of academic writing, and the need to shift from prohibitive control models toward a culture of responsible digital tool use and enhanced information literacy among faculty and students. The work’s scientific novelty lies in developing a holistic model for fostering a culture of academic integrity within the university, synthesizing five interconnected components: regulatory, organizational, educational, digital, and value-based. Implementing the proposed model enables higher education institutions to shift from fragmented administration to systemic, strategic governance of educational quality and the innovative development of the academic community. Keywords: academic integrity, university, academic culture, quality of education, reputation, digitalization, artificial intelligence, strategic development, internal system of ensuring the quality of education.

papers.title: Neurotechnological toolkit for sales management of intermediary commercial structures in social media
papers.authors: Olha Ye. Haponenko, Tetiana M. Kutsenko, Yuliia Tataryntseva
papers.journal: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
papers.abstract: This article develops an integrative conceptual toolkit for sales management by intermediary commercial structures operating in social media, combining the classical sales process framework with neurotechnological methods of consumer behavior diagnostics. The study employs systematic analysis of prior empirical research, comparative analysis, and conceptual modeling. Intermediary commercial structures increasingly rely on social media not only for product promotion but for the full sales cycle, from prospecting to post-purchase engagement. However, conventional behavioral metrics such as clicks, impressions, and conversion rates fail to capture the underlying cognitive and affective mechanisms driving purchase decisions at each stage of the sales process. At the same time, academic coverage of neuroscience applications in sales management remains substantially narrower than in consumer marketing, and no integrative framework currently links established sales-process stage models with neurotechnological diagnostic methods for the specific context of intermediary commercial structures acting through social media channels. The article proposes an integrative matrix that maps the seven stages of the classical sales process onto the three core social selling activities and further onto the appropriate neurotechnological instruments (electroencephalography, functional magnetic resonance imaging, galvanic skin response, eye-tracking and brain-computer interfaces), grounded in real predictive-validity and adoption-barrier evidence from prior empirical studies. Practical selection criteria are formulated: instrument choice should depend on the specific sales stage and diagnostic task rather than on a generic preference for neurotechnology, and instrument adoption should be evaluated jointly through reliability and predictive validity rather than reliability alone. The scientific novelty lies in the first systematic linkage of the sales-process stage model, operationalized social selling activities, and neurotechnological diagnostic methods for intermediary commercial structures. Sales managers can use the results to select diagnostic tools by sales stage. Further research should empirically test the matrix in campaigns of Ukrainian intermediary commercial structures. Keywords: sales management, social media, neuromarketing, intermediary commercial structures, social selling, sales process, neurotechnology.

papers.title: Educational research in hybrid ecosystems: the role of generative AI as a sparring partner
papers.authors: Lorenza Maria Capolla, Francesca Gratani, Maila Pentucci, Lorella Giannandrea, Pier Giuseppe Rossi
papers.abstract: The article examines the role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in educational research as a socio-material and epistemic infrastructure embedded in contemporary regimes of power and knowledge production. It aims to move beyond techno-optimistic and techno-sceptical dichotomies by conceptualising AI as a non-neutral assemblage shaped by platform capitalism, data colonialism, and infrastructural dependencies. Drawing on more-than-human perspectives, the article explores how interactions between researchers and generative systems reconfigure processes of knowledge production and agency. While AI may reinforce existing forms of epistemic control, it can also open spaces for critical inquiry and resistance. To support such possibilities, the paper discusses some practices as ways of reconfiguring human–AI relations and avoiding the delegation of epistemic agency. Rather than treating AI as a device for generating answers, the article proposes understanding it as a dialogic sparring partner capable of provoking questions, challenging assumptions, and reshaping the co-construction of knowledge. The value of AI thus lies not in replacing human judgment but in expanding the dialogical spaces through which knowledge is produced.

papers.title: THE INFLUENCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE TEACHING PROCESS AND EDUCATION IN THE SYSTEM OF HIGHER EDUCATION
papers.authors: Sabira Gasimzada
papers.abstract: This article examines the theoretical foundations, practical possibilities, and prospects for the development of artificial intelligence technologies in the education system, particularly in higher education institutions. From a scientific and pedagogical perspective, it analyzes the role of artificial intelligence in personalizing the educational process, increasing the objectivity of assessment, optimizing teacher performance, and developing analytical decision-making mechanisms in education management. It also evaluates the impact of adaptive learning systems, automated assessment platforms, and data-driven analytical approaches on the quality of training in higher education. The study found that the integration of artificial intelligence technologies into the higher education system significantly contributes to the increased effectiveness of the educational process, improved student performance, and more efficient organization of teachers' professional activities. Furthermore, information security, protection of ethical standards, transparency of algorithms, development of technological infrastructure, and the development of digital skills are identified as key conditions for the successful application of these technologies. The results obtained in the article demonstrate that artificial intelligence technologies are a strategic area for the development of higher education and the need for continuous improvement of their application within a scientific and pedagogical framework.

papers.title: PENGEMBANGAN MODEL ADOPSI AI UMKM PEDESAAN MENGGUNAKAN METODE TECHNOLOGY-ORGANIZATION-ENVIRONMENT
papers.authors: Desy Candra Novitasari, Imam Riadi, Herman Herman
papers.abstract: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI), khususnya Large Language Models (LLM), telah mentransformasi lanskap bisnis global, namun tingkat adopsinya pada UMKM pedesaan masih sangat terbatas. Kesenjangan ini disebabkan oleh keterbatasan infrastruktur, rendahnya literasi digital, serta minimnya dukungan ekosistem yang spesifik sesuai konteks pedesaan. Penelitian ini berfokus pada adopsi AI/LLM dalam konteks pemasaran digital dan layanan pelanggan, dengan contoh use case seperti pembuatan konten promosi otomatis, chatbot untuk menjawab pertanyaan pelanggan, serta analisis sentimen terhadap ulasan produk. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan model konseptual adopsi AI pada UMKM pedesaan dengan menggunakan kerangka Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) sebagai landasan analisis. Metode yang digunakan adalah systematic literature review terhadap artikel-artikel terkait adopsi AI, penerapan TOE framework, serta karakteristik UMKM pedesaan yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2022–2026. Hasil review mengidentifikasi bahwa faktor-faktor dalam dimensi teknologi meliputi relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, LLM capability, dan cost efficiency; dimensi organisasi meliputi digital literacy, leadership support, dan resource readiness; serta dimensi lingkungan meliputi competitive pressure, government support, dan digital ecosystem support. Penelitian ini juga menemukan bahwa dalam konteks pedesaan, faktor digital ecosystem support berperan sebagai prasyarat utama, cost efficiency harus dipahami berdasarkan total cost of ownership, serta digital literacy memoderasi hubungan antara dukungan kepemimpinan dan adopsi AI

papers.title: PERBANDINGAN PERFORMA RESNET-18, EFFICIENTNET-B0, DAN ENSEMBLE LEARNING DENGAN VISUALISASI GRAD-CAM PADA DETEKSI KATARAK
papers.authors: Wahyu Putra Pratama, Dwi Arman Prasetya, Andri Fauzan Adziima
papers.abstract: Katarak merupakan salah satu penyebab utama kebutaan di dunia yang memerlukan deteksi dini untuk mencegah penurunan penglihatan permanen. Namun, diagnosis manual oleh tenaga medis rentan terhadap bias subjektif dan membutuhkan waktu yang tidak singkat, sehingga diperlukan sistem deteksi otomatis berbasis kecerdasan buatan yang akurat sekaligus interpretatif. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan model klasifikasi katarak menggunakan pendekatan stacking ensemble yang menggabungkan ResNet-18 dan EfficientNet-B0 sebagai base learner dengan Logistic Regression sebagai meta-learner, untuk mengklasifikasikan citra slit-lamp mata ke dalam tiga kelas, yaitu normal, immature, dan mature. Untuk meningkatkan transparansi model, penelitian ini juga mengintegrasikan metode Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) sebagai teknik Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) guna memvisualisasikan area citra yang paling berkontribusi terhadap keputusan prediksi model. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri atas 2.421 citra yang diperoleh dari platform Roboflow dan Kaggle, dengan tahap prapemrosesan meliputi resize, augmentasi, normalisasi, dan pembagian data. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa model ensemble stacking mencapai akurasi tertinggi sebesar 98,37%, melampaui performa model tunggal ResNet-18 (92,15%) dan EfficientNet-B0 (94,01%). Visualisasi Grad-CAM mengonfirmasi bahwa model secara konsisten memusatkan perhatian pada area sentral lensa yang mengalami kekeruhan, sesuai dengan karakteristik klinis katarak. Penelitian ini membuktikan bahwa pendekatan stacking ensemble yang dikombinasikan dengan XAI mampu menghasilkan sistem klasifikasi katarak yang akurat dan transparan, sehingga berkontribusi pada pengembangan sistem deteksi katarak berbasis kecerdasan buatan.

papers.title: Knowledge Construction In Arabic Language Learning In The Chatgpt Era: Opportunities And Pedagogical Transformations
papers.authors: Faza Naila Fathimatuz Zahra, Syamsul Maarif
papers.journal: Al Mi yar Jurnal Ilmiah Pembelajaran Bahasa Arab dan Kebahasaaraban
papers.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, has brought significant changes to the process of Arabic language learning at the university level. This study aims to analyze students' knowledge construction in Arabic language learning in the ChatGPT era, identify emerging pedagogical opportunities, and examine the pedagogical transformations resulting from the integration of AI technology to enhance learning effectiveness. This study employs a qualitative method using a library research approach through content analysis of various relevant academic literature. The findings reveal that: first, knowledge construction occurs through adaptive scaffolding, dialogic practice, instant feedback, and vocabulary exploration, which are aligned with Vygotsky’s Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD), enabling students to actively construct knowledge in collaborative and contextual learning environments; second, ChatGPT provides substantial opportunities through personalized learning, the simulation of authentic Arabic language environments, the development of critical digital literacy, and the enhancement of academic writing skills in innovative and sustainable ways; third, a pedagogical transformation has occurred in the form of a shift from teacher-centered learning to AI-mediated learner-centered learning, the reconfiguration of lecturers’ roles as critical facilitators and validators of AI-generated outputs, and the need for a curriculum that is adaptive to technological advancement. This study offers a comprehensive conceptual contribution to the development of AI-based Arabic language learning while upholding critical thinking, reflective learning, and academic integrity.

papers.title: Analisis Problematika Pembelajaran Mahārah Kalām Secara Daring: Studi Kasus di Universitas Sunan Gresik
papers.authors: Abdullah Abdullah, Ahmad Syafa'at Junaidi, Muhammad Syihabul Ihsan Al Haqiqy, Mira Mira, Evy Nur Rohmawaty
papers.journal: Al Mi yar Jurnal Ilmiah Pembelajaran Bahasa Arab dan Kebahasaaraban
papers.abstract: This research aims to comprehensively and in-depth analyze the problems experienced by students in online mahārah al-kalām learning. This qualitative research with a case study design involved 40 students of the Arabic Language Education study program at Universitas Sunan Gresik. Data collection was carried out through participatory observation and documentation techniques during virtual lectures. The results of the study indicate that the problems are divided into two main dimensions: non-linguistic and linguistic. In the non-linguistic dimension, the generation invisible phenomenon was found where students massively turned off their cameras (off-camera) to perform multitasking (such as teaching at other institutions and caring for children), resulting in a critical loss of cognitive presence and non-verbal interaction. Furthermore, network infrastructure constraints worsened communication quality. In the linguistic dimension, the virtual format thwarted the effectiveness of ṭarīqah al-mumārasah (drill) due to audio latency which prevented lecturers from correcting makhārij al-ḥurūf precisely. Furthermore, there was a severe disruption of academic integrity due to the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Students rely heavily on AI when asked to compose spontaneous muḥādatsah sentences, and exploit virtual proctoring loopholes (e-cheating) during mufradāt memorization exams. In conclusion, the online format significantly disrupts the acquisition process of Arabic speaking skills, demanding urgent methodological engineering and more adaptive, cheat-proof oral evaluation systems.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Students' Academic Performance in Higher Education
papers.authors: X. Ren
papers.abstract: In higher education, student academic performance is considered a key educational outcome. Consequently, improving academic performance is a pressing objective for many higher education institutions. Predicting and classifying student performance can provide valuable insights and facilitate the development of appropriate strategies to enhance academic results. In recent years, data mining methods have been widely applied and have demonstrated significant success in classification and prediction tasks. This article presents and analyzes the EASP student performance dataset. Seven machine learning methods were applied to classify and predict student academic performance: Multinomial Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and k-Nearest Neighbors. The performance of these methods was evaluated using precision, recall, the area under the ROC curve (AUC), and the F1-score. Experimental results demonstrated that Logistic Regression achieved the best predictive performance on the EASP test set, with a precision of 0.75.

papers.title: Environmental Regulation Pressure and Green Innovation Bubbles: Resource Channels and the Amplifying Role of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: 嶂彩 何, Xinbin Zhao, Jipeng Xie
papers.abstract: Environmental regulation may expand visible green-innovation inputs without proportionate contemporaneous patent output. We examine a supplied residual measure of this input–output mismatch in a matched sample of 27,157 observations on 4560 Chinese A-share listed firms from 2014 to 2022. In the industry- and year-adjusted specification, regulatory pressure is positively associated with the residual (0.031, firm-clustered p<0.001). Complete mediation equations identify the WW financing index and environmental investment as exploratory resource channels. Conditional effects of regulatory pressure are positive across the reported AI-disclosure distribution. The magnitude is modest: a one-standard-deviation increase in regulatory pressure corresponds to approximately 0.0066 outcome units, or 0.039 standard deviations. The evidence documents systematic cross-firm covariation and motivates closer attention to input–output conversion. Firm fixed-effects sensitivity and the contemporaneous construction limit within-firm and causal interpretation; future research should validate the construct using forward patent output, patent quality, and physical environmental performance.

papers.title: Linking Perceived Corporate Social Responsibility to Brand Loyalty and Brand Advocacy Intention: Brand Trust and Value Co-Creation in Hotel Customer Relationships
papers.authors: Ming-Hsuan Wu
papers.abstract: This study examines how hotel customers’ perceptions of corporate social responsibility (CSR) are associated with brand loyalty and brand advocacy intention through brand trust and value co-creation. Drawing on signaling theory, relationship-based social exchange reasoning, and service-dominant logic, survey data collected from 638 hotel customers recruited in Taiwan between May and June 2026 were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Perceived CSR was positively associated with brand trust; brand trust was positively associated with value co-creation; and both brand trust and value co-creation were positively associated with loyalty and advocacy intention. The direct CSR–outcome associations were not significant, whereas the proposed indirect associations were significant. Competing-model analyses qualified the serial interpretation: a parallel model remained plausible, and a partial sequential model showed significant CSR–VCC and BT–VCC paths, indicating that trust is a meaningful but not exclusive pathway to participation. Supplementary measurement analyses supported an overarching value co-creation representation while confirming borderline first-order convergent validity. The findings concern customer–brand relationship associations rather than sustainability-specific behavior or hotel sustainability performance. Managerially, hotels should emphasize credible CSR communication and accessible opportunities for customer participation rather than assuming that favorable CSR perceptions directly translate into loyalty or advocacy.

papers.title: Pooled Information and Model Flexibility: Decomposing Machine-Learning Gains in Corporate Budgeting and Forecasting
papers.authors: Muteb Ahmed Almihbash
papers.journal: Journal of risk and financial management
papers.abstract: Corporate financial planning and analysis (FP&A) is being reorganised around machine learning, yet the supporting evidence consists largely of vendor case reports using undefined accuracy measures. This study decomposes the machine-learning advantage into components that prior work bundles together—information recency versus model re-estimation, and pooled estimation versus learner flexibility—measured on corporate income-statement data rather than retail or equity series. An open benchmark from SEC XBRL data covering 2599 non-financial US filers and 118,406 firm-quarters, from 2011 to 2025, evaluates five pre-registered hypotheses under rolling-origin validation with clustered inference. First, the advantage of continuous re-forecasting over annual budgeting derives from information recency rather than parameter updating: supplying current quarterly actuals to a model estimated once at fiscal year start recovers 27 to 58 percent of forecast error, whereas quarterly re-estimation produces no detectable improvement (p = 0.82), a result that holds across the COVID-19 and 2022 inflation regimes. Second, the advantage is an interaction rather than a main effect: a pooled linear model modestly outperforms a Theta benchmark, a flexible learner fitted per firm underperforms it, and a foundation model pooled across unrelated domains underperforms further; only pooling across comparable firms combined with a flexible learner realises the full gain. Third, model ranking reverses under asymmetric budget-variance cost.

papers.title: Design and Open-Water Validation of an Autonomous Underwater Robot for Physical Diver Safety Assistance
papers.authors: Min-Gyu Kim, Hyungjoo Kang, Hansol Jin, Jihong Li, Gun Rae Cho, Gyeongmin Kim, Minshik Noh
papers.journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
papers.abstract: Diving accidents remain frequently fatal, and most stem from preventable human factors: panic, failed buoyancy control, and disorientation. Underwater human–robot interaction research has focused on observing the diver and offers little help when a diver must be pulled to safety. This paper presents the design and sea validation of NADIA, an autonomous underwater robot that combines diver guidance and following with diver-commanded physical assistance. A rear handle converts the diver’s grip into thrust and springs back to neutral on release; a diver-facing display shows depth, distance, battery state, and warnings. Six vector thrusters, with mounting angles optimized by gradient descent against drag-model thrust-ratio targets, are driven by an operational-space time-delay controller (TDC-OSF) that keeps the robot in the diver’s view; stereo vision and imaging sonar are fused for diver detection. In test-bed, tank, and sea trials, surge and heave thrusts matched design targets within 5–7%; approval-gated guidance held the robot 1–2 m from the diver with position and heading errors below 0.15 m and 3.5°; and the robot towed a diver at about 1 m/s and rose from 5 m to the surface in about 4 s. An underwater robot can thus serve as a physical safety layer for divers.

papers.title: Ethical Boundaries for Large Language Models in Mental-Health Care: A Review of Psychological Safety, Relational Governance and Human Escalation
papers.authors: Eunice Ya Ping Lim, Fang Chen, Chi Eung Danforn Lim
papers.journal: Journal of Mind and Medical Sciences
papers.abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence is increasingly encountered by people seeking support during distress, social isolation, or delays in accessing mental-health care. In these settings, the central ethical concern extends beyond factual inaccuracy. Large language models (LLMs) may produce responses that appear empathic while failing to detect suicidal intent, exceeding the limits of a non-clinician support role, undermining patient autonomy, or weakening the clinician–patient relationship. This narrative review reframes ethical boundaries for LLMs in mental-health care around three clinically important contexts: crisis support, psychiatric triage, and therapy augmentation. A narrative approach was adopted to support conceptual synthesis rather than pooled effect estimation. The literature on digital psychiatry, conversational agents, LLMs, artificial intelligence ethics, suicide-safety responses, patient perspectives, and clinical reporting guidance was reviewed from major medical and interdisciplinary sources. The primary search covered publications from 1 January 2021 to 30 June 2026, with earlier foundational chatbot studies retained selectively and interpreted separately from contemporary LLM evidence. Four interrelated priorities are proposed for evaluation: governance centred on psychological safety, autonomy, trust and the clinician–patient relationship; crisis-response safeguards combining supportive recognition with human escalation; bounded lower-acuity support with transparent uncertainty; and co-designed evaluation of patient-experienced and relational outcomes. These are candidate design priorities, not demonstrated mechanisms of risk reduction. The proposed framework integrates existing ethical principles with mental-health scenarios, external control functions, verified human handoffs, and staged evaluation. Study-level findings are distinguished from technical background and author-derived proposals. The framework is exploratory and has not been empirically or clinically validated; it is intended to generate research questions, not guide routine clinical care. Future studies would need to assess clinically meaningful outcomes: whether the system recognises acute risk, maintains a bounded support role, preserves patient autonomy and trust, and enables timely human escalation when vulnerability, ambiguity, or risk is disclosed.

papers.title: GenAI Literacy and Students’ Exploitative and Exploratory Innovation: The Moderating Role of Critical Thinking
papers.authors: Yali Tang, Liang Wu
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) literacy, encompassing the knowledge, skills, and attitudes for effective use, is becoming essential in education. However, its distinct associations with exploitative versus exploratory innovation and the role of critical thinking remain unclear. Grounded in social cognitive theory, this study surveyed 228 students to examine these relationships. GenAI literacy was positively associated with exploitative innovation and showed a U-shaped association with exploratory innovation, in which benefits emerged only after a literacy threshold; the U-shaped association was robust to correction for multiple comparisons. Critical thinking negatively moderated the association between GenAI literacy and exploitative innovation, and this interaction was robust to correction for multiple comparisons; the hypothesized moderation of the U-shaped exploratory association, in contrast, did not reach the 0.05 level and did not receive empirical support. The findings extend theory by differentiating how GenAI literacy relates to distinct innovation types and offer practical guidance—drawn from the supported associations and from theoretical reasoning—for fostering balanced human–AI collaboration. Because participation was voluntary, the self-selected sample may have overestimated the reported associations, and all results should be interpreted with this caveat in mind.

papers.title: Beyond Overlap: Development and Validation of the Inclusion of AI in Self (IAIS) Scale and Its Moderating Role in the Relationship Between AI Identity and AI Threat
papers.authors: Jiali He, 이한미, Xiang Yao
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly integrated into people’s self-concepts, yet a psychometrically robust multi-item pictorial instrument for assessing the inclusion of AI in self (IAIS) is lacking. Drawing on self-expansion theory and the AI-mediated communication (AI-MC) model, we developed and validated the IAIS scale. The IAIS comprises four pictorial items capturing overlap, distance, centrality, and size, designed as indicators of a single dimension. In Study 1, Chinese university students (N = 195, 56.9% male) were recruited through campus online platforms using convenience sampling. We conducted exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses (EFA/CFA), examined reliability and convergent, discriminant, and criterion-related validity (the last via Steiger’s Z tests), and assessed gender invariance with multigroup CFA. In Study 2, the scale was cross-validated in a sample of Chinese employees (N = 513, 38.4% male) recruited through the Credamo online research platform. In Study 3, a mixed student–employee sample (N = 240, 43.3% male) completed a two-wave longitudinal survey with a 15-day interval. The moderating role of IAIS in the relationship between AI identity and AI threat was tested with PROCESS Model 1 (5000 bootstrap resamples). Results supported a replicable single-factor structure, good reliability, and convergent, discriminant, and criterion-related validity. IAIS significantly moderated the association between AI identity and AI threat. We conclude that IAIS is a psychometrically sound instrument for assessing the inclusion of AI in self, and that the negative association between AI identity and AI threat is stronger among individuals who include AI more deeply in the self.

papers.title: AI Dependency, Academic Self-Efficacy, and Depressive Symptoms Among Medical Students: A Structural Equation Modeling Study in Saudi Arabia
papers.authors: Saeed Asiri
papers.abstract: Background: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into medical education has opened up new possibilities for academic support. However, it has also raised concerns about over-dependence on AI. Students’ use of AI may have implications for students’ academic self-concept and psychological well-being, but the interrelationships among these constructs are not yet sufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the association between AI dependency and academic self-efficacy and depressive symptoms among medical students in Saudi Arabia. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study among 207 medical students recruited from three public universities in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Data were collected anonymously using an online questionnaire distributed through QR-coded recruitment announcements. AI dependency was assessed using a 9-item subset of the AI Dependence Scale, academic self-efficacy using the 5-item General Academic Self-Efficacy Scale, and depressive symptoms using the two depression items of the PHQ-4. AI dependency and academic self-efficacy were modeled as latent constructs in a structural equation model. The model examined the direct association between AI dependency and depressive symptoms and the indirect associational pathway through academic self-efficacy. Results: The mean AI dependency score was 2.83 (SD = 0.78), while the mean academic self-efficacy score was 3.87 (SD = 1.07) and the mean depressive symptom score was 2.05 (SD = 1.42). AI dependency was positively associated with academic self-efficacy (β = 0.298, 95% CI 0.157–0.439, p < 0.001). Academic self-efficacy was inversely associated with depressive symptoms (β = −0.212, 95% CI −0.382–0.041, p = 0.016). AI dependency showed a strong positive direct association with depressive symptoms (β = 0.608, 95% CI 0.491–0.725, p < 0.001). The indirect association through academic self-efficacy was negative (β = −0.063, 95% CI −0.124–0.002, p = 0.052), while the total association remained positive and significant (β = 0.545, 95% CI 0.409–0.671, p < 0.001). The model explained 49% of the variance in academic self-efficacy and 37% of the variance in depressive symptoms. Conclusions: Greater AI dependency was associated with higher academic self-efficacy but also with substantially higher depressive symptom levels among medical students. Academic self-efficacy was inversely associated with depressive symptoms, although evidence for an indirect pathway between AI dependency and depressive symptoms was limited. Our findings highlight the importance of distinguishing productive AI use from excessive dependence. This supports the need for responsible AI integration alongside attention to medical students’ psychological well-being.

papers.title: A Focused Narrative Review of Selected Evidence on Gymnastics Training Optimization, Technology, Athlete Health, and Injury Prevention
papers.authors: Nicoleta Zaharie, Sonia Gabriela Neagu, Delia Bădescu, Vlad Teodor Grosu, Alina Georgeta Mag, Cristian Stanciu, Ioan Sabin Sopa
papers.abstract: Background: Sustainable gymnastics training requires a balance between performance development, injury prevention, workload management, athlete health, psychological well-being, and long-term participation. This focused narrative review aimed to synthesize selected evidence on training optimization, technological applications, athlete health and injury prevention in gymnastics. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted using the Web of Science Core Collection. The literature search covered publications issued between 1 January 2005 and 30 September 2025, with the final search performed on 30 September 2025. English-language publications retrieved through three predefined Topic searches in the Web of Science Core Collection were considered. The searches covered the period from 1 January 2005 to 30 September 2025 and were restricted to the Sport Sciences category. No additional publications were identified through reference-list screening. Three complementary thematic searches addressing gymnastics training models, technological applications, and injury prevention identified 485 records. After applying the eligibility criteria, removing duplicates, assessing full texts, and excluding ineligible or retracted publications, 140 publications were included in the narrative synthesis. No formal risk-of-bias assessment was performed. Results: The reviewed evidence emphasized progressive and individualized training, workload monitoring, recovery, physical preparation, age-appropriate development, and early identification of pain, fatigue, and other health-related concerns. Injury occurrence was associated with biomechanical loading, rapid growth, training exposure, previous injuries, insufficient recovery, menstrual dysfunction, psychological factors, and discipline-specific technical demands. Wearable sensors, video analysis, biomechanical modelling, artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and digital learning platforms supported movement assessment, technical feedback, training monitoring, and education. Evidence for several emerging technological applications, particularly artificial intelligence and automated assessment, remains preliminary and requires further validation in gymnastics-specific and real-world settings. However, substantial differences in study designs, populations, technologies, outcome measures, and methodological characteristics limited direct comparison across studies. Coaching communication, athlete motivation, psychological well-being, and access to validated technologies also influenced the sustainability of gymnastics training. Conclusions: Sustainable gymnastics training may benefit from an interdisciplinary and athlete-centered approach integrating individualized load management, injury prevention, health monitoring, recovery, educational coaching practices, and appropriately validated technologies. The evidence identified in this review highlights converging themes suggesting the potential value of combining these components to support safe performance development and long-term participation. However, more longitudinal, discipline-specific, and methodologically consistent research is needed.

papers.title: Navigating Disruption: A Transformative Learning Theory Examination of Faculty Perceptions of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Academic Practices
papers.authors: Gibin Mannathikulathil Raju, Trini Balart, Kristi J. Shryock
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT have rapidly entered higher education, challenging longstanding norms around authorship, assessment, and disciplinary expertise. While early GenAI scholarship has largely emphasized student outcomes, adoption trends, and academic integrity, comparatively little empirical work has examined how faculty and staff make sense of this disruption over time. Guided by Transformative Learning Theory (TLT) as an interpretive lens for faculty discourse, this qualitative study examines how educators interpret GenAI as a “disorienting dilemma” and how patterns in faculty discourse differ across two cross-sectional cohorts during the first year of widespread adoption. We analyzed open-ended survey responses to the question, “How do you think AI tools like ChatGPT will impact the future of your discipline?” collected at a large U.S. R1 Hispanic-serving public research university. Two cohorts were examined: an early-adoption dataset gathered in 2023 (n = 104) and a follow-up dataset collected in 2024 (n = 313). Using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis procedures, we identified persistent themes and qualitative differences in how participants described GenAI-related concerns and opportunities. No educator-navigation theme differed significantly in proportional prevalence between cohorts. Accordingly, interpretations of cross-cohort differences rest on variations in thematic framing, tone, and illustrative detail rather than on statistically demonstrated temporal change. The 2023 responses more often foregrounded academic-integrity concerns and defensive assessment redesign, whereas the 2024 responses included more concrete descriptions of pedagogical experimentation and potential uses of GenAI to support faculty productivity and professional practice. Across both years, persistent anxieties regarding student dependency, erosion of foundational skills, and the potential dehumanization and homogenization of academic discourse remained salient. These results highlight faculty as active agents engaged in reflection and adaptation and show how aggregate patterns of faculty sensemaking are compatible with early processes described by Transformative Learning Theory. TLT is used here as an interpretive lens for cohort-level faculty discourse, not as evidence that individual instructors underwent internal perspective transformation. This underscores the need for institutionally supported, human-centered approaches to GenAI integration, including policy clarity, sustained faculty development, and communities of practice that enable ethical, reflective experimentation.

papers.title: Students’ Generative AI Use in Studio-Based Design Education: Selective Use, Design Judgment, and Studio Context
papers.authors: Michelle Boyoung Huh, Alp Tural, Elif Tural
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping studio-based design education, yet relatively little is known about how students decide when and how AI should support their design process. This study examined students’ use, adaptation, and perceptions of generative AI, with particular attention to task-specific use, contextual adaptation, and factors associated with AI-related decision-making. An online survey of 112 undergraduate and graduate design students combined structured questionnaire items with optional open-ended responses to examine AI use across studio tasks, project stages, and learning contexts. Students reported higher AI use for concept development, research, and written articulation than for visual refinement, technical documentation, and later stages of design development. Students also reported becoming more selective in their AI use as projects progressed, while instructor expectations, peer influence, and concern about negative judgment were associated with students’ AI-related decisions. Qualitative responses further highlighted authorship, learning, and professional responsibility as important considerations. Together, these findings suggest that students’ selective and context-dependent AI use can be interpreted as boundary-setting around when and how AI participates in the design process. Rather than viewing AI use simply as technology adoption, the findings suggest value in a judgment-centered, process-based approach to AI pedagogy that emphasizes accountability and reflective decision-making.

papers.title: Validation of a Questionnaire to Explore Artificial Intelligence Use Among Upper-Secondary and Higher Education Teachers
papers.authors: Rodrigo Narváez, Miguel Ángel Rivera-Navarro, Luis Medina Gual
papers.abstract: Research on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education has shifted from students to teachers, yet available teacher instruments rest on technology acceptance models, professional knowledge frameworks, or AI literacy, and none articulates dispositional conditions, teaching activities, and contextual consequences within a single functional logic. This study extends to teachers an instrument previously validated with students and grounded in Functional Behavior Analysis and the Interbehavioral Model of Didactic Performance. Participants were 233 Mexican upper-secondary and higher education teachers (mean age 47.22 years, SD = 10.44). The study is strictly psychometric in scope: it reports initial reliability and internal structure evidence, not a profile of teacher practice. Reliability was estimated with Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega with bootstrap confidence intervals, and the number of components was determined through Horn’s parallel analysis. Alpha coefficients ranged from 0.703 to 0.957 (omega, 0.755 to 0.962). The benefits dimension split into two uncorrelated components, pedagogical benefits (α = 0.953) and risks to academic integrity (α = 0.771). Domains of didactic performance proved unidimensional (63.0% of variance); the consequences dimension behaved as a formative index rather than a reflective scale; and the dispositional dimension failed to separate individual from contextual variables and required redesign. A second-order analysis yielded two orthogonal axes, favourable pedagogical orientation and risk recognition, on which four quadrants are described for illustrative purposes only. The instrument discriminates across self-reported frequency of AI use. Because components were extracted from Pearson correlations on ordinal items in a single convenience sample, the structure reported here is provisional and requires confirmation with polychoric matrices and robust estimators on an independent sample.

papers.title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence Tools in Post-Treatment Breast Cancer Survivors: A Scoping Review of Measurement Approaches and Associated Outcomes
papers.authors: K.E. Johnston, Aoife M Twomey, Samantha J. Cushen
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nutrition is an important yet underexplored determinant of cancer survivorship outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests that greater adherence to the Mediterranean diet (MedD) is associated with improved health status, enhanced quality of life (QoL), and reduced mortality. However, evidence specifically targeting post-treatment breast cancer survivors remains limited, and substantial heterogeneity in MedD scoring tools and adherence thresholds restricts comparability across studies. This review aimed to (i) identify and characterise the tools used to assess MedD adherence in breast cancer survivors following completion of active treatment, including their components, scoring systems, and adherence thresholds; and (ii) map the range of health outcomes that have been examined in relation to MedD adherence in this population. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched (2000-2026) for English-language intervention and observational studies reporting MedD adherence in adult female breast cancer survivors after treatment completion. Two reviewers independently extracted data, which were synthesised descriptively, including study characteristics, MedD scoring tools, adherence outcomes, and clinical, metabolic, and QoL findings. The methodological structure protocol of this scoping review was retrospectively registered in the Open Science Framework. RESULTS: = 4174, excluding non-cancer comparators) met inclusion criteria. Ten MedD scoring tools were identified, most frequently MEDAS-14 (original or modified, 7/20 studies), varying in components (range 9-18), scoring approach, and adherence thresholds. Most intervention studies reported improved MedD adherence following intervention, generally as a within-group change; between-group differences in adherence were reported less often and inconsistently significant. Anthropometric outcomes (body weight, body mass index (BMI), waist circumference) were most frequently improved, but significant differences between groups were found in only a small number of controlled studies. Mortality was assessed in only one observational cohort study, which found no association with breast-cancer-specific outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: This scoping review identified considerable heterogeneity in how MedD adherence is measured in breast cancer survivors, with ten different scoring tools identified across 20 studies. Although improvements in MedD adherence appear achievable, the evidence is limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous assessment tools, and short intervention durations. Larger, standardised longitudinal studies are needed, particularly to determine whether MedD adherence influences cancer recurrence and survival, for which current evidence remains minimal.

papers.title: Beyond Local Gating: Toward Network-State-Dependent Neuromodulation
papers.authors: Paolo Belardinelli, Elena Mongiardini, Sonia Turrini, Alessio Avenanti
papers.abstract: Brain stimulation is progressively evolving from anatomically targeted interventions toward individualized, adaptive, and network-oriented approaches. Recent developments in brain-state-dependent stimulation have demonstrated that neuromodulation can be optimized by synchronizing stimulation with ongoing neural activity, while adaptive cortico-cortical paired associative stimulation (ccPAS) has extended this principle to distributed cortical networks. However, current approaches continue to define brain state primarily through local electrophysiological features, such as oscillatory phase or power, even though ccPAS is specifically designed to modify communication between interconnected cortical regions. In this opinion paper, we argue that the endogenous variable guiding ccPAS should instead describe the instantaneous physiological state of the targeted cortico-cortical pathway. We propose that online source-space functional connectivity provides a biologically meaningful and technically feasible estimate of this pathway state, thereby enabling a new framework of network-state-dependent neuromodulation. As illustrative applications, we consider pathways spanning different levels of experimental characterization, from established sensorimotor interactions to the less-characterized ventral premotor cortex (PMv)-posterior superior temporal sulcus (pSTS) pathway within the action-observation network (AON). This distinction highlights that the proposed framework is pathway-general, while its experimental implementation requires pathway-specific characterization of stimulation parameters and appropriate physiological readouts. In this framework, resting-state EEG is rapidly reconstructed in source space to estimate pathway connectivity, which is subsequently used to personalize stimulation targets and guide state-dependent ccPAS of a functionally defined cortico-cortical circuit. Finally, we discuss the technological prerequisites, methodological challenges, biological rationale, and open scientific questions that must be addressed before pathway-state-guided neuromodulation can be experimentally validated. We argue that redefining brain state as the instantaneous physiological state of the communication pathway targeted by stimulation may represent the next conceptual step in brain stimulation.

papers.title: Physiological Responses Evoked by Single-Pulse Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation: A Systematic Review of Corticospinal Excitability Measures
papers.authors: Kapka Mancheva, Georgi Atanasov
papers.abstract: Single-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (spTMS) is widely used to investigate human corticospinal and cortical physiology, yet individual physiological measures provide only partial information about cortical function. This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on human physiological responses evoked by spTMS, with particular emphasis on resting and active motor thresholds, motor-evoked potentials (MEPs), corticospinal silent periods (CSPs), and biological and technical determinants of response variability. The review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, supplemented by citation tracking. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively because of substantial heterogeneity in stimulation protocols, populations, recording methods, and outcomes. Across the included literature, no single measure fully characterized corticospinal excitability: motor thresholds primarily reflected membrane/axonal excitability, MEPs reflected integrated corticospinal output, and CSPs provided information on intracortical inhibitory processes. Age, sex-related anatomical and hormonal factors, cortical anatomy, coil position and orientation, pulse waveform, stimulation intensity, muscle state, attention, fatigue, sleep, and medication contributed to response variability. The findings support an integrated interpretation of spTMS measures, standardized protocols, and individualized electric field modeling. TMS-evoked EEG potentials (TEPs) methodology is discussed only as complementary contextual information; TEPs were not systematically targeted by the original search strategy and were therefore not included among the outcomes of the systematic synthesis. The exact historical search date could not be reconstructed from the available documentation and is reported transparently as a limitation.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Rehabilitation: A Systematic Mapping Review
papers.authors: Daniele Coraci, Gianluca Regazzo, Gabriele Santilli, Stefano Masiero
papers.abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly entering rehabilitation, but the maturity and functional distribution of the evidence remain unclear. Methods: We conducted a mapping review reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR as applicable. PubMed and Scopus were searched using controlled vocabulary and free-text terms for GenAI, large language models, and rehabilitation. After deduplication, the records were manually screened by title and abstract, and full texts were consulted for uncertainty. Results: Of 1313 unique records, 233 met the eligibility criteria. Publications appeared from 2023 to 2026. Multi-label coding identified rehabilitation clinical and workflow support in 106/233 records (45%), patient-level rehabilitation intervention or functional assistance in 64/233 (27%), rehabilitation professional education in 56/233 (24%), and patient or caregiver education within rehabilitation in 45/233 (19%). Twenty-eight records (12%) addressed more than one application. Model/output evaluation or technical development predominated (155/233; 67%), whereas 13/233 records (6%) were interventional or feasibility studies. Conclusions: GenAI research in rehabilitation has expanded rapidly, but its most frequent use is clinician-facing support rather than direct patient-level intervention. The evidence remains dominated by technical, simulated, and observational evaluations, with limited clinical experimentation. Future research should prioritize prospective patient-level evaluation, transparent model reporting, safety, and human oversight.

papers.title: LLM-Enabled Educational Artefacts in Computer Science Education: A Systematic Mapping Study
papers.authors: Franklin L. Sanchez, Carlos Alario‐Hoyos, Danny S. Guamán, Julio C. Caiza
papers.abstract: The use of Large Language Models in computer science education has produced a fast-growing body of primary studies. Existing secondary studies tend to categorise this literature by external criteria, such as the model used, the course it operates in, or the benefit it reports; the educational artefact itself is discussed but not adopted as the unit of analysis. This study adopts it: the LLM-enabled educational artefact (LEEA), a deliverable built on an LLM for educational purposes, either technological, such as a tool, system, or agent, or methodological, such as a model or technique, rather than the general-purpose model that powers it. Through a review of scientific databases, 158 primary studies published between 2022 and February 2025 were analysed using a six-dimensional codification scheme and six research questions. The mapped studies concentrate on a few options: 69.6% of contributions focus on tools and systems, 84.8% rely on the GPT family, and 86.1% target undergraduate education. Feedback appears in 76.6% of studies, while other instructional stages remain underexplored. Evidence comes mainly from user perception and system performance, which rarely overlap; only 21.5% of studies measure learning gains, so the evidence on learning remains limited. The study contributes a multidimensional map of this literature and a codification scheme detailing eleven educational functions and seven families of effectiveness metrics derived from the corpus.

papers.title: A Layered Decision-Aware Forecasting Architecture for Noisy Panel Environments
papers.authors: Mohamed Sameh Hassanein, Reham Nasser Farag, Samar Turki, Osama Emam
papers.abstract: Machine learning forecasting systems in noisy, non-stationary, multi-entity environments are commonly optimized for pointwise predictive accuracy, although many downstream decisions depend on the relative ordering of entities rather than exact numerical forecasts. This creates a potential prediction–ranking–decision misalignment, where the model with the lowest forecast error may not generate the most useful ranking or decision outcome. This paper proposes a Layered Decision-Aware Forecasting Architecture (LDFA) that separates predictive calibration from decision-oriented transformation. Layers 1 and 2 generate heterogeneous forecasts through base learners, stacking, and adaptive weighting, while the main methodological contribution is Layer 3: a selective post-prediction controller based on source selection, activation gating, veto logic, and regime-aware scaling. LDFA is evaluated using daily data for 30 EGX firms from 2020 to 2025 under a leakage-controlled expanding-window walk-forward protocol. The results show that prediction, ranking, and decision metrics favor different models: the Ridge meta-model provides the strongest target-scale accuracy, the XGBRankerLTR learning-to-rank baseline achieves the strongest ranking information coefficient (IC), and the SoftmaxHybridGate achieves the highest Sharpe ratio. The Layer 3 controller slightly improves over the Ridge backbone in mean daily IC, Sharpe ratio, and maximum drawdown, but the gains are modest and not statistically conclusive. Ablation and sensitivity analyses show that uncontrolled correction is harmful, while selective activation is the main value-adding mechanism. Transaction-cost, dynamic-controller, bootstrap, and top-k robustness tests further indicate that LDFA is most useful under selective decision settings rather than as a universally dominant model. The findings position LDFA as a transparent decision-aware forecasting architecture for studying and managing prediction–ranking–decision trade-offs in noisy panel environments.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Medical and Surgical Information: A Systematic Review of Accuracy, Readability, Reliability, and Emotional Resonance
papers.authors: Francesco Leonforte, Andrea Sebastiano Cavallaro, Vito Nicosia, Alessia Scapellato, Agata Gambera, Cristina Genovese, Antonio Mistretta, Antonio Zanghi, Guido Basile, Massimiliano Veroux, Paolo Di Mattia, Andrea Pio Calabrò, Kenya Tiralongo, Yossef Gatthas
papers.abstract: Background: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly utilized for patient-facing healthcare communication. However, their clinical utility remains constrained by communicative, ethical, and safety challenges. This systematic review provides a cross-specialty evaluation of conversational AI, synthesizing evidence on accuracy, readability, informational quality, and emotional resonance. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD420251021428), PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from 2020 through November 2025. Eligible studies evaluated LLM-generated medical or surgical information against healthcare professionals, validated benchmarks, or alternative AI platforms. Assessed outcomes included factual accuracy, standardized readability indices (e.g., FKGL, FRES), validated quality metrics (e.g., DISCERN, GQS), and emotional or empathetic impact. Results: Eighty-two studies (published 2023–2025) were included. Accuracy was evaluated in 45 studies, demonstrating generally high performance (mean Likert scores > 3.5/5); advanced GPT models frequently showed parity or superiority to comparators, though factual errors persisted in complex clinical reasoning. Readability, assessed in 69 studies, emerged as the primary limitation: baseline outputs consistently required high school or university-level comprehension (FKGL > 10–12), substantially exceeding recommended patient literacy thresholds (≤8th grade). Informational quality, appraised in 35 studies, was rated moderate-to-high across DISCERN and GQS metrics. Six studies evaluating emotional resonance indicated that LLMs can alleviate situational anxiety and deliver structured cognitive empathy comparable or superior to brief clinician text, though lacking genuine emotional depth. Conclusions: LLMs demonstrate strong factual accuracy and structural quality across diverse clinical disciplines. However, autonomous, patient-facing deployment remains premature due to excessive lexical density that threatens health equity. Conversational AI should function as a clinical adjunct to support providers rather than an unsupervised educational tool. Future research must prioritize dynamic literacy alignment and robust clinical validation.

papers.title: Smart Agriculture Technology: A Review of Robotic Platforms, Sensing Modalities, Artificial Intelligence, Datasets, Evaluation Metrics, and Future Research Directions
papers.authors: Ghaith Al-refai, Mahmoud Al-Sarayreh
papers.abstract: Smart agriculture has moved beyond isolated precision-farming tools toward integrated cyber–physical systems that combine robotics, multimodal sensing, connectivity, artificial intelligence, and data-driven decision support. This review synthesizes recent developments in the field using a systematic critical review approach. It proposes a systems-level framework for analyzing smart agriculture across robotic platforms, sensing and digital infrastructure, AI methods, public datasets and benchmarks, evaluation metrics, application domains, and deployment maturity. The review covers ground robots, UAVs, harvesting manipulators, multi-robot systems, RGB and spectral sensing, LiDAR, IoT networks, edge/cloud platforms, AI-based perception and decision-making, and multimodal vision–language models. The analysis shows that the literature has made clear progress in prototypes, datasets, and task-specific performance, but several gaps still limit practical deployment. These include weak cross-season and cross-region validation, fragmented benchmarking practices, limited deployment-oriented metrics, insufficient techno-economic reporting, and unresolved challenges related to interoperability and human–robot interaction. Public datasets and emerging multimodal benchmarks show that the field is moving toward greater standardization; however, strong benchmark performance does not yet consistently translate into reliable field operation. The review concludes by outlining future research directions in benchmark realism, field-robust AI, edge deployment, digital twins, privacy-preserving learning, human-centered autonomy, and long-term agronomic and economic validation.

papers.title: Governance-Specific Use of AI, Ownership Structure, Financing, and Operational Agility: Evidence from Indian SMEs
papers.authors: Samreen Akhtar
papers.abstract: BAs firms begin integrating AI into governance functions, research on how ownership structure and financing relate to this shift remains early-stage, especially among SMEs. To address this gap, this study draws on an unweighted analytical sample of 1215 Indian SMEs from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys India 2025 round linked to the 2026 AI Follow-up Survey. The follow-up sample overrepresents digitally intensive sectors, testing ten hypotheses via logistic regression and bootstrapped decomposition. The analysis showed that owner-managed firms were less likely to use AI for strategic decision-making (OR = 0.30, p < 0.001) yet more likely to hold a loan or credit line (OR = 2.16, p < 0.001) and score higher on operational agility (OR = 1.69, p < 0.001). Notably, general AI adoption was not associated with agility, whereas governance-specific use of AI and financing were strongly associated with operational agility (OR = 3.96–4.15 and OR = 4.20, p < 0.001), though no association was detected between them (p = 0.961); the indirect component was negative for strategic AI use, positive for financing, both under extended controls. Together, results indicate functional AI use, not adoption, is associated with agility, so binary adoption measures may inadequately evaluate SME digital transformation. The results describe associations within the observed analytical sample and should not be interpreted as nationally representative estimates.

papers.title: Perceptions of ChatGPT- and veterinarian-generated responses to pet owners’ medical questions
papers.authors: Aïnoha Griot, Rob Ward
papers.abstract: Background: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly significant in veterinary medicine, particularly in answering pet owners' medical questions. AI's integration could reduce veterinary professionals' workload while improving access to medical advice. However, the reliability and quality of AI-generated responses compared to veterinarians' remain unexplored. The objective was to determine whether AI-generated responses were perceived as comparable to veterinarian-generated responses. Methods: This cross-sectional study analysed the answers to a sample of pet owners' medical questions. Both a veterinarian and ChatGPT (GPT-4o, May 2024) provided answers, which were anonymised and presented in a survey distributed through mailing lists and public Facebook groups. Participants were asked to assess each response based on structure, quality, and empathy, using a five-point Likert scale. They then had to indicate whether they trusted the response, and which response they preferred. Results: < 0.05), which were rated higher in structure, quality, and empathy. Limitations: This study has several limitations, including a small sample size, reliance on a single veterinarian, and use of only two Reddit-derived scenarios. Response accuracy was not assessed, and word count restrictions may have affected perceived response quality. Additionally, prior research suggests that irrelevant patient details can impact ChatGPT's accuracy, raising questions about user trust if clinical inaccuracies were present. Conclusion: AI-generated responses received higher participant ratings in structure, quality and empathy, suggesting AI may enhance veterinary client communication when used under appropriate professional supervision.

papers.title: Creative entrepreneurship as a socially embedded form of work: a sociological ecology for the platform society
papers.authors: Linchu Rajan, Lekshmi Mohan, Joel George, Ajimon George, Anoop Tom Thomas, Maria Susan Mathew
papers.abstract: Creative entrepreneurship increasingly combines creative production with entrepreneurial, communicative, and platform-mediated work. Existing scholarship has generated important insights into opportunity recognition, innovation, value creation, and creative labor, but these perspectives often examine entrepreneurial activity, social relations, cultural recognition, and platform governance as analytically separate processes. This Perspective develops the Sociological Ecology of Creative Entrepreneurship (SECE), a conceptual framework that positions creative entrepreneurship as socially embedded work within platform society. Drawing on economic sociology, sociology of work, labor process theory, digital sociology, and platform studies, SECE integrates five analytically distinct but relationally connected dimensions: identity construction, relational capital, platform governance, cultural legitimacy, and institutional embeddedness. The framework is presented as a relational and multilevel heuristic rather than a tested causal model. It proposes that creative entrepreneurial practice emerges through interactions among workers, audiences, collaborators, platforms, cultural fields, and institutions. The Perspective further considers how these relations are shaped by power, inequality, and human-AI interaction and identifies directions for empirical research into platform-mediated creative work, occupational sustainability, and changing forms of employment.

papers.title: Beyond diagnostic accuracy: navigating the artificial intelligence data tsunami toward value-based implementation in gastroenterology
papers.authors: Konstantinos A. Ekmektzoglou, Theodore Rokkas
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy has evolved from its early application in simple edge detection to highly sophisticated technologies designed to improve detection of neoplastic and preneoplastic lesions and support clinical decision-making. However, this rapid technological evolution has generated a “ data tsunami ” or “ datanami ”: an overwhelming and continuously expanding volume of information that, frequently, exceeds the ability of clinicians and patients to process, interpret, and apply it effectively. Substantial investments in AI have been driven by expectations of improved efficiency and reduced healthcare costs. Nevertheless, the metrics used to justify the adoption of AI-assisted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain inadequately standardized, leaving the true cost-effectiveness of these technologies uncertain. Current AI research in gastroenterology has primarily focused on improving diagnostic performance rather than evaluating long-term clinical outcomes or economic value. To address this limitation, investigators employ stochastic microsimulation models, which simulate individual patient trajectories and enable more robust assessments of cost-effectiveness. As the field progresses from AI to extended intelligence and, ultimately, intelligent assistance, the role of humans becomes increasingly central. Rather than replacing clinical judgment, AI should augment human expertise, with healthcare professionals serving as the critical link between technological innovation and meaningful clinical benefit. This review examines whether AI applications in GI diseases can be implemented cost-effectively in routine clinical practice for diagnosis and treatment. It further explores the indispensable human dimension of AI adoption, emphasizing accountability, reliability, ethical oversight, and responsible implementation as essential safeguards for current and future clinical applications.

papers.title: Explainable AI for phishing URL detection: a Bayesian-optimized stacking ensemble framework with SHAP-guided feature learning
papers.authors: Hafiz Aziz Khan, Sonia Akter, Abdur Rahman Lindon, Taslima Akter, Iftekhar Rasul, Mamunur Rahman, Nasrin Akter Tohfa, Iftekhar Hossain
papers.abstract: Introduction Phishing remains one of the most persistent and financially damaging threats facing modern organizations, with over 4.7 million incidents recorded in 2023 alone. Existing AI-based phishing detection frameworks are constrained by limited benchmarking scope, absent model interpretability, and insufficient statistical validation — three limitations that collectively restrict operational utility in real-world security environments. Methods We present an explainable, end-to-end machine learning pipeline evaluated on a large public benchmark of 247,950 URLs described by 41 structural and lexical features.
