The pipeline integrates SHAP-driven feature selection (reducing 41 to 24 features via a 95% cumulative-signal rule), a systematic benchmark of 12 classifiers spanning seven algorithmic families, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization via Optuna TPE sampling (40 trials each for XGBoost and CatBoost), and a heterogeneous stacking ensemble combining Optuna-tuned XGBoost, CatBoost, Extra Trees, and Random Forest under a logistic-regression meta-learner. A four-layer statistical validation protocol — comprising a Friedman omnibus test, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, paired t-tests, and Cohen's d effect sizes — was applied to five-fold cross-validation accuracy distributions to assess directional consistency, with the limited inferential resolution of five folds explicitly acknowledged. Results SHAP-driven selection reduced the feature space by 41.5% while retaining 95% of predictive signal. The stacking ensemble achieved 96.75% accuracy, 96.74% F1-score, and AUC of 0.9947, attaining the lowest Brier score among all 13 models (0.0246), indicating superior probability calibration. The Friedman omnibus test confirmed significant performance differences across models (χ 2 F = 59.84, p < 0.0001), and all 12 Wilcoxon pairwise comparisons yielded the minimum attainable p-value ( p = 0.0313), confirming the ensemble never lost a cross-validation fold against any baseline. Post-hoc SHAP analysis identified subdomain structure, URL length, and URL entropy as the dominant phishing indicators at both ensemble and base-learner levels. Discussion The co-leaders — the stacking ensemble and Extra Trees — demonstrate that rigorous, interpretable AI pipelines can advance phishing detection accuracy and transparency simultaneously. The framework's calibrated risk scores, threshold flexibility, and multi-level SHAP explainability support analyst-facing decision-making in security operations, while its leakage-free

papers.title: Loneliness to consumption intention: emotional bonding and escapism in AI emotional companion app use
papers.authors: Pei Yao, Zirong Tian, J. Kim
papers.abstract: With the diffusion of generative AI, AI emotional companion apps have emerged as a new domain of digital consumption in which users may pay to extend relationship-like experiences. This study examines how loneliness and actual-ideal self-discrepancy are associated with experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention through two competing pathways: emotional bonding with the AI (relational compensation) and escapism (avoidant compensation). The emotional bond with the AI is modeled as a second-order construct comprising anthropomorphism, emotional responsiveness, and parasocial intimacy. Data were collected from 393 adult users in China who used AI emotional companion apps at least twice per week and were analyzed using structural equation modeling. Loneliness and actual-ideal self-discrepancy were positively associated with both emotional bonding and escapism. However, significant indirect associations with experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention emerged only through the emotional-bond pathway. Direct comparisons further showed that the relational indirect effects were significantly stronger than the avoidant indirect effects across all antecedent-outcome combinations. Escapism was significantly associated with both outcomes when modeled alone but became nonsignificant when emotional bonding was included, suggesting that its association with consumer responses largely overlaps with the relational pathway. A partial-mediation analysis further showed that actual-ideal self-discrepancy retained a significant direct association with continuance intention. These findings suggest that relational compensation, rather than avoidant compensation, is more closely associated with willingness to pay for experience enhancement and intention to continue using AI companions. The study extends compensatory-use, self-discrepancy, and parasocial-interaction perspectives to the AI-companion context by linking psychological vulnerability to experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention, while highlighting implications for responsible relational design and user protection.

papers.title: Copenhagen Magnetic Personalized Accelerated Brain Circuit Therapy (CoMPACT) trial: study protocol for a randomized, double-blinded, sham-controlled, three-armed, parallel-group trial of transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment-resistant depression
papers.authors: Armita Faghani Jadidi, Iman Ibrahim, Lasse Christiansen, Mikkel Malling Beck, Vytautas Labanauskas, Björn Sigurðsson, Marlene Gomes Antunes, Thomas Thomsen, Simon Hjerrild, Axel Thielscher, Maj Vinberg, Hartwig Roman Siebner, Poul Videbech
papers.abstract: Background: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD), characterized by poor response to conventional antidepressant therapies, remains a major clinical challenge. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) has emerged as a promising alternative. Employing intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS), TMS protocols have yielded rapid antidepressant effects in recent accelerated treatment studies. These findings warrant further investigation in larger samples to confirm efficacy and in-depth investigation into the underlying mechanisms. Moreover, other cortical sites may also represent suitable targets for accelerated iTBS treatment of TRD. Methods: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial will assess the efficacy, feasibility and mechanisms of a novel, personalized, and accelerated iTBS protocol for TRD, targeting two left hemispheric regions, the left dlPFC and inferior parietal lobule (IPL), both characterized by anticorrelated functional connectivity with the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex. 78 adults (aged 18-95 years) will be recruited from Danish mental health centers and randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) active iTBS of the left dlPFC, (2) active iTBS targeting of the left IPL, or (3) sham iTBS at either site. The intervention includes five daily sessions over five consecutive days. Targeting informed by group-level functional connectivity will be combined with individualized coil placement and stimulation dosing using electric field modeling based on whole-brain anatomical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Antidepressant efficacy will be evaluated using the 6-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale as the primary outcome, assessed at an early post-intervention follow-up (F1) within three days after the final stimulation session. Multimodal post-treatment assessments, including MRI, will be conducted within five days after the intervention (T1). A four-week follow-up (T2) will assess the durability of clinical and cognitive outcomes. Neurophysiological mechanisms will be investigated using electroencephalography as well as structural and functional MRI. Discussion: By testing a novel stimulation protocol and evaluating the efficacy of a new parietal target, this study will help advance the development of innovative, circuit-based interventions for TRD, with potential implications for broader applications across neuropsychiatry. Clinical trial registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/, identifier NCT06895863.

papers.title: Physical education and psychosocial vulnerability in adolescent suicide-related risk: a transnational cross-sectional explainable machine-learning analysis of student health survey data
papers.authors: Heyi Liu, Jianbin Guo, Xinwei Ma, Xinwei Ma, Cheng Shi, Xiaoming Ma, Xiaoming Ma, Jingwei Li
papers.abstract: Background: Adolescent suicide attempt is a major public health concern linked to psychosocial distress, school environment, health-risk behaviors, and physical activity patterns. This study aimed to develop an explainable XGBoost model for adolescent suicide-attempt status and to determine whether physical inactivity and low physical education (PE) participation could serve as informative school-based indicators. Methods: Data were obtained from the Global School-based Student Health Survey conducted in Argentina in 2018, Anguilla in 2016, and Jamaica in 2017. The Argentina dataset was used for model training, while Anguilla and Jamaica were combined as an independent validation cohort. The outcome was self-reported suicide attempt during the past 12 months. Candidate predictors included demographic, anthropometric, dietary, psychosocial, violence- and injury-related, tobacco-related, sexual behavior, physical activity, and PE-related variables. An XGBoost model was developed using nested cross-validation, staged hyperparameter tuning, and Bayesian fine-tuning. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). SHAP and partial dependence plots were used for interpretation. Results: A total of 27,710 adolescents were included; 5,165 (18.6%) reported at least one suicide attempt. The final model achieved an independent validation AUC of 0.7928 (95% CI: 0.7790-0.8066). The top 18 SHAP-ranked predictors retained a cumulative 10-fold cross-validated AUC of 0.7865. Loneliness was the most influential predictor, followed by sex, insomnia, early cigarette use, PE days, physical attack, school peer kindness, and physical activity. Physical inactivity and low PE participation showed nonlinear associations with predicted suicide-attempt risk. Conclusions: Loneliness and insomnia represented the psychosocial vulnerability profile, while physical inactivity and limited PE participation emerged as potentially informative school-based indicators requiring further longitudinal investigation. These findings support risk-stratified prevention strategies integrating early psychological identification with inclusive, socially supportive physical activity and PE programs.

papers.title: Self-reported learning-oriented GenAI use under perceived teacher-referenced normative tension in Chinese higher education
papers.authors: Zhenzhen Yang, Yong Yang, WEI LIU
papers.abstract: Objective The educational implications of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) depend not only on whether students use these tools, but also on how they orient their use when acceptable-use expectations remain unsettled. This study examined whether perceived teacher-referenced GenAI normative tension (PNT) was associated with self-reported learning-oriented GenAI use (LOU) and whether LOU remained distinguishable from related academic experiences and learning tendencies in Chinese higher education. Methods Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 1,004 students at three public universities. Covariance-based structural equation modelling was used to evaluate the proposed five-factor measurement representation and a theory-constrained six-path associational model. Internal split-sample measurement analyses, alternative measurement models, covariate-adjusted models, an ordinal-estimator sensitivity analysis, institution sensitivity analyses, a reverse focal specification, and exploratory structural extensions were also conducted. Results The proposed five-factor measurement representation showed close fit and was reproduced in a held-out subsample. The focal PNT–LOU association was positive and statistically significant, while the remaining structural paths positioned LOU within a broader network of related academic experiences and learning tendencies. PNT was positively associated with self-reported LOU (β = 0.568, p < 0.001), and the model explained 32.2% of the variance in LOU. The focal association remained positive after adjustment for GenAI guidance clarity (β = 0.478, p < 0.001), demographic and institutional covariates (β = 0.570, p < 0.001), and use of an ordinal estimator. An observationally equivalent reverse specification produced the same global fit, indicating that temporal direction could not be identified. Exploratory extensions further indicated that the six-path specification did not exhaust the observed covariance structure, particularly for ACS. Conclusion Perceived difficulty locating one’s GenAI practices relative to teacher-referenced expectations and self-reported learning-oriented GenAI use can coexist rather than functioning as opposite ends of a single continuum. However, the cross-sectional, same-source design does not establish that normative tension improves learning-oriented behaviour. Reverse direction, shared unmeasured characteristics, common-method inflation, social desirability, and legitimacy-oriented self-presentation remain plausible explanations.

papers.title: Short-term responses across two sequential plant-based activity sessions: an exploratory fixed-order pilot study
papers.authors: Li-Li Chang, Yun-Hsien Ku, Chuen-Yu Chuang, Yu-Sen Chang
papers.abstract: Background Structured plant-based activities combine natural materials, purposeful manual work, sensory engagement, and social interaction, but direct comparisons of practical formats in community adults remain limited. We characterized short-term responses during two sequential sessions and compared within-session changes. Methods Twenty-five adults participated in a single-group, fixed-order pilot study. Session 1 involved horticultural crafting; 1 week later, Session 2 involved balm crafting followed by horticultural crafting. Twenty-three attended both sessions. DASS-21 and STAI-S were principal outcomes; horticultural wellbeing, HRV, and forehead single-channel EEG were exploratory. Within-session changes and complete-case between-session differences were estimated with 95% CIs. Post hoc TOST examined exploratory equivalence bounds. Results Both sessions were followed by favorable short-term psychological changes. DASS-21 scores decreased by 8.57 points in Session 1 [95% CI (5.41, 11.72), n = 23] and 5.53 in Session 2 [(2.65, 8.41), n = 17]. STAI-S scores decreased by 7.30 points in Session 1 [(5.23, 9.37), n = 25] and 6.86 in Session 2 [(4.07, 9.66), n = 22]; all four Holm-adjusted p values were <0.001. Complete-case comparisons showed no statistically detectable between-session difference in DASS-21 improvement [3.12 points, 95% CI (−1.51, 7.75)] or STAI-S improvement [0.34 points, (−3.15, 3.83)]. STAI-S changes met the exploratory TOST criterion only at the broad ±0.50 standardized bound. Horticultural wellbeing improved in both sessions; SDNN and RMSSD increased, whereas EEG findings did not remain significant after multiplicity correction. Conclusion Both sessions were associated with favorable short-term psychological changes, particularly reduced distress and state anxiety. These findings support the feasibility and potential value of brief, hands-on plant-based activities in community settings and provide estimates for larger randomized, counterbalanced trials. Given the fixed order and absence of a control group, the findings are preliminary rather than definitive causal or modality-specific evidence.

papers.title: Generative AI in creative education: baseline-linked evidence on learning processes, artistic performance, and authorship
papers.authors: Ningtao Shen, Lai Soon Lee, Aneng He
papers.abstract: Introduction: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly shaping creative learning in higher education art courses, yet its educational value remains contested when creative support, output generation, authorship, and skill development become intertwined. This study investigates AI-supported creative learning in an undergraduate art course. Methods: The study used linked data from 133 students, including prior course performance, final creative-performance assessment, and post-project questionnaire responses. AI use was operationalized through two dimensions: assistive use for ideation, refinement, process management, and technique learning, and content-generative use involving AI contributions to creative output. The analysis combined baseline-adjusted outcome models, performance-change models, propensity-score adjustment, AI-use intensity comparisons, and robustness checks across alternative AI-use definitions. Results: The findings show a clear process-outcome decoupling pattern. AI use was associated with stronger perceived support and skill transfer, while final artistic performance and baseline-to-final performance change showed no corresponding improvement. Content-generative AI use was associated with lower evaluated authorship, suggesting that AI-shaped artifacts may reduce the visibility of students' creative decision-making in final outcomes. Discussion: The study contributes a differentiated account of AI in creative education and argues that responsible AI integration should focus on how students use, document, justify, and reflect on AI within the creative process.

papers.title: Contemporary AI attitude scale research: a systematic mapping review and bibliometric analysis
papers.authors: Yusuf Ziya Olpak
papers.abstract: Introduction: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) has been accompanied by growing efforts to measure individuals' attitudes toward these technologies. However, existing AI attitude scales vary considerably in their theoretical foundations, dimensional structures, target populations, and application contexts, raising questions about the extent to which they represent equivalent conceptualizations of the construct. Methods: This systematic mapping review examined contemporary AI attitude scale research and mapped its thematic, intellectual, methodological, and conceptual structure. A predefined Web of Science Core Collection search identified 298 eligible AI-related psychometric scale studies published between 2022 and June 2026; within this corpus, AI attitude was the most frequently represented construct, with 51 studies forming the final analytic sample. The review integrated descriptive and conceptual synthesis with bibliometric mapping analyses, including author keyword and abstract-term co-occurrence, co-citation, and bibliographic coupling. Results: The findings showed that scale development and psychometric evaluation constitute prominent methodological themes in the literature. Co-citation analysis linked the broader technology-acceptance tradition with AI-specific approaches to attitude measurement, while bibliographic coupling revealed four interconnected contemporary research fronts involving scale refinement and contextual extension, education and generative AI, population- and domain-specific measurement, and cross-cultural validation around established scale families. Despite these overlapping knowledge bases, substantial conceptual heterogeneity was evident across instruments, including unidimensional, positive-negative, cognitive-affective-behavioral, functional, ethical, and domain-specific multidimensional conceptualizations. Discussion: Overall, the findings indicate that bibliographic and methodological commonality has not produced conceptual uniformity in AI attitude measurement. Future research should therefore prioritize explicit construct definition, conceptual fit between instruments and research purposes, measurement invariance, cross-cultural validation, and cumulative evaluation of established measures rather than assuming equivalence across scales carrying the same construct label.

papers.title: Body image and maladaptive eating behaviors in Chinese early adolescents: a latent profile analysis
papers.authors: Chungan ZHANG, Yichu Han, Shuhua Cheng, Yuqian Qi
papers.abstract: Background Body image undergoes significant changes during early adolescence, yet empirical evidence on how the combination of negative and positive body image in this stage relates to maladaptive eating behaviors remains limited. To address this, employing a person-centered approach, this study aimed to identify distinct profiles of body image and to explore the relationships between profile membership, gender, body mass index (BMI), socioeconomic status (SES), and maladaptive eating behaviors among Chinese early adolescents. Methods Using indicators from three dimensions of positive body image (i.e., body self-appreciation, body other-appreciation, resilience against negative appearance feedback) and negative body image (i.e., body dissatisfaction), latent profile analysis (LPA) was conducted with a sample of 1,248 junior high school students (aged 12–15 years, M = 13.42, SD = 1.03; 50.4% boys) from Heilongjiang Province, China. Results Three distinct body image profiles were identified: the Positive Body Image Group (66.59%), the Body Other-Appreciation Dominant Group (23.88%), and the Moderate Body Image Group (9.54%). Gender and BMI significantly predicted profile membership, whereas SES did not. Regarding maladaptive eating behaviors, both the Body Other-Appreciation Dominant Group and the Moderate Body Image Group reported significantly higher levels of restrained eating than the Positive Body Image Group. The Moderate Body Image Group also reported significantly higher levels of emotional eating compared with the Positive Body Image Group. No significant differences were found in external eating among the three profiles. Conclusion Early adolescents' body image profiles exhibit significant heterogeneity, with distinct patterns of association with maladaptive eating behaviors across profiles. Accordingly, interventions should consider gender and body mass index and be tailored to the characteristics of each profile to improve body image and eating behaviors.

papers.title: An explainable machine learning model based on multidimensional task-state electroencephalography for identifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbid developmental dyslexia
papers.authors: Keduo Huang, Pengxiang Zuo, Xuemei Luo, Chun Ji, Fang Yang, Yuhao Huang, Xiaole Wang
papers.abstract: Background: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and developmental dyslexia (DD) are highly comorbid, yet objective differentiation from individual disorders remains challenging due to the lack of neurophysiological biomarkers. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model leveraging multidimensional task-state EEG features to distinguish ADHD-DD comorbidity from ADHD and typical development (TD). Methods: Ninety children (27 ADHD-DD, 40 ADHD, 23 TD) underwent EEG during a VSWM task. Five feature categories were extracted: event-related potentials, time-frequency characteristics, functional connectivity, graph-theoretic metrics, and nonlinear dynamics. Three feature-processing strategies and nine classifiers were compared within a nested cross-validation framework. Feature contribution was quantified by coefficient back-projection of the optimal PCA-LR mode. Sensitivity and permutation analyses were performed. Results: The PCA-LR model achieved a balanced accuracy of 80.5%, a Macro-F1 of 0.799, and a Macro-AUC of 0.912. Class-wise AUCs were 0.905 for ADHD-DD, 0.904 for ADHD, and 0.927 for TD. Left temporal α-band functional connectivity was a shared high-contribution feature in both disorder groups. ADHD-DD was distinguished by widely distributed cross-regional connectivity spanning θ and α bands and by P200 amplitude. ADHD was characterized primarily by α-band network metrics and α-ERD, whereas TD relied mainly on θ and α bands functional connectivity and graph-theoretic metrics. Conclusion: Our findings suggest that multidimensional task-state EEG features may help differentiate children with ADHD-DD comorbidity from those with ADHD or typical development. They also indicate that machine-learning approaches may be useful for identifying neurodevelopmental comorbid conditions.

papers.title: Co-creating point-of-care ultrasound education for family medicine in Ethiopia: reflections on pedagogy, faculty development, and academic partnership
papers.authors: Bilal Negash, Leila Makhani, Jamie Rodas, Eden Habtemariam, Praseedha Janakiram, Michael Bartucci
papers.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly becoming an essential clinical and educational tool in low to middle income countries (LMICs), where formal imaging is often delayed or inaccessible. This commentary reflects on the co-creation and longitudinal implementation of a Family Medicine-focused point-of-care ultrasound education initiative at Addis Ababa University (AAU), developed through the Toronto Addis Ababa Academic Collaboration in Family Medicine (TAAAC-FM). We discuss how this initiative, while addressing an immediate diagnostic need, also functions as a curricular lever for faculty development, a pathway for professional identity formation, and can foster unique pathways for ongoing departmental sustainability. We discuss the partnership structures and equity considerations that shaped program design and situate this work within broader efforts to strengthen Primary Health Care (PHC) and advance Universal Health Coverage (UHC). These reflections offer transferable insight for academic collaborations seeking to align educational innovation with health system transformation in resource-constrained settings.

papers.title: Refining teachers’ ethical knowledge in smart learning environments - a Delphi study within the TPCEK framework
papers.authors: Huihui Wu, Vishalache Balakrishnan
papers.abstract: Smart Learning Environments (SLEs) increasingly integrate artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies, creating new ethical demands for teachers’ professional knowledge. This study employed a three-round Delphi design to refine the definitions and conceptual boundaries of eight predefined ethics-related dimensions of the Technological Pedagogical Content Ethical Knowledge (TPCEK) framework for preservice preschool teachers in SLEs. Twenty experts evaluated the dimensions in terms of necessity, definitional clarity, contextual appropriateness, and conceptual distinctiveness. Quantitative evaluations were integrated with qualitative feedback to guide iterative refinement. All eight dimensions met the predefined necessity criterion. Round 1 identified conceptual ambiguity primarily in Content Ethical Knowledge, Technological Pedagogical Ethical Knowledge, Technological Content Ethical Knowledge (TCEK), and Pedagogical Content Ethical Knowledge (PCEK). Following revision, remaining concerns centred on the distinctiveness of TCEK and PCEK. Further refinement resulted in both dimensions meeting the predefined criteria in Round 3. The final definitions more clearly distinguish ethical issues associated with educational content, pedagogical technology use, technological mediation of content, and pedagogical transformation of content. The refined definitions provide a foundation for future empirical research and ethics-focused preservice teacher education.

papers.title: Teachers’ use of generative artificial intelligence in K–12 education: a systematic review
papers.authors: Oğuz Cincioğlu, Duygu Mutlu Bayraktar, Tuğba Altan
papers.abstract: Background The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has created new opportunities and challenges for teachers, leading to a growing body of research on its educational applications. AI has become increasingly integrated into instructional processes, supporting teachers in tasks such as lesson planning, assessment, feedback generation, content creation, and classroom support. Despite the rapidly increasing number of studies on AI in education, the literature on teachers’ use of GenAI is distributed across different contexts, methodologies, and theoretical perspectives. Therefore, this systematic review aims to provide a comprehensive synthesis of research on teachers’ use of GenAI in Pre-12 and K-12 education. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, studies were screened and selected based upon the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in 79 empirical studies included in the final analysis. The analysis examined methodological trends, AI and GenAI technologies, functional and pedagogical roles, theoretical foundations, and key research focuses related to teachers’ use of GenAI. Results The findings indicate a sharp increase in research output, particularly in recent years, with Asia as the most productive region. Qualitative and mixed-methods designs dominated the literature, while language education and STEM were the most frequently represented domains. Large language models emerged as the dominant GenAI type. Instructional design and co-planning represented some of the most prominent functional roles, highlighting a strong emphasis on teachers’ preparatory practices. The focal point of studies was on cognitive, affective, and pedagogical constructs, with technology acceptance frameworks such as Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) being most frequently employed. Conclusions Overall, the findings reveal that GenAI is primarily positioned as a collaborative tool that supports teachers’ professional practice, particularly in instructional design and preparation, rather than replacing instructional roles. The review identifies key trends, gaps, and directions for future research on AI integration in education.

papers.title: Associations of metacognition, self-directed learning ability, and AI literacy with academic achievement among university students predominantly enrolled in health-related majors: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Han-Mook Choi, Ha-Kyeong Jo, Young-Hun Kim, Jung-Hee Park
papers.abstract: The expanding integration of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has heightened the need to identify learner competencies associated with academic achievement. This study examined the associations of metacognition, self-directed learning ability, and AI literacy with self-reported academic achievement among university students in the Republic of Korea. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted with 175 undergraduates from 11 universities between September 30 and November 1, 2025; 78.3% were enrolled in health-related majors. Metacognition, self-directed learning ability, and AI literacy were measured using the SMI, SDLI, and MAILS, respectively; academic achievement was measured as self-reported cumulative GPA on a 4.5-point scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, Pearson correlations, and hierarchical multiple regression with HC3 heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors. GPA differed by age, school life satisfaction, and AI-related course experience in unadjusted comparisons. Metacognition (r = .348, p < .001) and self-directed learning ability (r = .377, p < .001) were positively correlated with GPA, whereas AI literacy was not (r = .105, p = .167). In the adjusted six-predictor model, age ( β = .151, p = .023), AI-related course experience ( β = .145, p = .040), and self-directed learning ability ( β = .329, p = .023) were independently associated with GPA; metacognition and AI literacy were not. The model explained 20.0% of the variance (adjusted R 2 = .171). These findings identify self-directed learning ability as the only examined learner competency that remained significantly associated with GPA after adjustment. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed before causal or mediational conclusions can be drawn.

papers.title: A proof-of-concept EEG study of responses to peer speech in collaborative learning
papers.authors: Chihiro Minami, Hiroki Watanabe, Yasushi Naruse, Yusuke Morita
papers.abstract: Background This study focused on internal aspects, including cognitive states and motivational engagement, that may be overlooked by external indicators of participation in collaborative learning, such as utterance counts or observable behaviors. This proof-of-concept feasibility study explored whether neurophysiological responses related to auditory attention could provide information relevant to interpreting conventional behavioral indicators of participation. Using electroencephalogram (EEG) indices (N1 and P2 components), associations with self-regulated learning and interest during collaborative learning were explored. Methods EEG data were collected during real, discussion-based collaborative learning activities conducted in a university classroom setting. EEG data were recorded using wearable devices from nine Japanese university students enrolled in the course. Utterances were categorized as surface- or deep-level regulation utterances according to definitions from a prior study. Using a multivariate temporal response function approach, the N1 and P2 amplitudes elicited by each type of utterance were estimated. The degree of self-regulated learning was indexed by the number of deep-level regulation utterances, and interest in learning was evaluated using subjective rating scores. The relationships between these indices and the N1 and P2 amplitudes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Results The number of deep-level regulation utterances was significantly associated with the N1 amplitude, irrespective of whether the utterances were categorized as deep or surface regulation. In contrast, subjective interest ratings were significantly associated with the N1 amplitude, particularly in response to deep-level-regulation utterances. Conclusion The N1 component, which is related to auditory attention, showed exploratory associations with self-regulatory behavior and learners’ interest.

papers.title: A multilevel living lab using a digital-twin-based modelling environment for sustainability education and decision support
papers.authors: Dace Paule, Jeļena Pubule, Undine Gabranova, Andra Blumberga, Dagnija Blumberga
papers.abstract: Sustainability education increasingly requires learning environments that connect systems understanding with real-world decision-making. This study examines the integration of a district-heating digital-twin-based modelling environment into a multilevel living-lab process at Riga Technical University, Latvia. An exploratory mixed-method case study was conducted over 13 months and involved 24 professionals in the co-creation stage, 196 undergraduate students working in 98 pairs, 30 master's students working in 15 pairs, and eight external stakeholders. Data included World Café outputs, 294 undergraduate scenario responses, modelling-environment simulation outputs, master's student multi-criteria decision analyses, and stakeholder evaluations. Quantitative scenario outputs were examined in relation to emissions, costs, and system performance, while participant-produced materials were analysed to identify patterns in systems reasoning, trade-off recognition, and decision priorities. Undergraduate students used the modelling environment to explore relationships between technical parameters and environmental and economic outcomes. At the master's level, 12 of the 15 groups (80%) prioritised environmental performance when selecting their preferred scenarios, whereas external stakeholders assigned greater priority to investment cost and practical feasibility. This divergence suggests that the modelling environment may help make competing decision priorities visible and support structured discussion between learner and practitioner groups. The study is limited by its single-institution design, absence of a control group and pre-test/post-test learning assessment, limited stakeholder sample, and reliance on participant-produced work. The findings therefore provide preliminary case-based evidence of the educational and decision-support potential of digital-twin-supported living labs rather than evidence of general effectiveness.

papers.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on the quality of legal education in the UAE: a critical analysis of legal, pedagogical, and ethical considerations
papers.authors: Mohamed Morsi Abdou, Farouq Saber Al-Shibli, Saleh Al Shraideh, Mohammed NourEldeen Sayed, Okba Kazar
papers.abstract: The adequate application of artificial intelligence (AI) technology in legal education in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has been barely covered by scholarly literature, especially, from the perspectives of legal and educational sciences. The current paper attempts to fill in an existing gap in literature about the appropriate usage of AI in legal education. The research is intended to help curriculum designers in UAE universities to improve undergraduate legal education programs using innovative AI systems and, thus, to provide UAE policy makers with the academic and ethical standards for the use of AI in legal education. The current paper critically discusses the possible contribution of AI systems in the improvement of the quality of legal education. Moreover, the research analyzes the probable implications of using AI in law curricula for the learning process and for the development of critical legal skills in UAE law students, stressing on the importance of ensuring academic integrity. Furthermore, the current research uses a qualitative approach to analyze the legal, educational, pedagogical, and ethical aspects of AI integration into legal education in the UAE and suggests a legal-pedagogical model of its responsible integration. The goal of the analysis is to determine what opportunities may be offered by AI systems in improving the quality of legal education in the UAE and to discuss their ability to educate students to perform independent legal practice. The discussion focuses on four main areas: (i) the quality of legal education in the UAE’s legal context; (ii) understanding of the AI-enabled legal education systems; (iii) identifying the educational and ethical risks of using AI in legal education; and (iv) setting the standards for the responsible use of AI in legal education. To conclude, the article argues that the adequate use of AI can improve significantly the quality of legal education, if appropriate ethical and academic standards will be developed to ensure the integrity of the process and to develop legal competencies of the students.

papers.title: ARAM: a threshold model for understanding occupant acceptance of architectural robot adaptations
papers.authors: Alex Binh Vinh Duc Nguyen, Rania Christoforou, Ilaria Pigliautile, Verônica Martins Gnecco, Anja Pogladič, Sara Arko, Anna Laura Pisello, Davide Schaumann, Marcel Schweiker, Andrew Vande Moere
papers.abstract: Physical interior elements are increasingly becoming roboticised to support occupant needs. Partitions, ceilings, and furniture can now physically and autonomously change shape or move to architecturally “adapt” indoor spaces, with the aim of improving occupant comfort, satisfaction, and wellbeing. However, occupants sometimes reject these adaptations when they are perceived as disruptive, unpredictable, or difficult to control. Motivated by the goal of making architectural robots more acceptable, we involved an interdisciplinary team of experts in human-building interaction, human-robot interaction, psychology, anthropology, and human comfort to qualitatively re-analyze how occupants accepted adaptations across three previous studies on robotic partitions. We found that an occupant tended to accept an adaptation when they recognized a personal need that the architectural robot was capable of addressing in a socially justifiable way. Accordingly, we developed the Architectural Robot Acceptance Model (ARAM), in which three qualitative thresholds along a continuum of perceived stress severity define four distinct acceptance responses to a specific adaptation. As the positions of these thresholds may vary across occupants and situations, ARAM supports testable estimates of how an occupant may respond to different appraisal states of personal need, adaptation capability, and social justification. Because architectural robot adaptations may simultaneously be experienced as robotic behaviors, building automation, and socially situated environmental adjustments, ARAM is particularly relevant to individual adaptations that enter occupants' spatial experience and may affect co-located others. We then discuss how the model can inform situated estimates of occupant acceptance of architectural robot adaptations, and outline how its broader relevance to other robotic, automated, intelligent, and smart technologies embedded in the built environment may be evaluated in future work.

papers.title: A digital tutor; artificial intelligence as an aid among undergraduate medical students
papers.authors: Anas Bin Tariq, Iqra Bukhari, Aqsa Khan, Arshia Shaheen, Saba Khan, Syeda Urooj Zehra
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate student’s perceived effectiveness in the use of AI as digital tutors in supporting them for studies. Material and methods This cross-sectional analytical study was done at Al-Tibri Medical College, Isra University, Karachi, Pakistan. Using purposive sampling, 315 students consented to participate in the study. After ethical approval, a questionnaire was designed and pilot tested before being distributed to the students. There were total of six sections of the questionnaire. The quantitative data was tested using SPSS v23.0. Students responded to Likert scale which was subjected to ordinal and interval data analysis both for better presentation of results. Open ended questions which were subjected to thematic analysis using Braun and Clarke six-steps for thematic analysis. Results and Discussion The study found that undergraduate medical students widely use and positively perceive AI tools, particularly for understanding complex topics, exam preparation, and solving MCQs. ChatGPT was the most frequently used platform. Students appreciated AI for its efficiency and academic support, though some noted concerns about misinformation and over-dependence. Significant differences in perceptions were observed across years, with senior students reporting greater benefits. Overall, AI was seen as a valuable supplement to medical education. Conclusion Artificial Intelligence tools, were widely used and positively perceived by undergraduate medical students as effective aids in learning, though concerns about over-reliance and misinformation highlighted the need for guided integration into medical education. Bangladesh Journal of Medical Science Vol. 25 No. 04 October’26 Page: 1115-1123

papers.title: When AI becomes an intellectual intermediary: A situated correspondence framework linking epistemic responsibility, intellectual engagement, and independent capability in higher education
papers.authors: Mario Guadalupe López Ayala, Israel Osuna-Flores
papers.journal: Revista Científica Arbitrada de la Fundación MenteClara
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has unsettled a familiar educational inference: that the quality of an academic product is adequate evidence of the intellectual work performed by the student who submits it. This conceptual article develops the Situated Correspondence Framework, an analytical architecture that connects three moments often treated separately: the intellectual operations a task assigns to the learner, evidence that those operations were enacted during AI-mediated activity, and the capabilities that remain demonstrable when assistance conditions change. The framework distinguishes Assigned Epistemic Responsibility (AER) and Constitutive Intellectual Operations (CIO) from Enacted Intellectual Engagement (EIE), AI-Assisted Performance (AIP), and Demonstrated Independent Capability (DIC), while treating AI Assistance Configuration (AIC) and Situated Opportunity Conditions (SOC) as proximal interpretive conditions rather than learner attributes. Drawing on research on cognitive offloading, human–technology partnership, evaluative judgement, assessment validity, AI literacy, and educational capability, six propositions are formulated for empirical challenge. The contribution is not a new label for offloading, engagement, or independent performance. It lies in linking ex ante intellectual responsibility to observed enactment and later demonstrability without assuming that assisted performance and learner capability coincide. This evidentiary layer extends a broader human-centered learning agenda while leaving open a question that cannot be settled in the abstract: which operations should remain attributable to the learner across different disciplines and assessment purposes?

papers.title: PELATIHAN PEMANFAATAN WAYGROUND BERBASIS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE UNTUK MENYUSUN MEDIA PEMBELAJARAN BAGI GURU MADRASAH ALIYAH
papers.authors: Reni Oktaviani, Siti Ansoriyah, Muhamad Fajar Rizkia, Selly Oktarini
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Pemanfaatan Wayground berbasis artificial intelligence untuk menyusun media pembelajaran ini dapat meningkatkan keterampilan guru dalam penguasaan teknologi informasi dan komunikasi. Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk melatih pemanfaatan Wayground berbasis artificial intelligence untuk menyusun media pembelajaran bagi guru Madrasah Aliyah di Banten. Pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini menggunakan metode demonstrasi. Kegiatan pengabdian masyarakat ini melibatkan guru sebanyak 16 orang di Cilegon, Banten. Evaluasi berdasarkan pemanfaatan Wayground berbasis artificial intelligence. Hasil pengabdian ini meliputi menyusun media pembelajaran sebesar 100%, pemahaman pemanfaatan Wayground berbasis artificial intelligence dalam menyusun media pembelajaran sebesar 100%, menyusun media pembelajaran dengan pemanfaatan Wayground berbasis artificial intelligence dengan ketercapaian 100%, penyusunan media pembelajaran melalui pemanfaatan Wayground berbasis artificial intelligence secara mandiri dengan presentasi ketercapaian 91%, dan penggunaan Wayground berbasis artificial intelligence dalam menyusun media pembelajaran di kelas sebesar 87%. Penyusunan media pembelajaran dengan memanfaatkan Wayground berbasis artificial intelligence yang inovatif dan kreatif yang dilakukan oleh guru agar tujuan pembelajaran dapat tercapai.Abstract: The use of artificial intelligence-based Wayground to develop instructional materials can enhance teachers’ skills in information and communication technology. This community service project aims to train Madrasah Aliyah teachers in Banten on how to use artificial intelligence-based Wayground to develop instructional materials. This community service project employs a demonstration method. This community service activity involved 16 teachers in Cilegon, Banten. The evaluation was based on the use of the artificial intelligence-based Wayground platform. The results of this service project include the development of learning materials at 100%, an understanding of how to use the AI-based Wayground platform to develop learning materials at 100%, and the development of learning materials using the AI-based Wayground platform with 100% achievement, The development of instructional materials through the independent use of the artificial intelligence-based Wayground platform, with a 91% achievement rate, and the use of the artificial intelligence-based Wayground platform in developing instructional materials in the classroom at a rate of 87%. Teachers developed instructional materials using the innovative and creative artificial intelligence-based Wayground platform to ensure that learning objectives were met.

papers.title: OPTIMALISASI PENGGUNAAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE UNTUK MENDUKUNG PERANCANGAN PEMBELAJARAN INOVATIF BAGI GURU SMA
papers.authors: Sri Suryanti, Dian Savitri, Ayunin Sofro, Muhammad Husnul Khuluq, Vita Eka Hainis, Vita Chamelia Sofiatul Ula
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Keterbatasan guru dalam mengintegrasikan Artificial Intelligence (AI) secara pedagogis, kritis, dan etis masih menjadi kendala dalam perancangan pembelajaran inovatif. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan meningkatkan kompetensi guru SMA dalam memanfaatkan AI untuk menyusun perangkat pembelajaran. Program dilaksanakan melalui pelatihan, workshop, praktik langsung, dan pendampingan terstruktur kepada 35 guru SMA di Kabupaten Jombang. Evaluasi dilakukan melalui pretest–posttest, penilaian produk, observasi keterlibatan, dan refleksi peserta. Dari 35 peserta, 22 peserta memiliki data pretest–posttest lengkap dan digunakan dalam analisis evaluasi berpasangan. Hasil menunjukkan rata-rata skor pengetahuan meningkat dari 97,50 menjadi 99,09 atau sebesar 1,59 poin. Indeks persepsi kompetensi meningkat dari 79,66% menjadi 87,84%, atau sebesar 8,18 poin persentase. Peningkatan tertinggi terjadi pada kemampuan menyusun prompt efektif, dari 73,86% menjadi 86,36% atau meningkat 12,50 poin persentase. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa program memperkuat kompetensi guru dalam merancang perangkat pembelajaran berbantuan AI secara kontekstual, kritis, dan bertanggung jawab.Abstract: Teachers' limited ability to integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) in a pedagogical, critical, and ethical manner remains a challenge in designing innovative instruction. This community service initiative aimed to enhance the competence of high school teachers in utilising AI to develop instructional materials. The intervention was delivered through training, workshops, practical exercises, and mentorship to 35 high school teachers from Jombang Regency. The evaluation was carried out via the use of pre-tests and post-tests, product evaluation, engagement observation, and reflection of participants. Out of 35 participants, 22 had full pre- and post-test data for the paired evaluation analysis. From the data obtained, there has been an increase in the mean knowledge score from 97.50 to 99.09, which is a total increase of 1.59. The competence index increased from 79.66% to 87.84%, which is an increase of 8.18%. The biggest increase was seen in the creation of good prompts where the score increased from 73.86% to 86.36%, which is an increase of 12.50%. From all the above information, it can be concluded that the program improved the competence of teachers in creating AI-assisted instructional materials.

papers.title: GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE EDUCATIONAL FUNCTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION: A SOCIOLOGY OF EDUCATION PERSPECTIVE
papers.authors: Fitriani Fitriani
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Studi mengenai Generative AI di pendidikan tinggi lebih banyak mengkaji aspek teknologi, pedagogi, dan etika, sementara implikasinya terhadap fungsi-fungsi sosial pendidikan belum banyak menjadi fokus penelitian. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mensintesiskan peran Generative AI dalam pelaksanaan fungsi-fungsi sosial pendidikan di perguruan tinggi berdasarkan perspektif Talcott Parsons. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan Integrative Literature Review dengan menganalisis artikel peer-reviewed yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2023–2026. Teknik analisis menggunakan thematic synthesis melalui tahapan data extraction, coding, categorization, comparison, dan theme development untuk mengidentifikasi pola, persamaan, perbedaan, dan kesenjangan temuan antarstudi. Hasil sintesis menunjukkan bahwa Generative AI berperan dalam dua fungsi utama pendidikan, yaitu fungsi sosialisasi dan fungsi alokasi peran. Pada fungsi sosialisasi, Generative AI berkontribusi dalam memperluas akses terhadap pengetahuan, mendukung pembelajaran yang dipersonalisasi, memperkuat literasi AI dan literasi digital, serta mentransformasikan praktik akademik dan proses internalisasi nilai-nilai akademik. Sementara itu, pada fungsi alokasi peran, Generative AI berkontribusi terhadap pengembangan kompetensi digital, penguatan kemampuan berpikir kritis, pengembangan literasi AI sebagai kompetensi profesional, serta peningkatan kesiapan mahasiswa menghadapi pasar kerja yang semakin terdigitalisasi.Abstract: Studies on Generative AI in higher education primarily examine aspects of technology, pedagogy, and ethics, while its implications for the social functions of education have not yet been a major focus of research. This study aims to synthesize the role of Generative AI in the implementation of social functions of education in higher education based on the perspective of Talcott Parsons. The research uses an Integrative Literature Review approach by analyzing peer-reviewed articles published in the period 2023–2026. The analysis technique uses thematic synthesis through the stages of data extraction, coding, categorization, comparison, and theme development to identify patterns, similarities, differences, and gaps in findings across studies. The synthesis results show that Generative AI plays a role in two main educational functions, namely the socialization function and the role allocation function. In the socialization function, Generative AI contributes to expanding access to knowledge, supporting personalized learning, strengthening AI and digital literacy, and transforming academic practices and the internalization of academic values. Meanwhile, in the role allocation function, Generative AI contributes to the development of digital competencies, strengthening critical thinking skills, developing AI literacy as a professional competency, and enhancing students' readiness to face an increasingly digitalized job market.

papers.title: STORY-HEALING: PENINGKATAN KEMAMPUAN PENULISAN CREATIVE WRITING BERBASIS AI SEBAGAI MEDIA KATARSIS PSIKOLOGIS BAGI SISWA SEKOLAH MENENGAH ATAS
papers.authors: Muchammad Sofyan Firmansyah, Syaefani Arif Romadhon, Ahmad Fadil
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Program Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat ini dilatarbelakangi oleh terbatasnya media katarsis emosional, tingginya foreign language writing anxiety, dan rendahnya literasi pemanfaatan Generative AI secara etis di Sekolah Menengah Atas. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan kemampuan menulis kreatif berbahasa Inggris sekaligus menyediakan media ekspresi emosional melalui pendekatan AI-Augmented Narrative Writing. Metode yang digunakan meliputi asesmen kebutuhan, psikoedukasi, workshop, praktik interactive prompting, pendampingan penulisan, kurasi karya, serta evaluasi menggunakan instrumen DASS-21, SLWAI, dan kuesioner literasi AI sebanyak 48 pertanyaan. Mitra kegiatan adalah 35 siswa sekolah menengah atas, sedangkan 26 siswa mengikuti program hingga selesai. Hasil menunjukkan penurunan distres emosional sebesar 54,4%, penurunan kecemasan menulis bahasa asing sebesar 58,9%, dan peningkatan literasi prompting AI sebesar 122,8%. Selain itu, sebanyak 26 karya puisi dan prosa berbahasa Inggris berhasil diterbitkan dalam e-antologi ber-ISBN dan HKI sebagai luaran literasi sekolah.Abstract: This community service program addressed the limited availability of emotional catharsis media, high foreign language writing anxiety, and inadequate ethical use of Generative AI among students at senior high school. The program aimed to improve English creative writing skills while providing a constructive medium for emotional expression through the AI-Augmented Narrative Writing approach. The implementation included needs assessment, psychoeducation, workshops, interactive prompting practice, writing mentoring, manuscript curation, and evaluation using the DASS-21, SLWAI, and AI literacy questionnaires contained 48 questions. The partner was 35 students, with 26 participants completing the entire program. The outcomes showed a 54.4% reduction in emotional distress, a 58.9% decrease in foreign language writing anxiety, and a 122.8% improvement in AI prompting literacy. In addition, 26 original English poems and short prose works were compiled and published as an ISBN-registered and copyrighted digital anthology.

papers.title: PENINGKATAN LITERASI KARIER PADA ERA ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE MELALUI WEBINAR NASIONAL BAGI SISWA SMA
papers.authors: Feliks Prasepta Sejahtera Surbakti
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Pemilihan program studi dan perencanaan karier menjadi semakin menantang seiring pesatnya perkembangan AI dan perubahan kebutuhan dunia kerja. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan literasi siswa SMA mengenai pemilihan program studi dan perencanaan karier melalui webinar nasional "Menentukan Arah Studi dan Karier". Kegiatan dilaksanakan secara daring menggunakan metode edukasi interaktif melalui ceramah dan diskusi, dengan melibatkan narasumber dari kalangan akademisi, praktisi industri, dan profesional. Sebanyak 118 siswa kelas XI dan XII dari berbagai sekolah di Indonesia mengikuti kegiatan ini. Efektivitas kegiatan dievaluasi menggunakan metode pre-test, post-test, masing-masing terdiri dari 8 pertanyaan, dan survei kepuasan peserta. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa nilai rata-rata peserta meningkat dari 62 pada pre-test menjadi 84 pada post-test atau meningkat sebesar 22 poin (35,5%). Selain itu, 91% peserta menyatakan puas terhadap materi dan pelaksanaan webinar. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa webinar mampu meningkatkan pemahaman siswa mengenai hubungan antara potensi diri, pemilihan program studi, perkembangan AI, dan prospek karier masa depan. Kegiatan ini meningkatkan literasi karier siswa melalui integrasi perspektif akademik, industri, dan teknologi.Abstract: Choosing a university major and planning a career are becoming increasingly challenging amid the rapid development of AI and changing workforce demands. This community service activity aimed to improve high school students’ literacy regarding university major selection and career planning through a national webinar entitled “Determining Study and Career Directions.” The activity was conducted online using an interactive educational approach through lectures and discussions, involving speakers from academia, industry, and professional backgrounds. A total of 118 Grade 11 and 12 students from various schools across Indonesia participated in the activity. The effectiveness of the activity was evaluated using pre-test and post-test methods, each consisting of 8 questions, as well as a participant satisfaction survey. The evaluation results showed that the participants’ average score increased from 62 on the pre-test to 84 on the post-test, representing an increase of 22 points (35.5%). In addition, 91% of participants expressed satisfaction with the webinar content and implementation. These results indicate that the webinar improved students’ understanding of the relationship between their personal potential, university major selection, AI developments, and future career prospects. This activity enhanced students’ career literacy by integrating academic, industry, and technological perspectives.

papers.title: AI/Robotic Awareness, Job-Related Technology Anxiety, and Turnover Intention among Hotel Employees in Dhangadhi City, Sudurpaschim Province, Nepal
papers.authors: Ravindra Pariyar, Ghanshyam Bhatta, Hem Raj Joshi
papers.abstract: Background: In South Asia, the introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic technologies in hospitality organizations has created heightened job uncertainty among frontline hotel workers. How AI/robotic awareness, technology-induced anxiety, and turnover intention relate to one another remains unexamined in the peripheral hospitality markets of Sudurpaschim Province, Nepal. Methods: A cross-sectional survey of 218 hotel workers in Dhangadhi City used a 26-item instrument with mixed 5-point and 7-point Likert scales, including reverse-coded items. Hierarchical OLS regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis (5,000 resamples) were conducted. Results: AI/robotic awareness had a significantly negative direct effect on turnover intention (β = −0.465, p < .001). Unexpectedly, AI awareness was positively linked to technology anxiety (β = +0.271, p < .001), and anxiety increased turnover intention (β = +0.597, p < .001). The bootstrapped indirect effect (+0.162, 95% BC-a CI [0.080, 0.254]) indicates an inconsistent-mediation (suppression) pattern. Perceived organizational support negatively predicted turnover intention (β = −0.265, p < .001) and competitive psychological climate positively predicted it (β = 0.207, p = .001). The model explained 44.4% of variance (F(4, 213) = 42.45, p < .001). Conclusion: AI/robotic awareness exerts a double-edged influence on retention: it directly reduces turnover intention while raising technology anxiety that offsets part of that benefit. Managers should combine AI literacy training with anxiety-relieving interventions. Novelty: This is the first study in a provincial South Asian setting to identify an inconsistent-mediation (suppression) pattern between AI awareness and turnover intention through job-related technology anxiety, broadening conservation of resources theory.

papers.title: “I wouldn’t trust her with my life but...” - Exploring trust in voice-based assistants through user-generated content
papers.authors: Katharina Frehmann, John J. Peters
papers.abstract: Investigating trust in conversational AI, such as voice-based assistants (VBAs), is increasingly important for understanding their rising popularity and the tasks users entrust to them. Howev-er, since VBAs are technical devices perceived as human-like and sometimes serving as infor-mation sources, it is unclear what forms trust in them takes. Technical, interpersonal, and media trust approaches may all be relevant, yet previous studies have not fully considered this poten-tial multidimensionality of trust in AI, especially regarding the inclusion of media trust. Fur-thermore, research on VBAs lacks qualitative studies that provide insights into users’ perspec-tives. This study therefore pursues two objectives: First, to develop a more comprehensive theo-retical perspective on trust in VBAs by integrating technical, interpersonal, and media trust ap-proaches. Second, to empirically explore signs of trust in VBAs in German user-generated online content. To this end, we conducted a qualitative content analysis of 169 postings about Alexa, Siri, and Google Assistant found on marketplaces, under media coverage, and on dis-cussion platforms. The results show that users evaluate typical and new technical, interpersonal, and media trustworthiness indicators for VBAs and sometimes combine these dimensions when discussing AI capabilities. When explicitly speaking of trust, users mostly refer to the parent company in high-risk situations rather than to the VBA itself. Users also discuss aspects that may represent consequences, processes, and external factors of trust. Based on these findings, the paper proposes a preliminary model of hybrid trust in VBAs that can inform future research on trust in conversational AI.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture: Enhancing Yield and Sustainable Farming Practices among Farmers in India
papers.authors: Seema R. Wankhade, Subhash Patil
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across sectors, including agriculture. In India, agriculture remains central to employment, rural livelihoods, and national food security. Rising population pressure, climate change, declining land availability, pest and disease risks, labour shortages, and resource constraints have intensified the need for more productive and sustainable farming systems. This paper uses secondary data to examine how AI can enhance agricultural yield and support sustainable farming practices among farmers in India. It reviews applications such as precision agriculture, drones, crop disease detection, digital advisory services, market information systems, and resource optimisation tools. The paper also analyses the major barriers to AI adoption, including weak rural connectivity, high initial investment, limited digital literacy, and the need for localised solutions. The study concludes that AI has strong potential to improve productivity and sustainability in Indian agriculture, provided that adoption is supported through public investment, affordable access models, local-language advisory systems, farmer training, and public- private partnerships.

papers.title: A golden era for open-ended questions? Using LLMs to scale the qualitative coding of open-ended survey responses
papers.authors: Ansgar Hudde, Shannon Taflinger
papers.abstract: Open-text questions in quantitative surveys can yield rich information from large samples, but analysing and coding these data using qualitative text analysis is resource-intensive. Large Language Models (LLMs) are a promising tool for scaling up such analyses, reducing time and costs. We first use thematic qualitative text analysis to create a typology of responses; we then let LLMs code texts based on our typology and instructions and compare their coding accuracy with that of student assistants, defining accuracy as agreement with a researcher-coded benchmark dataset. We assess performance on an interpretive coding task: applying a 15-category typology to approximately 1,400 open-ended responses from young US Americans about dating across party-political lines. We evaluate models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Mistral, with and without training data. The most advanced models outperform student assistants, and performance further increases with training data. This study contributes by applying LLMs to a use case with great analytical potential, namely open-ended survey responses, and testing whether the resulting codes support the same substantive conclusions as hand-coded data. We offer applied social scientists practical recommendations for a division of labour in which researchers retain conceptualisation and codebook construction and delegate the standardised coding to an LLM.

papers.title: Measuring Students’ Attention Boundaries in GAI-Assisted Learning: Development and Validation of the GAI-Mediated Learning Boundary Scale and Latent Profile Analysis
papers.authors: Xi Zhan, Yuxiang Shi, Peiyun He
papers.abstract: The Generative AI (GAI) is reshaping the temporal and spatial organization of college learning and the perceived boundary crossing between teacher-assigned tasks and self-directed learning. This study developed and validated a scale to assess college students’ attention boundary management in GAI-mediated learning. Analyzing data from 1904 students at 3 colleges in China, the study established a five-dimensional structure: Flexibility, Fragmentation, Immersion, Positive Spillover, and Negative Spillover. Exploratory and Confirmatory Factor Analysis confirmed the scale’s psychometric properties. A Latent Profile Analysis identified four distinct student profiles, Protective, Strained, Overextended, and Engaged Permeability Management. Supplementary heterogeneity analyses examined differences across the four profiles by gender, grade level, university, purposes and duration of AI use, and other learning-related characteristics. Based on these, this study proposed profile-specific recommendations. The study provides a validated instrument for assessing students’ attention boundaries in GAI-mediated learning, identifies heterogeneous student profiles, and offers differentiated practical implications.

papers.title: Epistemic Stances in Humanoid Robot Evaluation: Evidence from the Frankenstein Syndrome Questionnaire and Morph-Based Perceptual Judgements
papers.authors: Ilaria Maria Antonietta Benzi, Francesca Ciardo
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots occupy an ambiguous position between social partners and artefacts, and people differ markedly in how they evaluate them. Research on individual differences in human–robot interaction has focused on personality, anthropomorphic tendencies and technology acceptance, leaving largely unexamined the processes by which people decide whether an artificial agent can be treated as a credible source of social information. The present study introduces epistemic stances, as conceptualised within the mentalizing tradition, to this literature. Seventy adults completed the Epistemic Trust, Mistrust and Credulity Questionnaire, along with measures of generalized attitudes toward robots (Frankenstein Syndrome Questionnaire, Negative Attitudes toward Robots Scale, Robotic Social Attributes Scale), and a morph-based task in which robot faces varying in human likeness were rated for likeability, eeriness and human likeness. Epistemic stances were selectively associated with generalized social evaluations: Epistemic Trust predicted higher Robot Anxiety and lower attributed Warmth, whereas Credulity predicted higher attributed Warmth, with no associations for perceived Competence. At the stimulus level, morph condition strongly shaped all three judgements, whereas epistemic stances added little. Rather than a failure to extend person-level effects, this dissociation follows from the claim that epistemic stances operate on socially communicated information rather than on perceptual appraisal. Epistemic functioning may therefore shape the social meaning attributed to artificial agents, offering a testable framework for the design of robot communication.

papers.title: Beyond Turing Equivalence: The Human Premium in Human–AI Interaction
papers.authors: Ophelia Deroy
papers.abstract: Asking whether we can know whether a given text or output is coming from a machine or a human, which was at the core of the Turing test, is being progressively retired. This opens a new and no less interesting question: what happens when we know? This paper reviews evidence that when humans encounter exactly the same content, presented here as coming from a human and there from an AI, they do not behave similarly. The evidence across different kinds of interaction, advice giving, compliance, reciprocal interaction, and preferential choice, is that humans respect other humans more than they respect machines. This difference is often described as a 'machine penalty' where we distrust machines or lack familiarity with them, and predicted to decrease as AI becomes more prevalent. The paper offers a different interpretation, showing that we treat humans better for good reasons, including utility calculations, and that this human premium is likely to stay.

papers.title: Bridging the Trust Gap: A Contractualist Framework for Trustworthy AI
papers.authors: Luis Marcos Vidal, Clara Pretus
papers.abstract: Trustworthy AI is defined by properties built into a system, but trust depends on how users perceive it, so a system can meet every requirement and still fail to be trusted. Human and artificial agents that justify decisions in contractualist terms, by appeal to what affected parties could reasonably accept, are trusted more than those that appeal to aggregate welfare or fixed rules, irrespective of the action selected, but why is unexplained. We propose that a contractualist justification discloses individualized regard, evidence that the affected party's standpoint entered the decision, which is what trust, as a judgment that an agent is willing to act well, is sensitive to. Perceived regard is the mediating inference and raises trust through two pathways: warmth, and the expectation that the agent's future decisions will take the perceiver's own stakes into account. The intentional stance is a gating condition rather than a mediator, deciding whether an agent can be the object of this inference at all, so the mechanism is shared by human and artificial agents and needs no genuine intentions. Such justification is the observable trace of virtual bargaining, a theory-of-mind process, and does not require agents with genuine mental states. We state five falsifiable hypotheses that discriminate the account from warmth, anthropomorphism, and mere-transparency alternatives, and identify moderators and a possible moral uncanny valley as further tests.

papers.title: INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) AND CARTOON ANIMATION FILMS IN THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE LEARNING PROCESS AT SD IT IMAM SYAFI'I CENDEKIA 2 PEKANBARU
papers.authors: Resy Oktadela, Yusti Elida, Putri Octa Hadiyanti, Cyntia Kumalasari, Fitri Wulandari, Rezky Maulana
papers.journal: Journal of English Language and Education
papers.abstract: English language learning in elementary school requires instructional media that can deliver meaningful, engaging, and contextual language input to support children's vocabulary development. This study examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and a cartoon animation film the AI-supported Bluey series into the English language learning process of sixth-grade students at SD IT Imam Syafi'i Cendekia 2 Pekanbaru. A quantitative pre-experimental design with a one-group pretest-posttest model was employed, involving 26 sixth-grade students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through a vocabulary test administered before and after the treatment, then analyzed descriptively (mean and standard deviation) and inferentially using a paired-sample t-test with the assistance of SPSS software. The results showed that students' mean vocabulary score increased from 62.88 (SD = 18.23) on the pretest to 80.57 (SD = 11.60) on the posttest. Hypothesis testing yielded a t-test value of 7.723 with df = 25, which exceeded the t-table value at the 5% significance level, indicating that the alternative hypothesis (Ha) was accepted and the null hypothesis (H0) was rejected. These findings confirm that integrating AI with cartoon animation film has a statistically significant effect on improving students' English vocabulary mastery. The combination of authentic audiovisual input from animated cartoons with AI-supported personalization and feedback is recommended as an engaging supplementary approach for English instruction in elementary schools, provided its implementation remains guided by teachers to ensure age-appropriate content and balanced screen time.

papers.title: STAFF SOFT SKILLS IN ENSURING MANAGEMENT RESILIENCE IN E-COMMERCE ENTERPRISES
papers.authors: Halyna Kupalova, Yevhenii Dmytryshyn, Yevhenii Oleshko
papers.abstract: The article examines the role of personnel soft skills in ensuring the management resilience of e-commerce enterprises under martial law. An analysis of scientific publications on personnel management and the development of employees’ competencies and soft skills is carried out, and domestic and foreign approaches to their interpretation and assessment are considered. The dynamics of e-commerce development in Ukraine are revealed: the volume of e-commerce turnover increased from UAH 28.2 billion in 2017 to UAH 69.9 billion in 2024, or 2.5 times. It is established that since the outbreak of hostilities the share of enterprises engaged in e-commerce has been increasing annually, from 10.3% in 2022 to 15.6% in 2024, while wholesale and retail trade and the repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles are among the four types of economic activity with the highest level of its development. A structural and logical framework for building the organizational resilience of e-commerce enterprise management through the development of personnel soft skills is proposed, and groups of these skills are identified by functional categories of employees. It is shown that strategic thinking and leadership competencies under uncertainty are critical for top management, whereas psychological endurance and communication skills come to the fore for operational and service staff. It is determined that adaptability is common to all categories of personnel and, under martial law, acquires the character of a basic functional competence. It is proven that, to increase labor productivity and the quality of customer service in e-commerce, it is advisable to implement a set of managerial measures: introducing psychological support and stress resilience programs for employees; improving the digital literacy of personnel using artificial intelligence; developing a system of internal mentoring and functional job rotation; incorporating personnel resilience indicators into the performance evaluation system; and expanding cooperation with educational institutions, industry associations and civic organizations.

papers.title: What Vibrates Before the Encounter
papers.authors: Rodrigo Junges
papers.abstract: Participatory design is often structured around methods, tools, and carefully planned activities intended to facilitate collaboration. Yet, such approaches may overlook the subtle relational conditions that allow participation to emerge in the first place. This essay reflects on a lived experience of engaging with a vulnerable community in Porto Alegre, Brazil, and explores how participation often begins not in formal co-creation activities, but in the ordinary gestures that precede them. Through sustained presence, informal encounters, and the gradual building of trust, the groundwork for participation slowly takes shape. Drawing on phenomenological reflections and research on intimacy in participatory design, the text proposes intimacy as a lens for understanding the relational dynamics that sustain participatory processes. Intimacy is approached not as forced closeness or total transparency, but as a condition that allows things to come into appearance without being extracted or demanded. From this perspective, participation emerges less as a method-driven event and more as a situated posture of attention, reciprocity, and ethical responsibility toward what becomes visible in the encounter. By foregrounding micro-dynamics such as rhythm, presence, and trust, the essay invites designers to reconsider the foundations of participatory practice beyond procedural frameworks.

papers.title: Association between mental well-being, body composition, and physical activity among adolescents in the Eastern Cape, South Africa
papers.authors: Z. Siduli, Maya Maria van Gent, Rudolph Leon Van Niekerk
papers.journal: Journal of Child and Adolescent Mental Health
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which health behaviours are established and may influence physical and mental well-being across the life course. However, evidence on the associations between body composition, physical activity, and mental well-being among South African adolescents remains limited. AIM: The study aimed to determine the association between mental well-being, body composition, and physical activity among adolescents in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. METHOD: < 0.05 with a 95% confidence interval. Logistic regression was used to examine the association between metabolic risk and mental well-being, as well as to assess the extent to which body composition components and physical activity predict mental well-being. RESULTS: Most participants (65.4%) fell in the normal body mass index (BMI) category. An average of 502.70 minutes (SD = 574.20 minutes) per week of physical activity was displayed by the total sample. Body fat percentage emerged as the only statistically significant predictor of mental well-being. CONCLUSIONS: Although most adolescents exceeded the recommended 300 minutes of physical activity per week, neither physical activity nor BMI predicted mental well-being. Instead, body fat percentage was the only significant predictor, indicating that higher body fat was associated with poorer mental well-being. These findings suggest that body composition, rather than overall physical activity levels or BMI alone, plays a critical role in adolescent mental well-being.

papers.title: Use of AI tools among allied healthcare students: Academic integrity, online learning integrity, and nomophobia as predictors
papers.authors: John Mark R. Asio, Jason M. Yap, C. A. Casabella Garcia
papers.journal: International Journal of Changes in Education
papers.abstract: The swift convergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), online instruction, and mobile dependence has transformed higher education, introducing both innovations and ethical problems for allied health training.
