For the Spanish corpus, AI-assisted procedures enabled data processing in Python (Python Software Foundation, 2025) using the spaCy library (Honnibal et al., 2020), followed by Bayesian mixed-effects logistic regression in R (brms package). Results identified key predictors of gender assignment, including proficiency level (β = 1.96, 95% CrI [1.62, 2.32]), non-prototypical gender markers (β = –2.47, 95% CrI [–3.25, –1.71]), and cross-linguistic gender mismatches (β = -1.45, 95% CrI [-1.81, -1.10]). For the English corpus, AI-supported analyses using spaCy and SciPy revealed significantly greater complexity in gerund and participle use at higher proficiency levels (χ² (15) = 26.85, p = .043). Findings aligned with previous research and expert evaluations, demonstrating that AI can effectively support corpus analysis workflows and generate functional code. This study highlights the potential of generative AI to make corpus linguistics more accessible, while also underscoring the value of medium-scale learner corpora for identifying systematic patterns in L2 development.

papers.title: The «lawyer-architect» as a novel type of professional agency and a product of legal anthropocentrism in the context of the digital revolution in society
papers.authors: Рустам Зайниддинович Махмадиев
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Introduction. The article presents the results of a study of the development of anthropocentric approaches in Russian philosophical and legal thought, the doctrinal systematization of which can serve as a methodological and axiological basis for transforming the competence based model of a lawyer towards the «lawyer-architect», the key method of which should be the reintegration of various regulators of social relations in the context of digital reality. The conclusion is drawn that it is necessary to incorporate the achievements of legal anthropology into the methodological toolkit of a lawyer. The author attempts to substantiate the need to overcome the epistemological bias in the methodology of law and shift towards its praxeological function. The approaches proposed in the article make it possible to adapt the legal profession to the technologization of society and to build a sovereign, value rich domestic model of legal engineering.The aim of the study is to develop and provide a theoretical and methodological justification for a new competency model of a «lawyer-architect» in the context of the principles of legal anthropocentrism, legal anthropology, and the axiological heritage of domestic philosophical and legal thought.Materials and methods. The theoretical foundation of the study is based on the fundamental works of domestic and foreign researchers in the fields of philosophy and history of law, methodology of law, and legal anthropology (B.N. Chicherin, O.A. Puchkov, V.N. Sinyukov, D.A. Pashentsev, E. Anners, and others), as well as the latest conceptual developments in the field of legal design and anthropocentrism (R.Z. Makhmadiev, S.Yu. Kashkin).The methodological basis of the work is the principles of interdisciplinarity and the combination of theoretical-legal and applied (legal-technical) knowledge. The key research methods used were: praxeological and axiological methods, the method of comparative legal analysis, the ontological approach, and general scientific methods.Results. The axiological and ontological crisis of the paradigm of the competence-based model of the “lawyer-craftsman” is revealed in the face of modern challenges and the latest technologies, including generative AI. In the context of the growing complexity of the normative structure of society, law has shared the regulatory space with software code (“Code as Law”), platform algorithms, and network ethics. The model of the «lawyer-architect» is conceptualized as a reintegrator of various regulators of social relations in the context of the digital revolution. Requirements for the anthropological modernization of legal education have been formulated.Conclusions. The paper substantiates the need to transform the methodology of law from a predominantly epistemological (contemplative) focus towards ontological and praxeological functions. As an axiological basis for the modern lawyer’s understanding of law, it is proposed to establish the principles of legal anthropocentrism, based on the values of the national cultural, legal, and philosophical tradition, which, in the author’s view, can serve as a methodological shield for the autonomy of the individual in the era of digital dehumanization.

papers.title: Effects of the Integration of Medical Treatment and Prevention on Glycaemic Control Among Patients with Diabetes in Qianjiang District, China: A Difference-in-Differences Study
papers.authors: Tan H, He X
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Huawei Tan,1,2 Xiaochong He31School of Public Management, Chongqing Technology and Business University, Chongqing, 400067, People’s Republic of China; 2Department of Health Management, School of Medicine and Health Management, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, 430030, People’s Republic of China; 3Department of Nursing, Army Medical University, Chongqing, 400038, People’s Republic of ChinaCorrespondence: Xiaochong He, Email hexiaochong879@tmmu.edu.cnBackground: The Integration of Medical Treatment and Prevention (IMTP) is one approach to integrated disease management within China’s primary healthcare system. Evidence on its association with glycaemic control and potential behavioural pathways among patients with diabetes remains limited.Methods: We conducted a retrospective quasi-experimental study of 5676 adults with diabetes in Qianjiang District during 2023Q1– 2024Q4. Four primary healthcare (PHC) facilities implemented IMTP in January 2024 (treatment group), while 26 formed the control group. Patient-level propensity score matching via the Super Learner machine learning algorithm (PSM-SLMLA) at the 2023Q4 baseline retained 1240 patients per group (19,840 patient-quarter observations). Weighted difference-in-differences (DID) models included facility and quarter fixed effects with facility-clustered inference.Results: IMTP was associated with a 3.73% relative reduction in HbA1c (95% CI, 0.04%– 7.29%; β = − 0.0380; 95% CI, − 0.0757 to − 0.0004; P = 0.048), equivalent to approximately 0.27 HbA1c percentage points at the pre-intervention mean. Pre-intervention coefficients were not jointly significant (P = 0.857), and sensitivity estimates remained negative. Exploratory indirect associations were − 0.0021 through active follow-up behaviour (95% bootstrap CI, − 0.0037 to − 0.0007; P = 0.004) and − 0.0006 through staple-food intake behaviour (95% bootstrap CI, − 0.0026 to − 0.0001; P = 0.014); the exercise adherence estimate included zero. Formal interaction tests did not identify heterogeneity (all P for interaction > 0.05).Conclusion: IMTP was associated with modest short-term glycaemic improvement. Active follow-up behaviour may be a potential pathway. Increased staple-food intake raises a dietary-compensation hypothesis, but concurrent behavioural and HbA1c measurements preclude causal interpretation.Keywords: integrated disease management, patients with diabetes, Integration of Medical Treatment and Prevention, glycaemic control, active follow-up behaviour

papers.title: The chatbot as a complementary tool in the training ofthe university subject
papers.authors: Sofía Guillermina Idiart
papers.journal: El Servicio de Difusión de la Creación Intelectual (National University of La Plata)
papers.abstract: Para este trabajo se pondrá el foco de atención en cómo se puede utilizar la herramienta ChatGPT y otros chatbots en la formación del sujeto universitario, específicamente en el campo de la comunicación y las ciencias sociales. Este recorte se debe a que cuando hablamos de inteligencia artificial nos referimos a diferentes dispositivos tecnológicos que no todos cumplen las mismas funciones. En este caso, el ChatGPT fue lanzado en noviembre de 2022 y pertenece a la empresa OpenIA. Su surgimiento amplió y profundizó ciertos debates en torno a los usos que le podemos dar a estas nuevas tecnologías que atraviesan no solo el campo de la educación, sino también nuestras prácticas y nuestras vidas cotidianas. En primer lugar, se parte de entender a la tecnología como una herramienta social y no neutral. Sobre esto, Raymond Williams (1992) manifiesta que a este concepto no debemos pensarlo de forma aislada, sino todo lo contrario, de forma integral en conjunto con las sociedades y comunidades. Otro autor que nos puede ayudar a reflexionar sobre el uso de estas tecnologías en la formación del sujeto universitario es Roger Silverstone (2004), quien explica que cuando hablamos de tecnologías debemos pensarlas como habilitantes o inhabilitantes.

papers.title: El ejercicio como terapia no farmacológica
papers.authors: Martín Rodríguez
papers.journal: Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Diabetes
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is a metabolic, cardiovascular, muscular and inflammatory disease. Therefore, exercise should be considered a central therapeutic intervention rather than a simple lifestyle recommendation. During skeletal muscle contraction, glucose uptake increases through a pathway that is partly independent of insulin and involves GLUT-4 translocation, AMPK activation, calcium-dependent signaling, AS160/TBC1D4, Rab proteins, RAC1 and enhanced microvascular blood flow. The interaction between insulin and exercise helps explain how skeletal muscle takes up glucose during physical activity and how, after exercise, insulin sensitivity increases in previously active muscle to promote glycogen resynthesis. These mechanisms improve glucose and fatty acid utilization, reduce lipotoxicity and promote mitochondrial adaptations. Skeletal muscle should also be regarded as an endocrine organ. Through myokines and exercise-induced factors, or exerkines, contracting muscle communicates with adipose tissue, liver, cardiovascular system, bone and brain. Interleukin-6 released by myocytes during exercise does not necessarily reproduce the pro-inflammatory profile of macrophage-derived IL-6. On the contrary, exercise-induced IL-6 participates in anti-inflammatory responses, stimulates IL-1 receptor antagonist and IL-10, and contributes to energy metabolism. This concept helps explain why regular exercise reduces low-grade chronic inflammation, visceral adiposity, oxidative stress and cardiometabolic risk. Clinical evidence shows that exercise improves HbA1c, blood pressure, body composition, lipid profile, functional capacity and quality of life. Cardiorespiratory fitness is a powerful prognostic marker and should be considered a clinical vital sign. However, implementation remains a major challenge. In a multicenter Argentine study of adults with type 2 diabetes, 52.3% showed low levels of physical activity. The most frequently reported barriers were lack of willpower, lack of energy and lack of time. Low physical activity was associated with older age, higher HbA1c, higher BMI, female sex and lack of social support. Therefore, exercise prescription should be individualized, progressive and realistic. It should include reduction of sedentary behavior, frequent interruptions of prolonged sitting, promotion of daily-life physical activity, at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise, and resistance training two to three times weekly. Exercise is a biological, accessible and powerful “polypill” for the prevention and treatment of type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Obesidad en el adulto mayor: ¿cuándo tratar con fármacos?
papers.authors: Romina Clemente
papers.journal: Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Diabetes
papers.abstract: The prevalence of obesity in older adults (≥ 60 years) has reached critical levels of 42%, representing a public health challenge due to its association with disability, mortality, and frailty. With aging, body composition changes, increasing visceral adiposity and decreasing muscle mass, which gives rise to a phenotype with higher cardiometabolic risk known as sarcopenic obesity. Clinical management must transcend chronological age, prioritizing the patient's functional status and biological health. Evaluation must be comprehensive, analyzing comorbidities, frailty using validated scales (Fried, Edmonton), and anthropometric assessment. It is essential to diagnose sarcopenic obesity by measuring muscle strength (handgrip or chair-stand test) and quantifying lean mass (DXA or BIA). Treatment indications are the same as for the general population, but taking certain precautions into account. According to ADA standards, pharmacological treatment is indicated with a BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² or ≥ 27 kg/m² in the presence of complications such as prediabetes, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, established cardiovascular disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, steatohepatitis, sleep apnea, or osteoarthritis. Although older adults are often underrepresented in clinical trials, evidence from pivotal studies on the efficacy of drugs in weight loss is overwhelming: Orlistat (XENDOS): 3-5% weight loss; requires monitoring hydration and supplementing fat-soluble vitamins to protect bone and muscle health. Naltrexone/Bupropion (COR): 5% weight loss; useful in emotional eating, but requires caution due to the risk of neuropsychiatric effects such as agitation and insomnia. Liraglutide (SCALE/LEADER): 8% weight loss and a 34% reduction in MACE in individuals ≥ 75 years. Semaglutide (STEP/SELECT): 16% weight loss and a 20% reduction in MACE. Tirzepatide (SURMOUNT/SUMMIT): 21% weight loss and a 38% reduction in heart failure events. Precautions include: evaluating interactions due to polypharmacy, gradual titration, optimal hydration, and a protein intake of 1.2 to 1.5 g/kg/day along with individualized strength exercises to preserve muscle mass and autonomy. Advanced age is not a contraindication for pharmacotherapy. Cardiometabolic benefits are evident as long as continuous evaluation of adverse effects is performed. However, long-term studies specifically targeting the older adult population are required. The goal of treatment is not only to lose weight but to improve functionality and quality of life.

papers.title: Transforming Corporate University Learning Culture Through Cognitive Growth Mindset
papers.authors: Muh. Asdig Fanani, Muhammad Ramaditya, Abdul Razak Abdul Hadi
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: The research investigates the direct and indirect impacts of Organizational Learning Culture (OLC) and Digital Literacy (DL) on employees’ Readiness for Change (RFC) via a Growth Mindset (GM) during a Corporate University (CorpU) governance transformation. Utilizing an explanatory quantitative case study design, data from 357 lecturers and administrative staff at a State Islamic University are analyzed through Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). The structural results reveal that OLC, DL, and GM significantly and directly enhance RFC, with GM operating as a complementary partial mediator. The core originality of this research lies in validating an asymmetric cognitive path, showing that an individual’s localized technical capacity (DL) is a substantially stronger psychological activator of GM than macro-environmental learning cultures. However, the IPMA highlights that the behavioral dimensions of OLC severely underperform despite registering high institutional importance. Methodologically, the research acknowledges generalizability boundaries due to its single-locus, cross-sectional design. Practically, these findings imply that systemic digital overhauls within highly autonomous academic ecosystems cannot be forced via abstract cultural campaigns. Institutional leaders should formalize cross-faculty communities of practice and launch experimental artificial intelligence pedagogy incentive schemes to cultivate a tangible climate of digital psychological safety.

papers.title: Abordaje de la diabetes tipo 2 en la población pediátrica y adolescente
papers.authors: Carla Mannucci
papers.journal: Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Diabetes
papers.abstract: Youth-onset type 2 diabetes (T2D) has emerged as a major challenge in pediatric endocrinology. Its incidence continues to rise in parallel with the increasing prevalence of childhood obesity and currently accounts for approximately 8% of all pediatric diabetes cases, exceeding 40% of new diagnoses in certain high-risk ethnic groups. In Argentina, no national epidemiological registry is currently available. In Brazil, the ERICA study, which included nearly 38,000 adolescents, reported a prevalence of 22% for prediabetes and 3.3% for T2D. Unlike adult-onset disease, youth-onset T2D follows a more aggressive clinical course, characterized by accelerated β-cell function decline, more severe insulin resistance, and the early development of both microvascular and macrovascular complications. The TODAY and TODAY2 studies, which enrolled 699 adolescents with recently diagnosed T2D and followed them for more than 13 years, demonstrated that diabetes-related complications develop early and progress rapidly. After five years of disease duration, approximately one-third of participants had developed hypertension, while more than 10% had diabetic kidney disease or diabetic retinopathy. By young adulthood (mean age, 26 years), 60% of participants had developed at least one diabetes-related complication and nearly 30% had two or more, highlighting the substantial burden of early morbidity associated with youth-onset T2D. Accordingly, current international guidelines recommend an intensive, multidisciplinary approach beginning at diagnosis, including screening for metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), diabetic retinopathy, diabetic kidney disease, dyslipidemia, and hypertension, together with comprehensive lifestyle intervention involving both the patient and family, psychological support, and early individualized pharmacological therapy. Although metformin remains the recommended first-line agent for metabolically stable patients, the introduction of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors has expanded treatment options, providing benefits not only in glycemic control but also in body mass index (BMI), with the potential to modify disease progression. Therapeutic perspectives continue to evolve. The SURPASS-PEDS trial evaluating tirzepatide and the PIONEER TEENS trial evaluating oral semaglutide represent major advances that are likely to influence the management of youth-onset T2D in the coming years. Overall, current evidence supports an early, individualized treatment strategy aimed at long-term cardiometabolic and kidney risk reduction from the time of diagnosis.

papers.title: Obesidad en la niñez: detección precoz y abordaje
papers.authors: Nuria Grimberg
papers.journal: Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Diabetes
papers.abstract: Obesity is a chronic, complex, and relapsing disease associated with genetic, physiological, socioeconomic, and environmental factors, representing a major global public health challenge1. In Argentina, 13.6% of children under 5 years of age and 41.1% of children and adolescents aged 5–17 years have excess weight2. Pediatric obesity is associated with an increased risk of obesity in adulthood and exposes children and adolescents to serious short and long term adverse health outcomes, including cardiovascular disease and diabetes1. Body mass index (BMI) correlates well with the degree of adiposity and, at the population level, with the risk of comorbidities and mortality. Despite its limitations, BMI remains the recommended tool for screening and diagnosing overweight and obesity. It should be complemented by other anthropometric measurements, such as waist circumference. Personal and family medical history, physical examination findings, and appropriate laboratory investigations should also be considered1,2. Children and adolescents with overweight or obesity should undergo a comprehensive evaluation, including medical history, physical examination, psychological assessment, screening for eating disorders, and evaluation of the social determinants of health. The presence of obesity-related comorbidities should also be assessed. Laboratory testing should be guided by the patient's age, clinical presentation, and medical history1. The prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of obesity without comorbidities should be managed by pediatricians in the primary care setting. Children and adolescents who do not respond adequately to initial treatment or who present with obesity-related comorbidities should be referred to a pediatric nutrition specialist and a multidisciplinary team2. Treatment should be comprehensive and include multicomponent behavioral and psychological interventions encompassing nutrition, physical activity, and psychological support. Care should adopt a patient- and family-centered approach, recognizing obesity as a chronic disease while avoiding weight stigma. Pediatric obesity specialists should consider weight loss pharmacotherapy as an adjunct to lifestyle interventions after carefully evaluating its indications, risks, and potential benefits1,3. Further evidence is needed regarding optimal weight-loss targets and the long-term risks and benefits of available interventions4. Addressing the primary prevention of childhood obesity remains a fundamental public health priority3.

papers.title: Educación centrada en la persona
papers.authors: María Lidia Ruiz Morosini
papers.journal: Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Diabetes
papers.abstract: Diabetes education has evolved from models primarily focused on knowledge transmission toward approaches that recognize the individual as the central actor in health-related decision-making. In this context, the apparent controversy between structured diabetes education and person-centered education represents, rather than a dichotomy, an opportunity to explore how both approaches can be integrated to achieve better clinical and human outcomes. The conceptual evolution of therapeutic education has progressed from competency-based structured programs to the current paradigm of person-centered care, which advocates tailoring education to each individual's values, priorities, goals, and life context. This transformation implies moving beyond questions focused exclusively on the disease ("What did you eat?", "How many carbohydrates did you consume?", "Why didn't you exercise?") toward questions that explore the lived experience of diabetes ("What concerns you most?", "What goals would you like to achieve?", "What prevents you from reaching them?", "What role does diabetes play in your life?"). Current evidence demonstrates that structured education programs remain essential to ensure quality, equity, and the acquisition of self-management competencies. However, their effectiveness is enhanced when they incorporate person-centered strategies, empathetic communication, shared decision-making, and ongoing behavioral support. A recent meta-analysis of person-centered interventions reported a 0.56% reduction in HbA1c, while a network meta-analysis of Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES) programs demonstrated HbA1c reductions approaching 0.6%, together with improvements in additional cardiometabolic outcomes. Furthermore, person-centered education has become both a challenge and a necessity in the era of diabetes technology. Continuous glucose monitoring, automated insulin delivery systems, and artificial intelligence require educational strategies capable of transforming data into meaningful, individualized decisions. True innovation does not lie in replacing structured education but in strengthening it through a person-centered approach. Structure defines what should be taught; person-centered care determines how learning can become meaningful, foster autonomy, and translate into sustainable behavioral change. Rather than opposing models, structured education and person-centered care represent complementary dimensions of truly transformative diabetes education.

papers.title: Obesidad monogénica: lo que todo médico debe saber
papers.authors: María Eugenia Andrés
papers.journal: Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Diabetes
papers.abstract: High-penetrance monogenic and syndromic obesities result from rare genetic variants with minimal environmental influence. These conditions can be differentiated from polygenic obesity based on key symptoms, such as hyperphagia (overwhelming hunger), severe early-onset obesity (before 5 years of age), and suboptimal responses to non-targeted therapies. Therefore, timely diagnosis is essential to guide management strategies and reduce the burden of disease. A deep understanding of the underlying pathophysiology and the molecular mechanisms that define these pathologies substantially facilitates both diagnosis and the therapeutic approach. In recent years, advances in genetic analysis have made it possible to develop innovative pharmacological treatments for various forms of genetic obesity. It is now viable to identify specific patients who can benefit from targeted therapies based on their unique genetic mechanisms, through an understanding of the molecular pathways involved in the development of the disease. As recently demonstrated, two drugs—metreleptin (an LPR agonist) and setmelanotide (MC4R agonists)—have been identified as potentially effective interventions in the treatment of certain rare forms of monogenic obesity caused by loss-of-function variants in genes involved in the leptin-melanocortin pathway. Evidence supports the efficacy and safety of these precision molecules in even younger age groups (from 2 years of age). Likewise, international regulatory indications have expanded, covering not only deficiencies in the leptinmelanocortin pathway (POMC, LEPR, PCSK1) and ciliopathies (Bardet-Biedl syndrome), but also complex forms of acquired hypothalamic obesity. These precision medications have demonstrated robust clinical efficacy in intervening directly within hypothalamic signaling pathways, successfully achieving a reduction in BMI. Therefore, when faced with a clinical presentation of obesity in early childhood, implementing targeted genetic testing becomes a priority. The timely diagnosis of these variants is indispensable in clinical practice to effectively mitigate extreme hyperphagia and the increase in BMI. The recognition of these distinctive features empowers medical personnel to abandon ineffective interventions and adopt individualized treatments that drastically improve long-term quality of life. Under this premise, it is essential to continue translational research on monogenic and syndromic diseases of the MC4R pathway, a/s multiple challenges remain to be addressed.

papers.title: Inteligencia artificial en el consultorio, tips prácticos
papers.authors: Lucas Sosa
papers.journal: Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Diabetes
papers.abstract: The incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical practice has moved from promise to an everyday decision. Using a computer or phone, clinicians can now transcribe an encounter, summarize a lengthy medical record, draft a report, or retrieve scientific evidence within seconds. Availability, however, does not equal usefulness or guarantee safety. This presentation offers a pragmatic tour of this ecosystem, using the diabetes clinic as its starting point and clinical need —rather than technology— as the criterion for selecting a tool. Four families of tools with concrete applications in daily work will be discussed. First, ambient documentation assistants can produce draft clinical notes from the patient-clinician conversation. Their use has been associated with lower documentation burden, less after-hours work, and reduced professional burnout, although consent, data protection, and clinician review are required before any text enters the medical record.¹ Second, general-purpose language models can support writing and synthesis, including insurance reports, referral summaries, patient instructions, and educational materials adapted to individual health literacy. Third, environments that query clinician-provided documents can interrogate guidelines, protocols, longitudinal records, glucose sensor reports, or insulin delivery data while keeping answers linked to the supplied sources. Fourth, AI-assisted evidence search tools can accelerate the initial response to focused clinical questions without replacing critical appraisal of the original research. The session will also provide operational recommendations for structuring an effective instruction, de-identifying information, checking outputs, and recognizing tasks that should not be delegated. The approach adopts a human-in-the-loop model: AI proposes; the professional verifies, decides, and signs. Access to a model alone does not necessarily improve clinical reasoning; benefit depends on training and deliberate integration into the workflow.² Known limitations will be addressed, including hallucinations, fabricated references, response variability, bias, confidentiality, and professional accountability. Mitigation strategies include restricting answers to selected sources, retrieval-augmented generation, and systematic human verification, while recognizing that none of these measures eliminates risk completely.³ Finally, the presentation will distinguish control algorithms already validated in automated insulin delivery systems from generative applications, whose clinical maturity remains limited.⁴ The objective is for participants to leave with criteria they can apply the following Monday: select a real problem, design a small and repeatable workflow, measure its benefit, and keep clinical accountability in professional hands. Used in this way, AI may reduce friction and recover time for listening, interpreting context, and making decisions together with the person living with diabetes.

papers.title: Niños y adolescentes: fármacos aprobados y su uso actual en la práctica clínica
papers.authors: Adriana Roussos
papers.journal: Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Diabetes
papers.abstract: Pediatric obesity is a chronic, complex, and multifactorial disease that affects physical and psychosocial health and increases the risk of morbidity and mortality throughout life. The rise in obesity incidence has been accompanied by a greater incidence of metabolic, cardiovascular, hepatic, respiratory, orthopedic, and psychological complications from an early age, as well as a high probability of persistent obesity into adulthood, with the consequent increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), cardiovascular disease, and premature mortality. Lifestyle interventions remain the cornerstone of treatment and should be implemented in all patients. However, they may be insufficient, especially in adolescents with severe obesity or multiple comorbidities. In this context, pharmacotherapy should not be understood as an isolated weight-loss strategy, but rather as a tool to modify the course of the disease, improve its complications, and promote adherence to sustained behavioral changes. The pharmacological treatment of pediatric obesity has transformed significantly in recent years: it has gone from having limited options with modest efficacy to incorporating therapies targeting specific physiological pathways, particularly those related to the incretin system and the melanocortin pathway, with results significantly superior to those previously obtained with other drugs. Therefore, pharmacotherapy can be an effective therapeutic tool in carefully selected patients, always combined with intensive behavioral and lifestyle interventions. However, evidence is insufficient regarding its safety and long-term effects, its benefits beyond BMI reduction, and its application in certain patient groups, such as children under 12 years of age and minority populations. This presentation will aim to analyze the available evidence on the pharmacological treatment of pediatric obesity, considering the efficacy, safety, clinical indications, limitations, and quality of evidence for each available drug.

papers.title: Evaluating the Accuracy and Level-Appropriateness of ChatGPT Feedback for Beginning Korean Learners: Implications for AI-Assisted Language Teaching
papers.authors: 정인호
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into language learning has introduced new opportunities for personalized instruction and real-time feedback. This study investigates the accuracy and level-appropriateness of ChatGPT’s feedback for beginning Korean learners at Brigham Young University (BYU-Provo). Using the free version of ChatGPT 3.5 within the beginning level curriculum, the research examines how accurately and appropriately ChatGPT provides meaningful and effective feedback to students. Employing Feedback theory, the study collects data through interaction logs and surveys to assess the accuracy of ChatGPT’s feedback, its impact on student confidence and engagement, and its role in fostering individualized learning experiences. The findings will provide insights into AI’s feasibility as a supplementary language tutor, highlight the need for developing a customized GPT for specific learner groups and for training students how to create specific prompts tailored to their learning goals. Additionally, this study explores how AI can assist teachers in providing effective language instruction.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence, creativity, and autonomy of mind
papers.authors: Lorraine Tolmie
papers.abstract: After a software update, my notes app began auto-suggesting words with great enthusiasm. The first time this happened I noticed the word ‘end’ had appeared. Although this was what I had intended to write, I couldn’t remember typing it and wondered if I had briefly entered a fugue state. Feeling slightly disconcerted I deleted the three letters and typed them in again. Nothing happened. However, when I continued writing and typed ‘of the’ the word ’spectrum’ materialised. It was at this point that I realised it was a new predictive feature in the application. In the context, ‘spectrum’ was actually a pretty good option and I had to admit that maybe it was even better than what I had originally intended. Unfortunately, I couldn’t compare because whatever I had been thinking was lost. It had retreated into the mysterious mind-field where words spring from. In the end, I never finished that sentence because what began to spill through my fingers were a lot of thoughts about automation and AI. Some of that content is here.

papers.title: Μια διερευνητική μελέτη για τον ψηφιακό μετασχηματισμό στη λογιστική από τη σκοπιά της θεωρίας της ανατρεπτικής καινοτομίας
papers.authors: Γεώργιος Καμπιώτης
papers.abstract: This doctoral dissertation investigates the digital transformation of accounting through the theoretical lens of the Theory of Disruptive Innovation, examining how emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), Blockchain, Big Data, Cloud Computing, and Industry 4.0 technologies are reshaping traditional accounting and auditing practices. The primary objective of the study is to systematically map the existing body of knowledge, evaluate the impact of disruptive technologies on accounting functions, and explore the competencies, organizational transformations, and institutional adaptations required for their effective integration. The dissertation consists of four distinct yet interrelated research studies. The first chapter presents a systematic literature review conducted in accordance with the PRISMA framework, providing a comprehensive analysis of the international literature on disruptive technologies in accounting. The findings reveal that these technologies accelerate automation, enhance transparency, improve decision-making processes, and transform the role of accountants from transactional processors to strategic advisors. At the same time, significant adoption barriers are identified, including technological limitations, regulatory uncertainty, ethical concerns, governance challenges, and cultural resistance within organizations. The second chapter introduces NeuralACT, an innovative accounting analytics framework that utilizes artificial neural networks to process large-scale datasets in real time, offering enhanced predictive capabilities, pattern recognition, and decision support functionality. The results demonstrate that machine learning techniques can surpass the capabilities of traditional accounting systems by delivering greater accuracy and responsiveness in complex business environments. The third chapter focuses on the transformation of digital accounting through the integration of Big Data, the Internet of Things (IoT), and Industry 4.0 technologies. The analysis highlights how the convergence of physical and digital systems enables continuous data collection and processing, improving the quality of financial reporting, operational monitoring, and forecasting accuracy. Furthermore, the study emphasizes the necessity of developing new digital competencies and redesigning accounting information systems to meet the demands of an increasingly digitalized business ecosystem. The fourth chapter proposes the AGILANCE Framework, an intelligent accounting system designed to support agile financial planning through the utilization of Big Data and advanced analytical techniques. The proposed framework combines automated data analytics, predictive modeling, and decision-support mechanisms, enabling organizations to respond more effectively to dynamic market conditions. Overall, the dissertation demonstrates that digital transformation represents far more than a technological upgrade; it constitutes a profound organizational and professional shift that fundamentally redefines the accounting profession. The study contributes to the literature by bridging the Theory of Disruptive Innovation with the field of accounting and by proposing novel models, frameworks, and practical approaches for the effective adoption of emerging technologies. The findings suggest that the future sustainability and relevance of the accounting profession will depend on the ability of accountants, organizations, and regulatory bodies to embrace technological innovation, cultivate advanced digital and analytical competencies, and establish governance frameworks that ensure transparency, reliability, accountability, and the ethical use of technology in an increasingly digital future.

papers.title: Generative AI and Mathematical Reasoning: Evaluating the Accuracy, Justification, and Proof Quality of AI-Generated Mathematics Solutions
papers.authors: Godfred Appiah, Raphael Oduro Boafo, Bismark Osei Antobre
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems can provide mathematical solutions, explanations and proofs, but it should be borne in mind that the correctness of an answer does not automatically imply that the mathematical reasoning that a GenAI system was applied was sound. The present critical review investigates the current accomplishments in the field of applying large language models (LLMs) in mathematics and focuses on three basic parameters of output quality: accuracy, justification and proof quality. Available evidence from benchmark tests, mathematics education research as well as studies focused on errors detection and validation indicates that the field of evaluation of mathematical performance in the field of AI has made substantial progress, but different aspects of quality work are analyzed separately that are often mixed together. The results of literature review completed as a part of this research have shown the importance of AJP framework. Accuracy deals with the correctness of the answer. Justification refers to the correctness of reasoning steps. Finally, proof quality indicates whether the proof in question is valid and does not use faulty assumptions or circular reasoning.

papers.title: Dimensionally Engineered Nanotherapeutics for Pulpitis and Periodontitis: From Structural Design to Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Precision Therapy
papers.authors: Zhang F, Zhang W, Lu T, Meng Y, Su M, Zhang Q, Shi H
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Fuzhong Zhang,1 Wenyue Zhang,1 Ting Lu,1 Yao Meng,1 Meihui Su,1 Qixiong Zhang,2,3 Houkui Shi41Key Laboratory of Oral Disease Research of the Education Department of Guizhou Province, School and Hospital of Stomatology, Zunyi Medical University, Zunyi, People’s Republic of China; 2Department of Pharmacy, Personalized Drug Research and Therapy Key Laboratory of Sichuan Province, Sichuan Provincial People’s Hospital, School of Medicine, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Chengdu, People’s Republic of China; 3Department of Pharmacy, Sichuan Provincial People’s Hospital East Sichuan Hospital & Dazhou First People’s Hospital, Dazhou, 635000, People’s Republic of China; 4Department of Innovation Research, Chengdu Institute of Chinese Herbal Medicine, Chengdu, People’s Republic of ChinaCorrespondence: Qixiong Zhang; Houkui Shi, Email zhangqixiong@uestc.edu.cn; 976336742@qq.comAbstract: Pulpitis (Pul) and periodontitis (PD) are oral infectious diseases with extremely high global prevalence. These pathologies can induce severe pain, significantly elevate the risk of tooth mobility and eventual tooth loss, and have been confirmed to be closely correlated with multiple chronic systemic disorders including diabetes mellitus and cardiovascular diseases. Conventional clinical interventions for these diseases are frequently characterized by incomplete debridement and inefficient drug delivery. Additionally, the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance presents an ongoing challenge for traditional treatments, leading to overall unsatisfactory therapeutic outcomes. Nanomaterials offer an innovative approach to overcoming the aforementioned limitations of conventional treatments, owing to their distinctive physicochemical properties, intrinsic antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, as well as their ability to facilitate bone and cementum regeneration. However, the development of nanotherapeutics for Pul and PD currently remains inefficient. Most existing nanomaterial systems exhibit poor adaptability to the complex oral microenvironment, and are unable to achieve closed-loop dynamic regulation during the entire therapeutic process. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has brought unprecedented new opportunities to resolve these bottlenecks. By enabling an intelligent "sense-analyze-respond” feedback loop, AI can optimize the key performance parameters of nanomaterials and facilitate dynamic adjustment of clinical therapeutic regimens. This review firstly sorts out the pathogenesis of Pul and PD, as well as the corresponding targeted intervention strategies enabled by nanomaterials. Subsequently, the existing nanomaterial systems are categorized based on their dimensional classification (0D to 3D), and their therapeutic applications and current limitations in the treatment of both diseases are analyzed. Finally, this paper discusses the research prospects of AI-enabled nanomaterials in structural design and in the management of Pul and PD. This review aims to provide theoretical reference for the development of more precise and effective therapeutic strategies for these two prevalent oral diseases.Keywords: oral infection, pulpitis, periodontitis, nanomaterials, artificial intelligence

papers.title: Оптимизация маршрутизации беременных с факторами риска гестационного сахарного диабета на уровне первичной медико-санитарной помощи: разработка и внедрение стандартизированного чек-листа
papers.authors: А.А. Есжанова, Ризаев Ж.А., Л.Р. Агабабян
papers.abstract: Relevance: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a pressing medical and social problem, as its development is associated with an increased risk of obstetric complications and adverse perinatal outcomes. The effectiveness of prevention and early detection largely depends on the quality of primary health care (PHC) organization, where a pregnant woman’s first visit and risk-factor assessment take place. Mechanisms for early identification of at-risk patients and their timely referral for specialized examinations still need improvement. Developing and implementing a standardized checklist at the PHC level will standardize the GDM risk assessment process, improve continuity between stages of medical care, and create conditions for earlier initiation of preventive and therapeutic measures. The study aimed to develop an evidence-based clinical checklist and referral algorithm for the early identification of pregnant women at high risk of GDM. Materials and Methods: Based on a retrospective cohort study of 600 delivery records (300 with GDM, 300 controls), we identified GDM predictors using multivariate logistic regression and ROC analysis. Results: We developed a prognostic risk scale for GDM (AUC = 0.849). Cut-off points and score weights for predictors were: chronic arterial hypertension (3 points), previous GDM(3 points), BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²(3 points), HbA1c ≥ 5.51%(2 points), fasting glucose ≥ 4.81 mmol/L(2 points), positive family history(2 points), age ≥ 30 years(1 point). A total score ≥ 3 showed high sensitivity and specificity for GDM development. We proposed an early referral algorithm for pregnant women before 12 weeks of gestation. Conclusion: Implementing the modified checklist in practice allows general practitioners to shift from late screening to personalized targeted prevention of GDM.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Rubric-Based Essay Grading in Dental Hygiene Education: A retrospective observational study.
papers.authors: Courtney D Routh, Richard M. Halpin, J Nathaniel Holland, Tulsi Patel
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence-based grading demonstrated strong reproducibility and rapid evaluation, with systematic differences in score calibration compared with faculty assessment. The use of AI may complement faculty-driven assessment by supporting consistent, scalable grading practices in dental hygiene education, potentially enhancing grading reliability while reducing faculty workload.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Public Governance: Its Impact on Citizens' Trust and Government Legitimacy
papers.authors: Mahmoud Khalifa
papers.journal: World Research of Political Science Journal
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming public governance by enabling record-breaking decisions with implications for citizen consensus and government legitimacy long sought. This study analyzes how AI-enabled governance influences these interrelated principles through a comparative policy study of Singapore and the United Arab Emirates — leaders in AI adoption. Using the PESTLE framework, the analysis reveals how AI complements the authorities’ transparency, commitment, fact-dissemination, and citizen participation, potentially strengthening public trust and legitimacy. However, the findings show that those outcomes depend on context-specific elements and implementation techniques. A.I. The rapid autonomy and complexity of AI systems pose challenges to citizen knowledge and acceptance, requiring adaptive governance models that can manage risks of misinformation, cyber threats, and social inequalities. This underscores the importance of comprehensive regulatory frameworks with per-firm and policy measures to protect the digital security landscape of AI integration in authorities, emphasizing the need for carefully nuanced approaches that align technology diffusion with societal values.

papers.title: An Analytical Scoping Review of How Artificial Intelligence Reliance Deprives Academics of Creative Synthesis
papers.authors: Parhlad Singh Ahluwalia
papers.journal: Siddhanta's International Journal of Advanced Research in Arts & Humanities
papers.abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now embedded in academic reading, writing, and ideation. Its benefits for speed and fluency are well publicised. Its costs to the higher-order intellectual act that defines scholarship, creative synthesis, are far less examined. Creative synthesis means combining distant ideas, tolerating uncertainty, and producing a new conceptual arrangement that neither the sources nor the scholar held beforehand. Objective: This paper analyses how habitual reliance on AI systems can deprive academics of the conditions under which creative synthesis develops, and it appraises the strength of the evidence for this claim. Methods: A PRISMA-informed scoping review was conducted in two strands. Strand A was a transparent, title-level screening of the 117-record corpus supplied for this study. Strand B was a purposive search for theoretical and empirical anchor studies in cognitive psychology, creativity research, and AI ethics. Records were charted against five mechanisms of deprivation. Results: Twenty-nine corpus records and eighteen external sources were retained (n = 47). Evidence converged on five mechanisms: cognitive offloading, the loss of productive difficulty, automation complacency, output homogenisation, and epistemic narrowing. Experimental evidence shows that AI assistance raises individual output quality while reducing the diversity of ideas across a group, and that performance gains during assisted work do not always survive its removal. Conclusions: The evidence does not show that AI use is inherently harmful. It shows that unstructured, substitutive reliance erodes the effortful integrative processes on which synthesis depends. The paper closes with an evidence-graded framework for scholars and institutions.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Aeronautical Education: Towards an Ethical and Metacognitive Framework
papers.authors: Italo Serra Panetta, Carmen Teresa Ramírez Pérez
papers.journal: Revista Venezolana de Pedagogía y Tecnologías Emergentes
papers.abstract: El objetivo del artículo es develar los nudos críticos derivados del vacío normativo e institucional producto de la integración acelerada de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) de carácter generativo en la praxis pedagógica y científica universitaria en el Instituto Universitario de Aeronáutica Civil May (Av) Miguel Rodríguez (IUAC). Es el resultante de una investigación bajo la metódica cualitativa fundada en el paradigma Interpretativo con enfoque fenomenológico–hermenéutico. La unidad informante constó de seis informantes clave, tres docentes con doctorados y tres estudiantes de diversas carreras, seleccionados bajo criterios de idoneidad conceptual y operativa. La recolección de información se realizó mediante entrevistas en profundidad, procesadas con técnicas de categorización, triangulación cruzada y contrastación teórica. Los hallazgos revelan una marcada vulnerabilidad axiológica caracterizada por la erosión del pensamiento crítico reflexivo del discente y el riesgo de plagio sui generis. Como contribución medular se plantea la noción de conciencia ética tecnoeducativa, que postula la interconexión cibernético–humanista entre la técnica avanzada, los imperativos categóricos de responsabilidad y la preservación irrenunciable del juicio crítico.

papers.title: Exploring the Causes of Authenticity Crisis in Social Commerce: Consumer Perspectives from Indonesia
papers.authors: Nurul Haeriyah Ridwan
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of social commerce has fundamentally transformed digital purchasing behavior while simultaneously intensifying concerns regarding the authenticity of online commercial interactions. Consumers are increasingly exposed to manipulated digital content, undisclosed commercial partnerships, and artificial intelligence (AI)-generated promotional materials, leading to a gradual erosion of trust within social commerce platforms. This study aims to explore the root causes of the authenticity crisis in Indonesian social commerce from consumers' perspectives and to identify strategic priorities for restoring digital trust. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed by integrating a systematic literature review with Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) involving experts in digital marketing, consumer behavior, and social commerce. The collected data were analyzed using a cause-and-effect (Fishbone) framework to identify multidimensional causal relationships, followed by the Urgency, Seriousness, and Growth (USG) matrix to prioritize critical determinants. The findings reveal that the authenticity crisis is primarily driven by three interconnected factors: non-transparent communication, fake customer reviews, and AI-generated promotional content without adequate disclosure. These issues significantly increase information asymmetry, weaken the credibility of digital information, and reduce consumer confidence in online purchasing decisions. The study suggests that restoring authenticity requires an integrated strategy emphasizing transparent communication, verified user-generated content, responsible AI governance, and stronger platform accountability. Theoretically, the findings extend the Resource-Based View and Signaling Theory by positioning digital authenticity as a strategic intangible resource for sustainable competitive advantage. Practically, this research provides a strategic roadmap for businesses, digital platforms, and policymakers to strengthen consumer trust and promote a more transparent, ethical, and sustainable social commerce ecosystem in Indonesia.

papers.title: A Comparative Analysis of Plagiarism across Written and Technical Disciplines
papers.authors: Parhlad Singh Ahluwalia
papers.journal: Siddhanta's International Journal of Advanced Research in Arts & Humanities
papers.abstract: Background: Plagiarism is usually discussed as one phenomenon with one definition and one remedy. Scholarly disciplines, however, differ in what they treat as an original contribution, how they attribute knowledge, and which artefacts they produce. Those artefacts range from argumentative prose to source code, numerical data, mathematical derivations and images. This study asks whether plagiarism means the same thing in written disciplines (humanities, social sciences, law and literary studies) as in technical disciplines (engineering, computer science, mathematics and the natural sciences). Methods: A PRISMA-guided structured narrative synthesis was carried out, drawing on the PRISMA 2020 statement and its scoping-review extension. Eligible sources were peer-reviewed reviews, meta-analyses, empirical surveys, detection-technology evaluations, linguistic analyses and policy documents published before 2026. Findings were charted against seven analytical dimensions: definition, unit of borrowing, citation culture, detection feasibility, prevalence evidence, sanction and remediation, and susceptibility to generative artificial intelligence. Results: Written disciplines concentrate risk in textual and ideational appropriation, including patchwriting, uncredited paraphrase and contract authorship. Technical disciplines distribute risk across code, data, figures, mathematical content and reused methods text. Text-matching software serves the first group reasonably well and the second group poorly. Prevalence estimates are not comparable across fields because the underlying instruments differ. Evaluations of AI-text detectors consistently show limited accuracy and demonstrable bias against non-native writers. Conclusions: Plagiarism is best understood as a family of discipline-conditioned integrity breaches rather than a single offence. Policy, detection and pedagogy that ignore this conditioning will over-penalise some communities and under-detect misconduct in others. A discipline-sensitive, education-first integrity framework is proposed, together with eight citable propositions to guide later empirical work.

papers.title: Growing Up With Conversational AI: A Developmental Framework for Adolescent Agency Over Conversational AI Use
papers.authors: Mary Kate Koch, Shanting Chen, Cindy Liu, Renkai Ma, Natalie C. Ebner
papers.abstract: Conversational generative AI has rapidly reached majority adoption among U.S. adolescents. These systems now provide advice, emotional support, academic assistance, simulated social interaction, and opportunities for identity exploration at a critical phase in development when mental health needs are rising and capacities for self-regulation, autonomy, and social competence are still developing. Scholars and clinicians have raised urgent questions about what these systems do to adolescents, and early findings point to both benefits and risks. In this article, we ask what adolescents do with AI and introduce the concept of adolescent agency over conversational AI use: the degree to which adolescents purposefully direct, critically evaluate, and set limits on their engagement with conversational AI. Existing constructs such as AI literacy and AI self-efficacy describe what young people know or believe about AI and the risks associated with its use, but they do not capture how adolescents exercise agency across areas of their lives. We identify nine processes that arise at the intersection of conversational AI’s features and key developmental tasks during the period of adolescence, which we label AI-ERA: autonomy, identity, emotion regulation, relationships, and achievement. We distinguish this agency from existing constructs, including agentic engagement with AI and AI overreliance, and then propose how it is shaped by adolescents’ developing capacities, adult scaffolding, and peer influence. We conclude with implications for families, schools, clinicians, and researchers, as well as considerations regarding the design, regulation, and ethics of AI systems.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Strategic Enabler in Enhancing Firm Performance: A Comparative Study of SMEs and Large Firms
papers.authors: Febiha Yildiz
papers.journal: Journal of Management and Training for Industries
papers.abstract: In the current study, the researcher explores the impact of AI on firm performance, paying attention to the differences between SMEs and large enterprises in this respect. Combining the theories of the diffusion of innovations and dynamic capabilities, the research takes advantage of a comparative secondary-data approach based on recent EU sources. Data will be extracted from the EU publications like Digitalisation in Europe 2025 Edition, Eurostat statistics on AI (2025), Eurostat statistics on innovation-active enterprises (2024), and OECD Compendium of Productivity Indicators 2025. In addition, peer-reviewed articles on AI capability, AI adoption by SMEs, and firm performance will be analysed. According to empirical findings, the discrepancy is obvious and related to size: in 2025, 19.95% of EU enterprises used at least one AI technology, whereas AI adoption was more common in larger companies (55.03%), compared to SMEs (17.00%). Furthermore, there was a difference in complementary capabilities, with larger companies being characterised by higher levels of ICT training, digital intensity, cloud adoption, e-sales, and innovation. Moreover, the major reasons for AI non-adoption among companies that had considered this technology were a lack of adequate expertise, legal uncertainty, as well as data protection issues. In conclusion, it may be stated that there exist certain conditions of AI adoption, which depend on company size. Thus, the paper demonstrates that firm size is associated with discrepancies in the strategic enabling mechanisms and the outcomes in terms of performance. Thanks to the comparative consideration of harmonised EU evidence, the study makes significant theoretical and practical contributions into the topic under investigation. It should be noted, however, that the analysis is primarily descriptive and does not consider financial accounting data. The data comes from sources with slightly different size definitions and reference periods.

papers.title: Motor imagery in children born preterm and its association with degree of prematurity and motor skill
papers.authors: Tal Krasovsky, Samar Safe
papers.abstract: Background. Mental imagery is the ability to generate or reconstruct a perceptual experience voluntarily or involuntarily in the absence of a corresponding external stimulus. Motor imagery is the cognitive simulation of movement without overt movement and is considered relevant to body schema, motor planning, praxis, and motor learning. Children born preterm are at increased risk for neurodevelopmental delays and for difficulties in developing internal body representations, potentially affecting later motor imagery and motor skill. Aim. This study will examine motor imagery in children born preterm and test whether motor imagery is associated with degree of prematurity and with motor skill. Design. Single-center, cross-sectional observational study. Children aged 8 to 10 years who were born before 37+0 weeks of gestation will attend one assessment session. Motor imagery will be assessed using the Hand Laterality Test (HLT). Motor function will be assessed using the Movement Assessment Battery for Children, Second Edition (M-ABC-2). Parents will complete the Developmental Coordination Disorder Questionnaire and the Conners Parent Rating Scale. Medical data will be extracted from the clinical record. Planned added outcome measurement. In addition to HLT accuracy and mean reaction time, this preregistration specifies reaction time variability metrics based on the approach used by Breuer Asher et al. [5]: within-participant reaction time variance, reaction time coefficient of variation, and a composite motor imagery score combining accuracy with reaction time variability.

papers.title: How Implementation Context Shapes Clinician Acceptance and Engagement with Guideline-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: A Qualitative Study
papers.authors: Mehta P, Pavani Rangachari, Tran A, Susan Lambrecht-Smith
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Purvi Mehta,1 Pavani Rangachari,1 Alvin Tran,1 Susan Lambrecht-Smith21Department of Population Health and Leadership, School of Health Sciences, University of New Haven, West Haven, CT, USA; 2Department of Health Professions, School of Health & Natural Sciences, Mercy University, Dobbs Ferry, NY, USACorrespondence: Pavani Rangachari, Department of Population Health and Leadership, School of Health Sciences, University of New Haven, 300 Boston Post Road, West Haven, CT, 06516, USA, Tel +91 203-479-4274, Email prangachari@newhaven.eduBackground: Guideline-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools have become central to promoting evidence-based, high-quality primary care. Despite widespread implementation, clinician adoption and sustained use remain inconsistent. Existing research has typically examined technological usability or organizational implementation factors separately, providing limited understanding of how these influences interact in real-world primary care settings. This study examined how organizational implementation context and clinician technology acceptance jointly shape adoption and sustained use of guideline-based CDS tools in US primary care using an integrated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) perspective.Methods: A qualitative study using reflexive thematic analysis was conducted with 13 US primary care clinicians, including physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and pharmacists with prescribing authority. Participants were purposively recruited from diverse ambulatory settings. Semi-structured interviews explored experiences with CDS usability, workflow integration, organizational support, trust, cognitive burden, and implementation processes. Data were analyzed iteratively using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis, informed by CFIR and TAM.Results: Six interrelated themes emerged. Clinician acceptance and sustained use of CDS were shaped by (1) workflow integration, (2) organizational legitimacy and leadership support, (3) preservation of clinical judgment, particularly with emerging AI-enabled CDS, (4) social reinforcement and team-based implementation, (5) cognitive and resource constraints, and (6) clinician role, experience, and digital comfort. Across themes, acceptance was driven less by technological capability than by the interaction of workflow design, organizational context, implementation climate, trust, and clinician perceptions.Conclusion: Guideline-based CDS implementation is fundamentally a sociotechnical process requiring alignment between technology, workflow, organizational context, and clinician acceptance. Integrating CFIR and TAM provides a comprehensive framework for understanding these interactions. The findings informed the TRUST framework, which offers practical implementation guidance emphasizing tailored workflow integration, reinforced organizational legitimacy, usability, social reinforcement, and transparent, trustworthy AI-supported CDS to support sustainable implementation in primary care.Keywords: clinical decision support systems, primary care, implementation science, technology acceptance model, CFIR, sociotechnical systems, electronic health records, AI in healthcare

papers.title: Cross-Domain AI Evolution: A Framework for Capability Transformation and Value Enhancement
papers.authors: Minh Quang Nguyen, Linh Anh Tran
papers.journal: European International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Management Studies
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly evolving from domain-specific automation toward reusable capabilities that can be transferred, recombined, governed, and commercialized across heterogeneous application environments. However, cross-domain AI adoption is not equivalent to simply migrating an existing model from one sector to another. Effective migration requires adaptation of technical capabilities, data structures, governance mechanisms, incentives, security controls, and value-generation processes. This research develops a conceptual framework for understanding cross-domain AI evolution as a progression from capability transfer to capability transformation and ultimately to value enhancement. The framework synthesizes evidence from studies addressing AI-enabled medical image segmentation, unsupervised learning, financial forecasting, ESG-related financial analysis, privacy-preserving digital commerce, AI commercialization, and AI-driven cybersecurity. The methodology employs comparative thematic synthesis and architectural abstraction to identify reusable capability layers and transformation mechanisms across domains. The analysis indicates that cross-domain AI value depends on four interdependent dimensions: capability portability, contextual adaptation, trustworthy governance, and measurable value realization. The resulting framework positions AI evolution as a continuous process in which technical capabilities are transferred, contextualized, integrated with domain constraints, and converted into economic, operational, scientific, or social value. The study contributes a structured theoretical model for researchers and practitioners seeking to design scalable AI systems capable of operating beyond their original application boundaries.

papers.title: แนวทางการพฒนาการบรหารวชาการในยคปญญาประดษฐ: กรณศกษาโรงเรยนเตรยมอดมศกษานอมเกลา ปทมธาน สงกดสำนกงานเขตพนท การศกษามธยมศกษาปทมธาน
papers.authors: Peerakorn Chotjirathanasak, Prompilai Buasuwan, Suchada Nanthachai
papers.abstract: The purposes of this research article were 1) to examine the current status, desired state, and needs regarding academic administration in the era of Artificial Intelligence at Triam Udom Suksa Nomklao Pathum Thani School; and 2) to develop guidelines for academic administration in the era of Artificial Intelligence of school. This study was a mixed-methods research divided into two phases: Phase 1 was a quantitative research involving a population of 76 administrators and teachers of Triam Udom Suksa Nomklao Pathum Thani School. The research instrument was a questionnaire with a reliability coefficient of 0.987. Data were analyzed using mean, standard deviation, and the Modified Priority Needs Index (PNI_modified); Phase 2 was the qualitative research conducted through focus group discussions with 15 administrators and teachers serving as heads of academic administration units. Data were analyzed using content analysis. The research findings revealed that 1) the overall current state of academic administration in the Artificial Intelligence era was at a high level (μ = 3.70, σ = 0.73), whereas the overall desired state was at the highest level (μ = 4.54, σ = 0.65). The top three areas of highest need were curriculum development (PNI_modified = 0.300), instructional management (PNI_modified = 0.254), and measurement and evaluation (PNI_modified = 0.243), respectively; 2) guidelines for developing academic administration in the Artificial Intelligence era comprised nine aspects: 1) regarding curriculum development, Artificial Intelligence should be used to analyze data for curriculum improvement; 2) in terms of teaching and learning management, the use of Artificial Intelligence in designing learning experiences should be encouraged; 3) in the aspect of measurement and evaluation, Artificial Intelligence should be used to collect and analyze learning outcomes; 4) regarding research aimed at improving the quality of education, Artificial Intelligence should be utilized to support research in an appropriate and ethical manner; 5) in terms of development of media, technology, and learning resources, support for resources and the enhancement of teachers' skills should be provided; 6) in the aspect of supervision, monitoring, and evaluation, Artificial Intelligence should be used to analyze data for teacher development; 7) in the aspect of promotion of academic knowledge within the community, Artificial Intelligence should be utilized to develop media and activities that aligned with community needs; 8) in terms of academic planning, Artificial Intelligence should be used to analyze data for systematic planning; and 9) regarding information management, Artificial Intelligence should be utilized to manage data and support the development of teaching and learning.

papers.title: How AI chatbots shape political attitudes when they are not prompted to persuade
papers.authors: Jens Koed Madsen, Sayeh Yousefi
papers.abstract: People increasingly turn to AI chatbots to find information, including information about politicians and political issues. Given evidence that Large Language Models (LLMs) have high persuasive capacities, this has raised concerns about their potential to have undue influence on political attitudes. However, most existing research on AI persuasion explicitly prompts the LLM to persuade the user, which is not representative of how people typically engage with LLMs. Whether undirected political conversations with LLMs shift political attitudes, and whether personalisation amplifies any such effect, remains unclear. We address these questions across two studies. First, in a quota-matched survey of UK adults (N = 2,137), we find that political use of AI is already widespread and its outputs are generally perceived as being politically neutral. Second, in a pre-registered randomised controlled trial (N = 2,081), participants conversed with an LLM about either a politician or political issue, with the LLM not being prompted to persuade. We find that conversations about politicians increased favourability toward them, while conversations about policies modestly reduced support. Conversation personalisation did not amplify these effects. Our findings show that AI chatbots are already a meaningful source of political information in the UK, and that undirected chatbot conversations can influence political attitudes.

papers.title: Generative AI and L2 Cognitive Processing: An Exploratory Study of AI Use among First-Year University Language Learners
papers.authors: Lawrennce Lau Man Sum
papers.abstract: This study examines how first-year university L2 learners use generative AI across language-learning tasks. Its long-term goal is to investigate how different forms of AI use shape learners’ engagement in SLA-related cognitive processes, such as noticing, retrieval, language production, feedback processing, and monitoring, and how these differences may eventually influence L2 acquisition. Generative AI is not assumed to create new cognitive processes or produce a fixed learning effect. Rather, its immediate generation, adjustable assistance, and multi-turn interaction may support, repeat, delay, or bypass existing SLA processes. The present study therefore identifies recurring patterns of natural AI use and provides an empirical basis for selecting a specific cognitive process for subsequent controlled research (Godwin-Jones, 2024; Han, 2024).

papers.title: GEOGRAPHICAL EDUCATION IN PORTUGAL: PATHS TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH
papers.authors: Cristiana Martinha
papers.journal: International online journal of education and teaching
papers.abstract: Geography Education has in recent years undergone significant development in Portugal, that it is also observed by the crescent number of doctoral theses defended on the matter. The objective of this article is to present a content analysis of these theses underlining key topics developed and identifying issues that need to be developed in the next years, especially Artificial Intelligence. To the international community in Geography Education, this analysis also gives deep knowledge about this reality in Portugal and motivates similar studies in other countries that can contribute to the development of Geography Education knowledge around the world. Geography Education is a research field that connects “Geography” and “Education”. As Geçit (2010) shows, the process of Geography Education development as a specific research area occurred in several countries. Portugal has seen the development of this research field since 2000. We built a database of doctoral theses in Geography Education in Portugal. In this content analysis, we identified the following key topics: Geography Teacher Education; Education for Sustainable Development and Environmental Education in Geography; Citizenship Education in Geography; Technologies in Geography Teaching; Pedagogy and Curriculum in Geography, and Theory of Geography and Geography Education. The next graph shows the specific themes that these theses developed. The analysis of these theses shows that there are still some topics not worked on in doctoral theses in Geography Education in Portugal, such as Artificial Intelligence, Hazards Education, Misconceptions in Geography Education, Powerful Knowledge in Geography Education, and others. For the near future, Artificial Intelligence is the challenge topic to be developed. A reflection on this matter must be done. With this research, we want to stimulate the Commission on Geographical Education of UGI to continue to construct a database of master’s and doctoral theses on Geography Education around the world, which is still ongoing. We truly believe this database can help researchers in several countries, new doctoral candidates, and the development and recognition of Geography Education.

papers.title: AI as a Mountain Shepherd’s Doll, a Trusted Companion, and a Tool with Intellectual Reciprocity: Essay
papers.authors: Mario Schlegel
papers.abstract: Die KI als neues technologisches Werkzeug, das unser Zusammenleben in vielen Bereichen verändert, wird aus mythologischer Perspektive betrachtet, wobei auch evolutionsbiologische und psychotherapeutische Gesichtspunkte einbezogen werden. Diese Arbeit geht davon aus, dass die KI eine aktuelle Manifestation des Mythos der Herstellung künstlicher Menschen darstellt, wie er bereits bei den alten Griechen zum Ausdruck kommt. Damals galt dies als Frevel gegen die Götter. Heute besteht die Gefahr, dass die KI zum Frevel gegen die Natur des Menschen als selbstbestimmtes Individuum wird. Als Beispiel, an dem diese Problematik gezeigt wird, dient die Sennenpuppe, ein Sagenmotiv aus den Alpen. Es zeigen sich Parallelen zwischen der in der Sage lebendig gewordenen und selbstständig handelnden Puppe und heutigen Geschehnissen rund um die KI. Wird sie als Instrument zur Machtausübung benutzt oder als Werkzeug, das allen dient? Oder unterwirft sie uns und handelt selbstständig, ohne dass wir sie kontrollieren können? Die Kontrolle zu behalten über die KI entscheidet, ob sie zu einer gesellschaftlichen Utopie oder Dystopie führen wird. Auf der individuellen Ebene im Umgang mit der KI zeigt sich ihre Anthropomorphisierung als Problem, eine Tatsache, die sich auf dem Hintergrund unserer sozialen Fähigkeiten ableitet.

papers.title: AI-Supported Inside Reading for Academic Word List Development: Effects on Vocabulary Learning and Sentence Writing in an Azerbaijan, EFL University Classroom
papers.authors: Banovsha Ibrahimova, Nurana Mammadova, Ulviyya Safarova, Alaviyya Bahruz Nuri, Elnara Edilova, Zulfiyya Ismail
papers.journal: International online journal of education and teaching
papers.abstract: The current study analyzed the impact of using AI-supported inside reading on the acquisition of the words of the Academic Word List (AWL) and sentence writing (SW) performance of EFL university students in Azerbaijan. Sixty undergraduate students were randomly assigned to an experimental and a control group, following a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control group design. The study drew upon the theory of AI-mediated feedback and adopted a combination of structured academic reading and the Involvement Load Hypothesis from the field of vocational education to ensure that both receptive and productive lexical development were encouraged using AI-mediated feedback. The experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in gain scores (in AWL) (F(1,57) = 358.72, p < .001, η²p = .863), showing an average gain score of 10.83 points (43.4%) while the control group gained an average score of 2.87 points (11.6%). Sentence writing outcomes followed the same pattern (F(1, 57) = 452.20, p < .001, η²p = .888), with experimental gains of 12.50 points (39.9%) substantially exceeding control gains of 2.30 points (7.6%). A high correlation between AWL–SW (r = .74, p < .001) in the experimental group was obtained, which indicated that receptive and productive vocabulary development occurred simultaneously. The results of the research support the use of the inside reading pedagogical approach with the assistance of artificial intelligence as an effective method in academic vocabulary teaching in the post-Soviet university context. The limitations are a single-site sample and the lack of delayed retention measurement.
