papers.title: When AI Therapists Feel Human: The Role of Social Judgments and Psychological Closeness in Mental Health App Adoption
papers.authors: JEONG SOO KIM

papers.title: From Consultation to Partnership: Leadership for Patient, Family, and Community Engagement in People-Centred Health Systems in LMICs: A Narrative Review
papers.authors: Ahmed MA
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Mohamed Abubakar AhmedDepartment of Critical Care Medicine, Dr. Sumait Hospital, SIMAD University, Mogadishu, SomaliaCorrespondence: Mohamed Abubakar Ahmed, Department of Critical Care Medicine, Dr. Sumait Hospital, SIMAD University, Mogadishu, Somalia, Tel +252615663300, Email mohamedabubakara@simad.edu.so; mohamedabukar320@gmail.comAbstract: People-centred health systems depend on more than inviting patients, families, and communities to provide feedback. Meaningful engagement requires opportunities for people to influence decisions and healthcare organizations that can respond to their priorities. This structured narrative review used targeted searches of PubMed-indexed literature and World Health Organization sources to identify relevant reviews, health-systems studies, and recent evidence. The synthesis focused on leadership approaches that support a shift from one-way consultation to meaningful partnership in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), drawing on literature on community participation, patient and public involvement, co-creation, social accountability, and people-centred care. The literature indicates that partnership is more credible when leaders create inclusive representation, share decision-making, allocate time and resources, clarify accountability, and close feedback loops by showing how community input affects services. Common barriers include hierarchical decision processes, limited institutional capacity, unequal opportunities to participate, communication gaps, and poor follow-through on feedback. Drawing these findings together, this review proposes the LISTEN leadership framework: Listen, Include, Share Decisions, Train and Resource Participation, Establish Accountability Loops, and Notice Equity and Outcomes. The framework is presented as a practical synthesis rather than a validated instrument. People-centred leadership should therefore be assessed not only by whether patients and communities are invited to participate, but also by whether their involvement influences decisions, strengthens trust and responsiveness, and contributes to more equitable and higher-quality health systems.Keywords: people-centred care, patient experience, healthcare leadership, community engagement, quality improvement, health systems

papers.title: INTERACTIVE METHODS OF TEACHING FOREIGN LANGUAGES IN TECHNICAL HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
papers.authors: Alla Martyniuk, Аlla Hubina, Natalia Kyseliuk, Svitlana Lobanova, Viktoriia Prykhodko, Alvina Alyieva
papers.journal: International online journal of education and teaching
papers.abstract: The aim of the article is to study the theoretical and methodological foundations and empirical substantiation of the feasibility of introducing interactive methods and artificial intelligence tools into the process of teaching foreign languages in technical institutions of higher education, as well as to develop a structural and functional model of their integration into the professionally oriented training of future engineers. Methods: a complex of theoretical (systemic, comparative, content analysis of scientific sources) and empirical methods was applied – analysis of official Eurostat statistical data, OECD and UNESCO reports; calculation of the aggregate index of digital-AI-educational activity; correlation analysis of the relationship between the level of digital competence and academic success; pedagogical modeling. Participants in the empirical study were not involved, since the work is based on the analysis of open statistical data and theoretical modeling. Data collection was carried out through a systematic review of scientific publications (from the Web of Science / Scopus databases) and official statistical products of Eurostat and OECD for the period 2022–2026. Data analysis was performed using thematic coding, comparative analysis, correlation analysis (Pearson coefficient) and structural-functional modeling. As a result, a stable positive dynamics of the use of online learning and generative AI by young people in EU countries was revealed (growth by 5.5 pp for 2022–2024), a direct correlation between the level of education and digital skills was confirmed (correlation coefficient with success r=0.67–0.71). A structural-functional model of the implementation of interactive methods in technical higher education was developed, which covers target, content, procedural, technological and assessment components, ensuring the integration of linguistic, professional and digital competencies.

papers.title: การพฒนาโมเดลความสมพนธเชงสาเหตและแนวทางการจดระบบนเวศการเรยนรทสงผลตอการเรยนรแหงอนาคตของผเรยน สงกดสำนกงานเขตพนทการศกษามธยมศกษาสโขทย
papers.authors: กฤษณวรรณ ยนต์นิยม, Nattakan Prachanban
papers.abstract: The objectives of this research article 1) to develop and verify a causal relationship model of learning ecosystems affecting learners' future learning under the Sukhothai Secondary Educational Service Area Office, with empirical data; and 2) to examine guidelines for organizing a learning ecosystem affecting learners’ future learning under the Sukhothai Secondary Educational Service Area Office. This study was a mixed-methods research. The quantitative research involved a sample of 192 students in Mathayom Suksa 4–6, selected via stratified random sampling. Two questionnaires were used, namely one regarding the learning ecosystem and another concerning learners' future learning with item-objective congruence (IOC) indices ranging from 0.80 to 1.00 and reliability coefficients of 0.952 and 0.961, respectively. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation coefficients, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. The qualitative research involved 5 key informants selected through purposive sampling; an interview form served as the research instrument, and data were analyzed using content analysis. The research findings revealed that 1) the causal relationship model of the learning ecosystem affecting learners' future learning was consistent with empirical data (p-value = 0.089, CFI = 0.994, TLI = 0.990, RMSEA = 0.050, and SRMR = 0.017. The organization of the learning ecosystem affecting learners' future learning had direct and total effect sizes of 0.801, statistically significant at the .05 level; 2) guidelines for organizing the learning ecosystem affecting learners' future learning comprised two aspects: (1) promoting a learning ecosystem by organizing environments and learning resources that were conducive to learners, developing learning management processes that encouraged participation, utilizing technology appropriately, developing teachers, and building collaborative networks; and (2) promoting learners' future learning by implementing learner-centered instruction, integrating digital technology and Artificial Intelligence, and fostering 21st-century skills, adaptability, collaborative learning, and lifelong learning.

papers.title: Banking Phygitalization: A Source of Value Creation
papers.authors: Hafsa MOUFAKKIR, Mohammed Qmichchou
papers.abstract: The digital transformation of banking has reshaped the ways in which customers access services and interact with financial institutions. Yet digital channels have not eliminated the relevance of the branch: some operations remain difficult to complete remotely, while customers differ considerably in their ability, willingness, and confidence to use digital services. Banking phygitalization responds to this tension by linking physical touchpoints with digital interfaces within a unified service environment. Such integration can generate relational and experiential value by combining technological convenience with human assistance and by adapting service delivery to individual circumstances. This conceptual paper examines how value may emerge from this hybrid configuration. It mobilizes two complementary perspectives—assemblage theory and value co-creation theory—to explain how interactions among customers, employees, technologies, channels, and other resources can contribute to value formation in contemporary banking.

papers.title: Unseen efforts, untold stress: Associations of workload and mental health among ASHA workers in rural West Bengal
papers.authors: Trina Paul Das, Upasana Chowdhury, Tamal Das, Somnath Gangopadhyay
papers.journal: INDIAN JOURNAL OF PHYSIOLOGY AND ALLIED SCIENCES
papers.abstract: Background: Health workers face continuous emotional pressure. The ASHA workers are not exempt from this and have to face high work-related stress while serving the community, and this can influence their mental health. The aim of this study is to assess the association of work nature, work-related physical strain, and psychological stress on the health status of ASHA workers in rural areas of West Bengal. Method: In this study, a total of 200 ASHA workers were initially approached, and 180 participants met the eligibility criteria and were included in the final analysis from the Kultali Block in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal. Parameters such as BMI, heart rate, and blood pressure were measured. Psychological stress was assessed using the DASS-42 questionnaire, and insomnia was checked by the Insomnia Severity Index(ISI) questionnaire. Results: Depression, anxiety, and stress were found to be moderately high to severely high in most participants. Severe anxiety was found to be present in 67.2% of the participants, while stress was moderate in more than 50% of them. Conclusion: ASHA workers suffer not only physically but emotionally as well, and hence, there is a dire need to give special attention to their psychological health.

papers.title: EVALUATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-SUPPORTED SUPERVISION APPLICATIONS IN EDUCATIONAL MANAGEMENT AND SUPERVISION
papers.authors: Ozgu Sanli, Fahriye Altınay, Gökmen Dağlı, Zehra Altınay, Betül Yıkıcı
papers.journal: International online journal of education and teaching
papers.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the current functioning of educational supervision, the advantages, disadvantages, limitations, risk factors, and integrability of AI-assisted supervision applications, and to determine opinions on the situation. The study, therefore, focuses on the problems existing in educational supervision, regulatory efforts to address these problems, and the problem situation regarding the use of AI-assisted supervision applications to solve these problems. In the study, a case study sub-design from qualitative research methods was uilized, employing semi-structured interview forms and in-depth interviews to obtain the opinions of educational supervisors regarding the use of AI-assisted supervision applications. Data were collected from 12 educational supervisors actively working at MEDDYK, affiliated with the Ministry of National Education of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, during the 2025-2026 academic year. They were selected using the Expert Sampling Method from Purposive Sampling Techniques. The findings have indicated that AI-assisted supervision applications provides convenience in all areas of the supervision process, saving time, improving archiving, and offering advantages to future generations of supervisors. However, while the findings highlight positive perceptions among supervisors, they also emphasize risk factors such as AI-assisted supervision potentially replacing humans, ethical issues related to malicious users gaining access to confidential information, and the inadequacy of the existing technological infrastructure in the TRNC. Although the research findings conclude that there is largely a positive perception, the general validity of these results should be questioned and supported by research conducted in different contexts. The study is expected to contribute to the literature on educational supervision and evaluation processes. The study suggests that teachers’ opinions and critics regarding AI-assisted supervision applications should be obtained from teachers, the existing internet and technology infrastructure in schools should be strengthened, in-service training on technology and information systems should be provided to teachers and school administrators, improvements should be made to the supervision criteria, and existing laws, regulations, and decrees should be reviewed and updated to meet current needs. Keywords: Educational supervision, Artificial Intelligence, AI-assisted supervision, digital transformation, ethics, data security

papers.title: Polymeric Nanomedicines for siRNA Delivery in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Emerging Therapeutic Strategies, Combination Approaches, and Translational Perspectives
papers.authors: Thalij KM, You HW, Habeeb M, Joan Vijetha Ratchagar, Khot VS, Gorde PL
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Karkaz M Thalij,1 Huay Woon You,2 Mohammad Habeeb,3 Joan Vijetha Ratchagar,4 Vidyarani Sujitkumar Khot,5 Prasad Laxman Gorde61Department of Food Science, College of Agriculture, Tikrit University, Tikrit, Iraq; 2Faculty of Science and Technology, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Bangi, Selangor, Malaysia; 3Department of Pharmaceutics, Crescent School of Pharmacy, B.S. Abdur Rahman Crescent Institute of Science and Technology, Chennai, Tamilnadu, India; 4Department of Pharmaceutics, School of Pharmacy, Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology, Chennai, Tamilnadu, India; 5Department of Pharmacology, School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Sanjay Ghodawat University, Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India; 6Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, College of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Pravara Institute of Medical Sciences (Deemed to be University), Loni, Maharashtra, IndiaCorrespondence: Mohammad Habeeb, Email mdhabeebqa@gmail.comAbstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma is the sixth most common cancer worldwide and a leading cause of cancer related mortality. Risk factors include chronic hepatitis B/C, obesity, alcohol abuse, diabetes and metabolic disorders. In advanced stages, normal treatments such as surgery, transplantation and chemotherapy are not as effective as tumors develop resistance and do not target oncogenic pathways well. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics have the potential to change treatment paradigms by silencing specific biological pathways, thus suppressing tumor progression. Polymeric nanoparticles (PNPs) such as poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA), polyethyleneimine (PEI) and stimuli-responsive copolymers have attracted attention as effective delivery systems for siRNA. These carriers protect siRNA from enzymatic degradation and facilitate its cellular uptake. Furthermore, the surface of the carriers can be modified with targeting ligands, eg, galactose or ASGPR antibodies, to improve tumor-specific delivery. The PNPs can be tuned to change their physical and chemical properties, are more stable and responsive to signals from the tumor microenvironment for regulated release. This means they perform better than lipophilic or metallic carriers. Hepatocyte specific absorption pathways even enhance the liver tropism. This review focuses on recent advances in siRNA based therapeutic strategies against hepatocellular carcinoma, with a special focus on PNPs mediated drug delivery systems. It describes significant oncogenic pathways like β-catenin and STAT3 and formulation techniques including nanoprecipitation and layer by layer assembly. The review also reports the increasing importance of artificial intelligence in siRNA design, formulation optimization, and personalized therapeutic methods to improve the clinical applicability of HCC treatment.Keywords: siRNA, hepatocellular carcinoma, polymeric nanomedicines, drug delivery

papers.title: Nano-Enabled Microfluidic Platforms for Functional Immunomonitoring in Pediatric Sepsis
papers.authors: Zhang Q, Ren H, Zhang H
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Qi Zhang,1,2 Hengjie Ren,2,3 Haiyang Zhang2,31Outpatient Department, West China Second University Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, People’s Republic of China; 2Key Laboratory of Birth Defects and Related Diseases of Women and Children, Sichuan University, Ministry of Education, Chengdu, People’s Republic of China; 3Department of Pediatrics, West China Second University Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, People’s Republic of ChinaCorrespondence: Haiyang Zhang, Department of Pediatrics, West China Second University Hospital, Sichuan University, No. 1416 Chenglong Avenue, Jinjiang District, Chengdu, Sichuan, 610041, People’s Republic of China, Tel/Fax +86 157 5627 3633, Email icudoc@163.comAbstract: Pediatric sepsis involves dynamic, developmentally conditioned immune dysfunction that a single cytokine concentration or one-time severity label cannot represent. This structured narrative Review examines how nano-enabled microfluidic systems could support blood-sparing, serial assessment of functional immune states in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). We separate soluble-protein concentration, cell phenotype, ex vivo stimulation response, cellular effector function, immunometabolic function, and physiology, linking each measurement class to its evidence level and permitted inference. Direct pediatric studies support the biological relevance of longitudinal antigen-presentation, inducible cytokine, lymphocyte, and metabolic readouts, but cohorts remain few, small, and heterogeneous; secondary-infection findings are conflicting. Recent pediatric studies of serial soluble biomarkers and temperature trajectories expand monitoring evidence but do not validate functional immune trajectories. Engineering studies demonstrate nanoscale capture, amplification, transduction, and low-volume processing, including portable multicytokine sensing, yet these Level 4 results do not constitute pediatric clinical validity. We propose a staged sample-to-answer architecture. It distinguishes patient draw from device input, controls stimulation and preanalytics, retains developmental context, and progresses from analytical validation through pediatric feasibility and clinical validity to prospective prediction and decision utility. Artificial intelligence is restricted to age adjustment, longitudinal modeling, multimodal fusion, uncertainty display, and clinician- or nurse-facing visualization. Within the verified accessible corpus through 16 September 2026, no prospectively validated pediatric longitudinal immune-function trajectory model or nano-enabled functional immune assay for immunomodulatory treatment selection was identified. The near-term objective is a verifiable measurement-and-interpretation pathway, not an autonomous treatment selector, tested in multicenter serial cohorts with transparent blood-volume accounting, independent validation, and PICU human-factors evaluation.Keywords: sepsis, pediatrics, nanomedicine, microfluidics, functional immunomonitoring, blood-sparing diagnostics

papers.title: ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization
papers.authors: Sungho Park, Wonjoong Kim, Jue Zhang, Wook-Shin Han, Pengfei Gao, Chanyoung Park, Yongqiang Yao, Rao Fu, Elsie Nallipogu, Qingwei Lin, Victor Rühle
papers.abstract: Automated harness optimization can substantially improve LLM agents by iteratively updating their prompts, tool interfaces, and control logic from execution feedback. However, existing methods primarily optimize how the harness is updated while largely fixing which training scenarios generate the feedback that drives those updates. As the harness evolves, the scenarios most useful for further optimization can change, suggesting that the training curriculum itself should adapt alongside the harness. We formulate this missing dimension of harness optimization as an automated curriculum learning problem and introduce ActiveSaddler. ActiveSaddler models the evolving curriculum as a non-stationary bandit with dynamically instantiated optimization targets. It abstracts recurring failures into reusable failure-pattern arms, estimates the potential learning progress from further targeting each pattern, and adaptively balances revisiting known weaknesses with exploring unseen scenarios for new ones. Optimization outcomes continually update both the set of discovered failure patterns and their priorities, allowing the curriculum to co-evolve with the harness. Experiments on GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench 2.0 show that ActiveSaddler consistently discovers stronger harnesses, improving test Pass@1 by 4.4 and 7.5 percentage points over the same harness optimizer using a scenario order fixed before optimization, respectively. Ablations further show that these gains depend on dynamically constructing optimization targets, estimating their evolving utility, and balancing continued optimization with new failure discovery. Together, these results establish automated curriculum learning as a new crucial optimization dimension for harness optimization.

papers.title: Supporting Perspective Acquisition and Opinion Formation on Societal Issues Through AI-Generated Japanese Rap Battle Debates
papers.authors: Ryota Mibayashi, Toru Urakawa, 大 高梨, Tomoya Morohoshi, Kanata Yamagishi, Ryuho Sekikawa, Yasuhiko Nishimura, Yuta Takeuchi, Hideaki Tamori, Takehiro Yamamoto, Hidenari Kiyomitsu, Hiroaki Ohshima
papers.abstract: Acquiring diverse perspectives and forming informed opinions on societal issues are essential for critical thinking and informed decision-making. Although observing debates between opposing viewpoints can promote perspective acquisition, conventional debates require substantial time and human resources, limiting their accessibility. This study investigates whether brief AI-generated rap battle-style debates can support perspective acquisition and opinion formation on societal issues. Rap battles are debate-style performances in which opposing viewpoints are expressed through rhymed verses, making them engaging while preserving the structure of argumentative dialogue. To conduct this investigation, we automatically generated rap battle-style debates using GPT-5.4-mini and presented them to participants with synthesized audio through a web-based viewing interface. We evaluated the educational effectiveness of this approach through a user study involving six participants who viewed 40 debates generated from topics on societal issues used in the All Japan Junior and Senior High School Debate Championships. The results showed that watching approximately 1.5 minute rap battle-style debates nearly doubled the number of opinions and discussion points identified by participants. Furthermore, participants reconsidered or changed their stances in 52.5% of the evaluated cases. These findings demonstrate that even brief AI-generated rap battle-style debates can effectively support perspective acquisition and opinion formation on societal issues.

papers.title: WIP: DBWorkout: A Gamified SQL Practice Platform to Support Formative Learning in Database Courses
papers.authors: Sehrish Basir Nizamani, Deepika Devaraj, Tien Nguyen, Khyati Goyal, Saad Nizamani, Sally Hamouda, Jaren Goldberg
papers.abstract: This research WIP paper presents DBWorkout, a web-based platform that supports formative SQL learning through sandbox-based execution, automated result-based feedback, and session-based gamification. Learning Structured Query Language (SQL) remains challenging for undergraduate students due to limited opportunities for interactive practice and immediate feedback. Students iteratively practice SQL on live database instances while receiving multi-dimensional feedback on query correctness, including row values, column structure, and ordering. To reduce instructor workload, DBWorkout incorporates large language model (LLM)-assisted tools for schema and task generation within a human-in-the-loop workflow. A pilot study with teaching assistants and a classroom deployment involving 170 undergraduate students across two in-class sessions show strong perceived learning value (90% agreement) and engagement (87% enjoyment), alongside low reported pressure (22%). However, only 42% of students found the automated feedback sufficiently actionable, a finding independently corroborated by 40% of open-ended responses raising feedback quality concerns, providing cross-method triangulation of this gap. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility and early pedagogical potential of DBWorkout while identifying directions for enhancing feedback quality and supporting sustained SQL learning.

papers.title: An Agile Branding Framework for Educational Startups in Volatile E-Learning Markets
papers.authors: Saeed Abbasi Zahandeh
papers.journal: AI and Tech in Behavioral and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: The e-learning market is a rapidly changing business ecosystem shaped by technological innovation, shifting educational policies, and evolving learner expectations. Static and linear branding approaches may therefore be inadequate for educational startups that must build trust while adapting quickly to market change. This study developed and tested an agile branding framework for educational startups. A quantitative, applied, descriptive-correlational design was used. The target population comprised founders and senior managers of 300 educational startups operating in Districts 2, 8, and 17 of Tehran, Iran. A proportionate stratified random sample of 169 individuals was invited to participate, and 158 valid questionnaires were analyzed (response rate = 93.5%). Data were collected using a researcher-developed instrument and analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling. Agile branding was operationalized through rapid responsiveness, value co-creation, and strategic iteration. The findings indicated significant positive effects of agile branding on business performance (β = 0.456, p < 0.001) and brand equity (β = 0.512, p < 0.001). Brand equity positively predicted business performance (β = 0.483, p < 0.001) and significantly mediated the relationship between agile branding and business performance (indirect β = 0.289, p < 0.001). Dynamic capabilities significantly strengthened the association between brand equity and business performance (β = 0.198, p = 0.004). The model explained 56.7% of the variance in brand equity and 54.7% of the variance in business performance; predictive relevance was supported for both endogenous constructs (Q² = 0.384 and 0.361, respectively). These results position agile branding as a strategic organizational capability that can help educational startups strengthen brand equity and improve performance in volatile digital education markets.

papers.title: Digital Transformation of Agribusiness: Pathways Towards Smart and Sustainable Food Systems in Nordic and Indian Agricultural Contexts
papers.authors: Anjali Adhikari
papers.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping agribusiness by integrating advanced technologies into production, processing, marketing, and supply chain management, thereby creating more efficient, resilient, and sustainable food systems. In India, increasing demand for food, climate variability, shrinking landholdings, and resource constraints have accelerated the need for smart agricultural solutions. This review examines the emerging role of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, precision agriculture, the Internet of Things, blockchain, big data analytics, drones, and digital platforms, in modernizing agribusiness and strengthening food value chains. It synthesizes recent scientific evidence on technological innovations, adoption patterns, opportunities, barriers, and sustainability outcomes across the agricultural sector. The review highlights that digital technologies improve productivity, resource-use efficiency, traceability, market connectivity, and climate resilience while supporting informed decision-making. However, challenges related to digital infrastructure, affordability, data governance, and digital literacy remain significant. The paper concludes that supportive policies, inclusive innovation, capacity building, and multi-stakeholder collaboration are essential to accelerate India's transition toward smart, resilient, and sustainable food systems.

papers.title: Advisory Bodies’ Principles for Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Independent Advisory and Evaluation Service
papers.journal: CGSPace A Repository of Agricultural Research Outputs (Consultative Group for International Agricultural Research)
papers.abstract: As the Secretariat for the Independent Science for Development Council (ISDC) and Standing Panel on Impact Assessment (SPIA), and implementing CGIAR’s independent evaluation function, IAES has adopted a set of principles providing a common framework for responsible use of AI. Considering lessons learned in implementation to date across IAES workstreams, learning from ongoing international discussions on responsible use of AI, along with evolving governance, seven principles are included: 1) Human agency and oversight; 2) Transparency; 3) Technical capacity and fitness for purpose; 4) Privacy and data governance; 5) Fairness and inclusion; 6) Social and environmental responsibility; and 7) Independence and accountability. Throughout its incremental testing and adoption of AI tools, CGIAR Advisory Bodies have been de-facto implementing numerous provisions listed. With the adoption of the principles, the document now serves a common reference point, allowing workstream-specific protocols to develop.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence tools in university LMS: Identification, classification, and integration trends through a systematic review
papers.authors: Orlando Ascayo León, José Francisco Robles León, Esteban Naupay Pérez, Yonson Tarazona Tucto
papers.abstract: La integración de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en los sistemas de gestión del aprendizaje (LMS) está transformando la educación superior al favorecer experiencias más personalizadas, interactivas y orientadas al seguimiento del estudiante. Sin embargo, la diversidad de herramientas disponibles dificulta su organización según funciones pedagógicas claramente diferenciadas. El objetivo de este artículo fue identificar y clasificar los tipos de herramientas de inteligencia artificial integradas en sistemas de gestión del aprendizaje utilizados en educación superior. Se desarrolló una revisión sistemática de la literatura, siguiendo las directrices PRISMA 2020, mediante una búsqueda realizada en Scopus y la aplicación de criterios de inclusión y exclusión previamente establecidos. Los resultados permitieron identificar seis categorías funcionales principales: gestión inteligente, personalización y adaptación, tutoría y asistencia inteligente, evaluación y retroalimentación, seguimiento y analítica, y generación de contenidos. Entre las herramientas más frecuentes se encontraron chatbots, asistentes conversacionales, sistemas adaptativos, analítica predictiva, agentes inteligentes, aplicaciones de IA generativa y sistemas de recomendación. Los beneficios reportados se relacionaron principalmente con personalización, retroalimentación inmediata, autonomía, participación y apoyo continuo, aunque persistieron limitaciones asociadas con privacidad, sesgo, precisión, infraestructura y dependencia tecnológica. Se concluye que la integración de IA en LMS debe responder prioritariamente a criterios pedagógicos y no solo tecnológicos.

papers.title: Association of Obesity with Microalbuminuria in Children and Adolescents with Diabetes Mellitus in a Tertiary Care Hospital of Bangladesh.
papers.authors: ST Huq, T Hamid, M Parveen, M B Hossain
papers.abstract: The study, a cross sectional survey, was carried out at the Changing Diabetes in Children (CDiC) Outpatient Department of CDiC, BIRDEM-2 Hospital over a 1-year period from July 2018 to June 2019. Diabetes mellitus was diagnosed according to WHO, ISPAD and Mohan's criteria. Height, weight and waist circumference were recorded and body mass index (BMI) scores were calculated as weight (kg)/height (m²). BMI was classified using the cutoff points (<5th percentile underweight, 5th - 85th percentile normal, 85th - <95th percentile overweight and ≥95th percentile as obese) using the Center for Disease control and Prevention growth chart. To determine microalbuminuria, urine microalbumin and spot urine creatinine were measured by Immunoturbidimetry method using 2000 DCA plus analyzer and Albumin Creatinine Ratio (ACR) was calculated. Microalbuminuria was defined when two consecutive samples of spot urine were positive. Statistical analysis was performed with the help of software SPSS for Windows (statistical package for social science), 20.0 version. Association between the two groups was evaluated by using Students chi square test. Of the total participant 512, type 1 diabetes mellitus were 61.9% and type 2 diabetes mellitus 38.1% were observed that microalbuminuria was 88.7% and macroalbuminuria was 3.6% in diabetes mellitus children and adolescents. The study revealed that overweight and obesity were high in microalbuminuria than other parameters of BMI and that were statistically significant (p<0.001). Early diagnosis and screening of these diabetic children and adolescents with obesity can regress microalbuminuria and also prevent further progression.

papers.title: GUIDED BY INNOVATION: A PHENOMENOLOGICAL STUDY OF VIRTUAL ELEMENTARY TEACHERS’ PERCEPTIONS OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE INTEGRATION
papers.authors: Lisa Marie Berry
papers.abstract: The purpose of this qualitative phenomenological study was to explore the lived experiences of elementary virtual teachers who integrate generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools in their pedagogical practices at a large elementary virtual school. Participants were purposively sampled because those in the specified virtual school program provided relevant, experience-based insights and allowed the researcher practical, feasible access (Creswell & Poth, 2018). The participant sample for this study consisted of virtual elementary teachers who taught students in kindergarten through fifth grade. The researcher conducted semi-structured interviews with 10 teachers. The researcher followed Creswell and Poth’s (2018) data analysis spiral to systematically analyze data and determine themes. Four themes emerged from significant participant statements: efficiency, preservation of the teacher role, instructional enhancement, and AI literacy. The themes suggest that elementary virtual teachers are consistently balancing the positive elements of efficiency and enhanced instructional quality with the adverse aspects of misinformation, privacy protection, ethical concerns, and misuse. The themes suggest that virtual elementary teachers view GAI as a dynamic tool; however, its value depends on thoughtful, informed, and human-centered application. Future research would build on the findings by expanding the participant population and focusing on early adopters and the longitudinal implications of GAI use.

papers.title: Evaluating the Reliability, Accuracy, and Readability of ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 in Providing Patient Education Related to Glenohumeral Joint Osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Mohamad Y. Fares, Tarishi Parmar, Peter Boufadel, Mohammad Daher, Jonathan Berg, Adam Z. Khan, Brian W. Hill, John G. Horneff, Joseph Albert Abboud
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Chatbots have been increasingly recognized as modern tools that provide patients with reliable health-related information. This study aimed to evaluate and compare ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4's ability to answer glenohumeral osteoarthritis-related questions. METHODS: Fifteen questions were derived from the 2020 AAOS Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Surgical Management of Glenohumeral Joint Osteoarthritis. Questions were categorized into three groups: risk factors, implant/intraoperative considerations, and pain/functional outcomes. ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were prompted with these questions, and responses were evaluated by four fellowship-trained shoulder and elbow surgeons. Each response was rated on a scale (scores:1-5) based on relevance, accuracy, clarity, completeness, and evidence-based support. Data was analyzed descriptively and statistically to compare the scores between ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4. RESULTS: Average score for ChatGPT-3.5 was 19.7/25, with "Risk Factor" prompts achieving the highest mean score. GPT-4 averaged 18.7/25, with "Functional Outcomes" prompts scoring highest. However, there were no statistically significant differences between different prompt themes for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. "Clarity" category received the highest score for GPT-3.5, while "Relevance" was highest for GPT-4. Both models scored lowest on "Evidence-based" prompts. On the Flesch- Kincaid scale, GPT-3.5 responses had a significantly higher score of 18.3 compared to GPT-4's 15.4, indicating a more difficult reading level in GPT-3.5's responses. CONCLUSION: Both ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 performed adequately in providing well-informed medical responses to patient queries about glenohumeral osteoarthritis. Future chatbot versions should focus on providing evidence-based content through systematic and reliable reviews of literature, in an accessible readable manner.

papers.title: Rethinking Regional Energy Poverty:An Intersectional Modelling Approach
papers.authors: Sara Tavakoli, Pedro Sampaio, Ali Hassanzadeh
papers.abstract: Energy poverty remains a persistent policy challenge across Europe, particularly in the context of the ongoing energy transition and rising pressure on household energy affordability (Washington2016). Despite extensive research, its underlying drivers are often treated as separate and additive. This study examines whether such approaches are sufficient to capture how vulnerability actually forms at the regional level. This assumption of separable effects can lead to misclassification of vulnerable groups and limit the effectiveness of policy targeting. To address this, a three-level modelling framework is developed in which intersectionality is operationalised as a mediating structure linking socio-economic characteristics to energy poverty (Crenshaw2013). Rather than treating drivers as independent, the framework captures how combinations of characteristics interact to produce vulnerability. The analysis uses regional data for England and combines statistical and machine learning methods to identify underlying patterns in the data. The results show that similar levels of energy poverty can emerge from different combinations of conditions. While a socio-economic gradient, related to labour market position, education, and health, plays a dominant role, additional intersectional patterns capture life-stage differences and energy system characteristics, particularly heating types. This suggests that identifying where energy poverty occurs is not enough on its own. What matters is identifying the root causes of energy poverty and how different drivers intersect to produce it. Modelling these relationships provides a more useful basis for place-based policy, especially in the context of Europe’s energy transition. Ongoing work extends this approach to finer spatial scales and develops a policy-oriented modelling framework. This is intended to function as a policy lab tool to assess how different interventions may affect different population groups, with particular attention to fairness across regions.

papers.title: Protocol for the Registration to Conduct the SLR on "Factors Influencing the Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced and Inclusive Library Services for Patrons with Disabilities"
papers.authors: Khurram Shahzad
papers.abstract: Problem Statement: The growing application of artificial intelligence in libraries has created opportunities to improve the accessibility, personalization, efficiency and responsiveness of library services. However, the transition from general awareness and experimentation with AI to the effective adoption of Generative AI (GenAI) for inclusive services remains insufficiently understood, particularly in relation to patrons with disabilities (PWDs). Existing studies have examined AI readiness, awareness, staff perceptions, service innovation, accessibility and emerging applications of AI in libraries (Lund et al., 2020; Ajani et al., 2022; Echedom and Okuonghae, 2021; Mwantimwa and Msoffe, 2025). Some studies have considered AI-enabled accessibility and disability inclusion, including AI-powered services for people with visual disabilities and the potential of GenAI to support individualized and accessible learning and services (Abutayeh et al., 2025; Almufareh et al., 2024; Eilert and Robinson, 2025; Gazpio, 2025; Sakowicz and Hamidi, 2024). However, this body of evidence is dispersed across different technological, organizational, service, accessibility, and disability-related contexts that make it difficult to establish a consolidated understanding of the factors that influence GenAI adoption for inclusive library service delivery. The problem is further complicated by the fact that adoption of GenAI is not determined solely by the availability and functionality of the technology. Library staff readiness, AI literacy, organizational support, institutional policies, technological infrastructure, service compatibility, privacy and security, ethical considerations, and users’ diverse accessibility requirements can affect whether and how GenAI is incorporated into library services (Lund et al., 2020; Ajani et al., 2022; McCusker and Michalak, 2025; Gmiterek and Kotuła, 2025; Khan, 2025). At the same time, the use of GenAI for PWDs introduces additional concerns related to accessibility, personalization, bias, privacy, digital equity, and the suitability of AI-generated information and interactions for users with diverse disabilities (Abutayeh et al., 2025; Almufareh et al., 2024; Eilert and Robinson, 2025). These conditions create a practical and knowledge-based problem for libraries. Although GenAI may support more accessible and personalized services, libraries require clear evidence about the conditions that facilitate its adoption and the challenges that may constrain its responsible and sustainable integration. A further problem is the fragmentation of the existing literature. Research has addressed AI adoption and readiness in libraries, emerging GenAI applications, AI-supported service delivery, and disability-oriented applications separately while broader reviews have examined the application of GenAI in library operations and services (Ajani et al., 2022; Mwantimwa and Msoffe, 2025). However, the available evidence does not provide a sufficiently consolidated account of how technological, organizational, human, ethical, accessibility and service-related factors interact in shaping the adoption of GenAI specifically for enhanced and inclusive library services for PWDs. Consequently, library decision-makers and practitioners may lack a synthesized evidence base for understanding the conditions under which GenAI can be incorporated to improve services while addressing the diverse requirements and potential risks associated with disability-inclusive access. Therefore, the research problem addressed by this systematic literature review is the lack of a consolidated and systematically synthesized evidence base identifying the factors that influence GenAI adoption, the challenges that constrain its integration and the implementation considerations required for enhanced and inclusive library service delivery to PWDs. Addressing this problem is important because identifying adoption-related factors alone does not explain how libraries can translate the potential of GenAI into inclusive practice. A systematic synthesis is therefore needed to bring together the dispersed evidence, identify recurring enabling factors and barriers, and use these findings to develop a conceptual framework that can guide libraries in planning, implementing, and sustaining GenAI-supported services for patrons with disabilities. Accordingly, this review examines the factors influencing GenAI adoption, the challenges associated with its integration, and the elements that can inform a framework for enhanced and inclusive library service delivery to PWDs. Objectives The study’s objectives are as follows: • To identify the factors influencing the adoption of Generative AI (GenAI) for enhanced library services delivery to patrons with disabilities (PWDs) • To reveal challenges for integrating GenAI in providing inclusive access to library service delivery to PWDs • To propose a framework for the incorporation of GenAI in library settings to support enhanced and inclusive library service delivery to PWDs Research Questions The research questions of the study are as below: • Which are the factors influencing the adoption of Generative AI (GenAI) for enhanced library services delivery to patrons with disabilities (PWDs)? • Which challenges are associated to the integration of GenAI for enhanced and inclusive library service delivery to PWDs? • What framework can be proposed for the incorporation of GenAI in library settings to support enhanced and inclusive library service delivery to PWDs?

papers.title: Examining the Relationships Between Executive Functioning and Mind Wandering in Individuals and with and without Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
papers.authors: Chelsie M. Hart, Julia W. Y. Kam
papers.abstract: This two-part study is part of a larger doctoral dissertation project which aims to examine the relationship between executive functioning and mind wandering multidimensionally, and then extend this by examining how these relationships change in individuals with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) (Hart et al., n.d.). Specifically, we will look at the relationships between executive functioning in terms of working memory, task switching, and response inhibition facets; and mind wandering in terms of frequency, meta-awareness, and intentionality aspects. We will use common cognitive tasks to quantify ability in each executive functioning facet. For mind wandering, this study will utilize thought sampling during a separate task to measure how frequently individuals mind wander in general and mind wander with or without meta-awareness and intention. We will also examine electrophysiological correlates of these thought patterns using electroencephalogram (EEG) measures. Finally, we will examine how ADHD symptom severity -measured using a clinical rating scale- impacts the relationships between the facets of executive functioning and aspects of mind wandering in individuals with and without diagnosis of ADHD. Previous findings for the relationship between executive functioning and mind wandering have been inconsistent when separate facets of executive functioning are considered (e.g., Kam & Handy, 2014; Keulers & Jonkman, 2019) and few studies have examined the mind wandering aspects of meta-awareness and intentionality. This unexplored territory is important to investigate to inform contrasting theoretical accounts of the relationship between executive functioning and mind wandering (Kane & McVay, 2012; Smallwood, 2010; Smallwood & Schooler, 2006; Thomson et al., 2015). This is also important clinically for disorders such as ADHD, a heterogeneous disorder associated with executive functioning deficits and frequent mind wandering (e.g., working memory: Agnew-Blais et al., 2020; task switching: Irwin et al., 2019; response inhibition: Boonstra et al., 2010; Roselló et al., 2020; mind wandering: Madiouni et al., 2020). Research over the past decades has increasingly demonstrated how detrimental ADHD can be in multiple areas of life, across the lifespan (Barkley et al., 2006; Christiansen et al., 2021; Kessler et al., 2010; Küpper et al., 2012; Luo et al., 2019). Whether or not the relationship between executive functioning and mind wandering differs across the spectrum of ADHD symptom severity, this research will inform what behavioural and electrophysiological dimensions could be used to examine the cognitive underpinnings of ADHD. This study will thus contribute to our understanding of ADHD, offering insight into improving diagnosis and intervention.

papers.title: Trust in Human-Chatbot Interaction: An Integrated Model of Performance Expectancy and Decision Making
papers.authors: Anindya Deb, Alisha Pathak
papers.abstract: The communicative behaviour of users has changed with the evolution and advancements of technology, significantly altering the dynamics of human machine interactions.The rapid integration of chatbots into everyday life, particularly in healthcare, has intensified the need to understand the role of trust in human–computer interaction. While existing models of technology adoption—such as the UnifiedTheory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)—emphasize performance expectancy and ease of use, they often overlook the socio-psychological construct of trust that shapes users' willingness to depend on conversational agents. This study integrates UTAUT, TAM, and the Human–Computer Trust Model (HCTM) to examine how trust influences performance expectancy and decision-making in human–chatbot communication.A web-based survey of 255 users aged 18–45 in South Asia was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results demonstrate that trust has a strong and direct positive effect on both performance expectancy and decision-making. Model evaluation indicated robust predictive power (R² values above 0.89) and acceptable fit indices (SRMR = 0.042, NFI = 0.929). These findings highlight trust as a central determinant in chatbot adoption, shifting the discourse from purely functional acceptance to relational and affective dynamics.By empirically validating trust as a key predictor of technology use outcomes, this study extends current acceptance models and provides actionable insights for the design of reliable, transparent, and ethically responsible chatbots. The findings have particular relevance for healthcare and other high-stakes domains, where user trust is indispensable for effective decision support and engagement

papers.title: Can AI replace Teachers? An Indian Knowledge Systems Perspective
papers.authors: Subhodeep Mukhopadhyay, Sudarshan Therani Nadathur, Madhusudan Therani
papers.abstract: The question of whether artificial intelligence (AI) can replace teachers is an important one. Recent studies and public discourse increasingly suggest that AI systems can equal or even outperform human instructors in selected tasks such as content delivery, personalization, assessment, and feedback. This paper examines the question of AI replacing teachers from the perspective of Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS). The question we ask is whether AI can move beyond transmitting information and fulfill the deeper epistemic and civilizational role of the teacher. Among the different types of teachers in the Sanskrit tradition, we use the concept of Apta, a trustworthy authority on a topic, as seen in the Nyaya framework. We assess contemporary AI against the three criteria of an Apta: trustworthy source possessing direct knowledge, an intention to communicate truth, and the capacity to convey it properly. A desk review of current AI literature is conducted. Our results show that current AI systems do not qualify as an Aptasince none of the three criteria are met. We conclude that while AI may simulate or partially perform certain instructional functions, it cannot be a complete substitute for the human teacher in the Indian philosophical sense.

papers.title: Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Filmmaking: A Diffusion of Innovation Perspective
papers.authors: Dr.Madala Sindhu
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing its role from a tool to a collaborative partner in creative practices, particularly in Filmmaking. The current study investigates the perceptions, learning interests and adoption behavior of Generation Z film and media students towards AI in filmmaking. This study was conducted among 120 undergraduate and postgraduate students who are enrolled in film and media subjects. All the participants are engaged in filmmaking at various levels. The study is grounded in the Diffusion of Innovation theory by conceptualising AI as an innovation and studying its adoption among the students. The results state that even though the learning interest (75%) is high, AI adoption remains limited. The correlation analysis states that there is a significant relationship between perceived value and learning interest (r = 0.337, p < .05). As per the regression analysis, neither the perceived value nor learning interest significantly predicts the adoption behaviour. The study clearly highlights the gap between attitudinal acceptance and behavioural adoption. The study has identified key barriers, including limited technical exposure, ethical dilemmas and accessibility constraints. The study results positioned students within the persuasion-to decision stage of the Diffusion of Innovation process. The study contributes to the literature on human-AI co-creation by focusing on the development of academic discourse and structured training in AI for film and media students.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Adaptive Simulation Integrated With a Workforce Decision-Support System to Improve Simulated Nursing Leadership Performance: A Randomized Controlled Study
papers.authors: Mohammed Saleh Almalki
papers.abstract: Background The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare necessitates that nurse leaders develop advanced competencies in decision-making, communication, and data-informed clinical judgment. Traditional simulation-based education, while effective, often relies on fixed scenarios with limited adaptability and minimal real-time decision support. AI-enhanced simulation offers a potential solution by creating responsive, adaptive learning environments that support leadership development. Methods This randomized controlled, parallel-group, pretest-posttest trial included 130 final-year nursing students who were randomly allocated to an intervention group (n = 65), receiving AI-adaptive simulation integrated with an AI-based workforce decision-support system, or a control group (n = 65). Twenty-one clinical preceptors served as trained and blinded outcome assessors and were not included in the randomized sample. Leadership performance was assessed using the Creighton Simulation Evaluation Instrument (C-SEI). Secondary outcomes included team performance, general self-efficacy, and AI acceptance. Results At Week 10, the intervention group demonstrated greater improvement in leadership performance than the control group (between-group difference in change = 5.20, 95% CI 4.18-6.22, p < 0.001), with a large standardized effect (Cohen's d = 1.78). Greater improvements were also observed in team performance (between-group difference in change = 0.63, 95% CI 0.44-0.82, p < 0.001, d = 1.24) and general self-efficacy (between-group difference in change = 5.30, 95% CI 3.82-6.78, p < 0.001, d = 1.37). Intervention-group students reported favorable AI acceptance, including perceived usefulness and ease of use. Conclusions AI-adaptive simulation integrated with an AI-based workforce decision-support system was associated with improved leadership performance, team performance, and self-efficacy among final-year nursing students under controlled simulation conditions. Further research is needed to determine whether these effects are sustained and transfer to clinical practice.

papers.title: HEY @GROK, IS THIS TRUE? AN EXAMINATION OF NEWS VERIFICATION PRACTICES ON X
papers.authors: Mesut YILMAZ
papers.journal: The Turkish Online Journal of Design Art and Communication
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) systems have become a new actor in the process by altering users’ news verification behaviors. This article aims to examine the news verification requests submitted to Grok by Turkish-speaking users on the X platform, with the goal of identifying user behavior and Grok’s role in the news verification process. The study analyzed 276 news verification requests addressed to Grok on the X platform in June 2026 through qualitative content analysis. Verification requests were assessed according to news topic, content type, news source, account verification status, account verification badge, the national or international scope of the news, and Grok’s responses. The results demonstrate that Grok responds to news verification requests by mirroring the users’ tone and providing detailed explanations of the verification process. The most frequently requested news topics for verification were sports, politics, and legal cases, while explanatory content attracted more verification requests than other content types. Additionally, the majority of user accounts submitting verification requests were anonymous, and these requests encompassed both national and international news. The tendency of users to request verification of posts from government and official organization accounts suggests a notable level of trust in Grok. In conclusion, Grok is regarded as an AI-based verification tool that supports the news verification ecosystem on the X platform and enhances users’ ability to verify information.

papers.title: RECONSTRUCTING AUTHENTICITY IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: A QUALITATIVE CONTENT ANALYSIS OF AI-ASSISTED INSTAGRAM POSTS
papers.authors: Büşra Sarıkaya
papers.journal: The Turkish Online Journal of Design Art and Communication
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has introduced new questions concerning authenticity, transparency, and human creative agency in social media communication. While previous research has largely examined audience responses to AI-generated or AI-assisted content, comparatively less attention has been given to how creators themselves communicate AI involvement in naturally occurring social media posts. Addressing this gap, this study examines how authenticity is communicatively constructed in AI-assisted Instagram posts through qualitative content analysis. The dataset consists of 20 publicly accessible Instagram posts published between 1 and 30 June 2026 that explicitly disclose the use of generative AI. Posts were selected through purposive and maximum variation sampling across different creator categories. The analysis shows that AI disclosure extends beyond simply identifying technology use and is frequently integrated into descriptions of creative processes, production decisions, and human intervention. Across the analyzed posts, AI is predominantly positioned as a supporting or collaborative resource, while creators continue to emphasize aesthetic judgment, selection, revision, and responsibility for the final output. Transparency is similarly communicated through explanations of how and where AI enters the production process. The findings suggest that authenticity in AI-assisted social media communication is constructed not through the absence of technological mediation but through the communicative visibility of human involvement. By focusing on creator practices rather than measuring audience responses, the study contributes to AI-mediated communication research by conceptualizing authenticity as a relational communicative process shaped by AI disclosure, transparency, and representations of human agency.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND YOUTH: A PHENOMENOLOGICAL STUDY ON UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
papers.authors: Şule YENİGÜN ALTIN
papers.journal: The Turkish Online Journal of Design Art and Communication
papers.abstract: With rapid advancements in information and communication technologies, generative artificial intelligence tools have become significant tools that change young people's habits in areas such as communication and access to information. This study examines the effects of university students' experiences using AI-powered digital applications on their communication practices and daily lives using a phenomenological research design. As part of the study, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 14 university students. Six different themes were identified from the findings: "Information orientation and changes in learning habits," "Cognitive decline anxiety," "Occupational uncertainty anxiety," "Artificial intelligence as an alternative emotional support mechanism," "Emotional support data security and privacy perception," and "Manipulation." These findings demonstrate that young people's experiences regarding the use of artificial intelligence largely overlap with studies in the literature and support existing research. This study offers a qualitative and experience-based contribution to the existing literature by addressing the cognitive, emotional, and social effects of artificial intelligence on young people from a phenomenological perspective.

papers.title: Nano-totalitarianism: Brain-computer interfaces, fusion databases, and the weaponisation of consciousness
papers.authors: John Hawkins
papers.abstract: Debate about interrogational torture still returns to the ticking-bomb scenario, despite the weight of evidence that it neither works nor withstands moral scrutiny. The post-9/11 record, from Abu Ghraib to the CIA black sites, already marked a decisive shift toward psychological forms of coercion. The technologies now emerging make a different kind of coercion possible. This paper argues that defence-funded brain-computer interfaces, of which Synchron's Stentrode is the clearest current example, combined with large language models and fusion databases, could support what I call nano-totalitarianism: the convergence of pervasive personal data, neurodata, adaptive AI, and technologically mediated coercion in ways that could penetrate or continuously condition the inner sphere of the person. Operationalised, this is a self-sustaining regime in which a detainee is held in continuous psychological distress through fabricated scenarios, interference with memory, and synthetic social contact. Such a system would turn neuroplasticity into an instrument, laying down durable neural pathways of fear, while automated monitoring assesses compliance in real time. Its lineage runs from MKULTRA's psychochemical experiments to the extraction logic of surveillance capitalism, and its endpoint is a panopticon inside the skull. The essay proceeds anticipatorily, distinguishing throughout between demonstrated current capability, plausible convergence of existing components, and speculative future possibility.

papers.title: Digital Transformation and the Future of Higher Education: A Comprehensive Umbrella Review
papers.authors: Maksud Zaloidinov, Aafia Shahid, Muhammad Uzair Khan, Sumaya Batool, Mazhar Ali, Dua Mobin, Naji Ullah
papers.abstract: Digital transformation (DT) is fundamentally changing the higher education institutions (HEIs) around the globe. The COVID-19 pandemic has drastically increased using digitally enabled approaches for teaching, learning, research, and administration, driven by the convergence of technologies encompassing the industry 4.0. Despite the various existing reviews that tackle digital transformation separately, some, such as those on the technology adoption or strategic planning, or pedagogical innovation, have limited scope and do not offer an overall, multi-dimensional synthesis. This rather comprehensive umbrella review combines dimensions, technologies, strategic processes and actors related to the implementation of DT in HEIs, based on the systematic and multivocal literature reviews, analyses via PRISMA, and thematic synthesises of articles, published from 2015 to 2024, in Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Springer Link and ACM Digital Library databases. A total of 47 studies in the analytical corpus, two of which were anchor reviews and 43 were complementary primary studies, were identified in an initial pool of 312 records. The findings showed that most digital transformation projects (DTIs) in the education sector are concentrated on competitive education (24%) and that the dominant enabling technologies are analytics (23%), cloud computing (20%), and artificial intelligence (16%). Most of all, just one-quarter of HEIs can speak with any degree of fluency about a digital strategy and only 56% of DTIs are part of a broader institutional agenda. The review concludes that, based on the importance of those topics in the curriculum, student demand satisfaction (12%) and digital culture (9%) fall short of expected levels of investment. The results are derived from the existing reviews and primary studies and thus share the limitations of the primary literature reviewed. The results highlight the need for university leaders to create digital strategies that are integrated, invest in faculty development and digital culture, and embrace a transformative approach instead of a technology-only approach to the implementation of digital transformation.

papers.title: Human–AI Collaboration and Students' Higher-Order Thinking Skills in Higher Education
papers.authors: Faiz ul Hassan Shah, Kashif Nawaz, Iman Afroz, Qaisar Abbas
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes more widely used in higher education, there are new opportunities for students to interact with information, ideas, feedback, and problem-solving. But its pedagogical impact could vary with the students' engagement with AI alongside a human's judgment and cognitive investment. The present study investigated the relationship between Human – AI Collaboration and students' Higher Order Thinking Skills: Analyzing, Evaluating, and Creating skills among the Higher Education HTS students. Use of quantitative, cross sectional (correlational) design. A structured questionnaire was filled out by the respondents, and the data were then processed by descriptive statistics, Cronbach alpha and simple linear regression techniques, with a total of 379 students of public university in Sindh. The results showed statistically significant positive correlation between Human–AI Collaboration and Analysing/Evaluating skills and Creating skills. Human – AI Collaboration was the best predictor of all higher-order thinking skills, particularly analyzing skills. The study found purposeful and active synergies with AI behavior to be correlated with higher order thinking. It is recommended that universities advocate for the structured use of AI to support learning activities, with a focus on questioning, checking, reflecting, making independent judgements as well as considerate use of AI.

papers.title: Lightweight Explainable Machine Learning for Early Detection of Academic Performance Risk among Students
papers.authors: Furqan Ali
papers.journal: ComputeX - Journal of Emerging Technology & Applied Science
papers.abstract: Predictive models are rarely used unless educators can understand them and if they can, they can intervene before students complete their education and get the signs of academic failure. Three classifiers were designed and evaluated in this study: logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) with publicly available UCI Student Performance dataset (math course, n = 395) to predict academic performance risk. The final grade of less than 10 out of 20 was defined as risk, and 32.9% of students were at risk. The models were fine-tuned with stratified five-fold cross-validation on 80% of the data, and then tested once on a 20% stratified hold-out set, using cost-sensitive learning techniques to address the class imbalance problem. All models discriminated well (hold-out ROC-AUC 0.933–0.941; recall 0.846–0.962) and differences among them were small when compared with sampling uncertainty for the first (only) period for which the grade was available. The discrimination of the first period grade alone was 0.698–0.713 ROC-AUC. Results from the SHAP analysis of the XGBoost model revealed that most important variable for making predictions was prior assessment performance, with a mean absolute SHAP value of about 27 times higher than the next important variable. The results indicate that the predictive signal of the early term grades is relatively high, and that the signal of behavioural and demographic variables is relatively low. They also show that any methodology used to make the model explainable should be used in tandem with careful consideration of ethics and fairness when implementing it into real world use.

papers.title: The relationship between the primary school teachers’ attitude towards learning AI technology usage and their professional development
papers.authors: Atika Raheem, Nargis Abbas
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education has created new opportunities for teachers’ professional learning and development. The current study investigated relationship between the primary school teacher's learning AI technology usage and their professional growth. A quantitative survey research design was employed and data were collected from government primary school teachers in District Khushab, Punjab, through a structured questionnaire. Stratified random sampling technique was used to select the respondent of the study from public sector primary schools of tehsil Khushab. Descriptive statistics, correlation and regression analyses were used to analyze the data. The findings revealed the teachers’ positive perceptions about AI technology usage for their professional development. AI competency, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of learning and use were found significantly positive correlated with their attitude to learn AI use. The results further showed that teachers’ attitude towards leaning AI technology usage significantly predicted positively their professional development (β=1.42, p <0.05). The study concludes that primary school teachers’ attitude towards using AI technology positively affect their usage of this technology to enhance their professional development. It is recommended that by providing AI-tools usage trainings, practical learning opportunities, and professional interventional strategies through their CPD programs may accelerate the readiness to use these technologies in their teaching and non-teaching tasks for addressing the future challenges.

papers.title: Effect of digital technology and leadership competencies on students’ engagement at higher education institutions
papers.authors: Adeela Aslam, Nargis Abbas, Saima Nasreen
papers.journal: Research Journal of Human and Social Aspects
papers.abstract: In innovative pedagogies supported by Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies, higher education is experiencing a revolution that reprograms the learning, engagement and contributions of students to social change. With the goal of enhancing learning effectiveness and fostering student-centred learning, various AI-tainted technologies have found their application in modern educational methods, such as intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning systems, and automated feedback systems. The study's objective is to measure the effect of teacher’s leadership quality, their AI literacy and use of AI in teaching on their students’ engagement in learning. A quantitative survey research design was employed in analysing the data obtained from the university teachers through a questionnaire. A multi stage sampling technique was used to select the respondent faculty members of the study. Data was collected from 250 teaching faculty member’s teachers belonging to faculty of social sciences in three public universities of Punjab province. The results showed that AI Literacy, teacher leadership and Use of AI in teaching significantly predict the students’ engagement (F =56.51, p<.001). Therefore, the study suggests that in order to successfully integrate AI in higher education, it is necessary to train the teachers for integrating AI in pedagogy to enhance students’ engagement. Further, Universities need to increase institutional support, continuous faculty development, and AI supported infrastructure, which encourage and promote the use of AI technologies in an effective and ethical manner.

papers.title: Examining the relationships and relative predictive contributions of artificial, moral, and spiritual intelligence to academic achievement among PhD scholars in Punjab, Pakistan
papers.authors: Najma Iqbal, Hafiz Kosar
papers.journal: Research Journal of Human and Social Aspects
papers.abstract: As AI becomes more prevalent in higher education, PhD scholars have opportunities to leverage AI tools and technologies to enhance their learning, research, and academic productivity. But there are also moral and spiritual attributes which influence scholars' academic aspirations, drive and choices that could also be linked to academic performance. Thus the present study examined the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), Moral Intelligence (MI), Spiritual Intelligence (SI) and Academic Achievement (AA) among PhD scholars of Punjab, Pakistan. The research design was quantitative correlational while the data collection was done by using a structured questionnaire with 5-point likert scale. Pearson correlation analysis revealed significant positive correlations between AI and AA (r = .712, p < .001), MI and AA (r = .699, p < .001) and SI and AA (r = .469, p < .001). The highest correlation found was between AI and AA. Multiple regression analysis revealed that AI and MI significantly positively contributed to academic achievement, with AI contributing more (β = .455, p < .001) than MI (β = .419, p < .001). SI did not appear significant (β = .014, p = .566). The model explained 62.4% of the variance in academic achievement (R² = .624, p < .001). The results underline the significance of AI and MI in the context of academic performance of doctorate degree holders but the role of SI needs to be explored in conjunction with other factors

papers.title: Ascetic Knowledge System in Age of AI: Integrating Indian Religious Asceticism within IKS driven Digital Epistemologies
papers.authors: Devesh Kumar Singh, Hitendra Singh Rathore -
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science Research (IJSSR)
papers.abstract: The Indian Knowledge System is delicately stitched into the cultural, traditional, and philosophical heritage of India. It encompasses the ways of teaching, learning, knowing, propagating and applying knowledge rooted in indigenous epistemologies. In present era of technology and rapidly changing world, it is very important to be connected with one’s root. This paper integrates the rich heritage of Indian Knowledge System with that of Artificial Intelligence in special connection with ascetic teachings. The traditional knowledge system has been preserved by the numerous great religious ascetics who have transmitted the ideas, knowledge and composed many literary sources. But in digitized world, where technology is the driving force, it is important to preserve the traditional knowledge to impend one’s own identity and cultural existence. This paper explores such relations and delves into the impact of such integration on future. The paper employs qualitative methodology, following descriptive research design. The paper is ultimately relying on secondary resources, a systematic interdisciplinary analysis of historical, sociological, academic articles and textual studies have been done. The paper establishes the clear need of integrating IKS with digital epistemologies of present Indian Education system. It also emphasizes the possible impact of it in decolonizing the young Indian minds. The paper also establishes its link with NEP 2020 and portrays active use of IKS in teaching and nurturing the young blood.

papers.title: Beyond Faster Learning: How GenAI Learning Efficiency Translates into Effective Learning Outcomes
papers.authors: Papia Sarkar
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science Research (IJSSR)
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can make learning faster and less demanding, but greater efficiency does not necessarily result in better learning. This study examines how GenAI learning efficiency is translated into effective learning outcomes among higher-education students in India. GenAI Learning Efficiency (GLE) is conceptualized as a higher-order construct comprising learning time efficiency, cognitive effort efficiency, learning task efficiency, and knowledge access efficiency. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory and Self-Regulated Learning theory, the study examines cognitive engagement and self-regulated learning as parallel mechanisms connecting GLE with effective learning outcomes. Data were collected from 548 undergraduate and postgraduate students with prior experience using GenAI for academic purposes and analysed using PLS-SEM. The findings show that GLE strengthens both cognitive engagement and self-regulated learning, which subsequently contribute to effective learning outcomes. Both mechanisms mediate the relationship between GLE and learning outcomes, while a smaller direct effect remains. The study shows that the educational value of GenAI lies not simply in making learning easier or faster, but in whether learners use the resulting efficiency to engage more deeply and regulate their learning effectively.

papers.title: GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND COPYRIGHT LAW: CHALLENGES IN DETERMINING AUTHORSHIP AND OWNERSHIP
papers.authors: Joylin Jacob Y
papers.journal: LawFoyer International Journal of Doctrinal Legal Research.
