First, generative AI has accelerated the shift from mass political broadcasting to hyper-personalized, data-driven persuasion that can tailor messages to individual psychological and behavioral profiles at unprecedented scale and low cost. Second, AI-generated misinformation, including deceptive robocalls, synthetic visual advertisements, and inaccurate voting-information outputs, increases information pollution and creates opportunities for voter suppression and electoral manipulation. Third, beyond direct deception, AI contributes to affective polarization and strengthens the “Liar’s Dividend,” enabling political actors to challenge the authenticity of legitimate information and thereby eroding public trust in democratic institutions. The study contributes to the emerging literature on AI governance by developing an integrated conceptual framework that links hyper-personalized persuasion, information disorder, and democratic resilience in electoral environments. The analysis demonstrates that the principal democratic risk of generative AI lies not solely in misinformation but in its capacity to undermine public trust structurally and shared epistemic foundations. To address these challenges while preserving First Amendment protections, the study proposes a multi-layered regulatory framework incorporating mandatory content provenance standards, targeted amendments to the Federal Election Campaign Act (FECA), enhanced transparency obligations for political AI content, and conditional platform accountability measures during critical election periods. The findings provide policy-relevant guidance for regulators, election authorities, technology platforms, and democratic institutions seeking to safeguard electoral integrity in the age of generative AI.

papers.title: Association of Body Mass Index, Hemoglobin Level, and Stress Level with the severity of Dysmenorrhea among Female Patients Attending Al-Kadhimayn Teaching Hospital, Baghdad: Cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Anaam Katran Zughair, Haider Ali Hussain, Maitham Katran AL-Reqapi
papers.abstract: Background: Dysmenorrhea is a common menstrual complaint among women of reproductive age and can interfere with daily activities, work, and quality of life. Several factors have been associated with dysmenorrhea, including body mass index (BMI), hemoglobin level, and perceived stress. Aim: To examine the relationship between BMI, hemoglobin level, perceived stress, and the occurrence of dysmenorrhea among female patients attending the gynecology outpatient clinic of Al-Kadhimayn Teaching Hospital, Baghdad. Methods: An observational analytic cross-sectional study was conducted among 180 female patients selected through systematic random sampling from the clinic register. Data were collected using a structured interview that included demographic and lifestyle characteristics, anthropometric measurements, capillary hemoglobin testing, and the Arabic-validated 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) [16]. BMI was categorized into three groups: underweight, normal weight (reference), and overweight. Chi-square tests and binary logistic regression were used for statistical analysis. Result: Dysmenorrhea was reported by 67.8% of the participants. Nutritional status, hemoglobin status, and perceived stress were significantly associated with dysmenorrhea (p < 0.05). The logistic regression model had a Nagelkerke R² of 0.518, indicating that the included factors explained 51.8% of the variation in dysmenorrhea. Compared with normal-weight participants, both underweight (adjusted OR = 4.31, 95% CI: 1.31–14.18) and overweight participants (adjusted OR = 8.57, 95% CI: 2.71–27.07) had significantly higher odds of dysmenorrhea, with the strongest association observed among those who were overweight. Anemia (adjusted OR = 4.64) and high perceived stress (adjusted OR = 3.92) were also independently associated with dysmenorrhea. Conclusion: In this single-center sample, underweight and overweight status, anemia, and high perceived stress were statistically associated with dysmenorrhea. However, because of the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted as causal. Longitudinal and multicenter studies are recommended to clarify the temporal relationships and clinical relevance of these factors.

papers.title: Multiple-choice questions as a means of assessment in the face of generative AI: a Python analysis of master’s students’ perceptions
papers.authors: Ahmed M’hamdi
papers.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research and Innovative Studies
papers.abstract: The justifiable multiple-choice question, which requires students to select an answer and then justify it, is often presented as a defence against the unauthorised use of generative AI. This case study focuses on 41 of the 50 Master’s students at the Higher School of Education and Training (Ibnou Zohr University) who sat an exam in this format (response rate: 82 per cent). Data from a mixed-methods questionnaire were processed using a reproducible analysis pipeline in Python: descriptive statistics, reliability, non-parametric tests, k-means clustering and automated analysis of open-ended responses. The students recognise the format’s high educational value (71 per cent believe it forces them to understand better; α = 0.85), but only 25 per cent consider it more difficult to circumvent using AI (Wilcoxon, p < 0.001, r = 0.62). This scepticism is shared by both identified profiles and does not depend on the frequency of AI use. Students attribute the resistance to the contextual nature of the questions (7 per cent consider a question relating to classroom experience to be vulnerable) and the majority suggest redesigning the tasks rather than increasing supervision (71 per cent versus 22 per cent). Keywords: Justification-based multiple-choice questions; generative AI; academic integrity; authentic assessment; educational data analysis; Python; case study. Received Date: August 17, 2026 Accepted Date: September 09, 2026 Published Date: October 01, 2026 Available Online at: https://www.ijsrisjournal.com/index.php/ojsfiles/article/view/986

papers.title: The adoption of artificial intelligence in internal audit: determinants, uses and challenges – a systematic review of the literature based on Prisma
papers.authors: Nadia TOUTOUH, Houda Benarbi
papers.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research and Innovative Studies
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into internal audit is progressing rapidly, driven by developments in machine learning, predictive analytics, natural language processing and, more recently, generative artificial intelligence. This study aims to systematically analyse the determinants of AI adoption in internal audit; its main uses and the challenges associated with its integration. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, using the Scopus and Web of Science databases, covering the period 2015–2026. Following identification, deduplication, screening and eligibility assessment, 35 studies were selected for analysis. The results show that the adoption of AI depends primarily on technological maturity, data quality, auditors’ skills, organisational support, governance and trust in the systems. Its main applications relate to risk assessment, anomaly detection, task automation, continuous auditing, document analysis and decision support. The main challenges relate to governance, explainability, reliability, skills, human oversight and data protection. The review highlights the multidimensional nature of AI adoption and emphasises the importance of aligning technologies, human capabilities and governance mechanisms to ensure controlled integration within the internal audit function. Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Internal audit; Technology adoption; Generative artificial intelligence; Systematic review. Received Date: August 17, 2026 Accepted Date: September 09, 2026 Published Date: October 01, 2026 Available Online at: https://www.ijsrisjournal.com/index.php/ojsfiles/article/view/975

papers.title: Educación aumentada
papers.authors: Grijalva Mena Diana Carolina Grijalva Mena, León Almeida Julia Elizabeth León Almeida Julia Elizabeth, Monteros Remache Yajaira Elizabeth Monteros Remache Yajaira Elizabeth, Mera Viteri Jaime Andrés Mera Viteri Jaime Andrés
papers.abstract: Augmented Education: Artificial Intelligence, Neuroscience, and New Frontiers of Human Learning explores the transformation of the contemporary educational paradigm resulting from the convergence of intelligent technologies, neuroscience, and pedagogy. The work defines "augmented education" as a human-centered approach aimed at amplifying the cognitive, creative, and self-regulatory capacities of students and educators, preventing indiscriminate automation and technological dependence. Across three chapters, it examines the evolution of digital ecosystems toward adaptive and immersive environments, brain function in digital settings (analyzing neuroplasticity, attention, executive functions, and neuroethics), and the establishment of new pedagogical frontiers focused on challenge-based learning, formative assessment, and digital humanism.

papers.title: AI-Supported Digital Storytelling: Effects on Learning Outcomes and Student Perceptions in Solar System Education
papers.authors: Günay PALİÇ ŞADOĞLU, Derya Kaya Usta
papers.journal: International Journal of Educational Studies and Policy
papers.abstract: In recent years, the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies into education has gained importance for enriching student-centered learning processes and supporting 21st-century skills. This study examines changes in the academic achievement, digital literacy skills, creative thinking tendencies, and lesson-related views of 6th-grade female students who learned about the Solar System through AI-supported Digital Storytelling (DST) using Gemini. The study was conducted with 38 students over four weeks and employed a mixed-methods design consisting of a single-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design for the quantitative component and a qualitative descriptive approach based on students’ views for the qualitative component. Quantitative findings indicated statistically significant increases in students’ academic achievement and creative thinking tendency scores following the intervention. However, changes in digital literacy skills were limited, suggesting that exposure to AI tools alone may not be sufficient to promote meaningful development in this area. Qualitative findings further showed that students perceived AI-supported DST as engaging, supportive, and beneficial for understanding complex scientific concepts. The findings suggest that AI-supported DST may provide a useful instructional approach for enriching science learning experiences when integrated within a well-designed instructional framework. While these promising findings highlight the potential of AI-supported DST, the observed changes should be interpreted cautiously due to the absence of a control group. Ultimately, sustaining and extending these potential benefits may require targeted pedagogical guidance, minimization of technical limitations, and further optimization of AI tools for educational purposes.

papers.title: CAN GENERATIVE AI REPLACE HUMAN ESSAY RATERS? A PSYCHOMETRIC COMPARISON OF GPT-5.2, GEMINI, AND TEACHER RATINGS
papers.authors: A. U. Serikbayeva, Diana Akizhanova
papers.abstract: Evaluating student writing is a crucial yet time-consuming process. Large Language Models (LLMs)and other recent advancements in generative AI provide potential solutions to support teachers in essayassessment. This study psychometrically evaluates large language models such as GPT-5.2 and Gemini withhuman raters to examine reliability of these solutions. All 55 essays were collected and assessed by GPT 5.2,Gemini and an experienced teacher using a four-criterion scoring rubric. The aim of this study is to psychometrically compare the results of human raters, GPT-5.2, and Gemini assessments on English essays,to determine their rating reliability, intercorrelation, rating differences, and the construct validity of the ratingrubric. The results demonstrated that GPT-5.2 assigned the highest vocabulary scores, while Geminiproduced the highest grammar scores. Overall, GPT-5.2 showed high agreement with teacher ratings and canbe used as a reliable adjunct to essay grading. However, teacher professional judgment remains importantwhen assessing complex content and contextual features. These findings support the use of generative AI as asupplementary tool for improving the efficiency and consistency of essay assessment in EFL contexts.

papers.title: EVALUATING AI RESPONSES IN LITERATURE TEACHING: THE LITERARY INTERIOR IN KAZAKH PROSE
papers.authors: M.E. Ospanaly, Assem Kalieva, Nezir Temür
papers.abstract: This article examines the methodological potential of generative language models for developing philology students’ ability to analyse and interpret the poetics of the interior in literary texts. The empirical basis of the study is an initial dialogue with Google Gemini held in February 2026 and the responses to the same prompts put to Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude eight months later. The models’ responses were compared against predefined criteria, and their statements about the interior in Mukhtar Magauin’s novel Zharmak were checked against the text of the novel and a published literary review. The analysis showed that all the models were useful as a source of methodological guidance. The analytical questions they proposed are consistent with the theories of literary space developed by Yuri Lotman, Gaston Bachelard and Alexander Chudakov, and they used the conceptual vocabulary of the traditional Kazakh dwelling correctly. In the close analysis of a specific literary text, however, their reliability proved limited. Of Gemini’s 11 claims, only 2 were fully and 6 partly confirmed. ChatGPT confined itself to directing the user back to the text, while Claude drew on web sources. The novel's key spatial details, which none of the models quoted, emerged only through close reading. The study produced a three-stage model for teaching work with artificial intelligence in university philology courses and a seminar tasks that develops students’ critical analysis skills.

papers.title: MEASUREMENT INVARIANCE OF AN AI-GAMIFIED ADAPTIVE LEARNING ACCEPTANCE SCALE ACROSS ENGLISH PROFICIENCY AND YEAR OF STUDY
papers.authors: Ainur Zhorabekova, Marzhan Moldakassymovna Duisenova, Moldir Kurmasheva, A. Yesnazar
papers.abstract: Students' acceptance of adaptive learning tools that combine artificial intelligence with gamification is usually measured with multidimensional questionnaires, but whether such questionnaires show the same measurement properties across student subgroups is rarely examined. This study tested the measurement invariance of a 13-item scale of acceptance of AI-gamified adaptive learning across English proficiency and year of study and estimated latent mean differences where invariance held. Previously collected data from 401 EFL students at a Kazakhstani pedagogical university were analysed with multi-group confirmatory factor analysis. A second-order factor model served as the primary measurement model, and a four-correlated-factor model estimated with MLR and WLSMV was used as a sensitivity analysis. Across proficiency levels A2, B1 and B2+, the scale showed full scalar invariance, with CFI decreasing by no more than .003 and no significant chi-square difference at any step, and the latent mean of general acceptance did not differ between levels. Across year of study, comparing first-year students with those in years two to four, metric invariance was supported and scalar invariance was partial. Once the intercept of one item concerning AI feedback was freed, constrained and unconstrained models no longer differed significantly. Within the reported partial invariance model, the latent mean of general acceptance was higher for upper-year students than for first-year students by about0.3 standard deviations. The findings provide a full psychometric basis for comparisons across proficiency and a partial basis for latent mean comparisons across year of study. The main limitations are a single-institution convenience sample, self-reported proficiency, a ceiling effect and the possibility of common-method variance.

papers.title: L’intelligence artificielle comme levier de transformation des politiques éducatives : opportunités, risques et perspectives pour le système marocain
papers.authors: NAAMA EHIRI
papers.abstract: L’essor de l’intelligence artificielle (IA), et plus particulièrement de l’IA générative, reconfigure les conditions de conception, de mise en œuvre et d’évaluation des politiques éducatives. Au-delà des usages instrumentaux dans la classe, l’IA introduit de nouvelles capacités de personnalisation des apprentissages, d’assistance aux enseignants, d’analyse des données scolaires et d’aide à la décision publique. Ces possibilités s’accompagnent toutefois de risques structurels : biais algorithmiques, atteintes à la protection des données, dépendance cognitive, fragilisation de l’intégrité académique, accentuation des inégalités numériques et dépendance envers des infrastructures ou modèles propriétaires. Cet article analyse ces tensions à partir d’une revue critique de la littérature scientifique récente et d’une analyse documentaire des principaux référentiels internationaux et marocains. L’étude met en relation les travaux sur l’IA en éducation avec la Feuille de route 2022–2026 du ministère marocain de l’Éducation nationale, la stratégie Digital Morocco 2030 et les orientations lancées en 2026 autour de « AI Made in Morocco » et de Maroc IA 2030. Les résultats montrent que l’IA ne constitue un levier de transformation des politiques éducatives que si son adoption est gouvernée selon une logique centrée sur l’humain, la qualité pédagogique et l’équité. L’article propose un cadre intégré de gouvernance de l’IA éducative pour le Maroc articulé autour de six conditions : gouvernance et responsabilité humaines, compétences IA, protection des données, équité d’accès, évaluation pédagogique et souveraineté numérique et linguistique. Ce cadre vise à faire de l’IA non un substitut à l’action éducative, mais une infrastructure publique de capacité, encadrée par des finalités pédagogiques explicites et des mécanismes de redevabilité.

papers.title: Feedback Valence in Organizations: A Structured Literature Review and Future Research Agenda
papers.authors: Syeda Sumaira Kousar, Faisal Qadeer
papers.journal: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
papers.abstract: Valence of feedback - the sign of the information people receive concerning their own performance - is a well-researched yet theoretically fragmented construct. Even though scholars have been studying feedback for many years, current field-level review studies still characterize the literature on performance-related feedback in terms of inconsistent definitions, isolated theoretical perspectives, and conflicting conclusions as to which valence of feedback (positive or negative) works better for people and organizations. This study is an attempt to systematize the existing literature on the topic of feedback valence by conducting a theoretically-oriented review of academic studies from scientific databases. The purpose of the review is to follow the evolution of the feedback valence concept and identify major theoretical perspectives that scholars used to study it (Feedback Intervention Theory, feedback seeking cost-benefit perspective, self-verification/attribution theory, and social exchange theory). The synthesis indicates that the effect of valenced feedback is highly situation-specific: positive feedback consistently promotes motivation, creativity, and feedback seeking behavior, but negative feedback effect depends on the nature of the relationship, delivery of feedback, and agency of the person receiving it. The paper concludes with the discussion of theoretical, methodological, and situational limitations and suggestions for future research in this area. References Anseel, F., Beatty, A. papers.title: Takeda Pharmaceutical: Reimagining R&D With AI
papers.authors: George F. Westerman, David J. Kiron
papers.abstract: Takeda Pharmaceutical reimagined drug discovery by embedding AI into R&D workflows, shifting scientists from broad laboratory experimentation to data-driven prediction and targeted validation. This case study shows how executive accountability, strong data foundations, workforce transformation, and a culture of trust and experimentation are critical to scaling AI innovation.

papers.title: Criminal-law qualification of fraud committed using information and communication technologies
papers.authors: Вікторія Миколаївна Щерба
papers.journal: Ûridičnij časopis Nacìonalʹnoï akademìï vnutrìšnìh sprav
papers.abstract: The growing use of information and communication technologies in fraudulent offences makes their criminal-law qualification more difficult, particularly when these acts have to be distinguished from related criminal offences. The study therefore aimed to determine criteria for assessing fraud committed through information and communication technologies and to establish how these acts should be separated from related criminal offences. The research used the formal legal method, analysis of judicial practice, and conceptual modelling. The analysis considered the criminal-law characteristics of fraud and how these characteristics appear when information and communication technologies are used. Digital tools do not change the basic legal characteristics of fraud. They change the practical way in which deception, abuse of trust, and transfer of property take place. The judicial decisions examined in the study showed how fraud can be distinguished from theft, unauthorised interference with information systems, unlawful use of payment instruments, and use of another person’s identification data. For criminal-law qualification, the fact that digital technology was used is not decisive. More important are the role of that technology in obtaining property, the victim’s volition, and the way the property left the victim’s possession. The study identified five criteria for this differentiation: the victim’s volition, the reason for the transfer of property, the function of the digital tool, the time and manner in which property was obtained, and the offender’s initial intent. An algorithm for qualifying digital forms of fraud was proposed, involving the sequential establishment of the digital act, the informational influence, its effect on the victim’s property-related decision, the manner in which the property left the victim’s possession, the function of the digital tool, and the initial intent. The results may be used by investigators, prosecutors, and courts in the criminal-law qualification of digital forms of fraud and in preparing methodological guidance on distinguishing fraud from related criminal offences

papers.title: Effects of Menstruation on Oral Health: A Cross-Sectional, Questionnaire-Based Study
papers.authors: Quareena Javed, Chanika Singhal
papers.journal: Oral Sphere Journal of Dental and Health Sciences
papers.abstract: Background: Hormonal changes throughout the menstrual cycle have an impact on many areas of women's health, and may even impact oral health.Gingival inflammation, oral discomfort, plaque buildup and other periodontal issues can be caused by changes in estrogen and progesterone levels. Materials and Methods:The study was a cross-sectional study with random sampling of females age group 18-50 years.This was done using a pre-validated, self-administered Google Forms questionnaire designed to assess demographic characteristics, oral health awareness, and oral symptoms related to menstruation.Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27.Results: OG was a very common occurrence (most frequently reported, especially during the luteal phase), as were gingival bleeding, swelling, and oral discomfort.There was a trend of positive relationship between higher educational status and higher oral health awareness, which did not necessarily follow through to preventative oral health measures.Postmenopausal women reported higher levels of xerostomia, which may be due to the impact of hormones on salivation.Higher BMI was correlated to menstrual irregularities and overweight and obese participants experienced more menstrual and oral discomfort.There were indications that oral manifestations might be influenced systemically.Conclusion: This study indicates the importance of awareness and awarenessraising in the field of oral health care among women in various reproductive phases.Oral health promotion within reproductive health programs and routine dental care can help to reduce the impact of hormonal changes on the oral cavity.Longitudinal studies are required to confirm causal relationships and mechanisms that link indicators.

papers.title: Following the Traces of Tesla's Creativity: From Tesla's Resonant Coil to Bioresonant Integrative Medicine
papers.authors: Dejan I. Raković
papers.abstract: Tesla's visions and inventions realized in his controlled altered states of consciousness contributed to his legendary aura as the greatest inventor in the history of electrical engineering at the end of 19th century, and what makes him fascinating is his unusual mental control of his creative visions, with significant quantum-holographic transpersonal creative–educational implications (including limits of Artificial Intelligence). At the beginning of the 20th century, Tesla's previously almost mythical scientific reputation and intuition began to darken, but he has still fascinated contemporaries by self-healing with HF currents, which subsequently led not only to the foundations of today's physical electrotherapy, but also represented inspiration for biomedical research and development of the field of bioresonant medicine, contributing also to the rapid development of nowadays integrative medicine (including transpersonal psychology) – with additional hints for reorientation to ecologically holistic subtle actions for solutions of the global risk society.

papers.title: Sociological Theory Meets Generative AI: A Pedagogical Guide
papers.authors: Kimberly Murray
papers.journal: The Journal of Public and Professional Sociology
papers.abstract: This paper considers the relationship between sociology and generative AI (GenAI) as a phenomenon that may be studied using common sociological concepts and theories, including the Sociological Imagination, Structural Functionalism, Conflict Theory, and Symbolic Interactionism, which are considered foundational to the discipline of sociology. Within each section are contemporary examples of GenAI and how they connect to sociology. This paper benefits a wide audience, as students, faculty, and those who use these theories and concepts in practice settings may adopt them within a variety of contexts, including the classroom, a scholarly presentation, a workshop, or a training opportunity. Sources include both scholarly journals and books, as well as more easily accessible data visualizations and journalistic essays intended for a non-academic audience that tend to be helpful when readers are looking for versatile and accessible sources for a wide audience or larger viewership. Although the focus is sociological, this paper is also helpful from an interdisciplinary standpoint, as these concepts and theories may be applied and critically discussed across related disciplines.

papers.title: EXPLAINABLE MACHINE LEARNING FOR INSURANCE CLAIM FRAUD DETECTION: A COMPARATIVE PYTHON-BASED STUDY
papers.authors: Ermira MEMETI
papers.abstract: Today insurance fraud is a big problem for insurance companies since it is challenging to detect potential fraud cases within a large amount of claims data. Traditional rule-based models can detect already known fraud cases, but they often fail to detect new ones and can flag too many false positives. In this paper, several machine learning algorithms will be compared to detect insurance claim fraud. The analysis will focus on comparing models’ performance, handling class imbalances, interpretability and feature engineering. A publicly available dataset with 1,000 cases of insurance claims will be used in the analysis and at the same time, eight classification algorithms will be considered: majority-class baseline, Gaussian Naive Bayes, k-NN, weighted logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, gradient boosting, and XGBoost. To ensure responsible modeling, the study leaves out direct identifiers and sensitive variables like sex, ZIP code, education, occupation, hobbies, and relationship status. The analysis includes missing-value treatment, date-based feature engineering, one-hot encoding, stratified train-test splitting, 5-fold stratified cross-validation, and model evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC- AUC, and confusion matrices. The results indicate that XGBoost achieved the highest cross-validated F1-score, while the decision tree achieved the strongest F1-score on the holdout test set. Random forest had the highest holdout ROC-AUC, and weighted logistic regression was a useful and interpretable benchmark. SHAP analysis found that factors like incident severity, vehicle claim amount, policy age, incident state, vehicle year, annual premium, and other claim-related variables affected the model’s predictions.

papers.title: THE AI SAFETY GAP: A SCENARIO-BASED STUDY OF RISKY HEALTH DECISIONS AND MISPLACED TRUST
papers.authors: Adriatik KRASNIQI
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly integrated into healthcare and everyday life, offering rapid and accessible medical information to the public. Despite its benefits, concerns remain regarding the accuracy of AI-generated medical advice and the potential risks associated with excessive reliance on these technologies without professional medical consultation. Understanding how individuals perceive and use AI in healthcare is important for promoting safer digital health practices. This study aimed to evaluate public trust in AI-generated medical advice and explore attitudes and behaviors related to AI use in healthcare decision-making. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 150 participants from the general population. The questionnaire assessed demographic characteristics, frequency of AI use, trust in AI-generated health information, and healthcare-related decision-making behaviors through hypothetical clinical scenarios. The results demonstrated moderate overall trust in AI-generated medical advice, with frequent use of AI tools reported among participants. While most individuals preferred physician guidance when presented with conflicting medical opinions, a proportion of participants still demonstrated uncertainty or willingness to rely on AI recommendations in potentially serious situations. Participants also expressed strong support for clearer safety measures, physician consultation recommendations, and greater public education regarding the responsible use of AI in healthcare. These findings highlight both the growing role of AI in healthcare decision-making and the importance of ensuring safe and responsible use of these technologies. Strengthening public awareness and implementing safety-oriented AI guidance may help reduce inappropriate reliance on AI-generated medical advice and improve patient safety.

papers.title: DRUG MISUSE AMONG YOUTH IN THE ERA OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Arta ADILI
papers.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and online health information has increasingly influenced how young people access and interpret medical knowledge, contributing to a tendency toward self-medication. This study aimed to evaluate drug use patterns among young people and the influence of AI and digital resources on medication-related decisions. A descriptive study was conducted using an anonymous questionnaire with 54 participants, assessing over-the-counter drug use, types of medications, responses to symptoms, and use and trust of AI and online information. Most participants were female and aged 19–26 years. The majority reported rare use of over-the-counter drugs, with analgesics being the most commonly used medications. In response to new symptoms, most participants consulted a physician, while fewer relied on AI tools, online sources, pharmacists, or self-medication. Trust in AI and internet-based health information was generally moderate to low. Physicians remained the primary influence in medication decisions. Although self-medication was present, professional medical advice was still the dominant approach. AI and online resources were mainly used as supportive tools rather than primary decision-making sources. The findings suggest that while digital technologies are becoming part of health information seeking, their impact on drug use behavior remains limited. These results highlight the need for improved health education and responsible use of medications in the digital age.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF CHATGPT IN ENHANCING ENGLISH WRITING COMPETENCE AMONG VOCATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS: A CASE STUDY AT SMKN 1 TAPAK TUAN
papers.authors: Yulita Halim, Derliana Hasibuan, Dian Anggraini Harahap, Datulina Ginting
papers.journal: CARONG Jurnal Pendidikan Sosial dan Humaniora
papers.abstract: English writing proficiency is essential for vocational high school students, yet many still face difficulties in vocabulary, grammar, and organizing ideas. These challenges highlight the need for effective approaches to improve students’ English writing skills. This study examines how ChatGPT assists vocational high school students at SMKN 1 Tapak Tuan in improving their English writing capabilities. Adopting a qualitative case study design, data were gathered through in-depth interviews, observational fieldwork, and document analysis. The primary participants comprised 12 Computer and Network Engineering (TKJ) students selected via purposive sampling, complemented by an English teacher serving as a secondary informant. The qualitative data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s (2022) thematic framework, while trustworthiness was secured through source and method triangulation. The results indicate that: (1) students generally exhibit a favorable stance toward using ChatGPT for English composition; (2) the tool aids key writing dimensions, such as grammatical accuracy, vocabulary enrichment, idea generation, structural flow, and sentence construction; and (3) several barriers persist, including technical limitations, AI output constraints, and instructional issues. Conceptually, this work enriches literature on AI integration within vocational English pedagogy, while offering practical insights for educators, institutions, and learners seeking to incorporate ChatGPT into writing instruction.

papers.title: Educational assessment in the twenty-first century: theoretical foundations, contemporary trends, and future challenges
papers.authors: Alaviyya Bahruz Nuri
papers.journal: Revista Mexicana de Investigación e Intervención Educativa
papers.abstract: Educational assessment constitutes an essential component of the teaching and learning process, whose role has evolved from the simple measurement of academic achievement toward a comprehensive approach focused on competency development, continuous improvement, and evidence-based pedagogical decision-making. The present study aimed to analyze the theoretical foundations of educational assessment and identify the principal contemporary trends that are transforming its implementation across different educational levels. To achieve this objective, an integrative literature review was conducted based on scientific publications indexed in international databases, prioritizing recent research and influential theoretical contributions. The analysis revealed that diagnostic, formative, and summative assessment represent complementary processes that support instructional planning, learning monitoring, and the certification of learning outcomes. The findings also demonstrated a growing emphasis on authentic, student-centered assessment models that incorporate continuous feedback, self-regulated learning, and the evaluation of higher-order competencies such as critical thinking, creativity, communication, collaboration, and problem-solving. Furthermore, the review showed that digital transformation and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence are significantly reshaping educational assessment systems by creating new opportunities for implementing more personalized, flexible, and evidence-based assessment practices. At the same time, these technological advances present important challenges related to academic integrity, equity, and the validity of assessment instruments.

papers.title: Integrating AI-Driven Motion Recognition Systems in University Volleyball Instruction: A Case Study
papers.authors: Zhu Xin, Xie Yu
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: University-level volleyball training often depends on subjective coach evaluations, which can lead to inconsistent, time-consuming, and less scalable instruction. With the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in sports analytics, this study develops a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based motion recognition system for classifying volleyball actions, including serving, passing, blocking, and spiking. The model was trained using the Hyper AI volleyball motion dataset containing 4,830 annotated frames from collegiate match footage. The preprocessing pipeline included normalization, denoising, frame extraction, and data augmentation. A retrospective simulation case study was designed to replicate a university training environment and evaluate the system’s practical applicability. Experimental results showed a recognition accuracy of 97.36% and a micro-average AUC score of 0.995, with particularly strong performance in identifying spike and block actions. Compared with traditional coaching approaches, the AI-based framework provided more consistent evaluations, reduced misclassification errors, and accelerated error detection. The findings demonstrate the potential of AI-driven systems to support personalized feedback, objective performance assessment, and scalable coaching in university sports education. The framework also offers opportunities for adaptation to other sports and future pedagogical innovations.

papers.title: AI-Based Financial Literacy, Perceived Ease of Use, Technology Readiness, and Personal Financial Management Behavior: the Mediating Role of Trust in AI
papers.authors: Jamal Hanaffy, Dewi Listiorini, Sukma Hendri
papers.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed personal financial management, yet the gap between the adoption of digital financial tools and the financial literacy and trust required for effective use remains underexplored, particularly in urban Indonesia. This study examines the effects of AI-Based Financial Literacy, Perceived Ease of Use, and Technology Readiness on Personal Financial Management Behavior, with Trust in AI as a mediating variable. The study extends the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Technology Readiness Index (TRI) through the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework by integrating trust into an AI-based financial behavior model. A quantitative explanatory design was employed using survey data from 200 purposively selected respondents in Depok City, aged 18–40 years and using AI-based financial applications. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The results show that AI-Based Financial Literacy (β = 0.214; p = 0.001), Perceived Ease of Use (β = 0.187; p = 0.005), and Technology Readiness (β = 0.168; p = 0.008) positively and significantly affect Personal Financial Management Behavior. All hypotheses (H1–H6) were supported, with R² = 0.612. The findings confirm that Trust in AI mediates these relationships. The study contributes to TAM and TRI by highlighting trust as a mechanism linking AI-related capabilities to financial behavior and offers implications for developing an inclusive and trustworthy digital financial ecosystem.

papers.title: The Impact of Robotics and Artifical Intelligence on Entrepreneurial Skills Development and Marketing Innovation
papers.authors: Efa Wakhidatus Solikhah, Riky Dwi Puriyanto
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed business operations and accelerated digital innovation among technology startups. However, limited studies have simultaneously examined the roles of AI adoption, technological infrastructure, and digital entrepreneurship literacy in shaping digital entrepreneurial capability, marketing innovation, and entrepreneurial performance. This study investigates these relationships within technology startups in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from startup founders, managers, and directors. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The findings reveal that robotics and AI adoption significantly enhances digital marketing innovation but does not have a significant effect on digital entrepreneurial capability. Technological infrastructure positively influences both digital marketing innovation and digital entrepreneurial capability, while digital entrepreneurship literacy significantly improves digital entrepreneurial capability but shows no significant impact on digital marketing innovation. Furthermore, digital marketing innovation and digital entrepreneurial capability positively contribute to entrepreneurial performance. These findings highlight that the benefits of robotics and AI adoption are primarily realized through innovation-oriented mechanisms rather than direct capability development. This study contributes to the digital entrepreneurship literature by providing empirical evidence from technology startups in an emerging digital ecosystem and emphasizing the importance of infrastructure readiness and entrepreneurial literacy in improving organizational performance.

papers.title: Politeness Toward Artificial Intelligence: Linguistic Ritual, Behavioral Conditioning, and the Ethics of Human–AI Interaction
papers.authors: Ruijie Lin
papers.abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence has transformed digital interaction from mechanical command exchange into sustained linguistic communication. Although AI systems possess neither consciousness nor emotion, the language people repeatedly use toward them can still shape human habits. Drawing on theories of politeness, interaction ritual, anthropomorphism, and behavioral conditioning, this paper argues that courteous communication with AI is socially valuable because it rehearses restraint, reciprocity, and civility. At the same time, courtesy must not be confused with recognition of machine personhood: excessive anthropomorphism may encourage emotional dependency and obscure the difference between simulated empathy and genuine human reciprocity. The ethical question is therefore not whether machines deserve respect, but how human communicative norms should be preserved in increasingly automated environments.

papers.title: Evaluation of Universal Basic Income as a Viable Policy Response to AI-Induced Technological Unemployment in the US Labor Market
papers.authors: Jeffrey Chen
papers.abstract: This study discusses whether Universal Basic Income (UBI) can serve as an effective policy to address structural unemployment caused by the widespread adoption of AI in the U.S. labor market. Unlike previous technological advances, generative AI threatens cognitive and middle-class professional roles, exposing many loopholes in traditional welfare systems of the old era. This article will analyze secondary data from four different pilot projects (Stockton SEED, Alaska Permanent Fund dividends, Finland's Basic Income Experiment, and Kenya's GiveDirectly) and combine macroeconomic models to make policy comparisons. The study mainly examines three intrinsic dimensions: labor market incentives, psychological resilience for retraining, and financial feasibility. The results show that UBI does not reduce labor force participation rates. On the contrary, it can serve as an important social stabilizer, improving mental health and providing the cognitive bandwidth needed for retraining. However, macroeconomic estimates show that implementing a nationwide UBI in the U.S. would face extremely severe fiscal constraints, with annual costs reaching $3 trillion. The findings suggest that although UBI is generally not feasible for government finances in the short term, targeted basic income is a practical and vital policy tool that can ensure income security during AI-driven economic transformation.

papers.title: Hubungan Paparan RNG pada Game Online terhadap Tingkat Stres dan Gangguan Siklus Menstruasi pada Wanita Usia 17-30 Tahun
papers.authors: Yeuis Diah Sri Lestari, Muhammad Azwar, Zamli Zamli, Freddy Chandra Montolalu
papers.abstract: Background: Menstrual cycle disorders may be influenced by psychological and lifestyle factors, including exposure to Random Number Generator (RNG) mechanisms in online games. Objective: To determine the relationships between RNG exposure, stress, and menstrual cycle disorders, as well as stress, BMI, physical activity, sleep quality, and dietary habits with menstrual cycle disorders. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among 97 women aged 17–30 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using the Chi-Square test and logistic regression. Results: RNG exposure was significantly associated with stress and menstrual cycle disorders (p=0.000). Stress, BMI, physical activity, sleep quality, and dietary habits were also significantly associated with menstrual cycle disorders (p=0.000). Stress was the most dominant factor. Conclusion: RNG exposure, stress, BMI, physical activity, sleep quality, and dietary habits were significantly associated with menstrual cycle disorders among women aged 17–30 years.

papers.title: Analisis Majas Metafora dalam Lirik Lagu Album Help Ever Hurt Never Karya Fujii Kaze
papers.authors: Bintang Purnama Putra, Subandi Subandi
papers.journal: Pragmatik Jurnal Rumpun Ilmu Bahasa dan Pendidikan
papers.abstract: This study aims to describe the forms, meanings, and functions of metaphorical expressions in the lyrics of Fujii Kaze’s album Help Ever Hurt Never based on Ullmann’s (2014) theory. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, using eleven song lyrics from the album as the data source. Data were collected through non-participant observation and note-taking techniques, while the analysis involved data reduction, classification, meaning interpretation, functional analysis, and descriptive presentation of the findings. The results reveal four types of metaphor. First, anthropomorphic metaphors are found in “優しさに殺られた” (yasashisa ni yarareta) and “忍び足” (shinobiashi), which portray emotional experiences and moral temptation. Second, animal metaphors appear in “さぁ羽のばして” (saa hane nobashite) and “飛べないこの鳥” (tobenai kono tori), representing freedom and limitation. Third, concrete-to-abstract metaphors are identified in “この空に捨てて” (kono sora ni sutete) and “わたし泳ぐだけ” (watashi oyogu dake), depicting the release of burdens and the depth of emotional experience. Fourth, synesthetic metaphors occur in “凍えた心が愛に溶けてゆく” (kogoeta kokoro ga ai ni tokete yuku) and “着色の言葉 無味無臭の心” (chakushoku no kotoba, mumi mushuu no kokoro), representing emotional healing and insincerity. These four types of metaphor operate through the principle of similarity in semantic transfer while simultaneously strengthening the aesthetic value and emotional messages conveyed in the lyrics.

papers.title: Large Language Models - an Overview
papers.authors: Saleh Ramezani
papers.abstract: Large Language Models: Foundations and Applications in Clinical Text is an educational presentation introducing the development, architecture, and clinical applications of modern language models. The presentation traces the evolution of language modeling from early neural-network concepts and rule-based systems through n-gram models, recurrent neural networks, LSTMs, GRUs, word embeddings, transformers, and pretrained models such as BERT, GPT, and LLaMA.The presentation explains how transformer architectures and self-attention overcome limitations of sequential models by allowing language models to capture relationships across longer passages of text. It also compares encoder-based and decoder-based architectures, with particular emphasis on BERT and its bidirectional representation of language, masked-language-model training, and ability to capture context in complex biomedical text.A major focus is the application of language models to clinical information extraction. Using pathology reports as an example, the presentation demonstrates how Clinical BERT can represent medical concepts such as p16-positive and p16-negative findings as embeddings and use semantic similarity to classify information from new clinical text. It concludes with a practical multi-layered strategy for clinical text extraction that combines structured data, regular-expression matching, Clinical BERT, and more computationally intensive large language models for increasingly complex cases. The presentation emphasizes the tradeoffs among speed, accuracy, semantic understanding, and computational cost when designing real-world clinical natural language processing workflows.

papers.title: Global templates, local logics: Ethical legitimacy in banking across countries
papers.authors: Miia Chabot, Elisabeth Paulet, Francesc Relaño
papers.abstract: This study examines how banks communicate ethical commitments through annual reports, comparing ethical and conventional institutions across national contexts. We develop an AI-based model (BERT) to detect customer- and society-oriented ethical themes in disclosures from 2019 to 2023. We then conduct panel regressions to examine how governance, culture, and financial health are associated with ethical communication patterns. Drawing on institutional theory and cultural evolution, we show that while customer ethics dominate across the sample, societal ethics are more prominent in ethical banks and selectively adopted by conventional ones. The findings highlight how global sustainability pressures interact with national traditions and institutional settings, producing differentiated ethical narratives and informing debates on legitimacy and responsibility in international banking.

papers.title: CRITICAL THINKING OF UNIVERSITY STUDENTS IN THE ERA OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
papers.authors: Botagoz B. Bermukhambetova, Zhanar Sabyrovna Bekbayeva, Moldir Seidina, С. С. Алдабергенова, P. Bogacz
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in higher education has reopened fundamental questions about the trajectory of students' critical thinking (CT) development. This article reports the results of a longitudinal cohort diagnostic study conducted at three higher education institutions in Astana, Republic of Kazakhstan L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University, Kazakh National University of Sports, and Saken Seifullin Kazakh Agro Technical Research University across four measurement points: 2020, 2022, 2024, and 2026, with a total sample of 334 students. CT was assessed using the Starkey Critical Thinking Test, adapted for Russian-language audiences, which measures analytical reasoning, argument evaluation, fallacy identification, evidence assessment, and problem-solving capacity. Inferential analyses employed the Mann–Whitney U test, Cohen's d effect sizes, and the Kruskal–Wallis omnibus test. Three research hypotheses were formulated and tested: that CT levels would demonstrate a statistically significant positive trajectory over the study period; that the period of active AI adoption (2023–2024) would coincide with a peak in CT performance; and that subsequent normalisation of AI use would be associated with a partial decline. The results confirm statistically significant improvement from 2020 (M = 14.07, SD = 3.71) to 2024 (M = 18.58, SD = 4.44), with a large effect size (d = 1.10, p < 0.001), and a statistically non-significant partial decline in 2026 (M = 17.03, p = 0.059). The overall Kruskal–Wallis test confirms significant between-cohort differences (H = 43.13, p < 0.001). The findings are discussed in relation to active pedagogical strategies, media literacy, and the dual role of AI as both a stimulus and a potential inhibitor of critical reasoning. Implications for competency-based curriculum reform within the Bologna Process framework are considered.

papers.title: AI ALGORITHMS FOR OPTIMIZING UNIVERSITY RESOURCE MANAGEMENT
papers.authors: Азиза Жунусбекова, Samal Askarkyzy, Bakhyt N. Alipova
papers.abstract: This article examines the potential of AI algorithms for optimizing university resource management in the context of the digital transformation of higher education. Modern approaches to the intellectualization of management processes, based on the use of optimization algorithms and machine learning methods, are analyzed. Attention is paid to heuristic and meta-heuristic approaches such as genetic algorithms, particle swarm modeling, and ant colony modeling, which are used to allocate educational, scientific, and human resources at universities. The research methodology includes a combination of complementary scientific methods: analysis of scientific publications and regulations, a comparative analytical approach, algorithmic modeling and optimization methods, statistical data processing, and conceptual modeling. The empirical basis of the study is data from 11 universities located in the cities of Astana and Almaty. The results demonstrate the significant potential of using AI algorithms to improve the efficiency of university resource management. The use of intelligent analysis and optimization methods enables more informed management decisions, promotes the rational allocation of educational, research, and human resources, and improves the quality of educational activities in the context of the digitalization of higher education.

papers.title: Uso ético de la inteligencia artificial generativa en las aulas universitarias: una revisión sistemática
papers.authors: Walter Társilio Pilar Bueno, Mariella Elvira Ramos Huacho, Luis Orlando II Salas Flores, Jessica Arámbulo Palacios
papers.abstract: Introduction: The use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools has transformed educational practices in higher education and introduced new challenges related to academic integrity, privacy, and the responsible use of automated technologies. In this context, it is necessary to establish criteria to guide the ethical integration of these tools into teaching and learning processes. Objective: To analyze the challenges, contributions, limitations, and strategies associated with the ethical use of generative artificial intelligence in higher education contexts. Methodology: A descriptive systematic literature review was conducted using a documentary research design, content analysis, and a data-extraction form as the research instrument. The search was performed in the Web of Science, Scopus, and SciELO databases, considering studies published between 2023 and 2026. After applying the established selection criteria, 20 studies were included in the analysis. Results: The findings showed that 65% of the studies identified risks related to academic integrity, while 55% reported concerns regarding privacy and data protection. Furthermore, 70% emphasized the need to establish institutional policies to guide the use of these tools. The evidence also highlights the importance of strengthening teachers' digital and ethical competencies and promoting oversight mechanisms and transparent criteria for their academic use. Conclusions: The ethical implementation of generative artificial intelligence in higher education requires institutional regulatory frameworks, teacher digital literacy, and clear criteria for academic responsibility. Its integration should be oriented toward complementing educational processes without replacing critical thinking, intellectual autonomy, or the responsibility of university stakeholders.

papers.title: Competencias digitales en estudiantes de educación básica: revisión sistemática de la evidencia científica 2023-2026
papers.authors: Claudia Antonella Mauricio Rojas
papers.abstract: Introduction: Digital competencies are essential for learning, participation, and the holistic development of students. Objective: to analyze the scientific evidence on digital competencies in basic education students. Methodology: the PRISMA 2020 methodology was employed; 25 articles published between 2023 and June 2026 in Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were selected. Results: the development of these competencies is heterogeneous and associated with accessibility, teacher support, and socioeconomic context; artificial intelligence, gamification, and active methodologies favored their strengthening, although gaps in infrastructure, teacher training, and social inequality persist. Conclusion: it is necessary to strengthen teacher training and promote innovative pedagogical strategies that ensure equitable access to technological resources for quality and inclusive basic education.

papers.title: Aplicación de la inteligencia artificial para potenciar la comprensión lectora en estudiantes de educación primaria
papers.authors: Salle Raul Allasi Mendoza, Frine Maria Yucra Chambi
papers.abstract: Introduction: Reading comprehension constitutes an essential competency in primary education due to its influence on learning processes, cognitive development, and students' academic performance. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as an educational tool with the potential to personalize teaching processes and strengthen reading skills. Objective: To analyze the impact of artificial intelligence on strengthening reading comprehension among primary education students. Methodology: A systematic literature review was conducted through the selection of studies following the PRISMA protocol. A categorization matrix was used as an instrument to organize and analyze the information obtained from 20 studies selected according to thematic and methodological relevance criteria. Results: The findings showed that 75% of the studies reported significant improvements in reading comprehension after the incorporation of artificial intelligence-based tools. Research focused on adaptive platforms and educational chatbots predominated, accounting for 60% of the studies analyzed. These technologies supported processes such as personalized feedback, adaptation to students' learning pace, motivation, and active engagement. Conclusions: Artificial intelligence represents a resource with significant potential for strengthening reading comprehension in primary education when integrated through structured pedagogical approaches. Its effectiveness depends on implementation guided by instructional criteria, teacher training, and continuous evaluation to ensure meaningful and appropriate educational use.

papers.title: Transformación digital en la gestión pública educativa: evolución, tendencias globales y agenda de investigación (2015–2025)
papers.authors: José Nazario Tarrillo Gonzáles
papers.abstract: Background: Digital transformation has reshaped traditional models of public educational management, generating the need to strengthen institutional frameworks, digital capabilities, and governance strategies aimed at addressing contemporary technological challenges. Objective: To analyze the evolution, trends, and research agenda on digital transformation in public educational management during the 2015-2025 period. Methodology: A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA protocol. The search was performed in the Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, and Google Scholar databases through the combination of descriptors such as "digital transformation," "digital government," and "educational governance," using Boolean operators AND and OR. A total of 1,173 initial records were identified, and after removing duplicates and applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 23 empirical and review studies were selected for the final analysis. Results: The findings revealed sustained growth in scientific production since 2021, with a predominance of qualitative approaches and thematic concentration on digital governance, teachers' digital competencies, and artificial intelligence applied to educational management. The evidence also showed that digital transformation requires overcoming limitations related to technological infrastructure, institutional capacities, and inequalities in access, particularly in Latin American contexts. Conclusions: Digital transformation in public educational management constitutes a multidimensional process that requires articulation among public policies, technological infrastructure, and the development of educational stakeholders' capacities. Although research in this field is expanding, regional gaps persist, requiring institutional strategies aimed at achieving inclusive, sustainable, and context-responsive digitalization.

papers.title: Generative AI interaction patterns, cognitive autonomy, and delegation: Initial versus final semesters in STEM higher education
papers.authors: Sergio Juárez Vázquez, Francisco Javier Sol Sampedro, Gabriela Rivadeneyra-Romero, José Luis Carrillo Valdés, Tania Castillo Villegas
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: The intensive use of generative AI tools in higher education raises questions about their impact on students' cognitive autonomy. This study compares students' interaction with these tools and examines factors potentially associated with differences in cognitive autonomy between students in the early semesters (2nd to 4th) and final semesters (8th to 10th) of STEM programs. Using a cross-sectional comparative mixed-methods design, cognitive autonomy is assessed with the self-regulation subscale of the Motivated Learning Strategies Questionnaire (MSLQ) and a prompt coding system measuring complexity, critical iteration, and cognitive delegation. Semi-structured interviews identified factors associated with the observed differences between groups. A sample of 188 STEM students participated (116 in early and 72 in final semesters). The results reveal distinct profiles of interaction with AI according to academic progress, with a delegative prompt profile predominating among early-semester students (75.9 %) compared to final-semester students (19.4 %), and a higher overall interaction-autonomy index among the latter (d = 3.92). These findings are consistent with an association, rather than a causal or developmental effect, given the cross-sectional design, between academic trajectory and a more critical, epistemically reflective use of this technology. The results indicate potential risks of technological dependence and a possible weakening of autonomous thinking among students with less disciplinary maturity.

papers.title: Do students’ perceived benefits of generative AI correspond to higher grades in online master’s programs?
papers.authors: Renata Marciniak
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has raised questions about its relationship with academic performance in online higher education. Although students perceive benefits from using GenAI tools, it remains unclear whether these benefits are reflected in their academic results. This exploratory and observational study examines how students in online master’s programs use GenAI, how they perceive its impact on academic performance, and to what extent these perceptions align with their grades. The study combines survey data from 206 students with a longitudinal analysis of 1,185 institutional grades across 11 courses between 2021 and 2024, analyzed at the aggregate level. These grades were used to describe changes over time and were not linked to individual survey responses. In addition, individual-level survey data were used to examine associations among GenAI use, perceived impact on academic performance, and self-reported average grades. Results show a significant association between the frequency of GenAI use and perceived impact on academic performance, with more frequent users reporting a more positive impact. However, no consistent increase in aggregate grades was observed over time, and individual-level analyses did not indicate that more frequent use of GenAI was associated with higher self-reported grades. Positive perceptions were not associated with higher self-reported grades. These findings reveal a gap between students’ perceived impact on academic performance and the grade-based evidence in this study. Students perceived GenAI as having a positive impact on academic performance, but this perception was not associated with higher self-reported grades, and aggregate grades showed no systematic upward trend.

papers.title: Consciousness Bandwidth and Frequency Orthogonality (II): Artificial Intelligence as a High-Energy Non-Cognitive Information Metabolism System
papers.authors: Bo Zhang
papers.journal: Journal of the British Interplanetary Society
papers.abstract: This paper develops a physical framework for understanding contemporary artificial intelligence as a high-energy, non- cognitive information metabolism system. Building on scale-centric causality and frequency orthogonality, it relates energy- flux density to characteristic coherence frequency and argues that large-scale AI computation can generate internally coherent causal dynamics without implying biological cognition or subjective awareness. The mismatch between machine and human timescales is analysed through sampling theory as causal aliasing, with implications for interpretability, alignment, and human–AI interaction. The framework also suggests a local analogue of the Fermi paradox: advanced intelligences operating at substantially different energetic and temporal scales may become causally inaccessible despite spatial proximity.

papers.title: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence for Construction Skills Development: Exploring Educators' and Industry Professionals' Perspectives on Integrating Automation-Driven Competencies into Construction-Related TVET
papers.authors: Joyce Ogheneruona Onatere-Ubrurhe
papers.abstract: This study investigates the integration of human-centered artificial intelligence (HCAI) into construction-related Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes in Nigeria, focusing on educators’ and industry professionals’ perspectives regarding automation-driven competencies. As artificial intelligence transforms the construction sector through technologies such as robotics, digital twins, and predictive analytics, the competencies required of professionals are shifting from traditional technical skills to include AI literacy, digital collaboration, ethical reasoning, and systems thinking. Using a qualitative research approach, the study explores how stakeholders perceive the role of HCAI in enhancing construction education, the essential competencies for future professionals, and the challenges hindering effective integration. Findings reveal strong consensus that HCAI should augment rather than replace human expertise, emphasizing creativity, ethical judgment, and collaboration. Educators and industry experts identified critical automation-driven competencies, such as data interpretation, computational problem-solving, and adaptability, as vital for workforce readiness. However, persistent barriers including outdated curricula, inadequate infrastructure, limited educator preparedness, and weak industry–institution collaboration constrain implementation. The study underscores the need for curriculum reform, educator professional development, and institutional capacity building to align construction education with global digital transformation trends. It recommends embedding AI-supported learning experiences across curricula, strengthening partnerships between TVET institutions and industry, and establishing ethical frameworks to ensure responsible AI adoption. By situating AI integration within a human-centered paradigm, the research contributes to sustainable workforce development and supports Nigeria’s transition toward an AI-enabled construction sector that values human creativity, ethical responsibility, and lifelong learning. Keywords: Human-centered AI, Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET), automation-driven competencies, construction education, workforce development, Nigeria.
keywords: technical and vocational education and training

papers.title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Capacity Building in Technical Teacher-Education: Empirical Insights from Anambra State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Ikenna Anthony Okafor, Chukwuma Uka, Festus Ikechukwu Aduhuekwe
papers.abstract: This study examined the potential of artificial intelligence for capacity building in technical teacher education and the challenges affecting its integration in tertiary institutions in Anambra State, Nigeria. Two research questions guided this descriptive survey. The population comprised 105 technical educators from Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, and the Federal College of Education (Technical), Umunze; no sampling was undertaken. Data were collected using a questionnaire containing 20 items. Three experts established content validity, while Cronbach alpha produced a reliability coefficient of 0.87. Mean and standard deviation answered the research questions, and Welch tests for independent samples compared institutional responses at the 0.05 significance level. Findings showed agreement on listed potentials and challenges. The grand means for AI potential were 3.41 at Nnamdi Azikiwe University and 3.32 at the Federal College, while the corresponding challenge means were 3.43 and 3.39. All item means exceeded the 2.50 criterion, but none of the institutional differences was statistically significant. Respondents particularly recognised personalised learning, current industry knowledge, funding constraints, inadequate infrastructure, pedagogical change, and data security concerns. The study concluded that AI can strengthen instruction, assessment, professional development, and practical trade training, but implementation depends on infrastructure, institutional support, secure policies, and sustained lecturer training. It recommended investment in AI resources, curriculum integration, digital literacy, and phased, supervised adoption of adaptive learning, automated grading, and virtual simulation tools. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Capacity Building, Technical, Teacher-Education, harnessing
keywords: technical and vocational education and training

papers.title: AI Ethics and Integrity in Education 5.0: ChatGPT’s Role in Assessments for Nigerian Pre-Service Teachers
papers.authors: Adekunle Emmanuel Makanjuola, Blessing Mary Aninkan, Titilayo Omobolanle Onajide, Saheed Akanbi Sanusi, Saidat Animot Odunmbaku
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT are increasingly reshaping teaching, learning, and assessment practices in higher education. This study examines the use of ChatGPT in academic assessments among pre-service teachers in four Federal Colleges of Education in Southwest Nigeria. Adopting a qualitative research design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 20 pre-service teachers and 4 lecturers and analysed thematically. The findings reveal that while ChatGPT enhances learning efficiency, supports content organisation, and aids conceptual understanding, its unregulated use raises significant concerns regarding academic integrity, fairness, and assessment validity. Participants reported instances of over-reliance on AI, difficulties in defending AI-generated responses, and unequal access to digital resources, which further exacerbate existing educational inequalities. The absence of clear institutional guidelines also contributes to uncertainty and inconsistent practices among both students and lecturers. Framed within the context of Education 5.0, the study highlights the need for ethically grounded and digitally competent educators capable of integrating AI responsibly into teaching and assessment. The paper concludes by recommending the development of context-specific AI policies, the integration of ethical AI literacy into teacher education, and the redesign of assessment practices to prioritise critical thinking and learning processes. These measures are essential for maintaining academic integrity and ensuring equitable participation in AI-enhanced education. Keywords: ChatGPT; artificial intelligence; academic integrity; Education 5.0; pre-service teachers

papers.title: CHEMISTRY STUDENTS’ AWARENESS AND INTENTIONS TO USE AI-DRIVEN TUTORING SYSTEMS FOR LEARNING
papers.authors: Abiola Tawa Ahmed, Hameed Olalekan Bolaji, Semiu Olawale Makinde, A. Bakr Ibrahim, Aishat Oyenike Salami, Lukman Ayomide Adegboyega
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven technologies are increasingly being integrated into chemistry education to facilitate personalised and adaptive learning. This study examined the awareness, intention, and perceived usability of AI-driven tutoring systems among senior secondary school students in Ilorin City. The study adopted a descriptive survey design using a quantitative approach. The study population comprised senior secondary school students studying Chemistry, from whom 255 students were selected through a multi-stage sampling procedure. Information was gathered with a researcher-designed questionnaire that focused on the students’ awareness, intention, and perceived usefulness of AI-supported tutoring systems. The instrument was subjected to expert review to establish its validity and produced a satisfactory reliability coefficient. The data obtained were analyzed using mean and standard deviation, while simple linear regression was employed to test the relevant relationship at the 0.05 level of significance. The findings showed that the students had a high level of awareness of AI-supported tutoring systems, as reflected by an overall mean score of 3.45. Their intention to use these systems for chemistry learning was moderately positive (overall mean = 2.83), while the perceived usability of the systems was rated as moderate to high (overall mean = 2.82). The regression results showed that students’ awareness had a significant effect on their perceived usability of AI-driven tutoring systems (β = 0.377, p = 0.010). Similarly, students’ intention to use these systems was found to have a significant and positive relationship with perceived usability (β = 0.401, p < 0.05). Based on these findings, the study established that students’ level of awareness and intention to use AI-driven tutoring systems are important factors influencing their acceptance and use in Chemistry education. The study therefore recommends the continuous implementation of AI literacy programmes and the appropriate incorporation of AI-based tools into Chemistry teaching. Such efforts could help students make better use of emerging technologies and potentially improve their learning experiences and academic achievement. Keywords: Artificial intelligence, AI-driven tutoring systems, chemistry education, students’ awareness, intention to use

papers.title: Pedagogy for Education 5.0: Co-Intelligence Frameworks and Human-AI Collaborative Learning
papers.authors: Ritu Dhaliwal
papers.abstract: Education 5.0 represents an emerging human-centered approach to education in which technological innovation is expected to complement, rather than replace, human capabilities. The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has intensified the need to reconsider how students interact with technology, moving beyond the conventional use of AI as a tool for information retrieval towards more purposeful human–AI collaboration. This paper explores the co-intelligence frameworks in which students engage with AI agents as collaborative cognitive partners while retaining human agency, critical judgement, creativity, ethical reasoning and responsibility for learning. Drawing on constructivist, inquiry-based, collaborative, reflective and human-centered perspectives, it proposes a curricular approach involving questioning, AI interaction, verification, reflection, peer collaboration and independent conclusion-building. The paper also incorporates reflective classroom observations concerning AI-assisted learning and examines ethical challenges including overdependence, inaccurate information, bias, privacy, academic integrity and reduced human interaction. A review of recent literature indicates that AI can support idea generation, communication, reflection, knowledge development and collaborative learning. The paper argues that Education 5.0 should therefore focus not merely on adopting AI but on developing students’ capacity to think, question, verify, collaborate and make informed decisions with AI. Keywords: Education 5.0, Co-Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence in Education, Human-AI Collaboration, Digital Pedagogy, Reflective Learning, Collaborative Intelligence

papers.title: Role of Cognitive Computing in Next-Generation Human–Machine Interaction Systems
papers.authors: Shipra Sharma
papers.abstract: Cognitive computing (CC) has emerged as a transformative paradigm in the development of intelligent systems, enabling machines to emulate key aspects of human cognition, including learning, reasoning, perception, problem-solving, and decision-making. The convergence of CC and human–machine interaction (HMI) has facilitated the development of intelligent systems capable of interpreting user intent, learning from user behaviour, and delivering adaptive, context-aware, and personalised interactions. Unlike traditional HMI systems that rely on predefined commands, fixed interfaces, and rule-based interactions, cognitive HMI systems utilize advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, and affective computing to facilitate seamless communication between humans and machines. These systems support multimodal interaction through speech, gestures, facial expressions, eye movements, and behavioural patterns, thereby enhancing usability, accessibility, and user engagement. Thus, this paper explores the basic role of CC in shaping next-generation HMI systems by examining key components, including emotion recognition, adaptive user interfaces, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), context-aware computing, and collaborative robotics.
