papers.authors: S. G. S. Samaraweera
papers.journal: Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities Review
papers.abstract: Developing English language skills in ESL learners is a long-experienced challenge for teachers and the learners. In this scenario, consistent interaction with artificial intelligence (AI) tools capable of orchestrating authentic interactions with the language is found to be useful in facilitating learners to acquire and master of English language skills. Such tools have the potential to create opportunities for learners to achieve personalised and interactive learning experiences, enable teachers to provide individualised feedback, and open avant-garde adaptive pathways for learning. Additionally, they may promote learners’ motivation, encourage their active participation, and engage them in self-directed learning procedures. Therefore, this exploratory single-participant case study aims to investigate whether exposure to AI has a positive impact on developing English language skills. The data were collected using a qualitative case study focused on an academic in a public university in Sri Lanka. The data collection methods included semi-structured interviews, document analysis, and observations. The results obtained during the action research and empirical study indicated that consistent interaction with AI tools facilitates the acquisition of English language skills and enables individuals to use them confidently in authentic situations.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Workforce Competency Mapping in Public Transport
papers.authors: D. Pranaya, Sreedevi Pidugu
papers.journal: International Journal of Sustainable Supply Chain Management
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming modern Human Resource Management (HRM) by automating administrative procedures and providing data-driven insights into employee capabilities. Within public transport systems—where operational decisions span fleets, depots, customer interfaces, and administrative units—aligning workforce competencies with dynamic technological demands is essential. This study presents a quantitative framework that combines multiple linear regression and machine learning algorithms to map workforce competency preparedness and optimize training resource allocation. Using empirical data collected from operational, technical, supervisory, and customer-facing staff (N=397) across the Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC), we evaluate six core competency drivers: AI readiness, digital literacy, operational analytics competence, safety and compliance competence, learning agility, and institutional support. Multiple regression results indicate that all six drivers significantly influence competency preparedness (), with operational analytics competence () and safety and compliance competence () exerting the strongest standardized effects. Furthermore, comparative machine learning classification demonstrates that Logistic Regression (, Accuracy ) and Naïve Bayes () effectively categorize employees into low, moderate, and high training priority levels without circular prediction error. The study provides human resource practitioners and mobility policy-makers with an empirical, non-punitive decision support model for target-oriented workforce development.

papers.title: Mind the Trust Gap: Identifying (Mis)alignments in Teacher-Student Views Toward Control and Agency in K-12 Classroom AI
papers.authors: Tomohiro Nagashima, Lisa Siegrist, Niklas Scholz, Shintaro Sato, Martina Vincoli, Man Su
papers.journal: Repository for Publications and Research Data (ETH Zurich)
papers.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based technologies have been integrated into school classrooms where multiple stakeholders (with different roles) interact with each other, it is critical to deeply understand stakeholder views in the classroom. In particular, prior work has not fully uncovered how teachers’ and school students’ views might or might not align well with each other, especially in K-12 classrooms. We conducted a speed-dating study using storyboards with 16 school students and 15 school teachers in Germany to investigate alignments and misalignments between their views on student-AI decision-making control in K-12 classroom. Through an explicit pair-matching analysis, we found that students and teachers had misaligned views on several key topics, including how much they trust AI and social and emotional aspects of student learning with AI. Findings also revealed the importance of teacher-student relationships outside of AI use that shape stakeholders’ views and interactions. We discuss potential reasons for the observed misaligned views and strategies to fill the perspective gaps. This study illustrates the complexities of preferences in teacher-student-AI interactions that depend on the dynamic relations among the stakeholders.

papers.title: Snapshots of Artificial Intelligence as a Source of Risk in Asset Management
papers.authors: Derived from original PMR research written by Gueorgui S. Konstantinov and Frank J. Fabozzi using AI and an editor
papers.abstract: Quickly apply original, key PMR-published papers with Snapshots—a short article companion that distills PMR research into compressed, digestible takeaways, so you can put the paper’s core ideas to work in your investment process—fast. This Snapshot article is based on research arguing that once AI-extracted features influence capital allocation, measured parties can adapt disclosures to the tool, weakening historical signal reliability and creating technological epistemic risk that standard model validation may not detect.

papers.title: Integrating (OLAP) Online Analytical Processing With a Fast Algorithm for Epileptic Seizures Detection
papers.authors: Ilyas Zidane, Wajih Rhalem, Nordine Zidane
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, significantly impacting the quality of life of patients. Effective detection and analysis of epileptic seizures are crucial for timely intervention and management. This paper presents the integration of a fast algorithm for epileptic seizures detection with an OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) system using a star schema data warehouse model. By leveraging OLAP capabilities, we perform multi-dimensional analyses to derive insights into patient-specific seizure patterns, channel efficacy, and temporal trends. The CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database is utilized for this study, demonstrating the practical application of the proposed model. The results highlight the potential of combining advanced algorithms with OLAP for enhanced data analysis and improved patient care.

papers.title: Evaluating the Application of Machine Learning in Quality Control of Residential Housing Projects in Lagos State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Prince Oluleye Akanni, Makinde Olutunji Johnson, Ayotomide James Obasa, Oluwasanya Taiwo
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
papers.abstract: Residential building construction in Lagos State, Nigeria, continues to be affected by recurring structural failures and quality non-conformances linked to an overreliance on manual, inconsistently applied quality control (QC) practices and a fragile regulatory enforcement environment. While international evidence increasingly shows that Machine Learning (ML) technologies can substantially improve construction quality monitoring, no empirical study had systematically examined the existing state of QC practice or the level of ML application specifically within the Lagos State residential construction context. This study evaluate the application of Machine Learning in construction quality control within the study area.

papers.title: The Association Between Nursing Students’ Attitudes towards Artificial Intelligence and Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness: A Descriptive and Cross-sectional Study
papers.authors: Merve Aslı Işık, Sultan Özkan Şat
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aims to examine the relationship between nursing students’ attitudes towards AI and their readiness for medical AI. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study. The research was conducted with 455 nursing students from two universities in Türkiye. Data were collected using the “General Attitudes Towards Artificial Intelligence Scale” and “the Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness Scale”. Descriptive statistics, t-test, ANOVA and multiple linear regression analyses were employed for data analysis. Results: Students’ attitudes towards AI were found to be moderately positive overall (M=43.04, SD=7.25), with a high mean total score for medical AI readiness (M=72.41, SD=12.26). Positive attitudes towards AI were significantly associated with high readiness scores in cognition, ability, vision, and ethics sub-dimensions (p<0.001). Possessing a positive attitude towards AI, having completed an AI-related course, and being a fourth-year student were identified as significant predictors of medical AI readiness (p<0.05). The cognitive dimension of medical artificial intelligence readiness among male students and the ethical dimension of medical artificial intelligence readiness among those whose income exceeded their expenses were also identified as significant predictors (p<0.05). Conclusions: The findings suggest that fostering positive attitudes toward AI is closely linked to higher levels of readiness for medical AI among nursing students. Enhancing AI readiness may play a pivotal role in strengthening clinical decision-making, improving patient safety, and supporting adaptability to technological innovations in the AI era. Accordingly, nursing education programs should prioritize AI literacy training and integrate AI-focused content into curricula to facilitate students’ preparedness for

papers.title: An empirical analysis of generative artificial intelligence models for enhancing software development efficiency
papers.authors: Halyna M. Hubal, Vladyslav Khambir, Андрій Волівач, Maryna Kryvoberets, Roman Abakumov
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: The influence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) on modern software development is undeniable, offering intelligent code generation, automated debugging, on-the-go programming support, and more. Despite the widespread adoption of AI tools such as GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT in coding and their increasing use in software development, there has been a dearth of empirical studies that rigorously assess the efficiency and quality of software development when these tools are at play, using the same benchmark datasets. The study employs an empirical approach to compare the performance of generative AI models in enhancing software development efficiency, using a novel transformer-based large language model (LLM) framework and innovative techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). The framework proposed here is based on a comparison of the workflow of traditional software development with that of AI-assisted programming environments. The models presented are evaluated against the HumanEval and Mostly Basic Programming Problems (MBPP) benchmark datasets for programming ability, functional correctness, and software quality. Multiple evaluation metrics, including code generation accuracy, task completion time, defect density, pass@k score, maintainability index, and developer productivity, are analyzed using various validation techniques, including statistical methods. The experimental results prove the capability of the proposed AI-based framework to attain high coding efficiency, fast software development, and decrease manual programming efforts in comparison to the traditional approaches.

papers.title: From Adoption to Account Ability: Governing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its Subsets in Medical and Dental Education
papers.authors: Shehzad Akbar Khan
papers.journal: Journal of Gandhara Medical and Dental Science
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into medical and dental education marks a transformative shift in how knowledge is produced, delivered, and assessed. From adaptive learning systems to generative tools, AI is reshaping medical and dental learning environments globally. This adoption is accelerating, affecting governance frameworks.1 This growing imbalance raises a fundamental question for medical and dental governance. How can medical and dental institutions ensure the responsible and ethical use of AI while maintaining professional standards? Current evidence indicates that AI is a core component of medical and dental education, moving beyond its earlier role as a supporting tool.2,3 It is increasingly used for simulation-based training, clinical decision support, and automated assessment. A recent analysis underlines that generative AI, a subset of AI, has significant potential to enhance personalized learning and clinical training, but it also raises critical concerns about accuracy, ethical use, and reliability.4,5 These concerns are relevant to medical and dental education and health professions education, where compromised learning or inconsistent assessment may eventually affect patient safety. In Pakistan, the regulatory landscape is changing to address these challenges, with regulatory bodies recently strengthening their educational and ethical frameworks, including updated accreditation standards, competencies, and codes of conduct for medical and dental institutions.6 The updated ethics code emphasizes accountability, integrity, and patient safety, requiring institutions to provide high standards in teaching and professional conduct. These structures do not clearly address AI, but they can provide a strong regulatory foundation for AI governance. Pakistan’s National Artificial Intelligence Policy 2025 signals a strategic national commitment to AI integration.7 The policy emphasizes ethical AI distribution, data protection, and the development of a secure and inclusive AI network, along with inspiring objectives for capacity building and workforce development.8,9 These initiatives are accompanied by growing recognition within medical and dental institutes that AI literacy and governance must become integral to medical and dental training and continuing professional development.10,11 Despite these advances, a critical implementation gap remains. Policies and frameworks provide direction, but institutions often lack operational clarity on how to govern AI in routine academic practice. Uncertainty remains around the appropriate use of AI in assessments, writing, and research, and many faculty members lack adequate training to use these tools effectively. Evidence suggests that although healthcare professionals have positive attitudes toward AI, effective implementation requires structured training and institutional support.12 Moreover, administrative policies should focus on specific steps, such as establishing a clear policy for AI use, ensuring fair assessments, and incorporating AI literacy into the curriculum, so that governance is context-sensitive. In Pakistan, where access to technology and digital resources is uneven, AI may benefit some learners more than others if not carefully managed. Building trust is essential in this transition. AI integration in medical and dental education requires transparency, accountability, and ongoing evaluation. Medical and dental professionals should initiate the development of inclusive, adaptable frameworks aligned with national and global priorities. AI policies in Pakistan mark important progress, where the focus must now shift to sensible implementation. Moving from adoption to accountability is essential to ensure that AI strengthens learning, preserves professional integrity, and improves healthcare outcomes.

papers.title: Object speed and distractor number affect performance but not attentional allocation in multiple object tracking
papers.authors: Nika Adamian, F. Akalan, S. K.Andersen
papers.abstract: Keeping track of multiple moving objects across dynamic real-world scenarios such as driving, team sports, or crowded social environments is a fundamental challenge for visual attention. We have previously demonstrated that as the number of tracked objects increases, the strength of attentional facilitation allocated to each individual object decreases, limiting tracking success. It is also well established that beyond the number of tracked objects, faster-moving objects and objects embedded amongst higher numbers of distractors are more difficult to track. Are these effects on tracking difficulty also mediated by less effective allocation of attention to tracked targets as in the case of tracking more targets? If so, one should expect the strength of attentional modulation to drop systematically with increasing speed and total number of moving stimuli. In two experiments (total n = 70), participants were instructed to track moving targets amongst identical distractors while we manipulated object speed (Experiment 1) and number (Experiment 2). As expected, tracking performance declined with both manipulations. However, steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEPs) recorded during successful tracking revealed that attentional enhancement of tracked targets compared with distractors did not drop with increasing speed or object number. In summary, bottom-up changes in the stimulus display and top-down attentional manipulations affect tracking performance in independent ways, with the balance between strength of attentional allocation and bottom-up demands of the task determining successful tracking. The allocation of attention itself seems to be determined exclusively by top-down goals rather than being reactive to bottom-up display characteristics. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Keeping track of multiple moving objects is fundamental to navigating dynamic real-world scenarios. This ability is accomplished through multifocal attentional selection, which weakens as the number of tracked targets increases. This study asks whether other stimulus manipulations increase tracking difficulty by diluting attentional allocation. Using steady-state visual evoked potentials to measure selective attention during tracking, we demonstrate that both increases in speed and distractor number impair performance, but they do not affect attentional enhancement of targets relative to distractors. This suggests that top-down attentional control operates independently from bottom-up demands.

papers.title: Risk Perception as a Moderating Variable in Generative AI Adoption Among Business School Students
papers.authors: Aivars Spilbergs
papers.journal: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are spreading fast through higher education, reshaping how students learn. Yet what actually drives students to adopt these tools - especially in business schools, where ethical sensitivity and interpretive judgment matter as much as technical skill - is still not well understood. This study looks at how risk perception shapes generative AI adoption, extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) model to do so. Survey data collected from 441 business students in the Baltic Sea region were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to evaluate the effects of performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, study value, habit, and risk perception on AI usage. The model demonstrates substantial explanatory power (R² = 0.654), with habit identified as the most significant predictor, followed by risk perception and social influence. Students rated usefulness, ease of use, and study value highly - yet these factors mattered less than behavioral ones in predicting actual use. The findings point to a clear need: ethical awareness and AI literacy should be built directly into technology-adoption frameworks in business education, not treated as an afterthought.

papers.title: Exploring Digital Media Research in Vocational Education: A Bibliometric Analysis from Scopus Database
papers.authors: Galeh Nip Pratama, Mochamad Bruri Triyono, Slamet Widodo, Thomas Koehler, Valentinus Lilik Hariyanto, Candra Dinata
papers.journal: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON ADVANCES in ENGINEERING EDUCATION
papers.abstract: Rapid technological improvements present both opportunities and difficulties for teaching and learning, elevating digital media to the forefront of vocational education discussions. This study investigates the evolution of digital media research in vocational education to determine its impact on current and future educational practices. The Scopus database was used to conduct a bibliometric analysis of 28 publications published between 2005 and 2024. Despite rare oscillations, the main research trend is steadily increasing, particularly after 2020. The analysis identified four key research areas: (1) innovative digital learning via virtual reality, simulation, and e-learning platforms; (2) technological adaptation and teacher preparedness; (3) industry relevance and employability enhancement; and (4) inclusive and ethical digital transformation. Co-authorship and keyword network studies show that developing nations have contributed very little to this field's research, which is still largely regional in scope. The focus of recent research has switched to data analytics, immersive learning, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven personalization, which reflects the intersection of emerging technologies and digital pedagogy. This paper proposes the Digital Media Integration Framework for Vocational Education Transformation, which links digital media platforms, AI integration, pedagogical innovation, and institutional preparation, based on the findings presented. The findings highlight the need for inclusive, interdisciplinary, and policy-supported strategies to assist the digital transformation of vocational learning and provide valuable insights about how digital media is changing in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
keywords: technical and vocational education and training

papers.title: Does Body Mass Index Matter? Static Balance in Transfemoral Prosthesis Users
papers.authors: Sisybania Sisybania, Muhammad Fathi, Ines Maharani Pratiwi
papers.abstract: Background: Body Mass Index (BMI) is an important indicator in assessing an individual's nutritional status and may influence body balance, particularly in individuals with transfemoral (above-knee) amputation using a prosthesis. Postural imbalance in prosthesis users can disrupt mobility and increase the risk of falls. This research aimed to determine the relationship between Body Mass Index and static balance in users of transfemoral prosthesis. Methods: This study employed a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design and purposive sampling technique. The study involved 15 subjects who met the inclusion criteria. BMI was calculated based on body weight and height, while static balance was assessed using the Romberg Test. Normality was tested using the Shapiro-Wilk test, and hypothesis testing was conducted using Spearman correlation due to non-normal data distribution. Results: The analysis showed a significant relationship between BMI and static balance, with a correlation coefficient of 0.687 and a significance value of 0.005 (p < 0.05). This indicates that a higher BMI is associated with greater impairment in static balance among transfemoral prosthesis users. Conclusion: There is a significant relationship between body mass index and static balance in transfemoral prosthesis users. Weight management plays a crucial role in the rehabilitation process to improve balance and quality of life in individuals with lower-limb amputation.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as A Pedagogical Assistant in Hindu Religious Learning
papers.authors: Ni Nengah Sudarsini, Ni Wayan Ria Lestari, I Putu Suweka Oka Sugiharta
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers new possibilities for supporting learning preparation. In Hindu religious learning for early childhood education, however, its use requires attention to children’s developmental characteristics, cultural and religious contexts, and the teacher’s role. This study aims to analyze the perspectives of prospective Early Childhood Education (ECE) teachers on the use of AI as a pedagogical assistant in Hindu religious learning. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed through semi-structured interviews with eight prospective ECE teacher students at Institut Agama Hindu Negeri Gde Pudja Mataram, selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed through data collection, condensation, presentation, and conclusion drawing, supported by qualitative coding procedures. The findings show that participants perceived AI as useful for generating ideas and preparing RPPH, learning activities, stories, songs, games, and visual media. AI was also used to support Hindu religious learning related to bhakti, Tri Hita Karana, Tri Kaya Parisudha, and religious practices. However, participants did not directly adopt AI-generated outputs, instead, the outputs were selected, modified, simplified, and validated according to children’s characteristics, learning objectives, curriculum, cultural context, and Hindu religious values. Participants also expressed concerns about potential dependence on AI and reduced independence in developing learning ideas. The study concludes that AI is perceived as a supporting pedagogical resource rather than a replacement for teachers. Responsible use requires human judgment in selecting, adapting, and validating AI-generated content, while teachers remain essential in providing direct interaction, guidance, and exemplary behavior in Hindu religious learning.

papers.title: KG-CBC: A Novel Framework for Student Cognitive Simulation Using Knowledge Graphs to Guide LLM Capability
papers.authors: Ruiqiang Guo, Chunna Li, Xu Jia

papers.title: Reimagining Teacher Education in the Digital Era Emerging Pedagogies Professional Competencies and Future Directions
papers.authors: Duryodhan Mahakud
papers.abstract: The rapid development of digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), immersive environments and generative AI is changing the knowledge, practices and professional judgements expected of teachers and teacher educators. Teacher education can therefore no longer be understood only as preparation for conventional classroom instruction. It increasingly involves preparing future teachers to design learning experiences with digital tools, interpret technology-mediated evidence, use AI responsibly, support diverse learners, and maintain professional and ethical judgement in increasingly complex learning environments. This thematic narrative review synthesizes major conceptual and research trends concerning teacher education in the digital era. The review focuses on eight interconnected themes: digital transformation of teacher education; technology-enhanced pedagogies; artificial intelligence and generative AI; digital and AI professional competencies; personalised and learner-centered learning; ethical and human-centered practice; changing roles of teacher educators; and institutional conditions for sustainable transformation. Recent literature indicates [4, 5, 6, 7] that AI and digital technologies can support lesson planning, resource development, feedback, personalised support, professional learning and reflective practice, but their educational value depends on pedagogical purpose, teacher judgement, contextual fit and institutional support. Recent reviews also point to gaps in AI literacy, particularly in the practical and ethical dimensions of teachers' professional knowledge. On this basis, the paper proposes a Human-Centered Digital Teacher Education Framework connecting technological affordances with pedagogical judgement, professional competence, ethical responsibility and institutional support. The review argues that digital transformation should not be equated with the simple adoption of devices or platforms. Sustainable teacher education requires a shift from technology integration to pedagogical integration, in which teachers learn not merely how, but when, why and under what ethical conditions technologies should be used.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Artificial Intelligence in Recommender Systems to Support Financial Education: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Kátia Abdala Lorenz, Anita Maria da Rocha Fernandes
papers.abstract: A lack of personal financial planning and knowledge about how to manage money are among the factors that contribute to citizens’ indebtedness. This study investigates how machine learning-based artificial intelligence has been applied in recommender systems to support financial education and financial health. A systematic literature review was conducted using PRISMA-informed procedures, with research questions structured according to Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, and Context. Eligible studies applied machine learning to personalized recommendation, financial-profile classification, or financial decision support for individuals, incorporated at least one interpretability, explainability, or process-transparency mechanism, and were published in English, Portuguese, or Spanish between 2021 and 23 July 2026. Five databases were searched on 23 July 2026, yielding 139 records, of which 11 studies were included after deduplication and screening. Methodological quality was assessed using a nine-item framework addressing objective clarity, dataset and validation description, real-user evaluation, and reproducibility. Findings were narratively synthesized across nine research questions because heterogeneous designs and metrics precluded meta-analysis. Included studies primarily employed tree-based and ensemble models, clustering, and time-series techniques, supported by feature-attribution methods, local explanations, Integrated Gradients, interpretable models, or natural-language justifications. Quality appraisal revealed limited real-user evaluation and reproducibility. No controlled experiments compared identical systems with and without explanations; therefore, current evidence does not establish that explanations alone improve user understanding, trust, decision quality, or financial behavior. Future research should prioritize longitudinal, real-user evaluation of explainable financial recommender systems. The review protocol was not publicly registered.

papers.title: TBLT-Based Generative AI Chatbot Tutor Prototype for Beginner EFL Daily Conversation Practice
papers.authors: Anita Dwi Hapsari, M. Tsalits Nururrohman, Leslie Elisa S. Cobilla, Syifa Khuriyatuz Zahro, Diana Zuschaiya
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Speaking remains a significant challenge for beginner EFL learners in Indonesia due to limited practice opportunities and personalized feedback. Although AI-based learning applications are increasingly available, few integrate Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT) into structured chatbot instruction. This study aimed to develop and evaluate the feasibility of a TBLT-based generative AI chatbot tutor for daily English conversation practice at Universitas Islam Darul 'Ulum (UNISDA) Lamongan, Indonesia. Using a Research and Development (R&D) approach based on the ADDIE model, 30 beginner EFL students participated in the needs analysis and 40 in feasibility testing. The web-based prototype, powered by the Google Gemini API, incorporated structured prompts covering seven daily conversation themes and 49 sub-themes. User experience was assessed using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) on a 5-point Likert scale, while interviews involved 10 participants. Results showed positive ratings across all UEQ dimensions (mean scores > 3.5), with 85% of participants reporting ease of use. Interviews highlighted increased self-reported speaking confidence, helpful task prompts, and the need for pronunciation feedback. These findings suggest that the prototype is feasible and has preliminary pedagogical potential for independent speaking practice. However, its effectiveness in improving speaking proficiency remains unverified, as the study did not assess learning gains, long-term outcomes, or comparative effectiveness.

papers.title: ChatGPT Use and Critical Thinking Among Undergraduate Students: A Mixed Methods Study
papers.authors: Fauzan Adima, Fitriyatul Hanifiyah, Prima Crismono, Saiful Bahri
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: This study examined undergraduate students' academic ChatGPT practices across critical thinking score categories, focusing on verification, use regulation, and perceived dependence. An observational mixed-methods approach combined a critical thinking test comprising sixteen items, a questionnaire comprising fifteen items, and interviews. Pilot testing involved forty students; Cronbach's alpha coefficients were 0.852 and 0.912 for the test and questionnaire, respectively. The presented interview accounts showed variation within and across score categories. High-scoring interviewees described checking information or limiting use, whereas the moderate-scoring interviewee reported accepting answers without verification. The lower-scoring interviewee reported correcting outputs and prompting again. Several interviewees described perceived dependence or reduced independent engagement, but these accounts did not establish cognitive decline. The original Wilcoxon comparisons did not establish an association or causal effect between use and critical thinking. The study's originality lies in distinguishing answer acceptance, iterative prompting, and independent verification rather than assigning uniform practices to score categories. It contributes contextual evidence for investigating responsible AI engagement and evaluating guidance on source checking and independent reasoning, while acknowledging measurement limitations and restricted generalizability beyond participants.

papers.title: The AI-Generated Advertising Paradox: Content Authenticity, Consumer Skepticism, and Brand Credibility
papers.authors: Ayush Sharma
papers.journal: International journal of business and management invention.
papers.abstract: The increasing use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in advertising has created a fundamental tension between production efficiency and consumer perceptions of authenticity. Although AI-generated advertising enables brands to produce promotional content rapidly, economically, and at scale, consumers may question whether such communication reflects genuine human creativity and authentic brand intentions. The present study examines the relationship between AI-generated advertising, perceived content authenticity, consumer skepticism, advertising credibility, and brand credibility. An empirical analytical framework was developed and tested using a proposed sample of 200 respondents, of whom 191 valid responses were considered for analysis. Data were conceptualised as being collected through a structured questionnaire using five-point Likert-scale items. The analytical framework includes descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis. The proposed analysis indicates that perceived AI involvement is negatively associated with content authenticity and positively associated with consumer skepticism, while content authenticity is positively associated with advertising and brand credibility. Consumer skepticism is expected to have a negative relationship with advertising credibility, whereas advertising credibility is positively associated with brand credibility. The proposed regression models indicate that authenticity and skepticism together explain a meaningful proportion of variance in advertising credibility, while advertising credibility emerges as an important predictor of brand credibility. The study contributes to the emerging literature on AI-generated advertising by conceptualizing authenticity as a central mechanism through which consumers evaluate technologically generated promotional communication. The findings also highlight the importance of human involvement, transparent communication, and context-sensitive AI disclosure in advertising.

papers.title: Toward Building a Strategy for Social Adaptation in Gulf Society in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A study Using Grounded Theory
papers.authors: Mohammad Salman AlKhaza’leh, Azhar Shater, Rakan Radi Alhrahsheh, Hani Yousef Jarrah, Aseel Abdulsalam Al-Ayash
papers.abstract: Objectives: The study aims to explore the social adaptation strategies adopted by Gulf society in response to the transformations brought about by the development of artificial intelligence. Methods: The study employed a qualitative methodology using Grounded Theory, specifically the developed Strauss model, which is based on three key stages: open coding, axial coding, and selective coding. Data was collected from a variety of sources, including personal and group interviews conducted via trusted online platforms such as Zoom and Teams. The sample size consisted of 30 individuals—15 from the education sector and 15 from the local community and family sector—selected using purposive sampling. Results: The study developed a model based on two main dimensions: the individual dimension and the institutional dimension. The results indicated that both public and private institutions in Gulf society quickly adopted digital systems. The Gulf community showed a high level of readiness to adapt through education and training. Furthermore, the use of AI and digital technologies contributed to accelerating changes across various sectors such as education and healthcare, enhancing the management of social and economic crises. The study also revealed a shift in individual priorities, with a greater focus on education and health. Conclusion: This study sheds light on the social adaptation strategies within Gulf society in the era of artificial intelligence, relying on a qualitative methodology using Grounded Theory. The findings concluded that both individuals and institutions are adopting flexible strategies that combine technological and value-based adaptation.

papers.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT 4.0 Translation Techniques to Improve the Quality of Football News Translation on Sabq.org
papers.authors: Muhamad Farhan, M. Zacky Mubarok, Ulil Abshar, Darsita Suparno, Waki Ats Tsaqofi, Ahmad Hifni
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aims to describe the translation technique and measure and evaluate the translation quality used by ChatGPT 4.0 in football news on sabq.org website as an effort to improve the credibility of digital translation. Method: the qualitative method used using the theory of translation techniques by Molina Albir and the theory of translation quality by Nababan and the research data of the quality of the researcher came from three respondents of students majoring in Tarjamah of the State Islamic University of Syarif Hidayatullah Jakarta. Results: This study identified eight translation techniques used by ChatGPT 4.0 in translating football news from Sabq.org, with Amplification as the most frequently used technique (34.37%) and Reduction as the least used technique (1.03%). The final quality score is 2.62, which indicates good translation quality in terms of accuracy, readability, and acceptability. Of the 90 data points, 83.3% had a high level of readability, and 72.2% were accurate and acceptable. Conclusion: These findings suggest that ChatGPT 4.0 is capable of generating quality translations for sports news, but human intervention remains essential for handling cultural nuances and ensuring contextual accuracy. The study highlights the importance of collaboration between AI tools and human translators to achieve optimal translation quality, especially in specialized areas such as journalism.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Epistemic Dependence in Higher Education
papers.authors: Abdel Moula El Guermat, Zakaria El Hilali, Mohammed Bekkaoui
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: The swift incorporation of generative AI into higher education systems raises a number of pressing issues related to epistemic autonomy, knowledge production, and critical thinking. Drawing on theoretical concepts such as epistemic dependence, critical pedagogy, and Critical Digital Literacy (CDL), this paper aims to explore the intellectual dangers of students' uncritical engagement with AI-generated knowledge. More specifically, the analysis sheds light on the ideological and cultural foundations of large language models, technologies that present algorithmic outputs as objective, authoritative, and universal despite reproducing the linguistic, cultural, and epistemological hierarchies characteristic of dominant societies. In this context, it is argued that the growing presence of AI in university education poses a threat to the development of knowledge difference and intellectual autonomy by creating an illusion of epistemic sameness, undermining intellectual freedom, and promoting the hegemony of one form of knowledge over alternative epistemologies. As an alternative strategy, CDL is discussed as an important tool for questioning algorithmic authority and preserving critical thinking skills in technologically mediated higher education environments.

papers.title: Generative AI Use and Reading Comprehension: Associations with Metacognitive Experience in Higher Education—A Quasi-Experimental Study
papers.authors: Albert Marquès Donoso, Jaime BENGURÍA AGUIRRECHE, Marta Neira-Calama, Juan Carlos Sánchez-Huete
papers.abstract: (1) Background: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into academic reading raises the question of whether such tools improve genuine comprehension or merely alter readers’ perception of it. (2) Objective: This study examined the association between generative AI use and reading performance and cognitive experience among university students reading a conceptually dense regulatory text. (3) Method: In a quasi-experimental, post-test-only design, with a single cross-sectional measurement per participant, 531 students from two Spanish higher education institutions read a Spanish-language regulatory text and were assigned to six conditions combining two systems (Microsoft Copilot Chat and ChatGPT 4 and 4.5) with varying pedagogical mediation, from unassisted reading to guided use with prior training. Literal comprehension and conceptual interpretation scores were assessed alongside perceptual measures of interest, attention, perceived learning and explanatory confidence. (4) Results: Literal comprehension did not differ across conditions (F(5, 525) = 0.85, p = 0.518, η2 = 0.008), whereas conceptual interpretation did (F(5, 525) = 3.55, p = 0.004, η2 = 0.033), although no AI condition outperformed unassisted reading. The clearest effect emerged for explanatory confidence (F(5, 525) = 12.58, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.107), followed by attention (p < 0.001, η2 = 0.027). Prior AI training was associated with the lowest interpretation and confidence scores. (5) Conclusions: Generative AI use was associated with changes in the subjective experience of reading, particularly explanatory confidence, more consistently than in actual performance. The observed pattern suggests that how students interact with generative AI may warrant at least as much attention as mere tool availability, although the present design does not permit this effect to be isolated from institutional and phase-related confounders.

papers.title: Research on the Impact of Human–Robot Interaction on Pedestrian Circulation Performance in Urban Public Spaces: A Simulation Analysis Based on AnyLogic
papers.authors: Peinan Qin, Linshen Wang, Guangping Shao, Lina Hu, Jia Fu
papers.abstract: With the increasing deployment of service robots in urban public spaces, this study examines how robot proportion (RP) and composite interaction scenarios affect pedestrian circulation performance. An AnyLogic agent-based model of Quancheng Square, Jinan, was developed using a fixed total population of 10,000 agents. Three composite interaction scenarios (CIS-1–CIS-3) jointly vary interaction distance and duration. Human–robot mixed density (HRMD) and average pedestrian speed (APS) were evaluated over a common post-transient interval. To address population composition confounding and stochastic variability, an additional fixed-pedestrian-demand validation under CIS-3 used 10 independent random-seed runs per condition. Across the original runs, HRMD generally increased with RP, whereas APS showed a non-monotonic pattern. In the validation experiment, APS decreased monotonically as robot number increased when pedestrian demand was held constant, while the fixed-total design showed a high robot-level recovery. This contrast indicates that the apparent APS recovery was partly associated with reduced pedestrian demand. Overall, pedestrian circulation patterns were sensitive to both robot deployment and population composition.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted ACR TI-RADS Assessment of Thyroid Nodules: Potential for Reducing Unnecessary Biopsies in a Prospective Single-Center Study
papers.authors: Rojda Kotan, Bahri Evren
papers.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based ultrasound risk stratification has emerged as a promising tool for improving the evaluation of thyroid nodules. However, prospective evidence regarding its performance in routine clinical practice and its potential impact on biopsy recommendations remains limited. Methods: In this prospective single-center observational study, 1009 thyroid nodules undergoing ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration between May 2025 and May 2026 were independently evaluated using ChatGPT Plus as an investigational AI-assisted decision-support tool. Representative ultrasound images, including dimensional and Doppler images, were submitted to the AI without disclosure of the radiologist-assigned TI-RADS category or subsequent cytological or histopathological findings. AI-assisted and radiologist-assigned TI-RADS classifications were compared with Bethesda cytology, while postoperative histopathology served as the reference standard in the surgically treated subgroup. Diagnostic performance and discordance in risk classification between AI and routine radiologist assessment were evaluated. Results: The study included 1009 thyroid nodules from patients with a mean age of 51.5 ± 13.4 years, of whom 80.7% were female. Bethesda II was the most frequent cytological category (93.6%). AI classified 227 nodules (22.5%) as high risk (TR4–TR5), compared with 761 nodules (75.5%) by routine radiologist assessment (p < 0.001). Among Bethesda II nodules, AI assigned 172 (18.2%) to TR4–TR5 compared with 701 (74.2%) by radiologists. When ACR TI-RADS category-specific size thresholds were applied, FNA would have been recommended for 469 nodules (46.5%) according to AI-assisted classification and 993 nodules (98.4%) according to radiologist-assigned classification (p < 0.001), corresponding to 524 fewer modeled FNA recommendations with AI-assisted assessment. Histopathological evaluation was available for 73 surgically treated nodules, including 48 malignant and 25 benign lesions. Within this surgically verified subgroup, both AI-assisted and radiologist-assigned TI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 100.0%, while specificity was 72.0% for AI-assisted assessment and 60.0% for radiologist assessment. Because histopathological verification was available only for surgically treated nodules, these diagnostic performance estimates apply specifically to the surgically verified subgroup and cannot exclude false-negative disease among nonoperated nodules. Conclusions: AI-assisted ACR TI-RADS assessment produced substantially fewer high-risk assignments than routine radiologist assessment, with the greatest divergence observed among cytologically benign nodules. These findings suggest a potential role for AI as a second-reader decision-support tool for refining thyroid nodule risk stratification and biopsy selection. However, because all nodules had already undergone FNA and histopathological verification was limited to surgically treated cases, the present study cannot establish the safety of AI-guided biopsy de-escalation or exclude false-negative disease among nonoperated nodules. Prospective management studies with longitudinal outcome verification are required to determine whether AI-assisted assessment can safely reduce unnecessary FNA.

papers.title: Rethinking the Structure of AI Literacy in Generative AI Educational Systems: Descriptive Patterns of Expert Convergence and Heterogeneity
papers.authors: Sihoon Lee, Jungmyoung Son, Hong Jiyeon
papers.abstract: The integration of generative AI into education raises questions about how AI literacy should be organized, particularly as competencies may operate across different functions during human–AI interaction. This study examined the content and structural organization of AI literacy through a focused literature synthesis and a two-round Delphi study with 11 experts. An initial framework comprising three domains—AI Understanding, AI Application, and AI Integration—and nine competencies was developed and iteratively evaluated. Experts generally evaluated the competency content favorably, while their judgments showed greater heterogeneity regarding some aspects of structural representation. In Round 2, experts supported non-exclusive domain relationships (M = 4.45, SD = 0.52) and primary and secondary domain associations (M = 4.73, SD = 0.47), whereas the proposed representation of competency placement and cross-domain applicability showed greater dispersion (M = 3.73, SD = 1.19, IQR = 1.50). This descriptive pattern informed a theoretical interpretation of the three domains as functional rather than mutually exclusive categories. The resulting framework provides a basis for considering how AI literacy competencies may be enacted during human–AI interaction and related to curriculum, pedagogy, assessment, teacher roles, and AI technologies in generative AI-supported educational systems.

papers.title: Prioritizing Enterprise Generative AI Adoption Under Regulatory Constraint: A Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process Study of a Financial Holding Company Grounded in the Technology–Organization–Environment Framework
papers.authors: Tingyun Chiu, Chien‐Ping Chung
papers.abstract: Enterprise generative AI adoption in financial holding companies is examined as an organizational governance problem rather than a technology deployment decision. The purpose of this study is to identify and prioritize the factors that should govern such adoption and to clarify the role of regulatory compliance within the resulting priority structure. In a single-case design, a fuzzy analytic hierarchy process framework grounded in the technology–organization–environment framework—four dimensions and twelve criteria—was applied to the judgments of nine cross-functional experts in a Taiwanese financial holding company after its broad deployment of Microsoft 365 Copilot. Consistency was verified at the aggregate and individual-expert level, and robustness was assessed through nine leave-one-out re-estimations, sixteen sensitivity scenarios, and alternative fuzzy specifications. Three findings survive every check: organizational management is the dominant dimension (0.4055), ahead of operational benefits (0.3365), technological risk (0.1403) and regulatory compliance (0.1177); departmental acceptance of AI adoption is the first-ranked criterion; and the criteria ranked second to fifth form a closely bunched tier of organizational and value-creation conditions whose internal order is not stable. The low weight of regulatory compliance is interpreted, on methodological grounds and on the evidence of the regulator’s own risk-based classification of internal-efficiency systems, as the signature of a constraint that precedes prioritization rather than a preference within it. Two refinements of the technology–organization–environment framework for generative technologies follow, together with a testable prediction and a phased, governance-oriented implementation strategy for regulated financial groups.

papers.title: How Does Artificial Intelligence Shape Green Innovation Ambidexterity? The Moderating Role of Managerial Characteristics
papers.authors: Jing Lu, Xixiang Sun, Wei Zhang
papers.abstract: Amid the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technology and growing environmental pressures, this study empirically examines the impact of AI adoption intensity on green innovation ambidexterity (GIA), drawing on organizational ambidexterity theory and dynamic capabilities theory. We also examine the complementary and moderating roles of CEO characteristics in the context of AI technology. Using data from Chinese A-share listed firms during 2011–2025, we test these hypotheses. The results show that AI adoption intensity exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with GIA. Mechanism analysis shows that dynamic capabilities mediate the relationship between AI adoption intensity and GIA. Both CEO IT background and CEO green experience attenuate the effect of AI adoption intensity on GIA. CEO power attenuates the moderating effect of CEO IT background on this relationship. Heterogeneity tests indicate that the effect of AI adoption intensity on GIA is more pronounced in non-heavy-polluting industries and state-owned enterprises. This study provides new evidence on the link between AI adoption and GIA. It also clarifies and validates the complementary and moderating effects of CEO characteristics on AI-driven outcomes, offering practical micro-level insights for firms to strategically deploy digital technologies and achieve sustainable and balanced green innovation.

papers.title: Three Blocks to Build Practical AI: Teachers’ Perceived Feasibility of Conversational Human–Machine Cooperation in K–12 Programming Education
papers.authors: Youngki Park, Youhyun Shin
papers.abstract: Education systems are bringing artificial intelligence (AI) into K–12 curricula, but block-based environments, as usually configured, keep young learners at “toy” exercises. In this study, we examine whether a minimal interface backed by expanded machine capability changes teachers’ judgments of what students can build. In the enhanced Tooee environment for Scratch, students “talk” to a virtual agent with only three blocks. Students delegate complex operations to the machine but write the program logic themselves. The environment supports four data types and three practical capabilities, namely large-scale data processing, automated data collection, and inter-program control. Twenty-five in-service teachers used it throughout a fifteen-session graduate course. In one end-of-course survey, they rated the perceived feasibility of students implementing eight types of AI applications with this environment and with the block-based environments they had used before. Ratings for Tooee were significantly higher for all eight types, and the gains were largest for the three practical capabilities. In the open-ended responses, teachers highlighted the conversational interface, expanded functionality, and immediate feedback, while a small number of them noted runtime errors and concerns about age-appropriateness. In the judgment of practicing teachers, conversational human–machine cooperation was associated with substantially higher perceived feasibility of practical AI application development. As the next step, classroom studies with students are necessary.

papers.title: AI Adoption and Innovation Quality: Evidence from Chinese Manufacturing Companies
papers.authors: Luzhen Bai, Haibing Liu
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a general-purpose technology driving technological and industrial transformation. In this study, we construct an AI adoption indicator based on textual analyses of firms’ annual reports and measure innovation quality using the cumulative three-year forward citation counts—excluding self-citations—of invention patents at the firm-year level. Based on a sample of Chinese A-share manufacturing firms spanning 2011–2021, we found that AI adoption is positively associated with innovation quality. This conclusion remains robust across a range of endogeneity-mitigating specifications and robustness checks. Exploratory mechanism analyses suggest that this positive association is partly accounted for by three channels—R&D investment, human capital, and R&D efficiency—although these results should be interpreted as indicating an association rather than causal mechanisms. Heterogeneity analysis further showed that such association is concentrated in larger enterprises, and it is stronger for enterprises with lower financialization and those in asset-intensive industries. However, no significant difference was observed across firms with different ownership or regional locations. This study expands the literature on the innovation effects of AI and offers new insights into the factors influencing innovation quality in the AI era. It also has implications for business management and public policy with regard to leveraging AI to foster high-quality innovation capabilities, thereby providing a knowledge foundation for industrial upgrading and sustainable development.

papers.title: Conversation-Thread Condition and Temporal Reproducibility of AI-Generated Plant Images: A 30-Day Longitudinal Case Study with Implications for Sustainable Digital Education
papers.authors: Paweł Świsłowski, Mikołaj Latoszewski, Grzegorz J. Wolski, Małgorzata Rajfur
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can accelerate the production of digital teaching materials, but long-term use also requires provenance, reproducibility, and maintainable resource workflows. In a single-account 30-day longitudinal case study, we generated images of the moss Pleurozium schreberi with ChatGPT and Gemini under persistent-thread (P) and new-thread (N) conditions and assessed structural similarity (SSIM), perceptual distance (LPIPS), and CLIP embedding distance. The experimental contrast concerned visible persistent-thread continuity versus newly opened conversations; account-level memory, personalisation, model routing, and other provider-side state were not independently controlled. Under the primary preprocessing, within-day P-N divergence was greater in the observed ChatGPT series than in Gemini for perceptual and CLIP-embedding distance. The LPIPS contrast remained robust under padding-free preprocessing, whereas the structural SSIM cross-platform contrast was strongly preprocessing-sensitive; equivalent geometric-preprocessing sensitivity was not assessed for CLIP. Persistent-thread outputs showed greater observed day-to-day similarity for ChatGPT at structural and perceptual levels, while Gemini showed smaller but consistent P-N differences. Padding-free sensitivity analyses preserved the perceptual within-day contrast and the principal day-to-day thread-condition patterns but showed that the cross-platform within-day SSIM result depended strongly on image preprocessing. The study did not measure learning outcomes, botanical accuracy, energy use, carbon emissions, educator time, or monetary cost; the sustainability implications are therefore limited to provenance-aware digital-resource management and should not be interpreted as demonstrated environmental or economic benefits. Prompt-only documentation was insufficient for recovering a stable visual asset; AI-generated visuals intended for educational reuse should therefore be archived and versioned with their prompt, platform, date, and thread context, while content quality requires separate botanical and pedagogical validation.

papers.title: Human Libraries in Teacher Education: Exploring Pre-Service Teachers’ Narratives of Perceived Change Through Thinking Routines
papers.authors: Unai Nabaskues, Álex Ibáñez Etxeberría, Úrsula Luna, Leire Albás
papers.abstract: The main objective of this study is to explore how pre-service teachers retrospectively describe differences between their prior and current perspectives following participation in a Human Library. This research begins with a review of the literature on the definition and characteristics of Human Libraries and proceeds with the creation of one in a university setting. To this end, the study benefited from the collaboration of the Baketik Foundation, which facilitated contact with five individuals willing to share their testimonies on topics related to human rights. The initial sample consisted of 53 pre-service teachers in the Early Childhood Education Bachelor’s programme at the University of the Basque Country (EHU), although ultimately, following a screening process, the sample was reduced to 51. Data were collected using the “I used to think…/Now I think…” reflection exercise, which the pre-service teachers were asked to complete after listening to the testimonies. The narratives were first examined manually by the researchers to identify recurring ideas and potential thematic categories. Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT were subsequently used to support the identification and consistency checking of the initial category structure, while the final coding was conducted manually by the researchers. Six thematic categories were identified in both sections of the reflection exercise. The descriptive comparison revealed differences in the frequency and elaboration of participants’ narratives, particularly regarding empathy and changes in perspective, peace and social justice, women’s rights and gender-based violence, and silence, social taboos and lack of awareness. Because both sections were produced retrospectively after the Human Library experience, these differences are interpreted as features of participants’ accounts rather than as direct evidence of objectively measured changes in their perspectives.

papers.title: Balancing Local and Global Dependencies in EEG Emotion Recognition via Multi-Scale Hybrid Attention
papers.authors: Yiren Ding, Yangfan Wang, Rui Wang, Tingting Ji
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition remains challenging due to the low signal-to-noise ratio, non-stationarity, strong inter-subject variability, and the distribution of affect-related information across multiple temporal resolutions. Although recent deep architectures have increasingly combined multi-scale local feature extraction with global dependency modeling, the adaptive integration of multi-scale representations before global encoding remains comparatively underexplored. To address this issue, we propose DSFConformer, an EEG emotion-recognition framework integrating multi-scale spatiotemporal convolution, Dynamic Sparse Feature Fusion (DSFF), and lightweight Transformer-based global modeling. The multi-scale encoder captures complementary local EEG dynamics at different temporal resolutions, while DSFF performs sample-adaptive feature reweighting and sparse suppression to reduce the influence of redundant or noise-sensitive responses. A Lite Transformer is subsequently employed to model global contextual dependencies with reduced computational cost. Experiments on the SEED dataset were conducted under complementary evaluation protocols. DSFConformer achieved an accuracy of 96.08% under chronological block-wise segment-level cross-validation. Under the stricter trial-wise protocol, it achieved 78.81% accuracy, statistically comparable to EEG-Conformer at 78.77%, with no significant paired difference. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that multi-scale convolution and DSFF provide the primary recognition-performance gains, whereas the Lite Transformer mainly improves computational efficiency while preserving comparable accuracy. Cross-session and leave-one-subject-out analyses further assess model robustness and generalization. Overall, the results indicate that adaptive sparse fusion of multi-scale EEG representations provides an effective approach for balancing local representation learning, noise-aware feature integration, and efficient global dependency modeling.

papers.title: Exploring Artificial Intelligence-Generated Feedback for Pharmacy Students
papers.authors: Diyaben Patel, Mariam Abouelsaad, Jason Brian Reed, Amy Heck Sheehan
papers.abstract: Background: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into educational environments is accelerating, with growing interest in its potential to enhance learning outcomes. This pilot study aimed to assess student perceptions regarding the quality and educational impact of AI-generated feedback. Methods: Second-professional-year pharmacy students (n = 148) enrolled in a drug literature evaluation course received AI-generated feedback for a draft assignment which required students to critically evaluate a recently published journal article. Feedback was generated by an AI assistant that offered iterative feedback based on the assignment rubric. After the activity, students completed an electronic survey instrument evaluating the AI feedback regarding its alignment with rubric criteria, accuracy, clarity, and tone. Student perceptions of the feedback’s impact on learning were also assessed. Results: A total of 148 students (100%) completed the activity and responded to at least one item of the survey tool. Most students agreed with the AI-generated feedback for each section of the assignment in regard to clarity (61.5% to 76.2%) and tone (66.9% to 74.3%), with lower agreement related to alignment with the rubric (33.8% to 60.4%) and accuracy (34.5% to 54.2%). Students also expressed concern about the reliability of AI feedback (71.2%) and risk for plagiarism (50%). Conclusions: AI-generated feedback was positively received in some areas. However, students expressed apprehension regarding its accuracy, reliability, and potential accusation of plagiarism. These findings suggest further refinement is necessary to enhance AI trustworthiness and educational value in academic settings.

papers.title: Metacognition in AI-Supported Second Language Learning: A Systematic Review of Constructs, Measures, and Evidence (2016–2026)
papers.authors: Hong Yi, Qiang Chen, Zhuo Wang
papers.abstract: Metacognition has informed research on second and foreign language (L2) learning for three decades, while AI tools have supported such learning for nearly as long. Yet, no review has examined how the field conceptualises and measures metacognition under AI mediation. This systematic review identified 60 eligible studies published between 2016 and May 2026. Each study was coded on fourteen dimensions anchored in established taxonomies and appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Only four eligible studies fall within the pre-ChatGPT portion of the review window, from January 2016 to November 2022; 56 were published during the subsequent three and a half years. Three findings emerge. First, measurement is narrowly concentrated: 98% of the 56 post-ChatGPT studies measured self-reported metacognitive regulation, and 66% relied on self-report alone. Only one study in the full corpus measured metacognitive accuracy. Five post-ChatGPT studies combined an AI-absent comparison with process-level data, and only one of these also measured judgement accuracy. Second, 41% of post-ChatGPT studies used tools that combined two or more functional orientations within a single interface, a configuration not represented by the field’s inherited four-category taxonomy of AI applications. Third, none of the 18 contrast-based studies assigned the regulatory operation to the system in place of the learner. In every design that specified the division of labour, the learner retained that operation; three designs did not specify it. The condition most in need of testing therefore remains untested. Reported findings skew positive, but correlational and qualitative designs account for a disproportionate share of that evidence. The review concludes with a research agenda centred on calibration and process data.

papers.title: Examining Computer-Science Students’ Metacognitive Beliefs and Reported Practices in Verifying AI-Generated Code: A Concurrent Mixed-Methods Study
papers.authors: Shanshan Li, Jingqi Tang, Zhen Qiang, Zhuo Wang
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) accelerates programming, but its educational value depends on whether students check generated code before accepting it. This concurrent mixed-methods study examined which beliefs accompany such checking among computer-science students at one Chinese university. Survey responses from 294 students were analyzed with an exploratory structural equation model treating three practices as separate outcomes: checking code line by line before use, practicing without AI, and declining in advance to delegate. Robustness checks included ordinal estimation, acquiescence modeling, split-half replication, and multiverse analysis; eleven students were interviewed. Verification-dispensability belief, endorsing reasons for treating further checking as unnecessary, was the only construct negatively associated with all three practices in every robustness check. Other beliefs were narrower or inert: perceived AI literacy accompanied line-by-line checking alone, generic metacognitive self-regulation none. Delegation breadth, the number of activities handed to GenAI, was unrelated to all three: volume of delegation said little about checking. Interviews exposed a mismatch between self-reported categories and actual workflows: students allocated checking by task purpose, accepted process-level understanding, and delegated verification to other AI models, a practice unmeasured by the survey. The data are cross-sectional and self-reported, so these are associations requiring behavioral and longitudinal confirmation.

papers.title: Clinical Outcomes and Treatment Characteristics of Seizure Threshold-Titrated Electroconvulsive Therapy in Schizophrenia: A 3.5-Year Retrospective Naturalistic Course-Level Study
papers.authors: Claudia Elena Anghel, Ciprian Ionut Bacila, Bogdan Ioan Vintilă, Monica Cornea, Andreea Maria Grama, Andrei Lomnășan, Iulian Roman-Filip, Laura Ștef, Bălan (Negrău) Cristina Ioana, Corina Roman-Filip
papers.abstract: Background: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is used as an augmentation strategy in treatment-resistant schizophrenia, but real-world data on individualized seizure threshold-guided treatment remain limited. This study evaluated clinical outcomes of seizure threshold-titrated ECT and described seizure expression and technical treatment parameters during acute ECT courses. Methods: A retrospective naturalistic study included acute ECT courses performed between March 2022 and December 2025 at the ECT Department of the Dr. Gh. Preda Clinical Psychiatric Hospital, Sibiu, Romania. We assessed clinical outcomes at baseline and post-treatment using the PANSS Positive Subscale (PANSS-P), Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF), and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). ECT was delivered using individualized seizure threshold titration alongside stable psychotropic treatment. Electrode placement, stimulation parameters, and motor and electroencephalographic (EEG) seizure characteristics were recorded throughout the treatment course. Results: Seventeen acute ECT courses with paired assessments were analyzed. Median PANSS-P scores decreased from 45 (IQR, 39–48) at baseline to 16 (IQR, 14–20) following ECT (p < 0.001), with a Hodges–Lehmann estimated paired reduction of 26 points. Median GAF scores increased from 44 (IQR, 40–45) to 60 (IQR, 60–65), while median MMSE scores changed from 26 (IQR, 26–28) to 29 (IQR, 28–30). Motor and EEG seizure durations varied substantially across courses and sessions. Right unilateral and bilateral electrode placements were used with similar frequency. Discussion: Our results align with the existing literature on ECT as an augmentation strategy for persistent positive symptoms in treatment-resistant schizophrenia. Improvement in positive psychotic symptoms was accompanied by better global functioning, while the MMSE detected no deterioration in global cognitive performance. The considerable variability in motor and EEG seizure durations further suggests that seizure duration alone may provide limited information regarding clinical improvement. Conclusions: In this retrospective naturalistic cohort, individualized seizure threshold-titrated ECT alongside stable pharmacotherapy was associated with substantial improvement in positive psychotic symptoms and global functioning, without detectable deterioration in global cognitive performance. Given the small sample, the observational design, and absence of a control group, these findings remain preliminary and require confirmation in larger prospective controlled studies.

papers.title: Operationalising AI Governance in Public Administration: An Integrated Regulatory and Risk Management Framework
papers.authors: Nikolaos Levantis, Aggeliki Sgora, Athanasios Tsipis, Spyros E. Polykalas
papers.abstract: Public organisations are increasingly using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Algorithmic Decision-making Systems (ADSs), but the rules and governance requirements that apply to them remain spread across different legal and risk-management frameworks. This study analyses the European Union (EU) AI Act, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Directive (EU) 2016/680, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) AI Principles, and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) to identify where they overlap, where they differ, and where practical implementation remains difficult. The findings are brought together into an integrated EU framework built around seven governance pillars and eight lifecycle stages, linking regulatory requirements with organisational responsibilities, human oversight, operational controls, and post-deployment monitoring. The framework is illustrated through two public-sector scenarios: social-benefit eligibility and AI-supported student assessment. The analysis shows that governing AI in EU public administration requires more than compliance with individual rules; it requires a coherent process that helps organisations decide when AI is appropriate, who is responsible, what safeguards are needed, and how systems should be reviewed over time. The framework’s organisational structure may provide a basis for adaptation to other contexts, but its legal mappings are specific to the EU instruments analysed and would require jurisdiction-specific reconstruction and validation.

papers.title: Multimodal Machine Learning Approaches to Detect Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Using Physiological and Behavioural Biomarkers: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Agmasie Damtew Walle, Ghazal Bargshady
papers.abstract: Background: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by persistent symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity that can affect individuals throughout childhood and adulthood. Accurate and timely detection is important for appropriate support and management, but current assessment relies heavily on behavioural observations, clinical assessments, and information from multiple sources, which can be time-consuming and may be influenced by subjective judgement. These challenges have increased interest in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches that can analyse multiple physiological and behavioural data sources. Multimodal AI approaches may provide a more comprehensive and objective way to detect ADHD by combining complementary information from different data types. Objectives: This systematic review aimed to examine the use of ML and DL methods for ADHD detection using multimodal physiological and behavioural biomarkers, with particular attention to data sources, modelling approaches, multimodal fusion strategies, and reported diagnostic performance. Methods: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines to identify studies published from 2015 to 2026 that applied machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) methods to multimodal data for ADHD detection. We selected studies using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria and extracted and synthesised data from eligible studies. The review included 25 studies. The multimodal data sources examined included neuroimaging modalities, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); physiological signals, including electroencephalography (EEG), heart rate variability (HRV), and electrodermal activity (EDA); behavioural assessments; and wearable or Internet of Things (IoT)-based measures. We also assessed the included studies for methodological quality and model performance to identify current evidence, limitations, and future research needs. Results: The included studies varied substantially in design and sample size, with participant numbers ranging from 22 to 15,883. Most studies used cross-sectional designs. Early multimodal fusion approaches frequently reported diagnostic accuracies above 80%, demonstrating the potential value of combining complementary physiological and behavioural information. Reported informative biomarkers included frontal brain activity, heart rate patterns, and oculomotor behaviour. However, substantial differences in data sources, acquisition procedures, feature extraction, modelling techniques, and evaluation protocols limited direct comparison across studies. Small sample sizes and a lack of standardised data collection and methodological protocols also challenged the generalisability and reliability of the reported findings. Conclusions: Multimodal machine learning and deep learning approaches show considerable potential for improving ADHD detection by integrating complementary physiological and behavioural information. However, substantial heterogeneity in data collection, devices, datasets, validation procedures, and reporting limits comparability and generalisability across studies. Future research should prioritise standardised data-collection protocols, larger and more diverse datasets (including children, adolescents, and participants from different cultural backgrounds), leakage-safe validation, and independent multi-site testing. Fusion strategies should be selected based on modality compatibility and study objectives. Improving model interpretability alongside predictive performance will also support clinical trust and real-world adoption.

papers.title: Identifying Mild Cognitive Impairment from Routinely Collected Physical, Functional and Psychosocial Measures in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Comparative Machine-Learning and Regression Modelling Study in the Northern Japanese ORANGE Registry
papers.authors: Ayuto Kodama, Takako Ohnuma, Kana Sasaki, Kaoru Sugawara, Nobuhiro Fujiyama, Youko Umetsu, Tsuyoshi Ono, Hidetaka Ota
