papers.abstract: Background: Community health check-ups routinely collect non-cognitive data. Whether these support mild cognitive impairment (MCI) triage, and whether machine learning outperforms regression, is unclear. Methods: Cross-sectional analysis of 2650 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 65 in Akita, Japan (2018–2025). MCI was defined by the NCGG-FAT (1.5 SD, age/education-adjusted norms). Thirty-four pre-specified non-cognitive predictors were modelled using tree ensembles, penalised regression, other machine-learning families and simple reference scores, with stratified 70/30 splitting, DeLong tests, 100 repeated splits, training-derived thresholds, calibration metrics and decision-curve analysis. Results: MCI prevalence was 28.6%. Random forest discriminated best (ROC AUC 0.722, 95% CI 0.681–0.761; PR-AUC 0.542) and was well calibrated (slope 1.048; intercept −0.024), but its advantage over LASSO regression was marginal (ΔAUC +0.031, p = 0.044) and absent versus gradient boosting (p = 0.059). All multivariable models greatly outperformed the Kihon Checklist (AUC 0.550, p < 0.001). Neither operating point was deployable: at 0.5, sensitivity was 0.269 (166/227 cases missed); at the training-derived Youden threshold (0.321), sensitivity was 0.604, specificity 0.699, and PPV 0.445. Net benefit exceeded assess-all/assess-none between threshold probabilities 0.15–0.60. Conclusions: Routine non-cognitive data support moderate, well-calibrated MCI discrimination, but machine learning added little over regression. This is an exploratory triage aid requiring external validation.

papers.title: Distributed Artificial Intelligence for Agentic Intent-Based Networking in Mobile Networks
papers.authors: Iacovos I. Ioannou, Susanne Naegele-Jackson, Sonja Filiposka, Vincent Burkard, Michael Georgiades, Michael Mackay, Vasos Vassiliou
papers.abstract: Through intent-based networking (IBN), network objectives are specified declaratively, yet in mobile networks their realisation spans administrative domains that compete for coupled radio, transport and compute resources but cannot share local models and telemetry. A distributed artificial intelligence (DAI) controller with a Belief-Desire-Intention-eXecution (BDIX) cycle is presented, centred on shared-space coordination. The local decision of each domain agent is mapped through Gi into a common p-dimensional resource space, so that only resource contributions and a common price vector cross domains, after a minimum-slack feasibility certificate and behind a trust-admission gate. Typed refinement, deficit feedback and conflict mediation support it. In a coordination-layer benchmark (4 to 64 domains, twenty seeds), the full-information objective is matched to the reported numerical precision without disclosure of local models (cost gap 0.00%), whereas, at the principal β=0.60 setting, aggregate-only allocation loses 2.27% to 3.83% and equal split loses 25.21% to 37.67%. When 12.50% to 25.00% of the domains understate their contributions fivefold, honest-domain cost rises by 24.48% to 50.95% without the gate and by at most 2.26% with it, while mild falsification is not reliably detected by the trust gate, leaving containment dependent on the delegated resource bounds. On the single-domain analytical plant (twenty hold-out seeds), the controller attains the joint-highest displayed score (0.80), the lowest mean latency and significantly higher scores than seven of eleven comparators; end-to-end workflow execution is demonstrated separately by bridge dry runs. Shared-space coordination is thus the allocation of choice where local models cannot be shared.

papers.title: Digital Dependency and Academic Identity Among Postgraduate Students in the Era of Generative AI
papers.authors: Mona Saleh Alwazzan
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has become embedded in everyday university life, often faster than institutional guidance has developed. This qualitative hermeneutic phenomenological study examined how postgraduate students experienced the boundary between generative-AI assistance and digital dependency, and how these experiences related to academic identity. In-depth, semi-structured interviews were conducted with eleven postgraduate students (five males and six females) at a public university in Saudi Arabia, selected through maximum-variation purposive sampling. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and returned to participants for verification. Analysis followed Van Manen’s holistic, selective, and detailed approaches to phenomenological reflection. Two themes captured the experience: negotiating the boundary of digital dependency, and academic identity between agency and dependence. Rather than locating dependency in frequency of use, participants located it in the recurring transfer of substantive ideation, judgment, and authorship to the tool. Verification and the ability to explain and defend the final work helped preserve epistemic agency, whereas time pressure sometimes shifted practice toward substitution. Within this sample, strategic use as a coach, critic, or organizer supported confidence and skill development; extensive delegation was associated in participants’ accounts with diminished ownership, guilt, and concealment-oriented assessment practices. The findings offer a provisional, sample-grounded account of digital dependency and suggest that perceived ambiguity in institutional expectations may make concealment more salient, without establishing a causal relationship.

papers.title: Generative-AI/LLM-Enabled E-Assessment in Higher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research Trends, Collaboration Networks, and Thematic Evolution
papers.authors: Hayat Elyacoubi, El Mustapha Baytar, Nadia Saqri, Lynda Ouchaouka
papers.abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on generative-AI/LLM-enabled e-assessment in higher education, drawing on 243 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2023 and 2026 and indexed in the Scopus database. Employing VOSviewer and Bibliometrix software tools, the analysis integrates performance metrics and science mapping techniques. The findings reveal rapid growth, with annual publications increasing from 4 in 2023 to 117 by July 2026 (H-index = 35; 3854 total citations). China leads scientific production (39 articles), while Assessment and Evaluation in Higher Education is the most prolific journal (14 articles). The most cited study addresses LLM-generated feedback effectiveness (494 citations). VOSviewer keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies four thematic clusters: (1) generative AI and feedback processes, (2) health-professions education and methodological designs, (3) AI in education and pedagogical systems, and (4) large language models and automated assessment. The co-authorship network reveals a dispersed collaboration structure with 28.0% international co-authorship. Thematic evolution analysis reveals a shift from foundational explorations of AI viability toward specialized applications in feedback literacy and self-regulated learning. Several research gaps are tentatively identified as hypotheses for future verification, including the underrepresentation of developing countries, limited attention to ethical dimensions, and a scarcity of longitudinal studies.

papers.title: Impact of Data Quality on School Enrollment Forecasting for Brazil’s National Textbook Program (PNLD)
papers.authors: Victor André Lopes Brasileiro, Marcelo Palmeira Falcão, Breno Duarte, Romildo dos Santos Escarpini Filho, Luciano Cabral, Dalgoberto Miquilino Pinho Júnior, Laisa Gomes de Sousa José, Rafael de Amorim Silva, Nicholas Joseph Tavares da Cruz, Lenardo Chaves e Silva, Bruno Almeida Pimentel
papers.journal: International Conference on Time Series and Forecasting (ITISE)
papers.abstract: Ensuring the availability of didactic materials within Brazil’s National Textbook Program (PNLD) depends on reliable school enrollment forecasts. However, administrative time series often exhibit limited historical coverage and heterogeneous stability, which can constrain predictive accuracy. This study investigates the impact of data quality on forecasting performance using Brazilian School Census enrollment records from 2007 to 2023. We stratify school–stage series into three data-quality regimes defined from the available records, based on historical availability (number of observed years) and stability (coefficient of variation (CV)): Light (at least 4 years; CV up to 1.0), Medium (at least 5 years; CV up to 0.5), and Rigorous (at least 8 years; CV up to 0.3). We adopt a one-step-ahead protocol ( h = 1 ) evaluated on two horizons: a pre-pandemic forecast targeting 2019 (training through 2018) and a post-onset forecast targeting 2020 (training through 2019), the latter potentially affected by the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil. We evaluate 14 predictive models spanning classical statistical methods, machine learning algorithms, and fuzzy time series (FTS) architectures, using mean absolute error (MAE) as the primary metric. Results show that regime-driven effects are consistent across both horizons: moving from the Light to the Rigorous regime reduces MAE by approximately 30% for 2020 and 32% for 2019, while the best-to-worst model spread within a single regime is at most 4.6 points. This gain, however, comes at a substantial coverage cost—the eligible dataset shrinks from 77,315 to 8677 series (11.2%). Under the highest-quality regime, FTS models show robust performance, with SeasonalFTS achieving the best MAE across both horizons (13.00 for 2019; 12.39 for 2020). To our knowledge, this is the first large-scale empirical quantification of the coverage–precision trade-off induced by data-quality stratification in administrative enrollment forecasting. The findings support quality-aware forecasting strategies for PNLD planning.

papers.title: Longitudinal Changes in Insomnia, Sleep Continuity, and Sleep Timing During Residential Treatment for Eating Disorders: A Six-Month Observational Study
papers.authors: Francesco Monaco, Annarita Vignapiano, Stefania Landi, Ernesta Panarello, Raffaele Malvone, Alessandra Marenna, Chiara D’Alessandro, Nicoletta Faiella, Alessia Collura, Luca Steardo, Gennaro Sosto, Giulio Corrivetti
papers.abstract: Background: Sleep disturbances are a clinically relevant and transdiagnostic dimension of eating disorders (EDs), particularly during adolescence and young adulthood. Although early improvements in insomnia severity during residential treatment have been described, the longitudinal trajectory of sleep disturbances, habitual sleep timing, and eating disorder psychopathology across a six-month residential stay has not been systematically characterised. Methods: This prospective real-world observational study enrolled 30 female adolescents and young adults (aged 14–22 years) in a small exploratory cohort, predominantly with anorexia nervosa (AN; 83.3%) and a minority with bulimia nervosa (BN; 16.7%), all with clinically significant insomnia at admission (Insomnia Severity Index [ISI] > 14). All sleep outcomes were based on subjective self-report; no objective sleep assessment (actigraphy or polysomnography) was available. Participants were consecutively recruited from the Regional Residential Centre for Eating Disorders “Mariconda”, ASL Salerno, Italy. Of 38 consecutive admissions assessed for eligibility, 8 were excluded (ISI ≤ 14 at admission: n = 5; incomplete baseline data: n = 3), yielding a final enrolled sample of n = 30. All 30 participants completed the six-month residential programme; no drop-outs occurred. ISI was assessed monthly (T0–T6); PSQI and EDE-Q were assessed at T0, T3, and T6; diary-derived sleep timing (sleep midpoint) was assessed monthly (T0–T6), while diary-derived sleep continuity parameters (SOL, WASO, TST, SE%) were available at T0, T1, T3, and T6. Linear mixed-effects models (LMM) and bootstrap-resampled paired analyses were used. Results: ISI declined progressively from 21.1 ± 2.5 at baseline to 7.4 ± 2.7 at month 6 (Δ = −13.7; 95% CI [−14.4, −13.1]; p < 0.001). By month 6, 56.7% of participants had achieved remission (ISI < 8) and 100% had met response criteria (ΔISI ≤ −8). Sleep midpoint advanced progressively by 86 min over six months (from ~04:41 to ~03:16 after midnight), with no significant association with BMI or pharmacological treatment in linear mixed-effects models. EDE-Q global scores decreased from 4.57 ± 0.49 to 2.06 ± 0.58. Changes in ISI were not correlated with changes in EDE-Q at month 3 (r = 0.042, p = 0.826) but were significantly correlated at month 6 (r = 0.480, p = 0.007). All pharmacological regimens remained stable throughout the six-month observation period. The association between improvement in insomnia severity and eating-disorder psychopathology was not evident at month 3 but emerged at month 6, suggesting that these domains may change at different rates during residential treatment. Given the exploratory nature of the analyses, p-values are reported without adjustment for multiple comparisons and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Conclusions: Across six months of residential treatment, progressive improvements were observed in insomnia severity, subjective sleep continuity, habitual sleep timing, BMI, and eating-disorder psychopathology. In the absence of a control group, spontaneous remission, regression to the mean, and non-specific components of care, including the routinely administered Passiflora incarnata L. adjunct, cannot be individually distinguished as contributors to the observed changes, and these findings should be interpreted within the constraints of an uncontrolled observational design relying on subjective sleep measures. Controlled studies are needed to determine whether these changes are directly attributable to treatment or primarily reflect concurrent weight restoration and clinical improvement.

papers.title: Beyond BMI: The Clinical Relevance of Sarcopenia and Muscle Quality in Gynecologic Oncology from Meta-Analyses to Practice—The Potential Role of Body Composition Assessment, Including BIA, in Supportive Care
papers.authors: Beata Pięta, Karolina Gajewska, Małgorzata Mikołajczyk, Michalina Wiśniewska, Alicja Rzymska, Bartłomiej Burzyński, Paweł Rzymski
papers.abstract: Sarcopenia, low muscle mass, and low muscle radiodensity are increasingly being considered factors associated with treatment outcomes in patients with gynecological malignancies. Despite the growing body of evidence, body composition assessment is not routinely incorporated into clinical practice. The aim of this review was to present current evidence on the associations of muscle parameters with survival, complications, systemic treatment toxicity, and quality of life, as well as to discuss the opportunities and limitations of computed tomography (CT) and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) in body composition monitoring. A narrative literature review was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases, primarily covering publications from 2019 to 2026, together with earlier studies relevant to the topic. Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and selected observational, longitudinal, and interventional studies were included. The available evidence indicates that low muscle mass and low muscle radiodensity are primarily associated with poorer overall survival and an increased risk of selected postoperative complications. Evidence regarding progression-free survival, disease recurrence, chemotherapy toxicity, and quality of life remains less consistent. Low muscle mass may occur independently of body weight and body mass index (BMI); therefore, routine anthropometric assessment may fail to identify adverse changes in body composition. CT image analysis enables quantitative assessment of muscle mass and evaluation of muscle radiodensity, whereas BIA may serve as a complementary tool for repeated body composition monitoring. However, its use is limited by the effects of hydration status, edema, and ascites, as well as by the lack of validated cut-off values for patients with gynecological malignancies. Body composition assessment should be interpreted in conjunction with evaluations of muscle strength, physical performance, nutritional status, treatment toxicity, and quality of life. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether body composition monitoring and the implementation of targeted supportive care improve treatment tolerance and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence into Architectural Education: An Online Model Proposal for Instructor Training for Studio Courses
papers.authors: Fatma Kaya Orhon, Kamil Çekerol, Serap Uğur
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is driving a fundamental paradigm shift in architectural design, transitioning from deterministic drafting to algorithmic curation. While the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) sector rapidly adopts these tools, academic curricula face a critical "Techno-Instructional Void." This gap risks inducing a "Zero Order Thinking State" (ZOTS)—a cognitive passivity rooted in Cognitive Load Theory, where students uncritically accept unbuildable machine hallu-cinations. Developed through comprehensive preliminary consultations with academ-ic colleagues and longitudinal studio observations, this study introduces the "Twin Houses" methodology and the "Technical Sealing" protocol. By enforcing "Cognitive Friction," the framework compels students to validate probabilistic GenAI outputs against deterministic physical laws (e.g., Blondel's Formula 2R + T = 63 cm) and safety norms. Crucially, Building Information Modeling (BIM) acts as an automated Proof-Assistant, utilizing visual programming APIs (Revit Dynamo, Allplan Python-Parts) and IFC 4.3 data schemas for rigorous Rule-Based Checking (RBC). To confirm cross-border transferability and optimize the time-costs of curriculum integration via an asynchronous AI-TPACK module, the framework is currently undergoing verifica-tion interviews with a bilateral expert panel (n=8) from Germany and Türkiye. Ulti-mately, this framework provides a structured pedagogical approach, equipping in-structors to guide students in transforming machine hallucinations into legally builda-ble, tectonic realities. Sample videos showcasing student works are available in the Supplementary Materials.

papers.title: Uncanny Valley in Conversation? Effects of Internal and External Human-Likeness on Intimacy and Trust
papers.authors: Jungwoo Jang, Jae-gil Lee, Hayeon Song
papers.abstract: Conversational agents built on large language models increasingly converse like humans, expressing emotions and disclosing their own experiences. Human-likeness, however, has been studied largely as a matter of appearance—how human an agent looks. Language now also lets an agent display internal human-likeness by conveying an inner life, raising the question of how deeply an AI should express its own experiences—and whether that depends on its appearance. In a 2 (appearance: machine-like vs. human-like) × 3 (self-disclosure: none vs. low vs. high) between-subjects experiment, 193 university students completed a single, brief, fully scripted counseling session with an AI counselor prototype and evaluated it on six measures, controlling for prior mind perception. The effects of disclosure depth depended on appearance: with the machine-like counselor, intimacy and social presence peaked at low and declined at high disclosure, with trust and perceived authenticity showing the same direction—an uncanny valley-like pattern—whereas with the human-like counselor evaluations generally rose with depth. Deeper disclosure was not judged more inappropriate, and moderated mediation analyses showed that deepening disclosure from low to high reduced anthropomorphism—and, through it, intimacy and trust—only for the machine-like counselor. Internal and external human-likeness were read together: how deeply an AI should speak about itself cannot be decided apart from how it looks.

papers.title: Beyond Creativity Scores: Exploring PRE–POST Differences in Teachers’ Semantic Networks After SCIP Training
papers.authors: Edith Haim, Kurt Haim, Wolfgang Aschauer, Giulio Rossetti, Massimo Stella
papers.abstract: Teacher creativity plays a central role in fostering creative learning environments. However, most evaluations of creativity training focus on performance outcomes and self-report measures rather than changes in underlying cognitive organisation. We investigated whether an eight-month certified teacher-training course based on the Scientific Creativity in Practice (SCIP) framework was associated with changes in Austrian secondary teachers’ creative performance, semantic organisation, and professional mindsets. Seventeen teachers completed pre- and post-training assessments, including the Alternative Uses Task, Verbal Fluency, Word-Sentence-Construction, Behavioural Forma Mentis associations with valence ratings, and written reflections. We assessed originality in the AUT with two independent AI-based systems. Semantic and affective changes were modelled through cognitive networks, mindset streams, and measures of emotional framing. At POST, teachers had higher AUT originality scores and generated largely different concepts than at PRE. They produced broader conceptual repertoires and larger semantic networks, although other structural changes differed across tasks. Affective changes were more modest. Positive valence predominated at both measurement points and became slightly more common, while negative valence declined. Separate PRE and POST mindset streams showed substantial pathway turnover but remained predominantly positive. These findings suggest that creativity training may support changes in how teachers organise and connect professional knowledge, and does not only impact how creatively they perform. Furthermore, our findings show that cognitive network analyses can complement traditional creativity assessments by revealing changes in semantic organisation and professional mindsets that remain invisible in performance scores alone.

papers.title: Toward Culturalized Generative AI for the Creative and Cultural Industries: Lessons from Adaptive Cultural Mediation
papers.authors: Martín López-Nores, Angeliki Antoniou, Menna Maged Kamel, Ahmed Dahroug, Ioanna Lykourentzou
papers.abstract: This paper argues that today’s mainstream generative AI models do not yet provide the level of culturalization required in the creative and cultural industries (CCIs). Debates on generative AI in cultural domains have focused primarily on productivity, innovation, intellectual property, labor disruption and bias. While these concerns are important, they do not fully capture a more basic issue: cultural production depends on forms of meaning that are historically situated, socially mediated and unevenly distributed across languages, communities and markets. In such contexts, fluency, safety and technical usefulness are not sufficient measures of system quality. The paper discusses how an existing line of thought from localization, cross-cultural design and culturalization research should be carried into the era of generative AI as explicit attention to cultural context, symbolic meaning and interpretive plurality. The CCIs provide a particularly revealing testbed for this claim because they expose the limits of generic AI systems in domains where value depends on tone, memory, symbolism and representation. To ground the argument, the article revisits earlier work on targeted narratives, personalization and adaptive cultural mediation across museums, heritage sites and pilgrimage routes, and uses recent exploratory attempts with widely used generative AI models to show what remains missing. On that basis, the article proposes a framework for culturalized generative AI and outlines an integrated research and governance agenda spanning AI, the humanities and cultural-sector practice.

papers.title: How well do large language models answer postoperative lumbar fusion questions? A blinded comparative analysis of accuracy, quality, readability, and safety-related content
papers.authors: Ahmet Kürşat Kara, Ozan Işık
papers.abstract: Background Patients recovering from lumbar fusion increasingly seek guidance from large language model (LLM) chatbots when their surgeon is unavailable, but the accuracy, completeness, and safety-related content of such responses have not been compared across models for the postoperative period. Objective To compare the accuracy, quality, safety-related content, and readability of responses from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude to frequently asked postoperative lumbar fusion questions, and to identify the question types for which responses are weakest. Methods Thirty questions, compiled by three neurosurgeons and grouped into six clinical categories, were submitted to each model, each with a standardized, patient-oriented prompt requesting warning signs. Ninety anonymized, randomized responses were rated independently by three blinded neurosurgeons for accuracy and four quality subdomains (clarity, completeness, relevance, and patient safety) on 4-point scales. Readability (Flesch–Kincaid, Flesch Reading Ease, and Gunning Fog), word count, and responses meeting an operational screening criterion for potential harm were also assessed. Models were compared with Friedman and Holm-corrected pairwise tests. Results Accuracy was high for all models without significant differences. Quality, clarity, completeness, relevance, and patient safety differed globally, but effect sizes were small (Kendall's W : 0.10–0.21) and, after correction across the six outcome families, only quality and completeness remained significant, with Gemini scoring lower than ChatGPT and Claude. Gemini had the most favorable readability. ChatGPT responses were the shortest (mean 294 vs. 462 and 445 words); length was unrelated to completeness or readability. Two Gemini responses (6.7%) and none from ChatGPT or Claude met a post hoc operational screening criterion for potential harm (a score of ≤2 on accuracy or patient safety from at least one of three raters, without concurrence from the other two); no response was adjudicated as actually harmful. In exploratory question- and category-level analyses, responses tended to be rated highest for standardized questions and lowest for those requiring individualized judgment or interpretation of wound-related symptoms. Conclusion Responses from contemporary LLMs to common postoperative lumbar fusion questions were generally rated as accurate, with small between-model differences and a model-level divergence between readability and completeness. Because safety-related content was explicitly prompted and no patient outcomes were assessed, these findings describe the quality of safety-related information rather than clinical safety. LLMs may support postoperative patient education but should not replace physician guidance, particularly for warning signs and patient-specific recovery decisions.

papers.title: How to express social presence: a comparison of perceptions of social robots’ cognitive abilities
papers.authors: Thomas Sievers, Nele Rußwinkel
papers.abstract: In light of the problems posed by an aging society and the associated challenges-particularly regarding the care and support of older citizens-questions arise concerning technological solutions. Social robots equipped with appropriate cognitive abilities can provide support in this area by reducing loneliness and social isolation through communication and personalized interaction. To this end, the robot's perceived social presence is of crucial importance. Social presence (or co-presence) refers to the sense of being with another person and depends on how easily one feels able to access that person's intelligence, intentions, and sensory impressions. This study examined the potential of robots' cognitive abilities for social dialogic interactions with humans, such as (i) unrestricted conversational abilities, (ii) the incorporation of visual cues into interactions, and (iii) memories of individual encounters, and investigates the perceived social presence in each case. In addition, we evaluated the degree of anthropomorphism using the Human-Robot Interaction Evaluation Scale. Our results show a trend toward a higher degree of social presence in terms of visual perception, but only one statistically significant difference out of a total of seven questions on this topic. Memories, as well, had only one statistically significant influence, namely, on the anthropomorphic dimension of disturbance. Gender-specific differences were observed with regard to social presence and the anthropomorphic dimensions. However, these differences are most likely attributable to professional background or certain predispositions rather than to gender itself.

papers.title: Large-scale conversational data auditability via cryptographic commitments and hash-chained audit-ledger verification
papers.authors: Iván Ortiz-Garcés, Pablo Palacios, Washington Loza, William Eduardo Villegas-Ch
papers.abstract: The auditability of large language model-based systems requires verifiable evidence without exposing the sensitive content of interactions. This article proposes a hash-chained audit-ledger framework to transform public LLM conversations into canonical off-chain units, generate cryptographic commitments using SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-256, build a lightweight ledger with Merkle roots, and verify integrity against induced tampering. The study integrates three heterogeneous sources, LMSYS-Chat-1M, WildChat, and Chatbot Arena, and produces 3,971,887 auditable units. In the full-corpus HMAC-SHA-256 experiment, the 11,899.55 MiB normalized repository was represented by 1,473.44 MiB of hash-only audit records, 2.03 MiB of ledger block headers, and 380.52 MiB for the operational ledger plus membership structures required for record-level verification. Five induced tampering categories, Merkle and decision-hash integrity, hash-chain linkage integrity, block ordering integrity, membership completeness, and dataset-membership consistency, were detected without false acceptance; a separate clean-ledger baseline validated the untampered ledger with zero error signals. Load experiments showed near-linear growth of mean total pipeline time with respect to the number of audit records. Operational ledger-stage throughput increased across the intermediate workloads but declined at the largest evaluated load, while full record-set verification throughput remained comparatively stable up to 250,000 interactions before decreasing in the 500,000-interaction scenario. This contribution demonstrates that the traceability of decisions generated by LLM can be formulated as a measurable, private, and cryptographically verifiable experimental chain. The framework provides a documented numerical-audit basis for independent consistency assessment, regulatory compliance, and forensic analysis when ledger states are evaluated against preserved artifacts, trusted checkpoints, or externally anchored commitments.

papers.title: From community diagnosis to policy dialogue: co-creating childhood obesity prevention strategies in rural and urban Portugal
papers.authors: Tânia Gaspar, Maria Rosa Nóbrega, Fábio Botelho Guedes, Ana Cerqueira, Leonor Quelhas Pinto, Miguel Telo de Arriaga
papers.abstract: Introduction: Promoting healthy lifestyles from early childhood is central to balanced development and the prevention of health problems throughout life. The European HEALTH4EUKids project examines a participatory process of community diagnosis, co-creation into local policies for child health promotion and childhood obesity prevention in two Portuguese territories with distinct rural and urban profiles. Methods: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted within a mixed-methods action-research framework. The study provides an exploratory assessment of children's wellbeing indicators and contextual differences, without permitting causal inference. Participants included 202 primary-school pupils (mean age = 7.43 ± 1.14 years) and 54 community adults (mean age = 48.76 ± 11.51 years), alongside stakeholders from health, community, and local decision-making sectors. Data included a questionnaire adapted from the 2022 Health Behavior in School-aged Children (HBSC) protocol, KIDSCREEN-10, the Living Healthy Tool (LHT) which was translated and culturally adapted for the Portuguese context, satisfaction questionnaires and focus groups. LHT-student version was administered exclusively in Alter do Chão. Quantitative and qualitative data were analyzed using SPSS v.28.0 and thematic analysis supported by MAXQDA. Results: Descriptive analyses indicated that 57% of pupils reported irritability or bad mood and 46.7% reported nervousness, while quality of life and sleep were generally favorably rated. Regarding nutritional status, 66% had age-adjusted BMI within the reference range, whereas 36% reported not engaging in regular physical activity. Frequent screen use and exposure to violence during leisure time were also identified as concerns. Community LHT responses indicated differences between municipalities in perceptions of school meals, safety, and access to public services. Focus groups highlighted priorities concerning physical activity, school food environments, and coordination between schools, families, and the community. Conclusions: The findings indicate context-specific strengths and areas for further attention in child health and wellbeing. Quality of life, sleep patterns, and certain family health practices were generally favorable. Conversely, challenges were identified regarding physical activity, screen time, and psychological symptoms, as well as less favorable assessments of school meal quality, community safety, access to services, and opportunities for active leisure.

papers.title: AI technostress and professional identity among Chinese university teachers: the mediating role of teaching self-efficacy and the moderating role of perceived organizational support
papers.authors: Youming Yang
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has entered university teaching faster than the evidence needed to guide its use, and teachers carry much of the resulting strain. This study examined whether AI technostress is associated with the professional identity of university teachers through teaching self-efficacy, and whether perceived organizational support buffers this pathway. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted with a convenience sample of 486 full-time teachers from five public universities in Guangxi, China, all of whom had used at least one generative AI tool in their teaching or course preparation. Respondents completed Chinese adaptations of established measures of AI technostress, teaching self-efficacy, professional identity, and perceived organizational support. The measurement properties of the adapted scales were verified with confirmatory factor analysis and competing-model comparisons, and the hypotheses were tested with a moderated mediation path analysis based on 5,000 bootstrap resamples. AI technostress was negatively associated with professional identity, and teaching self-efficacy partially accounted for this association. Perceived organizational support moderated the first link of the pathway: the negative association between AI technostress and teaching self-efficacy was weaker among teachers who perceived stronger institutional backing, and the indirect association with professional identity was correspondingly smaller. These findings suggest that teachers' professional identity is vulnerable to technology-related strain and that institutional support may attenuate this vulnerability. Universities that invest in efficacy-oriented professional development and visible organizational support are better positioned to help teachers sustain their professional identity as generative AI becomes embedded in teaching.

papers.title: AI feedback-seeking and learning engagement in art education: psychological antecedents and reflective mechanisms
papers.authors: Tianbi Hu, Guangyao Li
papers.abstract: Introduction: Generative artificial intelligence provides students with a feedback source that differs from traditional teacher and peer interaction, yet limited research has explained why students actively seek feedback from AI or how such feedback-seeking is associated with subsequent learning engagement. Drawing on transactional stress and coping theory and social cognitive theory, this study examined the psychological antecedents and reflective mechanisms of AI feedback-seeking in art education. Methods: Two complementary studies were conducted. Study 1 utilized survey data from 315 higher education students with recent experience in art learning and generative AI use to investigate whether a fear of negative evaluation was associated with AI feedback-seeking through interpersonal help-seeking avoidance. Study 2 involved 172 students who completed a standardized AI-supported art-creation task. It examined whether AI feedback-seeking was associated with task behavioral engagement through reflective learning and whether openness strengthened this indirect relationship. The proposed relationships were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Results: In Study 1, fear of negative evaluation was positively associated with interpersonal help-seeking avoidance, which in turn was associated with greater AI feedback-seeking. The indirect association between fear of negative evaluation and AI feedback-seeking through interpersonal help-seeking avoidance was significant, whereas the direct association was not. In Study 2, AI feedback-seeking was positively associated with reflective learning, which was further associated with task behavioral engagement. Reflective learning significantly mediated the association between AI feedback-seeking and task behavioral engagement. Openness strengthened both the association between AI feedback-seeking and reflective learning and the corresponding indirect association with task behavioral engagement. Discussion: The findings indicate that avoiding interpersonal help does not necessarily reflect withdrawal from feedback. Under evaluation concerns, students may instead select AI as a feedback source involving less interpersonal exposure. However, seeking AI feedback is not uniformly associated with stronger learning engagement; its relevance depends on whether students reflect on the information obtained and remain receptive to alternative perspectives. The study positions AI feedback-seeking as both a coping-oriented form of feedback-source selection and a learner-initiated resource for reflective engagement in art education.

papers.title: Does learning burnout link physical exercise and problematic short-video use? Evidence from a three-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel model and supplementary machine-learning analysis among Chinese high school students
papers.authors: Tian Yin, Yanfeng Peng, Longjiang Chen, Zetian Wang, Xu Liu, Changcheng Xie, Zeng Gao
papers.abstract: Background Problematic short-video use has become a growing behavioral health concern among adolescents, yet its longitudinal links with physical exercise and learning burnout remain insufficiently understood. This study examined the within-person bidirectional associations among physical exercise, learning burnout, and problematic short-video use, tested whether learning burnout served as a longitudinal pathway linking physical exercise to later problematic short-video use, and explored the predictive value of these variables for subsequent problematic short-video use. Methods A three-wave longitudinal survey with 6-month intervals was conducted among 1,327 students aged 16–18 years from five high schools in Yunnan Province, China. Physical exercise, learning burnout, and problematic short-video use were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale-3 (PARS-3), the Adolescent Student Burnout Inventory, and the Short-Video Addiction Scale. Random-intercept cross-lagged panel modeling was used to separate stable between-person differences from within-person fluctuations while controlling for demographic and educational covariates. The longitudinal indirect association was estimated using 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap samples. Supplementary ridge regression and extreme gradient boosting models, using nested cross-validation and a holdout test set, examined the incremental predictive value of physical exercise and learning burnout for later problematic short-video use. Results At the between-person level, higher long-term physical exercise was associated with lower learning burnout and problematic short-video use, whereas higher learning burnout was associated with higher problematic short-video use. At the within-person level, higher-than-usual physical exercise predicted lower subsequent learning burnout and problematic short-video use. Learning burnout and problematic short-video use showed positive reciprocal associations over time, and both predicted lower subsequent physical exercise. The longitudinal indirect association from physical exercise to later problematic short-video use through learning burnout was statistically significant but small. In supplementary machine-learning analyses, the best holdout R 2 was 0.311, but adding physical exercise and learning burnout did not improve prediction beyond prior problematic short-video use. SHAP results from the extended XGBoost model were therefore interpreted as exploratory feature attributions. Conclusion Physical exercise, learning burnout, and problematic short-video use showed interconnected longitudinal associations among Chinese high school students. Learning burnout may represent one small longitudinal indirect pathway linking physical exercise to later problematic short-video use, while recent problematic short-video use provides the most informative signal for future risk. These findings may inform the development and evaluation of school-based health-promotion strategies that support physical exercise, address learning burnout, and respond to recent problematic-use symptoms.

papers.title: Comparing researcher-curated AI-drafted feedback styles for negative automatic thought believability: an online randomized scenario-based experiment
papers.authors: Yu Liu, Junting Mu, Ying Li, Yingzi Ke, Yingge Zhang
papers.abstract: Introduction: AI-drafted feedback is increasingly used in learning support, emotional support, peer support, and self-guided reflection, yet empirical studies often combine emotional validation, advice, reappraisal, and Socratic questioning within the same response. This study compared four researcher-curated AI-drafted feedback styles: neutral information, empathetic feedback, Socratic challenge, and integrated feedback. Methods: An online randomized scenario-based experiment was conducted using four daily stress scenarios crossed with the four feedback conditions. After screening 427 questionnaire records collected from March 12 to March 20, 2026, valid responses from 389 adults were analyzed. Participants read one scenario, rated negative automatic thought (NAT) believability and negative affect, received one feedback text, completed post-test and feedback evaluation measures, and wrote a balanced alternative thought. Regression models controlled for pre-test scores, scenario, trait NAT tendency, AI trust, and trait reactance. Results: All three active feedback styles predicted lower post-test NAT believability than neutral information, with the largest adjusted difference observed for integrated feedback, followed by Socratic challenge and empathetic feedback. Empathetic feedback produced higher perceived empathy and greater affect reduction, whereas Socratic challenge produced higher cognitive reappraisal and reframing quality. Integrated feedback combined high feedback acceptance with strong evidence-based examination of the negative thought. Discussion: In this scenario-based task, researcher-curated AI-drafted feedback produced larger reductions in NAT believability and higher evidence-based reframing quality when emotional validation was followed by evidence testing, alternative explanation, and fact-inference distinction.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence in jazz improvisation: an Actor-Network Theory perspective
papers.authors: Chenge Gao
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) plays an increasingly significant role in the artistic creation process. In the domain of highly interactive human-machine composition, GAI is no longer a passive tool but exhibits a certain degree of agency. Based on Actor-Network Theory (ANT), a social science theoretical framework proposed by French sociologist Bruno Latour and other scholars, GAI can be viewed as a non-human subject endowed with the status of an actor. In jazz improvisation, a representative creative activity, the agency of GAI is manifested in the generation of its specific musical works, presenting a contrast to human creation. Furthermore, this process reveals the leading and constraining factors in the actions of GAI, as well as the potential pathways and mutual interactions of its future co-creative development with humans.

papers.title: Association between discretionary screen time and depressive symptoms in Chinese adolescents: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Zhi Xu, Shuye Yang, Shibin Wang, Xing Wang
papers.abstract: Background: Adolescents globally exhibit growing engagement with discretionary screen time, but its association with depressive symptoms remains unclear in developing economies. Objective: To examine the relationship between discretionary screen time and depressive symptoms among Chinese adolescents. Methods: = 1,025). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the validated CESD-9, with a cutoff score of ≥10. The primary analysis was a multilevel logistic regression model with random intercepts for school and class, adjusted for all measured covariates except BMI, anxiety and insomnia; a model additionally adjusted for BMI, anxiety and insomnia served as a sensitivity analysis. Subgroup analyses evaluated potential effect modification. Results: -interaction >0.05). Conclusion: Prolonged discretionary screen time is significantly associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms among Chinese adolescents, indicating a graded association that strengthens with increasing screen time. These findings are relevant to public-health monitoring of discretionary screen use in adolescents.

papers.title: Predictors of body appreciation in mothers of children living with ASD: the role of physical activity, self-compassion, and emotional eating
papers.authors: Marina Reuter Pierote, Isabela Pereira Rocon, Gabriela Grillo da Silva, Fabíola Lacerda Pires Soares
papers.abstract: Introduction: Mothers of children living with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) often experience high levels of emotional overload, which can negatively impact their eating behaviors and body image. In this context, body appreciation-a key facet of positive body image-serves as an important protective factor. However, evidence regarding the determinants of body appreciation among caregivers of children with ASD remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the sociodemographic, clinical, lifestyle, and psychological factors associated with body appreciation in mothers of children living with ASD. Materials and methods: This cross-sectional study evaluated 143 mothers of children with ASD residing in Espírito Santo, Brazil. Data were collected online through self-administered questionnaires assessing sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, nutritional status, lifestyle habits, self-compassion, emotional eating, and body appreciation. Multiple linear regression analysis was conducted using Jeffreys's Amazing Statistics Program (JASP, version 0.18.0) to identify predictors of body appreciation. Results: < 0.001) were inversely associated with body appreciation. Discussion: Self-compassion and physical activity emerged as key positive correlates of body appreciation, whereas elevated BMI and emotional eating were identified as negative predictors in this population. Given the cross-sectional design, longitudinal studies across diverse geographical settings are needed to confirm causality and support generalizability. Identifying these predictors provides actionable insights for designing targeted interventions aimed at promoting positive body image and mitigating dysfunctional eating behaviors in mothers of children with ASD.

papers.title: Multimodal assessment of NIBS-induced adaptive plasticity in aging prefrontal networks: ERP and cognitive evidence
papers.authors: Davide Crivelli, Michela Balconi
papers.abstract: Non-invasive brain stimulation may enhance age-sensitive executive functions by modulating task-engaged prefrontal networks, but behavioral effects remain heterogeneous and their physiological specificity is poorly understood. This pre-post study examined neuropsychological and electrophysiological responses to cognitive training paired with active or sham transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Thirty-three older adults were randomly assigned to active tDCS plus cognitive training, sham tDCS plus cognitive training, or wait-list control. Training groups completed 24 sessions across 8 weeks. Before and after intervention, participants underwent neuropsychological assessment and EEG recording during a Stroop-like task; N2 amplitude and latency were extracted at F3, Fz, and F4. Linear mixed-effects models tested Group × Time effects. Significant interactions emerged for non-verbal executive functions and associative fluency, with improvements confined to the active-tDCS group. Other cognitive measures improved over time without group-specific effects. Active tDCS selectively increased N2 amplitude in correspondence to the stimulated site, whereas no comparable change occurred after sham stimulation or in controls. These findings suggest that repeated right-prefrontal tDCS may specifically support higher-order executive functions and induce selective modulation near the stimulation site. Physiological measures may help clarify the anatomical and functional specificity of NIBS-related modulation.

papers.title: Eye-movement-based machine learning for identifying Parkinson’s disease dementia in a retrospective cohort: an interpretable model-development study
papers.authors: Jing Wu, Qing Liu, Song Yang, 张宇清, Yuanlu Shu, Junwen Wang, Min Wu, Tian Tian
papers.abstract: Background: Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD) is a major non-motor complication of Parkinson's disease (PD), but conventional cognitive screening is influenced by education, language, motor impairment, fatigue, and testing conditions. We developed and interpreted machine-learning models using eye-movement and demographic features to identify PDD among patients with PD. Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, 486 patients were screened between December 2024 and February 2025. After exclusions, 297 patients with idiopathic PD were analyzed, including 84 without dementia and 213 with PDD. Thirteen machine-learning algorithms were trained using demographic and task-derived eye-movement variables. Performance was assessed using ROC AUC, PR AUC, classification metrics, calibration, the Brier score, and decision-curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the final model. Results: Patients with PDD showed poorer cognitive performance and abnormalities in antisaccade inhibition, saccade execution, and fixation stability. Seven predictors were retained: age, sex, education level, antisaccade accuracy, mean overlap-saccade completion duration, mean gap-saccade velocity, and lateral-gaze deviation duration >4°. Logistic regression and elastic net achieved the highest test-set ROC AUCs (both 0.962), while logistic regression had the lowest Brier score (0.077). A radial basis function support vector machine (SVM) was retained as the primary classifier for detailed evaluation because it provided balanced performance across threshold-dependent metrics and could capture potentially nonlinear relationships and interactions. In the test set, the SVM achieved a ROC AUC of 0.947 and PR AUC of 0.979. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score were 0.867, 0.870, 0.857, and 0.904, respectively. SHAP identified education, antisaccade accuracy, mean overlap-saccade completion duration, mean gap-saccade velocity, and lateral-gaze deviation duration >4° as the leading contributors. Conclusion: A seven-feature model combining demographic and eye-movement measures showed promising internal discrimination of PDD from PD without dementia. Eye-movement-based machine learning may complement clinical cognitive assessment, but external validation in larger and more representative cohorts is required before clinical use.

papers.title: Reconfiguring graphic design education for generative AI in higher education: a human-agency and adaptive-curriculum framework
papers.authors: Khaled Mostafa Ahmed Mohamed
papers.abstract: Introduction Generative AI creates a curriculum-transformation problem by redistributing activities through which disciplinary expertise is learned, practised, demonstrated, and assessed. This study examines that problem within graphic design education as a bounded empirical case. Methods A survey of 270 participants was analysed using exploratory factor analysis ( N = 265 complete cases), and semi-structured interviews with 12 design academics and practitioners were analysed using a frozen rule-based codebook across 650 meaning units. The quantitative and qualitative strands were analysed independently and integrated through a joint display. Results The quantitative analysis yielded a broad, sample-specific Transformative–Normative response orientation and a narrower Curricular Diagnostic Critique cluster; neither is interpreted as a validated latent construct. The final qualitative dataset contained 504 normative/transformative units (77.5%), 35 diagnostic units (5.4%), and 111 units retained as X0 (17.1%). Both the N-family and D-family occurred in all 12 interviews. Discussion The integrated interpretation informed the Bot-Haus Curriculum Architecture, which organises human creative agency, experiential human–AI practice, adaptive curriculum, critical and ethical governance, foundational design principles, and educational outcomes. The architecture is presented as an empirically informed, theory-guided design proposition developed from the graphic design case, not as a validated causal model. Transfer to other practice-based disciplines remains a proposition for future empirical testing.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in university physics education: a systematic review of empirical studies
papers.authors: Zhanara MALİKOVA, Bayan Saparbekovna Ualikhanova, Torebai Abdrakhmanovich Turmambekov, Bakytgali Rakhashev, Dauletbay Berdaliyev
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into higher education, yet empirical evidence on its pedagogical use in university physics remains fragmented. This systematic review synthesized empirical research on the applications, reported learning and pedagogical outcomes, methodological quality, challenges, and educational implications of AI-supported university physics education. We used six search sources: SpringerLink, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and ERIC. The searches in the five original sources were updated through September 2026, and ERIC was added as an additional search source. Eligibility criteria were defined using the PICOS framework, study selection followed PRISMA 2020, and methodological quality was appraised using the 2018 Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Eleven empirical studies met the inclusion criteria and were synthesized narratively. Across the included studies, AI was used for tutoring and explanations, formative feedback and scaffolding, collaborative problem solving, simulation and modeling, instructional design, and developing AI literacy. Reported outcomes were mixed and context-dependent. Some studies identified favorable short-term or task-specific outcomes related to feedback, learning performance, simulation-based activities, and AI-related competencies, whereas others reported limitations in transfer to independent performance, the pedagogical quality of AI-generated materials, and students’ ability to recognize scientifically inaccurate AI-generated responses. Cross-study patterns suggested that instructional structure, alignment between AI-supported activities and learning tasks, students’ disciplinary knowledge, and opportunities to critically evaluate AI outputs shaped the educational use of AI. The current evidence does not support a general conclusion that AI is uniformly effective in university physics education. Rather, its educational value appears to depend on how AI is integrated into learning activities and on the extent to which students and instructors retain responsibility for reasoning, evaluation, and pedagogical decision-making. Given the small and heterogeneous evidence base, larger longitudinal and multi-institutional studies are needed to examine the durability and transferability of reported outcomes.

papers.title: Traditional and modern education systems in Ayurveda education: a critical integrative review
papers.authors: Sangeeta Singh, Dr. Bhawani Singh, Radhika Bhattrai -, Chandra Shekhar Pandey
papers.abstract: The evolution of Āyurveda education reflects a shift from an ancient, philosophically grounded educational model to a contemporary, institutionalized, competency-based one. Historically, Āyurveda was transmitted through the Gurukul system, a personalized, residential pedagogical model combining textual study with hands-on clinical training, emphasizing moral discipline ( Dharma ) and the Guru-Śiṣya Paramparā (teacher-disciple lineage). Learning was structured around the Trividha Jñānopāya (three-fold means of knowledge) and the cognitive sequence of Śravaṇa (listening), Manana (reflection), and Nididhyāsana (internalization). Colonial administrative frameworks and subsequent modernization transitioned Āyurveda education into a structured, time-bound, standardized university system. Today, under the governance of the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and guided by the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, Āyurveda education employs Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME), integrating digital technologies, Simulation-Based Learning (SBL), and objective assessment tools such as the Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE). This modernization has increased scalability, standardization, and interdisciplinary integration, but has also introduced challenges including faculty shortages, infrastructural constraints, and epistemological tension between traditional and biomedical frameworks. This integrative review critically examines the historical trajectory, pedagogical shifts, and comparative methodologies of traditional and modern Āyurveda education, giving balanced weight to the strengths and limitations of each system. It further examines the current landscape of technological integration, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Virtual Reality (VR) in anatomical and clinical training, with attention to validation, cost, and governance barriers, and identifies systemic barriers to reform. Finally, the review proposes policy, curricular, and research-oriented recommendations toward a critically synthesized model of Āyurveda education.

papers.title: Strategic leadership for agentic AI in education: a conceptual framework with reference to the United Arab Emirates
papers.authors: Tamra Alshloul, Hosam R. I. Badawy, Hesham R. I. Badawy, Khawla M. Hassan Almaazmi, Maram Al Hasan, Shaikha Alzaabi
papers.abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) shifts educational leadership from whether to adopt a tool to which actions a configured system may take, under whose authority, and with what capacity for intervention and remedy. Through critical integrative synthesis of educational leadership, organisational decision-making, AI governance, and agentic-AI scholarship, this Conceptual Analysis develops educational agentic alignment: a relational judgement about whether delegated machine authority fits educational purposes, human decision rights, professional capabilities, safeguards, pedagogy, and public-value obligations. The focal unit is a dated and versioned educational delegation arrangement. The framework separates agentic capability, use-related exposure, and usable governance capacity; organises leadership decisions through seven domains across four levels; and proposes three mechanisms concerning safeguard shortfall, responsibility–capacity mismatch, and evidence-linked realignment. Each proposition specifies the analytical unit, variables, expected direction, measurable outcomes, time order, moderators, rivals, and evidence that would count against it. Official evidence from the United Arab Emirates illustrates contextual boundaries without implying national implementation or framework validation. The contribution is an education-specific explanation of fit and misfit in human–machine authority, together with a practical basis for bounded decisions and comparative research.

papers.title: Factors associated with Chinese vocational college students’ intention to use generative artificial intelligence for learning: an extended UTAUT mode
papers.authors: Dong Cao, Yikun Peng, Xue Yang, Biyin Chen, Zhiyuan Chen, Qiankun Sun
papers.abstract: This study focuses on examining the factors influencing Chinese vocational college students’ behavioral intention to use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for learning and further analyzing the relationships between these factors and changes in GenAI behavioral Intention. Based on the Unified Theory of behavioral Intention and Use of Technology (UTAUT), an extended model incorporating anxiety (ANX) was developed, and a two-stage analytical approach combining structural equation modeling (SEM) and ordered Probit (OProbit) regression was adopted. In the first stage, SEM was employed to examine the effects of various factors on behavioral intention within the extended UTAUT model. In the second stage, an OProbit model was applied, with changes in GenAI behavioral Intention specified as an ordinal outcome variable, to further examine the relationships between the relevant factors and changes in behavioral Intention while controlling for individual characteristics, including gender, grade level, and prior AI usage experience. The results indicate that effort expectancy (EE), social influence (SI), and facilitating conditions (FC) are significantly and positively associated with vocational college students’ behavioral intention to use GenAI for learning, whereas ANX is significantly and negatively associated with behavioral intention. In addition, GenAI behavioral Intention varies to some extent across student groups with different genders, grade levels, and levels of AI usage experience. This study provides empirical evidence for the application of GenAI in vocational education and offers practical implications for optimizing GenAI-based teaching and adoption strategies, enhancing students’ engagement in learning, and improving the quality of talent development in vocational education.

papers.title: An artificial intelligence-driven concept-aligned framework for adaptive multilingual verbal communication learning
papers.authors: Ashik Kumar, Neil A Vivo
papers.journal: International Journal of Computing and Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: This paper proposes CAMVCF-AI, an artificial intelligence-driven extension of the Concept-Aligned Multilingual Verbal Communication Framework. The system treats communicative meaning as a language-independent intermediate representation and maps that representation to language-specific spoken realizations. Instead of organizing beginner learning primarily by isolated vocabulary lists or sequential grammar chapters, CAMVCF-AI represents an utterance through intent, semantic slots, discourse context, target language, register, and learner state. The proposed application combines a semantic concept graph, multilingual embeddings, a controlled language-realization layer, automatic speech recognition, pronunciation and fluency assessment, learner modeling, adaptive exercise selection, retrieval scheduling, and text-to-speech. Six structurally diverse languages—Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Spanish, Mandarin Chinese, and Arabic—are used as the initial test bed. A mathematical formulation is introduced for concept representation, cross-lingual semantic alignment, response scoring, mastery estimation, and adaptive task selection. The paper specifies an implementable software architecture and a research protocol for evaluating semantic accuracy, transfer to unseen sentences, response latency, pronunciation, retention, and user learning efficiency. No empirical superiority claim is made because participant data have not yet been collected. CAMVCF-AI is presented as a buildable AI research system whose central hypothesis is that concept-aligned, adaptive, speech-centered practice can support efficient access to practical multilingual communication while preserving language-specific grammar and pragmatics.

papers.title: Vivoz OpenMovie: A structured generative AI framework for consistent character, voice, and cinematic scene production
papers.authors: Ashik Kumar
papers.journal: International Journal of Computing and Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has made it possible to create high-quality images, voices, music, and short video clips from textual and multimodal instructions. However, movie production requires continuity across many independently generated assets. A character must remain recognizable across scenes; costumes, locations, voices, camera language, and narrative state must persist; and corrections should not destroy elements that are already acceptable. This paper presents Vivoz OpenMovie, a structured generative AI framework for consistent character, voice, location, scene, and cinematic shot production. The framework transforms a screenplay into persistent production assets including Character Sheets, Location Sheets, Voice Sheets, Scene Specifications, Shot Specifications, reference images, structured cinematic prompts, generated shots, consistency evaluations, and versioned corrections. A composite multimodal consistency formulation is introduced to represent character, location, voice, costume, motion, camera, and narrative consistency. A targeted regeneration loop is further defined to preserve approved properties while correcting identified defects. An illustrative case study demonstrates how the framework can be evaluated without claiming unperformed empirical results. The proposed architecture is model-independent and is intended to provide a reproducible bridge between creative filmmaking intent and rapidly changing generative AI models.

papers.title: Vivoz OpenMovie-Agent: An agentic generative AI framework for autonomous movie production using planning, persistent memory, multimodal consistency, and human-in-the-loop control
papers.authors: Ashik Kumar
papers.journal: International Journal of Computing and Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can create images, voices, music, and short video clips, yet movie production remains a long-horizon coordination problem. A production must preserve character identity, location state, costume, voice, narrative dependencies, camera intent, object continuity, and approval decisions across many independently generated assets. This paper presents Vivoz OpenMovie-Agent, an agentic generative AI framework that operates a structured movie-production workflow through planning, persistent multimodal memory, tool and model orchestration, consistency evaluation, targeted correction, and human-governed approval. The framework extends structured cinematic production from a manually coordinated sequence into a goal-directed control process. The agent decomposes production goals into scene- and shot-level tasks, retrieves canonical production state, selects appropriate generative or analytical tools, evaluates candidate outputs against explicit continuity constraints, and chooses whether to accept, correct, regenerate, escalate, or request human intervention. A persistent memory architecture separates immutable identity anchors from evolving narrative state and episodic production history. A multimodal evaluator preserves component-level consistency scores so that correction policies can act locally rather than indiscriminately regenerating successful content. The paper formalizes the agent state, action space, planning objective, memory retrieval, approval policy, and correction loop, and proposes an experimental design for evaluating autonomy, consistency, correction efficiency, human workload, and controllability. The contribution is an architecture for human-governed autonomous movie production rather than a claim that unrestricted autonomy should replace creative direction.

papers.title: From artificial intelligence to synthetic intelligence: A mathematical and physical framework for human–AI collaboration
papers.authors: Neil A Vivo • Ashik Kumar, Ashik Kumar
papers.journal: International Journal of Computing and Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence has progressed from task-specific machine-learning systems to multimodal foundation models and agentic systems capable of planning, retrieval, tool use, and iterative action. Yet current systems remain vulnerable to hallucination, incomplete context, distribution shift, opaque internal representations, error propagation, and failures that require human correction. This paper proposes Synthetic Intelligence (SI) as a human-centered intelligence framework created through structured interaction among artificial intelligence, human judgment and creativity, persistent memory, agentic reasoning, computational tools, environmental feedback, and uncertainty-aware control. SI is not presented as machine consciousness or as a replacement for human cognition; intelligence is modeled at the level of the coupled human–machine system. A mathematical formulation is introduced using state-space modeling, collaboration gain, information theory, calibration, feedback stability, and energy-aware computation. Physics-inspired concepts including entropy, dynamical stability, information processing, and computational energy are used as analytical tools without proposing a new physical law of intelligence. The paper also specifies a prototype application and controlled evaluation framework comparing Human Only, AI Only, conventional Human+AI, and Synthetic Intelligence conditions. A data-quality benchmark is proposed as an initial reproducible test bed. Finally, the Transdimensional Nexus is presented only as a future cross-domain extension in which SI can act as the reasoning engine connecting informational, perceptual, cognitive, simulated, and physical domains.

papers.title: Digitization and digital preservation of Ayurvedic manuscripts: Challenges and new trends
papers.authors: Savita Assistant Librarian
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Academic Studies
papers.abstract: The Ayurvedic manuscripts comprise an incredibly rich treasure trove of traditional knowledge concerning medicine, pharmaceutics, medicinal plants, surgery, preventive health care, and the holistic approach to well-being of humans. A vast amount of this information is stored in highly fragile manuscripts which are subject to deterioration as a result of aging, climatic conditions, improper handling, biological degradation, and inaccessibility. Digitization and digital preservation can be considered an essential way to preserve such unique and valuable cultural and scientific heritage for the future generations. The current paper discusses the importance, approaches, challenges, and new trends in the area of Ayurvedic manuscripts' digitization and digital preservation. In order to preserve physical manuscripts by transferring them into a digital format, one needs to perform scanning, digital photography, image processing, metadata creation, and storage. Nonetheless, there are quite a few challenges that should be taken into consideration during this process. Recent innovations in Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), online storage libraries, high-resolution imaging, and connected digital archives have opened up avenues for automation in transcription, classification, indexing, translation, and knowledge retrieval. Combination of the conventional Ayurvedic studies along with contemporary technological advancements could help in achieving better preservation, accessibility, research collaborations, and educational uses of manuscript library collections. This paper focuses on the requirement of established digitization standards, sustainability of digital libraries, cross-disciplinary collaboration, trained manpower, and ethical considerations to guarantee the authenticity and security of the digitized Ayurvedic knowledge for future generations. Therefore, digital preservation can prove extremely valuable for documenting and disseminating India’s traditional medicine heritage worldwide.

papers.title: Implementation of human-centered artificial intelligence practices of school leaders and students’ academic empowerment in a teachers’ college in Inner Mongolia
papers.authors: Suzhen Li
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Science and Education Research
papers.abstract: This study examined the implementation of human-centered artificial intelligence practices of school leaders and students’ academic empowerment in a teachers’ college in Inner Mongolia. It employed a quantitative, descriptive-comparative, and correlational research design involving 356 teacher-respondents and 374 student-respondents. The teacher-respondents assessed human-centered artificial intelligence practices in terms of adaptive governance, alignment, augmentation design, classroom oversight, trust and redress, workflow fit, capacity building, ethics stewardship, evidence-driven adoption, and purpose communication. Meanwhile, the student-respondents assessed academic empowerment in terms of self-directed learning and metacognitive regulation, well-being and sustained engagement, mentoring and caring climate, data agency and transparency, academic integrity and reasoning, and inclusive participation and community. Findings showed that human-centered artificial intelligence practices were generally assessed as practiced, with an overall mean of 2.94. Among the subconstructs, augmentation design obtained the highest mean of 3.05, suggesting that teachers perceived artificial intelligence as a tool that supports rather than replaces human judgment. Capacity building received the lowest mean of 2.82, indicating the need for more sustained training, clearer documentation, and stronger peer support. Students’ academic empowerment was likewise assessed as favorable, with an overall mean of 3.01. Academic integrity and reasoning ranked highest, with a mean of 3.12, while data agency and transparency ranked lowest, with a mean of 2.89. This suggests that students were more confident in academic standards and reasoning than in understanding how learning data and automated recommendations affect them. Difference tests revealed that teachers’ assessment did not significantly vary by age or overall academic rank, although ethics stewardship differed significantly by academic rank. Prior artificial intelligence training significantly differentiated teachers’ overall assessment and selected areas such as workflow fit, evidence-driven adoption, and purpose communication. For students, sex and residence did not significantly affect overall academic empowerment, while age produced a significant difference only in data agency and transparency. Correlation analysis showed no significant overall relationship between human-centered artificial intelligence practices and academic empowerment, r = 0.071, p = 0.180, although selected weak but significant relationships appeared in specific subconstructs. Based on the findings, a strategic action plan was proposed to strengthen faculty capacity building, workflow fit, evidence-driven adoption, data transparency, ethical governance, inclusive participation, and student-facing academic support.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence in English language teaching: Pedagogical value, challenges, and practical pathways
papers.authors: Yu Zhang, 陈红林
papers.journal: International Journal of Humanities and Education Research
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence, exemplified by tools such as ChatGPT, is reshaping English language teaching by expanding the ways in which instruction is designed, learning is supported, and assessment is conducted. For teachers, GenAI can assist with lesson planning, material development, task design, and feedback; for learners, it can provide conversational practice, personalized support, language revision, and immediate responses. These affordances extend the conventional teacher-student-textbook triad toward a more interactive instructional model in which AI becomes an additional participant in teaching and learning. At the same time, the pedagogical use of GenAI raises concerns about the authenticity of learning, academic integrity, the reliability of feedback, cultural bias, overreliance on technology, and uneven benefits across learners. Without appropriate guidance, students may bypass essential processes of language production, critical evaluation, and autonomous learning. This article examines the pedagogical value and major challenges of GenAI in English language teaching and outlines practical pathways for its responsible integration. It argues that effective implementation requires sustained teacher guidance, active learner agency, the development of human-AI interaction competence and critical AI literacy, a deliberate balance between AI-assisted and non-AI-assisted activities, and stronger process-based assessment, academic integrity, privacy protection, and ethical governance.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in filmmaking: Creativity, authorship and audience trust
papers.authors: Swarn Suman
papers.journal: International Journal of Humanities and Education Research
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence can help filmmakers explore ideas, organise material and create images that would otherwise be difficult to produce. It also raises questions about who deserves credit, whose work supports the technology and what audiences should know. This article examines these questions through a critical discussion of research, industry documents and selected production examples. It separates tools that assist human work from tools that generate expressive material or reproduce a person’s appearance and voice.
