The central argument is that creative value depends on more than speed or visual quality. It also depends on meaningful human decisions, fair treatment of workers and a clear account of how the material was made. AI can support filmmaking, but its use does not automatically make a film original, economical or trustworthy. The article proposes that disclosure should explain significant uses in language the audience can understand. It also discusses the importance of local knowledge in Indian cinema, where language, cultural detail and performance need careful attention. These are interpretive and ethical arguments, rather than findings from an audience survey.

papers.title: The self-efficacy–SEL nexus in digital teacher education: A structural model of pre-service teachers’ readiness for future classrooms
papers.authors: Deisy Kushwaha, Jyoti Dwivedi
papers.journal: International Journal of Humanities and Education Research
papers.abstract: The explosion of digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and technology-enabled learning spaces is changing the skill set demanded of future educators. In this critical review, literature on teacher self-efficacy, social-emotional learning (SEL), Digital Teacher Training, and preparation of future classroom teachers is reviewed. Systematic or structured review methodology is utilized to analyze peer-reviewed articles identified through various major academic databases, such as Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and Google Scholar, using a predetermined review protocol. The focus of this review is on articles related to self-efficacy, SEL competencies, digital competency, technological readiness, flexibility, and future-ready teaching by pre-service teachers. In this synthesis, the links between psychological confidence, socio-emotional skills, digital skills, and preparedness to respond to emergent needs in the classroom environment are examined. While individual studies address specific aspects, broader literature lacks theoretical integration, leaving the intersections among psychological, socio-emotional, and digital factors largely unexamined. To fill this gap, the current research presents an integrative conceptual framework describing the ways in which self-efficacy and socio-emotional learning might together impact preparedness of pre-service teachers in a digitally advanced and AI-based classroom setting.

papers.title: Bridging the digital divide in mathematics education: Digital access, AI literacy and equitable opportunities for mathematical learning
papers.authors: Neeraj Kumar
papers.journal: International Journal of Humanities and Education Research
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new possibilities for mathematics education while simultaneously generating new forms of educational inequality. Digital platforms, mathematical software, intelligent tutoring systems and generative AI can support visualisation, feedback, personalised learning, mathematical exploration and problem solving. However, the educational benefits of these technologies are not distributed equally. The digital divide has therefore moved beyond differences in access to devices and internet connectivity towards differences in digital competencies, quality of technology use, AI literacy, teacher support and the ability to convert digital resources into meaningful learning opportunities. This conceptual paper examines this changing nature of the digital divide in mathematics education and explores the relationship among digital access, digital literacy, AI literacy and pedagogically meaningful technology use. The paper argues that digital access is a necessary but insufficient condition for digital equity. Particular attention is given to AI literacy as an emerging dimension of digital inequality, as learners increasingly encounter AI-generated mathematical explanations, solutions and feedback. Based on a conceptual synthesis of relevant literature, the paper proposes an Equitable Digital Mathematics Learning Framework (EDMLF). The framework connects meaningful digital access, digital and mathematical technology literacy, AI literacy and learner-centred technology use with equitable opportunities for mathematical learning, while positioning teacher support and pedagogical guidance as cross-cutting conditions. The paper contributes a mathematics-specific perspective to discussions of digital equity and suggests directions for future empirical research, particularly concerning rural–urban differences, socioeconomic inequalities, AI literacy, teacher mediation and mathematical reasoning.

papers.title: Determinants of utility perception of MahaVISTAAR-AI mobile app among the user farmers
papers.authors: JJ Mamdi, Pravin Sharadchandra Kapse, Rajesh Prabhatrao Kadam, PR Deshmukh, Dheeraj T Pathrikar
papers.journal: International Journal of Agriculture and Food Science
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence-enabled mobile advisory platforms are increasingly being deployed to bridge the information gap faced by farmers in accessing timely and reliable agricultural knowledge. The present study was undertaken to examine the utility perception of the MahaVISTAAR-AI mobile app among its user farmers and to identify the profile characteristics that determine this perception. The study was conducted in Nanded district of the Marathwada region of Maharashtra. Two tehsils, namely Loha and Ardhapur, were randomly selected from the district and six villages were randomly drawn from each tehsil, thus covering twelve villages. From each selected village, ten users of the MahaVISTAAR-AI app were randomly chosen, constituting a total sample of 120 respondents. The study followed an ex-post-facto research design and data were gathered through a structured interview schedule. Pearson's coefficient of correlation was used to study the relationship between the profile characteristics of the users and their utility perception of the app. The findings revealed that annual income, extension contact, innovativeness, internet connectivity and techno-savviness of the respondents had a positive and highly significant relationship with utility perception, while education, land holding and source of information showed a positive and significant relationship. Age showed negative and non-significant relationship, whereas family size and social participation showed a positive but non-significant relationship with utility perception. The study suggests that strengthening farmers' techno-savviness, extension linkages and access to information sources can substantially enhance the utility they derive from AI-based mobile advisory applications.

papers.title: Role of artificial intelligence in digital marketing in agriculture
papers.authors: Devika Mehrotra
papers.journal: International Journal of Agriculture Extension and Social Development
papers.abstract: Agriculture is undergoing a digital transformation driven by artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, big data analytics, the Internet of Things, and digital communication technologies. Conventional agricultural marketing can be constrained by fragmented markets, information asymmetry, limited buyer access, and communication barriers. AI-enabled tools can support demand analysis, customer segmentation, content generation, multilingual communication, product recommendations, and automated customer support. In India, where agricultural systems and language preferences are highly diverse, these technologies may help improve the reach and relevance of agricultural information and marketing services. Adi Vaani, an AI-powered tribal-language translation initiative, provides a useful example of how language technology may contribute to more inclusive communication, although it is not itself an agricultural marketing platform. This review examines AI applications in agricultural digital marketing, potential benefits for farmers and rural enterprises, challenges related to infrastructure, data quality, privacy and translation accuracy, and future directions for responsible adoption. AI should complement rather than replace agricultural expertise, local knowledge, and human oversight. Its value should ultimately be assessed through measurable improvements in access to information, market participation, communication quality, and producer outcomes.

papers.title: Factors influencing investors’ adoption of AI-based investment tools
papers.authors: Mohan Prakash. K, Sureshrajan. SG
papers.journal: International Journal of Financial Management and Economics
papers.abstract: This study describes and finds out to the Factors Influencing Investors’ Adoption of AI-Based Investment Tools, Here the research identified the AI-Based Investment Tools are ‘AI investment tools enable investors to analyse large volumes of financial and market data rapidly and efficiently’ (AIIT-1), ‘AI investment tools support consistent and data-driven investment decision-making while reducing the influence of emotional biases’ (AIIT-2), ‘AI investment tools provide personalised investment recommendations based on investors’ financial goals, risk tolerance, and individual needs’ (AIIT-3), ‘AI investment tools assist investors in identifying potential investment risks and developing well-diversified portfolios’ (AIIT-4), ‘AI investment tools facilitate the identification of market trends and patterns for forecasting potential investment opportunities’ (AIIT-5), ‘The convenience, accessibility, continuous availability, and potential cost-effectiveness of AI investment tools enhance their attractiveness to investors’ (AIIT-6), ‘Investors are more likely to trust AI-generated investment recommendations when the system provides clear and understandable explanations for its recommendations’ (AIIT-7) and ‘Investors have greater confidence in AI-assisted investment decisions when qualified financial professionals can review or override AI-generated recommendations’ (AIIT-8). In the study to finds out Factors Influencing Investors’ Adoption of AI-Based Investment Tools through the Factor Analysis.

papers.title: Innovations in Teaching; the Implementation of ICT in the Teaching of Scientific and Artistic Subjects and their Impact on the Personalization of Learning
papers.authors: Radoslav Karásek, Anna Vlčeková, Mária Strenáčiková
papers.journal: European Journal of Teaching and Education
papers.abstract: In modern education, the information and communication technologies are having an increasing impact on personalized learning. Their implementation responds to the digital transformation in our society and requires the development of digital literacy as a key competence of both teachers and students. In Mathematics, Physics, Music and Art education, individualizing learning is supported by selected tools such as GeoGebra, Corinth 3D, Musescore, Solfy or graphic editors (GIMP, Procreate, Adobe Fresco). They enable adaptive and personalized forms of learning, support visualization, creativity, and self-directed learning. Although artificial intelligence presents challenges related to overreliance, academic integrity, and the development of critical and creative thinking, Information and communication technologies (ICT) and Artificial Intelligencie (AI) technologies can enhance education by supporting visualization, collaboration, creativity, differentiated instruction, and personalized learning.

papers.title: Teachers' Navigation of Assessing Written Work in Times of Generative AI
papers.authors: Karin Stolpe, Marit Deubler Holmlund
papers.journal: European Journal of Teaching and Education
papers.abstract: Teachers’ assessment practices are changing as generative artificial intelligence (genAI) becomes embedded in students’ schoolwork. While existing research has highlighted teachers’ concerns about AI use in written assignments, assessment practices have received limited analytical attention. This exploratory qualitative study investigates how teachers reason about assessment practices in genAI-rich contexts and examines the adequacy of the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework for understanding these practices. Drawing on survey responses and interviews from licensed Swedish secondary school teachers, the reflexive thematic analysis reveals that assessment emerges as the central practice through which teachers renegotiate what counts as knowledge and how assessment judgements can be legitimised. Teachers describe assessment as epistemically uncertain and reliant on professional judgement, while also raising concerns about equity and legal certainty. The study suggests that assessment constitutes an integrative dimension of teachers’ professional knowledge and proposes extending TPACK to include an explicit assessment dimension (TPACK-A).

papers.title: Understanding Learner Engagement and Persistence in AI-Assisted Interactive Climate Fiction Learning
papers.authors: Charlotte Briggs
papers.journal: European Journal of Teaching and Education
papers.abstract: Advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled educators to create increasingly sophisticated interactive learning materials, yet relatively little research has examined how learners engage with and persist in such interventions over time. This exploratory case study investigated learner engagement and persistence within a five-stage AI-assisted interactive climate fiction (cli-fi) intervention delivered through H5P activities embedded within the Moodle learning management system as part of an extracurricular sustainability initiative at an English-medium university in China. Participation, activity scores, completion data, and time-on-task measures were analysed descriptively across a five-week intervention. While learners who engaged with the intervention demonstrated high levels of engagement, reflected in strong activity scores and substantial interaction with the materials, participation declined markedly across successive stages, falling from 25 learners in Story 1 to six learners by Story 5. Descriptive improvements were observed in environmental knowledge scores among the small number of learners completing both pre- and post-tests, although these findings were inconclusive. The findings highlight a clear distinction between engagement and persistence, suggesting that engaging digital learning experiences do not necessarily translate into sustained participation. The study contributes to emerging research on AI-assisted learning design by emphasising the importance of considering persistence as a distinct outcome when designing and evaluating multi-stage digital learning environments.

papers.title: The Role of Big Data and AI In Capital Market Based Accounting
papers.authors: Masradin Masradin, Syamsuddin Syamsuddin, Neks Triani, Syarifuddin Rasyid, Sahrir Sahrir
papers.abstract: This study used a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to examine the role and use of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in capital market-based accounting and identify factors influencing the effectiveness of their implementation. The study followed the PRISMA 2020 protocol. From 437 records obtained through eight keyword combinations in the Scopus database, 29 studies were selected after filtering based on the 2016–2026 publication period, Q1–Q4 journal quality, and thematic relevance. The study grouped the literature into four main aspects: data infrastructure, analytical processing, disclosure and reporting, and governance and assurance. These four aspects were then integrated into the AI-Accounting Value Chain and Governance Loop (AVC-GL) model. The findings indicate that Big Data expands information sources for accounting and capital market analysis, while AI helps process complex data and supports decision-making. However, the effectiveness of its implementation is highly dependent on data quality, governance, professional oversight, and human ability to evaluate technological outcomes. The use of generative AI also improves the efficiency of corporate disclosures, but introduces new risks, including greenwashing. This study contributes through the development of a functional taxonomy and AVC-GL model to explain the relationship between technology, governance, information quality, and decision-making in capital markets.

papers.title: Peningkatan Kompetensi Guru melalui Pelatihan Pemanfaatan Canva AI Code dalam Pengembangan Media Pembelajaran Interaktif di SMA Darul Hijrah Putri
papers.authors: Rusma Yulidawati Rusma, Rusma Yulidawati Rusma, Sri Hartini Astuti
papers.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has brought significant impacts and new opportunities for teachers in designing more creative and interactive learning. (Aryanti & Anwar, 2025) Canva AI Code is Canva's newest feature that allows users to create simple programming-based designs with the help of AI. This training activity aims to improve teachers' digital literacy competencies through training and mentoring in the use of AI-based Canva Code. The activity's implementation method included preparation, training, mentoring, and evaluation. Participants were 43 teachers from Darul Hijrah Puteri Martapura High School. The activity used a participatory approach through demonstrations, hands-on discussions, and reflection. Observations showed a shift in teachers' attitudes from pessimism about coding to enthusiasm after understanding that the programming process is assisted by AI and ChatGPT features. Most participants successfully created interactive learning using AI-based Canva Code with attractive and applicable designs. This activity demonstrates that integrating AI in digital training can improve technological literacy and teachers' confidence in developing interactive learning

papers.title: AI Adoption in Supply Chain Management among Lebanese Food and Beverage SMEs: Drivers, Barriers, and Strategic Implications
papers.journal: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
papers.abstract: This study examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Supply Chain Management (SCM) among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Lebanon's Food and Beverage (F&B) sector.Using a qualitative approach based on 45 semi-structured interviews, it explores the drivers, barriers, and strategic implications of AI adoption.Even though AI technologies offer significant opportunities, adoption remains uneven especially among SMEs.The findings reveal that participants recognize AI's potential to improve efficiency and competitiveness.Participants reported that AI enhances operational efficiency, cost optimization, and decision support.On the other hand, AI adoption remains limited by technical barriers, financial constraints, skill shortages, and low trust.Based on the Technology Organization Environment (TOE) framework, the Resource-Based View (RBV), the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and Institutional Theory, the study highlights that successful AI integration depends on several factors.These factors include technological readiness, organizational capabilities, managerial acceptance, and institutional pressures.It suggests enhancing digital infrastructure, developing human capital, and improving governance frameworks to support SMEs.

papers.title: Value Co-Destruction in a Sustainability Service System: How Greenwashing and Herding Behavior Shape Green Purchase Intention Through Green Brand Love
papers.journal: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
papers.abstract: The bottled-water sector operates as a high-frequency, low-involvement sustainability service system in which recurring service encounters rely on external quality signals rather than direct verification.In such a system, greenwashing does more than undermine brand legitimacy -it destabilizes the trust on which value co-creation depends.Although the harmful effects of greenwashing are well documented, the affective pathways and social boundary conditions through which it propagates within concentrated service ecosystems remain poorly understood.Drawing on Service-Dominant Logic (SDL), Affect-Behavior-Cognition (ABC) theory, and Social Influence Theory (SIT), this study frames greenwashing as an information-system failure that triggers value co-destruction along two routes -a direct erosion of trust and a slower, affective erosion mediated by green brand love (GBL) -and positions herding behavior (HB) as an informal governance mechanism moderating this propagation.Survey data from 315 bottled-water consumers in Surabaya, Indonesia, were analyzed using PLS-SEM.Greenwashing significantly reduced both GBL and green purchase intention (GPI), with GBL partially mediating the effect (the affective pathway accounting for roughly 39% of greenwashing's total impact on GPI).Herding behavior shaped the direct pathway: greenwashing's negative effect on GPI was pronounced when herding was low but non-significant when herding was high -indicating that social conformity masks consumer scepticism and delays market correction.These findings clarify how information failure spreads through affective and social channels in concentrated markets and inform the design of sustainable services that pair information transparency with the management of social dynamics.

papers.title: A Web-Based Multi-Modal AI Framework for Intelligent Content Moderation with Constructive Feedback
papers.authors: Marwah Zaid Mohammed Al-Helali, Naveen Palanichamy, Su-Cheng Haw, Subhashini Gopal
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Traditional content moderation systems primarily rely on punitive measures that focus on removing offending or inappropriate content without offering users any form of educational feedback or guidance. Traditional content moderation systems primarily rely on punitive measures that focus on removing offending or inappropriate content without offering users any form of educational feedback or guidance. This lack of constructive interaction often leads to a poor user experience, leaving users frustrated and uninformed regarding the reasons behind content removal. Moreover, such a system fails to encourage long-term positive behavioural changes within online communities, as users do not gain insights on how to improve their conduct. This paper proposes a new constructive Artificial Intelligence (AI) intervention system that integrates a number of AI models in order to conceptualize content moderation as a limiting process rather than an educational process. The framework suggested in the paper combines HuggingFace's BERT-based toxicity analysis, SightEngine's image processing, and Google's Gemini large language model to provide end-to-end content moderation with construction of feedback. Based on comprehensive testing through user interaction analysis and comparative analysis, the study demonstrates the effectiveness of educational intervention in content moderation. The study advances the field by developing a novel approach to content moderation that puts user education and community development first while upholding safety regulations.

papers.title: Unraveling the impact of Prolific: Exploring the presence of bias when studying psychological constructs related to the use of technology
papers.authors: Margherita Lanz, Rossella Caliciuri, Alessia Spina, Anna Ongaro, Gaia Virginia De Sanctis, Gabriella Anna Vaughn, Marta Mastroni, Martina Barbieri, Martina Milani, Angela Sorgente
papers.abstract: This study investigates potential biases in data collected through online paid platforms, specifically Prolific, compared to traditional snowball convenience sampling, when studying psychological constructs related to technology. The researchers analyzed data from a separate study examining ChatGPT adoption among Italian university students, using both Prolific and snowball sampling methods. Three technology-related constructs were examined: technology self-efficacy (SE), technology anxiety (AX), and social norms related to technology use (SN). Analysis of covariance revealed a significant difference between groups in technology self-efficacy (SE), with Prolific participants exhibiting higher scores. No significant differences were found in AX and SN. The findings highlight potential selection bias, suggesting Prolific may attract participants with higher technological confidence. It is important to stress that this difference may also reflect a combination of self-selection into the platform, the presence of financial compensation, and the inherent biases of convenience snowball samples. The study underscores the importance of considering such recruitment-related biases when generalizing research findings, particularly in technology-related studies, and emphasizes the need for transparency in reporting sampling methods.

papers.title: Geografie sperimentali negli outdoor urbani. Quattro pratiche artistiche, ludiche e co-creative
papers.authors: Cecilia Pasini, Matteo Puttilli, Giacomo Spanu
papers.abstract: This introductory paper addresses the theoretical and methodological intersections between geography and experimentation. Drawing on the debate surrounding experimental geographies, the contribution highlights the potential of experimental practices to capture complex, non-linear, and emergent socio-spatial dynamics that traditional approaches often struggle to reveal. The paper is organized into three main sections. First, it reviews the theoretical trajectories of experimental geographies, discussing key debates and tensions regarding creativity, methodological rigor, privilege, and the epistemological value of failure. Second, it examines three core dimensions of experimental approaches in urban outdoor environments: collaborative co-creation, the relational nature of outdoor spaces, and the disruptive role of arts-based and performative practices. Finally, it introduces the four contributions comprising this special issue—focusing on play, affective intimacy, urban care, and street art—while reflecting on the ethical, political, and practical challenges of experimental research, particularly regarding public engagement and the non-academic dissemination of knowledge. Ultimately, the paper posits experimentation not as a rigid set of tools, but as an open, situated, and reflexive research posture for investigating contemporary urban transformations.

papers.title: Consumer Engagement in SME-Based Circular Economy Practices: Evidence from a Plastic Upcycling Enterprise in Indonesia
papers.authors: D. W. Putra, Fahrais Zahrudy, Yulia Arisnani Widyaningsih
papers.journal: Journal of Environmental and Development Studies
papers.abstract: Circular economy practices depend not only on waste-processing technologies but also on consumer participation in sustaining material circulation and value creation. This study examines how consumers engage in circular economy practices and contribute to economic, social, and environmental value creation in Paste Lab Yogyakarta, a community-embedded plastic upcycling SME in Indonesia. Using a qualitative single-case design, the study collected data through seven semi-structured interviews with six consumer informants and one internal informant for triangulation, complemented by observation and documentation. The study analyzed the data thematically, guided by stakeholder theory and perspectives on value co-creation. The findings identify three recurring consumer roles: material contributors who supply post-consumer plastic, co-design collaborators who support product and application development, and advocates who extend sustainability narratives and stakeholder networks. These roles contribute to resource circulation, commercial opportunities, social legitimacy, and environmental value, although participation is constrained by limited consumer literacy, durability concerns, price sensitivity, and restricted design options. The study concludes that consumer engagement can support distributed value co-creation in SME-based circular economy practices by linking material recovery, application, and network diffusion within a local circular value chain.

papers.title: Implementation of artificial intelligence in islamic accounting to enhance transparency in digital financial reporting
papers.authors: Sigid Eko Pramono
papers.abstract: The implementation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed accounting practices by enabling automated data processing, anomaly detection, predictive analysis, and continuous financial monitoring. However, its application in Islamic accounting requires consideration of transparency, accountability, ethical responsibility, and Sharia compliance in digital financial reporting. This study aims to examine how AI can contribute to enhancing transparency in Islamic digital financial reporting. The study employs a library research approach using relevant books, academic journals, research articles, reports, and other scholarly sources. Data were analyzed using content analysis to identify patterns, relationships, and significant findings concerning AI, Islamic accounting, and digital financial reporting. The findings indicate that AI can strengthen financial reporting transparency through improved data accuracy, processing efficiency, anomaly detection, traceability, accessibility, and timely disclosure. Nevertheless, effective implementation requires data quality, human oversight, explainability, governance, and Sharia-based controls. The study concludes that integrating AI with Islamic accounting principles can support more transparent, accountable, and ethically responsible digital financial reporting.

papers.title: Experiencing AI Together: A Design-Based Research Approach to Collaborative Prompting in Education
papers.authors: Benedikt Brünner, Michael Nestler, Martin Ebner
papers.journal: TUGraz OPEN Library (Graz University of Technology)
papers.abstract: Slides of the presentation at ICL2026 (TH Köln, Cologne, Germany). The talk reports on a Design-Based Research study on collaborative prompting in teacher education using the platform collab.prompting.school with in-house LLM hosting. Building on the RETURN Manifesto, it explores how AI use can become observable, discussable and revisable without requiring learners to disclose their full private AI histories. Baseline surveys show that about 70% of participants were reluctant to share their entire prompt history, while they engaged productively with controlled collaborative prompting across four settings. Qualitative feedback shows that prompt revision became central, suggesting that collaborative prompting should make revision pedagogically visible rather than focusing only on final artefacts or best prompts.

papers.title: Flipped AI Literacy Classrooms: Student Motivation and Engagement in Secondary Education
papers.authors: Katja Urak, Benedikt Brünner, Gerald Franz Geier, Martin Ebner
papers.journal: TUGraz OPEN Library (Graz University of Technology)
papers.abstract: Slides of the presentation at ICL2026 (TH Köln, Cologne, Germany). The talk presents a study on how secondary school students experienced a flipped classroom design using the AI literacy platform prompting.school with regard to motivation, engagement and perceived learning. One implementation cycle with 56 students was evaluated through a post-unit questionnaire. Results indicate high interest in artificial intelligence, positive perceptions of the platform, strong task clarity and a heterogeneous but moderate motivational effect of gamification. Flipped designs for AI literacy work well when pre-class platform work and in-class activities are explicitly aligned and supported by clear tasks.

papers.title: AI-Driven Writing Assistance in a Flipped Classroom Model: A Pedagogical Approach to Enhancing Academic Writing and Critical Thinking in EFL Learners
papers.authors: Pirman Ginting, Yenni Hasnah, Adib Jasni Kharisma, Dodi Mulyadi
papers.abstract: This study explores the AI-based flipped model to enhance academic writing proficiency and critical thinking among EFL learners. Employing a mixed method through a one-group pretest-posttest design, the study combined quantitative assessment using the IELTS Academic Writing Task 2 rubric and Facione's Critical Thinking framework with qualitative data drawn from open-ended post-intervention questionnaires. Descriptive statistics showed that the students' writing skills advanced from a pre-test mean of 4.75 to a post-test mean of 6.17, which stand for an average increase of 1.42 points (29.8%). Meanwhile, critical thinking scores increased from a mean of 42.87 to 68.14 with an average increase of 25.27 points (58.9%). The Wilcoxon signed-rank test further confirmed substantial rises for both outcomes (writing: Z = -5.163, p < .001; critical thinking: Z= -5.107), with the effect sizes (writing: r = .873, rrb = 1.000; critical thinking: r = .851, rrb = .976). Qualitative findings corroborated this trend, denoting significant improvements in writing organization, argument construction, evidence-based argumentation, and source evaluation. However, challenges such as over-reliance on AI output and difficulties related to adapting to self-paced learning were also observed. Implications for pedagogical design were highlighted, implying that AI-integrated flipped learning supported the teaching of writing and critical thinking skills.

papers.title: Checkpointed Evaluation in AI-Assisted Integrated Reading-to-Write Revision: Conscious-Access Routines and No-AI Transfer
papers.authors: Hesham Abdel Karim Aldamen, Mohamad Almashour, Marwan Ali Jarrah
papers.abstract: Integrated reading-to-write (RTW) tasks in English for Academic Purposes (EAP) ask students to work carefully with sources. Writers must keep the original meaning, connect claims to evidence, and manage stance and voice when using several texts. Generative AI can make revision easier, but it may also produce wording that sounds convincing without enough evidence. This qualitative longitudinal multiple-case study examined how EFL university writers used conscious-access routines during AI-assisted revision and whether these routines later appeared in no-AI writing. Twenty-four third- and fourth-year English majors in a 16-week EAP course completed four RTW cycles. Each cycle included no-AI drafting and a 60-minute Gemini-supported revision session. Two revision conditions kept tool access and time-on-task the same. The checkpointed condition required uptake decisions, short reasons, and confidence ratings. The non-checkpointed condition allowed students to evaluate suggestions as they wished. Six data sources produced 384 coded revision episodes. The findings also showed clear differences between the two conditions. Evidence-first routines increased across cycles, while fluency-first routines decreased. No-AI milestone writing showed more evidence-first instances in the checkpointed condition at Weeks 8 and 12. Structured checkpointing may therefore help students use AI more responsibly by checking sources and evidence before accepting fluent suggestions.

papers.title: MACHINE LEARNING-BASED DETECTION OF AI-GENERATED CONTENT IN STUDENTS’ WRITTEN WORKS
papers.authors: Aigerim Sultanali, Gulnur Kazbekova
papers.journal: NEWS OF THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES OF THE REPUBLIC OF KAZAKHSTAN
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence has complicated the interpretation of authorship in educational writing and increased the need for transparent methods that distinguish machine-generated from human-written text without treating automated detection as conclusive evidence of misconduct. This study compares lexical and content-independent stylometric approaches to detecting AI-generated educational essays. The experiments used 44,868 English-language texts from the DAIGT V2 multi-source corpus, including 27,371 human-written and 17,497 AI-generated essays. The lexical representation used TF-IDF unigrams and bigrams with a Linear Support Vector Machine, while the content-independent representation consisted of fourteen structural and stylometric features classified with Logistic Regression. Human and AI texts were additionally compared using the Mann–Whitney U test and effect-size estimates. The TF-IDF model achieved 99.69% accuracy, 99.60% F1-score and 99.98% ROC-AUC on a stratified held-out test set. The stylometry-only model achieved 87.90 ± 0.40% accuracy, 84.34 ± 0.48% F1-score and 95.08 ± 0.17% ROC-AUC under five-fold stratified cross-validation. Average word length showed the strongest selected stylometric separation, while differences were also observed in text length, lexical diversity and punctuation use. The findings show that lexical information provides highly discriminative signals in the analyzed corpus, but substantial predictive information remains even when direct vocabulary is removed. The results support the use of stylometric indicators as an interpretable supplementary signal for educational text analysis, while also emphasizing that detector outputs should not be treated as definitive proof of AI use in individual student work. Robustness checks showed 99.75% accuracy after near-duplicate filtering, 96.46% accuracy for unseen prompts, and 95.39% accuracy when Llama-70B was held out, indicating measurable distribution sensitivity. The contribution is therefore a robustness-oriented comparison of established lexical and interpretable stylometric representations rather than a new classifier.

papers.title: ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES AND CONSTRAINTS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION IN KAZAKHSTAN’S RESOURCE-ORIENTED ECONOMY
papers.authors: Ravil I. Mukhamediev, Farida Abdoldina, Y. A. Gertsen
papers.journal: NEWS OF THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES OF THE REPUBLIC OF KAZAKHSTAN
papers.abstract: The article explores the economic opportunities and structural constraints of artificial intelligence adoption in Kazakhstan in a resource-oriented economy where extractive industries are a significant part and the level of high-tech diversification is relatively low. The study seeks to assess the potential macroeconomic impact of AI in several areas and to determine the conditions of its contribution to sustainable economic development. A sectoral analytical framework is used, which involves integrating information from the national accounts with AI productivity coefficients from international empirical research. It examines the main sectors of the economy, such as industry, trade, transport, energy, finance, agriculture and health, as well as the communications industry. Emphasis is placed on new technologies like machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and generative AI, which offer further automation and decision support opportunities for various sectors. Under the adopted assumptions, the model-based scenario estimate suggests that the potential economic impact of AI use in Kazakhstan may range between USD 1.6 and 2.59 billion per year, or around 0.9%–1.5% of GDP. This estimate should be interpreted as an indicative scenario-based result derived from international productivity coefficients and Kazakhstan’s sectoral GDP structure, rather than as a direct empirical measurement of the current level of AI adoption by Kazakhstani enterprises. The most substantial potential effect is concentrated in industry, trade, and transport, whereas the contribution of other sectors is more moderate but remains macroeconomically relevant. At the current stage, AI is mainly considered as a tool for efficiency improvement rather than as a driver of structural transformation. The study also highlights crucial constraints, such as a lack of digital infrastructure, human capital, research and development intensity, and reliance on resource-intensive industries. These all limit the diffusion and multiplier effects of AI technologies. It shows the need for policies that are coordinated with respect to technological modernization, education and economic diversification in order to attain the long-term benefits of AI. If left unchecked, AI can exacerbate existing structural imbalances, instead of helping to transition to a knowledge-based economy.

papers.title: RETRIEVAL BEATS FINE-TUNING: ADAPTING A KAZAKH SMALL LANGUAGE MODEL FOR HISTORICAL QUESTION ANSWERING
papers.authors: G. Askar, A. Mutaikhan, M. Aitkozhayeva, Guldana Nauryzbaikyzy, Zhanat Makhataeva
papers.journal: NEWS OF THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES OF THE REPUBLIC OF KAZAKHSTAN
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown a strong ability to solve a wide range of language tasks. However, they became less practical for subject-specific applications, especially when dealing with low-resource languages. This paper shows an example of adaptation of small language models (SLMs) to solve subject-specific language tasks in the history field. As a base model, we used the small vision language model (VLM) Qolda, developed by the Institute of Smart Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ISSAI) at Nazarbayev University. In the paper, 4 architectures are compared: 1) base model Qolda; 2) Qolda model with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) created using 48 000 instruction pairs retrieved from Wikipedia; 3) Qolda with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework based on 29 digital history textbooks with 2.25 million indexed tokens; 4) Qolda combined with both SFT and RAG. To establish whether the research findings follow the same patterns across other Kazakh language models, we apply our evaluations to two external larger baseline models: 1) KazLLM and 2) Sherkala-Chat. All architectures are evaluated on 1,081 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) from the Unified National Test (UNT) in the history of Kazakhstan and on a 500-query open-ended test set. Results show that Qolda+RAG achieves 74.93 ± 0.43% MCQ accuracy and a mean quality score of 3.34 ± 1.64. In these settings, SFT acts as a response formatter, reducing the average response length from 51.8 to 14.64 words. Qolda-SFT+RAG completes inference in roughly half the time of Qolda+RAG with comparable quality of 3.10 ± 1.42. The study findings provide a foundation for the design and development of future Kazakh-language-supported AI agents across broad application domains. The project implementation, datasets, and evaluation methodology are available on the project’s GitHub page with the corresponding Hugging Face datasets: https://github.com/IS2AI/history-qolda-ui.

papers.title: QOLDA-MATH: A SMALL VISION-LANGUAGE MODEL FOR MATHEMATICAL REASONING IN KAZAKH
papers.authors: A. Alibekov, Aspandiyar Nurimanov, A. Mukhametkali, D. Kassym, Hüseyin Atakan Varol
papers.journal: NEWS OF THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES OF THE REPUBLIC OF KAZAKHSTAN
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities. However, Kazakh language supporting VLMs capable of mathematical reasoning and being deployed on edge devices are yet to be developed. The aim of this study is to develop and evaluate a compact vision-language model that solves school-level mathematical problems in Kazakh with step-by-step reasoning and runs on consumer hardware. In this work, we present the Qolda-Math model, a 4.3-billion-parameter small VLM developed at the Institute of Smart Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ISSAI) to solve mathematical reasoning tasks in Kazakh. We use a Qolda VLM model and add an additional stage to the training pipeline. We utilize a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) algorithm that uses a dataset composed of 395,309 training examples. Specifically, the dataset spans school curriculum-aligned math problems along with chain-of-thought (CoT) solutions generated by the Qwen3-235B model. We also use general-knowledge data and prompt instructions, including “solve”, “explain”, “teach”, “verify+/verify–”, and handwritten feedback in three languages (i.e., Kazakh, Russian, and English). Under a unified evaluation protocol, Qolda-Math reaches 61.60% on the Kazakh-adapted MathVista benchmark and 50.39% on MathVision-KK, improving over the checkpoint it was fine-tuned from by 3.40 and 4.57%, respectively; both improvements are statistically significant, with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals excluding zero. In addition, the Qolda-Math model maintains competitive performance on general text and vision benchmarks (i.e., the average text benchmark score changed from 72.09 to 72.68). Qolda-Math model is deployable on consumer devices that could further support offline mathematical tutoring in Kazakh. The development of Qolda-Math builds upon advances in mathematical reasoning with language models, AI-powered educational tools, visual mathematical understanding, and Kazakh language processing. The model weights are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/issai/math_qolda.

papers.title: Developing an AI Chatbot Platform for Kasepuhan Cicarucub Cultural Literacy in a Community Reading Centre
papers.authors: DC Aryadi, Eneng Sri Susilawati, Sri Purwantiningsih, Dede Kurnia Adiputra, Suwarno
papers.abstract: The intangible cultural heritage of customary communities is at risk because its transmission depends on oral narration and embodied apprenticeship, while community reading centres seldom hold local cultural materials that young people can explore independently. This study developed an AI chatbot-based educational platform to strengthen the cultural literacy of the Kasepuhan Cicarucub community and examined its feasibility, practicality, and potential effectiveness. The research applied the ADDIE model. The analysis phase drew on field observation, interviews with the customary leader and reading-centre managers, and a user needs assessment. The product was validated by three experts in cultural content, media, and language using 30-item five-point instruments. Trials involved 43 participants across one-to-one, small-group, and field stages, followed by pretest-posttest measurement with 32 participants using a 20-item cultural literacy test. Expert validation reached 147 of 150, or 98.00 percent, on every aspect and was categorised as highly feasible, with the lowest scores concentrated on content depth, technical stability, and readability. User responses averaged 4.73, 4.83, and 4.85 across the three stages, all very good, while the weakest items concerned the visibility of the chatbot feature rather than content quality. Mean scores rose from 61.72 to 90.78, a gain of 29.06 points, with a normalised gain of 0.769 in the high category and a significant Wilcoxon test. The platform is feasible and practical for community reading centres, although the large effect size warrants caution because the design used a single group without a comparison condition.

papers.title: Traditional values as a sociocultural phenomenon: spiritual meanings and contemporary dimension
papers.authors: Зугура Ягануровна Рахматуллина
papers.abstract: The article explores the nature and variety of traditional spiritual and moral values, and their relevance in the context of the diverse Russian nation which has to respond the fundamental question of existence in the current geopolitical situation – "to be or not to be?" Should Russia be considered a significant player in global history, safeguarding its diverse population and future generations, its unique cultural identity, and its technological, cultural, and moral independence from extremism, false ideals, and "false idols" of Faustian culture? As is well known, radical civilizational transformations in the recent history of the Russian Federation, orientation towards the West and its value orientations as an "ideal type" (M. Weber) the arrangements of national life and the spiritual sphere have caused serious damage to the national socio-cultural tradition, national spirituality and morality. Today, the Russian government is building its own world based on dialogical and equal communication with others, on the priority of its own national interests and the protection of its own people and its ancestral values, which for centuries have nourished the collective multicultural life with patriotism, citizenship, genuine faith, interethnic harmony, friendship, and respect for each other. Russian traditional values are rooted in the socio-cultural biography and historical memory of ethnic groups, reflecting their ideological, spiritual, moral, aesthetic, artistic, and other ideals, ideas about goodness, truth, and beauty, principles of co-existence and co-creation, which educate and consolidate. They offer proper guidelines for ensuring a stable, guaranteed and spiritual life, and are peculiar markers of both ethnic and civil identity. The axiosphere of modern Russian society is distinctive and unique, absorbing into its space key spiritual and cultural meanings determined by the peculiarities of mentality, religious beliefs, lifestyle, historical development, natural environment, etc. The value universe is quite mobile and open to new meanings, adapts to spiritual challenges, but always protects its humanistic and ethical "core" from destruction and reinterpretation. This "core" is the key basic meanings based on vital, "fateful" norms that have been tested by time and historical cataclysms to ensure the unity, reliable present and future of society, preserve socio-cultural memory and continuity of generations. Today, in the context of numerous threats to national and spiritual security, traditional Russian values and their purposeful cultivation as a response to geopolitical challenges are one of the most effective mechanisms for countering extremist ideology, attempts to split the united Russian society, and destroy the national socio-cultural tradition.

papers.title: Navigating AI Integration in Final Project Supervision: Academic Integrity, Challenges, and Best Practices
papers.authors: Ardiyansyah Ardiyansyah, Ayu Nurkhayati
papers.abstract: Abstract: This study examines the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the thesis supervision process for students in the Islamic Communication and Broadcasting Study Program at Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin State Islamic University (UIN) Jambi. Employing a qualitative approach, the study involved in-depth interviews with 10 students who were actively completing their undergraduate theses during the 2025/2026 academic year and five thesis supervisors. The findings indicate that the integration of AI provides various benefits, including increased efficiency, more personalized guidance, and improved accessibility to academic references. Students reported that AI accelerated the thesis revision process by providing real-time feedback and recommendations for relevant literature. Meanwhile, lecturers experienced a reduced administrative workload through the automation of routine tasks, allowing them to focus more on providing guidance on conceptual and methodological aspects. The recommendations emphasize the importance of institutional policies to enhance technology training and develop digital infrastructure for academic staff and students. Thus, AI can be effectively integrated to support the thesis supervision process and help students achieve their academic potential more optimally. The main limitation of this study lies in its limited sample size, which prevents the findings from being statistically generalized. In addition, the findings reflect a specific phase of generative AI adoption that may change in response to the rapid evolution of the technology.Abstrak: Penelitian ini mengkaji penggunaan Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) dalam proses pembimbingan skripsi bagi mahasiswa Program Studi Komunikasi dan Penyiaran Islam di Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin Jambi. Dengan menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif, penelitian ini melibatkan wawancara mendalam terhadap 10 mahasiswa yang sedang aktif menyelesaikan tugas akhir pada tahun akademik 2025/2026 serta lima dosen pembimbing. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa integrasi AI memberikan berbagai manfaat, seperti peningkatan efisiensi, bimbingan yang lebih personal, dan aksesibilitas yang lebih baik terhadap referensi akademik. Mahasiswa melaporkan bahwa AI mempercepat proses revisi skripsi dengan memberikan umpan balik secara real-time dan rekomendasi literatur yang relevan. Sementara itu, dosen merasakan berkurangnya beban kerja administratif berkat otomatisasi tugas-tugas rutin, sehingga mereka dapat lebih fokus pada pemberian arahan terkait aspek konseptual dan metodologis. Rekomendasi yang diajukan menekankan pentingnya kebijakan institusional untuk meningkatkan pelatihan teknologi serta mengembangkan infrastruktur digital bagi staf akademik dan mahasiswa. Dengan demikian, AI dapat diintegrasikan secara efektif untuk mendukung proses pembimbingan skripsi dan membantu mahasiswa mencapai potensi akademik mereka secara optimal. Keterbatasan utama studi ini terletak pada cakupan sampel yang terbatas, sehingga temuan ini tidak dapat digeneralisasi secara statistik Selain itu, temuan mencerminkan fase tertentu adopsi AI generatif yang berpotensi berubah seiring laju evolusi teknologi.

papers.title: Co-creating change in agriculture and food systems: A systematic review of co-creation processes and approaches for evaluating their contributions to sustainability transformation
papers.authors: Sara Delaney, Sophia Alami, Maria Busse, Bonnie Averbuch, Fanny Boeraeve, Pauline Cassart, Valéria Csonka, Graeme Dean, Cédric Gossart, Bienvenu Kambashi, Toni Klemm, Raffaela Kozar, Elke Plaas, Azahara Isabel Seller Priego, C. Gallagher-Squires, Tiffanie Stone, Martin Hvarregaard Thorsøe
papers.abstract: Co-creation is widely proposed to address complex sustainability challenges by bringing together diverse forms of experience and expertise. Yet practical, evidence-based guidance on how co-creation processes can support sustainability transformation remains fragmented and insufficient, including for agriculture and food systems. We conducted a systematic literature review to characterize scholarly work on co-creation for environmental sustainability and to identify process insights relevant to Living Labs and related participatory initiatives. Following a four-stage screening procedure, we reviewed 5,291 articles and retained 266 studies describing multi-stakeholder, action-oriented, experimental processes; 51 agriculture- and food-focused articles were subjected to in-depth qualitative analysis. We combined bibliometric and descriptive analyses, including co-authorship network mapping, with framework-guided qualitative coding of co-creation inputs, processes, outcomes, impacts, and evaluation practices.Publications on this topic increased substantially over the past decade, but relatively few studies documented action and experimentation in sufficient methodological detail. Agriculture and food studies constituted a moderately self-contained segment of the broader literature. Across the qualitative sample, five enabling factors were most consistently associated with productive co-creation: participant alignment, institutional support, strong facilitation, inclusive participation and trust, and sufficient time for iteration. Studies also identified recurring trade-offs between diversity and alignment, resource-intensive engagement and scalability, and place specificity and transferability. Frequently reported outcomes were new knowledge, communication and networks, empowerment or efficacy, and skills. However, evidence of longer-term sustainability impacts was limited: most articles described intermediate outcomes rather than demonstrated transformation. Only sixteen articles evaluated the co-creation process itself, and participatory development of evaluation criteria was rare. Co-creation efforts can build the practical and relational capacities, and “social infrastructure” needed for sustainability transitions, but stronger methodological reporting and participatory, longitudinal evaluation are needed for validation of criteria and proxies for impact and establishment of how these processes contribute to lasting transformation.

papers.title: L’IA dans les élections municipales 2026 : Des usages qui appellent un regard nuancé
papers.authors: Antoine Marie
papers.abstract: The municipal elections of March 15 and 22, 2026 constitute the firstFrench local election in which generative artificial intelligence hasmassively entered campaign practices. This research brief offers abalanced analysis of documented uses, distinguishing legitimateapplications (poster generation, programmatic chatbots, contentsynthesis) from confirmed abuses (defamatory deepfakes, misleadingimages, astroturfing). While these new technological capabilities raiselegitimate concerns for the integrity of democratic debate, we argue thattheir impact must be put in perspective in light of the literature on thelimited effects of mass political communication and the actualdeterminants of disinformation consumption. Rather than acatastrophism that risks fueling generalized distrust, we advocate for anapproach grounded in media literacy and the strengthening ofprofessional journalism.

papers.title: Women and AI: A Large-Scale, Validated Mapping of Women’s Under-Represented and Under-Recognized Contributions to AI Research
papers.authors: Chiara Binelli, Elena Cossu
papers.abstract: Participation in AI research shapes which type of AI is built, whose societal needs it addresses, and how it is used in society. Despite increasing attention to gender diversity in AI, we lacksystematic evidence on the research topics, methods used, and collaboration structures associated with female AI researchers. This paper addresses this significant gap by developing the first large-scale, validated mapping of women’s contributions to both generative and non-generative AI research across data science and the main social science disciplines (economics, political science, and sociology). Using a sample of over 500,000 papers published between 2023 and 2026, we document three key findings. First, women are under-represented among academic AI authors across all four disciplines and recent years, and least represented in data science. Second, conditional on participating, women’s AI research is thematically distinctive: it is more applied, social and purpose-driven, concentrated in health, education and fairness, and, in data science, oriented towards using rather than building AI. Third, this distinctive work is heard less: conditional on working on the same AI topic women and men are cited equally, but the topics women disproportionately work on are themselves cited less, so women’s ideas receive systematically fewer citations. This voice gap is therefore a topic-composition penalty rather than a same-topic penalty, and it reduces efficiency by giving a distinctive, society-oriented research agenda too little voice in how AI develops.

papers.title: Citizen Trust in AI Regulatory Regimes in Four EU Countries
papers.authors: Benjamin Leidorf‐Tidå, Pascal D. König
papers.abstract: Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) applications is deemed crucial for uptake of the technology and the development of an AI market. In the present article, we argue that the institutional design of regulatory regimes matters for whether citizens trust AI systems. We study how trust in AI systems depends on who the responsible regulator is, the scope of the regulator’s scrutiny of AI systems, and the involvement of external stakeholders in regulatory oversight. Based on a conjoint design, we examine how respondents value these institutional design choices for the case of high-risk AI systems used in health care. Using samples from Lithuania, Romania, Sweden, and the Netherlands, with 4001 respondents overall, the pre-registered experiment shows that citizens have more trust in AI systems if vendors, civil society and especially independent researchers are involved in oversight, and if regulators actively scrutinize AI systems rather than relying solely on self-reporting. At least in two countries, citizens also seem to have more trust in AI systems if the sectoral health care regulator is the responsible regulator instead of a cross-sectoral regulator such as the national Data Protection Authority or a specific AI regulator.

papers.title: AI or Human Support for Suicide Prevention? Examining Help-Seeking Intention in Suicidal Crisis
papers.authors: Daisuke Nakamura, Hajime Sueki, Jiro Ito
papers.abstract: This preprint has now been published in the peer-reviewed journal Suicide Policy Research. Please read and cite the published version:Nakamura, D., Sueki, H., & Ito, J. (2026). AI or human support for suicide prevention? Examining help-seeking intention in suicidal crisis. Suicide Policy Research, 5(1), 1–12.The published article is freely available at:https://jscp.or.jp/assets/img/SPR_5-1_1_Nakamura.pdfBackground:Chat-based crisis support is a common strategy for suicide prevention, and artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots have the potential to improve the low response rates to such support. Although AI chatbots are technically feasible for crisis support, it remains unclear whether individuals experiencing suicidal ideation intend to use them.Aims:To examine the intentions of adults with depressive symptoms experiencing suicidal ideation to use chat-based crisis support (human vs AI) and explore how these intentions relate to their background characteristics.Methods:A cross-sectional web-based survey was performed, recruiting participants aged 18–69 with a Kessler-6 score ≥13 from an internet research company’s database in Japan. Participants completed a questionnaire assessing their intention to use chat-based crisis support when feeling suicidal, sociodemographic factors, and suicide-related characteristics. Subsequently, participants were categorized into four groups: (1) those intending to use both human and AI-based chats, (2) AI chat only, (3) human chat only, and (4) neither. We calculated the proportions of each group and used the chi-square, Kruskal–Wallis, and Fisher’s exact tests to compare group differences.Results:Overall, 1,024 participants completed the survey, and we determined that 19.5% intended to use AI chat support and 21.3% intended to use human chat. The proportions of participants who intended to use both human- and AI-based chat, AI chat only, human chat only, and neither option were 15.6 %, 3.9 %, 5.7 %, and 74.8 %, respectively. Significant differences were observed in gender (p = 0.028), history of crisis support use (p <0.001), and current issues (financial problems [p = 0.002)] and sexuality-related concerns (p = 0.006) across the groups.Conclusion:In this web-based survey, approximately 20% of individuals with depressive symptoms feeling suicidal were willing to seek help, even if it was provided by AI.

papers.title: Old Test, New Tricks: Using Large Language Models to Generate New Divergent Thinking Test Items
papers.authors: Averie Elizabeth Linnell, Simone A Luchini, Austin Swanson, Roni Reiter‐Palmon, Roger E. Beaty, Antonio Laverghetta
papers.abstract: Automated item generation (AIG) using large language models (LLMs) is emerging as a promising solution for scalable creativity assessments, yet the potential of AIG to create psychometrically rigorous creativity items has thus far received little attention. In the present study, we evaluated the psychometric properties of LLM-generated items for the classic Consequences task of divergent thinking, comparing them to human-written items. A sample of 192 undergraduates completed six Consequences tasks—two human-written, two standard LLM-generated, and two genre-inspired LLM-generated, drawing on sci-fi and fantasy themes—along with measures of personality, cognitive ability, and creative behavior. We found that LLM-generated items elicited significantly higher fluency and flexibility. Genre-inspired items (fantasy and sci-fi) additionally elicited higher originality, enjoyment, and positive valence ratings; LLM-generated items were similar to human-written items. Genre-inspired items did not unfairly advantage participants with more exposure to genre content, demonstrating measurement invariance. Together, these findings suggest that LLMs can generate consequences items with psychometric properties comparable to those of human-written items. We discuss the implications for creativity assessment, item bank development, and best practices for AIG in creativity research, and we provide the prompts we used for item generation to enable researchers to generate new Consequences items at scale.

papers.title: Growing Up With Conversational AI: A Developmental Framework for Adolescent Agency Over Conversational AI Use
papers.authors: Shanting Chen, Mary Kate Koch, Renkai Ma, Cindy H. Liu, Natalie C. Ebner
papers.abstract: Conversational generative AI has rapidly reached majority adoption among U.S. adolescents. These systems now provide advice, emotional support, academic assistance, simulated social interaction, and opportunities for identity exploration at a critical phase in development when mental health needs are rising and capacities for self-regulation, autonomy, and social competence are still developing. Scholars and clinicians have raised urgent questions about what these systems do to adolescents, and early findings point to both benefits and risks. In this article, we ask what adolescents do with AI and introduce the concept of adolescent agency over conversational AI use: the degree to which adolescents purposefully direct, critically evaluate, and set limits on their engagement with conversational AI. Existing constructs such as AI literacy and AI self-efficacy describe what young people know or believe about AI and the risks associated with its use, but they do not capture how adolescents exercise agency across areas of their lives. We identify nine processes that arise at the intersection of conversational AI’s features and key developmental tasks during the period of adolescence, which we label AI-ERA: autonomy, identity, emotion regulation, relationships, and achievement. We distinguish this agency from existing constructs, including agentic engagement with AI and AI overreliance, and then propose how it is shaped by adolescents’ developing capacities, adult scaffolding, and peer influence. We conclude with implications for families, schools, clinicians, and researchers, as well as considerations regarding the design, regulation, and ethics of AI systems.

papers.title: How AI chatbots shape political attitudes when they are not prompted to persuade
papers.authors: Sayeh Yousefi, Jens Koed Madsen
papers.abstract: People increasingly turn to AI chatbots to find information, including information about politicians and political issues. Given evidence that Large Language Models (LLMs) have high persuasive capacities, this has raised concerns about their potential to have undue influence on political attitudes. However, most existing research on AI persuasion explicitly prompts the LLM to persuade the user, which is not representative of how people typically engage with LLMs. Whether undirected political conversations with LLMs shift political attitudes, and whether personalisation amplifies any such effect, remains unclear. We address these questions across two studies. First, in a quota-matched survey of UK adults (N = 2,137), we find that political use of AI is already widespread and its outputs are generally perceived as being politically neutral. Second, in a pre-registered randomised controlled trial (N = 2,081), participants conversed with an LLM about either a politician or political issue, with the LLM not being prompted to persuade. We find that conversations about politicians increased favourability toward them, while conversations about policies modestly reduced support. Conversation personalisation did not amplify these effects. Our findings show that AI chatbots are already a meaningful source of political information in the UK, and that undirected chatbot conversations can influence political attitudes.

papers.title: Mere co-presence and evaluative observation differentially shape motor response execution and inhibition: Behavioral, signal-detection, and ERP evidence
papers.authors: Cuihong Liu, Guoliang Chen, Yi Wei, Yansong Li
papers.abstract: This study examined how mere co-presence and evaluative observation shape motor response execution and inhibition in a Go/NoGo (GNG) task. In Experiment 1, 199 participants were randomly assigned to mere co-presence, evaluative observation, or control. Mere co-presence slowed Go responses and reduced self-reported concentration relative to both other groups without affecting Go accuracy or the NoGo commission error rate relative to control. Only in this group was slower responding associated with greater perceptual sensitivity (d′), suggesting compensatory slowing. By contrast, evaluative observation reduced the NoGo commission error rate and increased d′ relative to both other groups without affecting Go performance relative to control. Experiment 2 used a within-subject event-related potential (ERP) design (N = 44) and replicated the lower NoGo commission error rate and higher d′ under evaluative observation without affecting Go performance. Additionally, evaluative observation produced evaluation-related affective costs—increased evaluative pressure and anxiety—that predicted smaller d′ gains and attenuated its benefit in mediation analyses. Eletrophysiologically, evaluative observation attenuated NoGo-N2 and NoGo-P3 amplitudes without affecting Go components, suggesting that enhanced Go–NoGo discrimination facilitated inhibition by reducing early conflict-monitoring and later reactive-control demands. These findings suggest two dissociable pathways through which distinct forms of social presence shapes motor control.

papers.title: Are replication failures reflected in public knowledge?
papers.authors: Wu Youyou
papers.abstract: Behavioural sciences now routinely replicate to verify published findings. Replication is a powerful mechanism for science to self-correct, but it is only the first step. New evidence must also reach researchers, students, and the public to update their understanding. Within academic scholarship, there is mixed evidence about whether failed replications are linked to reduced citations of the original studies. Far less is known about how many non-replicable findings continue to circulate through mainstream channels where students and the public access knowledge. This study tracked research findings with well-established replication failures to assess whether three public knowledge channels revised their content in response. We also queried two AI platforms about the original findings to assess whether the AI responses incorporated new replication evidence. Traditional channels, including Wikipedia, textbooks, and university course syllabi, acknowledged replication failures roughly one-third of the time, which was more often than researchers predicted in a pre-registered survey. AI systems performed substantially better: ChatGPT acknowledged replication failures for up to 80% of findings, rising to 95% among findings with high online visibility. We also discovered that knowledge revision was more likely to occur when replication records appeared on a simple, openly accessible webpage, and less likely when buried in large-scale replication projects. Our research highlights a gap between knowledge production and uptake when new evidence challenges established findings. Closing that gap is a multi-actor endeavour. We recommend that researchers and funders invest in dissemination as an integral part of replication work. Knowledge curators and consumers should use tools such as replication databases and AI to keep their materials and beliefs up to date.

papers.title: Hybrid Neural Network-Based Real Time Inverse Kinematics Method for a Six-Axis Anthropomorphic Leg without a Spherical Joint
papers.authors: Dotti Pablo, N. Poberezkin
papers.abstract: Abstract In humanoid robot control, the inverse kinematics solver constitutes a critical real-time component, as any latency may compromise stable operation. This study presents the development and evaluation of two hybrid methods for solving the real-time inverse kinematics of a six-axis anthropomorphic leg lacking a spherical joint. The absence of this joint makes closed-form analytical solutions not possible, necessitating fast and accurate numerical approaches for real-time applications. To accelerate convergence and reduce the overall number of required iterations, we propose two distinct strategies for generating an initial guess for a Damped Least Squares numerical solver. The first is a novel geometry-based method designed for the specific kinematic constraints and reachable workspace of the leg structure. The second employs a custom neural network trained on forward kinematics data. Comprehensive testing was conducted to evaluate convergence behavior based on iteration count. Execution time measurements obtained directly on a microcontroller showed that from the proposed methods, the quickest one takes an average of 3.24 ms of calculation time with a maximum of 3.9 ms. This validates the real-time viability of both proposed approaches, demonstrating a 37% increase in computational speed compared to established alternatives when considering the platform on which they were calculated.

papers.title: PREDICTING SCHOOL NUMERACY PERFORMANCE THROUGH EDUCATIONAL DATA MINING: AN INTEGRATED K-NEAREST NEIGHBOR AND MULTINOMIAL LOGISTIC REGRESSION APPROACH
papers.authors: Sitti Busyrah Muchsin, Dadang Juandi, Suhendra Suhendra, Hasan Hamid
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: International large-scale assessments such as PISA consistently indicate that numeracy achievement in Indonesia remains below the international average, highlighting the need for early identification of schools requiring targeted educational support. Although previous studies have examined factors associated with numeracy performance, few have integrated predictive machine learning with explanatory statistical modelling to support evidence-based educational decision making. This study aimed to develop a hybrid analytical framework by combining the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) algorithm optimized using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) with Multinomial Logistic Regression to predict school numeracy performance and identify its significant determinants. Secondary data were obtained from the 2023 Indonesian Education Report, comprising 181 elementary schools in Makassar, South Sulawesi. The predictive model utilized four educational indicators: reading literacy, formulating, employing, and interpreting competencies. The optimized KNN model (k = 5) achieved a macro classification accuracy of 90%, demonstrating strong predictive performance across numeracy proficiency levels. Furthermore, the trained model successfully classified an unseen school profile into the Basic numeracy category, illustrating its practical applicability for early institutional mapping. Multinomial Logistic Regression revealed that all predictor variables significantly influenced numeracy performance (p < 0.05), with the employing competency emerging as the strongest determinant, indicating that higher application skills substantially increased the likelihood of schools progressing from the Basic to the Proficient category. Reading literacy also exhibited a significant positive contribution, reinforcing the close relationship between language comprehension and contextual mathematical problem solving. These findings demonstrate that integrating machine learning prediction with statistical interpretation provides an effective data-driven framework for supporting educational policy, identifying at-risk schools, and designing timely interventions to improve numeracy achievement.

papers.title: The interplay between diabetes distress, disordered eating behaviors, and antidiabetic medications in Type 2 diabetes mellitus
papers.authors: Şebnem Burhan, Muhammed Zeki Cicek
papers.abstract: Aim: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) imposes psychological and behavioral challenges. While prior research links eating habits, distress, and glycemic control, few studies explore these factors together. This study assessed the associations between night eating, eating patterns, diabetes distress (DDS), glycemic control, BMI, gender, and medication use in adults with T2DM. Methods: This study included 105 adults with T2DM. Night eating behavior, eating patterns, and DDS were evaluated using the Night Eating Questionnaire (NEQ), the 18-item version of the Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire-Revised (TFEQ-R18), and the Diabetes Distress Scale (DDS). Results: NEQ score correlated with BMI (r=0.38, p=0.001) and remained significant after adjusting for age, gender, and HbA1c (p=0.002). TFEQ-R18 emotional eating inversely correlated with BMI (r=−0.36, p=0.001) and persisted after adjustment (p=0.004). Uncontrolled eating and cognitive restraint showed no links. Men scored higher on emotional eating than women (10.0 ± 2.54 vs. 8.69 ± 3.20, p = 0.02). Poor glycemic control had higher DDS emotional burden and regimen-related distress; NEQ and TFEQ-R18 scores did not differ by glycemic status or medication classes. Conclusion: DDS, particularly emotional burden and regimen-related distress, differed across HbA1c categories, but this was not confirmed in multivariable models. BMI, not glycemic control, more consistently predicted eating behavior and distress. Given the cross-sectional design and small sample size, the no significant association between eating behavior and glycemic control does not rule out a relationship. These findings support routine distress screening in diabetes care and larger prospective studies of these associations and their relationship to body weight.

papers.title: Pengaruh Literasi Digital dan Kecemasan Karier terhadap Niat Calon Akuntan menggunakan AI dalam Audit
papers.authors: Siti Anggraeni Mulidinisa, Seto Satriyo Bayu Aji
papers.journal: Inisiatif Jurnal Ekonomi Akuntansi dan Manajemen
papers.abstract: Digitalization and the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) are forcing the audit profession to adapt, yet Generation Z accounting students in the pre-professional stage having completed or currently undertaking an Audit course, here regarded as prospective accountants remain constrained by digital competence and career anxiety. This study examines the influence of digital literacy and career anxiety on prospective accountants' intention to use AI in auditing, with career anxiety as a moderating variable. A quantitative explanatory design was employed, involving three constructs: digital literacy, career anxiety, and intention to use AI. Primary data were collected via an online questionnaire administered to 77 Generation Z undergraduate accounting students selected through purposive sampling, analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results show that digital literacy has a positive and significant effect on intention to use AI, while career anxiety has a negative and significant effect. Career anxiety also moderates the relationship by weakening the positive effect of digital literacy on intention to use AI. These findings imply that psychological factors, particularly career anxiety, should not be overlooked in preparing accounting students for AI-based digital transformation in auditing, underscoring the need for curricula balancing digital literacy with career anxiety management.
