papers.title: Seven Technology-Based Active Learning Models for Educational System Transformation: A Policy Brief
papers.authors: Zahra Sadeqi-Arani, Hamed Taherdoost
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Introduction: With the spread of new technologies, significant changes have occurred in teaching and learning, which can be used to overcome the challenges of the traditional education system,such as lecture-based teaching methods, limited opportunities for active learning, lack of attention to problem-solving skills such as creative and critical thinking, and rote assessment methods.Method: The study adopts a policy analysis and conceptual synthesis approach, reviewing existing literature to propose seven technology-based educational models: gamified learning,problem-based learning, AI-driven classrooms, IoB-based smart schools, team-based learning, lifelong learning, and flipped learning.Results: Results indicated that these models collectively enhanced student engagement, motivation, personalization, collaboration, critical thinking, and well-being. Gamified learning increased motivation and participation; PBL strengthened problem-solving and experiential learning. Also, AI-driven classrooms enabled adaptive, personalized learning, and IoB-based smart schools supported real-time monitoring of learning behaviors and mental health. Moreover, team-based learning improved collaboration and communication skills, and lifelong learning fostered self-regulated and continuous skill development; flipped learning increased active classroomparticipation and academic performance. Together, these approaches provide complementary pathways for addressing structural inefficiencies in traditional education systems and improving overall educational quality and equity.Conclusion: Integrating these seven models offers a coherent framework for transforming traditional education into a technology-enhanced, learner-centered system. However, successful implementation requires phased adoption, infrastructure development, teacher training, and attention to ethical and equity considerations. Gradual integration, starting with low-cost pedagogical models and progressing toward advanced AI and IoB systems, can lead to sustainable and context-sensitive educational reform in developing educational contexts overall.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence–Based Computer Vision Feedback to Improve Clinical Performance in Surgical Technology Education
papers.authors: KIARASH KAMBOOZIA, Sedigheh Hanani, Nazanin Sarraf Shahri, Zeynab Barzegar, SAEID ZARIF GHASEMIAN
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Introduction: Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision offer new opportunities to improve clinical skills training. This study developed a real-time, AI-based computer vision system for detecting surgical instruments and evaluated its association with clinical performance among surgical technology students.Methods: A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test study with a control group was conducted among 48 eligible surgical technology students at Iran University of Medical Sciences during the 2025–2026 academic year. Participants who met the predefined inclusion criteria were enrolled using census sampling. Following ethics approval (IR.IUMS.REC.1403.928), the participants were allocated to an intervention group (n=31), which received immediate AI-generated visual feedback after each instrument arrangement task, and a control group (n=17), which received routine instructor-led training without AI feedback. A YOLOv8-based deep learning model was trained using transfer learning on annotated images of surgical table setups. Clinical performance was assessed using a validated observational checklist (CVI=0.90; Cronbach’s α=0.87). Data were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Spearman’s correlation, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) in SPSS version 27. All 48 participants completed the study (attrition rate=0%).Results: The AI model achieved excellent object detection performance (precision=0.974, recall=0.979, mAP@0.5=0.981, mAP@0.5:0.95=0.808), with an average inference time of 1.6 seconds per image. Clinical performance was significantly higher following AI-assisted feedback (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Z=−4.879, p<0.001, r=0.88). After adjustment for baseline performance using ANCOVA, AI-assisted feedback was associated with higher post-intervention performance scores than conventional training (F (1,45)=19.51, p<0.001, partial η²=0.302). Excellent agreement was observed between AI-generated assessments and expert human ratings (ICC=0.984).Conclusions: Real-time, AI-based computer vision feedback was associated with improved surgical instrument arrangement performance among surgical technology students while providing an objective and reliable assessment of practical skills. The proposed system represents a promising proof-of-concept educational tool for simulation-based training and competency assessment and may complement conventional instructional approaches in surgical technology education.

papers.title: Regulation and Ethical Frameworks for AI in Health Professions Education: A Critical Narrative Review
papers.authors: Yasar Ahmed, Simaa Khayal
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Introduction: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI)—particularly generative AI and large language models (LLMs)—into health professions education offers substantial pedagogical opportunities, while highlighting critical gaps in existing ethical and regulatory frameworks. This critical narrative review examines how contemporary literature conceptualizes and addresses these challenges.Methods: Publications from 2020–2025 were identified through searching PubMed, Scopus, and ERIC, focusing on AI, medical and health professions education, ethics, governance, and regulation. The initial search yielded 452 records; following two-stage screening (title/abstract and full-text review), thirty-four sources met the pre-defined inclusion criteria. These sources, includingempirical studies, systematic reviews, policy documents, and conceptual papers, were included. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to synthesize the findings, while SANRA (Scale for theAssessment of Narrative Review Articles) informed the weighting of sources, which were categorized into high-, moderate-, and low-weight tiers.Results: Four themes emerged: 1) a regulatory vacuum marked by policy lag and fragmented institutional responses; 2) reinterpretation of autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, andjustice in relation to opaque, datadriven systems, 3) generative AI’s impact on scholarship, authorship, and academic integrity; and 4) equity, bias, and professional identity formation in AImediated learning environments. Integrating these themes with crosssector frameworks and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the review develops a riskbased governance taxonomy for AI in Health Professions Education, distinguishing low, medium and highrisk educational use cases.Conclusion: This synthesis indicates that current literature favors evolving beyond reactive policies. Consequently, we propose a theoretical shift toward risk-proportionate governance. We suggest that human-in-the-loop pedagogy should be prioritized as a conceptual framework to guide future research and policy development, rather than presenting it as a validated outcome.

papers.title: Integrating ChatGPT into digital material design on socioscientific issues: Teacher candidates’ reflections on a three-phase design process
papers.authors: Banu Avşar Erümit and Ayşegül Yılmazer Göçer
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: This study investigates how science and social studies teacher candidates (TCs) integrate ChatGPT, an AI-powered tool, into the development of digital instructional materials on socioscientific issues (SSIs). Conducted with 45 TCs in Turkiye, the study employed a phenomenological design and collected data through pre- and post-interviews, weekly reflections, initial drafts, ChatGPT conversations, and final products. Findings reveal that most TCs had limited prior experience with ChatGPT but developed more positive and informed perceptions through hands-on use. ChatGPT contributed to material development by offering diverse content, saving time, and enhancing design quality. However, analysis using the SAMR model indicated that technology integration remained largely at substitution and augmentation levels. The extent of material revision was heavily determined by cognitive demand, demonstrating that AI’s utility varied significantly between structural (convergent) and creative (divergent) design needs. The study provides crucial insights into AI-supported instructional design, demonstrating that technology integration depth in generative AI contexts is fundamentally governed by teacher candidates’ pedagogical autonomy and emerging critical AI literacy when navigating tasks demanding creative and ethical judgment.

papers.title: Toward trustworthy AI in education: Stakeholders’ risk perceptions in Korea’s AI digital textbook implementation
papers.authors: Sangmin-Michelle Lee and Nam Ju Kim Junseong Bang
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in educational systems, concerns about its ethical, technical, and social risks are growing, particularly in large-scale deployments such as Korea’s nationwide AI-powered digital textbook (AIDT) initiative. Despite growing discourse on AI ethics, there remains a critical gap in empirical research that compares how different stakeholder groups, such as developers and teachers, perceive these risks in real-world educational contexts. This study examines stakeholder perceptions of AI-related risks in AIDT by comparing the responses of two key groups: developers (N = 31) and teachers (N = 40). The study uses a mixed-methods approach, combining survey data based on a nine-principle AI risk assessment checklist with in-depth interviews. Quantitative results reveal a significant divergence between developers and teachers in perceived risk likelihood and severity, with teachers consistently rating risks higher, especially in educational domains. Qualitative analysis further reveals differences in priority, awareness, and concern between stakeholder roles, highlighting a gap between technical development and classroom realities. Developers emphasized compliance and infrastructure, while teachers emphasized limitations in pedagogy, students’ overreliance, and the lack of AI transparency. These discrepancies are interpreted through Sociotechnical Systems Theory, emphasizing the misalignment between technical and social subsystems. The study calls for collaborative optimization through co-design and communication to build trustworthy, equitable AI in education. This research provides critical insights for education policymakers, AI developers, and practitioners seeking to implement AI in education responsibly while balancing innovation and student protection.

papers.title: Effects of ChatGPT on academic writing: A systematic review
papers.authors: Norhakimah Khaiessa Ahmad and Lilliati Ismail Zhen Zou
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Academic writing is important in English as a foreign language (EFL) research and education, but it is difficult for teachers and students to teach and learn about the organized expression of ideas, evidence-based arguments, and logical reasoning. Advances in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) now offer new opportunities to solve these challenges. In particular, the Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT), released by OpenAI in November 2022, has gained a lot of attention for its ability to perform language tasks and generate human-like responses. However, its use in academic writing has raised concerns about ethics and the authenticity of scholarly work. This study focuses on the impact of ChatGPT on teaching and learning processes as well as writing performance and provides some practical recommendations for its use in the writing process by using a systematic review approach. A total of 77 empirical studies that were published between 2022 and 2024 were identified after searching Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar. From these studies, this review synthesized 10 topics related to the teaching and learning processes, 10 topics on writing performance, and 3 topics that make practical recommendations. The results demonstrate that the advantages of using ChatGPT in academic writing outweigh the disadvantages. Rather than only concentrating on the possible concerns, it is important to discuss solutions, such as reforming pedagogical strategies, developing institutional policies and equipping teachers and students with specific AI literacy, to take advantage of the potential of the technology effectively.

papers.title: AI’nspired: Evaluating AI-generated versus web images as sources of design inspiration
papers.authors: Ewa Angoneze-Grela, Barbara Linowiecka, Magda Matuszewska, Łukasz Borak, Jakub Jagła, Marcin Kapiszewski, Marcel Rojewski, Adam Tomys and Dariusz Brzezinski
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Recent advances in image-generative artificial intelligence (AI) have provided designers with powerful tools for quickly exploring and iterating on their creative concepts. However, the effectiveness of different sources of inspiration in supporting design development remains underexplored, particularly within design education. This study examines the impact of AI-generated images versus web-sourced images on designers’ creative outcomes. For this purpose, we have gathered a dataset of design projects created by 50 students, who used AI-generated and web-sourced images as inspiration. To identify sources of inspiration in each project, we propose computer vision metrics that measure contrast and color similarity, as well as deep learning embedding similarity. The similarities computed between final designs and inspiration images are compared with student surveys expressing their perception of sources of inspiration and with expert ratings assigned to each project. The comparison shows that the students’ stated inspiration is positively correlated with the computed inspiration-design similarity and that students exhibit a preference for AI-generated inspiration, even if they are first-time users of generative tools. Moreover, our study reveals that both web and AI images are inspirational, but they affect different aspects of design. AI inspirations correlate strongly with the overall composition and mood, and web-sourced inspirations play an important role in defining color, materials, and grounding the design in reality.

papers.title: Developing self-regulated learning skills in senior secondary students through generative artificial intelligence tools: Evaluation of a GenAI course using mixed-methods
papers.authors: Siu Cheung Kong and Luwei Ye
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Research has highlighted the importance of self-regulated learning (SRL) for personal development and lifelong learning. Therefore, it is essential to foster SRL skills in learners from a young age to prepare them to adapt to and succeed in a rapidly changing world. Generative AI (GenAI) tools offer significant potential for helping learners develop these skills through immediate, individualised feedback. This study evaluated the use of GenAI learning tools to enhance students’ SRL skills. Eighty-four senior secondary students completed a 30-hour GenAI application course and were required to reflect on their SRL skills. A mixed-methods approach was employed to evaluate the course. Pre- and post-survey comparisons indicated that the students’ SRL skills improved significantly after attending the course. A thematic analysis of their self-reflective writings revealed that the students strongly believed the course had inspired them to apply GenAI tools for acquiring subject knowledge and managing their learning. The effectiveness of this course can guide and inspire future empirical research and pedagogical practices focused on integrating GenAI tools into the educational process to develop students’ SRL.

papers.title: Analyzing the impact of objective vs. subjective student engagement on performance predictions in virtual reality co-creation settings
papers.authors: Hsin-Yun Wang and Jerry Chih-Yuan Sun
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: This study examined how objective and subjective engagement data predict learning outcomes in virtual reality (VR) co-creation environments. Conducted at a public high school in northern Taiwan, 83 students participated in an 18-week online-merge-offline (OMO) VR co-creation course. Random Forest (RF) models compared objective indicators (e.g., EEG, logs, performance scores) with self-reported surveys. Results showed that objective data provided greater predictive accuracy and explanatory power, while subjective measures were constrained by retrospective bias and unidimensional data structure. However, incremental validity analyses revealed comparable gains in explained variance across both data types with each added engagement dimension. This suggests that although objective data excel in predictive performance, subjective measures capture complementary insights into learners’ internal states, metacognitive awareness, and contextual experiences. Moreover, multimodal data outperformed unidimensional inputs, underscoring the value of data fusion in representing the complexity of student engagement. Sentiment analysis revealed trust as the dominant emotion, along with a mix of negative feelings, underscoring the emotional dynamics of immersive learning. To enhance instructional relevance, the study calls for the development of real-time multimodal dashboards co-designed with teachers and instructional designers – ensuring that feedback is pedagogically meaningful and context-sensitive. These findings support the integration of diverse data sources to advance adaptive support and deepen understanding of engagement in immersive learning.

papers.title: Measuring digital inequality among K-12 teachers: Construction of a comprehensive index system
papers.authors: Zhi-Xian Zhong and Ran-Xi Yan Xiao-Fen Shi
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Amid the global trend toward educational digitalization, the concept of human-machine collaboration is reshaping the ecosystem of basic education. However, the digital transformation of K-12 education faces profound challenges. Uneven resource allocation has led to a pronounced stratification pattern, resulting in a widening digital divide among K-12 teachers. This divide has emerged as a critical barrier to achieving the goal of inclusive education. To address this issue, the present study adopts grounded theory with a three-level coding approach to systematically analyze the manifestations of the digital divide among K-12 teachers. Through iterative refinement using the Delphi method, an assessment framework was developed, comprising three primary dimensions, eleven secondary indicators, and thirty-five tertiary indicators. Subsequently, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was employed for subjective weighting, while the entropy weight method was used for objective weighting, leading to the determination of integrated weight coefficients. This study provides a theoretical basis and methodological tools for the future assessment of teachers’ digital development index and for bridging the digital divide within the teaching profession.

papers.title: Beyond ChatGPT: Evaluating pedagogical GenAI agents for enhanced teacher professional development
papers.authors: Mu-Sheng Chen and Ting-Chia Hsu Tai-Ping Hsu
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: While generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) such as ChatGPT offers potential for education, its widespread use by teachers often leads to inefficient interactions, and it lacks pedagogical structure. This can diminish learners’ engagement and increase their cognitive load, hindering effective professional development. This study investigated whether a Pedagogical GenAI Agents Teaching Mode (Pedagogical GenAI Agents-TM), integrating Design Thinking as a pedagogical framework, could enhance in-service teachers’ professional development compared to a conventional ChatGPT Teaching Mode (GPT-TM). A quasi-experimental design involved 76 Taiwanese in-service teachers assigned to either Pedagogical GenAI Agents-TM or GPT-TM groups, with a focus on designing Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)-related teaching activities. Quantitative and qualitative analyses revealed that, compared to GPT-TM, Pedagogical GenAI Agents-TM significantly improved teachers’ SDG learning achievement and TPACK self-efficacy, while reducing their cognitive load. The Pedagogical GenAI Agents-TM group demonstrated more collaborative AI interaction and adopted effective learning strategies, perceiving AI as a learning partner, contrasting with the GPT-TM group’s tool-centric view and less effective information processing. The study concludes that pedagogically structured AI interaction, as embodied by Pedagogical GenAI Agents-TM, more effectively overcomes the limitations of general-purpose AI for teacher professional development. Integrating established pedagogical frameworks into AI systems fosters deeper learning, enhances teacher confidence, and alleviates cognitive strain. We therefore advocate for specialized, Pedagogical GenAI Agents designed as collaborative partners rather than mere informational tools.

papers.title: A capability-based framework for task allocation in human-AI collaboration
papers.authors: 陳年興 Nian-Shing Chen
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Generative AI produces convincing work quickly, but this convenience breaks the link between a finished product and its author’s capability. The central problem is no longer whether AI should be used, but which parts of a task should be performed, learned, or delegated. While current frameworks in automation, self-regulated learning, cognitive offloading, and human-AI interaction illuminate facets of this problem, none offer a systematic method for task allocation that balances immediate workflow needs with the preservation of long-term human capability. A framework is needed to optimize work distribution while safeguarding long-term human capability and value. This paper introduces the Know-Learn-Delegate (KLD) framework, a capability-based solution that treats the relation between a person, a task, and that person’s developmental intention as the unit of allocation. Users decompose a task and classify each component according to whether they can perform it unaided and, if not, whether they intend to learn it. AI then serves as proxy executor, tutor, or autonomous agent. KLD’s originality lies in connecting immediate efficiency with capability formation, human agency, capability maintenance, and assessment. To prevent inflated claims of competence, a three-part “Know” test comprising Perform, Specify, and Detect (PSD) is introduced. Delegation is further constrained by state-specific application of Verifiability, Consequence, and Reversibility (VCR) principles. This framework also mandates ongoing practice for essential capabilities and establishes stronger restrictions during formative learning stages. Design principles translate KLD into multi-agent workflows in which planning, generation, evaluation, and human acceptance remain essential. The paper proposes assessing human-AI contribution through observable agency across the production process rather than percentages inferred from the final artifact. KLD thus offers educators, learners, and knowledge workers a defensible way to gain AI’s efficiency without quietly surrendering human value in terms of agency, judgment, or future capability.

papers.title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Restore Standards in Medical and Dental Education in Pakistan
papers.authors: Orooj Bashir, Syeda Kashaf Abbas, Javed Ashraf
papers.journal: Journal of College of Physicians And Surgeons Pakistan
papers.abstract: Pakistan's medical and dental education has experienced declining standards, inconsistent regulation, and periodic loss of degree recognition. This viewpoint proposes a structured role for artificial intelligence (AI) to analyse past failures and to guide prospective reforms. As medical education globally adapts to information overload and AI‑assisted clinical reasoning, curricula must balance knowledge management, communication, and empathy. Natural language processing (NLP) can mine inspection reports and policy documents to detect regulatory weaknesses, while machine learning (ML) can identify predictors of institutional under‑performance. Retrospective AI can uncover patterns of governance breakdown, admissions irregularities, and curriculum gaps. Prospectively, predictive modelling, adaptive learning platforms, and AI‑driven accreditation dashboards can enable real‑time monitoring and decision support. Generative AI, virtual reality (VR), and augmented reality (AR) can expand faculty development and clinical simulation opportunities. Embedding AI into accreditation and institutional practice can align Pakistan with World Federation for Medical Education (WFME) standards, strengthen accountability, and rebuild global credibility. Adoption of AI is essential for restoring public trust and ensuring the competitiveness of Pakistan's healthcare workforce. Key Words: Artificial intelligence, Medical education, Dental education, Accreditation, Pakistan, WFME, Data governance, Faculty development, Digital divide.

papers.title: Strategi Pengembangan Bisnis Arsitektur Lanskap Digital pada OKE Garden
papers.authors: Nadya Kamilia Faiqoh, Popong Nurhayati, Heny Kuswanti Suwarsinah
papers.abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has significantly transformed consumer behavior and business models, including in the landscape service sector. This study aims to formulate a business development strategy for OKE Garden, a digital-based landscape service startup, by integrating internal and external strategic analysis. The research adopts a mixed-method approach with a sequential explanatory design. Qualitative data were collected through in-depth interviews with internal and external stakeholders, while quantitative analysis employed the IFE, EFE, IE Matrix, SWOT, and QSPM frameworks. The results show that OKE Garden operates in a favorable external environment (EFE score = 3.166), driven by urban greening trends, youth interest, and digital marketing potential. However, the internal capability remains underdeveloped (IFE score = 2.488), particularly in service digitalization and partner quality control. The company is positioned in Quadrant II of the IE Matrix, indicating the need for growth strategies supported by internal improvements. The top-priority strategy identified through QSPM is the development of a self-onboarding user system, AI chatbot, and integration of real-time digital financial transactions (TAS = 2.411). This strategy addresses key performance gaps, such as security, usability, clarity of information, service timeline, and price transparency, while reducing reliance on manual WhatsApp communication. Complementary strategies include partner certification, modular franchise expansion, AR/VR visualization, green marketing campaigns, and AI-based weather prediction. This study contributes a strategic formulation model tailored to the digital landscape service sector, an area that remains underexplored in previous landscape planning literature.

papers.title: Exploring the effects of AI-generated feedback on EFL writing fluency and quality: a process and product-based perspective
papers.authors: Oumaima Belgamra
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) tools become increasingly embedded in educational contexts, their role in supporting EFL writing development warrants closer empirical examination. Grounded in Flower and Hayes' Cognitive Process Model and informed by psycholinguistic research using keystroke logging, this exploratory pilot study explores the potential effects of AI-generated feedback on EFL learners' writing quality and writing processes from both product- and process-oriented perspectives. Using a between-subjects experimental design, fourteen EFL undergraduates were randomly assigned to either a ChatGPT-assisted revision group or a self-revision control group. Participants produced an initial draft and subsequently revised their texts under their assigned condition. Writing processes were examined through Inputlog keystroke data capturing pausing behavior and revision patterns, while writing quality was assessed using an analytic rubric with established inter-rater reliability. The findings indicate that both revision conditions improved writing quality; however, participants who received AI-generated feedback achieved significantly higher post-revision writing quality scores than those who relied on self-revision. AI-assisted revision was also associated with reductions in several pausing- and revision-related measures, suggesting changes in observable writing behavior during revision. These findings highlight the potential of AI-generated feedback to support both the product and process dimensions of EFL writing.

papers.title: LLM-Enhanced Bayesian Knowledge Tracing for Continuous Performance Modeling and Adaptive Programming Learning
papers.authors: Mariam Mahdaoui, Saïd Nouh, Seddiq El Kasmi Alaoui, Khalid Kandali
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of learners’ skill mastery is essential for adaptive learning systems, particularly in programming education, where evaluating learner performance remains challenging due to the complexity of code assessment and the need to capture partial correctness and diverse learning behaviors. This study aims to improve mastery estimation and adaptive exercise recommendations through a continuous knowledge-tracing approach based on an extension of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing. The proposed approach integrates continuous performance scores from an automated evaluation process that combines structural code analysis, dynamic testing, and large language model–based analysis, while accounting for task difficulty and guidance format. The estimated mastery is then used to recommend programming exercises adapted to the learner’s knowledge state. To evaluate the approach, controlled simulations involving diverse learner profiles and real interaction data were conducted. Results show that the proposed model variants reduce mastery estimation error by up to 70% compared with the baseline model, particularly for learners with low and average proficiency levels. Furthermore, the approach improves estimation stability and generates recommendations consistent with learner progression. The main contribution of this work is a continuous extension of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing that leverages fine-grained assessment data to improve learner modeling and adaptive exercise recommendation in programming education.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence, Innovativeness, and Country-of-Origin Image as Drivers of High-Tech Product Choice: The Moderating Role of Product Customization
papers.authors: Stefan Zdravković, Jelena Živković, Snežana Maksimović, Tomašević Dragana
papers.abstract: The rapid development of high-technology markets has intensified the need for a deeper understanding of the factors influencing consumers’ purchasing decisions regarding technologically advanced products. This study examines the effects of artificial intelligence, consumer innovativeness, and country-of-origin image on the choice of high-tech products, with a particular focus on computers and mobile phones. In addition, the study investigates the moderating role of product customization, conceptualized as consumers’ perceived opportunities to adapt product features and functionalities to their individual preferences. The empirical research was conducted in the Republic of Serbia from January to April 2026 on a sample of 549 respondents, using a structured questionnaire administered through both online and in-person channels. Data were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) in AMOS 24, with gender, age, and education included as demographic control variables. The results indicate that artificial intelligence, consumer innovativeness, and country-of-origin image are positively and statistically significantly associated with high-tech product choice, while these relationships remain significant after accounting for demographic controls. Product customization also exhibits a positive direct association with high-tech product choice and significantly strengthens the relationships between each of the three focal predictors and high-tech product choice. The study contributes to a better understanding of high-tech consumer behavior by jointly examining technological, individual, and country-related factors and by providing additional empirical evidence on the moderating role of perceived product customization. From a managerial standpoint, the findings suggest that firms operating in high-technology industries may benefit from combining favorable perceptions of AI-enabled functionality, innovation-oriented positioning, and country-of-origin image with opportunities for consumers to adapt product features and functionalities to their preferences.

papers.title: User Experience of Working with ChatGPT: A Phenomenological Analysis
papers.authors: A. D. Vorobyeva, V. A. Dmitriev
papers.abstract: The article presents a phenomenological analysis of the user experience of interacting with ChatGPT, based on descriptions produced by the authors, statements from respondents, and information from open sources. The purpose of the study is to identify the specific features of the experience of interacting with ChatGPT from the perspective of user perception. The justification of the chosen approach rests on the idea that the noumenon of a neural network is fundamentally inaccessible to human perception due to the opacity of its inner mechanisms. The analysis distinguishes between the experience of communicating with ChatGPT as a kind of «you» and the experience of using it as a handy tool. In the first case, the user perceives the neural network either as a you-machine or as a you-interlocutor. At the same time, the status of interlocutor proves unstable: errors in responses generate disappointment, whereas increased friendliness creates an impression of understanding and acceptance. The mode of working with ChatGPT as an instrument for solving practical tasks is described as an experience of interacting with a helpful assistant willing to fulfill even absurd requests. These modes, however, are not strictly separated, which allows the user to switch between different ways of interacting. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the phenomenological description of the dual user perception of ChatGPT, which combines an attitude toward it as a handy tool and as a distinct participant in communication. As a distinctive feature of the experience of working with ChatGPT–regardless of the mode–the authors identify «answerability», that is, the situation in which any question or remark is guaranteed to receive a response.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence as a Factor of Transformation of the Professional Activity of a Presentation Designer
papers.authors: K. V. Akhmetshina, Р.В. Габдулхакова
papers.abstract: The relevance of the study stems from the contradiction between the rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) technologies in visual communication practice and the uncertainty regarding the limits of automation of creative labour performed by presentation designers. The aim of the article is to determine the character and boundaries of the transformation of a presentation designer's professional activity under the influence of generative artificial intelligence and to identify the functional division of tasks between humans and algorithmic systems. The leading method is a qualitative comparativefunctional analysis of presentation design operations, supplemented by a case analysis of the application of generative text, image and video models; the theoretical framework draws on the sociology of professions, cognitive load theory and the cognitive theory of multimedia learning. The study establishes that operational and technical functions (visual asset search, image processing, draft generation, animation) are subject to automation, whereas the strategic functions of communication design (audience analysis, argumentation development, scenario design) remain dependent on the designer's expertise. The novelty of the work lies in systematising the functional map “designer – generative AI” with respect to presentation design and in substantiating a model of professional transformation from “designer-executor” to “designer-curator and operator of generative systems”, which is of practical relevance for revising educational programmes and professional standards.

papers.title: Representation of Artificial Intelligence in VKontakte News Groups: Critical versus Apologetic Discourses
papers.authors: E. V. Kononenko, Liliya R. Nizamova
papers.abstract: The widespread use of artificial intelligence (AI) is reflected in the mass media, with social networks playing a special role as public spaces for constructing social reality. AI representation varies ranging from skeptical assessments to complimentary. The purpose of this article is to assess the nature and relationship of AI coverage strategies in VKontakte news groups using discourse analysis, which allows us to identify the specific features of AI representation in social media. Research revealed that the representation of AI is asymmetrical. The discourse of technophobia (images of AI as a criminal, a substitute for humans, and a fool) is more pronounced and appears as a more complex phenomenon than the discourse of technophilia (images of an assistant, a high-status holder, and a student), which does not form a sufficient body of meanings to counteract the panic narratives. While critical rhetoric relies on strategies of "deligitimization," "criminalization," and "catastrophization," apologetic discourse resorts to "normalization," "personalization," and "quantification," which are insufficient to establish stable positive narratives and overcome societal anxieties.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy: Problems of Sociological Measurement
papers.authors: Ilya A. Bykov, Mariia V. Medvedeva, Larisa Valentinovna Sharakhina
papers.abstract: This article examines the sociological measurement of artificial intelligence (AI) literacy using Russian university students as an example. The relevance of the study is driven by the widespread adoption of AI technologies, which poses cognitive, social, and educational risks. The authors analyze international approaches to conceptualizing AI literacy as the ability to critically understand, use, and interact with AI systems. The empirical basis for the study was a questionnaire survey of 401 undergraduate and graduate students (December 2024 – January 2025). The integrated literacy score (maximum 17) averaged 8.2. The results confirm that a technical education profile is the strongest predictor of knowledge (the difference with humanities students was 1.7 points, p < 0.001). Gender differences were statistically insignificant after controlling for the educational profile. A weak positive correlation with age (r = 0.21) was found, with the main increase in competencies occurring during the transition from school to university (ages 19–20). The authors conclude that interdisciplinary programs are needed to bridge the AI-literacy gap between technical and humanities professionals.

papers.title: Chronic Illness and the Structural Integration of Physical Literacy, Physical Activity, and Body Composition in Older Women
papers.authors: Karlo Mužinić, Barbara Gilić Škugor, Dean Kontić, Ivan Kvesić, Nataša Zenić
papers.abstract: Chronic non-communicable diseases are highly prevalent in older women and are associated with unfavorable changes in body composition (BC). Physical literacy (PL) and physical activity (PA) are key determinants of healthy aging but it remains unclear whether chronic illness modifies not only their levels but also the structural relationships among PL, PA, and BC. This study aimed to examine differences in PL, PA, and BC between older women with- and without-chronic-illness and to compare the structural organization of associations among these variables in two observed groups. The sample included 60 women aged 66.1±9.6 years, categorized in two groups, those with- (n=36) and without-chronic-illness (n=24). PL, and PA were assessed using the validated questionnaires (Perceived Physical Literacy Questionnaire for South Eastern Europe, and Nordic Physical Activity Questionnaire – short version), and BC via bioelectrical impedance analysis. Between-group differences were examined using Welch’s t-tests with Cohen’s d effect size (ES). Pearson correlations were calculated separately by group, and Fisher’s z-tests with FDR correction were applied (91 comparisons). Correlation networks (|r|≥0.25) were constructed to assess cross-domain integration. Women with chronic illness demonstrated lower PL-competence (moderate ES) and higher PL-confidence and PL-knowledge, as well as higher moderate-to-vigorous PA (all moderate ES). No significant differences were observed in BMI, fat mass, skeletal muscle mass, or visceral fat. Prior to correction, PA showed stronger negative associations with fat mass (r=−0.54 vs. 0.11) and visceral fat (r=−0.55 vs. 0.04) in women without-, compared to women with-chronic-illness. Network analysis indicated reduced cross-domain integration between PA and BC in the chronic-illness group. Chronic illness in older women appears to modify the structural relationships among PL, PA, and BC rather than uniformly reducing their levels. The attenuated coupling between PA and BC suggests partial behavioral–physiological decoupling in the presence of chronic disease.

papers.title: Connecting Young Minds (CYM) 2025 Undergraduate Research Conference: 5-Minute Scientific Research Presentations
papers.authors: Grace L. Tongue, Rachel Y. Pang, Jordan J. Yin, Nuha Khan, Maxime Laniel, Gabrielle Yuen-Wong, Omid Yeganeh, Tiana Yuen
papers.journal: Undergraduate Research in Natural and Clinical Science and Technology (URNCST) Journal
papers.abstract: Connecting Young Minds (CYM) is the University of Ottawa’s largest bilingual undergraduate Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) research conference dedicated to advancing student-led scientific innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and research communication. Organized by students, CYM provides undergraduate researchers with a platform to present original research and proposals through 5-minute scientific presentations followed by question-and-answer periods evaluated by expert judges. In 2025, the conference introduced poster presentations, enabling students to further engage with judges, keynote speakers, researchers, and attendees through interactive scientific discussion. The conference featured diverse projects spanning health sciences, engineering, natural sciences, artificial intelligence, environmental sciences, and biotechnology, reflecting the interdisciplinary nature of modern STEM research. Beyond the conference, CYM organized multiple fundraising initiatives supporting undergraduate scientific research, raising over CA$50,000, while its scientific outreach initiatives generated more than 2,000,000 social media views. Across all CYM events in 2025, over 800 attendees participated, including more than 300 attendees at this fully booked conference. As the University of Ottawa’s leading bilingual undergraduate STEM research conference, CYM continues to foster scientific engagement and innovation among emerging researchers. Abstracts in this booklet were submitted by participants on a volunteer basis.

papers.title: Analysis of fine-tuned foundation interatomic potentials and their knowledge distillation into a cluster expansion for Ni–Pt ordering thermodynamics
papers.authors: Jungjae Hwang, Jaejun Lee, Channyung Lee, Elif Ertekin, Kyoungmin Min
papers.abstract: Predicting alloy ordering thermodynamics requires the energies of thousands of atomic arrangements at fixed composition, far more than density functional theory (DFT) can routinely provide. Fine-tuned foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are a promising alternative, but whether they resolve the small energy differences between arrangements has not been established. Here, we examine this for fcc Ni–Pt in three steps. First, six foundation MLIPs fine-tuned on the same DFT data are evaluated on a 64-structure DFT benchmark. All six reach low global errors (2-20 meV/atom), but these errors are dominated by a composition-dependent offset that cancels between arrangements of one composition. We therefore evaluate the configurational energy Econf, the energy of a structure relative to the other structures of the same composition. After relaxation only four models reproduce DFT Econf (R2conf = 0.93-0.94), whereas fine-tuned eqV2 and CHGNet do not (0.48 and 0.37). Second, we locate the source of this failure. Linear probes on the frozen embeddings of all six models recover EconfDFT (R2 = 0.87 to 0.98), showing that the learned representations are intact. The accuracy is lost during relaxation: through the cell response of eqV2 and through inaccurate forces near the energy minimum in CHGNet. Third, we use the most accurate model, fine-tuned eqV3, as a teacher for knowledge distillation into a cluster expansion. Trained on 6,434 MLIP energies instead of 64 DFT energies, the distilled cluster expansion reduces the held-out DFT error from 4.43 to 2.79 meV/atom and reproduces the DFT-based transition temperatures within 167 K, comparable to the 120 K statistical uncertainty of the DFT-trained expansion itself. These results establish when fine-tuned foundation MLIPs can be trusted for alloy ordering and provide a route for transferring their accuracy to thermodynamic simulations.

papers.title: Exploring Open Science Through AI: A Student Research Journey - UPDATED FILES
papers.authors: Christin Monroe
papers.abstract: This assignment guides students through researching an open science resource and incorporating AI as a learning partner in their exploration. It begins with a midterm planning stage where students select an open science platform or dataset, define research questions, outline their approach, and reflect on initial AI use. The final deliverable is a creative presentation structured around flexible prompts that highlight the project’s focus, significance, research insights, process, and key takeaways, along with reflections on responsible AI integration and future directions. The goal is to foster critical thinking about open science practices while encouraging innovative, transparent, and accessible approaches to using AI in scientific inquiry.
