papers.title: Confidence at the crossroads: A systematic review of AI literacy, parental influence, and self-confidence in students’ career choice
papers.authors: Hafid Fadilah, Isma Widiaty, Ahmad Satibi, Kennedy Barfi Yaw Agyeibi
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping labour markets, positioning AI literacy as an understudied antecedent of students’ career choice alongside established influences such as parental support and self-confidence. This systematic review mapped the trends, theoretical frameworks, measurement instruments, and analytical methods linking these constructs and asked whether they had been examined jointly. Following PRISMA 2020 and a retrospectively registered protocol (Open Science Framework; registration pending), a single Scopus search in July 2026, limited to English-language articles and reviews, returned 107 records; independent dual screening with third-reviewer adjudication of disagreements yielded 79 studies, each appraised for methodological quality (AXIS/JBI). Because the query required an explicit self-efficacy, self-confidence, or self-esteem term, all coverage findings were limited to studies that measured self-confidence. The evidence base was dominated by Social Cognitive Career Theory (43 of 79 studies, 54.4%; 55 of 79, 69.6%, for the wider social-cognitive family) and by structural equation modelling; self-confidence, chiefly career decision self-efficacy, mediated contextual effects in 33 of the 41 studies that specified a mediator. Parental influence appeared in 74 studies but AI literacy in only six, all from 2025–2026, and just one measured all four constructs together. Within this corpus, no study modelled AI literacy and parental influence jointly through self-confidence. The review consolidated the framework, validated instruments, and methods needed to test such an integrative model and delineated the specific gap it would fill, offering a foundation for confirmatory research and AI-literacy instruction in vocational (SMK/TVET) science and engineering education.

papers.title: Preventing weight gain in Higher Education students: a systematic review and a feasibility randomised controlled trial of daily self-weighing or mindfulness in undergraduate nursing students (DOMIN NO)
papers.authors: Paul Tierney
papers.abstract: Background The prevalence of obesity in the UK remains high and continues to rise. Undergraduate nursing students are at significant risk for weight gain. Despite this, few weight gain prevention interventions have targeted this group, and none have been evaluated in the UK. Stress is a well-recognised factor contributing to weight gain, and mindfulness interventions have demonstrated effectiveness in stress reduction. This thesis explores the feasibility and acceptability of two interventions: daily self-weighing and mindfulness training. Aims To assess the feasibility and acceptability of daily self-weighing and mindfulness interventions for preventing weight gain among first-year undergraduate nursing students, using a three-arm randomised controlled trial with embedded process evaluation. Systematic review and meta-analysis A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to evaluate interventions aimed at preventing weight gain among higher-education students. Following Cochrane guidance, six electronic databases (Embase, Medline, CENTRAL, CINAHL, PsycINFO, ERIC) were searched, resulting in the identification of 14 randomised controlled trials involving 3,149 participants. The interventions varied widely, and study quality was mixed with considerable heterogeneity. Meta-analyses showed small but statistically significant effects favouring interventions for both weight (−1.20 kg) and BMI (−0.22 kg/m²). All included studies were conducted in North America, highlighting the lack of UK-based evidence and supporting the rationale for the subsequent feasibility trial. Methods This pilot RCT was conducted at a single UK higher education institution, involving first-year undergraduate nursing students at the start of the academic year. Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio using block randomisation to one of three groups: self-weighing, mindfulness training, or control. The study duration was 14 weeks. The self-weighing intervention involved providing digital scales, offering brief habit formation advice, and encouraging daily weighing with weight diary recording. The mindfulness intervention consisted of four weekly, one-hour online group mindfulness training led by a certified mindfulness instructor, and daily mindfulness practice encouraged through email reminders. The control group received standard healthy eating advice consistent with national guidelines. Quantitative outcome measures included weight, BMI, weighing frequency, perceived stress, mindfulness, and self-regulation of eating behaviour. An embedded qualitative process evaluation was conducted, including semi-structured interviews with participants, analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings A total of 33 first-year nursing students were recruited and successfully randomised in equal numbers (n=11) to the self-weighing, mindfulness, or control groups. Despite successful randomisation, the study faced challenges, including a 21.2% attrition rate at the first follow-up and complete loss to follow-up by the second follow-up point. Adherence to both self-weighing and mindfulness interventions was low. Nine participants completed semi-structured interviews as part of the qualitative process evaluation. Reflexive thematic analysis generated seven key themes, five of which were common across both intervention groups, including “I know it’s important, but I didn’t think it would happen to me,” “Peer observation,” and the interconnected stress-related themes “It’s all down to stress,” “Financial strain,” and “Too busy.” Two unique themes were developed for each intervention arm: “Mindfulness is good, but I need permission” reflected the structural barriers encountered during clinical placements, while “I would forget, and the numbers would upset me” highlighted emotional and behavioural challenges associated with daily self-weighing. Conclusions Preventing weight gain among undergraduate nursing students is an important yet understudied issue. However, this pilot study revealed significant challenges related to recruitment, retention, and adherence, indicating that a full trial is currently unfeasible without major changes. More foundational research is required to better understand weight gain in this population before progressing to intervention evaluation. Future work should focus on developing risk prediction tools, addressing structural and financial barriers, and tailoring interventions to the realities of students undertaking clinical placements with shift work, which present unique challenges, while incorporating stakeholder perspectives and socioeconomic considerations.

papers.title: Human-robot coordination during hand-over tasks in virtual reality
papers.authors: Róisín Rita Keenan
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in robotics have increased the integration of robotic systems into workplaces, necessitating effective human-robot collaboration. This thesis investigates human-robot coordination during handover tasks using Virtual Reality (VR) to analyze motor control and task dynamics across robot movement configurations. A behavioral study compared a repetitive pick-and-place task performed in physical and VR environments, establishing baseline differences. Results highlighted altered motor coordination timing and increased reliance on visual feedback in VR. Using a VR-based robot handover simulation, three studies explored human-robot interactions. The first study examined control modes and synchrony, showing improved pickup efficiency when robots initiated task onset. Minimum jerk trajectories facilitated smoother interactions, particularly when visual trajectory cues were available before participants’ forward motion. The second study focused on integrating biological motion into robot kinematics through two experiments. The first compared human and robot virtual partners, finding superior final end-effector control when interacting with human partners, especially for elevated elbow positions that emphasized joint kinematics. The second experiment analyzed robot velocity profiles—minimum jerk, constant velocity, constant acceleration, and biphasic. Results demonstrated strong benefits of minimum jerk trajectories, enhanced by early visual motion cues and a deceleration phase during movement. The third study investigated the timing of rotational movements during robot translation, comparing early, synchronized, and late rotations. Findings indicated that early or synchronized rotations enabled smoother handovers, while late rotations adversely affected coordination, emphasizing the importance of early visual orientation information. Overall, the thesis findings indicate that differences in task dynamics and movement configurations have large effects on human-robot coordination throughout the entirety of the task, the potential applications and implications of these insights are discussed, with directions for future research in this area outlined.

papers.title: Machine learning and electroencephalography for enhanced learning in human-computer interaction
papers.authors: Thomas Simpson
papers.abstract: Human-computer interaction has become fundamental to modern society. Improvements in this field have extensive potential across a number of important application domains, such as the capacity to augment human efficiency in the industry sector, evolve technology consumption in recreational settings, and transform learning environments in education. A successful human-computer interface requires a complex synthesis of multiple sophisticated technologies. Despite a rich and diverse corpus of literature that investigates various components and approaches, there are many elements under exploited. In particular, electroencephalography and machine learning are powerful tools that can assist computer interpretation of human behaviour and amplify communication protocols more generally. This thesis looks at different techniques for leveraging electroencephalography and machine learning in human-computer interaction to improve pedagogical technology, utilising driving as a training scenario. The work investigates the relationships between neurological features, learning, memory, and task performance; making effective predictions of vehicle trajectory based on participant behaviour data; and explaining neural networks to elevate transparency of computer reasoning. Multiple contributions are made in these research areas. Specifically, the P300 is demonstrated as a marker of working memory in virtual training environments, extending understanding of this neural response. Then, delta and theta band activity are demonstrated as modulating with different aspects of driving performance, allowing improvements in behavioural analysis. Furthermore, integrating neurological data into time series recurrent neural networks is verified as a valid technique for improving vehicle trajectory predictions. Finally, a contribution is made to the AI explanation literature, whereby the genetic algorithm is implemented to explain video classifiers.

papers.title: ChatGPT jako narzędzie we współczesnej praktyce dydaktycznej
papers.authors: Milena Miałkowska-Kozaryna, Diana Aksamit
papers.abstract: The study examines the growing presence of generative artificial intelligence in education and focuses on teachers' perceptions of ChatGPT as a support tool in the teaching and learning process. The development of AI is transforming teaching practices by enabling content personalisation, the creation of educational materials, and more efficient lesson preparation; at the same time, it raises questions about the reliability of generated content, ethical considerations, and teachers' digital competencies. In the context of the specific characteristics of the Polish education system—an ageing workforce, the feminisation of the profession, and the outflow of young teachers—the implementation of technological innovations may be uneven. The study aims to explore teachers’ familiarity with ChatGPT, its use in their daily practice, and the barriers and concerns associated with its adoption. The findings contribute to the discussion on the responsible integration of AI in education and indicate directions for teachers’ professional development.

papers.authors: Milena Miałkowska-Kozaryna, Diana Aksamit

papers.title: Wykorzystanie narzędzi sztucznej inteligencji przez rodziców małych dzieci – poczucie rodzicielskiej skuteczności i kwestie etyczne
papers.authors: Katarzyna Ziębakowska-Cecot, Dorota Szymborska
papers.abstract: This article examines the use of AI tools in everyday caregiving and educational practices by parents of young children (aged 0–6 years); N=103. The aim of the study was to understand the extent of AI use in family life, the perception of benefits and concerns associated with it, and factors differentiating the use of AI. A survey questionnaire and the Generalized Self-Efficacy Scale (GSES) were used. The study identified two groups of parents: AI users (45.6%) and non-users (44.4%). Respondents most often use AI incidentally and task-based. These tools are primarily used to generate ideas for activities, explain difficult issues, and support daily organization; however, they do not translate into a reduction in parents' time burden. Respondents express concerns about the effectiveness of privacy protection when using AI. Parents who do not use AI tools attribute this to a lack of need, a lack of trust in the credibility of generated content, and a lack of data protection. Some express a willingness to use AI. The level of self-efficacy does not differentiate between AI users and non-users. The research results allowed us to formulate a thesis about the selective openness of parents towards AL and practical recommendations in the area of supporting families in developing digital competences.

papers.title: The use of artificial intelligence tools by parents of young children – parental self-efficacy and ethical issues
papers.authors: Katarzyna Ziębakowska-Cecot, Dorota Szymborska

papers.title: Phenotypic Variability of Body Composition in Men Adjusted for Body Mass Index and Body Fat Percentage
papers.authors: Laura Hačková, Martina Gažarová, Petra Lenártová
papers.journal: Acta fytotechnica et zootechnica/Acta fytotechnica  et zootechnica
papers.abstract: Obesity represents major health and social problem, and in clinical practice, its assessment is based primarily on body mass index (BMI). This index is practical and widely used, but it has certain limitations which, especially in men, can lead to incorrect classification. The aim of the study was to evaluate the body composition of a group of 201 men in terms of several anthropometric indices adjusted for body mass index and body fat percentage (PBF), and five phenotypes were defined. BMI was unable to distinguish between phenotypes with different body composition within the same weight category, such as the phenotypes normal weight obesity (NWO) and normal weight without obesity (NWWO). Both groups were defined as normal weight by BMI, but NWO had higher PBF, VFL, and WC compared to NWWO (P < 0.05). The phenotypes overweight obesity (OWO) and overweight without obesity (OWWO) were also evaluated similarly. OWO had significantly higher fat mass than OWWO (P < 0.05). An interesting contrast was observed between the NWO and OWO phenotypes, as their fat mass indices did not differ significantly. In contrast, significant differences were found in the fat-free mass indices (P < 0.05). These findings suggest that based on BMI alone, the NWO phenotype would be considered non-risk without further specification, although its fat mass is comparable to the morbid obesity of the OWO phenotype. Increased fat mass is associated with cardiometabolic risk, which is exacerbated when accompanied by low muscle mass, representing a particularly adverse phenotype with higher morbidity and mortality. Therefore, the assessment of obesity should also be based on body composition indices and not solely on BMI.

papers.title: La Justicia Social en Educación: Nuevos Desafíos para un Concepto en Transformación
papers.authors: Francisco Javier Murillo
papers.journal: REICE Revista Iberoamericana sobre Calidad Eficacia y Cambio en Educación
papers.abstract: The concept of social justice in education needs to be updated to address present-day transformations without losing the critical force of its foundational traditions. This article proposes a conceptual framework that retains the distributive, recognition, and political-participatory dimensions while incorporating two additional demands: the epistemic and the relational. Alongside these dimensions, it distinguishes three transversal axes—time, territory, and intersectionality—that reconstruct how injustices are formed, inherited, situated, and given specific configurations. The framework is examined against four scenarios: the ecological crisis; artificial intelligence and the transformation of knowledge; migration, borders, and segregation; and democratic erosion and exclusionary discourses. The proposal rests on a demanding criterion: any expansion of the concept must demonstrate its irreducibility, analytical gain, clarity of level, and educational fecundity. Its contribution lies in distinguishing which demands of justice are being violated, how injustices take concrete form, and against which contemporary conflicts the framework must demonstrate its explanatory capacity. The framework seeks to strengthen the capacity of education, research, and policy to recognise relations of power, avoid reductive diagnoses, and guide responses capable of transforming the conditions that produce and reproduce injustice.

papers.title: Magnifica Humanitas de León XIV: Apuntes bíblico-teológicos
papers.authors: Hanzel José Zúñiga Valerio
papers.abstract: This text expands upon the inaugural lecture delivered in the Clodomiro Picado Twight Auditorium at the National University (UNA) as part of a series of reflections on the Encyclical Letter Magnifica Humanitas by the Bishop of Rome, Leo XIV, concerning the human being in the age of the scientific-technical revolution and Artificial Intelligence (AI). After situating the discussion within the anthropological, rather than the technological, sphere, some general elements of the encyclical are outlined, and the “grammar” of understanding the Church’s Social Doctrine that it contains is explained. Furthermore, in-depth biblical-theological observations are made regarding the uses and abuses of the biblical text, disparate philosophical interpretations of the Augustinian dualism employed, and the importance of the “development” or “evolution” of the theological understanding of dogma in the field of Christian anthropology is discussed.

papers.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence & Bioinformatics to Teach Phylogeny & Biodiversity in Introductory Biology
papers.authors: Erica F. Kosal
papers.abstract: The following activity introduces introductory college and AP high school biology students to the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and bioinformatics tools for studying biodiversity and phylogenetic relationships. Students select a taxonomic group (e.g., insects, fungi, amphibians) and utilize an AI image recognition tool (Google Lens) to quickly identify a set of species, bypassing traditional, time-consuming identification keys. The identified species are then copied into a public bioinformatics resource (phyloT) that utilizes the established National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Taxonomy database and algorithms to rapidly generate an evolutionary tree (cladogram).

papers.title: The application value of artificial intelligence in medical imaging: foundations, progress, and challenges
papers.authors: Hongzan Sun, Yushan Zhang, Yu Shi, Bing Ji, Chen Li, Jiajia Yang, Marcin Grzegorzek, 郭启勇
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming medical imaging, reshaping the field as it does everyday life. As imaging data grow in complexity and clinical workloads continue to rise, AI has become increasingly essential for improving diagnostic efficiency and precision. However, despite these technical advances, the clinical adoption of AI in medical imaging remains fragmented, with limited generalizability, insufficient interpretability, and unclear clinical responsibility. In this review, we critically examine the evolution of AI in medical imaging, with a particular focus on its functional roles across the imaging workflow and its actual contributions to contemporary clinical needs. We systematically analyze current application paradigms, identify methodological and translational bottlenecks, and discuss emerging strategies to improve model robustness, interpretability, and clinical integration. In addition, we identify key barriers to the practical implementation of AI in medical imaging, including challenges related to cross-domain generalizability, data privacy issues and regulatory compliance. By examining these opportunities and challenges, this review aims to guide future research directions and foster deeper interdisciplinary collaboration among AI, clinical medicine, and biomedical engineering.

papers.title: From data literacy to AI-integrated Laboratory 4.0
papers.authors: Jakob Adler, Böhm Johannes
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Laboratory medicine is undergoing a profound transformation towards a completely digitized and connected “Laboratory 4.0” driven by advances in laboratory automation, interoperability, and artificial intelligence. At the same time, it also faces challenges such as declining funding, a shortage of qualified laboratory professionals, increasing workforce constraints, and regulatory requirements. Digital competence thus becomes a crucial skill for addressing these challenges.

papers.title: Minimal-Input Deep Learning for Remote Screening of REM Sleep Behavior Disorder
papers.authors: Khrystyna Semkiv, Walter Karlen
papers.abstract: Abstract This work investigates whether a deep learning model with minimal inputs can accurately identify Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavioral Disorder (RBD). We propose an interpretable two-step approach using two convolutional neural networks for sleep staging and RBD classification. Experiments on data from 18 RBD participants and 178 healthy controls demonstrate that reliable classification can be achieved using frontal electroencephalogram (EEG) and electrooculogram (EOG) input signals. GradCAM attention reveals a 22% increase in importance in the 9-22 Hz band of EOG for RBD cases. Our findings highlight the potential for remote, wearable-based RBD screening at home.

papers.title: ROCKMIND: Multimodal neurophysiological assessment of grip force control and fatigue in sport climbing
papers.authors: Lorenzo Semeia, Tim Brümmer, Philipp Bulling, Mohamed Taher Idell, Anh Zoe Nguyen, Thomas Klotz, Oliver Röhrle, Justus Carl Marquetand
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction. Sport climbing performance critically depends on sustaining submaximal grip forces under fatigue while maintaining precise force control. From a neurophysiological perspective, this process requires coordinated recruitment of motor units in the forearm musculature and effective corticospinal control originating in motor cortical areas. Despite the importance of these mechanisms for force regulation and fatigue, the neurophysiology of sustained gripping in climbing remains insufficiently understood. Hangboard training represents a central component of climbing-specific training. These exercises involve repeated or sustained isometric contractions using body weight and induce controlled loading of the forearm musculature. Importantly, hangboard tasks provide a highly standardized and experimentally tractable paradigm, making them well-suited for investigating neuromuscular and neural mechanisms of grip force control. Methods. The ROCKMIND project introduces a multimodal experimental framework combining high-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG) of the forearm musculature, electroencephalography (EEG), and force measurements during standardized hangboard tasks to investigate peripheral and central mechanisms of force control and fatigue. Ninety participants will be stratified according to the International Rock Climbing Research Association (IRCRA) reporting scale into non-climbers, recreational climbers (IRCRA 10-17 men, 10-14 women), and elite climbers (IRCRA >24 men, >21 women). Participants will perform controlled isometric grip contractions (finger flexion) on the hangboard at 20%, 35%, and 50% of their maximal voluntary contraction. Results. Preliminary measurements in one participant using HD-sEMG of the forearm musculature show the feasibility of the hangboard setup and reflect clear fatigue-related changes in electromyographic activity during sustained contractions. EEG acquisition and corticomuscular coherence analyses will be performed as part of the ongoing study. Conclusion. The preliminary findings support the feasibility of the proposed methodology for investigating grip force control and fatigue in sport climbing. By examining how grip force is maintained and how control strategies change as a function of fatigue and climbing expertise, the project aims to identify neurophysiological markers relevant for performance assessment and training monitoring.

papers.title: The Radiology Sparring Partner: A PoC Study of Multi-Agentic Workflows for Clinical Decision Support and Teaching
papers.authors: Jonas Schewior, Mohamed Ashfaq Anwerdeen, Birim Ertürk, Oliver Grösser, Ingo Siegert, Maciej Pech, Andreas Wendemuth
papers.abstract: Abstract Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into radiology is often hindered by the inability of monolithic architectures to balance clinical reasoning with pedagogical safety. This study evaluates MedGemma-27B-IT across two specialized agentic frameworks: a clinical "Radiology Sparring Partner" and a "Socratic Teacher". For clinical decision support, we compared three architectures: Raw (base model output, no prompt), Minimal Prompted (single-shot prompt), and Multi-Agentic, using a 4-stage pipeline for clinical synthesis. Separately, the educational track employs a dual-agent architecture for progressive educational scaffolding. A pooled evaluation of 120 interaction transcripts (10 per architecture with three independent LLM-as-a-judge runs) was finalized using an expert-anchored combined mean approach, anchored via Bühlmann credibility calibration against radiologist-authored references (5 per architecture). Results demonstrate that agentic orchestration outperforms monolithic baselines in high-level reasoning. Most notably, Pathophysiological Logic scores rose from 3.20 (Raw) to 4.14 (Agentic) on a 5-point Likert scale, with a simultaneous reduction in standard deviation from 1.23 to 0.70. While this Proof of Concept (PoC) highlights the advantages of modularity, results remain subject to evaluator formulation bias and a measurable "latency tax" inherent in sequential agent hand-offs. Future work will focus on longitudinal clinical validation and optimization of cached memory architectures to refine reasoning depth while mitigating latency.

papers.title: Designing Trust, Autonomy, and Acceptance in AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems: A Comparative Experimental Analysis
papers.authors: Sophia Ackerhans, Carsten Schultz
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems (AI CDSS) have the potential to improve clinical decision-making and patient outcomes, yet their adoption remains limited. Prior research highlights trust in AI and concerns about professional autonomy as key barriers to implementation. While explainability and system integration may foster trust, they may simultaneously threaten professional identity and decision authority. At the same time, perceived usefulness has been identified as the central driver of technology acceptance, although it is shaped by autonomyrelated concerns, particularly among physicians. This study integrates two experimental investigations (1,2) to examine how AI-CDSS design features jointly influence trust, autonomy-related perceptions, and acceptance across patients and physicians. Methods: The analysis combines and compares findings from two vignette-based experimental studies. The first study (n = 292) employs a 2 × 2 × 2 factorial design manipulating AI explainability, workflow integration, and accountability to assess their effects on trust and professional identity threat among physicians. The second study consists of three experiments across patients (n = 209), potential future users (n = 1062), and physicians (n = 185), manipulating AI-CDSS system type (hybrid vs. autonomous) and recommendation risk (lifestyle vs. medical) (2 x 2 factorial design). Regression-based mediation and sequential mediation models (SPSS PROCESS Macro) were applied using bootstrapping procedures. Results: Results from the first study show that explainability and workflow integration significantly increase trust in AI-CDSS. At the same time, explainability and system-induced accountability increase perceived professional identity threat. Trust is negatively associated with identity threat and partially mediates the relationship between explainability and identity threat, indicating that trust can mitigate but not fully offset these concerns. Results from the second study demonstrate that perceived usefulness is the strongest predictor of intention to use among both patients, potential future users, and physicians. However, the underlying mechanisms differ. Patients and potential future users evaluate AI-CDSS primarily based on perceived usefulness, whereas physicians’ evaluations depend on professional autonomy preservation. For physicians, hybrid systems increase intention to use only indirectly through reduced professional autonomy concerns and increased perceived usefulness. High-risk medical recommendations consistently increase perceived or anticipated professional autonomy concerns across all groups but do not directly reduce perceived usefulness or intention to use. Conclusion: AI-CDSS acceptance is shaped by the interplay of trust, perceived usefulness, and professional autonomy-related concerns. Design features exhibit ambivalent effects, simultaneously enabling and constraining adoption. Successful implementation requires aligning system design with professional expectations, particularly by preserving physician decision authority while demonstrating clear clinical value.

papers.title: A Comparative Study of Human and AI Assessment in Japanese Sakubun Writing
papers.authors: Jeni Putra, Masashi Umemoto, Susi Widianti, Novia Hayati, Muthi Afifah
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: This study compares the assessment of Japanese sakubun by a native Japanese teacher and two large language model based AI tools, Gemini AI (3.1) and ChatGPT (5.5), and examines the extent to which AI generated scores align with human assessment. The data comprised eight sakubun texts on the theme of meiwaku (inconvenience) written by second year students with approximately JLPT N4 level Japanese proficiency. Each sakubun was assessed using the same rubric covering four dimensions: content, organization, expression, and accuracy, as well as an overall score. The scores were descriptively compared across the three evaluators at both the criterion and overall levels. The results showed that the Japanese teacher assigned the highest average overall score of 16.25, followed by Gemini AI with 14.25 and ChatGPT with 13.75. Of the two AI tools, Gemini AI demonstrated closer overall alignment with the teacher’s assessment. Both AI systems also exhibited a score compression tendency. Higher quality sakubuns were generally evaluated lower than by the teacher, whereas some lower quality sakubuns received relatively higher scores. The most substantial discrepancies were observed in content and expression, indicating that AI assessment was less sensitive to idea development, contextual appropriateness, naturalness of expression, and subtle linguistic nuances. These findings suggest that although Gemini AI and ChatGPT can provide useful supplementary assessment, human evaluator judgment remains essential, particularly for evaluating qualitative and context sensitive aspects of Japanese writing.

papers.title: นวตกรรมการจดการอาหารสวนเกนดวยการสรางคณคาการมสวนรวม ดานสงแวดลอมในชมชน จงหวดนนทบร
papers.authors: นภเกตน์ สายสมบัติ
papers.journal: Journal of Academic for Public and Private Management
papers.abstract: This research aimed to investigate the factors affecting surplus food management through environmental value co-creation and community participation in Nonthaburi Province. A mixed-methods approach was employed. The quantitative phase involved 447 household food managers, and data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation, and stepwise multiple regression. The qualitative phase included in-depth interviews with 15 purposively selected key informants. Findings showed that the perception of food surplus management (β = 0.367), community and social factors (β = 0.447), and motivation (β = 0.254) significantly influenced management behavior, accounting for 73.0% of variance (R² = 0.730). Innovation in surplus food management was also significantly influenced by four predictors—perception, behavior, attitude, and motivation—explaining 50.1% of variance (R² = 0.501). Key barriers included a lack of knowledge, limited technology access, and insufficient incentives. However, strong community networks played a critical role in promoting sustainable behavior. The study highlights the importance of integrating community participation and environmental awareness into public policy and local innovation to improve household-level food waste management. Findings can support policymaking and practical models in urbanizing areas across Thailand.

papers.title: AI Agents as Policy Instruments in Education: Reducing School Abandonment through Adaptive Governance Systems
papers.authors: Florina Bran, Dumitru-Alexandru Bodislav, Liviu Purcărea, Amelia Diaconu
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes the deployment of AI agents within national education strategies aimed at improving learning outcomes and reducing early school abandonment. It conceptualizes AI agents not only as educational technologies, but as policy instruments capable of reshaping governance, resource allocation, and early-warning mechanisms in public education systems. The study focuses on the use of AI agents for student risk detection, personalized learning pathways, administrative burden reduction, and real-time policy feedback loops. Drawing on policy design and socio-economic analysis, the paper highlights how AI agents can identify structural drivers of dropout, such as poverty, regional inequality, and institutional rigidity, earlier and more accurately than traditional administrative tools. At the same time, it examines key risks related to data bias, algorithmic labeling of vulnerable students, and the potential reinforcement of socio-economic stratification. The paper proposes a governance framework for educational AI agents based on transparency, pedagogical alignment, and social safeguards, ensuring that automation complements rather than replaces human judgment. The central argument is that AI agents, when embedded in inclusive and accountable policy architectures, can function as preventive governance mechanisms, shifting education policy from reactive remediation to proactive social investment. Keywords: Artificial intelligence agents; education policy; school abandonment; early warning systems; personalized learning; public sector digitalization; social inequality

papers.title: Building the Educational Foundation for Sustainable Digital Governance: A Survey of AI and Public Administration Competencies among Romanian Students
papers.authors: Sorin Burlacu, Carmen Valentina Radulescu, IOAN I. GÂF-DEAC, Ion Pârgaru
papers.abstract: The accelerated digital transformation of public administration and the emergence of regulations on artificial intelligence require the redefinition of the skills needed by future civil servants in relation to the demands of sustainable digital governance. Although literature analyzes institutional digitalization and administrative capacity, there is a gap regarding the systematic assessment of students’ preparation for the integration of AI, data-driven skills and the ethical dimension in the context of sustainable development. The study aims to assess the perceived level of preparation and skills gaps among students in the field of Public Administration and Environmental Economics in Romania, with a focus on advanced digital skills, AI literacy, administrative skills and transversal skills. The methodology consists of an online questionnaire applied to students from bachelor’s and master’s degree programs analyzed through descriptive statistics, comparative tests between groups and regression models to identify the relationships between skills, institutional trust and the intention to use AI in the public sector. Preliminary results indicate significant differences between study levels and highlight gaps in applied AI skills and algorithmic governance. The added value lies in integrating the educational dimension into the debate on sustainable digital governance, contributing to the substantiation of curricular reform and the alignment of administrative education with the European sustainable development agenda. Limitations concern the transversal nature of the research and the use of self-assessment of skills. Future directions include international comparative extension and the integration of mixed methods for in-depth validation. Keywords: survey, AI, public administration, competencies

papers.title: Strengthening the Practice Pillar of Sustainable Development: A Survey-Based Assessment of AI, Digital and Leadership Competencies among Romanian Public Servants
papers.authors: Carmen Valentina Radulescu, IOAN I. GÂF-DEAC, Sorin Burlacu, Victor Adrian Troacă
papers.abstract: The acceleration of the digital transformation of public administration in Romania, supported by the reforms undertaken by the new European regulations on artificial intelligence, requires the strengthening of institutional capacity and the skills of civil servants in relation to the sustainable development objectives. Although the specialized literature addresses digitalization and algorithmic governance, there is a gap regarding the empirical assessment of the real skills and training needs of civil servants in the context of AI implementation and skills-based reform. The study aims to analyze the level of training and existing gaps in the field of advanced digital skills, AI literacy, cybersecurity, administrative skills and leadership skills in the Romanian public sector. The methodology consists of an online questionnaire applied to civil servants in central and local administration, complemented by comparative analyses between executive and management functions and regression models to identify the relationship between skills, confidence in the use of AI and the perceived capacity to implement digital reforms. The results highlight significant differences between hierarchical levels, as well as gaps in strategic competencies regarding algorithmic governance and change management. The added value lies in the empirical substantiation of the practical dimension of sustainable development, by correlating individual competencies with the institutional capacity to implement responsible digitalization. The study contributes to the literature on sustainable digital governance and provides recommendations for public policies and training programs. Limitations concern the self-reported nature of the data and the cross-sectional design of the research. Future directions include longitudinal analyses and comparative extension at the European level. Keywords: AI, digital competencies, leadership competencies

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Crisis Counseling: Opportunities, Risks, and Ethical Challenges of Social and Psychological Practice
papers.authors: Анастасія Бессараб, Анастасія Володимирівна Турубарова, Marharyta KUDINOVA, Катерина Сергіївна Червоненко, Mariia Kanibolotska
papers.abstract: The modern development of artificial intelligence, in particular large language models and chatbots, opens up new opportunities for crisis counseling, but at the same time generates significant clinical and ethical risks. The article is aimed at a systematic analysis of the opportunities, risks and ethical challenges of using artificial intelligence in crisis counseling in the context of social and psychological practice. A systematic scoping review of the literature was carried out according to the recommendations of the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews. A structured search in the Scopus database for the period 2020–2026 allowed the identification of 556 documents, from which the most relevant sources were selected for high-quality thematic synthesis and bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer. The results demonstrate the significant potential of artificial intelligence in increasing the availability of care, early detection of suicidal risk, personalized interventions, and hybrid “artificial intelligence + specialist” models. At the same time, serious risks have been identified: inadequate responses in suicidal crises, anthropomorphization, emotional dependence (especially among adolescents), hallucinations and cultural prejudices. Ethical challenges include issues of responsibility, privacy, digital divide, algorithm explainability, and trust in technology. The data obtained indicate the ambivalent nature of the impact of artificial intelligence on the field of mental health. Secure integration requires a strong regulatory framework, mandatory human oversight, further empirical research, and the development of national ethical standards, especially in post-conflict societies such as Ukraine. Keywords: artificial intelligence, crisis counseling, suicidal prevention, large language models, ethical challenges, digital mental health, hybrid models of care

papers.title: Protocol for the REVELIO test-track pilot study: A randomised, controlled, single-centre trial in healthy recreational cannabis users investigating real-time in-vehicle detection of cannabis-impaired driving
papers.authors: Robin Deuber, Michal Bechný, Christoph Heck, Joel Brügger, Matthias Pfäffli, Mia Jovanova, Elgar Fleisch, Felix Wortmann, Wolfgang Weinmann
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Driving under the influence of cannabis is associated with impaired cognitive and psychomotor performance and an increased risk of traffic accidents. Reliable real-time in-vehicle systems for detecting cannabis-related driving impairment are currently lacking; but hold great potential for improving road safety. METHODS: This protocol describes the REVELIO test-track pilot study: a randomised, controlled, open-label, interventional, single-centre trial. The study assesses the feasibility and methodological requirements for developing and evaluating a multimodal in-vehicle detection approach using vehicle and driver state data. A total of 45 healthy recreational cannabis users will be enrolled and randomly allocated to an intervention or a reference control group. During the main study day, all participants will undergo biological sampling for tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and related metabolites, as well as pre-driving assessments, followed by a sober baseline driving session on a closed test track using a dual-pedal vehicle with a certified driving instructor onboard. Participants in the intervention group will then receive a single controlled inhalative cannabis dose (target 0.67 mg THC per kg body weight), while the reference group will receive no cannabis. All participants will subsequently complete three additional standardized 50-minute driving sessions at predefined time points up to approximately six hours after administration, following identical schedules to enable within- and between-group comparisons. Between driving sessions, structured breaks will include recovery periods, repeated biological sampling, and traffic-medical, traffic-psychological, and pre-driving performance assessments, to characterise the temporal dynamics of cannabis-related impairment. DISCUSSION: Multimodal data will be collected, including vehicle controller area network (CAN) data, driver monitoring camera (DMC) data, physiological signals using wearables, and biological samples (capillary blood, breath, oral fluid. Machine-learning-based models will be developed and evaluated to distinguish sober from cannabis-influenced driving states under controlled conditions. Secondary analyses will examine changes in driving performance over time and associations between functional measures and biological THC concentrations. As an exploratory pilot study conducted on a secured test track, the protocol aims to generate standardized reference data and quantitative performance metrics to inform both feasibility and system design considerations. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07401628).

papers.title: Near-optimal P300 speller performance using large language models: A multi-model analysis with performance bounds
papers.authors: Nithin Parthasarathy, Nithin Parthasarathy, James Soetedjo, Saarang Panchavati, Nitya Parthasarathy, Nitya Parthasarathy, Dongwoo Lee, Corey Arnold, Nader Pouratian, William Speier
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a progressive neurodegenerative disease, severely impairs communication, requiring assistive technologies that restore interaction. The P300 speller brain-computer interface (BCI) enables communication by translating EEG responses into text; however, its practical adoption is limited by slow typing speed and the need for subject-specific calibration. Recent work has demonstrated that large language models (LLMs), such as GPT-2, can significantly improve the performance of the P300 speller by predicting words. However, it remains unclear whether these gains are model-specific or represent a broader trend across language models. Furthermore, the framework-specific performance bounds of LLM-assisted P300 spellers have not been systematically characterized within a unified decoding framework. In this study, we address these gaps through a systematic multi-model theoretical analysis framework. We evaluate a wide range of language models and introduce an idealized LLM to establish upper bounds on achievable performance. In addition, we incorporate cross-subject classifier training to reduce calibration requirements and assess generalization across subjects. Using extensive simulations on EEG data from 78 subjects, we demonstrate that the evaluated models consistently achieve substantial improvements in typing speed, with gains of up to ~45% (within-subject training) and ~75% (across-subject training) over conventional approaches. More importantly, we show that several high-performing models, despite architectural differences, operate within 5% of the theoretical performance bound, indicating diminishing returns from further model scaling. These improvements generalize across both within-subject and across-subject classifiers. Our results suggest that LLM-assisted P300 spellers are approaching oracle-based upper bounds within the considered decoding framework, shifting the primary bottleneck from language modeling to neural signal decoding. This work provides both a practical framework for improving BCI communication and a theoretical perspective on its achievable limits.

papers.title: Co-Creating Hybrid Corn: Innovation, Science and Farming in Galicia, Northwest Iberian Peninsula, 1921–36
papers.authors: Alberto González Remuiñán, Roque Sanfiz Arias, Lourenzo Fernández Prieto, Dulce Freire
papers.abstract: abstract: Histories of hybrid corn have largely been written through the American experience of scientific breeding and the commercialization of hybrid seed. This article argues that the early European development of hybrid corn followed a different trajectory. Focusing on Galicia in northwestern Spain, it shows how international advances in genetics were adapted through sustained collaboration between researchers and farming communities. Drawing on the archives of the Galician Biological Mission and its fieldwork branch, the Seed Producers Trade Union, the article demonstrates that farmers' knowledge shaped breeding decisions, cultivation practices, and systems of seed production and distribution. Rather than portraying innovation as the one-way transfer of scientific expertise, the Galician case reveals a model of scientific co-creation in which public institutions, international research networks, and local agricultural communities jointly produced Europe's first double hybrid corn. In doing so, the article offers an alternative history of agricultural innovation before World War II.

papers.title: Focus: New Questions for Kranzberg's Laws
papers.authors: Amy Sue Bix
papers.abstract: abstract: Melvin Kranzberg's 1986 "laws" have long served as touchstones for historians of technology, offering provocations for thinking about the complex relationships between technology and society. Forty years later, the field has expanded dramatically through global perspectives, gender history, environmental history, histories of maintenance and failure, and new studies of computing and artificial intelligence. Reflecting on both the fortieth anniversary of Kranzberg's laws and the fiftieth anniversary of Women in Technological History (WITH), this essay argues that the laws remain remarkably productive points of departure for teaching and historical inquiry. Drawing on classroom experience and recent scholarship, it shows how Kranzberg's insights can be reconsidered alongside questions of gender, equity, power, and historical contingency. Read against the field's subsequent transformations, the laws remain useful not as settled principles but as prompts for asking new questions about technology and historical change.

papers.title: Model-free control strategy of exoskeletons based on control barrier function
papers.authors: Gaowei ZHANG, Jiawei GAO, Jie WANG, Xi Vincent Wang, Sanbo DING
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: In this study, we addressed the problem of trajectory tracking control for a two-degree-of-freedom wrist-joint upper-limb rehabilitation exoskeleton robot with unknown model information. A novel model-free prescribed-time control framework based on prescribed-time high-order control barrier functions is proposed. The developed approach simultaneously guarantees prescribed-time convergence and strict satisfaction of safety constraints without relying on an accurate dynamic model. In practical rehabilitation scenarios, obtaining an accurate dynamic model of the human–robot system is extremely difficult because of the complex physical interactions, significant parameter uncertainties, time-varying external disturbances, and variations in human parameters among different patients. To solve this problem, a second-order ultra-local model was constructed to describe the system dynamics. In this model, the uncertainties, external disturbances, and human–robot interaction torques are unified into a lumped disturbance term. Furthermore, radial basis function (RBF) neural networks are incorporated to estimate the lumped disturbances online in real time, enabling a fully model-free control implementation without requiring prior knowledge of system dynamics. Based on this formulation, a prescribed-time sliding-mode control strategy based on state transformation was designed to ensure that the desired motion trajectories are rapidly and stably tracked by the system states. Specifically, by utilizing the controller, the tracking errors between the states and described trajectories can be forced to zero within a predefined time bound, which can be explicitly assigned according to practical rehabilitation requirements. It should be noted that the convergence time is independent of the initial conditions, thereby ensuring uniform transient performance even when the system starts from different or unfavorable initial states. To enhance the safety of the rehabilitation training process further, a prescribed-time high-order control barrier function was constructed that explicitly incorporates safety constraints into the controller design. This formulation explicitly encodes the state constraints and guarantees that the system states are driven into the safe set within a prescribed time and remain there thereafter, even when starting from outside. In contrast to existing barrier Lyapunov function-based methods, the proposed approach relaxes the requirement of the initial conditions by allowing the system states to start outside the safe set and ensuring their convergence within a prescribed time. The optimal control law satisfying the safety constraints is solved by incorporating the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions. As a result, the proposed method ensures that the system states not only converge to the desired trajectories within the prescribed time but also enter and remain within the safe set in a guaranteed manner, achieving both transient safety and long-term forward invariance. The global stability of the closed-loop system and forward invariance of the safe set were rigorously established using the Lyapunov stability theory, providing strong theoretical guarantees for the proposed approach. Numerical simulation results were obtained to validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. The results demonstrate that the system states converge within the prescribed time bound, regardless of the initial conditions, even when the initial states lie outside the safe set. Comparative studies under sudden disturbances further highlight the superiority of the proposed control barrier function in terms of maintaining safety. In addition, compared with finite- and fixed-time control schemes, the proposed method not only accelerates the convergence process but also provides a flexible and user-defined convergence time.

papers.title: Polymer informatics: A review of ai-driven structure-property modeling and material design
papers.authors: Haiyan GONG, Jingzhi Yang, Annan Kong, Lingwei MA, Dawei ZHANG
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Polymer science is undergoing a profound paradigm shift from labor-intensive, empirical trial-and-error experimentation to AI-guided, data-driven, and predictive material design. Owing to their multiscale structural diversity (spanning atomic connectivity, chain-packing behavior, and macroscopic morphology), polymer materials possess an enormous chemical design space that traditional experimental and computational methods cannot efficiently explore. High-precision quantum-chemical calculations are too computationally expensive for large-scale screening, whereas classical molecular dynamics simulations often involve trade-offs between force-field accuracy and accessible time scales. Against this backdrop, polymer informatics has emerged as a transformative interdisciplinary field that leverages artificial intelligence algorithms to mine structure–property–processing relationships from accumulated experimental, simulation, and literature data, enabling accurate property prediction and on-demand inverse design of polymer materials. This Review systematically summarizes recent advances in AI-guided informatics for polymer science based on an analysis of representative literature published between 2023 and 2025. The survey covers the current state of polymer informatics across four interconnected dimensions, organized around the logical backbone of data foundation, property prediction, inverse design, interpretability, and physical constraints. In the domain of polymer representation and data strategies, we evaluate the essential differences and applicable boundaries of major representation methods, including SMILES-based variants (PSMILES, BigSMILES, and HAPPY), molecular graph representations (including the hierarchical polymer graph, HPG), and topology-based multi-cover persistence (MCP) descriptors. We further discuss data augmentation techniques and transfer learning strategies developed to address the critical challenge of scarce high-quality labeled data and highlight the growing trend of multi-representation fusion for capturing both local chemical environments and global topological features. In the domain of machine learning for polymer property prediction, we review models and strategies for predicting thermodynamic properties (e.g., glass transition temperature (Tg)), mechanical properties (tensile and flexural moduli), transport properties (gas permeability and diffusivity), electrical properties (dielectric constant, breakdown strength, and energy storage density), and functional service performance. In particular, we examine the complementary roles of graph neural networks (GNNs), Transformer-based architectures, large language models (e.g., PolyBERT, PolyNC), and multimodal learning frameworks in building accurate forward mappings from polymer structure to target properties and critically compare their performance-cost trade-offs. In the domain of generative models and inverse design, we discuss how variational autoencoders (VAEs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), reinforcement learning, and Bayesian optimization are integrated into closed-loop design frameworks that couple structure generation, property prediction, synthesizability evaluation, and experimental validation. We highlight emerging system-level approaches that move beyond single-objective generation toward multi-constraint, application-oriented polymer discovery, including de novo design of antimicrobial polymers, recyclable vitrimeric polymers, and high-performance dielectric materials. In the domain of model interpretability and physics-informed modeling, we review how attention mechanisms, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis, and physics-informed neural networks are being applied to transform AI models from opaque black boxes into scientifically interpretable tools that can provide chemical insights and respect fundamental physical laws (e.g., thermodynamic constraints and scaling laws). Finally, we identify key challenges and outline five future research directions: (1) polymer data standardization and the construction of unified, community-shared benchmark datasets; (2) coupled physicochemical process modeling that integrates molecular-scale predictions with manufacturing-scale simulations; (3) multi-scale modeling bridging atomistic, mesoscale, and macroscopic descriptions; (4) generative artificial intelligence for creative, beyond-training-distribution polymer discovery; and (5) application-oriented material design with explicit consideration of synthesizability, processability, recyclability, and lifecycle performance. This Review aims to provide comprehensive references and valuable insights for researchers working at the intersection of polymer science, materials informatics, and artificial intelligence.

papers.title: (Repositioning) AI as trickster in organizations for bias mitigation
papers.authors: Shan Wang
papers.abstract: As a contribution to the ongoing discussions on artificial intelligence (AI) ethics, I propose a feminist way of thinking on the positioning of AI in organizations. Inspired by the trickster figure that originates in mythology and folklore, I develop the notion of ‘trickster AI’ to conceptualize the fluid, relational, and ambivalent role of AI in organizational contexts. The ‘trickster AI’ is further supported by an empirical study drawing on a series of co-creation workshops on AI design for bias mitigation in hiring. Four AI-based solutions from the workshop – neutralization , standardization , customization , and diversification – are identified and analysed to examine how different configurations of AI and human actors shape the construction of bias and fairness. Rather than treating AI as inherently fair or biased, the findings show how the role of AI is continuously negotiated and reconfigured across practices. Interpreting these configurations through the lens of the trickster, the article highlights AI’s fluid positionality, inherent ambivalence, and capacity for boundary crossing. It contributes to feminist organization studies and feminist approaches to AI by moving beyond binary understandings of technology and foregrounding the situated, relational, and multiple enactments of fairness in sociotechnical practices.

papers.title: AI and the Quality of ESG Assurance: The Role of Auditor Expertise in Increasing the Reliability of Non-Financial Reporting
papers.authors: Essam AlArbed
papers.journal: Universal Journal of Accounting and Finance
papers.abstract: This study examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption affects ESG assurance quality (ESGQUAL) and whether Certified Public Accountant (CPA) expertise moderates this relationship. Using a longitudinal panel of 1,000 firm-year observations from 100 U.S. firms spanning 2016 to 2025, the analysis employs firm- and year-fixed-effects regressions with firm-clustered robust standard errors. Results reveal a positive direct association between AI adoption and ESG assurance quality (B = 0.158, p < 0.01) as well as a positive direct effect of CPA expertise (B = 0.176, p < 0.01). Crucially, the interaction term (AI × CPA) is positive and significant (B = 0.089, p < 0.01), confirming that CPA expertise strengthens the beneficial impact of technology. The full model accounts for 48% of the variance in assurance quality ( =0.480). Further tests show AI adoption significantly reduces ESG assurance subjectivity (B = -0.143, p < 0.01). Marginal effects analysis indicates that AI's impact is statistically insignificant at low CPA expertise (B = 0.042), but increases to 0.161 at mean levels and 0.284 at high levels of expertise (p < 0.01). Robustness checks using alternative AI metrics, investment proxies, and lagged specifications confirm these results. The evidence supports a technology-complementarity model where AI enhances data scale and analytical consistency, while CPAs retain core responsibility for professional judgment, ethical oversight, and contextual interpretation.

papers.title: Making stroke science accessible to people with lived experience: a narrative review
papers.authors: Stacie Broek, Marianne Elisabeth Klinke, Stacy Quinn, Melinda Berg Roaldsen
papers.abstract: Background: Adult stroke survivors and families may experience substantial barriers to accessing, understanding and using research evidence. Aphasia, cognitive changes, fatigue, health-literacy demands, restricted access to published literature and the technical presentation of research may all affect whether evidence is meaningful to stroke survivors and families. Aims: To examine barriers to accessible stroke research and consider how nurses, other health professionals, healthcare organisations, researchers, professional bodies and survivor-led initiatives can support the translation of evidence for stroke survivors and families. Methods: This clinical narrative review draws on selected stroke-specific and broader literature identified through focused searches in PubMed and CINAHL, supplemented by citation searching, recent guidelines and relevant practice examples. Sources were selected by author consensus, with broader evidence included where stroke-specific research was limited. Findings: Making research accessible requires clear language, relevance to survivor priorities, appropriate timing and format, communication support, family involvement where preferred, access to reliable information and verification of understanding. Nurses and allied health professionals have a distinctive role through sustained contact with survivors and families, and their responsibilities for assessment, education, interdisciplinary coordination and transition planning. Supported communication, visual formats, teach-back and co-designed resources may improve accessibility, although their effectiveness in stroke populations remains incompletely established. Survivor-led digital and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches offer further possibilities but require careful evaluation and human oversight. Conclusions: Making stroke evidence understandable and practical is a shared responsibility. Health professionals are fundamental to connecting evidence with the communication needs, priorities and lived circumstances of stroke survivors and families, but this role requires organisational and interdisciplinary support across the pathway.

papers.title: Serious-Play Cards for Teaching AI Applications in Manufacturing
papers.authors: Torbjørn H. Netland, Damian Borth
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a serious-play card deck designed to teach artificial intelligence (AI) use case applications in manufacturing. The deck comprises 42 cards, each presenting a real-world problem paired with a corresponding AI use case. Instructors can use these cards to facilitate structured and engaging group discussions. The paper describes the design of the cards and their implementations across four executive education classes in both classroom and metaverse settings. For the most recent intervention, we conducted a structured evaluation using an anonymous, theory-anchored survey instrument. The results indicate that the cards are perceived as engaging and valuable, particularly for supporting application-oriented learning and peer-based discussion while contributing less strongly to perceived knowledge acquisition. These findings suggest that serious-play cards are most effective as a complement to conventional teaching methods, enabling learners to translate abstract AI concepts into context-specific managerial reasoning. The paper provides full instructions and card details that support reuse by instructors.

papers.title: Research on the Influence of Artificial Intelligence Application on the Professional Creativity of Leather Products Designers
papers.authors: Ling Dai, Hui XIE
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: ObjectiveBased on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this study investigates the influence mechanism of artificial intelligence (AI) application on the professional creativity of leather product designers, and constructed a theoretical model of "AI application - technology perception - professional creativity". MethodsPerceived ease of use and perceived usefulness were introduced as mediating variables. Based on the Williams creativity theory, professional creativity was divided into four dimensions: curiosity, imagination, risk-taking, and challenge. Data were collected from leather product designers via a structured questionnaire and empirically tested using Confirmatory Factor Analysis and Structural Equation Modeling. ResultsAI application exerted a significant positive influence on all four dimensions of professional creativity. Both perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness played significant mediating roles in the dimensions of curiosity, imagination, and challenge. Regarding the risk-taking dimension, only perceived ease of use served as a significant mediator, whereas the impact of perceived usefulness was not statistically significant. ConclusionThis study reveals the intrinsic link between technology cognition and design creativity in the context of AI. It provides theoretical grounds and practical references for the leather industry in promoting digital design, establishing AI training systems, and enhancing the innovation capabilities of design teams.

papers.title: Research on AIGC-driven Footwear Intelligent Design Methods and Applications
papers.authors: Junqing MENG, Xuemei LI
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThis research is aimed at solving the problems exposed by AIGC technology in the field of footwear design, such as generation homogeneity, low process feasibility, and market demand disconnection. A dedicated AIGC generation model and an intelligent design methodology for footwear design are built, which realize the transformation of the design process from the traditional linear mode to a data-driven, human-machine collaboration closed-loop system, and promote the integration of AIGC technology in design innovation and industrial implementation.MethodsThe study adopts a research path of "theoretical analysis, technology construction, system verification, and method refinement" is adopted. In the early theoretical research stage, the application status and bottlenecks of AIGC in footwear design are systematically sorted out through literature analysis and questionnaire survey, providing the theoretical basis and problem orientation for model construction. In the model construction stage, the label is extracted with the help of code detection algorithm, and the footwear model is constructed by using the diffusion model architecture. In the stage of shoe generation design method, the intelligent design method of footwear is proposed by comparing and studying the traditional linear design process and the collaborative process after AIGC intervention. In the stage of building a digital asset library, core data such as materials, processes, soles, and lasts are integrated to build a structured and correlated asset library. In the construction stage of the intelligent design system, from demand analysis to design positioning, a collaborative group of "planning-AI creator-craftsman" is established to carry out multi-end reviews and realize a closed loop of marketing and data feedback.ResultsThe research has achieved the following three outcomes: First, an intelligent auxiliary design system for shoes is constructed: according to its structural characteristics, a detection code is developed to extract the labels of shoe design elements. A large model of shoe generation is built based on the diffusion model, combined with LoRA to accurately control the design language (such as contour lines, material matching, and color system), providing high-quality solution divergence support for the early design stage. Second, the closed-loop reconstruction of the design process is achieved: the traditional linear process of "design→testing→production" has been upgraded to a three-dimensional intelligent closed-loop of "data insight→real-time verification→and dynamic optimization". The design direction is defined through market data and trend analysis, the scheme is quickly generated by AIGC, and the manufacturability is preliminarily evaluated in combination with the database, effectively improving the design response efficiency and feasibility. Third, a human-machine collaborative design path is established: AIGC is not a substitute for designers, but rather expands the boundaries of creative exploration through rapid generation, multi-scheme comparison and stylistic control. It establishes a collaborative work model of "human creativity guidance + AI efficient transformation", which clarifies the core position of designers in creative planning, aesthetic judgment and cultural narrative, while AI tools exert efficiency advantages in stages such as scheme transformation, component combination, and parametric adjustment.ConclusionsThe research confirms that AIGC technology should move towards a development path with a high degree of human-machine collaboration as the core: technically, developing a generation architecture that integrates footwear specialties by embedding biomechanical parameters, material properties and process constraints to enhance the rationality and feasibility of the model; procedurally, building a traceable and interpretable generation system in the process to achieve transparent association from concept to element and rebuild the authenticity and credibility of the design process; and instituionally, establishing an ethical framework covering copyright identification, contribution assessment, and cultural compliance to promote the formation of a human-machine co-creation environment with clear rights and responsibilities, collaboration and order. Finally, it will promote the development of AIGC from an efficiency tool to a co-creation partner, and build an industrial application system with sustainable evolution and deep symbiosis between data and design. In the long run, the development of AIGC in footwear design should not stop at being an efficiency improvement tool, but should further realize the full-link data closed loop of design creativity, engineering manufacturing and market feedback, and ultimately promote the evolution of the footwear design industry in a smarter, more humanistic and more sustainable direction.

papers.title: Innovative Application of Splicing Method in Leather Bag Design from the Perspective of Semiotics
papers.authors: Jinbin ZHANG, Si MU
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aims to innovatively apply splicing methods to leather bag design, thereby facilitating the innovative development of leather product design. Through semiotic analysis and design research on splicing methods, it explores the underlying logic of their innovative application and specific manifestation mechanisms. MethodsTaking splicing methods in leather bag design as the research object, in the semiotic analysis stage of the splicing methods, based on Saussure’s semiotic theory, a systematic analysis is conducted of the symbiotic relationship between "signifiers", such as material splicing, technique splicing, and element splicing in the semiotic system, and their corresponding "signifieds" of function, aesthetics, and connotation. In the semiotic design research stage of the splicing methods, first, the target demand and style positioning are determined through market research; second, the symbiotic relationship between the signifiers and signifieds of the splicing methods in innovative design is constructed by combining the brainstorming method; third, the above symbiotic relationship exploration is sorted out and structured into AIGC prompt words, and artificial intelligence generated content (AIGC) technology is used as the symbol translation medium to batch generate a series of leather bag design schemes with application value of signifiers and signifieds; finally, the generated schemes are ranked by satisfaction and the optimal design is selected through the customer satisfaction (CSAT) survey method.ResultsThe research achieved three main results. First, a batch of 20 series of leather bag solutions with the application value of signifiers and signifieds is generated. Second, the evaluation and analysis show that in terms of reliability, the internal consistency of the scale is good and the measurement results are reliable (the individual α values of the 20 bags all exceed 0.80). In terms of validity, the scale has good structural validity (KMO=0.866 4, and the Bartlett sphericity test is significant (P<0.001)). In terms of satisfaction, the average overall satisfaction of the 20 bags ranges from 3.34 to 3.48, which is generally at a medium to upper level. Among them, B27 has the highest overall satisfaction rate and can be regarded as a key model for mass production and promotion. From the perspective of dimensions, the satisfaction of dimension C (value provision: fun, pleasure, self-expression) is slightly higher than that of dimension A (style design) and dimension B (design approach), reflecting that respondents have a relatively high recognition of the emotional value of leather bag design. However, there is still room for further improvement in the visual impact of the "Y2K" style characteristics and the uniqueness of design details. Third, a complete design closed loop of "theoretical analysis - market research - innovative application - effectiveness verification" is formed.ConclusionsResearch shows that taking Saussure’s semiotic theory as methodological guidance can not only achieve a visual breakthrough in the "form" of the splicing method in leather bag design, but also reach a connotation innovation at the "meaning" level, that is, it is conducive to the dual innovation of the form and meaning of the splicing method. The application of the brainstorming method helps to deeply explore and construct the symbiotic relationship of "interaction", "coordination" and "coupling" between the signifier and signified of symbols, endowing the design with more profound emotional, cultural, functional and other connotations and depth. The introduction of AIGC technology can significantly enhance the innovation level and overall efficiency of design, providing strong support for the expression of symbolic signifieds and the optimization of schemes. The application of the CSAT survey method is conducive to ensuring that the design outcome can ultimately be completed with high quality and more accurately aligned with the design positioning.

papers.title: Enablers of Sustainable Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery: A Qualitative Exploration of Global Neurosurgery.
papers.authors: Rya Muller, Omolabake Oyetayo, Emmanuel Wegoye, David Bieber, Shadrack Khisa, Khrystyna Moskalyk, Robert Kabuye Sebunya, Richard Idro, Humphrey Okechi, Elysa Widjaja, Sandi Lam
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Of 50 million people with epilepsy globally, up to 10 million with lesional drug resistance epilepsy may be able to achieve seizure control with surgical options. Although multidisciplinary surgical care for epilepsy is available in high-income countries, few programs exist in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). In 2019, a global collaboration between CURE Uganda and Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital in the United States established a surgical epilepsy program in Uganda for the pediatric population. This study identifies key pillars for sustainable neurosurgical program development in LMICs. METHODS: Interdisciplinary health care providers from CURE and Lurie Children's who participated in the development of the surgical epilepsy program from 2019 to 2024 underwent semistructured qualitative interviews. A thematic analysis framework was used to identify themes from interviews related to program development, sustainability, and targets for future work. RESULTS: Nine participants were interviewed, with representation from roles of pediatric neurologist, pediatric neuroradiologist, electroencephalogram technologists, medical officer, and pediatric neurosurgeon.
