Thematic analysis revealed 4 themes (with subthemes) related to sustainable global surgical program development: (1) Intentional planning (integrating global policies into program development, rigorous case selection for great outcomes to build confidence for public/administrative support, defining barriers and optimizing solutions); (2) interdisciplinary collaboration (communication and trust are vital, new initiatives may require sacrifice, true partnerships allow for bidirectional learning, creative problem solving is crucial); (3) skill transfer and education (on-the-ground skill transfer needed, technology integration facilitates continuous learning, enable development opportunities for teammates); and (4) targets for future work (public education, expanding clinical capacity in LMICs, sustainable education centers, research dissemination). CONCLUSION: Global collaborations create opportunities to increase access to neurosurgical care. Creating interdisciplinary programs across borders requires trust and open communication by all members. Sustainable programs can be further enabled with intentional planning, humility, and bidirectional skill transfer.

papers.title: Ethical Dilemmas and Humanistic Return Paths in Medical Artificial Intelligence Nursing Practice
papers.authors: Yangyang SONG, Beilei Qiu, Wanbing HUANG, 叶哲伟, 朱宏梅
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence has been widely applied in various nursing practice scenarios. This study analyses the ethical dilemmas arising from its application in nursing education, clinical decision-making, workflow management, and emotional support, and examines core issues such as the objectification of the nurse-patient relationship, emotional absence, and erosion of the autonomy of nursing practice. It is proposed that the nursing profession should shift from passive adaptation to proactive leadership in the transformation of medical artificial intelligence, by constructing a comprehensive ethics governance framework centered on "humanistic care", deeply participating in the design, development, implementation, and evaluation feedback of medical artificial intelligence technologies, strengthening nurses' ethical leadership, reforming the education evaluation system, and promoting algorithm transparency and other specific paths. This will balance the tension between the professional attributes of the nursing profession centered on empathy, trust, and humanistic care and the technical attributes of intelligent medical technology, thereby promoting the sustainable development of the nursing profession in the digital era.

papers.title: A Study on the Ethical Risks and Governance Pathways of Ambient Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Clinical Documentation
papers.authors: Zixun LI, 沙卫红, Hao CHEN
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence-assisted clinical documentation captures clinician-patient conversations and automatically performs transcription, information extraction, and structured processing to generate draft medical records. Although it can reduce the burden of clinical documentation and improve clinician-patient communication, its role as a "third-party recorder" in clinical encounters may also give rise to ethical risks, including inadequate informed consent, disclosure of sensitive information, constraints on patient expression, inaccuracies in medical records, and ambiguity in the allocation of responsibility. This article reviews its operating mechanism and clinical application, analyzes the associated risks through four clinical cases, and proposes governance strategies from the aspects of patient rights, physician review, data security and hospital governance, such as improving the informed consent and opt-out mechanism, strengthening data protection throughout the data lifecycle, implementing substantive physician review, clarifying responsibilities among multiple stakeholders, and strengthening predeployment as asessment and continuous monitoring, so as to promote the safe and standardized application of this technology in clinical practice.

papers.title: Practical Issues and Governance Insights in the Ethical Review of High-Risk Technological Activities: A Case Study of Invasive Brain-Computer Interface Projects in Shanghai
papers.authors: Chanqin Gao
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: Based on the review of five invasive brain-computer interface projects in Shanghai, this paper analyzes the main issues identified by expert re-review after institutional preliminary review. These issues primarily focus on the sufficiency of preclinical evidence, the feasibility of research protocols, the compliance of innovative devices and research pathways, risks of complex systems, therapeutic misconceptions in informed consent, and long-term rights protection for implants. Some issues were not entirely neglected during the initial review; rather, they concern whether the available scientific evidence is sufficient to demonstrate the scientific and ethical justification for conducting human research. Ethical re-review of high-risk scientific and technological activities should strengthen the ethics-oriented reassessment of scientific validity, shift from the review of individual technologies to the assessment of technological system risks, extend protection from the research period to the full lifecycle of rights protection, and promote the improvement of institutional preliminary review capabilities through re-review, continuing review, and on-site supervision.

papers.title: Digital maternal health interventions in resource-constrained settings: a RE-AIM evaluation of the e-SAATHI chatbot in Assam, India
papers.authors: Swapnil Rawat, Charlotte Warren, Ben Bellows, Sowmya Ramesh, Jitender Nagpal
papers.abstract: Despite national progress in maternal health, Assam continues to face high maternal mortality and persistent gaps in antenatal (ANC) and postnatal care (PNC). Digital platforms offer scalable solutions to strengthen service uptake in resource-constrained settings. The objective is to assess the reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and maintenance of the e-SAATHI intervention in improving maternal health service utilization and engagement in Assam between 2023 and 2025. e-SAATHI was implemented as a stage-based digital intervention delivering tailored health information, reminders, and referral support to pregnant and postpartum women (up to 15 weeks after delivery). The evaluation was grounded in the RE-AIM framework, drawing on both quantitative and qualitative data sources. Data sources included system-generated analytics, user feedback, and routine health facility records. Key indicators assessed included user enrollment, message delivery fidelity, service uptake (ANC and PNC), and user satisfaction. The intervention expanded from one pilot site to five districts, onboarding 54,297 women across 180 + facilities. Assisted onboarding via QR codes and offline forms enabled inclusion of remote populations. Message delivery fidelity exceeded 98%, supported by iterative adaptations such as simplified sign-up and multimedia content. In paired facility-based surveys of postpartum women in Assam (pre-intervention n = 210; post-intervention n = 303), reported first-trimester ANC registration was higher in the post-intervention phase, rising from 66% to 83%, completion of ≥ 4 ANC contacts increased from ~ 49.5% to 61.7%; selected provider-delivered care indicators were also higher. As the evaluation was single-arm and based largely on self-report, these differences cannot be attributed to e-SAATHI. Monthly ANC confirmations surpassed 1,000 by 2025, and PNC engagement increased tenfold after content upgrades. Over 95% of users rated messages as “very useful,” and health workers reported enhanced client preparedness. Adoption was facilitated by integration into state workflows and real-time dashboards. Government endorsement and scale-up funding support sustainability. The e-SAATHI intervention shows that human-supported, digitally enabled solutions can be delivered at scale in low-resource settings, with wide reach, strong adoption and high fidelity of implementation. Embedding such tools within routine health systems and adapting them to user needs are critical for scale and sustainability. Future efforts should focus on expanding postpartum support, enhancing personalization, and conducting rigorous impact evaluations. Not required.

papers.title: Prevalence and determinants of food insecurity among displaced and vulnerable adolescents in accommodation centers in Metuge (Cabo Delgado) and KaMavota (Maputo City), Mozambique
papers.authors: Angela Patricio Joaquim, Alice Pedro Magaia de Abreu, José da Cruz Francisco
papers.abstract: Food insecurity constitutes a major public health problem, particularly in the contexts of forced displacement, poverty, and socioeconomic vulnerability, and significantly affects adolescents’ health, nutrition, and development. However, evidence on the magnitude and factors associated with food insecurity among adolescents remains limited. The present study aimed to determine the prevalence and factors associated with food insecurity among adolescents aged 15 to 19 years living in situations of displacement and vulnerability in the districts of Metuge, Cabo Delgado Province, and KaMavota, Maputo city. This cross-sectional study involved 341 adolescents aged 15–19 years who were selected through stratified probabilistic sampling in the districts of Metuge and KaMavota. Data collection was carried out through semistructured interviews via the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale (HFIAS), adapted to the local context. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant characteristics. Associations between independent variables and food insecurity were initially assessed using Pearson’s chi-square test. Variables with p < 0.20 were included in a multivariable logistic regression model. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) were estimated, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Model fit and multicollinearity were assessed. All analyses were conducted using SPSS version 28. The results revealed that more than 9 out of every 10 adolescents experienced food insecurity, with a prevalence of severe food insecurity of 96.6%, which was higher in Metuge (97.8%) than in KaMavota (92%). Adolescents reported consuming, on average, two meals per day, whereas a considerable proportion of those in Metuge consumed only one meal daily. Significant associations were observed between food insecurity and factors such as weight, height, body mass index, BMI classification, educational level, type of household occupation, and monthly household income. The dietary diversity was lower in Metuge, whereas KaMavota presented greater consumption of processed foods. Food insecurity is highly prevalent among adolescents living in accommodation centers in Metuge and KaMavota, affecting a substantial proportion of the study population. These findings indicate that food insecurity remains a severe, persistent, and multidimensional challenge in these settings and may adversely affect adolescent health, growth, and development. The results underscore the urgent need for integrated and multisectoral interventions that extend beyond immediate food assistance, including strengthened social protection, improved livelihood opportunities, enhanced access to education, greater dietary diversity, and targeted health, nutrition, and income-generation programs for adolescents and their parents/caregivers in contexts of displacement and social vulnerability.

papers.title: Exploring learner–parent–AI interaction patterns in an AI-supported EFL learning game during informal learning: insights from sequence and epistemic network analyses
papers.authors: Simin Xu, Chung Kwan Lo
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of digital technologies (e.g., generative artificial intelligence [AI] and digital games) has enhanced informal learning of English as a foreign language (EFL). However, few studies have explored AI-mediated informal learning in primary EFL education settings. The objectives of this study are to explore learner–parent–AI interactions in an AI-supported EFL learning game and to make recommendations regarding AI-mediated informal learning of English. We developed an AI-supported EFL learning game and invited 50 participants (25 pairs of young learners and parents) to engage with the game for informal learning during the summer holiday. Data were collected from (1) video recordings of gameplay, (2) learner–AI dialogues, (3) learners’ pre- and post-tests, and (4) semi-structured interviews with the participants and were analysed using sequence analysis, epistemic network analysis (ENA), the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Quade’s non-parametric ANCOVA, multiple regression analysis, and qualitative analysis, respectively. Two distinct learner–parent–AI interaction profiles were identified. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test indicated significant increases in scores from pre-test to post-test within both profiles. However, learners’ post-test scores did not differ significantly across the learner profiles after controlling for their pre-test scores. The regression analysis results indicated that learners’ pre-test scores, their engagement in knowledge-learning tasks, and parental cognitive engagement strategies were positively associated with learners’ post-test scores. By contrast, learner–AI interaction types showed no significant association with learners’ post-test scores. Hence, this study informs the future development of AI-supported EFL learning games (e.g., incorporating knowledge-learning tasks and adaptive scaffolding). This study also highlights the potential role of parental cognitive engagement strategies and contributes to an enhanced design framework for AI-supported EFL learning games in informal learning contexts.

papers.title: Heart, soul, and recovery: a real-time modified Delphi study on an integrated mental health, substance use and cardiovascular care intervention for justice-involved Black/African American men
papers.authors: Ayorkor Gaba, Gilbert A. Nick, Samantha N Fagan, Williams Ojo, David D. McManus
papers.abstract: Criminal legal system involvement is strongly associated with poorer cardiovascular health, the leading cause of death among incarcerated individuals, with Black/African American men disproportionately affected. Co-occurring substance use and mental health disorders (COD) further compound risks for this population. Despite the urgent need to address these risk factors and disparities, few culturally tailored, integrated cardiovascular disease risk and COD interventions exist for this population. The purpose of this study was to combine current research evidence with the experience of people with lived experience (PWLE) and people with professional experience (PWPE) to inform the core components of a new intervention for system-involved Black/African American men with co-occurring substance use, mental health, and cardiovascular disease risks. We conducted a real-time modified Delphi study with people with lived experience (PWLE; n = 14) and professional experience (PWPE; n = 11) in the criminal legal system, COD, and CVD. Informed by a focused literature review and initial stakeholder input, 102 statements addressing intervention priorities were generated and then rated using a Likert scale. Statements meeting ≥ 80% agreement were retained. Percent consensus was calculated, and thematic analysis of qualitative responses was conducted. Experts reached consensus on 76 of 102 items (74.5%), identifying strong agreement on target population, intervention type, setting, and cultural tailoring. They endorsed developing a transdiagnostic, culturally tailored intervention for Black/African American men with any co-occurring substance use and mental health disorder and any level of criminal legal system involvement preferring in-person or hybrid formats over digital-only approaches. Experts prioritized addressing key CVD risk factors, particularly smoking, hypertension, diabetes and high cholesterol through direct, in-program strategies and emphasized trust, flexibility, and co-creation as an essential component to engagement and impact. Findings provide foundational insight into components of an optimal culturally responsive, integrated intervention to address CVD and COD among justice-involved Black/African American men and can further inform public health strategies to reduce health disparities and guide behavioral, carceral, and public health system improvements.

papers.title: Locus coeruleus activity is related to sleep and 24-h rest-activity rhythms in the context of plasma Alzheimer’s disease markers: a 7T MRI study of older individuals
papers.authors: Yuliya Patsyuk, Prokopis C. Prokopiou, Nicholas James Ashton, Shorena Janelidze, Kaj Blennow, Oskar Hansson, Henrik Zetterberg, Benedikt Andreas Poser, Heidi I.L. Jacobs, Maxime Van Egroo
papers.abstract: The brainstem locus coeruleus (LC), an early site of tau pathology and a key regulator of arousal and sleep-wake dynamics, has emerged as a potential neurobiological substrate underlying the relationship between sleep-wake disturbances and AD pathogenesis. Yet, the interplay between LC functional metrics, sleep-wake regulation, and early AD pathology remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether plasma AD-related biomarkers moderate the relationship between LC activity and objective sleep-wake measures in asymptomatic older individuals. Fifty-five cognitively unimpaired older adults underwent 10 days of actigraphy, blood drawing, and a daytime 7T MRI protocol including dedicated LC imaging and an affective visual task comprising high-arousing and low-arousing images. Arousal-based LC activity was determined by the high-versus-low-arousal (H > L) contrast. A subset of individuals ( n = 30) also performed three nights of at-home sleep EEG recordings. Plasma AD-related biomarkers included glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and tau phosphorylated at threonine 181 (ptau 181 ), 217 (ptau 217 ) and 231 (ptau 231 ). Interaction models adjusted for age, sex, BMI and device wear duration showed that, at higher levels of GFAP and several ptau markers, lower LC activation to the emotional stimuli during the task was related to shorter actigraphy-derived sleep duration, lower sleep efficiency (SE), and higher wake after sleep onset (WASO%). We observed similar patterns using 24-h rest–activity rhythm, such that, at higher burden of GFAP and several ptau markers, lower H > L LC was associated with higher intradaily variability (IV) and lower interdaily stability (IS). Examining sleep architecture, we showed that participants with lower LC activation to emotional stimuli during the task and higher burden of different ptau markers exhibited a higher proportion of time spent in N2 sleep stage, along with lower time spent in N3 sleep stage. Lower daytime task-related LC activity was related to shorter, lighter, and more fragmented sleep as well as to disruption of circadian rest-activity patterns in the presence of biomarker evidence of early AD pathology in asymptomatic older individuals. These findings suggest that LC dysfunction may aggravate, while preserved LC function may protect against early AD-related sleep-wake disturbances.

papers.title: Symptom assessment experience of novice nurses based on artificial intelligence standardized patients: a qualitative study
papers.authors: Tingting Dong, Zijuan Yu, Xiao Zhou, Yifan Cui
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence standardized patient (AISP)-based symptom assessment training has emerged as a promising approach to complement clinical nursing education. However, little is known about how novice nurses experience such training, and qualitative evidence is needed to inform the design of training that supports their clinical development. To explore novice nurses’ experiences and perceptions of an Artificial Intelligence Standardized Patient (AISP) symptom assessment training system, and to provide evidence for optimizing the system design. A qualitative exploratory design was used. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 17 novice nurses who had used the AISP system at a tertiary grade A general hospital in Beijing. Three semi-structured focus group interviews (five to six participants each) were conducted in January 2026. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis, with two researchers coding independently. The study was reported in accordance with the COREQ checklist. Participants had a mean age of 24 years, and all held a bachelor’s degree or above. Three themes and eight subthemes were developed: participants perceived a favorable user experience with the AISP system (a pocket-sized inquiry coach: convenience and accessibility; an immersive inquiry partner: scenario authenticity and sense of engagement; a personalized review mentor: real-time and structured feedback); perceived learning value of AISP for symptom assessment (perceived role of structured guidance in organizing inquiry logic; perceived opportunities for communication practice through immersive interaction); and participants’ perceived limitations and optimization suggestions for the AISP system (insufficient coverage of diverse scenarios; limited flexibility of voice interaction; demands for functional iteration of the evaluation mechanism). Positive accounts were often qualified by concerns about speech recognition and the rigidity of interaction. Participants perceived the AISP system as a useful auxiliary tool for supporting symptom-assessment learning, while identifying limitations in scenario diversity, voice interaction, and feedback functions. These findings reflect subjective perceptions rather than demonstrated educational effectiveness. Future development should focus on improving interaction technologies, enriching training scenarios, and refining feedback mechanisms, and future studies should evaluate learning outcomes using objective measures. Not applicable.

papers.title: Changes in medical students’ ethical and acceptability-related perceptions of an AI-supported doctor–patient communication learning pathway: a longitudinal empirical ethics survey
papers.authors: Xiaoxiang Ma, Yang Chen, Jiulin Li, 阳妍华, Jianyu Liu
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported learning is increasingly used in medical education, including doctor–patient communication training. Such systems may provide virtual dialogue practice, immediate structured feedback, reflection prompts and opportunities for further practice after feedback. However, educational usefulness does not necessarily imply ethical acceptability. This study examined changes in medical students’ ethical and acceptability-related perceptions before and after participation in an AI-supported doctor–patient communication learning pathway. This longitudinal empirical ethics survey was nested within a course-based randomised educational trial but was analytically independent of the parent trial’s educational outcome analysis. Surveys were administered after random allocation to the AI-supported pathway but before exposure to AI-supported learning functions (T0), at the end of the 8-week course (T1), and at the 3-month follow-up (T2). The main analysis focused on students in the AI-supported pathway with complete T0–T1–T2 ethics-related scale data and analysable T2 open-text responses ( n = 31). The open-text question was included only at T2. The primary comparison was the within-participant T0–T2 change across six ethics-related domains. Two domains showed statistically significant T0–T2 changes. Trust in AI feedback decreased from 3.86 (0.55) to 3.20 (0.62), with a mean change of − 0.66 (95% confidence interval [CI] − 0.88 to − 0.42), Cohen’s d z = − 1.04 and Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001. Room to question AI outputs increased from 2.71 (0.68) to 3.67 (0.58), with a mean change of 0.96 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.23), Cohen’s d z = 1.29 and Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001. The remaining four domains showed small, non-significant changes after Holm–Bonferroni correction. T2 open-text responses indicated that students recognised the formative value of AI feedback while emphasising critical use, teacher supervision, preservation of interpersonal interaction and clearer data governance. This exploratory longitudinal empirical ethics survey showed that, following participation in an AI-supported doctor–patient communication learning pathway, two of the six ethics-related domains showed statistically significant changes: trust in AI feedback decreased, while perceived room to question AI outputs increased. These findings support continued attention to ethics-focused evaluation and clear governance arrangements in AI-supported learning pathways.

papers.title: Do question type and topic affect the performance of large language models in answering periodontology questions? A comparative study
papers.authors: Hanife Merva Parlak
papers.abstract: There is increasing interest and ongoing debate about the integration of artificial intelligence and the large language models it supports in health science education. The performance of these models may vary depending on educational domains, clinical branches, complexity of questions, and question formats. This study aimed to compare the performance of ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Copilot on periodontology questions and to determine whether their performance was affected by question type and topic. One hundred thirty-four multiple-choice periodontology questions from the dental specialty exam in Türkiye were fed to these models. The responses were evaluated based on both their accuracy and the quality of their explanations. A Likert scale was used to examine the quality of explanation. The answers from the models were analyzed comparatively based on question type and topic. Regression analyses were performed to determine the effect of question type and topic. The total accuracy rates of ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Copilot were similar. Overall, Gemini 2.5 Flash outperformed the others in terms of adequacy of response explanation ( p < 0.05). Gemini provided more consistent explanations than others on basic science and clinical periodontology questions, as well as standardized and information-based questions ( p < 0.05, for all). Regression analysis showed that question type and topic were related to explanation quality. According to the findings of this study, question types and topics seem to affect the consistency and quality of large language models’ explanations more than the accuracy of the answers. This suggests that large language models are promising for periodontology education, but they still have limitations that require improvement. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously within the limitations of the study.

papers.title: A closed-loop AI virtual simulation platform for preclinical fiber post-core restoration: two-year prospective evaluation of learning outcomes and student perceptions
papers.authors: Li Yue, Chunxia Chen, Xiaoling Liao
papers.abstract: Preclinical prosthodontic education faces challenges in cultivating the integrated clinical decision-making and operational skills required for complex procedures like fiber post-core restoration. While virtual simulation (VS) is widely used, most systems function primarily as skill trainers and lack support for systematic clinical reasoning training. This two-year prospective study aimed to report implementation‑related observations and evaluate student acceptance of a novel AI-enhanced virtual simulation (AI-VS) platform integrating dynamic AI virtual patient consultation, domain‑specific procedural Q&A assistant, and a standardized rubric-based medical record evaluation workflow for comprehensive fiber post-core restoration training. This pre-post design included two independent fourth-year dental student cohorts: 2024 ( n = 38) and 2025 ( n = 42). The AI-VS platform provided a complete training cycle. Objective outcomes included pre-and post-training clinical case analysis scores (assessing clinical reasoning) and post-training simulator operation scores (assessing procedural performance at course completion). Subjective experience was measured using a study‑specific questionnaire developed for this investigation. Face‑and‑content validity assessment was performed via internal review by the three study authors who also developed the questionnaire; this represents internal‑team assessment and does not constitute independent external expert validation. Internal‑consistency reliability assessment was performed for multi‑item dimensions; survey constructs covered learning interest/satisfaction, self‑perceived outcomes, career expectation, and AI acceptance. Following curriculum implementation, both cohorts showed statistically significant improvements in clinical reasoning scores compared to baseline (2024: median 69 to 81.5; 2025: 71 to 83; both p < 0.001). A strong negative correlation was found between pre-training scores and score changes (2024: ρ = -0.879; 2025: ρ = -0.789; both p < 0.001). However, this pattern should be interpreted with caution, as it may reflect statistical artifacts including regression to the mean, ceiling effects, and the mathematical coupling inherent in correlating baseline scores with change scores. Post-training clinical reasoning and operational scores were strongly positively correlated (2024: r = 0.927; 2025: r = 0.722; overall: r = 0.840; all p < 0.001), suggesting a positive association between decision-making and procedural performance at course completion. Subjectively, students reported high course satisfaction (mean = 4.26/5), strong subjective endorsement of AI’s utility‑‑particularly its perceived ability to compensate for limited one‑on‑one teacher guidance (mean = 4.29/5)—and very positive career expectations (mean = 4.34/5). Following implementation of the AI‑VS curriculum, clinical‑case analysis scores increased in both student cohorts, post‑training procedural performance was positively associated with clinical‑reasoning scores, and students reported high acceptance of the course. Because the study used an uncontrolled pre‑post design and procedural performance was assessed only after training, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary implementation‑related observations rather than evidence of platform effectiveness, educational equity, or improvement in procedural skills.

papers.title: Mechanism-aware benchmarking of large language models as learning aids in pediatric difficult airway training: true hallucinations vs. false contraindications
papers.authors: Merve Bulun Yediyıldız, İrem Durmuş
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) are being investigated for their potential applications in perioperative decision-making and as informal "just-in-time" learning tools for trainees. This study evaluated five LLMs in pediatric difficult-airway management using a mechanism-aware scoring approach that distinguishes true hallucinations from false contraindications and examines their suitability for supervised learning. METHODS: In a simulation study involving a comparative blinded evaluation, 50 cases of pediatric difficult airway management were presented to five LLMs using a standardized prompt based on the 2022 American Society of Anesthesiologists Difficult Airway Guidelines. Two anesthesiologists evaluated the responses on a modified 0-5 scale. RESULTS: The inter-rater agreement was deemed to be of the highest caliber, as evidenced by a quadratic weighted κ value of 0.982. A statistically significant variation in overall performance was observed among the models (Friedman χ²(4) = 100.12, p < 0.001). In this single-pass evaluation, GPT-5.2 Thinking had the highest mean score and proportion of acceptable responses, whereas Claude Opus 4.5 had the highest combined critical-error rate (23.0% vs. 6.5% for both GPT models). True hallucinations were most frequent with Claude Opus 4.5 (11.8%; other models 0.5-2.2%), while false contraindications occurred across all models (5.0-13.0%) and clustered around rocuronium. Scenario inadequacy (score ≤ 2) increased with complexity: 32-98% for difficult intubation, 46-94% for difficult ventilation, and 52-92% for CICO. CONCLUSION: The contemporary generation of LLMs exhibits model-specific performance characteristics and error patterns in pediatric difficult airway management. Dosing-related failures manifest through different mechanisms of true hallucination vs. false contraindication. The findings reveal a marked inadequacy of the scenarios employed in these models, particularly as complexity and critical error rates increase. Current LLMs may have value as supervised supplementary learning tools, but not as autonomous sources of clinical or educational guidance.

papers.title: Comparative accuracy of large language models in restorative and endodontic dentistry multiple-choice questions: implications for dental education
papers.authors: İkbal Esra Pehlivan, Sema Kaya, ELİF BAŞTUĞ GÜVEN, Beyza Batmaz
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as learning and question-answering tools in health professions education. However, their reliability in dental multiple-choice assessments may depend not only on overall accuracy but also on disciplinary context and the structural validity of the questions. This study aimed to compare the performance of 14 large language model-based artificial intelligence systems on multiple-choice questions in restorative dentistry and endodontics and to evaluate their ability to identify structurally invalid items. This cross-sectional experimental study evaluated the performance of 14 large language model (LLM)-based artificial intelligence systems on 200 five-option multiple-choice questions prepared in Turkish. The questions were equally distributed between Restorative Dentistry and Endodontics and categorized into four structural types: Type 1 (valid question, single correct answer), Type 2 (semantically invalid question), Type 3 (valid question, no correct option), and Type 4 (valid question, no incorrect option). The model responses were coded as correct (1) or incorrect (0). Cochran’s Q and McNemar tests were used to compare models, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests evaluated discipline-based differences ( p < 0.05). Significant inter-model differences were observed for types 1, 2, and 4 ( p < 0.001), but not for type 3 ( p = 0.448). Gemini Pro and Gemini Pro (Deep Research) achieved the highest accuracy in Type 1, while DeepSeek and ChatGPT 5.2 led in Type 2. Manus demonstrated outstanding performance on structurally contradictory questions (Types 3 and 4; 98%). Overall, seven of the fourteen models showed significant discipline-based differences. Endodontics was favored in five models: Gemini Pro, Gemini Pro (Deep Research), ChatGPT 5.2 Web, Perplexity, and SciSpace, whereas DeepSeek and DeepSeek (Deep Search) favored restorative dentistry. When analyzed by question type, differences favoring endodontics were clustered in Type 2, whereas differences favoring Restorative Dentistry predominated in Types 3 and 4. The performance of LLMs in dental education varies across disciplines, question structures, and model systems. Accuracy alone is insufficient for evaluating reliability. The ability to detect structurally invalid items varies markedly across models, with important implications for assessment validity, examination security, and the responsible integration of artificial intelligence into dental education.

papers.title: Improving the implementation of an adolescent obesity prevention intervention in under-resourced schools
papers.authors: Yuxin Nie, Qiaoyin Tan, Paul Son, Pengfei Yang, Jared N. Androzzi, Renee A. Underwood, Amanda E. Staiano, Richard R. Rosenkranz, Fahui Wang, Senlin Chen
papers.abstract: Guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research ( CFIR 2.0 ), this study examined the implementation and impact of an adapted, school-based, multi-component adolescent obesity prevention intervention called the Pr eventing O besity U sing D igital-Assisted M ovement and E ating (ProudMe) across two phases, with refinements made in between. Twelve middle schools from two districts ( N = 266 students) participated in the study. Phase 1 included six schools (ProudMe: n = 3 schools, 33 students; control: n = 3 schools, 46 students), and phase 2 included six schools (ProudMe: n = 5 schools, 165 students; control: n = 1 school, 22 students). ProudMe comprised four components: ProudMe Cafeteria (i.e., simplified Smarter Lunchrooms strategies), ProudMe PE (i.e., a purposeful physical education [PE] curriculum), ProudMe Tech (i.e., AI-assisted behavioral counseling), and ProudMe PD (i.e., a half-day staff professional development [PD] with continual support). Mixed methods data were used to assess three implementation outcomes (i.e., penetration, fidelity, sustainability). Pre-to-post changes in cafeteria scores, health behaviors (physical activity, screen time, fruit/vegetable intake), and BMI z-scores were compared across groups. Phase 2 demonstrated stronger implementation outcomes than phase 1 across ProudMe components. Penetration index was high in phase 2 and/or showed marked improvement. Fidelity index was high for ProudMe Cafeteria and ProudMe PD in both phases, while a moderate to high level of modification was observed with ProudMe PE implementation. Phase 2 demonstrated positive sustainability (8.4 ± 1.83 on a 10-point Likert scale). For impact, the cafeteria scores gained more in phase 2 ( M diff = + 8.3, p = 0.10; d = 1.53) than those in phase 1 ( M diff = + 4.67, p = 0.06; d = 1.14) versus a decline in control schools ( M diff = − 2.36, p = 0.61; d = − 0.36). No significant group differences were observed for student health behaviors or BMI z-scores. Qualitative results further suggested that phase 2 reflected improved perceived feasibility, contextual fit, and implementer buy-in across components. CFIR analysis revealed more facilitators and fewer barriers in phase 2 than phase 1, although time constraints, testing schedules, technology-related disruptions, and low parental consent remained persistent barriers. The refined ProudMe trial (phase 2) yielded improved implementation outcomes and measurable impact on school cafeteria policy and environmental changes. Student-level behavioral and weight status change may require longer duration to emerge.

papers.title: Exploring patients’ experiences with artificial intelligence and digital health literacy in chronic disease self-management: a qualitative study
papers.authors: Eidah Farhan AL-Anazi, Seham Mansour Alyousef
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital health tools are increasingly incorporated into chronic disease self-management, providing personalized monitoring and decision-making support. However, the experiences of patients with these technologies and the influence of Digital Health Literacy (DHL) in promoting their effective utilization are inadequately comprehended, especially in the context of Saudi Arabia. Method This qualitative descriptive study explored patients’ experiences with AI-based and digital health technologies in the self-management of chronic diseases. A purposive sample of nine patients with chronic illnesses were collected in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Data were collected using semi-structured interviews as guided by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) conducted on Zoom, each lasting 20 to 30 minutes. Interviews were audio- recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically in accordance with Braun and Clarke’s methodology. Trustworthiness was established via member checking, peer review, and maintaining of an audit trail. Result Four main themes emerged: [1] Usability of AI-based health tools [2], Perceptions and meaning of AI technologies [3], Digital health literacy, and [4] Integration into self-management behaviors. Participants predominantly regarded AI technologies as user-friendly, especially when utilized on smartphones, and indicated frequent incorporation into their daily routines. AI technologies were perceived as supporting tools that improved health monitoring and understanding, along with an increasing trust and reliance over time. DHL was recognized as a critical element influencing participants’ ability to interpret health information and proficiently utilize digital tools. AI-based technologies facilitated self-monitoring behaviors and supplemented, rather than replaced traditional healthcare engagement. Conclusion AI-based and digital health tools assist in the self-management of chronic diseases; yet, their benefit is dependent upon usability, positive user perceptions, and a significant digital health literacy. Improving DHL and prioritizing user-centered design are crucial for optimizing the incorporation of AI technologies into patient self-management practices.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning for identifying poor physical fitness in adults across three high-altitude regions of Tibet: a cross-sectional study
papers.authors: Ting Chen, Xin Zhao, Ruizhe Sun, Ba Bian, Weibao Liang
papers.abstract: Rapid identification of adults with poor physical fitness may help target early behavioural and clinical resources in resource-constrained high-altitude settings. We developed and internally–externally validated (leave-one-city-out) interpretable machine-learning classifiers to identify adults with currently poor physical fitness using Tibet National Physical Fitness Monitoring data. This cross-sectional analysis included 5,750 adults aged 20–69 years from Nyingchi (3100 m), Lhasa (3658 m), and Nagqu (4500 m), drawn from 6,160 sampled residents. Poor physical fitness was defined using age-specific total-score cut-points from the Chinese National Physical Fitness Standard (< 23 points at age 20–39 years, < 18 at 40–59 years, and < 15 at 60–69 years). To limit outcome (label) leakage, predictors were prespecified to variables obtainable before the scored performance battery: demographics, exercise behaviour, adiposity markers, and resting haemodynamic measurements. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were compared using internal-external cross-validation by site (leave-one-city-out). Pooled held-out predictions were used to estimate discrimination, precision-recall, calibration, classification metrics at clinically relevant thresholds, and decision-curve performance, with 95% confidence intervals from bootstrap resampling. Robustness was examined with multiple imputation, an anthropometry-free model, and site-adjusted analyses. SHAP applied to a matched gradient-boosting model was used to describe the dominant predictors, and concordance with random-forest permutation importance was assessed. Poor physical fitness was present in 2,046 of 5,750 adults (35.6%). Event rates varied markedly by site, from 27.6% in Lhasa to 46.9% in Nyingchi. The random forest showed the highest pooled held-out discrimination point estimates (AUROC 0.664, 95% CI 0.649–0.681; AUPRC 0.560, 95% CI 0.537–0.583; Brier score 0.212, 95% CI 0.208–0.216), followed by XGBoost (AUROC 0.652, 95% CI 0.637–0.667) and logistic regression (AUROC 0.646, 95% CI 0.631–0.661). Differences in discrimination between models were small, and XGBoost had a slightly lower Brier score than the random forest. Calibration of the champion random forest was moderate (intercept − 0.26; slope 0.86). At a prevalence-matched threshold the random forest reached a sensitivity of 0.71 and specificity of 0.48; at a lower fixed threshold of 0.30 sensitivity rose to 0.81 with specificity 0.33, underscoring the screening-only nature of the tool. Results were robust in complete-case analysis, under multiple imputation (AUROC 0.667), and in a leaner predictor set; an anthropometry-free model performed substantially worse (AUROC 0.55). SHAP highlighted BMI, education level, height, sex, arm skinfold thickness, urbanicity, exercise intensity, waist-to-height ratio, and systolic blood pressure as the dominant contributors, and the ordering of the 12 leading predictors showed substantial rank agreement with random-forest permutation importance (Spearman ρ = 0.78). Interpretable tree-based models using simple demographic, behavioural, and anthropometric variables achieved only moderate discrimination for identifying current poor physical fitness in high-altitude adults, with site-wise validation indicating limited but non-trivial transportability. Adiposity and socioeconomic-behavioural features dominated model attribution, although the anthropometric scoring component of the fitness standard partly explains the prominence of body-size variables. As a preliminary screening aid, the model may help prioritise adults for more complete fitness assessment where full testing is difficult, but it should complement rather than replace direct physical fitness assessment and requires independent external validation before use. Not applicable.

papers.title: Clinical performance and practical limitations of large language models in respiratory medicine
papers.authors: Simon Høj, Casper Jensen, Howraman Meteran
papers.abstract: This Journal club discusses three recent studies evaluating large language models (LLMs) in respiratory medicine and allergy. In COPD, ChatGPT-3.5 was rated higher than Bing Chat by respiratory specialists for accuracy, completeness, clarity and safety, although clinically important omissions remained. In asthma, 13 out of 14 models exceeded 85% accuracy on multiple-choice questions and five exceeded 95%, but performance was lower and more variable in objective structured clinical examinations. In allergen immunotherapy, ChatGPT-4 achieved fair overall DISCERN quality, but showed insufficient Journal of the American Medical Association ( JAMA ) benchmark reliability and produced responses that were often difficult to read. Together, these studies show that LLMs perform best on structured and familiar knowledge tasks, while weaknesses persist in completeness, transparency, readability and clinically nuanced application. Current evidence supports supervised educational use in respiratory medicine and allergy, but not unsupervised patient counselling or autonomous clinical deployment.

papers.title: Involving palliative care: Development of a framework for people with life-threatening severe and enduring anorexia nervosa
papers.authors: Noëmie Fauchère, Anna Zumbühl, Tanja Krones, Anna Lisa Westermair, Markus Feuz, Patrick Rodolphe Pasi, Caroline Hertler, David Blum
papers.abstract: Background Anorexia nervosa is a severe metabo-psychosomatic disorder with high morbidity and mortality, predominantly affecting young women. Approximately 20% of anorectic patients develop a severe and enduring course (SE-AN), characterized by repeated unsuccessful specialized treatments, persistent underweight, and marked quality-of-life impairment. While current guidelines emphasize early, multimodal interventions with curative intent, therapeutic options become limited in treatment-refractory cases. Early palliative care integration has been proposed for chronic psychiatric disorders, including SE-AN. Given scarce structured frameworks for such integration, we aimed at developing a treatment framework based on a thorough clinical-ethical analysis and current evidence, integrating palliative care as an additional pathway for SE-AN patients in a University Hospital setting. Methods The standard operating procedure for anorexia nervosa at our tertiary referral centre was comprehensively revised in 2025. Based on structured literature review, clinical experience, and iterative consensus meetings, specialists from psychiatry, palliative care, and clinical ethics collaboratively developed a treatment framework for SE-AN. Ethical roundtables including palliative care specialists were established as core decision-making element. Results Key ethical and clinical controversies were identified, regarding repeated coercive treatments, assessment of patients’ decision-making capacity in severe malnutrition, and concerns about therapeutic futility versus abandonment. Complementing the existing curative pathway, two reversible, patient-centred palliative pathways were defined: (A) harm-reduction prioritizing quality-of-life while tolerating non–life-threatening underweight (BMI >14 kg/m 2 ), integrating somatic stabilization and specialized palliative support; and (B) a best supportive care/end-of-life approach for cases with predominant suffering and very low likelihood of quality-of-life improvement. Advance care planning was incorporated as essential component to ensure goal-concordant care, including emergency planning. Conclusions Structured integration of palliative care into SE-AN management provides an ethically grounded, interdisciplinary framework broadening therapeutic goals beyond weight normalization toward harm reduction and best-possible quality-of-life. Early, needs-based palliative involvement may reduce futile or burdensome interventions while maintaining openness to recovery-oriented care.

papers.title: Noradrenergic gain failure and cognitive-state instability in aging and Alzheimer's disease
papers.authors: Seyyed Kiarash Sadat Rafiei, Mahsa Faramin Lashkarian, Seyede Helma Naseri Sadr, Pariya Yazdani GhareChal, Shahrzad Zarrehparvar Ghouchani Nezhad, Kosar Amini, Bahar Hosseindoost Damuchali, Anita Basiri
papers.journal: Journal of Alzheimer s Disease Reports
papers.abstract: Aging and Alzheimer's disease are usually characterized by average cognitive decline, yet early impairment may also appear as fluctuating attention, variable memory access, inconsistent reaction time, and state-dependent performance. This hypothesis-driven narrative review integrates adaptive gain theory, locus coeruleus–norepinephrine (LC–NE) anatomy and pathology, LC-sensitive MRI, pupillometry, EEG/fMRI state dynamics, sleep research, behavioral variability, and Alzheimer's disease biomarkers to examine how disease-related vulnerability becomes expressed as unreliable cognition. We formulate a reduced control-layer model in which LC–NE dysfunction may weaken the stability of task-relevant neural states. Three candidate latent operating patterns are considered: hypogain, hypertonic noise, and gain mistiming. These patterns occupy continuous and potentially overlapping regions rather than discrete biological subtypes. Individual readouts are nonspecific and correlated; inference therefore requires temporally aligned convergence across dynamic arousal measures, neural-state consequences, behavioral instability, repeated observations, and prespecified alternative explanations. A supplementary forward simulation maps imposed differences in gain amplitude, tonic volatility, and timing onto model outputs but does not estimate latent modes from patient data. The framework predicts that LC-related measures will add explanatory value for cognitive variability and task-state persistence beyond mean performance and Alzheimer's disease biomarker burden. Whether the candidate patterns can be recovered reliably and provide incremental explanatory value remains an empirical question.

papers.title: Epistemic Cognition in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
papers.authors: Rebekah Cole
papers.journal: Journal of Medical Education and Curricular Development
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) makes information increasingly easy to obtain, medical students face a growing challenge: determining what information is credible, when it should be verified, and whether it is appropriate for a particular context. Huang et al.’s finding that students preferred teacher-generated responses even when experts rated several large language models more favorably illustrates the complexity of these judgements. This discrepancy raises a broader question for medical education: How do students decide what information to trust and use in AI-mediated learning environments? Drawing on concepts of epistemic cognition, uncertainty, and competency-based medical education, this commentary argues that responsible AI use requires more than determining whether an AI-generated response is correct. Students need to develop the judgement required to critically evaluate information regardless of whether it comes from AI or a human source. Medical education should therefore make epistemic judgement an explicit focus of instruction and assessment. Structured comparison of human- and AI-generated information offers one approach for making students’ reasoning visible and providing feedback on these capabilities. Future research should examine how students develop and demonstrate epistemic judgement in AI-rich learning environments.

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Powered Chatbots on Self-Directed Learning in Health Sciences Students: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.authors: Amir Torab-Miandoab, Mansour Ghafourifard, Sogand Habibi-Chenaran, Mahsa Maghalian
papers.journal: Journal of Medical Education and Curricular Development
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of AI-powered chatbots on self-directed learning (SDL; primary outcome), satisfaction, confidence, and critical thinking in health professions students. Methods We systematically searched five databases Library up to July 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment (RoB 2 for RCTs; ROBINS-I for quasi-experimental studies). Random-effects meta-analyses using REML estimation were performed, with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals and prediction intervals where feasible. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Results Fourteen studies (11 RCTs, 3 quasi-experimental; N=1,182) met inclusion criteria. Of these, 5 studies (365 participants) contributed to the primary meta-analysis of self-directed learning, 5 studies (320 participants) to satisfaction, and 3 studies (227 participants) to confidence. AI chatbots may improve self-directed learning (Hedges’s g=0.85; 95% HKSJ CI: 0.50-1.21; p=0.003; 5 studies; I 2 =29.1%; prediction interval: 0.21-1.50; low certainty). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness for self-directed learning (SMD range: 0.75–0.93; all p < 0.05). Chatbots may improve satisfaction (g=1.05; 95% CI: 0.36-1.75; p=0.014; 5 studies; I 2 =75.9%; prediction interval: -0.67 to 2.77; low certainty). The confidence finding was methodologically fragile: the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) 95% CI crossed the null (-0.37 to 1.98; p=0.098), whereas the conventional Wald-type CI suggested significance (0.27 to 1.35; p=0.003), underscoring the importance of using HKSJ correction with sparse data. Meta-analysis was not performed for critical thinking and self-efficacy due to extreme heterogeneity. Conclusion AI chatbots may enhance self-directed learning and may improve satisfaction in health professions education. However, the certainty of this evidence is low due to indirectness (variability in SDL measurement tools) and imprecision (sample size below optimal information size). These findings support chatbot integration into pedagogically sound designs, though future research requires longer-term evaluations and standardized measures. In particular, future studies should adopt validated, multi-item SDL scales (e.g., Self-Directed Learning Scale, SRSSDL) to enhance comparability across studies.

papers.title: The effectiveness of health information systems in supporting early detection and referral pathways for high-risk pregnancies: A systematic review
papers.authors: Atma Deharja, Arief Hargono
papers.abstract: Maternal mortality remains a major public health challenge, particularly in low and middle-income countries, where delayed detection and referral of high-risk pregnancies contribute to preventable complications. This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of Health Information Systems (HIS) in supporting the early detection and management of high-risk pregnancies through improved referral processes, monitoring, and clinical decision-making. The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420250641958). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched for peer-reviewed English-language empirical studies published between January 2015 and March 2025. Eligible studies evaluated HIS interventions for maternal health or detection and reported outcomes related to early detection, referral effectiveness, clinical decision support or maternal health improvement. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Findings from 19 eligible studies were synthesized narratively according to HIS type. HIS interventions improved early detection accuracy, antenatal follow-up, screening compliance, and clinical decision support. mHealth improved antenatal care adherence, while telemedicine and telemonitoring supported remote monitoring and reduced unnecessary hospitalization. EHR and e-Registries enhanced risk classification, and artificial intelligence models demonstrated promising predictive performance for preeclampsia and other maternal complications. However, the evidence base was limited by heterogeneous study designs, limited direct mortality outcomes, infrastructure constraints, digital literacy gaps, and interoperability challenges. Direct evidence demonstrating reductions in maternal mortality remains limited. HIS can strengthen maternal surveillance, referral pathways, and clinical decision support for high-risk pregnancies. Sustainable impact requires integrated infrastructure, workforce training, effective data governance, and standardized outcome evaluation.

papers.title: The Discursive Ripples of Human-AI Interaction: A Three-Case Observation Based on Social Distance Theory
papers.authors: Mengjiao Yin, Wei Wang, Wei Xu
papers.abstract: With the proliferation of large language models, Human-AI Interaction (HAI) is shifting from instrumental applications toward emotionally charged relationships, necessitating systematic investigation into its societal implications. Existing research predominantly focuses on the psychological mechanisms of direct users, the so-called “primary effects”, while largely overlooking how HAI generates “secondary effects” across broader societal contexts through public discourse. To address this gap, this study introduces the concept of “discursive ripples” to describe how HAI influences public opinion across varying levels of social distance. Drawing on social distance theory, we propose three analytical layers: the Immediate Interaction Level (IIL), the Proximal Interpersonal Level (PIL), and the Distant Interpersonal Level (DIL). Through a mixed-methods analysis of comment sections from three representative social media cases involving intimate AI relationships, including LDA topic modeling, word co-occurrence network analysis, and sentiment-based content coding, we find that discursive ripples exhibit distinct stratification: IIL users express high levels of empathy and reflection; PIL commenters demonstrate moderate empathy with a relationship-centered perspective; and DIL audiences display cognitive detachment and conceptual prioritization under low empathy. These findings suggest that public perceptions and affective responses toward HAI do not simply attenuate with social distance but undergo a structural transformation, from embodied experience to relational disruption, and ultimately to value negotiation. This study offers a novel empirical pathway for understanding the social embeddedness of AI-intimate relationships and provides an evidence base for differentiated technology governance and public communication strategies.

papers.title: The Transformation of Writing and Creativity Through Artificial Intelligence in Education: A Bibliometric and Thematic Analysis in the Context of Divergent and Convergent Thinking (2000-2025)
papers.authors: Nurullah Aydın
papers.abstract: This study examined the structural and conceptual development of research on writing, creativity, divergent–convergent thinking, and artificial intelligence (AI) in educational contexts from 2000 to 2025. Using a mixed-methods design, 806 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection were analyzed through bibliometric mapping, including publication trends, collaboration networks, and keyword-based conceptual structures. To complement the bibliometric analyses, a thematic analysis was conducted of 22 highly cited, structurally central studies identified through co-citation analysis. The findings indicated a substantial increase in publication and citation activity after 2023, coinciding with the rapid expansion of generative AI research. Bibliometric analyses revealed a growing concentration around a limited number of influential journals, countries, institutions, and collaborative research networks. The thematic analysis identified three interconnected domains: AI-mediated cognitive and writing processes, pedagogical applications and learner experiences, and theoretical and methodological foundations. Across these domains, generative AI, automated feedback, AI literacy, authorship, and academic integrity emerged as closely related areas of inquiry. The findings further showed that cognitive, pedagogical, ethical, and theoretical dimensions were increasingly interconnected within AI-assisted writing research. While convergent thinking processes associated with evaluation, regulation, feedback, and optimization were strongly represented across the literature, divergent thinking processes related to creativity, idea generation, and exploration appeared comparatively less prominent. By integrating bibliometric mapping with thematic analysis, this study provides a comprehensive account of the evolution of AI-assisted writing research and introduces a divergent–convergent analytical perspective to examine how writing, creativity, thinking, and artificial intelligence are conceptualized in contemporary educational research.

papers.title: Extending the Information Adoption Model to Explain Consumer Adoption of AI-Generated Advertising Through Credibility, Relevance, Transparency, Trust, Risk, Experience, and Usefulness
papers.authors: Tanvir Ahmed, S Abdur Rahman, Khaled Hossain Rocky, Bipasha Sukrana, Tasfia Tabassum, Md. Jahid Hasan
papers.abstract: Prior Information Adoption Model (IAM) research explains adoption of online reviews, e-WOM, and social media information, but offers limited evidence on how consumers adopt advertising information generated or personalized through AI. This study extends IAM by integrating message-level evaluations and AI-process evaluations within a partial-mediation framework. Survey data from 462 digitally active consumers were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The model explained 41.2% of the variance in perceived information usefulness and 44.6% of the variance in Intention to Adopt. Information relevance showed the strongest association with perceived information usefulness (β = 0.276, p < 0.001), while trust in AI-generated advertising showed the strongest direct association with Intention to Adopt (β = 0.217, p < 0.001). Perceived AI risk was negatively associated with both perceived information usefulness (β = -0.153, p < 0.001) and Intention to Adopt (β = -0.136, p < 0.001). Perceived information usefulness was also positively associated with Intention to Adopt (β = 0.304, p < 0.001), and all specific indirect effects were significant. The findings refine IAM by showing that usefulness remains central, while consumer adoption of AI-generated advertising is also associated with credibility, relevance, transparency, trust, risk, and prior AI-mediated experience.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Blended Learning: A Mixed-Methods Study
papers.authors: Fatma Nur Büyükbayraktar
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the effects of using artificial intelligence (AI) tools in educational environments. A mixed method was used to investigate the effects of an AI application (ChatGPT) used in a blended environment on achievement scores and students’ learning experiences. The experimental group was given artificial intelligence-based blended learning (AIBL), one control group was given face-to-face learning (F2F), and the other control group was given online learning (OL). The quantitative findings indicated a statistically significant difference among the three instructional conditions in post-test achievement scores, F (2,80) = 7.33, p = .001, η 2 = .16. Post hoc comparisons indicated that the AIBL ( M = 37.58, SD = 10.40) scored significantly higher than the OL ( M = 28.02, SD = 5.90), whereas no statistically significant difference was found between the AIBL and the F2F ( M = 35.40, SD = 10.92; p = .667). These findings suggest that AIBL may offer an advantage over fully OL, while producing achievement outcomes comparable to F2F instruction. Qualitative findings were analysed in the themes of experience with ChatGPT in AIBL, perceived benefits, perceived limitations, and learning support. Preservice teachers believe that the use of AI applications in the educational environment has both positive and negative effects on their learning. ChatGPT’s ability to facilitate students’ access to summarised and focused information was rated positively. Preservice teachers have reported that they sometimes perceived ChatGPT’s answers and operations as incorrect and that this is the main adverse effect of AI. This study provides important insights that will guide the effective use of AI applications in educational environments.

papers.title: Concept Borrowing or Theory Reconstructing? A Bibliometric Analysis of the Impact of AI on Foreign Language Teaching Using MANOVA and PCA Biplot
papers.authors: Liyang Fan, Jiaxing Jiang
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is currently engendering profound changes across multiple disciplinary domains, and foreign language teaching (FLT) is no exception. Previous research on the status quo of the integration between AI and FLT has focused predominantly on bibliometric indicators such as cocitation networks and research hotspots but has failed to depict the essential characteristics of the current integration trend. Therefore, in this research, multivariate statistical analyses (i.e., MANOVA and PCA biplot) is conducted to illustrate the relationships among keyword frequency, betweenness centrality, publication year, and disciplinary category on the basis of the results of the bibliometric analysis. The research suggests a progressive “degeneration–centralization–integration” relationship in the AI and FLT integration process. The MANOVA and PCA biplot results further indicate that within the current hot topics of AI-assisted FLT research, most relevant studies remain at the stage of borrowing concepts from AI, and only a minority attempt to reconstruct FLT theories through AI technology.

papers.title: Constructing University Teachers’ Digital Identity in AI-Enhanced Education: The Mediating Roles of Digital Literacy and Psychological Capital
papers.authors: Chongya Liu, Shuo Liu
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly embedded in higher education, raising important questions about how university teachers understand their professional roles in technology-rich classrooms. Drawing on identity theory, this study examined the associations among human-AI co-teaching, digital literacy, psychological capital, and university teachers’ digital identity. Survey data were collected from 700 university teachers in China and analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapped mediation analysis. The results showed that human-AI co-teaching was positively associated with teachers’ digital identity. Digital literacy and psychological capital both served as significant mediators, indicating that teachers’ cognitive adaptation to digital tools and positive psychological resources are important pathways linking AI-supported teaching practices to digital identity. The study contributes to identity theory by showing how an AI-enhanced teaching context may be connected to teachers’ identity verification through cognitive and affective-motivational resources. Because the study used cross-sectional self-report data from Chinese university teachers, the findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal. The findings suggest that universities should support teachers not only through AI teaching infrastructure but also through digital literacy development and support for psychological capital.

papers.title: Exploring the Editing Quality of ChatGPT and Grammarly in EFL Writing: A Comparative Study
papers.authors: Anas Huneety, Bassil Mohammad Mashaqba, Sahail M. Asassfeh, Haifa Al‐Nofaie, Bara'ah Al-Duneibat
papers.abstract: The quest for improving writing quality, especially in EFL/ESL contexts, has recently led to students’ reliance on automated writing assistance tools (AWATs). This study aims to draw a comparison between two AWATs, ChatGPT and Grammarly, on improving the writing quality of 100 argumentative essays. Ten common writing errors were traced among the students’ compositions, including subject-verb agreement, misuse of articles, verb tense consistency, lack of proper punctuation, monotonous and repetitive writing, over-reliance on literal translation, verbless sentences, lack of cohesion and coherence, collocation errors, and long sentences. Findings demonstrated that both ChatGPT and Grammarly had remarkably improved the quality, readability, and accuracy of student compositions. Yet, ChatGPT was more efficient than Grammarly in addressing collocation patterns, organising long sentences, and enhancing overall coherence. The post-test scores revealed a dramatic improvement in writing quality, with scores rising from an average of 2.50 (SD = 0.092) for essays edited with ChatGPT (M = 4.56/5.00; SD = 0.49) compared to those edited with Grammarly (M = 2.86, SD = 0.76). These results confirm the findings of previous studies that AI-based writing assistance tools can be valuable resources for EFL learners in improving their writing quality. The study emphasises the importance of integrating these tools into writing courses to improve the quality and coherence of written texts, save time and effort, and provide valuable support to learners in their writing development.

papers.title: Predictors of University Students’ Intention to Use ChatGPT for Language Learning: An Integrated Model Based on UTAUT2 and TTAT
papers.authors: Yu Xia, Liwen Zhang
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in language learning, learners’ continuance intention has received growing attention. Based on UTAUT2 and TTAT, this study develops an integrated model to examine how technology acceptance factors and risk avoidance cognitions are associated with continuance intention toward ChatGPT through perceived interactivity. Using standardized scales, a survey of 620 undergraduate students was conducted, and hypotheses were tested via structural equation modeling and multigroup analysis. The results indicate that all UTAUT2 dimensions and perceived avoidability are positively associated with perceived interactivity, whereas perceived threat is negatively associated. Perceived interactivity is positively associated with continuance intention, with a stronger association observed among female students.

papers.title: Bridging Personalization and Pedagogy: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence in Vocabulary Learning
papers.authors: Abdualmuhsin Nagi I. Aldabou, Behbood Mohammadzadeh
papers.abstract: This systematic review explores how artificial intelligence (AI) supports context-based vocabulary learning in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) and English as a Second Language (ESL) contexts. Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework, the review synthesizes evidence from 65 peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2010 and 2025. The findings show that AI can enhance vocabulary learning and learner motivation, particularly when vocabulary is learned through meaningful contexts, interactive activities and adaptive feedback. However, existing evidence focuses mainly on short-term learning gains, with limited understanding of long-term retention, transfer to broader language skills and implementation across diverse educational settings. This review also identifies key gaps in the literature, including the dominance of short-term experimental research, the concentration of studies in higher education and limited attention to collaborative and socially mediated learning. Drawing on these findings, this review proposes an integrated framework linking AI-driven personalization, pedagogical design and learning outcomes. Overall, the evidence suggests that AI has considerable potential to support vocabulary instruction, but its effectiveness depends on how well personalization is aligned with sound pedagogy and meaningful learning experiences.

papers.title: From Neural Machine Translation to Generative AI: A Systematic Review of English Translation Teaching in Higher Education
papers.authors: Haoyu Lu, Jie Guo
papers.abstract: This systematic review aims to synthesise empirical research on GenAI- and NMT-assisted English translation teaching in higher education from 2015 to 2025 and to evaluate cutting-edge teaching outcomes and emerging pedagogical implications. Drawing on 31 studies identified through PRISMA procedures, the review maps the rapid evolution from NMT-based post-editing and output comparison to GenAI-supported feedback, prompting, and collaborative revision. Organised through a task-, course-, and model-level framework and informed by Cognitive Load Theory and Sociocultural Theory, the synthesis shows that NMT and GenAI-supported feedback can improve efficiency, error awareness, and terminological consistency in informational and general academic texts. However, evidence remains conditional and sometimes contradictory: effects on cognitive load, learner motivation, and translation quality vary according to task type, tool quality, learner proficiency, self-regulation, and instructional scaffolding. The review also identifies risks of overreliance, superficial revision, weak prompt or post-editing competence, assessment ambiguity, and unequal access. It therefore argues for sustained, process-oriented pedagogy in which teachers scaffold comparison, revision justification, feedback evaluation, ethical disclosure, and human oversight. Ultimately, the study argues that translation education must strengthen human agency within AI-rich learning, prioritising contextual understanding, value judgement, and intercultural decision-making as core competencies.

papers.title: Enhancing EFL Writing With GenAI: Design, Testing, and Pedagogical Guidelines for Chinese University Classrooms
papers.authors: Min Xiao, Yanhong Huang, Jintao Qu
papers.abstract: This study investigates the integration of generative AI (GenAI) into university-level English writing instruction for Chinese intermediate EFL students, addressing the absence of context-sensitive, needs-based guidelines for AI-supported writing pedagogy. Utilizing survey data from 103 non-English majors and in-depth interviews with students, experienced teachers, and education/AI experts, the research systematically identifies key writing challenges and practical demands for AI support. A mixed-methods design within a design and development research (DDR) framework is employed, combining quantitative analysis, thematic coding, and iterative focus group consultation across three stages: needs analysis, instructional integration mapping, and pedagogical guideline development. The study seeks to characterize learners’ writing-related needs for GenAI support, determine which instructional modules benefit most from GenAI integration, and develop pedagogical guidelines for AI-enhanced writing instruction. Within this framework, an AI-assisted writing prototype was developed and tested using authentic student drafts, with subsequent adjustments informed by classroom feedback and expert evaluation. The findings indicate that vocabulary selection, content organization, and revision remain core difficulties for learners, while GenAI tools are most effective when targeted to workshop and assignment modules and tailored by proficiency levels. The resulting pedagogical guidelines articulate principles for customizing and implementing GenAI-supported writing activities, highlight best practices for teacher facilitation and learner autonomy, and incorporate safeguards to ensure ethical and academic integrity. Overall, this research offers a replicable model for the adaptive integration of GenAI into EFL writing instruction and provides actionable insights for practitioners and platform developers in diverse educational contexts.

papers.title: Traditional and Artificial Intelligence-Supported Constructivist Learning in Health Professions Education
papers.authors: Banan Mukhalalati, Farah Bakri, Alaa Al-Qadhi, Youmna Alalami, Ayat Khan, Sara Elshami, Dalal Hammoudi Halat
papers.abstract: Constructivist learning theory emphasizes active, contextualized, and collaborative knowledge construction. Despite its strong theoretical foundation, evidence of its comprehensive application in health professions education (HPE) remains limited, as most studies focus on isolated strategies rather than constructivism as an integrated framework across disciplines and academic levels. Concurrently, artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in HPE, yet its pedagogical alignment with constructivist principles is poorly understood. This study examines traditional and AI-supported constructivist learning strategies in undergraduate HPE and their influence on students’ preparedness for clinical practice. A mixed-methods approach was used. In the quantitative phase, 466 undergraduate students from HPE programs at Qatar University completed the Constructivist Practices in the Learning Environment questionnaire, assessing seven constructivist domains. In the qualitative phase, focus groups were conducted with a purposive sample of students (n=26). Thematic analysis explored experiences of active engagement, real-world relevance, social interaction, self-regulation, and AI use. The findings indicated that ‘Making meaning through real-life examples’ was the highest-rated domain ( M = 3.84, SD = 0.89), reflecting strong emphasis on contextualized learning. ‘Conceptual conflicts and dilemmas’ scored lowest ( M = 2.57, SD = 0.94), indicating limited exposure to cognitive challenge. Qualitative findings showed that clinical rotations, collaborative activities, and AI tools supported reflection, inquiry, and personalized learning. Students perceived AI as supportive but emphasized the need for instructor guidance. Integrating AI within constructivist learning environments can enhance active and personalized learning in HPE.
