However, deliberate inclusion of conceptual challenges and structured guidance for AI use is necessary to strengthen educational outcomes and clinical readiness among health professions students.

papers.title: Trust in Generative AI and Critical Thinking Among College Students: A Structural Equation Modeling Analysis Based on Perceived Usefulness, Cognitive Offloading, and AI Self-Efficacy
papers.authors: Yanjun Cheng, Muyan Li
papers.abstract: This study examines how college students’ trust in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is associated with critical thinking engagement in GenAI-supported learning through multiple psychological mechanisms. Drawing on Distributed Cognition Theory (DCT), we propose and test a structural model including five constructs: trust in AI, perceived usefulness, cognitive offloading, AI self-efficacy, and critical thinking. Drawing on survey data from a convenience sample of college students who engaged in learning activities using GenAI tools (e.g., ChatGPT), we assessed hypothesized relationships using structural equation modeling (SEM). The results show that trust in AI is positively associated with perceived usefulness and AI self-efficacy, and both constructs are positively associated with critical thinking. In contrast, cognitive offloading is negatively associated with critical thinking, indicating a potential constraining pathway through which stronger reliance on GenAI may be associated with lower engagement in higher-order thinking. Overall, the findings suggest that trust in GenAI is linked to critical thinking through both supportive and constraining pathways. This study extends DCT in GenAI-supported learning by showing that trust in AI is not uniformly beneficial. The findings highlight the importance of educational approaches that cultivate students’ efficacy beliefs and strategic use of GenAI while discouraging overreliance that reduces cognitive engagement.

papers.title: AI Policy, Innovation, and Green Productivity: Quasi-Experimental Evidence From China
papers.authors: Wenqing Li, Xiaobing Peng
papers.abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has garnered significant attention as both a driving force for green innovation and a potential source of environmental pressure. However, empirical research on its policy-driven effects remains relatively limited. This study examines the impact of China’s “National New Generation Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Application Pilot Zones” (AIIDPZ) on urban green total factor productivity (GTFP). Using panel data from 280 prefecture-level cities between 2013 and 2023, the study employs a difference-in-differences (DID) model for empirical analysis and validates the reliability of the results through robustness tests such as instrumental variable estimation, placebo tests, and propensity score matching. The study finds that the AIIDPZ significantly enhances the GTFP levels of pilot cities. Mechanism analysis reveals three pathways: first, policies promote green technological innovation by improving educational standards; second, they enhance GTFP by improving energy efficiency and optimizing resource allocation; and third, they drive green development by improving digital infrastructure. Heterogeneity tests indicate that policy effects are more pronounced in non-resource-based cities, regions with more advanced industrial structures, smaller cities, and areas with weaker digital infrastructure. This study enriches empirical evidence on the promotion of sustainable productivity by AI policies at the micro level, expands academic discussions on the “double-edged sword” effect of AI, and provides policy implications for formulating AI strategies that balance technological innovation and low-carbon development.

papers.title: Aligning AI and Human Feedback in EFL Writing: A Mixed-Methods Comparison of ChatGPT, Peer, and Teacher Feedback
papers.authors: Jui-Jung Tsao, Chih-yang Liu
papers.abstract: This mixed-methods study compared three feedback modalities—ChatGPT-only feedback, ChatGPT plus peer feedback with checklist and peer writing conferences, and ChatGPT plus teacher oral feedback during writing conferences—in an EFL writing course. Twenty-five second-year university English majors participated in a semester-long intervention, completing three writing assignments and receiving feedback according to their group. Quantitative analyses of the 22 participants with complete pretest and posttest data indicated significant overall improvement, with statistically significant gains observed only in the ChatGPT plus peer feedback with checklist and peer writing conferences group; between-group comparisons showed no significant differences. Qualitative analysis of 22 complete open-ended surveys revealed that each feedback method offered distinct advantages and challenges across four dimensions: satisfaction, motivation, engagement, and perceived effectiveness. ChatGPT feedback was valued for its immediacy and technical accuracy, but was seen as impersonal and less supportive of higher-order skills. Peer feedback was perceived as supporting collaboration and motivation, although inconsistencies in quality were noted. Teacher-supported feedback was valued for promoting clearer understanding by contextualizing ChatGPT suggestions, although motivational responses were mixed and conference time was limited. Findings suggest that a blended feedback approach integrating ChatGPT and human feedback may support writing improvement and engagement. Pedagogical recommendations include training students to interpret ChatGPT feedback, improving peer review practices, and increasing structured teacher-student interactions to complement technological affordances.

papers.title: A Training Program for Improving Teachers’ Knowledge and Attitudes Toward AI Apps Supporting Speech and Language Skills of Deaf and Hard-Of-Hearing Students
papers.authors: Nourah Ibrahim Abdullah Albash
papers.abstract: The current study aimed to examine the effectiveness of a training program designed for improving teachers’ knowledge and attitudes toward the use of applications (apps) enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) to develop the language skills of Deaf and Hard-of-hearing (DHH) students. The goal was not only to measure general improvements but also to explore whether specific teacher characteristics influenced the outcomes of the training. The study sample consisted of 31 female elementary school teachers of DHH students in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. A quasi-experimental approach (Single-group design (was applied that incorporated a scale and program developed by the author. The study measured changes in knowledge and attitudes before and after the intervention. The findings indicate statistically significant differences in the participants’ scores on pre- and post-tests of knowledge and attitudes in favor of post-training, indicating the effectiveness of the training program. No statistically significant differences regarding the of attitudes dimension were found related to the variables of participants’ educational achievement, years of teaching experience, grade level taught, or type of DHH teaching specialization. However, statistically significant differences regarding knowledge were found related to the sole variable of teaching specialization in favor of those with specialization in deaf education over those with specializations in hard of hearing education and the comprehensive category of DHH education. These findings emphasize the importance of structured training in preparing teachers to effectively use AI-enhanced language learning apps with DHH students and ensure all DHH teachers are ready to integrate AI technologies into their classrooms.
keywords: deaf and hard of hearing students

papers.title: Engaging the Human Mind: The Effects of Anthropomorphism on Engagement, Trust, and Ad Attitude in Fashion Brands
papers.authors: Md. Asaduzzaman Babu
papers.abstract: This study examines the role of anthropomorphism in AI-driven fashion advertising and its impact on consumer engagement, perceived trust, and attitude toward advertisements. Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) model, the study conceptualizes anthropomorphism as a stimulus that is positively associated with cognitive and emotional engagement, which, in turn, shapes consumer responses. A quantitative research design was employed using survey data collected from fashion consumers, and the proposed model was tested using structural equation modeling. The findings reveal that anthropomorphic features in fashion advertisements significantly enhance both cognitive and emotional engagement, thereby fostering greater trust and more favorable attitudes toward the advertisements. The study further demonstrates the mediating role of engagement in linking anthropomorphism with consumer outcomes. These results contribute to the literature by extending the S-O-R model to AI-driven fashion advertising and by highlighting the importance of human-like design elements in shaping consumer psychology. The results of this study provide empirical support to the idea that advertisements featuring AI with human-like characteristics can increase consumer engagement with brands by appealing to their cognitive and emotional processes. Marketers can enhance consumer trust and favorable ad evaluations by designing AI-driven campaigns that strike a balance between human-like features and emotionally and cognitively engaging content. In addition, the classical idea that human design alone improves positive appraisal is refined through this dual-mediation method. Instead, the results provide a process-oriented explanation that has been overlooked in prior research that anthropomorphism’s effectiveness depends on the extent to which the consumer is emotionally and cognitively invested.

papers.title: “Why I Do It and What I Can Do”: How Hedonic/Eudaimonic Motives Foster Environmental Passion and Pre-stage Value Co-creation Behaviors in the National Park Science Popularization Volunteering Activity
papers.authors: Changbin Xu, Dengming Xie, Biao He, Yanfei Tang, Yueli Tang
papers.abstract: Encouraging diverse stakeholders to actively take part as volunteers in the sustainability of national parks is a common practice; nevertheless, a central challenge for volunteer managers is how to enhance these participants’ active participation and value co-creation. Given that, the purpose of this study is to uncover the mechanism from participation motives to value co-creation behavior. Members in the Hainan national park science popularization volunteering activity were invited to participate in a questionnaire survey, yielding a total of 437 valid responses. PLS-SEM was employed to test the conceptual model. The findings indicate that eudaimonic motives exert strong direct effects on environmental passion and indirect effects on pre-stage value co-creation behaviors, whereas the impacts of hedonic motives are weak and negligible. Environmental passion positively affects both attitude towards the volunteering activity and pre-stage value co-creation behaviors. Attitude towards the volunteering activity exerts a positive effect on pre-stage value co-creation behaviors, and prior knowledge positively moderated this relationship. This study enriches the knowledge on the mechanism of how hedonic/eudaimonic motives toward the volunteering activity differentially affect actors’ emotion, cognition, and behavior. It also offers volunteering project organizers and national park managers practical and actionable guidance.

papers.title: Learner Resources and Grammar Achievement in AI-Assisted EFL Learning: A Motivation-Mediation Model in Chinese Private Higher Education
papers.authors: Yadan Wang, Soon Singh Bikar Singh
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted grammar learning is increasingly common in higher education, yet grammar achievement cannot be assumed to follow automatically from tool access. This study tested a motivation-mediation model linking academic engagement, self-management, and AI literacy with grammar achievement through intrinsic motivation. Grounded mainly in self-determination theory and supported by self-regulated learning and AI literacy frameworks, the study used a quantitative cross-sectional design. Data were collected from 438 non-English-major undergraduates enrolled in a compulsory English as a foreign language (EFL) grammar course at a private undergraduate university in southern China. Students completed adapted measures of academic engagement, self-management, AI literacy, and intrinsic motivation; official end-of-semester grammar examination scores were used as the achievement outcome. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples was used to evaluate the measurement model, direct paths, indirect effects, and explanatory-predictive performance. Results showed that academic engagement, self-management, and AI literacy were positively associated with intrinsic motivation, with self-management showing the strongest path. All four direct paths to grammar achievement were statistically significant, although incremental effect sizes were small. Intrinsic motivation partially mediated the associations of academic engagement, self-management, and AI literacy with grammar achievement. The model explained 45.2% of the variance in intrinsic motivation and 24.0% of the variance in grammar achievement. The findings suggest that AI-assisted grammar learning depends on a broader configuration of learner resources, especially self-management and intrinsic motivation, rather than on AI literacy alone. Because the data were cross-sectional, the results should be interpreted as model-based associations rather than causal effects.

papers.title: Role-Based Differences in Self-Assessed Professional Competence for AI-Mediated Psychological Crisis Management Among Higher Education Professionals
papers.authors: Mao Li, Zhiyi Long, Bingqing Li
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to identify and manage psychological crisis risk in higher education, yet little is known about how professionals in different institutional roles perceive their competence once AI-generated signals enter student-support decisions. This study aimed to examine self-assessed professional competence across five dimensions of the Student-Centred AI Professional Competence Model (SC-AIPCM) among higher education professionals. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 322 higher education professionals in Central China. Separate and simultaneously adjusted multivariate models assessed differences by professional role, experience, educational qualification, and gender. The results show that professional role remained associated with human–AI boundary judgement after adjustment, whereas experience showed no reliable multivariate pattern. Educational qualification remained strongly associated with all five dimensions in adjusted and heteroscedasticity-robust analyses; however, all doctoral respondents were men and their scores showed marked range restriction, precluding a clean separation of education and gender. Broad unadjusted gender differences were substantially attenuated after adjustment. The findings concern self-assessed rather than demonstrated competence and support role-sensitive development, human contestability, and clearer institutional accountability.

papers.title: Teaching Strategy Linkages in University Entrepreneurship Education: A Human-AI Collaborative Learning Perspective
papers.authors: Dan Chen, Jinling Wang, 朱士友, 王梦瑶
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly integrated into university entrepreneurship courses, how teaching strategies are associated with students’ entrepreneurial competencies remains insufficiently understood. From the perspective of Human-AI Collaborative Learning, this study combines structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis to examine the linkage structure between five teaching strategies and university students’ entrepreneurial competencies from both variable-level and configurational perspectives. The findings show that reflective guidance strategy and feedback strategy display stable associations across both analyses and serve as key links connecting GAI outputs with students’ deeper cognitive processing. Scaffolding strategy provides strong process support at the variable level, but it also shows configurational substitutability: when task design strategy, collaborative organization strategy, and feedback strategy are jointly configured, part of the process-support function of scaffolding may be jointly assumed by other teaching conditions. Task design strategy and collaborative organization strategy do not show uniformly significant net effects across all competency dimensions, yet they become important contextual conditions in specific configurations. Based on these results, this study proposes a three-layer collaborative framework consisting of cognitive regulation, process support, and contextual construction, suggesting that teaching strategies in Human-AI Collaborative Learning show functional differentiation and hierarchical linkage. The findings provide empirical evidence for understanding the relationship between teaching strategies and competency performance in Human-AI Collaborative Learning and offer practical implications for integrating GAI into university entrepreneurship education.

papers.title: Determinants and Impact of AI-Based Chatbot Adoption in Higher Education: A TAM–ISSM Perspective
papers.authors: Mehmet Fikret Gelibolu
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has the potential to transform higher education by enabling data-driven learning design and evidence-based educational decision-making. Among GenAI applications, chatbots provide real-time feedback, content support, and personalized guidance, thereby reshaping the way students engage with learning environments. While the use of AI-based chatbots by students is becoming increasingly widespread, empirical evidence on their adoption and impact in higher education remains limited. This study investigates the determinants of GenAI–based chatbot adoption and its perceived educational impact among university students, integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and the Information System Success Model. Drawing on survey data from 303 university students collected through online questionnaires and analysed via PLS-SEM, the findings highlight the critical role of perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, information quality, system quality, and instructor attitude in shaping satisfaction and continued usage. Furthermore, results demonstrate that GenAI-based chatbot usage is perceived by students to significantly enhance their academic performance, learning motivation, and productivity. Beyond adoption dynamics, this study underscores how AI-based chatbots can contribute to the future of AI-supported learning design by clarifying which system and user level factors drive engagement and effectiveness. In particular, the unique focus on students’ perceptions of instructor attitude provides new insights for curriculum modifications, showing how perceived faculty endorsement legitimizes AI use and contributes to more inclusive and effective technology integration. By connecting adoption, satisfaction, and individual learning outcomes, this research contributes to ongoing debates on how GenAI tools can support evidence-based educational decision-making and the design of learning environments.

papers.title: A Study on User Satisfaction With Generative Artificial Intelligence: From the Perspective of the Technology Acceptance Model
papers.authors: Min Tang, Renqiang Xie
papers.abstract: While generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) drives innovation across various domains, user satisfaction varies considerably under the influence of multiple factors, including ethical compliance and technical performance. Existing studies on user satisfaction with GenAI lack systematic investigation of multidimensional factors and provide limited analysis of the underlying influence mechanisms. To explore the key influencing factors and their underlying mechanisms, this paper develops a user satisfaction model for GenAI based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), integrating three dimensions: legal-ethical considerations, technical attributes, and user capabilities. A total of 408 valid questionnaire responses were collected, and CB-SEM (Covariance-Based Structural Equation Modeling) analysis was performed using AMOS 26.0 software. The empirical results indicate that technical reliability exerts a significant positive effect on user trust ( β =0.43, P <0.001) and satisfaction ( β =0.305, P <0.05), and also significantly promotes perceived usefulness. Technical literacy has significant positive impacts on perceived ease-of-use ( β =0.356, P <0.001) and user trust ( β =0.168, P <0.05); it influences satisfaction through multiple pathways including independent mediation and chained mediation of “perceived ease-of-use → perceived usefulness” and trust. Perceived usefulness significantly and positively drives user satisfaction ( β =0.267, P <0.001). Ethical compliance directly improves user satisfaction ( β =0.127, P <0.01), yet shows no significant effect on user trust. User trust plays a partial mediating role between technical reliability and user satisfaction. This study broadens the analytical perspective on user behavior toward GenAI, and provides empirical evidence and practical guidance for enterprises seeking to optimize technical services, regulators to formulate policies, and interventions for improving user literacy.

papers.title: Factors Affecting the AIGC Implementation in Chinese Higher Design Education: DEMATEL Analysis With Structured Expert Elicitation
papers.authors: Fangyuan Zhang, Can Wei Zhu
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming global higher education, yet its integration into the design discipline presents unique challenges at the intersection of technological innovation and creative autonomy. To date, systematic understanding of the factors influencing artificial intelligence in design education remains fragmented. This study aims to identify key factors affecting the application of AIGC in higher design education in China. A preliminary system of influencing factors was identified through a systematic literature review. Evaluation data from 15 experts were analyzed using the DEMATEL method. The Technology-Organization- Environment framework serves as the theoretical foundation for this study, 17 factors across the dimensions of technology, organization, and environment was constructed. In the technical dimension, creativity support emerged as the core driving factor, while three risk-related factors, such as dependence risk, had higher weights, which highlight the importance of risk management. The organizational dimension revealed a closely connected network of factors, including attitude, ability, and knowledge. Among these, facilitating conditions emerged as the most influential factor, forming the basis for strengthening other organizational elements. In the environmental dimension, policies and regulations were the most prominent. Although the digital divide received the lowest weight in the analysis, it showed the strongest causal influence, which reflects its critical role in promoting educational equity. This research reveals characteristic factors and their mechanisms within the Chinese context. It offers data-driven insights for international educators, policymakers, and technology developers to balance AI-driven efficiency with human-centered creativity in design education.

papers.title: From AI-Generated Answers to Collaborative Inquiry: How Socratic Questioning Scaffolds Reorganize Peer Dialogic Feedback in GenAI-Supported Learning
papers.authors: Rongqing Zhuo, Xin Sun
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can enrich peer dialogic feedback, yet its educational value depends on whether learners critically examine AI-generated content rather than accept it as ready-made knowledge. This study investigated how Socratic questioning scaffolding reorganizes peer dialogic feedback in a GenAI-supported collaborative learning environment. In an eight-week classroom intervention, 94 undergraduates were stratified by gender and learning orientation and randomly assigned to a scaffolded GenAI condition or a control condition with basic dialogue support. A total of 1,980 valid discourse units were analyzed through SOLO-based cognitive engagement coding, IRF-based feedback behavior coding, lag sequential analysis, epistemic network analysis, and mixed-effects models accounting for discourse units nested within students and collaborative groups. Results showed that the scaffolded condition was associated with higher cognitive engagement and a greater likelihood of response- and feedback-level dialogue behaviors. Sequential and network analyses further indicated that Socratic questioning shifted dialogue from linear question-answer exchanges toward progressive cycles of questioning, elaboration, and constructive suggestion, with more integrative cognitive structures centered on relational reasoning. These findings suggest that Socratic questioning may help reposition GenAI outputs from endpoints of answer acceptance as shared objects of verification, comparison, reconstruction, and collaborative inquiry.

papers.title: Earning Trust Through Clarity: A Sequential Model of ChatGPT Clarification, Uncertainty Reduction, and Destination Visit Intention
papers.authors: Adi Prasetyo Tedjakusuma, Joshi Maharani Wibowo, Andri Dayarana K. Silalahi
papers.abstract: Tourism decisions are uncertainty-intensive, committing resources to experiential outcomes only knowable after consumption. Grounded in Uncertainty Reduction Theory (URT), we position ChatGPT as a conversational tool tourists use to clarify uncertain travel decisions. We test a sequential model in which tourism decision uncertainty — a higher-order construct spanning choice, knowledge, needs, and outcome facets — increases clarification seeking from ChatGPT, which enhances perceived uncertainty reduction, strengthens trust in ChatGPT recommendations, and raises destination visit intention. Survey data analyzed via two-stage PLS-SEM support this chain: uncertainty reduction and trust both directly predict visit intention, with trust partially mediating the uncertainty reduction–intention link. Findings inform destination managers, travel agencies, and chatbot developers designing and governing AI-based decision support. The study extends URT to generative conversational AI, identifying clarification seeking as its mechanism, trust as the main bridge to action, and uncertainty reduction alone as sometimes sufficient to prompt intention before full trust forms.

papers.title: Game Theory Research on the Development and Promotion of Artificial Intelligence Teaching Platform Based on Multi-Participant University-Enterprise Collaboration
papers.authors: Haoran Qiu, Xianglong Li, Yun Wang
papers.abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence and education, university-enterprise cooperation has become a key approach for the development and promotion of artificial intelligence (AI) teaching platforms. However, differences in the interests of various stakeholders lead to insufficient stability in cooperation. Therefore, based on evolutionary game theory, this study constructs a dynamic game model involving enterprises, universities, and teachers. By establishing a replicating dynamic equation, the equilibrium point is solved and its stability is analyzed. Numerical simulations are then used to explore the evolutionary mechanism of each stakeholder’s strategy and key influencing factors. The study finds that enterprise strategy selection is influenced by teacher feedback and university support; university decisions focus on long-term educational benefits; and teachers’ willingness to use the platform depends on the balance between learning costs and benefits. Simulation analysis shows that factors such as benefit structure, training costs, and financial rewards significantly affect the evolutionary trend. This research provides theoretical basis and practical insights for promoting industry-university collaboration and optimizing platform construction and promotion.

papers.title: AI Identity Threat and Creative Teaching Among College Teachers: A Job Demands-Resources Mechanism With the Moderating Roles of AI Literacy and Organizational Support
papers.authors: Yan Li, Eric Mao
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has raised growing concerns about its potential to threaten educators’ professional identities. Although prior research has examined AI identity threat in general workplace settings, its implications for creative teaching in higher education, a highly discretionary and self-initiated pedagogical behavior, remain insufficiently addressed. Drawing on the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) framework, this study conceptualizes AI identity threat as an identity-based job demand and examines its motivational and strain-related mechanisms. Using snowball sampling with a 15-day interval, data were collected from 538 college teachers. The results reveal that AI identity threat negatively predicts teachers’ motivation and positively predicts strain. Motivation is positively associated with creative teaching, whereas strain is negatively associated with it. Moreover, motivation is positively associated with meaningfulness of work, job satisfaction, and work engagement, while strain is positively related to role conflict, emotional exhaustion, and psychological distress. Regarding buffering conditions from job resources, AI literacy attenuates the negative effect of AI identity threat on motivation but does not significantly reduce its effect on strain. In contrast, perceived organizational support weakens the positive relationship between AI identity threat and strain but does not significantly moderate its effect on motivation. Overall, this study advances our understanding of how AI-induced identity threats shape the psychological processes and creative teaching behaviors of college teachers within a JD-R framework.

papers.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Enhanced Analysis of Online Course Reviews: An Empirical Study on Sentiment Analysis, Satisfaction Prediction, and Topic Modeling
papers.authors: Wen Jun Xiao, Juan Hu
papers.abstract: Online course reviews encapsulate students’ authentic feedback on course content, teaching implementation, and learning experiences, serving as critical data for evaluating online course quality. This study examined the efficacy of five high-performing Large Language Models (LLMs)—namely DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-plus, ChatGPT, GPT-4, and Claude-4—in analyzing online course reviews, with a focus on three core analytical tasks: sentiment analysis, satisfaction prediction, and topic modeling. The results showed that LLMs could generate comprehensive, pedagogically sound analytical prompts from minimal input, integrating appropriate methodologies and logical procedural steps. For sentiment analysis, LLM-based results demonstrated higher alignment with expert annotations (Cohen’s Kappa = 0.61, Mutual Information = 0.24). In satisfaction prediction, the models produced estimates closer to students’ actual ratings (Mean Absolute Error [MAE] = 0.11, Root Mean Square Error [RMSE] = 0.18, Pearson’s Correlation = 0.69). For topic modeling, the extracted topics and associated terms exhibited superior coherence (C_v = 0.64, UMPI = 0.45), interpretability, and functional relevance. Additionally, through LLM-driven topic modeling, four key dimensions influencing students’ satisfaction with online courses were identified: course design and organization, instructional content quality, learning and assessment activities, and instructor support and services. This study reveals comparative strengths of LLMs when processing online course reviews, and offers empirically grounded practical references for educators and relevant educational organizations.

papers.title: Development Strategies of Lingnan Ceramic Cultural and Creative Industries in the AI Era: A Visualization Analysis Based on CiteSpace
papers.authors: Xiao Song, Longjia Cai, Qian Yu, Yudan Shen
papers.abstract: This study constructs a bibliometric knowledge map on the ceramic cultural and creative industries in the Lingnan region, examines their developmental trajectories, and proposes corresponding strategies for innovation and transformation in the age of artificial intelligence. Drawing on CiteSpace, the study employs bibliometric methods to visually analyze relevant scholarly publications from six dimensions: publication volume, disciplinary distribution, author and institutional collaboration, national and regional distribution, research hotspots, and emerging trends. The analysis reveals that owing to the constraints imposed by region-specific research, a systematic research on the ceramic cultural and creative industries has yet to take shape and the lack of international collaboration has further limited the depth of scholarly inquiry. Meanwhile, the research focus has gradually shifted from ceramic material technology and cultural-creative product development to AI-enabled research and development of new ceramic materials and the dissemination of ceramic culture, with current hotspots encompassing diversified technological innovation and industrial upgrading. Therefore, by constructing the evolutionary model of research findings in the ceramic cultural and creative industries in the Lingnan region, this study provides a case reference for the innovation of regional ceramic cultural heritage and the transformation and upgrading of the industries.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Education: Conceptual Dimensions, Trends, and Research Directions
papers.authors: Seda AKTI ASLAN, Ahmet Ayaz, Özcan Özyurt, Alper Aslan
papers.abstract: Research into generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in the field of education has been growing rapidly in recent years. The rapid expansion of the literature has necessitated a systematic examination of the field. In this study, the thematic structure of GenAI research in the field of education during the 2023–2025 period was examined. Given the need to work with a large-scale dataset comprising 15,036 studies, a Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)-based topic modelling analysis was selected. A search conducted on Scopus resulted in the inclusion of 15,036 studies in the analysis. The LDA analysis identified 12 prominent topics based on consistency scores. Descriptively, these prominent topics were grouped under four broad thematic areas. Among these axes, the technical axis holds the largest share (25%). It was observed that whilst technical topics were on the rise during the 2023–2025 period, topics such as ethics and chatbots showed a relative downward trend. The observed trends suggest that scholarly attention is increasingly directed towards technically oriented research. The findings also indicate a need for theoretical frameworks to ensure pedagogical depth. It is anticipated that the study’s findings will serve as an important reference point for future research.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Tools in English-Medium Academic Publishing: A Comparative Study of Scholarly Writing Practices in Iraq and Türkiye
papers.authors: Sami Alhasnawi, Batuhan Selvi, Mustafa Radif, Suheyla Demirkol Orak
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of AI writing tools, combined with English’s dominance in academic publishing, creates new challenges for multilingual scholars. This comparative qualitative study examines how academics in Iraq and Türkiye use AI when writing for English-medium publication—translating, drafting, paraphrasing, editing, and etc. Interviews with 92 scholars across disciplines were analyzed through Academic Literacies and Sociotechnical theories, focusing on who or what brokers scholars’ access to English-medium conventions and how infrastructure and institutional conditions shape that brokering. Both settings are resource-constrained, with limited, unevenly distributed internet access, paid-tool funding, and institutional training. Findings show AI’s role in scholarly writing depends on the writer’s available infrastructure. Iraqi scholars relied mainly on free platforms for translation and grammar checking, while Turkish participants used paid tools more strategically for argument development and stylistic revision. Both groups reported little institutional guidance and instead developed informal personal rules about acceptable assistance. Challenges included unstable connectivity, restricted access to paid features, uncertain institutional expectations, and limited training. Participants distinguished language repair from content generation, independently verified AI-produced information, and treated acceptability as varying by genre and discipline. They envisioned discipline-specific, culturally responsive tools that support rather than replace scholarly authorship. This is, to our knowledge, the first cross-national comparison of AI-supported academic writing in two Middle Eastern higher education systems. The findings extend literacy-brokering accounts by showing how AI-mediated support’s quality hinges on access to paid resources, and suggest equitable AI integration requires context-sensitive policy, infrastructure investment, and ethical guidelines that preserve authentic scholarly voice.
keywords: higher education in the Middle East

papers.title: Effectiveness of a Community-Based Stroke Prevention Intervention Among Older Adults at High Risk of Stroke: A Quasi-Experimental Study in China
papers.authors: Min Gao, Kwanjai Amnatsatsue, Patcharaporn Kerdmongkol, Natkamol Chansatitporn, Ariya Bunngamchairat
papers.journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health
papers.abstract: Objectives To evaluate the effectiveness of a community-based primary health care (CB-PHC) intervention for stroke prevention among older adults at high risk. Methods A quasi-experimental study was conducted in two communities in Xinxiang City, China, including adults aged 60-79 years at high stroke risk. The intervention group (n = 33) received a 12-week CB-PHC intervention based on the World Health Organization (WHO) Technical Package for Cardiovascular Disease Management in Primary Health Care (HEARTS) package and the Innovative Care for Chronic Conditions Framework (ICCCF), while the comparison group (n = 32) received usual care. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention using linear mixed models. Results All 65 participants completed the study, with no baseline differences between groups (all P > 0.05). Significant group × time interactions were observed for all outcomes (all P < 0.001). The intervention group showed significant improvements in stroke-related knowledge, self-management, and physiological risk factors, including body-mass index (BMI) (β = −2.91), blood pressure (including systolic blood pressure (SBP) β = −3.82; diastolic blood pressure (DBP) β = −4.25), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) (β = −0.85), and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) (β = −1.08). Satisfaction with CB-PHC services also increased significantly (β = 1.32). Conclusions The CB-PHC intervention improved behavioral, cognitive, and clinical outcomes, supporting its potential as a scalable strategy for stroke prevention in high-risk older adults.

papers.title: Empowerment, not replacement: How AI trust fosters green creativity among tourism hotel managers through green self-efficacy and green job crafting
papers.authors: WANG KANG, Ah Kiaw Phan, Shee Mun Yong
papers.abstract: The prevailing narrative of AI as a threat to human replacement fosters anxiety and undermines sustainability goals in the hotel industry. In contrast, the current research reimagines AI as an enabling force. Based on social cognitive theory, a two-path model is constructed to investigate how AI trust empowers hotel managers to achieve green creativity and generate novel and useful environmental protection ideas. Through a cross-sectional survey of 253 hotel managers in Hainan, China, this study found that AI trust not only directly promotes green creativity, but more importantly, it operates through two unique enabling mechanisms. First, it achieves cognitive empowerment by enhancing managers’ green self-efficacy. Second, it achieves behavioral empowerment by incentivizing green job crafting. The results confirm that green self-efficacy and green job crafting are significant and parallel mediating variables. This research shifts the discourse from substitution to empowerment, providing a novel perspective on AI as a partner in the tourism industry. It demonstrates that cultivating AI trust can unleash the agency of managers, transforming them into proactive contributors to a sustainable and innovative future for the industry. These insights are crucial for tourism stakeholders seeking to leverage human and technological assets for a competitive advantage.

papers.title: A Landscape of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Student Dropouts in Developing Countries: Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Yuda N. Mnyawami, Hellen H. Maziku, Joseph Cosmas Mushi
papers.abstract: In Sub-Saharan countries the student dropout rate elevated to 19% of secondary school age, followed by Northern Africa and Western Asia (9%) and Southern Asia (7%) in 2019. In Tanzania, student dropouts in secondary schools increased from 3.8% in 2018 to 4.2% in 2019. The persisting dropout problem especially in secondary schools is attributed to a lack of proper identification of root causes and unavailability of formal methods that can be used to project the severity of the problem. This study applied PICO and PRISMA to conduct systematic literature reviews to analyze and synthesize and report key results. Digital databases such as ACM library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google scholar yielded 21 exhaustive articles from January 2014 to October 2023 regarding the student dropout features identification using machine learning models. Results revealed that distance, absence, child pregnancy, early marriage, and family income are the most evident predictors for student dropout. Presented articles did not cover psychological features leading to student dropout in developing countries. Student dropouts have complex psychological and behavioral issues demand a comprehensive analysis and understanding by machine learning algorithms. Disassociating psychological factors in dropout prediction remains inappropriately answered to determine root causes of student dropouts. Moreover, this study intends to synthesize the prediction accuracy of ML models when influential features are applied to predict student dropout in developing countries. This study concluded by highlighting the most evident Machine learning algorithms that showed high prediction accuracy; Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Neural Networks, and K -Nearest Neighbors.

papers.title: Neuro-Design Strategies in Enclosed Spaces: The Impact of Visual Openness on Attention, Memory, and Physiological Stress
papers.authors: İlker Erkan
papers.abstract: This study investigates the impact of systematically increasing window number—and thus visual access—on cognitive performance and physiological stress in enclosed spaces. Visual access was operationalized by the number of windows, luminance levels, and window-to-wall ratio (0–40%). Seventy participants experienced five controlled environments (0–4 windows) in a Latin square design, while completing three cognitive tasks: Flanker (attention), D2 (selective attention), and N-Back (working memory). Physiological responses were recorded through electroencephalography (EEG, alpha/beta power) and galvanic skin response (GSR). Results revealed a dose-dependent effect of visual openness: as window number increased, reaction times shortened, accuracy improved, and working memory performance increased. EEG analyses indicated higher frontal beta activity and reduced alpha suppression in windowed conditions, while GSR levels decreased significantly with greater visual access. These findings demonstrate that incremental increases in visual openness enhance both cognitive efficiency and stress regulation. Beyond advancing the neuro-architectural understanding of window design, the study provides evidence-based guidelines for interior design and architectural practice, particularly in workplaces and learning environments where cognitive load and well-being are critical.

papers.title: Neurotrauma During Military Training: Results of the INVestigating traIning assoCiated blasT pAthology (INVICTA) Study
papers.authors: Michael J. Roy, David O. Keyser, Marcia Dovel, Rie Leverett, Alexander Hill, Kenneth Andres Manlapaz, Christopher K. Rhea, Joshua T. Lawton, Thaddeus J. Haight, Chen Lai, Devon Kulinski, Douglas S. Brungart, Grant D. Tays, Walter S. Carr
papers.abstract: Concern is growing that subconcussive blast exposure during military exercises such as heavy weapons training (HWT) may adversely affect brain function. HWT involves firing shoulder-mounted weapons that can expose the gunner, assistant gunner, and instructors (range safety officers [RSOs]) to blast overpressure >4.0 psi. Every HWT participant sustains repeated blast exposure: gunner and assistant alternate firing within an event, and instructors supervise multiple firings at approximately 12 HWTs over two years. This five-year study was designed to quantify blast exposure and serially assess a broad array of brain function measures in HWT participants and corresponding controls. Two hundred and twenty-four participants were prospectively assessed: 104 exposed special operators (SOs) firing live rounds in HWT; 47 SOs completing land warfare training without firing live rounds during HWT (training controls); 36 conventional active duty controls (ADCs); and 37 instructors. Assessments were conducted at baseline and at 30 min, 6, 24, and 72 h, 2 weeks, and 3 months post-HWT. Instructors were also assessed 9 and 18 months after their first HWT, with repeat of all acute assessments (30 min through 3 months) after their 18-month HWT. Blast exposure was measured with the Black Box Biometrics Generation 7 Blast Gauge System. Assessments included blood biomarkers, symptom scales, memory, cerebrovascular reactivity, electroencephalography (EEG), oculomotor function, gait, tactile discrimination, and hearing acuity. SOs exhibited significant alterations in short-term memory, complexity of electroencephalographic signals, and the blood biomarkers tau and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 within minutes after HWT, while gait and oculomotor function were measurably altered within hours. More than 20% of the exposed had at least one significant change in a hearing threshold on audiologic assessment, though this, as well as changes in levels of the blood biomarker neurofilament-light, were observed two weeks after HWT. Instructors who experienced repeated HWT exposure over two-year duty tours demonstrated greater magnitude and duration alterations in memory and gait toward the end of those tours. The blood biomarker glial fibrillary acidic protein, vasomotor reactivity of the middle cerebral arteries, and seven cognitive tests comprising the Automated Neuropsychological Assessment Metrics Version 4 showed no significant changes in association with subconcussive blast exposure in this setting. Blast exposure during HWT is associated with acute changes in some blood biomarker levels and measures of brain function such as short term recall memory and gait. The effects appear to be short in duration, but recovery may be delayed after repeated exposure.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and vascular surgeons in patient communication: A comparative analysis of intelligibility and clinical appropriateness in acute deep vein thrombosis
papers.authors: Oliver Antonio Gómez-Gutiérrez, Oscar A. De la Torre, Gabriela Marta Cassagne, Jorge Flores-Orduña, Luis Leon, Mario Alejandro Fabiani
papers.journal: Phlebology The Journal of Venous Disease
papers.abstract: Objective Effective patient communication is critical in acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT) management. This study evaluated and compared the intelligibility and clinical appropriateness of patient-directed explanations for acute DVT generated by vascular surgeons versus a diverse panel of large language models (LLMs), using a balanced, unit-matched design. Methods In this observational, cross-sectional study, 11 board-certified vascular surgeons and 11 distinct, independently developed LLMs each produced one response to a standardized acute DVT vignette in Spanish. Responses were blinded and scored using an 8-item clinical appropriateness grid (two independent graders, consensus) and five validated Spanish readability indices. Central tendency was assessed with Mann-Whitney U tests; dispersion was assessed descriptively (coefficient of variation, range) and, exploratorily, with Brown-Forsythe tests. Results Clinical appropriateness did not differ significantly between groups (median 7/8 in both; p = 0.258), dispersion was descriptively far smaller for LLMs (SD 0.40 vs 1.92; coefficient of variation 5.9% vs 32.5%). LLM responses were more readable on three of four content-complexity indices (Fernández-Huerta, Gutiérrez de Polini, Szigriszt-Pazos; all p < 0.02) and required a numerically lower educational grade level (Crawford 5.4 vs 6.1; p = 0.075). Readability dispersion was descriptively far lower for LLMs (Fernández-Huerta range 31 vs 200 points; coefficient of variation 15% vs 181%), driven in the surgeon cohort by a single response that fell far outside the interpretable range; formal variance tests did not reach significance at this sample size. LLM responses were longer (median 903 vs 354 words; p = 0.003) and took longer to read (4.5 vs 1.8 min; p < 0.001). Neither group addressed screening for silent pulmonary embolism. Free-versus-premium comparisons were model-specific rather than uniform. Conclusion Current-generation LLMs matched board-certified surgeons in clinical completeness and produced more readable, descriptively far more consistent patient-facing explanations, without the communication failures observed in a minority of human responses. Both cohorts share an important, guideline-adjacent counseling gap.

papers.title: Adaptive local temporal weighting for short-window EEG-based SSVEP recognition using FB-eTRCA
papers.authors: Guozhu Zhao, Zijing Feng, Zehua Wang
papers.abstract: To improve short-window SSVEP recognition, we integrated adaptive temporal local weighting (ATLW) with filter-bank ensemble task-related component analysis (FB-eTRCA). ATLW estimates local discriminability from training trials, converts window scores into sample weights, and applies the training-derived weights to training and test trials within each cross-validation fold. Experiments were conducted on two public 40-target SSVEP datasets: the Benchmark dataset containing 35 subjects and six blocks, and the BETA database containing 70 subjects and four blocks. Seven observation windows ranging from 0.2 to 1.4 s were evaluated using subject-specific leave-one-block-out validation, with six folds for the Benchmark dataset and four folds for the BETA database. On the Benchmark dataset, only the 0.2-s accuracy gain remained significant after Holm correction (44.79% vs 44.07%; adjusted p = 0.0300); other windows were nonsignificant. On the Benchmark dataset, ablation analysis showed that adaptive weighting was more stable than fixed temporal weighting. After Holm correction, eTRCA+ATLW significantly outperformed eTRCA at 0.4 s (gain: 0.86 percentage points; adjusted p = 0.0023), but not at 0.2 s, supporting transferability to another TRCA-based decoder. EEGNet and BiLSTM were included as representative CNN and RNN baselines; both performed below the TRCA-family methods under the present subject-specific limited-calibration protocol. On the BETA database, FB-eTRCA+ATLW remained close to FB-eTRCA across all seven observation windows without BETA-specific parameter retuning, but no paired difference was statistically significant. These findings indicate that ATLW is a lightweight temporal refinement that can be applied to more than one TRCA-based decoder. Its measurable benefit may depend on SSVEP signal quality and the amount of available subject-specific calibration data. Accuracy increased with longer windows, whereas the information transfer rate peaked at 0.6 s on the Benchmark dataset. Therefore, no observation window was optimal for both accuracy and communication speed.

papers.title: Early wildfire escalation prediction with temporal validation and statistical benchmarking in a mediterranean region
papers.authors: Gökhan Yüksek, Ali Akdağlı, Serdar Ekinci, Davut İzci, Erdal Akin
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate an incident-level framework for predicting whether a newly reported wildfire would reach at least 10 ha, emphasizing temporal validation, statistical benchmarking, and transparent optimizer assessment using only information available at or near incident registration.MethodsThis retrospective modelling study integrated 1,901 operational wildfire records documented by the Mersin Regional Directorate of Forestry during 2004-2025 with event-day meteorology and Canadian Fire Weather Index variables. Burned area was known for 1,898 incidents, including 68 major fires. Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost were evaluated under default settings, Random Search, Optuna/TPE, and repeated Enhanced Ruppel's Fox Optimization (eRFO), together with regularized logistic regression using the identical early-stage predictors. Three expanding-window folds within 2004-2020 guided development, while 471 incidents from 2021-2025, including 17 major fires, formed a locked recent-year evaluation.ResultseRFO produced the highest development PR-AUC for Random Forest (0.142) and Gradient Boosting (0.167), whereas Optuna/TPE achieved the highest XGBoost score (0.170). In the locked recent-year evaluation, the logistic benchmark achieved the highest discrimination (ROC-AUC 0.870; PR-AUC 0.217), compared with ROC-AUC 0.813 and PR-AUC 0.210 for XGBoost-eRFO and ROC-AUC 0.774 and PR-AUC 0.145 for Gradient Boosting-eRFO. Reviewing the highest-ranked 20% of incidents captured 9 of 17 major fires with Gradient Boosting-eRFO and 10 of 17 with XGBoost-eRFO. Out-of-sample SHAP analysis identified wind speed, relative humidity, district, temperature, and drought-related Fire Weather Index components as leading model associations.ConclusionsIncreased learner and optimizer complexity did not guarantee superior temporal generalization. The principal contribution is a leakage-controlled evaluation framework combining early-available predictors, temporally ordered development, simple-model benchmarking, calibrated probabilities, and interpretable risk ranking for human-in-the-loop prioritization of newly reported wildfires.

papers.title: Leveraging AI to enhance vocabulary instruction
papers.authors: Elfrieda H. Hiebert
papers.abstract: Teachers face a challenge when selecting which vocabulary words deserve instructional time from many words students encounter in texts. Conventional approaches rely heavily on publisher or educator choice, creating a demanding decision-making process. Elfrieda H. Hiebert demonstrates how artificial intelligence (AI) can assist educators in identifying thematically important vocabulary that supports both immediate text comprehension and long-term vocabulary development. Using examples from narrative ( Ninth Ward ) and informational texts ( Hurricanes ), she illustrates AI's capacity to identify themes, provide background texts, and generate semantic maps and semantic gradients. While AI tools can significantly reduce teacher workload and expand instructional possibilities, professional judgment remains essential for evaluating AI outputs and ensuring instruction meets students' specific needs.

papers.title: School librarians still matter in the age of AI
papers.authors: Keith Curry Lance, Caitlin Gerrity
papers.abstract: School librarians play a vital role in helping students and teachers build digital literacy skills that are growing in importance in the age of artificial intelligence. Keith Curry Lance and Caitlin Gerrity review national survey data on the use of librarians in schools to teach digital literacy. They find that 43% of schools do not have librarians or similar professionals doing this work, and that schools in low-income communities, those with a large percentage of students of color, small schools, and high schools were less likely than others to have a librarian teaching digital literacy. They describe state legislation that seeks to promote digital literacy, what librarians are already doing, and how school decision makers can support the work of librarians in this area.

papers.title: What is the future of education?
papers.authors: Kathleen Vail
papers.abstract: Kappan asked educators, researchers, school leaders, and advocates to share what they believe schools should change, strengthen, and carry into the future. Contributors called attention to artificial intelligence, literacy, career-connected learning, teacher preparation, student voice, educator working conditions, and the need to reconsider how schools prepare young people for work, citizenship, and life. Their responses repeatedly mentioned the human experience of learning. They wrote about teachers who know their students and believe in their potential; about relationships, belonging, curiosity, mentorship, agency, and community.

papers.title: Dual Mechanisms of Impaired Visual Processing in Glaucoma: Insights From Resting-State and Task-Related EEG
papers.authors: Xiaolin Mei, Lilin Chen, Lok Hin Chan, Anqi Lyu, Celia Tsang, Christopher Kai-Shun Leung, Benjamin Thompson, Allen M. Y. Cheong
papers.abstract: Purpose: To examine both resting-state and task-related electroencephalography (EEG) changes associated with visual processing in glaucoma. Methods: Thirty glaucoma patients (mean age, 63 ± 8.26 years; visual field mean deviation, -15.41 ± 6.34 dB) and 28 age-matched controls (62.86 ± 9.19 years) underwent resting-state EEG for 3 minutes under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Alpha suppression, calculated as the difference between conditions, was assessed as a measure of cognitive state transition capacity. Visual evoked potentials (VEPs) were recorded using a 64-channel EEG system during a checkerboard reversal task under monocular and binocular viewing. Results: Resting-state EEG revealed that significantly reduced alpha suppression was highly specific to a high-alpha subband (10.0-12.9 Hz; P < 0.001), and low-alpha (7.0-9.9 Hz) modulation remained intact in the glaucoma group. Task-related EEG showed delayed latency and reduced amplitude in both P100 and N75-P100 components in the glaucoma group, indicating impaired visual processing. Effect size analysis indicated that P100 amplitude and N75-P100 latency showed the largest group differences, highlighting these as the most prominent cortical changes. Notably, alpha suppression deficits showed no significant correlation with glaucoma severity or VEP parameters, suggesting distinct neurophysiological mechanisms beyond direct visual pathway damage. Conclusions: Both resting-state and task-related EEG measures differed between the glaucoma and control groups, indicating alterations in cortical activity and visual-pathway responses. Specifically, the localized high alpha modulation deficit suggests altered top-down visual network dynamics in glaucoma.

papers.title: Dialogising Video Assessment in Higher Education: Students and Lecturer-Teacher Voicing our Lived Experiences of Initial Teacher Education
papers.authors: Fiona Westbrook, Teisa Bernard, Briana Maleko, Iunisi Taukolo
papers.journal: Video Journal of Education and Pedagogy
papers.abstract: Abstract Video assessment in higher education, especially initial teacher education ( ITE ), has been linked to enhanced knowledge acquisition, creativity and critical thinking. Conversely, the stipulated benefits of video have been claimed to, at times, reach beyond what can be known. Modern, epistemic crises within higher education are bringing these tensions of video assessment to the fore. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is unsettling traditional forms of academic integrity, whilst politically motivated pedagogical reforms position university-based ITE as antiquated, and thus inadequate at producing ‘ready’ graduates for vocational training. This article enters this discursive landscape with a dialogue of students and a lecturer-teacher, each voicing their everyday, lived experiences with video assessment, situated within a university-based ITE degree. Employing Mikhail Bakhtin’s dialogic philosophy, these authors form a polyphony, each with an equal right to speak in a chorus of unmerged voices. Their dialogue suggests video assessment can encourage student voice as an ethical, visible encounter, decentring the authority of written academic conventions. With video posing an epistemic, localising provocation, it is further signalled as having potential to subvert an over-reliance on GenAI and bridge the perceived theory to practice divide of vocational degrees.

papers.title: Application of adaptive artificial intelligence for personalizing learning paths in e-learning
papers.authors: Mohammed Salihoun, Abdelali Elmounadi
papers.journal: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: The field of education and online education in particular, has undergone radical change thanks to digital transformation. The integration of adaptive artificial intelligence (AI) into the latter has given a further significant evolution, enabling the online personalization of learning paths. The result is clearly effective, engaging and specific education for every student. This article analyzes how adaptive AI can improve e-learning, with a specific accentuation on algorithms and tools—such as machine learning and deep learning that enable this level of customization. Technical and ethical challenges will be discussed, as we go over their benefits, precisely with regard to improving learning outcomes and promoting student involvement and engagement. Additionally, the paper examines the potential applications of adaptive AI in online learning, stressing the anticipated advancements and the significance of a thoughtful strategy that considers moral and legal concerns. The paper highlights the ways in which adaptive AI can revolutionize distance learning and stimulates critical thought about the implications of its broad implementation.

papers.title: An efficient computational framework for abstracting program slices from Java code
papers.authors: Aparna Kudloor Siddalingaiah, Raghavendra Narayanrao Kulkarni
papers.journal: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Over the past decades, Java-based applications have formed the backbone of enterprise, web, and mobile software systems, often containing complex business logic and domain-specific requirements embedded in older codebases (Java SE 1.2-8). Maintaining and migrating such systems is difficult due to unstructured code, missing documentation, and outdated design artifacts. To address these challenges, the paper introduces a computationally efficient static-backward slicing framework for Java programs. The framework restructures the source code, abstracts control and data flow information, computes functional dependencies using a data flow table (DFT), and extracts precise program slices. Extracted slices are further represented using object-Z notation to formalize software specifications. Furthermore, the extracted backward slices and object-Z specifications can be leveraged with artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) to automatically generate human-readable software requirements. This integration also ensures structured, accurate, and minimal requirements outputs, facilitating AI-assisted software modernization. Experimental evaluations on Java programs such as automated teller machine (ATM), student grading, and quadratic root calculators exhibit significant reductions in extracted code size while preserving functional dependencies. In comparison with traditional dynamic and machine learning (ML)-based slicing approaches, the proposed framework offers improved precision, computational efficiency, and scalability, making it suitable for modernizing legacy Java systems and supporting AI-driven software engineering tasks.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-based epileptic seizure classification using a sparse iterative recursive-gated recurrent unit
papers.authors: Santhosh Kumar Gorva, Mohan Gowda Venkateshappa, K R Pradeep, Narayan Naik, Shivamma Devanna, Navya Rajashekara
papers.journal: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Epileptic seizure classification using electroencephalography (EEG) plays a significant role in clinical diagnosis, long-term patient monitoring, and treatment planning. However, accurate seizure classification remains challenging due to its high complex and non-stationary nature of brain signal, which leads to misdiagnosis. This research proposes a sparse iterative recursive (SIR)-gated recurrent unit (GRU) to classify epileptic seizures accurately. By incorporating GRU into SIR, the model effectively learns and retains significant temporal patterns in EEG signals over long sequences. The gated structure minimizes the vanishing gradient, resulting in effective learning from sequential seizure patterns. Sparsity and recursion enhance the feature representation with lesser computational complexity for accurate seizure classification. Time-and frequency domain feature extract with sparsity and iterative recursion enables the model to selectively concentrate on seizure relevant temporal patterns, which minimizes redundant and noisy information. Hence, SIR-GRU achieves higher accuracies of 99.75% and 99.54% on the Bonn EEG as well as Children's Hospital Boston-Massachusetts Institute of Technology (CHB-MIT) dataset, respectively, compared to the existing method including spatio-temporal feature fusion dual attention (STFFDA). These findings indicate that SIR-GRU provides rapid and reliable performance, which improves accuracy in clinical practice.

papers.title: Stacking ensemble for multilingual aspect-based sentiment analysis of tourism reviews
papers.authors: Basworo Ardi Pramono, Rahmat Gernowo, Aghus Sofwan
papers.journal: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Multilingual tourism reviews often express opinions about multiple destination attributes within a single text, making aspect-level sentiment classification challenging. This study compares classical machine learning and ensemble methods for multilabel aspect-based sentiment analysis of amenities, attractions, and accessibility. The dataset comprises 13,085 Indonesian- and English-language Google Reviews labeled through a rule-based procedure. Reviews were represented using term frequency-inverse document frequency features and classified using logistic regression, multinomial naive Bayes, random forest, soft voting, adaptive boosting (AdaBoost), and stacking under a one-vs-rest framework. The stacking classifier combined logistic regression and random forest as base learners with logistic regression as the meta-learner. It achieved the best performance among the evaluated models, with a micro-F1 of 0.8626, macro-F1 of 0.7285, Hamming loss of 0.0633, and subset accuracy of 0.6825. These findings indicate that stacking effectively integrates complementary decision patterns and provides a reproducible framework for multilingual multilabel analysis of tourism reviews.

papers.title: Novel deep learning framework with hierarchical temporal feature refinement for enhanced epileptic seizure detection
papers.authors: Namitha Arakere Raju, Boddula Siddartha
papers.journal: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Epileptic seizure detection remains a significant challenge in the field of neurology due to the complexity and variability of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Traditional manual methods of analyzing EEG data are time-consuming, subjective, and prone to misdiagnosis, particularly in long-term recordings. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel hierarchical temporal feature refinement network for epileptic seizure detection (HTFRNet-ESD) framework designed to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of epileptic seizure detection. The methodology comprises three key components: a spatial-temporal signal encoder (STSE) for capturing spatio-temporal attributes, an adaptive temporal dynamics encoder (ATDE) for detailed temporal feature analysis, and a hierarchical temporal refinement unit (HTRU) module for integrating frequency-driven power features. The proposed model leverages advanced deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers, to effectively learn both coarse and fine-grained temporal dynamics of EEG signals. Evaluation on publicly available EEG datasets demonstrates the model’s superior sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy compared to existing approaches. The HTFRNet-ESD sets a new benchmark for automated seizure detection, offering a reliable and scalable solution for real-world clinical applications. This work paves the way for improved patient outcomes through timely and precise epilepsy diagnosis.

papers.title: Leveraging AI and pedagogical competence to enhance learning interest and outcomes: evidence from Islamic university
papers.authors: Cecep Wahyu Hoerudin, Susanto Susanto, Apri Wardana Ritonga, Ayu Desrani, Darwis Hude, Dzaki Aflah Zamani, Ahmad Ari Masyhuri
papers.journal: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: This study investigates the effects of artificial intelligence (AI)-supported intelligent educational systems and teacher pedagogical competence (TPC) on students’ learning interest (LI) and learning outcomes (LO) in an Islamic higher education context. AI is operationalized as AI-supported learning system features embedded in institutional learning platforms, particularly natural language processing (NLP)-based automated feedback and AI-driven recommendation functionalities that support adaptive and personalized learning. The study was conducted at the As-Syifa Institute, Subang, Indonesia, involving 366 undergraduate students from the first, third, and fifth semesters. Data were analyzed using partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4 to examine the structural relationships among AI system use, TPC, LI, and LO. The results demonstrate that AI-supported learning system features have significant positive effects on both LI and LO. TPC also shows a strong direct effect and mediates the relationship between AI-supported systems and student outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of human-AI integration, indicating that pedagogical competence plays a critical role in translating AI system functionalities into meaningful educational benefits. This study contributes to the AI-in-education literature by providing empirical evidence on pedagogically mediated AI-supported learning systems and offers insights for the design and evaluation of adaptive and intelligent learning environments in higher education.

papers.title: Perspectives of Indonesian dental practitioners on application of artificial intelligence in dentistry
papers.authors: Ivan Djuarsa, Vania Ewitrawati, Andry Sentosa, Hilmy Irsyadi Hanif, Santhia Pramanthi
papers.journal: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Limited evidence exists about the knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of Indonesian dental practitioners with regard to artificial intelligence (AI). A cross-sectional survey was performed among 235 licensed dentists throughout Indonesia, assessing their attitudes on the potential benefits and barriers of AI in dentistry, and its perceived influence on their profession. A “positive attitude – knowledge gap” was observed: attitudes towards AI were very positive (79.6% good), with comparatively low levels of basic AI knowledge (54.3% good). Dentists are positive towards the impact of AI on their professional efficiency (86.4%) and accuracy (82.1%), but remain concerned over the potential barriers of its implementation, specifically the ambiguity in legal liability (82.1%), high cost (77.0%), and data security issues (71.9%). The majority of dentists do not believe that AI will replace them (65.5%), but most worry that the use of AI may erode their skills (54.9%). There is strong support for curricular change (83.4%). Overall, Indonesian dentists are amenable to AI but are currently limited by low knowledge and many AI-related barriers. To increase its adoption, future efforts should focus on promoting practitioner education, as well as increasing confidence in legal and regulatory structures.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of machine learning models for concentration level prediction in e-learning
papers.authors: Abdessamad Chanaa, Fatima-Ezzahra Ait-Bennacer, Nour-eddine El Faddouli
papers.journal: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
papers.abstract: Concentration level plays an important role while accomplishing cognitive tasks. Although there are several methods for predicting concentration levels, the majority of the methods now in use for assessing concentration levels rely on labor-intensive and time-consuming human coding. In this work, learners’ performance and involvement in online assessments are utilized to categorize the concentration level using a publicly accessible dataset. The goal of the project is to identify the best machine learning (ML) model for concentration level prediction. Six distinct ML classifiers are employed for comparative analysis in this context. When compared to alternative classifiers for the assessment of concentration level, the eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model has the best precision (80.87%). These findings are highly promising and have implications for the future development of automated concentration level analytic tools for online learning.

papers.title: Educator Trust Calibration as Sociotechnical Practice: A Field Study of Generative AI Use in Indian Higher Education
papers.authors: Surbhi Sethi, Savneet Singh
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) systems are increasingly used in higher education, yet educator trust in these systems is often treated as an individual attitude rather than as a situated sociotechnical practice. Drawing on a 14-week field study with 42 faculty members at a mid-tier Indian technical university, this paper examines how educators encountered GenAI failures, interpreted system reliability, and developed verification-oriented routines across teaching, assessment, and administrative work. The study combines diaries, prompt logs, interviews, observations, surveys, reflective workshops, and structured red-teaming exercises. We analyze trust calibration as an ongoing process shaped by surface fluency, institutional authority, disciplinary expertise, peer reflection, and the labor of verification. Our findings identify three mechanisms of initial over-reliance: surface fluency deference, authority projection, and confirmation-seeking use. Participants later encountered fabricated citations, unstable answers, and locally specific policy failures that disrupted their mental models of GenAI reliability. We identify four educator trust postures—High-Adoption Uncritical, Low-Adoption Skeptical, Selective Verifiers, and Reflective Collaborators—and synthesize these into the Educator-AI Trust Calibration (EATC) framework. We do not claim that red-teaming caused trust recalibration. Instead, red-teaming functioned as one structured site within a broader field process through which educators made AI failures visible, negotiated verification responsibilities, and reworked use practices. The paper contributes a process-oriented account of educator-AI trust calibration and introduces the local knowledge verification gap as a mechanism through which fluent but unreliable GenAI outputs become difficult to contest in underrepresented institutional and regional contexts.

papers.title: NeuroPriv: Adversarial Representation Learning for Privacy in Wearable EEG Systems
papers.authors: Sarmistha Sarna Gomasta, Bhawana Chhaglani, Prashant J. Shenoy
papers.abstract: Wearable EEG systems may expose sensitive information beyond their intended health function, creating substantial risks to neuroprivacy. In this work, we show that commonly used EEG features can reveal participant identity and demographic attributes in addition to supporting the intended cognitive task. Wearable EEG is increasingly being explored for cognitive monitoring, neurological assessment, and longitudinal digital-health applications, yet many systems assume that transmitting compact spectral or spatial features instead of raw EEG provides sufficient privacy protection. Using EEGMAT as a motivating case study, we find that compact EEG features achieve a balanced accuracy of 0.788 for cognitive-state classification while enabling gender, age, and subject-identity inference with balanced accuracies of 0.858, 0.789, and 0.692, respectively. We further show that privacy-aware representation learning preserves task performance at 0.781 while reducing these inference accuracies to 0.563, 0.467, and 0.206. These findings motivate purpose-limited representations and explicit privacy auditing in wearable neurohealth systems.

papers.title: T-REX: Teaching Large Language Models to Reason with Verbalized Execution Semantics
papers.authors: Yan Wang, Ling Ding, Jiechen Sun, Tien N. Nguyen, Shaohua Wang, Aashish Yadavally, Xin Xia, Yanan Zheng
papers.journal: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in static code tasks like code search, summarization, and generation, but remain limited in dynamic code reasoning, which involves inferring how programs behave during execution without actually running them. This limitation stems from LLMs being trained on static code and lacking the necessary runtime context. In this paper, we present T-REX, a novel teacher-student framework for execution prediction that addresses these limitations by grounding LLM training in actual execution and corresponding execution semantics. T-REX uses a large teacher model (Explainer) to generate fine-grained, stepwise natural language rationales explaining how program state transitions from one statement to another during actual execution. These rationales are used to train a smaller student model (Reasoner) to predict next program states, enabling accurate simulation of program behavior with lower computational cost.
