Scarlato, Margherita, and Giorgio d'Agostino. 2019. “The Political Dimension of Cash Transfers in Latin America and Sub‐Saharan Africa: A Comparative Perspective.” Politics & Policy 47, no. 6: 1125–1155. https://doi.org/10.1111/polp.12332 .

papers.title: Neural Oscillatory Signatures of Predictive Processing in Visual Statistical Learning
papers.authors: Pasqualetti Martina, Jakob C. B. Schwenk, Andrea Alamia
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Several studies suggest that neural oscillations play a role in cognition, including predictive processing. Recent models propose that backward alpha-band traveling waves reflect top-down predictions, while forward waves may reflect bottom-up prediction errors. We tested this hypothesis using a visual statistical learning task in which participants (N = 31) detected target shapes presented with varying levels of predictability. Electrophysiological activity and pupillometry were recorded throughout the task. Behavioral results showed faster responses for predictable targets, and pupil dilation increased for unexpected shapes. Evoked response potential analyses revealed predictability effects on the P300 component across occipital and frontal electrodes, along with modulation of alpha oscillations. However, traveling wave analyses did not show a clear effect of predictability between conditions. Instead, wave patterns showed a modest association with individual differences in cognitive strategy, with stronger top-down alpha-band waves in participants who relied more on statistical regularities. Overall, these findings challenge the view that alpha-band traveling waves implement predictive coding during visual perception, suggesting instead that they may reflect more general cognitive strategies rather than specific predictive processes.

papers.title: Neurophysiological Correlates of Pain‐Related Cognitive–Affective Dysregulation in Adolescent Depression
papers.authors: Hong Li, Yujiao Wen, Wentao Cheng, Lexuan Zhuang, 刘志芬
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by altered processing and regulation of negative emotional and bodily experiences. Pain lies at the interface of sensory and cognitive-affective processing, encompassing both perceptual sensitivity and appraisal of pain-related experiences. Yet, how pain catastrophizing, a pain-specific cognitive-affective pattern characterized by rumination, magnification, and helplessness, relates to depressive severity and neurophysiological dynamics during adolescence remains poorly understood. In this cross-sectional case-control study, we recruited 140 participants aged 12-23 years with and without MDD and investigated behavioral and electrophysiological correlates of pain-related cognitive-affective dysregulation using clinical assessments and resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). Structural equation modeling revealed a significant indirect association between pain catastrophizing and depressive severity through anxiety, highlighting anxiety-related processes within this relationship. Compared with healthy controls, adolescents with MDD exhibited increased δ- and θ-band power and altered EEG microstate dynamics, characterized by greater temporal involvement of microstate B, reduced temporal persistence of microstate D, and increased bidirectional B-C transitions. EEG-informed path models further linked microstate features to the indirect relationship between pain catastrophizing, anxiety, and depressive severity. Together, these findings identify convergent behavioral and neurophysiological correlates of pain-related cognitive-affective dysregulation and highlight dynamic EEG features for further investigation in adolescent MDD.

papers.title: Audience Gaze and Felt Social Connection With Individual Performers During Live Dance
papers.authors: Albane Arthuis, Sonia Abad-Hernando, Anastasia Kokkinou, Mirko Febbo, Laura A. Rai, 이해은, Matthias Sperling, Jamie A. Ward, Daniel C. Richardson, Guido Orgs
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: In everyday social interactions, our looking behavior reflects our relationships with others, but the role that social perception plays for engagement with the performing arts is understudied. We commissioned the durational, community-focused, 16-h dance performance How Shall We Begin Again?, comprising a continuous relay of individual improvised performances by 50 people over 2 consecutive days. During the performance, we recorded eye movements and mobile EEG from 88 audience members who entered and exited the performance space freely. Audience members reported on their experience of individual performers immediately after leaving the performance space. Gaze toward people in the scene showed a significant indirect association with felt social connection through self-reported focus on individual performers; the overall gaze-connection association, however, was not statistically significant. Individual differences in mind wandering, dance experience, and empathy were associated with gaze and engagement measures, but not with felt social connection. Finally, EEG alpha power decreased and EEG delta/gamma power increased when dance was accompanied by music. Together, these data suggest that engagement with dance depends not only on what is being performed (dance/choreography/music) but also on who is performing, highlighting that dance is an inherently embodied art form that can foster social connections between people.

papers.title: Susceptibility to algorithmic recommendations in simulated jury decision making
papers.authors: Mario Álvarez, Helena Matute
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction AI decision‐support systems have become increasingly integrated into judicial contexts. This research asks about their influence on human judgements, particularly when they are erroneous or biased. Method Experiment 1 examined whether algorithmic recommendations conflicting with the evidence previously presented through standardized testimonies could change the judgements of participants acting as mock jurors. Experiment 2 replicated Experiment 1 and warned participants about potential AI errors. Results Experiment 1 showed that participants’ judgements shifted in the direction suggested by the algorithmic recommendation. Experiment 2 replicated the findings of Experiment 1 and further showed that warning participants about potential AI errors and biases reduced algorithmic influence, particularly when the algorithm suggested guilt and the testimonies suggested innocence. Discussion These findings highlight the importance of understanding how algorithmic recommendations influence legal decision‐making and how excessive trust in AI recommendations could be reduced. Data The data supporting the findings of this study are openly available in the Open Science Framework at https://osf.io/9gwh7 .

papers.title: Evidence Specificity and Sensory Convergence in Upcycled Food Communication: A Five‐Cue Consumer Experiment in Vietnam
papers.authors: Vo Trieu Tra, Duong Hong Luan
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Prior research already shows that sustainability information can influence evaluations of upcycled foods; the more discriminating question is whether advantages created by different message configurations persist after tasting. This study compared five finalized cue packages among 300 Gen Z consumers in Vietnam: control, generic upcycled, narrative sustainability, evidence‐rich sustainability, and AI‐disclosed sustainability. Participants evaluated the same upcycled tropical fruit snack before and after tasting. Because wording, evidential specificity, and AI disclosure varied jointly, the experiment is interpreted as a comparison of message packages rather than a causal test of AI versus human authorship. Cue condition affected pre‐tasting overall liking expectation, perceived sustainability, and cue credibility. The narrative and evidence‐rich conditions produced higher expected liking than control, while the evidence‐rich condition showed the strongest credibility and sustainability profile. After all participants tasted the identical product, post‐tasting overall liking and consumer acceptance did not differ by condition. Purchase intention and willingness to pay showed smaller condition effects, concentrated in the contrast between the evidence‐rich and narrative conditions. Open‐ended responses repeatedly emphasized objective evidence and human verification. The main contribution is therefore bounded but practically relevant: message specificity and substantiation can create a pre‐tasting informational advantage, yet that advantage does not automatically translate into superior sensory liking once the product is experienced.

papers.title: Global Implementation of the Nutrition‐Friendly School Initiative ( NFSI ): A Scoping Review of Strategies, Challenges, Barriers, and Facilitators
papers.authors: Maryam Karkhaneh, Nasrin Omidvar, Farid Zayeri, Vahid Yazdi‐Feyzabadi, Hamid Abbasi, Saeid Doaei, Azam Doustmohammadian
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Nutrition-Friendly School Initiative (NFSI) is a whole-school approach designed to address the triple burden of malnutrition among school-aged children. However, evidence on its implementation across diverse settings remains fragmented. METHODS: This scoping review followed Arksey and O'Malley's framework and searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and gray literature sources for studies explicitly implementing the NFSI framework. FINDINGS: Sixteen records were included. Evidence suggests that NFSI implementation improves nutrition knowledge, dietary behaviors, and selected health outcomes, including BMI, stunting, and micronutrient status. Major facilitators included institutional commitment, multisectoral collaboration, and stakeholder engagement. Common barriers were limited resources, insufficient training, weak policy enforcement, and sociocultural resistance. IMPLICATIONS FOR SCHOOL HEALTH POLICY, PRACTICE, AND EQUITY: Integrating NFSI principles into education and public health systems may strengthen school nutrition policies and reduce health inequities. Sustainable implementation requires cross-sector collaboration, equitable resource allocation, supportive school food environments, and stronger monitoring systems, particularly in resource-constrained settings. CONCLUSION: The NFSI is a promising framework for promoting child nutrition and health, but stronger long-term evaluations and more comprehensive implementation strategies are needed.

papers.title: Cushing's syndrome is associated with an advanced chronotype
papers.authors: Hanna Franziska Nowotny, Adriana Albani, Mina Mazari, Stephanie Zopp, Martha W. Merrow, Nicole Reisch, Luis Gustavo Perez‐Rivas, Marily Theodoropoulou
papers.abstract: Cushing's syndrome is characterised by chronic glucocorticoid excess that abolishes the physiological circadian cortisol rhythm. We investigated whether this circadian disruption alters chronotype. In a single-centre case-control study, chronotype was assessed using the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire (MCTQ; n = 119) and wrist actigraphy (n = 39) in patients with active Cushing's syndrome, patients in biochemical remission, and healthy controls. The primary outcome was mid-sleep on free days corrected for sleep debt (MSFsc). Multivariable analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of chronotype. Agreement between methods was assessed by Bland-Altman analysis. Patients with active Cushing's syndrome had a significantly earlier chronotype than patients in remission and controls (MSFsc by MCTQ: 2.38 h [IQR 1.22; 3.41] vs. 3.29 h [IQR 2.65; 4.32] vs. 3.73 h [IQR 3.16; 4.08]; p = .007 and p = .0003, respectively; actigraphy: 3.15 ± 0.90 h vs. 4.03 ± 0.96 h vs. 4.46 ± 0.75 h; p = .039 and p = .001, respectively). Chronotype did not differ significantly between patients in remission and controls. In a multivariable quantile regression model, active Cushing's syndrome was an independent predictor of chronotype (1.32 h earlier than controls; p = .049), while age, BMI, psychiatric symptoms and sleep disturbance had no significant influence. Actigraphy confirmed earlier sleep offset and acrophase in active Cushing's syndrome. MCTQ and actigraphy were significantly correlated (Pearson r = 0.619, p = .0003, n = 29); agreement analysis revealed no systematic bias, but a significant proportional bias, reflecting wider dispersion of MCTQ-derived values. Patients with active Cushing's syndrome have an earlier chronotype than patients in remission and healthy controls, as determined by both subjective and objective methods. Chronotype assessment, particularly with the MCTQ, may complement biochemical monitoring.

papers.title: Body Size Discrimination, Family Emotional Climate, and Chronic Health Incidence in Middle Age: A Longitudinal Study
papers.authors: Maggie L. Smith, Sarah Woods
papers.journal: Journal of Marital and Family Therapy
papers.abstract: Body size discrimination has been significantly linked to adverse health outcomes. Although family emotional climate has been shown to influence health outcomes, few studies have tested if various aspects of family emotional climate either buffer or exacerbate chronic disease onset related to size discrimination. Using a subsample of the MIDUS 1 and 2 projects, we conducted a longitudinal analysis to test the relationship between perceived size discrimination, family support, and family strain and likelihood of various adverse outcomes as well as interaction effects between both family support and family strain with size discrimination. Size discrimination was found to be significantly related to increased chances of diabetes and chronic sleep problems 10 years later when controlling for BMI, basic demographics, and baseline outcome variable levels. Findings surrounding family support and family strain varied by outcome variable. Interaction effects had no significant results within the models. Implications for family therapists are discussed.

papers.title: Diet Quality and Physical Activity at 3–4 Years Following a Hypertensive Pregnancy: A Blood Pressure Postpartum Cross‐Sectional Sub‐Study
papers.authors: Yining Chen, Megan L. Gow, Katie Harris, Lynne M. Roberts, Amanda Henry
papers.journal: Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), as well as being a leading global cause of maternal mortality, confer lifelong increased maternal cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Although lifestyle interventions may mitigate these risks, robust evidence remains scarce. Material and Methods This cross‐sectional sub‐study of the three‐armed, multicenter BP 2 randomised controlled trial primarily assessed diet quality, physical activity, and their association with CVD risk markers in women 3–4 years after HDP, following different BP 2 postpartum care/lifestyle intervention strategies implemented between six and 12 months post‐HDP. Diet quality was evaluated using the Australian Recommended Food Score (ARFS) derived from the Australian Eating Survey. Duration of moderate‐vigorous physical activity (MVPA) was estimated using the International Physical activity Questionnaire. Associations between key lifestyle outcomes and clinical cardiovascular markers were examined using linear regression models. Secondary lifestyle outcomes include estimated daily energy intake, food consumption, nutrients, estimated duration and engagement of specific physical activity types, and sedentary behaviour. Results In 180 participants, the mean ARFS was 33.8 ± 10.5 (SD), with 61% scoring < 38 indicating suboptimal diet quality. Median MVPA was 515 (IQR 690) minutes/week with 87% meeting physical activity recommendations of at least 150 min/week. No significant differences were observed across BP 2 lifestyle intervention strategies, HDP subtypes (chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and superimposed preeclampsia), or baseline body mass index (BMI) categories (< 30 vs. ≥ 30 kg/m 2 ). Neither ARFS nor MVPA showed significant associations with blood pressure, BMI, or waist circumference. Conclusions Suboptimal diet was observed 3–4 years after HDP despite prior lifestyle interventions, highlighting the need for postpartum support and long‐term lifestyle interventions to reduce CVD risks post‐HDP.

papers.title: When the Algorithm Speaks First: Trust, Reliance and the Reconstruction of Clinical Metacognition
papers.authors: Joël Hanhart, Anat Zohar
papers.journal: Journal of Evaluation in Clinical Practice
papers.abstract: AIMS OF THE JOURNAL ADDRESSED: This paper addresses three of the aims of the Journal: clinical decision making, health philosophy and person-centred healthcare. Retinal imaging serves as the analytic case. The question at issue, what epistemic attitude a clinician may properly hold towards an algorithmic output issued for an individual patient, arises in every discipline and every health system in which such systems are deployed, and the argument is tested throughout against systems that read no images. RATIONALE, AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: Diagnostic artificial intelligence increasingly delivers a conclusion before the clinician has formed one, and medical education has responded by adding modules on the critical appraisal of algorithmic output. Such curricula rest upon two unsound foundations: they extend a form of metacognitive instruction shown not to improve diagnostic accuracy and they ask clinicians to cultivate an attitude whose defining feature is the relaxation of validation. This paper establishes what epistemic attitude a clinician may hold towards an algorithmic output and derives the form that clinical metacognition must take in consequence. METHODS: Conceptual analysis, drawing upon the philosophy of trust and epistemic dependence, the cognitive science of clinical reasoning and empirical studies of artificial intelligence in clinical practice. Retinal medicine serves as the analytic case, chosen because it is the domain in which the position under contest is strongest; the argument is tested throughout against systems that process no images. RESULTS: Trust and reliance are distinct attitudes. On the account adopted here, to trust a medical algorithm is to rely upon it while relaxing the monitoring of the conditions that make it reliable; trust is reliance from which validation has been withdrawn. Regulatory clearance, institutional adoption and published performance supply legitimate grounds for trusting the assemblage that produces a system, yet none of them, singly or together, warrants reliance upon its output for an individual patient. Three asymmetries separate algorithmic from human epistemic dependence: the algorithm can be neither interrogated nor held to account; its errors fall on whole classes of patients at once; and its warrant holds of a population while the decision is owed to a person. The metacognition this situation demands is knowledge, not disposition, and stands untouched by the evidence against generic metacognitive instruction. CONCLUSIONS: Clinical metacognition requires reconstruction around three competences: calibrated reliance, awareness of distributed epistemic labour, and vigilance towards confidence-masked uncertainty. Each is content-dependent, teachable and assessable. Since none can be exercised where institutions supply neither the means of interrogation nor the time it takes, the reform of education and the reform of clinical governance are, in this respect, a single undertaking.

papers.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Pressure Injury Staging Among Nurses: A Multisite Study Using Knowledge Assessment and Image‐Based Evaluation
papers.authors: Nahla Tayyib, Mousa Yahya Asiri
papers.abstract: This study aims to evaluate nursing staff knowledge of the pressure injury (PI) staging system, assess their accuracy in classifying PIs using a photo-based assessment and explore factors associated with performance outcomes in tertiary hospitals in Saudi Arabia. A cross-sectional design was used. The target population was registered nurses (RNs) who had direct contact with admitted patients with PIs during the previous 2 years in three tertiary hospitals in Saudi Arabia. A total of 330 RNs participated in this study. Data were collected through an online survey using the Pressure Ulcer Prevention Knowledge Test related to PI stages, which included 21 items, and a photo-based PI staging test that included 18 photographs. The survey took approximately 10-15 min to complete. The data were statistically analysed using descriptive and correlational statistics. Among 572 eligible RNs, 330 completed the online survey and were included in the analysis. The findings indicated that the average RN knowledge score was 62.54%, suggesting insufficient knowledge of the PI staging system. This finding was consistent with the average accuracy of 62.04% in classifying the PI photographs according to the staging system. Moreover, no significant associations were observed between RNs' knowledge of the PI staging system or their ability to accurately stage PIs and their sex, age, work experience or education level. Significant gaps were identified in nurses' knowledge and accuracy in staging PIs despite relatively high educational attainment and workshop attendance. Given the importance of accurate PI staging in standardized assessment, communication, documentation, monitoring and healthcare resource allocation, these findings highlight the need for strategies to support and improve the delivery of quality patient care. Targeted competency-based training and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence-driven image analysis, may help improve staging accuracy. Further research is needed to evaluate the clinical feasibility and impact of these approaches.

papers.title: Selected Meeting Abstracts From 2026 International Workshop on Psychology and Mental Health
papers.journal: International Journal of Mental Health Nursing
papers.abstract: Objective: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for transforming mental health continuing education by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) to establish a dynamic and personalized educational ecosystem.It aims to address the shortcomings of traditional models, enhance the efficiency and accessibility of professional training, and ultimately improve service quality to meet evolving societal needs.Methods: The framework is developed through a multidisciplinary synthesis of existing literature and models.It incorporates adult learning theories, digital pedagogy, AI technologies in education, and the specific competency and ethical requirements of mental health practice.The construction process focuses on analyzing the synergies among these domains to define the core principles and structural components of an AIenhanced learning ecosystem.Results: The resulting framework presents a learner-centered ecosystem built on several key components: 1. AI-Driven Personalization: Adaptive learning pathways tailored to individual profiles and goals.2. Immersive & Simulated Learning: Use of VR, AR, and AI simulations for safe clinical skills practice.3. Data-Informed Analytics: AI-powered feedback and competence mapping to identify learning gaps.4. Collaborative Networks: AI-facilitated platforms for peer and expert collaboration across distances.5. Ethical Governance: Mechanisms ensuring data privacy, algorithmic fairness, and content credibility.Conclusion: This AI-driven framework outlines a necessary shift towards a more responsive and effective continuing education model in mental health.It highlights AI's role in enabling adaptive, situated learning beyond mere content delivery.Successful implementation requires focused efforts in technology design, educator development, supportive policy, and ongoing ethical evaluation to empower professionals in meeting contemporary practice challenges.

papers.title: Co‐Creation for Health System Innovation: Developing a Model and an Action Plan for Future Primary Care in Switzerland
papers.authors: A Romanova, Andreas Balthasar, Manuela Oetterli, Sarah Mantwill
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Primary care in Switzerland faces a set of interrelated systemic challenges that exemplify a wicked problem. Addressing such complexity requires participatory approaches that integrate diverse perspectives and generate context-sensitive solutions. The project Health2040 engaged stakeholders in a co-creation process to co-design a future model of ambulatory primary care for Switzerland and an accompanying action plan to support its implementation. METHODS: The project employed a structured co-creation process, beginning with context exploration, evidence synthesis, and stakeholder consultations. Following the preparation phase, two co-design workshops with more than 50 stakeholders, including patients, healthcare professionals, government authorities, social care representatives, insurers, and researchers. The workshops combined customised participatory methods such as patient personas, visioning, system mapping through building blocks, fishbowl discussions, and the X-Curve. RESULTS: The process produced two main outputs: (1) the 'Health Network for All' model, a vision for patient-centred, network-based, and digitally supported primary care, and (2) the Action Plan, which identifies three central action areas, profession-specific activities, and implementation strategies. Thirty-one individuals endorsed the plan. CONCLUSION: The project illustrates how co-creation can be used to address wicked problems in health systems by linking visionary model-building with actionable strategies. The outputs provide a framework that may inform ongoing efforts to shape the future of Swiss primary care. Beyond the Swiss context, the study illustrates how internationally established primary care principles can be operationalized through co-creation in a local context and highlights methodological design principles that may inform similar processes in other settings. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients and members of the public contributed at different stages of the project. Stakeholder feedback informed workshop design and materials, and representatives from all relevant groups participated in developing and refining the project outputs and supporting dissemination activities. Patient representatives shared lived experiences, contributed to patient-specific model development, and participated in group discussions during the workshops.

papers.title: Development of a Women's Empowerment Nurse‐Led Group Intervention for Benzodiazepine and Z‐Hypnotic Deprescription in Primary Healthcare: Results of a Co‐Creation Process
papers.authors: Amaia Cuesta‐Zigorraga, Carlota Las Hayas, Garazi Aldanondo, Clara Sánchez-Sánchez
papers.abstract: AIM: The aim of this study was to co-create a nurse-led women's empowerment group intervention to facilitate the deprescription of benzodiazepines and Z-hypnotics in primary care. DESIGN: User-centred design based on co-creation. METHODS: A literature review was conducted to identify female empowerment programmes that served as an initial prototype. The subsequent user-centred design applied a co-creation methodology in two structured phases: (1) Exploratory, to identify contextual needs and barriers, and (2) Development, to collaboratively define the intervention's final structure and content. Participants included chronic users of benzodiazepines and Z-hypnotics and primary care professionals (doctors, nurses, and pharmacists) who actively engaged in the collaborative design process. RESULTS: The Exploratory phase identified structural and clinical deprescribing barriers, and female clients' knowledge gaps. Empowerment was confirmed as a key facilitator. The Development phase prioritised content (self-esteem, self-image, and healthcare) and adjusted the group intervention's format (duration, frequency, and structure) based on participant input. CONCLUSION: The co-creation process resulted in an eight-session intervention, with support cards and a training video for nurse-facilitators. This collaboration ensured the final design was precisely tailored to women's needs and clinical practice, maximising its feasibility and relevance. The intervention facilitates the tapering of benzodiazepines and Z-hypnotics by combining women's empowerment with individualised and supervised dose reduction by primary care clinicians. WHAT DOES THIS PAPER CONTRIBUTE TO THE WIDER GLOBAL CLINICAL COMMUNITY?: Demonstrates how co-creation with clients and healthcare professionals can lead to contextually adapted nurse-led interventions centred on women's empowerment. Highlights the role of women's empowerment as a catalyst for deprescribing long-term benzodiacepines and Z-hypnotics in primary healthcare. Introduces a structured and co-created eight-session intervention supported by a nurse-training video and support cards, offering practical toolkits. PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Clients (as users) and primary care healthcare professionals actively participated in the design of the intervention aimed at empowering women. Their involvement included participation in co-creation workshops, in which needs and everyday realities relevant to the process of deprescribing benzodiazepines and Z-hypnotics were identified. The structure and content of the group intervention, as well as its relevance and feasibility, were defined collaboratively. This direct participation made it possible to develop an intervention that was more client-centred, equitable, and aligned with clinical practice. REPORTING METHOD: This manuscript follows the short-form Guidance for Reporting Patient and Public Involvement (GRIPP2) checklist (Staniszewska et al., 2017) to ensure transparent reporting of the co-creation process, in which clients and healthcare professionals actively participated in the design, development, and evaluation of the intervention (Additional file 1. GRIPP 2).

papers.title: Obesity and Low Handgrip Strength as Contrasting Predictors of Cognitive Impairment in Indonesian Older Adults
papers.authors: Lala Sri Fadila, Ernis Asanti
papers.journal: Geriatrics and gerontology international/Geriatrics & gerontology international
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Obesity and low handgrip strength represent two contrasting physical and nutritional conditions in older adults, each with distinct implications for cognitive health. Prior studies have reported inconsistent associations between obesity and cognitive impairment, whereas low handgrip strength has shown a more consistent detrimental effect. Limited evidence is available from Indonesia, a country experiencing rapid demographic aging. Objectives To examine the associations of obesity and low handgrip strength with cognitive impairment among older Indonesians using the Indonesia Longitudinal Aging Survey (ILAS) data. Methods A cross‐sectional analysis was conducted using data from 1495 ILAS participants aged ≥ 60 years. Cognitive impairment was assessed using the Six‐Item Screener (SIS). Obesity was defined using Body Mass Index (BMI) categories for Asian populations and central obesity using waist circumference cutoffs. Low handgrip strength was identified according to the AWGS 2019 cutoff points. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results The prevalence of cognitive impairment was 35.7%. After adjusting for sociodemographic and health‐related covariates, obesity by BMI was inversely associated with cognitive impairment (OR = 0.56, 95% CI: 0.41–0.75), as was central obesity (OR = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.49–0.84). In contrast, low handgrip strength was associated with increased odds of impairment (OR = 1.89, 95% CI: 1.48–2.41). Conclusions Obesity and low handgrip strength emerged as contrasting predictors of cognitive impairment in Indonesian older adults, highlighting the “obesity paradox”. Further studies are needed to clarify mechanisms and guide tailored nutritional strategies for healthy aging.

papers.title: Frequency‐Enhanced Single‐Channel EEG Sleep Staging via Cross‐Frequency Interaction
papers.authors: Huihui Zhou, Aiping Liu, Heng Cui, Chun‐Ren Phang, Feng Wan, Yanyan Wang, Xun Chen
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Automatic sleep staging using single‐channel electroencephalography (EEG) is important for reducing the acquisition complexity of sleep monitoring and may support future wearable and home‐based applications. Although recent deep learning models have demonstrated promising performance, they usually prioritize time waveform representations or frequency domain features in isolation, neglecting the synergy between these two domains. Moreover, the intrinsic cross‐frequency interactions in sleep EEG signals are rarely modelled explicitly in existing studies. To address these limitations, we propose a frequency‐enhanced single‐channel sleep staging framework via cross‐frequency interaction. The proposed model simultaneously learns temporal‐domain representations from raw EEG signals and frequency‐domain representations derived from the short‐time Fourier transform (STFT). To better capture oscillatory dynamics in sleep EEG, amplitude and phase components are explicitly decoupled and independently projected to construct amplitude and phase tokens. A cross‐attention mechanism inspired by phase–amplitude coupling (PAC) is introduced to explicitly capture cross‐frequency interactions, in which phase information modulates amplitude responses within the frequency domain. Finally, temporal and spectral features are fused and further modelled using sequence learning to capture sleep stage transitions across successive epochs. Experiments conducted on two public datasets, Sleep‐EDF and MASS‐SS3, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The model achieves 87.0% accuracy and 82.0% macro F1‐score on Sleep‐EDF, and 87.8% accuracy and 83.1% macro F1‐score on MASS‐SS3. These results indicate that the proposed dual‐domain and cross‐frequency interaction modelling framework can effectively improve the discriminative capability of single‐channel sleep staging models.

papers.title: Optimized Cardiorespiratory State at Tone Onset Enhances Sensory Responses but Not Associative Learning in Healthy Adults
papers.authors: Praghajieeth Raajhen Santhana Gopalan, Miriam S. Nokia
papers.abstract: Previous studies suggest that when a tone-conditioned stimulus (CS) predicting an airpuff towards the eye is presented at diastole during expiration, both sensory responses to the CS and trace eyeblink conditioning (TEBC) are enhanced. However, not all participants learn and individual variation in the body-brain relationship remains overlooked. We studied whether timing the CS based on an individually optimized bodily state enhances sensory responses and TEBC. We assumed so, as sensory response magnitude reflects attention and stimulus salience: A salient CS should facilitate TEBC. Forty-one young adults and 19 older adults completed a passive auditory task while electrocardiogram, respiration and electroencephalogram were recorded. The cardiorespiratory state associated with the largest N1-P2 response was identified individually. Optimal states varied across participants and did not differ between age groups. Participants underwent TEBC at their optimal state (Personalized) or at diastole during expiration (Control). As expected, the CS evoked a larger N1-P2 response in the Personalized than the Control group. However, conditioned responding, peak performance, and learning rate, or the proportion of good learners did not differ between groups. Older adults learned more slowly, made fewer conditioned responses, and were less aware of the tone-airpuff association than young adults. These findings tentatively suggest that enhancing early sensory processing of the CS may not improve TEBC, although the low reliability of the individually determined optimal state limits this conclusion. Future studies should examine whether timing external stimuli to specific bodily states effectively influences behaviour in tasks that rely on rapid sensory processing.

papers.title: Aging in Autism: An Event‐Related Potentials Study of Auditory Change Detection
papers.authors: Mariela Besse, Shasha Morel‐Kohlmeyer, Emmanuelle Houy‐Durand, Philippe Prévost, Laurie Tuller, Badiâa Bouazzaoui, Laurence Taconnat, Julia Capdeville, Lucie Angel, Marie Gomot
papers.abstract: Autistic individuals are often thought to exhibit reduced tolerance for change, which may stem from atypicalities in sensory processing, particularly in the detection of environmental changes. Within the predictive coding framework, this intolerance may reflect altered generation and updating internal predictions in response to sensory input, leading to increased prediction errors. Mismatch negativity and the P3a component are event-related potentials (ERPs) indexing automatic auditory change detection and involuntary attention shift. While studied in autistic children and young adults, little is known about how these components evolve during aging, an important gap as 21 million autistic adults over 60 are expected by 2050. This study examined mismatch negativity and P3a responses in 43 autistic adults (aged 21-64) and 60 nonautistic adults (aged 20-69) using a passive auditory oddball paradigm with standard (1000 Hz) and deviant (1100 Hz; p = 0.15) tones. Electroencephalography recording revealed no significant differences between autistic and nonautistic individuals on mismatch negativity and P3a amplitude or latency. However, mismatch negativity amplitude decreased with age over frontal site, similarly across both groups. No age-related effects were found for mismatch negativity latency or P3a measures in either group. These findings suggest that, from adulthood onward, the neural mechanisms underlying automatic change detection and preattentional processes are similar in both autistic and nonautistic adults, and that their overall time course of aging appears comparable, supporting the parallel aging hypothesis. Nonetheless, future research should explore how these preserved neural responses relate to behavioral reactivity to change in autism.

papers.title: Towards a Brain–Computer Interface (BCI) for Improving Phonological Processing in Developmental Dyslexia: An Exploratory Study
papers.authors: Xuanci Zheng, João Araújo, Quentin Busson, Usha Goswami
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have immense potential regarding the provision of therapies for disorders of development, but to date have typically been created for non-linguistic disorders such as ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder). Here, we present a BCI designed to improve linguistic phonological processing during natural speech listening, aimed at participants with developmental dyslexia. Phonological 'deficits' are considered a core feature of dyslexia across languages and are present from infancy in those later diagnosed with dyslexia. Here, a non-invasive EEG-BCI relying on auditory inputs and visual feedback was developed to optimise brain patterns related to phonological development in infants and children. The BCI focused on neural patterns identified using Temporal Sampling theory, which has found the theta/delta ratio during natural speech listening to be a key neural associate of impaired phonology. As a first step, the BCI was tested with adults. Adults with and without dyslexia played the BCI for 16 sessions and received pre- and post-testing regarding phonological awareness and single word and non-word reading skills. Learning was assessed both online, as in most BCI studies, and offline, enabling removal of a greater number of potential EEG artefacts. Significant associations between offline BCI scores (a measure of BCI learning) and improvements in non-word reading were found for all participants who learned the BCI, both dyslexic and control. BCI learning also showed significant associations with improvements in real word reading and amplitude rise time discrimination. The data are interpreted with respect to Temporal Sampling theory.

papers.title: Dynamic Phase Synchrony in Cortical Networks Underlying Conscious Awareness of Flicker
papers.authors: Yusuke Uchiyama, Toshimitsu Takahashi, Kensaku Nomoto, Soichiro Fujiki, Teruyuki Fukushima, Narumi Katsuyama, Toshihiro Kawase, Satoko Koganemaru, Kenji Kansaku
papers.abstract: Flickering light sources, such as fluorescent lamps, evoke neural oscillations in the occipital cortex aligning with the flicker frequency; however, this flicker often remains outside conscious awareness. This discrepancy suggests neural mechanisms gating flicker perception. While functional magnetic resonance imaging studies have indicated the involvement of large-scale frontal and parietal networks in conscious flicker perception, their low temporal resolution limits insights into the underlying dynamic interactions. Using electroencephalography and physically identical stimuli near the critical flicker-fusion frequency, we investigated the temporal dynamics of phase synchrony and power distribution. Flicker perception was characterized by an early increase in higher beta-band (19-28 Hz) synchrony, followed by an increase in gamma-band (29-48 Hz) synchrony between fronto-parietal and parieto-occipital regions at approximately 300 ms post-stimulus. This was accompanied by a global expansion of gamma-band power from occipital to fronto-parietal areas-effects not observed during fused perception. Conversely, alpha-band (8-14 Hz) synchrony between anterior and posterior regions showed a more pronounced reduction specifically during fusion. These findings suggest that frequency-specific coordination and global information sharing across large-scale networks may underlie conscious flicker perception. The emergence of broad gamma-band synchrony at around 300 ms may reflect the integration of local sensory signals into distributed cortical networks. Early beta-band synchrony may facilitate the initiation of this process through top-down modulation, whereas attenuated alpha-band synchrony during fusion may reflect insufficient engagement of these networks. Such dynamic interplay within distributed networks is suggested to be involved in shaping the temporal resolution of visual awareness.

papers.title: Double Negation Without Double Effort: ERP Evidence From Mandarin Chinese
papers.authors: Xiaodong Xu, Zichen Lin
papers.abstract: Accounts of negation processing, including two-step simulation, pragmatic, and monotonicity-based accounts, differ in their predictions about whether double negation requires additional cognitive effort relative to affirmation. Using event-related potentials, we investigated a Mandarin Chinese double-negation structure ("méiyǒu X bù Y") that is logically equivalent to its affirmative counterpart ("suǒyǒu X dōu Y"). Forty native speakers read context sentences (double negation vs. affirmation) followed by critical sentences containing semantically congruent or incongruent target words. Crucially, the target word appeared in a separate sentence, downstream from the negation operators; the design, therefore, tests whether a pragmatically licensed double negation establishes a discourse representation functionally equivalent to affirmation at the point of propositional evaluation. At the critical word, incongruent words elicited larger N400/P600 amplitudes, and these congruency effects did not differ between contexts, indicating equivalent representations and no detectable downstream cost. Post-critical analyses, however, revealed context-specific differences: the affirmation context showed a prolonged negativity to incongruency-plausibly reflecting sustained engagement with its more salient violation-whereas the double negation context did not. A representational similarity analysis (RSA) further showed greater neural tracking of incongruency magnitude in the double negation context at a later window (726-798 ms). Together, these findings indicate that a pragmatically licensed double negation supports downstream semantic integration as efficiently as affirmation, while later processing remains context-sensitive. Because this early equivalence is also consistent with a monotonicity-based account, we frame the early-equivalence/late-divergence pattern as a tentative dual-stage characterization to be tested in future work, rather than a decisive adjudication between theories.

papers.title: Perceptions of AI‐generated informational texts and effects of the source: An online experiment
papers.authors: Laura Maria König, Maren Catherina Podszun, Wolfgang Gaissmaier, Helge Giese
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly common for health information seeking, yet many people are still skeptical of its performance. This between-subjects online experiment tested whether informing readers that a text was produced by AI influenced their ratings in 774 participants. They were randomly assigned to read one of six brief texts and rated trustworthiness, interest, and perceived understanding, as well as intention to act upon the received information and willingness to share the information with others. Source information did not influence ratings, but only 41.5% of participants in the AI source condition noticed the source. Source awareness was associated with higher education and greater nutrition knowledge. Nutrition information produced by AI chatbots is generally seen as trustworthy, although source information is often ignored. Our research highlights critical implications for public health messaging in the digital age as consumers may not differentiate between information generated by AI versus other sources, although future research is required to assess source perceptions in AI-generated texts in more detail.

papers.title: A defense of instrumentalized flirtation
papers.authors: Mathew Gagné
papers.abstract: AnnaJochymek's account of flirtation in research with farright groups offers a valuable intervention into long-running debates concerning the ethics of intimacy in fieldwork.For some time now, anthropologists have generally accepted that researchers forge intimate relationships while in the field, relationships that fulfill both affective and social needs and provide richer data through bonds of trust and disclosure.At the same time, these relationships have been ethically scrutinized, often leading to developments within scholarship on fieldwork, reflexivity, and situated ethics.Underpinning these conversations is the assumption that these relationships are more ethically sound when they are based on shared emotion, when both the researcher and the interlocutor are engaging each other through genuinely shared feelings.But what happens when these emotions are one sided, creating asymmetric emotional investment and vulnerability?Jochymek describes how she uses flirting as a methodological tactic to maintain contact with Kordian, an elusive, wily gatekeeper.Although she does not reciprocate the feelings implied by his flirting, she appropriates flirting as a tool for achieving research aims.She uses humor, deflection, and conversational warmth to maintain rapport with him while keeping the erotic charge suspended.Her tactic is to downplay the erotic feeling while also leveraging it to keep him involved.At first glance, it may be easy to criticize this tactic as instrumentalizing one's erotic emotions for another's gain, creating an intrinsic power imbalance between parties.Her account, however, challenges this ethical formulation in two ways.First, Jochymek delinks flirtation from emotion, rendering it primarily a communications tactic.Flirtation can express genuine attraction or shared chemistry, but it can also function as a strategic performance to build rapport, negotiate boundaries, and solidify her power in an exchange in which Kordian is trying to dominate the negotiation.Jochymek chooses to go along with the flirtation without reciprocating it, complicating the notion that if flirtation is to be ethically stable,
