Despite these advancements, challenges remain around algorithmic transparency, pedagogical integration, and maintaining human agency. In contrast, developing countries are often in an access–readiness phase, where AI is primarily considered for expanding access, addressing resource limitations, and fostering basic digital literacy. Barriers such as infrastructure deficits, low AI literacy, and reliance on external algorithms hinder equitable adoption and localization efforts. The study highlights the contrasting challenges faced by each context: developed regions focus on ethical oversight amid innovation, while developing regions struggle with foundational capacity and sustainability. Based on these insights, an equity-driven framework for inclusive AI integration is proposed, centered on four pillars: governance and policy alignment, infrastructure and access equity, algorithmic transparency, and AI literacy. This framework aims to guide institutions in aligning AI adoption with local realities and promoting inclusive and sustainable education.

papers.title: Designing and Evaluating a Socratic-Scaffolded Conversational AI Assistant for Educational Tasks: Cross-Cohort Effectiveness, User Perception, and the Effort Signature
papers.authors: Kuei-Hao Li, Chia-Kai Chang
papers.abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) assistants are proliferating, yet direct-answer interaction can yield short-term task gains alongside skill regression on later unaided work. We report the design and three-semester evaluation of a Socratic-scaffolded conversational AI assistant in an introductory programming course at a northern Taiwanese university. The system layers retrieval grounding to instructor materials, Socratic-by-default response prompting, and metacognitive interaction tracking using Bloom's taxonomy. A cross-cohort task-effectiveness study (pooled N = 82) found large pre-to-post gains (d = 1.20) replicated across cohorts, although the absence of a non-scaffolded control precludes causal attribution. A perception study (N = 203) showed positive usability, acceptance, and satisfaction (normalized means 75–79%), with no decay across semesters. An interaction-pattern study (N = 90) revealed the predicted effort signature: users judged the Socratic mode more effortful yet endorsed it for perceived depth of understanding. We discuss implications for designing assistants for skill-building rather than task completion.

papers.title: How do we measure creativity? A systematic review and taxonomy of evaluative methods in human-AI co-creativity
papers.authors: Mahima Ahsan, Wenfang Shi, D. Vaughn Becker, Gonzalo Ramos, Daricia Wilkinson
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly integrates as a cognitive partner in day-to-day creative tasks, to truly understand the value and effects of this integration, it is critical to know how co-creativity is defined, measured, and understood. Without a coherent understanding of the evaluative practices in the field, it is challenging for researchers to determine which metrics are appropriate, for practitioners to adopt effective evaluative methods, and for the field to build cumulative knowledge. To address this pressing need, we conduct a systematic review of Human-AI (HAI) co-creativity measurement metrics and evaluative methods. Through a critical analysis of how creativity is conceptualized and measured, we synthesize existing evaluation practices into a taxonomy for interpreting HAI co-creativity research. This taxonomy provides a multidimensional framework for interpreting how creativity is operationalized across the literature. By mapping these measurement patterns and gaps, this study ultimately offers researchers and practitioners a deeper understanding of how creativity can be meaningfully assessed in Human-AI co-creative tasks and provides a starting point for the development of more rigorous and context-sensitive measurement strategies for HAI co-creativity and cognitive support.

papers.title: Fostering frontline employee trust in service robots through outcome interdependence
papers.authors: Qiushi Wang, Ping Han, Shuwei Hao

papers.title: How AI-vulnerable is Australian higher education assessment? A computational audit of Group of Eight Arts and Humanities units, 2022–2026
papers.authors: Gonzalo Villanueva
papers.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is profoundly disrupting higher education, prompting educators to redesign course and assessment practices. Yet evidence of the potential impact of GenAI on assessments and subsequent module redesigns remains unclear. Through data scraping and classification, this article audits 15,587 annual Arts and Humanities unit records and 53,915 assessment items across Australia’s Group of Eight universities from 2022 to 2026. This article presents the AI Vulnerability Index (AIVI) which rates assessment exposure against relative GenAI capabilities in each year. At all seven institutions with comparable data, average exposure rose sharply between 2022 and 2024 and remained above 2022 levels in 2026, although subsequent trends differed between institutions. In 2026, very-high-exposure items accounted for 53.1% to 70.7% of allocated marks, while 53.1% to 79.1% of units scored at least 0.60. Exposure was concentrated in unsupervised writing, especially take-home essays and research reports. Institutional policy categories showed no clear pattern of lower exposure. High exposure, however, is not intrinsically undesirable. Where GenAI use is authorised and aligned with learning outcomes, it may offer a pedagogical opportunity. Governance should therefore examine the mix of assessments, the intended role of GenAI, and evidence of learning required of students.

papers.title: Exploring the prediction of English learning self-efficacy by behavioural intention to use AI, dangerous beliefs in AI and AI skills
papers.authors: Rui Jiang, Ying Zhou, Qinghua Zou, Yushun Li
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping students’ English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning. This study applied the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) to explore AI attitudes for fostering English learning self-efficacy. A survey of 612 senior high school students confirmed the reliability and validity of eight constructs: English learning self-efficacy (SE), dangerous beliefs in AI, AI skills, behavioural intention to use AI, effort expectancy, performance expectancy, social influence and facilitating conditions. Results indicated that behavioural intention, dangerous beliefs and AI skills significantly predicted self-efficacy, confirming the direct prediction of students’ attitudes towards AI on EFL learning self-efficacy. Although dangerous beliefs did not significantly predict behavioural intention or AI skills, AI skills predicted behavioural intention and were predicted by social influence and facilitating conditions. Social influence emerged as a key factor, predicting dangerous beliefs, AI skills, behavioural intention and broader AI perceptions. These findings highlight the essential role of social context in AI adoption and suggest rethinking the functions of dangerous beliefs in AI and AI skills in AI-supported environments. These findings offer theoretical and practical insights for researchers, teachers and policymakers to enhance AI integration in EFL by addressing students’ learning self-efficacy and AI perceptions.

papers.title: A type of optimum online learning from quantile estimating equation and objective function
papers.authors: Lu Lin, Yujie Gai
papers.journal: Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation
papers.abstract: {The significance and novelty of this work are established through methodological development, theoretical analysis, and numerical experiments for quantile regression in streaming data.} Estimating equation and objective function are perhaps the most common tools in classical statistics and machine learning. The optimum frameworks are frequently used for optimizing the statistical inference and learning. Up to now, however, the optimum forms of the online updating have not been well explored. In this paper, these classical optimum notions are utilized to solve the modern issue: online learning. For quantile and quantile regression, a type of optimum frameworks of the online updating estimating equation and objective function are proposed, the notion of expectation derivative and the smoothing techniques are introduced to deal with non-differentiable objective functions, and the relevant iterative algorithms are suggested to implement the estimation procedures. The proposed methods can be applied to the models with possible heterogenous distributions. Theoretically, the asymptotic normality and oracle property are established. The behaviours of the methods are further illustrated by various numerical examples from simulation experiments and real data analysis.

papers.title: Control or co-creation: exploring ecosystem configurations based on power dynamics and sustainability focus
papers.authors: Taylan Kilinc, Wiebke Reim
papers.abstract: As manufacturing firms increasingly pursue sustainability and digital transformation, production systems are becoming more dependent on collaboration across industrial ecosystems. However, industrial ecosystems differ in governance, coordination, and steering, raising questions about why different arrangements produce divergent transition pathways in coordination, inclusiveness, and sustainability focus. While collaboration is widely emphasised as essential for sustainability transitions, less is known about how variations in power dynamics and sustainability focus shape ecosystem configurations and direction. This study examines how differences in power dynamics and sustainability focus generate distinct configurations and shape sustainability transitions. Drawing on 35 interviews across three industrial ecosystems in Northern Europe, we develop a typology based on two dimensions – power dynamics and sustainability focus – identifying four configurations: enforced efficiency, balanced optimisation, dominated innovation, and collaborative innovation. The findings show that sustainability transitions depend not only on sustainability focus but also on ecosystem coordination, creating trade-offs between control, collaboration, and transformation scope. By conceptualising configurations as outcomes of power dynamics and sustainability focus, the study explains why similar ambitions generate divergent pathways. The findings contribute to production research by showing how different ecosystem configurations influence coordination, collaboration, and sustainability implementation, while offering guidance for managers and policymakers supporting industrial sustainability transitions.

papers.title: Comparison of NotebookLM-Generated Podcasts and Article Reading for Radiology Learning
papers.authors: Aidan C. Sander, Benjamin Y. M. Kwan, Laura Wong, Umaseh Sivanesan, Arsalan Rizwan, Shane Natalwalla, Andrew David Chung
papers.abstract: Though podcasts are becoming increasingly popular in medical education due to their convenience, portability, and amenability to multitasking, their role in radiology education remains unclear. The emergence of artificial intelligence tools such as Google's NotebookLM, which can generate structured podcasts from peer-reviewed journal articles, presents a novel opportunity to integrate podcast-based learning into radiology education. We conducted an institutional initiative comparing resident learning using NotebookLM-generated podcasts to reading radiology research articles on knowledge acquisition and learner satisfaction. Reading produced more consistent knowledge gains, whereas gains with podcasts were more heterogeneous. Despite this, residents perceived the podcasts as more engaging, convenient, and less cognitively demanding. Qualitative feedback indicated that while podcasts show promise as accessible learning tools, they are currently constrained by limited technical detail, repetition, and the absence of visual content. In contrast, articles were described as comprehensive and rich in visuals, but also lengthy and dense. Our findings suggest that NotebookLM-generated podcasts are best positioned as complementary resources rather than replacements for reading, providing a brief overview of an article or reviewing previously studied material. Educators should consider verifying generated content for accuracy and pairing podcasts with original articles when visual or technical details are important.

papers.title: AI assisted development of interactive multimedia modules for resident self-directed learning
papers.authors: Sameed Khan, Charit Tippareddy, Navid Faraji
papers.abstract: Traditional digital supplements for resident self-directed learning, such as PowerPoint slides and recorded lectures, are primarily passive and may have lower effectiveness due to limitations of the communication medium. Interactive multimedia modules incorporating text explanations, dynamic interactive diagrams, and interspersed assessments represent stronger candidates for supplementing resident self-directed instruction alongside traditional avenues of teaching. Creating interactive modules requires a high time commitment and relevant technical expertise, however, AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT can enable radiology educators to produce comprehensive, aesthetic, and well-crafted educational modules. This article provides guidance for educators on how to use AI assistants to create effective and accurate interactive multimedia modules. Using an example of a module for hip arthrocentesis, the article walks through a pedagogy-first workflow from learning objective to finished artifact.

papers.title: Learning cylinder wake dynamics across Hopf bifurcation via a regime-adaptive dual-branch physics-informed neural network
papers.authors: Cong Li, Q Wang, Wei Song
papers.abstract: The ability to represent fluid dynamics across regime transitions remains a fundamental challenge in physics-informed machine learning. In cylinder wake flows, the Hopf bifurcation at the critical Reynolds number Rec≈52 induces a transition from a steady, nearly symmetric base state to periodic von Kármán vortex shedding, accompanied by a qualitative reorganization of the underlying solution manifold. This raises a key question of whether nonlinear fluid systems admit a unified neural representation across bifurcation-induced reorganization of the solution manifold. Here, we propose a regime-adaptive dual-branch physics-informed neural network to investigate this question. The model explicitly decomposes the solution space into steady and unsteady dynamical components, which are coupled through a continuous Re-dependent gating mechanism centered at Rec≈52, thereby reducing cross-regime interference during optimization. To ensure stable learning under continuous parameterization, we combine continuous Reynolds-number feature embeddings with a multi-stage curriculum learning protocol that progressively restores the contributions of time-resolved observations and transient physical constraints while retaining the complete Reynolds-number range throughout training. Using supervised computational fluid dynamics data at 11 Reynolds numbers over 5≤Re≤120, the framework is evaluated on six held-out in-range Reynolds numbers and two extrapolation cases, Re=2 and 126. The model accurately reconstructs the principal wake structures and key flow statistics at unseen Reynolds numbers, with particularly strong performance across the held-out in-range cases. These results show that explicitly encoding regime separation in the neural architecture improves the representation of bifurcation-induced solution-manifold reorganization and enables continuous parametric surrogate modeling across steady and periodically shedding wake regimes.

papers.title: Lie detection using RoBERTa with bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) optimized by enhanced running game optimization (ERGO)
papers.authors: Yan Jin
papers.abstract: Identifying deceptive statements accurately remains challenging due to subtle linguistic cues, contextual ambiguity, and domain variability. The suggested model includes several state-of-the-art elements, such as RoBERTa-based contextual word embeddings, a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) for sequential modeling, and an enhanced running game optimization (ERGO) algorithm for hyperparameter optimization. RoBERTa offers highly contextualized textual input representations, whereas the BiGRU layer focuses on these representations by learning bidirectional temporal dependencies. ERGO optimizer also improves the performance of the models by dynamic optimization of important parameters that include learning rate, dropout rate and batch size, and size of hidden units, which enhances convergence stability. The model was tested on two benchmark datasets, namely, the LIAR dataset, containing 12 836 fact-checked political statements, and the generalized deception dataset, which contains 125 590 deceptive and truthful texts in a wide variety of fields, including reviews, phishing emails, job scams, political statements, and news articles. A tenfold cross-validation was used to ensure sound and unbiased analysis. The results of the proposed ERGO-RoBERTa-BiGRU model have been shown to be very impressive with an accuracy of 98.87%, a precision of 98.75%, a recall of 98.38%, and an F1-score of 98.56%, which are much higher than all base and comparative models. Ablation studies also helped establish the fact that every architectural element contributes to the general performance.

papers.title: Predicting second-language learning performance through deep linguistic embeddings and behavioral indicators: A RoBERTa–IFPA–decision tree framework
papers.authors: Yingnan Wang, Xinyu Liang, Zhen Liu, Zhongxing Zhao
papers.abstract: This study proposes a hybrid data-driven framework that integrates deep linguistic, behavioral, and psychological features to predict second-language learning performance with high accuracy and interpretability. Using the Education First Cambridge Open Language Dataset (EFCAMDAT), this study employs a Robustly Optimized BERT Approach (RoBERTa), a transformer-based language model, to extract context-sensitive lexical, syntactic, and semantic representations from learner essays. Behavioral and psychological indicators, including engagement, motivation, and self-control, are combined with deep linguistic embeddings to construct a multimodal dataset. The improved flower pollination algorithm (IFPA) is used to identify the most informative features, while a decision tree performs the final predictive modeling because of its transparent structure and ability to handle heterogeneous feature types. Fivefold cross-validation on the EFCAMDAT corpus showed that the proposed RoBERTa + IFPA + decision tree framework outperformed six classical machine-learning baselines and three neural architectures, achieving an overall accuracy of 92.36% and an F1-score of 0.91. Statistical significance testing (p < 0.05) supported the observed performance gains, while the interpretability analysis identified lexical complexity, engagement level, and motivational stability as key predictors. The analysis of errors showed that misclassifications were mostly found at intermediate proficiency levels and reflected greater overlap among learner profiles rather than model failure. Overall, this framework offers an evidence-based connection between artificial intelligence and second-language acquisition, with implications for adaptive language assessment and individualized learning support.

papers.title: Impact of Fatigue on Mind-Wandering in Drilling Crews for Engineering Safety: A Lab-in-the-Field Experiment
papers.authors: Shen Liaoyuan, Su Hao, Qing Xin, Wang Xiaoqin, Wang Jian, Liu Lu, Zeng Yuxi, Zeng Yuhang, Song Yuqi
papers.journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Abstract Fatigue among drilling crews significantly impairs their attentional capacity and physiological functioning, potentially triggering a mind-wandering (MW) state that may ultimately lead to serious accidents. However, the underlying brain network mechanisms through which fatigue influences MW remain largely unclear, representing a critical research gap that requires in-depth analysis. This study is the first lab-in-the-field experiment conducted at oil and gas drilling sites to systematically examine the brain network characteristics associated with mind-wandering under fatigue and awake conditions among drilling crews. In terms of behavior, the results showed that participants in the fatigue group exhibited significantly longer reaction times during periods of MW compared to those in the awake group, with notable correlations between the MW state and specific brain network indices. Electroencephalography (EEG) network topology analysis showed that the fatigue group demonstrated reduced global efficiency and algebraic connectivity, increased modularity, and evidence of brain network reconfiguration. At the theoretical level, this study integrates fatigue and mind-wandering into a unified framework, in which their influence is chiefly manifested through reduced global efficiency, impaired sensory gating, and a reconfiguration of brain networks, i.e., mechanisms that together elucidate how fatigue reshapes the neural basis of mind-wandering. At the practical level, the findings provide a scientific foundation for safety management in high-risk industries: work arrangements should be optimized so that workers undertake pivotal tasks at the beginning of shifts, when their information processing capacity is comparatively intact. In addition, minimizing extraneous sensory interference and refining interface design can further reduce the likelihood of mind-wandering.

papers.title: Neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest: evidence review and institutional protocol proposal
papers.authors: Eduardo Drews Amorim, Rose Plotnik, Raphael Machado Castilhos
papers.abstract: Background: Cardiac arrest (CA) is associated with high mortality and neurological morbidity, mainly due to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Accurate neurological prognostication in CA survivors is essential to guide therapeutic decisions and provide appropriate care. Objective: To review the current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA and to propose an institutional protocol adapted to the resources of Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre (HCPA). Methods: The current narrative review was conducted in two stages: a literature review and the development of an institutional protocol. Articles were selected according to their clinical relevance and their contribution to current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA. The PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and SciELO databases were searched. The protocol was developed considering the clinical tools available at HCPA, including neurological examination, electroencephalography (EEG), and neuroimaging. Results: Brain injury after CA occurs in three stages: intra-arrest ischemia, immediate reperfusion, and delayed postreperfusion injury. Prognostic modalities include neurological examination, EEG, somatosensory-evoked potentials (SSEPs), serum biomarkers, and neuroimaging. Reliable predictors of poor outcome include absent brainstem reflexes at 72 hours, persistent EEG suppression, bilateral absence of cortical N20 potentials, and diffuse abnormalities on magnetic resonance imaging. The proposed protocol organizes assessments from admission to the Intensive Care Unit through day 5 after the return of spontaneous circulation. Conclusion: A standardized post-CA neurological prognostication protocol at HCPA may improve care quality, enhance communication with families, and support ethically-sound decision-making.

papers.title: Comparison of DeepSeek AI and Human Reviewers in Structured Evaluation of Neurosurgical Manuscripts: A Pilot Study
papers.authors: Kishore Balasubramanian, Daniel O’Connor, Beste Gülsuna, Visish M. Srinivasan, Daniel A. Donoho, Nicholas Sader, Christopher Salvatore Graffeo
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives Increasing manuscript volume has strained peer review, prompting interest in artificial intelligence (AI) as a supportive tool. We evaluated DeepSeek R1 as a structured peer reviewer of neurosurgical case-based manuscripts and compared its scoring patterns with those of an experienced editor and student reviewers. Design Exploratory, cross-sectional comparative study using a convenience sample of consecutively submitted manuscripts. Setting Single skull-base neurosurgical journal during a 6-month submission window (January–June 2025). Participants Three reviewer groups independently assessed 11 de-identified, unpublished neurosurgical manuscripts: first-year medical students (n = 154; each randomly assigned one manuscript after a course in biostatistics, epidemiology, and critical appraisal), the journal’s Editor-in-Chief (Experienced Reviewer), and DeepSeek R1. Main Outcome Measures Each manuscript was rated on a 3-point Likert scale (1 = low, 2 = intermediate, 3 = high) across five domains: Study Objective, Novelty, Study Design, Thoroughness, and Clarity. Results Significant between-group differences were found in four of five domains: Study Objective (H = 8.31, p = 0.02), Novelty (H = 9.74, p = 0.008), Thoroughness (H = 10.49, p = 0.005), and Clarity (H = 8.13, p = 0.02); Study Design did not differ (H = 1.45, p = 0.483). DeepSeek scored significantly higher than the Experienced Reviewer for Study Objective (p = 0.015) and higher than both human groups for Novelty. Conclusions DeepSeek showed consistency in structured domains but systematically inflated subjective ratings, particularly Novelty. A human-in-the-loop model integrating AI efficiency with expert judgment may optimize peer review.

papers.title: Research on keyword extraction algorithms for English teaching materials knowledge graph based on machine learning
papers.authors: Jiewen Chen
papers.abstract: In the process of higher education teaching, a large amount of teaching materials is generated, and collecting and managing these materials is of great significance. Taking the management of English teaching materials in universities as an example, this paper utilizes the advantages of knowledge graphs and graph databases in data storage and processing, combined with text information extraction algorithms, to explore the intrinsic relationships among teaching materials for better organization and integration. By incorporating the textual features of teaching materials into the TF-IDF algorithm and improving it, this paper proposes a machine learning-based algorithm for extracting themes from teaching materials. The algorithm extracts key knowledge points from the text and conducts experiments based on a defined dataset. Experimental results show that the algorithm significantly improves performance metrics such as recall rate, precision, and F1-Measure, validating its accuracy. Therefore, key knowledge points can be used to associate teaching materials with the constructed attribute graph model of university teaching materials, establishing connections between teaching materials and knowledge points as well as among the teaching materials themselves.

papers.title: Research on adaptive methods for EEG fatigue model based on cross-subiect transfer learning
papers.authors: Qianhui Zhong, Xuetai Chen, Yimiao Li, Mingdong Ke, Hao Chen
papers.abstract: When EEG fatigue detection is applied across individuals, the performance will plummet due to physiological differences. This paper proposes a Dynamic Feature Alignment and Adversarial Transfer Learning (DFA-ATL). This method dynamically weights the characteristics of source domain and target domain through attention mechanism to realize the gradual narrowing of distribution differences; Design multi-scale confrontation training of global domain confusion and local category alignment to suppress negative transfer and improve classification boundary clarity; Depthwise Separable Convolution (DSC) and knowledge distillation are introduced to compress the model by 3.9 times without loss of accuracy. Experiments on the public SEED-VIG data set show that the macro F1 score of DFA-ATL reaches 83.8%, which is 3.2% higher than the existing optimal method. The lightweight version only needs 5.1 ms for a single inference in embedded devices, which meets the real-time monitoring requirements.

papers.title: Fatigue state multi-index fusion annotation and early warning system for power operation safety
papers.authors: Qianhui Zhong, Xuetai Chen, Yimiao Li, Mingdong Ke, Hao Chen
papers.abstract: Aiming at the problem of poor robustness and high false alarm rate of single fatigue monitoring index in complex environment such as high temperature and strong electromagnetic interference in power operation, this paper proposes a multi-index fusion labeling and early warning system for safety fatigue state of power operation. The system constructs 12 key index systems, covering EEG power spectral density, operating speed variation coefficient, temperature and humidity index, etc. An adaptive weight adjustment mechanism based on the combination of analytic hierarchy process (AHP) - entropy weight method and reinforcement learning is designed to realize the real-time dynamic optimization of index weight; The edge computing early warning terminal is developed, and the reasoning delay is controlled within 300 ms by using model compression and quantization technology to meet the real-time demand on site. The average F1 score of the system is 85.5%, which is 16.4 percentage points higher than that of the best single index method. The early warning delay of 97.2% is less than 300 ms, which is significantly better than the traditional monitoring methods. The experimental results verify the effectiveness and practicability of multi-index fusion and dynamic weighting mechanism in complex power operation environment, which provides reliable technical guarantee for power operation safety.

papers.title: Fatigue recognition method based on multi-entropy feature fusion of prefrontal single-lead EEG signals
papers.authors: Xuetai Chen, Qianhui Zhong, Yimiao Li, Mingdong Ke, Hao Chen

papers.title: Research on EEG artifact removal method based on PCA and LLE and its application in fatigue detection
papers.authors: Xuetai Chen, Qianhui Zhong, Yimiao Li, Mingdong Ke, Hao Chen
papers.abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) signal is easily disturbed by electro-oculogram and electromyogram artifacts in fatigue detection. A hybrid framework of dynamic threshold principal component analysis (PCA) and incremental local linear embedding (LLE) is proposed. In this method, firstly, the energy entropy of sliding window wavelet packet is used to locate the artifact burst adaptively, and the spatial correlation coefficient is used to guide PCA component removal to realize strong artifact coarse removal. Then incremental LLE is introduced to suppress the residual nonlinear artifacts while preserving the fatigue related low dimensional manifold through the neighborhood cache and weight update mechanism. Experiments on public SSVEP-Fatigue (25 subjects, 64 guides) and self-driving monotonous driving (20 subjects, 32 guides) data sets show that the proposed method is superior to FastICA, PCA-JADE, CEEMDAN-KICA and other controls in RMSE, δ SNR and correlation coefficient, and RMSE decreases by 40.9% and δ SNR increases by 84.0%. The features such as θ/β, (α+θ)/β power ratio, sample entropy and prefrontal lobe-occipital lobe phase lock value extracted after artifact removal are input into online Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) for fatigue classification. The accuracy rate is 88.63%, and the sensitivity is 89.24%, which is 16.29% higher than the original EEG baseline, and meets the needs of real-time vehicle warning.

papers.title: Design and implementation of a multimodal fatigue state assessment system for power operation scenarios
papers.authors: Xuetai Chen, Qianhui Zhong, Yimiao Li, Mingdong Ke, Hao Chen
papers.abstract: Based on the requirement of real-time fatigue monitoring in power high-risk operation scenarios, a multimodal fatigue state assessment system with a three-layer structure of "sensing-edge-cloud" is proposed. The sensing layer centers on a flexible electroencephalogram (EEG) headband, distributed surface electromyography (sEMG) patches, and low-power electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. It employs differential transmission combined with adaptive filtering to suppress strong electromagnetic interference. At the edge, a quantitative 3D-CNN-LSTM hybrid model is deployed in Jetson Nano to realize real-time fatigue classification with more than 92% accuracy within 150 ms; Cloud-based graph neural network (GNN) network is used to construct the fatigue Knowledge Graph (KG) of workers, which supports long-term trend analysis and scheduling optimization. The dynamic weight fusion module of entropy method is innovatively proposed, and the physiological/behavioral modal weights are adjusted in real time according to the environmental noise, and the strong interference scene F1 is improved by 12.5%. Experiments on 28 electric power workers show that the average accuracy of the system is 95.2%, and the extreme temperature fluctuation is less than or equal to 0.5%, which meets the requirements of real-time and robustness on site and provides a lightweight solution for power safety operation.

papers.title: Optimization of reinforcement learning algorithm for digital talent training
papers.authors: Zhaolin Zhang, Jianhui Sun, 邹静
papers.abstract: In the digital age, there is an increasing demand for talents with digital skills and innovative ability. Reinforcement learning (RL), as an advanced machine learning framework, provides a new idea for the cultivation of digital talents. However, the existing RL algorithm still has some shortcomings in sample efficiency, generalization ability and personalized learning support. Aiming at these problems, this paper puts forward a series of optimization strategies. Firstly, the sample efficiency of the algorithm is improved and the learning process is accelerated by experience playback and priority sampling. Secondly, regularization and domain randomization are used to enhance the generalization ability of the algorithm, so that it has better adaptability in different scenarios. Finally, based on multi-agent and hierarchical RL method, personalized learning support for learners with different learning styles and ability levels is realized. The experimental results show that the optimized RL algorithm has obvious advantages in learning speed, accuracy and generalization ability, which provides strong algorithm support for the efficient cultivation of digital talents.

papers.title: Research on algorithm-driven optimization of higher education teaching process
papers.authors: Jun Dong
papers.abstract: This study focuses on the algorithm-driven optimization of higher education teaching process, and improves the teaching quality and efficiency through algorithm technology to meet the individualized development needs of students. First of all, the algorithm is used to collect and analyze students' learning behavior data to form a learning portrait, which provides support for personalized teaching. Then, by optimizing the teaching content and choosing the appropriate teaching mode, the pertinence and effectiveness of teaching can be improved. In addition, the algorithm technology is also applied to improve the interaction between teachers and students. Through intelligent question answering system and other tools, it promotes real-time interactive communication and improves the efficiency and quality of interaction. In teaching evaluation and feedback, the algorithm can objectively and accurately evaluate students' learning effect and teachers' teaching quality, and provide timely suggestions for teaching improvement. The case analysis of the course "Fundamentals of Machine Learning" shows that the teaching scheme optimized by the algorithm has significantly improved the teaching effect, improved the students' average grade and class participation, reduced the knowledge forgetting rate, and further enhanced the personalization and interactivity of teaching through the behavior prediction model and intelligent teaching assistant system. The research results show that the algorithm technology has obvious advantages and broad application prospects in the optimization of higher education teaching process.

papers.title: Application of artificial intelligence algorithm in piano performance skill assessment
papers.authors: He Le
papers.abstract: In this study, we advocate the building of an assessment model of piano playing skills using CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) to solve the subjectivity and inconsistency of traditional assessment methods. By collecting and preprocessing the audio data of piano performance, the characteristics related to performance skills are extracted, and the CNN model is designed and trained. The experimental results show that compared with SVM (82%) and random forest (91%) methods, the CNN accuracy is higher than 95%, and the stability of this model can be achieved more than 90% in different data sets. The results demonstrated the high accuracy and stability of CNN model in evaluating piano playing skills, and could successfully recognize analytic piano different playing skills. This study contributes not only a new perspective and method for automatic assessment of piano performance, but also robust support for music education and learning.

papers.title: Healthcare professionals’ perceptions on AI-assisted decision-making in clinical practice: a qualitative meta-synthesis
papers.authors: Zihao Song, 侯东江, Ting Zhang, Huaping Huang, Xinyu Chen, Xianying Lu, Dingxi Bai, Xuemei Xie, Yue Li, Ting Cao, Yuhang Li, Xiaohui Dong, Jing Gao
papers.abstract: Healthcare professionals’ perceptions are central to how AI-assisted decision-making (AI-ADM) is understood, accepted, and used across clinical contexts. This qualitative meta-synthesis, guided by Normalization Process Theory (NPT), synthesized healthcare professionals’ perceptions on AI-ADM and identified factors shaping its clinical use. Ten databases were searched through November 9, 2025. We conducted a framework-guided qualitative synthesis by combining the first two stages of Thomas and Harden’s thematic synthesis with NPT-based deductive framework interpretation. Analysis of 13 studies from nine countries revealed that while healthcare professionals recognized AI-ADM’s potential in accelerating diagnosis, optimizing workflows, and enabling personalized medicine, critical challenges emerged across NPT’s four constructs: Coherence (challenged by difficulties in understanding the reasoning and evidence base underlying AI-ADM recommendations), Cognitive Participation (hindered by responsibility ambiguity and autonomy concerns), Collective Action (complicated by privacy, data security, and informed consent concerns), and Reflexive Monitoring (shaped by concerns about real-world reliability, over-reliance on AI-ADM, weakening humanistic care, and equity in resource allocation). Successful AI-ADM use requires clear accountability frameworks, transparent and interpretable models with explicit performance boundaries, and validated monitoring systems addressing algorithmic bias. Addressing these interconnected challenges may support responsible AI-ADM use while upholding the fundamental values of fair, transparent, and patient-centered healthcare.

papers.title: Beyond the sycophantic vs. cold divide: towards flexible, emotionally intelligent agents to foster healthier human-AI interactions
papers.authors: Christian Montag, Michiel Spapé, Derek F. Wong, Haiyan Wu, Joseph P. Dexter, Chengzhong Xu
papers.abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) have only recently become ubiquitous, psychological distress following user-LLM interaction has already been documented in both the scientific literature and the popular media. Such distress may be related to the tendency of some LLMs to provide sycophantic responses that uncritically reinforce the views of the user. To support users’ healthy emotional regulation, flexible, emotionally aware AI systems are needed.

papers.title: Cloud-deployable deep learning for smartphone-based body fluid cytology: a multi-architecture evaluation of YOLO and RT-DETR models
papers.authors: Sirinart Chomean, Noppmats Khemtonglang, Ekchol Mukda, Nutchanart Sittiphokkhasap, Yotsombat Changtrakul, Kornphon Wongphat, Areerut Mungmai, Tanatorn Tanantong, Chollanot Kaset
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate cytological evaluation of body fluid specimens is essential for diagnosing inflammatory and malignant conditions, yet manual interpretation remains labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability. This study developed and deployed a smartphone-based deep learning framework for multi-class body fluid cell classification integrating object detection, ROI-based classification, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Three hundred Wright–Giemsa–stained cytospin slides, one per patient, were used to generate 7149 smartphone-acquired images, which were annotated and curated into seven predominant cell classes. To reduce data leakage, images were partitioned at the source-photograph (slide-field) level. Five detection architectures (YOLOv8n, YOLOv10n, YOLOv11n, YOLOv11n-seg, and RT-DETR) were trained and evaluated on a held-out test set. YOLOv11n-seg achieved the highest mAP@50 (0.840), mAP@50–95 (0.757), and precision (0.772), while YOLOv11n achieved the highest recall (0.823). For YOLOv11n-seg, confusion-matrix macro-F1 and weighted-F1 were 0.720 and 0.730, respectively. Eosinophils, lymphocytes, and neutrophils were among the better-recognized classes, whereas errors were more frequent among monocytes, macrophages, and mesothelial cells. Grad-CAM++ analysis showed that model activation was predominantly centered within cell regions but was interpreted only as supportive model-inspection evidence. A Streamlit web application demonstrated browser-based inference with detection overlays, cell counts, differential composition, and data export. The system should currently be regarded as research, educational, and decision-support prototype rather than a standalone diagnostic device. External validation with patient-level separation, multiple imaging configurations, and broader cell populations is required before clinical application can be considered.

papers.title: Patient and healthcare professional preferences among predefined features of a peritoneal dialysis monitoring application in South Korea: an exploratory choice-based conjoint study
papers.authors: Ji Eun Kim, Taeyeon Kim, Sang Gyu Lee, Beom Seok Kim, Hyung Woo Kim
papers.abstract: Abstract Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is performed at home, where contact with healthcare professionals between clinic visits is limited. This exploratory study examined how patients receiving PD and healthcare professionals traded off five predefined attributes of a mobile monitoring application, derived from the Korean PD home-care reimbursement framework (monthly price, regular consultation, unscheduled consultation, educational content, and data management), and estimated conditional willingness-to-pay (WTP) . Between March and May 2022, 130 patients and 32 healthcare professionals completed a forced-choice conjoint survey without an opt-out alternative. Within the experiment, price accounted for about one quarter of relative importance in both groups. Among the functional attributes, patients assigned the greatest importance to unscheduled (23.0%) and regular consultation (22.2%), whereas healthcare professionals assigned it to data management (22.4%). Both groups preferred nurse consultation over a 24-hour chatbot (part-worth utility 0.814 vs. 0.117 in patients; 0.901 vs. − 0.185 in professionals). Among healthcare professionals, perceived institutional WTP was highest for monitoring patients’ daily health records. These values were reported by individual clinicians, not institutional purchasers, and are conditional on the selected price range, an assumed linear price coefficient, and the forced-choice design. These exploratory findings describe stakeholder trade-offs within a predefined, reimbursement-based choice set and are hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Sustainable construction and artificial intelligence: the role of agile project management in construction project resilience in Pakistan
papers.authors: Miao Miao, Mishal Hasnain Naqvi, Muhammad Hasnain Abbas Naqvi, Ehsan ullah Jamal
papers.abstract: This research analyzes sustainable construction practices and technology adoption, and their relationships with the adoption of Agile Project Management and the resilience of construction projects. Agile Project Management is incorporated in the model as a bridge. Employing DCT as the major research foundation, this study assesses the role of integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and sustainable construction practices with project resilience through Agile Project Management. The Technology-Organization-Environment framework provides context to the integration of AI and construction in Pakistan. The CAS theory provides a wider framework to think about the system. The T-O-E framework and the CAS theory are integrated and do not require empirical evidence. Agile Project Management combines sustainability and construction practices with Artificial Intelligence to facilitate achievement of project resilience. Findings demonstrate that both the integration of AI with construction practices and project resilience are positively influenced by sustainable construction practices. Of all the relationships evaluated, AI integration with construction practices showed the highest positive influence on project resilience. It is important to exercise caution when interpreting this relationship, as all the relationships were assessed in a single, cross-sectional survey, therefore, it could be attributed to common method biases. The T-O-E framework addresses the integration of AI with construction in Pakistan, while the CAS theory is integrated and does not require empirical evidence. A Construct validity approach was used to assess professionals and students of Construction and related disciplines in the Punjab province of Pakistan. Of the 300 questionnaires distributed, 244 completed responses were received. PLS-SEM analysis was performed on 188 questionnaires, from which 56 were rejected due to failure to meet quality standards. The analysis was conducted using an adapted form of multi-item scales of 5-point Likert scale, to assess sustainable construction, artificial intelligence, and agile project management. Data were analyzed through the framework of PLS-SEM. Results showed that integration of Artificial Intelligence in project management enhanced project resilience. The effect of agile project management on project resilience also was positive. Further, the effect of sustainable construction on project resilience also was positive. Additionally, the effects of integration of Artificial Intelligence and sustainable construction combined positively influenced project resilience. This research extends Dynamic Capabilities Theory, by incorporating AI and construction methods focused on sustainability in the field of agile project management and project resilience.

papers.title: Application of a PBL-ChatGPT combined package in teaching film-reading for laboratory medicine residents
papers.authors: Sisi Feng, ZHONG Baiyun
papers.abstract: Abstract Teaching film-reading is the most basic clinical teaching activity in the standardized residency training of laboratory medicine department. How to integrate theoretical knowledge with clinical cases and imaging data in a resident-centered manner remains a challenge. Problem-based learning (PBL) is a student-centered teaching method that fosters critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Considering that artificial intelligence technology has a wide range of application prospects in the field of medical education, we introduced a combined pedagogical package of PBL and ChatGPT in teaching film-reading. The aim of the study was to measure the effectiveness of the PBL-ChatGPT combined package in teaching film-reading for laboratory medicine residents in comparison with traditional teaching. Residents were randomly assigned to receive either the PBL-ChatGPT combined package (hereafter referred to as the PBL-ChatGPT group) or traditional teaching (traditional group). After each course, the members of each group were required to complete in-class quizzes and a standardized film-reading assessment form for residency training. Residents’ acceptance and satisfaction with the combined package were evaluated through a survey. Both the theoretical and film-reading examination scores were significantly higher in the PBL-ChatGPT group than in the traditional group (both P < 0.001), with large effect sizes (rank-biserial correlation 0.72 and 0.65, respectively). On the standardized film-reading assessment form, the PBL-ChatGPT group scored significantly higher in the preparation, methodology and overall evaluation domains (all P < 0.001, below the Bonferroni-corrected threshold of 0.0125 applied across the four pre-specified domains) and in the total score ( P < 0.001), whereas no significant difference was detected in the process domain ( P = 0.121). Residents’ feedback on the combined package was highly positive. The study indicates that the PBL-ChatGPT combined package holds significant potential as an innovative model for teaching film-reading to laboratory medicine residents.

papers.title: Emotionally intelligent preference optimization for conversational behavior change support
papers.authors: Ben Chen, Nina Dethlefs
papers.abstract: Abstract Procrastination negatively affects productivity and well-being, yet current large language models (LLMs) often lack the nuanced emotional understanding necessary for effective behavior-change support. This study proposes emotionally intelligent preference optimization (EIPO), a unified framework integrating emotional chain-of-thought reasoning, teacher-guided self-correction, and direct preference optimization to enhance emotional intelligence in conversational user interfaces. Through ablation experiments evaluated using the emotional generation score (EGS), we demonstrate that EIPO significantly improves empathetic and constructive responses in procrastination-related interactions. Crucially, cross-model validation on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Gemma-2-2B confirms EIPO’s model-agnostic design, with consistent EGS gains ( $$\Delta = +0.13$$ to $$+0.27$$ ) and robust independent evaluation using Claude-3.5-Sonnet. These findings establish EIPO as a principled, transferable framework for embedding emotionally intelligent behavior-change support into diverse LLM-driven CUIs.

papers.title: Translational evidence of tricarboxylic acid cycle disruptions in obesity: relevance to neuropsychiatric symptoms
papers.authors: Cassandra Elise Gheorghe, Juliette Montet, Sylvie Vancassel, Camille Amadieu, Quentin Leyrolle, Sandra Dexpert, Cédric Beau, Damien Forestier, Patrick Ledaguenel, E. Magne, Nathalie Castanon, Lucile Capuron
papers.abstract: Abstract Obesity is a major public health concern frequently associated with an increased susceptibility to neuropsychiatric symptoms, highlighting the need to elucidate the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying this comorbidity. While converging evidence supports a role for chronic low-grade inflammation, emerging data suggest that additional immunometabolic alterations may also participate, particularly disruptions in mitochondrial tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle activity, a central component of cellular energy production. This translational study investigated whether TCA cycle alterations are associated with obesity-related neuropsychiatric symptoms, and whether their associations differ across symptom dimensions. Plasma levels of TCA cycle metabolites were assessed in 83 adults with obesity (BMI > 30 kg/m²), along with depressive (Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale, MADRS), anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, STAI-state form), and fatigue symptoms (Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory, MFI). Concurrently, depressive-like (Sucrose Preference Test, Forced Swim Test) and anxiety-like behaviors (Elevated Plus-Maze) were measured in C57BL/6J male mice chronically exposed to high-fat diet (HFD), together with plasma and brain (striatum, hippocampus, frontal cortex) TCA cycle metabolite levels. Lower circulating metabolite levels were associated with more severe neuropsychiatric symptoms in obese participants, particularly fatigue and reduced motivation. In addition, the preclinical study identified region-specific associations between brain TCA cycle metabolite levels and behavioral outcomes, which may be modulated by HFD exposure. By providing novel evidence linking TCA cycle dysregulation and neuropsychiatric comorbidities in obesity, these findings highlight metabolites of potential interest and suggest that mitochondrial immunometabolic alterations may contribute to obesity-related neuropsychiatric symptoms.

papers.title: From stigma to trust: A paradigm shift for understanding perceptions of individuals with bipolar disorder.
papers.authors: Thomas Bradford Bitterly, Lisa A. O’Donnell, Melvin G. McInnis
papers.abstract: Individuals with bipolar disorder (BD) face professional and personal challenges such as underemployment. Navigating these challenges involves the dilemma of whether to disclose their illness or conceal it and risk presenting symptoms. Examinations of these challenges are often anchored in stigma, which has attributed negative employment outcomes for individuals with BD to adverse reactions from managers following disclosure. Across three experiments, including a managerial sample and a novel chatbot interaction, and eight supplemental studies (N = 8,112), the present research proposes and tests a trust-based attributional model. Mania, the hallmark symptom of BD, signals activation-based unpredictability, which serially erodes the perceived trustworthiness of an employee, ultimately compromising a manager's trust and willingness to retain the employee. The current findings demonstrate that disclosure is not uniformly harmful and that stigma operates as a distal moderator. An employee disclosing in the absence of mania can appear less predictable, and managers high in preexisting stigma toward BD generally view employees as less predictable. However, when manic symptoms are visible, disclosure buffers against their negative impact by providing an explanation for the erratic behavior. Together, this research reveals that moving beyond stigma-centric accounts clarifies managerial perceptions of employees with BD, with disclosure and stigma shaping this trust-based process. papers.title: From microstates to network connectivity: Age-related differences in resting-state electroencephalography and their implications for cognitive abilities in adulthood.
papers.authors: Ying Cui, Yating Bai, Chenghui Tan, Ling Bao, Qingfang Zhang
papers.abstract: The relationship between resting electroencephalography brain characteristics and cognitive abilities, particularly in the context of aging, remains unclear. In this study, we analyzed dynamic microstates, power spectrum, and functional connectivity in electroencephalography resting-state data collected from 123 younger individuals (17-32 years) and 99 older adults (60-81 years) experiencing normal aging, under both eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. We also examined correlations between these brain features and cognitive abilities, including working memory, processing speed, and inhibition. Our results revealed age-related differences in the balance between microstates C' and D, as well as in power across the delta, theta, and alpha bands, and in intra- and interhemispheric connectivity patterns. Older adults also exhibited an anterior shift and decreased asymmetry in power. Notably, significant associations emerged between these brain features and cognitive abilities, particularly in forward and backward working memory, with the effects being more pronounced in the older group. Our findings indicate a decline in overall resting-state electroencephalography brain activity with age, along with a shift in the balance between attentional and default mode networks, emphasizing the strong connection between these neural changes and cognitive abilities. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Implementing a Course-Specific Chatbot in Undergraduate Biochemistry
papers.authors: Michael C. Marvin
papers.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly available to students, but their educational value depends on how they are configured, constrained, and integrated into course practices. This technology report describes a no-code workflow for implementing a course-specific chatbot in upper-division undergraduate biochemistry using a custom GPT configured with instructor-generated lecture slides, class transcripts, handouts, syllabus information, and custom instructions. The workflow emphasized course alignment, frequent updating, instructor validation, assessment scoping, and student prompt guidance. The chatbot was used in biochemistry I lecture across two consecutive fall offerings and extended to biochemistry II lecture for follow-up use. Student survey responses indicated substantial adoption and generally positive perceptions; peer-led supplemental instruction attendance and course-grade data are presented only as contextual information. The report highlights a practical, transferable approach for using no-code custom GPT tools to extend course-aligned study support while preserving instructor oversight and existing academic support structures.

papers.title: Growth patterns of children with congenital Zika syndrome in Brazil: a matched-cohort study
papers.authors: Juliana Freitas de Mello e Silva, Helena Benes Matos da Silva, Luciana Lobato Cardim, Mariana Ramos Pitta Lima, Rita Carvalho-Sauer, Maria da Conceição Nascimento Costa, Elizabeth Bailey Brickley, Bethânia de Araújo Almeida, Laura C Rodrigues, Maria Glória Teixeira, Rita de Cássia Ribeiro Silva, Mauricio Lima Barreto, Enny S. Paixão
papers.abstract: Background Children born with congenital Zika syndrome typically present with structural abnormalities and neurological impairments that can disrupt postnatal growth. We aimed to evaluate longitudinal anthropometric trajectories of children with congenital Zika syndrome compared with children without congenital Zika syndrome in Brazil. Methods In this matched-cohort study, we used Brazilian administrative data on singleton livebirths from Jan 1, 2015, to Dec 31, 2018, with follow-up routine primary care health data from birth to age 5 years. We excluded children with missing or inconsistent information about sex, type of pregnancy, birthweight, gestational age, date of birth, and anthropometric measurements. Cases of congenital Zika syndrome were obtained from the Brazilian Ministry of Health's Public Health Event Registry. For children classified with congenital Zika syndrome, we excluded those with a diagnosis of congenital syphilis or toxoplasmosis. An exactly matched comparison group of children with a similar likelihood of exposure to the Zika virus was selected. Descriptive statistics was used to compare anthropometric characteristics among children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly, children with congenital Zika syndrome without microcephaly, and children without congenital Zika syndrome. Using mixed-effects models, we estimated mean trajectories of length or height (cm), weight (kg), and BMI (kg/m 2 ) for these three groups. Multi-state models, stratified by microcephaly status and sex, were applied to compare transitions between nutritional status (based on WHO growth indicators) over time. Findings We analysed growth measurements for 1268 children with congenital Zika syndrome and 6340 matched controls. Measurements indicative of stunting (length-for-age and height-for-age Z score <−2), underweight (weight-for-age Z score <−2), malnutrition (BMI-for-age Z score <−2), and wasting (weight-for-length and weight-for-height Z score <−2) were more frequent among children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly (1676 [49·2%] of 3408, 1623 [39·3%] of 4126, 743 [21·8%] of 3408, and 839 [24·6%] of 3408, respectively) and children with congenital Zika syndrome but no microcephaly (924 [30·5%] of 3028, 857 [24·0%] of 3577, 566 [18·7%] of 3028, and 602 [19·9%] of 3028, respectively) than among children without congenital Zika syndrome (3489 [11·0%] of 31 836, 1355 [3·5%] of 38 172, 1490 [4·7%] of 31 836, and 1410 [4·4%] of 31 836, respectively; all p<0·0001). At age 5 years, adjusted mean height was 6·61 cm less in children with congenital Zika syndrome and microcephaly and 4·21 cm less in those without microcephaly than matched controls. In transition models, the 6-month probability of recovery from severe stunting (≥–6 SD to <–3 SD) among children with congenital Zika syndrome with microcephaly was 0·32 (95% CI 0·27–0·37) in males and 0·24 (0·20–0·29) in females. The transition probabilities increased among children with congenital Zika syndrome and no microcephaly (0·47 [95% CI 0·40–0·53] in males and 0·37 [0·30–0·44] in females). By contrast, the transition probabilities were at least 0·75 among all children without congenital Zika syndrome. Expected first passage times, representing the expected time to transition from one nutritional state to another, also indicated slower recovery in children with congenital Zika syndrome. Interpretation A substantial and persistent burden of growth impairment in children with congenital Zika syndrome highlights the need for sustained growth monitoring and targeted nutritional interventions to support long-term health in this population. Funding Wellcome Trust, Brazilian Ministry of Health. Translation For the Portuguese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

papers.title: Perceived Human Agency and AI-Assisted Idea Generation
papers.authors: Sarah Wu, Yuewen Yang, Angela Yuson Lee, Alex Liebscher, Kristina M. Rapuano, Kate Gaynor Niederhoffer, Jeffrey T. Hancock
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are popular tools for creative ideation, but have been shown to homogenize outputs across users. We test if encouraging people to use an AI tool with high (vs. low) human agency can mitigate this homogenization effect by augmenting one’s creativity, rather than offloading it. Participants were experimentally assigned to one of three conditions (high-agency approach with AI access, low-agency approach with AI access, or a human-only control) and generated creative uses for everyday objects. Contrary to our expectations, on the whole ideas did not differ in individual-level perceived creativity (as rated subjectively by human evaluators). However, a per-protocol, preregistered similarity-to-centroid analysis and an exploratory cluster analysis provided convergent evidence of AI-induced homogenization among the low-agency condition—conditional associations among participants who complied with the AI-use instructions. Thus, while readily available LLMs afford rapid idea generation at scale, our research suggests the degree of agency with which people approach their AI tool has downstream consequences on collective creativity.

papers.title: Longitudinal Changes in Cervical Length Prior to the Onset of Spontaneous Labor at Term Gestation
papers.authors: Puntabut Warintaksa, Supakorn Chaiyakarn, Maolee Bhuwapathanapun, Chalongraj Ratanawongsaroj, Orathai Munggaranonchai, Sasivimol Rattanasiri, Piya Chaemsaithong
papers.abstract: Background Common pathways of parturition include myometrial contractility, choriodecidual activation, and cervical shortening/remodeling. Currently, cervical component assessment is usually performed by digital examination, but this method is invasive, subjective, and inaccurate in evaluating the internal os. Cervical sonography provides an objective assessment of cervical effacement and other changes. Objectives The aims of this study were to: 1) characterize cervical length profile prior to the onset of spontaneous labor at term; 2) compare the cervical length profile between nulliparous and multiparous women; 3) evaluate the association between the magnitude of cervical length changes and the onset of spontaneous onset of labor within 24- or 48-hours after cervical length assessment. Study Design Design: A prospective longitudinal cohort study, Setting: Labor and Delivery unit, Bangkok, Thailand. Methods: A total of 135 patients were enrolled in this study. Thirty pregnant women met the exclusion criteria. Therefore, 105 patients who underwent transvaginal cervical length measurements every 3-4 days at 37-38 weeks and every 2-3 days thereafter until the spontaneous onset of labor were included in the analysis. Main Outcome Measures The primary outcome was the time interval from each cervical length assessment to the spontaneous onset of labor at term, defined as the interval between the date of the cervical length examination and the onset of spontaneous labor. Secondary outcomes included the association between the magnitude of cervical length changes and the subsequent spontaneous onset of labor within 24 or 48 hours after a cervical length assessment. Spontaneous onset of labor is defined as regular uterine contractions occurring at a frequency of at least 4 in 20 minutes for a minimum of 1 hour with either cervical dilatation ≥4 cm or effacement of ≥ 80% or cervical changes, or spontaneous rupture of membranes, followed by delivery within 24 hours of the onset of labor. Results 1) Cervical length demonstrated a gradually progressive reduction during the few weeks preceding the spontaneous onset of labor, with an evident reduction in 48 hours, 2) nulliparous and multiparous women had similar absolute cervical length profile; 3) among the cervical length changes patterns, absolute cervical length changes from the previous visit have the highest discrimination ability for the identification of spontaneous labor within 24 hours; 4) absolute cervical length reduction of >5 mm compared with the prior visit was associated with a significantly higher hazard of spontaneous onset of labor within 24 hours (hazard ratio 11.76; 95% CI: 3.27-42.28; p<0.001), after adjusting for maternal age, BMI, parity, gestational age at measurement and baseline cervical length. Conclusions Cervical length demonstrated a gradually progressive reduction during the few weeks preceding the spontaneous onset of labor, with an evident reduction in 48 hours. Absolute cervical length reduction of >5 mm compared with the prior visit was associated with a significantly higher hazard of having a spontaneous onset of labor within 24 hours (hazard ratio, 11.76). This knowledge may help identify women at an increased likelihood of spontaneous onset of labor within 24 hours.

papers.title: Cost-Effectiveness of AI in Breast Cancer Screening and Lung Cancer Diagnostics: A Case Study From Costa Rica
papers.authors: Lolita Kévine Aboa, Jean Carlo Segura Aparicio, Zheng Yang Fei, Pascal N. Tyrrell
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into breast and lung cancer diagnostic workflows in Costa Rica, addressing the scarcity of health economic evidence for AI adoption in low- and middle-income countries and focusing on context-specific systemic barriers. METHODS: Two state-transition Markov models compared AI-assisted workflows (AI as a first reader) with conventional radiologist-only strategies over a 10-year horizon. AI-supported mammography screening was evaluated in asymptomatic women aged 50 to 70 years. For lung cancer, symptom-driven pathways were modeled using GLOBOCAN 2022 incidence data. Inputs included region-specific costs (USD), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and progression probabilities, calibrated to Costa Rica's cancer registry. Methodological rigor adhered to the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 guidelines. RESULTS: AI in breast cancer screening demonstrated economic dominance: it improved QALYs by 49% (10.46 vs 7.04) and reduced costs by 49% (USD 93 102 vs USD 183 278), yielding a net monetary benefit of USD 212 119 at Costa Rica's willingness-to-pay threshold. For lung cancer, the AI strategy also proved dominant: it reduced total costs to USD 1 218 507 (vs USD 1 337 640) while increasing QALYs to 6.88 (vs 4.15), driven by earlier detection that averts expensive late-stage palliative care. CONCLUSIONS: AI significantly improved cost-effectiveness in both breast and lung cancer diagnostics, demonstrating economic dominance by mitigating diagnostic delays and reducing late-stage treatment burdens. These findings stress AI's context-dependent impact in low- and middle-income countries and the necessity of early detection investments and equity-focused implementation to align innovation with healthcare system realities.

papers.title: MT3 INFLUENCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING IN HEALTHCARE: A KAP STUDY AMONG FUTURE PHARMACISTS
papers.authors: Gautam Sahu, Sandeep Arora, Tapan Behl, Deepika Yadav
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare delivery and clinical decision-making through early diagnosis, precision medicine, and patient-centred care. Future pharmacists are expected to play a crucial role in integrating AI into healthcare systems. This study assessed the knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) regarding AI in clinical decision-making among pharmacy students, emphasising healthcare affordability, accessibility, and patient outcomes.

papers.title: Technology acceptance of passive brain-computer interfaces in vehicles for adaptive automation
papers.authors: Theresa Wehrle, Lisa Sophia Krahnen, Günther Bauernfeind, Adrian Haar, Bertolt Meyer
papers.journal: Transportation Research Part F Traffic Psychology and Behaviour
papers.abstract: Driver monitoring systems (DMS) enhance traffic safety by detecting critical driver states such as drowsiness and cognitive overload. Future brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) for driver monitoring and workload-adaptive automation promise direct access to neurophysiological signals, potentially offering higher sensitivity than conventional systems. Despite this potential, drivers' acceptance of BCIs in real-world driving remains largely unexplored. Because driving constitutes a complex sociotechnical system context, user, task, and system characteristics are likely to shape acceptance. This study thus examines the acceptance of non-invasive, wearable BCIs for workload-adaptive driver assistance from a sociotechnical perspective. We conducted an online experimental vignette study using a between-participant design ( N = 1201). Participants evaluated one of twelve animated driving scenarios in which a BCI detected high workload and initiated assistance. The scenarios varied three sociotechnical characteristics: driver status (able-bodied vs. disabled), the function within the assisted driving task (primary, secondary, or tertiary), and type of automation (adaptive vs. hybrid). Respondents evaluated acceptance using an adapted Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT2) framework. Acceptance of BCI-based adaptive automation varied systematically across conditions. Findings show that scenario evaluations indicated higher acceptance when BCIs supported driving-related functions and when the scenario depicted a driver with a disability. No differences were observed between the two activation modes tested. By integrating sociotechnical characteristics into an established acceptance framework, this study advances understanding of BCI acceptance in driving and informs the user-centered design of neuroadaptive driver assistance systems.

papers.title: From patient to partner: Bridging the divide from laboratory to patient through a “dragons' Den” style model of co-creation in cancer research
papers.authors: Ashwini Job, Beverly Agass, Charlotte Elizabeth Coles, Helene Judge, Andrew Land, Deborah Pitfield, Hilary Stobart, Amy Tang, Rhys Grant, Nicola Le Blond, N.G. Burnet
papers.journal: Technical Innovations & Patient Support in Radiation Oncology
papers.abstract: Patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) in cancer research is increasingly recognised as valuable; yet meaningful participation early in the cancer research pathway remains less common, particularly in pre-clinical science [2]. The Radiation Research Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement (PPIE) group at Cambridge has adapted a format similar to one used in a popular UK TV programme to develop a "Dragons' Den" style model of involvement. In this model, researchers pitch their proposed studies to a panel of patients and carers who provide structured, direct feedback using their lived experience. We describe the delivery model, early impact measures and its potential for broader adoption.

papers.title: Preparing nursing students for artificial intelligence in practice: A cross-sectional needs assessment of perceived readiness and curricular preferences

papers.title: Relationship analysis and visualization of research prompts using AI-based semantic topic modeling and knowledge graphs
papers.authors: Müzeyyen Bulut Özek, Bihter Das
papers.abstract: The rapidly increasing volume of unstructured textual data generated on digital platforms has intensified the need for robust, interpretable, and semantically consistent topic modeling approaches. Although classical probabilistic and matrix factorization–based methods such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA), and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) can identify latent thematic structures, they often fail to adequately capture contextual semantics and complex linguistic relationships. However, comparative explainable evaluation frameworks integrating semantic analysis, optimization, and knowledge graph (KG)–based interpretability remain limited in the literature. To address this gap, this study proposes a comprehensive hybrid topic modeling framework that combines classical statistical models and semantic embedding–based approaches within a unified explainable evaluation pipeline. The framework integrates LDA, LSA, NMF, BERTopic, Top2Vec, and Sentence-BERT + KMeans models with grid search–based coherence optimization, semantic similarity analysis, and KG-based visualization. Experiments were conducted on the publicly available Stable Diffusion Prompts dataset containing approximately 81,000 AI-generated creative text prompts. Model performance was evaluated using c_v and u_mass coherence metrics, runtime-based efficiency analysis, semantic similarity matrices, and graph-based topic relationship analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that BERTopic achieved the highest overall coherence performance, while SBERT + KMeans produced highly balanced and semantically rich topic distributions. Among the classical statistical topic modeling approaches, NMF achieved the strongest coherence performance, whereas BERTopic demonstrated the highest overall contextual semantic interpretability and embedding-based clustering capability. Moreover, KG-based analysis revealed meaningful inter-topic semantic relationships and improved the interpretability of thematic structures through graph-based visualization. The proposed framework contributes to the literature by providing an explainable and optimization-driven comparative topic modeling architecture that bridges symbolic and semantic paradigms for large-scale text analysis.

papers.title: Identifying students at-risk with explainable artificial intelligence: A case study for Australia
papers.authors: S. Janifer Jabin Jui, A. A. Masrur Ahmed, Ravinesh Chand Deo, Angela Murphy, Salvin Sanjesh Prasad, Sujan Ghimire, Shahab Abdulla, Aruna Devi, Zaher M. Yaseen, Prabal Datta Barua, Rajendra Acharya
papers.abstract: Learning analytics models may offer timely support to enhance student’s preparedness and educator’s success metrics in their education career. This study models student performance using assessment data as a predictor for EAP7381 (a Mathematical and Computing Literacy course). To estimate the overall score (OS) for EAP7381, the proposed predictive model incorporates unique input combinations for models designated as (M01, M02, …, M09) that are drawn from five different types of assessments: computer skills (CS), problem solving (PS), class surveys/analysis (SA), revision exams (REs) and final exams (FTs). Using a 10-fold cross-validation approach on 466 student records, the support vector regression (SVR) model was benchmarked against extreme gradient boosting (XGB), K-nearest neighbour (KNN), and random forest (RF) models. The proposed SVR model demonstrated high degree of accuracy, yielding relatively low prediction errors that were between the estimated and actual OS values. In Model M02, the assessment PS that was administered between two and eight weeks demonstrated a strong correlation with OS, revealed through explainable artificial intelligence techniques: SHAP (SHapley Additive explanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) The results indicated that PS was a significant contributor to the performance of our proposed model. The LIME and SHAP results also demonstrated that the predictor variables based on FT and PS were the most influential indicators of the proposed learning analytics model. In the context of an applied educational setting, we therefore conclude that such assessments, when used to model students at-risk can be further explored for its potential utility to address student performance issues, failure s and attrition in order to develop necessary interventions. To support the educators in developing multidimensional pedagogical strategies, the proposed SVR model can be thus integrated into future commercially viable education technologies that offer data-driven guidance for enhancing the learning journey of our students.
