papers.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) and the choroidal challenge: A comprehensive review of AI applications in choroidal imaging
papers.authors: Oscar Matteo Gagliardi, Jay Kumar Chhablani, Marco Lupidi, Maria Carmela Saturno, Alessandro Lambìase, Danilo Iannetta
papers.abstract: The choroid is a densely vascular layer that sustains the outer retina and may reflect systemic microvascular health. With the advent of new imaging techniques, choroidal imaging has become increasingly detailed, generating vast data volumes. Conventional analytic tools often fall short in managing these high-dimensional datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) automatically enhances, segments, and analyzes choroidal images, facilitating the discovery of choroidal biomarkers relevant to ocular and systemic disease. Yet, anatomical complexity, heterogeneous protocols, and a lack of large, annotated datasets hinder AI adoption. Overcoming these barriers is essential to assess AI-derived choroidal biomarkers as reliable diagnostic and prognostic tools.

papers.title: Generative AI in Bangladeshi EFL assignment writing: Academic integrity, learner responsibility, and pedagogical implications
papers.authors: Md. Kawser Ahmed
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) assignment writing raises linked questions about writing development, authorship, and learner responsibility. This qualitative interpretive study examined how students and instructors at three universities in Dhaka used and understood GenAI under conditions of uneven academic support and limited local guidance. The 31 participants comprised 17 students and 14 instructors or academic staff. The dataset contained 26 individual interviews (12 students and 14 instructors/staff), three focus group discussions involving 12 students (seven of whom were also interviewed), and available institutional and assignment-related documents and voluntarily supplied writing samples. Reflexive thematic analysis, supported by NVivo 14, combined inductive coding with theoretically informed interpretation. Five themes were developed: mobile-facilitated but uneven use; unsettled understandings of academic integrity; a locally salient “EFL justification” that distinguished language support from intellectual outsourcing; difficulty verifying confident but inaccurate output; and instructor-led pedagogical adaptation amid limited institutional guidance. Within the participating institutions, the findings suggest that responsible GenAI use cannot be reduced to detection or prohibition. It requires explicit AI literacy, assessment practices that make learning processes visible, and guidance that recognises the linguistic pressures of EFL writing while preserving intellectual ownership. The study offers context-bound, analytically transferable insights rather than statistically generalisable claims.

papers.title: Generative AI and digital productivity: Transitions, institutional misalignment, and human role redefinition
papers.authors: Sarach Tuomchomtam
papers.abstract: Generative AI is widely framed as a productivity tool. This framing understates its significance: when a technology lowers the cost of a fundamental input to the point of abundance, it disrupts not only the tools of an activity but the evaluation systems and professional cultures built around prior cost structures. This paper argues that generative AI constitutes the third transition in digital productivity, following the internet's reduction of information access costs and open data movements that restructured information flows, and develops five contributions toward understanding its institutional consequences. First, a three-transition model characterizes each transition by the input it makes abundant; the current transition makes structured written output abundant on demand. Second, a digitalization prerequisite thesis identifies machine-readable data foundations as a readiness condition most organizations and many individuals have not yet met. Third, a collaborative intelligence framework maps human comparative advantage shifting toward framing, critical evaluation, and contextual judgment as AI absorbs generative work, revealing that institutional credit concentrates at the production stage precisely where AI advantage is now greatest. Fourth, five structural tensions are identified: productivity surplus distribution and automatable job persistence, educational assessment disruption, AI authorship ambiguity, the professional performance threshold, and epistemic risks from fully AI-mediated communication chains. Fifth, a three-part governance framework (disclose, originate, accountable) provides actionable minimum conditions for AI-collaborative knowledge work across institutions and jurisdictions.

papers.title: Chatbots and digital transformation in Colombian banking: Drivers of continuance intention in an emerging market
papers.authors: Ernesto Barrera Duque, Jose Andres Areiza-Padilla, Iván A. Veas-González, David Andrés Londoño Bedoya, Karla Barajas-Portas, Jorge Isaac Lechuga Cardozo
papers.abstract: This study investigates users’ continuance intention toward AI-powered chatbots in the Colombian banking sector, a setting characterized by institutional asymmetries, trust-related concerns around digital financial services, and the continued relevance of interpersonal service expectations. Drawing on a Global South perspective as an interpretive lens, this study examines chatbot continuance intention in an emerging-market banking context where digital service evaluation is shaped by usefulness, satisfaction, perceived quality, and trust. Rather than treating institutional conditions as directly measured mechanisms, the study uses the Colombian context to interpret how post-use service evaluations operate in a relational and highly regulated financial environment.Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), data from 439 Colombian banking users were analyzed to assess four antecedents of continuance intention: perceived chatbot quality, trust, satisfaction, and perceived usefulness. The findings show that satisfaction is the strongest predictor of continuance intention, followed by perceived usefulness, perceived chatbot quality, and trust. Specifically, satisfaction showed the strongest effect (β = 0.380), followed by perceived usefulness (β = 0.250), perceived chatbot quality (β = 0.150), and trust (β = 0.110). The model explained approximately 58.1% of the variance in continuance intention. These results suggest that, in the Colombian banking context, positive post-use evaluations play a particularly central role in continuance intention, even when trust in digital financial technologies remains more cautious or uneven.

papers.title: Redefining Surgical Outcomes after Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: An American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Narrative Literature Review of Composite Response Metrics and Body Composition
papers.authors: Pavlos K. Papasavas, Faiz U. Shariff, Sofiane El Djouzi, Colleen M. Tewksbury, Jonathan T. Carter, R. Wesley Vosburg
papers.journal: Surgery for Obesity and Related Diseases
papers.abstract: Background Traditional assessment of response to metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) has relied predominantly on weight- and BMI-based outcomes. However, these measures, which are important to patients, fail to capture important dimensions of treatment response, including changes in body composition, obesity-related diseases, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Objectives To evaluate emerging approaches that incorporate composite response metrics and body composition assessment as outcome measures after MBS, complementing weight and BMI changes, which may not fully capture clinically meaningful improvements. Methods A narrative review of the current literature was conducted to examine composite outcome measures after MBS and body composition changes. Results BMI and conventional weight-based outcomes have limitations in assessing response to MBS and may systematically misclassify outcomes across patient populations. Composite measures such as the Bariatric Analysis and Reporting Outcome System (BAROS), Bariatric Quality of Life Index (BQL), and Swiss-Finnish Bariatric Metabolic Outcome Score (SF-BARI) integrate multiple dimensions of response, including weight loss, improvements in obesity-related disease, complications, and HRQoL. Furthermore, body composition assessment provides clinically meaningful information regarding changes in fat mass, visceral adiposity, lean tissue, and bone mineral density that are not captured by BMI or body weight alone. Conclusions Response to MBS should not be defined solely by weight or BMI change from baseline. A multidimensional framework incorporating composite outcome measures, patient-reported outcomes, and body composition provides a more comprehensive and patient-centered evaluation of MBS outcomes. Future research should focus on standardizing these measures and evaluating their feasibility for integration into routine clinical practice and outcomes reporting.

papers.title: Factors associated with artificial intelligence literacy of nursing students: A scoping review
papers.authors: Yu Xin, Mengqi Zhang, Shanna Jin, Chunxiao Feng, YuXiao Zhu, Ying Jin
papers.abstract: This study aims to integrate existing evidence through a scoping review method, sort out its key influencing factors, and provide a solid theoretical basis for constructing scientific and reasonable educational strategies. With the rapid development of smart healthcare, artificial intelligence technology has become an indispensable tool in clinical nursing practice. However, when nursing students face this industry transformation, they show insufficient application ability of artificial intelligence and uneven cognitive levels. This deficiency not only hinders the professional competitiveness of nursing students but may also affect the quality of future nursing services. Currently, the academic community has not systematically sorted out and analyzed the influencing factors of artificial intelligence literacy among nursing students. Understanding these factors will provide a key basis for solving the imbalance between nursing education and clinical needs and establishing a talent cultivation path that conforms to the development of the industry.

papers.title: Diagnostic AI tools in musculoskeletal imaging—Present and future
papers.authors: Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as the next step in musculoskeletal (MSK) imaging, yet its translation into routine clinical care, including osteoarthritis (OA), has been selective and challenging. This Perspective summarizes where diagnostic MSK AI tools stand today and argues that the central question is not whether models perform well in benchmarks, but whether they create measurable clinical value. Based on a keynote presentation at IWOAI 2026, we relate diagnostic AI tools in MSK imaging to the theme "Linking OA Tissues" by asking whether current AI tools can connect tissue-level imaging findings with whole-joint disease, longitudinal change, and clinical context. Drawing on the regulatory landscape and peer-reviewed evidence, we show that AI tools have been selectively translated into clinical routine: radiographic morphometry and fracture detection dominate among commercially available products because they are narrow, standardized tasks with transparent, easily verifiable outputs and an obvious clinical need. By contrast, MRI, the modality on which advanced OA assessment largely depends, remains a bottleneck. OA is a particularly challenging target because it is a multi-tissue, whole-joint, longitudinal, and context-dependent disease for which binary, single-task outputs are too crude. Furthermore, we propose a deliberately non-quantitative framework in which useful AI is the product of model performance, relevant endpoints, workflow fit, and human-AI interaction; failures of translation typically reflect deficits in the latter three rather than in model performance alone. Realizing clinical value in MSK and OA imaging will require validation against patient-relevant endpoints, attention to how readers interact with AI, and reference standards that go beyond curated benchmarks.

papers.title: Orforglipron Improved Physical and Psychosocial Functioning in Adults with Obesity: Results from ATTAIN Phase 3 Randomized Trials
papers.authors: Michelle Look, Harold Bays, Carel Wynand le Roux, Neena Xavier, Sheryl Elaine Allen, Irina Jouravskaya, Adam Stefański, Georgios K. Dimitriadis, Benjamin Behrend, Wenyu Ye, Jinhong Li, Theresa Hunter Gibble, Christy R. Houle
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background In ATTAIN, phase 3, randomized, placebo-controlled trials, orforglipron treatment resulted in substantial weight reduction among people with obesity with or without type 2 diabetes. Methods This was a prespecified secondary and post-hoc analyses of patient-reported outcomes (PRO) (ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2). Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) was assessed from baseline to week 72 (efficacy estimand) using Short Form-36 Version 2 Health Survey acute form (SF-36v2), Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite-Clinical Trials Version (IWQOL-Lite-CT), EQ-5D-5L and associated EQ visual analog scale (EQ VAS), and Patient Global Impression of Severity (PGIS) and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC) for Physical Activity. Post-hoc analysis assessed changes in outcomes among orforglipron-treated participants by body mass index (BMI) subgroups (<35 kg/m 2 , ≥35 to <40 kg/m 2 , and ≥40 kg/m 2 ) and by baseline physical function limitations, as defined by PGIS. A mixed-model for repeated-measures (MMRM) was used, adjusting for treatment and key covariates. Results Across both ATTAIN trials, participants receiving orforglipron demonstrated greater improvements than those on placebo in PROs across most SF-36v2, IWQOL-Lite-CT and EQ-5D-5L domain scores from baseline through week 72. Significant improvements were observed across PROs related to physical function. In the exploratory subgroup analyses, participants in ATTAIN-1 with higher baseline BMI and those with baseline physical function limitations were more likely to have greater improvements. Conclusion Across the ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 trials, orforglipron treatment was associated with substantial body weight reduction and improvements in patient-reported HRQoL, with consistent enhancements in physical functioning and heterogeneous effects on psychosocial functioning. ATTAIN-1: NCT05869903; ATTAIN-2: NCT05872620

papers.title: PAKISTANI ESL UNDERGRADUATES' PERCEPTIONS ABOUT THE ROLE OF CHATGPT IN ACADEMIC WRITING
papers.authors: Faheemuddin Shaikh, Sarala Thulasi Palpanadan, Insaf Ali Siming, Ashwaque Ahamd Abbasi
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of AI tools and Natural Language Processing (NLP) chatbots, most prominently Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT), is increasing among Pakistani students. ESL undergraduates use ChatGPT to assist with their writing skills. On the contrary, they often receive no AI training. In this regard, this mixed-method study examined Pakistani ESL undergraduates' frequency and perceptions of using ChatGPT. The data were collected through a cross-sectional questionnaire with 14 closed-ended and 4 open-ended items from 109 participants enrolled in two public-sector rural universities in the province of Sindh, Pakistan. Quantitative findings indicated that participants most frequently used ChatGPT for academic writing skills (M = 3.36) and language errors (M = 3.09), followed by university writing assignments (M = 2.98), with AI training context scoring lowest (M = 2.73). Qualitative data, which were analysed through Braun and Clarke's (2006) thematic analysis, produced seven cross-question themes, revealing that students perceive ChatGPT as a useful and easy-to-use tool for specific writing functions, while a notable subset expressed caution against over-reliance on the tool. Critically, both datasets converged on a substantial gap in institutional guidance. The participants reported receiving no formal training in using AI tools for academic writing. Furthermore, when interpreted through the Technology Acceptance Model (Davis, 1989), these findings suggest that participants independently adopt AI for writing, underscoring the need for structured AI literacy training within academic writing curricula. This study contributes context-specific insight into AI-assisted writing practices in Pakistani higher education and offers practical implications for institutional policy.

papers.title: Circadian and Sleep-Wake Modulation of EEG Functional Connectivity Across Brain States and Its Associations With Cognition in Humans
papers.authors: Alpár S. Lázár, Zsolt I. Lázár, Nayantara Santhi, June Chi-Yan Lo, John A Groeger, Derk-Jan Dijk
papers.abstract: Sleep and circadian rhythms both influence human brain function, but their distinct contributions to large-scale network organization remain unclear. We quantified the effect of brain state (wake, NREM, REM), sleep-wake history, and circadian phase on functional connectivity using over 1,200 hours of artifact-free EEG recorded during a 10-day forced-desynchrony protocol. We derived principal components of functional connectivity and found that both sleep-wake history and circadian phase significantly modulated functional connectivity, with sleep-wake history exerting a broader influence. Complementary cosinor analyses further demonstrated circadian rhythmicity in several NREM and REM connectivity measures. Across sleep, global connectivity increased progressively during NREM sleep, particularly in the delta and sigma bands, but declined during REM sleep. During controlled resting wakefulness, increasing time awake was associated with higher global alpha-band connectivity, which was associated with poorer concurrent cognitive performance. Connectivity during NREM sleep was also associated with subsequent cognitive performance, with lower global theta and, to a lesser extent, higher sigma connectivity linked to better performance. REM connectivity was not associated with these cognitive measures. Together, these findings reveal opposing NREM and REM trajectories in large-scale EEG functional connectivity and show that these brain-state-specific network dynamics are shaped by both sleep-wake history and circadian phase and are associated with cognitive performance.

papers.title: Resting EEG as a Condition-Dependent Ageing Phenotype: Periodic and Aperiodic Trajectories, Reliability, and Five-Year Change
papers.authors: Yiran Du
papers.abstract: Resting-state electroencephalography is increasingly proposed as a scalable marker of healthy brain ageing, yet its interpretability depends on distinguishing stable individual characteristics from condition-dependent measurement effects. This secondary analysis of an open lifespan dataset examined periodic alpha activity, alpha-peak detectability, aperiodic spectral structure, short-term repeatability, and longitudinal change under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions before and after an extended cognitive battery. Eye state strongly organised both whether a posterior alpha peak could be detected and the values of periodic and aperiodic measures. Age-related trajectories were prominent for the aperiodic exponent and full-sample alpha activity, whereas evidence that age modified post-battery change was weak. Across follow-up, detectable alpha frequency and the aperiodic exponent showed mean decreases, while alpha power was comparatively stable. Level measures demonstrated moderate-to-high repeatability and rank-order stability, but post-battery and difference-in-differences change scores were considerably less reliable. The findings position resting EEG as a condition-dependent ageing phenotype rather than a unitary baseline. They further show that peak detection, recording context, attrition, and the reliability of change must be modelled explicitly when resting EEG is used for lifespan inference or normative applications.

papers.title: A demonstration of machine learning approaches and visualizations for HIV research: identifying key predictors of barriers to antiretroviral therapy
papers.authors: Dominic Chu, Tibor Schuster, Kim Engler, Serge Vicente, David Lessard, Jean-Pierre Routy, Nadine Kronfli, Joseph Cox, Alexandra de Pokomandy, Romain Palich, Karine Lacombe, Bertrand Lebouché
papers.abstract: Although machine learning is increasingly used in health research, its adoption in HIV research remains limited, particularly for clarifying subpopulations of at-risk individuals facing antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence barriers. This study demonstrates the methodological use of machine learning approaches to examine sociodemographic patterns as predictors of barriers to ART adherence. In a cross-sectional study with self-administered online or in-person surveys among people living with HIV in Montreal, Canada, we collected data on sociodemographic variables (age, immigration status, education level, gender, and sexual orientation) and six domains of barriers to ART adherence. We used hierarchical clustering to identify sociodemographic patterns of ART adherence barriers, then applied ensemble learning (random forests, quantile regression forests, and Bayesian Additive Regression Trees) to predict barrier intensity. Model outputs were evaluated with visualizations and pseudo-examples serving as reference profiles to aid interpretation. Of 221 participants, most reported low barrier intensity. Hierarchical clustering revealed distinct patterns among subpopulations affected by ART adherence barriers, with younger people with HIV facing greater barriers than older participants. Ensemble models demonstrated marginal predictive performance, with variable importance scores <5%, poor out-of-bag prediction fit (R 2 < 0.15), and visual inspection of predicted-versus-observed plots, suggesting that sociodemographics alone are insufficient to reliably predict barrier intensity. This study provides a reference for applying machine learning, highlighting both the utility and challenges of these methods. Although the available feature space constrained the predictive performance of sociodemographic factors, the work highlights the value of machine learning for uncovering complex patterns in HIV data.

papers.title: Repurposing the Industrial Digital Twin: A Framework and Case Study in Digital Twin Modification for an Interactive Educational Application
papers.authors: Nicholas Dewberry, Issa W. AlHmoud, Kevin Benton, Shuva Chowdhury, Derick Suarez, Jagannathan Sankar, Balakrishna Gokaraju
papers.abstract: The paradigm of Industry 4.0 is driven by the integration of advanced technologies such as Digital Twins (DTs), which provide a high-fidelity virtual model of physical systems. While these DTs excel at process optimization and predictive maintenance, they often remain inaccessible to non-experts, creating a barrier to workforce development. This paper addresses this gap by presenting a novel, gamified educational framework designed to repurpose an existing industrial DT for accessible, hands-on training. We experiment with a basic soft-body physics model that prioritizes intuitive, real-time feedback on material deformation over precise engineering accuracy, making a simplified simulation for educational contexts. Furthermore, we demonstrate the process of augmenting a pre-existing DT with layered pedagogical elements. These include the integration of a Large Language Model (LLM) to act as a chatbot, a flexible and secure server to serve as the networking backend, and the implementation of a hand-scoring system to provide learners with immediate, quantitative feedback on their procedural technique within immersive environments. The result is a cross-platform educational tool that transforms a complex industrial system into an engaging learning experience, thereby lowering the barrier to entry for users seeking to engage with advanced manufacturing technologies.

papers.title: Immersive XR-Based Aseptic Transfer Training for Manufacturing Education: A Qualitative Study Using Apple Vision Pro at Purdue University
papers.authors: Sai Ashish Kumar Karanam, Nathan W. Hartman, Aathman Tharmasanthiran, Nathaniel Milton, Alina A Alexeenko
papers.abstract: Manufacturing organizations increasingly explore extended-reality (XR) technologies to support workforce training while reducing safety risks and material dependency. Aseptic transfer requires precise sequencing, flame sterilization control, and contamination-aware handling skills that remain difficult to rehearse without physical cleanrooms and instructor oversight. The study presents a pilot immersive XR aseptic-transfer training module developed in Unity for Apple Vision Pro and supported by a dialog-based BioTrain GPT assistant grounded in curated pharmaceutical manufacturing documents. Three graduate-level learners with prior aseptic experience completed the module and participated in semi-structured interviews. Qualitative analysis using descriptive coding, interpretive coding, and thematic synthesis identified five experiential themes: realism supports procedural focus, risk-free repetition reinforces confidence, iterative trials strengthen cognitive sequencing, system limitations affect immersion, and dialog-based clarification aids task understanding. Participants reported enhanced procedural awareness and reduced performance pressure during rehearsal, while noting hand-tracking constraints. Findings represent feasibility and user-experience evidence rather than learning-transfer validation. Results inform design considerations for XR-based aseptic training and outline integration pathways for AI-assisted guidance in manufacturing education environments.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Fatigue Performance Prediction in Metal Additive Manufacturing: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Saifur Rahman Tushar, Michael Khonsari, Mahathir Mohammad Bappy
papers.abstract: Metal additive manufacturing (AM) has revolutionized the design and production landscape for critical sectors, including aerospace, automotive, and energy. It enables the production of lightweight, topology-optimized, and functionally graded components that are impractical to produce through conventional manufacturing methods. However, the widespread adoption of AM parts in load-bearing applications remains constrained by their limited and variable fatigue performance, strongly influenced by process-induced defects (e.g., porosity, lack of fusion), microstructural anisotropy, surface conditions, and post-processing treatments. In recent years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as powerful tools for modeling complex process–structure–property–performance relationships and predicting fatigue life, strength, and crack growth in metal AM systems. This study presents a comprehensive PRISMA-guided systematic review of peer-reviewed publications that apply AI and ML for fatigue prediction in metallic AM components. The review synthesizes modeling approaches ranging from conventional “shallow” learners, such as support vector machines (SVM), random forests (RF), and XGBoost, to advanced deep learning frameworks, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). We categorize existing studies based on their input data modalities, including defect-sensitive models that utilize XCT or SEM data, microstructure-aware models that leverage crystallographic features, and hybrid surrogates that integrate process, structure, and property information. Furthermore, we highlight strategies to address data scarcity, including transfer learning, synthetic data augmentation, and cross-validation. Key research gaps are identified in the areas of dataset standardization, physics integration, uncertainty quantification, and cross-material generalization. Finally, the review outlines emerging directions for developing physically grounded, interpretable, and generalizable AI frameworks capable of reliable fatigue performance prediction across diverse AM materials and platforms.

papers.title: A Multimodal Manufacturing Safety Chatbot: Knowledge Base Design, Benchmark Development, and Evaluation of Multiple RAG Approaches
papers.authors: Ryan R. Singh, Austin Hamilton, Amanda White, Michael Wise, Ibrahim Yousif, Arthur Carvalho, Zhe Shan, Reza Abrisham Baf, Mohammad Mayyas, Lora Anne Cavuoto, Fadel M. Megahed
papers.abstract: Ensuring worker safety remains a critical challenge in modern manufacturing environments. Industry 5.0 reorients the prevailing manufacturing paradigm toward more human-centric operations. Using a design science research methodology, we identify three essential requirements for next-generation safety training systems: high accuracy, low latency, and low cost. We introduce a multimodal chatbot powered by large language models that meets these design requirements. The chatbot uses retrieval-augmented generation to ground its responses in curated regulatory and technical documentation. To evaluate our solution, we developed a domain-specific benchmark of expert-validated question and answer pairs for three representative machines: a Bridgeport manual mill, a Haas TL-1 CNC lathe, and a Universal Robots UR5e collaborative robot. We tested 24 RAG configurations using a full-factorial design and assessed them with automated evaluations of correctness, latency, and cost. Our top 2 configurations were then evaluated by ten industry experts and academic researchers. Our results show that retrieval strategy and model configuration have a significant impact on performance. The top configuration, selected for chatbot deployment, achieved an accuracy of 86.66%, an average cost of $0.005 per query, and an average end-to-end latency of 10.04 seconds. This latency is practical for delivering a complete safety instruction and is measured from query submission to full instruction delivery rather than generation onset. Overall, our work provides three contributions: an open-source, domain-grounded safety training chatbot; a validated benchmark for evaluating AI-assisted safety instruction; and a systematic methodology for designing and assessing AI-enabled instructional and immersive safety training systems for Industry 5.0 environments.

papers.title: Deployment of a Multilingual, Embodied, Holographic AI Concierge in Ambulatory Care: Early Implementation Lessons From ARIA
papers.authors: Ellen C. Meltzer, Jared T. Staal, Alyssa B. Chapital, Pete J. Pallagi, Katelyn M. Cheetham, Haley Wang, Qiuyu Jin, Rafael Fonseca, Aman Anand, Mark R. Stemler, Chris S. Jaeckel, Danielle M. Stricker, Jacob M. Dison, Cherish D. Caputo, Tharana Maran, Beverly Hansen, Praneetha Elugunti, Biju T. Samkutty, Anjali Bhagra
papers.abstract: Healthcare environments can be difficult to navigate, particularly for individuals with limited language proficiency, hearing impairment, low digital literacy, or unfamiliarity with the facility. Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) systems may support accessibility and navigation, although descriptions of real-world implementation in healthcare settings remain limited. As a descriptive, single-site quality-improvement pilot, this report characterizes the experience of implementing a conversational AI agent in the lobby of a large, outpatient, academic practice. The Artificial Intelligence Responsive Interactive Agent (ARIA) is a multilingual, three-dimensional, holographic conversational AI concierge developed to provide real-time assistance with navigation, digital onboarding, and information regarding amenities and services. ARIA leverages natural language processing and large language model technology to provide voice-enabled interactions in English, Spanish, Mandarin, and Arabic, with real-time closed captioning. The system can also generate quick response (QR) codes that push information directly to users' mobile devices. Piloted in a large ambulatory lobby from October 21, 2025, to February 2, 2026, ARIA recorded 1,429 device-activation sessions. Of these, 689 sessions (48%) contained analyzable user interaction data. Wayfinding and general information requests were the most common use cases. Deployment surfaced operational challenges, including audio capture, network reliability, interaction timing, workflow integration, QR transfer, and content governance. As the use of AI in clinical settings expands, there may be a role for an embodied agent serving as a digital concierge if these barriers can be addressed. Future evaluations should prospectively define implementation outcomes, use systematic utilization denominators, and assess user experience and operational impact with validated measures.

papers.title: Integrating Remote Presence Virtual Care into Medical Education in Canada
papers.authors: Jarol Boan, Amal Shahzad Khan, Fazle Rafi, Puneet Kapur, Scott Adams, Ivar M. Mendez
papers.abstract: Access to healthcare in Canada remains limited for rural and remote communities, despite rapid technological advancements in virtual care. Medical education has not consistently prepared learners to deliver comprehensive virtual care that extends beyond traditional telemedicine. We describe the design and implementation of a two-week course in remote presence virtual care for fourth-year medical students delivered through the Virtual Health Hub, a center of excellence dedicated to improving access to care in underserved and remote communities using advanced virtual care technologies. The curriculum is grounded in an expanded model of virtual care that integrates remote presence robotics, artificial intelligence, peripheral diagnostic technologies, and community-engaged models of care. It was developed using Kern's six-step approach, informed by a targeted needs assessment addressing gaps in virtual care training and health system constraints. Educational strategies include didactic teaching, simulation-based learning, case-based discussions, supervised virtual clinical encounters, and summative assessment through an objective structured clinical examination. By reframing how virtual care is understood and taught, this work aims to equip future physicians with the clinical skills required to deliver equitable care in technologically enabled healthcare systems. We suggest that incorporating a course in comprehensive remote presence virtual care can function as a building block for a competency-based curriculum in medical training and prepare students for the use of these technologies to deliver health care in the future.

papers.title: Exploring learners’ well-being in AI-supported English learning from a self-determination theory perspective
papers.authors: Jiayong Liu, Ting Wang
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping English learning, yet limited attention has been paid to how AI-supported learning environments are associated with learners’ well-being. Drawing on self-determination theory, this study examined the relationships among basic psychological needs, flow, self-efficacy, peace of mind, and well-being. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 694 undergraduate students from universities in China who had used AI-enabled tools for English learning. Structural equation modelling (SEM) tested the hypothesized direct and mediating relationships, while artificial neural network (ANN) analysis identified the relative predictive importance of the antecedents of well-being. The SEM results showed that basic psychological needs were positively associated with well-being, flow, self-efficacy, and peace of mind. Flow, self-efficacy, and peace of mind were also positively associated with well-being and mediated the association between basic psychological needs and well-being. The ANN results indicated that self-efficacy was the most important predictor, followed by peace of mind, flow, and basic psychological needs. These findings suggest that learners’ well-being is shaped by motivational, experiential, cognitive, and affective mechanisms in AI-supported English learning.

papers.title: Diffusion bridge networks simulate clinical-grade PET from MRI for dementia diagnostics: a retrospective cohort study
papers.authors: Yitong Li, Buchert Ralph, Benita Schmitz‐Koep, Timo Grimmer, Björn Ommer, Dennis Martin Hedderich, Yakushev Igor, Christian Wachinger
papers.abstract: Background Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET (FDG-PET) outperforms structural MRI in early and differential dementia diagnostics but is challenged by scanner availability, high cost, and radiation exposure. We aimed to develop and clinically validate a generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework that simulates clinical-grade FDG-PET from routine MRI and auxiliary patient information to broaden access to metabolic imaging for dementia diagnostics. Methods In this retrospective cohort diagnostic accuracy study, we developed SiM2P, a conditional three dimensional diffusion bridge model with diffusion Transformers to simulate FDG-PET from T1-weighted MRI and 13 auxiliary clinical variables (age, sex, education, mini-mental state examination, Alzheimer's disease assessment scale–cognitive subscale 13, apolipoprotein E ε4 status, and seven MRI-derived segmentation volumes). Eligible participants had baseline paired T1-weighted MRI and FDG-PET scans with accompanying clinical records, each participant contributed one baseline scan, and no longitudinal follow-up scans were included. No further exclusion criteria were applied. The framework was trained and evaluated using data from three independent cohorts: the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), the Japanese ADNI (J-ADNI), and an in-house Technical University of Munich University Hospital cohort. No age limit was imposed on participants and their cognitive continuum spanned from cognitively normal to mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and frontotemporal lobar degeneration. The primary endpoint was diagnostic accuracy in a masked clinical reader study in which two neuroradiologists independently interpreted MRI scans and two nuclear medicine physicians independently interpreted both simulated and real FDG-PET scans from a held-out in-house test set of individuals (who were cognitively normal or had Alzheimer's disease or behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia) for dementia diagnosis and three-class differential diagnosis. Secondary outcomes included image quality metrics against four competing methods and automated three-class differential diagnosis. Findings We analysed paired MRI and FDG-PET scans from 1889 participants (n=1247 for ADNI, n=319 for J-ADNI, and n=323 for in-house dataset). The participants were aged 41–91 years. The scans were acquired between Sept 22, 2005, and Oct 14, 2019 (ADNI); Sept 3, 2008, and May 17, 2012, (J-ADNI); and May 19, 2011, and Dec 27, 2018 (Technical University of Munich University hospital data). In the masked clinical reader study including a held-out in-house test set of 62 individuals (comprising 22 cognitively normal individuals, 19 with Alzheimer's disease, and 21 with behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia), simulated PET yielded an accuracy of 93% (95% CI 86·8–96·1) for dementia detection versus 83% for MRI (75·5–88·7; p=0·0076) and 85% (77.3–90·0) versus 75% (66·7–81·8) for three-class differential diagnosis of participants who were cognitively normal, had Alzheimer's disease, and had behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (p=0·044). Inter-rater reliability was substantially higher for simulated PET (Cohen's κ =0·899) than for MRI ( κ =0·644). Simulated PET also improved diagnostic confidence. A crossreading analysis further confirmed that the observed gain was attributed to the sensitive disease-relevant information provided by the simulated PET rather than reader-specific expertise. Interpretation AI-simulated PET generated from routine MRI can improve the diagnostic accuracy and inter-rater reliability of structural MRI for dementia detection and differential diagnosis. The data-efficient Local-Adapt workflow provides a practical pathway for deployment at clinical centres without PET infrastructure, thus potentially widening equitable access to metabolic PET diagnostics for dementia care. Funding German Research Foundation (DFG), Munich Center for Machine Learning, and the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) Konrad Zuse Schools of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence.

papers.title: Low energy diet plus supervised exercise vs. usual care alone in people with early-onset type 2 diabetes (RESET for Remission): a randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint efficacy trial
papers.authors: Kaberi Dasgupta, Normand G. Boulé, Joseph J. Henson, Emma L. Redman, Deborah Chan, Matthew McCarthy, Debora Rosa, Franciskos Arsenyadis, Stéphanie Chevalier, Jordan Rees, Jihoon Lim, Alex V. Rowlands, Michelle Hadjiconstantinou, Deborah Da Costa, Edward W. Gregg, Alice Cowley, Matthias G. Friedrich, Carla M. Prado, Mark H. Sherman, Melanie Jane Davies, Elham Rahme, Kamlesh K. Khunti, Roseanne O. Yeung, Gerry Patrick McCann, Richard B. Thompson, Thomas E. Yates, Kim Arrey, Ryan Kelsey, Nisha Gupta, Carolyn Currie, Henry Tung, Nayna Naliyapara, Christina Weiss, Harvinder Singh, Tricia Peters, Mikila Walters, Salma Rakani, Sam Cook, Alison Doucet, Martha Thomas, Emilie Chan-Thim, Chris Brough, Suneet Atwal, Robert Fraser, Roy Eappen, Ehtasham Ahmad, Mark Roper, Elizabeth Ward, Julia Champagne, Isabel Fortier, Renata Sava, Annick Gauthier, Sola Mansour, Rachel M. Bond, Michael A. Tsoukas, Norman Sabin, Vincent Larouche, Jill Pancer, Oriana Hoi Yun Yu, Mark Karanofsky, Jasvir Kaur, Patricia Kearns, Mark Marcinkiewicz, Josette Spencer, Suzanne N. Morin, Melissa‐Rosina Pasqua
papers.abstract: Background Low energy diets (LED) can induce type 2 diabetes remission but have not been studied in combination with structured supervised exercise. We aimed to determine if a combined intervention could induce remission in early-onset type 2 diabetes (EOT2D ≤ 45 years of age), a population with high lifetime risk of complications. Methods Across 3 centres in England and Canada, we conducted a randomised, open-label, blinded endpoint efficacy trial among adults 18–45 years of age with EOT2D and obesity, not on insulin therapy. The groups were usual care alone vs. an intervention combining 800–900 kcal/day LED, twice-weekly supervised (aerobic, resistance) and once-weekly independent exercise (weeks 1–12), followed by a weight-maintenance diet with independent exercise (weeks 13–24). An independent statistician generated web-based randomisation sequences (1:1, country- and sex-stratified, variable block size). The primary outcome was remission at 24 weeks (Hb A1c < 6.5% [48 mmol/mol], without glucose-lowering medication ≥12 weeks). The primary efficacy and harms analysis was in all randomised individuals, assuming no remission when data were unavailable. Secondary endpoints included cardiorespiratory fitness, body composition, and cardiac structure. The trial is registered at ISRCTN (15487120) and is now closed. Findings We randomised 96 participants (mean age 38 years, BMI 35.2 kg/m 2 ) between September 24, 2021 and June 6, 2025 (intervention group: 24 female, 26 male with 18 European, 17 South Asian, 15 Other ethnicity; control group: 21 female, 25 male with 19 European, 10 South Asian, 17 Other ethnicity). In total, 86 (90%) attended final assessments. Remission at 24 weeks occurred in 27/50 (54%) of intervention participants vs. 2/46 (4%) control participants (50% difference, 95% CI 33%–64%; adjOR 21.6, 95% CI 6.2 to 114.5), without serious adverse events. Most intervention group participants experienced at least one adverse event (43/50 vs. 6/46), mainly early LED effects (e.g., constipation, headache, dizziness, fatigue) that resolved. Interpretation High remission rates signal feasibility and efficacy of a combined LED and intensive exercise intervention in EOT2D, justifying examination of synergistic benefits beyond remission. Funding United Kingdom Medical Research Council, Canadian Institutes of Health Research, John R. McConnell Foundation.

papers.title: Twelve-Month Results of Cyanoacrylate Closure in Patients with Venous Leg Ulceration
papers.authors: Kathleen D. Gibson, Manjit Gohel, Ahmed Kayssi, Joseph E. Sabat, Nicolas Neaume, Leigh Ann O’Banion, Paul J. Gagne, Misaki M. Kiguchi, Neil M. Khilnani, Raghu Kolluri, Nicholas Salkowski, Daniel J. Denmark, Alun Huw Davies
papers.journal: Journal of Vascular Surgery Venous and Lymphatic Disorders
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Venous leg ulceration (VLU) is a major cause of patient distress and healthcare burden. Previous studies have highlighted the importance of early endovenous ablation of superficial venous reflux to expedite healing and prevent recurrence, but the optimal venous ablation modality is unclear. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of cyanoacrylate closure in patients with VLU. DESIGN: A global, prospective, single-arm observational study was conducted in 17 centers across the United States and Europe. A total of 125 participants with VLU were included and treated with the VenaSeal closure system, in addition to standard wound therapy, including multilayered compression. Adjuvant treatments to varicosities, perforators or the sub-ulcer plexus were left to the discretion of treating clinicians. The primary outcome was VLU healing through 12 months. Secondary outcomes included time to ulcer recurrence, anatomic vein closure, target limb adverse events, and changes in quality-of-life measures. RESULTS: One hundred twenty-five participants with VLU and saphenous vein reflux were enrolled. The mean (± standard deviation) age was 67.9 ± 14.76 years, with 38.4% females and an overall mean BMI of 32.4± 9.35. Concomitant foam sclerotherapy treatments were performed in 19.7% (31/157) of target veins. At 12 months, ulcer healing was 81.3% and ulcer recurrence was 17.0%. The median time to ulcer healing was 92 days (95% CI 74, 137). Anatomic vein closure was successful in 82.7% of all target veins. CEC-adjudicated AE and SAEs included: 2 granulomas, 1 hypersensitivity reaction, and 4 cases of phlebitis of the treated limb. Healthcare services utilized outside of the index procedure yielded 0.12 adjunctive therapies per vein-year. Venous-specific and generic QoL scores showed sustained improvement compared to baseline scores. CONCLUSION: VenaSeal effectively eliminated saphenous reflux in patients with VLU. The ulcer healing rate was high, and the recurrence rate was low. Complication rates were also low and QoL improved.

papers.title: Lactylation-associated CXCL12-mediated intercellular communication in rheumatic heart disease valves
papers.authors: Junyu Zhai, Zheng Zuo, Tao Yan, Fangyu Liu, Jiaxing Liu, Kai Zhu, Hao Lai, Chunsheng Wang, Jun Li
papers.abstract: Background Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is characterized by persistent valvular inflammation and fibrosis. Lactate-driven lysine lactylation may couple metabolic stress to inflammatory transcription, but its relationship with CXCL12-mediated immune recruitment in RHD valves remains unclear. Methods Paired aortic and mitral valve single-cell RNA-sequencing data from three patients with RHD were analyzed, yielding 47,237 quality-controlled cells. CXCL12-producing cell populations were identified, and lactylation-related transcriptional states and inflammatory pathways were assessed in CXCL12-high structural cells using complementary scoring and pseudobulk approaches. CellChat was used to infer CXCL12-mediated intercellular communication, with GSE153555 used for external validation. Human valve interstitial cells (VICs) were treated with lactate, the p300 inhibitor A-485, or the NF-κB inhibitor BAY 11-7082. CXCL12/CXCR4-dependent monocyte chemotaxis was evaluated using THP-1 cells, AMD3100, and a CXCL12-neutralizing antibody. Results VICs and myofibroblasts were the principal CXCL12-producing cells. Within CXCL12-high structural cells, a higher lactylation-related transcriptional state was associated with enhanced NF-κB and TNF signaling and increased IL6, BIRC3, REL, and TNFAIP3 expression. CellChat supported CXCL12-CXCR4 communication from structural cells to myeloid and lymphoid cells, while external validation confirmed increased CXCL12, IL6, and TNFAIP3 expression in diseased valves. In VICs, lactate increased Pan-Kla, H3K9la, H3K14la, and CXCL12 expression and secretion. A-485 attenuated lactylation-associated CXCL12 induction, whereas BAY 11-7082 suppressed NF-κB activation and CXCL12 expression. Lactate-conditioned medium enhanced THP-1 migration and inflammatory gene expression, which were reduced by pathway inhibition or CXCL12/CXCR4 blockade. Conclusion These findings link lactylation-associated metabolic signaling in RHD valve structural cells to NF-κB-dependent CXCL12 production and CXCL12-CXCR4-mediated monocyte recruitment, providing a mechanistic framework for stromal–immune communication in RHD.

papers.title: A novel risk scoring system to predict 30-day hospital readmission after pancreaticoduodenectomy utilizing a large national database
papers.authors: Jorge Urbina, Zhuo Li, Launia White, Mary P. Tice, John Andrew Stauffer, Katherine E. Poruk
papers.abstract: Background Pancreaticoduodenectomy remains a complex operation with significant morbidity and mortality. Readmission remains an issue, contributing to health care costs, decreased quality of life and delay in additional therapies. Identification of actionable predictors may improve discharge planning and reduce preventable readmissions. We aim to develop and validate a clinically applicable risk score for 30-day readmission using national NSQIP data. Methods The NSQIP Targeted Pancreatectomy Participant Use Data File (2014–2023) was queried for adults undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy. Patients were divided into training (n=34,556) and validation (n=8,144) cohorts. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were developed using preoperative variables alone and a combined perioperative model incorporating postoperative complications. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC). Predictors from the final multivariable model were converted into an integer-based risk score. Results Among 34,556 patients, 6,006 (17.4%) experienced 30-day readmission. The median hospital length of stay for the overall cohort was 8 days. In the preoperative model, BMI ≥25, chronic obstructive lung disease (COPD), congestive heart failure (CHF), hypertension, bleeding disorders, absence of preoperative biliary stenting, absence of recent chemotherapy, and node-negative status were independently associated with readmission (all p<0.05); discrimination was limited (AUC 0.56). In the combined perioperative model, CHF lost significance, while postoperative complications emerged as dominant predictors; model performance improved substantially (AUC 0.68; validation AUC 0.67). Independent predictors included pancreatic fistula (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.27–1.48), delayed gastric emptying (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.58–1.83), and percutaneous drainage (OR 2.89, 95% CI 2.68–3.12). Using an optimal cutoff of 8.5 points, the risk score demonstrated 59% sensitivity and 72% specificity (p<0.001). Conclusions Thirty-day readmission following pancreaticoduodenectomy is driven predominantly by postoperative complications rather than baseline comorbidities. This validated risk score uses available perioperative variables to identify high-risk patients and may support risk-stratified discharge planning and early outpatient surveillance.

papers.title: Confident but absent: AI use, self-efficacy for independent learning, and student absenteeism in higher education
papers.authors: FRANCO Joana, Mijail Naranjo-Zolotov, Tiago de Oliveira
papers.journal: International Journal of Information Management Data Insights
papers.abstract: Rising student absenteeism remains a persistent challenge in higher education, potentially exacerbated by the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools. Drawing on digital displacement theory, this study examines whether general AI use is associated with students’ self-efficacy for independent learning and absenteeism. Survey data from 291 Portuguese university students were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling, explaining 38.7% of the variance in absenteeism and 34.4% in self-efficacy. Internal locus of control, peer influence, time management, and AI use emerged as significant predictors. General AI use was positively associated with both self-efficacy and absenteeism, suggesting that AI may strengthen independent learning confidence while coinciding with reduced face-to-face engagement. Multigroup analysis provided exploratory evidence of gender differences, with the AI use–self-efficacy relationship stronger among males at the 5% level, while other gender differences appeared only at a more lenient 10% threshold.

papers.title: From awareness to action: A circle of trust approach to climate knowledge Co-creation
papers.authors: Dennis Pepple, Nadeesha Muthuthantridge, Aliyu Sani Sambo, Daminabo Pokubo, Sujeewa HERATH, Caroline Upton
papers.abstract: Climate change is increasingly recognised as a crisis not only of knowledge, but also of legitimacy and action. Although climate awareness is widespread, existing information-led and participatory approaches provide limited explanation of how climate knowledge becomes credible, culturally meaningful and practically actionable within marginalised communities. Addressing this gap, this study examines Circles of Trust (COT), a community-embedded approach organised through pre-existing trusted social relationships and investigates how COTs facilitate climate knowledge co-creation and the movement from awareness towards feasible possibilities for action within Black, Asian and minority ethnic (BAME) communities in the United Kingdom. Using a qualitative, interpretive research design, data were generated through five peer-led focus groups involving 30 participants embedded within faith, workplace and community networks. Data were analysed through an iterative open-coding and constant-comparative process informed by Corbin and Strauss (2008), enabling themes to emerge from participants’ accounts of climate knowledge, trust, learning and action. The findings reveal that the awareness–action gap reflects not simply insufficient climate knowledge but an interaction between financial pressures, linguistic and informational barriers, socio-cultural norms and mistrust of external institutions. More distinctively, COTs enabled climate knowledge to be negotiated through trusted peers, culturally familiar settings and everyday concerns, particularly cost and health, while peer modelling strengthened participants’ confidence in feasible low-cost actions. The study conceptualises COTs as a trust-embedded relational social-learning infrastructure for climate knowledge co-creation, rather than simply another participatory consultation mechanism. Its distinctive contribution lies in showing how this relational infrastructure embeds knowledge co-creation within existing relations of trust, enabling community members to act as knowledge holders who interpret, validate and contextualise climate knowledge into locally meaningful possibilities for action. The findings extend social learning and knowledge co-creation scholarship by showing how trust, cultural grounding and community epistemic authority condition the translation of climate awareness into perceived possibilities for action.
keywords: Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic communities

papers.title: Depressive symptoms are associated with poor asthma control in adults and adolescents
papers.authors: Brittany Duchene, Derek Devine, Olivia Johnson Garrow, Katherine E. Menson, Michelle N. Eakin, Anne E. Dixon
papers.journal: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology Global
papers.abstract: Background Clinically significant depressive symptoms are common among those with asthma, yet their impact on asthma outcomes is not well defined. Objective Evaluate the association between depressive symptoms and asthma outcomes. Methods In this pooled cross-sectional analysis of 741 participants aged ≥15 years from three multicenter studies, we examined whether depressive symptoms (through use of validated surveys) were associated with asthma control, symptoms, quality of life, lung function, and exacerbations. Associations between clinically significant depressive symptoms and asthma-related outcomes were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) and corrected for included age, sex, race, body mass index (BMI), education level, and parent study to account for potential confounding and between-study differences. Results Clinically significant depressive symptoms were present in a substantial proportion of participants (n=483/65.2%) and were associated with worse asthma control, with higher odds of poorly controlled asthma (Odds Ratio 1.98; 95% CI 1.45–2.71; p <0.001). 68.1% (n=329) of participants with depressive symptoms had poorly controlled asthma compared with 50.2% (n=130) without depressive symptoms. Symptom burden was greater among those with depressive symptoms, (0.727 vs 0.768; p <0.001). Asthma-specific quality of life scores were lower among those with depressive symptoms (4.85 vs 5.35; p <0.001). Health-related quality of life was also lower among those with depressive symptoms (63.62 vs 73.34; p <0.001). Depressive symptoms were not associated with spirometric measures or exacerbation frequency. Conclusions Clinically significant depressive symptoms in adults with uncontrolled asthma are associated with worse perceived disease burden and quality of life but not with objective measures of lung function or exacerbation risk.

papers.title: Video-Based Deception Detection and Financial Fraud
papers.authors: Binglei Duan, Danqi Hu, Hai Lu
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Based on a comprehensive visual deception score constructed from China’s mandatorily disclosed IPO roadshow videos using computer vision and machine learning, we find that visual cues embedded in these videos predict IPO financial fraud. The predictive power is incremental to financial, textual, and audio indicators. Further analyses show that these cues are well grounded in psychology research and focusing on the psychology-based deception-cue-area features improves fraud predicting performance. Furthermore, decomposing each video into five topics, we find that only the deception score of the topic on financial performance is positively associated with financial fraud. We further show that insiders of firms with higher visual deception scores are more likely to sell shares shortly after lock-up periods expire, and these firms experience significantly lower subsequent stock returns. Our study demonstrates the feasibility and potential value of using video information for fraud detection in accounting and finance.

papers.title: AI Narratives and Factual Response Gaps: Disclosure Choices and Market Responses in Investor-Firm Q&A
papers.authors: 辛世博, Yuechen Wang, Bowen Liang
papers.abstract: : We develop a demand-conditioned measure of disclosure quality for corporate AI narratives. Using public investor-firm Q&A records from China's exchange interactive platforms during 2018-2025, we define the AI Factual Response Gap as the 0-1 share of investor-asked AI fact dimensions that receive no matching factual response. Firms provide far fewer matching answers for commercially sensitive dimensions, including customers/orders, revenues/earnings, and project progress/timelines, than for products/models and application scenarios. Patent-based observable AI technological capability is associated with a smaller gap, mainly in product and technology-asset dimensions. Baseline market tests show no immediate response but a negative abnormal-return association over trading days 2 to 20. This association remains after controls for title-identified negative announcements, yet becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero with firm-year fixed effects, comprehensive inquiry-selection controls, cross-fitted nonlinear adjustment, investor fixed effects, and non-overlapping event-window restrictions. The paper's main contribution is a transparent, auditable measure of AI-narrative credibility and evidence on its disclosure-side determinants. The market evidence remains conditional and exploratory; it does not identify a capital-market learning mechanism.

papers.title: PeFG-MARA: Personalized feedback generation via multi-agent retrieval-augmented large language models
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Wu, Shuo Li, Shuang Liu, Zixuan Guo
papers.abstract: Generating personalized feedback requires identifying response-specific issues while grounding advice in reliable instructional evidence. We present PeFG-MARA, a modular workflow with three role-specific 7B LLM agents (Planner, Generator, and Critic) and a non-LLM Retrieval Module. The Planner turns a student’s response into a structured feedback plan and optional retrieval query; the retriever supplies instructional evidence; the Generator drafts a comment; and the Critic approves or requests revision. The agents share a base model and use separately trained LoRA adapters. We evaluate the system on four educational-feedback datasets covering science short answers, English writing, and mathematical problem solving, against neural, single-agent RAG, and prompted LLM baselines. On SAF, PeFG-MARA reaches BLEU/ROUGE-L/BERTScore scores of 32.8/37.4/0.921 versus 32.2/36.7/0.918 for GPT-4o Prompted. On the 20-essay EssayF test set, it yields the highest descriptive point estimates for BERTScore, coverage, specificity, and factual consistency; the larger LEAF test provides complementary writing-feedback evidence. Same-data controls and ablations indicate contributions from retrieval and coordinated planning and critique, while additional supervision improves performance further. The results suggest that an explicit feedback plan can help align evidence with a student’s particular errors. The inspectable plan could support instructor review of draft feedback, subject to retrieval quality, latency, and further classroom evaluation.

papers.title: KG-LLM: Knowledge graph-guided LLM augmentation for fine-grained subtitle similarity
papers.authors: Ze Li, Jing Zhang, Yufei Feng, Li Zhuo
papers.abstract: Measuring semantic similarity between short-video subtitles is critical for content retrieval, deduplication, and originality protection. However, existing semantic matching methods miss covert homogenization patterns, while unconstrained LLM-based augmentation risks unintended semantic drift and unstable similarity ordering when subtitles heavily rewrite surface expressions but partially retain deep semantic structures. To address this, we propose KG-LLM, a knowledge graph-guided LLM semantic augmentation framework for fine-grained subtitle similarity measurement. KG-LLM first constructs a short-video domain knowledge graph from extracted entities and semantic relations, and then uses this graph to guide multi-level semantic augmentation, generating variants with controllable semantic levels and providing structured semantic-level supervision for ranking learning. In addition, a prior-guided ranking contrastive learning strategy maps discrete semantic-level differences into a semantic-level prior matrix and fuses it with teacher-derived similarity scores, enabling the student encoder to capture fine-grained semantic distinctions. Experiments are conducted on BJUT-HCD_S, a short-video subtitle similarity dataset containing 5000 Chinese subtitle pairs, as well as Chinese STS-B and LCQMC. KG-LLM achieves Spearman correlations of 85.92%, 83.15%, and 82.38% on the three datasets, respectively, and improves Pearson correlation on BJUT-HCD_S by 1.06% over the strongest protocol-matched trainable baseline. Retrieval evaluation on BJUT-HCD_S further yields 87.95% Recall@1, 98.36% Recall@3, and 94.74% nDCG@5, demonstrating the effectiveness of KG-LLM for fine-grained subtitle similarity measurement and homogenized subtitle retrieval.

papers.title: Symbolic Representations for Human Activity Recognition: From Raw Signals to Lightweight Sensor-Language Models
papers.authors: Javier Medina-Quero, Jose Manuel Soto-Hidalgo, Oresti Baños-Legrán, Aurora Polo-Rodríguez
papers.abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) commonly relies on raw-signal temporal modelling, often achieving strong performance at the expense of interpretability, efficiency, and semantic transparency. This work proposes a symbolic HAR framework in which statistical descriptors and fuzzy logic-based abstractions are used to represent sensor behaviour in a more interpretable and semantically meaningful form. These symbolic representations are exploited both as discriminative features for HAR models and as sensor/class signatures that support explanation generation in lightweight language models. Building on this representation, we introduce Symbolic Sensor TinyLLaMA , a HAR-oriented lightweight sensor-language framework designed for comparatively resource-efficient deployment. Rather than simply replacing a larger sensor-language model with a smaller one, the proposed approach reformulates sensor-language modelling around HAR-specific symbolic signatures, teacher-guided explanation generation, and dual implicit-explicit evaluation. In particular, tree-based teacher models, such as XGBoost, are used to guide the association between activity classes and discriminative symbolic features through a distillation-like strategy. The framework is evaluated on heterogeneous wearable and ambient-sensing datasets, including IMU-based and multi-occupancy smart-home environments. Experimental results compare raw-signal and symbolic representations across classical machine learning methods, deep learning architectures, boosted tree-based models, and sensor-aligned lightweight language models. The results show that symbolic representations can achieve competitive HAR performance while improving interpretability and enabling explicit textual explanations of sensor-based activity predictions.

papers.title: An Explainable Weighted Ensemble Deep Learning Framework for Subject-Independent ADHD Detection Using EEG Signals
papers.authors: Nusrat Mahjabin, Md.Sanjid Hossain, Shahrin Kabir Tashin, Khandaker Mohammad Mohi Uddin
papers.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is one of the most prevalent neurodevelopmental disorders and diagnosis is still largely based on behavioral evaluations which can be subjective and time consuming. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are a promising objective source of information for the detection of ADHD, as they reflect the underlying neural activity. In this study, a subject independent weighted ensemble approach is proposed for automated classification of ADHD from raw EEG signals. Six deep learning architectures - EEGNet, DeepConvNet, ShallowConvNet, bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) with attention, convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM), and EEG Transformer were systematically evaluated under identical experimental conditions using a strict subject-independent protocol to eliminate data leakage. The three best-performing convolutional models are fused using validation-accuracy-based weighted fusion to form the proposed ensemble. The experimental results demonstrate that the ensemble obtained 94.84% accuracy, 94.85% F1-score, and 95.57% AUC-ROC, which is better than all individual baseline models. Subject-level soft voting correctly classified 18 of the 19 test children, achieving 94.74% accuracy. The observed improvements were statistically significant (p < 0.01), as confirmed by McNemar's test. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) were used to interpret the ensemble's predictions and enhance the model transparency. Frontal and parietal EEG channels, especially P3, F8 and Fp2, were identified as significant for classification, which is in line with previous studies in the field of ADHD. The results presented indicate that ensemble learning combined with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) can provide an accurate, interpretable, and clinically relevant framework for the detection of ADHD based on EEG signals.
