papers.title: Perceptions, acceptance, and concerns for AI adoption among Chinese Medicine Practitioners in Asia: a practitioner-based survey study
papers.authors: Chester Yan Jie Ng, Wen Xuan Kon, Wilson Wen Bin Goh, Linda L. D. Zhong
papers.abstract: Background Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been increasingly researched on its potential use in Chinese Medicine (CM), yet little is known about how CM practitioners (CMPs) believe, accept, trust and perceive its clinical utility. Methods A structured survey was conducted among CMPs across Asia assessing belief, acceptance, trust and perceived risk towards AI in four application domains of symptom identification, syndrome differentiation, treatment planning, and intervention. Data preprocessing included principal component analysis. Subgroup analyses were conducted using Mann–Whitney U tests and visualized with violin-plots. Ordinary least squares regression models were constructed to evaluate relationships between belief, acceptance, trust and perceived risk. Results Of 490 surveyed, 400 valid responses were analyzed. Respondents had a mean age of 37.0 (SD = 9.2), with a slight female majority (55.5%). While 56.0% reported prior AI use, most respondents reported familiarity with AI (93.5%). Scenario-based analyses showed lower belief, acceptance, and trust when AI was applied to CM-specific clinical intervention scenarios. No senior–junior differences were observed based on years of experience, but instead in clinical role and work setting. AI familiarity and prior use were strongly associated with higher belief, acceptance, and trust. Regression analyses demonstrated that belief strongly associated with acceptance (β = 0.50–0.73), acceptance strongly associated with trust (β = 0.77–0.96), while perceived risk had minimal influence. Conclusion Collectively, trust in AI appears to be associated with acceptance shaped by positive belief rather than risk perception, thus highlighting the need for training and education to support AI implementation in CM.

papers.title: Ensemble deep learning models for early detection of meningitis in ICU: Multi-center study
papers.authors: Han Ouyang, Ayush Singhal, Jesse Hamilton, Saeed Amal
papers.abstract: Background Meningitis is an inflammatory condition affecting the meninges, which may lead to neurological injury and death. The symptoms are similar to other severe diseases. It can take up to 48 hours for cerebrospinal fluid culture to confirm a diagnosis of meningitis. Furthermore, meningitis is a rare disease in terms of low prevalence in the USA, which increases the difficulty for early detection. However, advancement of machine learning with electronic health records has provided researchers and clinicians an innovative approach of detecting meningitis in the settings of intensive care unit and emergency room. Methods 214 meningitis patients (International Classification of Diseases, 9th Revision: 322.x) and 46,303 non-meningitis patients were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III v1.4 dataset with a positive-negative cases ratio of 1:216. After temporal filtering, 5580 samples with 6970 International Classification of Diseases, 9th Revision and demographic variables were extracted. We trained three base classifiers, namely random forest, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and a deep neural network (DNN) with cost-sensitive class weighting, and the outputs were aggregated by a logistic regression meta-learner. The performance of the ensemble classifier was evaluated on three different datasets including a balanced internal test set ( n = 68), an imbalanced internal test set ( n = 7382), and an external electronic intensive care unit (eICU) cohort ( n = 27,156), as well as measured through DeLong tests and SHapley Additive exPlanations. Results In the balanced test set, the ensemble model yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9424 (95% confidence interval: 0.8840–0.9870) with a sensitivity of 0.8514. The AUC of the imbalanced test set ( n = 7382) was 0.9305, with a negative predictive value of 0.9993. The stacking ensemble provided statistically significant AUC superiority over both LightGBM ( p = 0.0002) and DNN ( p = 0.0010) via DeLong tests. The AUC of the external eICU cohort ( n = 27,156) was 0.6855 with a sensitivity of 0.8455. Conclusions The stacking ensemble combining random forest, LightGBM, and DNN performed well on internal test sets, exhibiting a negative predictive value greater than 99.9% even with substantial class imbalance (positive: negative = 1:218). While performance was lower on the external eICU cohort compared to the internal test sets, sensitivity remained robust in heavily imbalanced setting. Therefore, the stacking ensemble may serve as a rule-out screening option for emergency rooms and intensive care units after additional prospective multi-site validation studies for its efficacy in real-world.

papers.title: Standards and guidance for transparent disclosure of human–AI collaboration content in medical research (2026)
papers.authors: Na Li, Jia yu Luan, Feng Qian
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) tools is propelling medical research into a new phase characterized by human–AI collaboration. In this process, AI has evolved from an external instrument into a functional component integrated into research workflows. As the boundary between human researchers and AI becomes increasingly blurred, governance challenges have become more salient. At the same time, internationally harmonized standards for disclosing AI-assisted content remain lacking, resulting in substantial gaps in both disclosure requirements and implementation in China and internationally. To address these issues, the Medical Journals Committee of the Society of China University Journals assembled a multidisciplinary expert team spanning medicine, biostatistics, epidemiology, medical ethics, scientific journal editing, and medical AI technology. Using a modified Delphi method, the team conducted three rounds of online surveys and two consensus meetings and drew on evidence including policy surveys of 1,692 medical journals, position statements from international organizations such as the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE), AI policy documents from major international academic publishers, and comparative studies of AI-detection tool performance. The process yielded ten recommendations addressing core issues in medical publishing. This guidance emphasizes four core principles—transparent disclosure, human accountability, risk stratification, and technology-assisted oversight—and aims to maximize the benefits of AI technology while safeguarding academic integrity. It provides a systematic framework for standardized disclosure of human–AI collaborative content in medical research and offers actionable guidance for researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, and academic institutions.

papers.title: Differing subjective and psychophysiological response patterns to a music-based auditory intervention for anxiety
papers.authors: Frank Russo, Yoseph Lahmany, Sean A. Gilmore, Harley Glassman, Rachel I. Ulrich, Rhiannon Y. Ueberholz, Adiel Mallik
papers.abstract: Anxiety comprises partially dissociable cognitive and somatic components, yet it remains unclear whether brief interventions modulate these systems in parallel. This randomized controlled trial examined subjective and psychophysiological responses to a brief music-based auditory intervention relative to an active auditory control (pink noise) in undergraduate students reporting recent generalized anxiety symptoms. Participants (N = 83) were randomized to the auditory intervention or pink noise. Cognitive and somatic anxiety were assessed before and after the intervention, while salivary cortisol, heart rate variability (HRV), and electroencephalography (EEG) indexed endocrine, autonomic, and neural processes. Cortisol showed a significant Condition × Time interaction, with larger reductions following the auditory intervention. Midline theta power also exhibited a significant Condition × Time interaction, reflecting opposing patterns of change across conditions, although within-condition changes were only significant in the pink noise condition. Cognitive anxiety, somatic anxiety, affective arousal, frontal alpha lateralization, and HRV did not show significant differential baseline-to-post change. During listening, HRV increased across conditions, but the Condition × Epoch interaction observed in the primary growth model was not retained when participant-specific slopes were included. Together, these findings indicate differing patterns of response across levels of analysis, with broad reductions in self-reported anxiety and arousal across both auditory conditions and greater condition sensitivity in the primary cortisol and midline-theta analyses. Because the cortisol and theta interactions were not retained in models including all physiologically valid observations, these condition-dependent findings should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.title: High resolution EEG microstate framework in fibromyalgia: An integrated multivariate and source localization approach to pain-related dynamics
papers.authors: Dino Soldic, María Carmen Martín-Buro, Cristina Rubio, Irene Peláez, Masaya Ueda, Ryouhei Ishii, Keiko Yamada, Keita Ueno, Martín García-Montes, David Ferrera, Roberto Fernandes-Magalhaes, Francisco Mercado
papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a nociplastic pain syndrome associated with altered central nervous system processing consistent with central sensitization, leading to enhanced pain perception. Despite its prevalence, the underlying neurophysiological mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we characterized resting-state EEG (RS-EEG) dynamics in FM using a high resolution microstate (MS) framework combined with multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) and source localization. 5-min eyes-closed RS-EEG was recorded from 57 female participants (29 FM patients and 28 healthy controls), and an 11-MS template was determined using the KL-GEV criterion. To assess the discriminative value of MS spatiotemporal features, we applied linear discriminant analysis with leave-one-out cross-validation. MS features were correlated with clinical measures, and source-level group differences were estimated using exact low-resolution electromagnetic tomography (eLORETA). MVPA identified MS G as the most discriminative state (AUC = 0.63), although it remained below commonly used thresholds for clinical interpretability (AUC > 0.75). Source-level analyses revealed significant differences in the insula (MS B and G), and in the middle frontal and postcentral gyri (MS E). No clinical associations survived correction for multiple comparisons, although exploratory trends suggested relationships between pain- and fatigue-related symptoms and MS B and E features. Overall, MVPA and eLORETA findings indicated altered spatiotemporal MS dynamics within somatosensory, salience, and executive networks in FM, consistent with central sensitization and dysfunction across large-scale pain networks. These findings highlight the potential of RS-EEG MS as candidate markers of pain-related neurophysiological heterogeneity within established FM, while their diagnostic utility remains to be established.

papers.title: Ethical dimensions of artificial intelligence in nursing and midwifery: A systematic review and online ethics toolkit
papers.authors: Xiaonyag Li, H Gin Chong, Mengying Zhang, Janet Delgado, Tamara Gonçalves Rezende Macieira, Sarah Collins Rossetti, Lu‐Yen Anny Chen, Vivian Chi Ching Hui, Lucija Gosak, Charlene H. Chu, Charlene Ronquillo, Jung Jae Lee, Elizabeth Nassuna, Helen Caton-Peters, Jin Zou, Siobhán O’Connor
papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, models, and tools are increasingly used in healthcare to support clinical decision-making, administrative workflows, and patient care but key ethical concerns such as accountability, equity, and transparency exist which affect nursing and midwifery practice. However, this discourse often overlooks the relational, contextual, and embodied aspects of care. This systematic review aimed to critically identify, appraise and synthesise the evidence on ethical dimensions of AI in nursing and midwifery to address these complex issues. Design A systematic review was undertaken, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses checklist. A comprehensive search using key AI, ethics, nursing and midwifery terms was conducted across CINAHL, Embase, MEDLINE, The Philosopher's Index and PsycINFO in March 2025. Results were screened on Covidence against eligibility criteria using independent reviewers and quality assessment performed. Data were extracted and inductive thematic synthesis applied to identify key themes. Results Six themes emerged. First, preserving humanity emphasised care ethics in AI-mediated nursing and midwifery practice. Second, beyond technical reliability explored safety as an ethical and relational imperative examining premature deployment risks, misinformation as patient harm, and risk mitigation. Third, autonomy, authority and accountability focused on governance challenges and solutions including patient and professional autonomy. Fourth, beyond transparency examined privacy threats, trust-building, and the governance roles of nurses and midwives. Fifth, justice in development and deployment concentrated on algorithmic bias and equitable implementation. Sixth, workforce preparation and deployment centred on capacity gaps and training, critical thinking and ethical awareness, academic integrity, and implementation barriers. Discussion This review offers timely and original insights of the ethical dimensions of AI in nursing and midwifery by capturing interconnected tensions between technological innovation and core professional values across relational care, patient safety, governance, information stewardship, equity and justice, and workforce preparedness. Clear recommendations include an urgent need for education to improve AI literacy, robust, inclusive and flexible AI governance, and the implementation of AI tools aligned with nurses and midwives' values and workflows. Furthermore, the review advocates for rigorous empirical research in AI ethics across diverse settings and populations. Addressing these issues requires policies that promote sustained leadership and investment to ensure nurses and midwives are meaningfully included in AI design, implementation, use and evaluation. Based on the review findings, an online AI ethics toolkit was developed to provide practical guidance and support for nurses and midwives in this emerging and important area of professional practice.

papers.title: Recursive nested innovation outcomes in AI-enabled learning: the role of capability renewal
papers.authors: Anjar Priyono, Irving Vitra Paputungan, Abdul Moin
papers.abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled learning generates heterogeneous innovation outcomes within organizations and how firms manage tensions among these outcomes through higher-order dynamic capabilities. Using a qualitative multi-case approach, this research investigates digitally intensive SMEs that have adopted AI in innovation activities. The findings show that AI adoption does not produce uniform innovation effects; instead, it generates three coexisting, interacting innovation outcomes within a recursive, nested system: efficiency-seeking innovation outcomes, pseudo-agility innovation outcomes, and transformative innovation outcomes. Efficiency-seeking innovation outcomes emerge when AI is primarily utilized for automation, standardization, and process optimization. Pseudo-agility innovation outcomes arise when AI enhances responsiveness and accelerates experimentation without sufficient integration of organizational learning processes. In contrast, transformative innovation outcomes develop when AI is embedded in more exploratory, strategically oriented organizational learning processes. The findings further reveal that the relationships among these innovation outcomes are recursive in nature. Strategic transformation remains influenced by deeply embedded efficiency logic, while transformative change simultaneously pressures operational efficiency logic. To manage these tensions, organizations need to develop higher-order capabilities, including optimization capability, adaptive coordination capability, and strategic renewal capability. This study contributes to the literature on AI-enabled learning, organizational learning, and dynamic capabilities by demonstrating that AI-driven innovation outcomes are not linear but emerge through recursive interactions among organizational logics, learning processes, and ongoing capability renewal.

papers.title: Innovative Adoption of AI-empowered Electronic Records and Information Management System in the Energy Sector
papers.authors: Shaikhah Rashed Alabdouli, Abdallah TA'AMANEH
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is considered a source of innovative technological transformation that has increasingly reshaped how firms govern, manage, and retrieve knowledge. However, its adoption in highly regulated sectors like energy remains underexplored in theory. This study examines the innovative adoption of AI-empowered electronic records and information management systems (ERIMS) in the energy sector of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), conceptualizing AI-empowered ERIMS as a form of knowledge management innovation entrenched within the energy sector. The study develops and examines an innovation readiness and adoption behavior model that draws on the technology readiness and acceptance model (TRAM) and the technology acceptance model (TAM). All the study variables were assessed using cognitive appraisal theory (CAT), which shapes employees’ responses to AI as an organizational innovation. The study employed a quantitative research design, with survey data analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings revealed that of the 26 relationships explored, only 7 proposed hypotheses were supported. Specifically, individuals evaluate the variables based on their ability to manage AI adoption in ERIMS and on their perceived benefits. The study adds to the theoretical literature and contributes to innovation studies by extending TAM and TRAM theories into the innovation adoption field in high-reliability settings, which, in turn, adds a knowledge management innovation layer to ERIMS governance and generates implications for innovation policy and organizational change strategies in energy-sector institutions undertaking digital transformation.

papers.title: From expert weighting to data-derived evidence: A leakage-safe, physics-motivated, uncertainty-aware machine-learning framework for CO₂ storage site screening in the Gulf of Mexico
papers.authors: Amir Hossein Nazari, Mohammadali Ahmadi
papers.journal: International journal of greenhouse gas control
papers.abstract: Selecting where to permanently store CO₂ across the offshore Gulf of Mexico (GoM) is a high-stakes decision that precedes every well, requiring thousands of candidate grid blocks to be ranked from sparse, spatially correlated evidence. The prevailing approach, expert-weighted multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), encodes this choice in subjective, scenario-dependent weights that cannot be validated, quantify no uncertainty, and predict none of the physical reservoir properties, storage capacity and injectivity, that ultimately govern where CO₂ can be stored. Data-driven models promise objectivity, but naïve machine learning (ML) on spatial geoscience data silently leaks information across neighboring blocks, inflates reported accuracy, recycles the very score it should predict (circularity), and returns point estimates with no error bars. Using the 2,559-block NETL GoM screening dataset as the sole data source, we build a leakage-controlled pipeline: an anti-circularity raw-feature whitelist, physics-based interaction features, per-target leakage whitelists, and a single spatial-block split tuned to match the train/test distribution of every target. Six complementary spatial learners, a physics-motivated gradient-boosting stack, a graph neural network, a physics-informed network, a geospatial transformer, a tabular foundation model, and a Gaussian-process kriging model, predict storage capacity, injectivity, and a multiplicative storage-deliverability index, each wrapped in distribution-free conformal uncertainty and explained with a common SHAP protocol. The best learner reaches a test R 2 of 0.98 on the composite suitability target under the original predictor set, and 0.89 under a stricter predictor set that additionally excludes two ordinal variables encoding part of that target's own containment-risk term; nominal 90% conformal intervals achieve empirical coverage of 0.83 to 0.95, and the data-derived suitability index reproduces the experts' geologic-storage rankings (quadratic-weighted κ up to 0.65). Because the composite target is constructed rather than observed, this figure quantifies learnability under leakage-safe spatial validation rather than validated storage performance. Where our ranking diverges from the expert screen, we show the divergence is driven by the weight carried by hydrocarbon-derived criteria rather than by superior storage quality, and we report it as a criterion-weighting diagnostic. The result is a reproducible, uncertainty-aware suitability surface for regional high-grading, intended to prioritize blocks for subsequent characterization rather than to initialize dynamic reservoir simulation.

papers.authors: Gökçer Eskikurt, Üzeyir Kement, Elif Güner, Çağkan GÜNER
papers.journal: International Journal of Gastronomy and Food Science

papers.title: ICT use and student achievement: Evidence from PIRLS 2021 using machine learning techniques
papers.authors: José Manuel Cordero Ferrera, Victor J. España, Lucía Mateos Romero
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the relationship between students’ ICT use and reading achievement using PIRLS 2021, adopting a cross-country approach with data on 138,100 fourth-grade pupils from 29 European education systems. Specifically, we focus on examining learning-related ICT practices at home and in the classroom and their relationship with reading achievement. To do this, we employ a machine-learning framework based on counterfactual prediction methods and a high-dimensional set of covariates to estimate differences in predicted outcomes across students with different ICT-related profiles, while also exploring heterogeneity by gender and socioeconomic status. We quantify uncertainty using resampling-based confidence intervals and assess robustness across alternative specifications and sample restrictions. Results suggest that learning-related ICT use at home is positively associated with reading achievement, particularly for activities related to online information search and the identification of reliable sources. These relationships appear to be stronger among socioeconomically disadvantaged students. By contrast, frequent use of digital tools in the classroom does not appear to be associated with better reading outcomes and, in some cases, are negatively associated with student performance. These findings suggest that education policies should prioritize supporting purposeful ICT use at home, particularly among socioeconomically disadvantaged students, while ensuring that classroom digital initiatives Are pedagogically meaningful rather than merely technology-driven.

papers.title: Predicting individual default in Australia: The role of socioeconomic conditions, macroeconomic shocks, and housing costs
papers.authors: Sharmeen Ara Rakhi, Simone Domenico Scagnelli, Rashid Zaman
papers.abstract: The scope of individual default extends beyond loans to various financial obligations such as utilities and telecommunications. However, earlier research rarely considers various financial obligations, leading to an insufficient assessment of individual default risk. Moreover, what factors that affect the individual default have received minimal attention. This study examines individual default in Australia over the period 2013–2023, focusing on both socioeconomic and macroeconomic determinants. The key variables include age, gender, ethnicity, employment, education, income, offence rate, and macroeconomic indicators such as GDP, inflation, house prices, and the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) cash rate. The study runs several models, including OLS regression, quantile regression, logistic regression and random forest machine learning methods, to determine what factors influence individuals to default. The results revealed that people who are employed and involved in a crime tend to be highly involved by default. On the other hand, with an increasing level of individual income, their possibility of default is reduced as income negatively affects individual default. Among the macroeconomic factors, both inflation and house prices lead individuals towards higher default while Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) cash negatively affects their individual default. Furthermore, moderation analysis indicates that rent expenditures and mortgage repayments significantly influence these relationships, with higher housing-related costs increasing the likelihood of default across different socioeconomic and macroeconomic conditions. Our results are almost robust across the random forest machine, except for the income level, which is the second-highest factor affecting individual default. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers, government agencies, and regulatory bodies by improving their understanding of the predictors of individual default and informing appropriate measures to mitigate default risk. The study also helps credit repair institutions identify factors associated with individual default and better support individuals in improving their credit profiles. Furthermore, the findings may help consumers better understand, monitor, and manage their financial health to improve their creditworthiness.

papers.title: Interconnecting diagnostic progress and management techniques in depression: A narrative review
papers.authors: Abdelrahman Mahrous, Hashim Hashim, Mohamed Gaafar, Hamid Alatas, Almoazzar Ibrahim, Mohammed Kheir, Mohamad Hetta
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder remains a leading cause of disability worldwide and continues to produce substantial personal, social, and economic burden. This narrative review critically examines recent progress in depression diagnosis and management, emphasizing the connection between diagnostic precision and treatment selection. Current diagnosis still depends on clinical assessment and validated rating scales, while biomarkers, neuroimaging, electroencephalography, digital phenotyping, and microbiome research remain promising but insufficiently validated as stand-alone diagnostic tools. Management has also evolved beyond first-line antidepressants and psychotherapy toward measurement-based care, augmentation strategies, somatic therapies, home-based neuromodulation, esketamine, ketamine, neuroactive steroids, glutamatergic agents, and carefully supervised psychedelic-assisted models. However, most emerging approaches face limitations related to cost, accessibility, long-term safety, implementation burden, and generalizability across populations. The review also addresses stigma, disparities between high-income and low- and middle-income settings, treatment-resistant depression, and personalized medicine. A clinically useful roadmap should integrate symptom profiles, comorbidity, patient preference, pharmacogenomics, biomarkers, digital measures, and longitudinal treatment response. Depression care is therefore moving from a single-modality model toward a coordinated, evidence-informed, and patient-centered framework in which diagnostic advances guide safer and more individualized management.

papers.title: Exploring user experience perspectives in co-creation of a balance exercise application for adults with intellectual disability: A qualitative study
papers.authors: Oscar Bergens, Eva Flygare Wallén, Marlene Sandlund
papers.abstract: Individuals with intellectual disabilities (ID) often experience poor balance, leading to a higher risk of falls. Exercise can help, but adherence is low because accessible and suitable exercise opportunities are often perceived as lacking. This study qualitatively analysed the user experience design preferences of adults with ID during the co-creation of a digital exercise application focused on balance and muscle strength. Two groups, comprising four and five adults with ID, participated in five co-creation workshops over 15 months, alongside two academic facilitators. Each workshop focused on one or more themes of developing an exercise application suitable for adults with ID. The workshops centred on developing, trialling, and improving the design of a new exercise application using an iterative approach. Facilitators coordinated the workshops and provided materials. Analysis was conducted in two steps. First, audio recordings of co-creation workshops were analysed using a qualitative approach to thematic analysis. Second, emerging sub-themes were structured deductively using the Optimised Honeycomb Model for User Experience. Thirteen sub-themes were identified within the seven facets of the Optimised Honeycomb Model for User Experience (findable, accessible, useable, desirable, credible, useful, and valuable), and further synthesised into the overarching concepts Use, Feel, and Think. Co-creators emphasised the need for a versatile application designed with consideration for users with diverse disabilities and circumstances, incorporating both visual and auditory methods to deliver appropriate information and exercise instructions. They also highlighted the importance of the application in conveying feelings of security, credibility, and belonging, as well as its ease of integration into everyday activities. The study offers practical guidance for inclusive design and highlights the value of co-creation in developing accessible health-promoting technologies.

papers.title: GPT-assisted formative feedback for middle-school linear function inquiry: Design and classroom evaluation of a gamified AlgeoMath module
papers.authors: Sejun Oh, Haemee Rim, Seongkyeong Kim, Yong Oh Lee
papers.abstract: Objective This study examined how GPT-assisted formative feedback could be integrated into classroom inquiry on linear functions. Methods A gamified AlgeoMath module combined rule-based graph checks, staged language-model hints, and rubric-based reports. The pilot involved 49 students in two convenience-sampled intact middle school classes. Analyses integrated submission logs, module scores, immediate pre-post surveys, expert review, and human-AI agreement. Results Task completion was near complete. Among initially incorrect task instances followed by a second submission, 57.5% were corrected on that submission. Module profiles highlighted covariation and mathematical justification as areas needing further support. Six of eight survey items increased after Holm correction in 48 matched pairs. Expert review primarily identified mismatches between feedback content and its intended scaffold level. Automated rubric categories agreed with each of two educators on 69% of 100 sampled responses. Conclusions The study connects classroom implementation with evidence about students' response patterns and feedback quality. It identifies scaffold calibration and the interpretation of partial reasoning as priorities for teacher-supervised AI feedback in linear function inquiry and provides a basis for evaluating learning outcomes in subsequent controlled studies.

papers.title: Gynecologic Oncologists’ Attitudes and Practices Towards Obesity Medicine in the Era of GLP-1 Inhibitors and Other Weight Loss Medications.
papers.authors: Youngeun C. Armbuster, Michelle Whittum, Tim D.V. Dye, Ashlee L. Smith
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate the awareness and interest in obesity medicine in a population of gynecologic oncologists. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted using REDCap, consisting of 19-questions regarding demographic data, practice setting, engagement in weight loss/obesity counseling and comfort in the practice of obesity medicine. The survey was emailed to 1364 Society of Gynecologic Oncology (SGO) members who were board eligible gynecologic oncologists, gynecologic oncologists, or gynecologic oncology fellows-in-training. The primary outcome was to assess awareness and interest of gynecologic oncologists in the practice of obesity medicine. Results 135 gynecologic oncologists participated in the survey. 84% (114) of respondents reported counseling their patients on the importance of weight loss, diet, and exercise, while 10% (14) reporting deferring the issue to the patient's primary care provider (PCP). 5% (8) of respondents reported prescribing anti-obesity medications, and 29% (40) of respondents reported feeling that gynecologic oncologists should be utilizing anti-obesity medications. The most common obstacles cited for prescribing weight loss medications was difficulty with insurance approval. 42.2% (57) respondents reported that greater than 50% of their patient population is obese (BMI 30.0-49.9 kg/m2), and 17.8% (24) respondents reported that greater than 25% of their patient population has BMI greater than 50 kg/m2. Believing gynecologic oncologists should be utilizing anti-obesity medications was found to be negatively associated with male gender, age greater than 40, and years in practice greater than 5 years. Conclusions Gynecologic oncologists report high incidences of obesity in their patient populations and treat cancers directly associated with obesity. While many gynecologic oncologists are interested in prescribing anti-obesity medications, only a small proportion of providers report doing so. Additionally, certain provider demographics may be associated with a lower likelihood of utilizing anti-obesity medications.

papers.title: Youth embodied perception of alleys in mountainous cities: Comparative neuroscience measurement between residential community and residential historic district
papers.authors: Cong Gong, Zhitao Wu, Changjuan Hu
papers.abstract: Although natural environments generally exert a more significant stress-relieving effect than built environments, emerging evidence indicates that pleasant built environments can also elicit positive emotional perception, offering new insights into improving youth mental health. This study employed questionnaire surveys, EEG, and fNIRS neuroscientific tools to capture perceptual data, and used point cloud data and 2D images to quantify spatial indicators. Environmental perception experiments in real-time environmental exposure were conducted in the alley spaces of two typical mountainous communities in Chongqing, China, with perceptual data collected from 44 participants. Through statistical description, non-parametric tests, and linear mixed-effects models, comparatively analyzed the following aspects between the two mountainous community alley spaces: (1) differences in young people's perception; (2) the pathways through which spatial indicators influence physiological indicators; (3) the interaction effects between spatial indicators and psychological perception in influencing physiological indicators. Results reveal that the residential historic district is associated with a more relaxed psychological state and lower brain activation intensity than the residential community. Perception of alley is sensitive to walking direction, with stronger brain activity when walking upstairs. The effects of spatial indicators on physiological indicators are context-dependent, with building color and spatial morphology showing stronger impacts in the residential historic district. The complexity of the alley environment weakens the influence of psychological perception on brain activity, and this moderating effect is more significant in the residential historic district. These findings support the development of youth-friendly communities in mountainous cities.

papers.title: Health-Related Quality of Life, Mood, and Sexual Function in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS): Assessing the Impact of Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills and Metformin Therapy (characters with spaces: 175, limit 125)
papers.authors: Sanjana Satish, Joshua Ewy, Christos Coutifaris, Allen R. Kunselman, Christina M. Stetter, Richard S. Legro, Anuja Dokras
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To study the effects of combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs), metformin, and their combination on health-related quality of life, depression, anxiety, and sexual function in women with hyperandrogenic polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and elevated BMI. DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a double-blind, double-dummy, parallel, randomized controlled trial (COMET-PCOS). SUBJECTS: , randomized to COCP, metformin, or COCP+metformin; analyses were subset to subjects with a response at both baseline and end of study. INTERVENTION: Six months of COCP (20μg ethinyl estradiol/0.15 mg desogestrel), metformin XR 2000 mg/day, or combination therapy. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Changes from baseline to study end in modified PCOS Health Related Quality of Life (mPCOSQ) domains, Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI Y-1 and Y-2), Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) and Female Sexual Distress Scale (FSDS). RESULTS: Compared to baseline, mPCOSQ scores improved across all domains in the combination group (n=60, p<0.01), COCP group (n=56, p<0.01, except menstrual health and acne domains), and metformin group (n=51, p<0.05, except body hair and weight domains). Depressive symptoms and depression prevalence were unchanged in the COCP and combined group but improved in the metformin group (p<0.001). State anxiety improved in the metformin and combined groups (p<0.01); trait anxiety improved across all groups (p<0.05). FSFI scores were lower in the COCP group for the desire (p<0.001) and arousal (p=0.03) domains with no difference in total score (p=0.07); however, sexual distress decreased in both the COCP (p=0.03) and metformin groups (p=0.03). There were no significant changes in the prevalence of sexual dysfunction in any group. CONCLUSION: Although COCPs and metformin are commonly used to manage PMOS, limited data exist on their impact on mental and sexual health. Our study demonstrates favorable or neutral effects of these therapies on mental health and quality of life in women with hyperandrogenic PMOS and elevated BMI. Metformin improved depressive symptoms and anxiety, while COCPs produced modest reductions in sexual desire without increasing sexual distress or dysfunction. These findings provide clinically relevant data for counseling women with PMOS, a group at high risk for mental health disorders.

papers.title: The evolution of robo-advisors in FinTech: a global bibliometric and thematic analysis, review and future agenda
papers.authors: Falak Khan, Abdullah Al Hejaili, Natalia Kryvinska, Farah Jabeen Awan, Neha Zainab
papers.abstract: This study presents a longitudinal bibliometric and thematic analysis of the global robo-advisory research landscape from 2017 to 2026, using a total of 384 peer-reviewed publications selected from an initial dataset of 865 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus databases. By employing co-citation, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis, the study attempts to highlight the structural and conceptual evolution of the field. The co-citation analysis shows that robo-advisor research sits at the crossroads of finance, marketing, and information systems, built on foundational work like TAM, UTAUT, SEM, and Markowitz’s portfolio theory; the co-authorship network reveals a diverse field dominated by small, internally cohesive teams, with limited cross-border collaboration, despite the citations that show substantial convergence. Bibliographic coupling shows the central presence of a trust- and intention-focused core, supported by broad adoption and behavioural literature, and a newer wave of extending the field outward into more outcome-based peripheries. The keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis differentiates well-known themes from accelerating ones. AI, trust, LLMs, UTAUT, perceived risk and value, anthropomorphism, GenAI, and DeFi remain robust across temporal specifications. The study concludes by providing actionable implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers with a call for future research by converting the findings into four research programs: adaptive and personalized investment intelligence, human–AI collaborative advisory, responsible and autonomous financial AI, and programmable and expanded investment ecosystems to ensure responsible and inclusive development of robo-advisory systems across diverse financial ecosystems.

papers.title: Interictal Epileptic Discharge > 1% Associated with Cognitive Impairment in Adult Patients with Epilepsy: A Cross-Sectional Study Based on Dose–Response Relationship and Discharge Characteristics
papers.authors: Qijian Lina, Huapin Huange, Junhan Lin

papers.title: Environmental Factors Associated with Long COVID Severity: A Lifelines Cohort Analysis
papers.authors: Judith C.S. Holtjer, C.H.L. Thio, L.D. Bloemsma, A.H. Maitland-Van der Zee, G.S. Downward, R.C.H. Vermeulen, Jochen O. Mierau, H. Lude Franke, Jackie A. M. Dekens, Patrick Deelen, Pauline Lanting, Judith M. Vonk, Ilja Nolte, Anil P.S. Ori, Annique Claringbould, Floranne Boulogne, Marjolein X.L. Dijkema, Henry H. Wiersma, Robert Warmerdam, Soesma A. Jankipersadsing, Irene van Blokland, Geertruida H. de Bock, Judith G.M. Rosmalen, Cisca Wijmenga
papers.abstract: Background Environmental components of the external exposome may influence the severity of long COVID, but population-based studies integrating multiple exposures remain scarce. Objectives To identify specific environmental factors most strongly associated with long COVID severity, measured as fatigue, quality of life (QoL), and number of symptoms, within a population-based sample of individuals with self-reported long COVID, and to compare results across multiple statistical approaches. Methods We analyzed data from 1,108 participants in the Lifelines COVID-19 cohort who had self-reported long COVID and had complete covariate information. Outcome information was obtained through questionnaires, and environmental exposures were estimated by geocoded linkage to participant’s residential addresses. Analyses were stratified by sex due to large differences in outcome distribution. Exposure-outcome associations were estimated using traditional regression models, horseshoe regression, Bayesian Model Averaging, and Random Forest, with adjustment for age, BMI, and education level. In secondary analyses we further stratified for urbanicity and severity of complaints. Results Findings varied across analytical methods. The most consistent associations were observed in men: higher neighborhood prevalence of low-income residents was associated with greater fatigue, represented by lower scores (B=-2.09), and greater distance to blue space was associated with lower QoL, represented by higher scores (B=0.26). We did not find any associations in females, or the number of present symptoms in either males or females. The secondary analyses showed differences between urban and rural populations for all outcomes, and when comparing the most fatigued and worst QoL (75 th percentile and above) to less diseased participants. Conclusion In this study, we found modest and context-dependent associations between certain urban features of the external exposome, particularly neighborhood socioeconomic status and access to blue space, and dimensions of long COVID severity. The heterogeneity of results across sex, urbanicity, and analytical methods highlights the need for targeted follow-up studies in diverse populations.

papers.authors: Yong Li

papers.title: Full-Domain Coupler: A Wireless Native Neural Backbone for Channel Representation and Deduction
papers.authors: Zirui Chen, Ziqing Xing, Zhaoyang Zhang, Hongning Ruan, Yuzhi Yang, Zhaohui Yang, Chongwen Huang, Merouane Abdelkader Debbah
papers.abstract: Data representation is a fundamental issue in deep learning. However, as wireless data scale and deeply couple across many physical domains such as time, space, and frequency, existing wireless artificial intelligence (AI) technologies lack dedicated representation solutions. Instead, they mainly rely on stitching general-purpose networks, a “tool-driven” paradigm that inevitably results in structural redundancy and bottlenecks in information flow. To fill this gap, this paper proposes Coupler, a wireless native-AI neural backbone designed for the representation learning of channel state information—the pivotal data in wireless systems. Leveraging the physical insights revealed by channel tensors, Coupler decomposes representation learning into individual domains on a layer-by-layer basis and then couples the learned domain-specific features through a dimension-staggered cascade. This full-domain interleaved learning architecture enables superior parameter efficiency and fine-grained multi-domain feature fusion. Based on this backbone, we use complex-domain multilayer perceptrons as spatial and frequency domain learners, while employing three optional mechanisms—convolution, attention, or gating—to capture temporal dependencies. This results in a series of efficient and extremely lightweight channel learning schemes with diverse functionalities, showcasing the compactness, versatility, and flexibility of Coupler. We evaluate these schemes on channel deduction, a general representation task encompassing channel estimation, interpolation, prediction, and feedback. Extensive experimental evaluations validate the significant performance gains and robust applicability, even for real-world measured data, demonstrating Coupler’s potential as a promising basic architecture in the design of wireless foundation models.

papers.title: Creation of a Global Sustainable Procurement Strategy for Kidney Care – an Initiative of the ISN-led Global Environmental Evolution in Nephrology and Kidney Care Procurement, Infrastructure, and Innovation Working Group
papers.authors: Caroline E. Stigant, Monica Moorthy, Katherine A. Barraclough, Nigel Suren Kanagasundaram
papers.abstract: Kidney care has a high environmental impact and significant inequity exists globally in access to kidney therapies. Over 70% of kidney care greenhouse gas emissions originate from the supply chain, making procurement practice a high-yield target for improvement. Via an environmental scan, the procurement, infrastructure and innovation working group of the ISN-led GREEN-K initiative identified six innovative procurement domains. Standardized interviews were subsequently conducted with experts in each domain. This information informed a draft global sustainable procurement framework, which was iteratively refined through consultation with broad stakeholders from both clinical and industry communities. This process led to the co-creation of a Joint Statement on Procurement (JSP), which aims to leverage procurement to drive innovation and improve global kidney health by increasing access to, affordability of, and environmental performance of kidney care goods and services. This paper outlines the methodology used.

papers.title: A Meta-analysis of the Effects of Biofeedback Interventions on Student Psychological Outcomes in Classroom Settings
papers.authors: Abdul Karim Ismail, Lars‐Erik Malmberg, Sonali Nag
papers.abstract: Biofeedback describes taking physiological measurements (reflecting various physical and psychological states) and presenting them back to the individual from whom they were recorded. Biofeedback may be integrated into classroom interventions to support awareness and possible regulation of internal states relevant to learning, with previous studies reporting favourable associated psychological and academic outcomes. Findings from 30 studies (N=2599, mean age 11.91 years) were synthesised to examine the effects of biofeedback interventions on students’ psychological outcomes with respect to a control. Biofeedback interventions varied in construction and primary aim but were all conducted with students and completed in classroom settings, a distinct intervention context. Biofeedback interventions improved attention-related outcomes (including self-reported attention or observed on-task behaviour) in both the general student population (g=0.77 [0.53, 1.02], p<0.001) and in students with identified neurodiversity (g=0.96 [0.51, 1.41], p<0.001). Similarly, biofeedback interventions improved stress-related outcomes (including self-reported reduction in anxiety, burnout and negative emotional states) in the general student population (g=0.75 [0.49, 1.00], p<0.001) and in students with mental health conditions (g=2.28 [0.97, 3.58], p<0.001). Biofeedback dose and intervention design features explained some between-study heterogeneity. This study advances current literature by aggregating the effects of biofeedback interventions on psychological outcomes in exclusively student populations within classroom settings, with the largest sample of similar studies to date, and including interventions constructed using measurements that reflect attention (e.g. EEG) or stress and related emotional states (e.g. HRV). Outstanding questions regard the effects of biofeedback interventions which reflect other physical and cognitive states relevant to the classroom setting.

papers.title: Exploring Artificial Intelligence in Teacher Education: A Scoping Review
papers.authors: Afaq Ahmed, Andrew Kwok, Kathy Ogden Macfarlane

papers.title: Human-AI interaction: themes, applications, and challenges
papers.authors: Li Zhou, Yu Li, Zining Zhang, Xiaoyun Chen
papers.abstract: In the digital economy era, artificial intelligence (AI) systems are driving human-computer interaction (HCI) beyond traditional interface optimization, shifting from command-response paradigms to dialogue-co-creation modes. Understanding the co-evolution of social and technical elements supports intelligent system design, governance, and innovation management. However, existing human-AI interaction (HAI) reviews exhibit three limitations. Methodologically, only 9% invoke Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and roughly 75% are descriptive syntheses lacking transparent retrieval protocols. In coverage, existing reviews remain fragmented, with no framework capturing the dynamic co-evolution of social and technical elements. Furthermore, approximately 85% of the reviews (105 of 124) do not address generative AI (GenAI) and fail to address the fundamental shift. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, this study reviewed the HAI literature. Publications were sparse before 2019 and have since risen sharply, while citations peaked in 2021 as recent cohorts have had little time to accumulate them. Distinct national patterns emerged: China led in publications but lagged in citations; the United States had the highest number of highly cited papers; the United Kingdom occupied the central bridging position in the collaboration network; Germany focused on explainable AI and human-robot interaction; and South Korea pursued both technical and social-science tracks. Thematic analysis identified five themes. Drawing on the literature, we developed the co-evolution framework for socio-technical systems (CFSTS), analyzed five HAI scenarios, and identified associated challenges and strategies. This study advances HAI research from fragmented descriptions toward systematic theory, providing evidence-based guidance for research and practice.

papers.title: Generative AI as a process of socio-technical co-evolution: a structured review of the transition from content generation to operational intelligence
papers.authors: Haowei Zhang, Ruobing Wu, Wenjie Hou, Ping Lan, Senchang Hu
papers.abstract: In the era of the digital economy, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become a transformative force, and its impact extends far beyond the scope of content creation. GenAI has rapidly evolved from generating text, images, and code to assuming operational roles across industries, science, healthcare, and governance. Tracing this evolution requires more than a catalog of technical milestones. A dedicated analytical framework is therefore needed. This study constructs a comprehensive analytical framework organized around three intertwined axes: technology generation, operational intelligence, and socio-technical co-evolution. The framework is applied comparatively across five domains: industry, healthcare, education, finance, and public governance. Three cross-cutting principles emerge from this cross-domain analysis. These are situation-sensitive anchoring, dynamic trust calibration, and responsibility-aware delegation. Risk tolerance, cultural background, and the depth of domain-specific knowledge are identified as key moderators that shape the transition from generative tools to operational intelligence. By synthesizing evidence across these dimensions, this review identifies future directions for research, design, and governance of GenAI systems.

papers.title: The effects of visual guidance interface on remotely operated vehicle operation performance using immersive virtual reality technology
papers.authors: Xiang Wang, Yewei Ouyang, Shiyi He, Ming Zhang, Xiaowei Luo
papers.abstract: Visual displays are central to the operation interfaces of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) in underwater environments, where scene clutter and poor visibility degrade operation performance. Visual guidance is a promising design strategy, but its efficacy across scene complexity levels, and its effects on efficiency and workload remain unclear. This study evaluated visual guidance using a virtual reality (VR)-based immersive display that simulated low-complexity and high-complexity underwater scenes. Forty-eight participants were divided into the visual guidance group and the non-visual guidance group and performed operational tasks in both low-complexity and high-complexity scenes. Results revealed that visual guidance significantly improved task performance in the high-complexity scene, reducing completion time and trajectory disorder while exhibiting limited benefits in the low-complexity scene. However, increased collisions in the visual guidance group suggest potential safety trade-off effects. Visual guidance also affected operations, manifesting as increased entropy in heave movements in complex environments. Visual guidance reduced overall workload as measured by NASA-TLX, particularly in dimensions of physical demand, mental demand, and temporal demand, while showing no significant effects on mental fatigue or mental attention levels. These findings contribute to understanding when and how visual guidance benefits ROV operation and highlight trade-offs relevant to display design. They support adaptive visual assistance that activates under high scene complexity, informing the design of effective visual assistance interfaces for ROV operations and advancing immersive display technologies for safe and efficient underwater human-robot interaction.

papers.title: iCyber-SkillBot: An HRI-Driven Platform for Skill-Based Robot in Industrial Warehouse
papers.authors: Ha Quang Thinh Ngo, Mai-Ha Phan, Thanh Phương Nguyễn
papers.abstract: Increasingly, warehouses are deploying robotic manipulators for cross-docking, pick-and-place, and sortation operations while engineers remain constrained in their ability to train with robotic systems because of the limitations in availability and accessibility of physical hardware. Though currently available robot simulators like CoppeliaSim, Webots, and Gazebo present a sophisticated general-purpose simulation software, they fall short in offering physical teach pendant hardware support, multimodal control based on vision, and skills acquisition specific to the warehouse environment. This paper introduces iCyber-SkillBot as a design solution integrating the concepts of 3D simulation, physical teach pendant hardware, vision-based gesture control, and warehouse-related skill progression through innovative synchronization architecture and multi-modal control. The novelty of the introduced solution does not come from the innovation of any new algorithms (kinematics, gesture recognition or motion planning are already known techniques). What makes iCyber-SkillBot unique is the combination of these concepts into an integrative real-time system used specifically for warehouse operator training. Main technical contributions are: (C1) Hardware-in-the-Loop synchronization architecture coordinating asynchronous input streams (RS232 pendant with 12.4 ms latency, GUI (Graphical User Interface) with 33 ms frame rate, Kinect vision with 87.6 ms gesture to motion latency) without overhead from distributed inter-process communication; (C2) Unified multi-modal control framework allowing smooth mid-task transitions among manual pendant, programmatic, and gesture-based control modes; (C3) Tight coupling of vision pipeline directly to kinematic solver for seamless gesture-based motion; and (C4) Warehouse-related skill progression framework providing structured training from level 1 (axis jogging) to level 2 (trajectory programming) or level 3 (gesture control) corresponding to practical cross-docking operator work flow. Case study simulation of a cross-docking operation in a controlled static environment proves the applicability of the platform for training warehouse operator basic skills (positioning, motion control, skill progression) with 98.9% motion execution success rate. Future work will be needed to test training transfer to more realistic dynamic warehouse environment taking into consideration conveyor timing variation, item position variation and WMS (Warehouse Management System) integration.

papers.title: How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis
papers.authors: Jingwen Li, Runke Huang, Hui Li
papers.abstract: The effects of school-based interventions (SBIs) on children’s neurodevelopment are poorly synthesized. This systematic review integrates neuroscientific evidence on how structured educational activities influence brain development in children aged 3-12 years. Following PRISMA guidelines, we identified 17 empirical studies (published 2014–2025) using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). Of these, 8 studies were included in a random-effects meta-analysis and all 17 in a thematic synthesis. The meta-analysis revealed a preliminary association between SBIs and reduced amygdala activity during stress regulation tasks ( r = –.28, 95% CI [–.50, –.02]), based on two studies, which should be interpreted as exploratory rather than confirmatory. No significant pooled effect for executive function, likely due to high heterogeneity. Thematic analysis distinguishes between mechanisms of plasticity and markers of intervention effectiveness: the first three characterize intra-individual mechanisms of experience-dependent plasticity, including (1) executive function interventions engaged prefrontal networks through both increased recruitment and enhanced neural efficiency; (2) socio-emotional programs modulated limbic-prefrontal circuits; (3) language and auditory programs shaped sensory-specific electrophysiological markers and cortical specialization; and the fourth theme identifies a neural marker of the effective process of intervention delivery, demonstrating that (4) teacher-child inter-brain synchrony was positively correlated with learning outcomes. By integrating findings across neural, cognitive, and affective domains, this review provides a conceptual framework linking pedagogical practices to neural plasticity and advances the understanding of the neurofunctional pathways through which educational experiences shape the developing brain.

papers.title: What does it take to grasp a tool? A fine-grained multiple-case analysis of hand-tool and tool-object interaction errors in apraxia
papers.authors: Josselin Baumard, Marie Teodoro-Oliveira, Léna Guezouli, Natacha Guzzo, Olivier Galaverna
papers.abstract: Apraxia of tool use is a neuropsychological syndrome characterized by difficulties in selecting or using familiar tools that cannot be better explained by primary motor, sensory, attentional, or language deficits. The neuropsychological literature indicates that tool use is a complex, multifaceted ability relying on heterogeneous cognitive processes and neural substrates. Patients may commit errors at different stages of the grasp-to-use sequence, including hand-tool interaction errors (e.g., holding tools upside-down), tool-object association errors (i.e., incorrect matching of the functional parts of tools and objects), and tool-object interaction errors (i.e., inappropriate mechanical actions), resulting in reduced performance efficiency. However, the cognitive origins of these distinct error types remain unclear, making their interpretation challenging for both researchers and clinicians. We report the case of D.B., a 69-year-old right-handed woman who sustained multiple strokes. D.B. demonstrated flawless tool selection and subnormal tool-object associations, but clearly abnormal hand-tool and tool-object interactions, in the context of impaired technical reasoning and preserved semantic tool knowledge and planning skills. This profile is discussed in light of previously reported cases of apraxia and optic ataxia. This analysis suggests that tool selection and tool-object association errors may stem from deficits in semantic tool knowledge, whereas hand-tool and tool-object interaction errors are more plausibly explained by deficits in technical reasoning. Motor imagery may also represent a contributing factor and warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Suppressed inquiry: The hidden toll of working with satisfaction-optimized AI
papers.authors: Ziv Carmon, Itai Linzen, Aner Sela, Yael Steinhart
papers.abstract: LLMs have become thinking companions for hundreds of millions worldwide, and they often do remarkable work. But their satisfaction-optimized design produces suppressed inquiry: the tendency for LLMs to inhibit rather than facilitate users' questioning process. LLMs appear fluent, confident, and seemingly all-knowing, their near-instant and polished output making non-LLM work feel unacceptably tedious and less eloquent. They affirm rather than interrogate users' assumptions, producing output that is deceptively adequate-shallower, less original, and less carefully reasoned than it appears. Seemingly competent systems also reduce vigilance and the monitoring impulse that independent judgment requires. Their responses also confine users within the frame they establish, narrowing what users think to ask. These costs are self-concealing: detecting them requires the very engagement that they suppress. And repeated delegation gradually atrophies users' capacity to reason independently. Three converging pressures make correction difficult: commercial incentives that reward satisfaction over substance, LLMs' tendency to revert to satisfaction-optimized defaults even when users push back, and a societal drift toward less-effortful engagement. We propose a research agenda to deepen the understanding of suppressed inquiry and how to counter it, to move closer to the remarkable thinking partners LLMs promised to be.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in higher education (2019–2026): A systematic review of applications and an evidence-derived multi-axial taxonomy
papers.authors: Maria Ranieri, Gabriele Biagini
papers.abstract: Generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) have expanded AI functions in higher education, challenging taxonomies developed before the generative-AI wave. Following PRISMA 2020, we reviewed 228 peer-reviewed journal publications from January 2019 to March 2026. The publication was the coding unit; codes represented the dominant educational AI use foregrounded in each publication. Inter-coder agreement was near-perfect for the Axis 1 coding scheme (Cohen’s κ = 0.98) and substantial overall for the observed interpretive distinctions (κ = 0.69–0.78). Full-corpus mapping placed 164 of 228 publications (71.9%) outside the four original Zawacki-Richter et al. (2019) categories, but this included transversal ethics/governance and adjacent scholarly-practice literature. The functional-adequacy test therefore used the 154 publications with a classifiable application-focused function: 64 (41.6%) fit the original four categories, whereas 90 (58.4%) required one of three additional domains—AI-enabled student support, content creation and instructional design, or institutional analytics and management. This result was essentially unchanged after removing the 2023 cohort (39/67, 58.2%), and all three added domains persisted in the held-out 2026 search block. Within functional categories, applications also differed in agency, epistemic position, and pedagogy. For agency, the corpus supports an observed assistive–augmentative–delegative gradient; the autonomous endpoint is retained as a prospective theoretical category rather than an empirically validated level. Pedagogical paradigm was less stable and remains the most provisional interpretive axis. We propose a configurational four-axis framework with ethics and equity as a transversal layer, intended to support decisions about oversight, verification, pedagogical alignment and governance rather than to predict educational outcomes.

papers.title: Topic landscapes and cross-period semantic connections in Computers & Education
papers.authors: Xieling Chen, Di Zou, Haoran Xie, S. Joe Qin
papers.abstract: For the 50th anniversary of Computers & Education, this study describes the topic landscape and cross-period semantic connections among 5,226 articles published from 1980 to 18 June 2026. Independently fitted BERTopic models for 1980–2003, 2004–2013, 2014–2019, and 2020–2026 identified 11, 15, 18, and 9 non-noise topics, respectively. We examine publication shares, exploratory annual trends, semantic similarity networks between adjacent periods, and within-period associations with a predefined artificial intelligence (AI) vocabulary. The retained semantic similarity networks include 22, 30, and 36 topic-level connections across the three adjacent-period comparisons. These networks consist mainly of one-to-many and many-to-many components rather than one-to-one correspondences. The 2014–2019 and 2020–2026 comparison contains one many-to-many component without unlinked nodes, whereas the earlier comparisons contain multiple connected components and several unlinked target topics. In 2020–2026, online learning and teacher competence have the largest publication shares, while generative AI shows the strongest association with the selected AI vocabulary. These analyses provide descriptive evidence on topic prevalence, annual trends, cross-period semantic similarity, and AI vocabulary association. The results should be interpreted within the scope of corpus coverage, modeling decisions, period definitions, and vocabulary selection, and do not imply causal relations or historical processes beyond the observed semantic patterns.

papers.title: StomataSeg: Semi-supervised instance segmentation for sorghum stomatal components
papers.authors: Zhongtian Huang, Zhi Chen, Zi Helen Huang, Xin Yu, Daniel Smith, C. R. Purushothama, Erik J van Oosterom, Alex Chi Wu, William T. Salter, Yan Li, Scott Cameron Chapman
papers.abstract: Sorghum is a globally important cereal grown widely in water-limited and stress-prone regions. Its strong drought tolerance makes it a priority crop for climate-resilient agriculture. Improving water-use efficiency in sorghum requires precise characterization of stomatal traits, as stomata control of gas exchange, transpiration and photosynthesis have a major influence on crop performance. Automated analysis of sorghum stomata is difficult because the stomata are small (often less than 40 μ m in length in grasses such as sorghum) and vary in shape across genotypes and leaf surfaces. Automated segmentation contributes to high-throughput stomatal phenotyping, yet current methods still face challenges related to nested small structures and annotation bottlenecks. In this paper, we propose a unified semi-supervised instance segmentation framework for multi-class segmentation of three nested sorghum stomatal components. We collect and annotate a sorghum leaf imagery dataset containing 11,060 human-annotated patches, covering the three stomatal components (pore, guard cell and complex area) across multiple genotypes and leaf surfaces. To improve the detection of tiny structures, we split high-resolution microscopy images into overlapping small patches. We then apply a pseudo-labelling strategy with class-specific confidence filtering and expert verification to unannotated images, producing an additional 56,428 pseudo-labelled patches. Patch-based preprocessing increases the top semantic segmentation mIoU from 65.93% to 70.35% and the top instance segmentation AP from 28.30% to 46.10%. Subsequent pseudo-label retraining further increases overall AP from 46.10% to 49.20% for Mask R-CNN with ConvNeXt-V2. These results demonstrate that combining patch-based preprocessing with semi-supervised learning significantly improves the segmentation of fine stomatal structures. The proposed framework supports scalable extraction of stomatal traits and facilitates broader adoption of AI-driven phenotyping in crop science.

papers.title: Evaluation of six generative large language models answering pre-analytical questions in medical microbiology
papers.authors: Michelle Bressan, Eline Nadieh Meijer, Vladimira Hinić, Tilia Ellendorff, Jean-Philippe Goldman, Tannon Kew, Oliver Nolte, Gerold Schneider, Adrian Egli, Magnus Ahlström, Diana Alame, Anton-Vazquez Vanesa, Demuyser Thomas, Flipse Jacky, Fabian Christoph Franzeck, Pauline Carlotta Göller, Imkamp Frank, Kaufmann Tina, Koliwer-Brandl Hendrik, Lindemann Vinzent, Lützen Lisbeth, Stefano Mancini, Menge Livia, Neidhöfer Claudio, Nielsen Stine Yde, Noger Thierry, Padrutt Maria, Petric Katarina, Píšová Barbora, Po-Yu Liu, Puthan Rosmi, Roulston Dallas, Kirstine K. Søgaard, Tagini Florian, Türkmen Recen Özlem, David Weller, Joel Wiederkehr
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Large language models (LLMs) have the potential to be integrated into diagnostics workflows, yet their reliability in pre-analytical diagnostic stewardship remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the performance of six LLMs answering common pre-analytical questions in the domain of medical microbiology. Next, we propose a blueprint to evaluate LLMs in medical microbiology. METHODS: We compared general-purpose models from OpenAI (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) and Meta AI (Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B), alongside two domain-enhanced versions (customised GPT-4 agent and Llama2-7B Medical) in a hybrid evaluation framework. First, we quantified the response length (word count), then assessed the similarity between LLM-generated responses and expert-reviewed reference answers (BLEU/ROUGE scores, BERTScore). Finally, thirty-three medical professionals rated the accuracy and completeness of the LLM-generated responses on a 1-7-point scale. RESULTS: Responses of OpenAI models showed greater similarity to the reference set and significantly outperformed Meta AI-based models in accuracy and completeness. The customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) matched performance of OpenAI's general-purpose models, while generating significantly shorter responses (p<0.001). Quality ratings varied markedly between professionals, as medical microbiologists and experienced infectious disease specialists assigned significantly lower scores compared to infectious disease trainees and medical students (p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: We observed considerable variation in LLM performance and highlight differences in perceived response quality across professional groups, emphasizing the need for critical appraisal when consulting LLMs for pre-analytical guidance.
