papers.title: Machine Learning‐Driven Noninvasive Prediction of Liver Fibrosis in Unclassified Liver Disease
papers.authors: Ye Yang, Yirui Hu, Ting Wei, Yue Chen, Wenkang Gao, Yupin Tan, Yuanqing Zhu, Yonggang Yuan, Zhuang Cao, Yunfei Zhao, Zexuan Li, Jiake Che, Yue Yang, Xinyang Wang, Shengqi Yan, Weiyan Huang, Shuyan Wang, Fuyu Yang, Lijia Yin, Xiaotong Du, Jiahao Liu, Rong Lin, Ling Yang, Huikuan Chu
papers.abstract: Chronic liver diseases (CLDs) frequently progress silently to advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, yet existing predictive models have largely been developed for patients with clearly defined etiologies. Here, we asked whether a noninvasive machine-learning model based on routine clinical variables and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) could accurately identify significant liver fibrosis in patients with CLD of uncertain etiology, and whether such a model would add value beyond conventional fibrosis scores for clinical decision-making. We retrospectively analyzed 503 patients who underwent liver biopsy at Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology. Twelve machine-learning algorithms were trained to predict significant hepatic fibrosis, and model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations. The best-performing model was then compared with four established noninvasive tools: FIB-4, GPR, Forns Index, and LSM alone. Among all candidate models, Categorical Boosting delivered the most favorable overall diagnostic performance, achieving the highest discriminative accuracy (AUC, 0.827; 95% CI, 0.754-0.900) and outperforming all conventional comparators across key classification metrics. We therefore establish an interpretable and clinically applicable panel integrating serological markers, age, LSM for noninvasive fibrosis assessment in patients with undefined or clinically ambiguous liver disease, with potential to reduce unnecessary biopsy and enable earlier intervention.

papers.title: From Challenge to Studio: A Prototype Frontline AI Innovation Mechanism to Address the AI Embedding Deficit in Healthcare and Educational Institutions
papers.authors: Bo Xie
papers.abstract: Introduction: Health systems are expanding access to artificial intelligence (AI), yet frontline integration into teaching, clinical workflows, and research practice remains uneven. We frame this gap as the "AI embedding deficit," reflecting limited organizational pathways that enable frontline professionals to translate local needs into legitimate, supported, and sustainable AI-enabled tools and workflows. This Experience Report describes a prototype intervention mechanism implemented at an academic nursing school: a rapid-cycle Nursing-AI Challenge followed by a year-round Nursing-AI Studio (NAIS) designed to stabilize and scale embedding. Methods: We implemented the Nursing-AI Challenge as a structured, time-bounded mechanism to solicit real-world challenges from nursing faculty, translate and curate submissions through an interdisciplinary facilitation role, match challenges to AI trainees and mentors, and support rapid proposal development culminating in a public showcase. We then developed NAIS to address continuity and embedding barriers revealed in the Challenge, incorporating continuous intake, environmental scanning, supported co-development, year-round coordination, formalized interdisciplinary partnerships, and a strategic memorandum of understanding with the Chief Information Officer's office to support legitimate integration pathways. Results: In the inaugural Challenge cycle (Spring 2025), nursing faculty identified 17 challenges spanning education, clinical practice, and research, and students in AI-related fields submitted eight proposals, followed by team formation, co-design of the AI prototypes, and a public showcase event. Implementation reflections identified key sustainability barriers including semester-bounded participation, summer momentum gaps, and intellectual property ambiguity. NAIS was established (Fall 2025 onward) to mitigate these barriers and support ongoing embedding. In early Spring 2026, NAIS launched "Teaching with AI," a clinical faculty innovation initiative piloting an AI-powered teaching tool fully deployed within the university's information technology infrastructure. Conclusions: A Challenge-to-Studio pathway may function as a practical prototype mechanism for learning health systems seeking to reduce embedding barriers and convert decentralized frontline innovation into durable, governable, and evaluable practice change.

papers.title: Low Serum Albumin, Body Mass Index, and Feeding Route Predict Treatment Interruptions During Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy in Head and Neck Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.authors: Kitti Jantharapattana, Nattarin Nilrat
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To identify nutrition‐related predictors of treatment interruption during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT), the primary outcome and to determine the secondary impact of interruption on 5‐year overall survival (OS). Methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed 440 head and neck cancer (HNC) patients receiving definitive CCRT (January 2013 to December 2016) at a tertiary academic center. Treatment interruption was defined as radiotherapy total treatment time > 56 days or cumulative delay > 7 days, and as chemotherapy delay > 7 days or premature discontinuation. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors; Kaplan–Meier analysis compared 5‐year OS by interruption status and tumor site. Results Among 440 patients (mean age 55 years; 81.7% male), 52.3% experienced chemotherapy interruptions and 14.4% radiotherapy interruptions. Independent nutritional predictors of chemotherapy interruption were: serum albumin < 3.5 g/dL (adjusted OR 2.54, 95% CI 1.19–5.43, p = 0.016), pretreatment BMI category (overall p = 0.032, driven mainly by a protective trend for BMI > 25 kg/m 2 [adjusted OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.30–1.00, p = 0.051]; the < 18.5 kg/m 2 subgroup showed a nonsignificant increase in risk: adjusted OR 1.41, 95% CI 0.84–2.35, p = 0.196), and oral feeding (vs. feeding tube as reference) (adjusted OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.07–4.76, p = 0.030). In non‐nasopharyngeal cancer, radiotherapy interruption significantly reduced 5‐year OS (14.3% vs. 29.9%, p = 0.03). Chemotherapy interruptions did not significantly affect survival. Conclusions Hypoalbuminemia (< 3.5 g/dL), pretreatment BMI category, and feeding route independently predict chemotherapy interruptions in HNC. Radiotherapy interruptions significantly impair survival in non‐nasopharyngeal cancers. These readily available markers should guide pretreatment nutritional optimization and feeding tube consideration in high‐risk patients.

papers.title: Underweight Versus Obesity and Gastrointestinal Cancer Mortality in Type 2 Diabetes: A Nationwide Cohort Study
papers.authors: Ji‐Hong Park, Kyungdo Han, Hun Jee Choe, Se Eun Park, Won‐Young Lee, Sun Joon Moon, Eun‐Jung Rhee
papers.journal: Journal of Cachexia Sarcopenia and Muscle
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Underweight is a well‐established risk factor for cancer mortality, yet its impact relative to obesity remains unclear in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), where current guidelines focus primarily on obesity management with limited guidance on underweight‐related risks. We evaluated the association between body mass index (BMI) and gastrointestinal (GI) cancer mortality across the full BMI spectrum in individuals with T2DM. Methods This nationwide population‐based cohort study utilized the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. We included 2 507 976 adults with T2DM screened in 2015–2016 and followed through 2022, with a 1‐year lag period applied to minimize reverse causality. BMI was categorized into eight groups: severe underweight (< 16.0 kg/m 2 ), moderate underweight (16.0–16.9 kg/m 2 ), mild underweight (17.0–18.4 kg/m 2 ), normal weight (18.5–22.9 kg/m 2 ), overweight (23.0–24.9 kg/m 2 ), Class I obesity (25.0–29.9 kg/m 2 ), Class II obesity (30.0–34.9 kg/m 2 ) and Class III obesity (≥ 35.0 kg/m 2 ). Multivariable‐adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for GI cancer mortality were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for clinical variables. Results During 5.75‐year mean follow‐up, 10 978 GI cancer deaths occurred (975 oesophageal, 4391 gastric, 5317 colorectal and 295 other GI cancers including small intestine and anal cancer). A reverse J‐shaped association was observed with mortality nadir at BMI 25.0–29.9 kg/m 2 , which served as the reference group. Underweight was consistently associated with increased mortality across all severity categories: mild underweight aHR 2.54 (95% CI 2.26–2.85), moderate underweight aHR 2.51 (95% CI 1.96–3.20) and severe underweight aHR 2.96 (95% CI 2.14–4.09), with the highest risk observed in severe underweight. Notably, all underweight categories were associated with substantially higher mortality risk than Class III obesity (aHR 1.35, 95% CI 1.05–1.73). Cancer‐specific analyses revealed that underweight was associated with the highest mortality risk for oesophageal cancer (aHR 13.23 [95% CI 6.77–25.85] for severe underweight), followed by gastric and colorectal cancers, whereas obesity significantly increased mortality only for colorectal cancer (aHR 1.52 [95% CI 1.10–2.08] for Class III obesity). Underweight was not significantly associated with GI cancer incidence after adjustment, and associations remained largely robust in 2‐, 3‐, and 4‐year lag and competing risk analyses, except for colorectal cancer. Conclusions In individuals with T2DM, underweight status is associated with substantially higher GI cancer mortality risk than obesity, with severe underweight showing nearly threefold higher risk compared to the reference group (BMI 25.0–29.9 kg/m 2 ). These findings suggest that underweight, rather than obesity alone, warrants greater clinical attention as a determinant of GI cancer mortality in this population.

papers.title: Physical Performance Moderates the Association Between Age and Executive Function in Older Adults at Elevated Risk of Dementia: Cross‐Sectional Analysis From the CITA GO‐ON Trial
papers.authors: Imanol Reparaz‐Escudero, Míkel Izquierdo, Mirian Ecay‐Torres, Miren Altuna, Carolina López, Ainara Estanga, Maite García‐Sebastián, María de Arriba, Naia Ros, Jon Saldias, Marina Limousin, Pablo Martínez‐Lage, Mikel Lopez Saez de Asteasu
papers.journal: Journal of Cachexia Sarcopenia and Muscle
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preservation of executive function is vital for independence and dementia prevention, yet the physical performance levels at which age-related executive vulnerability becomes detectable remain uncertain. This study examined whether gait speed, handgrip strength and leg muscle power influence the relationship between age and executive function in older adults at increased dementia risk and assessed how sex and white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden affect this relationship. METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of 920 community-dwelling older adults (aged 60-85) at high dementia risk, enrolled in the CITA GO-ON trial. Executive function was measured by the Trail Making Test (TMT B minus A) and the Stroop interference score. Physical performance included gait speed, handgrip strength and peak leg muscle power. Moderation analyses tested whether physical performance moderated the age-executive function association, adjusting for sex, socioeconomic status, depressive symptoms, cardiometabolic conditions, BMI and smoking; three-way interactions tested sex effects. The Johnson-Neyman technique identified regions of significance, the range of performance values over which the age-executive function association was statistically detectable. Sensitivity analyses included cognitively healthy participants and WMH adjustment. RESULTS: The average (SD) age was 69.5 (6.2) years; 48.4% were female, and average education was 13.0 (4.5) years. At baseline, 63 participants (6.8%) had mild cognitive impairment. Gait speed (β = -0.27, p < 0.05), handgrip strength (β = -0.08, p < 0.05) and peak leg muscle power (β = -0.007, p < 0.05) moderated the age-executive function link. Johnson-Neyman regions-of-significance were located in the upper range of the performance distribution. For TMT B minus A, the age-executive function association was statistically detectable below gait speed 1.83 m/s, handgrip 48.8 kg and leg power 438 W (1.0%-4.8% of participants), whereas for Stroop interference the corresponding values were lower (gait 1.68 m/s, handgrip 43.9 kg, leg power 366 W; up to 15.9% of participants). In sex-stratified analyses, gait speed moderated the age-executive function association for TMT B minus A in males and for Stroop interference in females. WMH burden was not independently associated with executive function. CONCLUSIONS: In older adults at increased dementia risk, higher physical performance was associated with a weaker relationship between age and executive function, independent of socioeconomic, emotional, body composition and cardiovascular factors. This moderation was most consistent for gait speed, with a sex pattern that differed by outcome. Longitudinal studies are needed to test whether maintaining high physical performance helps preserve executive function and inform preventive strategies.

papers.title: Fostering Clinical Pharmacology and Drug Development in India: A Perspective From SAC‐ACCP
papers.authors: Karthik Venkatakrishnan, Abhigyan Ravula, Sagar Bachhav, Mohammed Faruq, Bratati Kahali, AVS Suresh, Sanish Davis, Manish Lavhale, Amruta Gadade, Gurusharan Dumra, Vikas Dighe, Vipin V. Dhote, Bikash Medhi, Kiran Marthak, NirmalaN Rege, Tushar Garimella, Taruna Madan, Jagannath Kota, Ravi Shankar Prasad Singh, Gangadhar Sunkara, Manoj Jadhav, Nilima Arun Kshirsagar, Deven Parmar
papers.abstract: Since its inception in 2006, the South Asian College, Affiliate of the American College of Clinical Pharmacology (SAC-ACCP), headquartered in Mumbai, India, has fostered the discipline, emphasizing education, training and dialogue across academia, regulators, and industry. The 2026 Annual Conference, themed "Think Global Act Local," covered topics ranging from Artificial Intelligence in healthcare to the Genome India project and multi‑regional clinical trials, reflecting India's strategic maturation as it moves decisively from participation to co-leadership in global drug development. This Commentary highlights the proceedings of this summit, celebrating India's emergence as a globally visible leader in biomedical research and drug development at a key milestone of the 20th Anniversary of SAC-ACCP.

papers.title: Which Evaluation Strategies Help Students Spot Visual Misinformation on Social Media?
papers.authors: Shai Goldfarb Cohen, Sarit Barzilai, Linor Lea Hadar, Thuraia Copti-Mshael, Liron Primor
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The rapid spread of visual misinformation online, intensified by advances in generative artificial intelligence, presents new challenges for adolescents' digital information literacy. Although students' difficulties in evaluating online information are well documented, little is known about how they assess different forms of visual misinformation on social media. Objectives This study examined the extent to which lower secondary school students can successfully identify different types of visual misinformation on social media, the evaluation strategies they use, and whether these strategies predict misinformation detection across types of visual misinformation. Methods The participants were 272 students in Grades 7–9 who evaluated social media posts containing visual misinformation, including manipulated videos, manipulated images, and AI‐generated images. Students rated each item's credibility and provided written justifications. Evaluation strategies were coded using a theoretically grounded scheme. Results Students were moderately successful in identifying manipulated images and videos, but struggled to detect AI‐generated images, which were often perceived as credible. Students relied primarily on evaluation of visual appearance and content, while source evaluation and corroboration strategies were infrequently used. Across all visual misinformation types, examination of visual features, knowledge‐based evaluation, sourcing, and corroboration strategies predicted misinformation detection. However, corroboration was the only strategy that reliably predicted identification of AI‐generated images. Conclusions Students mostly rely on first‐hand evaluation of visual appearance and content, but these strategies are inadequate for detecting realistic AI‐generated visual misinformation. Instruction should emphasize active verification strategies, particularly corroboration, and support students in coordinating multiple evaluation strategies when engaging with online visual information.

papers.title: The Use of Cupping (Hijama) Therapy Among Athletes and Its Relationship With Sleep Quality: A Cross‐Sectional Study in Palestine
papers.authors: Faten Amer, Mahmoud Alatrash, Deema Salahat, Amir Kafrin, Nidal Amin Jaradat
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Wet cupping, or Hijama, is commonly used by athletes for recovery, yet evidence regarding its relationship with sleep quality remains limited. This study examined cupping use, perceived benefits, adverse effects, and factors associated with self‐reported sleep quality among Palestinian athletes. Methods A cross‐sectional survey was conducted among Palestinian athletes. Of 754 athletes screened at nine sports clubs and training centers across the West Bank, 470 (62.3%) reported previous wet‐cupping use; 468 had sufficient primary‐outcome data and were analyzed. Data were collected using a structured paper‐based questionnaire incorporating the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Analyses included descriptive statistics, exact and chi‐square tests, Spearman correlations, multiple linear regression, and path analysis. Results Improved mobility (30.8%), reduced muscle cramps (25.6%), enhanced immunity (16.2%), and increased endurance (9.0%) were the most frequently reported intended benefits. Cupping was commonly reported for chronic or recurrent conditions (99.6%), muscle strain (41.5%), and headaches (41.2%). Higher BMI and greater cupping‐session frequency were associated with greater perceived cupping benefit ( p = 0.010 and p < 0.001, respectively). Reported inflammation was associated with BMI category, gender, and competition level, while mild pain was associated with BMI category and competition level. Lower PSQI scores were associated with higher BMI, greater cupping‐session frequency, and greater perceived cupping benefit. In the multivariable model, higher BMI, vitamin use, greater cupping‐session frequency, greater perceived benefit, and manual rather than automated suction were independently associated with lower PSQI scores. The model explained 35.2% of the variance in sleep quality. Conclusion Cupping‐related practices and participant characteristics were associated with sleep quality. More frequent sessions, vitamin use, manual suction, higher BMI, and greater perceived benefit were associated with better sleep quality. These findings do not establish causality. Prospective studies are needed before cupping can be recommended to improve sleep or recovery.

papers.title: Building Graduate Capabilities Through a Course‐Wide Public Health and Health Promotion ECHA AI Curriculum Framework
papers.authors: Sarah Turner, Sara E. Dingle, Melissa Ensink, Emily Tomlinson, Tristan Duncan, Carah Figueroa, Shane Kavanagh
papers.abstract: ISSUE ADDRESSED: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming public health and health promotion (PHHP) practice, creating a need for graduates who can use AI ethically, critically and effectively. Although AI is increasingly being incorporated into higher education, the focus has been on individual units or assessment tasks, with limited guidance available for embedding AI capabilities across entire courses. This study responded to this gap by developing a curriculum framework for integrating AI capability across postgraduate PHHP programmes. METHODS: An iterative co-design approach was undertaken within a large Australian university to develop an AI curriculum framework for the Master of Public Health and Master of Health Promotion programmes. The framework was informed by competency-based education and integrated curriculum design principles. It was also aligned with local institutional AI principles and mapped to international accrediting competencies. RESULTS: The resulting 'ECHA' framework comprises four principles: Ethical and Responsible Use of AI; Critical Appraisal; Human-Centred Decision-Making and Professional Judgement; and Applied AI Literacy and Safe Practice in PHHP. Each principle is accompanied by discipline-specific learning outcomes, curriculum content and core graduate skills. CONCLUSIONS: The new framework offers a practical, programme-wide model for integrating AI capability into postgraduate PHHP education. Embedding AI within existing professional competency frameworks supports coherent curriculum design while preserving the human-centred values underpinning professional practice. SO WHAT?: This paper provides a coordinated, competency-informed approach to course-wide AI curriculum design, intended to assist universities in preparing PHHP graduates to use AI ethically, critically and responsibly.

papers.title: Pain Enhances the Auditory P2 but Attenuates Mismatch Response and P3a
papers.authors: Alexandre Lehmann, Marc Schönwiesner, Pierre Rainville
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Auditory input is known to modulate the perception of pain, yet the reciprocal influence, how pain affects auditory processing, remains less well understood. We investigated how continuous tonic pain dynamically alters auditory cortical responses in humans. METHODS: Using a three-stimulus auditory oddball paradigm combined with EEG, we recorded event-related potentials (ERPs) while participants experienced thermal stimulation under three conditions: baseline, non-painful warmth, and pain. We examined multiple stages of auditory processing, including early sensory encoding (N1, P2), automatic deviance detection (MMN), and attentional reorienting (P3a). RESULTS: Tonic pain modulated auditory ERPs in a stage- and component-specific manner. Compared to baseline and warm conditions, pain was associated with enhanced P2 responses to distractors and reduced MMN and P3a amplitudes, although no statistically significant differences in behavioural performance were observed. This pattern suggests enhanced early salience detection alongside reduced pre-attentive deviance detection and involuntary attentional shifts under pain. The warm condition selectively modulated N1 amplitude, indicating that some effects may be related to the affective and attentional demands of pain rather than somatosensory stimulation per se. CONCLUSIONS: Continuous tonic pain is associated with selective modulation of auditory processing, characterized by enhanced early sensory responsiveness and reduced higher-order attentional engagement. This biphasic neural pattern, observed in the absence of measurable behavioural differences, is consistent with predictive coding and salience network accounts of pain-attention interactions and highlights the sensitivity of ERPs for detecting pain-related neural reweighting. The absence of statistically significant behavioural effects should be interpreted with caution and may reflect relatively subtle or context-dependent influences of pain under the present task conditions. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study is among the first to systematically examine how experimentally induced tonic pain modulates distinct stages of auditory processing in healthy individuals using high-resolution ERPs, with a task design and hypothesis framework capable of teasing apart the cognitive mechanisms underlying these changes.

papers.title: Speech‐Driven Lip‐Synchronized Facial Motion in Humanoid Robots
papers.authors: Lei Li, Yongtong Zhu, Ji Hong, Jialang He, Qingdu Li, Ye Yuan, Jianwei Zhang, Jian Liu
papers.journal: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Speech‐driven human–robot interaction has advanced rapidly in recent years, resulting in a wide range of dialogue systems. However, achieving natural and immersive interaction requires not only fluent speech communication but also precise synchronization between the lip motion and facial motion. Modeling and controlling speech‐driven facial robots remain challenging due to the complex multimodal mapping between speech and facial motion, as well as the highly dynamic and individualized nature of human facial behaviors. In this article, we present a speech‐driven facial robot architecture that integrates matrix long short‐term memory (mLSTM) and generative adversarial networks (GANs). The system extracts deep features from speech signals, learns the mapping to facial motion parameters, and ultimately converts the generated facial motion parameters into servo control commands for the physical robot. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves accurate and consistent synchronization between speech and facial motion, thereby improving the naturalness of human–robot interaction.

papers.title: Connectivity‐Guided Individualized iTBS of the Posterior Parietal Cortex in Enduring Anorexia Nervosa: Network‐Level Target Engagement and Multimodal Response in a Single Case
papers.authors: Enrico Collantoni, Sofia Gentili, Arianna Menardi, Antonino Vallesi, Giovanni Librizzi, Elena Tenconi, Andrea Serino, Gaia Risso, Daniele Olivo, Fabio Sambataro, Angela Favaro, Valentina Meregalli
papers.abstract: AIMS: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe, often enduring disorder with scarce biological treatments, largely unable to address its core implicit features: habit-like food restriction and body-experience disturbances. We report a single-case application of resting-state connectivity-guided intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) to the posterior parietal cortex (PPC), a hub for body representation, peripersonal space, and affordance-based action. METHODS: A 31-year-old woman with 12 years of treatment-resistant restricting AN, enrolled in an ongoing sham-controlled feasibility trial, underwent 20 active iTBS sessions to an individualized left-PPC site maximally coupled with a body-representation × affordance reference network, assessed at baseline, post-treatment, and four-month follow-up. RESULTS: The protocol was fully feasible and well tolerated, without significant adverse events. Clinical change was gradual, with most of the weight gain occurring after the stimulation period: BMI rose from 15.65 to 16.01 at four-month follow-up and 16.40 over subsequent clinical follow-up. Blinded global improvement was minimal; anxiety fell below threshold, whereas eating-disorder and body-shape scores remained at floor. Target-reference connectivity increased in the a priori direction, toward the healthy-control mean. Exploratory measures changed heterogeneously, only partly tracking engagement. CONCLUSION: This case supports the feasibility and mechanistic plausibility of individualized parietal targeting in enduring AN, motivating a controlled trial to test its efficacy. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The parent trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07106645).

papers.title: Apoptin‐Derived Peptide Alleviates Temporal Lobe Epilepsy ( TLE ) by Limiting Neuronal Ca 2+ Overload Through the HSPA1A – AP2B1 Axis
papers.authors: Zixiao Tan, Qilong Zhai, Jingwen Cui, Xiaoying Gao, Xingan Liu, Zhijie Fan, Yu Liu, Jiahang Sun
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aims To determine whether the apoptin‐derived peptide (also named B9) reduces evoked seizure susceptibility and kainic acid (KA)‐associated cognitive and molecular abnormalities, and to define whether these effects involve the heat shock protein family A member 1A (HSPA1A)–adaptor protein complex 2 subunit beta 1 (AP2B1) pathway. Methods The therapeutic efficacy of B9 was examined in a pentylenetetrazol (PTZ)‐induced acute seizure model and a KA‐induced temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) model. Electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings were performed to evaluate epileptiform activity. The Barnes maze test was used to assess cognitive function in epileptic mice. Western blotting, co‐immunoprecipitation (Co‐IP), immunofluorescence (IF), and calcium imaging were used to investigate the underlying mechanism. Results B9 reduced seizure susceptibility, attenuated epileptiform activity, and improved spatial learning and memory. HSPA1A was markedly upregulated in TLE‐related datasets and experimental models. B9 suppressed the expression of HSPA1A and disrupted its interaction with AP2B1, which restored O‐linked β‐N‐acetylglucosamine (O‐GlcNAc) modification and protein stability of AP2B1, preserved GluA2 expression, and limited neuronal Ca 2+ overload. Knockdown of AP2B1 abolished the effects of B9 on evoked seizure susceptibility, cognitive performance, GluA2 abundance, and neuronal Ca 2+ overload, whereas AP2B1 overexpression reproduced the reductions in PTZ‐evoked seizure susceptibility and EEG activity observed with B9. Conclusion B9 reduces PTZ‐evoked seizure susceptibility and ameliorates KA‐associated cognitive and molecular abnormalities through modulation of the HSPA1A–AP2B1 axis. These findings support B9 as a potential therapeutic strategy for TLE.

papers.title: Residual Language Abilities Correlate With Diagnosis and Prognosis in Patients With Disorders of Consciousness
papers.authors: Chuan Xu, Jiaxin Gao, Jing Zheng, Jie Yu, Jian Gao, Jingqi Li, Nai Ding, Benyan Luo
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evaluating residual consciousness and predicting outcomes in unresponsive patients pose significant clinical challenges. Language assessment is crucial for these patients, and language-based EEG paradigms have shown promise in aiding diagnosis and prognosis in patients with disorders of consciousness (DoC). However, current language-based EEG paradigms either require higher-order cognitive functions, thereby misidentifying some conscious patients as unconscious, or rely on automatic processing, which fails to capture residual consciousness in DoC. METHODS: Newly developed, simple phrase sequences combined with neural frequency tagging were used to explore a language paradigm tailored to a critical processing threshold. This paradigm was designed to reflect the dynamic process of consciousness in DoC, while requiring minimal cognitive load. RESULTS: Our results showed that significant phrase-level EEG responses were observed in healthy subjects, MCS patients, and UWS patients in three conditions. Neural tracking of phrase structure showed a progressive decrease across three groups (healthy > MCS > UWS). Among the UWS patients, 52.38% (11 out of 21) and among the MCS patients, 45.83% (11 out of 24) exhibited significant ITPC at the syllable rate in at least one of the three conditions. Additionally, 38.10% (8 out of 21) of UWS patients and 33.33% (8 out of 24) of MCS patients demonstrated significant ITPC at the phrase rate. The language paradigm performance in this study was superior to that of other paradigms in detecting the proportion of residual language ability in DoC patients. Furthermore, cortical tracking at the phrase rate significantly correlated with 12-month outcomes and effectively classified patients according to their 12-month prognosis. CONCLUSIONS: The simplified language assessment demonstrates strong potential to detect residual language ability in DoC patients and could potentially be used to detect residual consciousness and determine prognosis in unresponsive patients.

papers.title: New Primary and Secondary Prevention Measures for Cutaneous Melanoma: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Maria Palau–del–Valle, Elena Bendala Tufanisco, María Amparo López-Ruíz
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cutaneous melanoma is the deadliest type of skin cancer, with increasing incidence and mortality rates. Therefore, primary and secondary prevention are of utmost importance. CLAIMS: The objective is to evaluate new recent evidence on primary and secondary prevention strategies for cutaneous melanoma. METHODS: Search of PubMed, Web of Science and EBSCOhost databases retrieved studies from February 2020 to January 2026, on prevention at both primary and secondary levels and that followed the PICO criteria selection process in the PRISMA method for a systematic review. Different assessment tools were used to evaluate methodological quality. RESULTS: A total of 404 citations were analysed, of which 24 studies met the inclusion criteria: 3 addressed primary prevention and 21 secondary prevention. Primary prevention found a possible chemopreventive agent and the possibility of a genetic control of the mechanisms of nevi fluctuation in life associated with height. The secondary prevention studies evaluated population-based screening strategies and emerging diagnostic tools, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tools included, and found a new wearable microneedle biosensor for in situ tyrosinase activity detection as a new approach for early cutaneous melanoma detection. It is clearly a limited primary prevention publication that shows poor new evidence for conclusions. CONCLUSIONS: Two new primary prevention approaches were identified, but both require further research before clinical implementation: aspirin as a potential chemoprotective agent and a possible genetic association between height and age-related nevus regression. Both require further study. Emerging diagnostic technologies, including AI-assisted tools and wearable biosensors for in situ tyrosinase detection, demonstrated high sensitivity but variable specificity, requiring further validation before routine clinical use. Population-based screening, patient education and risk-stratified surveillance improved early melanoma detection, particularly among high-risk populations. Most studies achieved moderate to high methodological quality, but diagnostic accuracy studies revealed some issues showing that require relevant improvements in diagnostic accuracy and standardization. The use of biomarkers is a promising new tool for early diagnosis.

papers.title: Body Weight Status and Its Association With Patient‐Reported Outcomes in Women With Non‐Metastatic ER ‐Positive Breast Cancer Undergoing Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy
papers.authors: Dalâyne Lopes dos Santos, Amanda Guimarães Castro Custódio, Fernanda Moura, Sulene Cunha Sousa Oliveira, Andrea Kazumi Shimada, Renata Arakelian, Heloisa Magda Resende, Anna Luiza Zapalowski Galvão, Bruno Santos Wance de Souza, Monalisa Ceciliana Freitas Moreira de Andrade, Yuri Cardoso Rodrigues Beckedorff Bittencourt, Maria Cristina Figueroa Magalhães, Luciana Castro Garcia Landeiro, Poliana Albuquerque Signorini, Daniela Jessica Pereira, Angélica Nogueira‐Rodrigues, Romualdo Barroso‐Sousa, Daniele Xavier Assad
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine associations of body mass index (BMI) with sociodemographic, clinical, treatment-related, psychosocial, and patient-reported outcomes among women with non-metastatic estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy. METHODS: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 557 women treated at 11 Brazilian public and private institutions from June 2021 to March 2024. Participants were classified as having normal weight, overweight, or obesity. Health-related quality of life was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-BR23. Characteristics were compared across BMI categories using chi-square or Fisher's exact test and Kruskal-Wallis test. Multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with BMI category, using normal weight as the reference. RESULTS: Of 557 participants, 172 had normal weight, 234 were overweight, and 151 had obesity. Education, comorbidities, hospital type, cancer stage, endocrine therapy, axillary dissection, prior chemotherapy, and radiotherapy differed across BMI categories. Participants with obesity had poorer physical functioning and greater pain. In the final model (n = 554), axillary dissection (OR = 2.51; 95% CI = 1.37-4.59) and continuous medication use (OR = 2.92; 95% CI = 1.78-4.79) were associated with obesity versus normal weight. Tamoxifen was inversely associated with overweight (OR = 0.58; 95% CI = 0.36-0.91), whereas low treatment adherence (OR = 1.54; 95% CI = 1.01-2.35) and continuous medication use (OR = 1.68; 95% CI = 1.10-2.58) were positively associated. CONCLUSION: Overweight and obesity were common and associated with sociodemographic, clinical, treatment-related, and selected quality-of-life characteristics. These findings support integrated survivorship care addressing weight-related health, comorbidities, functional limitations, and symptom burden. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships.

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models ( LLMs ) Against Medical Students Using Psychometrically Evaluated Authentic Clinically Oriented Anatomy Multiple‐Choice Questions ( MCQs ) at the Apply and Analyze Levels of Bloom's Taxonomy
papers.authors: Serdar Babacan
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by medical students as study aids, yet evidence regarding their performance on higher-order, clinically oriented anatomy questions relative to that of students-particularly at the Apply and Analyze levels of Bloom's Taxonomy-remains limited. This study aimed to compare the accuracy of five LLMs (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and DeepSeek R1) with that of medical students on authentic, psychometrically evaluated anatomy multiple-choice questions (MCQs) at the Apply and Analyze cognitive levels, and to qualitatively assess LLM response quality using a structured rubric. In this retrospective, cross-sectional study, 20 clinically oriented anatomy MCQs (10 Apply-level and 10 Analyze-level) administered at Bursa Uludag University Faculty of Medicine during the 2025-2026 academic year were identified from a pool of 397 questions and analyzed together with anonymized, aggregated student examination records. Each MCQ was presented once to all five LLMs using a standardized prompt. LLM and student accuracy were compared using Fisher's exact test. Item difficulty and discrimination indices were compared between Apply- and Analyze-level questions using independent-samples t-tests. LLM response quality was additionally scored using a six-domain LLM Anatomy Performance Assessment Rubric by two human observers and, in a cross-evaluation design, by peer LLMs. All five LLMs achieved perfect accuracy (100%, 20/20), significantly outperforming students, whose overall accuracy was 67.95% (p < 0.001). Student accuracy declined from the Apply level (74.79% ± 14.87%) to the Analyze level (61.13% ± 9.30%; p = 0.02), while LLM accuracy remained at ceiling across both levels (p < 0.001 for all comparisons). Analyze-level items showed significantly greater discrimination than Apply-level items (0.446 ± 0.070 vs. 0.248 ± 0.055; p < 0.001), despite being answered correctly by all LLMs regardless of difficulty. Because LLM accuracy showed zero variance, inter-model statistical comparisons were not applicable. Qualitative rubric evaluation showed all LLMs scored maximally on 4 of 6 domains (correct answer selection, Bloom's taxonomy appropriateness, scientific consistency, and absence of hallucination); differentiation emerged only in Anatomical Accuracy and Anatomical Reasoning, where Gemini 2.5 Pro and Claude scored highest (10.0/10) and Microsoft Copilot scored lowest (8.0/10) among human observers. Peer LLM evaluators rated model output as good as or better than human observers did across all comparisons, never lower (Spearman's ρ = 0.825, p = 0.086). Current-generation LLMs achieved uniform, ceiling-level accuracy on clinically oriented anatomy MCQs at both the Apply and Analyze cognitive levels, significantly exceeding student performance, and were unaffected by the item difficulty and discrimination properties that meaningfully differentiated student performance. However, a leniency bias among peer LLM evaluators raises concerns about the reliability of LLM-based peer assessment. These findings support the potential of LLMs as supplementary anatomy education tools while underscoring the continued need for expert oversight.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance in Anatomy: From Disclosure Toward Stewardship
papers.authors: İlke Ali̇ Gürses
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing anatomical education, research, scholarly publishing, and the development of digital anatomical resources. Current discussions of AI governance in anatomy have largely focused on author use and disclosure. However, AI now operates across multiple stages of scholarly communication and increasingly intersects with anatomical images, body donation, and donor-derived resources. These developments raise discipline-specific questions about visual authenticity, provenance, confidentiality, secondary use, and the continuing responsibilities associated with body donation and donor-derived knowledge. This viewpoint proposes the Anatomy Stewardship Framework as a conceptual approach to these challenges. Stewardship is defined as the continuing ethical, professional, and institutional responsibility associated with body donation. It guides decisions affecting prospective donors, body donors, donor-derived resources, and the knowledge generated from them throughout their life cycle. The framework organizes these responsibilities into four interconnected domains: stewardship of the donor, relational stewardship, stewardship of donor-derived resources, and stewardship of scholarly dissemination. Artificial intelligence is positioned as a technology that intersects with these domains and does not form a separate ethical domain. The framework is intended to support structured ethical reflection without prescribing specific decisions. It also provides a foundation for more specific guidance that may develop through engagement across the anatomical community.

papers.title: Co‐Creation Over R&D: External Knowledge as the Engine of Green Innovation in Italian SMEs
papers.authors: Angela Stefania Bergantino, Marco Cucculelli, Mario Intini, Syed Muhammad Ali Shah
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The transition towards a green and net‐zero economy has become a strategic priority for firms and policymakers, placing increasing pressure on SMEs to integrate diverse forms of knowledge to achieve both environmental and economic objectives. A recurring yet not fully resolved question is whether co‐creation among demand‐ and supply‐side actors is associated with firms' environmental performance while also contributing to firm‐level economic outcomes. Drawing on survey data from 6646 Italian firms, this paper investigates the associations between co‐creation, digital technologies, government support, and green innovation. Using a CDM‐inspired two‐stage econometric framework, we find that co‐creation and external enablers are strongly associated with green innovation. Green innovation is also positively associated with firm performance, suggesting that environmentally oriented innovation may be linked to economic benefits for SMEs. Moreover, our results indicate that internal R&D intensity has no significant direct association with green innovation among SMEs. These findings suggest that SMEs often rely on a network‐intensive model of green innovation, in which external collaborations play a central role, while internal R&D intensity becomes complementary only as firms develop greater organizational capacity.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities
papers.authors: Yao‐Chin Wang, Hsu‐Chong Yeh, Md. Mohaimenul Islam, Woon‐Man Kung
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches. METHODS: A title-field search of the Web of Science Core Collection identified 3,833 records related to ML and dementia. After restricting publications to 2000 onward and excluding non-analytic document types, 3,479 records were included in the bibliometric analysis. A subset of 3,223 original articles was used for thematic analyses. Publication trends, authorship, institutional collaboration, keywords, biomarker themes, ML objectives, data modalities, methods, shared research resources, and large language model (LLM) applications were evaluated. RESULTS: ML-related dementia research increased substantially over time. Diagnostic classification was the predominant ML objective (55.0%), followed by early detection or screening (10.3%), progression or cognitive-decline prediction (6.8%), and biomarker or feature discovery (4.7%). Structural magnetic resonance imaging was the most frequently identified modality (42.6%), followed by clinical or cognitive data (22.4%), positron emission tomography/single photon emission computerized tomography (10.3%), and genetic or genomic data (10.2%). Prominent biological themes included hippocampal measures, amyloid/Aβ, electroencephalogram, tau/p-tau, and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. Institutional networks showed distinct international collaboration clusters and frequent use of shared infrastructures. Transformer-based and LLM approaches emerged in recent years. CONCLUSIONS: ML research in dementia has expanded beyond diagnostic neuroimaging toward multimodal, biomarker, prognostic, and language model applications, although diagnostic classification and structural imaging remain dominant. Emphasis on biological integration, longitudinal validation, and clinical translation are needed.

papers.title: Resting‐State EEG Aperiodic Activity and Negative Affective Vulnerability: The Mediating Role of Big Five Personality Traits
papers.authors: Jin Lin, Zhiqing Dai, Sitong Feng, Ruiwen Song, Xinyue Jiang, Huanshu Xu, Ziyi Zhao, Hongpeng Lv, Hongxiao Jia
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Resting-state EEG aperiodic parameters characterize the broadband background component of neural activity. The offset reflects overall broadband power and has been linked to population-level firing, whereas the exponent is often interpreted, within a theoretical framework, as an indirect proxy for cortical excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance. These measures may therefore provide candidate neurophysiological trait markers of negative affective vulnerability, but it remains unclear whether their associations with trait anxiety and trait depression are direct or are statistically accounted for by stable personality traits. METHODS: A total of 164 healthy adults completed measures of the Big Five personality traits, trait anxiety, and trait depression and underwent eyes-closed resting-state EEG recording. Aperiodic exponent and offset were estimated at the whole-brain and regional levels using spectral parameterization. Partial correlations, hierarchical regression analyses, and bootstrap mediation analyses were conducted controlling for sex, age, and years of education. RESULTS: Neuroticism showed the strongest and most spatially widespread positive associations with the aperiodic exponent. Trait anxiety showed more limited associations, mainly with whole-brain and frontal aperiodic parameters. The association between whole-brain exponent and trait anxiety was no longer significant after the Big Five personality traits were entered into the model. Bootstrap mediation analyses identified significant indirect effects in this association through personality traits, with neuroticism showing the largest indirect effect and conscientiousness also showing a significant indirect effect. Trait depression was not directly associated with aperiodic parameters, although significant indirect effects through personality traits were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Resting-state EEG aperiodic activity, particularly the exponent, was more consistently associated with stable personality dispositions than with negative affective vulnerability directly. Personality traits, especially neuroticism, may statistically account for part of the association between aperiodic exponent and trait anxiety. Because the data were cross-sectional, the temporal and causal direction of these associations cannot be determined.

papers.title: Association of Cognitive Function With Event‐Related Potentials and Immune Inflammation in Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder
papers.authors: Lu Yang, Liemin Ruan, Zhongze Lou, ZhengLai Liu, Yiqin Huang, Li Zhang, 季蕴辛
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate cognitive function changes in adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD) and examine their associations with depression severity, event-related potentials (ERP), T lymphocyte subsets, and inflammatory cytokines to identify exploratory clinical and biological correlates for cognitive impairment in this population. METHODS: We enrolled 89 adolescent patients with MDD and 30 healthy controls, matched for age and gender. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment Scale (MoCA), depression severity with the Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD17), and anxiety with the Hamilton Anxiety Scale. ERP were recorded, and blood samples were analyzed for T lymphocyte subsets and inflammatory cytokines. RESULTS: Adolescents with MDD exhibited significantly lower MoCA scores, indicating cognitive impairment, particularly in attention, delayed recall, and executive function. ERP component analysis showed prolonged latencies and decreased amplitudes in the MDD group. Increased serum concentrations of interleukin-1 beta and interleukin-6, and elevated percentages of CD3+CD4+ and CD3+CD8+ cells were observed in the depressive group, with positive correlations between CD3+ cells and MoCA scores and between CD3+CD8+ cells and HAMD17 scores. CONCLUSION: Adolescents with MDD showed lower cognitive performance, which was associated with depression severity and immune-inflammatory indicators.

papers.title: Baseline Patient and Tumour Characteristics Associated with Mental Health in Men Undergoing Active Surveillance for Prostate Cancer
papers.authors: Beth A. Russell, Mia Tazi, Harriet Wylde, Alan Francis, Christian P. Pavlovich, Michael Peacock, Daan Nieboer, Lionne D. F. Venderbos, Prokar Dasgupta A, Mieke Van Hemelrijck
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives This study aims to examine how patient demographics and clinical characteristics relate to mental well‐being in men with prostate cancer (PCa) on active surveillance (AS). Subjects and Methods We analysed data from the GAP3 database, established in 2014. The study included men from three cohorts who completed baseline self‐reported well‐being assessments using either the Memorial Anxiety Scale for Prostate Cancer (MAX‐PC, n = 488) or the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy–Prostate Emotional Well‐being Score (FACT‐P EWB, n = 497). MAX‐PC scores were categorised as mild (<9), moderate (9–27) or high anxiety (≥27), while FACT‐P EWB scores were divided into tertiles (≤18, 19–20 and ≥21; higher scores indicate better emotional well‐being). Descriptive statistics and ordinal logistic regression were used to examine associations between baseline characteristics and questionnaire scores. Results Among the men across three cohorts, 488 completed the MAX‐PC and 497 the FACT‐P EWB. In the chi2 analysis for the MAX‐PC cohort, anxiety levels were significantly associated with baseline BMI, ethnicity, marital status, education, family history of PCa, PSA levels, T stage, smoking status, Charlson Comorbidity Index and erectile dysfunction (all p < 0.001). Ordinal logistic regression showed that a family history of prostate cancer was associated with higher anxiety (OR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.26–3.00). In contrast, no significant associations were observed in the FACT‐P EWB cohort. Conclusion Our findings highlight several baseline demographic and clinical factors associated with disease‐specific anxiety in men with PCa on AS. These results underscore the importance of routine psychosocial elements and of considering lifestyle and psychosocial factors when evaluating the supportive care needs of men considering or pursuing PCa AS.

papers.title: Multi‐Model Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Drainage Performance of Porous Asphalt Mixtures
papers.authors: Guangming Guo, Zhengchao Zhang, Fuyong Zhang, Guangyong Wang, Guoshan Liu, Kaidi Liu
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Porous asphalt mixtures (PAM), such as open‐graded friction course (OGFC) and porous asphalt concrete (PAC), are widely used in permeable pavement systems due to their excellent drainage capacity, noise reduction, and skid resistance. The drainage performance of PAM is influenced by macro‐scale void characteristics and meso‐scale pore structures. Traditional empirical models often struggle to capture the nonlinear, multi‐factorial relationships inherent in these systems, especially with small sample sizes typical in laboratory studies. This study introduces a comprehensive multi‐model machine learning (ML) framework to predict four critical drainage performance indicators—permeability coefficient, limit rainfall intensity, maximum runoff, and runoff duration—using 11 measurable void and pore characteristics. Nine regression algorithms, including Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR) and Lasso, were systematically evaluated on a standardized dataset of 98 PAC‐13/OGFC‐13 specimens. A stacking ensemble with a Ridge meta‐learner was employed to enhance model performance, achieving R 2 > 0.999 across all targets. Permutation importance analysis identified the connected void ratio, total void ratio, and volumetric mean pore diameter as the dominant predictors. This framework provides a robust, interpretable, and reproducible methodology for optimizing PAM mix design through data‐driven predictions of drainage performance.

papers.title: AI ‐Powered Personalization Across Digital Ecosystems: A Trust‐Centric Perspective on Intelligent, Ethical, and Adaptive User‐Centric Systems
papers.authors: Mohd Munazzer Ansari, Shailendra Kumar, Umair Tariq, Md Belal Bin Heyat
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Personalization based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a paradigm shift in user‐focused experiences in various digital ecosystems. We comprehensively and systematically discuss personalization methods through AI in the main domains including e‐commerce, healthcare, education, entertainment, and finance. The current paper critically examines the basic techniques such as collaborative filtering, content‐based filtering, hybrid recommendation methods, deep learning architectures, natural language processing (NLP), and reinforcement learning for their use in modeling complex user behavior and delivering personalized, context‐aware recommendations. We propose a clear conceptual framework that visualizes the end‐to‐end personalization pipeline, from data collection to user profiling, training, real‐time inference and feedback for optimization. Furthermore, the research uses mathematical concepts like a factorization of matrices and optimization methods to show how today's recommendation systems can be scaled and predicted. A real‐world analysis is also explored, providing real‐world benefits in user engagement, conversion rates and decision support systems. Besides technical improvements, this work also covers the key issues related to AI‐based personalization, such as data privacy, security, bias in algorithms, and fairness. This study highlights the importance of the inclusion of ethical AI principles such as transparency, explainability, and user control in order to deploy AI responsibly. New trends such as explainable AI, cross‐domain personalization and generative AI‐based adaptive systems have also been explained, outlining the future of research. Overall, this research offers a holistic perspective, by bridging the technical meaning and ethical concerns, and offers valuable insights to the researchers, developers and industry practitioners aiming at designing scalable, intelligent and reliable personalization systems in future digital environments.

papers.title: Intergenerational Green Artificial Intelligence Governance: Operationalising Environmental Accountability in Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems
papers.authors: Shukla Parul, Jackson Simango Magoge, I. B. Chatterjee, Praygod J. Mbilinyi, Malavika Nandivelugu
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence is increasingly promoted as a tool for sustainable development, climate governance and resource optimisation. Nevertheless, the environmental footprint of AI systems, including energy consumption, carbon emissions, water use, hardware production and electronic waste, remains insufficiently integrated into legal and regulatory frameworks. This article doctrinally examines Green AI through Edith Brown Weiss's tripartite framework of intergenerational equity comprising conservation of options, conservation of quality and conservation of access. It argues that current AI governance frameworks remain incomplete because they focus primarily on safety, bias, transparency and human oversight while treating environmental sustainability as a secondary or voluntary concern. The article develops an Intergenerational Green AI Accountability Framework that translates intergenerational equity into practical governance indicators, including FLOPs per task, CO 2 e per training run, CO 2 e per inference, kWh per inference, water usage effectiveness, renewable‐energy share, embodied hardware carbon, e‐waste destination and equitable access to green compute. It further proposes a polycentric governance architecture, such as model‐level environmental disclosure, lifecycle assessment, environmental model cards, independent audits, sustainable public procurement and equity‐sensitive international cooperation. The article concludes that AI should not be regarded as sustainable merely because it is deployed for climate or development objectives. It should be considered sustainable only where its own environmental costs are measured, disclosed, reduced and fairly governed.
